Magnolia championii Benth. 香港木蘭
FHK 8. 1861; FRPS 30(1): 117, pl. 26: 7–13. 1996; FGD 1: 7, fig. 6. 1987.
Magnolia pumila Andr. var. championii Finet et Gagnep., Bull. Soc. Bot. France 52(4): 36. 1906.
Magnolia liliflora Baill. var. championii Pampan., Bull. Soc. Tosc. Ort. Ser. 4, 1: 136. 1916.
Magnolia paenetalauma Dandy, J. Bot. 68(7): 206–207. 1930; FRPS 30(1): 117. 1996.
Magnolia pumila auct. non Andr.: FKH 28. 1912.
Magnolia tenuicarpella H.T. Chang, Acta Sci. Nat. Univ. Sunyatseni. 1: 56. 1961.

Evergreen shrub or small tree; twigs green and hairy when young; Stipular scars nearly reached apex of petioles. Petioles 0.5 –15 cm. Leaves elliptic, narrowly oblong-elliptic or narrowly obovate-elliptic, 7–14(–20) × 2– 4.5(– 6.5) cm, leathery, base slightly decurrent, cuneate or narrowly cuneate, apex acuminate or cuspidate, rarely acute, adaxially deep green and glossy, abaxially pale green, ± hairy on midvein; lateral veins 8 –12 on each side of midvein. Flowers globose, 1.5–2 cm in diam., very fragrant; peduncles 1–1.5 cm, densely covered with pale yellow silky hairs, with 3 – 4 spathose-bract scars ca. 1 cm below tepals; tepals 9, outer 3 pale green, oblong-elliptic, 3.5–4 × 2 cm, the inner 6 in two whorls, white, obovate, fleshy, 2–2.5 × 1.5 cm, apex sometimes emarginate; stamens 7–9 mm, anthers 6–7 mm, dehiscing introrsely, connectives exserted and forming a triangular mucro; gynoecium narrowly obovate, 1–1.4 cm, white villose; carpels 8 –9 mm, furrows reached to the base of style abaxially, ovules 2, parallel. Aggregate fruit 3–4 cm; follicles ca. 1 cm, each with a beak of 2 mm; seeds narrowly ellipsoid or irregular ovoid, 8 –12 × 4 – 6 mm.

Localities: Tai Tam, Tai Po Kau, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 1838; L. T. Lo 638.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi.
Ecology: Evergreen broadleaved forests. Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: Sep.– Oct.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: The type specimen (Champion 37, holotype, K) was collected between 1847 and 1850 from Hong Kong Island.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Authority: (Lour.) N. H. Xia & C. Y. Wu
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Magnolia coco (Lour.) DC. 夜香木蘭（夜合花）
Syst. 1: 459. 1818; FHN 1: 224. 1964; FGD 1: 6. 1987; FRPS 30(1): 113, pl. 26: 1– 6. 1996.
Liriodendron coco Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 347. 1790.

Evergreen shrub or small tree, 2–4 m, glabrous; bark grey, twigs green, smooth, slightly ridged and glossy. Stipular scars reached apex of petioles; petioles 5–10 mm. Leaves elliptic, narrowly elliptic or obovate-elliptic, 7–14(–28) × 2–4.5(–9) cm, leathery, base cuneate, apex long-acuminate, adaxially deep green and glossy, slightly wavy wrinked, margin slightly revolute; lateral veins 8–10 on each side of midvein, reticulations of veins sparse. Peduncles pendulous, with 3–4 bract-scars. Flowers globose, 3–4 cm in diam.; tepals 9, fleshy, obovate, adaxially concave, the outer 3 greenish, 5-veined, ca. 2 cm, the inner 6 in two whorls, purely white, 3–4 × 4 cm; stamens 4–6 mm, filaments white, ca. 2 mm, anthers ca. 3 mm, connectives exserted and forming a mucro; gynoecium green, ovoid, 1.5–2 cm; carpels ca. 10, narrowly ovoid, 5–6 mm, abaxially with 1 furrow downward to the base of style, stigma short.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. Y. S. Lau 1907; HK sheet 32247.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Flowering: Summer.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal (folklore).

Magnolia grandiflora L. 荷花玉蘭（洋玉蘭）
Syst. Nat. ed. 10, 2: 1802. 1759; FHN 1: 224. 1964; FGD 1: 8, fig. 7. 1987; FRPS 30(1): 125. 1996.

Evergreen tree, up to 30 m in native place; bark pale brown or grey, thin scaly fissured; twigs, buds, abaxial surfaces of leaves and petioles densely brown or greyish brown tomentellate. Petioles 1.5–4 cm, without stipular scar, deeply furrowed. Leaves elliptic, oblongelliptic or obovate-oblong, 10–20 × 4–7(–10) cm, thickly leathery, base cuneate, apex obtuse or mucronate, adaxially deep green, glossy; lateral veins 8–10 on each side of midvein. Flowers erect, white, fragrant, 15–20 cm in diam.; tepals 9–12, thickly fleshy, obovate, 6–10 × 5–7 cm; stamens ca. 2 cm, filaments flat, purple, anthers introrse, connectives exserted and forming a mucro; gynoecium ellipsoid, densely tomentose; carpels ovoid, 1–1.5 cm, styles reclinate. Aggregate fruit terete or ovoid, 7–10 × 4–5 cm, densely brown or pale greyish yellow tomentose; follicles dehiscing along dorsal sutures, abaxially rounded, apex long-beaked; seeds ovoid, ca. 14 × 6 mm; testa red.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. HK sheet 773, 23652.
Distribution: Cultivated in S China; native to SE region of N America.
Ecology: Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: Sep.– Oct.
Uses: Ornamental.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Victoria Peak, Ma On Shan, Tai Mo Shan, Sunset Peak
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Manglietia fordiana Oliv. 木蓮（綠楠）
Hook., Icon. Pl. 20(3): t. 1953. 1891; FKH 28. 1912; FGD 1: 4. 1987; FRPS 30(1): 105. 1996.
Magnolia fordiana (Oliv.) Hu, J. Arnold Arbor. 5(4): 228. 1924.
Paramanglietia microcarp Chang, Acta Sci. Nat. Univ. Sunyatseni 1: 53. 1961.

Trees, up to 20 m tall. Young twigs and buds reddish brown pubescent, glabrescent. Stipular scars semi-elliptic, 3– 4 mm. Petioles 1–3 cm, base slightly swollen. Leaves narrowly obovate, narrowly elliptic-obovate or oblanceolate, 8 –17 × 2.5 –5.5 cm, leathery, base cuneate, decurrent to petioles, apex acute, margin slightly involute, abaxially sparsely reddish brown pubescent; lateral veins 8 –12 on each side of midvein. Pedicels 6 –11 × 6 –10 mm, with 1 annular bract-scar, reddish brown pubescent; tepals white, in whorls of 3, the outer 3 slightly thinner, nearly leathery, oblong-elliptic, 6–7 × 3–4 cm, the inner ones smaller, usually fleshy, obovate, 5– 6 × 2–3 cm; stamens ca. 1 cm, anthers ca. 8 mm, connectives obtuse; gynoecium ca. 1.5 cm, 23–30-carpellate, smooth, basal carpels 5 –6 × 3–4 mm, middle ones ca. 5 mm wide on exposed side; styles ca. 1 mm; ovules 8–10, in 2 series. Aggregate fruit brown, ovoid, 2–5 cm; follicles dotted with protuberance on exposed side, apex with ca. 1 mm beak; seeds red.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Ma On Shan, Tai Mo Shan, Sunset Peak. Y. S. Lau 1439; HK sheet 33073.
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: May; fruiting: Oct.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal.
Notes: The type specimen (C. Ford 90, holotype K) was collected from Victoria Peak, Hong Kong Island in 1883. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Michelia × alba DC. 白蘭
Syst. 1: 449. 1818; FGZ 81, fig. 23. 1956; FHN 1: 226. 1964; FGD 1: 12, fig. 9: 8 –9. 1987; FRPS 30(1): 159, fig. 40: 8 –14. 1996.

Evergreen tree, up to 17 m tall; bark grey; young twigs and buds densely covered with pale yellowish white hairs. Stipular scars nearly reached middle of petioles. Petioles 1.5–2 cm, sparsely puberulous. Leaves long-elliptic or lanceolate-elliptic, 10–27 × 4–9.5 cm, thinly leathery, base cuneate, apex long acuminate or caudate-acuminate, adaxially glabrous, abaxially sparsely puberulous, reticulations of veins very conspicuous on both surfaces when dry. Flowers white, very fragrant; tepals 10, lanceolate, 3–4 × 0.3–0.5 cm; connectives exserted and forming a long tip; gynoecium puberulous, gynoecium stalk ca. 4 mm; carpels numerous, usually undeveloped.

Locality: Widely cultivated in gardens. Y. S. Lau 1840; L. T. Lo 96.
Distribution: Widely cultivated in S China and tropical and subtropical regions of the world.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr.–Sep.
Uses: Ornamental.

Michelia champaca L. 黃蘭
Sp. Pl. 536. 1753; FGZ 81. 1956; FHN 1: 227. 1964; FGD 1: 12, fig. 9: 1–7. 1987; FRPS 30(1): 157, fig. 40: 1–7. 1996.

Evergreen tree, up to 10 m or taller; buds, young twigs, young leaves and petioles covered with pale yellow appressed hairs. Stipular scars exceeding middle of petioles. Petioles 2– 4 cm. Leaves lanceolate-ovate or lanceolate-long elliptic, 10 –20(–25) × 4.5 –9 cm, base broadly cuneate or cuneate, apex long acuminate or subcaudate, abaxially slightly puberulous. Flowers yellow, fragrant, tepals 15–20, oblanceolate, 2–4 × 0.4 – 0.5 cm; connectives exserted and forming a long tip; gynoecium hairy; gynoecium stalk ca. 3 mm. Aggregate fruit 7–15 cm; follicles obovoid-ellipsoid, 1–1.5 cm, tuberculate; seeds 2– 4, rugose.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. Y. S. Lau 2617; HK sheet 820.
Distribution: Xizang, Yunnan, cultivated in Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan and Taiwan; India, Nepal, Myanmar, Vietnam.
Ecology: Flowering: Jun.–Jul.; fruiting: Sep.– Oct.
Uses: Ornamental.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Michelia chapensis Dandy 樂昌含笑（景烈含笑）
Journ. Bot. 67: 222. 1929; FGD 1: 17, fig. 16. 1987; FRPS 30(1): 170, pl. 45: 7–9. 1996.
Michelia tsoi Dandy, J. Bot. 68: 213. 1930.

Tree, up to 15–30 m tall; bark grey to dark brown; twigs glabrous or greyish puberulous on nodes when young. Petioles 1.5 –2.5 cm, without stipular scar, adaxially furrowed, puberulous when young, glabrescent. Leaves obovate, narrowly obovate or oblong-obovate, 6.5–15(–16) × 3.5 –6.5(–7) cm, thinly leathery, base cuneate or broadly cuneate, apex abruptly short-acuminate, tip blunt, adaxially deep green and glossy; lateral veins 9 –12(15) on each side of midvein. Peduncles 0.4 –1 cm, puberulous, with 2–5 bract scar. Flowers fragrant; tepals 6, pale yellow, in 2 whorls, outer 3 obovate-elliptic, ca. 3 × 1.5 cm; inner 3 narrower; stamens 1.7–2 cm, anthers 1.1–1.5 cm, connectives exserted and forming a 1 mm mucro; gynoecium narrowly cylindrical, ca. 1.5 cm; gynophore ca. 7 mm, densely covered with silvery appressed hairs; carpels ovoid, ca. 2 mm, styles ca. 1.5 mm; ovules 6 in each carpel. Aggregate fruit ca. 10 cm, fruiting peduncle ca. 2 mm; follicles ellipsoid or ovoid, 1–1.5 × 1 cm, base broad, apex with short and curved tip; seeds red, ovoid or ellipsoid-ovoid, ca. 1 × 0.6 cm.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai. N. H. Li 56; G. Barretto 283.
Distribution: Jiangxi, Hunan, Guangdong, Guangxi; Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Mar.–Apr.; fruiting: Aug.–Sep.
Notes: Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Michelia figo (Lour.) Spreng. 含笑
Syst. Veg. 2: 643. 1825; FGZ 82. 1956; FHN 1: 227. 1964; FGD 1: 12, fig. 10: 1– 6. 1987; FRPS 30(1): 165, pl. 43: 1– 6. 1996.
Liriodendron figo Lour. Fl. Cochinch. 1: 347. 1790.
Magnolia fuscata Andr., Bot. Repos. 4: t. 229. 1802.
Magnolia figo (Lour.) DC., Syst. Nat. 1: 460. 1817.
Michelia fuscata Bl. ex Wall., Fl. Javae 19-20: 8. 1829; FKH 28. 1912.
Liriopsis fuscata (Andr.) Spach, Hist. Nat. Veg. 7: 461. 1839.

Evergreen shrub, 2–3 m tall, much branched; buds, young twigs, petioles and peduncles densely yellowish brown-tomentose. Stipular scars reached petiole apex. Petioles 2–4 mm. Leaves narrowly elliptic or obovate-elliptic, 4–10 × 1.8–4.5 cm, base cuneate or broadly cuneate, apex obtusely acute, adaxially glossy and glabrous, abaxially covered with brown appressed hairs on midvein, other parts glabrescent. Flowers erect, sweet fragrant; tepals 6, fleshy, thick, long-elliptic, 1.2–2.0 × 0.6 –1.1 cm, pale yellow, margin sometimes red or purple; stamens 7–8 mm, connectives exserted and forming a sharp tip; gynoecium glabrous, ca. 7 mm, exceeding androecium; gynoecium stalk ca. 6 mm, pale yellow tomentose. Aggregate fruit 2–3.5 cm; follicles ovoid or globose, apex beaked.

Locality: Widely cultivated in gardens. Y. W. Lam 204; F. W. Xing 8626.
Distribution: S China, widely cultivated.
Ecology: Flowering: Mar.–May; fruiting: Jul. –Aug.
Uses: Ornamental.

Michelia maudiae Dunn 深山含笑（莫氏含笑）
J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 38: 353. 1908; FKH 28. 1912; FGD 1: 14, fig.12. 1987; FRPS 30(1): 179. 1996.
Michelia chingii W. C. Cheng, Contr. Biol. Lab. Chin. Assoc. Advancem. Sci., Sect. Bot. 10: 110. 1936.

Tree, up to 20 m tall, glabrous. Buds, young twigs, abaxial surfaces of leaves, bracts white farinose. Petioles 1–3 cm, without stipular scars. Leaves oblong-elliptic, rarely elliptic-oblong, 7–18 × 3.5–8.5 cm, leathery, base cuneate, broadly cuneate or obtuse, apex abruptly short-acuminate, tip blunt, adaxially deep green and glossy, abaxially greyish green and glaucous; lateral veins 7–12 on each side of midvein. Peduncles green, with 3 annular bract scars; spathose bracts pale brown, thinly leathery, ca. 3 cm. Flowers fragrant; tepals 9, purely white, slightly pale red at base, outer 3 obovate, 5–7 × 3.5–4 cm, base clawed, apex acute, inner 6 narrower, nearly spoon-shaped, apex acute; stamens 1.5–2.2 cm, filaments flat, pale purple, ca. 4 mm, connectives exserted and forming a 1–2 mm tip; gynoecium 1.5–1.8 cm; gynophore 5–8 mm; carpels green, narrowly ovoid, 5–6 mm including style. Aggregate fruit 7–15 cm; follicles ellipsoid, obovoid, ovoid, apex obtuse or abruptly mucronate. Seeds red, obliquely ovoid, ca. 1 × 0.5 cm, slightly compressed.

Locality: Lantau Peak, Sunset Peak. Y. S. Lau 2952; L. T. Lo 316.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Fujian, Zhejiang, Hunan.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Feb.–Mar.; fruiting: Sep.– Oct.
Uses: Timber; ornamental.
Notes: The lectotype specimen (S. T. Dunn s.n. in Herb. Hongk. No. 2065, HK sheet 834) was collected from “Fung Wong Shan” (Lantau Peak), Lantau Island in 1905. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): A rare species in Hong Kong, only found in Tai Mo Shan
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Michelia odora (Chun) B. L. Chen & Noot. 觀光木
Ann. Missouri Bot. Gard. 80(4): 1086. 1993.
Tsoongiodendron odorum Chun, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 8: 283. 1963; FHN 1: 230. 1964; FGD 1: 20, fig. 20. 1987; FRPS 30(1): 194, pl. 55. 1996.

Evergreen tree, up to 25 m tall; twigs, buds, petioles, abaxial surfaces of leaves and peduncles yellowish brown-strigose. Stipular scars nearly reached middle of petioles. Petioles 1.2–2.5 cm, flattened at base. Leaves obovate-elliptic, 8 –17 × 3.5–7 cm, base cuneate, apex acute or obtuse, adaxially green and glossy; lateral veins 10–12 on each side of midvein; midvein, lateral veins and reticulations impressed adaxially. Spathose bract dehiscing along one side, pubescent. Peduncles 6 mm, with 1 bract scar. Flowers fragrant; tepals ivory-yellow, dotted with red, narrowly obovate-elliptic, outer ones largest, 1.7–2 × 0.7–0.8 cm, innermost ones 1.5–1.6 × 0.5 cm; stamens 35–45, 7.5–8.5 mm, filaments white or reddish, 2–3 mm; carpels 9–13, narrowly ovoid, densely appressed pubescent, styles subulate, red, ca. 2 mm, ventral sutures conspicuous; gynophore stout, ca. 2 mm, sulcate, densely strigose. Aggregate fruit long-ellipsoid, sometimes globose because of upper carpels aborted, 13 × 9 cm, pericarp olive-green, dark brown when dried, markedly yellow-dotted; valves thick, 1–2 cm; fruiting: peduncle 1–2 × 1–2 cm; seeds 4– 6 in each carpel, ellipsoid or triangular-obovoid, ca. 1.5 × 0.8 cm.

Locality: A rare species in Hong Kong, only found in Tai Mo Shan. F. W. Xing 7898, 8928; Y. W. Lam 199.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Mar.; fruiting: Oct.–Dec.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Yulania × soulangeana (Soul.-Bod.) D. L. Fu 二喬木蘭（紫玉蘭）
J. Wuhan Bot. Res. 19(3): 198. 2001.
Magnolia soulangeana Soul.-Bod., Mem. Soc. L. Paris 269. 1826; FRPS 30(1): 132. 1996.

Deciduous small tree, 6–10 m tall; twigs glabrous. Stipular scars about 1/3 the length of petioles. Petioles 1–1.5 cm, pubescent. Leaves obovate, 6 –15 × 4 –7.5 cm, papery, base cuneate, gradually narrowed, apex short acute, adaxially remaining with hairs along midvein at base, abaxially ± pubescent; lateral veins 7–9 on each side of midvein. Flowers appearing before leaves, pale red to dark red; tepals 6 –9, the outer 3 usually one third shorter than the inner ones; stamens 1–1.2 cm, anthers ca. 6 mm, dehiscing laterally, connectives exserted and forming a mucro; gynoecium glabrous, cylindrical, ca. 1.5 cm. Aggregate fruit ca. 8 × 3 cm; follicles ovoid or obovoid, 1–1.5 cm, black when mature, white-lenticeled; seeds dark brown, broadly obovate or obovate, compressed laterally.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. HK sheet 3045, 31231.
Distribution: Widely cultivated in subtropical and temperate regions of the world.
Ecology: Flowering: Feb.–Mar.; fruiting: Sep.– Oct.
Uses: Ornamental.
Note: A hybrid of Y. denudata × Y. liliiflora, it varies in the shape, size and colour of tepals. There are about 20 cultivars in cultivation.

Yulania denudata (Desr.) D. L. Fu 玉蘭（玉堂春）
J. Wuhan Bot. Res. 19(3): 198. 2001.
Magnolia denudata Desr., Lam. Encycl. Bot. 3: 675. 1791, excl. syn.; FGZ 88, fig. 22. 1956; FGD 1: 9. 1987; FRPS 30(1): 131. 1996.
Lassonia heptapeta Buc’hoz, Pl. Nouv. Decour. 21, t. 19, fig. 1. 1779, nom. rej. prop.
Magnolia heptapeta (Buc’hoz) Dandy, J. Bot. 72: 103. 1934.
Magnolia conspicua Salisb., Parad. Lond. 1: t. 38. 1806.
Magnolia yulan Desf., Hist. Arb. 2: 6. 1809.

Deciduous tree, up to 25 m tall; bark deep grey, rough and fissured; winter buds and peduncles densely covered with pale greyish yellow silky hairs. Stipular scars 1/4 –1/3 the length of petioles. Petioles 1–2.5 cm, villose, adaxially narrowly furrowed. Leaves obovate to obovate-elliptic, 10–15(–18) × 6–10(–12) cm, papery, gradually narrowed below middle, apex broadly rounded, truncate or slightly emarginate, adaxially deep green, villose when young, pilose on veins in age, abaxially pale green, villose along veins; lateral veins 8–10 on each side of midvein, reticulations of veins conspicuous. Flower appearing before leaves, erect, fragrant, 10–16 cm in diam.; peduncles conspicuously enlarged, densely pale yellow sericeous; tepals 9, white, usually pinkish at base, subequal, oblong-obovate, 6–8 (–10) × 2.5–4.5(–6.5) cm; stamens 7–12 mm, anthers 6–7 mm, dehiscing laterally, connectives ca. 5 mm wide, exserted and forming a mucro; gynoecium pale green, glabrous, cylindrical, 2–2.5 cm; pistils narrowly ovoid, 3–4 mm; style conical 4 mm. Aggregate fruit cylindrical, often curved due to some undeveloped carpels, 12–15 × 3.5–5 cm; follicles thickly woody, brown, white lenticeled; seeds heart-shaped, laterally compressed, ca. 9 × 10 mm; testa red, endotesta black.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. HK sheet 799.
Distribution: Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Hunan, Guizhou.
Ecology: Flowering: Feb.–Mar.; fruiting: Aug.–Sep.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal (folklore).

Yulania liliiflora (Desr.) D. L. Fu 紫玉蘭（辛夷）
J. Wuhan Bot. Res. 19(3): 198. 2001
Lassonia quinquepeta Buc’hoz, Pl. Nouv. Decouv. 21, t. 19, fig. 2. 1779, nom. rej. prop.
Magnolia liliiflora Desr. in Lam. Encycl. Bot. 3: 675. 1791, excl. syn. “Mokkwuren fl. albo” Kaempfer; FRPS 30(1): 140. 1996.
Magnolia quinquipeta (Buc’hoz) Dandy, J. Bot. 72: 103. 1934.

Deciduous shrub, up to 3 m tall; twigs greenish purple or pale purplish brown. Stipular scars about 1/2 the length of petioles. Petioles 0.8 –2 cm. Leaves elliptic-obovate or obovate, 8–18 × 3–10 cm, base gradually narrowed, decurrent along petioles to stipular scars,apex acute or acuminate, adaxially deep green, sparsely pubescent when young, abaxially greyish green, pubescent along veins; lateral veins 8–10 on each side of midvein. Flowers appearing at the same time with leaves, vase-shaped, erect, slightly fragrant; peduncles thick, hairy; tepals 9–12, outer 3 calyx-like, purplish green, lanceolate, 2–3.5 cm, caducous, the inner two whorls fleshy, adaxially whitish, abaxially purple or purplish red, petaloid, elliptic-obovate, 8–10 × 3–4.5 cm; stamens purplish red, 8–10 mm, anthers ca. 7 mm, dehiscing laterally, connectives exserted and forming a mucro; gynoecium ca. 1.5 cm, pale purple, glabrous. Aggregate fruit dark purplish brown, cylindrical, 7–10 cm; follicles subglobose when mature, apex short-beaked.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. HK sheet 35819.
Distribution: Fujian, Hubei, Sichuan, Yunnan.
Ecology: Flowering: Mar.–Apr.; Fruiting: Aug.–Sep.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Zoological & Botanical Gardens, The University of Hong Kong Tai Po, Tai Mo Shan, Kei Ling Ha Hoi, Sai Kung (cultivated)
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Annona squamosa L. 番荔枝
Sp. Pl. 1: 537. 1753; FGZ 84, fig. 24. 1956; FHN 1: 258. 1964; FRPS 30(2): 171, pl. 79. 1979; FGD 2: 39. 1991; FYN 5:61, fig. 18: 1 –8. 1991.

Small trees, to 4 m. Young branches pubescent. Petioles 9– 15 × ca. 1.5 mm. Leaf blades 9– 13.5 × 4 – 5 cm, oblong or ellipticoblong, glabrous or slightly pubescent both sides, base cuneate, apex obtuse or subacute; midvein impressed adaxially; secondary veins 6 – 8 pairs. Inflorescences leaf-opposed or terminal, 1–2(–4)-flowered. Flowers greenish (to yellow); pedicel 17.5–20.5 × ca. 0.8 mm, glabrous; bracts adnate to base or middle of pedicel. Sepals broadly ovate. Outer petals ca. 18 × 5 mm, narrowly oblong, reddish towards base adaxially; inner petals rudimentary, ca. 2 × 2.3 mm, triangular. Stamens numerous, ca. 1 mm long; connective capitate. Carpels numerous per flower; ovary glabrous; stigma glabrous. Fruits 8–10 cm in diam. when mature, ovate or globose, tuberculate, glaucous, pulp creamy-yellow, soft. Seeds blackish, shiny.

Locality: Hong Kong Zoological & Botanical Gardens, The University of Hong Kong Tai Po, Tai Mo Shan, Kei Ling Ha Hoi, Sai Kung (cultivated). C. L. Law & R. Kendrick 00/06 (HKU); HK sheet 1027.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan (cultivated). Widely cultivated in tropical areas.
Ecology: Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: Sep.–Nov.
Uses: Food (fruit).

Artabotrys hexapetalus (L. f.) Bhandari 鷹爪花
Baileya 12: 149. 1964; FRPS 30(2): 122, pl. 55. 1979; FGD 2: 31. 1991; FYN 5: 44. 1991.
Annona hexapetala L. f., Suppl. Pl. 270. 1782.
Artabotrys uncinatus (Lam.) Merr., Philipp. J. Sci., C. 7: 234. 1912; FHN 1: 238, fig. 115. 1964.
Artabotrys odoratissimus R. Br. in Edward, Bot. Reg. 5: fig. 423. 1819; FHK 10. 1861; FKH 30. 1912.

Scandent shrubs. Young branches glabrous. Leaves subleathery; petioles 4 – 6 × 1.2 – 1.9 mm, without transverse ribs; leaf blades ca. 9– 16 × 3 – 6 cm, oblong, lanceolate or narrowly elliptical, glabrous, base cuneate, apex short acuminate; midvein impressed or flush adaxially; secondary veins 9– 12( – 14) pairs. Inflorescences ± leaf-opposed, 1 – 2-flowered. Flowers pale green or yellow; pedicels ca. 12 × 2 – 4 mm. Sepals 4.5– 7 × 3.5 – 5 mm, triangular, basally connate, puberulous abaxially. Petals oblong or ovate-lanceolate, pubescent; outer petals ca. 22– 28 × 7 mm; inner petals 22–24 × 4– 6 mm. Stamens numerous, ca. 1.5 mm long; connective peltate and prominent. Carpels 11–20 per flower; stigma ovoid. Monocarps 3 – 5( – 7) per fruit, 2.5 – 4 × 2.5 cm, ovoid, apiculate, glabrous; pedicel ca. 2 cm long; stipes ca. 1 – 3.5 mm long. Seeds 1– 2 per monocarp, blackish-grey.

Locality: Cultivated. L. Chau s.n. (HKU); L. T. Lo 235; Y. S. Lau 3250.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan. Widely distributed in tropical Asia.
Ecology: Lowland areas. Flowering: May–Aug.; fruiting: Aug.–Feb.
Uses: Flowers used for perfumes in India, roots used medicinally.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Tam, Nam Fung Road, Lantau Peak
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Artabotrys hongkongensis Hance 香港鷹爪花
J. Bot. 8: 71. 1870; FKH 30. 1912; FHN 1: 239. 1964; FRPS 30(2): 125, fig. 56: 1–9. 1979; FGD 2: 31, fig. 25: 5–8. 1991; FYN 5: 45. 1991.
Artabotrys blumei Hook. f. & Thomson, Fl. Ind. 1: 128. 1855, p.p.; FHK 10. 1861.

Scandent shrubs. Young branches sparsely pubescent. Leaves sub-leathery; petioles 1.5–3(–4.5) × 1–1.4 mm, with transverse ribs; leaf blades ca. 6.5– 10 × 3 cm, oblong or obovate, glabrous, base cuneate to subrounded, apex acuminate; midvein flush or prominent adaxially; secondary veins 5– 7 pairs. Inflorescences leaf-opposed, 1-flowered. Flowers whitish to yellow; pedicels (6.5–)8 –13.5 × 0.5–0.8 mm. Sepals 3.5–5 × 3.5–4 mm, triangular, basally connate, pubescent abaxially. Petals oblong, pubescent abaxially; outer petals 6.5– 11(–13.5) × 2–6.5 mm; inner petals 8–12 × 2.5–6 mm, with strongly concave claw. Stamens numerous, ca. 1.7 mm long; connective peltate and prominent. Carpels 7–10 per flower; stigma clavate. Monocarps (1–)2 – 3(– 5) per fruit, 2–3.5 × 1.5–3 cm, ovoid, apiculate, glabrous; pedicel ca. 2 cm long; stipes ca. 3–3.5 mm long. Seeds 1–2 per monocarp, black.

Locality: Tai Tam, Nam Fung Road, Lantau Peak. C. L. Law et al. 00/12 (HKU); L. T. Lo 341; Y. S. Lau 2802.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Hunan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Lowland forests. Flowering: May–Aug.; fruiting: Aug.–Feb.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from “Buddhist Temple, East Point” (now Causeway Bay) by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1850. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Desmos chinensis Lour. 假鷹爪
Fl. Cochinch. 1: 352. 1790; FRPS 30(2): 50, pl. 18: 1–7. 1979; FGD 2: 17, fig. 12. 1991; FYN 5: 19, fig. 5: 11 – 12. 1991.
Unona discolor Vahl, Symb. Bot. 2: 63, pl. 36. 1791; FHK 11. 1861; FKH 30. 1912.
Desmos cochinchinensis auct. non Lour.: FGZ 85, fig. 25. 1956; FHN 1: 256, fig. 129. 1964.

Scandent or erect shrubs, to 2 m. Young branches slightly pubescent. Petioles 2.5– 6 × 1–1.7 mm; leaf blades 8.5–13 × 3–4 cm, oblong or lanceolate, pubescent initially and then glabrous, glaucous abaxially, glossy adaxially, base cuneate, subrounded or subcordate and oblique, apex acuminate; midvein impressed adaxially; secondary veins 8 – 11 pairs. Inflorescences supra-axillary or leaf-opposed, 1-flowered. Flowers greenish (to yellow); pedicels 33– 37 × ca. 0.6 mm; bracts adnate to base or middle of pedicel, 2.5– 3.5 × ca. 1 mm, oblong. Sepals 4.5– 6.5 × 2.5 – 4 mm, triangular or oblong. Petals oblong or narrowly lanceolate; outer petals slightly larger than inner, 48 – 67 × 12–21 mm; inner petals 38–66 × 9 –20 mm. Stamens 150–200 per flower; connective discoid. Carpels 25 – 35 per flower; ovary hairy; ovules lateral; stigma clavate with U-shape groove. Monocarps 11 –20(–25) per fruit, moniliform, slightly apiculate. Seeds 1 – 5(– 8) per monocarp, 1-seriate, 5.5 – 6.5 mm in diam., globose, brown, smooth.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. C. L. Law & R. Kendrick 00/04 (HKU), Y. W. Lam 248; H. C. Tang 86.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan; Vietnam, Laos, Philippines, India, Sri Lanka, Malaysia, Indonesia.
Ecology: Very common on sunny slopes and roadsides. Flowering: Mar.–Jul.; fruiting: Oct.–Jan.
Uses: Medicinal.

Fissistigma glaucescens (Hance) Merr. 白葉瓜馥木
Philip. J. Sci. 15(2): 132. 1919; FHN 1: 251. 1964; FRPS 30(2): 136, pl. 60. 1979; FGD 2: 33. 1991; FTW ed. 2, 2: 415. 1996.
Melodorum glaucescens Hance, J. Bot. 19: 112. 1881; FKH 30. 1912.

Scandent shrubs. Young branches glabrous. Leaves sub-leathery; petioles 4–7 × ca. 2 mm; leaf blades 10–12 × ca. 2 cm, (obovate-) oblong or elliptic, glabrous adaxially, sparsely pubescent with simple hairs abaxially and glaucous when dry, base cuneate or subrounded, apex acute, obtuse or retuse; secondary veins 10–12 pairs; tertiary veins indistinct. Inflorescences terminal or axillary, (1–)6–10- flowered. Flowers light yellow; pedicels 4.5–7 × ca. 0.6 mm; bracts adnate to base or middle of pedicel, ca. 0.6 × 0.4 mm, ovate. Sepals 2–4.5 mm, triangular. Petals triangular; outer petals ca. 3.5–6 × 2–5 mm, pubescent both sides; inner petals ca. 5 × 4 mm, pubescent abaxially. Stamens numerous, ca. 1.5 mm long; connective pyramidal. Carpels ca. 15 per flower; ovary pubescent; stigma 2-cleft, glabrous. Monocarps few per fruit, 5.5–8.5 mm long, globose, glabrous; stipes ca. 2 mm long. Seeds 1–2 per monocarp, globose, pale yellow.

Locality: Happy Valley, Wu Kau Tang. C. L. Law & R. Kendrick 00/07b (HKU); HK sheet 107.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Lowland forest. Flowering and fruiting: Spring to autumn.
Notes: The type specimen (C. Ford s.n. in Herb. Hance No. 21141, BM) was collected from Victoria Peak, Hong Kong Island in August, 1879.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Mount Parker, Shek O, Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai, Shek Pik Reservoir
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Fissistigma oldhamii (Hemsl.) Merr. 瓜馥木
Philip. J. Sci. 15(2): 134. 1919; FHN 1: 250. 1964; FRPS 30(2): 162, pl. 57: 1–9. 1979; FGD 2: 36, fig. 26. 1991; FTW ed. 2, 2: 416, pl. 193. 1996.
Melodorum oldhamii Hemsl., J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 23: 27. 1886; FKH 30. 1912 (as M. oldhami).

Scandent shrubs. Young branches pubescent. Leaves leathery; petioles ca. 5 × 1.1–1.4 mm; leaf blades 7–12(–16.5) × 2.5–3.5 cm, oblong to elliptical, densely pubescent with simple hairs abaxially, glabrous adaxially, base cuneate to subrounded, apex acute to obtuse; secondary veins 13–15 pairs; tertiary veins distinct. Inflorescences terminal or leaf-opposed, 1–3-flowered. Flowers light yellow; pedicels 8.5–12(–20) × 1 mm; bracts towards middle of pedicel, 3–5 × 2–3.5 mm, oblong. Sepals 4.5–7.5 × 4–4.5 mm, ovate-triangular. Petals broad triangular; outer petals 12.5–16.5 × 5.5–7 mm, glabrous or hairy both sides; inner petals slightly smaller and more slender, glabrous. Stamens numerous, ca. 2 mm long; connective pyramidal. Carpels numerous per flower; ovary pubescent; stigma 2-cleft, glabrous. Monocarps 25–30 per fruit, ca. 18 mm long, globose, pubescent; stipes 2–2.5 cm long. Seeds ca. 10 per monocarp, broadly ellipsoid or lenticular, brown.

Locality: Mount Parker, Shek O, Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai, Shek Pik Reservoir. C. L. Law & R. Kendrick 00/03 (HKU); N. H. Li 32; Y. S. Lau 2125.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Mar.–Apr.; fruiting: Summer to autumn.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Wong Nai Chung, Tai Tam, Tai Po Kau, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Fissistigma uonicum (Dunn) Merr. 香港瓜馥木
Philip. J. Sci. 15(2): 137. 1919; FHN 1: 251. 1964; FRPS 30(2): 136, pl. 61. 1979; FGD 2: 34. 1991.
Melodorum uonicum Dunn, J. Bot. 48: 323. 1910; FKH 30. 1912.

Scandent shrubs. Young branches pubescent. Leaves papery; petioles 6–10 × 1.3–1.9 mm; leaf blades 7.5–14.5 × 2–3.5 cm, oblong, sparsely pubescent with simple hairs abaxially, glabrous adaxially, base cuneate to subrounded, apex obtuse to acute; secondary veins 14 – 16 pairs; tertiary veins indistinct. Inflorescences axillary, 1–2-flowered. Flowers yellow; pedicel ca. 6 × 2 mm; bracts near base of pedicel, small, oblong or ovate. Sepals ca. 2.5 × 2 mm, ovate-triangular. Petals ovate; outer petals ca. 24 × 13 mm, glabrous both sides; inner petals slightly smaller, glabrous. Stamens numerous, 1– 2 mm long; connective liguliform. Carpels few per flower; ovary pubescent; stigma clavate, glabrous. Monocarps 3 – 7 per fruit, 30 – 40 × 20 – 26 mm, ovoid, glabrous to pubescent; stipes ca. 4 mm long. Seeds 2– 3( – 11) per monocarp, flattened-ovoid, deep brown.

Locality: Wong Nai Chung, Tai Tam, Tai Po Kau, Lantau Island. C. L. Law & R. Kendrick 00/05 (HKU); HK sheet 1036, 34483.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Fuji an.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Apr.; fruiting: Autumn.
Notes: The type specimen was collected by W. J. Tutcher from Hong Kong Island in 1893.

Popowia pisocarpa (Blume) Endl. 嘉陵花
Walpers, Repert. Bot. Syst. 1: 74. 1842; FHN 1: 249, fig. 122. 1964; FRPS 30(2): 108, pl. 48. 1979; FGD 2: 27, fig. 21. 1991.
Guatteria pisocarpa Blume, Bijdr. 21. 1825.

Shrubs, to ca. 1 m. Young branches rufous-pubescent. Leaves membranous; petioles 3– 4 × ca. 1.5 mm, sparsely pubescent; leaf blades 9 – 11 × ca. 4 cm, elliptic, oblong or obovate, glabrous except sparsely pubescent veins adaxially, base cuneate, apex acute; midvein impressed adaxially; secondary veins 6 – 9 pairs. Inflorescences supra-axillary or leaf-opposed, 1 – 2( – 4)-flowered. Flowers white; pedicels ca. 6.5 –7.5 mm long, slender; bracts ca. 1 mm long, pubescent. Sepals 1.5 –2 × 1.5 –2.5 mm, triangular-ovate, pubescent abaxially, glabrous adaxially, persistent. Outer petals ca. 2 × 1.5–2 mm; inner petals ca. 3 × 2.7–4 mm. Stamens 15 – 18 per flower, ca. 1 mm long; connective truncate or slightly concave. Carpels 3 – 6 per flower; ovary pubescent; ovule 1, basal; style very short; stigma subcapitate. Monocarps 3 – 5 per fruit, ca. 6 × 5.5 mm, flattened-globose, glabrous; stipes 3 – 3.5 mm. Seeds ca. 5.5 mm in diam., globose, brown; raphes ribbed.

Locality: Lam Tsuen Valley. C. L. Law et al. 00/09 (HKU); Y. W. Lam 200, 446.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong; Vietnam, Thailand, Myanmar, Malaysia, Indonesia, Philippines.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Mar.; fruiting: Nov.–Dec.
Notes: Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Po Kau, Ma On Shan
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Uvaria boniana Finet & Gagnep. 光葉紫玉盤
Bull. Soc. Bot. France Mem. 4: 71, pl. 11A. 1906; FHN 1: 237. 1964; FGD 2: 9, fig. 5. 1991.

Scandent shrubs. Young branches stellate-pubescent. Leaves papery; petioles 5–7 × 1.3–1.7 mm, pubescent or glabrous; leaf blades 13.5–15 × 3.5–5 cm, elliptic to oblong, glabrous ab- and adaxially, base cuneate to subrounded, apex acuminate; secondary veins 10–13 pairs. Inflorescences leaf-opposed or extra-axillary, 1–2-flowered. Flowers purplish-red to pink, ca. 2.5 cm in diam.; pedicels ca. 22 × 0.9 mm, glabrous; bracts near base, ca. 1 mm long, oblong to ovate, pubescent. Sepals ca. 2.5–3 mm long, subrounded, basally connate, pubescent abaxially. Petals broad ovate, apically pubescent both sides; outer petals ca. 10 × 5.5–7.5 mm; inner petals slightly smaller. Stamens numerous, ca. 1 mm long; connective truncate, papillate. Carpels ca. 20 per flower; ovary oblong, densely hairy; stigma 2-cleft and incurved. Monocarps 10–20 per fruit, 1.5–4 × ca. 1.5 cm, ovoid or cylindrical, rarely globose, glabrous; stipes 4–5.5 cm long, glabrous. Seeds 1–8 per monocarp, ca. 10 × 7–10 mm, ellipsoid to lenticular, blackish brown.

Locality: Tai Po Kau, Ma On Shan. Y. W. Lam 182; F. W. Xing 6887.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Jiangxi; Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Mar–Apr.; fruiting: Autumn.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Aberdeen, Lady Clementi's Ride, Wong Chuk Hang, Tai Mo Shan
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Uvaria calamistrata Hance 刺果紫玉盤
J. Bot. 20: 77. 1882; FKH 29. 1912; FHN 1: 235. 1964; FRPS 30(2): 20, pl. 7. 1979; FGD 2: 10, fig. 6. 1991.

Scandent shrubs. Young branches stellate-pubescent. Leaves leathery; petioles 5.5–7.5 × 1.5–1.9 mm, pubescent; leaf blades 8.5–13.5 × 3.5–5.5 cm, ovate, obovate or elliptic, densely pubescent with short stellate hairs abaxially, glabrous adaxially, base cuneate or rounded, apex acuminate or acute; secondary veins 8– 12 pairs. Inflorescences leaf-opposed or axillary, 1– 4-flowered. Flowers pale yellow, ca. 1.8 cm diam.; pedicels ca. 6 × 4 mm, pubescent; bracts near base, ca. 5.5 × 4 mm, broad ovate, pubescent. Sepals ca. 5 × 4.5 mm, ovate, free, pubescent both sides. Petals oblong, pubescent both sides; outer petals 6–8 × 2.5–3.5 mm; inner petals subequal or slightly smaller. Stamens numerous, ca. 3 mm long; connective liguliform, slightly pubescent. Carpels 7–15 per flower; ovary cylindrical, hairy; stigma 2-cleft and incurved. Monocarps 1–3 per fruit, 2.7– 3 × 2–2.2 cm, ovate, rounded at apex, spiny; stipes 5.5–6.5 mm long, pubescent. Seeds ca. 6 per monocarp, ca. 12.5 × 9.5 mm, lenticular or discoid, brown.

Locality: Aberdeen, Lady Clementi's Ride, Wong Chuk Hang, Tai Mo Shan. Y. W. Lam 1477; P. S. Choi 103; Y. S. Lau 1203.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi; Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: Aug.–Nov.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Pokfulam, Victoria Peak, Lady Clementi's Ride, Aberdeen, Shatin, Tai Po Kau, Tai Mo Shan, Shing Mun
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Uvaria grandiflora Roxb. ex Hornem. 大花紫玉盤
Suppl. Hort. Bot. Hafn. 140. 1819; FRPS 30(2): 26, pl. 10. 1979; FGD 2: 11, fig. 8. 1991.
Uvaria purpurea Blume, Bijdr. 11. 1825; FHK 9. 1861; FKH 29. 1912; FHN 1: 235. 1964.
Uvaria platypetala Champ. ex Bentham, Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 3: 257. 1851.
Uvaria rhodantha Hance ex Walp., Ann. Bot. Syst. 2: 19. 1851.
Uvaria hamiltonii auct. non Hook. f. & Thomson: FKH 29. 1912.

Scandent shrubs. Young branches densely stellate-tomentose. Leaves papery or sub-leathery; petioles 6.5 –10 × ca. 1.7 mm, densely pubescent; leaf blades 15–23 × 7.5–9.5 cm, obovate or obovate-oblong, densely villous with long stellate hairs abaxially, sparsely pubescent adaxially, base truncate or shallowly cordate, apex acuminate; secondary veins 10– 14 pairs. Inflorescences leaf-opposed or terminal, 1(–3)-flowered. Flowers red, ca. 10 cm in diam.; pedicels 9.5 – 11.5 × 2.3–3.2 mm, tomentose; bracts ca. 3 × 2.5 cm, obovate, tomentose. Sepals 15 –25 × 15– 5 mm, broadly triangular, basally connate, tomentose abaxially, glabrous adaxially. Petals obovate or oblong, densely tomentose abaxially, sparsely tomentose adaxially; outer petals 24 –34 × 13–21 mm; inner petals 22–29 × 11–13 mm. Stamens ca. 250 per flower, ca. 7 mm long; connective liguliform, glabrous. Carpels numerous per flower; ovary cylindrical, hairy; stigma cylindrical, 2-cleft and incurved. Monocarps 15–20 per fruit, 2.9 –6.2 × 0.8 –1.5 cm, cylindrical, densely tomentose, slightly tuberculate; stipes ca. 1.5 cm long, tomentose. Seeds few to many, flat, pale brown.

Locality: Pokfulam, Victoria Peak, Lady Clementi's Ride, Aberdeen, Shatin, Tai Po Kau, Tai Mo Shan, Shing Mun. P. S. Choi 374; Y. S. Lau 3108.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi. Widely distributed in tropical Asia.
Ecology: Shrublands and forests. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.; fruiting: Jul.–Sep.

Uvaria macrophylla Roxb. 紫玉盤
Fl. Ind. 2: 663. 1824.
Uvaria microcarpa Champ. ex Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 3: 256. 1851; FHK 10. 1861; FKH 29. 1912; FRPS 30(2): 22, pl. 8: 1–8. 1979; FGD 2: 11, fig. 7: 1–8. 1991; FYN 5: 8, fig. 2: 1–8. 1991.
Uvaria macrophylla Roxb. var. microcarpa (Champ. ex Benth.) Finet & Gagnep., Bull. Soc. Bot. France 53, Mém. 4: 67. 1906; Finet & Gagnep., in Fl. Indo-Chine 1: 51. 1907.
Uvaria obovatifolia Hayata, Icon. Pl. Forms. 3: 11. 1913; FKH 29. 1912.
Uvaria synsepala Miq., J. Bot. Neerl. 1: 128. 1861; FKH 29. 1912.

Scandent shrubs. Young branches stellate-pubescent. Leaves leathery; petioles 3.5–7.5 × 2–2.5 mm, pubescent; leaf blades 14–16.5 × 5–8 cm, elliptic or obovate, sparsely pubescent with short stellate hairs abaxially, glabrous adaxially, base subcordate or rounded, apex obtuse or acute; secondary veins 11–13 pairs. Inflorescences terminal or leaf-opposed, 1–2-flowered. Flowers red, 2.5 – 3.5 cm in diam.; pedicels 7–14.5 × 1.3–2 mm, pubescent; bracts basal, 1.5– 3 × 2 mm, oblong, pubescent. Sepals ca. 5 × 10 mm, broad ovate, basally connate, hairy abaxially. Petals ovate, pubescent; outer petals 8.5 – 14 × 7 –8.5 mm; inner petals 9– 11 × 7–9 mm. Stamens ca. 120 per flower, 5.5– 8 mm long; connective liguliform, glabrous. Carpels ca. 40 per flower; ovary cylindrical, hairy; stigma subcapitate, 2-cleft and incurved. Monocarps 22 – 30 per fruit, 1.1 –1.8 × ca. 1 cm, globose or ovate, sparsely pubescent; stipes 0.9–1.5 cm, densely pubescent. Seeds 1–3 per monocarp, ca. 7.5 × 3.3 –4.5 mm, lenticular or discoid, brown.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. C. L. Law & R. Kendrick 00/01 (HKU); S. T. Chan s.n. (HKU); P. S. Choi 360; HK sheet 931, 940.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; Laos, Vietnam.
Ecology: Shrublands and forests. Flowering. May–Jun.; fruiting: Autumn–Dec.

Chimonanthus praecox (L.) Link. 臘梅
Enum. Pl. Hort. Berol. 2: 66. 1822; FRPS 30(2): 7. 1979; P.T. Li & Z. Q. Li, Higher Pl. China 3: 204. 2000.
Calycanthus praecox L., Sp. Pl. ed. 2, 718. 1762.

Shrub to 3 m tall, almost evergreen in Hong Kong; buds with imbricate scales. Leaves opposite; petioles ca. 5 mm; leaf blade papery to sub-leathery, elliptic-ovate to ovate-lanceolate, 5 –25 × 2– 8 cm, base rounded or cuneate, apex acute to acuminate, glabrous except the puberulent veins on abaxial surface. Flowers solitary on branches of the previous year's growth, fragrant, 2– 4 cm in diam., the outer tepals yellow, elliptic to oblong; the inner ones shorter, base clawed and striped purple brown. Fruit (enlarged receptacle) urn-shaped, 2–5 × 1–2.5 cm.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens.
Distribution: Fujian, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Jiangsu, Shandong, Anhui, Henan, Shaanxi, Hubei, Hunan, Guizhou, Sichuan, Yunnan.
Ecology: Flowering: Nov. to Mar. of the following year; fruiting: Apr.–Jun.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: The species is deciduous in N China, flowering before the leaves appear, but in Hong Kong it is almost evergreen.

Beilschmiedia fordii Dunn 廣東瓊楠
J. Bot. 45: 404. 1907; FKH 222. 1912; FRPS 31: 142, pl. 37: 1. 1982.

Tree, 6–18 m tall. Terminal buds ovate-lanceolate, glabrous. Branchlets angular, glabrous. Leaves leathery, alternate or opposite; petioles glabrous, 1–2 cm, leaf blade lanceolate, oblong-elliptic to broadly elliptic, 7–13 × 2.5–4.6 cm, base cuneate to broadly cuneate, apex shortly acuminate or obtuse, glabrous, adaxially dark green, abaxially paler, turning brown when dry; midvein impressed adaxially, raised abaxially; lateral veins slender, 6–9 on each side of midvein. Cymose panicles usually axillary, 1–3 cm, densely flowered. Pedicels 3–5 mm. Perianth-lobes yellowish green, ovate to oblong, 1.5–2 mm, glabrous. Fruit ellipsoid, 1.4–1.8 cm, rounded on both ends, usually warty.

Locality: Happy Valley. HK sheet 4746, 4754.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi; Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests in valleys. Flowering: Jun.–Dec.; fruiting: Dec.–Jun. of the following year.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Happy Valley, Hong Kong Island by C. Ford in August 1881.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Authority: N. H. Xia, F. N. Wei & Y. F. Deng
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Mount Gough, Mount Cameron, Bowen Road, Mount Parker, Tai Tam, Severn Road, Deep Water Bay Road, Ng Tung Chai, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Beilschmiedia glandulosa N. H. Xia, F. N. Wei & Y. F. Deng 腺葉瓊楠
J. Trop. & Subtrop. Bot. 14(1): 78, fig. 1. 2006.
Beilschmiedia fagifolia auct. non Nees: Dunn & Tutch., FKH 222. 1912.

Tree; branchlets greyish brown, pubescent, glabrescent, terminal buds pubescent. Leaves subopposite, leathery, elliptic, narrowly elliptic to oblanceolate, 4.5 – 8.5 × 1.5 –3.5 cm, base attenuate, apex obtuse, margin entire, glabrous, brownish abaxially when dry, densely glandular spotted adaxially; main veins elevated on both surfaces, lateral veins 5 –7 pairs, together with tertiary veins prominent on both surfaces. Petioles 5–8 mm. Inflorescences axillary, racemose or thyrsoid, 1–3 clustered, 1.5 –3 cm, shortly pedunculate. Bracteoles ovate, ca. 1 × 0.6 mm, pilose. Pedicels 2– 4 mm. Flowers ca. 4 × 4 mm, perianth-tube short. Perianthlobes 6, rarely 7– 8, ovate, ca. 2.5 mm, pilose inside, sparsely villose outside. Fertile stamens 9 in 3 whorls, 6 of outer two whorls opposite to perianth-lobes, filaments 1 mm, densely pilose, anthers ca. 0.8 mm, 2-celled, cells introrse, each of the third whorl stamens with a pair of short-stalked orbicular-reniform glands near the base of filaments, filaments ca. 0.5 mm, densely villose, anthers ca. 0.5 mm, 2-celled, cells extrorse. Staminodes 3 of the innermost whorl, ca. 0.8 mm, ovoid. Ovary cylindrical, ca. 2.5 mm, sparsely villose, style ca. 1 mm, stigma capitate. Fruit ellipsoid, apiculate, bluish black when maturing, 1.5–2.2 x 1–1.5 cm, smooth, wrinkled when dry. Seeds 1.3 –2 x 0.8 –1.2 cm.

Locality: Mount Gough, Mount Cameron, Bowen Road, Mount Parker, Tai Tam, Severn Road, Deep Water Bay Road, Ng Tung Chai, Lantau Island. HK sheet 34208; Y.S. Lau 440; K. L. Yip 4197.
Distribution: Endemic to Hong Kong.
Ecology: Thin forests on slopes. Flowering: Summer; fruiting: Jul.–Dec.
Notes: The species was reported as B. tsangii Merr. previously (Check List HK Plants 42. 2002). The type specimen (F. Yip s.n., HK sheet 34327) was collected from Tai Tam, Hong Kong Island in August 1982.

Cassytha filiformis L. 無根藤
Sp. Pl. 1: 35. 1753; FHK 294. 1861; FHN 1: 301, fig. 147. 1964; FRPS 31: 463, pl. 124. 1982; FTW ed. 2, 2: 437, pl. 203. 1996.

Stems filiform or wiry, pale green to yellow-green, glabrous or slightly pubescent when young, twining round and attaching to other plants by means of small suckers. Leaves reduced to tiny scales, alternate, ca. 1 mm. Inflorescences spicate, 2–5 cm, rarely reduced to single flower, densely rusty pubescent; bract and bracteoles broad ovate, small, ca. 1 mm, brown, ciliate. Flowers white, less than 2 mm, sessile; perianth-lobes 6 in 2 whorls, the outer 3 much smaller than the inner ones. Stamens 9; filaments of the outer stamens broad and petal-like, of the other 6 filiform; anthers all fertile. Fruit drupaceous, ovoid, enclosed in the succulent tube of the perianth and crowned by the persistent connivent perianth-lobes, to 4 mm in diam.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. P. S. Choi 172; Y. S. Lau 2307.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; tropical Asia, Africa, and Australia.
Ecology: Thin forests and thickets on slopes. Flowering and fruiting: May–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Tam, Tai Mo Shan, Shing Mun, Ma On Shan, Sunset Peak
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Cinnamomum appelianum Schewe 毛桂
Sitzungsber. Kaiserl. Akad. Wiss., Math.-Naturwiss. Cl., Abt. 1. 61: 20. 1925; FRPS 31: 222, pl. 60: 1–5. 1982.
Cinnamomum taimoshanicum Chun ex H. T. Chang, Acta Sci. Nat. Univ. Sunyatseni 1959(1): 21. 1959.
Cinnamomum villosulum S. Lee & F. N. Wei, Guihaia 8(4): 301, fig. 1. 1988.

Small tree, 4–6 m tall; branchlets subopposite, densely tawny hirsute-tomentose when young. Leaves alternate or subopposite; petioles thick, 4–5(–9) cm, tawny hirsute-tomentose; leaf blade leathery, elliptic, elliptic-lanceolate, ovate or ovate-elliptic, 4.5 –11.5 × 1.5–4 cm, base cuneate to subrounded, apex abruptly and shortly acuminate, adaxially tawny pubescent on veins, glabrous in age, abaxially densely tawny pubescent, triplinerved; midvein and lateral veins impressed adaxially, raised abaxially. Panicles or cymes 4 – 6.5 cm, densely tawny pubescent, usually shorter than the substanding leaves, (3 –)5 –7(–11)-flowered. Peduncles slender, 1–1.5(–3.5) cm. Pedicels 2–3 mm. Flowers white, 3 –5 mm; perianth tube obconical, 1–1.5 mm; lobes broadly obovate to oblong-ovate, 3 –3.5 × 2 mm, acute, silky puberulent on both surfaces. Stamens 9; filaments pilose. Immature fruit ellipsoid.

Locality: Tai Tam, Tai Mo Shan, Shing Mun, Ma On Shan, Sunset Peak. HK sheet 36068; Y. W. Lam 89.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi.
Ecology: Woods in ravines. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.; fruiting: Jun.–Aug.
Notes: The type specimen of C. taimoshanicum Chun ex H. T. Chang was collected from Tai Mo Shan by N. K. Chun.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Common in Hong Kong. Also cultivated
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Cinnamomum burmannii (C. G. & T. Nees) Blume 陰香
Bijdr. 569. 1826; FHK 223. 1912; FHN 1: 264. 1964; FRPS 31: 202, pl. 52: 1– 6. 1982.
Laurus burmannii C. G. & T. Nees, Disput. Cinn. 57, t. 4. 1823.
Cinnamomum dulce Nees in Wall. Pl. Asiat. Rar. 2: 75. 1831; FHK 290. 1861.

Tree, up to 14 m tall, all parts strongly camphor-scented. Leaves alternate or subopposite; petioles slender, 0.5–1.2 cm, subglabrous; leaf blade leathery, ovate, oblong to lanceolate, 5.5–10.5 × 2–5 cm, base broadly cuneate, apex shortly acuminate, margin entire, glabrous, green and shining adaxially, ± glaucous abaxially, triplinerved; midvein and lateral veins plane adaxially, raised abaxially. Panicles or cymes axillary or subterminal, 2–6 cm, ± greyish puberulent. Pedicels slender, 4–6 mm. Flowers greenish white, ca. 5 mm; perianth densely greyish puberulent on both surfaces; tube very short; lobes oblong-ovate. Stamens 9, filaments puberulent. Fruit ovoid, 8 × 5 mm, purplish black when mature.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Also cultivated. L. T. Lo 9; Y. S. Lau 2102.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Myanmar, Vietnam, Indonesia and Philippines.
Ecology: Mixed forests on hillslope or by streams. Flowering: Mar.–Apr.; fruiting: Oct.–Nov.
Uses: Additive (flavouring).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Common in Hong Kong. Also widely cultivated
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Cinnamomum camphora (L.) J. Presl 樟
Prir. Rostlin 2: 36 et 47–56, t. 8. 1825; FHK 223. 1912; FHN 1: 262. 1964; FRPS 31: 182, pl. 43: 1–3. 1982; FTW ed. 2, 2: 440, 1996.
Laurus camphora L., Sp. Pl. 369. 1753.

Tree, up to 30 m tall, all parts strongly camphor-scented. Leaves alternate; petioles slender, 2–3 cm, glabrous; leaf blade ovateelliptic, 6 –12 × 2.5 –5.5 cm, base broadly cuneate to rounded, apex acute, margin entire, subleathery, glabrous or sparsely puberulent abaxially when young, triplinerved, with domatia in axils of secondary and tertiary veins. Panicles or cymes axillary, 3.5–7 cm; peduncles 2.5 – 4.5 cm, glabrous or puberulent, especially on the nodes. Pedicels 1–2 mm, glabrous. Flowers yellowish white, ca. 3 mm; perianthtube obconical, ca. 1 mm; lobes elliptic, white or yellowish, ca. 2 mm. Stamens 9, filaments pubescent. Fruit ovoid or subglobose, 6 – 8 mm in diam., purplish black when mature.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Also widely cultivated. H. C. Tang 2354; Y. S. Lau 92.
Distribution: Widely distributed in South to Southwest China; Vietnam, Korea, Japan.
Ecology: In woods near villages. Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: Aug.–Nov.
Uses: Materials (essential oils, wood), medicinal (source of camphor), ornamental.

Cinnamomum aromaticum Nees 肉桂
Wall. Pl. Asiat. Rar. 2: 74. 1831.
Cinnamomum cassia Presl, Prir. Rostlin 2: 36 & 44 – 45, fig. 6 (sinister). 1825; FHK 223. 1912; FHN 1: 263. 1964; FRPS 31: 223, pl. 59: 1–5. 1982.

Tree, all parts strongly camphor-scented; branchlets dark brown, ± tetragonous, puberulent. Leaves alternate or subopposite; petioles thick, 1.2–2 cm, greyish yellow puberulent; leaf blade thick-leathery, oblong-elliptic to sublanceolate, 8 –16(–34) × 4 –5.5(–9.5) cm, base acute, apex slightly acute, tip blunt, margin cartilaginous, slightly involute, glabrous, green and shining adaxially, pale and sparsely yellowish puberulent abaxially when young, triplinerved; midvein and lateral veins prominently impresed on adaxial surface, strongly raised on abaxial surface. Panicles axillary, 8 –16 cm, many-flowered, densely tawny tomentulose. Pedicels 3 – 6 mm, glabrous. Flowers white; perianth densely tawny tomentulose on both surfaces; tube obconical, ca. 2 mm; lobes ovate-oblong, ca. 2.5 mm. Stamens 9, filaments pubescent. Fruit ellipsoid, 10 × 7–9 mm, purplish black when mature.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. P. S. Choi 411; L. T. Lo 616.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan. Also cultivated in India, Laos, Vietnam, Malaysia and Indonesia.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: Aug.–Nov.
Uses: Additive (flavouring), material (essential oils), medicinal (folklore).

Cinnamomum jensenianum Hand.-Mazz. 野黃桂
Sitzungsber. Kaiserl. Akad. Wiss., Math.-Naturwiss. Cl., Abt. 1. 58: 63. 1921; FRPS 31: 194, pl. 49: 8 –14. 1982.
Cinnamomum pauciflorum H. T. Chang, Acta Sci. Nat. Univ. Sunyatseni 1959(1): 21. 1959.
Cinnamomum pedunculatum auct. non Nees: Dunn & Tutch. FKH 223. 1912.

Small tree, to 6 m tall, all parts strongly camphor-scented. Leaves subopposite, thick-leathery; petioles slender, 2–3 cm, glabrous; leaf blade lanceolate or oblong-lanceolate, 5 –10(–20) × 1.5 –3(–6) cm, base broadly cuneate to subrounded, apex caudate-acuminate, margin thickened and entire, together with main veins yellowish, adaxial surface glabrous, green and shining, abaxial surface pulverulent when young, glabrous when aged; triplinerved, main veins and lateral veins raise on both surfaces. Cymes 2–5-flowered. Peduncles slender, usually 1.5 –2.5 cm, subglabrous. Pedicels 5–10(–20) mm, erect, gradually thickened upwards. Flowers yellowish or white; perianth tube short, ca. 1.5 mm; lobes obovate, subequal, 2–5(– 6) × 1.75(–2.2) mm, acute, abaxially glabrous, adaxially sericeous. Stamens 9, filaments pilose. Fruit ovoid, up to 1(–1.2) × 0.6(–0.7) mm, apiculate, glabrous.

Locality: Wong Lung Hang. Y. W. Lam 616.
Distribution: Guangdong, W Hunan, Hubei, Sichuan, Jiangxi, Fujian.
Ecology: Thin forests in valleys. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.; fruiting: Jul.–Aug.

Cinnamomum parthenoxylon (Jack) Meisn. 黃樟
Prodr. 15(1): 26. 1864; FHK 223. 1912; FHN 1: 261. 196; FRPS 31: 186, pl. 46: 1–6. 1982, pro syn. sub C. porrectum (Roxb.) Kosterm.
Laurus parthenoxylon Jack, Malayan Miscellanies 1: 28. 1820.
Camphora parthenoxylon Nees in Wall. Pl. Asiat. Rar. 2: 72. 1831; FHK 290. 1861.

Tree, 10–20 m tall, all parts strongly camphor-scented. Leaves alternate; petioles 1.5–3.5 cm, glabrous; leaf blade elliptic-ovate or long elliptic-ovate, leathery, 6–12 × 3–6 cm, much smaller on the flowering branchlets, base cuneate to broadly cuneate, apex usually acute or shortly acuminate, margin entire, dark green and shining adaxially, pale green or glaucous abaxially, glabrous on both surfaces, pinnately veined; lateral veins 4–5 on each side of midvein; domatia in axils of lateral veins inconspicuous. Panicles or cymes axillary on the upper part of twigs or subterminal, 4.5–8 cm, 5–10-flowered, glabrous. Peduncles 3–5.5 cm. Pedicels slender, up to 4 mm. Perianth-tube obconical, ca. 1 mm; lobes narrowly elliptic, ca. 2 × 1.2 mm, greenish yellow, puberulous adaxially. Stamens 9, filaments pubescent. Fruit globose, 6–8 mm in diam., black when mature.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 699; S. T. Dunn s.n. (HK sheet 4791).
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian; Pakistan, India, Indochina, Malaysia to Indonesia.
Ecology: Evergreen broadleaved forests. Flowering: Mar.– May; fruiting: Apr.– Oct.
Uses: Materials (essential oils).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Mount Parker, Jardine's Lookout, Ma On Shan, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Cinnamomum validinerve Hance 粗脈桂
J. Bot. 20: 80. 1822; FKH 223. 1912; FRPS 31: 198. 1982.

Small tree, all parts strongly camphor-scented; branchlets angular, glabrous or minutely tomentulose near apex. Leaves alternate; petioles 0.8 –1.3 cm, glabrous; leaf blade thick-leathery, elliptic, 4–9.5 × 2–3.5 cm, base cuneate, apex abruptly and shortly acuminate, tip blunt, dark green and shining adaxially, paler and reddish abaxially, triplinerved; midvein and lateral veins slightly impressed adaxially and strongly raised abaxially, transversal veins inconspicuous. Panicles about the length of the substanding leaves, cymosely branching, the utmost branch 3-flowered. Pedicels very short, greyish white sericeous. Perianth-lobes ovate, apex obtuse. Fruit unknown.

Locality: Mount Parker, Jardine's Lookout, Ma On Shan, Lantau Island. P. S. Choi 118; HK sheet 4804.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi.
Ecology: Thin forest. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.
Notes: The type specimen (Herb. Hance No. 21045, BM) was collected in the valley of Wong Nai Chung, Hong Kong Island by C. Ford in June 1879.

Cryptocarya chinensis (Hance) Hemsl. 厚殼桂
J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 26: 370. 1891; FKH 222. 1912; FHN 1: 282. 1964; FRPS 31: 443, pl. 116: 9–10. 1982; FTW ed. 2, 2: 449, pl. 207. 1996.
Beilschmiedia chinensis Hance, J. Bot. 20: 79. 1882.

Tree, up to 20 m tall. Branchlets terete, finely and longitudinally striated, initially tawny tomentose, glabrescent. Leaves leathery, alternate or opposite; petioles 1 cm long. Leaf blade long elliptic, 7–11 × 3.5 –5.5 cm, base broad cuneate, apex acuminate, adaxially green and shining, abaxially glaucous, initially tawny tomentose on both surfaces, glabrescent, triplinerved; midvein impressed adaxially, raised abaxially; lateral veins 3 – 4 on each side of midvein. Panicles axillary or terminal, 1.5 – 4 cm, tawny tomentellate. Flowers yellowish, ca. 3 mm long. Pedicels less than 0.5 mm. Perianth-tubes turbinate, 1–1.5 mm; lobes yellowish subobovate, ca. 2 mm, apex acute. Stamens 9; filaments pubescent. Staminodes sagittate, pubescent. Ovary clavate, ca. 2 mm. Fruit globose or compressed globose, 7.5–9 × 9–12 mm, longitudinally furrowed, purplish-black when mature.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. P. S. Choi 158; Y. W. Lam 1424.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Sichuan, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Evergreen forests. Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: Aug.–Dec.
Notes: The type specimen (C. Ford s.n. in Herb. Hance No. 21705, BM) was collected in the valley of “Su-kun-pu” (now So Kong Po), Hong Kong Island in May 1881.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Cape D'Aguilar Peak (Hok Tsui Shan), Stubbs Road
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Cryptocarya concinna Hance 黃果厚殼桂（黃果桂）
J. Bot. 20: 79. 1882; FKH 222. 1912; FHN 1: 282. 1964; FRPS 31: 455, pl. 122: 1– 6. 1982; FTW ed. 2, 2: 449, photo 183. 1996.
Cryptocarya konishii Hayata ex Kawakami, List Pl. Form. 1910.

Tree, up to 18 m tall; bark brownish. Young branches slender, angular, yellowish brown tomentellate. Leaves alternate, subleathery; petioles 0.4 –1 cm, yellowish-brown puberulous; leaf blade oblong elliptic or oblong, 5 –10 × 2–3 cm, base cuneate, often unequal, apex obtuse, subacute to shortly acuminate, adaxially shining, glabrous, abaxially ± glaucous, slightly puberulous when young, glabrescent, pinninerved; midvein impressed adaxially, raised abaxially; lateral veins 4 –7 on each side of midvein. Inflorescences paniculate, axillary or terminal, (2–)4– 8 cm, puberulous. Pedicels 1–2 mm, puberulous. Perianth-tubes campanulate, ca. 1 mm; lobes oblong, ca. 2.5 mm, apex obtuse, puberulous on both surfaces. Stamens 9; anthers oblong, ca. 1 mm; filaments pubescent at the base. Ovary enclosed in perianth tubes after anthesis. Fruit long ellipsoid, 1.5 –2 × 8 mm, with 12 longitudinal grooves, black to bluish-black when mature.

Locality: Cape D'Aguilar Peak (Hok Tsui Shan), Stubbs Road. Y. S. Lau 2341; HK sheet 24825.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Jiangxi, Taiwan; N Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests on slopes. Flowering: Mar.–May; fruiting: Jun.–Dec.

Cryptocarya densiflora Bl. 叢花厚殼桂
Bijdr. 556. 1826; FHN 1: 281. 1964; FRPS 31: 441, pl. 116: 1– 8. 1982.
Cryptocarya laevigata Elmer, Leafl. Philipp. Bot. 8: 2720. 1915.

Tree, 7–20 m tall. Branchlets angular, rusty tomentose. Leaves leathery; petioles 1–2 cm, rusty tomentose or glabrescent; leaf blade long elliptic to elliptic-ovate, 10–15 × 5–8.5 cm, base cuneate, broadly cuneate to rounded, apex shortly acuminate, adaxially glabrous and shining, abaxially glaucous, initially rusty pubescent, glabrescent, triplinerved; midvein impressed adaxially, raised abaxially; lateral veins 2–3 on each side of midvein. Panicles axillary or terminal, 2.5–8 cm, densely flowered. Pedicels less than 1 mm, densely tawny puberulous. Perianth white, ca. 4 mm, divided to middle, puberulous; tubes turbinate; lobes ovate, apex acute. Stamens 9, filaments pubescent. Staminodes sagittate, stalked. Ovary clavate, ca. 2 mm. Fruit subglobose, 1.2–1.8 × 1.5–2.5 cm, smooth, obscurely grooved, black when mature.

Locality: Ma On Shan. S. C. Ng 2864; Y. W. Lam 236.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Yunnan; Laos, Vietnam, Malaysia, Indonesia, Philippines.
Ecology: Forests in valley. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.; fruiting: Jul.–Nov.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Pat Sin Leng, Lai Chi Wo
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Lindera aggregata (Sims) Kosterm. 烏藥
Reinwardtia 9(1): 98. 1974; FHN 1: 299. 1964; FRPS 31: 434. 1982: FTW ed. 2, 2: 456, pl. 211. 1996.
Laurus aggregata Sims, Bot. Mag. 51: t. 2497. 1824.

Evergreen shrub or small tree, up to 5 m tall. Young shoots green, densely covered with golden silky hairs, glabrescent. Leaves alternate; petioles 0.5 –1 cm, brown pubescent, glabrescent; leaf blade leathery or subleathery, ovate, elliptic to suborbicular, usually 2.7–5(–7) × 1.5 – 4 cm, base rounded, apex long acuminate to caudate, adaxially green and shining, abaxially glaucous, densely brown pubescent when young, glabrescent, triveined; midvein and the basal pair of lateral veins impressed, rarely raised on adaxial surface, but prominently raised on abaxial surface. Umbels 6 –7-flowered, sessile, usually 6 –8 clustered on axillary spurs, each umbel subtended by a bract. Perianth-lobes 6, subequal, usually yellow or yellowish green, white pubescent abaxially. Pedicels ca. 0.4 mm, pubescent. Fruit ovoid or subglobose, 4 –7 mm in diam.; fruiting pedicels 5 – 8 mm, apex slightly enlarged.

Locality: Pat Sin Leng, Lai Chi Wo. P. S. Choi 420; N. H. Li 28.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam, Philippines.
Ecology: Thin forests and thickets on sunny slopes, or in valleys. Flowering: Mar.–Apr.; fruiting: May–Nov.

Lindera aggregata (Sims) Kosterm. var. playfairii (Hemsl.) H. P. Tsui 小葉烏藥
Acta Phytotax. Sin. 16(4): 69. 1978; FHN 1: 299. 1964; FRPS 31: 435. 1982: FTW ed. 2, 2: 458. 1996.
Litsea playfairii Hemsl., J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 26: 384. 1891; FKH 225. 1912.

Differs from the type variety by the following characteristics: hairs on young shoots, leaves and flowers thiner, usually greyish white, or subglabrous; leaves smaller, narrowly ovate to lanceolate, 4 – 6 × 1.3 –2 cm, apex usually caudate; flowers smaller.

Locality: Kat O. HK sheet 24475, 24573.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi; Vietnam.
Ecology: Thin forests and thickets. Flowering: Mar.–Apr.; fruiting: May–Nov.

Lindera communis Hemsl. 香葉樹
J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 26: 387. 1891; FKH 226. 1912; FRPS 31: 408,pl. 101: 6. 1982; FTW ed. 2, 2: 458. 1996.
Lindera glauca auct. non Blume: FKH 226. 1912 (quoad specimens from Hong Kong).

Evergreen shrub or small tree, (1–)3–4 m tall. Branchlets slender, sparsely or densely yellowish puberulous, glabrescent in age. Leaves alternate; petioles 5–8 mm long, yellowish puberuous or glabrescent; leaf blade leathery, usually lanceolate, ovate or elliptic, 4–9 × 1.5–3 cm, base broad cuneate or subrounded, apex acuminate, acute or sometimes caudate; adaxially glabrous, abaxially greyish green or yellowish, initially tawny pubescent, glabrescent in age, margin involute, pinnately veined; lateral veins 5–7 on each side of midvein, together with midveins impressed adaxially, raised abaxially. Umbels 5 – 8-flowered, solitary or paired in axils of leaves. Peduncles short and stout, 2–5 mm. Pedicels 2–2.5 mm, slightly golden puberulous. Perianth-lobes 6, ovate, subequal, ca. 3 × 1.5 mm, ± golden puberulous abaxially. Fruit ovoid, 7–8 mm in diam., glabrous, red when mature; fruiting pedicels 4–7 mm, yellowish brown puberulous.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 2804; N. H. Li 35.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Gansu, Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam, Myanmar, India, the Ryukyus.
Ecology: Mixed forests on hillslopes. Flowering: Mar.–Apr.; fruiting: Sep.– Oct.

Lindera megaphylla Hemsl. 黑殼楠
J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 26: 389. 1891; FKH 226. 1912; FRPS 31: 384. 1982.

Evergreen tree, 3 –15 m tall. Branches terete, stout, usually purplish black, minutely pubescent to glabrous, sparsely lenticellate. Leaves alternate or often crowded towards apex of branchlets; petioles 1.5–3 cm, glabrous; leaf blade leathery, oblanceolate to obovateoblong, 10 –23 × 2– 6 cm, base attenuate to cuneate, apex acute or acuminate, green and shining adaxially, pale greenish to glaucous abaxially, glabrous on both surfaces, pinnately veined, lateral veins 15 –21 on each side of midvein. Umbels many-flowered, usually borne on axillary spurs. Peduncles of male umbels 1–1.5 cm, those of pistillate umbels 6 mm, all tawny puberulous. Perianth-lobes 6, ± tawny puberulous at base abaxially. Fruit ellipsoid to ovoid, ca. 1.8 × ca. 1.3 cm, glabrous, purplish black at maturity; fruiting pedicels ca. 1.5 cm long, thickened upwards.

Locality: Ng Tung Chai. HK sheet 4953, 24577.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Sichuan, Yunnan, Guizhou, Shaanxi, Gansu, Hubei, Hunan, Anhui, Jiangxi, Fujian.
Ecology: Forests and thickets on slopes or in valleys. Flowering: Feb.–Apr.; fruiting: Sep.–Dec.

Lindera metcalfiana C. K. Allen 滇粵山胡椒
J. Arnold Arbor. 22: 3. 1941; FRPS 31: 401, pl. 104: 1– 4. 1982.
Lindera meissneri auct. non King: Merr. et Chun, Sunyatsenia 2: 1935.

Shrub or small tree, 3–12 m tall. Branchlets slender, brown to greyish brown, initially ± yellowish puberulous. Leaves alternate; petioles 5–8 mm long, yellowish brown pubescent; leaf blade leathery, elliptic or oblong, 5–13 × 2–4.5 cm, base broadly cunneate, apex acuminate or caudate, usually falcate, dark green to yellowish green adaxially, glaucous abaxially, tawny puberulous on veins of both surfaces, pinnately veined; lateral veins 6–10 on each side of midvein, turning purplish brown when dry, reticulation of veins prominent abaxially. Umbels 1–2(–3) on axillary spurs, tawny pubescent, inserted on axillary spurs. Male umbels 6–8-flowered; peduncles slender, 1–1.6 cm; pedicels 2–3 mm. Female umbels 4 –8-flowered; peduncles 0.6 –0.8 cm; pedicels 2–2.5 mm. Fruit globose, ca. 6 mm in diam., purplish black at maturity; fruiting pedicels ca. 6 mm, stout, slightly brownish puberulous.

Locality: Sunset Peak. Y. W. Lam 1744.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian.
Ecology: Forest on hillslopes. Flowering: Mar.–May; fruiting: Jun.– Oct.

Lindera nacusua (D. Don) Merr. 絨毛山胡椒
Lingnan Sci. J. 15: 419. 1936; FHN 1: 300. 1964; FRPS 31: 406. 1982.
Laurus nacusua D. Don, Prodr. Fl. Nepal. 64. 1825.
Daphnidium bifarium auct. non Nees, in Wall. Pl. Asiat. Rar. 2: 63. 1831; FHK 294. 1861.

Evergreen shrub or small tree, 2–10 m tall. Branchlets brown, densely tawny villose when young, glabrescent. Leaves alternate; petioles stout, 5–7(–10) mm, densely tawny pubescent; leaf blade leathery, broadly ovate, elliptic or oblong-ovate, 6 –11 × 3.5–6 cm, base cuneate to attenuate, sometimes rotunded, asymmetrical, apex usually acute, adaxially glabrous, sometimes puberulous on the midvein, abaxially densely tawny villose, pinninerved; lateral veins 5–10 on each side of midvein, together with midvein impressed adaxially, prominently raised abaxially. Male umbels 8–9-flowered, female umbels (2–)3–6-flowered, solitary or 2–4 clustered in axils of leaves; peduncules short, 2–3 mm. Pedicels 3–5.5 mm long, densely yellow villose. Perianth-lobes 6, ovate to broadly ovate, 2–3.5 mm. Fruit subglobose, ca. 6 mm in diam., red at maturity; fruiting pedicels stout, 5–7 mm, thickened upwards, slightly yellowish brown puberulous.

Locality: Hong Kong Island. H. C. Tang 727; Y. S. Lau 74.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Jiangxi, Fujian; Nepal, India, Myanmar, Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests in valley or on hillslopes. Flowering: May– Jun.; fruiting: in Jul.– Oct.

Litsea acutivena Hayata 尖脈木薑子
Icon. Pl. Formosan. 5: 163. 1915; FHN 1: 293. 1964; FRPS 31: 328. 1982; FTW ed. 2, 2: 465, pl. 215. 1996.
Actinodaphne acutivena (Hayata) Nakai, J. Jap. Bot. 14: 191. 1938.
Litsea dolichocarpa Hayata, Icon. Pl. Formosan. 5: 166. 1915.

Evergreen tree, to 7 m tall. Branchlets densely tawny villose when young, glabrescent in age; bud scales rusty pubescent abaxially. Leaves alternate or crowded towards apex of branches; petioles 6–12 mm, densely tawny pubescent; leaf blade leathery, lanceolate, oblanceolate or oblong-lanceolate, 4 –11 × 2–4 cm, base cuneate, apex acute or shortly acuminate, adaxially glabrous, abaxially yellowish tawny pubescent; pinnately veined, lateral veins 9 –10 on each side of midvein, midvein and lateral veins impressed adaxially, raised abaxially. Umbels 5–6-flowered, clustered near apex of branchlets. Peduncles 3 mm, pubescent. Pedicels densely pubescent. Perianth-lobes 6, long-elliptic, ca. 2 mm, abaxially pubescent on midvein. Fertile stamens 9; filaments pubescent. Ovary ovoid, subglabrous, style ca. 2.5 mm; stigma 2-lobed; staminodes pubescent. Fruits ellipsoid, 12–20 × 10–12 mm, black at maturity, subtended by enlarged, cupshaped perianth-tube; fruiting pedicels 1 cm.

Locality: Victoria Peak. Y. S. Lau 467; C. Ford s.n. (HK sheet 4975).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Taiwan; Cambodia, Laos, Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests on hillslopes. Flowering: Jul.–Aug.; fruiting: Dec.–Feb.

Litsea cubeba (Lour.) Pers. 木薑子（山蒼樹）
Syn. Pl. 2: 4. 1807; FHN 1: 289. 1964; FRPS 31: 271. 1982; FTW ed. 2, 2: 470, photo 198. 1996.
Laurus cubeba Lour. Fl. Cochinch. 252. 1790.
Tetranthera polyantha Wall., Cat. No. 2538, nom. nud.; FHK 293. 1861.
Litsea citrata auct. non Bl.: Dunn & Tutch., FKH 225. 1912.

Deciduous, aromatic shrub or small tree, 8–10 m tall. Branchlets slender, green, glabrous; terminal buds conical, pubescent. Leaves alternate; petioles 6–20 mm, glabrous; leaf blade papery, lanceolate, oblong or elliptic, 4–11 × 1.1 –2.4 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate or acute, dark green adaxially, glaucous abaxially, glabrous on both surfaces; pinnately veined, lateral veins slender, 6–16 on each side of midvein, together with midvein raised on both surfaces. Umbels 4–6-flowered, solitary or fascicled; peduncles slender, 6–10 mm; bracts ciliate. Perianth-lobes 6, broad ovate. Fertile stamens 9; filaments pubescent in the lower part; staminodes in female flowers pubescent on the lower part. Ovary ovoid, stigma capitate. Fruit subglobose, ca. 5 mm in diam., black at maturity; fruiting pedicels 2–4 mm, slightly enlarged at the apex.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 1304, 1480.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Sichuan, Xizang, Yunnan, Guizhou, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; SE Asia.
Ecology: Sunny slopes, thickets, thin forests. Flowering: Feb.–Mar.; fruiting: Jul.–Aug.
Uses: Materials (essential oil), ornamental, medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Tam, Wu Kau Tang, Lai Chi Wo
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Litsea elongata (Wall. ex Nees) Benth. & Hook. f. 黃丹木薑子
Gen. Pl. 3: 163. 1880; FKH 225. 1912; FHN 1: 294. 1964; FRPS 31: 329, pl. 86: 1. 1982.
Daphnidium elongata Nees in Wall. Pl. Asiat. Rar. 2: 63. 1831.

Evergreen tree, to 12 m tall. Branchlets yellowish brown or greyish brown, densely brown-tomentose; bud scales covered with silky short hairs abaxialy. Leaves alternate; petioles 10–25 mm, densely brown tomentose; leaf blade leathery, oblong, oblong-lanceolate, narrowly lanceolate or oblanceolate, 6–22 × 2–6 cm, base cuneate or subrounded, apex obtuse or shortly acuminate, adaxially glabrous, abaxially puberulous and villose along midvein and lateral veins; pinnately veined, lateral veins 10 –20 on each side of midvein, midvein and lateral veins immersed or slightly impressed adaxially, raised abaxially. Umbels 4 –5-flowered, solitary, rarely clustered. Peduncles stout, 2–5 mm, densely brown tomentose. Pedicels villose. Perianth-lobes 6, ovate, abaxially villose along midvein. Fertile stamens 9 –12; filaments villose. Female umbels smaller than the males. Ovary ovoid, glabrous. Fruit oblong, 11–13 × 7– 8 mm, subtended by enlarged, cup-shaped perianth-tube, blackish purple when mature; fruiting pedicels 2–3 mm.

Locality: Tai Tam, Wu Kau Tang, Lai Chi Wo. Y. W. Lam 156.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Sichuan, Xizang, Yunnan, Guizhou, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian; India, Nepal.
Ecology: Roadsides, streamsides, forests on mountain slopes; thickets, moist places in sparse forests. Flowering: May–Nov.; fruiting: Feb.–Jun.

Litsea glutinosa (Lour.) C. B. Rob. 潺槁樹
Philip. J. Sci. Bot. 6: 321. 1911; FHN 1: 291, fig. 144. 1964; FRPS 31: 285. 1982
Sebifera glutinosa Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 638. 1790.
Tetranthera citrifolia sensu Benth., FHK 293. 1861.
Litsea sebifera Pers., Syn. Pl. 2: 4. 1807; FKH 225. 1912.

Evergreen tree, 3 –15 m tall. Branchlets greyish brown, initially tawny tomentose. buds scales greyish yellow tomentose. Leaves alternate; petioles 1–2.6 cm, grey yellow tomentose; leaf blade leathery, obovate, obovate-oblong or elliptic-lanceolate, 3.5 –10(–26) × 1.5 –11 cm, base cuneate, obtuse or rotund, apex obtuse or rounded, initially tomentose on both surfaces, glabrate in age; pinnately veined, lateral veins 5–12 on each side of midvein, together with midvein slightly raised adaxially, distinctly raised abaxially; Umbels few flowered, solitary or several clustered on short spurs, or more often in axils of distal leaves. Peduncles 1–1.5 cm, together with pedicels tawny tomentose. Perianth inconspicuous or wanting. Fertile stamens 15 or more; filaments greyish pubescent. Ovary of female flowers subrounded, glabrous; staminodes pubescent. Fruit globose, ca. 7 mm in diam.; fruiting pedicels 5 – 6 mm, slightly thickened at apex.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 2220; P. S. Choi 290.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, S Yunnan, Fujian; India, Philippines, Vietnam.
Ecology: Forest edges, streamsides, or thickets.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), bark is used to make incense.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Victoria Peak, Happy Valley, Ma On Shan
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Litsea greenmaniana C. K. Allen 華南木薑子
Ann. Missouri Bot. Gard. 25: 394. 1938; FRPS 31: 316. 1982.
Litsea greenmaniana var. angustifolia Y. C. Yang & P. H. Huang, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 16(4): 56. 1978.
Litsea variabilis auct. non Hemsl.: Check List HK Plants 28. 1993.

Evergreen small tree, 6 – 8 m tall. Branchlets reddish brown, pubescent when young, glabrescent in age; bud scales covered with silky short hairs. Leaves alternate; petioles 0.7–1.3 cm, initially pubescent; leaf blade thin leathery, elliptic or suboblanceolate, 4 –13.5 × 0.7–3.5 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate or falcate, green and shining adaxially, glaucous abaxially, glabrous on both surfaces; pinnately veined, lateral veins slender, ca. 10 on each side of midvein, reticulation of veins prominent abaxially. Umbels 3 – 4-flowered, 1– 4 clustered on axillary spurs. Peduncles 3 – 4 mm, puberulous. Male flowers: pedicels puberulous; Perianth-lobes 6, yellow, ovate or elliptic, ca. 2 × 1 mm, pubescent abaxially, glabrous adaxially; fertile stamens 9, filaments villose. Fruit ellipsoid, 13 × 8 mm, subtended by enlarged, cup-shaped perianth tube (receptacles); fruiting pedicels 3 mm.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Happy Valley, Ma On Shan. W. J. Tutcher s.n.(HK sheet 4923); F. W. Xing 8467.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian.
Ecology: Forests on valleys, dense forests on mountain slopes; below 1200 m. Flowering: Jul.–Aug.; fruiting: Dec.–Mar. of the next year.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Sai Kung, Lantau
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Litsea monopetala (Roxb.) Pers. 假柿木薑子（假柿樹）
Syn. Pl. 2: 4. 1807; FHN 1: 292. 1964; FRPS 31: 302, pl. 78: 1– 4. 1982.
Tetranthera monopetala Roxb., Pl. Coromandel 2: 26, pl. 148. 1798; FHK 292. 1861.
Litsea polyantha Juss., Ann. Mus. Natl. Hist. Nat. 6: 211. 1805; FKH 225. 1912.

Evergreen tree, to 18 m tall. Branchlets and bud scales densely rusty pubescent. Leaves alternate; petioles 1–3 cm, densely rusty pubescent; leaf blade thin leathery, broadly ovate, obovate to ovate-oblong, 8 –20 × 4 –12 cm, base rounded or acute, apex obtuse or rounded, occasionally acute, adaxially rusty pubescent along midvein when young, glabrescent in age, abaxially densely rusty pubescent, pinnately veined, lateral veins of 8–12 on each side of midvein, impressed adaxially, raised abaxially. Umbels 4(– 6)-flowered, clustered on axillary spurs. Peduncles 4– 6 mm. Pedicels 6–7 mm, rusty pubescent. Perianth-lobes of male flowers 5– 6, lanceolate, ca. 2.5 mm, yellowish white. Fertile stamens 9; filaments slender, pubescent. Female flowers smaller, Perianth-lobes oblong, ca. 1.5 mm; staminodes pubescent. Ovary ovoid, glabrous. Fruit long-ovoid, 7 × 5 mm, subtended by slightly enlarged, shallow discoid perianth tube (receptacles); fruiting pedicels 1 cm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Sai Kung, Lantau. H. C. Tang 122, 984.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, SW Guizhou, S Yunnan; India, Pakistan, SE Asia.
Ecology: Thickets or sparse forests on sunny slopes; up to 1500 m, but mostly found on hills at low altitudes. Flowering: Nov.–Jun. of the next year; fruiting: Jun.–Jul.

Litsea rotundifolia (Nees) Hemsl. 圓葉豺皮樟
J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 26: 385. 1891; FKH 225. 1912; FRPS 31: 292. 1982.
Iozoste rotundifolia Nees, Pl. Asiat. Rar. 2: 63. 1831.

Evergreen shrub or small tree, up to 3 m tall. Branchlets slender, greyish brown, glabrous or nearly so; bud scales yellow silky puberulous. Leaves thin leathery, alternate; petioles 3 –5 mm, initially pubescent, glabrescent in age; leaf blade thin leathery, broadly ovate-rounded to suborbicular, 2.2–4.5 × 1.5 – 4 cm, base subrounded, apex rotund or shortly acuminate, adaxially dark green and shining, abaxially glaucous, glabrous on both surfaces; pinnately veined, lateral veins 3 – 4 on each side of midvein, midvein and lateral veins impressed adaxially, raised abaxially. Umbels 3 – 4-flowered, often 3 clustered in axils of leaves. Peduncles and pedicels almost lacking. Perianth-lobes 6, obovate-rounded, unequal. Fertile stamens 9; filaments villose. Fruit globose, ca. 6 mm in diam. subsessile, greyish bluish black when mature.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Fanling, Haihung. HK sheet 24421.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian; Vietnam.
Ecology: Sparse forests, thickets of lower parts on mountain, roadsides on mountains, riversides; below 800 m.

Litsea rotundifolia (Nees) Hemsl. var. oblongifolia (Nees) C. K. Allen 豺皮樟
Ann. Missouri Bot. Gard. 25: 386. 1938; FRPS 31: 292. 1982; FTW ed. 2, 2: 474, pl. 220. 1996.
Iozoste rotundifolia Nees var. oblongifolia Nees in J. D. Hooker & Arnott, Bot. Beechey Voy. 209. 1836 (based on Litsea chinensis Bl.).
Litsea chinensis Bl., Bijdr. 565. 1825, non Lam.
Actinodaphne chinensis Nees, Syst. Laur. 600. 1836; FHK 293. 1861.

Differs from var. rotundifolia by leaves ovate-oblong, 2.5 – 5.5 × 1–2.2 cm, base cuneate or obtuse, apex obtuse or shortly acuminate; reticulation of veins conspicuous on both surfaces.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 6; Y. W. Lam 960.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Thin forests, thickets.

Litsea verticillata Hance 輪葉木薑子（槁樹）
J. Bot. 21: 356. 1883; FHN 1: 289. 1964; FRPS 31: 287, pl. 76: 1–2. 1982
Litsea multiumbellata Lec. f. annamensis H. Liu, Laurac. Chine et Indochine 171. 1932 et 1934.

Evergreen shrub or small tree, 2–5 m tall. Branchlets brown, densely yellow hirsute, glabrous in age; bud scales densely tawny pubescent. Leaves 4–6 irregularly whorled; petioles 2–6 mm, densely yellow villose; leaf blade thin leathery, lanceolate or oblanceolate-oblong, 7–25 × 2–6 cm, base acute, obtuse or rotund, apex acuminate, adaxially green and glabrous excepting the puberulous midvein, abaxially greyish green or yellowish brown, brown pubescent, margin ciliate, pinnately veined, lateral veins 12–14 on each side of midvein, midvein impressed adaxially, raised abaxially. Umbels 5–8-flowered, subsessile, 2–10 clustered at apex of spurs; bracts 4–7, greyish brown puberulous; Perianth-lobes 6 (4), lanceolate, abaxially villose along midvein.
