Fertile stamens 9; filaments exserted, villose. Ovary ovoid or ellipsoid; styles slender; stigma 3-lobed. Fruit ovoid or ellipsoid, 10–15 × 5–6 mm, apiculate, subtended by enlarged, discoid perianth-tube.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 2765; P. S. Choi 418.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, S Yunnan; Cambodia, Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests or thickets in valleys, streamsides. Flowering: Apr.–Nov.; fruiting: Nov.–Jun. of the following year.

Machilus breviflora (Benth.) Hemsl. 短序潤楠（短花楠）
J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 26: 374. 1861; FKH 224. 1912; FRPS 31: 59. 1982.
Alseodaphne breviflora Benth., FHK 292. 1861.

Tree, ca. 8 m tall. Branchlets dark brown to greyish brown. Buds ovoid, with tomentose scales. Leaves clustered towards apex of branchlets; petioles 3–5 mm; leaf blade leathery, obovate to obovate-lanceolate, 4–5(9) × 1.5–2 cm, base attenuate, apex obtuse, glabrous on both surfaces, midvein impressed adaxially, raised abaxially, lateral veins and veinlets slender. Panicles 3 –5, terminal, glabrous. Peduncules 3–5 cm. Pedicels short, ca. 3 –5 mm. Perianth-lobes slightly unequal, outer 3 smaller, persistent or sometimes deciduous in fruit. Fruit globose, ca. 8 –10 mm in diam.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. N. H. Li 133; H. C. Tang 1967.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangxi.
Ecology: Mixed forests on hillslopes or in valleys. Flowering: Jul.–Aug.; fruiting: Oct.–Dec.
Notes: The type specimen of Alseodaphne breviflora was collected by C. Wright in Hong Kong Island between 1854 and 1855.

Machilus chekiangensis S. Lee 浙江潤楠
Acta. Phytotax. Sin. 17(2): 53, pl. 5, fig. 4. 1979; FRPS 31: 49, pl. 12: 2. 1982.
Machilus longipedunculata S. Lee et F. N. Wei, Guihaia, 4(2): 93, pl. 1, fig. 1. 1984.

Tree. Branches brown, with scattered labiate lenticels; young branches with bud scale scars at the base. Leaves usually aggregate at apex of branchlets; petioles slender, 8 –15 mm; leaf blade leathery or thin-leathery, oblanceolate, 6.5 –13 × 2–3.6 cm, base attenuate, apex caudate-acuminate, ± falcate, yellowish green when dry, initially appressed puberulous, midvein impressed adaxially, raised abaxially, lateral veins 10–12 on each side of midvein, veinlets slender, reticulation of veins foveolate. Flowers not seen. Infructescence 7–9 cm, borne on the base of branchlets of the current year's growth, greyish puberulous. Fruit globose, ca. 7 mm in diam.; fruiting pedicels ca. 4 mm, together with peduncles purplish reddish when fresh; persistent Perianth-lobes subequal, ca. 4 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 3296; HK sheet 35411.
Distribution: Zhejiang, Fujian.
Ecology: Mixed forests. Flowering: Feb.; fruiting: Apr.–May.

Machilus chinensis (Champ. ex Benth.) Hemsl. 華潤楠（香港楠）
J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 26: 374. 1891; FKH 224. 1912; FRPS 31: 59. 1982.
Alseodaphne chinensis Champ. ex Benth., J. Bot. Kew Misc. 5: 198. 1853; FHK 292. 1861.

Tree, 8–11 m tall, glabrous. Buds small, glabrous or sometimes pubescent. Petioles 6 –14 mm; leaf blade leathery, obovate-oblong to oblong-oblanceolate, 5 – 8(–10) × 2–3(– 4) cm, base attenuate, apex obtuse or shortly acuminate, glaucous or brownish yellow abaxially when dry, midvein impressed adaxially, raised abaxially, lateral veins ca. 8 on each side of midvein, veinlets finely reticulated. Panicles terminal, ca. 3.5 cm. Peduncles 2–2.5 cm. Pedicels ca. 3 mm. Perianth-lobes oblong lanceolate, slightly unequal, inner 3 larger than the outer ones, abaxially puberulous, adaxially glabrous or only puberulous at the base. Fruit globose, 8–11 mm in diam.

Locality: Aberdeen, Nam Fung Road. C. P. Lau 146; HK sheet 38389.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi; Vietnam.
Ecology: Mixed forest on hillslopes. Flowering: Sep.; fruiting: Feb.
Notes: The type specimen of Alseodaphne chinensis was collected by J. G. Champion in Happy Valley, Hong Kong Island between 1847 and 1850.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Po Kau, Sha Lo Tung
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Machilus gamblei King ex Hook. f. 黃心樹（芳槁潤楠）
Fl. Brit. India 5: 138. 1886.
Machilus suaveolens S. Lee, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 8(3): 187. 1963; FHN 1: 272. 1964; FRPS 31: 38. 1982.

Tree, to 25 m tall. Young shoots densely rusty sericeous, glabresent. Petioles 1–2 cm; leaf blade leathery, oblong, obovate or oblanceolate, (5–)6–15 × 1.5–5.5 cm, base cuneate to attenuate, apex bluntly acute or shortly acuminate, greenish or greenish white abaxial, densely rusty sericeous on both surfaces when young, glabresent adaxially. Puberulous abaxially, lateral veins 6–10 on each side of midvein, raised on both surfaces, veinlets inconsipicuous. Panicles arising from the base of branchlets, 4 –13 cm. Peduncles (2–)4–8.5 cm, densely greyish sericeous. Pedicels slender, ca. 5 mm. Perianth-lobes equal, oblong, 4 × 1.5 mm, sericeous on both surfaces. Fruit globose, 7–8 mm in diam., blackish when mature; fruiting pedicels slightly thickened, to 1.5 mm thick at the apex.

Locality: Tai Po Kau, Sha Lo Tung. X. Y. Zhuang 1950; Y. W. Lam 1457.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou; India, Nepal to Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests on slopes or in valleys. Flowering: Mar.–Apr.; fruiting: May–Jun.

Machilus grijsii Hance 黃絨潤楠（黃楠）
Ann. Sci. Nat., Bot., ser. 4, 18: 226. 1863; FKH 224. 1912; FHN 1: 268. 1964; FRPS 31: 32, pl. 8: 1. 1982.

Tree, up to 5 m tall. Buds, branchlets, petioles and abaxial surface of leaves tawny tomentulose. Petioles 7–18 mm; leaf blade leathery, obovate-oblong, 7.5–14(–18) × 3.7–6.5(–7) cm, base ± rounded, apex acuminate, glabrous adaxially, midvein and lateral veins impressed adaxially, raised abaxially, lateral veins 8–11 on each side of midvein, veinlets slender and indistinct. Cymes short, ca. 3 cm, fasciculate at apex of branchlets, densely tawny tomentulose. Pedicels ca. 5 mm. Perianth-lobes oblong elliptic, subequal, ca. 3.5 mm, tomentose on both surfaces. Fruit globose, ca. 1 cm in diam.

Locality: Ma On Shan. HK sheet 24155, 34136.
Distribution: Guangdong, Jiangxi, Zhejing, Fujian.
Ecology: Thickets, forests. Flowering: Mar.; fruiting: Apr.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Ho Sheung Heung, Sheung Shui (Kwu Tung)
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Machilus kwangtungensis Y. C. Yang 廣東潤楠
J. W. China Border Res. Soc. Ser. B. 15: 77. 1945; FRPS 31: 37, pl. 9: 2. 1982.

Tree, to 10 m tall. Young branches densely rusty tomentose. Leaves leathery; petioles 8–10(–15) mm, pubrulous; leaf blade oblong or oblanceotate, 6–11(–15) × 2–4.5 cm, base attenuate, apex acuminate, dark greenish and glabrous adaxially, paler and appressed puberulent abaxially, midvein impressed adaxially, raised abaxially, lateral veins slender, usually 10 –12 on each side of midvein, inconspicuous on both surfaces. Panicles arising from lower part of the current year's branchlets, 5 –10.5 cm, greyish yellow puberulous. Peduncles slightly compressed. Pedicels slender, 5 –7 mm. Perianth-lobes subequal, oblong, ca. 5 mm, apex obtuse, puberulous on both surfaces. Fruit subglobose, slightly compressed, 8–9 mm in diam., blackish when mature; fruiting pedicels 5 – 8 mm, puberulous.

Locality: Ho Sheung Heung, Sheung Shui (Kwu Tung). Y. W. Lam 1512, 1483.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hunan.
Ecology: Forest on hillslopes or in valleys. Flowering: Mar.–Apr.; fruiting: May–Jul.

Machilus leptophylla Hand.-Mazz. 薄葉潤楠
Symb. Sin. 7: 252. 1931; W. Y. Chun, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 2: 167, t. 32. 1953; FRPS 31: 44. 1982.

Tree, to 28 m tall. Branchlets stout, dark brown, glabrous. Terminal buds subglobose, with minutely sericeous scales. Leaves alternate or clustered on branchlets of the current year's growth; petioles 1–3 cm, glabrous; leaf blade firmly papery, obovate-oblong, 14 –24(–32) × 3.5 –7(– 8) cm, base cuneate, apex shortly acuminate, abaxial surface densely appressed sericeous when young, sparsely sericeous to glabrescent when aged; lateral veins 14–20(–24) on each side of midvein, reddish when fresh. Panicles 6–10 clustered at the base of branchlets, 8 –12(–15) cm, many-flowered, densely greyish puberulous. Pedicels slender, ca. 5 mm. Perianth-lobes subequal, oblongelliptic, pulverulent abaxially, puberulous or glabrous adaxially. Fruit globose, ca. 1 cm in diam.; fruiting pedicels 5 –10 mm.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. Y. W. Lam 1405, 1426.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hunan, Jiangsu, Zhejing, Fujian.
Ecology: Forests in valleys. Fruiting: Jul.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Po (Nam Hang), Sai Kung (Tsiu Hang)
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Machilus pauhoi Kanehira 刨花潤楠（多脈潤楠、密脈潤楠）
Trop. Woods 23: 8. 1930; FRPS 31: 43, pl. 11: 1–7. 1982.
Machilus polyneura H. T. Chang, Acta Sci. Nat. Sunyatseni 1960(1): 18. 1960.
Machilus salicina sensu Dunn & Tutch., FKH 224. 1912.

Tree, 6 –20 m tall. Branchlets glabrous or brownish puberulous at the base. Buds globose to subovoid, with brownish puberulous scales. Leaves usually clustered towards apex of branchlets; petioles slender, 8 –13 mm; leaf blade leathery, elliptic to narrowly elliptic, occasionally oblanceolate, 7–15(–17) × 2– 4(–5) cm, apex acuminate or caudate-acuminate, tip blunt, adaxial surface dark green and glabrous, abaxial surface except for the midvein and lateral veins densely covered with appressed tawny short hairs; lateral veins slender, 12–17 on each side of midvein, veinlets inconspicuous on both surfaces. Inflorescence cymose-paniculate, arising from the base of the current year's branchlets, puberulous. Pedicels slender, 8 –13 mm. Perianth-lobes ovate-lanceolate, ca. 6 mm, puberulous on both surfaces. Fruit globose, ca. 1 cm in diam., black when mature.

Locality: Tai Po (Nam Hang), Sai Kung (Tsiu Hang). Y. W. Lam 195, 657.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian.
Ecology: Thickets or open forests on hillslopes or in valleys.

Machilus robusta W. W. Sm. 粗壯潤楠
Notes Roy. Bot. Gard. Edinburgh 13: 169. 1921; FRPS 31: 62. 1982.
Machilus liangkwangensis Chun, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 2: 165, t. 30. 1953.

Tree, 15–20 m tall. Branchlets stout, more or less compressed and puberulous when young, glabrescent, lenticellate. Buds small, ovoid, with brownish densely puberulous scales. Petioles 2.5–5 cm; leaf blade thickly leathery, narrowly elliptic to obovate-elliptic or suboblong, 10–26 × 5.5–8.5 cm, base subrounded or broadly cuneate, apex acute or sometimes shortly acuminate, glabrous on both surfaces, glaucous abaxially, midvein impressed adaxially, strongly raised on abaxial surface, turning red when dry, lateral veins (5–)7–9 on each side of midvein, ca. 2.5 cm spaced, reticulation of veins foveolate. Panicles terminal or in axils of leaves near apex of branchlets, 4–12(–16) cm, much branched and many-flowered. Peduncles 2.5–11.5 cm, stout, compressed, reddish when fresh, densely puberulous, glabrescent. Pedicels 5–8 mm long, pubescent, reddish when fresh. Perianth-lobes subequal, ovate-lanceolate, 6–7(–9) × 2–3(–3.5) mm, acute, puberulous to glabrous on both surfaces. Fruit globose, 2.5–3 cm in diam., bluish black when mature; fruiting pedicels thickened, 1–1.5 cm, crimson.

Locality: Ng Tung Chai, Castle Peak. S. C. Ng 2874; HK sheet 24230.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, S Guizhou, S Yunnan; Myanmar.
Ecology: Evergreen forests, especially in valleys. Flowering: Jan.–Apr.; fruiting: Apr.–Jun.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan, Sunset Peak
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Machilus thunbergii Sieb. & Zucc. 紅楠
Abh. Bayer. Akad. Wiss., Math.-Naturwiss. Kl. 4(4): 202. 1846; FHK 291. 1861; FKH 224. 1912; FRPS 31: 19, pl. 4: 1. 1982; FTW ed. 2, 2: 483, photo 207. 1996.
Machilus rimosa auct. non Blume: FHK 291. 1861.

Tree, usually 10–15(–20) m tall, glabrous except the ciliate scales of the leaf-buds. Petioles slender, 1–3.5 cm, reddish when fresh; leaf blade leathery to obovate, obovate-lanceolate, 4.5 –9(–13) × 1.7– 4.2 cm, base cuneate, apex shortly cuspidate to shortly acuminate, dark green and shining adaxially, ± glaucous abaxially, midvein slightly impressed adaxially, prominently raised abaxially, lateral veins 7–12 on each side of midvein. Panicles loosely oblong or pyramidal, 5 –12 cm, terminal or arising from the base of twigs. Pedicels 5–8 mm. Perianth-lobes narrow-oblong, ca. 5 mm, outer 3 narrower and shorter, apex acute, Fruit compressed globose, 8 –10 mm in diam., blackish purple when mature; peduncles and fruiting pedicels bright red.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan, Sunset Peak. N. H. Li 18; Y. W. Lam 1408.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Shandong, Zhenjiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Korea.
Ecology: Forests on hill slopes or in valleys. Flowering: Feb.; fruiting: Jun.–Aug.

Machilus velutina Champ. ex Benth. 絨毛潤楠
Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 5: 198. 1853; FHK 291. 1861; FKH 224. 1912; FHN 1: 268. 1964; FRPS. 31: 31, pl. 8: 2. 1982.

Tree, up to 18 m tall. Branches, buds and inflorescences densely rusty tomentose. Petioles 1–2.5(–3) cm; leaf blade leathery, leaf blade leathery, narrowly obovate, elliptic, or narrowly ovate, 5–11(–18) × 2–5(5.5) cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate or shortly acuminate, shining adaxially, midvein slightly impressed adaxially, prominently raised abaxially, lateral veins 8–11 on each side of midvein, reticulation of veins inconspicous. Cymes solitary or 2–3 aggregated at apex of branchlets, shortly pedunculate or sessile, profusely and shortly branched. Flowers yellowish green, aromatic, densely rusty tomentose; perianth-lobes slightly unequal, inner 3 ovate, ca. 6 × 3 mm, outer 3 smaller and narrower. Fruit globose, ca. 4 mm in diam., purplish red when mature.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 21, 1148.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian; Indochina.
Ecology: Flowering: Oct.–Dec.; fruiting: Feb.–Mar.
Notes: The type specimen was collected by J. G. Champion from Hong Kong Island between 1847 to 1850.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Mount Parker, Kadoorie Farm, Tai Mo Shan
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Machilus wangchiana Chun 信宜潤楠（嘉道理楠）
Acta Phytotax. Sin. 2: 166. 1953; FRPS 31: 29. 1982.
Persea wangchiana (Chun) Kosterm., Reinwardtia 6: 194. 1962.
Persea kadooriei Kosterm., J. S. Afr. Bot. 47(1): 110. 1981.

Tree, 6 –15 m tall; branchlets dark grey, glabrous. Leaves clustered near apex of twigs; petioles ca. 2 cm; leaf blade leathery, oblong oblanceolate or oblong elliptic, 18–25 × 5–8 cm, base cuneate and decurrent, apex cuspidate, midvein thick, impressed adaxially, prominently raised abaxially, lateral veins 24 –30 on each side of midvein, reticulation of veins foveolate. Inflorescences subracemose, 5–12 cm, densely aggregated on branchlets of the current year's growth. Peduncles ± fleshy and purplish when fresh, branched above middle; the branches 1–3-flowered. Pedicels ca. 8 mm. Perianth-lobes, unequal, inner 3 oblong elliptic, ca. 7 mm long, outer 3 smaller, apex acute, initially puberulous. Fruit globose, ca. 2.5 cm in diam., black; pedicels purplish when mature.

Locality: Mount Parker, Kadoorie Farm, Tai Mo Shan. Y. W. Lam 170, 1459.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi.
Ecology: Forests in valleys. Fruiting: Apr.–May.
Notes: The type specimen of Persea kadooriei Kosterm. was collected by G. Barretto in Kadoorie Farm in 1972. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Neolitsea cambodiana Lecomte var. glabra C. K. Allen 香港新木薑子
Ann. Missouri Bot. Gard. 25: 418. 1938; FRPS 31: 346. 1982.
Actinodaphne angustifolia auct. non Nees: Benth., FHK 293. 1861.
Actinodaphne hongkongensis Chun, J. Arnold Arbor. 8: 22. 1927.
Neolitsea hongkongensis (Chun) C.K. Allen, Ann. Missouri Bot. Gard. 25: 418. 1938.

Tree, 8 –12 m tall. Branchlets tawny adpressed-pubescent. Leaves 3 –5, subverticillate; petioles 1–1.5 cm, adpressed-pubescent; leaf blade leathery, oblong-lanceolate, oblong-elliptic lanceolate, obovate or elliptic, 10 –17 × 3.5 – 6 cm, base attenuate or cuneate, apex acuminate or acute, glabrous on both surfaces, glaucous abaxially, pinnately veined or subtriplinerved, lateral veins 4 –5 on each side of midvein. Umbels 4 –5-flowered, clustered, sessile or subsessile; bracts 4, pubescent on the ridge of abaxial surface. Male flowers: Perianth-lobes ovate; fertile stamens 6, exserted, filaments villous at the base; pistillodes glabrous. Female flowers: Perianth-lobes linear or ovate-lanceolate, staminodes pubescent at the base; ovary ovoid, stigma bifid. Fruit globose, 8 –10 mm diam., on a discoid perianth tube; fruiting pedicels 7 mm.

Locality: Victoria Peak (Lugard Road), Happy Valley. Y. S. Lau 2524, 2649.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, S Jiangxi, Fujian; Cambodia, Laos.
Ecology: Mixed forests, thickets. Flowering: Oct.–Dec.; fruiting: Jul.–Aug.
Notes: The type specimen of Actinodaphne hongkongensis Chun was collected in Happy Valley Woods by C. Wilford between 1857 and 1858.

Neolitsea chuii Merr. 鴨公樹
Lingnan Sci. J. 7: 306. 1929; FRPS 31: 372, pl. 95: 1–2.1982; FGD 6: 50. 2005

Tree, to 8 m tall, glabrous, except for the inflorescence. Leaves alternate or crowded toward apex of the branchlets; petioles 2.5–4 cm; leaf blade elliptic to oblong-elliptic or ovate-elliptic, 8–16 × 3–9 cm, base acute, apex acuminate, glaucous abaxially, triplinerved, lateral veins of 3 –5 pairs. Umbels pubescent, 5 – 6-flowered, axillary or lateral, clustered; peduncles very short or almost obsolete; pedicels 4 –5 mm. Perianth-segments 4, ovate or oblong, abaxially puberulous at base and on midvein. Male flowers: fertile stamens 6; filaments pubescent at base; pistillodes ovoid. Fruit ellipsoid or subglobose, ca. 8 mmin diam.; fruiting pedicels 7 mm, slightly thickened.

Locality: Sai Kung, Tai Po Kau. S. C. Ng 3209, 3240; K. Y. Tam s.n. (HK sheet 39679).
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, SE Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian.
Ecology: Native forests in valleys. Flowering: Sep.– Oct.; fruiting: Dec.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Ma On Shan (Mau Ping Village), Sunset Peak
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Neolitsea kwangsiensis Liou 廣西新木薑子
Laurac. Chine & Indochine 146. 1932; Allen, Ann. Missouri Bot. Gard. 25: 423. 1938; FRPS 31: 370. 1982

Shrub or small tree, to 5 m tall; bark greyish, smooth. Branchlets stout, yellowish brown, glabrous. Bud scales subglabrous abaxially, margin ciliate. Leaves leathery, alternate or clustered towards apex of branchlets; petioles 2.5 –4 mm, slightly compressed, glabrous; leaf blade broadly ovate, ovate or ovate-oblong, 11–19 × 6.8 –12.5 cm, base rotund or attenuate, apex acuminate or obtuse, dark green and slightly lustrous adaxially, glaucous abaxially, glabrous on both surfaces; triplinerved, primary veins raised on both surfaces. Umbels 5-flowered, 5 –8 in axillary fascicles. Bracts 4, puberulous abaxially. Pedicels short, densely pubescent. Perianth-lobes 4, ovate or ovateorbicular, 3.5 × 2.5 –3 mm, puberulous on both surfaces. Fruit globose, 15 –16 mm in diam.; fruiting pedicels 6 –7 mm, puberulous.

Locality: Ma On Shan (Mau Ping Village), Sunset Peak. F. W. Xing 8547; Y. S. Lau 1486.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi.
Ecology: Forests in valleys. Flowering: Dec.; fruiting: Aug. of the following year.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Ma On Shan, Tai Mo Shan
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Neolitsea levinei Merr. 大葉新木薑子
Philipp. J. Sci. Bot. 13: 138. 1918; Allen, Ann. Missouri Bot. Gard. 25: 423. 1938; FRPS 31: 359. 1982
Neolitsea lanuginosa Gamble var. chinensis Gamble, Sarg. Pl. Wils. 2: 79. 1914.

Tree, up to 22 m tall. Branchlets terete, densely tawny pubescent when young, glabrate in age. Buds scales rusty puberulous abaxially. Leaves 4–5 whorled; leaf blade leathery, oblong-lanceolate to oblong-oblanceolate or elliptic, 15–30 × 4.5–9 cm, base acute, apex shortly acute, adaxially dark green and shining, glabrous, abaxially glaucous, initially densely tawny villose, glabrate in age; triplinerved, lateral veins 3 – 4 on each side of midvein, raised on both surfaces. Umbels 5-flowered, clustered. Pedicels 3 mm, densely tawny pubescent. Perianth-lobes 4, ovate, sparsely pubescent abaxially, margin ciliate. Fruit ellipsoid or globose, 12–18 × 8–15 mm, black when mature; fruiting pedicels 7–10 mm, densely pubescent, slightly enlarged at apex.

Locality: Ma On Shan, Tai Mo Shan. F. W. Xing 7554; Y. W. Lam 1232.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian.
Ecology: Forests in valleys. Flowering: Mar.–Apr.; fruiting: Aug.– Oct.

Neolitsea ovatifolia Yang & P. H. Huang 卵葉新木薑子
Acta Phytotax. Sin. 16(4): 44, fig. 5. 1978; FRPS 31: 369, pl. 94: 9 –10. 1982; FGD 6: 49. 2005.
Neolitsea ovatifolia var. puberula Yang & P. H. Huang, Act. Phytotax. Sin. 16(4): 44. 1978.

Shrub. Branchlets glabrous. Leaves alternate or crowded toward apex of branchlets; petiole 8 –10(–15) mm, slightly flattened, glabrous; leaf blade leathery, ovate, 4–6(–8.5) × 2–2.5(–4) cm, base obtusely rounded or broadly cuneate, apex acuminate, glabrous, glaucous abaxially, triplinerved, distinctly foveolate on both surfaces, due to the raised midvein and lateral veins. Umbels 5-flowered, solitary or 3–4 fascicled; peduncles very short or obsolete; pedicels sericeous-pubescent. Perianth-segments 4, elliptic. Male flowers: fertile stamens 6; filaments glabrous; pistillodes glabrous. Fruit globose or subglobose, ca 1 cm in diam., glabrous; fruiting pedicels 5–8 mm, very stout, glabrous.

Locality: Lantau Peak. S. C. Ng 3226, 3228.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi.
Ecology: Thin forests. Flowering: May–Jul.; fruiting: Aug.– Oct.

Neolitsea phanerophlebia Merr. 顯脈新木薑子
Lingnan Sci. J. 7: 305. 1929; Allen, Ann. Missouri Bot. Gard. 25: 430. 1938; FRPS 31: 360. 1982

Small tree, to 10 m tall. Branchlets, bud scales and petioles, densely rusty puberulous. Leaves in false whorls or scattered; petioles 1–2 cm; leaf blade papery or thin-leathery, oblong to oblong-elliptic or oblong-lanceolate to ovate, 6 –13 × 2– 4.5 cm, base acute or obtuse, apex acuminate, adaxially pale greenish, ± shining, glabrous except puberulous on veins when young, abaxially glaucous, densely appressed-pubescent and villous; triplinerved, lateral veins 3 –4 on each side of midvein, raised on both surfaces. Umbels sessile, 5 – 6-flowered, 2– 4 clustered in axils of leaves or leaf scars. Bracts 4, appressed-puberulous abaxially. Pedicels 2–3 mm, densely rusty pubescent. Perianth-lobes 4, ovate or orbicular, 3 × 2 mm, margin ciliate, pubescent at the base of adaxial surface. Fruit subglobose, 5 –9 mm in diam., glabrous, purplish black when mature; fruiting pedicels 5–7 mm, appressed-pubescent.

Locality: Sunset Peak, Lantau Peak. L. T. Lo 473, 592.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Jiangxi.
Ecology: Thin forests in valleys. Flowering: Oct.–Nov.; fruiting: Jul.–Aug. of the following year.

Neolitsea pulchella (Meisn.) Merr. 美麗新木薑子
Philip. J. Sci. Bot. 13: 137. 1918; Allen, Ann. Missouri Bot. Gard. 25: 427. 1938; FHN 1: 297. 1964; FRPS 31: 361. 1982
Litsea pulchella Meisn. in DC. Prodr. 15(1): 224. 1864; FKH 225. 1912.
Litsea ceylanca auct. non Nees: Benth., FHK 294. 1861.

Small tree, 6–8 m tall. Branchlets slender, initially brown pubescent; bud scales densely brown puberulous. Leaves alternate or crowded towards apex of branchlets in false whorls; petioles 6–8 mm, initially brown pubescent; leaf blade leathery, elliptic or oblong-elliptic, 4–6 × 2–3 cm, base cuneate or attenuate, apex acuminate or caudate-acuminate, adaxially dark green and shining, glabrous except for the pubescent midvein when young, adaxially glaucous, grey villous when young, glabrescent in age, triplinerved, lateral veins 2–3 on each side of midvein, raised on both surfaces. Umbels 4–5-flowered, solitary or 2–3 clustered in axils of leaves. Pedicels ca. 2 mm, densely villous. Perianth-lobes 4, elliptic, 2.5 × 1.5 mm, abaxially villous on midvein. Fruits globose, 4–6 mm in diam., on a discoid cupule; fruiting pedicels slender, 5–6 mm, slightly thickened at apex.

Locality: Aberdeen, Pok To Yan. Y. S. Lau 46; P. S. Choi s.n. (HK sheet 35879).
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian.
Ecology: Mixed forests. Flowering: Oct.–Nov.; fruiting: Aug.–Sep. of the following year.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Authority: (N. H. Xia, Y. F. Deng & K. L. Yip) J. Li, N. H. Xia & H. W. Li
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Syndiclis hongkongensis N. H. Xia, Y. F. Deng & K. L. Yip 香港油果樟
J. Trop. & Subtrop. Bot. 14(1): 75, fig. 1. 2006.

Tree, up to 16 m tall and up to 90 cm in diam. at base; bark reddish brown, peeling off in small pieces. Branchlets reddish brown, lenticellate, at apex somewhat angular, glabrescent; leaf buds small, hardly hairy. Leaves alternate; leaf blade leathery, elliptic, 6–10 × 2.5–4 cm, base cuneate but always asymmetrical, apex acuminate, with sharp tip, margin entire, glabrescent, dark green above, pale green and glaucous below, midvein and lateral veins brownish, flat above, prominent below, lateral veins 3–4 pairs, veinlets densely reticulate. Petioles slender, 1–2 mm long, flat above. Inflorescence a panicle, axillary, 1–3.5 cm long, slender, tomentose, short pedunculate. Bracteoles linear-triangular, rusty-tomentose, ca. 3 × 1 mm. Flowers globose, green-yellow, 1.5 mm long; pedicels 2–4 mm long; perianth-lobes 6, ovate, densely tomentose. Fertile stamens 6 in 2 whorls, slightly exserted, subsessile, villose, eglandular; the anthers 2-celled, cells introrse; staminodes 6, opposite to the fertile stamens, villose. Ovary ellipsoid, sparsely tomentose, styles tomentose at base. Fruit globose, rough, yellowish brown, ca. 4 cm diam., glabrous; pericarp woody, ca. 2 mm thick; fruiting pedicel 8 mm long, cylindrical, thickened under the fruit.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. L. T. Lo 337; Y. W. Lam 1276.
Distribution: Endemic to Hong Kong.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Nov.–Dec.; fruiting: Oct. of the following year.
Notes: The species was reported as Syndiclis furfuracea H. W. Li previously (Check List HK Plants 47. 2002). The type specimen (N. H. Xia et al. s.n., holotype: IBSC; isotype: HK sheet 39986) was collected from Tai Mo Shan in 2005. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Illigera celebica Miq. 寬藥青藤
Ann. Mus. Bot. Lugduno-Batavum 2: 215. 1866; Kubitzki, Fl. Cam. Laos Vietn. 12: 8–9. 1970; FRPS 31: 476, pl. 127: 4–7. 1982; FGD 3: 3. 1995.
Illigera platyandra Dunn, J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 38: 296. 1908.

Evergreen woody liana. Stems 5–8 m long, striate. Leaves 3-foliolate; petioles 5 –7(–14) cm, often twisted at middle; leaflets ovate to ovate-elliptic, 6 –15 × 3 –7 cm, base rounded or subcordate, apex acute, margin entire, papery or subleathery, glabrous; petiolules 1.5 –2 cm, glabrous. Cymes 15 –20 cm, glabrous. Perianth-segments 10, the outer 5 green, elliptic or oblong, pubescent, the inner 5 white, puberulent, with translucent glandular dots. Stamens 5, longer than perianth-segments. Fruit with 4 unequal wings.

Locality: Fung Yuen, She Shan. Y. W. Lam 298; P. S. Choi 475.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan;Indochina, Malesia.
Ecology: Thin forests and thickets. Flowering: Apr.–Oct.; fruiting: Jun.–Nov.
Notes: The type specimen of Illigera platyandra Dunn was collected by S. T. Dunn in Wong Nai Chung in 1906. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai, Kap Lung
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Chloranthus serratus (Thunb.) Roem. & Schult. 及己（四葉對）
Syst. Veg. 3: 461. 1818; FRPS 20(1): 91. 1982; FGD 3: 21, fig. 15. 1995; FOC 4: 136. 1999.
Nigrina serrata Thunb., Nova Acta Regiae Soc. Sci. Upsal. 7: 142, pl. 5, fig. 1. 1815.

Perennial herb, 15–50 cm tall. Rhizomes procumbent, short, ca. 3 mm in diam., with many yellowish brown fibrous roots. Stems erect, glabrous, with distinct swollen nodes. Leaves opposite, 4–6 on the upper part of stem; petiole 0.8–2.5 cm; leaf blade papery, elliptic, obovate, ovate-lanceolate, suborbicular, or broadly elliptic, sometimes ovate-elliptic or oblong, 7–15 × 3–6 cm, base cuneate, apex acute or acuminate, margin serrulate, with glandular-tipped teeth, glabrous or pubescent on veins abaxially; lateral veins 6–8 on each side of midvein. Spikes terminal, sometimes axillary, 1 or 2- or 3- branched; peduncles 1–3.5 cm; bracts triangular or nearly semiorbicular, usually several toothed at apex. Flowers white. Stamens 3, on outside of apical part of ovary; connectives oblong, connate at basal part, central anther with 2 locules; lateral ones each with 1 locule;. Ovary ovoid; style absent; stigma thick, short. Drupes green, globose or pyriform.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai, Kap Lung. HK Sheet 34863, 34448.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Hubei, Anhui, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Zhejiang, Jiangsu; Japan.
Ecology: Wet places in forests, swamps, streamsides, ravines. Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: Jun.–Aug.
Uses: Medicinal.

Chloranthus spicatus (Thunb.) Makino 金粟蘭（珍珠蘭）
Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 16: 180. 1902; FRPS 20(1): 83, pl. 26: 1–5. 1982; FGD 3: 20. 1995; FOC 4: 134. 1999.
Nigrina spicata Thunb., Nov. Gen. Pl. 59. 1783.
Chloranthus inconspicuous Swartz, Philos. Trans. 78: 359, t. 15. 1787; FHK 334. 1861; FKH 221. 1912.

Subshrub, erect or slightly prostrate at base, 30–60 cm. Stems terete, glabrous. Leaves opposite; petioles 0.8–1.8 cm, leaf blade thick papery, elliptic or obovate-elliptic, 5–11 × 2.5–5.5 cm, base cuneate, apex acute or obtuse, margin crenate-serrate, with glandular-tipped teeth, abaxially pale yellowish green, adaxially deep green and shiny; lateral veins 6–8 pairs, slightly prominent on both surfaces. Spikes arranged, in panicles, usually terminal, rarely axillary; bracts triangular. Flowers yellowish green, small, very fragrant. Stamens 3; connectives connate at base; central anther sometimes apex shallowly 3-lobed, with one 2 loucles; lateral anthers smaller, each with one locule. Ovary obovoid.

Locality: Cultivated. HK Sheet 23950.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Fujian; Japan, Vietnam, India, Indonesia.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Apr.–Jul.; fruiting: Aug.–Sep.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal.

Sarcandra glabra (Thunb.) Nakai 草珊瑚（雞爪蘭、九節楓）
Fl. Sylv. Koreana 18: 17. 1930; FRPS 20(1): 79, pl. 25: 1–5. 1982; FGD 3:18, fig. 14. 1995; FOC 4: 132. 1999.
Bladhia glabra Thunb., Trans. Linn Soc. 2: 331. 1794.
Chloranthus brachystachys auct. non Blume: FHK 334. 1861; FKH 221. 1912.

Subshrub, evergreen, 50–150 cm tall. Stems cylindric, erect, glabrous, nodes swollen. Stipules subulate; petioles 0.5–2 cm, connate, forming a short sheath; leaf blade leathery or papery, elliptic or ovate to ovate-lanceolate, or broadly elliptic to oblong, 6–20 × 2–8 cm, base cuneate or broad-cuneate, apex acute to acuminate, margin sharply coarse-serrate, with glandular-tipped teeth, glabrous; lateral veins 5–7 on each side of midvein, slightly prominent on both surface. Inflorescences terminal, spicate, usually branched, 1.5–4 cm including peduncle; bracts triangular or ovate. Flowers yellowish green. Stamen 1, fleshy, clavate to terete or ovoid; anther 2-celled, cells lateral or sometimes introrse, on both sides of apical part of connective or nearly as long as connective. Ovary globose or ovoid; style absent; stigma subcapitate or minutely spotted. Drupes green when young, shiny-red or yellowish red at maturity, globose or ovoid, ca. 3–4 mm in diam.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 381, 1472.
Distribution: S, SW, C & S China; SE Asia.
Ecology: Forests on hillslopes and in valleys. Flowering: Jun.; fruiting: Aug.– Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.

Houttuynia cordata Thunb. 蕺菜（魚腥草）
Kongl. Vetensk. Acad. Nya Handl. 4: 149, 151. 1783; FHK 334. 1861; FKH 220. 1912; FHN 1: 338. 1964; FRPS 20(1): 8, pl. 3: 1–3. 1982; FGD 1: 79, fig. 84. 1987; FOC 4: 109. 1999.

Herb, 30– 60 cm tall; rhizomes creeping. Basal part of stems creeping, rooted at nodes, apical part erect, glabrous or pubescent on nodes, sometimes purplish red. Stipules membranous, 1– 2.5 cm, lower part connate with petiole and forming a 8–20 mm sheath. Petiole 1–3.5 cm, glabrous; leaf blade thinly papery, broadly ovate or ovate-cordate, 4 –10 × 2.5 – 6 cm, base cordate, apex short acuminate, densely glandular, usually glabrous, sometimes pubescent at vein axils, usually purplish abaxially; veins 5 –7, basal or innermost pair arising ca. 5 mm above base. Inflorescences 1.5 –2.5 cm × 5 – 6 mm; peduncles 1.5 –3 cm, subglabrous; involucral bracts oblong or obovate, 10 –15 × 5 –7 mm, apex rounded. Stamens longer than ovary. Capsules 2–3 mm, with persistent styles.

Localitiy: Lam Tsuen, Sha Lo Tung. HK Sheet 23812, 23813.
Distribution: S, E, C, SW & NW China; SE Asia, Africa (Madagascar), Pacific Islands.
Ecology: In wet places. Flowering: Apr.–Aug.; fruiting: Jun.– Oct.
Uses: Medicinal, food (vegetable).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Tam, Sha Tin, Tai Po, Sha Lo Tung, Tai Mei Tuk
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Saururus chinensis (Lour.) Baill. 三白草
Adansonia 10(2): 71. 1871; FHN 1: 339. 1964; FRPS 20(1): 6, pl. 2. 1982; FGD 1: 78. 1987; FOC 4: 108. 1999.
Spathium chinense Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 217. 1790.
Saururus loureiri Decne., Ann. Sci. Nat. ser. 3, 3: 102. 1845; FKH 220. 1912.

Herb, to more than 1 m tall; rhizomes creeping, white, thick. Stems strong, basal part creeping and usually whitish, apical part erect and green. Stipular sheath 2–10 mm, ca. as long as petiole, slightly clasping; petioles 1–3 cm, glabrous; leaf blade papery, ovate to ovate-lanceolate, 10–20 × 5 –10 cm, base cordate or oblique-cordate, apex acute or acuminate, densely glandular, glabrous; veins 5–7, basal. Apical leaves smaller, 2 or 3 at stem apex, usually petal-like, white at anthesis. Inflorescences axillary or terminal, racemose, 12–20 cm; peduncles 3– 4.5 cm, glabrous; rachis densely pubescent. Bract beneath each flower spatulate, basal part linear and pilose, apical part orbicular and glabrous or sparsely ciliate, small, apex rounded to acute. Filaments slightly longer than anthers. Fruit subglobose, ca. 3 mm in diam., tuberculate.

Locality: Tai Tam, Sha Tin, Tai Po, Sha Lo Tung, Tai Mei Tuk. P. S. Choi 133; HK Sheet 35615.
Distribution: Hebei, Henan, Shandong and regions S of Changjiang River; Japan, Philippines to Vietnam.
Ecology: Margins of ponds, ditches and other wet places. Flowering: Apr.–Jun., fruiting: Jun.–Jul.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Ma On Shan, Tai Mo Shan
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Peperomia blanda (Jacq.) Kunth 石蟬草
Nov. Gen. Sp. 1: 67, t. 3. 1816; FOC 4: 130. 1999.
Piper blandum Jacq., Collectanea 3: 211. 1789.
Peperomia dindygulensis Miq., Syst. Pip. 122. 1843; FKH 221. 1912, ‘dingdigulensis’; FRPS 20(1): 75, pl. 24: 5 –7. 1982; FGD 1: 75, fig. 80. 1987.
Peperomia leptostachya Hook. & Arn., Bot. Beechey Voy. 96. 1832.
Peperomia leptostachya f. cambodiana C. DC., Fl. Indo-chine 5: 64. 1910.
Peperomia leptostachya var. cambodiana (C. DC.) Merr., Lingnan Sci. J. 5: 58. 1927; FHN 1: 336. 1964. FGD 1: 75. 1987.

Herb, perennial, usually terrestial, (10 –)20 – 45(–50) cm tall, all parts pubescent. Stolons present, slender, leafless. Stems fleshy, often reddish. Petioles (5 –)10–15 mm; leaf blade elliptic-obovate, lowermost sometimes suborbicular, abaxial surface often reddish, 20 – 40(– 65) x 10 –20(– 40) mm, ± membranous when dried, base tapered to cuneate, apex rounded to subacute; veins 3(–5), glandular. Spikes terminal and from axils of uppermost leaves, sometimes fascicled, (3.5 –)5 – 8(–12) cm, flowers lax; peduncle 0.5 –1.5(–2) cm, rachis 2.5 –10 cm, (0.5 –)1–2 mm thick; bracts ± orbicular, ca. 0.8 mm wide, glandular– dotted. Filaments short, anther-cells rounded–“D”-shaped. Ovary obovoid, apex obtuse to emarginate. Nutlet sometimes on short conical pseudopedicels when fully ripe, globose to broadly ellipsoidal, 0.5– 0.8(–1.2) mm, obscurely papillate.

Locality: Ma On Shan, Tai Mo Shan. Y. S. Lau 1593; H. C. Tang 562 (HK).
Distribution: Taiwan, Fujian, Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan; Japan, India, Bangaladesh, Sri Lanka, Thailand, Myanmar, Cambodia, N Vietnam, Malaysia, Africa, S America.
Ecology: Forests and other wet places. Flowering: Apr.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Peperomia pellucida (L.) Kunth 草胡椒
Nov. Gen. Sp. 1: 64. 1815; FKH 221. 1912; FHN 1: 336. 1964; FRPS 20(1): 77, pl. 24: 8–9. 1982; FGD 1: 76, fig. 81. 1987; FOC 4: 130. 1999.
Piper pellucidum L., Sp. Pl. 1: 30. 1753.

Herb, annual, fleshy, 20–40 cm tall, all parts glabrous. Stems erect or ascending, branched. Petioles 1–2 cm; leaf blade membranous, broad-ovate or ovate-triangular, length ± equal to width, 10–35 mm, translucent, base cordate, apex acute or obtuse; veins 5–7. Spikes terminal or leaf-opposed, slender, 2– 6 cm. Flowers lax; bracts suborbicular, ca. 0.5 mm wide, stalk short. Anthers subglobose. Ovary ellipsoidal; stigmas pubescent. Nutlet globose, ca. 0.5 mm in diam.

Locality: Naturalized in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 2292; H. C. Tang 1362 (HK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian; native to tropical America, widely naturalized in tropical Africa and Asia.
Ecology: Shaded old walls and other wet places. Flowering: Apr.–Jul.

Piper austrosinense Y. C. Tseng 華南胡椒
Acta Phytotax. Sin. 17: 36, fig. 12. 1979; FRPS 20(1): 54. 1982; FGD 1: 68. 1987; FOC 4: 125. 1999.

Climber, woody, glabrous except for rachis and bracts. Petioles 0.4–2 cm; leaf blades ovate or ovate-lanceolate to lanceolate, 6–11 × 5 – 6 cm, base usually oblique, rounded or slightly cordate, apex acuminate. Flowers unisexual (plant dioecious) in leaf-opposed spikes. Male spikes white, 3– 6.5 cm, ca. 2 mm thick; peduncle 1–1.8 cm; rachis and abaxial surface of bracts densely white pubescent; bracts orbicular, ca. 1 mm wide, peltate, sessile. Stamens 2, filaments nearly as long as anthers. Female spikes white, 1–1.5 cm, ca. 3 mm thick; peduncle nearly as long as rachis; bracts as in male flowers. Ovary partly immersed in rachis; stigmas 3 or 4, tomentose. Drupe globose, red, ca. 3 mm in diam., partly immersed in rachis.

Locality: Kwun Yam Shan Tsuen. K. Y. Tam s.n. (HK Sheet 39789).
Distribution: E & SW Guangdong, SE Guangxi, Hainan.
Ecology: Forests, climbing on trees or rocks. Flowering: Apr–Jun.
Notes: This species when without fruits may be confused with Piper hancei, but can be easily distinguished by its white spikes.

Piper betle L. 蔞葉
Sp. Pl. 1: 28. 1753; FRPS 20(1): 42. 1982; FGD 1: 67, fig. 70. 1987; FOC. 4: 120. 1999.

Climber; stems rooted at nodes. Petioles 2–5 cm, very finely powdery pubescent; leaf blade papery to ± leathery, ovate to ovateoblong, 7–15 × 5–11 cm, base cordate, sometimes rounded in upper leaves, symmetrical or nearly so, apex acuminate, abaxially densely glandular, with very finely powdery pubescent veins, adaxially glabrous; veins 7, apical pair arising 0.7–2 cm above base, usually opposite. Flowers unisexual (plant dioecious) in leaf-opposed spikes. Male spikes nearly as long as leaf blades at anthesis; peduncle nearly as long as petioles; rachis pubescent; bracts orbicular or suborbicular, rarely obovate, 1–1.3 mm wide, peltate, ± sessile. Stamens 2, filaments thick, ca. as long as anthers or longer, anthers reniform. Female spikes 3 –5 cm, longer in fruit, ca. 1 cm thick; rachis fleshy, densely pubescent. Ovary partly immersed in and connate to rachis, apex tomentose; stigmas usually 4 or 5, lanceolate, tomentose. Drupes fused to form fleshy, reddish cylindrical mass; tips tomentose, prominent.

Locality: Cultivated. N. H. Li 117 (HK).
Distribution: Cultivated in S, SW & E China; India, Sri Lanka, Vietnam, Malaysia, Indonesia, Philippines, Madagascar.
Ecology: Flowering: May–Jul.
Uses: Social (masticatory), medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Authority: M. G. Gilbert & N. H. Xia
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Mount Gough, Victoria Peak, Tai Po Kau
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Piper cathayanum M. G. Gilbert & N. H. Xia 華山蔞（青蒟）
Novon 9: 191. 1999; FOC 4: 118. 1999.
Chavica sinensis Champ. ex Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 6: 116. 1854.
Piper sinense (Champ. ex Benth.) C. de Candolle, Prodr. 16(1): 361. 1868, non Piper chinense Miq., 1845; FHK 335. 1861; FKH 221. 1912; FRPS 20(1): 38, pl. 13: 7–11. 1982; FGD 1: 71, fig. 74. 1987.

Climber, to 5 m or longer. Petioles 10 –15 mm, densely pubescent; leaf blade papery, ovate, ovate-oblong, or oblong, 8–15 × 3.5 – 6.5 cm, base deeply cordate, basal lobes often overlapping, ± symmetrical, apex obtuse or acute, abaxially pubescent, especially along veins, adaxially glabrous or sparsely pubescent at base; veins 7, usually opposite, apical pair arising 0.5–1 cm above base. Flowers unisexual (plant dioecious) in leaf-opposed spikes. Male spikes 2.5 – 4 cm, 4 –5 mm thick; peduncle shorter than petioles, roughly pubescent, rachis glabrous; bracts orbicular, ca. 1.2 mm wide, peltate, glabrous, ± sessile. Stamens 2. Female spikes to 3 cm in fruit; rachis and bracts as in male flowers. Stigmas usually 3. Drupe globose, ca. 2.5 mm in diam., partly connate to rachis.

Locality: Mount Gough, Victoria Peak, Tai Po Kau. Y. S. Lau 593; Y. W. Lam 17.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan.
Ecology: Forests streamsides, often climbing on trees. Flowering: Mar.–Jun.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Victoria Peak, Hong Kong Island by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1850.

Piper hancei Maxim. 山蒟
Bull. Acad. Imp. Sci. Saint-Pétersbourg, sér. 3, 31: 94. 1887; FKH 221. 1912; FRPS 20(1): 60, pl. 19: 1–3. 1982; FGD 1: 69, fig. 72. 1987; FOC 4: 127. 1999.
Chavica leptostachya Hance, J. Bot. 6: 301. 1868, non Piper leptostachyon Nutt. 1822.
Piper matthewii Dunn, J. Bot. 47: 377. 1909; FKH 221. 1912.

Climber, glabrous except for rachis and bases of bracts. Petioles 0.5 –1.2 cm; leaf blade papery to ± leathery, ovate-lanceolate or elliptic, rarely lanceolate, 6 –12 × 2.5 – 4.5 cm, base gradually tapered or cuneate, sometimes rounded, symmetrical or nearly so, apex acute or acuminate; veins 5(–7), apical pair arising 1–3 cm above base, alternate, nearly reaching leaf apex. Flowers unisexual (plant dioecious) in leaf-opposed spikes. Male spikes yellow, 6–10 cm, ca. 2 mm thick; peduncle ca. as long as petioles or slightly longer, rachis pubescent; bracts suborbicular, ca. 0.8 mm wide, peltate, adaxially pilose, ± sessile to short stalked. Stamens 2. Female spikes ca. 3 cm, longer in fruit; bracts as in male spikes. Ovary subglobose, distinct; stigmas (3 or) 4. Drupe yellow, globose, 2.5–3 mm in diam.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. P. S. Choi 499; HK sheet 34040.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Guizhou, Yunnan, Fujian, Zhejiang.
Ecology: Forests, usually climbing on trees or rocks; Flowering: Mar.–Aug.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan, Sunset Peak
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Piper hongkongense C. DC 毛蒟
Prodr. 16: 347. 1868; FOC 4: 121. 1999.
Chavica puberula Benth., FHK 335. 1861.
Piper puberulum (Benth.) Maxim., Bull. Acad. Imp. Sci. Saint-petersbourg 31: 94. 1887, non (Benth.) Seemann, 1868; FKH 221. 1912; FHN 1: 332. 1964, p.p.; FRPS 20(1): 34. 1982; FGD 1: 70. 1987.

Climber. Young branches softly hairy, glabrescent. Petioles 5 –10 mm, densely pubescent; leaf blade papery, ovate-lanceolate or ovate, 5 –11 × 2– 6 cm, base ± cordate, apex acute or acuminate, usually asymmetrical, abaxially pubescent, mixed with a few dichotomous hairs, adaxially ± glabrescent; veins 5 –7, apical pair arising 1.5 –3 cm above base, alternate, others ± basal. Flowers unisexual (plant dioecious), in leaf-opposed spikes. Male spikes ca. 7 cm long, ca. 3 mm thick; peduncle slightly longer than petioles, pilose; bracts orbicular, sometimes slightly tapered, peltate, glabrous. Stamens usually 3, filaments very short, anthers reniform. Female spikes 4–6 cm; peduncle, rachis, and bracts as in male flowers. Ovary subglobose; stigmas 4. Drupe globose, ca. 2 mm in diam.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan, Sunset Peak. N. H. Li 22 (HK); HK Sheet 35607.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi.
Ecology: Thickets or forests, often climbing on trees or rocks; Flowering: Mar.–May.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Hong Kong Island by Seemann around 1850.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Castle Peak, Tai Mo Shan, Sha Tin, Fanling, Ma On Shan
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Piper sarmentosum Roxb. 假蒟
Fl. Ind. 1: 162. 1820; FKH 221. 1912; FHN 1: 332. 1964; FRPS 20(1): 42, pl. 14: 7–10. 1982; FGD 1: 68, fig. 71. 1987; FOC 4: 119. 1999.
Chavica hainana C. DC., Annuaire Conserv. Jard. Bot. Geneve 2: 275. 1898.
Chavica sarmentosa (Roxb.) Miq., Syst. Piperac. 242. 1843; FHK 335. 1861.

Perennial stoloniferous herb, most parts very finely powdery pubescent at least when young. Fertile stems ± erect. Petioles 2–5 cm; leaf blade membranous, toward base of stem ovate to suborbicular, those toward apex of stem smaller, ovate or ovate-lanceolate, 7–14 × 6–13 cm, base cordate to rounded, sometimes cuneate on uppermost branches, subsymmetrical, apex acute, finely glandular, abaxially finely powdery pubescent along veins, adaxially glabrous; veins 7, glaucous when dry, abaxially very prominent, apical pair arising 1–2 cm above base, reaching leaf apex; reticulation of veins conspicuous. Flowers unisexual (plant dioecious) in leaf-opposed spikes. Male spikes white, 1.5–2.5 cm, 2–3 mm thick; peduncle nearly as long as spikes, rachis pubescent; bracts transversely elliptic, 0.5–0.6 mm, peltate, ± sessile. Stamens 2, filaments ca. two times as long as anthers, anthers subglobose. Female spikes 6–8 cm, to 8 mm thick in fruit; peduncle as in male spikes, rachis glabrous; bracts suborbicular, peltate, 1–1.3 mm in diam. Stigmas 3–5, hispidulous. Drupe subglobose, 4-angled, 2.5–3 mm, partly connate to rachis.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Castle Peak, Tai Mo Shan, Sha Tin, Fanling, Ma On Shan.
Distribution: Fujian, Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang; India, Cambodia, Laos, Vietnam, Malaysia, Philippines, Indonesia.
Ecology: Forests and wet places near villages. Flowering: Apr.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Victoria Peak, High West, Ma On Shan, Tai Mo Shan
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Aristolochia championii Merr. & Chun 長葉馬兜鈴
Sunyatsenia 5: 47. 1940; FGD 1: 55, fig. 54. 1987; FRPS 24: 219, pl. 51: 7–9. 1988; FOC 5: 264. 2004.
Aristolochia longifolia Champ. ex Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 6: 116. 1854, non A. longlifolia Roxb., Fl. Ind. 3: 490. 1832; FHK 333. 1861; FKH 219. 1912.
Aristolochia compressicaulis Z. L. Yang in J. Wuhan Bot. Res., 6(1): 32. 1988, nom. inval.

Woody vine; tubers fusiform, 3–5 cm in diam. Stems terete, densely pubescent with rusty soft hairs. Petiole 1–2.5 cm, densely villous; leaf blade leathery, lanceolate or linear-lanceolate, 15–25 × 2.5–4.5 cm, base rounded or shallowly cordate, apex narrowly acuminate, entire, subglabrous adaxially, densely brown villous abaxially, veins pinnate, 5–10 pairs. Flowers solitary or in 2–5-flowered racemes. Pedicel 3–4 cm, pendulous, brown villous; bracts small, lanceolate. Perianth yellow, with reddish brown veins; tube geniculately curved, abaxially villous; limb discoid, 4–6 cm in diam., 3-lobed, adaxially papillate; lobes broadly rounded, slightly unequal. Anthers ellipsoid, ca. 3 mm. Gynostemium 3-lobed. Capsule ellipsoid, ca. 6 × 3 cm, dehiscing basipetally. Seeds ovoid, ca. 5 × 3 mm.

Locality: Victoria Peak, High West, Ma On Shan, Tai Mo Shan. Y. W. Lam 1631; HK Sheet 34401.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Sichuan, Guizhou, Yunnan.
Ecology: Thickets, thin forests. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.; fruiting: Aug.– Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The type specimen was collected in Victoria Peak by J. G. Champion in 1848 to 1849. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants in Hong Kong.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Victoria Peak, Tai Mo Shan, Sunset Peak, Lantau Peak
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Aristolochia fordiana Hemsl. 福氏馬兜鈴（通城虎）
J. Bot. 23: 286. 1885; FKH 219. 1912; FGD 1: 48, fig. 46. 1987; FRPS 24: 231, pl. 55: 5– 8. 1988; FOC 5: 266. 2004.

Herbaceous vine; tubers terete, slender. Stems 6-angled, glabrous. Petiole 2–4 cm, glabrous; leaf blade leathery or thinly leathery, ovatecordate or ovate-triangular, 10–12 × 5–8 cm, base cordate, apex long-acuminate, glabrous adaxially, densely puberulous abaxially, veins palmate, 5–7 from base, reticulation of veins conspicuous. Racemes 3- or 4-flowered, 3–5 cm, or flowers solitary. Pedicel ca. 0.8 cm; bracts subulate to lanceolate-ovate. Perianth yellowish green; tube rectilinear or slightly curved, abaxially glabrous; utricle globose, ca. 3.5 mm in diam., sessile; tube ca. 15 × 2 mm; limb unilateral, ligulate, ovate-oblong, 1–1.5 ×0.5 cm. Anthers ellipsoid, ca. 0.3 mm. Ovary ellipsoid, ca. 5 mm. Gynostemium 6-lobed. Capsule ellipsoid or obovoid, 1.5–2 cm in diam., dehiscing acropetally. Seeds ovoid, ca. 5 × 5 mm.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Tai Mo Shan, Sunset Peak, Lantau Peak. HK Sheet 10460, 34033.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian.
Ecology: Forest, thickets, crevices of rocks. Flowering: Mar.–Apr.; fruiting: May–Jul.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The type specimen was collected by A. B. Westland from Tai Mo Shan.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Po, Fanling, Ho Chung. Also cultivated
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Aristolochia tagala Chamisso 印度馬兜鈴（耳葉馬兜鈴）
Linnaea 7: 207, pl. 5, fig. 3. 1832; FKH 219. 1912; FGD 1: 50, fig. 47. 1987; FRPS 24: 243, pl. 60: 1–5. 1988; FOC 5: 269. 2003.
Aristolochia roxburghiana Klotzsch, Monatsber. Konigl. Preuss. Akad. Wiss. Berlin 1859: 596. 1859.

Herbaceous vine; tubers terete, more than 1 m, 3 –5 cm in diam. Stems terete, slightly furrowed, glabrous. Petiole 2–5.4 cm, glabrous; leaf blade papery, ovate-cordate or oblong-ovate, 8–12(–24) × 4–14(–20) cm, base deeply cordate, apex short-acuminate, both surfaces glabrous, veins palmate, 5 from base. Racemes 2- or 3-flowered, 2– 6 cm. Pedicels ca. 1 cm; bracts ovate-lanceolate. Perianth pale yellowish or greenish; tube rectilinear or slightly curved; utricle globose, 5– 8 mm in diam.; limb ligulate, oblong, 2–3 × 0.6 cm. Anthers ovoid, ca. 1 mm. Gynostemium 6-lobed. Capsule obovoid-globose to ovoid-cylindric, 3–5.5 × 2–3.5 cm, dehiscing acropetally. Seeds subcordiform, ca. 8 × 8 mm.

Locality: Tai Po, Fanling, Ho Chung. Also cultivated. P. S. Choi 399; HK Sheet 33864.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Taiwan; India, Vietnam, Malaysia, Philippines.
Ecology: Thickets. Flowering: May–Aug.; fruiting: Oct.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Deep Water Bay, Wong Nai Chung Gap, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Aristolochia thwaitesii Hook. f. 海邊馬兜鈴（田氏馬兜鈴）
Bot. Mag. 82: t. 4918. 1856; FKH 220. 1912; FGD 1:57, fig. 57. 1987; FRPS 24: 225. 1988; FOC 5: 265. 2003 .

Erect subshrub; tubers ellipsoid or terete, up to 10 cm or longer, ca. 7 cm in diam. Stems up to 70 cm, terete, villous. Petioles ca. 1 cm, villous; leaf blade leathery, spathulate, narrowly oblanceolate, or oblong-oblanceolate, 10–15 × 2.5–3 cm, base attenuate to subcuneate, apex acute to shortly acuminate, subglabrous adaxially, densely brown-villous abaxially, veins pinnate, 12–16 pairs. Racemes arising from the base of plant, 3–7-flowered, up to 8 cm. Pedicel ca. 3 cm, recurved, villous; bracts lanceolate, villous. Perianth yellow-green; tube geniculately curved, densely brown villous abaxially; basal portion of tube 1.5–2.5 × 0.5–1.0 cm; limb subcylindric to conic, symmetric, 1.5–3 cm in diam., 5– or 6– dentate. Anthers ellipsoid, ca. 2 mm. Gynostemium 3-lobed. Capsule ovoid-globose, 3.5 × 2–2.5 cm, dehiscing basipetally. Seeds ovoid, ca. 4 × 3 mm.

Locality: Deep Water Bay, Wong Nai Chung Gap, Lantau Island. W. J. Tutcher 8273; Y. W. Lam 1633.
Distribution: Guangdong.
Ecology: Thickets, bamboo forests and crevices of rocks. Flowering: Mar.–May; fruiting: Aug.–Sep.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: Listed in Rare and Precious Plants in Hong Kong.

Aristolochia westlandii Hemsl. 香港馬兜鈴（威氏馬兜鈴）
J. Bot. 23: 286. 1885; FKH 219. 1912; FGD 1: 54, fig. 53. 1987;FRPS 24: 217, pl. 51: 1–3. 1988; FOC 5: 263. 2003.

Woody vine; tubers fusiform, 3 –5 cm in diam., usually moniliform. Stems terete, densely villous. Petioles 1–1.5 cm, slightly hairy; leaf blade leathery or papery, narrowly lanceolate to narrowly oblong, 12–20 × 2–5 cm, base narrowly auriculate, apex acute, glabrous adaxially, sparsely villous abaxially, glaucous, veins pinnate, 8–12 pairs. Flowers solitary, axillary, on leafy shoots or on old woody stems. Pedicels pendulous, 7–12 cm, villous. Perianth yellow with purple veins and blotches, 10–15 cm; tube geniculately curved, villous abaxially; basal portion of tube 5–6 × 1.5–2 cm; limb discoid, 8–13 cm in diam., shallowly 3-lobed or emarginate; lobes broadly rounded, slightly unequal. Anthers ellipsoid, 4.5– 5 mm. Gynostemium 3-lobed. Capsule ovoid, hexagonous.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. Y. W. Lam 1639; HK Sheet 23776.
Distribution: Guangdong.
Ecology: Forests of valleys. Flowering: Mar.–Apr.
Notes: The type specimen was collected by A. B. Westland from Tai Mo Shan around 1880. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants in Hong Kong.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Authority: S. M. Hwang & T. P. Wong Siu
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Asarum hongkongense S. M. Hwang & T. P. Wong Siu 香港細辛
Acta Phytotax. Sin. 28: 406. 1990; FOC 5: 252. 2003.

Perennial herb. Rhizomes horizontal, ca. 3 mm in diam. Leaves solitary; petiole 12–30 cm, glabrous; leaf blade nearly leathery, ovate-cordate to ovate, 6 –11 × 5 – 8 cm, base deeply cordate, basal lobes semi-orbicular, apex acute or apiculate, margin entire, shining adaxially, both surfaces glabrous; basal veins 7, impressed adaxially and elevated abaxially. Peduncle ascending, 1.5–4 cm. Perianth purple-green, campanulate-urceolate, ca. 2 × 2.5 cm; perianth-lobes connate beyond attachment to ovary, glabrous abaxially; tube broadly ovoid to subglobose, ca. 1.5 × 1.5 cm, slightly constricted at throat, adaxially longitudinally papillate-rugose, orifice ring inconspicuous; lobes broadly ovate, ca. 1.5 × 1.2 cm, base with purple papillate-corrugate area; lateral lobes erect or spreading. Stamens 12; filaments much shorter than anthers; connectives slightly extended beyond anthers, obtuse. Ovary subsuperior; styles connate, apex with 6, erect, slightly 2-cleft arms; stigmas subterminal.

Locality: Sunset Peak. P. Chow s.n. (HK sheet 34402).
Distribution: Endemic to Hong Kong.
Ecology: Thickets on hillslopes. Flowering: Apr.–Jul.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The type specimen was collected by P. Chow from Lantau Island in 1983. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Illicium angustisepalum A. C. Sm. 大嶼八角
Sargentia 7: 36. 1947; FGD 2: 2. 1991; FRPS 30(1): 207. 1996.
Illicium spathulatum auct. non Y. C. Wu: Xing et al, Memoirs HK Nat. Hist. Soc. (23): 66. 2000 (excl. synonym); Check List HK Plants 50. 2002; 23. 2004.

Small tree; branchlets slender, angled, yellowish brown. Petioles 1–2.5 cm, narrowly winged adaxially. Leaves 4 – 6, pseudoverticillate on distal nodes, leathery, oblong-elliptic, (5.5–)7– 12 × (2–)2.5–4.2 cm, base attenuate, apex nearly acute to acuminate; midvein slightly elevated adaxially, prominent abaxially; lateral veins elevated on both surfaces or slightly impressed adaxially. Flowers axillary; peduncles 1.2–1.4 cm; tepals 22–24, membranous, largest one narrowly oblong, 1.4–1.5 × 0.3–0.35 cm, inner ones lanceolate; stamens ca. 24, 2.5 –2.8 mm, filaments 1.2–1.6 mm, anthers 1.1–1.3 mm; carpels 11–13, at anthesis, 3.5–4 mm; ovaries 1.3–1.7 mm, styles subulate, 2.2–2.5 mm. Fruit unseen.

Locality: Sunset Peak, Lantau Peak. L. T. Lo 656; Y. S. Lau 3232.
Distribution: Endemic to Hong Kong.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Feb.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Lantau Peak, Lantau Island in 1905 by U. On. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants in Hong Kong.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Wu Kau Tang, Bride's Pool, Nam Chung, Luk Keng
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Illicium dunnianum Tutcher 紅花八角（鄧氏八角）
J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 37: 62. 1905; FKH 28. 1912; FGD 2: 3, fig. 1. 1991; FRPS 30(1): 222. 1996.

Shrub, usually 1–2 m, rarely to 10 m tall. Young twigs slender. Leaves congested near twig apex, 3 –8 fascicled, or pseudo-verticillate, thinly leathery, narrowly lanceolate or narrowly oblanceolate, 5–12 × 0.8–1.2(–2.7) cm, base attenuate, decurrent to petioles and evidently forming narrow wings, apex abruptly caudate or acuminate; midvein slightly impressed adaxially, prominnet abaxially. Flowers solitary at axils or 2–3 fascicled in axils of apical leaves; peduncles slender, 1–3.5 cm; tepals 12–20, pink to red, purplish red, the largest elliptic to suborbicular, 0.6 –1.1 × 0.4 – 0.8 cm; stamens (19 –)24(–31), rarely 11, 1.7–3.3 mm; carpels 8–13, 2.5 –3.5 mm; ovaries 1.2–1.5 mm, styles 1.4–2 mm. Fruiting peduncles slender, 2–5.5 cm; fruit small, 1.5 –3 cm in diam.; follicles usually 7–8, rarely 13, 0.9 –1.5 × 0.4 × 0.2– 0.3 cm, with a subulate (3–5 mm), slightly curved acumen. Seeds small, 4 –5 × 2.5 –3.3 × 1.7–2.2 mm.

Locality: Wu Kau Tang, Bride's Pool, Nam Chung, Luk Keng. Y. S. Lau 1940; F. W. Xing 6965.
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Guizhou.
Ecology: Forests and streamsides. Flowering: Mar.–Jul. or Oct.–Nov.; Fruiting: Jul.– Oct.
Note: The type specimen was collected from Sam Tam Lo near Bride's Pool, New Territories in March 1903 by W. J. Tutcher.

Illicium leiophyllum A. C. Sm. 平滑葉八角（野八角）
Sargentia 7: 54. 1947; FGD 2: 3. 1991, quod specimen from Hong Kong; FRPS 30(1): 219. 1996.

Shrub, 3 – 4 m. Petioles 0.8 –1.7 cm. Leaves 3 –5 fascicled, leathery, oblong-elliptic, (6–)8 –13 × (2–)2.5–4 cm, base attenuate and decurrent to petioles, apex acuminate; midvein evidently impressed adaxially, prominent abaxially; lateral veins 6–9 on each side of midvein, impressed. Flowers axillary or subterminal, 2– 4 in clusters; peduncles thick and short when young; tepals 21–23, outer ones papery, margin membranous, inner ones fleshy, outermost 3 –4 suborbicular-triangular, 4 –5 × 4–5 mm; stamens 29 –30, filaments fleshy, connectives obtuse or slightly emarginate, thecae slightly protuberant; carpels 11–12, styles nearly as long as ovaries; fruiting peduncles 2–2.5 cm; follicles 11–12, 1.1–1.9 × 0.5 – 0.7 × 0.3–0.4 cm.

Locality: Mount Nicholson. W. J. Tutcher s.n. (Herb. Hongkong 4661); HK sheet 749, 755.
Distribution: Endemic to Hong Kong.
Ecology: On rock slits.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Mount Nicholson, Hong Kong Island in 1906 by W. J. Tutcher. It was misidentified as Illicium griffithii Hook. f. by Dunn & Tutcher (Kew Bull. Misc. Inform. Add. Ser. 10: 28. 1912) and Herklots (Hong Kong Nat. 4: 21. 1933).

Illicium micranthum Dunn 小花八角
Icon. Pl. 28: pl. 2714. 1901; FRPS 30(1): 228. 1996.
Illicium wangii Hu, Bull. Fan. Mem. Inst. Biol. 10: 120. 1940.

Shrub or small tree, up to 10 m tall. Petioles slender, 0.4–1.2 cm. Leaves irregularly alternate or subopposite, or 3–5 fascicled towards apex of branchlets, leathery or thinly leathery, obovate-elliptic, narrowly oblong-elliptic, 4 –11 × 1.3 – 4 cm, base cuneate, apex usually caudate-acuminate or acuminate, with minute glands on both sufaces (visible under hand lens); midvein impressed adaxially, decurrent to petioles and forming a broad furrow. Flowers very small, fragrant, solitary in axils of leaves or several pseudoverticillate near apex of branchlets, young flowers greenish white; peduncles slender, 0.7–2.8 cm; tepals red or orange-red 14–17(–21), inconspicuously pelluciddotted, the largest elliptic, 5 – 8 × 3.5 – 8 mm; stamens 10 –12, rarely 8, 2.5 –3.5 mm; carpels 7– 8, 2.3 –3.2 mm; ovaries 1.3 –1.7 mm, styles 1–1.5 mm. Fruiting peduncles up to 2.8–3.5 cm; follicles 6–8, 1.7–2.1 cm in diam., single one 0.9–1.4 × 0.3–0.7 × 0.2–0.35 cm, acumen short, 0.5 –3 mm. Seeds 4.5 –5 × 3 –3.5 × 2 mm.

Locality: Mount Gough, Ma On Shan. P. S. Choi 284; F. W. Xing 7481.
Distribution: Hubei, Hunan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Sichuan, Guizhou, Yunnan.
Ecology: Thickets and forests. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.; Fruiting: Jul.–Sep.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Victoria Peak, Pak Ngan Shek (Kadoorie Farm), Lamma Island (Sok Kwu Wan)
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Kadsura coccinea (Lem.) A. C. Sm. 黑老虎
Sargentia 7: 166. 1947; R. M. K. Saunders, Syst. Bot. Monogr. 54: 41– 46. 1998 & Sp. Pl. 4: 32–34. 2001.
Kadsura chinensis Hance ex Benth., FHK 8. 1861, p.p.

Woody vine, glabrous. Petiole (9–)10–30(–41) mm; leaf blade papery to leathery, elliptic, rarely ovate-elliptic or ovate, 7–16(–19) × 2.5–7.5(–10) cm, base acute (younger leaves) to obtuse (older), rarely truncate, apex acute to short acuminate, rarely obtuse, margin entire, rarely denticulate with 1–17 teeth; secondary veins (3–)5–8(–12) pairs. Flowers borne solitary in axils of leaves, often at base of short shoot. Flowering peduncle (4.5–)7–38 mm. Receptacle elongate-conical. Tepals (8–)10–16(–24), white with red tips, or entirely (purple-) red (occasionally yellowish); outermost tepal ovate, 1–4 × 1.5–4.5 mm; innermost tepal variably ovate to oblong to obovate, (5–)7.5–19.5 × 2–5.5 mm; largest tepal variably ovate to oblong to obovate, (8–)12–23 × 6–12(–15) mm. Staminate flowers with androecium of (10–)20–50 essentially free stamens; distal apex of receptacle with 0–14(–22) sterile (occasionally partly fertile) staminodes. Pistillate flowers with gynoecium of 20–68 carpels; pseudostyle narrow, subulate, without pseudostigma. Fruit of up to 60 apocarps, ripening red or purple-red, apocarps ca. 14–24 × 7–17 mm. Fruiting peduncle 26–49 mm long. Seeds 1–2 per apocarp, pyriform, 10–18 × 7.5–11 mm.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Pak Ngan Shek (Kadoorie Farm), Lamma Island (Sok Kwu Wan). L. T. Lo 315; HK sheet 33466; S. Y. Hu 13701 (A, IBSC); R. M. K. Saunders & H. P. Y. Ho 96/1 (HKU).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi; Myanmar, Vietnam.
Ecology: Semi-open shrubland and forests. Flowering: May– Jul.; fruiting: Oct.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal, food (edible fruit).
Notes: The type specimen of Kadsura chinensis was collected by J. G. Champion in a ravine below Victoria Peak, Hong Kong Island around 1850.

Kadsura heteroclita (Roxb.) Craib 異形南五味子
Fl. Siam. 1: 28. 1925 (“1931”); R. M. K. Saunders, Syst. Bot. Monogr. 54: 46 –54. 1998 & Sp. Pl. 4: 35 –37. 2001.
Uvaria heteroclita Roxb., Hort. Bengal. 43. 1814.

Woody vine, glabrous. Petiole (7–)10 –20(–29); leaf blade ± papery to subleathery, elliptic, rarely ovate-elliptic, (6.5 –)7.5 – 13.5(–16) × (2.5–)3.5–6.5(–9.5) cm, base cuneate to obtuse, often short-attenuate, apex acute to (short) acuminate; margin entire, to denticulate, 0(–11) teeth per margin; secondary veins 5 –9(–16) pairs. Flowers borne solitary in axils of leaves, occasionally with secondary flower borne in axil of bract. Flowering peduncle (1.5–)3–33(–35) mm. Receptacle subglobose. Tepals 10–17(–25), white, cream or yellow; outermost tepal ovate, 1–2.5(– 8) × 1.5 – 4(– 9) mm; innermost tepal elliptic to ovate (rarely obovate), (2–)3.5 –10.5 × (1–)2–7 mm; largest tepal elliptic to ovate (rarely obovate), 4.5 –20.5 × (3.5 –)4.5 –12(–15) mm. Staminate flowers with androecium of 40– 62(–74) stamens, anthers ± sessile, closely appressed in subglobose to ellipsoid head, 2–4.5 mm in diam., connectives broader than thick, with lateral thecae so that thecae of adjacent stamens contiguous. Pistillate flowers with gynoecium of 28–72 carpels; pseudostigma broad, subpeltate. Fruit of ca. 33–41 (or more) apocarps, ripening red, apocarps ca. (7–)10 –22 × (6 –)8 –10(–15) mm. Fruiting peduncle ca. 14– 46 mm long. Seeds 1–2(–11) per apocarp, pyriform, discoid or reniform, 4 –5.5(–7.5) × 4.5 – 7 mm.

Locality: Pat Sin Leng, Lantau Island. L. T. Lo 212; Y. W. Lam 1696; R. M. K. Saunders & G. Hao 96/2 (HKU).
Distribution: Fujian, Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Hunan; Vietnam, Thailand, Laos, Bangladesh, India, Sri Lanka, Malesia.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: May–Aug.; fruiting: Aug.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal.

Nelumbo nucifera Gaertn. 蓮（荷花）
Fruct. Sem. Pl. 1: 73. 1788; FHN 1: 311, fig. 152. 1964; FRPS 27: 3. 1979; FOC 6: 114. 2001.

Aquatic plant. Rhizome 1–5 m, with many constricted nodes and stout internodes, bearing many scale-like leaves and foliage leaves. Foliage leaves peltate, without sinus; petioles 1–2 m, with scattered small prickles; leaf blade almost orbicular, 25–100 cm in diam., glabrous and ± glaucous. Flowers solitary and terminal, 16 –23 cm in diam., pink or white, scented. Pedicels as long as or longer than petioles, also prickly. Nuts ellipsoid or ovoid, 1.7 × 1.3 cm, exocarp leathery.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 1348, 40214.
Distribution: Asia-temperate, Indian Subcontinent, Indochina, Malesia, Australia, E Europe; naturalized elsewhere.
Ecology: In ponds or paddy fields.
Uses: Ornamental, food (nut, rhizomes).

Nymphaea lotus L. var. pubescens (Willd.) Hook. f. & Thom. 柔毛齒葉睡蓮
Fl. Brit. India 1: 114. 1872; FOC 6: 117. 2001.
Nymphaea pubescens Willd., Sp. Pl. 2: 1154. 1799.

Aquatic herb. Rhizomes erect, producing slender stolons. Leaves papery, suborbicular, 20 –40(–65) cm in diam., base deeply cordate, basal lobes subparallel or slightly spreading, margin with acute to subspinose teeth, adaxially glabrous, abaxially pubescent on the strongly raised veins. Flowers emergent, usually 15 –25 cm in diam.; sepals 4, abaxial surface green to purplish, conspicuously veined, adaxial surface white or red, oblong, 10–11 × 3 – 4 cm; petals 20–25, white or red, oblong to oblong-oblanceolate, 7–10 × 1.5 –3.5 cm decaying after anthesis; stamens numerous, shorter than the petals; filaments dilated at base; anther connectives apically unappendaged; ovary crowned by 15 –20 radiating furrowed stigmas. Fruit ovoid to subglobose, 3.5 –5 cm in diam.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 1324.
Distribution: S & SE Asia. Cultivated elsewhere in tropics and subtropics.
Ecology: Freshwater ponds. Flowering: Jun.–Dec. Flowers open from late evening till next noon.
Uses: Ornamental.

Nymphaea nouchali N. L. Burm. 延藥睡蓮
Fl. Ind. 120. 1768; FOC 6: 118. 2001.

Aquatic herb. Rhizomes erect, unbranched. Leaves papery, suborbicular, (15 –)20 – 40(–50) cm in diam., base deeply cordate, basal lobes parallel or slightly overlapping, margin subentire or with irregular and broadly triangular teeth, glabrous, secondary nerves raised abaxially, reticulation inconspicuous. Flowers emergent, usually 8–15 cm in diam.; sepals 4, leathery, broadly lanceolate, 6–10 × 3 –3.8 cm, abaxial surface green and shining, adaxial surface blue-violet, persistent; petals 20–25(–30), blue-violet, broadly lanceolate, 6 –9 × 2–3.8 cm; stamens numerous, shorter than the petals; filaments dilated at base; anther connectives apically appendaged; ovary crowned by 15 –25 radiating furrowed stigmas. Fruit globose, 1.5 – 4.5 cm in diam.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 1318.
Distribution: E & W Asia, Indochina, Indian Subcontinent, Malesia, Australia. Cultivated elsewhere in tropics and subtropics.
Ecology: Freshwater ponds. Flowering: Jun.–Dec. Flowers open in the morning till evening.
Uses: Ornamental.

Ceratophyllum demersum L. 金魚藻
Sp. Pl. 992. 1753; FRPS 27: 16, fig. 6. 1979.

Submerged perennial herb. Stems 40–50 cm, branched. Leaves 4 –12 in whorls, once or twice forked, segments filiform or linear, 15–20 × 0.1–0.5 mm, finely toothed on one side, apex with whitish cartilaginous tip. Bracts 9 –12, linear, 1.5 –2 mm, pale green, translucent, 3-toothed and with purplish hairs at apex. Stamens 10–16, ± congested. Ovary ovoid; style subulate. Achenes broadly ellipsoid, 4 –5 × 1.5 –2 mm, with 3 spines.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 26750, 26752.
Distribution: Cosmopolitan.
Ecology: Ponds and streams, in still or slow fresh water; also cultivated in aquarium as an ornamental plant.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Hang, Tai Po, Luk Keng
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Clematis chinensis Osbeck 威靈仙
Dagb. Ostind. Resa 205, 242. 1757; FRPS 28: 161. 1980; FTW ed. 2, 2: 581, pl. 240. 1996; FOC 6: 356. 2001; FGD 5: 15. 2003.
Clematis sinensis Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 345. 1790.

Woody climber, turning black in drying. Stems and branches almost glabrous or sparsely puberulous. Leaves pinnate; petioles 3.5 –6 cm; leaflets 3–7, usually 5, papery, ovate to lanceolate, 2.5 –5 × 1–1.8 cm, base broadly cuneate, rounded or shallowly cordate, apex acute to acuminate, rarely emarginate, margin entire, subglabrous. Panicles axillary or terminal, many-flowered. Flowers 1–2 cm in diam. Sepals 4(–5), white, spreading, oblong to oblong-obovate, 8 –10 × 2–3 mm, apex apiculate, densely white-pubescent at margin on abaxil surface. Stamens glabrous; anthers 2 times longer than filaments. Achenes compressed, 3–7, ovoid to broadly ellipsoid, persistent styles 2–5 cm, feathery.

Locality: Tai Hang, Tai Po, Luk Keng. H. C. Tang 2033; Ross s.n. (HK sheet 29).
Distribution: SE, C to SW China; Vietnam.
Ecology: Thickets and grassy slopes. Flowering: Jun.–Sep.; fruiting: Aug.–Nov.

Clematis crassifolia Benth. 厚葉鐵線蓮
FHK 7. 1861; FKH 26. 1912; FHN 1: 307. 1964; FRPS 28: 178, pl. 53. 1980; FTW ed. 2, 2: 518, pl. 241. 1996; FOC 6: 353. 2001; FGD 5: 14. 2003.

Woody climber, glabrous with exception of the flowers. Leaves ternately compound; leaflets leathery, oblong elliptic or ovate, 7–10 × 3–5 cm, base cuneate to broadly cuneate, apex acute or obtuse, margin entire, 3-nerved. Inflorescences paniculate, axillary or terminal, many-flowered. Flowers 2.4–5 cm in diam. Sepals 4, spreading, white or tinged with red, lanceolate to oblanceolate, 1.2–2 × 0.2– 0.5 cm, densely pubescent at margin and on adaxial surface. Stamens glabrous, anthers ellipsoid, ca. 2 mm; filaments 3 –5 times longer than the anthers. Achenes narrowly ovoid, puberulent; persistent style 1.2–2 cm feathery.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island. H. C. Tang 2127; Y. S. Lau 817; HK sheet 40220.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan.
Ecology: Forests in ravine. Flowering: Dec.–Jan.; fruiting: Feb.–Mar.
Notes: The type specimens was collected from Victoria Peak, Hong Kong Island by C. Wilford around 1858.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Ha Hang, Fanling, Fung Yuen, Lin Ma Hang
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Clematis loureiroana DC. 絲鐵線蓮（甘木通、長毛鐵線蓮）
Syst. Nat. 1: 144. 1817; FOC 6: 369. 2001.
Clematis filamentosa Dunn, J. Bot. 47: 197. 1909; FKH 26. 1912; FRPS 28: 233, pl. 78: 1– 6. 1980; FGD 5: 12. 2003.

Woody climber, glabrous with exception of the inflorescence. Leaves ternate; petioles 4 –10 cm; leaflets thinly leathery, ovate to lanceolate, 7–11 × 4– 8 cm, base rounded to subcordate, apex obtusely rotund, margin entire, 5-palmately veined; petiolules 2–5 cm. Racemes axillary, usually 5–7-flowered; pedicels 3 – 4 cm, initially brown pubescent near apex, glabrescent; bracts linear lanceolate; sepals 4, white, narrowly ovate to ovate-lanceolate, 13 –20 × 4–6 mm, spreading, rusty pubescent abaxially, glabrous adaxially. Stamens glabrous; connectives prolonged, 1–2 times longer than the anthers; staminodes broadly linear, glabrous. Achenes narrowly ovoid, brown, 10 × 2 mm, pubescent; persistent style 3–5 cm, filiform, villose.

Locality: Ha Hang, Fanling, Fung Yuen, Lin Ma Hang. Y. S. Lau 2827, 2848; HK sheet 76.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Yunnan.
Ecology: Thickets by streams and in valleys. Flowering: Nov.–Dec.; fruiting: Jan.–Feb.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Ha Hang near Tai Po by S. T. Dunn in January in 1904.

Clematis meyeniana Walp. 毛柱鐵線蓮（甘草藤）
Nov. Actorum Acad. Caes. Leop.-Carol. Nat. Cur. 19 (suppl.1): 297. 1843; FHK 6. 1861; FKH 26. 1912; FHN 1: 306. 1964; FRPS 28: 171, pl. 22. 1980; FTW ed. 2, 2: 532, pl. 249. 1996; FOC 6: 354. 2001; FGD 5: 14. 2003.
Clematis oreophila Hance ex Walp., Ann. Bot. Syst. 2: 3. 1851.

Woody climber. Leaves ternate; leaflets subleathery, ovate to oblong-ovate, sometimes broad-ovate, 4.5 –11.5 × 1.5– 6 cm, base rounded, broadly cuneate or sometimes cordate, apex acute, acuminate, or obtusely acute, margin entire, glabrous on both surfaces, 3 –5-nerved. Panicles axillary or terminal, loose and many-flowered. Flowers white, 1.5 –2 cm in diam. Sepal 4, spreading, oblong to lanceolate, 7–12 × 3–4 mm, pubescent only on the margin of abaxil surface. Stamens glabrous; anthers slightly longer than the filaments. Achenes narrowly falcate-ovoid, or narrowly obovoid, pubscent; persistent style up to 2.5 cm, feathery.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 341; N. H. Li 131; S. Y. Hu & P. P. H. But 24064.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou,Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Laos, Vietnam, Japan.
Ecology: Thicket in ravines. Flowering: Jun.–Aug.; fruiting: Sep.– Oct.
Notes: The type specimen of this species was collected near Kap Shui Mun by F. J. F. Meyen in 1831.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Victoria Peak, Ma On Shan, Tai Mo Shan
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Clematis meyeniana Walp. var. granulata Finet & Gagnep. 沙葉鐵線蓮
Bull. Soc. Bot. France 50: 530. 1903; FHN 1: 307. 1964; FRPS 28: 173. 1980; FOC 6: 355. 2001.

Differs from C. meyeniana var. meyeniana by the leaflets being finely tuberculate on abaxial surface.
Locality: Victoria Peak, Ma On Shan, Tai Mo Shan. H. C. Tang 547, 1804.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; Laos, Vietnam.
Ecology: Thickets and margins of forests. Flowering: May–Aug.; fruiting: Jul.–Sep.

Clematis parviloba Gardner & Champ. 裂葉鐵線蓮（小裂鐵線蓮）
Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 1: 241. 1849; FHK 6. 1861; FKH 26. 1912; FRPS 28: 180, pl. 54. 1980; FTW ed. 2, 2: 532, pl. 251. 1996; FOC 6: 351. 2001 ; FGD 5: 16. 2003.
Clematis pierotii Miq., Ann. Mus. Bot. Lugduno-Batavum 3: 1. 1867.

Subshrubby climber, stem and branches loosely clothed with short silky hairs. Leaves mostly twice ternate; leaflets papery, ovatelanceolate or oblong-ovate, 1.5 – 6 × 0.8 –2.3 cm, base rounded, apex acuminate, entire or coarsely serrate, appressed pubescent on both surfaces, 3-nerved. Panicles few flowered and leafy, axillary or terminal; pedicels 1–2.5 cm. Flowers 1.5–3.5 cm in diam. Sepals 4, white, sublanceolate to narrow obovate, 8 –20 × 3 –7 cm, densely covered with silky hairs abaxially. Stamens glabrous, anthers ca. 2 mm, much shorter than filaments. Achenes ovoid, ca. 4 × 3 mm, pubescent, persistent styles ca. 4 cm, feathery.

Locality: Hong Kong Island. H. C. Tang 1542, 1764; C. P. Lau 115.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Taiwan; Japan.
Ecology: Thickets and margins of forests. Flowering: May– Jun.; fruiting: Jul.–Sep.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from West Point, Hong Kong Island by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1850.

Clematis uncinata Champ. 柱果鐵線蓮（鉤葉鐵線蓮）
Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 3: 255. 1851; FHK 6. 1861; FKH 26. 1912; FRPS 28: 165. 1980; FTW ed. 2, 2: 544, pl. 257: 1–9. 1996; FOC 6: 359. 2001; FGD 5: 15. 2003.
Clematis uncinata var. floribunda Hayata, J. Coll. Sci. Univ. Tokyo 30: 18. 1911, & Icon. Pl. Formosan. 7: 20. 1911.
Clematis uncinata var. biternata W. T. Wang in L. K. Fu et al, Higher Plants of China 3: 374. 2000.

Subshrubby climber, turning black in drying. Leaves pinnate; leaflets 5 –15, thin leathery, broad-ovate, ovate to lanceolate, 5–11 × 1.5 –5 cm, base broadly cuneate, sometimes cordate or truncate, apex acuminate to acute, with a short hooked point, margin entire and ± thickened, glabrous, shining adaxially, 3-nerved at the base. Panicles axillary or terminal, many-flowered. Sepals 4, white, linear lanceolate to oblanceolate, 10 –17 × 2–3 mm, white-pubescent on the margin. Stamens glabrous; anthers linear, much longer than filaments. Achenes cylindric, terminating in awn-shaped feathery persistent style.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Shing Mun. L. T. Lo 146; W. J. Tutcher 4676; Y. S. Lau 998.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Gansu, Shaanxi, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Thickets and margins of forests in ravine. Flowering: Apr.–Jul.; fruiting: Sep.– Oct.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Mount Parker, Hong Kong Island by J. G. Champion in 1848.

Ranunculus cantoniensis DC. 禺毛茛（小回回蒜、自扣草）
Prodr. 1: 43.1842; FRPS 28: 321, pl. 99: 1–3. 1980; FTW ed. 2, 2: 550, pl. 260. 1996; FOC 6: 428. 2001; FGD 5: 22. 2003.
Ranunculus pensylvanicus auct. non L.: FKH 27. 1912.

Perennial herb. Stems erect, 20–50 cm tall, branched at the upper part, densely yellowish white hirsute. Basal leaves ternate; petioles 4.5–12 cm, hirsute; central leaflet stalked, elliptic or rhomboid 3–4.6 × 2–3.5 cm, 3-lobed or 3-parted, serrate, sparsely strigose on both surfaces; lateral leaflets unequally 2-parted, short-stalked or sessile; lower cauline leaves similar to the basal leaves, upper ones gradually reduced. Flowers terminal, solitary or in few-flowered cymes. Pedicels 2–5 cm, hirsute. Sepals ovate, ca. 3 mm. Petals 5, yellow, elliptic, 5–6 × 2–3 mm, base clawed. Stamens numerous, anthers ca. 1 mm. Receptacles oblong, white puberulous. Aggregate fruits subglobose, ca. 1 cm in diam.; achenes compressed, glabrous.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Sha Tin. H. C. Tang 801; Y. S. Lau 1241.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Vietnam, Korea, Japan.
Ecology: Wet places, ditches, paddy fields. Flowering: Mar.–Sep.; fruiting: Apr.–Jun.

Ranunculus sceleratus L. 石龍芮
Sp. Pl. 1: 551. 1753; FKH 27. 1912; FRPS 28: 310, pl. 96: 1–4. 1980; FTW ed. 2, 2: 560, pl. 267. 1996; FOC 6: 421. 2001; FGD 5: 21. 2003.
Hecatonia palustris Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 303. 1790.

Annual herb. Stems erect, 10–40 cm tall, branched above middle, glabrous or nearly so. Basal leaves long petioled, simple, pentagonous or reniform in outline, 1–4 × 1.5–5 cm, base broadly cordate, 3-partite; central lobes obovate-cuneate, apex obtuse, indistinctly 3-lobed, margin coarsely margin coarsely dentate, glabrous; lateral lobes obliquely fan-shaped, unequally 2-lobed. Petioles 3 –15 cm subglabrous. Cauline leaves many, lower ones similar to basal leaves, upper ones smaller, 3-divided, sparsely pubescent on abaxial surface. Cymes terminal, many-flowered. Flowers 4–8 mm in diam. Pedicels 1–2(– 3) cm, glabrous or sparsely pubescent. Sepals elliptic, 2–3.5 mm, puberulous abaxially. Petals 5, yellow, narrowly obovate, ca. 3.5 mm, base shortly clawed. Stamens 10 or more, ca. 2 mm. Receptacles cylindric, sparsely puberulous. Aggregate fruits oblong, 8–12 mm; achenes numerous, obovoid, slightly compressed, glabrous.

Locality: New Territories. H. C. Tang 2466; Y. S. Lau 2457.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China and in subtropical and temperate regions of the N hemisphere.
Ecology: Wet places, near ponds, ditches and in paddy fields. Flowering: Jan.–Jun.; fruiting: Mar.–Jun.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Ma On Shan, Sunset Peak, Lantau Peak
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Thalictrum acutifolium (Hand.-Mazz.) Boivin 尖葉唐松草（白蓬草）
Rhodora 46: 364. 1944; Ico. Cor. Sin. 1: 677. 1972; FRPS 27: 553. 1979; FOC 6: 285. 2001; FGD 5: 19. 2003.
