Thalictum clavatum auct. non DC.: FKH 26. 1912.
Thalictrum clavatum DC. var. acutifolium Hand.-Mazz., Akad. Wiss. Wien, Math.-Naturwiss. Kl., Anz. 43: 1. 1926.

Perennial herb, 20–40 cm tall, glabrous. Roots fleshy, carrotshaped, to 4 mm in diam. Basal leaves 2–3, long petiolate, biternate; terminal leaflets long stalked, ovate, 1–1.4 × 0.8–3.5 cm, base rounded, broadly cuneate or cordate, apex acute or obtuse, entire or obscurely lobed, margin sparsely dentate, glaucous abaxially; lateral leaflets smaller; petiolule ca. 1.2 cm. Cauline leaves smaller, shortly petiolate. Cymes lax-flowered. Flowers small, ca. 8 mm in diam. Sepals 4, ovate, ca. 2 mm, white or pinkish, caducous. Stamens numerous, ca. 5 mm; anthers oblong, 0.8–1.3 mm; filaments distally oblanceolate, ca. 3 times as broad as anthers, base filiform. Carpels 6–12, stalked; styles short. Achenes compressed, narrowly oblong, sometimes slightly falcate, 3–4 × 0.6–1.2 mm, longitudinally 8-ribbed.

Locality: Ma On Shan, Sunset Peak, Lantau Peak. Y. S. Lau 1401; P. S. Choi 36.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian.
Ecology: Ravines, margins of forests. Flowering and fruiting: Apr.–Jul.

Mahonia oiwakensis Hayata 海島十大功勞
Icon. Pl. Formosan. 6: 1. 1916; Li, Woody Fl. Taiwan 175. 1963; FTW ed. 2, 2: 583, pl. 279, photo 254 –255. 1996; FRPS 29: 220, pl. 42. 2001.
Berberis nepalensis auct. non Spreng.: FKH 32. 1912.
Mahonia hainanensis C. M. Hu et al., Guihaia 14 (1): 18. 1994.

Evergreen shrub, 1–7 m tall. Leaves crowded at apex of stems, odd-pinnate, narrowly oblong-elliptic in outline, 15 – 42 × 8 –15 cm; leaflets 12–20 pairs, sessile, ovate-lanceolate or lanceolate, 2–10 × 1–2.5 cm, base rounded, apex acute to acuminate, margin with 2–9 spinulose teeth on each side, adaxially dark green, abaxially yellowish green; terminal leaflet petiolulate or sometimes sessile. Racemes fascicled, upright, 9 –25 cm. Pedicels (2–)5 – 6 mm. Flowers golden yellow, outer perianth-segments ovate to elliptic, inner ones oblong, 4.5 – 6.5 × 22.7 mm, with 2 glands at the base, apex bilobed; stamens 3 – 4 mm; ovary 3 – 4 mm, with 2–3 ovules; style very short. Fruit ovoid, 5 – 6 mm in diam., blue to blue-black, white-farinose.

Locality: Sunset Peak. Y. S. Lau 2812; L. T. Lo 328.
Distribution: Taiwan, Hainan, Guizhou, Sichuan, Yunnan, Xizang.
Ecology: Forests by streams. Flowering: Jun.–Sep.
Notes: Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Nandina domestica Thunb. 南天竺
Fl. Jap. 9. 1784; Forb. & Hemsl., J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 23: 32. 1886; FGZ 98. 1956; FGD 3: 15. 1995; FRPS 29: 52, pl. 11. 2001.

Evergreen shrub, 1.5 –2 m tall, glabrous throughout. Stems tufted, unbranched. Leaves twice or thrice pinnate, 30 –50 cm; petioles sheathed and semi-amplexicaul at the base, rachis articulate; pinnae opposite; leaflets subsessile, thinly leathery, lanceolate to ellipticlanceolate, 1.5– 4(–7) × 0.8 –1.5 –2 cm, base cuneate, apex acute, apiculate, margin entire. Panicles terminal, erect, 13 –25 cm; pedicels 3 –5 mm. Sepals many, greenish, scarious, the lowest small, triangular, ca. 1 mm, upper ones larger, ovate to ovate-elliptic, to 4.5 mm. Petals 6, white, sub-scarious, elliptic, 6–7.5 × 3–3.5 mm. Stamens 6, rarely 7, subsessile, 4.5–5 mm, yellow. Ovary urceolate, about the length of the stamens; style very short. Fruit a globular berry, scarlet, ca. 8 mm in diam.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. HK sheet 32807; Y. S. Lau 1902.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Yunnan, Hunan, Hubei, Shaanxi, Henan, Shandong, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian; Japan.
Ecology: The plant shrives in calcareous soil, but also grows well in acid soil. Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: Nov. to Feb. of the following year.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Mount Parker, Wong Nai Chung, Ng Tung Chai
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Sargentodoxa cuneata (Oliv.) Rehd. & Wils. 大血藤
Sargent, Pl. Wils. 1: 351. 1913; FGD 4: 56, fig. 34. 2000; FRPS 29: 305. 2001; FOC 6: 454. 2001.
Holboellia cuneata Oliv., Hooker's Icon. Pl. 19: t. 1817. 1889.

Twining woody vine. Bark on old stems longitudinally fissured; branches reddish brown, glabrous. Leaves alternate, ternate; petioles 5 –10 cm. termianal leaflets rhomboid-obovate, 4 –14 × 3 –9 cm, base cuneate, apex acute; petiolules 5 –10 mm; lateral leaflets larger, obliquely ovate, bilaterally asymmetrical, subsessile. Racemes pendulous, 8 –15 cm, many-flowered. Flowers yellow or yellowish green, fragrant. Pedicels 1–1.5 cm, with an oblong bract at base and 2 linear alternate bracteoles near middle. Male flowers: sepals 6, narrowly oblong, 6 –10 × 2– 4 mm, margin slightly involute; nectariform petals very small, rhomboid-orbicular, ca. 1.2 mm; stamens ca. 4 mm; vestigial carpesl linear, ca. 1 mm. Female flowers: sepals and petals as in staminate flower; carpels numerous, spirally arranged on the globose receptalcle. Ripe carpel an ovoid berry, 7–10 mm in diam, dark blue and glaucous, usually 20 – 40 on the enlarged receptacle. Seeds black, ovoid, ca. 5 mm.

Locality: Mount Parker, Wong Nai Chung, Ng Tung Chai. W. J. Tutcher 8335; Y. S. Lau 1634.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, SE Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Hubei, Henan, Anhui, Jiangsu, Jiangxi, Zhejiang; Laos, Vietnam.
Ecology: Margins of forests, thickets on hillslopes and in ravines. Flowering: Spring.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Stauntonia elliptica Hemsl. 牛藤果
Hooker's Icon. Pl. 29: t. 2844. 1907; FGD 4: 50. 2000; FRPS 29: 28. 2001; FOC 6: 448. 2001.
Parvatia brunoniana (Wall.) Decaisne subsp. elliptica (Hemsl.) H. N. Qin, Cathaya 8–9: 61, fig. 36. 1997.

Woody twining shrub, glabrous throughout. Leaves trifoliate; petioles 10 –17 cm; leaflets elliptic, oblong to ovate-oblong or obovate, 3 –11 × 2–5 cm, base rounded, apex acute or obtuse, margin entire and slightly revolute, dark green adaxially, pale green abaxially; lateral nerves and veins raised on abaxial surface; petiolules 1–3 cm. Racemes several and fascicled in axils of leaves, with many pendent pale green to whitish flowers. Male flowers: pedicels 10 –12 mm; outer sepals ovate-elliptic, inner sepals lanceolate, 6–9 × 2–3 mm; nectariform petals ovate, 1–1.5 mm; stamens ca. 5 mm, connective apical appendages as long as anther. Female flowers: pedicels 18 –20 mm; sepals narrowly to linear lanceolate, 14 –15 × 2– 4 mm; staminodes ca. 1 mm; carpels 3, free, oblong, with elongated and pointed stigmas. Fruit ovoid or oblong, 4 –5 × 2– 4 cm.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. F. W. Xing 7226.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi.
Ecology: Thin forests and thickets. Flowering: May–Aug.; fruiting: Jun.–Dec.
Notes: The species was erroneously reported as Akebia trifoliate var. australis (Diels) Rehd. (Check List HK Plants 53. 2002).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Mount Parker, Mount Gough, Tai Mo Shan
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Stauntonia chinensis DC. 野木瓜
Syst. Nat. 1: 514. 1818; FHK 13. 1861; FKH 32. 1912; H. N. Qin, Cathaya 8–9: 151, fig. 67. 1997; FGD 4: 51, fig. 32. 2000; FRPS 29: 29, pl. 5: 1–7. 2001; FOC 6: 449. 2001.
Stauntonia hexaphylla auct. non Decaisne: FKH 32. 1912.

Woody twining shrub, glabrous throughout. Leaves digitate; petioles 5–10 cm; leaflets 5–7, leathery, oblong, elliptic or oblonglanceolate, 6–9(–11.5) × 2–4 cm, base obtuse, rounded or cuneate, apex acuminate, margin entire and ± thickened, adaxially dark green, abaxially paler and often maculate when young; reticulation of veins conspicuously raised on both surfaces; petiolules 6- 25 mm. Flowers usually 3–4 in corymbose-racemes; pedicels 2–3 cm. Male flowers: sepals 6, yellowish or cream white abaxially, purplish red adaxially, outer 3 lanceolate, ca. 18 × 6 mm, inner 3 linear lanceolate, ca. 16 × 3 mm; nectariform petals liguliform, ca. 1.5 mm; connective apical appendage as long as anther. Female flowers: sepals slightly larger than that of staminate flower; staminodes aciculiform, less than 1 mm; carpels 3, free, narrowly ellipsoid or oblong, with oblique capitate stigmas. Fruit oblong, 7–10 × 3 –5 cm.

Locality: Mount Parker, Mount Gough, Tai Mo Shan. Y. S. Lau 1745; HK sheet 1179, 39261.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian.
Ecology: Forests of hill slopes. Flowering: Mar.–Apr.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Authority: (Dunn) C. Y. Wu ex S. H. Huang
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Stauntonia decora (Dunn) C. Y. Wu ex S. H. Huang 翅野木瓜
FYN 2: 8. 1979; FGD 4: 50. 2000; FRPS 29: 26. 2001; FOC 6: 448. 2001.
Parvatia decora Dunn, Hooker's Icon. Pl. ser. 4, 8(1): t. 2712. 1901.

Stems, petioles and petiolules narrowly winged. Leaves trifoliate; petioles 3– 8 cm; leaflets leathery, elliptic, ovate, or oblong, 5–12 × 3 –7 cm, base rounded or broadly cuneate, apex acute to shortly acuminate, sometimes subrounded and mucronate, margin entire and slightly revolute, glabrous and shining adaxially, scurfy puberulous abaxially; lateral nerves and veins raised on abaxial surface; petiolules of terminal leaflets 2.5 –4 cm, lateral ones 1–1.5 cm. Racemes several to many, 1–2-flowered, fascicled in axils of leaves; peduncles 4–10 mm. Male flowers: pedicels 2.5–4 mm; outer sepals lanceolate, 20–25 × 5–6 mm, inner ones narrower, ca. 21 mm; petals lanceolate, ca. 2 mm; stamens 7–14 mm, connective apical appendage hornlike, equaling or longer than anther; pistillodes subulate. Female flowers similar to staminate flower; carpels 3, clavate, 6 –7 mm; stigmas lanceolate, reflexed. Fruit ellipsoid, 7– 8 × 2.5 –3.5 cm.

Locality: Ma On Shan. H. C. Tang 1175, 1928.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan.
Ecology: Open forests in ravines. Flowering: Oct.–Dec.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Mount Victoria, Mount Gough, Tai Mo Shan
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Stauntonia obovata Hemsl. 倒卵葉野木瓜
Hooker's Icon. Pl. ser. 4, 9: t. 2847, 1907; FKH 32. 1912; H. N. Qin, Cathaya 8–9: 130, fig. 56. 1997; FGD 4: 53. 2000; FRPS 29: 42, pl. 9: 10 –14. 2001; FOC 6: 452. 2001.
Holboellia obovata (Hemsl.) Chun, Sunyatsenia 1(4): 233. 1934.

Woody twining shrub, glabrous throughout. Leaves digitate; petioles slender, 2–6(–8) cm; leaflets 3–5(–6), leathery, very variable in size and shape, usually obovate, sometimes oblong or lanceolate, 3.5–6(–11) × 1.5–3(–6) cm, base cuneate to broadly cuneate, apex rounded, occasionally acute or acuminate, margin entire and ± revolute, adaxially dark green, abaxially glaucous; lateral veins 5 – 6 on each side of midvein, reticulation of veins obscure; petiolules 8–20 mm. Racemes 4–6 cm, 3–5 fascicled in axils of leaves. Pedicels 2– 4 cm. Male flowers: sepals 6, white, rarely yellowish white, outer 3 lanceolate, 10–11 × 3.5–4 mm, inner 3 linear, 6–10 × 1–1.5 mm; petals lacking; stamens ca. 3.5 mm, connectives slightly produced; vestigial carpels 3, very small. Female flowers: sepals as in staminate flower; carpels 3, free, stigmas capitate; staminodes squamiform, less than 0.5 mm. Fruit ellipsoid or ovoid, (3–)4–5(–6) × 2–2.5 cm.

Locality: Mount Victoria, Mount Gough, Tai Mo Shan. K. L. Yip 4139; Y. S. Lau 518, 2831.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangxu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan
Ecology: Margins of forests in ravines, by streams. Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: Sep.–Nov.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Hong Kong Island by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1849.

Cocculus orbiculatus (L.) DC. 木防己
Syst. Nat. 1: 523. 1817; Forman, Kew Bull. 22: 372–374. 1968; FGD 1: 37, fig. 38. 1987; FRPS 30(1): 32, pl. 7: 1– 8. 1996.
Menispermum orbiculatus L., Sp. Pl. 341. 1753.
Menispermum trilobus Thunb., Fl. Jap. 194. 1784.
Cocculus trilobus (Thunb.) DC., Syst. 1: 522. 1817; FHN 1: 321. 1964.
Cocculus thunbergii DC., Syst. Nat. 1: 524. 1818; FKH 31. 1912.
Cocculus ovalifolius DC., Syst. Nat. 1: 526. 1818; FHK 13. 1861.

Woody vine. Young shoots densely pubescent, glabrescent in age. Leaves papery or subleathery; petioles (0.5–)1–3 cm, puberulous; leaf blade variable in shape and size, usually ovate or elliptic, sometimes obovate or obcordate, or occasionally suborbicular or oblong, 3–8(–10) × 0.5–2.5(–5) cm, apex acute, obtuse or rounded, sometimes slightly emarginate, margin entire or obtusely 3-lobed; glabrous or pubescent especially on abaxial surface, palmately 3–5-nerved. Cymes axillary, few-flowered, or many-flowered and racemosely arranged, up to 10 cm or longer, puberulous. Male flowers: sepals 6, broadly elliptic, 6–15 mm, glabrous; petals 6, lanceolate, 1–2 mm, apex divided into 2 acuminate or acute lobes; stamens 6, shorter than petals. Female flowers: sepals and petals as in males; staminodes 6, very small; carpels 6, glabrous. Drupes subglobose, red to reddish purple, usually 7–8 mm in diam.; kernel bony, 5–6 mm in diam., dorsally ornamented with branched ridges.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 1285; Y. S. Lau 338, 900; HK sheet 1102.
Distribution: Most parts of China except NW China and Xizang; widely distributed in SE & E Asia and extending to Hawaii.
Ecology: Thickets near villages. Flowering: Apr.–Aug.; fruiting: Aug.– Oct.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Pok Fu Lam, Wong Nai Chung, Tai Tam, Victoria Peak, Mount Nicholson, Shing Mun, Ma On Shan, Tsing Yi
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Cyclea hypoglauca (Schauer) Diels 粉葉輪環藤
Pflanzenr. IV. 94: 319. 1910; FHN 1: 325. 1964; FGD 1: 45. 1987; FRPS 30(1): 75. 1996.
Cissampelos hypoglauca Schauer, Nov. Act. Acad. Leop. Carol. 11 (Suppl. 1): 479. 1843.
Cyclea deltoidea Miers, Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 3: 258. 1851; FHK 14. 1861; FKH 31. 1912.

Herbaceous or ± woody vine. Branchlets slender, glabrous. Leaves peltate, papery; petioles 1.5–4 cm; leaf blade broadly ovate to triangular ovate, 2.5–7 × 1.5–4.5 cm, base truncate to rounded, apex acuminate, margin entire, adaxially shining, abaxially glaucous, glabrous or sparsely pubescent, palmately 5–7- nerved. Panicles narrow, almost reduced to racemes. Male flowers: sepals 4 or 5, free, obovate or obovate-cuneate, 1–1.2 mm; petals 4 or 5, usually connate and saucer-shaped, scarcely lobed, 0.5–1 mm; stamens united in a central column, 1–1.2 mm, slightly exserted. Female flowers: sepals 2, suborbicular, ca. 0.8 in diam.; petals 2, unequal; ovary glabrous. Drupes red, glabrous; the kernel ca. 3.5 mm, dorsally with 3 rows of tuberculous ribs on each side.

Locality: Pok Fu Lam, Wong Nai Chung, Tai Tam, Victoria Peak, Mount Nicholson, Shing Mun, Ma On Shan, Tsing Yi. Y. W. Lam 149, 999; H. C. Tang 994.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian; Vietnam.
Ecology: Forest edges and bushes on hillsides. Flowering: May–Jul.; fruiting: Aug.– Oct.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Mount Parker, Cape D'Aguilar, Wan Chai, Tai Po Kau, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Diploclisia glaucescens (Blume) Diels 蒼白秤鈎風
Pflanzenr. IV. 94: 225. 1910; FHN 1: 320, fig. 159. 1964; Forman, Kew Bull. 22: 363. 1968; FGD 1: 35, fig. 36. 1987; FRPS 30(1): 31, pl. 6: 6. 1996.
Cocculus glaucescens Blume, Bijdr. 25. 1825
Diploclisia macrocarpa (Wright) Miers, Ann. Mag. Nat. Hist., ser. 2, 7: 42. 1851.
Cocculus macrocarpus Wright, Illstr. 1: 22, t. 7. 42. 1840; FHK 12. 1861; FKH 31. 1912.

Large woody vine, glabrous throughout. Stems up to 20 m or longer; branchlets light brown, striate. Leaves thinly leathery, sometimes peltate; petioles 3–7 cm; leaf blade triangular orbicular, sometimes broadly ovate-triangular, 3 –6 × 3–7 cm, base truncate, subrounded or slightly cordate, apex abruptly acute to rounded and apiculate, glaucescent on abaxial surface, usually palmately 5-nerved. Cymes forming panicles, 10 –30 cm, usually fascicled and borne on leafless old stems. Flowers light yellow, slightly fragrant. Male flowers: sepals ovate-oblong, 1.5 –2.5 mm; petals obovate or rhomboid, ca. 1.5 mm; stamens ca. 2 mm. Female flowers: sepals and petals as in males, except petals 2-lobed at apex. Drupes yellowish red, glaucous, narrowly oblong-obovate, 1.3 –2 × 0.7– 0.9 cm.

Locality: Mount Parker, Cape D'Aguilar, Wan Chai, Tai Po Kau, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 552, 2217; HK sheet 152.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; India, Ceylon, Myanmar, Thailand, Malesia.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Apr.; fruiting: Aug.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Hypserpa nitida Miers 夜花藤
Ann. Mag. Nat. Hist. ser. 3, 14: 363. 1864; Forman, Kew Bull. 12: 453. 1958; FHN 1: 318, fig. 157. 1964; FGD 1: 34, fig. 34. 1987; FRPS 30(1): 27. 1996.
Limacia cuspidata Hook. f. & Thoms., Fl. Ind. 1: 189. 1855; FHK 12. 1861; FKH 31. 1912.

Woody vine. Branchlets sparsely to densely pubescent with yellowish hairs when young, glabrous in age. Leaves papery to leathery; petioles 1–2 cm, pubescent or glabrescent; leaf blade ovate, ovateelliptic to oblong elliptic, rarely elliptic or broadly elliptic, 4–10(–12) × 1.5–5(–7) cm, base obtuse or rounded, sometimes cuneate, apex acuminate, acute or obtuse and mucronate, palmately 3- nerved, usually glabrous, rarely pubescent along nerves. Male panicles 1–2 cm, scarcely longer than the petioles, pubescent. Male flowers: sepals 7–11, the outer ones minute and bracteoliform, 0.5 – 0.8 mm, puberulous outside, the innermost 4 or 5 broadly obovate, ovate to ovate-orbicular, 1.5 –2.5 mm, ciliate; petals 4 or 5, subobovate, 1–1.2 mm; stamens 5 –10, free or ± connate at the base, 1–1.5 mm. Female flowers few or solitary; sepals and petals as in males, staminodes none; carpels 2; ovary glabrous. Drupes yellow or orangish red when mature, subglobose or slightly compressed; kernel broadly obovate, 5 – 6 mm long.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. K. Y. Tam 134; Y. S. Lau 997; HK sheet 122.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, S Yunnan, Fujian; Sri Lanka, India (Assam), Lower Myanmar, Thailand, Malesia.
Ecology: Thin forests or margins of forests. Flowering and fruiting: May–Aug.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): So Kon Po, Tai Hang, Mount Cameron, Tai Po
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Pericampylus glaucus (Lam.) Merr. 細圓藤
Interpr. Herb. Amboin. 219. 1917; FHN 1: 319, fig. 158. 1964; Forman, Kew Bull. 22: 366. 1968; FGD 1: 34, fig. 35. 1987; FRPS 30(1): 28. 1996.
Menispermum glaucum Lamarck, Dict. 4: 100. 1797.
Pericampylus incanus (Colebr.) Hook. f. & Thoms., Fl. Ind. 1: 194. 1855; FHK 13. 1861; FKH 31. 1912.
Cocculus incanus Colebr., Trans. Linn. Soc. London 13: 57. 1822.

Woody vine to 10 m or longer. Branchlets initially yellowish tomentose, glabrous in age. Leaves papery or thinly leathery, sometimes slightly peltate; petioles 3–7 cm, tomentose; leaf blade triangular ovate to triangular orbicular, 3.5–8(–10) cm long and wide, base subtruncate to cordate, rarely broadly cuneate, apex obtuse or rounded, rarely apiculate, margin obscurely undulate or subentire, tomentose on both surfaces, or sparsely pubescent to glabrescent abaxially, rarely glabrous on both surfaces, palmately (3–)5-nerved. Cymes axillary, dichotomous, 2–10 cm, tomentose. Male flowers: sepals 9, ± pubescent abaxially; petals 6, cuneate or sometimes spathulate, 0.5–0.7 mm, margin involute; stamens 6. Female flowers: sepals and petals as in males; staminodes 6; ovary glabrous; stigma 2-lobed. Drupes red or purple; kernel 5–6 mm in diam.

Locality: So Kon Po, Tai Hang, Mount Cameron, Tai Po. W. J. Tutcher 9146; Y. S. Lau 219, 2973.
Distribution: Widely distributed in the Yangtze River basin and southwards to Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, eastwards to Taiwan; SE Asia.
Ecology: Forests, thickets and on forest edges. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.; fruiting: Sep.– Oct.
Uses: Material (stems for weaving utensils).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Aberdeen, Tai Po Kau, Ma On Shan, Sheung Shui, Tai Mong Tsai
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Stephania longa Lour. 糞箕篤
Fl. Cochinch. 608. 1790; FHN 1: 322, fig. 160. 1964; FGD 1: 42. 1987; FRPS 30(1): 51, pl. 10: 7–9. 1996; FTW ed. 2, 2: 602. 1996.
Stephania japonica (Thunb.) Miers var. hispidula Yamam., Icon. Pl. Formosan., Suppl. 3: 33, fig. 11. 1927.
Stephania hernandifolia auct. non Walp: FHK 13. 1861; FKH 31. 1912.

Herbaceous vine, 1–4 m or longer, without tuberous roots, glabrous except inflorescence. Leaves usually more or less peltate, papery; petioles 1–4.5 cm, often twisted at the base; leaf blade broadly ovare, orbicular or nearly triangular, 3–9 × 2–6 cm, base subtruncate or subrounded, rarely slightly concave, apex obtuse, mucronate, sometimes glaucous on abaxial surface, palmately 10–11-nerved. Inflorescences an axillary umbel with 5 or 6 rays, each ray terminated by a head, or partial umbel of 8 to 12 small sessile or shortly pedicellate flowers; peduncles 1–4 cm. Male flowers: sepals 6–8, cuneate or obovate, ca. 1 mm; petals 4 or sometimes 3, greenish yellow, suborbicular, ca. 0.4 mm. Female flowers: sepals and petals 4, rarely 3, ca. 0.6 mm; ovary glabrous, stigma lobes divaricate. Drupes red, 5–6 mm; kernel obovate, dorsally with 2 rows transverse tuberculous ridges.

Locality: Aberdeen, Tai Po Kau, Ma On Shan, Sheung Shui, Tai Mong Tsai. L. T. Lo 79; Y. S. Lau 296, 2837; HK sheet 35909.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Margins of forests and in thickets. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.; fruiting: Aug.– Oct.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Ng Tung Chai, Ko Lau Wan
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Stephania tetrandra S. Moore 粉防己
J. Bot. 13: 225. 1875; FGD 1: 42, fig. 43. 1987; FRPS 30(1): 52, pl. 11: 7–9. 1996; FTW ed. 2, 2: 605, pl. 292. 1996.

Herbaceous vine, 1–3 m or longer, with fleshy, cylindrical taproot. Leaves peltate; petioles 3–7 cm; leaf blade papery, broadly triangular to triangular orbicular, usually 4–7 × 5–8.5 cm, base slightly cordate or truncate, apex acute and apiculate, appressed pubescent at least on abaxial surface, palmately 9- or 10-nerved, reticulation of veins conspicuous. Flowers in racemose discoid heads. Male flowers: sepals 4 or sometimes 5, usually obovate-elliptic, 0.8 mm including the claw; petals 5, fleshy, 0.6 mm. Female flowers: sepals and petals as in males. Drupes subglobose, red when mature; the kernel ca. 5.5 mm in diam. Dorsally cristate, with ca. 15 transverse ribs on each side.

Locality: Ng Tung Chai, Ko Lau Wan. HK sheet 34042, 35806.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Thickets. Flowering: Jun.–Aug.; fruiting: Aug.–Oct. Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Tinospora sagittata (Oliv.) Gagnep. 青牛膽
Bull. Soc. Bot. France 55: 45. 1908; Forman, Kew Bull. 36(2): 383, fig. 1 (d-e). 1981; FGD 1: 34, fig. 32. 1987; FRPS 30(1): 23. 1996.
Limacia sagittata Oliv., Hook. Icon. Pl. 1749. 1888.
Tinospora capillipes Gagnep., Bull. Bot. France 55: 44. 1908.
Tinospora imbricata S. Y. Hu, J. Arnold Arbor. 35: 195, t. 1 (2). 1954.

Herbaceous vine, with moniliform roots. Stems slender, striate, usually puberulous. Leaves papery to thinly leathery; petioles 2.5–5 cm or longer, pubescent or glabrescent; leaf blade lanceolate, rarely ovate or elliptic, 7–15(–20) × 2.4 –5 cm, base sagittate or hastate, apex acuminate, sometimes caudate, lobes rounded, obtuse or mucronate, usually puberulous on nerves, sometimes glabrescent adaxially or on both surfaces, palmately 5-nerved; reticulation of nerved raised abaxially. Cymes axillary, usually fascicled, or forming panicles, 2–10(–15) cm or sometimes longer; peduncles and pedicels filamentous; bracteoles 2, closely subtending sepals. Male flowers: sepals 6, or sometimes more, often unequal, the outermost minute, ovate or lanceolate, only 1–2 mm, inner ones conspicuous larger, broadly ovate to obovate, or broadly elliptic to elliptic, to 3.5 mm; petals 6, subrounded or broadly obovate, rarely subrhomboid, often clawed, 1.4 –2 mm. Female flowers: sepals similar to that in males; petals cuneate, ca. 0.4 mm; staminodes 6, usually clavellate, ca. 0.4 mm; carpels 3, subglabrous. Drupes ± subglobose; kernel half-globular, 6 – 8 mm wide.

Locality: Sai Kung, Mount Parker. Y. W. Lam 1451; HK sheet 126, 127, 33668.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, SE Xizang, Hunan, Hubei, Shanxi, Jiangxi, Fujian; N Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests, bamboo groves and grassy slopes. Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: Jul.–Aug.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Cape D'Aguilar, Tai Mong Tsai, Mau Ping, Yung Shue O, Ping Chau, Ching Chau
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Tinospora sinensis (Lour.) Merr. 中華青牛膽
Sunyatsenia 1: 193. 1934; FHN 1: 318, 1964; Forman, Kew Bull. 36: 386, fig. 1 (F, G). 1981; FGD 1: 33, fig. 33. 1987; FRPS 30(1): 20. 1996.
Campylus sinensis Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 113. 1790.
Cocculus tomentosus Colebrr., Trans. Linn. Soc. 13: 59. 1822.
Menispermum tomentosum (Colebr.) Roxb., Fl. Ind. 3: 813. 1832.
Tinospora tomentosa (Colebr.) Hook. f. & Thoms., Fl. Ind. 1: 183. 1855.

Vine up to 20 m or longer. Branches slightly fleshy; young shoots green, striate, pubescent; old branches thick, usually glabrous, with brownish, membranous epidermis and convex lenticels. Leaves papery; petioles (4 –)6 –13 cm, puberulous; leaf blade ovate-orbicular, rarely broadly ovate, 7–14 × 5 –13 cm, base deeply to slightly cordate, apex acute, margin entire, puberulent on both surfaces, palmately 5(–7)-nerved. Inflorescences appearing when plant is leafless. Male inflorescences 1– 4 cm or longer, solitary or fascicled. Male flowers: sepals 6 in 2 series, outer 3 minute, oblong-elliptic, 1–1.5 mm, inner ones broadly ovate, 5 × 3 mm; petals 6, sub-rhomboid, ca. 3 mm including the claw; stamens 6, filaments ca. 4 mm. Female inflorescences solitary. Female flowers: sepals and petals as in males; carpels 3. Drupes red, subglobose, to 10 mm; kernel semi-ovoid, with dorsal ridges and tubercles.

Locality: Cape D'Aguilar, Tai Mong Tsai, Mau Ping, Yung Shue O, Ping Chau, Ching Chau. L. T. Lo 308; Y. S. Lau 3010, 3104.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; Sri Lanka, India, Nepal, Thailand, Cambodia, Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Apr.; fruiting: May–Jun.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Meliosma fordii Hemsl. 香皮樹
J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 23: 14. 1886; FKH 68. 1912; FRPS 47(1): 118. 1985; FGD 1: 268, fig. 297. 1987.
Meliosma hainanensis How, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 3: 433. 1955.

Tree, to 10 m tall. Branchlets, petioles and inflorescences brownish pubescent. Leaves simple, subleathery; petioles 1.5 – 3.5 cm; leaf blade oblanceolate or lanceolate, 9 –18(–25) × 2.5 – 5(– 8) cm, base narrowly cuneate, decurrent, apex acuminate, margin entire or sometimes with a few teeth near apex, adaxially more or less shining, appressed pubescent on midvein and lateral veins, abaxially sparsely pubescent; lateral veins 11–20. Panicles terminal or subterminal, 4–5-branched. Flowers 1–1.5 mm in diam. Pedicels 1–1.5 mm. Sepals 4(–5), broadly ovate, 0.5 mm, sparsely pubescent abaxially, ciliolate. Petals white, outer 3 suborbicular, ca. 1.5 mm in diam., inner 2 smaller, bifid halfway at an obtuse angle; lobes linear. Ovary glabrous, style about the length of ovary. Drupes subglobose or compressed globose, 3–5 mm in diam.

Locality: Tai Po Kau. Y. S. Lau 339; HK sheet 32241.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, S Yunnan, Guizhou, S Hunan, S Jiangxi, Fujian; Vietnam, Laos, Cambodia, Thailand.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: May–Jul.; fruiting: Aug.– Oct.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Clear Water Bay, Tai Po Kau, Tai To Yan, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Meliosma rigida Sieb. & Zucc. 筆羅子
Abh. Bayer. Akad. Wiss., Math.-Naturwiss. Kl. 4(2): 153. 1845; FKH 68. 1912; FRPS 47(1): 117. 1985; FGD 1: 267, fig. 296. 1987; FTW ed. 2, 3: 612. 1993.
Meliosma patens Hemsl., J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 23: 145. 1886; FKH 68. 1912.
Meliosma glomerulata Rehd. & Wils., Sargent Pl. Wils. 2: 203. 1914.

Tree, to 7 m tall. Young branches, bud scales and inflorescences rusty tomentose. Leaves simple, leathery; petioles 1.5–4 cm; leaf blade oblanceolate or narrow obovate, 8–25 × 2.5–4.5 cm, apex acuminate or caudate-acuminate, tapering from middle into a cuneate base, margin entire or with a few teeth above middle, adaxially glabrous except the puberulous midvein and lateral veins, abaxially rusty pubescent; lateral veins 9–18 on each side of midvein. Panicles terminal, erect, thrice branched. Flowers sessile, 3–4 mm in diam. Sepals 4(–5), ovate or suborbicular, unequal, ciliolate. Petals white, outer 3 suborbicular, 2–2.5 mm in diam., inner 2 bifid halfway at an acute angle, lobes acute, apex ciliolate. Ovary glabrous; style 2 times the length of the ovary. Drupes globose, 5–8 mm in diam.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Clear Water Bay, Tai Po Kau, Tai To Yan, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 1262, 2978.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, S Yunnan, Guizhou, SW Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Summer; fruiting: Sep.– Oct.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Victoria Peak, Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai, Ma On Shan, Sunset Peak
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Meliosma squamulata Hance 樟葉泡花樹
J. Bot. 1: 364. 1876; FKH 68. 1912; FRPS 47(1): 111. 1985; FGD 1: 265, fig. 294. 1987; FTW ed. 2, 3: 612, pl. 314. 1993.

Evergreen small tree, to 15 m tall. Young shoots appressed pubescent, glabrescent. Leaves simple, thin leathery; petioles slender, 2.5– 6.5(–10) cm; leaf blades elliptic or ovate, 5 –12 × 1.5 –5 cm, base cuneate, more or less decurrent, apex caudate-acuminate, tip blunt, margin entire, adaxially glabrous and shining, abaxially glaucous, densely covered with yellowish brown tiny scales; lateral veins 3–5 on each side of midvein. Panicles terminal or axillary, 7–20 cm, densely tawny pubescent. Flowers white, 3 mm in diam. Sepals 5, ovate, ciliolate. Petals glabrous, outer 3 suborbicular, 2.5 mm in diam. inner 2 ca. 1 mm, bifid to middle, lobes acute divaricate. Ovary ovoid, glabrous; style ca. 1 mm. Drupes globose or obovoid, 4– 6 mm in diam.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai, Ma On Shan, Sunset Peak. Y. S. Lau 299; HK sheet 1216.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, S Hunan, S Jiangxi, S Fujian, Taiwan; Japan.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Summer; fruiting: Sep.– Oct.
Uses: Timber.

Meliosma thorelii Lecomte 山檨葉泡花樹
Bull. Soc. Bot. France 54: 677. 1907; FRPS 47(1): 109. 1985; FGD 1: 265, fig. 293. 1987.
Meliosma buchananifolia Merr., Philip. J. Sci. 23: 250. 1923.
Meliosma affinis Merr., J. Arnold Arbor. 21: 375. 1940.
Meliosma henryi Diels subsp. thorelii (Lecomte) Beusekom, Blumea 19: 449. 1971.
Meliosma simplicifolia auct. non Walp.: Merr., Lingnan Sci. J. 5: 119. 1927.

Tree, 6–14 m tall. Leaves simple, subleathery; petioles 1.5–2 cm; leaf blades oblanceolate-elliptic or oblanceolate, 15–25 × 4–8 cm, base cuneate, decurrent to the petioles, apex acuminate, margin entire or sharply serrulate, glabrous or sparsely pubescent abaxially and barbate in axils of nerves; lateral veins 15 –22 on each side of midvein, reticulation of veins raised on both surfaces. Panicles terminal or axillary, erect, 15 –18 cm, branches flatted, brownish pubescent. Flowers fragrant, 2–2.5 mm in diam., shortly pedicellate. Sepals 5, ovate, 0.6–0.8 mm, apex obtuse, ciliolate. Petals white, outer 3 suborbicular, ca. 2 mm in diam., inner 2 narrow lanceolate, entire, shorter than the outer ones. Ovary pubescent; style ca. 1 mm. Drupes globose, slightly oblique, 6–9 mm in diam.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. F. W. Xing 7221, 8588.
Distribution: SE Fujian, Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, S Guizhou, SE to SW Yunnan; Vietnam, Laos.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Summer; fruiting: Oct.–Nov.

Sabia limoniacea Wall. ex Hook. f. & Thoms. 檸檬清風藤
Fl. Ind. 1: 210. 1855; Benth., FHK 70. 1861; FKH 68. 1912; FRPS 47(1): 93. 1985.
Sabia limoniacea Wall. ex Hook. f. & Thoms. var. ardisioides L. Chen, Sargentia 3: 58. 1943.

Evergreen woody climber, up to 10 m, glabrous. Leaves leathery; petioles 1.5–2.5 cm; leaf blade elliptic, oblong-elliptic or ovate-elliptic to lanceolate, 7–15 × 4–6 cm, base broadly cuneate or rounded, apex short-acuminate or acute; lateral veins 6–7 on each side of midvein. Cymes 2–4-flowered, solitary, subtended by a leafy bract, or arranged in a long and narrow panicle up to 15 cm. Pedicels 1–3 mm. Sepals 5, ovate or oblong-ovate, 0.5–1 mm, apex acute or obtuse, glabrous, ciliolate. Petals 5, pale green, obovate or elliptic ovate, 1.5–2 mm, apex rounded. Stamens 5; filaments flattened; anthers introrse. Ovary glabrous. Drupes globose to obovoid, strongly compressed.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. L. T. Lo 1; Y. W. Lam 1379.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, SW Yunnan, Fujian; Indochina, Myanmar, N India, Thailand, Malay Peninsula.
Ecology: Forests, climbing on trees or rocks. Flowering: Aug.–Nov.; fruiting: Jan.–May of the following year.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Mount Parker, Kowloon Peak, Tai Mo Shan, Sunset Peak
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Sabia swinhoei Hemsl. ex Forb. & Hemsl. 尖葉清風藤
J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 23: 144. 1886; FRPS 47(1): 89. 1985; FTW ed. 2, 3: 614, pl. 315. 1993.
Sabia gracilis Hemsl., Hook. Icon. Pl. 29: t. 2831. 1907.
Sabia swinhoei Hemsl. var. hainanensis L. Chen, Sargentia 3: 44. 1943.

Evergreen woody climber or scandent shrub, up to 6 m. Branchlets pubescent or tomentose. Leaves papery to thin leathery; petioles 3–5 mm, pubescent; leaf blade elliptic, ovate-elliptic, ovate or broadly ovate, 5–12 × 2–5 cm, base cuneate to rounded, apex acuminate or abruptly and shortly acuminate to acute, adaxially glabrous but pubescent on midvein when young, abaxially all over laxly or densely pubescent, glabrescent in age; lateral veins 4–6 on each side of midvein, straight or curved, anastomosing at a distance of 5–8 mm from the margin. Cymes 2–7-flowered, axillary, sparsely pubescent or tomentose, 1.5–2.5 cm. Peduncles 0.7–1.5 cm. Pedicels 2–4 mm. Sepals 5, ovate, 1–1.5 mm, ciliate or not, with inconspicuous red dots abaxially. Petals 5, ovate-lanceolate or lanceolate, 3.5 –6 × 1–1.5 mm, light green. Stamens 5, 1–1.6 mm; filaments slightly flattened; anthers ellipsoid, often inflexed, introrse. Ovary glabrous; style 0.3–0.75 mm. Dupes more or less obovoid and compressed, 7–9 × 6–8 mm, blue or dark blue in fresh.

Locality: Mount Parker, Kowloon Peak, Tai Mo Shan, Sunset Peak. F. W. Xing 9865; Y. W. Lam 1437; K. Y. Tam s.n. (HK sheet 39787).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; N Vietnam.
Ecology: Margins of forests and thickets. Flowering: Mar.– Apr.; fruiting: Jul.–Sep.

Papaver rhoeas L. 虞美人
Sp. Pl. 1: 507. 1753; FFJ 2: 156, fig. 131. 1985; FGX 1: 406, pl. 168: 1–2. 1991; FRPS 32: 53. 1999; FGD 4: 61, fig. 38. 2000.

Annual herb; stems branched, 30 – 80 cm, sparsely hispid. Leaves alternate, pinnately or bipinnately lobed, 3–15 cm, lobes lanceolate, margin coarsely serrate, leaves on the upper part of stems coarse-serrate-pinnately lobed, sparsely hispid on both surfaces. Flowers solitary, pedicels 10–15 cm; sepals 2, broadly elliptic, 1–2 cm, green, hispid; petals 4, red, purple or white, usually with black patches at base, suborbicular or obovate, 2– 3.5 cm; stamens many, filaments red; ovary obovoid, ca. 1 cm, glabrous, stigmas plateform, with 5 –18-radiate lobes, persistent, 1.2–2 cm.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. W. Lam 32.
Distribution: Widely cultivated in China, native to Europe.
Ecology: Flowering: Jan.–May.
Uses: Ornamental.

Corydalis balansae Prain 台灣黃堇
J. Asiat. Soc. Bengal 65: 25. 1879; FRPS 32: 440. 1999; FGD 4: 64. 2000.
Corydalis tashiroi Makino, Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 33: 65. 1909.

Annual or biennial herb, ca. 50 cm tall, without tubers. Stems glabrous, many-branched, angulate. Petiole 7–16 cm; cauline leaves bipinnate, outline broadly ovate, 10 –20 × 10 –15 cm; leaflets pinnately parted to divided, segments obovate or ovate, base cuneate, apex obtuse, margin incised. Racemes leaf-opposed, ca. 12 cm. Bracts oblong-lanceolate or ovate. Flowers yellow, 1.2–2 cm. Petals often shallowly cristate, outer one shortly spurred. Stigma 2-fid. Capsules linear, 3–4.5 × 0.3 cm. Seeds black, many, densely small pitted, carunculate.

Locality: Lantau Island (Tung Chung). Y. W. Lam 33.
Distribution: S, E & SW China; Japan, Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering and fruiting: Mar.–Jul.

Platanus × acerifolia (Ait.) Willd. 二球懸鈴木
Sp. Pl. 4: 474. 1797; FRPS 35(2): 120, pl. 26. 1979; FGD 4: 248, fig. 148. 2000.
Platanus hybrida Brot., Fl. Lusit. 2: 487. 1804.
Platanus orientalis L. var. acerifolia Ait., Hort. Kew 3: 364. 1789.

Deciduous tree, to 30 m tall. Bark greyish green, exfoliating in large flakes. Young shoots brownish tomentose, glabrous and reddish brown in age. Leaves papery; petioles 3–10 cm, densely pubescent; leaf blade broadly ovate, 10 –24 × 12–25 cm, base truncate to cordate, upper part palmately (3 –)5(–7)-lobed; lobes triangular-ovate or broadly triangular, the middle one about as long as broad, entire or sparsely toothed, tawny tomentose when young, glabrous or nearly so at maturity. Infructescence a globular head, usually 2, rarely1 or 3 racemosely arranged, 2.5–3 cm in diam., bristly. Nutlet ovoid or rounded at apex and crowned by the persistent remnant of the style.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 1552, 2773.
Distribution: Probably a hybrid of P. occidentalis L. and P. orientalis L. Widely cultivated in temperate regions.
Ecology: Flowering: May; fruiting: Sep.– Oct.
Uses: Ornamental.

Altingia chinensis (Champ. ex Benth.) Oliv. ex Hance 蕈樹（阿丁楓、山荔枝）
J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 13: 103. 1873; FKH 101. 1912; FRPS 35(2): 64,pl. 14. 1979; FGD 1: 158, fig. 174. 1987; FOC 9: 21. 2003.
Liquidambar chinensis Champ. ex Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 4: 164. 1852; FHK 132. 1861.

Tree up to 20 m tall, glabrous except the inflorescences. Stipules caducous; petiole ca. 1 cm; leaf blade obovate-oblong, 7–13 × 3 – 4.5 cm, leathery, base cuneate, apex acute, margin serrate; lateral veins prominent on both surfaces. Male inflorescences ca. 1 cm, usually many arranged in panicles; peduncle pubescent. Female inflorescence solitary or many in panicles, 15–26-flowered; peduncle 2– 4 cm. Male flowers: stamens subsessile; anthers obovoid. Female flowers: calyx connate with ovary, styles 3 –4 mm, pubescent, apex recurved. Infructescences subglobose, 1.7–2.8 cm wide, base truncate, without persistent styles.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 206; HK sheet 34771.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Hunan, Fujian, Jiangxi, Zhejiang; Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Mar.–Jun.; fruiting: Jul.–Sep.
Uses: Timber.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Wong Nai Chung Valley woods, Hong Kong Island by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1850.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Pat Sin Leng, Wu Kau Tang, Nam Chung
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Altingia gracilipes Hemsl. 細柄蕈樹
Hooker's Icon. Pl. 29: t. 2837. 1907; FRPS 35(2): 66. 1979; FGD1: 159. 1987; FOC 9: 20. 2003.
Altingia gracilipes var. serrulata Tutch., Rep. Bot. & For. Dept. Hongk. 1914: 31. 1915; FRPS 35(2): 67. 1979; FGD 1: 159. 1979; Check List HK Plants 56. 2002; 25. 2004.
Altingia gracilipes f. uniflora H. T. Chang, Sunyatsenia 7: 74. 1948.

Tree 12–20 m tall; young branches hairy. Stipules absent; petiole slender, 1.3 cm, glabrous; leaf blade ovate-lanceolate, 4.7 × 1.5 –2.5 cm, leathery, base obtuse or narrowly rounded, apex caudate-acuminate, margin usually entire or sometimes serrate, abaxially glabrous; lateral veins 5 or 6 pairs. Male inflorescences globose, 0.5– 0.6 cm in diam., usually several arranged in a panicle. Female inflorescences solitary or arranged in raceme, 5 – 6-flowered; peduncle 2–3 cm, pubescent. Male flowers: stamens sessile; anthers red, obovoid, ca. 1.5 mm. Female flowers: styles ca. 2.5 mm, apex recurved. Infructescences obconical, 1.5 –2 cm wide, base cuneate.

Locality: Pat Sin Leng, Wu Kau Tang, Nam Chung. Y. S. Lau 2634; L. T. Lo 629.
Distribution: Guangdong, Hainan, Fujian, Zhejiang.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.; fruiting: Jul.–Sep.
Uses: Materials (resin).

Corylopsis multiflora Hance 瑞木（大果臘瓣花）
Ann. Sci. Nat., Bot., sér. 4, 15: 224. 1861; FHN 2: 335. 1965; FRPS 35(2): 82, pl. 18. 1979; FFJ 2: 254, fig. 213. 1985; FGD 1: 162, fig. 178. 1987; FOC 9: 37. 2003.
Corylopsis wilsonii Hemsl., Icon. Pl. 29: pl. 2819. 1919.

Shrub or small tree; young branches tomentose; older branches grey-brown, glabrescent; buds grey-white tomentose. Stipules oblong, 1.8–2 cm, hairy; petiole 1–1.5 cm; leaf blade leathery, ovate, obovate or obovate-elliptic, 7–15 × 4 – 8 cm, base almost symmetrical, cordate, apex acute, margin serrate, teeth mucronate, abaxially glaucous, stellately pubescent at least along veins; lateral veins 7–9 pairs. Inflorescence 2–4 cm, with 1–5 leaves at base, peduncle pubescent; general bracts ovate, 1.5–2 cm, abaxially hairy. Calyx tube glabrous. Petals oblanceolate, 4–5 × 1.5–2 mm. Stamens 6–7 mm, exserted. Ovary glabrous, styles slightly shorter than stamens. Capsules hard woody, glabrous, 1.2–2 × 0.8 –1.4 cm. Seeds 8–10 mm, black.

Locality: Lantau Peak, Sunset Peak. Y. W. Lam 2117; F. W. Xing 9194.
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hubei, Hunan, Taiwan, Yunnan.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.; fruiting: Jun.–Sep.

Distyliopsis dunnii (Hemsl.) P. K. Endress 尖葉假蚊母樹
Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 90: 30. 1970; FFJ 2: 260. 1985; FOC 9: 31. 2003.
Sycopsis dunnii Hemsl., Hooker's Icon. Pl. 29: t. 2836. 1907; FRPS 35(2): 114, pl. 24. 1979; FGD 1: 166, fig. 181. 1987.

Shrub or small tree; young branches with sessile, peltate scales. Petiole 1–1.5 cm, densely lepidote; leaf blade oblong or ovateoblong, occasionally oblong-lanceolate, 6 –9 × 2.5 –4.5 cm, leathery, base cuneate, apex acute or acuminate, margin entire, both surfaces glabrescent. Flowers arranged in axillary short spike or racemes. Bracts oblong. Male flowers: borne on lower part, sessile, calyx 5 – 6- teethed. Stamens 5–9, filaments 2–5 mm, without rudimentary ovary. Bisexual flowers: borne on the upper part, shortly pedicellate; floral cup 2–3 mm; stamens 4 –11. Ovary villous; styles 4 –5 mm, glabrous, recurved. Capsules 1– 4, stalked, 1–1.3 cm, grey-brown villous, persistent floral cup 3– 4 mm, with dense sessile scales.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. L. T. Lo 432; Y. W. Lam 1403.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian; Laos.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.; fruiting: Jun.–Sep.

Distyliopsis tutcheri (Hemsl.) P. K. Endress 鈍葉假蚊母樹
Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 90: 30. 1970; FFJ 2: 261. 1985; FOC 9: 32. 2003.
Sycopsis tutcheri Hemsl., Hooker's Icon. Pl. 29: t. 2834. 1907; FKH 101. 1912; FRPS 35(2): 115. 1979; FGD 1: 167. 1987.
Sycopsis oblanceolata H. T. Chang, Sunyatsenia 7: 72. 1948.

Shrub or small tree; young branches with sessile, peltate scales. Petioles 3– 6 mm, densely lepidote; leaf blade elliptic or obovate, 3 – 6 × 2–3 cm, leathery, base broadly cuneate, apex obtuse or subrounded, margin entire. Male flowers not seen. Female (or bisexual) flowers arranged in 1–2 cm long racemes. Peduncle and rachis lepidote; pedicels 3 – 4 mm; bracts oblong, lepidote; ovary villous, style 3–5 mm, recurved. Capsules 1–5, 1–1.3 cm, yellowbrown- villous, persistent floral cup 4 –5 mm, with sessile scales.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Lantau Island. HK sheet 10909, 10910.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.; fruiting: Jun.–Sep.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from east of Mountain Lodge, Victoria Peak, Hong Kong Island by W. J. Tutcher on 6 January 1904.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Ma On Shan, Tai Mo Shan, Tung Chung, Lantau Peak
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Distylium racemosum Sieb. & Zucc. 蚊母樹
Fl. Jap. 1: 178. 1835; FHK 133. 1861; FRPS 35(2): 102. 1979; FGD 1: 163. 1987; FOC 9: 29. 2003.

Shrub or small tree, glabrous except ovary; young branches stellate-lepidote; buds lepidote. Petioles 0.5 –1 cm, sparsely stellate-lepidote; leaf blade elliptic or obovate, 3 –6 × 1.5 –3.5 cm, leathery, base broadly cuneate, apex slightly obtuse, margin entire; lateral veins 5 or 6 pairs, reticulation of veins inconspicuous on both surfaces. Inflorescences 1.8 –2 cm, male and female flowers on the same inflorescence, with female ones on the top. Floral bracts lanceolate, 2–3 mm. Male flower: stamens 5 – 6, filaments 1.5–2 mm; anthers red, 2.5–3.5 mm. Female flower: ovary stellatetomentose; styles 6 –7 mm. Capsules ovoid, 1–1.3 cm, stellatepubescent with brown hairs. Seeds ovoid, 4–5 mm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Ma On Shan, Tai Mo Shan, Tung Chung, Lantau Peak. H. C. Tang 285, 2081.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian, Zhejiang, Taiwan; Korea, Japan (Ryukyu).
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.; fruiting: Jun.–Aug.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Eustigma oblongifolium Gardn. & Champ. 秀柱花
Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 1: 312. 1849; FHK 132. 1861; FKH 101. 1912; FHN 2: 335. 1965. FRPS 35(2): 96, pl. 21. 1979; FGD 1: 162, fig. 179. 1987; FOC 9: 34. 2003.

Shrub or small tree; young branches lepidote. Stipules linear; petioles 0.5 –1 cm; leaf blade oblong or oblong-lanceolate, 7–17 × 2.5 – 6 cm, leathery, base obtuse or cuneate, apex acuminate, margin entire or sometimes dentate towards apex, glabrous on both surfaces. Inflorescences 2–3 cm; general bracts ovate, ca. 1 cm; bracts and bracteoles ovate, stellate-pubescent. Floral cup ca. 2.5 mm, stellate-pubescent. Sepals ovate, ca. 3 mm, deciduous. Petals obovate, slightly shorter than sepals, apex 2-lobed. Anthers ovoid, 0.8 –1 mm. Styles 0.8 –1.2 cm. Capsule ca. 2 cm, glabrous. Seeds 0.8–1 cm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 222; P. S. Choi 471.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Apr.–Jun., fruiting: Jul.–Sep.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Happy Valley, Hong Kong Island by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1849.

Exbucklandia tonkinensis (Lec.) H. T. Chang 大果馬蹄荷
Acta Sci. Nat. Univ. Sunyatseni; 1959(2): 3. 1959; FRPS 35(2): 43, pl. 8. 1979; FGD 1: 152, fig. 167. 1987; FOC 9: 24. 2003.
Bucklandia tonkinensis Lec., Bull. Mus. Natl. Hist. Nat. 30: 392. 1924.
Bucklandia tonkinensis (Lec.) Steenis, Blumea 7(3): 595. 1954, nom. illeg.
Symingtonia tonkinensis (Lec.) Steenis, Fl. Malesiana, Ser. 1, Spermatoph. 5: 375. 1957; FHN 2: 332. 1965.

Tree to 30 m tall; young branches brown-pubescent. Stipules elliptic, 2– 4 × 0.8 –1.3 cm, puberulent; petioles 3 –5 cm; leaf blade broadly ovate, 8 –13 × 5 –9 cm, base broadly cuneate, apex acuminate, margin entire or sometimes 3-lobed, dark green and shining adaxially, glabrous and tuberculate abaxially; palmately 3–5-veined. Inflorescences capitate, solitary; heads 7–9-flowered; peduncles 1–1.5 cm, brown-tomentose. Petals absent. Stamens less than 1 cm. Ovary brown-pubescent; styles 4–5 mm. Capsules ovoid, 1–1.5 × 0.8 –1 cm, tuberculate. Seeds 6, narrowly winged at lower part.

Locality: Sunset Peak. Y. S. Lau 3242; N. H. Li 21.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian; Laos, Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: May–Jul.; fruiting: Aug.–Sep.
Notes: Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Common in Hong Kong. Also widely planted
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Liquidambar formosana Hance 楓香
Ann. Sci. Nat., Bot., ser. 5, 5: 215. 1886; FKH 101. 1912; FRPS 35(2): 55. 1979; FGD 1: 156. 1987.
Liquidambar formosana var. monticola Rehd. & E. H. Wils., Pl. Wils. 1: 422. 1913; FRPS 35(2): 55. 1979; FGD 1: 153. 1987.

Tree to 30 m tall; bark grey-brown; branchlets pubescent or glabrous, slightly lenticellate. Buds ovoid, glossy. Stipules linear, red, free or adnate to petiole, 1–1.4 cm, caducous; petioles to 12 cm, pubescent; leaf blade broadly ovate, palmately 3-lobed and 3-veined, central lobe longer, base rounded, apex caudateacuminate, margin glandular serrate, usually grey-white, pubescent or glabrous abaxially, veins prominent on both surfaces. Male inflorescence a short spike, several arranged in a raceme. Female inflorescence capitate, 20–40-flowered; peduncle 3–6 cm. Male flowers: stamens many. Female flowers: staminode-teeth 4 –7, needlelike, 4 – 8 mm; ovary hairy, styles 0.6 –1 mm. Infructescence globose, 3 – 4 cm wide. Capsules with persistent staminodes and styles.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Also widely planted. H. C. Tang 1473; Y. S. Lau 2487.
Distribution: S, SW, E & C China; S Korea, Laos, Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Mar.–Jun.; fruiting: Jul.–Sep.
Uses: Materials (timber, resin), ornamental, medicinal.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): North Point, Shing Mun, Castle Peak, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Loropetalum chinense (R. Br.) Oliv. 檵木（紙末花）
Trans. Linn. Soc. London 23: 459. 1862; FKH 101. 1912; FRPS 35(2): 70, pl. 16. 1979; FGD 1: 160, fig. 176. 1987; FOC 9: 33. 2003.
Hamamelis chinensis R. Br. in G. F. Abel, Narr. Journey China 375. 1818.

Deciduous or semi-evergreen shrub or small tree, much branched; branchlets stellate-pubescent. Petioles 2–5 mm, stellatepubescent; leaf blade leathery, ovate, elliptic or, rarely obovate, 2–6.5 × 1–3 cm, base unequal, rounded or cuneate, apex acute, margin entire, sparsely pubescent adaxially, densely stellate-pubescent and slighty greyish abaxially; lateral veins 4–8 pairs. Flowers usually 3–8 arranged in a short spike or head; peduncle 0.8–1 cm, stellatepubescent; bracts linear, ca. 3 mm. Flowers shortly pedicellate. Floral cup cupular, stellate-pubescent, 1.2–1.5 mm. Sepals 4, ovate, 2–3 mm. Petals 4, white to slightly yellowish, 1–2 cm. Stamens 4, filaments very short, connective elongated into a horn, anthers ovoid, 0.5–0.6 mm; staminodes 4, scale-like, alternate with stamens. Ovary inferior, stellate-pubescent, styles very short. Capsules ovoid or obovoid-globose, 7–8 mm, adnate to floral cup, stellate-tomentose. Seeds ovoid-globose or ellipsoid, 4–7 × 3.5–4 mm.

Locality: North Point, Shing Mun, Castle Peak, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 935; P. S. Choi 398.
Distribution: Areas S of Changjiang River to Tropic of Cancer; Japan, India.
Ecology: Tickets. Flowering: Mar.–Apr.; fruiting: May–Jul.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal (folklore).
Notes: Loropetalum chinense f. rubrum H. T. Chang (紅花檵木)(Photo 176) is also cultivated in Hong Kong. It differs from L. chinense by red petals.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Jardine's Lookout, Bowen Rd., Wong Lung Hang
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Loropetalum subcordatum (Benth.) Oliv. 四藥門花
Hooker's Icon. Pl. 15: t. 1417. 1883; FKH 101. 1912; FOC 9: 33. 2003.
Tetrathyrium subcordatum Benth., FHK 133. 1861; FRPS 35(2): 68, pl. 15. 1979; FGD 1: 159, fig. 175. 1987.

Evergreen shrub or tree, to 12 m tall; branchlets glabrous. Stipules lanceolate, 5 – 6 mm, stellate-pubescent, caducous; petioles 1–1.5 cm; leaf blade ovate-elliptic, 7–12 × 3.5 –5 cm, base rounded or subcordate, apex acute, margin entire or sparsely serrulate on distal part; lateral veins 6 – 8 pairs. Inflorescence axillary, 14 –25-flowered; peduncle 4 –5 cm; bracts linear. Flowers subsessile. Sepals 5, ca. 1.5 mm, stellate-pubescent. Petals 5, ca. 1.5 cm. Stamens 5, anthers ovoid; staminodes divergent. Ovary semiinferior, stellate-pubescent, styles very short, glabrous. Capsules subglobose, 10–12 mm in diam., adnate to floral cup, dehiscing into two valves. Seeds ovoid-ellipsoid, 6 –7 mm.

Locality: Jardine's Lookout, Bowen Rd., Wong Lung Hang. Y. W. Lam 281; P. Chow s.n. (HK sheet 38315).
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.; fruiting: Jul.–Aug.
Note: The type specimen was collected from “Black Mountain”, Hong Kong Island by C. Wilford between 1857 and 1858. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Rhodoleia championii Hook. f. 紅花荷（紅苞木、吊鐘王）
Bot. Mag. 76: t. 4509. 1850; FHK 131. 1861; FKH 101. 1912; FRPS 35(2): 46, pl. 9. 1979; FGD 1: 155, fig. 171. 1987; FOC 9: 24. 2003.
Rhodoleia latiovatifolia G. A. Fu, Guihaia 11(3): 208 –209. 1991.

Tree, to 12 m tall; young branches glabrous. Petioles 3 –5.5 cm; leaf blade ovate, 7–13 × 4.5 – 6.5 cm, leathery, base broadly cuneate, apex obtuse or subacute, green and shining adaxially, whitish grey abaxially; obscurely 3-veined at base, lateral veins 7–9 pairs, conspicuous on both surfaces, reticulation of veins inconspicuous. Inflorescences 3 – 4 cm, pendulous; peduncle 2–3 cm, with 5–6 scale-like bracts; involucral bracts many, ovate, brown-pubescent; bracteoles 5 or 6, scale-like. Petals spathulate, 2.5 –3.5(– 4) × 0.4 – 0.8 cm. Stamens as long as petals. Ovary glabrous; styles shorter than stamens. Infructescence ca. 3 cm wide, with 5 capsules. Capsule ovoid-globose, ca. 1.2–1.5 cm, without persistent styles.

Locality: Mount Nicholson, Mount Cameron, Aberdeen. H. C. Tang 865; HK sheet 1707.
Distribution: Guangdong, Hainan, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan; Indonesia (Sumatra), W Malaysia, Myanmar, Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Feb.–Apr.; fruiting: May–Aug.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Little Hong Kong, Hong Kong Island by J. G. Champion in 1849. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Daphniphyllum calycinum Benth. 牛耳楓
FHK 316. 1861; FKH 236. 1912; FHN 2: 187.1965; FRPS 45(1): 8. 1980; FGD 3: 224. 1995.

Shrub, 1–5 m tall. Branchlets sparsely lenticellate. Petioles 5– 15 cm; leaves papery, elliptic, obovate-elliptic or broadly elliptic, 10 –20 × 4 –10 cm, base cuneate, apex acute or subrounded, sometimes mucronate, margin entire, slightly pruinose and papillose abaxially; lateral veins 8–11 each side. Racemes 2–6 cm. Male flowers: calyx 3 – 4-lobed, lobes triangular, ca. 3 mm; stamens 9 –10, ca. 4 mm; filaments very short; anthers oblong. Female flowers: calyx lobes broadly elliptic or broadly triangular, ca. 2 mm; ovary ellipsoid; style very short. Drupes ovoid, ca. 1 cm, pruinose, papillose, base with persistent calyx lobes.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. W. J. Tutcher 9183; H. C. Tang 371.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian; Japan.
Ecology: Thin forests and thickets. Flowering: May–Aug.; fruiting: Oct.–Dec.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Hong Kong Island around 1850.

Daphniphyllum oldhamii (Hemsl.) Rosenth. 虎皮楠（交讓木）
Pflanzenr. 68 (IV, 147a): 8. 1919; FRPS 45(1): 6. 1980; FGD 3: 225. 1995.
Daphniphyllum glaucescens Blume var. oldhami Hemsl., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 26: 429. 1894.
Daphniphyllum roxburghii Baill., Euph. 565. 1858; FHK 316. 1861.
Daphniphyllum glaucescens auct. non Blume: FKH 236. 1912.

Shrub or tree, 5–10 m tall. Branchlets lenticellate. Petioles 2–5 cm. Leaves leathery, elliptic-lanceolate or oblong, 5–14 × 2.5–4 cm, base cuneate, rarely rounded, apex obtuse, shortly acuminate or acute, margin entire, abaxially distinctly pruinose and papillose; lateral veins 8 –15 pairs. Racemes axillary, 2–4 cm. Male flowers: calyx 4–5-lobed, lobes triangular, 0.5 –1 mm; stamens 6–9; anthers ovate, ca. 2 mm; filaments not more than 1 mm. Female inflorescence 4–6 cm. Female flowers: calyx 4–5-lobed; ovary ovoid-oblong, pruinose. Drupes ellipsoid or obovoid, 8 × 6 mm, base without persistent calyx lobes.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 669; Y. S. Lau 337.
Distribution: Areas S of Changjiang River; Korea, Japan.
Ecology: By streams in valleys. Flowering: Mar.–May; fruiting: Aug.–Nov.

Aphananthe aspera (Thunb.) Planch. 糙葉樹
Prodr. 17: 208. 1873; FGD 2: 224. 1991; FOC 5: 12. 2003.
Prunus aspera Thunb., Syst. Veg. (ed. 14) 463. 1784.

Tree, 7–20 m tall or more, monoecious. Branchlets slender, scabrous hairy when young. Stipules linear-lanceolate, nearly 1 cm. Petioles 7–15 cm; leaves papery, ovate, narrowly ovate, or rarely subelliptic, 5 –13 × 3 – 6 cm, base broadly cuneate or obtuse, apex attenuate to cuspidate, margin regularly and sharply serrulate except base, sparsely scabrous hairy on both surfaces, denser abaxially, 3-veined and pinninerved; lateral veins 6 –8 pairs, obliquely ascending to teeth. Male cymes fasciculated at base of young branchlets, axillary. Sepals 5, rarely 4, persistent; stamens as many as sepals; ovary hairy. Drupes black when dry, ovoid-globose, 8 –9 mm in diam., scabrous hairy.

Locality: Sha Tau Kok. Y. W. Lam 360.
Distribution: S, E & SW China, Hubei, Shanxi; Korea, Japan, Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Mar.–May; fruiting: Aug.– Oct.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Sha Tin, Tai Po, Lam Tsuen, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Aphananthe cuspidata (Blume) Planch. 滇糙葉樹（坡命工）
Prodr. 17: 209. 1873; FGD 2: 226. 1991; FOC 5: 12. 2003.
Cyclostemon cuspidatum Blume, Bijdr. 599. 1825.
Gironniera nitida Benth., FHK 325. 1861; FKH 243. 1912.
Gironniera cuspidata (Blume) Kurz, For. Fl. Brit. Burma 2: 479. 1877; FHN 2: 370. 1965.

Tree, 10 –18 m tall, dioecious. Branchlets slender, glabrous. Stipules lanceolate , 6–10 mm. Petioles 7–10 mm; leaves leathery, nitid, oblong to ovate-lanceolate, 6–13 × 2–5 cm, base obtuse, apex long acuminate, margin entire, glabrous on both surfaces, pinninerved; lateral veins 6 –10 pairs, anastomosing before reaching margin, or inconspicuously serrate, reticulate veins dense, conspicuous on both surfaces. Male inflorescences short, many-flowered. Male flowers: sepals 4–5, oblanceolate, ca. 2 mm; staminodes becoming a fascicle of yellow hairs. Female inflorescences ca. 1 cm, branched, sometimes 1–2-flowered, axillary; sepals oblong, ca. 12 mm, adnated to ovary. Drupes ovoid, 8 –10 mm in diam., glabrous, beak 3 – 4 mm at tip. Stalk up to 1 cm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Sha Tin, Tai Po, Lam Tsuen, Lantau Island. W. J. Tutcher 589; Y. S. Lau 2682.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Yunnan; India, Sri Lanka, Vietnam, Thailand, Myanmar, Malaysia, Indonesia.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Mar.–May, Sep.–Nov.; fruiting: Jul.–Sep., Nov.–Dec.

Celtis biondii Pamp. 紫彈朴
Nuovo Giorn. Bot. Ital., n.s., 17: 252, fig. 3. 1910; FGD 2: 220. 1991; FOC 5: 17. 2003.

Deciduous tree, 4–18 m tall; young shoots densely red-brown pubescent, glabrescent when old. Petioles 4 –7 mm; leaves leathery, abaxially, often becoming black when dry, ovate or ovate-elliptic, 4 –9 × 2.5 – 4.5 cm, base broadly cuneate, obtuse, oblique, apex acuminate, margin serrate on upper half, often densely strigose abaxially, shorter and sparser adaxially, 3-veined. Sepals 4, elliptic. Stamens 4. Drupes often 2, axillary, subglobose, 6 mm in diam., sparsely pubescent when young. Fruits stalk 12–15 mm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Peng Chau. Y. W. Lam 22271; F. W. Xing 9125.
Distribution: S, E, & C China, Gansu, Shaanxi; Japan, Korea.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Mar.–May.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Common in Hong Kong and widely planted
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Celtis sinensis Pers. 朴樹
Syn. Pl. 1: 292. 1805; FHK 324. 1861; FKH 243. 1912, p.p.; FHN 2: 368. 1965; FGD 2: 220. 1965; FOC 5: 18. 2003.

Deciduous tree, about 10 m tall; bark grey. Young shoots pubescent, glabrescent when old. Petioles 5–10 mm; leaves ovate or ovate-oblong, 5 –10 × 2.5 –5 cm, base rounded and slightly oblique, apex shortly acuminate, margin serrate on upper half, pubescent on both surfaces when young, glabrescent when old, prominently 3-veined. Male cymes at lower part of annual branchlets. Female flowers: axillary at upper branchlets; sepals 4; stamens 4, opposite to sepals; filaments hairy at base; ovary ovate, grown on densely white tomentose torus; style 2, reflexed. Drupes red-brown, subglobose, 5–7 mm in diam., fruit stalk equal or slightly longer than petioles.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong and widely planted. H. C. Tang 519; Y. W. Lam 897.
Distribution: S, E, C & SW China.
Ecology: Thin forests. Flowering: Mar.–May; fruiting: Sep.– Oct.
Uses: Timber, fibre.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Sha Tin, Shing Mun, Lam Tsuen, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Celtis timorensis Span. 假玉桂
Linnaea 15: 343. 1841; FOC 5: 16. 2003.
Celtis cinnamomea Lindl. ex Planch., Ann. Sci. Nat. ser. 3, Bot. 10: 303. 1848; FGD 2: 221, fig. 142. 1991.
Celtis philippensis auct. non Blanco: FHK 324. 1861; FKH 243. 1912; FHN 2: 368. 1965; FGD 2: 221. 1991.

Tree, 5–8 m tall. Branchlets slender, adpressedly red-brown pubescent when young. Petioles ca. 1 cm; leaves subleathery, ovate to ovate-lanceolate, 5 –15 × 2.5 – 6 cm, base oblique, obtuse or cuneate, apex acuminate, often cuspidate, entire or obscurely serrulate upper most, 3-veined. Cymes 2–3-branched, 15 –25 mm, elongated to 3.5–4 cm when fruiting, adpressed red-brown pubescent. Sepals 4, oblong, ciliate; styles 2. Drupes ellipsoid, 8 × 5 mm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Sha Tin, Shing Mun, Lam Tsuen, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 841, 2970.
Distribution: Xizang, Yunnan, Guizhou, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; E Asia.
Ecology: Flowering: Mar.–May.
Uses: Fibre, timber.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Tai Wai, Tai Po Kau, Lam Tsuen, Sheung Wo Hang, Bride's Pool
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Gironniera subaequalis Planch. 白顏樹
Ann. Sci. Nat., Bot., ser. 3, 10: 229. 1848; FHN 2: 371. 1965; FGD2: 227. 1991; FOC 5: 11. 2002.
Gironniera chinensis Benth., FHK 321. 1861; FKH 243. 1912.

Tree, 10 –20(–30) m tall; bark grey or dark grey. Branchlets yellow-green, sparsely yellow-brown hirsute. Stipules paired, lanceolate, 1–2.5 cm, enclosing bud. Leaves leathery, elliptic or elliptic-oblong, 10 –25 × 5–10 cm, base rounded or broad-cuneate, apex shortly caudate, margin subentire or sparsely and obtusely serrate at upper most, glabrous adaxially, scabrous on nerves abaxially; lateral veins 8 –12 pairs. Cymes paired, axillary; male cymes many branched, female racemose. Male flowers: sepals 5, broad-elliptic, margin membranaceous. Drupes yellow, elliptic, 4 –5 cm in diam., hirsute when young, with persistent sepals and styles.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Wai, Tai Po Kau, Lam Tsuen, Sheung Wo Hang, Bride's Pool. H. C. Tang 1921; Y. W. Lam 606.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; Indochina, Thailand, Myanmar, Sri Lanka, Malaysia, Indonesia.
Ecology: Flowering: Feb.–Apr.; fruiting: Jul.–Nov.
Uses: Timber, medicinal (folklore).

Trema cannabina Lour. 光葉山黃麻
Fl. Cochinch. 2: 563. 1790; FGD 2: 224. 1991; FOC 5: 15. 2003.

Shrub or small tree to 6 m tall, monoecious. Branchlets slender, with appressed pubescence when young, later glabrescent. Petiole 0.6–1 cm, with appressed hairs; leaves nearly membranous, ovate, long ovate or ovate-lanceolate, 4–10 × 1.5–4 cm, base rounded, truncate or shallowly cordate, apex acuminate to caudate-acuminate, margin crenate-serrate; smooth to slightly scabrous adaxially, glabrous abaxially except for scattered tightly appressed hairs on main veins, basally 3-veined; lateral veins usually 3 pairs. Cymes as long as petiole or slightly longer, subglabrous. Male flowers ca. 1 mm in diam. Female flowers ca. 2 mm in diam. Drupes ovoid-globose, ca. 3 mm in diam., shortly stalked, rugate when dry.

Locality: Shing Mun. HK sheet 40449.
Distribution: S, E & SE China; E & SE Asia, Australia, Pacific islands.
Ecology: Thickets and open places. Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: Nov.
Uses: Fibre.

Trema orientalis (L.) Blume 異色山黃麻
Mus. Bot. 2: 62. 1852; FHN 2: 369. 1965; FGD 2: 223. 1991; FOC 5: 13. 2003.
Celtis orientalis L., Sp. Pl. 1044. 1753.

Tree or shrub, up to 20 m. Branchlets grey-brown, hairy. Leaves leathery, ovate-oblong or ovate, 10 –18 × 5 –9 cm, base cordate, slightly oblique, apex acuminate or acute, margin serrulate, discolour on both surfaces, pale green or grey-green adaxially, grey-white or greenish-grey and densely pubescent abaxially, 3-veined; lateral veins 4 – 6 pairs. Male cymes 1.8 –2.5 cm. Male flowers: 1.5 –2 mm in diam., sessile; sepals 5, ovate-oblong, puberulent outside, ciliate. Female inflorescence 1–2.5 cm. Female flowers: stalked; sepals 5–4, triangular-ovate, 1–1.5 mm. Drupes black, subglobose, slightly compressed, 2.5 –3.5 mm in diam., slightly wrinkled. Seeds ovoid, 2–3 mm in diam.

Locality: Shek Kong. P. S. Choi 432; HK sheet 34720.
Distribution: S & SW China, Fujian, Taiwan; S flank of Himalayas, India, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, Myanmar, Indochina, Malay Peninsula, Indonesia, Philippines, Japan, Polynesia, Australia to Tropical Africa.
Ecology: Forests or open places. Flowering: May–Aug.; fruiting: Jun.–Nov.
Uses: Fibre.

Trema tomentosa (Roxb.) Hara 山黃麻
Fl. E. Himalaya 2nd. Rep. 19. 1971; FOC 5: 13. 2003.
Celtis tomentosa Roxb., Fl. Ind., ed. Carey 2: 66. 1832.
Trema amboinensis (Willd.) Blume, Mus. Bot. 2: 61. 1852, p.p.; FKH 243. 1912.
Celtis amboinensis Willd., Sp. Pl., ed. 4., 4(2): 997. 1805, p.p.
Sponia velutina Planch., Ann. Sci. Nat. Bot. 10: 327. 1848, p.p.; FHK 324. 1861.

Small tree or shrub, up to 10 m tall. Branchlets densely tomentose. Leaves broadly ovate or ovate-oblong, rarely broadly lanceolate, 7–5 × 3 –7 cm, base cordate, distinctly oblique, apex acuminate or cuspidate, rarely acute, margin serrulate, concolour on both surfaces, very rough and hirsute adaxially, brown or grey brown pubescent abaxially, 3-veined; lateral veins 4 –5 pairs. Male cymes 2–4.5 cm. Male flowers: 1.5 –2 mm in diam., subsessile; sepals 5, ovate-oblong, puberulous outside, ciliate; stamens 5; rudimentary ovary obovateoblong. Female inflorescences 1–2 cm. Female flowers: shortly stalked; sepals 5–4, triangular-ovate, 1–1.5 mm; ovary glabrous. Drupes brown-black or purple-black, ovoid, 2–3 mm in diam., irregularly rugate, with persistent calyx. Seeds ovoid, 1.5 –2 mm in diam.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 935, 2128.
Distribution: Xizang, Sichuan, Yunnan, Guizhou, Guangxi, Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian, Taiwan; Sikkim, Bhutan, Nepal, India, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, Myanmar, Indochina, Malaysia, Indonesia, Philippines, Japan, islands of South Pacific.
Ecology: Flowering: Dec.; fruiting: Apr. of the following year.
Uses: Materials (fibre, timber), medicinal (folklore).

Humulus scandens (Lour.) Merr. 葎草
Trans. Amer. Philos. Soc., n.s., 24: 138. 1935; FGD 6: 107. 2005; FOC 5: 75. 2003.
Antidesma scandens Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 1: 157. 1790.
Humulus japonicus Sieb. & Zucc., Fl. Jap. 2: 89. 1849.

Stems, branches and petioles with retrorse spines. Leaves papery, palmately 5 –7-lobed, rarely 3-lobed, 7–10 × 7–10 cm, base cordate, rough on both surfaces, sparsely strigose, pubescent and with yellow glands abaxially, lobes ovate to broadly lanceolate, margin serrulate, apex acute. Male flowers: small, yellowish green in laxly paniculate cyme, axillary; sepals 5; stamens 5; anthers pendulous on filaments. Female flowers in cone-like spikes of 5 mm in diam. Bracts violet, brown-green, triangular, apex acuminate, spinulose. Ovary enclosed by bracts; style 2, exserted from bracts. Infructescences 0.5 –1.5 cm. Achenes enclosed within enlarged calyx, compressedglobose, 5 mm in diam.

Locality: Sai Kung. Exotic. P. S. Choi s.n. (HK sheet 36004, 36005).
Distribution: Widely distributed in China except Xinjiang and Qinghai; Russia (Asian region), Japan, Korea, Vietnam.
Ecology: Wasteland, roadside, near villages. Flowering: Summer to autumn.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Artocarpus heterophyllus Lam. 菠蘿蜜
Encyl. 3: 209. 1789; FHN 2: 381. 1964; FGD 1: 182. 1987; FOC 5: 31. 2003.
Artocarpus intergrifolia auct. non L. f.: FKH 247. 1912.
Artocarpus macrocarpon Dancer, Cat. Bot. Gard. Jamaica: 1. 1792; Check List HK Plants 59. 2002, “macrocarpus”.

Tree, 10 –20 m tall; old trees buttressed. Petioles 1–3 cm; leaves spirally arranged, elliptic or obovate, 7–15 × 3 –7 cm, base cuneate, apex obtuse or acuminate, margin entire (young trees or germinate shoots often divided), glabrous adaxially, slightly coarse abaxially; lateral veins 6–8 pairs. Heads on trunk or on brachyblasts. Male heads cylindric or clavate-elliptic, 2–7 cm; peduncles 1–5 cm. Syncarps yellow-brown, ellipsoid to globose, or with irregular form, 30 –100 × 25 –50 cm, with stiff hexagonal tubercles and thick hairs.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 6569, 25816.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian (cultivated); native to India, widely cultivated in tropical regions.
Ecology: Flowering: Spring to summer; fruiting: Summer to autumn.
Uses: Food (fruit), timber, medicinal (folklore).

Artocarpus hypargyreus Hance ex Benth. 白桂木
FHK 325. 1861, “hypargyrea”; FKH 248. 1912; FHN 2: 383. 1965; FGD 1: 185. 1987; FOC 5: 33. 2003.
Ficus laceratifolia auct. non Lévl. & Van.: FKH 246. 1912.

Large tree, 10–25 m tall; bark dark purple. Young branches white pubescent. Petioles 1.5–2 cm, hairy; leaves leathery, oblong, elliptic to obovate, 8–15 × 4–7 cm, base cuneate, apex narrowacuminate, margin entire or slightly sinuate-toothed (leaves of young trees often pinnately divided), glabrous and shining adaxially, rough with powdery white tomentum abaxially; lateral veins 6–7 pairs, reticulate veins raised and pubescent. Head solitary, axillary. Male heads obovoid to ellipsoid, 1.5–2 × 1–1.5 cm; peduncles 2–4.5 cm, hairy. Male flowers: perianth 4-lobed, lobes spathulate plumosehairy, adnated to clavate or subpeltate bracts; stamen 1, anther ellipsoid. Female heads rather smaller. Female flowers: perianth densely hairy; style shortly protruding. Syncarps subglobose, 3–4 cm in diam., yellowish to orange, brown pubescent, slightly papillary on surfaces; stalk 3–5 cm; pubescent.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 587; Y. S. Lau 1958.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian.
Ecology: Flowering: May–Aug.; fruiting: Jun.–Aug.
Uses: Timber, food (fruit).
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Hong Kong Island by H. F. Hance around 1850. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Artocarpus nitidus Trécul subsp. lingnanensis (Merr.) F. M. Jarrett 桂木（紅桂木）
J. Arnold Arbor. 41: 124. 1960; FHN 2: 382. 1965; FGD 1: 182. 1987; FOC 5: 33. 2003.
Artocarpus lingnanensis Merr., Lingnan Sci. J. 7: 302. 1929.

Tree to 17 m tall. Bark black to brown, longitudinally fissured. Branchlets wrinkled, appressed puberulent, rapidly glabrescent. Stipules lanceolate, caducous. Petiole 0.5 –1.5 cm; leaves distichous, thinly leathery, oblong-elliptic to obovate-elliptic, 7–15 × 3 –7 cm, base cuneate to ± rounded, apex mucronate to caudate, margin entire or irregularly shallowly toothed, glabrous on both surfaces; secondary veins 6 –10 on each side of midvein, adaxially prominent. Male inflorescences capitate, obovoid, or oblong, 2.5 –12 × 2.7–7 mm. Peduncle of female inflorescences 1.5 –5 mm. Male flowers: perianth-lobes 2– 4, basally connate for 0.5 – 0.5 mm. Syncarps red when mature, ± globose, with coarse pubescence.

Locality: Cultivated.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan; Vietnam, Cambodia, Thailand.
Ecology: Flowering: Mar.–May; fruiting: May–Sep.
Uses: Timber, food (fruit).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Ma On Shan, Tai Po, Wu Kau Tang
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Artocarpus styracifolius Pierre 二色菠蘿蜜
Bull. Soc. Bot. France 2: 492. 1905,“styracifolia”; FHN 2: 382. 1965; FGD 1: 183. 1987; FOC 5: 32. 2003.

Tree, up to 20 m tall; young branchlets densely white pubescent. Petioles 8 –14 mm, hairy; leaves distichous, oblong or obovatelanceolate, sometimes elliptic, 4– 8 × 2.5 –3 cm, base cuneate, slightly decurrent, apex caudate, margin entire (young leaves often lobed), white powdery hairy abaxially; lateral veins 4 –7 pairs. Head axillary, solitary. Male heads elliptic, obovate or cyclindric, 6–12 × 4 –7 mm, densely white pubescent. Female heads yellow, red-brown when dry, globose, 6 –10 mm in diam. Syncarps globose, 4 cm in diam., villose, with many cylindric protuberances on surfaces; achenes globose.

Locality: Ma On Shan, Tai Po, Wu Kau Tang. Y. W. Lam 889; P. S. Choi s.n. (HK sheet 38342).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou; Vietnam, Laos.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Jun.–Aug.; fruiting: Aug.–Dec.
Uses: Timber, food (fruit).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Shing Mun, Tai Po, Lam Tsuen, Lai Chi Wo
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Artocarpus tonkinensis A. Chev. ex Gagnep. 胭脂樹
Bull. Soc. Bot. France 73: 90. 1926; FHN 2: 383. 1965; FGD 1: 184. 1987; FOC 5: 34. 2003.

Tree, 14 –16 m tall. Branchlets reddish-brown, adpressedly pubescent. Petioles 4–10 mm, puberulent; leaves elliptic, obovate or oblong, 8–20 × 4–10 cm, base rounded or cuneate, apex acute, margin entire or shallowly serrate, densely puberulent abaxially; lateral veins 6 –9 pairs, midvein purple-red when dry. Heads axillary, solitary. Male heads obovoid or ellipsoid, 0.8–1.5 cm wide; peduncles shorter than head. Bracts peltate. Male flowers: perianth 2–3-lobed, ciliate; stamen 1. Female heads globose. Female flowers: perianth perfectly confluent. Syncarps yellow, subglobose, 6.5 cm in diam.; stalk 3–4 cm. Achenes ellipsoid, 12–15 × 9–12 mm.

Locality: Shing Mun, Tai Po, Lam Tsuen, Lai Chi Wo. L. T. Lo 261.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou, Fujian; Vietnam, Cambodia.
Ecology: Flowering: Spring to summer; fruiting: Autumn to winter.
Uses: Timber, food (fruit).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Sha Tin, Ho Chung, Tai Mo Shan, Bride's Pool, Tai Po Kau, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Broussonetia kaempferi Sieb. var. australis Suzuki 藤構（葡蟠）
Trans. Nat. Hist. Soc. Taiwan 24: 433. 1934; FOC 5: 27. 2003.
Broussonetia kaempferi auct. non Sieb.: FKH 244. 1912

Climber, with milky juice, dioecious. Branches and branchlets elongate, brown pubescent when young. Leaves alternate, ovate-elliptic, 3.5–8 × 2–3 cm, base rounded or cordate, apex acuminate to caudate, margin serrulate, scabrous adaxially, pubescent abaxially. Male spikes 1.5–2.5 cm. Male flowers: perianth 4–3-parted; segments hairy abaxially; stamens 4–3, pistillode minute. Female heads globose. Female flowers: perianth hairy; style filiform, reddish violet. Syncarps red, globose, 1 cm in diam., with persistent exserted styles.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Sha Tin, Ho Chung, Tai Mo Shan, Bride's Pool, Tai Po Kau, Lantau Island. D. P. M. Guile s.n. (HK sheet 30347); P. S. Choi 350.
Distribution: Areas S of Qinling Range; Korea, Japan, Vietnam.
Ecology: Thickets. Flowering: Feb.–Jun.; fruiting: Mar.–Jul.
Uses: Fibre, medicinal (folklore).

Broussonetia papyrifera (L.) L'Hérit. ex Vent. 構樹
Tabl. Regn. Veg. 3: 458. 1799; FHN 2: 378. 1965; FGD 1: 178. 1987; FOC 5: 26. 2003.
Morus papyrifera L., Sp. Pl. 986. 1753.

Tree, 10 –20 m tall, dioecious. Branchlets densely pubescent. Stipules ovate, 1.5–2 × 0.8–1 cm. Petioles 2.5–8 cm; leaves thick papery, broad-ovate or oblong-ovate, 6–18 × 5–9 cm, base cordate, unequal, apex acuminute, margin serrulate or 3 –5-lobed, scabrous and sparsely hirsute adaxially, densely tomentose abaxially, basal veins 3; lateral veins 6 –7 pairs. Male catkin cylindrical, 4 – 8 cm. Male flowers: perianth 4-lobed, hairy; stamens 4. Female heads globose, bracts clavate. Female flowers: perianth tubular, apex adnated with style; ovary ovoid. Syncarps red, globose, 1.5–3 cm in diam., fleshy; bracts and perianth persistent, clustered together; achenes red, pericarp crustaceous.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 2350.
Distribution: Areas S of Shanxi Province; Japan, India, Vietnam.
Ecology: Wasteland, roadsides. Flowering: Mar.–May; fruiting: Apr.–Aug.
Uses: Fibre.

Fatoua villosa (Thunb.) Nakai 水蛇麻
Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 41: 516. 1927; FOC 5: 22. 2003.
Urtica villosa Thunb. ex Murray, Syst. Veg. ed. 14, 851. 1784.
Fatoua pilosa auct. non Gaudich.: FKH 244. 1912; FHN 2: 372. 1965; FGD 1: 169. 1987.a

Annual herb, 30–80 cm tall, few-branched. Branches slender, slightly villose. Petioles long, slender; leaves membranaceous, broad-ovate, 5 –10 × 3 –5 cm, base cordate or cuneate, slightly decurrent, apex acute, margin crenate-dentate, triplinerved; lateral veins 3 –11 each side, roughly and appressed-pilose on both surfaces. Cymes axillary, 5 mm in diam.; male and female flowers mixed together. Male flowers: perianth campanulate, 4-lobed; stamens 4, exserted, opposite perianth-lobes. Female flowers: perianth-lobes boat-shaped; ovary slightly compressed-globose; style lateral, filiform, 1–1.5 mm. Achenes compressed-trigonous, 1 mm, with dispersed, raised, minute spots, 1-seeded.

Locality: Causeway Bay. HK sheet 6429; H. C. Tang 1413.
Distribution: Anhui, Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hainan, Hebei, Henan, Hubei, Jiangsu, Jiangxi, Taiwan, Yunnan, Zhejiang; E & SE Asia to Australia, New Caledonia.
Ecology: Roadsides and by streams. Flowering and fruiting: Late spring to autumn.

Ficus altissima Blume 高山榕（雞榕）
Bijdr. 444. 1825; FKH 246. 1912; FHN 2: 391. 1965; FGD 1: 196. 1987; FOC 5: 43. 2003.

Large tree, 25–30 m tall; bark grey, glabrous. Young branchlets puberulent. Stipules 2–3 cm, grey sericeous. Petioles 2–5 cm; leaves thick leathery, broadly ovate to ovate-elliptic, 10–19 × 8–11 cm, base broadly cuneate, apex obtuse or acute, margin entire, glabrous on both surfaces; lateral veins 5–7 pairs. Figs paired, axillary, elliptic-ovoid, 17–28 mm in diam., enclosed within cauducous bracts when young, red or yellowish when ripen, apex umbilicate-salient, basal bracts short, broadly obtuse, leaving annular scars after falling off. Male flowers scattered in inner walls of figs; perianth 4-parted, membranous; stamen 1. Perianth of gall and female flowers as in male flowers. Achenes verrucose; style elongated.

Locality: Cultivated. Caine Rd. Y. S. Lau 1154; P. S. Choi s.n. (HK sheet 36186).
Distribution: Xizang, Yunnan, Guangxi, Hainan, Guangdong; SE Asia.
Ecology: Forests, margins of forests. Flowering and fruiting: Mar.– Oct.
Uses: Ornamental, host of lac insect.

Ficus benjamina L. 垂葉榕
Mant. 1: 129. 1767; FHN 2: 392. 1965; FGD 1: 196. 1987; FOC 5: 45. 2003.

Large tree, up to 20 m tall; crown broad, aerial roots pendulous from large branches, reaching ground and rooting, forming new trunks with drooping branches; bark grey, glabrous. Branchlets pendulous. Stipules lanceolate, ca. 6 mm. Petioles 1–2 cm; leaves thinly leathery, ovate to ovate-elliptic, 4–8 × 2–4 cm, base rounded or cuneate, apex abruptly acuminate, margin entire, not 3-veined at base; lateral veins many, parallel, fine, connected at margins. Figs paired or single, red, yellow or orange, globose or compressed-globose, 0.8–1.5 cm in diam., glabrous, basal bracts 3, triangular-ovate; male, female and gall flowers in one set. Male flowers: few, shortly pedicellate; perianth-lobes 4, broadly ovate; stamen 1; filament short. Gall flowers: many, pedicellate; perianth-lobes 4–5, narrowly spathulate; ovary ovoid; style lateral. Female flowers: sessile; perianth-lobes 3, shortly spathulate. Achenes ovate-reniform, shorter than style; styles sublateral; stigma dilated.

Locality: Cultivated. C. I. Lei 92.
Distribution: S to SW China; S Asia to Australia.
Ecology: Flowering and fruiting: Sep.–Nov.
Uses: Roadside tree.

Ficus concinna (Miq.) Miq. 雅榕
Ann. Mus. Bot. Lugd.-Bat. 3: 286. 1867; FGD 1: 198. 1987; FOC 5: 40. 2003.
