Tree, 15–20 m tall; bark dark grey, lenticellate. Branchlets thick, glabrous. Stipules lanceolate, ca. 1 cm. Petioles short; leaves alternate, elliptic, 5 –10 × 1.5 – 4 cm, base cuneate, apex acute to acuminate, margin entire, glabrous on both surfaces; lateral veins 4–8 pairs, conspicuously, net-veined. Figs light blue-purple, sometimes with yellow spots, paired or 3– 4-clustered, axillary, globose, 5–8 mm in diam., basal bracts minute; peduncles 1–5 mm; male, female and gall flowers in one set. Male flowers: few, near mouth, perianth-lobes 2, lanceolate; ovary oblique-ovate; style lateral, stigma round. Gall flowers similar to female flowers; style filiform, short.

Locality: Ma On Shan Village. Y. W. Lam 1675.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Yunnan.
Ecology: Flowering and fruiting: May– Oct.

Ficus elastica Roxb. ex Hornem. 印度榕（印度橡樹）
Fl. Ind. 3: 543. 1832; FHN 2: 391. 1965; FGD 1: 196. 1987; FOC 5: 42. 2003.

Large tree, 20–30 m tall. Branchlets thick. Stipules membranaeous, up to 10 cm, leaving annular scars on branches after falling down. Petioles 2–5 cm; leaves thick leathery, oblong or elliptic, 8–30 × 4 –11 cm, base rounded, apex acute, margin entire, shining abaxially, midvein distinct; lateral veins many, parallel. Figs paired, borne on axils of leaf scars, ovate-oblong, 10 × 5–8 mm, male, gall and female flowers in one set. Male flowers: pedicellate; perianth-lobes 4, ovate, stamens 1. Gall flowers: perianth-lobes 4, ovary glabrous; style subsessile, curved. Female flowers: sessile. Achenes ovoid, verrucose, persistent style long; stigma subcapitate.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 25431; P. S. Choi s.n. (HK sheet 35991).
Distribution: Cultivated in S to SW China. Widely cultivated in tropical and subtropical regions; native to Sikkim, NE India, Myanmar, N Malaysia, Indonesia.
Ecology: Flowering and fruiting: Sep.–Nov.
Uses: Ornamental.

Ficus erecta Thunb. 天仙果
Diss. Ficus 5. 1786; FKH 246. 1912; FOC 5: 54. 2003.
Ficus erecta Thunb. var. beecheyana (Hook. & Arn.) King, Ann. Bot. Gard. Calcutta 1(2): 142, pl. 178A. 1888; FRPS 23(1): 134. 1998; FGD 1: 208. 1987.

Small tree or shrub, 2–7 m tall. Branchlets densely hirsute. Stipules caducous. Petioles 1–4 cm, slender, densely white hirsute; leaves thick papery, obovate-elliptic, 7–20 × 3 –9 cm, base rounded to shallowly cordate, apex shortly acuminate, margin entire or rarely undulate on upper margin, surfaces scabrous, sparsely pubescent adaxially, pubescent abaxially; lateral veins 5–7 pairs. Figs yellow-red or purple-black, solitary axillary, globose or pyriform, 1.2–2 cm in diam., terminal bracts umbilicate, basal bracts 3, ovate-triangular, male and gall flowers in one set, female flowers in another set. Male flowers: pedeicellate or sessile; perianth-lobes 3 or 2– 4, elliptic to ovate-lanceolate; stamens 2–3. Gall flowers: subsessile or shortly pedicellate; perianth-lobes 3 –5, lanceolate, hairy; ovary ellipsoid-globose; style lateral; stigma 2- fid. Female flowers; perianth-lobes 4 –6, broadly spathulate; ovary glabrous, shortly stalked; style lateral; stigma 2-fid.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 382, 597.
Distribution: SW to SE China; Japan, Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests or thickets. Flowering and fruiting: Apr.–Sep.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Ma On Shan, Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai, Ta Tit Yan
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Ficus esquiroliana H. Lév. 黃毛榕（馬鞍天仙果）
Bull. Acad. Int. Geogr. Bot. 24: 252. 1914; Hill, Figs. Hongk. 59, pl. 39. 1967; FOC 5: 60. 2003.
Ficus fulva auct. non Reinw. ex Blume: FKH 247. 1912; FHN 2: 390. 1965; FGD 1: 193. 1987.

Small tree or shrub, 4–10 m tall; bark with longitudinal ridges. Young branchlets yellow hirsute, hollowed at center. Stipules lanceolate, 1–1.5 cm, caducous. Petioles 5 –11 cm, sparsely brown hirsute; leaves alternate, thick papery, broadly ovate, but lobed when young, 17–27 × 12–20 cm, base shallow-cordate, apex caudate, tip ca. 1 cm, margin serrulate, teeth point pilose, sparsely strigose adaxially, long or short, brown-yellow or grey white hairy; basal veins 5 –7, lateral veins 5 – 6 pairs. Figs paired, sessile, axillary, conic-ovoid, 20 –25 mm in diam., light brown hairy; basal bracts ovate-lanceolate, 8 mm, terminal bracts umbilicate. Male flowers at inner wall of mouth, stipitate; perianth-lobes 4; stamens 2. Gall flowers same as female flowers; perianth-lobes 5; ovary globose, glabrous; style lateral, short; stigma funnel-shaped. Achenes obliquely ovoid, verrucose.

Locality: Ma On Shan, Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai, Ta Tit Yan. HK sheet 25476, 32110.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Xizang, Fujian; S to SE Asia.
Ecology: Forests or along streams. Flowering and fruiting: May–Nov.

Ficus fistulosa Reinw. ex Blume 水同木
Bijdr. 442. 1825; FGD 1: 192. 1987; FOC 5: 50. 2003.
Ficus harlandii Benth., FHK 330. 1861; FKH 247. 1912; FHN 2: 388. 1965.

Small tree; bark black-brown. Stipules ovate-lanceolate, ca. 1.7 cm. Petioles 1.5–4 cm; leaves alternate, papery, obovate to oblong, 10–20 × 4–7 cm, base oblique cuneate or rounded, apex mucronate, margin entire or repand, glabrous adaxially, slightly pubescent or minutely punctate-scabrous abaxially; basal veins short, lateral veins 6–9 pairs. Figs clustered on verrucose brachyblast from old wood, orange, subglobose, 1.5–2 cm in diam., glabrous. Peduncles 8–24 mm, male and gall flowers in one set, pedicellate. Male flowers near mouth, few; perianth-lobes 3–4; stamen 1, filaments short. Gall flowers: perianth-lobes very short or absent; ovary glabrous, obovoid; style sublateral, slender; stigma ampliate. Female flowers: in another set; perianth tubular, enclosed lower part of fruit stalk. Achenes rhomboidal, verrucose; style elongated, clavate.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 2196; Y. S. Lau 1970.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; S to SE Asia.
Ecology: Forests in valleys or by streams. Flowering and fruiting: Mar.–Dec.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Mo Shan, Tai Po Kau
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Ficus formosana Maxim. 台灣榕
Bull. Acad. Imp. Sci. Saint-Petersbourg 27: 546. 1881; FKH 246. 1912; FHN 2: 397. 1965; FGD 1: 206. 1987; FOC 5: 58. 2003.
Ficus formosana var. shimadai (Hayata) W. C. Chen, FGD. 1: 207. 1987, nom. illeg.
Ficus formosana f. shimadai Hayata, Ic. Pl. Form. 8: 118. 1919.

Shrub, 1.5 –3 m tall. Branchlets sparsely pilose. Stipules linear-lanceolate, 0.5 cm. Petioles 0.7–1 cm; leaves membranaceous, oblanceolate to linear, 4–11 × 1.5–3.5 cm, base narrowly cuneate, apex acuminate, margin entire or rarely coarsely dentate; lateral veins 5–15 pairs. Figs green with reddish, solitary, axillary, ovoid-globose, 6 –9 cm in diam., apex mucronate, basal bracts 3; stalk stout, 0.5–1 cm; male and gall or female flowers mixed. Male flowers: perianth-lobes 3–4, ovate; stamens 2, rarely 3. Gall flowers: perianth-lobes 4–5; ovary globose, stipitate; style lateral. Female flowers: pedicellate or sessile; perianth-lobes 4; styles elongated; stigma infundibular.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Tai Po Kau. HK sheet 36154, 36288, 36249.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering and fruiting: Mar.–Dec.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Shing Mun, Tai Po Kau
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Ficus hederacea Roxb. 藤榕（爬牆榕）
Fl. Ind. 3: 538. 1832; FHN 2: 398. 1965; FGD 1: 211. 1987; FOC 5: 68. 2003.

Climber. Young branchlets pubescent. Petioles 10 –20 mm; leaves distichous, thickly leathery, elliptic to ovate-elliptic, 6–11 × 3.5 –5 cm, base broadly cuneate or obtuse, apex obtuse, rarely round, margin entire, hairy when young, papillary on both surfaces; lateral veins 3–5 pairs. Figs simple or paired, axillary, globose, 7–14 mm in diam., apex umbonulate; basal bracts connate below medium, upper 3-lobed. Peduncles 10–12 mm. Male flowers: few, sparsely, sessile; perianth-lobes 3– 4; stamens 2, filaments free. Gall flowers: pedicellate; perianth-lobes 4, lanceolate; ovary black, obovate; style short, subterminal; stigma curved. Female flowers: pedicellate, in another figs; perianth-lobes 4, linear. Achenes ellipsoid, keeled abaxially; style elongated.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Shing Mun, Tai Po Kau. C. Ford s.n. (HK 25645); Y. S. Lau 482.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang; S to SE Asia.
Ecology: Forests, on rocks. Flowering and fruiting: Feb.–Jul.

Ficus hirta Vahl 粗葉榕（牛奶仔）
Enum. Pl. 2: 203. 1806; FHK 328. 1861; FKH 247. 1912; FGD 1: 194. 1987; FOC 5: 60. 2003.
Ficus simplicissima var. hirta Migo in Bull. Shanghai Sci. Inst. 14: 331. 1944; FHN 2: 390. 1965.

Shrub or small tree. Young branchlets shollowed, branchlets, leaves and figs golden hirsute. Stipules red, ovate-lanceolate, 1–3 cm. Petioles 2–8 cm; leaves alternate, papery, very variable in shape, oblong-lanceolate to broadly ovate, 10 –25 cm, base rounded, shallow-cordate, or broadly cuneate, apex acute or acuminate, margin serrulate, entire or deeply 3 –5-lobed, basal veins 3 –5; lateral veins 4 –7 pairs. Figs paired, axillary, or on leafless branches, globose or ellipsoid, 10–15 mm in diam., sessile or subsessile, apex umbonulate, basal bracts ovate-lanceolate. Male flowers near mouth, pedicellate; perianth-lobes 4, red, lanceolate; stamens 2–3; anthers longer than filament. Gall flowers: perianthlobes 4; ovary globose; style lateral; stigma infundibular. Female flowers: pedicellate or sessile; perianth-lobes 4. Achenes ellipsoid, glabrous; style elongated; stigma clavate.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 36; Y. S. Lau 2319.
Distribution: SW to SE China; S to SE Asia.
Ecology: Forests, thickets, near villages by streams. Flowering and fruiting: almost all year round.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Ficus hispida L. f. 對葉榕
Suppl. Pl. 442. 1781; FHK 329. 1861; FKH 247. 1912; FHN 2: 387. 1965; FGD 1: 190. 1987; FOC 5: 49. 2003.

Shrub or small tree; young branches hispid. Stipules ovate-lanceolate, often 4, decussate. Petioles 1– 4 cm, hispid; leaves mostly opposite, thickly papery, ovate or obovate to oblong, 10 –25 × 5 –10 cm, base rounded to cuneate, apex shortly acuminate, margin entire or crenateserrate, very rough on both surfaces with stiff hairs; lateral veins 6 –9 pairs. Figs yellow, axillary or 2–3 together on leafless branches of old stem, turbinate, 1.5–2.5 cm in diam., densely hirsute. Male flowers near mouth, many; perianth-lobes 3, membranous; stamen 1, perianth of gall and female flowers truncate, thin and transparent (easily overlooked). Gall flower: style subterminal, short. Female flower: style lateral, hairy.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. HK sheet 6501; L. T. Lo 488.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan; S & SE Asia to Australia.
Ecology: Thickets of wasteland, by streams. Flowering and fruiting: May– Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Ma On Shan, Wu Kau Tang, Lai Chi Wo
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Ficus langkokensis Drake 青藤公
J. Bot. (Morot) 10: 215. 1896; FGD 1: 208. 1987; FOC 5: 53. 2003.

Tree, 6–15 m tall; bark red-brown or grey-yellow. Branchlets slender, ferrugineo-scurfy. Stipules lanceolate, 7–10 mm. Petioles 1–4 cm. Leaves alternate, papery, elliptic-lanceolate to elliptic, 7–19 × 2–6 cm, base broadly cuneate, apex caudate, margin entire, glabrous on both surfaces; basal nerves 3, lateral veins 2–4 pairs. Figs paired or simple, axillary, globose, 5–12 mm in diam., ferrugineo-scurfy, apex umbonulate; basal bracts 3, broadly ovate; peduncles slender, 5–15 mm, ferrugineo-scurfy. Male flowers: pedicellate; perianthlobes 3– 4, ovate; stamens 1–2, filaments short. Female flowers: perianth-lobes 4, obovate, dark red; styles lateral.

Locality: Ma On Shan, Wu Kau Tang, Lai Chi Wo. W. J. Tutcher s.n. (HK sheet 25749); Y. W. Lam 525.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan, Fujian; India, Laos, Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering and fruiting: Feb.–Sep.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Common in Hong Kong. Also widely cultivated
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Ficus microcarpa L. f. 榕樹（細葉榕）
Suppl. Pl. 442. 1781; Corner, Gard. Bull. Singapore 17: 397. 1959; FHN 2: 393. 1965; FGD 1: 198. 1987; FOC 5: 44. 2003.
Ficus retusa auct. non L.: FHK 327. 1861; FKH 246. 1912.

Large tree, 15–25 m tall; bark deep grey, crown ample. Branches often bearing pendulous aerial roots. Stipules lanceolate, 1.5 –3.5 cm. Petioles stout, 5–10 mm, glabrous; leaves leathery, elliptic, ovate-elliptic or obovate, 4–8 × 3–4 cm, base cuneate, apex bluntly apiculate, entire, rarely emarginate, basal veins 3; lateral veins 3–10 pairs. Figs yellowish or reddish, paired or solitary, axillary, obovoid, 6–8 mm in diam., without peduncles, basal bracts 3, oval, persistent; male, gall and female flowers in one set, with few bristles mixed with them. Male flowers: pedicellate or sessile; perianth-lobes 3–4, elliptic to oblanceolate; stamen 1. Gall flowers: pedicellate; perianth-lobes 3–5, broadly spathulate; ovary globose; style lateral, rather long; stigma trumpet-shaped. Female flowers: sessile; perianth-lobes 3–5; ovary ovoid; style slender; stigma acute.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Also widely cultivated. Y. S. Lau 2323; L. Gibbs 7567.
Distribution: SW, S to SE China; S & SE Asia to Australia.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering and fruiting: May–Dec.
Uses: Roadside tree.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Ma On Shan, Mui Tsz Lam, Yim Tso Ha, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Ficus nervosa B. Heyne ex Roth 九丁樹（凸葉榕）
Nov. Pl. Sp. 388. 1819; FHK 327. 1861; FKH 246. 1912; FHN 2: 393. 1965; FGD 1: 200. 1987; FOC 5: 46. 2003.

Medium sized tree; bark dark brown. Branchlets pubescent. Stipules fugacious. Petioles 1.5–2.5 cm, scurfy; leaves leathery, oblanceolate, oblong to elliptic, 6 –15(–20) × 2.5 – 6 cm, base obtuse or cuneate, apex short-acuminate, margin entire, basal nerves 3; lateral veins 7–11 pairs, midvein and lateral veins prominent abaxially. Figs yellow or reddish-brown, solitary or paired, axillary, globose, 1–1.2 cm in diam., glabrous, basal bracts none; stalks slender; male, gall and female flowers mixed in one fig. Male flowers: few near apex of figs; perianthlobes 3–5; stamen 1, filament short. Gall flowers: pedicellate; perianth-lobes 3 – 4; ovary ovoid; style sublateral; stigma clavate. Female flowers: perianth-lobes 3– 4, ovoid; style slender, terminal or sublateral; stigma elongate.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Ma On Shan, Mui Tsz Lam, Yim Tso Ha, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 2271; P. S. Choi s.n. (HK sheet 34799).
Distribution: SW, S to SE China; India, Sri Lanka, Myanmar, Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests, along roadside by streams. Flowering and fruiting: Mar.–Dec.
Uses: Timber.

Ficus pandurata Hance 琴葉榕
Ann. Sci. Nat., Bot., ser. 4, 18: 229. 1862; FHN 2: 400. 1965; FGD 1: 205. 1987; FOC 5: 59. 2003.
Ficus holophylla Migo, Bull. Shanghai Instit. 14: 329. 1944.
Ficus pandurata Hance var. holophylla Migo, Bull. Shanghai Sci. Inst. 14: 329. 1944; Check List HK Plants 27. 2004.

Small shrub, 1–2 m tall. Branchlets white, pubescent when young. Stipules lanceolate. Petioles 3 –5 mm; leaves papery, pendurate, obovate, lanceolate or linear-lanceolate, 3 –15 × 1.2– 6 cm, base rounded or to broadly cuneate, sometimes constricted at middle, apex acute, mucronate, glabrous adaxially, verrucose and sparsely pubescent on nerves abaxially; lateral veins 3 –5 pairs. Figs scarlet, solitary, axillary, elliptic or globose, 4–10 mm in diam., apex umbonate, basal bracts 3, ovate. Peduncles slender, 4 –5 mm. Male flowers: near the mouth; perianth-lobes 4, linear; stamens 3, rarely 2, unequal. Gall flowers: pedicellate or sessile; perianth-lobes 3 – 4, oblanceolate to linear, ovary subglobose; style lateral, very short. Female flowers: perianth-lobes 3 – 4, elliptic; style lateral, elongate; stigma infundibular.

Locality: Cape D'Aguilar, the New Territories. P. S. Choi s.n. (HK sheet 35391); Levine & Kwok s.n. (HK sheet 25463, 25465).
Distribution: SW, S to SE China.
Ecology: Open field, near villages. Flowering and fruiting: Mar.–Nov.

Ficus pumila L. 薜荔（文頭郎）
Sp. Pl. 1060. 1753; FKH 246. 1912; FHN 2: 395. 1965; FGD 1: 212. 1987; FOC 5: 69. 2003.
Ficus stipulata Thunb., Dissert. Ficus 8. 1786; FHK 328. 1861.

Shrub prostrate or creeping, adventitious roots arising from unfruiting branches. Stipules 2, lanceolate, yellow-brown silk hairy. Leaves on sterile branches thin leathery, ovate-cordate, ca. 2.5 cm, base slightly unequal, apex acuminate. Petioles 5–10 mm, very short; leaves on fertile branches leathery, ovate-elliptic, 5–10 × 2–3.5 cm, base rounded to shallow cordate, apex acute to obtuse, margin entire, glabrous adaxially, yellow-brown pubescent abaxially; lateral veins 3–4 pairs, reticulate veins distinct, alveolar. Figs solitary or paired, axillary, yellow-green or reddish, pearshaped or turbinate, 3.5 – 6.5 cm in diam., somewhat pubescent, basal bracts 3, stalk short and thick, 0.5 –1.5 cm, pubescent. Male flowers: long-pedicellate; perianth-lobes 3 – 4; stamens 2, sessile. Gall flowers: long-pedicellate to sessile; perianth-lobes 4, linear; ovary sessile; style lateral; stigma dilated. Female flowers in another fig: long pedicellate or sessile; perianth-lobes 4–5; ovary sessile. Achenes subglobose, mucilaginous.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 714, 2271; Y. S. Lau 1347.
Distribution: Areas S of Changjiang River; Japan, India, Vietnam.
Ecology: On walls and trees. Flowering and fruiting: Apr.– Dec.
Uses: Edible, medicinal (folklore).

Ficus pyriformis Hook. & Arn. 舶梨榕
Bot. Beechey Voy. 216. 1836; FHK 328. 1861; FKH 246. 1912; FHN 2: 396. 1965; FGD 1: 203. 1987; FOC 5: 54. 2003.

Shrub, 1–2 m tall, branchlets hirsute. Stipules red, lanceolate, ca. 1 cm. Petioles 1–1.5 cm; leaves papery, oblanceolate or oblonglanceolate, 4–11 × 2– 4 cm, base cuneate, round, apex obtuse-acuminate, margin entire slightly revolute, puberulent and verrucose abaxially; lateral veins 5 –9 pairs, anastomosing very near margin. Figs solitary, axillary, pear-shaped, 2–3 cm in diam., glabrous, white, maculate, much constricted at base. Male flowers: perianth-lobes 3–4, lanceolate; stamens 2. Gall flowers: perianth-lobes 4, linear; ovary globose; style lateral. Female flowers in another fig; perianth-lobes 3 – 4; ovary reniform; style lateral, elongated. Achenes verrucose.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1347; L. T. Lo 51.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan, Fujian; Vietnam.
Ecology: Along ditches, in thickets. Flowering and fruiting: Feb.–Nov.

Ficus religiosa L. 菩提樹
Sp. Pl. 1059. 1753; FGD 1: 197. 1987; FOC 5: 41. 2003.

Large tree, epiphytic when young, 15 –25 m tall; crown ample. Branchlets grey-brown, pubescent. Stipules small. Petioles slender, articulate, as long as leaf-blade or longer; leaves leathery, triangular-ovate, 9 –17 × 8 –12 cm, base truncate to shallow-cordate, apex caudate, margin entire or undulate, 2–5 cm, basal veins 3; lateral veins 5 –7 pairs. Figs red, globose to oblate, 1–1.5 cm in diam., basal bracts 3, ovoid; peduncles 4–9 mm; male, gall and female flowers in one set. Male flowers: few, near mouth, sessile; perianth-lobes 2–3, involute; stamen 1, filament short. Gall flowers: pedicellate; perianth-lobes 3 – 4; ovary globose, glabrous; style short; stigma dilated, 2-fid. Female flowers: sessile; perianth-lobes 4, broadly lanceolate; style slender; stigma narrow.

Locality: Cultivated. S. P. Lau 15; Y. S. Lau 2261.
Distribution: Cultivated in Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; native to India.
Ecology: Flowering and fruiting: Sep.–Nov.
Uses: Ornamental.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Cultivated in parks and along roadsides
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Ficus rumphii Blume 心葉榕
Bijdr. Fl. Ned. Ind. 437. 1825; FOC 5: 42. 2003.

Tree, ca. 15 m tall, usually epiphytic when young. Bark grey. Stipules caducous, ovate-lanceolate, 1.5–2.5 cm, scar conspicuous. Petiole 6–8 cm, glabrous; leaf blade ± leathery, cordate to ovate-cordate, 6–13 × 6–11 cm, glabrous, base ± cordate to broadly cuneate, apex acuminate; basal lateral veins 5, secondary veins 5 or 6 on each side of midvein. Figs axillary on leafy branchlets, paired or in small clusters on leafless older branchlets, globose, 1–1.5 cm in diam., with dark spots when young, dark purple when mature, sessile; involucral bracts orbicular, small; apical bracts ± navel-like. Male, gall, and female flowers within same fig. Male flowers: few, scattered among other flowers; perianth-lobes 3, lanceolate; stigma clavate. Achenes tuberculate and with adherent liquid; style long; stigma clavate.

Locality: Cultivated in parks and along roadsides.
Distribution: Yunnan; Bhutan, India, Indonesia, Malaysia, Myanmar, Nepal, Sikkim, Thailand, Vietnam.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: May–Sep.
Uses: Ornamental.

Ficus sagittata Vahl 羊乳榕（箭葉榕）
Symb. Bot. 2: 185. 1806; FHN 2: 395. 1965; FGD 1: 204. 1987; FOC 5: 68. 2003.

Tree when mature, epiphytic vine when young; rooting from nodes. Stipules caducous. Petioles ca. 15 mm, slightly pubescent; leaves leathery, ovate to ovate-elliptic, 7–13 × 5 –10 cm, base cordate, apex acute to short-acuminate, margin entire to sinuate, nerves pubescent abaxially when young; basal veins 3 –5, lateral veins 5 – 6 pairs. Figs paired or solitary, axillary, rarely clustered on leafless branches or verrucose brachyblasts, orange, subglobose, 8–15 mm in diam., apex umbonulate, basal bracts 3, base constricted in short stalk. Male flowers: Perianth-lobes 3, ovate; stamens 3; filaments connate. Gall flowers: Perianth-lobes 3; ovary obovate; style lateral, short. Female flowers in another set; perianth-lobes 3. Achenes elliptic; styles long.

Locality: No precise locality. W. J. Tutcher s.n. (HK sheet 6562, 6563).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou; S Asia to Australia.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering and fruiting: Mar.–Dec.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Tai Mun Shan, Tai Mo Shan, Lautau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Ficus sarmentosa Buch. -Ham. ex Smith var. impressa (Champ. ex Benth.) Corner 爬藤榕（凹葉榕）
Gard. Bull. Singapore 18(1): 6. 1960. FHN 2: 398. 1965; FGD 1: 212. 1987; FOC 5: 71. 2003.
Ficus impressa Champ. ex Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 6: 76. 1854; FHK 328. 1861; FKH 246. 1912.

Shrub prostrate or creeping. Stem much branched. Petioles 5 –10 mm; leaves distichous, leathery, oblong, elliptic or lanceolate, 4 –7 × 1–2 cm, base obtuse, apex acuminate; lateral veins 6 – 8 pairs, reticulate veins prominent abaxially. Figs paired, axillary, globose, 7–10 mm in diam., pubescent when young. Basal bracts 3, triangular. Peduncles 5 –15 mm, bristles dispersed in inner wall of figs. Male and gall flowers in one set, female ones in another set. Male flowers: pedicellate; perianth-lobes 3– 4, oblanceolate; stamens 2, filaments very short. Gall flowers: pedicellate; perianth-lobes 4, obovate-spathulate; ovary ellipsoid; style short; stigma shallow-infundibular. Female flowers similar to gall flower; ovary obovoid; style subterminal. Achenes ovoid-ellipsoid, mucilaginous.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Mun Shan, Tai Mo Shan, Lautau Island. HK sheet 6506, 25549.
Distribution: Area S of Hebei; India, Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests and thickets. Flowering and fruiting: May–Dec.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Hong Kong Island by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1850.

Ficus subpisocarpa Gagnep. 筆管榕
Notul. Syst. (Paris) 4: 95. 1927; FOC 5: 40. 2003.
Ficus superba var. japonica auct. non Miq.: Hill, Figs Hongk. 18. 1967; FRPS 23(1): 96. 1998.
Ficus wightiana auct. non Wall. ex Miq.: FHK 327. 1861; FKH 246. 1912; FHN 2: 392. 1965.

Deciduous tree, sometimes with aerial roots; bark black-brown. Branchlets reddish, glabrous. Stipules lanceolate, ca. 2 cm. Petioles 3 –7 cm; leaves alternate or clustered, subpapery, elliptic to oblong, 10–15 × 4 – 6 cm, base round, apex short-acuminate, margin entire or slightly undurate; lateral veins 7–9 pairs. Figs purple-black, solitary or paired, axillary or on leafless branches, oblate, 5 – 8 mm in diam., apex concave, basal bracts 3, bradly ovate; peduncles 3–4 mm; male, gall and female flowers in one set. Male flowers: few, sessile; perianth-lobes 3, broadly ovate; stamen 1, anthers ovate, filament short. Gall flowers: pedicellate or sessile; perianth-lobes 3, lanceolate; ovary stipitate, stigma linear; style short, lateral. Female flowers as gall flowers but ovary sessile; stigma capitate.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 290; Y. S. Lau 1966.
Distribution: S, SW to SE China; E, S to SE Asia.
Ecology: Open field and forests. Flowering and fruiting: Feb.–Sep.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Lam Tsuen Valley, Ng Tung Chai, Ma On Shan, Mau Ping, Wu Kau Tang, Sha Tau Kok
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Ficus subulata Blume 假斜葉榕
Bijdr. 461. 1825; FKH 246. 1912; FHN 2: 393. 1965; FGD 1: 201. 1987; FOC 5: 66. 2003.

Shrub scandent, male plants erect. Branchlets slender. Stipules subulate, 1.5 –2 cm. Petioles 1–1.5 cm; leaf blade papery, obliquely elliptic or obovate-elliptic, 8 –15 × 2.5 –7 cm, usually asymmetrical, apex abruptly acute to acuminate, margin entire, glabrous on both surfaces when grown up, verruculose abaxially; lateral veins 7–10 pairs. Figs orange, paired or clustered, axillary or on leafless branches, globose or ovoid, 2–5 mm in diam., verruculose. Basal bracts sometimes sheath-shaped. Male flowers: perianth tubiform, 4-toothed; stamens 1. Gall flowers: perianth as in male flowers; ovary globose; stigma capitate. Female flowers in another set: perianth connate, apex toothed, hairy. Achenes ellipsoid; style lateral, elongated.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Lam Tsuen Valley, Ng Tung Chai, Ma On Shan, Mau Ping, Wu Kau Tang, Sha Tau Kok. Y. S. Lau 1631, 2118.
Distribution: Xizang, Yunnan, Guizhou, Guangxi, Hainan, Guangdong, Taiwan; Bhutan, Sikkim, Malaysia, Indonesia.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering and fruiting: Feb.–Nov.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Ma On Shan, Tai Po, Yuen Long, Fung Kat Heung, Tuen Mun, Sheung Shui, Sha Tau Kok
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Ficus tinctoria G. Forst. subsp. gibbosa (Blume) Corner 斜葉榕（水榕）
Gard. Bull. Singapore 17: 476. 1960 & 21: 74. 1965; FOC 5: 65. 2003.
Ficus gibbosa Blume, Bijdr. Fl. Ned. Ind. 466. 1825; FKH 246. 1912; FHN 2: 394. 1965; FGD 1: 201. 1987.

Tree or epiphyte when young. Branchlets brown. Stipules ca. 7 mm. Petioles 0.6 –2 cm, stout; leaves alternate, leathery, very variable in shape, ovate-elliptic or subrhomboid, unequalsided, less than 13 × 5 cm on large trees, base cuneate or obtuse, apex obtuse, acute or short-acuminate, margin entire or angulate, glabrous on both surfaces, basal veins 3; lateral veins 5 –7 pairs, slightly prominent on both surfaces. Figs yellow, paired or solitary, axillary, subglobose, 5– 6 mm in diam., base abruptly constricted into a 5 –10 mm stalk, glabrous or puberulent, apex umbonulate, basal bracts 3. Male flowers: white; perianth-lobes 4 – 6, linear; stamen 1, rudimentary ovary present. Gall flowers: perianth as male one; ovary oblique-ovate; style lateral. Female flowers in another set: perianth-lobes 4, linear, hyaline. Achenes elliptic, verrucose and keeled; style lateral, elongate; stigma dilated.

Locality: Ma On Shan, Tai Po, Yuen Long, Fung Kat Heung, Tuen Mun, Sheung Shui, Sha Tau Kok. HK sheet 25493, 36769.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou, Fujian, Jiangxi, Hunan, Taiwan; S Asia to Australia.
Ecology: Forests near villages. Flowering and fruiting: Apr.– Oct.
Uses: Timber, host of lac insect, ornamental.

Ficus variegata Blume 青果榕
Bijdr. Fl. Ned. Ind. 459. 1825; FHN 2: 388. 1965; FGD 1: 191. 1987; FOC 5: 49. 2003.
Ficus chlorocarpa Benth., FHK 330. 1861; FKH 247. 1912.
Ficus variegata var. chlorocarpa (Benth.) Benth. ex King, Ann. Bot. Gard. Calcutta 1: 170. 1888; FRPS 23(1): 174. 1998.

Large tree, up to 15 m tall; bark grey. Young branchlets green, sparse pubescent. Stipules ca. 1 cm. Petioles 5–7 cm; leaves thickly papery, broadly ovate to ovate-elliptic, 7.5–15(–20) × 6–13 cm, base round or shallowly cordate, apex acuminate, margin entire, shallowly sinuate or sparsely serrulate, sparsely pubescent or glabrous; basal veins 5, lateral veins 4–6 pairs, with reticulate veins distinct abaxially. Figs usually green, clustered on brachyblasts of trunk or branch, pear-shaped or globose, 1–2.5 cm in diam., apex umbonulate; basal bracts 3, caducous; peduncles 2–4 cm. Male flowers: perianth-lobes 3–4, broadly ovate; stamens 2, filaments base connate into a stalk. Gall flowers: perianth tubular, 4–5 toothed; style lateral; stigma infundibular. Female flowers: perianth-lobes 3–4, linear-lanceolate, membranaceous. Achenes obovate, slightly verrucose; style as long as achenes; stigma clavated.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. HK sheet 6470; L. T. Lo 490.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian; Thailand, Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering and fruiting: Mar.–Dec.
Uses: Ornamental, host of lac insect.
Notes: The type specimen of Ficus chlorocarpa was collected from Hong Kong Island by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1850.

Ficus variolosa Lindl. ex Benth. 變葉榕
London J. Bot. 1: 492. 1842; FHK 328. 1861; FKH 246. 1912; FHN 2: 399. 1965; FGD 1: 209. 1987; FOC 5: 55. 2003.

Shrub or small tree, 3 –10 m tall; bark grey-brown. Branchlets with short internodes. Stipules long-triangular , ca. 8 mm. Petioles 5 –10 mm; leaves thinly leathery, narrowly elliptic, elliptic-lanceolate, 5–12 × 1.5– 4 cm, base cuneate, apex obtuse or acute, margin entire; lateral veins 7–11 pairs. Figs paired or solitary, axillary, globose, 10 –12 mm in diam., verrucose, apex umbonulate; basal bracts 3, ovate-triangular , base slightly connate; peduncles 8–12 mm. Male flowers: near apical pore. Gall flowers: ovary globose; style short, lateral. Female flowers in another set; perianth-lobes 3 – 4; ovary reniform; style lateral, slender. Achenes verrucose.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 19; Y. S. Lau 1306.
Distribution: S, SW to SE China; Laos, Vietnam.
Ecology: Thickets or forests. Flowering and fruiting: Feb.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), fibre.

Ficus vasculosa Wall. ex Miq. 白肉榕
London J. Bot. 454. 1848; FKH 246. 1912; FOC 5: 46. 2003.
Ficus championii Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 6: 76. 1954; FHK 328. 1861; FGD 1: 204. 1987.

Tree, 10 –15 m tall. Branchlets grey-brown. Stipules ovate, ca. 6 mm. Petioles 1–2 cm; leaves leathery, elliptic to oblong-lanceolate, 4 –11 × 2– 4 cm, base cuneate, apex obtuse or acuminate, margin entire or irregularly lobed, dark green and shining adaxially, pale or whitish abaxially; lateral veins 10 –12 pairs, prominent on both surfaces, reticulate veins distinct adaxially. Figs yellow or yellow-red, globose, 7–10 mm in diam., base constricted into a short stalk. Peduncles 7–8 mm, basal bracts 3, deciduous; male, gall and female flowers within same fig. Male flowers: few, shortly pedicellate; perianth-lobes 3–4; stamens 2, rarely 1 or 3. Gall and female flowers: many, pedicellate or sessile; perianth-lobes 3–4; ovary obovate; stigma 2-fid. Achenes glabrous, apex keeled one side.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 327, Y. S. Lau 1232.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou; Thailand, Laos, Vietnam, Malaysia.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering and fruiting: Feb.–Dec.
Uses: Timber.
Notes: The type specimen of Ficus championii was collected from woods of the Happy Valley by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1850.

Ficus virens Aiton 黃葛樹（大葉榕）
Hort. Kew 3: 451. 1789; FGD 1: 199. 1987; FOC 5: 40. 2003.
Ficus virens var. sublanceolata (Miq.) Corner, Gard. Bull. Singapore 17: 377. 1959, et 21: 9. 1965; FRPS 23(1): 95. 1998.
Ficus wightiana Wall. ex Benth., FHK 327. 1861; FHN 2: 392. 1965.
Ficus infectoria auct. non Willd.: FKH 247. 1912.

Deciduous or semideciduous tree, epiphytic when young, with buttressed or prop roots. Stipules lanceolate-ovate, up to 10 cm. Petioles 2–5 cm; leaves leathery or rigid papery, sublanceolate, 10–15(–20) × 4–7 cm, base obtuse-rounded, cuneate or shallow-cordate, apex acuminate, margin entire; lateral veins 7–10 pairs, prominent abaxially. Figs purple-red, solitary, paired, axillary or clustered on leafless branches, globose, 7–12 mm in diam., basal bracts 3, minute; peduncles absent; male, gall and female flowers in one set. Male flowers: few, sessile; perianth-lobes 4–5, lanceolate; stamen 1, filament short. Gall flowers: pedicellate; perianth-lobes 3–4; style lateral, shorter than ovary. Female flowers: like gall flowers; style longer than ovary. Achenes wrinkled.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 1844, 2426.
Distribution: SW, S to SE China; S Asia to Australia.
Ecology: Flowering and fruiting: Apr.– Oct.
Uses: Roadside tree, timber, medicinal (folklore), host of lac insect.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Sai Kung, Tai Au Mun, Tai Po, Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Maclura cochinchinensis (Lour.) Corner 構棘（葨芝）
Gard. Bull. Singapore 19: 239. 1962; FOC 5: 35. 2003.
Cudrania cochinchinensis (Lour.) Kudo & Masam., Annual Rep. Taihoku Bot. Gard. 2: 27. 1932; FHN 2: 379. 1965; FGD 1: 180. 1987; FRPS 23(1): 58. 1998.
Vanieria cochinchinensis Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 564. 1790.
Cudrania rectispina Hance, J. Bot. 365. 1876; FKH 247. 1912.
Cudrania javanensis Tréc, Ann. Sci. Nat., Bot., ser. 3, 8: 123. 1847.

Erect or scandent shrub. Branches glabrous, with axillary spines. Petioles 0.5 –1 cm; leaves alternate, leathery, ellipticlanceolate or oblong, 3– 8 × 2–2.5 cm, base cuneate, apex obtuse or shortly acuminate, margin entire, glabrous on both surfaces; lateral veins 7–10 pairs. Head axillary, yellowish, 6–10 mm in diam., glabrous. Flowers dioecious, bracts subulate, with 2 yellow glands inside. Male flowers: perianth-lobes 4, unequal; stamens 4, pistillodes subulate or peltate. Female flowers: bracts tomentose; perianth-lobes 4, free or connate below; style 2-lobed, stigma filiform. Syncarp orange, globose, 2–5 cm in diam., slightly hairy; achenes ovoid, brown.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Sai Kung, Tai Au Mun, Tai Po, Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan, Lantau Island. HK sheet 29810, 31248.
Distribution: SW to SE China; E Africa, E, S & SE Asia to Australia, New Caledonia.
Ecology: Open thickets, forests, near villages. Flowering and fruiting: May–Nov.

Maclura tricuspidata Carr. 柘樹
Rev. Hort. 390. 1864; FOC 5: 36. 2003.
Cudrania tricuspidata (Carr.) Bureau ex Lavallée, Arb. Segrez. 243. 1877; FGD 1: 181. 1987; FRPS 23(1): 63. 1998; Check List HK Plants 61. 2002.

Deciduous shrub or small tree, 1–7 m tall. Branchlets slightly angulate, with spines. Petioles 1–2 cm; leaves ovate or rhomboidovate, 5 –14 × 3– 6 cm, base cuneate or rounded, apex acuminate, margin entire or occasionally trilobed, green-white and glabrous or pubescent abaxially; lateral veins 4 – 6 pairs. Head globose, solitary or paired, axillary; peduncles short. Male heads 5 mm in diam., bracts 2, adnated on perianth-lobes. Male flowers: perianth-lobes fleshy, apex thick, involute, with yellow glands; stamens 4, pistillode subulate. Female heads: 10–15 mm in diam. Female flowers: perianth-lobes shield-shaped at apex, others as in male one. Syncarp orange, subglobose, ca. 2.5 cm in diam., fleshy.

Locality: Fanling. W. J. Tutcher 9536.
Distribution: S Hebei; Korea, Japan, Vietnam.
Ecology: Thickets. Flowering: Early summer; fruiting: Summer to autumn.
Uses: Leaves for feeding silkworms, medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Man Kam To, Tai O, Fan Lau, Shui Hou, Tong Fuk, Tai A Chau
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Malaisia scandens (Lour.) Planch. 牛筋藤
Ann. Sci. Nat. Bot. Ser. 4, 3: 293. 1855; FHN 1: 377. 1964; FGD 1: 177. 1987; FOC 5: 27. 2003.
Caturus scandens Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 612. 1790.
Trophis scandens (Lour.) Hook. & Arn., Bot. Beechey Voy. 214. 1836.

Climbing shrub. Branchlets slender, with white lenticels. Petioles 3 mm; leaves alternate, papery, oblong or elliptic-obovate, 5–12 × 2–4.5 cm, base rounded to shallow-cordate, asymmetric, apex acute, margin entire or obscurely serrate, slightly rough abaxially; lateral veins 7–12 pairs. Male spikes cylindric, solitary or 2– 4-clustered; peduncles 2– 4 cm; bracts connate at base. Male flowers: perianth 3–4-lobed, lobes triangular , pubescent; stamens as many as perianth-lobes and opposite to them, anther subglobose; pistillodes minute; female heads 3–5 in clusters, subglobose, ca. 6 mm in diam., densely pubescent; bracts crowded; peduncles ca. 10 mm, hairy. Female flowers: perianth urceolate, 1–1.5 mm, enlarged later; ovary included; style 2-fid, filiform, 10 –13 mm. Achenes red, ovoid, 6–8 mm.

Locality: Man Kam To, Tai O, Fan Lau, Shui Hou, Tong Fuk, Tai A Chau. HK sheet 36190, 36496.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Taiwan; SE Asia to Australia.
Ecology: Thickets or forests, often on trees and rocks.
Uses: Fibre.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Common in Hong Kong. Also cultivated
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Morus alba L. 桑
Sp. Pl. 2: 986. 1753; FKH 244. 1912; FHN 2: 374. 1965; FGD 1: 172. 1987; FOC 5: 23. 2003.

Tree or shrub, 3–10 m tall or more; winter buds red-brown, scales imbricate. Branchlets fine hairy. Petioles 1.5–5.5 cm; leaves ovate or broad-ovate, 5–15 × 5–12 cm, base rounded or slightly cordate, apex acute, acuminate or obtuse, margin serrate, sometimes variously lobed, pubescent along veins abaxially. Flowers unisexual. Male spike pendulous, 2–3.5 cm, densely white villose. Male flowers: perianth-lobes broad-elliptic, greenish; anther globose or reniform. Female spike 1–2 cm. Female flowers: perianth-lobes obovate, outside and margin hairy; style absent, stigma 2-parted. Syncarps ovoid-ellipsoid, 1–2.5 cm, red or dark purple when mature.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Also cultivated. H. C. Tang 1164; Y. S. Lau 279.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; cultivated in Korea, Japan, C Asia, Europe.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Feb.–Aug.
Uses: Host (silkworms), food (fruit), fibre, medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Stubbs Road, Lugard Road, Pok Fu Lam
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Boehmeria densiflora Hook. & Arn. 密花苧麻
Bot. Beechey Voy. 271. 1838; FKH 250. 1912; FOC 5: 174. 2003.
Boehmeria penduliflora Wedd. ex Long var. loochooensis (Wedd.) W. T. Wang, FRPS 23(2): 355. 1995; FGD 6: 103. 2005.
Boehmeria platyphylla D. Don. var. loochooensis Wedd., Prodr. 16(1): 213. 1869.

Shrub to 2 m tall. Branchlets densely covered with appressed short hairs. Leaves opposite, rarely subopposite; stipules subulate, to 1.5 cm; petioles 1–2 cm, hispid; leaf blade lanceolate to narrowly lanceolate, 5 –19 × 1.2–3.5 cm, base obtuse or subrounded, apex acuminate, margin obtusely denticulate above the base, adaxial surface scabrous, sparsely pubescent, glabrescent, bullate due to impressed reticulation of veins, abaxial surface covered with appressed short hairs on raised veins; lateral veins 3 – 4 on each side of midvein. Female spikes axillary, 4–12 cm; male spikes shorter, borne on separate plants, or on the same plant but below the females. Male flower clusters 1–2 mm in diam.; female flower cluster 2.5 – 6 mm in diam. Male flowers: perianth-segments 4, elliptic, ca. 1.2 mm, puberulent abaxially; stamens 4, ca. 1.8 mm; rudimentary pistil elliptic, ca. 0.5 mm. Female flowers rhomboid or oblanceolate, 1–1.5 mm; stigma 0.7–1 mm. Achene compressed elongate-ellipsoid to fusiform, ca. 0.5 mm, margin more or less flattened.

Locality: Stubbs Road, Lugard Road, Pok Fu Lam. HK sheet 31319.
Distribution: Guangdong, Taiwan; Japan, Philippines.
Ecology: Roadsides, hillslopes, stream banks. Flowering: Apr.–May.

Boehmeria macrophylla Hornem. 水苧麻
Hort. Bot. Hafn. 2: 890. 1815; Grierson & Long, Fl. Bhutan 1(1): 126. 1983; FRPS 23(2): 336, pl. 75: 1–2. 1995; FOC 5: 169. 2003; FGD 6: 105. 2005.
Boehmeria platyphylla D. Don, Prodr. Fl. Nepal. 60. 1825; FKH 250. 1912.

Subshrub, 1–2(–3.5) m tall. Stems covered with appressed short hairs on upper part. Leaves opposite or nearly so; petioles 0.8– 8 cm, unequal in the same pair; leaf blade ovate to elliptic-ovate, 6.5 –14 × 3.2–7.5 cm, base rounded or shallowly cordate, ± oblique, apex longcuspidate or acuminate, margin denticulate above the base, adaxial surface slightly scabrous, covered with appressed short hairs, abaxial surface sparsely covered with appressed short hairs; lateral veins 2–3 on each side of midvein. Flower-clusters (glomerules) 1–2.5 mm in diam., forming axillary, solitary spikes of 7–15 cm, or the rachis with a few branches, usually the males below the females. Male flowers: perianth-segments 4, navicular or elliptic, ca. 1 mm, sparsely puberulent abaxially; stamens 4, ca. 1.5 mm; rudimentary pistil narrowly obovoid, ca. 0.4 mm. Female flowers: perianth-segments rhomboid or elliptic, ca. 1 mm, apex with 2 small teeth, puberulent abaxially; style 1–1.6 mm.

Locality: Mount Gough, Victoria Peak. H. C. Tang 1417; W. J. Tutcher 11209.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, SE Xizang; Vietnam, Myanmar, Nepal, India.
Ecology: Ravines, margins of forests or by streams.
Uses: Material (fibre).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Common in Hong Kong, either wild or in cultivation
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Boehmeria nivea (L.) Gaudich. 苧麻
Voy. Uranie, Bot. 12: 499. 1830; FHK 331. 1861; FKH 250. 1912; FHN 2: 414. 1965; FRPS 23(2): 327, pl. 73: 1– 4. 1995; FOC 5: 166. 2003; FGD 6: 101, fig. 43. 2005.
Urtica nivea L., Syst. 985. 1753.

Subshrub, 0.5–1.5 m tall. Stems and petioles covered with spreading long hairs and appressed short hairs. Leaves alternate; stipules free, subulate-lanceolate, 7–11 mm, hairy abaxially; petioles 2.5–9.5 cm; leaf blade orbicular-ovate or broadly ovate, 6–15 × 4–11 cm, base subtruncate or broadly cuneate, apex cuspidate, margin dentate, adaxial surface slightly scabrous, sparsely strigose, abaxial surface densely white-tomentose; lateral veins 3 on each side of midvein. Flowers unisexual (plants monoecious or dioecious), in glomerules. Female glomerules globular, 0.5–2 mm in diam., numerous, in axillary panicles. Male glomerules 1–3 mm in diam., in panicles, usually below the females. Male flowers: perianth-segments 4, narrowly elliptic, ca. 1.5 mm, united to middle, apex acute, sparsely pubescent abaxially; stamens 4, ca. 2 mm; rudimentary pistil narrowly obovoid, ca. 0.7 mm. Female flowers: perianth-segments elliptic, 0.6–1 mm, apex minutely 2–3-toothed, puberulent abaxially; style filiform, 0.5 –0.6 mm. Achene subglobular, ca. 0.6 mm in diam.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong, either wild or in cultivation. HK sheet 25985, 25989, 40468.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Gansu, Shaanxi, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam, Laos.
Ecology: Waste places near villages. Flowering: May–Aug.; fruiting: Sep.– Oct.
Uses: Material (fibre).

Boehmeria nivea var. tenacissima (Gaudich.) Miq. 青葉苧麻
Fl. Ind. Bat. 1(2): 253. 1859; FOC 5: 167. 2003; FGD 6: 102. 2005.
Boehmeria nivea (L.) Gaudich. var. nippononivea (Koidz.) W. T. Wang, Acta Bot. Yunnan. 3(3): 320. 1981; FRPS 23(2): 330, pl. 73: 5. 1995; FOC 5: 166. 2003.
Boehmeria nipononivea Koidz., Acta Phytotax. Geobot. 10: 223. 1941.
Boehmeria tenacissima Gaudich., Voy. Uranie, Bot. 500. 1830.

It differs from var. nivea mainly by the following characters: Stems and petioles only covered with appressed short hairs, without spreading hairs; leaf blade generally ovate, rarely orbicular-ovate, base abruptly narrowed, cuneate; stipules united at the base.

Locality: Tseng Lan Shue. Y. S. Lau 2716; HK sheet 25986.
Distribution: Guangdong, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan.
Ecology: Waste places near villages.
Uses: Material (fibre).

Gonostegia hirta (Blume ex Hassk.) Miq. 糯米團
Ann. Mus. Bot. Lugd.-Bat. 4: 303. 1868; FRPS 23(2): 367, pl. 82: 2–7. 1995; FOC 5: 178. 2003; FGD 6: 99, fig .42. 2005.
Memorialis hispida Buch.-Ham. ex Wall. Cat. sub n. 4601; FHK 332. 1861.
Memorialis hirta (Blume ex Hassk.) Wedd., Prodr. 16(1): 235(6). 1869.
Pouzolzia hirta Blume ex Hassk. in Teismann & Binnendijk, Cat. Hort. Bogor. 80. 1844, based on Urtica hirta Blume (1826), not Swartz (1797); FKH 250. 1912.

Perennial herb. Stems prostrate or upper part ascending, 50–100 cm or longer, pubescent. Leaves opposite; stipules subulate, ca. 2.5 mm; petioles 1– 4 mm; leaf blade lanceolate to narrowly ovate, (1.5 –)3–10 × 1–2.8 cm, base shallowly cordate or rounded, apex acuminate, margin entire, adaxial surface ± scabrous, sparsely strigose or subglabrous, abaxial surface sparsely pubescent on the veins or glabrescent, 3 – 5-nerved. Flowers in axillary clusters of 2–9 mm in diam. Male flowers: pedicels 1–4 mm; bud turbinate, top flat, with a ring of hairs on the rim; perianth‑segments 5, free, oblanceolate, 2–2.5 mm, apex abruptly acute; stamens 5; staminodes very small. Female flowers sessile, perianth tube ovoid, ca. 1.6 mm, longitudinally 10-ribbed, apex 2-toothed; stigma ca. 3 mm, hairy. Achene ovoid, ca. 1.4 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 937, 2152; Y. S. Lau 606.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, SE Xizang, Sichuan, S Shaanxi, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; tropical and subtropical Asia and Australia.
Ecology: Waste and shady places. Flowering; May–Sep.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Oreocnide frutescens (Thunb.) Miq. 紫麻
Ann. Mus. Bot. Lugd.-Bat. 3: 131. 1867; FHN 2: 419. 1965; FRPS 23(2): 386, pl. 84: 3 – 6. 1995; FOC 5: 184. 2003; FGD 6: 85, fig. 33. 2005.
Villebrunea frutescens (Thunb.) Blume., Mus. Bot. Luggd. Bat. 2: 168. 1856; FHK 332. 1861; FKH 250. 1912.
Urtica frutescens Thunb., Fl. Jap. 70. 1784.

Shrub or rarely small tree, 1–3 m tall. Branchlets and petioles purplish brown, strigose or pubescent, rarely grey tomentose. Leaves usually borne on the upper part of branches; stipules linear-lanceolate, ca. 10 mm, apex caudate-acuminate; petioles 1–7 cm; leaf blade ovate to narrowly ovate, rarely obovate, 3–15 × 1.5–6 cm, base rounded, rarely broadly cuneate, apex acuminate to caudate-acuminate, serrate or coarsely dentate above the base, adaxial surface sparsely strigillose, sometimes subglabrous, abaxial surface usually ashy-white-tomentose, later glabrate, or only with short hairs on veins, 3-nerved. Flowers in subsessile clusters on older branches. Male flowers: perianth-segments 3, oblong-ovate, incurved, united at base, hairy on the upper part of outside; stamens 3; rudimentary pistil clavate, ca. 0.6 mm, white-wooly. Female flowers sessile, ca. 1 mm. Achene ovoid, slightly compressed, ca. 1.2 mm, surrounded by the fleshy cupular receptacle at base.

Locality: Mount Parker. HK sheet 6596.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan, SE Gansu, S Shaanxi, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian; Japan, N India, Indochina, Myanmar, Thailand, Malaysia.
Ecology: Moist places in ravines, margins of forests or thickets. Flowering: Mar.–May; fruiting: Jun.– Oct.

Oreocnide frutescens subsp. insignis C. J. Chen 細梗紫麻
Acta Phytotax. Sin. 21(4): 475. 1983; FOC 5: 185. 2003; FGD 6: 85. 2005.

It differs from subsp. frutescens mainly by the following characters: female inflorescence distinctly pedunculate; peduncles 5 –13 mm; leaves narrowly obovate to oblong-obovate, adaxial surface glabrous, abaxial surface sparsely pubescent, margin with 13 –21 serratures above middle.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Shing Mun. S. T. Dunn 7055; Y. S. Lau 1522, 3004.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi.
Ecology: Forests in ravines. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.; fruiting: Jul.–Aug.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Mount Gough, Victoria Peak, Tai Po Kau, Sunset Peak
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Pellionia brevifolia Benth. 短葉赤車
FHK 330. 1861; FKH 249. 1912; FHN 2: 409. 1965; FRPS 23(2): 174, pl. 38: 4. 1995; FOC 5: 125. 2003; FGD 6: 79. 2005.

Perennial herb. Stems prostrate, 10–30 cm or longer, rooting at nodes, hispid, hairs recurved or slightly spreading. Leaves alternate; stipules subulate, 1.2–2 mm; petioles 1.5 –2 mm; leaf blade very obliquely elliptic to obovate, 5 –32 × 4 –20 mm, base very unequal, slightly obtuse or cuneate on the narrow side, auriculate on the broad side, apex obtuse or rounded, sparsely and obtusely serrate above the middle, adaxial surface glabrous or with scattered, appressed short hairs, abaxial surface pubescent on veins, subtriplinerved. Male cymes 8–15 mm in diam.; peduncles 2.5 – 4 cm, puberulent; female cymes compact, 2.5–4 mm in diam., almost sessile or on peduncles of 2–6 mm. Male flowers: perianth-segments 5, elliptic, ca. 2 mm, slightly unequal, glabrous; stamens 5. Female flowers: perianth‑segments 5, very unequal, linear-lanceolate, 1–1.8 mm; staminodes lanceolate, bent in at about the middle. Achene narrowly ovoid, ca. 1.2 mm, tuberculate.

Locality: Mount Gough, Victoria Peak, Tai Po Kau, Sunset Peak. W. J. Tutcher 7248.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Fujian.
Ecology: Ravines. Flowering: May–Jul.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Mount Gough and Victoria Peak, Hong Kong Island by C. Wilford (No. 227, K) between 1857 and 1858.

Pellionia grijsii Hance 華南赤車
J. Bot. 6: 49. 1886 & 12: 262. 1874; FRPS 23(2): 178. 1995; FOC 5: 126. 2003; FGD 6: 81. 2005.

Perennial herb. Stems 40 –70 cm tall, unbranched, or occasionally with a few branches, hirsute, the hairs 0.5 –2 mm, slightly recurved or spreading. Leaves alternate; stipules subulate, ca. 4 mm, glabrous; petioles 1– 4 mm, hirsute; leaf blade obliquely oblong to oblong-lanceolate or oblique-elliptic, 6 –14(–18) × 2.4 – 5(– 6) cm, base very unequal, cuneate or obtuse on the narrow side, auriculate on the broad side, apex long-acuminate or acuminate, sometimes caudate, obtusely serrate above the base, adaxial surface glabrous or with scattered short hairs, rarely densely strigose, abaxial surface hirsute on veins, sub–pinnately nerved; lateral veins 4 – 5 on each side of midvein. Male cymes 2–3 times branched, 0.5 – 5.6 cm in diam.; peduncles 0.9 – 8 cm, together with the branches hirsute; female cymes more compact and densely flowered, 3 –10 mm in diam.; peduncles 1.5–7 mm, hirsute. Male flowers: perianth-segments 5, elliptic, ca. 2 mm; stamens 5; rudimentary pistil ca. 0.2 mm. Female flower: perianthsegments 5, ca. 0.6 mm, unequal, 3 larger, narrowly navicularoblong, 2 smaller, narrowly lanceolate; staminodes very minute or none. Achene ellipsoid, ca. 0.8 mm, tuberculate.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. S. Y. Hu 11443 (CUHK).
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, SE Yunnan, Jiangxi, S Fujian.
Ecology: Ravines, by streams or on rocks. Flowering: Winter.

Pellionia radicans (Sieb. & Zucc.) Wedd. 赤車
Prodr. 16(1): 167. 1869; FKH 249. 1912; FHN 2: 408. 1965; FRPS 23(2): 171, pl. 37: 6. 1995; FOC 5: 125. 2003; FGD 6: 79. 2005.
Procris radicans Sieb. & Zucc., Fl. Jap. 218. 1846.

Perennial herb. Stems ascending from the procumbent base, 20 –60 cm or longer, glabrous or puberulent, the hairs ca. 0.1 mm. Leaves alternate; stipules subulate, 1–4 mm; petioles 1–4 mm; leaf blade obliquely rhomboid-ovate or lanceolate, (1.2–)2.4 – 5(– 8) × 0.9– 2(–2.7) cm, base very unequal, obtuse on the narrow side, auriculate on the broad side, apex shortly acuminate to long-acuminate, serrate above the middle, glabrous on both surfaces or nearly so, subtriplinerved. Flowers usually dioecious. Male cymes loose, 1– 5(– 8) cm; peduncles 0.4 –3.5(–7) cm, glabrous or papillose-puberulent; female cymes compact, 3– 5 mm in diam.; peduncles 0.5 –3(–18) mm, with a few short hairs. Male flowers: perianth-segments 5, elliptic, ca. 1.5 mm, glabrous or puberulent outside; stamens 5; rudimentary pistil narrowly obconical, ca. 0.6 mm. Female flowers: perianth-segments 5, ca. 0.4 mm, 3 larger, navicular-oblong, 2 smaller, narrowly oblong; staminodes very minute or none; ovary about the length of the perianth-segments. Achene ellipsoid, ca. 0.9 mm, tuberculate.

Locality: Ma On Shan. F. W. Xing 8463.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; N Vietnam, Korea, Japan.
Ecology: Thickets, forests in ravines. Flowering: May–Dec.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Mount Gough, Victoria Peak, Tai Mo Shan
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Pellionia scabra Benth. 蔓赤車
FHK 330. 1861; FKH 249. 1912; FGZ 404. 1956; FHN 2: 407. 1965; FRPS 23(2): 168, pl. 37: 5 & 44: 3 – 4. 1995; FOC 5: 124. 2003; FGD 6: 79, fig. 29. 2005.

Subshrub. Stems erect or ascending, 30–100 cm tall, woody at base, upper part hirsute; hairs 0.3–1 mm. Leaves alternate; stipules subulate, 1.5–3 mm; petioles 0.5–2 mm; leaf blade obliquely rhomboid-oblanceolate or narrowly oblong, 3.2–6.5(–10) × 1.3–3.2(–4) cm, base very unequal, slightly obtuse on the narrow side, broadly cuneate, rounded or auriculate on the broad side, apex acuminate to caudate-acuminate, serrate above the middle, adaxial surface scabrous, with short hairs on the midvein, abaxial surface pubescent, sub-triplinerved. Male cymes loose, on slender peduncles of 0.3 –3.6 cm, puberulent; female cymes very compact, subsessile, densely puberulent. Male flowers: perianth-segments 5, elliptic, ca. 1.5 mm, united at base, unequal, 3 larger, the other 2 smaller; stamens 5; rudimentary pistil subulate, ca. 0.3 mm. Female flowers: perianth-segments 4 – 5, narrowly oblong, ca. 0.5 mm, 2 or 3 larger than others; staminodes very minute or none. Achene ellipsoid, ca. 0.8 mm, tuberculate.

Locality: Mount Gough, Victoria Peak, Tai Mo Shan. H. C. Tang 2435; L. T. Lo 591; Y. W. Lam 1388.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Vietnam.
Ecology: Ravines, on shady and wet places. Flowering: Mar.–Jul.
Notes: The type specimens were collected from Hong Kong Island in 1850s by A. W. Harland, C. Wright and C. Wilford.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Robin's Nest (Sha Tau Kok) (fide Xing et al. 2000)
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Pilea aquarum Dunn subsp. acutidentata C. J. Chen 銳齒濕生冷水花
Bull. Bot. Res. (Harbin) 2(3): 60. 1982; FRPS 23(2): 90. 1995; FOC 5: 102. 2003; FGD 6: 94. 2005.

Perennial herb, 30 –70 cm tall. Stems fleshy, puberulent or subglabrous. Leaves unequal on the same pairs, membranous when dry; stipules subcordate, 3 – 5 mm, apex acute; petioles 1– 4 cm; leaf blade ovate, 5 –14 × 2.5 –7 cm, base broadly cuneate or obtuse, slightly oblique, apex acute, margin sharply dentate, in dry state adaxial surface dark green, shining, abaxial surface paler, puberulent or subglabrous on both surfaces, trinerved. Male inflorescence cymose-paniculate, 2– 6 cm including peduncle. Female inflorescence cymose, compact or cluster-like, ca. 2 cm. Male flowers: perianth-segments 4, elliptic; stamens 4; rudimentary pistil very small. Female flowers: perianth‑segments 3, unequal, in fruiting time the middle one sub-navicular, about half length of the fruit, the lateral 2 much small. Achene subglobose, ca. 0.7 mm, apex slightly oblique, tuberculate.

Locality: Robin's Nest (Sha Tau Kok) (fide Xing et al. 2000).
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi.
Ecology: Ravines, by streams or on other shade places. Flowering: Mar.–May; fruiting: Apr.–Jun.

Pilea chartacea C. J. Chen 紙質冷水花
Bull. Bot. Res. (Harbin) 2(3): 63. 1982; FRPS 23(2): 92. 1995; FOC 5: 103. 2003; FGD 6: 96. 2005.

Perennial herb, with creeping rhizomes, glabrous. Stems fleshy, above 30 cm tall, pinkish. Leaves papery; stipules membranous, ovate, ca. 3 mm; petioles 0.7–1.5 cm; leaf blade elliptic-lanceolate, 3–7 × 1.2–2.3 cm, base broadly cuneate or obtuse, apex acuminate, margin shallowly serrate, in dry state adaxial surface dark green, sometimes bullate, abaxial surface paler, often with purplish scattered red scaly dots along veins; trinerved. Male cymes shortly pedunculed, 1–1.5 cm; female cymes subsessile, ca. 7 mm across. Male flowers: perianth pink, ca. 2.5 mm in the bud, united at base; segments 4, ovate-oblong; stamens 4; rudimentary pistil coniform. Female flowers: perianth-segments 3, unequal, the middle one ovate-oblong, about one-third length of the fruit, the lateral 2 much smaller; sterile. Achene ovoid, ca. 1 mm, apex slightly oblique, inconspicuously tuberculate.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. S. Y. Hu 11621 (CUHK, PE).
Distribution: Guangdong.
Ecology: Ravines, wet shady places. Flowering: Mar.–Sep.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Tai Mo Shan by S. Y. Hu in 1972.

Pilea glaberrima (Blume) Blume 點乳冷水花
Mus. Bot. 2(4): 54. 1856; Gierson & Long, Fl. Bhutan 1(1): 112. 1983; C. J. Chen, Bull. Bot. Res. (Harbin) 2(3): 71. 1982; FRPS 23(2): 100. 1995; FOC 5: 105. 2003; FGD 6: 96. 2005.
Urtica glaberrima Blume, Bijdr. Fl. Ned. Ind. 493. 1826.

Straggling herb or subshrub, stoloniferous, 0.5–1.5 m tall, glabrous. Stems much branched, woody at base. Leaves opposite; stipules triangular, 1–2 mm; petioles 1.5–5 cm; leaf blade ovate, elliptic, oblong-lanceolate or elliptic-lanceolate, 6–15 × 2.5 –7 cm, base rounded, obtuse or cuneate, apex acuminate, margin shallowly serrate or crenate above middle, sometimes subentire; trinerved. Flowers in clusters; the clusters forming axillary panicles, usually shorter than the subtending leaves. Male flowers: perianth-segments 4, elliptic-navicular; stamens 4; rudimentary pistil very small. Female flowers: perianth-segments 3, unequal. Achene ovoid, slightly compressed, ca. 1 mm, minutely tuberculate.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. HK sheet 31557.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan; Nepal, India, Myanmar, Indonesia.
Ecology: Ravines. Flowering: Jul.–Sep.; fruiting: Oct.–Nov.

Pilea microphylla (L.) Liebm. 小葉冷水花
Kongel. Danske Vidensk. Selsk. Skr., Naturvidensk. Math. Afd., ser. 5, 5(2): 302. 1851; FOC 5: 119. 2003; FGD 6: 90. 2005.
Parietaria microphylla L., Syst. Nat., ed. 10, 1308. 1759.
Pilea muscosa Linndl., Coll. Bot. t. 4. 1821, nom. illeg.; FKH 248. 1912.

Delicate herb, 3–17 cm tall, glabrous. Stems fleshy, erect or ascending, simple or branched, with dense cystoliths. Leaves membranous when dry; stipules triangular, ca. 0.5 mm; petioles slender, unequal in length, 1– 4 mm; leaf blade obovate or spathulate, unequal in size, 2–7 × 1.5 –3 mm, base cuneate or attenuate, apex obtuse, margin entire, adaxially green, abaxially paler, foveolate when dry, pinnately nerved. Flowers in compact cymose capitulum on a peduncle of 1.5 – 6 mm, sometimes sessile. Male flowers: perianth-segments 4, ovate, corniculate near apex; stamens 4; rudimentary ovary minute. Female flowers smaller, perianth-segments 3, subequal, oblong, the ventral one larger, subequal to achene, the lateral 2 ovate, acute. Achene ovoid, ca. 4 mm, compressed, smooth, enclosed by persistent perianth.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong (naturalized). H. C. Tang 1406, 1795; L. T. Lo 156.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan (naturalized). Native to tropical America, naturalized elsewhere in tropical regions of Asia and Africa.
Ecology: Shady old walls, moist rocks and other wet places. Flowering; Jun.–Aug; fruiting: Sep.– Oct.

Pilea peploides (Gaudich.) Hook. & Arn. 齒葉冷水花
Bot. Beechey Voy. 96. 1832; FKH 248. 1912; FOC 5: 119. 2003.
Pilea peploides (Gaudich.) Hook. & Arn. var. major Wedd., Prodr. 16(1): 109. 1869; C. J. Chen, Bull. Bot. Res. 2(3): 115. 1982; FRPS 23(2): 150, pl. 33: 1–3. 1995.

Annual herb, 5–30 cm tall, glabrous. Stems fleshy, often clumped. Leaves membranous when dry; stipules small, triangular; petioles slender, 3–20 mm; leaf blade rhomboid-orbicular to depressed orbicular, sometimes fan-shaped, (7–)10–21 × (7–)11–23 mm, apex rounded or broadly obtuse, base obtuse or sub-rounded, sometimes broadly cuneate, shallowly dentate or undulate above middle, rarely sub-entire, trinerved. Flowers in subsessile clusters, or in compact cymes on short peduncles. Male flowers: perianth‑segments 4, ovate; stamens 4. Female flowers: perianth-segments 2, unequal, the ventral one larger, navicular or obovate-oblong, thickened in fruit, about the length of the fruit or slightly shorter. Achene ovoid, with scattered minute spiny projections.

Locality: Hong Kong Island. W. J. Tutcher 4619.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Vietnam, Philippines, Indonesia.
Ecology: Forests, moist rocks and wet places. Flowering; Apr.–May; fruiting: May–Jul.

Pilea sinofasciata C. J. Chen 粗齒冷水花
Bull. Bot. Res. (Harbin) 2(3): 85. 1982; FRPS 23(2): 115, pl. 24: 5 – 8. 1995; FOC 5: 110. 2003; FGD 6: 95. 2005.
Pilea wightii auct. non Wedd.: FKH 248. 1912.

Perennial herb, 25–100 cm tall. Stems fleshy, scarcely branched, glabrous or sometimes puberulent on the upper part. Leaves subequal on the same pair; stipules membranous, triangular, ca. 2 mm; petioles 1– 5 cm, ± puberulent; leaf blade elliptic, or oblong-lanceolate, (2–)4–17 × 2–7 cm, base cuneate or rounded, slightly oblique, apex caudate-acuminate, margin coarsely serrate, adaxial surface green, initially with scattered pellucid short hairs, glabrescent, often with 2 white stripes along the midvein, abaxial surface subglabrous, or sometimes puberulent on veins; trinerved. Leaves on the lower part of the stem smaller, obovate or fan-shaped, apex acute or subrounded. Flowers in cymose panicles, usually shorter than petioles of the subtending leaves. Male flowers: perianth united at base, segments 4, elliptic, concave, apex obtuse; stamens 4; rudimentary pistil small, conical. Female flowers: perianth-segments 3, subequal. Achene ovoid, ca. 0.7 mm, apex slightly oblique.

Locality: Lantau Island. HK sheet 25864, 25867.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, SW Shaanxi, SE Gansu, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang.
Ecology: Ravines, by streams. Flowering: Jun.–Jul.; fruiting: Aug.– Oct.

Pilea swinglei Merr. 三角冷水花
Philip. J. Sci. 13: 136. 1918; Hand.-Mazz., Symb. Sin. 7: 141. 1929; FRPS 23(2): 151. pl. 33: 4 –9. 1995; FOC 5: 120. 2003; FGD 6: 92. 2005.

Annual herb, 7–30 cm tall, glabrous. Stems fleshy. Leaves membranous when dry; stipules small, triangular, ca. 1 mm; petioles 5 –30 mm; leaf blade broadly ovate, triangular or narrowly ovate, 1– 5.5 × 0.8 –3 cm, apex acute, sometimes obtuse or shortly acuminate, base cordate, obtuse or truncate, margin sparsely serrate, adaxial surface green, abaxial surface paler, foveolate when dry, often densely marked with purple minute dots; trinerved. Leaves on the lower part of the stem much smaller, ovate-orbicular or sub-orbicular, apex obtuse or subrounded. Flowers in head-like clusters, 2.5 – 5 mm in diam.; the clusters 2–4 arranged on a slender, simple or little branched rachis, usually shorter than the subtending leaves. Male flowers: perianth-segments 4, obovate-oblong; stamens 4; rudimentary pistil inconspicuous. Female flowers: perianth-segments 2, very unequal, the larger one oblong-navicular, 2‑keeled on upper part of abaxil surface, another very small. Achene broadly ovoid, slightly compressed, ca. 0.5 mm, apex slightly oblique.

Locality: Sunset Peak. Y. S. Lau 1550, 2739.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian.
Ecology: Rocks by streams and wet places near villages.

Pouzolzia zeylanica (L.) Benn. 霧水葛
Pl. Jav. Rar. 67. 1838; Wight, Ic. Pl. Ind. Or. 6: t. 2101, f. 45. 1853; FGZ 403, fig. 209. 1956; FRPS 23(2): 364, pl. 81: 1–4. 1995; FOC 5: 177. 2003; FGD 6: 83, fig. 32. 2005.
Parietaria zeylanica L., Sp. Pl. 1052. 1753.
Pouzolzia indica auct. non Gaudich.: FHK 331. 1861; FKH 250. 1912.

Perennial herb. Stems ascending or erect, 12– 40 cm tall, covered with appressed short hairs and mixed with spreading hairs. Leaves opposite, or alternate near apex; petioles 0.3–1.6 cm; leaf blade ovate to broadly ovate, 1.2–3.8 × 0.8 –2.6 cm (leaves on short branches much smaller), base rounded, apex shortly acuminate or slightly obtuse, margin entire, sparsely covered with appressed hairs on both surfaces; lateral veins 1–2 on each side of midvein. Flowers in small sessile, axillary clusters, 1–2.5 mm in diam., the males and females usually mixed. Male flowers: perianth-segments 4, narrowly oblong, ca. 1.5 mm, united at the base; stamens 4, ca. 1.8 mm; rudimentary pistil narrowly obovate, ca. 0.4 mm. Female flowers: perianthsegments elliptic or subrhomboid, ca. 0.8 mm, enlarged to 1.5 mm in fruiting time, apex minutely 2-toothed, densely pubescent outside; stigma 1.2–2 mm. Achene ovoid, ca. 1.2 mm in diam.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 1374; Y. S. Lau 1583, 2234.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, SE Yunnan, Sichuan, S Gansu, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian; widely distributed in tropical Asia.
Ecology: Thickets or grasses. Flowering: Autumn.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Procris crenata C. B. Robinson 藤麻
Philipp. J. Sci. 5(6): 507. 1911; FOC 5: 163. 2003.
Procris wightiana Wall. ex Wedd., Arch. Mus. Hist. Nat. 9: 336. 1856; FRPS 23(2): 317, pl. 71: 1–2. 1995; FGD 6: 87. 2005.
Procris laevigata auct. non Blume: FKH 249. 1912.

Perennial herb. Stems fleshy, 30–80 cm tall, glabrous. Leaves alternate, borne on the upper part of stems and branches; stipules very small, ovate, deciduous; petioles 1.5–12 mm; leaf blade narrowly oblong to oblong, (4.5–)8–20 × (1.5 –)2.2– 4.5 cm, base attenuate, slightly asymmetrical, apex acuminate, margin with a few teeth or undulate above middle, glabrous; lateral veins 5 – 8 on each side of midvein. Flowers in clusters; male clusters with short and slender peduncle; the females on a short and thick peduncle and usually borne above the males. Male flowers: perianth-lobes 5, oblong or ovate, ca. 1.5 mm, corniculate below apex; stamens 5. Female flowers sessile; perianth-lobes often 4, ca. 3.5 mm, glabrous; ovary ellipsoid, ca. 0.3 mm; stigma very small. Achene narrowly ovoid, 0.6–0.8 mm, compressed, often minutely punctate or almost smooth.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai. P. S. Choi 361; Y. S. Lau 1758.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, SE Xizang, Sichuan, Fujian, Taiwan; Bhutan, India, Sri Lanka, Laos, Thailand, Indochina and Malesia.
Ecology: Shady, moist places in forests, on rocks or tree trunks. Flowering: Jul.–Aug.; fruiting: Aug.– Oct.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Ma On Shan
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Engelhardia fenzelii Merr. 白皮黃杞
Lingnan Sci. J. 7: 300. 1929; FRPS 21: 13, pl. 3: 2. 1979; FGD 2: 322. 1991.
Engelhardtia roxburgiana auct. non. Wall.: FOC 4: 278. 1999, p.p. (quoad syn. Engelhardtia fenzelii Merr.)

Tree, 5–15 m; bark greyish yellow; branchlets greyish white, lenticellate. Bud, young branches, leaf axis, inflorescence and fruit with golden or brownish yellow peltate scales. Petioles 1.5–3 cm. Leaves 8 –18 cm; leaflets usually 2 pairs, sometimes 1 pair, subopposite, leathery, elliptic to oblong-elliptic, 6 –9 × 2.5 – 5 cm, asymmetrical, base cuneate, apex acuminate, margin entire, olive or pale brown and glossy when dried; lateral veins 5–7 pairs, inconspicuous; petiolules 3– 6 mm. Inflorescence terminal, slightly pendulous, ca. 10 × 4 cm; peduncle 2– 4 cm, with peltate scales. Nutlet glabrous, 3– 4 mm. Persistent bract membranous, 3-lobed, densely covered with brownish yellow peltate scales; lobes glabrous, central lobe 2.5 × 0.8 cm, lateral lobes 1.5 × 0.6 cm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Ma On Shan. H. C. Tang 887; C. P. Lau 115.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Zhejiang.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: May–Jul.; fruiting: Sep.– Oct.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Ma On Shan, Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai, Tai Po Kau, Tseng Lan Shue
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Engelhardia roxburghiana Lindl. ex. Wall. 黃杞
Pl. Asiat. Rar. 2: 85. 1831; FRPS 21: 12, pl. 3: 1. 1979; FGD 2: 322, fig. 212. 1991; FOC 4: 278. 1999, excl. syn. E. fenzelii Merr. & E. unijuga Chun ex P. Y. Chen.
Engelhardtia chrysolepis Hance, Ann. Sci. Nat. Ser. 4, 15: 227. 1861.
Engelhardtia formosana Hayata, Icon. Pl. Formosan. 6: 61. 1916.
Engelhardtia wallichiana auct. non Lindl.: FKH 251. 1912.

Tree to 30 m tall; bark dark brown. Branchlets purplish or dark brown. Buds, young branches, abaxial surfaces of leaves and inflorescence covered with brown peltate scales. Petioles 3 –8 cm. Leaves 12–25 cm; leaflets 3 – 5 pairs, oblong, oblong‑elliptic or ovate, 5 –12 × 2– 4 cm, asymmetrical, base cuneate or broadly cuneate, apex acuminate, margin entire, lateral veins 10 –13 pairs; petiolules 0.6 –1.5 cm. Inflorescence terminal, pendulous. Infructescence 15 –25 cm. Nutlet globose, densely covered with peltate scales, 4 mm in diam. Persistent bract membranous, 3‑lobed, densely covered with peltate scales, lobes glabrous, central lobe 3 –5 × 0.8 –1.2 cm, lateral lobes 1.5 –2 × 0.5 –0.8 cm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Ma On Shan, Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai, Tai Po Kau, Tseng Lan Shue. Y. S. Lau 1437, 2718.
Distribution: S & SW China; Indochina, Indonesia, Myanmar, E Pakistan, Thailand.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: May–Jul.; fruiting: Sep.– Oct.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Common in Hong Kong. Also cultivated
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Myrica rubra (Lour.) Sieb. & Zucc. 楊梅
Abh. Math.-Phys. Cl. Königl. Bayer. Akad. Wiss. 4: 230. 1846; FHK 322. 1861; FKH 251. 1912; FGD 3: 239, fig. 160. 1995; FOC 4: 276. 1999.
Morella rubra Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 2: 548. 1790.

Evergreen tree, dioecious, to 15 m tall; bark grey. Branchlets robust, glabrous. Petioles 0.2–1 cm. Leaves obovate-oblong to oblanceolate, 5–14 × 1– 4 cm, leathery, base cuneate, apex obtuse to acute, margin entire or serrate at upper part, glabrous on both surfaces, sparsely to moderately golden-glandular abaxially. Male spikes solitary or sometimes several together in leaf axils, 1–3 cm, usually not branched; bracts imbricate, suborbicular, ca. 1 mm, glabrous, with golden glands abaxially. Male flowers: bracteoles 2– 4, ovate; stamens 4 – 6; anthers dark red, ellipsoid. Female spikes often solitary in leaf axils, 0.5 –1.5 cm, many-flowered; bracts imbricate, glabrous, with golden glands abaxially. Female flowers: bracteoles 4; ovary ovoid, velutinous; stigmas 2, bright red. Drupe dark red or purple-red at maturity, globose, 1–1.5 cm in diam.; pericarp fleshy, juicy, papilliferous.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Also cultivated. H. C. Tang 2408, 2486; Y. S. Lau 501.
Distribution: Areas S of Changjiang River; Vietnam, Philippines, Korea, Japan.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Mar.–Apr.; fruiting: May–Jul.
Uses: Food (fruit), medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Tam, Victoria Peak, Wu Kau Tang, Tai Mo Shan, Tai Po Kau, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Castanopsis carlesii (Hemsl.) Hayata 米櫧（小紅栲）
Icon. Pl. Formosan. 6 (suppl.): 72. 1917; H. L. Li, Woody Fl. Taiwan 88. 1963; FFJ 1: 384, fig. 335. 1982; FRPS 22: 66, pl. 18: 5– 8. 1998; FOC 4: 330. 1999.
Quercus carlesii Hemsl., Hooker's Icon. Pl. 26: t. 2591. 1899.
Castanopsis cuspidata (Thunb. ex Murray) Schott. var. carlesii (Hemsl.) Yamazaki, J. Jap. Bot. 62(11): 333. 1987; FTW ed. 2, 2: 55, pl. 20, photo 19. 1996.

Tree, to 20 m tall. Young shoots and rachis of inflorescences sparsely reddish brown scurfy. Leaves thinly leathery; petioles to 1 cm, base thickened; leaf blade lanceolate to ovate-laceolate, 4 –12 × 1– 4.5 cm, base cuneate, ± oblique, apex acuminate to narrowly caudate, margin entire or with a few shallow teeth above middle, abaxial surface initially reddish brown scurfy, greyish brown to silvery when full grown; lateral veins 8 –11 on each side of midvein. Male spikes simple or branched, 5 –7 cm; rachis glabrous or glabrescent. Female spikes 3– 4 cm, lengthening to 7–8.5 cm in fruiting time, glabrous; flower 1 per cupule. Cupule subglobose to ovoid, 0.8 –1.2 cm in diam., usually entirely enclosing nut, wall 0.5–1 mm thick, yellowish brown to reddish brown tomentose abaxially; bracts spine-like or reduced to tubercles, arranged into 6–7 continuous or interrupted rings. Nut subglobose to broadly conical, 0.8 –1 cm in diam., apex shortly pointed; scar ca. 5 mm in diam.

Locality: Tai Tam, Victoria Peak, Wu Kau Tang, Tai Mo Shan, Tai Po Kau, Lantau Island. W. J. Tutcher 9119; Y. S. Lau 1722; L. T. Lo 379.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Yunnan, Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Woods. Flowering: Mar.–Jun.; fruiting: Sep.–Nov. of following year.
Uses: Material (wood), food (seeds).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Deep Water Bay, Wong Nai Chung, Happy Valley, Sai Kung, Tai Wai, Tai Mo Shan
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Castanopsis concinna (Champ. ex Benth.) A. DC. 華南錐（毛葉栲栗）
J. Bot. 1: 182. 1863; FRPS 22: 30, pl. 5: 5 –7. 1998; FOC 4: 322. 1999.
Castanea concinna Champ. ex Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 6: 115. 1854; FHK 319. 1861.

Tree, 10–15 m tall. Branches of the current year growth and rachis of inflorescences softly tomentose. Leaves firmly leathery; petioles 4–12 mm; leaf blade oblong-elliptic to oblong-lanceolate, 5–10 × 1.5–3.5(–5) cm, base subrounded or broadly cuneate, apex acuminate, margin entire, slightly revolute, adaxially glabrous or sparsely pilose on midvein when young, abaxially reddish brown scurfy; lateral veins 12–16 on each side of midvein. Male spikes 5–10 cm, solitary in the axils of the young leaves and forming a terminal leafy panicle. Female spikes solitary, 4–8 cm in fruiting time. Cupule globose, 5–6 cm in diam., splitting into 4 regular segments, wall 2–4 mm thick, densely crowded with stout clustered branching spines. Nut 1 per cupule, compressed globular, ca. 1 × 1.4 cm, densely pubescent; scar covering 1/3–1/2 of nut.

Locality: Deep Water Bay, Wong Nai Chung, Happy Valley, Sai Kung, Tai Wai, Tai Mo Shan. W. J. Tutcher 8410; Y. S. Lau 199; H. C. Tang 1469.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi.
Ecology: Woods. Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: Sep.– Oct. of following year.
Uses: Material (wood), food (seeds).
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Happy Valley by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1850. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Aberdeen, Middle Gap, Wong Nai Chung
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Castanopsis eyrei (Champ. ex Benth.) Tutch. 甜櫧（埃氏栲）
J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 37: 68. 1905; FKH 254. 1912; FFJ 1: 390. 1982; FTW ed. 2, 2: 57, pl. 22. 1996; FRPS 22: 53, pl. 13: 5 –9. 1998; FOC 4: 327. 1999.
Quercus eyrei Champ. ex Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 6: 114. 1854; FHK 320. 1861.

Tree, 8 –15 m tall. Bark greyish brown, longitudinally fissured. Branchlets glabrous. Leaves leathery; petioles to 0.7–1(–1.5) cm, base thickened; leaf blade ovate to ovate-lanceolate, rarely ovate-elliptic, 5–7(–13) × 1.5 –2.5(– 5) cm, base cuneate, ± oblique, apex caudate-acuminate, margin entire or with a few coarse serratures towards apex, green, glabrous and shining on both surfaces; lateral veins 8 –10 on each side of midvein, very slender but evident. Male spikes 3.5– 5 cm, in a terminal panicle; rachis glabrous. Females spikes simple and shorter; flowers 1 per cupule. Cupule subglobose to broad ovoid, 1.5–3 cm in diam., splitting irregularly when mature, wall ca. 1 mm thick, greyish to yellowish grey puberulent outside; bracts spine-like, 4 – 8 mm, usually entirely covering cupule. Nut 1 per cupule, broadly conical, 1–1.4 cm in diam., glabrous; scar basal, 8 –10 mm in diam.

Locality: Aberdeen, Middle Gap, Wong Nai Chung. W. J. Tutcher 2031, 4675; Y. S. Lau 2953.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Qinghai, Xizang, Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Woods. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.; fruiting: Sep.–Nov. of following year.
Uses: Material (wood), food (seeds).
Notes: The type specimen was collected in Wong Nai Chung by Eyre between 1849 and 1851.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Pok Fu Lam, Tai Tam Tuk, Victoria Peak, Wan Chai Gap, Mount Parker, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Castanopsis fabri Hance 羅浮錐（白櫞）
J. Bot. 22: 230. 1884; FKH 254. 1912; FFJ 1: 386. 1982; FTW ed. 2, 2: 57, pl. 23, photo 21. 1996; FRPS 22: 71, pl. 20: 6–13. 1998; FOC 4: 331. 1999.

Tree, to 20 m tall. Young shoots glabrescent or sparsely pubescent. Leaves leathery; petioles (0.5–)1–1.5 cm; leaf blade ovate-elliptic to elliptic-lanceolate, 6–10(–15) × 2.5– 4.5(– 5) cm, base subrounded to cuneate, rarely broadly cuneate, ± oblique, apex acuminate to caudate, margin serrate on the upper 1/3, rarely entire, adaxially glabrous, abaxially reddish brown to yellowish brown scurfy when young; lateral veins 10–12 on each side of midvein. Male spikes simple or branched and forming panicles, rachis sparsely pubescent. Female spikes 8 –17 cm in fruiting time; flowers 2 or 3 per cupule. Cupule globose, broadly ellipsoid or ovoid, 2–3 cm in diam., entirely enclosing nut, splitting irregularly when mature, wall ca.1 mm thick; bracts spine-like, 4– 6(–10) mm, brown to yellowish brown when dry, sparsely pubescent to glabrescent, base connate into bundles and 4 – 5 interrupted rings, apex branched. Nut (1–)2(–3) per cupule, conical, 1–1.4 × 1–1.2 cm, glabrous; scar 8 –10 mm in diam.

Locality: Pok Fu Lam, Tai Tam Tuk, Victoria Peak, Wan Chai Gap, Mount Parker, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island. W. J. Tutcher 4609; Y. S. Lau 455; H. C. Tang 792.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Yunnan, Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Laos, Vietnam.
Ecology: Woods. Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: Sep.–Nov. of following year.
Uses: Material (wood), food (seeds).

Castanopsis fargesii Franch. 栲
J. Bot. (Morot) 13: 195. 1899; FFJ 1: 388, fig. 341. 1982; FTW ed. 2, 2: 61, pl. 24. 1996; FRPS 22: 55, pl. 15: 1–9. 1998; FOC 4: 328. 1999.

Tree, 10 –20 m tall. Branchlets rusty scurfy when young, glabrous in age. Leaves leathery; petioles 1–1.5(–2) cm; leaf blade oblong or elliptic-lanceolate rarely ovate, 6.5 – 8(–15) × 1.8 –2.5(– 5) cm, base subrounded to broadly cuneate, sometimes oblique, apex shortly acuminate, margin entire or with 1–3 pairs of shallow teeth towards apex, densely reddish brown scurfy on abaxial surface; lateral veins 10–15 on each side of midvein. Male spikes solitary or forming panicles; flowers solitary, but crowded on the rachis. Female spikes solitary, glabrous, to 30 cm; flowers 1 per cupule and scattered on rachis. Cupule globose to broadly ovoid, 1.5 –2.5 × 9 –30 cm in diam., splitting irregularly, wall ca. 1 mm thick, whitish grey to brownish puberulent abaxially; bracts spine-like, 6 –10 mm, base connate into 4 –6 zoned bundles. Nut 1 per cupule, ovoid, 1–1.5 × 0.8 –1.4 cm, glabrous; scar 8–10 mm in diam.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan (Ng Tung Chai). F. W. Xing 6932, 8971.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Yunnan, Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan.
