Ecology: Woods. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.; fruiting: Aug.– Oct. of following year.
Uses: Material (wood), food (seeds).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Authority: (Champ. ex Benth.) Rehder & E. H. Wilson
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Common in Hong Kong. Also widely planted
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Castanopsis fissa (Champ. ex Benth.) Rehd. & Wils. 黧蒴錐（裂斗錐栗）
Pl. Wilson. 3: 204. 1916; FFJ 1: 386, fig. 338. 1982; FRPS 22: 21, pl. 3: 5 –14. 1998; FOC 4: 320. 1999.
Quercus fissa Champ. ex Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 6: 114. 1854; FHK 320. 1861; FKH 252. 1912.

Tree, to 20 m tall. Bud-scales and apex of young leaves reddish purple or yellowish brown puberulent. Leaves thickly papery; petioles 1–2.5 cm; leaf blade elliptic, oblong to obovate-elliptic, very variable in size, usually 11–23(–30) × 5 –9 cm, base cuneate, apex shortly acuminate to rounded, margin undulate and crenate on the lower half, adaxially glabrous, abaxially yellowish brown puberulent when young; lateral veins 15 –20(–28) on each side of midvein. Spikes erect, 8 –15 cm, forming a terminal panicle; the males usually many, with 1 terminal female or sometimes 1–2 androgynous spikes just below the female one; rachis glabrous. Infructescence 8–18 cm. Cupule ovoid to ellipsoid, 1–1.5 cm in diam., entirely enclosing the nut when young, afterwards splitting into 2–3(– 4) irregular segments, wall 0.5 –1 mm thick, slightly tomentose outside; bracts scale-like, triangular and imbricate when young, irregularly zoned with age. Nut 1 per cupule, globose to elliptic, 1.3 –1.8 × 1.1–1.6 cm, apex tawny tomentose; scar 4 –7 mm in diam.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Also widely planted. H. C. Tang 858, 2091, 2386.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian; N Thailand, N Vietnam.
Ecology: Secondary forests. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.; fruiting: Oct.–Dec.
Uses: Afforestation.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from the Happy Valley Woods, Hong Kong Island by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1850.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Ma On Shan, Tiu Shau Ngam
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Castanopsis fordii Hance 毛錐
J. Bot. 22: 230. 1884; FKH 254. 1912; FFJ 1: 387, fig. 340. 1982; FRPS 22: 33, pl. 5: 8 –10. 1998; FOC 4: 323. 1999.

Tree, to 20 m tall. Bark rough, dark grey, finely fissured. Branchlets and rachis of inflorescence densely tawny tomentose. Leaves leathery; petioles short and stout, 1–3(–5) mm; leaf blade oblong to lanceolate or oblanceolate-oblong, 9–14(–21) × 3–7 cm, base slightly cordate, rarely rounded, apex acute, or rarely rounded, margin entire and revolute, densely reddish brown tomentose on abaxial surface; lateral veins (12–)14 –18 on each side of midvein. Male spikes usually forming panicle, densely flowered. Female spikes 6–12 cm in fruiting time; flowers 1 per cupule. Cupule globose, 4.5 – 6 cm in diam. including spines, splitting into 4 – 5 regular segments when mature, wall 0.5 –1 mm thick; bracts spine-like entirely covering cupule; spines 10 –15(–20) mm, connate into bundles, pubescent. Nut 1 per cupule, compressed conical, 1.2–1.5 × 1.5 –2 cm, with appressed hairs; scar basal, 4–7 mm in diam.

Locality: Ma On Shan, Tiu Shau Ngam. Y. W. Lam 220; F. W. Xing 8787.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian; N Thailand, N Vietnam.
Ecology: Woods. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.; fruiting: Oct.–Dec.
Uses: Fuelwood.
Notes: The type specimen was collected by C. Ford from Lo Fau Shan, Guangdong Province in Sept. 1888.

Castanopsis kawakamii Hayata 吊皮錐
J. Coll. Sci. Imp. Univ. Tokyo 30(1): 300. 1911; H. L. Li, Woody Fl. Taiwan 86. 1963; FFJ 1: 389, fig. 342. 1982; FTW ed. 2, 2: 64, pl. 27, photo 24. 1996; FRPS 22: 26, pl. 5: 1–4. 1998; FOC 4: 321. 1999.
Castanopsis greenii Chun, J. Arnold Arbor. 9: 150. 1928.

Tree, to 30 m tall. Bark fissured, exfoliating in long stripes hanging on the trunk. Branchlets reddish brown, glabrous. Leaves leathery; petioles 1–1.5(–2.5) cm; leaf blade ovate, ovate‑lanceolate or elliptic-lanceolate, 6–12 × 2–5 cm, rarely broader, base broadly cuneate to subrounded, ± oblique, apex acuminate or caudate, margin entire or rarely with 1–3 minute teeth towards apex, glabrous on both surfaces; lateral veins 8–12 on each side of midvein, reticulation of veins conspicuous abaxially. Male spikes usually forming panicles; rachis sparsely pubescent. Female spikes 5–10 cm, glabrous; flowers 1 per cupule. Cupule globose, 5 –8(–10) cm in diam. including the spines, splitting into 4, rarely 5 segments; bracts spine-like, 20–30 mm, connate to middle into radial branched bundles. Nut 1 per cupule, compressed globose, 1.2–1.5 × 1.7–2 cm, densely tawny tomentose; scar covering 1/3 of nut.

Locality: Sha Tin, Wu Kau Tang. W. Y. Chun 4966.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Woods. Flowering: Mar.–Apr.; fruiting: Aug.– Oct. of the following year.
Uses: Material (wood), environmental.
Notes: The type specimen of Castanopsis greenii Chun (W. Y. Chun 4966, HK sheet 26578) was collected in Shatin by W. Y. Chun on 24 March 1927. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Victoria Peak, Pok Fu Lam, Mount Kellet, Mount Parker, Mount Gough, Wong Nai Chung, Tai Po Kau, Ta Tit Yan, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Castanopsis lamontii Hance 鹿角錐（鐵錐樹）
J. Bot. 13: 368. 1875; FKH 254. 1912; FFJ 1: 387. 1982; FRPS 22: 74, pl. 21: 1– 5. 1998; FOC 4: 332. 1999.
Castanopsis tribuloides auct. non A. DC.: FKH 254. 1912.

Tree, to 30 m tall. Bark greyish brown, longitudinally fissured, inner bark dark reddish brown. Branchlets dark brown, glabrous. Leaves thick-papery or subleathery; petioles 1.5 –2.5 cm, base dark brown when dry; leaf blade elliptic, ovate or oblong, (6 –)12–23(–30) × (2–)3 –5(–8) cm, base broadly cuneate to subrounded, ± oblique, apex acuminate to long-acuminate, margin entire, or sometimes with a few obtuse serratures near apex, glabrous, abaxially glaucous when full grown; lateral veins 10 –12(–15) on each side of midvein. Male spikes axillary, 8–9 cm, usually forming leafy panicle. Female spike axillary, above the male ones, 10–20 cm in fruiting time, flowers 3 per cupule; rachis very thick. Cupule globose to subglobose, 4– 6 cm in diam. including spines, wall ca. 1 mm thick; bracts spine-like, stout, 0.5 –1(–1.5) cm, connate into 4 – 6 spine-zones. Nut 2–3 per cupule, broadly conical, 1.5 –2.5 cm high, densely pubescent; scar covering 2/5 –1/2 of nut.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Pok Fu Lam, Mount Kellet, Mount Parker, Mount Gough, Wong Nai Chung, Tai Po Kau, Ta Tit Yan, Lantau Island. HK sheet 7011, 25062, 25671.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian.
Ecology: Woods. Flowering: Mar.–May; fruiting: Sep.–Nov. of the following year.
Uses: Material (wood), environmental.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Wong Nai Chung, Hong Kong Island by J. Lamont (in Herb. Hance No. 18992, K, BM) in 1874.

Castanopsis sclerophylla (Lindl.) Schott. 苦櫧
Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 47: 638. 1912; FFJ 1: 385, fig. 337. 1982; FRPS 22: 25, pl. 4: 8 –9. 1998; FOC 4: 321. 1999.
Quercus sclerophylla Lindl. in Lindl. & Paxton, Fl. Gard. 1: 59. 1850; FKH 252. 1912.

Tree, 5–10 m tall. Bark shallowly fissured, exfoliating in flakes. Branchlets of the current year reddish brown, glabrous. Leaves leathery; petioles 1.2–1.6(–2.5) cm; leaf blade oblong to ovateelliptic, sometimes obovate-elliptic, 6–12(–17) × 2–5(–7) cm, base subrounded to broadly cuneate, ± oblique, apex acuminate or abruptly and shortly caudate, margin serrulate from middle to apex, glabrous, abaxially silver-grey when full grown; lateral veins 10–15 on each side of midvein, slender but evident. Male spikes usually solitary, axillary, 5 –15 cm. Female spikes to 15 cm; rachis glabrous. Cupule globose to subglobose 1.4 –1.5 cm in diam., enclosing completely (when young) or 3/5 – 4/5 (when mature) of nut, wall ca. 1 mm thick, yellowish brown puberulent outside; bracts scale-like, mostly reduced and base united in 6–7 zoned ribs. Nut 1 per cupule, subglobose , 1–1.4 cm in diam., top puberulous; scar to 1 mm in diam.

Locality: Happy Valley, Garden Road. C. P. Lau 40.
Distribution: Guangxi, Guizhou, E Sichuan, Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian.
Ecology: Woods. Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: Oct.–Nov.
Uses: Materials (wood), food (nut).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Authority: (Chun & Tsiang) Chun ex Y. C. Hsu & H. W. Jen
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Cyclobalanopsis bella (Chun & Tsiang) Chun ex Y. C. Hsu & H. W. Jen 檳榔青岡
J. Beijing Forest Univ. 15(4): 45. 1993; FRPS 22: 302, pl. 95: 1– 4. 1998; FOC 4: 393. 1999.
Quercus bella Chun & Tsiang, J. Arnold Arbor. 28: 326. 1947.

Tree, to 30 m tall. Branchlets angular, initially pubescent, glabrescent with age. Leaves thinly leathery; petioles 1–2 cm, glabrous; leaf blade oblong-lanceolate, 8 –15 × 2–3.5 cm, base cuneate, slightly oblique, apex acuminate, margin serrate above middle, adaxially glabrous, abaxially covered with short appressed hairs when young, glabrous and glaucous in age; lateral veins 12–14 on each side of midvein. Male spikes unknown. Female spikes 1–2 cm, usually with 2–3 cupules. Cupule discoid, ca. 5 mm high, 2.5–3 cm in diam., greyish yellow-puberulent outside, surrounding the base of nut; bracts in 6 –8 concentric rings. Nut compressed globose, 1.5 –2 cm high, 1.5 –2 cm in diam., pubescent when young; scar slightly concave, 1–1.4 cm in diam.

Locality: Tai Po, Yin Ngam. Y. W. Lam 215.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi.
Ecology: Woods. Flowering: Mar; fruiting: Oct.–Dec.
Uses: Material (wood), environmental.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Ta Tit Yan, Tai Po, She Shan Tsuen
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Cyclobalanopsis blakei (Skan) Schott. 櫟子青岡
Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 47: 649. 1912; FRPS 22: 304, pl. 95: 5 –10. 1998; FOC 4: 393. 1999.
Quercus blakei Skan, Hooker's Icon. Pl. 27: t. 2662. 1901; FKH 253. 1912.

Tree, to 35 m tall. Bark greyish black, smooth. Branchlets glabrous. Leaves thinly leathery; petioles slender, 1.5–3 cm, glabrous; leaf blade narrowly ovate-elliptic to obovate-oblanceolate, variable in size, 7–12 × 1.5 –2 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, margin serrate on the upper 1/3, reddish-tomentose on both surfaces when young, soon glabrescent; lateral veins 8–14 on each side of midvein. Male spike ca. 4 cm, tawny tomentose. Female spikes 1–2 cm, with 1–2 cupules. Cupule solitary or in pairs, discoid, 5–10 mm high, 2–3 cm in diam., dark-brown-tomentose outside, surrounding the base of nut; bracts in 6 –7 concentric rings. Nut ellipsoidal or ovoid, 2.5 –3.5 cm high, 1.5 –3 cm in diam., scar 7–11 mm in diam.

Locality: Ta Tit Yan, Tai Po, She Shan Tsuen. W. J. Tutcher 7288, 11293; S. C. Ng 3525.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou; Vietnam, Laos.
Ecology: Woods. Flowering: Mar.; fruiting: Oct.–Dec.
Uses: Material (wood), environmental.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from “Tatitin”, New Territories by C. Ford.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Victoria Peak, Mount Nicholson, Mount Cameron, Ma On Shan, Tai Mo Shan, Lautau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Cyclobalanopsis championii (Benth.) Oerst. 嶺南青岡
Vidensk. Meddel. Dansk Naturhist. Foren. Kjobenhavn 1866: 79. 1876; H. L. Li, Woody Fl. Taiwan 100. 1963; FFJ 1: 405, fig. 361. 1982; FTW ed. 2, 2: 69, pl. 29, photo 25. 1996; FRPS 22: 281, pl. 103: 3 –7. 1998; FOC 4: 388. 1999.
Quercus championii Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 6: 113. 1854; FHK 321. 1861; FKH 253. 1912.

Tree, to 20 m tall. Young shoots, petioles and inflorescence tawny tomentose. Leaves thickly leathery; petioles 0.8–1.5 cm; leaf blade obovate to oblong, 3.5 –10(–13) × 2–3.5(– 6) cm, base cuneate to acute, apex broadly obtuse or rounded, with a blunt tip, rarely retuse, margin revolute, entire or sometimes slightly crenulate near apex, adaxially glabrous and shining when full-grown, abaxially densely brownish stellate-tomentose; lateral veins 6 –10 on each side of midvein, as is the midvein impressed adaxially, conspicuously raised abaxially. Male spike 4– 8 cm. Female spikes erect, ca. 4 cm, with 3–10 cupules. Cupule bowl-shaped, 7–10 mm high, 1.4 –1.7 cm in diam., brownish-tomentose abaxially, enclosing 1/3–1/4 of nut; bracts in 4–7 concentric rings. Nut broadly ovoid or compressed globose, 1.5 –2 cm high, 1.2–1.5(–1.8) cm in diam., rounded on both ends, pubescent when young; scar 4 – 5 mm in diam.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Mount Nicholson, Mount Cameron, Ma On Shan, Tai Mo Shan, Lautau Island. H. C. Tang 621; C. P. Lau 60; HK sheet 6718
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian.
Ecology: Woods. Flowering: Dec. to Mar. of the following year; fruiting: Nov.–Dec.
Uses: Material (wood), environmental.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Hong Kong Island by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1850.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Authority: (Metc.) Y. C. Hsu & H. W. Jen ex Q. F. Zheng
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Cyclobalanopsis chungii (Metc.) Y. C. Hsu & H. W. Jen ex Q. F. Zheng 福建青岡
FFJ 1: 405, fig. 362. 1982; FRPS 22: 282, pl. 103: 8 –10. 1998; FOC 4: 388. 1999.
Quercus chungii Metc., Lingnan Sci. J. 10: 481. 1931.

Tree, to 15 m tall. Branchlets, petioles and inflorescence densely brown stellate tomentose. Leaves thinly leathery; petioles 1–2.2 cm; leaf blade obovate, obovate-elliptic to elliptic, 5–12 × 1.5–4 cm, base broadly cuneate to subrounded, apex short-caudate, rarely acute, margin obscurely serrulate or crenulate towards apex, rarely entire, adaxially glabrous and shining when full-grown, abaxially densely greyish brown stellate-tomentose; lateral veins 9–15 on each side of midvein. Male spike unknown; Female spikes erect, 1.5–2 cm, with 2–6 cupules. Cupule discoid, 6–8 mm high, 1.2–1.8 cm in diam., brown-tomentose outside, enclosing 1/4–1/3 of nut; bracts in 5–7 concentric rings. Nut compressed globose or ovoid, 1.5–2.1 cm high, 1.4–1.8 cm in diam., top flat-rounded, minutely tomentose; scar 1–1.2 cm in diam.

Locality: Castle Peak, So Kwun Wat. P. S. Choi s.n. (HK sheet 38401); F. W. Xing 9333, 10205.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian.
Ecology: Woods. Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: Oct.–Nov.
Uses: Material (wood), environmental.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Mount Kellet, Sai Kung, Tai Wai, Ta Tit Yan
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Cyclobalanopsis edithiae (Skan) Schott. 華南青岡
Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 47: 650. 1912; FRPS 22: 306, pl. 86: 5–7. 1998; FOC 4: 393. 1999.
Quercus edithiae Skan, Hooker's Icon. Pl. 27: t. 2661. 1901; FKH 253. 1912.

Tree, to 20 m tall. Branchlets slightly angular, glabrous. Leaves leathery; petioles 2–3 cm, glabrous; leaf blade oblong to obovateoblong, 5–16 × 2–6 cm, base cuneate, apex broadly acute, margin shallowly serrulate on the upper 1/3, adaxially dark green, glabrous, abaxially greyish brown-tomentose when young, glabrous in age; lateral veins 9 –12 on each side of midvein, inconspicuous. Male spike 2–3 cm, densely yellow-tomentose. Female spikes 1–2 cm in fruiting time, with 3– 4 cupules. Cupule bowl-shaped, 12–15 mm high, 1.8 –2.5 cm in diam., wall 2–3 mm thick, dark-yellow-tomentose outside, enclosing 1/4 –1/3 of nut; bracts in 6 – 8 concentric rings. Nut ellipsoid to cylindrical-ellipsoid, 3– 4.5 cm high, 2–3 cm in diam.; scar slightly convex, ca. 7 mm in diam.

Locality: Mount Kellet, Sai Kung, Tai Wai, Ta Tit Yan. W. J. Tutcher 8049, 9486; L. T. Lo 371.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi.
Ecology: Woods. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.; fruiting: Oct.– Dec.
Uses: Material (wood), environmental.
Notes: The leaves of this species are somewhat similar to C. blakei, but can be easily distinguished by its bowl-shaped and yellow-tomentose cupule. The type specimen was collected from “Tatitin”, New Territories, by C. Ford.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Shek O, Cape d'Aguilar, Pok Fu Lam, Ma On Shan
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Cyclobalanopsis glauca (Thunb.) Oerst. 青岡
Vidensk. Meddel. Dansk Naturhist. Foren. Kjobenhavn 1866: 78. 1867; H. L. Li, Woody Fl. Taiwan 101. 1963; FFJ 1: 408, fig. 365. 1982; FTW ed. 2, 2: 72, pl. 31. 1996; FRPS 22: 315, pl. 98: 1. 1998; FOC 4: 396. 1999.
Quercus glauca Thunb., Syst. Veg., ed. 14, 858. 1784; FKH 253. 1912.

Tree, to 20 m tall. Branchlets glabrous. Leaves leathery; petioles 1–2.5 cm, glabrous; leaf blade obovate-elliptic or elliptic, 6–15(–18) × 2.5 – 5(– 8) cm, base rounded or broadly cuneate, apex acuminate to caudate-acuminate, margin remotely serrate on the upper half, adaxially glabrous and shining, abaxially glaucous, with appressed hairs and scurfy lepidote; lateral veins 9 –10 on each side of midvein. Male spike (2–)5 – 6 cm, rachis brown-tomentose. Female spikes 1.5 –3 cm in fruiting time, with 1–3 cupules. Cupule bowl-shaped, 6 –7 mm high, 0.8 –1 cm in diam., sparsely pubescent outside, enclosing 1/3 of nut; bracts in 5–7 concentric rings. Nut ellipsoid-ovoid or ellipsoid, 1–1.5 cm high, 0.9 –1.2 cm in diam., scar flat or slightly convex, ca. 5 mm in diam.

Locality: Shek O, Cape D'Aguilar, Pok Fu Lam, Ma On Shan. X. Y. Zhuang 1931; Y. S. Lau 1514, 3009.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Yunnan, Xizang, Hunan, Hubei, Henan, Shaanxi, Gansu, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Korea, Japan, Vietnam, N India, Bhutan.
Ecology: Woods. Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: Oct.
Uses: Material (wood), environmental.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Authority: (Chun) Chun ex Y. C. Hsu & H. Wei Jen
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Cyclobalanopsis hui (Chun) Chun ex Y. C. Hsu & H. W. Jen 雷公青岡
J. Beijing Forest. Univ. 15(4): 45. 1993; FRPS 22: 282, pl. 85: 1–3. 1998; FOC 4: 388. 1999.
Quercus hui Chun, J. Arnold Arbor. 9: 126. 1928.

Tree, 10–15 m tall. Branchlets, petioles and inflorescences densely tawny-tomentose when young, glabrescent with age. Leaves thinly leathery; petioles 1–1.4 cm; leaf blade oblong, oblanceolate or elliptic-lanceolate, 7–13 × 1.5 –3 cm, base broadly cuneate, often slightly oblique, apex obtuse, rarely acuminate, margin recurved, entire or obscurely serrulate towards apex, adaxially glabrous and shining when full-grown, abaxially tawny-tomentose when young, gradually glabrate; lateral veins 6 –10 on each side of midvein. Male spike 5–9 cm, 2–4 clustered. Female spikes 1–2 cm, with 2–5 cupules crowded at apex of rachis. Cupule shallow bowl-shaped, 6–10 mm high, 1.5 –3 cm in diam., brown-tomentose outside, enclosing 1/2 of nut; bracts in 4 – 6 concentric rings. Nut compressed globose, 1.5–2 cm high, 1.5 –2.5 cm in diam., densely tawny-tomentose when young, but glabrescent later; scar concave, 7–10 mm in diam.

Locality: Pat Sin Leng. Y. W. Lam 500, 501.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan.
Ecology: Woods. Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: Oct.–Dec.
Uses: Material (wood), environmental.

Cyclobalanopsis litseoides (Dunn) Schott. 木薑葉青岡
Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 47: 658. 1912; FRPS 22: 277, pl. 85: 6– 8. 1998; FOC 4: 387. 1999.
Quercus litseoides Dunn, J. Bot. 47: 377. 1909; FKH 253. 1912.

Tree, to 10 m tall. Branchlets slender, initially tomentose, gradually glabrate. Leaves subsessile, blade obovate-oblanceolate or narrowly elliptic, 2.5–7 × 0.8–3 cm, apex broadly obtuse to rounded, base cuneate, margin entire, adaxially dark green, abaxially greyish green, glabrous on both surfaces; lateral veins 6–9 on each side of midvein. Male spike 3–5 cm; rachis and perianth brown‑tomentose. Female spikes ca. 1 cm, with 2 apical cupules. Cupule bowl-shaped, 5–6 mm high, 1–1.5 cm in diam., sparsely greyish-brown-tomentose outside, enclosing 1/3 of nut; bracts in 5–7 concentric rings. Nut ellipsoidal, 1.5–1.8 cm high, ca. 1 cm in diam., puberulent at apex; scar flat 5–6 mm in diam.

Locality: Lantau Island. W. J. Tutcher 6597; H. C. Tang 2149; P. S. Choi s.n. (HK sheet 35584).
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi.
Ecology: Woods. Flowering: Jan.; fruiting: Dec.
Uses: Material (wood), environmental.

Cyclobalanopsis myrsinifolia (Blume) Oerst. 小葉青岡
Skr. Vidensk.-Selsk. Christiana, Math.-Naturvidensk. Kl. 9(6): 387. 1871; FFJ 1: 407. 1982; FRPS 22: 325, pl. 98: 3. 1998; FTW ed. 2, 2: 78, pl. 36. 1996; FOC 4: 398. 1999.
Quercus myrsinifolia Blume, Mus. Bot. 1: 305. 1850.

Tree, 10 –15 m tall. Branchlets glabrous, with raised light brown lenticels. Leaves leathery; petioles 1–2.5 cm, glabrous; leaf blade lanceolate to oblong-lanceolate or broadly ovate-oblong, 5–12 × 1.5 – 4 cm, base cuneate or sub-rounded, apex acuminate to caudate-acuminate, margin serrulate above middle, adaxially green, abaxially glaucous, becoming dark grey when dry, glabrous on both surfaces; lateral veins 10–14 on each side of midvein. Male spike 4 – 6(–9) cm, rachis slender, ± tawny tomentose. Female spikes 1.5–3 cm, with 2–3 cupules. Cupule cup-shaped, 5 –7 mm high, 0.7–1 cm in diam., whitish pubescent outside, enclosing 1/3 of nut; bracts in 6 –9 concentric rings. Nut ellipsoid, 1.3 –2 cm high, 0.8 –1.1 cm in diam., glabrous, apex rounded; scar flat, ca. 6 mm in diam.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 3164; H. C. Tang 11651; W. J. Tutcher s.n. (HK sheet 6801).
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Yunnan, Hunan, Hubei, Henan, Shaanxi, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Korea, Japan, Vietnam, Laos, Thailand.
Ecology: Woods by streams or ravines. Flowering: Jun.; fruiting: Oct. of the following year.
Uses: Material (wood), environmental.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Mount Gough, Mount Nicholson, Tai Tam, Wan Chai Gap
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Cyclobalanopsis neglecta Schott. 竹葉青岡
Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 47: 650. 1912; FOC 4: 387. 1999.
Cyclobalanopsis bambusifolia (Hance) Chun ex Y. C. Hsu & H. W. Jen, J. Forest. Univ. 15(4): 44. 1993; FRPS 22: 280, pl. 85: 4 –5. 1998.
Quercus bambusifolia Hance in Seem. Bot. Voy. Herald, t. 91. 1875, non Fortune (1860).
Quercus salicina auct. non Blume: FHK 321. 1861; FKH 253. 1912.

Tree, to 20 m tall. Young shoots silky-hairy, glabrous in age. Leaves thinly leathery, crowded towards apex of branchlets; petioles 2– 5 mm, glabrous; leaf blade narrowly lanceolate to ellipticlanceolate, 3–11 × 0.6–1.8 cm, narrowed to both ends, apex blunt, margin entire, adaxially dark green, glabrous, abaxially ± glaucous, glabrous or with some long hairs at base; lateral veins 7–14 on each side of midvein, inconspicuous. Male catkins axillary, very slender, 2.5–5 cm, rachis rusty-tomentose. Female spikes short and erect, 0.5–1 cm, with 2 flowers; styles 3 or 4. Infructescences 5–10 mm, usually with only one fruit. Cupule discoid or cup-shaped, 5–10 mm high, 1.3–1.8 cm in diam., enclosing ca. 1/2 of nut, greyish brown tomentose outside; bracts in 4–6 concentric rings. Nut obovoid or ellipsoid, 1.5–2.5 cm high, 1–1.6 cm in diam., slightly tomentose; scar convex, 5–7 mm in diam.

Locality: Mount Gough, Mount Nicholson, Tai Tam, Wan Chai Gap. Y. S. Lau 1703; H. C. Tang 1137; W. J. Tutcher s.n. (HK sheet 6819).
Distribution: Hainan. Guangdong, Guangxi; Vietnam.
Ecology: Woodlands. Flowering: Jun.; fruiting: Oct.

Lithocarpus attenuatus (Skan) Rehd. 尖葉柯
J. Arnold Arbor. 1: 123. 1919; FRPS 22: 134, pl. 40: 4 –7. 1998; FOC 4: 350. 1999.
Quercus attenuata Skan in F. B. Forbes & Hemsley, J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 26: 506. 1899; FKH 254. 1912.

Tree, 10 –15 m tall, glabrous throughout. Bud-scales with oily resin when dry. Branchlets of last year growth white-farinose. Leaves thin-leathery; petioles 1.5 –3 cm; leaf blade ovate-elliptic or lanceolate, 7–13 × 2–4 cm, base cuneate, decurrent to the petiole, apex long-acuminate, entire or sometimes undulate, abaxial surface glaucous when dry, with adhersive waxy-scales; lateral veins 9–13 on each side of midvein, slender; veins invisible or obscure. Male spike solitary or branched, axillary. Female flowers solitary and scattered on rachis; rachis sulcate, with white waxy scales. Cupules globose in fruiting time, base slightly narrowed like a stalk, 30–35 mm high, 25–30 mm in diam., enclosing nut completely, wall less than 0.5 mm thick, crustaceous; bracts triangular, small and obscure, the proximal ones united into concentric rings, the distal ones only remaining a subulate tip or wart-like. Nut subglobse, 20–25 mm high, 18 –28 mm in diam., white-farinose, wall ca. 0.5 mm , apex slightly narrowed, obtuse, base flat, scar 7–12 mm in diam., concave to 1–1.5 mm.

Locality: Happy Valley, Tai Tam. W. J. Tutcher s.n. (HK sheet 6708); HK sheet 4515.
Distribution: S Guangdong, SW Guangxi.
Ecology: Woods. Flowering: Jun.– Oct.; fruiting: Jun.– Oct. of the following year.
Uses: Material (wood), environmental.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Happy Valley woods by C. Ford.

Lithocarpus corneus (Lour.) Rehd. 煙斗柯（石柯）
Stand. Cycl. Hort. 3569. 1917; FFJ 1: 393, fig. 344. 1982; FRPS 22: 128, pl. 36: 1–3. 1998; FOC 4: 349. 1999.
Pasania cornea (Lour.) Liao, Taxon. Revis. Fam. Fagac. 118, fig. 34: 1–2. 1991; FTW ed. 2, 2: 96, pl. 46, photo 40. 1996.
Quercus cornea Lour., Fl. Cochinchin. 572. 1790; FHK 322. 1861; FKH 252. 1912.

Tree, to 15 m tall. Branchlets light tawny, glabrous or pubescent. Leaves papery or leathery, ± crowded towards apex of branches; petioles 0.5–2(–4) cm; leaf blade narrowly elliptic to ovate-oblong or lanceolate-elliptic, (4–)6–13(–20) × 1.5–4(–7) cm, base cuneate to subrounded, symmetric or oblique, apex acuminate to acute, margin serrate or dentate, sometimes shallowly undulate, rarely entire, adaxial surface glabrous, or puberulent on the compressed midvein, abaxial surface slightly pubescent on midvein, or only with tuft of hairs on axils of veins; lateral veins 9–12 on each side of midvein, ending in teeth. Spikes mostly androgynous, terminal, erect, 2.5–4 cm, with female flowers on the lower part of the rachis. Cupule broadly turbinate, 22–45 mm high, 25–55 mm in diam., enclosing most part of nut, wall woody and thickened at base; bracts deltoid or rhomboid, central and margin ridged, the upper ones turned inwards. Nut hemispherical and glabrous in the enclosed part, the exserted flat top slightly concave and tomentose, wall ± horny, usually thicker than the wall of cupule; scar covering 2/3 of the nut.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. C. P. Lau 44, 68; H. C. Tang 1893.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, S Guizhou, SE Yunnan, S Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Woods, frequent on sunny slopes. Flowering: Almost all the year round, but mainly May–Jun.; fruit matures in the following year.
Uses: Material (wood), environmental.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Po Kau, Ta Tit Yan
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Lithocarpus elizabethae (Tutch.) Rehd. 厚斗柯
J. Arnold Arbor. 1: 125. 1919; FRPS 22: 157, pl. 46: 1– 5. 1998; FOC 4: 357. 1999.
Quercus elizabethae Tutch., J. Bot. 49: 273. 1911; FKH 254. 1912.

Tree, 9 –15 m tall. Branches and leaves glabrous. Leaves thickly papery; petioles 1–2 cm; leaf blade narrowly oblong or lanceolate, 9 –17 × 2–4 cm, base cuneate, decurrent, apex acuminate, margin entire, concolorous or ± glaucous abaxially; lateral veins slender, 13 –16 on each side of midvein; veins almost invisible. Male spikes 3-many forming panicle, or sometimes solitary in axils of leaves; rachis sparsely pubescent. Female spikes 2–4 congested at apex of branches; rachis 4– 6(–10) mm thick in fruiting time; female flowers usually in cluster of 3. Cupule subglobose, apex abruptly narrowed and slightly elongate into a nipple, 15 –30 mm high, 15 –28 mm in diam., usually covering nut completely, wall 2 mm (upper part) to 4 mm (lower part) thick; bracts broadly triangular or rhomboid, imbricate, the apical ones incurved. Nut compressed globose or subglobose, 14–24 mm in diam.; scar concave, 13–16 mm in diam.

Locality: Tai Po Kau, Ta Tit Yan. HK sheet 26371; W. J. Tutcher 9114, 9469.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, SE Guizhou, SE Yunnan.
Ecology: Mixed forests, frequent in moist places. Flowering: Jul.–Sep.; fruiting: Aug.–Nov.
Uses: Material (wood), environmental.
Notes: The type specimens were collected from Victoria Peak and Tai Wai by W. J. Tutcher (nos. 4616, 9114, HK) around 1910.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Pok Fu Lam, Tai Po Kau, Lantau Peak
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Lithocarpus fenestratus (Roxb.) Rehd. var. brachycarpus A. Camus 泥柯
Bull. Soc. Bot. France 90: 201. 1934; FRPS 22: 172, pl. 51: 8 –9. 1998; FOC 4: 360. 1999, pro syn. sub L. fenestratus auct. non (Roxb.) Rehd.
Quercus fenestrata auct non Roxb.: FKH 253. 1912.

Tree, to 30 m tall. Young shoots tawny scurfy-lepidote. Leaves thickly papery; petioles 10 –18 mm; leaf blade ovate-elliptic or lanceolate, 9–15 × 2–7 cm, base cuneate, apex acute or shortly acuminate, margin entire, abaxially tawny scurfy-lepidote, ± greyish when dry; lateral veins 12–16 on each side of midvein, usually impressed adaxially; veins slender or invisible. Male spikes usually in panicles. Female spikes solitary and axillary, to 18 cm; rachis 5– 8 mm thick in fruiting time, scurfy-lepidote. Cupules in cluster of 3, only 1 or 2 developed, compressed globose, 10–15 mm high, 15 –28 mm in diam., covering most part of nut, wall ca. 0.5 mm thick, scurfy puberulent abaxially; bracts triangular, imbricate and appressed, only the subulate tips separate from the cupule. Nut compressed globose 10–15 mm high, 13 –25 mm in diam., apex rounded or pointed; scar concave, 10 –18 mm in diam.

Locality: Pok Fu Lam, Tai Po Kau, Lantau Peak. HK sheet 6707; W. J. Tutcher s.n. (HK sheet 6747).
Distribution: Hainan, SW Guangxi, SE Yunnan; NE Vietnam.
Ecology: Woods. Flowering: Aug.– Oct.; fruiting: Oct.–Dec. of the following year.
Uses: Material (wood), environmental.

Lithocarpus glaber (Thunb.) Nakai 柯
Cat. Sem. Spor. Hort. Bot. Univ. Imp. Tokyo 8. 1916; FFJ 1: 400, fig. 355. 1982; FRPS 22: 186, pl. 58: 6. 1998; FOC 4: 363. 1999.
Pasania glabra (Thunb.) Oerst., Nat. Foren. Vidensk. Meddel. 18: 83. 1866; H. L. Li, Woody Fl. Taiwan 91. 1963; FTW ed. 2, 2: 99, photo 42. 1996.
Quercus glabra Thunb., Murray, Syst. Veg., ed. 14, 858. 1784.
Quercus thalassica Hance, Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 1: 176. 1849; FHK 321. 1861; FKH 253. 1912.

Tree, to 15 m tall. Branchlets and bud-scales densely tawny tomentose. Leaves leathery or thick papery; petioles 1–2 cm, initially tomentose; leaf blade obovate, obovate-elliptic or oblong, 6 –12 × 2.5 – 4(– 5.5) cm, base cuneate, apex abruptly acute, shortly caudate or long-acuminate, margin entire or with 2– 4 teeth near apex, abaxially scurfy tomentose when young, later glabrate or nearly so; lateral veins 6– 8(–10) on each side of midvein; veinlets usually invisible. Male spikes forming panicle or solitary in axils of leaves, 5 –10(–15) cm; rachis densely tawny tomentose. Female spikes 7–13(–18) cm in fruiting time, often with a few male flowers; female flowers 3(– 5) clustered. Cupule discoid or cup-shape, 5 –7(–10) mm high, 9 –11(–15) mm in diam., thickened towards base, woody; bracts small, triangular, appressed, imbricate or united into concentric rings, densely puberulous abaxially. Nut ellipsoid, 12–25 mm high, 8 –15 mm in diam., apex pointed, ± white-farinose, dark chestnut brown; scar concave, 3 – 5(– 8) mm in diam.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. HK sheet 6850; C. P. Lau 147; Y. W. Lam 31.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hunan, Hubei, Henan, Anhui, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Taiwan.
Ecology: Woods, frequent on sunny slopes. Flowering: Jul.–Nov.; fruiting: Jul.–Nov. of the following year.
Uses: Material (wood), environmental.
Notes: The type specimen of Quercus thalassica was collected from Hong Kong Island by H. F. Hance before 1850.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Victoria Peak, Tai Po Kau, Ma On Shan
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Lithocarpus haipinii Chun 耳柯（卷葉石櫟）
J. Arnold Arbor. 28: 233. 1947; FFJ 1: 398, fig. 353. 1982; FRPS 22: 209, pl. 65: 1. 1998; FOC 4: 369. 1999.

Tree, to 30 m tall. Branchlets of the current year, petioles and rachis of inflorescence densely covered with greyish white or tawny long hairs. Leaves firmly leathery; petioles 2–3.5 cm; leaf blade broadly elliptic, ovate, obovate or obovate-elliptic, 8–15 × 4–8 cm, base rounded or broadly cuneate, often asymmetric, apex rounded or acute, sometimes shortly caudate, falcate, margin recurved, abaxial surface densely pilose; lateral veins 9–13 on each side of midvein, veins as is the lateral veins impressed adaxially. Male spike forming panicle. Female spikes shorter, usually terminal on apex of branches, 6–14 cm; female flowers 3–5-clustered. Young cupule covering entirely nut; bracts linear; mature cupule discoid, 3–6 mm high, 15–25 mm in diam., covering ca. 1/3 nut, wall almost woody; bracts reflexed, tip hooked. Nut subglobose but slightly compressed, bottom flat, 18–26 mm high, 20–30 mm in diam., white-farinose when young; scar concave, 8–14 mm in diam.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Tai Po Kau, Ma On Shan. Y. S. Lau 1268, 2053; P. S. Choi 512; W. Y. Chun 9159.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, S Hunan, S Guizhou.
Ecology: Woods, frequent on gentle, dry slopes. Flowering: Jul.–Aug.; fruiting: Jul.–Aug. of the following year.
Uses: Material (wood), environmental.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Victoria Peak in 1930 (C. L. Tso 22580, IBSC).

Lithocarpus hancei (Benth.) Rehd. 硬殼柯（漢斯石柯）
J. Arnold Arbor. 1: 127. 1919; FFJ 1: 400, fig. 356. 1982; FRPS 22: 176, pl. 54. 1998; FOC 4: 362. 1999.
Quercus hancei Benth., FHK 322. 1861; FKH 253. 1912.

Tree, to 15 m tall, glabrous except the inflorescence. Branchlets ± tawny or grey, usually with a thin layer of translucent wax. Leaves thinly papery to rigid leathery; petioles 1–2(– 4) cm; leaf blade variable in shape and size, ovate, obovate, broadly elliptic, obovate-elliptic, narrowly elliptic or lanceolate, usually 6–14 × 3 – 5 cm, the ratio of length/width = 1.2– 5:1, base attenuate to broadly cuneate, usually decurrent to the petiole, apex shortly caudate-acuminate, sometimes rounded obtuse or acute, margin entire, ± recurved, concolour or sometimes white farinose adaxially when dry; lateral veins 11–14 on each side of midvein, slender and closely spaced; veins reticulate. Male spikes rarely 4 –10(–13) cm, usually forming panicle, sometimes with female flowers on the basal part; rachis sometimes twisted. Female spikes 2–many crowded at apex of branches, 5 – 8 cm. Cupule usually 3 – 5 clusterd, rarely solitary, shallow-bowl-shaped or discoid, 3–7 mm high, 10 –20 mm broad, covering nearly 1/3 of nut; bracts scale-like, triangular, appressed, imbricate or connate into a few concentric rings. Nut compressed globose, subglobose or broadly conical, 8 –12 mm high, 6 –25 mm in diam., apex rounded to pointed, rarely flat, glabrous; scar concave, 5 –10 mm in diam.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 354, 418, 1329.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Yunnan, Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Zhejiang.
Ecology: Woods. Flowering: Jul.–Aug.; fruiting: Aug.–Nov. of the following year.
Uses: Material (wood), environmental.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Hong Kong Island around 1850 by J. G. Champion.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Aberdeen, Wong Nai Chung, Repulse Bay, Bowen Road, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Lithocarpus harlandii (Hance ex Walpers) Rehd. 港柯（夏蘭柯）
J. Arnold Arbor. 1: 127. 1919; FFJ 1: 402, fig. 358. 1982; FRPS 22: 193, pl. 60: 1– 5. 1998; FOC 4: 365. 1999.
Quercus harlandii Hance ex Walpers, Ann. Bot. Syst. 3: 382. 1852; FHK 321. 1861; FKH 253. 1912.

Tree, to 18 m tall, glabrous except inflorescences. Young branches sulcate, purplish brown, becoming dark brown when dry. Leaves firmly leathery; petioles 1.5 –3 cm; leaf blade oblong to elliptic 7–18 × 3 – 6 cm, base attenuate-cuneate, often slightly oblique, apex caudate-acuminate, often falcate, margin entire or obtusely undulate-dentate near apex, rarely entire, glabrous; lateral veins 8 –13 on each side of midvein; veinlets obscure. Male spikes 2.5– 5 cm, solitary in the upper axils of leaves or forming panicles to 15 cm, erect, tomentose. Female spikes terminal, rigid, flexuose, ca. 5 cm, lengthening to 5 –10 cm in fruiting time; female flowers in cluster of 3, scattered on rachis; rachis shortly tomentose. Cupule cup-shaped, 6–10 mm high, 14 –20 mm in diam.; bracts triangular or rhomboid, margin and midvein ± ridged, imbricate, puberulous outside. Nut conical or broadly ellipsoid, 22–28 mm high, 16 –2 mm in diam., apex rounded or obtuse, wall 1.5 –2 mm thick; scar concave, 9–12 mm in diam.

Locality: Aberdeen, Wong Nai Chung, Repulse Bay, Bowen Road, Lantau Island. C. P. Lau. 79; H. C. Tang 367; Y. S. Lau 2393.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, S Jiangxi, Taiwan.
Ecology: Woods. Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: Sep.– Oct. of the following year.
Uses: Material (wood), environmental.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Happy Valley woods around 1850.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Mount Cameron, Tai Tam, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Lithocarpus irwinii (Hance) Rehd. 廣南柯
J. Arnold Arbor. 1: 127. 1919; FRPS 22: 103. 1998; FOC 4: 342. 1999.
Quercus amygdalifolia auct. non Skan: FKH 252. 1912.
Quercus irwinii Hance, Ann. Sci. Nat. Bot. ser. 2, 18: 229. 1862.

Tree, 8–12 m tall. Young shoots sulcate, with raised lenticels, densely tawny pilose, soon glabrate. Leaves thickly and rigidly leathery; petioles usually less than 1 cm, brownish black when dry; leaf blade elliptic or lanceolate, 7–12 × 2– 4 cm, base cuneate, decurrent, apex acute or acuminate, margin ± revolute, entire or undulate on the upper half, dark brown and often oily on adaxial surface when dry, abaxial surface reddish brown scurfy and sparsely pilose on midvein when young, greyish when mature; lateral veins 10–15 on each side of midvein; veins very slender or inconspicuous. Male spike 3 – 5 cm, solitary in axils of leaves or 2–3 in panicles; rachis tawny pubescent. Female spike in pairs terminal on branchlets, 2–5 cm; rachis 5–8 mm thick in fruiting time; flowers in clusters of 3, sometimes solitary. Cupule turbinate, broadest at apex, 20 –26 mm high, 18 –24 mm in diam., apex almost flat, enclosing the nut completely, wall 2– 4 mm thick; bracts deltoid, middle and margins thickened in ridges, imbricate. Nut subglobose, ca. 15 mm in diam., densely covered with minute appressed hairs; scar convex, covering ca. 1/4 of the nut.

Locality: Mount Cameron, Tai Tam, Lantau Island. HK sheet 6694, 26307; W. J. Tutcher 5589.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian.
Ecology: Woods. Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: Oct.–Nov. of the following year.
Uses: Material (wood), environmental.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Wong Nai Chung, Hong Kong Island in Nov. 1862 by J. J. Irwin (in Herb. Hance No. 9818, BM).

Lithocarpus iteaphyllus (Hance) Rehd. 鼠刺葉柯
J. Arnold Arbor. 1: 127. 1919; FRPS 22: 146. 1998; FOC 4: 353. 1999.
Quercus iteaphylla Hance, J. Bot. 22: 229. 1884; FKH 253. 1912.
Lithocarpus iteaphylloides Chun, J. Arnold Arbor. 28: 236. 1947.

Tree, 5 –10 m tall. Branchlets of the current year growth conspicuously sulcate, dark reddish brown, glabrous; bud-scale glabrous. Leaves thickly papery; petioles usually 5– 8 mm, sometimes to 3 cm, ± thickened at base; leaf blade narrowly oblong or lanceolate, 8 –13 × 2.5 – 4.5 cm, apex acuminate, base broadly cuneate, decurrent to petiole, margin entire; midvein raised on both surfaces; lateral veins 8–12 on each side of midvein, slender, conspicuous on both surfaces. Spikes usually androgynous, 3 –7 cm, solitary or congested on apex of branches of last year growth, with male flowers on apical part and female ones on basal part, both solitary and scattered on tawny puberulous rachis. Cupule bowl-shaped, 5– 8 mm high, 10–14 mm broad, base thickly woody; bracts reduced and united into 6 – 8 concentric rings, tawny waxy-lepidote and sparsely puberulous abaxially. Nut ellipsoid, 10 –18 mm high, 10 –14 mm in diam., sometimes as broad as high, apex pointed or rounded, glabrous, light chestnut brown; scar concave, 5– 6 mm in diam.

Locality: Happy Valley, Causeway Bay. W. J. Tutcher s.n. (HK sheet 6791, 6792).
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, S Hunan, S Jiangxi.
Ecology: Woods on sunny slopes and banks of streams. Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: Jul.– Oct.
Uses: Material (wood), environmental.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Hong Kong Island by C. Ford in 1882.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Lan Nai Wan, Long Ke, Sai Wan Shan, Kau Ling Chung
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Lithocarpus konishii (Hayata) Hayata 油葉柯
Icon. Pl. Formosan. 6 (Suppl.): 72. 1917; FRPS 22: 145, pl. 43: 4 –9. 1998; FOC 4: 353. 1999.
Quercus konishii Hayata, J. Coll. Imp. Univ. Tokyo 25(19): 201. 1908.
Pasania konishii (Hayata) Schott., Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 47: 673. 1912; H. L. Li, Woody Fl. Taiwan 93. 1963; FTW ed. 2, 2: 108, pl. 53, photo 46. 1996.

Trees, usually to 5 m tall. Bud-scales with light grey silky short hairs. Spring shoots glabrous; autumn shoots tawny pubescent. Leaves firmly papery; petioles 0.5–1.5 cm; leaf blade ovate, obovate, elliptic or obovate-elliptic, 3–6 × 1.2–2.4 cm, apex acute or shortly caudateacuminate, base cuneate, margin with 3–6 obtuse teeth on each side, with tuft of hairs at axils of veins on abaxial surface when young; midvein puberulous adaxially; lateral veins 7–10 on each side of midvein, slightly impressed adaxially; veins slender but visible. Male spikes 3–5(–10) cm, solitary or forming panicles; rachis tawny tomentose; female flowers solitary or rarely 2 in clusters on the basal part of the male rachis, or in separate spike. Cupule discoid, 4–8 mm high, 15–23 mm in diam., enclosing the bottom of nut, wall 1.5–2 mm thick; bracts broadly triangular, midvein ridged, imbricate, greyish brown tomentose. Nut compressed globose, apex rounded or flat, 10–18 mm high, 15–25 mm in diam., wall 3–6 mm thick, horny, glabrous; scar margin concave, central ± convex, 13–24 in diam.

Locality: Lan Nai Wan, Long Ke, Sai Wan Shan, Kau Ling Chung. Y. S. Lau 1480; Y. W. Lam 294, 462.
Distribution: E Hainan, S Taiwan.
Ecology: Woods. Flowering: Apr.–Aug.; fruiting: Jul.– Oct. of the following year.
Uses: Material (wood), environmental.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Ta Tit Yan, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Lithocarpus litseifolius (Hance) Chun 木薑葉柯（多穗柯）
J. Arnold Arbor. 9: 152. 1928; FRPS 22: 201. 1998; FOC 4: 367. 1999.
Lithocarpus synbalanos (Hance) Chun, J. Arnold Arbor. 9: 152. 1928; FFJ 1: 399, fig. 354. 1982;
Quercus litseifolia Hance, J. Bot. 22: 229. 1884.
Quercus polystacha auct. non Wall. ex DC.: FKH 253. 1912.
Quercus synbalanos Hance, J. Bot. 22: 228. 1884; FKH 253. 1912.

Tree, to 20 m tall, glabrous except the inflorescence. Branchlets and petioles sometimes ± white-farinose when dry. Leaves papery or subleathery; petioles 1.5 –2.5 cm; leaf blade elliptic, obovate-elliptic or ovate, rarely narrowly elliptic, 8 –18 × 3 – 8 cm, base cuneate to broadly cuneate, apex acuminate or abruptly acute, margin entire, concolorous or ± glaucous abaxially; lateral veins 8–11 on each side of midvein, concealed near the edge; veins slender, reddish brown or brownish yellow when dry. Male spike 7–15(–25) cm, forming panicle, rarely solitary. Female spikes 14 –25 cm; female flowers 3 – 5 clustered, but the spikes sometimes androgynous, 2– 6 congested at apex of branches; rachis sparsely pubescent. Cupule discoid, 8 –14 mm in diam., glabrous, thickened towards base, woody; bracts triangular, appressed and imbricate, the basal ones connate into concentric rings. Nut broadly conical or subglobose, rarely compressed globose, 8–15 mm high, 12–20 mm in diam., glabrous, often ± white-farinose; scar concave, ca. 11 mm in diam.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Ta Tit Yan, Lantau Island. W. J. Tutcher s.n. (HK sheet 6813); HK sheet 6814; C. P. Lau 118.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Hubei, Zhejiang, Fujian; Vietnam, Myanmar, Laos.
Ecology: Woods. Flowering: May–Sep.; fruiting: Jun.– Oct. of the following year.
Uses: Material (wood), environmental.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Tam, Aberdeen, Cameron Road, Ma On Shan
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Lithocarpus macilentus Chun & C. C. Huang 粉葉柯
Guihaia 8: 30. 1988; FRPS 22: 184, pl. 57. 1998; FOC 4: 363. 1999.
Quercus irwinii auct. non Hance: FKH 253. 1912.

Tree, 7–12 m tall. Young shoots and petioles tawny tomentose. Leaves thinly leathery; petioles less than 1 cm; leaf blade lanceolate, rarely oblanceolate, 6 –11 × 2–3 cm, narrowed to both ends, base decurrent, margin entire, covered with fugacious, minute and crisped hairs on both surfaces when young, abaxially scurfy; lateral veins 6–9 on each side of midvein; veins inconspicuous. Male spikes forming panicle. Female spikes 7–10 cm, lengthening to 20 cm in fruiting time. Rachis tawny tomentose; female flowers in cluster of 3. Cupule bowl-shaped, 6– 8 mm high, 15–20 mm in diam., covering basal part of nut, wall thin, ± thickened at base. Nut broadly conical or compressed globose, glabrous, dark chestnut brown, 13 –15 mm high, 15–17 mm in diam., scar concave, 7– 8 mm in diam.

Locality: Tai Tam, Aberdeen, Cameron Road, Ma On Shan. Y. S. Lau 1721; HK sheet 6782; X. Y. Zhuang 1920; K. Wong 1188.
Distribution: W Guangdong, E Guangxi.
Ecology: Woods on banks of streams. Flowering: Jul.–Aug.; fruiting: Oct.–Nov. of the following year.
Uses: Material (wood), environmental.
Notes: The species was reported as Lithocarpus irwinii (Hance) Rehd. previously (Check List HK Plants 38. 1993).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Authority: C. C. Huang & Y. T. Chang
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Lithocarpus quercifolius C. C. Huang & Y. T. Chang 櫟葉柯
Guihaia 8(1): 16. 1988; FRPS 22: 142, pl. 43: 1–3. 1998; FOC 4: 352. 1999.

Tree, 5 – 6 m tall. Branchlets of the current year growth pubescent. Leaves usually crowded towards apex of branches, firmly papery, concolour; petioles 2– 5 mm; leaf blade oblong or obovate-elliptic, 4 –11 × 1– 4 cm, apex acute, base rounded or broadly cuneate, margin with a few acute teeth towards apex, usually with tuft of hairs on axils of veins on abaxial surface; lateral veins 8–11 on each side of midvein, branched near the edge; veinlets conspicuous or slender, ending in teeth. Male spike 3.5 –7 cm, with solitary and scattered female flowers on the proximal part of the rachis; rachis tawny pubescent. Cupule discoid, 2–5 mm high, 20–25 mm in diam., enclosing the basal part of nut; bracts lanceolate when young, rhomboid or broadly triangular when mature, imbricate, midvein ridged. Nut compressed globose, 12–16 mm high, 20 –14 mm in diam., with appressed minute hairs; scar with the margin concave, center convex, 16 –20 mm in diam.

Locality: Shek O, Mount Parker. W. J. Tutcher 6798; HK sheet 6733, 34314.
Distribution: Guangdong, S Jiangxi.
Ecology: Woods. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.; fruiting: Sep.– Oct.

Quercus acutissima Carr. 麻櫟
J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 6: 33. 1862; FFJ 1: 413, fig. 370. 1982; FRPS 22: 219, pl. 68: 1. 1998; FTW ed. 2, 2: 114. 1996; FOC 4: 372. 1999.

Deciduous tree, to 15 m tall. Bark dark greyish brown, deeply fissured. Branchlets yellowish brown, glabrescent. Leaves thinly leathery; petioles 1.5 –3.5 cm, glabrescent; leaf blade variable in shape, usually oblong-lanceolate, 9–13(–18) × 2– 4(– 6) cm, base subrounded or broadly cuneate, apex acuminate, margin serrate with bristle-like teeth, adaxially glabrous and shining, abaxially pubescent when young, soon glabrate, only with tuft of hairs on axil of veins; lateral veins 13–17 on each side of midvein. Male catkins, 3 – 4 cm; stamens usually 3 –7, rarely 2–10; filaments 2.5 –3 mm. Female flowers 2–3, clustered or in short catkins. Cupule cup-shaped, ca. 1.5 cm high, 2–4 cm in diam., enclosing 1/3 –1/2 of nut; bracts subulate to linear, reflexed, greyish-whitetomentose. Nut ovoid or ellipsoid, 1.6 –2.2 cm high, 1.5–2 cm in diam., top rounded; scar convex.

Locality: New Territories. HK sheet 26470, 40661.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Yunnan, Xizang, Hunan, Hubei, Henan, Shanxi, Shaanxi, Liaoning, Jiangxi, Anhui, Shandong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian; Korea, Japan, Vietnam, Myanmar, Thailand, N India, Nepal.
Ecology: Woods on sunny slopes.
Uses: Material (timber).

Quercus fabri Hance 白櫟
J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 10: 202. 1869; FFJ 1: 414, fig. 372. 1982; FRPS 22: 227, pl. 71: 1–2. 1998; FOC 4: 373. 1999; FKH 253. 1912.
Quercus serrata auct. non Thunb.: FKH 253. 1912.

Deciduous tree to 20 m tall, but often shrubby. Bark dark greyish brown, deeply fissured. Branchlets densely grey to greyish brown tomentose. Leaves thickly papery or thinly leathery; petioles 3 – 6 mm, yellowish-brown-tomentose; leaf blade obovate, to obovate-elliptic, 6 –16 × 2.5– 8 cm, base broadly cuneate or narrowly rounded, apex obtuse, margin undulate-serrate or coarsely and obtusely serrate, covered with greyish yellow stellate hairs on both surfaces when young, only on abaxial surface when mature; lateral veins 8 –12 on each side of midvein, tertiary veins conspicuous abaxially. Male catkins 3 – 4 cm, pendulous, rachis tomentose. Female catkins 1–4 cm, with 2– 4 flowers. Cupule cup‑shaped, 7– 8 mm high, 0.8 –1 cm in diam., enclosing 1/3 of nut; bracts ovate-lanceolate, imbricate. Nut ellipsoid to ovoid-ellipsoid, 1.5 –1.8 cm high, 0.8 –1 cm in diam., glabrous; scar convex.

Locality: Fanling. W. J. Tutcher s.n. (HK sheet 10934, 11656).
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Yunnan, Hunan, Hubei, Henan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian.
Ecology: Thickets and secondary forests. Flowering: Apr.; fruiting: Oct.
Uses: Fuelwood.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Authority: N. H. Xia, K. S. Pang & Y. H. Tong

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Casuarina cunninghamiana Miq. 細枝木麻黃（肯氏木麻黃）
Rev. Crit. Casuar. 56. 1848; FRPS 20(1): 3, pl. 1: 1–10. 1982; FOC 4: 107. 1999; FGD 5: 380. 2003.

Tree dioecious, to 25(–35) m tall, often with suckers from roots. Bark finely fissured and scaly, grey, inner layer pale red. Ultimate branchlets spreading to slightly pendulous, dark green, greyish green, or glaucous-green when dry, 15 –38 cm × 0.5 –0.7 mm; internodes 4 – 5 mm. Leaves erect, 8(–10) per whorl, narrowly lanceolate. Male spikes 1.2–2(– 4) cm. Cones ellipsoid or subglobose, 7–12 mm, truncate at both ends; apex of bracteoles acute. Samaras 3– 5 mm including wing.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 3324.
Distribution: Cultivated in Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian; native to Australia.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr.; fruiting: Jun.–Sep.
Uses: Ornamental, agroforestry.

Casuarina equisetifolia L. 木麻黃
Amoen. Acad. 4: 143. 1759; FRPS 20(1): 2. 1982; FOC 4: 106. 1999; FGD 5: 379. 2003.

Tree monoecious, to 35 m tall, without suckers from roots. Bark scaly, inner layer red-brown on old trees. Ultimate branchlets usually pendulous, greyish green, 10 –27 cm × 0.8 – 0.9 mm; internodes (2.5 –)4 –9 mm. Leaves erect and appressed to branchlets, 6 – 8 per whorl, lanceolate or triangular, 1–3 mm. Male inflorescences 1– 4 cm. Cones ellipsoid, 1.2–2.5 cm, greyish green or yellowish brown tomentose when young, glabrous at maturity, base and apex truncate to obtuse; apex of bracteoles slightly obtuse or acute. Samaras 5 – 8 mm including wing.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 35816, 34685.
Distribution: Cultivated in Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian. Native to Australia, Pacific Islands.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: Jul.– Oct.
Uses: Planted as wind breaks and for soil stabilizations.

Phytolacca acinosa Roxb. 商陸
Fl. Ind. 2: 458. 1832; Hook. f., Fl. Brit. Ind. 5: 21. 1886; FGD 2: 94, fig. 65. 1991; FOC 5: 435. 2003.

Perennial herb, glabrous throughout, with thick, conical tap root. Stems branched, green or reddish, 1–1.5 m tall. Petioles 1.5 –3 cm; leaf blade ovate-elliptic or oblong, 12–25 × 4 –10 cm, base cuneate, decurrent, apex acute or acuminate, margin entire. Racemes terminal and lateral, often opposite to leaves, 3 –15 cm, more or less erect; bracts linear-lanceolate. Pedicels slender, ca. 6 mm. Perianth-segments usually 5, cream or greenish, becoming pink or reddish in fruit, 2–3 mm. Stamens 8 –10; anthers pink; carpels 8–10, distinct; styles separate. Fruit compressed-spherical, purplish to black, with 8 –10 fused fruitlets.

Locality: Cultivated. P. S. Choi 515; HK sheet 23274, 33267.
Distribution: Dispersed over most parts of China except Liaoning, Jilin, Heilongjiang, Nei Mongol and Xinjiang; Korea, Japan, India.
Ecology: Cultivated, sometimes escaped from cultivation, in waste places near villages. Flowering: May–Aug.; fruiting: Jun.– Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Phytolacca americana L. 美洲商陸
Sp. Pl. 1: 441. 1753; FGD 2: 95. 1991; FRPS 26: 19, pl. 3: 6–7. 1996.
Phytolacca decandra L., Sp. Pl. (ed. 2) 631. 1763.

Perennial herbs, with thick, conical root. Stems erect, sometimes reddish purple, terete, 1–15 m tall. Petiole 1– 4 cm; leaf blade elliptic-ovate or ovate-lanceolate, 10 –30 × 5 –16 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate and mucronate, margin entire. Racemes terminal or lateral, 10 –15 cm. Pedicel 6 – 8 mm. Flowers ca. 6 mm in diam. Perianth-segments 5, white, slightly red. Stamens, carpels, and styles 10; carpels connate. Infructescence pendulous. Fruit purple-black when mature, oblate.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. W. Lam 731; HK sheet 32242.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Hebei, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Anhui, Fujian, Jiangsu, Jiangxi, Shandong, Zhejiang, Taiwan; native to N America; widely naturalized in Asia and Europe.
Ecology: Flowering: Jun.–Aug.; fruiting: Aug.– Oct.
Uses: Medicinal, ornamental.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hung Hom, Lantau Island, Ping Chau
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Boerhavia diffusa L. 黃細心
Sp. Pl. 3. 1753; FGZ 172. 1956; FGD 2: 108, fig. 75. 1991; FTW ed. 2, 2: 320, pl. 149, photo 135. 1996; FRPS 26: 11, pl. 2: 5 –7. 1996; FOC 5: 434. 2003.
Boerhavia repens L., Sp. Pl. 3. 1753; FKH 213. 1912.

Perennial herb, 1–2 m tall. Stems diffuse, glabrous or sparsely pubescent. Leaves opposite; petioles 1–3.5 cm; leaf blade ovate to ovate-oblong, 0.5 – 5 × 0.5 –3 cm, base obtuse, cuneate or cordate, apex obtuse, acuminate or acute, margin slightly undulate, sparsely pubescent on both surfaces, often glaucous and glandular on abaxial surface. Thyrses axillary, 0.5 –7 cm; pedicels 0.3 –2 mm; bracteoles 1–3, lanceolate. Calyx ca. 4 mm, constricted at middle, upper part campanulate, 1–2 mm, white, red or purple, 5-lobed, lower part tubular, 1–1.2 mm, 5-ribed. Stamens 1–3(–5), slightly exserted. Ovary obovate or obovate-oblong. Fruit clavate, 2.5–3.3 mm, 5-ribbed, covered with glands and hairs.

Locality: Hung Hom, Lantau Island, Ping Chau. Y. S. Lau 2478, 3125; HK Sheet 22959.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Indochina, Indian Subcontinent, Malesia, Australia.
Ecology: Open fields. Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: Autumn.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Boerhavia erecta L. 直立黃細心
Sp. Pl. 3. 1753; FGD 2: 108. 1991; FRPS 26: 12, pl. 2: 8. 1996; FOC 5: 433. 2003.

Perennial herb, 20– 80 cm tall. Stems erect or decumbent at base, initially puberulous, glabrescent. Leaves opposite; petioles 1.5 – 4 cm; leaf blade ovate or lanceolate, 1.5 – 5 × 1– 4 cm, base rounded or truncate, apex acute, rarely obtuse, margin entire, adaxially scabrous, abaxially white, puberulous or glandular. Thyrses axillary, 2–3 cm; pedicels 0.5 – 5 mm; bracteoles 1–2, lanceolate, 0.8 –1 mm. Calyx 1.7–2.5 cm, constricted at middle, upper part campanulate, 1.5–2 mm, white, red or purple, 5-lobed, lower part tubular, 1–1.2 mm, 5-ribbed. Stamens 2–3, slightly exserted. Fruit obconical, 3 –3.5 mm, 5-ribbed, glabrous.

Locality: Tai Po. Y. S. Lau 1269.
Distribution: Guangdong, Xisha Islands; Malesia, Pacific Islands.
Ecology: Open fields. Flowering & fruiting: Summer to autumn.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Cultivated in gardens or as a pot plant
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Bougainvillea spectabilis Willd. 葉子花（毛寶巾、簕杜鵑）
Sp. Pl. 2: 348. 1799; FGZ 170. 1956; FGD 2: 107. 1991; FRPS 26: 6. 1996; FOC 5: 432. 2003.

Scandent shrub. Stems to 10 m or longer, puberulous; branches often with spines. Leaves papery; petioles 1–2 cm; leaf blade ovate to ovate-lanceolate or elliptic, 4 –9 × 2– 4.5 cm, base broadly cuneate to subrounded or subtruncate, often slightly oblique, apex shortly acuminate, puberulent on both surfaces or glabrescent abaxially. Flowers in cluster of 3, subtended by 3 large bracts and forming large, terminal panicles. Pedicels adnate to the midvein of bracts. Bracts leafy, broadly ovate to subrounded, 3 –3.8 × 2.5 –2.8 cm, red, purple or orange. Calyx-tube ca. 1.4 mm, 5-ribed, puberulent abaxially; limb ca. 7 mm in diam., 5-lobed, white or pink. Stamens usually 8, unequal, included; filaments united at the base. Ovary elongate; stigma feathery, on one side of the style.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens or as a pot plant. Y. S. Lau 1087, 1091, 3064.
Distribution: Cultivated in S China; native to Brazil.
Ecology: The plant thrives in sunny places, flowering almost all the year round, but never set fruit in Hong Kong and S China.
Notes: Bougainvillea glabra Choisy is also cultivated in Hong Kong. It is very similar to this species, but can be distinguished by its glabrescent calyx-tube, young shoots and leaves.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Cultivated or sometimes escaped from cultivation
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Mirabilis jalapa L. 紫茉莉
Sp. Pl. 177. 1753; FGZ 171, fig. 75. 1956; Fl. Europ. 1: 111. 1964; FHN 1: 440, fig. 242. 1964; FGD 2: 107, fig. 74. 1991; FRPS 26: 7. 1996; FOC 5: 432. 2003.

Perennial herb, 30 –100 cm tall, glabrous or slightly pubescent, with thick, conical roots. Stems erect, much branched, often reddish, with tumid nodes. Leaves opposite; petioles to 6.5 cm; leaf blade ovate to ovate-triangular, 5 –11(–15) × 3.5 – 6 cm, base truncate or cordate, apex acuminate. Flowers in terminal dichotomous cymes, opening in the afternoon, each flower subtended by a involucre. Involucre calyx-like, green, 9 –10 mm, united to middle; lobes 5, narrowly triangular, 1-nerved, ± ciliate. Calyx corolla-like, red, yellow, white or striped; tube 4.5 – 5 cm, constricted above the ovary; limb 5-lobed, ca. 2.5 cm in diam. Stamens 5; anthers compressed globose, slightly exserted. Ovary ovoid; style filiform, as long as or longer than filaments; stigma capitate. Fruit ovoid, ca. 5 mm in diam., black, with tubercles.

Locality: Cultivated or sometimes escaped from cultivation. Y. S. Lau 1579, 2157.
Distribution: Native to tropical America; widely cultivated and naturalized elsewhere in tropical regions.
Ecology: Flowering: May.– Oct. Flowers opening late afternoon till next morning.
Uses: Ornamental.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Tam, Castle Peak, Lung Kwu Tan, Sai Kung, Pui O, Tung Chung
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Sesuvium portulacastrum (L.) L. 海馬齒
Syst. Nat. ed. 10, 1058. 1759; FKH 114. 1912; FHN 1: 383, fig. 201. 1964; FGD 2: 87, fig. 60. 1991; FTW ed. 2, 2: 329, pl. 152, photo 140 –141. 1996; FRPS 26: 30, pl. 5: 4– 6. 1996; FOC 5: 441. 2003.
Portulaca portulacastrum L., Sp. Pl. 446. 1753.

Perennial succulent herb. Stems prostrate, 20–80 cm or longer, glabrous, green or red, often with white tubercles, rooting at nodes. Leaves fleshy; petioles 7–15 mm, base dilated, with membranous, amplexicaul margins; leaf blade linear oblanceolate or linear spathulate, 1.5–5 × 0.2–1 cm, apex obtuse, tapering from middle to the base. Flowers solitary in axil of leaves. Pedicels 5–15 mm. Calyx 6–8 mm; tube ca. 2 mm; lobes 5, ovate-lanceolate, green abaxially, red adaxially. Petals absent. Stamens 15–40, inserted at apex of calyx-tube, shorter than the calyx-lobes; filaments free or united below middle. Ovary ovoid, glabrous, 3- or sometimes 4-locular; style 3, rarely 4–5. Capsule ovoid, opening transversely below middle.

Locality: Tai Tam, Castle Peak, Lung Kwu Tan, Sai Kung, Pui O, Tung Chung. H. C. Tang 1293; S. Y. Hu & P. P. H. But 24044; Y. S. Lau 3253.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian, Taiwan, Xisha Islands; tropical and subtropical coastal areas.
Ecology: Sandy beaches. Flowering: Apr.–Jul.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Stanley, Lan Nai Wan, Lung Kwu Tan, Tai O
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Tetragonia tetragonioides (Pall.) Kuntze 番杏
Rev. Gen. 264. 1891; FGD 2: 89, fig. 62. 1991; FTW ed. 2, 2: 331, pl. 153, photo 142–143. 1996; FRPS 26: 35, pl. 7: 5 –7. 1996; FOC 5: 440. 2003.
Demidovia tetragonioides Pall., Enum. Pl. 150, t. 1. 1781.
Tetragonia expansa Murr., Comm. Goett. 6: 13. 1783; FKH 114. 1912.

Annual succulent herb, glabrous, often with small tubercles. Stems thick, terete or slightly angled, initially erect, later elongate and ascending, 30– 60 cm or longer. Leaves alternate; petioles 0.5 –2.5 cm; leaf blade ovate-rhombic or ovate-triangular, 4 –11 × 1– 5 cm, base broadly cuneate to subtruncate, decurrent, apex obtuse or acute, margin entire or undulate. Flowers solitary or in cluster or 2–3, axillary. Pedicels ca. 2 mm. Calyx-tube 1.5 –2 mm; lobes 3 – 5, yellowish green adaxially, 2–3 mm. Stamens 4 –10; filaments yellow, 1–1.5 mm. Nutlet turbinate, 0.5 –1 cm, 4 – 5-angled.

Locality: Stanley, Lan Nai Wan, Lung Kwu Tan, Tai O. Y. W. Lam 814, 1523; HK sheet 2054.
Distribution: Guangdong, Fujian, Taiwan, Zhejiang, Jiangsu; E Asia, Malesia, Australia, New Zealand, S America; cultivated and naturalized elsewhere.
Ecology: Sandy seashores. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.– Oct.
Uses: Food (vegetable), medicinal (folklore).

Epiphyllum oxypetalum (DC.) Haw. 曇花
Phil. Mag. 6: 109. 1829; FHN 1: 494. 1964; FGX 1: 738. 1991; FRPS 52(1): 284. 1999; FGD 4: 138. 2000.

Shrubby succulent plant, 2.5–3 m tall. Branch-joints flat, green, 15–40 × 5–6 cm, thickened in the middle, margin undulate, with areoles, unarmed. Flowers solitary, arising from areoles, white, nocturnal. Perianth-tube 15–20 cm; limb 10–12 cm in diam.; segments many, outer ones scale-like, 2.5–3 mm, inner ones lanceolate, 5–6 cm; stamens many; anthers light yellow. Ovary ovoid, slightly angled; style 16–18-cleft.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 2053.
Distribution: Mexico, Mesoamerica; cultivated elsewhere.
Ecology: In Hong Kong usually cultivated as a pot plant. Flowering: Summer.
Uses: Ornamental.

Hylocereus undatus (Haw.) Britt. & Rose 量天尺
Fl. Bermuda 256. 1918; FHN 1: 493. 1964; FGX 1: 739. 1991; FRPS 52(1): 283. 1999; FGD 4: 136, fig. 84. 2000.
Cereus undatus Haw., Phil. Mag. 7: 110. 1830.

Succulent cactus, climbing by aerial roots. Stems 6 –7 m or longer, 3-angled, depth of ribs 1–2.5 cm, margin undulate; areoles borne on the ribs, 3 – 4 cm apart, with 1–3 small spines. Flowers solitary, 25 –30(–35) cm long; limb 10 –12 cm in diam.; segments many, outer ones yellowish green or purplish, inner ones white. Stamens many, cream-white, equaling the perianth-segments. Fruit a fleshy berry, oblong, ca. 10 cm, with large scales outside.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 12287.
Distribution: Originated from neotropics; widely cultivated in tropical regions.
Ecology: Climbing by aerial roots on walls and tree trunks. Flowering: Summer.
Uses: Ornamental, food (beverage base, vegetable).

Opuntia stricta (Haw.) Haw. var. dillenii (Ker-Gaw.) L. D. Benson 仙人掌
Cact. et Succ. J. (Los Angeles) 41: 126. 1968; FRPS 52(1): 277. 1999.
Cactus dillenii Ker-Gaw., in Edwards, Bot. Reg. 3: pl. 255. 1818.
Opuntia dillenii (Ker-Gaw.) Haw., Suppl. Pl. Succ. 79. 1819; FKH 114. 1912; FGX 1: 735. 1991; FGD 4: 138. 2000.

Shrubby or tree-like cactus, 1– 4 m tall. Trunk almost cylindric, woody at base. Stem-joints flat, green, obovate to oblong, 1–30 × 7–10 cm; areoles raised, with woolly hairs; spines solitary, white, tip dark brown. Leaves small, subulate, caducous. Flowers solitary, yellow, 5– 8 cm in diam. Fruit a berry, obovate, 6 – 8 cm, spineless.

Locality: Cultivated or naturalized. HK sheet 12291, 2049.
Distribution: Hainan, S Guangdong, S Guangxi; Mexico, S-C USA, S America; naturalized elsewhere.
Ecology: Dry grassy places. Flowering: Summer.
Uses: Ornamental.

Schlumbergera truncata (Haw.) Moran 蟹爪
Gentes Herbarium 8: 329. 1953; FGX 1: 738. 1991; FGD 4: 139, fig. 87. 2000.
Zygocactus truncates (Haw.) K. Schum. in Martius, Fl. Bras. 4: 224. 1890.
Epiphyllum truncatum Haw., Suppl. Pl. Succ. 85. 1819.

Small shrubby cactus. Stems dichotomously branched and short-jointed; joints flat, ovate to oblong, 3–6 × 1.5–2.5 cm, apex truncate, margin with 2–4 incurved teeth on each side, green on both surfaces. Flowers solitary, in various shades of red, borne on the apex of the joints; perianth-tube ca. 2.5 cm; limb 4–5 cm in diam.; segments 21–23, in 4–5 irregular tiers on the tube, basal ones ovate to ovate-lanceolate, 0.7–1.5 × 0.5–0.8 cm, distal ones oblong-lanceolate, 2.5–3.5 × 1–1.2 cm. Stamens many. Ovary turbinate, 4-angled, glabrous; stigma 6–7-lobed.

Locality: Cultivated. C. Chan 73 (CUHK); M. Y. Wong 36 (CUHK).
Distribution: Native to Brazil; widely cultivated elsewhere.
Ecology: In Hong Kong the species is usually cultivated as a pot plant, or grafted on a stock of Hylocereus undatus. Flowering: Dec.–Feb. of the following year.
Uses: Ornamental.

Atriplex maximowicziana Makino 海濱藜
Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 10: 2. 1896; FOC 5: 365. 2003.

Perennial herb, monoecious. Stem 30 –100 cm tall, densely farinose, many branched; branches ascending. Leaves alternate or lower ones subopposite, rhomboid-ovate or ovate-oblong, 2–3 × 1–2 cm, base cuneate, apex acute or obtuse and mucronate, margin slightly 3-lobed, densely farinose on both surfaces. Male flowers in ca. 1 cm long, terminal, densely packed spikes; perianth-lobes 5, obovate; stamens 5. Female flowers smaller, clustered into panicles. Utricles compressed-globose or biconvex, persistent bracteoles rhomboid-ovate, 6–9 mm, margin triangular-toothed, connate only at base. Seeds reddish brown, 2 mm in diam.

Locality: Tai O, Sha Chau. HK sheet 36803; S. P. Lau 128.
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong; Japan (Ryukyu).
Ecology: Sandy beach. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Dec.
Notes: The species was reported as A. nummularia Lindl. previously (Check List HK Plants 64. 1993).

Bassia scoparia (L.) A. J. Scott 地膚
Fedd. Repert. 89: 108. 1978.
Kochia scoparia (L.) Schrad. in Neues Journ. 3: 85. 1809; FGD 3: 63. 1995; FOC 5: 385. 2003.
Chenopodium scoparium L., Sp. Pl. 221. 1753.

Annual herb, 0.5–1 m tall. Stems terete, slightly pubescent or glabrous on lower parts. Leaves sessile, lanceolate or linear lanceolate, 0.7– 5 × 1–7 mm, base attenuate, apex shortly acuminate, margin entire, glabrous or slightly hairy, 3-veined. Spikes 1–3-flowered, axillary. Flowers bisexual or pistillate; perianth subglobose, green-yellowish; lobes 5, subtriangular, winged on outside. Stamens 5, exserted, inserted at base of perianth. Anthers yellowish, ovoid. Ovary oblate; style very short; stigmas 2–3, filiform. Utricles oblate, subtended by persistent perianth, pericarps membranaceous. Seeds black-brown, ovoid, 1.5 –2 mm.

Locality: Cultivated. Lam Tsuen (Kadoorie Farm).
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; Europe, Asia.
Ecology: Farmland, roadsides. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.– Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.

Beta vulgaris L. var. cicla L. 莙薘菜
Sp. Pl. 222. 1753; FHN 1: 398. 1964; FGD 3: 67. 1995; FOC 5: 354. 2003.

Annual or biennial succulent herbs, 0.3–1 m tall; roots fleshy, branched, not tuberous. Petioles rough, long; basal leaves ovate or oblong-ovate, 20–30 × 10–15 cm, base cuneate or cordate, decurrent, margin sinuate, apex obtuse, midvein elevated abaxially; cauline leaves smaller, rhombic-ovate to lanceolate. Flowers sessile, small, green, solitary or 2–3 clustered in paniculate spikes. Bracts linear. Perianth-lobes oblong, thickened at base when fruiting. Utricles with lower part enclosed in hardened perianth, upper part slightly fleshy. Seeds reddish brown, 2–3 mm in diam., shiny.

Locality: Cultivated.
Distribution: Widely cultivated in China; Europe, Asia & N Africa.
Ecology: Farmland, roadside. Flowering & fruiting: May–Jul.
Uses: Vegetable.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Shek O, Sai Kung, Tsing Lung Tau, Sheung Pak Nai, Ha Pak Nai, Pui O, Tung Chung
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Chenopodium acuminatum Willd. subsp. virgatum (Thunb.) Kitam. 狹葉尖頭葉藜
Acta Phytotax. Geobot. 20: 206. 1962; FGD 3: 65. 1995; FOC 5: 380. 2003.
Chenopodium virgatum Thunb., Nov. Act. Reg. Soc. Upsal. 143. 1815.
Chenopodium vachelii Hook. & Arn., Bot. Beechey Voy. 269. 1838.
Chenopodium acuminatum auct. non Willd.: FHK 28. 1861; FKH 215. 1912; FHN 1: 397. 1964.

Annual herb, up to 80 cm tall. Stems erect, angulate, much branched; branches ascending, farinose. Petioles 1.5 –2.5 cm; leaves narrowly ovate, oblong or lanceolate, 1– 4 × 0.5 –2.5 cm, base cuneate, rounded or truncate, apex acute or acuminate, mucronate, margin entire, translucent, greenish and glabrous adaxially, grey-white and farinose abaxially. Inflorescence a terminal leafy panicle. Flowers bisexual; perianth-lobes 5, broadly ovate, margin membranaceous, ridged near central. Stamens 5. Utricles compressed-globose, smooth. Seeds black, 1 mm in diam., shiny.

Locality: Shek O, Sai Kung, Tsing Lung Tau, Sheung Pak Nai, Ha Pak Nai, Pui O, Tung Chung. HK sheet 36802, 36805.
Distribution: Guangxi, Guangdong, Fujian, Taiwan, Zhejiang, Jiangsu, Hebei, Liaoning; Japan.
Ecology: Wastelands near seashore and on lakes. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Sep.

Chenopodium album L. 藜
Sp. Pl. 219. 1753; FHK 282. 1861; FKH 215. 1912; FRPS 25(2): 98. 1979; FGD 3: 67. 1995; FOC 5: 383. 2003.

Annual herb, 30 –150 cm tall. Stems rough, erect, angulate, with green or purple striae. Leaves petiolate, rhomboid-ovate to broad-lanceolate, 3– 6 × 2.5– 5 cm, base cuneate, apex acute or obtuse, lower ones more or less sinuately toothed or angular, upper ones usually narrow and entire. Clusters of flowers in short axillary spikes, either dense or interrupted, upper ones forming a long panicle, leafy at base. Flowers bisexual; perianth-lobes 5, broad-ovate to elliptic, keeled abaxially, mealy-white, apex emarginated. Stamens 5, exserted; stigmas 2. Utricles compressedglobose, smooth; entirely enclosed in perianth. Seeds horizontal, black, 1.2–1.5 mm in diam.

Locality: Sha Tin, Tai Lung. Y. S. Lau 960, 2156.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; temperate and tropical regions.
Ecology: Farmland and roadsides. Flowering: Jul.–Aug.; fruiting: Aug.–Sep.
Uses: Medicinal, noxious weed.

Chenopodium ficifolium Sm. 小藜
Fl. Brit. 1: 276. 1800; FKH 215. 1912; FOC 5: 383. 2003.
Chenopodium serotinum auct. non L.: FHN 1: 396. 1964; FGD 3: 66. 1995.

Annual herb, 20 – 50 cm tall. Stems erect, much branched; branches ascending, farinose when young. Leaves petiolate, ovateoblong, 2.5 – 5 × 1–3.5 cm, often shallowly 3-lobed, central lobe oblong, margin sinuate-toothed, farinose abaxially. Inflorescence a terminal leafy panicle, 4–12 cm; perianth subglobose, deeply 5- lobed; lobes broadly ovate, keeled and farinose abaxially. Stamens 5, exserted; stigmas 2, filiform. Utricles compressed-globose, smooth. Seeds horizontal, black, 1 mm in diam., shiny.

Locality: Ha Hang. K. Wong s.n. (HK sheet 23122, 23158).
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; temperate and tropical regions of the world.
Ecology: Farmlands, wastelands and roadsides. Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: Jun.–Aug.
Notes: The name Chenopodium serotinum L. has often been misapplied to this species but in fact refers to a species of Atriplex (FOC 5: 383. 2003).

Chenopodium ambrosioides L. 土荊芥
Sp. Pl. 219. 1753; FKH 215. 1912; FRPS 25(2): 82. 1979; FHN 1: 396. 1964; FGD 3: 65. 1995.
Dysphania ambrosioides (L.) Mosyakin & Clemants, Ukrayins’k. Bot. Zurn. 59: 382. 2002; FOC 5: 377. 2003.

Annual or perennial herb, 50–80 cm tall, with strong smell. Stems erect much branched, with whitish or yellowish glandular hairs (not farinose) or subglabrous. Leaves oblong or lanceolate, 2–10 × 0.5 –2 cm, base attenuate, apex acute or obtuse, margin sinuate, dentate to parted, glabrous adaxially, sparsely oil-spotted abaxially. Inflorescence a terminal leafy panicle or spike, 2–10 cm. Flowers bisexual and pistillate. Perianth-lobes 5, rarely 3. Stamens 5; stigmas 3, rarely 4, filiform, exserted. Utricles compressed-globose. Seeds horizontal or oblique, black or dark red, 0.7 mm in diam., smooth and shining.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Naturalized. HK sheet 36804; Y. S. Lau 3206.
Distribution: Guangxi, Guangdong, Fujian, Taiwan, Zhejiang, Jiangsu, Jiangxi, Hunan, Sichuan; native to tropical America, widely distributed in tropical and temperate regions of the world.
Ecology: Near villages, roadsides and riversides. Flowering & fruiting: May–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal.
Note: This species was transferred to Dysphania R. Br. by Mosyakin & Clements (2002) and accepted in Flora of China. But there are no distinct characters to separate Dysphania from Chenopodium, except the glandular hairs of Dysphania.

Spinacia oleracea L. 菠菜
Sp. Pl. 1027. 1753; FHN 1: 399. 1964; FGD 3: 68. 1995; FOC 5: 366. 2003.

Annual herb, up to 1 m tall; roots conical, often reddish. Stems erect, simple or branched. Leaves light green, tender and juicy, hastate or triangular-ovate, generally 5 –15 × 5 –10 cm, entire or dentately lobed. Male flowers arranged in interrupted spicate panicles; perianth-lobes 4. Female flowers in axillary clusters; bracteoles spinose abaxially; ovary globose; stigmas 4 or 5. Utricles brown, ovoid or subglobose 2.5 mm in diam.

Locality: Cultivated. S. Y. Hu 6741, 6988 (CUHK).
Distribution: Cultivated in China; native to Iran.
Ecology: Farmland. Flowering & fruiting: May–Aug.
Uses: Vegetable.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Sha Tin, Lau Fau Shan, Plover Cove, Yung Shue O, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Suaeda australis (R. Br.) Moq. 南方鹼蓬
Ann. Sci. Nat. 23: 318. 1831; FHN 1: 394. 1964; FHK 283. 1861; FKH 215. 1912; FOC 5: 394. 2003.
Suaeda maritima (L.) Dumort, Fl. Belg. 22. 1827; FGD 3: 62. 1995; FTW 2: 387. 1996.
Chenopodium maritimum L., Sp. Pl. 221. 1753.
Chenopodium australe R. Br., Prodr. Fl. Nov. Holl. 407. 1810.
Suaeda monoica auct. non Forssk.: FKH 215. 1912.

Perennial herb or subshrub, 7–10 cm tall. Stems much branched. Leaves fleshy, white or purple, semi-terete, linear, 10 –35 × 1–3 mm, base attenuate, apex slightly acute or obtuse, margin entire. Flowers small, polygamous, solitary or 2– 5-clustered in glomerules. Bracteoles 2–3, oblong, 0.8 –1 mm, persistent; perianth purple-green, 5-lobed; lobes ovate-oblong, enclosing fruit when fruiting. Utricle compressed globose, 1.2–1.5 mm in diam. Seeds black, lustrous.

Locality: Sha Tin, Lau Fau Shan, Plover Cove, Yung Shue O, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 437; HK sheet 36813.
Distribution: Guangxi, Guangdong, Fujian, Taiwan, Jiangsu; cosmopolitan.
Ecology: Sandy beaches and margins of mangroves. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Nov.

Achyranthes aspera L. 土牛膝
Sp. Pl. 204. 1753; FHK 285. 1861; FKH 214. 1912; FHN 1: 407. 1964; FRPS 25(2): 227. 1979; FGD 4: 108. 2000; FOC 5: 424. 2003.

Perennial herb, 50–120 cm tall, greyish pubescent throughout. Stems quadrangular, woody at the base. Leaves papery; petioles 5 –15 mm; leaf blade ovate, obovate or oblong-elliptic, 4 –10 × 1.5 – 6 cm, base cuneate, apex obtuse or acute, margin entire. Spikes terminal or axillary, 10 –30 cm. Flowers green, reflexed after anthesis. Bracteoles subulate and spiny, 2.5 –3.5 mm, base ovate, membranous, not lobed. Perianth-segments 5, lanceolate, 4.5 – 5 mm, with a hard and sharp point. Stamens 5; filaments united at the base; staminodes apex fimbriate. Utricle ellipsoid, enclosed in the persistent perianth.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. L. Gibbs 10192; Y. S. Lau 1505; HK sheet 36017.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; SW to SE Asia; naturalized elsewhere.
Ecology: Wastelands and grassy places near villages. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Achyranthes bidentata Blume 牛膝
Bijdr. 545. 1825; FKH 214. 1912; FHN 1: 408, fig. 218. 1964; FRPS 25(2): 228. 1979; FTW ed. 2, 2: 391. 1996; FGD 4: 108, fig, 68. 2000; FOC 5: 425. 2003.

Perennial herb, 25–120 cm tall. Stems angled or quadrangular; branches initially pubescent, glabrous in age. Leaves papery; petioles 5–30 mm, pubescent; leaf blade ovate, elliptic or ellipticlanceolate, rarely oblanceolate, 4.5–13 × 2.5–5 cm, base cuneate to broadly cuneate, apex shortly acuminate, margin entire, pubescent on both surfaces. Spikes terminal or axillary, 3 – 5 cm; rachis densely pubescent. Flowers green, spreading or reflexed after anthesis. Bracteoles subulate and spiny, 2.5 –3 mm, with 2 minute basal auricles. Perianth-segments 5, lanceolate, 3 –5 mm, with a hard and sharp point. Stamens 5; filaments united at the base; staminodes apex truncate. Utricle ellipsoid, enclosed in the persistent perianth.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai. HK sheet 31567.
Distribution: Most provinces of China; E Asia, Indochina, Indian Subcontinent, Malesia, W tropical Africa, S W Pacific.
Ecology: Wastelands, bushes and woodlands near villages. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Dec.
Uses: Traditional Chinese medicine.

Alternanthera bettzickiana (Regel) G. Nicholson 錦繡莧（紅草）
Ill. Gard. Dict. 1: 59. 1884; FRPS 25(2): 237. 1979; FTW ed. 2, 2: 395. 1996; FGD 4: 111. 2000; FOC 5: 427. 2003.
Telanthera bettzickiana Regel, Ind. Sem. Hort. Petrop. 28. 1862, et Gartenflora 11: 178. 1862.

Perennial herb, 20 – 50 cm tall. Stems erect or prostrate at base, much branched, young shoots pubescent. Leaves papery; petiole 1– 4 cm; leaf blade rhombic, elliptic to narrowly spatulate, 1– 8 × 0.5 –2.5 cm, apex obtuse or acute, gradually tapering to the base, sparsely pubescent on both surfaces when young, later glabrescent, purplish or green, with white-yellow to red blotches. Flowers in terminal and axillary, sessile heads. Bracts and bracteoles ovate-lanceolate, 1.5–3 mm. Perianth-segments 5, unequal, the outer 3 longer, pubescent. Stamens 5; anthers linear oblong. Ovary glabrous, with a short style and capitate stigma.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 1557, 2176.
Distribution: Widely cultivated in tropics; possibly originated from Brazil.
Ecology: Flowering: Oct.–Nov.
Uses: Ornamental.

Alternanthera dentata (Moench) Stuchl. ex R. E. Fr. f. rubiginosa Suess. 紅龍莧
Repert. Spec. Nov. 35: 299. 1934.
Alternanthera dentata (Moench) Stuchl. ex R. F. Fr. cv. Rubiginosa

Short-lived perennial herb, 30–160 cm tall, all parts dark purple except inflorescence. Stems obtusely quadrangular, ± swollen at nodes, sparsely pubescent. Leaves opposite; petioles 5 –20 mm; leaf blade ovate elliptic to elliptic lanceolate, 3–6 × 1.5–3 cm, base attenuate, apex short-acuminate or acute, margin entire, sparsely strigillose on adaxial surface and on veins of abaxial surface. Flowers in axillary and terminal subglobose heads of 6 –9 mm in diam.; peduncles 3–15 mm; bracts and perianth scarious, white to greenish; stamens usually 5, equaling to the perianth.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens.
