Distribution: West Indies to Brazil. Widely cultivated in tropic and subtropical areas.
Ecology: Flowering and fruiting: Sep.–Mar. of the following year.
Uses: Ornanmental.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Mai Po, Tai Shan Wai. Exotic
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Alternanthera paronychioides A. St.-Hil. 星星蝦鉗菜
Voy. Distr. Diam. 2: 439. 1833; FTW ed. 2, 2: 395. 1996; FGD 4: 112. 2000; FOC 5: 427. 2003.

Annual or perennial herb. Stems tufted, prostrate, 30 –50 cm or longer, young shoots white-pubescent, glabrescent. Leaves opposite; petioles 0.5 –1.5 cm; leaf blade elliptic, ovate or obovate, 1–3 × 0.4 –1 cm, apex obtuse or acute, gradually narrowed to the base, margin entire, adaxially glabrous, sparsely pubescent on abaxial surface. Flowers in axillary, sessile clusters; flower-clusters globose, ovoid, ca. 1 cm in diam. Bracteoles ovate-oblong, ca. 2 mm, white and scarious 1–1.5 mm. Perianth -segments 5, nearly equal, oblong-lanceolate, ca. 4 mm, scarious, apex acute and mucronate, 3-nerved and sparsely pubescent on the lower part. Stamens 5, very short, with intervening teeth or appendages (staminodes). Utricle obcordate, laterally compressed, ca. 1.5 mm long.

Locality: Mai Po, Tai Shan Wai. Exotic. P. S. Choi 526; Y. W. Lam 736.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong (naturalized). Native to tropical America, widely dispersed over most tropical regions.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides. Flowering: Mar.–Sep.

Alternanthera philoxeroides (Mart.) Griseb. 空心莧（空心蓮子草）
Abh. Konigl. Ges. Wiss. Gottingen 24: 36. 1879; FRPS 25(2): 236. 1979; FTW ed. 2, 2: 395. 1996; FGD 4: 112. 2000; FOC 5: 427. 2003.
Bucholzia philoxeroides Mart., Nov. Actorum Acad. Caes. Leop.-Carol. Nat. Cur. 13(1): 107. 1825.

Perennial herb. Stems ascending from the prostrate base, 50 –120 cm or longer, obscurely quadrangular, with a line of short hairs in the groove on both sides. Leaves papery; petiole 3 – 5 mm; leaf blade oblong-oblanceolate, to narrowly obovate, 2.5 – 5 × 1–2 cm, apex acute or obtuse, gradually narrowed to the base, margin entire, glabrous or with appressed hairs on adaxial surfaces. Flowers in axillary, peduncled clusters of 1–1.5 cm in diam. Peduncles 1–2(–3) cm, sparsely pubescent. Bracts ovate; bracteoles lanceolate, both about 2 mm, white and scarious. Perianthsegments 5, oblong, 4–5(–6) mm, apex acute, white, scarious and shining. Stamens usually 5, alternating with linear-oblong staminodes. Ovary pyriform.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Naturalized. Y. S. Lau 2719; L. T. Lo 506.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian (naturalized). Native to S
America; naturalized in N America, tropical Asia, and Australia.
Ecology: Wet places on roadsides and cultivated fields or wastelands. Flowering: May– Oct.

Alternanthera pungens Kunth 刺花蓮子草
Nov. Gen. Sp. (quarto ed.) 2: 206. 1817; FRPS 25(2): 234. 1979; K. Larsen, Fl. Thailand, 5(4): 403. 1992; FOC 5: 427. 2003.
Alternanthera repens (L.) Link, Enum. Hort. Berol. Alt. 1: 154. 1821.
Achyranthes repens L., Sp. Pl. 205. 1753.

Annual herb. Stems prostrate, 20–30 cm or longer, densely white-strigose. Leaves papery; petiole 3 – 5 mm, glabrous or hairy; leaf blade ovate, obovate or oblong-obovate, 1–2.5 × 0.5 –1.5 cm, base cuneate, apex rounded, margin entire, glabrous or sparsely pubescent with appressed hairs on both surfaces. Flowers in axillary, sessile clusters; flower-clusters globose to oblong-ovoid, 0.5–1 cm. Bracts lanceolate, ca. 4 mm, strongly spinescent. Bracteoles lanceolate, 3– 4 mm, apex acuminate or acute. Perianth-segments 5, the outer 2 navicular, ca. 5 mm, apex pungent, with tuft of hairs near base, middle one oblong-elliptic, 3 –3.5 mm, acute, inner 2 smaller, embracing ovary, with dorsal hair-tuft, scarious. Stamens 5, with intervening teeth (staminodes). Ovary compressed globose; style very short. Utricle compressed ovoid, 1–1.5 mm.

Locality: The New Territories. Exotic. Y. S. Lau 3315.
Distribution: Guangdong, Fujian (naturalized). Native to Brazil; naturalized elsewhere.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides. Flowering & fruiting: May– Oct.

Alternanthera sessilis (L.) DC. 蝦鉗菜（蓮子草）
Cat. Pl. Horti Monsp. 77. 1813; FHK 286. 1861; FKH 214. 1912; FHN 1: 409. 1964; FRPS 25(2): 234. 1979; FTW ed. 2, 2: 396, pl. 184, Photo 154. 1996; FGD 4: 111. 2000; FOC 5: 427. 2003.
Gomphrena sesselis L., Sp. Pl. 225. 1753.
Alternanthera nodiflora R. Brown, Prodr. 1: 417. 1810; FKH 214. 1912; FGD 4: 111. 2000.

Perennial herb. Stems prostrate, 15 – 50 cm or longer, with a line of short hairs on one side. Leaves subsessile; leaf blade variable in shape and size, linear lanceolate, oblong-elliptic to oblong obovate, 1–8 × 0.2–2 cm, apex rounded, obtuse or acute, gradually narrowed to the base, margin entire, glabrous on both surfaces. Flowers in axillary, sessile clusters, surrounded by a few short woolly hairs; flowerclusters initially globose, afterwards elongate and cylindric, to 1–1.5 cm. Bracts and bracteoles ovate, white and scarious 1–1.5 mm. Perianth-segments 5, oblong-lanceolate, 1.5 –2 mm, scarious, apex acute, but not pungent. Stamens 3, very short. Utricle obcordate, laterally compressed, falling with the perianth.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. HK sheet 4547; Y. S. Lau 399; H. C. Tang 2017.
Distribution: A common weed widely distributed throughout tropics and subtropics.
Ecology: Roadsides, wastelands and cultivated fields. Flowering & fruiting: May–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), animal food.

Amaranthus blitum L. 凹頭莧
Sp. Pl. 990. 1753; FKH 214. 1912; FOC 5: 421. 2003.
Amaranthus lividus L., Sp. Pl. 990. 1753; FRPS 25(2): 217. 1979; FGD 4: 101. 2000.

Annual herb, 10 –30 cm tall. Stems decumbent or ascending, green or purplish, branched from the base. Leaves alternate; petioles 1–4 cm; leaf blade ovate to rhombic-ovate, 1.5– 4.5 × 1–3 cm, base broadly cuneate, apex retuse, with a mucro in the sinus, margin entire or obscurely undulate, glabrous on both surfaces. Flowers many, greenish, in dense axillary clusters, the upper ones forming long dense terminal spikes or panicles. Bracts and bracteoles ovate, less than 1 mm. Perianth-segments 3, oblong, 1–1.5 mm; stigmas 2 or 3. Utricles ovoid, 1.5–3 mm, distinctly longer than perianth, smooth or slightly wrinkled.

Locality: Ping Shan. Y. W. Lam 372, 1349.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China, except NW dry regions. A pantropical weed, adventive to warm temperate regions.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides. Flowering & fruiting: Feb.–Sep.
Uses: Food (vegetable).

Amaranthus spinosus L. 刺莧
Sp. Pl. 991. 1753; FHK 284. 1861; FKH 214. 1912; FHN 1: 404. 1964; FRPS 25(2): 210. 1979; FTW ed. 2, 2: 398, pl. 185, photo 155. 1996; FGD 4: 99. 2000; FOC 5: 419. 2003.

Annual herb, 30 –100 cm tall. Stems erect, green or purplish. Leaves alternate, armed with 1 or 2 straight spines in each axil; petioles 1– 8 cm; leaf blade ovate to ovate-lanceolate, 3 –12 × 1– 5.5 cm, base cuneate, apex obtuse, aristate, margin entire, glabrous or sparsely puberulent on veins when young. Flowers many, greenish, in dense axillary clusters, the upper ones forming long dense terminal spikes, either simple or paniculately branched. Female flowers always on the lower part of the spikes. Bracts and bracteoles ovate triangular, ca. 5 mm. Perianth-segments 5, oblong, ca. 1.5 mm. Stigmas 2–3. Utricles oblong, 1–1.2 mm, opening transversely.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Naturalized. L. Gibbs 7752; Y. S. Lau 2166, 3084.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Henan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian. A common weed of the tropics, subtropics and warm temperate regions; probably originated from neotropics.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides and cultivated fields. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Dec.
Uses: Food (vegetable), medicinal (folklore).

Amaranthus tricolor L. 莧菜
Sp. Pl. 989. 1753; FHN 1: 404. 1964; FRPS 25(2): 212. 1979; FGD 4: 100. 2000; FOC 5: 420. 2003.

Annual herb, 30–150 cm tall. Stems erect, green or purplish, glabrous or puberulous when young. Leaves alternate; petioles 2–6 cm; leaf blade ovate to rhombic-ovate or ovate-triangular, 4 –10 × 2–7 cm, base broadly cuneate, apex obtuse or emarginate with mucro at the tip, margin entire or obscurely undulate, glabrous on both surfaces. Flowers many, greenish, in dense axillary clusters, the upper ones forming long dense terminal spikes or panicles. Male and female flowers mixed on the rachis. Bracts and bracteoles ovate-lanceolate, 2.5 –3 mm, aristate. Perianth-segments 3, oblong, 3– 5 mm. Stigmas 3. Utricles oblong-ovoid, 2–2.5 mm, opening transversely.

Locality: Cultivated. S. T. Dunn 9313; Y. S. Lau 3128.
Distribution: Widely cultivated and naturalized in tropics, probably originated from tropical Asia.
Ecology: Sometimes escaped from cultivation, in wastelands. Flowering & fruiting: May–Sep.
Uses: Food (vegetable), ornamental.

Amaranthus viridis L. 綠莧（野莧）
Sp. Pl. ed. 2, 1405. 1763; FHK 284. 1861; FKH 214. 1912; FHN 1: 405, fig. 216. 1964; FRPS 25(2): 216, pl. 47: 5 – 8. 1979; FTW ed. 2, 2: 400, pl. 186. 1996; FGD 4: 100. 2000; FOC 5: 420. 2003.

Annual herb, 20–60 cm tall, glabrous throughout. Stems erect, green or purplish, branched on the upper part. Leaves alternate; petioles 3– 6 cm; leaf blade ovate to rhombic-ovate, 3 –9 × 2.5 – 6 cm, base broadly cuneate or subtruncate, apex obtuse or emarginate, margin entire or obscurely undulate, glabrous on both surfaces. Flowers many, greenish, in dense clusters, the upper ones forming long dense terminal panicles. Bracts and bracteoles lanceolate, less than 1 mm. Perianth-segments 3(– 4), oblong, ca. 1.5 mm. Stigmas 3. Utricles subglobose, 1–1.5 mm, not or slightly longer than perianth, strongly wrinkled, indehiscent or bursts irregularly.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 2148; Y. W. Lam 951.
Distribution: A pantropical weed, adventive to warm temperate regions.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides near villages. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.– Oct.
Uses: Food (vegetable).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Kowloon, Sha Tin, Fanling, Sheung Shui, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Celosia argentea L. 青葙（野雞冠）
Sp. Pl. 205. 1753; FHK 284. 1861; FKH 213. 1912; FHN 1: 402. 1964; FTW ed. 2, 2: 400, pl. 187. 1996; FRPS 25(2): 200, pl. 44: 1– 4. 1996; FGD 4: 102. 2000; FOC 5: 416. 2003.

Annual herb, 30–100 cm tall, glabrous throughout. Stems erect, angled, young shoots purplish. Leaves alternate; petioles 2– 15 mm; leaf blade lanceolate to elliptic-lanceolate, 5 –8 × 1–3 cm, gradually narrowed to both ends, margin entire or very minutely serrulate. Spikes terminal, 3 –10 cm, densely flowered; bracts and bracteoles lanceolate, 3–5 mm, white, scarious. Perianth-segments oblong-lanceolate, 6–8 mm, pink, with white and scarious margins. Stamens 5; filaments and anthers pink or purplish; style 3– 5 mm, minutely 2-lobed. Utricles ovoid, 3 –3.5 mm, enclosed in the persistent perianth.

Locality: Kowloon, Sha Tin, Fanling, Sheung Shui, Lantau Island. W. J. Tutcher 11720; Y. S. Lau 1157, 2192.
Distribution: A pantropical weed, dispersed over most parts of China.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides near villages. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal, animal food.

Celosia argentea L. var. cristata (L.) Kuntze 雞冠花
Revis. Gen. Pl. 2: 541. 1891; FHN 1: 403. 1964; FGD 4: 103. 2000.
Celosia cristata L., Sp. Pl. 205. 1753; FHN 1: 403. 1964; FTW ed. 2, 2: 403. 1996; FRPS 25(2): 201. 1979; FOC 5: 416. 2003.

This variety is a tetraploid cultigen derived from Celosia argentea. Leaves ovate, ovate-lanceolate or lanceolate, 6–15 × 1.5– 6 cm. Spikes terminal, the main axis strongly flattened or much branched, cristate or feathered, or with plumy slender spikes and panicles; bracts, bracteoles and perianth variously colored, ranging from white to orange, red to purple.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 23009, 23010.
Distribution: Cultivated worldwide.
Ecology: Cultivated in flowering beds or as a pot plant. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.– Oct.
Uses: Ornamental.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Aberdeen, Sai Kung, Tai Po, Lam Tsuen
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Cyathula prostrata (L.) Blume 杯莧
Bijdr. 549. 1825; FHK 285. 1861; FKH 214. 1912; FHN 1: 405. 1964; FTW ed. 2, 2: 403, pl. 188. 1996; FRPS 25(2): 218. 1979; FGD 4: 104, fig, 65. 2000; FOC 5: 421. 2003.
Achyranthes prostrata L., Sp. Pl. ed. 2, 296. 1762.

Perennial herb, pubescent throughout. Stems prostrate, usually purplish, rooting at nodes; flowering branches ascending or erect, 15–50 cm tall. Leaves opposite; petioles 2–3 mm; leaf blade obovate to obovate-elliptic, 1–6(– 8) × 0.5 –3 cm, base broadly cuneate, apex obtuse or abruptly acute, margin entire. Racemes terminal, 5 –20 cm; flower-clusters reflexed, 3 – 8 mm spaced on rachis, consisting of 2–3 perfect flowers and 2–3 cluster of purplish hooked bristles. Perianth segments 5, oblong, ca. 5 mm, densely white pubescent outside. Stamens 5; staminodes apex truncate or slightly 2-toothed. Utricles globose, ca. 5 mm in diam., indehiscent.

Locality: Aberdeen, Sai Kung, Tai Po, Lam Tsuen. Y. S. Lau 1343; Y. W. Lam 2187; HK sheet 4539.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Taiwan; Indochina, Indian subcontinent, tropical Africa, Australia.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides near villages, also in bushes in valleys or by streams. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Harlech Road, Ngau Chi Wan, Sha Tin, Sai Kung, Sham Tseng, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Gomphrena celosioides C. Martius 銀花莧（野千日紅）
Nova Acta Phys.-Med. Acad. Caes. Leop.-Carol. Nat. Cur. 13(1): 301. 1825; FHN 1: 410. 1964; FRPS 25(2): 239. 1979; FTW ed. 2, 2: 407. 1996; FGD 4: 113. 2000; FOC 5: 428. 2003.

Annual herb, 10–35 cm tall. Stems erect or ascending, white-pilose. Leaves papery, shortly petiolate or subsessile; leaf blade oblong to somewhat spathulate, 3– 4.5 × 0.5 –1.5 cm, base attenuate, apex acute or obtuse, margin entire and ciliate, adaxially ± with appressed hairs or glabrous, abaxially pubescent. Inflorescence a terminal head, initially globose, afterwards elongate into a short spike, to 2– 4 cm. Bracteoles triangular lanceolate, ca. 6 mm, silvery white, winged dorsally. Perianth-segments lanceolate, ca. 5 mm, woolly outside; filament-tube slightly shorter than perianth-segments; style 2 branched. Utricles ellipsoid, enclosed by the woolly persistent perianth.

Locality: Harlech Road, Ngau Chi Wan, Sha Tin, Sai Kung, Sham Tseng, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 400, 1641; H. C. Tang 2113.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Taiwan (naturalized). Native to S America, widely naturalized in tropics.
Ecology: Roadsides, wastelands. Flowering & fruiting: Feb.–Sep.

Gomphrena globosa L. 千日紅
Sp. Pl. 224. 1753; FHN 1: 410. 1964; FRPS 25(2): 238. 1979; FGD 4: 113. 2000; FOC 5: 428. 2003.

Annual herb, 20–60 cm tall. Stems erect, covered with hoary long hairs. Leaves papery; petioles 0.5–1.5 cm, hairy; leaf blade oblong to elliptic or somewhat obovate, 3.5–13 ×1.5–5 cm, apex acute or obtuse, base attenuate, margin entire and ciliate, white-pilose on both surfaces. Inflorescence a dense globular head, 2–3 cm in diam., closely subtended by 2 broad leafy bracts. Bracteoles triangular lanceolate, ca. 1 cm, violate, red, yellowish or white in different garden races, winged dorsally. Perianth-segments lanceolate, 5–6 mm, woolly outside. Filamenttube as long as perianth-segments. Style 2 branched. Utricles subglobose, 2–2.5 mm in diam., enclosed by the woolly persistent perianth.

Locality: Cultivated. L. T. Lo 640; Y. S. Lau 1011.
Distribution: Widely cultivated throughout tropical and warm temperate regions, sometimes naturalized.
Ecology: Usually cultivated as a pot plant in Hong Kong. Flowering & fruiting: Feb.–Sep.
Uses: Ornamental.

Portulaca oleracea L. 馬齒莧
Sp. Pl. 445. 1753; FHK 127. 1861; FKH 41. 1912; FHN 1: 384. 1964; FGD 2: 91. 1991; FTW ed. 2, 2: 336, photo 144. 1996; FRPS 26: 38. 1996; FOC 5: 443. 2003.

Annual succulent herb. Stems prostrate or spreading, 10 –50 cm or longer, usually purplish, glabrous, with inconspicuous scales or minute hairs in axils of leaves. Leaves alternate or subopposite, subsessile; leaf blade flat, obovate to cuneate-oblong, 1–2.5(–4) × 0.5 –2 cm, apex obtuse to rounded. Flowers yellow, solitary or in terminal clusters of 3– 5, sessile above the leafy bracts. Sepals ca. 6 mm. Petals yellow, broadly obovate, fugacious and scarcely exceeding the sepals. Stamens 7–10(–15); styles mostly 5. Capsule ovoid, opening transversely.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. S. T. Dunn 1072, 4204; HK sheet 298.
Distribution: Worldwide weed.
Ecology: Cultivated grounds, waste places. Flowering: May–Aug.; fruiting: Jun.–Sep.
Uses: Food (vegetable), medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Shek O, Lan Nai Wan, Tseng Tau, Pui O, Cheung Chau, Waglan Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Portulaca pilosa L. 毛馬齒莧
Sp. Pl. 445. 1753; FHN 1: 384. 1964; FGD 2: 91. 1991; FTW ed. 2, 2: 336, photo 145. 1996; FRPS 26: 38. 1996; FOC 5: 442. 2003.

Annual succulent herb. Stems erect or ascending, 10 –30 cm tall, with long hairs in axils of leaves. Leaves alternate, short petiolate; leaf blade ± terete, linear to elliptic, 0.4 –2.8 × 0.1–0.4 cm, apex acute. Flowers yellow, solitary or in terminal clusters of 2–10, sessile, surrounded by 4 –9 verticillate leaves and axillary hairs. Sepals oblong, 2– 6 mm. Petals 4– 6, obovate, 2.5 –12 × 1.8 –11 mm, red, pink or yellow. Stamens usually 20 –30; style 3 –7-lobed. Capsule ovoid or subglobose, opening transversely.

Locality: Shek O, Lan Nai Wan, Tseng Tau, Pui O, Cheung Chau, Waglan Island. H. C. Tang 2097; K. L. Yip 4194; Y. S. Lau 1473.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, S Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; Malesia and tropical America.
Ecology: Sandy places near seashore. Flowering & fruiting: May–Aug.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Common in Hong Kong, cultivated or naturalized
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Talinum paniculatum (Jacq.) Gaertn. 土人參
Fruct. Sem. Pl. 2: 219, t. 128. 1791; FGD 2: 92, fig. 64. 1991; FTW ed. 2, 2: 337, 1. 155. 1996; FRPS 26: 42, pl. 8: 6 –11. 1996; FOC 5: 444. 2003.

Perennial herb, 30 –70 cm tall, with thick roots, glabrous throughout. Stems erect, little branched. Leaves alternate or sub‑opposite, short stalked or subsessile; leaf blade obovate, obovate-oblanceolate or elliptic, 4–12 × 2– 4.5 cm, base cuneate, apex acute or shortly acuminate, margin entire. Inflorescence a terminal thyrse, to 18 cm, usually dichotomous. Pedicels 5 – 10 mm. Sepals 2, ovate, purplish red, 1–3 mm, caducous. Petals 5, pink to light purplish red, oblong obovate or elliptic, 6 –12 mm. Stamens 10–20. Ovary globose, 1-locular; style 3-lobed. Capsule globose, ca. 3 mm in diam., opening by 3 valves.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong, cultivated or naturalized. H. C. Tang 1953; HK sheet 36018.
Distribution: Cultivated and sometimes naturalized in C & S China. Native to tropical America; naturalized elsewhere.
Ecology: Usually cultivated as a pot plant, sometimes escaped, growing on waste places. Flowering: Jun.–Aug.; fruiting: Sep.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.

Basella alba L. 落葵（潺菜）
Sp. Pl. 272. 1753; FTW ed. 2, 2: 340. 1996; FRPS 26: 44. 1996; FGD 4: 115, fig. 72. 2000; FOC 5: 445. 2003.
Basella rubra L., Sp. Pl. 272. 1753; FGZ 149, fig. 60. 1956; FHN 1: 411, fig. 221. 1964.

Perennial twining vine. Stems fleshy, glabrous, green or purplish. Leaves fleshy; petioles 1–3 cm; leaf blade ovate or suborbicular, 3–12 × 3–10 cm, base shallowly cordate or rounded, apex acute or shortly acuminate, margin entire. Spikes axillary, 4–20 cm. Flowers small, sessile, in small clusters. Perianth fleshy, lower part white, apex purple, with 5 obtuse lobes. Stamens 5, included; filaments erect in bud. Ovary globose; styles 3. Fruit subglobse, 5 –7 mm in diam., enclosed within fleshy persistent perianth, dark purple when mature.

Locality: Cultivated. P. S. Choi 495; Y. S. Lau 2846.
Distribution: Pantropical. Widely cultivated in China, sometimes escaped from cultivation.
Ecology: Flowering: May–Sep.; fruiting: Jul.– Oct.
Uses: Food (vegetable), ornamental.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Mount Cameron, So Kong Po, Sha Tin
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Mollugo stricta L. 粟米草
Sp. Pl. 2: 131. 1762; FHK 23. 1861; FKH 114. 1912; FRPS 26: 28, pl. 6: 7. 1996; FTW ed. 2, 2: 326, pl. 151, photo 139. 1996; FOC 5: 439. 2003.
Mollugo pentaphylla auct. non L.: FHN 1: 382. 1964; FGD 2: 85. 1991.

Annual glabrous herb, 10– 40 cm tall. Stems diffuse, much branched. Basal leaves rosulate, oblong-obovate 1.5– 5 × 0.6–1 cm; stem-leaves opposite or in false whorls of 4–6; petioles 1–3 mm; leaf blade lanceolate to linear-lanceolate, rarely narrowly elliptic, 1.5–5 × 0.2–0.8 mm, base attenuate, apex acute or acuminate, margin entire. Flowers very small, in slender bifid racemes or dichotomous cymes, on slender peduncles. Pedicels filiform, 1–2.5 mm. Sepals 5, light green, with white edges. Petals none. Stamens 3–5; filaments dilated at base. Ovary 3-locular; styles 3, linear, very short. Capsule subglobose, opening by 3 valves; seeds tuberculate.

Locality: Mount Cameron, So Kong Po, Sha Tin. Y. S. Lau 2284; HK sheet 36034.
Distribution: Widely distributed in areas S of Qingling and Yellow River. Dispersed over tropical and subtropical regions of Asia.
Ecology: Wastelands, cultivated fields, sandy places near seashore.

Mollugo verticillata L. 種棱粟米草
Sp. Pl. 89. 1753; FGD 2: 85. 1991; FRPS 26: 29. 1996; FTW ed. 2, 2: 328. 1996; FOC 5: 439. 2003.

Annual glabrous herb, 10–30 cm tall. Stems erect or ascending, much branched. Basal leaves rosulate, obovate or obovate-spathulate 1.5–5 × 0.6–1 cm; stem-leaves opposite or in false whorls of 3–8, subsessile; leaf blade oblanceolate to linear-oblanceolate, 1.5 –2.5 × 0.15 –0.5 mm, base narrowly cuneate or attenuate, apex acute or obtuse, margin entire. Flowers in umbellate-clusters of 3 – 5, on one side of nodes. Pedicels slender, 3 – 5 mm. Sepals 5, or rarely 4, oblong to ovate-oblong, 2.5–3 mm, whitish adaxially, with scarious edges. Petals none. Stamens 3, rarely 2, or 4 – 5; filaments slightly dilated at base. Ovary 3-locular; styles 3. Capsule ellipsoid or subglobose, opening by 3 valves; seeds smooth and shining.

Locality: Pak Nai, Castle Peak. Y. W. Lam 1513; HK sheet 32383.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, tropical America, S Europe.
Ecology: Grassy slopes, farmlands. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Dec.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tsiu Hang, Mui Tsz Lam, Mau Ping, Chung Mei, TaiM Po Kau, Ng Tung Chai, Tai Mo Shan, Lin Fa Shan
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Drymaria cordata (L.) Schult. 荷蓮豆
Syst. Veg. 5: 406. 1819; FHK 22. 1861; FKH 40. 1912; Hand.-Mazz., Symb. Sin. 7: 202. 1929; FHN 1: 377, fig. 196. 1964; FGD 2: 80, fig. 55. 1991; FOC 6: 6. 2001.
Drymaria diandra Bl., Bijdr. 62. 1825; FRPS 26: 61, pl. 10: 8 –12. 1996; S. S. Ying, FTW ed. 2, 2: 360, pl. 167. 1996.

Annual herb. Stems prostrate, rooting at nodes, glabrous. Leaves opposite, short petiolate; leaf blade ovate-cordate or orbicular, about 1–1.5 cm long and broad, 3 – 5-nerved. Flowers in axillary or terminal cymes. Pedicels 1.5–3 mm, with glandular hairs. Sepals narrowly ovate, 2–3.5 mm, herbaceous, with scarious margin, 3-nerved, glandular-hairy. Petals white, obovate-cuneate, ca. 2.5 mm, deeply 2-lobed. Stamens slightly shorter than sepals; filaments slightly dilated at base. Ovary ovoid; styles 3, united at base. Capsule ovoid, 3-valved.

Locality: Tsiu Hang, Mui Tsz Lam, Mau Ping, Chung Mei, TaiM Po Kau, Ng Tung Chai, Tai Mo Shan, Lin Fa Shan. W. J. Tutcher 11146; Y. S. Lau 1342, 1627.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; E Asia,
Indian subcontinent, Malesia, Australia, N Africa.
Ecology: Margins of forests, streamsides and other damp shaded places. Flowering: Apr.– Oct.; fruiting: Jun.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Victoria Peak, Pok Fu Lam, So Kon Po, Tai Long Wan, Shing Mun, Mui Tsz Lam
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Myosoton aquaticum (L.) Moench 鵝腸菜（牛繁縷）
Methodus 225. 1794; FRPS 26: 74, pl. 16: 1–9. 1996; FOC 6: 38. 2001. Stellaria aquatica (L.) Scop., Fl. Carn. 2(1): 319. 1774; FHK 20. 1861; FKH 40. 1912; FGD 2: 79. 1991; FTW ed. 2, 2: 373, pl. 174, photo 150. 1996.
Cerastium aquaticum L., Sp. Pl. 439. 1753.

Biennial or perennial herbs. Stems ascending from the prostrate base, 50– 80 cm or longer, glabrous or glandular hairy on upper part. Leaves ovate to broadly ovate, 2.5 –5.5 × 1–3 cm, apex acute, base cordate, margin entire, sometimes ciliate, upper ones smaller, on long petioles; lower ones sessile or stem-clasping. Flowers in terminal dichotomous cymes. Bracts foliaceous, ciliate. Pedicels slender, 1–2 cm, lengthening after flowering, with glandular hairs. Sepals ovate-lanceolate, 4 – 5 mm, with scarious margin and glandular hairs abaxially. Petals white, deeply 2-lobed to near base; lobes linear to linear-lanceolate, 3 –3.5 × 1 cm. Stamens 10, slightly shorter than petals. Capsule ovoid, opening to middle into five 2-toothed valves.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Pok Fu Lam, So Kon Po, Tai Long Wan, Shing Mun, Mui Tsz Lam. Y. W. Lam 516, 611; HK sheet 294.
Distribution: Dispersed over most parts of China. Widely distributed in temperate Asia; Indian subcontinent; Europe, and naturalized elsewhere in temperate regions.
Ecology: In fields, wet places by streams. Flowering: May– Aug.; fruiting: Jun.–Sep.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), food (vegetable).

Polycarpaea corymbosa (L.) Lam. 白鼓釘
Tabl. Encycl. 2: 129. 1793; FHK 22. 1861; FKH 40. 1912; FHN 1: 378, fig. 197. 1964; FGD 2: 81. 1991; FRPS 26: 63, pl. 13: 4 –7. 1996; FOC 6: 7. 2001.
Achyranthes corymbosa L., Sp. Pl. 205. 1753.

Perennial herb, 15–35 cm tall. Stems erect, more or less hoary with loose cotton hairs. Leaves sessile, often clustered at nodes in false whorls; leaf blade linear to subulate, 15 –20 × 1–1.5 mm, apex acute, glabrescent. Flowers many, in dense cymes and forming broad terminal dichotomous corymbs. Bracts lanceolate, scarious and translucent. Pedicels slender, white-puberulent. Sepals lanceolate, 2–3 mm, scarious and shining, white or reddish brown. Petals broadly ovate, obtuse, not half so long as sepals. Stamens shorter than petals. Ovary ovoid; style single, entire. Capsule ovoid, not half so long as the persistent sepals.

Locality: Silverstrand, Deep Water Bay. L. Gibbs 7665; HK sheet 297, 2625.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Anhui, Fujian; throughout tropical regions.
Ecology: Grassy slopes, waste places and sandy seashores. Flowering: Jul.–Aug.; fruiting: Sep.– Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Polycarpon prostratum (Forssk.) Asch. & Schweinf. ex Asch. 多莢草
Oesterr. Bot. Z. 39: 128. 1889; FOC 6: 6. 2001.

Annual herb. Stems diffuse or prostrate, 10–25 cm, much branched, usually pubescent, rarely glabrescent. Leaves opposite or almost in whorls; petioles very short; leaf blade oblanceolate, linear-oblanceolate, spathulate or narrowly elliptic, 6–20 × 1.5 – 5 mm, base cuneate or attenuate, apex acute or obtuse, glabrous, veins obscure; stipules ovate-lanceolate, about 1/4 the length of leaf blade, scarious. Cymes axillary or terminal, 2–4 cm. Flowers small, ca. 3 mm in diam.; sepal lanceolate, 2.5–3 mm, midvein raised, apex obtuse and more or less hooked, margin hyaline; petals often fewer than 5, linear oblong, less than half the length of sepals; stamens 5, opposite with sepals. Capsules ovoid, shorter than sepals.

Locality: Ho Pui Reservoir. Y. W. Lam 1490.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian; tropical regions of Asia and Africa.
Ecology: Open fields, farmlands. Flowering and fruiting: Almost all year round.

Sagina japonica (Sw.) Ohwi 漆姑草
J. Jap. Bot. 13: 438. 1937; FGD 2: 77. 1991; FRPS 26: 255, pl. 61: 5 –7. 1996; FTW ed. 2, 2: 362, pl. 168. 1996; FOC 6: 10. 2001.
Spergula japonica Sw., Ges. Naturf. Freunde Berlin Neue Schriften 3: 164. 1801.
Sagina linnaei auct. non Presl: FKH 40. 1912.

Annual smalll herb, 5 –20 cm tall. Stems tufted, ± diffuse, sparsely glandular hairy on the upper part. Leaves sessile, linear, 5–20 × 0.8–1.5 mm, apex acute, connate at base, glabrous. Flowers small, solitary, terminal or in axils of apical leaves. Pedicels slender, 1–2 cm, sparsely pubescent. Sepals 5, ovate-elliptic, ca. 2 mm. Petals 5, white, narrowly ovate, slightly shorter than sepals, apex rounded, entire. Stamens 5, shorter than petals. Ovary ovoid; styles 5, linear. Capsule ovoid, slightly longer than the persistent sepals, opening to the middle into 5 valves.

Locality: Wong Chuk Hang, Sunset Peak. W. J. Tutcher 4620; Y. W. Lam 1771; HK sheet 31558.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; also in Russia (Far East), Korea, Japan, Indian subcontinent; naturalized elsewhere in temperate regions.
Ecology: Wastelands, grassy banks. Flowering: Mar.–May; fruiting: May–Jun.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Spergularia marina (L.) Griseb. 擬漆姑
Spic. Fl. Rumel. 1: 213. 1843; FOC 6: 5. 2001.
Spergularia salina J. & C. Persl., Fl. Cech. 95. 1819.
Arenaria rubra L. var. marina L. Sp. Pl. 423. 1753.

Annual or biennial herb. Stems 8 –20(–30) cm tall, densely pubescent. Leaves linear, 5 –30 × 1–1.5 mm, ± fleshy, apex mucronate; stipules broadly triangular, forming a sheath. Flowers terminal or axillary. Sepals ovate, abaxially glandular pubescent, margin membranous. Petals pink above, white near base, rarely entirely white, shorter than sepals, apex obtuse. Capsules ovoid, 5– 6 mm, slightly longer than calyx.

Locality: Nien Wan (Mei Hui Hu). Y. W. Lam 2018.
Distribution: Most provinces in China; widely distributed Asia, Europe, N Africa and N America.
Ecology: Stream-sides, lake-sides, farmlands near seaside.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Mo Shan, Shing Mun, Sha Tin
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Stellaria alsine Grimm 雀舌草
Acta Phys.-Med. Acad. Caes. Leop.-Carol. Nat. Cur. 3. (app.): 313. 1767; FOC 6: 21. 2001.
Stellaria uliginosa Murr., Prodr. Stirp. Gott. 55. 1770; FHK B22. 1861; FKH 40. 1912; FGD 2: 78, fig. 54. 1991; FRPS 26: 129, pl. 30: 1– 5. 1996.

Annual or biennial herb, 15 –25(–35) cm tall, glabrous throughout. Stems tufted, ascending, much branched. Leaves sessile, lanceolate to oblong lanceolate, 5 –20 × 2– 4 mm, base cuneate and semi-amplexicaul, apex acuminate, margin cartilaginous, ± glaucous on both surfaces. Flowers in terminal 2–3- flowered cymes, rarely solitary in axils of leaves. Pedicels slender, 5–20 mm, turned down in fruiting time. Sepals 5, lanceolate 2–4 × 1 mm, margin scarious. Petals 5, white, shorter than or equaling to sepals, deeply 2-lobed to near base; lobes linear. Stamens 5(–10), slightly shorter than petals. Ovary ovoid; styles 3, or sometime 2. Capsule ovoid, opening at top into 6 teeth.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Shing Mun, Sha Tin. L. T. Lo 287; S. P. Lam 107; Y. W. Lam 1345.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Gansu, Nei Mongol, Henan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; N Africa, Europe, temperate Asia.
Ecology: Rice fields, moist places by streams. Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: Jul.–Aug.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Stellaria media (L.) Vill. 繁縷（魚腸草）
Hist. Pl. Dauphine 3: 615. 1789; FHK 21. 1861; FKH 40. 1912; FHN 1: 376. 1964; FGD 2: 79. 1991; FTW ed. 2, 2: 376, pl. 176. 1996; FRPS 26: 104. 1996; FOC 6: 15. 2001.
Alsine media L., Sp. Pl. 272. 1753.

Annual or biennial herb, 10 –30 cm tall. Stems decumbent or ascending, much branched, with a line of hairs down one side. Leaves opposite, lower ones long petioled; upper ones usually sessile; leaf blade broadly ovate or ovate, 1.5 –2.5 × 1–1.5 cm, base abruptly narrowed or sub-cordate, apex acuminate or acute, margin entire. Flowers in terminal 2–3-flowered cymes. Pedicels slender, with a line of hairs, lengthening and turning down in fruiting time, 7–14 mm. Sepals 5, lanceolate ca. 4 mm, apex obtuse or sub-rounded, margin scarious, with short glandular hairs abaxially. Petals 5, white, oblong, shorter than sepals, deeply 2-lobed to near base; lobes linear. Stamens 3 – 5, slightly shorter than petals. Ovary ovoid; styles 3. Capsule ovoid, slightly longer than persistent sepals, opening at top into 6 teeth.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. HK sheet 40607.
Distribution: Dispersed over all China except Xinjiang and Heilongjiang. Widely spread in temperate regions.
Ecology: Waste places, roadsides, cultivated fields. Flowering: Jun.–Jul.; fruiting: Jul.–Aug.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), food (vegetable).

Antigonon leptopus Hook. & Arn. 珊瑚藤
Bot. Beech. Voy. 308. 1841; FHN 1: 385, fig. 203. 1964; FTW ed. 2, 2: 294; 1996; FGD 4: 80, fig. 53. 2000.

Perennial tendril-climbing vines, to 10 m or longer, with thick tuberous root. Stems angular, woody at base, covered with short hairs. Leaves papery; petioles 0.8–2 cm; leaf blade ovate-triangular, 6–15 × 4– 8 cm, base cordate to sagittate, apex acuminate, tip blunt, margin crenate-undulate, covered with soft short hairs on both surfaces; veins impressed adaxially, raised abaxially. Flowers in terminal panicles and axillary racemes, 5 –10 cm, densely flowered, with the rachis terminating in forked tendrils; pedicels slender, 0.5 –1 cm, pubescent. Perianth-segments 5, pink or white, the outer 3 elliptic, 1–1.5 × 0.6 –1.2 cm, apex rounded, base cordate, inner 2 oblong, 1–1.2 × 0.4 –0.6 cm, apex obtuse, narrowed to the base. Stamens 8; filaments united at base, the free parts covered with rusty glandular hairs. Achenes 1–1.5 cm, 3-angled, enclosed in the enlarged, persistent perianth.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. H. C. Tang 176; L. T. Lo 561.
Distribution: Native to Mexico, widely cultivated or naturalized in tropical regions.
Ecology: Flowering and fruiting: Aug.–Dec.
Uses: Ornamental.

Polygonum multiflorum Thunb. 何首烏
Syst. Veg. ed. 14, 379. 1784; FKH 218. 1912; FGD 4: 86. 2000.
Fallopia multiflora (Thunb.) Harald., Symb. Bot. Upsl. 22(2): 77. 1978; FRPS 25: 102. 1998; FYN 11: 357. 2000; FOC 5: 317. 2003.

Perennial herb, with thick, tuberous rhizomes. Stems twining, 2–4 m or longer, much branched, glabrous, woody at base. Leaves alternate; petioles 1–3.5 cm; leaf blade ovate to oblong-ovate, 3–7 × 2– 5 cm, base cordate, apex acuminate, margin entire, glabrous on both surfaces. Ocrea tubular, scarious, brown, 3 – 5 mm, apex oblique, glabrous. Inflorescence paniculate, terminal or axillary, 10–20 cm. Peduncles papillose. Bracts triangular ovate, papillose, each embracing 2– 4 flowers. Pedicels slender, 2–3 mm, articulate at lower part. Perianth white or light green, 3– 4 mm, deeply 5- lobed; lobes elliptic, unequal, the outer 3 larger, dorsally winged; wings suborbicular, enlarged to 6 –7 mm in diam. in fruit. Stamens 8; filaments dilated at base. Ovary ovoid; styles 3, very short; stigmas capitate. Achenes ovoid, 3-ribbed, 2.5 –3 mm, dark brown and shining, enclosed in the winged persistent perianth.

Locality: Severn Road, Stubbs Road. H. C. Tang 687; P. S. Choi 168; Y. S. Lau 176.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, S Shaanxi, S Gansu, Hunan, Hubei, Henan, Anhui, Jiangxi, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian; Japan.
Ecology: Thickets and thin forests on rocky slopes and in valleys. Flowering: Aug.–Sep.; fruiting: Sep.– Oct.
Uses: Medicinal.

Polygonum barbatum L. 毛蓼
Sp. Pl. 1: 362. 1753; FHK 288. 1861; FKH 217. 1912; FHN 1: 390. 1964; FTW ed. 2, 2: 298. 1996; FRPS 25: 21, pl. 6: 1–2. 1998; FGD 4: 93. 2000; FYN 11: 346. 2000; FOC 5: 288. 2003.

Perennial herb, 40–100 cm tall, with creeping rhizomes. Stems erect, pubescent. Leaves alternate; petioles 5–8 mm, densely pilose; leaf blade lanceolate to elliptic-lanceolate, 6–15 × 1.5–4 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, margin entire, ciliate, sparsely pubrulous on both surfaces, pilose along midvein abaxially. Ocrea tubular, 1.5–2 cm, densely pilose and mixed with rigid, curly hairs, apex truncate, with 1.3–3 cm long fine bristles. Racemes spikes-like, 4–8 cm, densely flowered, forming terminal or axillary panicles. Bracts weakly funnel-form, glabrous, apex acute, ciliate, each embracing 3–5 flowers. Pedicels very short. Perianth 1.5–2 mm, deeply 5-lobed; segments elliptic, white or light green, apex acute. Stamens 5–8. Ovary ovoid; styles 3-cleft; stigmas capitate. Achenes triangular, 1.5–2 mm, black, smooth, and shining.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. P. S. Choi 275; Y. W. Lam 904; HK sheet 9904.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Yunnan, Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Myanmar, Philippines.
Ecology: Swamps and wet places. Flowering: Aug.–Sep.; fruiting: Sep.– Oct.

Polygonum capitatum Buch.-Ham. ex D. Don 頭花蓼
Prodr. Fl. Nep. 73. 1825; FRPS 25: 57. 1998; FGD 4: 91. 2000; FYN 11: 326. 2000; FOC 5: 301. 2003.

Perennial herb. Stems tufted, prostrate, sparsely glandular pubescent or glabrescent, woody at base; branches of the current year growth nearly erect, sparsely glandular pubescent. Leaves alternate; petioles 2–3 mm, sometimes with auricles at base; leaf blade ovate to elliptic, 1.5 –3 × 1–2.5 cm, base cuneate, apex acute, margin entire, glandular-ciliate, adaxial surface sparsely glandular-pubescent, sometimes with crescent-shaped, dark brown blotches. Ocrea tubular, scarious, 5 – 8 mm, glandular-pubescent, apex truncate, ciliate. Flowers in terminal, globular head of 6 –10 mm in diam., solitary or in pairs. Peduncles glandular-pubescent. Bracts oblong-ovate, scarious. Perianth pink, 2–3 mm, deeply 5-lobed; segments elliptic. Stamens 8, included. Ovary triangular; styles 3-cleft; stigmas capitate. Achenes triangular, 1.5 –2 mm, dark brown, enclosed in the persistent perianth.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. Y. W. Lam 825.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Yunnan, Xizang, Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi; India, Bhutan, Nepal, Myanmar, Vietnam.
Ecology: Wet places on slopes or in valleys. Flowering: Jun.–Sep.; fruiting: Aug.– Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Polygonum chinense L. 火炭母
Sp. Pl. 363. 1753; FHK 289. 1861; FKH 217. 1912; FHN 1: 392. 1964; FTW ed. 2, 2: 298. 1996; FRPS 25: 55, pl. 12: 1. 1998; FGD 4: 91, fig. 60. 2000; FYN 11: 324, pl. 91: 1–2. 2000; FOC 5: 300. 2003.

Perennial herb to 1 m tall, with creeping rhizomes. Stems initially erect, later elongate and diffuse, glabrous or glabrescent. Leaves alternate; petioles 0.6–1.5 cm, purplish, usually with 2 caducous auricles at base; leaf blade ovate to oblong-ovate, 5–10 × 2–6 cm, base truncate or broadly cordate, apex acute to shortly acuminate, margin entire or obscurely undulate, glabrous, usually with purplish blue blotches. Ocrea tubular, scarious, 1.5–2.5 cm, glabrous, apex oblique, not ciliate. Flowers in little globular head, forming dichotomous, corymbose panicles, terminal or in axils of upper leaves. Peduncles and pedicels glandular-pubescent. Bracts broadly ovate, glabrous, each embracing 1–3 flowers. Perianth ca. 3.5 mm, 5-lobed beyond middle; segments ovate, greenish white or pink. Stamens 8, included. Ovary ovoid; styles 3-cleft. Achenes triangular, 3–4 mm, enclosed in fleshy, blue-black persistent perianth.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 1167; HK sheet 4576, 32345.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, India, Malesia.
Ecology: Ditches, wastelands, and on roadsides. Flowering: Jul.–Sep.; fruiting: Aug.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Wo Hop Shek, Ho Chung, San Wai, Fanling
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Polygonum dichotomum Blume 二歧蓼
Bijdr. 11: 529. 1826; FHN 1: 392. 1964; FTW ed. 2, 2: 299, pl. 145. 1996; FRPS 25: 76. 1998; FGD 4: 87. 2000; FOC 5: 314. 2003.

Annual herb, 40 –100 cm tall. Stems ascending or erect, longitudinally ribbed, sparsely armed with retrorse prickles on the ribs. Leaves alternate; petioles 0.5 –1.5 cm; leaf blade lanceolate or narrowly elliptic, 5 –10 × 1–3 cm, base cuneate, truncate or sub-sagittate, apex acute, adaxially green, glabrous, abaxially glaucous, sometimes sparsely armed with short prickles on midvein. Ocrea tubular, 1.5–2 cm, scarious, apex oblique, glabrous or sparsely strigose. Racemes head-like, 1–2 cm, forming dichotomous, corymbose panicles, terminal or in axils of upper leaves. Peduncles covered with glandular hairs. Bracts broadly elliptic, 2–3 mm, ciliate, each embracing 2–3 flowers. Perianth white or pink, 2–2.5 mm, deeply 5-lobed; segments broadly elliptic. Stamens 5, included. Ovary ovoid; styles 2-cleft, stigmas capitate. Achenes subglobose, 2–2.5 mm, convex on both sides, dark brown, not shining, enclosed in the persistent perianth.

Locality: Wo Hop Shek, Ho Chung, San Wai, Fanling. Y. W. Lam 429, 837; HK sheet 39288.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Vietnam, India, Phillippines and Indonesia.
Ecology: Ditches and wet places. Flowering: Jun.–Jul.; fruiting: Aug.– Oct.

Polygonum glabrum Willd. 光蓼
Sp. Pl. 2: 477. 1799; FHK 288. 1861; FKH 217. 1912; FHN 1: 389. 1964; FTW ed. 2, 2: 301. 1996; FRPS 25: 21. 1998; FGD 4: 90. 2000; FOC 5: 288. 2003.

Annual glabrous herb, 70 –100 cm tall, glabrous throughout. Stems erect, reddish brown, weekly branched. Leaves alternate; petioles 8–10 mm, rather thick; leaf blade lanceolate to oblong-lanceolate, 8–20 × 1.5–3 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, margin entire. Ocrea tubular, scarious, 1–3 cm, apex truncate, without hairs. Racemes spikes-like, 4 –12 cm, forming terminal or axilllary panicles. Bracts weakly funnel-form, glabrous, apex truncate, each embracing 3– 4 flowers. Pedicels very short. Perianth 3– 4 mm, deeply 5-lobed; segments elliptic, apex rounded, white or pink. Stamens 6 –8. Ovary subglobose; styles 3-cleft below middle. Achenes ovoid, 1.5 –2 mm, convex on both sides, dark brown to black, smooth and shining.

Locality: Ta Kwu Ling, Sheung Shui. W. J. Tutcher 11451; Y. W. Lam 392.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Hubei, Fujian; India, Myanmar, Thailand, Vietnam, Phillippines, Africa and America.
Ecology: Ditches and other wet places. Flowering: Jun.–Aug.; fruiting: Jul.–Sep.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Ho Chung, Fanling, Wo Hop Shek, Sai Wan
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Polygonum hastatosagittatum Makino 長葉箭蓼
Makino 長葉箭蓼
Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 17: 119. 1903; Sam., Symb. Sin. 7: 182. 1929; FTW ed. 2, 2: 301. 1996; FRPS 25: 80. 1998; FGD 4: 88, fig. 58. 2000; FYN 11: 314. 2000; FOC 5: 315. 2003.

Annual herb, 40 –90 cm tall. Stems erect or ascending from the prostrate base, longitudinally ribbed, armed with short, retrorse prickles on the ribs. Leaves alternate; petioles 1–2.5 cm, with retrorse prickles; leaf blade lanceolate or elliptic, 3– 8(–10) × 1–2(–3) cm, base sagittate or almost hastate, apex acute to acuminate, margin shortly ciliate, adaxially glabrous or puberulous, abaxially prickly on midvein, and sometimes with stellate hairs. Ocrea tubular, 1.5–2 cm, scarious, apex truncate, long-ciliate. Racemes spike-like, 1–2.5 cm, forming terminal or axillary panicles. Peduncles densely pubescent and mixed with glandular hairs. Bracts broadly elliptic or ovate, 2.5 –3 mm, ciliate, usually each embracing 2 flowers. Pedicels 4– 6 mm, densely covered with glandular hairs. Perianth pink, 3– 4 mm, deeply 5-lobed; segments broadly elliptic. Stamens 7–8. Ovary ovoid; styles deeply 3-cleft, stigmas capitate. Achenes ovoid, 3-ribbed, 3 – 4 mm, dark brown and shining, enclosed in persistent perianth.

Locality: Ho Chung, Fanling, Wo Hop Shek, Sai Wan. P. S. Choi 163; W. J. Tutcher 8138; Y. S. Lam 814.
Distribution: Widely distributed from S to NE China; also in Siberia, Korea and Japan.
Ecology: Wet places near ponds and ditches. Flowering: Aug.–Sep.; fruiting: Sep.– Oct.

Polygonum hydropiper L. 水蓼
Sp. Pl. 361. 1753; FHK 288. 1861; FKH 218. 1912; FHN 1: 391. 1964; FTW ed. 2, 2: 302, pl. 146. 1996; FRPS 25: 27, pl. 6.: 3 – 4. 1998; FGD 4: 95. 2000; FYN 11: 351. 2000; FOC 5: 291. 2003.

Annual herb, 0.3–1.3 m tall. Stems erect or ascending, much branched, glabrous. Leaves alternate; petioles 4 – 8 mm; leaf blade lanceolate to elliptic-lanceolate, 4–8 × 0.5–2.5 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, margin entire, ciliate, glabrous or sometimes with appressed hairs on midvein, with glandular dots on both surfaces. Ocrea tubular, 1–1.5 cm, scarious, sparsely strigose, apex truncate, shortly ciliate. Racemes spike-like, 3–8(–15) cm, terminal or in axils of upper leaves. Bracts funnel-form, 2–3 mm, green, margin scarious, sparsely ciliate, each embracing 3–5 flowers. Pedicels longer than the bracts. Perianth 3–3.5 mm, deeply 5(–4)-lobed; segments elliptic, pink or white, with translucent glandular dots. Stamens 5, rarely 8, included. Ovary elliptic-triangular; styles 2–3-cleft; stigmas capitate. Achenes ovoid, 3-ribbed, 2–3 mm, punctate, enclosed in persistent perianth.

Locality: Lai Chi Kok, Sha Tin. H. C. Tang 1911; S. P. Lau 111.
Distribution: Widely distributed from S to N China; Korea, Japan, India, Malesia, Europe and N America.
Ecology: Ditches, rice-fields and other wet places. Flowering: May–Sep.; fruiting: Jun.– Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Kwai Chung, Shan Liu, Ha Tsuen, Tung Chung
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Polygonum japonicum Meisn. 日本蓼（蠶繭蓼）
Prodr. 14(1): 112. 1856; FKH 218. 1912; FTW ed. 2, 2: 302. 1998; FRPS 25: 19. 1998; FGD 4: 94. 2000; FYN 11: 344. 2000; FOC 5: 287. 2003.

Perennial herb, 50 –100 cm tall, with creeping rhizomes. Stems erect, usually pink, glabrous or sometimes sparsely and shortly strigose. Leaves alternate; petioles very short or almost obsolete; leaf blade lanceolate, 7–15 × 1–2 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, margin entire, bristly ciliate, sparsely and shortly strigose on both surfaces, especially on the midvein. Ocrea tubular, scarious, 1.5–2 cm, strigose, apex truncate, fringed with long (1–1.2 cm) hairs. Racemes spikes-like, 6 –12 cm, forming terminal or axillary panicles. Bracts funnel-form, glabrous, upper part pink, ciliate, each embracing 3–6 flowers. Pedicels 2.5–4. Flowers unisexual (plant dioecious). Perianth white or pink, 2.5–3 mm, deeply 5-lobed; segments elliptic. Stamens 8 in male flowers. In female flower ovary ovoid; styles 2–3-cleft. Achenes ovoid, 3-ribbed or convex on both sides, 1.5 –2 mm, black and shining, enclosed in persistent perianth.

Locality: Kwai Chung, Shan Liu, Ha Tsuen, Tung Chung. Y. W. Lam 374, 867, 902.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Yunnan, Xizang, Hunan, Hubei, Henan, Shaanxi, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Shandong, Fujian, Taiwan; Korea, Japan.
Ecology: Wet places and on grasslands of valleys. Flowering: Aug.– Oct.; fruiting: Sep.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Ng Tung Chai, Tai Om, Lin Au, Ho Pui
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Polygonum jucundum Meisn. 愉悅蓼
Monogr. Polyg. 71. 1826; FKH 218. 1912; FRPS 25: 34. 1998; FGD 4: 94. 2000; FYN 11: 354. 2000; FOC 5: 293. 2003.

Annual herb, 50–100 cm tall. Stems much branched, erect from the prostrate base, glabrous. Leaves alternate; petioles 3–6 mm; leaf blade oblong-lanceolate, 3 –10 × 1–2.5 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, margin entire, shortly ciliate, sparsely strigose or glabrescent on both surface. Ocrea tubular, scarious, 0.5 –1 cm, sparsely strigose, apex truncate, ciliate. Racemes spike-like, 3 – 6 cm, densely flowered, terminal or in axils of upper leaves. Bracts funnel-form, green, ciliate, each embracing 3–5 flowers. Pedicels 4–6 mm. Perianth 2.5 –3.5 mm, deeply 5-lobed; segments oblong, pink or white. Stamens 7– 8. Ovary ovoid; styles 3-cleft below middle. Achenes ovoid, 3-ribbed, ca. 2.5 mm, black and shining, enclosed in persistent perianth.

Locality: Ng Tung Chai, Tai Om, Lin Au, Ho Pui. B. Gloria s.n. (HK sheet 32369); Y. W. Lam 449; Y. S. Lau 2433.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Gansu, Shaanxi, Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Fujian.
Ecology: Wet places near ditches, and grassy slopes. Flowering: Aug.–Sep.; fruiting: Sep.–Nov.

Polygonum tenellum Blume var. karagoeanum (Makino) G. Murata 柔莖蓼
Acta Phytotax. Geobot. 26 (3–4): 88. 1974; FYN 11: 353. 2000.
Polygonum micranthum Meisn., Ann. Mus. Bot. Lugduno-Batavum 2: 59. 1865; FTW ed. 2, 2: 305. 1996.
Polygonum tenellum var. micranthum (Meisn.) C. Y. Wu, Index Fl. Yunnan. 1: 282. 1984; FRPS 25: 33. 1998.
Polygonum kawagoeanum Makino, Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 28: 115. 1914; FOC 5: 293. 2003.
Polygonum minus auct. non Huds.: FKH 218. 1912; FHN 1: 390. 1964; FGD 4: 93. 2000.

Annual herb, 20 – 50 cm tall. Stems slender, ascending from the prostrate base, glabrous, reddish brown. Leaves alternate; petioles very short; leaf blade linear-lanceolate to narrowly lanceolate, 3–6 × 0.4–0.8 cm, base usually rounded, apex acute, margin entire, ciliate, sparsely pubescent on both surface or glabrescent, but strigose along midvein. Ocrea tubular, 8 –10 mm, scarious, sparsely strigose, longciliate. Racemes spike-like, 2–3 cm, densely flowered, terminal or in axils of upper leaves. Bracts funnel-form, ciliate, each embracing 2– 4 flowers. Perianth 1–1.5 mm, deeply 5-lobed; segments elliptic, pink or white. Stamens 5 – 6. Ovary ovoid; styles 2-cleft, stigmas capitate. Achenes ovoid, 1–1.5 mm, flat, but rather thick, concave on both sides, black and shining, enclosed in persistent perianth.

Locality: Tai Kwu Ling. W. J. Tutcher 5269; Y. W. Lam 393.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, India, Malesia.
Ecology: Wet places near rice-fields, and valleys. Flowering: May–Sep.; fruiting: Jun.– Oct.
Notes: The specimen W. J. Tutcher 5269 was reported as Polygonum longisetum var. rotundatum A. J. Li in Check List of Hong Kong Plants (2002, 2004).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tsuen Wan, Sha Tin, Ha Tsuen, Ta Kwu Ling, Sheung Shui
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Polygonum lapathifolium L. 大馬蓼
Sp. Pl. 360. 1753; FHK 288. 1861; FKH 217. 1912; FHN 1: 388, fig. 205. 1964; FTW ed. 2, 2: 304, photo 127. 1996; FRPS 25: 23. 1998; FGD 4: 93. 2000; FYN 11: 347. 2000; FOC 5: 289. 2003.

Annual herb, 0.5 –2 m tall. Stems erect, glabrous, with longitudinal furrows, nodes tumid. Leaves alternate; petioles 0.2– 1 cm, shortly strigose; leaf blade lanceolate to broadly lanceolate, 6–15 × 1–3.5 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate or acute, margin entire, ciliate, strigose on midvein, usually with crescent-shaped, dark blotches on adaxial surface. Ocrea tubular, 1.5–3 cm, scarious, light brown, glabrous, apex truncate, not ciliate or slightly hairy. Racemes spikes-like, 2–6 cm, densely flowered, terminal or in axils of upper leaves. Peduncle simple, rarely branched, with glandular hairs. Bracts funnel-form, sparsely ciliate. Perianth ca. 2 mm, 4 (–5)- lobed; segments elliptic, pink or white. Stamens usually 6. Ovary compressed ovoid; styles 2-cleft. Achenes broadly ovoid, 1.5–2 mm, flat, but rather thick, concave on both sides, black and shining.

Locality: Tsuen Wan, Sha Tin, Ha Tsuen, Ta Kwu Ling, Sheung Shui. L. T. Lo 576; Y. W. Lam 1351; HK sheet 39381.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; also in Mongolia, Korea, Japan, Philippines, India and Parkistan.
Ecology: Roadsides, wastelands and other wet places. Flowering: Jun.–Aug.; fruiting: Jul.–Sep.

Polygonum lapathifolium L. var. salicifolium Sibth. 綿毛酸模葉蓼
Fl. Oxon. 129. 1794; FRPS 25: 24. 1998; FGD 4: 93. 2000; FYN 11: 348. 2000; FOC 5: 290. 2003.

It differs from the type variety by the leaves densely covered with cottony-white hairs abaxially.

Locality: Lai Chi Kok, Sha Tin. S. P. Lau 109; Y. S. Lau 249.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; also in Mongolia, Korea, Japan, Philippines, India and Parkistan.
Ecology: Wet places. Flowering: Jun.–Aug.; fruiting: Jul.–Sep.

Polygonum longisetum Bruijn 長鬃蓼
Pl. Jungh. 307. 1854; Meisn. in DC. Prodr. 14(1): 10. 1856; FKH 218. 1912; FTW ed. 2, 2: 304. 1996; FRPS 25: 30. 1996; FGD 4: 94. 2000; FYN 11: 352. 2000; FOC 5: 292. 2003.

Annual herb, 25–60 cm tall. Stems erect from the prostrate base, glabrous, nodes tumid. Leaves alternate; petioles very short; leaf blade lanceolate to broadly lanceolate, 4 – 8(–15) × 1–2.5 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, margin entire, ciliate, adaxial surface subglabrous, abaxial surface with short hairs on veins. Ocrea tubular, 5–10 mm, sparsely pubescent, apex truncate, fringed with long (6 –7 mm) bristles. Racemes spike-like, 2–5 cm, terminal or in axils of upper leaves. Peduncles glabrous. Bracts funnel-form, sparsely ciliate, each embracing 3–6 flowers. Perianth ca. 2.5 mm, deeply 5-lobed; segments elliptic, pink or purplish. Stamens 6–8. Ovary ovoid; styles 3-cleft, stigmas capitate. Achenes broadly ovoid, ca. 2 mm, 3-ribbed, black and shining, enclosed in persistent perianth.

Locality: Tai Tam Reservior. L. T. Lo 569.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China, except Gansu, Xinjiang, and Xizang; Korea, Japan, Myanmar, India, Malesia, Philippines.
Ecology: Valleys and grasslands by streams. Flowering: Jun.–Aug.; fruiting: Jul.–Sep.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Shatin, Tai Om, Ho Pui, Kuk Po
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Polygonum muricatum Meisn. 小花蓼
Monogr. Polyg. 74. 1826; FTW ed. 2, 2: 306. 1996; FRPS 25: 78, pl. 18: 1– 4. 1998; FGD 4: 87. 2000; FYN 11: 314. 2000; FOC 5: 314. 2003.

Annual herb, 80 –100 cm tall. Stems erect or ascending from the prostrate base, longitudinally ribbed, sparsely armed with retrorse prickles on the ribs. Leaves alternate; petioles 0.7–2 cm, sparsely and shortly prickled; leaf blade broadly ovate to oblong-ovate, 2.5–6 × 1.5 –3 cm, base broadly truncate, rounded or subcordate, apex acuminate or acute, margin entire, densely and shortly ciliate, usually glabrous to sparsely pubescent, or rarely with stellate hairs on adaxial surface, pubescent and with short stellate hairs on abaxial surface, with short retrorse prickles or bristles on midvein. Ocrea tubular, scarious, glabrous, 1–2 cm, apex truncate, long-ciliate. Racemes spikelike, very short, forming terminal or axillary panicles. Peduncles densely pubescent and mixed with some glandular hairs. Bracts broadly elliptic or ovate, apex acute to acuminate, ciliate, each embracing 2 flowers. Pedicels ca. 2 mm. Perianth white or pink, 2–3 mm, deeply 5-lobed; segments broadly elliptic. Stamens usually 6– 8. Ovary ovoid; styles 3; stigmas capitate. Achenes ovoid, 3-ribbed, 2–2.5 mm, yellowish brown, shining, enclosed in persistent perianth.

Locality: Shatin, Tai Om, Ho Pui, Kuk Po. L. T. Lo 545, 587; Y. W. Lam 560, 2163.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Jiangxi, Hubei, Anhui, Zhejiang, Jilin, Heilongjiang; Korea, Japan, India, Nepal, Thailand.
Ecology: Wet places by streams and rice-fields. Flowering: Jul.–Aug.; fruiting: Sep.– Oct.

Polygonum orientale L. 紅蓼（紅草）
Sp. Pl. 362. 1753; FHK 288. 1861; FKH 218. 1912; FHN 1: 389. 1964; FTW ed. 2, 2: 306. 1996; FRPS 25: 24. 1998; FGD 4: 92. 2000; FYN 11: 348, pl. 96: 1–3. 2000; FOC 5: 290. 2003.

Annual herb, 1–2(–3) m tall. Stems erect, much branched, densely pilose. Leaves alternate; petioles 2– 5(–10) cm, pilose; leaf blade ovate to broadly ovate or ovate-lanceolate, 10 –20 × 6 –12 cm, base subrounded or slightly cordate, ± decurrent, apex acuminate, margin entire, ciliate, pubescent on both surfaces and densely pilose on veins. Ocrea tubular, 1–2 cm, scarious, densely pubescent, upper margin enlarged and foliaceous, with long hairs. Racemes spike-like, 3 –7 cm, densely flowered, terminal or in axils of upper leaves. Peduncles pubescent. Bracts broadly funnel-form, 3 – 5 mm, herbaceous, green, puberulous, upper margin with long hairs, each embracing 3 – 5 flowers. Pedicels longer than the bracts. Perianth 3 – 4 mm, deeply 5-lobed; segments elliptic, pink or white. Stamens usually 7. Ovary compressed ovoid; styles 2-cleft below middle; nectaries present. Achenes subglobose, flat, 2–3.5 mm in diam., enclosed in persistent perianth.

Locality: Sha Po, Yuen Long. Y. W. Lam 1269; HK sheet 4585.
Distribution: Widely dispersed over all provinces of China except Xizang; Japan, India, Malesia and Australia; widely cultivated and naturalized elsewhere.
Ecology: Wet places near villages. Flowering: Jun.–Sep.; fruiting: Aug.– Oct.
Uses: Ornamental.

Polygonum perfoliatum L. 杠板歸（貫葉蓼）
Syst. Nat. (ed. 10) 1006. 1759; Sp. Pl. ed. 2, 521. 1762; FHK 289. 1861; FKH 218. 1912; FHN 1: 393, fig. 206. 1964; FTW ed. 2, 2: 307, photo 129. 1996; FRPS 25: 68, pl. 15: 1– 4. 1998; FGD 4: 86. 2000; FYN 11: 309, pl. 88: 2. 2000; FOC 5: 311. 2003.

Annual herb. Stems climbing or twining, much branched, angled and armed with retrorse prickles. Leaves peltate; petioles 3 –7 cm, with retrorse prickles; leaf blade deltoid, 2–7(–10) × 2– 6(– 8) cm, base truncate or slightly cordate, apex obtuse or ± acute, adaxially glabrous, abaxially with retrose prickles on veins. Ocrea foliaceous, green, orbicular, perfoliate, 1.5 –3 cm in diam. Racemes spike-like, 3 – 5 cm, terminal or in axils of upper leaves. Peduncles prickly, 2–4 cm. Bracts ovate-elliptic, glabrous, apex acute, each embracing 2– 4 flowers. Perianth ca. 3 mm, deeply 5‑lobed; segments elliptic, 2–3 mm, white or pink, becoming fleshy and blue in fruit. Stamens 8; styles deeply 3-cleft; stigmas capitate; nectaries present. Achenes globose, 3– 4 mm in diam., black and shining, enclosed in the fleshy persistent perianth.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 667, 1393; L. T. Lo 57.
Distribution: Dispersed over all parts of China. Widely distributed in E Asia, India Subcontinent, Malesia; naturalized in N America.
Ecology: Roadsides, wastelands and other wet places. Flowering: Jun.–Aug.; fruiting: Jul.– Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Polygonum posumbu Buch.-Ham. ex D. Don 叢枝蓼
Prodr. Fl. Nep. 71. 1825; FKH 218. 1912; FTW ed. 2, 2: 308. 1996; FRPS 25: 29. 1998; FGD 4: 94. 2000; FYN 11: 352. 2000; FOC 5: 291. 2003.

Annual herb, 30–70(–100) cm tall. Stems slender, ascending from the prostrate base, glabrous, with longitudinal furrows. Leaves alternate; petioles 5–7 mm, shortly strigose; leaf blade ovate-lanceolate to ovate, 3 – 6 × 1–3 cm, base broadly cuneate, apex caudate, margin entire, ciliate, sparsely covered with rigid, appressed hairs on both surface or glabrescent. Ocrea tubular, 4–6 mm, scarious, with appressed hairs, apex truncate, ciliate. Racemes spike-like, 4–12 cm, terminal or in axils of upper leaves. Bracts funnel-form, light green, glabrous, ciliate, each embracing 2– 4 flowers. Perianth 2–2.5 mm, deeply 5-lobed; segments elliptic, pink. Stamens 8. Ovary ovoid; styles 3-cleft, stigmas capitate. Achenes ovoid, 3-ribbed, 2–2.5 mm, dark brown to black, enclosed in the persistent perianth.

Locality: Sha Tau Kok. Ross 11452; Y. W. Lam 2214.
Distribution: Dispersed over all parts of China, except Xinjiang and Xizang; Korea, Japan, India and Malesia.
Ecology: Margins of forests in valleys and wet places. Flowering: May–Sep.; fruiting: Jun.– Oct.

Polygonum praetermissum Hook. f. 疏蓼
Fl. Brit. Ind. 5: 47. 1886; FTW ed. 2, 2: 309. 1996; FRPS 25: 73, pl. 16: 1. 1998; FYN 11: 312. 2000; FOC 5: 312. 2003.

Annual herb, 30–90 cm tall. Stems ascending from the prostrate base, sparsely armed with retrorse prickles. Leaves alternate; petioles prickly, 0.5 –1 cm, or almost sessile in the leaves near apex of stem; leaf blade lanceolate to narrowly oblong, 4 – 8 × 0.5 –1.5 cm, base hastate to sagittate, apex obtuse or acute, glabrous or sparsely pubescent on both surfaces, abaxially with prickles on midvein. Ocrea tubular, 1–1.5 cm, scarious, apex oblique, glabrous or bristly on the veins, usually ciliate. Spikes 2– 5 cm, sparsely flowered, terminal or in axils of upper leaves. Peduncles dichotomous branching, glandular pubescent. Bracts funnel-form, each embracing 2–4 flowers. Perianth pink, 3 – 4 mm, deeply 4-lobed; segments broadly elliptic. Stamens 4– 5, included. Ovary subglobose; styles deeply 3-cleft. Achenes subglobose, obscurely 3-ribbed, ca. 3 mm, dark brown, enclosed in persistent perianth.

Locality: Tai O, Ping Chau. Y. W. Lam 995, 996, 2161.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Jiangsu; Korea, Japan, India, Philippines.
Ecology: Wet places by streams and ditches. Flowering: Jun.–Aug.; fruiting: Jul.–Sep.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Sai Kung, Sheung Shui, Tai Kwu Ling
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Polygonum pubescens Blume 伏毛蓼（短毛蓼）
Bijdr. 2: 532. 1825; FTW ed. 2, 2: 309, photo 131. 1996; FRPS 25: 29, pl. 4: 4 – 5. 1998; FGD 4: 88, fig. 57. 2000; FYN 11: 351. 2000; FOC 5: 291. 2003.

Annual herb, 70–100 cm tall. Stems erect, much branched, sparsely strigose, often reddish. Leaves alternate; petioles 4–7 mm, densely strigose; leaf blade ovate-lanceolate or broadly lanceolate, 5–10 × 1–2.5 cm, base broadly cuneate, apex acuminate or acute, margin entire, ciliate, densely strigose on both surface, with dark blotches on the center of adaxial surface. Ocrea tubular, 1–1.5 cm, scarious, strigose, apex truncate, long-ciliate. Racemes spike-like, 7–15 cm, terminal or in axils of upper leaves. Bracts green, funnel-form, margin scarious, ciliate, each embracing 3–4 flowers. Perianth 3–4 mm, deeply 5-lobed; segments elliptic, green, upper part pink. Stamens 8, included. Ovary ovoid; styles 3-cleft, stigmas capitate. Achenes ovoid, 3-ribbed, 2.5–3 mm, black, enclosed in persistent perianth.

Locality: Sai Kung, Sheung Shui, Tai Kwu Ling. L. T. Lo 577; Y. W. Lam 394; HK sheet 9902.
Distribution: Dispersed over all parts of China except dry regions in NW; also in Korea, Japan, India, Malesia.
Ecology: Wet places by streams, ditches and rice-fields. Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: Jul.–Sep.

Polygonum senticosum (Meisn.) Franch. & Sav. 刺蓼（廊茵）
Enum. Pl. Jap. 1: 401. 1875; FKH 218. 1912; FTW ed. 2, 2: 311, photo 133. 1996; FRPS 25: 71, pl. 15: 5 – 8. 1998; FGD 4: 87. 2000; FOC 5: 312. 2003.

Annual herb. Stems climbing or twining, much branched, 1–1.5 m or longer, quadragular, pubescent and with retrorse prickles along the angles. Leaves alternate; petioles 2–7 cm, with retrorse prickles; leaf blade deltoid or triangular hastate, 4 – 8 × 2–7 cm, base cordate to hastate, apex acute or acuminate, pubescent on both surfaces, with retrorse prickles on veins abaxially. Ocrea tubular, margin winged; wings reniform, herbaceous and green, shortly ciliate. Racemes head-like, terminal or in axils of upper leaves. Peduncles densely glandular pubescent, 2–5 cm. Bracts oblong-ovate, light green, margin scarious, shortly ciliate, each embracing 2–3 flowers. Perianth pink, 3 – 4 mm, deeply 5-lobed; segments elliptic. Stamens 8, in 2 whorls, included. Ovary 3-angled; styles deeply 3-cleft; stigmas capitate. Achenes globose, 2.5–3 mm, obscurely 3-ribbed, dark brown, enclosed in the fleshy persistent perianth.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Hunan, Hubei, Henan, Hebei, Heilongjiang, Liaoning, Jilin, Shandong, Jiangsu, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian.
Ecology: Forests of valleys. Flowering: Jun.–Jul.; fruiting: Jul.–Sep.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Shau Kei Wan, Mai Po, Mo Fan Heung, Ta Kwu Ling, Lamma Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Polygonum strigosum R. Br. 糙毛蓼
Prodr. Fl. Nov. Holl. 420. 1810; FKH 218. 1912; FRPS 25: 77, pl. 16: 2–3. 1998; FGD 4: 88. 2000; FYN 11: 313. 2000; FOC 5: 314. 2003.
Polygonum bodinieri Lével. & Van., Bull. Acad. Int. Geogr. Bot. 11: 343. 1902; FKH 218. 1912.

Perennial herb, 50 –100 cm tall. Stems erect or prostrate at base, longitudinally ribbed, with retrorse prickles on the ribs. Leaves alternate; petioles 1–3 cm, with retrorse prickles; leaf blade oblong or lanceolate, 6 –10 × 1–3.5 cm, base sub-cordate to truncate, sometimes sagittate, apex acuminate or acute, ciliate on margins, glabrous or sparsely strigose adaxially, with retrorse prickles on midvein abaxially. Ocrea tubular, 1.5 –3 cm, scarious, apex truncate, fringed with long (ca. 5 mm) hairs. Racemes spike-like, 2– 5 cm, forming terminal or axillary panicles. Peduncles densely pubescent and mixed with some glandular hairs. Bracts elliptic or ovate, 2–3 mm, usually strigose, each embracing 2–3 flowers. Perianth white or pink, 2– 4 mm, deeply 5-lobed; segments elliptic. Stamens 5 –7, included. Ovary broadly ovoid; styles deeply 2–3-cleft; stigmas capitate. Achenes subglobose, ca. 3 mm, 3-ribbed or convex on both sides, dark brown, not shining, enclosed in the persistent perianth.

Locality: Shau Kei Wan, Mai Po, Mo Fan Heung, Ta Kwu Ling, Lamma Island. W. J. Tutcher 11176; Y. W. Lam 1743; HK sheet 33196.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Fujian; Nepal, India, Indochina, Malesia, Philippines.
Ecology: Wet places in forests and valleys. Flowering: Aug.–Sep.; fruiting: Sep.– Oct.

Polygonum tinctorium Ait. 蓼藍
Hort. Kew. 2: 31. 1789; FKH 217. 1912; FHN 1: 390. 1964; FRPS 25: 26. 1998; FGD 4: 91. 2000; FYN 11: 349. 2000; FOC 5: 290. 2003.

Annual herb, 50–80(–90) cm tall. Stems erect, weekly branched, glabrescent. Leaves alternate; petioles 5–10 mm; leaf blade ovate or broadly elliptic, 3–8 × 2–4 cm, base broadly cuneate, apex rounded, margin entire, shortly ciliate, glabrous adaxially, sometimes sparsely hairy on veins of abaxial surfaces, dark blue-green when dry. Ocrea tubular, 1–1.5 cm, scarious, covered with appressed hairs, apex truncate, fringed with long hairs. Racemes spike-like, 2–5 cm, terminal or in axils of upper leaves. Bracts funnel-form, green, ciliate, each embracing 3–5 flowers. Pedicels slender, subequal to bracts. Perianth 2.5–3 mm, deeply 5-lobed; segments ovate, pink or purplish, apex acute. Stamens 6–8, included. Ovary ovate-ellipsoid; styles 3-cleft. Achenes broadly ovoid, 3-ribbed, 2–2.5 mm, brown and shining, enclosed in persistent perianth.

Locality: Sai Wan. HK sheet 9906.
Distribution: Dispersed over all parts of China; cultivated or naturalized.
Ecology: Flowering: Aug.–Sep.; fruiting: Aug.– Oct.
Uses: Materials (tannin, dyestuff).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Authority: (Buch.-Ham. ex D. Don) H. Gross ex Nakai
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Po Kau, Fanling, Sai Kung
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Polygonum viscosum Buch.-Ham. ex D. Don 黏毛蓼（香蓼）
Prodr. Fl. Nep. 71. 1825; FHK 287. 1861; FKH 217. 1912; FTW ed. 2, 2: 312. 1996; FRPS 25: 21. 1998; FGD 4: 92. 2000; FYN 11: 346. 2000; FOC 5: 288. 2003.

Annual aromatic herb, 50–90 cm tall. Stems erect or ascending, much branched, densely covered with harsh long hairs and glandular hair. Leaves alternate; petioles 1–2 cm; leaf blade ovate-lanceolate to elliptic-lanceolate, 4–15 × 1–4 cm, base cuneate, decurrent to the petioles, apex acuminate, margin entire, densely short-ciliate, densely hirsute on both surfaces, especially on the veins. Ocrea tubular, 1–1.2 cm, densely covered with glandular and harsh hairs, apex truncate, with long hairs. Racemes spikes-like, 2–5 cm, forming terminal or axillary panicle. Peduncles 2–5 cm. Bracts funnel-form, as is the peduncle densely covered with glandular and harsh hairs, apex acute, sparsely ciliate, each embracing 3– 5 flowers. Pedicels longer than bracts. Perianth ca. 3 mm, deeply 5-lobed; segments elliptic, pink or purplish. Stamens 8. Ovary ovoid; styles 3-cleft; stigmas capitate. Achenes triangular, 1.5–2 mm, black, smooth, and shining.

Locality: Tai Po Kau, Fanling, Sai Kung. Y. S. Lau 269, 949.
Distribution: Dispersed over all parts of China except dry regions in NW; also in Russia (far east), Korea, Japan, India.
Ecology: Wet places on roadsides and in ditches. Flowering: Jul.–Sep.; fruiting: Aug.– Oct.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Fanling, Tai Po, Wu Kau Tang, Mui Wo
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Polygonum plebeium R. Br. 腋花蓼（習見蓼）
Prodr. Fl. Nov. Holl. 420. 1810; FHK 287. 1861; FKH 217. 1912; FHN 1: 388. 1964; FTW ed. 2, 2: 308. 1996; FRPS 25: 11, pl. 1: 1–3. 1998; FGD 4: 89, fig. 59. 2000; FYN 11: 309. 2000; FOC 5: 285. 2003.

Annual herb. Stems prostrate, branched from the base, 10 – 40 cm, internodes usually shorter than leaves. Leaves subsessile or with a very short petiole; leaf blade narrowly elliptic or oblanceolate, 5 –15 × 2– 4 mm, base narrowly cuneate, apex obtuse or acute, glabrous on both surfaces; lateral veins obscure. Ocrea tubular, 2.5–3 mm, white and translucent, apex lacerate. Flowers 3– 6 in axillary clusters. Pedicels slender, 1–2 mm, articulate at middle. Bracts scarious. Perianth green, margin white or pink, 1–1.5 mm, deeply 5-lobed; segments elliptic. Stamens 5; filaments slightly dilated at base, included. Ovary 3-angled; styles 3 rarely 2, very short; stigmas capitate. Achenes broadly ovoid, 1.5 –2 mm, sharply 3-ribbed or convex on both sides, blackish brown, smooth and shining, enclosed in the fleshy persistent perianth.

Locality: Fanling, Tai Po, Wu Kau Tang, Mui Wo. Y. S. Lau 2450; HK sheet 9932, 32384.
Distribution: Dispersed over all parts of China except Xizang; also in Japan, India, Australia, Europe and Africa.
Ecology: Cultivated and in waste places. Flowering: May–Aug.; fruiting: Jun.–Sep.

Polygonum cuspidatum Siebold & Zucc. 虎杖
Abh. Math.-Phys. Cl. Konigl. Bayer. Akad. Wiss. 4: 208. 1846; FTW ed. 2, 2: 299, photo 126. 1996; FGD 4: 90. 2000.
Reynoutria japonica Houtt., Nat. Hist. 2(8): 640, t. 51, f. 1. 1777; FRPS 25: 105, pl. 22: 1–3. 1998; FYN 11: 359, pl. 98: 1–3. 2000; FOC 5: 319. 2003.

Perennial stout herb, with creeping rhizomes. Stems erect, fistulous, 1–2 m tall, glabrous, with scattered red or reddish purple dots, woody at base. Leaves alternate; petioles 1–2 mm, papillose; leaf blade broadly ovate to ovate-elliptic, 5 –12 × 4 –9 cm, base broadly cuneate, truncate or subrounded, apex acuminate, margin entire, glabrous, papillose on veins. Ocrea tubular, scarious, 0.3 –1 cm, apex oblique, glabrous, usually caducous. Inflorescence paniculate, axillary, 3 – 8 cm. Peduncles papillose. Bracts funnel-form, 1.5 –2 mm, apex acuminate, eciliate, each embracing 2– 4 flowers. Pedicels 2– 4 mm, articulate at the lower part. Flowers unisexual (plant dioecious); perianth light green, 2–3 mm, deeply 5-lobed. Male flowers: perianth-segments with green midvein, not winged; stamens 8, exserted; female flowers: the outer 3 perianth-segments winged dorsally; wings enlarged in fruit. Ovary ovoid; styles 3; stigmas fimbriate. Achenes ovoid, 3-ribbed, 4 – 5 mm, dark brown and shining, enclosed in the persistent perianth.

Locality: Castle Peak. Y. S. Lau 2167.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Gansu, Hunan, Hubei, Henan, Anhui, Jiangxi, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian; Korea, Japan.
Ecology: Valleys and other wet places. Flowering: Aug.–Sep.; fruiting: Sep.– Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), food (vegetable).

Rumex dentatus L. 齒果酸模
Mant. Pl. 2: 226. 1771; Forb. & Hemsl., J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 26: 356. 1891; Sam, Symb. Sin. 7: 168. 1929; FRPS 25: 161. 1996; FYN 11: 379, pl. 102: 6 –8. 2000; FOC 5: 339. 2003.

Annual herb. Stems erect, furrowed, 30–70 cm tall, branched from base; branches ascending. Petioles 1.5– 5 cm. Radical leaves oblong or oblong-elliptic, 4–12 × 1.5 –3 cm, base rounded or cordate, apex obtuse or acute, margin undulate; stem-leaves smaller, upwards gradually passing into bracts; ocrea tubular, 8 –15 mm, scarious, glabrous. Flowers bisexual, in many whorls, forming terminal or axillary panicles, to 35 cm. Perianth-segments 6, light green, outer ones elliptic, ca. 2 mm, inner ones enlarged in fruit, triangular ovate, 3.5 – 4 × 2–2.5 mm, with tubercles, apex acute, base sub-rounded, margin with 2–4 spine-like teeth on each side. Achenes ovoid, sharply 3-angled, 2– 2.5 mm, yellowish brown and shining.

Locality: Shatin. Y. S. Lau 2151.
Distribution: Spread over most parts of China; Nepal, India, Afghanistan, Kazakstan and SE Europe.
Ecology: Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: Sep.– Oct.

Rumex japonicus Houtt. 羊蹄
Nat. Hist. 2(8): 394. 1777; FRPS 25: 156, pl. 37: 3– 4. 1998; FYN 11: 376. 2000; FOC 5: 338. 2003.
Rumex crispus auct. non L.: FHK 286. 1861; FKH 218. 1912; FGD 4: 83. 2000.

Perennial herb, with thick root-stock. Stems erect, furrowed, 50 –100 cm tall. Radical leaves oblong to lanceolate-oblong, 8 – 20(–25) × 4– 8(–10) cm, base rounded or cordate, apex acute or obtuse, margin undulate, abaxially papillose on veins; petioles 2– 4 cm; stem-leaves smaller, narrowly oblong, shortly petiolate or sessile, upwards gradually passing into bracts; ocrea tubular, scarious, 1.5–2 cm, glabrous. Flowers bisexual, in many whorls, forming terminal panicles. Pedicels slender, 5 –10 mm. Perianthsegments 6, light green, outer ones elliptic, 1.5–2 mm, inner ones enlarged in fruit, broadly ovate, 4 – 5 mm, with tubercles, apex acuminate, base cordate, margin irregularly denticulate. Achenes broadly ovoid, sharply 3-angled, ca. 2.5 mm, dark brown and shining.

Locality: Tuen Mun. Y. S. Lau 2164, HK sheet 30751.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Jiangxi, Hunan, Hubei, Henan, Anhui, Shandong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Korea, Japan.
Ecology: Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: Jun.–Jul.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Rumex microcarpus Campd. 小果酸模
Monogr. Rum. 143. 1819; FRPS 25: 166. 1998; FGD 4: 83. 2000; FYN 11: 380. 2000; FOC 5: 341. 2003.
Rumex wallichii Meisn., DC. Prodr. 14(1): 48. 1856; FHN 1: 387. 1964.

Annual herb, 40– 80 cm tall. Stems erect, ± furrowed, glabrous, branched on the upper part. Radical leaves oblong-elliptic, 10–15 × 2– 5 cm, base cuneate, apex acute or slightly obtuse, margin entire; petioles 2–4 cm; stem-leaves smaller, narrowly elliptic; ocrea tubular, scarious, caducous. Flowers bisexual, in many whorls, forming terminal leafy panicles. Perianth-segments 6, yellowish green, outer ones lanceolate, ca. 1 mm, inner ones enlarged in fruit, narrowly triangular, 3 – 4 × 1.5 –2 mm, with tubercles, apex acute, base truncate, margin entire. Achenes ovoid, sharply 3-angled, 1–2 mm, brown and shining.

Locality: Lai Chi Kok. H. C. Tang 1912, 2468; Y. S. Lau 247.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Liaoning, Hebei, Jiangsu, Taiwan; Vietnam, India.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr.–Jul.; fruiting: May–Jul.

Rumex trisetifer Stokes 長刺酸模（假菠菜）
Bot. Mat. Med. 2: 305. 1814; FRPS 25: 161. 1998; FYN 11: 379, pl. 102: 4– 5. 2000; FOC 5: 340. 2003.
Rumex maritimus auct. non L.: FKH 218. 1912; FGD 4: 83. 2000.

Annual herb, 30 – 80 cm tall, with thick root-stock. Stems erect, brown to reddish brown, furrowed, glabrous. Petioles 1.5– 6 cm; Lower stem-leaves oblong to lanceolate-oblong, 8–20 × 2– 5 cm, base cuneate, apex acute, margin undulate; upper leaves smaller, narrowly lanceolate; ocrea tubular, 15–20 mm, scarious, caducous. Flowers bisexual, in many whorls, forming terminal or axillary panicles. Pedicels slender, 2– 6 mm, articulate near base. Perianth-segments 6, in 2 whorls, yellowish green, outer 3 smaller, lanceolate, inner ones enlarged in fruit, narrowly triangular ovate, 3 – 4 × 1.5 –2 mm, with tubercles, base truncate, apex acute, margin with 1 spine on each side. Achenes ellipsoid, sharply 3-angled, 1.5–2 mm, yellowish brown and shining.

Locality: Hong Kong Islands. Y. S. Lau 1807.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Jiangxi, Hunan, Hubei, Henan, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Indochina, Thailand, India.
Ecology: Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: Jun.–Jul.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Shatin, Sai Kung, Chek Keng, Tai Po, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Limonium sinense (Girad) Kuntze 補血草
Rev. Gen. Pl. 2: 396. 1891; FHN 3: 439, fig. 841. 1974; FRPS 60(1): 30, pl. 5: 5. 1987; FGD 3: 314, fig. 204. 1995; FOC 15: 199. 1996; FTW ed. 2, 4: 80, pl. 35, photo 50. 1998.
Statice sinensis Girad, Ann. Sci. Nat. 3, 2: 329. 1844; FHK 281. 1861; FKH 155. 1912.

Perennial herb, 15–50 cm tall, with thick tap root. Leaves in a basal rosette, obovate-oblanceolate or spatulate, 4–10 × 0.8–2 cm including petiole, apex obtuse or rounded, tapering from middle into the petiole, glabrous, margin entire. Spikes with 2–3 secund flowers, arranged in cymose panicle, terminal on scape; Bracteoles scarious, elliptic, 5–6 mm. Calyx funnel-form, 6–7 mm, with white hairs on ribs. Petals pale yellow, connate only at base, slightly longer than calyx. Stamens 5, inserted at the base of petals. Ovary obovate; style 5, filiform. Capsule cylindrical, ca. 3 mm long and 1 mm in diam.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Shatin, Sai Kung, Chek Keng, Tai Po, Lantau Island. H. C. Tang 757; C. Ford s.n. (HK sheet 2814); Y. S. Lau 557.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Taiwan, Fujian, Zhejiang, Jiangsu, Shandong, Hebei, Liaoning; Japan, Vietnam.
Ecology: Sandy grassy lands near seashore. Flowering: Almost all year round.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Sai Kung, Sha Kok Mei, San Tin, Castle Peak, Cheung Chau
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Plumbago zeylanica L. 白花丹
Sp. Pl. 151. 1753; FKH 156. 1912; FGZ 561, fig. 297. 1956; FRPS 60(1): 4, pl. 1: 1–2. 1987; FGD 3: 315. 1995; FOC 15: 191. 1996; FTW ed. 2, 4: 80, photo 51. 1998.

Semi-climbing subshrub, 1–2 cm tall. Leaves alternate, or sometimes in cluster of 3 on branches, ovate to ovate-elliptic, unequal, 3–10 × 2–2.5 cm, base broadly cuneate, ± decurrent, apex acute or acuminate; petioles often dilated in auricles and amplexicaul, usually with a few small leaves in axils. Spikes terminal and axillary, 8–17 cm, often branched; rhachis glandular; each flower subtended by 3 bracts. Calyx-tube ca. 11 cm, 5-ribbed, with glandular hairs. Corolla white or bluish; tube 17–20 mm; lobes elliptic or obovate, ca. 5 mm, spreading. Ovary oblong; style slender; stigma with 5 linear lobe. Capsule oblong, 5–7 mm, opening transversely.

Locality: Sai Kung, Sha Kok Mei, San Tin, Castle Peak, Cheung Chau. H. C. Tang 18; Y. S. Lau 2418; W. J. Tutcher s.n. (HK sheet 17239).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, S Guizhou, Sichuan, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; tropical Asia.
Ecology: Grassy lands and thickets. Flowering: Sep. to Mar. of the following year.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal (folklore).

Tetracera asiatica (Lour.) Hoogland 錫葉藤
Fl. Malesiana 1(4): 143. 1951; FHN 1: 446. 1964; FRPS 49(2): 191. 1984.
Segnieria asiatica Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 341. 1790.
Tetracera sarmentosa (L.) Vahl. subsp. asiatica (Lour.) Hoogland, Blumea 9: 588. 1959; FGD 3: 93. 1995.
Leontoglossum scabrum Hance, Ann. Bot. Syst. 2: 18. 1851.
Dilima sarmentosa auct. non L.: FHK 7. 1861; FKH 27. 1912.

Woody vine, 3 – 5 m or more; branches scabrous, strigose. Petioles 0.5–1.0 cm; pubescent or glabrescent; leaf blade leathery, obovate to broadly lanceolate, 3 –15 × 2–7 cm, base rounded or cuneate, apex acute or obtuse, margin entire or serrate-crenuate, scabrous on both surfaces; lateral veins 7–16 on each side of midvein, elevated abaxially.
