Inflorescence paniculate, terminal or axillary, many-flowered; flower white, ca. 8 –10 mm. in diam.; pedicels 1–5 mm; bracts and bracteoles linear, sparsely pubescent abaxially, margin ciliate; sepals 5, suborbicular, margin ciliate, sparsely pubescent abaxially, the outer two 2 × 1.5 mm, the inner three 4 × 3 mm; petals 3; ovate, ca. 3.5 × 2.5 mm, membranaceous, glabrous; stamens numerous, 3– 4 mm, filaments filiform, dilated at the distal end; anther-cells slightly separated at the apex; carpels 1(–2), with ca. 10–12 ovules, glabrous. Follicles ovoid, 6–10 × 4 – 6 mm with a 2– 5 mm long beak, 1(–2)-seeded. Seeds ovoid, black, ca. 4 × 3 mm with an up to 5 mm fringe-margined aril.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. L. T. Lo 108.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi; Thailand, Vietnam, Malesia.
Ecology: Thin forests on hillslopes and in ravines.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Pat Sin Leng, Nam Chung, Sze Tau Leng
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Adinandra glischroloma Hand.-Mazz. var. jubata (H. L. Li) Kobuski 長毛楊桐
J. Arnold Arbor. 28: 21. 1947.
Adinandra jubata Li, J. Arnold Arbor. 25: 422. 1944; FGD 2: 158. 1991.

Shrub or small tree, branchlets and terminal buds densely villose, with spreading tawny or rusty hairs. Leaves leathery; petioles 8–10 mm, densely hirsute; leaf blade oblong-elliptic, 8–13 × 2.5–4.5 cm, base cuneate, rarely rounded, apex acuminate, margin entire, dark green and glabrous adaxially, yellowish green and rusty-hirsute abaxially. Flowers white, axillary, 2–3 clustered, rarely solitary. Pedicel 0.5–1.5 cm, often recurved, densely hirsute; bracteoles 2, caducous. Sepals broadly ovate, 5–14 mm, apex acute, densely rusty hirtellous abaxially. Petals oblong or ovate-oblong, 8–15 × 4–6 mm, apex rounded, hirtellous abaxially. Stamens ca. 25, 5–9 mm; filaments glabrous; anthers linear, 2–4.5 mm, hispid, connective prolonged. Ovary ovoid, densely hirsute, 3-locular, many ovules per locule; style l, ca. 8 mm, densely hirsute. Fruit globose, black when mature, 0.8–1.3 cm in diam., densely hirsute.

Locality: Pat Sin Leng, Nam Chung, Sze Tau Leng. Y. W. Lam 243; F. W. Xing 8009; S. C. Ng 4486; K. L. Yip 4083.
Distribution: Guangdong, S Guangxi, S Fujian.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: May–Jun.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Authority: (Hook. & Arn.) Benth. & Hook. f. ex Hance
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Sai Kung, Tai Mong Tsai, Ma On Shan, Fanling, Tai Lam Chung, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Adinandra millettii (Hook. & Arn.) Benth. & Hook. f. ex Hance 黃瑞木
J. Bot. 16: 9. 1878; FKH 43. 1912; FGD 2: 158. 1991; FRPS 50(1): 48. 1998.
Cleyera millettii Hook. & Arn., Bot. Beechey Voy. 171, t. 33. 1841.

Shrub or small tree, 2–10 m tall; branchlets greyish brown, pubescent when young; terminal buds appressed pubescent. Leaves leathery; petioles 3 – 5 mm, sparsely pubescent, glabrescent ; leaf blade oblong-elliptic, 4 –9 × 2–3 cm, base cuneate, apex shortly acuminate, margin entire or sparsely serrate towards apex, glabrous and shining adaxially, paler, appressed pubescent or glabrescent abaxially. Flowers white, solitary, axillary. Pedicels slender, ca. 2 cm, sparsely pubescent or glabrescent; bracteoles linear-lanceolate, ca. 2 × 1 mm, caducous. Sepals ovate-lanceolate or ovate-triangular, 7– 8 × 4 – 5 mm, apex acute, margin ciliolate and glandular, sparsely pubescent or glabrescent abaxially. Petals ovate-oblong to oblong, ca. 9 × 4–5 mm, apex acute, glabrous. Stamens ca. 25, 6–7 mm; filaments ca. 3 mm, glabrous or white pubescent proximally; anthers linear-oblong, ca. 2 mm, hispid, connective prolonged. Ovary globose, pubescent, 3-locular, many ovules per locule. Style simple, 7–8 mm, glabrous. Fruit globose, pubescent, ca. 1 cm in diam., black when mature, many seeded.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Sai Kung, Tai Mong Tsai, Ma On Shan, Fanling, Tai Lam Chung, Lantau Island. L. T. Lo 109; Y. S. Lau 1409; K. L. Yip 4076.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian.
Ecology: Secondary forests and thickets. Flowering: Jul.

Anneslea fragrans Wall. var. hainanensis Kobuski 海南茶梨
J. Arnold Arbor. 33: 86. 1952; FHN 1: 503. 1964; FGD 2: 176. 1991; FRPS 50(1): 180. 1998.
Anneslea hainanensis (Kobuski) Hu, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 8: 265. 1963.

Evergreen tree, up to 15 m tall. Leaves leathery; petioles 2–3 cm; leaf blade oblong to elliptic, 7–15 × 3–7 cm, base cuneate to broadly cuneate, apex obtuse or rarely rounded, margin entire or sparsely serrate towards apex. Flowers in axillary clusters; pedicels 1–2 cm; bracteoles 2, broadly ovate to triangular-ovate, ca. 4 × 3 mm, margin sparsely glandular; sepals reddish, broadly ovate, 1–1.5 cm, glabrous, base slightly connate, apex rounded to obtuse, margin glandular; petals red or white, broadly ovate, 6 – 8 mm, connate at base; stamens ca. 40, ca. 1.5 mm; filaments connate at base; anthers linear, glabrous, connective prolonged; ovary half-inferior, 3-locular, glabrous; styles ca. 1.5 mm, 3-lobed. Fruit ovoid, 2–2.5 cm, 2–3-locular with 2–3 seeds per locule, indehiscent, wrapped by persistent enlarged sepals; carpopodium 2–4 cm. Seeds long obovate, 7–10 × 5 mm.

Locality: Ma On Shan. Y. W. Lam 218; F. W. Xing 6893; P. S. So 4.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Nov.–Dec.; fruiting: Jul.–Aug. of the following year.
Uses: Materials (timber).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Castle Peak, Victoria Peak, Ma On Shan, Tai Mo Shan
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Camellia caudata Wall. 長尾毛蕊茶
Pl. Asiat. Rar. 3: 36. 1832; FKH 46. 1912; FRPS 49(3): 192. 1998.
Thea caudata (Wall.) Seem., Trans. Linn. Soc. London 22: 348. 1859.
Theopsis caudata (Wall.) Hu, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 8: 266. 1963; FHN 1: 497. 1964.
Camellia assimilis Champ. ex Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 3: 309. 1851; FHK 30. 1861; FKH 46. 1912; FGD 2: 144. 1991; FRPS 49(3): 193. 1998.

Shrub or small tree, branchlets pubescent. Leaves membranaceous; petioles 3–7 mm, pubescent; leaf blade oblong or oblong-lanceolate, 4–12 × 1–3.5 cm, base cuneate to broadly cuneate, apex long-caudate to caudate, margin serrulate, glabrous adaxially except for the hirsute midvein, slightly hirsute to nearly glabrous abaxially; Flowers axillary, solitary or 2–3 clustered; pedicels 3 –6 mm, pubescent; bracteoles 3 –6, semiorbicular to broadly ovate, 1– 6 mm, abaxially pubescent, margin ciliolate; sepals 5, 2– 4 mm, broadly ovate to suborbicular, silky-hairy abaxially, margin ciliolate; petals 5–7, white, 1–3 cm, connate at base, silky-hairy abaxially; stamens many, in 2 whorls, 1–2.5 cm, connate to middle, filaments densely silky-pilose; ovary globose, 2 mm in diam., densely tomentellous; styles 1–2.5 cm, tomentellous, 3-lobed at apex. Capsule ellipsoid-globose, 2 cm in diam., l-locular and l-seeded. Seeds brown, globose, ca. 1 cm in diam.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Castle Peak, Victoria Peak, Ma On Shan, Tai Mo Shan. Y. S. Lau 1680; P. S. Choi 516.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Xizang, Yunnan; Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Vietnam.
Ecology: Forest. Flowering: Oct.–Jan.; fruiting: Sep.– Oct.
Uses: Materials (lipids).
Notes: The type specimen of Camellia assimilis was collected from Mount Gough and Victoria Peak, Hong Kong Island by J. G.Campion around 1850.

Camellia crapnelliana Tutch. 紅皮糙果茶
J. Linn. Soc. London 37: 63. 1904; FKH 46. 1912; FGD 2: 129. 1991; FRPS 49(3): 18. 1998.
Thea crapnelliana (Tutch.) Rehd., J. Arnold Arbor. 5: 238. 1924.

Tree or shrub, branches and branchlets reddish brown, glabrous. Leaves leathery; petioles 6–12 mm, glabrous; leaf blade elliptic to oblong-elliptic, 7–19 × 3–6 cm, base cuneate to broadly cuneate, apex bluntly cuspidate, margin denticulate, glabrous; lateral veins 7–9 on each side of midvein, obscure adaxially, raised abaxially. Flowers axillary or subterminal, solitary or paired, 6–10 cm in diam., subsessile; bracteoles and sepals 7–13, persistent, suborbicular, 0.3–2 cm, tawny tomentellous abaxially; petals 6–8, white, obovate to obovate-oblong, 3.5–6.5 × 2–4 cm, connate at base, apex rounded to emarginate; stamens many, ca. 1.5 –1.7 cm; filaments glabrous, basal ca. 5 mm connated; ovary ca. 2 mm in diam., 3–5-locular, densely tomentose; styles 3–5, free, ca. 1.5 cm, proximal part pubescent to tomentose. Capsule greyish brown, subglobose, 5–10 cm in diam., 3–5-locular with 3–5 seeds per locule, furfuraceous, dehiscing into 3–5 valves; central axis thick, persistent; pericarp woody, (6–)10–15 mm thick. Seeds brown, semiglobose, 1.5–2 cm in diam., glabrous.

Locality: Mount Parker, Mau Ping. W. J. Tutcher 967; Y. S. Lau 1328.
Distribution: Guangdong, E Guangxi, E Jiangxi, Fujian, S Zhejiang.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Dec.–Jan.; fruiting: Sep.– Oct.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Mount Parker, Hong Kong Island in 1903. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Mount Parker, Pat Sin Leng, Nam Chung, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Camellia euryoides Lindl. 柃葉茶
Bot. Reg. 1: 983. 1826; FGD 2: 140. 1991; FRPS 49(3): 162. 1998.
Thea euryoides (Lindl.) Booth, Trans. Hort. Soc. London 7560. 1830.

Shrub or small tree, young branches densely greyish yellow-pubescent, glabrescent. Petioles 1–3 mm, pubescent; leaf blades thinly leathery, elliptic to ovate-elliptic, 2– 4 × 0.7–1.4 cm, base broadly cuneate, apex bluntly acuminate, margin serrulate, hirtellous along midvein adaxially, sparsely appressed villose or glabrescent abaxially; lateral veins obscure on both surfaces. Flowers axillary or subterminal, solitary, ca. 1.5 cm in diam.; pedicels 5–9 mm, slender, glabrous; bracteoles 4 or 5, triangular to broadly ovate, 1–1.5 mm, abaxially puberulous near apex, margin ciliolate; sepals 5, ca. 2.5 mm, connate at base, abaxially puberulous near apex, adaxially sericeous, margin ciliolate; petals 5, white, obovate to broadly obovate, ca. 2 cm, connate at base, abaxially glabrous, apex emarginate to truncate; stamens many, in 2 whorls, 0.9 –1.5 cm, glabrous; proximal 2/3 of filaments connate into a cup; ovary ovoid, 1.5–2 mm, glabrous; styles ca. 1.8 mm, glabrous, 3-lobed at apex. Capsules subglobose, 1–1.5 cm in diam., 1-locular with l seed; pericarp green to brown, thinly woody; central axis abortive. Seeds brown, globose, ca. 1 cm in diam.

Locality: Mount Parker, Pat Sin Leng, Nam Chung, Lantau Island. F. W. Xing 8066; HK sheet 35553.
Distribution: Guangdong, Jiangxi, Fujian.
Ecology: Forest. Flowering: Mar.–May; fruiting: Aug.– Oct.

Camellia furfuracea (Merr.) Cohen-Stuart 糙果茶
Bull. Jard. Bot. Buitenzorg, ser. 3, 1: 240. 1919; FGD 2: 130. 1991; FRPS 49(3): 19. 1998.
Thea furfuracea Merr., Philipp. J. Sci. 13(3): 149. 1918.
Theopsis furfuracea (Merr.) Nakai, J. Jap. Bot. 16(12): 706. 1940.

Small tree or shrub, branches and branchlets greyish brown, glabrous. Leaves papery, narrowly to broadly elliptic or oblong-elliptic, 8–15 × 2.5 – 5.5 cm, base cuneate to broadly cuneate, apex acuminate or shortly acuminate, margin mucronulate-denticulate, glabrous; lateral veins 7–9 on each side of midvein, slightly impressed above, elevated below; petioles 4 –9 mm, glabrous. Flowers axillary or subterminal, solitary or paired, 2–3.5 cm in diam., subsessile; bracteoles and sepals 7–8, persistent, semiorbicular to suborbicular, smaller ones 2.5 –4 mm long, larger ones 8 –13 mm long, pubescent or yellow-tomentose abaxially; petals 6 –8, white, obovate, 1.5 –2 × 0.9–1.2 cm, connate at base for about 4 mm; stamens many, ca. 1.3–1.5 cm; filaments glabrous, connate at base, filament tube 5–6 mm; ovary ca. 1.5 mm in diam., 3-locular, densely tomentose, ovules 2– 4 per locule; styles 3, free, ca. 1.8 cm, pubescent almost to apex. Capsule subglobose, greyish brown, furfuraceous, 2–4 cm in diam., dehiscing into 3 valves; central axis thick, persistent; pericarp woody, 2–4 mm thick. Seeds brown, semiglobose, 1.5 –2 × 0.8 –1.7 cm, glabrous.

Locality: Au Pui Wan. K. L. Yip 4166; P. S. So 11.
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan, Jiangxi; Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Dec.–Jan.; fruiting: Sep.– Oct.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Camellia granthamiana Sealy 大苞山茶
J. Roy. Hort. Soc. 81: 182. 1956; FGD 2: 127. 1991; FRPS 49(3): 6. 1998.

Shrub or tree, up to 8 m tall. Petioles 8–12 mm; leaf blades leathery, oblong-elliptic or elliptic, 7–11 × 3– 5 cm, base rounded to obtuse, apex acuminate, margin serrulate, glabrous, lateral veins 6–7 on each side of midvein, rugose adaxially when dry. Flowers axillary or subterminal, solitary, 10–14 cm in diam., subsessile; bracts and sepals 12, persistent, crustaceous, leathery, orbicular, 3– 4 cm, grey silky-hairy abaxially; petals 8 –10, white, broadly obovate, 5 –7 × 3.8 – 5 cm, basal 1.5 cm united, glabrous; stamens many, ca. 2.5 cm, basal 5– 6 mm united, glabrous. Ovary globose, 4 – 5 mm in diam., 5-locular, densely white-tomentose; styles 2 cm, 5-lobed at apex, densely white-tomentose. Capsule subglobose, ca. 6 cm in diam., furfuraceous, surrounded by persistent sepals, dehiscing into 5 valves; pericarp 5 mm thick. Seeds dark brown, spherical, 1–1.5 cm long.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan. Y. S. Lau 2056; P. S. Choi 246.
Distribution: Guangdong.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Dec.–Jan. of the following year; fruiting: Aug.–Sep.
Uses: Ornamental, materials (lipids).
Notes: The type specimen was collected in a ravine of Tai Mo Shan by Hong Kong Herbarium staff in 1955. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Victoria Peak, Pok Fu Lam, Mount Nicholson, Mount Parker
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Camellia hongkongensis Seem. 香港茶
Trans. Linn. Soc. London 22: 342, t. 60. 1859; FHK 30. 1861; FKH 46. 1912; FGD 2: 134. 1991; FRPS 49(3): 71. 1998.
Thea hongkongensis (Seem.) Pierre, Fl. For. Cochinch. 2: t. 117. 1887.

Shrub or small tree, up to 10 m tall, young branches reddish brown, glabrous. Leaves leathery; petioles ca. 1 cm, glabrous; leaf blade oblong, 7–13 × 2–4 cm, base cuneate to obtuse, apex acuminate, margin entire or obscurely undulate-denticulate, light green adaxially, dark green and glabrous abaxially; midvein impressed adaxially, prominent abaxially, lateral veins 7–10 on each side of midvein. Flowers subterminal, solitary, subsessile; bracteoles and sepals 9–11, 3 –20 mm, silky hairy, deciduous or persistent in fruit; petals 6–7, broadly obovate, 3.5–4 cm, connate at base; stamens many, ca. 3 cm, glabrous, connate at base; ovary globose, ca. 2 mm in diam., 3-locular, densely tomentose; styles 3 – 4, free, 2.8 –3.3 cm, glabrous. Capsule brown, globose to oblate, ca. 3 cm in diam., 3– 4-locular with 1–2 seeds per locule. Seeds brown, subglobose to globose, ca. 1.5 cm in diam., glabrous.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Pok Fu Lam, Mount Nicholson, Mount Parker. W. Y. Chun 9172; C. Wang 30303; N. K. Chun 40030, 40280, 40286; H. T. Chang 6558, 6559.
Distribution: Guangdong.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Dec.–Jan.; fruiting: Aug.– Sep.
Uses: Ornamental, materials (lipids).
Notes: The type specimen was collected in a ravine of Victoria Peak, Hong Kong Island in 1849. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Camellia japonica L. 山茶
Sp. Pl. 2: 698. 1753; FGD 2: 134. 1991; FRPS 49(3): 87. 1998.
Thea japonica (L.) Baill., Hist. Pl. 4: 229. 1873.

Shrub or small tree, branches and branchlets greyish brown, glabrous. Leaves leathery; petioles 8 –15 mm, glabrous; leaf blade oblong or obovate-oblong, 5 –12 × 3 – 6 cm, base cuneate to broadly cuneate, apex shortly acuminate or acute, margin serrulate, glabrous, lateral veins 7– 8 on each side of midvein. Flowers axillary or subterminal, solitary or in pairs, 5 – 8 cm in diam., subsessile; bracteoles and sepals 10, suborbicular to orbicular, 0.5 –2 cm in diam., pubescent; petals 6 –7, 2.5 –3.5 cm, rose or white, connate at base, silky-pubescent abaxially; stamens many, filaments connate about half way into a tube and united at base with petals, glabrous, 2.5 –3.5 cm, anthers oblong, 2 mm; ovary ovoid, 2.5 mm in diam., glabrous, 3-locular; styles ca. 2.8 cm, 3-lobed at the apex, glabrous. Capsule globose, 2.5 – 4.5 cm in diam., 3-locular with 1 or 2 seeds per locule; pericarp woody, 5 – 8 mm thick when dry. Seeds brown, semiglobose to globose, 1–2 cm in diam., glabrous.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 32805; C. H. Tsou 1824.
Distribution: Shandong, Zhejiang; S Japan, S Korea. Widely cultivated in gardens.
Ecology: Flowering: Jan.–Mar.; fruiting: Sep.– Oct.
Uses: Ornamental.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Mo Shan, Kwun Yam Shan, Pat Sin Leng, Bride's Pool
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Camellia kissii Wall. 落瓣油茶
Asiat. Res. 13: 429. 1820; FHN 1: 500. 1964; FGD 2: 131. 1991; FRPS 49(3): 24. 1998.
Thea sasanqua var. kissi (Wall.) Pierre, Fl. For. Cochinch. 2: sub. t. 115 – 6. 1887.

Shrub or small tree; branchlets greyish brown, pubescent. Leaves leathery; petioles 4 –7 mm, densely pubescent; leaf blade oblong, or oblong-elliptic, 5 –7 × 1.5 –3 cm, base cuneate to obtuse, apex acute or acuminate, margin serrulate; hirtellous along midvein adaxially, villose or glabrescent abaxially, lateral veins 6– 8 on each side of midvein, slightly impressed adaxially, raised abaxially, or slightly raised on both surfaces. Flowers axillary, solitary or in pair, 2–3 cm in diam., subsessile; bracteoles and sepals 9–10, 2–7 mm, pubescent, caducous; petals 5– 8, white, nearly free, obovate to ovate, 1.2–1.5 cm, pubescent abaxially; stamens 6–9 mm, glabrous, filaments basal 1–3 mm connate; ovary 3-locular, white-tomentose; styles 3, 3–7 mm, connate at base, glabrous or tomentose proximally. Capsule subglobose to globose-pyriform, 1.4 –2.5 × 1.5 –2 cm, usually l locule developed with 1 seed per locule, dehiscing into 2–3 valves; pericarp thickly, ca. 1.5 mm thick. Seed brown, globose, 1–1.5 cm in diam.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Kwun Yam Shan, Pat Sin Leng, Bride's Pool. Y. S. Lau 2811; HK sheet 33868.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan and Yunnan; Nepal, India, Myanmar, Sikkim, Vietnam.
Ecology: Evergreen forests and thickets. Flowering: Nov.–Dec.; fruiting: Sep.– Oct.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Cape D'Aguilar, Tai Mo Shan, Sunset Peak, Lantau Peak
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Camellia oleifera Abel 油茶
Narr. Journey China 174, 363. 1818; FHN 1: 500. 1964; FGD 2: 128. 1991; FRPS 49(3): 13. 1998.
Camellia drupifera Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 411. 1790; FKH 46. 1912, non. rej. prop.
Thea oleifera (Abel) Rehd. & Wils., Pl. Wilson. 2: 393. 1915.

Shrub or small tree, young branchlets reddish brown, pubescent. Leaves leathery; petioles 5–10 mm, pubescent; leaf blade elliptic or obovate, 6–10 × 2–4 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, margin serrate to serrulate, sparsely pilose along midvein or glabrous adaxially, hirtellous along midvein abaxially, lateral veins 5– 8 on each side of midvein. Flowers axillary or subterminal, solitary or in pairs, 4 – 6 cm in diam., subsessile; bracteoles and sepals 8–11, broadly ovate, 3 –12 mm, yellow-tomentose abaxially, margin membranous and ciliolate, caducous; petals 5–7, white, nearly free, obovate, oblong-obovate, or oblanceolate, 2.5– 4 × 1.5 –2.5 cm, 2-lobed at apex; stamens 1–1.5 cm, glabrous, filaments connate at base into a tube; ovary globose, 2–3 mm in diam., 3-locular, white-tomentose; styles 0.8–1.2 cm, glabrous or tomentose at base, 3-lobed. Capsule globose to ellipsoid, 2– 4 cm in diam., 1–3-locular with 1–2 seeds per locule, dehiscing into 2–3 valves; pericarp 3 – 6 mm thick, villose. Seeds brown to reddish brown, globose to semiglobose, 1.5 –2 cm in diam.

Locality: Cape D'Aguilar, Tai Mo Shan, Sunset Peak, Lantau Peak. L. T. Lo 652; Y. S. Lau 3275; Y. W. Lam 134.
Distribution: Area S of Changjiang River; N Laos, N Myanmar, N Vietnam.
Ecology: Forest. Flowering: Dec.–Jan. of the following year; fruiting: Sep.– Oct.
Uses: Materials (lipids).

Camellia reticulata Lindl. 滇山茶
Bot. Reg. t. 1078. 1827; FRPS 49(3): 68. 1998.
Desmitus reticulata (Lindl.) Rafin., Sylva Tellur 39. 1838.
Thea reticulata (Lindl.) Kochs, Bot. Jahbr. Syst. 27: 595. 1900.

Shrub or tree, branches and branchlets greyish brown, pubescent or glabrescent. Leaves leathery; petioles 6–13 mm, pubescent or glabrescent; leaf blade oblong to oblong-elliptic, 5 –12 × 3 – 5.5 cm, base cuneate to broadly cuneate, apex acute to shortly acuminate, margin serrulate, sparsely appressed pubescent or glabrescent adaxially, glabrous abaxially; lateral veins 6 – 8 on each side of midvein and raised on both surfaces. Flowers axillary or subterminal, solitary or 2–3 clustered, 7–10 cm in diam., subsessile; bracteoles and sepals 9 –11, deciduous after anthesis; petals 5–7 but often more for some cultivars, rose to pink, rarely white, obovate to broadly obovate, 4–6 × 3 – 4.5 cm, apex emarginate, connate at base; stamens many, 3 – 4 cm, glabrous, filaments connate at base; ovary globose, 3 – 4 mm in diam., 3 – 5-locular, tomentose; styles 2.5 –3.5 cm, glabrous or hairy proximally, 3– 5-lobed at apex. Capsule globose to oblate, 3.5– 4 × 4 – 5 cm, 3 – 5-locular with 1–2 seeds per locule; pericarp firmly fleshy, ca. l cm thick or 5– 6 mm when dry. Seeds brown, semiglobose to globose, 1–1.5 cm in diam.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 33869, 33870.
Distribution: Guizhou, Sichuan, Yunnan.
Ecology: Flowering: Jan.–Mar.; fruiting: Sep.– Oct.
Uses: Ornamental.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Victoria Peak, Mount Parker, Tai Mo Shan
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Camellia salicifolia Champ. ex Benth. 柳葉茶
Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 3: 309. 1851; FHK 30. 1861; FKH 46. 1912; FGD 2: 142. 1991; FRPS 49(3): 194. 1998.
Thea salicifolia (Champ.) Seem., Trans. L. Soc. 22: 349. 1859.
Camelliastrum salicifolia (Champ.) Nakai, J. Jap. Bot. 16: 701. 1940.

Shrub or small tree, young branchlets densely pubescent, glabrescent. Petioles 1–3 mm, densely pubescent; leaf blades membranaceous, lanceolate, 6 –10 × 1.5 –2.5 cm, base rounded, apex long-acuminate to caudate, margin serrulate, glabrous adaxially except for the pubescent midvein, densely pubescent abaxially; lateral veins 6–9 pairs. Flowers axillary, solitary; pedicels 4– 5 mm, densely villose; bracteoles 4– 5, lanceolate, 4 –10 mm, pubescent, persistent; sepals 5, lanceolate, 1–1.5 cm, silky-hairy abaxially; petals 5 – 6, white, subequal, obovate to obovate-elliptic, 1.5 –2 × 0.8 –1.5 cm, silky-hairy abaxially, connate at base; stamens many, in 2 whorls, filaments ca. 1–1.5 cm, connate to 3/4 of its length, free portion hairy, anthers pubescent; ovary densely tomentellous; styles ca. 1 cm, densely tomentellous, 3-lobed. Capsule globose, 1.5 –2.5 cm in diam., llocular with l seed, apex shortly conical; pericarp ca. 1 mm thick. Seed brown, subglobose.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Mount Parker, Tai Mo Shan. H. C. Tang 1487; N. H. Li 3.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Jiangxi, Fujian,Taiwan.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Nov.; fruiting: Sep.– Oct.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Happy Valley, Hong Kong Island by J. G. Champion around 1850.

Camellia sasanqua Thunb. 茶梅
Fl.: Jap. 273, t. 30. 1784; FKH 46. 1912; FHN 1: 500. 1964; FRPS 49(3): 12. 1998.

Small tree; young branchlets pubescent. Leaves leathery; petioles 4 – 6 mm, glabrescent; leaf blade elliptic, 3 – 6 × 1–3 cm, base cuneate, or sometimes rounded, apex acute, margin serrulate; lateral veins 5 –6 on each side of midvein, obscure on both surfaces. Flowers axillary or terminal, 4 –7 cm in diam.; bracteoles and sepals 6 –7, pubescent; petals 6–7, red, nearly free, unequal, broadly obovate, the largest one 5 × 6 cm; stamens many, free, 1.5 –2 cm; ovary pilose, styles 1–1.3 cm, free or 3-lobed at apex. Capsules globose, 1.5 –2 cm across, 1–3-locular. Seeds brown, glabrous.

Locality: Cultivated. L. T. Lo 274; Y. S. Lau 3021.
Distribution: Native to Japan. Widely cultivated.
Uses: Ornamental.

Camellia sinensis (L.) Kuntze 茶
Trudy Imp. S.-Peterburgsk. Bot. Sada 10: 195. 1887; FGD 2: 137. 1991; FRPS 49(3): 130. 1998.
Thea sinensis L., Sp. Pl. 1: 515. 1753; FHN 1: 496. 1964.
Camellia thea Link., Enum. Hort. Berol. Alt. 2: 73. 1822; FKH 45. 1912.

Shrub or small tree; young branches pubescent, glabrescent; terminal buds silvery grey sericeous. Petioles 3 – 8 mm, glabrous; leaf blades leathery, elliptic to oblong, 4 –12 × 2– 5 cm, base cuneate, apex acute or obtuse, margin serrate to serrulate, glabrous adaxially, glabrous or pubescent abaxially, lateral veins 6–9 pairs. Flowers axillary, solitary or 2–3 clustered, 2–3 cm in diam.; pedicels 4– 6 mm, recurved, pubescent or glabrous; bracteoles 2, caducous, ovate, ca. 2 mm; sepals 5, persistent, leathery, broadly ovate to suborbicular, 3–4 mm, glabrous or white-pubescent abaxially, white-sericeous adaxially, margin ciliolate; petals 6 –8, white, outer 1–3 sepaloid, inner ones obovate to broadly obovate, 1–1.6 × 1.2–2 cm, connate at base, apex rounded, glabrous or pubescent; stamens many, 0.8 –1.3 cm, glabrous, in 3– 4 whorls, connate at base; ovary globose, 3-locular, pubescent; styles ca. 1 cm, glabrous or pubescent at base, 3-lobed at apex. Capsule oblate, rarely globose, 1–1.5 × 1.5–3 cm, 1–2-locular with 1–2 seeds per locule; pericarp ca. l mm thick; central axis persistent. Seeds brown, subglobose, 1–1.4 cm in diam.

Locality: Mount Parker, Tai Mo Shan. Y. W. Lam 1390; HK sheet 32921.
Distribution: Area S of Changjiang River; Japan, Korea, Laos, Myanmar, Thailand, Vietnam; widely cultivated in tropical and subtropical parts of the world.
Ecology: Forests and thickets, or cultivated. Flowering: Oct.–Feb.; fruiting: Aug.– Oct.
Uses: Food (beverage base), medicinal (source of caffeine & theophylline).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan, Wu Kau Tang
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Camellia sinensis (L.) Kuntze var. waldenae (S. Y. Hu) H. T. Chang 香花茶
Acta Sci. Nat. Univ. Sunyatsenia 20(1): 98. 1981; FGD 2: 137. 1991; FRPS 49(3): 131. 1998.
Camellia waldenae S. Y. Hu, Wild Flowers of Hong Kong. 61. 1977.

Differs from var. sinensis by its narrowly oblanceolate leaves and sweet-smelling flowers.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan, Wu Kau Tang. S. Y. Hu 12573 (CUHK); L. T. Lo 428.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi.
Ecology: Forest.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Tai Mo Shan by S. Y. Hu.

Cleyera japonica Thunb. 紅淡比
Nov. Gen. 3: 69. 1783, p. p.; FGD 2: 159. 1991; FRPS 50(1): 56, 1998

Shrub or small tree, branches and branchlets greyish brown, glabrous. Leaves leathery; petioles 5–10 mm, glabrous, canaliculate; leaf blade oblong to elliptic-oblong, 5–9 × 2–3 cm, base cuneate or broadly cuneate, apex acuminate or shortly acuminate, margin entire, glabrous. Flowers axillary, or 2– 5 clustered; pedicels ca. 1.5 cm, glabrous; bracteoles 2, alternate, deciduous; sepals 5, subrounded, ca. 3.5 × 3.5 mm, imbricate, apex rounded, apex acuminate or shortly acuminate, margin ciliate; petals 5, white, obovate-oblong, ca. 1 × 0.5 cm, reflexed at anthesis; stamens about 25, in 2 series, unequal, 5 –7 mm; filaments slender, glabrous; anthers elliptic, hispid; ovary glabrous, 2-locular; style 6–10 mm, 2- lobed. Fruit baccate, globose, purplish black when mature, 6–9 mm in diam. Seeds many, compressed, dark brown and shining.

Locality: Chek Keng, Tung Lung Chau. F. W. Xing 9393; S. C. Ng 2171.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian; India, Japan.
Ecology: Shrublands and forests. Flowering: Apr.–May.

Cleyera parvifolia (Kobuski) Hu ex L. K. Ling. 小葉紅淡比
Iconogr. Cormophytorum Sinicorum Suppl. 2: 481. 1983; FRPS 50(1): 61. 1998.
Cleyera japonica Thunb. var. parvifolia Kobuski, J. Arnold Arbor. 18(2): 125. 1937; FTW 2: 604. 1976; FGD 2: 160. 1991.

Small tree or shrub, branches reddish brown, branchlets greyish brown, glabrous. Leaves leathery, elliptic, 3–5.5 × 1.5–2 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, margin entire, slightly revolute, glabrous, midvein prominent on both surfaces, lateral veins 5 –6 pairs; petioles 3 – 5 mm, glabrous, sulcate above. Flowers axillary, solitary or 2–3 in cluster; pedicels 5 – 8 mm, glabrous; bracteoles 2, deciduous; sepals 5, triangular, ca. 3.5 × 2 mm, imbricate, apex acute, margin ciliate, persistent in fruit; petals 5, white, oblong or obovate-oblong, 5 – 6 × 2.5 –3 cm; stamens about 25, 2-seriate, unequal, ca. 5 mm long; filaments filiform, glabrous; anthers ovoid, hispid, 2-celled, longitudinally opening, ca. 2 mm; ovary spherical, glabrous, 2-locular; style ca. 4 mm, apex 2-fid. Fruit baccate, globose, black, 5 mm in diam. Seeds many, compressed, dark brown, shiny, ca. 2 mm in diam.

Locality: Pat Sin Leng, Nam Chung. S. C. Ng 2176; Y. W. Lam 1427; K. L. Yip 4085.
Distribution: Guangdong, Taiwan.
Ecology: Forest. Flowering: May; fruiting: Sep.

Eurya acuminatissima Merr. & Chun 尖葉毛柃
Sunnyatsenia 1: 72. 1930; FGD 2: 166. 1991; FRPS 50(1): 100. 1998.

Shrub or small tree, 1.5 –7 m tall; young branchlets densely covered with spreading long hairs; terminal buds villose. Leaves thinleathery; petioles 2–3 mm; leaf blade lanceolate, 5 –9 × 1.1–2.5 cm, base cuneate, apex caudate-acuminate, margin closely serrulate, dark green and shining adaxially, light green abaxially, glabrous or initially sparsely appressed pubescent on abaxial surface, lateral veins ca. 9 on each side of midvein. Flowers white, axillary, solitary or in cluster of 3; pedicels 1–3 mm, glabrous or nearly so. Male flowers: bracteoles orbicular; sepals ovate, 1 mm, apex rounded, mucronate; petals oblong, ca. 2.5 mm; stamens 14–16; anthers not locellate; pistillode densely pubescent. Female flowers: sepals ovate, apex acuminate; petals lanceolate, 2–2.5 mm; ovary ovoid, densely pubescent, 3-locular; styles slender, 3 –3.5 mm, 3-lobed. Fruit ellipsoidal-ovoid or globose, 3 – 4 mm, sparsely pubescent.

Locality: Lantau Peak, Sunset Peak. P. S. Choi 99; Y. W. Lam 688, 1358.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi. Guizhou, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian.
Ecology: Forests on mountain slopes or in valleys. Flowering: Sep.–Nov.; fruiting: Jul.–Aug. of the following year.

Eurya chinensis R. Brown 米碎花
Narr. J. China 379, t. 1818; FKH 44. 1912; FGD 2: 175. 1991; FRPS 50(1): 132. 1998.

Shrub, 1–3 m tall; young branchlets 2-ribbed, pubescent; terminal buds densely yellowish brown, pubescent. Leaves thinly leathery; petiole 2–3 mm; leaf blade obovate, 3 – 4.5 × 1–2 cm, base cuneate, apex obtuse or slightly emarginate, rarely acuminate, margin closely serrulate, glabrous, lateral veins 6 – 8 on each side of midvein. Flowers axillary, solitary or 2– 4 clustered; pedicel ca. 2 mm, glabrous. Male flowers: bracteoles very small, glabrous; sepals ovate, 1.5–2 mm, apex subrounded, glabrous; petals obovate, 3–3.5 mm, glabrous; stamens ca. 15; anthers not locellate; pistillode glabrous. Female flowers: bracteoles lightly smaller; sepals ovate, 1–1.5 mm, glabrous; petals ovate, 2–2.5 mm; ovary ovoid, glabrous, 3-locular; styles 1.5 –2 mm, apex 3-lobed. Fruit globose, 3 – 4 mm in diam. Seeds reniform, blackish brown, shining.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 950; Y. W. Lam 1275; Y. S. Lau 2239.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Thickets on hillslopes or by streams.

Eurya chinensis R. Brown var. glabra Hu & L. K. Ling 光枝米碎花
Acta Phytotax. Sin. 11: 314. 1966; FGD 2: 175. 1991; FRPS 50(1): 133. 1998.

Differs from var. chinensis by its terminal buds and the branchlets of the current year's growth are completely glabrous.

Locality: Stanley, Ho Pui, Ninepin Group. S. P. Lau 130; Y. W. Lam 141, 1144.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Thickets on hillslopes or by streams. Flowering: Nov.–Dec.; fruiting: Jun.–Jul. of the following year.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Mo Shan, Mount Parker, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Eurya distichophylla Hemsl. 二列葉柃
J. Linn. Soc. 23: 77. 1886; FKH 43. 1912; FGD 2: 167. 1991; FRPS 50(1): 89. 1998.
Eurya swinglei Merr., Philip. J. Sci. Bot. 12: 106. 1917.

Shrub; young branchlets terete, densely covered with spreading long hairs. Leaves thin-leathery; petioles short, ca. 1 mm, villose; leaf blade lanceolate, 3– 6 × 0.8 –1.5 cm, base obliquely rounded or oblique-cordate, apex acuminate or long-acuminate, margin serrulate, glabrous adaxially, densely appressed villose abaxially, lateral veins 8–11 on each side of midvein. Flowers white, axillary, solitary or in clusters of 3; pedicels ca. 1 mm, villose. Male flowers: bracteoles ovate, very small; sepals ovate, ca. 1.5 mm, apex slightly acute or obtuse, densely villose abaxially; petals obovate-oblong to obovate, ca. 2.5 mm, apex rounded; stamens 15–18; anthers locellate; pistillode densely pubescent. Female flowers: sepals ovate, ca. 1 mm, apex acute or obtuse, densely villose abaxially; petals lanceolate, 2–2.5 mm; ovary ovoid, densely pubescent, 3-locular; styles 3–5 mm, 3-lobed almost to base. Fruit globose or ovoid, 4–5 mm in diam., pubescent. Seeds orbicular-reniform.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Mount Parker, Lantau Island. H. C. Tang 2497; L. T. Lo 213; Y. S. Lau 3060.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Jiangxi, Fujian; Vietnam.
Ecology: Ravines.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Mount Parker, Tai Po Kau, Pat Sin Leng, Wu Kau Tang
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Eurya groffii Merr. 崗柃
Philipp. J. Sci. Bot. 25: 247. 1919; FHN. 1: 507. 1964; FGD 2: 170. 1991; FRPS 50(1): 119. 1998.
Eurya acuminata DC. var. groffii (Merr.) Kobuski, Ann. Missouri Bot. Gard. 25: 325. 1937.

Shrub or small tree, 2–7 m tall; young branchlets terete, densely yellowish brown-pubescent or glabrescent; terminal buds densely yellowish brown-villose. Leaves leathery; petioles ca. 1 mm, densely villose; leaf blade lanceolate, 5–10 × 1.2–2.2 cm, base obtuse or broadly cuneate, apex acuminate or long acuminate, margin closely serrulate, dark green and glabrous adaxially, yellowish green and appressed pilose abaxially, lateral veins 10 –14 on each side of midvein. Flowers axillary, solitary or 3 –9 clustered; pedicels 1–1.5 mm, densely pubescent. Male flowers bracteoles ovate, ca. 1 mm; sepals ovate, 1.5–2 mm, apex obtuse and mucronate, yellowish brownpubescent abaxially; petals obovate, ca. 3.5 mm; stamens ca. 20; anthers not locellate; pistillode glabrous. Female flowers: bracteoles and sepals as in male flower, but slightly smaller; petals lanceolate, ca. 2.5 mm; ovary ovoid, glabrous, 3-locular; style 2 mm, 3-lobed to the base. Fruit globose, ca. 4 mm in diam.

Locality: Mount Parker, Tai Po Kau, Pat Sin Leng, Wu Kau Tang. C. P. Lau 5; Y. W. Lam 558; K. L. Yip 4251.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Fujian; Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests and thickets.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Eurya loquaiana Dunn 細枝柃
J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 38: 355. 1908; FHN 1: 508. 1964; FGD 2: 171. 1991; FRPS 50(1): 124. 1998.

Shrub or small tree, young branchlets terete, puberulous. Leaves thinly leathery; petioles 2– 4 mm, puberulous; leaf blade ovate-elliptic, 4 –9 × 1.5–2.5 cm, base cuneate or broadly cuneate, apex long-acuminate, margin serrulate, adaxially dark green or yellowish green, glabrous, abaxially light green, becoming purplish red when dry, sparsely puberulous or only hairy on midvein, lateral veins 10 –20 on each side of midvein. Flowers axillary, solitary or in clusters of 4; pedicel 2–3 mm, puberulous. Male flowers: bracteoles ovate, ca. 1 mm; sepals ovate or suborbicular, ca. 2 mm, subglabrous; petals obovate, ca. 3.5 mm; stamens 10–15; anthers not locellate; pistillode glabrous. Female flowers: bracteoles and sepals as in male flowers, but smaller; petals elliptic, 3 mm, ovary glabrous 3-locular; style 2–3 mm, 3-lobed. Fruit globose, 3–4 mm in diam. Seeds reniform, dark brown and shining.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan. F. W. Xing 9030; Y. W. Lam 1442, 1755.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou, Sichuan, Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Forests and thicktets in ravines. Flowering: Oct.– Dec.; fruiting: Jul.–Sep. of the following year.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Lion Rock, Shing Mun, Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Eurya macartneyi Champ. 黑柃
Proc. Linn. Soc. Lond. 2: 99. 1850; FHK 27. 1861; FKH 43. 1912; FHN 1: 509. 1964; FGD 2: 172. 1991; FRPS 50(1): 144. 1998.

Shrub or small tree, glabrous throughout; young branchlets terete. Leaves leathery; petioles 3– 4 mm; leaf blade oblong or elliptic, 6 –14 × 2– 4.5 cm, base broadly cuneate or obtuse, apex shortly acuminate, margin subentire or serrulate on distal portion, adaxially yellowish green, abaxially reddish brown when dry, lateral veins 12–14 on each side of midvein. Flowers axillary, solitary or 3 –4 clustered; pedicels 1–1.5 mm. Male flowers: bracteoles suborbicular, ca. 1 mm; sepals leathery, orbicular, ca. 3 mm, apex rounded, mucronate or retuse; petals obovate, 4 – 6 mm; stamens 17–24; anthers not locellate; pistillode glabrous. Female flowers: bracteoles as in male flower; sepals ovate, 2–2.5 mm; petals obovate, ca. 4 mm; ovary ovoid, 3-locular; styles 3, free. Fruit globose, ca. 5 mm in diam., purplish black. Seeds reniform, dark brown and shining.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Lion Rock, Shing Mun, Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan, Lantau Island. H. C. Tang 2101; N. K. Chun 41907; K. L. Yip 4403.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian.
Ecology: Forests on mountain slopes and in ravines. Flowering: Nov.–Jan.; fruiting: Jun.–Aug.

Eurya muricata Dunn 格葯柃
J. Bot. 48: 324. 1910; FKH 43. 1912; FGD 2: 172. 1991; FRPS 50(1): 115. 1998.
Eurya huiana Kobuski f. glaberrima H. T. Chang, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 3: 36. 1954.

Shrub or small tree, glabrous throughout; young branchlets terete. Leaves leathery; petioles 3 – 5 mm; leaf blade elliptic, 5 – 8.5 × 2–3.2 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, margin subentire, dark green adaxially, light green or yellowish green abaxially, lateral veins 9 –11 on each side of midvein. Flowers axillary, solitary or 3 – 4 clustered; pedicels 1–2 mm. Male flowers: bracteoles suborbicular, 1–1.5 mm; sepals orbicular, 2–2.5 mm; petals oblong, 3–3.5 mm; stamens 15–22; anthers locellate; pistillode very small. Female flowers: bracteoles as in male flower; sepals ovate, 1.5 –2 mm; petals obovate, 2.5 –3 mm; ovary ovoid, 3-locular; styles 3-lobed. Fruit globose, ca. 4 mm in diam. Seeds reniform, dark brown, shining.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Mount Gough. S. T. Dunn s.n. (Herb. Hongk. No. 1772).
Distribution: Guangdong, Guizhou, Sichuan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian.
Ecology: Forests and thickets. Flowering: Nov.–Jan.; fruiting: Jun.–Aug.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Mount Gough around 1909.

Eurya nitida Korth. 細齒葉柃
Verh. Nat. Gesch. Bot. 3: 115, t. 17. 1840; FHN 1: 509. 1964; FGD 2: 176. 1991; FRPS 50(1): 134. 1998.
Eurya japonica var. nitida (Korth.) Th.-Dyer, Fl. Brit. Ind. 1: 284. 1874.
Eurya japonica auct. non Thunb.: Benth., FHK 28. 1861; FKH 43. 1912.

Shrub or small tree, glabrous throughout; young branchlets 2-ribbed. Leaves thinly leathery; petioles ca. 3 mm; leaf blade oblong or obovate-oblong, 4–7 × 1.5–2.5 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, margin closely serrulate or crenulate, dark green and shining adaxially, light green or yellowish green abaxially, lateral veins 9 –12 on each side of midvein. Flowers axillary, solitary or 3 – 4 clustered; pedicels ca. 3 mm. Male flowers: bracteoles suborbicular, ca. 1 mm; sepals suborbicular, 1.5–2 mm, apex rounded; petals obovate, 3.5– 4 mm; stamens 14 –17, as long as petals; anthers not locellate; pistillode very small. Female flowers: bracteoles and sepals as in male flower; petals oblong, 2–2.5 mm; ovary ovoid, 3-locular; styles 1.5–3 mm, apex 3-lobed. Fruit globose, 3– 4 mm in diam., bluish black. Seeds reniform or globose-reniform, brown and shining.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 450, 2140; Y. S. Lau 1360; Y. W. Lam 1244.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hubei, S Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian; Vietnam, Myanmar, Malaya, Indonesia, Philippens.
Ecology: Forests and thickets.

Polyspora axillaris (Roxb. ex Ker-Gawl.) Sweet 大頭茶
Hort. Brit. 1: 61. 1827; FHN 1: 501. 1964.
Camellia axillaris Roxb. ex Ker-Gawl., Bot. Reg. t. 349. 1818.
Gordonia axillaris (Roxb. ex Ker-Gawl.) D. Dietr., Syn. Pl. 4: 863. 1847; FGD 2: 148. 1991; FRPS 49(3): 207. 1998.
Gordonia anomala Spreng., Syst. Veg. 3: 126. 1826; FHK 29. 1861; FKH 45. 1912.

Tree or shrub, up to 8 m tall; young branchlets and terminal buds densely pubescent. Leaves leathery; petioles 1.0 –1.5 cm; leaf blade oblong-ovate to oblanceolate, 6–15 × 2.5 – 4.5 cm, base cuneate and decurrent, apex rounded or obtuse, margin entire or remotely crenate on distal part, dark green and glabrous adaxially, paler and slightly pubescent abaxially when young, midvein impressed adaxially, veins obscure on both surfaces. Flowers axillary or subterminal, solitary or in pairs, nearly sessile, 7–13 cm in diam., bracteoles 4 – 5, deciduous, suborbicular, densely pubescent abaxially; sepals 5, ovate, 1–1.5 cm, densely pubescent abaxially, persistent; petals 5, white, broadly obovate, 3.5–5 cm, emarginate at the apex, pubescent abaxially; stamens many, unequal, 1.5 –2 cm, glabrous, connate at base and adnate to petals at the base; ovary 5-locular, pubescent; style ca. 2 cm, sericeous. Capsule oblong or oblong-ovoid, ca. 5 cm, pilose. Seeds compressed, oblong, 1.5–2 cm including wing.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 2258; Y. W. Lam 418; K. L. Yip 4187.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan, Taiwan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Thickets and early secondary forests. Flowering: Sep.– Oct.; fruiting: Nov.–Dec.
Uses: Ornamental, materials (timber).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Mount Nicholson, Lin Fa Shan, Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai, Wu Kau Teng, Sunset Peak
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Pyrenaria microcarpa (Dunn) H. Keng 小果石筆木
Gard. Bull. Singapore 26: 134. 1972.
Tutcheria microcarpa Dunn, J. Bot. 47: 197. 1909; FKH 45. 1912; FGD 2: 147. 1991; FRPS 49(3): 203. 1998.

Tree or shrub; young branches yellowish brown, pubescent, soon glabrescent. Leaves leathery; petioles 5–8 mm, sparsely pubescent or glabrous; leaf blade elliptic to oblong, 5 –12 × 2– 4 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, margin serrate, sparsely pubescent or glabrous, lateral veins 8 –10 on each side of midvein, conspicuous on both surface. Flowers axillary, solitary, white or light yellow, 1.5 –2.5 cm in diam.; pedicels 1–2 mm, pubescent; bracteoles 2, caducous, broadly ovate to crescent-shaped, 2–3 mm, densely yellow sericeous abaxially, glabrous adaxially; sepals 5–7, caducous, semiorbicular to reniform, unequal, 3 – 8 × 5 –10 mm, leathery, densely yellow sericeous abaxially, glabrous adaxially, apex rounded; petals 5–7, obovate, 1–1.5 × 1–1.3 cm, sericeous abaxially, slightly connate at base; stamens many, 6 – 8 mm, glabrous; adnate to petals; ovary 3-locular, densely sericeous; styles 5– 8 mm, glabrous. Capsule triangular-globose, 1.0 –1.8 × 1–1.5 cm, 3-locular with 3 seeds per locule, dehiscing from base, sparsely sericeous; pericarp 1–1.5 mm thick when dry. Seeds brown, compressed, oblong-ovate, 6 – 8 mm.

Locality: Mount Nicholson, Lin Fa Shan, Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai, Wu Kau Teng, Sunset Peak. L. T. Lo 660; Y. S. Lau 2984; Y. W. Lam 1661.
Distribution: Anhui, Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hainan, Jiangxi, Taiwan, Yunnan, Zhejiang; Japan, Vietnam.
Ecology: Broadleaved evergreen forests. Flowering: Apr.–Jul.; fruiting: Aug.–Nov.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Mount Nicholson in September 1909.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Authority: (Champ.) C. Y. Wu & S. X. Yang
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Ma On Shan, Tao Po, Kwai Tau Leng, Wu Kau Tang, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Pyrenaria spectabilis (Champ.) C. Y. Wu & S. X. Yang 石筆木
Novon 15(2): 381. 2005.
Camellia spectabilis Champ., Trans. Linn. Soc. Bot. London 21: 111. 1850; et in Hook., Kew Journ. 3: 131. 1851.
Thea spectabilis (Champ.) Kochs, Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 27: 595. 1900.
Tutcheria spectabilis (Champ.) Dunn, J. Bot. 46: 324. 1908; FKH 45. 1912; Yip, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 42: 575. 2004.
Pyrenaria championii (Nakai) H. Keng, Gard. Bull. Singapore 26(1): 134. 1972, nom. illeg.
Tutcheria championii Nakai, J. Jap. Bot. 26: 708. 1940; FGD 2: 145. 1991; FRPS 49(3): 197. 1998, nom. illeg.
Camellia reticulata auct. non Lindl.: FHK 31. 1861.

Tree or small tree, branches greyish brown, young branches puberulous, soon glabrescent. Leaves leathery; petioles 0.5–1.5 cm; leaf blade oblong or lanceolate, 12–18 × 4–7 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, margin entire or undulate-serrate, yellowish when dry, shining and glabrous adaxially, sparsely pubescent, soon glabrescent abaxially; lateral veins 10 –14 on each side of midvein, conspicuous on both surfaces. Flowers axillary or subterminal, solitary, white, 4–7 cm in diam; pedicels 0.6–1.0 cm, pubescent; bracteoles 2, ovate, 1–1.5 × 1.5 –2 cm, densely yellow sericeous abaxially; sepals 9 –11, white, suborbicular, 2–3 cm in diam., yellowish sericeous abaxially, apex rounded to retuse, margin membranous; petals 5 or 6, broadly obovate, 4– 5 × 2– 3 cm, yellowish sericeous abaxially, apex emarginate, margin membranous; stamens many, ca. l. 5 cm, glabrous, slightly connate at the base and adnate to base of petals; ovary 3 – 6-locular with 2– 5 ovules per locule, densely yellowish tomentose; styles 3 – 6- lobed, pubescent at proximal part. Capsule globose to oblate, 4–7 cm in diam., 3– 6-locular with 2– 5 seeds per locule, dehiscing from base, greyish tomentose. Seeds brown, oblong, 1.5 –2.0 cm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Ma On Shan, Tao Po, Kwai Tau Leng, Wu Kau Tang, Lantau Island. C. P. Lau 25; N. K. Chun 40709; K. L. Yip 4199.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian.
Ecology: Broad-leaf evergreen forests. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.; fruiting: Sep.–Nov.
Uses: Onamental, materials (timber, lipids).
Notes: The type specimen (Champion s.n., K) was collected from Happy Valley, Hong Kong Island between 1847 and 1850.

Schima superba Gardn. & Champ. 木荷
Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. l: 246. 1849; FHN 1: 501. 1964; FGD 2: 150. 1991; FRPS 49(3): 224. 1998.
Schima noronhae auct. non Reinw. ex Blume: FHK 29. 1861; FKH 45. 1912.

Tree or small tree, branches greyish brown or reddish brown, glabrescent. Leaves papery or leathery; petioles 1–2 cm; leaf blade elliptic to oblong-elliptic, 7–13 × 3 – 6 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, margin crenulate to crenulate-serrate, glabrous, midvein slightly impressed adaxially, veins distinct on both surfaces. Flowers white, 2–3 cm in diam., in short terminal racemes; pedicel stout, 1–2.5 cm, glabrous or sparsely pubescent; bracteoles 2, deciduous; calyx 5-lobed, lobes semiorbicular, 2–3 mm, glabrous abaxially, pubescent adaxially, margins ciliolate; petals 5, obovate, 1–1.5 cm, proximally connate into a short tube, pubescent at base; stamens many, 5 –7 mm, connate at base; ovary ovoid, densely pubescent on proximal part, glabrescent on distal part; style ca. 5 mm. Capsule subglobose, 1–1.5 cm in diam, pubescent; seeds flat, reniform, narrowly winged, 7–9 × 4.5 – 5 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 554, 2146; K. Y. Tam 105.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdung, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Jun.–Aug.
Uses: Materials (timber, fuelwood).
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Wong Nai Chung, Hong Kong Island by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1849.

Stewartia villosa Merr. 柔毛紫莖
Lingnan Sci. J. 7: 315. 1931.
Hartia villosa (Merr.) Merr., J. Arnold Arbor. 19: 55. 1938; FGD 2: 153. 1991; FRPS 49(3): 235. 1998.

Evergreen tree, to 8 m tall; branchlets and petioles villose or appressed pubescent. Leaves leathery; petioles 1–2 cm, narrowly winged; leaf blade oblong or oblong-lanceolate, 8 –13 × 3 – 5 cm, base rounded to obtuse, apex acuminate to acute, margin sparsely serrate, villose or pubescent on both surfaces, glabrescent in age, lateral veins 10 –16 on each side of midvein. Flowers solitary, white; pedicels 6 – 8 mm, villose; bracteoles lanceolate, 0.8 –1.5 cm, villose; sepals ovate-lanceolate, unequal, 1.5 –1.8 × 0.5 –0.8 cm, villose abaxially, apex acute; petals yellowish white, obovate, ca. 1.8 × 1.2 cm; stamens ca. 1 cm, filaments connate at the base; ovary tomentose, style short. Capsule conical, ca. 1.8 cm.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Ngong Ping. H. C. Tang 2440; Y. S. Lau 421; S. T. Dunn s.n. (HK sheet 3263).
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Jun.–Jul.; fruiting: Oct.
Uses: Materials (timber).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Ternstroemia gymnanthera (Wight & Arn.) Beddome 厚皮香
Fl. Sylv. 19. 1871; FHN 1: 504. 1964; FGD 2: 161. 1991; FRPS 50(1): 11. 1998.
Cleyera gymnanthera Wight & Arnott, Prodr. Pl. Ind. Occ. 87. 1834.
Ternstroemia japonica auct. non Thunb.: Benth., FHK 27. 1861; FKH 43. 1912.

Shrub or small tree, glabrous throughout. Leaves leathery; petiole 5 –10 mm; leaf blade obovate to broadly elliptic, 5 –10 × 2.5–4.5 cm, base cuneate, apex acute to shortly acuminate, margin entire, dark green and shining adaxially, light green becoming reddish brown when dry abaxially, midvein impressed adaxially, lateral veins 7–9 on each side of midvein. Flowers andro-dioecious, axillary; pedicels 1.5 –3 cm; bracteoles 2, ovate, ca. 2 mm, margin glandular dentate, apex acute; sepals ovate or oblong-ovate, 4– 5 × 3 – 4 mm, glabrous, apex rounded, margin glandular dentate; petals obovate, 6 – 8 × 4 – 6 mm, apex rounded or retuse; stamens 4 – 5 mm; anthers oblong, longer than filaments; ovary ovoid, 2-locular with 2 ovules per locule; style short, 2-lobed. Fruit purplish red when mature, globose, 1–1.5 cm in diam., 2-locular with 1–2 seeds per locule. Seeds reniform, ca. 6 × 4 mm, with red aril.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan, Lantau Island. H. C. Tang 2363; Y. S. Lau 2556; K. L. Yip 4451.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Bhutan, Cambodia, India, Laos, Myanmar, Nepal, Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests and shrublands. Flowering: Jul.–Aug.
Uses: Ornamental.

Ternstroemia kwangtungensis Merr. 廣東厚皮香（厚葉厚皮香）
Philip. J. Sci. 13: 148. 1918; FGD 2: 161. 1991; FRPS 50(1): 5. 1998.

Shrub or small tree, 4 – 5 m tall; branchlets stout, greyish brown, glabrous. Leaves thickly leathery; petioles stout, 1–2 cm, glabrous; leaf blade broadly elliptic to obovate, 7–12 × 3 – 6 cm, apex abruptly acute, tip blunt, base broadly cuneate to obtuse, margin entire, glabrous, dark green and shining adaxially, light green and densely reddish brown or brown punctuate abaxially; midvein raised adaxially, plane or slightly impressed abaxially, lateral veins 5–7 on each side of midvein. Flowers axillary, solitary or in pairs, white; pedicels 1.5–2 cm, slightly recurved, glabrous. Male flowers: bracteoles 2, ovate to triangular-ovate, 4– 5 × 3 mm, margin sparsely glandular dentate; sepals ovate to suborbicular, 6 – 8 mm in diam., glabrous, margin glandular dentate, apex rounded; petals obovate to oblong-obovate, ca. 10 × 8 mm, apex rounded; stamens many, ca. 6 mm; anther ovate, ca. 3 mm; pistillode very small. Female flowers: bracteoles 2, obovate or triangular obovate, ca. 3 × 4 mm; sepals suborbicular, 6 –7 mm in diam.; ovary 3 –4(– 5) locular, glabrous, styles 3 – 4(– 5)-lobed, 6 –7 mm long. Fruit baccate, depressed-globose, 1.5 –1.8 × 1.5 –2 cm, 3 – 4(– 5)-locular, 1 seed per locule; bracteoles and sepals persistent. Seeds subreniform, 7– 8 × 6 mm, aril red.

Locality: Ping Fung Shan. Y. W. Lam 401, 499; F. W. Xing 9984.
Distribution: Guangdong, S Guangxi, Jiangxi, Fujian.
Ecology: Forests and thickets on hillslopes and by streams.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Tai Po, Ping Fung Shan, Wu Kau Tang, Tai Long Sai Wan
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Ternstroemia luteoflora L. K. Ling 尖萼厚皮香
FRPS 50(1): 183. 1998.

Tree; branchlets glabrous. Leaves leathery; petioles 1–2 cm; leaf blade elliptic to oblong-lanceolate, 5–11 × 2.5–4 cm, base cuneate, apex shortly acuminate, margin entire and slightly revolute, glabrous, dark green and shining adaxially, light green and becoming reddish brown when dry abaxially, lateral veins 6–8 on each side of midvein. Flowers andro-dioecious, ca. 1.5 cm in diam; pedicels 2–3 cm, more or less incurved. Male flowers: bracteoles 2, ovate-lanceolate, ca. 3 × 2 mm, margin glandular dentate, apex acuminate; sepals ovatelanceolate, 5–7 × 3 – 4 mm, apex acuminate to long-acuminate, margin glandular ciliolate; petals 5, white or yellowish white, obovate or suborbicular, 8 –10 × 8 –10 mm, apex retuse; stamens 35 – 45, ca. 5 mm; anthers oblong, 2– 4 mm; pistillode small, flattened. Female flowers: bracteoles, sepals and petals as in male flower, ovary globose, 2-locular with 2 ovules per locule; style 2-lobed. Fruits globose, 1.5 –2 cm in diam., 2-locular with 2 seeds per locule, bracteoles and sepals persistent. Seeds reddish brown, ellipsoid, ca. 8 × 6 mm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Tai Po, Ping Fung Shan, Wu Kau Tang, Tai Long Sai Wan. H. C. Tang 584; P. S. Choi 388; Y. W. Lam 244.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian.
Ecology: Secondary forests. Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: Aug.– Oct.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Pat Sin Leng, Wong Leng, Nam Chung, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Ternstroemia microphylla Merr. 小葉厚皮香
Sunyatsenia 3: 254. 1937; FGD 2: 163. 1991; FRPS 50(1): 20. 1998.
Ternstroemia pseudoverticillata Merr. & Chun, Sunyatsenia 5: 131. 1940

Shrub or small tree; branchs greyish brown, glabrous. Leaves leathery to thickly leathery; petioles ca. 3 mm, glabrous; leaf blade obovate, oblong-obovate, or oblanceolate, 2– 6 × 1–2 cm, base cuneate and decurrent, apex acute, obtuse, or rounded, margin subentire or sparsely serrulate towards apex, green and shining adaxially, light green abaxially, glabrous on both surfaces; midvein impressed adaxially, raised abaxially, lateral veins 3–5 on each side of midvein. Flowers white, polygamous, axillary, solitary or several borne on leafless branchlets, 5–8 mm in diam; pedicels slender, 5–10 mm, glabrous. Bisexual flower: bracteoles ovate-triangular, ca. 1 mm, apex acute, marigns glandular dentate; sepals ovate-orbicular, 2–3 mm in diam., apex rounded, margin sparsely glandular dentate; petals broadly obovate, ca. 4 × 3.5 mm; stamens 35–45, ca. 3 mm; anthers oblong, ca. 1.5 mm; ovary ovoid, 2-locular with 1 ovule per locule; style 2 mm, 2-lobed. Male flower: bracteoles, sepals, and petals as in bisexual flower; stamens 35–45; pistillode very small. Fruit ellipsoidal, 8–10 × 5–6 mm, 2-locular, with 1 seed per locule. Seeds long reniform, 5–7 mm long, aril red.

Locality: Pat Sin Leng, Wong Leng, Nam Chung, Lantau Island. S. P. Lau 33; P. S. Choi 444; Y. W. Lam 400.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian.
Ecology: Forests and shrublands. Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: Aug.– Oct.

Actinidia callosa Lindl. var. discolor C. F. Liang 異色獼猴桃
FRPS 49(2): 315, pl. 64: 6 –7. 1984; FFJ 3: 455, fig. 317. 1988; FGD 4: 144. 2000.
Actinidia fanjingshanensis S. D. Shi & Q. B. Wang, Acta Bot. Yunnan. 16(4): 345. 1994.

Deciduous woody vine. Branches glabrous, greyish yellow when dried. Pith solid, pale brown, lamellate. Petioles reddish, 2–4 cm, glabrous; leaf blade obovate or elliptic, 5 –12 × 3–6 cm, base cuneate or obtuse, slightly oblique, apex acute to acuminate, margin serrate to nearly entire, dark brown adaxially and greyish brown abaxially when dried, glabrous on both surfaces; lateral veins 6 – 8 pairs. Cymes 1–3-flowered; peduncles 0.5 –1.2 cm; pedicels 0.5 –1.5 cm. Flowers white. Sepals 5, ovate, 4 – 5 mm, glabrous. Petals 5, obovate-oblong, 8 –10 mm. Filaments 3 – 5 mm; anthers yellow, ovoid, 1.5 –2 mm, sagittate at base. Ovary subglobose, densely white-tomentose; styles slightly longer than ovary. Fruit subglobose to ellipsoid, 1.5 –2 cm, glabrous when mature, greenish brown, with conspicuous spots outside and with reflexed persistent sepals at base.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. K. Y. Tam 101; Y. W. Lam 1638.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan, Zhejiang, Anhui, Shanxi.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: Jul.–Sep.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai, Ma On Shan, Sai Kung, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Actinidia latifolia (Gardn. & Champ.) Merr. 闊葉獼猴桃
J. Straits Branch Roy. Asiat. Soc. 86: 330. 1922; FRPS 49(2): 255, pl. 72: 1. 1984; FFJ 3: 458. 1988; FGD 4: 148, fig. 95. 2000.
Heptaca latifolia Gardn. & Champ., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 1: 243. 1849.
Actinidia championii Benth., FHK 26. 1861; FKH 44. 1912.

Deciduous woody vine. Branchlets subglabrous, whitish lenticellate; pith white, lamellate, solid or hollow. Petioles 3–7 cm, glabrous to puberulous; leaf blade broadly ovate, 8–13 × 5–8.5 cm, base rounded, shallowly cordate or broadly cuneate, apex acute to acuminate, margin remotely callose-serrulate, glabrous adaxially, densely greyish to yellowish brown-tomentose, with appressed stellate hairs on abaxial surface; lateral veins 6–7 pairs. Cymes 3- or 4-branched, many-flowered; peduncles 2.5– 8.5 cm, densely brownish tomentose; pedicels 0.5 –1.5 cm, densely brownish tomentose; bracts linear, 1–2 mm. Flowers white, fragrant, 1.4 –1.6 cm in diam. Sepals 5, spathulate-ovate, 4–5 mm, reflexed after anthesis, yellowish tomentose on both surfaces. Petals 5–8, oblong to obovate-oblong, 6–8 mm, reflexed after anthesis. Filaments 2– 4 mm, slender; anthers sagittate-ovoid, ca. 1 mm, pubescent. Ovary globose, ca. 2 mm, densely pilose; styles 2–3 mm. Fruit brown, subglobose to ovoid, 3 –3.5 × 2–2.5 cm, spotted, glabrous when mature. Seeds 2–2.5 mm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai, Ma On Shan, Sai Kung, Lantau Island. H. C. Tang 946; Y. S. Lau 2514, 3019.
Distribtution: SW, S to E China; Vietnam, Laos, Cambodia, Malaysia, Thailand.
Ecology: Forests and thickets. Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: Oct.–Nov.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Hong Kong Island by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1849.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Saurauia tristyla DC. 水東哥（米花樹）
Mem. Ternstroem. 31, t. 4. 1822; FHK 27. 1861; FKH 45. 1912; FHN 1: 512. 1964; FRPS 49(2): 296. 1984; FGD 3: 152. 1995.

Small tree or shrub, 1– 5 m or taller. Branchlets stout, densely tomentose to glabrescent, with unguiculate hairs or subulate scales. Petiole 2.5 – 5.5 cm, with appressed scales or subulate stiff hairs; leaf blade elliptic, oblong or obovate-oblong, 10–30 × 5 –14 cm, papery, base broadly cuneate or rounded, apex acuminate, sparsely pubescent with appressed stiff hairs along midvein and lateral veins on both surfaces, glabrescent; lateral veins 8 –20 pairs. Cymes solitary or 2–3 fascicled, 2–5 cm, hairy and scaly. Pedicels 0.8 –1 cm. Flowers pink to white. Sepals broadly ovate, 3– 4 mm. Petals ovate, ca. 8 mm, recurved at apex. Stamens 25 –34. Ovary ovoid to globose; styles 3 or 4(or 5), connate at proximal half. Berry globose, 0.6–1 cm in diam., green to white or pale yellow.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island. C. P. Lau 87; W. J. Tutcher 5262; Y. S. Lau 633.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Malaysia, Nepal and Thailand.
Ecology: Broadleaved forests and thickets in ravines. Flowering: Mar.–Jul.; fruiting: Aug.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Ma On Shan, Pat Sin Leng, Wu Kau Tang, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Pentaphylax euryoides Gardn. & Champ. 五列木
Hook. J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 1: 245. 1849; FHK 28. 1861; FKH 44. 1912; FHN 1: 510. 1964; FRPS 45(1): 136, pl. 39. 1980; FGD 4: 141. 2000.

Shrub or tree, 4 –15 m tall, glabrous except bracteoles and sepals. Branchlets terete, greyish brown. Petioles 1–1.5 cm, grooved adaxially; leaf blade ovate, ovate-oblong or oblong–-lanceolate, 4–9 × 2– 5 cm, leathery, base rounded to broadly cuneate, apex caudate, margin entire and slightly revolute, dark green adaxially, pale green abaxially, lateral veins 6 – 8 pairs. Pseudo-racemes axillary or terminal, 4.5–12 cm. Pedicels ca. 0.5 mm; bracteoles triangular, 1–1.5 mm, sparsely white puberulous adaxially, margin ciliolate. Sepals 5, orbicular, 1.5 –2.5 mm in diam., sparsely white puberulous adaxially, apex slightly 2-cleft, margin ciliolate. Petals white, oblong-lanceolate to oblanceolate, 4– 5 × 1.5 –2 mm, apex retuse to 2-cleft; filaments oblong, petaloid, 2.5 –3.5 mm; anthers globose, ca. 0.5 mm in diam. Ovary ca. 1 mm long; style columnar, ca. 2 mm, 5-ridged. Capsule ellipsoid, 6–9 × 4 – 5 mm, purplish brown to dark brown, dehiscing into 5-valves when mature. Seeds reddish brown, 5 – 6 mm long, apex very compressed or winged.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Ma On Shan, Pat Sin Leng, Wu Kau Tang, Lantau Island. W. J. Tutcher 10912; P. S. Choi 212; K. L. Yip 4452.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian; Vietnam, Malaysia, Indonesia.
Ecology: Thickets and forests. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.; fruiting: Oct.–Nov.
Uses: Timber.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Hong Kong Island by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1849.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan, Wu Kau Tang, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Calophyllum membranaceum Gardn. & Champ. 胡桐
Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 1: 309. 1849; FHK 25. 1861; FKH 42. 1912; FRPS 50(2): 83. 1990; FHN 2: 56. 1965; FGD 3: 211. 1995

Shrub or small tree, 1–5 m tall. Branchlets narrowly 4-winged, glabrous. Petioles 0.4–1 cm; leaves thinly leathery, oblong, elliptic or lanceolate, 4 –13 × 1.5 – 4.5 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, acute or caudate-acuminate, margin entire, often slightly sinuaterevolute, shining on both surfaces, midvein elevated on both surfaces; lateral veins many, slender, parallel. Cymes axillary, 1–3 cm, (1–)3–9-flowered. Flowers white, reddish. Sepals 4, outer 2 suborbicular, ca. 4 mm; inner 2 petal-like, obovate, ca. 8 mm. Petals 4, obovate, ca. 8 mm. Stamens many; filaments united into 4 bundles at base. Ovary ovoid; style 4.5–5.5 mm. Drupes yellow, ovoid-oblong, 16 –20 × 10 –12 mm, apex mucronate. Seeds ca. 15 mm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan, Wu Kau Tang, Lantau Island. H. C. Tang 393; K. L. Yip 4099.
Distribution: Hainan, Taiwan, Guangdong, Guangxi; India, Sri Lanka, Indochina, Malaysia, Indonesia, Philippines, Polynesia, Madagascar, Australia.
Ecology: Secondary forests. Flowering: Mar.–May; fruiting: Aug.– Oct.
Uses: Medicinal.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Victoria Peak, Hong Kong Island by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1849.

Cratoxylum cochinchinense (Lour.) Blume 黃牛木
Mus. Bot. Lugd. Bat. 2: l7. 1852; FRPS 50(2): 76.1990; FHN 2: 53. 1965; FGD 3: 204. 1995.
Hypericum cochinchinense Lour. Fl. Cochinch. 472. 1790.
Cratoxylum polyanthum Korth. Verh. Nat. Gesch. Bot. 175, t. 36. 1842; FHK 24. 1861; FKH 42. 1912.

Shrubs or trees, 1–10 m tall, bark yellowish-white, glabrous. Petioles 2– 5 mm; leaves elliptic, narrow-elliptic, ovate-oblong or rarely subovate, 3 –11 × 1.5– 4 cm, base cuneate, rarely rounded, apex acute, shortly acuminate or slightly obtuse; lateral veins slightly obvious on both surfaces. Cymes axillary or extra-axillary, 1– 5-flowered. Flowers red, ca. 1 cm in diam. Sepals elliptic, 5 –7 mm. Petals obovate, ca. 10 –14 mm, base cuneate, without scale, with linear-glands. Stamens usually united into 3 bundles, 4–8 mm, glands 3, alternate with staminal bundles, conic, 2–3 mm. Capsules elliptic, 8–12 mm, with persistent calyx. Seeds 6 mm, winged on one side.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 110, 2270; Y. S. Lau 2180.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, S Yunnan; Indochina, Thailand, Myanmar, Philippines, Indonesia.
Ecology: Thickets or secondary forests. Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: Jun.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Garcinia multiflora Champ. ex Benth. 多花山竹子
Hook. J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 3: 310. 1851; FHK 25. 1861; FKH 42. 1912; FRPS 50(2): 94. 1990; FGD 3: 209. 1995; FHN 2: 54. 1965.

Shrub or tree, 3–12 m tall; bark grey-white. Petioles 0.5–4 cm; leaves leathery, obovate, oblong-obovate to oblanceolate, 5 –20 × 3 –10 cm, base cuneate, apex obtuse, acute or acuminate, margin slightly revolute; lateral veins 10–20 each side, oblique. Cymes rearranged in corymbs, terminal. Flowers orange, unisexual, rarely polygamous. Male flowers: sepals 4, orbicular, concave, outer ones 6 –7.5 mm, inner ones 8–10 mm; petals obovate-spathulate, 12–14 × 6–7 mm; stamens united into 4 bundles; anthers densely on top of bundles, globose. Female flowers: sepals and petals similar to those of male flowers; ovary 2-locular, without style; stigma peltate, persistent. Berries green-yellow, globose, ovoid or obovoid, 1.8 –3 cm in diam.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai. L. T. Lo 98; Y. S. Lau 920; P. S. Choi 85.
Distribution: Taiwan, Fujian, Jiangxi, Hunan, Guangdong, Hainan, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan.
Ecology: Secondary forests on higher grounds. Flowering: Jun.–Aug.; fruiting: Nov.–Dec.
Uses: Food (fruit).
Notes: The type specimen was collected from “the Black Mountain”, Hong Kong Island by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1850.

Garcinia oblongifolia Champ. ex Benth. 嶺南山竹子（黃牙果）
Hook. J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 3: 331. 1851; FHK 25. 1861; FKH 42. 1912; FRPS 50(2): 106. 1990; FHN 2: 55. 1965; FGD 3: 210. 1995.

Shrub or tree, 5–15 m tall. Petioles 0.5 –1.5 cm; leaves thinly leathery or papery, oblong, obovate-oblong, elliptic to oblanceolate, 4–14 × 1.5–4.3 cm, base cuneate, apex obtuse or acute rarely shortly acuminate, margin entire; lateral veins 10 –18 pairs, slender. Flowers unisexual, solitary or a few in fascicle, axillary or terminal. Male flowers: sepals 4, orbicular, 3– 4 mm; petals 4, obovateoblong, 7–9 mm; stamens many consolidated into a fleshy mass; pistillode absent. Female flowers: sepals and petals similar to male flowers; staminodes united into 4 bundles; ovary ovoid, without style; stigma peltate. Berries ovoid or subglobose, 2– 4 × 2–3.5 cm, with persistent calyx at base and stigma at apex.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 23; W. J. Tutcher 10542; Y. S. Lau 2178.
Distribution: Guangxi, Guangdong, Hainan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Fung Shui Woods and lowland secondary forests. Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: Oct.–Dec.
Uses: Materials (timber).
Notes: The type specimen was collected in the Happy Valley woods, Hong Kong Island by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1850.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Pok Fu Lam, Aberdeen, Victoria Peak, Tsim Shan, Fanling, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Hypericum japonicum Thunb. ex Murray 地耳草（田基黃）
Syst. Veg. ed. 14, 702. 1784; FHK 23. 1861; FKH 42. 1912; FRPS 50(2): 47. 1990; FHN 2: 52. 1965; FGD 3: 207. 1995.

Annual or perennial herb, 2– 45 cm tall. Branches diffuse or ascending, 4-angled. Leaves sessile, ovate or ovate-lanceolate, 2–18 × 1–10 mm, base slightly cordate, amplexicaul, rarely cuneate, apex obtuse, with transparent dots, 3-basinerved. Cymes terminal. Flowers yellow, 4 – 8 mm in diam. Sepals narrow-oblong or elliptic, 2– 5.5 mm, often with glandular dots. Petals elliptic, oblong or obovate, equaling to sepals. Stamen many; filaments base united; ovary ovate to elliptic, 1–1.8 mm; style 3 –2. Capsules ellipsoid, 2.5 – 6 × 1.3 –2.8 mm, dehiscing into 3 valves when ripen. Seeds yellow-brown, 0.5 mm.

Locality: Pok Fu Lam, Aberdeen, Victoria Peak, Tsim Shan, Fanling, Lantau Island. Y. W. Lam 661; H. C. Tang 2472; Y. S. Lau 2134.
Distribution: Liaoning, Shandong to S regions of Changjiang River; Japan, Korea, Nepal, Sikkim, India, Sri Lanka, Myanmar to Indonesia, Australia, New Zealand, Hawaii.
Ecology: Along roadside. Flowering: May–Aug.; fruiting: Jun.– Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Hypericum monogynum L. 金絲桃
Sp. Pl. ed. 2, 2: 1107. 1763; FRPS 50(2): 12. 1990; FGD 3: 206. 1995.
Hypericum chinense L., Syst. Nat. ed. 10, 2: 1184. 1759 non Osbeck (1757).

Small shrub, 0.5 –1 m tall, many branched. Leaves papery, elliptic, oblong, obovate, oblanceolate or ovate-oblong, 2.5 –11 × 1–4 cm, base cuneate or slightly cordate, sometimes amplexicaul; lateral veins 4–5 pairs, slender, obvious abaxially. Cymes terminal. Flowers yellow, ca. 3 – 6.5 cm in diam. Sepals ovate-oblong, 4.5 –13 mm. Petals obovate, 2–3.5 cm; stamens many, base united into 5 bundles, slightly shorter than petals. Ovary ovoid, 3– 4 mm, 5-locular; style 5-lobed. Capsules ovoid, 6 –10 × 4 –7 mm. Seeds dark red, ca. 1.3 mm.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. HK sheet 2695.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hunan, Sichuan, Hubei, Anhui, Zhejiang, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan, Henan, Hebei, Shaanxi, Shandong, Jiangxi.
Ecology: Flowering: May–Aug.; fruiting: Aug.–Sep.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal (folklore).

Hypericum sampsonii Hance 元寶草
J. Bot. 3: 378. 1865; FKH 41. 1912; FRPS 50(2): 60. 1990; FGD 3: 205. 1995.

Perennial herbs, 0.2–0.8 m tall, often branched above. Leaves opposite, in perfoliate pairs, oblong-lanceolate, 3 –15 × 1–3.5 cm, base wholly connate, apex obtuse or rounded, sparsely black glandular dotted; lateral veins ca. 4 pairs. Cymes terminal. Flowers yellow, 6 –15 mm in diam. Sepals elliptic or oblong, 3 –7 mm, with black glandular dotted. Petals oblong or obovate, 4– 8 mm, persistent, sparsely glandular dotted. Stamens united into 3 bundles. Ovary 3-locular; styles 3. Capsules ovoid to narrowly pyramidal, 6 –9 × 4 – 5 mm, with yellow-brown vesicular glands. Seeds orange-brown, ca. 1 mm.

Locality: Ma On Shan (Ngong Ping).
Distribution: Areas S of Changjiang River; India, Japan.
Ecology: Farmland. Flowering: Mar.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Elaeocarpus chinensis (Gardn. & Champ.) Hook. f. ex Benth. 中華杜英（野杜英）
FHK 43. 1861; FGD 1:118. 1987; FRPS 49 (1): 22, pl. 4:1– 6. 1989.
Friesia chinensis Gardn. & Champ., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 1: 243. 1849; l. c. 3: 264. 1851.
Elaeocarpus integripetalus Gagnep., Notul. Syst. (Paris) 11: 6. 1943

Small tree, 3 –7 m tall. Branchlets puberulous at first, glabrescent. Petioles 1.5 –2 cm; leaf blade ovate-lanceolate or lanceolate, 5 –8 × 2–3 cm, thin leathery, base rounded, rarely broadly cuneate, apex acuminate, margin minutely crenate, abaxially pubescent at first, later glabrescent, black glandular-punctate; lateral veins 4– 6 pairs. Racemes in axils of fallen leaves, 3– 4 cm; rachis and peduncles puberulous. Pedicels ca. 3 mm. Flowers polygamous. Bisexual flowers: sepals lanceolate, ca. 3 mm, puberulous on both surfaces. Petals oblong, ca. 3 mm, margin nearly entire, sparse-puberulous adaxially, glabrous abaxially. Stamens 8 –10, ca. 2 mm; filaments very short; anthers without hairs at apex. Ovary 2-locular. Male flowers: sepals and petals as in bisexual flowers; stamens 8 –10, without pistillodes. Drupe ellipsoid, 7– 8 mm, endocarp with 2 ventral sutures.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. S. C. Ng 3145; Y. W. Lam 645; P. S. Choi 30.
Distribution: Fujian, Zhejiang, Jiangxi, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan; Vietnam, Laos.
Ecology: Evergreen broadleaved forests. Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: Autumn.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Happy Valley Woods by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1849.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Tai Long Sai Wan, Long Ke
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Elaeocarpus decipiens Hemsl. 杜英
J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 23: 94. 1886; FGD 1: 117, fig. 123: 1A–1D. 1987; FRPS 49(1): 33, pl. 6: 10 –14. 1989.
Elaeocarpus lanceaefolius auct. non Roxb.: FHK 42. 1861; Forbes & Hemsley, J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 23: 95. 1885.

Small tree, 5 –15 m tall. Branchlets puberulous at first, glabrescent. Petioles ca. 1 cm; leaf blade oblanceolate, 7–12 × 2– 4 cm, leathery, base attenuate, apex acuminate, tip blunt, margin serrulate, glabrous on both surfaces; lateral veins 7–9 pairs. Racemes 5 –10 cm, puberulous; peduncles slender; pedicels 4 – 5 mm. Flowers bisexual. Sepals 5, lanceolate, ca. 5 – 6 mm. Petals 5, white, obovate, as long as sepals, puberulous near base adaxially, glabrous abaxially, laciniate on distal half; segments 10 –16. Stamens 25 –30, anthers without appendage at apex. Disc 5‑lobed, pubescent. Ovary 3-locular, tomentose; ovules 2 per locule. Drupe ellipsoid, 1-locular, 2–3 cm; exocarp glabrous; endocarp bony, with many ventral sutures; seed 1, ca. 1.5 cm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Long Sai Wan, Long Ke. H. C. Tang 2392; Y. S. Lau 166; Y. W. Lam 1335.
Distribution: Taiwan, Fujian, Zhejiang, Jiangxi, Hunan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan; Japan, Vietnam.
Ecology: Evergreen broadleaved forests. Flowering: Jun.–Jul.; fruiting: Autumn.
Uses: Ornamental.

Elaeocarpus dubius A. DC. 顯脈杜英（山模果）
Bull. Herb. Boiss. Ser. 2, 3: 366. 1903; FHN 2: 70. 1965; FGD 1: 121, fig. 126: 1A-1E. 1987; FRPS 49(1): 16, pl. 3: 1– 5. 1989.

Tree to 25 m tall. Branchlets slender, silver-grey-pubescent at first, glabrescent. Petioles slender, 1–2.5 cm; leaf blade oblong or lanceolate, 5–7(–10) × 2–2.5(–4) cm, thin leathery, base broadly cuneate or obtuse, apex acute or acuminate, margin crenate, glabrous; lateral veins 8–10 pairs, reticulation of veins conspicuous when dry. Racemes axillary, 3–5 cm; peduncles silvery grey-white pubescent, 4 –7-flowered. Pedicels 7–9 mm. Sepals 5, narrowly lanceolate, conspicuously keeled, 7–8 mm, puberulous on abaxial surface. Petals 5, as long as sepals, oblong, 7–8 × ca. 2.5 mm, grey-white-pubescent on both surfaces, distal 1/3 laciniate; segments 9–11. Stamens 20 –23; anthers ca. 3.5 mm, with awns (ca. 1.5 mm) at apex. Disc 10-lobed, pubescent. Ovary 3-locular, pubescent; style ca. 5 mm. Drupe ellipsoid, 1–1.3 cm, glabrous; endocarp bony, with 3 ventral sutures.

Locality: Tai Po, Wu Kau Tang. W. J. Tutcher 10219; Y. S. Lau 1516.
Distribution: Guangdong, Hainan, Guangxi, Yunnan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Evergreen broadleaved forests. Flowering: Mar.–Apr.; fruiting: Autumn.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: The species was misidentified as E. griffithii Mast. by Tutcher (Rep. Bot. For. Hongk. 1914: 30. 1915).

Elaeocarpus hainanensis Oliv. 水石榕
Hooker's Icon. Pl. 25: t. 2462. 1896; FHN 2: 67. 1965; FGD 1: 116, fig. 122: 1A–1E. 1987; FRPS 49(1): 8. 1989.

Small tree, to 5 m tall. Branchlets glabrous. Leaves clustered at twig apices; petioles 1–2 cm; leaf blade narrowly lanceolate, or oblanceolate, 7–15 × 1.5–3 cm, leathery, base cuneate, apex acuminate, margin denticulate, glabrous; lateral veins 14–16 pairs. Racemes axillary, 5–8 cm, 2–6-flowered. Flowers 3–4 cm in diam. Bracts persistent, leaf-like, sessile, ovate or elliptic, 1–1.6 cm, base rounded or auriculate, margin dentate. Pedicels 4 cm. Sepals 5, lanceolate, 1.2–2 cm. Petals 5, white, as long as sepals, obovate, hairy, apex laciniate; segments 30–46, 4–6 mm. Stamens many; connective prolonged and awn-like. Disc many-lobed, tomentose. Ovary 2-locular, glabrous; ovules 2 per locule. Style ca. 1 cm. Drupe fusiform, 4–5 cm, ca. 1–1.2 cm in diam.; endocarp hard, with 2 ventral sutures. Seeds ca. 2 cm.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 1492; P. S. Choi 359.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, SW Guangxi, SE Yunnan; Vietnam, Thailand and Myanmar.
Ecology: Flowering: Jun.–Jul.; fruiting: Jul.–Sep.
Uses: Ornamental.

Elaeocarpus japonicus Sieb. & Zucc. 日本杜英
Abh. Math.-Phys. Cl. Konigl. Bayer. Akad. Wiss. 4: pt. 2. 165. 1845; FGD 1: 119. fig. 125: 2A–2D. 1987; FRPS 49(1): 20. 1989.
Elaeocarpus yunnanensis Brandis ex Tutch., Rep. Bot. For. Dept. Hongk. 1914: 30. 1915.
Elaeocarpus japonicus var. euplebius Merr., Lingnan Sci. J. 5: 123. 1928; FHN 2: 68. 1965.

Tree, to 25 m tall. Branchlets glabrous. Buds sericeous. Petioles 2– 6 cm; leaf blade varied in shape and size, often ovate, sometimes elliptic, obovate, or lanceolate to narrowly oblong, 6–12(–17) × 3–6 cm, leathery, base rounded or obtuse, acute, or broadly cuneate, apex acuminate or acute, margin sparsely dentate, both surfaces densely silvery-grey-sericeous at first, glabrescent, black glandular-punctate abaxially; lateral veins 5– 8 pairs. Racemes axillary, 3– 6 cm. Flowers polygamous. Pedicels 3– 4 mm, puberulous. Bisexual flowers: sepals oblong, ca. 4 mm, pubescent on both surfaces. Petals oblong, as long as sepals, entire or incised, pubescent on both surfaces or only on abaxial surface. Stamens 15; anthers ca. 2 mm, without awns at apex, puberulous. Disc 5- or 10-lobed. Ovary pubescent, 3‑locular; style ca. 3 mm, pubescent. Male flowers: stamens 9 –12; pistillodes present or not. Drupe ellipsoid, 1–1.3 × ca. 0.8 cm, shiny, with 3 ventral sutures; seed 1, ca. 8 mm.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island. Y. W. Lam 2159; Y. S. Lau 298; N. K. Chun 40646.
Distribution: Areas S of Changjiang River; Vietnam, Japan.
Ecology: Evergreen broadleaved forests. Flowering: Apr. –May; fruiting: May–Jul.
Uses: Ornamental.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Pok Fa Lam, Wu Kau Tang, Sheung Wo Hang
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Elaeocarpus nitentifolius Merr. & Chun 絹毛杜英
Sunyatsenia 2: 279. 1935; FHN 2: 68. 1965; FGD 1: 119, fig. 125: 1A–1E. 1987; FRPS 49(1): 19, pl. 5: 1– 5. 1989.

Tree to 20 m tall. Branchlets and petioles silvery-white-sericeous. Petioles 2–4 cm; leaf blade elliptic or oblong, 8–15 × 3.5–7.5 cm, leathery, base broadly cuneate, apex long acuminate or nearly caudate, margin densely serrulate, adaxially glabrescent, sericeous along veins, abaxially silvery-white-sericeous, not black-punctate; lateral veins 6 – 8 pairs. Racemes axillary, 2–4.5 cm; rachis hairy; bracts caducous, lanceolate. Flowers polygamous, usually pendulous. Pedicels 4 – 5 mm. Sepals 4 – 5, lanceolate, 4 mm, gray-puberulous abaxially. Petals 4– 5, oblong, ca. 4 mm, glabrous, incised, with 5 or 6 segements. Stamens 12–15; anthers without awns at apex. Disc inconspicuously lobed. Ovary 2-locular, sparsely sericeous; style ca. 2.5 mm, pubescent, 2- or 3-lobed at apex. Drupe ellipsoid, small, shining, 1.5 –2 × 1 cm.

Locality: Pok Fa Lam, Wu Kau Tang, Sheung Wo Hang. W. J. Tutcher 11152; Y. W. Lam 1278; K. L. Yip 4464.
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong, Hainan, Guangxi, Yunnan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Evergreen broadleaved forests. Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: Sep.
Uses: Ornamental.

Elaeocarpus sylvestris (Lour.) Poir. 山杜英（膽八樹）
Encycl. Suppl. 11: 704. 1811; FGD 1: 121, fig. 121: 1A–1F. 1987; FRPS 49(1): 24, pl. 1: 1– 6. 1989.
Adenodus sylvestris Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 294. 1790.
Elaeocarpus henryi Hance, J. Bot. 23: 322. 1885.
