Elaeocarpus kwangtungensis Hu, J. Arnold Arbor. 5: 229. 1924.

Trees to 15 m tall. Branchlets slender, glabrous or sparsely pilose. Petioles 1–1.5 cm; leaf blade narrowly obovate, 4–8 × 2–4 cm, papery, base narrowly cuneate, apex ± rounded, margin crenate, glabrous on both surfaces; lateral veins usually 5 –6 pairs. Racemes axillary, 4–6 cm, glabrous. Flowers bisexual. Pedicels 3–5 mm, slender, glabrous. Sepals 5, lanceolate, ca. 4 mm, sparsely pubescent. Petals 5, obovate, laciniate on distal half; segments 10–12, pubescent at base abaxially. Stamens ca. 15, 3 mm; anthers without awns at apex. Disc 5-lobed, white-pubescent. Ovary pubescent, 2–3-locular; style ca. 2 mm. Drupe ellipsoid, 1–1.2 cm; endocarp thinly bony, with 3 ventral sutures.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1126; P. S. Choi 140; K. L. Yip 4495.
Distribution: Fujian, Zhejiang, Jiangxi, Hunan, Guangdong, Hainan, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Evergreen broadleaved forests. Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: May–Aug.
Uses: Ornamental.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Wong Nai Chung, Aberdeen, Repulse Bay, Shing Mun, Tai Mo Shan, Sham Tseng, Tate's Cairn, Ma On Shan, Pat Sin Leng
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Sloanea sinensis (Hance) Hemsl. 猴歡喜
Hooker's Icon. Pl. 27(2): t. 2628. 1900; FGD 1: 123, fig. 129. 1987; FRPS 49(1): 43, pl. 9. 1989.
Echinocarpus sinensis Hance, J. Bot. 22: 103. 1884; FKH 52. 1912.
Sloanea hongkongensis Hemsl., Hook. Icon. Pl. t. 2628. 1900; Hayata, Fl. Form. 49. 1911; FKH 52. 1912.
Sloanea sinensis Hu, J. Arnold Arbor. 5: 230. 1924.
Sloanea chinensis Hu, Contr. Biol. Lab. Sci. Soc. China 1: 4. 1925, nom. illeg.
Sloanea oligophlebia Chun & Ting, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 8: 269. 1963.
Sloanea parvifolia Chun & How, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 7: 14, pl. 5. 1958; FHN 2: 65. 1965.

Tree to 20 m tall. Branchlets glabrous. Petioles 1– 4 cm; leaf blade variable in shape and size, usually oblong or narrowly obovate, 6 –12 × 3 – 5 cm, thinly leathery, base cuneate or rounded, apex acute, margin usually entire or rarely sparsely dentate on distal half, glabrous; lateral veins 5 –7 pairs. Flowers clustered, axillary. Pedicels 3 – 6 cm. Sepals 4, broadly ovate, 6 – 8 × 5 – 6 mm, puberulous. Petals 4, white, 7–9 mm, puberulous, laciniate at apices. Stamens many, as long as petals; anthers awned at apex. Ovary ovoid, 3–7- locular, 4 – 5 mm, pubescent; style 1, 4– 6 mm, puberulous on proximal half. Capsule variable in size, 2–4 cm in diam., dehiscing into 3 –7 valves; prickles 1–1.5 cm; endocarp purple-red. Seeds black, shiny, 1–1.3 cm; aril yellow.

Locality: Wong Nai Chung, Aberdeen, Repulse Bay, Shing Mun, Tai Mo Shan, Sham Tseng, Tate's Cairn, Ma On Shan, Pat Sin Leng. H. C. Tang 1861; Y. S. Lau 2386; Y. W. Lam 1377.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Zhejiang, Taiwan; Cambodia, Laos, Myanmar, Thailand, Vietnam.
Ecology: Evergreen broadleaved forests. Flowering: Jun.– Oct.; fruiting: May–Nov.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: The type specimen of Sloanea hongkongensis was collected from Happy Valley and Aberdeen New Road by W. J. Tutcher (Herb. Hongk. No. 611) in 1895.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Sha Tin, Sai Kung, Tai Long Sai Wan, Tsing Yi, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Corchorus aestuans L. 甜麻（假黃麻）
Syst. Nat. (ed. 10) 1079. 1774; FTW 3: 695. 1977; FFJ 3: 396, fig. 279. 1987; FRPS 49(1): 80, pl. 20: 4 –7. 1989; FGD 4: 163. fig. 105. 2000.
Corchorus acutangulus Lam., Encycl. 2: 104. 1786; FHK 40. 1861; FKH 50. 1912; FHN 2: 64. 1965.

Annual herbs, up to ca. 1 m tall; stem red brown, slightly yellowish puberulous. Stipules subulate, 4mm. Petioles ca. 0.5–2 cm, pale yellow-hispid; leaf blade ovate, 2–6.5 × 1– 4 cm, base rounded, apex short acuminate or acute, margin serrate, one pair of teeth near base usually elongating into caudate appendages, sparsely hispid on both surfaces; basal veins 3, lateral veins 3– 6 pairs. Peduncle and pedicels very short or almost obsolete. Sepals 5, narrowly oblong, ca. 5 mm, boat-shaped at distal half, horned at apex, purple red abaxially. Petals nearly as long as sepals, obovate, yellow. Stamens many, ca. 3 mm, yellow. Ovary long cylindric, pubescent. Style clavate; stigma 5-toothed. Capsule cylindrical, angular cylindric, ca. 1.5–3 cm, 6-ribbed, 3–4 of the ribs expaned into narrow wings, terminating in 3 entire or bifid points or horns, dehiscing into 3–4 valves when mature. Seeds many.

Locality: Sha Tin, Sai Kung, Tai Long Sai Wan, Tsing Yi, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 899, 2382.
Distribution: Areas S of Changjiang River; tropical Asia, C America, Africa.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides and near villages. Flowering & fruiting: Summer to autumn.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Ma On Shan, Tai Po, Fanling, Luk Keng, Sha Po, Pui O (cultivated or naturalized)
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Corchorus capsularis L. 黃麻
Sp. Pl. 529. 1753; FHK 40. 1861; FKH 50. 1912; FHN 2: 63. 1965; FRPS 49(1): 78. 1989; FGD 4: 163. 2000.

Annual erect woody herbs, 1–2.5 m tall, glabrous; stems erect woody. Stipules filiform, deciduous. Petioles 1–3.5 cm; leaf blade ovate lanceolate or lanceolate, 5–12 × 2–5 cm, papery, base round, apex acuminate, margin rough coarsely serrate, one pair of teeth near base subulate and curved downward; 3 basal veins ascending but not exceeding middle of leaf blade, lateral veins 6–7 pairs. Peduncle and pedicels short. Sepals 5, pale purple, 3 –4 mm. Petals yellow, narrowly obovate, as long as sepals. Stamens 8–22, inserted on short androgynophore. Ovary globose, 5-locular; stigma lobed. Capsule globose, 1 cm in diam., without horns at apex, ribbed and verrucose on the surface, dehiscing into 5 valves when mature.

Locality: Ma On Shan, Tai Po, Fanling, Luk Keng, Sha Po, Pui O (cultivated or naturalized). Y. S. Lau 1313, 1991; Y. W. Lam 1234.
Distribution: Commonly cultivated in regions S of Changjiang River; native to tropical Asia.
Ecology: Flowering: Summer; fruiting: Late autumn.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Tam, Aberdeen, Cape D'Aguilar, Sai Kung, Tai Wan, Beaufort Island, Po Toi
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Grewia biloba G. Don 扁擔桿
Gen. Hist. 1: 549. 1831; FFJ 3: 401, fig. 282. 1987; FRPS 49(1): 94, pl. 24: 5 –9. 1989; FGD 4: 158, fig. 101. 2000.
Grewia glabrescens Benth., FHK 42. 1861; FKH 51. 1912.
Grewia parviflora Bunge var. glabrescens Rehd. & Wils., Pl. Wils. 2: 371. 1916.
Grewia biloba G. Don var. parviflora auct. non (Bunge) Hand.-Mazz.: Check List HK Plants 43.1993.

Shrub or small tree, 1–2.5 m tall, much branched. Branchlets covered with yellow stellate hairs. Stipules subulate, 3–4 mm; petioles 6–15 mm, stellate hairy; leaf blade ovate, rhomboid-orbicular or obovate elliptic, 4–12 × 2.5–7 cm, thin leathery, base cuneate or obtuse, apex acute, margin irregularly serrate, rough and sparsely stellatehispid abaxially and adaxially; basal veins 3, lateral veins 3–5 on each side of midvein. Cymes axillary, many-flowered, peduncle less than 1 cm. Pedicels 3–6 mm, bract subulate, 3–5 mm. Sepals narrow oblong, 4 –7 mm, hairy abaxially, glabrous adaxially. Petals 1–1.5 mm. Stamens 2 mm. Ovary hairy; style as long as sepals; stigma swollen, disk-shaped, lobed. Drupe red, with 2–4 drupelets.

Locality: Tai Tam, Aberdeen, Cape D'Aguilar, Sai Kung, Tai Wan, Beaufort Island, Po Toi. Y. W. Lam 1563, 653; S. P. Lau 166.
Distribution: Taiwan, Zhejiang, Jiangxi, Anhui, Hunan, Hubei, Guangdong, Sichuan.
Ecology: Shrubby forests. Flowering: May–Jul; fruiting: Jul.–Sep.

Grewia eriocarpa Juss. 毛果扁擔桿
Ann. Mus. Natl. Hist. Nat. 4: 93. 1804; FHN 2: 60. 1965; FRPS 49(1): 91, pl. 24: 1– 5. 1989; FGD 4: 156. 2000.
Grewia celtidifolia Juss. var. eriocarpa (Juss.) Hsu & Zhuge, Bot. Journ. South China 2: 19. 1993.
Grewia asiatica auct. non L.: FKH 51. 1912 (quoad Birdwood s.n.).

Shrub or small tree, 1– 8 m tall. Young branchlets grey stellate-pubscent; branchlets subglabrous, dark brown to brown after dried. Stipules linear-lanceolate, 0.5–1 cm; petioles 0.6 –1 cm, densely stellate hairy; leaf blade oblique ovate or ovate-oblong, 6–13 × 3 – 6(–9) cm, papery, base oblique and rounded, apex acuminate or acute, margin serrulate, sparsely stellate hairy and rough adaxially, grey stellate-pubescent abaxially; basal veins usually 5, rarely 4 or 6, lateral veins 2–3 pairs. Cymes 3- to several-flowered, axillary, 1.5 –3 cm, densely yellow or greyish yellow stellate-pubescent; peduncle 3 – 8 mm. Bract lanceolate, densely yellow or greyish yellow stellate-pubescent abaxially. Flowers bisexual. Sepals narrowly oblong, 6–8 mm, hairy on both surfaces. Petals subulate, ca. 3 mm, glands less than 1 mm. Stamens distinct, unequal, shorter than sepals. Ovary densely villose. Style pubescent; stigma peltate, 4-lobed or entire. Drupe subglobose, 6– 8 mm in diam., stellate hairy, slightly grooved or nearly smooth, apex mucronate, not divided into drupelets.

Locality: Cultivated but nowadays not common. L. T. Lo 458; Y. S. Lau 381; Birdwood s.n. (HK sheet 3763).
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Taiwan, Yunnan; India, Indochina, Indonesia, Philippines.
Ecology: Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: Jun.–Jul.
Notes: This species was reported as Grewia tiliaefolia Vahl (椴葉扁擔桿) previously (Check List HK Plants 94. 2002).

Grewia oligandra Pierre 寡蕊扁擔桿（粗毛扁擔桿）
Fl. Forest. Cochinch. 2: 163. 1888; FRPS 49(1): 102. 1989; FGD 4: 157. 2000.

Shrub. Branchlets stellate tomentose, old branches dark brown. Stipules subulate, 4 mm, caducous. Petioles 5–8 mm, densely stellate-tomentose; leaf blade lanceolate or oblong lanceolate, 9–10.5 × 2–3.5 cm, papery, base round, apex acute, margin serrulate with alternating large and small teeth, sparsely stellate-hispidulous and dark brown when dry adaxially, densely grey-brown-tomentose abaxially; basal veins 3, lateral veins 4–5 pairs. Cymes 3–5-flowered; peduncle 4–7 mm, tomentose. Pedicels 3–4 mm, tomentose. Bracts 3–4 mm. Sepals 5– 6 mm, tomentose abaxially, glabrous adaxially. Petals oblong, 2–3 mm; glands scale-like, surrounded by hairs. Stamens shorter than sepals. Ovary hairy; stigma multi-lobed. Drupe double or tetra-globose, 1 cm in diam., shiny; stalk 0.5–1 cm, densely tomentose.

Locality: Chuen Lung. Y. S. Lau 2542, 2331; L.T. Lo 382.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi; Indochina.
Ecology: Shrubby forests or thin forests. Flowering: Jul.–Aug.; fruiting: Sep.– Oct.
Notes: This species was reported as Grewia hirsuta Vahl previously (Check List HK Plants 94. 2002).

Microcos nervosa (Lour.) S. Y. Hu 破布葉（布渣葉）
J. Arnold Arbor. 69(1): 79. 1988.
Fallopia nervosa Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 336. 1790.
Grewia microcos L., Syst. Ed 12. 2: 602. 1767; FHK 42. 1861; FKH 51. 1912.
Microcos paniculata auct. non. L.: FHN 2: 58. 1965; FFJ 3: 402, fig. 283. 1987; FRPS 49(1): 87. 1989; FGD 4: 154, fig. 100. 2000.

Shrub or small tree, 3 –12 m tall. Branchlets hairy. Stipule linear-lanceolate, 5 –7 mm. Petioles 1–1.5 cm, hairy; leaf blade ovate or ovate oblong, 8 –18 × 4 – 8 cm, thin leathery, base round, apex acuminate, margin finely serrulate, stellate-pubescent initially, glabrescent on both surfaces in age. Inflorescence paniculate, terminal or axillary, 4 –10 cm, stellate hairy; bracts lanceolate, yellowish-pubescent and stellate-pubescent; pedicels short and slender. Sepals oblong, 5–7 mm, stellate hairy abaxially. Petals oblong, about 1/3 –1/2 the length of sepals, yellowish-pubescent on both surfaces; glands as large as half of petals. Stamens shorter than sepals. Ovary subglobose, glabrous, dark brown; stigma pointed. Drupe subglobose or obovoid, ca. 1 × 0.7 cm, dark brown, glabrous.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. S. P. Lau 150.
Distribution: Guangdong, Hainan, Guangxi, Yunnan; SE Asia.
Ecology: Thickets on hillslopes. Flowering: Jun.–Jul.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Aberdeen, Sai Kung, Tai Mo Shan, Yuen Tun Ha, Shek Kong, Tai To Yan, Wu Kau Tang
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Triumfetta cana Bl. 毛刺蒴麻
Bojer. 1: 126. 1825; FRPS 49(1): 106. 1989; FGD 4: 161. 2000.
Triumfetta pilosa auct. non Roth: FHK 41. 1861.
Triumfetta pseudocana Sprag. & Craib, Kew Bull. Misc. Inform. 1: 23. 1911.
Triumfetta tomentosa Bojer, Bouton Rapp. Ann. Maur. 19. 1842; FHN 2: 62. 1965.

Erect subshrub, 0.6 –2 m tall. Branchlets densely yellowish brown-stellate-tomentose. Petioles 0.5–3 cm; leaf blade ovate or ovate lanceolate, 4– 8 × 2.4 cm, papery, base rounded, apex acuminate, margin irregularly serrate, adaxial surface sparsely, abaxial surface densely stellate-tomentose; basal veins 3– 5. Cymes often 2–6 clustered in leaf axils; peduncle ca. 3 mm; pedicels 1.5 mm. Sepals narrowly oblong, 5–7 mm, stellate-tomentose abaxially. Petals oblong, slightly shorter than sepals, yellow, shortly stalked at base, sparsely stellate-tomentose. Stamens 8 –10(–12). Ovary covered with spiny hairs, 4-locular; stigma 3 – 5-lobed. Capsule globose, ca. 1–1.5 cm in diam. with spines, dehiscing into 4 valves, spines slender, 5– 8 mm, curved, tip straight, not hooked, pubescent. Seeds 2 per locule.

Locality: Aberdeen, Sai Kung, Tai Mo Shan, Yuen Tun Ha, Shek Kong, Tai To Yan, Wu Kau Tang. Y. S. Lau 2633; P. S. Choi 371; H. C. Tang 1422.
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Xizang; SE Asia.
Ecology: Secondary forests and dry thickets. Flowering & fruiting: Summer to autumn.

Triumfetta rhomboidea Jacq. 刺蒴麻
Enum. Syst. Pl. 22. 1760; FRPS 49(1): 109. 1989; FGD 4: 160, fig. 103. 2000.
Triumfetta bartramia L., Syst. ed. 10: 1044. 1757, nom. superfl. for Bartramia indica L.; FHN 2: 62. 1965.
Bartramia indica L., Sp. Pl. 389. 1753, non Triumfetta indica Lam. 1791.
Triumfetta angulata Lam., Encycl. 3: 421. 1791; FHK 41. 1861.

Erect subshrub, 0.5 –1.5 m. Branchlets greyish browntomentose. Petioles 1– 5 cm; leaf blade variable, those on the lower part of stem broadly ovate-orbicular, or rhomboid-ovate, 3 – 8 × 2– 6 cm, papery, upper part 3-lobed, base rounded; those on the upper part of stem smaller, oblong to ovate-lanceolate, not lobed, sparsely hairy adaxially, stellate-pubescent abaxially; margin irregularly serrate; basal veins 3 – 5. Cymes several in leaf axils. Peduncle and pedicels very short. Sepals narrowly oblong, 5– 6 mm, with a mucro at apex, stellate-hispid abaxially. Petals slightly shorter than sepals, yellow, hairy along margin. Stamens 10. Ovary spiny. Capsule subglobose, ca. 4 – 6 mm in diam. with spines, indehiscent, grey yellow-pubescent; spines 2–3 mm, glabrous, hooked. Seeds 2– 6 per locule.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 2079; L. T. Lo 191; Y. S. Lau 2184.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; tropical Asia and Africa.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides and thickets. Flowering & fruiting: Summer to autumn.

Abroma augusta (L.) L. f. 昂天蓮
Suppl. Pl. 341, 1781; FHN 2: 85. 1965; FRPS 49(2): 181. 1984; FGD 1: 148. 1987.
Theobroma angusta L., Syst. Nat. (ed. 12) 233. 1767.
Abroma fastuosa Jacq., Hort. Vind. 3: 3, t. 1. 1776; FKH 50. 1912.

Shrub, 1– 4 m tall. Branchlets densely stellate-tomentose. Petioles 1–10 cm; leaves cordate or ovate-cordate, occasionally slightly 3– 5-lobed, 10 –22 × 9 –18 cm, base cordate or obliquely cordate, apex acute or acuminate, sparsely stellate pubescent adaxially, densely tomentose abaxially. Cymes 1– 5-flowered. Flowers purple; sepals lanceolate, 15 –18 mm; petals 2– 5 cm; ovary oblong, ca. 1–5 mm. Capsules membranous, obconic, 3–6 in diam., apex truncate, stellate-hairy, 5-winged, margin long tomentose. Seeds black, ellipsoid, ca. 2 mm.

Locality: Cultivated, though not common nowadays. HK sheet 543, 544, 3732.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou; India, Vietnam, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia, Philippines.
Ecology: Flowering: Spring to summer.

Byttneria aspera Colebr. 刺果藤
Fl. Ind. ed. Carey, 2: 283. 1824; FRPS 49(2): 186. 1984; FGD 1: 149. 1987.
Buettneria aspera Colebr. in Roxb., Fl. Ind. ed. Carey, 2: 283. 1824; FHK 39. 1861; FKH 50. 1912; FHN 2: 86. 1965;.

Large woody climber, slightly tomentose on young parts. Petioles 2–8 cm, hairy; leaves broad-ovate, cordate or suborbicular, 7–23 × 5.5 –16 cm, base cordate, apex obtuse or acute, nearly glabrous adaxially, white stellate-pubescent abaxially, 5-veined. Panicles shorter than leaves. Flowers small, yellowish and slightly pink adaxially; sepals ovate, 2 mm, pubescent; petals shortly bifid at top, with linear appendage longer or equal to sepals; staminal tube short; anther alternate with staminodes. Capsules globose, 3 – 4 cm in diam., covered with short stout prickles, pubescent. Seeds black, oblong, ca. 12 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 503, 2218; H. C. Tang 2159.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; India, Vietnam, Cambodia, Laos, Thailand.
Ecology: Margin of forests or valleys. Flowering: Spring to summer.
Uses: Fibre, medicinal.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Deep Water Bay, Shek O (Tai Long Wan), Sai Kung, Sai Wan, Po Toi. Cultivated or naturalized
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Firmiana simplex (L.) W. Wight 梧桐
U.S.D.A. Bur. Pl. Industr. Bull. 142: 67. 1909; FHN 2: 75. 1965; FGD 1: 130 1987.
Hibiscus simplex L., Sp. Pl. ed. 2, 2: 977. 1763.
Firmiana platanifolia (L. f.) Marsili, Sagg. Sci. Lett. Acc. Padova 1: 106 –116. 1786; FRPS 49(2): 134. 1984.
Sterculia plantanifolia L. f., Suppl. Pl. 423. 1781; FHK 36. 1861; FKH 49. 1912.

Deciduous tree; bark green, smooth. Petioles as long as leaf-blade; leaf blade suborbicular in outline, palmately 3 –5-lobed, 15–30 cm in diam., base cordate, apex acuminate, glabrous or slightly pubescent abaxially, 7-veined. Panicles terminal 20– 50 cm; calyx yellowgreenish, 5-lobed, lobes linear, 7–9 mm, abaxially yellowish pubescent; anthers about 15; cells usually unequal and very irregularly crowded in a terminal head, often with imperfect, sessile anthers round the base of ovary in female flowers. Follicles stipulate, dehiscent before maturity, each carpel with seeds 1–2 on edge near base.

Locality: Deep Water Bay, Shek O (Tai Long Wan), Sai Kung, Sai Wan, Po Toi. Cultivated or naturalized.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; Japan.
Ecology: Flowering: Jun.
Uses: Ornamental, timber.

Helicteres angustifolia L. 山芝麻
Sp. Pl. 963. 1753; FHK 37. 1861; FKH 50. 1912; FHN 2: 80. 1965; FGD 1: 141. 1987; FRPS 49(2): 156. 1984.

Small shrub, to 1 m tall. Branchlets grey-green pubescent. Petioles 5–7 mm; leaves narrow-oblong or linear-lanceolate, 3.5–5 × 1.5–2.5 cm, base rounded, apex obtuse or acute, glabrous or nearly so adaxially, grey white or yellowish stellate-tomentose abaxially, sometimes mixed setae. Cymes 2–several-flowered; bracteoles 4; calyx 4 mm, stellate-pubescent, 5-lobed; lobes triangular ; petals 5, reddish or purple, with 2 appendages at base; stamens 10; staminal column 10-cleft, with 1-celled anther; staminodes 5; ovary 5-locular, hairy. Capsules straight, ovoid-oblong, 12–20 × 7–8 mm, apex acute, densely stellate hairy and mixed with long tangled hairs. Seeds brown with small elliptic spots.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 595; Y. S. Lau 2202; K. L. Yip 4381.
Distribution: Taiwan, Fujian, Jiangxi, Hunan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; India, Myanmar, Malaysia, Vietnam, Cambodia, Laos, Thailand, Indonesia, Philippines.
Ecology: Grassy slopes or thickets. Flowering: May–Aug.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), fibre.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Po Kau, Yung Shue O, Lai Chi Wo
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Heritiera littoralis Aiton 銀葉樹
Hort. Kew, 3: 546. 1789; FHK 36. 1861; FKH 49. 1912; FHN 2: 76. 1965; FRPS 49(2): 140. 1984; FGD 1: 133. 1987.

Evergreen tree. Branchlets white lepidote when young. Petioles 1–2 cm; leaves leathery, oblong-lanceolate, elliptic or ovate, 10 –20 × 5 –10 cm, base obtuse, apex acute or obtuse, margin entire, densely silvery-lepidote abaxially. Panicles axillary, manyflowered densely stellate-hairy and lepidote. Flowers red-brown; calyx campanulate, 4– 6 mm. Male flower: stamens 4– 5. Female flowers with 4–5 carpels; stigmas as many as carpels. Ripe carpels woody, yellow-brown, nut-like, ovoid, 6 × 3.5 cm, with a slightly projecting inner edge, and a strong projecting almost winged keel along the outer edge.

Locality: Tai Po Kau, Yung Shue O, Lai Chi Wo. Y. W. Lam 683; Y. S. Lau 1698; H. C. Tang 1436.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan, Taiwan; Japan, Philippines, SE Asia, E Africa, Australia.
Ecology: Seashores. Flowering: Autumn.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong, Ma Liu Shui, Fanling, Ho Pui, Sha Po, Tuen Mun
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Melochia corchorifolia L. 馬鬆子
Sp. Pl. 675. 1753; FHN 2: 82. 1965; FRPS 49(2): 167. 1984; FGD 1: 143. 1987.

Subshrub, less than 1 m tall. Branchlets slightly stellatepubescent. Stipules linear, 2– 4 mm. Petioles 5 –25 mm; leaves thinly papery, ovate, oblong-ovate or lanceolate, rarely indistinctly 3-lobed, 2.5 –7 × 1–1.3 cm, base rounded or cordate, margin serrate, apex acute or obtuse, nearly glabrous adaxially, slightly stellate-pubescent abaxially, 5-veined. Cymes or glomes terminal or axillary; bracteoles linear; calyx campanulate, slightly 5- lobed, hairy; petals reddish, oblong, ca. 6 mm, base attenuate; ovary densely pubescent. Capsules globose, 5 – 6 mm in diam., 5-angulate, pilose. Seeds brown-black, subtriangular, 2–3 mm.

Locality: Hong Kong, Ma Liu Shui, Fanling, Ho Pui, Sha Po, Tuen Mun. Y. W. Lam 673; L. T. Lo 221; W. J. Tutcher 11554.
Distribution: Areas S of Changjiang River, Taiwan; tropical Asia.
Ecology: Open fields. Flowering: Summer to autumn.
Uses: Fibre.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Ho Chung, Tai Mo Shan, Tai Po, Pat Sin Leng, Kop Tong, Au Ha, Ha Wo Hang, Ma Wan, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Pterospermum heterophyllum Hance 翻白葉樹
J. Bot. 6: 112. 1865; FKH 50. 1912; FHN 2: 84. 1965; FRPS 49(2): 178. 1984; FGD 1: 146. 1987.
Pterospermum acerifolium auct. non (L.) Willd.: FHK 39. 1861.

Tree. Leaves on coppices: petioles 12 cm; leave blade peltate, palmately 3 – 5-lobed, ca. 15 cm in diam., densely brown stellatepubescent abaxially; leaves on normal branches: petioles 1–2 cm; leave blade oblong to ovate-oblong, 7–15 × 3–10 cm, brown pubescent abaxially. Flowers solitary or 3– 4 in cymes, axillary; bracteoles squamiform; sepals linear, up to 28 mm; petals oblanceolate, equaling sepals; androgynophore 2.5 mm; stamens 15; staminodes 5, linear, slightly longer than fertile stamens; ovary ovoid, 5-locular, hairy. Capsules woody, oblong-ovoid, 6 × 2–2.5 cm, yellow-brown tomentose, stalk thick, 1–1.5 cm. Seeds winged.

Locality: Ho Chung, Tai Mo Shan, Tai Po, Pat Sin Leng, Kop Tong, Au Ha, Ha Wo Hang, Ma Wan, Lantau Island. S. T. Dunn 7143; Y. S. Lau 2624; P. S. Choi 267.
Distribution: Guangxi, Guangdong, Fujian.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Autumn.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), materials (timber, fibre).

Reevesia thyrsoidea Lindl. 梭羅樹
Quart. Journ. Sci. Lit. Arts, 2(2): 112. 1827; FHK 37. 1861; FKH 49. 1912; FRPS 49(2): 150. 1984; FHN 2: 79. 1965; FGD 1: 137. 1987.

Tree; bark grey-brown. Petioles 1–3 cm, inflated at both ends; leaves leathery, lanceolate or ovate-lanceolate, 5 –7 × 2.5 –3 cm, base round or obtuse, apex acute or acuminate, margin quite entire, glabrous on both surfaces. Inflorencence corymbose, terminal. Flowers dense; calyx campanulate, 6 mm, 5-lobed, stellate hairy abaxially; petals 5, white, spathulate, 1 cm, slightly spreading; androgynophore ca. 2 cm, with 15 anthers at apex forming a terminal head; ovary globose, 5-locular, hairy. Capsules ellipsoid, pear-shaped, ca. 3 cm, 5-angulate.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 851; K. T. Tso 20207; N. K. Chun 40707.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; Vietnam, Cambodia.
Ecology: Secondary forests, thickets and grassland. Flowering: Mar.–Apr.
Uses: Fibre, timber.

Sterculia lanceolata Cav. 假蘋婆
Diss. 5: 287, pl. 143, fig. 1. 1788; FHK 36. 1861; FKH 49. 1912; FHN 2: 73. 1965; FRPS 49(2): 132. 1984; FGD 1: 129. 1987.

Tree. Petioles 2.5–3.5 cm; leaves leathery, elliptic, lanceolate or elliptic-oblong, 9–20 × 3.5–8 cm, base obtuse or subrounded, apex acute, margin entire; lateral veins 7–9 pairs, curved, connected near margin. Panicles much branched, axillary, more or less tomentose; calyx 5-parted nearly to base, segments stellately spreading, green and slightly reddish at base, oblong-lanceolate, 4–6 mm, margin ciliate, abaxially pubescent; staminal column shorter than sepals; anthers 10, nearly sessile on outside of the very short lobes, forming a terminal globose head. Follicles bright scarlet, long-ovate or oblong, 5 –7 × 2–2.5 cm, base attenuate, apex rostrate, densely pubescent. Seeds black-brown, ellipsoid-ovoid, 1 cm in diam.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1363; H. C. Tang 460, 845.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou, Sichuan; Myanmar, Vietnam, Thailand, Laos.
Ecology: Lowland secondary forests and valleys. Flowering: Apr.–May.
Uses: Fibre, medicinal (folklore), ornamental.

Sterculia nobilis Smith 蘋婆
Cycl. no. 4. 1816; FKH 49. 1912; FHN 2: 73. 1965; FRPS 49(2): 121. 1984; FGD 1: 127. 1987.

Tree, bark brown-black. Petioles 2–3.5 cm; leaves thinly leathery, oblong or elliptic, 8–25 × 4 –15 cm, base rounded or obtuse, apex acute or obtuse, glabrous on both surfaces. Panicles terminal or axillary. Male flowers: calyx initially milk-white, becoming reddish, campanulate, ca. 10 mm, pubescent abaxially, 5-fid, lobes linear-lanceolate, as long as calyx tube, incurved and sticking together at apex; staminal column curved; anther yellow. Female flowers: slightly larger than male; ovary globose, 5-grooved. Follicles scarlet, thickly leathery, ellipsoid-ovoid, 5 × 2–3 cm, apex rostrate. Seeds 1–4 per follicle, black-brown, ca. 1.5 cm in diam.

Locality: Tsuen Wan, Shatin. Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 2723; HK sheet 3603.
Distribution: Yunnan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Vietnam, Indonesia.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr.–May.
Uses: Food, ornamental.

Waltheria indica L. 蛇婆子
Sp. Pl. 673. 1753; FKH 50. 1912; FRPS 49(2): 169. 1984;
Waltheria americana L., Sp. Pl. 673. 1753; FHK 38. 1861; FHN 2: 83. 1965; FGD 1: 144. 1987.

Suberect or decumbent subshrubs, up to 1 m or taller, many branched. Branchlets densely pubescent. Petioles 0.5–1 cm; leaves ovate or oblong-ovate, 2.5–4.5 × 1.5–3 cm, base rounded or shallow-cordate, margin serrulate, apex obtuse, densely pubescent on both surfaces. Cymes axillary, head-form; bracteoles narrowlanceolate, ca. 4 mm; calyx tubiform, 5-lobed; lobes triangular, longer than tube; petals 5, yellowish, spathulate, slightly longer than calyx; stamens 5; filaments connate, enclosing ovary; ovary sessile, pubescent; styles excentric; stigma fimbriate. Capsules obovate, ca. 3 mm, opening into 2 valves, hairy, enclosed by persistent calyx. Seeds obovate, minute.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Lantau Island. P. S. Choi 250; Y. S. Lau 3000; Gibbson 7710.
Distribution: Taiwan, Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; widely distributed in tropical regions of the world.
Ecology: Sunny hillslopes. Flowering: Summer to autumn.

Bombax ceiba L. 木棉
Sp. Pl. 511. 1753.
Gossampinus malabarica (DC.) Merr., Lingnan Sci. J. 5: 126. 1927; FGZ 243. 1956; FHN 2: 87, fig. 337. 1965.
Bombax malabaricum DC., Prodr. 1: 479. 1824; FRPS 49(2): 106, pl. 29: 5 –9. 1984; FGD 3: 215, fig. 146. 1995.

Tree, up to 25 m tall; bark greyish white, trunk of young trees and branches of older trees usually very spiny. Stipules small. Petioles 10 –20 cm; petiolules 1.5– 4 cm; leaflets 5–7, oblong to oblong-lanceolate, 10 –20 × 3.5 –7 cm, base broad cuneate, apex acuminate, margin entire, glabrous; lateral veins 15 –17 pairs. Flowers usually red, sometimes orange-red, ca. 10 cm in diam.; calyx 2– 4.5 cm, glabrous abaxially, densely yellowish sericeous adaxially, 3 – 5-lobed, lobes semiorbicular, 1.5 × 2.3 cm; petals fleshy, obovate-oblong, 8 –10 × 3 – 4 cm, stellate-puberulous on both surfaces; stamen-tubes short, filaments thick; style longer than stamens. Capsule ellipsoid, obtuse, 10 –15 × 4.5 – 5 cm, densely greyish-white-villous and stellate-puberulous. Seeds many, obovate, smooth.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 1104, 2454; HK sheet 3573.
Distribution: S & SW China; tropical Asia.
Ecology: Flowering: Mar.–Apr.; fruiting: May.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal (folklore).

Ceiba pentandra (L.) Gaertn. 吉貝（美洲木棉）
Fruct. Sem. Pl. 2: 244. 1791; FGD 3: 216. 1995.
Bombax pentandrum L., Sp. Pl. 1: 511. 1753.

Tree, up to 30 m tall; branches verticillate, spiny when young. Petioles 7–14 cm; petiolules 3– 4 mm; leaflets 5–9, thin-leathery, oblong-lanceolate, 5 –16 × 1.5– 5 cm, base cuneate, apex acute or acuminate, margin entire or remotely and minutely toothed toward the apex, glabrous, glaucous abaxially. Flowers fascicled in leaf axils on upper part of twigs, sometimes solitary, reddish or yellowish white. Pedicels 2.5 – 5 cm. Calyx 1.25 –2 cm, glabrous adaxially. Petals obovate-oblong, 2.5 – 4 cm, densely white-villous abaxially. Filaments in 5 bundles, each bundle with 1 anther; anthers reniform. Ovary glabrous; styles 2.5–3.5 cm, stigma clavate, 5-lobed. Capsule ellipsoid, 7.5 –15 × 3– 5 cm, stipe 7–25 cm, dehiscing into 5 valves, densely covered with silky wool abaxially. Seeds globose, endocarp leathery, smooth.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 2277; HK sheet 35803.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan (cultivated); native to tropical America.
Ecology: Flowering: Mar.–Apr.
Uses: Ornamental, timber.

Chorisia speciosa A. St.-Hil. 絲木棉（美人樹）
Pl. Usuel. Bras. 63. 1828.

Deciduous trees, 8–15 m tall, trunk with short spines. Leaves spirally arranged on the current years’ branches; petioles 4 –12 cm, petiolules 6–15 mm, glabrous; leaflets 6–7, firmly papery, narrowly oblong to oblong-oblanceolate, the center one larger, 5.5–12 × 1.5–2.5 cm, base cuneate, apex ± acuminate, margin serrate above the base, glabrous, adaxially bright green, abaxially pale green. Flowers solitary or 2–3 clustered in axils of apical leaves, sometimes appearing a cymose-panicle due to the subtending leaves falling off. Pedicels 1.5 –2.5 cm. Caylx cup-shaped, 2–2.5 cm, apex shallowly 4–6-lobed; lobes unequal, apex obtuse or sub-rounded. Petals 5, distinct, oblanceolate, 9.5 –10.5 cm, broadest at middle (ca. 3.5 cm), dark red, pink, white with dark strips on the proximal half of adaxial surface. Outer stamen-tube ca. 1.8 cm; anthers 10, sterile, dark purplish red, covered with crisped hairs; inner stamen-tube 8.5 cm, with 5 fertile anthers. Style slightly longer than inner stamen-tube; stigma capitate, hairy.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 39817, 39818.
Distribution: Brazil, S to SW America; cultivated in tropical regions.
Ecology: Flowering: Oct.–Feb. of the following year.
Uses: Ornamental.

Abelmoschus esculentus (L.) Moench 咖啡黃葵（金寶菜）
Methodus 617. 1794; FRPS 49(2): 56, pl. 13: 3. 1984; FGD 2: 187. 1991.
Hibiscus esculentus L., Sp. Pl. 696. 1753; Forbes & Hemsl., J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 23: 87. 1886.

Tall annual herb, up to 1.5 m tall, strigose-hirsute throughout. Petioles 7–15 cm; stipules linear, 7–8 mm; leaf blade broadly elliptic to orbicular in outline, 10 –30 cm in diam., wider than long, base cordate, palmately 5- or 7-lobed; lobes triangular, the central one 2–6 × 3 – 4.5 cm at the base, margin dentate. Flowers solitary; pedicels 1–2 cm. Corolla yellow with maroon eye, 5–7 cm across. Capsules 8 –10 cm or longer, cylindric, beaked, strigose-hirsute. Seeds glandularly striate.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 6988, 32923; S. Y. Hu 11054 (CUHK).
Distribution: Cultivated in Hebei, Shandong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Hunan, Hubei, Yunnan, Guangdong; native to India.
Ecology: Flowering: May–Sep.
Uses: Food (A common food plant of the Mediterranean area, introduced to Hong Kong in some vegetable gardens).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Shing Mun, Tai Au Mun, Tai Po, Lam Tsuen, Yuen Tun Ha, Luk Keng, Nam Chung, Tai Mo Shan, Bride's Pool, Wong Wan Chau
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Abelmoschus moschatus (L.) Medik. 黃葵
Malvenfam. 46. 1787; FRPS 49(2): 58, pl. 15: 1–3. 1984; FGD 2: 188, fig. 116. 1991; FTW ed. 2, 3: 737, pl. 371. 1993.
Hibiscus abelmoschus L., Sp. Pl. 696. 1753; FHK 34. 1861; FKH 48. 1912.

Tall annual or perennial herb, up to 2 m tall, long-hirsute throughout. Petioles 9–15 cm; stipules lanceolate, 6–7 mm; leaf blade suborbicular in outline, 6–15 cm in diam., palmately 5–7-lobed, lobes of the lower ones ovate-triangular, those of the upper ones elliptic or linear, the central lobe 6–12 × 1.5–3 cm. Flowers solitary, axillary; pedicels 3– 8 cm; bracteoles 7–10, linear, caducous. Corolla 10 cm in diam., yellow, dark purple at base. Staminal tube 2.5 cm. Capsules ovate-ellipsoid, 4 – 6 cm, 2 cm in diam., shortly beaked, long-strigose. Seeds longitudinally and glandularly striate.

Locality: Shing Mun, Tai Au Mun, Tai Po, Lam Tsuen, Yuen Tun Ha, Luk Keng, Nam Chung, Tai Mo Shan, Bride's Pool, Wong Wan Chau. Y. S. Lau 770; S. Y. Hu 5618, 12417 (CUHK).
Distribution: Cultivated or naturalized in Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Taiwan; Indochina, Thailand, India; native to the Old World tropics.
Ecology: Flowering: Feb.–Jul.
Uses: Medicinal, essential oil, fibre.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Deep Bay, Yung Shue O, Tai Po, Shatin, Yuen Tun Ha, Plover Cove, Sam A Tsuen, Stonecutters Island, Lantau Island, Leung Shuen Wan Chau (Tall Island)
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Abutilon indicum (L.) Sweet 磨盤草
Hort. Brit. 54. 1826; FHK 33. 1861; FKH 47. 1912; FHN 2: 94. 1965; FRPS 49(2): 37. 1984; FTW ed. 2, 3: 739, pl. 372. 1993.
Sida indica L., Cent. Pl. 2: 26. 1756; FRPS 49(2): 37. 1984; FGD 2: 198, fig. 126. 1991; FTW ed 2, 3: 739. 1993.

Annual or perennial herb, 0.5 –1 m tall, much branched, greyish stellate puberulent throughout. Petioles 2–4 cm; stipules subulate, 1–2 mm; leaf blade ovate or suborbicular, 1.5–7(–9) × 2.5–7 cm, base cordate, apex acute or acuminate, margin coarsely dentate. Flowers solitary, axillary; pedicels slender, 4– 5(–7) cm, articulate towards apex. Calyx patelliform, 6 –10 mm across; lobes 5, broadly ovate, mucronate. Corolla yellow, 2–2.5 cm across. Staminal tube stellate-hirsute. Fruit depressed globose, 1.5 cm in diam., top flat; carpels 15 –20, very short-awned. Seeds reniform, stellate-pilose.

Locality: Deep Bay, Yung Shue O, Tai Po, Shatin, Yuen Tun Ha, Plover Cove, Sam A Tsuen, Stonecutters Island, Lantau Island, Leung Shuen Wan Chau (Tall Island). Y. S. Lau 1275; HK sheet 11174; S. Y. Hu 5769, 12617 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; Indochina, Thailand, Myanmar, India, Sri Lanka, Indonesia.
Ecology: Wastelands, thickets near villages. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), fibre.

Abutilon pictum (Gillies ex Hook. & Arn.) Walp. 金鈴花
Repert. Bot. Syst. 1: 324. 1842.
Abutilon striatum Dicks. ex Lindl., Edwards's Bot. Reg. 39. 1839; FRPS 49(2): 33, pl. 8: 2–3. 1984.
Sida picta Gillies ex Hook., Bot. Misc. 3: 154. 1833.

Shrub, to 2 m tall; branchlets glabrous. Leaves 5 –7 cm in diam., palmately (3 –)5–7-lobed, basal portion reniform, large lobes caudate at apex, glabrous or sparsely stellate pubescent abaxially. Flowers golden-orange with red veins, solitary, axillary; peduncles slender, 10 –17 cm, bending at anthesis. Calyx cup-shaped, deeply cleft; lobes deltoid lanceolate, 1.3 –1.8 cm. Corolla lantern-like, hanging; petals imbricate, clawed, 4 cm, 1.6 cm across middle, branches of red veins reticulate. Staminal column exceeding petals, basal threefourth sterile, styles 10 –12, exceeding petals, distinct; stigmas discoid. Fruit not known.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 2658; HK sheet 32799; S. Y. Hu & P. H. But 22038 (CUHK).
Distribution: Cultivated in China; native of Brazil.
Ecology: Flowering: May– Oct.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Yuen Long, Mo Fan Heung, Jubilee Reservoir
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Abutilon theophrasti Medik. 苘麻
Malvenfam. 28. 1787; FRPS 49(2): 36. 1984; FGD 2: 199. 1991.
Sida abutilon L., Sp. Pl. 685. 1753.
Abutilon avicennae Gaertn., Fruct. Sem. Pl. 2: 251, t. 135, fig. 1. 1791.

Annual herb or subshrub, 1–2 m tall, much branched. Branches, petioles and pedicels stellate puberulous. Petioles 3–12 cm; leaf blade suborbiculate, 3.5 –15 cm in diam., base cordate, apex long-acuminate, margin slightly crenulate, stellate hirsute adaxially, tomentose abaxially. Flowers solitary, axillary. Pedicels 1–3 cm, articulate towards apex. Calyx cup-shaped, densely tomentellate; lobes 5, orbicular, oblong in fruit, mucronate. Corolla yellow; lobes obovate, ca. 1cm. Staminal tube glabrous, filamentiferous at apex. Fruits black, depressed globose, 2 cm across, top flat; carpels 12 to 16, strongly birostrate, awns 5 mm. Seeds reniform, stellate-pilose.

Locality: Yuen Long, Mo Fan Heung, Jubilee Reservoir. Y. W. Lam 1498; HK sheet 36223; S. Y. Hu 10742 (CUHK).
Distribution: Cosmopolitan in the temperate region of the N hemisphere.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides. Flowering: Jul.–Aug.
Uses: Materials (fibre).

Althaea rosea (L.) Cav. 蜀葵
Diss. 2: 91, t. 28, fig 1. 1786; S. Y. Hu, Malvaceae. 9, pl. 3. 1955; FRPS 49(2): 11, pl. 3: 1–3. 1984; FGD 2: 196, fig. 123. 1991.
Alcea rosea L., Sp. Pl. 687. 1753.

Biennial herb, 1–2 m tall at anthesis; densely bristly throughout. Leaves alternate; stipules ovate, 8 mm; petioles 5–15 cm; leaf blade suborbicular in outline, 6–16 cm in diam., palmately and shallowly 5–7-lobed; lobes triangular or subrotundate, sparsely stellate pubescent on adaxial surface, stellate bristly or tomentose and bristly on abaxial surface. Flowers solitary or subfasciculate, axillary, often raceme-like due to subtending leaves gradually diminishing into leaf-like bracts; pedicels 2– 5 mm, lengthening to 15 mm in fruit, densely lanate and bristly; involucral bracts 6- or 7-lobed, ovate-lanceolate. Calyx longer than bracts, densely bristly, striate and sulcate. Corolla 6 – 8 cm across, color various, usually red. Fruit 2 cm in diam., pubescent; carpels suborbicular, back 1 mm wide, longitudinally sulcate, sides 4 mm in diam., striate-sulcate, reticulate, rugose, black.

Locality: Cultivated. S. Y. Hu 7275, 7275A, 13018 (CUHK).
Distribution: Widely cultivated, origin unknown.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr.–Aug.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Extensively cultivated, wild plants observed below Victoria Peak
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Hibiscus mutabilis L. 木芙蓉（芙蓉花）
Sp. Pl. 694. 1753; FKH 48. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Malvaceae. 49. 1955; FRPS 49(2): 73. 1984; FGD 2: 184. 1991; FTW ed. 2, 3: 742. 1993.

Tall shrub, 2– 5 m tall; branchlets, petioles, pedicels and calyx very densely lanate, the hairs straight and stellate mixed. Leaves papery; petioles 5–20 cm; stipules lanceolate, 5 – 8 mm, caducous; leaf blade broadly ovate to ovate-orbicular in outline, 10 –15 cm in diam., base cordate, apex acuminate, 5- or 7-lobed and 7- to 11-nerved, sparsely stellate-hispid and punctate adaxially, densely tomentose abaxially. Flowers solitary in axils of leaves near apex of branches. Pedicels 5 –8 cm, articulate towards apex. Bracteoles 8, linear, 10 –12 × 2 mm. Calyx campanulate, 2.5 –3 cm, conspicuously 5-lobed; lobes ovate, acuminate, 1.6 –2 cm. Corolla white, pink or red, the color changing from morning to afternoon; lobes suborbicular, 4– 5 cm in diam. Capsules subglobose, 2.5 cm in diam., setose and lanate, inside of the sutures densely villose. Seeds reniform, the back long villose, 2 to 6 hairs sharing a common base.

Locality: Extensively cultivated, wild plants observed below Victoria Peak. H. C. Tang 1452; Y. S. Lau 2044; S. Y. Hu & P. H. But 21356 (CUHK).
Distribution: Native to China; cultivated elsewhere.
Ecology: Flowering: Aug.– Oct.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal (folklore), fiber.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Commonly cultivated in Hong Kong gardens
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Hibiscus rosa-sinensis L. 朱槿（扶桑、大紅花）
Sp. Pl. 694. 1753; FKH 48. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Malvaceae. 47. 1955; FHN 2: 98. 1965; FRPS 49(2): 69. 1984; FGD 2: 185. 1991.

Shrub, 1–4 m tall; branchlets sparsely stellate pubescent. Leaves papery; petioles 5–20 mm, pubescent; stipules linear, 5–12 mm; leaf blade ovate, 4 –9 × 2– 5.5 cm, base rounded or broadly cuneate, apex acuminate, coarsely dentate above base, glabrous and punctate on both surfaces. Flowers solitary; pedicels 3.5 –7.5 cm, articulate towards the apex; bracteoles linear, 8 –15 × 1.2–2 mm, hardly connate at the base. Calyx campanulate, 1.7–2.5 cm, glandularly stellate puberulous; lobes 5, obovate deltoid, 7–10 mm. Corolla scarlet, funnel-form, 6 –15 cm in diam. Staminal tube 4 – 8 cm long, the upper 1/3 stameniferous. Flowers dropping off after anthesis, fruit not observed.

Locality: Commonly cultivated in Hong Kong gardens. Y. S. Lau 903, 3069; S. Y. Hu & P. H. But 22141 (CUHK).
Distribution: Long been accredited as a native of China, cultivated in temples and gardens of South China; wild form not yet discovered; many cultivars with double pink, red and even tinge orange flowers in Hong Kong.
Ecology: Flowering: Almost all year round.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: A cultivated form with double red flowers (Hibiscus rosa-sinensis L. var. rubro-plenus Sweet 重瓣朱槿) is also commonly cultivated in gardens and flowers almost all year round.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Commonly cultivated in Hong Kong gardens
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Hibiscus schizopetalus (Masters) Hook. f. 吊燈花（裂瓣槿）
Bot. Mag. 106: t. 6524. 1880; FHN 2: 98. 1965; FRPS 49(2): 69, pl. 17: 6. 1984; FGD 2: 185. 1991.
Hibiscus rosa-sinensis var. schizopetalus Masters, Gard. Chron. n. s. 12: 272, fig. 45. 1879.

Shrub 2–3 m tall; branchlets glabrous. Leaves papery; petioles 1–2 cm, stellate-pubescent; stipules subulate, ca. 2 mm, caducous; leaf blade elliptic or oblong, 4–7 × 1.5– 4 cm, base obtuse, apex acute or shortly acuminate, glabrous on both surfaces, basal half entire, apical half serrate. Flowers solitary, pendulous; pedicels slender, 10 –14 cm, articulate at the middle; bracteoles 8, very minute, 1–2 mm, ciliate. Calyx spathulate, tubular, 1.5 cm, shallowly 5-toothed. Corolla scarlet; lobes 4 –5 cm, reflexed, laciniate. Staminal tube 9–11 cm. Capsules oblong-cylindrical, 4 × 1 cm. Seed smooth.

Locality: Commonly cultivated in Hong Kong gardens. Y. S. Lau 1821; HK sheet 3506; S. Y. Hu 5827 (CUHK).
Distribution: Said to be native to E tropical Africa; cultivated in Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Flowering: Almost all year round, flowers drop after anthesis; fruit not observed.
Uses: Ornamental.

Hibiscus syriacus L. 木槿
Sp. Pl. 695. 1753; S. Y. Hu, Malvaceae 50. 1955; FHN 2: 99. 1965; FRPS 49(2): 75. 1984; FGD 2: 185. 1991; FTW ed. 2, 3: 742. 1993.
Hibiscus chinensis auct. non DC.: Forbes & Hemsl., J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 23: 88 (Ind. Fl. Sin. I). 1886.

Shrubs, 2–4 m tall. Young branches and pedicels stellate puberulous. Leaves papery; petioles 3–16(–25) mm, stellate pilose adaxially; stipules linear, ca. 6 mm; leaf blade ovate-rhomboid to narrowly elliptic, 3 –10 × 2–4 cm, apex acuminate, base cuneate, irregularly dentate or shallowly 3-lobed, glabrous or sparsely stellate pubescent on both surfaces. Flowers solitary, axillary. Pedicels 4 –14 mm. Bracteoles 6 or 7, linear, 7–9 × 1–1.5 mm, very sparsely stellate pilose. Calyx campanulate, 1.4–1.7 cm, densely short stellate tomentellate, 5-toothed; lobes triangular, 6– 8 mm. Corolla lilac, 5– 6 cm in diam.; lobes obovate, 3.5– 5 cm, ciliate and puberulous abaxially. Staminal tube 2.5 –3 cm, antheriferous to the base. Capsules oblong-ellipsoid, densely golden stellate tomentose, 1.5–2 cm, apex 1.5 cm in diam., shortly rostrate. Seed glabrous, with a row of long white hairs along the back, like the mane of a horse.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. Y. S. Lau 1864; HK sheet 3526; S. Y. Hu & P. H. But 22193 (CUHK).
Distribution: Native to China; cultivated elsewhere.
Ecology: Flowering: May– Oct.
Uses: Ornamental, food (vegetable), fibre.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Shek O, Ma Liu Shui, Mai Po, Leung Shuen Wan Chau (Tall Island)
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Hibiscus tiliaceus L. 黃槿
Sp. Pl. 694. 1753; FKH 48. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Malvaceae. 44. 1955; FRPS 49(2): 64, pl. 16: 2–3. 1984; FGD 2: 182, fig. 115. 1991; FTW ed. 2, 3: 743, pl. 373. 1993.

Small tree, 3–7 m tall; branchlets glabrescent. Leaves leathery; petioles 2–4 cm; stipules foliaceous, oblong, 2 × 12 mm, rounded at the apex, caducous; leaf blade roundish or broadly ovate, 6 –15 cm in diam., base cordate, apex acute or shortly acuminate, margin entire or crenulate, inconspicuously stellate pilose adaxially, grey, densely and shortly stellate tomentose abaxially, 7- or 9-nerved, with glands at the base of the main nerves. Flowers in simple axillary or terminal cymes; peduncles 4 – 5 cm; pedicels 1–3 cm, subtended by a pair of stipule-like bracts; bracteoles 7–10, linear-lanceolate, connate about the middle. Calyx 3 cm, basal 1/4 connate; lobes 5, lanceolate, 1.5 × 5 – 6 mm. Corolla campanulate; lobes obovate, 4.5 cm, united at the base, yellow, crimson at base. Capsules oblong-ellipsoid, 2.5 × 2 cm; pericarp woody. Seeds smooth, glandularly papillose.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Shek O, Ma Liu Shui, Mai Po, Leung Shuen Wan Chau (Tall Island). Y. S. Lau 1435, 1910; S. Y. Hu 6007; S. Y. Hu & P. H. But 21922 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; coastal regions in tropical and subtropical Asia.
Ecology: Thickets, seashores behind mangroves. Flowering: Jul.–Aug.
Uses: Ornamental, timber, fibre.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Authority: M. G. Gilbert, Y. Tang & Dorr

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Malva verticillata L. 冬葵（冬莧葵）
Sp. Pl. 689. 1753; FKH 46. 1912; FRPS 49(2): 5, pl. 1: 5 – 6. 1984; FGD 2: 196, fig. 122. 1991.

Annual or perennial herb, 0.5–1 m tall at anthesis; stem stellate villose. Leaves basal and alternate on stem; petioles 5–8 cm; stipules ovate-lanceolate; leaf blade reniform or orbicular, 5–11 cm in diam., usually 5–7-lobed; lobes of the lower leaves rounded, those of the upper ones triangular, apex obtuse, margin crenulate-dentate. Flowers in compact fascicles. Pedicels very short, stellate villose; involucral bracts linear-lanceolate. Calyx cup-shaped, 5-lobed. Corolla white or pale purple, almost twice as long as the calyx. Staminal tube setose. Fruit 5–7 mm in diam., entirely glabrous; carpels 10 or 11, smooth abaxially, rugose along the rounded angles, palmately striate on the side.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 455, 3320.
Distribution: Widely distributed over China; India, Myanmar, Korea and N Africa.
Ecology: Flowering: Feb.–May.
Uses: Food (leaves edible), ornamental.

Malvastrum coromandelianum (L.) Garcke 賽葵
Bonplandia 5: 297. 1857; FRPS 49(2): 14, pl. 3: 4 – 6. 1984; FGD 2: 197, fig. 124. 1991; FTW ed. 2, 3: 745, pl. 374. 1993.
Malva coromandeliana L., Sp. Pl. 2: 687. 1753.
Malvastrum tricuspidatum (R. Br.) A. Gray, Pl. Wright. 1: 16. 1852; FHK 32. 1861; FKH 47. 1912.

Perennial herb, usually shrubby, up to 1 m tall, sparsely covered with simple and 4-armed stellate strigose hairs. Leaves alternate; petioles 1–3 cm, densely pilose; stipules lanceolate, 5 mm; leaf blade ovate, or ovate-elliptic, 3 – 6 × 1–3.5 cm, apex obtuse, base subrounded, margin coarsely serrate, sparsely pilose on both surfaces. Flowers yellow, solitary, axillary, ca. 1.5 cm in diam. Pedicels 5 mm. Bracteoles linear, 5 × 1 mm. Sepals ovate, acuminate, 8 mm, basal 1/3 connate. Petals obovate, 8 × 4 mm. Fruit depressed globose, 6 mm in diam.; carpels reniform, weakly stellate pilose, with 2 spines at the middle, and a stiff, persistent style.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1974; HK sheet 35650; S. Y. Hu & P. H. But 22236, 22302 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; pantropical, native to N America.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides. Flowering: Jun.–Jul.

Malvaviscus arboreus Cav. var. penduliflorus (DC.) Schery 垂花懸鈴花
Ann. Missouri Bot. Gard. 29: 223. 1942; FRPS 49(2): 50. 1984; FGD 2: 193, fig. 120. 1991.
Malvaviscus penduliflorus DC., Prodr. 1: 445. 1824.

Shrub, 1–3 m tall; young branchlets and pedicels sparsely pubescent and with a line of long hairs on one side. Leaves narrowly ovate to ovate-lanceolate, 6 –12 × 2.5– 6 cm, undivided, or rarely shallowly 3-lobed, base broadly cuneate to rounded, apex long acuminate, margin obtusely dentate, glabrescent or sparsely stellate pubescent on nerves. Flowers bright red, hanging at anthesis. Pedicels 1–4 cm, pubescent. Bracteoles lanceolate to spathulate, 1.2–1.5 cm, pubescent adaxially. Calyx bell-shaped, 1.5 –2 cm, 5-lobed; lobes triangular, 5 –7 mm. Corolla 5 –7 cm.

Locality: Commonly cultivated in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 683, 1889; S. Y. Hu & P. H. But 22634 (CUHK).
Distribution: Cultivated in Guangdong & Yunnan. Native to Mexico & Columbia.
Ecology: Flowering: Almost all year round in Hong Kong.
Uses: Ornamental.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Lai Chi Kok, Tai Po, Lau Fau Shan, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Sida acuta Burm. f. 黃花稔
Fl. Ind. 147. 1768; FHK 32. 1861; FKH 47. 1912; FRPS 49(2): 19. 1984; FGD 2: 201. 1991; FTW ed. 2, 3: 748. 1993.

Herb, usually shrubby, 0.3 –1 m tall, much branched; branchlets pubescent or glabrescent. Petioles 4– 5 mm, villose; stipules linear, longer than the petioles; leaf blade lanceolate or linear-lanceolate, 1.5–7 × 0.5–2.5 cm, base obtuse or rounded, apex acute or acuminate, margin serrate, both surfaces glabrous or sparsely stellate-pubescent. Flowers solitary or paired, axillary; pedicels 4–12 mm, the longer ones articulate at the middle. Calyx glabrous, cup-shaped, 6 mm, the lower half connate; lobes 5, deltoid, caudate. Corolla yellow, 8–10 mm across; lobes obovate, ciliate. Fruit subglobose, 4 mm in diam., 6-carpellate; carpels birostrate, reticulately striate and sulcate.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Lai Chi Kok, Tai Po, Lau Fau Shan, Lantau Island. H. C. Tang 375, 2077; S. Y. Hu 8802 (CUHK); K. L. Yip 4242.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam, Laos, India.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides near villages. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Mo Shan, Chung Chi College
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Sida alnifolia L. 榿葉黃花稔
Sp. Pl. 684. 1753; FHN 2: 93. 1965; FRPS 49(2): 21. 1984; FGD 2: 203. 1991.
Sida rhombifolia auct. non L.: FHK 33. 1861; FKH 47. 1912.

Subshrub, 0.5 –1(–2) m tall; branchlets slender, densely stellate villose. Petioles 3 – 5 mm, stellate pubescent; stipules subulate, 4 – 4.5 mm; leaf blade ovate, suborbicular or obovate, 2–5 × 1–2 cm, base cuneate, apex obtuse or truncate, margin evenly serrate, stellate pilose adaxially, stellate villose abaxially, Flowers solitary. Pedicels 5 mm (2 cm in fruit), articulate near middle, densely stellatevelutinous. Calyx cup-shaped, 5–8 mm, stellate-velutinous, long-villose along angles and margins. Corolla yellow, 6 mm across. Staminal tube hirsute. Fruit subglobose, 6 mm in diam., enclosed, the apical end pubescent; carpels 8, birostrate, awns 2 mm.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Chung Chi College. W. J. Tutcher 5570; F. W. Xing 9914; S. Y. Hu 8768, 7899 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; Indochina, India.
Ecology: Open fields and thin forests. Flowering: Jan.–Feb.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Clear Water Bay, Tai Po Kau, Sheung Pak Nai, Ha Pak Nai, Fung Kat Heung
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Sida cordata (Burm. f.) Borss. 長梗黃花稔
Blumea 14: 182. 1966; FRPS 49(2): 26, pl. 5: 6 –7. 1984.
Sida humilis Cav., Diss. 5: 277, t. 134, fig. 2, 1788; FHK 32. 1861; FKH 47. 1912.

Diffuse herb, 0.3–1 m tall; branchlet slender, spreading, covered with long spreading hairs, mixed with short stellate hairs. Petioles 1–3 cm, stellate pilose; stipules linear, 2–3 mm, sparsely pubescent; leaf blade cordiform, 1– 5 cm, apex shortly acuminate, margin obtusely dentate or serrate, stellate pubescent on both surfaces. Flowers solitary or in leafy racemes. Pedicels slender, 2– 4 cm, sparsely stellate pubescent, articulate above middle. Calyx cup-shaped, ca. 4 mm; lobes triangular, acute. Corolla yellow. Fruit depressed globose; carpels 5, not curved.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Clear Water Bay, Tai Po Kau, Sheung Pak Nai, Ha Pak Nai, Fung Kat Heung. L. T. Lo 539; Y. S. Lau 2022, 2168.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; tropical Asia.
Ecology: Waste places, roadsides. Flowering: May–Jun.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Lai Chi Kok, Sha Tin, Tai Po, Tai Long Sai Wan, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Sida cordifolia L. 心葉黃花稔
Sp. Pl. 684. 1753; FHK 33. 1861; Dunn, J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 39: 494. 1911; FKH 47. 1912; FRPS 49(2): 25, pl. 5: 2–3. 1984; FGD 2: 203. 1991; FTW ed. 2, 3: 748, pl. 375. 1993.
Sida hongkongensis Gandoger, Bull. Soc. Bot. France 71: 629.1924, nom. subnud.
Sida humilis Willd., Check List HK Plants 40. 2004.

Subshrub, 0.3 –1 m tall, densely stellate hispid and mixed with simple long hairs throughout. Petioles 1–2.5 cm, stipules filiform, 5 mm; leaf blade ovate or subcordate, 1.5 –3 × 1–4 cm, base cordate or rounded, apex rounded or obtuse. Flowers solitary or fasciculate; pedicels 4–15 mm, the longer ones articulate near apex. Calyx cup-shaped; lobes 5, triangular, 5 – 6 mm. Corolla yellow, 15 mm in diam.; lobes oblong, 6 – 8 mm. Staminal tube hirsute. Fruit subdiscoid, 6 – 8 mm across; carpels 10, birostrate, the apical end shortly strigose, awns to 3 mm, exposed, covered with stiff reflexed hairs.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Lai Chi Kok, Sha Tin, Tai Po, Tai Long Sai Wan, Lantau Island. Y. W. Lam 801, 1185; S. Y. Hu & P. H. But 23289 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan, Fujian, Taiwan; Asia and Africa tropical and subtropical regions.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides. Flowering: Nearly all the year round.
Notes: The type specimen of Sida hongkongensis was collected by Bodinier (No. 922) from Hong Kong.

Sida rhombifolia L. 白背黃花稔
Sp. Pl. 684. 1753; FRPS 49(2): 20. 1984; FGD 2: 203. 1991; FTW ed. 2, 3: 748. 1993.

Subshrub, 0.5–1 m tall, much branched. Branchlets, petioles and pedicels stellate lanate. Petioles 3–5 mm; stipules linear, 3–5 mm; leaf blade rhombic or oblong-lanceolate, 2.5 – 4.5 × 0.6 –3 cm, base broadly cuneate or obtuse, apex obtuse or acute, margin serrate, shortly stellate or subglabrous adaxially, stellate-velutinous abaxially. Flowers solitary, axillary. Pedicels 10 mm, (15–25 mm in fruit), geniculate, articulate above middle. Calyx 4– 5 mm, the basal 2/3 connate, stellate velutinous. Petals yellow, ca. 8 mm. Staminal tube glabrous, or sparsely glandularly papillose. Fruits subdiscoid, 6–7 mm in diam.; carpels 8 –10, birostrate, subglabrous.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. L. T. Lo 43; Y. S. Lau 189; S. Y. Hu & P. H. But 20048, 23292 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hubei, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Indochina.
Ecology: Thickets on hillslopes or in valleys. Flowering & fruiting: May–Dec.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Long Ke, Tai Po, Lam Tsuen, Chung Uk Tsuen, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Sida subcordata Span. 榛葉黃花稔
Linnaea 15: 172. 1814; FRPS 49(2): 24, pl. 5: 1. 1984; FGD 2: 202, fig. 128. 1991.
Sida corylifolia Wall., Num. List. no. 1865. 1829; FKH 47. 1912.

Subshrub, 1(–2) m tall. Branchlets and abaxial surface of leaves sparsely stellate-pubescent when young, soon glabrescent. Petioles 1.5 –2.5 cm; stipules linear, 3 – 4 mm; leaf blade ovate to oblong, 5 –10 × 2.5 –7.5 cm, base rounded or obtuse, apex shortly acuminate, margin crenulate-serrate. Inflorescence corymbose, subpaniculate; peduncles 2–7 cm; pedicels 6–20 mm, articulate at middle, geniculate. Calyx 8–10 mm. Corolla campanulate, 3 cm in diam.; petals obovate. Staminal tube glabrous. Fruit subglobose, 1 cm in diam.; carpels 8 –10, birostrate, awns 6 mm, exposed, covered with reflexed bristles.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Long Ke, Tai Po, Lam Tsuen, Chung Uk Tsuen, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 2410; Y. W. Lam 484; S. Y. Hu & P. H. But 22720 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam, Laos, Myanmar, India, Malesia area.
Ecology: Wastelands, thickets, partially shaded woods near villages. Flowering & fruiting: Sep.–Jan. of the following year.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Tam Reservoir, Tai Po, Butterfly Beach, Lung Kwu Tan, Nam Chung, Luk Keng, Lantau Island, Ma Wan, Po Toi
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Thespesia populnea (L.) Solander ex Corr. 恆春黄槿（繖楊）
Ann. Mus. Hist. Nat. Paris 9: 290, t. 8, fig. 2. 1807; FRPS 49(2): 93. 1984; FGD 2: 190. 1991; FTW ed. 2, 3: 750, pl. 376. 1993.
Hibiscus populneus L., Sp. Pl. 694. 1753.

Evergreen small tree, 6– 8 m tall; branchlets scabrous, densely covered with brown scurfy scales. Petioles 4–10 cm; stipules linear lanceolate, ca. 7 mm; leaf blade ovate-cordate, 7–18 × 4.5 –11 cm, base cordate, apex long caudate, margin entire, adaxially glabrous, abaxially sparsely scurfy. Flowers solitary, axillary; pedicels 2–6 cm, densely scurfy. Calyx cup-shaped, ca. 15 mm in diam., apex truncate, 5-toothed. Corolla campanulate, ca. 5 cm, yellow, with purple blotches at base adaxially. Fruit pyriform, ca. 5 cm in diam. Seed triangularly ovoid, striate, lanuginose.

Locality: Tai Tam Reservoir, Tai Po, Butterfly Beach, Lung Kwu Tan, Nam Chung, Luk Keng, Lantau Island, Ma Wan, Po Toi. Y. S. Lau 1530; HK sheet 32395; S. Y. Hu & P. H. But 23447 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangxi, Guangdong, Taiwan; Indochina, Thailand, India, Sri Lanka, Philippines and tropical Africa.
Ecology: Sunny places near seashores. Flowering: Almost all year round.

Urena lobata L. 肖梵天花（地桃花、黐頭婆）
Sp. Pl. 692. 1753; FHK 34. 1861; FKH 48. 1912; FHN 2: 96, fig. 341. 1965; FRPS 49(2): 43. 1984; FGD 2: 194, fig. 121. 1991; FTW ed. 2, 3: 752, pl. 377. 1993.

Small shrub, to 1 m tall, much branched. Branchlets, petioles and pedicels stellate-tomentose. Petioles 1–4 cm; stipules linear, ca. 2 mm, caducous, leaf blade variable in shape, the lower ones subrotundate, rotundate or subcordate at base, shallowly 3-lobed at apex, 4 – 5 × 5 – 6 cm, often broader than long, the middle ones ovate, 5–7 × 3 – 6.5 cm, the upper ones ovate or ovate-elliptic, margin evenly serrate, adaxially pubescent, abaxially grey or yellowish tomentose, the hairs all short, erect, stellate. Flowers solitary; pedicels 3 mm. Epicalyx lobes 6 mm, basal 1/3 connate, stellate pilose. Calyx lobes 5–7 mm, densely lanate at base of keel. Corolla pink; petals 15 mm. Fruit 1 cm in diam., carpels stellate pubescent and glochidiate.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. L. T. Lo 324, 325; Y. S. Lau 1990; S. Y. Hu 8766 (CUHK).
Distribution: Areas S of Changjiang River; Indochina, Thailand, Myanmar, Japan.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides near villages. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Feb. of the following year.
Notes: A very variable species, some individuals or populations may differing from the typical form in the shape of the leaves and in the nature and density of the hairs.

Urena procumbens L. 梵天花（狗腳跡）
Sp. Pl. 692. 1753; S. Y. Hu, Malvaceae 77. 1955; FHN 2: 96. 1965; FRPS 49(2): 47. 1984; FGD 2: 195. 1991; FTW ed. 2, 3: 752. 1993.
Urena sinuata auct. non L.: FHK 34. 1861; FKH 48. 1912.

Small shrub, ca. 0.5 m tall, with horizontal spreading branches; branchlets stellate tomentose. Petioles 4–15 mm; stipules subulate, 1.5 mm, caducous; leaf blade various in shape, the lower ones ovate in outline, sinuate below the middle, 3-lobed, 1.5–6 × 1–4 cm, apex obtuse, base rounded or subcordate, evenly serrate; the upper ones ovate to elliptic, not sinuate, serrate; all leaves scabrid-hirsute on both surfaces, the hairs homogenous, all short and rigid. Flowers subfasciculate or solitary. Pedicels 2–3 mm. Epicalyx lobes 7 mm, basal onethird connate, sparsely stellate hairy. Calyx lobes 4–7 mm, ovate, acute, stellate along the median longitudinal line, the rest glabrous. Corolla pink to red; petals 10–15 mm. Staminal tube glabrous. Fruits globose, 6 mm in diam., hirsute and echinate, glochidiate. Seeds glabrous.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. P. S. Choi 329; S. Y. Hu & P. H. But 21108, 22727 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), fibre.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Lam Chung, So Kwun Wat, Castle Peak, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Nepenthes mirabilis (Lour.) Druce 豬籠草
Bot. Exch. Club Brit. Isles Rept. 4: 637. 1916; FHN 1: 329, fig. 164. 1964; FRPS 34(1): 12, pl. 5. 1984; FGD 2: 46, fig. 32. 1991; FOC 8: 198. 2001.
Phyllamphora mirabilis Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 606. 1790.
Nepenthes phyllamphora Willd., Sp. Pl. 4(2): 874. 1806, nom. illeg.; FKH 219. 1912.

Erect or climbing herb, 0.5 –2 m tall; young parts densely tomentose, later glabrescent. Basal leaves forming dense rosette, subsessile; leaf blade lanceolate, ca. 10 cm, base semi-amplexicaul, margin usually denticulate; tendril shorter than blade; pitcher variable in size, narrowly ovoid to terete, 2– 6 cm long, 0.6 –2 cm in diam., pilose and stellate hairy, 2-winged, 2–8-spurred between lid and mouth; lid ovate or rounded, densely glandular inside. Cauline leaves petiolate; leaf blade oblong to lanceolate, 10–25 × 4–8 cm, base decurrent, entire or ciliate-denticulate, with purplish red dots on both surfaces; tendril nearly as long as blade, with or without pitcher; pitcher subcylindrical, slightly enlarged at base, 8–16 cm long, 2–5 cm in diam., often with purplish red dots, pilose and stellate hairy, 2-winged, inner wall smooth on distal half and densely glandular on proximal half; mouth narrowed or not, with 1–2 spurs on the place bearing lid; lid ovate to oblong, densely glandular inside. Raceme 20–50 cm, villous, opposite to leaves or terminal; pedicels 0.5–1.5 cm. Flower red or purple. Male flowers: tepals 4, elliptic or oblong, 5 –7 mm, densely glandular adaxially, villous abaxially; stamens in 1 whorl, slightly contorted, filament column slightly shorter than tepals. Female flowers: tepals ca. 0.5 cm; ovary ellipsoid, shortly stipitate or subsessile, densely pale yellow-pubescent or stellate hairy. Capsule with persistent perianth at base, dehiscing into 4 valves when mature; valves lanceolate, 1.5 –3 × 0.3 –0.5 cm, brown, shiny. Seeds filiform, ca. 1.2 cm.

Locality: Tai Lam Chung, So Kwun Wat, Castle Peak, Lantau Island. Y. W. Lam 915; P. S. Choi 35; Y. S. Lau 3045.
Distribution: Guangdong, Hainan; Indochina, Malaysia.
Ecology: Swamps and marshes. Flowering: Mar.–Dec.; fruiting: Aug.–Dec.
Uses: Ornamental, carnivorous plant.
Notes: Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Aberdeen, Pok Fu Lam, Mount Nicholson
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Drosera burmannii Vahl 錦地羅
Symb. Bot. 3: 50. 1794; FKH 100. 1912; FHK 129. 1861; FHN 1: 371. 1964; FRPS 34(1): 18. 1984; FGD 2: 64. 1991; FOC 8: 199. 2001.

Annual or biennial herb, with few fibrous roots; stem unbranched, extremely short, without tuber below ground. Leaves basal, forming a flat rosette, yellowish green or red to reddish violet, spathulate to obovate-spathulate, 6–15 × 5–7 mm, base attenuate, apex fimbriate, glandular hairy or glabrous; petioles short or absent; stipule 3–7 mm, connate with petiole at base, 5–7-fid, lobes laciniate. Inflorescence scapiform; racemes 1–3, 2–19-flowered, 6 –22 cm, subglabrous or with white or red to reddish violet glands; bracts hastate, 3- or 5-lobed, 1–3 mm; pedicels erect, 1–7 mm, glandular hairy or glabrous; sepals 5, united at base, light green, red, or reddish violet, narrowly oblong, 2–3 mm, striate, tuberculate, glandular hairs and white glands abaxially; petals 5, obovate, white to light red to reddish violet, ca. 4 × 2–3 mm; stamens 5, ca. 3 mm; ovary subglobose, glabrous; placentas 5, rare 6; styles 5, rare 6, filiform, 2–3 mm, incurved; stigma tooth-like. Capsule 5- (or rarely 6-) valved. Seeds many, dark-brown to black, veined.

Locality: Aberdeen, Pok Fu Lam, Mount Nicholson. H. C. Tang 2314; HK sheet 36058.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; widely distributed in tropical and subtropical regions of Asia, Africa and Australia.
Ecology: Sandy places. Flowering and fruiting: Almost all year round.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Drosera indica L. 長葉茅膏菜
Sp. Pl. 1: 282. 1753; FKH 100. 1912; FHN 1: 372. 1964; FRPS 34(1): 18. 1984; FGD 2: 65. 1991; FOC 8: 200. 2001.

Annual herb, with fibrous roots; stem unbranched, erect or procumbent, 2– 40 cm, not forming tubers below ground, pubescent with short, glandular hairs. Leaves cauline, alternate, light green or red, narrowly linear, 2–12 × 0.1–0.3 cm, white or reddish glandular pubescent, or glabrous, apex acute; stipule absent or reduced and hair-like; petioles 5–10 mm, glandular hairy or glabrous. Inflorescence axillary or leaf opposed, 6–30 cm, 1–30-flowered, glandular pubescent; peduncles to 12 cm; bracts linear, 2–8 mm; pedicels 0.6–1.5 cm, glandular pubescent; sepals 5, united near the base, lanceolate to narrowly oblong, 3 – 5 × 1–2 mm, margin entire or serrate, glandular pubescent abaxially; petals 5, white, light red, orange, or reddish violet, obovate to oblanceolate, ca. 6 mm; stamens 5, 3–5 mm, papillose, filaments flattened; ovary obovoid or subglobose, 1–2 mm; placentas 3; styles 3, deeply 2-lobed nearly to base, usually incurved; stigma simple, 2–3 mm. Capsule globose-obovoid, 3-valved, 4– 6 mm. Seeds black, small; venation thick and scrobiculate.

Locality: Cape D'Aguilar, Tung Chung. Y. M. Wan 6; Y. W. Lam 1265; S. P. Lau 58.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; widely distributed in tropical and subtropical regions of Asia, Africa and Australia.
Ecology: Wet places, soggy soils. Flowering and fruiting: Almost all year round.
Notes: Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Drosera oblanceolata Y. Z. Ruan 長柱茅膏菜
Acta Phytotax. Sin. 19: 340. 1981; FRPS 34(1): 21. 1984; FGD 2: 65. 1991; FOC 8: 200. 2001.

Perennial herb, with fibrous roots. Stems unbranched, short, without tuber below ground. Leaves basal, dense, petiolate, circinately 2-folded towards stipule when young; stipules light red, 1.5 –4.6 cm, scarious, deeply 3-parted, middle lobe 2- or 3-fid; petioles 3 –7 mm; leaf blade orbicular to oblanceolate, elliptic, or linear, 1.5 – 4.6 cm × (1–)2– 4 mm, pilose with glandular hairs, ciliate. Inflorescences 1 or 2, scapiform, 5–9 cm; peduncle glabrous; cincinnus corymbose, 8–10-flowered; bracts linear, ca. 2 mm; pedicels 3– 5 mm. Sepals 5, united at base, green, narrowly obovate to oblong, ca. 4 mm, glabrous, persistent. Petals pink, obovate to cuneate. Stamens 5. Ovary ellipsoid-globose to globose, ca. 2 mm; placentas 3; styles 3, 2–3 mm, each style deeply 2-lobed, sometimes again 2-lobed; stigma multi-fid. Capsule 3-valved. Seeds black, ellipsoid-globose, ca. 0.3 mm; venation scrobiculate.

Locality: Sunset Peak. H. G. Ye et al. 1176; Y. S. Lau 2599.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi.
Ecology: Sunny meadows and bogs. Flowering and fruiting: May– Oct.
Notes: Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Pat Sin Leng, Ping Fung Shan
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Drosera peltata Smith ex Willd. 光萼茅膏菜（茅膏菜）
Sp. Pl. 1: 1546. 1797; FKH 100. 1912; FOC 8: 201. 2001
Drosera peltata Smith ex Willd. var. glabrata Y. Z. Ruan, FRPS 34(1): 27. 1984; FGD 2: 66. 1991.

Perennial herb; stems erect or climbing, branched distally, 9 – 45 cm, with a tuber below ground, glabrous or with black, papillose glands. Basal leaves densely whorled, or absent in some populations, peltate, orbicular to suborbicular, 2– 4 × 6 – 8 mm, some leaves reduced, linear, ca. 2 mm, yellowish green to green; exstipulate; petioles 2–8 mm. Cauline leaves remote, peltate or lunate to semiorbicular, 2–3 × 4– 5 mm, margin glandular hairy, yellowish green; petioles 0.8 –1.3 cm; exstipulate. Inflorescence terminal; cincinnus 2–6 cm, 3 –22-flowered; bracts cuneate to oblanceolate or subulate; pedicels 0.6–2 cm; sepals 5–7, united near base, yellowish green, lanceolate to ovate, 2– 4 mm × ca. 1.5 mm, glabrous to glandular hairy, apex 5 –7-fid; petals usually white, rarely pink or red, oblong-cuneate, 4 – 6 × 2–3 mm; stamens 5, 2–4 mm; ovary subglobose, ca. 1.5 mm in diam.; styles 3– 5, sometimes 2 or 6, ca. 0.8 mm, each style deeply bi-lobed, again 2–5-lobed; stigma 2–3-fid. Capsule subglobose, (2–)3– 5(– 6)-valved. Seeds many, ellipsoid, ovoid to globose, ca. 0.4 mm; venation scrobiculate.

Locality: Pat Sin Leng, Ping Fung Shan. K. Y. Tam 132; Y. W. Lam 26, 241.
Distribution: Anhui, Gansu, Guangdong, Guangxi, W Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Taiwan; tropical Asia, Australia.
Ecology: Grassy fields, thickets and thin forests. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Sep.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Ho Pui, Ma On Shan, Castle Peak, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Drosera spathulata Labill. 寬苞茅膏菜
Nov. Holl. Pl. 1: 79. 1804; FRPS 34(1): 20. 1984; FOC 8: 200. 2001
Drosera loureirii Hook. & Arn., Bot. Beechey Voy. 31: 167. 1833; FHK 130. 1861; FKH 100. 1912.
Drosera spathulata Labill. var. loureirii (Hook. & Arn.) Y. Z. Ruan, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 19: 341. 1981; FGD 2: 64. 1991.

Perennial herb, with 1 or 2 black, fibrous roots; stem short, without tuber below ground. Leaves forming a dense, flat rosette, circinately 1-folded toward stipule when young, obovate or spathulate, or cuneate, 0.9–2.8 × 0.2–0.5 mm, glandular hairy; stipules light red, narrow, 4 – 8 mm, scarious, apex fimbriate, setaceous; petioles flattened, gradually dilated distally, 8–10 mm, glandular hairy. Inflorescences 1– 6, scapiform, sometimes branched, 4 –25 cm; peduncle densely glandular hairy; racemes 1-sided, 10 –20-flowered; bracts linear to oblanceolate, ca. 2 mm or more, 3-lobed; pedicels 1–3 mm, densely glandular hairy; sepals 5, united at base, lanceolate or narrowly ovate, 1.5 – 4 mm, apex obtuse or rounded, margin entire or l-toothed, densely glandular hairy outside; petals white or pink to reddish violet, obovate, 2–6 mm; stamens 5, 2.5– 6 mm; filaments flat, ca. 5 mm; anthers oblong, ca. 1.5 mm; ovary ellipsoid; placentas 3– 4; styles 3– 4, ca. 2.5 mm, each style deeply 2-lobed to base, sometimes again lobed distally; stigma simple, persistent. Capsule 3 – 4-valved, ca. 1.5 mm; valves obdeltoid, incurved. Seeds small, black, ovoid or ellipsoid; venation thick and scrobiculate.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Ho Pui, Ma On Shan, Castle Peak, Lantau Island. L. T. Lo 662; Y. S. Lau 2172; H. C. Tang 2251.
Distribution: Guangdong, S Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Malaysia, Indonesia, Philippines, Australia, Pacific Islands.
Ecology: Grassy fields and thickets. Flowering & fruiting: Mar.–Sep.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Mount Parker, Shatin, Tai Po Kau, Fanling, Sai Kung
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Casearia glomerata Roxb. 嘉賜樹
Fl. Ind., ed. 2, 2: 419. 1832; FHK 122. 1861; Forb. & Hemsl., J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 36: 311. 1904; FKH 110. 1912; FHN 1: 463. 1964; FFJ 4: 16, fig. 15. 1989; FGD 2: 111. 1991; FRPS 52(1): 76, pl. 18: 1. 1999.
Casearia glomerata Roxb. f. pubinervis How & Ko, Acta Bot. Sin. 8(1): 31. 1959; FGX 1: 667. 1991.

Shrub or small tree, 2–10 m tall. Young branches puberulous; old branches terete and glabrous. Petioles 0.6–1.4 cm, subglabrous; leaf blade oblong to oblong-elliptic, 9 –12 × 3 – 5 cm, thinly leathery, base obtuse or rounded, slightly oblique, apex acuminate, margin repand or obtusely dentate, sparsely puberulous when young, glabrescent; lateral veins 7– 8 pairs. Pedicels 0.7–1 cm, densely yellowish brown-puberulous; bracts broadly triangular, ca. 1 mm. Flowers in glomerules, 10 –30-flowered. Calyx lobes 5, oblong, 2–3 mm, densely yellowish puberulous. Stamens 8 –10; filaments puberulous; anthers suborbicular; staminodes elliptic, apex with a bundle of hair. Ovary glabrous, ovoid-conical, ca. 1.5 mm; styles short; stigmas capitate. Capsule ovoid, leathery, 1.2 cm, yellow to orange-red, densely tuberculate when dry; seeds many, ovoid, ca. 4 mm, with red arils.

Locality: Mount Parker, Shatin, Tai Po Kau, Fanling, Sai Kung. Y. S. Lau 1459; K. Y. Tam 1459; L. T. Lo 442.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Xizang; India, Vietnam.
Ecology: Thin forests on slopes. Flowering: Aug.–Dec.; fruiting: Oct. to spring of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Ma On Shan, Mui Tsz Lam, Tai Po Kau, Wu Kau Tang
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Casearia velutina Bl. 毛嘉賜樹
Mus. Bot. 1: 253. 1850; FFJ 4: 15. 1989; FRPS 52(1): 73, pl. 17: 6. 1999.
Casearia balansae Gagnep., Notul. Syst. (Paris) 3: 234. 1914; FRPS 52(1): 71. 1999.
Casearia balansae Gagnep. var. cuneifolia Gagnep., Notul. Syst. (Paris) 2: 244. 1914.
Casearia villilimba Merr., Philip. J. Sci. 23: 254. 1923; FHN 1: 463. 1964; FGD 2: 110, fig. 76. 1991.
Casearia petelotii Merr., J. Arnold Arbor. 19: 56. 1938.

Small tree, to 10 m tall; branchlets zigzag, densely rusty pubescent. Petioles 0.5–1 cm, stout, densely brown-pubescent; leaf blade black when dry, elliptic or elliptic-oblong, 7–20 × 4 – 8 cm, thickly papery, base rounded, unequilateral, apex acuminate, margin serrate, sparsely pilose initially, glabrescent or only pubescent along midveins adaxially, densely yellowish brown villose abaxially; lateral veins 6–12 pairs. Flowers several to many in glomerules. Pedicels 2– 4 mm, pilose. Calyx lobes 5, oblong-elliptic, 2–3 mm, pilose on both surfaces. Stamens 8; filaments puberulous; anthers ellipsoid. Staminodes hairy, apex with a bundle of hair. Ovary ellipsoid, pilose; styles short, ca. 1.5 mm; stigmas discoid. Capsule ellipsoid, 1–1.2 cm, glabrous, fleshy, yellow when mature, black when dried; stipe slightly pubescent. Seeds many, ovoid, pale yellow.

Locality: Ma On Shan, Mui Tsz Lam, Tai Po Kau, Wu Kau Tang. H. C. Tang 2508; Y. S. Lau 1367; Y. W. Lam 221.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Guizhou, Yunnan; SE Asia.
Ecology: Thin forests. Flowering: Mar.–May.
Notes: The species was reported as C. grewiaefolia Vent. previously (Check List HK Plants 40. 1993).

Flacourtia rukam Zoll. & Mor. 大葉刺籬木
Syst. Verz. 2: 33. 1846; FHN 1: 457. 1964; FGD 3: 107. 1995; FRPS 52(1): 42, pl. 9: 9 –11. 1999.

Tree, 5–15 m tall; trunk and old branches zigzag. Young plants armed; spines up to 10 cm; branches spiny or not. Mature plants without spines. Bark brown to grey, smooth; branchlets terete, puberulous, tuberculate and lenticellate when young. Petioles 6–8 mm, brown-pubescent; leaf blade ovate, elliptic to lanceolate, 6 –12 × 4 – 6 cm, more or less leathery, base rounded to obtuse, apex acuminate, margin crenate, glabrous adaxially, pubescent along midvein and lateral veins abaxially; lateral veins 5 –11 pairs. Racemes axillary, 0.5 –1 cm, puberulous. Bracts long-ovate, ca. 1 mm. Pedicels 3– 4 mm. Flowers yellowish green or white. Sepals (3–)4(–6), ovate, puberulous on both surfaces. Male flower: stamens ca. 25; filaments subglabrous, 3 – 4 mm; anthers yellow, small; disc fleshy, 8-lobed. Female flower: staminodes usually absent; ovary bottle-shaped, with 4– 6 parietal placentas; ovules 2 per placenta; styles 4 –6, distinct; stigmas 2-lobed. Drupe globose, deep red, 1.4 cm in diam., 4 – 6-angled, with persistent styles.

Locality: Shing Mun. L. T. Lo 459.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Taiwan; India, Vietnam, Thailand, Malaysia, Philippines.
Ecology: Thin forests on hillslopes or near villages. Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: Jun.– Oct.
Uses: Food (fruit).

Homalium cochinchinense (Lour.) Druce 天料木
Rep. Bot. Exch. Club. Brit. Isles 4: 628. 1917; FHN 1: 461. 1964; NFFJ 4: 17, fig.16. 1989; FGD 2: 114. 1991; FRPS 52(1): 30, pl. 6: 6. 1999.
Astranthus cochinchinensis Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 222. 1790.
Homalium digynum Gagnep., Notul. Syst. (Paris) 3: 247. 1914
Homalium fagifolium Benth., J. Linn. Soc.4: 35. 1860; FHK 122. 1861; FKH 110. 1912.
Homalium phanerophlebium How & Ko, Acta Bot. Sin. 8: 44. 1959.

Shrub or small tree; bark grey-brown; branchlets densely rusty tomentellate when young, glabrescent in age. Petioles 2–3 mm, yellow-pubescent; leaf blade broadly elliptic to obovate-oblong, 6 –10(–15) × 3 –7 cm, papery, base cuneate, apex acute to shortly acuminate, margin remotely and obtusely dentate, pubescent along midvein and lateral veins on both surfaces, rarely sparsely pubescent abaxially; lateral veins 7–9 pairs. Racemes axillary, sometimes with short branches, (5–)8–15 cm, densely yellow-tomentellate. Pedicels filiform, densely yellow-tomentellate, 2–3 mm. Flowers 7- or 8-merous, 8–9 mm in diam. Calyx tube turbinate, 2–2.5 mm, sparsely pilose and grooved; lobes linear or oblanceolate, ca. 3 × 0.3 mm, subglabrous abaxially, sparsely villous adaxially, margin ciliate, apex slightly obtuse. Petals spatulate, 3– 4 × 1 mm, subglabrous or sparsely hairy abaxially, sparsely puberulous adaxially, margin ciliate, conspicuously veined; filaments longer than petals; disc glandular; glands nearly square, hairy. Ovary hairy, styles usually 3, filiform, ca. 3 mm, hairy near base; parietal placentas 3, ovules 2– 4 per placenta. Capsule obconical, 5– 6 mm, subglabrous.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. L. T. Lo 512; Y. S. Lau 717, 1033.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests or thickets. Flowering: Almost all year round; fruiting: Sep.–Dec.
Uses: Timber.

Scolopia chinensis (Lour.) Clos 刺柊
Ann. Sci. Nat. Bot. Ser. 4, 8: 249. 1857; FHK 19. 1861; FGZ 179. 1956; FHN 1: 452, fig. 249. 1964; FFJ 4: 12, fig. 13. 1989; FGD 3: 98. 1995; FRPS 52(1): 16, pl. 4, fig. 1–3. 1999.
Phoberos chinensis Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 1: 318. 1790.
Phoberos cochinchinensis Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 1: 318. 1790.
Scolopia crenata auct. non Clos: FKH 37. 1912.

Shrub or small tree, sometimes with stout spines on trunk and branchlets. Petioles 1–5 mm; leaf blade elliptic to oblong-elliptic, 4 –7 × 2–4 cm, leathery, base rounded to broadly cuneate, with 1 gland on each side, apex rounded or obtuse, margin entire or rarely serrulate, glabrous on both surfaces. Racemes axillary, 2– 6 cm. Flowers pale yellow. Sepals ovate-triangular, 1–2 mm, glabrous on both surfaces, margin ciliate. Petals long-obovate, longer than sepals, glabrous, margin ciliate. Anthers globose, connective-appendages triangular, as long as connectives, apex hairy; disc fleshy, 10-lobed. Ovary ovoid, glabrous, with 2–3 parietal placentas; ovules 2 per placenta, pendulous; styles as long as stamens; stigmas slightly 3-lobed. Berry globose, ca. 4 mm in diam. Seeds 2–6.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 2261; Y. S. Lau 209, 1999.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian; India, Sri Lanka, Laos, Vietnam, Thailand, Malaysia.
