Ecology: Lowland forests. Flowering: Late autumn to early winter; fruiting: Late winter.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Scolopia saeva (Hance) Hance 廣東刺柊
Ann. Sci. Nat. Bot. Ser. 4, 8: 217. 1862; FHN 1: 452. 1964; FFJ 4: 13. 1989; FGD 3: 98, fig. 67. 1995; FRPS 52(1): 18, pl. 4: 7. 1999.
Phoberos saeva Hance, Ann. Bot. Syst. 3: 825. 1852.
Scolopia cinnamomifolia Gagnep., Fl. Indo-Chine 1: 207. 1939.

Shrub or small tree; trunk usually armed with hard spines; young branches glabrous, lenticellate. Petioles 0.8–1 cm; leaf blade ovate or elliptic, 6– 8 × 3– 5 cm, leathery, base cuneate, not glandular, apex abruptly acuminate, margin remotely and shallowly repandserrate, glabrous on both surfaces. Racemes axillary or terminal, shorter than leaves. Sepals ovate, ca. 1.2 mm, margin ciliate. Petals obovate, two times as long as sepals, margin ciliate. Stamens ca. 6 mm; anthers ovoid, connectives-appendages triangular, glabrous; disc 8-lobed. Ovary with 2 or 3 parietal placentas, ovules 2 per placenta; styles thick, shorter than stamens. Berry reddish, ovoid, ca. 8 × 3 – 5 mm. Seeds long-ellipsoid, angled.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 689; K. L. Yip 4228; C. P. Lau 112.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangxi, Guangdong, Fujian; Vietnam.
Ecology: Thin forests on slopes. Flowering: Summer to autumn; fruiting: Autumn to winter.
Uses: Timber.

Xylosma congestum (Lour.) Merr. 柞木
Philipp. J. Sci. 15: 249. 1919; H. L. Li, Woody Fl. Taiwan 611, fig. 241. 1963, & FTW 3: 766, pl. 808. 1977; FFJ 4: 14, fig. 14. 1989; FGD 3: 105, fig. 73. 1995.
Croton congesta Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 582. 1790.
Hisingera japonica Sieb. & Zucc., Abh. Math.-Phys. Cl. Konigl. Bayer. Akad. Wiss. 4(2): 168. 1845.
Hisingera racemosa Sieb. & Zucc., Fl. Jap. 1: 169, 189, t. 88, 100, pl. 3, fig. 1–14. 1835.
Xylosma japonica A. Gray, Mem. Am. Acad. Sci. Art. n. ser. 2, 6: 381. 1859.
Xylosma racemorum (Sieb. & Zucc.) Miq., Ann. Mus. Bot. Lugduno-Batavum 2: 155. 1866; FRPS 52(1): 37, pl. 8: 1–3. 1999.
Xylosma senticosum Hance, J. Bot. 1868. 328; FKH 37. 1912.

Evergreen shrub or small tree, to 15 m tall. Branches spinescent when young, spineless in age, glabrous or puberulous. Petioles ca. 2 mm, glabrous or puberulous; leaf blade broadly ovate or ovate to ovate-elliptic, 3 – 8 × 2–3(– 4.5) cm, leathery, base cuneate or rounded, apex acuminate, margin serrate, glabrous or puberulous along veins on both surfaces; lateral veins 3 – 4 pairs. Racemes 1–2 cm, puberulous. Sepals 4 –6, ovate, 2.5–3.5 mm. Male flower: filaments ca. 4.5 mm, slender; anthers ellipsoid. Female flower: ovary ellipsoid, ca. 4.5 mm, glabrous; styles short; stigmas 2-lobed; disc rounded, margin slightly repand. Berry globose, 4 – 5 mm in diam., black, with persistent sepals at base.

Locality: Wan Chai Gap, Fanling. S. C. Ng 4508; W. J. Tutcher 9204; HK sheet 262.
Distribution: S, E, SW & NW China; Japan, Korea.
Ecology: Thin forests on slopes. Flowering: Spring; fruiting: Winter.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Fanling, Lam Tsuen, Tai Po Kau, Tai Po, Sha Tau Kok
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Xylosma longifolium Clos 長葉柞木
Ann. Sci. Nat., Bot., ser. 4, 8: 231. 1857; FHN 2: 457. 1964; FFJ 4: 15.1989; FGD 3: 105. 1995; FRPS 52(1): 40, pl. 7: 7. 1999.
Xylosma congesta (Lour) Merr. var. kwangtungensis Metc., J. Arnold Arbor. 2: 272. 1931.

Evergreen shrub or small tree, up to 7 m. Branchlets spiny, slender, glabrous. Petioles 5 – 8 mm; leaf blade oblong-lanceolate or lanceolate, 5 –12 × 1.5 – 4 cm, leathery, base cuneate, apex acuminate, margin obtusely serrate, glabrous on both surfaces; lateral veins 4 – 8 pairs. Racemes 0.5 –2 cm, glabrous or puberulous, many-flowered; bracts ovate, small. Sepals 4(– 5), small, ovate, 2– 4 mm. Male flower: yellowish green; pedicels 2–3 mm, puberulous; filaments ca. 4.5 mm; anthers ellipsoid, disc 8-lobed. Female flower: ovary bottleshaped, 3.5– 4 mm; styles short; stigmas 2-lobed. Berry globose, 4– 6 mm in diam., purple, usually with reflexed persistent sepals.

Locality: Fanling, Lam Tsuen, Tai Po Kau, Tai Po, Sha Tau Kok. P. S. Choi 282, 326; Y. S. Lau 2939.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan; India, Indochina.
Ecology: Thin forests. Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: Jun.– Oct.

Bixa orellana L. 紅木
Sp. Pl. 512. 1753; FGZ 176, fig. 80. 1956; FRPS 50(2): 180. 1990; FGD 4: 132. 2000.

Evergreen shrubs or small trees, 2–10 m tall; bark greyish brown or brown, smooth; young branchlets and inflorescence densely covered with red-brown glandular hairs. Petioles 2.5– 7.5 cm, glabrous. Leaves ovate, 8 –20 × 5 –13 cm, base cordate, apex acuminate, glabrous on both surfaces, dotted with resin-like glands; palmately 5-veins arising from the base. Thyrses 5 –10 cm. Flowers large, pink, 4 –5 cm in diam. Sepals obovate, ca. 2 cm, densely red-brown lepidote, with glands at base. Petals obovate, 1–2 cm. Anthers ellipsoid, yellow, 2-celled. Ovary 1-locular, style 1, stigmas bilobed. Capsule subglobose or ovoid, 2.5 – 4 cm, 2-valved, densely spiny; spines purplish brown, 1–2 cm. Seeds obovoid, dark red.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 216, 430, 1236.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian (cultivated); native to tropical America.
Ecology: Flowering: May–Aug.; fruiting: Autumn to winter.
Uses: Ornamental, materials (dye).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Sha Tau Kok, Ma On Shan, Shing Mun, Tai Mo Shan
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Viola verecunda A. Gray 堇菜
Mém. Amer. Acad. Nat. Sci. n. ser. 6: 382. 1858; Forbes & Hemsl., J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 23: 56. 1886; FKH 36. 1912; FRPS 51: 106. 1991; FGD 4: 71, fig. 45. 2000.

Perennial herb, with a short rootstock. Stems 5 –20 cm, glabrous. Leaves basal and alternate on stems; leaf blade broadly cordate, ovate-cordate or reniform, 1.5 –3 × 1.5 –3.5 cm, base cordate, apex broadly obtuse, margin crenate-serrate, subglabrous on both surfaces. Petioles 1.5 –7 cm, usually longer on basal leaves. Stipules of basal leaves adnate to the petioles, free parts lanceolate, 5–10 mm, those of stem leaves free, ovate-lanceolate to spatulate, 6–12 mm. Flowers small, white or pale purple, solitary in axils of stem leaves. Peduncles exceeding the leaves, with a pair of linear bracteoles above middle. Sepals ovate-lanceolate, 4 –5 mm, apex acuminate, basal appendages short. Petals obovate to oblong-obovate, the laterals ca. 10 × 2.5 mm, bearded at base inside, the abaxial one ca. 10 mm including the spur, emarginate at apex; spurs 1.5–2 mm, gibbous. Capsules oblong or ellipsoid, ca. 8 mm, glabrous.

Locality: Sha Tau Kok, Ma On Shan, Shing Mun, Tai Mo Shan. Y. S. Lau 1718, 3057; Y. W. Lam 583.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; Korea, Japan, Mongolia, Russia.
Ecology: Open grassy fields, roadsides. Flowering & fruiting: May–Oct.

Viola betonicifolia J. E. Smith 戟葉堇菜
Cycl. 37(I): 7. 1819; FRPS 51: 71, 1991; FGD 4: 78, fig. 52. 2000.
Viola patrinii auct. non DC.: FHK 20. 1861; FKH 36. 1912.

Perennial herb, stemless, with tufted stock. Leaves all basal; petioles 1.5–13 cm, narrowly winged on the distal half, usually glabrous; Stipules 3/4 adnate to the petioles, free parts linear lanceolate or subulate; leaf blade narrowly lanceolate, narrowly triangular-hastate or triangular-ovate, 2–5 × 0.5 –3 cm, base broadly cuneate or truncate, or sometimes slightly cordate, apex acute, margin sparsely and shallowly undulate-serrate, glabrous or nearly so on both surfaces. Peduncles 6–28 cm, equaling or exceeding leaves, with a pair of linear bracteoles at middle, glabrous or sometimes pubescent on the proximal part. Flowers 10 –20 mm across, white or purple, with darker strips. Sepals 5 –9 × 1–3 mm, ovate-lanceolate to lanceolate, basal appendages 0.5 –1 mm, tip rounded. Petals obovate to oblongobovate, 1–1.2 cm, the laterals bearded at base inside, the abaxial one 1.3 –1.5 cm including the spur; spurs 2– 6 mm, tip rounded. Capsules ellipsoid, 6–9 mm, glabrous.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tsim Shan. H. C. Tang 721; HK sheet 230.
Distribution: Areas S of Qinling Range; Himalayas, India, Sri Lanka, Australia, Indonesia, Japan.
Ecology: Open grassy fields, summits of hills, margins of forest. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Sep.

Viola diffusa Ging. 蔓堇菜
Prodr. 1: 298. 1824; FHK 20. 1861; FKH 36. 1912; FRPS 51: 100. 1991; FGD 4: 75, fig. 48. 2000.

Annual herb, pubescent throughout. Rootstock short, emitting leafy stolons. Leaves tufted on the stock and crowded towards apex of the stolons; petioles 2–4.5 cm, winged; stipules 1/3 adnate to the petioles, free parts linear lanceolate, 4–12 mm; leaf blade ovate or ovate-oblong, 1.5–3.5 × 1–2 cm, base broadly cuneate to truncate, rarely shallowly cordate, decurrent to the petioles, apex obtuse or acutish, margin crenate-serrate. Peduncles 1.5– 8.5 cm, exceeding leaves, with a pair of linear bracteoles at middle. Flowers pale purple to yellowish, not fragrant. Sepals lanceolate, 4–5.5 mm, acute, basal appendages up to 0.5 mm, tip rounded, fimbriate-ciliate. Petals obovate to oblong-obovate, the laterals 6 – 8 mm, not bearded, the abaxial one shorter, ca. 6 mm including the spur; spurs very short, only 1.5 mm. Capsules ellipsoid, 8–10 mm, glabrous.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. W. Lam 478, 773; L. T. Lo 510.
Distribution: Areas S of Qinling Range; India, Nepal, Philippines, Malaysia, Japan.
Ecology: Summits of hills, grassy fields, margins of forests.
Flowering: Mar.–May; fruiting: May–Aug.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Mount Parker, Tai Po, Ng Tung Chai
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Viola inconspicua Blume 長萼堇菜
Bijdr. Fl. Ned. Ind. 1: 58. 1825; FRPS 51: 52. 1991; FGD 4: 77, fig. 51. 2000.
Viola confusa Champ. ex Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 3: 260. 1851, p.p.; FHK 20. 1861, p.p.
Viola serpens auct. non Wall. ex Ging.: FKH 36. 1912.

Perennial herb, stemless, with a short rootstock and long tap root. Leaves all basal; petioles 2–7 cm, glabrous; Stipules 3/4 adnate to the petioles, free parts lanceolate, 3–5 mm; leaf blade triangular or triangular-ovate, 1.5 –7 × 1–3.5 cm, broadest at base, base broadly cordate, with rounded basal lobes, apex acuminate or acute, margin crenate-serrate, usually glabrous on both surfaces. Peduncles slender, equaling or exceeding leaves, glabrous or pubescent. Flowers pale purple, with dark strips. Sepals ovate-lanceolate to lanceolate, 3–6 mm; basal appendages 2–3 mm, apex acute or sometimes incised. Petals oblong-obovate, the laterals 7–9 mm, bearded inside, the abaxial one 10 –12 mm including the spur. Capsules 6–9 mm, ellipsoid, glabrous.

Locality: Mount Parker, Tai Po, Ng Tung Chai. Y. S. Lau 1628; HK sheet 37538, Y. W. Lam 864.
Distribution: Areas S of Qinling Range; Myanmar, Philippines, Malaysia.
Ecology: Margins of forest, grassy fields. Flowering & fruiting: Mar.–Nov.
Notes: The type specimen of Viola confusa was collected from Mount Parker, Hong Kong Island by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1850.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Cultivated in gardens or as pot-plants
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Viola tricolor L. 三色堇
Sp. Pl. 935. 1753; FRPS 51: 127, pl. 25: 7–9. 1991; FGD 4: 69. 2000.
Viola tricolor L. var. hortensis DC., Prodr. 1: 303. 1824.

Annual or short-lived perennial herb, glabrous throughout. Stems to 30 cm tall, erect or becoming diffuse and much-branched. Basal leaves long-petioled, orbicular-cordate to oblong-ovate; stem-leaves ovate-oblong or lanceolate, base rounded, apex obtuse, margin crenate-dentate; stipules large, pinnately parted toward base. Flowers solitary and axillary, 3.5 – 6 cm in diam., usually having three colors, mostly blue, whitish and yellow. Sepals 5, oblong-lanceolate, 12–22 × 3 –5 mm. Petals 5, nearly or quite orbicular, imbricate, the lower petal with a short and obtuse spur. Capsules ellipsoid, 7–12 mm, glabrous.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens or as pot-plants. Y. S. Lau 1582, 1787.
Distribution: Native in Europe; cultivated elsewhere.
Ecology: Flowering: May–Aug.
Uses: Ornamental.

Tamarix chinensis Lour. 檉柳
Fl. Cochinch. 1: 182, pl. 24. 1790; FRPS 50(2): 157, pl. 43: 1–7. 1990. FGD 4: 133, fig. 82. 2000.
Tamarix gallica L. var. chinensis (Lour.) Ehrenb., Linnaea 2: 267. 1827.

Small tree or shrub, 3–6 m; old branches erect, bark reddish brown, fine striate; young branches slender, pendulous, dark purplish red or dark brown. Leaves scalelike, subulate or ovate-lanceolate, 1–3 mm, base attenuate, apex acuminate and incurved, keeled abaxially. Racemes lateral on the apex of current year branches, often clustered in large panicles. Flower pink; bract linear-subulate, as long as or slightly longer than pedicel; pedicel slender, shorter than calyx. Calyx lobes 5, narrowly ovate, 0.7–1.3 mm. Petals 5, obovate, ca. 2 mm, persistent. Stamens 5, longer than petals, filaments inserted between disc lobes, exserted. Disc fleshy, 5–10-lobed. Ovary conical, styles 3, clavate. Capsule conical, 3 mm long, dehiscing into 3 valves; seeds minute, apex with a bundle of hair.

Locality: cultivated. P. S. Choi 341; HK sheet 2654, 33473
Distribution: Anhui, Jiangsu, Shandong, Henan, Hebei, Liaoning; widely cultivated in E, S & SW China.
Ecology: Seasides, sandy places and wastelands. Flowering: Apr.–Sep.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal (folklore).

Passiflora moluccana Reinw. ex Blume var. teysmanniana (Miq.) de Wilde 蛇王藤
Fl. Mal. 1: 7. 1972 & Blumea 20: 239. 1972; FGD 2: 118, pl. 78: 1– 6. 1991; FRPS 52(1): 101. 1999.
Disemma horsfieldii Miq. var. teysmanniana Miq., Fl. Ned. Ind. 1: 700. 1856,
Passiflora cochinchinensis Spreng., Syst. Veg. 4(Cur. Post.): 346. 1827; FHN 1: 466, fig. 257. 1964.
Passiflora ligulifolia Mast., Trans. Linn. Soc. Lond. 27: 632. 1871; FKH 110. 1912.
Passiflora hainanensis Hance, J. Bot. 16: 227. 1878.

Stems glabrous, rarely angled. Stipules absent. Petioles 0.6 –1.5 cm, pilose; leaf blades alternate or sometimes opposite, leathery, variable in shape, linear, linear-oblong or broadly elliptic, 4 –14 × 1– 6 cm, base rounded or obtuse, apex rounded and emarginate or very short acute, margin entire, glabrous and shining adaxially, sometimes pubescent and glandular abaxially. Cymes 1–2-flowered. Bracts and bracteoles very small, linear. Flowers white, 3.5–5 cm in diam.; pedicels 2.5–4.5 cm. Sepals 5, narrowly oblong, 2 cm, pilose abaxially, without appendage at apex. Petals oblong, ca. 1.5 cm; corona consisting of many filiform lobes, lobes in 2 whorls, outer ones 1.2–1.5 cm, inner ones 1.5–3 mm, greenish purple or yellow. Stamens 5, filaments distinct, 6 –10 mm; anthers ellipsoid, ca. 4 mm. Ovary globose, sessile, subglabrous; styles 3, distinct, curved, ca. 5 mm. Berries ovoid or subglobose, 1.5 –2.5 cm or longer, 1–2 cm in diam., glabrous, green, glaucous. Seeds greyish yellow, compressed, ca. 4 mm.

Locality: Lung Kwu Tan, Po Toi. Y. W. Lam 2252; HK sheet 40262, 40294.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan.
Ecology: Thickets. Flowering: Jan.–Apr.; fruiting: May–Aug.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Passiflora foetida L. 龍珠果
Sp. Pl. 2: 959. 1753; FHK 123. 1861; FKH 110. 1912; FHN 1: 466. 1964; FRPS 52(1): 111, pl. 25: 8 –11. 1999; FGD 2: 120. 1991;
Passiflora hispida DC. ex Triana & Planch., Ann. Sci. Nat., Bot., ser. 5, 17: 172. 1873; C. Y. Wu & W. T. Wang, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 6: 236. 1957.
Dysosmia foetida (L.) M. Roem., Fam. Nat. Syn. Monogr. 2: 150. 1846.

Stems slender, terete, angled, pubescent or glabrous. Stipules filiform, lobed, glandular at apex. Petioles 2– 6 cm, villous; leaf blades broadly ovate to oblong-ovate, membranous, 4.5 –13 × 4–12 cm, 3-lobed, base cordate, apex acute or acuminate, margin irregularly undulate, ciliate or glandular-ciliate, villous on both surfaces, mixed with a few glandular hairs adaxially and with scattered small glands abaxially. Cymes 1-flowered. Flowers white or pale purple, white patched, 2–3 cm in diam.; bracts pinnately 1–3-lobed, forming many filiform lobules, lobules glandular hairy at apex. Sepals oblong, 1.5 –1.8 cm, with a horn-like appendage near apex abaxially. Petals as long as sepals. Corona lobes in 3–5 whorls, outer 2 whorls 4–5 mm, those of the inner 3 whorls 2.5 mm. Androgynophore 5–7 mm; filaments connate at base; anthers ellipsoid, 4 mm. Ovary ellipsoid, ca. 6 × 4 –5 mm, stipitate, glandular hairy or glabrous; style 3(– 4), 5 – 6 mm, stigmas capitate. Berries ovoid or globose, 2–3 cm in diam. Seeds ellipsoid, ca. 5 mm, glabrous.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Naturalized. H. C. Tang 1785; Y. S. Lau 1930; G. Gibbs 7546.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan (naturalized); native to Mexico, S & C USA, S America, widely naturalized in tropical regions worldwide.
Ecology: Thickets on wastelands. Flowering: Jul.–Aug.; fruiting: Apr.–May.
Uses: Food (fruit edible).

Carica papaya L. 番木瓜
Sp. Pl. 1036. 1753; FHN 1: 492, fig. 268. 1964; FRPS 52(1): 122. 1999; FGD 5: 23, fig. 17. 2003.
Papaya carica Gaertn., Fruct. Sem. Pl. 2: 191, fig. 122. 1791.

Small tree, to 8 m tall, usually unbranched, sometimes branched due to injury, containing white latex in all parts, dioecious or polygamous. Petioles hollowed, to 1 m; leaf blades suborbicular, 25 –75 cm in diam., palmately and deeply 7–11- lobed, glabrous, lobes deeply and broadly toothed. Male flowers sessile, in pendulous panicles, up to 1 m; calyx small, connate at base, 5-lobed; corolla light yellow, tube 2.5 cm, lobes ca. 1.8 cm; stamens 10, in 2 whorls, alternate to corolla lobes. Female flowers solitary or in several-flowered cymes, short pedicelled or sessile; corolla-tube very short, lobes 5, oblong to lanceolate, fleshy, ca. 5 × 2 cm; ovary ovoid, 2–3 cm long, 1 locular, ovules many; styles short, 5, stigmas 5, fan-shaped, sessile, deeply 5-cleft. Bisexual flowers: stamens 5 or 10, inserted on long or very short corollatubes. Berries ellipsoid or obovoid, 15 –30 cm, orange-yellow when mature. Seeds many, black, globose, testa fleshy, endotesta woody, rugose.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 2144.
Distribution: S & SW China (cultivated); native to tropical America.
Ecology: Flowering and fruiting: Almost all year round.
Uses: Food (fruit).

Benincasa hispida (Thunb.) Cogn. 冬瓜
Mor. Phan. 3: 513. 1881; FRPS 73(1): 198. 1986; FFJ 5: 253, fig. 237. 1993; FGD 3: 128. 1995.
Cucurbita hispida Thunb., Syst. Veg. (ed. 14) 868. 1784; Fl. Jap. 322. 1784.

Annual large herbaceous vine. Stems and branches yellow-brown-hispid and villous, sulcate and angled. Tendrils short and slender. Petioles stout, 5 –20 cm, yellow-brown-hispid and villous; leaf blade reniform-suborbicular, 19 –24 × 10 –30 cm, base deeply cordate, apex acute, margin dentate, 5 –7-lobed, lobes broadly triangular or ovate, pilose to subglabrous adaxially, scabrous and hispid abaxially. Pedicels hispid, 5 –15 cm in male flowers, shorter than 5 cm in female flowers. Bracts pubescent, 6 –10 mm. Calyx-tube villous, lobes lanceolate, dentate, 8 –12 mm. Corolla-lobes 3 –6 × 2.5–4 cm, pubescent on both surfaces, densely hispid at margin near base; filaments 2–3 mm, expanded at base, hispid; anthers 5 mm. Ovary ovoid or cylindric, densely hispid, 2– 4 cm long; styles 2–3 mm, stigmas 3, 12–15 mm wide, 2-lobed. Fruit ellipsoid or terete, 25 –70 × 10 –25 cm, glaucous, hairy. Seeds many, flattened, ovate, 10 –11 × 5 –7 mm, with or without thickened margin.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 12036.
Distribution: Cultivated in tropical and subtropical Asia, E Australia, Madagascar.
Ecology: Flowering: Jun.–Sep.; fruiting: Jul.–Nov.
Uses: Food (fruit), Medicine (folklore).

Benincasa hispida (Thunb.) Cogn. var. chieh-qua How 節瓜
Acta Phytotax. Sin. 3(1): 76. 1954; FRPS 73(1): 200. 1986; FFJ 5: 253. 1993; FGD 3: 129. 1995.

It differs from var. hispida by its yellow-hispid ovary and the fruit being terete, 15 –20 × 4 –11 cm, densely white hispid, not glaucous or slightly glaucous.

Locality: Cultivated. L. T. Lo 515.
Distribution: Widely cultivated in S China.
Ecology: Flowering and fruiting: Spring and summer.
Uses: Food (fruit).

Citrullus lanatus (Thunb.) Matsum. & Nakai 西瓜
Cat. Sem. Spor. Hort. Bot. Univ. Imp. Tokyo 30: n 854. 1916; FRPS 73(1): 200. 1986; FFJ 5: 254, fig. 238. 1993; FGD 3: 125. 1995.
Momordica lanata Thunb., Prodr. Pl. Cap. 13. 1800.
Citrullus vulgaris Schrad. ex Kckl. & Zeyh., Enum. Pl. Afr. Austr. 2: 279. 1836; FHK 125. 1861; FGZ 188. 1956; FHN 1: 475. 1964.

Annual herb. Stems and branches stout, sulcate-angular, villous. Tendrils puberulous, 2-branched. Petioles 3 –12 cm, densely pubescent; leaf blade triangular-ovate, 8 –20 × 5 –15 cm, base cordate, apex acute or acuminate, margin denticulate, hispid on both surfaces, 3-partitioned, middle lobe longer; lobes pinnately partitioned. Flowers solitary. Male flowers: pedicels 3 – 4 cm, villous; calyx-tube villous, lobes narrowly lanceolate, as long as tubes; corolla pale yellow, 2.5–3 cm in diam., greenish and villous abaxially, lobes ovate-oblong, 1–1.5 × 0.5 –0.8 cm. Female flowers: calyx and corolla as in male flowers; ovary densely villous, 5 – 8 mm; styles 4 –5 mm; stigmas 3, reniform. Fruits globose or ellipsoid. Smooth, with pale green or bluish stripes and patches; pulp red, white or pale yellow, juicy. Seeds many, flattened, ovate, black or white, striped or patched, 1–1.5 × 0.5 –0.8 cm.

Locality: Cultivated. L. T. Lo 530, 244; HK sheet 2012.
Distribution: Cultivated in China; native to Africa.
Ecology: Flowering and fruiting: Apr.– Oct.
Uses: Food (fruit), medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Wong Chuk Hang, Tsuen Wan, Shan Liu, Ping Shan

Coccinia grandis (L.) Voigt 紅瓜
Hort. Suburb. Calcutt. 59. 1845; FRPS 73(1): 263. 1986; FGD 3: 140, fig. 101. 1995.
Bryonia grandis L., Mant. 1: 126. 1767.
Coccinia indica Wight & Arn., Prodr. Fl. Penins. Ind. Or. 1: 347. 1834; FKH 112. 1912.

Herbaceous vine, dioecious. Stems angulate and sulcate, glabrous or with scattered pubescence. Tendrils not branched. Petioles 1–5 cm; leaf blade broadly heart-shaped, 4–10 × 4–10 cm, usually pentagonal or 5-lobed, base deeply cordate, with several glands, apex obtuse, with raised spots on both surfaces. Flowers white or yellowish, solitary. Male flowers: pedicels slender, 2– 4 cm, glabrous; calyx-tube broadly campanulate, lobes linearlanceolate, 3 – 4 mm; corolla 2.5 –3.5 cm, lobes ovate, glabrous abaxially, pubescent adaxially; stamens 3, filaments and anthers connate, filaments 2–3 mm, anthers subglobose, 6 –7 mm long. Female flowers: pedicels 2.5–6 cm; staminodes 3, subulate; ovary fusiform, 1.2–1.5 cm, styles 6–7 mm, stigmas 3, 5–6 mm. Berries ellipsoid, 5 × 2.5 cm, red when mature, glabrous. Seeds yellow, oblong, 6 –7 × 2.5 – 4 mm, densely tuberculate.

Locality: Wong Chuk Hang, Tsuen Wan, Shan Liu, Ping Shan. Y. W. Lam 369, 371, 834.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; tropical Africa, SE Asia.
Ecology: Thickets and forests. Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: Jul.–Sep.

Cucumis melo L. 甜瓜
Sp. Pl. 1011. 1753; FRPS 73(1): 202. 1986; FFJ 5: 255, fig. 239. 1993; FGD 3: 126. 1995.
Cucumis bisexualis A. M. Lu & G. C. Wang ex Lu & Z. Y. Zhang, Bull. Bot. Res. North-east Inst. 4(2): 126. 1984.

Annual creeping or climbing herb. Stems angled, hispidulous. Petioles 7–12 cm, setose; leaf blade suborbicular or reniform in outline, pentagonal or 3–7-lobed, 7–15 × 7–15 cm, base cordate, margin dentate, pubescent on both surfaces, hispid along veins abaxially. Male flowers: solitary or clustered; pedicels filiform, 0.5 –4 cm; calyx-tube villous, 6 –8 mm, lobes subulate, shorter than tubes; corolla yellow, 2 cm long; tube 1–2 mm, lobes ovate-oblong; stamens 3; anther cells flexuous, 3– 4 mm; pistillodes 1 mm. Female flowers: solitary; pedicel 1–2 cm; ovary ellipsoid or fusiform, densely white-lanate, villous or puberulous; style 1–2 mm; stigmas 3, connivent, 2–2.5 mm. Fruit polymorphic, usually globose or ellipsoid, often grooved or patched, not spiny, pubescent or glabrous. Seeds many, yellow-white, oblong, 10 –12 × 5 –7 mm, margin not thickened.

Locality: Cultivated.
Distribution: Widely cultivated worldwide.
Ecology: F1owering and fruiting: May–Sep.
Uses: Food (fruit), medicinal (folklore).

Cucumis melo L. var. conomon (Thunb.) Makino 白瓜（越瓜）
Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 16: 16. 1902; FGZ 190. 1956; FHN 1: 476. 1964; FFJ 5: 256. 1993; FGD 3: 126. 1995.

It differs from var. melo by its fruit being terete, obtuse or slightly truncate at both ends, up to 60 cm long, 5 – 6 cm in diam., smooth, striped, pulp white or pale green.

Locality: Cultivated. S. Y. Hu 12131 (CUHK).
Distribution: Cultivated worldwide.
Ecology: Flowering and fruiting: Summer.
Uses: Food (fruit)

Cucumis sativus L. 黃瓜（青瓜）
Sp. Pl. 1012. 1753; FRPS 73(1): 205. 1986; FFJ 5: 256, fig. 240. 1993; FGD 3: 127, fig. 89. 1995

Annual climbing or creeping herb, monoecious. Stem angled, hispid. Tendrils slender, not branched. Petioles 2.5–23 cm; leaf blade broadly ovate-cordate, membranous, 7–20 x 7–20 cm, margin 3 –5-angular or -lobed, lobes triangular-ovate, usually pentagonal, base deeply cordate, apex acute or acuminate, margin dentate, hispidulous on both surfaces. Flowers yellow. Male flowers: often clustered; pedicel filiform, 5 –15 mm, puberulous; calyx-tube tubular, lobes linear-lanceolate or subulate, 1.2 cm; corolla lobes oblong-lanceolate, 2.5 × 1.6 cm; stamens 3, filaments subglabrous, anthers 3 – 4 mm, connective 1 mm. Female flowers: solitary or clustered, pedicels 1–3 cm, pubescent; ovary fusiform, muricate. Fruit cylindrical, 10 –30 cm, 3.5 –5 cm in diam., green or yellow-green, muricate, usually verrucose. Seeds small, oblong, white, 5–10 mm, without thickened margin.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 12078, 34060.
Distribution: Cultivated in tropical and temperate regions.
Ecology: Flowering and fruiting: Summer.
Uses: Food (fruit).

Cucurbita moschata Duchesne 南瓜
Essai Hist. Nat. Courges 7, 15-16. 1786; FHN 1: 483. 1964; FRPS 73(1): 262. 1986; FFJ 5: 257, fig. 241. 1993; FGD 3: 139, fig. 100. 1995.
Cucurbita pepo L. var. moschata Duch. ex Lam., Encycl. 2: 152. 1786.

Annual prostrate or climbing herb. Stems terete or slightly 5-ridged, densely white-setose. Tendrils 3– 4-branched, hispid and tomentose. Petioles stout, to 25 cm, setose; leaf blade broadly ovate or ovate-orbicular in outline, pentagonal or 5-lobed, 15– 40 × 20 – 40 cm, margin serrulate, setose and white patched on both surfaces. Male flowers: pedicels to 33 cm, setose; calyx setose, tube short, 5 – 6 mm, lobes linear, 1–1.5 cm, pubescent, enlarged or leaf-like at apex; corolla tubular, 8 cm long, 6 cm in diam., hairy, lobes spreading, rugose, 5 × 6 cm, with 3 longitudinal veins; stamens 3, filaments glandular, 5– 8 mm, enlarged at base, anthers connivent. Female flowers: ovary 1-locular, style short, stigma enlarged, 2-lobed. Fruiting pedicel stout, angled and sulcate, 5–7 cm, enlarged at apex. Fruits varied in shape, size and color, usually sub-pyriform, compressed globose, ovoid. Pericarp sulcate and verrucose. Seeds many, ovate or oblong, grey-white, margin thickened, 1–1.5 × 0.7–1 cm.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 2757; L. T. Lo 175; HK sheet 2013.
Distribution: Widely cultivated worldwide; native to Mexico and C America.
Ecology: Flowering and fruiting: Apr.–Nov.
Uses: Food (fruit).

Gymnopetalum chinense (Lour.) Merr. 金瓜（越南裸瓣瓜）
Philipp. J. Sci. 15: 256. 1919; FRPS 73(1): 213. 1986; FGD 3: 130. 1995.
Bryonia cochinchinensis Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 595. 1790.
Evonymus chinensis Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 156. 1790.
Gymnopetalum cochinchinense (Lour.) Kurz, J. As. Soc. Bengal 40: 57. 1871; FKH 112. 1912; FHN 1: 479. 1964.
Gymnopetalum quinquelobatum Merr., J. Arnold Arbor. 19: 70. 1938

Perennial herbaceous vine, monoecious. Stems 5-angled, hispid, glabrescent. Petioles 1–5 cm; leaf blade membranous or thinly papery, ovate-heart-shaped in outline, pentagonal or 3 –5-lobed, 4 – 8 × 4 – 8 cm, base cordate, apex acuminate, margin dentate or undulate, scabrous and tuberculate on both surfaces. Male flowers: solitary or 3 – 8 in racemes; peduncle slender, 10 – 15 cm; bract leaf-like, rhomboid, pubescent; calyx-tube narrow, 2 cm, pubescent, lobes linear, 7 mm; corolla white, lobes oblongovate, 15 mm; filaments 0.5 mm, anthers 7 mm. Female flowers: solitary; pedicels 1– 4 cm; ovary ellipsoid, 1–1.2 cm, 5 mm in diam., yellow-brown-villous, acute at the both ends, style 5 –8 mm, stigmas 3. Fruits ellipsoid, orange, 4 –5 cm, smooth, 10-ridged, acute at the both ends. Seeds oblong, 7 x 3 –3.5 mm, both ends obtuse, rugose and marginate.

Locality: Tai Po. Y. S. Lau 2535; HK sheet 12023.
Distribution: Yunnan, Guangxi, Hainan, Guangdong; India to SE Asia.
Ecology: Forests and thickets. Flowering: Jul.–Sep.; fruiting: Sep.–Dec.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai, Tsz Mun Tin
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Gynostemma pentaphyllum (Thunb.) Makino 絞股藍
Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 16: 179. 1902; FHN 1: 485. t. 266. 1964; FRPS 73(1): 269. 1986; FFJ 5: 242, fig. 226. 1993; FGD 3: 140. 1995.
Vitis pentaphylla Thunb., Fl. Jap. 105. 1784.

Stems slender, ridged and sulcate, glabrous or pubescent. Tendrils long, 2-branched at apex. Petioles 2–7 cm, hairy. Leaves membranous or papery, palmately (3 –)5(–7)-foliolate, pubescent or glabrous; leaflets ovate-oblong or lanceolate, 2–15 × 0.8 –5 cm, central one larger, lateral ones smaller, base attenuate, apex acute or acuminate, mucronate, margin undulate-dentate, glabrous or pilose on both surfaces, lateral veins 4–8 pairs; petiolules 1–5 mm. Male inflorescences 10 –16 cm, many-branched. Male flowers: pedicels filiform, 1– 4 mm; bracteole subulate; calyx-tube very short, lobes triangular, 0.7 mm; corolla pale green or white, lobes ovate-lanceolate, 2.5–3 mm, ciliolate. Female inflorescences much shorter. Female flowers: calyx and corolla as in male flowers; staminodes 5, short; ovary globose, 2–3-locular, styles 3, stigmas bifid. Berries globose, 5 – 6 mm in diam., indehiscent, black when mature, glabrous, 2-seeded. Seeds compressed, papillose.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai, Tsz Mun Tin. Y. W. Lam 419, 420, 421.
Distribution: S Shaanxi and regions S of Changjiang River. E Asia to tropical Asia.
Ecology: Forests and thickets. Flowering: Mar.–Nov.; fruiting: Apr.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal.

Lagenaria siceraria (Molina) Standl. 葫蘆
Publ. Field Mus. Nat. Hist. Chicago Bot. Ser. 3: 435. 1930; FHN 1: 480. 1964; FRPS 73(1): 216. 1986; FFJ 5: 247, fig. 231. 1993; FGD 3: 131, fig. 93. 1995.
Cucurbita siceraria Molina, Sag. Stor. Nat. Chili 133. 1782.

Stems and branches sulcate and ridged, sticky pubescent. Petioles 5–20 cm, pubescent; leaf blade papery, suborbicular-cordate in outline, pentagonal or slightly 3 –5-lobed, 10 –35 × 10 –35 cm, margin irregularly dentate, puberulous on both surfaces, palmately 5 –7-nerved. Male flowers: calyx-tube infundibular, 2 cm, 1 cm in diam., pubescent, lobes lanceolate, 12 × 1.5–2 mm; corolla lobes 3 – 4 × 2–3 cm, slightly rugose, conspicuously veined; filaments 3– 4 mm, anthers 8 –10 mm. Female flowers: calyx and corolla as in male flowers; ovary ellipsoid, 3 × 1.3 cm, densely pubescent; stigma enlarged. Fruits varied in shape and size, flask-shape, clavate etc., 20 – 60 cm long, 9–16 cm in diam. Seeds white, obovate or triangular, apex truncate or bifid.

Locality: Cultivated. K. Li 5388; HK sheet 12025, 12035.
Distribution: Cultivated in tropical and temperate regions.
Ecology: Flowering: Summer; fruiting: Autunm.
Uses: Food (fruit), medicinal.

Luffa acutangula (L.) Roxb. 廣東絲瓜（絲瓜）
Hort. Beng. 70. 1814; FKH 112. 1912; FRPS 73(1): 196. 1986; FFJ 5: 251, fig. 235. 1993; FGD 3: 123, fig. 86. 1995.
Cucumis acutangula L., Sp. Pl. 1011. 1753.

Stems stout, sulcate and angled, pubescent. Tendrils often trifid. Petioles 8–12 cm; leaf blade membranous, suborbicular in outline, often 5–7-lobed, 15–20 × 15–20 cm, base cordate, apex acute, margin sparsely dentate, slightly scabrous on both surfaces, sometimes with raised white spots adaxially. Male flowers: 17–20 arranged in racemes; peduncles 10 –15 cm; pedicels 1– 4 cm; calyx-tube campanulate, 5–8 × 10 mm, lobes lanceolate, 4–6 × 2–3 mm, slightly reflexed; corolla rotate, lobes obcordate, 2 × 2–2.5 cm, apex emarginate; stamens 3, filaments 4–5 mm, anthers puberulous. Female flowers: ovary clavate, ridged. Fruits cylindric or clavate, 8 –12-ribbed and sulcate, glabrous, 15 –75 cm long, 6 –10 cm in diam., dark green, scabrous. Seeds ovate, black, 1–1.2 × 0.7–0.8 cm, margin not winged.

Locality: Cultivated. L. T. Lo 520; HK sheet 12028, 12030.
Distribution: Widely cultivated in tropical regions.
Ecology: Flowering and fruiting: Summer to autumn.
Uses: Food (fruit).

Luffa aegyptiaca Mill. 水瓜
Gard. Dict. ed. 8. 1768.
Luffa cylindrica (L.) Roem., Syn. Mon. 2: 63. 1846; FRPS 73(1): 194. 1986; FFJ 5: 250, fig. 234. 1993; FGD 3: 124. 1995.
Momordica cylindrica L., Sp. Pl. 1009. 1753.

Stems and branches scabrous, ridged and sulcate. Tendrils usually trifid. Petioles scabrous, 4–12 cm, puberulous; leaf blade triangular or suborbicular in outline, base cordate, 10–25 × 10–25, often palmately 5–7-lobed, lobes triangular, apex acute or acuminate, margin dentate, puberulous on both surfaces, white punctate adaxially. Male flowers: usually 15 –20-flowers in a raceme; peduncles stout, 10 –15 cm, pubescent; pedicels 1–2 cm; calyx broadly campanulate, 5 –9 mm, puberulous, lobes ovate-lanceolate or nearly triangular, 1cm; corolla rotate, 5 –9 cm in diam., lobes oblong-cuneate, 2– 4 × 2–2.8 cm, densely yellow-white-villous adaxially, apex rounded to truncate, base attenuate. Stamens 5, filaments 6 – 8 mm. Female flowers: pedicels 2–10 cm; ovary long cylindrical, puberulous, stigmas 3, expanded, bifid. Fruit cylindrical, straight or slightly curved, 15–55 cm, grooved or striped, not ridged, puberulous, strongly fibrous inside when mature. Seeds ovate, smooth, black, margin slightly winged.

Locality: Cultivated. L. T. Lo 332; Y. S. Lau 2627, 2618.
Distribution: Cultivated in tropical and temperate regions.
Ecology: Flowering and fruiting: Summer to autumn.
Uses: Food (fruit), medicinal (folklore).

Momordica charantia L. 苦瓜
Sp. Pl. 1009. 1753; FHK 125. 1861; FKH 112. 1912; FHN 1: 473. 1964; FFJ 5: 249, fig. 233. 1993; FRPS 73(1): 189. 1986; FGD 3: 122, fig. 85. 1995.
Momordica indica L., Herb. Amb. 24. 1754.

Annual herbaceous vine, many-branched, monoecious; stems and branches pubescent. Tendrils unbranched. Petioles slender, pilose, glabrescent, 4 –17 cm; leaf blade papery, ovate-reniform or suborbicular, 4–24 × 2.5 –12 cm, base cordate, puberulous or subglabrous on both surfaces, 5–7-partitioned, lobes ovate-oblong, margin crenate or irregularly lobed. Flowers yellow, solitary and axillary. Male flowers: pedicels slender, puberulous, 3 –7 cm; calyx-tube ovoid, 5 mm, pubescent; lobes ovate-lanceolate, 7 × 5 mm, pubescent; corolla 4 cm in diam.; lobes obovate, 2 × 1.3 cm, pubescent; stamens 3, distinct, anther cells conduplicate. Female flowers: pedicels 10 –12 cm, with a bract at base; perianth as in male flowers; ovary fusiform, densely verrucose. Fruits fusiform or cylindrical, verrucose, 10–20 cm, orange when mature, glabrous, dehiscing into 3 valves. Seeds many, compressed, oblong, with red arils.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. W. Lam 870, 871; Y. S. Lau 2616.
Distribution: Cultivated in tropical and temperate regions.
Ecology: Flowering and fruiting: May– Oct.
Uses: Food (fruit), medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Po, Lam Tsuen, Fanling, Sha Tau Kok

Momordica cochinchinensis (Lour.) Spreng. 木鼈子
Syst. Veg. 3: 14. 1826; FHN 1: 473. 1964; FRPS 73(1): 192, pl. 49: 8 –12. 1986; FFJ 5: 249, fig. 232. 1993; FGD 3: 122. 1995.
Muricia cochinchinensis Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 596. 1790.

Perennial stout herbaceous vine, dioecious. Root tuberous. Stems and branches glabrous or puberulous. Tendrils unbranched. Petioles stout, 5–10 cm, with 2–4 glands at the base or middle; leaf blade broadly ovate-cordate, 8 –20 × 6–20 cm, 3–5-lobed, median lobe larger, base cordate, with several glands at margin, apex acute or acuminate, margin undulate-dentate, rarely entire, glabrous on both surfaces, or white punctate abaxially. Male flowers: solitary or in a short racemes; pedicels stout, 3–5 cm, bracteate at the apex, bracts orbicular-reniform; calyx-tube infundibular, lobes oblonglanceolate or oblong, 10–16 mm, scabrous or pubescent; corolla white, yellowish, lobes ovate-oblong, 5– 6 cm, densely pubescent along veins, yellow-glandular at the base; stamens 3, anther cells reflexed. Female flowers: solitary; pedicel 5–10 cm, bracteate at the middle; bracts 2 mm; calyx and corolla as in male flowers; ovary ovoid, 1 cm long, densely spiny. Fruit ovoid, 12–15 cm in diam., red, fleshy, densely spiny. Seeds many, ovate or square, both surfaces sculptured, margin undulate-sublobulate.

Locality: Tai Po, Lam Tsuen, Fanling, Sha Tau Kok. Y. S. Lau 765, 891; W. J. Tutcher 9613.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Bangladesh, India, Indochina, Malaysia, Myanmar.
Ecology: Margins of forests. Flowering: Jun.–Aug.; fruiting: Aug.– Oct.
Uses: Medicinal.

Sechium edule (Jacq.) Swartz 佛手瓜（合掌瓜）
Fl. Ind. Occ. 2: 1150. 1800; FRPS 73(1): 277, pl. 65: 5 – 8. 1986; FFJ 5: 252, fig. 236. 1993; FGD 3: 141, fig. 103. 1995.
Sicyos edulis Jacq., Enum. Syst. Pl. 32. 1760.

Stem angled and sulcate. Petioles slender, glabrous, 3 –15 cm; leaf blade membranous, ovate-cordate in outline, 8 –20 × 8 –20 cm, base cordate, apex short-acuminate, margin entire or denticulate, polygonal or 3–5-lobed, slightly scabrous adaxially, puberulous abaxially. Male inflorescences: racemose 10–30-flowered; peduncle 8 –30 cm long; pedicels 1–6 mm. Male flowers: calyx-tube short, lobes explanate, 5 –7 mm; corolla pale yellow, rotate. Female flowers: pedicels 1–1.5 cm; calyx and corolla as in male flowers; ovary obovoid, 5-angled, style 2–3 mm, stigma 2 mm broad. Fruit pale green, obovoid, slightly hispid, 8–15 cm long, 6– 8 cm in diam., 5- sulcate in upper part. Seed large, 10 x 7 cm, ovate, compressed.

Locality: Cultivated. S. P. Lau 72; H. C. Tang 1455; HK sheet 12124.
Distribution: Yunnan, Guangxi, Guangdong, Sichuan (cultivated or naturalized); native to America.
Ecology: Flowering: Jul.–Sep.; fruiting: Aug.– Oct.
Uses: Food (fruit).

Solena amplexicaulis (Lam.) Gandhi 茅瓜
Fl. Hassan District 179. 1976; FRPS 73(1): 178, pl. 47: 1–9. 1986; FFJ 5: 243, fig. 227. 1993; FGD 3: 121, fig. 84. 1995.
Bryonia amplexicaulis Lam., Encycl. 1: 496. 1785.
Bryonia umbellata Klein ex Willd., Sp. Pl. 4(1): 618. 1805.
Karivia umbellata (Klein ex Willd.) Arn., J. Bot. (Hooker) 3: 275. 1841; FHK. 124. 1861.
Melothria heterophylla (Lour.) Cogn., Mon. Phan. 3: 618. 1881; FGZ 184. 1956; FHN 1: 472. 1964.
Solena heterophylla Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 2: 514 –515. 1790.
Zehneria umbellata Thw., Enum. Pl. Zeyl. 125. 1859; FKH 112. 1912.

Plant dioecious. Roots fusiform, 1.5 –2 cm in diam. Stems and branches glabrous. Petioles 0.5 –1.8 cm; leaf blades papery or leathery, very variable, triangular-hastate, narrowly triangular-lanceolate, ovate-cordate, subtriangular, undivided or 3 –5-lobed, 3.5–15 × 3 –12 cm, base cordate, apex obtuse or acuminate, margin entire or undulate or sparsely denticulate, often scabrous and glabrous on both surfaces. Male inflorescences umbellate,10 –20-flowered; peduncle very short; pedicels 2–8 mm. Male flowers: calyx-tube 5 mm, lobes subulate, 0.2–0.3 mm; corolla yellow, lobes triangular, 1.5 mm; filaments filiform, ca. 3 mm, anthers curved. Female flowers: solitary; pedicels 0.5 –1 cm; ovary ovoid, 2.5 –3.5 × 2–3 mm; stigmas 3. Fruit red-brown, ellipsoid or subglobose, 2– 6 cm long, 2–5 cm in diam., pubescent. Seeds grey-white, ovoid, 5–7 mm long, 5 mm in diam., emarginate.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 321, 709, 3132.
Distribution: Xizang, Yunnan, Sichuan, Guizhou, Guangxi, Hainan, Guangdong, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Sri Lanka, Sikkim, Vietnam, Indonesia (Java), Nepal.
Ecology: Forests or thickets in valleys. Flowering: May–Aug.; fruiting: Aug.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Trichosanthes anguina L. 蛇瓜
Sp. Pl. 2: 1008. 1753; FHN 1: 480. 1965; FRPS 73(1): 248, pl. 61: 1–3. 1986; FFJ 5: 260, fig. 243. 1993.
Trichosanthes cucumerina L. var. anguina (L.) Haines, Bot. Bihar Orissa 388. 1922; FGD 3: 134. 1995.

Annual herbs, monoecious, without tuberous root. Stems slender, branched, ridged and sulcate, pubescent and hispid. Tendrils 2–3-branched. Petioles 3 –8 cm; leaf blade membranous, suborbicular or reniform-orbicular, 8–16 × 12–16 cm, base cordate, margin sparsely serrate, deeply (3–)5(–7)-lobed, pubescent on both surfaces, sparsely hispid adaxially. Male racemes 8 –15-flowered, usually paired with a female flower; peduncle 10 –18 cm; pedicels 5–2 cm, erect; bracteoles minute, subulate-lanceolate, 3 mm; Male flowers: calyx-tube subcylindrical, 2.5 –3 cm, densely pubescent and sparsely hispid; lobes reflexed, ca. 2 mm; corolla white, lobes ovate-oblong, 7– 8 mm, 3-veined, apex long fimbriate. Female flowers: solitary; pedicles to 1 cm, villous; perianth as in male flowers; ovary clavate, densely pubescent and hispid. Fruit cylindric, smooth, often contorted, 1–2 m long, 3– 4 cm in diam., orange when mature. Seed oblong, embedded in fresh red pulp, finely rugulose, margin undulate.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. W. Lam 885; L. T. Lo 517; HK sheet 12016.
Distribution: Cultivated in China. Native to India; also cultivated in E Africa, Japan, Malaysia, Philippines.
Ecology: Flowering and fruiting: Summer to autumn.
Uses: Food (fruit), medicinal (root and seed).

Trichosanthes cucumeroides (Seringe) Maxim. 王瓜
Enum. Pl. Jap. 1: 172. 1873
Bryonia cucumeroides Ser., Prodr. 3: 308. 1828.

Perennial herbaceous vine, dioecious, with tuberous roots. Stems slender, branched, grooved, pubescent. Petioles 3–10 cm, densely minutely tomentose and hispidulous; leaf blade broadly ovate or orbicular, papery, 5 –13(–19) × 5 –12(–18) cm, often 3 –5-lobed, sometimes unlobed, base deeply cordate, apex obtuse or acuminate, margin serrulate or undulate-dentate; minutely tomentose and hispidulous adaxially; densely and minutely tomentose abaxially. Male flowers in racemes; peduncle 5–10 cm, striate, pubescent; bracteoles linear-lanceolate, 2–3 mm, entire, pubescent, rarely bracteoles absent; calyx-tube 6–7 cm, minutely tomentose, lobes linearlanceolate, 3– 6 × 1.5 mm, entire; corolla white, lobes oblong-ovate, 14–15 × 6 –7 mm, very long fimbriate at apex. Female flowers solitary; pedicels 0.5–1 cm; ovary ellipsoid, densely pubescent; perianth as in male flowers. Fruit ovoid, ovoid-ellipsoid or globose, 6 –7 × 4 –5.5 cm, orange-red, smooth, beaked. Seeds transversely ellipsoid, 7–12 × 7–14 mm, deep brown, 3-locular; the two lateral ones large ca. 4.5 mm in diam., tuberculate.

Locality: Hong Kong without locality. [fide Dunn & Tutcher, 1912]
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Jiangxi, Sichuan, Zhejiang; Japan.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: May–Aug.; fruiting: Aug.–Nov.

Trichosanthes pedata Merr. & Chun 叉指葉栝樓
Sunyatsenia 2: 20. 1934; FHN 1: 482. 1956; FRPS 73(1): 234. 1986; FGD 3: 137, fig. 98. 1995.
Trichosanthes pedata Merr. & Chun var. yunnanensis C. Y. Cheng & Yueh, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 12(4): 445, pl. 87: 4b & pl. 88: 28. 1974.

Perennial herbaceous vine, dioecious. Stems slender, striate, grooved. Tendrils 2-branched. Leaves (3 –)5-foliolate. Petioles 2.5 – 5.5 cm; leaflets lanceolate or oblong-oblancelate, papery, 3 –14 × 1.2– 4 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, margin sparsely denticulate, hispidulous or white-punctate adaxially, glabrous abaxially; petiolules 2– 4 mm. Male racemes 8 –19 cm; peduncle and pedicels brownpubescent; bracteoles obovate or rhombic-ovate, 1–2 cm, pubescent, apex laciniate or dentate. Male flowers: calyx-tubes 2– 4 cm, lobes triangular-lanceolate, 0.7–1 cm, entire; corolla white. Female flowers: solitary. Fruit globose, 5 – 6 cm in diam., orange-yellow, smooth. Seeds many, ovate or obovate, slightly tumid, 1–1.2 × 0.8 cm.

Locality: Kop Tong.
Distribution: Guangdong, Hainan, Hunan, Yunnan, Jiangxi; Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests or thickets. Flowering: Jun.–Aug.; fruiting: Jul.–Dec.

Trichosanthes ovigera Blume 全緣栝樓（野王瓜）
Bijdr. 934. 1826; FRPS 73(1): 255, pl. 63: 6–13. 1986; FGD 3: 133, fig. 94. 1995, p.p. excl. syn. T. cucumeroides (Ser.) Maxim., T. dicoelosperma Clarke, T. baviensis Gagnep., T. hainanensis Hayata, T. trichocarpa C. Y. Wu ex C. Y. Cheng & Yueh.
Trichosanthes himalensis C. B. Clarke, Fl. Brit. India 2(6): 608. 1879; FKH 111. 1912.

Perennial herbaceous vine, dioecious. Stems slender, grooved, pubescent. Petioles 4–12 cm, striate, pubescent; leaf blade papery, ovate-cordate to suborbicular, 7–19 × 7– 8 cm, unlobed or shortly trilobed or 3 –5-lobed, base deeply cordate, apex acuminate, margin sparsely serrulate or undulate-dentate, pubescent and hispidulous adaxially, minutely tomentose abaxially. Male flowers in racemes, peduncle 10 –26 cm, striate, densely pubescent; pedicels ca. 5 mm; bracteoles lanceolate or oblanceolate, ca. 1.6 × 0.5 –0.6 cm, margin triangular-dentate; calyx-tube tubular, ca. 5 mm; lobes triangular-ovate, 7–10 × 2–3 mm, entire. Female flowers solitary; pedicels 1–3.5 cm, striate, pubescent; calyx-tube terete, 2–5 cm, glabrous or pubescent; ovary ovoid, 1–1.5 × 0.3 –0.5 cm. Fruit ovoid or fusiform ellipsoid, 5 –7 × 2.5 – 4 cm, smooth, beaked. Seeds triangular in outline, 7–9 × 7– 8 mm, turgid with a central thickened zone; 3-locular; two lateral locules empty.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Chuen Lung, Tai Mo Shan, Tai Po Kau, Ping Shan, Lantau Island, Lamma Island. Y. W. Lam 368, 959, 1019.
Distribution: Yunnan, Guizhou, Guangxi, Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, E Himalaya, Thailand, Vietnam, Indonesia.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: May–Sep.; fruiting: Sep.–Dec.

Trichosanthes rosthornii Harms 中華栝樓
Engl., Bot. Jahrb. 29: 603. 1901; FRPS 73(1): 243. 1986; FGD 3: 134, pl. 95. 1995.
Trichosanthes crenulata C.Y. Cheng & C.H. Yueh, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 18(3): 343 –344, pl. 6: 9, 20, 23. 1980.
Trichosanthes kirilowii auct. non Maxim.: FKH 111. 1912.
Trichosanthes guizhouensis C.Y. Cheng & C.H. Yueh, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 18(3): 344 –345, pl. 3 & pl. 6: 10. 1980.
Trichosanthes stylopodifera C.Y. Cheng & C.H. Yueh, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 18(3): 341, pl. 6: 7, 22. 1980.
Trichosanthes uniflora Hao, Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 68(5): 640 – 641. 1938.

Perennial herbaceous vine, dioecious. Stems grooved, glabrous or sparsely puberulous. Tendrils 2–7-branched. Petioles 2.5 –7 cm, sparsely puberulous; leaf blade variable in shape, broadly ovate to suborbicular, papery, 7–18 × 6 –16 cm, deeply 3–7-lobed, base cordate or hastate, apex acuminate, rarely acute or obtuse, margin remotely dentate or sometimes undulate, glabrous or sparsely puberulous on both surfaces. Male racemes 8–20 cm, several to many-flowered; peduncle 8–10 cm; pedicels up to ca. 7 cm; bracteoles leaf-like, 6 –25 mm, margin irregularly erose. Male flowers: calyx-tube narrowly cylindric, 1.5–3 cm, lobes subulate-linear, 7–14 mm. Female flowers: solitary; pedicels 5 –8 cm, puberulous; ovary ellipsoid, 1–2 × 0.5 –1 cm, puberulous. Fruit globose or ellipsoid, 8 –16 × 7–10 cm, smooth, glabrous, orange-yellow. Seeds ovate-oblong, compressed, 1.2–2.2 cm, brown, marginate.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Wu Kau Tang, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 1509; W. J. Tutcher 9544.
Distribution: Yunnan, Sichuan, Guizhou, Guangdong, Jiangxi, Hubei, Shaanxi, Gansu.
Ecology: Forests and thickets. Flowering: Jun.–Aug.; fruiting: Aug.– Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (root & fruit).
Notes: The species was reported as Trichosanthes kirilowii Maxim. previously (Check List HK Plants 42. 1993).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Mo Shan, Tai Po, Tai Po Kau, Kap Lung

Zehneria japonica (Thunb.) H. Y. Liu 老鼠拉冬瓜
Bull. Nation. Mus. Nat. (Taiwan) 1: 40. 1989.
Aechmandra odorata Hook. f. & Thoms. ex Benth. FHK 124. 1861.
Bryonia japonica Thunb., F1. Jap. 325. 1784.
Melothria indica Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 35. 1790; FKH 113. 1912; FGZ 184. 1956.
Melothria odorata Hook. f. & Thoms. ex C. B. Clarke, Fl. Brit. India 2(6): 626. 1879; FKH 113. 1912.
Zehneria indica (Lour.) Keraudren, Fl. Cambodge, Laos & Vietnam 15: 52, fig. 5 – 8. 1975; FRPS 73(1): 170, pl. 45: 1–7. 1986; FFJ 5: 244, fig. 228. 1993; FGD 3: 118, fig. 82. 1995.

Plant monoecious. Stems and branches filiform, glabrous. Tendrils unbranched. Petioles slender, 1–3.5 cm; leaf blade membranous, triangular-ovate, undivided or 3 –5-lobed, 2–10 × 2–10 cm, base cordate, apex acute or acuminate, margin entire or sparsely denticulate, scabrous and white-punctate adaxially, glabrous or puberulous along veins on both surfaces. Male flower solitary or in 2–3-flowered racemes; pedicels filiform, 1–2.5 cm, glabrous; calyx broadly campanulate, 1.5 × 2–2.5 mm; corolla white or yellow, puberulous, lobes ovate-oblong, 2–2.5 × 1– 1.5 mm; filaments short, 0.5 mm; anthers ellipsoid, pubescent, 1 mm, anther cells curved, puberulous, connective protrudent at apex. Female flower solitary or rarely paired in the same axil together with male flowers; corolla broadly campanulate, ca. 2.5 mm in diam., lobes lanceolate, 2.5 –5 × 1–1.5 mm; staminodes glandular; ovary narrowly ovoid, 3.5 – 4 × 1–2 mm, tuberculate; style 1.5 mm. Berries ellipsoid or ovoid, 1–1.5 cm long, 5 – 8 mm in diam., obtuse at both ends, orange or red. Seeds greyish white, ovate, 3 –5 × 3 –4 mm, margin inconspicuous.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Tai Po, Tai Po Kau, Kap Lung. Y. W. Lam 1151; Y. S. Lau 772, 3259.
Distribution: Yunnan, Sichuan, Guangxi, Hainan, Guangdong, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Zhejiang, Jiangsu, Anhui, Hubei; Korea, Japan, India, Vietnam, Indonesia, Philippines.
Ecology: Forests and thickets. Flowering: Apr.–Jul.; fruiting: Jul.– Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

(Sweet) L. B. Sm. & B. G. Schub.
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Begonia cucullata Willd. var. hookeri (Sweet)）L. S. Sm. & Schub. 四季秋海棠
Darwiniana 5: 104. 1941; C. M. Hu in FGD 3: 146. 1995.
Begonia hookeri Sweet, Hort. Brit. (ed. 2) 437. 1850.
Begonia semperflorens auct. non Link & Otto: FGZ 190. 1956; FHN 1: 489. 1964.

Perennial herbs, 15 – 45 cm tall. Stems succulent, green or reddish. Leaves alternate, ± fleshy; petioles 0.5 –2 (–3) cm; leaf blade ovate to broadly ovate, 5 –10 × 3.5 –7.5 cm, apex rounded or obtuse, base broadly rounded or slightly cordate and oblique, margin serrulate, ciliate, shining adaxially. Cymes axillary. Peduncle 1.5 – 4 cm. Flowers rosy, pink or white; male flowers: 1–2 cm in diam., perianth-segments 4, outer 2 suborbicular, ca. 1.5 cm in diam., inner 2 obovate-oblong, 8–10 × 4–5 mm; female flowers: smaller, perianth segments 5; ovary 3-locular. Capsule 10–12 mm long, with 3 slightly unequal wings.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. HK sheet 12255.
Distribution: Native to Brazil; widely cultivated elsewhere.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr.–Dec.
Uses: Ornamental.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Ng Tung Chai, Ma On Shan, Sunset Peak
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Begonia fimbristipula Hance 紫背天葵
J. Bot. 21: 202. 1883; FKH 113. 1912; FHN 1: 490. 1964; FGD 3: 146. 1995; FRPS 52(1): 190. 1999.

Perennial small herb, with tuberous root. Stem very short, less than 1.5 cm, usually with only one leaf. Petioles shorter or longer than leaf blade, with coarse hairs or glabrescent. Stipules small 2–3 mm, ovate-lanceolate, margin fimbriate. Leaf blade orbicular- or ovatecordate, 4 –15 × 3 –12 cm, apex acuminate, base cordate, basal lobes more or less overlapped, sparsely or densely covered with small coarse hairs on adaxial surface, usually purplish and strigose along veins on abaxial surface, margin irregularly double-serrate. Cymes twice or thrice branched. Peduncles slender, 3 –15 cm, red, glabrous. Flowers pink, slightly scented; male flowers: perianth segments 4, outer 2 ovate, 6 –12 mm, inner 2 obovate-oblong; female flowers: smaller, perianth-segments 3, two larger, half-orbicular, ca. 3 mm, another one smaller and narrower, oblong; ovary 3-locular. Capsule triangular, glabrous, with 3 unequal wings.

Locality: Ng Tung Chai, Ma On Shan, Sunset Peak. Y. S. Lau 1402; L. T. Lo 47.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian.
Ecology: Clefts of stones by streams or shaded and wet places. Flowering: May–Aug.
Uses: Ornamental, beverage.

Begonia hongkongensis F. W. Xing 香港秋海棠
Ann. Bot. Fennici 42: 151, fig. 1–2. 2005.

Perennial herbs, with creeping rhizome. Stems 10 –21 cm, glabrous. Petioles of basal leaves 5 –10 cm, sparsely covered with short hairs near apex. Stipules membranous, lanceolate, 1–2 × 2–2.5 mm. Leaf blade oblong-ovate to rhombic-ovate, 7–14 × 2.3 – 4.5 cm, apex acuminate, base cuneate to broadly cuneate, slightly oblique, margin irregularly and remotely serrate and shallowly 1–4-lobed, glabrous adaxially, sparsely covered with brown short hairs along veins on abaxial surface; cauline leaves 2–3, similar to basal leaves, 4.5–9 × 1.7–5.3 cm. Cymes dichotomous. Peduncles ca. 5 cm in fruiting time, glabrous. Flowers white. Male flowers: pedicels 7–14 mm; perianth-segments 4, outer 2 broadly ovate or oblong, 10 × 9 mm, inner 2 smaller, ovate. Female flowers: pedicels 2–2.5 cm; perianth 5, 7–12 × 6 –12 mm; ovary 2-locular. Capsule oblong, subglabrous, with 3 unequal wings.

Locality: Kau Keng Shan, Shum Tseng. Xing et al. 9972, 15248 (IBSC).
Distribution: Endemic to Hong Kong.
Ecology: Ravines. Flowering: Jul.–Sep.; fruiting: Oct.–Dec.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Kau Keng Shan by F. W. Xing in 1997.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Ma On Shan, Mui Tsz Lam, Tsz Mun Tin
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Begonia crassirostris Irmsch. 粗喙秋海棠
Mitt. Inst. Allg. Bot. Hamburg 10: 513. 1939; FHN 1: 488, fig. 267. 1964; FGD 3: 147. 1995; FRPS 52(1): 150. 1999.

Perennial herb, 90–150 cm tall. Stems erect, glabrous, usually unbranched. Leaves alternate; petioles slender, the lower ones up to 10 cm; leaf blade obliquely oblong, 11–27 × 3.5 –10 cm, apex acuminate, base cordate and strongly oblique, the outer basal lobe 1.5 –6 × 2.5–6 cm, the inner one orbicular, margin ± irregularly denticulate. Cymes axillary. Peduncles 9–11 mm. Pedicels ca. 10 mm. Flowers white; male flowers: perianth-segments 3, outer 2 broadly obovate or suborbicular, 9 –10 × 8 –9 mm, inner 2 slightly smaller, broadly orbicular; female flowers: perianth-segments 6, obovate, outer ones 14–16 × 8–9 mm, inner ones ca. 13 × 7 mm; ovary subglobose, 3-locular. Capsule subglobose, to 14 mm long, without wings.

Locality: Ma On Shan, Mui Tsz Lam, Tsz Mun Tin. HK sheet 34613; F. W. Xing 7242; Y. W. Lam 1699.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi.
Ecology: Thin forests by streams and wet places. Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: Jul.
Uses: Ornamental.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai, Ma On Shan, Pat Sin Leng, Sunset Peak, Lantau Peak
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Begonia palmata D. Don 裂葉秋海棠
Prodr. Fl. Nepal. 223. 1825; Hara, Fl. E. Himal. 215. 1966; FGD 3: 149, fig. 107. 1995.
Begonia laciniata Roxb., Fl. Ind. ed. 2, 3: 649. 1832; FHK 126. 1861; FKH 114. 1912.
Begonia palmata D. Don. var. bowringiana (Champ. ex Benth.) J. Golding & C. Kareg., Phytologia 54: 494. 1984; FRPS 52(1): 234. 1999.
Begonia bowringiana Champ. ex Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 4: 120. 1852.

Perennial herb, 15 – 60 cm tall, with horizontal rhizomes. Stems erect or decumbent at base, ± tawny tomentose. Leaves alternate; petioles usually shorter than leaf-blade, tawny tomentose; leaf blade obliquely ovate, 12–20 × 10 –15 cm, apex acuminate, base obliquely cordate, margin irregularly and shallowly 5 –7- lobed or coarsely toothed, adaxially strigose or with remaining small tubercles when the hairs falling off, abaxially pale green, tawny tomentose on veins. Cymes axillary or terminal. Peduncles 3 –12 mm, densely tawny tomentose. Flowers pink or white; male flowers: perianth-segments 4, outer 2 ovate-elliptic to oblong, 10 –25 × 7–11 mm, inner 2 smaller, elliptic to oblong; female flowers: perianth segments 5, oblong, subequal, 9–15 mm long; ovary 2-locular, puberulous. Capsule 10 –15 mm long, with 3 unequal wings.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai, Ma On Shan, Pat Sin Leng, Sunset Peak, Lantau Peak. Y. S. Lau 918; HK sheet 12233; H. C. Tang 1827.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Yunnan, Xizang, Hunan, Jiangxi; also in India, Nepal, Myanmar and Vietnam.
Ecology: Streamsides, margins of forests and other wet places. Flowering: Summer.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: The type specimen of Begonia bowringiana was collected from Hong Kong Island by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1850; Begonia circumlobata Hance reported from Lantau Island (FKH 114. 1912) was a misidentification of B. palmata.

Salix babylonica L. 垂柳
Sp. Pl. 1017. 1753; Schneid., Pl. Wils. 3: 42. 1916; FGZ 378. 1956; FRPS 20(2): 138. 1984.

Deciduous tree, to 10 m tall, with slender pendulous branches; young shoots slightly silky, soon glabrous. Leaves alternate; petioles (3–)5–10 mm; leaf blade lanceolate to linear-lanceolate, 8–16 × 0.5–1.5 cm, base cuneate, apex long-acuminate, margin serrulate, glabrous, adaxially dark green, abaxially greyish green. Catkins short-stalked: male 1.5–2(–3) cm, female 2–3(–5) cm; bracts scale-like, villous at base; ovary sessile or nearly so, glabrous; style very short; stigmas oblong, 2-lobed; gland about 1/3 as long as ovary.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 2942; S. P. Lau 105; HK sheet 26653.
Distribution: Widely distributed in Yellow River and Changjiang River basin.
Ecology: Usually planted in gardens, by streams, on banks of ponds. Flowering: Mar.–Apr.
Uses: Ornamental.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Wan Chai, Wong Chuk Hang, Shing Mun
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Cleome viscosa L. 黃花草（臭屎菜）
Sp. Pl. 672. 1753; FHN 1: 344. 1964; FGD 1: 81, fig. 86. 1987; FTW ed. 2, 2: 739, pl. 348, photo 329. 1996; FRPS 32: 537, pl. 135. 1999.
Polanisia viscosa DC., Prodr. 1: 242. 1824; FHK 17. 1861; FKH 35. 1912.

Annual herb, 30 –100 cm tall, covered with short glandular hairs and disagreeably scented. Leaves digitately compound; petioles (1–)2– 4 (– 6) cm; leaflets 3 –5(–7), subsessile, blade obovate to obovate-oblong, the middle one larger, 1–5 × 0.5 – 1.5 cm, margin entire, ciliate. Flowers solitary in axils of gradually reduced upper leaves, in appearance of a terminal raceme. Bract leafy, 3-lobed. Pedicels slender, 1–2 cm. Sepals narrowly elliptic to oblanceolate-elliptic, 6 –7 ×1–3 mm. Petals yellow, narrowly obovate or spathulate, 7–12 × 3 –5 mm, without claw. Stamens 10–22(–30), inserted on disc. Gynophore none. Ovary cylindrical, ca. 8 mm, with viscid glandular hairs; style very short. Capsule cylindrical, 4 –10 cm.

Locality: Wan Chai, Wong Chuk Hang, Shing Mun. Y. S. Lau 118; Y. W. Lam 1548; HK sheet 189.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; widely distributed in tropical and subtropical regions.
Ecology: Waste places. Flowering: Jul.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Tsuen Wan, Tai Mo Shan, Sha Tau Kok, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Capparis acutifolia Sweet 獨行千里（尖葉槌果藤）
Hort. Brit. (ed. 2) 585. 1830; FGD 1: 89, fig. 100. 1987; FTW ed. 2, 2: 735. photo 322. 1996; FRPS 32: 498. 1999.
Capparis membranacea Gardn. & Champ., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 1: 241. 1849; FHK 18. 1831; FKH 35. 1912.

Scandent shrub, glabrous, or sometimes with caducous yellowish short hairs on young shoots and petioles, with or without spines. Leaves membranous or slightly leathery; petioles 5–7 mm; leaf blade oblong-lanceolate or ovate-lanceolate, very variable in size, 4 –15(–19.5) × (0.8 –)1– 4(– 6.3) cm, base acute or cuneate, sometimes rounded, apex acuminate, glabrous, yellowish green when dry. Flowers white, solitary, borne a little above axils of leaves, often 2–4 together in a vertical row on flowering branches. Pedicels 1–1.5 cm. Sepals narrowly oblong, 5 –7 × 3 – 4 mm, outer ones glabrous, inner ones with caducous yellowish hairs when young. Petals oblong, ca. 1 × 0.3 cm. Stamens 20 –30. Gynophore 1.5 –2.5 cm, glabrous. Ovary ovoid or conical, glabrous. Fruit subglobose, 1–2.5 × 1–1.5 cm, usually with a short beak at apex.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tsuen Wan, Tai Mo Shan, Sha Tau Kok, Lantau Island. HK sheet 208, 212, 10395, 38797.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Flowering: Mar.–Jul.; fruiting: Aug.–Feb. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The type specimen of Capparis membranacea was collected from Victoria Peak by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1849.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Lantau Island, Cheung Chau, Po Toi
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Capparis cantoniensis Lour. 廣州槌果藤
Fl. Cochinch. 331. 1790; FGZ 107. 1956; Jacobs, Fl. Mal. 1. 6: 76. 1960; FHN 1: 349. 1964; FGD 1: 88, fig. 97. 1987; FRPS 32: 526. 1999.
Capparis pumila Champ. ex Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 3: 260. 1852; FHK 18. 1861; FKH 36. 1912.

Scandent shrub. Branches slender, with small recurved spines, glabrous or slightly pubescent on the upper part. Leaves subleathery; petiole 4– 6(–10) mm, pubescent; leaf blade oblongovate to oblong-lanceolate, 5 –10(–12) × 1.5– 4 cm, base broadly cuneate or obtuse, apex usually acuminate, glabrous. Panicles consisting of few-flowered umbels, terminal or axillary. Pedicels 4–10 mm, puberulent. Flowers white, ca. 1 cm in diam. Sepals 4–5 × 2.5 –3 mm, with white membranous margins. Petals obovate or oblong, 4–6 × 1.5–2.5 mm. Stamens 20–45; filaments 8–15 mm. Gynophore 6–8(–12) mm. Ovary ovoid or conical, glabrous. Fruit globose, 6 –10(–15) mm in diam., apex rounded, glabrous.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Lantau Island, Cheung Chau, Po Toi. K. Y. Tam s.n. (HK sheet 38775, 40219).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Fujian; S to SE Asia.
Ecology: Thin forests on slopes. Flowering: Mar.–Nov.; fruiting: Jun.–Mar. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The type specimen of Capparis pumila was collected from “the Black Mountain”, Hong Kong Island by J. G. Champion in January 1850.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Chuen Lung, Sheung Pak Nai. Naturalized
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Cleome burmannii Wight & Arn. 印度白花菜
Prodr. 1: 22. 1834; Hook. f. & Thoms., Fl. Brit. Ind. 1: 170. 1875.

Annual herb, 30 –65 cm tall. Stems, branches and pedicels glabrous, but sparsely pubescent when young. Leaves alternate, 3-foliate; petioles 1.5–3 cm; leaflets rhomboid-ovate, the middle one larger, 1.8 –3 × 0.7–1.4 cm, narrowed to both ends, tip blunt, lateral leaflets smaller, 1–2 × 0.5 –1 cm glabrescent or sparsely pubescent on abaxial veins, margin entire, ciliate. Flowers solitary in axils of leaves. Pedicels slender, ca. 2.5 cm. Sepals 4, lanceolate, ca. 2.5 mm. Petals 4, purplish red, oblanceolate, ca. 5 mm. Capsule 4– 6 cm, terete, tapering at both ends, glabrous.

Locality: Chuen Lung, Sheung Pak Nai. Naturalized. L. T. Lo 346; Y. W. Lam 376.
Distribution: India.
Ecology: Roadsides, wastelands. Flowering & fruiting: Summer to autumn.

Cleome rutidosperma DC. 皺子白花菜
Prodr. 1: 241. 1824; FTW ed. 2, 2: 739, pl. 347. 1996; FRPS 32: 539. 1999.

Annual herb, to 90 cm tall. Stems erect or decumbent, covered with viscid glandular hairs, but sometimes glabrescent. Leaves digitate-trifoliolate; petioles 2–20 mm, glandular hairy; leaflets subsessile; leaf blade elliptic lanceolate, the middle one larger, 1–2.5 × 0.5 –1.2 cm, base cuneate, apex acute, acuminate, obtuse or rounded, glandular hairy on veins abaxially. Flowers solitary in axils of upper leaves, forming interrupted leafy racemes. Pedicels slender, 1–2 cm, lengthening to 3 cm in fruit. Sepals 4, green, lanceolate, ca. 4 mm. Petals 4, oblanceolate-elliptic, ca. 6 × 2 mm, base narrowed into a short claw. Stamens 6; filaments 5 –7 mm. Gynophore 1.5 –2 mm. Ovary cylindrical, glabrous; style very short; stigma capitate. Capsule cylindrical, 3.5– 6 cm.

Locality: Cultivated. S. Y. Hu & P. P. H. But 22192, 22155 (CUHK).
Distribution: Yunnan, Taiwan; native to tropical Africa, naturalized elsewhere in tropics.
Ecology: Wastelands, farmlands, roadsides. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Sep.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Pat Sin Leng, Ng Tung Chai, also cultivated
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Crateva trifoliata (Roxb.) B. S. Sun 鈍葉魚木
FRPS 32: 489. 1999.
Capparis trifoliata Roxb., Fl. Ind. ed. Carey 2: 571. 1832.
Crateva adansonii subsp. trifoliata (Roxb.) Jacobs, Blumea 12(2): 199. 1964.
Crateva erythrocarpa Gagn., Bull. Soc. Bot. France 55: 322. 1908; FHN 1: 345. 1964.

Deciduous tree or shrub, 1.5 –30 m tall. Branches greyish brown, with leaf-scars. Leaves digitately ternate; petioles 4.5 – 12 cm, canaliculated. Leaflets papery; petiolules 3–10 mm; blade ovate, elliptic or ovate-lanceolae, 7–12 × 3 –5 cm, base cuneate, apex acute or acuminate, rarely obtuse, lateral ones inaequilateral, glabrous; lateral veins usually 5 –7 on each side of midvein. Corymbs lateral or terminal. Pedicels 4– 6 cm. Sepals 3–5 × 2–3 mm, orange red when dry. Petals initially white, later turning pale yellow, ovate or oblong, 1–2 × 1–1.3 cm; claw 4 – 8 mm. Stamens 15–26, purple, unequal. Gynophore 1.5 – 4.5 cm. Ovary ellipsoid; stigma sessile. Fruit globose, ca. 4 cm in diam., smooth, red when mature.

Locality: Pat Sin Leng, Ng Tung Chai, also cultivated. L. T. Lo 281; F. W. Xing 8162; HK sheet 40177.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; Vietnam, Myanmar, India, Malaysia.
Ecology: Flowering: Mar.–May; fruiting: Aug.–Nov.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: This species was reported as Crateva religiosa G. Forst. previously (Check List HK Plants 41. 1993).

Crateva unilocularis Buch.-Ham. 樹頭菜
Trans. Linn. Soc. 15: 121. 1827; FGD 1: 83, fig. 90. 1987; FRPS 32: 486, pl. 123. 1999.
Crateva religiosa auct. non Forst. f.: FKH 36. 1912; FGZ 108, fig. 40. 1956; FHN 1: 346, fig. 175. 1964.

Deciduous tree, 4–6(–15) m tall. Leaves digitately ternate; petioles 4–12 cm, with glands at apex. Leaflets thinly leathery; petiolules 5 –10 mm; blade ovate or elliptic, (4–)7–18 × (2.5–)3–8 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate or acute, lateral ones inaequilateral, glabrous, adaxially ± shining, abaxially greyish; lateral veins usually 8 –11 on each side of midvein. Corymbs terminal. Pedicels 3 –7 cm. Sepals lanceolate, 3 –7 × 2–3 mm. Petals white or pale yellow; petal-blade ovate or oblong, 1–3.5 × 0.5 –2.5 cm; claw 0.7–1 cm. Stamens 13 –30. Gynophore 4 – 7 cm. Ovary ovoid, 3 – 4 mm; stigma capitate, subsessile. Fruit subglobose, 2.5– 4 cm in diam., initially smooth, with yellow or cream tubercles when mature.

Locality: Cultivated. L. T. Lo 486; H. C. Tang 131.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Yunnan; tropical Asia and Australia.
Ecology: Flowering: Spring; fruiting: Summer to autumn.
Uses: Ornamental.

Cleome gynandra L. 白花菜
Sp. Pl. 2: 671. 1753; FHN 1: 344, fig. 174. 1964; FTW ed. 2, 2: 739, pl. 346. 1996; FRPS 32: 533. 1999; FGD 1: 82, fig. 88. 1987.

Annual herb, ca. 1 m tall. Stems erect; young branches, petioles and inflorescence ± with glandular hairs. Leaves digitately compound; petioles 2–6 cm; leaflets 3–7, sessile or nearly so, blade obovate-elliptic to oblanceolate, the middle one larger, 1–5 × 0.8 –1.6 cm, apex acute, obtuse or rounded, base cuneate, margin serrulate, glabrescent on both surfaces. Racemes terminal, 15 –30 cm. Bract leafy, 3- lobed. Pedicels 1–2 cm, hairy. Sepals lanceolate, elliptic or ovate, 3 – 6 × 1–2 mm. Petals white, suborbicular or broadly obovate, 6–12 × 2– 6 mm , claw ca. 5 mm. Stamens 6, exserted. Androgynophore 5 –18(–22) mm. Ovary cylindrical, with viscid glandular hairs; style very short. Capsule cylindrical, 4– 8 cm.

Locality: Cheung Chau. Exotic. Y. W. Lam 1550; HK sheet 204.
Distribution: Widely distributed from Hainan northwards to Hebei, and from Yunnan eastwards to Taiwan; widely distributed in tropical and subtropical regions.
Ecology: Roadsides, wastelands near villages. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.– Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Cleome hassleriana Chodat 醉蝶花
Bull. Herb. Boissier 6 (App. I): 12. 1898.
Cleome spinosa auct. non Jacq.: FGZ 109, fig. 41. 1956; FGD 1: 82, fig. 87. 1987; FRPS 32: 534. 1999.

Annual herb, 1–1.5 m tall, disagreeably scented. Stems erect, with glandular hairs and spiny stipules. Leaves digitately compound; petioles 2– 8 cm, often with yellowish prickles; leaflets 5 –7, elliptic-lanceolate or oblanceolate, the middle one larger, 6 –10 × 1–2.5 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate or acute, hairy on both surfaces. Racemes terminal, to 40 cm, densely covered with viscid glandular hairs. Bract leafy, ovate-oblong, 5 –20 mm, sessile or nearly so, base ± cordate. Pedicels 2–3 cm, with short glandular hairs. Sepals 4, oblongelliptic, ca. 6 mm. Petals pink or white, oblanceolate-spathulate,10 –15 × 4– 6 mm; claw 5–12 mm. Stamens 6; filaments 3.5– 4 cm. Gynophore 4 –5 cm. Ovary cylindrical, 3 – 4 mm, glabrous; style very short. Capsule cylindrical, 5– 6.5 cm.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. W. Lam 1752.
Distribution: Native to tropical America; widely cultivated.
Ecology: Flowering and fruiting: Mar.–Aug.
Uses: Ornamental.

Brassica juncea (L.) Czern. 芥菜
Conspect. Fl. Chark 8. 1859; FGD 3: 30. 1995; FOC 8: 20. 2001.
Brassica juncea var. crispifolia L. H. Bailey, Gentes Herb.1:：91. 1891; FGD 3: 30. 1995.
Brassica juncea var. foliosa L. H. Bailey, Gentes Herb. 2: 263. 1930; FGD 3: 30. 1995.

Annual herbs, 30–150 cm tall, glaucous, with pungent smell. Basal leaves broad-ovate to obovate, 15–20 cm, lyrate, lateral lobes 2–3 pairs, margin incised or dentate. Petioles 3–9 cm, with small lobes; cauline leaves smaller, not amplexicaul. Racemes terminal. Flowers yellow, 7–10 mm in diam.; pedicles 4–10 mm. Sepals oblong-elliptic, 4–5 mm. Petals obovate, 8–10 mm, claw 4–5 mm. Siliques linear, 3 –5.5 cm, beak 6–12 mm, slightly constricted between seeds; stalk 15–25 mm. Seeds purple-brown, globose, ca. 1 mm in diam.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 183.
Distribution: Widely cultivated.
Uses: Vegetable, spice, medicinal (seed).

Brassica oleracea L. 葉甘藍
Sp. Pl. 2: 667. 1753; FOC 8: 17. 2001.

Biennial or perennial herb, rarely annual, 0.6–1.5 m tall, glabrous, glaucous. Stems erect or decumbent, branched at or above middle, sometimes fleshy at base. Basal and lowermost cauline leaves long petiolate, sometimes strongly overlapping and forming a head; petiole to 30 cm; leaf blade ovate, oblong or lanceolate, to 40 × 15 cm, margin entire, repand or dentate, sometimes pinnatifid or pinnatisect and with a large terminal lobe and smaller, 1–13, oblong or ovate, lateral lobes on each side of midvein; upper cauline leaves sessile or subsessile, oblanceolate, ovate or oblong, to 10 × 4 cm, base amplexicaul, auriculate or rarely cuneate, margin entire, repand, or rarely dentate. Racemes sometimes fleshy and condensed into a head. Sepals oblong, 0.8 –1.5 cm, erect. Petals creamy yellow or rarely white, ovate or elliptic, 1.8 –2.5 cm, claw 0.7–1.5 cm. Siliques linear, 3–9 × 3–5 mm, terete, 10–20-seeded per locule, valves with a prominent midrib. Seeds dark brown or blackish, globose, 1.5 –2.5 mm in diam., minutely reticulate.

Wild populations of var. oleracea are known only from the coastal cliffs of W Europe; five varieties are cultivated in Hong Kong for vegetable.

Brassica oleracea L. var. albiflora Kuntze 芥蘭
Revis. Gen. Pl. 1: 19. 1891; FOC 8: 18. 2001.
Brassica alboglabra L. H. Bailey, Gentes Herb. 1: 79. 1922; FGD 3: 27. 1995.

Stems 30–40 cm tall, not fleshy, narrowly cylindric. Basal and lower cauline leaves green, few to several, widely spaced, not grouped into a head, ovate, 6–10 cm, base auriculate, decurrent, margin sinuate or irregularly serrulate. Inflorescence lax, not fleshy. Flowers white or rarely creamy white.

Locality: Cultivated.
Distribution: Widely cultivated.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr.
Uses: Vegetable.

Brassica oleracea L. var. botrytis L. 椰菜花
Sp. Pl. 667. 1753; FGD 3: 26. 1995; FOC 8: 18. 2001.

Stems 60–90 cm tall, glaucous, base elongated, not fleshy. Basal and lower cauline leaves green, few to several, widely spaced, not group into a head. Inflorescence fleshy, forming a compact globose head. Flower buds, pedicels, rachis and peduncles white.

Locality: Cultivated.
Distribution: Widely cultivated.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr.
Uses: Vegetable.

Brassica oleracea L. var. capitata L. 椰菜（甘藍）
Sp. Pl. 667. 1753; FGD 3: 26. 1995; FOC 8: 18. 2001.

Stems highly shortened, not fleshy, conical. Basal and lower cauline leaves green, many, oblong-obovate to orbicular, overlapped layer upon layer forming a globose or compressed-globose head, 20 – 40 cm in diam.

Locality: Cultivated.
Distribution: Widely cultivated.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr.
Uses: Vegetable.

Brassica oleracea L. var. gongylodes L. 芥蘭頭
Sp. Pl. 667. 1753; FOC 8: 18. 2001.
Brassica caulorapa (DC.) Pasq., Catal. Ort. Bot. Nap. 17. 1867; FGD 3: 27. 1995.

Stems 30– 60 cm tall, base highly shortened, fleshy, globose. Basal leaves not overlapping into a head, broad-ovate to oblong, 13 –20 cm, margin irregularly dentate; cauline leaves oblong to linear-oblong, margin sinuate. Inflorescences neither fleshy nor condensed into a head.

Locality: Cultivated. Leung & Wong s.n. (CUHK).
Distribution: Widely cultivated.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr.
Uses: Vegetable.

Brassica oleracea L. var. italica Plenck 西蘭花
Icon. Pl. Medic. 6: 29. 1794; FOC 8: 18. 2001.

Different from the above variety by: inflorescence somewhat loose, usually obconical; flower buds, pedicels, rachis and peduncles green.

Locality: Cultivated.
Distribution: Widely cultivated.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr.
Uses: Vegetable.

Brassica chinensis L. 白菜（青菜）
Gent. Pl. 1: 19. 1755; FKH 34. 1912; FHN 1: 355. 1964; FGD 3: 29. 1995.
Brassica rapa var. chinensis (L.) Kitamura, Mem. Coll. Sci. Univ. Kyoto, ser. B, 19: 79. 1950; FOC 8: 20. 2001, p.p.

Annual or biennial herb, 25–70 cm tall, glabrous. Basal leaves obovate, oblong or broad-ovate, 20 –30 cm, spreading, blades glabrous, entire or repand. Petioles green or white, 3 –5 cm, fleshy or thickened, wingless, base amplexicaul or not. Racemes terminal. Flowers yellowish, ca. 9 mm. Sepals oblong, 3 – 4 mm. Petals oblong, ca. 5 mm, base broad-clawed, apex obtuse. Siliques linear, 2–6 cm, beak 8–12 mm; stalk up to 3 cm. Seeds purple-brown, globose, 1–1.5 mm in diam.

Locality: Cultivated. W. J. Tutcher 9121; S. T. Dunn 1078.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; native to Asia.
Ecology: Farmlands, on wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–May.
Uses: Vegetable.

Brassica pekinensis (Lour.) Rupr. 大白菜（黃牙白）
Fl. Ingr. 96. 1860; L. H. Bailey, Gentes Herb. 1: 97, fig. 43. 1922; FHN 1: 355. 1964; FGD 3: 29. 1995.
Brassica rapa var. glabra Regel, Gartenflora 9: 9. 1860; FOC 8: 20. 2001.

Biennial herb, 40 – 60 cm tall. Basal leaves many and large, thin, obovate-oblong or broad-ovate, margin sinuate. Petioles complanate, 5 –10 × 8 cm, margin crisped, thin, wing-like; cauline leaves amplexicaul, entire or serrate. Flowers light yellow, 1.2–1.5 cm in diam.; pedicles 4 – 6 mm. Sepals oblong or ovatelanceolate, 4 –5 mm. Petals obovate, 7– 8 mm, base clawed. Siliques 3 – 6 cm × 3 mm, compressed, beak 4 –10 mm. Seeds brown, globose, 1–1.5 mm in diam.

Locality: Cultivated.
Distribution: Widely cultivated; native to N China.
Ecology: Flowering: May.
Uses: Vegetable.

Brassica parachinensis L. H. Bailey 菜心
Gentes Herb. 1: 102. 1922; FGD 3: 29. 1995.
Brassica rapa var. chinensis auct. non (L.) Kitamura: FOC 8: 20. 2001, p.p.

The differences between the above species and this species are the base of basal leaves of this species not amplexicaul and petioles slender and sulcate.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 3074.
Distribution: Widely cultivated.
Uses: Vegetable.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Aberdeen, Victoria Peak, Sai Kung, Ng Tung Chai, Wun Yiu
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Capsella bursa-pastoris (L.) Medik. 薺菜
Pfl.-Gatt. 85. 1792; FHK 16. 1861; FKH 35. 1912; FGD 3: 34. 1995; FOC 8: 43. 2001.
Thlaspi bursa-pastoris L., Sp. Pl. 2: 647. 1753.

Annual or biennial herb, 10–15 cm tall, glabrous or with simple or furcate hairs. Stems erect, simple or branched. Basal leaves rosulate, lyrate, up to 12 cm, terminal lobes ovate to oblong, lateral lobes 3–8 pairs. Petioles 5–40 mm; cauline leaves narrowly lanceolate or lanceolate up to 6 cm, base auriculate, amplexicaul. Racemes terminal and axillary, up to 20 cm; pedicel 3 – 8 mm. Flowers white, 2.5 mm. Sepals oblong, 1.5–2 mm. Petals ovate, 2–3 mm, shortly clawed. Silicles obtriangular or obcordate-triangular, 5 – 8 mm, flat, apex emarginate, stalk 5–15 mm. Seeds 2-ranked, brownish, oblong, 1 mm.

Locality: Aberdeen, Victoria Peak, Sai Kung, Ng Tung Chai, Wun Yiu. P. S. Choi 115; Y. S. Lau 81, 1752.
Distribution: Widely distributed in temperate regions.
Ecology: Farmlands. Flowering & fruiting: Jan.–Mar.
Uses: Vegetable, medicinal.

Cardamine flexuosa With. 彎曲碎米薺
Arr. Brit. Pl. (ed. 3) 3: 578. 1796; FGD 3: 38. 1995; FOC 8: 105. 2001.
Cardamine hirsuta auct. non L.: FHK 16. 1861; FKH 34. 1912.

Annual or biennial herb, ca. 30 cm tall, sparsely pubescent. Stems erect, ascending or decumbent branched from base, usually flexuous. Leaves pinnately compound; basal leaves not rosulate; leaflets 3 –7 pairs, ovate, obovate or oblong, 2–5 mm, petiolulate; cauline ones 3–5 pairs, ovate or linear, entire or 1–3-lobed. Racemes terminal; rachis flexuous; pedicles 2–4 mm. Sepals oblong, 1.5– 2.5 mm. Petals white, spathulate, ca. 3.5 mm. Stamens 6, rarely 4. Ovary 18–40-ovuled. Siliques linear, 1.2–2 cm, flat. Seeds brown, oblong, 1 mm, flat, apex narrowly margined or not.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. L. T. Lo 532; S. P. Lau 26; Y. S. Lau 2095.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian (cultivated); Sri Lanka, India, Malaysia, Vietnam, Philippines.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr.–May.
Uses: Medicinal.

Coronopus didymus (L.) J. E. Smith 臭薺
Fl. Brit. 2: 691. 1804; FGD 3: 33. 1995; FOC 8: 34. 2001.
Lepidium didymus L. , Syst. Nat. (ed. 12) 2: 433. 1767.
Senebiera pinnatifida DC., Mem. Soc. Hist. Nat. Paris 7: 144, pl. 9. 1799; FKH 35. 1912.

Annual or biennial herb, with foul smell, 10–50 cm tall. Stems usually prostrate, several tufted, branched above. Petioles 5–8 mm; leaves pinnatisect or bipinnatisect, lateral lobes 2–7 on each side or rachis, variable in size, linear or narrow-oblong, 4 – 8 mm, glabrous on both surfaces; cauline leaves similar to basal ones, progressively smaller and less divided upward. Racemes terminal or lateral and leaf-opposed. Flowers 1 mm in diam. Sepals ovate, 0.5–0.7 mm. Petals white, elliptic to linear, 0.4–0.5 mm. Stamens often 2, rarely 4, filaments white, dilated at base, anthers ovoid. Silicles 1.5 × 2–2.5 mm, didymous, compressed, emarginate at both ends; valves semiorbicular, prominately reticulate or rugose. Seeds red-brown, reniform, ca. 1 mm, finely reticulate.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Tai Hang, Shatin. Y. S. Lau 2100, 1785; W. J. Tutcher 6763.
Distribution: Guangdong, Fujian, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Taiwan, Shandong, Hubei, Sichuan, Yunnan; Europe, N America, Asia.
Ecology: Roadsides, valleys. Flowering: Mar; fruiting: Apr.

Lepidium virginicum L. 北美獨行菜
Sp. Pl. 2: 645. 1753; FGD 3: 32. 1995; FOC 8: 32. 2001.
Lepidium ruderale auct. non L.: FKH 35. 1912.
