Annual or biennial herb, 10 –25 cm tall. Stems erect, with clavate glandular hairs. Petioles 1–1.5 cm; basal leaves oblanceolate, 1–5 cm, pinnatifid; lobes apex acute, margin serrate or dentate, adpressedly pubescent on both surfaces; cauline leaves shortly petiolate, oblanceolate or linear, 1.5 –5.5 cm × 5 –10 mm, apex acute, margin serrate or entire. Racemes terminal. Sepals elliptic, ca. 1 mm. Petals white, spathulate, 1–1.2 mm, rarely rudimentary. Stamens 2 or 4. Silicles orbicular, 2–3 mm, narrowly winged apically, apex emarginate. Seeds reddish brown, ovate, ca, 2 mm, narrowly winged, cotyledons accumbent.

Locality: Lantau Island. HK sheet 35619, 38871, 40207.
Distribution: Anhui, Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hebei, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangsu, Jiangxi, Liaoning, Shandong, Sichuan, Taiwan, Yunnan; Bhutan, India, Japan, Pakistan, Russia; native to N America; introduced elsewhere.
Ecology: Fields, roadsides, waste places, grassy areas. Flowering: May–Jul.; fruiting: May–Sep.
Notes: This species was reported as Lepidium apetalum Willd. previously (Check List HK Plants 111. 2002).

Nasturtium officinale R. Br. 西洋菜
Hort. Kew. 4: 110. 1812; FGD 3: 40 1995; FOC 8: 136. 2001.
Rorippa nasturtium-aquaticum (L.) Hayek, Sched. Fl. Stir. Exs. 22. 1905.
Sisymbrium nasturtium-aquaticum L., Sp. Pl. 657. 1753.

Perennial herb, 20 – 40 cm tall, glabrous. Stems decumbent or prostrate on water surface, many branched, rooting at nodes. Leaves all cauline, pinnately compound, 3–9-foliolate, leaflets sessile, ovate, oblong or suborbiculate, 2–3 cm, base obtuse or subcordate, margin subentire or repand. Racemes terminal. Sepals oblong, 2–3 mm, lateral pair slightly saccate. Petals white or pink, obovate or spathulate, 3–4 mm, claw slender. Stamens 6. Siliques cylindric, 0.5 –2 cm. Seeds biseriate, reddish brown, ovoid, ca. 1 mm.

Locality: Cultivated.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Sichuan, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Hebei, Shanxi, Shandong, Henan, Anhui, Jiangsu, Shaanxi, Heilongjiang.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr.–May.
Uses: Vegetable, medicinal.

Raphanus sativus L. 蘿蔔
Sp. Pl. 669. 1753; FHK 17. 1861; FHN 1: 356. 1964; FGD 3: 31. 1995; FOC 8: 25. 2001.

Annual or biennial herb, up to 1 m tall; roots fleshy, white or purple, globose or oblong. Stems erect. Basal leaves petiolate, oblong to oblanceolate, 8 –30 cm, lyrate or pinnatisect, lateral lobes 4 – 6 on each side of midrib, oblong or ovate, 10 × 5 cm; upper cauline leaves often narrow and entire. Racemes terminal and axillary; pedicels 5 –15 mm. Sepals oblong, 5 –7 mm. Petals white or pink, often with dark veins, obovate, 1–1.5 cm, claw ca. 5 mm. Siliques cylindric, 3 – 6 cm, constricted between seeds, separated by a pithy substance filling the pods. Seeds red-brown, ovoid, ca. 3 mm in diam.

Locality: Cultivated. S. P. Lau 20; J. L. Sample 7; C. O. Levine 3272.
Distribution: Widely cultivated.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: May–Jun.
Uses: Vegetable.

Rorippa cantoniensis (Lour.) Ohwi 廣州蔊菜（微子蔊菜）
Acta Phytotax. Geobot. 6: 55. 1937; FGD 3: 39. 1995; FOC 8: 134. 2001.
Ricotia cantoniensis Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 2: 482. 1793.
Nasturtium microspermum DC., Syst. Nat. 2: 199. 1821; FKH 34. 1912.

Annual or biennial herb, 10 –30 cm tall, glabrous. Stems erect or decumbent. Basal leaves petiolate, rosulate, lyrate or pinnatisect, 4 –7 cm, lateral lobes 4 – 6 on both sides of midveins, margin 2–3-dentate; cauline leaves gradually becoming smaller upwards, sessile, base auriculate, obovate-oblong or spathulate, 1.5–5 cm, margin dentate or entire. Racemes terminal, bracteate. Sepals broadly lanceolate, 0.5 –2 mm. Petals yellow, obovate or narrowly spathulate, 2–3 mm. Siliques cylindric, 6 – 8 × 2 mm, dehiscent. Seeds many, reddish brown, ovate or ovate-reniform, 0.4 –0.6 mm, foveolate.

Locality: Sheung Shui. Y. S. Lau 2954; A. Lao 1123.
Distribution: Liaoning, Hebei, Shandong, Henan, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan, Hubei, Hunan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Shaanxi, Sichuan, Yunnan; Korea, Russia, Vietnam, Japan.
Ecology: Farmlands, on wet places. Flowering: Mar.–Apr.

Rorippa dubia (Pers.) Hara 無瓣蔊菜
J. Jap. Bot. 30: 196. 1955; FGD 3: 39. 1995; FOC 8: 133. 2001.
Sisymbrium dubium Pers., Syn. Pl. 2: 199. 1807.

Annual herb, 10 –30 cm tall, glabrous. Stems erect or decumbent. Basal and lower cauline leaves usually lyratepinnatipartite, 3 – 8 cm, lateral lobes 2–4 on each side of midveins, margin sinuate-serrate; uppermost leaves usually sessile, lanceolate or oblong, margin entire or serrulate. Racemes terminal or lateral, ebracteate. Sepals often pinkish, lanceolate or linear, ca. 3 mm, margin membranous. Petals mostly absent, rarely present and linear or narrowly oblanceolate, often shorter than sepals. Siliques linear, 2–3.5 cm × 1 mm, dehiscent. Seeds uniserrate, brown, ovoid, 0.5 –0.8 mm, foveolate.

Locality: Hong Kong Island. HK sheet 180, 32234.
Distribution: Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Jiangxi, Fujian, Hebei, Hunan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Shaanxi, Gansu, Sichuan, Yunnan, Xizang; Japan, Philippines, Indonesia, India, United States.
Ecology: Farmlands, on wet places. Flowering: May–Jul.; fruiting: Jun.–Aug.
Uses: Medicinal (whole plant).

Rorippa indica (L.) Hiern 蔊菜（塘葛菜）
Cat. Afr. Pl. 1: 26. 1896; FHN 1: 355. 1987; FGD 3: 38. 1995; FOC 8: 133. 2001.
Sisymbrium indicum L., Sp. Pl. ed. 2, 2: 917. 1763.
Nasturtium montanum Wall. ex Hook. f. & Thoms., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 5: 139. 1861; FHK 16. 1861; FKH 34. 1912.
Cardamine lamontii Hance, Journ. Bot. 14: 363. 1876; FKH 34. 1912.

Annual or biennial herb, 20–40 cm tall, glabrous or rarely sparsely pubescent. Stems often branched. Basal and lower cauline leaves long-petiolate, often lyrate-pinnatipartite, 4–10 cm, lateral lobes absent or 1–5 on each side of midvein; upper cauline leaves broadly lanceolate or spathulate, margin serrulate. Racemes terminal and lateral, ebracteate. Flowers small, many. Sepals ovate-oblong, 3–4 mm. Petals yellow, spathulate, 3–4 mm, shortly clawed. Siliques linear-cylindric, 1–2 cm × 1–1.5 mm, dehiscing into 2 valves. Seeds reddish brown, ovate or ovate-orbicular, 0.5–0.9 mm, foveolate.

Locality: New Territories, Lantau Island. L. T. Lo 77; Y. S. Lau 1789, 281.
Distribution: Guangdong, Hunan, Sichuan, Yunnan, Xizang, Shandong, Henan, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan, Shaanxi, Gansu; Japan, Korea, Philippines, Indonesia, India.
Ecology: Farmlands, on wet places. Flowering: Apr.–May.
Uses: Medicinal (whole plant).
Notes: The type specimen of Cardamine lamontii was collected from Hong Kong Island by J. Lamont (in Herb. Hance No. 19355, BM) in September 1874.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Harlic Road, Wong Nai Chung, Beacon Hill, Kadoorie Farm & Botanic Garden, Pat Sin Leng, Wu Kau Tang, Sunset Peak
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Enkianthus quinqueflorus Lour. 吊鐘花
Fl. Cochinch. 1: 277, 1790; FHK 200. 1861; FKH 154. 1912; FRPS 57(3): 12, pl. 4: 1–2. 1991; FOC 14: 245. 2005.

Deciduous or semi-deciduous shrub or trees, 1–3(–10) m tall, glabrous throughout, with whorled branches. Leaves crowded at ends of branches; petiole 0.5–1.5 cm; leaf blade obovate-lanceolate to elliptic, rarely lanceolate, 5–12.5 × 1.8–4 cm, base cuneate to attenuate, apex acuminate or shortly to abruptly acuminate, margin entire, thick papery to leathery, shining adaxially, reticulation of veins raised and prominent on both surfaces. Inflorescence single and terminal, umbellate, 6–8(–16)-flowered, enclosed in imbricate, reddish scales in buds; scales ovate to pyriformis, glabrous, margins ciliated, apex obtuse with a blunt point, up to 9–16 × 6–8 mm. Pedicels 1–2 cm, usually curved and pointing downward. Calyx 5-lobed, reddish; lobes triangular ovate to triangular, 2–3 × 1.5–2 mm. Corolla broadly campanulate, ca. 1.2 cm in diam., depth ± equals to diam., pink, red, or white, shortly 5- lobed; tube broad; limb 0.8–1.2 cm in diam.; lobes triangular ovate, obtuse, about 1/3 length of corolla-tube, more or less recurved. Stamens 10, included; filaments puberulent; anther-cells tipped with awn-like appendages. Ovary glabrous or densely pubescent; style ca. 4 mm. Capsule ovoid, 5-angled, ca. 1.2 × 1.0 cm; stalk erect; seeds several to many.

Locality: Harlic Road, Wong Nai Chung, Beacon Hill, Kadoorie Farm & Botanic Garden, Pat Sin Leng, Wu Kau Tang, Sunset Peak. H. C. Tang 1860; Y. S. Lau 1754; S. Y. Hu 13593 (IBSC); F. W. Xing 6879 (HKU).
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Sichuan, Yunnan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Common in Hong Kong, occasionally abundant in open hillside shrublands, alt. 50–700 m. Flowering: Jan.–Mar.; fruiting: Sep.–Dec.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: Majority of individuals in Hong Kong are deciduous; emergence of young leaves occur after the older leaves fall, and the leafless period often coincides with flowering. However, a significant proportion of plants produce young leaves and even flowers before old leaves fall.

(Franch. ex F. B. Forbes & Hemsl.) Chun
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Lyonia ovalifolia (Wall.) Drude var. hebecarpa (Franch. ex Forb. & Hemsl.) W. Y. Chun 毛果珍珠花
Sunyatsenia 4: 253. 1940; FOC 14: 463. 2005
Pieris ovalifolia (Wall.) D. Don var. hebecarpa Franch. ex Forb. & Hemsl., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 26: 17. 1889.
Xolisma ovalifolia (Wall.) Rehd. var. hebecarpa (Franch. ex Forb. & Hemsl.) Metcalf, J. Arnold Arbor. 12(4): 275. 1931.

Shrub, deciduous or semi-deciduous, 1–2(–4) m tall. Branchlets, petioles, abaxial surface of leaves inflorescence puberulent. Buds narrowly ovoid, 4–7 × 3–4 mm, glabrous. Leaves papery; petioles 2–8 mm; leaf blade ovate, ovate-lanceolate to elliptic-lanceolate, 3–7.5 × 1.5–4 cm, base usually rounded, apex shortly acuminate, margin entire, adaxial surface glabrescent; midvein and secondary veins prominently raised on abaxial surface. Inflorescences racemose or paniculate, terminal or axillary, 5–7(–20) cm. Pedicel 2–5 mm, with 1–3 leafy bracts near base. Calyx 5-lobed; lobes ovate to triangular-lanceolate, ca. 1.4 × 1.2 mm. Corolla white, tubular or tubular-urceolate, 8–10 mm, shortly 5-lobed. Stamens 10; filaments with a pair of appendages near apex. Ovary ovoid, densely puberulent. Capsule subglobose, 3–5 mm in diam.

Locality: Ma On Shan. Y. S. Lau 1398; Y. W. Lam 1290; K. Y. Tam s.n. (HK sheet 38879).
Distribution: Anhui, Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hubei, Jiangsu, Jiangxi, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Yunnan, Zhejiang.
Ecology: Very rare locally, only several plants were found in shrublands at open exposed rocky cliffs, alt. ca. 450 m. Flowering: May; fruiting: Aug.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: Lyonia ovalifolia is a highly variable species with up to six varieties differs slightly in leaf shape and hair covers being distinguished in China. At least three of them (var. ovalifolia, var. hebecarpa, and var. lanceolata) have almost overlapping ranges and were recorded in Guangdong. Among them, var. hebecarpa only differs from the other two varieties in having pubescent, instead of glabrous, ovary and capsule. The typical variety (var. ovalifolia) is very variable and therefore needs further studies to ascertain the taxonomic status.

Pieris swinhoei Hemsl. 長萼馬醉木
J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 26: 17. 1889; FKH 154. 1912; FGD 1: 301, fig. 321. 1987; FRPS 57(3): 27, pl. 7: 9 –12. 1991; FOC 14: 461. 2005.

Shrub, evergreen, 1.2(–3) m tall. Branchlets slender, shortly pubescent. Leaves and spirally arranged, crowded towards the nodes of branches. Petiole 3–6 mm, shortly pubescent, ± swollen at the base; leaf blade leathery, narrow elliptic to oblong oblanceolate, 4.5–13 × 0.6–1.5 cm, base attenuate, ± decurrent, apex acute, often with a blunt to sharp point, margin serrulated above middle, glabrous to sparsely puberulent on both surfaces, lateral veins almost in right angle with the midvein. Inflorescences terminal, single to several, racemose or paniculate, erect, 10–15(–20) cm, shortly pubescent, 20–30-flowered. Pedicels 3–4(–7) mm, shortly pubescent. Calyx-lobes lanceolate 5–6 × 2–2.5 mm, thick papery, pubescent adaxially, puberulent abaxially. Corolla tubular-urceolate, 7–9 mm; lobes broadly triangular, 1–2 mm. Stamens 10; filaments ca. 3.5 mm, flat, geniculate at top, 5.5–7.5 mm; filaments puberulent at base. Ovary conical to subglobous, densely pubescent; style ca. 7.5 mm, glabrous, base sunken into apex of ovary. Capsule ovoid, ca. 5 mm in diam.

Localities: Shing Mun. HK sheet 16851; IBSC sheet 53317.
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong.
Ecology: Flowering: Mar.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: The above cited specimens are probably duplicates of a single collection from Shing Mun in 1931. The author has not yet noticed this species in the wild.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Victoria Peak, Ma On Shan, Lantau Island (Tai O)
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Rhododendron championiae Hook. f. 毛葉杜鵑
Bot. Mag. 77: t. 4609. 1851; FHK 200. 1861; FKH 155. 1912; P. C. Tam, Survey of Genus Rhododendron in S. China 72, pl. 9. 1983; W. R. Phillipson & M. N. Phillipson, Not. Bot. Gard. Edinb. 44(1): 9. 1986; FRPS 57(2): 365, pl. 121: 5–10. 1994; FOC 14: 430. 2005.
Rhododendron subespitatum Chun ex P. C. Tam, Bull. Bot. Res., Harbin 2(4): 90, fig. 3. 1982.
Rhododendron championiae var. ovatifolium P. C. Tam., Survey of Genus Rhododendron in S. China 73, 112. 1983.

Shrub or small tree, evergreen, 1.5–3(–5) m tall, much branched. Young branches, petioles and pedicels densely covered with stiff, bristle-like glandular hairs up to 2.5 mm, hairs persistent on 2- or 3-year stem. Leaves crowded towards apex of branches; petiole 0.7–1.7 cm; leaf blade papery, elliptic to elliptic-ovate, 6.2–12.5(–17) × (1.6–)2.5–5 cm, base cuneate, apex acute to acuminate, margin entire, fringed with bristle-like hairs, adaxial surface dark green, more or less bullate, abaxial surface rather rusty-colored, both surfaces initially clothed with glandular hairs; reticulation of veins prominent. Flower buds borne in axils at stem apex, 1–3(–5) per stem, up to 5 × 2 cm; scales ovate to elliptical, up to 4.0 × 1.7 cm, apex acute, adaxial side often with sticky secretion, abaxial side weakly pubescent, margin ciliated. Inflorescence umbellate, 2–5(–7)-flowered. Pedicels 1–2.2 cm. Calyx 4 –5-lobed; lobes triangular to triangular-lanceolate, 1–5 × 1–1.5 mm, apex acute to obtuse, margin densely fringed with long hairs. Corolla funnel-shaped, 6–12 cm in diam., 4–6 cm deep, white to very pale pink, with yellow dots on posterior lobes; lobes spreading, elliptic to ovate; limb 6–12 cm in diam. Stamens 10, 4–4.5 cm, exserted; filaments pubescent on the lower half. Ovary oblong, 5–6-locular, densely hairy; style ca. 5 cm, protruding out of the corolla, glabrous. Capsule cylindrical, straight to strongly falcate, (1–)3–6 × 0.5–0.8 mm, covered with long hairs. Seeds many, elliptic, ca. 2.5 × 0.8 mm, with winged appendages on both ends.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Ma On Shan, Lantau Island (Tai O). H. C. Tang 1715; P. S. Choi 389; S. C. Ng 98 (HKU).
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang.
Ecology: Locally restricted in distribution, usually on exposed open hillsides. Large populations can be found on hillfire-maintained hillslopes near Tai O, alt. 50–500 m. Flowering: Mar.–May; fruiting: Oct.–Dec.
Uses: Ornamental (garden plants), medicinal (roots and stems).
Notes: This species was first described from Victoria Peak based on the type specimen collected by J. G. Champion in 1849 and was named after his wife. A distinctive species characterized by large flowers and long stiff hairs on all parts of the plants except the petals, otherwise it is morphologically similar to R. moulmainense, with the largest and the most fragrant flowers, often having a strong sweet scent, among the six native rhododendrons. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Victoria Peak, Ma On Shan, Pat Sin Leng, Sha Tau Kok, Castle Peak, Pok To Yan, Tai O
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Rhododendron farrerae Tate 華麗杜鵑
Brit. Fl. Garden ser. 2, 1: t. 95. 1831; FKH 155. 1912; P. C. Tam, Survey of Genus Rhododendron in S. China 28. 1983; D. F. Chamberlain & Rae, Not. Bot. Gard. Edinb. 47(2): 145. 1990; FRPS 57(2): 371. 1994; FOC 14: 433. 2005.
Azalea squamata Lindl., J. Hort. Soc. Lond. 1: 152. 1846 & Bot. Reg. t. 3. 1847; FHK 201. 1861.

Shrub, semi-deciduous, 1–1.5(–3) m tall, with false-verticillate branches. Young branches, leaves, petioles, pedicels and calyx densely clothed with tawny hairs up to 2 mm long. Leaves often crowded towards apex of branches to almost pseudo-verticillate; petiole 2.0–5.2 mm; leaf blade thick papery, ovate to rarely elliptic or obovate, 1.2–6.2 × 0.7–2.7 cm, base rounded to truncate, apex acute or obtuse, with a blunt point, margin entire, fringed with golden to dark brown hairs when young; adult leaves glabrous on both surfaces or with dark brown pilose hairs remaining along veins on abaxial side; reticulation of veins prominent. Flower buds borne in axils at stem apex, 1(–2) per stem, up to 9 × 5 mm; scales persistent until flower wilted, broad triangular to oblong-ovate, up to 5 × 8 mm, apex obtuse, abaxially covered in sericeous hairs, especially towards apex. Flowers usually solitary, rarely in pairs. Pedicels 2–5 mm, covered in tawny pilose hairs. Calyx small and inconspicuous; lobes broad triangular, 0.5 × 1.0 mm. Corolla funnel-shaped, 1.5–2.0 cm in diam., 2.5–3.5 cm deep; purplish pink, pink to pale pink, with magenta dots on posterior lobes; lobes round to elliptic-ovate. Stamens 8–10, 2.0–2.5 cm; filaments, glandular pubescent on lower portion. Ovary ovoid, 5-locular, ca. 3.5 × 1.8 mm, 5-locular, densely tawny pilose. Capsule ovoid, 5-celled, 6–10 × 5– 6 mm, densely strigose when young, stalk erect. Seeds many, ellipsoidal to barely crescent-shaped, ca. 1–1.5 × 0.4–0.6 mm.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Ma On Shan, Pat Sin Leng, Sha Tau Kok, Castle Peak, Pok To Yan, Tai O. W. J. Tutcher 8263, 11676; H. C. Tang 81.
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Jiangxi.
Ecology: Locally common, especially in hillfire-maintained shrublands and grasslands on ridges and cliffs, alt. 100–900 m. Flowering: Nov.–Apr.; fruiting: Oct. Dec.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: This species was first described from Hong Kong in 1846 as Azalea squamata, which is now considered one of the many synonyms of R. farrerae. It is distinctive among the six native rhododendrons in having deciduous flowering individuals and its leafless period usually coincides with flowering. Non-flowering individuals, however, often retain their older leaves until young leaves fully expand.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Happy Valley, Ma On Shan, Pat Sin Leng, Wong Lung Hang
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Rhododendron hongkongense Hutch. 香港杜鵑
Sp. Rhodod. 562. 1930; P. C. Tam, Survey of Genus Rhododendron in S. China 71. 1983; W. R. Phillipson & M. N. Phillipson, Not. Bot. Gard. Edinb. 44(1): 5–6. 1986; FRPS 57(2): 345. 1994; FOC 14: 424. 2005.
Azalea myrtifolia Champ., Bot. Mag. 77, sub pl. 4609. 1851, non Rhododendron myrtifolium Lodd. (1824), nec Schott & Kotschy (1851).
Azalea ovata auct. non Lindl.: FHK 201. 1861.
Rhododendron ovatum auct. non Maxim.: FKH 155. 1913.

Shrub or small tree, evergreen, 1–3(–7) m tall, much branched. Branchlets short glandular hairy when young. Leaves crowded towards apex of branches; petioles 0.5–1.4 cm, puberulent; leaf blade thin leathery to papery, rhombic-elliptic to oblanceolate, 3.2–7.6 × 1.4–3.0 cm, base cuneate, apex acute to retuse, with a blunt point, margin entire and slightly deflexed, glabrous on both surfaces, but pubescent along midvein. Flower buds borne in axils at stem apex, 1–2(–6) per stem, ca. 1.6 × 0.5 cm; scales ovate to elliptical, up to 1.5 × 0.9 cm, apex acute to round, with a sharp to blunt point, abaxially pubescent to rarely glabrous, margin ciliated. Inflorescence umbellate, 1(–2)-flowered. Pedicel 0.7–1.4 cm, glandular hairy. Calyx 5-lobed, glandular hairy at base; lobes ovate to broad elliptic, 3–5 × 3–4.5 mm, apex rounded, margin densely to sparsely glandular ciliate. Corolla sub-rotate, spreading with a shallow tube, 4.5–6 cm in diam., 1.5–2.0 cm deep, white to very pale pink or very pale magenta, rarely very pale green, with magenta (rarely green) dots on posterior lobes; tube very short ; limb 4.5–6 cm in diam. Stamens 5, filaments 2.0–2.5 cm, pubescent below middle. Ovary subglobose to broad ovoid, ca. 1.8 × 2.0 mm, densely glandular hairy; style 2.5–3.2 cm, glabrous. Capsule subglobose to broad ovoid, 5-locular, ca. 5 × 5 mm, tuberculate and sparsely glandular hairy. Seeds many, ellipsoidal to ovoid, multi-faceted, ca. 1 × 0.4 mm.

Locality: Happy Valley, Ma On Shan, Pat Sin Leng, Wong Lung Hang. H. C. Tang 493; Y. S. Lau 2684; Y. W. Lam 612; HK sheet 33103, 33104; S. C. Ng 85 (HKU).
Distribution: Guangdong, Jiangxi.
Ecology: Locally restricted in distribution. Populations could be found on rocky outcrops and steep hillside forests, or along streamsides, alt. 100–700 m. Flowering: Jan.–Apr.; fruiting: Oct.–Dec.
Uses: Ornamental (garden plants).
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Hong Kong Island by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1850. This species had been misidentified as “Azalea ovata” and “Rhododendron ovatum” in FHK and FKH respectively. Rhododendron hongkongense is morphologically very similar to R. ovatum and R. bachii H. Léveillé, both of which are widespread in S China and recorded in Guangdong and Jiangxi where R. hongkongense was also found. Differs from R. hongkongense, R. ovatum lacks glandular hairs on calyx margin whereas R. bachii bears ovate leaves and calyx lobes. Despite both R. ovatum and R. bachii showed variable flower colour ranging from purple to light pink, R. hongkongense is consistently paler and usually white. These characters are, however, variable within respective species. Specimens of R. hongkongense collected in Hong Kong showed that glandular hairs on sepal margin vary continuously from filling the whole length of the margin (e.g. Y. W. Lam 612 and HK sheet 33103) to complete absence or replacement by cilia (e.g. Y. S. Lau 2684 and HK sheet 33104). Further studies are, therefore, needed to ascertain the taxonomic status of R. hongkongense. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Ma On Shan, Wu Kau Tang, Pat Sin Leng, Lantau Peak
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Rhododendron moulmainense Hook. f. 羊角杜鵑
Bot. Mag. 82: t. 4909. 1856; P. C. Tam, Survey of Genus Rhododendron in S. China 78. 1983; W. R. Phillipson & M. N. Phillipson, Not. Bot. Gard. Edinb. 44(1): 13–14, pro parte. 1986; FRPS 57(2): 355, pl. 118: 1–5. 1994; FOC 14: 427. 2005.
Rhododendron westlandii Hemsl., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 26(173): 31–32. 1889; FKH 155. 1913.

Shrub or small tree, evergreen, 2–4(–10) m tall, much branched, glabrous throughout except filaments and rarely young leaf margin. Leaves crowded towards nodes of branches; petiole 1.0–1.5 cm, glabrous; leaf blade thick-papery to leathery, elliptic, elliptic-obovate, (5–)6.6–10.5(–14) × (1.5–)2.5–5.2 cm, margin entire or rarely ciliated when young, flat to slightly deflexed, base cuneate, apex acute to shortly and abruptly acuminate; midvein impressed adaxially, raised abaxially; secondary and fine veins inconspicuous on both surfaces. Flower buds borne in axils at stem apex, 1–2(–5) per stem, up to 4 × 2 cm; scales ovate to elliptical, up to 3.0 × 2.5 cm, apex acute, abaxial side glabrous, margin ciliated. Inflorescence umbellate, (2–)3–5(–7)-flowered. Pedicels 1–1.7 cm. Calyx small; lobes broad triangular to broad ovate, 0.5–1 × 1–1.5 mm, apex obtuse. Corolla funnel-shaped, 5–8 cm in diam., 3–4 cm deep, pink to pale pink lobes spreading, elliptic to elliptic-obovate. Stamens 10, 3.5–4 cm; filaments pubescent on the lower part. Ovary oblong, 5–6 mm, 5–6-locular; style 4–4.5 cm, protruding out of the corolla, glabrous. Capsule cylindrical, straight to strongly falcate, (2–)4–6 × 0.4–0.7 cm. Seeds many, ellipsoidal, 2.5–3.0 × 0.5–1.0 mm, with winged appendages on both ends.

Locality: Ma On Shan, Wu Kau Tang, Pat Sin Leng, Lantau Peak. A. B. Westland 1697; W. J. Tutcher 10609; H. C. Tang 492; S. C. Ng 88 (HKU).
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hunan, Jiangxi, Yunnan; Cambodia, Laos, Malaysia (Peninsular), Myanmar, Thailand, Vietnam.
Ecology: Locally restricted to steep hillside forests, alt. 300–900 m. Flowering: Jan.–Apr.; fruiting: Oct.–Dec.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: This species is morphologically variable throughout its range from S China to Indochina. It was described under various names [see FRPS and Phillipson & Phillipson (1986)], including R. westlandii, the type specimen of which was collected from Lantau Island by A. B. Westland in 1886. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Rhododendron mucronatum (Bl.) G. Don 白杜鵑
Gen. Syst. 3: 846. 1834; Sleumer, Fl. Males. Ser. I, 6(4): 662. 1967; P. C. Tam, Survey of Genus Rhododendron in S. China 39. 1983; D. F. Chamberlain & Rae, Not. Bot. Gard. Edinb. 47(2): 116–117. 1990; FRPS 57(2): 389, pl. 125: 1–5. 1994; FOC 14: 441. 2005.
Azalea mucronata Bl., Cat. Gewass. Buitenz. 44. 1823.

Shrub, evergreen, 1–2(–3) m tall, much branched. Young branches, petioles and pedicels densely covered with ± appressed long narrow triangular flat scale-like hairs and intermixed with glandular hairs and harsh hairs. Leaves alternate, spirally arranged, often crowded towards nodes of branches; petiole ca. 2 mm; leaf blade papery, elliptic, oblong lanceolate to oblong-obovate, deflexed, 1.5–4.7 × 0.7–1.5 cm, base cuneate, apex obtuse to acute and a blunt point, margin entire, fringed with long hairs, adaxial surface sparsely strigose, abaxial surface strigose and intermixed with short glandular hairs. Flower buds borne in axils at stem apex, 1(–several) per stem; scale of flower buds ovate to elliptic, 4–7 × 4–5 mm, apex obtuse, abaxially pilose and often with sticky secretion. Inflorescence umbellate, 1–2(–3)-flowered, with sticky secretion. Pedicels 5–10 mm. Calyx 5-lobed, glandular hairy at base; lobes 5, ovate to lanceolate, 6–8 × 2.5–3 mm, apex rounded to acute, margin glandular hairy. Corolla funnel-shaped, 3–5 cm in diam., 3–4 cm deep, white; lobes elliptic to broad obovate. Stamens 10; filaments glabrous to puberulent below middle. Ovary ovoid, 5-locular, densely strigose, style glabrous, 3–5 cm. Capsule not seen.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. Y. S. Lau 1455.
Distribution: Widely cultivated in China, Japan and introduced to Europe and America, but no wild population has been found.
Ecology: Flowering: Mar.–Apr.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: This species was probably originated from R. mucronatum var. ripense (Makino) Wilson which is native to Japan (Chamberlain & Rae, 1990).

Rhododendron pulchrum Sweet 錦繡杜鵑
Brit. Fl. Garden ser. 2, 2: t. 117. 1832; P. C. Tam, Survey of Genus Rhododendron in S. China 41, pl. 2. 1983; D. F. Chamberlain & Rae, Not. Bot. Gard. Edinb. 47(2): 141. 1990; FRPS 57(2): 384. 1994.

Shrub, evergreen, 1–2(–3) m tall. Young branches, petioles, leaf blade, pedicels and calyx covered with ± appressed, harsh long hairs and intermixed with short glandular hairs. Leaves alternate, spirally arranged, often crowded towards nodes of branches; petioles ca. 2 mm; leaf blade papery, elliptic to oblong-obovate or elliptic-lanceolate, 2.7– 6.1 × 0.9 –2.1 cm, base cuneate, apex obtuse or acute, with a blunt point, margin entire and slightly deflexed, fringed with long hairs, glabrescent adaxially when full-grown. Flower buds borne in axils at stem apex, 1(–several) per stem; scales elliptic to ovate, 7–18 × 6–12 mm, apex acute to short acuminate, basal scales occasionally with leafy extension at apex; abaxially shortly pubescent and glandular papillate. Inflorescence umbellate, 2–4(–5)-flowered. Pedicel 7–10 mm. Calyx 5-lobed; lobes ovate to lanceolate, 7–12 × 3–4 mm, covered in long hairs and shorter glandular hairs, apex rounded to acuminate, margin long hairy. Corolla funnel-shaped, 4–4.5 cm diam., 3–3.5 cm deep, pink to purple, with bright pink to dark purple dots on posterior lobes, 4 –7 cm in diam.; lobes elliptic to obovate. Stamens 10; filaments sparsely puberulent on the lower portion. Ovary ovoid, densely tawny strigose, style 3.5–5.0 cm, glabrous. Capsule not seen.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. Y. S. Lau 1453, 2467.
Distribution: Widely cultivated in China and worldwide, but no wild population has been found.
Ecology: Flowering: Mar.–May.
Uses: Ornamental (garden plants).
Notes: A putative hybrid of unknown parentage (Chamberlain & Rae, 1990), this species has long been cultivated in China and worldwide. A number of cultivars of different flower colour and slightly different vegetative morphology are available and at least two cultivars are present in Hong Kong.

Rhododendron simiarum Hance 南華杜鵑
J. Bot. 22(1): 22–23. 1884; FKH 155. 1913; D. F. Chamberlain, Not. Bot. Gard. Edinb. 39: 320, 1982; P. C. Tam, Survey of Genus Rhododendron in S. China 20, pl. II, 1983; FRPS 57(2): 157, pl. 48: 6 –10. 1994; FOC 14: 371. 2005.
Rhododendron fordii Hemsl., Kew Bull. Misc. Inform. 1894(85): 5. 1894; FKH 155. 1913.
Rhododendron fokiense Franch., Bull. Soc. Bot. France 46: 210. 1899; P. C. Tam, Survey of Genus Rhododendron in S. China 21, fig. 19. 1983.

Erect shrub or small tree, evergreen, 1–3(–5) m tall. Branchlets glabrescent. Leaves clustered towards stem apex; thick-leathery; petiole 1.2–2.5 cm, ± pubescent; leaf blade obovate, elliptic-obovate to elliptic, (3.2–)5.4 –9.5 × (1.0–)1.5–3.5 cm, base cuneate, apex subrounded, sometimes retuse, margin entire and usually strongly deflexed, glabrous and shiny adaxially, abaxial surface initially covered with grey or light tawny tangled hairs, forming a thin but compact and persistent light brown indumentum; midvein impressed adaxially, raised abaxially; lateral veins inconspicuous, reticulation of veins ± foveolate. Flower buds usually borne singly to very rarely in pair at stem apex, ca. 3.5 × 2.7 cm; scale fall off as flower opened, broad ovate to elliptical, up to 3.5 × 2.7 cm, apex obtuse to round, abaxially glabrous to sparsely pubescent, especially towards the apex and along the longitudinal axis, often with sticky secretion. Inflorescence an umbel-like raceme, 3–7- flowered; rachis 1–2.5 cm, glandular hairy. Pedicels 2.2–3.4 cm, glandular hairy. Calyx small, cup-shaped, inconspicuously 5-lobed, lobes round to broad triangular, 0.5–0.7 mm × 1.5–2.0 mm, apex round, glandular hairy. Corolla oblique-campanulate, 3.5–4.5 cm, pink to rosy red initially, soon turning white to pink, with yellow to pink dots on posterior petals, lobes round to broadly elliptic-ovate, 1.7–2.5 cm × 1.5–1.7 cm. Stamens 10–12, 3–4 cm, similar to or shorter than corolla; pubescent on the 1/3 section. Ovary covered with stellate hairs, sticky when fresh; style 3–5 cm, glandular hairy at lower half. Capsule ellipsoid to oblong-ellipsoidal, 1–3 × 0.5–1.2 cm, glabrous and often with sticky secretion. Seeds many, ellipsoidal to ovoid, 2–2.5 × 1–1.5 mm.

Locality: Ma On Shan, Lantau Peak. U. A. On s.n. (HK sheet 16955); C. Ford s.n. (HK Sheet 16954); Y. S. Lau 936; S. C. Ng 93 (HKU).
Distribution: Anhui, Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hainan, Hunan, Jiangxi, and Zhejiang.
Ecology: Locally restricted in distribution, specialized in shrubland habitats on rocky outcrops or cliffs and often in small rock crevices and surface, abundant and form dense populations wherever occur. Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: Nov.–Dec.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: This species shows considerable variation within its range. The specimens from outside Guangdong and Hong Kong often have glabrous stamens and acute leaf apexes (Chamberlain, 1982; M.Y. Fang 1994). The species is widespread in S China mainly on ridges and cliffs above 1000 m. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Victoria Peak, Mount Collinson, Kowloon Peak and Lion Rock, Ma On Shan, Tai Mo Shan, Sharp Island, Castle Peak, Pat Sin Leng, Sai Kung Peninsula, Lantau
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Rhododendron simsii Planch. 紅杜鵑
Fl. des Serres 9: 78. 1854; Sleumer, Fl. Males. Ser. I, 6(4): 665. 1967; P. C. Tam, Survey of Genus Rhododendron in S. China 28, pl. 1. 1983; FRPS 57(2): 386, pl. 124: 1–6. 1994; FOC 14: 440. 2005.
Azalea indica auct. non L.: Sims, Bot. Mag. 35: t. 1480. 1812; FHK 201. 1861.
Rhododendron indicum auct. non Sweet: FKH 155. 1912.

Ascending shrub, usually evergreen, 1–2(–3) m tall, much-branched. Branchlets, petioles, pedicels, calyx and ovary densely strigose with stiff appressed light brown triangular flat scale-like hairs. Leaves alternate, spirally arranged, often crowded towards nodes of branches; petiole 1.0–3.0 mm; leaf blade thick papery, elliptic to obovate, 1.5–5.5 × 1.0–2.2 cm, margin entire and flat, base cuneate, apex acute, obtuse, to round, with a blunt point, strigose on both surfaces, often becoming glabrous adaxially, but always retaining the hairs on abaxial surface, especially towards leaf base. Flower buds borne in axils at stem apex, 1(–several) per stem; scales ovate, 7–10 × 4–8 mm, apex acute to obtuse, basal scales occasionally with leafy extension at apex; abaxially covered in strigose hairs, especially towards apex and axis. Inflorescence 1–2(–3)-flowered. Pedicels 4–6 mm. Calyx 5-lobed; lobes elliptic ovate to triangular ovate, 2–2.6 × 3–4.7 mm, apex round, rarely acute, margin entire, fringed with narrow triangular scale-like hairs. Corolla funnel-shaped, 3.5–4.5 cm in diam., 3–3.5 cm deep, bright red, with dark red dots on posterior lobes; lobes elliptic to obovate. Stamens 10, 2.7–4.7 cm; filaments inclusive, sparsely pubescent below middle. Ovary ovoid, ca. 3.0 × 1.7 mm, 5-locular, densely strigose; style glabrous. Capsule ovoid to rarely ellipsoid, 7–9 × 3–5 mm, strigose. Seeds many, elliptic, 1.2–1.5 × 0.3–0.4 mm.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Mount Collinson, Kowloon Peak and Lion Rock, Ma On Shan, Tai Mo Shan, Sharp Island, Castle Peak, Pat Sin Leng, Sai Kung Peninsula, Lantau. H. C. Tang 1267; L. T. Lo 423.
Distribution: Anhui, Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangsu, Jiangxi, Sichuan, Taiwan, Yunnan; Japan, Laos, Myanmar, Thailand.
Ecology: Common in secondary shrubland on hillsides and along streams, alt. 50–980 m. Flowering: Dec.–May; fruiting: Oct.– Dec.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: Rhododendron simsii was first described by Sims in 1812 who mistook it as Azalea indica. It was not properly identified until 1854 by Planchon. As a result, this species was often mentioned as “R. indicum” or “A. indica” in 19th century literature as well as FHK and FKH. This wide-ranging species is probably the most common wild rhododendron in S China and also one of the most widely cultivated rhododendrons in E Asia.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Victoria Peak, Causeway Bay, Repulse Bay, Tai Tam, Mount Parker, Aberdeen, Stanley, Kadoorie Farm & Botanic Garden, Ng Tung Chai, Ma On Shan, Castle Peak, Pat Sin Leng, Lautau Peak
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Vaccinium bracteatum Thunb. var. chinense (Lodd.) W. Y. Chun ex Sleumer 小葉烏飯樹
Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 71: 474. 1941; FGD 1: 335. 1987; FRPS 57(3): 109. 1991; FOC 14: 488. 2005.
Andromeda chinensis Lodd., Bot. Cab. 17, t. 1648. 1830.
Vaccinium chinense (Lodd.) Champ. ex Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 4: 297. 1852; FHK 199. 1861.
Vaccinium bracteatum auct. non Thunb.: FKH 153. 1913, p.p.

Shrub or small tree, evergreen, 1.5–4(–9) m tall, much branched. Branchlets initially ± puberulent, becoming glabrous in age. Leaves alternate, firmly papery to thin leathery; petiole 2–5.5 mm, puberulous; leaf blade rhombic-elliptic to elliptic or lanceolate-elliptic, 1.1–4.5 × 0.5–2.5 cm, base cuneate or broadly cuneate, apex acuminate to acute-acuminate, rarely long acuminate, margin thickened, serrulate at least on the distal half, glabrous; midvein and secondary veins slightly raised on both surfaces. Inflorescences terminal or axillary, racemose, 2–4 cm, glabrous to puberulent. Bracts caducous or rarely persistent, leaf-like, elliptic to lanceolate, ca. 5 × 2 mm; bracteoles subulate, persistent. Pedicels 2.4–4.5 mm, pubescent to glabrous. Calyx pubescent, 5-lobed; lobes triangular, 0.9–1.1 × 0.9–1.1 mm, apex acute to acuminate. Corolla white, rarely reddish, tubular-urceolate, 4.0–6.3 × 2.1–3.2 mm, puberulent abaxially, shallowly 5-lobed; lobes reflexed, triangular. Stamens 10, included; filaments hairy; anther (theca and tubule) 2.5–3 mm; appendage very short and inconspicuous to absent; tubule 2–2.5 times as long as thecae. Style glabrous; ovary inferior, 5-locular, densely pubescent at least surrounding base of style. Berry globose, 6–7 mm in diam., puberulent to pubescent.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Causeway Bay, Repulse Bay, Tai Tam, Mount Parker, Aberdeen, Stanley, Kadoorie Farm & Botanic Garden, Ng Tung Chai, Ma On Shan, Castle Peak, Pat Sin Leng, Lautau Peak. Y. S. Lau 114, 198; S. L. Thrower 764 (HKU).
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi.
Ecology: Locally common in shrublands and young secondary forests on open hillsides, alt. 200–980 m. Flowering: Jun.–Aug.; fruiting: Aug.– Oct.
Notes: Vaccinium bracteatum is known to have edible fruits and its leaves and stems can also be used as herbal medicinal. However, there is no documented uses of var. chinense. This variety only differs from V. bracteatum var. bracteatum in leaf size and shape, although the latter also shown considerable variation. Specimens collected from Guangdong seemed to show a continuous range in leaf size and shape. More detailed studies are therefore needed to ascertain its taxonomic status. The type specimen of V. chinense was collected from Hong Kong Island by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1850.

Vaccinium iteophyllum Hance 黃背越橘
Ann. Sci. Nat., Bot., ser. 4, 18: 223. 1862; FGD 1: 333, fig. 367. 1987; FRPS 57(3): 122. 1991; FOC 14: 492. 2005.
Vaccinium iteophyllum Hance var. fragrans Rehd. & Wils., Pl. Wilson. 1(3): 558. 1913.

Shrub or small tree, evergreen, 1(–7) m tall. Young branches, petioles, inflorescence and calyx-tube pubescent with light brown to rusty hairs. Leaves spirally arranged, papery to thin leathery; petioles 1.5–3.0 mm; leaf blade ovate or ovate-lanceolate to lanceolate, 3.4–6 × 1.8–2.5 cm, apex acuminate, base cuneate to rounded, margin shallowly serrulate, turned yellow-brown when dry, glabrous, only with short hairs remained on midvein of abaxial surface. Inflorescence terminal or axillary, racemose, 1.5–4(–7) cm. Bracts and bracteoles caducous. Pedicel 2–2.5 mm. Calyx 5-lobed; lobes triangular, ca. 1 × 1 mm, apex acute to slightly acuminate. Corolla white or tinged with red blotches, tubular-urceolate, 7–8.5 × 2.5–3.5 mm, glabrous, shallowly 5-lobed; lobes reflexed, triangular. Stamens 10, filaments 2–2.5 mm, hairy; anthers (theca and tubule) 5.0 mm; appendage ca. 1.0 mm, present at the top of each theca cell; tubule ca. 4 times as long as theca. Ovary inferior, densely pubescent; style glabrous. Berry globose, ca. 6 mm in diam., purplish red when mature.

Localities: Ma On Shan. H. C. Tang 491.
Distribution: Anhui, Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangsu, Jiangxi, Sichuan, Xizang, Yunnan, Zhejiang.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr.
Notes: Previously unrecorded for Hong Kong. Only a single specimen collected from Ma On Shan in 1950 is known, which was previously misidentified as V. bracteatum. The author has not yet noticed this species in the wild.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Happy Valley, Wong Nai Chung, Lai Chi Wo
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Chrysophyllum lanceolatum (Blume) A. DC. var. stellatocarpon P. Royen 金葉樹
Blumea. 9: 32. 1958; FHN 3: 161, fig. 642. 1974; FRPS 60(1): 60, pl. 11: 3 – 4. 1987; FGD 2: 350. 1991; FOC 15: 208. 1996.
Chrysophyllum roxburghii auct. non G. Don: FKH 160. 1912.

Trees, 10 –20 m or taller. Branchlets yellow pubescent when young. Petioles shorter than 1 cm, glabrous or pubescent; leaf blade thinly leathery, oblong to oblong-lanceolate, slightly asymmetrical, 7–12 × 1.8–4 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate to caudate-cuspidate, glabrous on both surfaces, yellowish brown when dry; lateral veins many, closely spaced and slender. Flowers fascicled. Pedicels slender, 5 mm, rusty pubescent. Sepals 5, slightly pubescent abaxially, margin fimbriate. Corolla white, broadly campanulate, 1.8–3 mm, glabrous, 5-lobed; lobes as long as sepals, margin fimbriate. Stamens 5, filaments short. Ovary ca. 0.6 mm, 5-locular, 5-ridged, rusty tomentose. Style ca. 1.5 mm, glabrous. Berry subglobose, brown to purplish black, 5-ridged, 1.5 –2 cm in diam., rusty tomentose when young. Seeds often 5, obovoid, compressed laterally, 11–13 mm.

Locality: Happy Valley, Wong Nai Chung, Lai Chi Wo. HK sheet 3092; K. Y. Tam 121; Y. W. Lam 1898.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi; Indonesia, Sri Lanka, Indochina to Singapore.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: May; fruiting: Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (root & leaves), food (fruit).

Manilkara zapota (L.) P. Royen 人心果
Blumea 7: 410, fig. l–q. 1953; FHN 3: 160. 1974; FRPS 60(1): 50, pl. 9: 1–3. 1987; FFJ 4: 310. 1989; FGD 2: 351. 1991.
Achras zapota L., Sp. Pl. ed. 2. 1190, 1753; FGZ 469, fig. 257. 1956.
Sapota achras Mill., Gard. Dict. ed. 8. Sapota no. 1. 1768.

Tree, 6 –10 m, with milky juice. Branches brown, with conspicuous leaf scars. Petioles 2 cm; leaf blades oblong or ovate-elliptic, 6 –19 × 2.5 – 4 cm, thinly leathery, base cuneate, apex short-acuminate to obtuse, sometimes emarginate, margin sometimes undulate, glabrous on both surfaces; lateral veins many, nearly parallel, inconspicuous. Flowers usually solitary and axillary. Pedicels 2 cm or longer, yellowish brown-tomentose. Sepals ovate, 6 – 8 mm, rusty tomentose abaxially. Corolla white, 6 – 8 mm; lobes ovate, 3 –5 mm, irregularly dentate at apex. Staminodes petaloid, as wide as half of corolla lobes. Ovary densely brown-tomentose. Berry ovoid or ovoid-ellipsoid, 4 – 8 cm, brown.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 17906; Y. S. Lau 2721.
Distribution: Fujian, Taiwan, Hainan, Guangxi, Guangdong, Yunnan (cultivated); native to C America.
Ecology: Flowering: Summer; fruiting: Autumn.
Uses: Food (fruit).

Sarcosperma laurinum (Benth.) Hook. f. 肉實樹
Gen. Pl. 2: 655. 1876; FKH 161. 1912; FHN 3: 163. 1974; FRPS 60(1): 83. 1987; FFJ 4: 314. 1989; FGD 2: 358, fig. 224. 1991; FOC 15: 214. 1996.
Reptonia laurina Benth., FHK 208. 1861.

Tree, to 20 m tall, conspicuously buttressed. Branchlets angulate, glabrous. Leaves mostly alternate, sometimes opposite or whorled; petioles 1–2 cm; leaf blades almost leathery, obovate to oblanceolate, rarely narrowly elliptic, 7–16 × 2.5 – 4 cm, base cuneate, apex short-acuminate, glabrous on both surfaces; lateral veins 6–9 pairs; stipules small, caducous. Racemes or panicles 2–13 cm, puberulous. Flowers 4 mm in diam. Pedicels 1–5 mm, yellowish brown-tomentose. Sepals 2–3 mm, subrounded, glabrous adaxially, yellowish brown-tomentose abaxially. Corolla white or pale green, 3 –4 mm; lobes broadly obovate to subrounded, 2–2.5 mm. Staminodes subulate, nearly as long as stamens. Ovary ovoid, 1–1.5 mm, 1-locular, glabrous. Drupe ellipsoid, 1.5 –2.5 × 0.8–1 cm, red and shining, base with recurved persistent calyx. Seed 1, ca. 1.7 × 0.8 cm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. L. T. Lo 417; K. Y. Tam 114; Y. W. Lam 208.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Zhejiang; Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Aug.–Sep.; fruiting: Dec.–Jan. of the following year.
Uses: Timber.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Hong Kong Island by W. A. Harland in 1850s.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Wong Nai Chung, Victoria Peak, Shing Mun, Shatin, Lion Rock, Ma On Shan, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Sinosideroxylon wightianum (Hook. & Arn.) Aubr. 革葉鐵欖（鐵欖）
Fl. Cambodge, Laos & Vietnam. 3: 68. 1963; FRPS 60(1): 75, pl. 14: 1–3. 1987; FFJ 4: 312, fig. 247.1989; FGD 2: 357, fig. 243. 1991; FOC 15: 212. 1996.
Sideroxylon wightianum Hook. & Arn., Bot. Beechey Voy. 196. 1837; FHK 209. 1861; FKH 161. 1912.
Sideroxylon wightianum var. balansae Lecomte, Observ. Bot. 3: 887. 1930.
Mastichodendron wightianum (Hook. & Arn.) P. Royen, Blumea 10(1): 123, 125, fig. 1. 1960.

Evergreen small trees, 4 –10 m tall. Branchlets and leaves rusty tomentose when young, glabrescent, conspicuously lenticellate. Petioles 1–2 cm; leaf blade oblong, elliptic, lanceolate or oblanceolate, 9 –15(–17) × 2.5 – 4 cm, leathery, base cuneate, apex abruptly acuminate and caudate, glabrous; lateral veins 12–17 pairs. Flowers solitary or 2–5 clustered in leaf axils, greenish white, fragrant. Pedicels 4 –10 mm, pubescent. Sepals ovate to lanceolate, rusty tomentose, ca. 2.5 mm. Corolla white, 6– 8 mm, lobes suborbicular to ovate, glabrous. Stamens slightly longer than corolla lobes. Staminodes lanceolate to subtriangular, petaloid, 2.5 –3 mm. Ovary ovoid, tomentose. Berry ellipsoid or ovoid, 1–1.5(–1.8) × 0.5–0.8 cm, glabrous, deep purple. Seed 1, ellipsoid, compressed; shiny, scar basal to lateral-basal, suborbicular.

Locality: Wong Nai Chung, Victoria Peak, Shing Mun, Shatin, Lion Rock, Ma On Shan, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island. H. C. Tang 2025; Y. W. Lam 2303; C. H. Tsou 1871.
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong, Guizhou, Yunnan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Thickets and forests. Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: Aug.– Oct.

Diospyros eriantha Champ. ex Benth. 烏柿（烏材）
Hooker's J. Bot. Kew. Gard. Misc. 4: 302. 1852; FHK 210. 1861; FKH 161. 1912; FHN 3: 151. 1974; FRPS 60(1): 133, pl. 31: 3 –5. 1987; FFJ 4: 318, fig. 251. 1989; FGD 3: 304. 1995; FOC 15: 231. 1996.

Evergreen tree or shrub, to 13 m tall; young branches, young leaves and inflorescense rusty strigose, old branches glabrescent. Leaves distichous. Petioles 5 – 6 mm, densely brown-strigose; leaf blade papery, oblong-lanceolate, 5 –15 × 1.8 – 4 cm, base broadly cuneate to rounded, apex acuminate, glabrous and shining adaxially, rusty-strigose along midvein and lateral veins abaxially; lateral veins 4 –8 pairs. Male flowers 1–3 clustered in leaf axils, subsessile, with several imbricate ovate bracts; calyx 4-lobed, lobes lanceolate, 4 –5 mm, strigose; corolla white, salverform, strigose abaxially; tubes 7– 8 mm; lobes 4, lanceolate, 4 –5 mm; stamens 14 –16; pistillodes small. Female flowers solitary and axillary, subsessile; perianth as in male flowers; ovary densely strigose, 2-locular; staminodes 8. Fruit ellipsoid, 1.5 × 1 cm, hairy initially, later only hairy at apex. Seeds 1–2; persistent calyx lobes ovate, ca. 1 cm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. N. H. Li 103; Y. S. Lau 1923; C. P. Lau 1.
Distribution: Guangdong, Hainan, Guangxi, Taiwan, Fujian; Japan, Laos, Vietnam, Malaysia, Indonesia.
Ecology: Lowland thin forests and streamsides. Flowering: Jul.–Aug.; fruiting: Oct.–Feb. of the following year.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Happy Valley woods by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1850.

Diospyros kaki Thunb. 柿
Nova Acta Regiae Soc. Sci. Upsal. 3: 208. 1780; FKH 161. 1912; FGZ 467. 1956; FHN 3: 150. 1974; FRPS 60(1): 141, pl. 34: 1. 1987; FFJ 4: 322, fig. 256. 1989; FGD 3: 302. 1995; FOC 15: 225. 1996.

Deciduous tree, 5–12 m tall, polygamous. Young branchlets densely brown-pubescent, glabrascent. Petioles 1–2.5 cm; leaf blade papery or leathery, ovate-elliptic, broadly ovate or obovate, 7–17 × 5–10 cm, base attenuate or subrounded, pubescent on both surfaces when young, pubescent abaxially when mature; lateral veins 5 –7 pairs. Male flowers small, 3–5 in cymes; pedicels 0.6–1 cm, pubescent. Calyx nearly as long as corolla, hairy on both surfaces, lobes 4; corolla urn-shaped, tubes ca. 1 cm, glabrous, 4-lobed; lobes broadly ovate, ca. 4 mm, reflexed. Stamens 16 –24. Female flowers solitary; staminodes 8(–16); ovary glabrous or pubescent, 8-locular, styles distinct, pubescent. Berries ovoid or depressed globose, 3.5– 8.5 cm in diam. Pericarp thin, orange or pale red, persistent calyx lobes 3 – 4 cm in diam., fruiting stipes ca. 1 cm, pubescent.

Locality: Cultivated. H. C. Tang 920; L. T. Lo 571; Y. S. Lau 1111.
Distribution: Native to China, widely cultivated.
Ecology: Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: Sep.– Oct.
Uses: Food (fruit), medicinal (folklore).

Diospyros morrisiana Hance 羅浮柿
Ann. Bot. Syst. 3: 14. 1852; FHK 210. 1861; FKH 161. 1912; FGZ 468. 1956; FHN 3: 154. 1974; FRPS 60(1): 119, pl. 21: 2–3. 1987; FFJ 4: 319, fig. 253. 1989; FGD 3: 297, fig. 193. 1995; FOC 15: 223. 1996.

Deciduous shrub or tree, to 20 m tall. Young branches very sparsely puberulous, glabrescent. Petioles ca. 1 cm; leaf blade thinly leathery, elliptic, oblong or ovoid, 5–10 × 2.5–4 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate to obtuse, margin sometimes slightly undulate and recurved, glabrous on both surfaces; lateral veins 4–8 pairs, inconspicuous. Male flowers: 2–3 in cymes; pedicels ca. 2 mm; calyx campanulate, 4-lobed; lobes triangular, tomentose, ca. 5 mm; corolla white, urn-shaped, ca. 7 mm, glabrous, 4-lobed; lobes ovate, ca. 2 × 2 mm; stamens 16–20, conspicuously hairy. Female flowers solitary; calyx-lobes 4, divided to about middle, tomentose; corolla nearly urn-shaped, ca. 7 mm; corolla lobes 4, ca. 3 × 3 mm, glabrous abaxially, densely brown-tomentose adaxially; staminodes 6; ovary globose, glabrous, styles 4, tomentose, connate at lower half. Berries yellow, subglobose, 1.5–2 cm in diam., 4-locular, glabrous, apex sometimes apiculate. Seeds castaneous, oblong, 10–14 × 5–7 mm, persistent calyx nearly square, subglabrous; fruiting pedicels very short.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 1762; S. Y. Hu & P. P. H. But 24065; H. C. Tang 1402.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan, Yunnan, Sichuan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Thin forests on hillslopes or by streams. Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Victoria Peak by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1850.

Diospyros tsangii Merr. 油杯子（延平柿）
Lingnan Sci. J. 13: 43. 1934; FRPS 60(1): 126, pl. 29: 1–3. 1987; FFJ 4: 318, fig. 252. 1989; FGD 3: 300, fig. 194. 1995; FOC 15: 225. 1996.

Shrub or small tree, 3–10 m tall; young branchlets slender, rusty pubescent, old branches glabrous. Petioles 3–6 mm, rusty pubescent; leaf blade papery, oblong or oblong-elliptic, 4–9 × 1.5–3 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, sparsely rusty pubescent along midvein and lateral veins adaxially, sparsely rusty pubescent along midvein and lateral veins or subglabrous abaxially; lateral veins 3 –5 pairs. Male flowers 1–3 in cymes, peduncles ca. 3 mm, white-pubescent; pedicels ca. 2 mm, white-pubescent; calyx densely pubescent abaxially, lobes 4, lanceolate, ca. 10 × 2.5 mm; corolla urn-shaped, white, glabrous, 4-lobed, lobes ovate, ca. 3 mm, white-pubescent on both surfaces; stamens 16, in pairs. Female flowers solitary, larger than male flowers; staminodes 8; ovary hairy. Berries globose or ellipsoid, 1–3.5 cm in diam., orange when mature, pilose; persistent calyx-lobes to 1.5 cm, pubescent.

Locality: Tai Tam, Sai Kung. F. W. Xing 8764.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Hunan, Jiangxi.
Ecology: Thin forests. Flowering: Feb.–May; fruiting: Aug.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Mount Gough, Findlay Road, Tai Tam, Tai Mo Shan, Pat Sin Leng
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Diospyros tutcheri Dunn 嶺南柿
Bull. Misc. Inform. Kew. 1913: 354. 1913; FOC 15: 230. 1996.
Diospyros taamii Merr., J. Arnold Arbor. 26(2): 166, fig. 3. 1945.

Small tree 6 m tall. Young branchlets yellowish brown, glabrous. Petioles 0.5 –1 cm; leaf blade thinly leathery, elliptic or oblong, 6 –14 × 2.5 –5 cm, base obtuse, apex acuminate, glabrous on both surfaces; lateral veins 5 or 6 pairs. Male flowers in cymes; pedicels 5 – 6 mm, articulate near apex; calyx 4-lobed, 1–2 mm, lobes triangular; corolla urn-shaped, 7– 8 mm, sericeous abaxially, 4-lobed, lobes broadly ovate, reflexed; stamens 16, in pairs; filaments pubescent; pistillodes small, hispid. Female flowers solitary, pendulous; pedicels 1.3 –1.5 cm, sericeous; calyx-lobes 4, ovate, 8 mm; corolla urn-shaped, ca. 5 mm, constricted at mouth, lobes 4, shorter than tubes, tomentose on both surfaces; staminodes 4; ovary depressed globose, 3 mm, 8-locular. Berries globose, ca. 3 cm in diam., glabrous; persistent calyx lobes long ovate, 1–2 cm fruiting pedicels 1–3 cm, slender.

Locality: Mount Gough, Findlay Road, Tai Tam, Tai Mo Shan, Pat Sin Leng. H. C. Tang 1871; S. C. Ng 3515; F. W. Xing 7084.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Guizhou.
Ecology: Thin forests in ravines. Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: Aug.– Oct.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Mount Gough by W. J. Tutcher in 1911.

Diospyros vaccinioides Lindl. 小果柿
Exot. Fl. 2: 139. 1825; FKH 161. 1912; FRPS 60(1): 99. 1987; FGD 3: 296. 1995; FOC 15: 221. 1996.
Rospidios vaccinioides A. DC., Prodr. 8: 220. 1844; FHK 210. 1861.
Diospyros vaccinioides var. oblongata Merr. & Chun, Sunyatsenia 5: 162. 1940; FHN 3: 150. 1974; FRPS 60(1): 100. 1987.

Evergreen shrub 1–3 m tall, much branched. Young branchlets firmly rusty villous. Petioles 1–2 mm, rusty pubescent, glabrescent; leaf blade leathery, elliptic, oblong to ovate, 1–3.5 × 1–1.5 cm, base cuneate, apex acute and mucronate, glabrous except pilose along midveins abaxially; lateral veins 5– 6 pairs. Male flowers solitary or in cymes, small, pendulous, subsessile; calyx divided nearly to base, lobes 4, narrowly lanceolate, pubescent; corolla ca. 4.5 mm, lobes 4; stamens 16. Female flowers solitary; calyx and corolla as in male flowers; staminodes 4– 8, linear; ovary glabrous. Berries globose or ellipsoid, 0.8 –1 cm in diam., subsessile; seeds 1–3, testa dark brown; persistent calyx lobes lanceolate, 5– 8 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 1402; C. H. Tsou 1867; Y. S. Lau 562.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan.
Ecology: Thin forests and thickets in ravines or on hillslopes. Flowering: May; fruiting: Autumn and winter.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Happy Valley, Mount Nicholson, Kwun Yam Shan, New Territories, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Alniphyllum fortunei (Hemsl.)Makino 赤楊葉
Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 20: 93. 1906; FGD 1: 383. 1987; FRPS 60(2): 122. 1987; FOC 15: 264. 1996.
Halesia fortunei Hemsl., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 26: 75. 1889.
Alniphyllum pterospermum auct. non Matsum.: FKH 164. 1912.

Tree to 20 m tall; bark greyish brown; branchlets, leaves, inflorescence brownish stellate-pubescent. Leaves papery; petioles 1–2 cm; leaf blade elliptic to obovate-elliptic, 8 –18 × 4 – 8 cm, apex acute to acuminate, base broadly cuneate to cuneate, margin remotely serrate, sparsely to densely brownish stellate pubescent to tomentose, sometimes glabrescent abaxially, lateral veins 7–12 on each side of midvein. Inflorescences terminal or axillary, racemose or paniculate, 10 –20-flowered, 8 –15 cm; flowers 1.5 –2 cm, reddish white; pedicels 4 – 8 mm; calyx cup-shaped, 4 –5 mm, densely grey stellate pubescent, with ovate-lanceolate teeth; corolla lobes elliptic, 10 –15 × 5 –7 mm; stamens 10, filament-tube ca. 8 mm, anthers 3 mm; style 1.5 –1.8 cm, villose. Fruit oblong to ellipsoid, 1–2.5 cm, black, sparsely white stellate pubescent or glabrous. Seeds many, oblong, 5–7 mm, winged at both ends.

Locality: Happy Valley, Mount Nicholson, Kwun Yam Shan, New Territories, Lantau Island. HK sheet 18179, 35066; W. J. Tutcher 8484.
Distribution: Hainan, Anhui, Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Jiangsu; India, Laos, Myanmar, Vietnam.
Ecology: Secondary forests on hill slopes. Flowering: Apr.– Jul.; fruiting: Aug.– Oct.

Huodendron biaristatum (W. W. Smith) Rehd. var. parviflorum (Merr.) Rehd. 嶺南山茉莉
J. Arnold Arbor. 16: 346. 1935; FGD 1: 384. 1987; FRPS 60(2): 128. 1987; FOC 15: 265. 1996.
Styrax parviflorus Merr., J. Arnold Arbor. 8: 15. 1927.
Huodendron biaristatum (W. W. Smith) Rehd. subsp. parviflorum (Merr.) Y. C. Tang, Ic. Corm. Sin. 3: 335. 1974, nom. nud.

Shrub or tree, to 7 m tall; bark greyish brown, exfoliating; branchlets reddish brown or greyish brown, tomentose or glabrous. Leaves sub-leathery; petiole 7–9 mm; leaf blade oblong-elliptic or oblong-lanceolate, 6–11 × 2.5– 4.5 cm, apex acute or short acuminate, base cuneate, margin remotely serrate, glabrous on both surfaces, lateral veins 4–6 on each side of midvein. Inflorescences terminal or axillary, sub-corymbose, ca. 5 cm, densely grey-tomentose; pedicels 1 cm; calyx 2-2.5 mm; petals yellowish, narrowly oblong, ca. 6 mm, densely greyish tomentose; stamens 10, as long as petals; filaments flattened, pubescent; anthers as long as filaments, connectives 3-toothed, the middle one smaller than lateral ones, pubescent; styles slightly longer than stamens, 3-lobed at apex. Fruit ellipsoid, ca. 5mm, densely greyish tomentose. Seeds ca. 1 mm.

Locality: Ng Tung Chai. P. S. Choi 502; Y. W. Lam 36.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi.
Ecology: Forests in valleys.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Ng Tung Chai, Kwun Yam Shan
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Rehderodendron kwangtungense Chun 廣東木瓜紅
Sunyatsenia. 1: 290. 1943; FGD 1: 383. 1987; FRPS 60(2): 136. 1987; FOC 15: 270. 1996.
Rehderodendron hui Chun, Sunyatsenia 1(4): 291. 1934.

Tree to 15 m tall, bark grey; branchlets reddish brown, smooth; winter buds ovoid to obconical, red-brown. Leaves leathery; petioles 1–1.5 cm; leaf blade oblong-elliptic to elliptic, 7–16 × 3–8 cm, apex acute to acuminate, base cuneate, margin remotely serrate, glabrous or slightly stellate pubescent and villose along veins abaxially, lateral veins 7–11 on each side of midvein. Racemes 6–8-flowered, ca. 7 cm; rhachis, pedicels, bracts and calyx densely grey-yellow stellate tomentose; pedicels ca. 1 cm; calyx campanulate, ca. 6 mm, lobes lanceolate; corolla lobes ovate, slightly unequal in length, 2–2.5 × 1–1.4 cm, densely stellate pubescent on both surfaces; stamens 10, longer ones as long as corolla. Fruit cylindrical, obovoid or ellipsoid, 4.5 – 8 × 2.5 – 4 cm, brown to grey-brown, glabrous or slightly pubescent, 5–10-ribbed, smooth between ribs, exocarp ca. 1 mm thick, mesocarp 0.8 –1.2 cm thick, endocarp woody. Seeds 2– 4, spindly, 2–3 cm.

Locality: Ng Tung Chai, Kwun Yam Shan. P. S. Choi 348, 323; Y. S. Lau 2746.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Yunnan.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Mar.–Apr.; fruiting: Jul.–Sep.

Styrax confusus Hemsl. 賽山梅（狗肝柴）
Bull. Misc. Inform. Kew. 1906: 162. 1906; FGD 1: 391. 1987; FRPS 60(2): 113. 1987; FOC 15: 262. 1996.
Styrax mollis Dunn, Kew Bull. Misc. Inform. 1911: 273. 1911; FKH 164. 1912.

Tree 2– 8 m tall; bark greyish brown; branchlets densely brownish stellate pubescent. Leaves alternate, leathery to subleathery; petioles 1–3 mm; leaf blade elliptic to obovate-elliptic, 4 –14 × 2.5–7 cm, apex acute to shortly acuminate, base rounded to broadly cuneate, margin irregularly serrulate, sparsely stellate pubescent, gradually glabrescent, lateral veins 5 –7 on each side of midvein. Racemes terminal, 3 – 8-flowered, 4 –10 cm; rachis densely brownish stellate pubescent; pedicels 1–1.5 cm, densely brownish stellate pubescent; flowers 1.3 –2.2 cm; calyx 4 –10 × 4–6 mm, densely yellowish to grey stellate tomentose and villose; teeth 5, deltoid; corolla tube 3– 4 mm, lobes lanceolate, 12–20 × 3 – 4 mm, imbricate or sparsely valvate in buds; stamens 10, filaments slightly expanded, 8–10 mm, free parts basally densely white villose. Fruit sub-globose to obovoid, 0.8 –1.5 cm in diam., densely yellowish stellate tomentose; exocarp 1–2 mm thick, rugose. Seeds brown, obovoid, smooth or deeply rugose.

Locality: Lantau Island. HK sheet 18182.
Distribution: Anhui, Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Jiangsu, Zhejiang.
Ecology: Thin forests, margins of forests. Flowering: Apr.– Oct.
Notes: The species was reported as styrax faberi Perkins previously (Check List HK Plants 35. 1993). The type specimen was collected from Lantau Island by Mr. Ford's native collector in May 1888.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Repulse Bay, Wan Chai Gap, Wong Chuk Hang, Pok Fu Lam, Aberdeen, Tai Tam Tuk, Mount Victoria, Mount Gough, Causeway Bay, Sunset Peak
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Styrax odoratissimus Champ. ex Benth. 芳香安息香
Hooker's J. Bot. Kew. Gard. Misc. 4: 304. 1852; FHK 213. 1861; Forb. & Hemsl., J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 26: 76. 1889, p.p.; FKH 164. 1912, “odoratissimum”; FGD 1: 388. 1987; FRPS 60(2): 99. 1987; FOC 15: 258. 1996.

Tree 4 –10 m tall; bark grey-brown; young branchlets densely stellate pubescent. Leaves alternate; petioles 5–10 mm; leaf blade leathery to papery, ovate to ovate-elliptic, 4–15 × 2–8 cm, base broadly cuneate to rounded, apex acuminate to acute, margin entire or remotely serrulate, densely brown stellate pubescent on both surfaces when young, glabrescent in age, lateral veins 6 –9 on each side of midvein. Inflorescence terminal, racemose or paniculate, 8 –12 cm, 6 –12-flowered, densely yellow stellate tomentose; flowers 1.2–1.5 cm; pedicels 1.5 –1.8 cm; calyx ca. 5 × 5 mm, membranous, apex truncate to undulate; corolla lobes elliptic to obovate-elliptic, 9 –11 × 4 –5 mm, membranous, imbricate in buds; stamens shorter than corolla; filaments slightly flexuous at middle, densely white stellate pubescent. Fruit subglobose, 8–10 mm in diam., densely grey-yellow stellate tomentose, apex with a slightly curved rostrum. Seeds ovoid, brown, tuberculate, densely brown scaly.

Locality: Repulse Bay, Wan Chai Gap, Wong Chuk Hang, Pok Fu Lam, Aberdeen, Tai Tam Tuk, Mount Victoria, Mount Gough, Causeway Bay, Sunset Peak. Y. S. Lau 1544; H. C. Tang 809; H. G. Ye et al. 1223.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian.
Ecology: Thin forests, margins of forests. Flowering: Mar.–Apr.; fruiting: Jun.–Sep.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Victoria Peak, Hong Kong Island by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1850.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Victoria Peak, Mount Nicholson, Tai Tam, Cape D'Aguilar, Tai Mo Shan, Happy Valley, Pok Fu Lam, Mount Kellet
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Styrax suberifolius Hook. & Arn. 栓葉安息香（紅皮）
Bot. Beechey Voy. 196. 1841; FHK 213. 1861; FKH 164. 1912, “suberifolium”; FHN 3: 182. 1974; FTW 4: 111. 1978; FGD 1: 389. 1987; FRPS 60(2): 109. 1987; FOC 15: 260. 1996.
Cyrta suberifolia (Hook. & Arn.) Miers, Contr. Bot. 1: 182. 1851.

Tree 4 –20 m tall; bark dark brown. Young branchlets, petioles and inflorescence densesly rusty stellate tomentose. Leaves alternate, leathery; petioles 1–1.5 cm; leaf blade elliptic to oblong-lanceolate, 5 –15 × 2–5 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate or acute, margin subentire, glabrous adaxially, densely greyish or brownish stellate tomentose abaxially, lateral veins 5 –12 on each side of midvein. Inflorescences terminal or axillary, racemose or paniculate, many-flowered, 6 –12 cm; pedicels 1–3 mm; flowers white, 1–1.5 cm; calyx cup-shaped, 3–5(–7) × 2– 4(–7) mm, densely grey-yellow tomentose mixed with few stellate hairs; teeth ± rudimentary, deltoid to undulate; corolla tube ca. 3 mm, lobes 4 –5, lanceolate to oblong, 8 –12 × 2–3 mm, valvate in buds; stamens 8 –10, shorter than corolla; filaments expanded, stellate pubescent on free part; anthers oblong, 3 mm; styles subequal to corolla, glabrous. Fruit ovoid-globose, 1.2–3 × 0.8–1.6 cm, densely grey to brown stellate tomentose, 3-valvate dehiscent with persistent calyx enclosing to middle. Seeds 1–2, ellipsoid, brown, smooth or rugose, glabrous or scale-like pubescent.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Mount Nicholson, Tai Tam, Cape D'Aguilar, Tai Mo Shan, Happy Valley, Pok Fu Lam, Mount Kellet. P. S. Choi 339; H. C. Tang 980, 1742.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Myanmar, Vietnam.
Ecology: Thin forests. Flowering: Mar.–May; fruiting: Aug.–Nov.

Symplocos adenophylla Wall. ex G. Don 腺葉山礬
Gen. Hist. 4: 3. 1837; FRPS 60(2): 37. 1987; FGD 1: 408, fig. 445. 1987; FOC 15: 245. 1996.

Tree 4 –10 m tall; branchlets reddish brown. Young shoots, buds, inflorescences, bracts, and calyx reddish brown powdery puberulent. Leaves thick papery; petioles 5 –10 mm, with marginal glands; leaf blade narrowly elliptic, elliptic, or narrowly ovate, 6 –11 × 1.8 –3 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate to caudateacuminate, margin subentire to crenate-serrulate, with ellipsoidal glands at sinus of the teeth; lateral veins 4 –12 pairs. Racemes 2–4 cm, with 1–3 branches, rachis puberulent when young; bracts triangular-ovate, 1–1.5 mm; bracteoles less than 1 mm. Calyx 2–2.5 mm; lobes 5, triangular-ovate, 0.3 –0.5 mm. Corolla white, ca. 3 mm; lobes 5, 2.5 –2.8 mm. Stamens 30 –35; filaments ± united at base. Ovary 3-locular, glabrous; style ca. 2 mm; stigma capitate; disc annular, glabrous. Drupes ellipsoid-cylindric, 6–12 × 3 –5 mm.

Locality: Ma On Shan. F. W. Xing 8459.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Yunnan; Vietnam, India, Malaysia, Singapore, Indonesia.
Ecology: Thin forests, valleys. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.– Aug.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): No precise locality, only one specimen collected in Hong Kong
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Symplocos adenopus Hance 腺柄山礬
J. Bot. 21: 322. 1883; FKH 163. 1912; FRPS 60(2): 61. 1987; FGD 1: 409, fig. 447. 1987; FOC 15: 250. 1996.

Shrub or small tree. Branchlets ± angulate; buds, young branchlets and petioles brown pubescent. Leaves papery; petioles 0.5 –1.8 cm, marginal ridges densely glandular dentate; leaf blade elliptic-ovate to ovate, 5 –16 × 2– 6 cm, base rounded or broadly cuneate, apex acute or acuminate, margin glandular dentate, abaxially appressed pilose to tomentose, especially on the veins; lateral veins 6–14 pairs, impressed adaxially. Glomerules axillary; bracts suborbicular, 2–3 mm in diam., tomentose at least toward apex, margin with large glands; bracteoles elliptic, 1–2 mm, tomentose at least toward apex, margin with small glands. Calyx 2–3 mm; lobes 5, semi-orbicular, 1.5–2 mm, glabrous, sometimes ciliate. Corolla white, ca. 5 mm, divided nearly to base, 5-lobed; lobes elliptic to elliptic-ovate, 3.5 – 4 mm. Stamens 20–30. Ovary 3-locular, glabrous; disc cylindric, 0.5 –1 mm long, glabrous. Drupes cylindric, 7–10 mm, apex with persistent erect calyxlobes.

Locality: No precise locality, only one specimen collected in Hong Kong. HK sheet 17993.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Yunnan, Guizhou.
Ecology: Valleys or thin forests. Flowering: Nov.–Dec.; fruiting: Jul.–Aug. of the following year.

Symplocos anomala Brand. 薄葉山礬
Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 29: 529. 1900; FRPS 60(2): 15. 1987; FGD 1: 404, fig. 439. 1987; FOC 15: 242. 1996.
Symplocos anomala Brand var. nitida Li in J. Arnold Arbor. 24: 452. 1943.

Shrub or small tree; terminal buds and young branchlets brown tomentose. Leaves thin leathery; petioles 4 – 8 mm; leaf blade narrowly elliptic, elliptic or oblanceolate, 2–7(–11) × 1.2–3 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, margin entire or sparsely and shallowly serrulate; glabrous or rarely young leaves finely appressed hairy on abaxial surface; midvein and lateral veins adaxially prominent; lateral veins 7–10 on each side of midvein. Racemes 0.8 –1.5 cm, axillary, sometimes 1–3-branched from base, pubescent. Bracts and bracteoles ovate, margin ciliate, 0.8 –1.5 mm. Calyx 2–2.5 mm, puberulent; lobes 5, semi-orbicular, ciliate. Corolla white, 4 – 6 mm, divided nearly to base; lobes 5, elliptic, 3– 4 mm. Stamens ca. 30; filaments ± united at base in fascicles. Ovary 3-locular; disc annular, pubescent. Drupes brown, obovoid, 7–10 mm, puberulent, apex with persistent erect or inflexed calyx-lobes.

Locality: Sunset Peak. Y. W. Lam 1647, 1745.
Distribution: Areas S of Changjiang River.
Ecology: Broadleaved forests. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Dec.

Symplocos cochinchinensis (Lour.) S. Moore var. laurina (Retz.) Nooteb. 黃牛奶樹
Rev. Symploc. 156. 1975; FOC 15: 249. 1996.
Myrtus laurina Retz. Obs. 4: 26. 1786.
Symplocos laurina (Retz.) Wall. ex G. Don, Gen. Syst. 4: 3. 1837; FRPS 60(2): 55. 1987; FGD 1: 417, fig. 460. 1987.
Symplocos spicata Roxb., Fl. Ind. ed. Carey, 541. 1832; FHK 212, 1861; FKH 163. 1912.

Evergreen tree. Branchlets glabrous; buds brown pubescent. Leaves leathery; petioles 1–1.5 cm; leaf blade ovate-elliptic to narrowly elliptic, 5.5–11 × 2–8.5 cm, base cuneate to broadly cuneate, apex acute or acuminate, margin denticulate, glabrous on both surfaces; midvein impressed abaxially, lateral veins 4–5 on pairs. Spikes terminal or axillary, 3–6 cm, usually branched at base, pubescent at flowering time; bracts broadly ovate, ca. 2 mm, margin glandular punctate. Calyx glabrous, ca. 2 mm; lobes 5, semi-orbicular, shorter than the tube. Corolla white, ca. 4 mm, 5-lobed nearly to the base. Stamens ca. 30; filaments 3–5 mm, ± united at base in fascicles. Ovary 3-locular; disc annular, glabrous. Drupes globose, 4–6 mm in diam., apex with persistent erect calyx-lobes.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 2098; HK sheet 36098.
Distribution: S, C, SW & E China; India, Sri Lanka.
Ecology: Secondary forests and thickets. Flowering: Aug.–Dec.; fruiting: Mar.–Jun. of the following year.

Symplocos confusa Brand 南嶺山礬
Pflanzenr. 6 (IV. 242): 88. 1901; FKH 163. 1912; FRPS 60(2): 74. 1987; FGD 1: 423, fig. 470. 1987.
Symplocos pendula var. hirtistylis (C. B. Clarke) Noot., Rev. Symplocac. 42. 1975; FOC 15: 252. 1996.

Evergreen small tree; buds, inflorescences, bracts, and calyx grey pubescent. Leaves subleathery; petioles 1–2 cm; leaf blade ellipticobovate to ovate, 5 –12 × 2–4.5 cm, base cuneate, apex acute to shortly acuminate, tip blunt, margin entire or dentate; midvein abaxially impressed, lateral veins 5–9 per side. Racemes 1–2.5(–4.5) cm, axillary; bracts oblong-ovate, 1.5 –2 mm, apex obtuse; bracteoles narrowly ovate, 1–1.2 mm, apex acute. Pedicels 3 –5 mm. Calyx campanulate, 2.2–3.2 mm, 5-lobed; lobes shorter and rounded. Corolla white, 4.5 –7 mm, 5-lobed; tube 1–2 mm. Stamens 40 –50, filaments flat, connate into a tube and adnate to the throat of corolla tube. Ovary 2-locular; disc annular, pubescent; style ca. 5 mm; stigmas semi-orbicular. Drupes ovoid, 4–5 mm, pubescent, apex with persistent erect or inflexed calyx-lobes.

Locality: Lantau Peak. HK sheet 18014.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Secondary forests. Flowering: Jun.–Aug.; fruiting: Sep.–Nov.

Symplocos congesta Benth. 密花山礬
FHK 211. 1861; FKH 163. 1912; FRPS 60(2): 69. 1987; FGD 1: 410, fig. 448. 1987; FOC 15: 251. 1996.

Evergreen tree or shrub; young branchlets and buds brown pubescent. Leaves papery; petioles 1–1.5 cm; leaf blade elliptic or obovate, 8 –10(–17) × 2–6 cm, base cuneate to broadly cuneate, apex acuminate or acute, margin usually entire, rarely and sparsely glandular serrulate, glabrous on both surfaces; lateral veins 5 –10 on each side of midvein. Glomerules, axillary; bracts and bractlets brown pubescent, margin with 4 or 5 oblong glands. Calyx often reddish brown, 3 – 4 mm, glabrous. Corolla white, 4 – 6 mm, divided nearly to the base; lobes 5, elliptic ovate. Stamens ca. 50, filaments ± united at base in fascicles. Ovary 3-locular; disc flat to annular, glabrous. Drupes purplish blue, cylindric, 8 –13 × 3 – 4 mm, apex with persistent erect calyx-lobes.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Lantau Island. P. S. Choi 156; HK sheet 37536.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan, Jiangxi, Hunan, Fujian, Taiwan, Yunnan.
Ecology: Mixed forests. Flowering: Aug. –Nov.; fruiting: Jan. –Feb. of the following year.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Hong Kong Island by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1850.

Symplocos decora Hance 美山礬
J. Bot. 12: 369. 1874; FKH 164.1912; FRPS 60(2): 25. 1987; FGD 1: 402, fig. 435. 1987; FOC 15: 244. 1996, pro syn. sub S. sumuntia Buch.-Ham. ex D. Don
Dicalix decorus (Hance) Migo, J. Shanghai Sci. Inst. 13: 200. 1943.

Evergreen small tree, 4 – 6 m tall; branchlets glabrous, greyish when young, turning purplish black in age. Leaves leathery; petioles 0.5 –1 cm; leaf blade elliptic-obovate or elliptic, 4 –11 × 2.5 – 4 cm, base broadly cuneate or rounded, apex shortly acuminate, tip blunt, margin shallowly serrate, glabrous on both surfaces; midvein abaxially impressed, lateral veins indistinct. Racemes 3–6 cm, glabrous or slightly pubescent. Bracts suborbicular, ca. 5 mm in diam., caducous; bracteoles oblong-lanceolate, 3–5 × 1.2 mm, caducous. Pedicels 0.8 –5 mm, jointed. Calyx 3– 4 mm, glabrous; lobes 5, triangular-ovate. Corolla white, 5 –7 mm, divided nearly to the base; lobes 5, ovate-orbicular. Stamens ca. 25; filaments united at base in fascicles. Ovary 3-locular; disc annular, glabrous. Drupes urceolate, 6–9 mm, apex with persistent erect or slightly inflexed calyx lobes.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. Y. W. Lam 211; HK sheet 8887.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Zhejiang.
Ecology: Secondary forests. Flowering: Mar.–May; fruiting: Jul.– Oct.
Notes: The type specimen was collected by H. F. Hance in March 1874 from the Hong Kong Botanic Gardens. This species was recorded as a synonym of Symplocos sumuntia Buch.-Ham. ex D. Don previously (Check List of HK Plants 45. 2004).

Symplocos fordii Hance 三裂山礬
J. Bot. 20: 78. 1882; FKH 163.1912; FRPS 60(2): 27. 1987; FGD 1: 414, fig. 455. 1987; FOC 15: 244. 1996.
Symplocos cordatifolia H. L. Li, J. Arnold Arbor. 25: 424. 1944.

Shrub to 2 m tall. Branchlets slender, dark brown; young shoots, petioles and abaxial surface of leaves covered with spreading greyish yellow long hairs. Leaves thin leathery, subsessile, narrowly ovate or ovate, 3.5 –9 × 1.5–3.5 cm, base cordate, slightly oblique, apex long caudate-acuminate, margin sharply serrate; lateral veins 5 –11 pairs, together with tertiary veins prominent on both surfaces. Spikes short, 5–10 flowered, rachis ca. 1 cm, pubescent; bracts broadly ovate, ca. 1 mm, bracteoles ovate, acute. Calyx ca. 2 mm, glabrous; lobes 3, broadly ovate, slightly longer than the tube. Corolla white, ca. 3.5 mm, divided nearly to base; lobes 5, oblong. Stamens 15 –30, filaments ± connate at base. Ovary 3-locular, glabrous. Drupes narrowly ovoid, ca. 1 cm, apex with persistent erect calyx-lobes.

Locality: Victoria Peak, High West. HK sheet 3273, 37728.
Distribution: Guangdong.
Ecology: Thin forests on summits. Flowering & fruiting: May–Nov.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Victoria Peak by C. Ford in 1881.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Tam Tuk, Cape D'Aguilar, Tai Au Mun, Ho Chung, Sai Kung, Tai Mo Shan, Tai Po, Lai Chi Wo
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Symplocos glauca (Thunb.) Koidz. 羊舌樹
Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 39: 313. 1925; FRPS 60(2): 30. 1987; FGD 1: 413, fig. 454. 1987; FOC 15: 244. 1996.
Laurus glauca Thunb. Fl. Jap. 173. 1784.
Symplocos neriifolia Sieb. & Zucc., Abh. Bayer. Akad. Wiss. Math.-Phys. 4(3): 134. 1846; FKH 163. 1912.

Evergreen shrub or tree. Buds, young branchlets, and inflorescences densely tawny tomentose. Leaves leathery; petioles 1.5–3 mm; leaf blade narrowly elliptic or oblanceolate, 6–15 × 2–4 cm, base cuneate, apex acute or short acuminate, margin entire, glabrous or rarely abaxially with cobwebby hairs, adaxially dark green, abaxially glaucous, turning brown when dry; midvein adaxially impressed, lateral veins 5 –8 on each side of midvein. Spikes 1–1.5 cm, mostly basally branched; bracts broadly ovate, ca. 2 mm, downy tomentose. Calyx ca. 3 mm; lobes 5, ovate, tawny tomentose. Corolla 4–5 mm, divided nearly to base; lobes 5, elliptic, apex rounded. Stamens 30 – 40; filaments slender, ± united at base in fascicles. Ovary 3-locular, glabrous; disc cylindric, glabrous. Drupes narrowly ovoid, 1.2–2 cm, apex with persistent erect calyx lobes.

Locality: Tai Tam Tuk, Cape D'Aguilar, Tai Au Mun, Ho Chung, Sai Kung, Tai Mo Shan, Tai Po, Lai Chi Wo. L. T. Lo 349; Y. S. Lau 948.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan, Zhejiang; Japan.
Ecology: Lowland secondary forests. Flowering: Apr.–Aug.; fruiting: Aug.– Oct.

Symplocos lancifolia Sieb. & Zucc. 光葉山礬
Abh. Bayer. Akad. Wiss. Math.-Phys. 4(3): 133. 1846; FRPS 60(2): 52. 1987; FGD. 1: 420, fig. 464. 1987; FOC 15: 248. 1996.
Symplocos microcarpa Champ. ex Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 4: 303. 1852; FHK 212. 1861; FKH 164. 1912.

Evergreen shrub or small tree; branchlets slender, dark brown, yellowish brown when young, glabrous in age. Leaves papery; petioles 1–5 mm; leaf blade ovate to broadly lanceolate, 3 –9 × 1.5–3.5 cm, base broadly cuneate or subrounded, apex caudate-acuminate, margin finely dentate to crenate, abaxially yellowish brown pubescent on veins when young; lateral veins 6–11 on each side of midvein. Spikes 1– 4 cm; bracts elliptic-ovate, ca. 2 mm; bracteoles broadly triangular-ovate, 1.5 × 2 mm, ciliate. Calyx 1.6 –2 mm; lobes 5, ovate, apex rounded, abaxially puberulent; tube glabrous. Corolla cream yellow, divided nearly to base; lobes 5, elliptic, 2.5– 4 mm. Stamens ca. 25; filaments in fascicles. Ovary 3-locular, apex glabrous. Drupes ellipsoid to subglobose, ca. 4 mm in diam., apex with persistent erect calyx lobes.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 1320, 1443.
Distribution: Areas S of Changjiang River; Japan.
Ecology: Thin forests and thickets. Flowering: Mar.–Nov.; fruiting: Jun.–Dec.
Notes: The type specimen of Symplocos microcarpa was collected from Happy Valley woods by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1850.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Ma On Shan, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Symplocos crassifolia Benth. 厚葉山礬（光亮山礬、厚皮灰木）
FHK 212. 1861; Forb. & Hemsl., J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 26: 72. 1889; FKH 163. 1912; FRPS 60(2): 13. 1987; FGD 1: 399, fig. 430. 1987; FOC 15: 242. 1996, pro syn. sub S. lucida (Thunb.) Sieb. & Zucc.
Symplocos howii Merr. & Chun ex Li, J. Arnold Arbor. 25: 211. 1944.

Evergreen small tree or tree; young branchlets, buds and leaves glabrous. Leaves leathery or thick leathery; petioles 0.8 –1.4 cm; leaf blade ovate-elliptic, elliptic or narrowly elliptic, 6.5–10 × 2.5– 4 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, margin entire or sparsely serrate; midvein raised adaxially; lateral veins slender, 6–10 on each side of midvein, Racemes 1–2 cm, pubescent, branched basally, 4 –7-flowered; bracts oblong-ovate, pubescent abaxially; bracteoles broadly triangular-ovate. Calyx 3 –3.5 mm; lobes 5, broadly ovate or orbicular, margin and abaxial surface puberulent. Corolla white, 4 –5 mm, 5-lobed nearly to base. Stamens 60– 80; filaments united at base in fascicles. Ovary 3-locular; disc with 5 glands, villose. Drupes oblong-ovoid or obovoid, 1–1.5 cm, apex with persistent erect or slightly inflexed calyx-lobes.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Ma On Shan, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island. L. T. Lo 196; HK sheet 3269.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan.
Ecology: Secondary forests. Flowering: Jun.–Nov.; fruiting: Dec.–May of the following year.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Victoria Peak, Hong Kong Island by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1850. This species was recorded as Symplocos lucida (Thunb.) Siebold & Zucc. previously (Check List of HK Plants 45. 2004)
