PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Long Wan, Shing Mun, Tai Po Kau, Fanling, Ho Pui, Tai Lam Chung, Castle Peak

Symplocos paniculata (Thunb.) Miq. 白檀
Ann. Mus. Bot. Lugduno-Batavum 3: 102. 1867; FRPS 60(2): 72. 1987; FGD 1: 422, fig. 469. 1987; FOC 15: 252. 1996.
Prunus paniculata Thunb., Fl. Jap. 200. 1784.
Symlocos sinica Ker-Gawl., Bot. Reg. 9: t. 710. 1823; FKH 163. 1912.
Symplocos crataegoides Buch.-Ham. ex D. Don, Prodr. Fl. Nepal. 145. 1825; FKH 163. 1912.
Symplocos hunanensis Hand.-Mazz., Symb. Sin. 7: 807. 1936.

Deciduous shrub or small tree; branchlets greyish white pilose when young, glabrous in age. Leaves membranous to thin papery; petioles 3 –7 mm; leaf blade broadly obovate, elliptic-obovate or ovate, 3–11 × 2–4 cm, base broadly cuneate or subrounded, apex acute or acuminate, margin sharply serrulate, adaxially glabrous or puberulent, abaxially usually glabrous or sometimes pubescent on veins; midvein adaxially impressed on proximal half, with 4–8 lateral veins on each side. Panicles 5–10 cm, usually pilose; bracts linear, 1(–3) mm, brown glandular, caducous. Calyx 2–3 mm long; tube brown, glabrous or sparsely pubescent; lobes 5, ovate or semi-orbicular, slightly longer than tube. Corolla white, 4– 6 mm, divided nearly to base; lobes 5, elliptic, shortly ciliate. Stamens 40 – 60, unequal. Ovary 2-locular; disc 5-glandular, glabrous or hairy. Drupes bluish, ovoid-globose, 3– 8 mm, apex with persistent erect calyx-lobes.

Locality: Tai Long Wan, Shing Mun, Tai Po Kau, Fanling, Ho Pui, Tai Lam Chung, Castle Peak. H. C. Tang 1245; Y. S. Lau 2471.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; Japan, Korea, India.
Ecology: Thickets or grasslands. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.; fruiting: Sep.–Nov.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Victoria Peak, Ma On Shan, Lantau Island

Symplocos sumuntia Buch.-Ham. ex D. Don 山礬
Prodr. Fl. Nepal. 145. 1825; FRPS 60(2): 22. 1987; FGD 1: 401, fig. 433. 1987; FOC 15: 243. 1996, p.p. excl. syn. S. decora Hance.
Symplocos caudata Wall. in DC. Prodr. 8: 256. 1844.
Symplocos punctata Brand in Fedde, Repert. Nov. Sp. 3: 217. 1906.

Evergreen tree; young branchlets brown, mostly glabrous. Leaves thin leathery; petioles 0.5 –1 cm; leaf blade ovate, narrowly ovate, or elliptic-oblanceolate, 3.5– 8 × 1.5–3 cm, base cuneate or rounded, apex caudate-acuminate, margin slightly serrate or sinuolatedentate, glabrous; midvein adaxially impressed; lateral veins 4 – 6 on each side of midvein. Racemes 2.5 – 4 cm, pubescent. Bracts and bracteoles broadly ovate or obovate, 0.5 –1.5 mm, densely pubescent. Calyx 2–2.5 mm; tube glabrous; lobes 5, triangular-ovate, equal or slightly shorter than tube. Corolla white or yellow, 4 – 8 mm, divided nearly to base; lobes 5, obovate-elliptic, 3 –3.5 mm, slightly puberulent adaxially. Stamens 25–35; filaments united at base in fascicles. Ovary 3-locular; disc annular, glabrous. Drupes ovoidurceolate, 7–10 mm, apex with persistent erect calyx lobes.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Ma On Shan, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 931, 1528.
Distribution: Areas S of Changjiang River; Nepal, Bhutan, India.
Ecology: Thin forests on summits. Flowering: Feb.–Mar.; fruiting: Jun.–Jul.

Symplocos wikstroemiifolia Hayata 微毛山礬
Icon. Pl. Formosan. 5: 119. 1915; Noot., Fl. Taiwan 4: 131. 1978; FRPS 60(2): 16. 1987; FGD. 1: 400, fig. 432. 1987; FOC 15: 243. 1996.

Tree or shrub; young branchlets, petioles and abaxial surface of leaves covered with appressed hairs. Leaves papery to thin leathery; petioles 3 –10 mm; leaf blade elliptic, broadly oblanceolate, or obovate, 4 –12 × 1.5 – 4 cm, base narrowly cuneate, decurrent to the petioles, apex shortly acuminate, acute, or obtuse, margin entire or obscurely sinuolate-dentate; lateral veins 6–10 on each side of midvein; Racemes 1–2 cm, branched; rachis, bracts and bracteoles pubescent; bracts caducous, oblong or orbicular, 1.2–2 mm, margin ciliate. Calyx ca. 2 mm; lobes 5, broadly ovate or suborbicular, as long as or slightly longer than the tube. Corolla ca. 3 mm, divided nearly to base; lobes 5, obovate-oblong. Stamens 15–20. Ovary sparsely pubescent or glabrous; disc annular, nearly glabrous or sparsely pilose. Drupes ovoid, black or black-purple, 5 –10 mm, apex with persistent erect calyx-lobes.

Locality: Ma On Shan. HK sheet 37724, 37725.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Fujian, Taiwan, Zhejiang, Yunnan, Guizhou.
Ecology: Secondary forests. Flowering: Mar.; fruiting: Oct.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tytam Took (Tai Tam Tuk), Sai Wan, Shek O, Shatin, Ma Wan Island, Mai Po, Sai Kung, Yung Shue Au, Ho Chung
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Aegiceras corniculatum (L.) Blanco 蠟燭果
Fl. Filip. 79. 1837; Mez, Pflanzenr. IV. 236(Heft 9): 55, fig. 8. 1902; B. C. Stone, Tree Fl. Malaya 4: 266. 1989; K. Larsen & C. M. Hu, Fl. Thailand, 6(2): 176. 1996; FOC 15: 9. 1996.
Rhizophora corniculata L., Amoen. Acad. 4: 123. 1759.
Aegiceras majus J. Gaertner, Deucr. & Sem. 1: 216, pl. 46, fig. 1. 1788; FHK 208. 1861; FKH 160. 1912.

Shrub or small tree, 1.5– 4 m tall, much branched; branchlets terete, glabrous, brownish black when dry. Leaves alternate; petioles 5–10 mm; leaf blade obovate or elliptic, 3–10 x 2–4.5 cm, base cuneate, apex rounded or emarginate, margin entire and slightly recurved, leathery, glabrous, with many minute pores on both surfaces; lateral veins 7–11 pairs, slender and slightly raised on both surfaces, ascending and anastomosing near the edge; veinlets obscure. Umbels terminal, axillary or leaf-opposed, sessile or very shortly peduncled, usually many flowered. Pedicels ca. 1 cm. Flowers white, without bracteole. Calyx split to base; lobes leathery, oblique-oblong, ca. 6 × 3 mm, gibbous and thickened at base. Corolla-tube ca. 3.5 mm, villous adaxially; lobes ovate to ovate-lanceolate, ca. 6.5 × 3 mm, apex acute, reflexed. Stamens shorter than corolla; filaments 6 –7 mm, base fused into a tube, densely villous, free part slightly longer than the tube, glabrous; anthers 2.5 –3 mm, dorsifixed. Ovary ovoid; style 6 –8 mm, subulate, with black glandular dots. Fruit cylindric, curved, falcate or crescent-shaped, 5 – 8 cm, acuminate at apex.

Locality: Tytam Took (Tai Tam Tuk), Sai Wan, Shek O, Shatin, Ma Wan Island, Mai Po, Sai Kung, Yung Shue Au, Ho Chung. Y. S. Lau 1377, 2707; P. S. Choi 131, 207, 208; H. C. Tang 1291, 1902.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian, Guangxi; India, Malaysia, Philippines, Sri Lanka, Vietnam, Australia.
Ecology: Sea coasts, mangroves, muddy flats. Flowering: Dec.–Feb; fruiting: Oct.–Dec.

Ardisia crenata Sims 朱砂根
Bot. Mag. 45: pl. 1950. 1817; FRPS 58: 68. 1979; FOC 15: 19. 1996, p.p. excl. syn. A. kusukusensis Hayata.
Ardisia crispa A. DC., Trans. Linn. Soc. London 17: 124. 1834, & Prodr. 8: 134. 1844, nom. confus., non Bladhia crispa Thunb. 1784; FHK 206. 1861; FKH 160. 1912.
Ardisia linangensis C. M. Hu, Bot. J. South China 1: 5. 1992.

Shrub, 1–2 m rarely to 3 m tall. Branchlets slender, terete or slightly angular, glabrous, generally bearing 2–5 leaves on upper half. Leaves alternate; petioles 4–10 mm, glabrous; leaf blade papery, ± leathery elliptic to oblong-lanceolate or oblanceolate, (4.5–)6–15(–20) × 1.2–4 cm, base cuneate, apex acute or acuminate, crisp- or undulate-crenate, margin ± recurved, with large marginal glands, glabrous, minutely rusty lepidote on abaxial surface; glandular dots many, scattered, black or sometimes colorless, slightly convex when dry; lateral veins 12–18 pairs, ± raised abaxially, meeting in an irregular intramarginal vein near edge; veins usually obscure. Inflorescence subumbellate or corymbose, simple or compound, terminal on branchlets, glabrous or puberulous; primary rays 2–4 cm. Pedicels 5–10 mm. Calyx split almost to base; lobes ovate to oblong-ovate, ca. 1.5 mm, acute or obtuse, punctate. Corolla white or pinkish, 4–5.5 mm, deeply lobed; lobes ovate, acute, ca. 3 mm wide, with scattered glandular dots. Anthers triangular-lanceolate, 3.5–4 mm, usually punctate on back. Ovary glabrous; style 3–4.5 mm; ovules ca. 5, in 1 series on placenta. Fruit globose, 6–8 mm in diam., bright red, with black glandular dots.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. HK sheet 17735, 34491; H. C. Tang 14, 2143.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Taiwan, Fujian, Zhejiang, Jiangxi, Anhui, Hubei, Hunan, Yunan, SW Xizang; India, Myanmar, Thailand, Malay Peninsula, Cambodia, Vietnam, Philippines, Japan.
Ecology: Forest , hillsides, valleys and stream banks. Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: Oct.–Dec.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Mount Parker, Wu Kau Tang, Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Ardisia cymosa Blume 小紫金牛
Bijdr. 689. 1826; C. M. Hu, Blumea 44: 393. 1999.
Ardisia chinensis Benth., FHK 207. 1861; FKH 160. 1912; FRPS 58: 90. 1979; FOC 15: 26. 1996.
Ardisia triflora Hemsl., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 26: 67. 1889.
Ardisia argenticaulis Yang & Dwyer, Taiwania 34: 287. 1989; FOC 15: 27. 1996, syn. nov.

Small shrub, up to 45 cm tall. Stem ascending-erect, longitudinal ridged by shrinking when dry, often creeping and rooted at base, young parts densely rusty scaly. Leaves alternate; petioles 3 – 8 mm, brown scaly; leaf blade papery, obovate to elliptic, 2.7–9(–12) × 1.2– 4 cm, base cuneate-attenuate, apex acuminate or acute, margin ± revolute, subentire or more often obtusely dentate above middle, glabrous adaxially, ± brown scaly abaxially, epunctate; lateral veins 12–28 pairs, with many shorter intercalated pairs and ramified copiously, marginal vein present or imperfect. Inflorescence subumbellate, 3 –7-flowered, in axils of leaves near apex of stem, brown scaly. Peduncle 1–3 cm. Pedicels 5 – 8 mm. Flowers white or tinged pink, 3 –3.5 mm. Calyx ca. 1.2 mm, split nearly to base; lobes ovate-triangular, ca. 1 mm, acute, ciliate, punctate or not. Corolla deeply lobed; lobes ovate, ca. 3 × 2 mm, ± acuminate, not punctate. Anthers ovate, 1.5–2 mm, apiculate, not punctate. Ovary glabrous; style ca. 3 mm; ovules 5 – 6, in 1 series on placenta. Fruit globose, ca. 5 mm in diam., from purple to black when mature.

Locality: Mount Parker, Wu Kau Tang, Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai. HK sheet 3009, 17726; L. T. Lo 430.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Taiwan, Fujian, Zhejiang, Jiangxi, Hunan, Sichuan; Vietnam, Thailand, Malaysia.
Ecology: Thin forests, valleys, stream banks. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.; fruiting: Oct.–Dec.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Cultivated in Fairview Park, Mai Po
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Ardisia elliptica Thunb. 東方紫金牛
Nov. Gen. Pl. 8: 119. 1798; Merr., Lingnan Sci. J. 11: 54. 1932; Larsen & C. M. Hu, Fl. Thailand, 6 (2): 128. 1996; FOC 15: 14. 1996, p.p. excl. syn. A. squamulosa Presl., A. kotoensis Hayata.
Ardisia litoralis Andr., Bot. Rep. T. 630. 1811; King & Gamble, J. Asiat. Soc. Bengal 74(2): 135. 1906.
Ardisia humilis auct. non Vahl (s. str.): Mez, Pflanzenr. IV. 236(Heft 9): 127, fig. 20: A–E. 1902.

Shrub or small tree, 1–3 m or occasionally up to 10 m tall, glabrous throughout; branchlets terete or slightly angular, greyish brown. Leaves alternate; petioles 10–15 mm; leaf blade subleathery, elliptic to obovate-oblong, 6 –12 × 2.5 –5 cm, base cuneate, apex bluntly acute to rounded, entire; glandular dots many, scattered, evident only with illumination or sometimes blackish and visible on both surfaces; lateral veins 13–18 pairs, with shorter and thinner intercalated pairs, invisible in fresh plants, ± prominent in dry state, usually not forming an uniform intramarginal vein. Inflorescence corymbose-racemose or subumbellate, (2–)4 – 8-flowered, in axils of normal leaves on upper part of branches, 3 – 8 cm including the peduncle. Pedicels 8 –15 mm. Flowers pink. Calyx ca. 3 mm, split to 2/3 of its length; lobes broadly ovate or orbicular, obtuse, thickly dotted with brown or black glands, margin ± scarious, distinctly ciliate. Corolla deeply lobed; lobes lanceolate, apex acuminate, with scattered purple glandular lines. Anthers lanceolate, ca. 5 mm, locellate, apiculate, punctate on back. Ovary glabrous; style ca. 6 mm; ovules many, in 3 series on placenta. Fruit slightly compressed globose, grey, with dark purple dots, 6 – 8 mm in diam.

Locality: Cultivated in Fairview Park, Mai Po. HK sheet 36156, 36197.
Distribution: Macau; India, Sri Lanka, Thailand, Indochina, Malay Peninsula, Indonesia, New Guinea.
Ecology: Along coasts behind mangroves. Flowering: Feb.–Apr.; fruiting: Sep.–Nov.

Ardisia faberi Hemsl. 月月紅
J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 26: 64. 1889; FRPS 58: 88. 1979.

Small shrub with creeping rhizomes. Stem ascending, up to 30 cm tall, densely rusty crisped villous when young. Leaves subverticillate or subopposite on the lower part of the stem; petioles 3– 8 mm, densely crisped villous; leaf blade papery, ovate- to lanceolate-elliptic or oblanceolate, 4–10 × 1.5 – 4 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate or acute, margin coarsely serrate, not glandular, crisped villous on both surfaces; lateral nerves 5 –9 pairs; marginal veins absent. Inflorescence in axils of reduced leaves or normal leaves, subumbellate, few flowered. Peduncle 1.5–2.5 cm, densely pilose. Pedicels 6–12 mm, crisped villous. Calyx split nearly to base, lobes linear-lanceolate, ca. 5 mm, densely villous. Corolla white to pink, deeply lobed; lobes broadly ovate, 4 –5 mm, ± glandular, glabrous, apex acute or obtuse. Anthers ovate, apiculate, not glandular on back. Ovary glabrous; ovules 5 – 6, in 1 series. Fruit globose, ca. 6 mm in diam., glabrous or puberulous, turning red when mature.

Locality: Tsing Yi. HK sheet 35864, 36113; Xing 8825 (IBSC).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Hubei, Guizhou, Sichuan, Yunnan.
Ecology: Evergreen forests, valleys and stream banks. Flowering: May–Jul.; fruiting: Nov.–Jan.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Mo Shan, Tai Po Kau, Wu Kau Tang, Sha Tau Kok
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Ardisia fordii Hemsl. 灰色紫金牛
J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 26: 64. 1889; FRPS 58: 56. 1979; Larsen & C. M. Hu, Fl. Thailand 6(2): 89. 1996; FOC 15: 27. 1996.
Embelia fordii Mez, Pflanzenr. IV. 236 (Heft 9): 326. 1902.

Small shrub, 30 – 60 cm tall; branches slender, terete, densely covered with rusty scales. Leaves alternate; petioles ca. 3 mm, rusty scaly; leaf blade papery, lanceolate or narrowly elliptic, 2.5 –5 × 1–1.6 cm, apex acute or subacuminate, tip blunt, cuneately tapering to the obtuse or rounded base, entire, abaxial surface with scattered rusty peltate scales; lateral veins many and fine, parallel, meeting in an intramarginal vein near edge. Inflorescence umbellate, with (1–)2 flowers, axillary on the upper part of branches or subterminal, glabrous or nearly so. Peduncle 2–5 mm. Pedicels 5–7 mm, flowers pink, ca. 4 mm. Calyx split almost to base; lobes ovate, ca. 1.5 mm long, acute or subobtuse, dotted with black glands, ciliolate. Corolla deeply lobed; lobes broadly ovate, acute, sparsely punctate. Anthers ovate apiculate, not punctate on back. Ovary glabrous; style equaling corolla-lobes; ovules ca. 5, in 1 series on placenta. Fruit globose, 5 – 6 mm in diam., deep red with black glandular dots.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Tai Po Kau, Wu Kau Tang, Sha Tau Kok. P. S. Choi 390, 514; Y. S. Lau 2813.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi; Thailand.
Ecology: Evergreen forest , stream banks, valleys. Flowering: Jun.–Aug.; fruiting: Oct.–Dec.
Notes: The species was reported as Ardisia affinis Hemsl. previously (Check List HK Plants 51. 1993).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Little Hong Kong, Cape D'Aguilar, Mount Nicholson, Wong Chuk Yeung, Sai Kung, Ma On Shan, Ng Tung Chai, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Ardisia hanceana Mez 郎傘樹（大羅傘樹）
Pflanzenr. IV. 236(Heft 9): 149. 1902; FKH 160. 1912; C. M. Hu, Bot. J. South China 1992: 6. 1992; FOC 15: 21. 1996, p.p. excl. syn. A. impressa H. R. Fletcher
Ardisia elegantissima H. Leveille, Feddes Repert. Sp. Nov. 10: 373. 1912.
Ardisia elegans auct. non Andr.: Walker, Philipp. J. Sci. 73: 110. 1940; FRPS 58: 66. 1979.

Shrub 1–3 m tall, glabrous except for inflorescence. Branches 20–50 cm, terete or slightly angulate on the upper part. Leaves alternate, ± evenly distributed on the upper 2/3 of branches; petioles channelled and marginate, 6–15 mm; leaf blade rigidly papery, oblong-lanceolate or sometimes elliptic-obovate, 7–12(–15) × 2– 4(–5) cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, margin coarsely crenate, with 4 – 8(–10) marginal glands on each side, abaxial surface ± minutely lepidote, often with very small pores, not punctate; lateral veins 12–15 pairs, slender, at an angle about 60˚ with the midvein, curved-ascending at a distance (ca. 4– 8 mm) from the edge, usually not forming an uniform intramarginal vein; veins invisible. Inflorescence compound-corymbose, glabrescent or minutely puberulous, terminal on branches. Peduncle 0.5 –2(–4) cm; primary rays 2.5 –5.5 cm, each bearing 5 –10 flowers. Pedicels 1–2 cm. Calyx 2–2.5 mm, split nearly to base; lobes ovate to oblong-ovate, acute or obtuse, usually broadest at base, scarcely punctate or with a few light brown glandular dots. Corolla pink, rarely white, 6 –7(– 8) mm, deeply lobed; lobes broadly ovate, ± acuminate, scarcely punctate or with a few orange glandular dots. Anthers ovate-lanceolate, ca. 5 mm, apiculate. Ovary glabrous; style 6–7 mm; ovules 5, in 1 series on placenta. Fruit globose, dark red or black when mature, 8 –10 mm in diam.

Locality: Little Hong Kong, Cape D'Aguilar, Mount Nicholson, Wong Chuk Yeung, Sai Kung, Ma On Shan, Ng Tung Chai, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island. HK sheet 3042, 17764, 31587; Y. S. Lau 1541; Y. W. Lam 505, 650.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Jiangxi, Hunan; Laos, Vietnam.
Ecology: Thin forests, valleys, stream banks. Flowering: Jun.–Jul.; fruiting: Dec.–Apr.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Hong Kong Island around 1850.

Ardisia lindleyana D. Dietr. 山血丹
Syn. Pl. 1: 617. 1839, excl. syn. Ardisia macrocarpa Wall.; C. M. Hu, Bot. J. South China 1992: 7. 1992; FOC 15: 19. 1996.
Ardisia punctata Lindl., Bot. Reg. 10: pl. 827. Sep. 1824, non Jack ex Wall. Mar–Jun. 1824; FHK 206. 1861; FKH 160. 1912; FRPS 58: 72. 1979.

Shrub, 0.5 –2 m tall, young parts and branchlets rusty puberulous. Leaves alternate; petioles 1–1.5 cm, densely rusty puberulous; leaf blade, ± leathery or rigidly papery, oblong to elliptic-lanceolate, rarely lanceolate, 7–18 × (1.2–)1.5– 4 cm, base cuneate or obtuse, apex acute or shortly acuminate, margin narrowly recurved, subentire or ± undulate due to the projecting marginal glands, adaxially glabrous, abaxially minutely tawny-puberulous, especially on the midvein, punctate, with bigger and denser glands along the margins; lateral veins 6–12 pairs, at an angle about 60˚ with the midvein, meeting in a conspicuous intramarginal vein 4– 8 mm apart from the edge; veins obscure. Inflorescence subumbellate, usually simple, 6–16-flowered, terminal on special flowering branches, subtended by 1–2(–3) reduced leaves or leaflike bracts. Pedicels 6 –12 mm, lengthening to 2.5 cm in fruit, rusty puberulous. Calyx 2–2.5 mm, split to base; lobes oblong-ovate, acute, puberulous or glabrescent sparsely punctate. Corolla white, deeply lobed; lobes oblong-elliptic, ca. 4.5 × 2.5mm, apex obtuse, with thick black-glands. Anthers lanceolate, ca. 3.8 mm, acute, black-punctate on back. Ovary glabrous; style ca. 3.5 mm; ovules 4 –5, in 1 series on placenta. Fruit globose, ca. 6 mm in diam., dark red when mature, black punctate.

Locality: Widely distributed in Hong Kong. HK sheet 3011, 34244; Y. S. Lau 2742; Y. W. Lam 1356.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Zhejiang; Vietnam.
Ecology: Thin forests and shrubby areas, mountain slopes. Flowering: May–Jul.; fruiting: Oct.–Dec.

Ardisia maclurei Merr. 心葉紫金牛
Philipp. J. Sci. Bot. 21: 351. 1922; H. L. Li, Woody Fl. Taiwan 714. 1963; FTW 3: 53. 1978; FRPS 58: 89. 1979; FOC 15: 25. 1996.
Ardisia sciophila Suzuki-tokio, J. Jap. Bot. 13: 507, fig. 1, 2. 1937.

Small shrub, 4 –15 cm tall. Stem erect or ascending from creeping rhizomes, densely rusty crisped villous when young. Leaves alternate, rarely almost whorled; petioles 0.5 –2.5 cm, rusty pilose; leaf blade papery, ovate- or oblong-elliptic, 4 – 6 × 2.5 –4 cm, base cordate, apex acute to obtuse, margin irregularly serrate, pilose on both surfaces, especially on the midvein; lateral veins ca. 6 pairs, prominent, ending in teeth. Inflorescence axillary from reduced leaves or normal leaves, subumbellate, rarely racemose, rusty-villous, 4 – 6-flowered. Peduncle 1– 4 cm. Bracts linear to narrowly lanceolate, 3–5 mm, pilose. Pedicels slender, 3–7 mm. Calyx split nearly to base; lobes lanceolate, ca. 3.5 mm, pilose on midvein or almost glabrous, margin ciliate, apex acuminate. Corolla white or pink , ca. 4 mm, deeply lobed; lobes ovate, ca. 2 mm broad, glabrous, sparsely punctate, apex acuminate. Anthers ovate, not punctate dorsally, apex acute. Ovary glabrous; style ca. 2.5 mm; ovules ca. 5, in 1 series on placenta. Fruit globose, ca. 6 mm in diam., glabrous, dark reddish when mature.

Locality: Tai Po Kau Nature Reserve. F. W. Xing 8875 (IBSC).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Taiwan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests of hillsides and valleys. Flowering: May–Jul.; fruiting: Dec.–May.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Po, Tai Mo Shan, Kap Lung
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Ardisia mamillata Hance 虎舌紅
J. Bot. 22: 290. 1884; FKH 160. 1912; FRPS 58: 84, pl. 13: 3– 4. 1979; FOC 15: 26. 1996.

Small shrub. Stem erect or ascending-erect from a creeping rhizome, 5–15 cm , rarely up to 25 cm, densely rusty pilose on young parts. Leaves alternate, often crowded towards apex of stem; petioles 5 –15(–18) mm, densely pilose; leaf blade papery, elliptic to obovate-elliptic, 7–14 × 3 –5 cm, base cuneate to obtuse or narrowly rounded, apex acute or obtuse, margin obscurely undulate-crenate, marginal glands inconspicuous, densely covered with rusty appressed hairs and black glandular dots on both surfaces; the hairs on adaxial surface rising from tuberculate processes, to 3 mm long; lateral veins 6 –9 pairs, slender, departing at an angle about 60˚ from the midvein; veins very fine. Inflorescence simple, subumbellate, 10–15-flowered, terminal on special flowering branches of 3– 8 cm long, with 1–2(–3) small leaves near apex. Pedicels 5–12 mm, densely rusty pilose. Calyx split to near base; lobes lanceolate, ca. 5 mm, sparsely pilose and punctate. Corolla pink or whitish, deeply lobed; lobes ovate-lanceolate, ca. 6 mm, apex acute, black-punctate. Anthers ovate-lanceolate, ca. 4 mm, apiculate. Ovary glabrous or nearly so; ovules many, in 3 series on placenta. Fruit globose, ca. 6 mm in diam., ± punctate, bright red when mature.

Locality: Tai Po, Tai Mo Shan, Kap Lung. Ford s.n. (GH); P. S. Choi 230; Y. W. Lam 1998.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Hunan, Guizhou, Sichuan, Yunnan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Evergreen forest, valleys, shady damp places. Flowering: Jun.–Jul.; fruiting: Nov.–Jan.
Uses: Ornamental.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Mount Parker, Sai Kung, Tai Po Kau, Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Ardisia primulifolia Gardn. & Champ. 蓮座紫金牛
Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 1: 324. 1849; FHK 207. 1861;FKH 159. 1912; FRPS 58: 86, pl. 13: 5. 1979; FOC 15: 25.1996.

Small subshrub. Stem almost absent or rarely up to 6 cm high. Leaves aggregate at apex of stem forming a rosette; petioles 2–5 mm, ± rusty pilose; leaf blade papery, elliptic to ellipticobovate, 7–17 × 3 –10 cm, base obtuse, apex rounded or rarely broadly acute, margin obscurely undulate-crenate, densely covered with rusty appressed long (3– 4 mm) hairs on adaxial surface and mainly on midvein and veins of abaxial surface, minutely punctate on both surfaces; lateral veins about 6 pairs, at an angle about 80˚ with the midvein, ramifying and curved-ascending at half way from the margin, with branches ending in marginal glands near the edge. Inflorescence terminal on a 3 –9(–15) cm long scape-like peduncle, arising from the leaf rosette, subumbellate, simple or compound, secondary rays (if present) 6 –10(–20) mm, each bearing 3 –5 flowers. Pedicels 5–9 mm, rusty pilose. Calyx split to near base; lobes lanceolate, 3.5 – 4 mm, rusty pilose at base and near margins, sparsely black-punctate. Corolla pink, deeply lobed; lobes  vate lanceolate, 4.5–5 × 2–3 mm, apex acute, black-punctate towards apex. Anthers ovate, ca. 2.5 mm, apiculate, punctate on back; style slender ca. 3 mm. Ovary glabrous; ovules 3 –5 in one series on placenta. Fruit globose, ca. 5 mm in diam., bright red when mature.

Locality: Mount Parker, Sai Kung, Tai Po Kau, Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai, Lantau Island. Champion s.n. (K); E. D. Merrill
11094; H. C. Tang 430; Y. S. Lau 2584.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Jiangxi, Hunan, Guizhou, Yunnan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Jun.–Jul.; fruiting: Nov.–May.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Victoria Peak, Hong Kong Island by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1849.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Mount Parker, Tai Po Kau, Lantau Island, Lamma Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Ardisia pusilla A. DC. 九節龍
Trans. Linn. Soc., London 17: 126. 1834; FKH 160. 1912; FRPS 58: 88. 1979; Larsen & C. M. Hu, Fl. Thailand, 6(2): 146.1996; FOC 15: 24. 1996.
Ardisia reptans Merr., Philipp. J. Sci. Bot. 5: 220. 1910.
Ardisia villosa Mez, Pflanzenr. IV. 236 (Heft 9): 152. 1902, non Roxb. (1824).

Small shrub, stem creeping at base, upper part ascendent, to 30 cm tall, densely covered with light brown crisped long hairs when young. Leaves opposite or subverticillate; petioles ca. 5 mm, villous; leaf blade papery, elliptic-ovate or obovate, 1.5 – 6.5 × 1–3.5 cm, base acute or rounded, apex broadly acute or obtuse, serrate or denticulate, adaxial surface sparsely strigose at least when young, abaxial surface strigose or mixed with long crisped hairs, with scattered minute orange glandular dots, especially along the margin; lateral veins 4–6(–8) pairs, prominent abaxially, ending in callose teeth; reticulation of veinlets conspicuous on both surfaces. Inflorescence umbellate, (1–)2– 4-flowered, pubescent or hirsute, in axils of reduced leaves. Peduncle slender, 1– 4 cm. Pedicels 4–10 mm. Calyx split nearly to base; lobes lanceolate, 2.5–3 mm, acuminate, pilose or glabrescent, indistinctly punctate. Corolla white or pink, 3– 4 mm, deeply lobed; lobes ovate or broadly ovate, acute, sparsely punctate. Anthers ovate, generally punctate on back. Ovary glabrous; style equaling corolla-lobes; ovules 6 –7, in 1 series on placenta. Fruit globose, ca. 5 mm in diam., red when mature, dotted with small dark glands.

Locality: Mount Parker, Tai Po Kau, Lantau Island, Lamma Island. HK sheet 3060, 17829, 36155.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Taiwan, Fujian, Jiangxi, Hunan, Guizhou, Sichuan; Korea, Japan, Philippines, Thailand.
Ecology: Evergreen forests, hillsides, stream banks. Flowering: May–Jul.; fruiting: Jul.–Dec.

Ardisia quinquegona Blume 羅傘樹
Bijdr. 689. 1826; FKH 160. 1912; FRPS 58: 54, pl. 8: 1–2. 1979; Larsen & C. M. Hu, Fl. Thailand 6(2): 91. 1996; FOC 15: 14. 1996.
Ardisia pauciflora Heyne ex Roxb., Fl. Ind. ed. Carey, 2: 279. 1824; FHK 206. 1861.

Shrub 1–2 m tall. Branchlets slender, ± dilated at insertion, weakly angulate and ± rusty scaly when young, becoming terete and smooth in age. Leaves papery; petioles channelled, 5–10 mm, initially lepidote; leaf blade oblong-elliptic to oblong-lanceolate, rarely oblanceolate 5 –16 × 2– 4 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, entire, adaxial surface dull green and glabrous, abaxial surface covered with appressed rusty scales; glandular dots many, pellucid, evident under transillumination; lateral veins many, very fine, nearly at right angle with the midvein, meeting in an intramarginal vein near edge; veinlets obscure. Inflorescence axillary or lateral, ± brown scaly, subumbellate, usually simple, rarely with 1–2 branches, often appearing a terminal lax panicle due to falling or lack of subtending leaves on lateral branches. Peduncle 1–3.5 cm; branches (if present) 4–8 mm, each bearing 3–8 subumbellate flowers. Pedicels 3–8 mm. Flowers white or pink, ca. 3 mm. Calyx ca. 1 mm, split nearly to base; lobes triangular-ovate, acute, glabrous, sparsely punctate and minutely ciliate. Corolla 2–2.5 mm, deeply lobed; lobes broadly elliptic-ovate, 1.25 –1.8 mm wide, acute, distinctly punctate with reddish or dark small glandular dots. Anthers ovate, ca. 1 mm, apiculate, scarcely punctate on back. Ovary glabrous; style ca. 2.5 mm; ovules many, in 2 series on placenta. Fruit typically compressed globose, 5 –7 m in diam., ± 5-angled, sometimes globose and without angles.

Locality: Widely distributed in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 1149, 1754, 2179.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Taiwan, Fujian, Sichuan; Vietnam, Thailand.
Ecology: Forests, hillsides and in valleys. Flowering: Mar.–Jun.; fruiting: Aug.–Feb.

Ardisia sieboldii Miq. 多枝紫金牛
Cat. Mus. Bot. Lugd.-Bat. 3: 190. 1867; H. L. Li, Woody Fl. Taiwan 709, fig. 291. 1963; FRPS 58: 50, pl. 6: 12–13. 1979; FOC 15: 14. 1996.

Shrub or small tree, to 10 m tall. Branchlets terete, finely wrinkled when dry, sparsely brownish lepidote near apex. Leaves alternate; petioles marginate, 5–10 mm; leaf blade subleathery, obovate to elliptic, 5 –8(–14) × 2.3–4(–5) cm, base cuneate, apex broadly to narrowly acute, tip blunt, margin entire, glabrous or sometimes minutely brown scaly on abaxial surface; lateral veins 12–18 pairs, slender, at an angle about 60˚ to the midvein, forming an intramarginal vein near edge. Inflorescences compound, subumbellate or cymose, axillary near end of branches. Peduncle 2–4(–7) cm, secondary branches 5–15 mm, each bearing 4– 6 subumbellate flowers. Pedicels ca. 5 mm, brown scaly. Flowers white, ca. 3 mm. Calyx united for 1/3 their length, lobes ca. 1.5 mm, ovate-triangular, acute, sparsely punctate. Corolla white, ca. 3 mm, deeply lobed; lobes broadly ovate, apex acute, inconspicuously punctate. Anthers ovate, apiculate, punctate on back. Ovary glabrous; style exserted before anthesis; ovules many, multiseriate. Fruit subglobose, red to blackish, 6–7 mm in diam.

Locality: Yeung Chau Island. HK sheet 3047.
Distribution: Fujian, Taiwan, Zhejiang.
Ecology: Thin forests near seashore. Flowering: Mar.–Jun.; fruiting: Jan.–Apr.
Notes: The species was reported as Ardisia obtusa Mez previously (Check List HK Plants 51. 1993).

Ardisia villosa Roxb. 雪下紅
Fl. Ind. 2: 274. 1824; FRPS 58: 83, pl. 13: 1. 1979; FOC 15: 25. 1996.
Ardisia dumetosa Tutch., Rep. Bot. & For. Dep. Hongkong 1914: 33. 1915.

Small shrub, 30 –100 cm tall. Stem erect, densely rusty villose-tomentose when young. Leaves alternate; petioles 5–10 mm, rusty villose; leaf blade papery, elliptic to elliptic-lanceolate, rarely oblanceolate, (4 –)7–15 × 2.5 –5 cm, base cuneate, apex acute or shortly acuminate, margin narrowly recurved, subentire or slightly notched at the marginal glands, adaxial surface glabrous except for the puberulous midvein, abaxial surface rusty villose especially on the midvein, black-punctate on both surfaces; lateral veins 12–16 pairs, at an angle about 60˚ with the midvein, ending in marginal glands and forming an irregular intramarginal vein near the edge; veins very fine, conspicuous on abaxial surface. Inflorescence subumbellate, simple or compound, 6–12-flowered, densely rusty villose, terminal on leafy or leafless specialized branches or rarely lateral on main stem. Peduncle 5 –20(– 40) mm; secondary rays (if present) 4 – 8 mm, each bearing 3 –5 flowers. Pedicels 5 –10 mm. Calyx split to near base; lobes oblong lanceolate, ca. 4 mm, apex ± obtuse, villose on both surfaces. Corolla pink or white, deeply lobed; lobes ovate, ca. 4 mm, acute, black-punctate. Anthers ovate-lanceolate, ca. 3 mm, ± punctate on back. Ovary ovoid; style ca. 4.5 mm, ± puberulous at base; ovules ca. 5, in 1 series on placenta. Fruit globose, 5–7 mm in diam., dark red or blackish when mature.

Locality: Fanling, Sheung Shui. HK sheet 17752, 17860.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Taiwan; Mynamar, Thailand, West Malaysia , Vietnam.
Ecology: Thin forests and thickets, on mountain slopes and valleys. Flowering: Apr.–Jul.; fruiting: Feb.–Jul.

Embelia laeta (L.) Mez 酸藤子
Pflanzenr. IV. 236(Heft 9): 326. 1902; FRPS 58: 120, pl. 19: 4. 1979; FOC 15: 31. 1996.
Samara laeta L., Mant. Pl. (ed. 2) 199. 1771.
Samara obovata Benth., FHK 205. 1861.
Embelia obovata (Benth.) Hemsl., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 26: 62. 1889; FKH 159. 1912.

Scandent shrub or climber, 1–3 m or longer. Branches glabrous, ± wrinkled when dry, lenticellate. Leaves alternate; petioles 5 – 10 mm, glabrous; leaf blade papery, obovate to oblong-obovate, 2.5 –5(–7) × 0.8 –2(–2.8) cm, base cuneate, apex subrounded to obtuse, sometimes emarginate, margin entire, glabrous, deep green adaxially, greyish green abaxially, not punctate; lateral nerves 6 –10(–12) pairs, at an angle about 50˚ with midrib, obliquely ascending, anastomosing near edge; veins very fine but conspicuous on both surfaces. Inflorescence lateral or axillary, racemose, 3– 8 mm, 3 – 8-flowered, ± glandular puberulous. Bracts ovate, ca. 1 mm, ciliolate. Pedicels 1.5 –2 mm. Flowers white, 4-merous, functionally unisexual, but bear vestigial organs of the opposite sex. Calyx 0.6 –0.8 mm, split to 2/3 of its length; lobes ovate, acute. Corolla-lobes almost free, ovate to oblong-ovate, 1.8 –2 mm, obtuse, glabrous outside, densely papillose adaxially, obscurely punctate. In male flowers, stamens comparatively larger, inserted on base of corolla-lobes, with filaments ca. equaling corolla-lobes; ovary much reduced, without ovules. In female flowers, ovary glabrous, pyriform, with well developed ovules; stamens much reduced. Fruit globose, ca. 5 mm in diam., obscurely punctate.

Locality: Widely distributed in Hong Kong. HK sheet 17698; H. C. Tang 115, 785.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Taiwan, Fujian, Jiangxi, Yunnan; Laos, Vietnam.
Ecology: Margin of forest, shrubby mountain slopes, roadsides. Flowering: Dec.–Mar.; fruiting: Apr.–Jun.

Embelia parviflora Wall. ex A. DC 當歸藤
Trans. Linn. Soc. London 17: 130. 1834; FRPS 58: 113, pl. 17: 5 –7. 1979; FOC 15: 31. 1996.
Embelia myrtifolia Hemsl. & Mez, Notizbl. Bot. Gart. Berlin 3: 107. 1901; FKH 159. 1912.

Scandent shrub or climber, up to 3 m or longer. Branches light brown, with scattered elongate lenticelles; branchlets slender, usually distichous, densely rusty villose, with ± glandular or stellate-tipped hairs. Leaves distichous; petioles 0.5–1 mm, villose; leaf blade papery, ovate to oblong-ovate, ovate, 1–2 × 0.6 –1 cm, base rounded or subtruncate, apex obtuse to broadly obtuse, entire, adaxial surface glabrous, abaxial surface ± puberulous, especially on the raised midvein; glandular dots many, visible on both surfaces when dry; lateral veins fine and very obscure. Inflorescence axillary, subumbellate or cymose, 2–4-flowered, rusty puberulous. Peduncle 1–1.5 mm. Pedicels 2–4 mm. Flowers white, 5-merous. Calyx 0.5 –0.8 mm, split to near base; lobes ovate-triangular, acute, minutely ciliate. Corolla slightly united at base; lobes oblong or oblong-elliptic, 1.5 –2 × 1 mm, obtuse, densely papillose on margins and inside. Stamens in male flowers inserted on the lower 1/3 of the corolla-lobes; filaments ca. 1 mm; anthers ovoid. In female flowers ovary ovoid, glabrous; style twice as long as the ovary, ± pubescent at base; stigma flattened or disc-shaped. Fruit globose, ca. 5 mm in diam., dark reddish, ± punctate.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. HK sheet 17670.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Zhejiang, Guizhou, Yunnan; India, Myanmar, Vietnam.
Ecology: Thin forests and shrubby areas. Flowering: Dec.–May; fruiting: Jan.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Embelia ribes N. L. Burman 白花酸藤子
Fl. Ind. 62, pl. 23. 1768; FHK 204. 1861; FKH 159. 1912; FRPS 58: 104, pl. 16: 4 – 6. 1979; Larsen & C. M. Hu, Fl. Thailand 6(2): 154. 1996; FOC 15: 32. 1996.

Scandent shrub or climber, usually 3 – 6 m or longer. Branchlets slender, new growth under the inflorescence minutely puberulous, soon becoming glabrous. Leaves alternate; petioles 5 –10 mm; leaf blade obovate-elliptic to oblong-elliptic, 4 – 8(–10) × 1.2–3 cm, base cuneate or rounded, apex shortly acuminate, tip blunt, margin entire, slightly recurved, glabrous; glandular dots many, scattered, black or colorless, ± convex when dry; lateral veins many; reticulation of veins distinct on abaxial surfaces when dry. Panicle terminal, 10 –20 cm, with a spread of 10 –18 cm cm at base, densely puberulous, 2–3-branched; secondary branches slender, each bearing many racemosely arranged flowers. Pedicels 1–2 mm. Flowers greenish or whitish, 5- rarely 4-merous, functionally unisexual, but bear vestigial organs of the opposite sex. Calyx ca. 0.5 mm, split about to middle; lobes triangular, acute or obtuse, densely puberulous. Corolla-lobes almost free, elliptic, ca. 1.5 –2 mm, with a few glandular dots, densely papillose outside. In male flowers, stamens adnate ± to middle of corolla-lobes and slightly shorter than them; anthers ovoid or oblong, punctate on back; ovary highly reduced and lack ovules. In female flowers, pistil fully developed, slightly shorter than corolla-lobes, with ovoid glabrous ovary and capitate stigma on a short style; stamens much reduced. Fruit globose, 3– 4 mm in diam., reddish or black, wrinkled when dry.

Locality: Widely distributed in Hong Kong; H. C. Tang 11, 2321; Y. S. Lau 924, 1353.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang; widely distributed in India, Sri Lanka, Myanmar, Thailand, Indochina, southwards through Malay Peninsula to Indonesia and New Guinea.
Ecology: Open thickets and disturbed evergreen forest. Flowering: Jan.–Jul.; fruiting: May–Dec.

Embelia rudis Hand.-Mazz. 網脈酸藤子
Akad. Wiss. Wien, Math.-Naturwiss. Kl., Anz. 59: 108. 1922; H. L. Li, Woody Fl Taiwan 717. 1963; FRPS 58: 108. 1979; FOC 15: 33. 1996, pro syn. sub E. vestita Roxb.

Scandent shrub, to 10 m or longer. Branchlets glabrous, copiously lenticellate. Leaves alternate, subleathery; petioles 6–8 mm, marginate, ± puberulous; leaf blade oblong-ovate to ovate, rarely broadly lanceolate, 5–10 × 2–4 cm, base rounded or obtuse, rarely cuneate, apex acute or acuminate, margin finely or coarsely serrate, glabrous, sparsely and indistinctly punctate; lateral veins many, ending to the teeth; reticulation of veins prominent, raised on both surfaces. Inflorescence racemose, axillary, 1–2(–3) cm, puberulous. Pedicels 2–3(–5) mm; bracteoles subulate, ca. 1 mm, papillose. Flowers greenish or white, 5-merous, 1–2 mm. Calyx united at base; lobes ovate, ca. 0.7 mm, ciliate. Corollalobes almost free, ovate-oblong or elliptic, 1–2 mm, apex obtuse or rounded, ciliate, puberulous or papillose in middle and especially near the base adaxially. Stamens in male flowers ca. equaling corolla-lobes; anthers oblong or ovate, punctate on back. In female flowers ovary pear-shaped or globose, glabrous; style ca. 0.5 mm, curved. Fruit globose, 4–5 mm in diam., blue black or reddish when mature.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Lantau. Y. W. Lam 1397; P. S. Choi 343, 492; H. C. Tang 2231; F. W. Xing 7092, 8192 (IBSC).
Distribution: Guangdong, Taiwan, Fujian, Zhejiang, Jiangxi, Hunan, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Yunnan.
Ecology: Forests and shrubby areas. Flowering: Oct.–Dec.; fruiting: Apr.–Jul.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Little Hong Kong, Mount Nicholson, Sheung Wo Hang, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Embelia undulata (Wall.) Mez 平葉酸藤子
Pflanzenr. IV. 236(Heft 9): 327. 1902; FOC 15: 33. 1996.
Myrsine undulata Wall., Fl. Ind. 2: 299. 1824.
Samara longifolia Benth., FHK 205. 1861.
Embelia longifolia (Benth.) Hemsl., J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 26: 62. 1889; FKH 159. 1912; Anonymous, Check List HK Plants 51. 1993.

Scandent shrub, rarely arborescent, 2– 4 m tall. Branchlets terete, glabrous, ± lenticellate-warty. Leaves alternate; petioles 1–1.5(– 2) cm, deeply channelled, black punctate; leaf blade papery to subleathery, elliptic to oblong, or rarely obovate, (4 –)7.5 –11.5(–18) × (1.8 –)3 –5(– 8) cm, base acute or cuneate, decurrent on petiole, apex acute or acuminate, rarely rounded, margin entire, glabrous, with many minute black glandular dots or lines on abaxial surface; lateral veins many, prominent. Inflorescence racemose, 1–2(– 6) cm, usually rising from axils of leaf scars on branches of previous year's growth, puberulent. Flowers yellowish or greenish, 4-merous. Pedicels 1.5 –3 mm. Calyx less than 1 mm, deeply split; lobes triangular or ovate, black punctate. Corolla-lobes almost free, elliptic to ovate, apex obtuse or acute, red punctate abaxially. Stamens inserted at base of corolla-lobes and exserted up to 1 mm, staminodes ca. 2/3 petal length; anthers narrowly oblong, ca. 1 mm. Ovary globose, glabrous; style straight, epunctate; stigma capitate. Fruit globose, (8 –)10 –15 mm in diam., longitudinally ribbed, black punctate.

Locality: Little Hong Kong, Mount Nicholson, Sheung Wo Hang, Lantau Island. HK sheet 2970, 17667; Y. W. Lam 1281.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian, Jiangxi, Hunan, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Yunnan; India, Nepal.
Ecology: Evergreen forests and shrubby areas. Flowering: Apr.–Aug.; fruiting: Nov.–Jan.

Embelia vestita Roxb. 密齒酸藤子
Fl. Ind. 2: 288. 1824; FOC 15: 33. 1996, p.p. excl. syn. E. rudis Hand.-Mazz.
Embelia oblongifolia Hemsl., J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 26: 62. 1882; FKH 159. 1912; FRPS 58: 110, pl. 17: 1–3. 1979.

Scandent shrub or climber, to 10 m or longer. Branchlets glabrous or puberulous; old branches copiously lenticellate. Leaves alternate; petioles 5–10 m, with narrow crisped wings on distal part; leaf blade papery, oblong-elliptic to oblong-ovate or elliptic-lanceolate, 6–10 × 2–3.5 cm, base rounded or obtuse, apex acute, margin usually remotely serrate on upper half or near apex, rarely entire, glabrous and glossy, not punctate or with minute glands near apex on abaxial surface; lateral veins 10–18 pairs, with shorter intermediates, at an angle about 70˚ with the midvein, curved-ascending, anastomosing near the edge; reticulation of veins prominent on both surfaces. Inflorescence axillary, racemose, 1–3 cm, rusty puberulous. Pedicels 3–4 mm, patent, usually at right angle to the rachis. Flowers 5-merous, greenish or white, 2.5–3 mm. Calyx deeply split; lobes broadly ovate, 0.5–0.7 mm, ciliate, sparsely and minutely punctate, glabrous or nearly so. Corolla-lobes almost free, oblong or oblong-lanceolate, ca. 1 mm wide, broadly obtuse or slightly emarginate, glabrous abaxially, densely papillose adaxially, dotted with brown glands. Stamens in male flowers adnate to base of corolla-lobes; anthers ovate, punctate on back. In female flowers ovary pyriforms, glabrous, with a short, curved style. Fruit globose, 6–8 mm in diam., red when mature, ± punctate.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. HK sheet 17686, 25195, 30556; Y. S. Lau 1746.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Hunan, Guizhou, Yunnan; Laos, Vietnam.
Ecology: Margin of forests, shrubby mountain slopes. Flowering: Oct.–Dec.; fruiting: Oct.–Jul.

Maesa japonica (Thunb.) Moritzi & Zoll. 杜莖山
Syst. Verz. 3: 61.1855; FRPS 58: 27.1979; FOC 15: 7. 1996.
Doraena japonica Thunb., Nov. Gen. Pl. 3: 59. 1783; Fl. Jap. 84. 1784.
Maesa coriacea Champ. ex Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 4: 300. 1852; FHK 204. 1861.
Maesa doraena Blume ex Sieb. & Zucc., Abh. Bayer. Akad. Wiss. Math.-Phys. 4: 138. 1846; FKH 158. 1912.

Shrub 1–3(–5) m tall, glabrous throughout; branchlets wrinkled with longitudinal lines when dry, sparsely lenticellate. Leaves alternate; petioles channelled, 6–12 mm; leaf blade generally elliptic but variable from elliptic-lanceolate to obovate or oblong-ovate, (5–)7–12(–15) × 2–4(–5) cm, base cuneate to obtuse or sometimes rounded, apex acuminate or acute, subentire or remotely serrate with callose teeth, leathery, without veinlike glandular lines; lateral veins 5–8 pairs, curved-ascending, ending in the teeth; reticulation of veins very fine, but visible on both surfaces. Inflorescence axillary, solitary or sometimes 2–3 together, 1–3(–4) cm, racemose or with a few branches near base. Pedicels 2–3 mm, with a pair of minute bracteoles near apex. Calyx ca. 2 mm, split to middle; lobes ovate to orbicular, apex obtuse or rounded, distinctly glandular striate. Corolla white, tubular-campanulate; tube 3.5–4 mm, glandular striate; lobes ca. 1/3 length of tube, ovate or reniform, apex obtuse or rounded, ± spreading. Stamens adnate to upper part of corolla-tube, included; anthers oblong or ovate, as long as filaments. Ovary conical; style slender, ca. equaling calyx; stigma lobed. Fruit globose, 4–5 mm in diam., fleshy, with longitudinal glandular lines.

Locality: Widely distributed in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 56, 1078, 1174; P. S Choi 364; Y. W. Lam 510.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan, Zhejiang, Jiangxi, Anhui, Hunan, Hubei, Sichuan, Guizhou, Yunnan; Japan, Vietnam.
Ecology: Thin forests and thickets on hillsides. Flowering: Jan.–Mar.; fruiting: Oct.–May.
Notes: Flowers of this species are functionally unisexual, but with limited sexual dimorphism; the staminate flowers possess carpels with aborted ovules, and the pistillate flowers have degenerate stamens that lack pollens. The type specimen of Maesa coriacea was collected from Hong Kong Island by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1850.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan, Sha Tau Kok
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Maesa montana A. DC. 金珠柳
Prodr. 8: 79. 1844; FHK 204. 1861; FRPS 58: 18. 1979; FOC 15: 3. 1996.
Maesa indica auct. non (Rox.) A. DC.: FHK 203. 1861.
Maesa tenera auct. non Mez: FKH 158. 1912.

Shrubs or small trees, 2–3(–10) m high; branchlets generally sparsely pilose or puberulent, sometimes glabrous, with scattered lenticels when mature. Leaves alternate; petioles channelled, 5 –10 mm; leaf blade oblong-elliptic to oblong-lanceolate, rarely broadly ovate, 7–16 × 3 –7 cm, base cuneate or obtuse, apex acute or acuminate, coarsely serrate or undulate-dentate, with callose teeth, firmly papery, adaxial surface glabrous, abaxial surface glabrescent or occasionally sparingly hirsute, especially on veins; glandular nervilliform lines invisible or sometimes evident; lateral veins 8–12 pairs, curved-ascending, ending to the teeth; veinlets not evident. Inflorescence axillary, racemose or paniculate, 2–7(–10) cm, sparingly hirtellous or puberulent. Bracts lanceolate, ca. 1 mm. Pedicels 1–2(–3) mm, with a pair of minute ovate or lanceolate bracteoles at apex. Calyx split a little below middle; lobes ovate, ca. 0.6 mm, obtuse, minutely ciliate. Corolla white, lobed to middle; lobes broadly ovate or suborbicular, ca. 1 m wide, apex obtuse or rounded, entire or slightly crenulate. Stamens adnate to middle of corolla-tube, included; anthers suborbicular, ca. 0.25 mm, equaling filaments. Pistil slightly longer than calyx; stigma minutely bilobed. Fruit globose or ovoid, 2.5 – 4 mm in diam.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan, Sha Tau Kok. F. W. Xing 8212, 8468 (IBSC).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan, Sichuan, Guizhou, Yunnan, SE Xizang; India, Myanmar, Thailand, Vietnam.
Ecology: Thickets and thin forests, hillsides and stream banks. Flowering: Feb.–Apr.; fruiting: Oct.–Dec.

Maesa perlarius (Lour.) Merr. 鯽魚膽
Trans. Amer. Philos. Soc., n. ser. 24. 298. 1935; FRPS 58: 25. 1979; K. Larsen & C. M. Hu, Fl. Thailand 6(2): 173. 1996; FOC 15: 6. 1996.
Dartus perlarius Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 124. 1790.
Maesa tonkinensis Mez, Pflanzenr. IV. 236 (Heft 9): 30. 1902.
Maesa sinensis A. DC., Ann. Sci. Nat., Bot., ser. 2, 16: 80. 1841; FHK 203. 1861; FKH 158. 1912.

Shrub 1–3 m high; branchlets hirtellous or pubescent. Leaves alternate; petioles channelled, 5–10 mm; leaf blade elliptic to ellipticlanceolate, 7–11 × 3–5 cm, base cuneate, apex acute or abruptly acuminate, coarsely serrate except for a short distance near base, papery, adaxial surface hirsute or pilose when young, rapidly becoming glabrous except midvein, abaxial surface hirsute, especially on veins; lateral veins 7–9 pairs, raised abaxialy, curved-ascending, ending to the callose teeth. Inflorescence axillary, racemose or paniculate (with 2–3 branches near base), hirtellous or pubescent, 1–5 cm. Pedicels 1.5–2 mm, with a pair of small ovate bracteoles at apex. Calyx ca. 1 mm, split below middle; lobes ovate, acute, ciliate, puberulous abaxially. Corolla white, ca. 2 mm, lobed to middle; lobes broadly ovate to suborbicular, obtuse, with brown glandular lines. Stamens inserted on the upper part of corolla-tube; anthers broadly ovate to reniform, not punctate. Ovary glabrous; style ca. 0.75 mm; stigma obscurely 4-lobed. Fruit globose, ca. 3 mm in diam., striate from the elongated vertical glands.

Locality: Widely distributed in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 32, 520; E. D. Merrill 10961; Lei 356; Xing 7144 (IBSC).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Taiwan, Guizhou, Yunnan; Vietnam, Thailand.
Ecology: Margins of forests and shrubby areas. Flowering: Mar.–Apr.; fruiting: Dec.–May.

Myrsine seguinii H. Léveillé 密花樹
Fl. Kouy-Tcheou 288. 1915; FOC 15: 37. 1996.
Myrsine neriifolia Sieb. & Zucc., Abh. Math.-Phys. Cl. Konigl. Bayer. Akad. Wiss. 4: 137. 1846, non Casarato (1843).
Rapanea neriifolia (Sieb. & Zucc.) Mez, Pflanzenr. IV. 236(Heft 9): 361.1902.
Myrsine capitellata auct. non Wall.: FHK 205. 1861; FKH 158. 1912.

Shrubs or small trees, 2–7 m, occasionally to 15 m tall. Branches somewhat thick, greyish brown to dark brown, glabrous, wrinkled when dry. Leaves spirally arranged; petioles subterete, 0.9–1.5 mm; leaf blade leathery, narrowly oblong to oblong-lanceolate, 5–15 × 1.3 –3 cm, apex acute or obtuse, base cuneate, entire, narrowly recurved, glabrous, with many tiny sunken pits on abaxial surface; lateral veins usually more than 15 pairs, inconspicuous, meeting in an intramarginal vein near edge. Inflorescence umbellate, terminal on short verrucose spurs, 3 –10-flowered. Pedicels rather thick, 1– 4 mm. Flowers white to light green, sometimes reddish. Calyx-lobes ovate, ca. 1 mm, obtuse or acute, fused at base, ciliate, sparsely punctate or not. Corolla 2.5–3 mm; lobes split to 3/4 of its length, lobes ovate to elliptic, acute or obtuse, punctate, densely papillose along the margin. Stamens adnate about to the base of corolla-lobes; filaments very short; anthers ovate, ca. 1.2 mm. Ovary glabrous; stigma as long as or longer than corolla-lobes, cylindric at base, upper part ± flattened, sometimes split at apex. Fruit subglobose, 4–5 mm in diam., punctate.

Locality: Widely distributed in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 984, 2884; L. T. Lo 594; H. C. Tang 12244.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Taiwan, Fujian, Zhejiang, Anhui, Jiangxi, Hunan, Hubei, Sichuan, Yunnan, SE Xizang; Japan, Vietnam, Myanmar, Thailand.
Ecology: Thickets and disturbed evergreen forests. Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: Oct.–Dec.

Anagallis arvensis L. 琉璃繁縷
Sp. Pl. 148. 1753; FKH 157. 1912; FRPS 59(1): 136, pl. 36: 1– 4. 1989; FOC 15: 79. 1996.

Annual or biennial glabrous herb, 10 –30 cm tall. Stems quadrangular, erect or ascendent from the decumbent base. Leaves decussate, sessile; leaf blade ovate to narrowly ovate, 7–18(–25) × 3–12(–15) mm, base subrounded, apex obtuse or acute, margin entire. Flowers solitary in axils of upper leaves. Pedicels slender, 2–3 cm, recurved in fruiting. Calyx 3.5–6 mm, divided nearly to the base; lobes linear lanceolate, margin membranous. Corolla rotate, reddish, divided nearly to base; lobes obovate, 4–6 × 2.7–3 mm. Stamens included; filaments puberulous. Capsule globose, ca. 3.5 mm in diam.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 4335.
Distribution: Guangdong, Fujian, Taiwan, Zhejiang; temperate Asia, Indian Subcontinent, Europe, N Africa.
Ecology: Cultivated areas, wastelands, roadsides. Flowering: Mar.–Apr.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Shing Mun, Ma On Shan
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Lysimachia alpestris Champ. ex Benth. 香港過路黃
Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 4: 299. 1852; FHK 202. 1861; FKH 157. 1912; FGD 1: 552. 1987; FRPS 59(1): 98, pl. 26: 5. 1989; FOC 15: 56. 1996.

Perennial herb, stiffy hairy throughout. Stem extremely abbreviated, 1–4 cm tall, often emitting runners. Leaves subsessile, spirally arranged, ± forming a rosette on stems and apex of runners; leaf blade spathulate to narrowly oblanceolate, 3 –6 × 0.6–1.5 cm, apex rounded and mucronate, tapering toward base. Flowers solitary, axillary. Pedicels ca. as long as to slightly longer than leaves. Calyx lobes lanceolate, 5– 6 × 2 mm, apex acute. Corolla yellow, deeply parted; tube 1–1.5 mm; lobes obovate-elliptic, 4–15 mm wide, apex rounded, erose. Filaments ca. 3 mm, connate into a tube at base; anthers dorsifixed, opening by lateral slits.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Shing Mun, Ma On Shan. Y. W. Lam 1449, 230; C. P. Choi 460.
Distribution: Outside Hong Kong only found in Gu Dou Shan (Xin Hui Xian) of Guangdong province.
Ecology: Damp places on banks of streams, secondary forests and thickets. Flowering: Apr.–May.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: The type specimen was collected from Victoria Peak by J. G. Champion around 1850. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Lysimachia candida Lindl. 澤珍珠菜
J. Hort. Soc. London 1: 301. 1846; FKH 157. 1912; FGD 1: 552. 1987; FRPS 59 (1): 127. 1989; FOC 15: 77. 1996.

Annual or biennial glabrous herb, 10–30 cm tall. Stems erect, simple or branched from base. Basal leaves spatulate to oblanceolate, 2.6–6 × 0.5–2 cm, with winged petioles, usually withered before anthesis; stem leaves alternate, rarely subopposite, sessile or subsessile; leaf blade obovate to oblanceolate or linear, 1–5 × 0.2–1.2 cm, base attenuate, apex acuminate to obtuse, with sparse black or reddish glandular dots on both surfaces. Racemes terminal, initially short and coniform, lengthening to 5 –10 cm in fruiting. Bracts linear, 4 – 6 mm. Pedicels ca. two times as long as bracts, the lowest to 1.5 cm. Calyx lobes lanceolate, 3–5 mm, with black glandular stripes abaxially, margin membranous. Corolla white, 6 –12 mm, divided to middle; lobes oblong to oblong-obovate, apex rounded. Stamens slightly shorter than corolla lobes; anthers dorsifixed, opening by lateral slits. Capsule subglobose, 2–3 mm in diam.

Locality: So Kon Po. HK sheet 2834.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Anhui, Shandong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Myanmar, Vietnam.
Ecology: Cultivated areas, banks of ditches, rice paddies and other wet places. Flowering: Mar.–Jun.
Uses: Ornamental.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tsat Muk Kiu, Luk Keng, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Lysimachia decurrens Forst. f. 延葉珍珠菜
Fl. Ins. Austr. 12. 1786; FKH 157. 1912; FGD 1: 552, fig. 633. 1987; FRPS 59(1): 120. 1989; FOC 15: 73. 1996; C. M. Hu, Fl. Thailand 7(1): 161. 1999.

Perennial herb, 40–90 cm tall, glabrous throughout. Stems erect, with raised lines descending from the base of leaf petioles, usually much branched. Leaves alternate; petioles 1–4 cm, narrowly winged; leaf blade lanceolate to elliptic lanceolate, 6–13 × 1.5– 4 cm, base cuneate, apex acute or acuminate, with scattered black glandular dots or short stripes on both surfaces, especially near margins. Racemes terminal, 10 –25 cm. Bracts subulate, 2–3 mm. Pedicels 2–9 mm, lengthening to 10 –18 mm in fruit. Calyx split nearly to base; lobes narrowly lanceolate, 3 – 4 mm, glandular ciliate, with black glandular stripes abaxially. Corolla white or tinged purple; tube ca. 1.5 mm; lobes oblong-spathulate, 1–2.5 mm, apex rounded. Stamens long-exserted; anthers ovoid, purple, ca. 1 mm. Ovary ovoid; style slender, ca. 5 mm. Capsule globose or slightly compressed, 3– 4 mm in diam.

Locality: Tsat Muk Kiu, Luk Keng, Lantau Island. K. Y. Tam 141; Y. W. Lam 664; L. T. Lo 55.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; Indochina, Indian Subcontinent, Malesia, Pacific Islands.
Ecology: Margins of forests, damp places by streams, wastelands near villages. Flowering: Apr.–May.

Lysimachia fortunei Maxim. 紅根草
Bull. Acad. Imp. Sci. Saint-Petersbourg 12: 68. 1868; FKH 157. 1912; FGD 1: 551, fig. 632. 1987; FRPS 59(1): 104, pl. 27: 6 –10. 1989; FOC 15: 71. 1996.

Perennial glabrous herb, with creeping, reddish rhizomes. Stems erect, 30 –70 cm tall, terete, usually unbranched, with black glandular dots. Leaves alternate, subsessile; leaf blade oblong-lanceolate to narrowly elliptic, 4 –11 × 1–2.5 cm, base attenuate, apex shortly acuminate, with many scattered glandular dots on both surface when dry. Racemes slender, 10–20 cm. Bracts lanceolate, 2–3 mm. Pedicels as long as to slightly shorter than bracts. Calyx lobes ovate-elliptic, ca. 1.5 mm, apex obtuse, margin membranous. Corolla white, ca. 3 mm, divided slightly below middle; lobes elliptic to ovate-elliptic, with black glandular dots, apex rounded. Stamens included; filaments adnate to base of corolla lobes; anthers dorsifixed, opening by lateral slits. Capsule globose, 2–2.5 mm in diam.

Locality: Pok Fu Lam. HK sheet 2832.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Korea, Japan, Vietnam.
Ecology: Margins of forests, banks of rice paddies and other wet places. Flowering: Jun.–Aug.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Rourea microphylla (Hook. & Arn.) Planch. 小葉紅葉藤（紅葉藤）
Linnaea 23: 421. 1850; FHK 71. 1861; FKH 70. 1912; FHN 3: 112, fig. 608. 1974; FFJ 2: 338, fig. 184. 1984; FRPS 38: 140, pl. 25: 1 – 8. 1986; FGD 4: 280. 2000; FOC 9: 437. 2003.
Connarus microphyllus Hook. & Arn., Bot. Beech. Voy. 179. 1833.
Santaloides microphyllum G. Schellenb., Pflanzenr. 103: 130. 1938.
Rourea minor subsp. microphylla (Hook. & Arn.) Vidal, Fl. Cambodge, Laos & Vietnam 2: 28. 1962.

Climbing shrub, 1 – 4 m, many-branched. Branchlets glabrous or sparsely pubescent when young. Petioles, rachis, and petiolules glabrous; leaflets 7 – 17( – 27), papery to thinly leathery, ovate or lanceolate to oblong-lanceolate, 1.2 – 5.5 × 0.5 – 2 cm, base cuneate to rounded, often oblique, apex obtuse and acuminate, glabrous on both surfaces, slightly glaucous abaxially; petiolule 2 mm. Inflorescences in axillary clusters, usually 3 – 6 cm, central one often longer, many-flowered; peduncles and pedicels slender. Flowers 4 – 5 mm in diam., fragrant. Sepals ovate, 2.5 × 2 mm, ciliolate. Petals elliptic, white, pale yellow or pink, 5 × 1.5 mm. Stamens 10, unequal, longer ones to 6 mm, shorter ones ca. 4 mm. Carpels free, 3 – 5 mm. Follicle red when mature, cylindric or obliquely obovoid-cylindric, slightly curved or straight, 1 – 1.5 × 0.5 cm, longitudinally striate. Seed orange, oblong, ca. 1 cm, with membranous aril at base.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. P. S. Choi 283; Y. S. Lau 1273.
Distribution: Yunnan, Guangxi, Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian; India, Sri Lanka, Vietnam, Indonesia.
Ecology: Hillslopes or forests. Flowering: Mar. – Sep.; fruiting: May – Mar. of following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Aberdeen, Hoi Ha, Chek Keng, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Rourea minor (Gaertn.) Alston 大葉紅葉藤（牛栓藤）
Fl. Ceylon 6(2): 67. 1931; Li., Woody Fl. Taiwan 329, fig. 114. 1963; FRPS 38: 142, pl. 26: 4 – 6. 1986; FGD 4: 281, fig. 166. 2000; FOC 9: 437. 2003.
Aegiceras minus Gaertn., Fruct. 1: 216, fig. 46. 1788.
Rourea santaloides Wight & Arn., Prodr. Fl. Ind. Orient. 1: 144. 1834; FHK 71. 1861; FHN 3: 112. 1974.
Rourea millettii Planch., Linnaea 23: 420. 1850; FKH 70. 1912.

Vine or climbing shrub, to 25 m long. Branchlets, terete, glabrous or sparsely pubescent when young. Petioles, rachis, and petiolules glabrous; leaflets 3 – 7, usually 3, papery, ovate or elliptic to lanceolate, 3 – 15 × 2 – 6 cm, base broadly cuneate to rounded, equilateral or slightly oblique, apex acute to shortly acuminate, glabrous on both surfaces; petiolules 5 mm. Inflorescences in axillary clusters, 3 – 9 cm, many-flowered, central one much longer than others; peduncles 3 – 9 cm, glabrous. Flowers ca. 1 cm in diam., fragrant. Sepals ovate, 2 – 3 × 1.2 – 2 mm, ciliate at apex. Petals white or yellow, oblong, 4 – 6 × 1 – 1.5 mm, striate, glabrous. Stamens 2 – 6 mm. Carpels free, ca. 4 mm, glabrous. Follicle dark green, turning black when dry, obliquely ellipsoidal, slightly curved, 1.5 – 2.5 × 0.6 – 1.5 cm, striate. Seed red, ellipsoidal, 1.5 × 0.6 cm, completely covered by membranous aril.

Locality: Aberdeen, Hoi Ha, Chek Keng, Lantau Island. Y. W. Lam 27; P. S. Choi 164.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Taiwan; India, Sri Lanka, Laos, Vietnam, Cambodia, Philippines, Australia (Queensland).
Ecology: Thickets or forests. Flowering: Apr. – Oct.; fruiting: May – Mar. of following year.

Pittosporum glabratum Lindl. 光葉海桐（崖花子）
J. Hort. Soc. London 1: 230. 1846; FHK 19. 1861; FKH 37. 1912; FRPS 35(2): 11. 1979; FFJ 2: 241. 1984; FGD 1: 102, fig. 111: 2. 1987; FOC 9: 6. 2003.
Pittosporum fortunei Turcz., Bull. Soc. Imp. Naturalistes Moscou 236: 562. 1863.

Shrub or small tree, 2 – 3 m tall, glabrous except pedicels. Petioles 6 – 14 mm; leaf blade narrowly oblong or oblanceolate, 5 – 10 × 2 – 3.5 cm, thinly leathery, base cuneate, apex obtuse or acute, margin slightly rugose. Inflorescences 1 – 4 in leaf axils at branchlet apex, umbellate or corymbose; pedicels 4 – 12 mm, puberulous. Sepals ovate, ca. 2 mm. Petals oblanceolate, 0.8 – 1.2 cm. Stamens 4 – 7 mm. Ovary long ovoid, 3-carpellate; placentae 3; ovules ca. 6 in each placenta; style ca. 3 mm. Capsule ellipsoidal, 2 – 2.5 cm, dehiscing by 3 valves; pericarp thinly leathery. Seeds red, subglobose, 5 – 7 × 4 – 5 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 2195; L. T. Lo 3.
Distribution: Guangdong, Hainan, Guangxi, Hunan, Guizhou, Hubei, Fujian.
Ecology: Thin forests and shrublands on slopes. Flowering: Mar. – Aug.; fruiting: Jun. – Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Aberdeen, Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Pittosporum glabratum Lindl. var. neriifolium Rehder & E. H. Wilson 狹葉海桐
Pl. Wilson. 3(2): 328. 1916; FRPS 35(2): 12. 1979; FGD 1: 103. 1987; FOC 9: 6. 2003.
Pittosporum cavaleriei Levl., Fedde, Rep. Spec. Nov. 11: 492. 1913.

Leaf blade narrowly lanceolate, 8 – 18 × 1 – 2 cm.
Locality: Aberdeen, Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan. Y. W. Lam 1439; HK sheet 271, 40905.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Yunnan; India.
Ecology: Forests or thickets. Flowering: Mar. – May; fruiting: Jun. – Nov.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Ninepin Group, Sung Kong and Ng Fan Chau; also cultivated in parks and gardens
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Pittosporum tobira (Thunb.) Aiton 海桐
Hort. Kew. (ed. 2) 2: 37. 1811; FKH 37. 1912; FHN 1: 449. 1964; FRPS 35(2): 6. 1979; FFJ 2: 240, fig. 202. 1984; FGD 1: 103, pl. 112, fig. 1. 1987; FOC 9: 4. 2003.
Euonymus tobira Thunb., Nova Acta Regiae Soc. Sci. Upsal. 3: 208. 1780.

Shrub or small tree, to 3 m tall. Young branchlets lenticellate, brown hairy. Petioles ca. 2 cm; leaf blade obovate or obovate-lanceolate, 4 – 9 × 2 – 4 cm, leathery, base narrowly cuneate, apex rounded or obtuse, usually emarginate, margin revolute. Inflorescences terminal or near so, umbellate or corymbose; pedicels 1 – 2 cm. Sepals lanceolate, 3 – 4 mm. Petals oblanceolate, 1 – 1.2 cm. Stamens 5 – 6 mm, sometimes sterile. Ovary long ovoid, densely pubescent, 3-carpellate; placentas 3; ovules many per locule. Capsule globose, angular, ca. 1 – 1.2 cm in diam., dehiscing by 3 valves, ± pubescent; pericarp ca. 1.5 mm thick. Seeds red, ca. 4 mm.

Locality: Ninepin Group, Sung Kong and Ng Fan Chau; also cultivated in parks and gardens. S. P. Lau 137; F. W. Xing 9708.
Distribution: Areas S of Changjiang River; Japan, Korea.
Ecology: Seashore hillslopes. Flowering: Mar. – May; fruiting: May – Oct.
Uses: Ornamental.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Victoria Peak, Tai Mo Shan, Sai Kung, Lam Tsuen, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Dichroa febrifuga Lour. 常山
Fl. Cochinch. 301. 1790; FHK 128. 1862; FKH 98. 1912; FHN. 2: 190, fig. 399. 1965; FFJ 2: 231, fig. 196. 1984; FGD 2: 213. 1991; FRPS 35(1): 178, pl. 36: 1 – 3. 1995; FOC 8: 405. 2001.
Adamia chinensis Gardner & Champ., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 1: 311. 1849.
Dichroa febrifuga Lour. var. glabra S. Y. Hu, J. Arnold Arbor. 61(1): 77. 1980.

Shrub, 1 – 2 m. Branchlets often fleshy, terete or slightly 4- angular, glabrous or very sparsely pubescent, usually purplish. Petioles 1.5 – 5 cm, glabrous or puberulent; leaf blade papery, varied in shape, elliptic, obovate-oblong to lanceolate, 6 – 25 × 2 – 10 cm, attenuate at both ends, margin denticulate or serrulate, abaxially glabrous or sparsely puberulent, purplish. Inflorescence terminal, a corymbose panicle, 3 – 20 cm. Flowers bluish, ca. 8 mm in diam. when blooming; pedicel 3 – 5 mm. Calyx obconical; lobes 4 – 6, broadly triangular, ca. 1 mm. Petals 4 – 6, narrowly elliptic, slightly fleshy. Stamens 10 – 20; filaments slightly flat; anthers ellipsoidal. Ovary inferior; styles 4 – 6, clavate; stigma long elliptic-ovate. Berry blue when mature, 3 – 7 mm in diam.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Tai Mo Shan, Sai Kung, Lam Tsuen, Lantau Island. G. Barretto s.n. (HK sheet 34338); Y. W. Lam 548.
Distribution: Areas S of Changjiang River; India, Vietnam, Myanmar, Malaysia, Philippines, Indonesia, Japan (Ryukyu).
Ecology: Wet places in forests and thickets. Flowering: Feb. – Apr.; fruiting: May – Aug.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The type specimen of Adamia chinensis was collected from Victoria Peak by J. G. Champion between 1847 and 1849.

Hydrangea macrophylla (Thunb.) Ser. 繡球
Prodr. 4: 15. 1830; FFJ 2: 226, fig. 192. 1985; FRPS 35(1): 226. 1995.
Hydrangea hortensia Sieb., Acta Phys.-Med. Acad. Caes. Leop.-Carol. Nat. Cur. (pt. 2) 14: 688, fig. 2. 1829.
Hydrangea macrophylla (Thunb.) Ser. f. hortensia (Regel) Rehd., J. Arnold Arbor. 7(4): 240. 1926; FGD. 2: 208. 1991.
Hydrangea scandens auct. non Maxim.: FKH 98. 1912.
Viburnum macrophyllum Thunb., Fl. Jap. 125. 1784.

Deciduous shrub, 1 – 4 m. Branchlets robust, with conspicuous lenticels and leaf scars. Leaves opposite; petioles 1 – 3 cm; leaf blade elliptic, broadly ovate to obovate, 7 – 20 × 4 – 10 cm, base broadly cuneate, apex shortly acuminate, margin coarsely serrate except the base, green and glossy adaxially, glabrous or hirsute along veins abaxially. Inflorescence terminal, corymbose, globose, to 20 cm in diam.; pedicels pubescent. Flowers white, pink or bluish, mostly sterile. Sterile flower: sepals 4, broadly ovate or orbicular, 1 – 2 cm. Fertile flower: calyx 5-lobed, lobes ovate or triangular; petals 5, oblong; stamens 10, unequal in length, to 4 mm; ovary semi-inferior, styles usually 3. Capsules narrowly ovoid, ribbed.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 1899.
Distribution: S, C & E China; Korea, Japan.
Ecology: Flowering: Jun.-Aug.
Uses: Ornamental.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Mo Shan, Ho Pui Reservoir
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Pileostegia tomentella Hand.-Mazz. 星毛冠蓋藤
Anz. Akad. Wiss. Wien. Math.-Nat. 59: 55. 1922; FFJ 2: 230. 1984; FRPS 35(1): 175, pl. 35: 4 – 7. 1995; FGD 2: 212, fig. 135. 1991; FOC 8: 404. 2001.

Branchlets, petioles, inflorescences and abaxial surface of leaves densely rusty stellate hairy. Petioles 0.5 – 1.5 cm; leaf blade leathery, oblong to obovate-oblong, 5 – 10( – 18) × 2.5 – 5( – 8) cm, base shallowly cordate, apex acute, margin entire and slightly revolute, irregularly undulate or sparsely serrate at upper part. Inflorescences 5 – 25 × 10 – 25 cm; pedicels ca. 2 mm. Calyx tube turbinate, ca. 2 mm; lobes triangular, sparsely stellate hairy. Petals white, broadly triangular, ca. 2 mm, glabrous. Stamens 10; filaments 3 – 6 mm; anthers globose, ca. 0.7 mm in diam. Ovary truncate at apex; style ca. 1.5 mm; stigma conical, 4 – 6-lobed. Capsule dark brown, turbinate, ca. 4 mm in diam., 5 – 10-ribbed, apex truncate, sparsely stellate hairy. Seeds ca. 2 mm.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Ho Pui Reservoir. F. W. Xing 10094; HK sheet 10543.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian.
Ecology: Margins of forests in valleys. Flowering: Mar. – Aug.; fruiting: Sep. – Dec.
Uses: Ornamental.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Mount Parker, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Peak
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Pileostegia viburnoides Hook. f. & Thomson 冠蓋藤
J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 2: 76, fig. 2. 1857; FKH 98. 1912; FHN 2: 190. 1965; FFJ 2: 230, fig. 195. 1984; FGD 2: 212. 1991; FTW ed. 2, 3: 57, pl. 32. 1993; FRPS 35(1): 173, pl. 35: 1 – 3. 1995; FOC 8: 404. 2001.
Pileostegia viburnoides Hook. f. & Thomson var. parviflora Oliv. & Maxim., Mem. Acad. Sci. St. Petersb. ser. 7, 10(16): 18. 1867.

Branchlets decussate, glabrous or sparsely stellate pubescent. Petioles 1 – 3 cm; leaf blade thinly leathery, elliptic-lanceolate to oblong-obovate, 7 – 18 × 2 – 6 cm, base cuneate, apex acute, margin entire, abaxially glabrous or sparsely stellate pubescent. Inflorescences 7 – 25 × 15 – 25 cm, glabrous or pubescent; pedicel 3 – 5 mm. Flowers small. Calyx tube ca. 1.5 mm; lobes 4 – 5, triangular, glabrous. Petals 4 – 5, white, ca. 2.5 mm. Stamens 8 – 10; filaments 3 – 6 mm, usually coiled; anthers compressed subglobose. Ovary inferior, truncate at apex; style ca. 1 mm; stigma 4 – 6-lobed. Capsule turbinate, ca. 4 × 2 – 3 mm. Seeds ca. 2 mm.

Locality: Mount Parker, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Peak. D. P. M. Guile s.n. (HK sheet 30346); L. T. Lo 360; P. S. Choi 544.
Distribution: Areas S of Changjiang River; India, Vietnam, Japan.
Ecology: Valleys. Flowering: Jul. – Aug.; fruiting: Sep. – Dec.

Itea chinensis Hook. & Arn. 老鼠刺（鼠刺）
Bot. Beech. Voy. 189, fig. 39. 1833; FHK 129. 1861; FKH 99. 1912; FGZ 285. 1956; FFJ 2: 237, fig. 200. 1984; FRPS 35(1): 271, pl. 62: 1 – 2. 1995; FGD 3: 228. 1995; FOC 8: 426. 2001.

Shrub or small tree, 4 – 15 m. Young branchlets glabrous. Petioles 1 – 2 cm, glabrous; leaf blade thinly leathery, obovate or ovate-oblong, 5 – 12( – 15) × 2.5 – 6 cm, base cuneate, apex acute, margin obscurely glandular-crenulate at upper half or subentire, slightly revolute, glabrous on both surfaces. Racemes axillary, erect, 3 – 6 cm, glabrous or puberulous; bracts linear-subulate, 1 – 2 mm. Flowers many; pedicels slender, ca. 3 mm, puberulous. Calyx shallowly cupular; lobes triangular-lanceolate, ca. 1 mm, puberulous. Petals erect at anthesis, white, lanceolate, 2.5 – 3 mm. Stamens nearly as long as petals or slightly longer; filaments puberulous. Ovary superior, puberulous. Capsule narrowly ellipsoidal, 6 – 9 mm, puberulous, apex acuminate.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 793, 2387, 7021.
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Hunan; Bhutan, Laos, India.
Ecology: Thin forests. Flowering: Apr. – May; fruiting: Jun. – Aug.
Notes: Some specimens were misidentified as Itea chinensis var. oblonga (Hand.-Mazz.) C. Y. Wu previously (Check List HK Plants 122. 2002).

Kalanchoe integra (Medik.) Kuntze 匙葉伽藍菜
Revis. Gen. Pl. 1: 229. 1891; FOC 8: 205. 2001.
Cotyledon integra Medik., Hist. & Commentat. Acad. Elect. Sci. Theod.-Palat. 3: 200, pl. 9. 1775.
Kalanchoe spathulata DC., Pl. Grass. pl. 65. 1799 – 1829; FKH 99. 1912; FRPS 34(1): 38. 1984; FGD 3: 44, fig. 30: 5. 1995.

Annual succulent herb, 0.3 – 1.2 m tall, glabrous. Leaves opposite; petioles 2 – 3 cm; leaf blade oblong-spathulate, 7 – 10 × 2 – 4 cm, base attenuate, apex obtuse. Cymes terminal and paniculate, to 10 cm; flowers erect. Sepals green, deeply 4-lobed; lobes triangular or narrowly ovate, 5 – 12 mm, apex acuminate. Corolla yellow, salverform, 1.5 – 2 cm; lobes 4, lanceolate, apex acuminate. Stamens 8, in two whorls; filaments very short, inserted near apex of corolla-tube. Carpels 4, free, apically narrowed into styles. Fruit a group of follicles, many-seeded.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. S. Y. Hu 5249, 9377 (CUHK); HK sheet 1686.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Xizang, Fujian, Taiwan; widespread over tropical Asia.
Ecology: Flowering: Jan.-Mar.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: The species was reported as Kalanchoe spathulata DC. previously (Check List HK Plants 47. 2004).

Kalanchoe laciniata (L.) DC. 伽藍菜
Hist. Pl. Grass. 2: 100. 1802; DC., Prodr. 3: 395. 1828; FKH 99. 1912; FHN 1: 370, fig. 190. 1964; FRPS 34(1): 39, pl. 13: 1 – 6. 1984; FGD 3: 44, fig. 30: 1 – 4. 1995.

Perennial succulent herb. Stems erect, to 1 m tall, few-branched. Leaves opposite; petioles 2.5 – 4 cm; leaf blade 8 – 18 × 5 – 15 cm, pinnatipartite; lobes lanceolate, entire, irregularly toothed or lobed again. Cymes terminal and paniculate, 10 – 30 cm, many-flowered. Sepals green, deeply 4-lobed; lobes linear-lanceolate, 4 – 7 mm, membranous, apex acute. Corolla salverform, yellow or reddish; tube ca. 1.5 cm, inflated at the base; limb ca. 2 cm in diam.; lobes 4, ovate, 5 – 6 mm, apex acute. Stamens 8, in two whorls; filaments very short, inserted near apex of corolla-tube. Carpels 4, free, apically narrowed into styles. Fruit a group of follicles, many-seeded.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 2669; W. J. Tutcher s.n. (HK sheet 1685).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; widespread and naturalized in tropical regions of Asia and Africa.
Ecology: Flowering: Almost all the year round.
Uses: Ornamental.

Kalanchoe pinnata (L. f.) Pers. 落地生根
Syn. Pl. 1: 446. 1805; Backer, Fl. Malesia I. 4: 199, fig. 1. 1951; FHN 1: 371, fig. 191. 1964.
Crassula pinnata L. f., Suppl. Sp. Pl. 191. 1781.
Bryophyllum calycinum Salisb., Parad. Lond., pl. 3. 1805; FHK 127. 1861; FKH 99. 1912.
Bryophyllum pinnatum (L. f.) Oken, All. Naturgesch. 3: 1966. 1841; FRPS 34(1): 36, pl. 12: 11 – 17. 1984; FTW ed. 2, 3: 10, pl. 5. 1993; FGD 3: 42, fig. 29. 1995; FOC 8: 204. 2001.
Cotyledon pinnata Lam., Encyclopédie Méthodique, Botanique 2: 141. 1786.

Succulent perennial herb, glabrous throughout. Stems erect, 0.5 – 1.5 m tall, ± woody at base. Leaves opposite, simple (early ones) or pinnate, petiolate; leaflets 3 – 5, ovate to ovate-oblong, 5 – 10 × 3 – 8 cm, apex rounded or obtuse on both ends, margin crenate. Flowers in paniculate cymes, pendulous. Calyx campanulate, light green or tinged with reddish-yellow, 2.5 – 4 mm; lobes 4, triangular. Corolla tubular, 4 – 5 cm, inflated at base; lobes 4, ovate-lanceolate, pink or purplish red. Stamens 8, attached to the base of corolla-tube. Follicles ca. 5 mm, included in corolla and calyx.

Locality: Cultivated and naturalized. W. J. Tutcher s.n. (HK sheet 10721); Y. S. Lau 2124, 2733.
Distribution: Native to Africa, but naturalized elsewhere in tropical and subtropical regions of the world.
Ecology: Wastelands near villages. Flowering: Summer to autumn.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: The species was reported as Bryophyllum pinnatum (L. f.) Oken previously (Check List HK Plants 47. 2004).

Kalanchoe synsepala Baker 趣蝶蓮
J. Bot. 20: 110. 1882.

Perennial succulent herb. Stems very short, 2 – 8( –15) cm; runners slender, 15 – 25 cm, arising from axils of leaves and rooting at the tip. Leaves decussately opposite, forming rosette-like tufts crowded on apex of stem and runners; leaf blade broadly ovate to suborbicular, (3– )5 – 10( –15) cm in diam., base subtruncate, abruptly narrowed into a short and broad petiole, apex rounded, margin purplish, with sharp teeth. Flowers in dichasial cymes terminal on axillary long peduncles; pedicels ca. 4 mm. Calyx ca. 4 mm, lobed to one-third of its length; lobes 4, triangular, acute. Corolla white, salverform; tube ca. 1 cm, glabrous; lobes 4, ovate-elliptic, 6 – 7 mm, apex acuminate. Stamens 8, in two whorls; filaments very short, inserted near apex of corolla-tube; anthers purple, exserted. Carpels 4, free, slightly longer than the corolla-tube, apically narrowed into styles. Fruit unknown.

Locality: Cultivated as a pot plant.
Distribution: Native to Madagascar, but cultivated elsewhere.
Ecology: Flowering: Summer to autumn.
Uses: Ornamental.

Kalanchoe tubiflora (Harv.) Raym.-Hamet 洋吊鐘
Beih. Bot. Centrabl. 29(2): 41. 1912.
Bryophyllum tubiflorum Harv., Fl. Cap. 2: 380. 1862.
Bryophyllum verticillatum (Scott-Elliot) A. Berger, Nat. Pflanzenfam. (ed. 2), 18a: 411. 1930; FGD 3: 43. 1995.
Kalanchoe verticillata Scott-Elliot, J. Linn. Soc. 29: 14. 1981.

Succulent perennial herb, to 1 m tall, glabrous throughout. Stems erect, simple or branched from the base. Leaves opposite or verticillate, sessile, linear, subcylindric, 2.5 – 15 × 0.4 – 0.5 cm, greyish green, mottled with violet-brown, producing plantlets at the tips. Flowers pendulous, in terminal cymes. Calyx campanulate, 6.5 – 10 mm; lobes 4, triangular to triangular-lanceolate. Corolla tubular, 2.5 – 3 cm, inflated, constricted above ovary; lobes 4, suborbicular or broadly ovate, salmon to scarlet. Stamens 8, in 1 whorl; filaments as long as corolla-tube, attached to the base of corolla-tube. Fruit a group of follicles.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. S. Y. Hu & K. H. Yung 200, 453, 688 (CUHK).
Distribution: Native to S Africa, cultivated elsewhere.
Ecology: Preferred sunny and dry places. Flowering: Oct.-Mar. of the following year.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: The species was reported as Kalanchoe verticillata Scott-Elliot previously (Check List HK Plants 47. 2004).

Sedum lineare Thunb. 佛甲草
Syst. Veg. ed. 14, 430. 1784; FRPS 34(1): 144, pl. 32: 17 – 24. 1984; FGD 3: 49. 1995; FOC 8: 250. 2001.

Perennial succulent herb, glabrous throughout. Stems 10 – 20 cm tall, erect or ± diffuse, rooting at the nodes. Leaves sessile, in whorls of 3 or 4, sometimes alternate on the upper part of flowering stems; leaf blade linear or linear oblanceolate, 1 – 2.5 × 0.1 – 0.2 cm, base spurred; spurs truncate or obtuse, apex obtuse. Cymes terminal, with 2 – 3 secund branches, 4 – 5 cm in diam. Flowers sessile, but with one flower between the branches, shortly pedicellate. Sepals 5, narrowly lanceolate, usually unequal, 1.5 – 6 mm. Petals 5, yellow, elliptic-lanceolate, 4 – 6 × 1 – 1.5 mm. Stamens 10, in 2 whorls, shorter than the petals. Carpels 5, 4 – 5 mm, connate at the base, apically narrowed into a short style. Follicles stellately spreading, many-seeded.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 859, 2788.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Gansu, Shaanxi, Henan, Jiangxi, Hunan, Hubei, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr. – May.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal (folklore).

Saxifraga stolonifera Curtis 虎耳草
Philos. Trans. 64(1): 308, no. 2541. 1774; FOC 8: 287. 2001.
Saxifraga chinensis Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 281. 1790.
Saxifraga sarmentosa L. f., Suppl. Pl. 240. 1781; FKH 98. 1912.
Saxifraga stolonifera Meerb., Afbeeld. pl. 23. 1775; FFJ 2: 218, fig. 184. 1984; FRPS 34(2): 75, pl. 15: 7 – 9. 1992; FGD 3: 59. 1995; Check List HK Plants 124. 2002.

Perennial herb; rhizomes short; prostrate stems slender, branched. Stems 10 – 30 cm tall, glandular villous.
