Lianas to 10 m; branchlets pubescent when young, soon glabrous. Petioles 0.5–1.5 cm; leaf blade 5–11 × 2.5 – 4.5 cm, pubescent or glabrous abaxially, lateral veins 5–7 on each side of midvein. Cymes many‑flowered, 1.5–8(–13) cm. Calyx densely pubescent. Corolla tube ca. 2.5 mm; lobes narrowly oblong, ca. 5 mm; anthers elliptic; disk lobes free, linear, longer than ovary. Ovary pubescent. Follicles cylindric, 8–15 cm × 4–5 mm, slightly torulose, pubescent. Seeds linear, coma ca. 2.5 cm.

Locality: Aberdeen, Mount Nicholon, Cape D'Aguilar, Sha Tin, Lam Tsuen, Ching Chau. L. T. Lo 340; Y. S. Lau 3176; Y. W.
Lam 783.
Distribution: Hainan, Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan; S Asia, Indochina, Malesia to Australia.
Ecology: Thickets, thin forest. Flowering: Apr – Jul.; fruiting: Aug. – Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.

Ichnocarpus jacquetii (Pierre) D. J. Middleton 少花腰骨藤
Novon 4: 152. 1994; FOC 16: 186. 1995.
Micrechites jacquetii Pierre in Spire, Contr. Apocyn. 48. 1905.
Ichnocarpus oliganthus Tsiang, Sunyatsenia 3: 156 – 159, pl. 17, fig. 10. 1936; FGD 1: 476, fig. 536. 1987.

Lianas to 20 m, branchlets, abaxial surface of leaves, petioles and inflorescences rusty tomentose. Petioles 1 – 2 cm; leaf blade narrowly elliptic to oblong‑elliptic, 4–8 × 1.5–3.5 cm, base broadly cuneate, apex shortly acuminate, lateral veins 7 – 9 on each side of midvein. Cymes 1.5 – 2.5 cm, 2–8‑flowered; bracts many, ovate, ca. 2 mm. Calyx rusty tomentose outside, inside with 20 glands at the base. Corolla red, ca. 6.5 mm in diam., villous inside at throat; tube ca. 3 mm, dilated at middle; lobes long falcate, ca. 3 × 1.2 mm. Stamens inserted near base of corolla‑tube; disk 5‑lobed, slightly united at base, shorter than ovary. Ovary glabrous. Follicles linear‑cylindric, 12 – 18 cm × 5 mm, rusty tomentose. Seeds dark brown, linear, 1‑2 cm × ca. 1 mm, coma creamy white, to 3 cm.

Locality: Wu Kau Tang. W. J. Tutcher 10924 (HK sheet 18830).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi; Vietnam, Laos.
Ecology: Thin forests and thickets. Fruiting: Mar.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.
Notes: The plant was known in Hong Kong only by a specimen collected from Wu Kau Tang in 1914, identified as I. polyanthus (Blume) P. I. Forst previously. This specimen was cited in the protologue of Ichnocarpus oliganthus Tsiang (1936).

Kopsia arborea Blume 蕊木
Catalogus 13. 1823; FOC 16: 162. 1995; D. J. Middleton, Fl. Thailand 7(1): 61, fig. 20. 1999.
Kopsia lancibracteolata Merr., Philip. J. Sci. 23(3): 262. 1923; FGD 1: 434, fig. 481. 1987; FRPS 63: 41, pl. 14. 1977.
Kopsia officinalis Tsiang & P. T. Li, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 11: 356, pl. 40. 1973. FRPS 63: 43, pl. 15. 1977.

Trees to 15 m tall. Branches greenish, terete, slightly compressed, puberulent when young. Petioles 5 – 15 cm; leaf blade elliptic, narrowly elliptic, or narrowly ovate, 8 – 24 × 3.5 – 8.5 cm, glabrous, apex acute or short acuminate, lateral veins 10 – 20 on each side of midvein. Cymes corymbose, many‑flowered; peduncle to 14 cm, puberulent or glabrous; bracteoles narrowly oblong, puberulent or glabrous. Pedicel 3 – 4 mm. Sepals narrowly oblong, 4 – 6 mm, puberulent or glabrous. Corolla white; tube ca. 2.5 cm; lobes narrowly oblong, 1.5 – 2 cm. Disk scales narrowly oblong, longer than ovary, fleshy. Ovary ovoid, puberulent. Drupes black or blue‑black, ellipsoidal, 2.5 – 3.5 × 1.5 – 2 cm.

Locality: Kadoorie Farm. HK sheet 32239, 32240.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; Vietnam, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia, Philippines, N Australia.
Ecology: Wet places under forest. Flowering: Apr.–Sep.; fruiting: Jul.–Dec.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Mount Parker, Victoria Peak, Wong Chuk Yeung, Ng Tung Chai, Sai Kung, Ma On Shan, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Melodinus fusiformis Champ. ex Benth. 尖山橙
Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 4: 332. 1852; FHK 218. 1861; FKH 167. 1912; FRPS 63: 29. 1977; FGD 1: 431, fig. 477. 1987; FOC 16: 150. 1995.

Lianas stout, to 10 m, juvenile parts pubescent, glabrous when older. Bark grey‑brown. Petioles 4–6 mm; leaf blade elliptic or oblong, rarely narrowly elliptic, 4.5–12 × 1–5.3 cm, somewhat leathery, base cuneate or rounded, apex acuminate; lateral veins ca. 15 on each side of midvein, obliquely spreading and reticulate toward margin. Cymes terminal, 3–5 cm, 6–12‑flowered. Pedicels 5 – 10 mm. Sepals ovate, 4–5 mm, acute. Corolla white; tube 1.2–2 cm; lobes obliquely narrow ovate or obovate, (0.8–)1.1–2 cm × 3.5–9 mm; corona scales 5, indistinct, apices 2‑ or 3‑cleft, exserted, villous. Stamens inserted near base of corolla tube. Berries fusiform, 3.5 – 5.3 × 2.2 – 4 cm.

Locality: Mount Parker, Victoria Peak, Wong Chuk Yeung, Ng Tung Chai, Sai Kung, Ma On Shan, Lantau Island. P. S. Choi 394; HK sheet 38556, 40138.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou.
Ecology : Thickets, thin forests. Flowering: Feb.–Jun.; fruiting: May–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.
Notes: The type specimen was collected by J. G. Champion from Victoria Peak between 1847 and 1850.

Melodinus suaveolens (Hance) Champ. ex Benth. 山橙
Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 4: 333. 1852; FHK 218. 1861; FKH 167. 1912; FRPS 63: 22, pl. 7. 1977; FGD 1: 430, fig. 476. 1987; FOC 16: 148. 1995.
Lycimnia suaveolens Hance, Ann. Bot. Syst. 3(1): 31. 1852.
Melodinus monogynus auct. non Roxb.: FHK 218. 1861; FKH 167. 1912.

Lianas to 10 m, glabrous except for inflorescences. Petioles to 1.2 cm; leaf blade elliptic or ovate, 5–10 × 1.8–5 cm, leathery, base attenuate to rounded, apex short acuminate. Cymes terminal and axillary. Flower buds rounded or obtuse at apex, minutely pubescent outside. Flowers fragrant. Sepals ovate, ca. 3 mm, minutely pubescent abaxially, apex rounded or obtuse. Corolla white; tube 1–1.4 cm; lobes shorter than or as long as tube, suborbicular, falcate, with a distinct notch near apex; corona campanulate or tubular, apex 5‑cleft, exserted from throat. Berries globose, 5–8 cm in diam.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 454, 3070; HK sheet 39868.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi; Vietnam.
Ecology: Open forests, humid thickets; 100 – 800 m. Flowering: Feb.–Jun.; fruiting: Apr.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.
Notes: The type specimen was collected by J. G. Champion from Happy Valley Woods between 1847 and 1850.

Nerium oleander L. 夾竹桃
Sp. Pl. 1: 209. 1753; FGD 1: 460, fig. 515. 1987; FRPS 63: 149. 1977; FOC 16: 173. 1995; D. J. Middleton, Fl. Thailand 7(1): 79. 1999.
Nerium indicum Mill., Gard. Dict. ed. 8, n. 2. 1786; FRPS 63: 147, pl. 49. 1977.
Nerium odorum Sol., Hort. Kew 1: 297. 1789.

Evergreen shrubs, to 6 m tall. Leaves very narrowly elliptic, 5–21 × 1–3.5 cm, leathery, base cuneate or decurrent on the petiole, apex acuminate or acute. Flowers showy, fragrant. Sepals narrowly triangular to narrowly ovate, 3–10 mm. Corolla purplish red, pink, white, salmon, or yellow, tube 1.2 – 2.2 cm; lobes 1.3 – 3 cm, single or double. Follicles cylindric, 12 – 23 cm. Seeds oblong, coma 0.9 – 1.2 cm.

Locality : Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 1436; L. T. Lo 201; HK sheet 34938.
Distribution: Native to S Europe, N Africa and SW Asia; widely cultivated in tropical, subtropical, and temperate regions.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr.–Sep.
Uses: Ornamental.

Plumeria rubra L. 雞蛋花
Sp. Pl. 1: 209. 1753; FRPS 63: 78. 1977; FGD 1: 446, fig. 499. 1987; FOC 16: 154. 1995; D. J. Middleton, Fl. Thailand 7(1): 39, fig. 13. 1999.
Plumeria acuminata Aiton, Hort. Kew 2: 70. 1789.
Plumeria acutifolia Poir., Encycl. Suppl. 2: 667. 1811.
Plumeria rubra var. acutifolia (Poir.) Bailey, Man. Cult. Pl. 810. 1949; FHN 3: 223, pl. 673. 1974 (as P. rubra ‘Acutifolia’).

Trees to 8 m tall. Bark pale green, smooth. Petioles to 7 cm; leaf blade elliptic to very narrowly so, 14 – 30 × 6 – 8 cm, glaucous adaxially, apex acute or acuminate; lateral veins 30 – 40 on each side of midvein, slightly elevated abaxially. Corolla tinged with pink or purple at least abaxially, 4 – 6 cm in diam.; lobes pink, yellow, or white, with a yellow base, 3 – 4.5 × 1.5 – 2.5 cm, obliquely spreading. Follicles oblong, 11 – 25 × 2 – 3 cm.

Locality: Commonly cultivated in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 141; Y. S. Lau 875, 1636.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian (cultivated); native to Mexico, C America, widely cultivated in tropical and subtropical regions.
Ecology: Flowering: Mar. – Sep.; fruiting: May – Oct.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: The cultivar with yellowish white flowers was recorded as P. rubra var. acutifolia (Poir.) Bailey previously (Check List HK Plants 56. 1993).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Sha Tin, Sai Kung, Hok Tau, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Pottsia laxiflora (Blume) Kuntze 簾子藤
Revis. Gen. Pl. 2: 416. 1891; FRPS 63: 137, pl. 46. 1977; FGD 1: 457, fig. 511. 1987; FOC 16: 173. 1995; D. J. Middleton, Fl. Thailand 7(1): 139, fig. 44. 1999.
Vallaris laxiflora Blume, Bijdr. Fl. Ned. Ind. 16: 1043. 1826.
Pottsia cantonensis Hook. & Arn., Bot. Beechey. Voy. 199, pl. 43. 1837; FHK 222. 1861; FKH 168. 1912.

Lianas to 10 m; branches and branchlets slender, pubescent or glabrous. Petioles 1.5–4 cm; leaf blade ovate, narrowly ovate, or elliptic, 6–12 × 3–7 cm, base obtuse to rounded or subcordate, pubescent or glabrous on both surfaces, lateral veins 4 – 6 on each side of midvein. Cymes to 25 cm, long‑pedunculate, many‑flowered. Corolla purple or rose, ca. 7 mm; tube glabrous, longer than lobes; lobes narrowly ovate, ca. 2 mm, spreading. Ovary pilose. Style thickened in middle. Follicles linear, to 26–40 cm × 3–4 mm, pubescent to glabrous. Seeds linear, ca. 2 cm; coma 2.5 – 3 cm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Sha Tin, Sai Kung, Hok Tau, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 2314; P. S. Choi 264, 501.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian; India, Vietnam, Laos, Cambodia, Malaysia, Indonesia.
Ecology: Thickets, thin forests. Flowering: Jun. – Sep.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.
Notes: The species was recorded as Pottsia grandiflora Markgr. previously (Check List HK Plants 57. 1993; 74. 2004).

Rauvolfia verticillata (Lour.) Baill. 蘿芙木
Hist. Pl. 10: 170. 1889; FRPS 63: 55, pl. 19. 1977; FGD 1: 440, fig. 490. 1987; FOC 16: 159. 1995; D. J. Middleton, Fl. Thailand 7(1): 54. 1999.
Dissolena verticillata Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 1: 137. 1790.
Rauvolfia chinensis (Spreng.) Hemsl., J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 26(173): 95. 1889; FKH 168. 1912.
Rauvolfia perakensis King & Gamble, J. Asiat. Soc. Bengal 74(2): 424. 1908; FRPS 63: 53. 1977.

Shrubs to 3 m tall, erect, glabrous. Branchlets pale grey, lenticellate. Lower leaves opposite, terminal leaves in whorls of 3 or 4; petioles 0.5 – 1.5cm; leaf blade narrowly to broadly ovate or oblong, 3.5 – 25 × 5 – 13 cm, nearly papery to membranous, lateral veins 6 or 7 on each side of midvein. Cymes rather lax, 3 – 9 together; peduncle 2 – 15 cm. Pedicel 3 – 6 mm. Corolla white, tube cylindric, 1 – 1.8 cm, inflated and villous from middle to throat; lobes broadly elliptic or ovate, 1 – 4.5 mm. Stamens inserted at middle of corolla tube. Ovary of 2 carpels completely free up to the single style. Drupes ellipsoidal or ovoid, free from each other, ca. 10 × 5 mm.

Locality: Aberdeen, Victoria Peak, Mount Gough. H. C. Tang 2406; Y. S. Lau 223, 2347.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Taiwan; Cambodia, India, Indonesia, Malaysia, Myanmar, Philippines, Sri Lanka, Thailand, Vietnam.
Ecology: Thickets. Flowering: Jan. – Oct.; fruiting: Apr. – Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Strophanthus divaricatus (Lour.) Hook. & Arn. 羊角拗
Bot. Beechey Voy. 199. 1837; FRPS 63: 152, pl. 51. 1977; FGD 1: 462, fig. 517. 1987; FOC 16: 178. 1995.
Pergularia divaricatus Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 1: 169. 1790.
Strophanthus divergens Graham, Edinburgh New Philos. J. 179. 1827; FHK 220. 1861.
Strophanthus chinensis (Hunter ex Roxb.) G. Don, Gen. Hist. 4: 85. 1837; FKH 172. 1912.

Lianas or sarmentose shrubs, to 4.5 m tall, stolon‑bearing when pruned, glabrous except for corolla; latex clear or yellowish. Branches dark grey, densely lenticellate, branchlets reddish brown. Petioles 5–10 mm; leaf blade elliptic or slightly obovate, 3–10 × 1.5–5 cm; lateral veins 4–9 on each side of midvein. Cymes 3–15‑flowered; peduncle to 1.5 cm; bracts linear or narrowly ovate, deciduous. Pedicels to 1 cm. Sepals narrowly triangular, 4 – 11 mm. Corolla yellow, tube 0.9 – 1.6 cm, puberulent on both sides or glabrous inside; lobes with a red basal spot adaxially, ovate, to 10 cm, abruptly narrowed into pendulous tails to 1 mm wide; corona‑lobes 10, greenish yellow, triangular or awl‑shaped, 0.9–3 mm. Anthers included, connective tail to 0.6 mm. Ovary glabrous. Follicles ellipsoidal‑oblong, 9 – 15 × 2–3.5 cm, hard, woody, divergent at an angle 180 – 250°. Seeds fusiform, 1.3–2 cm, beak 1.2–3.4 cm, coma 3.5–5.5 cm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. L. T. Lo 16; Y. S. Lau 2369; HK sheet 40116.
Distribution: Hainan, Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan; Laos, Vietnam.
Ecology: Thickets or thin forests. Flowering: Mar. – May; fruiting: Jun. – Oct.

Tabernaemontana divaricata (L.) R. Br. ex Roem. & Schult. 狗牙花
Syst. 4: 427. 1819; FOC 16: 153. 1995; D. J. Middleton, Fl. Thailand 7(1): 31. 1999.
Nerium divaricatum L., Sp. Pl. 1: 209. 1753.
Ervatamia divaricata (L.) Burkill, Rec. Bot. Surv. India 10(2): 320. 1925; FRPS 63: 100. 1977; FGD 1: 450, fig. 504. 1987.

Shrubs or small trees, 0.5–5 m tall, glabrous. Petioles 3–10 mm; leaf blade elliptic or narrowly so, 3–18 × 1 – 6 cm, apex acuminate; lateral veins 5–17 on each side of midvein. Cymes dichotomous, 1 – 8‑flowered; bracts scalelike. Flower buds with an ovoid head, apex acute or obtuse. Calyx lobes often ciliate. Corolla white; tube 1.5 – 2.7 cm; lobes simple or double, obovate or broadly so, 1.5–2.7 × 0.8 – 2 cm. Stamens inserted at basal third of corolla‑tube. Folliciles obliquely and narrowly ellipsoidal, 2–7 × 0.6 – 1.5 cm.

Locality: Commonly cultivated. C. P. Lau 102; Y. S. Lau 2006; HK sheet 31543.
Distribution: S Yunnan; cultivated in Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Yunnan; Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Thailand, cultivated in tropical and subtropical Asia.
Ecology: Flowering: May–Nov.
Uses: Ornamental.

Thevetia peruviana (Pers.) K. Schum. 黃花夾竹桃
Nat. Pflanzenfam. 4(2): 159. 1895; FRPS 63: 36, pl. 12. 1977; FGD 1: 433, fig. 479. 1987; FOC 16: 164. 1995; D. J. Middleton, Fl. Thailand 7(1): 69. 1999.
Cerbera thevetia L., Sp. Pl. 1: 209. 1753.
Cerbera peruviana Pers., Syn. Pl. 1: 267. 1805.

Trees to 6 m tall. Bark chocolate‑brown, lenticellate; lower branches pendulous, young branches greenish grey. Petioles ca. 3 mm; leaf blades lustrous green adaxially, light green abaxially, very narrowly oblong, 10 – 15 × 0.5 – 1.2 cm, somewhat leathery, glabrous, apex acuminate, lateral veins obscure. Pedicels 2.5 – 5 cm. Flowers fragrant. Sepals green, narrowly triangular, apex acuminate. Corolla 6–7 × 4.5–5.5 cm; tube 4–5 cm, shorter than the lobes; corona scales present, connected by a transverse row of long white hairs; lobes obliquely obovate. Drupes compressed triangular‑globose, 2.5–4 cm in diam. Seeds light grey, lenticular, ca. 2 × 3.5 cm.

Locality: Commonly cultivated in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 35, 2385.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan (cultivated); native to S & C America; widely cultivated in tropical and subtropical regions.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr. – Dec.; fruiting: Aug. – Feb. of the following year.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal (folklore).
Notes: Thevetia peruviana ‘Aurantiana’ (紅酒杯花; Photo 21) is also cultivated in Hong Kong. It differs from T. peruviana by red petals.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Happy Valley, Wan Chai Gap, Tai Mo Shan, Tai Po Kau
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Trachelospermum jasminoides (Lindl.) Lem. 絡石
Jard. Fleur. 1: t. 61. 1851; FKH 169. 1912; FRPS 63: 216, pl. 75. 1977; FGD 1: 472, fig. 531. 1987; FOC 16: 167. 1995.
Rhynchospermum jasminoides Lindl., J. Hort. Soc. London 1: 74. 1846.
Trachelospermum jasminoides (Lindl.) Lem. cv. Variegatum, FRPS 63: 219. 1977.
Trachelospermum jasminoides (Lindl.) Lem. var. heterophyllum Tsiang, Sunyatsenia 2: 146, fig. 15. 1934; FRPS 63: 218. 1977.

Lianas woody, to 10 m or longer. Stems brownish, lenticellate; young branchlets pubescent, glabrous when older. Petioles 3–12 mm; leaf blade ovate to obovate or narrowly elliptic, 2–10 × 1–4.5 cm, papery, glabrous or sometimes sparsely pubescent abaxially. Cymes paniculate, terminal and axillary; peduncle 2–6 cm, puberulent to glabrous. Sepals narrowly oblong, 2–5 mm, spreading or reflexed, pubescent abaxially, ciliate, apex obtuse or acute. Corolla white, tube dilated at middle, 5 – 10 mm, throat glabrous or pilose facing stamens; lobes obovate, as long as tube. Stamens included, inserted at middle of corolla tube. Ovary glabrous. Follicles linear, 10–25 cm × 3 – 10 mm. Seeds oblong, 1.5–2 cm, coma 1.5–4 cm.

Locality: Happy Valley, Wan Chai Gap, Tai Mo Shan, Tai Po Kau. Y. S. Lau 970; HK sheet 18790, 33872.
Distribution: E, C, S & SW China, Shanxi, Shaanxi, Xizang; Japan, Vietnam.
Ecology: Sunny edges of forests, thickets. Flowering: Feb. – Jun.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Authority: (Wall. ex G. Don) D. J. Middleton
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Urceola micrantha (Wall. ex G. Don) D. J. Middleton 杜仲藤
Novon 4: 151. 1994; FOC 16: 184. 1995; Fl. Thailand 7(1): 145, fig. 46. 1999.
Echites micrantha Wall. ex G. Don, Gen. Hist. 4: 75. 1837.
Ecdysanthera micrantha (Wall. ex G. Don) A. DC., Prodr. 8: 442. 1844; FHK 222. 1861; FKH 169. 1912.
Parabarium micranthum (Wall. ex G. Don) Pierre ex Spire, Caoutchouc Indo‑Chine 38. 1906; FRPS 63: 239, pl. 85. 1977; FGD 1: 479, fig. 541. 1987.

Lianas to 50 m or longer. stem 10–30 cm in diam.; branches often lenticellate. Petioles puberulent, 1.5–3 cm; leaf blade elliptic or narrowly ovate, 5–15 × 1.5–6 cm, base obtuse, apex narrowly acuminate, glabrous, lateral veins 3–7 on each side of midvein. Cymes paniculate, compact, to 9 cm; peduncle pubescent. Sepals ovate, ca. 0.8 – 1 mm, apex subacute. Corolla pink, lobes oblong, as long as to longer than the tube, to 2 mm, 1‑toothed near base. Filaments ca. 0.5 m; disk ring‑like. Ovary pilose; pistil head conical. Follicles narrowly ovoid, 9 – 23 × (0.4 – )1 – 1.2 cm, base dilated. Seeds oblong, 2 – 4 cm, coma ca. 4 cm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Lantau Island. W. J. Tutcher 10169; HK sheet 3789, 40675.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan, Xizang, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Indonesia, Ryukyu Islands, Laos, Malaysia, Nepal, Thailand, Vietnam.
Ecology: Mixed forests, thickets. Flowering: Mar. – Jul.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Urceola rosea (Hook. & Arn.) D. J. Middleton 酸葉膠藤
Novon 4: 151. 1994; FOC 16: 184. 1995; Fl. Thailand 7(1): 149. 1999.
Ecdysanthera rosea Hook. & Arn., Bot. Beechey Voy. 198, pl. 42. 1837; FHK 222. 1861; FKH 169. 1912; FRPS 63: 234. 1977; FGD 1: 477, fig. 538. 1987.

Lianas to 20 m. Stems dark brown, lenticels absent; branches tawny grey, young ones brownish. Petioles 0.8 – 1.2 cm; leaf blade broadly elliptic, rarely subovate, 3–7 × 1–4 cm, apex acute, glabrous, ± lustrous adaxially, glaucous abaxially, lateral veins 4 – 6 on each side of midvein. Sepals ovate, ca. 3 mm, obtuse. Corolla pink; tube ca. 4 mm; lobes ca. 2 mm, acute.; disk ring‑like, entire. Ovary pubescent. Follicles to 15 cm, terete, densely spotted. Seeds oblong, ca. 1 cm, coma ca. 3 cm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island. P. S. Choi 438; N. H. Li 105; Y. W. Lam 921.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Yunnan, Hunan, Fujian, Taiwan; Indonesia, Thailand, Vietnam.
Ecology: Thickets, thin forests. Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: Jul.–Jan. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Yuen Tun Ha
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Wrightia laevis Hook. f. 藍樹
Fl. Brit. India 3(9): 654. 1882; FRPS 63: 125, pl. 42. 1977; FGD 1: 455, fig. 509. 1987; FOC 16: 175. 1995; D. J. Middleton, Fl. Thailand 7(1): 85. 1999.
Wrightia hainanensis Merr., Philipp. J. Sci. 21: 352. 1922.
Wrightia hainanensis Merr. var. variabilis Tsiang, Sunyatsenia 4: 37, pl. 14. 1939.

Trees to 40 m tall, glabrous except for flowers. Bark dark grey; branchlets brownish, lenticellate. Petioles 5 – 7 mm; leaf blade oblong or narrowly elliptic, rarely ovate, 7 – 18 × 2.5 – 8 cm, apex acuminate to caudate‑acuminate, lateral veins 5 – 11 on each side of midvein. Cymes ca. 6 cm; peduncle ca. 1 cm, puberulent to glabrous; pedicels 1 – 1.5 cm. Sepals broadly ovate, ca. 1 mm, pubescent abaxially, apex rounded or obtuse. Corolla white or yellowish, funnelform, tube 1.5 – 3 mm; lobes narrowly elliptic, 5.5 – 13.5 mm, papillate; corona fringed; scales 25 – 35, linear, puberulent. Anthers as long as corona, puberulent. Ovary of 2 separate carpels. Fruit of paired follicles cylindric, distinct, 20 – 35 cm × 5 – 7 mm, lenticellate. Seeds sublinear, 1.5 – 2 cm, coma to 4 cm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Yuen Tun Ha. H. C. Tang 100; Y. S. Lau 986; HK sheet 38592.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan; India, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, Philippines, Thailand, Vietnam, N Australia.
Ecology: Forests and thickets in ravines. Flowering: Mar.–Jun.; fruiting: Jul.–Dec.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal (folklore).

Asclepias curassavica L. 馬利筋（蓮生桂子花）
Sp. Pl. 1: 215. 1753; FHK 225. 1861; FKH 170. 1912; FRPS 63. 388, pl. 141. 1977; FGD 1: 511, fig. 582. 1987; FOC 16: 203. 1995.

Perennial herbs to 1 m tall. Stems pale grey, puberulent to glabrous. Leaves opposite; petioles to 1 cm; leaf blade lanceolate or oblong‑lanceolate, 6–15 × 1–4 cm, base decurrent to petiole, apex acuminate or acute, glabrous or abaxially puberulent along veins. Cymes up to as long as leaves, 10–20‑flowered; peduncle 3.5 – 6 cm, pubescent. Pedicels 1.2–1.5 cm, pubescent. Sepals lanceolate, 3 × 1 mm, pubescent. Corolla purple or red, 7 – 9 mm; lobes oblong, 5–8 × 3 mm, reflexed. Corona lobes yellow or orange, 3.5 – 4 mm; gynostegium 2.5 – 3 mm. Follicles fusiform, 5–10 × 1–1.5 cm. Seeds ovate, 6–7 × 3 mm; coma 2 – 4 cm.

Locality: Cultivated. C. P. Lau 59; H. C. Tang 398; Y. S. Lau 235.
Distribution: Native to tropical America, widely cultivated and naturalized in tropical and subtropical regions.
Ecology: Flowering: Almost all year round.
Uses: Ornamental.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Shing Mun, Yuen Long, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Cryptolepis sinensis (Lour.) Merr. 白葉藤
Philipp. J. Sci. 15: 254. 1919; FRPS 63: 263, pl. 90. 1977; FGD 1: 538, fig. 618. 1987; FOC 16: 193. 1995.
Pergularia sinensis Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 167. 1790.
Cryptolepis elegans Wall. ex G. Don, Gen. Hist. 4: 162. 1837; FKH 170. 1912.

Lianas to 3 m; glabrous throughout. Branchlets red‑brown, exfoliating. Petioles 5–7 mm; leaf blade oblong to lanceolate, 1.5–6 × 0.8–2.5 cm, base rounded to shallowly cordate, apex rounded, apiculate; lateral veins 5–9 on each side of midvein. Cymes terminal or axillary, lax, longer than leaves. Pedicels 1–3.5 cm. Sepals ovate, ca. 1 mm; basal glands 10. Corolla yellowish; tube ca. 5 mm; lobes oblong‑lanceolate or linear, 1–1.5 cm. Corona lobes club‑shaped. Anthers glabrous. Follicles cylindric, to 12.5 cm × 6.8 mm. Seeds brown, oblong, ca. 1 cm × 2 mm; coma ca. 2.5 cm.

Locality: Shing Mun, Yuen Long, Lantau Island. L. T. Lo 267; HK sheet 1844.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Taiwan; Cambodia, India, Indonesia, Malaysia, Vietnam.
Ecology: Thin forests or thickets. Flowering: Apr. – Sep.; fruiting: Jun. – Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan, Tin Fu Tsai
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Cynanchum corymbosum Wight 刺瓜
Contrib. Bot. Ind. 56. 1834; FRPS 63: 379, pl. 138. 1977; FGD 1: 504, fig. 571. 1987; FOC 16: 212. 1995.

Perennial herbs, with thick tubers. Stems twining, to 2 m, pale grey, pubescent along 2 lines. Petioles 2.5–4.5 cm; leaf blade ovate or ovate‑oblong, 4.5–12(–20) × 3.5–8(–10) cm, thinly papery, base deeply cordate, basal lobes rounded, apex apiculate or acuminate, glabrous except for veins, abaxially glaucous, adaxially darkening on drying, basal veins 5, lateral veins 3 on each side of midvein. Inflorescences raceme‑like, 2.5–7 cm, laxly branched and less often to 13 cm; cymules 2‑flowered; peduncle 1–5 cm, puberulent; pedicels 2–18 mm, pubescent. Sepals ovate, 1.5–2 × 1 mm, glabrous or pubescent; basal glands 5, minute. Corolla greenish white drying dark, subrotate; lobes oblong‑lanceolate, ca. 5 × 1.5 mm, glabrous. Corona ± tubular, pure white, 3–4 mm high, plicate and with ± free adaxial appendages between acute teeth, marginal teeth 10, alternately rounded and acute, ca. 0.5–0.7 mm. Anther with oval appendages; pollinia oblong. Stigma head 2‑fid, included within anthers. Follicles fusiform, 9–12 × 2–3 cm, conspicuously echinate; spines curved at tip. Seeds brown, 7–10 × 5 mm, conspicuously dentate at end opposite coma; coma 3–4 cm.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan, Tin Fu Tsai. L. T. Lo 635; HK sheet 34041.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Fujian; Cambodia, India, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, Vietnam.
Ecology: Thickets, open woods, riversides, valleys. Flowering: May–Oct.; fruiting: Aug.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Cynanchum insulanum (Hance) Hemsl. 海南杯冠藤
J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 26(173): 107. 1889; FRPS 63: 383. 1977; FGD 1: 507, fig. 575. 1987; FOC 16: 213. 1995.
Cynoctonum insulanum Hance, J. Bot. 6(71): 330. 1868.

Twining herbs, to 60 cm, glabrous except for pubescent nodes, petioles and leaf margins. Leaves opposite; petioles 1–15 mm; leaf blade oblong‑hastate, ovate‑triangular to linear‑lanceolate, 2–3.5 × 0.5–1.5 cm, base rounded to subcordate‑hastate, apex acute or short apiculate, lateral veins 5 or 6 on each side of midvein. Inflorescences umbel‑like, much shorter than leaves, 4‑ or 5‑flowered. Sepal oblong, ca. 1 × 0.5 mm, acute; basal glands 5. Corolla greenish white, subrotate; tube ca. 0.5 mm; lobes ovate‑oblong, ca. 2 × 1 mm, acute. Corona‑tube cupular, thinly membranous, ca. 2 mm, longer than gynostegium, longitudinally plicate; anthers nearly square, appendages ovate; pollinia oblong. Stigma head capitate, included within anthers. Follicles lanceolate, 4.5 – 5 × 0.7–0.8 cm, with 2 inconspicuous longitudinal ridges, glabrous. Seeds oblong, 3 mm; coma 2 cm.

Locality: Sai Kung (Tai Wan). Y. W. Lam 466, 1219; HK sheet 39286.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi.
Ecology: Sandy beaches. Flowering: May–Oct.; fruiting: Oct.–Nov.
Notes: Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Clear Water Bay, Ko Lau Wan
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Cynanchum paniculatum (Bunge) Kitag. 徐長卿
J. Jap. Bot. 16: 20. 1940; FRPS 63: 351, pl. 125. 1977; FGD 1: 509, fig. 578. 1987; FOC 16: 218. 1995.
Asclepias paniculata Bunge, Enum. Pl. China Bor. 43. 1833.

Perennial herbs. Roots numerous fibrous, fragrant. Stems slender, erect, to 1 m, glabrous or hispid on lower part, unbranched or with few branches from upper parts. Leaves opposite; petioles 3 mm; leaf blade lanceolate to linear, 5–13 × 0.5–1.5 cm, stiffly papery, both ends acute, glabrous or adaxially puberulent, ciliate, lateral veins obscure. Inflorescences terminal and from upper nodes, laxly branched, to 7 cm; peduncle 2.5–4 cm; pedicels 5–10 mm. Sepals lanceolate, 1–1.5 × 0.5 mm; with or without glands. Corolla yellow‑green, subrotate, globrous; tube short; lobes ovate, 4–5.5 × 1.5–3 mm. Corona deeply 5‑lobed, lobes ovate‑oblong, fleshy, slightly laterally compressed, apex obtuse, as long as anthers, adaxially keeled up to middle and adnate to anthers. Anther with semiorbicular appendages, slightly shorter than stigma head; pollinia oblong. Stigma head slightly umbonate. Follicles lanceolate in outline, 4–8 × 0.3–0.8 cm. Seeds oblong, 5 × 3 mm; coma 1.5–3 cm.

Locality: Clear Water Bay, Ko Lau Wan. Y. S. Lau 3114; HK sheet 32938.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; Japan, Korea, Mongolia.
Ecology: Sunny grassy hillslopes. Flowering: Jun.–Sep.; fruiting: Jul.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Po Kau, Wu Kau Tang, Castle Peak, Fo Tan, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Dischidia chinensis Champ. ex Benth. 眼樹蓮（瓜子金）
Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 5: 55. 1853; FHK 228. 1861; FKH 173. 1912; FRPS 63: 504, pl. 188. 1977; FGD 1: 489, fig. 551. 1987; FOC 16: 237. 1995.

Herbs, glabrous throughout; stems green, clinging, twining, or hanging from trees or rocks, to 2 m. Petioles 2 – 3 mm; leaf blade ovate‑elliptic, 1.5 – 3 × 1 cm, base cuneate or obtuse, apex acute to rounded, lateral veins 4 or 5 on each side of midvein. Umbels to 9‑flowered; peduncle ca. 2 mm; pedicels 1 mm. Sepals ovate, ciliate. Corolla yellowish white, throat thickened, villous; lobes ovate‑triangular, 1 × 1 mm. Corona‑lobes anchor‑shaped, stalked, apex linear, 2‑cleft, spreading and recurved at both ends, with a small rounded papilla in sinus of divaricate arms. Pollinia oblong, caudicles enlarged at apex; apical membrane of anther acute. Ovaries glabrous; stigma head slightly apiculate. Follicles lanceolate or linear‑lanceolate, 5 – 8 × 0.4 cm, smooth. Seeds ovate‑oblong; coma 2.5 cm.

Locality: Tai Po Kau, Wu Kau Tang, Castle Peak, Fo Tan, Lantau Island. W. J. Tutcher 10223; Y. S. Lau 1215; HK sheet 39857.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi; Vietnam.
Ecology: Mixed woods, often climbing on trees. Flowering: May – Jul.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental. Notes: The type specimen was collected by J. G. Champion from Victoria Peak between 1847 and 1850.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Aberdeen, Fung Yuen, Fanling, Ping Kong, Kei Ling Ha
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Dregea volubilis (L. f.) Benth. ex Hook. f. 南山藤
Fl. Brit. India 4: 46. 1883; FKH 172. 1912; FRPS 63: 493, pl. 183. 1977; FGD 1: 525, fig. 600. 1987; FOC 16: 250. 1995.
Asclepias volubilis L. f. Suppl. 170. 1781.

Lianas to 12 m. Branches pale grey, lenticellate; branchlets green, smooth. Petioles 2.5–6 cm; leaf blade broadly ovate or suborbicular, 7–18 × 4–17 cm, base shallowly cordate, apex acute or short‑acuminate, glabrous or ± softly pubescent, lateral veins 4 pairs. Inflorescences pendulous, many‑flowered; peduncle 2–6 cm, slender, puberulent. Pedicels 2–2.5 cm; flowers green or yellowish green, fragrant. Sepals ovate‑oblong, 2.5–3 mm, pubescent, ciliate. Corolla glabrous, lobes broadly ovate, 6–12 × 5–12 mm, obtuse, ciliate. Corona yellowish green, 4–4.5 mm in diam. Anther appendage white; pollinia oblong. Ovaries pilose. Follicles narrowly ovoid, 10–15 × 3–4 cm, longitudinally wrinkled‑striate or irregularly ribbed. Seeds ovate, 12 × 6 mm, flattened, marginate; coma 4.5 cm.

Locality: Aberdeen, Fung Yuen, Fanling, Ping Kong, Kei Ling Ha. S. C. Ng 2520; HK sheet 34046, 40152.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Taiwan; Bangladesh, India, Indonesia, Nepal, Malaysia, Sri Lanka, Thailand, Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests or thickets. Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: Jun.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Authority: (Champ. ex Benth.) Benth. & Hook. f. ex Maxim.
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Chek Keng, Tai Po Kau, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Graphistemma pictum (Champ. ex Benth.) Benth. & Hook. f. ex Maxim. 天星藤
Melanges Biol. Bull. Phys.‑Math. Acad. Imp. Sci. Saint‑Petersbourg 9: 776. 1876; FKH 170. 1912; FRPS 63: 412, pl. 152. 1977; FGD 1: 490, fig. 552. 1987; FOC 16: 228. 1995.
Holostemma pictum Champ. ex Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 5: 53. 1853; FHK 224. 1861.

Lianas to 8 m, glabrous. Stipules present, leafy, rounded to ovate, 10–35 × 8–15 mm, amplexicaul; petioles 1–4.5 cm, flat, with group of adaxial glands; leaf blade oblong‑lanceolate, 6–20 × 2.5–7 cm, base rounded, sometimes slightly cordate, apex acuminate or acute, veins pale, lateral veins ca. 10 on each side of midvein. Inflorescences 3–12‑flowered; peduncle 0.5–5 cm. Pedicels 0.5–1.5 cm. Corolla abaxially green, adaxially purplish with yellow margin; lobes oblong, 8–10 × 3–4 mm, minutely ciliate. Follicles 9–11 × 3–4 cm. Seeds brownish, ovate, 1.3 cm; coma to 4 cm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Chek Keng, Tai Po Kau, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 600; L. T. Lo 353; HK sheet 40095.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi; Vietnam.
Ecology: Thin forests or thickets; 100–700 m. Flowering: Apr.–Aug.; fruiting: Jun.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.
Notes: The type specimen was collected by J. G. Champion from Victoria Peak between 1847 and 1850.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Tam Tuk, Sha Tin, Sai Kung, Tsing Yi, Yuen Long, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Gymnanthera oblonga (Burm. f.) P. S. Green 海島藤
Kew Bull. 47: 33. 1992; FOC 16: 193. 1995; P. T. Li & X. M. Chen, High. Pl. China 9: 136, pl. 213. 1999.
Jasminum oblongum Burm. f., Fl. Indica 6, t. 3, fig. 2. 1768.
Gymnanthera nitida R. Br., Prodr. 464. 1810; FGD 1: 537, fig. 617. 1987.

Lianas to 2 m. Branchlets tawny‑brown, lenticellate, slightly pubescent. Petioles 5–10 mm; leaf blade oblong or elliptic, 3 – 5.5 × 1.5 – 2. cm, papery, glabrous, base rounded or broadly cuneate, apex rounded, apiculate. Cymes aparently axillary, nearly sessile, congested, ca. 2 cm wide, to 7‑flowered, glabrous. Pedicels 5 – 10 mm. Sepals ovate, 2 × 1 mm, basal glands 5 – 10. Corolla yellowish green; tube 6 – 9 mm; lobes ovate, 7 × 5 mm, obtuse. Corona‑lobes ovate, apex apiculate. Pollen carriers short cylindric, erect. Ovary of 2 separate carpels, glabrous. Follicles dark brown, 8 – 12 × 0.5 – 0.6 cm. Seed tawny‑brown, oblong, 7 × 2 mm; coma ca. 2 cm.

Locality: Tai Tam Tuk, Sha Tin, Sai Kung, Tsing Yi, Yuen Long, Lantau Island. Y. W. Lam 1721; HK sheet 39781, 40264.
Distribution: Hainan, S Guangdong; Cambodia, Indonesia, Malaysia, New Guinea, Philippines, Thailand, Vietnam, Australia.
Ecology: Sandy beaches or rocks by streams. Flowering: Aug. –Oct.; fruiting: Sep. –Feb. of the following year.
Uses: Ornamental.

Gymnema inodorum (Lour.) Decne. 廣東匙羹藤
Prodr. 8: 551. 1844; FRPS 63: 425. 1977; FGD 1: 501, fig. 567. 1987; FOC 16: 240. 1995.
Cynanchum inodorum Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 166. 1790.

Lianas to 10 m. Stems glabrous; young branchlets pale grey, lenticellate, puberulent. Petioles 2–6 cm; leaf blade membranous, ovate‑oblong to ovate or broadly ovate, 4–13 × 2–9 cm, base rounded to shallowly cordate, apex acuminate to caudate, glabrous or thinly puberulent along veins, lateral veins 4–6 on each side of midvein. Inflorescences eventually raceme‑like with sessile umbel‑like cymes arranged in spiral, up to 4 cm; peduncle 1–2 cm. Pedicels 1–1.5cm. Sepals oblong, 2–3 × 1.4 mm, shorter than corolla‑tube, puberulent, ciliate. Corolla yellow, 6–7 mm, minutely puberulent outside; tube cylindric, glabrous except for longitudinal bands of stiff hairs alternating with lobes; lobes oblong, 3–4 × 1.6–1.8 cm, apex rounded, glabrous except for ciliate margins. Pollinia oblong. Stigma head dome‑shaped, exserted from corolla‑tube. Follicles lanceolate in outline, up to 16 × 3 cm, wall thick and slightly fibrous, glabrous. Seeds ca. 15 × 10 mm; coma 4 cm.

Locality: Sai Kung, Fung Yuen. Y. S. Lau 2841; L. T. Lo 343.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan; India, Nepal, Sikkim, Thailand, Vietnam, Philippines.
Ecology: Thin forests or thickets. Flowering: Jan.–Jun.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.

Gymnema sylvestre (Retz.) R. Br. ex Schult. 匙羹藤
Syst. Veg. 6: 57. 1820; FRPS 63: 418, pl. 154. 1977; FGD 1: 500, fig. 565. 1987; FOC 16: 238. 1995.
Periploca sylvestris Retz., Obs. Bot. 2: 15. 1781.
Gymnema affine Decne., Prodr. 8: 622. 1844; FHK 227. 1861; FKH 170. 1912.

Woody lianas, with white latex. Stems to 8 m, sparsely lenticellate; yong branchlets pubescent, glabrescent. Petioles 3–12 mm; leaf blade obovate to ovate, 3–8.5 × 1.5–5.5 cm, thick‑papery, adaxially pubescent to glabrous except for groove of midvein, abaxially tomentose to glabrous except for veins, lateral veins 4 or 5 on each side of midvein, convergent. Cymes much shorter than leaves, pubescent; peduncle 2–5 mm, rachis with close‑spaced spiral of pedicel‑scars. Sepals ovate, ciliate. Corolla greenish white; lobes ovate, glabrous. Corona‑lobes and stigma head exserted. Follicles mostly solitary, broadly lanceolate in outline, 5–9 × 2 cm, glabrous, with an acuminate beak. Seeds ovate, 8 × 4 mm; coma silky white, 3.5 cm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. S. P. Lau 162; N. H. Li 141; HK sheet 39262.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Zhejiang,
Fujian, Taiwan; India, Sri Lanka, Vietnam, Japan, Malaysia, Indonesia, Africa, Australia.
Ecology: Margins of forests and thickets. Flowering: May–Oct.; fruiting: Aug.–Feb. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), poisonous.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, West Buffalo Hill, Ma On Shan, Ng Tung Chai, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Hoya carnosa (L. f.) R. Br. 球蘭
Mem. Wern. Nat. Hist. Soc. 1: 27. 1810; FHK 228. 1861; FKH 172. 1912; FRPS 63: 481, pl. 179. 1977; FGD 1: 488, fig. 549. 1987; FOC 16: 232. 1995.
Asclepias carnosa L. f., Suppl. Pl. 170. 1781.

Shrub, epiphytic, climbing on trees or rocks, glabrous except for inflorescences. Stems robust, to 6 m, pale grey, smooth. Petioles 1–1.5 cm; leaf blade broadly ovate‑cordate, ovate, to ovate‑oblong, fleshy, 3.5–13 × 3–5 cm, base rounded to shallowly cordate, apex obtuse or short‑acuminate, lateral veins ca. 4 on each side of midvein, obscure. Umbels extra‑axillary, globose, ca. 30‑flowered, pubescent; peduncle 4 cm; pedicels 2–4 cm. Corolla white, sometimes with a pink center, rotate, 1–2 cm in diam.; lobes triangular, densely papillate inside, margin recurved, apex reflexed. Corona‑lobes stellately spreading, outer angle acute, middle ridge prominent, margin strongly reflexed and enclosing a hollow space at base, inner angle acute, incumbent on anthers. Stigma head obtuse or obscurely apiculate. Follicles linear‑lanceolate, 6–10 × 0.5–1.5 cm. Seeds small; coma 2.5 cm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, West Buffalo Hill, Ma On Shan, Ng Tung Chai, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 1251; P. S. Choi 540; K. Y. Tam 140.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Japan, Malaysia, Vietnam.
Ecology: On trees or rocks. Flowering: Apr.–Sep.
Uses: Ornamental.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Authority: (Blanco) W. D. Stevens & P. T. Li
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Happy Valley, Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Jasminanthes mucronata (Blanco) W. D. Stevens & P. T. Li 黑鰻藤
Novon 5: 10. 1995; FOC 16: 242. 1995.
Apocynum mucronatum Blanco, Fl. Filip. 852. 1837.
Stephanotis chinensis Champ. ex Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 5: 53. 1853; FHK 227. 1861; FKH 172. 1912.
Stephanotis mucronata (Blanco) Merr., Sp. Blancoan 316. 1918; FRPS 63: 466, pl. 174. 1977; FGD 1: 520, fig. 594. 1987.

Lianas, to 12 m. stems with 2 lines of hairs, lenticellate. Petioles 2–3 cm; leaf blade ovate‑oblong, 7–12 × 4.5–8 cm, papery, base cordate, apex acuminate, pubescent or glabrescent, lateral veins ca. 8 on each side of midvein. Cymes usually 2–4‑flowered; peduncle 1.5–2 cm; bracteoles ovate, pubescent abaxially. Pedicels 2–3 cm. Sepals oblong, 7 mm. Corolla white, with purple juice; tube 2 cm, glabrous outside; lobes falcate, 3 × 0.5 cm, spreading. Gynostegium shorter than corolla‑tube. Corona‑lobes 5, shorter than anthers. Apical appendage of anther oblong‑ovate, longer than stigma; pollinia ellipsoidal. Stigma head capitate, apex obscurely 2‑lobed. Follicles lanceolate, 12 × 1 cm, glabrous. Seeds oblong, 1 cm; coma 2.5 cm.

Locality: Happy Valley, Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan, Lantau Island. Y. W. Lam 222; HK sheet 19025, 30755.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Hunan, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Montane forests, often attached to trees; 100–600 m. Flowering: Feb.–May.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.
Notes: The type specimen was collected by J. G. Champion from Happy Valley between 1847 and 1850.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): North Point, Ma On Shan, Sai Kung, Tung Lung Chau
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Marsdenia lachnostoma Benth. 毛喉牛奶菜
FHK 226. 1861; FKH 172. 1912; FRPS 63: 450. 1977; FGD 1: 518, fig. 590. 1987; FOC 16: 248. 1995.

Lianas, suffrutescent, to 2 m or longer, stems, petioles and inflorescences thin pubescent, glabrescent. Petioles 6–17 mm; leaf blade ovate to oblong, 2.5–9 × 2–4 cm, base rounded or subcordate, apex acute or obtuse, abaxially pale or glaucous. Inflorescences umbel‑like, branched, compact, much shorter than leaves; peduncle 10–15 mm; pedicels 1.5–2 mm, ciliolate. Sepals ovate, 2 mm. Corolla campanulate, 3.5–4 mm; tube longer than lobes, with reflexed hairs inside and a very dense tuft of woolly hairs at throat, conspicuous in dried material; lobes oblong, glabrous except at base. Corona‑lobes ovate‑lanceolate, shorter than anthers; pollinia oblong or reniform. Stigma head conical. Follicles ellipsoidal, thickly walled, 4.5–5.5 × 1.5–2 cm. Seeds ca. 0.9–1.3 cm × 6–8 mm; coma 2–2.5 cm. Follicles oblong‑ovate or elliptic, 3.5–5 × 2–3 cm, glabrous, greenish; fruit stalk 2–2.5 cm; seeds broadly ovate or suborbicular, flat, 2–2.5 mm, margin membranous; coma white, 2–2.5cm.

Locality: North Point, Ma On Shan, Sai Kung, Tung Lung Chau. Y. S. Lau 1400; S. C. Ng 2170; HK sheet 38590.
Distribution: Hong Kong; Cambodia, Laos, Thailand.
Ecology: Thin forests or thickets. Flowering: May–Jul.; fruiting: Jul.–Nov.
Notes: The type specimen was collected by C. Wright from Hong Kong Island in 1854. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Marsdenia tinctoria R. Br. 藍葉藤
Mem. Wern. Nat. Hist. Soc. 1: 30. 1810; FHK 226. 1861; FKH 172. 1912; FRPS 63: 444, pl. 165. 1977; FGD 1: 516, fig. 588. 1987; FOC 16: 248. 1995.

Lianas to 5 m or longer, densely to sparsely pubescent when young, glabrescent. Petioles 1–4 cm; leaf blade oblong to broadly ovate, 5–13 × 2–7 cm, thin‑papery, bluish when dry, base rounded to cordate, apex acuminate, lateral veins 5–7(–10) on each side of midvein. Inflorescences densely flowered, globose to long raceme‑like cluster of cymules, (1.5–)3–15 cm; peduncle (0.5–)2.5–5 cm; pedicels 3–5 mm. Sepals suborbicular, ca. 2 mm. Corolla yellowish white, dark blue when dry, urceolate, 3.5–4(–6) mm, throat with a ring of hairs, otherwise glabrous; tube ca. 2.5 mm; lobes ovate, 1–1.5 mm, apex rounded. Corona‑lobes 5, lanceolate, as long as anther. Pollinia narrowly oblong. Stigma head discoid, slightly convex at apex. Follicles oblong‑lanceolate, 5–10 × 0.8–1 cm, pilose to sub‑tomentose. Seeds ovate, 1 × 0.3 cm; coma 1–2 cm.

Locality: Aberdeen. HK sheet 3917.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Taiwan; India, Indonesia, Myanmar, Philippines, Sri Lanka, Thailand, Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests or thickets. Flowering: Mar.–May; fruiting: Aug.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore)

Pentasachme caudatum Wall. ex Wight 石蘿藦
Contr. Bot. India 60. 1834; FOC 16: 262. 1995.
Pentasachme championii Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 5: 54. 1853; FHK 228. 1861; FKH 172. 1912; FRPS 63: 415, pl. 153. 1977; FGD 1: 499, fig. 564. 1987.

Herbs to 80 cm tall, branched, glabrous throughout. Petioles 1 – 2 mm; leaf blade linear‑lanceolate, 4–16 × 0.5–2 cm, midvein prominent on both surfaces, lateral veins obsolete. Cymes subsessile, much shorter than leaves, raceme‑like, 4 – 8‑flowered. Pedicels 0.3–2 cm. Sepals lanceolate, 1.5–3 × 1 mm. Corolla white; tube short; lobes linear‑lanceolate, 6–15 × 2 mm. Corona‑lobes white, thick, margin denticulate. Anthers laterally flattened; pollinia attached to caudicle at middle, retinaculum 1/3 of pollinia. Follicles cylindric‑lanceolate, 5–7.5 × 0.3 cm. Seeds minute; coma 1.5 cm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 2247; Y. S. Lau 420, 1804.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Jiangxi, Guangxi, Yunnan; Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Malaysia, Myanmar, Nepal, Singapore, Thailand, Vietnam.
Ecology: Streamsides in forests, open woodlands and thickets. Flowering: Feb.–Oct.; fruiting: May–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.
Notes: The type specimen was collected by J. G. Champion from Hong Kong Island between 1847 and 1850.

Telosma cordata (Burm. f.) Merr. 夜來香
Philipp. J. Sci. Bot. 19: 372. 1921; FRPS 63: 438, pl. 163. 1977; FGD 1: 514, fig. 586. 1987; FOC 16: 241. 1995.
Asclepias cordata Burm. f., Fl. Indica 72, fig. 2. 1768.

Lianas frutescent, latex white. Stems 1–10 m, yellowish green, pubescent when young, pale grey, glabrescent and usually sparsely lenticellate in age. Petioles 1.5–5 cm; leaf blade ovate, 4–12 × 3–10 cm, base deeply cordate with narrow sinus, apex acuminate, basal veins 3, lateral veins 6 on each side of midvein. Cymes umbel‑like, 15–30‑flowered. Peduncle 0.5–1.5 cm, puberulent. Sepals oblong‑lanceolate, puberulent. Corolla yellowish green; tube 6–10 × 4–6 mm, puberulent outside, pilose or glabrous with pilose throat inside; lobes oblong 6–12 × 3–6 mm, ciliate. Corona‑lobes slightly fleshy, basal part ovate, apex acuminate, often notched to deeply lobed, internal appendage often longer than lobe proper. Pollinia oblong or reniform. Stigma head capitate. Follicles lanceolate in outline, 7–13 × 2–3.5 cm, glabrous, somewhat obtusely 4‑angled. Seeds broadly ovate, 1 × 1 cm, flat, apex truncate, margin membranous; coma 3–4 cm.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 1276, 2999; Y. W. Lam 1127.
Distribution: Native to S China; widely cultivated in tropical and subtropical Asia, Europe and America.
Ecology: Flowering: May–Oct.; fruiting: Oct.–Dec.
Uses: Food (flowers edible), ornamental.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Mount Nicholson, Tai Mo Shan, Wong Chuk Yeung, Kai Kung Shan
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Toxocarpus fuscus Tsiang 鏽毛弓果藤
Sunyatsenia. 4: 81. 1939; FRPS 63: 288. 1977; FGD 1: 491, fig. 553. 1987; FOC 16: 197. 1995.

Lianas to 5 m. Young branchlets rusty pubescent, glabrescent and lenticellate with age. Petiole ca. 2.5 cm, rusty tomentose; leaf blade broadly ovate‑oblong, 9–15 × 5–5.8 cm, papery, adaxially glabrous except for rusty hairs along midvein, abaxially rusty pubescent, base rounded, apex acute or short acuminate; lateral veins 5–7 pairs. Cymes to 8.5 cm, shorter than leaves, few branched, 12–20‑flowered, rusty pubescent; peduncle less than 1 cm. Flower buds long acuminate. Pedicel ca. 5 mm. Sepals lanceolate, ca. 3 mm. Corolla yellow, ca. 9 mm, glabrous; lobes oblong‑lanceolate. Corona lobes ovate, longer than anthers, apex acute. Stigma head long beaked.

Locality: Mount Nicholson, Tai Mo Shan, Wong Chuk Yeung, Kai Kung Shan. F. W. Xing 8951.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan.
Ecology: Open woods. Flowering: May.

Toxocarpus wightianus Hook. & Arn. 弓果藤
Bot. Beechey. Voy. 200. 1836; FHK 224. 1861; FKH 170. 1912; FRPS 63: 284, pl. 97. 1977; FGD 1: 493, fig. 556. 1987; FOC 16: 197. 1995.
Toxocarpus ovalifolius Tsiang, Sunyatsenia 2: 193, pl. 35. 1934; FRPS 63: 282. 1977.

Lianas, slender, to 8 m.; branchlets tawny brown puberulent, lenticellate. Petioles 1–1.5 cm, rusty tomentose; leaf blade elliptic or elliptic‑oblong to ovate‑orbicular, 2.5–6 × 1.5–4.5 cm, somewhat leathery, base rounded to slightly cordate, apex acute to rounded or slightly emarginate, apiculate to cuspidate, glabrous, lateral veins 5–8 on each side of midvein. Cymes ± umbel‑like, to 10‑flowered, much shorter than leaves; peduncle to 6 mm, rusty pubescent. Pedicels 3 mm, minutely villous. Sepals ovate‑oblong, membranous, rusty tomentose. Corolla yellowish, ± rotate, glabrous; tube 2 × 3 mm; lobes narrowly lanceolate, 8 × 1–2 mm. Corona‑lobes triangular, 2 mm, obtuse. Pollinia minute. Stigma head fusiform. Follicles narrowly lanceolate in outline, 8–9 × 1 cm, divaricate at an angle 180–200°, densely rusty tomentose, pericarp thick. Seeds ovate‑oblong, 1 × 0.3–0.5 cm, not beaked; coma 3 cm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. S. P. Lau 184; Y. W. Lam 781, 808.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan; India, Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests and thickets. Flowering: Jun.–Aug.; fruiting: Aug.–Jan. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Tylophora ovata (Lindl.) Hook. ex Steud. 娃兒藤
Nomencl. Bot. (ed. 2) 2: 726. 1841; FRPS 63: 533, pl. 200. 1977; FGD 1: 535, fig. 616. 1987; FOC 16: 258. 1995.
Diplolepis ovata Lindl., Trans. Hort. Soc. London 6: 286. 1826.
Tylophora hispida Decne., Prodr. 8: 610. 1844; FHK 225. 1861; FKH 172. 1912.

Lianas, to 5 m, rusty hispid, villous, or pubescent except for adaxial surface of leaves and sometimes follicles. Petioles 0.5–3 cm; leaf blade ovate, 2.5–12.5(–16) × 1.2–9 cm, base cordate to subcordate, apex acute or short‑acuminate and mucronate, lateral veins 4–6 on each side of midvein. Inflorescences 4–13 cm; peduncle 0.5–2 cm; rachis simple, zigzag, occasionally forked. Cymules sessile, raceme‑like, densely flowered; pedicels threadlike, 5 – 10 mm. Sepals subulate‑acuminate to ovate, ciliate; basal glands 5 or absent. Corolla yellowish or yellow‑green, rotate, ca. 5 mm in diam., glabrous or puberulent; tube ca. 1 mm; lobes oblong‑ovate or ovate, ca. 1.5–2.5 × 1–1.2 mm, obtuse. Corona‑lobes ovoid, pouched, apex obtuse, covering the base of anthers. Anther with rounded appendages; pollinia globose to ovoid, horizontal. Ovaries glabrous; stigma head depressed. Follicles lanceolate to oblong‑lanceolate in outline, 40–70 × 3–12 mm, puberulent or glabrous, apex sometimes recurved. Seeds oval, 5–7 × 2–4 mm; coma 2–3.5 cm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 2339, 3226; P. S. Choi 543.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Pakistan, Nepal, Myanmar, Laos, Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests and thickets. Flowering: Apr.–Aug.; fruiting: Aug.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Brunfelsia calycina Benth. 大鴛鴦茉莉
Prodr. 10: 199. 1847; FGZ 579. 1956; FFJ 5: 5. 1993.

Evergreen shrubs, 1–1.5 m tall, much branched, glabrous or nearly so. Leaves alternate; petioles 3–5 mm; leaf blade oblong to elliptic‑oblong, 5.5–8.5(–10) × 1.5–3(–3.5) cm, base cuneate to broadly cuneate, apex acuminate, margin entire. Flowers solitary or in few‑flowered cymes; pedicels 1–2 mm. Calyx tubular, 12–16 mm, 5‑toothed. Corolla salverform; tube slender, 1.5–2 cm; limb spreading, 2.5–3.5 cm in diam., initially violet but change to white later. Stamens and style included. Fruit subglobse, berry‑like, pale yellow when mature, 5–7 mm in diam., indehiscent.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 34809.
Distribution: Native to Brazil; widely cultivated in tropical and subtropical regions.
Ecology: Flowering: Spring and autumn.
Uses: Ornamental.

Capsicum annuum L. 辣椒
Sp. Pl. 188. 1753; FHN 3: 469, fig. 861. 1974; FRPS 67(1): 62. 1978; FGD 2: 368. 1991; FOC 17: 313. 1994; FTW ed. 2, 4: 550. 1998.

Annual or perennial herbs, 50–80 cm tall. Stems much branched, woody at base. Leaves alternate or the upper paired or clustered; petioles 2–6 cm; leaf blade ovate to ovate‑lanceolate, 4–10 × 1.5–4 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate or acute, margin entire or obscurely sinuate, sparsely pubescent along midvein on adaxial surface, with tufts of hairs in axils of veins on abaxial surface. Flowers solitary in axils of leaves or branches. Calyx cup‑shaped, obscurely 5‑toothed. Corolla white, 5‑lobed. Stamens 5; anthers blue‑purple. Berry usually red, orange‑yellow, variously shaped.

Locality: Cultivated. S. P. Lau 21.
Distribution: Native to Mexico and S America; widely cultivated worldwide and naturalized in tropical and subtropical regions.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Summer to autumn.
Uses: Food (vegetable), additive (colouring, flavouring).
Notes: Three varieties of this species, C. annuum var. conoides (Mill.) Irish (朝天椒; Photo 103), C. annuum var. fasciculatum (Sturtev.) Irish (簇生椒) and C. annuum var. grossum (L.) Sendtn. (菜椒; Photo 104), are also cultivated.

Cestrum nocturnum L. 夜香樹
Sp. Pl. 191. 1753; FGZ 577. 1956; FRPS 67(1): 149, pl. 40: 6 – 10. 1978; FGD 2: 387, fig. 266: 1–3. 1991; FFJ 5: 6, fig. 4. 1993; FOC 17: 331. 1994.

Shrubs 2–3 m tall, with slender reclining branches, glabrous throughout. Leaves alternate; petioles 0.5–1 cm; leaf blade oblong‑ovate to oblong‑lanceolate, 5–15 × 2–4.5 cm, base subrounded or broadly cuneate, apex acuminate, ± oblique, margin entire. Flowers in terminal and axillary cymes, 5–10 cm, very fragrant at night. Pedicels ca. 0.5 mm. Calyx narrowly campanulate, 2.5–3 mm, apex 5‑toothed. Corolla salverform, pale green to cream‑coloured; tube slender, ca. 2 cm, slightly contracted at throat; apex 5‑lobed; lobes triangular, ca. 4 mm, erect or spreading. Stamens 5, attached to the upper part of corolla‑tube; filaments with a pair of dentoid appendages at the base; anthers reaching the throat. Ovary ovoid, with a short stipe; style equaling corolla‑tube; stigma capitate. Berry oblong, 6–7 mm, 1‑seeded.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 664, 2959; L. T. Lo 596.
Distribution: Native to S America; widely cultivated in tropical regions.
Ecology: Flowering: Jun.–Nov.
Uses: Ornamental.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Shek O, Ng Tung Chai, Tai Long Sai Wan, Ap Lei Chau, Ping Chau
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Datura metel L. 洋金花
Sp. Pl. 179. 1753; FHN 3: 470, fig. 863. 1974; FRPS 67(1): 147, pl. 38: 3–4. 1978; FGD 2: 386, fig. 265: 1–4. 1991; FOC 17: 330. 1994; FTW ed. 2, 4: 552, pl. 251. 1998.
Datura alba Rumph. ex Nees, Trans. Linn. Soc. London 17: 73. 1873; FHK 245. 1861; FKH 183. 1912.

Annual stout herbs, 50–150 cm tall, glabrous throughout. Stem erect, woody at base. Leaves alternate; petioles 2–6 cm; leaf blade ovate to broadly ovate, 5–20 × 4–15 cm, apex acuminate, base asymmetrical, rounded, truncate or cuneate, margin irregularly sinuate‑dentate, lobed or occasionally entire. Flowers solitary in branch forks or in axils of leaves; pedicels ca. 1 cm. Calyx tubular, 4–9 cm, with triangular or lanceolate lobes. Corolla long funnelform, 14–20 cm, white, yellowish, or pale purple; limb 6–10 cm in diam.; lobes broadly triangular, mucronate at apex. Stamens 5. Ovary bristly; style 11–16 cm. Capsule horizontal, subglobose or depressed globose, ca. 3 cm in diam., with short prickles, bursting irregularly in 4‑valves.

Locality: Shek O, Ng Tung Chai, Tai Long Sai Wan, Ap Lei Chau, Ping Chau. Y. S. Lau 2108; S. P. Lau 47; HK sheet 40300.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; widely naturalized or cultivated in tropical and subtropical regions.
Ecology: Wastelands and roadsides near villages. Flowering & fruiting: Mar.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Datura stramonium L. 曼陀羅
Sp. Pl. 1: 179. 1753; FRPS 67(1): 144, pl. 38: 1–2. 1978; FGD 2: 387, fig. 265: 5–7. 1991; FOC 17: 330. 1994.

Annual stout herbs or subshrubs, 30–150 cm tall, glabrescent or pubescent on the young parts. Stem erect, woody at base. Leaves alternate; petioles 2–5 cm; leaf blade broadly ovate or ovate, 6–18 × 4–12 cm, base asymmetrical cuneate, apex acuminate, margin irregularly sinuous or dentate‑lobed, lobes triangular; lateral veins 3–5 on each side of midvein. Flowers solitary in branch forks or in axils of leaves, erect; pedicels ca. 1 cm. Calyx tube 4–5 cm, 5‑angular, shallowly 5‑lobed. Corolla funnelform, 6–10 cm, white or pale purple; limb 3–5 cm in diam., shallowly 5‑lobed; lobes mucronate at apex. Stamens 5, included. Ovary bristly; style ca. 6 cm. Capsule erect, globose or ovoid, ca. 3–4.5 × 2–4 cm, with short prickles, bursting regularly in 4‑valves.

Locality: Cultivated. L. T. Lo 447.
Distribution: Widely naturalized or cultivated in tropical and subtropical regions.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Mar.–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Victoria Peak, Pok Fu Lam, Kowloon Peak, Shing Mun, Tai Mo Shan, Wang Shan Keuk Ha Tsuen
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Lycianthes biflora (Lour.) Bitter 紅絲線
Abh. Naturwiss. Vereine Bremen 24: 461. 1920; FHN 3: 466, fig. 859. 1974; FRPS 67(1): 122, pl. 30. 1978; FGD 2: 383, fig. 263. 1991; FOC 17: 326. 1994; FTW 2, 4: 552, pl. 252, photo 295. 1998.
Solanum biflorum Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 1: 129. 1790.
Solanum decemdentatum Roxb., Hort. Beng. 16. 1814; Fl. Ind. 2: 247. 1824; FKH 243. 1861.

Erect herbs or subshrubs, 0.5–1.5 m tall. Branchlets, petioles, pedicels and calyx densely covered with pale yellow, simple hairs and mixed with 1–2‑rayed hairs. Leaves solitary or the upper unequal paired; petioles 0.5–4 cm, narrowly winged; leaf blade sparsely pubescent adaxially, denser and mixed with 1–2‑rayed hairs abaxially; blade of the larger leaves elliptic‑ovate to oblong, 9–15 × 3.5–7 cm, base cuneate and decurrent to the petioles, apex acuminate; blade of smaller leaves broadly ovate, base broadly cuneate to rounded, apex shortly acuminate. Flowers usually 2, rarely 3–6 fascicled in axils of leaves; pedicels 5–13 mm. Calyx broadly campanulate, ca. 5 mm, with 10 subulate teeth. Corolla white or pale purple; tube ca. 1.5 mm; limb deeply 5‑lobed; lobes ovate to narrowly ovate, ca. 6 × 1.5 mm. Stamens 5; filaments ca. 1 mm; anthers ca. 3 mm, opening by subapical and introrse pores. Ovary ovoid, glabrous; style slender, ca. 8 mm. Berry globose, 6–8 mm in diam., red when mature.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Pok Fu Lam, Kowloon Peak, Shing Mun, Tai Mo Shan, Wang Shan Keuk Ha Tsuen. Y. S. Lau 302, 2306; L. T. Lo 648.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; S and SE Asia to Malaysia.
Ecology: Ravines, streamsides and other wet places. Flowering: May–Aug.; fruiting: Jul.–Nov.

Lycium chinense Mill. 枸杞
Gard. Dict. ed. 8, no. 5. 1768; FHK 245. 1861; FKH 183. 1912; FHN 3: 470, fig. 862. 1974; FRPS 67(1): 15, pl. 3: 1–4. 1978; FGD 2: 364, fig. 247. 1991; FFJ 5: 5, fig. 3. 1993; FTW ed. 2, 4: 557, pl. 254, photo 297. 1998.

Shrubs, 50–100 cm tall, glabrous, much branched; branches often with spines. Leaves alternate, or in clusters of 2–4; petioles 4–10 mm; leaf blade lanceolate‑oblong or obovate, 1.5–5 × 0.5–2.5 cm, base cuneate, apex acute or obtuse, margin entire. Flowers solitary or in pairs on long shoots, or clustered with leaves on short shoots. Pedicels 1–2 cm. Calyx 3–4 mm, 3–5‑lobed. Corolla funnelform, 9–12 mm, pale purple, limb broadly campanulate, deeply 5‑lobed; lobes ovate, apex rounded. Stamens 5, exserted. Berries ovoid or shortly oblong, 7–15 mm, orange‑red.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 1508; L. T. Lo 50; HK sheet 34820.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; also in Korea and Japan.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Nov.
Uses: Food (vegetable), medicinal (folklore).

Lycopersicon esculentum Mill. 番茄
Gard. Dict. ed. 8, no. 2. 1768; FHN 3: 467. 1974; FRPS 67(1): 137, pl. 35. 1978; FGD 2: 385, fig. 264. 1991; FOC 17: 329. 1994; FTW ed. 2, 4: 557. 1998.

Annual herbs, erect or sprawling, 1–2 m tall, viscid pubescent and strong‑smelling. Leaves odd‑pinnate, ovate‑oblong in outline, unequal, 10–35 cm or longer; leaflets usually 5–9, ovate or oblong, 5–7(–12) × 2–5 cm, base oblique, apex acuminate, margin irregularly toothed or lobed. Cymes lateral, 5–8 cm, 3–7‑flowered; peduncles 2–4 cm; pedicels 1–1.5 cm. Calyx deeply 5‑lobed; lobes lanceolate. Corolla rotate, yellow, ca. 2 cm in diam. Berry red or yellow, usually subglobose, flattened at the ends.

Locality: Cultivated. S. Y. Hu 5341, 9025, 12904 (CUHK).
Distribution: Native to Mexico and S America; widely cultivated throughout the world.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Summer to autumn.
Uses: Food (vegetable, fruit).

Nicandra physalodes (L.) Gaertn. 假酸漿
Fruct. Sem. Pl. 2: 237. 1791; FRPS 67(1): 6. 1978; FOC 17: 301. 1994.
Atropa physalodes L., Sp. Pl. 1: 181. 1753.

Annual herbs, up to 1 m tall; stems erect, angular, glabrescent or sparsely pubescent. Leaves alternate; petiole 1.5–6 cm; leaf blade ovate or elliptic, 4–12(–20) × 2–8(–13) cm, apex acute or shortly acuminate, base cuneate, margin coarsely sinuate‑dentate or lobed, papery, sparsely pubescent on both surfaces. Flowers solitary, axillary or in branch forks. Pedicel 1.5–4 cm. Calyx 0.8–3 cm, deeply 5‑parted; lobes broadly ovate, apex acute, base cordate‑sagittate, with 2 acute auricles. Corolla pale blue, blue‑purple, or bluish with white center, 2.5–4 cm in diam. Berry brown or yellow, 1–2 cm in diam. Seeds pale brown, 1–1.2 mm in diam.

Locality: Naturalized. Y. S. Lau 2995.
Distribution: Naturalized in Gansu, Guizhou, Hebei, Sichuan, Xinjiang, Xizang, Yunnan; a widely distributed weed, native to Peru.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides near villages. Flowering & fruiting: Summer to autumn.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.

Nicotiana tabacum L. 煙草
Sp. Pl. 180. 1753; FHN 3: 471. 1974; FRPS 67(1): 152, pl. 39. 1978; FGD 2: 389, fig. 267: 1–2. 1991; FOC 17: 332. 1994.

Annual herbs, 0.5–2 m tall, viscid‑pubescent throughout. Leaves alternate, sessile or nearly so; leaf blade oblong‑lanceolate, lanceolate to oblong‑ovate, 10–30(–70) × 8–15(–30) cm, base attenuate, auriculate or semi‑amplexicaul, apex acuminate, margin entire or slightly sinuate. Panicles terminal, many‑flowered; pedicels 5 – 20 mm. Calyx tubular or tubular‑campanulate, 5‑lobed; lobes triangular‑lanceolate. Corolla funnelform, pink; tube 4 – 6.5 cm; limb 1.5–2 cm in diam., 5‑lobed. Stamens 5; filaments pubescent at base. Ovary 2‑locular; stigma 2‑lobed. Capsule ovoid, ca. 1.5 cm, many‑seeded.

Locality: Cultivated. L. T. Lo 129; Y. S. Lau 2107, 2552.
Distribution: Native to S America; cultivated elsewhere.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Oct.
Uses: Tobacco (source of nicotine).

Petunia hybrida Hort. ex Vilm. 碧冬茄
Fl. Pleine Terre 1: 615–616. 1863; FRPS 67(1): 154, pl. 40: 1–5. 1978; FGD 2: 390, fig. 268. 1991; FOC 17: 332. 1994.

Annual herbs, 30–60 cm tall, much branched, viscid‑pubescent throughout. Leaves alternate or the upper opposite; petioles short or almost obsolete; leaf blade ovate, 3–8 × 1.5–4.5 cm, base broadly cuneate, apex acute, margin entire. Flowers solitary in axils of leaves; pedicels 3–5 cm. Calyx 5‑lobed to near base; lobes linear, 1–1.5 cm, obtuse, persistent. Corolla funnelform, 5–7 cm, white, purple or violet; limb shallowly 5‑lobed, 5–7 cm in diam. Stamens 5, inserted in the lower part of corolla‑tube, 4 long, the fifth shorter. Ovary 2‑locular. Capsule conical, ca. 1 cm opening by 2 valves when mature.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 1885.
Distribution: A hybrid of garden origin, cultivated elsewhere.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Summer to autumn.
Uses: Ornamental.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Deep Water Bay, Mai Po, Tai Po
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Physalis angulata L. 苦蘵
Sp. Pl. 183. 1753; FHK 244. 1861; FKH 183. 1912; FRPS 67(1): 56, pl. 15: 3–4. 1978; FGD 2: 366, fig. 249: 1–4. 1991; FOC 17: 312. 1994; FTW ed. 2, 4: 560, pl. 255, photo 298. 1998.

Annual herbs. 30–50 cm tall, much branched, sparsely pubescent or glabrescent. Leaves alternate; petioles 1–5 cm; leaf blade ovate, oblong or almost lanceolate, 3–6 × 2–4 cm, base broadly cuneate or cuneate, apex acuminate or acute, margin entire or with a few coarse irregular teeth, almost glabrous on both surfaces. Flowers solitary in axils of leaves; pedicels 5–12 mm. Calyx campanulate, 4–5 mm, 5‑lobed to middle; lobes lanceolate, as are the pedicels sparsely and shortly pubescent. Corolla 4–8 mm, pale yellow, often marked with 5 purple spots near the throat, shallowly 5‑lobed; limb 6–8 mm in diam. Stamens 5; anthers blue‑purple or yellow. Fruiting calyx globular, 1.5–2.5 in diam., papery, pale green. Berry globose, ca. 1.2 cm in diam., completely enclosed by the persistent calyx.

Locality: Deep Water Bay, Mai Po, Tai Po. P. S. Choi 415; Y. W. Lam 2210; HK sheet 35170.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Hubei, Henan, Anhui, Jiangxi, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; widely spread over tropical and subtropical region.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides near villages. Flowering & fruiting: May–Dec.

Solanum americanum Mill. 少花龍葵
Gard. Dict. ed. 8, no. 5. 1768; FFJ 5: 9. 1993; FOC 17: 317. 1994; TW ed. 2, 4: 564, pl. 256. 1998.
Solanum photeinocarpum Nakam. & Odash., J. Soc. Trop. Agric. 8: 54, fig. 2. 1936; FRPS 76(1): 77. 1978.

Annual herbs, 25–100 cm tall. Stems glabrous or nearly so. Leaves simple; petioles slender, 1–2 cm, sparsely pubescent; leaf blade ovate or ovate‑oblong, 4–8 × 2–4 cm, base cuneate, decurrent to the petiole, apex acuminate, margin subentire, sinuate or irregularly and coarsely toothed, sparsely pubescent on both surfaces. Cymes extra‑axillary, 3–6(–10)‑flowered, almost contracted into umbels; peduncles 1–2.5 cm; pedicels 5–8 mm. Calyx small, 5‑lobed to middle; lobes ovate. Corolla white, sometimes with a yellow eye, 5‑lobed to middle or beyond middle; lobes ovate‑oblong, 3–4 mm, pubescent abaxially. Stamens 5; filaments short, pubescent. Ovary ovoid, white‑tomentose on the lower part. Berry globose, ca. 5 mm in diam., black when mature.

Locality: Naturalized in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 530.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; perhaps native to S America, widely spread to all tropical and warm regions.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides near villages. Flowering & fruiting: Nearly all year round.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Solanum capsicoides All. 牛茄子（癲茄）
Philos. Math. Soc. Roy. Turin 5: 64. 1773; FOC 17: 323. 1994; FTW ed. 2, 4: 564. 1998.
Solanum surattense acut. non Burm. f.: FRPS 67(1): 105, pl. 27: 3–5. 1978.

Herbs or subshrubs, 0.5–1 m tall. Stems and branches glabrous or pilose, with pale yellow straight prickles. Leaves simple; petioles stout, 2–7 cm; leaf blade broadly ovate, 5–13 × 4–12 cm, base cordate, apex acute or acuminate, margin 5–7‑lobed to middle, pubescent on adaxial surface, glabrous, or hairy only along veins on abaxial surface, with prickles along veins on both surfaces. Cymes 1–4‑flowered, extra‑axillary; peduncle short or obsolete; pedicels 5–12 mm. Calyx 5–8 mm, 5‑lobed beyond middle; lobes ovate, pubescent. Corolla white, greenish at base, tube ca. 2.5 mm; limb deeply 5‑lobed; lobes lanceolate, ca. 10 × 4 mm. Stamens 5; filaments ca. 2.5 mm. Ovary ovoid, glabrous. Berry subglobose, 3.5 – 6 cm in diam., initially stellate‑tomentose, orange‑red when mature.

Locality: Naturalized in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1345; HK sheet 19995.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Jiangsu, Fujian, Taiwan; perhaps native to Brazil, but widely spread over warm regions.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides near villages and thickets. Flowering: Summer to autumn; fruiting: Autumn to winter.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Solanum erianthum D. Don 假煙葉樹
Prodr. Fl. Nepal. 96. 1825; FFJ 5: 12, fig. 11. 1993; FOC 17: 316. 1994; FTW ed. 2, 4: 566. 1998.
Solanum verbascifolium auct. non L.: FKH 183. 1912; FRPS 67(1): 72. 1978.

Shrubs or small trees, 1.5–10 m tall, densely tomentose. Leaves simple; petioles thick, 1.5–5.5 cm; leaf blade ovate‑oblong, 10–29 × 4–12 cm, base broadly cuneate or obtuse, apex shortly acuminate, margin entire or obscurely sinuate, adaxially green, abaxially greyish green; lateral veins 7–9 on each side of midvein. Cymes corymbose, subterminal; peduncle 3–10 cm; pedicels 3 – 5 mm. Calyx campanulate, 5‑lobed to middle. Corolla white, tube as long as calyx; limb ca. 1.5 cm in diam., deeply 5‑lobed; lobes oblong. Stamens 5; filaments 1–1.5 mm. Ovary ovoid, densely stellate‑tomentose. Berry globose, ca. 1.5 cm in diam., initially stellate‑tomentose, glabrescent, yellowish brown when mature.

Locality: Naturalized in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 240, 477, 2948.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Fujian, Taiwan; native to S America, widespread in tropical Asia and Australia.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides near villages. Flowering & fruiting: Almost all year round.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Sai Kung, Mau Ping, Shing Mun, Tai Po, Sha Tau Kok
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Solanum lasiocarpum Dunal 毛茄
Hist. Nat. Solanum 222. 1813; FOC 17: 323. 1994; FTW ed. 2, 4: 567, photo: 300. 1998.
Solanum ferox auct. non L.: FHK 243. 1861; FKH 183. 1912; FRPS 67(1): 110, pl. 27: 6–9. 1978.

Herbs or subshrubs, 1–1.5 m tall, densely covered with pale yellow stellate hairs throughout. Stems and branches with flat, erect or slightly recurved prickles. Leaves simple; petioles 3–8 cm, often prickly; leaf blade ovate, 10–20 × 8–18 cm, base truncate or subhastate, apex acute, margin with 5–11 sinuate lobes, pubescent and prickly along veins on both surfaces. Scorpioid cymes extra‑axillary, several‑flowered; peduncle ca. 3 mm; pedicels ca. 1 cm. Calyx cup‑shaped, 5‑lobed beyond middle; lobe ovate‑lanceolate, ca. 8 mm. Corolla white, tube ca. 1 mm; limb ca. 2 cm in diam., deeply 5‑lobed; lobes ovate‑lanceolate, ca. 1 cm. Stamens 5; filaments very short. Ovary ovoid, pubescent. Berry globose, ca. 2 cm in diam., covered with tawny hairs.

Locality: Sai Kung, Mau Ping, Shing Mun, Tai Po, Sha Tau Kok. Y. S. Lau 479, 1344; L. T. Lo 220.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Taiwan; widely distributed in SE Asia.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides. Flowering: Summer; fruiting: Autumn to winter.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Solanum mammosum L. 乳茄（五代同堂茄）
Sp. Pl. 187. 1753; FRPS 67(1): 106, pl. 21: 15 – 19. 1978; FOC 17: 323. 1994
Stout herbs, to 1 m tall. Stems and branches covered with articulate hairs, glandular hairs and compressed prickles. Leaves simple; petioles 2.5–8 cm; leaf blade ovate, 5–10 × 4.5–9.5 cm, base ± cordate, apex acute or obtuse, margin irregularly and coarsely (3–)5(–7)‑lobed; lobes triangular, both surfaces densely covered with hairs, and with prickles on the midvein and veins. Scorpioid cymes extra‑axillary, 2–4‑flowered, sometimes reduced to 1 flower; peduncle 3–10 mm; pedicels 5–10 mm. Calyx shallowly cup‑shaped, deeply 5‑lobed; lobes ovate‑lanceolate. Corolla violet; tube ca. 1.5 mm; limb ca. 1.8 cm in diam., deeply 5‑lobed; lobes lanceolate. Stamens 5; filaments ca. 1.5 mm. Ovary ovoid, glabrous or nearly so. Berry inverse pear‑shaped, 4.5–5.5 cm, often with 4–5 protuberances at base, yellow when mature.

Locality: Cultivated. K. L. Yip 4413, 4475.
Distribution: Native to Brazil; widely cultivated in tropical regions.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Oct.
Uses: Ornamental.

Solanum melongena L. 茄（矮瓜）
Sp. Pl. 186. 1753; FRPS 67(1): 118. 1978; FFJ 5: 18, fig. 19. 1993; FOC 17: 325. 1994.

Annual herbs or shrubby, to 1 m tall. Branches often purplish and stellate‑tomentose when young, glabrescent. Leaves simple; petioles thick, 2–4.5 cm, stellate‑tomentose; leaf blade ovate to oblong‑ovate, 8–18 × 5–11 cm, base broadly cuneate or subrounded, oblique, apex obtuse, margin shallowly or deeply sinuate‑lobed, stellate‑tomentose and sometimes with a few prickles on both surfaces; lateral veins 4–5 on each side of midvein. Flowers usually solitary; peduncle obsolete; pedicels 1–1.8 cm, stellate‑tomentose. Calyx stellate‑tomentose, 5‑lobed to middle; lobes lanceolate. Corolla purplish or violet; tube ca. 2 mm; limb 3(–5) cm in diam., deeply 5‑lobed; lobes triangular. Stamens 5; filaments ca. 2.5 mm; anthers ca. 7.5 mm. Ovary ovoid, apex densely stellate‑tomentose. Berry greatly variable in shape and size, usually subglobose or cylindric, more than 6 cm in diam., purple, white or yellow when mature.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 20078.
Distribution: Probably originated from SE Asia; widely cultivated from tropical to temperate regions.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Summer to autumn.
Uses: Food (vegetable), medicinal (folklore).

Solanum nigrum L. 龍葵
Sp. Pl. 186. 1753; FHK 242. 1861; FKH 183. 1912; FRPS 67(1): 76, pl. 19: 1–6, 1978; FFJ 5: 9, fig. 6. 1993; FOC 17: 318. 1994; FTW ed. 2, 4: 571, pl. 259, photo 302. 1998.

Annual or biennial herbs, 30–100 cm tall, glabrous or nearly so. Leaves simple; petioles 1–2 cm; leaf blade ovate, 2.5–10 × 1.5–5.5 cm, base cuneate to broadly cuneate, apex shortly acute, margin entire or irregularly and coarsely toothed; lateral veins 5–6 on each side of midvein. Scorpioid cymes extra‑axillary, 3–6(–10)‑flowered, almost contracted into umbels on short (2–4 cm) lateral peduncles; pedicels 5–12 mm. Calyx small, shallowly cup‑shaped, 5‑toothed. Corolla white; limb ca. 9 mm in diam., deeply 5‑lobed; lobes ovate. Stamens 5; filaments very short. Ovary ovoid, white‑tomentose on the lower part. Berry globose, ca. 8 mm in diam., black when mature.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. S. P. Lau 9; Y. S. Lau 2361; Y. W. Lam 441.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; also in warm regions of Asia, Europe and America.
Ecology: Wastelands and roadsides. Flowering & fruiting: Summer to autumn.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Solanum torvum Sw. 水茄
Prodr. 47. 1788; FRPS 67(1): 95. pl. 26: 7–8. 1978; FFJ 5: 15, fig. 16. 1993; FOC 17: 321. 1994; FTW ed. 2, 4: 576, pl. 262, photo 304. 1998.

Shrubs 1–3 m tall, sparsely armed with pale yellow or reddish prickles. Branchlets, petioles, abaxial surface of leaves and peduncles densely covered with tawny stellate hairs. Leaves solitary or in pairs; petioles thick, 2–4 cm; leaf blade ovate to elliptic, 6–19 × 4–13 cm, base cordate or cuneate, ± oblique, apex acute, margin 5 – 7‑lobed or sinuate, densely covered with stellate hairs on both surfaces; lateral veins 3–5 on each side of midvein, unarmed or sometimes prickly. Cymes extra‑axillary, 2–3‑branched; peduncle 1–1.5 cm, sometimes prickly; pedicels 5–10 mm. Calyx cup‑shaped, covered with stellate and glandular hairs abaxially, apex 5‑lobed. Corolla white; tube ca. 1.5 mm; limb ca. 1.5 cm in diam., deeply 5‑lobed; lobes ovate‑lanceolate, ca. 8 mm. Stamens 5; filaments ca. 1 mm; anthers ca. 7 mm. Ovary ovoid, glabrous. Berry globose, 1–1.5 cm in diam., glabrous, yellowish when mature.

Locality: Naturalized in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1949; L. T. Lo 78; HK sheet 39452.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, S Xizang, Fujian, Taiwan; native to Caribbean; widely naturalized in tropical regions.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides near villages. Flowering & fruiting: Almost all year round.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Solanum tuberosum L. 馬鈴薯
Sp. Pl. 185. 1753; FHN 3: 463. 1974; FRPS 67(1): 94, pl. 23: 7–10. 1978; FOC 17: 320. 1994.

Perennial herbs, 30–80 cm tall, with subterranean tubers; tubers globose, oblate, or ellipsoidal, 3–10 cm in diam. Leaves odd‑pinnate, ovate in outline, 10–20 cm or longer; leaflets 3 or 4 pairs, mixed with small irregular lobes on the rachis, ovate or oblong, unequal, (1–)2 – 6(–8) × 1–4.5 cm, base rounded, apex acute, margin entire, sparsely pilose on both surfaces. Flowers in subterminal, leaf opposed, or axillary sparingly branched panicles. Calyx campanulate, sparsely pilose; lobes 5, lanceolate. Corolla rotate, white, pink or blue‑purple, 2.5–3 cm in diam.; limb 5‑lobed, lobes triangular. Ovary ovoid, glabrous. Berry globose, smooth, ca. 1.5 cm in diam.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 3328.
Distribution: Native to S America; cultivated worldwide.
Ecology: Flowering: Summer.
Uses: Food.

Solanum undatum Lam. 野茄
Tab Encycl. 2: 22. 1793; FOC 17: 325. 1994; FTW ed. 2, 4: 578. 1998.
Solanum cumingii Dunal, Prodr. 13(1): 363. 1852; FRPS 67(1): 119. 1978.
Solanum coagulans auct. non Forssk.: FRPS 67(1): 116. 1978; Check List HK Plants 220. 2002; 76. 2004.
Solanum sanctum auct. non L.: FHK 243. 1861.
Soanum incanum auct. non L.: FKH 182. 1912.

Herbs or subshrubs, 0.5–1.5 m tall. Stems and branches shaggy‑tomentose with stellate hairs, glabrescent, sparingly armed with prickles. Leaves unequal paired; petioles 1–4 cm; leaf blade ovate or elliptic, 15–14 × 4–7 cm, base obtuse or truncate, apex acute or obtuse, margin 5(–7)‑sinuate lobed, both surfaces densely shaggy‑tomentose with stellate hairs, and with short stout prickles along veins. Scorpioid cymes extra‑axillary; peduncles very short; pedicels 0.5–2 cm. Calyx campanulate, 6–9 mm, 5‑lobed beyond middle; lobes triangular lanceolate. Corolla purple blue or white; limb 1.5–3 cm in diam., deeply 5‑lobed; lobes broadly triangular or ovate. Stamens 5; filaments 1.5–1.8 mm; anthers 5–8 mm. Ovary ovoid, glabrous. Berry globose, 2–3 cm in diam., glabrous, yellow when mature.

Locality: Tai Po, Sheung Shui. Y. S. Lau 475, 2945; L. T. Lo 260.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; widely distributed in SW and SE Asia, also in Africa.
Ecology: Thickets. Flowering: Summer; fruiting: Autumn to winter.

Solanum violaceum Ortega 刺天茄
Nov. Pl. Descr. Dec. 56. 1798; FOC 17: 322. 1994; FTW ed. 2, 4: 578, pl. 263, photo 305. 1998.
Solanum chinense Dunal, Hist. Nat. Solanum 240. 1813.
Solanum indicum auct. non L.: FHK 242. 1861; FKH 182. 1912; FRPS 67(1): 100, pl. 26: 1–6. 1978; Check List HK Plants 220. 2002; 77. 2004.

Shrubs 0.5–2 m tall, much branched. Branchlets sparingly prickled and densely tawny grey stellate‑tomentose. Leaves simple, unequal‑paired; petioles thick, 1.5–4 cm, densely stellate‑tomentose and sparingly prickled; leaf blade ovate, 5–11 × 2–8.5 cm, base cordate or truncate, apex obtuse or acute, margin 5–7 sinuate‑lobed, adaxial surface tomentose with short‑stalked, stellate hairs, abaxial surface with long‑stalked hairs and straight needle‑like prickles; lateral veins 3–4 on each side of midvein. Scorpioid cymes extra‑axillary, 2–6 cm; peduncle ca. 1.5 cm; pedicels 4–15 mm, pubescent and prickly. Calyx cup‑shaped, 4–7 mm, 5‑lobed beyond middle; lobes lanceolate, 3–5 mm. Corolla blue‑purple or white; tube ca. 1.5 mm; limb 1–2 cm in diam., deeply 5‑lobed; lobes ovate to ovate‑lanceolate, 5–8 × 2–5 mm, obtuse. Stamens 5; filaments ca. 1 mm; anthers oblong, 5–6 mm. Berry globose, 0.8–1.3 cm in diam., shiny orange when mature.

Locality: Tai Po, Fanling. W. J. Tutcher 9175; Y. S. Lau 476; HK sheet 36079.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Fujian, Taiwan; widely spread over tropical Asia.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides, thickets. Flowering & fruiting: Almost all year round.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Solanum wrightii Benth. 大花茄
FHK 243. 1861; FKH 183. 1912; FRPS 67(1): 115. 1978; FOC 17: 322. 1994.

Trees to 10 m tall. Branches and petioles hispid with stiff stellate hairs or bristles, and armed with a few straight stout prickles. Leaves simple; petioles 5–10 cm; leaf blade broadly ovate, 25–30 × 15–20 cm, base oblique, apex acute or obtuse, margin entire or sinuate lobed, with irregular ovate or lanceolate lobes, scabrid with dispersed bristle‑like hairs on adaxial surface, coarsely stellate‑hairy on abaxial surface. Cymes many‑flowered, axillary or extra‑axillary; peduncles unbranched or bifid; pedicels 0.6–1.5 cm, very hispid. Calyx 1–1.5 cm, densely hispid, deeply 5‑lobed; lobes lanceolate, apex long‑subulate. Corolla initially deep purple, gradually fading through blue to white; limb 6–9 cm in diam., 5‑lobed to 1/3 of its length, the lanceolate center of each lobe stellate‑hairy outside.
