Stamens 5; filaments 2–3 mm; anthers 1.2–1.5 cm. Berry globose, 3–4 cm in diam., red when mature.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 4101, 4102, 4103.
Distribution: Tropical and subtropical regions; native to Bolivia and Brazil.
Ecology: Flowering: Summer to autumn.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: The type specimen of this species was collected by C. Wright from Hong Kong Island between 1853 and 1854. Bentham (1861) described this species based on a plant cultivated in Hong Kong. Dunn & Tutcher (1912) last recorded the species on the Bonham Road, Hong Kong.

Argyreia acuta Lour. 白鶴藤
Fl. Cochinch. 135. 1790; FGZ 588. 1956; FHN 3: 494, fig. 878. 1974; FRPS 64(1): 135. 1979; FOC 16: 320. 1995; FGD 4: 342, fig. 203. 2000.
Lettsomia chalmersii Hance, J. Bot. 16(188): 230. 1878.

Twining vine. Stems terete, densely silvery sericeous when young, later yellowish or glabrescent. Petiole 3–4(–6) cm; leaf blade elliptic, ovate or suborbicular, 5–12 × 3–8(–11) cm, base rounded, slightly cordate, or truncate, adaxially glabrous, abaxially firmly appressed silvery sericeous. Cymes many‑flowered, axillary or terminal; peduncle 3.5–7 cm, silvery sericeous; bracts elliptic or obovate, 0.8–2.2 cm, silvery sericeous abaxially, deciduous. Pedicel ca. 5 mm. Sepals ovate‑oblong, unequal; outer ones 9–12 mm; inner ones 6–7 mm, silvery apex obtuse, sericeous abaxially. Corolla white, funnelform, ca. 2.8 cm, silvery sericeous abaxially; limb deeply 5‑lobed; lobes oblong, 1.5 mm, apex emarginate, midpetaline bands slivery sericeous. Stamens exserted; filaments hairy at base. Pistil exserted; ovary glabrous, 2‑locular. Berry enclosed by enlarged calyx, red, globose, ca. 8 mm in diam. Fruiting sepals leathery, red inside. Seeds 2–4, brown, ovoid‑trigonous, ca. 5 mm.

Locality: Victoria Peak. HK sheet 33906.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi; India, Vietnam, Laos.
Ecology: Thin forests and thickets. Flowering: Aug.–Oct.; fruiting: Oct.–Jan. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Castle Peak, Shek Kong, Lam Tsuen
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Argyreia capitiformis (Poir.) Ooststr. 頭花銀背藤
Fl. Malesiana, ser. 1. 6(6): 941. 1972; FOC 16: 317. 1995.
Convolvulus capitiformis Poir., Encycl. Suppl. 3: 469. 1814.
Convolvulus capitatus Vahl, Symb. Bot. 3: 28. 1794
Argyreia capitata (Vahl) Choisy, Mém. Soc. Phys. Genève 6: 423. 1833; FHN 3: 494. 1974; FRPS 64(1): 129. 1979; FGD 4: 342. 2000; Check List HK Plants 221. 2002; 77. 2004.
Argyreia verrucosohispida Y. Y. Qian, Guihaia 11(3): 211, fig. 2. 1991.
Ipomoea capitata (Vahl) Roem. & Schult., Syst. Veg. 4: 238. 1819
Lettsomia capitata (Vahl) Benth. & Hook. f., Gen. Pl. 2(2): 870. 1876.
Lettsomia capitiformis (Poir.) Kerr, Fl. Siam. 3(2): 30. 1954.
Lettsomia strigosa Roxb., Fl. Ind., ed. 1832, 1: 491. 1832; FKH 178. 1912.

Scandent shrub, 10–15 m tall. Stems spreading brown hirsute. Petiole 3–10 cm; leaf blade papery, ovate to suborbicular, rarely oblong, 7–18 × 4–13 cm, base cordate, apex acute or acuminate, dull yellow hirsute on both surfaces. Cymes capitate, dense, many‑flowered; peduncle 6 – 15 cm, spreading hirsute; bracts persistent, elliptic to lanceolate, 1.5–4 cm, both ends acute, hirsute abaxially. Pedicel short or absent. Sepals long‑ovate to broadly lanceolate, apex acuminate, densely hirsute abaxially, outer 3 sepals ca. 1.5 cm, inner 2 sepals 1–1.2 cm. Corolla pink to reddish purple, funnelform, 4–5 cm, hirsute abaxially; limb shallowly lobed or subentire. Stamens and pistil inclusive; filaments ca. 1.5 cm, glandular pilose basally. Ovary ovoid, glabrous, 2‑locular. Berries orange‑red, globose, ca. 8 mm in diam. Seeds 4 or fewer, ovoid‑trigonous, ca. 7 mm.

Locality: Castle Peak, Shek Kong, Lam Tsuen. L. Gibbs 7651; Y. S. Lau 2409, 3076.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan; India, Myanmar, Thailand, Vietnam, Laos, Cambodia, to Malay Peninsula, Indonesia.
Ecology: Forests or thickets. Flowering: Sep.–Dec.; fruiting: Feb.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Glenealy, Victoria Peak, Castle Peak, Plover Cove, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Argyreia mollis (Burm. f.) Choisy 銀背藤
Mém. Soc. Phys. Genève. 6: 421. 1833; FOC 16: 315. 1995.
Convolvulus mollis Burm. f., Fl. Indica 44, t. 17. 1768.
Argyreia championii Benth., FHK 236. 1861.
Argyreia obtecta (Choisy) C. B. Clarke, Fl. Brit. India 4(10): 186. 1883.
Lettsomia championii (Benth.) Benth. & Hook. f., Gen. Pl. 2: 879. 1876; FKH 178. 1912.
Argyreia obtusifolia auct. non Lour.: FHN 3: 494. 1974; FRPS 64(1): 120. 1979; FGD 4: 341. 2000; Check List HK Plants 221. 2002; 77. 2004.

Large twining vine, to 10 m tall. Stems densely pubescent when young. Petiole 1.5–4 cm, pubescent; leaf blade elliptic to oblong, 7–11 × 2.5–7 cm, base broadly cuneate or rotund, apex shortly acuminate, acute or obtuse, adaxially sparsely strigose or glabrous, abaxially densely pale yellow pubescent. Cymes (1–)5–7‑flowered. Peduncle 2.5–3.5 cm, densely pale yellow pubescent; bracts caducous, ovate, ca. 5 mm. Pedicel 0.5–1.5 cm. Sepals unequal, densely firmly appressed pubescent abaxially, enlarged in fruit; outer 2 broadly elliptic, 8–10 mm; inner 3 oblong, slightly shorter. Corolla pale red or pale purple, broadly campanulate, 4–5 cm, midpetaline bands appressed pubescent abaxially; limb ± entire or slightly lobed. Stamens and pistil inclusive; filaments pilose at base. Ovary glabrous, 4‑locular. Berry red or orange‑red, subglobose, 0.8–1 cm in diam. Seeds 4 or fewer, black, ca. 5 mm.

Locality: Glenealy, Victoria Peak, Castle Peak, Plover Cove, Lantau Island. S. T. Dunn 5147; H. C. Tang 2158; Y. S. Lau 1310.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong; Vietnam, Laos, Cambodia, Thailand, Myanmar, Malay Peninsula.
Ecology: Dense forests. Flowering & fruiting: Sep. – Feb. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: Convolvulus sericeus L. (Mant. Pl. 43. 1767) was included in the synonymy of this species. If Convolvulus sericeus L. is conspecific with this species, a new combination should be made.

Argyreia nervosa (Burm. f.) Bojer 美麗銀背藤
Hortus Maurit. 224. 1837; FRPS 64(1): 123, pl. 29: 2–3. 1979; FGD 4: 341. 2000.
Convolvulus nervosus Burm. f., Fl. Indica 48, pl. 20, fig. 1. 1768.
Argyreia speciosa (L. f.) Sweet, Hort. Brit. 289. 1827; FKH 178. 1912.
Lettsomia nervosa (Burm. f.) Roxb., Fl. Ind., ed. 1820, 2: 78. 1824.
Rivea nervosa (Burm. f.) Hallier f., Bull. Herb. Boissier 5: 381. 1897.

Vine. Stems densely white pubescent when young, glabrescent. Petiole shorter than or as long as leaves, tomentose; leaf blade ovate to orbicular, 10–30 × 8–25 cm, base cordate, apex acute or obtuse, glabrous adaxially, white or greyish white pubescent abaxially. Cymes many‑flowered. Peduncle to 20 cm or longer, tomentose. Bracts large, ovate to elliptic, caducous. Pedicels short, angular. Sepals subequal, ovate to broadly ovate, 1.5–2 cm, apex obtuse or acute, tomentose abaxially. Corolla pink, tubular‑funnelform, ca. 6 cm; limb shallowly lobed, midpetaline bands pubescent. Stamens and pistil inclusive; filaments pilose at base. Ovary glabrous, 4‑locular. Berries subglobose, 1–1.5 cm.

Locality: Green Island (probably cultivated). Y. W. Lam 1211; F. W. Xing 9491.
Distribution: Guangdong; India, Bengaladesh, Indonesia, Malaysia.
Ecology: Flowering: Sep.; fruiting: Nov.
Uses: Ornamental.

Calystegia hederacea Wall. 打碗花（旋花）
Fl. Ind. 2: 94. 1824; FRPS 64(1): 47. 1979; FFJ 4: 484. 1989; FOC 16: 287. 1995; FGD 4: 339, fig. 201. 2000.
Calystegia hederacea Wall. var. elongata Liou & Ling, Fl. Ill. Nord Chine 1: 25, pl. 8, fig. 2. 1931.
Volvulus hederaceus (Wall.) Kuntze, Rev. Gén. Bot. 447. 1891.

Annual herb, glabrous. Stems erect when young, later shoots prostrate or twining, finely striate. Petiole 1–5 cm; basal leaf blade oblong, 2–3(–5.5) × 1–2.5 cm, base hastate, apex rounded, distal leaf blade 3‑lobed, middle lobe oblong or oblong‑lanceolate, lateral lobes subtriangular, entire or 2–3‑lobed. Lower peduncles exceeding leaves, upper peduncles shorter; bracteoles ± ovate, 0.7–1.4(–1.8) cm × (4–)6–10(–12) mm, flat, apex acute to ± obtuse. Corolla pale pink or occasionally whitish or purplish, 2–3.5 cm. Stamens 1.1–1.6(–1.9) cm; anthers 3–4 mm.

Locality: New Territories. Y. S. Lau 3022.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; Afghanistan, India, Japan, Korea, Malaysia, Mongolia, Myanmar, Nepal, Pakistan, Russia, Tajikistan, NE Africa, rarely introduced in N America.
Ecology: Wastelands and farmlands. Flowering: Mar. – Sep.; fruiting: Jun.–Sep.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The species was reported as Calystegia sepium (L.) R. Br. previously (Check List HK Plants 222. 2002; 77. 2004).

Dichondra micrantha Urban 馬蹄金
Symb. Antill. 9: 243. 1924; FTW 4: 353, pl. 1036. 1978; FOC 16: 275. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 349, pl. 156. 1998; FGD 4: 332, fig. 195. 2000.
Dichondra repens var. micrantha (Urban) Lu, Quart. J. Chin. Forest. 6: 166. 1972.
Dichondra repens auct. non. J. R. Forst. & G. Forst.: FHK 240. 1861; FKH 181. 1912; FHN 3: 473, fig. 864. 1974; FRPS 64(1): 8, pl. 1: 1 – 4. 1979; FFJ 4: 475, fig. 380. 1989; Check List HK Plants 222. 2002; 77. 2004.

Perennial herb. Stems slender, prostrate, freely branching, sparsely greyish white pubescent, rooting at nodes. Petiole 2 – 5 cm, greyish white pubescent; leaf blade reniform to heart‑shaped or orbicular, 0.5 – 2.5 cm in diam., abaxially sparsely appressed pilose, adaxially glabrous. Pedicel erect, shorter than petiole, pubescent. Calyx broadly campanulate, deeply 5‑lobed; lobes obovate‑oblong to spathulate, ca. 2 mm, margin densely pubescent. Corolla yellow, ca. 2 mm, 5‑lobed to middle, glabrous. Stamens equal, filaments short. Ovary greyish white pubescent. Styles free, slightly unequal. Capsule subglobose, ca. 2 mm in diam.; pericarp membranous, sparsely pubescent, purplish when mature. Seeds yellow to brown, glabrous.

Locality: Tai Tam, Sha Lo Tung. S. P. Lau 96; Y. W. Lam 264.
Distribution: Areas S of Changjiang River; Japan including Ryukyu Islands, S Korea, Thailand, N & S America, Pacific islands.
Ecology: Grassy hillslopes. Flowering & fruiting: Apr. – Sep.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Stanley, Cape Collinson, Cape D'Aguilar, Lung Fu Shan, Lantau Island, Tung Lung Chau, Lamma Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Erycibe obtusifolia Benth. 丁公藤
FHK 236. 1861; FHN 3: 477. 1974; FRPS 64(1): 20, pl. 4: 5 – 6. 1979; FOC 16: 279. 1995; FGD 4: 333, fig. 196. 2000.
Erycibe versatilihirta C. Y. Ma, Acta Bot. Yunnan. 7(1): 91, pl. 1. 1985.

Woody vine, glabrous except for inflorescences. Stems to 5 cm in diam.; branchlets distinctly striate‑angular, yellowish brown when dry. Petiole 0.8–1.2 cm; leaf blade leathery, elliptic or obovate, 6–10 × 2.5–4 cm, base cuneate, apex obtuse or acute; lateral veins 4–6 pairs, prominent abaxially. Inflorescences terminal or axillary, paniculate or racemose, 4–15 cm. Pedicels 4–6 mm. Sepals suborbicular, ca. 3 mm in diam., ± dull yellow pubescent abaxially. Corolla yellowish white, 8–10 mm; lobules broadly elliptic, undulate, entire. Stamens unequal, apex acuminate; filaments ca. as long as anthers. Ovary ellipsoidal, glabrous. Stigma conical, adnate to ovary, spirally ridged. Fruit red to yellow, ellipsoidal, 1.2–1.4 × 0.7–0.8 cm.

Locality: Stanley, Cape Collinson, Cape D'Aguilar, Lung Fu Shan, Lantau Island, Tung Lung Chau, Lamma Island. Y. W. Lam 1448; S. C. Ng 2172; HK sheet 38756.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests and thickets. Flowering: May; fruiting: Oct.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Aberdeen, Tsim Bei Tsui, Castle Peak, Sha Chau, Lamma Island, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Evolvulus alsinoides (L.) L. 土丁桂
Sp. Pl., ed. 2, 392. 1762; FHK 240. 1861; FKH 181. 1912; FHN 3: 473, fig. 865. 1974; FRPS 64(1): 12, pl. 2: 1 – 4. 1979; FFJ 4: 477, fig. 381. 1989; FOC 16: 276. 1995; FGD 4: 335, fig. 197. 2000.
Convolvulus alsinoides L., Sp. Pl. 1: 157. 1753.
Evolvulus chinensis Choisy, Mém. Soc. Phys. Genève 8: 77. 1837.
Evolvulus pudicus Hance ex Walp., Ann. Bot. Syst. 3: 115. 1852.

Perennial herb. Stems slender, prostrate or ascending, slender, with appressed and spreading pale yellow hairs. Petiole short, hairy; leaf blade petiolate or subsessile, 1–2 × 0.4–0.9 cm, base rounded or broadly cuneate, apex obtuse or acute, mucronate, appressed pale yellow pubescent on both surfaces, sometimes subglabrous adaxially; lateral veins 3 pairs, slightly prominent abaxially. Cymes 1 – few‑flowered, pubescent; peduncles filiform, 2.5–3.5 cm; bracts linear‑subulate to linear‑lanceolate, 1.5–4 mm. Pedicels 2.5–4 mm, hairy. Sepals lanceolate, 2.5–4 mm, villous. Corolla rotate, white, pale blue, sometimes pale purple, 6–10 mm in diam. Stamens inclusive; filaments filiform, adnate to base of corolla tube. Ovary glabrous. Styles 2, distinct. Capsule globose, 4‑valved. Seeds 4 or fewer, black, smooth.

Locality: Aberdeen, Tsim Bei Tsui, Castle Peak, Sha Chau, Lamma Island, Lantau Island. S. P. Lau 129; P. S. Choi 382; Y. S. Lau 1533.
Distribution: Areas S of Changjiang River; S & SE Asia, E Africa.
Ecology: Sandy soil, dry slopes, maritime areas, grasslands, thickets, roadsides. Flowering & fruiting: May–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island, Cheung Chau, Tai A Chau

Hewittia malabarica (L.) Suresh 豬菜藤
An Interpretation of Van Rheede's Hortus Malabaricus. 88. 1988; FOC 16: 285. 1995; FGD 4: 338, fig. 200. 2000.
Convolvulus malabaricus L., Sp. Pl. 1: 155. 1753.
Convolvulus bicolor Vahl, Symb. Bot. 3: 25. 1794.
Convolvulus bracteatus Vahl, Symb. Bot. 3: 25. 1794.
Convolvulus sublobatus L. f., Suppl. Pl. 135. 1781[1782].
Hewittia bicolor (Vahl) Wight & Arn., Madras J. Lit. Sci. 1(5): 22. 1837.
Hewittia sublobata (L. f.) Kuntze, Revis. Gen. Pl. 2: 441. 1891; FHN 3: 479, fig. 870. 1974; FRPS 64(1): 43, pl. 10: 1 – 2. 1979; Check List HK Plants 222. 2002; 77. 2004.
Shutereia sublobata (L. f.) House, Bull. Torrey Bot. Club 33: 318. 1906.

Perennial herbaceous herb. Stems twining or prostrate, ± pubescent. Petiole 1–6 cm; leaf blade ovate, 3–10 × 3–8 cm, base cordate, hastate, or truncate, margin entire or 3‑lobed, apex acuminate, acute, or mucronate, appressed pilose or subglabrous on both surfaces; basal veins 5. Cymes often 1‑flowered; peduncle 1.5 – 10 cm, pilose; bracts oblong‑lanceolate, 0.5–1.5 cm, pubescent. Pedicel 2–4 mm. Sepals unequal, pubescent abaxially; outer 3 broadly ovate, ca. 1.5 cm; inner 2 oblong‑lanceolate, smaller, ca. 1.1 cm. Corolla pale yellow or whitish, with a purple center, 2–2.5 cm, midpetaline bands densely pilose. Stamens ca. 9 mm. Ovary villous. Capsule enclosed by persistent calyx, depressed globose, 8–10 mm in diam., pilose, irregularly 4‑valved.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island, Cheung Chau, Tai A Chau. Y. W. Lam 456, 1169, 1183.
Distribution: Taiwan, Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; tropical Africa, tropical Asia.
Ecology: Sandy soil and thickets. Flowering & fruiting: All year round.

Ipomoea alba L. 月光花
Sp. Pl. 1: 161. 1753; FTW 4: 363. 1978; FOC 16: 309. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 357. 1998.
Calonyction aculeatum (L.) House, Bull. Torrey Bot. Club 31(11): 590. 1904; FHN 3: 491, fig. 875. 1974; FRPS 64(1): 106. 1979; FFJ 4: 497, fig. 397. 1989. FGD 4: 358, fig. 210. 2000; Check List HK Plants 222. 2002; 77. 2004.
Calonyction aculeatum var. lobatum (Hallier f.) C. Y. Wu, Report on tropical and subtropical flora of Yunnan 1: 114. 1965; FRPS 64(1): 107. 1979.
Calonyction album (L.) House, Bull. Torrey Bot. Club 31(11): 591. 1904.
Calonyction bona‑nox (L.) Bojer, Hortus Maurit. 228. 1837.
Calonyction speciosum Choisy, Convolv. Orient. 59. 1834.
Convolvulus aculeatus L., Sp. Pl. 1: 155. 1753.
Ipomoea aculeata (L.) Kuntze, Revis. Gen. Pl. 2: 442. 1891.
Ipomoea aculeata var. bona‑nox (L.) Kuntze, Revis. Gen. Pl.3(2): 212. 1898.
Ipomoea bona‑nox L., Sp. Pl. ed. 2, 1: 228. 1762.

Annual or perennial twining herb, usually glabrous, rarely puberulent. Stems terete, smooth or with soft prickles, sap milky. Petiole 5–20 cm; leaf blade ovate, rarely ovate‑oblong, 10–20 × 5–16 cm, base cordate, angular to 3‑lobed, apex acuminate, mucronulate, margin entire, glabrous. Helicoid cymes 1–several‑flowered. Peduncle stout, 5–20 cm, tuberculate. Bracts caducous, small. Pedicel 7–15 cm, clavate. Flowers nocturnal, fragrant. Sepals unequal, ± leathery, elliptic to ovate, glabrous; outer 3 sepals 5–12 mm, apex with a stout spreading 4 – 9 mm awn; inner 2 sepals 7–15 mm, mucronate. Corolla white, with greenish bands, salverform; tube 7–12 cm, ca. 5 mm in diam.; limb 7–12 cm in diam. Stamens exserted; filaments inserted in apical 1/2 of corolla tube. Pistil exserted; ovary narrowly conical, glabrous. Stigma 2‑lobed. Capsule ovoid, 2.5 – 3 cm, apiculate. Seeds white, brown, or black, ca. 1 cm, glabrous.

Locality: Naturalized. Y. S. Lau 2321; Y. W. Lam 880.
Distribution: Taiwan, Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Shaanxi, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Jiangsu, Sichuan; native to tropical America, widely naturalized in tropical regions of the Old World.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr.–Nov.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal (folklore).

Ipomoea aquatica Forssk. 蕹菜
Fl. Aegypt.‑Arab. 44. 1775; FKH 180. 1912; FHN 3: 487. 1974; FTW 4: 363. 1978; FRPS 64(1): 94. 1979; FFJ 4: 492, fig. 393. 1989; FOC 16: 307. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 357. 1998; FGD 4: 354. 2000.
Convolvulus repens Vahl, Symb. Bot. 1: 17. 1790.
Ipomoea repens Roth, Nov. Pl. Sp. 110. 1821.
Ipomoea reptans Poir., Encycl. Suppl. 3: 460. 1814; FGZ 587, fig. 313. 1956.

Annual terrestrial and repent or floating herb. Stems terete, thick, hollow, rooting at nodes, glabrous. Petiole 3–14 cm, glabrous; leaf blade variable in shape, ovate, ovate‑lanceolate, oblong, or lanceolate, 3.5–17 × 0.9–8.5 cm, base cordate, sagittate or hastate, occasionally truncate, apex acute or acuminate, margin entire or undulate, glabrous or rarely pilose. Cymes 1–3(–5)‑flowered. Peduncle 1.5–9 cm. Bracts squamiform, 1.5–2 mm. Pedicel 1.5–6 cm. Sepals subequal, ovate, ca. 9 mm, apex obtuse, glabrous. Corolla white, pink, or lilac, with a darker center, funnelform, 3.5–5 cm, glabrous. Stamens unequal, inclusive. Pistil inclusive; ovary conical, glabrous. Stigma 2‑lobed. Capsule ovoid to globose, ca. 1 cm in diam., tardily dehiscent; pericarp soft leathery. Seeds densely yellowish brown pubescent, sometimes glabrous.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 2956; L. T. Lo 579; Y. W. Lam 1162.
Distribution: Widely cultivated in the tropics.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Sep.–Feb. of the following year.
Uses: Vegetable.
Notes: Based on growing conditions (terrestrial vs. aquatic) and the colour of plant and flower (greenish plants with white flowers vs. purplish tinged plants with lilac flowers), several races without formal taxonomic designation are recognized.

Ipomoea batatas (L.) Lam. 番薯
Encycl. 2: 465. 1793; FKH 180. 1912; FHN 3: 486. 1974; FTW 4: 363. 1978; FRPS 64(1): 89. 1979; FFJ 4: 493. 1989; FOC 16: 306. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 357. 1998; FGD 4: 353. 2000.
Convolvulus batatas L., Sp. Pl. 1: 154. 1753.
Batatas edulis (Thunb. ex Murray) Choisy, Convolv. Orient. 53. 1833.
Convolvulus candicans Sol. ex Sims, Bot. Mag. 39: pl. 1603. 1813.
Convolvulus edulis Thunb. ex Murray, Syst. Veg. (ed. 14) 203. 1784.
Ipomoea batatas var. edulis (Thunb. ex Murray) Makino, Fl. Japan 476. 1927.
Ipomoea edulis (Thunb. ex Murray) Makino, Somoku‑Dzusetsu 4: pl. 25. 1903.
Ipomoea fastigiata (Roxb.) Sweet, Hort. Brit. 1: 288. 1826.

Annual herb with ellipsoidal, fusiform, or elongate subterranean tubers; sap milky. Stems prostrate or ascending, green or purplish, much branched, rooting at nodes, glabrous or pilose. Petiole 2.5–20 cm; leaf blade broadly ovate to orbicular, 4–13 × 3–13 cm, margin entire or palmately 3–5(–7)‑lobed, herbaceous; lobes broadly ovate to linear‑lanceolate, sparsely pilose or glabrous. Cymes (1–)3–7‑flowered. Peduncle 2–10.5 cm, stout, angular. Bracts caducous, lanceolate, 2–4 mm. Pedicel 2–10 mm. Sepals ± unequal, oblong or elliptic, apex acute, mucronulate, margin ciliate, glabrous or pilose abaxially; outer 2 sepals 0.7–1 cm, inner 3 sepals 0.8–1.1 cm. Corolla pink, white, pale purple to purple, with a darker center, campanulate to funnelform, 3–4 cm, glabrous. Stamens inclusive. Pistil inclusive; ovary pubescent or glabrous.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 2849; HK sheet 9363, 19756.
Distribution: Widely cultivated in tropical and subtropical regions.
Ecology: Flowering: Oct.–Dec.
Uses: Food.

Ipomoea biflora (L.) Pers. 心萼薯
Syn. Pl. 1: 183. 1805; FOC 16: 304. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 358, pl. 159, photo 208. 1998.
Convolvulus biflorus L. Sp. Pl., ed. 2, 1668. 1763, non Forssk. 1775.
Aniseia biflora (L.) Choisy, Mém. Soc. Phys. Genève 6: 483.1833; FRPS 64(1): 41, pl. 10: 3. 1979; FFJ 4: 481, fig. 384. 1989; Check List HK Plants 221. 2002; 77. 2004.
Convolvulus sinensis Desr., Encycl. 3(2): 557. 1789.
Ipomoea sinensis (Desr.) Choisy, Mém. Soc. Phys. Genève 6: 459. 1834; FGZ 588. 1956; FTW 4: 373, pl. 1046. 1978; FGD 4: 350. 2000.

Annual, scandent or twining herb. Stems slender, finely striate, greyish white hirsute. Petiole slender, 1.5–9 cm, hairy; leaf blade papery, heart‑shaped or triangular‑heart‑shaped, 3–9 × 2–7 cm, base cordate, apex acuminate, margin entire, rarely slightly 3‑lobed, hirsute‑villous on both surfaces; lateral veins 4 – 5 pairs. Cymes (1–)2(–3)‑flowered, shorter than petiole. Peduncle 0.3–1.5 cm. Outer 3 bracts linear‑lanceolate, small. Pedicel 0.8 – 1.5 cm. Sepals slightly enlarged in fruit; outer 3 deltate‑lanceolate, 0.8–1 × 0.4–0.5 cm, greyish white hirsute abaxially, ciliate, subglabrous adaxially, base auriculate; inner 2 linear‑lanceolate, ca. as long as outer ones or slightly longer. Corolla white, narrowly campanulate, 1–1.5 cm; limbs 5‑lobed, midpetaline bands pubescent. Stamens ca. 3 mm; anthers ovoid‑deltoid, base sagittate. Ovary conical, glabrous. Style clavate. Stigma capitates, 2‑lobed. Capsule subglobose, 0.8–1 cm in diam., glabrous. Seeds ovoid‑trigonous, ca. 4 mm, black, puberulent to tomentellous, margin sometimes white woolly.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 2415, 2779; Y. W. Lam 1141.
Distribution: Taiwan, Fujian, Jiangxi, Hunan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan; India, Indonesia, Japan (Ryukyu Islands), Myanmar, Vietnam, E Africa, N Australia.
Ecology: Hillslopes, valleys, thickets and forests. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Jan. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Ipomoea cairica (L.) Sweet 五爪金龍
Hort. Brit., ed. 1, 287. 1827; FGZ 586, fig. 312. 1956; FHN 3: 489, fig. 874. 1974; FTW 4: 364, pl. 1040. 1978; FRPS 64(1): 97. 1979; FFJ 4: 494, fig. 394. 1989; FOC 16: 309. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 358, pl. 160, photos 209 – 210. 1998; FGD 4: 353, fig. 208. 2000.
Convolvulus cairicus L., Syst. Nat. (ed. 10) 2: 922. 1759.
Ipomoea palmata Forssk., Fl. Aegypt.‑Arab. 43. 1775; FKH 181. 1912.

Perennial twining herb with a tuberous root, glabrous throughout. Stems often tuberculate. Petiole 2–8 cm, base with leafy pseudostipules; leaf blade palmately 5–7‑parted to base; lobes ovate, ovate‑lanceolate or elliptic, apex acute or obtuse, mucronulate, entire or minutely undulate, basal pair usually again lobed or parted; middle lobe larger, 3–9 cm. Cymes 1–several‑flowered. Peduncle 1.5–2.5 cm. Bracts and bracteoles caducous, small. Pedicel 2.5–3 cm. Sepals equal or the outer ones slightly shorter, 6–7 mm, abaxially ± verruculose. Corolla pink, purple, or reddish purple, with a darker center, funnelform, 5–7 cm. Stamens inclusive, unequal. Capsule ± globose, ca. 1 cm. Seeds black, ca. 5 mm, densely tomentose, margin with longer hairs.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1592, 2388; L. T. Lo 188.
Distribution: Taiwan, Fujian, Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; widely distributed in tropical regions of the world.
Ecology: Thickets, wastelands, sunny slopes. Flowering: Nearly all year round.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), weed.

Ipomoea carnea Jacq. subsp. fistulosa (Mart. ex Choisy) D. F. Austin 樹牽牛
Taxon 26(2 – 3): 237. 1977; FOC 16: 311. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 361. 1998.
Ipomoea fistulosa Mart. ex Choisy, Prodr. 9: 349. 1845; FRPS 64(1): 101. 1979; FFJ 4: 494. 1989; FGD 4: 351. 2000; Check List HK Plants 223. 2002; 77. 2004.
Batatas crassicaulis Benth., Bot. Voy. Sulphur 134. 1845.
Ipomoea crassicaulis (Benth.) B. L. Rob., Proc. Amer. Acad. Arts 51(10): 530. 1916; FTW 4: 364. 1978.

Shrub, 1–3 m. Branches terete or angular, stout, solid or hollow, pubescent when young. Petiole 2.5–15 cm; leaf blade ovate or ovate‑oblong, 6–25 × 4–18 cm, base cordate or truncate, apex acuminate, mucronulate, margin entire, adaxially subglabrous, pubescent abaxially; midvein 2‑glandular abaxially at base. Cymes several‑flowered. Peduncle stout, 5–10 cm. Bracts caducous, small, ovate. Pedicel 1–1.5 cm, pubescent. Sepals ovate, thinly leathery, equal or inner ones longer, 5–6 mm, abaxially puberulent, often with glands alternating to sepals at base. Corolla pink, darker inside, funnelform, 7–9 cm; tube and midpetaline bands pilose abaxially. Stamens inclusive; filaments unequal. Pistil inclusive; ovary puberulent. Style puberulent at base. Capsule pale brown, ovoid, 1.5–2 cm, 4‑valved, apiculate. Seeds black, ca. 1 cm, brown sericeous‑pubescent.

Locality: Cultivated. L. T. Lo 284; Y. S. Lau 2770, 2844.
Distribution: Taiwan, Fujian, Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi; native to tropical America, widely cultivated in tropical regions of the world.
Ecology: Flowering: All year round.
Uses: Ornamental.

Ipomoea fimbriosepala Choisy 狹花心萼薯
Prodr. 9: 359. 1845; FOC 16: 304. 1995.
Aniseia stenantha (Dunn) Ling ex R. C. Fang & S. H. Huang, FRPS 64(1): 42. 1979; FFJ 4: 481. 1989; Check List HK Plants 221. 2002; 77. 2004.
Ipomoea setifera Poiret var. fimbriosepala (Choisy) Fosberg, Smithsonian Contr. Bot. 36: 24. 1977.
Ipomoea stenantha Dunn, FKH 180. 1912; FGD 4: 355. 2000.

Annual twining herb. Stems slender, sparsely hairy to glabrescent or hirsute on nodes. Petiole 2–5 cm, glabrous; leaf blade triangular or ovate‑triangular, or oblong‑cordate‑sagittate to narrowly hastate, 5–9 × (1–)3–6 cm, base auriculate or sagittate, apex acuminate, mucronulate, glabrous on both surfaces; lateral veins 5 – 6 pairs, inconspicuous. Inflorescences axillary, 1(–2)‑flowered; peduncle 5(–9) cm or shorter; bracts 2, ± ovate, 0.5 – 1.5 cm, glabrous. Pedicel angular, 1.3–4 cm. Sepals unequal; outer 3 larger, ovate to lanceolate, 1.5–2.2 cm, base shallowly cordate, apex mucronate, strongly 3‑keeled abaxially, keels toothed basally, glabrous. Corolla red, with a darker center, funnelform, ca. 3.5 cm, glabrous; limb lobed, lobes slightly triangular. Stamens inclusive; filaments pilose below middle. Ovary conical, glabrous. Style filiform, ca. 5 mm; stigma capitate, 2‑lobed. Capsule ovoid to globose, pale brown outside, whitish inside, ca. 1.2 cm. Seeds blackish brown, densely tomentellous.

Locality: Sai Kung. HK sheet 35671.
Distribution: Guangdong, Fujian, Zhejiang; New Guinea, Africa, Mexico, Pacific islands, S America.
Ecology: Grasslands. Flowering & fruiting: Sep.–Dec.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Long Sai Wan, Tai Wan, Soko Islands, Fan Lau
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Ipomoea imperati (Vahl) Griseb. 假厚藤
Cat. Pl. Cub. 203. 1866; FOC 16: 308. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 361, pl. 161, photo 212. 1998.
Convolvulus imperati Vahl, Symb. Bot. 1: 17. 1790.
Convolvulus sinuatus Petagna, Inst. Bot. 2: 353. 1787.
Convolvulus stoloniferus Cirillo, Pl. Rar. Neapol. 1: 14, pl. 5. 1788, nom. illeg. superfl.
Ipomoea carnosa R. Br., Prodr. 485. 1810; FKH 181. 1912.
Ipomoea stolonifera (Cirillo) J. F. Gmel., Syst. Veg. 1: 345. 1796, nom. illeg. superfl.; FHN 3: 488. 1974; FTW 4: 375, pl. 1047. 1978; FRPS 64(1): 96, pl. 20: 2 – 3. 1979; FFJ 4: 496, fig. 396. 1989; FGD 4: 352. 2000.

Perennial prostrate herb, glabrous throughout. Stems to 5 m, rooting at nodes. Petiole 0.5–5 cm; leaf blade variable in shape, often linear, lanceolate, oblong, or ovate, 1.5–3 × 0.8–2 cm, base truncate or shallowly cordate, apex obtuse or emarginate to 2‑lobed, margin entire, undulate, or 3–5‑lobed; middle lobe ovate to oblong, lateral lobes smaller. Cymes 1(–3)‑flowered. Peduncle ca. 2 cm. Bracts deltate, ca. 2 mm. Pedicel ca. 6 mm, stout. Sepals unequal, oblong, ± leathery, apex obtuse or acute, mucronulate; outer 2 ca. 0.7–1.1 mm; inner ones to 1.5 cm. Corolla white, with a pale yellow tube and a dark red center, funnelform, 3.5–4 cm. Stamens and styles inclusive. Capsule subglobose, ca. 1 cm, smooth. Seeds ca. 8 mm, tomentose, margin with longer hairs.

Locality: Tai Long Sai Wan, Tai Wan, Soko Islands, Fan Lau. Y. S. Lau 2583; Y. W. Lam 459; HK sheet 39425.
Distribution: Taiwan, Fujian, Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi; widely distributed in tropical and subtropical regions.
Ecology: Sandy beach. Flowering: May–Dec.
Notes: It was reported as Ipomoea stolonifera previously (Check List HK Plants 223. 2002; 78. 2004), which is illegitimate, because it is based on the same type as the earlier Convolvulus sinuatus which is a later homonym of I. sinuata Ortega.

Ipomoea indica (Burm.) Merr. 變色牽牛
Interpr. Herb. Amboin. 445. 1917; FOC 16: 305. 1995; FTW 4: 363, pl. 162, photo 213. 1998.
Convolvulus indicus Burm., Index Univ. Herb. Amb. 7: 6. 1755.
Convolvulus acuminatus Vahl, Symb. Bot. 3: 26. 1794.
Convolvulus congestus (R. Br.) Spreng., Syst. Veg. 1: 601. 1825.
Convolvulus mutabilis (Ker Gawl.) Spreng., Syst. Veg. 1: 593. 1825.
Ipomoea acuminata (Vahl) Roem. & Schult., Symb. Bot. 4: 228. 1819, non Ruiz & Pav. 1799; FTW 4: 347. 1978.
Ipomoea congesta R. Br., Prodr. 485. 1810.
Ipomoea insularis (Choisy) Steud., Nomencl. Bot. ed. 2, 1: 817. 1840.
Ipomoea learii Knight ex Paxton, Paxton's Mag. Bot. 6: 267. 1839; FKH 181. 1912.
Ipomoea mutabilis Ker Gawl., Bot. Reg. 1: 39. 1813; FGZ 586. 1956.
Parasitipomoea formosana Hayata, Icon. Pl. Formosan. 6: 33. 1916.
Pharbitis indica (Burm.) R. C. Fang, FRPS 64(1): 105. 1979; Check List HK Plants 225. 2002; 78. 2004.
Pharbitis insularis Choisy, Mém. Soc. Phys. Genève 6: 439. 1833.
Pharbitis learii (Knight ex Paxton) Lindl., Edwards's Bot. Reg. 27: pl. 56. 1841.

Annual herbaceous herb. Stems twining or sometimes prostrate, 3–6 m, sometimes rooting at nodes, ± densely retrorse pilose. Petiole 2–18 cm; leaf blade ovate or orbicular, 5–15 × 3.5–14 cm, base cordate, apex acuminate or abruptly acuminate, margin entire or 3‑lobed, adaxially sparsely pubescent, abaxially densely short, soft, pubescent. Cymes dense, umbellate, several‑flowered. Peduncle 4–20 cm. Bracts linear, sometimes lanceolate. Pedicel short. Sepals subequal, broadly lanceolate, 2–2.5 cm, glabrous to appressed pilose. Corolla bright blue or bluish purple, funnelform, 5–8 cm, glabrous. Stamens and styles inclusive. Ovary glabrous. Stigma 3‑lobed. Capsule subglobose, 1–1.3 cm in diam. Seeds 4–6, ca. 5 mm, brown, glabrous.

Locality: Naturalized in Hong Kong. L. T. Lo 608; Y. W. Lam 1029, 1161.
Distribution: Taiwan, Hainan (Tong Sha Islands), Guangdong; native to S America, widely cultivated and naturalized in the tropics.
Ecology: Forests near seashore. Flowering: Jan.–Oct.
Uses: Ornamental.

Ipomoea mauritiana Jacq. 七爪龍
Collectanea 4: 216. 1791; FOC 16: 310. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 363, photo 215. 1998.
Ipomoea digitata auct. non L.: FKH 181. 1912; FGZ 587. 1956; FHN 3: 489. 1974; FTW 4: 366. 1978; FRPS 64(1): 99. 1979; FFJ 4: 489. 1989; FGD 4: 354. 2000.

Perennial twining herb with tuberous roots, glabrous throughout. Stems to 10 m, thinly angular. Petiole 3 – 11 cm; leaf blade orbicular in outline, usually palmately (3–)5–7(–9)‑divided to or beyond middle, rarely entire or shallowly lobed, 5–18 cm, base cordate or truncate; segments lanceolate or elliptic, apex acuminate or acute, mucronulate, entire or irregularly undulate. Cymes several–many‑flowered. Peduncle 3–10 cm. Bracts caducous, triangular, 3–6 mm. Pedicel 1–2.5 cm. Sepals broadly ovate, thinly leathery, equal or outer 2 shorter, 7–12 mm, glabrous, apex obtuse. Corolla pink or reddish purple, with a darker center, campanulate, 5 – 6 cm; limb 5 – 7 cm in diam., undulate. Stamens and styles inclusive. Capsule ovoid, 1.2–1.4 cm, 2‑locular, 4‑valved. Seeds dark brown, ca. 6 mm, densely woolly‑sericeous.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1440, 2001; S. P. Lau 165.
Distribution: Taiwan, Fujian, Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; tropical regions of the world.
Ecology: Thickets and wastelands. Flowering: May–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), weed.
Notes: The species was reported as Ipomoea digitata L. previously (Check List HK Plants 223. 2002; 77. 2004), which is endemic to West Indies and does not occur in Asia.

Ipomoea nil (L.) Roth 牽牛
Catal. Bot. 1: 36. 1797; FHN 3: 486. 1974; FTW 4: 369. 1978; FOC 16: 305. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 366, photo 216. 1998.
Convolvulus nil L., Sp. Pl. ed. 2, 219. 1762.
Ipomoea hederacea (L.) Jacq., Collectanea 1: 124, pl. 36. 1787; FKH 181. 1912; FGZ 585. 1956.
Pharbitis nil (L.) Choisy, Mém. Soc. Phys. Genève 6: 439. 1833; FRPS 64(1): 103. 1979; FFJ 4: 490, pl. 391. 1989; FGD 4: 356. 2000; Check List HK Plants 225. 2002; 78. 2004.

Annual twining herbaceous herb. Stems 2–5 m, retrorsely hirsute. Petiole 2–15 cm; leaf blade broadly ovate or suborbicular, 4–15 × 4.5–14 cm, base cordate, apex acuminate, margin entire or 3(or 5)‑lobed, hirtellous. Cymes 1–several‑flowered. Peduncle 1.5–18.5 cm, hirsute. Bracts linear or narrowly lanceolate, 5–8 mm, spreading hirtellous. Pedicel 5–8 mm. Flowers large. Sepals subequal, lanceolate, 1–2.5 cm, abaxially spreading hirsute, slightly enlarged in fruit. Corolla pale to bright blue with whitish tube, funnelform, 5–6(–8) cm, glabrous. Stamens inclusive, unequal. Pistil inclusive; ovary glabrous, 3‑locular. Stigma 3‑lobed. Capsule straw coloured, ovoid to subglobose, 8–10 mm in diam., glabrous. Seeds black, ovoid‑trigonous, 5–6 mm, grey puberulent.

Locality: Naturalized in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 2052; Y. S. Lau 2801; HK sheet 35870.
Distribution: Native to S America, now widely cultivated and naturalized in tropical and subtropical regions of the world.
Ecology: Thickets on slopes, roadsides, wastelands. Flowering: Aug.–Oct.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal (folklore).

Ipomoea obscura (L.) Ker Gawl. 小心葉薯
Bot. Reg. 3: t. 239. 1817; FKH 181. 1912; FHN 3: 487. 1974; FTW 4: 369. 1978; FRPS 64(1): 92, pl. 12: 1. 1979; FOC 16: 307. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 366, photo 217. 1998; FGD 4: 352. 2000.
Convolvulus obscurus L., Sp. Pl. ed. 2, 2: 220. 1762.

Twining herb. Stems slender, 1–2 m, sparsely villose or glabrous. Petiole 1.5–3.5 cm; leaf blade broadly ovate to suborbicular, occasionally reniform, 2–8 × 1.5–8 cm, base cordate, apex attenuate, acute, margin entire or minutely undulate, subglabrous, sometimes ciliolate; lateral veins 3 pairs. Cymes 1–3‑flowered. Peduncle almost filiform, 1.5–6 cm. Bracts subulate, ca. 1.5 mm. Pedicel 1 – 2 cm, subglabrous, thickened and recurved in fruit distally. Sepals subequal, reflexed in fruit, elliptic‑ovate, 4 – 5 mm, glabrous or ± pubescent, mucronulate. Corolla white or pale yellow, with darker midpetaline bands and a purple center, funnelform, 2–2.5 cm. Stamens and styles inclusive. Capsule ovoid, 0.8–1 cm in diam., apiculate. Seeds black‑brown, 4–5 mm, densely greyish brown tomentellous.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. L. T. Lo 70; Y. S. Lau 2477; HK sheet 35850.
Distribution: Taiwan, Hainan, Guangdong, Yunnan; tropical Africa, tropical Asia, N Australia.
Ecology: Sandy beach, thin forests or thickets. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Dec.
Uses: Ornamental.

Ipomoea pes-caprae (L.) R. Br. 厚藤（海灘牽牛）
Narr. Exped. Zaire. 477. 1818; FHK 238. 1861; FHN 3: 488. 1974; FRPS 64(1): 96. 1979; FFJ 4: 495, fig. 395. 1989; FOC 16: 308. 1995; FGD 4: 352. 2000.
Convolvulus pescaprae L., Sp. Pl. 1: 159. 1753.
Convolvulus bilobatus Roxb., Fl. Ind., (ed. 1820) 2: 73. 1824.
Convolvulus brasiliensis L., Sp. Pl. 1: 159. 1753.
Convolvulus maritimus Desr., Encycl. 3(2): 550 – 551. 1792.
Ipomoea biloba Forssk., Fl. Aegypt.‑Arab. 44. 1775; FKH 180. 1912.
Ipomoea maritima (Desr.) R. Br., Prodr. 486. 1810.
Ipomoea pes‑caprae var. emarginata Hallier f., Bull. Soc. Roy. Bot. Belgique 37: 332. 1898.
Ipomoea pes‑caprae subsp. brasiliensis (L.) Ooststr., Blumea 3(3): 533. 1940; FTW 4: 371, pl. 1043. 1978; FTW ed. 2, 4: 367, pl. 164, photo 218. 1998.

Perennial prostrate herb, with a thick tap root, glabrous throughout. Stems 5–30 m, pale red. Petiole 2–10 cm; leaf blade thickly papery, ovate, elliptic, orbicular or reniform, 3.5–9 × 3–10 cm, base broadly cuneate, truncate, or shallowly cordate, apex emarginate or deeply 2‑lobed, mucronulate, margin entire, abaxially with two glands near midvein at base. Cymes 1–several‑flowered. Peduncle stout, 4–15 cm. Bracts caducous, broadly deltate, 3–3.5 mm. Pedicel 2–2.5 cm. Sepals unequal, ± leathery, ovate, apex obtuse, glabrous, 3‑veined; outer 2 ca. 1 cm; inner ones slightly longer. Corolla purple or reddish purple, with a darker center, funnelform, 4–5 cm. Stamens and styles inclusive. Capsule subglobose, ca. 1.7 cm in diam., glabrous, leathery. Seeds black, trigonous‑globose, 7–8 mm, densely brownish tomentose.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. P. May 11496; L. Gibbs 5382; Y. S. Lau 387.
Distribution: Taiwan, Zhejiang, Fujian, Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi; tropical regions of the world.
Ecology: Sandy beach. Flowering & fruiting: Nearly all year round.
Uses: Forage, medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Wai, Tai Lam Chung, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Ipomoea pileata Roxb. 帽苞薯藤
Fl. Ind. 2: 94. 1824; FHN 3: 485. 1974; FRPS 64(1): 88, pl. 18: 4. 1978; FOC 16: 306. 1995.
Convolvulus pileatus (Roxb.) Spreng., Syst. Veg. 4(Cur. Post): 61. 1827.

Annual twining herb. Stems slender, retrorse hispid‑pilose. Petiole 1.5 –6 cm; leaf blade ovate or broadly ovate, 3.5–8 × 2.5–7 cm, base cordate, apex acuminate or attenuate, margin entire, sparsely appressed pubescent. Cymes capitate, several‑flowered. Peduncle 1.5–7 cm. Involucral bracts navicular, 3–5.5 cm, tapered at both ends, long hirtellous adaxially, densely pubescent abaxially; bracteoles oblong‑spatulate, much smaller, villous. Sepals subequal, 0.8–1 cm; outer 3 elliptic‑spatulate; inner 2 narrower, lanceolate, villous, apex obtuse. Corolla pink or purple, salverform, 2.5–3 cm; tube cylindric; limb with deltate lobes, midpetaline bands pilose. Stamens inserted near middle of corolla tube, inclusive. Ovary glabrous. Capsule subglobose, 5–6 mm in diam., glabrous. Seeds dark brown, 3–4 mm, glabrous or short pubescent.

Locality: Tai Wai, Tai Lam Chung, Lantau Island. W. J. Tutcher 4813; H. C. Tang 1890; HK sheet 34505.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; tropical Asia, tropical E Africa, Mascarene Islands.
Ecology: Margins of forests, sunny grassy hillslopes. Flowering: Aug.–Dec.

Ipomoea purpurea (L.) Roth 圓葉牽牛
Bot. Abh. 27. 1787; FOC 16: 305. 1995.
Convolvulus purpureus L., Sp. Pl. ed. 2, 1: 219. 1762.
Ipomoea hispida Zucc., Collectanea 127. 1806.
Pharbitis hispida (Zucc.) Choisy, Convolv. Orient. 56. 1833.
Pharbitis purpurea (L.) Voigt., Hort. Suburb. Calcutt. 354. 1845; FRPS 64(1): 104. 1979; FFJ 4: 490, fig. 392. 1989; FGD 4: 356, fig. 209. 2000; Check List HK Plants 225. 2002; 78. 2004.

Annual twining herb. Stems and petioles short pubescent and long retrorse hirsute. Petiole 2–12 cm; leaf blade suborbicular or broadly ovate, 4–18 × 3.5–16.5 cm, base cordate, apex acute or ± abruptly acuminate, margin entire or ± 3‑lobed, strigose on both surfaces. Cymes 1 – 5‑flowered. Peduncle 4 – 12 cm. Bracts linear, 6–7 mm, hirsute. Pedicel 1.2–1.5 cm, short pubescent and long retrorse hirsute. Sepals subequal, 1.1–1.6 cm, spreading hirsute abaxially at lower half; outer 3 oblong, apex acuminate; inner 2 linear‑lanceolate. Corolla red, reddish purple, or blue‑purple, funnelform, 4–6 cm, glabrous. Stamens inclusive, unequal; filaments pubescent at base. Pistil inclusive; ovary glabrous, 3‑locular. Stigma 3‑lobed. Capsule subglobose, 9–10 mm in diam., 3‑valved. Seeds black or straw coloured, ovoid‑trigonous, glabrous or hilum sparsely pilose.

Locality: Naturalized. Aubrey 11570.
Distribution: Most provinces of China; native to America, now introduced and naturalized worldwide.
Ecology: Flowering: Aug.–Dec.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal (folklore).

Ipomoea quamoclit L. 蔦蘿松
Sp. Pl. 1: 159. 1753; FTW 4: 337. 1978; FTW ed. 2, 4: 371. 1998.
Convolvulus pennatus Desr., Encycl. 3: 567. 1791.
Quamoclit pennata (Lam.) Bojer, Hort. Maurit. 224. 1837; FHN 3: 492, fig. 876. 1974; FRPS 64(1): 110, pl. 23: 1. 1979; FFJ 4: 498, fig. 398. 1989; FGD 4: 359, fig. 211. 2000; Check List HK Plants 225. 2002; 78. 2004.

Annual twining slender herb, glabrous throughout. Petiole 1–4 cm; leaf blade ovate to oblong in outline, 2–10 cm, pinnately parted; segments 10–18 pairs, linear, basal one pair often 2‑lobed. Cymes 1–several‑flowered. Peduncle 1.5–10 cm. Bracts small, triangular, deciduous. Pedicel 1–2 cm, clavate in fruit. Sepals slightly unequal, elliptic, 4–6 cm, apex obtuse, apiculate. Corolla bright red, rarely white, salverform, ca. 3.5 cm; limb 5‑lobed, lobes nearly triangular. Capsule ovoid, 6–7 mm, glabrous. Seeds elliptic, black.

Locality: Cultivated. L. T. Lo 136.
Distribution: Widely cultivated in China; native to S America, widely cultivated in tropical and temperate regions of the world.
Ecology: Flowering: Nearly all year round.
Uses: Ornamental.

Ipomoea triloba L. 三裂葉薯
Sp. Pl. 1: 161. 1753; FTW 4: 378, pl. 1048. 1978; FRPS 64(1): 90, pl. 19: 4. 1979; FOC 16: 307. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 371, pl. 167, photo. 219. 1998; FGD 4: 352. 2000.
Batatas triloba (L.) Choisy, Mém. Soc. Phys. Genève 8: 49. 1838.
Convolvulus trilobus (L.) Desr., Encycl. 3(2): 564. 1792.

Annual twining or prostrate herb. Stems glabrous or nodes sparsely pubescent. Petiole 2.5–6 cm, glabrous, sometimes tuberculate; leaf blade broadly ovate to orbicular in outline, 3–7 × 2–6 cm, base cordate, margin coarsely dentate to deeply 3‑lobed, or entire, glabrous or sparsely pilose. Cymes dense, umbellate, 1–several‑flowered. Peduncle 2.5–9 cm, glabrous, angular, verruculose at upper part. Bracts triangular, minute, ca. 3 mm. Pedicel 5–8 mm, glabrous, verruculose. Sepals subequal, oblong, 5–9 mm, apex obtuse or acute, mucronulate, margin ciliate. Corolla pink or pale purple, funnelform, 1.5–2 cm, glabrous; limb obtusely 5‑lobed. Stamens and styles inclusive. Ovary pubescent. Capsule subglobose, 5–8 mm, pilose. Seeds dark brown, ca. 3.5 mm, glabrous.

Locality: Naturalized in Hong Kong. L. T. Lo 215, 535; Y. W. Lam 397.
Distribution: Anhui, Guangdong, S Shaanxi, Taiwan, Zhejiang; native to the tropical West Indies, now a circumtropical weed.
Ecology: Thickets and grassy hillslopes, roadsides. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Jan. of the following year.

Jacquemontia paniculata (Burm. f.) Hallier f. 小牽牛
Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 16: 541. 1893; FHN 3: 478, fig. 869. 1974; FTW 4: 380, pl. 1049. 1978; FRPS 64(1): 45, pl. 1: 5 – 6. 1979; FFJ 4: 485, fig. 387. 1989; FOC 16: 285. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 374, pl. 168. 1998; FGD 4: 340, fig. 202. 2000.
Ipomoea paniculata Burm. f., Fl. Indica 50. 1768.
Convolvulus parviflorus Vahl, Symb. Bot. 3: 29. 1794; FKH 181. 1912.
Convolvulus violaceus Vahl, Symb. Bot. 3: 29. 1794.
Jacquemontia parviflora (Vahl) Roberty, Candollea 14: 32. 1952.
Jacquemontia violacea (Vahl) Choisy, Mém. Soc. Phys. Genève 8(1): 61. 1838; FHK 239. 1861.

Twining herb. Stems slender, terete, stellate‑pubescent when young, glabrescent. Petiole 1–5 cm, stellate‑pubescent; leaf blade ovate or ovate‑oblong, 3.5–7 cm, base cordate to truncate, apex acuminate, mucronulate, rarely acute or obtuse, ± stellate‑pubescent or subgl abrous on both sur fa c e s . Inf lor e s c enc e s umbelliform‑cymose, loose to dense, several – many‑flowered; peduncle 1 – 6 cm; bracts subulate, ca. 2 mm. Pedicel 3–6 mm, pubescent. Sepals unequal, stellate‑pubescent on both surfaces; outer 3 ovate to ovate‑lanceolate, ca. 6 mm; inner 2 smaller, ovate. Corolla pale purple or red, funnelform, 1–1.2 cm; limb shallowly 5‑lobed. Ovary glabrous. Style filiform, ca. 8 mm; stigmas 2, oblong. Capsule globose, 3–4 mm in diam., 8‑valved, glabrous. Seeds 1.5–2 mm, minutely tuberculate, glabrous, edges narrowly winged.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 758, 2961; Y. W. Lam 1131.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Taiwan; tropical Asia, tropical E Africa, Madagascar, Australia.
Ecology: Thickets, roadsides, often dry soils. Flowering & fruiting: Feb.–Dec.

Merremia dissecta (Jacq.) Hallier f. 多裂魚黃草
Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 16: 552. 1893; FRPS 64(1): 68. 1979; FOC 16: 294. 1995.
Convolvulus dissectus Jacq., Observ. Bot. 2: 4. 1767.
Ipomoea dissecta Willd., Phytogr. 5, t. 2. 1794; FKH 181. 1912.
Ipomoea sinuata Ortega, Nov. Pl. Descr. Dec. 7: 84. 1798
Operculina dissecta (Jacq.) House, Bull. Torrey Bot. Club 33: 500. 1906.

Semi‑woody vine. Stems woody basally, tuberculate, ± yellowish spreading hirsute, glabrescent. Petiole 2.5–7 cm; leaf blade palmately 5–7‑divided nearly to base; segments lanceolate, middle 2.5–10 × 0.5–3 cm, lateral ones smaller, apex mucronulate, margin coarsely dentate to irregularly pinnately lobed, glabrous or pubescent along veins abaxially. Cymes 1 – several‑flowered. Peduncle 5–10 cm. Pedicel 1.5–2 cm, thicker distally, minutely tuberculate, glabrous. Sepals subequal, ovate‑lanceolate, 2–2.5 cm, enlarged and leathery in fruit, glabrous. Corolla white, with purple‑red throat, funnelform, midpetaline bands distinct. Ovary glabrous. Capsule globose, glabrous. Seeds black, glabrous.

Locality: Stubbs Rd., Tai Hang. Y. S. Lau 215; H. C. Tang 1895.
Distribution: Coastal Islands of Guangdong; India, Indonesia, Myanmar, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, Thailand; native in N & S America.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides. Flowering: Nov.

Merremia hederacea (Burm. f.) Hallier f. 魚黃草
Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 18: 118. 1894; FGZ 584. 1956; FHN 3: 480. 1974; FTW 4: 383. 1978; FRPS 64(1): 61. 1979; FFJ 4: 487, fig. 389. 1989; FTW ed. 2, 4: 378. 1998; FGD 4: 347. 2000.
Evolvulus hederaceus Burm. f., Fl. Indica 77, t. 30, fig. 2. 1768.
Convolvulus chryseides (Ker Gawl.) Spreng., Syst. Veg. 1: 598. 1825.
Ipomoea chryseides Ker Gawl., Bot. Reg. 4: pl. 270. 1818; FHK 239. 1861; FKH 180. 1912.
Lepistemon glaber Hand.‑Mazz., Sinensia 5(1 – 2): 7. 1934.
Merremia chryseides (Ker Gawl.) Hallier f., Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 16(4 – 5): 552. in obs. 1893.
Merremia convolvulacea Dennst. ex Hallier f., Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 16(4 – 5): 552. in obs. 1893.347. 2000.

Twining or prostrate herb. Stems often minutely tuberculate, glabrous or sparsely hirsute. Petiole 1–5 cm, glabrous or pubescent; leaf blade ovate, 1.5–6 × 1.5–4 cm, base cordate or broadly cordate, irregularly crenate, or 3‑lobed, margin entire, subglabrous to spar sely puberulent on both sur faces . Cymes (1–)several – many‑flowered, umbelliform. Peduncle slender, 1–7 cm, thicker than petiole. Bracts caducous, minute, narrowly obovate. Pedicel 2–5 mm, glabrous or sometimes tuberculate. Sepals unequal, broadly obovate to spatulate or oblong, reflexed in fruit; outer 2 sepals 3.5–4 mm, apex emarginate, mucronate, glabrous, sometimes hairy along margin; inner 3 ca. 5 mm. Corolla yellow, campanulate, 6–10 mm, villous at base adaxially, glabrous abaxially, midpetaline bands 5‑veined, glabrous. Filaments dilated and sparsely villous at base. Ovary globose, glabrous; stigma globose. Capsule compressed globose or broadly conical, 5–6 mm, reticulate or wrinkled when dry. Seeds trigonous‑globose, 2.5–3.5 mm, puberulent, woolly along angles and at hilum.

Locality: Wah Fu Tsuen, Sai Kung, Sha Tin, Tai Po, Tai Wai, Ta Kwu Ling, Sham Tseng. L. T. Lo 528; P. S. Choi 425; Y. W. Lam 396.
Distribution: Taiwan, Fujian, Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Jiangxi, Yunnan; tropical Asia, tropical Africa, Mascarene Islands, N Australia, Pacific islands.
Ecology: Thickets, roadsides. Flowering & fruiting: Sep.–Apr. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Merremia hirta (L.) Merr. 毛山豬菜
Philipp. J. Sci. 7: 224. 1912; FGZ 584. 1956; FHN 3: 481. 1974; FTW 4: 384. 1978; FRPS 64(1): 63, pl. 14: 2 – 4. 1979; FOC 16: 294. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 378. 1998; FGD 4: 348. 2000.
Convolvulus hirtus L., Sp. Pl. 1: 159. 1753.
Ipomoea linifolia Blume, Bijdr. Fl. Ned. Ind. 13: 721. 1825; FKH 181. 1912.
Lepistemon decurrens Hand.‑Mazz., Sinensia 5(1 – 2): 6. 1934.
Merremia decurrens (Hand.‑Mazz.) H. S. Kiu, FHN 3: 586. 1974.

Twining or prostrate herb. Stems rooting at nodes or internodes, spreading yellow hirsute to glabrous. Petiole 1 – 1.5 cm; leaf blade variable in shape, linear, oblong‑lanceolate, ovate‑oblong, or ovate, 1.5 – 5 × 0.5–2.5 cm, base truncate, rounded, ± auriculate to hastate, apex obtuse, acute or slightly emarginate and mucronulate, margin entire, sparsely appressed hirsute or glabrous. Cymes 1–4(–8)‑flowered. Peduncle slender, 1–2.5 cm, sparsely pubescent at base. Bracts persistent, ovate, 1–2 mm, glabrous. Pedicel 3 – 10 mm, glabrous. Sepals unequal, elliptic or elliptic‑oblong; outer 2 sepals 3–5 mm; inner 3 ca. 6 mm, apex obtuse. Corolla pale yellow or whitish, campanulate, 1–2 cm, midpetaline bands 5‑veined, glabrous abaxially. Stamens inclusive; filaments dilated and pubescent at base. Ovary glabrous. Capsule broadly ovoid to globose, 6–7 mm; pericarp thinly papery, glabrous. Seeds brownish black, trigonous‑ellipsoidal, ca. 3 mm, glabrous or sparsely floccose at margin and hilum.

Locality: Tai Po. Aubrey 11571.
Distribution: Taiwan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; India, Sikkim, Thailand, Malaysia, N Australia.
Ecology: Grasslands and margins of forests.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Merremia quinata (R. Br.) Ooststr. 指葉山豬菜
J. Arnold Arbor. 29: 417. 1948; FHN 3: 482. 1974; FRPS 64(1): 66, pl. 1. 1979; FTW 4: 384. 1978; FFJ 4: 489, fig. 390. 1989; FOC 6: 294. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 379. 1998; FGD 4: 346. 2000.
Ipomoea quinata R. Br., Prodr. 486. 1810; FHK 237. 1861; FKH 181. 1912.
Convolvulus quinatus (R. Br.) Spreng., Syst. Veg. 1: 590. 1825.
Ipomoea pentadactylis Choisy, Mém. Soc. Phys. Genève 6: 471. 1833.

Perennial twining herb. Stems slender, yellow spreading hirsute. Petiole 1–2.5 cm; leaf blade palmately compound; leaflets 5, linear‑lanceolate to narrowly oblong, 1.5–4 × 0.5–1 cm, base attenuate, apex obtuse and mucronulate, entire, margin entire, often glabrous on both surfaces, sometimes hirsute along midvein and margin abaxially. Cymes 1(–2)‑flowered. Peduncle nearly as long as petiole, glabrous or hirsute at base. Pedicel 5 ‑6 mm. Bracts ovate‑triangular, 2–4 mm. Sepals thickly papery, unequal, elliptic to ovate‑oblong, glabrous; outer 2 sepals 8–10 mm; inner ones ca. 1.1–1.5 cm. Corolla white or pale yellow, campanulate or funnelform, ca. 3–4 cm, midpetaline bands 5‑veined, glabrous. Ovary glabrous. Capsule ovoid, 1–1.3 cm. Seeds oblong, 4–6 mm, pale yellow pubescent at apex.

Locality: Deep Water Bay. W. J. Tutcher 11726.
Distribution: Taiwan, Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; SE Asia, N Australia.
Ecology: Sunny places of hillslopes. Flowering & fruiting: Sep.–Dec.

Merremia tuberosa (L.) Rendle 木玫瑰
Fl. Trop. Afr. 4(2): 104. 1905; FTW ed. 2, 4: 379. 1998; FGD 4: 346. 2000.
Ipomoea tuberosa L., Sp. Pl. 1: 160. 1753.

Woody vine. Stems glabrous. Petiole glabrous; leaf blade palmately compound; leaflets 5, lanceolate to elliptic, central one larger, 6–12 cm, apex acuminate, entire, glabrous on both surfaces. Cymes axillary, (1–)several‑flowered. Peduncles 3 – 10 cm, glabrous. Pedicels ca. 1 cm, gradually thickened upward, glabrous. Sepals unequal, oblong, glabrous, outer ones 2.5 cm, apex obtuse; inner ones ca. 3 cm. Corolla yellow, campanulate, ca. 5 cm, midpetaline bands glabrous. Stamens inclusive. Capsules subglobose, ca. 3 cm in diam., irregularly dehiscing. Seeds black, tomentellus.

Locality: Cultivated and naturalized. Y. S. Lau 205, 809.
Distribution: Native to tropical Africa, cultivated in the tropics.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Oct.–Dec.
Uses: Ornamental.

Merremia umbellata (L.) Hallier f. subsp. orientalis (Hallier f.) Ooststr. 山豬菜
Fl. Malesiana, ser. 1, Spermatoph. 4(4): 449. 1953; FHN 3: 483, fig. 872. 1974; FRPS 64(1): 72, pl. 16: 3–5. 1979; FFJ 4: 488. 1989; OC 16: 297. 1995; FGD 4: 347. 2000.
Merremia umbellata (L.) Hallier f. var. orientalis Hallier f., Verslag Staat Lands Plantentuin Buitenzorg 132. 1895 (1896).
Ipomoea cymosa auct. non Roem. & Schult.: FHK 238. 1861; FKH 180. 1912.
Ipomoea fulvicoma Hance, Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 1: 176. 1849.

Twining herb. Stems densely pubescent or subglabrous. Petiole 1–10 cm, pubescent; leaf blade variable in shape, ovate, ovate‑oblong, or oblong‑lanceolate, 4–14 × 1.5–10 cm, base cordate, rarely hastate, apex emarginate, acute to acuminate, margin entire, sparsely puberulent or subglabrous adaxially, pale greyish pubescent abaxially. Cymes umbelliform, several–many‑flowered. Peduncle 1–6 cm, densely pubescent. Bracts caducous, lanceolate, minute, 2–3 mm. Pedicel 0.5–2 cm. Sepals slightly unequal, thinly leathery, strongly concave; outer 2 broadly elliptic or nearly circular, 0.8–1.4 cm, rounded or emarginate, abaxially pubescent; inner ones usually slightly longer. Corolla white, sometimes yellow, funnelform, 2.5–5.5 cm, midpetaline bands inconspicuously 5‑veined, with a strip of whitish pubescence at apex; limb slightly lobed. Stamens inclusive; anthers not twisted. Ovary glabrous or sparsely pubescent apically. Capsule conical‑ovoid, ca. 1 cm; pericarp glabrous. Seeds ca. 5 mm, densely spreading villous.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 1457; L. T. Lo 418; Y. S. Lau 3273.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Taiwan; tropical E Africa, N Australia, Pacific islands.
Ecology: Thin forests, thickets or roadsides. Flowering: Sep.–Jan. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Fung Yuen, Luk Keng, Ping Chau
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Operculina turpethum (L.) Silva Manso 盒果藤
Enum. Subst. Bras. 16. 1836; FHN 3: 484, fig. 873. 1974; FRPS 64(1): 80. 1979; FOC 16: 300. 1995; FGD 4: 344, fig. 205. 2000.
Convolvulus turpethum L., Sp. Pl. 1: 155. 1753.
Ipomoea turpethum (L.) R. Br., Prodr. 485. 1810; FKH 180. 1912.
Merremia turpethum (L.) Rendle, Fl. Trop. Afr. 4: 102. 1905.
Spiranthera turpethum (L.) Bojer, Hortus Maurit. 226. 1837.

Perennial herbaceous vine, to 4 m. Stems reddish, narrowly 3–5‑winged, ± angular, sparsely pilose or glabrous. Petiole 2–10 cm, often winged; leaf blade papery, broadly ovate to ovate‑oblong, 5–17 × 3.5–14 cm, base cordate, truncate or obtuse, apex acute or obtuse, mucronulate, margin entire or undulate, adaxially appressed pilose to glabrous, abaxially pubescent. Cymes often 2‑flowered. Peduncles 3 – 5 cm or longer. Bracts 2, oblong to ovate‑oblong, 1–2.5 cm, concave, pubescent. Pedicel 1.5–2 cm, striate‑angular, clavate, to 4 cm in fruit, pubescent. Sepals ovate to broadly ovate, unequal; outer 2 sepals 1.5–2 cm, abaxially pubescent; inner 3 shorter, subglabrous. Corolla white, broadly funnelform, ca. 4.5 cm, glabrous; limb 5‑lobed. Filaments pubescent at base. Fruit enclosed in cupular calyx, compressed globose, ca. 1.5 cm in diam. Seeds dull black, ovoid‑trigonous, ca. 6 mm, glabrous.

Locality: Fung Yuen, Luk Keng, Ping Chau. L. T. Lo 249; Y. S. Lau 2874; Y. W. Lam 1139.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Taiwan; tropical E Africa, Mascarene Islands, Seychelles, tropical Asia, tropical Australia, Polynesia, Antilles.
Ecology: Thickets, grassy fields, roadsides. Flowering & fruiting: All year round.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Stanley, Tai Po, Lam Tei, Pui O, Po Toi Islands, Soko Islands
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Xenostegia tridentata (L.) D. F. Austin & Staples 地旋花
Brittonia. 32: 533. 1980; FOC 16: 300. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 383, pl. 170, photo 224. 1998.
Convolvulus tridentatus L., Sp. Pl. 1: 157. 1753.
Evolvulus tridentatus (L.) L., Sp. Pl. ed. 2, 392. 1762.
Ipomoea tridentata (L.) Roth, Arch. Bot. (Leipzig) 1(2): 38. 1798.
Merremia hastata Hallier f., Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 16(4 – 5): 552. in obs. 1893.
Merremia tridentata (L.) Hallier f., Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 16(4 – 5): 552, in obs. 1893.
Merremia tridentata subsp. hastata (Hallier f.) Ooststr., Blumea 3(2): 317, fig. 2: o. 1939; FHN 3: 482. 1974; FTW 4: 349. 1978; FRPS 64(1): 66, pl. 14: 1. 1979; FFJ 4: 486, fig. 388. 1989; FGD 4: 349. 2000; Check List HK Plants 224. 2002; 78. 2004.
Ipomoea angustifolia auct. non Jacq.: FKH 180. 1912.
Ipomoea filicaulis auct. non Blume: FHK 238. 1861.

Prostrate or twining herb, with a stout root. Stems ± angular to narrowly winged, glabrous. Petiole 1–3 mm or absent; leaf blade narrowly oblong, linear‑oblong, to linear, dilated toward base, 2–8 cm × 0.3–1.5 mm, base hastate, ± amplexicaul, basal lobes dentate, apex acute or obtuse, mucronulate, subglabrous. Cymes 1–3‑flowered; peduncle (1–)5–6 cm, slender, pubescent at base, glabrescent distally; bracts minute, subulate. Pedicel 6–8 mm. Sepals ovate‑lanceolate, subequal or outer 2 shorter, 6–8 mm, glabrous, apex attenuate‑acuminate forming a sharp point. Corolla pale yellowish or white, with or without a maroon to brown center, funnelform, ca. 1.6 cm, glabrous abaxially. Stamens inclusive, subequal; filaments sparsely pubescent at base. Ovary glabrous. Capsule globose or ovoid, papery. Seeds blackish, 3–4 mm, glabrous, apex acute.

Locality: Stanley, Tai Po, Lam Tei, Pui O, Po Toi Islands, Soko Islands. P. S. Choi 25; Y. W. Lam 1048, 1177.
Distribution: Taiwan, Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; tropical E Africa, S & SE Asia, tropical Australia.
Ecology: Sandy grounds, thin forests. Flowering & fruiting: All year round.

Cuscuta australis R. Br. 南方菟絲子
Prodr. 491. 1810; FTW 4: 351, pl. 1034. 1978; FRPS 64(1): 144, pl. 32: 1 – 3. 1979; FFJ 4: 474, fig. 379. 1989; FOC 16: 322. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 344, pl. 154, photo 202. 1998; FGD 4: 330. 2000.
Cuscuta hygrophilae H. Pearson, Icon. Pl. 28, pl. 2704. 1901.
Cuscuta kawakamii Hayata, Icon. Pl. Formosan. 5: 125. 1915.
Cuscuta millettii Hook. & Arn., Bot. Beechey Voy. 201. 1837.
Cuscuta obtusiflora Kunth var. australis (R. Br.) Engelm., Trans. Acad. Sci. St. Louis 1: 492. 1859.
Cuscuta chinensis auct. non Lam.: FGZ 581. 1956.

Annual herb. Stems golden, thin, ca. 1 mm in diam. Inflorescences lateral, compact cymose glomerules, several – many‑flowered, subsessile. Bracts scale‑like. Pedicel 1–2.5 mm. Calyx nearly as long as corolla tube; sepals (3–)4–5, often unequal, oblong or orbicular, ca. 1.5 mm. Corolla white or creamy white, cupular, ca. 3 mm; lobes persistent, erect, ovate or oblong, as long as tube. Stamens inserted at sinus, shorter than lobes; scales shorter than tube, deeply 2‑cleft, fimbrillate. Ovary compressed globose. Styles 2, ca. 1 mm; stigmas capitate. Capsule enclosed by persistent corolla at lower half, subglobose, 3–4 mm in diam., irregularly opening, not circumscissile. Seeds 4, brownish, ovoid, ca. 1.5 mm, scabrous.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 774, 1052; HK sheet 19970.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; tropical Asia, Australia.
Ecology: Parasitic on plants of Leguminosae, Compositae or Verbenaceae. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Cuscuta campestris Yunck. 田野菟絲子
Mem. Torrey Bot. Club. 18: 138. 1932; FOC 16: 323. 1995.
Cuscuta arvensis Beyr. ex Engelm., Manual ed. 2, 336. 1856.

Annual herb. Stems yellowish green to yellow or orange, 0.5–0.8 mm in diam., smooth. Inflorescences lateral, usually compact globular clusters, 4–18‑flowered, subsessile. Pedicel ca. 1 mm. Calyx enclosing corolla tube, ca. 1.5 mm; sepals 5, oval or orbicular, sometimes wider than long. Corolla white, short campanulate, ca. 2.5 mm, 4‑ or 5‑lobed; lobes broadly triangular, apex acute or obtuse, often reflexed. Stamens shorter to longer than corolla lobes; anthers ovate, shorter than filaments; scales distinct, ovate, ca. as long as corolla tube, fimbrillate. Ovary globose. Styles 2; stigma capitate. Capsule compressed globose, ca. 3 mm in diam., ca. 2 mm high, with persistent corolla at base, irregularly opening. Seeds 1–4, often 3 or 4, dull yellow, ovoid.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. HK sheet 37677, 41647, 41859.
Distribution: Fujian, Xinjiang, Guangdong (cultivated for biocontrol of Mikania micrantha Kunth); Africa, Asia, Australia, Europe, N & S America, Pacific islands.
Ecology: Roadsides, fields, margins of beaches, parasitic on Mikania micrantha, Spinifex littoreus, Urena lobata, etc. Flowering & fruiting: Dec.–Jul. of the following year.

Cuscuta chinensis Lam. 菟絲子
Encycl. 2: 229. 1786; FKH 182. 1912; FRPS 64(1): 145, pl. 31: 4 – 7. 1979; FFJ 4: 473, fig. 378. 1989; FOC 16: 323. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 347. 1998; FGD 4: 330. 2000.

Annual herb. Stems yellow, thin, ca. 1 mm in diam. Inflorescences lateral, compact cymose glomerules, several–many‑flowered, subsessile. Bracts and bracteoles scale‑like. Pedicel ca. 1 mm. Sepals 5, triangular, ca. 1.5 mm, apex obtuse, connate at lower half. Corolla white, urceolate, ca. 3 mm; lobes persistent triangular‑ovate, apex acute or obtuse, reflexed. Stamens inserted at throat; scales oblong, long fimbriate. Ovary subglobose. Styles 2, ca. 1 mm; stigma capitate. Capsule nearly completely enclosed by persistent corolla, subglobose, ca. 3 mm in diam., circumscissile. Seeds 2–4, pale brown, ovoid, ca. 1 mm, scabrous.

Locality: Sha Tin. L. T. Lo 12, 364.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; W, E & S Asia, Madagascar, Australia.
Ecology: Fields, open mountain slopes, thickets, sandy beaches, parasitic often on plants of Leguminosae and Compositae. Flowering & fruiting: Jul. – Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Cape D'Aguilar, Aberdeen, Victoria Peak, High West, Shek O, Po Toi Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Cuscuta japonica Choisy 金燈藤
Syst. Verz. 2: 130. 1854; FHK 241. 1861; FKH 182. 1912; FRPS 64(1): 147, pl. 31: 8 – 11. 1979; FFJ 4: 475. 1989; FGD 4: 331. 2000; FOC 16: 323. 1995.
Cuscuta reflexa Roxb. var. densiflora Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 5: 57. 1853; Check List HK Plants 226. 2002; 79. 2004.

Annual herb. Stems yellow or often with purplish spots, slightly stout, 1–2 mm in diam., multibranched. Inflorescences spicate or paniculate, 1–3 cm. Bracts and bracteoles scale‑like, broadly ovate, ca. 2 mm. Flowers subsessile. Sepals 5, ca. 2 mm, semi‑orbicular, purplish tuberculate abaxially. Corolla pink or greenish white, campanulate to tubular, 3–5 mm, shallowly 5‑lobed; lobes erect or reflexed, ovate‑triangular, much shorter than tube, apex obtuse. Stamens inserted at throat; filaments very short or absent; scales oblong, fimbriate. Ovary globose, smooth. Style 1, longer than or as long as ovary; stigma elongate, 2‑lobed, lobes tongue‑shaped. Capsule ovoid, ca. 5 mm, circumscissile near base. Seeds 1–3, brown, 2–2.5 mm, smooth.

Locality: Cape D'Aguilar, Aberdeen, Victoria Peak, High West, Shek O, Po Toi Island. P. S. Choi 336; HK sheet 39388, 40810.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; Japan, Korea, Russia, Vietnam.
Ecology: On herbs or shrubs. Flowering & fruiting: Oct.–Mar. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The type specimen of Cuscuta reflexa var. densiflora (J.G. Champion s.n., K) was collected from Hong Kong.

Nymphoides cristatum (Roxb.) Kuntze 水皮蓮
Revis. Gen. Pl. 2: 429. 1891; FRPS 62: 417. 1988; FFJ 4: 407. 1989; FOC 16: 141. 1995; FGD 4: 327. 2000.
Menyanthes cristata Roxb., Pl. Coromandel 2: 3, pl. 105. 1798.
Limnanthemum cristatum (Roxb.) Griseb., Gen. Sp. Gent. 342. 1839[1838]; FKH 175. 1912.
Villarsia cristata (Roxb.) Spreng., Syst. Veg. 1: 582. 1825[1824].

Stems unbranched, with a terminal leaf. Petiole 1–3 cm; leaf blade subleathery, ovate‑orbicular to suborbicular, 3 – 10 cm, base cordate, margin entire, abaxially densely glandular, veins inconspicuous. Flowers many, grouped on nodes, 5‑merous. Pedicel slender, 3–4.5 cm. Calyx 3–5.5 mm, lobes ovate‑elliptic to ovate, apex obtuse. Corolla white with a yellow base, 4–8 mm; lobes ovate with a keeled fold from base to apex, apex obtuse. Filaments linear, 1–2 mm; anthers 0.8–1 mm. Ovary sessile. Style short; stigma lobes triangular. Capsules subglobose, 3–5 mm in diam., few seeded. Seeds light brown, globose, 1.3–1.5 mm in diam.; seed coat smooth or scabrous.

Locality: Sha Tin, Fanling, Yuen Long. W. J. Tutcher 8154, 8390, 9983.
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong, Hainan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangsu, Sichuan, Taiwan; E India.
Ecology: Ponds. Flowering & fruiting: Sep.–Oct.

Nymphoides peltatum (S. G. Gmel.) Kuntze 荇菜
Revis. Gen. Pl. 2: 429. 1891; FRPS 62: 415, pl. 67: 4 – 6. 1988; FFJ 4: 407, fig. 335. 1989; FOC 16: 141. 1995.
Limnanthemum peltatum S. G. Gmel., Novi Comment. Acad. Sci. Imp. Petrop. 14(1): 527. 1770.
Menyanthes nymphoides L., Sp. Pl. 1: 145. 1753.

Perennial herb, glabrous throughout. Stem unbranched, terete, sometimes rooting from nodes. Leaves alternate at stem base but opposite at apex; petiole 5–10 cm, base amplexicaul; leaf blade subleathery, ovate‑orbicular to orbicular, 1.5–8 × 1.5–8 cm, base cordate, margin entire, adaxially glabrous, abaxially purple‑brown and densely glandular, veins indistinct. Flowers usually densely clustered at nodes, 5‑merous. Pedicel 3–7 cm. Calyx 7–9 mm, lobes elliptic‑lanceolate to elliptic, apex obtuse. Corolla golden yellow, 2.5–3 cm, rotate, lobed to near base; lobes obovate, margin broadly membranous and irregularly laciniate, apex rounded to emarginate. Filaments sparsely pilose, 1–2 mm; anthers 2–3.5 mm. Ovary 0.7–1.7 cm; style to 1 cm; stigma large, 2‑lobed, suborbicular. Glands golden yellow. Capsules elliptic, 1.7 – 2.5 × 0.8–1.1 cm. Seeds brown, compressed, elliptic, 4–5 mm, densely ciliate.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 1000.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China except Hainan, Qinghai, Xizang; Japan, Korea, Mongolia, Russia, C & SW Asia, Europe.
Ecology: Ponds. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Oct.
Uses: Ornamental.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): South Bay Rd., Fanling, Sheung Shui, Lam Tsuen, Peng Shan
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Bothriospermum zeylanicum (J. Jacq.) Druce 柔弱斑種草
Bot. Exch. Club Brit. Isles. 4: 610. 1917; FOC 16: 420. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 388. 1998.
Anchusa zeylanica J. Jacq., Ecl. Pl. Rar. 1: 47, t. 29. 1812.
Anchusa tenella Hornem., Hort. Bot. Hafn. 1: 176. 1815.
Bothriospermum tenellum (Hornem.) Fisch. & C. A. Mey., Index Sem. (St. Petersburg) 1: 24. 1835; FHK 235. 1861; FKH 177. 1912; FGZ 569, fig. 304. 1956; FTW 4: 393. 1978; FRPS 64(2): 218. 1990; FFJ 4: 514, fig. 408. 1989; Check List HK Plants 227. 2002; 79. 2004.

Annual herb, 15–30 cm tall. Stems slender, crowded, erect or prostrate, multibranched, appressed hispid. Leaf blade elliptic to narrowly elliptic, 1–2.5 cm × 5–10 mm, base broadly cuneate, apex obtuse, mucronulate, sparsely short appressed bristly or strigose. Racemes numerous, to 12 cm; lower bracts several, lanceolate, 1.5– 5 mm, apex acute; upper ones very small. Pedicel 1–2 mm, not elongate or somewhat elongate in fruit. Calyx 1 – 1.5 mm, to 3 mm in fruit, with short ascending white bristles. Corolla blue or pale blue, 1.5 – 1.8 mm, base ca. 1 mm wide, slightly longer than calyx; throat appendages ca. 0.2 mm; limb 2.5–3 mm wide; lobes orbicular, ca. 1 mm. Style terete, ca. 0.5 mm. Nutlets grey, reniform, 1–1.2 mm.

Locality: South Bay Rd., Fanling, Sheung Shui, Lam Tsuen, Peng Shan. Y. S. Lau 2673, 3059; Y. W. Lam 2267.
Distribution: S, SW, E, N & NE China; Korea, Japan, Russia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Afghanistan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan, Pakistan, Pakistan, India, Vietnam, Indonesia (Java, naturalized).
Ecology: Grasslands along roadsides. Flowering & fruiting: Jan.–Oct.

Carmona microphylla (Lam.) G. Don 基及樹（福建茶）
Gen. Hist. 4: 391. 1837; FHN 3: 453. 1974; FRPS 64(2): 21. 1990; FOC 16: 337. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 388. 1998.
Ehretia microphylla Lam., Encycl. Meth. 1: 425. 1783; FTW 4: 400. 1978; FFJ 4: 506, fig. 403. 1989.
Carmona heterophylla Cav., Icon. 5: 22, pl. 23. 1799.
Ehretia buxifolia Roxb., Pl. Coromandel 1: 42, pl. 57. 1795.
Ehretia dentata Courchet, Fl. Indo‑Chine 4: 206. 1914.

Shrub, 1–4 m tall, multibranched; bark brown; branches slender, sparsely hirtellous when young. Petiole 1–5 mm; leaf blade leathery, obovate to spatulate, 0.8–4 × 0.5–2 cm, base attenuate, apex rounded to acute, margin coarsely crenate, adaxially hirtellous or spotted, abaxially subglabrous. Glomerules spreading, 0.5–1.5 cm wide. Peduncle slender, 1–1.5 cm, pubescent. Pedicel 1–1.5 mm, or ± obsolete. Calyx 4–6 mm, parted nearly to base; lobes linear or linear‑oblanceolate, 0.5–0.8 mm, spreading hirtellous, densely appressed pubescent inside. Corolla white or slightly reddish, campanulate, 4–6 mm; lobes spreading, oblong, longer than tube. Filaments 2.5–4 mm, inserted near base of corolla; anthers ellipsoidal, 1.5–1.8 mm. Style 4–6 mm, glabrous. Drupes 3–4 mm in diam.; endocarp globose, reticulate‑wrinkled, 2–3 mm in diam., apex short beaked.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 2312.
Distribution: Hainan, S Guangdong, Taiwan, widely cultivated in S China; S & E Asia, New Guinea, Solomon Islands, Australia.
Ecology: Flowering: Aug.
Uses: Ornamental.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Stanley, Garden Rd., Lai Chi Kok, Tai Po, Lam Tsuen, Ma On Shan, Tai Mo Shan, Sai Kung (Tai Long), Sha Tau Kok, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Cordia dichotoma G. Forst. 破布木
Fl. Ins. Austr. 18. 1786; FGZ 566. 1956; FHN 3: 452, fig. 852. 1974; FTW 4: 395. 1978; FRPS 64(2): 9, pl. 1: 8 – 12. 1990; FFJ 4: 505, fig. 402. 1989; FOC 16: 333. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 390, photo 226. 1998.
Varronia sinensis Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 1: 138. 1790.
Cordia myxa auct. non L.: FKH 176. 1912.

Tree, 3–8 m tall. Branches sparsely pilose when young, glabrescent. Petiole 2–5 cm; leaf blade thinly leathery, ovate to broadly ovate or elliptic, 6–13 × 4–9 cm, base rounded to broadly cuneate, apex obtuse to mucronate, margin usually subundulate to undulate dentate, rarely entire, sparsely pubescent or glabrous. Inflorescences terminating leafy lateral branches, dichotomously branched into corymbose cymes, widely spaced, 5–8 cm wide. Flowers dimorphic, sessile. Calyx campanulate, 5–6 mm, 5‑lobed; lobes unequal, triangular. Corolla white, nearly as long as calyx; lobes shorter than tube. Filaments of male flowers ca. 3.5 mm, filaments of bisexual flowers 1–2 mm. Rudimentary pistil globose. Style united portion 1–1.5 mm, first branches ca. 1 mm, second branches 2–3 mm; stigma spatulate. Drupes yellow or reddish, subglobose, 1–1.5 cm in diam., with sticky mesocarp, surrounded by persistent calyx.

Locality: Stanley, Garden Rd., Lai Chi Kok, Tai Po, Lam Tsuen, Ma On Shan, Tai Mo Shan, Sai Kung (Tai Long), Sha Tau Kok, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 878, 1390; P. S. Choi 344.
Distribution: Xizang, Yunnan, Guizhou, Guangxi, Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian, Taiwan; Kashmir, Myanmar, Pakistan, N India, Japan (Ryukyu Islands), Cambodia, Laos, Malaysia, Thailand, Vietnam, Indonesia, NE Australia, Pacific islands
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.; fruiting: Jun.–Sep.
Uses: Oil, medicinal (folklore), timber.

Ehretia acuminata R. Br. 厚殼樹
Prodr. 147. 1810; FKH 177. 1912; FOC 16: 334. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 393, photo 228. 1998.
Cordia thyrsiflora Siebold & Zucc., Fl. Jap. 2: 26. 1846. (Abh. Bayer. Akad. Wiss. Math. Phys. Cl. 4(3): 150, pl. 3. 1846.)
Ehretia acuminata var. obovata (Lindl.) I. M. Johnst., J. Arnold Arbor. 32(1): 21. 1951; FHN 3: 454. 1974.
Ehretia taiwaniana Nakai, J. Arnold Arbor. 5(1): 38. 1924; FGZ 567. 1956.
Ehretia thyrsiflora (Siebold & Zucc.) Nakai, Trees & Shrubs Japan Proper, ed. 1, 327. 1922; FRPS 64(2): 12. 1990; FFJ 4: 507. 1989.

Tree to 15 m tall, glabrous except young parts; bark black‑grey, laciniate; branchlets brown, conspicuously lenticellate. Petiole 1.5–3.5 cm; leaf blade elliptic to obovate or oblong‑obovate, 5–15 × 4–6 cm, base broadly cuneate, apex acute or apiculate, margin serrulate with teeth curved upward, glabrous or sparsely puberulent. Inflorescences paniculate, terminal, 8–15 cm. Flowers small, crowded, fragrant. Calyx 1.5–2 mm; lobes ovate, ciliate. Corolla white, campanulate, 3–4 mm; lobes spreading, oblong, longer than tube. Filaments 2–3 mm, inserted on 0.5–1 mm from the base of tube; anthers ovoid, ca. 1 mm. Style 1.5–2.5 mm. Drupes yellow or orange, 3–4 mm in diam.; endocarp wrinkled, divided into two 2‑seeded pyrenes at maturity.

Locality: Deep Water Bay, Tai Wai, Sha Tin, Kam Tin, Lantau Island. L. T. Lo 531; P. S. Choi 214; HK sheet 39744.
Distribution: S, SW, C & E China; Bhutan, India, Indonesia, Japan, Vietnam, Australia.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Sep.
Uses: Timber, medicinal (folklore), dye, ornamental.
