Ehretia longiflora Champ. ex Benth. 長花厚殼樹
Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 5: 58. 1853; FHK 234. 1861; FKH 176. 1912; FTW 4: 400. 1978; FRPS 64(2): 18. 1990; FFJ 4: 507. 1989; FOC 16: 336. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 395, photo 230. 1998.
Ehretia glaucescens Hayata, Icon. Pl. Formosan. 3: 153. 1913.

Deciduous tree, 5–15 m tall; bark dark grey to dark brown, scaly; branchlets glabrous. Petiole 1–2 cm, glabrous; leaf blade papery, elliptic to oblong or oblong‑oblanceolate, 8–15 × 4–8 cm, base broadly cuneate, rarely rounded, apex acute, margin entire, glabrous; lateral veins 4–7 pairs. Cymes corymbose, terminating lateral branches, glabrous or sparsely pubescent, ebracteate. Flowers sessile or short pedicellate. Calyx 1.5–2 mm, glabrous; lobes semiorbicular, inconspicuously ciliate. Corolla white, tubular‑campanulate, 0.7–1 cm, glabrous; throat 4–5 mm wide; lobes slightly recurved, ovate to elliptic‑ovate, 2–3 mm, shorter than tube. Filaments 0.8–1 cm; anthers ca. 1 mm. Ovary glabrous. Style 0.7–1.5 cm. Drupes pale yellow or red, globose, 0.8–1.5 cm in diam.; endocarp ribbed, divided into four 1‑seeded pyrenes at maturity.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Ma On Shan, Ng Tung Chai, Bride's Pool, Castle Peak, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 140, 2393; HK sheet 40351.
Distribution: Guangxi, Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering & fruiting: Jan.–Sep.
Notes: The type specimen (J. G. Champion s.n., K) was collected from Happy Valley woods between 1847 and 1850.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Lai Chi Wo, Butterfly Beach, Wu Kau Tang, Lantau Island, Cheung Chau
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Heliotropium indicum L. 大尾搖
Sp. Pl. 1: 130. 1753; FHK 235. 1861; FKH 177. 1912; FGZ 568, fig. 303; 1956; FHN 3: 457, fig. 855. 1974; FTW 4: 403. 1978; FRPS 64(2): 29. 1990; FFJ 4: 509, fig. 405. 1989; FOC 16: 341. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 396. 1998.

Annual herb, 20–50 cm tall. Stems erect, stout, multibranched, spreading strigose. Leaves alternate or subopposite; petiole 2–5 cm; leaf blade ovate, 3–9 × 2–4 cm, base rounded or truncate, decurrent to petiole, apex acute, margin undulate, pubescent or strigose on both surfaces; lateral veins 5–7 pairs, impressed adaxially, spreading hirsute or strigose. Cymes solitary, scorpioid, unbranched, 5–15 cm, ebracteate. Flowers sessile, crowded. Calyx lobes lanceolate, 1.5–2 mm, strigose. Corolla light blue or blue‑purple, salverform, 3–4 mm, ca. 1 mm wide at base; throat evidently contracted; limb 2–2.5 mm wide; lobes suborbicular, ca. 1 mm wide, margin crispate. Anthers narrowly ovoid, ca. 0.5 mm, inserted ca. 1 mm above base. Ovary glabrous. Style ca. 0.5 mm; stigma conical, pubescent. Fruit glabrous or nearly so, ribbed, 3–3.5 mm, deeply 2‑cleft into mericarps, each mericarp divided into two 1‑seeded pyrenes.

Locality: Lai Chi Wo, Butterfly Beach, Wu Kau Tang, Lantau Island, Cheung Chau. Y. W. Lam 1544, 1549; HK sheet 41517.
Distribution: Yunnan, Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian, Taiwan; tropical and subtropical regions of the world.
Ecology: Hills, river banks, open wastelands. Flowering & fruiting: May–Aug.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: Heliotropium strigosum Willd. (細葉天芥菜) was previously recorded from Lantau Island (FKH 177. 1912) and differs in its leaf blade being small and linear‑lanceolate.

Tournefortia montana Lour. 紫丹
Fl. Cochinch. 1: 122. 1790; FKH 177. 1912; FGZ 568, fig. 302. 1956; FHN 3: 458, fig. 856. 1974; FRPS 64(2): 31. 1990; FOC 16: 341. 1995.
Tournefortia brachyantha Merr. & Chun, Sunyatsenia 2(3 –4): 314, fig. 43. 1935.
Tournefortia sampsonii Hance, J. Bot. 6(71): 330. 1868.

Scandent shrub, 1–2 m tall; branchlets pubescent. Petiole 5–10 mm; leaf blade lanceolate to ovate‑lanceolate, 8–14 × 1.5–4 cm, base cuneate to rounded, apex acuminate to caudate‑acute, sparsely strigose on both surfaces, black when dry. Cymes scorpioid, terminating leafy branches, sparsely branched, 2–15 cm, strigose. Flowers unilateral, sessile. Calyx parted to middle or slightly below, ca. 2 mm, strigose; lobes lanceolate to triangular‑lanceolate. Corolla white, urceolate; limb 5‑lobed. Stamens sessile. Stigma sessile at apex of globose ovary. Fruit subglobose, ca. 5 mm in diam.; endocarp divided at maturity into two 2‑seeded mericarps.

Locality: Castle Peak. K. L. Yip 4154; HK sheet 39588, 39667.
Distribution: Yunnan, Hainan, Guangdong; Vietnam.
Ecology: Thickets. Flowering & fruiting: Spring to summer.
Notes: Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Lan Nai Wan, Tai Po, Nam Chung, Luk Keng, Mai Po, Sheung Pak Nai, Ha Pak Nai, Kei Ling Ha, Yung Shue O, Chek Keng, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Avicennia marina (Forssk.) Vierh. 海欖雌（白骨壤）
Denkschr. Kaiserl. Akad. Wiss., Math.‑Naturwiss. Kl. 71: 435. 1907; FHN 4: 6. 1977; FTW 4: 410. 1978; FRPS 65(1): 5. 1982; FFJ 4: 517, fig. 410. 1989; FOC 17: 49. 1994; FGD 3: 340, fig. 223. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 404, pl. 175, photo 238 – 239. 1998.
Sceura marina Forssk., Fl. Aegypt.‑Arab. 37. 1775.
Avicennia officinalis auct. non L.: FKH 205. 1912.

Shrub 1.5–6 m tall. Branchlets ridged when young. Leaves subsessile; leaf blade elliptic to ovate, 2–7 × 1–3.5 cm, base acuminate, apex obtuse, adaxially glabrous and shiny, abaxially pubescent; midvein conspicuous, lateral veins 4–6 pairs. Cymes dense, capitates. Peduncle 1–2.5 cm. Bracts 5, ca. 2.5 × 3 mm, in 2 whorls, outer ones densely tomentose, inner ones smooth, blackish brown. Flowers ca. 5 mm in diam. Calyx‑lobe ca. 3 × 2–3 mm, tomentose abaxially. Corolla yellow, tube short, limb 4‑lobed, lobes ca. 2 mm, tomentose abaxially. Stamens slightly exserted. Ovary densely tomentose distally. Fruit subglobose, ca. 1.5 cm in diam., hairy.

Locality: Lan Nai Wan, Tai Po, Nam Chung, Luk Keng, Mai Po, Sheung Pak Nai, Ha Pak Nai, Kei Ling Ha, Yung Shue O, Chek Keng, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 1496, 2793; Y. W. Lam 795.
Distribution: Guangdong, Hainan, Fujian, Taiwan; SE Asia, E Africa, N Australia.
Ecology: Mangrove. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Oct.

Callicarpa brevipes (Benth.) Hance 短柄紫珠（短序紫珠）
Ann. Sci. Nat. Bot., ser. 5, 5(5): 233. 1886; FKH 203. 1912; FRPS 65(1): 69. 1982; FFJ 4: 533. 1989; FOC 17: 14. 1994; FGD 3: 359. 1995.
Callicarpa longifolia Lam. var. brevipes Benth., FHK 270. 1861.
Callicarpa longifolia auct. non Lam.: FKH 202. 1912, p.p.

Shrub 1–2.5 m tall. Branchlets obscurely tetragonal, yellow‑brown stellate pubescent when young, glabrescent. Petiole ca. 5 mm; leaf blade papery, narrowly lanceolate to lanceolate, 9–24 × 1.5–4 cm, base obtuse, rarely cuneate or slightly cordate, apex acuminate, margin subentire to sparsely serrulate along apical part, adaxially glabrous, abaxially stellate pubescent on veins and yellow glandular; lateral veins 9–12 pairs. Cymes ca. 1.5 cm across. Peduncle slender, subequal to slightly longer than petioles. Calyx cup‑shaped, yellow glandular, subglabrous, subtruncate to minutely 4‑dentate. Corolla white, ca. 3.5 mm, glabrous. Filaments nearly as long as corolla; anthers ellipsoidal, densely yellow glandular, dehiscing by apical pores. Ovary glabrous, glandular. Style slightly longer than stamens. Fruit subglobose, red to purple, 3–4 mm in diam.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 3134; HK sheet 39931, 40464.
Distribution: Guangdong, Hainan, Guangxi, Hunan, S Zhejiang; Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests on hillslopes. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.; fruiting: Jul.–Oct.
Notes: The syntypes (Champion s.n., Wright s.n. and Wilford s.n.) were collected from Hong Kong in 1850. The species was reported as Callicarpa longifolia Lam. previously (Check List HK Plants 59. 1993).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Po, Fanling, Tai Mo Shan
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Callicarpa cathayana H. T. Chang 華紫珠
Acta Phytotax. Sin. 1(3 – 4): 305. 1951; FYN 1: 412, pl. 98: 16 – 18. 1977; FRPS 65(1): 65, fig. 30. 1982; FFJ 4: 533. 1989; FOC 17: 13. 1994; FGD 3: 357. 1995.

Shrub, 1.5–3 m tall. Branchlets slender, slightly stellate tomentose when young, glabrescent. Petiole less than 1 mm; leaf blade elliptic, elliptic‑ovate or ovate, 4–8 × 1.5–3 cm, base narrowly cuneate, apex acuminate, margin serrulate, subglabrous and red glandular on both surfaces; lateral veins 5–7 pairs, slightly prominent on both surfaces. Cymes slender, 1–1.5 cm across, sparsely stellate tomentose. Peduncle and pedicels slenlder, ± stellate hairy and red glandular. Bracts small. Calyx cupular, truncate to minutely 4‑dentate, teeth obtusely triangular, stellate tomentose, red glandular. Corolla purple, sparsely stellate tomentose and red glandular abaxially. Filaments equal or slightly longer than corolla. Ovary glabrous. Style slightly longer than stamens. Fruit globose, purple, ca. 2 mm in diam.

Locality: Tai Po, Fanling, Tai Mo Shan. Y. S. Lau 732; L. T. Lo 126; HK sheet 40823.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Hubei, Anhui, Jiangxi, Fujian, Zhejiang, Jiangsu.
Ecology: Mixed forests on hillslopes or in valleys. Flowering: May–Jul.; fruiting: Aug.–Nov.

Callicarpa dichotoma (Lour.) K. Koch 白棠子樹
Dendrologie 2: 336. 1872; FGZ 631. 1956; FRPS 65(1): 54, fig. 23. 1982; FFJ 4: 531, fig. 421. 1989; FOC 17: 11. 1994; FGD 3: 355. 1995.
Porphyra dichotoma Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 1: 70. 1790.
Callicarpa purpurea auct. non Juss.: FKH 202. 1912.

Shrub 1–1.5(–3) m tall, multibranched. Branchlets slender, with stellate hairs when young. Leaves sessile or subsessile; leaf blade papery, lanceolate to obovate, 2–6(–10) × 1–3 cm, base cuneate, apex usually very short acuminate with an obtuse tip, margin coarsely dentate along apical part, adaxially glabrous and subscabrous, abaxially densely yellow‑glandular and with glandular stellate hairs; veins 4–6 pairs. Cymes 1–2.5 cm across. Peduncle and pedicels slender, stellate hairy at first, glabrescent in fruit. Bracts linear. Calyx cupular, less than 1 mm, subtruncate or obscurely dentate, glabrous, ± glandular abaxially. Corolla purple, tube twice as long as calyx tube, glabrous. Stamens exserted; filaments twice as long as corolla tube, glabrous. Ovary glabrous, sparsely yellow glandular. Fruit subglobose, 1–2 mm in diam., ± glandular.

Locality: New Territories. W. J. Tutcher 8141.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hunan, Hubei, Anhui, Fujian, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Jiangsu, Shandong, Henan, Hebei; Japan, Korea, Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: Jul.–Nov.

Callicarpa formosana Rolfe 杜虹花
J. Bot. 20(240): 358. 1882; FKH 203. 1912; FHN 4: 11. 1977; FYN 1: 406, pl. 97: 5 – 7. 1977; FTW 4: 413. 1978; FRPS 65(1): 43. 1982; FFJ 4: 529, fig. 419. 1989; FOC 17: 8. 1994; FGD 3: 353. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 406, pl. 176. 1998.
Callicarpa aspera Hand.‑Mazz., Sitzungsber. Kaiserl. Akad. Wiss., Math.‑Naturwiss. Cl., Abt. 1 59: 110. 1877.
Callicarpa integerrima Champ. var. serrulata H. L. Li, J. Arnold Arbor. 25(4): 425. 1944.
Callicarpa ningpoensis Mats., Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 27: 273. 1913.
Callicarpa rubella Lindl. f. robusta C. P’ei, Mem. Sci. Soc. China 1(3): 39. 1932.

Shrub 1–3 m tall. Branchlets, petioles, cymes and calyx densely greyish yellow stellate tomentose. Petiole robust, 1–2.5 cm; leaf blade thin leathery, elliptic to ovate‑elliptic, 6–15 × 3–8 cm, base obtuse to rounded, apex acuminate or nearly acute, margin serrate, adaxially slightly rough, minutely hispid, abaxially greyish yellow stellate tomentose and yellow glandular; lateral veins 8–12 pairs. Cymes dense, subglobose, 3–4 cm across. Peduncle 1.5–2.5 cm. Bracts small. Calyx cupular, greyish yellow stellate tomentose; teeth 4, triangular. Corolla purple to purplish, ca. 2.5 mm, glabrous, lobes ca. 1 mm, apex rounded. Stamens ca. 5 mm, 2 times as long as corolla or slightly longer. Ovary glabrous. Fruit subglobose, purple, ca. 2 mm in diam.

Locality: Deep Water Bay, Sai Kung, Tai Po Kau, Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 605, 1319; Y. W. Lam 1617.
Distribution: Guangdong, Hainan, Guangxi, Yunnan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Philippines.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: May–Jul.; fruiting: Aug.–Nov.
Notes: The species was reported as Callicarpa pedunculata R. Br. previously (Check List HK Plants 59. 1993).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Bowen Rd., Cheung Sheung, Luk Keng, Nam Chung, Tung Chung
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Callicarpa integerrima Champ. 全緣葉紫珠
Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 5: 135. 1853; FHK 270. 1861; FKH 202. 1912; FRPS 65(1): 34, fig. 9. 1982; FFJ 4: 525. 1989; FOC 17: 6. 1994; FGD 3: 350. 1995.
Callicarpa integrifolia Forbes & Hemsl., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 26: 253. 1890.

Scandent shrub. Branchlets terete, brown; young branchlets, petioles, and inflorescences densely yellowish brown tomentose, hairs branched to densely dendritic. Petiole ca. 2 cm; leaf blade broadly ovate, ovate or elliptic, 7–17 × 4–9 cm, base cuneate to rounded, apex acuminate to acute, margin entire, adaxially yellow‑brown stellate tomentose, abaxially densely greyish yellow tomentose; lateral veins 7–9 pairs. Cymes large, 6–11 cm across. Peduncle 2–5 cm. Pedicel and calyx densely stellate tomentose. Calyx‑limb subtruncate. Corolla purple, ca. 2–2.5 mm, glabrous. Stamens 2 times as long as corolla; anthers longitudinally dehiscing. Ovary stellate tomentose. Fruit subglobose, purple, ca. 2 mm in diam., stellate tomentose when young, glabrescent.

Locality: Bowen Rd., Cheung Sheung, Luk Keng, Nam Chung, Tung Chung. H. C. Tang 2210; Y. S. Lau 2072; HK sheet 4319.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Jiangxi, Fujian, Zhejiang.
Ecology: Forests on hillslopes or in valleys. Flowering: Jun.–Jul.; fruiting: Aug.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The type specimen was collected by J. G. Champion from Hong Kong Island between 1847 and 1850.

Callicarpa kochiana Makino 枇杷葉紫珠
Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 28(331): 181–182. 1914; FRPS 65(1): 30. 1982; FFJ 4: 524, fig. 415. 1989; FOC 17: 6. 1994; FGD 3: 349, fig. 229. 1995.
Callicarpa longiloba Merr., Philipp. J. Sc. 13(3): 156. 1918.
Callicarpa loureiri Hook. & Arn., Bot. Beechey Voy. 205. 1837; FGZ 629. 1956.
Callicarpa tomentosa auct. non Willd.: FHK 269. 1861.

Shrub 1–4 m tall. Branchlets, petioles, and inflorescences densely yellowish brown branched stellate tomentose. Petiole 1–3 cm; leaf blade oblong‑lanceolate, elliptic, or ovate‑elliptic, 12–22 × 4–8 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate or acute, margin serrate, adaxially glabrous or slightly pilose especially on veins, abaxially densely yellowish brown stellate tomentose, obscurely yellow glandular on both surfaces; lateral veins 10–18 pairs, prominent abaxially. Cymes 3–6 cm across. Peduncle 1–2 cm. Flowers subsessile. Calyx tubular, 2–2.5 mm, tube tomentose, teeth acute. Corolla pink to purple, lobes densely tomentose. Stamens exserted; filaments ca. 3.5 mm; anthers ovoid, ca. 1 mm. Style longer than stamens. Stigmas enlarged. Fruit globose, ca. 1.5 mm in diam., nearly completely enclosed by persistent calyx.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 575, 1038; L. T. Lo 142.
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong, Hunan, Jiangxi, Henan, Zhejiang, Taiwan; Japan, Vietnam.
Ecology: Forest edges, forests in valleys. Flowering: Jul.–Aug.; fruiting: Sep.–Dec.

Callicarpa longibracteata H. T. Chang 長苞紫珠
Acta Phytotax. Sin. 1(3 – 4): 277. 1951; FRPS 65(1): 37, fig. 11. 1982; FOC 17: 7. 1994; FGD 3: 350. 1995.

Shrub to 3 m tall. Young branches yellow stellate tomentose. Petiole ca. 2 cm, yellow stellate tomentose; leaf blade oblong‑elliptic to elliptic‑lanceolate, 15–20 × 5–8 cm, base obtuse to rounded and oblique, margin entire or serrulate above to middle, adaxially glabrous but stellate tomentose along midvein when young, abaxially densely yellow‑grey stellate tomentose; lateral veins 14 pairs, prominent abaxially. Cymes 6–9 cm across. Peduncle 3–5 cm. Bracts lanceolate, 3–4 × 1 cm. Calyx campanulate, stellate tomentose; teeth linear, ca. 1 mm. Corolla pink, ca. 2 mm, puberulent. Filaments ca. 5 mm; anthers ca. 0.6 mm, longitudinally dehiscing. Ovary glabrous. Style 6–7 mm. Fruit globose, ca. 1.5 mm in diam.

Locality: Luk Keng, Lantau Island. S. C. Ng 2858; Y. W. Lam 1705.
Distribution: Endemic to Hong Kong.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.
Notes: The type specimen (W. Y. Chun 5121, IBSC) was collected from mixed forests of altitude 100 – 300 m in Hong Kong in Aug. 1926.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Callicarpa longissima (Hemsl.) Merr 尖尾楓
Philipp. J. Sci. 12(2): 108. 1917; FGZ 631. 1956; FTW 4: 416. 1978, excl. syn. C. taiwaniana; FRPS 65(1): 52. 1982; FFJ 4: 531. 1989; FOC 17: 10. 1994; FGD 3: 354. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 411. 1998.
Callicarpa longifolia Lam. var. longissima Hemsl., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 26: 253. 1890.
Callicarpa longifolia auct. non Lam.: FKH 202. 1912, p.p.

Shrub or small tree, 1–3.5(–7) m tall. Branchlets purplish brown, tetragonal, with a ring of hair at node, stellate hairy when young. Petiole 1–1.5 cm; leaf blade papery, lanceolate to oblong‑lanceolate, 13–25 × 2–7 cm, base cuneate, apex acute, margin subentire to obscurely serrulate, adaxially subglabrous except long villous pubescence mainly along veins, abaxially glabrous, yellow glandular when fresh; veins 12–20 pairs, elevated on both surfaces. Cymes hairy, 3–6 cm across. Peduncle 1.5–3 cm. Calyx subtruncate to obscurely dentate, glabrous, glandular, limb inconspicuously 4‑dentate or truncate. Corolla pale purple, ca. 2.5 mm, glabrous. Stamens ca. twice as long as corolla tube. Ovary glabrous. Fruit oblique globose, 1–1.5 mm in diam., glabrous, glandular.

Locality: Tai Po Kau, Nam Hang, Fung Yuen, Ha Hang, Luk Keng, Lantau Island. H. C. Tang 2275, Y. S. Lau 1314, 2960.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Sichuan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests on hillslopes and open fields. Flowering: Jul.–Sep.; fruiting: Aug.–Dec.
Notes: It was reported as Callicarpa longifolia var. lanceolaria (Roxb.) C. B. Clarke previously (Check List HK Plants 59. 1993).

Callicarpa macrophylla Vahl 大葉紫珠
Symb. Bot. 3: 13, pl. 53. 1794; FHK 270. 1861; FKH 202. 1912; FGZ 630, fig. 336. 1956; FYN 1: 403, pl. 96: 9–12. 1977; FRPS 65(1): 38. 1982; FOC 17: 7. 1994; FGD 3: 351. 1995.
Callicarpa dunniana H. Lév., Repert. Spec. Nov. Regni Veg. 9(222 – 226): 456. 1911.
Callicarpa macrophylla var. kouytchensis H. Lév., Fl. Kouy‑Tchéou 440. 1915.

Shrub or small tree, 3–5 m. Branchlets nearly tetragonal, densely greyish mealy branched tomentose. Petiole robust, 1–3 cm, densely grey unevenly stellate tomentose; leaf blade oblong‑lanceolate, narrowly elliptic, or ovate‑elliptic, 10–23 × 5–11 cm, base cuneate to broadly obtuse, apex shortly acuminate, margin serrulate, adaxially pubescent especially on veins, abaxially densely unevenly grey stellate tomentose and glandular; lateral veins 8–11 pairs; veinlets slightly impressed adaxially. Cymes 4–8 cm across, densely unevenly grey stellate tomentose. Peduncle robust, 2–3 cm. Bracts linear. Calyx cupular, ca. 1 mm, subtruncate, grey stellate tomentose, yellow glandular. Corolla purple, ca. 2.5 mm, sparsely stellate tomentose; filaments ca. 5 mm; anthers yellow glandular. Ovary puberulent. Fruit globose, ca. 1.5 mm in diam., puberulent, glandular.

Locality: Nam Chung, Luk Keng, Kau Yi Chau, Tai A Chau. S. P. Lau 151; HK sheet 34818, 34907.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan; Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Thailand, Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Dec.

Callicarpa nudiflora Hook. & Arn. 裸花紫珠
Bot. Beechey Voy. 206, pl. 46. 1837; FGZ 630. 1956; FRPS 65(1): 37. 1982; FFJ 4: 526. 1989; FOC 17: 7. 1994; FGD 3: 351. 1995.
Callicarpa acuminata Roxb., Fl. Ind., ed. 1820, 1: 408. 1820, nom. illeg.
Callicarpa acuminata var. angustifolia F. P. Metcalf, Lingnan Sci. J. 11(3): 407. 1932.
Callicarpa macrophylla Vahl var. sinensis C. B. Clarke, Fl. Brit. India 4(12): 568. 1885.
Callicarpa reevesii Wall. ex Schauer, Prodr. 11: 641. 1847; FHK 270. 1861; FKH 202. 1912.

Shrub or small tree, 3–4(–7) m. Old branches glabrous, evidently lenticellate. Young branchlets, petioles, abaxial leaf surfaces, and inflorescences unevenly greyish brown stellate tomentose. Petiole 1–2 cm; leaf blade ovate‑elliptic to lanceolate, 12–22 × 4–7 cm, base obtuse to subrounded, apex acute or acuminate, margin serrate, slightly undulate, or subentire, adaxially dark green and subglabrous except for stellate tomentose veins, abaxially densely greyish brown unevenly stellate tomentose; lateral veins 14–18 pairs. Cymes 8–13 cm across. Peduncle 3– 8 cm. Bracts linear‑lanceolate. Pedicel ca. 1 mm. Calyx cupular, usually glabrous, truncate to obscurely 4‑dentate. Corolla purple to pink, ca. 2 mm, glabrous. Stamens 2–3 times as long as corolla; anthers ellipsoidal, dehiscing by longitudinal slits. Ovary glabrous. Fruit subglobose, ca. 2 mm in diam., red, turning black when dry.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 1138, 1896; Y. S. Lau 365.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan; Bangladesh, India, Malaysia, Myanmar, Singapore, Sri Lanka, Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Jun.–Aug.; fruiting: Aug.–Dec.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Tam, Tsim Shan, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Callicarpa rubella Lindl. 紅紫珠
Bot. Reg. 11: pl. 883. 1825; FHK 271. 1861; FKH 203. 1912; FYN 1: 410, pl. 98: 6 – 10. 1977; FRPS 65(1): 63. 1982; FFJ 4: 526, fig. 417. 1989; FOC 17: 13. 1994; FGD 3: 357. 1995.
Callicarpa dielsii (H. Lév.) C. P’ei, Mem. Sci. Soc. China 1(3): 37. 1932.
Callicarpa panduriformis H. Lév., Repert. Spec. Nov. Regni Veg. 9(222 – 226): 455. 1911.
Callicarpa rubella var. dielsii (H. Lév.) H. L. Li, J. Arnold Arbor. 25(4): 425. 1944.
Callicarpa rubella var. hemsleyana Diels, Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 29(3 – 4): 547 – 548. 1900.
Callicarpa tenuiflora Champ., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 5: 135. 1853.
Viburnum dielsii H. Lév., Repert. Spec. Nov. Regni Veg. 9(222 – 226): 443. 1911.

Shrub, 1.5–2 m tall. Branchlets robust, with brown stellate and glandular hairs. Petiole very short to subsessile; leaf blade papery, obovate or obovate‑elliptic, 10–15 × 4–8 cm, base cordate and sometimes oblique, apex acuminate to caudate, margin serrulate, irregularly serrate, or serrate, adaxially with glandular hairs, abaxially with stellate, simple, and glandular hairs and yellow glandular; lateral veins 6–10 pairs, midvein, lateral veins, and reticulate veins elevated on both surfaces. Cymes 2–4 cm across, covered with brown stellate and glandular hairs. Peduncle to 3 cm. Bracts small. Calyx subtruncate to slightly dentate with obtusely triangular teeth, with stellate hairs, glandular hairs, and yellow glands. Corolla purple, sometimes greenish, or white, ca. 3 mm, puberulent, yellow glandular. Stamens twice as long as corolla. Fruit subglobose, purple, ca. 2 mm in diam.

Locality: Tai Tam, Tsim Shan, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island. U. A. On 5605; Y. S. Lau 1253; P. S. Choi 210.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Anhui, Jiangxi, Zhejiang; Indonesia, Malaysia, Myanmar, Thailand, Vietnam.
Ecology: Thickets. Flowering: May–Jul.; fruiting: Jul.–Nov.
Notes: The type specimen of Callicarpa tenuiflora was collected by J. G. Champion from “Saywan” (Chai Wan) between 1847 and 1850.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Lamma Island, Tai A Chau, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Caryopteris incana (Thunb. ex Houtt.) Miq. 蘭香草
Ann. Mus. Bot. Lugduno‑Batavum 2: 97. 1866; FGZ 634. 1956; FTW 4: 418. 1978; FRPS 65(1): 198. 1982; FFJ 4: 551, fig. 431. 1989; FOC 17: 45. 1994; FGD 3: 384. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 414, photo. 178. 1998.
Nepeta incana Thunb. ex Houtt., Nat. Hist. 2(9): 307. 1778.
Barbula sinensis Lour., Fl. Cochchin. 367. 1790.
Caryopteris mastacantnus Schauer, Prodr. 11: 625. 1847; FHK 268. 1861; FKH 205. 1912.
Caryopteris ovata Miq., J. Bot. Neerl. 1: 144. 1861.
Caryopteris sinensis (Lour.) Dippel, Handb. Laubholzkunde 1: 59, fig. 24. 1889.

Perennial herb, 20–60 cm or taller, aromatic, with woody base. Branchlets terete, often slightly purple, greyish white pubescent, glabrescent. Petiole 0.3–1.7 mm; leaf blade thickly papery, oblong, ovate or lanceolate, 1.5–7(–9) × 0.4–4 cm, base cuneate, subrounded, or truncate, apex obtuse to acute, margin coarsely serrate to rarely subentire, greyish white pubescent and yellow glandular on both surfaces. Inflorescences dense corymbose cymes. Bracts and bracteoles absent. Calyx cupular, ca. 2 mm, pubescent and glandular abaxially, 5‑lobed, lobes oblong‑lanceolate, longer than tube. Corolla purplish to bluish, tube ca. 6 mm, throat with a ring of hairs, lower lobe fringed, pubescent and glandular on both surfaces. Stamens and style exserted. Ovary pubescent. Fruiting calyx 4– 5 mm. Fruit ca. 2.5 mm in diam., hirsute, nutlets with winged edges.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Lamma Island, Tai A Chau, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 1296; P. S. Choi 517; Y. W. Lam 1181.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Fujian, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Anhui, Jiangsu; Japan, Korea.
Ecology: Hillslopes. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Shing Mun, Wu Kau Tang, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Clerodendrum canescens Wall. ex Walp. 灰毛大青（獅子球）
Repert. Bot. Syst. 4: 105. 1845; FHK 272. 1861; FKH 205. 1912; FYN 1: 473, pl. 113: 7 – 8. 1977; FTW 4: 421. 1978; FRPS 65(1): 171. 1982; FFJ 4: 547. 1989; FOC 17: 39. 1994; FGD 3: 379, fig. 245. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 416. 1998.
Clerodendrum haematocalyx Hance, Ann. Bot. Syst. 3: 238. 1852.
Clerodendrum viscosum auct. non Vent.: FHN 4: 25. 1977; Check List HK Plants 59. 1993.

Shrub, 1–3.5 m tall. Petioles and peduncles densely yellowish to brownish tomentose to nearly villous. Branchlets tetragonal. Petiole 1.5–12 cm; leaf blade broadly ovate or cordate, rarely ovate, 6–18 × 4–15 cm, base cordate to subtruncate, apex acuminate, margin entire or sparsely mucronate‑dentate, villous especially on veins. Inflorescences terminal, subconical. Peduncle robust, 1.5–11 cm. Bracts leaf‑like, elliptic to ovate, 0.5–2.4 cm. Calyx green when young, ca. 1.3 cm, membranous, deeply 5‑lobed, lobes ovate to broadly ovate. Corolla white or pinkish, outside puberulent; tube slender, ca. 2 cm; lobes obovate‑oblong, 5–6 mm, reflexed. Stamens and style exserted. Fruiting calyx red. Drupes green when young, dark blue to black at maturity, subglobose, ca. 7 mm in diam.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Shing Mun, Wu Kau Tang, Lantau Island. H. C. Tang 540; Y. S. Lau 1281; P. S. Choi 379.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Vietnam.
Ecology: Thin forests on slopes. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Oct.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Sai Kung, Wun Yiu, Fung Kat Heung, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Clerodendrum chinense (Osbeck) Mabb. 重瓣臭茉莉
Pl.‑Book (corr. repr. 1989) 707. 1989; FOC 17: 39. 1994; FTW ed. 2, 4: 416. 1998.
Cryptanthus chinensis Osbeck, Dagb. Ostind. Resa 215. 1757.
Clerodendrum philippinum Schauer, Prodr. 11: 666. 1847; FTW 4: 423. 1978; FYN 1: 470, pl. 112: 3 – 6. 1977; FRPS 65(1): 173, fig. 91. 1982.
Clerodendrum fragrans auct. non Vent.: FKH 205. 1912, p.p.

Shrub, 0.5–1.2 m tall. Branchlets nearly tetragonal to terete, pubescent when young, glabrescent. Petiole 3–17 cm, pubescent to tomentose; leaf blade broadly ovate to nearly heart‑shaped, 9–22 × 8–21 cm, base truncate, broadly truncate, or subcordate, apex acuminate, margin sparsely irregularly dentate, adaxially strigose, abaxially pubescent especially on veins and with several large glands near base. Cymes terminal, dense corymbose. Peduncle tomentose. Bracts lanceolate, 1.5–3 cm; pubescent, with several large glands. Flowers double, fragrant. Calyx campanulate, 1.5–1.7 cm, deeply 5‑lobed, pubescent, with several large glands; lobes linear‑lanceolate, 0.7– 1 cm. Corolla white, pinkish, or red, tube short, lobes ovate.

Locality: Sai Kung, Wun Yiu, Fung Kat Heung, Lantau Island. H. C. Tang 103, 2211; HK sheet 21897.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan (cultivated); widely cultivated in tropical and subtropical Asia.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The species was reported as Clerodendrum fragrans (Vent.) Willd. previously (Check List HK Plants 59. 1993, p.p.).

Clerodendrum cyrtophyllum Turcz. 大青
Bull. Soc. Imp. Naturalistes Moscou 36(3): 222. 1863; FKH 205. 1912; FHN 4: 24, fig. 955. 1977; FYN 1: 460, pl. 110: 1 – 3. 1977; FTW 4: 421. 1978; FRPS 65(1): 164. 1982; FFJ 4: 549, fig. 429. 1989; FOC 17: 38. 1994; FGD 3: 378. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 417, photo 247. 1998.
Clerodendrum amplius Hance, Ann. Sci. Nat. Bot., sér. 5, 5: 233. 1866.
Clerodendrum formosanum Maxim., Bull. Acad. Imp. Sci. Saint‑Petersbourg 31: 85. 1886, ‘Clerodendron’.
Cordia venosa Hemsl., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 26(174): 143. 1890.

Shrub or small tree, 1–10 m tall. Branchlets yellowish brown, pubescent. Petiole 1–8 cm; leaf blade papery, elliptic, ovate‑elliptic, oblong or oblong‑lanceolate, 6–20 × 3–9 cm, base rounded to cuneate, apex acuminate to acute, margin entire, glabrous or sparsely pubescent along veins, abaxially glandular; lateral veins 6–10 pairs. Cymes corymbose, terminal or subterminal, 10–16 × 20–25 cm. Bracts linear, 3–7 mm. Flowers small, fragrant. Calyx cupular, 3–4 mm, minutely tomentose and glandular abaxially, glabrous adaxially; lobes triangular‑ovate, ca. 1 mm. Corolla white, sparsely puberulent, glandular; tube slender, ca. 1 cm; lobes ovate, ca. 5 mm. Stamens and style exserted. Ovary glabrous. Stigma 2‑lobed. Fruiting calyx red. Drupes blue‑purple, obovoid to globose, 5–10 mm in diam.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 886, 1979; P. S. Choi 380.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Henan, Hubei, Anhui, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Korea, Malaysia, Vietnam.
Ecology: Margins of forests, wastelands. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Feb. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Clerodendrum fortunatum L. 白花燈籠（鬼燈籠）
Sp. Pl. ed. 2, 889. 1763; FKH 205. 1912; FGZ 633, fig. 338. 1956; FHN 4: 23. 1977; FRPS 65(1): 156, fig. 79. 1982; FFJ 4: 544. 1989; FOC 17: 37. 1994; FGD 3: 377, fig. 243. 1995.
Clerodendrum castaneifolium Hook. & Arn., Bot. Beechey Voy. 205. 1837, ‘Clerodendron’.
Clerodendrum lividum Lindl., Bot. Reg. 11: pl. 945. 1825, ‘Clerodendron’.
Clerodendrum oxysepalum Miq., J. Bot. Neerl. 1: 114. 1861, ‘Clerodendron’.
Clerodendrum pentagonum Hance, Ann. Bot. Syst. 3: 238. 1852, ‘Clerodendron’.
Clerodendrum pumilum (Lour.) Spreng., Syst. Veg. 2: 759. 1825, ‘Clerodendron’.
Volkameria pumila Lour., Fl. Cochin. 388. 1790.

Shrub to 2.5 m tall. Branchlets densely yellowish brown pubescent when young. Petiole 0.5–3 cm, densely yellowish brown pubescent; leaf blade papery, long elliptic, obovate‑lanceolate, or rarely ovate‑elliptic, 5–17.5 × 1.5–5 cm, base cuneate to broadly cuneate, apex acuminate, margin entire or undulate, adaxially sparsely pubescent, abaxially pubescent along veins and densely small yellow glandular. Cymes axillary, shorter than leaves, 3– 9‑flowered. Peduncle 1–4 cm, densely brown pubescent. Bracts linear, densely brown pubescent. Calyx reddish purple, 5‑veined, like lantern in shape, 1–1.3 cm, deeply 5‑lobed, glabrous adaxially, pubescent abaxially; lobes broadly ovate. Corolla white or pinkish, salverform; tube straight, ± funnelform, slightly longer than calyx; limb oblique; lobes oblong, ca. 6 mm, reflexed. Stamens longer than corolla. Style filiform, shorter than stamens. Stigma 2‑lobed. Fruiting calyx inflated. Drupes dark blue‑green, subglobose, ca. 5 mm in diam., enclosed by persistent calyx.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 1767, 2124; K. L. Yip 4485.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Jiangxi; Philippines, Vietnam.
Ecology: Wastelands and thickets. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Clerodendrum inerme (L.) Gaertn. 苦郎樹（假茉莉）
Fruct. Sem. Pl. 1: 271, pl. 75. 1788; FHK 271. 1861; FKH 204. 1912; FGZ 632. 1956; FHN 4: 22. 1977; FRPS 65(1): 154, fig. 77. 1982; FFJ 4: 543, fig. 426. 1989; FOC 17: 42. 1994; FGD 3: 377. 1995.
Volkameria inermis L., Sp. Pl. 2: 637. 1753.

Scandent shrub, to 2 m. Stems erect or creeping. Branchlets tetragonal, yellowish grey, pubescent. Petiole ca. 1 cm; leaf blade thinly leathery, ovate, elliptic or elliptic‑lanceolate, 3–7 × 1.5–4.5 cm, base obtuse, apex obtuse, margin entire, slightly revolute, adaxially dark green, subglabrous, abaxially pale green, glabrous or sparsely pubescent along veins, small glandular on both surfaces; lateral veins 4–7 pairs. Cymes axillary, usually 3‑flowered, pubescent. Peduncle 2–4 mm. Bracts linear, ca. 2 cm. Flowers fragrant. Calyx campanulate, finely pubescent abaxially, sparsely glandular, apex subtruncate, with minute rudimentary teeth. Corolla white; tube 2–3 cm, ca. 2 mm in diam. at throat, densely silky pubescent adaxially, subglabrous and inconspicuously glandular abaxially, 5‑lobed; lobes elliptic, ca. 7 mm. Stamens 4(–6), filaments purple, slender, exserted. Ovary glabrous. Style glabrous, exserted. Stigma 2‑lobed. Drupes greyish yellow, obovoid to subglobose, 6–11 mm in diam.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 712, 2152; Y. W. Lam 25.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; SE Asia, Australia, Pacific islands.
Ecology: Near seashore. Flowering & fruiting: Mar.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Clerodendrum japonicum (Thunb.) Sweet 赬桐
Hort. Brit. 1: 322. 1826; FHN 4: 23. 1977; FYN 1: 478, pl. 114: 5. 1977; FRPS 65(1): 187, fig. 99. 1982; FFJ 4: 544, fig. 427. 1989; FOC 17: 36. 1994; FGD 3: 381. 1995.
Volkameria japonica Thunb., Nova Acta Regiae Soc. Sci. Upsal. 3: 203. 1780.
Clerodendrum kaempferi (Jacq.) Siebold, Verh. Batav. Genootsch. Kunsten 3: 207. 1789; FGZ 634. 1956; FTW ed. 2, 4: 419, photo 249. 1998.
Volkameria kaempferi Jacq., Collectanea 3: 207. 1789.

Shrub, 1–4 m tall. Branchlets tetragonal, pubescent to subglabrous, nodes sometimes villous. Petiole 0.5–15 cm, densely yellowish brown pubescent; leaf blade nearly heart‑shaped, 8–35 × 6–27 cm, base cordate, apex acuminate to acute, margin sparsely serrulate to dentate, adaxially sparsely pubescent, abaxially densely covered with many peltate glands and yellowish brown pubescent. Thyrses terminal, 15–34 × 13–35 cm. Bracts broadly ovate, ovate‑lanceolate, linear‑lanceolate, reddish; bracteoles usually reddish. Calyx red, 1–1.5 cm, abaxially pubescent and peltate glandular, deeply 5‑lobed; lobes ovate‑lanceolate to ovate, 0.7–1.3 cm. Corolla red, rarely white; tube 1.7–2.2 cm, puberulous abaxially; lobes oblong, 1–1.5 cm. Stamens and style 3 times as long as corolla‑tube or longer. Ovary glabrous, 4‑locular. Stigma 2‑cleft. Fruiting calyx much longer than fruit, enlarged, enclosing fruit at first, reflexed at maturity. Drupes subglobose, bluish black at maturity, 7–10 mm in diam.

Locality: Cultivated. H. C. Tang 174; Y. S. Lau 985, 1901.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan, Zhejiang, Jiangsu; Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Vietnam.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: May–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.

Clerodendrum lindleyi Decne ex Planch. 尖齒臭茉莉
Fl. Serres Jard. Eur. 9: 17. 1853; FYN 1: 471, pl. 112: 8. 1977; FRPS 65(1): 174, fig. 92. 1982; FFJ 4: 548. 1989; FOC 17: 39. 1994; FGD 3: 380. 1995.
Clerodendrum fragrans auct. non Vent.: FKH 205. 1912, p.p.

Shrub, 0.5–3 m tall. Branchlets pubescent, nearly tetragonal when young, becoming subterete, pubescent. Petiole 2–11 cm, pubescent; leaf blade papery, broadly ovate to heart‑shaped, 6.5–12.5(–22) × 5.5–10(–20) cm, base truncate to cordate, apex acuminate, margin irregularly serrate or undulate, pubescent especially abaxially, with several peltate glands at base. Cymes terminal, dense, corymbose. Peduncle pubescent. Bracts many, lanceolate, 2.5–4 cm, puberulent, with several peltate glands. Calyx 1–1.5 cm, deeply 5‑lobed, densely puberulent, with several peltate glands; lobes linear‑lanceolate, 4–10 mm. Corolla purplish red or pale red, tube 2–3 cm; lobes obovate, 5– 7 mm. Stamens exserted. Style exceeding stamens. Drupes enclosed in purple, inflated, persistent calyx, bluish black, subglobose, 5–6 mm in diam.

Locality: New Territories. S. T. Dunn 1194.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Zhejiang, Jiangsu, Anhui.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The species was reported as Clerodendrum fragrans (Vent.) Willd. previously (Check List HK Plants 59. 1993, p.p.).

Clerodendrum thomsonae Balf. 龍吐珠
Edinburgh New Philos. J. 15(2): 233, t. 2. 1862; FGZ 632. 1956; FHN 4: 22. 1977; FYN 1:458, pl. 109: 3 – 4. 1977; FRPS 65(1): 156. 1982; FFJ 4: 543. 1989; FGD 3: 377. 1995.

Scandent shrub, 2–5 m. Young branchlets tetragonal, yellowish brown tomentose, glabrescent. Petiole 1–2 cm; leaf blade papery, narrowly ovate or ovate‑oblong, 4–10 × 1.5–4 cm, base subrotund, apex acuminate, entire, adaxially slightly rough, hispidulous, abaxially subglabrous; basal veins 3. Cymes axillary or pseudoterminal, dichotomous, 7– 15 × 10–17 cm. Bracts narrowly lanceolate, 0.5–1 cm. Calyx white, connate at base, enlarged at middle, apex deeply 5‑lobed, finely pubescent abaxially; lobes elliptic, ca. 9 mm. Corolla‑tube as long as calyx. Stamens 4, exserted. Style exserted; stigma 2‑lobed. Fruiting calyx not enlarged, reddish purple. Drupes subglobose, ca. 1.5 cm in diam., pyrenes 2–4.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 1498, 1892; HK sheet 21984.
Distribution: Native to tropical W Africa, widely cultivated in the tropics.
Ecology: Flowering: Mar.–May.
Uses: Ornamental.

Clerodendrum wallichii Merr. 垂茉莉（黑葉龍吐珠）
J. Arnold Arbor. 33(3): 220. 1952; FYN 1: 461, pl. 110: 8 – 9. 1977; FRPS 65(1): 158, fig. 80. 1982; FOC 17: 36. 1994.
Clerodendrum nutans Wall. ex D. Don, Prodr. Fl. Nepal. 103. 1825, nom. illeg.

Shrub or small tree, 2–4 m tall. Branchlets tetragonal, ± winged, glabrous. Petiole ca. 1 cm; leaf blade subleathery, oblong to oblong‑lanceolate, 11–18 × 2.5–4 cm, base narrowly cuneate, apex acuminate to acute, margin entire, glabrous; lateral veins 7–8 pairs, adaxially slightly prominent. Thyrses terminal, 20–33 cm, pendulous, glabrous, axis and peduncle tetragonal or winged; cymes opposite or decussate, several‑flowered. Bracts small, linear or subulate. Calyx red to purple, ca. 1 cm, tube very short; lobes ovate‑lanceolate, 7–8 mm, enlarged in fruit. Corolla white, tube ca. 1.1 cm; lobes obovate, 1.1–1.5 cm. Stamens and style exserted. Fruiting calyx red to purple, inflated, thickened. Drupes yellowish green when young, black and shiny at maturity, globose, 1–1.3 cm in diam., often 2‑sulcate.

Locality: Cultivated. P. S. Choi 184.
Distribution: Guangxi, Yunnan, Xizang; Bangladesh, India, Myanmar, Vietnam.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Oct.–Apr. of the following year.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: The species was reported as Clerodendrum nutans Wall. previously (Check List HK Plants 59. 1993).

Duranta erecta L. 假連翹
Sp. Pl. 2: 637. 1753; FOC 17: 2. 1994.
Duranta repens L., Sp. Pl. 2: 637. 1753; FGZ 626. 1956; FHN 4: 5, fig. 947. 1977; FYN 1: 399, pl. 95: 3 – 4. 1977; FRPS 65(1): 22, fig. 7. 1982; FFJ 4: 522, fig. 414. 1989; FGD 3: 347, fig. 228. 1995.

Shrub, often scandent, 1.5–3 m. Branches spiny, pubescent when young. Leaves opposite, sometimes whorled. Petiole ca. 1 cm, pubescent; leaf blade papery, ovate to ovate‑lanceolate, 2–6.5 × 1.5–3.5 cm, base cuneate, apex acute to obtuse, margin entire to crenate distally, pubescent. Calyx‑tube tubular, ca. 5 mm, 5‑veined, pubescent on both surfaces. Corolla often bluish purple, ca. 8 mm, slightly irregular 5‑lobed. Stamens inclusive. Ovary glabrous. Styles shorter than corolla‑tube. Drupes globose, ca. 5 mm in diam., shorter than calyx, shiny, glabrous.

Locality: Cultivated. H. C. Tang 48, 183; L. T. Lo 572.
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Taiwan, Zhejiang; native to America.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: May–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental (hedges).

Gmelina chinensis Benth. 石梓（華石梓）
FHK 272. 1861; FKH 203. 1912; FRPS 65(1): 129, fig. 64. 1982; FFJ 4: 537, fig. 423. 1989; FOC 17: 33. 1994; FGD 3: 370. 1995.

Tree or shrub, 4–12 m tall; bark grey. Branchlets robust, yellowish brown pubescent when young, glabrescent. Petiole 2–5.5 cm, sulcate, pubescent when young, glabrescent; leaf blade papery to thickly papery, ovate‑elliptic to ovate, 5–15 × 3–7(–9) cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, margin entire, adaxially glabrous, abaxially greyish white, puberulent and glandular; basal veins 3, lateral veins 3–5 pairs, prominent abaxially. Inflorescences terminal thyrses. Bracts leaf‑like, deciduous. Peduncle 5–10 cm, hairy. Calyx campanulate, 0.5–1.2 cm, apex truncate or 4‑denticulate, adaxially sparsely glandular and glabrous, abaxially pubescent, grey downy and with several disk‑shaped glands. Corolla funnelform, white or pinkish, 3–3.5 cm, throat ca. 2.5 cm in diam., sparsely glandular adaxially, densely glandular abaxially. Filaments flat, sparsely glandular‑hairy. Ovary obovoid, apically densely pubescent, basally glabrous. Drupes obovoid, ca. 2.2 cm.

Locality: Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 1279, 2730; HK sheet 36035.
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: May–Sep.; fruiting: Aug.–Sep.
Notes: The type specimen was collected by C. Wright from Hong Kong between 1853 and 1854. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Holmskioldia sanguinea Retz. 冬紅花
Observ. Bot. 6: 31. 1791; FRPS 65(1): 192, pl. 21. 1982; FFJ 4: 550, fig. 430. 1989; FGD 3: 383. 1995.

Evergreen shrub, 3–7 m. Branchlets tetragonal, 4‑sulcate, hairy. Petiole 1–2 cm, sulcate, hairy and glandular; leaf blade membranous, ovate or broadly ovate, base rounded or subtruncate, margin serrate, sparsely hairy and glandular on both surfaces, hairs dense along veins. Thyrses composed of 2–6 cymes, each cyme 3‑flowered. Peduncle and pedicels with glandular hairs and long simple hairs. Calyx red to orange‑red, to 2 cm in diam., sparsely ciliate, reticulate veins conspicuous. Corolla red; tube 2–2.5 cm, glandular. Stamens 4, filaments 2.5–3 cm, glandular. Fruit obovoid, ca. 6 mm, enclosed in enlarged persistent calyx.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 1458, 3197; HK sheet 22007.
Distribution: Taiwan, Guangdong, Guangxi (cultivated); native to Himalaya.
Uses: Ornamental.

Lantana camara L. 馬纓丹（如意草）
Sp. Pl. 2: 627. 1753; FHK 268. 1861; FKH 201. 1912; FRPS 65(1): 17, fig. 4. 1982; FFJ 4: 520, fig. 412. 1989; FOC 17: 2. 1994; FGD 3: 343. 1995.

Erect shrub 1–2 m or taller. Stems and branches tetragonal, armed with stout recurved prickles, pubescent. Petiole 1–2 cm, pubescent; leaf blade papery, wrinkled, very rough, with short stiff hairs, aromatic when crushed, ovate to oblong, 3–8.5 × 1.5–5 cm, base rounded to subcordate, apex acute or acuminate, margin crenate; lateral veins 5 pairs, elevated. Capitula terminal, 1.5–2.5 cm across. Peduncle robust, longer than petiole. Bracts lanceolate, 3 times as long as calyx, hirsute abaxially. Calyx tubular, membranous, ca. 1.5 mm, limb very short dentate. Corolla yellow or orange, often turning deep red soon after opening, tube ca. 1 cm, 4–6 mm in diam., pubescent on both surfaces; limb 4–5‑lobed, spreading. Ovary glabrous. Drupes globose, ca. 4 mm in diam., purplish black.

Locality: Naturalized in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 579, 2536; L. T. Lo 487.
Distribution: Naturalized in S China; native to America, widely naturalized in the tropical and subtropical regions of the world.
Ecology: Thickets and open fields. Flowering & fruiting: Nearly all year round.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.
Notes: A very wide range of flower colours has been developed within cultivars of this species. Lantana camara ‘Snow White’ (雪白馬纓丹) is also cultivated for ornamental uses.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Shek O, Mount Kellet, Tai Mo Shan, Tai Long Sai Wan, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Phyla nodiflora (L.) Greene 過江藤
Pittonia 4(20E): 46. 1899; FTW 4: 427. 1978; FRPS 65(1): 19, fig. 5. 1982; FFJ 4: 520, fig. 413. 1989; FOC 17: 3. 1994; FGD 3: 344, fig. 225. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 421, photo. 252. 1998.
Verbena nodiflora L., Sp. Pl. 1: 20. 1753.
Lippia nodiflora (L.) Michx., Fl. Bor.‑Amer. 2: 15. 1803; FKH 201. 1912; FGZ 623. 1956; FHN 4: 4, fig. 945. 1977.
Phyla chinensis Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 66. 1790.

Perennial herb, multibranched. Branches many, creeping, rooting at distal nodes, minutely strigose. Leaves subsessile; leaf blade papery, spatulate, obovate to oblanceolate, 1–3 × 0.5–1.5 cm, base narrowly cuneate, apex obtuse, margin distally sharply serrate, pubescent. Spikes cylindric to ovoid, 0.5–3 × 0.6 cm. Peduncle 1– 7 cm. Bracts broadly ovate, ca. 3 mm wide. Calyx ca. 2 mm. Corolla pinkish purple or white, glabrous. Stamens inclusive. Ovary glabrous. Capsules pale yellow, ca. 1.5 mm in diam., enclosed by persistent calyx.

Locality: Shek O, Mount Kellet, Tai Mo Shan, Tai Long Sai Wan, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 658, 2582; Y. W. Lam 777.
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong, Guizhou, Hainan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangsu, Jiangxi, Sichuan, Taiwan, Xizang, Yunnan; widely distributed in tropical and subtropical regions.
Ecology: Grasslands, along streams. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Clear Water Bay, Sha Tin, Kei Ling Ha, Castle Peak, Ma On Shan, Ping Chau
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Premna serratifolia L. 傘序臭黃荊（美娘子）
Mant. Pl. 2: 253. 1771; FHK 203. 1861; FOC 17: 26. 1994; FTW ed. 2, 4: 423, photo 254. 1998.
Cornutia corymbosa Burm. f., Fl. Indica 132. pl. 41, fig. 1. 1768.
Premna corymbosa (Burm. f.) Rottler & Willd., Ges. Naturf. Freunde Berlin Mag. Neuesten Entdeck. Gesammten Naturk. 4: 187. 1803. ; FHN 4: 17. 1977; FRPS 65(1): 114. 5. 1982; FFJ 4: 537. 1989; FGD 3: 366. 1995.
Premna integrifolia L., Mant. Pl. 2: 154. 1771; FKH 203. 1912.
Premna integrifolia var. obtusifolia (R. Br.) C. P’ei, Mem. Sci. Soc. China 1(3): 75. 1932.
Premna obtusifolia R. Br., Prodr. 512. 1810; FGD 3: 367, fig. 238. 1995.

Shrub or small tree, 1–4(–8) m tall, erect or rarely scandent. Branchlets pale yellow lenticellate, densely pubescent when young, subglabrescent. Petiole 0.3–5 cm, puberulent; leaf blade papery to subleathery, oblong, broadly ovate, oblong‑ovate, obovate to suborbicular, 3–15 × 2.5–9.5 cm, base broadly cuneate, rounded, or truncate, apex acute to rarely acuminate or obtuse, margin entire, slightly undulate, or crenate, subglabrous or pubescent only along veins on both surfaces. Inflorescences 1.5–15 × 2.5–24 cm. Peduncle 0.8–3 cm. Bracts to 6 mm, puberulent. Calyx cupular, 1.5–3 mm, 2‑lipped, lower lip subentire to shortly 3‑dentate, upper lip longer than lower lip and 2‑dentate, abaxially puberulent and yellow glandular. Corolla pale yellow, abaxially glandular, slightly 2‑lipped; lower lip 3‑lobed, lobes subequal or middle lobe slightly longer and broader; upper lip entire or emarginate. Ovary glabrous, apically glandular. Style 3.5–4 mm. Fruit globose or obovoid, 2–4 mm in diam., sparsely yellow glandular.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Clear Water Bay, Sha Tin, Kei Ling Ha, Castle Peak, Ma On Shan, Ping Chau. Y. S. Lau 308, 389; HK sheet 39784.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Taiwan; S & SE Asia, Australia, Pacific islands.
Ecology: Forests, hillslopes. Flowering: Summer; fruiting: Autumn.

Stachytarpheta jamaicensis (L.) Vahl 假馬鞭
Enum. Pl. 1: 206. 1804; FHN 4: 4, fig. 946. 1977; FYN 1: 397, pl. 95: 1 – 2. 1977; FTW 4: 431. 1978; FRPS 65(1): 20, fig. 6. 1982; FFJ 4: 522. 1989; FOC 17: 3. 1994; FGD 3: 345, fig. 226. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 424. 1998.
Verbena jamaicensis L., Sp. Pl. 1: 19. 1753.

Perennial robust herb or subshrub, 0.6–2 m tall. Branchlets tetragonal when young, sparsely pubescent to subglabrous. Petiole winged, 1–3 cm; leaf blade thickly papery, elliptic to oblong‑ovate, 2.4–8 × 2–4.5 cm, base elongate, apex acuminate, margin coarsely serrate, sparsely pubescent to subglabrous; lateral veins 3–6 pairs, prominent abaxially. Spikes 10–30 cm. Bracts ca. 5 mm, margin membranous, ciliate. Calyx tubular, membranous, transparent, ca. 6 mm, glabrous. Corolla dark blue; tube 0.7–1.2 cm, slightly curved. Ovary glabrous.

Locality: Naturalized in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1980, 2205; L. T. Lo 568.
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan, Taiwan, Yunnan (naturalized); native to tropical America, widely naturalized in tropical regions of the Old World.
Ecology: Shaded grassy places in valleys. Flowering: Aug.; fruiting: Sep.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Tectona grandis L. f. 柚木
Suppl. Pl. 151. 1781 [1782]; FGZ 632. 1956; FHN 4: 25, fig. 956. 1977; FYN 1: 415, pl. 99: 3 – 4. 1977; FRPS 65(1): 80, fig. 41. 1982; FFJ 4: 534. 1989; FOC 17: 16. 1994; FGD 3: 361, fig. 235. 1995.

Tree to 40 m tall. Branchlets grey to greyish brown, tetragonal and sulcate, yellowish to greyish brown stellate tomentose. Petiole robust, 2–4 cm or longer; leaf blade papery, ovate‑elliptic to ovate, 15–50 × 8–25 cm, base cuneate and decurrent, apex acuminate to obtuse, adaxially scabrous and puberulent along veins, abaxially densely greyish brown to yellowish brown minutely stellate tomentose; lateral veins 7–12 pairs, veinlets subparallel, evidently prominent abaxially. Panicles 25–40 × 30 cm. Flowers fragrant. Calyx‑tube 2–3 mm, white stellate tomentose, limb slightly shorter than calyx‑tube. Corolla white; tube 2.5–3 mm, abaxially puberulent and glandular; lobes ca. 2 mm, apex obtuse. Ovary strigose. Style 3–4 mm. Drupes globose, 1.2–1.8 cm in diam., minutely tomentose.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 2934; K. C. Chau 3330; HK sheet 34486.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan (cultivated or naturalized); native to India, Myanmar, Malaysia, Indonesia.
Ecology: Flowering: Aug.; fruiting: Oct.
Uses: Timber, medicinal (folklore).

Verbena officinalis L. 馬鞭草
Sp. Pl. 1: 20–21. 1753; FGZ 624, fig. 330. 1956; FHN 4: 2, fig. 943. 1977; FYN 1: 392, pl. 93: 1–2. 1977; FTW 4: 432. 1978; FRPS 65(1): 15, fig. 3. 1982; FFJ 4: 518, fig. 411. 1989; FOC 17: 3. 1994; FGD 3: 342. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 425. 1998.

Perennial erect herb, 0.3–1.4 cm tall. Stems tetragonal, often hirsute at nodes and along ridges. Petiole 0.3–4 cm; leaf blade papery, ovate, obovate, or oblong‑lanceolate, 2–8 × 1–5 cm, margin coarsely dentate or cut to sometimes deeply pinnatifid or lobed, hirsute especially on abaxial veins. Spikes long, slender, to 25 cm in fruit. Bracteoles slightly shorter than calyx, hirsute. Calyx 1–4 mm, hirsute, glandular, 5‑veined. Corolla blue to pink, 4–8 mm, puberulent abaxially. Ovary glabrous. Fruit ellipsoidal, ca. 2 mm, splitting into 4 nutlets.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. L. Gibbs 7681; Y. S. Lau 1836; HK sheet 38725.
Distribution: S, SW, E & NW China; tropical and temperate regions.
Ecology: Grassy slopes or hillslopes. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Vitex negundo L. 黃荊
Sp. Pl. 2: 638. 1753; FHK 273. 1861; FKH 204. 1912; FGZ 628. 1956; FTW 4: 432. 1978; FRPS 65(1): 141. 1982; FFJ 4: 540, fig. 425. 1989; FOC 17: 30. 1994; FGD 3: 374, fig. 242. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 426, pl. 180. 1998.

Shrub or small tree. Branchlets tetragonal, densely greyish white tomentose. Leaves usually (3–)5‑foliolate; leaflets papery, oblong‑lanceolate or lanceolate, base cuneate, apex acuminate, margin entire or rarely with several teeth along apical part, adaxially green, glabrous or puberulent, abaxially greyish white, tomentose; central leaflet 4–13 × 0.5–4 cm, distinctly petiolulate. Inflorescences terminal, 10–27 cm. Peduncle densely greyish white tomentose. Calyx campanulate, ca. 2 mm, abaxially greyish white tomentose, 5‑dentate. Corolla bluish purple or pale purple, ca. 7 mm, 2‑lipped, 5‑lobed, puberulent abaxially. Stamens exserted. Ovary subglabrous. Drupes subglobose, ca. 2 mm in diam., mostly enclosed by persistent calyx.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 8; Y. W. Lam 1027, 2181.
Distribution: S, SW, E & NW China; Japan, E Africa, SE Asia, Pacific islands.
Ecology: Thickets on hillslopes. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.; fruiting: Jul.–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Wong Nai Chung Gap, Quarry Bay, Fung Yuen, Lo Wu, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Vitex negundo L. var. cannabifolia (Siebold & Zucc.) Hand.‑Mazz. 牡荊
Acta Horti Gothob. 9(4): 67. 1934; FRPS 65(1): 143. 1982; FFJ 4: 541. 1989; FOC 17: 31. 1994; FGD 3: 375. 1995.
Vitex cannabifolia Siebold & Zucc., Abh. Math.‑Phys. Cl. Königl. Bayer. Akad. Wiss. 4(3): 152. 1846.
Vitex negundo f. intermedia C. P’ei, Mem. Sci. Soc. China 1(3): 105. 1932; FYN 1: 452. 1977.

It differs from var. negundo by leaflets often regularly coarse serrate, abaxially greenish, minutely pilose.

Locality: Wong Nai Chung Gap, Quarry Bay, Fung Yuen, Lo Wu, Lantau Island. W. J. Tutcher 8113; Y. S. Lau 342, 1918.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hebei, Henan, Hunan, Sichuan; India, Nepal, SE Asia.
Ecology: Thickets on hillslopes. Flowering: Jun.–Jul.; fruiting: Aug.–Nov.

Vitex quinata (Lour.) F. N. Williams 山牡荊
Bull. Herb. Boissier, ser. 2, 5(5): 431. 1905; FHN 4: 19. 1977; FTW 4: 434. 1978; FRPS 65(1): 135. 1982; FFJ 4: 539, fig. 424. 1989; FOC 17: 29. 1994; FGD 3: 373. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 426, photo 255. 1998.
Cornutia quinata Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 2: 387. 1790.
Vitex loureiri Hook. & Arn., Bot. Beechey Voy. 206. 1837; FHK 273. 1861.
Vitex heterophylla Roxb., [Hort. Beng. 46. 1814, nom. nud.] Fl. Ind. ed. 1832, 3: 75. 1832; FKH 204. 1912.

Tree, 4–12 m tall; bark brown. Branchlets tetragonal, pubescent and glandular. Leaves 3(–5)‑foliolate; petiole 2.5– 6 cm; petiolules 0.5–2 cm; leaflets thickly papery, obovate‑lanceolate to elliptic‑lanceolate, base cuneate, apex acuminate, acute, or cuspidate, margin entire, puberulent along midvein on both surfaces, abaxially yellow glandular; central leaflet 5–9 × 2–4 cm; lateral ones smaller. Panicles terminal, 9–18 cm, densely yellowish brown pubescent. Calyx campanulate, 2–3 mm, densely yellowish brown pubescent and glandular abaxially, 5‑denticulate. Corolla pale yellow, 7–8 mm, 2‑lipped, 5‑lobed, abaxially pubescent and glandular. Stamens exserted. Ovary glandular. Fruiting calyx truncate. Fruit obovoid to globose, black, 4–8 mm in diam., subtended by plateform truncate persistent calyx.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 394, 889, 2375.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Japan, Malaysia, Philippines.
Ecology: Open places, forests on hillslopes. Flowering: Jul.; fruiting: Sep.–Nov.

Vitex rotundifolia L. f. 單葉蔓荊（白背蔓荊）
Suppl. Pl. 294. 1781; FTW 4: 434. 1978; FOC 17: 30. 1994; FTW ed. 2, 4: 428. 1998.
Vitex ovata Thunb., Fl. Jap. 257. 1784.
Vitex trifolia L. var. simplicifolia Cham., Linnaea : 107. 1832; FRPS 65(1): 140, fig. 70. 1982; FFJ 4: 539. 1989; FGD 3: 374. 1995.
Vitex trifolia L. var. unifoliolata Schauer, Prodr. 11: 683. 1847.

Shrub. Stems prostrate to creeping, rooting at nodes; branchlets silky tomentose when young. Leaves mostly 1(–3)‑foliolate, sessile or short petiolate; blade obovate, 2.5–5 × 1.5–3 cm, base attenuate to rounded, apex abruptly subacuminate to rounded, margin entire, adaxially usually pale green and pubescent, abaxially densely tomentose. Thyrses terminal, 3–10 × 1–2.5 cm. Calyx cupular, 4–5 mm, slightly 2‑lipped, 5‑denticulate, glabrous adaxially, slightly silky tomentose and glandular abaxially. Corolla bluish purple, salverform, slightly silky tomentose and glandular abaxially, villous in tube and adaxially. Stamens and style exserted. Ovary globose, glabrous, densely glandular. Fruit dark brown when dry, globose.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 2325; S. P. Lau 152; HK sheet 40601.
Distribution: Guangdong, Taiwan, Fujian, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Jiangsu, Shandong, Hebei; Japan, SE Asia, Pacific islands.
Ecology: Sandy beaches. Flowering: Jul.–Sep.; fruiting: Sep.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Fanling, Castle Peak, Lin Tong Mei, Yuen Long, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Vitex trifolia L. 蔓荊
Sp. Pl. 2: 638(as 938). 1753; FHK 273. 1861; FKH 204. 1912; FHN 4: 18. 1977; FYN 1: 442, pl. 105: 1 – 3. 1977; FRPS 65(1): 138. 1982; FFJ 4: 539. 1989; FOC 17: 29. 1994; FGD 3: 374. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 428. 1998.

Shrub, rarely small tree, 1.5–5 m tall. Branchlets tetragonal, densely pubescent. Leaves (1–)3(–5)‑foliolate; petiole 1–3 cm; leaflets sessile, ovate, obovate or ovate‑oblong, base cuneate, apex obtuse, margin entire, ± hairy adaxially, densely grey tomentose abaxially; lateral veins 5–8 pairs, slightly prominent on both surfaces; central leaflet 5–9 × 1.7–3 cm, lateral ones smaller and subsessile. Thyrses terminal, 3–10(–15) cm. Peduncle densely grey tomentose. Calyx campanulate, ca. 2 mm, slightly 5‑dentate, glabrous adaxially, grey pubescent abaxially. Corolla purplish blue, 8–10 mm, villous adaxially, white mealy pubescent abaxially, 2‑lipped, upper lip 2‑lobed, lower lip 3‑lobed with central one larger. Stamens exserted. Ovary glabrous, glandular. Style glabrous. Fruit subglobose, 4–5 mm in diam., black.

Locality: Fanling, Castle Peak, Lin Tong Mei, Yuen Long, Lantau Island. P. S. Choi 342; Y. W. Lam 1531; HK sheet 34489.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; SE Asia, Australia, Pacific islands.
Ecology: Open fields, streamsides. Flowering: Jul.–Aug.; fruiting: Aug.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Wong Chuk Hang, Tai Mo Shan, Shing Mun, Ping Shan, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Ajuga nipponensis Makino 紫背金盤
Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 23(267): 67 – 68. 1909; FRPS 65(2): 76. 1977; FOC 17: 68. 1994; FGD 3: 392. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 438, pl. 186. 1998.
Ajuga genevensis L., Sp. Pl. 2: 561. 1753; FKH 212. 1912.
Ajuga decumbens auct. non Thunb.: FKH 212. 1912.

Annual or biennial herbs, 10–20 cm or taller; stems usually erect, branched from base, villous or pilose. Leaves opposite, petiolate; leaf blade broadly elliptic or ovate‑elliptic, 2–4.5 × 1.5–2.5 cm, base cuneate, decurrent, apex obtuse, margin irregularly undulate‑crenate, ciliate, sparsely hirsute or pubescent on both surfaces. Verticillasters many‑flowered, forming terminal spike‑like inflorescence; lower bracts similar to stem leaf, gradually reduced upward, ovate to broadly lanceolate, 0.8–1.5 cm, green or sometimes tinged with purple, ciliate; pedicels short or almost absent. Calyx campanulate, 3–5 mm, villous on upper half, the teeth triangular, subequal, about half the length of the calyx. Corolla bluish or blue‑purple, rarely white or greenish, with dark lines, 7–11 mm, base slightly swollen, sparsely pubescent adaxially, villous annulate at throat abaxially; lower lip 3‑lobed, middle lobe flabellate, truncate or emarginate at apex, lateral lobes narrowly oblong. Nutlets obovoid rugose‑reticulate dorsally.

Locality: Wong Chuk Hang, Tai Mo Shan, Shing Mun, Ping Shan, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 2683; P. S. Choi 531; Y. W. Lam 1307.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian; Japan, Korea.
Ecology: Wet places, old walls. Flowering: Dec.–Mar. of the following year; fruiting: Mar.–Apr.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Kau Wa Keng, Tai Po, Tin Fu Tsai, Castle Peak, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Anisomeles indica (L.) Kuntze 廣防風
Rev. Gen. Pl. 512. 1891; H. Keng, Garden's Bull. Sing. 24: 34. 1969; FOC 17: 188. 1994; FTW ed. 2, 4: 445, pl. 189. 1998.
Anisomeles ovata R. Br., Hort. Kew. ed. 2, 3: 364. 1811; FHK 278. 1861; FKH 211. 1912.
Epimeredi indica (L.) Rothm., Repert. Spec. Nov. Regni Veg. Beih., 53: 12. 1944; FRPS 66: 42, pl. 6. 1977; FGD 3: 429. 1995.

Robust herbs, or sometimes shrubby, 0.5–2 m tall; stems erect, 4‑angled, sparingly hairy to densely pubescent. Leaves simple; petioles 1.5–4 cm, tomentose; leaf blade ovate to broadly ovate, 4–9 × 2.5–6.5 cm, base rounded to truncate, subcordate, less often shortly cuneate, entire, apex acute, margin irregularly serrate‑dentate, hirsute or woolly on both surfaces. Verticillasters forming interrupted or dense spikes; bracts linear, 3–4 mm, pilose. Calyx campanulate, 5–7 mm, lengthening to 10 mm in fruit, shortly pedicellate, hirsute and pilose; teeth triangular‑lanceolate, subequal, ciliate. Corolla purplish, ca. 1.3 mm, glabrous abaxially. Filaments hirsute. Nutlets broadly ovoid, 1.8–2 × 1.4–1.5 mm, ± compressed.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Kau Wa Keng, Tai Po, Tin Fu Tsai, Castle Peak, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 3126; S. P. Choi 160; S. Y. Hu & P. P. H. Butt 24037.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam, Thailand, Myanmar, Laos, Cambodia, Malaysia, Philippines.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides near villages, margins of forests. Flowering: Jun. – Nov.; fruiting: Sep.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Authority: (Thunb.) C. Y. Wu ex H. W. Li
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Clerodendranthus spicatus (Thunb.) C. Y. Wu ex H. W. Li 腎茶
Acta Phytotax. Sin. 12: 233. 1974; FRPS 66: 574, pl. 123. 1977; FOC 17: 299. 1994; FGD 3: 477, fig. 298. 1995.
Clerodendrum spicatum Thunb., Fl. Jav. 22. 1825.
Clerodendranthus stamineus (Benth.) Kudô, Mem. Fac. Sci. Taihoku Imp. Univ. 2: 117. 1929.
Orthosiphon stamineus Benth., Pl. Asiat. Rar. 2: 15. 1830.
Ocimum aristatum Blume, Bijdr. Fl. Ned. Ind. 14: 833 – 834. 1826.
Orthosiphon aristatus (Blume) Miq., Fl. Ned. Ind. 2: 943. 1858; FTW ed. 2, 4: 500. 1998.

Perennial herbs, 1–1.5 m tall. Stems erect, many‑branched, retrorse pubescent. Leaves opposite; petiole (3–)5–15 mm; leaf blade ovate, rhombic‑ovate to ovate‑oblong, (1.2–)2–5.5 × (0.8–)1.3–3.5 cm, base broadly cuneate to truncate‑cuneate, apex acute, margin coarsely mucronate, dentate to remotely mucronate‑crenate, pubescent and sparsely impressed glandular on both surfaces. Verticillasters 6‑flowered, forming loose terminal racemes of 8–12 cm; rachis densely pubescent; bracts orbicular‑ovate, ca. 3.5 mm, entire, apex cuspidate, longitudinally parallel veined. Pedicel to 5 mm, densely pubescent. Calyx 5–6 mm, puberulous and rusty glandular outside; upper lip orbicular, ca. 2.5 mm in diam.; teeth of lower lip triangular, awned, margin ciliolate, interior 2 teeth ca. 2 times as long as lateral teeth; fruiting calyx to 1.1 cm, reticulate veins distinct; upper lip conspicuously reflexed. Corolla purplish or white, puberulous and sparsely rusty glandular on upper lip; tube 0.9–1.9 cm; upper lip reflexed, ca. 6 mm in diam., 3‑lobed, middle lobe larger, apex emarginate; lower lip oblong, ca. 5 mm; filaments 2–4 cm exserted from corolla‑tube. Nutlets dark brown, ovoid, ca. 2 × 1.6 mm, wrinkled.

Locality: Cultivated. L. T. Lo 190; HK sheet 32793.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan (cultivated); SE Asia and N Australia.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: May–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Clinopodium gracile (Benth.) Matsum. 細風輪菜
Index Pl. Jap. 2: 538. 1912; FRPS 66: 235, pl. 54: 1 – 6. 1977; FOC 17: 230. 1994; FGD 3: 440. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 452, pl. 193. 1998.
Calamintha gracilis Benth., Prodr. 12: 232. 1848; FKH 210. 1912.

Perennial herbs. Stems ascending from the prostrate base, puberulous, rooting on the lower nodes. Leaves papery; petioles 0.5–1 cm, puberulous; leaf blade broadly ovate or subrounded 1–2 × 0.8–1.5 cm, base rounded or broadly cuneate, apex acute, margin crenate‑serrate, glabrous on both surfaces except on the veins. Verticillasters many‑flowered in axils of upper leaves, sometimes aggregated in racemose or subcapitate terminal inflorescence; bracts subulate, puberulous. Calyx tubular‑campanulate, 2–3 mm, lengthening to 4–4.5 in fruit, sparsely hirsute; tube slightly inflated below; upper teeth recurved, highly connate, slightly shorter than the lower ones; lower teeth subulate, ciliate, slightly incurved. Corolla straight, 3–4 mm, barely exserted. Anther‑cells parallel, connivent. Nutlets rounded, compressed, 0.5–0.6 mm across, pale brown, finely reticulate.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan. Y. S. Lau 2209; P. S. Choi 128; Y. W. Lam 1559.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Vietnam, Laos, Myanmar, Thailand, India, Indonesia.
Ecology: Open fields, wastelands, roadsides near villages. Flowering: Apr.–Aug.; fruiting: Jun.–Oct.

Coleus scutellarioides (L.) Benth. 五彩蘇（洋紫蘇）
Edward's Bot. Reg. 15: t. 1300. 1830; FRPS 66: 542. 1977; FOC 17: 293. 1994; FGD 3: 468. 1995.
Coleus blumei Benth., Labiat. Gen. Sp. 56. 1832.
Solenostemon scutellarioides (L.) Codd, Bothalia 11(4): 439 – 440. 1975.
Ocimum scutellarioides L., Sp. Pl. ed. 2, 2: 834. 1763.

Annual herbs, erect or ascending, 0.5–1 m tall. Stems and branches finely pubescent or glabrous. Leaves opposite; petioles 1–5(–8) cm; leaf blade variable in size, shape and colour, generally ovate in outline, 3–7(–15) × (1–)3–5(–10) cm, base rounded or cuneate, apex acute or acuminate, margin crenate, serrate or sometimes laciniate, variously coloured with yellow, dull red and purplish or green, puberulent on midvein and secondary veins; verticillasters many‑flowered, forming panicles of 5–10(–25) cm, puberulent. Calyx campanulate, 2–3 mm, lengthening to 7 mm in fruit, 10‑veined, minutely hispid, glandular; middle lobe of upper lip broadly ovate, as long as or longer than lobes of lower lip, reflexed in fruit; lateral lobes ovate, about half the length of middle lobe; lower lip rhombic, longer than upper lip, lobes narrowly triangular. Corolla purple to blue, 0.8 – 1.3 cm, puberulent, tube abruptly recurved, throat to 2.5 mm wide, upper lip erect. Nutlets brown, broadly ovoid to globose, 1–1.2 mm, shiny.

Locality: Cultivated. L. T. Lo 90; HK sheet 4437.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; cultivated elsewhere.
Ecology: Flowering: Dec.–Jul. of the following years; fruiting: May–Oct.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: This species was also reported as Coleus pumilus Blanco or Coleus scutellarioides var. crispipilus (Merr.) H. Keng previously (Check List HK Plants 76. 1993; 81. 2004). Other Coleus species were also cultivated for ornamental purpose, including such occasional examples as Coleus aromaticus Benth. (芳香鞘蕊花), Coleus carnosifolius (Hemsl.) Dunn (肉葉鞘蕊花) and others.

Dysophylla stellata (Lour.) Benth. 水虎尾
Pl. Asiat. Rar. 1: 30. 1830; FRPS 66: 382. 1977; FOC 17: 262. 1994; FGD 3: 456, fig. 285. 1995.
Dysophylla verticillata Benth., Pl. Asiat. Rar. 1: 30. 1830; FKH 208. 1912.
Dysophylla stellatus (Lour.) Kuntze, Gen. Pl. 2: 429. 1891; FTW ed. 2, 4: 511, pl. 228. 1998.
Mentha stellata Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 2: 361. 1790.

Annual herbs, 15–50 cm tall. Stems erect, verticillately branched above middle, glabrous or very sparsely hirsute, nodes sometimes grey villous. Leaves in whorls of 4–10, sessile or very shortly petiolate; leaf blade linear to lanceolate, 2–7 cm × 0.2–0.5 cm, base attenuate, apex acute, margin remotely serrulate or entire, revolute or flat, glabrous, abaxially grey. Spikes cylindric, 0.5–7(–9) cm × 4–6.5(–8) mm, continuous, densely flowered; bracts lanceolate, conspicuously longer than calyx. Calyx campanulate, 1–1.2 mm, lengthening to 1.8 mm in fruit, densely grey tomentose abaxially. Corolla purple‑red, 1.8–2 mm, lobes subequal. Nutlets brown, obovoid.

Locality: Sha Tau Kok. S. B. C. Ross 11449.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian; Bangladesh, Bhutan, Cambodia, India, Indonesia, Japan, Laos, Malaysia, Thailand, Vietnam, Australia.
Ecology: Paddy fields, wet areas along streams. Flowering & fruiting: Nearly all year round.

Elsholtzia argyi H. Lév. 紫花香薷
Repert. Spec. Nov. Regni Veg. 8: 425. 1910; FRPS 66: 343. 1977; FOC 17: 254. 1994; FGD 3: 449. 1995.

Herbs 50–100 cm tall. Stems often purplish, grooved, with white hairs in grooves. Leaves opposite; petiole 0.8– 2.5 cm, narrowly winged, white pubescent; leaf blade ovate to broadly ovate, 2–6 × 1–3 cm, base rounded to broadly cuneate, decurrent, apex shortly acuminate, margin crenate or crenate‑serrate, adaxially sparsely pilose, abaxially impressed glandular, white pubescent on veins. Verticillasters 8‑flowered, forming secund spikes of 2–7 cm; bracts rounded, ca. 5 mm, apex abruptly spinescent, spines to 2 mm, abaxially white villous, yellow glandular, purplish, adaxially glabrous, margin ciliate. Pedicel ca. 1 mm, white pilose. Calyx tubular, ca. 2.5 mm, white villous abaxially; teeth subulate, subequal, apex spinescent, margin ciliate. Corolla rose‑purple, ca. 6 mm, white villous abaxially, glandular at apex; upper lip notched, margin villous; lower lip slightly spreading, middle lobe oblong, apex usually mucronate; lateral lobes arcuate. Anthers dark purple. Nutlets dark brown, oblong, ca. 1 mm, minutely tuberculate.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Tai Mo Shan. S. B. C. Ross 11450; Y. S. Lau 2077, 3025.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian; Japan, Vietnam.
Ecology: Thickets, forests, streamsides. Flowering & fruiting: Sep.–Nov.
Notes: The species was reported as Elsholtzia ciliata (Thunb.) Hyl. previously (Check List HK Plants 76. 1993).

Glechoma longituba (Nakai) Kuprian. 活血丹
Bot. Zhurn. (Moscow & Leningrad) 33(2): 236, fig. 1(4), 2. 1948; FRPS 65(2): 316, pl. 61: 1 – 3. 1977; FOC 17: 118. 1994; FGD 3: 410. 1995.
Glechoma hederacea L. var. longituba Nakai, Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 35(418): 173 – 174. 1921.
Glechoma brevituba Kupr., Bot. Zhurn. (Moscow & Leningrad) 33(2): 236. 1948

Perennial herbs, 10–30 cm tall; stems ascending, often purplish red at base, young parts sparsely villous. Leaves opposite; petioles 1–2 times as long as blade; leaf blade upper leaves cordate, 1.8–2.6 × 2–3 cm, apex acute to obtuse, margin coarsely crenate or serrate‑crenate, adaxially sparsely strigose or puberulent, abaxially purplish, veins pilose or hirsute. Verticillasters usually 2‑flowered, rarely 4–6‑flowered; bracts and bracteoles linear, to 4 mm, ciliate. Calyx tubular, 0.9–1.1 cm, villous especially on veins; teeth ovate‑triangular, 3–5 mm, apex awned, ciliate, adaxial ones longer. Corolla blue to purple with dark spots on lower lip, long‑tubed corolla 1.7–2.2 cm, short‑tubed corolla 1–1.4 cm, ± pilose or puberulent abaxially; upper lip straight, 2‑lobed, lobes subreniform; lower lip elongate, obliquely spreading, middle lobe reniform, 2–3 times as long as upper lip, apex emarginate; lateral lobes oblong, ca. 1/2 as long as middle lobe. Nutlets ca. 1.5 × 1 mm, basally ± triquetrous, apex rounded.

Locality: Lai Chi Chong, Kop Tong. W. J. Tutcher 11721; HK sheet 34038.
Distribution: Spread over all provinces except Gansu, Qinghai, Xinjiang, Xizang; far E of Russia, Korea.
Ecology: Thin forests, streamsides, roadsides near villages. Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: May–Jul.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tate's Cairn, Pyramid Hill, Fo Tan
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Gomphostemma chinense Oliv. 中華錐花
Hooker's Icon. Pl. 15: 54. 1884; FKH 212. 1912; FRPS 65(2): 116, pl. 23: 1 – 6. 1977; FOC 17: 74. 1994; FGD 3: 398. 1995.

Perennial herbs, 20–80 cm tall, rhizomatous. Stems erect, obtusely 4‑angled, densely stellate tomentose. Leaves subleathery; petiole 2–6 cm, densely stellate tomentose; leaf blade elliptic to ovate‑elliptic, 4–13 × 2–7 cm, base obtuse to rounded, apex obtuse, margin irregularly coarse serrate to subentire, adaxially stellate pubescent and sparsely strigose, abaxially dense grey stellate tomentose. Flowers solitary or in 4–many‑flowered whorls at the axils of the lower leaves; peduncle to ca. 2.2 cm; bracts elliptic to lanceolate, 11–16 × 5–7 mm, margin coarsely serrate or entire on apical half; bracteoles linear, shorter than bracts. Calyx narrowly campanulate in flower, 12–13 mm, densely grey stellate tomentose outside; teeth lanceolate to narrowly lanceolate, 6 – 7 mm, apex acuminate. Corolla yellowish to white, ca. 5.2 cm, sparsely puberulent outside; upper lip erect, ca. 6 × 8 mm, apex rounded and emarginate; lower lip 1–1.4 × 1.3–1.9 cm, middle lobe obovate‑subcircular, 7–8 × 6–7 mm; lateral lobes ovate, ca. 5 × 5 mm. Stamens almost as long as upper lip of corolla; filaments complanate, margin puberulent. Style shorter than stamens, slightly thicker on apical 2/3, apically unequally 2‑cleft. Nutlets 4 per flower at maturity, obovoid, triquetrous, ca. 4 × 2.8 mm, brown, bullate, hairy.

Locality: Tate's Cairn, Pyramid Hill, Fo Tan. HK sheet 32249, 38428, 39407.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Jiangxi, Fujian; Vietnam.
Ecology: Ravines, margins of forests. Flowering: Jul.–Aug.; fruiting: Oct.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Hyptis rhomboidea M. Martens & Galeotti 吊球草
Bull. Acad. Roy. Sci. Bruxelles. 11(2): 188. 1844; FRPS 66: 408, pl. 85: 7. 1977; FOC 17: 267. 1994; FGD 3: 459. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 466, pl. 201. 1998.
Hyptis decurrens (Blanco) Epling, Repert. Spec. Nov. Regni Veg. 34(891 – 894): 120–122. 1933.
Pycnanthemum decurrens Blanco, Fl. Filip. ed. 2, 33. 1846.

Annual stout herbs, 0.5–1.5 m tall, non aromatic. Stems and branches pubescent on the angles. Leaves opposite; petioles 1–3.5 cm; leaf blade lanceolate or rhomboid‑elliptic, 6–18 × 1.5–4(–6) cm, base cuneate and decurrent, apex acute or acuminate, margin crenate‑serrate or serrate, adaxially sparsely minute hispid, abaxially densely glandular, pilose on veins. Flowers numerous, forming axillary, solitary globular heads, 1–1.5 cm in diam.; peduncle 1–10 cm; basal involucral bracts linear‑lanceolate, hairy, 3–6 mm. Calyx 3–4 mm, lengthening to 6 – 8 mm in fruit, ca. 4 × 2 mm, minutely hispid, base villous; teeth subulate, as long as or shorter than the tube. Corolla cream‑white, 5 – 6 mm, puberulent; upper lip 1–1.2 mm, lobes ovate, reflexed; lower lip longer than the upper lip. Nutlets ovoid, compressed, ca. 1.2–2 mm.

Locality: Naturalized in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 238, 2070; HK sheet 34819.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Taiwan (naturalized); native to tropical America.
Ecology: Hillslopes, open fields near villages. Flowering: Oct.–Nov.

Hyptis suaveolens (L.) Poit. 山香
Ann. Nat. Hist. 7: 472. 1806; FKH 208. 1912; FRPS 66: 406, pl. 85: 1 – 6. 1977; FOC 17: 267. 1994; FGD 3: 460. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 466, pl. 203. 1998.
Ballota suaveolens L., Syst. Nat. ed. 10, 2: 1100. 1759.

Annual robust herbs, 0.5–1.5 m tall, aromatic. Stems erect, hirsute. Leaves opposite; petioles slender, 0.53(–6) cm; leaf blade ovate to broadly ovate, 1.4–11 × 1.2–9 cm, base rounded to truncate, often slightly oblique, apex subacute to obtuse, margin irregularly serrulate, adaxially olive green, sparsely pilose, abaxially densely pubescent. Flowers in lax, (1–)2–5‑flowered, secund cymes, arranged racemosely towards apex of branches in the axils of smaller leaves; peduncles 5–10 mm, pubescent; bracts minute, setaceous. Calyx campanulate 5–5.5 mm, lengthening to 8 – 10 mm in fruit, strongly ribbed, mouth villous; teeth erect, setaceous, ciliate. Corolla blue, 6–8 mm, puberulent except near base; tube ca. 2 mm wide at throat; upper lip lobes reflexed; middle lobe of lower lip notched. Nutlets narrowly oblong, granulate.

Locality: Naturalized in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 1888; Y. S. Lau 2401; L. T. Lo 414.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan (naturalized); native to tropical America.
Ecology: Wastelands near villages. Flowering & fruiting: Almost all year round.

Isodon amethystoides (Benth.) H. Hara 香茶菜
J. Jap. Bot. 60: 233. 1985; FOC 17: 274. 1994; FTW ed. 2, 4: 470, pl. 204. 1998.
Rabdosia amethystoides (Benth.) H. Hara, FRPS 66: 429. 1977; FGD 3: 463. 1995.
Plectranthus amethystoides Benth., Labiat. Gen. Spec. 45. 1832; FKH 208. 1912.

Perennial herbs, with thick, woody rhizomes. Stems erect, 30–150 cm tall, quadrangular, 4‑sulcate, densely appressed incurved‑pilose or puberulent. Leaves opposite; petioles 0.2 – 2.5 cm; leaf blade ovate‑orbicular to lanceolate, 0.8–11 × 0.7–3.5 cm, base abruptly attenuate or broadly cuneate‑attenuate, apex acuminate, acute or obtuse, margin crenate, adaxially olive green, ± densely hispidulous, sometimes subglabrous, abaxially greenish, pilose or tomentulose, sometimes subglabrous. Cymes many‑flowered, arranged in loose, terminal panicles; floral leaves ovate, similar to stem leaves but smaller, gradually reduce to bracts upward. Calyx campanulate, ca. 2.5 mm, sparsely hirtellous or subglabrous abaxially, with scattered white or yellow glands; teeth 5, subequal, triangular; fruiting calyx erect, broadly campanulate, 4–5 mm, slightly shorter than wide. Corolla white bluish, white, or purplish, purple bluish on upper lip, ca. 7 mm, sparsely puberulent abaxially. Stamens included. Style included. Nutlets ovoid, ca. 2 mm, brown to yellow or white glandular.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Fanling. W. J. Tutcher 8394.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hubei, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Forests, wet grasslands. Flowering: Jun.–Oct.; fruiting: Sep.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Isodon coetsa (Buch.‑Ham. ex D. Don) Kudô 細錐香茶菜
Mem. Fac. Sci. Taikoku Imp. Univ. 2: 131. 1929; FOC 17: 286. 1994.
Rabdosia coetsa (Buch.‑Ham ex D. Don) H. Hara, J. Jap. Bot. 47(7): 194. 1972; FRPS 66: 494. 1977; FGD 3: 464. 1995.
Plectranthus coetsa Buch.‑Ham. ex D. Don, Prodr. Fl. Nepal. 117. 1825.

Perennial herbs or subshrubs, 0.5–2 m tall, with woody rhizomes and numerous fibrous roots. Stems erect, obtusely 4‑angled, puberulous or subglabrous. Stem leaves opposite; petiole 1–5.5 cm; leaf blade ovate, 3–9 × 1.5–6 cm, base broadly cuneate, apex acuminate, margin crenate, glandular, adaxial surface sparsely strigose, minutely hispid on veins, abaxial surface densely minutely hispid on veins. Cymes 3–5‑flowered, forming narrow, terminal or axillary panicles, pubescent; peduncle of cymes 2–3 mm; pedicels 1–3 mm, puberulous; lower floral leaves sessile, ovate, upper floral leaves bract‑like, ovate‑lanceolate, shorter than pedicels. Calyx campanulate, ca. 1.5 × 1.5 mm, pubescent abaxially, glandular, slightly 2‑lipped; teeth ovate‑triangular, ca. 1/3 as long as calyx, apex acute; fruiting calyx tubular‑campanulate, dilated to ca. 4 mm, slightly curved, netted at apex. Corolla purple to purple‑blue, ca. 6 mm, pubescent, tube ca. 2.5 mm, upper lip ca. 2.5 mm; lower lip broadly ovate, ca. 3.5 mm. Stamens included. Style included or slightly exserted. Nutlets brown, obovoid, ca. 1 mm wide, glabrous.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. Y. S. Lau 3241.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Hunan; Vietnam, Laos, Thailand, Myanmar, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, India, Nepal.
Ecology: Margins of forests, thickets. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Feb. of the following year.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): A Ma Wat, Sheung Miu Tin, Lantau Island

Isodon lophanthoides (Buch‑Ham. ex D. Don) H. Hara 線紋香茶菜
J. Jap. Bot. 60: 235. 1985; FOC 17: 278. 1994.
Rabdosia lophanthoides (Buch.‑Ham. ex D. Don) H. Hara, J. Jap. Bot. 47(7): 194, 197. 1972; FRPS 66: 479. 1977; FGD 3: 466. 1995.
