Plectranthus striatus Benth., Pl. Asiat. Rar. 2: 17. 1830; FKH 208. 1912.
Isodon striatus (Benth.) Kudô, Mem. Fac. Sci. Taihoku Imp. Univ. 2: 134. 1929.
Hyssopus lophanthoides Buch.‑Ham. ex D. Don, Prodr. Fl. Nepal. 110. 1825.

Perennial herbs, 0.5–1.5 m tall, with underground globose root tubers. Stems erect or ascending from repent base, puberulent or pilose. Stem leaves opposite; petiole equal to or longer than blade; leaf blade broadly lanceolate to ovate, 1.5–20 × 0.5–8.5 cm, base cuneate to rounded, rarely shallow cordate, apex obtuse to acuminate, margin crenate, minutely hirsute, adaxially olive green, abaxially greenish, sparsely brown glandular. Cymes helicoid, 11– 13‑flowered, forming terminal and axillary panicles of 7–20 cm; floral leaves bract‑like, ovate; bracteoles linear, 3– 5 mm, slightly longer than pedicels. Calyx campanulate, ca. 2 mm, lengthening to 4.5–5 mm in fruit, base sparsely villous abaxially, sparsely red‑brown glandular, 2‑lipped; teeth ovate‑triangular, lower 2 longer. Corolla white or rose, with purple spots on limb, 2–7 mm; tube 3.7–5 mm, straight; upper lip 1.6–2 mm, lower lip slightly longer. Stamens and style much exserted. Nutlets brown, compressed ovoid, ca. 1 × 0.75 mm, glabrous, smooth.

Locality: A Ma Wat, Sheung Miu Tin, Lantau Island. HK sheet 22119.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Gansu, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian; Vietnam, Laos, Thailand, Myanmar, India, Nepal.
Ecology: Forests, thickets in ravines. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Mo Shan, Pat Sin Leng
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Isodon ternifolius (D. Don) Kudô 牛尾草
Mem. Fac. Sci. Taihoku Imp. Univ. 2: 137. 1929; FOC 17: 273. 1994.
Rabdosia ternifolia (D. Don) H. Hara, J. Jap. Bot. 47(7): 201. 1972; FRPS 66: 436, pl. 92: 1. 1977; FGD 3: 464. 1995.
Plectranthus ternifolius D. Don, Prodr. Fl. Nepal. 117. 1825; FKH 208. 1912.

Perennial robust herbs or subshrubs, 0.5–2 m tall. Stems erect; branches hexagonal, densely tomentose‑villous. Leaves opposite or in whorls of 3 or 4; petiole 2–3(–10) mm; leaf blade narrowly lanceolate to oblong, rarely ovate‑oblong, 2–12 × 0.7–5 cm, base broadly cuneate to cuneate, rarely rounded, apex acute to acuminate, rarely obtuse, margin serrate, adaxially ± wrinkled, pilose to villous, abaxially densely whitish or dull yellow tomentose. Cymes many‑flowered, ca. 6 mm in diam., forming terminal and axillary, compact spikes; floral leaves similar to stem leaves, gradually reduced, bract‑like apically. Calyx campanulate, ca. 2.3 mm, lengthening to 4 mm in fruit, densely grey or tawny villous; teeth triangular, equal, ca. 0.5 mm, obscurely veined. Corolla white to purplish; upper lip purple‑spotted, 5–6 mm. Stamens and style usually included. Nutlets triquetrous, ovoid, ca. 1.8 × 1 mm, glabrous.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Pat Sin Leng. HK sheet 22127, 22128, 22130.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan; Vietnam, Myanmar, Bangladesh, India, Nepal.
Ecology: Open grassy uplands, thickets and thin forests. Flowering: Sep.–Feb. of the following year; fruiting: Dec.–May of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Po Kau, Tai Po, Plover Cove, Sai Kung, Yuen Long, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Leonurus japonicus Houtt. 益母草
Nat. Hist. 9: 366. 1778; FOC. 17: 163. 1994; FTW ed. 2, 4: 480, pl. 210. 1998.
Leonurus artemisia (Lour.) S. Y. Hu, J. Coll. Sci. Imp. Univ. Tokyo 2(2): 381. 1974; FRPS 65(2): 508, pl. 99: 1 – 7. 1977; FGD 3: 420. 1995.
Stachys artemisia Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 2: 365 – 366. 1790.
Leonurus sibiricus auct. non L.: FHK 276. 1861; FKH 211. 1912.

Annual or biennial herbs, 30–120 cm tall. Stems obtusely angled, furrowed, retrorse strigose. Leaves very variable in shape, the lower and basal leaves ovate in outline, base broadly cuneate, 3‑palmatipartite; lobes oblong‑rhombic to ovate, 2.5–6 × 1.5–4 cm, pinnately divided, adaxially strigose, abaxially pilose, glandular; upper leaves deeply divided into 3 or more oblong‑linear to linear segments, or the uppermost sometimes linear and entire. Verticillasters 8–15‑flowered, 2–2.5 cm in diam., the lower ones axillary and distant, the upper ones forming a terminal spike; bracts subulate or spinescent, 4–10 mm. Calyx tubular‑campanulate, 5–6 mm, lengthening to 7–8 mm in fruit, appressed puberulent; teeth 5, subulate. Corolla red or white, 10–12 mm; tube often obliquely hairy annulate inside; upper lip erect, obovate, entire, pubescent abaxially; lower lip 3‑lobed, the middle lobe obcordate, pubescent. Filaments sparsely scaly. Nutlets ellipsoidal, apex truncate, smooth.

Locality: Tai Po Kau, Tai Po, Plover Cove, Sai Kung, Yuen Long, Lantau Island. L. T. Lo 76; P. S. Choi 461; Y. W. Lam 1553.
Distribution: Widely distributed in all provinces of China; Korea, Japan, Vietnam, Laos, Cambodia, Myanmar, Thailand, Malaysia, Africa, America.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides near villages. Flowering: Jan.–May.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Leucas lavandulifolia Sm. 線葉白絨草
Cycl. 20, sect. 2, pt. 40. 1812; FRPS 65(2): 426, pl. 83: 7 – 8. 1977; FOC 17: 143. 1994; FGD 3: 416. 1995.
Leucas linifolia (Roth.) Spreng., Syst. Veg. 2: 743. 1825; FKH 212. 1912.
Phlomis linifolia Roth., Nov. Pl. Sp. 260. 1821.

Annual herbs, 20–80 cm tall, often many‑branched. Stems and branches grey pubescent. Leaves papery; petioles very short or almost obsolete; leaf blade linear‑lanceolate, rarely lanceolate, 3–7 × 0.5–1.2 cm, base cuneate‑attenuate, apex obtuse, margin entire or sparsely undulate‑serrate, greyish puberulent on both surfaces. Verticillasters many‑flowered, 1.5–2.5 cm in diam.; bracts linear, 3–4 mm, puberulous. Calyx obliquely turbinate, 5– 6 mm, lengthening to 7–9 mm in fruit, puberulent or glabrescent abaxially, veins inconspicuous, mouth oblique; teeth varying from 8 – 10, the uppermost one the largest. Corolla white, ca. 1.5 cm; tube villous annulate inside near the middle; upper lip oblong, woolly; lower lip patent, the middle lob large, obovate. Nutlets ovoid, brown.

Locality: Chai Wan. HK sheet 4479.
Distribution: Guangdong, Yunnan; India to Cochichina, Malesia.
Ecology: Thickets, margins of forests. Flowering: Oct.–Dec.; fruiting: Dec.–Jan. of the following year.

Leucas mollissima Wall. ex Benth. var. chinensis Benth. 疏毛白絨草
Prodr. 12: 525. 1848; FRPS 65(2): 421. 1977; FOC 17: 142. 1994; FGD 3: 415. 1995.
Leucas mollissimum auct. non Wall. ex Benth.: FHK 279. 1861; FKH 212. 1912.

Annual or perennial herbs, 40–60 cm, sometimes up to 1 m tall. Stems slender, twisted, and many‑branched, appressed tomentose‑villous. Leaves papery; petioles short, less than 1 cm, or subsessile in upper leaves; leaf blade ovate, 1.5–4 × 1–2.3 cm, usually the leaves on the lower part of branches larger, gradually reduced in size upwards, base broadly cuneate to cordate, apex acute, margin crenate or serrate, densely appressed tomentose on both surfaces, the lower often silvery glaucous. Verticillasters axillary, globose, 1.5–2 cm in diam.; bracts linear, 2–3 mm, densely villous. Calyx cylindric, 6–7 mm, densely pubescent abaxially, 10‑veined, mouth truncate; teeth 10, 5 long and 5 short. Corolla white, yellowish to pink, ca. 1.3 cm, curved, puberulent near throat abaxially; upper lip 3– 4 mm; lower lip 7–9 mm, nearly flat. Nutlets ovoid, triquetrous.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 3072; Y. W. Lam 780, 1067.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan.
Ecology: Grassy hillslopes, roadsides. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: This species was recorded as Leucas flaccida R. Br. previously (Check List HK Plants 76. 1993).

Mentha canadensis L. 薄荷
Sp. Pl. 2: 577. 1753; FOC 17: 237. 1994; FTW ed. 2, 4: 487, pl. 214. 1998.
Mentha haplocalyx Briq., Bull. Soc. Bot. Geneve, ser. 2, 5: 39. 1889; FRPS 66: 262, pl. 60. 1977; FGD 3: 442. 1995.
Mentha arvensis auct. non L.: Benth., FHK 276. 1861; FKH 209. 1912.

Perennial aromatic herbs, 30–60 cm tall, with creeping rhizomes. Stems erect, ± hoary with adpressed retrorse hairs. Petioles 2–10 mm, puberulent; leaf blade oblong‑lanceolate, lanceolate to elliptic or ovate‑lanceolate, 3–5(– 7) × 0.8–3 cm, base cuneate to subrounded, apex acute, margin remotely coarse dentate‑serrate, sparingly puberulous on adaxial surface or only on the veins, often densely puberulous on veins of abaxial surface. Verticillasters axillary, globose, ca. 1.8 cm in diam. Calyx tubular‑campanulate, 2.5–3 mm, puberulous and glandular abaxially, glabrous adaxially, obscurely 10‑veined; teeth subequal, lanceolate or subulate. Corolla purplish or white, 4–5 mm, puberulent abaxially. Nutlets ellipsoidal, finely granular.

Locality: Cultivated. W. J. Tutcher 8119; Y. S. Lau 2621; HK sheet 39283.
Distribution: Widely distributed in all provinces of China; also in Korea, Japan, Vietnam, Laos, Cambodia, Thailand, Malaysia, Russia (Far East) and N America.
Ecology: Flowering: Aug.–Sep.; fruiting: Oct.
Uses: Material (essential oils), spice, medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Shek O, Tai Tam Tuk, Shing Mun, Tai Mo Shan
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Mesona chinensis Benth. 涼粉草
FHK 274. 1861; FKH 207. 1912; FRPS 66: 547, pl. 116. 1977; FOC 17: 294. 1994; FGD 3: 470, fig. 293. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 487, pl. 215. 1998.

Annual herbs. Stems erect or decumbent, 15–100 cm, slightly pubescent or hairy, glabrescent. Leaves opposite; petiole 2–15 mm; leaf blade oblong‑ovate to broadly ovate, 2–5 × 0.8–2.8 cm, base cuneate to sometimes rounded, apex acute to obtuse, margin serrate, finely hispid, pubescent, or only hairy along veins abaxially. Verticillasters forming interrupted or nearly continuous terminal racemes of 2–10(–13) cm; floral leaves or bracts ovate or lanceolate, scarcely longer than the flowers, mostly coloured at the base. Pedicel 3 – 4( – 5) mm, short hairy. Calyx 2–2.5 mm in flower, densely white pilose, middle lobe of upper lip acute to obtuse, lower lip sometimes emarginate; fruiting calyx 3–5 mm, subglabrous or hairy on veins, deeply reticulate and pitted between the veins. Corolla white or reddish, ca. 3 mm, puberulent, throat inflated; upper lip 4‑lobed, lateral 2 lobes distinct, longer than middle lobes, or upper lip subentire. Nutlets black, oblong.

Locality: Shek O, Tai Tam Tuk, Shing Mun, Tai Mo Shan. Y. S. Lau 679, 779, 3012.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Ravines, grassy fields. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Oct.
Uses: The decoction of dried plants mixed with starch and water is used to make a jelly‑like cooling drink in S China.
Notes: The type specimen was collected by C. Wilford from “Saywan” (Chai Wan) between 1857 and 1858.

Mosla dianthera (Buch.‑Ham.ex Roxb.) Maxim. 小魚仙草
Bull. Acad. Imp. Petersbourg. Ser. 3, 20: 457. 1875; FKH 209. 1912; FRPS 66: 297, pl. 64: 1 – 7. 1977; FOC 17: 245. 1994; FGD 3: 447, fig. 280. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 492, pl. 217. 1998.
Lycopus dianthera Buch.‑Ham. ex Roxb., Fl. Ind. 1: 144. 1820.

Annual aromatic herbs, up to 1 m tall. Stems erect, many‑branched, subglabrous, often woody at base. Leaves opposite; petioles 3–18 mm. pubescent; leaf blade rhomboid or ovate 1.2–3.5 × 0.5–1.8 cm, base acute or cuneate, apex acute, margin few‑toothed, glabrous or nearly so, sparsely dotted with sunk glands. Racemes terminal, 3–15(–30) cm, often branched; bracts lanceolate, 1–2 mm subtending the flowers. Calyx campanulate, 2– 2.5 mm, lengthening to 4–5 mm in fruit, throat hairy annulate inside; teeth deltoid, the lower 2 teeth larger than the upper ones. Corolla purplish, 3.5–5 mm, puberulent abaxially, glabrous or obscurely hairy annulate adaxially. Nutlets ellipsoidal 1–1.6 mm in diam.

Locality: Tai Po Kau. Y. S. Lau 3257.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Vietnam, Myanmar, Malaysia, India, Bhutan, Nepal, Pakistan.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides. Flowering: Aug.–Oct.; friuting: Oct.–May of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Authority: (Thunb.) C. Y. Wu & H. W. Li
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Cheung Sheung, Plover Cove, Tai Lam
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Mosla scabra (Thunb.) C. Y. Wu & H. W. Li 石薺薴
Acta Phytotax. Sin. 12: 230. 1974; FRPS 66: 294. 1977; FOC 17: 244. 1994; FGD 3: 446. 1995.
Perilla lanceolata Benth., Prodr. 12: 164. 1848; FHK 276. 1861.
Mosla lanceolata Maxim., Melanges Biol. Bull. Phys.‑Math. Acad. Imp. Sci. Saint‑Petersbourg 9: 434. 1879; FKH 209. 1912.
Ocimum scabrum Thunb., Trans. Linn. Soc. London 2: 338. 1794.

Annual aromatic herbs, 20–100 cm tall. Stems erect, many‑branched, densely pubescent. Leaves opposite; petioles 3–6 mm, pubescent; leaf ovate to ovate‑lanceolate, 1.5–3.5 × 0.9–1.7 cm, base rounded or broadly cuneate, apex acute or obtuse, margin serrate, adaxially grey puberulent, abaxially subglabrous or slightly puberulent, densely dotted with sunk glands. Racemes terminal, 2.5–15 cm; bracts ovate, 2.7–3.5 mm, apex caudate‑acuminate; pedicels ca. 1 mm, lengthening to 3 mm in fruit, densely grey pubescent. Calyx campanulate, ca. 2.5 mm, sparsely pubescent abaxially; limb 2‑lipped, upper lip 3‑toothed; teeth ovate‑lanceolate, apex acuminate, the middle one slightly smaller, the lower lip 2‑toothed, teeth linear, apex acute. Corolla pink, 4–5 mm, puberulent abaxially, hairy annulate near base adaxially. Nutlets globose, ca. 1 mm in diam.

Locality: Cheung Sheung, Plover Cove, Tai Lam. L. T. Lo 642; HK sheet 39291, 40259.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Sichuan, Gansu, Shaanxi, Liaoning, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Vietnam.
Ecology: Open fields near villages. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Ocimum basilicum L. 羅勒
Sp. Pl. 2: 597. 1753; FKH 206. 1912; FRPS 66: 561. 1977; FOC 17: 296. 1994; FGD 3: 473. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 495, pl. 219. 1998.

Annual herbs, 20–80 cm tall. Stems erect, many‑branched, often tinged red, glabrous or retrorse puberulent when young. Leaves opposite; petiole 1–2 cm; leaf blade ovate or elliptic ovate, 2.5–5 × 1–2.5 cm, base attenuate, apex subobtuse to acute, margin irregularly dentate or subentire, glabrescent or hairy, glandular abaxially. Verticillasters many‑flowered, forming simple or branched racemes of 10–15 cm or more, puberulent or densely pilose; bracts sessile, oblanceolate, 5–8 mm, ciliate, often coloured. Pedicel ca. 3 mm in flower, lengthening to 5 mm in fruit. Calyx campanulate, ca. 4 mm in flower, 5–6 mm in fruit, pubescent outside, pilose at throat inside; middle tooth of upper lip suborbicular, concave, apex mucronate; lower lip teeth lanceolate, ca. 2 mm, apex spinescent, ciliate. Corolla purplish or with upper lip white, limb puberulent outside; upper lip wide, ca. 3 × 4.5 mm, 4‑lobed, ± flat; lower lip purple, ca. 6 mm. Stamens free, slightly exserted, upper filaments with a tooth above the base. Nutlets dark brown, ovoid, ca. 2.5 × 1 mm, glandular foveolate.

Locality: Deep Water Bay, New Territories. Y. S. Lau 2018; HK sheet 25715, 40312.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Xinjiang, Jilin, Hebei, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; widely spread throughout the Old World tropics.
Ecology: Wastelands near villages. Flowering: Nearly all year round; fruiting: Sep.–Dec.
Uses: Additive (flavouring), material (essential oils).

Ocimum tenuiflorum L. 聖羅勒
Sp. Pl. 597. 1753.
Ocimum sanctum L., Mant. I. 85. 1767; FRPS 66: 566, pl. 121. 1977; FOC 17: 297. 1994; FGD 3: 474, fig. 296. 1995.

Perennial herbs or subshrubs, 0.5–1 m tall. Stems erect, many‑branched, covered with spreading soft hairs. Leaves opposite; petiole 1–2.5 cm; leaf blade elliptic‑oblong or elliptic, 2.5–6 × 1–3 cm, base cuneate to rounded, apex obtuse, margin shallowly undulate‑serrate, puberulent and glandular on both surfaces, especially on veins abaxially. Verticillasters 6‑flowered, forming terminal racemes or panicles of 6–10 cm; bracts sessile, cordate, ca. 1.5 × 1.5 mm, apex acute. Pedicel ca. 2.5 mm. Calyx campanulate, ca. 2.5 mm in flower, to 6 mm in fruit, villous; middle tooth of upper lip broadly oblate, abruptly acute; lateral teeth broadly triangular, shorter than lower lip teeth, spinescent; lower lip teeth lanceolate, apex spinescent. Corolla white to reddish, ca. 3 mm, slightly exserted, sparsely puberulent; upper lip less than 1 × 2.5 mm, lobes ovate; lower lip oblong, ca. 1 × 0.6 mm, flat. Stamens slightly exserted; upper filaments puberulent at base. Nutlets brown, ovoid, ca. 1 × 0.7 mm, glandular foveolate.

Locality: Luk Keng. Y. S. Lau 2875.
Distribution: Hainan, Sichuan, Taiwan; pantropical.
Ecology: Dry grassy fields. Flowering: Feb.–Jun.; fruiting: Mar.–Aug.
Uses: Additive (flavouring, leaves used as a condiment in salads and other foods).

(Vaniot) C. Y. Wu & H. W. Li
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Mount Parker, Ma On Shan, Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Paraphlomis javanica (Blume) Prain var. coronata (Vaniot) C. Y. Wu & H. W. Li 小葉假糙蘇
Acta Phytotax. Sin. 13(1): 72. 1975; FRPS 65(2): 552. 1977; FOC 17: 172. 1994; FGD 3: 422. 1995.
Lamium coronatum Vaniot, Bull. Acad. Int. Geogr. Bot. 14: 174. 1904.
Phlomis rugosa Benth., Numer. List n. 2067. 1829; FKH 212. 1912.

Herbs or subshrubs, 0.5–1.5 m tall. Stems usually solitary, retrorse strigose. Leaves succulent; petioles slender, 2– 8 mm; leaf blade elliptic to oblong‑elliptic, 3–9( –15) × 1.5–6 cm, base rounded to subtruncate, apex acuminate to acute, margin shallowly and remotely serrate to crenate, with minute scattered hairs on both surfaces. Verticillasters many‑flowered, globose, ca. 3 cm in diam., subtended by few bracteoles at base. Calyx turbinate, 8–12 mm, abruptly spreading at mouth, hairy on veins abaxially; tube slightly curved; teeth 5, lanceolate, the base triangular, often broken off in fruit. Corolla yellow or yellowish, 2–2.5 cm, pubescent annulate inside; both lips pubescent abaxially, upper lip narrow, rounded at apex; lower lip 3‑lobed; the middle lob oblong, the lateral lobes lanceolate. Stylar branches subequal. Nutlets obovoid, acute and triquetrous at base.

Locality: Mount Parker, Ma On Shan, Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai. Y. S. Lau 1338; L. T. Lo 359; Y. W. Lam 379.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Taiwan.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Aug.–Nov.; fruiting: Sep.–Feb. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Perilla frutescens (L.) Britton 紫蘇
Mem. Torrey Bot. Club 5(18): 277. 1894; FRPS 66: 282, pl. 62. 1977; FOC 17: 241. 1994; FGD 3: 444. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 506, pl. 225. 1998.
Ocimum frutescens L., Sp. Pl. 2: 597. 1753.
Perilla ocymoides L., Gen. Pl. ed 6, 578. 1764; FKH 209. 1912.
Ocimum acutum Thunb., Fl. Jap. 248. 1784.

Annual herbs, 0.5–1.5 m tall. Stems erect, obtusely 4‑angled, densely villous. Leaves opposite; petioles 3–5 cm, densely villous; leaf blade broadly ovate to suborbicular, 7–13 × 4.5–10 cm, base rounded or broadly cuneate, apex acute or mucronate, margin coarsely serrate, stained with purple abaxially, or sometimes on both surfaces, sparsely pubescent adaxially, appressed pubescent abaxially. Verticillasters forming 1‑sided racemes of 5–15 cm, densely villous; bracts broadly ovate to suborbicular, ca. 4 mm in diam., apex mucronate; pedicels ca. 1.5 mm, densely pubescent. Calyx campanulate, 10‑veined, ca. 3 mm, lengthening to 1.1 cm in fruit, straight, base villous, limb 2‑lipped, lower lip longer than upper lip. Corolla white or purplish red, 3–4 mm, ± puberulous abaxially, 2‑lipped, upper lip emarginate, lower lip 3‑lobed, the middle lobe the largest. Stamens not exserted. Nutlets subglobose, ca. 1.5 mm in diam.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 1835; HK sheet 22248.
Distribution: Widely cultivated and naturalized in China and elsewhere.
Ecology: Flowering: Oct. – Dec.; fruiting: Nov. –Feb. of the following year.
Uses: Additive (flavouring), medicinal (folklore).

Perilla frutescens (L.) Britton var. crispa (Benth.) Deane ex Bailey 回回蘇
Manual Cult. Plants ed. 1, 646. 1924; FOC 17: 242. 1994; FGD 3: 445. 1995.
Perilla arguta Benth., Prodr. 12: 164. 1848; FHK 276. 1861.
Perilla frutescens var. arguta (Benth.) Hand.‑Mazz., Acta Horti Gothob. 13(10): 351 – 352. 1939.
Perilla nankinensis (Lour.) Decne, Rev. Hort. 1: 61, pl. 4. 1852; FKH 209. 1912.
Dentidia nankiensis Lour., Fl. Cochinch. ed. 2, 448. 1793.

Leaves fimbriate‑serrate and crisped, with narrow and deep teeth.

Locality: Cultivated. Hance s.n. (fide Bentham, 1861)
Distribution: Widely cultivated in China; Japan.
Ecology: Cultivated in gardens or escaped in wastelands.
Uses: Additive (flavouring), medicinal (folklore).

Perilla frutescens (L.) Britton var. purpurascens (Hayata) H. W. Li 野生紫蘇
Act Bot. Yunnan. 13: 350. 1991; FOC. 17: 241. 1994.
Perilla ocymoides L. var. purpurascens Hayata, Icon. Pl. Formos. 8: 103. 1919.
Perilla frutescens L. var. acuta (Odash.) Kudô, Mem. Fac. Sci. Taihoku Imp. Univ. 2: 74. 1929; FGD 3: 445. 1995.

Stems finely pilose. Fruiting calyx 4–4.5 mm, sparsely pilose and glandular at base.

Locality: Cultivated and naturalized. W. J. Tutcher 7283; L. T. Lo 269; HK sheet 4443.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Shanxi, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan.
Ecology: Wastelands near villages, sometimes cultivated.
Uses: Additive (flavouring).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Tam, Mau Ping, Pak Sha O, Tai Po, Shing Mun, Tai Mo Shan, Ha Hang, Luk Keng, Plover Cove, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Pogostemon auricularius (L.) Hassk. 水珍珠菜
Tijdsch. Nat. Geschied. 10: 127. 1843; FRPS 66: 379, pl. 79: 1 – 7. 1977; FOC 17: 262. 1994; FGD 3: 454. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 508, pl. 226. 1998.
Dysophylla auricularia (L.) Blume, Bijdr. Fl. Ned. Ind. 14: 826 – 827. 1826; FHK 275. 1861; FKH 208. 1912.
Mentha auricularia L., Mant. Pl. ed. 1, 81. 1767.

Annual herbs, 0.4–1.5 m tall. Stems ascending from the prostrate base, rooting at nodes, densely yellow spreading hirsute. Leaves opposite, shortly petiolate, upper stem leaves subsessile; leaf blade oblong to ovate‑oblong, 2.5–7 × 1.5–2.5 cm, base rounded to shallowly cordate, rarely cuneate, apex obtuse to acute, margin serrate, yellow hirsute on both surfaces and with scattered impressed glands on abaxial surface. Spikes 6–18 cm, apex caudate‑acuminate, continuous or sometimes interrupted at base; bracts ovate‑lanceolate, as long as corolla, margin strigose. Calyx campanulate, ca. 1 × 1 mm, glabrous, yellow glandular; teeth broadly triangular, margin pilose. Corolla purplish to white, ca. 2–2.5 mm, glabrous. Stamens long‑exserted, exserted parts bearded. Nutlets brown, subglobose, ca. 0.5 mm in diam., glabrous.

Locality: Tai Tam, Mau Ping, Pak Sha O, Tai Po, Shing Mun, Tai Mo Shan, Ha Hang, Luk Keng, Plover Cove, Lantau Island. L. T. Lo 541; HK sheet 39645, 39825.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam, Laos, Myanmar, Thailand, India, Sri Lanka, Malaysia, Indonesia, Philippines.
Ecology: Wet places along streams, in forests. Flowering & fruiting: May–Dec.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Mo Shan, Fung Yuen, Ha Hang
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Pogostemon championii Prain 短穗刺蕊草
Bull. Misc. Inform. 1908: 254. 1908; FKH 208. 1912; FRPS 66: 369. 1977; FOC 17: 259. 1994; FGD 3: 454. 1995.
Pogostemon parviflorus Benth., sensu FHK 275. 1861.

Perennial herbs or subshrubs, to 80 cm tall. Stems ascending from the prostrate base, initially pubescent. Leaves opposite; petioles of lower stem leaves 3–6 cm, those of upper leaves 1–1.5 cm, sparsely strigose; leaf blade ovate to ovate‑lanceolate, 6–11 × 2.5–6 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, margin double serrate or crenate, sparsely appressed pubescent on adaxial surface, strigose along veins abaxially. Spikes short‑cylindric, 1.5–4 × 1 cm, continuous or rarely interrupted, appressed pubescent; bracts ovate‑lanceolate, 3–4 mm, ca. as long as calyx. Calyx narrowly campanulate, ca. 4 mm, pubescent abaxially; teeth 5, triangular, subequal, about 1/3 the length of calyx. Corolla purplish, slightly longer than calyx, glabrous, margin sparsely ciliate, lobes subequal. Filaments bearded. Style lobes subequal. Nutlets broadly ovoid, smooth.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Fung Yuen, Ha Hang. Y. S. Lau 2825; HK sheet 22172, 30337.
Distribution: Guangdong.
Ecology: Thin forests on hillslopes. Flowering: Dec.–Apr. of the following year.
Notes: The type specimen was collected by J. G. Champion from Mount Parker between 1847 and 1850. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Aberdeen, Mount Kellet, Mount Nicholson, Ma On Shan, Sunset Peak
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Salvia chinensis Benth. 華鼠尾草
Labiat. Gen. Spec. 725. 1835; FRPS 66: 181, pl. 45: 1 – 5. 1977; FOC 17: 219. 1994; FGD 3: 431, fig. 272. 1995.

Annual herbs, 20–60 cm tall. Stems erect or prostrate at base, pubescent. Leaves simple or 3‑foliolate toward stem base; petiole very short or up to 7 cm, villous; leaf blade of simple leaves ovate to ovate‑elliptic, 1.3–7 × 0.8–4.5 cm, base cordate to rounded, apex obtuse or acute, margin crenate or obtusely serrate, pubescent along veins on both surfaces; terminal leaflet 2.5–7.5 cm, petiolule 0.5–1.7 cm. Verticillasters 6‑flowered, forming terminal racemes or panicles of 5–24 cm, pubescent; bracts lanceolate. Pedicel 1.5–2 mm. Calyx campanulate, purple, veins villous; tube 4–4.5 mm, throat densely hirsute annulate; upper lip ± semicircular, ca. 1.5 × 3 mm, apex 3‑mucronate; lower lip longer than upper lip, ca. 2 × 3 mm; teeth narrowly triangular, apex acuminate. Corolla blue‑purple or purple, ca. 1 cm, pubescent; tube ca. 6.5 mm, pilose annulate inside; upper lip oblong, ca. 3.5 × 3.3 mm, spreading; lower lip ca. 5 × 7 mm, middle lobe obcordate, curved downward, ca. 4 × 7 mm, margin crenulate, apex emarginate; lateral lobes semiorbicular, ca. 1.3 mm wide. Stamens nearly exserted. Nutlets brown, ellipsoidal‑ovoid, ca. 1.5 × 0.8 mm.

Locality: Aberdeen, Mount Kellet, Mount Nicholson, Ma On Shan, Sunset Peak. Y. S. Lau 380, 2601; Y. W. Lam 1579.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Shandong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Margins of forests, grassy hillsides. Flowering: Jul.–Sep.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Salvia coccinea Buc'hoz ex Etlinger 朱唇
De Salvia 23. 1777; FRPS 66: 174. 1977; FOC. 17: 217. 1994; FGD 3: 436. 1995.

Annual or biennial herbs. Stems erect, to 70 cm, covered with spreading and recurved hairs. Leaves simple; petiole 0.5 – 2 cm; leaf blade ovate to triangular‑ovate, 2–5 × 1.5–4 cm, base cordate or truncate, apex acute, margin serrate or obtusely serrate, adaxially pubescent, abaxially grey minutely tomentose. Verticillasters 4–many‑flowered, forming terminal, interrupted racemes; bracts ovate, apex caudate‑acuminate, margin ciliate. Pedicel 2–3 mm, white pilose. Calyx tubular‑campanulate, 7–9 mm, finely pubescent, intermixed with yellowish glands; upper lip ovate, ca. 2.5 mm, ciliolate, apex mucronate; lower lip nearly as long as upper, deeply 2‑toothed. Corolla scarlet or deep red, 2–2.3 cm, pubescent abaxially; tube ca. 1.6 cm; upper lip shorter than lower lip; lower lip ca. 7 mm. Stamens exserted; filaments ca. 4 mm; connectives ca. 1.5 mm, slender. Nutlets yellow‑brown with blackish spots, obovoid, 1.5–2.5 mm.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 22372.
Distribution: S & C USA, Mexico, S America.
Ecology: Flowering: Feb.–May.
Uses: Ornamental

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): D'Aguilar Peak, Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Salvia japonica Thunb. 鼠尾草
Syst. Veg. ed. 14, 72. 1784; FKH 210. 1912; FRPS 66: 179. 1977; FOC 17: 219. 1994; FGD 3: 432. 1995.
Salvia fortunei Benth., Prodr. 12: 354. 1848; FHK 277. 1861; FTW ed. 2, 4: 523, pl. 235. 1998.

Annual herbs, 40–60 cm tall. Stems obtusely quadrangular, sparsely villous on angles or subglabrous. Leaves 1– 3‑pinnate; petiole 7 –9 cm; leaf blade 6–13 × 5–9 cm, pilose or glabrous; upper stem leaves 1‑pinnate, short petiolate; terminal leaflet lanceolate or rhombic, to 10 × 3.5 cm, base cuneate; lateral leaflets subsessile, ovate‑lanceolate, 1.5–5 × 0.8–2.5 cm, base obliquely rounded, margin obtusely serrate. Verticillasters 2 – 6‑flowered, forming terminal racemes or panicles; rachis densely glandular pilose or pilose; bracts and bracteoles lanceolate, 2–5 mm, glabrous. Pedicel 1–1.5 mm, pubescent. Calyx tubular, 4–6 mm, sparsely glandular pilose, hairy annulate on throat inside, 2‑lipped to 1/3 of its length; upper lip triangular or nearly semicircular, ca. 2 × 3 mm; teeth narrowly triangular, apex long acuminate. Corolla reddish, purplish, bluish, to white, ca. 1.2 cm, densely villous; tube obliquely pilose annulate inside, ca. 9 mm, exserted, ca. 2 mm wide at base, to 3.5 mm wide at throat; upper lip elliptic to ovate, ca. 2.5 × 2 mm; lower lip ca. 3 × 4 mm, margin crenulate. Stamens exserted; filaments ca. 1 mm; connectives ca. 6 mm, straight or slightly curved. Nutlets brown, ellipsoidal, ca. 1.7 × 0.5 mm.

Locality: D’Aguilar Peak, Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 2522; D. P. M. Guile 1185; Y. W. Lam 1653.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Sichuan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan.
Ecology: Hillsides, thickets, margins of forests. Flowering: Jun.–Sep.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Mui Tsz Lam, Fanling, Kuk Po
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Salvia plebeia R. Br. 荔枝草（雪見草）
Prodr. 501. 1810; FHK 277. 1861; FKH 210. 1912; FRPS 66: 168, pl. 39: 5 – 9. 1977; FOC 17: 216. 1994; FGD 3: 437, fig. 273. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 527, pl. 238. 1998.

Annual or biennial herbs, with thick tap root. Stems erect, 20–60(–90) cm tall, many‑branched, grey pilose or glabrescent. Leaves simple; petiole 4–15 mm; leaf blade elliptic‑ovate to elliptic‑lanceolate, 2–6 × 0.8–2.5 cm, base rounded to cuneate, apex obtuse to acute, margin crenate, dentate, or serrate, sparsely hirsute adaxially, finely pilose and sparsely yellow‑brown glandular abaxially. Verticillasters 4 – 6‑flowered, numerous, often forming terminal and axillary panicles. Bracts small, linear‑lanceolate. Pedicels 1 – 2 mm, hairy. Calyx campanulate, ca. 2 mm (2.7 mm in fruit), sparsely pilose and yellow‑brown glandular, 2‑lipped; upper lip obtuse, often shortly 3‑fid at the tip; lower lip deeply 2‑toothed, teeth triangular. Corolla reddish, purplish, purple, blue‑purple, to blue, rarely white, 3–4 mm; tube glabrous, hairy annulate inside; upper lip oblong, obtuse, densely puberulent; lower lip 3‑lobed, the middle lobe largest, broadly obovate. Stamens slightly exserted; filaments ca. 1.5 mm; connectives ca. 1.5 mm, arcuate, arms subequal. Nutlets obovoid, 0.4–0.6 mm in diam., brown, rugose.

Locality: Mui Tsz Lam, Fanling, Kuk Po. W. J. Tutcher 9177; Y. W. Lam 520; HK sheet 38878.
Distribution: Widely spread over all provinces except Gansu, Qinghai, Xinjiang, Xizang; Afghanistan, India, Indonesia, Japan, Korea, Malaysia, Myanmar, Russia, Thailand, Vietnam, Australia.
Ecology: Farmlands, margins of forests, streamsides. Flowering & fruiting: Oct.–Apr. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Salvia splendens Ker‑Gawl. 一串紅
Bot. Reg. 8: t. 687. 1822; FRPS 66: 172. 1977; FOC 17. 217. 1994; FGD 3: 436. 1995.

Perennial herbs. Stems erect, 50–90 cm tall. Leaves simple; petiole 3–4.5 cm, glabrous; leaf blade ovate to triangular‑ovate, 2.5–7 × 2–4.5 cm, base truncate or ± rounded, apex acuminate, margin serrate, glabrous, abaxially glandular. Verticillasters 2–6‑flowered, forming terminal racemes to 20 cm, all parts scarlet; bracts ovate, enveloping flowers in bud, apex caudate‑acuminate. Pedicel 4–7 mm, glandular villous. Calyx campanulate, ca. 1.6 cm in flower, dilated to 2 cm after anthesis, veins villous, 2‑lipped to ca. 1/3 of its length; upper lip triangular‑ovate, 5–6 mm, apex mucronate; lower lip slightly longer than upper, deeply 2‑toothed, teeth triangular. Corolla 4–4.2 cm, pubescent; tube slightly dilated at throat; upper lip straight, somewhat concave, oblong, 8–9 mm; lower lip shorter than upper. Filaments ca. 5 mm; connectives ca. 1.3 cm. Nutlets dark brown, ellipsoidal, ca. 3.5 mm, apex irregularly pleated, margin (or midvein) narrowly winged.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 1877; HK sheet 22452.
Distribution: Native to Brasil, widely cultivated elsewhere.
Ecology: Flowering: Jan.–May.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: The corolla is purple or even white in different varieties.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Shing Mun, Tai Po, Fung Hang, Sai Kung
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Scutellaria barbata D. Don 半枝蓮
Prodr. Fl. Nepal. 109. 1825; FRPS 65(2): 229, pl. 49: 5. 1977; FOC 17: 99. 1994; FGD 3: 406. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 532. 1998.
Scutellaria rivularis Wall. ex Benth., Numer. List n. 214. 1829; FKH 211. 1912.

Perennial herbs, 10–30 cm tall. Stems erect from short, thick rhizomes, glabrous or young parts sparsely puberulous. Leaves papery; petiole 1–3 mm, sparsely pubescent; leaf blade narrowly ovate to ovate, 10–25 × 7– 15 mm, base broadly cuneate to subtruncate, apex shortly acuminate or acute, sometimes obtuse, margin remotely and obtusely shallow dentate, subglabrous to sparsely appressed pubescent along veins. Flowers axillary; lower bracts similar to stem leaves, to 8 mm, reduced upward, adaxially sparsely pubescent, abaxially sparsely pubescent only on veins; bracteoles needle‑like, ca. 0.5 mm, inserted at middle of pedicels. Pedicel 1–2 mm, puberulent. Calyx ca. 2 mm, puberulent along veins abaxially, margin ciliolate, to 4.5 mm in fruit; scutellum ca. 1 mm, to 2 mm in fruit. Corolla purple blue, 9–13 mm, pubescent abaxially; tube saccate in front at base, gradually dilated from middle; limb 2‑lipped; upper lip semiorbicular, galeate, ca. 1.5 mm, emarginate at apex; lower lip broadly ovate, 3‑lobed, middle lobe emarginate, lateral lobes triangular‑ovate, ca. 1.5 mm wide, apex acute. Nutlets brown, oblate, ca. 1 mm in diam., warty.

Locality: Shing Mun, Tai Po, Fung Hang, Sai Kung. P. S. Choi 176, 450; HK sheet 39094.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Hebei, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Jiangsu, Shandong, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Korea, Japan, Vietnam, Laos, Myanmar, Thailand, India, Nepal.
Ecology: Farmlands, streamsides, grassy fields. Flowering & fruiting: Mar.–Jul.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Sham Tseng, Tuen Mun, Wong Lung Hang, Sunset Peak
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Scutellaria formosana N. E. Br. 藍花黃芩
Gard. Chron. Ser. 3. 16: 212. 1894; FKH 211. 1912; FRPS 65(2): 142. 1977; FOC 17: 81. 1994; FGD 3: 402. 1995.

Perennial herbs to 30 cm tall, with ± woody rhizomes. Stems ascending, simple or few‑branched, rooting at basal nodes, subglabrous, often purplish. Leaves subleathery; petioles 8–12 mm, subglabrous, glandular; leaf blade ovate to ovate‑lanceolate, 3–8 × 1.5–3.3 cm, base broadly cuneate, apex obtuse to acute, margin with 3‑ or 4‑undulate‑serration on each side, adaxially shiny, abaxially sometimes tinged purple, glabrous and glandular dotted on both surfaces, sometimes sparsely puberulous on veins abaxially. Flowers in terminal racemes of 7–17 cm; bracts narrowly rhombic, ca. 2 mm, pubescent. Pedicel ca. 4 mm, densely pubescent. Calyx ca. 3 mm, ca. 4 mm. in fruit, pubescent abaxially, glandular; scutellum spreading, semiorbicular, to 2 mm. Corolla blue, ca. 2.5 cm, glandular puberulent abaxially; tube ca. 2 cm, base bent, throat to 6 mm wide, villous near base inside; upper lip triangular‑ovate, ca. 8 mm wide; middle lobe of lower lip suborbicular, ca. 4.5 mm in diam., emarginate; lateral lobes ovate, ca. 3 mm wide. Nutlets tuberculate.

Locality: Sham Tseng, Tuen Mun, Wong Lung Hang, Sunset Peak. Y. S. Lau 2996; Y. W. Lam 620; K. L. Yip 4436.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Jiangxi, Fujian.
Ecology: Forest. Flowering & fruiting: Jul. –Feb. of the following year.

Scutellaria indica L. 韓信草
Sp. Pl. 2: 600. 1753; FHK 278. 1861; FKH 211. 1912; FRPS 65(2): 172. 1977; FOC 17: 87. 1994; FGD 3: 404. fig. 254. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 532, pl. 241. 1998.

Perennial herbs, 8–28 cm tall. Stems usually dark purple, 1–few, ascending‑erect from a short rhizome, puberulous, especially on angles and apex. Petioles 4–15(–28) mm, densely puberulous; leaf blade cordate‑orbicular to orbicular‑ovate, or elliptic, 1–2.6(–3) × 1–2.3 cm, base rounded to cordate, apex rounded to acute, margin crenate, puberulous or strigose, densely so on abaxial surface. Flowers opposite, in a terminal 1‑sided raceme of 4–8(– 12) cm; lower bracts leaf‑like, ovate, to 1.7 cm, crenate; upper ones sessile, ovate to elliptic, 3–6 × 1–2.5 mm, margin entire, puberulent. Pedicels 2.5–3 mm, puberulent. Calyx ca. 2.5 mm, hirsute and puberulent; scutellum ca. 1.5 mm, erect, dilated to 3 mm in fruit. Corolla blue‑purple, 1.3–1.8 cm, sparsely puberulent outside, pubescent on lips inside, to ca. 4.5 mm wide at throat; middle lobe of lower lip dark purple spotted, orbicular‑ovate, slightly constricted at middle, apex emarginate; lateral lobes ovate. Nutlets chestnut to dark brown, ovoid, less than 1 mm in diam., tuberculate.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. L. T. Lo 112; Y. S. Lau 2246; Y. S. Lau 2987.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Vietnam, Cambodia, Laos, Myanmar, Thailand, India, Malaysia, Indonesia.
Ecology: Margins of forests, grasslands. Flowering & fruiting: Nov.–Mar. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Scutellaria tayloriana Dunn 偏花黃芩
Notes Roy. Bot. Gard. Edinb. 8: 166. 1913; FRPS 65(2): 170. 1977; FOC 17: 87. 1994; FGD 3: 404. 1995.

Perennial herbs, 10–35 cm tall, sometimes with trailing rhizomes. Stems erect to ascending, covered with white multicellular hairs. Leaves in 3 or 4 pairs; petioles 2–5(–9) cm, those of mid stem leaves longest, densely white villose; leaf blade ovate to ovate‑oblong, lower ones 2–4 × 1.8–2.7 cm, middle ones 5–9 × 4.5–7 cm, base cordate or rounded, apex rounded or obtuse, margin shallowly undulate‑crenate, both surfaces white strigose especially on veins, orange glandular dotted abaxially. Racemes terminal, secund, 7–15 cm; peduncle 1–4.5 cm; bracts sessile, gradually narrowed toward apex, ovate, ca. 4 × 2 mm, margin entire. Pedicel ca. 2 mm, villous. Calyx ca. 2.5 mm, densely pubescent. Corolla purplish to purple‑blue, (1.5–)1.8–2.5(–3) cm, bent at base, to 6 mm wide at throat, sparsely puberulent abaxially; middle lobe of lower lip semiorbicular; lateral lobes ovate.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Sunset Peak. P. S. Choi 486; HK sheet 32233, 39913.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hunan.
Ecology: Forests, thickets. Flowering: Feb.–Apr.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The type specimen (Ford 107, E) was collected by C. Ford from Tai Mo Shan in March 1885.

Stachys geobombycis C. Y. Wu 地蠶（野芝麻）
Acta Phytotax. Sin. 10: 222. 1965; FRPS 66: 21. 1977; FOC 17: 182. 1994; FGD 3: 427, fig. 268. 1995.
Stachys asper auct. non Michx.: FKH 211. 1912.

Perennial herbs, 40–50 cm tall. Rhizomes enlarged into succulent tubers at the end. Stems and branches retrorse hispid on angles and at nodes. Leaves opposite; petioles 1–4.5 cm; leaf blade ovate to oblong‑ovate, 4.5–8 × 2.5– 3 cm, base shallowly cordate or rounded, apex obtuse, margin coarsely crenate‑serrate, sparsely pilose‑hispid, densely so on veins of abaxial surface. Verticillasters 4–6‑flowered, forming terminal spikes to 5 cm or more. Calyx obconical, ca. 5.5 mm, densely puberulent, 10‑veined; teeth 5, ca. 1.5 mm, callous‑tipped. Corolla pale purple to bluish purple, or sometimes pink, ca. 1.1 cm; upper lip erect, oblong‑ovate, ca. 4 mm; lower lip spreading, ca. 5 mm, 3‑lobed. Stamens included. Style slightly exserted.

Locality: Hung Mui Kuk. L. T. Lo 463; HK sheet 32792.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian.
Ecology: Wet grasslands and wastelands. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–May.
Uses: Food (rhizomes), medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Pok Fu Lam, Victoria Peak, Mount Nicholson, Mount Cameron, Aberdeen, Repulse Bay, Deep Water Bay, Ng Kwai Shan
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Teucrium quadrifarium Buch.‑Ham. 鐵軸草
Prodr. Fl. Nepal. 108–109. 1825; FHK 280. 1861; FKH 212. 1912; FRPS 65(2): 40, pl. 6. 1977; FOC 17: 59. 1994.

Subshrubs, 30–100 cm tall; stems and branches rusty villous or hirsute. Leaves opposite; petioles 1–1.5 cm, the uppermost leaves subsessile; leaf blade narrowly elliptic to very narrowly ovate, 3–8 × 1.5–4 cm, base truncate or cordate, often oblique, apex bluntly acute, margin serrulate, pubescent and slightly rugose adaxially, villous along veins abaxially. Verticillasters forming terminal and axillary raceme‑like inflorescence and rearranged in panicles of 7–10 cm; axis villous. Calyx tubular‑campanulate, 3–5 mm, 10‑veined, villous, 2‑lipped, upper lip 3‑toothed, the middle lobe large, oblate‑orbicular, the lateral 2 lobes much smaller, triangular. Corolla pink, 1.2–1.3 cm, pubescent abaxially, with a ring of hairs at the throat, limb seemly 1‑lipped, the middle lobe obovate‑orbicular, lateral lobes ovate‑oblong. Stamens exserted. Style equaling stamens. Nutlets obovoid‑globose, ca. 1 mm.

Locality: Pok Fu Lam, Victoria Peak, Mount Nicholson, Mount Cameron, Aberdeen, Repulse Bay, Deep Water Bay, Ng Kwai Shan. Y. S. Lau 2351; HK sheet 39830, 40883.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian; Nepal, India, Myanmar to Indonesia.
Ecology: Hillslopes, thickets. Flowering: Jul.–Dec.; fruitig: Aug.–Feb. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Teucrium viscidum Blume 血見愁
Bijdr. Fl. Ned. Ind. 14: 827. 1825; FRPS 65(2): 31. 1977; FGD 3: 389, fig. 247. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 545, pl. 250. 1998.
Teucrium stoloniferum Roxb., Fl. Ind. ed. 1832, 3: 3. 1832, nom. illeg., non Teucrium stoloniferum Ruiz & Pav. (1814).
Teucrium stoloniferum Hamilt. ex Benth. in Wall., Pl. Asiat. Rar. 1: 58. 1830; FHK 279. 1861; FKH 212. 1912.
Teucrium japonicum Willd in DC. Prodr. 12: 581.

Perennial herbs, 30–70 cm tall, stoloniferous; stems and branches glandular pubescent. Leaves opposite; petioles 1–3 cm; leaf blade ovate to ovate‑oblong, 3–7(–10) × 2.5–4 cm, base rounded, broadly cuneate or cuneate, decurrent, apex acute or shortly acuminate, margin crenate, subglabrous or very sparsely puberulent on both surfaces. Verticillasters forming terminal and axillary raceme‑like inflorescence of 3–7 cm, viscous; pedicels ca. 2 mm. Calyx campanulate, 2–3 mm, 10‑veined, glandular pubescent, limb subequally 5‑toothed. Corolla white, pink tinged with blue, 6–8 mm, limb seemly 1‑lipped, the middle lobe suborbicular, lateral lobes ovate‑triangular. Stamens exserted. Style equaling stamens. Nutlets depressed ovoid or globose, ca. 1.3 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. L. T. Lo 123; Y. S. Lau 2759, 3137.
Distribution: Areas S of Changjiang; Korea, Japan, Philippines, Vietnam, Myanmar, India to Indonesia.
Ecology: Wet places in ravines, thin forests, roadside. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Aug.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Callitriche palustris var. elegans (Petrov) Y. L. Chang 東北水馬齒
Fl. Pl. Herb. Chin. Bor.‑Orient. 6: 53. 1977; FRPS 45(1): 12, pl. 4: 6 – 7. 1980; FOC 11: 320. 2008.
Callitriche bengalensis Petrov, Izv. Glavn. Bot. Sada S.S.S.R. 27: 358. 1928.
Callitriche stagnalis auct. non Scop.: FKH 102. 1912.

Flowers generally with a carpellate and staminate flower in one of a pair of axils opposed by a single carpellate flower in other axil, very occasionally 2 carpellate flowers and 1 staminate flower in a single axil; bracts persistent, 0.8 – 1.2 mm, falcate; styles erect to slightly spreading, shorter than 1.5 mm; filaments ± straight, fugacious, rarely visible in axils below rosettes, shorter than 2.2 mm; anthers ca. 0.4 × 0.3 mm. Fruit black when mature, 1 – 1.4 × 0.7 – 1.1 mm, sessile, higher than wide, widest above middle, slightly strumose, mericarps sharply reticulate, reticulations appearing ± clearly in vertical rows; wing all around, mainly toward apex, less than 0.3 mm wide.

Locality: Lam Tsuen. S. Y. Hu & P. P. H. But 21976 (K); K. Y. Chan 1414 (IBSC, HK).
Distribution: N Heilongjiang, Jiangxi, E Jilin, Liaoning, E Nei Mongol; Japan, E Russia.
Ecology: Along ditches, in marshes. Flowering & fruiting: All year round.
Notes: The species was reported as C. stagnalis Scop. previously in various local literature (Hu, Enum. Vasc. Pl. Hongk. & N.T. 39. 1972; Corlett et al., Mem. Hongk. Nat. Hist. Soc. 23: 39. 2000; Check List HK Plants 240. 2002; 83. 2004), based on a specimen from Lam Tsuen (K. Y. Chan 1414); the duplicate at K was cited as C. palustris var. palustris by Lansdown (Novon 16: 358. 2006).

Callitriche palustris var. oryzetorum (Petrov) Lansdown 廣東水馬齒
Novon 16: 359. 2006; FOC 11: 320. 2008.
Callitriche oryzetorum Petrov, Izv. Glavn. Bot. Sada S.S.S.R. 27: 358. 1928; FRPS 45(1): 14. 1980; FGD 4: 130. 2000.

Flowers with a carpellate and staminate flower in each axil, very occasionally 2 carpellate flowers and 1 staminate flower in a single axil; bracts persistent, broadly ovoid, 0.58–0.9(–1) mm; styles erect to spreading, shorter than 1.7 mm; filaments straight; 1.6–2.7 mm; anthers 0.4–0.5 × 0.3–0.4 mm. Fruit brown when mature, 0.7–1 × 0.6–0.8 mm, widest near middle, smooth; wing lacking or up to 0.1 mm, only at apex.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. S. Y. Hu 11356 (PE).
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong, Taiwan, Yunnan, Zhejiang; Japan.
Ecology: Running water in ditches.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Victoria Peak, Wong Nai Chung Gap
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Plantago lanceolata L. 長葉車前
Sp. Pl. 13. 1753; FKH 212. 1912; FRPS 70: 338. 2002.

Herbs perennial. Leaves basal, rosulate; petioles 7–10 cm, base sheath‑like; leaf‑blade papery, linear‑lanceolate, elliptic‑lanceolate or lanceolate, 6–20 × 0.5–4.5 cm, base narrowly cuneate, decurrent, apex acuminate to acute, margin entire or very sparsely serrulate, glabrous or sparsely pubescent on both surfaces; (3–)5(–7)‑veined. Spikes cylindric or head‑like, 1–5(–8) cm. Bracts ovate or elliptic, 2.5 – 5 mm, apex caudate, densely hirsute. Sepals 4, 2– 3.5 mm, carinate, anterior 2 connate near top, posterior free. Corolla white; tube 1.5–3 mm; lobes lanceolate or ovate‑lanceolate, 1.5–3 mm. Anthers white to yellowish, elliptic, 2.5–3 mm. Capsules ovoid, 3–4 mm, circumscissile. Seeds (1–)2, light brown to dark brown.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Wong Nai Chung Gap. HK sheet 9650.
Distribution: S, E & NE China; Europe.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides. Flowering: Spring to summer.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Pok Fu Lam, Yuen Tun Ha, Tai Po, Sheung Shui, Yuen Long, Wu Kau Tang, Sai Kung, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Plantago major L. 車前草
Sp. Pl. 112. 1753; FHK 280. 1861; FKH 213. 1912; FGD 3: 317. 1995; FRPS 70: 324. 2002.

Herbs perennial. Leaves basal, rosulate; petioles about equaling to leaf‑blade in length, base expanded; leaf blade broad‑ovate, oblong‑ovate or suborbicular, 5–12 × 3.5–10 cm, base decurrent, apex obtuse, margin entire or irregularly obtuse‑dentate, pubescent or glabrous on both surfaces, 5–7‑veined. Spikes erect, 6–20 cm. Bracts green, scarious. Sepals elliptic, 2.3–3 mm, slightly unequal, carinate. Corolla‑tube constricted at throat; lobes deltoid, ca. 1.3 mm. Anthers purplish. Capsules elliptic, 3.5–4 mm, circumscissile. Seeds 8 – 18, dark‑brown.

Locality: Pok Fu Lam, Yuen Tun Ha, Tai Po, Sheung Shui, Yuen Long, Wu Kau Tang, Sai Kung, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 1946; L. T. Lo 74; P. S. Choi 357.
Distribution: Widely distributed in Asia and Europe.
Ecology: Roadsides in rural areas, wastelands. Flowering: Feb.–Jul.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Wan Chai Gap, Barker Rd., Bowen Rd., Mount Davis Rd., Fei Ngo Shan, Kadoorie Farm, Cheung Chau, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Buddleja asiatica Lour. 白背楓（駁骨丹）
Fl. Cochinch. 72. 1790; FHK 231. 1861; FKH 174. 1912; FRPS 61: 276. 1992.

Shrubs or subshrubs evergreen, 1–2 m tall. Branchlets, inflorescence and abaxial surface of leaves densely grey to yellow tomentose or villose. Leaves opposite, petioles 4–10 mm; leaf blade lanceolate, 7–18 × 1.5–4.5 cm, margin serrulate. Flowers 1–3 in cymes, rearranged in terminal and axillary panicles of 7–25 cm; pedicel 1 mm. Calyx campanulate or tubiform, 1.5–4 mm. Corolla white, sometimes greenish, tube cylindric, straight, 3–6 mm, sparsely pubescent abaxially; lobes very short. Stamens attached to upper part of corolla‑tube. Ovary glabrous; style short; stigma capitate. Capsules elliptic, 3–5 × 1.5–3 mm. Seeds grey‑brown, elliptic, 0.8–1 mm, shortly winged on both ends.

Locality: Wan Chai Gap, Barker Rd., Bowen Rd., Mount Davis Rd., Fei Ngo Shan, Kadoorie Farm, Cheung Chau, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 972, 2014; Y. W. Lam 639.
Distribution: Taiwan, Fujian, Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Shanxi, Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi; tropical Asia.
Ecology: Thin forests or thickets. Flowering: Feb.–Oct.; fruiting: Mar.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.

Buddleja lindleyana Fortune 醉魚草（百寶花）
Edwards's Bot. Reg. 25. 1844; FHK 231. 1861; FKH 174. 1912; FRPS 61. 308. 1992.

Shrubs deciduous, up to 2 m tall. Branches 4‑angulate, slightly winged; branchlets, abaxial surface of young leaves and inflorescence brown stellate hairy. Leaves opposite, ovate, ovate‑lanceolate or elliptic, 5–10 × 2–3 cm, base cuneate, apex acute or acuminate, margin entire or sparsely sinuate‑toothed. Cymes rearranged in terminal racemes, slightly pendulous, 10–45 cm, tomentose; flowers turning to one side, densely glandular lepidote; pedicels ca. 1.5 mm. Calyx campanulate, 4 mm. Corolla purple; tube 1–1.5 cm, slightly curved; lobes broad‑ovate or suborbicular, 3.5 × 3 mm. Stamens attached to lower part of corolla‑tube. Ovary ovoid, 1.5–2.2 mm, glabrous. Capsules oblong or elliptic, 5–6 mm, lepidote. Seeds brownish, small, without wing.

Locality: Wan Chai Gap. HK sheet 3933.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian.
Ecology: Thin forests or thickets. Flowering: Aug.–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental, poisonous.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Mount Nicholson, Ma On Shan, Ngau Ngak Shan, Wu Kau Tang
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Chionanthus ramiflorus Roxb. 枝花李欖
Fl. Ind. ed. 1, 106–107. 1820; FOC 15: 294. 1996; FGD 5: 421. 2003.
Linociera ramiflora (Roxb.) Wall. ex G. Don, Gen. Hist. 4: 52. 1837; FHN 3: 216, fig. 668. 1974; FRPS 61: 114, pl. 32: 1 – 3. 1992; Check List HK Plants 243. 2002; 84. 2004.
Linociera ramiflora f. pubisepala L. C. Chia, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 3(3): 352. 1955.

Trees, 6–15(–25) m tall, branchlets terete, usually compressed at nodes, lenticellate. Petiole 2–5 cm, glabrous; leaf blade elliptic, oblong‑elliptic, or ovate‑elliptic, rarely obovate‑oblong, (5–)8–20(–30) × (2–)4–7(–12) cm, base attenuate, apex acuminate, or blunt, subleathery, glabrous, densely dotted with raised pimples adaxially; lateral veins 7–15 on each side of midvein, raised on both surfaces or obscure adaxially. Panicles usually axillary, loose, 2.5–12 cm; pedicel 1–5 mm. Calyx ca. 1 mm; lobes ovate, ca. 0.5 mm, acute or blunt. Corolla white or yellow, 2.5 – 5.5; lobes oblong, 2–2.5 mm, slightly united at base. Anthers elliptic. Ovary elliptic; style very short or absent. Drupe blue‑black, pruinose, elliptic or long‑elliptic, 1–3 × 0.5–1.5 cm.

Locality: Mount Nicholson, Ma On Shan, Ngau Ngak Shan, Wu Kau Tang. F. W. Xing 8116, 8627; Y. W. Lam 643.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Taiwan; Vietnam, Nepal, India, Pacific islands, Australia.
Ecology: Forests and thickets in ravines. Flowering: Dec.–Jun. of the following year; fruiting: May–Mar. of the following year.

Chionanthus retusus Lindl. & Paxton 流蘇樹
Paxt. Fl. Gard. 3: 85, fig. 273. 1852; FKH 166. 1912; FFJ 4: 375, fig. 306. 1989; FRPS 61: 119, pl. 33: 1 – 3. 1992; FOC 15: 293. 1996; FTW ed. 2, 4: 129, pl. 48. 1998; FGD 5: 419, fig. 221. 2003.
Chionanthus serrulatus Hayata, Icon. Pl. Formosan. 3: 150–151, fig. 28. 1913.

Deciduous trees or shrubs to 20 m tall. Branchlets terete, glabrous, or pubescent when young. Petioles 0.5–2 cm, densely covered with curly hairs; leaf blade oblong, elliptic, or orbicular, sometimes ovate or obovate, 3–10 × 2– 4.5 cm, base rounded to cuneate, rarely subcordate, apex blunt, sometimes retuse or acute, ± leathery, abaxially villous along midvein, adaxially villous or glabrescent except on veins; lateral veins 3 or 4 on each side of midvein, slightly raised on both surfaces. Cymose panicles terminal on lateral shoots, 3–12 cm; pedicels 0.8–1 cm, glabrous. Calyx cup‑shaped, 4‑parted; lobes deltoid, 1–2 mm. Corolla white, 4‑parted; tube 2–4 mm; lobes linear‑spatulate, 1.5–2.5 cm. Anthers long ovate, 1.5–2 mm; connectives elongate. Drupe 1–1.5 cm × 6–10 mm, blue‑black or black, pruinose, ovoid.

Locality: Lantau Island. HK sheet 18463.
Distribution: Guangdong, Yunnan, Sichuan, Gansu, Shaanxi, Shanxi, Hebei, Henan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Korea.
Ecology: Forests and thickets. Flowering: Mar.–Jun.; fruiting: Jul.
Uses: Ornamental.

Fraxinus chinensis Roxb. 白蠟樹
Fl. Ind. 1: 150. 1820; FKH 166. 1912; FFJ 4: 364, fig. 296. 1989; FRPS 61: 30, pl. 8: 7 – 10. 1992; FOC 15: 277. 1996; FGD 5: 414. 2003.

Deciduous tree to 20 m tall; branchlets terete, glabrous, or initially villous; winter buds broadly ovoid or conical, brown tomentose, pubescent or glandular hairy. Leaves 12–25 cm; petiole 4–6 cm; axis puberulent or pilose at first; leaflets 3–7(–9); petiolule 2–15 mm; leaflet blade broadly ovate to lanceolate, or elliptic to obovate‑lanceolate, 3– 10 × 2–4 cm, terminal one somewhat larger, base blunt or cuneate, apex acuminate or acute, papery to leathery, glabrous or villous, sometimes villous along midvein abaxially, margin regularly serrate; lateral veins 7–10 on each side of midvein. Panicles terminal or lateral, 5–12 cm. Flowers dioecious, opening with leaves. Staminate flowers congested; calyx cupular, 1 mm; corolla absent; pistillate flowers lax; calyx tubular, 2–3 mm. Samara spatulate, 3–4 cm × 4–6 mm; wing decurrent to middle part of nutlet.

Locality: Cultivated. L. T. Lo 481; F. W. Xing 9319; HK sheet 18390.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; Vietnam, Korea.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: May–Sep.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Sunset Peak, Keung Shan, Tong Fuk, Lantau Peak
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Fraxinus griffithii C. B. Clarke 光蠟樹
Fl. Brit. India 3(9): 605. 1882; FHN 3: 217, fig. 669. 1974; FFJ 4: 363, fig. 294. 1989; FRPS 61: 10, pl. 3: 1 – 2. 1992; FOC 15: 274. 1996; FTW ed. 2, 4: 132. 1998; FGD 5: 413, fig. 218. 2003.
Fraxinus formosana Hayata, J. Coll. Sci. Imp. Univ. Tokyo 30(1): 189 – 190. 1911.
Fraxinus guilingensis S. K. Lee & F. N. Wei, Guihaia 2(3): 130 – 131, fig. 3. 1982.

Tree 10–20 m tall, semi‑evergreen. Branchlets greyish, with raised lenticelles; winter buds naked, scurfy‑pubescent. Leaves 10–25 cm; petiole 3–8 cm; axis glabrous or puberulent; leaflets 5–7(–11); petiolule 3–8 mm, with slightly dilated joint at base; leaflet blade ovate to lanceolate, 4–12 × 1.5–5 cm, leathery or thinly leathery, adaxially glabrous, abaxially glandular dotted, slightly asymmetrical, apex acuminate, mucronulate, margin entire; lateral veins 7–9 on each side of midvein, obscure or convex abaxially. Panicles terminal, 10–25 cm, puberulent, spreading, many‑flowered; leafy bracts persistent, spatulate‑linear, 3–10 mm, puberulent at first. Flowers polygamous, opening after leaves. Peduncle 4–5 cm; pedicel slender, 2–4 mm. Calyx cupular, ca. 1 mm, puberulent or glabrous, shortly toothed. Corolla white; lobes navicular, ca. 2 mm. Stamens ca. equal to corolla lobes. Samara broadly lanceolate‑spatulate, 2–3 cm × 4–5 mm, surface nerviform; wing decurrent to about middle of nutlet.

Locality: Sunset Peak, Keung Shan, Tong Fuk, Lantau Peak. Y. S. Lau 1285; F. W. Xing 7350; S. C. Ng 2214.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Philippines, India, Bangladesh, Indonesia.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: May–Jul.; fruiting: Jul.–Nov.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Happy Valley, Wong Chuk Hang, Deep Water Bay, Mount Kellet, Ma On Shan
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Fraxinus insularis Hemsl. 苦櫪木
J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 26(173): 86. 1889; FFJ 4: 367, fig. 299. 1989; FRPS 61: 20, pl. 5: 5 – 8. 1992; FOC 15: 276. 1996; FTW ed. 2, 4: 132, pl. 49. 1998; FGD 5: 414. 2003.
Fraxinus taiwaniana Masam., Trans. Nat. Hist. Soc. Taiwan 24: 210. 1934.
Fraxinus retusa Champ. ex Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 4: 330. 1852; FHK 214. 1861; FKH 166. 1912.
Fraxinus retusa var. calcicola C. Y. Wu ex P. Y. Bai, Acta Bot. Yunnan. 5(2): 178. 1983.
Fraxinus insularis var. henryana (Oliv.) Z. Wei, FRPS 61: 20, pl. 5: 4. 1992.

Deciduous tree, 20–30 m tall. Winter buds broadly obovate to conical, brown scaly or tomentose, becoming dark and shiny when dry. Leaves 10–25 cm or longer; petiole 3–8 cm; leaflets 3–5(–7); petiolule slender, (0.5–)1– 1.5 cm; leaflet blade ovate‑lanceolate, or elliptic‑lanceolate, 5–12 × 2–4 cm, thinly leathery, glabrous, base broadly cuneate or blunt, serrate or entire from below the middle, apex acuminate; lateral veins 7–11 on each side of midvein. Panicles terminal or terminal and lateral, 20–30 cm, many‑flowered. Flowers polygamous, appearing after leaves. Pedicels slender, ca. 3 cm. Calyx cupular, ca. 1 × 1.5 mm; teeth truncate, upper chaffy. Corolla white; lobes spatulate, ca. 2 × 1 mm. Stamens longer than corolla; anther 1.5 mm, apex blunt; Style almost equal to stigma; stigma 2‑lobed. Samara long spatulate, 2–4 cm × 3–5 mm, red to brown; wing decurrent to upper part of nutlet.

Locality: Happy Valley, Wong Chuk Hang, Deep Water Bay, Mount Kellet, Ma On Shan. Y. S. Lau 656, 3061; Y. W. Lam 261.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: May–Aug.
Notes: The type specimen of Fraxinus retusa was collected by J. G. Champion from Happy Valley Woods between 1847 and 1850.

Jasminum elongatum (Bergius) Willd. 扭肚藤
Sp. Pl. ed. 4, 1(1): 37. 1797; FRPS 61: 211, pl. 56: 2 – 3. 1992; FOC 15: 317. 1996; FGD 5: 434. 2003.
Nyctanthes elongata Bergius, Philos. Trans. 61: 289, pl. 11. 1772.
Jasminum undulatum Ker‑Gawl. Bot. Reg. 6: pl. 436. 1820; FKH 165. 1912.
Jasminum amplexicaule Buch.‑Ham. ex G. Don, Gen. Hist. 4: 60. 1837.

Scandent shrub, 1–7 m. Branchlets terete, densely tomentose. Leaves opposite, simple; petiole 2–5 mm; leaf blade papery, ovate to lanceolate, 4–7 × 2.5–4.5 cm, base rounded, truncate, or subcordate, apex acute or obtuse and mucronulate, pubescent or glabrescent except for hairy veins abaxially, lateral veins pinnate, 3 or 5 on each side of midvein. Cymes terminal or axillary, many‑flowered, congested, yellow‑pubescent; bracts 1–3, linear or ovate‑lanceolate, 1–5 mm, or absent. Flowers heterostylic; pedicels 1–4 mm. Calyx densely tomentose, tube 1.5– 3 mm; lobes 6–8, subulate‑filiform, ca. 1 cm. Corolla white, salverform; tube 2–3 cm; lobes 6–9, lanceolate, 10 × 2 – 3 mm. Fruit subglobose or ovoid, 10 × 5–8 mm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island. Y. S. Lau 2551.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; Vietnam, Myanmar to Himalayas.
Ecology: Margins of forests, thickets. Flowering: Aug.–Nov.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal (folklore).

Jasminum lanceolaria Roxb. 清香藤
Fl. Ind. 1: 97. 1820; FHN 3: 205. 1974; FFJ 4: 387, fig. 321. 1989; FRPS 61: 197, pl. 52: 1 – 2. 1992; FOC 15: 314. 1996; FTW ed. 2, 4: 134. 1998; FGD 5: 430. 2003.
Jasminum lanceolaria var. puberulum Hemsl., J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 26: 78. 1889.
Jasminum shimadai Hayata, Icon. Pl. Formosan. 9: 70 – 71, pl. 5, fig. 26. 1920.
Jasminum pachyllum Hemsl., J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 26(173): 79 – 80. 1889; FKH 165. 1912.
Jasminum paniculatum auct. non Roxb.: FHK 216. 1861; FKH 165. 1912.

Large scandent shrubs, 5–15 m. Branchlets terete, sometimes angled, glabrous or pubescent. Leaves opposite, trifoliolate; petioles 1–4.5 cm, adaxially canaliculate; leaflet blade elliptic, ovate, or lanceolate, 5–13 × 1.5–6.5 cm, leathery, base cuneate or rounded, apex acute or acuminate; lateral veins obscure; petiolules 1–3 cm; terminal leaflet slightly larger than or equal to lateral leaflets. Compound cymes paniculate, terminal or axillary, many‑flowered; bracts linear, 2–5 mm. Flowers fragrant, heterostylic; pedicels 0–5 mm, stout. Calyx tubular, 2–3 mm; lobes 5, deltate. Corolla white, salverform; tube 2–2.5 cm; lobes 4–5, ovate to oblong, 7–10 × 4 mm. Fruit globose or ellipsoidal, 0.5–1 × 0.8–1.5 cm, black when matured.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 42, 1287, 1341.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Gansu, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam, Thailand, Myanmar, Bhutan, India.
Ecology: Thickets and margins of forests. Flowering: Apr.–Oct.; fruiting: Sep.–Mar. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Jasminum mesnyi Hance 雲南黃素馨
J. Bot. 20(230): 37. 1882; FFJ 4: 387, fig. 322. 1989; FRPS 61: 183. 1992; FOC 15: 311. 1996; FGD 5: 430. 2003.
Jasminum primulinum Hemsl., Bull. Misc. Inform. Kew 1895(100 – 101): 109. 1895.

Evergreen shrubs, scandent, 1–3 m tall. Branchlets slight, 4‑angled, glabrous. Leaves opposite, trifoliolate; petioles 1 cm, adaxially canaliculate; leaflets sub‑leathery, narrowly ovate to ovate‑lanceolate, glabrous, terminal one larger 3–5 × 1–2 cm, basally decurrent into a short petiolule (ca. 1–2.5 mm); lateral leaflets smaller, sessile, 2.5–4 × 0.7–1 cm, base cuneate, apex obtuse and mucronulate; lateral veins and veinlets obscure. Flowers solitary in axils of leaves; pedicels stout, 3–8 mm; bracts 2–5, leafy, narrowly ovate to obovate, 5 × 2 mm. Calyx campanulate, tube 2.5–5; lobes 5–8, leafy, lanceolate, 4–7 mm. Corolla yellow, 2–4.5 cm in diam.; tube 1–1.2 cm; lobes 6–8, sometimes doubled, obovate to oblong, nerviform, 1.2–1.8 cm. Fruit ellipsoidal, 6–8 mm in diam., two carpels connate at base.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 2096
Distribution: Guizhou, Yunnan, SW Sichuan, widely cultivated in China.
Ecology: Flowering: Jan.–Mar.
Uses: Ornamental.

Jasminum multiflorum (Burm. f.) Andrews 毛茉莉
Bot. Repos. 8: t. 496. 1807; FRPS 61: 213, pl. 56: 1. 1992; FOC 15: 317. 1996; FGD 5: 435. 2003.
Nyctanthes multiflora Burm. f., Fl. Ind. 5: pl. 3, fig. 1. 1768.

Scandent shrubs, 1–6 m. Branchlets terete, slender, densely yellow‑pilose. Leaves simple, opposite; petiole 4–10 mm, densely pilose, articulate near base; leaf blade elliptic, ovate, 2.5–5.5 × 1.5–3 cm, base cordate or truncate, apex acuminate, acute or blunt, mucronulate, papery or thinly leathery, scattered pilose on both surfaces, or glabrous adaxially, lateral veins pinnate, 4–6 on each side of midvein, flat adaxially, raised adaxially. Cymes terminal or axillary, many‑flowered, congested, peduncle densely yellow‑tomentose; pedicels short or absent; bracts leafy, basal ovate, 1–3 cm, upper linear, 3–5 mm. Flowers fragrant. Calyx densely yellow‑pilose; tube ca. 1 mm; lobes 6–9, subulate, 2–6 mm. Corolla white, tube 1–1.7 × 0.2–0.3 cm; lobes 7–9, oblong, 1–1.5 cm × 0.4–0.6 cm. Fruit ellipsoidal, brown.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 30544, 40752.
Distribution: Native to SE Asia and India, widely cultivated in the world.
Ecology: Flowering: Oct.–Apr. of the following year.
Uses: Ornamental.

Jasminum nervosum Lour. 青藤仔
Fl. Cochinch. 1: 20 – 21. 1790; FHN 3: 207. 1974; FRPS 61: 209, pl. 54: 4 – 5. 1992; FOC 15: 316. 1996; FTW ed. 2, 4: 135, pl. 50. 1998; FGD 5: 434. 2003.
Jasminum elegans (Hemsl.) Yamam., Trans. Nat. Hist. Soc. Taiwan 13: 151. 1914, non Knobl. 1893.
Jasminum nervosum var. elegans (Hemsl.) L. C. Chia, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 2(1): 56. 1952.
Jasminum nervosum var. villosum (H. Lév.) L. C. Chia, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 2(1): 55. 1952.
Jasminum laurifolium auct. non Roxb.: FKH 165. 1912.

Scandent shrub, 1–5 m. Branchlets terete, glabrous or sparsely pubescent. Leaves simple, opposite; petioles 5– 10 mm, articulate; leaf blade ovate to elliptic‑lanceolate, 3–10 × 1.8–4 cm, papery, base broadly cuneate, rounded to subtruncate, apex acuminate to acute, glabrous or puberulous abaxially, especially on veins; veins 3 or 5 from base, outer pair usually obscure when 5‑veined. Cymes terminal or axillary, 1–5‑flowered; peduncle 0–12 mm, glabrous; bracts linear, 5–13 mm; pedicels 2–10 mm. Calyx glabrous, cupular, tube 2 – 2.5 mm; lobes 6 – 8, subulate to linear, 5–8 mm, often enlarged to 15 mm in fruit. Corolla white, salverform; tube 1–2 cm; lobes 8–10, linear to lanceolate, nearly as long as tube, apex acuminate to blunt. Fruit subglobose, red becoming black, 9–15 × 7–13 mm.

Locality: Cultivated. H. C. Tang 137, 1236, 1540.
Distribution: Taiwan, Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Taiwan; Vietnam, Laos, Cambodia, Myanmar, India, Bhutan, Sikkim, Nepal.
Ecology: Thickets and margins of forests. Flowering: Feb.–Apr.

Jasminum sambac (L.) Aiton 茉莉花
Hort. Kew. 1: 8. 1789; FHN 3: 208. 1974; FFJ 4: 385, fig. 319. 1989; FRPS 61: 218, pl. 55: 4. 1992; FOC 15: 318. 1996; FGD 5: 435. 2003.
Nyctanthes sambac L., Sp. Pl. 1: 6. 1753.

Diffuse or scandent shrubs, to 3 m. Branchlets terete, slightly compressed near nodes, pubescent to glabrous. Leaves opposite, simple; petioles 3–5 mm, pubescent, articulate; leaf blade ovate to elliptic, or sometimes obovate, 3–10 × 2.5–7 cm, base rounded, blunt or subcordate, apex acute, blunt or cuspidate, glabrous or sparsely pilose abaxially, usually with tufted hairs at vein axils, lateral veins pinnate, 5–6 on each side of midvein. Cymes terminal, usually 3‑flowered; peduncle 1–4 cm, pubescent; bracts subulate, 4–6 mm; flowers very fragrant; pedicel 0.5–1 cm. Calyx cupular, glabrous or sparsely pubescent; lobes 8 – 9, subulate to linear, 5–8 mm. Corolla white, usually doubled; tube 0.6–1.2 cm; lobes oblong to suborbicular, 11–15 × 7–10 mm. Fruit globose, purple‑black, ca. 1 cm in diam.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 1114, 1850.
Distribution: Native to India, widely cultivated.
Ecology: Flowering: May–Aug.; fruiting: Jul.–Sep.
Uses: Ornamental, additive (flavoring), material (essential oils), medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Cape D'Aguilar, Tai Mo Shan, Tai Po, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Jasminum sinense Hemsl. 華素馨
J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 26(173): 80 – 81. 1889; FKH 165. 1912; FFJ 4: 386, fig. 320. 1989; FRPS 61: 199, pl. 52: 3 – 4. 1992; FOC 15: 314. 1996; FTW ed. 2, 4: 135. 1998; FGD 5: 430. 2003.

Scandent shrub, 1–8 m. Branchlets terete, densely rusty villous. Leaves opposite, trifoliolate; petioles 5–15 mm; leaflet blade ovate to ovate‑lanceolate, papery; base rounded, apex acuminate to acute; rusty pubescent on both surfaces, rarely glabrous and rusty pubescent only along veins; terminal leaflet 3–10 × 2–5 cm, petiolule 0.8–3 cm; lateral leaflets smaller, 1.5–4.5 × 1–2.5 cm, petiolule 2–3 mm. Cymes terminal or axillary, many‑flowered congested panicles, rarely 1‑flowered in leaf axils. Flowers fragrant, heterostylic; pedicels 1–5 mm. Calyx pilose; lobes linear, 1–5 mm, enlarged in fruit. Corolla white or yellowish, salverform; tube 2–3.5 cm × 1–1.5 mm; lobes 5, oblong or lanceolate, apex acute, 7–14 mm; anthers lanceolate, 3 mm; style tenuous, 1.5–2 cm; stigma clavate. Fruit black, globose or subglobose, 8–17 mm × 6–10 mm.

Locality: Cape D'Aguilar, Tai Mo Shan, Tai Po, Lantau Island. F. W. Xing 8952, 9929; Y. W. Lam 1741.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian.
Ecology: Thickets and forests. Flowering: Jun.–Oct.; fruiting: Sep.–May of the following year.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Cape D'Aguilar, Victoria Peak, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Ligustrum liukiuense Koidz. 台灣女貞
Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 30: 82. 1916; FTW ed. 2, 4: 137. 1998.
Ligustrum japonicum Thunb. var. pubescens Koidz., Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 30: 82. 1916.
Ligustrum amamianum Koidz., Pl. Nov. Amami‑Ohsima 7. 1929; FRPS 61: 144, pl. 40: 1 – 2. 1992; FOC 15: 301. 1996.

Evergreen shrubs, 3–5 m tall. Branchlets terete, puberulent at first, soon glabrous, compressed near nodes. Petiole 4–8 mm, glabrous; leaf blade leathery, oblong to ovate, 3.5–7.5 × 1.8–3.8 cm, base obtuse to acute, decurrent, apex short acuminate or obtuse or acute, sometimes retuse, margin strongly revolute, glabrous, densely glandular dotted; lateral veins 5–8 on each side of midvein, impressed adaxially, slightly raised abaxially. Panicles terminal, 7–12 cm; rachis pubescent. Flowers subsessile; bract linear. Calyx ca. 1.8 mm. Corolla 4–6 mm; tube ca. as long as lobes. Stamens nearly approaching apex of corolla lobes; anthers ca. 2 mm. Fruit elliptic, 5–9 mm in diam.

Locality: Cape D'Aguilar, Victoria Peak, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 2474; P. S. Choi 477; K. L. Yip 4493.
Distribution: Taiwan; Japan.
Ecology: Woods on limestone mountain ridges. Flowering: Mar.–Jun.; fruiting: Jul.–Dec.

Ligustrum longipedicellatum H. T. Chang 長柄女貞
Acta Sci. Nat. Univ. Sunyatsen. 1982: 2. 1982; FOC 15: 304. 1996, pro syn. sub L. sinense var. luodianense M. C. Chang.
Ligustrum sinense var. luodianense M. C. Chang, Investig. Stud. Nat. 6: 77. 1986, p. p. quoad syn. L. longipedicellatum H. T. Chang.

Shrubs or small trees, 2–10 m tall. Young branchlets terete, glabrous. Petioles 1–2 cm, glabrous; leaf blade subleathery, glabrous, oblong, 7–14 × 2.5–5.5 cm, base broadly cuneate, apex acute, adaxially lustrous; margin entire; lateral veins 8–10 on each side of midvein. Panicles terminal, 6–27 × 5–15 cm, rachis villous to glabrescent, 4‑ribbed; pedicels 3–5mm, glabrous and tenuous; bracteoles leafy, lanceolate, 1–3.5 × 0.3–1.5 cm. Calyx 4‑lobed, 1 mm. Corolla 3–5 mm; tube ca. 1–2 mm; lobes 2.5–3 mm. Stamens reaching apex of corolla lobes; filament ca. 5 mm; anthers ca. 1.8 mm. Ovary spheroidal, glabrous; style shorter than stamens. Fruit ellipsoidal.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. HK sheet 41615, 41867, 41872.
Distribution: Guangdong.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Jul.–Aug.; fruiting: Oct.–Dec.
Notes: The species was considered as a synonym of L. sinense var. luodianense M. C. Chang, but it differs from the later by its oblong, glabrous leaves, and the terminal panicles.

Ligustrum lucidum W. T. Aiton 女貞
Hort. Kew. ed. 2, 1: 19. 1810; FKH 166. 1912; FFJ 4: 381, fig. 315. 1989; FRPS 61: 153. 1992; FOC 15: 302. 1996; FGD 5: 426. 2003.
Ligustrum nepalense Wall., Roxb. Fl. Ind. ed. 1, 151. 1820.
Ligustrum japonicum Thunb., Nova Acta Regiae Soc. Sci. Upsal. 3: 207. 1780; FKH 166. 1912.

Evergreen shrubs or trees, 4–8 m or taller, glabrous. Branchlets terete, lenticellate. Petiole 1–3 cm; leaf blade leathery, glabrous, ovate to long‑ovate or elliptic, or elliptic to lanceolate, 6–17 × 3–8 cm, base rounded or broadly cuneate, apex acute to acuminate, margin entire; lateral veins 6 – 8 on each side of midvein. Panicles terminal, 10– 23 cm, spreading; rachis angular in fruit. Flowers sessile or nearly so. Calyx campanulate, 1–2 mm. Corolla white, 3.5–4.5 mm; lobes elliptic, slightly longer than tube. Stamens approaching apex of corolla lobes; anthers oblong, 1 – 1.5 mm; style 1.5–2.5 mm; stigma clavate. Fruit 7–10 × 4–6 mm, reniform or nearly so, white farinose and red‑black when matured.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 2714; HK sheet 35579.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Gansu, Shaanxi, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian; Korea.
Ecology: Flowering: May–Jul.; fruiting: Jul.–Oct.
Uses: Ornamental, host (lac/wax insect), medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Chung Mei, Sam A Chung, Sham Chung
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Ligustrum punctifolium M. C. Chang 斑葉女貞
Acta Phytotax. Sin. 23(1): 53 – 54, pl. 1, fig. 1. 1985; FFJ 4: 379, fig. 311. 1989; FRPS 61: 142, pl. 39: 1 – 3. 1992; FOC 15: 301. 1996; FGD 5: 424. 2003.
Ligustrum quihoui auct. non Carr. 1869: Merr. & Chun in Sunyatsenia 1: 79. 1930, quoad specim.Y. Tsiang 2933.

Evergreen shrubs, to 2 m tall. Branchlets terete, puberulent. Petioles ca. 2 mm; leaf blade leathery, elliptic, rarely ovate or obovate, 1–2 × 0.8–1.2 cm, base cuneate to suborbicular, apex obtuse or retuse, occasionally acute, glabrous except for midvein adaxially, sometimes puberulent, brown glandular dotted and abaxially much denser; lateral veins 2 or 3 on each side of midvein, obscure. Panicles terminal, ca. 5 × 2 cm; peduncle puberulent; pedicels 0.5–1.3 mm, glabrous. Calyx ca. 1.5 mm, glabrous, apex undulate‑denticulate or truncate. Corolla 7.5–9 mm, white or yellowish; tube ca. as long as lobes. Stamens 2, reaching apex of corolla lobes; anthers oblong. Fruit subglobose, ca. 4 mm in diam.

Locality: Chung Mei, Sam A Chung, Sham Chung. W. J. Tutcher 10927, 10950; HK sheet 36612.
Distribution: Hainan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Tidal flood plains. Flowering: May–Sep.; fruiting: Oct.–Mar. of the following year.
Notes: The type specimen (Y. Tsiang 2933, IBSC) was collected from a tidal flood plain in Hong Kong on 12 Aug. 1929. Lai (2003, Porcupine No. 23: 19. 2001) provided a review of the history of discovery of this species. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Common in Hong Kong and widely cultivated
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Ligustrum sinense Lour. 山指甲
FL. Cochinch. 1: 19. 1790; FHK 215. 1861; FKH 166; 1912; FFJ 4: 382, fig. 316. 1989; FRPS 61: 158, pl. 44: 1 – 8. 1992; FOC 15: 303. 1996; FTW ed. 2, 4: 138, pl. 51. 1998; FGD 5: 427. 2003.

Deciduous shrubs or small trees, 2–4(–7) m tall. Branchlets terete, villous to glabrescent. Petiole 2–8 mm; leaf blade papery to thinly leathery, ovate, elliptic or suborbicular, 2–7 × 1.5–3 cm, base subrounded to broadly cuneate, apex acute to obtuse, sometimes retuse, villous to sparsely pubescent or puberulous on midvein, epunctate, lateral veins 4–8 on each side of midvein, impressed adaxially, raised abaxially. Panicles terminal or axillary, 4–11 ×3–8 cm; peduncle yellowish puberulent to glabrescent; pedicels 1–3 mm. Calyx campanulate, 1 mm, glabrous or pubescent. Corolla white, 3.5–5.5 mm; tube ca. 1.5–2.5 mm, lobes oblong to ovate‑oblong, ca. 2–3 mm, slightly longer than tube, apex blunt. Stamens reaching apex of corolla lobes or exserted; anthers oblong, ca. 1 mm. Fruit subglobose, 5–8 mm in diam.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong and widely cultivated. H. C. Tang 40, 104, 197.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Yunnan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam. Becomes invasive in Australasia and SE USA.
Ecology: Naturalized along thickets and roadsides. Flowering: Mar.–Jun.; fruiting: Sep.–Dec.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai, Sharp Peak, Sheung Wo Hang
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Olea tsoongii (Merr.) P. S. Green 異株木犀欖
Kew Bull. 50(2): 338. 1995; FOC 15: 297. 1996; FGD 5: 423. 2003.
Ligustrum tsoongii Merr., Philipp. J. Sci. 21: 506. 1922.
Olea brevipes Chia, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 3. 343. 1955.
Olea dioica auct. non Roxb.: FRPS 61: 133, pl. 37: 1 – 3. 1992; FFJ 4: 377, fig. 309. 1989; Check List HK Plants 243. 2002; 84. 2004.

Shrubs or trees, 3–20 m tall. Branchlets terete, slightly compressed at nodes, pubescent to glabrous. Leaves leathery; petioles 3–10 mm, pubescent to finely puberulent; leaf blade oblanceolate or elliptic‑lanceolate, 5–10 × 1.5–3.5 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate or blunt, margin entire or irregularly serrate; lateral veins 5–7 on each side of midvein, obscure or slightly raised on both surfaces. Flowers polygamodioecious, usually in subumbellate groups and rearranged in axillary panicles. Corolla white or yellowish; lobes subrotund, apex cucullate. Staminate flowers: pedicels 1–5 mm, slender; calyx 1–1.5 mm; corolla 2–3.5(–4.5) mm, lobes deltate. Bisexual flowers: pedicels 0–2 mm, stout; calyx 1–1.5 mm; corolla 2–4.5 mm, lobes 0.5–1.5 mm; filament short; anthers elliptic, 0.5– 1 mm; ovary elliptic with a sharp tip; stigma capitate. Drupe blue‑black, elliptic or subglobose, 6–13 × 3–9 mm.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai, Sharp Peak, Sheung Wo Hang. F. W. Xing 6936, 9890; Y. W. Lam 417.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Yunnan; Vietnam, Myanmar, India.
Ecology: Forests and thickets. Flowering: Mar.–Jul.; fruiting: May–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Osmanthus fragrans (Thunb.) Lour. 桂花（木犀）
Fl. Cochinch. 1: 29. 1790; FKH 166. 1912; FFJ 4: 373, fig. 305. 1989; FRPS 61: 107, pl. 29: 4 – 6. 1992; FOC 15: 292. 1996; FGD 5: 418. 2003.
Olea fragrans Thunb., Syst. Veg. ed. 14, 57. 1784.
Osmanthus longibrateatus H. T. Chang, Acta Sci. Nat. Univ. Sunyatsenia 2: 5. 1982.

Trees or shrubs, 3–12(–18) m tall. Branchlets glabrous. Petiole 8–12 mm; leaf blade elliptic to elliptic‑lanceolate, 4– 12 × 2–4 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, margin entire or usually serrulate on distal half, midvein and lateral veins (6–10 on each side of midvein) impressed adaxially, raised abaxially. Cymes fasciculate in leaf axils, 10 – 20‑flowered. Flowers androdioecious; bracts broadly ovate, 2–4 mm; pedicel 4–10 mm, slender. Calyx ca. 1 mm. Corolla white, yellowish, or orange, 3–4 mm, 4‑lobed to near base; lobes 2–3 mm; stamens attached to middle of corolla‑tube; anther 1 mm, connective elongate into an obscure mucro; style 0.5 mm; stigma 2‑lobed. Drupe elliptic, slightly oblique, 1–1.5 cm, purple‑black when matured.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 35994, 38727, 38776.
Distribution: Guizhou, Sichuan, Yunnan; widely cultivated.
Ecology: Flowering: Oct.–May of the following year; fruiting: Mar. of the following year.
Uses: Ornamental, material (essential oil, perfume).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Sha Tin, Pak Tam Chung, Long Ke, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Osmanthus marginatus (Champ. ex Benth.) Hemsl. 厚邊木犀（月桂）
J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 26(173): 88. 1889; FKH 166. 1912; FHN 3: 211. 1974; FFJ 4: 369, fig. 301. 1989; FRPS 61: 87, pl. 23: 1 – 3. 1992; FOC 15: 288. 1996; FTW ed. 2, 4: 142. 1998; FGD 5: 416. 2003.
Olea marginata Champ. ex Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 4: 330 – 331. 1852; FHK 215. 1861.

Shrubs or trees, 5–15 m tall. Branchlets glabrous, compressed.
