Petiole 1.5–2.5 cm; leaf blade broadly elliptic to narrowly lanceolate, 5–15 × 2–5 cm, thick leathery, base broadly cuneate, apex acuminate, margin entire, rarely serrate, revolute; midvein and primary veins somewhat impressed adaxially and raised abaxially. Cymes in short panicles (ca. 2 cm), congested, axillary, 10 – 20‑flowered. Flowers dioecious, yellowish or greenish; pedicel 1–2 mm. Calyx 1.5–2 mm, 4‑lobed to middle; lobes broadly deltate, ciliate. Corolla 3.5–4.5 mm; lobes oblong, ciliate, revolute. Stamens attached near top of corolla tube; anther suborbicular, connective not elongate; abortive pistil hemispheric, 0.3–0.5 mm; abortive stamens short. Ovary subglobose, 1.5 mm; style slender, 3 mm; stigma 2‑lobed. Drupe elliptic or oblong, 1.8–3 × 1–1.5 cm, black when matured.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Sha Tin, Pak Tam Chung, Long Ke, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 2646, 2653; Y. W. Lam 289.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan.
Ecology: Forests, ravines. Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: Jun.–Dec.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: The type specimen (J. G. Champion 436, K) was collected by J. G. Champion near the top of the Waterfall in the Happy Valley between 1847 and 1850.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Shing Mun, Ho Chung, Tai Wai, Tai Po Kau, Yuen Tun Ha, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Osmanthus matsumuranus Hayata 牛矢果
J. Coll. Sci. Imp. Univ. Tokyo. 30(1): 192. 1911; FHN 3: 211, fig. 665. 1974; FFJ 4: 370, fig. 302. 1989; FRPS 61: 89, pl. 23: 4 – 5. 1992; FOC 15: 288. 1996; FTW ed. 2, 4: 142. 1998; FGD 5: 416. 2003.
Osmanthus obouatifolius H. T. Chang, Acta Sci. Nat. Univ. Sunyatsenia 1982(2): 12. 1982.
Osmanthus maximus H. T. Chang, Acta Sci. Nat. Univ. Sunyatsenia 1982(2): 8. 1982.

Shrubs or trees, to 2–15 m tall. Branchlets glabrous, compressed. Petiole 1.5–3 cm; leaf blade oblanceolate, 5–15(–19) × 2.5–4.5(–6) cm, thin leathery to papery, base cuneate, decurrent, apex acuminate, margin usually serrate on distal half, midvein and lateral veins adaxially impressed and abaxially raised. Cymes in short panicles, axillary, 1.5–2 cm, 10–30‑flowered; bracteoles deltate‑ovate, 1–2 mm. Flowers dioecious, white or yellowish. Calyx lobes ciliate. Corolla 3–4 mm, 4‑lobed to middle, ciliate; stamens attached near top of corolla‑tube; connective not elongate; abortive pistil oblate; abortive stamens 1 mm. Ovary ovoid, 1–1.5 mm; style slender, 3 mm; stigma capitate, 2‑lobed. Drupe 1.5–2.5 × 0.8–1.2 cm, elliptic, 6 – 8‑ribbed, purple to black when matured.

Locality: Shing Mun, Ho Chung, Tai Wai, Tai Po Kau, Yuen Tun Ha, Lantau Island. L. T. Lo 222; Y. S. Lau 811, 2878.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam, Laos, Cambodia, India.
Ecology: Forests and thickets. Flowering; May–Aug.; fruiting: Sep.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Osmanthus minor P. S. Green 小葉月桂
Notes Roy. Bot. Gard. Edinburgh 22(5): 465, pl. 13. 1958; FFJ 4: 371, fig. 303. 1989; FRPS 61: 91, pl. 23: 6. 1992; FOC 15: 289. 1996; FGD 5: 416. 2003.

Shrubs or small trees, to 2–5(–10) m tall. Branchlets glabrous. Petiole 1–2 cm, glabrous; leaf blade narrowly elliptic or narrowly obovate, 4.5–10 × 1.5–3.5 cm, thin leathery, glandular dotted, base cuneate, apex acuminate or caudate, margin entire; lateral veins 5–8 on each side of midvein, adaxially obscure, abaxially slightly raised. Cymes in short panicles, axillary, 1–1.5 cm, slender, 8–12‑flowered; bracts deltate, thick, hairy abaxially; bracteoles thin, broadly ovate to lanceolate, apex tipped, crested abaxially, ciliate. Flowers dioecious, yellowish; pedicels 2 mm. Calyx 1–1.5 mm; lobes 0.5–1 mm, ciliate. Corolla 3–3.5 mm, 4‑lobed to middle. Stamens attached near top of corolla‑tube; connective not elongate; abortive pistil oblate, 0.5 mm. Drupe 1.5–2 × 0.8–1.2 cm, elliptic or obovate, 6 – 8‑ribbed, black when matured.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Chuk Kok. S. P. Lau 104; Y. W. Lam 1407.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian.
Ecology: Forests in ravines. Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: Nov.–Dec.

Adenosma glutinosum (L.) Druce 毛麝香
Bot. Exch. Club Soc. Brit. Isles 3: 413. 1914; FHN 3: 500. 1974; FGD 4: 368. 2000; FRPS 18: 25. 1998.
Gerardia glutinosa L., Sp. Pl. 2: 611. 1753.
Digitalis sinensis Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 378. 1790.
Pterostigma grandiflorum Benth., Prodr. 10: 380. 1846; FHK 247. 1861.
Adenosma grandiflorum (Benth.) Dunn & Tutcher, FKH 185. 1912.

Herbs, 30–100 cm tall. Stems erect, purplish, terete or upper part slightly 4‑angulate, densely villous with eglandular and glandular hairs. Leaves opposite or upper ones alternate; petioles 3–20 mm; leaf blade lanceolate‑ovate to broadly ovate, 2–10 × 1–5 cm, base cuneate, truncate or subcordate, apex acute, margin irregularly serrate and sometimes double serrate. Flowers axillary and solitary or in leafy racemes apically on stems and branches. Bracts small. Pedicel 0.5–1.5 cm, elongating to 2 cm in fruit. Calyx 0.7–1.3 cm; lobes narrowly lanceolate. Corolla purple‑red to violet, 0.9–2.8 cm; lower lip 3(–4)‑lobed; upper lip ovate‑orbicular, apex truncate to emarginate. Anterior anthers with 1 fertile cell; posterior anthers with 2 fertile cells; styles gradually widened and narrowly winged. Capsules ovoid, 5–9 × 3–6 mm, 2‑grooved, apex beaked. Seeds brown to dark brown.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 561, 2026; Y. S. Lau 32.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong Guangxi, Yunnan, Jiangxi, Fujian; Cambodia, India, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Thailand, Vietnam, Oceania.
Ecology: Thickets, grasslands. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.

Adenosma indianum (Lour.) Merr. 球花毛麝香
Trans. Amer. Philos. Soc. n.s. 24(2): 351. 1935; FHN 3: 501. 1974; FGD 4: 369. 2000; FOC 18: 25. 1998.
Manulea indiana Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 386. 1790.
Pterostigma capitatum Benth., Scroph. Ind. 21. 1835; FHK 248. 1861.
Adenosma capicatum Benth. ex Hance, J. Bot. Linn. Soc. Bot. 13: 114. 1872; FKH 186. 1912.

Annual herbs, 20–60(–100) cm tall, wholly glandular hairy. Stems erect, branched. Petiole 2–6 mm; leaf blade ovate to narrowly elliptic, 1.5–4.5 × 0.5–1.2 cm, base broad‑cuneate or acute, apex obtuse, margin serrate. Inflorescences globose to cylindric spicate, 0.7–2 cm. Bracts narrowly ovate, forming an involucre at the base of spikes. Flowers sessile. Calyx 4–5 mm; lobes narrowly ovate to oblong‑lanceolate, 2–3 mm. Corolla pale purple to dark blue, ca. 6 mm, throat hairy; lower lip lobes equal, suborbicular, ca. 1 mm. Anterior anthers with 1 fertile cell; posterior anthers with 2 fertile cells. Ovary narrowly ovoid. Capsules ovoid, ca. 3 mm, 2‑grooved. Seeds yellow.

Locality: Fanling. W. J. Tutcher 8396, 11236; HK sheet 20396.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan, Yunnan; Cambodia, India, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, Philippines, Sikkim, Thailand, Vietnam.
Ecology: Grassy hillslopes. Flowering & fruiting: Sep.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Antirrhinum majus L. 金魚草
Sp. Pl. 617. 1753; D. A. Webb in T. G. Tutin & V. H. Heywood, Fl. Europ. 3: 223. 1972.

Perennial herbs. Stems up to 150 cm, erect or straggling, glabrous. Leaves linear to ovate, 10–70 × 1–25 mm, base distinctly cuneate. Inflorescence glabrous or glandular‑pubescent. Pedicels 2–10 mm. Bracts ovate, 2–10 mm. Calyx‑lobes ovate‑oblong to suborbicular, 6–8 mm. Corolla usually pink or purple, 3–4.5 cm. Capsules oblong, 10 – 14 mm, glandular‑pubescent or glabrous.

Locality: Cultivated. K. Y. Chan 1428 (CUHK); S. Y. Hu 9646 (CUHK); H. T. Shun 28 (CUHK).
Distribution: Native to Mediterranean region, widely cultivated.
Ecology: Flowering: Summer to autumn.
Uses: Ornamental (aquarium).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Long Wan, Sha Tin, Plover Cove, Lai Chi Wo, Luk Keng, Kat O
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Bacopa monnieri (L.) Pennell 假馬齒莧
Proc. Acad. Nat. Sci. Philadelphia 98: 94. 1946; FOC 18: 21. 1998.
Lysimachia monnieri L., Cent. Pl. II, 2: 9. 1756.
Bacopa monnieri (L.) Wettst., Nat. Pflanzenfam. IV(3b): 77. 1891, nom. illeg.; FHN 3: 498. 1974; FRPS 67(2): 87. 1979; FGD 4: 383. 2000; Check List HK Plants 244. 2002; 84. 2004.
Herpestis monnieri Kunth, Nov. Gen. Sp. (quarto ed.) 2: 366. 1818; FHK 249. 1861; FKH 187. 1912.

Herbs creeping; stems ± succulent, glabrous. Leaves sessile, oblong‑oblanceolate, 0.8–2 cm × 3–6 mm, apex rounded, margin entire or rarely dentate. Flowers axillary; pedicels 0.5–3.5 cm. Bracteoles 2, linear. Sepals 5, ca. 5 mm, unequal. Corolla blue, purple, or white, 8–10 mm, obscurely 2‑lipped. Stamens didynamous. Stigma capitate. Capsules narrowly ovoid, enveloped in persistent calyx. Seeds yellow‑brown, ellipsoidal, truncate at one end, longitudinally striate.

Locality: Tai Long Wan, Sha Tin, Plover Cove, Lai Chi Wo, Luk Keng, Kat O. Y. S. Lau 1994, 2150, 3118.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; widespread in tropics and subtropics.
Ecology: Wet places. Flowering: May–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Mong Tsai, Sai Keng, Tsiu Hang, Peng Chau, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Bacopa repens (Sw.) Wettst. 田玄參
Nat. Pflanzenfam. IV(3b):76. 1895; FOC 18: 22. 1998.
Gratiola repens Sw., Prodr. 14. 1788.
Sinobacopa aquatica D. Y. Hong, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 25(5): 395. 1987.

Herbs creeping. Stems succulent, rooting at nodes. Leaves sessile, obovate to obovate‑lanceolate, 1.2–2.5 × 0.7– 1.3 cm, margin entire. Flowers axillary, pendulous; pedicels 1–2 cm. Bracteoles absent. Sepals 4 or 5, 3 – 4 mm, unequal, margin ciliate. Corolla white, almost as long as sepals; lobes obovate; upper lip lobed to middle, lobes narrowly obovate. Stamens equal in length, ca. 1.2 mm, inserted at throat; filaments as long as anthers. Anthers ± sagittate. Stigma 2‑parted. Capsules globose, ca. 1.7 mm in diam. Seeds columnar‑oblong, ca. 0.5 mm; testa reticulate.

Locality: Tai Mong Tsai, Sai Keng, Tsiu Hang, Peng Chau, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 1443; Y. W. Lam 982, 2227.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian; N & S America.
Ecology: Wet places, watersides. Flowering: Jul.–Aug.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Ta Kwu Ling, Kong Nga Po
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Buchnera cruciata Buch.‑Ham. ex D. Don 黑草（鬼羽箭）
Prodr. Fl. Nepal. 91. 1825; FHK 253. 1861; FKH 190. 1912; FOC 18: 88. 1998; FGD 4: 392. 2000.

Herbs 8–50 cm tall, with curved hairs. Stems simple or apically somewhat branched. Basal leaves rosulate; petioles inconspicuous; leaf blade obovate, 2–2.5 × 1–1.5 cm, base tapering. Stem leaves sessile, linear to linear‑oblong, 1.5–4.5 × 0.3–0.5(–1.2) cm, margin often with 2–few obtuse teeth. Spikes terminal, cylindric to subquadrangular, 1–4.5 cm, lengthening to 6.5 cm in fruit. Bracts ovate, ca. 4.8 × 2.5 mm, densely villous; bracteoles linear, 2–3 mm, villous. Calyx 4–4.5 mm, villous; tube slightly curved; lobes triangular, subequal. Corolla blue‑purple, narrowly tubular, somewhat curved, 6–7 mm, somewhat ribbed, villous on portion exserted from calyx, throat constricted; lobes obovate to oblanceolate, 1.5–2 × ca. 1 mm. Anthers ca. 1 mm. Ovary ovoid, 2–2.5 mm. Capsules oblong, ca. 5 mm. Seeds ± spirally striate.

Locality: Ta Kwu Ling, Kong Nga Po. L. T. Lo 256; P. S. Choi 78; Y. W. Lam 2011.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Fujian; S & SE Asia.
Ecology: Hillslopes, wastelands. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Jan. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Wan Chai, Mount Violet, Ma On Shan, Yung Shue O
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Centranthera cochinchinensis (Lour.) Merr. 胡麻草
Trans. Amer. Philos. Soc. 24(2): 353. 1935; FHN 3: 512. 1974; FOC 18: 85. 1998; FGD 4: 395. 2000.
Digitalis cochinchinensis Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 378. 1790.
Centranthera hispida auct. non. R. Br.: FHK 254. 1861; FKH 190. 1912.
Centranthera brunoniana auct. non Wall.: FKH 190. 1912; FGZ 592. 1956.

Herbs, (13–)30–60 cm tall. Stems erect, simple or few‑branched, hispid. Leaves opposite, rarely alternate, sessile, linear‑lanceolate, 2–3 cm × 3–4 mm, margin entire and subrevolute, hispid on both surfaces. Bracts shorter than or rarely as long as corolla. Flowers borne above middle of stem. Calyx spathaceous, 7–10 mm, densely hispid, apex shallowly 3‑lobed. Corolla reddish white with yellow stripes, 3.5–4 cm; lower lip 3‑lobed, orbicular, upper lip orbicular, 2‑lobed. Stamens 4, filaments woolly. Ovary glabrous. Capsules ovoid, 4–8 mm, apex mucronate. Seeds yellow, small, spirally striate.

Locality: Wan Chai, Mount Violet, Ma On Shan, Yung Shue O. Y. S. Lau 2787, 3260; Y. W. Lam 423.
Distribution: Areas S of Changjiang; tropical Asia, Australia.
Ecology: Grassy hillslopes. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Oct.

Centranthera tranquebarica (Spreng.) Merr. ex Merr. & Chun 矮胡麻草
Sunyatsenia 5: 182. 1940; FOC 18: 85. 1998; FGD 4: 395, fig. 239. 2000.
Razumovia tranquebarica Spreng., Mant. Prim. Fl. Hal. 45. 1807.
Centranthera tonkinensis Bonati, Not. Syst. Lecomte 1: 337. 1911; FGD 4: 395. 2000.
Centranthera humifusa Wall., Scroph. Ind. 50. 1835; Rep. Bot. & Forest. Dep. Hongk. (1916) 22. 1917.

Herbs, 5–30 cm tall. Stems erect or prostrate, slender, branched from base. Leaves linear‑lanceolate, 8–25 × 2– 3 mm, glabrous on both surfaces or abaxially short hairy. Bracts longer than corolla. Calyx ovate, ca. 3 mm at anthesis, hispidulous. Corolla yellow, brown striate, 9–13 mm; throat densely black punctate; lower lip lobes suboblong, ca. 3 mm; upper lip lobes suborbicular, 3 × 2 mm. Stamens 2–5 mm; filaments white lanose‑villous. Ovary oblong, 3 × 2.5 mm, glabrous. Capsules subglobose, 4–5 × ca. 4 mm, as long as persistent calyx. Seeds yellow, cylindric‑conical, ca. 1 mm; testa reticulate.

Locality: Shau Kei Wan, Fanling. W. J. Tutcher 11444; HK sheet 39461.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian; tropical Asia.
Ecology: Grasslands, roadsides. Flowering & fruiting: Sep.–Oct.

Dopatrium junceum (Roxb.) Buch.‑Ham. ex Benth. 虻眼
Scroph. Ind. 31. 1835; FHK 249. 1861; FKH 187. 1912; FHN 3: 499. 1974; FOC 18: 23. 1998; FGD 4: 397. 2000.

Annual herbs, to 50 cm tall. Stems succulent, erect, many‑branched from base. Branches slender, longitudinally striate, glabrous. Leaves sometimes scale‑like, gradually decreasing in size upward, sessile, lanceolate to subspatulate‑lanceolate, to 2 cm, base amplexicaul and generally narrowly attenuate, apex acute to ± obtuse, margin entire. Flowers solitary and axillary. Pedicels slender, to 1 cm. Calyx campanulate, ca. 2 mm, 5‑lobed. Corolla white, rose, or pale purple, ca. 5 mm; lower lip spreading flat; upper lip erect, short. Fertile stamens 2, staminodes 2. Capsules globose, ca. 2 mm in diam. Seeds ovoid‑oblong; testa reticulate.

Locality: East Point. W. J. Tutcher 1341.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Shaanxi, Henan, Jiangxi, Jiangsu, Taiwan; Japan, India, SE Asia, Australia.
Ecology: Marshy grounds. Flowering: Jun.–Oct.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Aberdeen, Tai Au Mun, Sai Kung (Sai Wan), Tsing Fai Tong, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Limnophila aromatica (Lam.) Merr. 紫蘇草
Interpr. Rumph. Herb. Amb. 466. 1917; FHN 3: 502. 1974; FOC 18: 27. 1998; FGD 4: 368. 2000.
Ambulia aromatica Lam., Encycl. Meth. 1: 123. 1783.
Limnophila punctata Blume, Bijdr. Fl. Ned. Ind. 14. 750. 1826; FHK 248. 1861.
Limnophila gratissima Blume, Bijdr. Fl. Ned. Ind. 14. 749. 1826; FKH 186. 1912.

Annual herbs or perennial. Stems 30–70 cm tall, simple to many‑branched, glabrous or glandular, base decumbent and rooting from nodes. Leaves opposite or in whorls of 3, sessile, ovate‑lanceolate to lanceolate‑elliptic, 1–5 × 0.3–1.5 cm, base semiamplexicaul, margin crenate and serrate; veins pinnate. Flowers solitary in leaf axils or in terminal racemes. Pedicel 0.5–2 cm, glabrous or glandular. Bracteoles linear to linear‑lanceolate, 1.5–2 mm. Calyx 4–6 mm, glabrous or glandular pubescent, with raised veins in fruit. Corolla white, blue‑purple or pink, 1–1.3 cm, sparsely and finely glandular, white villous adaxially; styles apex dilated. Capsules ovoid, ca. 6 mm.

Locality: Aberdeen, Tai Au Mun, Sai Kung (Sai Wan), Tsing Fai Tong, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 2528, 2957; Y. W. Lam 1215.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; tropical Asia, Australia.
Ecology: Wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Sep.–Feb. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: A morphologically similar form was described as Limnophila aromaticoides Yang & Yen (擬紫蘇草; Bot. Bull. Acad. Sinica 38: 285 – 295. 1997), which could be distinguished by its verticillate submerged leaves, white corolla with occasional pinkish colour at top of tube, and orbicularly ellipsoidal capsule; whereas L. aromatica, in strict sense, is characterized by its submerged leaves mostly lacking corolla (occasionally with 2 – 3 submerged leaves), pink or purple corolla and ellipsoidal capsule. This form is observed in Hong Kong growing and flowering together with L. aromatica. Other authorities, however, considered the distinguishing characters of L. aromaticoides fell within the range of variation of L. aromatica and therefore put in the synonymy of the latter (e.g. FOC 18: 28. 1998).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Shing Mun, Tai Mo Shan, Sai Kung (Tai Wan)
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Limnophila chinensis (Osbeck) Merr. 中華石龍尾
Amer. J. Bot. 3: 581. 1916; FHN 3: 503. 1974; FOC 18: 28. 1998; FGD 4: 365. 2000.
Columnea chinensis Osbeck, Dagb. Ostind. Resa 230. 1757.
Limnophila hirsuta (Heyne ex Benth.) Benth., Prodr. 10: 388. 1848; FHK 248. 1861; FKH 186. 1912.
Stemodia hirsuta Heyne ex Benth., Scroph. Ind. 24. 1835.

Herbs, 5–50 cm tall. Stems basally prostrate, rooting from nodes, simple or basally branched, villous or subglabrous. Leaves opposite or in whorls of 3 or 4, sessile, ovate‑lanceolate, linear‑lanceolate, or rarely spatulate, 0.5–5.3 × 0.2–1.5 cm, base subamplexicaul, margin serrate, abaxially villous along veins, adaxially glabrous or sparsely villous; veins pinnate, inconspicuous. Flowers solitary in leaf axils, or in terminal panicles. Pedicel 3–5 mm, villous to subglabrous. Bracteoles ca. 2 mm. Calyx 5–7 mm, villous or subglabrous, with raised veins in fruit. Corolla purple‑red, blue, or rarely white, 1–1.5 cm. Capsules compressed, broadly ellipsoidal, ca. 5 mm.

Locality: Shing Mun, Tai Mo Shan, Sai Kung (Tai Wan). C. G. Matthew 5230; HK sheet 35392, 37908.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; tropical Asia, Australia.
Ecology: Wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Oct.–Mar. of the following year.

Limnophila heterophylla (Roxb.) Benth. 異葉石龍尾
Scroph. Ind. 25. 1835; FKH 186. 1912; FOC 18: 27. 1998; FGD 4: 366. 2000.
Columnea heterophylla Roxb., Fl. Ind. 3: 97. 1832.

Perennial herbs, aquatic or mesic. Aerial stems with sessile glands, pilose or nearly glabrous. Submerged leaves to 50 cm, multiparted; segments capillary. Aerial leaves opposite or whorled, oblanceolate or oblong, ca. 15 × 3 mm, base subamplexicaul, apex obtuse, margin subcrenate, glabrous, veins 3–5, parallel. Flowers sessile, in terminal spikes, or shortly pedicellate and solitary in leaf axils. Bracteoles absent. Calyx ca. 3 mm, with sessile glands, without raised veins in fruit. Corolla pale purple or pink, ca. 5 mm, glabrous. Capsules pale brown, subglobose, ca. 2.5 mm.

Locality: Wong Nai Chung, Fanling. W. J. Tutcher 8156; HK sheet 4120, 20427.
Distribution: Guangdong, Jiangxi, Taiwan; tropical Asia.
Ecology: Margins of ponds. Flowering: Apr.–Nov.

Limnophila rugosa (Roth) Merr. 大葉石龍尾
Interpr. Rumph. Herb. Amb. 466. 1917; FHN 3: 502. 1974 ; FOC 18: 27. 1998; FGD 4: 367. 2000.
Herpestis rugosa Roth, Nov. Pl. Sp. 290. 1821.
Limnophila roxburghii auct. non. G. Don: Dunn & Tutcher, FKH 186. 1912.

Perennial herbs, 10–15 cm tall, with horizontal rhizomes. Stems 1 – few, ± fasciculate, erect or ascending, usually unbranched, glabrous. Leaves opposite; petiole 1–2 cm, narrowly winged; leaf‑blade ovate, rhomboid‑elliptic, or elliptic, 3–9 × 1–5 cm, margin crenate, abaxially hispidulous along veins, adaxially glabrous or sparsely hispidulous, veins pinnate, ca. 10 on each side of midvein. Peduncles 0.2–3 cm. Bracts subspatulate‑oblong, with flattened glands, margin entire or apically undulate‑toothed and ciliate. Flowers sessile, 5–10 congested on apex of axillary short branches, usually appearing a head. Bracteoles absent. Calyx 6–8 mm, smooth, in fruiting time with 5 raised veins and flattened glands. Corolla purple‑red to blue, to 1.6 cm; styles slender, pubescent, with a membranous auricle on both sides. Capsules pale brown, ovoid, ca. 5 mm.

Locality: Aberdeen, Lantau Island. HK sheet 4122, 20440.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Yunnan, Hunan, Fujian, Taiwan; tropical Asia.
Ecology: Grasslands, streamsides. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Limnophila sessiliflora (Vahl) Blume 石龍尾
Bijdr. Fl. Ned. Ind. 749. 1826; FKH 186. 1912; FOC 18: 26. 1998; FGD 4: 365. 2000.
Hottonia sessiliflora Vahl, Symb. Bot. 2: 36. 1791.

Herbs aquatic or terrestrial. Submerged stems slender and long, glabrous or subglabrous. Aerial stems 6–40 cm, simple or sparsely branched, hairy or rarely subglabrous. Submerged leaves 0.5–3.5 cm, multiparted; segments flattened or capillary. Aerial leaves whorled, blade elliptic‑lanceolate, 5–18 × 3–4 mm, glabrous, densely glandular punctate, margin crenate to lobed; veins 1–3. Flowers sessile or rarely with a pedicel to 1.5 mm, solitary in axils of submerged and aerial leaves. Bracteoles absent or rarely present and to 1.5 mm. Calyx 4–6 mm, hairy, without raised veins in fruit; lobes ovate, 2–4 mm, apex narrowly acuminate. Corolla purple‑blue to reddish, 6–10 mm. Capsules compressed, subglobose.

Locality: Fanling. HK sheet 20433.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Henan, Liaoning, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian; Korea, Japan, India, Nepal, Bhutan, Vietnam, Malaysia, Indonesia.
Ecology: Wet places, margins of ponds. Flowering: Apr.–Nov.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Lindernia anagallis (Burm. f.) Pennell 長蒴母草（長果母草）
J. Arnold Arbor. 24(3): 252. 1943; FHN 3: 506. 1974; FOC 18: 35. 1998; FGD 4: 389. 2000.
Ruellia anagallis Burm. f., Fl. Ind. 135. 1768.
Lindernia cordifolia (Colsm.) Merr., Enum. Philipp. Fl. Pl. 3: 437. 1923; FGZ 598. 1956.
Gratiola cordifolia Colsm., Prodr. Desc. Grat. 15. 1793.
Vandellia pedunculata Benth., Scroph. Ind. 37. 1835, & DC., Prodr. 10: 416. 1846; FKH 188. 1912.

Annual herbs, 10–40 cm. Stems creeping, striate, glabrous, rooting from nodes. Leaves shortly petiolate to subsessile; leaf blade triangular‑ovate, ovate, or oblong, 0.4–2 × 0.7–1.2 cm, base truncate to subcordate, apex rounded to acute, margin shallowly crenate. Flowers axillary, solitary. Pedicels 6–10 mm, to 2 cm in fruit. Calyx ca. 5 mm, basally connate; lobes lanceolate. Corolla white or light purple, 0.8–1.2 cm; lower lip slightly longer than upper lip, spreading flat, 3‑lobed, lobes subequal; upper lip ovate, 2‑lobed, filaments of anterior stamens basally with a clavate appendage, stigma 2‑lobed. Capsules linear‑ovoid, ca. 2 times as long as persistent calyx. Seeds ovoid, tuberculate.

Locality: Aberdeen, Tai Wai, Chuen Lung, Tai Po, Fanling, Sai Kung. H. C. Tang 2473; Y. S. Lau 2260; HK sheet 4130.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; S & SE Asia, Australia.
Ecology: Margins of forests, streamsides, wet places. Flowering: Apr.–Sep.; fruiting: Jun.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Lindernia antipoda (L.) Alston 泥花草
Handb. Fl. Ceyl. 6 (Suppl.): 214. 1931; FHN 3: 508. 1974; FOC 18: 36. 1998; FGD 4: 389. 2000.
Ruellia antipoda L., Sp. Pl. 635. 1753.
Bonnaya veronicifolia (Retz.) Spreng., Syst. Veg. 41. 1824; FHK 252. 1861; FKH 189. 1912.

Annual herbs, to 30 cm tall. Stems suberect or prostrate basally, many‑branched, channeled. Petiole short and wide; leaf blade oblong, oblong‑lanceolate, or linear‑lanceolate, 0.8–4 × 0.6–2 cm, base cuneate and decurrent, apex acute to rounded, margin obscurely to sharply serrate or subentire. Racemes terminal, to 15 cm, 2– 20‑flowered. Pedicels to 1.5 cm, ascending, spreading, to deflexed in fruit. Calyx lobed to base; lobes lanceolate, hispidulous along midvein and edges. Corolla purple, purplish white, or white, to 1 cm; tube to 7 mm; lower lip 3‑lobed, lobes subequal; upper lip 2‑lobed. Fertile stamens 2, posterior; filaments unappendaged. Reduced stamens 2, anterior; filaments slightly curved, glandular, stigma 2‑lamellate. Capsules cylindric, 2 times or more as long as persistent calyx. Seeds brown, irregularly triangular‑ovoid; testa reticulate.

Locality: Happy Valley, Shing Mun, Sha Tin, Fanling, Tai Lam Chung, Sai Kung, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 2529, 2548; Y. W. Lam 1216.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Margins of forests, streamsides, wet places or farmlands. Flowering & fruiting: Spring to autumn.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Lindernia ciliata (Colsm.) Pennell 刺齒泥花草
Brittonia 2: 182. 1936; FHN 3: 508. 1974; FOC 18: 36. 1998; FGD 4: 390. 2000.
Gratiola ciliata Colsm., Prodr. Desc. Grat. 14. 1793.
Bonnaya brachiata Link & Otto, Icon. Pl. Select. 25, pl. 11. 1820; FKH 189. 1912.
Ilysanthes serrata (Roxb.) Urban, Ber. Deutsch. Bot. Ges. 2: 436. 1884; FGZ 602. 1956.
Gratiola serrata Roxb., Fl. Ind. ed. Carey & Wall. 1: 139. 1820.

Annual herbs, to 20 cm tall. Stems diffuse, many‑branched. Branches decumbent. Leaves sessile or short petiolate; leaf blade oblong to lanceolate‑oblong, 0.7–4.5 × 0.3–1.2 cm, glabrous, base amplexicaul, apex acute to obtuse, margin densely aristate‑serrate. Racemes terminal. Bracts lanceolate, ca. 1/2 as long as pedicels. Calyx ca. 5 mm, lobed to base; lobes narrowly lanceolate, with a spine‑like tip. Corolla light purple or white, ca. 7 mm; tube to 4.5 mm; lower lip almost as long as upper lip, often unequally 3‑lobed, middle lobe larger than other lobes; upper lip ovate. Fertile stamens 2, posterior; sterile stamens 2, anterior, forming prominent plaits on base of lower lip. Capsules cylindric, ca. 3 times as long as persistent calyx, apex mucronate. Seeds irregularly triangular.

Locality: Aberdeen, Fanling. W. J. Tutcher 9599; Y. W. Lam 1076; HK sheet 4135.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Xizang, Fujian, Taiwan; tropical Asia, Australia.
Ecology: Margins of forests, wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Sep.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Kwai Chung, Shing Mun, Tsiu Hang, Ta Kwu Ling, Peng Chau, Lantau Island, Ping Chau
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Lindernia crustacea (L.) F. Muell. 母草
Syst. Census Austral. Pl. 1: 97. 1882; FHN 3: 507. 1974; FOC 18: 32. 1998; FGD 4: 388. 2000.
Capraria crustacea L., Mant. Pl. 1: 87. 1767.
Vandellia crustacea (L.) Benth., Scroph. Ind. 35. 1835; FHK 251. 1861; FKH 188. 1912.

Annual herbs, 10–20 cm tall, many‑branched. Branches widely spreading, subquadrangular, deeply sulcate, glabrous. Petioles 1–8 mm; leaf blade triangular‑ovate to broadly ovate, 1–2 × 0.5–1.1 cm, base broadly cuneate to rounded, apex obtuse to subacute, margin shallowly crenate to serrate, abaxially pilose along veins to subglabrous, adaxially subglabrous. Flowers axillary and solitary. Pedicels slender, 0.5–2.2 cm, subglabrous. Calyx 3–5 mm, 5‑toothed, often splitting into 5 lobes after anthesis, outside sparsely pubescent. Corolla purple, 5–8 mm; tube slightly longer than calyx; lower lip 3‑lobed, middle lobe larger and slightly longer than upper lip; upper lip ovate, sometimes shallowly 2‑lobed. Stamens didynamous, styles fugacious. Capsules broadly ellipsoidal, almost as long as persistent calyx. Seeds pale yellow‑brown, subglobose, scrobiculate.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Kwai Chung, Shing Mun, Tsiu Hang, Ta Kwu Ling, Peng Chau, Lantau Island, Ping Chau. Y. W. Lam 840, 1075, 2541.
Distribution: Areas S of Changjiang, Henan; a common weed widely distributed in tropical and subtropical regions of the world.
Ecology: Moist areas, rice fields, grasslands. Flowering & fruiting: May–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Lindernia hyssopioides (L.) Haines 尖果母草
Bot. Bilhar Orissa 4: 666. 1922; FHN 3: 509. 1974; FOC 18: 37. 1998; FGD 4: 387. 2000.
Gratiola hyssopioides L., Mant. Pl. 174. 1771.
Bonnaya hyssopoides (L.) Benth., Scroph. Ind. 34. 1835.
Ilysanthes hyssopoides (L.) Benth., Prodr. 10: 419. 1846; FHK 252. 1861; FKH 188. 1912.

Herbs, to 30 cm tall. Stems erect or somewhat ascending, simple, striate. Leaves sessile, subamplexicaul, narrowly ovate to ovate‑lanceolate, 5–15 × ca. 4 mm, margin entire or with 2 or 3 pairs of inconspicuous small teeth, veins 3, parallel. Flowers in axils of upper leaves, solitary. Pedicels 0.5–3 cm, slender, ascending in flower, spreading to reflexed after flowering. Calyx ca. 3 mm, lobed to base; lobes lanceolate. Corolla red, purple, or white, with 2 convex lines at throat, 0.9–1.1 cm; lower lip 3‑lobed, lobes subequal; upper lip deeply 2‑lobed, lobes narrowly triangular‑ovate. Fertile stamens 2, posterior; staminodes 2, anterior; filaments short, divided, styles apex 2‑lamellate. Capsules linear‑ovoid, ca. 6 mm, 2 times as long as persistent calyx. Seeds yellow‑brown, oblong, obscurely ribbed.

Locality: Hong Kong Island. Y. S. Lau 2750; HK sheet 4134.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Yunnan; Vietnam, India to Indonesia.
Ecology: Wet places. Flowering & fruiting: May–Oct.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Shing Mun, Plover Cove, Tung Chung
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Lindernia micrantha D. Don 狹葉母草
Prodr. Fl. Nepal. 85. 1825; FOC 18: 35. 1998.
Lindernia angustifolia (Benth.) Wettst., Nat. Pflanzenfam. 4(3b): 79. 1891; FHN 3: 507. 1974; FRPS 67(2): 141. 1979; FGD 4: 388. 2000; Check List HK Plants 246. 2002; 85. 2004.
Vandellia angustifolia Benth., Scroph. Ind. 37. 1835; FKH 188. 1912.

Annual herbs, to 40 cm tall. Stems usually erect, branches ascending, glabrous. Leaves sessile, linear to linear‑lanceolate, 1–4 cm × 2–8 mm, margin entire or somewhat irregularly serrate, glabrous. Flowers solitary, axillary. Pedicels to 3.5 cm in fruit. Calyx to 4 mm in fruit, lobed to base; lobes lanceolate. Corolla purple, blue purple, or white, ca. 6.5 mm, lower lip slightly longer than upper lip, spreading flat, 3‑lobed; upper lip 2‑lobed. Filaments of anterior stamens with a linear appendage; posterior anthers with connective of lower locule produced into a long tail. Capsules linear, to 1.4 cm, more than 3 times as long as persistent calyx. Seeds brownish, oblong.

Locality: Shing Mun, Plover Cove, Tung Chung. L. T. Lo 305; Y. W. Lam 1534, 1580.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hunan, Hubei, Henan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Fujian; Japan, Vietnam, Korea, Laos, Cambodia, Indonesia, Myanmar, India, Nepal, Sri Lanka.
Ecology: Farmlands, wet places along streams. Flowering: May – Oct.; fruiting: Jul. – Nov.

Lindernia oblonga (Benth.) Merr. & Chun 棱萼母草
Sunyatsenia 5: 180. 1940; FHN 3: 507. 1974; FOC 18: 32. 1998; FGD 4: 388. 2000.
Vandellia oblonga Benth., Scroph. Ind. 35. 1835; FHK 251. 1861; Hance, Ann. Sci. Nat. ser. 4, 15: 227. 1861.
Torenia oblonga Hance ex Maxim., Mel. Biol. 9: 411. 1875; FKH 187. 1912.

Perennial herbs. Stems erect or sometimes procumbent and ascending, subquadrangular, median internodes to 6 cm. Leaves short petiolate below, sessile and subamplexicaul above; leaf blade rhomboid‑ovate to rhomboid‑lanceolate, 5 – 20 × 3 – 8 mm, base broadly cuneate, apex subacute to rounded, margin often with few irregular undulate sinuses or small teeth, or entire. Racemes lax, usually less then 10‑flowered; bracts lanceolate. Pedicels slender, 0.7 – 2.5 cm. Calyx narrowly campanulate, lobed to 1/4 length; lobes triangular‑ovate, apex acute and recurved, midvein evident. Corolla purple to purple‑blue, to 1.3 cm or more; tube ca 7 mm; lower lip 3‑lobed; upper lip 2‑lobed, stigma broadly 2‑lamellate. Capsules ellipsoidal, shorter than persistent calyx. Seeds numerous.

Locality: Cape D'Aguilar, Tai Long Sai Wan, Long Ke, Beaufort Island, Lamma Island. S. P. Lau 157; Y. W. Lam 782, 1031.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong; Vietnam, Laos, Cambodia.
Ecology: Sandy soil. Flowering & fruiting: May–Sep.

Lindernia procumbens (Krock.) Borbás 陌上菜
Békés Vámegye 80. 1881; FOC 18: 32. 2002.
Anagalloides procumbens Krock., Fl. Siles. 2(1): 398, pl. 26. 1790.
Lindernia procumbens (Krock.) Philcok, Taxon 14: 30. 1965; FGD 4: 389. 2000; Check List HK Plants 247. 2002; 85. 2004.

Herbs erect, caespitose, 5–20 cm tall, basally many‑branched. Leaves sessile; leaf blade elliptic or oblong, somewhat rhomboid, 1–2.5 × 0.6–1.2 cm, apex obtuse to rounded, margin entire or weakly obtusely toothed. Flower axillary, solitary. Pedicels slender, 1.2–2 cm, longer than subtending leaf. Calyx lobed almost to base; lobes linear‑lanceolate, ca. 4 mm, outside sparsely pubescent. Corolla pink to purple, 5–7 mm, tube ca. 3.5 mm; lower lip ca. 3 mm, 3‑lobed, middle lobe rounded and longer than other lobes, upper lip ca. 1 mm, 2‑lobed. Stamens 4, all fertile; filaments of anterior stamens with a small glandular appendage; stigma 2‑lobed. Capsules globose to ovoid‑globose, as long as or slightly longer than persistent calyx. Seeds oblong, testa reticulate.

Locality: Chuen Lung, Pak Nai, Sheung Shui, Ta Kwu Ling, Peng Chau. L. T. Lo 258; Y. W. Lam 390, 998.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; Asia, S Europe.
Ecology: Wet places along streams. Flowering: Jul.–Oct.; fruiting: Sep.–Nov.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Aberdeen, Sha Tin, Shing Mun, Fung Yuen, Mui Tsz Lam, Ho Chung, Tai O
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Lindernia pusilla (Willd.) Bold. 細莖母草
Zakfl. Java 165. 1916; FHN 3: 505. 1974; FOC 18: 33. 1998; FGD 4: 386. 2000.
Gratiola pusilla Willd., Sp. Pl. 1: 105. 1797.
Vandellia scabra Benth., Scroph. Ind. 36. 1835; FHK 251. 1861; FKH 188. 1912; Philcox, Kew Bull. 22: 41. 1968.

Annual herbs, 6–30 cm tall, sometimes long stoloniferous. Stems suberect, subglabrous or hairy, densely coarsely hairy on nodes. Leaves shortly petiolate below, sessile above; leaf blade ovate, cordate, or occasionally orbicular, to 1.2 cm, sparsely covered with appressed coarse hairs, base cuneate to subcordate, margin subcrenate or entire. Inflorescences terminal, subumbellate‑racemose, 3–5‑flowered. Pedicels slender, 0.8–1.5 cm. Calyx deeply lobed; lobes lanceolate, coarsely hairy outside. Corolla purple, ca. 9 mm; lower lip ca. 5.5 mm, much longer than upper lip; upper lip broadly ovate, emarginate; filaments of anterior stamens slender, base geniculate, stigma 2‑lamellate. Capsules ovoid‑globose, almost as long as persistent calyx. Seeds oblong, tuberculate.

Locality: Aberdeen, Sha Tin, Shing Mun, Fung Yuen, Mui Tsz Lam, Ho Chung, Tai O. Y. S. Lau 2749; Y. W. Lam 519, 875.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Taiwan; India to Malaysia, Africa.
Ecology: Margins of forests, wet places. Flowering & fruiting: May–Sep.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Fung Yuen, Ng Tung Chai, Plover Cove
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Lindernia ruellioides (Colsm.) Pennell 旱田草
Brittonia 2: 182. 1936; FHN 3: 509. 1974; FOC 18: 36. 1998; FGD 4: 390. 2000.
Gratiola ruellioides Colsm., Prodr. Desc. Grat. 12. 1793.

Annual herbs, 10–15 cm tall; stolons to 30 cm. Stems usually branched, subglabrous, rooting from nodes. Petioles 0.3–2 cm; leaf blade oblong, elliptic, ovate‑oblong or orbicular, 1–4 × 0.6–2 cm, scabrous, pubescent to subglabrous, base subamplexicaul or broadly cuneate, apex obtuse to acute, margin above base densely and regularly acute‑serrate. Racemes terminal, 2–10‑flowered; bracts lanceolate‑linear. Pedicels short, distally gradually thicker, glabrous. Calyx ca. 6 mm, to 10 mm in fruit, base connate; lobes linear‑lanceolate, glabrous. Corolla purple‑red, 1–1.4 cm; tube 7–9 mm; lower lip 3‑lobed, lobes subequal or middle lobe slightly larger than other lobes; upper lip 2‑lobed. Fertile stamens 2, posterior, without appendages; sterile stamens 2, anterior; stigma flattened. Capsules conical, ca. 2 times as long as persistent calyx. Seeds brown, ellipsoidal.

Locality: Fung Yuen, Ng Tung Chai, Plover Cove. Y. S. Lau 2513; Y. W. Lam 887; HK sheet 40248.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; India to Indonesia, Philippines.
Ecology: Wet places, streamsides. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Mazus pumilus (Burm. f.) Steenis 通泉草
Nova Guinea n. s. 9(1): 31. 1958; FOC 18: 46. 1998.
Lobelia pumilus Burm. f., Fl. Ind. 186. 1768.
Mazus japonicus (Thunb.) Kuntze, Rev. Gen. 2: 462. 1891; FRPS. 67(2): 187. 1979; FGD 4: 372. 2000.
Lindernia japonica Thunb., Fl. Jap. 253. 1784.
Mazus rugosus Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 385. 1790; FHK 247. 1861; FKH 185. 1912.

Annual herbs, erect or decumbent, 10–20 cm tall, glabrous or sparsely pubescent. Stems few, few‑branched, rooting from prostrate nodes. Basal leaves rosulate, caducous; leaf blade spatulate to oblanceolate, 2–6 × 1–1.3 cm, base decurrent, margin dentate or lobed; stem leaves opposite or few alternate, usually smaller. Racemes terminal, usually 3–10‑flowered, laxly flowered. Pedicels 5–12 mm. Calyx campanulate, 3–8 mm, not enlarged in fruit; lobes ovate, as long as tube. Corolla white, purple or blue, 1–1.2 cm; lower lip 3‑lobed, middle lobe smaller than lateral lobes, obovate; upper lip 2‑lobed, lobes ovate. Ovary glabrous. Capsules globose, ca. 3 mm in diam.

Locality: Tai Wai, Tai Lam Chung, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 822; L. T. Lo 529; Y. W. Lam 840.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; Russia, Korea, Japan, Vietnam, Philippines.
Ecology: Wet grasslands, wastelands, margins of forests. Flowering & fruiting: Feb.–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Sha Tin, Tsiu Hang, Wu Kau Tang, Fanling
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Microcarpaea minima (K. D. Koenig ex Retz.) Merr. 小果草
Philipp. J. Sci. 7(2): 100. 1912; FOC 18: 49. 2000; FGD 4: 370. 2000.
Paederota minima K. D. Koenig ex Retz., Observ. Bot. 5: 10. 1789.
Microcarpaea muscosa R. Br., Prodr. 435. 1810; FHK 253. 1861; FKH 189. 1912.

Annual herbs, cushion‑like. Stems prostrate, slender, filiform, base 4‑angled, many‑branched, striate, glabrous. Leaves opposite, sessile, amplexicaul, linear to narrowly oblong, 3–6 × 1–2 mm, margin entire, somewhat thickened; glabrous on both surfaces, punctuate above, veins inconspicuous. Flowers solitary and axillary, sessile. Calyx campanulate, ca. 1.5 mm, lobes deltoid‑ovate, sparsely ciliate. Corolla pink, 2–3 mm, upper lip erect, lower lip spreading. Stamens 2. Capsules ovoid, shorter than calyx. Seeds brownish yellow, ca. 0.3 mm.

Locality: Sha Tin, Tsiu Hang, Wu Kau Tang, Fanling. L. T. Lo 534; Y. W. Lam 332, 1238.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guizhou, Yunnan, Zhejiang, Taiwan; India, Indonesia, Japan, Korea, Malaysia, Thailand, Vietnam, Australia.
Ecology: Wet places. Flowering: Jul. –Oct.

Picria felterrae Lour. 苦玄參
Fl. Cochinch. 2: 393. 1790; FHN 3: 504. 1974; FOC 18: 29. 1998; FGD 4: 384. 2000.

Herbs, to 1 m tall, rooting from lower nodes. Petioles 0.5 – 2 cm; leaf blade ovate to sometimes suborbicular, to 5.5 × 3 cm, base cuneate, rounded, or truncate, margin crenate‑serrate, abaxially hispid on veins, adaxially short hispid; lateral veins 4 or 5 on each side of midvein. Racemes 4 – 8‑flowered. Pedicels to 1 cm. Sepals oblong‑ovate, to 1.4 × 1 cm in fruit, veins conspicuously reticulate; lower and upper sepals enlarged in fruit, 2 lateral ones linear. Corolla red‑brown, ca. 1.2 cm; tube ca. 6.5 mm, constricted at middle; limb strongly 2‑lipped; lower lip ca. 6.5 mm, upper lip erect, ca. 4.5 mm. Anterior stamens 2, reduced, posterior stamens 2, fertile. Capsules ovoid, 5 – 6 mm. Seeds numerous.

Locality: Fung Yuen. Y. W. Lam 872, 873; HK sheet 38610.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan; India, Myanmar, Indochina, Thailand, Philippines.
Ecology: Thickets, grassy fields. Flowering: Summer to autumn.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Russelia equisetiformis Schltr. & Cham. 爆仗竹
Linnaea 6: 377. 1831; L. H. Bailey, Man. Cult. Pl. 899. 1949; FGZ 592. 1956.

Shrubs, 0.3–2 m tall, many‑branched and glabrous; branches verticillate, slender, green, rush‑like, striate, pendulous at top. Leaves small, ovate or linear‑lanceolate, less than 1.5 cm, mostly reduced to scales on branches. Flowers in racemose‑cymes; calyx light green, ovate or cup‑like, 3 mm; corolla scarlet, 2.5 cm, tube slightly expanded at top, lobes ovate or oblong‑ovate, ca. 3 mm.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. H. C. Tang 191; Y. S. Lau 1904, 2200.
Distribution: Widely cultivated in S China; native to Mexico.
Ecology: Flowering: Summer to autumn.
Uses: Ornamental.

Scoparia dulcis L. 野甘草
Sp. Pl. 116. 1753; FHK 252. 1861; FKH 189. 1912; FOC 18: 21. 1998; FGD 4: 382, fig. 230. 2000.

Herbs or subshrubs, 0.3–1 m tall, many‑branched; branches ribbed to narrowly winged. Leaves usually in whorls of 3; leaf blade rhomboid‑ovate to rhomboid‑lanceolate, 3.6 × 1.5 cm, upper ones small and narrow, glandular punctate, margin toothed above middle, sometimes slightly double serrate, or subentire, apex obtuse. Flowers usually axillary, 1 or 2 per node. Pedicels 5–10 mm. Calyx lobed to base; lobes 4, ovate‑oblong, ca. 2 mm, margin ciliate. Corolla white, ca. 4 mm in diam.; tube densely hairy at throat; upper lobe slightly larger than others. Stamens exserted, stigma truncate to 2‑parted. Capsules 2–3 cm in diam.; columella persistent.

Locality: Naturalized in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 1215, 1914; Y. S. Lau 185.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; native to tropical America, now through tropics and subtropics as a weed.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides. Flowering & fruiting: Nearly all year round.

Siphonostegia chinensis Benth. 陰行草
In Hook. & Arn., Bot. Beechey Voy. 203. 1837; FKH 191. 1912; FOC 18: 211. 1998.

Annual herbs, 30–60(–80) cm tall, black when dry, densely tawny hairy. Branches ± angled, densely pubescent. Leaves sessile or short petiolate; leaf blade broadly ovate, 0.8–5.5 × 0.4–6 cm, densely pubescent, 2‑pinnatisect; pinnae 3 pairs, lowermost pair 2‑pinnately parted; pinnules 1–3, linear to linear‑lanceolate, 1–2 mm wide, margin entire. Racemes few‑flowered; bracts pinnately parted or pinnatisect. Calyx tube 1–1.5 cm, densely pubescent; lobes green, subequal, linear‑lanceolate to oblong, 2.2–2.5 mm, outside densely pilose, inside pubescent, margin entire or 1–2‑toothed. Corolla tube 1.2–1.4 cm; lower lip yellow, lobes ovate; upper lip red‑purple, apex truncate. Filaments basally ciliolate. Ovary narrowly ovoid, ca. 4 mm. Capsules ovoid‑oblong, ca. 1.5 cm × 2.5 mm, apex suboblique and apiculate. Seeds black, ca. 0.8 mm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Lamma Island. Y. S. Lau 1536; Y. W. Lam 1022; HK sheet 20719.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; Russia, Korea, Japan.
Ecology: Grassy hillslopes. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Sep.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Deep Water Bay, Lady Clementi's Ride
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Siphonostegia laeta S. Moore 腺毛陰行草
J. Bot. 18: 5. 1880; FOC 18: 211. 1998.

Herbs, 30–70 cm tall, erect, blackish when dry, densely glandular hairy. Branches 3–5 pairs. Leaves short petiolate; leaf blade narrowly triangular‑ovate, 1.5–2.5 × 0.8–1.5 cm, densely glandular hairy, nearly palmately 3‑parted; median pinna larger than others, rhomboid‑ovate, pinnately parted, with 3–6 ovate pinnules; lateral pinnae oblique triangular‑ovate. Bracts foliaceous, as long as or shorter than calyx, rhomboid‑ovate to ovate‑lanceolate, densely glandular hairy, margin ± pinnately parted to subentire, apex acuminate. Pedicel 2–3 mm. Bracteoles 3–5 mm. Calyx tubular‑campanulate; tube 1–1.5 cm; lobes 6–10 mm, margin entire. Corolla yellow, sometimes galea purplish; lower lip as long as galea, lobes triangular‑ovate, ciliate with long multicellular hairs. Filaments densely pubescent. Ovary narrowly ovoid, 2–3 mm. Capsules 1.2–1.3 cm × 3.5 mm. Seeds yellow‑brown, 1–1.5 mm.

Locality: Deep Water Bay, Lady Clementi's Ride. Y. S. Lau 2519; P. S. Choi 534.
Distribution: Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Jiangxi.
Ecology: Grassy hillslopes. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Sep.

Sopubia matsumurae (T. Yamaz.) C. Y. Wu 毛果短冠草（短冠草）
Novon 9 (2): 288. 1999.
Petitmenginia matsumurae T. Yamaz., J. Jap. Bot. 25: 214. 1950.
Sopubia lasiocarpa P. C. Tsoong, FRPS 67(2): 405. 1979; FOC 18: 87. 1998.
Sopubia stricta auct. non (Benth.) G. Don: Rep. Bot. & Forest. Dep. Hongk. (1913): M21. 1914; (1914): M34. 1915.

Annual herbs, to 38 cm tall. Stems erect, basally terete, apically branched and ribbed, with short crisp hairs. Leaves opposite or subalternate on upper part of stem; leaf blade linear, to 5 cm × 1.5 mm, adaxially hispidulous, margin revolute. Racemes sparsely flowered, forming a large panicle. Pedicels 1.5–2 mm, pubescent. Bracteoles 2, attached near base of calyx. Calyx ca. 1.5 mm, inflated to 3.5 mm in fruit, 10‑veined; lobes narrowly triangular, subequal, outside hispidulous, inside glabrous, apex acute. Corolla purplish, ca. 1 cm; tube ca. 7 mm; lobes obovate, subequal. Capsules 5 –6 mm, much longer than persistent calyx, hispidulous, apex deeply concave, to 2/5 of capsule length. Seeds dark brown, irregularly oblong.

Locality: Fanling. W. J. Tutcher 10554.
Distribution: Hunan, Jiangsu, Zhejiang.
Ecology: Open fields. Flowering: Autumn.
Notes: This species was recorded as Sopubia stricta G. Don and S. lasiocarpa P. C. Tsoong previously (Check List HK Plants 73. 1993; 248. 2002; 85. 2004).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Wong Nai Chung Gap, Ma On Shan, Tai Mei Tuk, Sai Kung (Sai Wan), Lamma Island, Sunset Peak
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Striga asiatica (L.) Kuntze 獨腳金
Rev. Gen. Pl. 466. 1891; FOC 18: 88. 1998; FGD 4: 393, fig. 238. 2000.
Buchnera asiatica L., Sp. Pl. 2: 630. 1753.
Striga asiatica var. humilis (Benth.) D. Y. Hong, FRPS 67(2): 359, 405. 1979.
Striga hirsuta Benth., Prodr. 10: 502 – 503. 1846; FHK 254. 1861.
Striga hirsuta var. humilis Benth., Prodr. 10: 503. 1846.
Striga lutea Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 1: 22. 1790; FKH 190. 1912; FTW ed. 2, 4: 627.

Annual herbs, 10–20(–30) cm tall, hirsute throughout. Stems erect, simple, rarely branched. Leaf blade linear to narrowly lanceolate, 5–20 × 1–4 mm, sometimes reduced to scales. Flowers axillary, solitary or in a spike upward. Calyx 4–8 mm, 10‑ribbed; lobes 5, ± as long as the tube, subulate. Corolla usually yellow, rarely red or white; tube 0.8–1.5 cm, apically strongly curved; upper lip 2‑lobed. Capsules ovoid, enveloped in persistent calyx.

Locality: Wong Nai Chung Gap, Ma On Shan, Tai Mei Tuk, Sai Kung (Sai Wan), Lamma Island, Sunset Peak. Y. S. Lau 329, 1640; P. S. Choi 454.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Grasslands. Flowering: Jul.–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Striga masuria (Buch.‑Ham. ex Benth.) Benth. 大獨腳金
Compan. Bot. Mag. 1: 364. 1836; FHK 254. 1861; FKH 190. 1912; FOC 18: 88. 1998; FGD 4: 394. 2000; FTW ed. 2, 4: 627.
Buchnera masuria Buch.‑Ham. ex Benth., Scroph. Ind. 41. 1835.

Perennial herbs, 30–60 cm tall, entirely hispid. Stems erect, ± quadrangular, simple or weakly branched. Leaf blade linear, 2–3 cm, longest at middle of stem. Flowers solitary, rarely in a spike. Calyx ca. 1 cm at anthesis, to 1.5 cm in fruit, 15‑ribbed; lobes ca. 2 times as long as tube, linear‑elliptic. Corolla pink, white, or yellow; tube to 1.2 cm, apically curved forward; upper lip ca. 1/2 as long as lower lip, apex notched. Capsules ovoid, ca. 6 mm.

Locality: Deep Water Bay. H. F. Hance s.n.; W. A. Harland s.n. (fide FHK 254. 1861).
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangsu, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Myanmar to Philippines.
Ecology: Grassy slopes. Flowering: Summer to autumn.

Torenia asiatica L. 光葉蝴蝶草（光葉翼萼）
Sp. Pl. 2: 619. 1753; FOC 18: 39. 1998.
Torenia glabra Osbeck, Dagbok Ostind. Resa. 210. 1757; FHN 3: 510. 1974; FRPS 67(2): 161. 1979; Check List HK Plants 249. 2002; 86. 2004.
Torenia benthamiana auct. non Hance: FKH 188. 1912.

Herbs creeping to suberect, rooting from nodes. Branches numerous, long, slender. Petioles 2–8 mm; leaf blade triangular‑ovate, narrowly ovate, or obovate‑orbicular, 1.5–3.2 × 1–2 cm, glabrous or sparsely villose, base abruptly constricted, subtruncate to broadly cuneate, margin crenate‑serrate. Flowers axillary and solitary or in fascicles. Pedicels 0.5–2 cm. Calyx 2‑lipped, 0.8–1.5 cm, further lobed into 5 small lobes in fruit, 5‑winged; wings more than 1 mm wide, ± decurrent. Corolla purple‑red to blue‑red, 1.5–2.5 cm, exceeding calyx by 0.4–1 cm. Filaments of anterior stamens with linear appendages of 1–2 mm. Capsules 1–1.3 cm. Seeds yellow, ca. 0.4 mm.

Locality: Mui Tsz Lam. Y. W. Lam 518.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian; Japan, Vietnam.
Ecology: Shady places. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Jan. of the following year.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Deep Water Bay, Tai Po, Fung Yuen, Fanling, Tai O
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Torenia benthamiana Hance 毛葉蝴蝶草
Ann. Sci. Nat., Bot., ser. 4, 18: 226. 1862; FKH 188. 1912; FHN 3: 510. 1974; FOC 18: 38. 1998; FGD 4: 376. 2000.
Torenia hirsuta auct. non. Lam.: FKH 188. 1912.

Herbs creeping, densely white hirsute, rooting from lower nodes. Branches numerous. Petiole ca. 1 cm; leaf blade ovate to ovate‑cordate, 1.5–2.2 × 1–1.8 cm, margin crenate. Inflorescences axillary, usually 3–5 in fascicles, or racemose, rarely 1‑flowered. Pedicels 3 cm in fruit. Calyx slender, 6–9 mm at anthesis, to 1.5 cm in fruit, 5‑ribbed, somewhat 2‑lipped. Corolla purple‑red, pale blue‑purple, or whitish, 1.2–1.4 cm; lower lip ca. 4 mm, 3‑lobed, middle lobe slightly larger than lateral lobes; upper lip oblong, ca. 5 × 4 mm. Filaments of anterior stamens with appendages of 1.5–2 mm. Capsules narrowly ellipsoidal, ca. 10 × 3 mm.

Locality: Deep Water Bay, Tai Po, Fung Yuen, Fanling, Tai O. Y. S. Lau 1650; Y. W. Lam 839, 876.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Wastelands, wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–May of the following year.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Authority: T. L. Chin & D. Y. Hong
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Mount Parker, Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Torenia biniflora T. L. Chin & D. Y. Hong 二花蝴蝶草
FRPS 67(2): 399. 1979; FOC 18: 38. 1998, FGD 4: 376. 2000.

Annual herbs, sparsely hirtellous. Stems to 50 cm, creeping or ascending, rooting from lower nodes. Petioles 6–10 mm; leaf blade ovate to narrowly ovate, 2–4 × 1–2.5 cm, margin coarsely toothed. Inflorescences axillary, usually dichotomous, sometimes racemose, 2–8‑flowered. Pedicels 6–12 mm in fruit. Calyx tubular, ca. 1 cm, 5‑winged; wings unequal, 0.5–1 mm wide; lobes 5, 3–4 mm. Corolla yellow, rarely white and faintly blue, ca. 1.1 cm. Filaments of anterior stamens with appendages of 3 mm. Capsules ellipsoidal, ca. 7 × 3 mm.

Locality: Mount Parker, Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan. Y. W. Lam 1373, 1453; F. W. Xing 9861.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi.
Ecology: Secondary forests. Flowering: Jul.–Oct.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Shing Mun, Tai Mo Shan, Tai Po Kau
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Torenia concolor Lindl. 單色蝴蝶草（單色翼萼）
Edwards's Bot. Reg. 32: pl. 62. 1846; FKH 187. 1912; FOC 18: 39. 1998; FGD 4: 375. 2000.
Torenia rubens Benth. ex Maxim., Prodr. 10: 410. 1846; FHK 250. 1861 (including var. grandiflora).

Annual herbs. Stems 4‑angled. Branches ascending or erect, rooting at lower nodes. Petioles 2–10 mm; leaf blade triangular‑ovate, narrowly ovate, or rarely ovate‑orbicular, 1–4 × 0.8–2.5 cm, glabrous or villous, base broadly cuneate to subtruncate, margin serrate or crenate‑serrate, apex obtuse to acute. Flowers axillary or terminal, solitary or in fascicles. Pedicels 2–3.5 cm, lengthening to 5 cm in fruit. Calyx 1.2–1.7 cm, enlarged to 2.3 cm in fruit, base decurrent; wings 5, slightly more than 1 mm in wide; lips narrowly triangular with 5 small lobes evident in fruit. Corolla blue to blue‑purple, 2.5–3.9 cm, exceeding calyx lobes. Filaments of anterior stamens with filiform of appendages, 2–4 mm. Capsules 1.5–1.8 cm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Shing Mun, Tai Mo Shan, Tai Po Kau. W. J. Tutcher 11443; Y. S. Lau 2357; Y. W. Lam 1122.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Taiwan; Ryukyu Islands, Laos, Vietnam.
Ecology: Grasslands, margins of forests. Flowering & fruiting: May–Nov.

Torenia flava Buch.‑Ham. ex Benth. 黃花蝴蝶草
Scroph. Ind. 38. 1835; FHK 250. 1861; FKH 187. 1912; FHN 3: 510. 1974; FOC 18: 38. 1998; FGD 4: 377. 2000.

Annual herbs, erect, to 50 cm tall. Stems many‑branched, 4‑angled, villose. Petiole 5–13 mm; leaf blade ovate to elliptic, 3–5 × 1–2 cm, base cuneate, margin crenate, sparsely pilose on both surfaces or abaxially glabrous except for veins. Racemes terminal, 10–20 cm. Bracts oblong‑ovate, 5–8 mm. Calyx narrowly cylindric, ca. 8 × 2 mm, enlarged to 10–15 × 3–5 mm in fruit, villous, 5‑ribbed; lobes 5, narrowly lanceolate. Corolla yellow; tube 1–1.2 cm; lower lip shallowly 3‑lobed, lobes suborbicular, subequal; upper lip slightly larger than lower lobes, margin entire or apex emarginate. Filaments of anterior stamens with appendages of ca. 1 mm. Capsules narrowly ellipsoidal.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Sai Kung. Y. S. Lau 2363; HK sheet 40640.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Taiwan; S to SE Asia.
Ecology: Grasslands. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Sep.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Ng Tung Chai, Shing Mun, Sai Kung
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Torenia fordii Hook. f. 紫斑蝴蝶草（紫斑翼萼）
Bot. Mag. 111, pl. 6797B. 1885; FOC 18: 38. 1998; FGD 4: 377. 2000.

Herbs, 25–40 cm tall, villous. Stems erect, stout. Petioles 1 – 1.5 cm; leaf blade broadly ovate to ovate‑triangular, 3– 5 × 2.5–4 cm, sparsely white hairy, base abruptly constricted and broadly cuneate, margin coarsely triangular acute‑serrate. Racemes terminal. Bracts oblong‑ovate, 5–10 mm, margin ciliate. Pedicels ca. 1 cm, lengthening to 2 cm in fruit. Calyx obovate‑fusiform, ca. 12 × 5–7 mm, ca. enlarged to 1.8 × 0.8 cm in fruit, 5‑winged; wings unequal in width; lobes 5, subequal. Corolla yellow, 1.5–1.8 cm; lower lip lobes rotund, ca. 3–3.5 mm, middle lobe apically orange‑coloured, lateral lobes distally blue; upper lip ca. 4 × 5 mm, emarginate. Filaments of anterior stamens with tooth‑like appendages. Capsules cylindric, 9–11 × 2–3 mm, compressed, 4‑furrowed.

Locality: Ng Tung Chai, Shing Mun, Sai Kung. L. T. Lo 183; Y. S. Lau 2512; Y. W. Lam 877.
Distribution: Guangdong, Jiangxi, Hunan, Fujian.
Ecology: Margins of forests. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Oct.

Torenia fournieri Linden ex E. Fourn. 藍豬耳
Ill. Hort. 23: 129. 1876; FOC 18: 39. 1998; FGD 4: 376, fig. 226. 2000.

Herbs 15–50 cm tall. Stems erect, 4‑angled, simple or branched above middle, subglabrous. Petioles 1–2 cm; leaf blade obong‑ovate to ovate, 3–5 × 1.5–2.5 cm, subglabrous, margin coarsely serrate. Racemes often terminal. Bracts linear, 2–5 mm. Pedicels 1–2 cm. Calyx ellipsoidal, 1.3–1.9 cm, green or purple‑red at apex and margin, 5‑winged; wings 2–3 mm wide; lobes subtriangular, 1.5–1.7 cm. Corolla 2.5–4 cm; tube pale violet, upper side yellow; lower lip purple‑blue, middle lobe with a yellow patch near base, lobes oblong to suborbicular, ca. 10 × 8 mm, subequal; upper lip pale blue, erect, broadly obovate, 1–1.2 × 1.2–1.5 cm, emarginate. Filaments of anterior stamens without appendages. Capsules narrowly ellipsoidal, ca. 12 × 0.5 mm. Seeds yellow.

Locality: Cultivated or naturalized. Y. S. Lau 1633, 1654, 1953.
Distribution: Cultivated or naturalized in S China; native to Vietnam.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Oct.
Uses: Ornamental.

Veronica javanica Blume 多枝婆婆納
Bijdr. 742. 1826; FOC 18: 74. 1998; FGD 4: 380. 2000.

Annual or perennial herbs, 10–40 cm tall. Stems erect or ascending, many‑branched, densely white villose. Leaves alternate; petiole 1–7 mm; leaf blade ovate to ovate‑triangular, 1–4 × 1–3 cm, base ± cordate to truncate, apex obtuse, margin deeply incised dentate. Racemes axillary, initially short and subcorymbose, lengthening to 10 cm in fruit; bracts linear to oblanceolate, 4–6 mm; much longer than pedicels. Calyx 4‑lobed; lobes linear‑elliptic, 2–5 mm, subequal. Corolla white, pink or red‑purple, rotate, ca. 2 mm; tube ca. 1.4 mm, hairy in throat. Stamens about half the length of corolla. Capsules obcordate, strongly compressed, 2–3 × 3–4 mm, notched at apex.

Locality: Sai Kung. Y. W. Lam 1767.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Gansu, Shaanxi, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Korea, Japan, Philippines, Indochina, Bhutan, India, Indonesia, Africa.
Ecology: Wet places near villages. Flowering: Apr.

Veronica persica Poir. 阿拉伯婆婆納
Encycl. 8: 542. 1808; FOC 18: 70. 1998.
Veronica tournefortii C. C. Gmel., Fl. Ead. 1: 39. 1805.
Veronica didyma auct. non Tenore: Check List HK Plants 73. 1993.

Annual herbs, sometimes biennial. Stems diffuse, ca. 20–50 cm, densely pubescent with multicellular hairs, often more densely so along 2 lines. Leaves opposite, usually 3 or 4 pairs; petioles 1–8 mm; leaf blade ovate‑lanceolate to suborbicular, 10–20 × 8–15 mm, evenly and sparsely pubescent on both surfaces, margin obtusely crenate‑serrate. Racemes terminal, laxly flowered. Bracts alternate, leaf‑like, upper ones smaller than others. Calyx 4‑lobed; lobes ovate‑lanceolate, 5–8 mm in fruit, sparsely pubescent, 3‑veined. Corolla usually blue, rotate, 8–14 mm in diam., throat sparsely hairy; lobes ovate to orbicular. Stamens shorter than corolla. Capsules obcordate, strongly compressed, 4–6 × 6–9 mm, venation conspicuously reticulate. Seeds slightly navicular, usually 1.4–2.3 mm; testa deeply rugose dorsally.

Locality: Naturalized. Y. S. Lau 2856; P. S. Choi 322; K. L. Yip 4384.
Distribution: S, C, SW & E China; native to SW Asia and since the 19th century spread over most of the world.
Ecology: Grasslands on higher ground. Flowering: Feb.–May.

Veronica undulata Wall. ex Jack 水苦蕒
Fl. Ind. 1: 147. 1820; FOC 18: 79. 1998; FGD 4: 379. 2000.
Veronica anagallis‑aquatica auct. non L.: FKH 190. 1912, as ‘V. Anagallis’.

Perennial herbs, rarely annual. Stems erect or procumbent at base, 10–100 cm tall, ± succulent, sparsely covered with capitate glandular hairs. Leaves sessile, amplexicaul upward; leaf blade elliptic to ovate, sometime ovate‑oblong or linear‑lanceolate, rarely lanceolate, 2–10 × 1–3.5 cm, margin serrate. Racemes axillary, longer than leaves. Calyx 4‑lobed; lobes ovate‑lanceolate, ca. 3 mm. Corolla pale blue, pale purple, or white, rotate, 4–5 mm in diam.; tube short; lobes broadly ovate, slightly unequal in width. Stamens shorter than corolla. Capsules subglobose, as long as calyx, slightly compressed, apex rounded and slightly notched. Seeds slightly flattened, convex on both sides.

Locality: Wong Nai Chung, Sha Tin. Y. S. Lau 2965; HK sheet 4160, 4161.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; E Afghanistan, N India, Korea, Japan, Laos, Nepal, Pakistan, Thailand, Vietnam.
Ecology: Wet places near villages. Flowering: Feb.–Apr.; fruiting: Apr.–May.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Po, Chung Pui, Sheung Wo Che
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Myoporum bontioides (Siebold & Zucc.) A. Gray 苦檻藍
Proc. Amer. Acad. Art. & Sci. 6: 52. 1862; Dunn & Tutcher, FKH 200. 1912; Z.Y. Li, FRPS 70: 311. 2002.
Pentacoelium bontioides Siebold & Zucc., Abh. Akad. Wiss. Math. Phys. 4(3): 151, t. 3, B. 1846.
Polycoelium chinense A. DC., DC. Prodr. 11: 706. 1847.

Shrubs, evergreen, 50–80 cm tall. Petioles 1–1.5 cm. Leaves alternate; leaf blade narrow‑elliptic, lanceolate or oblong, 6–10 × 2–3 cm, base attenuate and decurrent, apex acuminate and mucronate, margin entire. Flowers solitary, axillary. Pedicels 1.5–2 cm. Calyx 5‑lobed, lobes ovate‑elliptic or deltoid‑ovate, 4–5 mm. Corolla white with purple‑blue spots, campanulate, 2–2.2 cm, 5‑lobed, lobes ovate to oblong, 8–10 mm. Stamens 4, on inside of corolla‑tube, filaments 15–18 mm. Ovary with 5–8 compartments. Drups purple‑red, globular, 1–1.5 cm, glabrous, 5–8‑angulate when dry.

Locality: Tai Po, Chung Pui, Sheung Wo Che. U. A. On 630; H. C. Tang 2509; Y. S. Lau 681.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Jiangxi, Hunan, Fujian, Taiwan, Zhejiang, Anhui, Jiangsu, Sichuan, Yunnan, Guizhou.
Ecology: Grasslands. Flowering & fruiting: Nov.–Apr. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Tai Po, Sai Kung
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Aeginetia indica L. 野菰
Sp. Pl. 2: 632. 1753; FHK 257. 1861; FKH 191. 1912; Hook. f., Fl. Brit. Ind. 4: 320. 1884; FRPS 69: 77, pl. 21: 1 – 8. 1990; FTW ed. 2, 4: 713, pl. 327. 1998; FOC 18: 240. 1998; FGD 4: 399, fig. 242. 2000.

Plant 20–35 cm tall. Root slightly fleshy. Stems very short, unbranched or branched from near base. Scales deltoid, 5–10 mm, apex acuminate, glabrous. Flowers usually solitary, 3–5 cm. Pedicels usually erect, 15–24 cm, glabrous. Calyx 2–3.5 cm, apex acute or acuminate. Corolla pinkish purple, indistinctly bilabiate, tubular‑campanulate, 2–4.5 cm; tube slightly curved; lobes subentire. Filaments purple, 7–9 mm, glabrous; anthers yellow. Ovary 1‑locular; parietal placentas 4; style 1–1.5 cm; stigma pale yellow. Capsule conical, or long ovoid‑globose, 2–3 cm; seeds yellow, ellipsoidal.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Tai Po, Sai Kung. Y. S. Lau 1004, 1270; HK sheet 41662.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Bangladesh, Bhutan, Cambodia, India, Indonesia, Japan, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, Nepal, Philippines, Sri Lanka, Thailand, Vietnam.
Ecology: Thin forests, hillslopes. Flowering: Jul.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Shing Mun, Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai, Pat Sin Leng, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Aeschynanthus acuminatus Wall. ex A. DC. 芒毛苣苔
Prodr. 9: 263. 1845; FKH 193. 1912; FRPS 69: 502. 1990; FOC 18: 377. 1998; FGD 6: 284, pl. 156. 2005.
Aeschynanthus chinensis Gardner & Champ., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 1: 328. 1849.
Aeschynanthus acuminatus var. chinensis (Gardner & Champ.) C. B. Clarke, Monogr. Phan. 5: 31. 1883.

Climber, stems 25–100 cm, branched, glabrous. Leaves opposite; petioles 2–5 mm; leaf blade thin leathery, oblanceolate to oblong, 4.5–9 × 1.5–3 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate or mucronate, margin entire, glabrous; lateral veins indistinct. Cymes axillary or pseudoterminal, 2–5‑flowered; peduncle 1–3 cm, glabrous; bracts 2, opposite, suborbicular, 3–9 × 5–10 mm, apex obtuse or rotund, glabrous; pedicel ca. 1 cm, glabrous. Calyx 5‑sect from base; lobes narrowly ovate to ovate‑oblong, 3–7 × 2–3 mm, apex obtuse, outside glabrous. Corolla red or greenish, 1.5–2.5 cm, outside glabrous, inside puberulent or purple spot at base of abaxial lip, without tufts of hairs, mouth strongly oblique; tube 0.8–1.6 cm long, ca. 5 mm in diam.; limb distinctly 2‑lipped; adaxial lip 2‑lobed, lobes erect, 4–6 mm long; abaxial lip 3‑lobed, lobes reflexed, 5–7 mm long, lobes narrowly ovate. Stamens 4, didynamous, exserted, adnate to corolla tube near middle; filaments purple, 1–2 cm; anthers coherent in pairs at apex, ca. 2 mm, glabrous; staminode 1, ca. 2 mm. Disk ring‑like. Pistil glabrous; ovary 1–1.5 cm; style ca. 5 mm; stigma 1, disk‑shaped. Capsule 6.5–10 cm, glabrous. Seeds narrowly oblong, with 1 hair‑like appendage at each end.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Shing Mun, Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai, Pat Sin Leng, Lantau Island. H. C. Tang 1726; Y. S. Lau 917, 2447.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Taiwan; Bhutan, India, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, Nepal, Thailand, N Vietnam.
Ecology: Trailing on trees and rocks by streams or in forests. Flowering: Dec.–Mar. of the following year; fruiting: Feb.–May.
Notes: The type specimen of Aeschynanthus chinensis was collected by J. G. Champion from Hong Kong between 1847 and 1850.

Boea hygrometrica (Bunge) R. Br. 旋蒴苣苔
Pl. Jav. Rar. 120. 1840 [On Cyrtandreae 120. 1839]; FRPS 69: 474. 1990; FOC 18: 368. 1998; FGD 6: 283. 2005.
Dorcoceras hygrometrica Bunge, Enum. Pl. China Bor. 54. 1833.

Herbs, perennial, stemless. Leaves basal and rosulate; petiole to 0.5 cm; leaf blade suborbicular to ovate, 1.5–4 × 1–2.5 cm, base cuneate to truncate, apex rounded, margin dentate to crenulate, adaxially white villous, abaxially densely white to brownish woolly; venation palmate, nearly parallel; veins 3–9. Cymes umbel‑like, 2–5‑flowered; peduncle 5–18 cm, puberulent to pubescent; bracts linear to lanceolate, 1–3 mm long; pedicels 1–3cm, pubescent. Calyx campanulate, 5‑sect from near base; segments narrowly lanceolate, 2–3 mm, apex obtuse, margin entire, abaxially puberulent, adaxially glandular puberulent. Corolla blue‑purple, 1–1.5 cm, abaxially sparsely pubescent; tube ca. 5 mm, 6–10 mm in diam.; limb distinctly 2‑lipped; adaxial lip lobes ca. 4 mm; abaxial lip lobes equal, obovate or ovate, 5–6 mm. Stamens 2, adnate to corolla tube near middle; filaments ca. 1 mm, glabrous; anthers coherent in pairs at apex, anther thecae obovate, ca. 2 mm; staminodes 3. Pistil pubescent; ovary oblong, ca. 5 mm; style ca. 4 mm, glabrous; stigma 1, terminal. Capsule oblong, 3–3.5 cm, pubescent, twisted. Seeds ovate.

Locality: Wu Kau Tang. W. J. Tutcher 10926.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Shanxi, Hebei, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Shandong, SW Liaoning, Zhejiang, Fujian.
Ecology: Rocks in ravines and forests. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Ma On Shan, Pat Sin Leng, Nam Chung, Luk Keng
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Boeica guileana B. L. Burtt 紫花短筒苣苔
Notes Roy. Bot. Gard. Edinburgh 35: 371. 1977; FRPS 69: 256. 1990; FOC 18: 288. 1998; FGD 6: 259. 2005.

Herbs, stemless. Leaves basal, rosulate; petioles 1–3 cm, densely villous; leaf blade elliptic, 2–5 × 1–3 cm, base cuneate to rounded, apex acute to rounded, margin serrate to double serrate, white villous and puberulent; lateral veins 5–7 pairs. Cymes 1‑flowered; peduncle 2–7 cm, purple villous; bracts 2, linear, ca. 3 mm, purple villose, margin entire; pedicels 1–2 cm, purple villose. Calyx zygomorphic, 5‑sect from base; segments lanceolate to linear, outside villous, margin entire. Corolla blue purple, ca. 1 cm, outside puberulent; tube ca. 2 mm; limb distinctly 2‑lipped; adaxial lip 2‑lobed from middle, lobes obovate, ca. 6 × 5 mm, apex obtuse; abaxial lip 3‑lobed from base, lobes obovate, ca. 10 × 6 mm. Stamens 4, free, adnate to corolla tube near base; filaments ca. 4 mm, sparsely puberulent; anthers obovate, ca. 2 mm, dehiscing longitudinally. Disk ring‑like. Pistil pubescent; ovary conical, ca. 3 mm long; style ca. 7 mm long; stigma 1, terminal. Capsule oblong, 1–1.5 cm, densely pubescent, much longer than persistent calyx. Seeds ellipsoidal.

Locality: Ma On Shan, Pat Sin Leng, Nam Chung, Luk Keng. P. S. Choi 542; S. C. Ng 2217; F. W. Xing 7345.
Distribution: Guangdong.
Ecology: Damp rocks in forests, in steep ravines or on cliffs. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Jul.
Notes: The type specimen was collected by D. P. M. Guile from Ma On Shan in July 1971. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Shing Mun, Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan, Tai Po Kau, Ng Tung Chai, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Chirita sinensis Lindl. 唇柱苣苔
Edward's Bot. Reg. 30: pl. 59. 1844; FHK 259. 1861; FKH 194. 1912; FRPS 69: 382. 1990; FOC 18: 334. 1998; FGD 6: 273. 2005.
Didymocarpus sinensis (Lindl.) H. Lév., Compt. Rend. Hebd. Seances Acad. Sci. 34: 427. 1906.
Chirita sinensis Lindl. var. angustifolia Dunn, J. Bot. 45(539): 403. 1907; FGD 6: 274. 2005.

Herbs, perennial, stemless. Leaves basal; petiole 4–8 × 1 cm, villose; leaf blade papery, ovate to oblong, (4–)5–10 × (2–)3.5–8 cm, base attenuate to cordate, apex obtuse or rounded, margin repand to crenate, appressed pubescent and pilose, glandular; lateral veins 3 – 5 pairs, inconspicuous. Cymes axillary, 2–6‑flowered; peduncle 8 – 14 cm, villose; bracts 2, ovate, 1–3 × 0.5–2 cm, apex obtuse, margin entire or crenulate, villous; pedicel 1 – 1.5 cm, densely pilose. Calyx 5‑sect from base; segments equal, ovate, 4–5 mm, outside puberulent to pilose, inside glabrous, margin entire, apex obtuse or rounded. Corolla purple or white, 3.5–4 cm, inside tinged purple with 2 yellow longitudinal lines adaxially of tube, outside sparsely pubescent to pilose, inside puberulent only on purple spot of adaxial lip; tube tubular to broadly funnelform, often gibbous abaxially, 2–2.5 cm long, ca. 1 cm in diam.; limb 2‑lipped; adaxial lip 2‑lobed, lobes ca. 5 mm long; abaxial lip 3‑lobed, lobes 0.7–1.5 cm long, ovate, apex obtuse. Stamens 2, adnate to abaxial side of corolla tube near middle, include; filaments ca. 1.5 cm, puberulent; anthers ca. 3 mm, glabrous to pubescent; staminodes 2, ca. 6 mm. Disk ring‑like, entire. Pistil puberulent; ovary linear, ca. 2 cm; style 5 mm; stigma 2‑lobed. Capsule ca. 4 cm, puberulent.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Shing Mun, Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan, Tai Po Kau, Ng Tung Chai, Lantau Island. H. C. Tang 2235; Y. S. Lau 417, 2761.
Distribution: Guangdong.
Ecology: Wet shady places by streams or rocks in valleys. Flowering: May–Feb. of the following year; fruiting: Aug.–Feb. of the following year.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Mo Shan, Kap Lung, Ng Tung Chai, Tai Po Kau, Ho Pui
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Didymostigma obtusum (C. B. Clarke) W. T. Wang 雙片苣苔
Acta Phytotax. Sin. 22: 189. 1984; FRPS 69: 273. 1990; FOC 18: 292. 1998; FGD 6: 261, pl. 144. 2005.
Chirita obtusa C. B. Clarke, Monogr. Phan. 5: 114. 1883.
Roettlera obtusa (C. B. Clarke) Kuntze, Revis. Gen. Pl. 2: 476. 1891.

Herbs, perennial. Stems erect, simple or branched, 10–30 cm tall, pubescent to densely pubescent. Leaves opposite; petioles 1–4 cm, villose; leaf blade ovate, 2–12 × 1.5–7 cm, base sometimes slightly oblique, broadly cuneate to rounded, apex acute to obtuse, margin crenate, adaxially pubescent, abaxially sparsely pubescent often with purple tinged spotted; lateral veins 5–8 pairs. Cymes axillary, 2–10‑flowered; peduncle 2–4 cm, pubescent; bracts 2, lanceolate‑linear, 3–6 mm, pubescent; pedicels ca. 1 cm. Calyx 5‑sect from base; segments linear, 7 – 10 mm, villose. Corolla white or purple‑blue, 3.5–5 cm, abaxially pubescent; tube slightly funnelform‑tubular, 3 – 3.5 cm, ca. 1 cm in diam.; adaxial lip 2‑lobed, lobes 5–7 mm; abaxial lip 3‑lobed, lobes 0.9 – 1.2 cm, rounded. Stamens 2, glabrous, adnate to abaxial side of corolla tube near base, included; filaments slightly tortuous, ca. 1 cm; anther ca. 2 mm; staminodes 2, ca. 5 mm. Disk ring‑like, entire. Pistil sparsely pubescent; ovary linear, ca. 2 cm; style ca. 1 cm; stigma 2. Capsule 4–8 cm. Seeds ellipsoidal.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Kap Lung, Ng Tung Chai, Tai Po Kau, Ho Pui. L. T. Lo 416; Y. W. Lam 1149; HK sheet 35341.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian.
Ecology: Forests, shaded streamsides. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Oct.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Sai Kung, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Oreocharis benthamii C. B. Clarke 大葉石上蓮
Monogr. Phan. 5: 63. 1883; FKH 193. 1912; FRPS 69: 165. 1990; FOC 18: 260. 1998; FGD 6: 253. 2005.

Herbs, perennial, 15–25 cm tall. Leaves basal; petioles 2–8 cm, densely light brown woolly; leaf blade elliptic or ovate‑orbicular, 4–20 × 2–8 cm, base slightly cordate, apex obtuse to acute, margin shallowly crenate to entire, adaxially densely pubescent, abaxially densely pubescent to densely woolly and densely brown woolly along veins; lateral veins 6–8 pairs. Cymes 6–10‑flowered; peduncle 5–20 cm, densely pale brown woolly; bracts 2, linear, 5– 10 mm, apex acute, margin entire, densely pubescent; pedicels 0.5–1.5 cm. Calyx campanulate, 5‑sect from base; segments lanceolate, ca. 4 mm, apex acute, margin entire, villose. Corolla purple, 0.8–1 cm, outside pubescent to puberulent; tube tubular, gradually ampliate from base to mouth, 8–10 mm; limb slightly 2‑lipped; adaxial lip 2‑lobed from middle, abaxial lip 3‑lobed from base, lobe equal, 1–2 mm, nearly rounded. Stamens 4, free, adnate to corolla tube near middle; filaments ca. 7 mm; anthers broadly oblong, ca. 1 mm. Disk ring‑like, entire. Pistil glabrous; ovary linear, ca. 5 mm; style ca. 2 mm; stigma 1, disk‑shaped. Capsule 2 – 3.5 cm, oblong.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Sai Kung, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 922; L. T. Lo 610; P. S. Choi 410.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Jiangxi.
Ecology: Cliffs in ravines and in forests. Flowering: Mar.–Oct.; fruiting: Aug.–Feb. of the following year.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Mo Shan, Fung Yuen, Tai Po Kau, Lantau Peak, Sunset Peak
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Rhynchotechum ellipticum (Wall. ex D. Dietr.) A. DC. 線柱苣苔
Prodr. 9: 285. 1845; FKH 192. 1912; FRPS 69: 558. 1990; FOC 18: 394. 1998; FGD 6: 287, pl. 158. 2005.
Corysanthera elliptica Wall. ex D. Dietr., Syn. Pl. 3: 582. 1843
Rhynchotechum formosanum Hatus., J. Jap. Bot. 15: 132. 1939; FRPS 69: 559. 1990; FOC 18: 394. 1998; Check List HK Plants 251. 2002; 86. 2004.

Subshrubs, 0.5–2 m tall, apically densely depressed rust‑brown woolly. Leaves opposite; petiole 1–4 cm, densely appressed rust‑brown woolly; leaf blade elliptic to obovate, 6.5–v32 × 2.5–10 cm, base cuneate to attenuate, apex abruptly acuminate to acute, margin denticulate, adaxially rust‑brown to brown woolly, glabrescent, abaxially densely rust‑brown woolly, glabrescent except along veins, lateral veins 13–26 pairs, almost parallel. Cymes 5– 30‑flowered; peduncle 2.5–3.5 cm, densely appressed rust‑brown villous; bracts narrowly lanceolate, 5–10 mm; pedicels 5–10 mm. Calyx 5‑sect from base; segments lanceolate, ca. 3 mm, abaxially rust‑brown villous, adaxially glabrous. Corolla white or pink, 4–5 mm, glabrous; tube ca. 2 mm; adaxial lip ca. 2 mm; abaxial lip ca. 2 mm, ovate, apex rounded. Stamens 4, adnate to corolla base, glabrous; filament 5–8 mm; anthers spherical, ca. 1 mm; staminode 1, 0.2–0.3 mm. Pistil glabrous; ovary conical, ca. 1 mm; style ca. 4 mm; stigma 1. Berry white, 5–6 mm, widely spherical.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Fung Yuen, Tai Po Kau, Lantau Peak, Sunset Peak. Y. W. Lam 1753; F. W. Xing 7008; HK sheet 31562.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam, Cambodia, Laos, Thailand, Malaysia, Myanmar, India, Bhutan, Nepal.
Ecology: Dense forests, shaded streamsides, rocky areas in valleys. Flowering: May–Sep.; fruiting: Oct–Feb. of the following year.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Shek O, Sha Tin, Sai Kung, Nam Sang Wai, Tai Lam Chung, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Acanthus ilicifolius L. 老鼠簕
Sp. Pl. 639. 1753; FHK 263. 1861; FKH 199. 1912; FHN 3: 553. 1974; FRPS 70: 45. 2002.
Dilivaria ilicifolia (L.) Juss., Gen. Pl. 103. 1789.

Erect shrubs, up to 2 m tall; stems rarely branched, stout, glabrous. Petioles thick, 3–6 mm, glabrous, with 2 stipule‑like spines at base; leaf blades oblong to oblong‑lanceolate, 6–14 × 2–5 cm, pinnatifid, base acute, apex truncate, margin with few large spines, glabrous, lateral veins 5–7 pairs, reaching to the teeth. Spikes terminal, to 16.5 cm; bracts broad ovate, 7–8 mm, innocuous, caducous; bracteoles ovate, about 5 mm, leathery. Calyx‑lobes 4, 2 outer ones larger, 10–13 mm, apex emarginate, scarious at margins, sometimes crispate, 2 inner ovate, about 10 mm, entire. Corolla pale, 3–4 cm; tubes 6 mm, upper lips reduced, lower lip obovate, about 3 mm, thin‑leathery, apex trifid, soft hairy on outer side, with a stripe of 3–4 mm broad on both sides of upper parts. Stamens 4, equal, anther‑theca 1, longitudinal scissile, with a line of hairs on both sides of suture; filaments 1.5 cm; anther‑theca longitudinally scissile; style 2.2 cm, longitudinal lineated; stigma 2‑fid. Capsule elliptic, 2.5–3 cm; seeds 4, ellipsoidal, complanate, light yellow.

Locality: Shek O, Sha Tin, Sai Kung, Nam Sang Wai, Tai Lam Chung, Lantau Island. H. C. Tang 2279, 2290; Y. S. Lau 225, 2216.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian; SE Asia and Australia.
Ecology: Mangrove swamps. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Jul.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

(R. T. Zhang) Y. F. Deng, N. H. Xia & H. B. Chen
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Acanthus ilicifolius L. var. xiamenensis (R. T. Zhang) Y. F. Deng, N. H. Xia & H. B. Chen 廈門老鼠簕
J. Trop. Subtrop. Bot. 14: 530. 2006.
Acanthus xiamenensis R. T. Zhang, Wuyi Sci. J. 5: 237. 1985.
Acanthus ebracteatus Vahl. var. xiamenensis (R. T. Zhang) C. Y. Wu & C. C. Hu, FRPS 70: 47. 2002.

Differs from var. ilicifolius in its leaf margin serrate or subentire, lateral veins not reaching to the teeth, and netted near the margin.

Locality: Mai Po, Tai Po. S. Y. Hu 11542 (CAS); S. Y. Hu 13544 (IBSC, PE).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian.
Ecology: Mangrove swamps. Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: Jun.–Jul.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hung Mui Kuk, Castle Peak, Man Uk Pin, Tung Chung
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Andrographis paniculata (Burm. f.) Nees 穿心蓮
Pl. As. Rar. 3: 116. 1832; FHN 3: 556. 1974; FRPS. 70: 207. 2002.
Justicia paniculata Burm. f., Fl. Ind. 9. 1768.

Annual herbs up to 30–50 cm tall, many‑branched. Stems quadrangular, glabrous. Petioles 0.3–1 cm; leaf blades papery, ovate‑lanceolate to narrowly lanceolate, 1.5–7 × 1–2.5 cm, base attenuate, decurrent onto the petioles, apex acute to shortly acuminate, margin entire, glabrous, adaxially green, abaxially pale green, lateral veins 3–5 pairs. Panicle axillary or terminal, 5–9 cm; rachis subglabrous. Pedicels 2–8 mm long, sparsely pubescent. Bracts linear‑lanceolate, ca. 3 × 1 mm; bracteoles linear, 2–2.5 mm. Calyx 5‑lobed almost to the base; lobes linear, 2.5–3 mm, abaxially glabrous or glandular‑pilose. Corolla white, ca. 1.5 cm, outside pilose; tube‑base cylindric ca. 0.8 cm; limb 2‑lipped, upper lip ca. 0.6 cm, reflexed, 2‑lobed, lobes ovate, ca. 1 × 1 mm, lower lips with purple dots, ca. 0.7 cm, erect, 3‑lobed, lobes lanceolate, ca. 3 × 1 mm. Stamens 2, exserted; filaments pubescent; anther 2‑thecous; anther‑thecae 2, unequal, the larger one hairy at base. Ovary ellipsoidal, ca. 2 mm, glabrous; style 6–9 mm, sparsely pilose towards base. Capsule narrowly cylindric, ca. 1.5 cm, glabous or sparsely glandular‑pubescent, many‑seeded. Seeds ovate, ca. 2 × 1.5 mm, glabrous, rugose.
