Locality: Hung Mui Kuk, Castle Peak, Man Uk Pin, Tung Chung. Y. W. Lam 399, 2044; Y. S. Lau 816, 2569.
Distribution: Areas S of Changjiang; SE Asia.
Ecology: Cultivated and naturalized, roadsides, margins of forests. Flowering & fruiting: Feb. Jun.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Asystasia gangetica (L.) T. Anderson 寬葉十萬錯
Enum. Pl. Zeyl. 235. 1860; FRPS 70: 217. 2002.
Justicia gangetica L., Cent. II Pl. 3. 1756.
Asystasia coromandelica Wight ex Nees, Pl. Asiat. Rar. 3: 89. 1832.

Perennial ascending herbs, up to 0.5 m tall. Stems quadrangular, pilose. Petioles 3–5 mm, pubescent; leaf blades ovate to elliptic, 3–12 × 1–5 cm, base truncate or rounded, apex acuminate, margin entire or slightly crenulate, glabrous or sparsely pilose, especially on the veins, adaxially covered with numerous cystoliths. Racemes axillary or terminal, up to 16 cm. Pedicels 2–3 mm, pilose. Bracts triangular, ca. 5 mm, pilose; bracteoles linear‑lanceolate, 1–2.5 mm, pilose. Calyx ca. 7 mm, 5‑lobed almost to the base; lobes linear‑lanceolate, 5–7 × 1–1.2 mm, abaxially pubescent, with glandular‑tipped pilose, margin ciliate. Corolla yellow or white, 3 – 3.5 cm, funnel‑shaped, outside glandular‑pilose, inside glabrous, tube‑base cylindric, ca. 8 cm, ventricose and gradually widened to ca. 1 cm wide at mouth; lobes obovate or semiorbicular, ca. 0.7–1.2 × 0.8–1 cm, middle lobe with a violet blotch. Stamens 4, didynamous, included; filaments glabrous, the longer pair ca. 5 mm, the shorter pair ca. 3 mm; anther‑thecae 3 × 1 mm, muticous. Ovary ellipsoidal, ca. 3.5 mm; style ca. 1.8 cm, velutinous; stigma capitellate, 2‑lobed. Capsule oblong, ca. 1.3 cm, pubescent 2–4‑seeded. Seeds irregularly obovate, flat, 3–5 mm, tuberculate‑rugose, margin with dense mucilaginous hairs.

Locality: Cultivated or naturalized. HK sheet 21382, 40596.
Distribution: Guangdong, Yunnan; pantropical weeds.
Ecology: Margins of forests. Flowering: Sep.–Feb. of the following year; fruiting: Jan.–Mar.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Authority: (Nees) Y. F. Deng & N. H. Xia
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Asystasia micrantha (Nees) Y. F. Deng & N. H. Xia, stat. nov. 小花十萬錯
Asystasia coromandeliana α micrantha Nees, Pl. Asiat. Rar. 3: 89. 1832.
Asystasia gangetica (L.) T. Anderson subsp. micrantha (Nees) Ensermu Kelbessa in J. H. Seyani & A. C. Chikuni (eds.), Proc. XIII Plenary Meet. AETFAT, Zomba, Malawi, 1991, 1: 343. 1994.

Perennial ascending herbs, ca. 0.5 m tall. Stems quadrangular, sulcate, pilose along sulci and on the nodes. Petioles 1–4 cm, slightly winged, pubescent; leaf blades ovate to elliptic, 5–11 × 2–5 cm, base truncate, rounded, decurrent onto the petioles, apex shortly acuminate or acute, margin entire or slightly crenulate, glabrous except for pilose on the veins, adaxially covered with numerous cystoliths, lateral veins 5–7 pairs. Racemes axillary or terminal, 3–8 cm. Pedicels 1–3 mm, pilose. Bracts linear‑lanceolate, ca. 2.5 × 1 mm, pubescent; bracteoles triangular‑lanceolate, ca. 2 × 1 mm, glabrescent except for the ciliate margin. Calyx 5‑lobed almost to the base; lobes linear‑lanceolate, 4–5 × 1–1.2 mm, apex acuminate, abaxially sparsely pubescent, margin ciliate. Corolla white, pale violet, spotted on the center lobe of the lower lip, 1.2–1.5 cm, campanulate, outside pilose, inside glabrous, tube‑base cylindric, ca. 3 cm, gradually widened to ca. 5 mm wide at mouth; lobes ovate or semiorbicular, ca. 3 × 2 mm, middle lobe with a violet blotch. Stamens 4, didynamous, included; filaments glabrous, the longer pair ca. 6 mm, the shorter pair ca. 4 mm; anther‑thecae 2 × 1 mm, muticous. Ovary ellipsoidal, ca. 3.5 mm, comose; style 0.8–1 cm, velutinous towards the base; stigma capitellate, 2‑lobed. Capsule oblong, 1.8–2 cm, ca. 2 mm wide, pubescent, base solid‑stalked, 2 – 4‑seeded. Seeds irregularly obovate, flat, 3–5 mm, margin angled, glabrous, tuberculate‑rugose.

Locality: Cultivated or naturalized. Y. W. Lam 2119; S. C. Ng 4128; F. W. Xing 8996 (IBSC).
Distribution: Taiwan; pantropical weeds.
Ecology: Margins of forests, gardens or roadsides. Flowering: Sep.–Feb. of the following year; fruiting: Jan.–Mar.

Barleria cristata L. 假杜鵑
Sp. Pl. 636. 1753; FHK 262. 1861; FKH 199. 1912; FHN 3: 553. 1974; FRPS 70: 63. 2002.

Under shrub, to 2 m tall; stems terete, branched, covered with soft hairs. Petioles (0–)0.3–1 cm; leaf blades papery, elliptic, oblong or ovate, 2–4 × 1.3–4 cm, base cuneate, decurrent onto the petioles, apex acute, sometimes acuminate, margin entire, villous on both surfaces, especially along the veins, lateral veins 4–7 pairs. Flowers subsessile, in dense axillary clusters becoming capitate at branch ends. Bracts absent; bracteoles very variable, linear to linear‑lanceolate, 1.0–2.2 × 0.5–1.5 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, margin usually spiny‑margined but sometimes bristly pilose‑margined, spinescent with age, 3–7‑veined. Outer calyx‑lobes narrowly elliptic to lanceolate, 1.2–2.5 × 0.5–1.3 cm, apex mucronate, margin spiny, pilose, reticulate, inner calyx‑lobes linear or lanceolate, 6–12 mm, scarious‑margined, 1‑veined. Corolla purplish‑blue, 5 – 6.5 cm; tube pilose, narrowly cylindric in the lower half, then gradually widened; lobes equal, oblong‑elliptic, ca. 1.5 cm, glabrous. Fertile stamens 4, didynamous; filaments pilose, especially towards the base; staminodes 1, filament sparsely pilose. Ovary oblong‑ellipsoidal, glabrous; styles linear, ca. 2.5 cm long, glabrous; stigma slightly inflated. Capsules oblong, 1.4–1.8 cm, black, acute at both ends, glabrous, 4‑seeded. Seeds suborbicular or ovate, ca. 5 × 4 mm, flattened, densely adpressed pubescent.

Locality: Cultivated and naturalized. Y. S. Lau 182; H. C. Tang 1478; Y. W. Lam 1209.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Fujian, Taiwan; SE Asia.
Ecology: Roadsides, hillslopes. Flowering: Oct.–Dec.
Uses. Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.

Clinacanthus nutans (Burm. f.) Lindau 鱷嘴花
Engler & Prantl, Pflanzenfam. 4(3b): 340. 1895; FHN 3: 566. 1974; FRPS 70: 252. 2002.
Justicia nutans Burm. f., Fl. Ind. 10: t. 5, fig. 1. 1768.
Clinacanthus burmanni Nees, Prodr. 11: 511. 1847

Herbs, up to 1 m tall. Stems terete, striped, glabrescent. Petioles 3–8 mm, sulcate, bifariously pubescent; leaf blades papery, lanceolate to linear‑lanceolate, 7–11 × 1–4 cm, base cuneate to rounded, apex caudate, margin subentire or dentate, pubescent when young on both surfaces, then glabrescent except for the pilose veins abaxially, lateral veins 4–6 pairs, elevated abaxially. Spikes terminal, subsecund, usually 3 – several forming a large, lax panicle to ca. 1.5 cm. Rachis glandular‑pubescent. Bracts and bracteoles linear, ca. 8 × 2 mm, apex acute, abaxially glandular‑pilose. Calyx 9–13 mm, 5‑lobed; lobes linear, apex acute, abaxially glandular‑pilose. Corolla dull red with a green base, 3–3.5 cm, outside pilose, inside glabrous except for a circled hairs ca. 5 mm above the base; tube‑base cylindric, ca. 5 mm long and ca. 3 mm, gradually widened to ca. 6 mm at mouth, 2‑lipped, upper lip erect, triangular, 1.5–2 × 0.5 cm, apex emarginate, lower lip nutant, 1.6–2 × 1 cm, with yellow streaks, 3‑lobed; lobes ovate, 3 × 1 mm. Stamens 2, exserted; filaments glabrous, ca. 1.5 cm; anthers ovate‑linear, ca. 4 × 1 mm, muticous. Ovary ovoid, ca. 3 mm, glabrous; styles ca. 3 cm, few hairs at base. Capsules oblong, ca. 2 cm, pilose. Seeds orbicular, ca. 2 mm in diam.

Locality: Cultivated or introduced. HK sheet 38978, 39670; P. H. Liang 8978 (IBSC).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; Vietnam, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia.
Ecology: Flowering: Mar.–May.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Codonacanthus pauciflorus (Nees) Nees 鐘花草
Prodr. 11: 103. 1847; FHK 267. 1861; FKH 199. 1912; FHN 3: 557. 1974; FTW ed. 2, 4: 651. 1998; FRPS 70: 228. 2002.
Asystasia pauciflora Nees, Pl. Asiat. Rar. 3: 90. 1832.
Codonacanthus acuminatus Nees, Prodr. 11: 103. 1847.

Perennial erect herbs, 20–60 cm tall, many‑branched. Stems quadrangular, sulcate, bifariously pubescent. Petioles 3–13 mm, puberulent or glabrous; leaf blades thin papery, elliptic, ovate or lanceolate, 5–12 × 1.5–4.5 cm, base rounded, cuneate, or attenuate and decurrent onto the petioles, apex acute or acuminate, margin entire or slightly undulate, adaxially green, glabrous or with few large‑celled hairs, with numerous cystoliths, abaxially pale green, glabrous except for loose puberulent on the midveins, lateral veins 5–7 pairs. Racemes simple or usually few forming a terminal panicle, 3–10 cm, flowers usually only one fertile on each node, distant. Peduncles 1–3 cm, puberulent. Rachis puberulent. Pedicels 1–3 mm, puberulent. Bracts lanceolate, ca. 2 mm, apex acute, puberulent; bracteoles ovate‑lanceolate, ca. 1.5 mm, apex acute, puberulent. Calyx ca. 2.5 mm, 5‑lobed almost to the base; lobes linear‑lanceolate, apex acuminate, puberulent. Corolla white, campanulate, 8–10 mm, glabrous; tube cylindric, ca. 2 mm, abruptly dilated and widened to 8–10 mm at mouth, upper lip 2‑lobed, rarely subentire, lower lip 3‑lobed, lobes ovate, ca. 4 × 4 mm, apex obtuse. Stamens 2, included, filaments ca. 2.5 mm, glabrous; anther‑thecae oblong, ca. 1.2 mm, parallel at unequal level. Ovary glabrous; styles filiform, ca. 6 mm; stigma shortly 2‑lobed. Capsule oblanceolate, ca. 1.5 cm, glabrous, (2 or )4‑seeded at upper half. Seeds orbicular, ca. 2 mm, glabrous, ridged on the margin.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 158; L. T. Lo 318; K. L. Yip 4460.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Vietnam, Laos, Thailand, Myanmar, India, Bhutan.
Ecology: Forests, wet places in ravines. Flowering & fruiting: Oct.–Jan. of the following year.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Deep Water Bay, Sha Tin, Tai Po
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Dicliptera chinensis (L.) Juss. 狗肝菜
Ann. Mus. Natl. Hist. Nat. 9: 268. 1807; FHK 266. 1861; FKH 200. 1912; FHN 3: 563. 1974; FTW ed. 2, 4: 654. 1998; FRPS 70: 236. 2002.
Justicia chinensis L., Sp. Pl. 16. 1753.

Annual or biannual herbs, 30–80 cm tall. Stems diffuse at base, erect above, quadrangular, ridged, glabrous except for pubescent on young branches and nodes. Petioles to 0.5–3 cm, puberulent; leaf blades ovate‑elliptic, 2–8 × 1.5–4 cm, base cuneate or attenuate and decurrent onto the petiole, apex short acuminate or acute, margin entire or slightly undulate, adaxially glabrous, abaxially sparsely puberulent along the veins, lateral veins 4 – 5 pairs, slightly prominent abaxially. Inflorescence axillary or terminal, a dichasial 3‑flowered cyme, or sometimes several forming a short panicle, 1–4 cm. Peduncles 2–5 mm; pedicels 0.5–3 mm, puberulent. Bracts 2, large, unequal, elliptic or narrowly obovate, 8–13 × 3–5 mm, apex acute, mucronate, margin ciliate, abaxially puberulent, 3‑veined; bracteoles linear, ca. 5 mm, apex acuminate, abaxially hirsute. Calyx ca. 5 mm, 5‑lobed almost to the base; lobes equal, linear, apex acuminate, margin hirsute. Corolla pale purple, 1–1.2 cm, outside puberulent; tube slender, ca. 6 mm; limb bilabiate, upper lip ovate, ca. 5 × 3 mm, apex entire, lower lip oblong, ca. 4 × 1.5 mm, shallowly 3‑lobed. Stamens 2, exserted, adnate near apex of corolla tube; filaments ca. 4 mm, glabrous; anther‑thecae spherical, ca. 1.2 mm in diam., parallel, one above the other. Ovary pilose at the tip; style filiform, ca. 1.4 cm; stigma unequally 2‑lobed. Capsule broadly ellipsoidal, apiculate, ca. 6 mm, puberulent, 4‑seeded. Seeds orbicular, ca. 2 mm in diam., pubescent, verrucose.

Locality: Deep Water Bay, Sha Tin, Tai Po. Y. S. Lau 2017; Y. S. Lau 2845.
Ecology: Roadsides, thin forests. Flowering: Jul.–Dec.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Vietnam.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Dipteracanthus repens (L.) Hassk. 楠草（蘆莉草）
Hoev. & De Vriense, Tidschr. Nat. Gesch. 10: 129. 1843; FHN 3: 549. 1974; FTW ed. 2, 4: 656, pl. 300, photo 338. 1998; FRPS 70: 50. 2002.
Ruellia repens L., Mant. 89. 1767; FHK 261. 1861; FKH 198. 1912; Check List HK Plants 51. 1974; 70. 1978.
Dipteracanthus lanceolatus Nees, Pl. Asiat. Rar. 3: 82. 1832.

Perennial creeping herb, 15–50 cm tall. Stems subquadrangular, finely pubescent or glabrescent. Petioles 3–5 mm; leaf blades thin papery, ovate to linear‑lanceolate, 1.4–4 × 0.8–2 cm, base broadly cuneate or rounded, apex acuminate or acute, margin subentire, sparsely strigose on both surfaces; lateral veins 4–5 pairs. Flowers axillary, solitary; pedicels ca. 1 mm. Bracteoles leaf‑like, ovate or ovate‑oblong, 0.8–1 cm. Calyx‑lobes ca. 5 mm, lanceolate, scarcely ciliate. Corolla white, ca. 2 cm, pilose outside, campanulate; tube‑base ca. 5 mm, ventricose and gradually widened to ca. 5 mm at mouth; lobes ovate, ca. 3 × 3 mm, apex obtuse. Stamens 4, included, didynamous, filaments glabrous, the longer pair ca. 5 mm, the shorter pair ca. 2 mm; anthers oblong, ca. 1 mm. Ovary comose; style ca. 1 cm, hirsute; stigma 2‑lobed, lobes unequal. Capsule spindle‑like, ca. 1.2 cm, brownish yellow, slightly pilose; 12–16‑seeded. Seeds orbicular, flat, ca. 3 mm in diam., appressed pilose, with a conspicuous entire white membranous wing.

Locality: Hong Kong Wai. C. Wright s.n. (K).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Taiwan; S to SE Asia.
Ecology: Grasslands, roadsides. Flowering: Early spring.

Eranthemum pulchellum Andrews 可愛花
Bot. Repos. 2: pl. 88. 1800; FRPS 70: 59. 2002.
Justicia pulchellum (Andrews) Roxb., Pl. Chrom. 2: 41, t. 177. 1805.
Pseuderanthemum pulchellum (Andrews) Merr., Philip. J. Sci. Bot. 7: 248. 1912.
Justicia nervosum Vahl, Enum. Pl. 1: 164. 1804.
Eranthemum nervosum (Vahl) R. Br. ex Roem. & Schult., Syst. Veg. 1: 174. 1817; FHN 3: 551. 1974; Check List HK Plants 252. 2002; 87. 2004.
Daedalacanthus nervosus (Vahl) T. Anderson, J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 9: 487. 1867.

Shrubs, 0.7–1.5 m tall. Stems quadrangular, sulcate, greyish green, glabrous or subglabrous. Petioles (0.3–)2– 3.5 cm, sulcate, glabrous; leaf blades ovate to elliptic, (3–)9–20 × (1–)4–9 cm, base attenuate and decurrent onto the petioles, apex acuminate, margin entire or crenate, glabrous, lateral veins 8–10 pairs, prominent on both surfaces, reticulate veins prominent abaxially, densely covered with cystoliths especially adaxially. Spikes terminal or axillary, 1.5–6 cm. Peduncle 0.5–3 cm, glabrous, densely covered with white cystoliths. Bracts leaf‑like, obovate, 1–1.5 × 0.6–0.9 cm, apex acute, reticulate veined, green along veins, otherwise white, sparsely puberulent; bracteoles linear lanceolate, greyish white, ca. 5 mm, abaxially sparsely pilose. Calyx 6–8 mm, whitish, sparsely puberulent, 5‑lobed; lobes lanceolate, ca. 4–5 mm, apex acuminate. Corolla blue, ca. 3 cm, curved, outside puberulent, inside bifariously pubescent; tube‑base narrowly cylindric, ca. 2 mm, abruptly widened to ca. 1.8 cm at mouth; lobes obovate, ca. 6–8 × 5–6 mm. Stamens 2, exserted; filaments ca. 6 mm; anther oblong, ca. 3 mm. Staminodes 2, ca. 2 mm. Ovary glabrous; styles ca. 2.5 cm, glabrous; stigma 2‑lobed, larger one linear‑lanceolate, sparsely pilose. Capsule stipitate, 1–1.3 cm, glabrous.

Locality: Cultivated. H. C. Tang 415; Y. S. Lau 1009, 1506.
Distribution: S & SW China (cultivated); India, Bhutan, Sikkim, Nepal, naturalized in tropical areas.
Ecology: Flowering: Oct.–Feb. of the following year.
Uses: Ornamental.

Hygrophila erecta (Burm. f.) Hochr. 小葉水蓑衣
Candollea 5: 230. 1934; FHN 3: 546. 1974; FRPS 70: 71. 2002.
Ruellia erecta Burm. f., Fl. Ind. 135. 1768.

Perennial herb, up to 1 m tall. Stems erect, quadrangular, bisulcate. Petioles (0–)3–5 mm, sulcate, hispid; leaf blades elliptic, obovate or oblong, 2–9 × 1–3 cm, base decurrent onto the petiole, apex acute or obtuse, margin entire or slightly undulate, hirsute on both surfaces, with numerous cystoliths, lateral veins 8–15 pairs, prominent abaxially. Flowers several‑fasciculate in leaf axil, sessile. Bracts leaf‑like, ovate, lanceolate or elliptic, ca. 1.1 cm, densely hispid‑ciliate; bracteoles linear‑oblong, ca. 6 mm, densely hispid‑ciliate. Calyx ca. 1.1 cm, 5‑lobed below to middle; lobes linear‑lanceolate, densely white hispid‑ciliate. Corolla purplish blue, 1.8–2.2 cm, pilose, tube‑base cylindric, ca. 5 mm, gradually widened to ca. 6 mm at mouth; limb 2‑lipped, upper lip triangular, 2‑lobed, lower lip oblong, 3‑lobed, lobes ovate, ca. 2 × 2 mm. Stamens 4, didynamous; filaments glabrous, the longer pair ca. 6 mm, the shorter pair ca. 3 mm; anther‑thecae linear, ca. 2 mm, divaricate at base. Ovary glabrous; style pilose. Capsule 1.2–1.5 cm. Seeds oblong, flattened, blackish brown, ca. 1.5 × 1 mm, glabrous, margin circled with translucent membrane.

Locality: New Territories. S. Y. Hu 6407 (PE).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangxi, Yunnan.
Ecology: Wet places. Flowering: Spring.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): So Kwun Po, Sha Kok Mei, Shek Pik Reservoir
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Hygrophila megalantha Merr. 大花水蓑衣
Philipp. J. Sci. 12(2): 110. 1917; FRPS 70: 71. 2002.
Hygrophila salicifolia var. megalantha (Merr.) H. S. Lo & L. D. Chou, Guihaia 16: 374. 1996.

Perennial herbs, 30–60 cm tall. Stems quadrangular, glabrous. Petioles 0.5–1.5 cm, glabrous; leaf blades narrowly oblong‑obovate to lanceolate, 4–9 × 1.5–2.5 cm, base attenuate, decurrent onto the petioles, apex rounded or obtuse, margin entire or undulate, glabrous, lateral veins 5–7 pairs. Flowers several‑fasciculate in leaf axil, sessile. Bracts oblong‑lanceolate, 0.8–1 × 0.3–0.5 cm, apex acute, ciliate; bracteoles oblong‑lanceolate, ca. 6 × 2 mm, apex acute, ciliate. Calyx 1.4–1.6 cm, 5‑lobed to the middle; lobes linear‑lanceolate, apex acuminate, sparsely hispid‑ciliate. Corolla purplish blue, 2–2.5 cm, pilose outside; tube‑base cylindric, ca. 7 mm; limb 2‑lipped, upper lip ovate‑oblong, ca. 1.2 × 0.8 cm, apex emarginate, lower lip oblong, ca. 1.3 × 0.8 cm, 3‑lobed, lobes ovate, ca. 4 × 2 mm. Stamens 4, didynamous; filaments glabrous, the longer pair ca. 1.4 cm, the shorter pair ca. 0.7 cm, anther‑thecae ovate, ca. 1.5 mm. Ovary glabrous, styles filiform, ca. 1.6 cm, slightly hairy, stigma quite unequally bilobed. Capsule oblong, 1.4–1.6 cm, glabrous, 12–16‑seeded. Seeds ovate, ca. 1.5 × 1.5 mm, glabrous.

Locality: So Kwun Po, Sha Kok Mei, Shek Pik Reservoir. W. J. Tutcher 1079; Y. S. Lau 799; HK sheet 34480.
Distribution: Guangdong, Fujian.
Ecology: Wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Oct.–Jan. of the following year.
Notes: The species was reported as Hygrophila quadrivalvis Nees previously (Check List HK Plants 253. 2002; 87. 2004).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Chuen Lung, Tai Po, Sai Kung
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Hygrophila salicifolia (Vahl) Nees 水蓑衣
Pl. Asiat. Pl. 3: 81. 1832; FHK 261. 1861; FKH 197. 1912; FHN 3: 545. 1974; FTW ed. 2, 4: 661. 1998; FRPS 70: 69. 2002.
Ruellia salicifolia Vahl, Symb. Bot. 3: 84. 1794.
Justicia lancea Thunb., Trans. Linn. Soc. 2: 338. 1794.
Hygrophila lancea (Thunb.) Miq., Ann. Mus. Bot. Lugd.‑Bat. 2: 123. 1865; FTW ed. 2, 4: 660. 1998; Check List HK Plants 252. 2002; 87. 2004.

Perennial herbs to 80 cm tall. Stems erect or decumbent at base, quadrangular, striate, slightly pubescent. Petioles 0.5–1 cm, glabrous; leaf blades narrowly lanceolate to oblanceolate, 3–10 × 0.5–1.5 cm, base attenuate and decurrent onto the petiole, apex acute or obtuse, margin entire or slightly undulate, glabrous, with numerous cystoliths on both surfaces, lateral veins 8–11 pairs. Flowers 2–10 fasciculate in leaf axil, sessile. Bracts ovate, ca. 5 mm, apex acute, pubescent on margin, with numerous cystoliths; bracteoles narrowly ovate, ca. 3 mm, apex obtuse, pubescent on margins. Calyx narrowly campanulate, ca. 6 cmm, 5‑lobed to the middle; lobes linear‑lanceolate, apex acuminate, sparsely hispid‑ciliate. Corolla ca. 1 cm, pale purple, tube ca. 7 × 2 mm, glabrous, 2‑lipped, upper lip elliptic, ca. 3 mm, shallowly 2‑lobed, puberulent outside, lower lip obovate, ca. 3 mm, 3‑lobed to the middle, lobes ovate, apex obtuse. Stamens 4, included, didynamous; filaments glabrous, the longer pair ca. 5 mm, the shorter pair ca. 3 mm; anthers oblong, ca. 1 mm. Ovary glabrous; style filiform, slender, included, ca. 8 mm; stigma unequally 2‑lobed. Capsule narrowly oblong, acute, 8–10 × ca. 1.5 mm, 12–18‑seeded. Seeds orbiculate, ca. 1 mm long, glabrous.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Chuen Lung, Tai Po, Sai Kung. H. C. Tang 1083; L. T. Lo 177; HK sheet 35582.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; SE Asia.
Ecology: Streamsides and other wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Sep.–Nov.
Notes: The species was also reported as Hygrophila phlomoides Nees previously (Check List HK Plants 253. 2002; 87. 2004).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Pok Fu Lam, Tai Tam, Shing Mun, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Hypoestes purpurea (L.) R. Br. 槍刀藥
Prodr. 1: 474. 1810; FHK 265. 1861; FKH 200. 1912; FHN 3: 564. 1974; FTW ed. 2, 4: 665. 1998; FRPS 70: 249. 2002.
Justicia purpurea L., Sp. Pl. 16. 1753.
Peristrophe purpurea (L.) Hochr., Candollea 5: 234. 1934.
Hypoestes sinica Miq., J. Bot. Neerland 1: 117. 1861.

Spreading to erect perennial herbs or shrubs, up to 1.5 m tall. Stems erect or decumbent, young stems subquadrangular, sulcate, slightly puberulent. Petiole 1–3.5 cm, sparsely pubescent; leaf blades ovate to ovate‑elliptic, 5–13 × 1.5–7 cm, base narrowed and cuneate, apex acuminate or acute, margin entire or subundulate, adaxially green, sparsely pubescent, or glabrous except for pubescent along the veins and on the margin, abaxially pale green, glabrous, lateral veins 5–8 pairs. Spikes 1–3 cm, terminal or axillary, often crowded in large panicles, these forming a lax thyrse up to 7 cm, flowers numerous, often secund. Bract leaf‑like, spathulate, ca. 1.1 cm, petiolate, ciliate, bracteoles 4, abaxially sparsely pubescent, 2‑paired, outer pair connate above middle, forming an obconical involucres, ca. 8 mm, inner pair lanceolate, ca. 7 × 3 mm, glabrous, free from each other but partially adnate to outer pair, ca. 2.5 mm. Calyx ca. 5 mm, 5‑lobed to middle; lobes equal. ciliate. Corolla reddish purple, 2 – 2.5 cm, outside puberulent; limb 2‑lipped, upper lip lanceolate, subentire, lower lip triangularly obovate, shallowly 3‑lobed at tip. Stamens 2, much exserted; filaments flat, to 1.2 cm glabrous; anther‑thecae muticous. Ovary glabrous; style exserted, glabrous; stigma shallowly 2‑lobed, lobes equal. Capsule oblong‑ovoid, ca. 1 cm, glabrous, 4‑ or few‑seeded. Seeds ellipsoidal‑ovoid, tuberculate.

Locality: Pok Fu Lam, Tai Tam, Shing Mun, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 797, 1747; L. T. Lo 262.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Taiwan; Philippines.
Ecology: Thickets. Flowering: Aug.–Nov.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Tam, Happy Valley, Ma On Shan Country Park, Tai Po Kau, Kadoorie Farm
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Justicia adhatoda L. 鴨嘴花
Sp. Pl. 15. 1753; FHK 264. 1861; FKH 199. 1912.
Adhatoda vasica Nees, Pl. Asiat. Rar. 3: 103. 1832; FHN 3: 571. 1974; FRPS 70: 277. 2002.

Shrubs, to ca. 4 m tall. Stems thickened, subquadrangular, lenticellate, pubescent when young, soon glabrescent. Petioles 0.8 – 3 cm, puberulent; leaf blades ovate to elliptic‑ovate, 7 – 18 × 2 – 7 cm, base broadly cuneate, apex acuminate, sometimes slightly falcate, margin entire, adaxially densely tomentose when young, becoming glabrescent except for tomentose along the veins, abaxially puberulent, lateral veins 9 – 12 pairs, meet near the margin. Spikes terminal and axillary, 3 – 7 cm, ovate or broadly ovate in outline. Peduncles 3 – 7 cm. Bracts ovate‑oblong, 1 – 2 × 0.5 – 1.5 cm, apex acute, margin ciliate, puberulent, 3 – 7‑veined, imbricate; bracteoles linear‑lanceolate, 1 – 1.4 × 0.4 cm, apex acute, margin ciliate, puberulent, 3 – 5‑veined. Calyx 5‑lobed; lobes linear‑oblong, ca. 1 × 0.3 cm, narrowly scarious at margins, ciliate. Corolla white or pink, purplish or pinkish striped inside, 2.5 – 3 cm, broadly tubular, outside pilose; tube‑base cylindric, ca. 5 mm, faintly inflated and bent above; limb 2‑lipped, upper lip erect, ovate‑oblong, ca. 1.8 cm, shallowly 2‑lobed, lower lip spreading, oblong‑orbicular, 3‑lobed, middle lobe suborbicular, ca. 9 × 5 mm, lateral lobes ovate, ca. 8 × 4.5 mm. Stamens 2, exserted; filaments declinate, ca. 1.5 cm, glabrous except for silky hairy at base; anther‑thecae equal, elliptic, ca. 3.5 mm, superposed, lower one with a spherical appendage at base. Ovary pubescent especially at the tip; style ca. 2.5 cm, recurved, pubescent at lower part; stigma simple. Capsule obovoid, woody, 2.5 – 4 × 0.5 cm, stalked at base. Seeds orbicular, compressed.

Locality: Tai Tam, Happy Valley, Ma On Shan Country Park, Tai Po Kau, Kadoorie Farm. Y. S. Lau 2867; HK sheet 4281; S. Y. Hu 12970 (K).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan (cultivated or naturalized); native to India, widely cultivated in the tropics.
Ecology: Cultivated or naturalized. Flowering: Mar. – May.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal (folklore), dye.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Ho Chung, Sai Kung, Ng Tung Chai, Castle Peak
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Justicia austrosinensis H. S. Lo & D. Fang 華南爵床
Guihaia 17(1): 52. 1997.
Mananthes austrosinensis (H. S. Lo & D. Fang) C. Y. Wu & C. C. Hu, FRPS 70: 292. 2002.

Herbs, 40–70 cm tall. Stems quadrangular, sulcate, glabrous. Petioles 0.5–3 cm, bifariously pubescent or glabrescent; leaf blades broadly ovate or ovate‑elliptic, 7–15 × 2.5–7 cm, base cuneate and decurrent onto the petioles, apex short acuminate or acute, margin crenate or entire, glabrous, adaxially green, cystoliths numerous especially on the veins, abaxially pale green, lateral veins 5–8 pairs. Spikes mostly terminal or rarely axillary, 5–7 cm, usually 1–2  flowers subtending by one bract. Peduncles 1–3 cm, glabrous, cystoliths numerous. Bracts flabellate or broadly obovate, 5–8 × 7–9 mm, apex acuminate or obtuse, mucronate, margin ciliate; bracteoles subulate, ca. 3 mm, apex acuminate, margin ciliate. Calyx 5‑lobed almost to the base; lobes lanceolate, ca. 4 mm, apex acuminate, margin ciliate. Corolla yellowish green, ca. 1.3 cm, outside pilose, inside glabrous except few hairs on the filaments; limb 2‑lipped, upper lip erect, ovate‑triangular, ca. 6 × 3 mm, apex emarginate, lower lip 3‑lobed, lobes ovate, ca. 2 × 2 mm, apex rounded. Stamens 2, exserted; filaments glabrous, ca. 4 mm; anther‑thecae unequal, ca. 2 mm, superposed, lower one spurred at base, upper one muticous. Ovary ovoid, ca. 2 mm, glabrous; style ca. 1 mm, pilose. Capsule clavate, ca. 1.2 cm, pubescent, base solid stalked, 4‑seeded. Seeds ovate, ca. 2 mm, rugose.

Locality: Ho Chung, Sai Kung, Ng Tung Chai, Castle Peak. Y. S. Au 3265; HK sheet 21462; C. J. Huang 694 (IBSC); S. Y. Hu & P. P. H. But 23472 (PE).
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Jiangxi.
Ecology: Thickets in ravines. Flowering: Mar.–Jun.
Notes: The species was reported as Justicia glauca Rottler previously (Check List HK Plants 253. 2002; 87. 2004).

Justicia brandegeana Wassh. & L. B. Sm. 蝦衣草
Flora Il. Catarin. 102. 1969.
Beloperone gutta Brandegee, Univ. Calif. Publ. Bot. 4: 278. 1912, non Justicia gutta Wall., 1830.
Calliaspidia guttata (Brandegee) Bremek., Verh. Kon. Ned. Akad. Wetensch. Afd. Natuurk., Sect. 2, 45: 54. 1948; FHN 3: 571. 1974;FRPS 70: 274. 2002; Check List HK Plants 252. 2002; 86. 2004.
Drejerella guttata (Brandegee) Bremek., Philipp. J. Sci. 80: 14. 1952.

Herbs, 0.3–1 m tall, many‑branched. Stems quadrangular, brown, densely tomentose. Petioles 1–2 cm, tomentose; leaf blades ovate to ovate‑elliptic, 2–6 × 1–3 cm, base acuminate to rounded, decurrent onto the petioles, apex acute, margin entire, adaxially sparsely pubescent, abaxially densely greyish white tomentose, especially along veins, lateral veins 4–6 pairs. Spikes terminal, 2–7 cm, densely flowered, pendulous. Peduncles 5–7 mm, densely greyish tomentose. Bracts ovate, green when young, becoming wine‑red when old, 1.2–1.8 × 0.9–1.3 cm, base rounded or slightly cordate, apex acute, adaxially glabrous, margin entire and ciliate, abaxially greyish white tomentose, pinnately‑veined; bracteoles broadly lanceolate to elliptic, 0.8–1.3 × 0.5–0.7 cm, base cuneate, apex acute, margin entire and ciliate, adaxially glabrous, abaxially greyish white tomentose. Calyx white, densely pilose on both surfaces, 5‑lobed; lobes narrowly triangular, ca. 5 × 1 mm, apex acuminate, margin ciliate. Corolla ca. 3.2 cm, white, red spotted on throat, outside densely tomentose; tube slender, ca. 2 mm wide at base, then gradually widened to ca. 5 mm at the base of the lips; limb 2‑lipped, upper lip ca. 3.5 mm broad, entire or emarginate, lower lip ca. 5 mm broad, 3‑lobed, 3‑striped, lobes ovate, ca. 1 × 1 mm. Stamens 2, exserted; filaments ca. 2 cm; anther‑thecae divergent, 2 – 3 mm, superposed, spurred at base. Ovary comose; style ca. 1.5 cm, retrorsely pubescent. Capsule obovate, ca. 8 mm, stalked at base, pubescent, 2‑seeded. Seeds suborbicular, ca. 2 mm in diam., glabrous.

Locality: Cultivated. H. C. Tang 250, 1218; L. T. Lo 372.
Distribution: S China (cultivated); native to tropical America.
Uses: Ornamental.

Justicia carnea Lindl. 珊瑚花
Edward's Bot. Reg. 17: pl. 1397. 1831.
Cyrtanthera carnea (Lindl.) Bremek., Verh. Ned. Akad. Wetensch. Naturk. Afd. Sect. 2, 45(21): 50. 1948.
Jacobinia carnea (Lindl.) G. Nicholson, Ill. Dict. Gard. 2: 206. 1885.

Herbs or subshrubs, to 2 m tall. Stems subquadrangular, sulcate, glabrous or minutely puberulent. Petioles 1–2.5 cm; leaf blades membranous, oblong‑ovate, to 25 × 7 cm, sparsely puberulent, base cuneate to rounded and decurrent onto the petiole, apex acuminate. Spikes terminal, sessile, ovoid or spherical in outline, to 19 × 8 cm, densely flowered, 1–several flowers on each node; rachis puberulent. Bracts elliptic or oblong, to 2 × 1 cm, diminished in size upward, apex obtuse or rounded, moderately firm, glabrous, or sparsely hirsute, sparsely ciliate; bracteoles lanceolate, ca. 1.5 × 0.1–0.2 cm. Calyx 5‑lobed; lobes lanceolate, ca. 1 × 0.2 cm, subhyaline, glabrous, or sparsely hirsute and ciliate towards the apex. Corolla lilac or red, outside sparsely glandular‑puberulent, ca. 6.5 cm; tube‑base ca. 2.5 mm, gradually widened to ca. 5 mm wide at throat, upper lip erect, arched and bilobed at apex, lobes ca. 1 × 0.7 mm, lower lip spreading or recurved, 3‑lobed, cuneate, ca. 8 mm wide at base of the lobes, lobes ovate, ca. 3 × 2 mm. Anther‑thecae slightly superposed. Capsule unseen.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 32965.
Distribution: Native to Brazil, widely cultivated in the tropics.
Uses: Ornamental.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Mount Gough, Aberdeen, Pok Fu Lam, Victoria Peak, Beacon Hill, Ma On Shan
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Justicia championii T. Anderson ex Benth. 杜根藤
FHK 264. 1861, “Championi”; FKH 199. 1912.
Adhatoda chinensis Champ., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 5: 134. 1853, non Justicia chinensis L. ex Walp., 1845‑46.
Justicia chinensis (Champ.) Druce, Bot. Exch. Club Brit. Rep. 1916: 629. 1917, non L. 1753, nec Vahl 1791.
Calophanoides chinensis (Champ.) C. Y. Wu & H. S. Lo ex C. C. Hu, FRPS 70: 281. 2002.

Herbs, ca. 50 cm tall. Stems quadrangular, sulcate, retrorsely pubescent. Petioles (0–)0.5–1.5 cm, sulcate, pubescent; leaf blades elliptic to oblong‑elliptic, ovate, 1–4(–7) × 0.5–2(–3.5) cm, base cuneate or attenuate, apex acute or obtuse, margin entire, sparsely pubescent when young, soon glabrescent or pilose along the midvein abaxially, cystoliths numerous adaxially, lateral veins 3–6 pairs. Flowers 1–several clustered in leaf axils. Pedicels 2–4 mm, sparsely pubescent. Bracts leaf‑like, orbicular to obovate‑spathulate, 5–8 × 3–6 mm, petiolate, glabrous or adaxially sparsely pilose, apex rounded or obtuse, pinnately‑veined; bracteoles subulate or triangular, ca. 1 mm, apex acute, glabrous or sparsely yellow puberulent. Calyx 5‑lobed almost to the base; lobes linear‑lanceolate, 6–7 mm, ciliate, 1–2‑veined, yellowish white except for green along the veins. Corolla 0.8–1 cm, white, with purplish red streaks in 2 lines, outside puberulent, bilabiate, upper lip lanceolate, ca. 3.5 × 1.5 mm, apex emarginate, lower lip ovate, ca. 4 × 3 mm, 3‑lobed, middle lobe semi‑orbicular, ca. 0.8 × 1.3 mm, lateral lobes ovate, ca. 1.2 × 1 mm. Stamens 2, exserted; filaments ca. 4 mm, glabrous; anther‑thecae superposed, lower one spurred, upper one muticous. Ovary ellipsoidal, ca. 2 mm, glabrous; style ca. 6 mm, with a few hairs towards the base; stigma capitate. Capsule ca. 8 mm, glabrous, base with a solid stalk, 4‑seeded. Seeds oblong, ca. 2 × 1.5 mm, verrucose.

Locality: Mount Gough, Aberdeen, Pok Fu Lam, Victoria Peak, Beacon Hill, Ma On Shan. HK sheet 34775, 40194, 40897.
Ecology: Ravines. Flowering: Autumn.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Fujian.
Notes: The holotype specimen (J. G. Champion s.n., K) was collected by J. G. Champion from Victoria Peak between 1847 and 1850.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tsuen Wan, Shing Mun, Tai Po, Kiu Tsui
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Justicia gendarussa Burm. f. 小駁骨
Fl. Ind. 10. 1768; FHK 264. 1861; FKH 200. 1912; FTW ed. 2, 4: 665. 1998.
Gendarussa vulgaris Nees, Prodr. 11: 410. 1768; FHN 3: 569. 1974; FTW 4: 632. 1978; FRPS 70: 300. 2002.

Subshrubs, 0.7–1.5 cm tall, many‑branched. Stems subterete, tumid above the nodes, glabrous. Petioles 0.3–1 cm; leaf blades narrowly lanceolate, 6–10 × 1–1.5 cm, base cuneate, attenuate, apex acute or shortly acuminate, margin subsinuate, glabrous, lateral veins 5–8 pairs. Spikes 3–12 cm, interrupted, terminal or axillary, usually in a leafy panicle. Peduncles 0.5–1.5 cm. Bracts triangular, ca. 2 × 1 mm, apex acute, ciliate; bracteoles elliptic to linear‑lanceolate, ca. 3 × 1 mm, apex acute, ciliate. Calyx ca. 5 mm, 5‑lobed; lobes linear‑lanceolate, 3 – 4 × 0.5 mm, subequal, apex acuminate. Corolla creamy‑white, 1.2–1.5 cm, tube‑base cylindric, 8–9 mm; limb bilabiate, upper lip triangular, ca. 7 × 3.5 mm, violet‑blotched, 2‑fid, lower lip cuneate‑obovate, basally violet dotted, 6–10 mm broad, 3‑lobed, lobes oblanceolate, 3 – 5 × 3.5 mm. Stamens 2, exserted, filaments glabrous, 3–6 mm; anther‑thecae superposed, one slightly above the other, oblong, ca. 1.2 mm, lower one spurred at base, upper one muticous. Ovary ovoid, ca. 3 mm, glabrous; style ca. 1 cm, glabrous; stigma capitate, shortly 2‑lobed. Capsule clavate, ca. 1.2 cm.

Locality: Tsuen Wan, Shing Mun, Tai Po, Kiu Tsui. H. C. Tang 1260; Y. S. Lau 1132, 2944.
Distribution: S & SW China; SE Asia.
Ecology: Flowering: Spring.
Uses: Ornamental.

Justicia hayatai Yamam. 早田氏爵床
Suppl. Icon. Pl. Formosa 2: 35. 1926.
Justicia procumbens L. var. hayatai (Yamam.) Ohwi, Bull. Nat. Sci. Mus. Tokyo 33: 86. 1953; FTW ed. 2, 4: 667. 1998, as “hayatae”.
Rostellularia hayatai (Yamam.) S. S. Ying, Mem. Coll. Agr. Natl. Taiwan. Univ. 29(2): 45. 1989.
Justicia hayatai Yamam. var. ciliata Yamam., Suppl. Icon. Pl. Formosa 2: 35. 1926
Rostellularia procumbens (L.) Nees var. ciliata (Yamam.) S. S. Ying, Mem. Coll. Agr. Natl. Taiwan. Univ. 29(2): 45. 1989; FRPS 70: 307. 2002.
Justicia ciliata (Yamam.) C. F. Hsieh & T. C. Huang, Taiwania 19(1): 21. 1974; FTW 4: 696. 1978.

Herbs, 0.3–0.5 m tall. Stems quadrangular, sulcate, bifariously pubescent along sulci. Petioles 1–9 mm, glabrous; leaf blades ovate, 1.5–3.5 × 0.8–2 cm, base attenuate, decurrent onto the petioles, apex acute, glabrous, adaxially green, cystoliths numerous, abaxially pale green, without cystoliths, lateral veins 3–4 pairs. Spikes mostly terminal or axillary at upper leaf axils, 1–4 cm, elongate to 7 cm in fruit. Peduncles (0–)0.5–2 cm, glabrous. Bracts obovate‑elliptic, 4–5 × 2 mm, glabrous, apex acute, white‑margined; bracteoles lanceolate‑elliptic, ca. 5 × 1.2 mm. Calyx 4‑lobed almost to the base; lobes lanceolate, ca. 4 × 1 mm, glabrous, white‑margined. Corolla ca. 6 mm, glabrous, 2‑lipped to middle, upper lip ovate, 3 × 2 mm, apex emarginate, lower lip oblong, ca. 3 × 3 mm, minutely 3‑lobed. Stamens 2, exserted; filaments glabrous except for hairs at base, ca. 2.5 mm; anther‑thecae ovate, ca. 1.3 mm long, superposed, the lower one spurred at base, upper one muticous. Ovary ovoid, ca. 1.3 mm, glabrous; style ca. 6 mm, glabrous. Capsule oblong, ca. 4 mm, brownish yellow short stipitate, glabrous, 4‑seeded. Seeds ovate, ca. 1 mm, glabrous, rugose.

Locality: High Island, North Ninepin Island. F. W. Xing 9253, 9704 (IBSC).
Distribution: Taiwan.
Ecology: Flowering: Aug.; fruiting: Sep.–Oct.

Justicia procumbens L. 爵床
Sp. Pl. 15. 1753; FTW ed. 2, 4: 665. 1998.
Ecbolium procumbens (L.) Kuntze, Revis. Gen. Pl. 2: 484. 1891.
Rostellularia procumbens (L.) Nees, Pl. Asiat. Rar. 3: 101. 1832; FHK 265. 1861; FRPS 70: 305. 2002.

Procumbent herbs, 20–50 cm tall. Stems quadrangular, sulcate, pubescent. Petioles 3–8 mm, pubescent; leaf blades elliptic, ovate‑elliptic or elliptic‑oblong, 1.5–4 × 0.8–1.5 cm, base broadly cuneate to subrounded, or slightly decurrent onto the petioles, apex acute or obtuse, margin entire or slightly undulate, subglabrous or sparsely hispid, cystoliths numerous, lateral veins 3–6 pairs, prominent. Spikes terminal or axillary in upper leaf axils, 1–6 cm. Peduncles 0.5–7 cm, densely pilose. Bracts elliptic lanceolate, 4–5 × 1 mm, abaxially pilose, ciliate; bracteoles lanceolate, 4–5 mm, abaxially pilose, ciliate. Calyx 5–6 mm, 4‑lobed to the base; lobes linear, 1‑veined, with yellowish white margin, abaxially pilose along the veins, ciliate. Corolla pink or white, red spotted on the lower lip, ca. 7 mm, 2‑lipped, upper lip ca. 3 mm, apex emarginate, lower lip ca. 3 × 3.5 mm, 3‑lobed, lobes ovate, the middle lobe slightly larger, ca. 1 × 1–1.5 mm. Stamens 2, exserted; filaments glabrous, ca. 4 mm; anther‑thecae superposed, lower one spurred at base, the upper one muticous. Ovary pubescent; style ca. 5 mm, pubescent. Capsule ca. 5 mm, with a solid stalk at base, 4‑seeded. Seeds ovate, ca. 1 × 1 mm, rugose.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. P. S. Choi 430; Y. S. Lau 3152; Y. W. Lam 774.
Distribution: Area S of Qinling Range to Huaihe Valley; S & SE Asia to Australia.
Ecology: Wastelands and open fields. Flowering: Jun.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Happy Valley, Wong Nai Chung, Sai Kung, Sha Tin, Hin Tin, Ma On Shan Country Park, Chuk Kok, Sha Lo Tung
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Justicia ventricosa Wall. ex Sims. 黑葉小駁骨
Curtis's Bot. Mag. Pl. 2760. 1867; FHK 264. 1861; FKH 200. 1912.
Gendarussa ventricosa (Wall. ex Sims.) Nees, Pl. Asiat. Rar. 3: 104. 1832; FHN 3: 569. 1974; FRPS 70: 299. 2002.
Adhatoda ventricosa (Wall. ex Sims.) Nees, Prodr. 11: 107. 1847.

Perennial herbs or subshrubs, up to 1 m tall. Winter buds ovate, ca. 2 mm long, pubescent. Stems subterete, glabrous. Petioles 0.5–1.5 cm, sulcate, glabrous; leaf blades elliptic or obovate, 6–17 × 2–6 cm, base attenuate, apex shortly acuminate or acute, margin entire or slightly undulate, glabrous, midveins impressed adaxially, prominent abaxially, lateral veins 6 – 8 pairs, meet near the margin, prominent on both surfaces. Spike terminal, 5–10 cm, densely flowered, usually 1–3 flowers on each node. Peduncles ca. 1 cm. Bracts leaf‑like, broadly ovate or suborbicular, 1–1.5 × 0.8–1 cm, apex acute, pinnately‑veined, abaxially pilose or subglabrous, margin ciliate, imbricate; bracteoles linear, 3–5 × 1–2 mm, margin ciliate. Calyx 5‑lobed; lobes linear‑lanceolate, ca. 3 mm, ciliate. Corolla creamy white, purplish pink striped on the lips, 1.5 – 1.8 cm, outside pilose, inside pubescent; tube‑base cylindric, ca. 1 cm; limb 2‑lipped, upper lip oblong‑ovate, 2‑lobed, lower lip 3‑lobed, lobes ovate, ca. 2 × 1 mm, apex rounded. Stamens 2, exserted; filaments glabrous, ca. 6 mm; anther‑thecae ovate, subequal, superposed, lower one with white appendage. Ovary ovoid, ca. 3 mm, cymose; style ca. 1.6 cm, pilose at base. Capsule ca. 8 mm, pubescent, 4‑seeded.

Locality: Happy Valley, Wong Nai Chung, Sai Kung, Sha Tin, Hin Tin, Ma On Shan Country Park, Chuk Kok, Sha Lo Tung. H. C. Tang 101; Y. S. Lau 3211; C. Wright 372 (A).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; SE Asia.
Ecology: Thin forests and thickets. Flowering: Mar.–May.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Lepidagathis incurva Buch.‑Ham. ex D. Don 鱗花草
Prodr. Fl. Nepal. 119. 1825; FHN 3: 552. 1974; FRPS 70: 200. 2002.
Lepidogathis hyalina Nees, Pl. Asiat. Rar. 3: 95. 1832; FHK 263. 1861; FKH 199. 1912.

Herbs, 0.3–1 m tall, many‑branched. Stems quadrangular, sulcate, pubescent along sulcus and on nodes, soon glabrescent. Petiole 0.5–3.5 cm, glabrescent; leaf blades ovate to elliptic, 3–11 × 1–4.5 cm, base cuneate and obviously decurrent onto the petioles, apex acute or shortly acuminate, margin entire and slightly undulate, pubescent, soon glabrescent with few hairs or sparsely pubescent along veins, sparsely covered with cystoliths, the lateral veins 7–9 pairs. Spike (0.5–)1–3 cm, mostly terminal or axillary, one‑sided, usually 2–3‑clustered. Bracts whitish yellow, oblong‑lanceolate, 6–8 × 1.5–2 mm, apex long acuminate, abaxially scarious, puberulent, margin ciliate; bracteoles whitish yellow, similar to bracts, but smaller, ca. 6 × 1.5 mm. Calyx whitish yellow, 5‑lobed; lobes heteromorphic, linear‑lanceolate, abaxially scarious, puberulent or glabrescent, margin ciliate, anterior two ca. 7 × 1 mm, connate to the middle, posterior one slightly longer than others, ca. 8 × 1.5 mm, lateral ones smallest, ca. 6 × 0.8 mm, Corolla white, streaked with purple, ca. 0.8–1 cm, outside sparsely pilose, inside densely white pubescent below throat tube‑base cylindric, ca. 5 mm; limb 2‑lipped, upper lip erect, ovate, 2 × 3 mm, emarginate, lower lip 3‑lobed, lobes ovate, ca. 3 × 2 mm. Stamens 4, didynamous, inserted near middle of corolla tube, exserted from mouth of corolla; filaments ca. 2.5 – 3 mm, glabrous; anther‑thecae ovate, ca. 1 mm. Ovary ca. 1 mm, hispid at tip; style ca. 8 mm, subglabrous. Capsule ca. 5 mm, ovate‑oblong, 4‑angled, glabrous except for pilose at tip, 4‑seeded. Seeds ovate, ca. 1 mm, pubescent.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. P. S. Choi 167; K. L. Yip 4466; HK sheet 39399.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; SE Asia.
Ecology: Thickets, grasslands, roadsides. Flowering: Oct.–Mar. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Odontonema tubiforme (Bertol.) Kuntze 紅樓花
Revis. Gen. Pl. 2: 494. 1891, “tubaeforme”.
Justicia tubaeformis Bertol., Novi Comment. Acad. Sci. Inst. Bononiensis 4: 405. 1840.
Thyrsacanthus tubaeformis (Bertol.) Nees, Prodr. 11: 324. 1847.
Odontonema strictum (Nees) Kuntze, Revis. Gen. Pl. 2: 494. 1891; Check List HK Plants 254. 2002; 87. 2004.
Thyrsacanthus strictus Nees, Prodr. 11: 324. 1847.

Shrubs, to 3 m tall. Stems quadrangular, sulcate, sparsely pubescent. Petioles 0.5–3 cm, sulcate, glabrous; leaf blades ovate, elliptic or ovate‑elliptic, 7–22 × 3–10 cm, base cuneate, attenuate, slightly decurrent onto the petiole, apex acuminate to falcate, margin entire, subglabrous on both surfaces or sparsely pubescent abaxially, cystoliths conspicuous adaxially, lateral veins 6–9 pairs. Racemes 6–15 cm, sometimes branched basally and forming a panicle, 1–3 flowers on each node; peduncle 6–9 cm; rachis quadrangular, subglabrous to pubescent usually concentrated in 2 or more lines. Pedicels 2–6 mm, pubescent. Bracts lanceolate to linear‑subulate, 2–4 × ca. 1 mm, abaxially puberulent or glabrous; bracteoles subulate, 2–4 × ca. 1 mm, abaxially puberulent or glabrous. Calyx 2–4 mm, 5‑lobed; lobes subulate, 1–3 × 0.5–1 mm, abaxially puberulent or glabrous. Corolla red, 2.4–3.3 cm, outside glabrous; tube slender, 2.0 – 2.7 cm, limb 2‑lipped, upper lip 4 – 5 mm, 2‑lobed, lobes orbicular, 2–3 × ca. 1.5 mm, lower lip 4–5 mm, 3‑lobed, lobes elliptic to suborbicular, 3–4 × 2–3 mm. Stamens 2; stamens of thrum flower 1.2–1.5 cm, those of pin flower 6–8 mm; anthers oblong, 2–3 mm. Ovary glabrous; styles of thrum flower to 1 cm, styles of pin flower 1–1.6 cm, pubescent, stigma 2‑lobed, lobes ca. 0.3 mm. Capsules 1.7–2.3 cm, glabrous, basal stalks 0.7–1.1 cm. Seed suborbicular, subelliptic to broadly obovate, 4–5 mm, ca. 3 mm wide, bumpy to tuberculate.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 2638, 2660; Y. W. Lam 1121.
Distribution: Native to C America, widely cultivated in the tropics.
Ecology: Flowering: Jul.–Oct.
Uses: Ornamental.

Pachystachys lutea Nees 金苞花（黃鴨咀花）
Prodr. 11: 320. 1847.

Subshrubs, to 2 m tall. Stems slightly quadrangular, brownish yellow, glabrous. Petioles ca. 2 mm; leaf blades papery, oblong‑lanceolate, 7–16 × 1.5–5 cm, base attenuate, auriculate, apex acuminate, margin entire, glabrous, densely covered with claviform cystoliths especially along veins, lateral veins 5–7 pairs, netted near the margin. Spikes terminal or axillary, 5–9 cm. Peduncle ca. 1 cm. Bracts yellow or orange, ovate, 1.6–3 × 1–1.8 cm, glandular‑pilose along the entire margin, pinnately‑veined, densely imbricate; bracteoles yellow, ovate‑elliptic, ca. 1 × 0.3 cm, 3‑veined. Calyx yellow, ca. 6 mm, 5‑lobed almost to the base; lobes lanceolate, ca. 1 mm broad, glabrous or ciliate on margin. Corolla white, 4.5–5 cm, outside pilose and glandular‑punctate, 2‑lipped, upper lip erect, lanceolate, ca. 2 cm, slightly 2‑lobed, lower lip spreading, ovate, ca. 1.5 cm, 3‑lobed. Stamens 2, attached near the corolla base; filaments subequal to the corolla, exserted; anther 2‑thecous, thecae subequal, sagittate, ca. 4 mm. Staminodes 2, rudimentary. Ovary glabrous; styles ca. 4 cm, sparsely pilose at base. Capsule 4‑seeded. Seeds brown.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 34738.
Distribution: Native to Peru, widely cultivated in tropical and subtropical regions.
Ecology: Flowering: Jul.–Sep.
Uses: Ornamental.

Pseuderanthemum carruthersii (Seem.) Guillaumin 擬美花
Ann. Inst. Bot.‑Geol. Colon. Marseille, ser. 6, 5 – 6: 48. 1948.
Eranthemum carruthersii Seem., Fl. Vit. 185. 1866.
Pseuderanthemum atropurpureum (W. Bull) Radlk., Sitzungsber. Math.‑Phys. Cl. Königl. Bayer. Akad. Wiss. München 13(2): 286. 1883.
Pseuderanthemum carruthersii var. atropurpureum (W. Bull) Fosberg, Smithsonian Contr. Bot. 45: 26. 1980.

Shrubs, to 2.5 m tall. Stems quadrangular, sulcate, glabrous except for retrorsely pubescent at node. Petioles 0–7 mm; leaf blades leathery, ovate‑elliptic to elliptic, 2.5–8 × 1.5–5 cm, base rounded to attenuate, apex rounded to acute, margin entire, revolute. Spikes terminal, up to 12 cm, flowers 1–3 at each node. Rachis glabrous. Peduncles 1–7 mm. Pedicels 3–6 mm, glabrous or sparsely pubescent. Bracts elliptic to ovate to triangular, 1.5  4 × 1–1.5 mm, abaxially glabrous or sparsely pubescent with antrorse, short hairs (ca. 0.1 mm); bracteoles lanceolate‑ovate to triangular, ca. 1.5 mm, abaxially glabrous or pubescent. Calyx ca. 4 mm, 5‑lobed; lobes lanceolate to lanceolate‑subulate, 2–3 mm, abaxially pubescent. Corolla white with maroon spots within, 1.7–2 cm, outside glabrous; tube‑base cylindric, ca. 9 mm, upper lip 8–11 mm, 2‑lobed, lobes ca. 8 × 3 mm, lower lip 9–11 mm, lobes ca. 9 × 4–7 mm. Stamens 2, exserted; filaments ca. 6 mm, glabrous; anther‑thecae oblong, ca. 2 mm. Staminodes 2, 1–2 mm. Ovary glabrous; style included or exserted ca. 1 mm from the mouth of corolla, 9– 10 mm, pubescent; stigma 2‑lobed, lobes ca. 0.7 mm. Capsule not seen.

Pseuderanthemum carruthersii 'Variegatum' 斑葉擬美花
Pseuderanthemum atropurpureum ‘Variegatum’

This cultivar is characterized by variegated venation on its bronze-purple leaves, marked with cream-yellow, and pink flowers.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. HK sheet 41913.
Distribution: Native to Polynesia.
Uses: Ornamental.

Rhinacanthus nasutus (L.) Kurz 靈枝草（扭序花）
J. Asiat. Soc. Bengal. 2: 79. 1870.
Justicia nastus L., Sp. Pl. 16. 1753.
Rhinacanthus communis Nees, Pl. Asiat. Rar. 3: 109. 1832. nom. superfl.

Perennial herbs, 0.5–1 m tall, many‑branched. Stems erect, subquadrangular, faintly striate, densely pilose. Petioles 0.5–1.5 cm, densely pilose; leaf blades elliptic to ovate‑elliptic, rarely lanceolate, 2–11 × 0.8–3.5 cm, base cuneate, apex acute or acuminate, sometimes obtuse, margin entire or slightly undulate, adaxially sparsely pilose or subglabrous, marked with copious cystoliths, abaxially densely pilose, lateral veins 5–6 pairs, meet near the margin. Panicles lax, terminal and axillary, 4–8 cm; flowers subsessile, discrete at the ends of divaricate branches. Rachis pilose. Bracts lanceolate, ca. 2 × 0.5 mm; bracteoles subulate, ca. 1 mm. Calyx ca. 3 mm, glandular‑bristly, 5‑lobed almost to the base; lobes lanceolate, unequal. Corolla greenish white; tube slender, ca. 3 cm, curved from the middle upwards, outside hirsute with downward pointing hairs, tube‑base cylindric, ca. 2.5 cm; upper lip erect, linear‑lanceolate, shorter than lower lip, apex reflexed, shallowly 2‑lobed, lower lip to 12 mm broad, abaxially hispid, 3‑lobed to the middle, lobes obovate. Stamens 2, exserted; filaments glabrous; anther‑thecae oblong. Ovary and style sparsely pilose; style ca. 1.5 cm. Capsule ca. 2 cm, with long solid stalk, bristly with gland‑tipped hairs, 4‑seeded. Seeds orbicular‑helicoid, ca. 2.3 mm in diam., papillose.

Locality: Cultivated or naturalized. Y. S. Lau 492, 1358; M. T. Kao 6355 (CAS).
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; Vietnam, Thailand, Laos, Myanmar, India, Sri Lanka, Malesia, S Africa, Madagascar.
Ecology: Roadsides, thickets. Flowering: Dec.–Mar. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Ruellia coerulea Morong 蘭花草
Ann. New York Acad. Sci. 7: 193. 1893.
Cryphiacanthus angustifolius Nees, Prodr. 11: 199. 1847 non Ruellia angustifolia Sw.
Ruellia brittoniana Leonard, J. Wash. Acad. Sci. 31: 96. 1941, based on Cryphiacanthus angustifolius Nees; Check List HK Plants 254. 2002; 87. 2004.
Ruellia spectabils Britton, Ann. New York Acad. Sci. 7: 192. 1893, non Nicholson 1886, based on Cryphiacanthus angustifolius Nees.

Erect perennial herbs, 30–70 cm tall. Stems quadrangular, sulcate, glabrous except for pubescent on the nodes. Petioles 0.5–2 cm, sulcate, sparsely pubescent or glabrescent; leaf blades linear to linear‑lanceolate, 8–20 × 0.5–2 cm, base attenuate, apex acuminate, sometimes falculate, margin entire or slightly undulate, glabrous, cystoliths numerous, lateral veins 6–8 pairs, prominent on both surfaces. Inflorescence of expanded dichasia, axillary, 5–10 cm; peduncles 5–6.5 cm, glabrous. Pedicels 0.5–1 cm, glabrous. Bracts lanceolate to linear, 3–15 × 1–15 mm, glabrous, densely covered with cystoliths; bracteoles 2, at the middle of pedicels, linear to linear‑lanceolate, 0.6–1 × 1 cm, glabrous, abaxially densely covered with cystoliths, often caducous. Calyx 5‑lobed almost to the base; lobes ca. 1 cm, abaxially puberulent. Corolla blue to purplish blue, 2.5–3.8 cm, campanulate, outside densely pilose in bud, then gradually glabrescent; tube‑base cylindric, ca. 1 cm, gradually widened to ca. 2 cm at mouth; lobes oblong, ca. 6 × 5 mm. Stamens 4, didynamous, included; filaments of the longer pair ca. 9 mm, the shorter pair ca. 6 mm; anther‑thecae oblong, ca. 3 mm. Ovary glabrous; style ca. 2.5 cm, pubescent; stigma 2‑lobed, lobes unequal, the larger ca. 3 mm, the smaller ca. 0.3 mm. Capsule oblong, 2.5–3 cm, glabrous except for the pilose tip, 12–20‑seeded. Seeds lenticular, 2–2.5 × 2–2.3 mm, covered with hygroscopic hairs.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. W. Lam 846; HK sheet 34793, 38429.
Distribution: S China (cultivated and naturalized); native to Mexico.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Sep.
Uses: Ornamental.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Mount Parker, Cape D' Aguilar, Po Toi Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Rungia chinensis Benth. 中華孩兒草
FHK 266. 1861; FKH 200. 1912; FTW 4: 658. 1978; FTW ed. 2, 4: 676. 1998; FRPS 70: 258. 2002.

Spreading to erect herbs, up to 70 cm tall. Stems slender, quadrangular, sulcate, slightly puberulent, usually rooting at lower nodes. Petioles 0.5–3 cm, pubescent; leaf blades membranous, ovate to oblong‑lanceolate, 2.5–9 × 1.8–3 cm, base cuneate or attenuate, apex acute or obtuse, margin entire or slightly undulate, glabrous except for sparsely hirsute along the veins, lateral veins 5–6 pairs. Spikes terminal or axillary, 1–7 cm, 2‑sided. Bract 4‑ranked, dimorphic, outer sterile ones elliptic, ca. 6 × 2–4 mm, sparsely ciliate, inner fertile bracts obovate, or obovate‑oblong, 6–8 × 2.5–4 mm, apex acute; bracteoles orbicular or ovate, 6–7 × 4–5 mm, apex mucronate, margin membranous, sparsely ciliate. Calyx deeply 5‑lobed; lobes linear‑lanceolate, ca. 5 mm. Corolla bluish, 6 – 8 mm, outside slightly pilose and glandular‑punctate; limb 2‑lipped, the upper lip shallowly dentate, lower lip 3‑lobed, lobes ca. 7 mm. Stamens 2; anthers 2‑thecous, thecae subequal in size, lower theca has basal spur. Ovary 2‑locular; style ca. 1 cm, glabrous, stigma obtuse. Capsule ovoid ca. 6 mm, 4‑seeded. Seeds lenticular, ca. 1.5 mm wide, minutely tuberculate.

Locality: Mount Parker, Cape D’ Aguilar, Po Toi Island. Y. W. Lam 1999; HK sheet 40867.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Grasslands. Flowering & fruiting: Oct.–Feb. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The type specimens was collected by J. G. Champion from Mount Parker between 1847 and 1850.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Clear Water Bay, Sai Kung, Tseng Kwan O, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Rungia pectinata (L.) Nees 孩兒草
Prodr. 11: 470. 1847; FHN 3: 563. 1974; FRPS 20: 262. 2002.
Justicia pectinata L., Amoen. Acad. 4: 299. 1760.
Rungia parviflora var. pectinata (L.) Hand.‑Mazz., Symb. Sin. 7: 898. 1936.
Rungia parviflora subsp. pectinata (L.) Cramer, Handbook Fl. Ceylon 12: 105. 1998.

Annual or perennial herbs, sometimes erect but usually prostrate and rooting at nodes. Stems many‑branched, minutely pubescent. Petioles 0–7 mm; leaf blades oblong‑elliptic, 1–4 × 0.4–1.4 cm, base cuneate, apex acute, margin entire, glabrous except for few hairs on veins, lateral veins ca. 4 pairs. Spikes axillary or terminal, 0.5–2 cm, 1‑sided, sometimes 2 or 3 compounded. Bracts dimorphic, outer sterile bracts elliptic, apex obtuse or rounded, green, ca. 4 × 0.7 mm, apex acute, glabrous, inner fertile bracts broadly ovate to orbicular, 4–5 × 2 mm, apex obtuse or rounded, mucronulate, pubescent, broadly hyaline‑margined; bracteoles elliptic, 2–3 mm, subacute, margin ciliate, apex 2‑fid. Calyx colourless, pubescent, lobes linear‑lanceolate, ca. 3 × 0.5 mm, narrowly hyaline‑margined, apex mucronulate. Corolla blue or white, ca. 5 mm, outside pubescent, upper lip ovate, 1–2 mm, emarginate, lower lip 3‑lobed, lobes triangular. Stamens 2; filaments glabrous; anther‑thecae superposed, lower one spurred at base. Ovary 2‑locular. Capsule ellipsoidal, ca. 2.5 mm, apiculate, glabrous, 2– 4‑seeded. Seeds orbicular, ca. 1 mm in diam., minutely verrucose.

Locality: Clear Water Bay, Sai Kung, Tseng Kwan O, Lantau Island. F. W. Xing 9654; Y. W. Lam 1724; S. Y. Hu 12433 (K).
Distribution: S & SW China; India, Bhutan, Sri Lanka.
Ecology: Wastelands. Flowering: Sep.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Sanchezia parvibracteata Sprague & Hutch. 小苞黃脈爵床
Bull. Misc. Inform. Kew 1908: 253. 1908; FRPS 70: 275. 2002.

Shrubs, 1–3 m tall. Young stems quadrangular, sulcate, glabrous. Petioles 1–2 cm, pubescent, soon glabrescent; leaf blades oblong, 7–20 × 3–9 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, margin undulate, entire or serrulate, adaxially glabrous, cystoliths numerous, yellow along the midvein and lateral veins, abaxially pale green, densely pubescent when young, then soon glabrescent or sparsely pilose along veins, lateral veins 8–12 pairs. Inflorescence of terminal dichasia spikes, 4–12 cm long. Peduncles 1–2.5 cm. Rachis quadrangular, sparsely pubescent. Bracts red or orange, ovate, 1–2.5 × 0.6–0.8 cm, apex acute, glabrous, abaxially densely covered with cystoliths; bracteoles ovate‑elliptic, 1.3–1.5 × 0.3–0.4 cm, glabrous, abaxially densely covered with acerose cystoliths, 3‑veined. Calyx ca. 1.5 cm, 5‑lobed almost to the base, lobes oblanceolate, unequal, 1–2 mm wide, apex obtuse, glabrous except for pilose upward, abaxially densely covered with cystoliths. Corolla yellow or orange, 4 – 5 cm, outside densely white pilose, tube 3.5–4.5 cm × 7–8 mm, lobes recoiled, 2–3 mm long. Stamens 2, exserted; filaments ca. 5 cm long, pubescent; anther thecae mucronate for ca. 1 mm at base. Staminodes 2, unequal, 2–2.3 cm long. Ovary ovoid, ca. 4 mm long; style 5–6 cm long, pilose towards the base; stigma 2‑lobed, lobes unequal, the larger ca. 3 mm long, smaller ca. 0.5 mm. Capsule 1.1–1.4 cm long, glabrous except for pilose at the tip.

Locality: Cultivated. K. Y. Chan 1337 (CHUK); S. Y. Hu 5495 (CUHK).
Distribution: S China (cultivated); native to Ecuador, widely cultivated in tropics.
Ecology: Flowering: Feb.–May.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: The plant was identified as Sanchezia nobilis Hook. previously but Sanchzia parvibracteata has much larger bracts than that species.

Staurogyne concinnula (Hance) Kuntze 糙葉叉柱花
Revis. Gen. Pl. 2: 497. 1897; FTW ed. 2, 4: 686. 1998; FRPS 70: 38. 2002.
Ebermaiera coninnula Hance, J. Bot. 1868: 200. 1868; FKH 197. 1912.

Perennial dwarf herbs, ca. 15 cm tall; stem generally short, partially underground, 0.5–6 cm long, usually simple, rarely few‑branched, terete, densely short pubescent. Leaves rosulate at the base of stem; petioles 0.3–3 cm, pubescent; leaf blades oblanceolate, 1.5–7 × 0.5–1.5 cm, base gradually attenuate, apex obtuse or rounded, margin obscurely undulate, adaxially green, scarious, sometimes pubescent along the veins, abaxially glaucous, pubescent along the veins, lateral veins 5–8 pairs, prominent abaxially. Spikes 1–4, axillary, sometimes loosely branched, forming a panicle of 5–15 cm; branches slender, with 3–10 interrupted flowers. Pedicels 1–4 mm, pubescent. Bracts linear to linear‑oblanceolate, 2–4 mm, apex obtuse or subacute; bracteoles 2, at the middle of pedicel, linear, ca. 2 mm, apex obtuse. Calyx campanulate, 5‑lobed almost to the base; lobes linear or linear‑lanceolate, unequal, 5–6 mm, apex acute, accrescent to 7 mm in fruit, glabrous except for minutely pilose on the margin. Corolla ca. 1 cm, white, tubular‑funnelform; tube ampliate, ca. 6 × 4 mm, 5‑lobed; lobes subequal, orbicular, ca. 3 mm. Stamens 4, included, didynamous; filaments glabrous, the longer pair ca. 5 mm, shorter pair ca. 2.5 mm; anthers ellipsoidal, ca. 1.5 mm, thecae equal. Ovary ellipsoidal, glabrous; style filiform, ca. 5 mm; stigma subulate. Capsule oblong, 4–5 × 1.5 mm, glabrous, shorter than persistent calyx, many‑seeded. Seeds suborbicular, ca. 0.2 mm.

Locality: Hok Tau. HK sheet 35393, F. W. Xing 10190 (IBSC).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan.
Ecology: Streamsides, forests. Flowering & fruiting: Mar.–Apr.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Tam, Lan Nai Wan, Wong Nai Chung, Pok Fu Lam
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Strobilanthes apricus (Hance) T. Anderson ex Benth. 山一籠雞
FHK 262. 1861; FKH 198. 1912.
Gutzlaffia aprica Hance, Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 1: 142. 1849; FRPS 70: 101. 2002; Fl. Guizhou. 10: 231. 2004; FYN 16: 675. 2006.
Phlebophyllum apricum (Hance) Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 5: 131. 1853.

Isophyllous perennial herbs or shrubs, to 70 cm tall. Stem quadrangular, sulcate, retrorsely white hirsute. Petiole 0.5–1 cm, slightly white pubescent or subglabrous; leaf blades leathery, elliptic to oblong‑elliptic, 2–7 × 1–3 cm, base rounded or broadly cuneate, apex acute, margin entire, ciliate, adaxially scabrous, hispid, especially on veins, abaxially yellowish silky tomentose, or glabrous except for the pubescent midvein, lateral veins 5 – 7 pairs. Spikes capitate, terminal or axillary; upper ones sessile or the lower ones with peduncle to 7 cm. Bracts subleathery, ovate‑lanceolate, 1.3–1.5 × 0.3–0.5 cm, apex acuminate, adaxially glabrous, abaxially and margin covered with white multicellular hairs; bracteoles linear, 1–1.1 × 0.1 cm, abaxially and margin sparsely covered with large‑celled hairs, adaxially glabrous, both surfaces covered white cystoliths. Calyx 1–1.3 cm, 5‑lobed almost to the base; lobes linear, with large‑celled multicellular hairs on margin, abaxially pubescent or subglabrous, adaxially glabrous. Corolla purple or white, ca 3.5 cm, outside glabrous, inside glabrous except for pilose retaining styles, basal cylindric tube ca. 1.3–1.5 cm, abruptly inflated to ca. 1 cm in diam. and cystiform; limb 5‑lobed, lobes subequal, suborbicular, ca. 5 × 5 mm, apex obtuse. Stamens 2, exserted; filaments glabrous, ca. 1 cm; anthers elliptic, ca. 2.5 mm. Ovary narrowly oblong, white, pilose at the tip, 2 ovules per locule; style ca. 3.5 cm, curved, pilose. Capsule oblong, ca. 1 cm, glabrous except for few hairs at tip, 4‑seeded. Seeds ovate, ca. 2 mm, convex on both surfaces, pubescent, soon glabrescent, areola large.

Locality: Tai Tam, Lan Nai Wan, Wong Nai Chung, Pok Fu Lam. H. C. Tang 1400; Y. S. Lau 255, 1464; F. W. Xing 8615, 9748 (IBSC).
Ecology: Dry forests, thickets on slopes. Flowering: Jul.–Jan. of the following year; fruiting: Mar.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Jiangxi; Vietnam, Thailand.
Notes: The type specimen was collected by H. F. Hance from Tai Tam, Hong Kong Island in 1840s.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Mount Parker, Sai Kung, Shing Mun, Fo Tan, Ma On Shan, Kwun Yam Shan Tsuen, Ng Tung Chai, Kop Tong
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Strobilanthes cusia (Nees) Kuntze 馬藍
Revis. Gen. Pl. 2: 499. 1891; FTW ed. 2, 4: 678. 1998.
Goldfussia cusia Nees, Pl. Asiat. Rar. 3: 38. 1832.
Dipteracanthus calycinus Champ. ex Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 5: 133. 1853, non Strobilanthes calycina Nees, 1836.
Strobilanthes championi T. Anderson ex Benth., FHK 261. 1861. Based on Dipteracanthus calycinus Champ.
Strobilanthes flaccidifolius Nees, Prodr. 11: 194, 1847; FKH 198. 1912;
Baphicacanthus cusia (Nees) Bremekamp., Verh. Ned. Akad. Wetensch. Afd. Naturk. Sect. 2, 41(1): 59, 190. 1944; FHN 3: 549. 1974; FRPS 70: 113. 2002.

Isophyllous herbs, 0.5–1.5 m tall. Stem erect, branched, glabrous or minutely brown puberulent. Petioles 0.5–3 cm; leaf blades papery, elliptic to ovate, 4–20 × 2–9 cm, base attenuate, apex acute, margin serrate, glabrous or abaxially minutely puberulent along veins, adaxially dark green, abaxially paler, black when dry; lateral veins 7–9 pairs. Spike 10–30 cm, usually branched and forming a leafy terminal panicle. Bracts leaf‑like, oblanceolate or spathulate, 1.2–2.5 cm, petiolate, deciduous with flower; bracteole linear‑oblanceolate, 2–3 mm, deciduous before bracts. Calyx 0.8–1.5 mm in flower, accrescent to 2.5 cm in fruit, minutely puberulent, 5‑lobed almost to the base, 4 lobes linear, acute, one spathulate and much longer. Corolla blue, glabrous, 3.5–4. cm, straight, base cylindric, 1–1.5 cm, gradually widened to ca. 1.5 cm at mouth, lobes subequal, oblong, ca. 6 × 6 mm. Stamens 4, didynamous, included, filaments glabrous, the longer pair ca. 7 mm, the shorter pair ca. 3 mm; anther oblong, ca. 3 mm; staminode absent. Ovary oblong, with 2 ovules per locule, apex puberulent with few glandular‑tipped hairs; styles ca. 3.2 cm, glabrous. Capsule 1.5–2.2 cm, glabrous, 4‑seeded. Seeds ovate, 3.5 mm, covered with hairs; areola small, glabrous.

Locality: Mount Parker, Sai Kung, Shing Mun, Fo Tan, Ma On Shan, Kwun Yam Shan Tsuen, Ng Tung Chai, Kop Tong. Y. S. Lau 1337; HK sheet 35337, 39052.
Distribution: S, SW & E China; SE Asia.
Ecology: Forests and wet places in ravines. Flowering & fruiting: Nov.–Feb. of the following year.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal (folklore), dye.
Notes: The holotype specimen (Champion s.n., K) of Dipteracanthus calycinus was collected by J. G. Champion from Mount Parker, Hong Kong between 1847 and 1850.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Shing Mun, Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Strobilanthes dalzielii (W. W. Sm.) Benoist 曲枝馬藍
Notul. Syst. (Paris) 5: 109. 1935; Fl. Indo-Chine 4: 679. 1935.
Acanthopale dalzielii W. W. Sm., Notes Roy. Bot. Gard. Edinburgh 11: 193. 1919.
Championella dalziellii (W. W. Sm.) Bremek., Verh. Ned. Aked. Werensch. Afd. Natuurk. II 41(1): 150. 1944.
Pteroptychia dalziellii (W. W. Sm.) H. S. Lo, FHN 3: 547, 592. 1974; FRPS 70: 194. 2002; FYN 16: 733. 2006.

Anisophyllous perennial herbs or shrubs, 0.4–1 m tall. Stems erect, slender, zigzag, branched, slightly pubescent or subglabrous. Leaves unequal in each pair, the smaller 1/3 to 1/2 of the larger in size; petiole very short, ca. 3 mm, or sessile; leaf blades ovate or ovate‑lanceolate, the larger 9–14 × 3–5 cm, the smaller 2–5 × 1–2 cm, membranous, base rounded, or cordate for upper leaves, apex acuminate or acute, sometimes falculate, margin serrate, adaxially green, glabrous, cystoliths prominent, abaxially glaucous, glabrous or sparsely pubescent along the veins, lateral veins 3–5 pairs. Spike terminal and axillary, 2–5 cm, 2–5‑flowered. Rachis usually zigzag, sparsely white puberulent, flowers distant, usually only one flower in each pair. Bracts linear‑lanceolate, ca. 3 × 1 mm, 1‑veined, glabrous; bracteoles linear, ca. 5 × 1 mm, glabrous or puberulent with glandular‑tipped hairs. Calyx ca. 1 cm, densely white pilose at base and along the midvein, 5‑lobed almost to the base, lobes linear. Corolla purplish blue or white, 3.5–4.5 cm, curved, outside densely white pilose in bud, inside glabrous except for hairs retaining the style, tube‑base cylindric, ca. 1 cm, ventricose and gradually widened to 1–1.5 cm at mouth; lobes suborbicular, ca. 8 mm in diam. Stamens 4, didynamous, slightly exerted; filaments hirsute, the longer pair ca. 8 mm, the shorter pair ca. 5 mm; anther oblong, ca. 2 mm. Ovary glabrous, with 2 ovules in each locule; style ca. 3.2 cm, pilose. Capsule linear‑oblong, compressed, ca 1.8 cm, apiculate, glabrous, 4‑seeded. Seeds ovate, ca. 2 × 2 mm, densely appressed tomentose; areola very small.

Locality: Shing Mun, Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai. L. T. Lo 186, 283;; P. S. Choi 257; F. W. Xing 7456, 7757 (IBSC).
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian; Vietnam.
Ecology: Streamsides and other wet places. Flowering: Aug.–Dec.
Notes: The species was reported as Strobilanthes divaricatus (Nees) T. Anderson previously (Check List HK Plants 255. 2002; 88. 2004).

Strobilanthes dimorphotricha Hance 球花馬藍
J. Bot. 21: 355. 1883.
Goldfussia dimorphotricha (Hance) Bremek., Verh. Nederl. Akad. Wetensch., Amst., Afd. Natuurk., Sect. 2, 41(1): 231, 274. 1944.

Anisophyllous perennial herbs, 0.4–1.5 m tall, many‑branched. Stems somewhat zigzag upward, glabrous or yellowish pubescent. Leaves unequal in each pair, the smaller about 1/3 to 2/3 of the larger in size; petiole 0.5–1.5 cm, sparsely pubescent or glabrous; leaf blades elliptic, elliptic‑lanceolate, ovate, papery, the larger ones 4–15 × 1.5–4.5 cm, the smaller ones 1.5–2.5 × 0.5–1.5 cm, base cuneate or attenuate, apex acuminate or caudate, margin serrulate, adaxially dark green, white appressed pubescent, cystoliths slightly prominent, lineolate, abaxially glabrous, or whitish pubescent along the veins, with or without multicellular hairs, lateral veins 5–7 pairs. Spikes terminal or axillary, very compact, head‑like, subspherical in outline, 2–3‑flowered, usually 1–3 forming a forked panicle. Peduncles ca. 2.5 cm, glabrous or pubescent. Bracts ovate‑elliptic, 1–1.3 cm, apex acute or acuminate, glabrous, caducous; bracteoles lanceolate, ca. 5 mm, caducous. Calyx 7–9 mm, accrescent to 15–17 mm, 5‑lobed almost to the base; lobes lanceolate, glandular pubescent. Corolla purple‑red, 3 – 4 cm, slightly curved, outside subglabrous or sparsely pilose, inside glabrous except for hairs retaining the style, tube‑base cylindric, ca. 5 mm, ventricose and gradually widened to ca. 1.5 cm at mouth; lobes subequal, orbicular, 5–6 mm in diam., apex emarginate. Stamens 4, didynamous, included; filaments glabrous, the longer pair unequal, erect, 5–7 mm, the shorter pair equal, incurved, ca. 2 mm; anther spherical, ca. 1 mm in diam. Ovary pilose, 2 ovules in each locule; style ca. 3.5 cm, pilose. Capsule oblong‑clavate, 1.4–1.8 cm, glandular‑pubescent, 4‑seeded. Seeds lenticular, ca. 2.5 × 2.5 mm, pubescent.

Locality: Tai No, Ho Chung. P. S. Choi 370; HK sheet 31572.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests and other wet places in ravines. Flowering: Aug.–Dec.; fruiting: Dec.–Feb. of the following year.
Notes: The species was reported as Strobilanthes penstmonoides (Nees) T. Anderson (2002) and Strobilanthes pentastemonoides (Nees) T. Anderson (2004) previously (Check List HK Plants 255. 2002; 88. 2004).

Strobilanthes tetraspermus (Champ. ex Benth.) Druce 四子馬藍
Rep. Bot. Exch. Club Brit. Isles 1916: 649. 1917; FFJ 5: 133. 1993; Fl. Guizhou. 10: 249. 2004.
Ruellia tetrasperma Champ. ex Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 5: 132. 1853.
Championella tetrasperma (Champ. ex Benth.) Bremek., Verh. Ned. Aked. Werensch. Afd. Natuurk. Sect. 2, 41(1): 163. 1944; FHN 3: 546. 1974; FRPS 70: 94. 2002.
Acanthopale tetrasperma (Champ. ex. Benth.) Hand.‑Mazz., Beih. Bot. Centralbl. LVI, B: 454. 1937.
Strobilanthes radicans T. Anderson, FHK 262. 1861; FKH 198. 1912, nom. illeg., based on Ruellia tetrasperma Champ.
Acanthopale radicans (T. Anderson) C. B. Clarke ex Benoist, Fl. Indo‑Chine 4: 673. 1953, nom. illeg.

Isophyllous herbs, 30–50 cm tall. Stems suffrutescent, often procumbent, and rooting at base, quadrangular, sulcate, retrorsely pubescent along sulci, glabrescent. Petioles 0.5–2.5 cm, sulcate, glabrous; leaf blades ovate, elliptic or oblong, papery, 1.5–11 × 1–4.5 cm, base attenuate or decurrent onto the petiole, apex acuminate or acute, margin serrate or dentate, glabrous, densely covered with cystoliths, lateral veins ca. 5 pairs. Spike short and abbreviated, head‑like or slightly elongate, few‑flowered. Bracts leaf‑like, obovate or spathulate, 1–1.5 × 0.4 – 0.5 cm, pinnately‑veined, sparsely pilose; bracteoles linear, 5–6 × 1 mm, abaxially glabrous or sparsely pilose, densely covered with cystoliths; Calyx 5‑lobed almost to the base; lobes linear, 5–7 × 1 mm, accrescent to ca. 8 mm in fruit, glabrous except for large‑celled hairs on the margin, densely covered with cystoliths. Corolla purple or purplish blue, 1.5–2 cm, straight, funnel‑shaped, outside pubescent, inside villose, tube‑base cylindric, ca. 5 mm long and ca. 2 mm, gradually widened to 1.5 cm at mouth; lobes oblong, ca. 4 × 5 mm, apex obtuse. Stamens 4, didynamous, included; filaments of longer pair ca. 5 mm, sparsely pubescent, the shorter pair ca. 2 mm, glabrous; anthers oblong, ca. 2 mm; staminodes short or absent. Ovary ovoid, ca. 3 mm, hispid at tip, 4 ovules per locule; style ca. 1.5 cm, hirsute; stigma 2‑lobed, lobes unequal. Capsule oblong, 0.7–1 cm, pubescent at tip, 4‑seeded. Seeds ovate, ca. 2 × 2 mm, pubescent.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 157; Y. W. Lam 1868; F. W. Xing 9772, 10033 (IBSC).
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian.
Ecology: Forests in ravines. Flowering: Aug.–Dec.
Notes: The holotype specimen (Champion 17, holotype, K) was collected by J. G. Champion from Victoria Peak, Hong Kong between 1847 and 1850.

Thunbergia alata Bojer ex Sims 翼葉老鴉嘴
Bot. Mag. 52: pl. 2591. 1825; FKH 197. 1912; FRPS 70: 24. 2002.

Herbaceous vine; stems subquadrate to flattened, bisulcate, pubescent. Petioles winged, 1.5–3 cm, sparsely pubescent; leaf blades sagittate to deltoid ovate, 2–7.5 × 2–6 cm, base hastate to cordate, apex acute, margin entire or undulate, adaxially sparsely strigose, abaxially hirsute; palmately 5‑veined. Flowers solitary, axillary. Peduncles 2.5–3 cm, sparsely strigose. Bracts subulate; bracteoles ovate, 1.5–1.8 × 1–1.4 cm, apex acute or acuminate, obtuse, 5–7‑veined, abaxially hirsute. Calyx annular, unequally 10–13‑lobed. Corolla 2.5–4.5 cm, orange with dark purple glandular “eye” in throat; tube‑base cylindric, 2–4 mm wide, gradually widened to ca. 4 cm at mouth; lobes obovate, apex truncate. Stamens 4, didynamous; filaments glabrous, ca. 4 mm; anther thecae unequal, 3.5–4 mm, pubescent at margin and base. Ovary glabrous; styles ca. 8 mm, glabrous; stigma 2‑lobed; lobes unequal, the upper one erect, the lower one spreading. Capsules pubescent, ca. 7 × 10 mm, beak ca. 1.4 cm, base ca. 3 mm wide. Seeds 2, reticulate on the dorsal surface.

Locality: Cultivated or naturalized. Y. S. Lau 2021, 2201; Y. W. Lam 512.
Distribution: Cultivated and naturalized in S & SW China; native to tropical Africa, now widely cultivated and naturalized in the tropical regions of the world.
Ecology: Flowering: Oct.–Apr. of the following year.
Uses: Ornamental.

Thunbergia erecta (Benth.) T. Anderson 硬枝老鴉嘴
J. Proc. Linn. Soc., Bot. 7: 18. 1864; FHN 3: 542. 1972; FRPS 70: 24. 2002.
Meyenia erecta Benth., Niger Fl. 476. 1848.

Erect shrubs, 1–2 m tall, many‑branched; younger stems quadrangular, greyish brown, winged, glabrous or pubescent on the node. Petioles 2–5 mm, subglabrous; leaf blades leathery or thick papery, ovate or ovate‑lanceolate, sometimes rhomboid, 2.5–9 × 1–5 cm, base cuneate, apex acute or acuminate, margin entire or sparsely serrate towards the apex, sometimes undulate, sparsely pilose or subglabrous, pinnately‑veined, lateral veins 4–6 pairs, netted near the margin. Flowers solitary or in pairs, axillary. Peduncles 1.5–2.5 cm, glabrous. Bract subulate; bracteoles oblong‑ovate, 1–2 × 0.5–0.8 cm, base obtuse, apex acute, glabrous or minutely puberulous at the apex. Calyx 12–15‑lobed; lobes unequal, ca. 1 mm, glandular‑pubescent. Corolla 5.5–6 cm, white, purplish or deeply violet with a white or yellowish throat, outside glabrous, tube‑base cylindric, ca. 1 cm long and 3 mm wide, gradually widened to 2.5–3 cm at mouth; lobes oblong ovate, subequal, ca. 1.5 × 1 cm. Stamens 4, didynamous, filaments glabrous, the longer pair ca. 1.2 cm, the shorter pair ca. 0.7 cm; anther thecae oblong, ca. 4 mm, with a short awn‑like appendage at base, puberulous at margin and base. Ovary glabrous; styles ca. 3.5 cm, sparsely puberulous towards the apex; stigma unequally lobed, the upper lobe erect and angular. Capsules glabrous, ca. 0.9 cm long, 1.2 cm broad, beak ca. 2 cm.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 1149, 3227; L. T. Lo 93; S. Y. Hu & P. P. H. But 20583, 21048 (KUN).
Distribution: Cultivated in Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; native to W tropical Africa, cultivated elsewhere in tropical regions.
Ecology: Cultivated. Flowering: Oct.–Apr. of the following year.
Uses: Ornamental.

Thunbergia fragrans Roxb. 碗花草
Pl. Coromandel 1: 47, pl. 67. 1795; FKH 197. 1912; FRPS 70: 30. 2002.
Thunbergia bodinier Lev., Repert. Spec. Nov. Regni Veg. 12: 21. 1913.

Herbaceous vines. Stems subquadrate to flattened, sulcate, hirsute. Petioles 0.5–4.5 cm, hirsute; leaf blades papery, oblong‑ovate to oblong‑lanceolate, 4–14 × 3–7 cm, base rounded, sometimes cuneate or cordate, apex acute to acuminate, margin entire to irregularly sinuate to shallowly and coarsely dendate, puberulous on both surfaces, gradually subglabrescent, palmately 5‑veined. Flowers solitary, axillary. Peduncles 3–5.5 cm. Bracts subulate; bracteoles ovate, 1.5–2.5 × 0.8–1.5 cm, apex acute, puberulous, persistent. Calyx unequally 10 – 13‑dentate, glabrous. Corolla white, sparsely puberulous, tube‑base cylindric, 4–7 mm wide, gradually widened to ca. 2 cm at mouth; lobes obovate, ca. 2.5 × 2.3 cm, 7–9‑veined. Stamens 4, included; filaments glabrous; anther‑thecae lanceolate, divergent. Ovary glabrous; style exerted; stigma funnel‑shaped. Capsules glabrous, brown, ca. 0.7 × 1 cm, beak ca. 1.5 cm. Seed smooth.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 677, 1260, 3117; E. Bodinier 1318 (E); M. S. Clemens 4267 (E).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Taiwan; native to India and Sri Lanka, widely cultivated and naturalized in tropical regions of the world.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Sep.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: The type specimen of Thunbergia bodinieri was collected by E. Bodinier from Hong Kong on 4 Sep. 1895.

Thunbergia grandiflora Roxb. 大花老鴉嘴
Bot. Reg., 6: pl. 495. 1820; FHK 260. 1861; FKH 197. 1912; FHN 3: 543. 1972; FRPS 70: 26. 2002.

Woody vines, up to 8 m or longer. Stem sulcate, glabrous or pilose. Petioles 1–7 cm, sulcate, pubescent; leaf blades papery, ovate or triangular‑ovate, 5–10 × 4–8 cm, base subcordate or truncate, apex acuminate to acute, margin undulate or irregularly lobed below the middle, rarely entire, pubescent, palmately 5–7‑veined. Flower solitary or paired in leaf axil, or in terminal panicle. Pedicles 4 –7 cm, sulcate, pubescent. Bracts subulate; Bracteoles oblong or ovate, 2.5–3 cm, apex acute with a short mucro, glabrous, margin ciliate, 5–7‑veined. Calyx annular, unlobed. Corolla bluish, 4–6 cm, abaxilly glabrous, tube‑base cylindric, ca. 7 × 3 mm, gradually widened to ca. 5 cm at mouth, limb 5‑lobed; lobes ovate, ca. 3 × 2.5 cm. Stamens 4, filaments 7–9 mm, anthers appendaged basally, pubescent dorsally. Ovary glabrous, stigma 2‑lobed; lobes subequal. Capsule pubescent, ca. 1.3 cm in diam., beak ca. 2.5 cm. Seeds ovoid, compressed, verrucose.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 729, 1884; HK sheet 32226.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian; SE Asia.
Ecology: Thickets, sometimes cultivated. Flowering: Mar. – Oct.
Uses: Ornamental.

Thunbergia laurifolia Lindl. 桂葉老鴉嘴
Gard. Chron. 1856: 260. 1856; FRPS 70: 28. 2002.
Thunbergia grandiflora (Roxb. ex Rottl.) Roxb. var. laurifolia (Lindl.) Benoist, Fl. Indo‑Chine 4: 618. 1935.
Thunbergia harrisii Hook., Bot. Mag. t. 4998. 1857.

Herbaceous or woody vines. Stems subquadrangular, glabrous. Petioles 0–3 cm, sulcate; leaf blades oblong, oblong‑lanceolate or lanceolate, subleathery, 7–16 × 1.5–6 cm, base rounded or broadly cuneate, apex acuminate or caudate, margin entire or irregularly undulate, glabrous, palmately 3‑veined. Racemes terminal or axillary. Pedicels 1–2 cm. Bracts subulate, ca. 4 × 1 mm, glabrous; bracteoles oblong‑elliptic, 2 – 2.5 × 0.9 – 1.2 cm, apex acuminate, abaxially densely pubescent upward. Calyx annular, unlobed. Corolla 4.5–6 cm; tube‑base white, cylindric, 1–1.3 cm × ca. 3 mm, gradually widened to ca. 3 cm at mouth; lobes bluish, orbicular, ca. 2 cm in diam. Stamens 4, included; filaments thickened basally; anthers‑thecae acute apically, pubescent dorsally. Ovary and style glabrous, style ca. 2.5 cm. Capsule ca. 1.5 × 1.5 cm, beak ca. 3 cm.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 2109; P. S. Choi 116; E. Bodinier 1417 (E); S. Y. Hu 9337 (K).
Ecology: Flowering: Mar.
Distribution: Guangdong, Fujian (cultivated); native to India, cultivated in other tropical regions.
Uses: Ornamental.

Sesamum indicum L. 芝麻（脂麻、巨勝）
Sp. Pl. 2: 634. 1753; FKH 196. 1912; FRPS 69: 63, pl. 18: 6 – 7. 1990; FFJ 5: 94, fig. 103. 1993; FOC 18: 226. 1998; FGD 4: 407, fig. 248. 2000.
Sesamum orientale L., Sp. Pl. 2: 634. 1753; FGZ 611, fig. 325. 1956.

Annual herb, erect, 0.75–1(–1.5) m tall. Stems 4‑angled, branched or unbranched, pith hollow or white.
