Leaves opposite or alternate; those on lower branches ovate to oblong‑ovate, 4–16 × 2–15 cm, base obtuse or rotund, apex mucronate or subrotund, margin lobed or tripartite; those on middle branches serrate at margin; those on upper branches ovate, oblong‑ovate or lanceolate to linear, 3–9 × 0.5–2.5 cm. Flowers white or mauve‑pink, bilabiate. Calyx persistent, 5‑parted to near base, lobes 4.5 – 8 mm, pubescent. Stamens inclusive. Ovary superior, 4(–8)‑locular, pubescent. Capsule erect, ellipsoidal, 1.8–2.8 × 0.6–0.7 cm, beak broad. Seeds many, 2.5–3 mm long, white or black.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 409, 3255; Y. W. Lam 1554.
Distribution: Cultivated in China; possibly native to India or Africa, widely cultivated.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Oct.
Uses: Oil, medicinal (folklore), edible.
Notes: According to Z. Y. Wu et al. (Acta Phytotax. Sin. 45: 458 – 472. 2007), the Chinese name “hu ma” (胡麻) should refer to Linum usitatissimum L. (亞麻) of the Linaceae.

Campsis grandiflora (Thunb.) Schum. 凌霄
Nat. Pflanzenfam. 4(3b): 230. 1894; FHN 3: 530, fig. 907. 1974; FRPS 69: 33, pl. 1: 1 – 3. 1990; FFJ 5: 82, fig. 90. 1993; FOC 18: 220. 1998.
Bignonia grandiflora Thunb., Fl. Jap. 253. 1784.
Bignonia chinensis Lam., Encycl. 1: 423. 1785.
Tecoma chinensis K. Koch, Dendr. 2: 307. 1872.
Campsis chinensis (Lam.) Voss., Vilm. Blumengart. ed. 3, 801. 1895.

Stems woody. Leaf rachis 4–13 cm; leaflets 7–9; petiolules 1–5(–10) mm, with a cluster of hairs between petiolules; leaf blade ovate to ovate‑lanceolate, 3–6(–9) × 1.5–3(–5) cm, base broadly cuneate, apex caudate‑acuminate, both surfaces glabrous, densely glandular abaxially; lateral veins 6–7 pairs. Thyrses large, lax. Peduncle to 20 cm. Flowers 4–6.5 cm. Calyx campanulate, ca. 3 cm, divided halfway; lobes triangular, ca. 1.5 cm, acuminate. Corolla red adaxially, orange‑red abaxially, ca. 5 cm in diam.; lobes semi‑orbicular, flat and erect. Stamens inserted at base of corolla tube; filaments linear, 2–2.5 cm; anthers divergent, yellow. Style linear, ca. 3 cm; stigma compressed, 2‑lobed. Capsule apex obtuse.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 2384.
Distribution: Areas S of Changjiang, Henan, Shandong, Hebei, Shaanxi (cultivated or wild); Japan, India, Pakistan and Vietnam.
Ecology: Flowering: May –Aug.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal (folklore).

Crescentia alata H. B. & K. 十字架樹
Nov. Gen. Sp. (quarto ed.) 3: 158. 1818 [1819]; FRPS 69: 58, pl. 16. 1990; FFJ 5: 86, fig. 94. 1993.

Small tree, 5–12 m tall, to 25 cm in d.b.h. Branches glabrous, terete, fissured. Leaves leathery, clustered on brachyblasts, usually simple leaves and digitately 3( – 5)‑foliolate compound leaves on the same brachyblast. Simple leaves subsessile, linear to elliptic‑linear, 1.9–3.2 × 0.3–1 cm, similar to leaflets or petiole of compound leaves. Compound leaves: petiole winged, 2.7–11.5 × 0.3–1.5 cm, oblanceolate, lepidote; leaflets subsessile, oblanceolate, 1–4.5 × 0.3–1.2 cm, base cuneate to broadly cuneate, apex rotund or emarginate, margin entire, lepidote and glabrous on both surfaces. Flowers solitary or in clusters of 2 on stems. Pedicels lepidote, 5–8 mm. Calyx divided to base, lobes 2, ovate, 1.5–2 cm, subequal, glabrous, slightly lepidote at base, often with impressed plateform glands. Corolla yellowish brown, with purplish red patches and stripes, campanulate, swollen at one side, tube 2.8–5.5 cm; limb 5‑lobed, lobes broadly triangular, 1–1.5 cm, apex mucronate, glandular‑lepidote abaxially. Fertile stamens 4, slightly exserted, thecae partly divergent. Ovary conical, glabrous and lepidote, 5–6 mm; ovules in many rows on 4 lateral placentations. Style filiform, exserted. Berries subglobose, 7 –10 cm. Seeds small, thin, 6–7 × 7–9 mm, not winged.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 1224; HK sheet 32500, 39028.
Distribution: S & SW China (cultivated); native to Mexico to Costa Rica, widely cultivated in tropical Asia.
Ecology: Flowering: Summer to autumn.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal (folklore).

Jacaranda mimosifolia D. Don. 藍花楹
Bot. Reg. 8: 631, t. 631. 1822; FRPS 69: 56. 1990; FFJ 5: 91, fig. 100. 1993.
Jacaranda acutifolia auct. non Humb. & Bonpl.: FGZ 609. 1956; FHN 3: 533. 1974.

Deciduous tree to 15 m tall, 45 cm in d.b.h.; bark grey. Leaves 2‑pinnately compound, 15–30 cm, pinnae over 10 pairs; pinnae 5–10 cm, leaflets 16–24 pairs; leaflets small, papery, sessile, narrowly elliptic, 0.6–1.2 × 0.2–0.7 cm, base cuneate, apex abruptly acuminate, margin entire, slightly revolute, glabrous or puberulent along veins and margin. Panicles terminal, many‑flowered. Calyx campanulate, ca. 1 mm, apex 5‑dentate. Corolla bilabiate, bluish purple, tube tubular‑campanulate, 3–4 mm, white adaxially, throat 0.7–1.2 cm wide, lobes 0.3–0.8 cm, pubescent abaxially. Stamens didynamous; filaments pubescent at lower half; anthers 1‑celled, ca. 2 mm; staminodes 2 – 2.5 cm, glandular hairy at upper part. Pistil 2.2–2.5 cm; ovary 2 – 3.5 mm, glabrous. Capsule orbicular, ca. 5 cm in diam.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 1830; HK sheet 21204.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Yunnan (cultivated); native to Brazil, widely cultivated in tropical regions of the world.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr.–Jun.
Uses: Ornamental.

Markhamia stipulata (Wall.) Seem. ex K. Schum. var. kerrii Sprague 貓尾木
Kew Bull. 1919: 310. 1919; FOC 18: 224. 1998.
Markhamia cauda‑felina (Hance) Benth. & Hook. ex Hemsl., J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 26: 235. 1890; FGZ 611, fig. 324. 1956.
Dolichandrone cauda‑felina (Hance) Benth. & Hook. f., Gen. Pl. 2: 1046. 1876; FHN 3: 534, fig. 912. 1974; FYN 2: 722, pl. 200: 2 – 3. 1979; FRPS 69: 50, pl. 14: 3 – 4. 1990; FFJ 5: 87, fig. 95. 1993; Check List HK Plants 256. 2002; 88. 2004.
Spathodea cauda‑felina Hance, Journ. Bot. 10: 257. 1872.
Dolichandrone stipulata var. kerrii (Sprague) C. Y. Wu & W. C. Yin, FYN 2: 724. 1979; FRPS 69: 52, pl. 14: 2. 1990.

Tree 5–15 m tall. Young branches, leaves, and peduncles yellowish brown pubescent to tomentose. Leaves 40– 50 cm, exstipulate, often with rudimentary simple leaves at the base of petiole; leaflets 3 – 9 pairs; petiolules 1–3 mm or subsessile; leaf blades papery, oblong, elliptic‑oblong, elliptic‑lanceolate or ovate‑lanceolate, 5–28 × 4–9 cm, base rounded, apex caudate‑acuminate, margin entire to serrulate, rusty yellow pubescent when young, glabrescent adaxially, pubescent to puberulent abaxially; lateral veins 8–9 pairs; petiolules 1–4 mm or leaflets subsessile. Racemes rusty yellow pubescent, 4–10‑flowered. Flowers 10–12 cm in diam. Pedicel 2–6 cm. Calyx 3.3–5.5 cm, yellowish brown tomentose to floccose, apex with 6–8 black tubercles. Corolla dark purple, yellow at upper part, funnelform, ca. 10 cm; tube red‑brown or purple on lower part, 1.5–2 cm in diam. at base; mouth 10–15 cm in diam.; lobes irregularly wrinkled. Stamens and style included; staminodes present or absent. Capsule linear, compressed, 30–70 × 2–3 cm, densely yellowish brown tomentose or floccose. Seeds long elliptic, including wing 3–5 × 1–1.3 cm.

Locality: Cultivated. H. C. Tang 2102; Y. S. Lau 644, 1708.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan (cultivated or wild); Thailand, Laos, Myanmar, Vietnam.
Ecology: Flowering: Oct.–Nov.; fruiting: Apr.–Jun.
Uses: Environmental (landscaping).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Sai Kung, Tai Po Kau, Lam Tsuen
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Oroxylum indicum (L.) Benth. ex Kurz 木蝴蝶（千層紙）
Forest Fl. Burma 2: 237. 1877; FOC 18: 215. 1998.
Bignonia indica L., Sp. Pl. 2: 625. 1753.
Bignonia pentandra Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 2: 379. 1790.
Calosanthes indica (L.) Blume, Bijdr. Fl. Ned. Ind. 760. 1826.
Oroxylum indicum (L.) Vent., Dec. Gen. Nov. 8. 1808, nom. inval; FKH 196. 1912; FGZ 610. 1956; FHN 3: 533, fig. 911. 1974; FYN 2: 696, pl. 194: 1 – 3. 1979; FRPS 69: 11, pl. 4: 1 – 3. 1990; FFJ 5: 92, fig. 101. 1993; Check List HK Plants 257. 2002; 88. 2004.

Trees 6–10(–15) m tall, 15–20 cm in d.b.h. Bark greyish brown. Leaves 2–3(–4)‑pinnately compound, borne nearly at stem apex, 50–150 cm; petiolules 5–20 cm; leaflets ovate to elliptic, 5–14 × 3–10 cm, base subrounded or cordate, oblique, apex short acuminate, glabrous, becoming blue after drying; lateral veins 5 – 6 pairs. Inflorescences 40–150 cm. Flowers usually open at night, with foul smell. Pedicel 2–7 cm, bracteolate. Calyx purple, campanulate, 2.2–4.5 × 2–3 cm, glabrous, leathery, becoming subwoody in fruit. Corolla purple‑red; tube fleshy, 4 – 4.5 cm; mouth 5.5 – 8 cm in diam.; upper lip 2‑lobed, lower lip 3‑lobed, lobes slightly reflexed. Stamens inserted at middle of corolla tube; filaments ca. 4 cm, slightly exserted from corolla tube, tomentose basally. Disk large, fleshy, 5‑lobed, 4–5 mm thick, ca. 1.5 cm in diam. Style 5–7 cm; stigma 2‑parted, ca. 7 mm. Capsule woody, 40–120 × 5–9 cm, ca. 1 cm thick; valves with midrib, margin convex. Seeds orbicular, 6–7 × 3.5 –4 cm including white membranous wing.

Locality: Sai Kung, Tai Po Kau, Lam Tsuen. S. T. Dunn 1173; HK sheet 21143.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan, Sichuan, Yunnan, Guizhou; tropical Asia.
Ecology: Forests near villages. Flowering: Sep.–Nov.; fruiting: Nov.–Jan. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), environmental.

Pyrostegia venusta (Ker‑Gawl.) Miers 炮仗花
Proc. Roy. Hort. Soc. London 3: 188. 1863; FRPS 69: 3, pl. 3: 4 – 5. 1990; FFJ 5: 84, fig. 92. 1993.
Bignonia venusta Ker‑Gawl., Bot. Reg. t. 249. 1818.
Pyrostegia ignea (Vell.) C. Presl, Bot. Bemerk. 93. 1845; FGZ 606, fig. 322. 1956; FHN 3: 530, fig. 906. 1974.

Stems robust, ridged; branchlets sulcate. Petiole ca. 2 cm; leaflets 2–3; petiolules 1–2.5 cm; leaf blades papery, ovate, 4.5–10 × 2.5–5 cm, base rounded, apex long acuminate, margin entire; glabrous and finely glandular on both surfaces; lateral veins 3–4 pairs; terminal leaflet often modified into a 3‑branched tendril. Panicles terminal, 10–12 cm. Calyx campanulate, ca. 7 mm, 5‑dentate. Corolla tubular, orange‑red, 7–8 cm, with a ring of white hairs at middle adaxially, base constricted, upper part bilabiate, upper lip 2‑lobed, lobes ca. 8 mm, erect, lower lip 3‑lobed, lobes long elliptic, ca. 1.6 cm, reflexed, margin white pubescent. Filaments filiform, anthers divergent. Ovary cylindric; style slender, exserted; stigma 2‑lobed, lobes lingulate, flat. Capsules long cylindric; valves leathery, boat‑shaped. Seeds in many rows, with membranous wing.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 2097.
Distribution: S & SW China (cultivated); native to Brazil, widely cultivated in tropical regions.
Ecology: Flowering: Jan.–Jun.
Uses: Ornamental.

Spathodea campanulata P. Beauv. 火焰樹
Fl. Oware 1: 47 – 48, t. 27, 28. 1805; FRPS 69: 23, pl. 7. 1990; FFJ 5: 88, fig. 96. 1993.

Tree to 12 m; bark greyish brown. Branches appressed puberulent when young, subglabrous and greyish white lenticellate when old. Leaves with petiole to 45 cm; leaflets (3–)9–13(–17), subsessile, elliptic to obovate, 5–10 × 2.5–5 cm, base subrounded, apex acuminate, entire, subglabrous on both surfaces; lateral veins 5 – 7 pairs. Inflorescences terminal, dense; rachis ca. 12 cm, brown puberulent. Pedicels 2–4 cm. Bracts lanceolate, ca. 2 cm. Bracteoles 2, 0.2–1 cm. Calyx spathaceous, tomentose abaxially. Corolla orange‑red to bright red, campanulate; tube swollen at one side; lobes erect, broadly ovate, unequal, corrugated, 3 × 3–4 cm. Stamens exserted; filaments 5–7 cm; anthers ca. 8 mm. Ovary glabrous; style 6 cm; stigma 2‑lobed; lobes ovate‑lanceolate. Capsule blackish brown, 15 – 25 × 3.5 cm. Seeds suborbicular, with peripheral wing.

Locality: Cultivated. H. C. Tang 125; L. T. Lo 29.
Distribution: S China (cultivated); native to Africa, widely cultivated in tropical regions of the world.
Ecology: Flowering: Jan.–May.
Uses: Environmental.

Tabebuia chrysantha (Jacq.) G. Nicholson 黃鐘木（風鈴木）
Ill. Dict. Gard. 4: 1. 1887.
Tabebuia chrysotricha (Mart ex DC.) Standl., Field Mus. Nat. Hist., Bot. Ser. 11(5): 176. 1936.

Small tree, semi‑deciduous, 5 – 10 m tall, erect, many‑branched, crown umbellate. Leaves opposite, palmately compound, with 4 – 5 leaflets, ovate, papery, margin serrate, covered with fine pubescence. Cyme terminal; flowers bisexual, zygomorphic, 5‑merous; calyx tube irregularly lobed; corolla golden yellow, funnelform; stamens 4, didynamous, attached to corolla, anther 2‑celled, splitting by longitudinal slits. Pistils 2, connate; ovary 2‑locular. Capsule linear, dehiscing loculicidally. Seeds winged.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 3283; HK sheet 34328, 39962.
Distribution: S China (cultivated); native to tropical America.
Ecology: Flowering: Spring.
Uses: Ornamental.

Tecoma stans (L.) Juss. ex Kunth 黃鐘花
Nov. Gen. Sp. (quarto ed.) 3: 144. 1818 [1819]; FGZ 610. 1956; FFJ 5: 89, fig. 98. 1993.
Bignonia stans L., Sp. Pl. ed. 2, 871. 1763.
Stenolobium stans (L.) Seem., Ann. Mag. Nat. Hist. 10: 30. 1862; FYN 2: 706. 1979; FRPS 69: 55, pl. 15: 4 – 6. 1990.

Erect shrub to 6 m. Leaves odd‑pinnately compound, 10–20 cm; leaflets 3–13, sessile or subsessile, oblong‑ovate to lanceolate, 4–10 × 3–5 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate to caudate, margin serrate, subglabrous adaxially, densely grey tomentose abaxially. Inflorescences racemose‑paniculate to 15 cm. Peduncles, pedicels, bracteoles and calyx hairy. Bracts subulate, ca. 1 mm. Calyx campanulate, 5‑dentate. Corolla yellow to orange‑yellow, tube narrowed at base, lobes 5, spreading, wavy at margin; anthers hairy. Ovary terete; style slender, stigma 2‑lobed, lobes lingulate. Capsules 8–10 × 0.5 cm.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 1623.
Distribution: S China (cultivated); native to America, widely cultivated in tropical regions of the world.
Ecology: Flowering: Autumn to winter.
Uses: Ornamental.

Utricularia aurea Lour. 黃花狸藻
Fl. Cochinch. 1: 26. 1790; Taylor, Fl. Males. ser. 1, 8: 296, fig. 21 – 23. 1977; Taylor, Kew Bull. Add. Ser. 14: 623, fig. 190. 1989; FRPS 69: 604. 1990; FTW ed. 2, 4: 719, pl. 329, photo 368. 1998.
Utricularia flexuosa Vahl, Enum. Pl. 1: 198. 1804; FHK 255. 1861; FKH 191. 1912.

Floating small herbs, with filiform, branched stolons, extending to 30 cm or longer. Leaves all submerged and root‑like, alternate on stolons, 2–8 cm long, pinnately divided, each pinna dichotomously divided into numerous capillary segments, interspersed with little globular traps or bladders. Traps obliquely ovoid, 1–4 mm, stalked. Scapes usually 7–15 cm, bearing a raceme of 3–6(–10) flowers; scales absent; bracts basifixed. Pedicels erect and slender at flowering time, turned downward at fruiting time. Calyx deeply bilobed; lobes ovate, unequal, enlarged and spreading in fruit. Corolla yellow, 10–15 mm, upper lip broadly ovate, apex rounded, about twice the length of upper calyx‑lobe, lower lip larger, transversely elliptic; the spur obtuse, about the length of lower corolla‑lip. Ovary ovoid; style distinct. Capsule globose, 4–5 mm in diam., circumscissile; persistent style about twice as long as the capsule.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Yuen Long. W. J. Tutcher 8130; HK sheet 20925.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; E to S Asia and Australia.
Ecology: Ponds and paddy fields. Flowering: Apr.–Nov.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Sheung Shui, Sai Kung, Lo Wu, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Utricularia bifida L. 挖耳草
Sp. Pl. 18. 1753; FHK 256. 1861; FKH 192. 1912; Taylor, Fl. Males. ser. 1, 8: 281, fig. 4. 1977; Taylor, Kew Bull. Add. Ser. 14: 307, fig. 82. 1989; FRPS 69: 588, pl. 162: 4 – 10. 1990; FTW ed. 2, 4: 721, pl. 331. 1998.

Small marsh herbs, with branched capillary stolons. Leaves alternate on stolons, linear to linear‑oblanceolate, 7–20(–30) × 1–4 mm, base tapering into a short petiole, apex or obtuse, margin entire, membranous, 1‑veined. Traps borne on stolons and leaf margins, globose, 0.5–1 mm, short‑stalked. Scapes usually 10–20 cm, bearing a raceme of 1–10(–16) flowers; scales present, similar to the bracts; bracts basifixed, ovate, 1–2 mm. Pedicels 2–5 mm, initially spreading, turned downward at fruiting time, usually flat and dilated under the calyx. Calyx deeply bilobed; lobes slightly unequal, 3–4 mm at flowering time, 5–6 mm in fruit. Corolla yellow, 6–10 mm long, upper lip oblong to oblong‑obovate, apex rounded, lower lip suborbicular; the spur subulate, about the length of lower corolla‑lip. Ovary ovoid; style short. Capsule broadly ellipsoidal, ca. 2.5 mm long, opening by longitudinal slits.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Sheung Shui, Sai Kung, Lo Wu, Lantau Island. S. P. Lau 40, 2318; Y. S. Lau 738.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Hubei, Henan, Shangdong, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; S to SE Asia to Australia.
Ecology: Marshes. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Jan. of the following year.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Ma On Shan, Ho Pui, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Utricularia caerulea L. 短梗挖耳草
Sp. Pl. 18. 1753; Taylor, Fl. Males. ser. 1, 8: 287, fig. 12. 1977; Taylor, Kew Bull. Add. Ser. 14: 187, fig. 43. 1989; FRPS 69: 593, pl. 163: 8 – 11. 1990; FTW ed. 2, 4: 724, pl. 332. 1998.
Utricularia racemosa Wall. ex Walp., Nov. Actorum Acad. Caes. Leop.‑Carol. Nat. Cur. 19(Suppl. 1): 401. 1843; FHK 256. 1861; FKH 192. 1912.

Annual marsh herbs, with branched capillary stolons, usually without any leaves at flowering time. Leaves borne on stolons nodes and at the base of scape, linear to linear‑obovate, 3–20 × 0.5–2 mm, base tapering into a short petiole, apex rounded, margin entire, membranous, 1‑veined. Traps borne on stolons and leaf margins, ovoid, 0.25–1 mm, stalked. Scapes usually 5–20 cm, bearing a raceme of 1–10(–16) flowers; scales few, similar to the bracts; bracts attached just above the middle, free and pointed at both ends. Pedicels very short, 0.2–1 mm. Calyx deeply bilobed; lobes unequal, upper lobe oblong, 2–3 mm, lower lobe shorter, transversely elliptic. Corolla violet, pink or white, 4–10 mm, upper lip oblong to ovate‑oblong, apex retuse, lower lip broadly ovate, apex rounded or emarginate; the spur narrowly conical, usually slightly longer than the lower corolla‑lip. Ovary globose; style short. Capsule globose or ellipsoidal, 1.5–2 mm, opening by longitudinal short slits.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Ma On Shan, Ho Pui, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 2453; Y. W. Lam 956, 1254.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Shandong, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; S & SE Asia to Australia.
Ecology: Marshes. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Jan. of the following year.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Happy Valley, Sha Tin, Tung Chung
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Utricularia gibba L. 少花狸藻
Sp. Pl. 18. 1753; FTW ed. 2, 4: 724, pl. 333. 1998.
Utricularia exoleta R. Br., Prodr. 430. 1810; Taylor, Fl. Males. ser. 1, 8: 294, fig. 20. 1977; Taylor, Kew Bull. Add. Ser. 14: 572, fig. 179. 1989; FRPS 69: 598. 1990; Check List HK Plants 258. 2002; 89. 2004.
Utricularia diantha Roxb. ex Roem. & Schult., Mant. 1: 169. 1822; FHK 256. 1861; FKH 191. 1912.

Floating small herbs, with filiform, branched stolons seldom above 5 cm long. Leaves all submerged and root‑like, alternate on stolons, 0.5–1.5 cm long, unbranched or dichotomously divided into a few capillary segments. Traps lateral on leaf segments, ovoid, 1–2.5 mm, stalked. Scapes slender, 5–10 cm, bearing a raceme of 1–2(– 3) flowers; scales 1, similar to the bracts; bracts basifixed. Pedicels erect or spreading, 2–12 mm. Calyx bilobed nearly to the base; lobes broadly ovate to suborbicular, subequal, 1.5–2 mm. Corolla yellow, 4–8 mm long, upper lip orbicular or broadly ovate, about twice the length of upper calyx‑lobe, apex obscurely 3‑lobed, lower lip slightly smaller; the spur conical, as long as the lower corolla‑lip, or slightly longer. Ovary ovoid; style distinct. Capsule globose, 2–3 mm in diam., opening by valves.

Locality: Happy Valley, Sha Tin, Tung Chung. HK sheet 4216, 38212.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; widely distributed in tropical and subtropical regions.
Ecology: Ponds and paddy fields. Flowering: Jun. – Nov.; fruiting: Jul.–Dec.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Happy Valley, Tai Tam, Victoria Peak, Shing Mun, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Utricularia striatula Sm. 圓葉挖耳草
Cycl. 37: Utricularia no. 17. 1819; Taylor, Fl. Males. ser. 1, 8: 289, fig. 13 – 14. 1977; Taylor, Kew Bull. Add. Ser. 14: 479, fig. 147. 1989; FRPS 69: 595, pl. 163: 1 – 5. 1990; FTW ed. 2, 4: 727, pl. 369. 1998.
Utricularia orbiculata Wall. ex A. DC., Prodr. 8: 18. 1844; FHK 256. 1861; FKH 192. 1912.
Utricularia harlandii Oliv. ex Benth., FHK 257. 1861; FKH 192. 1912.

Perennial lithophytic or marsh herbs, with simple, capillary stolons. Leaves borne on stolon nodes and clustered near the base of scape, persistent to the time of flowering; petioles slender, usually longer than the blade; leaf blades orbicular to transversely elliptic, 3–10 × 2–6 mm, base broadly cuneate to rounded, apex rounded, margin entire, membranous, with dichotomous veins. Traps borne on stolons, ovate, 0.6 – 0.8 mm, stalked. Scapes usually 5 – 15 cm, bearing a raceme of 1–10 flowers; scales few, similar to the bracts; bracts attached just below the middle, narrowly ovate or oblong, 1–1.5 mm. Pedicels 2–6 mm, initially spreading, turned downward after anthesis. Calyx deeply bilobed; lobes unequal, upper lip suborbicular or broadly obcordate, 1.5– 2.5 mm, apex rounded or emarginate, lower lip much smaller, oblong‑elliptic. Corolla lilac or white, 5–10 mm long, upper lip smaller, subobovate, apex 2‑toothed, lower lip orbicular to transversely elliptic, apex 3–5‑lobed; the spur subulate, about the length of lower corolla‑lip. Ovary globose; style short. Capsule broadly ellipsoidal, ca. 2.5 mm long, opening by longitudinal slits.

Locality: Happy Valley, Tai Tam, Victoria Peak, Shing Mun, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 1463; HK sheet 34406, 40768.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, SE Xizang, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; tropical Asia and Africa.
Ecology: Marshes and rocks by streams. Flowering: Jun.–Oct.; fruiting: Jul.–Nov.
Notes: The syntype specimens of Utricularia harlandii (Harland 307, K; Wilford 92, K) were collected from Hong Kong Island around 1857.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Cape D'Aguilar, Bride's Pool, Pat Sin Leng, Sai Kung, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Utricularia uliginosa Vahl 濕地挖耳草
Enum. Pl. 1: 203. 1804; Taylor, Fl. Males. ser. 1, 8: 282, fig. 5. 1977; Taylor, Kew Bull. Add. Ser. 14: 333, fig. 92. 1989; FTW ed. 2, 4: 729, pl. 335. 1998.
Utricularia affinis Wight, Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 1: 373, t. 1580. 1849.
Utricularia caerulea auct. non L.: FHK 256. 1861; FKH 192. 1912.

Small marsh herbs, with slender, simple, or rarely branched stolons, usually without any leaves at flowering time. Leaves alternate on stolons, linear to narrowly obovate, 25–45 × 1.5–6 mm, base attenuate, apex rounded to acute, margin entire, membranous, 3‑veined. Traps borne on stolons and leaf margins, globose, 1–1.5 mm, stalked. Scapes usually 3–12(–15) cm, bearing a raceme of 1–10 flowers; scales few, similar to the bracts; bracts basifixed, narrowly ovate, 0.8–1 mm. Pedicels filiform, 1–1.5 mm, lengthening to 5 mm in fruit, usually flat or narrowly winged. Calyx deeply bilobed; lobes subequal, broadly ovate or suborbicular, 2–2.5 mm, thin and membranous. Corolla lilac, violet or white, 3–7 mm long, upper lip oblong, apex rounded or emarginate, about the length of the upper calyx‑lobe, lower lip suborbicular; the spur subulate, about the length of lower corolla‑lip. Ovary ovoid; style short. Capsule ovoid, 2–4 mm long, opening by longitudinal slits.

Locality: Cape D'Aguilar, Bride's Pool, Pat Sin Leng, Sai Kung, Lantau Island. Y. W. Lam 408, 1253; HK sheet 39845.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Taiwan; tropical Asia, extending to S Japan and Korea, also in Australia.
Ecology: Marshes. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Dec.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Mo Shan, Kap Lung, Castle Peak
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Codonopsis javanica (Blume) Hook. f. 金錢豹
Ill. Himal. Pl. 116, t. 16B. 1855.
Campanumoea javanica Blume, Bijdr. Fl. Ned. Ind. 13: 727. 1825; FRPS 73(2): 70. 1983; FGD 3: 320. 1995.
Campanumoea pilosula auct. non Franch.: FKH 153. 1912.

Perennial twining herbs, glabrous throughout. Tap root thick and fleshy, cylindric or obconical, 5–10 cm, to 5 cm in diam. Leaves opposite, very rarely alternate; petioles 2–5 cm; leaf blade ovate, 2–7 × 1.5–6 cm, base cordate, apex obtuse or acute, margin entire or crenulate. Flowers solitary and axillary. Calyx not attached to ovary; 5‑lobed nearly to the base; lobes oblong or ovate‑lanceolate, 1–2 cm, persistent. Corolla campanulate, 1–1.3 cm, white or light green, with purple stripes inside; 5‑lobed to middle; lobes ovate. Stamens 5; filaments filiform, 3 – 9 mm; anthers 2–6 mm. Ovary 4–5‑locular, with numerous ovules. Fruit a berry, depressed globose, 10–12(–15) mm in diam.; purplish red when mature.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Kap Lung, Castle Peak. W. J. Tutcher 10550; P. S. Choi 134; HK sheet 31588.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan; Sikkim, Bhutan to Indonesia.
Ecology: Wet places in thickets and thin forests. Flowering: Sep.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Codonopsis lanceolata (Siebold & Zucc.) Trautv. 羊乳
Trudy Imp. S.‑Peterburgsk. Bot. Sada 6: 46. 1879; Hemsl., J. Soc. Bot. 26: 5. 1889; FKH 153. 1912; FRPS 73(2): 37. 1983; FGD 3:321, fig. 208. 1995.
Campanumoea lanceolata Siebold & Zucc., Fl. Jap. 1: 174, t. 91. 1835.

Perennial twining herbs, usually glabrous throughout. Tap root thick and fleshy, fusiform, to 20 cm long and 6 cm in diam., with milky latex. Leaves alternate on stems (usually small), 2–4 opposite or in false whorls at apex of branches; petioles short, 1–5 mm; leaf blade rhombic‑ovate or elliptic, 3–7(–10) × 1.5–3(–4.5) cm, base attenuate, apex acute or obtuse, margin entire or undulate‑serrate. Flowers solitary or in pairs terminal on branches. Calyx‑tube attached to the middle of the ovary; lobes 5, ovate‑lanceolate, 12–15 × 5–7 mm, persistent and slightly enlarged in fruit. Corolla broadly campanulate, 2 – 3 cm; lobes 5, triangular, 0.5 – 1 cm, creamy white outside, purple inside. Ovary half‑inferior; stigma 3‑lobed. Capsule hemispheric, 2–2.5 cm in diam.; seeds winged.

Locality: Ma On Shan. P. Chow 138; F. W. Xing 7340; HK sheet 40895.
Distribution: SE to NE China; Russia (Far East), Korea, Japan.
Ecology: Thin forests and grassy hillslopes. Flowering: Aug.–Sep.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Cultivated and naturalized in Hong Kong
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Laurentia longiflora (L.) Endl. 同瓣草
Gen. Pl. 512. 1838; E. Wimm., Field Mus. Nat. Hist., Bot. Ser. 13(6/2): 474 – 475. 1937; Das Pflanzenreich. IV. 276b (Heft 107): 405. 1953; FGD 3: 331, fig. 217. 1995.
Hippobroma longiflora (L.) D. Don, Gen. Hist. 3: 717. 1834; FTW ed. 2, 4: 787, pl. 364. 1998.
Isotoma longiflora C. Presl, Prodr. Monogr. Lobel. 42. 1836.; FKH 152. 1912.
Lobelia longiflora L., Sp. Pl. 930. 1753.

Perennial herbs. Stems erect, to 50 cm tall, ± pubescent, marked with raised lines descending from base of petioles. Leaves alternate; petioles very short or almost obsolete; leaf blades oblong‑oblanceolate or lanceolate, 6–16 × 2–3 cm, base attenuate, apex acute, margin coarsely serrate, sparsely pubescent on both surfaces when young. Flowers solitary in axils of upper leaves; pedicels 5–8 mm, densely hirsute; bracteoles 2, linear, attached to the base of pedicels. Calyx 5‑lobed; lobes linear, 8–10 mm, hairy and irregularly serrate. Corolla white, hairy; tube slender, 5 – 9 cm; lobes 5, subequal, lanceolate, 1.5–2 cm. Stamens adnate to the middle of corolla‑tube; anthers coherent, bearded at apex. Ovary usually with 10 ribs, densely hairy, especially on the ribs. Capsule ellipsoidal, ca. 1.5 cm.

Locality: Cultivated and naturalized in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 351, 2036; L. T. Lo 66.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi; native to W Indies and S America; widely cultivated or naturalized elsewhere in tropical regions.
Ecology: Wastelands. Flowering: May–Nov.
Uses: Ornamental, poison (mammals).

Lobelia alsinoides Lam. subsp. hancei (Hara) Lammers 假半邊蓮
Bot. Bull. Acad. Sin. 33: 286. 1992.
Lobelia hancei Hara, J. Jap. Bot. 17: 23. 1941; Check List HK Plants 89. 2004.
Lobelia alsinoides var. cantonensis (E. Wimm. ex Danguy) E. Wimm., Ann. Naturhist. Mus. Wien 56: 360. 1948.
Lobelia chinensis Lour. var. cantonensis E. Wimm. ex Danguy, Fl. Gén. Indo‑Chine 3: 681. 1930.
Lobelia alsinoides auct. non Lam.: FGD 3: 329. 1995.

Annual herbs, 10–30 cm tall, glabrous. Stems succulent, erect or ascending, simple or few‑branched, angular. Leaves alternate, spirally arranged; petioles 1–3 mm; leaf blades ovate to ovate‑lanceolate, 5–20 × 3–7 mm, base attenuate or obtuse, apex rounded or acute, margin crenate. Flowers solitary, axillary; pedicels slender, 1– 1.5 cm, with 2 lanceolate bracteoles at base. Calyx tube turbinate, 2–3 mm; calyx lobes linear‑lanceolate, entire. Corolla pale blue, 4–8 mm, 2‑lipped, upper lobes oblong‑oblanceolate, erect, lower lobes oblong‑elliptic, patent. Filaments connate above middle; anthers all barbate at apex. Capsule hemispheric or ovoid, 3–5 mm.

Locality: Sai Kung. HK sheet 39668.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Taiwan, Xizang, Yunnan; Japan.
Ecology: Paddy fields and other wet places by water. Flowering & fruiting: Almost all year round.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Sha Tin, Tai Mo Shan, Tai Po, Fanling, Ng Tung Chai, Tsiu Hang, Wu Kau Tang, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Lobelia chinensis Lour. 半邊蓮
Fl. Cochinch. 514. 1790; FKH 152. 1912; FRPS 73(2): 154. 1983; FGD 3: 329, fig. 215. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 789, pl. 366, photo 397. 1998.
Lobelia radicans Thunb., Trans. Linn. Soc. London 2: 330 – 331. 1794; FKH 152. 1912.

Perennial herbs, glabrous. Stems decumbent or ascendent, 6–15 cm or longer, rooting at the nodes. Leaves alternate, sessile or nearly so, linear to lanceolate 8–25 × 2–6 mm, base rounded or slightly narrowed, apex acute or obtuse, margin entire or shallowly serrate above middle. Flowers solitary in axils of upper leaves; pedicels 2–3 cm. Calyx‑tube 3–5 mm, narrowed at base; lobes 5, lanceolate, about the length of the tube, entire or with a pair of teeth on the lower part. Corolla pink, light purple or white, 10–15 mm, slit open on the upper side nearly to the base; tube white pubescent; limb 5‑lobed, lobes spreading in a plane, the 2 lateral longer, lanceolate, the other 3 oblong‑lanceolate; filaments united above middle, the free parts pubescent laterally; anther‑tube glabrous or sparsely pubescent dorsally, the 2 lower ones bearded at the top. Capsule obconical, 5–6 mm long.

Locality: Sha Tin, Tai Mo Shan, Tai Po, Fanling, Ng Tung Chai, Tsiu Hang, Wu Kau Tang, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 1607; L. T. Lo 76, 396.
Distribution: S, C & E China; SE Asia.
Ecology: Lower banks of paddy fields and other wet places. Flowering : Feb.–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Lobelia zeylanica L. 疏毛半邊蓮
Sp. Pl. 932. 1753; FKH 152. 1912; FRPS 73(2): 148. 1983; FGD 3: 329. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 792, pl. 369, photo 400. 1998.
Lobelia affinis Wall. ex G. Don, Gard. Dict. 3: 709. 1834; FKH 152. 1912.
Lobelia trigona auct. non Roxb.: FHK 196. 1861.

Annual herbs. Stems slender, decumbent or prostrate, 10–30(–40) cm, sparsely pubescent or glabrous, rooting at the lower nodes. Leaves alternate, spirally arranged; petioles 3–12 cm, sparsely pubescent; leaf blades ovate to broadly ovate, 1.5–4 × 1–3 cm, base truncate, shallowly cordate or cuneate, apex acute or obtuse, margin entire serrate, adaxially pubescent, abaxially sparsely covered with small coarse hairs on the veins. Flowers solitary in axils of leaves; pedicels 1–2 cm, sparsely pubescent. Calyx campanulate, 2–3 mm, sparsely pubescent; lobes 5, lanceolate or narrowly triangular, 3–5 mm, ciliate. Corolla light purple or white, bilabiate, 5–9 mm, the 2 upper lobes shorter, obovate‑oblong, the 3 lower ones ovate to spathulate; filaments with the upper 1/3 united; anthers 5, all shortly bearded at the top. Capsule obovoid, 3–7 mm long.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai, Lantau Island. L. T. Lo 317; Y. W. Lam 1312; HK sheet 16499.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; E to SE Asia.
Ecology: Paddy fields and other wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Feb. of the following year.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Castle Peak, Long Ke
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Platycodon grandiflorus (Jacq.) A. DC. 桔梗
Monogr. Camp. 125. 1830; FKH 153. 1912; FRPS 73(2): 77. 1983; FGD 3: 322, fig. 209. 1995.
Campanula grandiflora Jacq., Hort. Bot. Vindob. 3: 4, t. 2. 1776.
Wahlenbergia grandiflora Schrad., Cat. Hort. Götting. (ann. 1814); FHK 197. 1861.

Perennial herbs, 40–100 cm tall, glabrous and somewhat glaucous, with thick fleshy tap root. Leaves in whorls of 3 or opposite, rarely alternate on the upper part of stem, subsessile; leaf blades ovate, elliptic or lanceolate, 2–7 × 0.5–3.5 cm, base broadly cuneate or obtuse, apex acute, margin serrulate. Flowers solitary or 2–3 in terminal loose raceme. Calyx‑tube hemispheric; lobes 5, triangular to narrowly triangular, 2–8 mm. Corolla broadly campanulate, deep blue, 3–5 cm in diam.; lobes 5, triangular, apex acute. Stamens 5, flattened at base, hairy on the inner side. Capsule obovoid or globose, ca. 1 cm in diam., opening in 5 valves opposite to the calyx‑lobes.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Castle Peak, Long Ke. H. C. Tang 270; Y. S. Lau 2337; HK sheet 39269.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China except NW regions; Russia (Far East), Korea, Japan.
Ecology: Sunny grassy hillslopes. Flowering: Jul.–Sep.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.
Notes: Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Mo Shan, Tai Po, Ta Ti Yan, Lam Tsuen Valley, Sunset Peak
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Pratia nummularia (Lam.) A. Braun & Asch. 銅錘玉帶草
Index Sem. (Berlin) 1861, Append. 6. 1861; FHN 3: 446. 1974; FRPS 73(2): 168. 1983; FGD 3: 332, fig. 218. 1995.
Lobelia nummularia Lam., Dict. 3: 589. 1789; FTW ed. 2, 4: 792, pl. 367, photo 398. 1998.
Piddingtonia nummularia A. DC., Prodr. 7: 341. 1839; FHK 196. 1861.
Pratia begonifolia Lindl., Bot. Reg. 16: sub t. 1373. 1830; FKH 152. 1912.

Perennial herbs, juice milky. Stems prostrate, 12–55 cm, usually pubescent, rooting at the nodes. Leaves alternate, distichous; petioles 2–7 mm, pubescent; leaf blade ovate, or nearly orbicular, 8–16 × 6–18 mm, base cordate, apex subrounded or ± acute, margin serrate, sparsely pubescent on both surfaces. Flowers solitary in axils of leaves. Pedicels 7–35 mm, glabrous. Calyx‑tube urn‑shaped, 3–4 mm, glabrous; lobes 5, linear‑lanceolate, 3–4 mm. Corolla usually light purple, 6–7 mm, bilabiate, the 2 upper lobes linear‑lanceolate, the 3 lower lobes lanceolate, shorter than the upper ones. Anthers united into a ring, ca. 1 mm, the 2 lower ones with a short bristle on the top. Berry ovoid‑globular, purplish red, 8–10 mm in diam.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Tai Po, Ta Ti Yan, Lam Tsuen Valley, Sunset Peak. H. C. Tang 2502; Y. S. Lau 1523.
Distribution: S, E & SW China; E & S Asia to New Guinea and Australia.
Ecology: Wet places on margins of forests and in grassy slopes. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Dec.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tuen Mun, Kuk Po, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Sphenoclea zeylanica Gaertn. 尖瓣花
Fruct. Sem. Pl. 1: 113, pl. 24, fig. 5. 1788; FKH 153. 1912; FRPS 73(2): 176. 1983; FGD 3: 326, fig. 213. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 801, pl. 372, photo 403. 1998.

Annual herbs, glabrous throughout. Stems erect, 20–70 cm tall, usually many‑branched. Leaves alternate; petioles ca. 1 cm; leaf blades oblong to oblong‑lanceolate or ovate‑lanceolate, 2–9 × 0.5–2 cm, base cuneate, apex obtuse or acute, entire, adaxially green, abaxially greyish green; lateral veins slender, inconspicuous. Spikes densely flowered, 1–4 cm, 5–8 mm in diam., terminal or leaf‑opposite. Flowers small, sessile; calyx green, lobes 5, ovate; corolla white, campanulate, with 5 spreading lobes; stamens 5, attached to the lower part of the corolla‑tube, alternate with the corolla‑lobes; ovary inferior, bilocular, with numerous ovules in each locule. Capsule depressed globose, 2– 4 mm in diam., circumscissile, with numerous seeds.

Locality: Tuen Mun, Kuk Po, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 3272; F. W. Xing 7843; HK sheet 39068.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; widely distributed in tropical regions.
Ecology: Margins of paddy fields and other wet places. Flowering: Jul.–Aug.

Wahlenbergia marginata (Thunb.) A. DC. 藍花參
Monogr. Campan. 143. 1830; FRPS 73(2): 29. 1983; FGD 3: 323, fig. 210. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 4: 798, pl. 371, photo 402. 1998.
Campanula marginata Thunb., Syst. Veg. ed. 14, 211. 1784.
Wahlenbergia agrestis A. DC., Monogr. Campan. 145. 1830; FHK 197. 1861.
Wahlenbergia gracilis auct. non (Forst. f.) Schrad.: Dunn & Tutcher, FKH 152. 1912.

Perennial herbs, 10–40 cm tall. Stems erect or ascendent, branched from the base, glabrous or sparsely hirsute on the lower part. Leaves alternate, subsessile; leaf blade linear to narrowly elliptic, 1–5 × 0.2–0.6 cm, base cuneate or obtuse, apex acute or obtuse, margin undulate, slightly toothed or entire, glabrous or sparsely hirsute on the abaxial surface. Flowers solitary and terminal, or 2 – 3 forming a loose terminal dichotomous cyme. Pedicels slender, 1–10 cm. Calyx‑tube obovoid, ca. 2 mm, glabrous, with 10 indistinct vertical veins; lobes 3 – 5, lanceolate. Corolla campanulate, 5 – 8 mm, blue or rarely white; lobes 3–5, ovate. Stamens 5; style short; stigma 3‑lobed. Capsule obconical, 5–7 × 2.5–3.5 mm, shortly 3‑valved at the top.

Locality: Fanling, Yuen Long, Lantau Island. W. J. Tutcher 9168; K. L. Yip 4256; HK sheet 39467.
Distribution: Areas S of Changjiang; widely distributed in tropical and subtropical Asia.
Ecology: Rice fields, wastelands. Flowering: Feb.–May.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Pat Sin Leng
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Stylidium tenellum Sw. 狹葉花柱草
Ges. Naturf. Freunde Berlin Mag. Neuesten Entdeck. Gesammten Naturk. 1: 51. 1807; FKH 151. 1912; FRPS 73(2): 181. 1983; FGD 3: 334. 1995.
Stylidium roseum Kurz, J. Asiat. Soc. Bengal, Pt. 2, Nat. Hist. 46(2): 212. 1877.
Stylidium tenellum var. minimum C. B. Clarke, in Hook. f., Fl. Brit. India 3: 420. 1881, ‘minima’.
Epilobium tonkinense H. Lév., Bull. Herb. Boissier ser. 2, 7: 588. 1907.

Herbs, annual, erect, 6–16 cm tall. Stems slender, simple or laxly dichotomously branched, glabrous. Leaves alternate, few, sessile or nearly sessile; leaf blades oblong‑obovate to oblanceolate, 4–10 × 0.8–2 mm, apical ones smaller and graduating into bracts, glabrous, veins 3 inconspicuous and arcuate, base cuneate, apex obtuse, margin entire. Inflorescences terminal. Flowers solitary, in a spike of 2 or 3, or in a dichotomous inflorescence, sessile. Calyx glabrous or with glandular trichomes; tube (hypanthium) elongate, ca. 1 cm; 2 lobes connate into a slightly 2‑lobed segment. Corolla white or pink or rose purple, less than 2 mm, with sparse glandular trichomes; tube slightly longer than calyx‑lobes; lobes distinct, posterior one 2‑lobed, anterior ones much smaller; labellum minute, subulate; appendage at throat minute but visible. Capsule thinly columnar, to 1.5 cm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Pat Sin Leng. HK sheet 2743.
Distribution: S Fujian, Guangdong, Hainan, Yunnan (Xishuangbanna); India, Bangladesh, Cambodia, Laos, Myanmar, Vietnam, Malaysia, Indonesia.
Ecology: Paddy fields, swamps. Flowering: Oct.–Nov.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Mo Shan, Pat Sin Leng, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Stylidium uliginosum Sw. 花柱草
Ges. Naturf. Freunde Berlin Mag. Neuesten Entdeck. Gesammten Naturk. 1: 52. 1807; FHK 195. 1861; FKH 151. 1912; FRPS 73(2): 181. 1983; FGD 3: 333. 1995.
Stylidium sinicum Hance, Walp. Ann. Syst. 2: 1030. 1851.

Herbs, annual, 5–13(–19) cm tall. Leaves all basal, generally in a rosette, each with a short petiole; leaf blade ovate‑orbicular, ovate, or obovate, 4–10 × 2–6 mm, apex obtuse to rounded, margin entire, glabrous, veins obscure. Stems 1–3, leafless, simple or dichotomously branched, covered with sparse short glandular trichomes. Inflorescences a long and lax spike; bracts ovate, less than 1 mm. Flowers small, sessile. Calyx tube (hypanthium) narrow, with sparse glandular trichomes; lobes minute, anterior 2 connate into a shallowly 2‑lobed segment, ca. 1.8 mm, but others 3 linear and ca. 1.2 mm. Corolla white, ca. 2 mm; tube short; anterior lobe extremely small, ovate, reflexed, becoming a labellum; 4 remaining lobes patent toward posterior side with 2 most posterior longer, base with an appendage, apex shallowly 2‑lobed. Gynostemium ca. 3.5 mm, exserted. Ovary 2‑locular. Capsule columnar, 6 – 8 mm.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Pat Sin Leng, Lantau Island. L. T. Lo 435; HK sheet 19097.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong; India, Sri Lanka, NE Australia.
Ecology: Wet places by streams. Flowering: Oct.–Nov.

Calogyne pilosa R. Br. subsp. chinensis (Benth.) H. S. Kiu 火花離根香
Guihaia 9(3): 194. 1989.
Calogyne chinensis Benth., J. Linn. Soc. 5: 78. 1861; FGD 2: 361. 1991.
Calogyne pilosa auct. non R. Br.: FRPS 73(2): 179. 1983.

Perennial herbs, 5–15 cm tall, aromatic when dry; Stems erect, sparsely pubescent; branches slender, diffuse or procumbent after anthesis. Leaves fasciculate at the base of stem, subsessile; leaf blade narrowly lanceolate to linear, 10–25 × 1–3 mm, base attenuate, apex acute, sparsely hirsute on both surfaces, margin remotely undulate‑dentate, ciliate; upper stem leaves alternate and smaller, sometimes with ear‑like lobes at the base. Flowers solitary, axillary; pedicels slender, 5–10(–20) mm. Calyx‑tube ovoid, less than 2 mm, covered with white short hairs; lobes 5, lanceolate, 4–5 × 1–1.5 mm. Corolla yellow, 6–7 mm, hairy abaxially. Stamens 5; filaments ca. 2.5 mm. Capsule ovoid, 4 – 4.5 × 3–3.5 mm, 7–12‑seeded.

Locality: Fanling. W. J. Tutcher 10484.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian.
Ecology: Moist places, grassy hillslopes, pine forests. Flowering: May–Dec.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Cape D'Aguilar, Cheung Shue Tan, Kiu Tsui, Kau Sai Chau
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Scaevola hainanensis Hance 海南草海桐
J. Bot. 16(188): 229. 1878; FKH 151. 1912; FRPS 73(2): 179. 1983; FGD 2: 360, fig. 245. 1991; FTW ed. 2, 4: 803, pl. 373. 1998.

Small diffuse shrubs; stems thick, greyish, sparsely hirsute and with greyish woolly hairs in leaf‑axils. Leaves sessile, fasciculate at apex of short branches; leaf blade linear‑spathulate, 1.2–2.5 × 0.2–0.5 cm, ± succulent, base attenuate, apex obtuse, margin entire; midvein obscure. Flowers sessile to short‑petiolate, solitary in axils of upper leaves; bracts 2, similar to leaves, but slightly smaller. Calyx adnate to ovary; tube ca. 4 mm; limb cup‑shaped, obscurely 5‑lobed. Corolla initially pink, gradually turning white, ca. 10 mm when full blooming; tube 5–6 mm glandular and hairy adaxially, ± pubescent abaxially; lobes 5, slightly shorter than or equal to the tube, margin membranous, folded inwards. Drupe ellipsoidal, 6–7 × 4–6 mm, apex crowned with enlarged calyx‑lobes.

Locality: Cape D'Aguilar, Cheung Shue Tan, Kiu Tsui, Kau Sai Chau. L. T. Lo 639; Y. W. Lam 42, 361.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Taiwan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Sandy shores. Flowering & fruiting: May–Nov.

Scaevola taccada (Gaertn.) Roxb. 草海桐
Fl. Ind. 1: 527. 1820; R. K. Shannon, W. L. Wagner & D. H. Nicolson, Taxon 46(4): 801. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 4: 805, pl. 374. 1998.
Lobelia taccada Gaertn., Fruct. Sem. Pl. 1: 119, pl. 25, fig. 5. 1788.
Scaevola sericea Vahl, Symb. Bot. 2: 37. 1791; FRPS 73(2): 178. 1983; FGD 2: 361. 1991.
Scaevola lobelia L., Syst. Veg. ed. 13, 178. 1774; FHK 198. 1861.
Scaevola koenigii Vahl, Symb. Bot. 3: 36. 1794; FKH 151. 1912.

Shrubs or small trees, with a thick, ± succulent stem; branches, leaves and inflorescence silky‑pubescent or nearly glabrous, but always with a tuft of woolly or long silky hairs in leaf‑axils. Leaves alternate, crowded towards apex of branches; leaf blade obovate‑oblong to spathulate, 10–22 × 4–8 cm, , base narrowed into a very short and broad petiole, apex round to broadly obtuse, margin entire, rarely obscurely toothed; midvein raised on both surfaces, lateral veins indistinct. Cymes axillary, lax‑flowered, shorter than the leaves; peduncle 1–2 cm; bracts linear‑lanceolate, 6–8 mm, hairy at the base. Calyx‑tube turbinate, 3–5 mm; lobes 5, oblong‑linear, about the length of the tube. Corolla usually white, 20–22 mm, ± pubescent abaxially and always hairy adaxially; tube 10– 12 mm; lobes 5, lanceolate, about half the length of the tube, spreading, bordered on each side with a narrow wing folded inward in the bud. Drupe ovoid or globose, 8–12 mm in diam., apex crowned with enlarged calyx‑lobes.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 227, 360; L. T. Lo 445.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Philippines, Malaysia, Indonesia, Australia.
Ecology: Sandy and rocky seashores. Flowering: Apr.–Dec.; fruiting: Jul.–Dec.

Adina pilulifera (Lam.) Franch. ex Drake 水團花
J. Bot. (Morot) 9: 207. 1895; Hand.‑Mazz., Symb. Sin. 8: 1018. 1936; FHN 3: 288, fig. 727. 1974; Ridsdale, Blumea 24(2): 357, fig. 1(d), 3(h). 1978; FRPS 71(1): 274, pl. 73: 1 – 2. 1999; FYN 15: 132, pl. 25: 6 – 9. 2003; FGD 6: 162. 2005.
Adina globiflora Salisb., Parad. Lond. pl. 115. 1807; FHK 146. 1861; FKH 124. 1912.
Cephalanthus pilulifera Lam., Encycl. 1: 678. 1785.

Evergreen shrubs or small trees, to 5 m tall, many‑branched. Stipules bifid, caducous. Leaves opposite, thickly papery; petioles 2–6 mm; leaf blade elliptic to elliptic‑lanceolate, or sometimes obovate‑oblong or obovate‑oblanceolate, 4–12 × 1.5–3 cm, base obtuse or cuneate, apex acute to acuminate, tip blunt, adaxially glabrous, abaxially glabrous or puberulent, with hairy domatia in axils of lateral veins; lateral veins 6–12 on each side of midvein. Flowering head globular, 8–12 mm in diam. across corollas. Peduncles axillary, 2–5 cm, unbranched, rarely 3 together at the ends of the branches, each bearing a flowering head. Calyx‑tube 1.2–2 mm, pubescent at the base; lobes clavate to spathulate, 1–1.8 mm, glabrous or with a few scattered hairs. Corolla white, 3–5 mm, tube 2–3 mm, glabrous; lobes deltoid, ca. 0.5 mm. Stamens 5, inserted in the throat of corolla; filaments short; anthers 0.5–1 mm. Ovary 2‑locular, with many ovules in each locule; style exserted, with small, globose or obovoid stigma. Fruiting head globose, 8–10 mm in diam.; fruitlets 2–4 mm, glabrous or with a few scattered hairs.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. S. Y. Hu & P. P. H. But 24058, 24084; HK Sheet 39081.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian; Japan, Vietnam.
Ecology: Thickets by streams and in ravines. Flowering: May–Oct.; fruiting: Jul.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Tai Po, Ma On Shan, Fa Shan, Wu Kau Tang, Lamma Island, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Aidia canthioides (Champ. ex Benth.) Masam. 香楠（山黃皮）
Trans. Nat. Hist. Soc. Taiwan 28: 118 1938; FRPS 71(1): 351, pl. 92: 1 – 7. 1999; FYN 15: 177. 2003; FGD 6: 181. 2005.
Randia canthioides Champ. ex Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 4: 194. 1852; FHK 155. 1861; FKH 131. 1912; FTW ed. 2, 4: 318. 1998.

Shrubs or trees, unarmed, 1–12 m tall. Branches glabrous. Leaves papery or thinly leathery; petioles 5–18 mm; stipules broadly triangular, 3–8 mm, apex acute or acuminate, deciduous, leaf blade oblong‑elliptic, oblong‑lanceolate to lanceolate, 4–18 × 2–8 cm, base broadly cuneate or sometimes subrounded, apex acuminate to caudate‑acuminate, sometimes acute, glabrous; lateral veins slender, 3–7 on each side of midvein. Cymes umbel‑like, axillary, 3–5 cm in diam. Peduncle very short or none. Pedicels slender, 5–16 mm, glabrous. Calyx covered with appressed rusty hairs abaxially; tube turbinate, 4–6 mm; lobes 5, triangular, 1–2 mm, apex acute. Corolla salverform, white or yellow; tube 8–10 mm, glabrous abaxially, villose on the throat; lobes 5, oblong, 4–7 mm, apex acute, recurved. Anthers linear‑oblong, ca. 3.5 mm, exserted. Style ca. 10 mm; stigma fusiform, 2‑lobes. Berry globose, 5–8 mm in diam., rusty pubescent or glabrescent.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Po, Ma On Shan, Fa Shan, Wu Kau Tang, Lamma Island, Lantau Island. P. S. Choi 421; Y. W. Lam 480; K. L. Yip 4536.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan;  Japan, Vietnam.
Ecology: Thickets and forests. Flowering: Apr.–Sep.; fruiting: Jul.–Dec.
Notes: The type specimen was collected by J. G. Champion from Victoria Peak between 1847 and 1850.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Happy Valley, Ma On Shan, Wu Kau Tang, Sha Tau Kok, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Aidia cochinchinensis Lour. 茜樹（越南香楠）
Fl. Cochinch. 143. 1790; Masam., Trans. Nat. Hist. Soc. Taiwan 28: 118. 1938; FRPS 71(1): 354, pl. 93: 1 – 6. 1999; FYN 15: 178. 2003; FGD 6: 181, fig. 94. 2005.
Randia cochinchinensis (Lour.) Merr., Trans. Amer. Philos. Soc. n.s., 24(2): 365. 1935; FTW ed. 2, 4: 319, pl. 144, photo 193. 1998.
Randia densiflora (Wall.) Benth., FHK 155. 1861; FKH 131. 1912, p.p.
Webera densiflora Wall., Fl. Ind. ed. 1820, 2: 536. 1824.
Randia henryi E. Pritz., Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 29(5): 581. 1901.

Shrubs or trees, unarmed, 2–15 m tall. Branchlets petioles and stipules glabrous. Leaves leathery or papery; petioles 4–10(–18) mm; stipules lanceolate, 4–8(–10) mm, glabrous, deciduous; leaf blade elliptic‑oblong, oblong‑lanceolate or narrowly elliptic, 6 – 21 × 1.5 – 8 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate to caudate‑acuminate, glabrous, but often with tufts of short hairs in axils of veins on abaxial surface; lateral veins slender, 5–7 on each side of midvein. Cymes leaf‑opposed, or lateral on aphyllous nodes. Peduncles 5 – 10 mm. Pedicels 1 – 2 mm, together with peduncles pubescent. Calyx glabrous; tube cup‑shaped, 3.5 – 4 mm; lobes 4( – 5), triangular, 1 – 1.5 mm. Corolla yellow or white; tube 3 – 4 mm, glabrous abaxially, densely yellowish villose on the throat; lobes 4( – 5), oblong, 6 – 10 mm, apex acute, spreading or reflexed, pubescent with minute appressed hairs on abaxial surface. Anthers linear‑lanceolate, 4 – 8 mm, exserted. Style ca. 7 mm; stigma fusiform, 2‑lobes. Berry globose, 5 – 6 mm in diam., purplish black when mature.

Locality: Happy Valley, Ma On Shan, Wu Kau Tang, Sha Tau Kok, Lantau Island. Y. W. Lam 648; HK sheet 39493, 40772.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Jiangsu, Fujian, Taiwan; spreading over tropical Asia & Australia.
Ecology: Ravines under forests or in thickets. Flowering: Mar. – Jun.; fruiting: May–Feb. of the following year.
Notes: This species was recorded previously as Randia acutidens Hemsl. & Wils. var. laxiflora Dunn. (FKH 131. 1912).

Aidia pycnantha (Drake) Tirveng. 多毛茜草樹
Nord. Journ. Bot. 3(4): 455. 1983; FRPS 71(1): 349. 1999; FYN 15: 177. 2003; FGD 6. 182. 2005.
Randia pycnantha Drake in Morot, Journ. de Bot. 9: 218. 1895.
Randia acuminatissima Merr., Philip. J. Sci. 15(3): 259 – 260. 1919[1920].
Aidia acuminatissima (Merr.) Masam., Trans. Nat. Hist. Soc. Taiwan 29: 238. 1939.

Shrubs or trees, unarmed, 2–10 m tall. Young branches ferruginous soft hairy. Petioles 5–15 mm long, softy hairy; leaf blade oblong, oblong‑lanceolate or oblong‑oblanceolate, 10–20 × 3–8 cm, leathery or papery, apex acuminate to caudate‑acuminate, acuminate portion to 2.5 cm long, straight or curved, base cuneate, sometimes unaequilateral, when dry reddish brown, adaxially glabrous, slightly shiny, abaxially ferruginous soft hairy; lateral veins 10–14 pairs, together with reticulate veins prominent abaxially; stipules lanceolate, to 1 cm long, apex long pointed, pubescent. Inflorescence a cyme, leaf opposed, many‑flowered, 4–6, × 5–12 cm, ferruginous soft hairy; bracts and bractlets linear‑lanceolate, 2–4 mm long. Pedicels 1.5 – 4 mm long. Calyx and hypanthium 4 – 5 mm long, ferruginous soft hairy; tube cupulate, 3 mm long, limb slightly expanded, apically 5‑lobed; lobes triangular, apex pointed, 1–2 mm long. Corolla white or pale yellow, salverform, glabrous abaxially; tube ca. 4 mm long, densely villose in throat; lobes 5, oblong‑oblanceolate, 7–9 mm, reflexed at anthesis. Anthers linear‑lanceolate, exserted, ca. 7 mm long; filaments ca. 2.5 mm long. Ovary 2‑celled; style and stigma 7–8 mm long, glabrous; stigma fusiform, with shallow sulcate striate. Fruit a berry, globose, 6 – 8 mm in diam., sparsely ferruginous hairy or subglabrous, black when dry, apex with annular remnants of calyx limb.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 2966; P. S. Choi 293; Y. W. Lam 1702.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian; Vietnam.
Ecology: Thicket or lowland forest. Flowering: Feb.–Nov.; fruiting: Apr.–Dec.
Notes: This species was recorded previously as Randia densiflora (Wall.) Benth. (FKH 131. 1912, p.p.).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Ma On Shan, Tai Mo Shan, Shing Mun, Lamma Island, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Alleizettella leucocarpa (Champ. ex Benth.) Tirveng. 白果香楠（白果山黃皮）
Nordic J. Bot. 3(4): 455. 1983; FRPS 71(1): 358, pl. 92: 8 – 11. 1999; FGD 6: 183, fig. 96. 2005.
Randia leucocarpa Champ. ex Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 4: 194. 1852; FHK 154. 1861; FKH 132. 1912.

Shrubs, 1–3 m tall, unarmed. Branchlets and petioles rusty strigose, glabrescent in age. Leaves papery or thinly leathery; petioles 2.5–5(–10) mm; stipules broadly triangular, ca. 5 mm, apex acuminate, hairy; leaf blade oblong‑obovate, oblong, narrowly elliptic or lanceolate, 4.5–11(–17) × 1.5 – 6 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate to caudate‑acuminate, rusty strigose along midvein and lateral veins on abaxial surface; lateral veins slender, 4–7 on each side of midvein. Cymes few‑flowered, terminal on lateral short branches and on nodes of old branches, strigose. Peduncles to 2 mm or almost none. Pedicels ca. 2 mm. Calyx strigose; tube bell‑shaped, 2–2.5 mm, strigose; lobes 5, triangular, ca. 1 mm, apex acute. Corolla white, salverform; tube ca. 3 mm, strigose on the upper part of abaxial surface, villose on the throat; lobes 5, subovate, 2.5–3 mm, apex acute, spreading. Berry globose, 0.8 – 1.3 cm in diam., pale yellowish white when mature, sparsely pubescent or glabrous, 2–4‑seeded.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Ma On Shan, Tai Mo Shan, Shing Mun, Lamma Island, Lantau Island. P. S. Choi 422, 507; Y. W. Lam 1389.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian.
Ecology: Thickets and margins of forests. Flowering: Apr. –Jun.; fruiting: Apr.–Feb. of the following year.
Notes: The type specimen was collected by J. G. Champion from Victoria Peak between 1847 and 1850.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Authority: (Champ. ex Benth.) F. B. Forbes & Hemsl.
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Antirhea chinensis (Champ. ex Benth.) F. B. Forbes & Hemsl. 毛茶
J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 23(156): 384. 1888; FHN 3: 339, fig. 756. 1974; FRPS 71(2): 16, pl. 6. 1999; FGD 6: 196, fig. 106. 2005.
Guettardella chinensis Champ. & Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 4: 197. 1852; FHK 158. 1861.

Evergreen shrubs, 1–2 m tall. Branchlets covered when young with appressed hairs. Leaves papery; petioles 4–10 mm, densely sericeous; stipules triangular, ca. 4 mm, apex acuminate, sericeous; leaf blade oblong or oblong‑lanceolate, 3–7(–9) × 1–2.5(–3) cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, margin entire, slightly incurved, sprinkled with a few hairs or glabrous on adaxial surface, densely sericeous on abaxial surface. Cymes axillary, sericeous. Peduncles 1 – 3 cm. Calyx scarcely 2 mm, covered with appressed hairs; tube very short; limb enlarged, 4–5‑lobed; lobes linear or lanceolate, 0.5–1.5 mm, unequal. Corolla yellow, densely covered with greyish silky hair abaxially; lobes 4(–5), ovate, ca. 2 mm, apex obtuse. Drupe ellipsoidal, 5–7 mm, obtusely angled, pubescent.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. K. Y. Tam 145; S. Y. Hu & P. P. H. But 24062; HK sheet 39142.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian.
Ecology: Thickets and forests. Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: Jul.–Oct.
Notes: The type specimen was collected by J. G. Champion from Mount Gough and Victoria Peak between 1847 and 1850.

Canthium dicoccum (Gaertn.) Merr. 魚骨木（鐵矢米）
Philipp. J. Sci. 35(1): 8. 1928.
Canthium dicoccum (Gaertn.) Teysm. & Binn., Cat. Hort. Bog. 1866, nom. invalid.
Canthium didymum C. F. Gaertn., Suppl. Carp. 94, t. 196. 1806; FHK 159. 1861; FKH 132. 1912.
Psydrax dicoccos Gaertn., Fruct. Sem. Pl. 1: 125, t. 26, fig. 2. 1788

Shrubs or small trees, to 15 m tall, spineless. Branchlets dark brown, glabrous. Leaves opposite, leathery; petioles 8–15 mm; stipules 3–5 mm, with a broad base, apex acute or acuminate; leaf blade ovate or elliptic or ovate‑lanceolate, 4–10 × 1.5–4 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, obtuse or acute, glabrous, shining on both surfaces when dry; lateral veins slender, 3–5 on each side of midvein. Cymes axillary, loose and often many‑flowered, short‑pedunculate, shorter than the subtending leaves. Calyx‑tube obconical, 1–1.2 mm, apex truncate or inconspicuously 5‑toothed. Corolla greenish white or yellowish; tube ca. 3 mm, tomentose on the throat; lobes 4 or 5, oblong, slightly shorter than the tube. Drupes obovate or obovate‑ellipsoidal, 6 – 8 mm in diam.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 319, 1415; HK sheet 39115.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Xizang; Indochina, Malesia, Indian subcontinent, Australia.
Ecology: Ravines, forests and thickets. Flowering & fruiting: Mar.–Aug.

Canthium horridum Blume 豬肚木（小葉鐵矢米）
Catalogus 45. 1823; Bijdr. Fl. Ned. Ind. 16: 966. 1926; FHK 159. 1861; FYN 15: 199, pl. 40: 13 – 15. 2003; FGD 6: 195. 2005.
Canthium parvifolium auct. non Roxb.: FKH 132. 1912.

Shrubs, 2–3 m tall, armed with straight axillary thorns. Young shoots ± pubescent. Leaves opposite, papery; petioles 2– 3 mm, ± pubescent; stipules 2–3 mm, pubescent; leaf blade ovate or elliptic, 2–5 × 1–2 cm, base rounded or obtuse, apex acute or shortly acuminate, ± pubescent abaxially, at least when young; lateral veins slender, 2 – 3 on each side of midvein. Flowers small, sessile or short‑pedicellate, solitary or clustered in axils of leaves. Calyx‑tube obconical, 1 – 1.5 mm, apex with minute, undulate teeth. Corolla white; tube short, ca. 2 mm, glabrous outside, with retrorse beard on the throat; lobes 5, oblong, ca. 3 mm, apex acute. Drupes globular or didymous, 1–2 cm in diam.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. Y. W. Lam 1152.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan; Indochina, Malesia and Indian subcontinent.
Ecology: Thin forests and thickets. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.; fruiting: Jul.–Nov.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Wan Chai Gap, Mount Nicholson, Tai Po, Lai Chi Wo, Sha Tau Kok, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Catunaregam spinosa (Thunb.) Tirveng. 山石榴（山蒲桃）
Bull. Mus. Hist. Nat. (Paris) 35: 13. 1978; Taxon 27(5 – 6): 515. 1979; Verdc., Kew Bull. 36(3): 505. 1981; FRPS 71(1): 338, pl. 89. 1999; FYN 15: 170, pl. 34: 3 – 5. 2003; FGD 6: 177, fig. 91. 2005.
Randia dumetorum (Retz.) Lam., Tabl. Encycl. 2: 227. 1794; FHK 154. 1861; FKH 131. 1912.
Randia spinosa (Thunb.) Blume, Bijdr. Fl. Ned. Ind. 981. 1826; FHN 3: 321. 1974.
Gardenia spinosa Thunb., Diss. Gard. 7: 16. 1780.

Shrubs or small trees, 1–10 m tall, many‑branched, armed with axillary stout thorns. Leaves papary or subleathery; petioles 2–8 mm, sparsely pubescent or glabrous; stipules membranous, ovate, 3–4.5 mm, apex acute, deciduous, leaf blade obovate or oblong‑obovate, 2–8(–11) × 2–4.5(–5.7) cm, base cuneate, apex acute, or obtuse, sparsely and minutely strigose on adaxial surface and along midvein and lateral veins when young, soon glabrescent; lateral veins slender, 4–7 on each side of midvein. Flowers solitary or 2 – 3 clustered at apex of lateral short branches or tufts of leaves. Pedicels 2–5 mm, together with calyx covered with tawny long hairs. Calyx‑tube bell‑shaped or ovoid, 4–6 mm; lobes 5, broadly elliptic, 5–6 × 4–4.5 mm, apex broadly acute, green, 3 – 5‑veined. Corolla bell‑shaped, initially white, later turning pale yellow; tube 5 – 6 mm, densely sericeous near apex outside, with a ring of long hairs on upper part inside; lobes 5, broadly elliptic to subrounded, 8 – 11 × 8 – 9 mm, apex rounded, spreading. Anthers linear‑oblong, ca. 3 mm, exserted. Style 4–6 mm; stigma globular, with 2 coherent lobes. Berry globose, 2–4 cm in diam., crowned by persistent calyx‑lobes.

Locality: Wan Chai Gap, Mount Nicholson, Tai Po, Lai Chi Wo, Sha Tau Kok, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 696; Y. S. Lau 1895; HK sheet 40206.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; Indochina, Malesia, Indian subcontinent.
Ecology: Forests and thickets. Flowering: Mar.–Jun.; fruiting: May–Jan. of the following year.
Uses: Material (wood), environmental (hedges), medicinal (folklore).

Cephalanthus tetrandrus (Roxb.) Ridsdale & Bakh. f. 風箱樹
Blumea 23(1): 182. 1976; FRPS 71(1): 279, pl. 75. 1999; FGD 6: 163, fig. 82. 2005.
Cephalanthus occidentalis auct. non L.: Dunn & Tutch., FKH 124. 1912.
Nauclea tetrandra Roxb., Fl. Ind. ed. 1820, 2: 125. 1824.

Deciduous shrubs or small trees, 1–5 m tall. Branchlets pubescent when young, brown and glabrous in age. Stipules broadly ovate, 3–5 mm, usually with a black gland at the cuspidate apex. Leaves opposite or in whorls, subleathery; petioles 5–10 mm; leaf blade ovate or ovate‑lanceolate, 10–15 × 3–5 cm, base obtuse or subcordate, apex acute, adaxially glabrous or sparsely puberulent, abaxially glabrous or densely pubescent, especially in the axils of veins; lateral veins 8–12 on each side of midvein. Flowers heads globular, across calyces 8–12 cm in diam., terminal or axillary; peduncle 2.5–6 cm, simple or branched, pubescent. Calyx‑tube 2–3 mm, sparsely puberulent; lobes 4, apex obtuse, densely puberulent, usually with a black gland at the sinus of the lobes. Corolla white, tube 7–12 mm, glabrous abaxially, puberulent adaxially; lobes 4, oblong, with a black gland at the sinus of the lobes. Ovary inferior; style long exserted. Aggregate fruit globose, 10–20 mm in diam.; nutlets 4–6 mm, with persistent calyx at apex.

Locality: San Wai, Ta Kwu Ling. W. J. Tutcher 8153; HK sheet 40705.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Indochina to India and Malesia.
Ecology: Thickets by streams. Flowering: Late spring to autumn; fruiting: Jun.–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Mount Kellet, Ma On Shan, Sham Tseng, Tai O, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Coptosapelta diffusa (Champ. ex Benth.) Steenis 流蘇子
Amer. J. Bot. 56: 806. 1969; FTW ed. 2, 4: 248, pl. 109, photo 167. 1998; FYN 15: 112, pl. 21: 1 – 5. 2003; FGD 6: 154, fig. 73. 2005.
Thysanospermum diffusum Champ. ex Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 4: 168. 1852; FHK 146. 1861; FKH 125. 1912.

Evergreen trailing shrubs, to 5 m or longer, many‑branched. Branches slender, covered with appressed tawny hairs when young, glabrescent in age. Leaves firmly papery to leathery; petioles 2–5 mm, sparsely hairy; stipules lanceolate, 3–7 mm, deciduous; leaf blade ovate to ovate‑lanceolate, 2–7 × 1–2.5 cm, base rounded or broadly cuneate, apex shortly acuminate, adaxially glabrous, abaxially with appressed hairs on the midvein and edges. Flowers solitary in axils of leaves. Pedicels 3–18 mm, usually bearing 2 bracteoles above the middle. Calyx‑tube globose; lobes ovate, ca. 1 mm. Corolla white or yellowish; tube 1.2–2 cm, pubescent outside and on the upper part inside; lobes 5, oblong, 4–6 × 1.4–1.6 mm, pubescent on adaxial surface. Capsule globose but slightly compressed, 5–7 mm in diam., with 2 furrows. Seeds suborbicular, very thin, fringed with fimbriate wing.

Locality: Mount Kellet, Ma On Shan, Sham Tseng, Tai O, Lantau Island. Y. W. Lam 1284; HK sheet 40021, 40754.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan.
Ecology: Ravines, hillsides, trailing upon trees or rocks. Flowering: May–Jul.; fruiting: Jun.–Dec.
Notes: The type specimen was collected by J. G. Champion from Victoria Peak between 1847 and 1850.

Diplospora dubia (Lindl.) Masam. 狗骨柴（三萼木）
Trans. Nat. Hist. Soc. Taiwan 29: 269. 1939; Ali & Robbrecht, Blumea 35(2): 297. 1991; FRPS 71(1): 364, pl. 96: 1 – 8. 1999; FYN 15: 185, pl. 37: 6 – 10. 2003; FGD 6: 186, fig. 98. 2005.
Diplospora viridiflora DC., Prodr. 4: 477. 1830; FHK 157. 1861; FKH 132. 1912.
Tricalysia dubia (Lindl.) Ohwi, Acta Phytotax. Geobot. 102(2): 137. 1941; FHN 3: 328, fig. 750. 1974; FTW ed. 2, 4: 334, pl. 150, photo 196. 1998.
Canthium dubium Lindl., Bot. Reg. 12: pl. 1026. 1826.

Shrubs or trees, 1–12 m tall, unarmed, branches and leaves glabrous. Leaves leathery, or rarely thickly papery; petioles 4–10(–15) mm; stipules 5–8 mm, with a broad base, apex subulate, white pubescent at base adaxially; leaf blade ovate‑oblong, oblong, elliptic or lanceolate, 5–13(–19) × 1.5–5.5(–8) cm, base cuneate or acute, sometimes slightly oblique, apex shortly acuminate, abruptly acuminate or acute, tip often blunt, margin entire, often slightly revolute, yellowish green and ± shining in drying; lateral veins slender 5–11 on each side of midvein. Flowers clustered in short dense axillary cymes, 7.5–11 mm in diam. Peduncles 2–6 mm. Pedicels 1–4 mm, together with peduncle and calyx puberulent. Calyx‑tube ca. 1 mm; limb slightly dilated, 4‑toothed. Corolla white or yellow; tube ca. 3 mm; lobes 4, oblong, about the length of the tube, recurved. Berry subglobose, 4–6 mm in diam., sparsely pubescent or glabrous, orange‑red, turning black when dry, 4 – 8‑seeded.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. HK sheet 35352, 35598, 39958.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Vietnam.
Ecology: Thickets and forests. Flowering: Jan.–May; fruiting: May–Feb. of the following year.

Galium aparine L. var. echinospermum (Wallr.) Farw. 拉拉藤
Rep. Michigan Acad. Sci. 19: 260. 1917.
Galium aparine L. var. echinospermum (Wallr.) Cuf., Oesterr. Bot. Zeitschr. 89: 246. 1940; FRPS 71(2): 235, pl. 54: 5 – 8. 1999; FYN 15: 307, pl. 64: 8 – 11. 2003; FGD 6: 245, fig. 134. 2005; Check List HK Plants 262. 2002; 90. 2004.
Galium aparine auct. non L.: FHK 164. 1861; FKH 135. 1912.
Galium agreste Wallr. var. echinospermum Wallr., Sched. Crit. 59. 1822.

Annual herbs. Stems trailing or climbing, 30–90 cm or longer, with small, recurved prickles on the angles. Leaves sessile, (4–)6–8 in a whorl; leaf blade linear or linear‑lanceolate, 1–3(–5) × 0.2–0.7 cm, base gradually narrowed, apex mucronate, with small prickles on the margins and midveins of abaxial surface. Flowers small, greenish white, 3–8(–10) in loose cymes; peduncles axillary, usually longer than the subtending leaves; pedicels slender, to 10 mm in fruiting time. Calyx‑tube ovoid, covered with small prickles; limb truncate. Corolla rotate, 4‑lobed; lobes oblong, less than 1 mm. Fruit consisting of 1–2 subglobular segments, covered with hooked bristles.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Fanling (Loi Tung). H. F. Hance s.n. (fide FHK 164. 1861); F. W. Xing 6790 (HKU).
Distribution: Widely spread almost all over China; Japan, Russia, Europe, Africa, N America, Indian subcontinent.
Ecology: Wastelands and grassy hillslopes. Flowering: Mar.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Gardenia jasminoides J. Ellis 梔子（水橫枝）
Philos. Trans. 51(2): 935, pl. 23. 1761; FHN 3: 325. 1974; FTW ed. 2, 4: 259, pl. 112, photo 172. 1998; FRPS 71(1): 332, pl. 87: 1 – 5. 1999; FGD 6: 175, fig. 89. 2005.
Gardenia florida L., Sp. Pl. ed. 2, 305. 1762; FHK 153. 1861; FKH 131. 1912.

Evergreen, unarmed shrubs, 1–3 m tall, glabrous throughout, or young shoots pulverulent. Leaves opposite, or rarely in whorls of 3, subleathery; petioles 2–4 mm; stipules ca. 1 cm, united into a sheath, membranous, apex oblique; leaf blade elliptic, oblong‑elliptic or oblong‑lanceolate, 3–10 × 1–4.5 cm, base cuneate to broadly cuneate, apex acute or acuminate, lateral veins 7–12 on each side of midvein. Flowers terminal, solitary, sessile or nearly so. Calyx‑tube obconical, 8–20 mm, with 5 – 6 sharp ribs; limb usually 6‑lobed; lobes lanceolate, usually slightly longer than the tube. Corolla salverform; tube cylindric, 2.5–4 cm, green; limb 5–6 cm in diam., usually 6‑lobed; lobes white, obovate‑elliptic to oblong‑elliptic, 1.5–2.5(–4) × 0.6–2.8 cm. Anthers linear, 1.2–1.6 cm, exserted. Fruit ellipsoidal, 2.5–3 cm, crowned by the long linear‑lanceolate persistent calyx‑lobes, and marked outside by as many raised ribs or angles.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1833; S. P. Lau 135; HK sheet 40130.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Shandong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian,
Taiwan; Japan, Indochina, cultivated elsewhere.
Ecology: Ravines and thickets on hills. Flowering: Apr.–Aug.; fruiting: May–Dec.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal (folklore), material (dye).

Gardenia jasminoides var. fortuniana (Lindl.) H. Hara 白蟾
This variety differs in the double corolla.

Locality: Cultivated.
Distribution: Widely cultivated in S China; native to China and Japan.
Ecology: Shrub. Flowering: Spring to summer.
Uses: Ornamental.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tate's Cairn, Tai Om, Tai Po, Chuen Lung, Sai Kung
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Geophila herbacea (Jacq.) K. Schum. 愛地草
Nat. Pflanzenfam. 4(4): 119. 1891; FHN 3: 359, fig. 771. 1974; FTW ed. 2, 4: 261, pl. 113, photo 173. 1998; FRPS 71(2): 63, pl. 15: 5 – 9. 1999; FYN 15: 231, pl. 47: 5 – 7. 2003; FGD 6: 210, fig. 113. 2005.
Psychotria herbacea Jacq., Enum. Syst. Pl. 16. 1760.

Perennial creeping herbs, to 30 cm or longer. Stems and branches pubescent, rooting at nodes. Leaves membranous; petioles 1–5 cm, densely pubescent; stipules broadly ovate, 1–2 mm, apex obtuse or rounded, entire; leaf blade reniform or broadly ovate‑cordate, ca. 1–2(–3) cm in diam., base cordate, apex rounded or obtuse, subglabrous, palmately 5–8‑veined. Flowers solitary, or 2–3 in umbels; peduncles 1–4 cm, pubescent or glabrescent. Calyx‑tube 2–3 mm; lobes 4, linear‑lanceolate, 2–2.5 mm, ciliate. Corolla‑tube ca. 8 mm, hairy on both sides; lobes 4, ovate or ovate‑lanceolate. Drupe subglobose, 4–6 mm in diam., smooth, red when mature.

Locality: Tate's Cairn, Tai Om, Tai Po, Chuen Lung, Sai Kung. Y. W. Lam 453, 2053; K. Y. Tam 139.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; widely spread over tropical and subtropical areas.
Ecology: Ravines, margins of forests and other wet places. Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: May–Nov.
Notes: The species was reported as Geophila repens (L.) I. M. Johnst. var. asiatica (Cham. & Schld.) Fosberg previously (Check List HK Plants 90. 2004).

Hamelia patens Jacq. 長隔木（希美利）
Enum. Syst. Pl. 16. 1760; FRPS 71(1): 390, pl. 103: 1 – 5. 1999; FYN 15: 194, pl. 39: 10 – 13. 2003; FGD 6: 191, fig. 101. 2005.

Shrubs, 1.5–4 m tall, many‑branched, all young parts cinereous‑pubescent. Branchlets, petioles and peduncles reddish. Leaves usually in whorls of 3 or 4; petioles 1.5–4.5 cm; stipules subulate, ca. 6 mm; leaf blade elliptic to oblanceolate, 7–15(–20) × 4–6 cm, base cuneate, apex acute, lateral veins 7–9 on each side of midvein, impressed adaxially, raised abaxially. Cymes terminal, with 3–5 radiate branches; primary branches 2.5–4 cm, secondary branches 1.5–2 cm. Flowers arranged along one side of the ultimate branches. Pedicels 1–2 mm. Calyx‑tube cup‑shaped, ca. 3 mm; lobes 5, triangular, ca. 1 mm. Corolla scarlet‑orange, tubular, ca. 2.5 cm, glabrous; tube 5‑ribbed, slightly enlarged at the base; lobes 5, ovate‑triangular, ca. 2 mm erect. Stamens 5, equal to the corolla‑tube; filaments 5–6 mm; anthers linear, 9–10 mm, with projected connective. Style 11–12; stigma clavate. Fruit unknown.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. Y. S. Lau 991, 1945; L. T. Lo 152.
Distribution: Native to C America.
Ecology: Flowering: May–Sep. It is a typical ornithophilous plant. The flowers are pollinated by humming birds in the New World. It does not set fruit in S China.
Uses: Ornamental.

Hedyotis acutangula Champ. ex Benth. 金草（方骨草）
Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 4: 171. 1852; FHK 148. 1861; FKH 127. 1912; FHN 3: 303. 1974; FRPS 71(1): 46, pl. 9: 5 – 9. 1999; FGD 6: 123. 2005.
Oldenlandia acutangula (Champ. ex Benth.) Kuntze, Revis. Gen. Pl. 1: 292. 1891.

Perennial herbs, somewhat shrubby, 25–60 cm tall, glabrous. Stems woody at base; branches very acutely quadrangular, or even 4‑winged. Stipules ovate or triangular, 3–5 mm, margin entire or with minute glandular teeth. Leaves opposite, leathery, sessile or nearly so; leaf blade ovate‑lanceolate or lanceolate, 5–12 × 1.5–2.5 cm, base rounded or cuneate, apex acute or shortly acuminate; midvein distinct; lateral veins and reticulation of veins inconspicuous. Flowers 4‑merous, sessile, numerous, in loose dichotomous or trichotomous cymes, forming a terminal oblong or corymbose panicle. Peduncles 1.5–4(–6.5) cm. Calyx‑tube turbinate, ca. 1 mm; calyx‑teeth ovate, shorter than the tube. Corolla white, tube 2.2–3 mm, slightly expanded at throat, upper part tomentose inside; the lobes ovate‑lanceolate, ± equal to the tube. Stamens attached to the top of the corolla‑tube, included; filaments very short or almost wanting. Ovary inferior; style equal to the corolla; stigma bifid. Capsules obovate, 2–2.5 × 1–2 mm, top flat or slightly convex, separating septicidally into 2 carpels; carpels opening ventrally.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 1809; Y. S. Lau 24; HK sheet 40066.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong.
Ecology: Hillslopes, thickets and forests. Flowering: Apr.–Sep.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The type specimen was collected by J. G. Champion from Hong Kong Island between 1847 and 1850.

Hedyotis auricularia L. 耳草
Sp. Pl. 101. 1753; FHK 150. 1861; FKH 128. 1912; FHN 3: 299. 1974; FRPS 71(1): 37. 1999; FYN 14: 35. 2003; FGD 6: 119. 2005.
Oldenlandia auricularia (L.) F. Muell., Syst. Cons. Austral. Pl. 74. 1882.
Exallage auricularia (L.) Bremek., Verh. Kon. Ned. Akad. Wetensch., Afd. Natuurk., Tweede Sect. 48: 142. 1952.

Perennial herbs, 0.3–1 m tall. Stems almost erect or decumbent; young shoots ± quadrangular, densely hispidulous, or rarely glabrous in age. Stipules membranous, pubescent, united at the base into a short sheath, apex fringed with 5–7 bristle‑like lobes. Leaves opposite, subleathery; petioles ca. 2.5 mm; leaf blade lanceolate or elliptic, rarely ovate, 3–8 × 1–2.5 cm, base cuneate or slightly decurrent, apex acute or acuminate, adaxially smooth or scabrous, abaxially usually puberulent; lateral veins 4–6 on each side of midvein, conspicuous, obliquely ascending and in an acute angle with the midvein. Flowers 4‑merous, in axillary, densely flowered, head‑like cymes. Peduncles none. Pedicels ca. 1 mm or almost obsolete. Calyx‑tube pubescent, tube ca. 1 mm; calyx‑teeth lanceolate, 1–1.2 mm. Corolla white, tube 1–1.5 mm, hairy on throat; lobes lanceolate, 1.5–2 mm, spreading. Stamens inserted in throat of corolla‑tube; filaments very short. Ovary inferior; style ca. 1 mm, hairy; stigma bifid. Capsules globose, 1.2–1.5 mm in diam., sparsely hispidulous or almost glabrous, indehiscent.

Locality: Kwai Chung, Shing Mun. Y. W. Lam 1018, 1545.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan; Indochina, India, Nepal, Thailand, Myanmar, Malesia, Australia and tropical Africa.
Ecology: Grassy slopes, thickets. Flowering: Jul. – Oct.; fruting: Sep. –Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Pok Fu Lam, Wong Nai Chung Gap, Wong Chuk Hang, Tai Au Mun, Shing Mun, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Hedyotis biflora (L.) Lam. 雙花耳草
Tabl. Encycl. 1: 272. 1792; FHN 3: 308. 1974; FTW 2, 4: 265, pl. 115. 1998; FRPS 71(1): 77. 1999; FYN 14: 45, pl. 7: 7 – 10. 2003; FGD 6: 135. 2005.
Oldenlandia paniculata L., Sp. Pl. 119. 1753; FHK 152. 1861; FKH 128. 1912.
Oldenlandia biflora L. Sp. Pl. 1: 119. 1753.

Annual slender herbs, glabrous except flowers. Stems diffuse or nearly erect, 10–50 cm tall, usually many‑branched. Stipules membranous, ca. 2 mm, united at the base, apex cuspidate. Leaves opposite, membranous; petioles 2–5 mm; leaf blade oblong or elliptic‑ovate, 1–4 × 0.3–1 cm, base cuneate or decurrent, apex acute or shortly acuminate; midvein plane adaxially, slightly raised abaxially; lateral veins inconspicuous. Flowers 4‑merous, 3–8 together, in cymes on peduncles in the upper axils, sometimes paniculate. Peduncles slender, 8–18 mm. Pedicels slender, 6–10 mm. Calyx‑tube turbinate, 1–1.2 mm; calyx‑teeth triangular, ca. 0.5 mm. Corolla white, tube ca. 1 mm, pilose in throat; lobes oblong, 1.2–1.5 mm. Stamens sessile, inserted in the tube, included. Ovary inferior; style 0.8–1 mm, hairy on the upper part; stigma bifid. Capsules turbinate, membranous, 2.5 – 3 mm in diam., with 2–4 prominent ribs, opening loculicidally when mature.

Locality: Pok Fu Lam, Wong Nai Chung Gap, Wong Chuk Hang, Tai Au Mun, Shing Mun, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 2976; Y. W. Lam 689, 1478.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Jiangsu, Taiwan; Indochina, Malesia, Polynesia.
Ecology: Grasslands. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Oct.

Hedyotis bodinieri Lévl. 大帽山耳草
Repert. Spec. Nov. Regni Veg. 11(274 – 278): 64. 1912; FRPS 71(1): 49. 1999.
Oldenlandia bodinieri (Lévl.) Chun, Sunyatsenia 1: 310. 1934.
Hedyotis lancea auct. non Thunb. ex Maxim.: FKH 127. 1912.

Small shrubs, to 50 cm tall. Stems erect, oppositely branched; branchlets terete, puberulous. Stipules ovate triangular, ca. 2 mm, entire, with short hairs on the margin. Leaves opposite, papery; petioles ca. 2 mm; leaf blade elliptic to ovate elliptic, 2–3.5 × 0.8–2 cm, base broadly cuneate to subrounded, apex acute, glabrous on both surfaces; midvein slightly raised abaxially; lateral nerves 3–4 on each side of midvein, obscure. Cymes axillary, 3‑flowered or arranged in trichotomous cymes on axillary branchlets. Peduncles slender, 4–6 mm, puberulous. Pedicels 1–1.5 mm, puberulous. Flowers 4‑merous; calyx‑tube turbinate, ca. 1.5 mm, calyx‑teeth ovate‑lanceolate, slightly longer than the tube. Corolla white, ca. 4 mm; tube slightly longer than lobes, glarous. Capsules ellipsoid.
