Locality: Tai Mo Shan. N. K. Chun 40663 (IBSC); HK sheet 39914, 39925.
Distribution: Known only from Hong Kong.
Ecology: Forests in ravines. Flowering: Apr.; fruiting: Jul–Sep.
Notes: The type specimen (E. Bodinier 1158) of this species was collected from Tai Mo Shan on 7 May 1895.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Wu Kau Tang, Bride's Pool, Mirror Pool, Pat Sin Leng
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Hedyotis bracteosa Hance 大苞耳草
J. Bot. 23: 323. 1885; FKH 128. 1912; FRPS 71(1): 56, pl. 9: 1 – 4. 1999; FGD 6: 127. 2005.
Oldenlandia bracteosa (Hance) Kuntze, Revis. Gen. Pl. 1: 292. 1891.

Perennial herbs, to 50 cm tall, glabrous throughout. Stems erect, quadrangular. Stipules broadly triangular, 9–10 mm long, 7 mm at base, apex acute, margin revolute, with black glandular dots. Leaves opposite, or subverticillate on the upper part, sessile or nearly so; leaf blade papery, oblong to oblong‑lanceolate, 12–15 × 2–4 cm, base broadly cuneate or obtuse, apex acute or shortly acuminate, tip blunt; midvein depressed adaxially; lateral veins slender, 7 on each side of midvein, obliquely ascending at an acute angle from the midvein, prominent on both surfaces. Flowers 4‑merous, in axillary heads of 1.6 cm in diam. Peduncles 4–15 cm. Pedicels none. Bracts 4, broadly ovate, 1.5–2.5 × 1–1.8 cm, subtending the flowering heads. Calyx‑tube oblong, ca. 2 mm; calyx‑teeth ovate to ovate‑lanceolate, 2.5–3 × 1.8–2 mm, apex acute, sometimes ciliolate. Corolla white, ca. 5 mm; lobes lanceolate, equal to the tube, recurved outward. Stamens attached to the upper part of the corolla‑tube; filaments very short; anthers included. Ovary inferior; style exserted; stigma bifid. Capsules subglobose, ca. 3 × 2 mm, separating septicidally into 2 carpels when mature; carpels opening ventrally.

Locality: Wu Kau Tang, Bride's Pool, Mirror Pool, Pat Sin Leng. Y. S. Lau 2808, 3195; Y. W. Lam 829.
Distribution: Guangdong. Flowering: May –Dec.; fruiting: Aug.–Dec.
Ecology: Forests.

Hedyotis consanguinea Hance 擬金草（紅花耳草）
Ann. Sci. Nat., Bot., ser. 4, 18: 221. 1862; FKH 127. 1912; FRPS 71(1): 47. 1999; FGD 6: 124. 2005.
Oldenlandia consanguinea (Hance) Kuntze, Revis. Gen. Pl. 1: 292. 1891.

Erect herbs, 30 – 40 cm tall. Stems slender, unbranched, slightly angular, glabrous, becoming greyish yellow when dry. Stipules oblong‑ovate, apex acuminate, fringed with minute, glandular teeth. Leaves opposite, subsessile; leaf blade lanceolate or oblong‑ovate, 2 – 3 × 0.8 – 1 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, glabrous, except on the depressed midvein on adaxial surface, margin revolute when dry; lateral veins 2 – 3 on each side of midvein, obscure. Cymes terminal or axillary, or paniculate, 3 – 4 cm. Peduncles 2 – 3 cm. Pedicels 0 – 2 mm. Flowers 4‑merous. Calyx‑tube ca. 1.2 mm; calyx‑teeth lanceolate, ca. 0.8 mm. Corolla white or slightly tinged with purple, tube 2 – 2.5 mm; lobes lanceolate, equal to the tube. Stamens attached to the upper part of the corolla‑tube, exserted in short‑styled flowers, included in long‑styled flowers. Ovary inferior; style dimorphic (long or short); stigma bifid. Capsules ellipsoidal, ca. 3 × 2 mm, apex projecting from the calyx, separating septicidally into 2 carpels; carpels opening ventrally.

Locality: Lantau Island. W. J. Tutcher 5285; H. C. Tang 1253; K. L. Yip 4419.
Distribution: Guangdong, Fujian.
Ecology: Forests, grasslands. Flowering: Feb. – Sep.; fruiting: May – Jun.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Hedyotis corymbosa (L.) Lam. 傘房花耳草
Tabl. Encycl. 1: 272. 1791; FHN 3: 307. 1974; FTW 2, 4: 267. 1998; FRPS 71(1): 72. 1999; FYN 14: 44. 2003; FGD 6: 133. 2005.
Oldenlandia herbacea DC., Prodr. 4: 425. 1830; FHK 151. 1861.
Oldenlandia corymbosa L., Sp. 1: 119. 1753; FKH 128. 1912.

Annual slender herbs, 10–50 cm tall. Stems diffuse, many‑branched; branches glabrous or sparsely pubescent on the edge of angles. Stipule membranous, sheathing, 1–1.5 mm, apex truncate, fringed with short bristle‑like teeth. Leaves opposite, almost sessile, membranous; leaf blade linear to linear lanceolate, 1–2.5 × 0.1–0.3 cm, narrowed at the base, apex acute, margin revolute when dry, scabrous on both surfaces or slightly puberulent on the midvein adaxially; midvein depressed adaxially, plane or slightly raised abaxially; lateral veins obsolete. Peduncles axillary, usually solitary and shorter than the leaves, bearing either a single flower or a 2–5‑flowered cyme. Pedicels filiform, 5–10 mm. Flowers 4‑merous. Calyx‑tube tubular, slightly pubescent, 1–1.2 mm; calyx‑teeth narrowly triangular, ca. 1 mm, ciliate. Corolla white or pink, tube 1.2–1.5 mm; lobes oblong, ca. 1 mm. Stamens inserted in the corolla‑tube; filaments very short. Ovary inferior; style 1.3 mm; stigma bifid. Capsules globular, 1.5–1.8 mm in diam., with minute calyx‑teeth in a ring around the apex.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. S. P. Lau 1; Y. S. Lau 1973; Y. W. Lam 908.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Fujian, Zhejiang, Taiwan; tropical Asia, Africa and America.
Ecology: Wastelands, grasslands. Flowering & fruiting: May–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tung Chung, Tai Ho, San Tau, Pui O
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Hedyotis costata (Roxb.) Kurz 脈耳草
J. Asiat. Soc. Bengal. 45: 135. 1876; FHN 3: 297. 1974; FRPS 71(1): 32, pl. 4: 1 – 8. 1999; FYN 14: 33, pl. 6: 6 – 9. 2003; FGD 6: 117, fig. 51. 2005.
Spermacoce costata Roxb., Hort. Bengal. 10. 1814.

Perennial diffuse herbs, 30–50 cm tall, except for the flowers and fruits all parts sparsely covered with long hairs, which becoming golden yellow when dry. Stipules membranous, united at the base, apex truncate, fringed with several bristles. Leaves opposite, membranous; petioles 5 – 10 mm; leaf blade lanceolate to elliptic‑lanceolate, 5– 8 × 1.5–2.8 cm, base cuneate, slightly decurrent, apex acuminate; lateral veins slender, 4–5 on each side of midvein, obliquely ascending at an acute angle from the midvein. Flowers 4(–5)‑merous, in axillary, simple or compound cymes. Peduncles 5–12 mm. Pedicels very short or almost obsolete. Calyx‑tube turbinate, ca. 0.5 mm; calyx‑teeth lanceolate, ca. 1 mm, recurved outward. Corolla white or purplish, tube 1.2–1.5 mm, apex hairy; lobes oblong, ca. 1 mm. Stamens attached to the top of corolla‑tube; filaments ca. 1 mm; anthers exserted. Ovary inferior; style 1.2–1.5 mm, hairy on the upper half; stigma bifid. Capsules subglobose, 1–1.5 mm in diam., indehiscent.

Locality: Tung Chung, Tai Ho, San Tau, Pui O. Y. W. Lam 662, 799, 1248.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; Indochina, India, Malesia, Philippines.
Ecology: Margins of forests, grassy slopes. Flowering: Apr.–Dec.; fruiting: Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Mount Parker, Mount Gough, Sai Kung, Tai Po, Fung Yuen, Fanling, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Hedyotis diffusa Willd. 白花蛇舌草
Sp. Pl. 1: 566. 1797; FHN 3: 307. 1974; FTW ed. 2, 4: 267. 1998; FRPS 71(1): 75. 1999; FYN 14: 45, pl. 7: 4 – 6. 2003; FGD 6: 134. 2005.
Oldenlandia diffusa (Willd.) Roxb., Hort. Bengal. 11. 1814; FKH 128. 1912.
Oldenlandia herbacea L. var. uniflora Benth., FHK 150. 1861.

Annual diffuse herbs, 20–50 cm tall, glabrous throughout; branches slender, quadrangular. Stipules triangular, 1–2 mm, united at the base, apex aristate. Leaves opposite, membranous, sessile; leaf blade linear, 1–3 × 0.1–0.3 cm, narrowed at the base, apex acute, margin revolute when dry, adaxially smooth, abaxially sometimes scabrous; midvein depressed adaxially, raised abaxially; lateral veins inconspicuous. Flowers 4‑merous, solitary or in pairs in axils of leaves. Pedicels 2–5 mm, rarely longer. Calyx‑tube tubular, ca. 1.5 mm; calyx‑teeth linear oblong‑lanceolate, 1.5–2 mm, ciliate. Corolla white, tube 1.5–2 mm, glabrous; lobes ovate‑oblong, ca. 2 mm. Stamens inserted in the throat of the tube; filaments very short. Ovary inferior; style 2 – 3 mm; stigma bifid. Capsules membranous, depressed globular, 2–2.5 mm, in diam., opening loculicidally at apex.

Locality: Mount Parker, Mount Gough, Sai Kung, Tai Po, Fung Yuen, Fanling, Lantau Island. Y. W. Lam 301, 2310; HK sheet 39827.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Anhui; tropical Asia.
Ecology: Wastelands, grasslands. Flowering & fruiting: Mar.–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tung Chung, Tai O, Lung Chai, San Tau
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Hedyotis effusa Hance 鼎湖耳草
J. Bot. 17: 11. 1879; FKH 127. 1912; FRPS 71(1): 44. 1999; FGD 6: 123, fig. 55. 2005.
Oldenlandia effusa (Hance) Kuntze, Revis. Gen. Pl. 1: 292. 1891.

Perennial glabrous herbs. Stems erect, 0.5–1 m tall, woody at base. Stipules 2–3 mm, triangular or truncate but with a mucro at apex, margin entire. Leaves opposite, papery; petioles 2–5 mm; leaf blade ovate‑lanceolate, 4–9.5 × 2–4 cm, base subrounded or cuneate, apex acute, tip blunt; lateral veins slender, inconspicuous. Flowers 4‑merous, in dichotomous cymes, forming terminal panicles to 10–15 cm long and 4–10 cm broad, branches divaricate and often zigzag. Peduncles slender, 2–4 cm. Pedicels 2–4 mm. Calyx‑tube ovoid, ca. 0.7 mm; calyx‑teeth triangular, ca. 0.4 mm. Corolla white, tube ca. 2 mm; the lobes lanceolate, ca. 3 mm, spreading or recurved,. Stamens inserted in the tube. Ovary inferior; style exserted; stigma bifid. Capsules subglobose, top flat, separating septicidally into 2 carpels; carpels opening ventrally.

Locality: Tung Chung, Tai O, Lung Chai, San Tau. Y. W. Lam 838, 1241, 1658.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Dec.

Hedyotis hedyotidea (DC.) Merr. 牛白藤
Lingnan. Sci. J. 13: 48. 1934; FTW ed. 2, 4: 268, pl. 116. 1998; FRPS 71(1): 67, pl. 12: 1 – 6. 1999; FYN 14: 42. 2003; FGD 6: 131. 2005.
Hedyotis recurva Benth., Lond. J. Bot. 1: 486. 1842; FHK 148. 1861.
Hedyotis macrostemon Hook. & Arn., Bot. Beechey Voy. 192. 1833; FKH 128. 1912.

Half‑climbing subshrubs, 1–3 m or longer. Stems and old branches terete or nearly so; young shoots quadrangular, pulverulent. Stipules 4–6 mm, apex truncate, fringed with 4–6 bristles. Leaves opposite, membranous or papery; petioles 3–10 mm; leaf blade ovate to ovate‑oblong, 4–10 × 2.5–4 cm, base cuneate or obtuse, apex acute or shortly acuminate, adaxially scabrous, abaxially pubescent; lateral veins 4–5 on each side of midvein, obliquely ascending, appressed adaxially, raised abaxially. Flowers 4‑merous, heterostylic, 10–20 together, in little umbels on short peduncles in the upper axils, the upper ones forming a terminal oblong panicle. Peduncles 1.5–2.5 cm, puberulent. Pedicels ca. 2 mm. Calyx‑tube turbinate, ca. 1.5 mm; calyx‑teeth linear‑lanceolate, ca. 2.5 mm, recurved outward. Corolla white, tube ca. 2.5 mm; lobes lanceolate, 4–4.5 mm, spreading or recurved, sparsely pubescent on adaxial surface. Stamens included in long‑styled flowers, exserted in short‑styled flowers; filaments barbate at the base. Ovary inferior; stigma bifid. Capsules subglobose, ca. 3 × 2 mm, apex projecting from the calyx, separating septicidally in the upper part into 2 carpels; carpels opening loculicidally in 2 valves.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 1401, 2191; Y. S. Lau 1322.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Hillslopes, forests and thickets. Flowering & fruiting: All year round.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Clear Water Bay, Tai Mo Shan, Wu Kau Tang, Nam Chung, Pat Sin Leng, Ma On Shan, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Hedyotis loganioides Benth. 粵港耳草
FHK 149. 1861; FKH 127. 1912; FRPS 71(1): 54. 1999; FGD 6: 126. 2005.
Oldenlandia loganioides (Benth.) Kuntze, Revis. Gen. Pl. 1: 292. 1891.

Perennial herbs, to 30 cm tall, glabrous. Stems ascending or erect; branches terete, obtusely angular, slightly compressed when young. Stipules ovate triangular, entire. Leaves opposite, papery; petioles ca. 4 mm; leaf blade oblong or lanceolate, 2.5–5 × 1.4–3 cm, acute on both ends; midvein slightly raised abaxially; lateral veins 3 –5 on each side of midvein, obscure. Flowers 4‑merous, 10–20 together in trichotomous cymes. Peduncles 14–20 mm. Pedicels very short. Calyx‑tube turbinate, ca. 1.5 mm; calyx‑teeth linear slightly shorter than the corolla. Corolla white, tube short and slender, glabrous. Capsules ellipsoidal, ca. 2 mm long, crowned by the calyx‑lobes, the 2 carpels separating to the base, and opening wide by a fissure on the inner face.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Clear Water Bay, Tai Mo Shan, Wu Kau Tang, Nam Chung, Pat Sin Leng, Ma On Shan, Lantau Island. L. T. Lo 630; Y. S. Lau 3256; Y. W. Lam 1400.
Distribution: Guangdong.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Feb.–Dec.; fruiting: May–Dec.
Notes: A syntype specimen was collected from Mount Gough, Hong Kong Island by C. Wilford in 1858.

Hedyotis matthewii Dunn 疏花耳草
J. Bot. 47: 376. 1909; FKH 128. 1912; FRPS 71(1): 54, pl. 6: 7 – 10. 1999; FGD 6: 127. 2005.
Oldenlandia matthewii (Dunn) Chun, Sunyatsenia 1(4): 312. 1934.

Perennial herbs 30–75 cm tall, except the flowers glabrous. Stems erect, ± woody at the base, lower part terete, upper part quadrangular. Stipules ovate triangular, ca. 2 mm, margin with minute, glandular teeth or deeply lobed. Leaves opposite, papery; petioles ca. 3 mm; leaf blade lanceolate to elliptic‑lanceolate, 4–8 × 1.5–4 cm, base acute or cuneate, apex long acuminate; lateral veins 3 on each side of midvein, obliquely ascending at an acute angle from the midvein, appressed adaxially; veinlets obscure. Flowers 4‑merous, in terminal or axillary dichotomous cymes. Peduncles 0.5–3 cm. Pedicels 2–4 mm. Calyx‑tube turbinate or obovate, ca. 1 mm; calyx‑teeth lanceolate, 2–2.2 mm, apex acute. Corolla white or tinged with purple, tube 2–2.5 mm; the lobes lanceolate, ca. 3 mm, recurved, tomentose on adaxial surface. Stamens attached to the corolla‑tube. Ovary inferior; style ca. 8 mm, exserted; stigma capitate. Capsules ellipsoidal, 3–4 mm long, separating septicidally into 2 carpels; carpels opening ventrally.

Locality: Sunset Peak. Y. S. Lau 2578; HK sheet 30343.
Distribution: Guangdong.
Ecology: Forests and thickets. Flowering: Apr. –Dec.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Aberdeen, Shek O, Tsim Shan, Lamma Island, Lantau Island, Po Toi Islands
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Hedyotis pinifolia Wall. ex G. Don 松葉耳草
Gen. Hist. 3: 526. 1834; Hook. f., Fl. Brit. Ind. 3: 60. 1880; FKH 128. 1912; FHN 3: 301. 1974; FRPS 71(1): 43, pl. 4: 9 – 14. 1999; FYN 14: 36. 2003; FGD 6: 122. 2005.

Annual diffuse herbs, 10–25 cm tall. Stems many‑branched; branchlets slender, sharply 4‑angular, turning dark brown when dry. Stipules united into a short sheath at the base, apex truncate, fringed with 2–4 bristles. Leaves whorled or opposite, sessile; leaf blade linear, 1.2–4 × 0.1–0.2 cm, base cuneate, apex acute, margin revolute when dry, both surfaces scabrous, rarely pubescent; midvein depressed adaxially, raised abaxially; lateral veins inconspicuous. Flowers 4‑merous, 3–10 together, in axillary or terminal glomerules. Peduncles none. Pedicels ca. 1 mm. Calyx‑tube obconical, 1–1.5 mm, sparsely hispidulous; calyx‑teeth subulate, ca. 1 mm, ciliate. Corolla white, tube 4–4.2 mm; lobes oblong, equal to the tube. Stamens inserted in the throat of the tube; filaments ca. 2 mm; anthers exserted. Ovary inferior; style ca. 9 mm; stigma 2‑lobed; lobes linear, ca. 1 mm, spreading. Capsules ovoid, 2.5–3 × 1.5–2 mm, sparsely hispidulous, opening at apex when mature.

Locality: Aberdeen, Shek O, Tsim Shan, Lamma Island, Lantau Island, Po Toi Islands. Y. W. Lam 772, 1061; K. Y. Tam 147.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; India, Nepal, Vietnam, Malesia.
Ecology: Open fields, grasslands. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Sep.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai, Shing Mun Reservoir, Tai Po, Hoi Ha, Pat Sin Leng, Pin Fung Shan, Sai Kung
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Hedyotis shiuyingiae T. Chen 秀英耳草
Harv. Pap. Bot. 13(2): 283, fig. 1 – 2 A – C, E. 2008.

Perennial herbs or shrubs, erect, 15 – 35 cm tall, glabrous. Stems slightly quadrangular, internodes 1–3.5(–4.5) cm. Stipules triangular, 4–8 × 5–10 mm, acute at apex, with dense trichomes at margins. Leaves decussate, thick papery, subleathery when dry; petioles 5–10 mm or leaves subsessile; leaf blade broadly lanceolate or obovate‑lanceolate, (2–)3–12.5(–19) × (1.4–)2 – 4.5(–8) cm, base decurrent and cuneate, apex acuminate or acute; midvein prominent abaxially, flattened adaxially or slightly impressed; lateral veins 5–7 on each side of midvein, inconspicuous abaxially, slightly conspicuous adaxially. Flowers 4‑merous, heterostylic, shortly pedicellate, crowded in head‑like clusters, these clusters 2–3 together forming a terminal compound cymes of 12–35 cm, terminal, or sometimes 2 or more in uppermost leaf axils. Peduncles ca. 10 cm; lower bracts leaf‑like, becoming smaller upward and finally subulate. Calyx lobes 2.5–3 mm, subulate. Corolla purple outside; tube narrowly infundibuliform, 4– 5 mm; abaxially glabrous, adaxially white hairy; lobes 4, reflexed, 2–2.5 × 1.5–1.8 mm; stamens 4, included; long‑style ca. 5 mm, short‑style 1–2 mm. Capsules globular, ca. 2.5 mm in diam.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai, Shing Mun Reservoir, Tai Po, Hoi Ha, Pat Sin Leng, Pin Fung Shan, Sai Kung. H. C. Tang 2495, Y. S. Lau 422, L. T. Lo 612.
Distribution: Endemic to Hong Kong.
Ecology: Thickets and forests on wet rocks. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Nov.
Notes: The type specimen (T. Chen et al. 2007004, HK, holotype; A, SZG, isotypes) was collected from Tai Po in 2007. The species was reported previously as Hedyotis yangchunensis W. C. Ko & Zhang (陽春耳草) (Check List HK Plants 265. 2002; 91. 2004).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Ping Shan Chai, Ng Tung Chai, Po Toi Islands
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Hedyotis tenelliflora Blume 纖花耳草
Bijdr. Fl. Ned. Ind. 971. 1826; FKH 128. 1912; FHN 3: 300. 1974; FTW ed. 2, 4: 271, pl. 118. 1998; FRPS 71(1): 41. 1999; FYN 14: 36. 2003; FGD 6: 121. 2005.
Oldenlandia angustifolia Benth., FHK 151. 1861.
Hedyotis angustifolia Cham. & Schltdl., Linnaea 4: 153. 1829.

Perennial herbs. Stems diffuse or decumbent, 15–40 cm or longer; branchlets quadrangular, glabrous. Stipules 3– 6 mm, united at the base, slightly pubescent, with several bristle‑like teeth. Leaves opposite, almost sessile, thin‑leathery; leaf blade linear to linear lanceolate, 2–5 × 0.2–0.4 cm, base cuneate, slightly decurrent, apex acute or acuminate, in dry state margin ± revolute, adaxial surface turning black, covered with rounded, pellucid minute scales, abaxial surface paler, smooth; midvein depressed adaxially, raised abaxially; lateral veins inconspicuous. Flowers 4‑merous, sessile, 2–3 clustered in axils of leaves. Calyx‑tube obovate, ca. 1 mm; calyx‑teeth linear‑lanceolate, ca. 1.8 mm, ciliate. Corolla white, tube ca. 2 mm; lobes oblong, 1–1.5 mm. Stamens inserted in the throat of corolla‑tube; filaments ca. 1.5 mm; anthers exserted. Ovary inferior; style ca. 4 mm; stigma bifid. Capsules ovoid or nearly globular, 1.5–2 mm in diam., crowned by the linear lanceolate calyx‑teeth.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Ping Shan Chai, Ng Tung Chai, Po Toi Islands. H. C. Tang 1407; Y. S. Lau 1661; Y. W. Lam 898.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Taiwan.
Ecology: Abandoned farmlands, margins of fields. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Tai Au Mun, Shing Mun, Sai Kung, Ma On Shan
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Hedyotis uncinella Hook. & Arn. 長節耳草
Bot. Beechey Voy. 192. 1833; FHK 149. 1861; FKH 127. 1912; FHN 3: 304. 1974; FTW ed. 2, 4: 271, pl. 119. 1998; FRPS 71(1): 59. 1999; FYN 14: 38. 2003; FGD 6: 128. 2005.
Hedyotis borrerioides Champ. ex Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 4: 171. 1852.

Perennial herbs. Stems erect, quadrangular, glabrous, or rarely puberulent. Stipules triangular, 11–12 mm, united at the base, apex with several teeth or lobes. Leaves opposite, papery; petioles very short or almost obsolete; leaf blade ovate to ovate‑lanceolate, 3.5–7.5 × 1–3 cm, base obtuse or attenuate and decurrent, apex acuminate, glabrous or sparsely puberulent on the veins of adaxial surface, rarely puberulent on both surfaces; lateral veins slender, 4–5 on each side of midvein, obliquely ascending at an acute angle from the midvein; reticulation of veins inconspicuous. Flowers 4‑merous, densely crowded in terminal or axillary heads of 12–15 mm in diam., subsessile. Pedicels obsolete or very short. Calyx‑tube subglobular, ca. 3 mm; calyx‑teeth oblong‑lanceolate, ca. 3 mm, apex obtuse, glabrous or ciliolate. Corolla white or purple, tube ca. 3 mm, tomentose at throat; lobes oblong‑lanceolate, shorter than the tube. Stamens attached to the top of corolla‑tube; filaments very short; anthers included. Ovary inferior; style ca. 2 mm; stigma bifid. Capsules broadly ovate, 1.8–2 mm in diam., top flat, separating septicidally into 2 carpels; carpels opening ventrally.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Tai Au Mun, Shing Mun, Sai Kung, Ma On Shan. S. P. Lau 30; L. T. Lo 300, 456.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Taiwan; India.
Ecology: Grasslands. Flowering & fruiting: May–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The type specimen of Hedyotis borrerioides was collected by J. G. Champion from “Chuckchow” (Stanley), Hong Kong Island, between 1847 and 1850.

Hedyotis vachellii Benth. 香港耳草（華氏耳草）
FHK 148. 1861; FKH 127. 1912; FRPS 71(1): 49. 1999.

Perennial herbs, 30–40 cm tall, glabrous throughout. Stems woody at base; branches terete or scarcely angular. Stipules triangular, apex acute, ciliolate. Leaves opposite; petioles ca. 2 mm, or almost obsolete in the upper leaves; leaf blade oblong‑lanceolate, 4–7 × 1–2 cm, acute at both ends; midvein slightly raised adaxially, broad and plane abaxially; lateral veins almost invisible. Flowers 4‑merous, in dichotomous or trichotomous cymes, forming a terminal oblong or corymbose panicle to 4–4.5 cm long and ca. 3.5 cm broad. Peduncles ca. 2 cm, primary rays ca. 1.5 cm, secondary rays 0.8–1 cm. Pedicels ca. 2 mm. Calyx‑tube turbinate, ca. 0.5 mm; calyx‑teeth lanceolate, equal to the tube, spreading, apex obtuse. Corolla white, tube ca. 3 mm, pilose inside; the lobes ovate‑triangular, ca. 2 mm, glabrous. Stamens inserted in the tube, exserted. Ovary inferior; style included; stigma thick and bifid. Capsules subglobose, ca. 1.8 mm in diam., separating septicidally into 2 carpels; carpels opening ventrally.

Locality: Fanling, Lantau Island. W. J. Tutcher 11162; P. S. Choi 96; Y. W. Lam 2209.
Distribution: Endemic to Hong Kong.
Ecology: Valleys. Flowering: Mar. –Dec.; fruiting: Jun.–Dec.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Tai Po, Fung Yuen, Ta Kwu Ling, Lantau Island, Peng Chau
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Hedyotis verticillata (L.) Lam. 粗葉耳草（輪葉耳草）
Tabl. Encycl. 1: 271. 1792; Hara & al., Enum. Flow. Pl. Nepal. 2: 202. 1979; FTW ed. 2, 4: 271. 1998; FRPS 71(1): 42. 1999; FYN 14: 37. 2003; FGD 6: 121. 2005.
Hedyotis hispida Retz., Observ. Bot. 4: 23. 1786.

Annual diffuse herbs, 25–30 cm tall. Branches often decumbent, sparsely or densely hirtellous. Stipules united with petioles into a sheath, apex almost truncate, fringed with bristles. Leaves opposite, sessile or nearly so; leaf blade papery or thinly leathery, elliptic, ovate‑elliptic or lanceolate, 2.5–6.5 × 0.6–2 cm, base cuneate or obtuse, apex acute or acuminate, hispidulous on both surfaces, margin revolute when dry; midvein depressed adaxially, raised; lateral veins inconspicuous. Flowers 4‑merous, in axillary glomerules. Peduncles and pedicels none. Calyx‑tube obconical, ca. 1 mm, hispidulous; calyx‑teeth lanceolate, 1–1.5 mm. Corolla white, tube ca. 2 mm; lobes lanceolate, 1.8–2 mm, barbate at apex. Stamens inserted in throat of the tube; filaments ca. 2 mm; anthers exserted. Ovary inferior; style 4 – 4.5 mm; stigma capitate. Capsules ovoid, 1.5–2 mm in diam., hispidulous, opening only at apex when mature.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Po, Fung Yuen, Ta Kwu Ling, Lantau Island, Peng Chau. Y. S. Lau 1961; Y. W. Lam 874, 909.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Zhejiang, Taiwan.
Ecology: Ravines. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): To Fung Shan, Man Kam To, Sai Kung, Ha Pak Nai, also widely cultivated
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Ixora chinensis Lam. 龍船花
Encycl. 3: 344. 1789; FKH 132. 1912; FRPS 71(2): 37, pl. 11: 1 – 5. 1999; D. M. Bridson, Kew Bull. 55: 1012. 2000; FYN 15: 212, pl. 43: 8 – 12. 2003; FGD 6: 203. 2005.
Ixora stricta Roxb., Hort. Bengal. 10. 1814, nom nud.; Fl. Ind. ed. 1820, 1: 388. 1820; FHK 158. 1861.
Tsiangia hongkongensis (Seem.) But, Hsue & P. T. Li, Blumea 31: 311. 1986; FPRS 71(2): 110. 1999.
Gaertnera hongkongensis Seem., Bot. Voy. Herald 384. 1857.

Evergreen shrubs, 0.5–2 m tall, glabrous throughout. Leaves subleathery; petioles thick, 2–5 mm; stipules broadly ovate, 3–5 mm including the aristate apex; leaf blade lanceolate, oblong‑lanceolate or oblong‑oblanceolate, 6–13 × 2–5 cm, base cuneate or obtuse; apex acute, tip blunt, lateral veins slender, 7–8 on each side of midvein. Cymes terminal, trichotomous, subsessile, the branches and pedicels scarlet‑orange; primary branches 6–15 mm; pedicels 1–2 mm. Calyx‑tube 1–1.5 mm; lobes 4, triangular, ca. 0.8 mm. Corolla scarlet‑orange; tube slender, 3 – 4 cm; lobes 4, elliptic, (5–)7–9 × 3.5–7 mm, apex rounded, spreading. Style and anthers exserted. Drupe globular, 6–8 mm in diam., reddish black when mature.

Locality: To Fung Shan, Man Kam To, Sai Kung, Ha Pak Nai, also widely cultivated. L. T. Lo 558; Y. W. Lam 1012; HK sheet 40210.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Thickets and thin forests. Flowering: Jul.–Nov.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: The type specimen of Gaertnera hongkongensis was collected by J. G. Champion from Hong Kong Island between 1847 and 1850.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Mount Kellet, Lan Nai Wan, Shing Mun, Tai Po, Po Toi Islands, Peng Chau
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Knoxia corymbosa Willd. 紅芽大戟
Sp. Pl. ed. 4, 1(2): 582. 1789; FHK 164. 1861; FKH 132. 1912; FHN 3: 360, fig. 772. 1974; FTW ed. 2, 4: 274, pl. 120, photo 175. 1998; FRPS 71(2): 5, pl. 2. 1999; FYN 15: 197. 2003.

Perennial erect herbs, to 1 m tall. Stems and branches obtusely 4‑angled, pubescent. Leaves membranous; petioles 1–6 mm, or almost obsolete; stipules 3–6 mm, fringed with 3–5 bristle‑like teeth; leaf blade lanceolate or oblong, 3– 10 × 0.8–2.5 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, covered with appressed hairs on both surfaces; lateral veins 6–9 on each side of midvein, conspicuous on both surfaces. Flowers numerous, subsessile, loose, terminal dichotomous cymes of 2 – 6 cm long. Calyx‑tube ca. 1 mm, glabrous, with minute, triangular teeth. Corolla white or purple; tube ca. 2 mm, hairy inside; lobes less than 1 mm. Capsule ovoid, ca. 2–3 mm, with 4–8 weak ribs, usually falling off entirely from the filiform persistent axis.

Locality: Mount Kellet, Lan Nai Wan, Shing Mun, Tai Po, Po Toi Islands, Peng Chau. Y. S. Lau 1481; Y. W. Lam 277, 1053.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; Indochina, Malesia, Indian subcontinent.
Ecology: Open fields, thin forests and thickets on hillslopes. Flowering: Summer to autumn; fruiting: Oct.–Nov.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Victoria Peak, Sai Kung, Wong Chuk Yeung, Shing Mun, Yuen Tun Ha, Ng Tung Chai
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Lasianthus attenuatus Jack 斜基粗葉木（小葉雞屎樹）
Trans. Linn. Soc. London 14(1): 126. 1823; FYN 15: 237, pl. 49: 1–8. 2003; FGD 6: 215. 2005.
Lasianthus wallichii (Wight & Arn.) Wight, Calcutta J. Nat. Hist. 6: 503. 1846; FTW ed. 2, 4: 295, pl. 133, photo 180. 1998; FRPS 71(2): 72, pl. 18: 1 – 7. 1999; Check List HK Plants 267. 2002; 92. 2004.
Mephitidia wallichii Wight & Arn., Prodr. Fl. Ind. Orient. 1: 390. 1834.

Shrubs, 1–2(–3) m tall. Branchlets, petioles and abaxial surface of leaves densely yellowish hirsute. Leaves papery or subleathery; petioles 2–5 mm; stipules linear‑lanceolate; leaf blade elliptic‑ovate or oblong‑ovate, rarely lanceolate or oblong‑lanceolate, 4–10(–13) × 2–4.5 cm, base cordate and oblique, apex abruptly acuminate, adaxial surface glabrous and ± shining; lateral veins 6–8 on each side of midvein, conspicuous on both surfaces; tertiary veins slender, loosely reticulate. Flowers 5–6 in axillary sessile clusters. Bracts and bracteoles many, subulate‑lanceolate or linear, 10–15 mm. Calyx‑tube cupular, ca. 1.5 mm; lobes 5, triangular‑lanceolate, about the length of the tube or slightly longer. Corolla white, ± funnel‑shaped; tube 7–8 mm, villose inside; lobes 5, subovate, 3.5–4 mm, densely hairy on the adaxial surface. Drupes subglobose, 4–5(–10) mm in diam., hirsute, blue when mature.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Sai Kung, Wong Chuk Yeung, Shing Mun, Yuen Tun Ha, Ng Tung Chai. Y. S. Lau 1629; P. S. Choi 261; Y. W. Lam 508.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Malay Peninsula.
Ecology: Forests or thickets. Flowering: Apr.–Dec.; fruiting: Aug.–Dec.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan, Sai Kung, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Lasianthus chinensis (Champ. ex Benth.) Benth. 粗葉木
FHK 160. 1861; FKH 134. 1912; FHN 3: 337. 1974; FTW ed. 2, 4: 280, pl. 123, photo 177. 1998; FRPS 71(2): 84, pl. 22: 1 – 5. 1999; H. Zhu, Act. Phytotax. Sin. 39(2): 123. 2001; FGD 6: 221. 2005.
Mephitidia chinensis Champ. ex Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 4: 196. 1852.

Shrubs, 2–4 m tall. Branches flattened and shortly tomentose when young, terete and nearly glabrous in age. Leaves thin‑leathery or thickly papery; petioles 6–8 mm, shortly tomentose; stipules triangular‑subulate, the upper ones rather long; leaf blade oblong, elliptic or oblong‑lanceolate, 11–21 × 3.5–7.5 cm, base broadly cuneate or obtuse, apex acuminate, adaxial surface glabrous, tawny tomentose on abaxial surface; lateral veins 9–14 on each side of midvein, conspicuous on both surfaces; veinlets reticulate. Flowers 5 – 6 in axillary sessile clusters. Bracts absent. Calyx‑tube bell‑shaped, shortly tomentose outside; lobes triangular‑ovate. Corolla salverform; tube ca. 10 mm, white tomentellous on the upper part; lobes oblong‑lanceolate, about the length of the tube, very hairy on the abaxial surface. Drupes globular, 5–6 mm in diam., pubescent, blue or purplish when mature.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan, Sai Kung, Lantau Island. L. T. Lo 605; S. C. Ng 3789; K. L. Yip 4380.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Malay Peninsula.
Ecology: Forests or thickets. Flowering: Apr.–Dec.; fruiting: May–Dec.
Notes: The type specimens were collected by J. G. Champion from Wong Nai Chung and Victoria Peak between 1847 and 1850.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Wu Kau Tang, Tai Mo Shan, Tai Po Kau, Tai Po
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Lasianthus curtisii King & Gamble 廣東粗葉木
J. Asiat. Soc. Bengal. 73(3): 128. 1904; FTW ed. 2, 4: 280, pl. 124. 1998; FRPS 71(2): 92, pl. 24: 7 – 12. 1999; H. Zhu, Act. Phytotax. Sin. 39(2): 126. 2001; FGD 6: 219. 2005.
Lasianthus kwangtungensis Merr., Lingnan. Sci. J. 7: 323. 1929.

Shrubs, 1–3 m tall. Branchlets, petioles and stipules densely hirsute. Leaves papery; petioles rather thick, usually less than 10 mm; stipules small, narrowly triangular, 1.5–2 mm; leaf blade oblong‑lanceolate or oblong, sometimes subovate, 5–10 × 1.5–4 cm, base broadly cuneate or obtuse, apex acuminate or caudate, olive green or glaucescent when dry, adaxial surface glabrous, abaxial surface villose or hirsute; lateral veins 5–6 on each side of midvein; veinlets slender subparallel. Flowers more than 10 in axillary sessile clusters. Bracts none or very small. Calyx‑tube subobconical, ca. 1.5 mm, densely hirsute; lobes usually 5, linear‑lanceolate or narrowly lanceolate, 3 – 4(–5) mm, much longer than the tube. Corolla white, 7–8 mm, hirsute outside, villose inside; lobes 5, oblong‑lanceolate, about the length of the tube, very hairy on the abaxial surface. Drupes subglobose or ovoid, 4–5(–7) mm in diam., hirsute, blue to dark blue when mature.

Locality: Wu Kau Tang, Tai Mo Shan, Tai Po Kau, Tai Po. W. J. Tutcher 10919; Y. W. Lam 180, 497.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Malay Peninsula.
Ecology: Forests or thickets. Flowering: Apr.–Dec.; fruiting: May–Dec.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Shing Mun, Yin Ngam, Wong Chuk Yeung, Wu Kau Tang
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Lasianthus fordii Hance 羅浮粗葉木
J. Bot. 23(275): 324. 1885; FKH 134. 1912; FTW ed. 2, 4: 284, pl. 126, photo 178. 1998; FRPS 71(2): 97, pl. 25: 5 – 9. 1999; H. Zhu, Act. Phytotax. Sin. 39(2): 127. 2001; FGD 6: 221, fig. 119. 2005.

Shrubs, 1–2 m tall. Branchlets slender, slightly angled, glabrous. Leaves papery; petioles 5–10 mm, hirsute; stipules small, subtriangular, 1–1.5 mm; leaf blade oblong‑lanceolate or oblong‑ovate, sometimes oblong, 5–12 × 2–4 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate or caudate‑acuminate, glabrous or sparsely hirsute on midvein and lateral veins; lateral veins 4–5(–6) on each side of midvein; veinlets slender, subparallel. Flowers subsessile, in axillary clusters. Bracts very small or absent. Calyx‑tube obconical, 1.2–1.5 mm, usually glabrous; lobes 4 or 5, very small, 0.3–0.5 mm, sparsely hirsute. Corolla white, tubular or ± funnel‑shaped; tube 4–5 mm, glabrous outside, white‑villose on the upper part of inside; lobes 4–5, narrowly triangular‑lanceolate, ca. 1.5 mm, apex incurved and beak‑shaped, sparsely hirsute near apex abaxially, white pubescent adaxially. Drupes subglobose, ca. 6 mm in diam., glabrous, blue or purplish when mature.

Locality: Shing Mun, Yin Ngam, Wong Chuk Yeung, Wu Kau Tang. P. S. Choi 438; Y. W. Lam 495, 504.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Malay Peninsula.
Ecology: Forests or thickets. Flowering: Apr.–Dec.; fruiting: May–Dec.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Mount Nicholson, Happy Valley, Wong Chuk Yeung
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Lasianthus hirsutus (Roxb.) Merr. 雞屎樹
J. Arnold Arbor. 33(3): 229. 1952; FRPS 71(2): 79, pl. 27: 5 – 10. 1999; H. Zhu, Act. Phytotax. Sin. 39(2): 129. 2001; FGD 6: 217. 2005.
Lasianthus cyanocarpus auct. non Jack: FHK 160. 1861; FKH 134. 1912; FTW ed. 2, 4: 280, pl. 125. 1998.
Triosteum hirsutum Roxb., Fl. Ind., ed. 1820, 2: 180. 1824.

Shrubs, 1–2(–3) m tall. Branchlets, bracts and abaxial surface of leaves densely rusty hirsute. Leaves papery; petioles 8–15 mm or slightly longer, densely covered with appressed coarse hairs; stipules ovate‑triangular, 8–12 mm, densely hirsute; leaf blade oblong‑elliptic, oblong‑obovate, oblong, or sometimes oblanceolate, 15–25 × 4– 6 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate or caudate, broadly cuneate or obtuse, adaxial surface hirsute or glabrescent, abaxial surface thickly hirsute; lateral veins 8–12 on each side of midvein; veinlets parallel. Bracts many, outer ones larger, ovate or lanceolate, 2.5–3 × 1–1.5 cm, apex caudate, inner ones smaller, linear‑lanceolate. Flowers 5 – 6 in axillary sessile clusters. Calyx‑tube sub‑bell‑shaped, 1.5–2 mm, densely appressed setose on the upper part; lobes 4 or 5, subulate, ca. 1.5 mm. Corolla white, funnel‑shaped; tube 12–13 mm, sparsely glandular pubescent outside, densely villose on the upper part inside; lobes 4 or 5, oblong or lanceolate, ca. 3.5 mm, glandular‑ciliate. Drupes subglobose, 7–8 mm in diam., blue or purplish when mature, sparsely hairy or glabrescent.

Locality: Mount Nicholson, Happy Valley, Wong Chuk Yeung. Y. W. Lam 750, 507, 1642.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Malay Peninsula.
Ecology: Forests or thickets. Flowering: Apr.–Dec.; fruiting: May–Dec.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Tam, Fei Ngo Shan, Shing Mun, Wu Kau Tang, Kai Kung Leng
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Lasianthus verticillatus (Lour.) Merr. 斜脈粗葉木
Trans. Amer. Philos. Soc. n.s., 24(2): 372. 1935; H. Zhu, Act. Phytotax. Sin. 39(2):144. 2001; FYN 15: 245. 2003; FGD 6: 224. 2005.
Lasianthus obliquinervis Merr., Philipp. J. Sci. 1 (suppl. 1): 136. 1907; FRPS 71(2): 100, pl. 26: 1 – 6. 1999; Check List HK Plants 267. 2002; 92. 2004.
Lasianthus trichophlebus auct. non Hemsl.: FHN 3: 336. 1974.
Dasus verticillatus Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 142. 1790.

Shrubs, 1–3 m tall. Branches subterete, becoming black or dark grey when dry, sparsely puberulent (visible under hand lens). Leaves thickly papery or subleathery; petioles rather thick, usually less than 10 mm, densely appressed‑pubescent; stipules subtriangular, 3.5–5 mm, appressed‑pubescent; leaf blade oblong to narrowly oblong, occasionally elliptic or ovate‑elliptic, rarely obovate, 10–20 × 2.5–5.5 cm, base acute or obtuse, apex acute or acuminate, often slightly oblique, grey or greyish brown when dry, adaxial surface glabrous and shining, abaxial surface appressed‑pubescent on veins and veinlets; lateral veins 5–7(–9) on each side of midvein; veinlets subparallel. Flowers sessile, in axillary clusters. Bracts none. Calyx‑tube ± bell‑shaped, 4–5 mm, pubescent; limb almost truncate. Corolla white; tube ca. 6 mm, hirsute abaxially, white‑villose on the upper part adaxially; lobes 5, oblong or ovate, ca. 4 mm, villose on the adaxial surface. Drupes ovoid, 7 – 9 mm in diam., pubescent.

Locality: Tai Tam, Fei Ngo Shan, Shing Mun, Wu Kau Tang, Kai Kung Leng. S. C. Ng 3151; K. L. Yip 4458.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Malay Peninsula.
Ecology: Forests or thickets. Flowering: Apr.–Dec.; fruiting: May–Dec.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Deep Water Bay, Kwai Chung, Sha Tin, Sha Kok Mei
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Mitracarpus hirtus (L.) DC. 蓋裂果
Prodr. 4: 572. 1830.
Mitracarpus villosus (Sw.) Cham. & Schltdl., Linnaea 3(4): 363. 1828, nom. inval.
Mitracarpus villosus (Sw.) DC., 4: 572. 1830; Verdc., Fl. Trop. East Africa 375, fig. 55. 1976; FRPS 71(2): 210, pl. 50. 1999;Check List HK Plants 267. 2002; 92. 2004.
Spermacoce hirta L. Sp. Pl. ed. 2, 1: 148. 1762.
Spermacoce villosa Sw., Prodr. 29. 1788.

Perennial herbs, 40–80 cm tall. Stems erect, slightly angled on the upper part, sparsely hirsute. Leaves sessile; stipules united at base, apex with unequal bristle‑like lobes; leaf blade oblong or lanceolate, 3–4.5 × 0.7–1.5 cm, apex acute, tapering to the base, adaxially scabrous or with sparse short hairs, abaxially pubescent, margin scabrous; lateral veins slender, inconspicuous. Flowers small, in head‑like axillary clusters. Bracteoles linear, about the length of the calyx. Calyx pubescent; tube subglobular; lobes unequal, 2 larger ones 1.8–2 mm, smaller ones 0.8–1.2 mm, ciliate. Corolla funnel‑shaped, 2–2.2 mm, glabrous inside; lobes triangular, about 1/3 of the tube, apex obtuse. Capsule subglobose, ca. 1 mm in diam., scabrous or sparsely puberulent.

Locality: Deep Water Bay, Kwai Chung, Sha Tin, Sha Kok Mei. P. S. Choi 55, 159; Y. W. Lam 1017.
Distribution: Hainan; India, tropical America & Africa.
Ecology: Wastelands. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Dec.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Ma On Shan, Hoi Ha, Lai Chi Wo
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Morinda cochinchinensis DC. 大果巴戟
Prodr. 4: 449. 1830; Pit. in Lecomte, Fl. Gen. Indo‑chine 3: 420. 1924; FHN 3: 331. 1974; FRPS 71(2): 188. 1999; FGD 6: 236. 2005.
Morinda villosa auct. non Hook. f.: FKH 133. 1912.

Climbing shrubs. Branchlets, petioles and peduncles densely covered with rusty long hairs. Leaves opposite, papery; petioles 5–11 mm; stipules tubular, scarious, 6–10 mm, apex truncate, with 2 mucros on each side; leaf blade elliptic, oblong or obovate‑oblong, 8–14 × 3–6 cm, base obtuse or slightly cordate, apex caudate‑acuminate or shortly acuminate, adaxially sparsely strigose, abaxially densely rusty pubescent; lateral veins slender, 7–10 on each side of midvein. Flower‑heads 5 – 15‑flowered, arranged in terminal umbels; peduncles 1–3 cm. Calyx‑tube hemispherical, sparsely pubescent abaxially; limb 4 – 5‑lobed; lobes unequal, subulate, 1–2 m. Corolla white; tube ca. 2 mm, glabrous; lobes 4–5, oblong‑lanceolate, 4–5.5 mm, apex incurved, abaxially puberulent, densely bearded on the lower part of adaxial surface. Compound berry subglobose, 1–2 cm in diam., pubescent, orange when mature.

Locality: Ma On Shan, Hoi Ha, Lai Chi Wo. HK sheet 14148, 35586, 35712.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; N Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Aug.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Morinda parvifolia Bartl. ex DC. 雞眼藤
Prodr. 4: 499. 1830; FHN 3: 333. 1974; FTW ed. 2, 4: 299. 1998; FRPS 71(2): 194. 1999; FGD 6: 238. 2005.

Climbing shrubs. Branchlets hirsute on the distal nodes. Leaves opposite, papery; petioles 3 – 6 mm, glabrescent or ± puberulent; stipules 1.5–3 mm, apex truncate, glabrescent; leaf blade obovate or obovate‑elliptic, rarely elliptic‑oblong, 2–6 × 1–3 cm, base cuneate to broadly cuneate, apex acute or obtuse and mucronate, adaxially glabrous, abaxially with cluster of hairs in axils of veins, or sometimes with short hairs on the veins; lateral veins 3–4 on each side of midvein. Flower‑heads 4–8‑flowered, 2–6 arranged in terminal umbels; peduncles 5–10 mm, covered with short hairs. Calyx‑tube hemispherical, apex truncate. Corolla white or greenish white; tube ca. 1 mm, with curling hairs on the lower part of abaxial surface, bearded adaxially; limb deeply 4‑lobed, oblong. Compound berry depressed globose, 8 – 10 mm in diam., red when mature.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. L. T. Lo 41; S. P. Lau 174; P. S. Choi 533.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam, Philippines.
Ecology: Forests and thickets. Flowering: Apr.–Jul.; fruiting: Jun.–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Ma On Shan, Tai Po Kau, Sai Wan Shan, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Morinda umbellata L. 羊角藤
Sp. Pl. 176. 1753; FHK 159. 1861; FKH 133. 1912; FHN 3: 332. 1974; FTW ed. 2, 4: 301. 1998.
Morinda umbellata L. subsp. obovata Y. Z. Ruan, FRPS 71(2): 324. 1999.

Trailing, diffuse or somewhat climbing shrubs. Branchlets, petioles and peduncles glabrous or slightly puberulent. Leaves opposite, thinly leathery or papery; petioles 6–10 mm; stipules scarious, 2–5 mm; leaf blade lanceolate‑ovate, obovate‑oblong, or oblong‑lanceolate to ovate‑oblong, 5–12 × 1.5–3.5 cm, base cuneate, apex acute or shortly acuminate, adaxially glabrous, abaxially sometimes puberulent or with cluster of hairs in axils of veins; lateral veins slender, 5–7 on each side of midvein. Flower‑heads 6–8 mm in diam., 6–12‑flowered, arranged in terminal umbels; peduncles 5–12 mm. Calyx‑tube hemispherical, 0.8–1 mm, apex truncate or obscurely toothed. Corolla white; tube short, glabrous abaxially, bearded in throat; lobes 4, narrowly oblong, 3–3.2 mm, apex obtuse and recurved. Compound berry depressed globose, 8–12 mm in diam., red when mature.

Locality: Ma On Shan, Tai Po Kau, Sai Wan Shan, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 1264; Y. W. Lam 842, 2150.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Indochina, India, Sri Lanka, Malesia, Australia.
Ecology: Thickets. Flowering: May–Aug.; fruiting: May–Jan. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Ma On Shan, Tai Po, Ng Tung Chai, Ping Shan Chai, Fanling, Pat Sin Leng, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Mussaenda erosa Champ. ex Benth. 楠藤（野白紙扇）
Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 4: 193. 1852; FHK 153. 1861; FKH 130. 1912; FRPS 71(1): 293, pl. 78: 4 – 6. 1999; FYN 14: 146, pl. 28: 1 – 5. 2003; FGD 6: 167. 2005.

Evergreen scandent shrubs, to 3 m tall. Branchlets glabrous. Stipules narrowly triangular, 7–8 mm, glabrous or strigose, deeply 2‑lobed. Leaves opposite, papery; petioles 1–1.5 cm; leaf blade oblong, ovate to ovate‑oblong, 6–12 × 3.5–5 cm, base cuneate, apex acute to long‑acuminate, initially slightly pubescent on veins of adaxial surface, sparsely appressed‑pubescent on abaxial surface, but glabrous on both surfaces in age. Corymbs terminal, large and loose, long‑pedunculate. Calyx‑tube ellipsoidal, 3–3.5 mm, glabrous; lobes linear‑lanceolate, 2–2.5 mm, sparsely covered with short hairs at the base, one of them in a few of the outer flowers enlarged, broadly elliptic, white, 4–6 × 3–4 cm, apex rounded or acute, base abruptly narrowed into a long (0.9–1 cm) petiole, glabrous. Corolla yellow, tube 1.2–1.8 cm, pubescent abaxially, densely covered with clavate hairs at throat; lobes ovate, ca. 5 mm, apex acute, with minute yellow tubercles inside. Berries subglobular to broadly ellipsoidal, 8–10 mm in diam., glabrous.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Ma On Shan, Tai Po, Ng Tung Chai, Ping Shan Chai, Fanling, Pat Sin Leng, Lantau Island. H. C. Tang 390, 558; Y. S. Lau 616.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Vietnam.
Ecology: Ravines. Flowering: Feb.–Jul.; fruiting: May–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The type specimen was collected by J. G. Champion from Happy Valley between 1847 and 1850.

Mussaenda kwangtungensis H. L. Li 廣東玉葉金花
J. Arnold Arb. 25: 427. 1944; FRPS 71(1): 302, pl. 80: 4 – 6. 1999; FGD 6: 169, fig. 85. 2005.

Evergreen scandent shrubs 1–2.5 m tall. Branchlets covered with grey short hairs. Stipules 1.5–2 mm, divided to the base; lobes linear, puberulent. Leaves opposite; petioles ca. 5 mm, densely puberulent; leaf blade elliptic‑lanceolate, 7–8 × 2–3 cm, base attenuate, apex long acuminate, both surfaces pubescent on veins, other parts sparsely puberulent or glabrescent. Corymbs terminal. Peduncle ca. 5 mm. Calyx‑tube oblong, 2–2.5 mm, puberulent; lobes linear, 3–3.5 mm, densely puberulent, one of them in a few of the outer flowers enlarged, oblong‑ovate, white, 3.5–5 × 1.5–2.5 cm, apex acute, base narrowed into a 1.5 cm long petiole, pubescent. Corolla yellow, tube ca. 4 cm, puberulent abaxially, covered with clavate hairs on the upper part inside the tube; lobes ovate, ca. 5 mm, apex acute, densely pubescent abaxially, with minute golden yellow tubercle adaxially. Style short, included; stigma bifid.

Locality: Bowen Rd. W. Y. Chun 9183 (IBSC).
Distribution: SE Guangdong.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Spring to summer.

Mussaenda pubescens W. T. Aiton 玉葉金花
Hort. Kew. ed. 2, 1: 372. 1810; FHK 153. 1861; FKH 130. 1912; H. L. Li, Woody Fl. Taiwan 863, fig. 348. 1963; FTW ed. 2, 4: 302. 1998; FRPS 71(1): 296, pl. 79: 5 – 7. 1999; FYN 14: 146. 2003; FGD 6: 168. 2005.

Evergreen scandent shrubs. Branchlets densely appressed‑pubescent. Stipules 5–7 mm, lobed to 2/3 of its length; lobes subulate. Leaves opposite or sometimes subverticillate; petioles 3–8 mm, pubescent; leaf blade oblong‑elliptic, obovate‑elliptic to ovate‑lanceolate, 5–9 × 2–3.5 cm, base cuneate, apex shortly acuminate, pubescent, but the hairs denser on abaxial surface. Cymes corymbiform, terminal. Peduncle 0–7 mm. Pedicels scarcely 1 mm. Calyx‑tube turbinate, 2–2.5 mm, pubescent; lobes subulate, 6–7 mm, one of them in a few of the outer flowers enlarged, broadly ovate or orbicular, white, 2 –4.5 × 1–3.5 cm, apex obtuse or acute, base narrowed into a 1 – 2.8 cm long petiole. Corolla salverform; tube slender, 1.2 – 1.8 cm, green, sparsely appressed‑pubescent abaxially, densely yellowish villose on throat; lobes bright yellow, oblong‑lanceolate, ca. 4 × 2 mm, spreading, with minute golden‑yellow tubercles inside. Style short, included. Berries globular, 8–10 mm in diam., sparsely pubescent.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 2143; Y. W. Lam 259; HK sheet 39950.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Thickets on roadsides and in ravines. Flowering: Apr.–Jul.; fruiting: May–Oct.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Sheung Wo Hang, Wu Kau Tang
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Nauclea officinalis (Pierre ex Pit.) Merr. & Chun 烏檀
Sunyatsenia 5: 188. 1940; FHN 3: 287, fig. 728. 1974; Ridsdale,Blumea 24(2): 328. 1978; FRPS 71(1): 260, pl. 66. 1999.

Evergreen trees, 4–12 m tall. Branchlets slender, smooth; terminal bud obovoid. Stipules obovate, 6–10 mm, apex rounded, caducous. Leaves opposite, papery; petioles 10 – 15 mm; leaf blade elliptic, rarely obovate, 7–9 × 3.5–5 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, tip ± blunt, glabrous; lateral veins slender, 5–7 on each side of midvein, slightly raised on both surfaces. Flowering head solitary, terminal. Peduncles 1–3 cm. Calyx‑tubes connate, fleshy. Corolla funnel‑shaped, 5‑lobed. Stamens 5, inserted in the upper part of the corolla‑tube. Fruiting head globular, yellowish brown when ripen, 9–15 mm in diam., composed of numerous drupelets.

Locality: Sheung Wo Hang, Wu Kau Tang. S. C. Ng 2644; Y. W. Lam 2012; F. W. Xing 8643.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi; Indochina, Thailand, Malesia.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Summer; fruiting: Apr.–Dec.
Uses: Timber, medicinal (folklore).
Notes: Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Neanotis boerhaavioides (Hance) W. H. Lewis 卷毛新耳草
Ann. Missouri Bot. Gard. 53: 37. 1966; FRPS 71: 82. 1999; FGD 6: 135. 2005.
Hedyotis boerhaavioides Hance, J. Bot. 8(88): 73. 1870.
Anotis boerhaavioides (Hance) Maxim., Bull. Acad. Imp. Sci. Saint‑Petersbourg 29: 165. 1883; FKH 128. 1912.

Annual diffuse herbs, to 6 cm or longer. Stems decumbent at base, rooting at nodes, together with petioles, abaxial surface of leaves and stipules covered with pellucid, curling long hairs. Stipules 3–6 mm, strigose, united with petioles at the base. Leaves opposite; petioles 1–5 mm; leaf blade ovate or ovate lanceolate, 1.2–4 × 0.6–2 cm, base broadly cuneate or obtuse, ± decurrent, apex acute or shortly acuminate, adaxial surface sparsely pubescent; lateral veins 4–5(–6) on each side of the midvein. Flowers white, in terminal or axillary cymes. Peduncles 2 – 20 mm sparsely pubescent or glabrescent. Pedicels 1–2 mm or almost obsolete. Calyx‑tube obovate oblate; calyx‑teeth ovate. Corolla‑tube ca. 1.5 mm, glabrous; lobes ovate oblong. Stamens slightly exserted. Ovary inferior; stigma bifid. Capsules in pairs or solitary, oblate, 2–3 mm in diam., pubescent or glabrescent.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Yuen Long. Y. W. Lam 1268; HK sheet 38588.
Distribution: Guangdong, Jiangxi, Fujian.
Ecology: Grassy hillslopes. Flowering & fruiting: Autumn to winter.

Neanotis thwaitesiana (Hance) W. H. Lewis 新耳草
Ann. Missouri Bot. Gard. 53: 40. 1966; FRPS 71: 82, pl. 17: 1 – 4. 1999; FGD 6: 136. 2005.
Anotis thwaitesiana Hance, J. Bot. 6: 298. 1868; FKH 129. 1912.

Perennial diffuse herbs, glabrous except flowers. Stems slender, 4‑angled, woody at base. Stipules pectinate, united at the base, apex with a few linear lobes. Leaves opposite, submembranous; petioles 1–5 mm; leaf blade ovate or ovate‑lanceolate, 1–1.5 × 0.5–1 cm, base obtuse or subrounded, apex acute, scabrous on both surface and margins; lateral veins inconspicuous. Flowers white or pink, in axillary cymes or paniculate, 2–many times longer than the subtending leaf. Peduncles slender, 1.5–3 cm. Pedicels slender, 3–4 mm. Calyx‑tube cup‑shaped, 2–2.5 mm; calyx‑teeth triangular ca. 2 mm. Corolla‑tube ca. 1 mm, pubescent outside; lobes oblong‑lanceolate, ca. 3 mm. Stamens exserted. Ovary inferior; stigma clavate, bifid. Capsule oblate, 2 – 3 mm in diam., crowned with calyx‑teeth.

Locality: Yi O. HK sheet 35357, 40187.
Distribution: Guangdong.
Ecology: Wastelands, grasslands. Flowering: Apr.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Ophiorrhiza cantoniensis Hance 廣州蛇根草
Ann. Sci. Nat., Bot., ser. 4, 18: 222. 1862; FKH 129. 1912; Ferguson, Not. Roy. Bot. Gard. Edinb. 32(1): 111. 1972; FRPS 71(1): 165. 1999; FGD 6: 143. 2005.

Perennial herbs or subshrubs, 30–50 cm tall. Stems prostrate at base, rooting at nodes, upper part erect; young branches and inflorescence puberulent. Leaves papery; petioles 1.5–4 cm; stipules small, caducous; leaf blade usually oblong‑elliptic, or sometimes ovate‑oblong or oblong‑lanceolate, 5–13 × 2–5.5 cm, base cuneate, rarely subrounded, apex acuminate or abruptly acuminate, glabrous, or sometimes sparsely strigillose adaxially or on both surfaces. Flowers heterostylic, in loose, many‑flowered, terminal cymes or panicles; peduncles 2–7 cm, covered with rusty or reddish hairs. Calyx‑tube turbinate, 1.3–1.5 mm, with 5 ribs; calyx‑teeth small, triangular. Corolla white or slightly pink, glabrescent or sometimes puberulent abaxially; tube 1–1.2(–1.5) cm, with a ring of white long hairs inside the slightly dilated throat; lobes 5, triangular, 3–5 mm. Capsule 3–4 mm high and 7–9 mm broad subglabrous.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island. H. C. Tang 2438; Y. S. Lau 609, 1373.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan.
Ecology: Forests of valleys and by streams. Flowering: Winter to spring; fruiting: Apr.–May.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Ophiorrhiza japonica Blume 日本蛇根草
Bijdr. Fl. Ned. Ind. 978. 1826; FKH 129. 1912; Ferguson, Not. Roy. Bot. Gard. Edinb. 32(1): 112. 1972; FTW ed. 2, 4: 308, pl. 140. 1998; FRPS 71(1): 163. 1999; FGD 6: 142. 2005.
Ophiorrhiza eryei Champ., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 4: 170. 1852; FHK 147. 1861.

Perennial herbs, 20–50 cm tall. Stems ascending, rooting at the base, with 2 lines of hairs. Leaves papery; petioles 1–2(–3) cm, glabrous or pubescent; stipules small, caducous; leaf blade ovate, elliptic‑ovate or lanceolate, 4–8(– 10) × 1–3 cm, base cuneate or obtuse, apex acuminate or shortly acuminate, glabrous, or sometimes sparsely strigillose adaxially and pubescent on veins abaxially, with a red tint in drying. Flowers heterostylic, 5 – 10, or rarely more, in loose terminal cymes; peduncles usually 1–2 cm, ± puberulous. Calyx‑tube turbinate, ca. 1.3 mm; calyx‑teeth small, triangular. Corolla white or pink, glabrous abaxially; tube 1–1.3 cm, dilated in the upper half, pubescent inside; lobes 5, triangular, 2.5–3 mm. Capsule 3–4 mm high and 7–9 mm broad subglabrous.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island. L. T. Lo 4; HK sheet 38519, 39999.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, S Shaanxi, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, N Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests of valleys. Flowering: Feb.–May.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Shing Mum, Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Ophiorrhiza pumila Champ. ex Benth. 短小蛇根草
Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 4: 169. 1852; FHK 147. 1861; FKH 129. 1912; FTW ed. 2, 4: 311. 1998; FRPS 71(1): 171. 1999; FGD 6: 144. 2005.

Small herbs, 10–25 cm tall. Stems erect or decumbent, rooting at the base, ± pubescent. Leaves papery; petioles 0.5 – 1.5 cm, pubescent; stipules small, caducous; leaf blade ovate, lanceolate, elliptic or oblong, 2–5.5(–9) × 1–2.5 cm, base cuneate, ± decurrent, apex obtuse or subrounded, glabrescent or sparsely strigillose adaxially, puberulent abaxially. Flowers homostylic, crowded in small terminal cymes; peduncles ca. 1 cm, puberulous. Calyx small, shortly and densely pubescent; tube turbinate or subglobular, ca. 1.2 mm, with 5 ribs; calyx‑teeth small, triangular. Corolla white, ca. 5 mm, puberulent abaxially; tube slightly dilated at the base, with a ring of white long hairs inside throat; lobes 5, triangular, 1.2–1.5 mm. Capsule 2–2.5 mm high and 6–7 mm broad, shortly strigose.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Shing Mum, Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 608; P. S. Choi 493; Y. W. Lam 1546.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; N Vietnam.
Ecology: Wet and shaded places in forests and by streams. Flowering: Feb.–Oct.; fruiting: May–Oct.
Notes: The type specimen was collected by J. G. Champion from Victoria Peak between 1847 and 1850.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Lantau Island, Lamma Island, Po Toi Islands, Ping Chau
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Oxyceros sinensis Lour. 雞爪簕
Fl. Cochinch. 151. 1790; Yamazaki, J. Jap. Bot. 45: 340. 1970; FRPS 71(1): 345, pl. 91; 1 – 7. 1999; FYN 15: 173, pl. 35: 1 – 4. 2003; FGD 6: 179, fig. 93. 2005.
Oxyceros sinensis Lour. ex Roem. & Schult., Syst. Veg. 5: 248. 1819.
Randia sinensis (Lour.) Schult. in Roem. & Schult., Syst. Veg. 5: 248. 1819; FHK 155. 1861; FKH 131. 1912; FTW ed. 2, 4: 319. 1998.
Fagerlindia sinensis (Lour.) Tirveng., Nordic J. Bot. 3(4): 458. 1983.

Shrubs or small trees, sometimes straggling, 1–7 m tall. Branches stout, greyish white; branchlets, petioles and inflorescence covered with tawny hairs. Thorns axillary, in pairs or solitary, 4–15 mm. Leaves papery; petioles 5 – 15 mm; stipules triangular, 3–5 mm, pubescent, apex long‑acuminate, deciduous; leaf blade ovate‑elliptic, oblong or ovate, 2–21 × 1.5–9.5 cm, base cuneate or slightly rounded, apex acute or shortly acuminate, adaxial surface glabrous, abaxial surface pubescent or only with hairs on midvein, lateral veins and in axils of veins; lateral veins 6 – 8 on each side of midvein. Flowers in rather dense terminal cymes, on very short common peduncles, 3–4.5 cm in diam. Pedicels 1–1.5 mm. Calyx‑tube cup‑shaped, 4–6 mm; lobes 5, narrowly triangular or ovate‑triangular, 1–4 mm, apex acute. Corolla white or yellow, salverform; tube slender, 12–24 mm, pubescent on the throat; lobes 5, oblong, 5–9 × 4–4.5 mm, spreading. Anthers linear‑oblong, 4 – 5.5 mm, exserted. Style 12–18 mm; stigma fusiform, 2‑lobed. Berry globose, 8–12 cm in diam., often congested into a globular cluster.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Lantau Island, Lamma Island, Po Toi Islands, Ping Chau. L. Gibbs 7551; P. S. Choi 474; HK sheet 36023.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests and thickets. Flowering: Mar.–Dec.; fruiting: May–Dec.
Uses: Environmental (barrier).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Ma On Shan, Sai Kung (Wong Chuk Yeung)
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Paederia pertomentosa Merr. ex Li 白毛雞矢藤
Journ. Arnold Arb. 24: 458. 1943; FRPS 71(2): 115. 1999; FGD 6: 226. 2005.

Shurbby or herbaceous vines, to 3 m or longer; branches, petioles and inflorescence densely tomentellous. Petioles (0.5–)1–3(–5) cm; leaf blade papery, ovate to ovate‑elliptic or oblong‑elliptic, 4–12 × 2.2–5.5 cm, base rounded, sometimes slightly decurrent, apex acuminate, adaxial surface ±olive‑green, inicially puberulous, glabrescent, abaxial surface densely whitish tomentose; lateral veins ca. 4 on each side of midvein. Inflorescences axillary or terminal, 6 – 20 cm, paniculate, with opposite or subverticillate branches of 1–3 cm apart; flowers 5‑merous, arranged in compact cymes or glomerulate at the branches. Pedicels very short. Calyx densely tomentose; lobes triangular, apex acute, glabrous adaxially. Corolla purpleish; tube 5 mm, densely puberulous abaxially; lobes ovate, 1–1.2 mm, acute. Fruits globose at maturity, 4–5 mm in diam., straw‑yellow, shiny; pyrenes semi‑globose 3–4 mm in diam., without wings.

Locality: Ma On Shan, Sai Kung (Wong Chuk Yeung). Y. S. Lau 3167; HK sheet 40893, 41515; R. K. Huang 3201 (IBSC).
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian.
Ecology: Thickets or exposed grassy hillslopes. Flowering: Jun.–Aug.; fruiting: Sep.

Paederia scandens (Lour.) Merr. 雞矢藤
Contr. Arnold Arbor. 8: 163. 1934; FHN 3: 358. 1974; FRPS 71(2): 118. 1999; FYN 15: 257, pl. 55: 8 – 11. 2003; FGD 6: 226, fig. 122. 2005.
Gentiana scandens Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 1: 171. 1790.

Perennial herbs; stems glabrous, 3–5 m or longer, woody at the base, with disagreeable odour when bruised. Leaves papery or subleathery; petioles 1.5–7 cm; stipules triangular, 3–5 mm, glabrous; leaf blade ovate, ovate‑oblong or lanceolate, 5–15 × 1–6 cm, base cuneate, rounded, truncate, or sometimes shallowly cordate, apex acute or acuminate, glabrous or nearly so; lateral veins 4–6 on each side of midvein, sometimes with turf of hairs in the axils of veins. Flowers sessile along the branches of the loose dichotomous or trichotomous cymes, forming long loose panicles. Calyx‑tube turbinate, 1–1.2 mm; lobes 5, triangular, 0.8–1 mm. Corolla pale purple; tube 7–10 mm, pulverulent outside, tomentose inside; lobes 5, suborbicular, 1–2 mm. Anthers dorsifixed; filaments unequal. Fruit globular or ovoid, 5–7 mm in diam.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 2260; Y. S. Lau 1988, 2010.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Gansu, Shanxi, Shaanxi, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Shandong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Korea, Japan, Indochina, Malesia, Indian subcontinent.
Ecology: Thickets, wastelands near villages. Flowering: Aug.–Sep.; fruiting: Sep.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Mount Davis, Tai Po Kau, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Paederia scandens (Lour.) Merr. var. tomentosa (Blume) Hand.‑Mazz. 毛雞矢藤
Symb. Sin. 7(4): 1023. 1936; FHN 3: 358. 1974; FRPS 71(2): 119. 1999; FYN 15: 258. 2003; FGD 6: 226. 2005.
Paederia tomentosa Blume, Bijdr. Fl. Ned. Ind. 968. 1826; FKH 134. 1912.

Differs from var. scandens by its hairy branches, petioles, inflorescence and abaxial surface of leaves, and by its white (not pale purple) flowers.

Locality: Mount Davis, Tai Po Kau, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 1575; P. S. Choi 100, 372.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian; Japan, India, Malesia.
Ecology: Thickets, wastelands near villages.
Flowering: Jul. – Oct.; fruiting: Sep. – Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Pavetta hongkongensis Bremek. 香港大沙葉（茜木）
Repert. Spec. Nov. Regni Veg. 37 (961 – 973): 104. 1934; FHN 3: 346, fig. 763. 1974; FRPS 71(2): 27, pl. 9: 4–8. 1999; FYN 15: 205, pl. 41: 4 – 7. 2003; FGD 6: 200. 2005.
Pavetta indica auct. non L.: FHK 157. 1861; FKH 132. 1912.

Shrubs or small trees. Branchlets glabrous. Leaves thin‑papery; petioles 1–2 cm; stipules broadly ovate‑triangular, ca. 3 mm, glabrous abaxially, white villose adaxially; leaf blade oblong to elliptic‑obovate, 8–15 × 3–6.5 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, adaxially glabrous, abaxially glabrescent or pubescent on midvein and in axils of veins; lateral veins 6–8 on each side of midven. Cymes trichotomous, 7–15 cm in diam., sessile above the last leaves. Pedicels 3–6 mm. Calyx‑tube bell‑shaped, ca. 1 mm; limb inconspicuously 4‑toothed. Corolla white, tube to 15 mm or longer, glabrous outside, sparsely pubescent near the base inside; lobes oblong, ca. 6 mm, apex acute. Style ca. 35 mm, long exserted. Berry globular, ca. 6 mm in diam.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. L. T. Lo 99, 278; K. Y. Tam 146.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Thickets and forests. Flowering: Mar.–Oct.; fruiting: Jun.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The type specimen was collected by J. G. Champion from Happy Valley between 1847 and 1850.

Pentas lanceolata (Forssk.) Deflers 五星花
Voy. Yemen 142. 1889; FGD 6: 145, fig. 65. 2005.
Pentas lanceolata (Forssk.) K. Schum., Nat. Pflanzenfam. 4(4): 29. 1891; FRPS 71(1): 175. 1999; Check List HK Plants 270. 2002; 92. 2004.

Subshrubs, to 70 cm tall. Stems and branches quadrangular, covered with white multicellular hairs when young. Leaves opposite; petioles 1.5–3 cm, pilose; stipules short and broad, apex bristly; leaf blade oblong‑lanceolate, 5 – 14 × 2–5.5 cm, base cuneate, apex acute or shortly acuminate, adaxially pubescent or scabrous, abaxially densely pubescent on the veins. Corymbs terminal; peduncles 3–12 mm, together with bracts and calyx covered with white multicellular hairs. Calyx‑tube subglobose, apex with 5–6 unequal lobes. Corolla carmine‑rose, rosy or white, salverform; tube to 2 cm, sparsely pubescent abaxially, densely covered with white long hairs in throat; limb usually 5‑lobed, ca. 1.2 cm in diam.; lobes elliptic or oblong‑lanceolate. Anthers slightly exserted or included. Style 2‑lobed, purplish black.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. Y. S. Lau 1595; S. P. Lau 89; L. T. Lo 614.
Distribution: Native to tropical Africa and Arabia; widely cultivated in tropical areas.
Ecology: Flowering: Mar. – Aug.
Uses: Ornamental.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Authority: (Merr. ex H. L. Li) Y. F. Deng & C. M. Hu
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Pertusadina metcalfii (Merr. ex H. L. Li) Y. F. Deng & C. M. Hu 海南槽裂木
Blumea 51: 559. 2006.
Pertusadina hainanensis (How) Ridsdale, Blumea 24(2): 354. 1978; FRPS 71(1): 272. 1999; FGD 6: 161. 2005.
Adina hainanensis How, Sunyatsenia 6: 240, fig. 29. 1946.
Adina affinis How, Sunyatsenia 6: 238. 1946.
Adina metcalfii Merr. ex H. L. Li, J. Arnold Arb. 24: 454. 1943.

Trees or shrubs, up to 30 m tall; branchlets glabrous or nearly so. Leaves opposite; stipules linear‑oblong to subulate, 4–6 × 2 mm, glabrous; petioles 3–10(–25) mm, glabrous or pubescent; leaf blade thick‑papery, elliptic to elliptic‑oblong, 4 – 10 × 2 – 3.5 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, glabrous or pubescent on both surfaces, with domatia in axils of lateral veins; lateral veins 7–10 on each side of midvein; reticulation of veins inconspicuous. Flowering heads axillary, ca. 15 mm in diam. across corollas; peduncle unbranched or sometimes branched like a simple dichasium. Interfloral bracteoles filiform‑clavate to filiform‑spathulate, 0.5–1 mm, ciliate at apex. Hypanthium 0.5–0.7 mm, glabrous to sparsely hairy. Calyx‑tube 1.5–2 mm, sparsely hairy; lobes linear‑oblong, 1.2–1.6 mm. Corolla hypocrateriform, 3–3.5 mm, glabrous; lobes deltoid, 0.7–1 mm. Style 7–8 mm, exserted. Fruiting heads 4– 6 mm in diam.

Locality: Lantau Peak. W. Y. Chun 10036 (IBSC).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian.
Ecology: Forests in ravines. Flowering: Jun.–Jul.
Uses: Timber.
Notes: The holotype specimen (W. Y. Chun 10036) of Adina affinis How was collected from “Phoenix Mt.” (Lantau Peak) in October 1934.

Psychotria asiatica L. 九節（山大刀）
Syst. Nat. (ed. 10), 929, 1364. 1759; A. P. Davis et al., Bot. J. Linn. Soc. 135: 35 – 42. 2001; FGD 6: 207, fig. 111. 2005.
Psychotria rubra auct. non (Lour.) Poir.: Urban Serv. Dept., Hong Kong Shrubs: 79. 1976; FRPS 71(2): 58, pl. 14: 1 – 4. 1999.
Psychotria elliptica auct. non Ker Gawl.: FHK 161. 1861; FKH 133. 1912.

Evergreen shrubs or small trees, 0.5–5 m tall. Leaves papery or subleathery; petioles 1.5–3 cm, glabrous or nearly so; stipules membranous, 3–6 × 4–8 mm, connected into a sheath within the petioles, apex obtuse, deciduous; leaf blade oblong, elliptic‑oblong or oblong‑oblanceolate, 8–15(–20) × 3–6(–9) cm, base attenuate, apex shortly acuminate, or sometimes acute with a blunt tip, margin entire, glabrous, but often with tuft of minute hairs in axils of lateral veins on abaxial surface; lateral veins 5–15 on each side of midvein. Cymes corymbiform or paniculate, terminal; usually trichotomous; primary branches 2.5–3 cm, secondary branches 1–1.5 cm; pedicels ca. 1 mm. Calyx‑tube cup‑shaped, ca. 1.5 mm; limb subtruncate or inconspicuously 5‑toothed. Corolla greenish white; tube 2 – 3 mm, with white long hairs on the throat; lobes narrowly triangular, 2.5–3 × 1.5–2 mm, erect or ± spreading, tip incurved. Drupe globose or broadly ellipsoidal, 4–7 mm in diam., with longitudinal ribs, red when mature.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 2250; Y. W. Lam 527, 830.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Hunan, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Indochina, Malesia, India.
Ecology: Thickets and forests on hillsides and by streams. Flowering: Mar.–Sep.; fruiting: Jun.–Feb. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Psychotria serpens L. 蔓九節（穿根藤）
Novit. Fl. Suec. Mant. 2: 204. 1771; FHK 161. 1861; FKH 133. 1912; FHN 3: 353. 1974; FTW ed. 2, 4: 316, photo 191 – 192. 1998; FRPS 71(2): 60, pl. 14: 10 – 14. 1999; FGD 6: 208. 2005.

Evergreen small shrubs. Stems prostrate, many‑branched, 0.5–5 m or longer, climbing on trunks or rocks by aerial roots. Leaves papery or leathery; petioles 1–10 mm, glabrous or scurfy puberulent; stipules membranous, shortly sheathing, 2–3 × 2–5 mm, apex obtuse, deciduous; leaf blade ovate, elliptic or obovate‑oblong, 0.7–9 × 0.5–3.8 cm, base cuneate, apex acute or obtuse, margin entire, glabrous; lateral veins slender, 4–10 on each side of midvein. Cymes terminal, usually trichotomous; peduncles to 3 cm; pedicels 0.5–1.5 mm. Calyx‑tube obconical, ca. 2.5 mm; limb enlarged, obtusely and minutely 5‑toothed. Corolla white; tube 1.5–3 mm, with white long hairs on the throat; lobes 5, oblong, slightly longer than the tube. Fruit a berry‑like drupe, globose or ellipsoidal, 2.5–6 mm in diam., white when mature.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 2061; K. L. Yip 4142; HK sheet 39949.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Zhejiang, Taiwan; Korea, Japan, Indochina, Thailand.
Ecology: Forests or thickets, climbing on trunks or rocks. Flowering: Apr.–Jul.; fruiting: Aug.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Mount Nicholson, Mount Kellet, Wu Kau Tang, Ma On Shan
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Psychotria tutcheri Dunn 假九節（小葉九節）
J. Bot. 48: 324. 1910; FKH 133. 1912; FHN 3: 352. 1974; FRPS 71(2): 53. 1999; FGD 6: 207. 2005.

Evergreen shrubs, 0.5–4 m tall. Leaves papery or thinly leathery; petioles 0.5–2 cm, glabrous; stipules ovate‑triangular or lanceolate, 3–5 × 2–4 mm, connected into a sheath within the petioles, apex acuminate, with 2 bristle‑like lobes, deciduous; leaf blade oblong‑lanceolate, ovate‑lanceolate, lanceolate or oblong, 5.5–22 × 2–6 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate to caudate‑acuminate, margin entire, glabrous; lateral veins slender, 4–13 on each side of midvein. Cymes corymbiform, terminal or axillary. Peduncle 0.5–3 cm; pedicels ca. 1 mm. Calyx‑tube obconical, 1.5–2.5 mm; limb enlarged, lobes 4, broadly triangular, ca. 0.5 mm. Corolla white or greenish white; tube 2–3 mm, with white long hairs on the throat; lobes 5, oblong‑lanceolate, ca. 2 × 1 mm, recurved. Drupe globose, 4–6 mm in diam., with longitudinal ribs, red when mature.

Locality: Mount Nicholson, Mount Kellet, Wu Kau Tang, Ma On Shan. P. S. Choi 387; K. L. Yip 4253; HK sheet 40907.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian.
Ecology: Thickets and forests. Flowering: Apr.–Jul.; fruiting: Jun.–Dec.
Notes: The type specimen was collected by W. J. Tutcher from Happy Valley in 1906.

Richardia scabra L. 墨苜蓿
Sp. Pl. 1: 330. 1753; FTW ed. 2, 4: 321. 1998; FRPS 71(2): 203, pl. 48: 1 – 7. 1999; FGD 6: 242, fig. 131. 2005.
Richardia brasiliensis auct. non Gomes: Z. X. Li & F. W. Xing, Guihaia 9(1): 35. 1989.

Annual herbs. Stems creeping or ascending, to 80 cm or longer, sparsely hirsute. Leaves thickly papery; petioles 5 – 10 mm; stipules united with petioles into a sheath, apex truncate, fringed with 2–5 bristle‑like lobes; leaf blade ovate, elliptic or lanceolate, 1–5 × 0.5–3.5 cm, base attenuate, apex acute, tip blunt, margin ciliate, scabrous on both surfaces. Flowers in terminal sessile heads, subtended by 1 or 2 pairs of broadly ovate bracts. Calyx 2.5–3.5 mm; tube constricted at apex; lobes usually 6, lanceolate, about the length of the tube, ciliate. Corolla white, funnel‑shaped; tube 2 – 8 mm, with a ring of white long hairs near the base inside; lobes pubescent abaxially. Ovary usually 3‑locular; style 3‑branched, the branches bilobed again; stigma capitate. Capsule oblong to obovoid, 3‑furrowed, 2–3.5 mm high, densely and minutely strigose.

Locality: Naturalized. L. T. Lo 67; Y. S. Lau 1825; Y. W. Lam 1157.
Distribution: Naturalized in Hainan, S Guangdong, Taiwan, Xisha Islands; native to tropical America.
Ecology: Wastelands. Flowering: Feb.–Oct.; fruiting: Jun.–Oct.

Rubia wallichiana Decne. 多花茜草
Recherch. Anat. & Physiol. Garance 61: 1837; FRPS 71(2): 315. 1999; FGD 6: 248. 2005.
Rubia cordifolia auct. non L.: FHN 3: 363, fig. 774. 1974.

Trailing herbs, 1–3 m or longer. Stems and branches quadrangular, ± with recurved, short prickles on the angles, glabrous or pubescent on nodes. Leaves in whorls of 4 or 6, thinly papery or membranous; petioles 1–6 cm, with recurved prickles; leaf blade lanceolate or ovate‑lanceolate, 2–7 × 0.5–2.5 cm, base cordate or subrounded, apex acuminate, adaxial surface glabrous or scabrous, abaxial surface glabrous, glaucous when dry; 5‑veined, with minute prickles on the margins and midvein. Flowers in axillary thyrses, 1 – 5 cm; peduncles quadrangular, subglabrous; pedicels slender, 3–4 mm. Calyx‑tube ovoid, shallowly 2‑lobed. Corolla purplish red, greenish yellow or white; tube very short; lobes lanceolate, 1.3–1.5 mm, apex acuminate. Fruit black, globular or didymous, each segment 3.5–4 mm in diam.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Sunset Peak. L. T. Lo 319; Y. W. Lam 436, 2182.
Distribution: Hainan, Gungdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi; India, Indonesia.
Ecology: Thickets. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Serissa japonica (Thunb.) Thunb. 六月雪
Nov. Gen. Pl. 9: 132. 1798; FRPS 71(2): 160, pl. 43. 1999; FGD 6: 228, fig. 124. 2005.
Lycium japonicum Thunb., Nova Acta Regiae Soc. Sci. Upsal. 3: 207. 1780.
Lycium foetidum L. f., Sp. Pl. Suppl. 150. 1781.
Serissa foedida (L. f.) Poir. ex Lam., Tab. Encycl. 2: 211. 1819; FKH 134. 1912.

Evergreen shrubs, 60–90 cm tall. Branches grey, glabrous. Leaves leathery, opposite and crowded on short branchlets, subsessile; stipules very short, apex with 3 bristles; leaf blade elliptic, oblong or oblanceolate, 6–22 × 3 – 8 mm, base narrowed into a very short petiole, apex acute, glabrous on both surfaces. Flowers usually solitary in axils of leaves near apex or branchlets. Calyx‑tube ca. 1.5 mm, apex 6‑lobed; lobes triangular, ca. 1 mm. Corolla white or with pink tint; tube 4–5 mm, hairy inside; limb 1–1.2 cm in diam., 5–6‑lobed, lobes oblong, apex 3‑toothed, hairy adaxially. Ovary inferior; style ca. 5 mm; stigma 2‑lobed.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. Y. S. Lau 161; S. P. Lau 93, 94.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian; Japan, Vietnam, Nepal.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr.–Oct.
Uses: Ornamental.

Serissa serissoides (DC.) Druce 白馬骨
Rep. Bot. Exch. Club 1916: 646. 1917.
Democritea serissoides DC., Prodr. 4: 540. 1830.

It differs from Serissa japonica by its thinly papery and larger leaves (1–4 × 0.3–1.5 cm), and by its calyx‑lobes, which is equal to the corolla‑tube.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 2502, 38031.
Distribution: SW, S, C & SE China. Japan (Ryukyu).
Ecology: Flowering: Summer to autumn.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental, hedges.

Spermacoce articularis L. f. 糙葉豐花草
Suppl. Pl. 119. 1781; FTW ed. 2, 4: 327, pl. 147. 1998.
Borreria articularis (L. f.) F. N. Williams, Bull. Herb. Boissier 2, 5: 956. 1905; FHN 3: 362. 1974; FRPS 71(2): 206. 1999; FYN 15: 296. 2003; Check List HK Plants 261. 2002; 90. 2004.
Spermacoce hispida L., Sp. Pl. 1: 102. 1753; FHK 163. 1861; FKH 135. 1912.
Borreria hispida K. Schum., Nat. Pflanzenfam. IV(4): 144. 1891, nom. illeg., non B. hispida Spruce ex K. Schum. (1888).

Annual diffuse herbs, 30–60 cm or longer. Stems quadrangular, roughly pubescent or hispid on ribs. Leaves papery or leathery; petioles 1–4 mm, hairy; stipules membranous, pilose; bristles pinkish, longer than the sheath; leaf blade oblong, obovate or spathulate, 1–3.5 × 0.5–2 cm, base cuneate, apex acute or obtuse, initially hairy on both surfaces, later glabrescent, margin scabrous or shortly ciliate; lateral veins 3–4 on each side of midvein, inconspicuous. Flowers sessile or nearly so, 3–6 clustered in axils of stipules. Calyx‑tube cylindric, 2–3 mm, hispid; lobes 4, linear‑lanceolate, 1–1.5 mm. Corolla pink or white, funnel‑shaped; tube 4–4.5 mm, glabrous; lobes 4, oblong, ca. 1.5 mm, with a few hairs near apex of abaxial surface. Capsule ovoid, 3–5 mm long, 2–2.5 mm in diam., hispid, crowned by the 4 calyx‑teeth, separating into 2 valves.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 2525; Y. W. Lam 1264, 1504.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Indian subcontinent, Indochina, Malesia.
Ecology: Open fields and grassy slopes. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Oct.

Spermacoce latifolia Aubl. 闊葉豐花草
Hist. Pl. Guiane 1: 55, t. 19, fig. 1. 1775; FTW ed. 2, 4: 329. 1998.
Borreria latifolia (Aubl.) K. Schum., Fl. Bras. 6(6): 61. 1888; FRPS 71(2): 207, pl. 49: 6 – 9. 1999; FGD 6: 244. 2005; Check List HK Plants 261. 2002; 90. 2004.

Annual diffuse herbs, to 70 cm or longer. Stems quadrangular, with winged ribs, roughly pubescent. Leaves papery; petioles 3–10 mm, roughly hairy; stipules membranous, roughly hairy; bristles yellowish brown, longer than the sheath; leaf blade elliptic or ovate‑oblong, 2–7.5 × 1–4 cm, base broadly cuneate, decurrent, apex acute or obtuse, sparsely hispid on both surfaces; lateral veins 5 – 6 on each side of midvein, conspicuous. Flowers sessile, several clustered in axils of stipules. Calyx‑tube cylindric, ca. 1 mm, hispid; lobes 4, ovate‑lanceolate ca. 2 mm. Corolla pale purple, or rarely white, funnel‑shaped; tube 2–2.5 mm, sparsely pubescent and with a ring of hairs at base inside; lobes 4, triangular ovate, ca. 1.5 mm, often with a few long hairs near apex. Capsule subglobose, 3–3.5 mm in diam., hairy, separating into 2 valves.

Locality: Naturalized. L. T. Lo 468; Y. W. Lam 1156.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; native to tropical America, widely spread else where in tropical and subtropical areas.
Ecology: Open fields and grassy slopes. Flowering & fruiting: May–Oct.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Shing Mun, Tai Po Kau, Sha Lo Tung
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Spermacoce mauritiana O. Gideon 二萼豐花草
Kew Bull. 37(4): 547. 1983; FTW ed. 2, 4: 329. 1998.
Borreria repens DC., Prodr. 4: 542. 1803; FHN 3: 362. 1974; FRPS 71(2): 208. 1999; Check List HK Plants 261. 2002; 90. 2004.

Annual herbs, 30–60 cm tall. Stems diffuse or decumbent, quadrangular, roughly pubescent or hispid on ribs. Leaves papery or leathery; petioles 1–4 mm, hairy; stipules membranous, pilose; bristles pinkish, longer than the sheath; leaf blade oblong, obovate or spathulate, 1–3.5 × 0.5–2 cm, base cuneate, apex acute or obtuse, initially hairy on both surfaces, later glabrescent, margin scabrous or shortly ciliate; lateral veins 3–4 on each side of midvein, inconspicuous.
