Flowers 3–6 clustered in axils of stipules, sessile. Calyx‑tube cylindric, 2–3 mm, hispid; lobes 4, linear‑lanceolate, 1–1.5 mm. Corolla pink or white, funnel‑shaped; tube 4–4.5 mm, glabrous; lobes 4, oblong, ca. 1.5 mm, with a few hairs near apex of abaxial surface. Capsule ovoid, ca. 1 mm in diam.

Locality: Shing Mun, Tai Po Kau, Sha Lo Tung. Y. S. Lau 3003; Y. W. Lam 896.
Distribution: Hainan; Java, Mauritius.
Ecology: Open fields and wastelands. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Sep.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Stanley, Tai Mo Shan, Tsuen Wan, Sai Kung, Yuen Long, Po Toi Islands, Ping Chau
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Spermacoce stricta L. f. 豐花草
Suppl. Pl. 120. 1781; FHK 162. 1861; FKH 135. 1912.
Borreria stricta (L. f.) G. Mey, Prim. Fl. Esseq. 83. 1818; FHN 3: 361, fig. 773. 1974; FRPS 71(2): 208, pl. 49: 1 – 5. 1999; FGD 6: 243, fig. 132. 2005; Check List HK Plants 261. 2002; 90. 2004.

Annual herbs, 15–60 cm tall. Stems slender, erect or spreading, quadrangular, hispid on the ribs. Leaves leathery, subsessile; stipules united, short and broad, subglabrous or hispid, with a few pink, long bristles at apex; leaf blade linear or linear‑oblong, 2.5–5 × 0.25–0.6 cm, gradually narrowed to the base, apex acuminate, roughly pubescent on both surfaces, margin revolute; lateral veins inconspicuous. Flowers sessile, in dense, axillary whorl‑like clusters. Calyx‑tube 1.5–2.5 mm, glabrous; lobes 4, linear‑lanceolate, equal to the tube. Corolla white, funnel‑shaped; tube 1.5–2.5 mm, glabrous; lobes 4, linear‑oblong, ca. 1 mm, sparsely hispid adaxially. Capsule obovate‑globular, slightly compressed, 1–1.5 mm in diam., ± pubescent, separating into 2 valves.

Locality: Stanley, Tai Mo Shan, Tsuen Wan, Sai Kung, Yuen Long, Po Toi Islands, Ping Chau. Y. W. Lam 1155, 1143; HK sheet 38739.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian; Indochina, Indian subcontinent, Malesia.
Ecology: Open fields and grassy hillslopes. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Oct.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Sha Tin, Tai Wai, Lantau Island, Lamma Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Tarenna attenuata (Voigt) Hutch. 假桂烏口樹（達侖木）
Pl. Wilson. 3(2): 411. 1916; FHN 3: 317. 1974; FRPS 71(1): 382, pl. 100: 12 – 15. 1999; FYN 15: 188, pl. 38: 5 – 7. 2003; FGD 6: 190, fig. 100. 2005.
Stylocoryna attenuata Voigt, Hort. Suburb. Calcutt. 377. 1845.
Stylocoryna webera auct. non A. Rich.: FHK 156. 1861.
Webera attenuata Hook. f., Fl. Brit. Ind. 3(7): 104. 1880; FKH 130. 1912.

Evergreen shrubs or trees, 1–8 m tall, quite glabrous. Leaves papery or thinly leathery; petioles 0.5–1.5 cm; stipules 5–8 mm, united at the base, apex acuminate; leaf blade oblong‑lanceolate, oblong‑oblanceolate, oblanceolate or obovate, 4.5–1.5 × 1.5–6 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate or abruptly and shortly acuminate, margin entire, ± shining adaxially, turning black when dry, glabrous, or sometimes with short hairs in axils of veins on abaxial surface; lateral veins slender, 5 – 10 on each side of midvein. Cymes corymbiform, trichotomous, 4–6 cm in diam., shorter than the leaves. Pedicels 2–5 mm. Calyx‑tube turbinate, ca. 2 mm; lobes triangular, ca. 0.5 mm. Corolla white or yellowish; tube 2–2.5 mm, hairy on the throat; lobes 5, oblong, ca. 5 mm. Style ca. 8 mm; stigma exserted. Berry globular, 5–7 mm in diam., purplish black when mature.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Sha Tin, Tai Wai, Lantau Island, Lamma Island. Y. S. Lau 2727; P. S. Choi 513, 532.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; Indochina, India.
Ecology: Thickets and forests. Flowering: Dec.–Jun. of the following year; fruiting: Jul.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Ma On Shan, Pik Uk, Luk Wu
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Tarenna mollissima (Hook. & Arn.) B. L. Rob. 白花苦燈籠（烏口樹）
Proc. Amer. Acad. Arts, 45(17): 405. 1910; FHN 3: 318, fig. 745. 1974; FRPS 71(1): 376, pl. 99: 6 – 10. 1999; FYN 15: 190, pl. 38: 8 – 10. 2003; FGD 6: 189. 2005.
Stylocoryna mollissima Walp., Repert. Bot. Syst. 2: 517. 1843; FHK 156. 1861.
Webera mollissima Benth. ex Hance, J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 13: 105. 1873; FKH 130. 1912.

Evergreen shrubs or small trees, 1 – 6 m tall, softly and densely pubescent in every part. Leaves papery; petioles 0.4 – 2.5 cm; stipules 5 – 8 mm, ovate‑triangular, united at the base, apex pointed; leaf blade lanceolate, oblong‑lanceolate, or ovate‑elliptic, 5 – 16( – 25) × 2 – 6( – 10) cm, base cuneate, acute or obtuse, apex acuminate or long‑acuminate, margin entire, turning black in drying; lateral veins 8 – 12 on each side of midvein. Cymes corymbiform, trichotomous. Pedicels 3 – 6 mm. Calyx‑tube ± bell‑shaped, ca. 2 mm; lobes triangular, ca. 0.5 mm. Corolla white; tube 4 – 5 mm, densely pubescent on the throat; lobes 4 or 5, oblong, about the length of the tube or slightly longer, recurved in anthesis. Style ca. 8 mm; stigma exserted. Berry globular, 5 – 7 mm in diam., pubescent, black when mature.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Ma On Shan, Pik Uk, Luk Wu. L. T. Lo 111; P. S. Choi 213; Y. W. Lam 1754.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Jiangxi, Hunan, Zhejiang, Fujian; Vietnam.
Ecology: Thickets and forests. Flowering: May – Jul.; fruiting: Jul. – Feb. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Shek O, Ma On Shan, Kei Ling Ha, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Uncaria hirsuta Havil. 毛鈎藤
J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 33; 88. 1897; FKH 125. 1912; Ridsdale, Blumea 24(1): 94. 1978; FTW ed. 2, 4: 334. 1998; FRPS 71(1): 255. 1999; FGD 6: 157, fig. 75. 2005.

Woody climbers. Young shoots terete or slightly angular, hirsute. Stipules broadly ovate, deeply bifid; lobes ovate, sometimes with long acuminate apex, adaxially glabrous, but with glandular hairs at the base, abaxially puberulent, and with scattered long hairs. Leaves opposite, leathery; petioles 3–10 mm, hairy; leaf blade ovate to elliptic, 8–12 × 5–7 cm, base obtuse, apex acuminate, adaxially somewhat scabrous with scattered hairs, abaxially sparsely to densely strigose, with hairy domatia in axils of lateral veins; lateral veins 7–10 on each side of midvein. Flowers subsessile, densely crowded in globular heads of 3–5 cm in diam. across corollas. Receptacle densely hairy. Peduncles 2.5–5 cm, unbranched, pubescent, axillary or rarely 3 together at the ends of the branches, each bearing a flower‑head. Calyx‑tube ca. 2 mm, pubescent abaxially, 5‑lobed; lobes linear‑oblong, 2–3 mm, densely hairy. Corolla‑tube white, 7–10 mm, abaxially pubescent, 5‑lobed; lobes oblong, 2–3 mm, densely hairy on abaxial surface. Style 4–6 mm, exserted. Fruiting head 4.5–5 cm in diam.; fruitlets 10–15 mm, pubescent.

Locality: Shek O, Ma On Shan, Kei Ling Ha, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 1709; N. H. Li 37; K. Y. Tam 119.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Thickets by streams or in ravines. Flowering: Mar.–Apr.
Notes: The holotype specimen (C. Ford, s.n., K) was collected by C. Ford from Lantau Island. How (1946) cited the specimen W. J. Tutcher 613 as an “isotype”, which was collected from Lantau Island in April 1896.

Uncaria homomalla Miq. 北越鈎藤
Fl. Ned. Ind. 2: 343. 1857; Ridsdale, Blumea 24(1): 95. 1978; FRPS 71(1): 258. 1999; FYN 15: 124. 2003.
Uncaria tonkinensis Havil., J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 33: 89, pl. 2, fig. 19 – 20. 1897; Pitard in Lecomte, Fl. Gen. Indo‑Chine 3: 52. 1922.

Woody climbers, 10–25 m or longer. Young shoots tetragonal, slightly rusty puberulent. Stipules triangular to narrowly triangular, 5–8 mm, 2‑lobed to middle; lobes lanceolate. Leaves opposite, papery; petioles 3–6 mm, pubescent; leaf blade elliptic, elliptic‑lanceolate or ovate‑lanceolate, 8.5–10 × 3.5–5.5 cm, base obtuse to subrounded, apex acuminate or caudate, covered with short hairs on both surfaces; lateral veins 8 – 9 on each side of midvein. Flowers greenish yellow, subsessile, densely crowded in globular heads of 2.5–2.8 cm in diam. across corollas. Peduncles 2.5–3 cm, axillary, compressed, bearing a terminal flower‑head. Calyx‑tube ca. 1.5 mm, 5‑lobed; lobes linear, ca. 1 mm, puberulent. Corolla‑tube 7.5–9 mm, puberulent outside, 5‑lobed; lobes narrowly oblong, ca. 2 mm. Stamens attached to the apex of corolla‑tube; anthers exserted. Style filiform, 10–11 mm, long exserted; stigma clavate. Fruiting head globose; fruitlets obovate, 4 × 2 mm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island (Glenealy). W. J. Tutcher 8334.
Distribution: Guangxi, Yunnan; Indochina, India subcontinent and Malesia.
Ecology: Thickets. Flowering: May–Oct.

Uncaria macrophylla Wall. 大葉鈎藤
Fl. Ind., ed. 1820, 2: 132. 1824; Hook. f., Fl. Brit. Ind. 3: 32. 1880; Pitard in Lecomte, Fl. Gen. Indo‑Chine 3: 46. 1922; C. E. Ridsdale, Blumea 24(1): 78. 1978; FRPS 71(1): 249. 1999; FYN 15: 121. 2003; FGD 6: 155, fig. 74. 2005.

Woody climbers. Young shoots square to slightly angular, slightly hairy. Stipules ovate, deeply 2‑lobed; lobes narrowly ovate, abaxially pubescent, adaxially glabrous or sparsely pubecent, with colleters at the base. Leaves opposite, subleathery; petioles 3–10 mm, glabrous or sparsely puberulous; leaf blade ovate or broadly elliptic, 10– 16 × 6–12 cm, base obtuse or cordate, apex acute or acuminate, glabrous or ± pubescent on veins of adaxial surface, sparsely to densely hairy on abaxial surface, with hairy domatia in axils of lateral veins; midvein depressed adaxially, raised abaxially; lateral veins 6 – 9 on each side of midvein. Flowers densely crowded in globular heads of 4.5 – 5 cm in diam. across corollas. Receptacle densely hairy. Peduncles 3–7 cm, axillary, unbranched, or rarely 3 together at the ends of the branches, each bearing a flowering head; pedicels 2–5 mm. Calyx‑tube funnelform, 2 – 3 mm, covered with sericeous short hairs abaxially, 5‑lobed; lobes linear oblong, 3–4 mm, finely pubescent. Corolla‑tube 9–10 mm, pubescent abaxially, 5‑lobed; lobes oblong, ca. 2 mm, pubescent abaxially. Style ca. 6 mm, long exserted. Fruiting head 8–10 cm in diam.; fruitlets ca. 2 cm, pubescent.

Locality: Lantau Island. N. H. Li 33; S. Y. Hu & P. P. H. But 24077; HK sheet 35603.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; Vietnam, Laos, Thailand, Myanmar, Bhutan, India.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Mar.; fruiting: Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Abelia chinensis R. Br. 糯米條（茶條樹）
Narr. Journey China 376. 1818; FKH 122. 1912; FRPS 72: 117. 1988; FGD 4: 292, fig. 174. 2000.

Deciduous shrubs, 0.6–1 m tall. Young branchlets red‑brown, pubescent. Leaves opposite, rarely 3‑whorled, ovate to elliptic‑ovate, 2–5 × 1–3.5 cm, base rounded or cordate, apex acute or acuminate, margin sparsely crenate, veins densely white villose abaxially. Cymes on upper branchlets, axillary, paniculate. Flowers fragrant. Bracteoles 6, ca. 2 mm. Calyx‑tube cylindric, ca. 6 mm, pubescent; lobes 5, orbicular‑ovate. Stamens inserted at base of corolla‑tube. Achenes cylindric, 3–4 mm, crowned by persistent calyx.

Locality: Stanley, Lantau Island. HK sheet 13287, 24848, 40562.
Distribution: Areas S of Changjiang.
Ecology: Thickets. Flowering: Jul.–Oct.
Uses: Ornamental.

Lonicera confusa (Sweet) DC. 華南忍冬（山銀花）
Prodr. 4: 333. 1830; FKH 122. 1912; FRPS 72: 238, pl. 62: 5 – 6, 1988; FGD 4: 309, fig. 179. 2000.
Nintooa confusa Sweet, Hort. Brit. ed. 2, 258. 1830.
Lonicera multiflora Champ. ex Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 4: 167. 1852; FHK 144. 1861.

Semi‑evergreen climbers; young branchlets, petioles and peduncles densely grey‑yellow pubescent, with crisped hairs. Leaves papery; petioles 5–8 mm; leaf blade ovate or ovate‑oblong, 3–6 × 2–4 cm, base rounded, truncate or cordate, apex acute, margin ciliate, sometimes mucronate, densely pubescent abaxially; lateral veins 3–4 on each sides of midvein. Flower‑pairs axillary on branchlet top, or in short racemes with distinct involucrate bracts. Bracts lanceolate, 1–2 mm. Calyx 2.5–3 mm. Corolla white, becoming yellow when dry, 3.2 – 5 cm; limb slightly shorter than tube. Stamens and styles exserted. Berry black, elliptic or subglobular, 6–10 mm in length.

Locality: New Territories, Lantau Island. U. A. On 140; HK sheet 13346, 13348.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi; Vietnam, Nepal.
Ecology: Thickets on hillslopes. Flowering: Jul.–Aug.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Lonicera japonica Thunb. 忍冬（金銀花）
Syst. Veg. 14: 216. 1784; FKH 122. 1912; FRPS 72: 236, pl. 62: 1 – 4. 1988; FGD 4: 306, fig. 178. 2000.

Semi‑evergreen climbers; branchlets densely tawny hirsute, with spreading hairs and mixed with glandular hairs. Leaves papery; petioles 4–8 mm; leaf blade ovate to elliptic‑ovate, rarely obovate or ovate‑lanceolate, base rounded or broad‑cuneate, rarely subcordate, apex acute or obtuse, margin ciliate, glabrous or pubescent on both surfaces; lateral veins 3 – 5 on each side of midvein. Flowers paired, axillary on upper part of branchlets, often in racemose‑cymes. Peduncles 2 – 4 cm. Bracts leaf‑like, 2–3 cm. Calyx tube ca. 2 mm, glabrous, teeth ovate‑deltoid or long deltoid. Corolla white, becoming yellow, 2‑labiate, 3–4.5 cm, hirsute and glandular hairy, labium linear, reflexed. Stamens and styles exserted. Berry blue‑black, globular, 6–7 mm in diam., shining.

Locality: Tai Tam. Y. S. Lau 971; HK sheet 2243, 13394.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China except Heilongjiang, Nei Mongol, Qinghai, Xinjiang, Xizang and Hainan; Japan, Korea.
Ecology: Thickets, margins of forests. Flowering: Apr.–May.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Hung Mui Kuk, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Lonicera longiflora (Lindl.) DC. 長花忍冬
Prodr. 4: 331. 1830; FHK 143. 1861; FKH 122. 1912; FRPS 72: 242, pl. 66: 1 – 2. 1988; FGD 4: 308. 2000.

Climbers; branchlets glabrous or sometimes slightly yellow‑brown hirsute. Leaves leathery; petioles 5 – 8 mm; leaf blades oblong or oblong‑lanceolate, rarely ovate, 5–8 × 2–4 cm, base rounded or broad‑cuneate, apex acuminate, margin slightly revolute, glabrous on both surfaces; lateral veins 3–5 on each side of midvein, very obliquely ascending, net‑veins prominent abaxially. Flower‑pairs axillary or forming loose terminal heads or short racemes. Peduncles 5 – 8 mm. Bracts linear‑lanceolate, 2–2.5 mm. Calyx‑tube subobconic, ca. 2.5 mm, subglabrous, teeth deltoid‑lanceolate, ca. 1.5 mm. Corolla white, gradually becoming yellow, 2‑labiate, 5–10 cm; tube 2.5–4 cm, labium, rolled back at top, lower lip linear, upper lip 4‑toothed. Stamens and pistil exserted. Berry white.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Hung Mui Kuk, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 1167, 1247, 3205.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Yunnan.
Ecology: Thickets. Flowering: Apr. – Jun.; fruiting: Aug.–Oct.

Lonicera macrantha (D. Don) Spreng. 大花忍冬
Syst. Veg. 4(2): 82. 1827; FHK 143. 1861; FKH 122. 1912; FRPS 72: 240, pl. 63: 1 – 5. 1988; FGD 4: 308. 2000.

Semi‑evergreen climbers; young branchlets thickly pubescent and hirsute with spreading hairs and sometimes mixed with glandular hairs. Leaves papery or leathery; petioles 3–10 mm; leaf blade ovate‑elliptic or ovate‑lanceolate, 5 – 12 × 2 – 7 cm, base rounded or slightly cordate, apex acuminate, margin ciliate, slightly revolute, hirsute and red glandular hairy on abaxial surface; lateral veins 4–5 on each side of midvein. Flower‑pairs in axillary, corymbiform, clusters on upper parts of branchlets. Bracts lanceolate or linear, 2–5 mm. Calyx 3–4 mm. Corolla white or yellowish, fragrant, pubescent, 4.5–7(–10) cm; tube 3–5 cm; limb 2‑labiate, lower labium reflexed, upper lip long ovate. Stamens and style slightly exserted. Berry black, globular or ellipsoidal, 8–12 mm in length.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. P. S. Choi 505; K. Y. Tam 138; K. L. Yip 4104.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; Nepal, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Vietnam.
Ecology: Thin forests, thickets in ravines. Flowering: Mar.–Apr.; fruiting: May–Jul.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Tam, Magazine Gap, Victoria Peak, Ma On Shan
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Lonicera rhytidophylla Hand.‑Mazz. 皺葉忍冬（顯脈忍冬）
Symb. Sin. 7(4): 1049, pl. 16, fig. 8. 1936; FRPS 72: 246, pl. 67: 3 – 6. 1988; FGD 4: 309, fig. 180. 2000.
Lonicera reticulata Champ., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 4: 167. 1852. non Rafin. 1838; FHK 144. 1861; FKH 122. 1912.

Evergreen climbers; branchlets and inflorescence densely covered with a short soft velvety tomentum. Leaves leathery; petioles 8–15 mm; leaf blade broad‑elliptic, ovate, ovate‑oblong to oblong, 3 –10 × 1–4 cm, base rounded or broad‑cuneate, rarely truncate, apex obtuse and mucronate, margin entire, adaxially glabrous and shining, and winkled with a network of impressed veins, abaxially covered with a white or yellowish or white dense tomentum; lateral veins 4–5 on each side of midvein. Flower‑pairs 6 or 8 together in heads or short cymes, axillary or terminal. Bracts linear‑lanceolate, 2–3 mm, hairy. Calyx‑tube ca. 2 mm, calyx teeth subulate, 1–2 mm. Corolla white, then becoming yellow, 2‑labiate, 2.5–3.5 cm, densely hirsute and glandular hairy, lower lip reflexed, upper lip erect. Stamens and styles exserted. Fruit ellipsoidal, blue‑black when mature, 7 – 8 × 4–5 mm.

Locality: Tai Tam, Magazine Gap, Victoria Peak, Ma On Shan. H. C. Tang 998; L. T. Lo 469; HK sheet 36043.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian.
Ecology: Thickets and forests. Flowering: Apr.–Jul.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The type specimen was collected by J. G. Champion from Hong Kong Island between 1847 and 1850.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Shouson Hill, Bowen Rd., Sai Kung (Tai Long), Wu Kau Tang, Sha Tau Kok, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Sambucus chinensis Lindl. 接骨草
Trans. Hort. Soc. Lond. 6: 297. 1826; FRPS 72: 6, pl. 1: 3 – 5. 1988; FGD 4: 291, fig. 173.
Sambucus javanica auct. non Reinw. ex Blume: FKH 121. 1912.

Perennial herbs, 1–2 m tall. Stems striate; pith white. Stipules becoming glands or leaf‑like. Leaves imparipinnate; petioles 3–5 cm; leaflets opposite, 3–9, elliptic‑lanceolate, 8–15 × 2–3 cm, base cuneate or suborbicular, apex acuminate, margin serrulate, slightly asymmetric, glabrous or lepidoid hairy only on midvein, with glands on teeth near base. Compound umbel large, 10–30 cm in diam. Peduncles with leaf‑like involucrate bract. Flowers many, white, sometimes with cup‑like sterile flowers. Calyx‑tube campanulate, 1.5 mm; lobes deltoid, shorter than the tube. Corolla‑tube short; lobes ovate, ca. 2.5 mm. Stamens as long as corolla. Anthers yellow or purple. Ovary 3‑locular, styles very short; stigma 3‑fid. Drupes red, subglobose, 3–4 mm in diam., pyrenes ovate, ca. 2.5 mm.

Locality: Shouson Hill, Bowen Rd., Sai Kung (Tai Long), Wu Kau Tang, Sha Tau Kok, Lantau Island. W. J. Tutcher 9611; Y. S. Lau 2003, 2293.
Distribution: Areas of Qinling Range, westward to Gansu, S Qinghai and Xizang.
Ecology: Brick rubbish and ruins, streamsides, margins of forests. Flowering: May.–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Fanling, Sha Lo Tung, Pat Sin Leng, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Viburnum hanceanum Maxim. 蝶花莢蒾
Bull. Acad. Imp. Sci. Saint‑Petersbourg, Sér. 3, 26 (Mel. Biol. 10: 662): 487. 1880.; FKH 121. 1912; FRPS 72: 63. 1988; FGD 4: 295. 2000.

Deciduous shrubs, up to 2 m tall. Branchlets hairy or not. Leaves opposite; petioles 5–15 mm; leaf blade ovate or elliptic, 4–8 × 2.5–5.5 cm, base rounded or broad‑cuneate, apex rounded and mucronate, margin dentate, stellate hairy on both surfaces; lateral veins 5–7 on each side of midvein, running direct into teeth, veinlets parallel. Inflorescence an umbel‑like cymes, 5–7 cm in diam. Marginal sterile flowers 5–6; corolla white, 2–3 cm in diam. Corolla of fertile flowers 3 mm in diam.; lobes ovate, ca. 1.5 mm. Stamens as long as corolla. Drupes red, ovoid, ca. 5 mm, slightly compressed.

Locality: Fanling, Sha Lo Tung, Pat Sin Leng, Lantau Island. K. Barretto 305; Y. W. Lam 202; F. W. Xing 8829.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian.
Ecology: Thickets in ravines. Flowering: Mar.–Apr.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: This species was reported as Viburnum fordiae Hance previous (FKH 121. 1912; Check List HK Plants 36. 1993). Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Viburnum luzonicum Rolfe 呂宋莢蒾
J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 21: 310. 1884; FRPS 72: 94, pl. 20: 1 – 4. 1988; FTW ed. 2, 4: 756, photo 383. 1998; FGD 4: 301. 2000.

Deciduous shrubs, 2–3 m tall. Young branchlets, winter buds, petioles and inflorescence yellow‑brown stellate‑pubescent; branchlets of previous year dark purple‑brown, sparsely stellate‑pubescent. Leaves papery; petioles 4–10 mm; leaf blade ovate, elliptic‑ovate, or ovate‑lanceolate to oblong, sometimes subrhombic, 5–9 × 1.5–5 cm, base broadly cuneate to subrounded, apex acute to acuminate, margin serrate, abaxially sparsely stellate‑pubescent, adaxially with transparent glandular dots and fork‑like pubescent on midvein; lateral veins (5–)7–9 on each side of midvein, impressed adaxially, together with midvein prominent abaxially, ending in marginal teeth. Inflorescences a compound umbel‑like cyme, 3–5 cm in diam., usually terminal on branchlets or short lateral branchlets subtended by a pair of leaves; peduncle usually very short or nearly absent, very rarely to 1.5 cm, with 5 rays. Flowers small, on rays of 3rd and 4th orders. Calyx‑tube ovate‑orbicular, ca. 1 mm. Corolla white, rotate, 4– 5 mm in diam., outside stellate‑pubescent; lobes ovate, longer than the tube. Stamens shorter or slightly longer than corolla. Stigmas indistinctly 3‑lobed. Fruit red when mature, ovoid, 5–6 mm.

Locality: Lantau Peak. HK sheet 35751, 40326.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, SE Jiangxi, S Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Indochina, Philippines to Malaysia.
Ecology: Thickets on hillslopes. Flowering: Apr.–May.
Notes: This species is distinguished from Viburnum fordiae Hance by its leaves with hyaline, sessile small glands adaxially and the very short or absent peduncles, whereas leaves of V. fordiae are eglandular adaxially and the peduncles are up to 4 cm long.

Viburnum odoratissimum Ker Gawl. 珊瑚樹
Bot. Reg. 6: t. 456. 1820; FHK 143. 1861; FKH 122. 1912; FRPS 72: 56, pl. 12: 1 – 5.1988; FTW ed. 2, 4: 756, photo 384 – 385. 1998; FGD 4: 296. 2000.

Evergreen shrubs or small trees, 2–10(–15) m tall. Branchlets glabrous or slightly pubescent, with small, verrucose lenticels. Leaves opposite; petioles 1–2 cm; leaf blade elliptic, elliptic‑oblong or obovate, rarely suborbicular, 7–20 × 3.5–8 cm, base cuneate or broad‑cuneate, apex acute or acuminate, margin sparsely and shallowly sinuate or subentire, glabrous on both surfaces, or abaxially pubescent in axils of veins, sometimes sparsely dotted with dark‑red small glands; lateral veins 5–6 on each side of midvein; veins anastomosing near margin. Panicles terminal, ovoid or pyramidal, 6–14 cm. Flowers fragrant. Calyx‑tube campanulate, 2–2.5 mm, teeth deltoid. Corolla white or yellowish, rotate; tube ca. 2 mm; lobes ovate‑orbicular, 2–3 mm, reflexed. Stamens exserted; styles short, stigma capitate. Drupes red to black, ovoid, 8–5 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 1237; L. T. Lo 8; HK sheet 39426.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Fujian, Taiwan; Philippines, Indochina, Myanmar, Thailand, India.
Ecology: Flowering: Mar.–Apr.; fruiting: May–Sep.
Uses: Ornamental.

Viburnum sempervirens K. Koch 常綠莢蒾（堅莢樹）
Hort. Dendr. 300. 1853; FKH 121. 1912; FRPS 72: 74. 1988; FGD 4: 298. 2000.
Viburnum venulosum Benth., FHK 142. 1861.

Evergreen shrubs, 2–4 m tall. Branchlets purple or grey‑brown. Leaves opposite, leathery; petioles tinged with red‑purple colour, 5–15 mm; leaf blade elliptic to elliptic‑ovate, rarely oblong or oblanceolate, 4–12 × 2.5–5 cm, base narrowly cuneate to obtuse, apex acute or shortly acuminate, margin entire or slightly toothed towards end, shining adaxially, with small, brown glands on abaxial surface; lateral veins 3–4(–5) on each side of midvein, anastomosing at margin or running directly into teeth. Cymes arranged into compound umbel, terminal. Calyx‑tube ca. 1 mm. Corolla white, rotate, ca. 4 mm in diam.; lobes suborbicular. Stamens slightly exserted. Drupes red, subglobular or ovoid, 8 × 3–5 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 2404; P. S. Choi 451; Y. W. Lam 1747.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Jiangxi.
Ecology: Forests in ravines. Flowering: Apr. – May; fruiting: Aug.–Nov.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Aberdeen, Clear Water Bay, Nam Shan, Tai Mo Shan, Shing Mun Reservoir, Ta Tit Yan
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Adenostemma lavenia (L.) Kuntze 下田菊
Rev. Gen. Pl. 304. 1891; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 18(1 – 2): 92. 1965; FRPS 74: 50. 1985; FTW ed. 2, 4: 816. 1998; FGD 8: 217, fig. 129. 2007.
Adenostemma viscosum Forst., Char. Gen. Pl. 45, t. 45. 1775; FHK 171. 1861; FKH 139. 1912.
Verbesina lavenia L., Sp. Pl. 902. 1753.

Annual herbs, 40–100 cm tall. Stems erect, branched on upper portion, lower part nearly glabrous, puberulent upward. Basal leaves withered or remained at anthesis, smaller in size; middle leaves ovate, 4–9 × 2.5–4.5 cm, base cuneate‑attenuate, forming petiole 0.5–4 cm long with narrow wing, apex obtuse or acute, leaf margin crenate‑serrate, subglabrous on both surfaces, sparsely puberulent along the midvein; upper leaves smaller in size, 0.5–2 cm. Capitula in loose terminal corymbs; peduncles 1–4 cm, densely pubescent, hair multicellular. Involucres hemispherical, 5–8 mm across, or up to 10 mm at fruiting stage; phyllaries 2‑seriate, 4–5 × 1 mm, oblong, apex rounded, greenish, outer series connate at base. Florets all tubular, pinkish to maroon, 2–2.5 mm, broader at upper region, with 5 deltoid lobes at apex, glandular pilose especially at lower region; style white, branches clavate, prominently exserted; anther included, base obtuse, without apical appendages. Cypselae chestnut brown, 3–4 × 1 mm, oblanceolate, truncate distal end, glandular. Pappus 3–4 clavate projections, end up with sticky glands, base connate into a ring.

Locality: Aberdeen, Clear Water Bay, Nam Shan, Tai Mo Shan, Shing Mun Reservoir, Ta Tit Yan. C. P. Lau 032 (CUHK); S. Y. Hu & P. P. H. But 21201A (CUHK); Y. S. Lau 781.
Distribution: S to C China; SE Asia, Japan, India, Sri Lanka, Australia.
Ecology: Banks of paddy fields and wastelands. Flowering: Sep.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Naturalized and widely distributed in Hong Kong
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Ageratum conyzoides L. 藿香薊
Sp. Pl. 839. 1753; FHK 171. 1861; FKH 139. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 18(1–2): 93. 1965; FRPS 74: 53. 1985; FTW ed. 2, 4: 820. 1998; FGD 8: 217, fig. 128. 2007.

Erect aromatic herbs 8–80 cm tall, with or without branches, pubescent throughout the vegetative organs, with multicellular straight trichomes. Leaves opposite, ovate or elliptic, base usually cuneate or sometimes rounded, apex acute, margin crenulate‑dentate, trinerved or some inconspicuously 5‑veined, usually with yellow glands on abaxial surface; middle leaves 2–8 cm × 1–6 cm, with petiole 0.5–4 cm; upper and lower leaves smaller in size. Capitula in dense terminal corymbs. Involucres campanulate; phyllaries 2‑seriate, subequal, 3–4 mm, broad, oblong or lanceolate‑oblong, glabrous or occasionally with few hair, apex acute or acuminate, shallowly serrulate, not entire. Receptacle dome‑shaped, smoothed and pitted, with persistent phyllaries after fruit dispersal. Florets tubular, white, blue or violet, corolla 1.5–2.5 mm, 5‑lobed, slightly pilose on upper portion; stylar branches 1.5–2 mm, apical part glistering densely papillose. Cypselae brownish black, linear‑oblong, 1.5–1.8 mm, 5‑angulate, pilose. Pappus 5, scarious and awned, 2–2.5 mm, equal or longer than the corolla.

Locality: Naturalized and widely distributed in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1935, 2196; S. Y. Hu 5296 (CUHK).
Distribution: Native to C & S America, widely cultivated and naturalized.
Ecology: Flowering: Jun.–Oct.
Uses: Ornamental.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Naturalized and widely distributed in Hong Kong
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Ageratum houstonianum Mill. 熊耳草
Gard. Dict. ed. 8. 1768; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 18(1 – 2): 94. 1965; FRPS 74: 51. 1985; FTW ed. 2, 4: 820. 1998; FGD 8: 216. 2007.

Erect annual herbs 30–100 cm tall, with or without branches, pubescent throughout the vegetative organ. Leaves opposite, deltoid‑cordate, base cordate or sometimes truncate, apex acute or rounded, margin crenate‑dentate, pilose on both sides, trinervous or inconspicuously 5‑veined; mid‑cauline ones 2–6 × 1.5–3 cm, with petiole 0.7– 3 cm; upper and lower ones smaller. Capitula in corymbose form; peduncles densely villose. Involucres campanulate to hemispherical, 5–6 mm across; phyllaries 2–3‑seriate, narrowly lanceolate, 4–5 mm, densely hairy and glandular, apex long‑acuminate, entire. Receptacle dome‑shaped, with persistent phyllaries after fruit dispersal. Florets tubular, corolla 2–3.2 mm, shortly 5‑lobed, white to light‑violet, apex hairy; stylar branches violet, 1.5–2 mm. Cypselae black, 1.5–2 mm, 5‑angulate. Pappus 5, scarious and awned, 1.2–1.5 mm, shorter than corolla.

Locality: Naturalized and widely distributed in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1937; H. C. Tang 1233; L. T. Lo 89.
Distribution: Native to Mexico, widely naturalized in tropical and subtropical regions.
Ecology: Nature trail, farmlands and wastelands. Flowering: Nearly all year round.

Ainsliaea fragrans Champ. 杏葉兔兒風
Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 4: 236. 1852; FHK 192. 1861; FKH 149. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 18(1 – 2): 95. 1965; FRPS 79: 31. 1996; FTW ed. 2, 4: 822. 1998; FGD 8: 241. 2007.

Perennial herbs; stem erect, scapose and simple, 15–40 cm tall, brownish pubescent to pilose. Leaves 4–6 crowded at base or in the lower part of stem in subverticillate form, ovate to ovate‑oblong, 2–11 × 1.5–6 cm, base conspicuously cordate, apex obtuse to rounded and usually mucronulate, margin curved‑mucronulate, upper surfaces green, glabrous or loosely hairy, lower surfaces pale green or somewhat purple‑red, pilose, hair denser along veins and margins; petiole 2–7 cm, not winged, densely pilose. Capitula with 3 florets each, sessile or with short peduncle 1–2(–9) mm, arranged as spike or raceme; inflorescence axis brownish pubescent to pilose, bearing few subulate bracteoles 1–2 mm. Involucres narrow cylindric‑tubular, 8–10 × 3–4 mm; phyllaries about 5–7‑seriate, glabrous, sometimes tinged purplish red, apex acute; outer layers ovate, 1.2–2.2 × 0.5–1.3 mm; median layers ovate‑elliptic, 3–5 × 1.5–2 mm; inner ones linear‑oblong, 5.5–9 × 2–2.5 mm, margin scarious. Receptacle small, naked. All florets bisexual and fertile, colour white, aromatic, corolla tubular, 7 – 9 mm, upper limb deeply and obliquely cleft into 5 linear segments of 3–5 mm; anther bases sagittate and caudate, apical appendages oblong‑truncate; stylar branches short, 0.5 mm, obtuse apically. Cypselae brown, oblanceolate‑oblong, slightly compressed, 4–5 × 0.8–1 mm, ribbed, villous especially on the apical portion. Pappus pale brown, equal, plumose, 8–10 mm, base connate.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1573; C. P. Lau 083 (CUHK); S. Y. Hu 9118 (CUHK).
Distribution: Guangdong, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian; Japan.
Ecology: Thickets, grasslands. Flowering: Nov.–Feb. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Ainsliaea macroclinidioides Hayata 燈臺兔兒風
J. Coll. Sci. Tokyo 25(19): 141, pl. 22. 1908; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 18(1 – 2): 97. 1965; FRPS 79: 59. 1996; FTW ed. 2, 4: 824. 1998; FGD 8: 244. 2007.

Perennial herbs; stem erect or sometimes decumbent, simple, 25–40 cm tall, densely pilose or glabrescent later. Leaves crowded at the stem middle part or above, in rosette or verticillate form, sometimes with few leaves scattered below, ovate to ovate‑lanceolate, 2–6 × 1.5–4 cm, base truncate or faintly cordate, apex obtuse or acute, and usually mucronulate, margin entire and curved‑mucronulate, adaxial surface green, glabrous or villous, abaxial surface pale green, loosely or densely villous, much hair growing along veins and margins; petioles 1–6.5 cm, pilose. Capitula with 3 florets each, sessile or shortly pedunculate, arranged as spike or raceme, sometimes with few clustered at apical portion; inflorescence axis glabrous or loosely hairy, bearing few bracteoles. Involucres narrow cylindric‑tubular, 3–4 mm across; phyllaries 6–7‑seriate, purplish green, longitudinally veined abaxially, glabrous or slightly hairy near apices of those in the inner series; outer phyllaries ovate, 1.2–3 × 0.8–2 mm, obtuse; middle ones ovate‑oblong, 4–6 × 2–2.2 mm, obtuse; inner ones lanceolate‑oblong, 8 – 10 × 1.5 mm, acute. Receptacle plain, naked. All florets hermaphrodite and fertile, corolla white, tubular, 10 – 13 mm, upper limb deeply and obliquely 5‑cleft, lobes linear, 4–6 mm; anther bases sagittate and caudate, apical appendages oblong‑truncate; stylar branches divergent, less than 1 mm, rather flat, obtuse at apices. Cypselae brown, subcylindric, base narrowed, about 2–3 mm, ribbed, hairy. Pappus in 1 row, 6–7 mm, pale brown, plumose, base connate.

Locality: Ma On Shan, Sunset Peak. S. Y. Hu 11275 (CUHK); C. P. Lau 060 (CUHK); L. T. Lo 327.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Anhui, Fujian, Zhejiang, Taiwan.
Ecology: Thin forests, grassy hillslopes. Flowering: Aug.–Dec.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Tam, Bride's Pool, Luk Keng
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Ainsliaea walkeri Hook. f. 華南兔兒風
Bot. Mag. 102: t. 6225. 1876; FKH 149. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 18(1–2): 102. 1965; FRPS 79: 66. 1996; FGD 8: 245. 2007.

Perennial herbs; stem erect, simple, 15–40 cm high, loosely pubescent on apical part. Leaves crowded on middle portion of stem, sometimes with few scattered below, leaf blade oblong to linear, 3–8 × 0.3–0.7 cm, base gradually narrowed down, apex abruptly acute, margin of leaf apical half with 1–3 mucro growing along each side, upper surfaces green, lower surfaces pale green, glabrous above and below, midvein prominent on both sides; petioles 0.3–2 cm long, glabrous, base slightly broaden. Capitula with 3 florets each, bearing short peduncles of 2–11 mm, arranged as raceme to narrow panicle at terminal; inflorescence axis with few subulate bracteoles. Involucres narrow cylindric‑tubular, 9–11 × 2.5–3 mm; phyllaries 5‑seriate, glabrous or subglabrous, tinged purple‑red at apex and along margin; outer phyllaries ovate, 1–2.5 × 0.5–1 mm, shortly acuminate; median ones ovate‑lanceolate to lanceolate, 3–7 × 1.2–1.8 mm, acuminate or acute, margin thinly scarious; inner ones lanceolate to lanceolate‑oblong, 8–11 × 1.5–2 mm, acute, margin broadly scarious. Receptacle small, naked. All florets hermaphrodite and fertile, corolla white, ca. 1 cm, upper limb deeply and obliquely cleft into 5 linear segments; anther bases sagittate and caudate, apical appendages obtuse‑rounded to truncate; stylar branches divergent, short, less than 0.5 mm, flat, apices obtuse‑rounded. Cypselae brown, oblanceolate‑oblong, 4–6 × 0.6–1 mm, compressed, ribbed, densely villous. Pappus plumose, 6–6.5 mm, base connate.

Locality: Tai Tam, Bride's Pool, Luk Keng. P. S. Choi 229; Y. S. Lau 2636; S. Y. Hu 6565 (CUHK).
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian.
Ecology: Forests of valleys. Flowering: Oct.–Feb. of the following year.
Notes: The type specimen was derived from cultivated plants raised from seed collected by Captain Walker from Hong Kong Island before 1873.

Anisopappus chinensis (L.) Hook. & Arn. 山黃菊
Bot. Beech. Voy. 196. 1836; FHK 180. 1861; FKH 144. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 18(1 – 2): 116. 1965; FRPS 75: 317. 1979; FGD 8: 151, fig. 84. 2007.
Verbesina chinensis L., Sp. Pl. 901. 1753.

Annual herbs; stem erect, 25–110 cm tall, striate, glandular, pubescent with hair multicellular, lower portion less hairy or subglabrous, base woody. Leaves on lower part withered at anthesis; those on middle part lanceolate to lanceolate‑oblong, 3–5 × 0.7–2 cm, both surfaces pubescent and glandular, denser beneath, base broadly cuneate or truncate, apex obtuse‑rounded, margin irregularly dentate with the teeth obtuse, trinerved or triplinerved, with reticulate veinlets, prominent on lower leaf surfaces; petiole 0.5–2.5 cm. Upper leaves smaller in size and shorter‑petiolate. Capitula terminal to main stem or branches, several arranged as loose corymbs; peduncle 4–7 cm, densely pubescent. Involucres hemispherical, 6–9 mm; phyllaries 3‑seriate, lanceolate to linear‑oblong, 3–6 mm with outer ones shorter, densely pubescent and glandular on abaxial surfaces. Receptacle slightly convex, the center of areoles elevated; palea carinate, about 5 mm, enveloped the cypselae of disk florets, deciduous. Marginal ligulate florets female, corolla yellow, 6 mm, apex truncate and 3‑toothed, glandular. Disk tubular florets bisexual, corolla tubular‑campanulate, 3–3.5 mm, apex 5 ovate and glandular lobes. Cypselae subcylindric, loosely puberulent, truncate apically, narrowed at base; those of ligulate florets 2 mm, about 10‑striate‑costate; the disk ones 2.5 mm, 4–5‑angulate. Pappus scarious, coroniform and 2–3 mm together with 4–5 bristles of 0.5–1 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. P. S. Choi 383; S. Y. Hu 12405 (CUHK); N. H. Li 245 (CUHK).
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian.
Ecology: Margins of forests, wastelands. Flowering: Aug.–Nov.

Artemisia annua L. 黃花蒿
Sp. Pl. 1: 847. 1753; FHK 187. 1861; FKH 147. 1912; FRPS 76(2): 62. 1991; FTW ed. 2, 4: 834, pl. 386. 1998; FGD 8: 204, fig. 122. 2007.

Annual herbs, strongly aromatic; stem 70–150(–200) cm tall, branched above, initially puberulous, glabrescent. Lowermost cauline leaves ovate to triangular‑ovate in outline, 3–7 × 2–6 cm, 3(–4)‑pinnately parted, segments 5–8(–10) pairs, ultimate lobes deeply serrate, teeth triangular, 1–2 × 0.5 mm, Median cauline leaves 2(– 3)‑pinnately and pectinately parted; petiole 1–2 cm. Upper leaves 1(–2)‑pinnately parted. Capitula globose, numerous, 1.5–2.5 mm in diam., shortly pedunculate and with leafy bracts, arranged as pyramid‑shaped paniculate inflorescences. Involucres with 3–4 series of phyllaries, with green midvein, margin broadly scarious; outer layer oblong‑ovate to narrowly elliptic; middle and inner layers broadly ovate to ovate. Receptacle small, convex. Marginal pistillate florets 10–18, corolla filiform‑tubular, apex minutely 2–3‑lobed, glandular abaxially; style much longer than the corolla tube and conspicuously exserted, bifid. Disk bisexual florets 10–30, corolla tubular; anther linear, apical appendages elongate‑triangular; style slightly longer than the corolla. Cypselae small, ellipsoidal‑ovoid, slightly compressed. Pappus none.

Locality: New Territories. HK sheet 2668.
Distribution: Widely spread over Eurasia, from E Europe to Caucasus, Asia Minor, E Siberia and China, and widely naturalized.
Ecology: Cultivated lands, wastelands. Flowering: Aug.–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Sai Kung, Port Island, Tai A Chau, Ping Chau
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Artemisia capillaris Thunb. 茵陳蒿
Fl. Jap. 309. 1784; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 18(1 – 2): 126. 1965; FRPS 76(2): 216. 1991; FTW ed. 2, 4: 837. 1998; FGD 8: 209. 2007.
Artemisia scoparia auct. non Waldst.: Check List HK Plants 68. 1993.

Annual or biennial herbs or subshrubs, aromatic; stem 30–150 cm tall, reddish brown or brown, faintly striate, base woody, branched above, silky pubescent or glabrescent. Basal and lower leaves ovate or elliptic, 2–5 × 1.5–3 cm, 2(–3)‑pinnatisect, with 2–3 pairs of primary lateral segments, ultimate lobules straightly linear or linear‑lanceolate, 5–10 × 0.5–2 mm, both surfaces densely silky pubescent, usually withered at anthesis. Median leaves ovate or elliptic, 2–4 × 1.5–3 cm, (1–)2‑pinnatisect, leaf lobes straightly linear‑filiform, 5–15 × 0.3–1 mm, base subsessile, apex acute, subglabrous. Upper leaves 3‑ or 5‑sect. Capitula many, ovoid to ellipsoidal, 2 – 3 × 1.3–2 mm, shortly pedunculate, with small linear bracts at base, arranged as racemose panicles. Phyllaries 3–4‑seriate, pale yellow with a green line at midvein, glabrous, margin scarious; outer ones small ovate, 1–1.3 mm; middle and inner layers ovate‑oblong, 1.5–2 mm. Peripheral florets 6–10, female and fertile, corolla conical‑tubular, 0.6 – 0.7 mm long, apically 2–3‑lobed, glandular on abaxial side; style divided, branches long and exserted, acute. Central florets 3–7, bisexual but infertile, corolla ellipsoidal‑tubular, 1.5–1.8 mm, 5‑lobed at apex, abaxially glandular; anther bases obtuse, apical appendages elongate‑triangular; style short, clavate form, apex swollen, slightly bifid or not, ovary vestigial. Cypselae obovate‑oblong, length 0.8 – 1 mm, without pappus.

Locality: Sai Kung, Port Island, Tai A Chau, Ping Chau. P. S. Choi 469; Y. W. Lam 288; S. Y. Hu 8733 (CUHK).
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Hebei, Liaoning, Shandong, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Russia (Far East), Korea, Japan, Philippines, Cochinchina via Malaysia to Indonesia.
Ecology: Coastal grasslands. Flowering: Jul.–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Wu Kau Tang, Tai Po, Sheung Shui, High Island, Ping Chau, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Artemisia indica Willd. 五月艾
Sp. Pl. 3: 1846. 1800; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 18(1 – 2): 136. 1965; FRPS 76(2): 117. 1991; FTW ed. 2, 4: 839. 1998; FGD 8: 206, fig. 123. 2007.
Artemisia vulgaris auct. non L.: FHK 187. 1861; FKH 147. 1912.

Perennial herbs or subshrubs, strongly aromatic; stem 30–120 cm tall, branched above, reddish brown, striate, base glabrescent, upper part arachnoid. Basal leaves withered at anthesis, ovate to ovate‑oblong in outline, (1–)2‑pinnatisect, primary lobes elliptic, terminal one largest, lateral ones 3–4 pairs, midvein winged. Median cauline leaves similar, ovate, ovate‑oblong or elliptic, 4–9 × 2–5.5 cm, 1–2‑pinnatisect, lobes elliptic lanceolate, linear‑lanceolate to linear, base falsely stipulate, apex acute or acuminate, margin entire, coarsely serrate or lobed, terminal segment largest, 1.5–4 cm long, lateral ones 3–4 pairs, 1–2.5 cm. Upper leaves pinnately parted, with lateral lobes 1–3 pairs, or undivided and appeared as linear‑lanceolate in shape. Leaf upper surfaces loosely cobwebby or glabrescent, lower surfaces densely covered with greyish arachnoid woolly hair. Capitula ovoid to oblong‑ovoid, numerous, 2.5–4 × 2–2.5 mm, shortly pedunculate and with leafy bracts, arranged as leafy spike‑like to racemose panicles. Involucres with 3–4 series of phyllaries, woolly hairy, with green midvein, margin broadly scarious; outer layer ovate and obtuse, 1.5 mm; middle and inner layers elliptic oblong to oblong, apex rounded, 2–3 mm. Receptacle small, convex. Marginal pistillate florets 4–8, corolla filiform‑tubular, about 1–1.2 mm, apex minutely 2–3‑lobed, glandular abaxially; style much longer than the corolla tube and conspicuously exserted, bifid, apex acute. Disk bisexual florets 8–12, corolla tubular, about 2 mm, upper half funnelform to campanulate, lower half narrowed, abaxial side glandular; anther bases obtuse, apical appendages elongate‑triangular and long‑acuminate; style slightly longer than the corolla, branched, truncate and penicillate at distal ends. Cypselae oblong, about 0.8–1 mm, truncate at both ends, faintly striate. Pappus absent.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Wu Kau Tang, Tai Po, Sheung Shui, High Island, Ping Chau, Lantau Island. H. Y. Yeung 84 (CUHK); S. Y. Hu 7658 (CUHK); Y. S. Lau 154.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; C & S Asia.
Ecology: Farmlands and wastelands. Flowering: May–Sep.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Shing Mun, Kowloon Peak, Tai Mo Shan, Tai Po, Castle Peak, Ping Chau
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Artemisia japonica Thunb. 牡蒿
Fl. Jap. 308. 1784; FHK 186. 1861; FKH 147. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 18(3–4): 233. 1965; FRPS 76(2): 241. 1991; FTW ed. 2, 4: 839. 1998; FGD 8: 210. 2007.

Perennial aromatic herbs; stem 40–130 cm tall, striate, purplish brown or brown, branched at upper portion, puberulous and later glabrescent. Leaves subsessile or sessile, loosely puberulous or glabrous on both sides. Basal and lower leaves obovate or spatulate, 4–5.5 × 1.5–2 cm, apex rounded and irregularly toothed, usually withered at flowering stage. Median leaves spatulate‑cuneate, 2–5.5 × 0.4–1.5 cm, apical 1/3 incisely lobed and toothed, and / or obliquely pinnatifid from apex to centre, usually with small linear false stipules at base. Upper leaves smaller in size. Capitula numerous, arranged as leafy racemose panicles, shape ovoid‑ellipsoidal, 2–2.5 × 1.5–2 mm, heterogamous and disciform, sessile or with tiny peduncles. Phyllaries 3–4‑seriate, imbricate, abaxially glabrous, with green line along midvein, margin scarious; outer ones ovate, 1–1.2 mm, apex obtuse; middle ones ovate‑oblong, 1.5–1.8 mm, apex rounded; inner ones oblong, length about 2 mm, apex rounded, broadly scarious. Marginal pistillate florets 3–8, fertile, corolla conical‑tubular, apex 2–3‑lobed; style branched, long and exserted, acute. Central florets 5–10, bisexual but infertile, corolla ellipsoidal‑tubular; anther bases obtuse, apical appendages elongate‑triangular and long‑acuminate; style short and claviform, apex swollen, slightly divided or not, vestigial ovary inconspicuous. Cypselae obovate‑oblong, faintly striate, about 1 mm. Pappus absent.

Locality: Shing Mun, Kowloon Peak, Tai Mo Shan, Tai Po, Castle Peak, Ping Chau. L. T. Lo 185; Y. W. Lam 1134; S. Y. Hu 11290 (CUHK).
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Gansu, Shaanxi, Shanxi, Liaoning, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Shandong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Russia (Far East), Korea, Japan, Philippines, Vietnam, Thailand, Myanmar, India to Afghanistan.
Ecology: Margins of forests, grassy slopes. Flowering: Jul.–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Artemisia lactiflora Wall. ex DC. 白苞蒿（甜菜子）
Prodr. 6: 115. 1837; FKH 147. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 18(3 – 4): 238. 1965; FRPS 76(2): 174. 1991; FGD 8: 209. 2007.

Perennial aromatic herbs 50–100 cm tall; stem striate, loosely cobwebby pubescent, glabrescent later. Basal leaves withered at flowering stage. Middle cauline leaves ovate or ovate‑elliptic, 5–9 × 4–9 cm, upper part pinnatilobed into 3 ovate to ovate‑oblong lobes, lower part pinnatisect with 1–2 pairs of lateral lobes, ovate or ovate‑oblong, the basal one smallest in size, apex usually obtuse, sometimes acute, margin serrate, both surfaces sparsely pubescent or glabrescent; petiole 1.5–5 cm. Capitula sessile, without leafy bracts at base, heterogamous and disciform, oblong to subglobose, 4–5 × 3–4.5 mm, arranged as spikes. Phyllaries 3–4‑seriate, semi‑membranous, glabrous abaxially; outer ones ovate, about 1.5 mm; middle and inner ones oblong, length 2.5–3 mm. Receptacle conical. All florets fertile. Marginal female florets 3 – 6, corolla narrowly tubular, about 1 mm, glandular outside, apex 2‑lobed; style long and exserted, twice the length of corolla, divided. Disk bisexual florets 4–10, corolla funnelform‑tubular, 1.8–2 mm, glandular, apex 5‑lobed; anther bases obtuse, apical appendages elongate‑triangular, long‑acuminate; style subequal in length with the corolla, shortly branched, truncate and penicillate at distal ends. Cypselae oblong, faintly striate, 0.8–1 mm. Pappus none.

Locality: Shing Mun, Tai Po. H. Y. Yeung 526 (CUHK); Y. S. Lau 2635, 3033.
Distribution: Area S of Qinling Range; E & SE Asia.
Ecology: Margins of forests, thickets, wastelands. Flowering: Aug.–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Artemisia lavandulaefolia DC. 野艾蒿
Prodr. 6: 110. 1837; FRPS 76(2): 92, pl. 12: 1 – 8. 1991; FFJ 5: 380, fig. 351. 1993; FGD 8: 205. 2007.

Perennial herbs or shrubs, 50 – 120 cm tall; stems erect, striate, densely arachnoid‑pubescent. Leaves densely tomentose abaxially, white glandular punctate and sparsely arachnoid‑pubescent adaxially. Basal and lowermost leaves long petiolate; leaf blade ovate to suborbicular, 8 – 13 × 7 – 8 cm, 2‑pinnatisect. Petiole of middle cauline leaves 1 – 2( – 3) cm; leaf blade ovate, ovate‑elliptic, or suborbicular, 6 – 8 × 5 – 7 cm, (1 or) 2‑pinnatisect; segments 2 or 3 pairs, 30 – 50( – 70) × 5 – 7( – 9) mm; lobules 2 or 3 pairs, lanceolate or linear‑lanceolate, serrate. Uppermost leaves and leafy bracts pinnatisect or 3‑lobed or entire. Capitula numerous, ellipsoidal or oblong, 2 – 2.5 mm in diam., pedicellate or subsessile, arranged in panicles; phyllaries densely arachnoid‑tomentose. Marginal female florets 4 – 9. Disk bisexual florets 10 – 20; corolla limb purple. Cypselae oblong or obovoid.

Locality: Tsing Yi. L. T. Lo 182.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Hubei, Henan, Shaanxi, Shanxi, Hebei, Nei Mongol, Heilongjiang, Liaoning, Jilin, Shandong, Jiangsu; Japan, Korea, Mongolia, Russia (Far East).
Ecology: Margins of forests, grassy hillslopes. Flowering & fruiting: Jul. – Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Artemisia princeps Pamp. 魁蒿
Nuovo Giorn. Bot. Ital., n. s. 36(4): 444. 1930; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 18(3–4): 153. 1965; FRPS 76(2): 120. 1991; FGD 8: 207. 2007.

Perennial herbs, 40–150 cm tall; stem purplish brown or brown, striate, branched above, cobwebby tomentose or later glabrescent. Basal leaves withered at anthesis. Middle leaves petiolate, petiole 0.5–1.5 cm, leaf blade ovate to ovate‑elliptic, 6–10 × 4–6 cm, pinnatipartite to pinnatisect, usually with 2 pairs of lateral lobes, elliptic or ovate‑elliptic, apex obtuse, margin coarsely serrate or lobed, upper surfaces loosely arachnoid to glabrous, lower surfaces densely white cobwebby tomentose. Upper leaves smaller in size, 3‑parted or undivided. Capitula heterogamous and disciform, elliptic‑ovoid, 2.5–3.5 × 1.5–2.5 mm, sessile or subsessile, with small leafy bracts at base, arranged as spikes which form panicles. Phyllaries 3–4‑seriate, with green line on midvein, cobwebby hairy, scarious along margin, outer ones small ovate, middle ones oblong, inner ones obovate‑oblong, semi‑membranous. Marginal female florets 5–7, corolla narrowly tubular, 2‑lobed at apex; style long and exserted, branched. Central bisexual florets 4–9, corolla tubular, 5‑lobed at apex, glandular outside; anther bases short‑acute, apical appendages elongate‑triangular; style with length subequal to corolla, divided, apex truncate and penicillate. Cypselae oblong, 1.5 mm, without pappus.

Locality: Mount Gough. Y. S. Lau 1962.
Distribution: S, SW, C & N China, Shaanxi, Gansu, Nei Mongol, Liaoning; also in Korea and Japan.
Ecology: Margins of forests, thickets. Flowering: Jul.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Ng Tung Chai, Tai Mo Shan, Sunset Peak
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Aster ageratoides Turcz. 三脈紫菀
Bull. Soc. Imp. Naturalistes Moscou 17: 154. 1837; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 18(3–4): 270. 1965; FRPS 74: 159. 1985; FTW ed. 2, 4: 849. 1998; FGD 8: 174. 2007.

Perennial herbs; stem erect, 40–100 cm tall, ribbed, glabrous on lower portion, sparsely puberulent upward. Basal leaves ovate, 4–6 × 2.5–3.5 cm, attenuate to form 4–8 cm of petiole, usually withered at anthesis; middle leaves elliptic or oblong‑lanceolate, 6–8.5 × 3–5 cm, base attenuate‑cuneate to form broadly‑winged petiole 3–9 cm, apex acuminate, margin with 4–7 pairs of serrate teeth; upper leaves smaller in size, subentire or shallowly toothed, subsessile or shortly petiolate. All leaves thin, triplinerved, scabrous adaxially, pubescent and sometimes glandular abaxially. Capitula corymbose or panicle‑corymbose. Involucres obconic or hemispherical; phyllaries 3‑seriate, imbricate, thickly scarious or leathery, oblong, pubescent, ciliate along margin, apex obtuse to rounded, apical region green or sometimes tinged purple, outer ones 2 mm, middle 3 mm, innermost 4 mm. Receptacle flat, alveolate, with edges of areoles shallowly chaffy. Ray florets 10–15, corolla tube 2 mm, ligules white or rarely purple, linear‑oblong, 5–8 × 0.8–1.2 mm. Disk tubular florets yellow, 5 mm, lower half of corolla tube narrower, upper half broader, bearing 5 lobes, 1.5–2 mm. Cypselae brown, densely pubescent, obovate‑oblong, 2–2.5 mm, slightly compressed, laterally ribbed, with midrib on one or both surfaces. Pappus reddish, about 4 mm.

Locality: Ng Tung Chai, Tai Mo Shan, Sunset Peak. P. S. Choi 527; Y. S. Lau 3028; S. Y. Hu & & P. P. H. But 22966 (CUHK).
Distribution: SE to NE China; E Asia, Siberia, Mongolia, S Korea, Japan.
Ecology: Margins of forests, thickets. Flowering: May–Dec.

Aster ageratoides var. scaberulus (Miq.) Ling. 微糙三脈紫菀
FRPS 74: 162. 1985; FGD 8: 174. 2007; Check List HK Plants 275. 2002.
Aster scaberulus Miq., J. Bot. Neerl. 1: 100. 1861; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 18(3 – 4): 299. 1965.
Aster trinervius auct. non Roxb. ex D. Don: Benth., FHK 174. 1861; FKH 141. 1912.

Stem, lower surfaces of leaves and phyllaries more densely hairy, scaberulous and glandular. Leaves relatively thicker.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1317; P. S. Choi 105; HK sheet 38777.
Distribution: S to SW, and C to E China; Vietnam.
Ecology: Thickets, grassy hillslopes. Flowering: May–Dec.

Aster baccharoides (Benth.) Steetz 白舌紫菀
Bot. Voy. Herald 385. 1857; FHK 175. 1861; FKH 141 1912; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 18(3–4): 276. 1965; FRPS 74: 195. 1985; FGD 8: 175, fig. 96. 2007.
Aster brevipes Benth., FHK 175. 1861; FKH 141. 1912.
Diplopappus baccharoides Benth., Lond. J. Bot. 1: 487. 1842.

Subshrubs or herbs with lower portion woody; stem erect, 50–100 cm tall, covered with short curved hair. Lower leaves spatulate‑oblong, usually withered at anthesis; middle leaves elliptic, 2–6 × 0.6–1.5 cm, sessile or with very short petiole, apex acute, margin entire or loosely serrulate at apical half; upper leaves smaller in size, subentire. All leaves scabrid on adaxial surfaces, pubescent and glandular on abaxial surfaces, midvein protrude on abaxial side. Capitula arranged in panicle‑corymb. Involucres turbinate with 5–7 × 2–3 mm; phyllaries in 4–7 series, imbricate, puberulent, margin scarious and ciliate; outermost ones ovate, 1.5 mm, apex nearly acute; those in middle layers obovate‑oblong, apex obtuse, length increasing inward; innermost ones oblanceolate‑oblong, 5 – 6 mm, apex rounded. Receptacle alveolate, with flat top, turbinate shape can be observed when phyllaries removed. Ray florets 10–15, corolla tube 3 mm, ligules white, 4.5–5 × 1.5–2 mm. Disk florets tubular, yellow, corolla tube 3 mm, 5‑lobed, lobes 2–3 mm, reflexed and rolling back; anthers exposed. Cypselae narrowly oblong, 2–2.5 mm, slightly compressed, sometimes ribbed, densely pubescent. Pappus white, 3.5–4.5 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1290, 2048; L. T. Lo 565.
Distribution: Guangdong, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian.
Ecology: Thickets, grassy hillslopes. Flowering: Sep.–Dec.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Chai Wan, Shatin Pass Rd., Kowloon Peak, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Aster panduratus Nees ex Walp. 琴葉紫菀
Nov. Act. Cur. 19, Suppl. 1: 258. 1843; FKH 141. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 18(3–4): 296. 1965; FRPS 74: 145. 1985; FGD 8: 173. 2007.

Perennial erect herb, 30–150 cm tall, branched on upper part, ribbed, strigose villose and glandular throughout. Lower leaves usually withered at anthesis, pandurate or spatulate‑oblong, 5–8 × 1.5–2.5 cm; middle leaves pandurate to oblong, 3–6 × 1–1.5 cm, base cordate or auriculate, sessile and subamplexicaul, apex acute or obtuse, margin entire; those on the flowering branches smaller, ovate‑oblong, base cordate and amplexicaul, margin entire. All leaves hispid or pilose along veins and margin, glandular. Capitula 1.2–1.8 cm across, terminal to shoots, solitary or forming loose corymbose clusters; peduncles 0.5–6 cm, densely pubescent or pilose, with linear‑lanceolate or ovate bract subtending the head. Involucres hemispherical; phyllaries 3‑seriate, oblong‑lanceolate; outermost herbaceous, 3 mm, apex acute, pubescent; middle and inner ones 4 mm and 5 mm respectively, apex and midvein herbaceous, margin scarious. Receptacle chaffy. Marginal ligulate florets about 18–30, pale purple to white, corolla tube 1.5 mm, limb 5–8 mm. Disk tubular florets greenish yellow or yellow, 3 mm including lobe of 1 mm, hairy. Cypselae brown, obovate, 1.5–2 mm, ribbed along sides, puberulous. Pappus 3 mm, white to reddish.

Locality: Chai Wan, Shatin Pass Rd., Kowloon Peak, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 869, 2526; L. T. Lo 567.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Jiangsu.
Ecology: Grassy hillslopes, wastelands. Flowering: Apr.–Dec.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, South Ninepin Island, Beaufort Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Aster striatus Champ. ex Benth. 香港紫菀
Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 4: 233. 1852; FHK 174. 1861; FKH 141. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 18(3–4): 300. 1965.

Perennial erect herb, 12–30 cm tall; stem striate, strigose throughout. Radical leaves persist at anthesis, arranged in rosette form, spatulate, 3–7 × 1–1.5 cm, apex rounded to obtuse, scabrous on both surfaces, hair denser along margin and midvein on abaxial surface; cauline ones few, pandurate‑oblong, 1–4 × 0.5–0.8 cm, base usually auriculate, amplexicaul, apex acute. Capitula hemispherical. Phyllaries in 2–3 series, lanceolate‑oblong, apex acute or acuminate, herbaceous at the middle and apical region, margin scarious, slightly fimbriate at edges, outermost 4 mm, inner ones 5 mm. Ray florets about 30, corolla tube 1.5 mm, limb 5 mm. Central tubular ones 3 mm, funnelform, hairy on the tube. Cypselae obovate, 3 mm, puberulent. Pappus white to pale red, equal in length, 3 mm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, South Ninepin Island, Beaufort Island. S. L. Thrower 1518 (CUHK); W. J. Tutcher 4820; S. P. Lau 177.
Distribution: Endemic to Hong Kong.
Ecology: Grassy hillslopes. Flowering: Apr.–Oct.
Notes: The type specimen was collected by J. G. Champion from Hong Kong Island between 1847 and 1850.

Aster subulatus Michx. 鑽形紫菀
Fl. Bor.‑Amer. 2: 111. 1803; FTW ed. 2, 4: 861. 1998.

Annual or rarely biennial herbs; stem erect, 30–120 cm tall, branched on upper portion, glabrous, terete. Leaves linear to lanceolate, less than 1.5 cm wide, margin subentire or occasionally shallowly toothed, sessile and subamplexicaul, glabrous and smooth; those on branches smaller in size, bract‑like. Capitula arranged in loose panicle or corymb. Involucres subcylindric; phyllaries 4–5‑seriate, linear‑lanceolate to subulate, apex acute or acuminate, greenish, some tinged purple at the tip, margin scarious, outermost ones 2 mm, length gradually increased inward, innermost 5 mm. Marginal ligulate florets white or pale pink in colour, limb 1.5–5 mm, slightly exserted at anthesis, always recurved and rolling back when dried. Central tubular florets yellow, 3 mm, lower half of corolla tube narrower, upper half broader, 5‑lobed at apex. Cypselae pale brown, cylindric, 0.8–2 mm, pubescent. Pappus 4–5 mm, longer than tubular florets, white or reddish, easily shed off as a whole ring.

Locality: Naturalized. Y. W. Lam 365, 733, 985.
Distribution: Native to N America, introduced and distributed throughout temperate N hemisphere.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides. Flowering: May–Dec.
Notes: As a weed.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Naturalized and widely distributed in Hong Kong
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Bidens alba (L.) DC. 白花鬼針草
Prodr. 5: 605. 1836; F. R. Fosberg & M. H. Sachet, Smithsonian Contr. Bot. 46: 22. 1980.
Coreopsis alba L., Sp. Pl. 2: 908. 1753.
Bidens pilosa var. radiata Sch.‑Bip. in Webb & Berthel., Hist. Nat. Îles Canaries 3(2): 242. 1844; FTW ed. 2, 4: 870, pl. 404. 1998.

Annual erect herbs, 0.3–1.5 m tall; stems striate, subtetragonous, glabrous or somewhat puberulent. Leaves opposite, ternate to pinnatisect, median ones 3.5–11.5 cm long, margin serrate‑mucronate, glabrous on both surfaces except the margin with curved hair, leaf lobes ovate‑lanceolate to lanceolate, base usually cuneate, apex acute to acuminate, sometimes truncate or rounded, petiole 1–4.5 cm, narrowly winged, loosely hairy along the margin. Capitula radiate, heterogamous, 1.5–3 cm across, corymbose paniculate at terminal of main stem and lateral branches. Peduncle subglabrous or loosely pubescent, 1.8–8 cm. Involucres bowl‑shaped, 4–6 mm across, hairy near base; phyllaries 2‑seriate; outer ones herbaceous, spatulate with apex dilated, rounded and reflexed, 3–4 × 1–1.5 mm, ciliate along margin; inner rows scarious, linear‑lanceolate, 5–5.5 × 1.2–1.3 mm, ciliate near the apex. Marginal ligulate florets prominent and exposing outside the involucres, 5–8 per capitulum, neutral, corolla white, tube 1–2 mm, ligule 8–14 mm, apex with 3 rounded‑obtuse lobes. Disk tubular florets many, perfect, corolla yellow, 5 mm, the upper 2/3 broadly campanulate, the lower 1/3 narrowed, apically 5‑cleft, puberulent on abaxial side of the lobes. Cypselae linear, 7–9.5 × 0.8–0.9 mm, slightly compressed, striate, blackish brown, bearing pale brown hooks and tubercles near two distal ends. Pappus 2(–3) stiff awns of 2 mm long, retrorsely barbed, pale brown.

Locality: Naturalized and widely distributed in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 3191; Y. W. Lam 21.; S. Y. Hu & Y. C. Kong 050 (CUHK).
Distribution: Native to tropical America, widely naturalized in the tropics.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides. Flowering: May–Dec.
Notes: Often regarded as a variety of Bidens pilosa.

Bidens bipinnata L. 婆婆針
Sp. Pl. 2: 832. 1753; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 18(3 – 4): 315. 1965; FRPS 75: 380, pl. 64: 3 – 6. 1979; FGD 8: 136. 2007; FTW ed. 2, 4: 868, photo 422. 1998.

Annual erect herbs, 20–100 cm tall, subtetragonous, glabrous or sparsely puberulent on upper part. Petiole 1.5–5 cm. Leaves 3–14 cm long, bipinnate or bipinnatipartite, terminal leaflets rhomboid‑lanceolate, apex acuminate, lateral segments ovate and acute, both surfaces pubescent, especially along margin and veins, margin irregularly and loosely toothed or lobed. Capitula 6–10 mm across. Peduncle 1.5–10 cm, longer in fruiting stage. Involucres bowl‑shaped, base hairy; outer phyllaries herbaceous green, linear‑lanceolate, 4–5 mm, apex obtuse, hairy along margin and on abaxial side; inner phyllaries scarious brown, lanceolate‑oblong, 4–6 mm, pubescent, margin membranous and yellow, apex densely hairy. Paleae lanceolate and narrower. Marginal ligulate florets neutral, corolla 6–7 mm, yellow, ligule elliptic or obovate, apex entire or 2 – 3‑lobed. Central tubular florets hermaphrodite, corolla 4–4.5 mm, yellow, upper 2/3 campanulate, lower 1/3 narrowed, apex 5‑cleft. Cypselae blackish brown, linear, 3–4‑angulate, slightly compressed, 7–10 × 0.8–1 mm, tuberculate and shortly hooked at upper part. Pappus of (2–)3–4, stiff and retrorsely barbed awns, pale brown, 3 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 2297; Y. W. Lam 758; S. Y. Hu 6960 (CUHK).
Distribution: S to N and NE, E to SW China; America, Europe, Asia, E Africa.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides. Flowering: Jun.–Sep.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Peng Chau, Ping Chau, Tai Po
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Bidens biternata (Lour.) Merr. & Sherff 金盞銀盤
Bot. Gaz. 88(3): 293. 1929; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 18(3 – 4): 315. 1965; FRPS 75: 378, pl. 65: 1 – 4. 1979; FGD 8: 136, fig. 71. 2007; FTW ed. 2, 4: 869. 1998.
Coreopsis biternata Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 2: 508. 1790.

Annual erect herbs; stem 30–150 cm tall, subtetragonous, glabrous or sparsely puberulent. Leaves 1‑pinnatisect to pinnatipartite, 3–10 cm long, terminal segment ovate‑lanceolate, 2.5–7.5 × 1–3 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, lateral segments 1–2 pairs, ovate, smaller than the terminal ones, 1.5–5 × 0.7–2 cm, apex acute or obtuse; both regularly and densely serrate‑mucronate, pubescent on both surfaces. Capitula 6–9 mm across. Peduncles 1.5–7.5 cm, in fruiting stage appeared longer. Involucres bowl‑shaped, hairy below; outer phyllaries herbaceous green, linear, 2–3 mm when flowering, 3–4 mm when fruiting, width 0.5–0.8 mm, apex acute to obtuse, hairy along margin and on abaxial side; inner phyllaries scarious brown, lanceolate‑oblong, 5–6 mm, hairy outside, margin membranous and yellow, apex acuminate and densely hairy. Palea oblong, narrower. Ligulate florets 3–5, or sometimes absent, neutral, corolla pale yellow, oblong, 4–5.5 × 2.5–3 mm. Tubular florets bisexual, 4–4.5 mm, 5‑dentate, yellow. Cypselae blackish brown, linear, tetragonous, narrowed at two distal ends, 8–12 × 0.8–1 mm, finely hispid on the upper part. Pappus 3–4 stiff awns, about 3 mm, pale brown, retrorsely barbed.

Locality: Peng Chau, Ping Chau, Tai Po. HK sheet 2660; S. Y. Hu 7895 (CUHK); Y. Wong 008 (CUHK).
Distribution: S to N and E to SE China; Asia, Africa, Australia.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides near villages. Flowering: Jun.–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Naturalized and widely distributed in Hong Kong
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Bidens pilosa L. 鬼針草
Sp. Pl. 2: 832. 1753; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 18(3 – 4): 318. 1965; FRPS 75: 377. 1979; FGD 8: 135. 2007; FTW ed. 2, 4: 869. 1998.

Annual erect herbs; stems 20–100 cm tall, subtetragonous, glabrous or with upper portion sparsely puberulent. Leaves mostly ternate, the median ones 3–7 cm long, with petiole 1–3.3 cm and narrowly winged, leaf segments ovate, the terminal lobes larger, apically acuminate and basally rounded or narrowed to the petiole, lateral lobes smaller, base rounded or broadly cuneate, apex acute, both surfaces glabrous or loosely pubescent, margin serrate‑mucronate; upper leaves sometimes non‑divided, lanceolate in shape. Capitula 0.8–1 cm across, discoid with all florets tubular or heterogamous with several small rays. Peduncle 1.5–7.5 cm, those in fruiting stage longer. Involucres hairy near the base; outer phyllaries herbaceous green, spatulate, 3–4 mm at anthesis, up to 5 mm at fruiting stage, margin ciliate, apex obtuse‑rounded; inner phyllaries scarious, brown, lanceolate‑oblong, 4–5 mm when flowering, 5–6 mm when fruiting, margin yellowish membranous, apex densely hairy. Palea narrower, linear‑lanceolate. Ligulate florets, if present, 4–5 mm, nearly enclosed in the involucres and thus inconspicuous, neutral, white in colour. Tubular florets 3 mm, 5‑toothed, yellow, fertile. Cypselae blackish brown, linear, 5–9 × 0.7–1 mm, somewhat laterally compressed, slightly 4‑angulate, finely hispid in upper part. Pappus 2–3 stiff awns, pale brown, 2–2.5 mm, retrorsely barbed.

Locality: Naturalized and widely distributed in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 2357; Y. S. Lau 85; S. Y. Hu 5293 (CUHK).
Distribution: S to C, E to SW China; widely distributed in Asia and tropical America.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides. Flowering: Jun.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: Usually the plants bearing ray florets are regarded as B. pilosa var. minor, while the ones bearing discoid heads are known as B. pilosa var. pilosa.

Blainvillea acumella (L.) Philip. 百能葳
Blumea 6: 350. 1950; FHN 3: 405, fig. 808. 1974; FRPS 75: 348, pl. 59: 3 – 6. 1979; FGD 8: 122, fig. 61. 2007.
Spilanthes acmella (L.) Murray, Syst. Veg. ed. 13, 610. 1774.
Blainvillea latifolia (L. f.) DC. ex Wright, Contr. Bot. Ind. 17. 1834.
Eclipta latifolia L. f., Suppl. P. 378. 1781.
Verbesina acmella L., Fl. Zeyl. 309. 1748.

Annual herbs, 40 – 60 cm tall; stem erect, many‑branched, pubescent. Lower leaves opposite; petioles ca. 1 cm; leaf blade ovate to ovate‑lanceolate, 3 – 6 × 2 – 3 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, margin sparsely serrate, strigose or pilose on both surfaces; upper leaves smaller, usually alternate, ovate to ovate‑oblong, 2 – 3 × 1.3 – 1.5 cm, base usually rounded. Capitula axillary or terminal, ca. 1 cm in diam., peduncles slender, 1.5 – 4 cm. Phyllaries in two series; outer ones herbaceous, green, ovate‑oblong, ca. 6 mm long, apex shortly acute or obtuse, dorsally covered with harsh hairs; inner ones ovate to oblong‑linear, ca. 5 mm, apex acute, lower part scarious, sparsely pubescent. Paleae oblong‑lanceolate, ca. 5 mm, apex aristiform, dorsally pubescent. Ray florets one series, ligules yellow or yellowish white, ca. 3 mm, apex 2 – 4‑toothed. Disk florets campanulate, limbs 5‑toothed. Cypselae of ray florets cuneiform triquetrous, curved, ca. 4 mm, those of disk florets compressed, ca. 5 mm. Pappus of 2 – 5, unequal bristles, connate at the base.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. HK sheet 41860, 41861.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Yunnan; India, Indonesia, Malaysia, Myanmar, Philippines, Thailand, Vietnam, Africa, America, Australia.
Ecology: Grassy hillslopes, roadsides.

Blumea balsamifera (L.) DC. 艾納香
Prodr. 5: 447. 1836; Randeria, Blumea 10: 237. 1960; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 18(3 – 4): 321. 1965; FRPS 75: 19. 1979; FTW ed. 2, 4: 875, pl. 407, photo 424. 1998.
Conyza balsamifera L., Sp. Pl. ed. 2, 2: 1280. 1763.

Erect perennial herb or subshrub, 0.5–3 m tall, usually unbranched, whole plant tomentose with brownish white hairs, thinning out on older parts. Leaves oblong, thick papery when fresh, much thinner when old or dried, lower ones 25 × 7 cm, decreasing to ca. 11 × 4 cm towards the top; margins with sharp, forward‑pointing teeth. Petioles varying between 5–30 mm, bearing narrow auricles on both sides; auricles occurring opposite or sub‑opposite to one another on the petiole, 3–5 pairs on the lower petioles, 2–3 pairs on the upper ones. Capitula pedunculate, 5–8 mm across, forming a large, woolly panicle. Phyllaries 4–5‑seriate, the innermost longest, successively decreasing in length outward. Receptacles 2–3 mm across, glabrous; outer pistillate florets 6 mm, 2–4‑lobed; hermaphrodite ones in the centre, 6–7 mm in length, 5‑lobed, much less in number than the pistillate ones. Cypselae cylindric, 1 mm, densely hirsute; pappus reddish brown, 4–6 mm.

Locality: Lantau Island. S. Y. Hu & P. P. H. But 23124 (CUHK); Y. S. Lau 3218; E. M. Gibbs 5162.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; Pakistan, India, Thailand, Myanmar, Indochina, Malaysia.
Ecology: Margins of forests, grassy hillslopes. Flowering: Mar.–Apr.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Blumea clarkei Hook. f. 七里明
Fl. Brit. India 3(8): 267. 1881; Randeria, Blumea 10: 252. 1960; Kitam., Acta Phytotax. Geobot. 23: 66. 1968; FRPS 75: 29, pl. 5: 1–6. 1979; FGD 8: 156. 2007.
Blumea hongkongensis H. Lév. & Vaniot, Bull. Acad. Int. Geogr. Bot. 12(158): 22. 1903; FKH 143. 1912.

Perennial herbs, 0.5–1.5 m tall; stems unbranched, young parts velutinous. Leaves subsessile or with a petiole up to 5 mm; leaf blade oblong‑lanceolate to linear‑oblong, 8–14 × 3–5 cm, base cuneate, apex acute, margins distantly serrate or dentate with mucronate teeth, glabrous or sometimes velutinous with prominent‑based hairs on adaxial surface, tomentellous abaxially; upper leaves sessile, oblong, 3–5 × 1–2 cm, margin denticulate, rarely subentire. Capitula numerous, 8–12 in diam., usually 3–5 clustered, sessile or shortly pedunculate, forming narrow, terminal, compact panicles. Involucres ovoid‑cylindric, ca. 12 mm; phyllaries 4‑seriate, apex purplish red, outer ones lanceolate, 3–5 mm, apex acute or acuminate, densely pubescent abaxially, ciliate, middle and inner ones lanceolate or linear, ca. 11 mm, margin scarious, sparsely pubescent abaxially. Receptacles slightly convex, alveolate, sparsely pubescent. Flowers yellow; outer pistillate florets slender tubular, 6–7 mm, limb 3–5‑toothed; central hermaphrodite florets tubular, about the same length of the pistillate florets, limb 5‑toothed. Cypselae cylindric, ca. 1.2 mm, ribbed. Pappus white, ca. 7 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. W. J. Tutcher 8589; Y. S. Lau 1369; S. C. Ng 3218.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian; Indochina, India, Malaysia, Indonesia, Philippines.
Ecology: Grassy hillslopes, roadsides. Flowering: Oct.–Mar. of the following year.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Sai Kung, Shing Mun, Tai Po, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Blumea hieracifolia (D. Don) DC. 毛氈草
Contr. Bot. India 15. 1834; FHK 178. 1861 (incl. varieties); FKH 143. 1912; Randeria, Blumea 10: 246. 1960; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 18(3–4): 324. 1965; FRPS 75: 24, pl. 4: 1–7. 1979; FGD 8: 157. 2007; FTW ed. 2, 4: 878, pl. 410, photo 427. 1998.
Erigeron hieracifolium D. Don, Prodr. Fl. Nepal. 172. 1825.

Perennial erect herbs, to 1 m tall, whole plant covered with short, fine, viscid, glandular hairs. Leaves papery, subsessile; leaf blade obovate or oblanceolate, 7–13 × 2–4 cm, base attenuate, decurrent, apex acute or mucronate, margins serrate with mucronate teeth. Inflorescence terminal and axillary, length relatively short, the whole appearing fasciculate. Capitula ca. 5–8 mm across, 2–7 clustered, forming spicate‑panicles. Involucre cylindric or campanulate; phyllaries 4–5‑seriate, upper part purplish, outer ones linear‑lanceolate, 2–3 mm, apex acuminate, abaxially white‑tomentose, middle ones linear‑oblong, 4–6 mm, apex acute, margin scarious, sparsely pubescent abaxially or only on the upper part, inner ones filiform, scarious, glabrous, ca. 6 mm. Receptacles convex, glabrous. Flowers yellow; outer pistillate florets numerous, slender tubular, limb 3‑toothed; central bisexual florets tubular, about as long as the pistillate flowers, limb 5(–6)‑toothed. Cypselae cylindric, 1–1.2 mm; pappus white, 5–6 mm long. On flowering the basal leaves wither, turning dark brown to black, but stay on the plant.

Locality: Sai Kung, Shing Mun, Tai Po, Lantau Island. W. J. Tutcher 9160; Y. S. Lau 2663; S. Y. Hu 23231 (CUHK).
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou, Fujian, Taiwan; Pakistan, India, Myanmar, Indochina, Malaysia.
Ecology: Margins of cultivated fields and grassy banks. Flowering: Oct.–Apr. of the following year.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Tam, Tai Po, Sha Tin, Sai Kung, Castle Peak, Ping Chau
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Blumea lacera (Burm. f.) DC. 見霜黃
Contr. Bot. India 14. 1834; FHK 178. 1861; FKH 142. 1912; Randeria, Blumea 10: 264. 1960; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 18(3–4): 325. 1965; FRPS 75: 33. 1979; FGD 8: 158, fig. 86. 2007; FTW ed. 2, 4: 878, pl. 411, photo 428. 1998.
Conyza lacera Burm. f., Fl. Indica 180. 1768.

Perennial herbs, to 60 cm tall; stems simple or branched on the upper part, striate, tomentose to densely velutinous with silky whitish hairs. Lower leaves usually petiolate; petioles 1–3 cm; leaf blade elliptic‑oblong to obovate‑oblong, 7–15 × 4–5 cm, base cuneate or long attenuate, apex obtuse to rounded, margin irregularly and coarsely toothed, sometimes lyrately lobed on the lower half, tomentose to velutinous adaxially, tomentose to woolly abaxially; upper leaves sessile or very shortly petiolate, leaf blade obovate to oblong‑elliptic, 2.5–4 × 1.5– 2 cm, base attenuate, apex rounded or apiculate, irregularly toothed on upper half, sometimes entire, sericeous tomentose on both surfaces. Capitula 5–6.5 mm in diam., arranged in axillary and terminal, dense to lax panicles; peduncles 0–10 mm. Phyllaries ca. 4‑seriate, herbaceous, linear, apex long‑acuminate, entirely reflexed at maturity, outer ones white‑pilose abaxially, densely ciliate. Receptacles convex, alveolate, glabrous, yellow; outer pistillate florets tubular, ca. 4 mm, limb 3‑toothed; central hermaphrodite florets tubular, ca. 5 mm, limb 5‑toothed. Cypselae 1–2 mm, sparsely hirsute, ribbed; pappus 4 mm, white.

Locality: Tai Tam, Tai Po, Sha Tin, Sai Kung, Castle Peak, Ping Chau. K. M. Lau 546 (CUHK); S. Y. Hu 10099 (CUHK); W. J. Tutcher 8591.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; SE Asia, SE Africa, N Australia.
Ecology: Margins of cultivated fields and grassy banks. Flowering: Oct.–Mar. of the following year.

Blumea laciniata (Roxb.) DC. 六耳鈴
Prodr. 5: 436. 1836; Randeria, Blumea 10: 258. 1960; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 18(3 – 4): 325. 1965; Kitam, Acta Phytotax. Geobot. 23: 68. 1968; FRPS 75: 38, pl. 6: 7–12. 1979; FGD 8: 159. 2007; FTW ed. 2, 4: 882, pl. 412. 1998.
Conyza laciniata Roxb., Fl. Ind. ed. 1832, 3: 427. 1832.
Blumea glandulosa auct. non DC.: Benth., FHK 177. 1861.

Perennial herbs, to 1.8 m tall. Stems hairy, with fine, slightly raised ribs. Leaves obovate, papery, lower ones 12– 30 × 6–15 cm, base attenuate into narrowly winged petioles, apex obtuse, margins often runcinate‑lyrate and distantly dentate, possessing sharp, irregular teeth; upper leaves decreasing to 3 × 1 cm, petioles also decreasing to almost sessile. Capitula forming panicles which in turn forming a spreading inflorescence reaching 40 cm. Peduncles pubescent; involucres campanulate with bracts spreading and reflexed at maturity. Receptacles 2.5– 3.5 mm in diam., convex, areas surrounding the attachment points of the cypselae covered sparsely with short, coarse hairs. Corolla yellow; pistillate florets slender tubular, 4.5 mm, with 2–3 glabrous teeth on the limb; hermaphrodite florets tubular, 4.5 mm, limb opening wider towards apex, with 5 pubescent teeth. Cypselae cylindric to subfusiform, 0.7–1 mm, ribbed. Pappus white, 5 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. K. M. Lau 547 (CUHK); L. T. Lo 25; S. Y. Hu 13700 (CUHK).
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Pakistan, Indochina, Malaysia.
Ecology: Margins of cultivated fields, grassy banks. Flowering: Oct.–Mar. of the following year.
Notes: Blumea species do not have ligulate (or ray florets) but they have two types of disk florets (Photo 504, × 30). Those on the outside rims of the receptacle (Photos 506, 508, 515) are slender and all female (pistillate) and possess no anthers inside their corolla. Those in the centre are broader, possess both male and female parts (hermaphrodite or bisexual, Photo 505, × 25), and are less numerous. In Photo 505, both the outside corolla tube (light yellow) and the anther tube (bright yellow) are slit open and the central pistil is separated out. The anthers can just be seen attached to the base of the corolla by 5 column‑like appendages.

Blumea lanceolaria (Roxb.) Druce 千頭艾納香
Rep. Bot. Soc. Exch. Club Brit. Isles 4: 609. 1917; Kitam., Acta Phytotax. Geobot. 4: 155. 1935; Randeria, Blumea 10: 218. 1960; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 18(3–4): 326. 1965; FRPS 75: 17. 1979; FTW ed. 2, 4: 884, pl. 413. 1998.
Conyza lanceolaria Roxb., Fl. Ind. ed. 1832, 3: 432. 1832.
Blumea myriocephala DC., Prodr. 5: 445. 1836; FKH 142. 1912.

Erect perennial herbs, 1–2 m tall. Stems striate, woody at base.
