Leaves subleathery; petioles 2–3 cm; leaf blade narrow obovate to oblanceolate, 15–23 × 4–5 cm, base attenuate, decurrent, sometimes with auricular appendages, apex acuminate, margins with coarse teeth; dark green adaxially, lighter abaxially; glabrous or sometimes slightly hairy on abaxial surface. Capitula many, 3 mm in diam., usually 3–4 clustered, subsessile or with a short peduncle (5–10 mm), forming a terminal pyramidal panicle. Involucre cylindric or subcampanulate, 6– 8 mm; phyllaries 5–6‑seriate, green or purplish, outer ones ovate‑lanceolate, ca. 2 mm, apex obtuse or ± acute, pubescent abaxially, middle ones narrowly lanceolate or linear‑lanceolate, 3–4 mm, apex acute, margin scarious, inner ones linear, ca. 8 mm, apex acute, sparsely pubescent. Receptacle flat, foveolate, densely white pubescent. Flowers yellow; outer pistillate florets numerous, slender tubular, ca. 7 mm, limb 3‑lobed, glabrous; central bisexual florets tubular, limb 5‑toothed. Cypselae ca. 1.5 mm, 5‑ribbed; pappus yellowish.

Locality: Aberdeen, Fung Yuen, Sai Kung. Y. S. Lau 3093; W. J. Tutcher 11416.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou, Taiwan; India, Pakistan, Myanmar, Thailand, Indochina, Philippines, Indonesia.
Ecology: Margins of forests, grassy hillslopes. Flowering: Jan.–Apr.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Authority: (Randeria) C. C. Chang & Y. Q. Tseng
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Blumea megacephala (Randeria) C. C. Chang & Y. Q. Tseng 東風草（大頭艾納香）
Acta Phytotax. Sin. 12(3): 310. 1974; FRPS 75: 11, pl. 2: 1 – 7. 1979; FGD 8: 153, fig. 85. 2007.
Blumea riparia DC. var. megacephala Randeria, Blumea 10(1): 215. 1960; FTW ed. 2, 4: 888, pl. 417, photo 430. 1998.
Blumea chinensis auct. non DC.: Benth., FHK 177. 1861.

Scandent perennial herb, branches elongate and scandent. Stems cylindric, striate, growing to 1–3 m or longer. Leaves ovate to oblong, 7–10 × 2.5–4 cm, base rounded, apex acuminate, margins mucronulate or mucronulate‑denticulate, both surfaces sparsely hairy, becoming glabrous later; petioles 2–5 mm. Capitula relatively large, 10–15 mm in diam., arranged in axillary panicles or subcorymbose inflorescences. Peduncles 1– 3 cm. Involucres hemispherical; phyllaries 5–6 seriate, the outermost series shortest. Receptacle flat, with long white hairs. Outer pistillate florets many, corolla slender tubular, 2–4‑lobed, puberulent; the central bisexual florets tubular, corollas 5‑lobed, with white multi‑cellular hairs. Cypselae cylindric, ribbed, 0.7 mm long. Pappus white, 5 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 1458; Y. W. Lam 1147; S. Y. Hu 9200 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Margins of forests, thickets. Flowering: Oct.–Feb. of the following year.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Sha Tin, Tai Po, Fanling
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Blumea mollis (D. Don) Merr. 柔毛艾納香
Philipp. J. Sci. Bot. 5(5): 395. 1910; Randeria, Blumea 10: 261. 1960; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 18(3–4): 328. 1965; FRPS 75: 32. 1979; FGD 8: 158. 2007; FTW ed. 2, 4: 884, pl. 415, photo 429. 1998.
Erigeron molle D. Don, Prodr. Fl. Nepal. 172. 1825.
Blumea wightiana DC., Contr. Bot. India 14. 1834; Benth., FHK 178. 1861.

Annual erect herbs, to 60 cm tall. Stems slender, with soft, glandular, somewhat viscid hairs. Lower leaves obovate, 7–9 × 3–4 cm, base cuneate‑attenuate, apex broadly obtuse, margin irregularly serrulate, sericeous pilose with glandular hair on both surfaces; petioles 1–2 cm. Upper leaves subsessile, gradually decreasing, 1–2 × 0.3– 0.8 cm. Capitula numerous, sessile or on a very short peduncle, 3–5 mm in diam., usually 3 – 5 clustered, forming a narrow and short panicle. Involucres campanulate, ca. 5 mm; phyllaries in 4 series, purplish, outer ones linear, ca. 3 mm, apex acuminate, densely soft‑villous and with multicellular hairs and glands abaxially, innear ones linear, 5– 6 mm, margin scarious, ciliate. Receptacles convex, glabrous. Outer pistillate florets filiform, 4–5 mm, limbs 3‑toothed; central bisexual florets about 10; corolla tubular, purplish, 4–5 mm, limb 5‑toothed. Cypselae fusiform, ribbed, pubescent, ca. 0.7 mm. Pappus ca. 3 mm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Sha Tin, Tai Po, Fanling. K. M. Lau 545 (CUHK); H. C. Tang 1199; Y. S. Lau 2623.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Taiwan; S Asia, Indonesia to N Australia, Africa.
Ecology: Open grassy hillslopes, preferring sunny locations. Flowering: Feb.–Mar.

Blumea oblongifolia Kitam. 長圓葉艾納香
Acta Phytotax. Geobot. 2(1): 37. 1933; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 18(3–4): 328. 1965; FRPS 75: 30, pl. 5: 7–12. 1979; FGD 8: 156. 2007; FTW ed. 2, 4: 888, pl. 416. 1998.

Perennial herbs; stems erect, to 1.5 m tall, striate, velutinous particularly on young parts. Leaves subsessile or short petiolate, oblong to narrowly elliptic‑oblong, 9–14 × 3.5–5.5 cm, base cuneate‑attenuate, apex acute or obtuse, margin distantly serrate with mucronate teeth, pubescent adaxially, ± villous abaxially. Capitula numerous, 8–12 mm in diam., forming terminal and axillary panicles; peduncles up to 2 cm, densely villous. Involucres globose‑campanulate; phyllaries 4‑seriate, green, outer ones lanceolate, 4–5 mm, apex caudate‑acuminate, densely villous abaxially, middle and inner ones linear or linear‑lanceolate, 7–7.5 mm, apex caudate, margin scarious, pubescent abaxially. Receptacle slightly convex, alveolate, hairy. Flowers yellow; outer pistillate florets numerous, slender tubular, 5–5.5 mm, limb 3–4‑toothed; central hermaphrodite florets less numerous, tubular, 6 mm, limb 5‑toothed. Cypselae cylindric, ca. 1 mm, ribbed, sparsely hirsute. Pappus white, 5–6 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 2278, 2425; S. Y. Hu 22816A (CUHK).
Distribution: Guangdong, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Moist places in ravines. Flowering: Oct.–Mar. of the following year.
Notes: At first glance, and without the help of flowers, this species can be confused with B. lacera. Their leaf shapes are similar, and in some locations they grow close to each other. However, the leaves of this species are more oblong, with a firmer papery texture, both in the fresh and in the dried state. The present species does not usually branch, and can be over 1 m tall; B. lacera often branches, never reaches 1 m tall even at maturity.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): The Peak, Kowloon Peak, Sha Tin, Tai Lam Chung, Lamma Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Blumea sessiliflora Decne. 無梗艾納香
Nouv. Ann. Mus. Hist. Nat. 3: 140. 1834; Randeria, Blumea 10: 257. 1960; FRPS 75: 35. 1979.

Annual herbs, to 1.3 m tall; stems erect, usually unbranched, with slightly raised longitudinal ribs, covered sparsely with short, coarse hairs. Lower leaves sessile, oblanceolate to obovate‑oblong, 10–16 × 4–6 cm, base attenuate and decurrent, apex acute, margins runcinate‑lyrate, with irregular teeth, pilose on both surfaces; upper leaves decreasing gradually, sessile, oblanceolate to oblong, 3–6 × 0.5–1.5 cm; the uppermost leaves linear, bract‑like, entire or with a few sharp teeth. Capitula 3–4 mm across, 3 or more clustered, sessile or on a very short peduncle (2 mm), forming axillary panicles varying from 9 cm at the very bottom axils to 22 cm on mid‑stem, and gradually decreasing to 4–5 cm at apex. Involucre cylindric or subcampanulate, 4–6 mm; phyllaries 4– 5‑seriate, straw‑coloured or green, outer and middle ones lanceolate or linear‑lanceolate, 2–4 mm, apex acuminate, margin scarious, densely pubescent abaxially, inner ones linear, 4–6 mm, glabrous or sparsely pubescent abaxially. Receptacle slightly convex, foveolate, glabrous, scabrous, about 2 mm across. Flowers yellow; outer pistillate florets numerous; corolla slender tubular, 3.5–4 mm, limb 3‑lobed; bisexual florets fewer, corolla tubular, 4–5 mm, slightly enlarged at the 5‑lobed limb. Cypselae cylindric or subfusiform, 0.5 mm, ribbed. Pappus white, 3 mm.

Locality: The Peak, Kowloon Peak, Sha Tin, Tai Lam Chung, Lamma Island. S. Y. Hu & P. P. H. But 22903 (CUHK); S. L. Thrower 1487 (CUHK); N. H. Li & K. M. Lau 544 (CUHK).
Distribution: Guangdong, Jiangxi; India, Myanmar, Thailand, Indochina, Indonesia.
Ecology: Grassy hillslopes, prefering sheltered, damp locations. Flowering: Feb.–Mar.
Notes: Despite its production of numerous fruits, it is not common in Hong Kong.

Calendula officinalis L. 金盞花
Sp. Pl. 921. 1753; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 19(1 – 2): 10. 1966; FRPS 77(1): 327. 1999; FGD 8: 232, fig. 142. 2007.

Annual herbs 20–70 cm tall; stem branched, covered with glandular pubescent hair. Basal leaves spatulate to oblanceolate, 4.5–16.5 × 1–4 cm, apex obtuse‑rounded, margin entire. Middle cauline leaves oblanceolate‑oblong, sessile and amplexicaul, 4–10 × 1–3.5 cm, apex obtuse, margin undulate, loosely and minutely toothed, both surfaces puberulous to pubescent, hair denser along margin and midvein. Upper leaves smaller in size, lanceolate‑oblong. Capitula heterogamous and radiate, solitary to stem and branch terminals, 4–8 cm across. Involucres hemispherical; phyllaries herbaceous, 2‑seriate, lanceolate‑oblong, outer layer slightly longer than the inner ones, 10–13 × 1.5–2 mm, apex long acuminate‑caudate, abaxially hirsute, hair multicellular. Marginal ligulate florets in 2–3 series, colour yellow or orange‑yellow, ligule linear oblong, 1.5 – 3 × 0.4–0.8 cm, tube short and hairy, female and fertile. Disk tubular florets about 5 mm, apex with 5 lanceolate lobes, functionally staminate and infertile. Cypselae pale yellow or pale brown, incurved, abaxial side densely tuberculate and wrinkled, glandular hairy, adaxial side longitudinally striate. Pappus absent.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 15995; S. Y. Hu 9311A (CUHK); H. Y. Yeung 182 (CUHK).
Distribution: S Europe and N Africa, cultivated elsewhere.
Ecology: Flowering: Feb.–Oct.
Uses: Ornamental.

Callistephus chinensis (L.) Nees 翠菊
Gen. Sp. Aster. 222. 1832; FRPS 74: 109. 1985; FGD 8: 177, fig. 98. 2007.
Aster chinensis L., Sp. Pl. 877. 1753.

Erect annual herbs, 30–100 cm tall, hirsute throughout. Leaves in the middle portion of stem ovate or spatulate, 3–6 × 2–4 cm, base cuneate, serrate on margin; petiole winged, 2–4 cm; leaves changed to smaller size in upper portion, oblanceolate, long‑oblong or linear, entire or slightly serrate at distal end. Capitula terminal to branches, 4 – 8 cm across. Involucres hemispherical, 2–4 cm across; phyllaries 3‑seriate, nearly equal in length; outer ones foliaceous, oblong‑lanceolate or spatulate, 10–20 × 2–4 mm, apex rounded, coarsely ciliate on margin; those in middle layer spatulate, membranous, tinged purple; inner ones long‑oblong, apex obtuse, membranous, semi‑transparent. Ligulate florets in 1–several series, 10–30 × 2–5 mm; cultivated form with various colours, white, red, pink, purple or blue. Achenes oblong‑oblanceolate, slightly compressed, 3 mm, pilose on upper portion. Pappus 2‑seriate, outer ones short; inner ones plumose, caducous.

Locality: Cultivated. S. Y. Hu & K. H. Yung 113 (CUHK); S. Y. Hu & P. P. H. But 22444 (CUHK); S. Y. Hu 12979 (CUHK).
Distribution: Native to SW and N China; cultivated elsewhere.
Ecology: Flowering: May–Oct.
Uses: Ornamental.

Carpesium abrotanoides L. 天名精
Sp. Pl. 860. 1753; FKH 144. 1912; FRPS 75: 313. 1979; FTW ed. 2, 4: 893. 1998; FGD 8: 149, fig. 82. 2007.

Perennial herbs; stem 50–100 cm tall, striate, branches many, lower portion woody and subglabrous, upper part pubescent. Basal leaves withered at anthesis, median and upper ones 4–11.5 × 0.8–5.5 cm, base cuneate, apex obtuse to acute, margin irregularly dentate, adaxial surface puberulent, abaxial surface pubescent and glandular, petiole 5–15 mm; leaves on upper portion smaller in size, apex acute to acuminate, petioles much shorter or almost absent. Capitula axillary, subsessile or shortly pedunculate, arranged as spicate form, sometimes subtended by several elliptic or lanceolate leaves of 4–15 mm. Involucres depressed‑globose, 6–10 mm across; phyllaries 3‑seriate; outer ones ovate and shortest, about 3.5 mm, apex obtuse, basally scarious and apically foliaceous, margin of upper half ciliate, abaxial side pubescent; middle phyllaries lanceolate‑oblong, 4.5–5 mm; while inner ones oblong, 5–6 mm, both scarious, with rounded apex, margin ciliate and shallowly serrulate near the tip, not entire. Receptacle plane, nude, the centre of areoles elevated. Florets yellow, glandular near the limb apex, marginal ones female, corolla narrowly tubular, 1–1.5 mm, apex 5‑lobed; central florets hermaphrodite, corolla similar in shape but larger, 2–2.5 mm; anther sagittate at base with caudate and split lobes, the apical appendages oblong and truncate at tip; stylar branches subcomplanate, apex rounded. Cypselae oblong‑cylindric, 3–3.5 mm, striate‑costate, narrowed at base, apex rostrate and with an annular cartilaginous crown, glandular at the base and on the rostrum. Pappus absent.

Locality: Sha Tin, Wu Kai Sha. W. J. Tutcher 11229; HK sheet 32940; N. H. Li 12 (CUHK).
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; also in Japan, Korea, Myanmar, Sikkim.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides. Flowering: Jun.–Mar. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Centipeda minima (L.) A. Br. & Aschers. 石胡荽
Index Sem. (Berlin) 1867: App. 6. 1867; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 19(1 – 2): 21. 1966; FRPS 76(1): 132. 1983; FTW ed. 2, 4: 898. 1998; FGD 8: 201, fig. 121. 2007.
Myriogyne minuta (G. Forst) Less., Linnaea 6: 219. 1831; FHK 186. 1861; FKH 146. 1912.
Cotula minuta G. Forst., Fl. Ins. Austr. 57. 1786.
Artemisia minima L., Sp. Pl. 849. 1753.

Small annual herbs, branches many; stem decumbent, 4–20 cm or longer, glabrous or covered with cobwebby hair. Leaves alternate, sessile, oblanceolate to spatulate, 5–18 × 1–7 mm, base cuneate, apex obtuse to rounded, margin entire or with 1–2 pairs of teeth in upper half, glabrous or cobwebby hairy on both surfaces, abaxially glandular‑punctate. Capitula small, depressed globose, 3–4 mm in diam., solitary and axillary, sessile or subsessile. Involucres depressed hemispherical; phyllaries in 2–3 series, outer 1–2 layers oblong and larger in size, inner layers obovate‑oblong, all herbaceous green, with hyaline and lacerate margins and apices, glabrous or loosely cobwebby on abaxial side. Marginal florets pistillate, many‑seriate, corolla narrowly tubular, 0.2 mm, shorter than the ovary, pale greenish yellow in colour, minutely 2–3‑toothed at apex. Central florets bisexual, corolla tubular, 0.5 mm, apex 4‑lobed, colour pale purple. All florets fertile. Cypselae narrowly and obliquely oblong, 1–1.2 mm in length, 4‑angulate, base cuneate, brown in colour, ribs pale brown and hairy. Pappus wanting.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 2187; S. L. Thrower 1350 (CUHK); S. Y. Hu 11889 (CUHK).
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; Korea, Japan, India, Malaysia, Australia.
Ecology: Wastelands, margins of farmlands. Flowering: Mar.–Sep.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Chorisis repens (L.) DC. 苦蕒菜
Prodr. 7: 178. 1838; FRPS 80(1): 260. 1997.
Prenanthes repens L., Sp. Pl. 798. 1753.
Ixeris repens (L.) A. Gray, Mem. Amer. Acad. n.s. 6: 397. 1858; FHK 194. 1861; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 20(1 – 2): 6. 1967; FTW ed. 2, 4: 1001. 1998; FGD 8: 269. 2007; Check List HK Plants 284. 2002; 97. 2004.
Lactuca repens (L.) Benth. ex Maxim., Bull. Acad. Imp. Sci. Saint‑Petersbourg 19: 532. 1874; FKH 150. 1912.

Perennial herbs; stem creeping, up to 2 m or longer, glabrous, forming adventitious roots and long‑petiolate leaves at nodes. Leaves thick, broad‑ovate, 2.5–3 × 1.5–5 cm, palmatilobed to palmatisect, segments usually 3 or occasionally 5, elliptic, regularly or irregularly orbicular, apex rounded or broadly obtuse, margin mucronulate, shallowly sinuate or sometimes with an obtuse tooth or a small elliptic lobe on one side, both surfaces glabrous; petioles 1.5–6.5 cm, base clasping. Flowering branch axillary, 3–5.5 cm, bearing ovate‑oblong bracteoles, with 2–6 capitula arranged as loose corymbs. Capitula homogamous with all florets ligulate and hermaphrodite; peduncles 0.8–1.5 cm. Involucres cylindric, 10–12 mm; phyllaries glabrous abaxially, slightly ciliate and sometimes tinged purple near apex, 2–3‑seriate; outer two layers ovate or elliptic, 3–6 × 1.2–1.8 mm, apex acute or acuminate; inner layer lanceolate‑oblong, 10–12 × 2–2.5 mm, acute. Ligulate florets 12 – 20 per head, corolla yellow, about 10–11 mm, lower tube 4 mm, ligule 6–7 mm, 5‑lobed at apex. Cypselae fusiform, brown, slightly compressed, 4 × 1 mm, glabrous, obtusely 10‑ribbed, apex attenuate into a thick beak about 0.5 – 1 × 0.2–0.3 mm. Pappus growing on the beak, white in colour, 5 mm, minutely scaberulous.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. W. Lam 465; HK sheet 16359; S. Y. Hu 12472 (CUHK).
Distribution: Widely distributed in S, E, N & NE China; also in Japan, Korea, Russia (Far East region).
Ecology: Sandy beaches. Flowering: Apr.–Oct.

Chrysanthemum segetum L. 茼蒿
Sp. Pl. 889. 1753; FKH 146. 1912; FRPS 76(1): 22. 1983; FGD 8: 199, fig. 118. 2007.
Chrysanthemum coronarium var. spatiosum Bailey, Gentes Herb. 1: 47. 1920; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 19(1–2): 27. 1966.

Annual herbs; stems erect, 20–80 cm tall, fleshy, glabrous or subglabrous. Leaves elliptic, obovate‑elliptic to oblanceolate, margin coarsely and irregularly serrate or dentate, sometimes shallowly pinnatifid, 4–12 × 3–4 cm, base cuneate, sessile, apex rounded, both surfaces glabrous; leaves in upper stem smaller in size. Capitulum solitary at stem terminal or few at branches; peduncle about 5 cm. Involucres broad hemispherical, 1–2 cm across; phyllaries 4‑seriate, imbricate, ovate, rigidly herbaceous with margin and apices hyaline, the membranous apices of the innermost layer broaden as appendages. Marginal ligulate florets 1.5 cm, ligule linear‑oblong, yellow. Central tubular florets yellow or orange‑yellow, lower portion narrow and glandular, upper portion campanulate, 5‑lobed at apex. Cypselae of ray florets trigonous and narrowly 2‑winged on both lateral sides; those of disk florets oblong, inconspicuously ribbed, with one side broadly hard‑winged. Pappus absent.

Locality: Cultivated. S. Y. Hu 9409A, 11875 (CUHK); HK sheet 2665.
Distribution: Cultivated all over China; native to Mediterranean region.
Ecology: Flowering: Mar.–Aug.
Uses: Food (vegetable).

Cirsium hupehense Pamp. 湖北薊（馬刺薊）
Nuovo Giorn. Bot. Ital. n.s. 18(1): 86. 1911; FRPS 78(1): 121. 1987; FGD 8; 250. 2007.

Perennial herbs, 50–200 cm tall; stem erect, striate, branched or not, loosely greyish white tomentose especially on the upper portion. Leaves thick, upper surfaces green, subglabrous or scabrous, lower surfaces greyish white, densely woolly hairy, distinctly one‑veined. Median cauline leaves oblong or oblong‑lanceolate, 7–13 × 0.8–2.5 cm, sessile, apex acute, margin entire or sometimes basally dentate or dentate‑serrate, but never pinnatilobed or cleft, spinules alternatively long and short growing along margin, the longer ones 3–5 mm, the short ones 1–2 mm. Upper leaves smaller in size, oblong, lanceolate to linear. Capitula arranged as loose corymbs at branch terminal, seldom solitary. Involucres ovoid‑globose, 1.2–2.5 cm across; phyllaries 6‑seriate, imbricate, abaxial side viscid and arachnoid hairy; outer two layers ovate‑lanceolate, 4–5 × 1 mm, apical spinule about 1 mm; middle layers lanceolate, 6–7 × 2 mm, spinule 1–2 mm, sometimes scarious near the base of spine; inner two layers lanceolate‑oblong to oblong, 10–15 × 1–1.5 mm, apex dilated and scarious, forming appendages about 1–3 mm, purplish red. Florets purple, pink to red, corolla lower tube filiform, 9–11 mm, upper limb broaden, 9–10 mm, apex obliquely and deeply cleft as 5 linear lobes 5–6 mm. Cypselae cuneate‑obovate, about 2–4 mm, apex obliquely truncate and rostrate. Pappus plumose, unequal in length, varied from 1–1.6 cm, white to pale brown, base connate and deciduous as a ring.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 186, 1332; P. S. Choi 456.
Didtribution: Guangdong, Yunnan, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Hebei, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Fujian.
Ecology: Margins of forests, wastelands. Flowering: Oct.–May of the following year.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Cape D'Aguilar, Clear Water Bay, Sai Kung, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Cirsium japonicum Fisch. ex DC. 薊
Prodr. 6: 642. 1837; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 19(1–2): 55. 1966; FRPS 78(1): 103. 1987; FGD 8: 249, fig. 151. 2007;.
Cnicus japonicus (Fisch. ex DC.) Maxim., Bull. Acad. Imp. Sci. Saint‑Petersbourg 19(5): 503. 1874; FKH 149. 1912.

Perennial herbs; stem erect, 30–150 cm tall, striate, branched or not, loosely to densely multicellular‑hairy and tomentose, especially near the head. Leaves green and multicellular scabrous above and beneath. Leaves oblanceolate or oblong in outline, 6–30 × 2–10 cm, pinnatilobed to pinnatisect, lateral segments 6 – 12 pairs, triangular, hemispherical or oblong, width varied from 0.5–4 cm, those in the middle larger in size, margin coarsely and irregularly dentate, spines unequal in length, 1–6 mm, leaf base attenuate as short or long winged petiole, the petiole wing also toothed and spiny, apical segment ovate or triangular. Upper stem leaves gradually smaller in size, sessile, base dilated and semi‑amplexicaul. Capitula erect, seldom nodding, solitary or few at stem terminal. Involucres broadly campanulate, 2.5 – 3 cm across; phyllaries 6‑seriate, imbricate, abaxial side cobwebby hairy and with viscid glands along midvein, margin ciliate; outer layers lanceolate, 5–7 × 2 mm, apical spinules long and hard, 2.5–5 mm; middle layers oblong‑lanceolate, 10–13 × 1.5–2 mm, spinules short and soft, 1–3 mm; inner layers linear‑lanceolate with length 15–20 mm, width 1–1.2 mm, apex acuminate without spinules. Florets red or purple, 2–2.2 cm, lower filiform tube 0.9–1.1 cm, upper limb 1.1–1.2 mm and unequally cleft into 5 linear lobes 5–6 mm. Cypselae compressed, obliquely cuneate‑oblanceolate, 3.5 mm, apex obliquely truncate and with rostrum less than 1 mm. Pappus pale brown, feathery, length unequal, 1–1.6 cm, base connate and shed off as a ring.

Locality: Cape D'Aguilar, Clear Water Bay, Sai Kung, Lantau Island. T. K. Leung & T. K. Wang 2515; S. Y. Hu & P. P. H. But 23833 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Hebei, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Shandong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Korea, Japan.
Ecology: Grassy hillslopes. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Mount Gough, Ma On Shan, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Cirsium lineare (Thunb.) Sch. Bip. 絲葉薊
Linnaea 19: 335. 1874; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 19(1 – 2): 58. 1966; FTW ed. 2, 4: 909, pl. 428. 1998; FRPS 78(1): 120. 1987; FGD 8: 250. 2007; Kitam., Acta Phytotax. Geobot. 41: 179. 1991.
Carduus linearis Thunb., Fl. Jap. 305. 1784.
Cirsium chinense Gardner & Champ., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 1: 323. 1849; FHK 168. 1861.
Cnicus chinensis Benth. ex Maxim., Bull. Acad. Imp. Sci. Saint‑Petersbourg 19(5): 503 – 504. 1874; FKH 149. 1912.

Perennial herbs; stem erect, 50–150 cm tall, striate, branched in upper portion, glabrous, subglabrous or sparsely cobwebby hairy or multicellular hairy. Middle leaves oblong, lanceolate to oblanceolate, 6–12 × 2–2.5 cm, gradually smaller in size when growing upward, lanceolate to linear‑lanceolate, base attenuate, apex acute, obtuse or caudate‑acuminate, sessile or shortly petiolate, adaxial surfaces green, scabrous, abaxial surfaces pale green or whitish, loosely cobwebby hairy or subglabrous, margin entire, sometimes basally dentate, but not pinnatilobed, finely and closely curved‑spinulose. Capitula arranged as loose corymbs at branch terminal. Involucres ovoid; phyllaries 6‑seriate, imbricate; outer and median layers triangular to triangular‑lanceolate, 5–8 × 2–5 mm, apex spinules 2 mm; inner layers lanceolate to linear‑lanceolate, 1–1.5 cm, apex dilated, reddish scarious. Florets purplish red, corolla 2 cm, lower tube as long as upper limb, apex obliquely and deeply cleft into 5 linear lobes. Cypselae cuneate‑obovoid, 2.5–4 × 1.5–1.8 mm, smooth and glabrous, with many blackish brown lines, apex obliquely truncate and with small rostrum 0.5–1 mm. Pappus pale brown to greyish white, plumose, 1.3–1.5 cm, base connate and shed off as a ring.

Locality: Mount Gough, Ma On Shan, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island. S. L. Thrower 1431, 1422 (CUHK); S. Y. Hu 11148 (CUHK); C. P. Lau 178 (CUHK).
Distribution: Guangdong, Jiangxi, Anhui, Shandong, Liaoning, Nei Mongol, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Korea, Japan.
Ecology: Grassy hillslopes. Flowering: Sep.–Dec.
Notes: The type specimen of Cirsium chinense was collected by J. G. Champion from Victoria Peak between 1847 and 1849.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Naturalized and widely distributed in Hong Kong
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Conyza bonariensis (L.) Cronq. 香絲草
Bull. Torrey Bot. Club. 70: 632. 1943; FRPS 74: 350. 1985; FTW ed. 2, 4: 914. 1998; FGD 8: 186. 2007.
Erigeron bonariensis L., Sp. Pl. 863. 1753.
Erigeron linifolius Willd., Sp. Pl. 3(3): 1955. 1803; FHK 176. 1861.

Annual or biennial herb; stem erect, 25–60 cm tall; lateral branches usually grow over the main axis, pubescent throughout, sparsely hirsute. Leaves densely pubescent on both surfaces; basal leaves usually withered at flowering period, oblanceolate or oblong‑lanceolate, coarsely toothed or shallowly pinnatifid along margin, 3–10 × 0.2– 0.8 cm; middle leaves linear‑lanceolate to linear, entire or slightly toothed, 3–10 × 0.1–0.5 cm; upper leaves linear, entire, 1.5–6 × 0.1–0.2 cm or much smaller. Capitula 4 – 6 × 8 – 10 mm, arranged in terminal racemes or racemose‑panicles. Involucres urceolate, then widely spreading; phyllaries 2–3‑seriate, linear‑lanceolate, apex acuminate, herbaceous, margin scarious, densely covered with greyish white hair, inner layers 3–4 mm, outermost 2–3 mm. Receptacle flat. Marginal female florets numerous, white, corolla tube filiform, 3 mm, with or without minute ligules, 2–4‑cleft. Central bisexual florets tubular, yellow, 3 mm, upper part cylindric, lower part filiform, 5 lobes at apex. Cypselae oblong, 1.5 mm, compressed, pilose, straw‑coloured. Pappus bristles in 1 series, 3 mm, reddish brown.

Locality: Naturalized and widely distributed in Hong Kong. S. L. Thrower 1401 (CUHK); Y. S. Lau 2012, 2196.
Distribution: Origin from S America, widely naturalized in tropical and subtropical regions.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides. Flowering: Apr.–Sep.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Naturalized and widely distributed in Hong Kong
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Conyza canadensis (L.) Cronq. 小蓬草
Bull. Torrey Bot. Club. 70: 632. 1943; FRPS 74: 348. 1985; FTW ed. 2, 4: 916. 1998; FGD 8: 185, fig. 104. 2007.
Erigeron canadensis L., Sp. Pl. 863. 1753.

Annual herbs, 30–120 cm tall; stems erect, densely or loosely hirsute or glabrous, branched on upper portion. Basal leaves usually withered at flowering stage; middle cauline leaves linear‑lanceolate, 3.5–10 cm × 2–6 mm, leaf surfaces nearly glabrous, bearing loose and distinct, curved and stiff hair along margin; upper leaves much reduced to about 1 cm long, linear. Capitula 3–4 × 2–3.5 mm, numerous, forming large pyramidal panicle. Involucres subcylindric, then widely spreading; phyllaries in 3–4 series, linear to linear‑lanceolate; outer ones about or less than 1 mm, glabrous or loosely ciliate, herbaceous; inner ones ca. 3 mm, glabrous, scarious along margin. Receptacle flat. Marginal female florets white, ligulate, corolla tube 2 mm, filiform, ciliate near the throat, ligule 0.5 mm. Central bisexual florets yellow, tubular, 2.5 mm, upper part cylindric, lower part filiform, 4–5‑lobed and ciliate at apex. Cypselae linear‑oblong, ca. 1 mm, compressed, minutely pubescent, pale brown. Pappus bristles in 1 series, ca. 2 mm, white to yellowish brown.

Locality: Naturalized and widely distributed in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 2383; Y. W. Lam 1007;S. L. Thrower 1538 (CUHK).
Distribution: Native to N America, distributed worldwide.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides. Flowering: Jul.–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Conyza japonica (Thunb.) Less. 白酒草
Syn. Compos. 204. 1832; FKH 142. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 19(1–2): 70. 1966; FRPS 74: 342. 1985; FTW ed. 2, 4: 918. 1998; FGD 8: 185. 2007.
Erigeron japonicum Thunb., Fl. Jap. 312. 1784.
Conyza veronicaefolia Wall. ex DC., Prodr. 5: 382. 1836; FHK 176. 1861.

Annual or biennial herbs, 15–50 cm tall. Stems erect, branched in upper portion, striate, villose. Leaves amplexicaul, villous on both surfaces; radical leaves in rosettes, obovate to spatulate, 4–11 × 1.5–4 cm, base attenuate to form wing with petiole, apex rounded, crenate or dentate; middle leaves oblanceolate to oblong, sessile, 4–5 × 0.5–1.5 cm; upper leaves much reduced in size, linear‑lanceolate. Capitula globose, 7 – 10 mm across, numerous, in tight corymbs or clustered as glomerules in terminal. Involucres hemispherical; phyllaries 2 – 3‑seriate, imbricate, pubescent, green in the middle, scarious and purple along margin, apex acute or acuminate; outer ones ovate‑lanceolate, 2 mm; inner ones linear‑lanceolate, 4 mm. Receptacle hemispherical, areole of hermaphrodite florets larger than those of marginal female florets, fimbriate. Florets all fertile, yellow. Ray florets numerous, pistillate, corolla filiform, 1.8–2 mm, half the length of style, ciliate at tip; style 3 mm, reddish purple. Disk florets 15, hermaphrodite, corolla tubular, 4 mm, swollen in upper part, with 5 ovate lobes, each lobe bearing 2 or 3 hairs. Cypsela obovate, flattened, minutely puberulous, yellow; pappus bristles greyish white, 1‑seriate, 4 mm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan. H. C. Tang 2015; Y. W. Lam 582; S. Y. Hu & P. P. H. But 22842 (CUHK).
Distribution: S to C and E to SW China; Japan, India, Myanmar, Thailand, Malaysia.
Ecology: Margins of forests, wastelands. Flowering: Apr.–Aug.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Naturalized and widely distributed in Hong Kong
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Conyza sumatrensis (Retz.) Walker 蘇門白酒草
J. Jap. Bot. 46: 72. 1971; FRPS 74: 350. 1985; FTW ed. 2, 4: 919. 1998; FGD 8: 186. 2007.
Erigeron sumatrensis Retz., Observ. Bot. 5: 28. 1789.
Erigeron floribundus auct. non (H. B. K.) Sch.‑Bip.

Annual or biennial herbs, 50–100 cm tall. Stems erect, hirsute‑pubescent throughout. Basal leaves withered at flowering period; leaves in lower part oblanceolate or lanceolate, 5–15 × 0.5–2.5 cm, base attenuate, apex acute, margin coarsely toothed or subentire; middle and upper leaves gradually smaller upward, lanceolate to linear, subentire or shallowly toothed. All leaves pubescent on both surfaces. Capitula 3–5 × 5–8 mm, arranged in large panicle. Involucres urceolate, then widely spreading; phyllaries 3‑seriate, linear‑lanceolate, apex acuminate, greyish green, hirsute, outer ones 2–3 mm, innermost 4 mm, scarious along margin. Receptacle flat. Ray florets numerous, pistillate, corolla tube filiform, 4 mm, bearing minute ligule, pale yellow. Disk florets 5–10, hermaphrodite, pale yellow, narrowly tubular with 5 lobes at apex, 4 mm, upper part minutely ciliate. Cypselae oblong‑oblanceolate, 0.7–1.5 mm, compressed, slightly pubescent, pale brown. Pappus capillary, 4 mm, in 1 series, white to yellowish brown.

Locality: Naturalized and widely distributed in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1900; Y. W. Lam 994; S. Y. Hu & P. P. H. But 23103 (CUHK).
Distribution: Native to S America, widely naturalized in tropical and subtropical regions.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides. Flowering: Feb.–Aug.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Lai Chi Kok, Tai Po, Sha Tin, High Island, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Cotula anthemoides L. 芫荽菊
Sp. Pl. 891. 1753; FHK 185. 1861; FKH 146. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 19(3–4): 204. 1966; FRPS 76(1): 134. 1983; FGD 8: 200, fig. 119. 2007.

Small annual herbs; stem procumbent or decumbent, 4–15 cm or longer, branched and diffuse, glabrous or brownish villose. Leaves alternate, subglabrous or loosely villose on both surfaces, bipinnatisect, primary lateral lobes elliptic‑oblong, about 5 pairs, terminal lobes triangular to lanceolate, shortly acute; basal leaves oblanceolate‑oblong, 3–5 × 1–2 cm; median cauline leaves oblong or elliptic, 1.5–2.5 × 0.7–1.6 cm, base semi‑amplexicaul. Capitula heterogamous and disciform, 4–7 mm across, solitary on branch terminals, axillary, or opposite to leaves; peduncle 5–10 mm. Involucres dish‑like; phyllaries 2‑seriate, oblong, green with a red line on midvein, margin scarious, apex obtuse to rounded; outer layer larger in size, about 2–3 mm; inner layer smaller, 1–1.5 mm. Receptacle flat, naked. Marginal florets pistillate, in many rows, corolla none with the pistils only. Disk florets hermaphrodite, corolla tubular, yellow, 4‑lobed at apex. Cypselae obovate‑oblong, dorsiventrally compressed, 1–1.2 × 0.8 mm, smooth, glandular, margin broadly and thickly winged, base with stalks derived from the receptacle, especially appeared on the outer cypselae. Pappus absent.

Locality: Lai Chi Kok, Tai Po, Sha Tin, High Island, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 243; W. J. Tutcher 9163; S. Y. Hu 12909 (CUHK).
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian; Indochina, India, Pakistan, Africa.
Ecology: Wet places near streams, paddy fields. Flowering: Jul.–Apr. of the following year.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Naturalized and widely distributed in Hong Kong
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Crassocephalum crepidioides (Benth.) S. Moore 野茼蒿
J. Bot. 50: 211. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 19(3 – 4): 205. 1966; FTW ed. 2, 4: 922, pl. 434. 1998; FRPS 77(1): 304, pl. 67: 1–2. 1999; FGD 8: 228, fig. 139. 2007.
Gynura crepidioides Benth., Niger Fl. 438. 1849.

Annual erect herbs; stem 30–100 cm tall, striate, glabrous or pubescent. Leaves elliptic or elliptic‑oblong, 7–13 × 3–5 cm, petiole 1–2(–5.5) cm long, base narrowed to petiole, apex acute or acuminate, margin irregularly serrate or double‑serrate, some lyrately pinnatifid with terminal lobe large ovate‑elliptic, and 1–3 pairs of lateral lobes near base, smaller and elliptic‑oblong, both surfaces glabrous or subglabrous. Capitula homogamous and discoid, several arranged as corymbs at terminal. Involucres cylindric with base swollen, about 9–11 mm long, 5 mm across middle, 6–8 mm across base, calyculate with several linear bracteoles 2 3 mm; phyllaries linear‑lanceolate, 9–11 × 0.7–1.5 mm, abaxial side puberulous, margin scarious, apex acute and with tuft of minute hair. Receptacle flat, alveolate with margin of areoles shortly scarious, areoles elevated at centre. All florets tubular, bisexual and fertile, corolla yellow with limb purplish or reddish brown, or appeared as orange‑red, 8 – 11 mm long, tube filiform and slender, gradually and slightly dilated at summit, apex 5‑lobed; anthers included, base shortly sagittate, apical appendages elongate‑lanceolate; stylar branches exserted, acute apically, papillose hairy. Cypselae cylindric, 2–2.5 mm long, reddish brown to brown, ribbed, puberulent. Pappus bristles copious, capillary and silky, white in colour, 9–10 mm long, easily shed off.

Locality: Naturalized and widely distributed in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 1549; S. Y. Pang & S. L. Wong 302 (CUHK); S. Y. Hu 5453 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian; India, Indochina, Africa.
Ecology: Roadsides, wastelands. Flowering: Nearly all year round.
Uses: Food (vegetable), medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Cape Collinson, Basalt Island. Also cultivated as pot plants
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Crossostephium chinense (L.) Makino 芙蓉菊
Bot. Mag. Tokyo 20: 33. 1906; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 19(3–4): 231. 1966; FRPS 76(1): 131. 1983; FTW ed. 2, 4: 927. 1998; FGD 8: 194, fig. 114. 2007.
Artemisia chinensis L., Sp. Pl. 849. 1753.

Perennial aromatic herbs to subshrubs, 10–40 cm tall, branched in upper portion, branches ascending, densely greyish tomentose, with leaves crowded at shoot apices, the vegetative shoots having very short internodes, the flowering shoots with longer internodes. Leaves fleshy, narrowly spatulate to oblanceolate, 1.5–4 × 0.4–1.2 cm, base cuneate‑attenuate, sessile, entire or 3–5‑lobed near the tip, apex obtuse‑rounded, both surfaces densely covered with greyish lanate and stellate hair. Capitula heterogamous and disciform, subglobose, 7 mm across, in leafy racemose or racemose‑panicle form; peduncle short, 6–15 mm. Involucres hemispherical, 3 × 7 mm, densely lanate; phyllaries in 3 series, herbaceous; outer ones ovate‑deltoid, 1.5–2 mm, obtuse or acute; middle layers elliptic, 2–2.2 mm, scarious margined; inner layers oblong, 2.5–3 mm, with wider scarious margin. Receptacle hemispherical‑conical, areoles irregularly toothed, without palea. Peripherical florets female and fertile, in one row, corolla tubular, 1.5 mm, 2–3‑dentate at apex, glandular‑punctate. Central florets bisexual and fertile, many, corolla tubular, 1.5 mm, 5‑dentate apically, glandular punctate. Cypselae oblong, 0.8–1.5 mm, 5‑costate, glandular. Pappus of scarious crown about 0.2–0.5 mm, toothed along rims.

Locality: Cape Collinson, Basalt Island. Also cultivated as pot plants. Y. S. Lau 1773; F. W. Xing 9234.
Distribution: Distributed in coastal regions of SE China; Indochina, Japan, Philippines.
Ecology: Crevices of rocks near seashore. Flowering: Jul.–Apr. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Dahlia pinnata Cav. 大麗花（洋芍藥）
Icon. 1: 57. 1791; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 19(3 – 4): 232. 1966; FRPS 75: 367. 1979; FGD 8: 129, fig. 65. 2007.

Perennial herbs with large tuberous fleshy roots; stem erect and stout, branched, 0.5–1.5(–2) m tall. Leaves 1– 3‑pinnate, some upper leaves simple; leaflets ovate or ovate‑oblong, both surfaces glabrous. Capitula large, 6–12 cm across, long pedunculate, usually nodding. Involucres hemispherical; outer phyllaries foliaceous, ovate‑elliptic; inner ones scarious, elliptic‑lanceolate. Marginal ligulate florets 1‑seriate or multi‑seriate in some cultivation, neutral, colour various, white, red or purple, ligule ovate, apex entire or minutely 3‑toothed. Central tubular florets many, bisexual and fertile, yellow in colour, apical half of corolla campanulate; some cultivars with all florets ligulate. Cypselae oblong, 9 – 12 × 3–4 mm, black, adaxial side flattened, abaxial side convex, apex rounded, 2 inconspicuous teeth at summit.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. H. Y. Yeung 172 (CUHK).
Distribution: Native to Mexico, cultivated worldwide.
Ecology: Flowering: Aug.–Dec.
Uses: Ornamental.

Dendranthema indicum (L.) Des Moul. 野菊
Actes Soc. Linn. Bordeaux 20: 562. 1855; FRPS 76(1): 32. 1983; Peng, FTW ed. 2, 4: 929. 1998; FGD 8: 195, fig. 115. 2007.
Chrysanthemum indicum L., Sp. Pl. 889. 1753; FHK 184. 1861; FKH 146. 1912.

Perennial herbs with procumbent rhizomes, 25–100 cm tall; stem erect or decumbent, branched, pubescent mainly on upper portion. Basal and lower leaves withered at anthesis; middle cauline leaves ovate or ovate‑elliptic, 3–5 × 2–3.5 cm, leaf base truncate or cuneate, serrate, pinnatilobed to pinnatifid, terminal lobe largest, ovate‑elliptic, obtuse apically, lateral lobes in two pairs, elliptic‑oblong, acute or obtuse, upper surfaces pubescent, lower surfaces glandular and covered with branched T‑typed hair and short straight pubescent hair; petioles 0.5–1.5 cm. Capitula heterogamous and radiate, 1.5–2.5(–3.3) cm in diam., loosely corymbose. Peduncle 1.5–11 cm, densely hairy. Involucres in shallow disciform; phyllaries 4–5‑seriate, herbaceous, hairy, margins scarious and brownish, apex obtuse to rounded; outer ones smaller, ovate, 2–3 mm; median ones ovate, 4–8 mm; innermost ones oblong, 6–10 mm. Marginal ligulate florets yellow, 8–12 ×, 2–3 mm, ligule elliptic‑oblong, apex entire or 2–3‑lobed, tube long and glandular. Disk tubular florets yellow, glandular, 3–3.5 mm, tube lower half narrow, upper half campanulate, 5‑lobed at apex. Cypselae obliquely obovoid‑oblong, 1.5–1.8 mm, 5‑ribbed, brownish black with the ribs pale brown. Pappus absent.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. Y. Yeung 157 (CUHK); S. Y. Hu 12403 (CUHK); Y. S. Lau 1331.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; also in India, Korea, Japan.
Ecology: Grassy hillslopes, thickets. Flowering: Oct.–May of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Dendranthema morifolium (Ramat.) Tzvelev 菊花
Fl. URSS 26: 373. 1961; FRPS 76(1): 35. 1983; FGD 8: 196. 2007.
Chrysanthemum morifolium Ramat., Journ. Hist. Nat. 2: 240. 1792.
Chrysanthemum sinense Sabine, Trans. Linn. Soc. London 14(1): 142, 145 description. 1823.

Perennial herbs, 50–120 cm tall; stem erect, branched on upper portion, usually woody at base, pubescent. Lower and middle cauline leaves ovate, lanceolate or long‑elliptic, 5–8 × 3–5.5 cm, base cuneate, pinnatilobed to pinnatifid, lobes ovate or oblong, apex acute, margin dentate to serrate, abaxial surfaces densely pubescent, adaxial surfaces glabrous or subglabrous, petiolate. Upper leaves obovate or rhomboid. Capitula of many forms and colours, solitary or few as loose corymbs, size various, 2.5–25 cm in diam. Peduncle up to 9 cm, densely pubescent. Involucres shallow‑dish‑like; phyllaries 3–5‑seriate, herbaceous, hairy abaxially, scarious‑margined; outer rows linear‑lanceolate, 5–6 mm, hair denser; median and inner ones oblong to obovate, 8–12 mm, marginal scales broader. Ligulate florets many, oblong or narrowly linear‑oblong, length various, colour yellow, white, pink or purple. Disk tubular florets small, yellow. Cypselae 1.5–3 mm.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 3086; S. Y. Hu & K. H. Yung 112 (CUHK); S. Y. Hu 5507 (CUHK).
Distribution: Native to China; widely cultivated worldwide.
Ecology: Flowering: Oct.–Feb. of the following year.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal (folklore).

Dichrocephala integrifolia (L. f.) Kuntze 魚眼草
Revis. Gen. Pl. 1: 333. 1891; FTW ed. 2, 4: 933. 1998; FGD 8: 192, fig. 111. 2007.
Hippia integrifolia L. f., Suppl. Pl. 389. 1781.
Dichrocephala latifolia DC., Contr. Bot. India 2. 1834; Prodr. 5: 372. 1836; FHK 173. 1861; FKH 140. 1912.
Dichrocephala bicolor (Roth) Schltdl., Linnaea 25: 209. 1852; Li, FTW 4: 847. 1975.
Dichrocephala auriculata (Thunb.) Druce, Rep. Bot. Soc. Exch. Club Brit. Isles 4: 619. 1917; FRPS 74: 77, pl. 25: 1 – 3. 1985.

Annual herbs, 12–40 cm tall. Stems erect or decumbent, usually branched from the basal part, loosely pilose. Leaves ovate to elliptic, sparsely pubescent on both surfaces, those in middle part 2–11 × 1–4.5 cm, lyrately lobed with the terminal lobe largest, up to 4.5 cm across, ovate, 1–2 pairs of lateral lobes, oblong to obovate, base attenuate to form winged petiole of 1–3 cm, apex acute to obtuse, leaf margin irregularly crenate‑serrate; leaves in lower and upper parts smaller in size, but similar in shape, with the lower ones less lobed. Capitula small, 2–3.5 mm across, globose, forming panicles terminal or axillary to the stem. Phyllaries in 1–2 series, ovate‑oblong, apex acute, margin slightly scarious and fimbriate, central part and midvein green in colour, outer phyllaries 1 mm, the inner ones slightly shorter. Receptacle globose with flattened top. Marginal florets in many series, corolla tubular, usually 2‑lobed, 0.3–0.5 mm, white. Disk florets few, corolla tubular, funnelform to campanulate, tetramerous, 1 mm, green. Cypselae obovate‑oblanceolate, compressed, thickened on both sides, glandular at apical region. Pappus lacking, or bearing 1–2 short bristles on cypselae of central florets.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. S. Y. Hu 7620, 9617 (CUHK); Y. W. Lam 517.
Distribution: Areas S of Changjiang; widely distributed in tropical and subtropical Asia and Africa.
Ecology: Abandoned cultivated fields, banks of paddy fields. Flowering: Jan.–May.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Duhaldea cappa (Buch.‑Ham. ex D. Don) Pruski & Anderb 羊耳菊（白牛膽）
Comp. Newsl. 40: 44. 2003.
Inula cappa (Buch.‑Ham. ex D. Don) DC., Prodr. 5: 469, 1836; FHK 180. 1861; FKH 144. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 19(3 – 4): 296. 1966; FRPS 75: 271. 1979; FGD 8: 146. 2007; Check List HK Plants 283. 2002; 97. 2004.
Conyza cappa Buch.‑Ham. ex D. Don, Prodr. Fl. Nepal. 176. 1825.

Perennial herbs or subshrubs; stem erect, 50–100(–200) cm high, densely covered with brownish sericeous hair throughout. Lower leaves withered at anthesis, remaining the axillary buds; middle and upper leaves elliptic‑oblong, 3–11 cm long, 1.5–4 cm wide, with upper ones smaller in size, base rounded to subcuneate, apex acute to obtuse, margin with small curved teeth, scabrous above, with dense and thick layer of greyish white silky hair beneath, pinnately veined with those on lower surfaces prominent, subsessile or shortly petiolate, not longer than 5 mm. Capitula in terminal corymbose panicle. Involucres 5–7(–8) mm long, 4–5 mm across, campanulate; phyllaries 5‑seriate, apex acute, outer ones ovate‑lanceolate, 1.5–2 mm long, herbaceous, densely brownish hairy throughout the abaxial side; changing gradually inward in shape, sizes, texture with the innermost being linear‑lanceolate, 5–6 mm long, scarious, hairy only at base and along the midvein. Florets yellow, marginal ones female, corolla narrowly tubular, 3–4 mm long, apex 3–4‑lobed and glandular. Disk florets hermaphrodite, corolla tubular, 4.5 –6 mm long, apex 5 triangular lobes and glandular. Cypselae cylindric, 1.5–1.8 mm long, silky hairy and about 10‑ribbed. Pappus 4–5 mm long, persistent.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 1815; H. Y. Yueng 150 (CUHK); S. Y. Hu 12406 (CUHK).
Distribution: Widely distributed in E to S & SW China; Vietnam, Thailand, Myanmar, India, Malaysia.
Ecology: Wastelands and thickets. Flowering: Aug.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Eclipta prostrata (L.) L. 鱧腸
Mant. Pl. 2: 286. 1771; FHK 181, 1861; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 19(3–4): 241. 1966; FRPS 75: 344, pl. 58: 1–5. 1979; FTW ed. 2, 4: 935. 1998.
Verbesina prostrata L., Sp. Pl. 2: 902. 1753.
Eclipta alba (L.) Haask., Pl. Jav. Rar. 528. 1848; FHK 181. 1861; FKH 145. 1912.
Verbesina alba L., Sp. Pl. 2: 902. 1753.

Annual herbs; stems erect, ascending or prostrate, 8–70 cm tall, branched mainly at the bottom, covered with adpressed strigose hair throughout. Leaves opposite, subsessile or shortly petiolate, lanceolate or elliptic, 2–6.5 × 0.3–1.8 cm, base narrowed, apex acute‑acuminate, margin serrulate or sometimes slightly undulate, strigose on both surfaces. Capitula 6–8 mm across when flowering, enlarged to 10 mm in fruiting stage. Involucres hemispherical; phyllaries green, herbaceous, in 2 series, lanceolate‑oblong, 3–4 × 1.5–2 mm, outer ones slightly longer, apex acute, abaxial surfaces strigose. Receptacle convex, paleate; paleae 1.8–2.2 mm, linear, hairy at distal half. Marginal ligulate florets 2‑seriate, corolla white, tube 0.8–1 mm, ligule 1.6–1.8 mm, bifid or entire. Disk tubular florets many, corolla white, 1.3–1.5 mm, 4‑cleft at apex; anther bases sagittate and acute, apical appendages rounded; stylar branches flattened, apex obtuse, outer surfaces papillose. Cypselae brown, oblong, 2.5–2.8 × 1.3–1.5 mm, laterally compressed with those developed from female florets showing slightly 3‑angled in cross‑section, those from bisexual florets slightly 4‑angled, apex truncate, tuberculate on two surfaces, ribbed on lateral margins, glabrous, Pappus none or of few short teeth.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1984; S. Y. Hu 5289 (CUHK); S. L. Thrower 473 (CUHK).
Distribution: Spread over most provinces of China; widely distributed in tropical and subtropical regions.
Ecology: Streamsides, banks of paddy fields, roadsides and other wet places. Flowering: Jun.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Elephantopus scaber L. 地膽草
Sp. Pl. 814. 1753; FHK 170. 1861; FKH 139. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 19(3–4): 242. 1966; FRPS 74: 43. 1985; FTW ed. 2, 4: 938. 1998; FGD 8: 237, fig. 145. 2007.

Erect perennial herbs 15–50 cm tall; stem terete, branched dichotomously at upper portion, strigose and glandular throughout. Radical leaves remained at anthesis, rosulate in arrangement, oblanceolate to spatulate in shape, 5.5– 20 × 1.5–3 cm, base attenuate, apex obtuse or rounded, with a mucro, margin shallowly and irregularly crenate‑serrulate, strigose on both surfaces, and glandular abaxially, lateral pinnate veins 16–17 on each side of the midvein; cauline leaves few, scattered, oblanceolate to oblong, smaller in size, about 1–10 × 0.4–1.2 cm, sessile, strigose on both surfaces, glandular abaxially. Glomerules all stalked, the stalks 2–10 mm; each surrounded by 3 broadly ovate bracts, foliaceous, 6–10 × 10–12 mm, acute and mucronate at apex, shallowly serrulate along margin, densely hairy, glandular, strongly reticulate. Involucres cylindric‑oblong, phyllaries coriaceous, basal white, apical green or tinged purple, hairy and glandular, 2‑seriate; outer 4 involucral bracts lanceolate‑oblong, 4–5 mm, apex long‑acuminate; inner 4 elliptic‑oblong, 8–9 mm, twice longer than the outer ones, apex spinulose. Florets 4 per capitulum, 7 mm; corolla lobes purple, about 2 mm. Cypselae brown, 4 mm, apex truncate, basal portion gradually narrowed, strongly 10‑ribbed and grooved, puberulent and glandular. Pappus setae 5(6 – 8), stiff, purple, 4–5 mm, dilated and scaly at base, persistent.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. K. Y. Chan 1218 (CUHK); S. Y. Hu 11033 (CUHK); L. T. Lo 555.
Distribution: S, SW & E China; Asia, America and tropical regions of Africa.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides. Flowering: Jul.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Elephantopus tomentosus L. 白花地膽草
Sp. Pl. 814. 1753; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 19(3–4): 242. 1966; FRPS 74: 45. 1985; FGD 8: 238. 2007.
Elephantopus mollis Kunth, Nov. Gen. Sp. 4: 26. 1820; FTW ed. 2, 4: 938. 1998.

Perennial erect herbs 70–100 cm tall; stems striate; branches many on upper portion, strigose to hirsute, glandular. Basal leaves rosulate, deteriorate before anthesis; lower and middle cauline leaves numerous, obovate‑oblong, 5–17 × 2.5–5.5 cm, base attenuate to form winged petiole, subamplexicaul, apex acute, margin crenate‑serrate, lateral pinnate veins 10–12, pilose and glandular on both surfaces; upper cauline leaves elliptic‑oblong, 3–6 × 1–2 cm, or much smaller upward, subsessile, acute at apex. Capitula sessile and clustered into glomerules, each glomerule subtended with stalk 1–7 cm; and surrounded by 3 broadly ovate‑cordate foliaceous bracts, 8–18 × 8–12 mm, acute and awned at apex, strongly reticulate, serrulate, hairy and glandular. Involucres cylindric‑oblong; phyllaries scarious, hairy and glandular at distal half, in 2 series, each layer with 4 involucral bracts; outer series shorter, 3–4 mm, lanceolate‑oblong, apex long‑acuminate, green near the tip, 1‑veined at the middle; inner ones oblong, twice longer than the outer ones, 6–7 mm, upper half green, awned‑tip. Florets 4 per capitulum, corolla white, 3–4 mm, funnelform, tube slender, glabrous. Cypselae brown, linear‑oblong, 2.5–3 mm, 10‑ribbed, apex truncate, base gradually narrowed, puberulent. Pappus 5 stiff setae, 4 mm, dilated and scaly at base, persistent.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 2224; S. L. Thrower 472 (CUHK); S. Y. Hu 11726 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian, Taiwan; tropical regions.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides. Flowering: Mar.–Sep.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Pat Sin Leng, Ma On Shan, Sha Tau Kok, Wu Kau Tang, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Emilia prenanthoidea DC. 小一點紅
Prodr. 6: 302. 1838; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 19(3–4): 243. 1966; FRPS 77(1): 325. 1999.

Annual herbs; stem erect or ascending, 20–80 cm tall, somewhat glaucous, glabrous or loosely pubescent. Basal leaves small, obovate or obovate‑oblong, 3–8 × 1–3 cm, base attenuate into long winged petiole, apex obtuse to rounded, margin entire or loosely toothed. Middle cauline leaves oblong to linear‑oblong, 2.5–8 × 0.5–1.2 cm, sessile and amplexicaul, base sagittate or auriculate, apex obtuse or acute, margin slightly sinuate toothed, adaxial surface green, abaxial surface purplish, both glabrous or sparsely crisped hairy. Upper leaves linear‑lanceolate, smaller in size. Capitula homogamous and discoid, 1–1.5 cm across, loosely corymbose; peduncles (0.5–)2– 10.5 cm. Involucres cylindric or narrowly campanulate, shorter than florets, which only enclosing lower 1/2 to 2/3 of the florets, base without calyculus; phyllaries about 10 in 1 row, linear‑oblong, 6–8 × 1–2 mm, apex acute or obtuse, margin scarious, abaxial side glabrous. All florets hermaphrodite and fertile, corolla tubular, 8–11 mm, lower half filiform, upper half gradually widen, apex with 5 linear‑lanceolate lobes about 2 mm in length, colour red, pink or purple‑pink. Cypselae brown, cylindric, 3 × 0.5 mm, ribbed, glabrous. Pappus copious, capillary and slender, white, 4–5 mm.

Locality: Pat Sin Leng, Ma On Shan, Sha Tau Kok, Wu Kau Tang, Lantau Island. H. C. Tang 1251; S. Y. Hu 11808 (CUHK); S. Y. Hu & P. P. H. But 22134 (CUHK).
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Zhejiang, Fujian; Indochina to India.
Ecology: Wastelands, margins of cultivated lands. Flowering: Apr.–Nov.

Emilia sonchifolia (L.) DC. 一點紅
Contr. Bot. India 24. 1834; Prodr. 6: 302. 1838; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 19(3–4): 244. 1966; FRPS 77(1): 324, pl. 68: 1–2. 1999; FGD 8: 230, fig. 140. 2007.
Senecio sonchifolia (L.) Moench., Suppl. Meth. 231. 1802; FHK 189. 1861.
Cacalia sonchifolia L., Sp. Pl. 2: 835. 1753.

Annual herbs; stem erect or ascending, 15–40 cm tall, branched near base, glaucous, glabrous or loosely pilose. Leaves mainly clustered at base and lower stem portion, adaxial surfaces green, abaxial surfaces purplish, both subglabrous or sparsely crisped hairy. Basal and lower leaves lyrately pinnati‑lobed, 4.5–11 × 2–6 cm, terminal lobes large, broadly ovate‑deltoid to ovate‑cordate, base semi‑ or totally amplexicaul, for the leaves growing near the middle stem portion having base hastately amplexicaul, apex broadly obtuse or nearly rounded, margin irregularly dentate, midvein below thinly to broadly winged, lateral lobes usually in 1 pair, small triangular, oblong to lanceolate‑oblong, obtuse or acute, sometimes the lateral lobes inconspicuous and even absent in the lowermost leaves, resembling as long winged petiole. Uppermost leaves linear‑lanceolate or lanceolate, 3.5–6 cm, base sessile and amplexicaul, apex acute, margin subentire to irregularly toothed. Capitula homogamous and discoid, 3 – 5 mm across, pendulous before flowering, erect later, non‑calyculate, usually with 2–5 heads arranged as loose corymbs, pedunculate with length of peduncles 2–14 cm. Involucres cylindric with base swollen, 10 – 13 × 3 – 3.5 mm, length subequal to florets or enclosing 5/6 of the florets; phyllaries about 8 in 1 series, linear, apex acute, herbaceous green, margin narrowly scarious, glabrous abaxially. Florets pink or pale purple, 8–11 mm, corolla filiform‑tubular with limb gradually and slightly widen, apex 5 linear‑oblong lobes about 2 mm. Cypselae brown, subterete, 3–3.5 × 0.5 mm, 5‑angulate, puberulent along ribs. Pappus copious, white, capillary and slender, 7–8 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 2253; Y. Wong 011 (CUHK); S. Y. Hu & P. P. H. But 22274 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; tropical Asia and Africa.
Ecology: Wastelands, margins of cultivated lands. Flowering: Nearly all year round.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Fanling, Sha Tin, Tsim Bei Tsui, Pak Shek Kok, Ho Pui, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Epaltes australis Less. 球菊（鵝不食草）
Linnaea 5: 148. 1831; FKH 143. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 19(3 – 4): 245. 1966; FRPS 75: 56. 1979; FTW ed. 2, 4: 942. 1998; FGD 8: 166, fig. 92. 2007.
Sphaeromorphaea australis (Less.) Kitam., Acta Phytotax. Geobot. 6(2): 80. 1937.

Annual herbs; stem 7–30 cm, prostrate, branched at base, shallowly striate, loosely pilose. Leaves sessile, obovate to oblanceolate, 1–4 × 0.3–1.5 cm, base attenuate, apex obtuse to rounded, margin irregularly dentate, both surfaces sparsely pilose and pitted. Capitula many, growing laterally, subsessile or shortly pedunculate, globose first and then become broader. Involucres hemispherical, 4–5 mm across; phyllaries 4‑seriate, green, scarious; outer 2 layers ovate to obovate, 1–2 mm, apex rounded; inner 2 layers obovate‑oblong, 2–2.5 mm, obtuse. Receptacle slightly convex, glabrous. Outer pistillate florets numerous, fertile, corolla tubular, 1 mm, distally narrowed and with apex minutely 3‑lobed, bottom inflated, loosely glandular; stylar branches blunt and exserted. Central bisexual florets fewer, functionally staminate, corolla tubular, campanulate, 1.2 mm, apex 4 triangular and obtuse lobes, pale purple to pink in colour, slightly glandular; stamens 4. Cypselae of outer female florets obovoid‑oblong, 1 mm, 10‑ribbed, apex truncate, base narrowed and hairy, glandular. Those of disk florets similar but empty. Pappus absent.

Locality: Fanling, Sha Tin, Tsim Bei Tsui, Pak Shek Kok, Ho Pui, Lantau Island. Y. W. Lam 670; S. Y. Hu 11888, 12521 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Thailand, Indochina, Malaysia, Australia.
Ecology: Moist places of abandoned lands. Flowering: Mar.–Jun.

Erechtites valerianifolius (Link ex Spreng.) DC. 裂葉芹菊（菊芹）
Prodr. 6: 295. 1838; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 19(3–4): 247. 1966; FTW ed. 2, 4: 944, photo 447. 1998; FRPS 77(1): 307. 1999; FGD 8: 231. 2007.
Senecio valerianifolius Link ex Spreng., Syst. Veg. 3: 565. 1826.

Annual herbs; stem stout and erect, 50–150 cm tall, striate, branched in upper portion or not branched, glabrous. Leaves oblong or elliptic, 3.5–13 × 1.5–10 cm, base narrowed down to form winged petiole 1.5–9 cm, pinnately lobed, the terminal portion pinnatifid with lobes large, ovate‑elliptic, lower portion pinnatisect with 5–8 pairs of lanceolate‑oblong lateral lobes, smaller and narrower than the terminal ones, apex acuminate, margin double serrate or irregularly lobed; leaves pinnately‑veined, glabrous above and beneath. Upper leaves similar but smaller in size. Capitula erect or nodding, arranged as paniculate corymbs at stem terminal. Involucres cylindric‑campanulate with base swollen, 7–8 mm high, 3–4 mm across middle, 4–5 mm across base, calyculate; phyllaries 12–14 in one series, linear, 7–8 × 0.8–1 mm, acute or acuminate, herbaceous with margin scarious, abaxial side glabrous or loosely puberulent. Receptacle flat or slightly concave, alveolate with areoles elevated at centre. Florets many, pale yellowish purple in colour. Marginal ones 1–2 rows, female and fertile, corolla filiform‑tubular, 7–9 mm, apex 5‑toothed. Disk florets hermaphrodite and fertile, corolla narrow and long tubular, 9 mm, with distal 1–1.5 mm as funnelform, apex 5‑lobed and papillose. Cypselae cylindric, 3–4 mm, 10– 12‑ribbed, grooves brown and puberulent, ribs pale brown. Pappus bristles copious, fine and slender, white at base and tinged purplish red on upper part, subequal in length with the florets.

Locality: Naturalized. H. Y. Yeung 550 (CUHK); Y. W. Lam 559; P. S. Choi 479.
Distribution: Native to Brazil; widely distributed in the tropics.
Ecology: Margins of forests, wastelands. Flowering: May–Jun.
Notes: The species was reported as Erechtites valerianaefolia (Wolf) DC. previously (Check List HK Plants 96. 2004).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Cultivated and naturalized in Hong Kong
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Erigeron karvinskianus DC. 加勒比飛蓬
Prodr. 5: 285. 1836; C. M. Hu, Check List HK Plants 281. 2002.

Perennial herbs or subshrubs 30–50 cm tall; stems slender, many‑branched, growth of branches terminated by two capitula. Leaves dimorphous, sparsely pilose; those on vegetative shoots trilobed, ovate‑rhombic in outline, 1.5–3.5 cm × 5–15 mm, base cuneate, lobes ovate, entire, acute; upper cauline leaves narrowly elliptic, 1–2 cm × 2 – 5 mm, both ends acute. Capitula heterogamous, radiate, solitary or in a loose panicle. Involucre campanulate, 5 mm across; phyllaries 3‑seriate, herbaceous, lanceolate, 2–4 mm, the outer ones shorter. Receptacles flat, smooth, areoles inconspicuous, the attachments of ovaries each marked by a conic elevation and a fibrous remains of vascular tissue. Marginal ligulate florets white, turning purplish pink after anthesis, slightly over 40, 2‑seriate, neuter, ligules 5.5 × 1 mm, 3‑lobed, tube 1.5 mm, stylar branches exserted. Central tubular florets yellow, numerous, hermaphrodite, corolla 5‑lobed; stamens 5, anther bases obtuse, apical appendages ovate, acute; style appendages rounded or obtuse. Achenes brown, compressed‑oblong, 1.4 mm, sparsely pilose, base with a white spongy ring, each side with a stout rib, apex truncate, apiculate at center. Pappus 2‑seriate, with short scarious ones alternate with capillary bristles.

Locality: Cultivated and naturalized in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1239; S. Y. Hu 7197, 13245 (CUHK).
Distribution: Guangdong; native to Mexico and Panama.
Ecology: Cultivated or naturalized, usually found in wastelands. Flowering: Feb.–Oct.
Uses: Ornamental.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): San Wai, Tai Mo Shan, Lai Chi Wo, Shing Mun Reservoir, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Eupatorium chinense L. 華澤蘭
Sp. Pl. 837: 1753; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 19(3 – 4): 255. 1966; FRPS 74: 63, pl. 21: 4–6. 1985; FGD 8: 213. 2007.
Eupatorium reevesii Wall. ex DC., Prodr. 5: 179. 1836; FHK 171. 1861; FKH 140. 1912.

Perennial herbs, 70–100 cm tall; stem herbaceous or woody at base, striate, many‑branched, pubescent to tomentose. Leaves sessile or with short petiole (2–4 mm), ovate, base rounded, apex acute or acuminate, margin regularly crenate‑serrate, pinnately‑veined, scabrid and sparsely glandular adaxially, densely yellow glandular‑punctate abaxially; lower leaves usually withered at flowering stage, those on upper portion 3.5–5.5 × 2–3 cm. Capitula arranged in a loose corymb, with 1–2 ovate prophylls. Involucres cylindric‑oblong, 4.5–5 mm; phyllaries 2–3‑seriate, imbricate, apex obtuse or rounded; outer shorter ones ovate to ovate‑lanceolate, 1–2 mm, hairy and glandular; middle and inner longer ones lanceolate‑oblong or oblong, length increases inward, 5–6 mm, loosely hairy and glandular, apex and margin white and scarious. Receptacle small. Florets 5 per capitulum, corolla white, pink or red, 3–4 mm, apical half slightly broadened, 5 deltoid lobes, glandular; anther apical appendages triangular, acute; stylar branches 2.5–3 mm, slender, papillose. Cypselae cylindric‑oblong, pentagonous, 2 mm, base acute, blackish brown, slightly hairy, glandular. Pappus 3–4 mm, nearly equal to length of corolla.

Locality: San Wai, Tai Mo Shan, Lai Chi Wo, Shing Mun Reservoir, Lantau Island. K. Y. Chan 1260 (CUHK); S. Y. Hu 12435 (CUHK); Y. S. Lau 1321.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou, Sichuan, Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian.
Ecology: Thickets, grassy banks. Flowering: Jun.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Aberdeen, Mount Gough, Tai Mo Shan, Tai Po, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Eupatorium japonicum Thunb. 白頭婆
Fl. Jap. 307. 1784; FKH 139. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 19(3 – 4): 257. 1966; FRPS 74: 60. 1985; FGD 8: 213, fig. 125. 2007.
Eupatorium wallichii DC., Prodr. 5: 179. 1836; FHK 172. 1861.

Perennial herbs or subshrubs, 60–200 cm tall. Stem erect, few‑branched, pubescent, hair multicellular and kinky, those on peduncles much denser, but appearing looser or glabrescent on lower portion of stem. Petioles 0.5–2 cm, densely pubescent. Middle leaf blade long‑elliptic to lanceolate, 6–14 × 2.5–5 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, with 6–7 pairs of pinnate veins, both surfaces yellow punctate, pubescent or pilose, hair denser on midveins, veins and along margins, sharply serrate or double serrate; upper and lower leaves smaller in size, basal leaves withered at anthesis. Capitula arranged in tight corymb. Involucres cylindric‑oblong, 5–6 mm; phyllaries 3‑seriate, green or tinged red, apex obtuse or rounded; outer ones 2 mm, ovate; middle and inner layers 4–6 mm, long‑elliptic to oblong. Florets 5 per capitulum, corolla white, pink or purple, 4.5–5 mm, shallowly 5‑lobed, lobes about 0.5 mm; stylar branches 3–4 mm. Cypselae pale blackish brown, elliptic‑oblong, 3–4 mm, 5‑ribbed, glabrous, glandular. Pappus white, 4–5 mm, shorter than corolla.

Locality: Aberdeen, Mount Gough, Tai Mo Shan, Tai Po, Lantau Island. L. T. Lo 427; Y. S. Lau 1291.
Distribution: Area S of Huanghe; Japan, Korea.
Ecology: Thickets on hillslopes, wastelands. Flowering: Aug.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Victoria Peak, Sai Kung, Ma On Shan, Pat Sin Leng, Kau To Hang, Ping Chau, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Eupatorium lindleyanum DC. 林澤蘭
Prodr. 5: 180. 1836; FHK 172. 1861; FKH 139. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 19(3–4): 259. 1966; FRPS 74: 59. 1985; FTW ed. 2, 4: 960. 1998; FGD 8: 212. 2007.

Perennial erect herbs 50–150 cm tall, annual flowering stem solitary, emerging from the caudex, the leafy portion 1.5–4 mm across, striate, densely pubescent or pilose, hair multicellular. Lower leaves withered at anthesis; middle ones sessile or with very short petiole (3–5 mm), trinerved, linear‑lanceolate or lanceolate, 3–9 × 0.5–2 cm, base cuneate, apex acute, margin serrate or coarsely serrate, scabrid or pilose on both surfaces, densely glandular punctate abaxially; upper leaves smaller and narrower. Capitula form tight corymb at terminal, with 1–3 ovate prophylls at the distal end. Involucres 4–6 mm, cylindric‑campanulate; phyllaries about 10, arranged in 2– 3 series, imbricate, green at basal portion, straw‑coloured at apex and along margin, glandular, apex acute or acuminate; outermost ovate, 1–2 mm; median and inner ones oblong‑lanceolate to oblong, length increases inward, 5–6 mm. Receptacle small. Florets white, pink or purplish‑red, 5 per capitulum, corolla 3.5–4.5 mm, glandular, apical half broadened, bearing 5 deltoid lobes; anther apical appendages triangular, acute or obtuse; stylar branches 2 mm long, papillose. Cypselae cylindric oblong, pentagonous, 2.5 mm, brownish black, glandular; pappus 4 mm, white, persistent.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Sai Kung, Ma On Shan, Pat Sin Leng, Kau To Hang, Ping Chau, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 2614; P. S. Choi 455; S. Y. Hu 11024 (CUHK).
Distribution: Widely distributed in China except Xinjiang.
Ecology: Grassy hillslopes, margins of forests or in thickets. Flowering: May–Dec.

Eupatorium odoratum L. 飛機草
Syst. Nat. ed. 10, 2: 1205. 1759; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 19(3–4): 260. 1966; FRPS 74: 56. 1985; FGD 8: 211. 2007.
Chromolaena odorata (L.) R. M. King & H. Rob., Phytologia 20(3): 204. 1970.

Perennial herbs, 1–3 m tall, with sprawling rhizomes; stem erect, densely pubescent or tomentose, branches opposite, growing horizontally and perpendicular to the main axis. Leaves ovate or ovate‑deltoid, 4–10 × 1.5–5 cm, base broadly cuneate or truncate, apex acuminate, densely pilose on both surfaces, glandular abaxially, prominently trinerved, margin sparsely dentate, subentire towards apex; petioles 1–2 cm. Capitula in loose corymbs. Involucres cylindric, 7–10 × 3–4 mm; phyllaries 4–5‑seriate, imbricate, straw‑coloured with 3 conspicuous parallel green veines and scarious margin; outer ones ovate, 1.8–2 mm, puberulent, apex obtuse; median and inner ones narrowly oblong, length increases inward, 7–8 mm, apex obtuse to acute. Receptacle flat to slightly convex. Florets 25–30 per capitulum, corolla pink or white, 4–5 mm, 5‑lobed; stylar branches 5 mm. Cypselae blackish brown, 3–4 mm, 5‑ribbed, pilosulose along ribs; pappus capillary, subequal to corolla in length.

Locality: Naturalized. Y. W. Lam 2273; HK sheet 38396; C. P. Lau 064 (CUHK).
Distribution: Native to America, widely naturalized in tropical and subtropical regions.
Ecology: Wastelands. Flowering: Apr.–Dec.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Pok Fu Lam, Tai Mo Shan, Sai Kung, Sunset Peak and Lantau Peak
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Farfugium japonicum (L.) Kitam. 大吳風草
Acta Phytotax. Geobot. 8(4): 268. 1939; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 19(3 – 4): 262. 1966; FRPS 77(2): 1, pl. 1. 1989; FTW ed. 2, 4: 964, pl. 457, photo 453. 1998.
Tussilago japonica L., Mant. Pl. 1: 113. 1767.

Perennial herbs, the scapes, leaves, petioles, peduncles and phyllaries slightly to densely covered with greyish brown woolly hair especially when in young stage, later glabrescent; stem scapose, 25–70 cm tall, lanate hair much denser at base. Leaves mainly radical and in rosette, reniform, 3–10 × 4–20 cm, margin mucronulate‑dentate to broadly sinuate‑dentate, base cordate, apex rounded; petiole 6 – 28 cm with base dilated. Cauline leaves absent, or with few appeared as bracts, oblong or linear‑lanceolate, 1–2(–6) cm. Capitula heterogamous and radiate, 2–7 arranged as corymbs; peduncle 3–12 cm. Involucres broadly campanulate to turbinate; phyllaries 12–14 in 1 series, oblong, 10–15 × 2–2.5 mm, apex acuminate, abaxial side puberulent to lanate, margin scarious. Bracteoles narrowly lanceolate, 4–7 mm. Marginal pistillate florets 8–12, corolla ligulate, yellow, ligule oblong, 1.5–1.8 × 0.3–0.4 cm, 2‑lobed at apex, tube 7–10 mm. Disk bisexual florets many, corolla tubular, 11–12 mm, lower half narrow, upper half broaden as campanulate form, apex with 5 acute and lanceolate‑oblong lobes about 1.5 – 2 mm; anther tubes conspicuously exserted, base sagittate, apical appendages lanceolate‑oblong; stylar branches roughened on abaxial side, truncate and penicillate at distal ends. Cypselae cylindric, 3–6 mm, ribbed and villous, brown. Pappus white, unequal in length, 8–13 mm.

Locality: Pok Fu Lam, Tai Mo Shan, Sai Kung, Sunset Peak and Lantau Peak. H. Y. Yeung 160 (CUHK); S. Y. Hu 8295 (CUHK); L. T. Lo 326.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Hubei, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan.
Ecology: Forests, ravines. Flowering: Aug.–Dec.

Gaillardia pulchella Foug. 天人菊
Mém. Acad. Sci. Paris 1786: 5, t. 1. 1788; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 19(3–4): 265. 1966; FRPS 75: 390. 1979.

Annual herbs 20–60 cm tall, with ascending branches at upper half, pubescent. Lower leaves spatulate to oblanceolate, 5–10 × 1–2 cm, pinnatifid lobed, lobes obtuse to rounded, leaf base narrowed to stem, sessile, adaxial surfaces loosely pilose, abaxial surfaces densely hispid; upper leaves narrowly oblong, oblanceolate to spatulate, 3–10 cm, entire or loosely serrate or shallowly 3‑lobed, sessile or subamplexicaul. Capitula 2.5–6 cm across, terminal to branches and with long peduncles. Involucres with lanceolate phyllaries, foliaceous, acuminate at apex, ciliate along margin, densely pilose on abaxial side especially near the base, glandular. Marginal ligulate florets with ligule obovate to broad cuneate, and acutely 2–3‑toothed at apex, 1–2 × 1.5 cm, yellow at tip and purple at base, or yellow‑tipped and red‑based, hairy on tube. Central tubular florets yellow, red to dark purple, hairy, apex 5‑lobed, acuminate and caudate. Cypselae 2 mm, with long hair at base. Pappus scales stiff, ovate and long‑aristate, 5 mm, straw‑coloured.

Locality: Cultivated. S. Y. Hu 7094, 13663 (CUHK).
Distribution: Native to USA, cultivated worldwide.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Sep.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: Another species Gaillardia aristata Pursh. was also recorded previously in cultivation (Check List HK Plants 96. 2004). Native to America, this perennial species differs in leaves being basal and cauline, ray florets yellow, and receptacular setae of 3–6 mm long.

Galinsoga parviflora Cav. 牛膝菊
Icon. 3(2): 41, pl. 281. 1795; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 19(3 – 4): 267. 1966; FRPS 75: 384, pl. 66: 5–8. 1979; FTW ed. 2, 4: 967. 1998.

Annual herbs 10–70 cm tall; stem branched especially near the bottom, subglabrous below, pilose and stipitate glandular in upper portion. Leaves opposite; petioles 0.3–1.5 cm; leaf blade ovate, 1.8–4.8 × 0.4–3.4 cm, gradually smaller when growing upward, base rounded or cuneate, apex acute, both surfaces pilose, hair multicellular, denser along margin and veins, margin shallowly serrate or undulate‑serrate, sometimes entire. Capitula radiate, heterogamous, arranged as loose corymbs at terminal. Peduncles 1–2.5 cm, densely pilose and stipitate glandular. Involucres hemispherical, 3–4 mm across; phyllaries 1–2‑seriate; outer ones smaller, ovate, 2–2.5 × 1–1.2 mm, puberulent; inner ones ovate‑oblong, 3 × 2 mm, glabrous on abaxial surface; both membranous, ciliate along margin, and with obtuse apices. Receptacle conical, usually with phyllaries shed off upon fruiting stage. Paleae oblanceolate‑oblong, acute, about 3 × 1 mm, ciliate along margin especially at apical half. Marginal ligulate florets 5, female, white, 2.3–2.5 mm, ligule suborbicular with apex deeply 3‑lobed, lobes obtuse, corolla tube elongate and densely pilose. Disk tubular florets many, bisexual, yellow, 1–1.5 mm, densely pubescent on lower part, apex 5 deltoid lobes. Cypselae black or blackish brown, obovate‑oblong to obovate‑deltoid, 1.5–2 mm, 3‑ribbed or those developed from disk florets 4–5‑ribbed, pubescent. Pappus scarious, white, linear‑lanceolate, unequal in length with about 0.5–1.2 mm, apex aristate, margin fimbriate.

Locality: Naturalized. Y. S. Lau 3055; S. Y. Hu 9437; HK sheet 38970.
Distribution: Native to S America, widely naturalized in tropical and subtropical regions.
Ecology: Wastelands, margins of farmlands. Flowering & fruiting: Nearly all year round.

Gerbera jamesonii Bolus 非洲菊（扶郎花）
Gard. Chron. 1: 772. fig. 122. 1889; et ex Hook. f., Bot. Mag. t. 7087. 1889; FRPS 79: 96. 1996; FGD 8: 247. 2007.

Perennial herbs. Scape 15–50 cm tall, without scaly leaves on it, tomentose, hair longer and denser upward. Leaves all radical, in rosette arrangement, elliptic to oblong, 8–25 × 5–10 cm, base attenuate, apex obtuse to rounded, margin coarsely dentate or irregularly pinnatilobed, upper surfaces pubescent, lower surfaces pubescent‑tomentose, or glabrescent when aged, midvein prominent, lateral veins 4–7 pairs; petiole 3–25 cm, striate, hairy. Capitula solitary, terminal to scape, 5–10 cm across at anthesis. Involucres campanulate; phyllaries in 3–4 rows, apex long‑acute; outer ones linear or subulate, 4–7 × 0.5–1 mm, densely pubescent‑tomentose; middle ones lanceolate, 8–12 × 1–2 mm, pubescent‑tomentose, margin scarious; inner ones lanceolate‑oblong, 12–14 × 2 mm, scarious, abaxial side loosely pubescent or glabrous. Receptacle flat, glabrous, alveolate. Marginal florets 2‑seriate, the outermost florets colour various, pale red, purple‑red, orange‑red, orange to yellow, corolla ligulate‑bilabiate, ligule elongate‑oblong with length 2.5–3.5 cm, width 2–4 mm, apex 2–3‑lobed, the opposite lip 6–10 mm, deeply cut into 2 filiform segments, lower tube 2–3 mm, about 1/8 of the ligule, staminodes linear, slightly exserted; style conspicuously exserted, minutely branched. Inner female florets shorter, outer lip 6–7 mm, 2–3‑toothed, inner lip 4–5 mm, deeply cleft into 2 linear segments, lower tube 3–4 mm; staminodes linear, stylar branches tiny. Central florets numerous, corolla bilabiate, total 8–9 mm, inner lip deeply 2‑cleft; anther bases caudate, apical appendages subtruncate‑oblong; style usually hidden in anther tube, branches short, less than 1 mm, apex obtuse. Cypselae cylindric‑fusiform, 4–5 mm, densely pubescent. Pappus 6–7 mm, greyish white, or orange‑brown after dried.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 428; H. Y. Yeung 101 (CUHK); S. Y. Hu 6385 (CUHK).
Distribution: Native to Africa, cultivated elsewhere.
Ecology: Flowering: Winter to spring of the following year.
Uses: Ornamental.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Clear Water Bay, Ma On Shan, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island, Ping Chau
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Gerbera piloselloides (L.) Cass. 毛大丁草
Dict. Sci. Nat. 18: 461. 1820; FHK 191. 1861; FKH 149. 1912; FRPS 79: 94. 1996; FGD 8: 246. 2007.
Arnica piloselloides L., Pl. Rar. Afr. 22. 1760.
Piloselloides hirsuta (Forsk.) C. Jeffrey, Kew Bull. 21: 218. 1967.

Perennial herbs; stem scapose, 20–60 cm tall, usually without bract‑like leaves, or occasionally have one, densely tomentose, hair denser upward. Leaves radical and rosulate, obovate, obovate‑oblong or oblong, 5–15 × 1.8–6 cm, base attenuate or obtuse, apex rounded, margin entire and densely hairy, adaxial surfaces pubescent, or glabrescent when aged, abaxial side densely white arachnoid‑tomentose, midvein prominent on lower side, lateral veins 6–9 pairs; petioles 1–8.5 cm, densely tomentose. Capitula solitary to scape terminal, 2.5–4 cm across. Involucres tubular; phyllaries 2‑seriate, linear or linear‑lanceolate, apex acute, abaxial side densely brownish tomentose; outer ones 6–10 × 1–1.3 mm; inner ones 12–16 × 1.5–2 mm, margin scarious. Receptacle naked, alveolate. Marginal florets female, in 2 rows, outermost one with corolla ligulate‑bilabiate, 14–15 mm, outer lip ligule‑form, white adaxially, purple or purple‑pink abaxially, oblanceolate or spatulate‑oblong, 8–10 mm, apex faintly 3‑toothed; opposite lip 4–5 mm, deeply divided into 2 filiform segments; lower tube about 6 mm in length; style minutely branched. Inner female florets about 10 mm, outer lip nearly as long as inner lip, about 3 – 5 mm, outer lip minutely 3‑toothed, inner lip 2‑cleft; lower tube 5 mm; style shortly branched. Central florets bisexual, many, corolla 10–11.5 mm, outer lip and inner lip 2–2.5 mm, the outer one 3‑lobed, the inner one 2‑cleft; lower tube 8– 9 mm; anther bases caudate, apical appendages truncate; stylar branches short, about 1 mm, obtuse at apices. Cypselae fusiform, 6‑striate, 5–6 mm, pubescent, apex bearing glabrous beak 6 – 8 mm. Pappus capillary, 9– 10 mm, orange‑red or pale brown.

Locality: Clear Water Bay, Ma On Shan, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island, Ping Chau. Y. S. Lau 2127; S. P. Lau 43; S. Y. Hu 11946 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian; Japan, Vietnam, Thailand, Myanmar, India, Nepal, Indonesia, Australia.
Ecology: Grassy hillslopes, thickets. Flowering: Mar.–May.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Wong Nai Chung Gap, Tai Tam, Sha Tin, Sai Kung, Po Toi Islands
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Glossocardia bidens (Retz.) Veldkamp 鹿角草
Blumea 35(2): 468. 1991; FTW ed. 2, 4: 971, pl. 461, photo 455. 1998.
Zinnia bidens Retz., Observ. Bot. 5: 28. 1788.
