Glossogyne tenuifolia (Labill.) Cass. ex Less., Syn. Gen. Compos. 212. 1832; Benth., FHK 184. 1861; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 19(3 – 4): 271. 1966; FRPS 75: 381, pl. 66: 1 – 4. 1979; FGD 8: 137, fig. 72. 2007.

Perennial herbs 15–30 cm tall; stem branched mainly at base, glabrous. Radical leaves many and persistent, pinnatisect with 2–3 pairs of lateral segments, without clear distinction of lamina and petiole, totally 3.5–9 cm long, the apical divided portion 1.5–2.5 cm, the basal undivided petiole‑like portion 2–6.5 cm, lateral segments linear, the lowest ones longer, 5–20 × 1–2 mm, all apex rounded to obtuse, mucronate, both surfaces glabrous; cauline leaves few, usually linear, some pinnatisect. Capitula heterogamous and radiate, 5–8 mm across, solitary and terminating branches, base bearing one linear prophyll (ca. 2 mm). Involucres campanulate‑hemispherical; phyllaries in 2 series, lanceolate‑oblong, 2–3.5 mm with the inner layers longer, apex obtuse, margin scarious and ciliate. Receptacle flat. Paleae linear with hyaline and shallowly dentate margin, those subtending inner disk florets with broad bases. Ray florets 8–9 in one row, female, corolla yellow, about 4 mm, ligule elliptic‑oblong, 2.5–3 × 2.5 mm, spreading, apex 3‑dentate. Disk tubular florets bisexual, corolla yellow, 2.8–3 mm, basal 1/3 narrowed, apical 2/3 campanulate, apex 4‑lobed. Cypselae black, linear, 5–6 × 0.8–1 mm, flat, ribbed, glabrous. Pappus 2 stiff awns, 1–1.5 mm, pale brown, retrorsely barbed.

Locality: Wong Nai Chung Gap, Tai Tam, Sha Tin, Sai Kung, Po Toi Islands. L. T. Lo 144, 502; Y. W. Lam 1040.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Taiwan; Philippines, Malaysia, Australia.
Ecology: Sandy slopes and rocky places near seashore. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Sep.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Gnaphalium affine D. Don 鼠麴草
Prodr. Fl. Nepal. 173. 1825; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 19(3 – 4): 272. 1966; FRPS 75: 225. 1979: FGD 8: 170. 2007.
Gnaphalium multiceps DC., Prodr. 6: 222. 1837; FHK 188. 1861; FKH 144. 1912.
Gnaphalium luteoalbum subsp. affine (D. Don) Koster, Blumea 4: 484. 1941; FTW ed. 2, 4: 977. 1998.

Annual herbs; stem (4–)15–30 cm tall, striate, densely lanate, usually with creeping or ascending branches at base. Leaves sessile, oblanceolate‑spatulate, 1.5–6 cm × 2–10 mm, base attenuate and decurrent, apex rounded and mucronulate, margin entire, both surfaces tomemtose, woolly hair appearing much denser on lower surface. Capitula subsessile, compacted tightly into terminal corymbs. Involucres globose‑campanulate, 2–3 mm across; phyllaries 2–3‑seriate, membranous, shinny golden or lemon‑yellow, outer ones elliptic‑ovate, 2 mm, base densely woolly, apex rounded; middle and inner ones oblanceolate‑spatulate to long‑spatulate, 3 mm, subglabrous or slightly woolly, apex obtuse. Receptacle concave, naked. Florets yellow or pale yellow. Outer female florets numerous, corolla filiform‑tubular, 2 mm, apex minutely 3‑toothed. Central bisexual florets few, corolla tubular, 2–2.2 mm, apex shortly 5‑lobed. Cypselae obovate‑oblong, 0.5 mm, papillose. Pappus setae rough, 2 mm, yellowish white, deciduous separately or with several setae connate at base.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 2676, 2697; S. Y. Hu 6940 (CUHK).
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; also found in Japan, Philippines, Vietnam, Indochina, Indonesia.
Ecology: Wastelands near villages, weed in gardens. Flowering: Jan.–Apr., Aug.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Gnaphalium hypoleucum DC. 秋鼠麴草
Contr. Bot. India 21. 1834; FHK 187. 1861; FKH 144. 1912; FRPS 75: 226. 1979; FTW ed. 2, 4: 975. 1998; FGD 8: 172. 2007.

Annual herbs; stem 30–80 cm tall, striate, densely white‑lanate and with short glandular hairs, usually branched on the upper portion. Leaves sessile; basal leaves withering before anthesis; lower stem leaves narrowly lanceolate to linear, 6–13 cm × 3–10 mm, base attenuate and decurrent, apex acuminate or acute, margin entire, adaxial surfaces green, densely covered with short glandular hairs, and with sparsely lanate on the midvein, abaxial surface densely white woolly. Capitula numerous, sessile or shortly pedunculate, in terminal congested corymbs. Involucres globose‑campanulate, 3–5 mm across; phyllaries 4‑seriate, membranous, shinny golden‑yellow, subequal, 3–5 mm, outer ones obovate, apex rounded, abaxially white woolly at base; middle ones obovate‑oblong, apex obtuse, slightly white woolly at base abaxially; inner ones narrowly oblong to linear, apex acute, glabrous. Receptacle pitted. Florets yellow or pale yellow. Outer female florets numerous, corolla filiform‑tubular, 3 mm, apex minutely 3– 4‑toothed. Central bisexual florets few, corolla tubular, ca. 4 mm, apex shortly 5‑lobed, style exserted. Cypselae oblong, 0.5 mm. Pappus white, ca. 3 mm, deciduous.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. HK sheet 2592.
Distribution: Widely distributed in E, S, C, SW & NW China; Korea, Japan, Philippines, Indochina, India, Indonesia.
Ecology: Open fields and wastelands near villages, roadsides. Flowering: Aug.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Gnaphalium pensylvanicum Willd. 匙葉鼠麴草
Enum. Pl. Hort. Berol. 867. 1809; FRPS 75: 238. 1979; FTW ed. 2, 4: 979. 1998; FGD 8: 172. 2007.
Gnaphalium purpureum auct. non L.: FHK 188. 1861; FKH 144. 1912.

Annual herbs, 10–35 cm tall; stem erect, striate, white woolly, with or without ascending branches at base. Leaves sessile, oblanceolate or spatulate, 2–8 × 0.5–2 cm, base attenuate and decurrent, apex rounded, and some mucronulate, margin entire, both surfaces tomentose, woolly hair much denser on lower side, leaf smaller gradually upward. Capitula many, tightly compacted into terminal or axillary spike about 1–5 cm, together with some small leaves included inside. Involucres ovate‑urceolate, 2–3 mm across; phyllaries 2–3‑seriate; outer ones ovate‑oblong, 2–2.5 mm, densely woolly near base, centre green and herbaceous, apex brownish yellow, margin broadly membranous, acuminate; middle ones lanceolate, membranous, straw to brownish yellow in colour, slightly green‑veined at the middle, loosely woolly, apex acuminate; inner ones linear‑oblong, 3 mm, totally membranous, subglabrous, apex acute to obtuse. Receptacle deeply concave at centre, protruded at the periphery, naked. Marginal female florets numerous, corolla filiform‑tubular, about 2 mm, apex minutely 3‑toothed. Disk bisexual florets few, corolla tubular, about 2 mm, apex 5 triangular lobes, obtuse to rounded, glabrous. Cypselae elliptic‑oblong, 0.5 mm, finely glandular. Pappus 2 mm, white, connate at base and deciduous as a ring.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1189; S. Y. Hu 6788, 7184 (CUHK).
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Taiwan; tropical Asia, S America, S Africa, Australia.
Ecology: Wastelands. Flowering: Dec.–Apr. of the following year.

Gnaphalium polycaulon Pers. 多莖鼠麴草
Syn. Pl. 2: 421. 1807; FRPS 75: 239. 1979; FGD 8: 172. 2007.
Gnaphalium indicum auct. non L.: FHK 188. 1861; FKH 144. 1912.

Annual herbs, 8–10 cm tall; stems basally creeping or ascending, densely white woolly, many‑branched. Leaves sessile, oblanceolate, 5–25 × 2–4 mm, base decurrent, apex obtuse and mucronulate, margin entire, both surfaces white woolly and with abaxial surface more hairy. Capitula many, tightly arranged as terminal spike about 5–15 mm, together with some small leaves included inside. Involucres ovate‑urceolate, 2 mm across; phyllaries 2‑seriate, membranous, greyish or straw yellow, tinged purple at base, apex acute; outer series oblong‑lanceolate, 1.2–1.5 mm long, lanate; inner ones 2 mm, loosely hairy or subglabrous. Receptacle shallowly concave, naked. Marginal female florets numerous, corolla filiform‑tubular, 1–1.2 mm, apex finely 3‑toothed. Central bisexual florets few, corolla tubular, 1.2 mm, apex shortly 5‑lobed, acute, glabrous. Cypselae cylindric‑oblong, 0.5 mm long, minutely glandular. Pappus 1.2 mm, white, deciduous separately.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 831.
Distribution: Guangdong, Yunnan, Guizhou, Fujian, Zhejiang; India, Thailand, Australia, tropical Africa.
Ecology: Wastelands and paddy fields. Flowering: Jan.–Apr.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Happy Valley, Tai Tam Tuk Reservoir, Tai Lung, Ting Kok, Ho Pui Reservoir
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Grangea maderaspatana (L.) Poir. 田基黃（荔枝菊）
Encycl. Suppl. 2(2): 825 – 826. 1812; FHK 185. 1861; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 19(3 – 4): 279. 1966; FRPS 74: 83. 1985; FTW ed. 2, 4: 982. 1998; FGD 8: 191, fig. 110. 2007.
Artemisia maderaspatana L., Sp. Pl. 849. 1753.

Annual herbs; stems 5–20 cm, decumbent and ascending, branched at basal portion, strigose. Leaves obovate, oblanceolate to spatulate, 1.5–6 × 0.5–2.5 cm, base attenuate, sessile or some forming winged petioles, apex obtuse, margin sinuate‑pinnatifid with 2–5 pairs of lateral lobes, irregularly serrate‑crenate, pubescent and glandular punctate on both surfaces, abaxial surface covered with denser hair and glands. Capitula globose, 0.5– 1 cm across, solitary, growing terminal or axillary to the stems. Involucres bowl‑shaped; phyllaries 2–3‑seriate, herbaceous, hirsute, margin fimbriate; outer ones lanceolate‑oblong, 4–5 mm, apex acute to obtuse; inner ones oblanceolate or obovate, apex rounded, slightly shorter. Receptacle convex, spherical. Marginal pistillate florets numerous, in 2–6 series, corolla yellow, tubular, 1–1.2 mm, narrow, glandular, with 2–4 lobes at apex; style exserted. Disk hermaphrodite florets many, corolla yellow, tubular, funnelform, glandular, 1.5 mm, with 5 ovate‑deltoid lobes at apex. Cypselae compressed, with thickened ribs on margin, 1.5 mm, glandular. Pappus scarious cupular, about 1 mm, irregularly toothed and ciliate.

Locality: Happy Valley, Tai Tam Tuk Reservoir, Tai Lung, Ting Kok, Ho Pui Reservoir. Y. S. Lau 2469, 2483; Y. W. Lam 1486.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, S Yunnan, Taiwan; tropical Asia.
Ecology: Lowland thickets, abandoned fields. Flowering: Mar.–Aug.

Gynura divaricata (L.) DC. 白子菜
Prodr. 6: 301. 1838; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 19(3–4): 280. 1966; FRPS 77(1): 317, pl. 71: 5–8. 1999; FGD 8: 227, fig. 138. 2007.
Gynura ovalis (Ker Gawl.) DC., Prodr. 6: 300. 1837.
Cacalia ovalis Ker Gawl., Bot. Reg. 2: pl. 101. 1816.
Senecio divaricatus L., Sp. Pl. 866. 1753.
Gynura pseudochina auct. non DC.: FHK 189. 1861.

Perennial herbs, odorous like bad egg smell; stem erect or decumbent, about 0.3–1(–2) m tall, branched in upper inflorescence portion, glabrous or pubescent. Leaves fleshy, mainly growing at lower portion, petiole 0.5–4.5 cm, pubescent, base usually with pseudo‑stipules, leaf blade ovate, elliptic to oblanceolate, 3.5–13(–23) × 1.2–5(– 6.5) cm, base cuneate and narrowed down to petiole, apex obtuse or acute, margin coarsely dentate, adaxial surfaces green, abaxial surfaces pale green, both densely pubescent with hair multicellular, venation appeared as numerous black lines after dried. Median leaves smaller in size, subsessile to sessile, elliptic‑oblong, dentate. Upper leaves few, sessile, linear‑lanceolate to linear, 0.5–2 cm. Capitula 1.5–2 cm across, with 3 – 5 heads arranged as loose corymbs at terminal; peduncle 1–6.5(–9) cm, pubescent. Involucres campanulate, length 8 – 10 mm, base calyculate with several linear bracteoles 3–5.5 mm; phyllaries 11–14 in 1 series, linear‑lanceolate, 8–10 × 1–2 mm, apex acuminate, margin scarious, 3‑veined, subglabrous or puberulous abaxially. Receptacle flat, pitted with areoles elevated at centre. All florets hermaphrodite and fertile, corolla tubular, total 10–14 mm, lower portion filiform 7–10 mm, upper portion abruptly broaden as cylindric or campanulate form, 3–4 mm, apex with 5 acute ovate‑oblong lobes, floret colour brilliant orange‑yellow, some tinged red near apex; anther bases obtuse or shortly sagittate; stylar branches papillose hairy. Cypselae cylindric, 3–4 × 0.8 mm, 10‑ribbed, truncate at both ends, brown, puberulent. Pappus capillary, silky, white, 8–9 mm, easily shed off individually.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1425; S. Y. Hu 10072 (CUHK); T. W. Lau 0072 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Yunnan; N Vietnam.
Ecology: Margins of forests, streamsides. Flowering & fruiting: Nearly all year round.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Helianthus annuus L. 向日葵
Sp. Pl. 2: 904. 1753; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 19(3 – 4): 285. 1966; FRPS 75: 358. 1979; FGD 8: 118, fig. 58. 2007.

Stout annual herbs; stems erect, 1–2(–3) m tall, usually not branched, scabrous to hirsute, hair much denser near the head. Leaves mostly alternate except the lowest; petioles 2–17 cm or longer, not winged; leaf blade ovate to cordate‑ovate, 4.5–18 × 2–15 cm, or much larger, apex acute or acuminate, 3‑nerved, margin coarsely serrate, both surfaces scabrous. Capitula heterogamous and radiate, 10–25(–30) cm across, solitary at terminal, usually nodding. Involucres dish‑like, densely hairy at base; phyllaries 2 – 3‑seriate, foliaceous, ovate to lanceolate, 1.5– 7 cm, apex attenuate and long‑caudate, pilose. Receptacle nearly flat; paleae enfolding the cypselae, trilobed with the midlobe cuspidate, margin of all lobes pubescent. Ligulate florets 1‑seriate, corolla yellow, limb spreading, elliptic‑oblong, apex acute and entire, tube minute and densely pubescent, infertile. Tubular florets numerous, purplish black, reddish black or brownish black, corolla 5 hairy lobes apically, basally swollen as a ball and densely pubescent. Anther bases sagittate, apical appendages ovate‑acute, exserted; stylar branches short and hairy. Cypselae obovate or ovate‑oblong, white or greyish, black‑lineolate, about 9 × 4–8 mm, slightly compressed, pilose near the summit. Pappus 2 cuspidate scales, deciduous.

Locality: Cultivated. S. Y. Hu 7648 (CUHK); S. Y. Hu & K. H. Yung 205 (CUHK); H. Y. Yeung 171 (CUHK).
Distribution: Native to N America, cultivated worldwide.
Ecology: Flowering: Jul.–Sep.
Uses: Food (oil/fat), ornamental.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Sha Tin, Tai Po, Fanling, Sai Kung
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Hemisteptia lyrata (Bunge) Bunge 泥胡菜
Dorp. Jahrb. Litt. 1: 222. 1833; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 19(3–4): 287. 1966; FRPS 78(1): 138. 1985; FTW ed. 2, 4: 989. 1998; FGD 8: 253, fig. 154. 2007.
Cirsium lyratum Bunge, Enum. Pl. Chin. Bor. 36. 1833.
Saussurea carthamoides Benth., FHK 168. 1861.
Saussurea affinis Spreng. ex DC., Prodr. 6: 538. 1838; FKH 149. 1912.

Annual herbs; stem 30–100 cm tall, striate, arachnoid‑tomentose hairy, branched apically. Radical leaves usually withered at anthesis. Lower and middle cauline leaves oblong to oblanceolate, 4–21 × 1.5–9 cm, adaxial surface green and glabrous, abaxial surface greyish white and densely tomentose, lyrately pinnatisect or sometimes the lower leaves not lobed, lateral lobes 2–6 pairs, variable in shape, elliptic, obovate, to oblanceolate, those near base smaller; apical lobe large, rhomboid, deltoid or ovate, apex acute, obtuse to rounded, leaf margin shallowly toothed or not; petioles long in the lowermost leaves, gradually shorter for leaves growing upward. Upper leaves few, linear to linear‑lanceolate, sessile. Capitula arranged as loose corymbs at stem terminal, rarely solitary. Involucres ovoid; phyllaries many‑seriate, imbricate; outer few layers triangular‑ovate to elliptic‑ovate, 1.5–4 × 1.3–1.5 mm, acute or acuminate, with purple‑red cristate appendages on abaxial side near the apex; middle layers ovate‑oblong to oblong, 4–7 × 1.2–1.3 mm, apex not crested; inner ones linear‑lanceolate to linear, 6 – 12 × 0.8 – 1 mm, acuminate and without appendages, tinged red. Florets purple to red, corolla 8.5–13 mm; upper limb 2.2 – 3 mm, deeply cleft into 5 linear lobes 2–2.5 mm; lower tube filiform, 6.5–10 mm. Cypselae oblong‑cuneate, 2.5 – 4 × 1 mm, brown or reddish‑brown, 13 – 16‑ribbed, apex obliquely truncate. Pappus white, in 2 rows; inner ones plumose, 6–9 mm, base connate and deciduous as a ring; outer 3–9 short scales, growing on one side.

Locality: Sha Tin, Tai Po, Fanling, Sai Kung. Y. S. Lau 3294; Y. W. Lam 191; S. Y. Hu 22790 (CUHK).
Distribution: Widely distributed in China except Xinjiang and Xizang; also in Korea, Japan, Vietnam, Laos.
Ecology: Margins of forests, wastelands, margins of cultivated lands. Flowering: Mar.–Aug.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Shing Mun, Fanling, Pat Sin Leng, Sai Kung
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Ixeridium chinense (Thunb.) Tzvelev 中華小苦蕒（山苦蕒）
Fl. URSS 29: 390. 1964; FRPS 80(1): 251. 1997.
Prenanthes chinensis Thunb., Fl. Jap. 310. 1784.
Lactuca chinensis (Thunb.) Nakai, Bot. Mag. Tokyo 17: 89. 1903.
Ixeris chinensis (Thunb.) Nakai, Bot. Mag. Tokyo 34: 152. 1920; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 20(1 – 2): 1. 1967; FTW ed. 2, 4: 996. 1998; FGD 8: 271. 2007; Check List HK Plants 283. 2002; 97. 2004.
Ixeris versicolor auct. non DC.: FHK 193. 1861.
Lactuca versicolor auct. non Sch.‑Bip.: FKH 150. 1912.

Perennial herbs; stem erect, 15–60 cm tall, branched apically. Leaves glabrous on both surfaces. Basal leaves narrowly elliptic, linear or oblanceolate, 8–23 × 0.3–2 cm, base narrowed down as winged petiole, apex acute, obtuse or attenuate, margin subentire or toothed, undivided, or sometimes pinnatilobed, pinnatifid to pinnatisect with lateral segments 2–7 pairs; segments triangular, linear‑triangular or linear, the middle segments largest, becoming smaller towards both ends. Cauline leaves few, about 2–4, rarely none, lanceolate or oblong‑lanceolate, 5–9 cm, undivided or pinnatifid, margin entire or mucronate‑dentate, base slightly to broadly widen and auriculate, amplexicaul, apex acuminate. Upper leaves bract‑like. Capitula erect at maturity, homogamous with all florets ligulate and bisexual, corymbose at terminal. Involucres cylindric, about 7–9 mm; phyllaries 3 – 4‑seriate, glabrous; outer layers ovate, 1–1.8 × 0.8–1 mm, acute; inner layers oblong‑lanceolate, 7–9 × 1–2 mm, acute or obtuse, margin scarious. Florets 21–25 per head, corolla yellow, 7–10 mm. Cypselae brown or reddish brown, narrowly elliptic, 2.8–4 × 0.3–0.6 mm, obtusely 10‑ribbed, minutely hirtellous along ribs particularly the upper portion, apex acute and beaked, the beak filiform, 1.8–2.8 mm. Pappus 3–4 mm, white, scaberulous.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Shing Mun, Fanling, Pat Sin Leng, Sai Kung. P. S. Choi 423; Y. W. Lam 486; S. Y. Hu 10067(CUHK).
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; also in Japan, Korea, Russia (Far East region).
Ecology: Cultivated lands, wastelands. Flowering & fruiting: Mar.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Ixeridium gracile (DC.) J. H. Pak & Kawano 纖細苦蕒菜
Mem. Fac. Sci. Kyoto Univ., Ser. Biol. 15(1–2): 45. 1992.
Ixeridium gracile (DC.) Shih, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 31: 545. 1993; FRPS 80(1): 257. 1997.
Ixeris gracilis (DC.) Stebbins, J. Bot. 75: 50. 1937; FGD 8: 273, fig. 166. 2007; Check List HK Plants 284. 2002; 97. 2004.
Lactuca gracilis DC., Prodr. 7: 140. 1838; FHN 3: 427. 1974.

Perennial herbs, 15–50 cm tall, glabrous. Stem erect, slender, apically many‑branched. Basal leaves rosulate, with winged petiole; leaf blade linear to linear lanceolate, 7–15 cm × 5–9 mm, margin entire, narrowed towards both ends. Cauline leaves few, linear to linear‑lanceolate, base sessile. Capitula numerous, terminal, corymbose to corymbose‑paniculate, with ca. 6 florets. Involucre very small, cylindric, ca. 6 mm. Phyllaries in 2 rows, abaxially glabrous; outer phyllaries 2 or 3, ovate, less than ca. 1 × 0.5 mm; inner phyllaries linear‑elliptic, ca. 6 × 0.8 mm. Florets yellow. Achenes brown, narrowly pyramidal, ca. 3 mm, with 10 slender rib or lines, apically gradually narrowed into a filiform ca. 1 mm curved beak. Pappus brown to pale yellow, ca. 3 mm, scabridulous.

Locality: Sai Kung. Y. W. Lam 488.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Gansu, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang; Myanmar, India, Bhutan, Nepal.
Ecology: Cultivated areas, wastelands. Flowering & fruiting: Mar.–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Ixeris japonica (Burm. f.) Nakai 剪刀股
Bot. Mag. Tokyo 40: 575. 1926; FRPS 80(1): 242. 1997; FGD 8: 270. 2007.
Lapsana japonica Burm. f., Fl. Ind. 174. 1768.
Lactuca debilis (Thunb.) Benth. ex Maxim., Bull. Acad. Imp. Sci. Saint‑Petersbourg 19: 533. 1874; FKH 150. 1912.
Ixeris debilis A. Gray, Mem. Amer. Acad. Arts, n.s. 6(2): 397. 1858; Benth., FHK 193. 1861.
Lactuca stolonifera auct. non A. Gray: FKH 150. 1912.

Perennial herbs. Stem base creeping and forming adventitious roots at nodes, upper part erect, 12–35 cm tall. All leaves glabrous above and beneath. Radical leaves persistent at anthesis, spatulate‑oblanceoalte or ligulate, 3 – 17 × 1–3.5 cm, base narrowed into long petiole, margin entire, toothed, pinnatilobed, pinnatifid, or lyrately pinnatilobed to pinnatifid, apical lobes elliptic or obovate, apex obtuse or rounded, mucronulate; lateral segments 1 – 3 pairs, obliquely triangular or elliptic, acute or obtuse. Cauline leaves few, similar to the basal ones, or appearing narrowly elliptic or oblanceolate, base narrowed, sessile or shortly petiolate. Upper leaves small, ovate. Capitula corymbose at terminal. Involucres campanulate, 12–14 × 7 mm; phyllaries 2–3‑seriate; outer 1–2 layers ovate, 2–5.5 × 1–1.5 mm, acute; inner ones oblong‑lanceolate or lanceolate, 12–14 × 2–3 mm, obtuse, abaxial side glabrous, sometimes with crested appendages near apex. Ligulate florets 24 per head, corolla yellow, 12–15 mm. Cypselae brown, fusiform, 5–6 × 1 mm, glabrous, sharply and acutely 10‑ribbed as wings, apex acute and bearing filiform beak 2 mm. Pappus 6.5–7 mm, white, scaberulous.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 3249; Y. W. Lam 467; S. Y. Hu 10113 (CUHK).
Distribution: Distributed in S, E, C & NE China; also in Korea, Japan.
Ecology: Cultivated lands, wastelands. Flowering & fruiting: Mar.–Jun.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Ixeris polycephala Cass. 多頭苦蕒菜
Dict. Sci. Nat. 24: 50. 1822; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 20(1 – 2): 6. 1967; FRPS 80(1): 243. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 4: 998. 1998; FGD 8: 271. 2007.

Annual or perennial herbs; stem erect, 10–80 cm tall, branched, glabrous. Leaves glabrous above and beneath, margin entire or loosely mucronulate near base. Basal leaves linear or linear‑lanceolate, 6–12 × 0.5–0.8 cm, base attenuate to the short petiole, apex acute. Lower and middle cauline leaves sessile, linear or lanceolate, 5 – 24 × 1.2–3 cm, sagittate and semi‑amplexicaul basally, acute apically. Upper leaves gradually smaller in size when growing upward. Capitula many, corymbose or in false umbelliform at terminal, nodding after anthesis; peduncle 5 – 10 mm, having few bracteoles 0.5–2 mm. Involucres cylindric, 5–7 × 2.5–3.5 mm, becoming ovoid upon fruiting; phyllaries 2–3‑seriate; outer 1–2 layers tiny, ovate, 0.5–0.8 × 0.2–0.3 mm, acute, inner ones in one row, lanceolate, 5–6 × 1.1–1.5 mm, acute or obtuse, margin membranous, abaxial side sometimes with cristate appendages near apex. Ligulate florets 10 – 25 per head, corolla yellow, rarely white, 4 – 4.5 mm. Cypselae fusiform, 2.5 × 0.8 mm, brown, glabrous, sharply and acutely 10‑ribbed as wings, apex acute and rostrate, rostrum 1–1.2 mm, filiform. Pappus 3 mm, white, scaberulous, persistent.

Locality: Sai Kung, Fanling. Y. W. Lam 490; S. Y. Hu 6941, 10008 (CUHK).
Distribution: Distributed in S, SW, C & E China; also in Korea, Japan, India.
Ecology: Cultivated lands, wastelands. Flowering: Mar.–Jul.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Tseng Lan Shu, New Territories, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Kalimeris indica (L.) Sch.‑Bip. 馬蘭（雞兒腸）
Syst. Verz. 125. 1854; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 20(1 – 2): 11. 1967; FTW 4: 892. 1978; FRPS 74: 99, pl. 30: 1 – 3. 1985; FGD 8: 180, fig. 101. 2007.
Aster indicus L., Sp. Pl. 2: 876. 1753; FKH 141. 1912; FTW ed. 2, 4: 855. 1998.
Boltonia indica Benth., FHK 174. 1861.

Perennial rhizomatous herb, 30–75 cm tall; stems erect, with hair on upper portion. Leaves on basal part oblanceolate or obovate‑oblong, coarsely dentate above, 3–6 × 0.7–1.5 cm, base attenuate and narrowed down to form wing with petiole, apex acute or obtuse; those on upper part smaller in size, linear or lanceolate, subentire. Capitula solitary to each branch, or loosely corymbose. Involucres hemispherical, 0.5–1 cm across; phyllaries 2 – 3‑seriate, margin membranous and hair‑bearing; outer ones elliptic, 1.8 mm; middle ones obovate; inner ones oblanceolate‑oblong, 4 mm, apex obtuse. Receptacle convex with each areole elevated at centre. Ligulate marginal florets 15–20, 1‑seriate, 8–10 mm, limb purple; stylar branches papillose along margin. Tubular disk florets 3.5 mm, yellow, pilose; anther bases obtuse and entire, apex appendages ovate‑lanceolate; style with triangular appendage at apex. Cypselae obovate‑oblong, 1.8 mm, brown, hirsute, with a crown of scarious pappus, marginal one 3‑ribbed, inner disk one laterally compressed and 2‑ribbed.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tseng Lan Shu, New Territories, Lantau Island. L. T. Lo 438; C. P. Lau 051 (CUHK); S. Y. Hu & K. H. Yung 308 (CUHK).
Distribution: E to SW and S to NE China; S & E Asia.
Ecology: Margins of forests, grassy hillslopes. Flowering: May–Sep.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Lactuca sativa L. 萵苣
Sp. Pl. 785. 1753; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 20(1 – 2): 27. 1967; FRPS 80(1): 233. 1997; FGD 8: 262. 2007.

Annual or biennial lactiferous herbs 25–100 cm tall, glabrous throughout; stem white erect, apically branched. Basal and lower leaves large, undivided, oblanceolate, elliptic‑oblanceolate to elliptic, 6–15 × 1.5–7.5 cm, sessile, base cordate or sagittate, semi‑amplexicaul, apex obtuse to rounded, margin sinuous or bearing short teeth. Middle and upper leaves with shape similar to the basal and lower ones, or appearing as lanceolate, size gradually smaller when growing upward; the uppermost leaves small, ovate‑cordate, sessile, base cordate or sagittate, amplexicaul, margin entire or slightly sinuous. Capitula many, paniculate at stem and branch terminal. Involucres ovoid‑cylindric, 10 × 6 mm; phyllaries 5‑seriate, apex acute, abaxial side glabrous; outer ones broadly deltoid to ovate, 3–4 × 1.5–2.5 mm; middle and inner ones ovate‑lanceolate to lanceolate, 6–10 × 1.5–2 mm. All florets yellow, corolla ligulate, 6–7 mm long, ligule 4–5 mm, apex 5‑lobed, lower tube 2 mm, hairy near summit, hermaphrodite and fertile. Cypselae oblanceolate, 4 × 1.3 mm, compressed, pale brown, 6–7‑ribbed on each surface, apex acute and beaked, beak filiform, 4–5 mm, equal to or longer than the cypsela body. Pappus bristles in 2 rows, white, scaberulous.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 2962; HK sheet 16362.
Distribution: Native to Mediterranean region, cultivated worldwide.
Ecology: Flowering: Feb.–Sep.
Uses: Food (vegetable).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Ma On Shan, Tai Mo Shan, Sunset Peak
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Lagenophora stipitata (Labill.) Druce 瓶頭草（瓶頭菊）
Rep. Bot. Exch. Club Brit. Isles. 4: 630. 1917; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 20(1–2): 32. 1967; FRPS 74: 85. 1985; FGD 8: 190, fig. 108. 2007.
Bellis stipitata Labill., Pl. Nov. Holl. 2: 55, t. 205. 1806.
Lagenophora billardieri Cass., Bull. Soc. Philom. Paris 34. 1818; FHK 173. 1861; FKH 140. 1912.

Small perennial herbs; rootstock 5–7 mm, densely covered by remnant of petiole bases; bearing 2–5 tuberous storage roots. Leaves all radical, rosulate, obovate to spatulate, 1–3 × 0.5–1.3 cm, base cuneate and gradually running to become wing of the petioles, apex rounded or obtuse, margin inconspicuously 1–3 toothed, softly pubescent on both surfaces, especially on the veins and along the margin. Capitula 5 mm across, solitary and terminal; scape 2.5–13 cm, slender, rarely bearing a branch. Involucre hemispherical, 4 mm across; phyllaries 4‑seriate, apex acute, glabrous, margin membranous; outer ones ovate‑lanceolate; middle ones long‑oblong; inner ones linear. Receptacle 1 mm across, space between floret glandular. Ray florets 30, fertile, 3 mm, ligules 1.6 mm, entire; style short, branches stout. Disk florets 14, tubular, 2 mm, limb 4‑toothed; stamens 4, base obtuse, apical appendages small; stylar branches slender, appendages acute; ovary narrowed towards the apex. Cypselae brown, compressed oblanceolate, margin thickened, beaked, 2.5 mm including the glandular beak, end of beak with a waxy ring. Pappus absent.

Locality: Ma On Shan, Tai Mo Shan, Sunset Peak. Y. S. Lau 2989; Y. W. Lam 234, 1434.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Indochina, Indonesia, Australia.
Ecology: Grassy hillslopes. Flowering: Mar.–Jun.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Bride's Pool, High Island, Yung Shue O, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Laggera alata (D. Don) Sch.‑Bip. ex Oliv. 六棱菊
Trans. Linn. Soc. London 29: 94. 1873; FKH 143. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan. Mus. 20(1–2): 33. 1967; FRPS 75: 47. 1979; FTW ed. 2, 4: 1006. 1998; FGD 8: 163, fig. 89. 2007.
Erigeron alatum D. Don, Prodr. Fl. Nepal. 171. 1825.
Blumea alata DC., Prodr. 5: 448. 1836; FHK 177. 1861.

Perennial erect herbs; stem base woody, 50–100 cm tall, densely covered with glandular pubescent to tomentose hair, with wings 1–2 mm broad and entire. Cauline leaves oblong, 3–8 × 0.5–1.5 cm, base decurrent, apex obtuse to rounded, margin mucronulate or sometimes entire, densely glandular‑hairy and with strong midvein protruded on both surfaces. Upper leaves gradually smaller in size, especially those on branches, 1.5–3.5 × 3–6 mm, narrowly oblong to linear. Capitula many, drooping, growing as raceme on axillary winged branches, and branches grouped together as large racemose‑panicle. Peduncles 0.5–2 cm, glandularly pubescent, without wings. Involucres ovoid to campanulate, 7–10 mm; phyllaries 6‑seriate, shape changing inward from obovate, to ovate, lanceolate and linear‑oblong, length increases from outermost 2.5 mm to innermost 8 mm, apex acute; outer several layers herbaceous, green or apically green, some tinged purple near the tip, glandular and hairy on abaxial surfaces and along margins, usually recurved; inner series scarious, sparsely puberulent to glabrous. Receptacle plain and nude, areoles with elevated centers. Florets purple; marginal ones many‑seriate, pistillate, corolla filiform‑tubular, 5–6 mm, minutely 3 – 4‑lobed; disk ones few, hermaphrodite, 5–6 mm, bearing 5 lobes ovate and papillose, loosely hairy; anther bases sagittate and acute, apical appendages oblong and rounded; style reddish, papillose. Cypselae elliptic‑oblong, 0.8 mm, 10‑ribbed. Pappus bristles white, 5 mm, deciduous.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Bride's Pool, High Island, Yung Shue O, Lantau Island. Y. W. Lam 1291; S. L. Thrower 1408b (CUHK); S. Y. Hu 8590 (CUHK).
Distribution: S to SW and E China; Indochina, Malaysia, India, E Africa.
Ecology: Banks of paddy fields, grassy hillslopes. Flowering: Oct.–Feb. of the following year.

Launaea sarmentosa (Willd.) Sch.‑Bip. ex Kuntze 匍莖栓果菊
Revis. Gen. Pl. 1: 350. 1891; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 20(1 – 2): 35. 1967; FRPS 80(1): 164. 1997; FGD 8: 262. 2007.
Prenanthes sarmentosa Willd., Phyt. 10: t. 6, fig. 2. 1794.
Launaea pinnatifida Cass., Ann. Sci. Nat. (Paris) 23: 85. 1831; FKH 151. 1912.

Perennial creeping herbs; stem 20–250 cm or longer, glabrous, subglabrous or arachnoid hairy, with adventitious roots and rosulate leaves growing at nodes. Basal leaves in rosette, oblanceolate, 2–8(–15) × 0.5–2.5(–6) cm, pinnatilobed or with margin crenate‑sinuate, apical lobes irregularly rhomboid, triangular or elliptic, apex rounded or obtuse; lateral lobes 1–5 pairs, triangular to elliptic, gradually smaller downward, opposite or alternate with each other, apex obtuse to rounded. Cauline leaves growing on stem nodes, rosulate, shape similar to basal ones but smaller in size. All leaves with base attenuate into winged petiole 0.5–5 cm long or sessile, both surfaces glabrous. Capitula homogamous, about 12–14 florets per head, solitary to the rosettes of basal leaves and of stem nodes; peduncles 0.5–4.5 cm, bearing few ovate bracteoles about 3 mm long near the capitulum. Involucres cylindric, 12–14 × 3–4 mm; phyllaries 3–4‑seriate, margin membranous, glabrous abaxially; outer rows small, triangular or ovate, 2–4 × 1.2–2 mm, obtuse; median ones ovate‑lanceolate to lanceolate, 5–8 × 1.2–2 mm, acute to obtuse; inner ones linear, 10–14 × 1.5–2 mm, acute or obtuse. Ligulate florets yellow, 1.8 cm, lower tube 1 cm, ligule 0.8 cm, 5‑lobed apically; anther bases sagittate and serrulate, apical appendages rounded; stylar branches slender and hairy. Cypselae brown, cylindric, 3.5 mm, largely and obtusely 4‑ribbed, transversely rugose. Pappus white, capillary and slender, 8–10 mm, connate at base, shed off as a whole ring.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. S. P. Lau 42; Y. W. Lam 463; S. Y. Hu 10252 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong and other S China coastal regions; India, Egypt, W Africa.
Ecology: Sandy beaches. Flowering & fruiting: Mar.–Dec.

Leucanthemum vulgare Lam. 濱菊（延命菊）
Fl. Franc. 2: 137. 1778; FRPS 76(1): 25. 1983; FTW ed. 2, 4: 1010. 1998; FGD 8: 197, fig. 116. 2007.
Chrysanthemum leucanthemum L., Sp. Pl. 2: 888. 1753.

Perennial erect herbs 15–100 cm tall, with simple or branched stems, glabrous or subglabrous. Basal and lower cauline leaves obovate‑spatulate to oblanceolate‑spatulate, 5–10 × 1.5–2.2 cm, margin crenate to obtuse‑dentate, base cuneate‑attenuate, apex obtuse; upper cauline leaves oblong, margin crenate to pinnatifid, base attenuate, sessile, somewhat auriculate and semi‑amplexicaul, both surfaces glabrous; uppermost leaves smaller in size, sometimes pinnatisect. Capitula heterogamous and radiate, 2–5 cm across, long‑pedunculate, solitary, terminal to stem and branches. Involucres 0.5 – 1 × 1–2 cm; phyllaries 3–4‑seriate, ovate‑oblong to lanceolate, glabrous, green, margin and apex scarious, brownish or dark, the innermost one with apical scales broaden as rounded appendages. Ray florets pistillate, corolla white, ligule oblong, 0.8–2.5 cm. Disk florets hermaphrodite, corolla yellow, tube base swollen and skirt‑like, slightly covering the apical region of hypanthium, middle part constricted and upper part campanulate, 5‑lobed at apex. Cypselae subcylindric, cuneate at base, 2 – 3 mm, prominently 10‑ribbed, ribs projected into the apical rim, ribs pale brown and grooves black. Pappus absent or with short coronate scales or auricles on ray cypselae.

Locality: Cultivated. S. Y. Hu & K. H. Yung 586 (CUHK); S. Y. Hu & P. P. H. But 22008 (CUHK).
Distribution: Caucasus, W Asia, Europe.
Ecology: Flowering: Mar.–Oct.
Uses: Ornamental.

Ligularia japonica (Thunb.) Less. 大頭橐吾
Syn. Gen. Comp. 390. 1832; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 20(1–2): 61. 1967; FRPS 77(2): 14, pl. 2: 4–6. 1989; FTW ed. 2, 4: 1012, photo 472. 1998.
Arnica japonica Thunb., Fl. Jap. 319. 1784.
Senecio japonicus (Thunb.) Sch. Bip., Flora 28: 50. 1845; FKH 148. 1912.

Perennial herbs; stem erect, 50 – 100 cm tall, puberulous or glabrous, tinged purple. Radical and lower leaves revolute in young stage, leaf blade reniform, 5 – 15 × 7 – 22 cm, palmately lobed and veined, margin serrate, abaxial surface puberulous or glabrescent; petiole 4 – 27 cm. Cauline leaves few; shortly petiolate, sheath amplexicaul. Uppermost leaves much smaller and without sheath. Capitula heterogamous and radiate, 2 – 8 arranged as corymbs, without subtending bracteoles at base; peduncles 2 – 26 cm, tomentulose‑puberulous. Involucres hemispherical, abaxial side puberulous; phyllaries 9 – 12, oblong, 1.5 – 2 × 4 – 5 mm, acute or acuminate, margin scarious. Marginal female florets 1‑seriate, corolla ligulate, yellow, ligule oblong, 4 – 5 × 0.5 – 1 cm, tube 7 – 10 mm. Disk bisexual florets many, corolla tubular, about 1.5 cm, apex 5 linear‑lanceolate lobes about 5 mm. Cypselae cylindric, 0.7 – 1 cm, ribbed and glabrous. Pappus reddish brown, 1 – 1.4 cm.

Locality: Sunset Peak, Lautau Peak. HK sheet 15868, 15869, 35601.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Korea, Japan, India.
Ecology: Thin forests and thickets. Flowering: Feb.–Aug.
Uses: Ornamental.

Microglossa pyrifolia (Lam.) Kuntze 小舌菊
Rev. Gen. 1: 353. 1891; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 20(3 – 4): 286. 1967; FRPS 74: 337. 1985; FTW ed. 2, 4: 1014. 1998; FGD 8: 182, fig. 103. 2007.
Conyza pyrifolia Lam., Encycl. 2: 89. 1786.
Erigeron pyrifolius Benth., FHK 176. 1861.
Microglossa volubilis DC., Prodr. 5: 320. 1836; FKH 141. 1912.

Perennial scandent subshrubs, 70–150 cm tall; stem branches with prominent ribs, puberulous, glandular punctate. Leaves ovate or ovate‑oblong, 4–10 × 2.5–3.5 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, margin inconspicuously serrate or nearly entire, pubescent and with yellow glands abaxially; petiole 7–13 mm. Capitula 5–7 mm across, clustered in terminal corymb, with lanceolate bract 2–5 mm. Involucre campanulate, 5‑seriate, with scarious margin and brown midvein; outermost herbaceous, ovate‑lanceolate, apex obtuse, glandular and pilose; inner ones becoming increasingly longer, changing from lanceolate to linear, from herbaceous to scarious with hyaline margin, apex slightly acute or obtuse. Receptacle alveolate, each areole with a large elevation at center, naked or rarely scarious. Female florets numerous at the margin, ligulate, corolla 3 mm, filiform; bisexual florets 2–3 in the middle, 4.5 mm, tubular, 5‑lobed. Cypsela oblong, 1 mm, ribbed, minutely pubescent, apex truncate, base with white ring. Pappus bristles white to pink in colour, numerous.

Locality: Tai Po, Lantau Island. W. J. Tutcher 9136, 11286; S. Y. Hu 10022 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Taiwan; Africa and tropical Asia.
Ecology: Margins of forests and open grasslands. Flowering: Feb.–Jun.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Naturalized and widely distributed in Hong Kong
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Mikania micrantha Kunth 薇甘菊
Nov. Gen. Sp. (folio ed.) 4: 105. 1820.

Scandent herbs climbing over shrubs and small trees up to 5 m high; glabrous or subglabrous, slightly hairy at nodes. Leaves ovate‑deltoid, those on vegetative stems 4–9 × 2.5–6 cm, cordate with prominent broad sinus at the base, apex acuminate, the acumens 1–1.4 cm, margin undulate dentate or subentire, glandular on both surfaces; petiole 1–6 cm. Capitula 5 mm, in subumbelliform‑paniculate clusters terminal to lateral shoots with small leaves of 1–2.5 cm; each capitulum with 4 florets and 4 phyllaries, subtended by linear‑lanceolate bract 1.5–3 mm; phyllaries oblong, 3.5–5 mm, apex acuminate or obtuse, finely ciliate along margin of tip. All florets tubular, bisexual and fertile, corolla white, funnelform, 3–5 mm, 5‑lobed, the lower narrow tube glandular. Cypselae linear‑oblong, 4‑angled, 2–3 mm, glandular. Pappus of scabrid bristles 3–4 mm, white to reddish.

Locality: Naturalized and widely distributed in Hong Kong. S. Y. Hu 6146, 6280 (CUHK); Y. S. Lau 195.
Distribution: Native to S America, widely naturalized in the tropics
Ecology: A very troublesome weed commonly growing on margins of forests, open fields and especially in wastelands. Flowering: Jun.–Dec.

Paraixeris denticulata (Houtt.) Nakai 黃瓜菜
Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 34: 156. 1920; FRPS 80(1): 262, pl. 1: 3, pl. 58: 1 – 2. 1997.
Prenanthes denticulata Houtt., Nat. Hist. 10: 385. 1779.
Youngia denticulata (Houtt.) Kitam., Acta Phytotax. Geobot. 11(2): 128. 1942.
Ixeris denticulata (Houtt.) Stebbins, J. Bot. 75: 46. 1937; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 20(1 – 2): 2. 1967.
Lactuca denticulata (Houtt.) Maxim., Mélanges Biol. Bull. Phys.‑Math. Acad. Imp. Sci. Saint‑Pétersbourg 19: 529 – 530. 1874; FKH 150. 1912.
Ixeris ramosissima A. Gray, Mem. Amer. Acad.Arts n.s. 6: 397; FHK 193. 1861.
Brachyramphus ramosissimus Benth., London J. Bot. 1: 489. 1842.

Annual or biennial herbs; stem erect, 30–120 cm tall, branched in apical half, glabrous. Leaves glabrous on both surfaces. Radical and lower leaves ovate with margin irregularly dentate, or oblanceolate and lyrately pinnatisect, long‑petiolate, withered at flowering stage. Middle cauline leaves mostly sessile or sometimes broadly winged petiolate; leaf blade spatulate, pandurate, pandurate‑ovate, elliptic, oblong or lanceolate, 3.5–11 × 1–7 cm, undivided or sometimes lyrately pinnatilobed with 1–2 pairs of elliptic or triangular lateral lobes, base abruptly broaden as round auricles and amplexicaul, apex obtuse to rounded, and usually mucronate, margin entire, mucronate‑toothed, or irregularly dentate. Upper leaves sessile, smaller in size, elliptic, oblong to ovate‑cordate, base auriculate and amplexicaul. Capitula corymbose‑paniculate; peduncles 4–12 mm. Involucres cylindric, 6–8 mm, 1.5–2 mm wide; phyllaries in 2 series, glabrous; outer ones small ovate, 0.5 – 1 × 0.3 – 0.5 mm, apex acute; inner ones lanceolate to linear, 6–8 × 0.8–1.5 mm, acute or obtuse, abaxial side with spongy thickening along midvein, sometimes bearing horn‑like structure below apex. Ligulate florets 10–15 per head, corolla yellow, 7–8 mm, lower tube about 2.5 mm, upper ligule 4–6 mm, apex 5‑lobed. Cypselae cylindric‑elliptic, black or blackish brown, 3.2–5 mm including the apical beak, obtusely 10–11‑ribbed, hirtellous along ribs, apex attenuate to form a thick and brown beak. Pappus white, minutely scaberulous, 3–4 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. L. T. Lo 524; Y. W. Lam 779; S. Y. Hu 8579 (CUHK).
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; Russia (Far East region), Mongolia, Korea, Japan.
Ecology: Margins of forests, open fields and wastelands. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Nov.

Pertya pungens Y. C. Tseng 尖苞帚菊
Guihaia 5(4): 334. 1985; FRPS 79: 16, pl. 3: 6 – 9. 1996; FGD 8: 240. 2007.

Subshrubs, up to 1 m tall; stem and branches densely pubescent. Leaves alternate; petiole 3–5 mm; leaf blade ovate, 3–5.5 × 2–4 cm, papery, base subtruncate, apex acute, margin remotely callous‑denticulate, 3‑nerved, pilose on both surfaces. Capitula of 7 florets, usually 2–4 in terminal clusters. Involucre narrowly campanulate, 1.6–1.9 × 0.6 cm; phyllaries ca. 7‑seriate, glabrous or only the outer ones pubescent abaxially, apices acute to acuminate, pungent, outer phyllaries ovate, 1.8–4 mm, inner ones 1.2–1.3 cm. Florets hermaphrodite, corolla tubular, ca. 1.3 cm, deeply 5‑lobed; lobes linear, 3–6.5 mm, unequal. Cypselae fusiform, 6–7 mm, white villous, ribbed. Pappus scabrous, 1 – 1.2 cm, brownish, connate at the base.

Locality: Ma On Shan. K. Y. Tam 102; F. W. Xing 7347, 7511.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi.
Ecology: Streamsides, margins of forests. Flowering: Oct.–Dec.
Notes: Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Pluchea indica (L.) Less. 闊苞菊
Linnaea 6: 150. 1831; FHK 179. 1861; FKH 143. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 20(3 – 4): 301. 1967; FRPS 75: 51. 1979; FTW ed. 2, 4: 1036. 1998; FGD 8: 162, fig. 88. 2007.
Baccharis indica L., Sp. Pl. 861. 1753.

Upright shrubs, (0.3–)1–2 m tall; stem striate‑sulcate, sparsely puberulent to tomentulose in younger parts, older parts nearly glabrous. Leaves sessile or shortly petiolate, obovate, 3–7 × 0.8–3 cm, with upper leaves gradually smaller, base attenuate‑cuneate, apex rounded or obtuse, margin irregularly dentate, but entire near the base, puberulent on both surfaces, midvein prominent on both sides. Capitula arranged in terminal or axillary corymbs; peduncles 3–10 mm, tomentulose hair relatively denser. Involucres cylindric when fresh, campanulate when dried, 4–6 mm; phyllaries in 5–6 series, ciliate along margin; outermost ones broadly ovate, 2.5 × 2 mm, apex obtuse; middle layers changed from ovate‑lanceolate to lanceolate, length increased from 3 to 4 mm, width decreased from 2 to 1 mm, apex obtuse to acute; innermost 5 × 0.7 mm, apex attenuate. Receptacle flat, fimbriate. Florets purple. Outer florets numerous, pistillate, corolla filiform‑tubular, 4–5 mm, limb finely 3–4‑lobed; style exserted, shortly branched, papillose; cypselae cylindric, ribbed, 0.5 – 0.8 mm, nearly glabrous; pappus uniseriate, white or greyish white, 4–5 mm. Disk hermaphrodite florets few, functionally staminate, corolla tubular, 5–6 mm, apex with 5 triangular lobes glandular outside; anther tubes greatly exserted; cypsela vestigial; pappus white or greyish white, 5 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. S. Y. Hu 12248 (CUHK); K. Y. Chan 1344 (CUHK); Y. S. Lau 746.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Myanmar, Indochina, Malaysia.
Ecology: Marshes near seaside, tidal flats, and sandy beaches, adapted to saline habitats. Flowering: Nearly all year round.
Uses: Food (young leaves).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Authority: Hemsl. ex F. B. Forbes & Hemsl.
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Cape D' Aguilar, Mai Po, Po Toi Islands
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Pluchea pteropoda Hemsl. 光梗闊苞菊（翅煙茜）
J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 23: 422. 1888; FKH 143. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 20(3–4): 302. 1967; FRPS 75: 51. 1979; FTW ed. 2, 4: 1036. 1998; FGD 8: 161. 2007.

Subshrubs or herbs 20–30 cm tall; stems procumbent to ascending, striate‑sulcate, subglabrous to sparsely puberulent, woody at base. Leaves slightly succulent, obovate, oblanceolate or somewhat obovate‑spatulate, 2–5 × 0.4–3 cm, base sessile, attenuate, apex obtuse or rounded, margin irregularly dentate, both surfaces glabrous; upper leaves appeared smaller in size. Capitula arranged into tight corymbs, peduncle 0.5–2 cm or subsessile. Involucres ovoid‑hemispherical, or broadly campanulate; phyllaries glabrous, in 5–6 series, outer ones broadly ovate, 2 mm across, apex obtuse to rounded; middle layers about 3–4 mm, lanceolate‑oblong, apex acute or obtuse; inner ones 4.5–5 × 0.5–1 mm, linear‑oblong, apex acute‑attenuate. Receptacle flat. Florets purple, outer female ones numerous, corolla filiform‑tubular, 4–5 mm, minutely 3–4‑dentate or truncate apically, glandular near apex. Central florets few, hermaphrodite, corolla tubular, 5 mm, apex bear 5 short triangular lobes with glands outside. Cypselae 0.8–1 mm, oblong, 4–5‑angulate, slightly hairy. Pappus uniseriate, white, 4–5 mm, persistent, those of marginal female florets free; those on central bisexual florets united at base.

Locality: Cape D’ Aguilar, Mai Po, Po Toi Islands. HK sheet 40465; S. Y. Hu 11523, 11967 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; Indochina.
Ecology: Coastal areas and tidal flats. Flowering: May–Jan. of the following year.

Porophyllum ruderale (Jacq.) Cass. 葩葩洛（暫名）
Dict. Sci. Nat. ed. 2, 43: 56. 1826; Fl. N. Amer. 21: 233 – 234. 2006.
Kleinia ruderalis Jacq., Enum. Syst. Pl. 8, 28. 1760.

Annual herbs, 30–80 cm tall. Stems erect and branched, glabrous. Leaves odorous, simple and alternate, elliptic, 1.5–3.5 × 0.5–2 cm, base attenuate, apex obtuse to rounded and mucronulate, both surfaces glabrous, midvein prominent on lower side, margin entire and somewhat undulate, with linear oil glands 1–2 mm long growing along leaf margin; petiole 0.3–1.2 cm. Capitula homogamous, discoid, in corymbose arrangement; peduncles 3–6 cm, glabrous. Involucres herbaceous green, cylindric, 1.8–2 × 0.3–0.4 cm wide; phyllaries 1‑seriate, united at anthesis, without calycule at base, divided into 5 linear‑lanceolate involucral bracts and gradually spread out at fruiting stage, each segment 1.2–2 mm broad, margin scarious, apex acuminate or acute. Receptacle small and plain, alveolate, areoles sometimes with remnants of vascular tissue after fruit dispersal. All florets bisexual and fertile, about 50–60 per head or more, corolla yellow, slightly hairy outside, 13 mm, lower part slender filiform‑tubular with length 11–11.5 mm, upper part broaden as funnelform with length 1.5–2 mm, apex 5‑lobed, lobes acute‑ovate; anther bases rounded, apical appendages ovate and acute; stylar branches approximately 3 mm, exserted outside the involucres, bearing hairy subulate apical appendages. Cypselae narrow cylindric, 8 × 0.5–0.6 mm, black or blackish brown, hirtellous with brown adpressed hair pointing upward. Pappus persistent, 8–10 mm, capillary, pale brown.

Locality: Tai Po, Fung Yuen. S. Y. Hu & P. P. H. But 24093, 24097 (CUHK).
Distribution: SW United States, Mexico, West Indies, C & S America.
Ecology: Flowering: May–Sep.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Naturalized and widely distributed in Hong Kong
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Praxelis clematidea (Griesb.) R. M. King & H. Rob. 假臭草
Phytologia 20: 194. 1970.
Eupatorium clematideum Griseb., Jahresber. Pollichia 22–24: 258. 1866.
Eupatorium catarium Veldkamp, Gard. Bull. Singapore 51(1): 121. 1999; FGD 8: 214. 2007; Check List HK Plants 281. 2002; 96. 2004.

Perennial erect herbs 0.3–1 m tall, malodorous, covered with soft multicellular hairs, denser on branches and peduncles. Leaves ovate, trinerved, 2.5–5.5 × 1–4 cm, base cuneate, apex acute, margin coarsely serrate with 5 – 8 teeth on each side, scarcely puberulent on adaxial surfaces, pilose and denser on abaxial surface, especially along margin and veins; petioles 0.3–1.5 cm. Capitula in terminal simple or compound cyme. Involucres cylindric campanulate, 7–8 × 3–4 mm; phyllaries in 4–5 series, easily shed off, scarious and translucent with several yellowish green veins, apex caudate or long‑acuminate; outer smaller, ovate‑lanceolate, 4 × 1 mm, slightly hairy; middle lanceolate, 5–6 × 1.5 mm, sparsely ciliate; inner linear‑oblong, 6–7 × 1 mm, glabrous. Receptacle highly conical with phyllaries shed off at the fruiting stage. Florets blue or violet, corolla 3 – 4.5 mm, shortly 5‑lobbed; stylar branches 2 mm, exserted. Cypsela oblong, 4‑ribbed, 2–2.5 mm, black and slightly hairy. Pappus capillary, 4 mm, white, persistent.

Locality: Naturalized and widely distributed in Hong Kong. Y. Wong 037 (CUHK); S. Y. Hu 19958 (CUHK); Y. W. Lam 1130.
Distribution: Native to S America; naturalized in S Guangdong; SE Asia, Australia.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides. Flowering: Nearly all year round.
Notes: As a weed.

Pseudelephantopus spicatus (Juss. ex Aublet) C. F. Baker 假地膽草
Trans. Acad. Sci. St. Louis 12(5): 55. 1902; S. Y. Hu, Quart, J. Taiwan Mus. 20(3 – 4): 305. 1967; FRPS 74: 47. 1985; FTW ed. 2, 4: 1041. 1998.
Elephantopus spicatus Juss. ex Aublet, Hist. Pl. Guiane 2: 808. 1775; FKH 139. 1912.

Perennial herbs 45–100 cm tall; stem erect, striate, subglabrous on lower portion, pilose and glandular upward, hairs appearing denser on inflorescence branches. Leaves oblanceolate‑spatulate, 7–22 × 1–6 cm, base gradually attenuate to a short sheath, subamplexicaul, apex obtuse to rounded, margin with callous teeth or entire, pinnately‑veined, pilose on adaxial surfaces, along margins and midveins on abaxial surface, densely punctate abaxially. Upper leaves linear to linear‑lanceolate, 1–11 × 0.1–1 cm, smaller in size especially those on branches. Capitula sessile, solitary or 2–6 clustered into axillary aggregates without stalks, arranged as spicate‑panicle. Involucres oblong‑ellipsoidal, 1–1.2 × 0.3–0.4 cm; phyllaries distal half or 1/3 dark green, sparsely pilose and glandular, apex acuminate‑aristate, margin scarious, midvein prominent, in 2 series with 4 involucral bracts in each layer; outer ones ovate, 5–6 × 3 mm; inner ones oblong, twice longer than the outer ones, 1–1.2 mm. Florets 4 per capitulum, corolla white, 6–7 mm, 5 lanceolate apical lobes. Cypselae linear‑oblong, densely hairy and glandular, 10‑ribbed, 6–7 mm. Pappus few, bristle‑like but slender, dilated and scarious at base, unequal in length, usually with 2 longer and folded as sigmoid near apex.

Locality: Naturalized. S. Y. Hu & P. P. H. But 19973, 23090; L. T. Lo 480.
Distribution: Guangdong, Taiwan (naturalized); tropical America and Africa.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides near villages. Flowering: Jan.–May.

Pterocypsela indica (L.) C. Shih 翅果菊（山萵苣）
Acta Phytotax. Sin. 26(5): 387. 1988; FRPS 80(1): 229. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 4: 1043. 1998; FGD 8: 264. 2007.
Lactuca brevirostris Champ., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 4: 237. 1852; FHK 192. 1861; FKH 150. 1912.
Lactuca indica L., Mant. Pl. 278. 1771.

Large annual or biennial herbs; stem glabrous, erect, 0.5–2 m tall, branched apically. Leaves glabrous above and beneath. Lower leaves deciduous upon fruiting stage. Middle cauline leaves sessile, linear or linear‑lanceolate, 8.5–31 × 0.5–3 cm, not divided, base cuneate, apex acuminate, margin entire or mucronate near base. Upper leaves linear, smaller in size. Capitula homogamous with all florets ligulate and hermaphrodite, paniculate or racemose‑paniculate at terminal; peduncles 5–25 mm, bearing several linear‑subulate bracteoles. Involucres ovoid‑cylindric, 13–15 × 4–5 mm; phyllaries in 4 series, thick in texture, glabrous abaxially, margin and apex tinged purplish red and narrowly membranous; outer ones ovate, 2.5–3.5 × 1–2 mm, apex acute or obtuse; median ones ovate‑oblong, 5–8 × 2–2.5 mm, acute or obtuse; inner ones linear‑lanceolate, 13–14 × 2 mm, rounded. Ligulate florets 21–27 per head, corolla yellow, 12–14 mm, lower tube 4–4.5 mm, densely hairy near summit, ligule 8–9 mm, apex 5‑lobed. Cypselae black, elliptic, 3–4 × 1.8–2 mm, compressed, lateral margins thicken as wings, apex acute or acuminate, forming pale brown rostrum 1–1.5 mm, 1‑striate on each side. Pappus 2‑seriate, parachute‑like at the end of the rostrum, 7–8 mm, white.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 2072; Y. S. Lau 2629; S. Y. Hu 7840 (CUHK).
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; Indochina, India, Malaysia, Japan, Russia (Far East region).
Ecology: Margins of forests, wastelands. Flowering: Jul.–Nov.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Sha Tin, Ng Tung Chai, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Pterocypsela laciniata (Houtt.) C. Shih 多裂翅果菊
Acta Phytotax. Sin. 26(5): 388. 1988; FRPS 80(1): 230. 1997; FGD 8: 265. 2008.
Prenanthes laciniata Houtt., Nat. Hist. 10: 381. 1779.

Perennial herbs; stem erect, 0.6–2 m tall, stout, branched apically, glabrous. Lower and middle cauline leaves glabrous on both sides, oblanceolate, elliptic or oblong, 13–25 × 8–10 cm, or much larger, leaf base cuneate and sessile, regularly or irregularly 1–2‑pinnatisect, apical lobes long‑linear or sometimes lanceolate, primary lateral segments 1–5 pairs, elongate‑triangular, lanceolate or falcate, gradually smaller downward; secondary lateral segments linear or triangular, length various; all lobes apex mostly acuminate or sometimes acute, margin mucronulate. Upper leaves smaller in size, divided similarly as the middle leaves, or undivided and appearing linear. Capitula many, arranged as panicles at terminal, homogamous with all florets ligulate and bisexual; peduncles 0.5–3 cm, bearing few small ovate bracteoles. Involucres ovoid‑cylindric, 13–14 × 4–5 mm; phyllaries 4–5‑seriate, acute or obtuse apically, glabrous abaxially, margin and apex thinly membranous and tinged reddish purple; outer ones ovate, 2–3 × 1–2 mm; median ones ovate‑oblong, 4–5 × 1.8–2.2 mm; inner ones linear‑lanceolate or linear‑oblong, 8–13 × 1.2–2 mm. Ligulate florets about 21 per head, corolla yellow, 12–14 mm, lower tube 6–7 mm, densely hairy near summit, ligule 6–7 mm, 5‑lobed at distal end. Cypselae elliptic, compressed, black, 4 × 2–2.1 mm, margin thickly winged, 1‑striate on each side, apex with pale brown beak 1–1.2 mm. Pappus 2‑seriate, growing on the beak, white, 6–8 mm.

Locality: Sha Tin, Ng Tung Chai, Lantau Island. S. Y. Hu 12132 (CUHK); Y. W. Lam 641; HK sheet 34062.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; also in Japan, Russia (Far East region).
Ecology: Margins of forests, wastelands. Flowering: Jul.–Oct.

Pterocypsela raddeana (Maxim.) C. Shih 毛脈翅果菊
Acta Phytotax. Sin. 26(5): 386. 1988; FRPS 80(1): 227. 1997.
Lactuca raddeana Maxim., Bull. Acad. Imp. Sci. Saint‑Petersbourg 19: 526. 1874.

Biennial or perennial herbs; stem erect, 0.8–2 m tall; branched apically, usually densely hairy in lower portion, glabrous above. Leaves sessile, scabrous on upper surfaces, pilose along veins and margins on lower surfaces. Lower and middle cauline leaves elliptic‑oblong, 7–13.5 × 2–5.5 cm, or much larger in size, lyrately pinnatilobed, pinnatifid to pinnatisect, apical lobes larger than the lateral lobes, rarely equal‑sized, deltoid, ovate‑deltoid, subrhomboid or ovate‑lanceolate, apex acute or acuminate, margin shallowly and irregularly dentate‑sinuate; lateral segments 1–3 pairs, triangular or elliptic, acute, margin mucronulate. Upper leaves smaller, ovate, elliptic, oblong or ovate‑elliptic, acute or acuminate. Capitula homogamous, with all florets ligulate and bisexual, numerous at terminal forming narrow panicle. Peduncles 5–15 mm, bearing few small bracteoles. Involucres ovoid‑cylindric, 7–8 mm; phyllaries 4‑seriate, pale purplish red; outer ones ovate‑triangular, 1–1.5 × 0.5–1.5 mm, acute; middle ones ovate‑oblong, 2–3 × 1–1.5 mm, obtuse; inner ones linear‑lanceolate, 6 – 8 × 1.2–1.5 mm, obtuse. Ligulate florets yellow, lower tube densely hairy near summit, ligule 5‑toothed at apex. Cypselae elliptic, brown or reddish brown, compressed, each side 3‑striate, margin thickly winged, apex with beak 0.1–0.5 mm. Pappus in 2 series, growing on the beak, white, 4–6 mm.

Locality: Ma On Shan. S. Y. Hu 10554, 12045 (CUHK); HK sheet 30425.
Distribution: Widely distributed in S, E, C, N & NE China.
Ecology: Thickets and cultivated areas. Flowering: May–Sep.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Stanley, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Saussurea japonica (Thunb.) DC. 風毛菊
Ann. Mus. Natl. Hist. Nat. 16: 203. 1810; FHK 167. 1861; FKH 149. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 20(3 – 4): 330. 1967; FTW ed. 2, 4: 1049. 1998; FRPS 78(2): 47. 1999.
Serratula japonica Thunb., Fl. Jap. 305. 1784.
Saussurea linearis Champ. ex Benth., Hooker's Journ. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 4: 235. 1852.

Biennial or perennial herbs; stem erect, 0.5–2 m tall, striate, not winged, densely pubescent and glandular. Lower leaves petiolate, petioles 2–12 cm, narrowly winged, leaf blade lanceolate, elliptic to oblong, 6–22 × 3–9.5 cm, pinnately toothed, pinnatifid to pinnatisect, or sometimes not lobed and appeared as lanceolate form, apical lobes lanceolate, lateral lobes 3–7 pairs with shape varied from triangular, lanceolate to linear, the middle ones largest, others gradually smaller towards both ends; all lobes apices obtuse to rounded, margin entire or shallowly toothed. Median cauline leaves shortly petiolate, linear‑lanceolate, pinnatilobed or not, margin entire or toothed. Upper leaves sessile, much smaller, linear‑lanceolate, linear to bract‑like, entire or slightly toothed. All leaves densely glandular and pubescent on both surfaces. Capitula many, arranged as corymbs or corymbose panicles; peduncles 0.5–2 cm, densely glandular and hairy. Involucres cylindric, 10–12 × 5–8 mm; phyllaries 6‑seriate, abaxial side covered with glands and cobwebby‑tomentose hair, 1‑veined at the centre, all bearing purple‑red membranous apical appendages which are orbicular and with margin toothed; excluding the appendages, outer few layers of phyllaries ovate, 1.8–4 × 1–2 mm, mostly herbaceous; median ones lanceolate to lanceolate‑oblong, 3.5–8 × 1–2 mm, basal portion coriaceous and distal portion herbaceous; inner ones lanceolate to linear, 8–10 × 1 – 1.5 mm, leathery almost to the distal end. Receptacle densely fringed with hair about 5–7 mm. Florets bisexual and fertile, corolla purple, tubular, 1–1.2 cm, lower tube filiform, 6–7 mm, upper limb 5–6 mm, deeply cleft into 5 linear‑lanceolate lobes about 4 mm. Cypselae brown, cylindric and obtusely 4‑angled, 2.5 – 3 × 1 mm, with minute rostrum at apex. Pappus 2‑seriate; outer layers capillary, 2–3 mm, deciduous individually; inner layers plumose, 7–8 mm, united at base, shed off as a ring.

Locality: Stanley, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 1348, 3008; Y. W. Lam 461.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; also in Korea, Japan.
Ecology: Grassy hillslopes, wastelands. Flowering: Jun.–Dec.

Senecio scandens Buch.‑Ham. ex D. Don 千里光
Prodr. Fl. Nepal. 178. 1825; FKH 148. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 21(1–2): 143. 1968; FTW ed. 2, 4: 1056. 1998; FRPS 77(1): 294. 1999; FGD 8: 218, fig. 130. 2007.
Senecio chinensis (Spreng.) DC., Prodr. 6: 363. 1838; FHK 190. 1861.
Cineraria chinensis Spreng., Syst. Veg. 3: 549. 1826.

Perennial herbs with rhizomes; stem elongate and reclining, from 0.5–5 m, striate, branches many, pubescent or glabrescent, turning woody when old. Leaf petioles 0.5–2 cm, pubescent or subglabrous; leaf blade ovate lanceolate to elongate‑deltoid in shape, 4.5–8 × 1.5–4.5 cm, base broadly cuneate or truncate, apex acuminate, margin irregularly dentate, pinnately‑veined, adaxial surfaces subglabrous or puberulous, abaxial surfaces puberulous especially along veins. Leaves in upper stem portion appeared smaller in size, lanceolate to linear‑lanceolate, apex attenuate. Capitula heterogamous and radiate, 2–2.2 cm across, arranged as compound thyrse form; peduncles 0.7–2.5 cm, puberulous. Involucres cylindric campanulate, 6–7 × 3 mm, base with about 8 linear‑subulate bracteoles as calyculus of 2–3 mm; phyllaries 12–13, herbaceous, linear‑lanceolate, acuminate, margin scarious and ciliate near the apex, abaxially puberulous or glabrous, 3‑veined. Marginal ligulate florets 7– 10, tube 4 mm, ligule oblong with length 9–10 mm, width 2 mm, apex obtuse and minutely 3‑lobed, colour yellow, with 4 veins. Disk tubular florets 5–6 mm, funnelform with apical half broaden and lower half narrowed, 5‑lobed at apex, yellow. Cypselae cylindric, 3 × 0.7–0.8 mm, ribbed, brown, puberulous. Pappus white, 5–6 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. S. Y. Hu 12410 (CUHK); Y. Wong 084 (CUHK); Y. S. Lau 1370.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Bhutan, Nepal, Japan, Indochina, Philippines.
Ecology: Margins of forests, thickets. Flowering: Nov.–Feb. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Kowloon Peak, Fo Tan, Shing Mun, High Island, Po Toi Islands, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Senecio stauntonii DC. 閩粵千里光
Prodr. 6: 363. 1838; FHK 190. 1861; FKH 148. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 21(1–2): 146. 1968; FRPS 77(1): 293. 1999; FGD 8: 219. 2007.

Perennial rhizomatous herbs; stem ascending and subscandent, 30–100 cm tall, angular, branched, glabrous. Basal leaves withered at flowering stage. Cauline leaves sessile, narrowly oblong‑lanceolate, 4–14.5 × 0.6– 2.5 cm, base auriculate and semi‑amplexicaul, apex acuminate to attenuate, margin toothed, pinnately‑veined, pubescent or pilose on adaxial surfaces, and along veins and margins on abaxial sides, sometimes glabrous beneath. Upper leaves smaller and narrower. Capitula heterogamous and radiate, in loose corymbose arrangement; peduncle 1.5–3 cm, glabrous or loosely puberulous. Involucres campanulate; phyllaries 13 in 1 series, herbaceous, linear‑lanceolate, 6–8 × 1–1.5 mm, apex acute or acuminate, margin scarious and ciliate near apex, abaxial surface glabrous, base with 6–8 linear‑subulate bracteoles 2–3 mm. Marginal ray florets female, ligule oblong, 7–8 × 2.5–3 mm, tube 3.5 mm, apex obtuse and minutely 3‑lobed, 4‑veined, colour yellow. Disk tubular florets bisexual, funnelform, 6–6.5 mm, apical half broaden, lower half narrowed, apex 5‑lobed and papillose hairy, yellow. Cypselae brown, cylindric, 3 mm, ribbed and puberulent. Pappus white, 5–5.5 mm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Kowloon Peak, Fo Tan, Shing Mun, High Island, Po Toi Islands, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 778; S. Y. Hu 6318, 8878 (CUHK).
Distribution: Guangdong, Fujian.
Ecology: Wastelands, margins of forests. Flowering: Sep.–Dec.

Siegesbeckia orientalis L. 豨薟
Sp. Pl. 2: 900. 1753; FHK 182. 1861; FKH 145. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 21(3 – 4): 158. 1968; FRPS 75: 339, pl. 57: 4. 1979; FTW ed. 2, 4: 1062, pl. 506, photo 488. 1998.

Annual erect herbs; stem 30–100 cm tall, branched somewhat dichotomously, pubescent, hair multicellular and appeared denser on upper branches. Basal leaves withered at flowering stage; cauline ones papery, ovate‑triangular to ovate‑lanceolate, 3–12 × 1–7 cm, base broadly cuneate and narrowed down to form winged petiole, apex acute, margin irregularly toothed, pubescent on both surfaces, glandular abaxially, triplinerved; upper leaves smaller in size, elliptic, shortly petiolate or subsessile, shallowly serrate or subentire. Capitula heterogamous, radiate, 1–2 cm across, loosely arranged as panicles; peduncles 1–4 cm, densely pubescent. Involucres hemispherical; phyllaries herbaceous, hairy and stipitate purplish brown glandular, apex rounded, 2‑seriate; outer phyllaries 5–6, linear‑spatulate, spreading, 7–11 × 0.5–1 mm; inner ones obovate‑oblong, 3–4 × 1.2–2 mm, enclosing the hypanthium of marginal florets. Receptacle small; paleae obovate, 3–3.5 mm, puberulent and sparsely glandular on abaxial side, curved and enveloping the cypselae of disk florets. Florets yellow. Marginal female florets ligulate, corolla tube 1 mm, glandular and hairy, ligule 1.2 mm and 3‑lobed. Disk bisexual florets tubular, corolla 1.5 mm, 5‑lobed; anthers slightly exserted, basal lobes obtuse, apical appendages ovate‑lanceolate elongate; stylar branches very short and slightly flattened, rugose on the abaxial surface. Cypselae blackish brown, 3–3.5 mm, oblique‑tetragonous, narrowed basally, a short crown protruded at apex, glabrous. Pappus absent.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. L. T. Lo 34; H. Y. Yeung 82 (CUHK); S. Y. Hu 11524 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Gansu, Shaanxi, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; E Asia, Europe, tropical America.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides near villages. Flowering & fruiting: Mar.–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Solidago decurrens Lour. 一枝黃花
Fl. Cochinch. 501. 1790; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 21(3–4): 160. 1968; FRPS 74: 75. 1985; FGD 8: 190, fig. 109. 2007.
Solidago virgaurea var. leiocarpa (Benth.) A. Gray, Mem. Amer. Acad. Arts, n. s. 4: 395. 1857; FTW ed. 2, 4: 1064. 1998.
Solidago virgaurea auct. non L.: FHK 179; FKH 140. 1912.

Perennial erect herb, 25–80 cm tall, simple or branching on upper portion. Radical leaves ovate, oblong or lanceolate, 3–7 × 2–3 cm, base cuneate‑attenuate to form long winged petiole of 2–13 cm or more. Cauline leaves similar in shape, 2–5 × 1–2 cm, short‑petiolate, base cuneate, apex acute or acuminate, margin serrate or subserrate, much smaller in size upward, sparsely puberulous along margin, subglabrous on both surfaces. Capitula in tight or loose racemes or panicles. Involucres campanulate, 5–7 mm in diam.; phyllaries 3–4‑seriate; the outer ones ovate‑lanceolate, ca. 2 mm; the inner ones lanceolate‑oblong, ca. 6 mm. Ligulate florets pistillate, corolla yellow, ca. 8 mm; tubular florets bisexual, corolla yellow, ca. 4 mm. Cypsela glabrous or puberulous above, cylindric.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. Y. Yeung 163 (CUHK); S. Y. Hu 7168 (CUHK); Y. W. Lam 663.
Distribution: Widely distributed in S, SW, C & E China.
Ecology: Margins of forests, grassy slopes. Flowering: Oct.–Apr. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Kong Sin Wan, Wu Kai Sha, Tai Po, Fanling, Sheung Shui, Yuen Long, Lamma Island, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Soliva anthemifolia (Juss.) Sweet 裸柱菊
Hort. Brit. 243. 1826; FKH 146. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 21(3 – 4): 162. 1968; FRPS 76(1): 135. 1983; FTW ed. 2, 4: 1068. 1998.
Gymnostyles anthemifolia Juss., Ann. Mus. Natl. Hist. Nat. 4: 262. 1804.

Small prostrate annual herbs; stem short and seems to be stemless, stoloniferous. Leaves alternate, forming rosette at base, petioles 2–3 cm, leaf blade spatulate or oblanceolate, 3–13 × 1–2.5 cm, 2–3‑pinnatisect with segments linear‑elliptic, apex acute, margin entire or irregularly 1–3‑dentate, subglabrous or villose on both surfaces. Capitula subglobose, 7–11 mm in diam., sessile and axillary to leaves, solitary or sometimes with few heads aggregated at basal nodes. Involucres dish‑like; phyllaries 2‑seriate, ovate‑lanceolate, apex acuminate, herbaceous with margin scarious, hairy on abaxial side; outer phyllaries 3–3.5 mm long, 1–1.2 mm wide; inner ones 3–4 × 0.3–0.6 mm. Receptacle convex, naked. Outer florets in many series, female, corolla absent with pistil only, fertile; style minutely divided. Central florets few, about 8–12, bisexual but usually functionally staminate, corolla tubular, yellow, 1.2–2 mm, apex 3‑lobed, base narrowed; stamens 3, anthers enclosed, base obtuse, apical appendages acute; style without branches, apex capitate and flat. Cypselae oblanceolate, 2–2.5 × 0.8– 1.1 mm, dorsiventrally compressed, margin with thicken rugose wings which extended to the apex, colour brown with the wings orange‑brown, villous near the apical region, style persistent. Pappus none.

Locality: Kong Sin Wan, Wu Kai Sha, Tai Po, Fanling, Sheung Shui, Yuen Long, Lamma Island, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 1774, 1792; S. Y. Hu 6772 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; native to S America.
Ecology: Wastelands, cultivated lands. Flowering: Dec.–Apr. of the following year.

Sonchus arvensis L. 苣蕒菜
Sp. Pl. 793. 1753; FKH 151. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 21(3 – 4): 162. 1968; FRPS 80(1): 64. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 4: 1071. 1998; FGD 8: 260, fig. 161. 2007.

Perennial lactiferous herbs; stem erect, 0.3–1.5(–2) m tall, striate, apically branched, the upper stem portion, branches and peduncles covered with yellow to dark purple stipitate glandular hair. Basal and lower leaves oblanceolate to oblanceolate‑oblong, 6–30 × 1.5–7.5 cm, mostly simple, occasionally lyrately pinnatilobed or pinnatifid with several lateral lobes hemispherical, semi‑elliptic, ovate to deltoid, sometimes oblique; while apical lobes larger, ovate, ovate‑oblong to elliptic; leaf upper and lower surfaces glabrous, margin minutely denticulate or mucronulate; radical leaves with base narrowed and apex obtuse‑rounded; lower leaves with base auriculate and semi‑amplexicaul; apex obtuse to acute. Middle and upper leaves gradually smaller, lanceolate or linear, base sessile and semi‑amplexicaul, apex acute, auriculate or not. Capitula 2 cm across, in corymbose arrangement or sub‑umbelliform. Involucres campanulate‑urceolate with base slightly swollen, 14–15 × 6–8 mm; phyllaries herbaceous green, abaxial side stipitate glandular, margin hyaline, apex acute or acuminate, in 3–4 rows; outer series elongate‑triangular to lanceolate, 4–5 × 1–1.8 mm; middle ones lanceolate, 6–8.5 × 1.8–2.5 mm; inner layers linear, 10–13 × 1.5–2.5 mm. All florets yellow, hermaphrodite and fertile, corolla ligulate, 13 – 15 mm, lower tube 8–9 mm, hairy near the summit, ligule 5–5.5 mm, apex minutely 5‑lobed. Cypselae brown, ellipsoidal, somewhat compressed, 3–3.2 × 0.8–1 mm, narrowed at both ends, glabrous, ribbed, transversely rugose. Pappus white, 7–8 mm, capillary and slender, entangled with each other, deciduous.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. L. T. Lo 231; Y. S. Lau 87; S. Y. Hu 13053 (CUHK).
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; also in Europe.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides, cultivated lands. Flowering & fruiting: Jan.–Sep.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Naturalized and widely distributed in Hong Kong
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Sonchus oleraceus L. 苦苣菜
Sp. Pl. 794. 1753; FHK 194. 1861; FKH 151. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 21(3 – 4): 164. 1968; FRPS 80(1): 63. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 4: 1073. 1998; FGD 8: 260. 2007.

Annual or biennial herbs; stem erect, 30–150 cm tall, simple or branched in upper portion, striate, glabrous except the apical branches and peduncles covered with stipitate glandular hair. Basal leaves oblanceolate, lyrately pinnatifid or pinnatisect, base attenuate and narrowed down to form winged petiole, apex rounded or obtuse, margin toothed. Cauline leaves oblanceolate or elliptic, pinnatisect or lyrately pinnatisect, 4–20 × 1.8–9 cm, base abruptly narrowed down to form winged petiole, wing gradually broaden towards the base, forming circular auricles, semi‑amplexicaul, margin and auricle unequally mucronate and spiny, apical lobes broadly triangular, broadly hastate or ovate‑cordate; lateral lobes 1–5 pairs, elliptic to lanceolate, pointing backward, apices of all lobes acuminate, acute or obtuse. Upper leaves similar in shape, or appearing lanceolate to linear‑lanceolate, base widen and semi‑amplexicaul, apex acute to acuminate, margin entire, toothed throughout or on the apical half only. All leaves glabrous above and beneath. Capitula few, arranged as tight corymbs or racemes at branch terminals, or solitary. Involucres broad‑campanulate, 1 cm × 0.6–0.7 cm; phyllaries 3–4‑seriate, imbricate, stipitate glandular hairy on midvein or not, membranous along margin and apex, minutely hairy near apex; outer two layers lanceolate or elongat‑triangular, 3–7 × 1–1.5 mm; middle and inner ones lanceolate to linear‑lanceolate, 8–10 × 1.5–2 mm. All florets yellow, ligulate, about 10 mm, ligule 5 – 5.5 mm, 5‑toothed at apex, lower tube 4– 5 mm, hairy near summit. Cypselae brown, ellipsoidal or oblanceolate‑ellipsoidal, 3 × 1 mm, flattened, ribbed, transversely rugose, without hair, apex narrowed, beakless. Pappus white, 6–7 mm, capillary and entangled with each other.

Locality: Naturalized and widely distributed in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 3115; Y. W. Lam 724, 764.
Distribution: Native to Europe and C Asia; widely distributed in China.
Ecology: Wastelands. Flowering & fruiting: Jan.–Jul.
Uses: Food (vegetable), medicinal (folklore).

Spilanthes grandiflora Turcz. 大花金鈕扣
Bull. Soc. Imp. Naturalistes Moscou 24: 185. 1851.
Acmella grandflora (Turcz.) R. K. Jansen, Syst. Bot. Monogr. 8: 75. 1985.

Perennial herbs, 20–70 cm tall; stems erect to ascending or rarely decumbent, glabrous to moderately pilose. Petioles 2–12.5 mm, glabrous to moderately pilose; leaf blade ovate‑lanceolate or lanceolate, rarely ovate, 2.5– 8 × 0.3–3 cm, base attenuate, apex acute to acuminate or rounded, usually glabrous to sparsely pilose adaxially, glabrous to usually sparsely or moderately pilose abaxially, margin entire to very coarsely and irregularly dentate, sparsely to moderately ciliate. Capitula radiate, solitary, or several arranged as loose panicles, ovoid in shape, 7.5–15.5 × 5.5–11.5 mm. Peduncles 4–37 cm, glabrous to moderately pilose. Receptacle cylindric‑conical, 4.5–11.5 mm high, 0.9–2.7 mm in diam., apex acuminate. Phyllaries triseriate, lanceolate to narrowly ovate, apex acute. Pales 4.1–6.8 × 0.5–1.2 mm, apex acute to acuminate, stramineous. Ray florets 11–12, greatly exceeding the phyllaries; corollas yellow, tube 1.3 – 2.0 mm, limb 4.1–10.3 × 1.1–3.3 mm; cypselae 1.5 – 2.5 mm. Disk corollas 2.5–3 mm; anthers usually black; cypselae 2 – 2.7 mm. Pappus usually of 3 subequal bristles, 0.7 – 1.1 mm, or pappus absent.

Locality: Kowloon Reservoirs, Shing Mun. Y. S. Lau 2438, 3014.
Distribution: Widely distributed in tropical and subtropical regions.
Ecology: Wastelands. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Nov.

Spilanthes paniculata Wall. ex DC. 金鈕扣
Prodr. 5: 625. 1836; FRPS 75: 359, pl. 61: 1 – 2. 1979; FGD 8: 126, fig. 63. 2007.
Acmella paniculata (Wall. ex DC.) R. K. Jansen, Syst. Bot. Monogr. 8: 67. 1985; FTW ed. 2, 4: 814, pl. 376, photo 406. 1998.

Annual herbs; stems erect or ascending, rooting at nodes when lower portion of stem touched the ground, 20–60(–100) cm tall, branched, striate, subglabrous or sparsely puberulent, tinged purple. Petioles 0.3–2 cm, glabrous or loosely hairy; Leaves ovate to ovate‑lanceolate, 1.5–7 × 0.5–3.5 cm, base cuneate and decurrent to the petiole, apex acute, margin irregularly serrate or undulate‑serrate, sometimes entire, both surfaces glabrous. Capitula solitary, or several arranged as loose panicles, ovoid in shape, 6–11 × 5–10 mm, with or without ligulate florets. Peduncles 1.5–6 cm, sparsely puberulent near the head. Involucre like a shallow dish, bearing one series of herbaceous phyllaries, subtending the ligulate florets if present, ovate to ovate‑oblong, 2.8–4 × 1.2–2 mm, apex acute to obtuse, glabrous but ciliate along margin. Receptacle cylindric‑conical, 5 – 7 mm high, longer than the phyllaries. Paleae scarious, cymbiform, enfolding the hypanthia of disk florets, 2.2–4.5 × 1–2 mm. Florets yellow or white, fertile. Ray florets 4–6, with ligule broadly obovate, 1.5–2 mm, apex 3 rounded lobes, tube 1 mm, pubescent. Tubular florets 1.3–2 mm, usually 4‑toothed at apex; anthers included, base obtuse, apical appendages broad‑ovate; stylar branches short, apex truncate, penicillate. Cypselae black, obovate‑oblong, 1.5–2.5 mm, the marginal ones 3‑angled, the disk ones bilaterally flattened, both with concave apices, several hair growing near the summit, densely ciliate along margin. Pappus absent or of 2 unequal awns.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. W. Lam 546, 1348; S. Y. Hu 8981 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; Malaysia, S & SE Asia.
Ecology: Roadsides and wastelands near villages. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Naturalized and widely distributed in Hong Kong
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Synedrella nodiflora (L.) Gaertn. 金腰箭
Fruct. Sem. Pl. 2(3): 456. 1791; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 21(3 – 4): 173. 1968; FRPS 75: 363, pl. 61: 3 – 6. 1979; FGD 8: 132, fig. 68. 2007; FTW ed. 2, 4: 1075, pl. 513. 1998.
Verbesina nodiflora L., Cent. Pl. 1: 28. 1755.

Annual herbs; stem erect, 30–120 cm tall, dichotomously branched, appressed pilose, or glabrous in lower part. Leaves ovate to ovate‑lanceolate, middle cauline ones 3–12.5 × 1.2–6 cm, base decurrent to form winged petiole of 0.5–4 cm, apex acute, adaxial surface dark green, abaxial surface paler, both surfaces appressed pubescent, hair denser abaxially, triplinerved, margin crenulate‑serrulate. Upper leaves smaller. Capitula 8–10 × 4–5 mm, mostly sessile or sometimes shortly pedunculate, always with 2–6 heads aggregated in axil or at branch terminal. Involucres ovoid‑oblong; phyllaries few; outermost 2 phyllaries foliaceous green, lanceolate, 8–10 × 2.5 mm, apex acute, pubescent; inner phyllaries scarious, oblong, 6–7 × 2–3 mm, obtuse, glabrous or sparsely puberulent, shortly ciliate along margin, subtending the ray florets. Receptacle small; paleae linear, 6–7 × 0.5–1 mm, margin minutely ciliate, subtending the disk florets. Ray pistillate florets yellow, 3.2–3.5 mm, ligule elliptic, 2 rounded lobes at apex, tube nearly as long as the ligule. Disk florets bisexual, tubular, 3.2 – 3.5 mm, 4‑lobed at apex, yellow. All florets fertile. Cypselae developed from ligulate florets obovate‑oblong, 4 × 1 mm, compressed and slightly curved inward, black in colour, margin with brownish white broad and hard wings, bearing 4–6 pairs of upward‑directed spines; pappus 2 straight hard spines about 2 mm. Cypselae developed from tubular florets oblong‑cuneate, flat or subtrigonous, 4–4.5 × 0.8–1 mm, black or blackish brown, tuberculate, pubescent; pappus 2–4, spiny, 3–4 mm, pale brown.
