Locality: Naturalized and widely distributed in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 2039; H. Y. Yeung 46 (CUHK); S. Y. Hu 5810 (CUHK).
Distribution: Native to America, widely naturalized in tropical and subtropical regions.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides near villages. Flowering: Jun.–Oct.

Tagetes erecta L. 萬壽菊
Sp. Pl. 887. 1753; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 21(3–4): 176. 1968; FRPS 75: 389. 1979; FGD 8: 144, fig. 78. 2007.

Stout annual erect and branched herbs, 50–100 cm tall or more; stem striate, glabrous. Leaves opposite to alternate, odd‑pinnatifid, 5–15 × 4–8 cm, leaflets lanceolate‑oblong, lateral segments 4–7 pairs, margin serrate, apex acute, some teeth with long awns at tips when young, glandular‑dotted along the margin below the teeth. Capitula solitary and terminal to branches, 5–8 cm across; peduncle 5–10(–15) cm, the upper part cylindrically inflated. Involucres 1.5–2 × 0.7–1.5 cm, single series of phyllaries united as a cylindric‑campanulate tube with triangular lobes at top, glandular‑dotted. Florets yellow to dull orange in colour. Ray ones with fan‑shaped obovate ligule, 1.4–1.8 × 1.2–1.4 cm, apex broadly 2‑lobed, subtruncate and undulate, tube about 1 cm. Disk tubular florets 0.9 – 1.4 cm, apex deeply divided into 5 oblong‑ovate lobes, some cultivars with the limbs modified into ligules; anthers included, base truncate, apical appendages ovate‑acute; stylar branches elongate with appendages hairy on the abaxial surface. Cypselae linear‑oblong, 8–11 mm, compressed‑tetragonous, brownish black in colour, minutely hairy. Pappus of 1–2 lanceolate long‑awned scales and 2–3 short obtuse scales, sometimes together with some small hyaline linear scales.

Locality: Cultivated. S. Y. Hu 7094, 13663 (CUHK).
Distribution: Native to USA, cultivated worldwide.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Sep.
Uses: Ornamental.

Tagetes patula L. 孔雀草
Sp. Pl. 887. 1753; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 21(3–4): 176. 1968; FRPS 75: 387. 1979; FGD 8: 144. 2007.

Annual herbs 30–100 cm tall; stem erect and branched. Leaves odd‑pinnatifid, 2–10 × 1.5–3 cm, leaflets linear‑lanceolate, margin serrate, teeth often with long awns at tips when young, glandular dotted along the margin below the teeth. Capitula solitary and terminal to branches, 3.5–5 cm across. Peduncle 5–6.5 cm, apical portion somewhat inflated. Involucres with single row of phyllaries united into a campanulate tube 1.2–1.5 × 0.6–0.7 cm, acute‑triangular toothed on top, glandular‑dotted. Ray florets bright yellow or orange, with maroon‑red patches, ligule suborbicular, 8–10 × 6–7 mm, retuse at apex. Disk tubular florets yellow, 1–1.4 cm, 5‑lobed. Cypselae linear, 8–12 mm, black, pubescent. Pappus of several scales, 1–2 of them long‑awned, 2–3 short and obtuse.

Locality: Cultivated. H. Y. Yeung 134, 177 (CUHK).
Distribution: Native to Mexico, widely cultivated.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Oct.
Uses: Ornamental.

Taraxacum officinale F. H. Wigg. 藥用蒲公英
Prim. Fl. Holsat. 56. 1780; FKH 150. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Quart. Jn. Taiwan Mus. 22: 657. 1969; FTW ed. 2, 4: 1079. 1998; FRPS 80(2): 50. 1999.
Taraxacum dens‑leonis Desf., Fl. Atlant. 2: 228. 1799; FHK 192. 1861.

Perennial herbs; scapes erect and hollow, 5–40 cm tall, glabrous or cobwebby on upper portion, base usually tinged purple‑red. Leaves oblanceolate, 4–20 × 1–7 cm, or much larger, runcinate‑pinnatilobed to pinnatifid, apical lobes usually larger, triangular or triangular‑hastate, acute or obtuse; lateral lobes 4–7 pairs, triangular to triangular‑lanceolate, downward‑pointing, margin irregularly toothed; leaf base sometimes tinged purple‑red, both surfaces glabrous or sparsely arachnoid hairy along veins. Capitula 2.5–5 cm across, homogamous with all florets ligulate and hermaphrodite, solitary at scape terminal. Involucres broadly campanulate; phyllaries green, apex acuminate, without prominent horn‑like structure near apex or slightly thickened along midvein; outer involucral bracts 1–2 rows, lanceolate, 4–10 × 1.5–3.5 mm, reflexed at flowering stage; inner ones in 1 row, linear‑lanceolate, 16–25 × 1.2–1.5 mm, erect at first and later reflexed at fruiting stage. Ligulate florets yellow in colour, ligule 5‑toothed apically. Cypselae pale brown, obovate‑oblong, 3–4 × 0.8–1.2 mm, ribbed and sharply tuberculate along ribs on upper half, lower half slightly and obtusely roughened, apex forming a narrow pyramidal tubercle 0.4–0.6 mm, subtending the apical filiform beak with length 6–12 mm. Pappus white, 5–6 mm, growing on the beak, like a parachute.

Locality: Naturalized. Y. S. Lau 2508; L. T. Lo 653; P. S. Choi 127.
Distribution: Xinjiang; Kirghizstan, Kazakstan, Europe and N America.
Ecology: Grassy hillslopes. Flowering & fruiting: Mar.–Aug.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The species was reported as Taraxacum mongolicum Hand.‑Mazz. previously (Check List HK Plants 288. 2002; 98. 2004).

Tithonia diversifolia (Hemsl.) A. Gray 腫柄菊
Proc. Amer. Acad. Arts 19: 5. 1883; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 22(1–2): 13. 1969; FRPS 75: 356, pl. 59: 1–2. 1979; FGD 8: 120, fig. 59. 2007; FTW ed. 2, 4: 1083. 1998.
Mirasolia diversifolia Hemsl., Biol. Cent.‑Amer., Bot. 2(8): 168, pl. 47. 1881.

Large shrub‑like perennial herbs, 2–3 m tall; stems striate, puberulent in upper younger part. Leaves alternate in upper stem portion, opposite near base; petiole 1–5.5 cm; leaf blade ovate or ovate‑triangular, 6–18.5 × 2.5– 8.5 cm, 3–5‑lobed or sometimes with upper ones not lobed, lobes ovate‑lanceolate and acuminate, base attenuate and decurrent forming wings with petiole, margin crenate‑serrate, 3‑nerved, upper surfaces scaberulous to puberulent, lower surfaces densely pubescent‑tomentulose and glandular. Capitula radiate, heterogamous, 5– 15 cm across, solitary; peduncle 6–12 cm, swollen near the capitula. Involucres hemispherical, 2–4 cm across; phyllaries 3–4‑seriate; outer rows smaller, ovate‑elliptic, apex acute, 0.7–1 × 0.4–0.5 cm; inward series longer and becoming reflexed, oblanceolate‑oblong, apex obtuse to rounded, 1.8–2.2 × 0.5–0.9 cm, margin membranous on the apical half. Receptacle convex; paleae 11 mm, sharply toothed near the apex. Marginal ligulate florets sterile, 9–14 in one series, corolla yellow, ligule 4 cm, tube 1.5–2 mm and pubescent, apex 2–3‑lobed. Disk tubular florets bisexual, many, corolla yellow, 8 mm, narrowed at the middle, broadened in lower part and slightly contracted at base, pubescent on lower region, apex 5‑lobed. Cypselae blackish brown, oblong, 5 – 6 mm, flat and 4‑ribbed, shortly sericeous. Pappus of ligulate florets minutely scaly, those of tubular florets with scarious crown 1.5–2 mm, irregularly erose, together with 2 rigid awns 3.5–5 mm.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. W. Lam 1025; S. Y. Hu 6352 (CUHK); K. Y. Chan 1346 (CUHK).
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan and Fujian (cultivated); native to Mexico.
Ecology: Often cultivated on margins of farmlands near villages. Flowering: Jul.–Dec.
Uses: Green manure, ornamental.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Naturalized and widely distributed in Hong Kong
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Tridax procumbens L. 羽芒菊
Sp. Pl. 900. 1753; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 22(1–2): 15. 1969; FRPS 75: 385, pl. 65: 5 – 7. 1979; FGD 8: 138, fig. 74. 2007; FTW ed. 2, 4: 1084, pl. 517, photo 493. 1998.

Perennial herbs; stem slender and decumbent, 15–50 cm, branched near the base, pilose. Petiole short, 0.3–1 cm. Leaves ovate or ovate‑lanceolate, 1.5–4.5 × 0.8–3 cm, base cuneate or attenuate, apex acute, margin irregularly serrate with tooth size uneven, usually with 1–2 pairs of shallow lobes near base, pilose on both surfaces. Capitula 1–1.5 cm across, solitary. Peduncle 8–23 cm. Involucres campanulate, 7–8 × 6 mm; phyllaries 2–3‑seriate, acute or abruptly acute, outer 1–2 layers herbaceous green, tinged purple, strongly pilose; the outermost ones ovate, 5–6 × 2 mm; the median ones ovate‑oblong, longer and broader, 7 mm × 3 mm, with scarious purplish margin; the innermost scarious, oblong, 7–8 mm × 2.5 mm, purplish, less hairy. Receptacle convex, paleae persistent, linear, 7–8 × 1.2 mm, acuminate, slightly serrulate near apex, hyaline, shinny, yellowish to brownish purple apically and along midvein, hairy at apical portion. Marginal ligulate florets 5 or 6 in one row, pistillate, corolla pale yellow or cream white, ligule elliptic, 4 × 3 mm, apex deeply 2–3‑lobed, acute, with 3 longitudinal lines of hair on the abaxial side, tube elongate, 3–3.5 mm, pubescent. Disk tubular florets many, hermaphrodite, corolla yellow, narrowly trumpet‑shaped, 6–7 mm, distal end 5‑lobed, hairy outside. Cypselae brown, oblong‑cuneate, 2–2.5 mm, densely silky hairy. Pappus unequal in length, about 5–7 mm, spreading, plumose, yellowish or brownish.

Locality: Naturalized and widely distributed in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1432; H. Y. Yeung 528; S. Y. Hu 6790 (CUHK).
Distribution: Native to tropical America, distributed in S & SE China as well as Asia.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides near villages. Flowering: Nov. –Apr. of the following year.

Vernonia cinerea (L.) Less. 夜香牛
Linnaea 4(3): 291. 1829; FHK 169. 1861; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 22: 18. 1969; FRPS 74: 38. 1985; FGD 8: 236, fig. 144. 2007; FTW ed. 2, 4: 1086, pl. 518, photo 494. 1998.
Conyza cinerea L., Sp. Pl. 2: 862. 1753.

Erect annual or biennial herbs, 12–100 cm tall, greyish pubescent throughout, trichomes simple, mixed with T‑shaped and rarely stellate hairs. Stem cylindric, 2–4 mm in diam., glandular, striate‑sulcate, branching only after the formation of terminal capitulum. Middle and lower leaves ovate‑rhombic or ovate, 2–8 × 1.5–5 cm, base cuneate, apex acute to obtuse, margin undulate‑serrulate, subglabrous‑puberulent and greenish adaxially, densely covered with greyish matted hairs abaxially, gradually attenuate to form winged petiole 0.5–3 cm, sometimes mucronate; upper cauline leaves subsessile, gradually decreasing in size, becoming lanceolate‑linear. Capitula in corymbose panicle; pedunculate at anthesis, peduncles densely pubescent, 0.2–1.5 cm, bearing 1–3 small linear prophylls. Involucres campanulate, 4–5 × 2–3 mm; phyllaries green changing upward to purple, glandular and densely pubescent, apex acuminate to acicular, 4‑seriate; outer ones linear, 1–1.5 mm; middle and inner ones linear‑lanceolate; the innermost ones 4 mm. Receptacles flat, alveolate at anthesis and areolate after fruit dispersal. Florets 20–21 per capitulum, 4 mm, the tube slender, white, the distal enlarged portion and the lobes purple and hairy; stylar branches exserted, purple; anther bases sagittate, apical appendages ovate‑acute. Cypselae terete, apex truncate, slightly cuneate towards the corky ring at the base, 1.5–2 mm, pubescent and glandular. Pappus white, biseriate, outer ones numerous and minute, persistent; inner ones 4 mm, delicate and deciduous.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. S. Y. Hu & P. P. H. But 23987 (CUHK); S. Y. Hu 6974 (CUHK); P. S. Choi 397.
Distribution: S, SW to C & E China; Japan, India, Indochina, Malaysia, Africa.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides near villages. Flowering: Nearly all year round.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Shek O, Wong Nai Chung, The Peak, Nam Fung Rd., Tai Mo Shan, Luk Keng, Castle Peak
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Vernonia cumingiana Benth. 毒根斑鳩菊
Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 4: 232. 1852; FHK 170. 1861; FRPS 74: 21, pl. 9: 7–13. 1985; FGD 8: 234. 2007.
Vernonia andersonii auct. non C. B. Clarke, FKH 139. 1912.

Scandent shrubs or liana, current years’ flower‑bearing growth 60–80 cm, 4–5 cm in diam. near the base, branched off leafy shoots 6–7 mm across. Stem terete, striate, pubescent to densely tomentose, some hair stellate. Leaves ovate‑oblong, elliptic‑oblong or lanceolate‑oblong, 5–14 × 2–6 cm, base rounded or obtuse, apex acute or shortly acuminate, margin entire, major lateral veins 5 – 6 on each side of midvein, arcuate, reticulations on both surfaces, glabrous adaxially except the midvein and veins appearing puberulent, abaxial surfaces glandular and densely pilose or tomentose with rusty‑coloured hairs; leaf petiole densely pubescent, 0.5– 1 cm. Capitula numerous, in terminal or axillary panicles; peduncles 0.5–2 cm, rusty hirsute, the distal half with 1– 3 linear prophylls, gradually merging with the involucral bracts. Involucres campanulate to hemispherical, 6–7 × 6–12 mm when dry, apex acute or obtuse, 5‑seriate; outermost ones ovate, 3 mm, densely covered with yellowish hair on whole abaxial surfaces and along margin; middle and inner layers ranging from ovate‑oblong to oblong, 4–7 mm, hairy near the apex. Receptacle plain, fimbriate and with each areole elevated at centre. Florets 18 – 21 per capitulum, corolla 9–12 mm, twice the length of the innermost phyllaries, trumpet‑shaped with distal half enlarged, lobes 3–4 mm, colour pink to reddish purple; anther tubes 4 mm, slightly exserted, with long‑deltoid apical appendages and sagittate bases; stylar branches 2–3 mm, spinulose. Cypselae subcylindric, 3 mm, 10– 12‑ribbed, sparsely puberulent, basal end truncate with a corky ring. Pappus 2‑seriate, outer ones shorter and few; inner ones 1 cm, reddish brown.

Locality: Shek O, Wong Nai Chung, The Peak, Nam Fung Rd., Tai Mo Shan, Luk Keng, Castle Peak. P. S. Choi 497; W. Y. Chun 5054 (CUHK); S. Y. Hu 11831 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan, Fujian, Taiwan; Thailand, Indochina.
Ecology: Margins of forests, thickets along streams. Flowering: Oct.–Apr. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Vernonia elliptica DC. in Wight 光耀藤
Contrib. Bot. India 5. 1834; FTW ed. 2, 4: 1088, pl. 519. 1998.

Large sprawling woody lianas climbing over fences and trees up to 4 – 5 m high; branchlets, lower leaf‑surfaces and inflorescences silvery hairy. Leaves on flowering shoots petiolate, petioles curved, 2 – 5 mm, densely silky, leaf blade oblong‑elliptic, 2.5 – 9.5 × 1 – 6 cm, base and apex rounded or obtuse, glabrous or bearing little sericeous hair adaxially, densely covered with appressed silky hair abaxially, reticulate veins and midvein elevated on both surfaces. Capitulum subsessile, with 4 – 5 florets each, 3 – 6 capitula forming a stalked cluster, subtended by a diminutive leaf (prophyll). Involucres subcylindric, 3 – 4 × 1.5 – 2 mm; phyllaries herbaceous, imbricate, 4‑seriate, ciliate along margin; the outermost ones ovate, 1.5 × 1 mm, glandular and puberulent on abaxial surfaces, apex obtuse; length and width increases gradually inward; innermost ones obovate‑oblong, apex obtuse to rounded, 3 × 1.5 mm, glandular and hairy near apex. Florets white, tinged pink in bud or when first open, corolla 5 – 6, narrowly funnelform with upper half broaden, 1/3 divided into 5 lanceolate lobes and glandular outside; anther tube honey‑coloured, base sagittate, apical appendage ovate‑lanceolate; style white, base globose, attached to a brown glandular disk, distal end branched and recurved, the abaxial side of the branches bristly, apex acute‑acuminate. Cypsela glossy brown, 2.5 mm, 4 – 5‑ribbed, densely glandular. Pappus greyish to brownish white, persistent, unequal, the outer ones shorter, the inner ones equal to the corolla tube in length, radiating with diam. 0.8 – 1 cm.

Locality: Cultivated. S. L. Thrower 1577 (CUHK); S. Y. Hu & P. P. H. But 22143, 22182, 23942 (CUHK).
Distribution: Native to India and SE Asia, naturalized in Taiwan.
Ecology: Flowering: Feb. – May.
Uses: Ornamental

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Mo Shan, Tai Shing Stream
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Vernonia gratiosa Hance 台灣斑鳩菊
J. Bot. 20(238): 290. 1882; FRPS 74: 24, pl. 9: 1 – 6. 1985; FGD 8: 234. 2007; FTW ed. 2, 4: 1088, pl. 520, photo 495. 1998.

Scandent subshrubs up to 3 m tall; branches many, pubescent to tomentose. Leaves elliptic‑oblong, 6.5–11 × 1.8–4 cm, petiole densely pubescent, 0.4–1 cm, base cuneate, apex shortly acuminate, margin entire or loosely mucronulate, subglabrous or loosely pubescent adaxially, more hairy on the midvein, densely brownish tomentose abaxially. Capitula many, arranged as terminal or axillary panicles; peduncles much densely brownish tomentose. Involucres campanulate, 6 mm; phyllaries in 4 series, apex acute, brownish long hairs growing throughout or mainly distributed near apex and along margin; outer layers ovate, 2 mm; median and inner layers lanceolate to oblong, gradually increases in length inward, 2.5–7 mm. Receptacle slightly convex, areoles fimbriate. Florets about 10 per capitulum, tubular corolla purple, 1 cm, lower portion puberulent, apex divided into 5 linear‑lanceolate lobes about 2 mm, glabrous. Cypselae terete, 10‑ribbed, 3–3.5 mm, brown in colour, puberulent, truncate at apex, narrowed at base with corky ring. Pappus in 2 series, outer ones short, usually deciduous; inner ones 1 cm, brown to reddish brown, persistent.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Tai Shing Stream. C. P. Lau 188; P. S. Choi 528.
Distribution: Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Margins of forests, thin forests. Flowering: Aug.–Apr. of the following year.

Vernonia maritima Merr. 濱海斑鳩菊
Philipp. J. Bot. 3(6): 404. 1908; FRPS 74: 39, pl. 15: 1 – 8. 1985; FGD 8: 236. 2007.
Vernonia maritima Hayata, J. Coll. Sci. Imp. Univ. Tokyo 22: 202. 1906, nom. nud.
Vernonia kawakami Hayata, J. Coll. Sci. Imp. Univ. Tokyo 30(1): 149. 1911.

Dwarf subshrubs, usually 7–10 cm tall. Stems often procumbent at base, obliquely ascending in upper part, many‑branched, striate, grey‑white hispidulous. Leaves numerous, ± confert upwards, spathulate, 1.5–2.5 × 0.4–0.7 cm, base gradually attenuate into slender petioles, apex rounded or obtuse, margin entire or repand, densely grey‑white hispidulous. Capitula few, usually 3–5 corymbose, 5–7 mm in diam.; peduncles 5–12 mm, with 1–2 subulate bracteoles, densely hispidulous. Involucres ca. 4 × 5–7 mm; phyllaries 5‑seriate, imbricate, outer ones subsubulate 1.5–2 mm, spinescent, puberulous, median ones ovate, ca. 3 mm, acute and mucronulate, inner ones oblong, sparsely puberulous, with scarious margins. Receptacle flat, foveolate. Florets more than 40 per capitulum; corolla tubular, 2.5 mm, with campanulate limb; lobes lanceolate, apically glandular. Cypselae subcylindric, 1–1.2 mm, 5‑angled, truncate at apex, glandular between the ribs or sometimes sparsely puberulous. Pappus simple, white, ca. 1 mm, deciduous.

Locality: Lantau Island, Cheung Chau. W. J. Tutcher 11923; H. C. Tang 1252.
Distribution: Taiwan; Philippines.
Ecology: Wastelands near seashores. Flowering: Jun.–Oct.

Vernonia patula (Dryand.) Merr. 鹹蝦花
Philipp. J. Sci. 3(6): 439. 1908; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 22(1–2): 21. 1969; FRPS 74: 41, pl. 12: 8–15. 1985; FGD 8: 233, fig. 143. 2007; FTW ed. 2, 4: 1091, pl. 521, photo 497. 1998.
Vernonia chinensis (L.) Less., Linnaea 6: 105, 674. 1831; FHK 169. 1861; FKH 138. 1912.
Conyza patula Dryand., Hort. Kew 3: 184. 1789.

Erect annual herbs 40–60 cm tall; stem terete, striate‑sulcate, glandular and greyish pubescent, the lower portion 3–6 mm in diam. Leaves ovate or ovate‑oblong, the lower cauline ones usually withered at anthesis; the middle ones 3–4.5 × 1.5–3 cm, base cuneate and attenuate as wings of the upper portion of the petiole, apex obtuse, margin subentire with 2–6 small callous teeth, sparsely pilose above, glandular and greyish woolly beneath; petioles 2–10 mm; upper cauline leaves smaller, subsessile. Capitula 2–3 terminal to leafy branchlets; peduncles 0.4–2.8 cm, tomentose, with or without prophylls. Involucres hemispherical or depressed globose, 5–6 × 6–10 mm; phyllaries 4–5‑seriate, apex acuminate‑acicular, hairy and glandular; outermost ones lanceolate, 3 – 4 mm, greenish or sometimes tinged purple; middle and inner layers lanceolate‑oblong, 5–6 mm. Receptacle slightly convex, shortly scarious along margin of areoles. Florets 75–100 in each capitulum; corolla purple, 4–4.5 mm, apical lobes lanceolate; anther tube 1.5 mm; stylar branches exserted, 0.8 mm. Cypselae subcylindric, obtuse at the basal end, truncate at the apex, 2 mm, unequally pentagonous, glabrous, glandular. Pappus white, in 1 series, 2.5 – 3 mm, delicate and deciduous.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. P. S. Choi 233; Y. S. Lau 2214; Y. W. Lam 483.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Indochina, Malaysia.
Ecology: Wastelands. Flowering: Nearly all year round.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Mount Parker, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Vernonia saligna DC. 柳葉斑鳩菊
Prodr. 5: 33. 1836; FRPS 74: 25, pl. 10: 1–7. 1985; FGD 8: 235. 2007.

Perennial erect herbs, 60–100 cm tall; stem woody at base, branches terete, striate, puberulent to subglabrous. Leaves subsessile or shortly petiolate, leaf blade elliptic‑oblong to oblanceolate, 5–12 × 1.5–4 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate or acute, margin serrate to double serrate, both surfaces scabrous, abaxial side with denser hair and have glands. Capitula many, forming terminal or axillary corymb; peduncles 5 – 10 mm, densely pubescent and glandular. Involucres campanulate, 7–9 × 5–8 mm; phyllaries 4–5‑seriate, scarious, purple throughout or apically, margin ciliate; outermost ovate, ca. 2 mm, apex acuminate‑spinulose; middle and inner layers ovate‑oblong to oblong, length increases inward, innermost 8 mm, apex rounded‑ or obtuse‑spinulose. Florets 6–12 per capitulum, pale purple, tubular corolla 7–8 mm, glandular, trumpet‑shaped with apex divided into 5 lanceolate lobes. Cypselae oblong, 2.5–3 mm, 10‑ribbed, hairy and glandular. Pappus white, in 1 series, 7 mm, delicate and deciduous.

Locality: Mount Parker, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island. W. J. Tutcher 4822; L. T. Lo 421; HK sheet 14629.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou, Fujian; India, Nepal, Myanmar, Thailand, Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests or thickets. Flowering: Sep.–Feb. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Vernonia solanifolia Benth. 茄葉斑鳩菊（斑鳩菊）
London J. Bot. 1: 486. 1842; FHK 169. 1861; FKH 138. 1912; FGD 8: 234. 2007; FRPS 74: 12, pl. 1: 8–14. 1985

Densely woolly shrubby lianas, 1–4 m tall, with arching branches. Leaves ovate or ovate‑oblong, 4–14 × 3–7 cm, rounded or subcordate at the base, acuminate or obtuse at the apex, margin entire, undulate or loosely obtuse‑toothed, the adaxial surfaces pilose and glandular, and densely hirsute with simple and stellate hair along the midvein, the abaxial surfaces glandular and densely covered with yellowish or brownish matted hairs; petioles strong, 0.7–2 cm, tomentose. Capitula numerous, in axillary and terminal corymbose‑panicles; peduncles 0.7 – 1.2 cm, densely woolly. Involucres hemispherical, 4–5 × 4–6 mm; phyllaries 4–5‑seriate, ranging from ovate, ovate‑oblong to oblong, 2.5–5 mm, apex obtuse, outer ones woolly throughout the abaxial surface, inner ones woolly at apical region and slightly scarious along margin. Receptacle plain and alveolate. Florets 10–12, fragrant, corolla pink or pale purple, sparsely glandular, funnelform about 6 mm, 1/3 divided into 5 lanceolate lobes; stylar branches 2 mm, exserted. Cypselae brown,

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. S. Y. Hu 5044 (CUHK); Y. W. Lam 1313; P. S. Choi 498.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian; India, Myanmar, Indochina.
Ecology: Forests of valleys. Flowering: Dec.–Apr. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Wedelia biflora (L.) DC. 雙頭菊（孿花蟛蜞菊）
Contr. Bot. India 18. 1837; FHK 183. 1861; FKH 145. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 22(1–2): 26. 1969; FRPS 75: 351, pl. 60: 1 – 6. 1979; FGD 8: 124. 2007; FTW ed. 2, 4: 1093, photo 498. 1998.

Verbesina biflora L., Sp. Pl. ed. 2, 2: 1272. 1763.
Wollastonia biflora (L.) DC., Prodr. 5: 546. 1836; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 22(1 – 2): 28. 1969; Check List HK Plants 290. 2002; 99. 2004.
Melanthera biflora (L.) Wild, Kirkia 5: 4. 1965.

Perennial herbs or subshrubs, 1–2 m tall; stem branched, scandent, extending to 2–4 m or longer, glabrous or sparsely strigose. Leaves ovate to ovate‑lanceolate, 4–14 × 1–7.5 cm, those on upper stem appearing smaller in size, base varied from rounded, truncate to cuneate, showing slightly decurrent, apex acuminate, margin regularly serrate, both surfaces covered with short appressed hairs, denser on abaxial side; petiole slender, 0.7–5 cm. Capitula radiate, heterogamous, about 2 cm across, usually 2–6 or more heads arranged as loose corymbs at terminal, sometimes axillary; peduncles slender, 1.5–6 cm, densely strigose. Involucres hemispherical or ovoid; phyllaries 2‑seriate, foliaceous, ovate‑lanceolate, two layers subequal in length, 4.5–5 × 1.5–2 mm, apex obtuse or slightly acute, densely scabrous, subtending the ray florets. Paleae obovate‑oblanceolate, 5–6 mm × 1.5–2 mm, obtuse or shortly acute, upper portion foliaceous and scaberulous, lower half scarious and glabrous, enfolding the achenes of disk florets. Marginal ligulate florets pistillate, in 1 series, corolla yellow, ligule 6–7 × 3–4 mm, tube 1.5–2 mm, apex 2‑lobed, pubescent near the apical region of the abaxial side. Central tubular florets hermaphrodite, many, 4–5 mm, apex 5 lobes and pubescent on abaxial side. Cypselae 3–3.5 × 2–2.5 mm, those developed from ligulate florets thickly trigonous, those from tubular florets 4‑angled, both cuneate at base, broadly truncate at top, strongly pubescent near the summit, glabrous in lower part. Pappus none or of 1 bristle 1.5–2 mm, easily shed off.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 736; S. Y. Hu 6549 (CUHK); Joseph P. W. Woo & T. K. Woo 864 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; E & S Asia, Malaysia, Australia.
Ecology: Common on sandy beaches or in thickets near seashore. Flowering: Mar.–Nov.

Wedelia chinensis (Osbeck) Merr. 蟛蜞菊
Philipp. J. Sci. 12(2): 111. 1917; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 22(1 – 2): 26. 1969; FRPS 75: 354, pl. 60: 7 – 11. 1979; FGD 8: 125, fig. 62. 2007; FTW ed. 2, 4: 1094, pl. 522, photo 499. 1998.
Wedelia calendulacea (L.) Less., Syn. Gen. Compos. 222. 1832; FHK 182. 1861; FKH 145. 1912.
Solidago chinensis Osbeck, Dagb. Ostind. Resa 241. 1757.

Perennial creeping herbs; stems decumbent with the lower part rooting at nodes, upper part ascending and becoming erect, strigose‑pilose. Leaves elliptic‑oblong to linear‑oblong, 2.5–7 × 0.5–1.7 cm, subsessile or shortly petiolate, base cuneate, apex acute, margin entire or bearing 1–3 pairs of serrate teeth, scabrous on both surfaces, midvein prominent on abaxial side. Capitula heterogamous, radiate, 1.3–2.4 cm across, solitary. Peduncle 2.8–9.5 cm, densely strigose. Involucres campanulate; phyllaries 2–3‑seriate; the outer one or two layers foliaceous, green, oblong, subequal, 8–10 × 3–4 mm, apex obtuse to rounded, abaxially scabrous; the innermost layer scarious in lower portion and herbaceous in upper region, linear‑oblong, 6–7 × 1.8–2 mm, apex acute or acuminate, ciliate along margin of apical half. Receptacle flat, paleaceous; the paleae linear, 6 mm × 1 mm, acuminate, subtending the florets. Ray florets 1‑seriate, pistillate, fertile, corolla ligulate, spreading, yellow in colour, ligule oblong, 8 × 3–3.5 mm, apex 2–3‑dentate, tube 1–1.2 mm. Disk florets many, hermaphrodite, fertile, corolla tubular, yellow, 4–5 mm, apex 5 ovate obtuse lobes, glabrous or puberulent inside. Cypselae obovate‑oblanceolate, 3–4 mm, loosely hairy near apex, those developed from ligulate florets 3‑ridged, those from tubular florets laterally flattened. Pappus a short scarious crown with toothed rim.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. L. T. Lo 69; Y. S. Lau 2334; P. S. Choi 102.
Distribution: S, E & NE China; E & S Asia, Malaysia.
Ecology: Banks of paddy fields and other wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Mar.–Sep.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Shek O, Sai Kung (Ham Tin, Tai Long Wan and Long Ke Wan)
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Wedelia prostrata Hemsl. 滷地菊
J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 23(157): 434. 1888; FKH 145. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 22(1 – 2): 27. 1969; FRPS 75: 353. 1979; FGD 8: 125. 2007; FTW ed. 2, 4: 1094, pl. 523, photo 500. 1998.
Wollastonia prostrata Hook. & Arn., Bot. Beechey Voy. 265. 1838.
Verbesina prostrata Hook. & Arn., Beechey Voy. 195. 1837.

Annual creeping herbs; stem rooting at nodes in lower part, flowering branches ascending, hirsute with the hair basally swollen. Leaves ovate to ovate‑oblong, 1–2.5 × 0.3–0.9 cm, base cuneate, apex acute, margin 1–3 pairs of serrulate teeth, both surfaces scabrous, 3‑veined; petiole 2–6 mm. Capitula 1–2 cm across; peduncle 0.8–1.8 cm, densely hirsute. Involucres hemispherical; phyllaries 2‑seriate; the outer ones foliaceous, ovate or ovate‑oblong, 4–5 × 2–3 mm, acute or obtuse, densely scabrous; the inner ones basally scarious, apically herbaceous, oblanceolate‑oblong, 5–5.5 × 1–1.2 mm, acute‑acuminate, ciliate near apex. Paleae linear‑oblong, enfolding the floret hypanthia, length 6 mm, apically herbaceous and hairy, acute. Marginal florets pistillate, corolla ligulate, yellow, ligule oblong, 5.5–7 × 3–4 mm, apex lobe 3, tube 1 mm. Central florets many, hermaphrodite, corolla tubular, yellow, 4–5 mm, 5‑cleft at apex, lobes sparsely hairy on abaxial side. Cypselae oblong‑cuneate, 3–3.5 mm, apex truncate and hairy. Pappus 1–2 bristles or obsolete.

Locality: Shek O, Sai Kung (Ham Tin, Tai Long Wan and Long Ke Wan). Y. S. Lau 364, 2568; S. Y. Hu & P. P. H. But 22723 (CUHK); N. H. Li & K. M. Lau 157 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Zhejiang, Jiangsu, Taiwan; India, Vietnam, Philippines, Japan, Korea.
Ecology: Sandy places near seaside. Flowering & fruiting: Mar.–Sep.

Wedelia trilobata (L.) Hitchc. 三裂葉蟛蜞菊
Rep. (Annual) Missouri Bot. Gard. 4: 99. 1893; FTW ed. 2, 4: 1097. 1998.
Silphium trilobatum L. Syst. Nat. ed. 10, 2: 1233. 1759.

Perennial creeping herbs; stems prostrate or decumbent, green or dull red, glabrous or loosely hirsute. Leaves opposite, rhomboid to lanceolate in outline, trilobed at about middle, 4–10 × 2–5 cm, base attenuate to form wing with petiole, apex acute, margin coarsely serrate, triplinerved, scabrous on both surfaces with abaxial side glandular‑dotted, veins prominent beneath; the free part of petiole 3–7(–10) mm. Capitula solitary, heterogamous, radiate, 2.5–3 cm across. Peduncle elongate, 6–18 cm, densely pilose. Involucres campanulate; phyllaries in 3 series; the outer 2 layers green, foliaceous, elliptic‑oblong, subequal in length and width, 8–10 × 2.5–3 mm, apex acute, abaxially scabrous; the innermost ones scarious basally and slightly herbaceous adaxially, linear‑oblong, 6 × 1.5 mm, erose‑ciliate near apex, acute, subtending the ovaries of marginal ligulate florets. Receptacle plain or slightly convex, paleaceous; the paleae linear, 6–8 × 1–1.2 mm, serrulate near apex, enfolding the ovaries of tubular florets. Ray florets 12–16, corolla ligulate and spreading, yellow to orange‑yellow, ligule oblong, 6–7(–12) × 5 mm, apex 2–3‑toothed, tube short, 1–1.5(–1.8) mm. Tubular florets many, more than 40, corolla yellow, 4–5 mm, limb 5‑lobed, strongly barbate inside. Cypselae 4.5–5 mm, puberulent and glandular near apex, those of ligulate florets oblong‑cuneate, triangular in cross‑section, those of tubular florets clavate, terete. Pappus cup‑shaped with sharply toothed rim.

Locality: Naturalized and widely cultivated. Y. S. Lau 2587; Y. Wong 014 (CUHK); S. Y. Hu 11043 (CUHK).
Distribution: Native to tropical America, widely distributed in the tropics; introduced into Hong Kong in 1971 from S Africa by Mr. Horace Kadoorie.
Ecology: Commonly planted as ground cover for earth slopes and bare hillsides, recently becoming naturalized in Hong Kong. Flowering: Nearly all year round.

Wedelia wallichii Less. 山蟛蜞菊
Linnaea 6: 162. 1831; FRPS 75: 352. 1979; FGD 8: 124. 2007.
Wedelia urticifolia DC., Contr. Bot. India 18. 1834; FRPS 75: 352. 1979; FFJ 5: 353. 1993.

Perennial herbs, 20–60 cm tall. Stems suberect, hispid to glabrous. Lower leaves opposite; petioles 1–2 cm; leaf blade ovate or ovate‑lanceolate, 5–9 × 3–7 cm, base rounded or cuneate, apex acuminate, margin crenulate, hispid on both surfaces; upper leaves smaller, lanceolate, petiolate or sessile. Capitula ca. 15 mm in diam., solitary on elongate peduncle. Involucre broadly campanulate or hemispherical, 10–15 mm in diam. Phyllaries in two series; outer ones herbaceous, green, oblong, ca. 10 mm, apex obtuse or shortly acute, dorsally scabrous hairy; inner ones oblong to lanceolate, ca. 7 mm, scarious, dorsally pubescent in upper part, apex acuminate. Paleae oblong, sparsely pubescent. Ray florets one seriate, ligules oblong, 4–6 × 2 mm , yellow, apex 2–3‑toothed. Disk florets tubular, yellow, limbs 5‑toothed. Cypselae obovoid, compressed or obtusely 3‑angled, tip contracted. Pappus cup‑shaped, with 2 – 3 bristles.

Locality: Shing Mun. Y. S. Lau 2498.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan; Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Thailand.
Ecology: Margins of forests, grassy hillslopes, streamsides. Flowering: Apr.–Oct.

Xanthium sibiricum Patrin ex Widder 蒼耳
Repert. Spec. Nov. Regni Veg. Beih. 20: 32. 1923; FRPS 75: 325, pl. 55: 1 – 10. 1979; FGD 8: 142, fig. 76. 2007.
Xanthium strumarium L., Sp. Pl. 987. 1753; FHK 181. 1861; FKH 144. 1912; FTW ed. 2, 4: 1098, pl. 524, photo 501. 1998.

Annual herbs 0.5–1.5 m tall; stem pubescent. Leaves broadly ovate‑deltoid, median ones 3.5–15 × 3–16.5 cm, 3‑ or 5‑lobed, base cordate to broadly cuneate, apex acute to obtuse, margin irregularly dentate, both surfaces scabrous. Petioles 1.5–16 cm, scabrous. Capitula monoecious. Male head globose, 4–7 mm across, sessile or shortly pedunculate, shorter than 6 mm, densely pubescent and glandular. Phyllaries 1‑seriate, oblanceolate‑oblong, 1.5–2.5 mm, densely hairy and glandular, apex obtuse‑rounded. Receptacle cylindric. Paleae oblanceolate with length 2.2–2.5 mm, acute, hairy and glandular near apex. Male florets numerous, corolla tubular, bell‑shaped, 2–3 mm, apex 5‑lobed, white or greenish white, hairy and glandular in apical 1/3; anthers free and curved inward, conspicuously exserted. Female heads axillary; phyllaries in 1 row, linear, 2.5–3 mm, hairy; inner phyllaries hard, appeared as a bur with 2 female florets enclosed inside. The bur elliptic, green or yellow‑green, narrowed at base forming a short stipe, 2‑beaked apically, 1–2.3 cm including the stipe and beaks, 4–7 mm wide, the beak 2–7 mm in length, pubescent throughout and bearing hooked prickles of 1.2–4 mm. Receptacles microscopic. Female florets without corolla, with only the pistils; stylar branches long and exposed outside the bur. Cypselae 2 per each capitulum, obovate.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1426, 2785; S. Y. Hu 12134 (CUHK).
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; Japan, Korea, Russia, Iran, India.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides near villages. Flowering & fruiting: May–Sep.
Uses: Material (seed oil used in industry), medicinal (folklore).

Youngia heterophylla (Hemsl.) Babc. & Stebbins 異葉黃鵪菜
Publ. Carnegie Inst. Wash. 484: 87. 1937; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 22(1 – 2): 32. 1969; FRPS 80(1): 152. 1997.
Crepis heterophylla Hemsl., J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 23: 475. 1888.

Annual or biennial herbs; 30–100 cm tall; stem erect, solitary or fasciculate, branched, loosely hairy in lower portion. Leaves subglabrous or sparsely crisped scabrous above and beneath, upper surfaces green, lower surfaces tinged reddish purple especially for the radical leaves. Basal leaves elliptic or oblanceolate‑oblong, 7– 25 × 3–13 cm, lyrately deeply pinnatisect, apical lobes hastate, irregularly hastate, ovate or lanceolate, 4.5–14 × 2–11 cm, apex acuminate to long acuminate; lateral lobes 1–8 pairs, opposite to each other or obliquely opposite, elliptic or auriculate, apex acute or obtuse, growing smaller downward, all lobes margin mucronulate, faintly or conspicuously dentate‑sinuate; leaf petiole 3–7 cm, winged. Cauline leaves hastate or lyrately trifoliate. The upper leaves lanceolate to linear‑lanceolate, often non‑divided, those growing near or on peduncles much reduced in size, linear‑subulate. Capitula homogamous with all florets ligulate and hermaphrodite, with 11–25 florets per head, corymbose at terminal. Involucres cylindric, 6 mm long; phyllaries glabrous, apex acute; outer layers small ovate, 0.5–1 × 0.5–0.7 mm; inner layers linear‑lanceolate, 6 × 1–1.2 mm. Ligulate florets yellow, length 7–9 mm, lower tube 3 mm, pubescent outside, ligule 4–6 mm, apex 5‑lobed; anther tube exserted, base sagittate, apical appendages rounded; stylar branches slender, 1–1.2 mm. Cypselae brown, fusiform, 3 × 0.8 mm, 14–15‑ribbed, minutely hairy, apex without beaks. Pappus white, 3 – 4 mm, scaberulous.

Locality: Ng Tung Chai, Kadoorie Farm. P. S. Choi 330; N. H. Li 54; S. Y. Hu 11840 (CUHK).
Distribution: Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi.
Ecology: Margins of forests, wastelands. Flowering: Mar.–May.

Youngia japonica (L.) DC. 黃鵪菜
Prodr. 7: 194. 1838; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 22(1 – 2): 33. 1969; FRPS 80(1): 155. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 4: 1098. 1998; FGD 8: 268, fig. 165. 2007.
Crepis japonica (L.) Benth., FHK 194. 1861; FKH 150. 1912.
Prenanthes japonica L., Mant. Pl. 1: 107. 1767.

Annual herbs 10–100 cm tall; stem erect, lower portion covered with crisped multicellular hair. Radical leaves rosulate at base, obovate, oblanceolate, elliptic or oblong, 4–13 × 2.5–5.5 cm, lyrately pinnatilobed, pinnatifid to pinnatisect, apical lobes large, ovate, deltoid‑ovate or obovate, apex rounded or obtuse; lateral lobes 3–7 pairs, elliptic or triangular, gradually smaller downward, the lowermost one auriculate; leaf margin mucronulate and somewhat dentate‑sinuate, both surfaces crisped scabrous; petiole 1–11 cm, winged or not. Cauline leaves absent or rarely with 1–2, appearance similar to radical leaves. Capitula 7–8 mm across, corymbose paniculate at stem and branch terminal; peduncle 0.3–2 cm. Involucres cylindric, about 5 × 2–2.5 mm; phyllaries glabrous on abaxial surfaces, apex acute or obtuse, herbaceous with margin membranous; outer layers short ovate, 0.8–1.2 × 0.6 – 1 mm; inner layers linear, 5 × 0.8–1.2 mm. Ligulate florets 10–20 per head, yellow, corolla 5–6 mm, lower tube 2–2.2 mm, pubescent outside, ligule 3–4 mm, apex 5‑toothed; anther exserted, base sagittate, apical appendages rounded; stylar branches slender and recurved, about 1 mm long. Cypselae fusiform, brown, 2 – 2.2 × 0.5–0.8 mm, 10–13‑ribbed, minutely hairy, apex beakless. Pappus bristles 3 mm, white, scaberulous, persistent.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. L. T. Lo 32; Y. S. Lau 1960; S. Y. Hu 12989 (CUHK).
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; E & S Asia, Indochina.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides, margins of cultivated lands. Flowering & fruiting: Feb.–May.

Zinnia violacea Cav. 百日菊（魚尾菊）
Icon. 1(3): 57, pl. 81. 1791; C. M. Hu, Check List HK Plants 290. 2002.
Zinnia elegans Jacq., Coll. Bot. 3: 152. 1789; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 22(1–2): 39. 1969; FRPS 75: 336. 1979; FGD 8: 118, fig. 57. 2007.

Annual herb 30–100 cm tall; stem erect, sparingly branched, striate, scabrous. Leaves ovate‑lanceolate to ovate‑triangular, 3–7 × 1–3 cm, base subcordate, somewhat amplexicaul, sessile, apex acute or acuminate, scaberulous on both surfaces and along margin, entire, trinerved. Capitula heterogamous, radiate, 4–6 cm across, solitary and terminal. Involucres campanulate; phyllaries 3–4‑seriate, tricolour, margin black, rounded and hairy along apex; outermost broadly ovate or suborbicular, 4–5 × 2–4 mm; innermost obovate‑oblong, 9–10 ×4–5 mm. Receptacle conical; palea with purplish red, triangular and fimbriate appendages at apical end. Ligulate florets variously coloured, white, orange, red to purple, ligules oblanceolate to spatulate, 1.4 – 3 cm, entire or 2‑lobed at apex, scaberulous on both surfaces and along margin, glandular on lower side; style exposed, about 1 cm, branches 5 mm. Disk tubular florets yellow to orange, 7–8 mm, 5 apical lobes ovate‑lanceolate, yellowish hairy; anthers included, base obtuse, apical appendages ovate‑deltoid; stylar branches elongate, apical appendage penicillate. Cypselae compressed, that developed from ray florets obovate, 6–7 × 4–5 mm, ribbed in the middle and along both margins; those from disk florets obovate‑trigonous, 7–8 × 3–4 mm; both hairy and with remnant of corolla attached. Pappus reduced to 2 teeth or absent.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. S. Y. Hu 12297 (CUHK); H. Y. Yeung 181 (CUHK).
Distribution: Native to Mexico, widely cultivated elsewhere.
Ecology: Flowering: Jul.–Oct.
Uses: Ornamental.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Chinese Family Name: 黃花藺科 (黃花絨葉草科 )
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Sha Tin, also cultivated in Hong Kong Wetland Park
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Limnocharis flava (L.) Buchenau 黃花藺（黃花絨葉草）
Abh. Naturwiss. Vereine Bremen 2: 2. 1868; Fl. Males., Ser. I, 5(1): 120. 1954; FYN 4: 747, fig. 207. 1986; FRPS 8: 149, pl. 57. 1992; FOC 23: 89. 2010.
Alisma flavum L., Sp. Pl. 1: 343. 1753.
Limnocharis emarginata Bonpland, Pl. Aequinoct. 1: 116, t. 34. 1808[“1807”].

Aquatic herb. Petiole trigonous, 20–65 cm, stout; leaf blade 6–28 cm × 4.5–20 cm, veins 9–13, transverse veins many, parallel, base obtuse or subcordate, apex obtuse or retuse. Scapes upper trigonous, 20–90 cm; umbels 2–15-flowered; bracts green, orbicular to broadly elliptic, 1.5–2 × 1–1.5 cm. Pedicels thick, triquetrous, 2–7 cm. Petals yellowish but blackish toward base, broadly ovate to orbicular, 2–3 × 1–2 cm, apex rounded. Stamens shorter than petals; filaments green. Carpels yellowish green. Fruit cluster 1.5–2 cm in diam.; follicles suborbicular. Seeds brown.

Locality: Sha Tin, also cultivated in Hong Kong Wetland Park. Y. S. Lau 2603.
Distribution: Guangdong, S Yunnan; naturalized throughout S and SE Asia; native to tropical America.
Ecology: Marshes, shallow-water fields. Flowering: Jul.
Uses: Ornamental, forage.

Alisma plantago-aquatica L. 澤瀉
Sp. Pl. 342. 1753; Dandy in Tutin et al., Fl. Europ. 5: 2. 1980; FRPS 8: 141. 1992; R. Haynes, Fl. Thailand 7(3): 352. 2001; FGD 9: 159. 2009; FOC 23: 87. 2010.

Perennial herb, growing in tufts at the bottom of the water. Tuber fleshy, 1–3.5 cm in diam., or more. Submersed leaves linear or lanceolate; emersed leaves petiolate; petioles of 1.5–30 cm, base sheathed, upper part terete, spongy; leaf blades broadlanceolate, elliptic to ovate, 2–11 × 1.3–7 cm, base broad-cunneate to shallowly cordate, apex acuminate, rarely acute; veins 5. Scapes 78 – 100 cm tall or more. Inflorescences paniculate, with 4–9 whorls, each whorl with 3–5 flowers or branches. Flowers bisexual. Sepals 2.5–3.5 × 2–3 mm, 7-veined. Petals white, pink or purplish, suborbiculate, 3.5–6.5 × 3.6 mm. Stamens in 1 series, filaments filiform. Carpels 17–23 in a single whorl; styles ventral. Achenes elliptic or suboblong, 2.5 × 1.5 mm, compressed, dorsally with 1–2 shallow sulci. Seeds purple-brown.

Locality: Sha Tin. Y. S. Lau 2575.
Distribution: NE to NW China, Yunnan; widespread throughout most regions of Europe and Asia.
Ecology: Ponds, paddy fields. Flowering & fruiting: May–Oct.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal (folklore).

Sagittaria guayanensis Kunth subsp. lappula (D. Don) Bogin 冠果草
Mem. New York Bot. Gard. 2: 192. 1955; FHN 4: 61. 1977; FRPS 8: 129. 1992; FGD 9: 156. 2009; FOC 23: 85. 2010.
Sagittaria lappula D. Don, Prodr. Fl. Nepal. 22. 1825.
Lophotocarpus guayanensis (H. B. & K.) J. G. Sm., Rep. Miss. Bot. Gard. 4: 35. 1895; FKH 290. 1912.
Lophotocarpus formosanus Hayata, Ic. Pl. Form. 5: 249. 1915; FTW 5: 10. 1978.
Sagittaria cordifolia Roxb., Fl. Ind. 2: 647. 1824; FHK 346. 1861.

Perennial floating herb, stolons lacking. Submersed leaves linear or lanceolate, or petiole-like; floating leaves ovate or broadly ovate, 2–6 × 1–4 cm, base deeply cordate, apex obtuse; veins 4–8 forward, 3–6 backward; petioles 10–20 cm or more. Scapes erect, 8–25 cm, extending out from water surface. Inflorescences racemose, 2–15 cm, 2–5-whorled, each whorl 2–3-flowered; flowers bisexual or unisexual, usually bisexual flowers in 1–3 whorls at lower part of inflorescences; male flowers on upper part. Sepals 3, ovate, 5–9 × 3–6 mm, persistent. Petals 3, white, base yellowish, nearly of same size as sepals, fugacious. Stamens 6 – many. Carpels many. Achenes obliquely oblong, 2–3 × 1.5–2.5 mm, tuberculate, with 1–3 lateral wings, margins irregularly and deeply lobed.

Locality: Sha Tin, Fanling, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 752, 1277; Y. W. Lam 2229.
Distribution: SW to SE China; S & SE Asia, tropical Africa.
Ecology: Ponds, paddy fields and marshes. Flowering & fruiting: May–Nov.

Sagittaria trifolia L. subsp. leucopetala (Miq.) Q. F. Wang 慈姑
FOC 23: 85. 2010.
Sagittaria trifolia L., Sp. Pl. 993. 1753.
Sagittaria sinensis Sims., Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 39: 163. 1814.
Sagittaria sagittifolia L. f. sinensis (Sims.) Makino, Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 15(174): 105. 1901.
Sagittaria sagittifolia L. subsp. leucopetala (Miq.) Hartog, Fl. Males. ser. 1, 5: 332. 1957; FHN 4: 62. 1977; R. Haynes, Fl. Thailand 7(3): 358. 2001.
Sagittaria trifolia L. var. sinense (Sims.) Makino, Ill. Fl. Nippon 886, pl. 2657. 1940; FRPS 8: 133. 1992; FGD 9: 157. 2009.
Sagittaria sagittifolia auct. non. L.: FKH 290. 1912.

Perennial herb, emersed, stoloniferous; tuber ovoid-globular or globular, 5–7 cm. Leaves long-petiolate; blades sagittate, central lobe ovate to broadly ovate, 9–16 cm, 5–7-veined, apex central lobe, lateral lobes usually longer than central lobe. Scapes 40–70 cm. Racemes sometimes 1–3-branched at base; female flowers, on lower 1–8 whorls, pedicels 1–2 cm; male flowers with longer pedicels, on the upper part. Sepals ovate, 6–8 mm, reflexed. Petals white, twice as large as sepals. Stamens many, anthers yellow. Achenes obliquely obovate, 4 × 3 mm, winged, shortly beaked. Seeds brown.

Locality: Cultivated. W. J. Tutcher 11240; Y. S. Lau 750, 2619.
Distribution: Widely cultivated in China; Asia.
Ecology: Ponds, paddy fields and marshes. Flowering & fruiting: May–Oct.
Uses: Food (tuber).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Happy Valley, Chai Wan, Sai Keng, Tai O
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Blyxa aubertii Rich. 無尾水篩
Mem. Cl. Sci. Math. Phys. Inst. France 12(2): 19. 1812; Fl. Males. 5(4): 390. 1957; FHN 4: 61. 1977 [“auberti”]; FRPS 8: 174, pl. 68: 1–2. 1992; FFJ 6: 28. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 11. 2000; FGD 6: 298. 2005; FOC 23: 99. 2010.
Blyxa ecaudata Hayata, Icon. Pl. Formosan 5: 208, pl. 77c – f. 1915.
Blyxa roxburghii auct. non Rich.: FHK 347. 1861; FKH 257. 1912.

Submerged herb. Stems shortened. Leaves all in basal rosette, linear, 5–17(–60) cm × 3(–12) mm, veins 5–9, apex acuminate. Spathes green, 3–5 cm × ca. 2 mm, with peduncle 2.7–8 cm. Flowers bisexual. Sepals greenish purple, linear-lanceolate, 5–7 × ca. 1 mm. Petals 9–17 × ca. 0.5 mm. Stamens 3; filaments 3–6 mm; anthers 1–1.8 mm. Ovary narrowly cylindrical, 2.5–4 cm; styles ca. 7 mm. Fruit (2–)4–6(–8) cm. Seeds 30–70, oblong-ovoid, 1.2–1.8 × ca. 0.6 mm, ca. 6–12-ribbed; ribs obscurely tuberculate or ridged; rounded at both ends, without tails.

Locality: Happy Valley, Chai Wan, Sai Keng, Tai O. HK sheet 7051, 27111, 27112.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; E & S Asia, Africa, Australia, also introduced into N America.
Ecology: Paddy fields and ditches. Flowering & fruiting: May–Sep.
Notes: The species was reported as Blyxa octandra (Roxb.) Planch ex Thwaites previously (Check List HK Plants 77. 1993).

Blyxa japonica (Miq.) Maxim. ex Asch. & Gürke 水篩
Engler & Prantl, Pflanzenfam. 2(1): 253. 1889; FGZ 649, fig. 343. 1956; FRPS 8: 171, pl. 67: 1 – 2. 1992; FFJ 6: 29. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 13, pl. 6. 2000; FGD 6: 297, fig. 166. 2005; FOC 23: 98. 2010.
Hydrilla japonica Miq., Ann. Mus. Bot. Lugduno-Batavi 2: 271. 1866.
Blyxa laevissima Hayata, Icon. Pl. Formosan. 5: 208 – 209, fig. 77a – b. 1915.
Ottelia japonica Miq., Ann. Mus. Bot. Lugduno-Batavum 2: 271. 1866.
Lagarosiphon roxburghii auct. non Benth.: FKH 257. 1912.

Submerged herb. Stems elongate, 10–20 cm tall, branched. Leaves cauline, lanceolate, 3–6 cm × 1–3 mm, veins 3, apex acuminate. Spathes sessile, green, 1–3 cm × 1–3 mm. Flowers bisexual. Sepals green with purple midvein, linear-lanceolate, 2–4 × 0.5–1 mm. Petals 6–10 × 0.5–1 mm. Stamens 3; filaments 1–3 mm, smooth; anthers 1.8–2.5 mm. Ovary conical; styles 3–4 mm. Fruit 1–2.5 cm. Seeds 30 – 60, narrowly elliptic, smooth, obtuse at both ends.

Locality: Pat Heung. HK sheet 27094.
Distribution: NE, E, C & S China to Sichuan; Japan, Korea, Indochina to S Asia, Europe.
Ecology: Paddy fields, marshy pools and ditches. Flowering & fruiting: May–Oct.

Egeria densa Planch. 水蘊草
Ann. Sci. Nat., Bot., sér. 3, 11: 80. 1849; FOC 23: 102. 2010.

Submerged herb. Stems 1–3 mm in diam. Leaves whorled, recurved, 10–40 × 1.5–4.5 mm, margin minutely serrate. Male spathes 2–4-flowered, 7.5–12 mm; pedicel to 8 cm. Sepals 3; petals 3, ovate, white; stamens 9, anthers yellow.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 42833.
Distribution: Guangdong, Taiwan; native to tropical America.
Ecology: Ditches in cultivation areas. Flowering: Apr.–Oct.
Notes: This species is known to spread and become invasive in mild climate.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Tam Bay, Sheung Pak Nai, Ha Pak Nai
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Halophila beccarii Asch. 貝克喜鹽草
Nuov. Giorn. Bot. Ital. 3: 302. 1871; Fl. Males., Ser. I, 5(4): 411. 1957; FRPS 8: 188, pl. 74. 1992; FTW ed. 2, 5: 15. 2000; Kuo & den Hartog in Short & Coles, Global Seagrass Research Methods 50. 2001; FGD 6: 300, fig. 169. 2005; Yip & Lai, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 44(4): 460. 2006; FOC 23: 102. 2010.

Marine herb. Thin rhizomes with 2 scales covering the base of the erect stem bearing a group of 4–10 leaves at the top. Blades lanceolate, up to 13 mm long, 1–2 mm wide, with pointed apex but lacking cross-veins. Female flowers with 2 styles, 10–15 mm long. Fruits ellipsoidal to ovoid, 4–5 mm by 1.2 mm. Seeds globose, 1.2 × 1 mm.

Locality: Tai Tam Bay, Sheung Pak Nai, Ha Pak Nai. HK sheet 33274, 33275, 39064.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Taiwan; Indo-Pacific region.
Ecology: Coastal mudflats. Flowering: May.
Notes: The lack of cross-veins clearly distinguishes this species from other Halophila species. The species is usually associated with mangrove communities and often exposed at low tide (Kuo & den Hartog, 2001), and has high fecundity and rapid rhizome extension rates so that it can colonize some areas in very short time and disappear quickly when unfavourable conditions come (Fong, Asian Marine Biology 16: 109 – 121. 1999).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Tam, Ho Chung, To Kwa Peng, Hoi Ha, Tsam Chuk Wan, Sunny Bay
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Halophila minor (Zoll.) Hartog 小喜鹽草
Flora Males., Ser. I, 5(4): 410. 1957; FRPS 8: 188, pl. 73: 8. 1992; Kuo & den Hartog in Short & Coles, Global Seagrass Research Methods, 50. 2001; FGD 6: 301. 2005; Yip & Lai, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 44(4): 459. 2006; FOC 23: 102. 2010.
Lemnopsis minor Zoll., Syst. Verz. 1: 75. 1854.
Halophila lemnopsis Miq., Fl. Ind. Bat. 3: 230, fig. 176. 1856.
Halophila ovata auct. non Gaudich.: Hodgkiss & Morton, Mem. HK Nat. Hist. Soc. 13: 28–32. 1978; Check List HK Plants 73. 1978; 77. 1993 [quoad specim. May 1978, Morton s.n. (HK sheet 33276); 23 Jun 1971, Thrower s.n. (HK sheet 30426)].

Marine herb. Leaf blades ovate, 6–12 mm long, 3.5–6 mm wide with (4–)7–12 occasionally branched cross-veins, space between intramarginal veins and blade margin narrow. Dioecious. Male flowers with tepals l.5 mm long, anthers 2.5–3.5 mm long. Female flowers with 3 styles, 8–20 mm long. Fruits 2–3.5 mm in diam.

Locality: Tai Tam, Ho Chung, To Kwa Peng, Hoi Ha, Tsam Chuk Wan, Sunny Bay. HK sheet 38542, 39894, 39895.
Distribution: Hainan, Nansha Islands; Indo-Pacific regions.
Ecology: Coastal mudflats. Flowering: Aug.
Notes: This species has recently been recorded on mudflats adjacent to mangroves (Kwok, Lam & Yip, HK Biodiversity No. 10: 16. 2005). This also represents the first locality of the species in continental China (Yip & Lai, 2006). A re-examination of herbarium specimens found that this species was also previously recorded as Halophila ovata (Check List HK Plants 73. 1978; 77. 1993). There is recent molecular evidence indicating potential divergence between H. minor and H. ovalis (Xu et al., Am. J. Bot.: e56 – e57. 2010).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Tam Bay, Ho Chung, Lai Chi Wo, Wu Shek Kok, San Tau
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Halophila ovalis (R. Br.) Hook. f. 喜鹽草
Fl. Tasm. 2: 25. 1858; Fl. Males., Ser. I, 5(4): 408. 1957; FRPS 8: 186, pl. 73: 1–7. 1992; K. F. Zhao & F. T. Li, Halophytes of China 320. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 15. 2000; Kuo & den Hartog in Short & Coles, Global Seagrass Research Methods 50. 2001; FGD 6: 301. 2005; Yip & Lai, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 44(4): 459. 2006; FOC 23: 101. 2010.
Caulinia ovalis R. Br., Prod. Fl. Nov. Holl. 1: 339. 1810.
Halophila minor auct. non (Zoll.) den Hartog: Xing et al., Mem. HK Nat. Hist. Soc. 23: 122. 2000.
Halophila ovata auct. non Gaudich.: FKH 257. 1912; Fong, Asian Marine Biology 16: 111. 1999.

Marine herb. Rhizome internodes and petiole up to 10 cm long. Leaf blade varies in shape from oblong-elliptic, spatulate, obovate, to ovate, rarely linear, 10–40 mm long, 5–20 mm wide, with 12–28 often branched cross-veins on either side of the midrib. Dioecious. Male flowers with tepals 3–5(–6) mm, anthers 1.5–2.5 mm long. Female flowers with 3 styles, 10–40 mm long. Fruits 3–6 mm in diam. Seeds subglobose.

Locality: Tai Tam Bay, Ho Chung, Lai Chi Wo, Wu Shek Kok, San Tau. Y. W. Lam 821; HK sheet 39897, 39898.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Taiwan, Nansha Islands; N Pacific, S Africa, Indo-Pacific, S Australia.
Ecology: Coastal mudflats on shallow beaches. Flowering: Aug.
Notes: The species is the most common seagrass in the tropical and subtropical regions of the Indo-West Pacific and inhabits various environments, resulting in considerable morphological variation (Kuo & den Hartog, 2001). Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Hydrilla verticillata (L. f.) Royle 黑藻
Ill. Bot. Himal. Mts. 1: t. 376. 1839; FKH 257. 1912; FGZ 647. 1956; FHN 4: 59. 1977; FRPS 8: 183, pl. 72: 1 – 6. 1992; FFJ 6: 24, fig. 17. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 15. 2000; FGD 6: 295, fig. 164. 2005; FOC 23: 101. 2010.
Serpicula verticillata L. f., Suppl. Pl. 416. 1781[1782].

Submerged herb. Leaves in whorls of 3–8, linear or narrowly strap-shaped, 0.7–1.7 cm × 1–4 mm, midvein distinct, margin conspicuously denticulate, apex acute. Male spathe green; sepals white, ca. 2.3 × 0.7 mm; petals reflexed, white, or reddish, ca. 2×0.5 mm. Female spathe green; flowers similar to male ones. Fruit with 2–9 spine-like projections or smooth and without projection. Seeds (1–)2–6.

Locality: Cultivated. S. Y. Hu 13709.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China except NW; Asia, Australia and Europe, introduced into N America.
Ecology: Running freshwater in ponds and ditches. Flowering & fruiting: May–Oct.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Po, San Wai, Fanling, Lantau Island, also cultivated in Hong Kong Wetland Park
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Ottelia alismoides (L.) Pers. 龍舌草（水車前）
Syn. Pl. 1: 400. 1805; FKH 257. 1912; FGZ 649. 1956; FRPS 8: 153, pl. 58. 1992; FFJ 6: 26, fig. 19. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 18, pl. 7. 2000; FGD 6: 291. 2005; FOC 23: 95. 2010.
Statiotes alismoides L., Sp. Pl. 1: 535. 1753.
Damasonium indicum Willd., Sp. Pl. Editio quarta 2(1): 276. 1799, nom. illeg. superfl.
Ottelia alismoides (L) Pers. f. oryzetorum Kom., Izv. Imp. Bot. Sada Petra Velikago 10: 122. 1910.
Ottelia condorensis Gagnep., Bull. Soc. Bot. France 54(7): 543. 1907.
Ottelia dioecia S. Z. Yan, J. Sci. Med. Jinan Univ. 2: 162, fig. 187. 1982.
Ottelia indica Planch., Bombay Fl. 278. 1861.
Ottelia japonica Miq., Ann. Mus. Bot. Lugduno-Batavum 2: 271. 1866.

Submerged herb. Petiole varying greatly in length according to depth of water, 2–40 cm; leaf blade wholly submerged, varying greatly in shape and size, usually broadly ovate, ovate-elliptic, nearly orbicular, cordate, or sometimes lanceolate, ca. 20×18 cm or more, membranous, margins entire or serrate. Flowers bisexual or plants occasionally dioecious-polygamous. Spathe 2.5–4 × 1.5–2.5 cm, 2–3-lobed at apex, with 3–6 longitudinal wings. Flowers solitary, sessile. Petals white, slightly purple, or bluish, obovate, 2–3 cm. Stamens 3–9(–12); filaments glandular hairy; anthers narrowly oblong, yellow, 3–4 mm. Ovary nearly globose, with 3–9(–10) carpels; styles 6 – 12, deeply 2-lobed. Fruit 2–5 × 0.8–1.8 cm. Seeds fusiform, 1–2 mm, densely hairy, whitish.

Locality: Tai Po, San Wai, Fanling, Lantau Island, also cultivated in Hong Kong Wetland Park. W. J. Tutcher 9958; HK sheet 27121, 27129.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China especially in E & SW; Africa, E & S Asia, Australia; introduced into N America.
Ecology: Paddy fields, ponds and ditches. Flowering: Apr.–Oct.
Uses: Forage.

Vallisneria natans (Lour.) H. Hara 苦草
J. Jap. Bot. 49: 136. 1974; FYN 4: 750, fig. 208. 1986; FRPS 8: 177, pl. 69. 1992; FFJ 6: 26, fig. 20. 1995; FGD 6: 294, fig. 163. 2005; FOC 23: 99. 2010.
Physkium natans Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 663. 1790.
Vallisneria gigantea Graebn., Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 49: 68. 1912; Fl. Males. 5(4): 388, fig. 4. 1957; FTW ed. 2, 5: 18. 2000.
Vallisneria asiatica Miki, Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 48: 329. 1934.
Vallisneria spiralis auct. non L.: FKH 257. 1912; FGZ 648. 1956; Check List HK Plants 77. 1993.

Submerged herb. Rhizome tuberous; stolons white, ca. 2 mm in diam., usually smooth. Leaves 0.2–2 m × 0.5–2 cm, veins 5–9, margin entire or inconspicuously serrulate, apex obtuse. Male spathe ovate-conical, 1.5–2 cm × 5–10 mm, with more than 200 male flowers; sepals strongly convex; stamens 1, filaments sometimes 2-lobed at apex, with hairs at base. Female spathe 1.5–2 cm; peduncle 30–50 cm or longer, slender. Sepals greenish purple, 2–4 × ca. 3 mm, apex obtuse; petals white, minute; staminodes 3. Fruit cylindrical, 5–30 cm × ca. 5 mm. Seeds narrowly obovoid, glandular hairy.

Locality: Ho Chung, also cultivated. Y. S. Lau 3215.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China except NW; tropical and subtropical Asia, Japan, Australia.
Ecology: Paddy fields, ditches and ponds. Flowering: Nov.

Aponogeton lakhonensis A. Camus 水蕹
Notul. Syst.(Paris) 1: 273. 1910; FRPS 8: 34. 1992; FGD 6: 303. 2005; FOC 23: 104. 2010.
Aponogeton natans auct. non (L.) Engl. & Krause: FHN 4: 64. 1977.
Aponogeton monostachyon auct. non L. f.: FKH 291. 1912.

Aquatic herb; rhizomes ovoid-globular or oblong, toward 2 cm. Leaves basal, submersed or floating, narrow ovate to lanceolate, 4–6 × 0.7–2 cm, base cordate or rounded, apex obtuse or acute, margin entire, midvein 1, parallel veins 3–4 on each sides of midvein; petioles of submersed leaves 9–15 cm, of floating leaves 40–60 cm. Scapes ca. 20 cm, exserted from the water when flowering; spikes cylindrical, ca. 5 cm; spathes caducous. Flowers bisexual, tepals 2, yellow, free, spathulate-obovate, 2×0.7 mm, midrib obvious. Stamens 6, slightly longer than tepals, free, 2-cycled. Carpels 3–6, free or connate at base, ovary 4–6-ovuled. Follicle ovoid, apex attenuate into a short and obtuse beak.

Locality: Tsuen Wan. W. J. Tutcher 11576; HK sheet 29894.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Jiangxi, Fujian, Zhejiang; India, Thailand, Indochina, Malaysia.
Ecology: Ponds, ditches or paddy fields. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Oct.

Potamogeton pusillus L. 小眼子菜
Sp. Pl. 127. 1753; FRPS 8: 44, pl. 12. 1992; FGD 6: 306. 2005; FOC 23: 111. 2010.

Submersed herb, without rhizomes. Stems cylindrical or subcylindrical, 0.5 mm in diam., branched, internodes 1.5–6 cm. Stipules membranous, connate into tubiform, 0.5–1.2 cm. Leaves sessile, linear, 2–6 cm × 1 mm, apex acuminate, entire; veins 1–3, midvein clear, lateral veins inconspicuous; dormant buds thin, fusiform, 1–2.5 cm. Spikes pedunculate, terminal, 8–10 mm, with flowers 2–3 whorls, interruptedly arranged. Flowers small. Tepals 4, green. Drupelets oblique-obovate, 1.5–2 mm, apex with a curved beak.

Locality: Mai Po. S. T. Dunn 6815; Y. W. Lam 34.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China and temperate regions of N hemisphere.
Ecology: Ponds and marshes. Flowering & fruiting : May – Oct.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Shek O, Sai Kung, Mai Po
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Ruppia maritima L. 川蔓藻
Sp. Pl. 127. 1753; FKH 291. 1912; FRPS 8: 83. 1992; FGD 6: 307. 2005; FOC 23: 118. 2010.
Ruppia rostellata W.D.J. Koch ex Rchb., Iconogr. Bot., Ic. Pl. Crit. 2: 66, t. 174, fig. 306. 1824; FHN 4: 65. 1977.

Submersed herb. Stems slender, milk-yellow, angulate, muchbranched, 60–100 cm, internodes 1–6 cm. Leaves linear 2–10 cm × 0.3–0.5 mm, basally with membranous winged-sheath; sheath 2–10 × 0.4 mm, auricle rotund-obtuse, apex acuminate or acute, 1-veined. Spikes 2–4 cm, 2-flowered, exserted out sheath after flowering; peduncle 10–18 mm, not spirally twisted in fruiting. Stamens 2. Carpels 4–6; ovary long-neck bottle-like, asymmetric; stigma umbonate. Drupelets 4–6, ovate-rotund, 2 × 1.5 mm, with straight or slightly curved short beak, stalk 5–17 mm.

Locality: Shek O, Sai Kung, Mai Po. HK sheet 7778, 39602, 42835.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Zhejiang, Jiangsu, Shandong, Liaoning, Gansu, Qinghai, Xinjiang, Taiwan; temperate and subtropical sea area and salt lakes.
Ecology: Coastal lagoons, marshes. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Jun.

Najas graminea Delile 草茨藻
Descr. Égypte, Hist. Nat. 2: 282. 1813; FKH 291. 1912; Triest , Mém. Acad. Roy. Sci. Outre-Mer, Cl. Sci. Nat. Méd., Collect. 8vo. 22: 135. 1988; FRPS 8: 123. 1992; FGD 6: 312. 2005; FOC 23: 93. 2010.
Najas minor auct. non Allioni: FHK 345. 1861.

Stems unarmed, 10–20(– 60) cm tall, 0.5 – 1(– 1.5) mm in diam. Leaves narrowly linear to linear, 10–25(–33) × 0.4–1 mm; septa absent; fibres mostly present on and near both sides of the midrib and near margins; sheath 1.5–3(–4) × 1–2 mm, deeply auriculate; auricles narrowly triangular or lanceolate, 1–2 × 0.2–0.3 mm, serrulate with several teeth on each side, apex acute; leaf margin minutely and densely serrulate with 30–50 inconspicuous teeth on each side, consisting of brownish spine cells only. Plants monoecious; flowers solitary, or sometimes 2–4 together. Male flowers naked, usually more toward upper axils, ca. 1 mm, elliptic; spathe absent; anther 4-celled. Female flowers naked, 1.5–2(–3.7) mm; style ca. 1 mm; stigmas 2(–4)-lobed. Fruit oblong, 1.5–2 × ca. 0.8 mm. Seeds ellipsoidal-oblong, 1.5–2.4 × 0.5–0.7, with 25 – 35 rows of pits; areoles hexangular and irregularly polygonal toward ends, or rectangular, 0.06–0.08 mm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Sai Kung. C. Wright 511 (BM, K); HK sheet 42834.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hebei, Henan, Liaoning, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; widely distributed in Asia, Australia and Europe; introduced in N America.
Ecology: Ponds, paddy fields, usually in still or slow-moving water. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Sep.
Notes: The species was recorded as Najas minor Allioni previously (Check List HK Plants 293. 2002; 103. 2004), based on an un-confirmed sighting record in the 1990s. The earliest record is the specimen collected by Charles Wright during the U. S. North Pacific Exploring Expedition (1853–1856), then identified as “N. minor” (FHK, 1861). However, N. minor as currently recognised is distinguished by its stems armed with spines and leaves with septa. Recently, a population of N. graminea has been found in a sheltered pool in Sai Kung.

Najas pseudogracillima Triest 擬纖細茨藻
Mém. Acad. Roy. Sci. Outre-Mer, Cl. Sci. Nat. Méd., Collect. 8vo. 22: 98. 1988; FOC 23: 93. 2010.

Stems ca. 10 cm tall, ca. 0.5 mm in diam. Leaves often in pseudowhorls of 5, 9–11 × ca. 0.3 mm; midrib lacking spines; septa absent; fibres absent; sheath truncate, 1–2 mm; auricles orbicular to slightly obcordate, short, minutely serrulate with 3–5 teeth, upper margin on each side minutely serrulate with 6 – 10 teeth. Plants monoecious; flowers 1–3 per axil, male flowers in upper axils and female ones below. Male flowers elliptic, 0.6–0.8 mm; spathe absent; anther 1-celled; unisporangiate. Female flowers inconspicuous, ca. 1 mm; style ca. 1 mm; stigmas 2–3-lobed. Fruit 1.8–2 × ca. 0.5 mm. Seeds elliptic-oblong, 1.85–2.0 × 0.5 mm, with more than 25 rows of pits, not enclosed in spathe; areoles oblong, longitudinally elongate, rather irregularly arranged per 12–15 in each longitudinal row, irregularly shaped and longer than broad; cell walls not raised.

Locality: Sha Tin (Chung Chi College Campus). J. P. W. Woo 2 (P); S. Y. Hu 11263 (K).
Distribution: Endemic to Hong Kong.
Ecology: Ponds. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Nov.
Notes: The holotype specimen (S. Y. Hu 11263, K) was collected from the campus of Chung Chi College on 22 Nov. 1971. Triest (1988) noted that, in the specimen Woo 2 (deposited at P), this species was found mixed with N. pseudograminea. Najas pseudogracillima is vegetatively similar to N. gracillima but differs by having male flowers without a spathe, whereas N. gracillima has male flowers with a spathe.

Najas pseudograminea W. Koch 擬草茨藻
Ber. Schweiz. Bot. Ges. 44: 339. 1935; Triest, Mém. Acad. Roy. Sci. Outre-Mer, Cl. Sci. Nat. Méd., Collect. 8vo. 22: 121. 1988; FOC 23: 93. 2010.
Najas tenuifolia R. Br. subsp. pseudograminea (W. Koch) W. J. de Wilde, Fl. Malesiana 1(6): 168. 1962.

Stems ca. 10 cm tall, ca. 1 mm in diam. Leaves often in pseudowhorls of 3, 16–20 × 0.6–1.0 mm; midrib without spines; septa clearly visible up to halfway the margin; fibers present near each margin but absent on and near both sides of the midrib; sheath truncate to auriculate, 1–2 mm; auricles linear, short, minutely serrulate with 3–8 teeth, upper margin on each side minutely serrulate with 30–50 teeth. Plants monoecious; flowers 1–3 per axil, male flowers in upper axils and female ones below. Male flowers elliptic, 1.5–2.3 mm, enclosed in spathe with short neck; anther 4-celled. Female flowers inconspicuous, ca. 0.7–1 mm; style ca. 0.7 mm; stigmas 2- or 3-lobed. Fruit 1–1.3 × ca. 0.4 mm. Seeds not enclosed in spathe, elliptic-oblong, 1–1.3 × 0.24–0.43 mm, with more than 20 rows of pits; areoles regularly arranged per 25–30 in each longitudinal row, squarish to hexagonal or rectangular; cell walls not raised.

Locality: Sha Tin (Chung Chi College Campus). J. P. W. Woo 2 (P).
Distribution: Thailand, Philippines, Indonesia, East Timor, Solomon Islands, N Australia.
Ecology: Ponds. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.
Notes: Triest (1988) noted that, in the specimen Woo 2 (deposited at P), this species was found mixed with N. pseudogracillima.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Sheung Sze Wan, Lai Chi Wo, Tung Chung Pier
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Zostera japonica Asch. & Graebn. 矮大葉藻
Pflanzenr. 31(IV 11): 32. 1907; FRPS 8: 90. 1992; FOC 23: 107. 2010.
Zostera nana auct. non Roth: Check List HK Plants 78. 1993.

Submersed marine herb; rhizomes creeping. Stems slender. Leaves 5–35 cm × 1–2 mm, apex obtuse or emarginate, entire, with a conspicuous midvein and lateral veins, and with 3 or 4 secondary veins between the midvein and lateral veins; sheaths 2–10 cm, margin membranous, with rounded auricles; spathe sheath 5–8 cm, apex blade 8–15 cm; spadix enclosed in spathe sheath. Anther 4.5–6 mm. Ovary 2 mm, stigma 2. Fruits oblong, ca. 4 mm, beaked. Seeds brownish, smooth and nitid.

Locality: Sheung Sze Wan, Lai Chi Wo, Tung Chung Pier. Y. W. Lam 101, 111, 699.
Distribution: Shandong, Hebei, Liaoning; Eurasia and Africa.
Ecology: Sea water.
Notes: Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Sciaphila ramosa Fukuy. & T. Suzuki 多枝霉草
J. Jap. Bot. 12: 414. 1936; FRPS 8: 193. 1992; T. L. Wu et al., J. Trop & Subtrop. Bot. 8(2): 158. 2000; Hsieh et al, Taiwania 48(4): 244. 2003; FOC 23: 126. 2010.

Erect herb, 8–12 cm tall, purplish, glabrous. Stems usually branched, 0.5–0.7 mm in diam. Leaves scale-like, lanceolate, ca. 0.8–1.3 mm, apex acuminate to acute. Inflorescence terminal, racemose, erect, ca. 1 cm, 3–9-flowered; bracts lanceolate, 1.5–2 mm, apex acute; pedicels 3–4 mm, straight. Male flower on upper part, 2 mm in diam.; perianth segments 6, lobes subequal, ovate or ovate-lanceolate, ca. 0.75 mm, apex mucronate or acute; stamens 2 or 3, subssesile, anther 4-celled. Female flowers perianth segments 4–6, ± equal, oblong to triangular, ca. 0.7 mm, apex acute, without appendage. Carpels ca. 20–30, style subapical, awl-shaped, 0.5–0.6 mm, apex papillate, exceeding ovary. Mature carpels obovate, slightly curved, 0.7 mm.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. Y. W. Lam 1600.
Distribution: Taiwan.
Ecology: Litter layer in forests. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.
Notes: Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Sciaphila secundiflora Thwaites ex Benth. 大柱霉草
Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc 7: 10. 1855; Meerendonk, Fl. Males. ser. I. 10: 116. 1984; Hsieh et al., Taiwania 48(4): 245. 2003; FOC 23: 125. 2010.
Sciaphila megastyla Fukuy. & T. Suzuki, J. Jap. Bot. 12: 412. 1936; FRPS 8: 191. 1992; T. L. Wu et al., J. Trop & Subtrop. Bot. 8(2): 157. 2000; Check List HK Plants 293. 2002; 104. 2004.

Saprophytic herb, 4–12 cm tall, glabrous, pink or reddish. Stems slender, usually unbranched, 0.7–1 mm in diam. Leaves scale-like, ovate or ovate-lanceolate, 2–4 mm, apex acuminate to acute. Inflorescence terminal, racemose, erect, ca. 1–5 cm, 3–9-flowered; bracts lanceolate, 1–3 mm, acute; pedicels 1–2 mm, straight. Male flowers towards apex, 6–7 mm in diam., perianth segments usually 6, subulate, ca. 2.5–3.5 mm, patent, equal; stamens 2– 3, subsessile; anthers 4-celled. Female flowers towards base, globose, perianth segments 6, ± equal, oblong to lanceolate, ca. 2–2.5 mm, acuminate. Carpels 10–80, free, obovate, 0.5–1 mm, upper papillate; style club-shaped, 0.6–0.7 mm, inserted laterally at base or about halfway. Mature carpels obovoid, 1 mm, with persistent style.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan. Y. W. Lam 1599; HK sheet 33860.
Distribution: Guangdong, Taiwan; Sri Lanka, Malesia, Japan, Pacific islands.
Ecology: Litter layer in forests. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.
Notes: Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Authority: (Griseb. & H. Wendl.) H. Wendl. ex Becc.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Archontophoenix alexandrae (F. Muell.) H. Wendl. & Drude 假檳榔
Linnaea 39: 212. 1875; FHN 4: 170, fig. 1072. 1977; FGD 2: 460, fig. 323. 1991; FRPS 13(1): 130. 1991.

Evergreen tree, to 20 m tall, monoecious. Stems solitary, with leaf scar rings. Leaves pinnate, up to 2.5 m; pinnae arranged regularly, about 80 on each side of rachis, long lanceolate, up to 80 × 5 cm, green adaxially, whitish abaxially; petioles 20–40 cm; sheaths closed and forming a crownshaft on top of stem, green, thick and leathery. Inflorescences under the crownshafts, up to 70 cm, branched 3–4 orders, pendulous; prophylls tubular, deciduous. Flowers white, in triad of a pair of male flowers with a female one in the middle; male flowers: 5–6 mm, sepals usually 3, petals 3, stamens 9–16; female flowers: sepals 3, petals 3, staminodes 3–4. Fruits globose, 0.8–1 cm in diam., red when mature; epicarp smooth, mesocarp thin, fleshy, with fibres, endocarp smooth, thin and fragile. Seed usually 1, endosperm ruminate.

Locality: Commonly cultivated. HK sheet 29451, 29452, 29453.
Distribution: Australia; widely cultivated in tropical areas.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr.; fruiting: Apr.–Jul.
Uses: Ornamental.

Arenga pinnata (Wurmb.) Merr. 砂糖椰子（桄榔）
Interpr. Herb. Amboin.: 119. 1917; FOC 23: 151. 2010.

Evergreen tree; stems solitary, up to 20 m tall and 30–60 in diam., with long internodes. Leaves pinnate, up to 7 × 1.6 m; pinnae about 110 pairs pointed to different directions, 40–120 × 5 cm, linear, with ear-like bases, undulate margins and erose apices, green adaxially and whitish abaxially; petioles to 1.5 m; sheaths persistent, with black needle-like fibres. Inflorescences interfoliar or seldom infrafoliar, up to 3.5 m, branched 1 order, pendulous; flowers solitary, large; male flowers purplish, ovoid, about 2 cm, sepals 3, petals 3, stamens 60–120; female flowers subglobse, 5–6 cm in diam., sepals 3, petals 3, carpels 3. Fruits subglobose, 7 cm in diam., trigonous, with stigma remains, yellowish or orangish. Seed 1–3, ovoid, black, endosperm homogeneous.

Locality: Cultivated.
Distribution: Malaysia, Indonesia, Philippines, New Guinea.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Jun.; fruiting: Lasting 1–2 years after flowering.
Uses: Ornamental, additive (flavouring), food (sugar, starch).
Notes: Arenga westerhoutii Griff., a plant native to Hainan, Guangxi and Yunnan, was previously misidentified as A. pinnata (cf. FHN 4: 167, fig. 1068. 1977; FGD 2: 452. 1991; FRPS 13(1): 110. 1991) but differs in pinnae arrangement, with pinnae of A. westerhoutii being regularly arranged and spaced in same plane except for basal few pinnae.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Happy Valley, S of Wan Chai Gap
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Calamus ?egregius Burret 短葉省藤
Notizbl. Bot. Gart. Berlin-Dahlem 13: 599. 1937; FHN 4: 173. 1977; FGD 2: 469. 1991; FRPS 13(1): 105. 1991; FOC 23: 139. 2010.
Calamus latifolius auct. non Roxb.: FKH 286. 1912.

Climbing rattan. Stems clustered, to 30 m or longer. Leaves pinnate, pinnae 2–3-clustered in alternate groups, lanceolate, 10–23 × 2–3 cm, margins bristly; rachis 0.85–1.5 m long, with single recurved spines abaxially, apex of leaf rachis elongate to a whip-like cirri with clawed spines; sheath whitish green with flattened, 1–2 cm long spines and brown hairs, ocreas 1.5–5 cm, split, knees present, flagella absent. Inflorescences branched to 2 orders, 0.25–1 m long, not flagellate; prophylls tubular, 2-ridged laterally, with scattered, short spines, rachillae 2–4 cm long.

Locality: Happy Valley, S of Wan Chai Gap. W. J. Tutcher 4678, 8473; HK sheet 7683.
Distribution: Hainan.
Ecology: Forests or thickets.
Usage: Materials (handcrafts).
Notes: According to Dunn and Tutcher (1912), Calamus latifolius is present in Hong Kong, but the voucher specimens (W. J. Tutcher 4678, 8473), rather poor and without fruits, are here temporarily determined as Calamus egregius, and further material is necessary before its status can be settled. The species was reported as Calamus palustris Griff. previously (Check List HK Plants 294. 2002; 104. 2004).

Calamus tetradactylus Hance 白藤
J. Bot. 13: 289. 1875; FKH 286. 1912; FHN 4: 174, fig. 1075. 1977; FGD 2: 471. 1991; FRPS 13(1): 87. 1991; FOC 23: 140. 2010.
Calamus bonianus Becc., Webbia 3: 231. 1910; FRPS 13(1): 87. 1991.
Calamus tetradactylus Hance var. bonianus (Becc.) Conrard, Fl. Gén. Indo-Chine 6: 1047. 1937.

Climbing rattan. Stems clustered, to 6 m or longer, slender, 6–15 cm in diam. Leaves pinnate, 45–55 cm; pinnae 2–4-clustered, 4–5 at apex, lanceolate, 10–26 × 2–5.5 cm; rachis with few single hook-like spines; cirrus absent; sheath green, glabrous, with few triangular spines or not; knees present; flagellum slender, to 1 m, with hook-like single spines; petioles short. Inflorescences borne from flagella, prophyll tubular, male inflorescences branched 2–3 orders, ca. 50 cm, the lower branches ca. 8 cm; rachillae 10–13 mm, with 4–6 flowers per side; male flowers small, ca. 3 mm; female inflorescences branched 2 orders, branches 3–4, 8–15 cm, the lower rachillae 2.5–5 cm, with 5–6 flowers per side; female flowers small, 3–4 mm. Fruits globose, 8–9 mm in diam., whitish yellow, scales in 21–23 vertical rows, with a groove in the middle, persistent sepals and petals stalk-like. Seeds 1, 6 mm in diam., endosperm homogeneous or slightly ruminate.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1748, 2654; HK sheet 39265.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian; Vietnam, Cambodia, Laos, Thailand.
Ecology: Forests and thickets. Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: Jun.–Jul.
Uses: Materials (furniture, handcrafts).
Notes: The type specimen (Hance Herb. No. 18979, BM) was collected by G. Dods from Wong Nai Chung around 1870s.

Calamus thysanolepis Hance 毛鱗省藤
J. Bot. 12: 265. 1874; FKH 286. 1912; FGD 2: 474. 1991; FRPS 13(1): 68. 1991; FOC 23: 137. 2010.
Calamus hoplites Dunn, J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 38: 369. 1908; FRPS 13(1): 69. 1991.
Calamus thysanolepis Hance var. polylepis Wei, Guihaia 6: 24. 1986; FRPS 13(1): 69. 1991.

Erect shrubs. Stems clustered, to 5 m tall. Leaves pinnate, to 1.6 m, pinnae 2–6 in groups, point at different directions, not in the same plane, linear or elongate lanceolate, middle pinnae 30–38 × 1.5–2 cm, adaxial veins and margins bristly, abaxial rachis with short, single, hook-like spine; sheath open, without knee and flagellum, greenish brown; spines black and dense, to 2 cm; ocreas to 30 cm; petioles sparsely armed with straight, black-tipped spines. Inflorescences to 1 m, erect; male inflorescence branched 2–3 orders, female one branched 2 order; prophyll split to fibre-like, sometimes longer than the branch; male rachilla 3–4 cm, bearing 12–15 flowers each side; female rachilla 7.5 cm. Fruits ovoid, 15 × 10 mm, scales in 18–21 vertical rows, reddish brown, without groove in the middle, with cilia on the margins; persistent sepals and petals stalk-like. Seed 1, ellipsoidal, endosperm homogeneous.

Locality: Aberdeen, Tai Mo Shan. L. T. Lo 408, 451; K. L. Yip 4213.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian; Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Jun. – Jul.; fruiting: Sep.–Oct.
Uses: Materials.
Notes: The type specimen (Hance Herb. No. 18373, BM) was collected by G. Dods from Tai Tam Tuk in Nov. 1873.

Calamus walkeri Hance 多果省藤
J. Bot. 12: 266. 1874; FKH 286. 1912; FGD 2: 470. 1991; FRPS 13(1): 75. 1991; FOC 23: 141. 2010.
Calamus faberi Becc., Ann. Roy. Bot. Gard. Calc. 11(1): 274, t. 99. 1908; FHN 4: 175. 1977; FGD 2: 470. 1991; FRPS 13(1): 75. 1991 [“faberii”]; Check List HK Plants 294. 2002; 104. 2004.
Calamus faberi Becc. var. brevispicatus (Wei) S. J. Pei & S. Y. Chen, Act. Phytotax. Sin. 27: 133. 1989; FRPS 13(1): 76. 1991.
Calamus tonkinensis Becc., Ann. Roy. Bot. Gard. Calc. 11(1): 275. 1908.
Calamus tonkinensis Becc. var. brevispicatus Wei, Guihaia 9: 31. 1986.

Climbing rattan. Stems clustered, to 30 m or longer, about 3 cm in diam. Leaves pinnate, 1–3 m; pinnae arranged regularly on the same plane, linear-lanceolate, 30–45 × 1.5–2.5 cm, bristly on midveins and margins; rachis with single, black-tipped, claw-like spines; cirri absent; sheath green hairy and spiny; spines flattened to 2.5 cm; ocreas dense bristly; flagellum whip-like, to 5 m, with strong, claw-like spines. Inflorescences borne from flagella; female inflorescences branched 2 orders, branches 12–20 cm, with 10–20 rachillae on each side; prophyll tubular, flattened, with short sparse spines; lower rachillae 5–7 cm, with 12–16 flowers on each side; flowers small, ca. 3 mm. Fruits oblong-ovoid, 1–1.2 × 1 cm, yellowish brown when mature, scales in 15–18 vertical rows, with brown narrow margin; endosperm homogeneous.

Locality: Happy Valley, Mount Parker. Y. W. Lam 578; HK sheet 7709, 29556.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong; Vietnam.
Ecology: Lowland forests. Flowering: Jun.–Dec.; fruiting: Sep.–Mar. of the following year.
Uses: Materials (furniture, handcrafts).
