Notes: The type specimen (Hance Herb. No. 18225, BM) was collected by A. L. Walker from Hong Kong Island in Aug. 1873.

Caryota maxima Blume 魚尾葵
Mart., Hist. Nat. Palm. 3: 195. 1838; FOC 23: 150. 2010.
Caryota ochlandra Hance, J. Bot. 17: 174. 1879; FKH 285. 1912; FHN 4: 163, fig. 1064. 1977; FGD 2: 454, fig. 318. 1991; FRPS 13(1): 115. 1991; Check List HK Plants 294. 2002; 104. 2004.

Large tree. Stems solitary, to 25 m tall, to 50 cm in diam., nodes well spaced. Leaves bipinnate, to 4 m, borne along upper half of stems; pinnae 12–28 per side of secondary rachis, drooping, the top pinna being the biggest, triangular, other pinnae smaller downwards, rhombic, the outer margin straight, upper 1/4 to 1/2 of inner margin irregularly toothed; sheaths with black fibres on the margin. Inflorescences to 3.5 m, branched 1 order, rachillae many, 1.5–2.5 m; male flowers ovoid, 15–20 mm, yellowish, stamens 50–110, anthers linear; female flowers 5–6 mm in diam., staminodes 3. Fruits globose, 2–2.5 cm in diam., reddish or orange when mature.

Locality: Cultivated. W. J. Tutcher 10561.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; Indochina, Malay Peninsula, Indonesia, Indian Subcontinent.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: May–Jul.; fruiting: Aug.–Nov.
Uses: Ornamental, food (starch).

Caryota mitis Lour. 短穗魚尾葵（小魚尾葵）
Fl. Cochinch. 2: 569. 1790; FHN 4: 164. 1977; FGD 2: 453. 1991; FRPS 13(1): 115. 1991; FOC 23: 150. 2010.

Large shrub. Stems clustered, 5–8 m tall, 8–15 cm in diam., light green, with well spaced leaf nodes. Leaves bipinnate, to 3 m or longer; pinnae 10–20 on each side of secondary rachis, basal pinnae smaller than the upper ones, triangular, the outer margin straight, upper 1/2 of inner margin erose; sheaths margin with black fibres. Inflorescences 30–60 cm, branched 1 order, rachillae 20–60, 25–55 cm; male flowers elongate ovoid, 8–10 × 2.5–3 mm, stamens 12–25; female flowers 4–5 mm in diam., staminodes 3. Fruits globose, 1.5–2 cm in diam., purplish black when mature.

Locality: Cultivated.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi; Indochina, Malay Peninsula, Indonesia, Indian Subcontinent.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.; fruiting: Aug.–Nov.
Uses: Ornamental.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Victoria Peak, Wong Nai Chung, Tai Po, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Daemonorops jenkinsiana (Griff.) Mart. 黃藤
Hist. Nat. Palm. 3: 327. 1853; FOC 23: 142. 2010.
Calamus jenkinsianus Griff., Calcutta J. Nat. Hist. 5: 81. 1845.
Calamus margaritae Hance, J. Bot. 12: 266. 1874; FKH 286. 1912.
Daemonorops margaritae (Hance) Becc., Rec. Bot. Surv. India 2: 220. 1902; FHN 4: 172, fig. 1074. 1977; FGD 2: 476, fig. 335. 1991; FRPS 13(1): 59. 1991; Check List HK Plants 295. 2002; 104. 2004.

Climbing rattan, or sometimes shrubby. Stems clustered, to 20 m or longer, 4–6 cm in diam., covered by spiny leaf sheaths. Leaves pinnate, 1.5–3 m; pinnae many, regularly arranged, linear or linearlanceolate, middle one 30–45 × 1.5–2 cm, adaxially bristly on veins; rachis apex elongate into a cirrus to 2 m, which armed with strong claw-like spines; sheath densely covered with brown to black hairs, spiny; spines sparsely distributed or in rows, black, flattened or needle-like; ocreas obscure; knees conspicuous. Inflorescences erect, spindly before blooming, 25–30 cm; prophyll boat-like, with flat and straight spines outside, branched 2–3 orders; bracts with few spines or not; male rachillla ca. 3 cm; male flowers oblongovoid, ca. 5 mm; calyx cup-like, slightly 3-fid; petals 3; female rachilla 2–4 cm, 4–7 flowers per side. Fruits globose, 1.7–2 cm in diam., brownish yellow, scales in 18–20 vertical rows, distinctly grooved in the middle, margins slightly dark; persistent sepals and petals flattened. Seed 1, subglobose, endosperm ruminate.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Wong Nai Chung, Tai Po, Lantau Island. H. C. Tang 1135; K. L. Yip 4190; HK sheet 7687.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi; Vietnam, Cambodia, Laos, Myanmar, Thailand, Nepal, Bhutan, India, Bangladesh.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Mar.–May; fruiting: Apr.–Oct.
Uses: Materials (furniture, thatching).
Notes: The type specimen of Calamus margaritae (Hance Herb. No. 18407, BM) was collected by M. Dods from Wong Nai Chung Valley in Apr. 1874.

Dypsis lutescens (H. Wendl.) Beentje & J. Dransf. 散尾葵
Palms Madagascar. 212. 1995. Chrysalidocarpus lutescens H. Wendl., Bot. Zeitung (Berlin) 36(8): 117–118. 1878; FGD 462, fig. 325. 1991; FRPS 13(1): 125. 1991; Check List HK Plants 294. 2002; 104. 2004.

Shrub, 2–6 m tall, unarmed, monoecious. Stems clustered, yellowish green, crownshaft greenish grey, node rings conspicuous. Leaves pinnate, recurved, 1.5–2.5 m; pinnae 40–60 pairs, regularly arranged, linear or linear-lanceolate, 30–40 × 1–2 cm, shorter upwards, shallowly bifid at apex; sheaths closed and forming a crownshaft. Inflorescences borne below the sheaths, 50–70 cm, branched 2–3 orders; branches 20–30 cm; rachillae 8–10, 12–18 cm. Flower small, ovoid, golden yellow; male flowers: sepals 3, petals 3, stamens 6; female flower: sepals 3, petals 3, style short. Fruits obovoid or ovoid, 1.5–2 × 0.8–1 cm, yellow to purple. Seed slightly obovoid, endosperm homogeneous.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 1846.
Distribution: Madagascar; widely cultivated elsewhere.
Ecology: Flowering: May; fruiting: Aug.
Uses: Ornamental.

Licuala fordiana Becc. 穗花軸櫚
Malesia 3: 198. 1889; FKH 285. 1912; FHN 4: 159. 1977; FGD 2: 444. 1991; FRPS 13(1): 30. 1991; FOC 23: 149. 2010.

Moderate shrub, 1.5–2 m tall. Stems clustered, short. Leaves palmate, subrounded or fan-shaped in outline, deeply divided into 15–20 segments; middle segment wider than others, 25–45 × 2–5 cm, apex dentate; petioles 0.8–1 m, the lower half sparsely armed with recurved spines on margins, or sometimes without spines. Inflorescence axillary, 0.5–1.2 m, unbranched or only branched at base, rachillae 1–3, 15–20 cm, hairy; flowers hermaphroditic 6–8 × 2.5 mm. Fruits globose, 7–8 mm in diam., red when mature.

Locality: Aberdeen, Mount Parker. HK sheet 7673, 7675, 33472.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong.
Ecology: Forests, altitude below 500 m. Flowering: Feb.–Mar.; fruiting: Mar.–Jun.
Uses: Ornamental.

Livistona chinensis (Jacq.) R. Br. ex Mart. 蒲葵
Hist. Nat. Palm. 3: 240. 1838; FKH 286. 1912; FGD 2: 445, fig. 311. 1991; FRPS 13(1): 26. 1991; FOC 23: 148. 2010.
Latania chinensis Jacq., Fragm. Bot. 1: 16. 1800.
Livistona subglobosa Mart., Hist. Nat. Palm. 3: 319. 1838.
Livistona chinensis (Jacq.) R. Br. var. subglobosa (Mart.) Becc., Webbia 5: 16. 1912; FTW ed. 2, 5: 660. 2000.

Large tree, to 20 m tall. Stems 20–30 cm in diam., rough ringed with leaf scars; petiole bases persistent when young. Leaves palmate, blades rounded or subrounded, 1–1.8 m in diam., divided to 1/2 depth into single fold, linear-lanceolate segments; segment split to 20–30 cm depth and pendulous; petioles 1–2 m, proximally with green or black-brown, recurved spines on margins; hastula 1–3 cm. Inflorescences 1–1.5 m, branched to 3 orders, partial inflorescences 6–7, about 35 – 45 cm; rachillae 10–20 cm; flowers bisexual, 2–2.5 mm, 4–7 clustered, whitish yellow; calyx deeply 3-lobed, triangular; petals 3-lobed; stamens 6; carpels 3. Fruits ellipsoidal, about 1.8 × 1.2 cm, blue-black or black when matured. Seed 1, ellipsoidal, about 1.5 × 0.9 cm, endosperm homogeneous.

Locality: Cultivated. R. Helms 2953; Y. S. Lau 1691; HK sheet 29535.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Taiwan; Vietnam, S Japan.
Ecology: Coastal forests, often on sandy soils at low elevations. Flowering: Mar.–Apr.; fruiting: May–Jul.
Uses: Ornamental, material (weaving).

Phoenix loureiroi Kunth 刺葵
Enum. Pl. 3: 257. 1841; FOC 23: 144. 2010.
Phoenix hanceana Naudin, J. Bot. 17: 174. 1879; FKH 285. 1912; FHN 4: 165, fig. 1066. 1977; FGD 2: 455. 1991; FRPS 13(1): 10. 1991; FTW ed. 2, 5: 660. 2000; Check List HK Plants 295. 2002; 104. 2004.
Phoenix hanceana Naudin var. formosana Becc., Philipp. J. Sci., C 3: 339. 1908.
Phoenix acaulis auct. non Roxb.: FHK 340. 1861.

Small to moderate tree, 1–5 m tall. Stems solitary or clustered, 25–40 cm in diam., sometimes short and subterranean, rough, with petiole base remains. Leaves pinnate, to 2 m; pinnae 35–120, acanthophylls (pinnae on lower rachis) about 15 per side of rachis, linear, solitary, or 2–3 grouped, not in the same plane; middle pinnae 20–45 × 1–3 cm; sheaths and petioles to 40 cm. Inflorescences branched 1 order, with 30–40 rachillae; prophyll 15–20 cm, dark brown; peduncles to 50 cm. Flowers yellowish white; male flowers: calyx 1–1.5 mm, 3-lobed; petals 3, 4–5 × 1.5–2 mm; stamens 6; female flowers: calyx-lobe ca. 1 mm, petals 2 mm in diam., carpels 3, free, ovoid, 1.5 × 0.8 cm. Fruits oblong, 1.5–2 cm, black or purplish black. Seed 1, endosperm homogeneous.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 663; S. P. Lau 154; K. L. Yip 4414.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; Indian Subcontinent, SE Asia.
Ecology: Open forests. Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: Jun.–Oct.
Uses: Ornamental, material (weaving).

Phoenix roebelenii O'Brien 江邊刺葵（軟葉刺葵、日本葵）
Gard. Chron., ser. 3, 6: 475. 1889; FGD 2: 455, fig. 319. 1991; FRPS 13(1): 10. 1991; FOC 23: 144. 2010.

Small trees, 1–3 m tall. Stems solitary, slender, to 10 cm in diam., with spirally arranged remains of triangular petiole bases. Leaves pinnate, 1–1.5(–2) m; pinnae 25–50 per side of rachis, regularly arranged and in the same plane, linear, soft, 20–30 cm × 5–10 mm, with persistent grey scales on abaxial midribs; acanthophylls (pinnae on lower rachis) about 12 per side. Inflorescences branched 1 order, prophyll 30–50 cm. Male inflorescences 30–55 cm, rachillae ca. 20, 7–20 cm; male flowers: sepals ca. 1 mm; petals 3, ca. 9 mm, stamens 6. Female inflorescences to 35 cm; rachillae 35–45; female flowers subovoid, ca. 6 mm; carpels 3, free. Fruits oblong-obovoid, 14–18 × 6–8 mm, purplish brown. Seed 1, endosperm homogeneous.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 636; HK sheet 29497.
Distribution: Yunnan; Vietnam, Laos, Myanmar, Thailand.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr. – May; fruiting: Jun.–Sep.
Uses: Ornamental.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai, Lamma Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Rhapis excelsa (Thunb.) Henry ex Rehder 棕竹
Rehder, J. Arnold Arbor. 11: 153. 1930; FHN 4: 161, fig. 1062. 1977; FGD 2: 448, fig. 313. 1991; FRPS 13(1): 20, pl. 4: 1–3. 1991; FOC 23: 146. 2010.
Rhapis flabelliformis L’ Hér. ex Aiton, Hort. Kew. 3: 473. 1789; FHK 340. 1861; FKH 286. 1912.
Chamaerops excelsa Thunb., J. A. Murray, Syst. Veg., ed. 14, 984. 1784.

Moderate shrub, dioecious, rhizomatous, 1.2–3 m tall. Stems clustered, slender, 1.5–3 cm in diam., covered with fibrous interwoven leaf sheaths. Leaves palmate, split deeply into 5–12 uneven segments, segments 2–5-ribbed, 20–32 × 1.5–4 cm, apices erose; sheaths with black interwoven fibres; petioles elliptic in cross-section, unarmed; hastula small, semi-circled or triangular. Inflorescences axillary, branched 2–3 orders, ca. 30 cm; prophyll and peduncle bract brown hairy; rachilla glabrous; flowers spirally arranged; male flowers ovoid to oblong, 5–6 mm, calyx cup-shaped, 3-lobed, corolla 3-lobed, stamens 6; female flowers 4 mm, sepals and petals similar to male flower, carpels 3, free, staminodes 6. Fruits usually developed from 1 carpel, subglobose, 8–10 mm in diam., yellow. Seed 1, globose.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai, Lamma Island. H. C. Tang 1776; Y. S. Lau 856, 1873.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian, Yunnan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests or dry forests on slopes. Flowering: Jun.–Sep.
Uses: Ornamental.

Roystonea regia (Kunth) O. F. Cook 大王椰子（王棕）
Science, II, 12: 479. 1900; FGD 2: 463, fig. 326. 1991; FRPS 13(1): 129. 1991.

Large tree, to 30 m tall, dioecious. Stems solitary, to 50 cm in diam., grey-white, smooth, rings of leaf scars conspicuous when young. Leaves pinnate, about 15 in number, to 5 m long, recurved; pinnae to 250 per side, arranged on different planes, elongate lanceolate, 2-lobed at apices, to 90 × 4 cm; sheaths closed and forming a green, leathery crownshaft. Inflorescences to 1.5 m, branched 3–4 orders. Flowers small, white, male flowers 6–7 mm, stamens 6; female flowers 3–3.5 mm. Fruits subglobose, about 1.3 × 1 cm, dark-red. Seed 1, endosperm homogeneous.

Locality: Cultivated.
Distribution: SE USA, C Mexico, Caribbean, Mesoamerica, cultivated elsewhere.
Ecology: Flowering: Mar.–Apr.; fruiting: Oct.
Uses: Ornamental.

Syagrus romanzoffiana (Cham.) Glassm. 皇后葵（金山葵）
Fieldiana, Bot. 31: 382. 1968; FRPS 13(1): 146, pl. 35. 1991.
Cocos romanzoffiana Cham., Choris Voy. Pittor. (Chili): 5, t. 6. 1822.

Tree, 10–16 m tall. Stems solitary, 25–40 in diam., dark grey, leaf scars roughly ringed. Leaves pinnate, 2–5 m, recurved; pinnae many, linear-lanceolate, 40–70(–90) × 3–4(–5) cm, apex bifid, spreading in different planes, 2–6 in groups, with a small gap between groups; sheaths open. Inflorescences interfoliar, 1–2 × 0.6 m, branched 1 order, rachillae up to 80, 30–50 cm, usually zigzagged; male flowers borne on upper rachis, 7–16 mm, sepals 3, petals 3, stamens 6; female flowers borne on lower rachis, 4.5–6 × 4–6 mm, sepals 3, petals 3, staminodes 6-teethed, ovary 3-locular. Fruits globose or obovoid; 3 × 2.8 cm, orange; mesocarp fleshy, fibrous, endocarp thick, woody, with 3 germinating pores near base. Seed 1, endosperm homogeneous.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 3252; HK sheet 29595, 29600.
Distribution: Brazil, S America.
Ecology: Flowering: Feb.; fruiting: Nov.–Mar. of the following year.
Uses: Ornamental.

Pandanus austrosinensis T. L. Wu 露兜草
FHN 4: 535. 1977; FRPS 8: 20, pl. 7. 1992; FGD 6: 402. 2005; FOC 23: 129. 2010.
Pandanus austrosinensis T. L. Wu var. longifolius L. Y. Zhou & X. W. Zhong, J. Wuhan Bot. Res. 10(1): 12. 1992.

Herb. Stems underground branched, with many adventitions roots, stems terrestrial unbranched. Leaves subleathery, strap-shaped, 0.7–1.3 m × 3–5 cm, apex acuminate to triangular, with small serrated flagelliform tips, margin with hamate spine, midrib raised abaxially, sparsely spinose. Male inflorescence consisting of several spikes; spathes towards 25 cm; male flowers many; stamens 5–9, filaments connate into a column; anthers linear, ca. 3 mm, connective prolonged into a small point. Syncarps ellipsoidal-cylindrical, 9–15 × 5–8 cm, consisting of 120–260 drupes; drupes obconical, ca. 3 cm, persistent stigma spinose, furcated or not.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. HK sheet 38938, 39341.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan.
Ecology: Forests, streamsides or roadsides. Fruiting: Sep.

Pandanus kaida Kurz 簕古子（露兜簕）
J. Asiat. Soc. Bengal, Pt. 2, Nat. Hist. 38(2): 148. 1869; Warb., Pflanzenr. 3(9): 52. 1900; B. C. Stone, Fl. Cambodge Loas et Vietnam 20: 43. 1983; FOC 23: 129. 2010.
Pandanus forceps Mart., Webbia 1: 363. 1905; FKH 287. 1912; FHN 4: 177. 1977; FRPS 8: 15. 1992; FGD 6: 401. 2005; Check List HK Plants 296. 2002; 105. 2004.

Shrub or small tree, 1–3 m tall. Stems branched, without aerial roots. Leaves loriform, 1(– 4) m × 3–5 cm, margin and midrib spiniferous, apex acuminate, long flagelliform-caudate. Male inflorescences consisting of several spikes, each spikes ca. 10 cm, spathes in lower part 45 × 4.5 cm; male flowers white, fragrant; stamens 10–20, nearly on top of filament bundle, free parts of filaments ca. 1 mm; anther long-elliptic, ca. 3 mm, apex cuspidate; female inflorescences capitate, 4 × 1.7 cm; spathes several, 14–20 × 2–3 cm; carpels 2–3 connate into a drup, stigma short, forked. Syncarps composed of ca. 150 drupes; drupe obconic, 3 × 1.7 cm, top 5-angled, persistent stigmas 2, opposite, forked, dentiform.

Locality: Tai Tam, Tai Mo Shan. W. J. Tutcher 7222, 5137.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong; Vietnam.
Ecology: Near seashore in forests or cultivated. Flowering: May – Jul.
Uses: Cultivated as hedges, food (young shoot edible).

Pandanus tectorius Parkinson 露兜樹
J. Voy. South Seas 46. 1773; Li, Woody Fl. Taiwan 903, fig. 364. 1963; FHN 4: 176. 1977; FRPS 8: 18. 1992; FGD 6: 401. 2005; FOC 23: 129. 2010.
Pandanus fascicularis Lam., Encycl. 1: 372. 1783; FKH 287. 1912.
Pandanus odoratissimus L. f., Suppl. 424. 1781, excl. syn.; FKH 287. 1912; Stone, Rev. Fl. Ceylon 3: 311, fig. 6 – 7. 1981; Fl. Cambodge Laos et Viet-nam 20: 23. 1983.
Pandanus odoratissimus L. f. var. sinensis (Warb.) Kanehira, Form. Trees rev. ed. 63, fig. 24. 1936; Li, FTW 5: 825. 1978.
Pandanus remotus St. John, Pacif. Sci. 16: 70. 1962. Pandanus sinensis (Warb.) Martel. in Kanehira, Fl. Micrones 69. 1933.
Pandanus tectorius Parkinson var. sinensis Warb., Pflanzenr. 3(9): 48. 1900; FRPS 8: 20. 1992; FGD 6: 402. 2005.

Shrub or small tree, 1–4 m tall; stem branched, with aerial roots. Leaves aggregated on top of stem, leathery, loriform, usually over 1 m × 2–5 cm, margin and midrib abaxially with strong and upward spines, apex long caudate. Male inflorescence consisting of several 4–8 cm spikes; Spathes whitish, long-lanceolate, 20–40 × 1–5 cm, decrescent toward upper; stamens 10–15(–25) on a column of 1 cm, free part of filament ca. 1 mm; anther linear, 3 mm, conective prolonged into a small point. Female inflorescence terminal, globular; spathes several, milk white, 14–35 × 1–3 cm, margin serrate; carpels 2–12, connate, but free at apex. Syncarps pendent, red, yellow to orange, consisting of 40–80 drupes; drupe obconical, ca. 4 cm, truncate, angular, persistent stigma subsessile, slightly protruded, auriculate, nipple-shaped or hippocrepiform.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 2880; HK sheet 7724.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; tropical Asia to Australia.
Ecology: Sandy beaches or cultivated in gardens. Flowering: May–Aug.; fruiting: Jan.–Oct.
Uses: Ornamental, material (fiber), medicinal (folklore).
Notes: A mutant cultivar ‘Sanderii’ is cultivated in Hong Kong for ornamental use. It is characterized by the leaves with several lengthwise golden-yellow bands from midrib to margin, and with minute spines on the margins.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Pandanus urophyllus Hance 分叉露兜
J. Bot. 13: 68. 1875; FKH 287. 1912; B. C. Stone, Fl. Cambodge, Laos et Vietnam 20: 34. 1983; FOC 23: 130. 2010.
Pandanus furcatus auct. non Roxb.: FRPS 8: 15. 1992; FGD 6: 400. 2005; Check List HK Plants 296. 2002; 105. 2004.

Tree, 7–12 m tall; stem with thick aerial roots, dichotomous branched. Leaves aggregated on top of stem, leathery, loriform, 1–4 m × 3–10 cm, margin densely denticulate-spiniferous, spines incurved, abaxially midrib with upward curved acute spines, apex 3-angulate-flagelliform-caudate. Male inflorescence consisting of several spikes; spikes golden yellow, cylindrical, 10–15 cm, spathes towards 1 m × 10 cm; male flowers many, stamens usually 3–5-clustered on top of filament bundle; anther linear, 5 mm, connective with long and curved awn-like point; female inflorescences a head, to 80 cm, with many spathes; female flowers with 1 carpels, rarely 2 connate; stigma forked, spineform, incurved. Syncarps red-brown, oblongoid to ellipsoidal, 23 × 12 cm, drupes bony, top pyramidal, 1–2-locular, exocarp fleshy, sweet and fragrant, persistent stigma dichotomous, spine-form.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island. W. J. Tutcher 7107, 7222; L. T. Lo 455.
Distribution: Xizang, Yunnan, Guangdong, Guangxi; Sikkim to Indochina.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Aug.
Uses: Cultivated as hedges.
Notes: The type specimen (Hance Herb. No. 18394, BM) was collected by J. Lamont and C. Harland from Hong Kong Island before 1875.

Pandanus utilis Bory 扇葉露兜樹（馬達加斯加露兜）
Voy. Îles Afrique 2: 3 – 5. 1804.

Tree to 15 m tall, trunk smooth with aerial roots, much branched. Leaves spirally arranged in 3 series, crowded towards top of stems, erect, stiff, long-linear, 40–180 × 3–11 cm, uniformly green throughout, grey glaucous abaxially, tapering in a long point at apex, margins and ribs abaxially with many sharp, ascending reddish, 1–4 mm spines. Male inflorescence a branched spadix, 30–80 cm , in axil of a pale spathe; female inflorescence a subglobose head. Male flowers odorous, with 8–12 stamens inserted pseudo-umbellately on slender column of 10–15 mm. Syncarps solitary, pendulous, long-pedunculate, yellow when ripen, subglobose, 15–20 cm in diam., comprising of 100–200 fibrous drupes, each drupe 2.5–3.5 cm, with lower part prism-shaped and upper part convex-pyramidal, 2–8-celled, persistent stigma sessile, reniform.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 743.
Distribution: Widely cultivated in tropical regions, no wild populations are known.
Ecology: Flowering: Jul.
Uses: Ornamental, food (fruit), leaves also used for making baskets and domestic articles.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Mo Shan, Tai Po Kau, Ha Hang, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Acorus gramineus Soland. ex Aiton 金錢蒲
Hort. Kew. 1: 474. 1789; FKH 289. 1912; FRPS 13(2): 8. 1979; FFJ 6: 411. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 665. 2000; FGD 9: 176. 2009.
Acorus calamus auct. non L: FHK 345. 1861.
Acorus tatarinowii Schott, Oster. Bot. Zeitschr. 9: 101. 1859.

Perennial aromatic herb, 15–55 cm tall, with short, creeping rhizomes and many fleshy roots. Leaves distichous, ensiform, (15–)20–45(–55) × 0.3–1.4 cm, apex acuminate, dark green, venation parallel, midrib lacking. Peduncle 9–25 cm, compressed triangular. Spathe green, leaf-like, ± equaling the peduncle. Spadix narrowly cylindrical to subcylindrical, nearly erect, 3–14 cm, 3–14 cm, densely flowered, yellow; tepals 6, in 2 whorls, ± oblong, 1.5–2 × 0.7–1 mm, membranous, apex rounded or acute; anthers yellow, 0.4–0.5 mm in diam. Infructescence yellowish at maturity. Berry obovoid-globose, several-seeded. Seed ellipsoidal, 2–3 × 0.8–1.2 mm, hairy at base.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Tai Po Kau, Ha Hang, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 1728; Y. W. Lam 642; HK sheet 35813.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Xinjiang, Qinghai, Ningxia, Gansu, Shanxi, Sichuan, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Shandong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Russia (Far East), Korea, Japan, Philippines, SE Asia.
Ecology: Wet places and rocks near water. Flowering: Feb.–Jul.; fruiting: Jul.–Aug.
Uses. Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.

Aglaonema modestum Schott ex Engl. 廣東萬年青
Monogr. Phan. 2: 442. 1897; FHN 4: 134, fig. 1039. 1977; FRPS 13(2): 43. 1979; FYN 2: 760. 1979; FFJ 6: 418, fig. 378. 1995; FGD 9: 187, fig. 103. 2009; FOC 23: 23. 2010.

Perennial evergreen herb. Stems erect, green and smooth, 40–70 cm tall; internodes 1–2 cm. Leaves mostly crowded towards stemapex; petiole 5–20 cm, green, the lower half sheathed and clasping stem at base; leaf blade ovate to ovate-lanceolate, 15–25 × 6–13 cm, base broadly cuneate, apex caudate-acuminate, margin entire, dark green above, paler beneath; lateral veins 4–5 pairs. Peduncle slender, 5–10 cm. Spathe yellow-green, oblong-lanceolate, 5.5–7 × 1.5 cm, apex long-acuminate. Spadix cylindrical, about 2/3 the length of spathe; female portion 5–7.5 mm; male portion elongate, 2–3 cm. Flowers unisexual, without scales or perianth. Berries oblong-ovoid, ca. 2 cm, orange-red when mature, oblong.

Locality: Commonly cultivated in Hong Kong. HK sheet 28245, 29749.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; Vietnam, Philippines.
Ecology: Flowering: May; fruiting: Oct.–Nov.
Uses: Ornamental.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Happy Valley, Victoria Peak, Sha Tin, Tai Mong Tsai, Sai Keng, Nam Chung, Luk Keng
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Alocasia cucullata (Lour.) Schott 尖尾芋
Melet. Bot. 18. 1832; FKH 289. 1912; FRPS 13(2): 75, pl. 14: 1. 1979; FTW ed. 2, 5: 667. 2000; FGD 9: 202. 2009.
Arum cucullatum Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 2: 536. 1790.
Alocasia cucullata (Lour.) G. Don, Hort. Brit. ed. 3, 631. 1839; FFJ 6: 434. 1995; FOC 23: 78. 2010; Check List HK Plants 105. 2004.

Herb evergreen, caulescent stock erect, 3–6 cm thick, branched, stoloniferous. Leaves peltate; petiole green, 25–80 cm, sheathed below medium; blade broadly ovate to ovate-cordate, 10–16 (–40) × 7–18(–28) cm, base shallowly cordate, apex acute, margin entire; lateral veins 4–8 on each side, the lowest one basal. Inflorescences usually solitary, axillary. Peduncle terete, 20–30 cm. Spathe green, tube oblong-ovoid, 4–8 cm; limb cymbiform, 5–15 cm, margin convolute. Spadix shorter than spathe, ca. 10 cm; female portion cylindrical, 1.5–2.5 cm; sterile male portion 2–3 cm; fertile male portion subfusiform, 3.5 cm; appendage pale green, yellowish green, narrowly conical, ca. 3.5 cm. Berry subglobose, 6–8 mm in diam., 1-seeded.

Locality: Happy Valley, Victoria Peak, Sha Tin, Tai Mong Tsai, Sai Keng, Nam Chung, Luk Keng. HK sheet 33004, 33063.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Sichuan, Guizhou, Yunnan, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, India, Sri Lanka, Myanmar, Thailand.
Ecology: Forests, streamsides, wet places. Flowering: May.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Alocasia macrorrhizos (L.) G. Don 海芋
Hort. Brit. ed. 3, 631. 1839; FFJ 6: 435, fig. 394. 1995.
Arum macrorrhizum L., Sp. Pl. ed. 1: 965. 1753.
Arum indicum Lour., Fl. Cochich. 2: 536. 1790.
Caladium odorum Lindl., Bot. Reg. 8: t. 641. 1822.
Colocasia odora (Lindl.) Bornyn., Nouv. Ann. Mus. Hist. Nat. 3: 145, t. 7. 1834; FHK 343. 1861.
Alocasia odora (Roxb.) K. Koch, Index Seminum Hort. Berol. 1854(App.): 5. 1854; FOC 23: 77. 2010; Check List HK Plants 105. 2004.
Colocasia indica (Lour.) Kunth., Enum. Pl. 3: 39. 1841; FHK 343. 1861.
Alocasia macrorrhiza (L.) Schott, Osterr. Bot. Wochenbl. 4: 409. 1854; FKH 289. 1912; FRPS 13(2): 76. 1979; FGD 9: 203, fig. 117. 2009; Check List HK Plants 298. 2002, nom. illeg. prior.

Large evergreen perennial herb, to 2(–3) m tall; caulescent stock stout, to 15 cm thick, unbranched. Leaves spirally arranged, crowded toward apex of the stock, ± peltate; petiole green, 0.5–2(–3) m, sheathing at base; leaf blade broadly ovate, 50–100 × 40–100 cm, base sagittate, apex acute, margin entire; lateral veins 9–12 pairs. Peduncle 2–3 together, terete, green, 12–60 cm. Spathe tube inrolled, green, narrowly ellipsoidal, 5–9 cm, convolute and constricted at apex; limb yellowish green or pale green, lanceolate and concave, 10–20 × 4–5 cm. Spadix rather short: female portion green, 2–4 cm; sterile male portion white or pale green, 2.5–6 cm; fertile male portion 3–7 cm; appendage yellowish, conical, 3–5.5 cm. Berries ovoid, 8–10 mm, red when mature, 1–2-seeded.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. HK sheet 7732, 29735.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian; Bangaladesh, India, Malay Peninsula, Indochina, Philippines, Indonesia.
Ecology: Forests and shaded places. Flowering: All year round in tropics.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.
Notes: Some authors consider Alocasia odora a distinct species which differs from A. macrorrhizos in having shortly peltate leaves, whereas leaves of A. macrorrhizos are deeply cordate at the base with the lateral costae partially naked in the sinus.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Mount Parker, Ng Tung Chai, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Amorphophallus dunnii Tutcher 南蛇棒（鄧氏蒟蒻）
Journ. Bot. 49: 273. 1911; FKH 288. 1912; FHN 4: 138, fig. 1044. 1977; FRPS 13(2): 92, pl. 16: 5 – 9. 1979; FYN 2: 790. 1979; W. Hett. & Vander Ham, Blumea 46: 281. 2001; FGD 9: 196. 2009; FOC 23: 26. 2010.
Amorphophallus odoratus W. Hett. & H. Li, Blumea 39: 265. 1994.

Perennial herb; tuber subglobose or depressed-globose. Leaf solitary; petiole 30–90 cm, 1 cm in diam., with many, elongate, confluent, pale green or brownish green spots; leaf blade green, dissected; leaflets lanceolate or oblanceolate, 7–14 × 8 cm, base cuneate, apex abruptly acuminate. Inflorescence solitary. Inflorescence solitary; peduncle 20–60 cm; spathe broadly ovate to elliptic, 12–26 × 14 cm, strongly concave, top acute, overarching the spadix, base shortly convolute, externally bright pale green, basally with rounded white spots; spadix slightly shorter than spathe, stipitate or subsessile, 8–20 cm; female portion cylindrical, yellowish, 1.5–3 cm, base narrow; male portion 1.5–4.5 cm, appendage conical, ovate, greenish white, 4.5–14 cm, narrowing above middle, apex obtuse. Ovary obovate, 1–2.5 mm. Berries blue, cylindrical; seed solitary, black.

Locality: Mount Parker, Ng Tung Chai, Lantau Island. HK sheet 7729, 29714.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Yunnan.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Mar.–Apr.; fruiting: Jul.–Aug.
Notes: The type specimens were collected by S. T. Dunn and W. J. Tutcher from Lantau Island and Mount Parker in between 1909 and 1911 respectively. The type specimen of A. odoratus was collected by Simmons from Tai Mo Shan in 1994.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Victoria Peak, Shing Mun, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Amorphophallus kiusianus (Makino) Makino 東亞魔芋
Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 27: 244. 1913; Hett. & Peng, Bot. Acad. Sin. 36. 105, f. 4. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 671. 2000; FGD 9: 195. 2009; FOC 23: 29. 2010.
Amorphophallus konjac K. Koch ex Matsum. & Hayata var. kiusiana Makino, Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 25: 16. 1911.
Amorphophallus variabilis auct. non Blume: FHK. 343. 1861; FKH 288. 1912; FRPS 13(2): 95. 1979; Check List HK Plants 298. 2002; 105. 2004.

Perennial herb; tuber depressed-globose. Leaves trisected, lobes lanceolate or oblong-elliptic, 6–20 × 3–4.5 cm; petiole glabrous, 80 cm, with grey or pale green spots. Peduncle 120 cm; spathe triangular, 9–25 × 4–13 cm, base and blade constricted, blade margins inrolled or wavy, pink-green or purple-brown externally, with small white spots; spadix sessile or subsessile, 9–22 cm, female portion conical, 1–4 cm, male portion cylindrical or slightly obconical, 2.5–4.5 cm, appendage fusiform-conical or long cylindrical, 4–16 cm, abruptly acute or obtuse. Ovary obovoid. Berries rounded or ovoid.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Shing Mun, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island. HK sheet 29717, 29718.
Distribution: Guangdong, Jiangxi, Fujian; Japan.
Ecology: Thin forests. Flowering: Jul.

Arisaema cordatum N. E. Br. 心檐南星
J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 36: 177. 1903; FKH 288. 1912; FRPS 13(2): 163, pl. 31: 4 – 5. 1979; FGD 9: 206. 2009; FOC 23: 61. 2010.
Arisaema brevistipitatum Merr., Lingnan Sci. J. 13(1): 19. 1934.

Perennial slender herb; tuberous rhizome globose, 1–1.5 cm in diam. Leaves solitary, bipinnatifid-pedate; petiole slender, 10–30 cm; leaflets (5–)7, sessile, oblong, 7–10 × 1.5–3 cm, broadly cuneate at base, apex acute to abruptly acuminate. Peduncle slender, 2–4.5 cm. Spathe violet when dried, tube funnelform, 3–3.5 cm, throat margins broadly auriculate; limb triangular-ovate, apex acuminate. Spadix unisexual: male portion shortly stipitate, synandria composed of 2 anthers, anthers globose, dehiscing by apical pores; appendage 15–27 cm, lower portion fusiform, exceeding from throat then narrowed into filiform and hanging.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Sunset Peak. HK sheet 33108, 35025.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi.
Ecology: Forest and thickets. Flowering: Apr.
Notes: The holotype specimen (A. B. Westland 92, K) was collected by A. B. Westland from Tai Mo Shan in 1887.

Arisaema erubescens (Wall.) Schott 一把傘南星
Melet. Bot. 17. 1832; FRPS 13(2): 189, pl. 37: 1 – 8. 1979; FYN 2: 830, fig. 220: 1–8. 1979; FFJ 6: 425, fig. 386. 1995; FGD 9: 207. 2009; FOC 23: 67. 2010.
Arum erubescens Wall., Pl. Asia. Rar. 2: 30, t. 135. 1831.
Arisaema consanguineum Schott, Bonplandia (Hanover) 7: 27. 1859; FKH 288. 1912; FTW ed. 2, 5: 673. 2000.

Perennial herb; tuberous rhizome depressed globose. Leaf 1–2, radiately 9–15(–20)-foliolate; petiole, 40–80(–120) cm, basal 1/3–1/2 sheathing; leaflets lanceolate, oblong-lanceolate to elliptic, usually 1 upward, the others radiately spreading. Peduncle shorter than petiole, erect. Spathe green to dark purple, with stripes or not, slightly recurved at mouth; tube cylindrical, 4–8 cm, auriculate at mouth limb oblong-ovate, acuminate with a filiform tail to 12–14 cm. Plants dioecious: male spadix 2–2.5cm, flowers dense; female spadix ca. 2 cm; appendage clavate, erect, 2–4.5 cm. Berries red when mature, 1–2-seeded.

Locality: Sunset Peak, Lantau Peak. HK sheet 29667, 33667.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China (except Nei Mongol, Heilongjiang, Jilin, Liaoning, Xinjiang); India, Nepal, Sikkim, Myanmar, Thailand.
Ecology: Forests and thickets. Flowering: May – Jul.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Arisaema heterophyllum Blume 異葉天南星
Rumphia 1: 110. 1835; FRPS 13(2): 157, pl. 30: 1–3. 1979; FYN 2: 822, fig. 218: 1 – 3. 1979; FFJ 6: 428, fig. 389. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 675. 2000; FGD 9: 205, fig. 118. 2009; FOC 23: 60. 2010.
Arisaema kwangtungensis Merr., Philipp. J. Sci. 15(3): 228 – 229. 1919[1920].

Perennial herb; tuberous rhizome depressed globose, 2–4 cm in diam. Leaf usually 1–2, pedately compound; petiole glaucous, 30–60 cm, basal 3/4 sheathing; leaflets 11–19(–21), oblanceolate, oblong or linear-oblong, cuneate at base, apex acuminate; terminal one shorter than the others. Peduncle usually longer than petiole. Spathe tube cylindrical, 3–8 cm, glaucous externally, whitish green internally, throat slightly recurved; limb ovate to ovatelanceolate, 5–11 × 3–5 cm, apex acuminate, dark green to pale green. Bisexual spadix: female portion 1–2.2 cm, at the base; male portion 1.5–3.2 cm, higher up, ending in appendage. Unisexual spadix: male portion 3–5 cm; appendage elongate, filiform. Ovaries globose, style distinct, stigma punctate, ovules 3–4. Synandria stalked, anthers 2–3, dehiscing by apical slits. Berries yellowish red or red, cylindrical, usually with a single clavate seed.

Locality: Sunset Peak. HK sheet 32931, 34879.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China except NW region and Xizang; Japan, Korea.
Ecology: Forests and thickets. Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: Jul.–Sep.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Victoria Peak, Ma On Shan, Castle Peak
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Arisaema penicillatum N. E. Br. 畫筆南星
J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 18: 248, t. 5. 1880; FKH 288. 1912; FHN 4: 140. 1977; FRPS 13(2): 123, pl. 23: 11 – 13. 1979; FYN 2: 804, fig. 216: 11 – 13. 1979; FGD 9: 204. 2009; FOC 23: 48. 2010.
Arisaema laminatum auct. non Blume: FHK 342. 1861.

Perennial herb; tuberous rhizome subglobose. Leaves 2; petioles 25–30 cm, basal 1/2 sheathing; leaf blade 3-partite; lobes ovatelanceolate to oblong-lanceolate, 8–14 cm, oblique at the base, apex acuminate and aristate, the central one petiolulate, lateral ones almost sessile. Peduncle usually shorter than petiole; spathe tube pale green, 4 cm, convolute; limb pale green to white, broadly ovate and ending in a fine and long (12–25 mm) point. Spadix unisexual or bisexual: female portion pyramidal, green, ca. 1 cm; male portion long conical, sparsely bearing male flowers; appendage filiform, 3–5 cm, covered with filiform or subulate neuter flowers at apex. Synandria of 3 stamens; anthers ovate, opening by longitudinal apical slits. Ovaries ovoid, apex constructed into a short style, stigma capitate.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Ma On Shan, Castle Peak. HK sheet 7727, 34081.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Jun.
Notes: The syntype specimens were collected by Harland, Hance, Urquhart, Lamont and C. Ford between 1840s and 1880. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Colocasia esculenta (L.) Schott 芋
Melet. Bot. 18. 1832; FYN 2: 778. 1979; FFJ 6: 432, fig. 393. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 678. 2000; FGD 9: 201, fig. 116. 2009; FOC 23: 74. 2010.
Arum esculentum L., Sp. Pl. 2: 965. 1753.
Colocasia antiquorum Schott, Melet. Bot. 18. 1832; FKH 288. 1912.

Perennial herb; tuber ovoid to ellipsoidal. Leaves 2–3 or more, peltate; petiole 20–90 cm, green or purplish, sheathing at base; leaf blade ovate to oblong-ovate in outline, 20–50 × 10–35 cm, base deeply cordate, apex acute or shortly acuminate; lateral veins 4 pairs. Peduncle usually solitary, shorter than petiole. Spathe various in length, usually 20 cm, tube green, ovoid, ca. 4 cm; limb pale yellow to greenish, lanceolate or elliptic, acuminate, ca. 17 cm, margins inrolled; spadix ca. 10 cm, female portion conical, 3–3.5 cm, at the base; sterile portion slender, cylindrical, 3–3.3 cm; male portion cylindrical, 4–4.5 cm; appendage subulate ca. 1 cm.

Locality: Cultivated or wild. HK sheet 32847, 36157.
Distribution: Areas S of Changjiang River; widely cultivated in the tropics. E
cology: Flowering: Aug.–Sep.
Uses: Food.

Epipremnum pinnatum (L.) Engl. 麒麟葉
Pflanzenr. 37(4, 23B): 60. 1908; FGZ 694. 1956; FRPS 13(2): 28, pl. 4: 1 – 7. 1979; FYN 2: 749, fig. 203: 1 – 7. 1979; FFJ 6: 414, fig. 375. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 681, pl. 293, photo 72. 2000; FGD 9: 183, fig. 100. 2009; FOC 23: 15. 2010.
Pothos pinnata L., Sp. Pl. ed. 2: 1374. 1763.
Epipremnum mirabile Schott, Gen. Aroid. t. 79. 1858; FKH 289. 1912.
Rhaphidophora pinnata Schott, Bonplandia 5: 45. 1857; FHN 4: 133, fig. 1037. 1977.

Robust liana; stem terete, 2.5–4 cm thick at base, adhering to trees or rocks by means of aerial roots. Leaves large; petiole 25–40 cm, articulate at apex. Leaf blade of juvenile plants lanceolate to lanceolate-oblong, base shallowly cordate, that of adult plants oblong to broadly oblong, 40–60 × 30 – 40 cm, base broadly subcordate, apex acute, regularly pinnatifid and often small perforations along both sides of midrib; lateral lobes 12–13 on each side, narrowly lanceolate to somewhat falcate. Peduncle terete, 10–14 cm; spathe 10–12 cm, apex acuminate; spadix cylindrical, ca. 10 cm, sessile; ovary hexagonal, apex truncate. Berries ellipsoidal, several-seeded.

Locality: New Territories. W. J. Tutcher 9122.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Malay Peninsula, Philippines, Pacific islands.
Ecology: Forests, climbing on trees and rocks. Flowering: Apr.–May.
Uses: Ornamental.

Lasia spinosa (L.) Thwaites 刺芋
Enum. Pl. Zeyl., 336. 1864; FGZ 687. 1956; FHN 4: 129, fig. 1033. 1977; FRPS 13(2): 14. 1979; FYN 2: 740. 1979; FFJ 6: 413, fig. 374. 1995; FGD 9: 179, fig. 95. 2009; FOC 23: 16. 2010.
Dracontium spinosum L., Sp. Pl. 2: 967. 1753.
Lasia heterophylla (Roxb.) Schott, Melet. Bot. 1: 21. 1832; FKH 289. 1912.
Pothos heterophylla Roxb., Fl. Ind. ed. 1820, 1: 457. 1820.

Perennial herb, 1 – 2 m tall; stem ascending or creeping, prickly. Leaves of juvenile plants sagittate-hastate on 6–10 × 9–10 cm, that of adult plants deeply pedate-lobed, 15–45 × 15–20 cm, abaxial surface sparsely covered with curved prickles on veins, basal lobes oblong-lanceolate, central lobe larger, ovate-lanceolate; petiole 20–60 cm, longer than blade, prickly, sheathed at base. Peduncle, 20–35 cm, prickly; spathe 15–30 cm, dark-red abaxially, upper portion twisted; spadix yellow-green, cylindrical, 3–5 cm; tepals oblong, 1.5–3 mm, apex triangular-hooded, keeled; ovary ovoid. Fruits obovoid, apex truncate, densely warty-aculeate; seed ovoid-cordate, 5–7 mm.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 29773, 33099.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; Sikkim, Bangaladesh, India, Myanmar, Thailand, Indochina, Malaysia.
Ecology: Forests, near water. Flowering: Sep.; fruiting: Feb.
Uses: Food (vegetable), medicinal (folklore).

Pinellia ternata (Thunb.) Breitenb. 半夏
Bot. Zeitg. (Berlin) 37: 687. 1879; FRPS 13(2): 204, pl. 40: 1–7. 1979; FYN 2: 837. 1979; FFJ 6: 430, fig. 391. 1995; FTW ed 2, 5: 682, pl. 294. 2000; FGD 9: 200, fig. 115. 2009; FOC 23: 42. 2010.
Arum ternatum Thunb., Fl. Jap. 233. 1784.
Pinellia ternata (Thunb.) Makino f. angustata (Schott) Makino, Check List HK Plants 300. 2002; 106. 2004.
Pinellia tuberifera Tenore, Atti Accad. Sci. Fis. Mat. Napoli 4: 57. 1839; FKH 288. 1912.

Perennial herb, tuber globose, 1–2 cm in diam. Leaves (1–)2–3(–5); petiole 15–20 cm, base sheathing; leaf blade of seedlings usually simple, ovate-cordate to hastate, that of adult plants trifoliolate; leaflets oblong-elliptic or lanceolate, base cuneate, apex acuminate, terminal one 3–10(–20) × 1–3(–5) cm; lateral ones smaller; lateral veins 8–10 pairs. Peduncle longer than petiole, 25–35 cm; spathe greenish or whitish green, tube narrowly cylindrical, 1.3–2 cm; limb oblong, green or usually purplish at margin, 4–5 cm, apex obtuse or acute; spadix: female portion 1.3–2 cm, sterile portion 3 mm, male portion 5–7 mm, appendage linear, green to purplish, 6–12 cm, erect or sigmoid. Berries ovoid, yellowish green.

Locality: Mount Violet. HK sheet 34816.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China except Nei Mongol, Xinjiang, Xizang, Qinghai; Korea, Japan.
Ecology: Grasslands, farmlands and thin forests. Flowering: May–Jul.; fruiting: Aug.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The species was reported as Pinellia ternata (Thunb.) Makino previously (Check List HK Plants 300. 2002; 106. 2004).

Pinellia tripartita (Blume) Schott 三裂葉半夏
Syn. Aroid. 5. 1856; FOC 23: 41. 2010.
Atherurus tripartitus Blume, Rumphia 1: 137. 1835.

Perennial herb, tuber subglobose, ca. 2.5 cm in diam. Leaves 2–5; petiole green, 30–35 cm; leaf blade green, 3-partite; leaflets broadly ovate to ovate-oblong; anterior leaflet ca. 15 × 4–7 cm, apex ca. 1.5 cm; lateral leaflets smaller; primary lateral veins 8–12 per side on each leaflet, forming a distinct marginal collective vein, also with 2 thinner collective veins along margin. Inflorescence solitary; peduncle to 25 cm, shorter than petioles, slender. Spathe whitish to light green, slightly constricted, 7–9(–10) cm; tube oblong to subcylindrical, ca. 3.5 × 1–1.25 cm; limb boat-shaped, oblong, ca. 4 × 2.5 cm. Spadix 20–25 cm; female portion ca. 3 cm, adnate to spathe; female flowers densely arranged; pistil 1–1.2 mm; ovary ovoid, 0.9–1 mm; style distinct, 0.2–0.3 mm, attenuate; stigma subhemispheric; sterile portion between female and male portion 0.6–0.7 cm; male portion 1.8–2 cm; thecae elongate, opening by a slit; appendage long exserted from spathe, sigmoid, 15–20 cm, base ca. 3 mm in diam., smooth. Berries 1-seeded, pale green to whitish, ovoid.

Locality: Hong Kong Island. C. Wright 508 (P).
Distribution: Japan.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: May–Jul.
Notes: The species can be easily distinguished from P. ternata by petioles lacking bulbils.

Pistia stratiotes L. 大薸
Sp. Pl. 2: 963. 1753; FKH 288. 1912; FGZ 687, fig. 362. 1956; FHN 4: 141, fig. 1047. 1977; FRPS 13(2): 83, pl. 12: 6–9. 1979; FYN 2: 784, fig. 209: 6–9. 1979; FFJ 6: 421, fig. 382. 1995; FTW ed 2, 5: 682, pl. 295, photo 73. 2000; FGD 9: 193, fig. 111. 2009; FOC 23: 79. 2010.

Aquatic herb, with many feathery roots, floating on stagnant water. Leaves in rosulate clusters on a very short stem; petioles almost absent; leaf blade broadly cuneate to obovate-cuneate, 1.3–10 × 1.5–6 cm, truncate or emarginate at apex, entire or undulate, pubescent on both surfaces, especially near the base. Characters of inflorescence and flowers as the description of the genus.

Locality: Sha Tin, Sai Kung. HK sheet 7726, 30264.
Distribution: Hainan, Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Anhui, Shandong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; widely distributed in tropical and subtropical regions.
Ecology: Ponds and ditches. Flowering: May–Nov.
Uses: Animal food.

Pothos chinensis (Raf.) Merr. 石柑
J. Arnold Arb. 19: 210. 1948; FHN 4: 130. 1977; FRPS 13(2): 19, pl. 3: 10. 1979; FYN 2: 742, fig. 202: 8. 1979; FTW, ed. 2, 5: 685, photo 74. 2000; FGD 9: 179, fig. 96. 2009; FOC 23: 7. 2010.
Tapanava chinensis Raf., Fl. Tellur. 4: 14. 1838.
Pothos seemannii Schott, Bonplandia 5: 44. 1857; Aroid. 22, t. 43. 1858; Prodr. Aroid. 564. 1860; FKH 289. 1912.
Pothos scandens auct. non L.: FHK 344. 1861.

Epiphytic liana; stems adhering to rocks or trees by means of aerial roots. Leaves alternate, subleathery; petiole dilated, obovateoblong or cuneate, 1–4 cm; leaf blade ovate-elliptic to oblonglanceolate, 6–13 × 1.5–5.6 cm, base obtuse, apex acuminate or long acuminate. Peduncle 8 – 20 mm, with 3 – 4 concave ovate bracts; spathe green, ovate, 8 × 10–15 mm, apex acute; spadix globular or slightly ovoid, yellow green, yellowish, 7–11 mm in diam. Berries ovoid to ellipsoidal, red when mature.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. N. H. Li 12; K. Y. Tam 150; HK sheet 40008.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Taiwan; Vietnam, Laos, Thailand.
Ecology: Trees and rocks in forests. Flowering & fruiting: All year round.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.
Notes: The type specimen of P. seemannii was collected by Seemann from Hong Kong Island in 1850s.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai, Ma On Shan, Bride's Pool, Castle Peak, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Rhaphidophora hongkongensis Schott 獅子尾（崖角藤）
Bonplandia. 5: 45. 1857; FHN 4: 133, fig. 1038. 1977; FRPS 13(2): 36, pl. 6: 3–4. 1979; FYN 2: 754, fig. 204: 3–4. 1979; FFJ 6: 415, fig. 376. 1995; FTW ed 2, 5: 687, pl. 296. 2000; FGD 9: 185, fig. 101. 2009; FOC 23: 12. 2010.
Rhaphidophora peepla auct. non Schott: FHK 344. 1861.
Rhaphidophora angustifolia auct. non Schott: FKH 284. 1912.

Epiphytic liana. Stems rooting and attaching themselves to trees or rocks. Leaves papery to subleathery, distichous; petioles 5–10 cm, sulcate adaxially. Leaf blade falcate-elliptic to oblonglanceolate or oblanceolate, (10–)20–35 × 5–6(–14) cm, lateral veins many, diverging at an angle about 45˚ from the midrib. Peduncle inserted in long sheathing bracts, cylindrical, 4–5 cm; spathe green to pale yellow, ovate, 6–9 cm, apex acuminate, deciducous; spadix cylindrical, 5–8 cm; ovary hexagonalcylindrical, apex truncate. Berries yellowish green.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai, Ma On Shan, Bride's Pool, Castle Peak, Lantau Island. HK sheet 27434, 31061.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Fujian; Myanmar, Laos, Vietnam, Thailand, Kalimantan.
Ecology: Climbing on trees and rocks in forests. Flowering: Apr.–Aug.; fruiting: the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The type specimen (J. G. Champion 525, K) was collected from Hong Kong Island between 1847 and 1850.

Typhonium blumei Nicolson & Sivad. 犁頭尖（山半夏）
Blumea 27: 494, fig. 4. 1981; A. Hay, Blumea 37: 373, fig. 17. 1993; FGD 9: 198, fig. 113. 2009; FOC 23: 34. 2010.
Typhonium divaricatum auct. non (L.) Decne: Nouv. Ann. Mus. Paris 31: 367. 1834; FKH 288. 1912; FRPS 13(2): 111. 1979. Arum divaricatum auct. non L.: FHK 342. 1861.

Perennial herb; tuber subglobose, 1–2 cm in diam. Leaves 4–8; petiole green, 20–40 cm, basal; leaf blade cordate-hastate, ovate or deltoid in outline, 5–10 × 3–9 cm, apex acuminate, the 2 basal lobes ovate-lanceolate or oblong, divaricate; lateral veins 3–5 pairs. Peduncle emerging from petiole sheath, pale green. Spathe tubular and green at the base for 14–20 mm, upper part expanded into a deep purple ovate limb, ca. 5 cm broad, and tapering into a long and slender apex. Spadix subequaling spathe, deep purple; female portion at the base, 0.4–0.6 cm, with several rows of female flowers, then followed with several rows of subulate neutral flowers; male portion 0.6–0.8 cm, orange; appendage purple, 10–13 cm, emerging very bad excrement smell, long cylindrical. Berries obovoid, few-seeded.

Locality: Magazine Gap, Pok Fu Lam. HK sheet 30636, 31436.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Sichuan, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Philippines.
Ecology: Grassy slopes, roadsides. Flowering: May–Jul.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Lemna minor L. 浮萍
Sp. Pl. 2: 970. 1753; FKH 290. 1912; FRPS 13(2): 210, pl. 42: 3. 1979; FGD 4: 410, fig. 249: 4–6. 2000; FOC 23: 82. 2010.

Small aquatic herb, free floating on water surface. Frond flat, suborbicular, obovate to obovate-elliptic, 2–6 × 2–3 mm, 1–many cohering in small groups, green and shining, sometimes reddish adaxially, scarcely reddish abaxially, margins entire, with a pouch on one side; veins 3(–5), reaching nearly apex. Root usually 2–4 cm, mostly with a rounded tip. Flowers minute, petalless; stamens 2; ovary 1-locular, with 1 ovule. Fruit winged laterally towards top; seed with 10–16 distinct ribs.

Locality: New Territories. HK sheet 29837.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; tropical to temperate regions.
Ecology: Ponds, paddy fields and ditches.
Uses: Animal food.

Spirodela polyrhiza (L.) Schleid. 紫萍
Linnaea 13: 392. 1839; FRPS 13(2): 207, pl. 42: 1. 1979; FGD 4: 409, fig. 249: 1 – 3. 2000; FOC 23: 80. 2010.
Lemna polyrhiza L., Sp. Pl. 970. 1753; FKH 290. 1912.

Small free floating herb, often forming a complete green carpet on water. Fronds flat or rarely gibbous, obovate to circular, 3 – 8( – 10) × 4 – 6 mm, each with 5 – 21 roots, adaxial surface green, sometimes with indistinct papillae along veins, abaxial surface usually purplish, or sometimes green, palmately 5 – 11-veined. Daughter fronds connected to mother frond by thin white stipe. Flowers minute, male and female separate but within same spathe. Fruit laterally winged towards top.

Locality: New Territories. Y. W. Lam 1339, 1751.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; tropical and temperate regions.
Ecology: Ponds, paddy fields and ditches.
Uses: Animal food, medicinal (folklore).

Wolffia globosa (Roxb.) Hartog & Plas 無根萍
Blumea 18(2): 367. 1970; FOC 23: 86. 2010.
Lemna globosa Roxb., Fl. Ind. 3: 565. 1832.
Wolffia arrhiza auct. non (L.) Horkel ex Wimm., Fl. Schles. 140. 1857; Hodgkiss, H. K. Freshwater Plants 82. 1978; FRPS 13(2): 211, pl. 42: 4. 1979; FGD 4: 411, fig. 249: 7–8. 2000; FTW ed. 2, 5: 696. 2000; Check List HK Plants 302. 2002; 106. 2004.

Minute thalloid herb, rootless, free floating on or just below water surface. Fronds ovoid to hemispherical, 0.5–1.5 mm, in diam., rounded or slightly pointed at apex, adaxial surface green, with stomata in parallel rows, abaxial surface transparent green, conspicuously convex, epidermal cells pentagonal or hexagonal. Plants rarely flowering.

Locality: New Territories (fide Hodgkiss 1978).
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; tropical to temperate regions.
Ecology: Ponds and ditches.
Uses: Forage.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Kowloon Peak, Shing Mun, Tai Lam Chung
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Xyris bancana Miq. 中國黃眼草
Fl. Ned. Ind., Eerste Bijv. 608. 1861; FKH 282. 1912, excl. syn. X. schoenoides; van Royen, Fl. Males., ser. 1, 4: 369. 1953; Hansen, Fl. Camb., Laos, Vietnam 20: 156. 1983; FOC 24: 5. 2000; FGD 6: 333. 2005.
Xyris chinensis Malme, Svensk Bot. Tidskr. 21: 386. 1927; FRPS 13(3): 17. 1997.
Xyris schoenoides auct. non Mart.: FHK 379. 1861.

Tufted herb, 30–50 cm tall. Leaf blade narrowly ensiform-linear, 8–12(–20) cm × 1.5–2 mm, apex acute, smooth or minutely and transversely rugulose; sheath 2–4 cm. Peduncle 15–40(–50) cm, slender, subterete, smooth, basally subtended by a sheath. Head ellipsoidal, 5–12 × 5–8 mm. Basal bracts oblong-ovate, ca. 4 mm, indistinctly keeled, apex rounded and usually emarginate; median bracts obovate, ca. 5 × 3.5 mm, conchiform, not keeled, apex rounded and ± erose, with a papillate triangle in the upper half. Lateral sepals free, subequilateral, linear to narrowly obovate, curved, 4.5–5 mm, less than 1 mm wide, margin ± erose, keel narrow and entire at base and apex but central portion slightly wider and denticulate.

Locality: Kowloon Peak, Shing Mun, Tai Lam Chung. L. Gibbs 7768; Y. S. Lau 3088; HK sheet 7651.
Distribution: Guangdong; Indochina, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia, New Guinea.
Ecology: Swamps and other wet places. Flowering: Aug.–Sep.
Notes: The species was reported as Xyris capensis Thunb. var. schoenoides (Mart.) Nilsson previously (Check List HK Plants 302. 2002; 106. 2004).

Xyris indica L. 黃眼草
Sp. Pl. 1: 42. 1753; FKH 282. 1912; van Royen, Fl. Males., ser. 1, 4: 373. 1953; Hansen, Fl. Camb., Laos, Vietnam 20: 157. 1983; FRPS 13(3): 13, pl. 4: 1 – 5. 1997; FOC 24: 4. 2000; FGD 6: 332, fig. 189. 2005.

Perennial, robust herb, 25–70 cm tall. Leaves linear-ensiform, 20–50(–70) cm × (2.5–)3–6(–8) mm, apex acute to obtuse, glabrous, veins indistinct when dry, with many short, prominent, transverse ribs connecting longitudinal veins; sheath 7–20(–30) cm. Peduncle (15–)30–80 cm, with prominent furrows. Head ovoid to subglobose, 1–1.5 × 0.8 – 1.5 cm. Median bracts suborbicular, obovate, or conchiform, 5–8 × 5–7 mm, minutely papillate in the upper third, margin gold-coloured, membranous, apex entire or emarginate. Lateral sepals linear-spatulate, 5–7 × 0.8–1.4 mm, crest denticulate, apex obtuse; median sepal cap-shaped, 4–6 × 2–2.5 mm. Petals yellowish to yellow; limb obovate to suborbicular, 3–4.5 × 3–4 mm, margin serrulate; claw 3.5–5 × ca. 0.5 mm. Stamens ca. 4 mm. Staminodia 2–3 mm. Ovary obovoid, 1-locular. Capsule globose to obovoid, 3–4 mm.

Locality: Fanling. W. J. Tutcher 8392.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian; Indochina, Malaysia, Thailand, India, Sri Lanka, Philippines, Australia.
Ecology: Inundated paddy fields, wet places. Flowering: Sep.–Nov.; fruiting: Oct.–Dec.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Lan Nai Wan, Tai Po, Fanling, Sheung Shui, Sai Kung, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Xyris pauciflora Willd. 蔥草
Phytographia. 1: 2. 1794; FHK 379. 1861; FKH 282. 1912; van Royen, Fl. Males., ser. 1, 4: 371. 1953; Hansen, Fl. Camb., Laos, Vietnam 20: 160. 1983; FRPS 13(3): 18, pl. 4: 6 – 9. 1997; FOC 24: 5. 2000; FGD 6: 334, fig. 190. 2005.

Tufted herb, 14–50 cm tall. Leaves linear-lanceolate, striate when dry, 8–22 cm × 1–3 mm, apex acute to acuminate, sparsely papillose on the margin and between the longitudinal veins on both surfaces; sheath 1–5 cm. Peduncle 5–35 cm, subterete. Head globose to ovoid, usually less than 1 cm in diam. Basal bracts elliptic, papillose along apical 1/2 of midvein, apex emarginate to obtuse; median bracts suborbicular to broadly obovate, 3–5 × 3–4 mm, with a papillate triangular patch in the upper third, margin membranous, mucronate at the top. Lateral sepals boat-shaped, 3.5–4.5 × ca. 1.5 mm, membranous, keel narrow, coarsely serrulate, apex subacute; median sepal cap-shaped, ca. 3.5 mm. Petals yellow; limb obovate, 2.5–3.5 mm; claw 3–4 mm. Stamens 0.9–1.3 mm. Staminodes 2-brachiate, shorter than stamens. Ovary obovoid. Style 1.2–2 mm; stigma capitate. Capsule ovoid to ellipsoidal, 4–5 mm.

Locality: Lan Nai Wan, Tai Po, Fanling, Sheung Shui, Sai Kung, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 1438; Y. W. Lam 1263, 1782.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; Indochina, Thailand, Bhutan, Nepal, India, Sri Lanka, Malaysia, Philippines, New Guinea, Australia.
Ecology: Ravines damp sandy soils, swamps. Flowering: Sep.–Nov.; fruiting: Oct.–Dec.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Ng Tung Chai, Kap Lung, Mau Ping
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Amischotolype hispida (Less. & A. Rich.) D. Y. Hong 穿鞘花
Acta Phytotax. Sin. 12: 461. 1974; FHN 4: 80, fig. 997. 1977; FRPS 13(3): 71, pl. 19: 1–3. 1997; FOC 24: 23. 2000; FGD 6: 314, fig. 178. 2005.
Forrestia hispida Less. & A. Rich., Voy. Astrolabe 2: t. 1. 1834.
Forrestia chinensis N. E. Br., J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 36: 158. 1903; FKH 284. 1912.

Perennial herb, up to 1 m tall; stems erect, creeping at the base, glabrous. Leaves borne on the upper part of stem; leaf sheaths to 4 cm, densely brownish yellow hirsute; leaf blade elliptic, 15–50 × 5–10.5 cm, base long-attenuate into a winged petiole, apex acuminate, brownish yellow hirsute near margin on both surfaces and below middle of abaxial major veins. Heads 2–3 cm in diam., with 20 or more flowers. Sepals green, obovate, 5–13 mm, abaxially densely brown hirsute along midvein, rarely subglabrous, elsewhere glabrous or very sparsely hairy. Petals white, lanceolate, 4–10 mm, apex obtuse, glabrous. Stamens 6, ca. 12 mm; filaments bearded. Capsule ovoid-globose, trigonous, ca. 7 mm, much shorter than persistent sepals, sparsely hirsutulous near obtuse apex. Seeds ca. 3 × 2 mm, rugose.

Locality: Ng Tung Chai, Kap Lung, Mau Ping. Y. S. Lau 3023; Y. W. Lam 979.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Indochina, Thailand, Malaysia, Philippines, Indonesia, New Guinea.
Ecology: Streamsides, forests. Flowering: Jul.–Aug.; fruiting: Sep.–Dec.

Commelina auriculata Blume 耳苞鴨跖草
Enum. Pl. Javae 1: 2. 1827; FKH 283. 1912; FFJ 6: 455. 1995; FRPS 13(3): 132. 1997; FOC 24: 38. 2000; FGD 6: 321, fig. 183. 2005.

Perennial herb, stems ascending to 1.4 m, glabrous except sparsely hairy in a line distally. Leaf sheaths 0.6–1.8 cm, hairy, fringed with long hairs at mouth; leaf blade elliptic-lanceolate to lanceolate, 2–4(–8) × 1–2 cm, base ± oblique and narrowed into a short (ca. 3 mm) petiole, apex acuminate, adaxially sparsely scabrid, abaxially sometimes pubescent, or glabrous on both surfaces. Involucral bracts opposite to upper leaves, solitary or 2–3 aggregated at apex of branches, with ca. 5 mm long stalk, funnelform, ca. 1 cm, glabrous or slightly white hispid, proximal margins connate, apex acute. Peduncle simple (one branch reduced), with 2 – 5 small, bisexual flowers. Sepals 3, pale green, lanceolate or obovate, 3–4 mm, apex obtuse, posterior 2 ± connate. Petals 3, blue or with a white one, 2 longer ones ca. 7 mm, the other shorter, ca. 3 mm. Capsule globose, trigonous, ca. 4 mm, 2–3-valved with posterior valve indehiscent. Seeds 1 per valve, grey-brown, ellipsoidal, ca. 3.5 mm, smooth, flat on one surface.

Locality: Yuen Long. Y. W. Lam 748.
Distribution: Guangdong, Fujian, Taiwan; Indonesia, W Oceania.
Ecology: Ravines, shaded and humid places. Flowering: Jun.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Wai, Ting Kau, Yuen Long, Nam Sang Wai
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Commelina benghalensis L. 飯包草
Sp. Pl. 1: 41. 1753; FHK 376. 1861; FKH 284. 1912; FFJ 6: 455, fig. 409. 1995; FRPS 13(3): 128, pl. 31: 3 – 4. 1997; FOC 24: 37. 2000; FGD 6: 321. 2005.

Perennial herb; stems much branched, creeping at the base, ascending distally to 70 cm or more, sparsely pubescent. Leaves petiolate; leaf sheaths 0.5–1.5 cm, sparsely hirsute-ciliate; leaf blade ovate to elliptic-ovate, 3–7 × 1.5–4 cm, base rounded and narrowed into a broad petiole, apex obtuse or acute, subglabrous, ciliate on leaf sheath and petiole. Involucral bracts opposite to the upper leaves, solitary, or 2–3 aggregated at apex of branches, sessile or very shortly stalked, funnelform and ± compressed, 1–1.4 cm, sparsely hairy, margins connate, open at the apex only. Peduncle 2-branched; the proximal branch longer than the bract, with 1 male flowers, the distal branch shorter, with 2–3 included, fertile flowers. Sepals 3, green unequal, lanceolate or obovate, ca. 2 mm, glabrous. Petals 3, blue, ovate, 3–5 mm, posterior 2 ± connate, stalked. Capsule ellipsoidal, 4–6 mm, 3-valved. Seeds black, cylindrical or semi-cylindrical, ca. 2 mm, rugose, irregularly reticulate, truncate at one end.

Locality: Tai Wai, Ting Kau, Yuen Long, Nam Sang Wai. Y. W. Lam 747, 766; HK sheet 39783.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Hebei, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Shandong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; tropical and subtropical Africa and Asia.
Ecology: Lowland wet places. Flowering: Summer to autumn.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Commelina communis L. 鴨跖草
Sp. Pl. 1: 40. 1753; FHK 376. 1861; FKH 284. 1912; FFJ 6: 454, fig. 408. 1995; FRPS 13(3): 127, pl. 29: 6–7. 1997; FOC 24: 36. 2000; FGD 6: 321. 2005.

Annual herb; stems much branched, creeping or ascending to 50 cm or more, rooting at nodes, glabrous or puberulent on the upper portion. Leaves sessile or nearly so; leaf sheaths 0.7–1 cm, glabrous, scarcely ciliate; leaf blade lanceolate to ovate-lanceolate, 2.5–7(–9) × 1–2 cm, base obtuse, apex acuminate, glabrous. Involucral bracts cordate, folded, 1.2–2.5 cm, apex acute, base with 1.5–4 cm long stalk, often hirsute-ciliate. Peduncle 2-branched; one branch ca. 8 mm, with 1–2 male flowers, the other branch shorter, with 3–4 bisexual flowers, nearly included in the bract; pedicels ca. 3 mm at anthesis, curved and less than 6 mm in fruit. Sepals 3, green, membranous, the posterior 2 ovate, ca. 4 × 3 mm. Petals 3, the anterior 2 dark blue, ovate, ca. 9 × 8 mm, the posterior one white, ca. 5 mm. Capsule ellipsoidal, 5–7 mm, 2-valved. Seeds 2 per valve, brown-yellow, irregularly pitted, truncate at one end.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 2763; Y. W. Lam 414; HK sheet 41587.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China except for Qinghai, Xinjiang, and Xizang; Russia (Far East), Korea, Japan, Indochina, Thailand.
Ecology: Shaded and humid places. Flowering: Summer to autumn.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Commelina diffusa Burm. f. 節節草
Fl. Indica 18, pl. 7, fig. 2. 1768; FFJ 6: 453. 1995; FRPS 13(3): 126. 1997; FOC 24: 36. 2000; FGD 6: 320. 2005.
Commelina salicifolia auct. non Roxb.: FHK 376. 1861.
Commelina nudiflora auct. non L.: FKH 284. 1912.

Annual herb; stems creeping at the base, branching and ascending to 40 cm or more. Leaves subsessile; leaf sheath 0.6–3 cm, with red spots when dry, hispidulous throughout or in a line, ciliate on the edge; leaf blade lanceolate or proximal ones oblong, 3–12 × 0.8–3 cm, base obtuse, apex acuminate or acute, margin scabrous. Involucral bracts ovate-lanceolate, folded, 1–4 cm, glabrous or hispidulous abaxially, base cordate or rounded, apex acuminate or shortly so. Peduncle 2 branched; 1 branch 1.5–2 cm, with 1–4 long-exserted male flowers; the other much shorter, with 3–5 included bisexual flowers; pedicels thick and curved, ca. 3 mm, lengthening to 5 mm in fruit. Sepals 3, unequal, the anterior one lanceolate, ca. 3 × 2 mm, the posterior 2 obovate, ca. 5 × 3 mm, ± connate at the base. Petals blue, 2 longer ones broadly ovate, ca. 4.5 × 6 mm, clawed; the third smaller, ovate, ca. 4 × 4 mm, scarcely clawed. Fertile stamens 3; filaments 5–7 mm. Capsule oblong, trigonous, ca. 5 mm, 3-valved. Seeds black, ovoid-globose, ca. 2 mm, reticulate.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 2313; L. T. Lo 525; HK sheet 41520.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Fujian, Taiwan; worldwide in Tropics and Subtropics.
Ecology: Margins of forests, streamsides and other moist places. Flowering & fruiting: May–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Fanling, Tai Po, Tai Mo Shan, Shing Mun, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Commelina paludosa Blume 大苞鴨跖草
Enum. Pl. Javae 1: 2. 1827; FFJ 6: 456, fig. 410. 1995; FRPS 13(3): 129, pl. 31: 1 – 2. 1997; FOC 24: 37. 2000; FGD 6: 322. 2005.
Commelina obliqua Buch.-Ham. ex D. Don, Prodr. Fl. Nepal. 45. 1825; FKH 284. 1912.

Perennial herb; stems often erect from the geniculate base to 1 m, simple or sometimes branched distally, glabrous or sparsely hispidulous. Leaves sessile; leaf sheath 2–3.5 cm, hispid in a line on one side, fringed with long hairs at mouth, sometimes either glabrous with only a few hairs at mouth or hirsute throughout; leaf blade lanceolate to ovate-lanceolate, 6–18 × 2–4.5(–7) cm, base attenuate, apex long acuminate, glabrous on both surfaces or adaxially granular hairy and abaxially hirsute. Involucral bracts often 4–10 aggregated at apex of branches, sessile, funnelform, ca. 2 × 1.5–2 cm, proximal margins connate, apex acute or shortly so, glabrescent. Peduncle unbranched, ca. 1.2 cm, with (1–)3–7 flowers nearly included in involucral bracts; pedicels ca. 7 mm, twisted. Sepals 3, pale green, lanceolate, 3–6 mm. Petals 3, blue or sometimes the posterior one white, obovate to spathulate, 5–8 mm. Fertile stamens 3, unequal; filaments glabrous. Capsule ovoid-globose, trigonous, ca. 4 mm, 3-valved. Seeds 1 per valve, dark brown, ellipsoidal, slightly flattened, finely reticulate.

Locality: Fanling, Tai Po, Tai Mo Shan, Shing Mun, Lantau Island. L. T. Lo 250; K. L. Yip 4089; HK sheet 29280.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, SE Xizang, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; Indochina, Myanmar, Thailand, Bhutan, Nepal, India, Malaysia.
Ecology: Forests, streamsides in ravines. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Ma On Shan, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Cyanotis arachnoidea C. B. Clarke 蛛絲毛藍耳草
Monogr. Phan. 3: 250. 1881; FRSP 13(3): 122, pl. 30: 10. 1997; FOC 24: 22. 2000; FGD 6: 318. 2005.

Perennial herb, with fibrous roots; main stem strongly abbreviated and amply branched; branches diffuse, 20–80 cm. Leaves on the main stem rosulate, linear, 8–20(–30) × 0.5–1.5 cm; leaves on fertile branches much shorter, 5–7 cm, abaxially rather densely arachnoid. Flowers in terminal and axillary heads, sessile or on peduncle to 4 cm; bracts 7–8 mm. Sepals connate at base, linear-lanceolate, ca. 5 mm, abaxially arachnoid. Petals blue-purple, blue, or white, ca. 6 mm. Filaments blue arachnoid. Capsule broadly oblong, trigonous, ca. 2.5 mm, densely hirsutulous at apex. Seeds grey-brown, pitted.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Ma On Shan, Lantau Island. P. S. Choi 254; Y. W. Lam 924.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam, Laos, Myanmar, Thailand, India, Sri Lanka.
Ecology: Ravines, humid rocks. Flowering: Jun.–Sep.; fruiting: Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Cyanotis axillaris (L.) D. Don ex Sweet 鞘苞花
Hort. Brit. 430. 1826; FHK 378. 1861; FKH 284. 1912; FOC 24: 23. 2000.
Commelina axillaris L., Sp. Pl. 1: 42. 1753.
Amischophacelus axillaris (L.) R. S. Rao & Kammathy, J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 59: 379. 1966; FRPS 13(3): 120, pl. 30: 6 – 9. 1997; FGD 6: 323. 2005; Check List HK Plants 302. 2002; 107. 2004.

Annual herb, 30–40 cm tall, with roots fibrous; stems with long creeping branches. Leaves all cauline, linear or linearlanceolate, (2–)5–10 cm × 5–8 mm, abaxially glabrous or sparsely pubescent. Flowers 2–3 together, nearly sessile within the short loose leaf sheath. Sepals linear-spatulate, 6–9 mm, divided nearly to the base, hirsute on abaxial surface. Petals ovate, deep blue, ca. 12 mm. Filaments thickened above a dense tuft of articulate hairs. Capsule oblong, trigonous, 4–5 mm, hispid at apex, with 6 horned projections. Seeds grey-black or grey-brown, pitted.

Locality: Tai Au Mun. Y. S. Lau 2597.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangxi; Indochina, Myanmar, Thailand, India, Sri Lanka, Malaysia, Indonesia, Philippines.
Ecology: Moist sandy lowlands. Flowering: Spring and autumn.

Cyanotis vaga (Lour.) Schultes & J. H. Schultes 藍耳草
Syst. Veg. 7: 1153. 1830; FRPS 13(3): 122, pl. 30: 1 – 2. 1997; FOC 24: 22. 2000; FGD 6: 319. 2005.
Tradescantia vaga Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 1: 193. 1790.
Cyanotis barbata D. Don, Prodr. Fl. Nepal. 45. 1825; FKH 284. 1912.
Cyanotis fasciculata auct. non Roem. & Schult.: FHK 378. 1861.
Cyanotis kewensis auct. non C. B. Clarke: FKH 284. 1912.

Perennial herb, with globose bulbs, ± white woolly or glabrescent; stems ascending, 10–60 cm tall. Leaves all cauline, linear to lanceolate, 5–15 cm × 3–15 mm. Flowers in small clusters, 2–3 together, unequally pedunculate or nearly sessile, terminal or in the upper axils, and each cluster surrounded by 8–10 lanceolate much calcite imbricate bracts; proximal bracts 8–12 mm. Sepals connate at base, oblong-lanceolate, ca. 5 mm, abaxially white hirsute. Petals purple or blue-purple, 6–8 mm. Filaments woolly below the anthers. Capsule obovoid, trigonous, ca. 2.5 mm, hirsutulous at apex. Seeds grey-brown, striate and finely reticulate.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Lantau Island. H. C. Tang 1987; Y. W. Lam 924.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Taiwan; Vietnam, Laos, Myanmar, Thailand, Bhutan, Nepal, India.
Ecology: Thin forests, grassy slopes. Flowering: Jul.–Sep.; fruiting: Oct.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Lam Tsuen, Fanling, Sai Kung, Tai Mong Tsai, Yung Shue O, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Floscopa scandens Lour. 聚花草
Fl. Cochinch. 1: 193. 1790; FKH 284. 1912; FHN 4: 69, fig. 991. 1977; FRPS 13(3): 81. 1997; FOC 24: 25. 2000; FGD 6: 317, fig. 181. 2005.
Floscopa paniculata Hassk., Pl. Jungh. 151. 1852; FHK 377. 1861.

Perennial herb, 20–70 cm tall; stems simple, usually glabrous, creeping at the base. Leaves sessile or with short, winged petiole; leaf sheath hairy or only with hairs on 1 side, margin fringed with long hairs, at least at the top; leaf blade elliptic to ovate-lanceolate, 4–12 × 1–3 cm, scabrous adaxially; covered with multicellular hairs near the base abaxially. Panicle terminal, to 8 × 4 cm, densely glandular with long hairs; peduncle nearly absent; pedicels very short. Sepals shallowly boat-shaped. Petals blue or purple. Fertile stamens 6; filaments glabrous. Capsule ovoid, compressed, ca. 2 × 2 mm. Seeds grey-blue, semi-ellipsoidal, ca. 1.5 mm, shallowly radiate striate.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Lam Tsuen, Fanling, Sai Kung, Tai Mong Tsai, Yung Shue O, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 2642; Y. W. Lam 454, 1378.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian; Vietnam, Laos, Thailand, Myanmar, Sikkim, Bhutan, India, Oceania.
Ecology: Forests, wet places in ravines. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Authority: (C. B. Clarke) J. K. Morton ex D. Y. Hong
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Murdannia bracteata (C. B. Clarke) Kuntze ex J. K. Morton 大苞水竹葉
J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 59(380): 472. 1966.
Murdannia bracteata (C. B. Clarke) J. K. Morton ex D. Y. Hong, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 12: 473. 1974; FRPS 13(3): 109. 1997; FOC 24: 30. 2000; FGD 6: 330. 2005.
Aneilema nudiflorum (L.) R. Br. var. bracteatum C. B. Clarke, Monogr. Phan. 3: 211. 1881.

Perennial herb, with horizontal rhizomes; roots fibrous, 0.5–1 mm thick, densely tomentose. Main stem strongly abbreviated, with basal rosulate leaves and usually 2 fertile stems arising from the base of main stem, creeping or ascending apically, 20–60 cm; internodes ca. 10 cm, pubescent throughout or only on one side. Basal leaves linear, 20–30 × 1.2–1.8 cm, glabrous on both surfaces or abaxially puberulent, margin ciliate proximally. Cauline leaves ovate-lanceolate or lanceolate, 3–12 × 1–1.5 cm, glabrous or scabrous abaxially; leaf sheath pubescent throughout or only hispid-ciliate at mouth. Cincinni (1–)3–5, densely flowered, capitate; peduncle 2–3 cm; involucral bracts leaf-like but smaller; bracts orbicular, 5–7 mm, caducous; pedicels very short, strongly curved, lengthening to 2 – 3 mm in fruit. Sepals ovate-elliptic, ca. 4 mm. Petals blue, obovate-orbicular. Fertile stamens 2; filaments pubescent; staminodes 3; antherodes 3-parted. Capsule broadly ellipsoidal, trigonous, ca. 4 mm, Seeds 2 per valve, yellow-brown, radiate striate, white reticulate, not pitted.

Locality: New Territories.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; Vietnam, Laos, Thailand.
Ecology: Ravines, sandy soil by water. Flowering & fruiting: May–Nov.

Murdannia loriformis (Hassk.) R. S. Rao & Kammathy 牛軛草
Bull. Bot. Surv. India 3: 393. 1961; FRPS 13(3): 108, pl. 27: 3 – 4. 1997; FOC 24: 30. 2000; FGD 6: 330. 2005.
Aneilema loriforme Hassk., Pl. Jungh. 2: 143. 1852.
Aneilema nudiflorum R. Br. var. rigidior Benth., FHK 377. 1861. A
neilema angustifolium N. E. Br., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 36(251): 151. 1903; FKH 283. 1912.

Perennial herb, without rhizomes; roots fibrous, 0.5–1 mm thick, glabrous or tomentose. Main stem undeveloped, with several fertile stems arising from leaf rosette, diffuse or ascending, 15–50(–100) cm, glabrous or puberulent on one side, very rarely densely hirsute. Basal leaves in rosulate tufts, blade linear, 5 – 15( –30) cm × 6–9 mm, apex acute, margin ciliate only proximally; cauline leaves smaller, 2.5–8 cm × 4–7 mm, ciliate only on one side of sheath mouth, glabrous elsewhere, very rarely densely hirsutulous. Cincinni terminal, with several densely arranged flowers, solitary or 2–3 forming a subcapitate panicle; proximal involucral bracts leaf-like but smaller, distal ones very small, less than 10 mm; peduncle ca. 2.5 cm; bracts suborbicular, ca. 4 mm, caducous; pedicels slightly curved, 2.5–4 mm in fruit. Sepals ovate-elliptic, 3–4 mm. Petals blue or purple-red, obovate-orbicular. Fertile stamens 2; filaments pubescent; staminodes 3; antherodes 3-parted. Capsule ovoid-globose, trigonous, 3–4 mm. Seeds 2 per valve, yellow-brown, radiate striate, finely white reticulate, neither pitted nor verrucose.

Locality: New Territories. HK sheet 39300, 39301.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Philippines, Vietnam, Thailand, Sri Lanka, New Guinea.
Ecology: Wet grassy fields, streamsides. Flowering & fruiting: Apr. – Sep.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Shing Mun, Sai Kung, Lai Chi Chong, Luk Keng, Po Toi Islands
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Murdannia nudiflora (L.) Brenan 裸花水竹葉
Kew Bull. 7: 189. 1952; FFJ 6: 460, fig. 415. 1995; FRPS 13(3): 106, pl. 27: 1–2. 1997; FOC 24: 30. 2000; FGD 6: 330. 2005.
Commelina nudiflora L., Sp. Pl. 1: 41. 1753.
Aneilema nudiflorum (L.) R. Br., Prodr. 271. 1810; FHK 376. 1861; FKH 283. 1912.

Annual herb, without rhizomes; roots fibrous less than 0.3 mm thick; stems in tufts, diffuse or ascending from the creeping base, 10 – 50 cm, glabrous. Leaves nearly all cauline, sometimes 1–2 basal; leaf sheath mostly less than 10 mm, hirsute throughout, sometimes glabrous except for a hirsute line along mouth slit; leaf blade linear or lanceolate, 2–7(–10) × 0.5–1 cm, glabrous or sparsely hispid on both surfaces, apex obtuse or acuminate. Cincinni several, in terminal panicles, or solitary, with several densely arranged flowers; peduncle slender, to 4 cm; proximal involucral bracts leaf-like but smaller than leaves, distal ones less than 10 mm; bracts caducous; pedicels slender, straight, 3–5 mm. Sepals ovate-elliptic, ca. 3 mm. Petals purple, obovate-orbicular. Fertile stamens 2; filaments bearded proximally; staminodes 2–4; antherodes 3-parted. Capsule ovoid-globose, trigonous, 3–4 mm. Seeds 2 per valve, yellow-brown, deeply pitted, or shallowly pitted and radiate white verrucose.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Shing Mun, Sai Kung, Lai Chi Chong, Luk Keng, Po Toi Islands. Y. S. Lau 2357; Y. W. Lam 1065; HK sheet 41521.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan, Henan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Shandong, Jiangsu, Fujian; Japan, Philippines, Cambodia, Laos, Myanmar, Bhutan, India, Sri Lanka, Malaysia, Indonesia, New Guinea, Indian Ocean and Pacific islands
Ecology: Shaded and wet places, watersides. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Oct.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Cape D'Aguilar, Sai Kung, Fanling, Castle Peak, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Murdannia simplex (Vahl) Brenan 細竹篙草
Kew Bull. 7: 186. 1952; FRPS 13(3): 110, pl. 27: 5 – 6. 1997; FOC 24: 31. 2000; FGD 6: 331. 2005.
Commelina simplex Vahl, Enum. Pl. 2: 177. 1806.
Aneilema sinicum Ker Gawl., Bot. Reg. t. 659. 1822; FKH 283. 1912.

Perennial herb, without rhizomes; roots robust, 2–3 mm thick, densely tomentose. Main stem strongly abbreviated, with 2–4 fertile stems arising from the base of main stems, usually erect, sometimes ascending, to 50 cm. Basal leaves rosulate, with sheath hirsute only on one side; leaf blade linear, 15–35 × 0.6–1.5 cm, glabrous. Cauline leaves often 2–3, rarely more, proximal one longer, to 12 cm, distal ones shorter, sometimes only ca. 1 cm, glabrous. Cincinni several, to 2 cm, forming narrow panicles ca. 5 cm; peduncle ca. 1 cm; involucral bracts ovate or ovate-lanceolate, less than 1 cm, membranous, caducous; bracts subequaling sepals, caducous; flowers pendulous in bud, ascending after anthesis; pedicels straight, ca. 5 mm in fruit. Sepals elliptic, 4–5 mm. Petals purple, obovate-orbicular. Fertile stamens 2; filaments bearded; staminodes 3; antherodes 3-parted. Capsule ovoid-globose, trigonous, 4–5 mm. Seeds 2 per valve, brownblack, white radiate verrucose.

Locality: Cape D'Aguilar, Sai Kung, Fanling, Castle Peak, Lantau Island. S. P. Lau 52; Y. W. Lam 283, 1778.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan; Africa, India to Indonesia.
Ecology: Marshes, wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Oct.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Authority: (Wall. ex C. B. Clarke) G. Brückn.
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Mong Tsai, Lai Chi Wo
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Murdannia triquetra (Wall. ex C. B. Clarke) G. Brückn. 水竹葉
Nat. Pfl.-Syst. (ed. 2), 15a: 173. 1930; FFJ 6: 460, fig. 414. 1995; FRPS 13(3): 95, pl. 25: 1 – 3. 1997; FOC 24: 27. 2000; FGD 6: 327, fig. 188. 2005.
Aneilema triquetrum Wall. ex C. B. Clarke, Monogr. Phan. 3: 208. 1881.

Perennial herb, with elongate, horizontal rhizomes and fibrous roots. Stems ascending from the creeping base, to 40 cm, with a line of harsh, white hairs on one side. Leaves sessile; leaf sheath fringed with white hairs; leaf blade linear-lanceolate or linear-elliptic, 1.5–4(–6) cm × 4–6(–8) mm, apex acuminate or obtuse, ciliate only in proximal part. Cincinni terminal and axillary, usually 1-flowered; peduncle 1–4 cm, with linear bract at middle, sometimes with a flower in axil of bract; pedicels 1–2 cm. Sepals narrowly oblong, 4–6 mm. Petals pink, purple-red, or blue-purple, obovate. Fertile stamens 3; filaments bearded; staminodes 3; antherodes sagittate. Capsule ovoidglobose, trigonous, 5–7 × 3–4 mm, obtuse or acute at both ends. Seeds (1–)3 per valve, uniseriate, reddish grey, not flattened.

Locality: Tai Mong Tsai, Lai Chi Wo. Y. S. Lau 307; HK sheet 39267.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian; Vietnam, Laos, Myanmar, Thailand, India.
Ecology: Wet places, watersides. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Oct.
Uses: Animal food, medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Sha Tin, Sai Kung, Wu Kau Tang, Fanling, Lo Wu, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Murdannia vaginata (L.) G. Brückn. 細柄水竹葉
Nat. Pfl.-Syst. (ed. 2), 15a: 173. 1930; FRPS 13(3): 99. 1997; FOC 24: 28. 2000; FGD 6: 329. 2005.
Commelina vaginata L., Mant. Pl. 2: 177. 1771.
Aneilema vaginatum (L.) R. Br., Prodr. 271. 1810; FKH 283. 1912.
Dictyospermum vaginatum (L.) D. Y. Hong, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 12(4): 477. 1974.

Perennial herb, with elongate rhizomes and fibrous roots; stems slender and creeping or slightly robust and ascending, 15–50 cm, branched at base, glabrous or with a line of hairs on one side. Leaves sessile; leaf sheath open, ciliate; leaf blade linear, 4–10(–20) cm × 4–7 mm, glabrous, margin ciliate. Flowers 1–5, fasciculate in sheath-like involucral bracts; peduncle slender, 5–10(–20) cm; involucral bracts 1–3 on each stem, distant, striate; pedicels 1–1.5 cm, with 2 bracteoles at middle, hirsute distally. Sepals lanceolate, ca. 3 mm, initially hairy, glabrescent, persistent. Petals blue, obovate-orbicular. Fertile stamens 2; filaments pubescent; staminodes 3 or 4; antherodes 3-parted. Capsule globose, ca. 3 mm in diam. Seeds 1 per valve, grey-black, reticulate.
