Locality: Sha Tin, Sai Kung, Wu Kau Tang, Fanling, Lo Wu, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 2777; Y. W. Lam 893; HK sheet 41814.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Jiangsu; Philippines, Vietnam, Thailand, India, Sri Lanka.
Ecology: Sandy beaches. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Oct.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Victoria Peak, Cape D'Aguilar, Causeway Bay
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Pollia secundiflora (Blume) Bakh. f. 長花枝杜若（杜若）
Bekn. Fl. Java. 10 (Fam. 211): 10. 1949; FRPS 13(3): 89, pl. 24: 2 – 3. 1997; FOC 24: 34. 2000; FGD 6: 316. 2005.
Commelina secundiflora Blume, Enum. Pl. Javae 1: 3. 1827.
Aclisia sorzogonensis E. Mey., Reliq. Haenk. 1: 138, pl. 25. 1827.
Pollia sorzogonensis (E. Mey. ex Presl) Endl., Gen. Pl. 1029. 1836; FHK 377. 1861; FKH 284. 1912.

Perennial herb, 1–2 m tall, with slender and long horizontal rhizomes. Stems erect, sparsely white pubescent. Leaves sessile; leaf sheath ca. 2.5 cm, densely pubescent; leaf blade broadly ovatelanceolate or oblong, 10–15 × 3–8 cm, base attenuate, apex acuminate, verrucose adaxially, densely puberulent abaxially. Panicle with 3–4 branches, with peduncle to more than 20 cm, densely brown-yellow hooked hirsute; involucral bracts leaf-like, nearly as large as leaves, distal ones much smaller, to 5 mm, densely brown-yellow hirsute; bracts membranous. Sepals nearly orbicular, boat-shaped, ca. 3 mm, glabrous, persistent. Petals white, obovate, shallowly boat-shaped, ca. 5 mm. Stamens 6; fertile stamens 3, anterior; staminodes 3, with shorter filaments. Fruit globose, ca. 6 mm in diam.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Cape D'Aguilar, Causeway Bay. C. Wright 545 (K), H. F. Hance 1035 (BM).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Guizhou, Yunnan; Indochina, Thailand, Myanmar, India, Malaysia, Indonesia.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Apr.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Ng Tung Chai
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Pollia siamensis (Craib) Faden ex D. Y. Hong 長柄杜若
FRPS 13(3): 89, pl. 24: 4. 1997; FOC 24: 34. 2000; FGD 6: 316, fig. 180. 2005.

Perennial herb, 30–100 cm tall, with slender and long horizontal rhizomes; stems erect or ascending, glabrous or nearly so. Leaves alternate; leaf sheath 2–4 cm, glabrous or sparsely puberulent; leaf blade elliptic to narrowly ovate, 10–25 × 2.5–8 cm, base narrowed into a petiole of 2–4 cm, apex acuminate, glabrous or subglabrous adaxially on both surfaces. Panicle 5 – 10 cm including the peduncle, densely glandular pubescent; involucral bracts leaf-like, but much smaller than leaves, densely glandular pubescent; bracts membranous, often persistent. Sepals ovate-orbicular, boat-shaped, ca. 3 mm, glabrous. Petals white, ovate-elliptic, shallowly boat-shaped, ca. 4 mm. Stamens 6; fertile stamens 3, anterior; staminodes 3, with shorter filaments. Fruit globose, ca. 5 mm in diam.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Ng Tung Chai. Y. S. Lau 2432; HK sheet 38314.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangxi, S Yunnan; Indochina, Thailand, Philippines, Indonesia, New Guinea.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Apr.–Aug.

Tradescantia pallida (Rose) D. R. Hunt 紫鴨跖草
Kew Bull. 30: 452. 1975; FFJ 6: 457. 1995.
Setcreasea pallida Rose, Contrib. U. S. Natl. Herb. 13(9): 294. 1911.

Perennial herb, whole plant purple in colour; stems ascending or decumbent, much branched. Leaves alternate, sessile; leaf sheath 1–1.2 cm, not closely clasping the stem; leaf blade lanceolate to oblong-lanceolate, 5–10 × 1.5–3 cm, base narrowed to the sheath, apex acute or acuminate, glabrous, long-ciliate on the narrowed portion of the base. Flower clusters subsessile, terminal on apex of branches, subtended by bracts; bracts 2, leaf-like, conduplicate, one larger up to 6 × 2 cm, glabrous. Sepals 3, free, oblong. Petals 3, purple. Stamens 6, all fertile; filaments covered with moniliform hairs.

Locality: Cultivated.
Distribution: Native to tropical Mexico to Mesoamerica; widely cultivated.
Ecology: Flowering: May–Oct.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: The species was reported as Setcreasea purpurea B. K. Boom previously (Check List HK Plants 304. 2002; 107. 2004).

Tradescantia spathacea Sw. 紫背萬年青
Prodr. 57. 1788; FFJ 6: 458, fig. 412. 1995; FOC 24: 38. 2000.
Rhoeo discolor (L’Hér.) Hance, Ann. Bot. Syst. 3: 660. 1853; FGZ 653, fig. 346. 1956.

Herb perennial, glabrous, 20–45 cm tall. Stems simple, erect, to 2 cm in diam. Leaves alternate, spirally arranged, sessile, crowded toward apex of stem; leaf blade lanceolate, 15–35 × 2.5–5(–6) cm, somewhat fleshy, base narrowed and into the sheath, apex acuminate, dark green adaxially, purple abaxially. Flowers clusters many-flowered, shortly pedunculate, in axils of leaves and subtended by 2 bracts; bracts ovate, conduplicate, 3–4 cm. Sepals white, 3–6 mm. Petals white, ovate, 5–8 mm, apex abruptly acute. Stamens 6, all fertile; filaments white hairy. Capsule 3-valved.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 29373.
Distribution: Native to Caribbean region and C America, widely cultivated in tropical and subtropical regions.
Ecology: Flowering: Autumn to winter.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Tradescantia zebrina Heynh. 吊竹梅（水竹草）
Alph. Aufz. Gew. 735. 1847.
Tradescantia zebrina Bosse, Vollst. Handb. Bl.-gärtn. 4: 655. 1849, nom. illeg.; FFJ 6: 457, fig. 411. 1995; FOC 24: 38. 2000.
Zebrina pendula Schnizl., Bot. Zeitung (Berlin) 7: 870. 1849; FGZ 654. 1956.

Perennial herb, ± succulent; stems prostrate or decumbent, branched, rooting at nodes. Leaves alternate, sessile; leaf sheath 8–12 mm, green, with purple longitudinal lines, sparsely villous or glabrescent, mouth fringed with long hairs; leaf blade elliptic-ovate, 3–7 × 1.5–3 cm, base rounded, ± oblique, apex acute or acuminate, adaxially green or purplish, with 2 longitudinal, silver stripes, abaxially purple, glabrous or sparsely pilose at base near the sheath. Flowers in clusters subtended by bracts; bracts 2, leaf-like, 1 larger, ciliate. Sepals lanceolate to oblong-lanceolate, ca. 5 × 1.5 mm. Corolla tube white, ca. 1.2 cm; lobes rose pink, ovate, ca. 6 mm, apex obtuse. Stamens 6, all fertile; filaments covered with purplish blue multicellular hairs. Capsule 3-valved. Seeds rugulose.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 1724, 1769.
Distribution: Native to tropical America, cultivated elsewhere.
Ecology: Flowering: Jun.–Aug.
Uses: Ornamental.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Shek O, Quarry Bay, Sha Tin, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Eriocaulon australe R. Br. 毛穀精草
Prodr. 254. 1810; FHK 382. 1861; FKH 292. 1912; FHN 4: 83. 1977; FRPS 13(3): 31, pl. 8: 1–11. 1997; Z. X. Zhang, Diss. Bot. 154. 1999; FOC 24: 10. 2000; FGD 9: 162. 2009.

Annual herb. Roots many, fibrous, tufted. Leaves linear, usually 10–30 cm × 1.5–3(–5) mm, sometimes up to 50 cm long and 5–8 mm broad, sparsely villous, veins 10–15. Scapes 15–60 cm, 5–7-ribbed. Flower-heads subglobose, 6–8 mm in diam., glaucous, base truncate; receptacle villous; involucral bracts broadly obovate, ca. 2.5 mm in diam., in 2–3 series, much shorter than flower-head, leathery, apex obtuse or acute, abaxially sparsely villous; floral bracts obovate, abaxially densely white clavate hairy toward acute apex. Male flowers: sepals 3, slightly connate at base, 2 larger, boat-like, dorsally winged, abaxially hairy toward apex, another one smaller, oblanceolate-oblong glabrous; petals 3, linear, connate at base into a tube, white clavate hairy at apex, gland black, ovate; anthers black. Female flowers: sepals 3, similar to that in males, 2–2.3 mm; petals 3, linear, white clavate hairy at apex, with black glands at centre; ovary 3-locular; style 3-cleft.

Locality: Shek O, Quarry Bay, Sha Tin, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 171, 2545; Y. W. Lam 1260.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Yunnan, Jiangxi, Fujian; Indochina, Thailand, Malaysia, Australia, Pacific islands.
Ecology: Marshlands and boggy grounds. Flowering & fruiting: Summer to autumn.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Deep Water Bay, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Eriocaulon cinereum R. Br. 白藥穀精草
Prodr. 254. 1810; FKH 292. 1912; FRPS 13(3): 49, pl. 14: 1–11. 1997; Z. X. Zhang, Diss. Bot. 189. 1999; FOC 24: 13. 2000; FGD 9: 166. 2009.
Eriocaulon heteranthum Benth., FHK 382. 1861; FHN 4: 85, fig. 1000. 1977.
Eriocaulon sieboldianum Siebold & Zucc. ex Steud., Syn. Pl. Glumac. 2: 272. 1855.

Annual herb. Roots many, fibrous, tufted. Leaves all radical, narrowly linear, 1–5(–7) cm × 0.8–1.5 mm, ending in fine points, glabrous. Scapes many and slender, 3–12(–18) cm, 4–6-ribbed. Flower-heads light yellow to dark green, at first hemispherical, broadly ovoid when full grown, 2–4 mm in diam.; receptacle villous, occasionally glabrous; involucral bracts pale green-yellow to blackish, oblong to obovate-oblong, ca. 1.5 mm, about half the length of the head, membranous, glabrous; floral bracts oblong to oblanceolate, glabrous or occasionally abaxially villous. Male flowers: sepals united at base into a tube, upper part flat, spathe-like, apex irregularly 3-toothed, glabrous or abaxially hairy toward apex; petals united into a tube at base, limb 3-lobed, lobes ovate to oblong, anterior one slightly larger than others, shortly hairy at apex, gland black or brown; anthers white to dusky. Female flowers: sepals 2(–3), blackish, free, linear, glabrous or sparsely villous abaxially and at margin; petals absent; ovary 3-locular; style 3-cleft.

Locality: Deep Water Bay, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island. W. J. Tutcher 5299; HK sheet 7794, 7797.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Gansu, Shaanxi, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Korea, Japan, Philippines, Indochina, Indian Subcontinent, Indonesia, Australia, Africa.
Ecology: Paddy fields and other moist situations. Flowering & fruiting: Jun. – Oct.

Eriocaulon nantoense Hayata 南投穀精草
Icon. Pl. Formosan. 10: 51. 1921; FRPS 13(3): 26, pl. 6: 1 – 11. 1997; Z. X. Zhang, Diss. Bot. 99. 1999; FOC 24: 9. 2000; FGD 9: 162. 2009.
Eriocaulon luzulifolium auct. non Mart.: FKH 292. 1912.

Annual herb. Roots many, fibrous, tufted. Leaves all radical, linear to linear-lanceolate, 2–5 cm × 1.5–3 mm, apex pointed. Scapes slender, 5–20(–26) cm, 4 – 5-ribbed. Flower-heads blackish when dry, subglobose, 3.5–5(–6) mm in diam.; receptacle sparsely pubescent, or densely white villous; involucral bracts straw-coloured, obovate-cuneate, slightly shorter than the head, apex rounded or nearly so, rigid, glabrescent; floral bracts obovate to oblanceolate, apex shortly acuminate, abaxially white clavate hairy toward apex. Male flowers: sepals 3, connate into a spathe, split on abaxial side, or only united at base and with 3 free lobes, blackish, with white short hairs at the top; petals united into a tube, upper part 3-lobed, lobes equal or the anterior one slightly larger than others, white clavate hairy toward apex, gland brownish, grey, black, inconspicuous, or absent; anthers black. Female flowers: sepals 3, dusky, free, boatlike, dorsally keeled, with white clavate hairy toward apex; petals 3, oblanceolate-linear, membranous, hairy, gland present or absent; ovary 3-locular; style 3-cleft.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. Y. W. Lam 1175; HK sheet 29957.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Marshlands and paddy fields. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Dec.

Eriocaulon setaceum L. 絲葉穀精草
Sp. Pl. 1: 87. 1753; FHK 383. 1861; FKH 292. 1912; FHN 4: 84. 1977; FRPS 13(3): 37, pl. 10: 16 – 26. 1997; Z. X. Zhang, Diss. Bot. 68. 1999; FOC 24: 11. 2000; FGD 9: 164. 2009.

Annual herb. Stem 1–5(–25) cm; roots many fibrous, tufted. Leaves radical, filiform, 3–5 cm × 0.1–0.2 mm, slightly enlarged at the base, glabrous, transparent, pale yellowish green, with transverse minor veins between parallel-veins under lens. Scapes very slender, 5–11 cm, 6-ribbed, glabrous. Flower-heads dusky, ovoid-globose, ca. 3 mm in diam.; receptacle subglabrous or villous; involucral bracts reflexed, straw-coloured, ovate, ca. 1 mm, membranous, glabrous; floral bracts orbicular to oblanceolate, abaxially white clavate hairy toward apex or glabrous. Male flowers: sepals spathe-like, apex 3-lobed, shortly hairy abaxially; petals 3, elliptic to subulate, small, anterior one slightly larger than others, white clavate hairy adaxially and toward apex abaxially, gland black, sometimes absent; anthers black. Female flowers: sepals 3, free, boat-like to obovate, abaxially white clavate hairy toward margin; petals 3, free, oblanceolatelinear, unequal, membranous, gland black, sometimes absent; ovary 3-locular; style deeply 3-cleft.

Locality: Fanling. W. J. Tutcher 7210, 11577.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Sichuan, Yunnan; Japan, Indochina, Myanmar, Thailand, Sri Lanka, India, Bangladesh, Indonesia, N Australia.
Ecology: Paddy fields, ponds, marshes. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Oct.

Eriocaulon sexangulare L. 華南穀精草
Sp. Pl. 1: 87. 1753; FRPS 13(3): 35, pl. 8: 12 – 22. 1997; Z. X. Zhang, Diss. Bot. 189. 1999; FOC 24: 11. 2000; FGD 9: 163, fig. 87. 2009.
Eriocaulon wallichianum Mart., Pl. Asiat. Rar. 3: 26 – 27, pl. 249. 1832; FHK 381. 1861; FKH 292. 1912; FHN 4: 84. 1977.
Eriocaulon cantoniensis Hook. & Arn., Bot. Beech. Voy. 219. 1837.
Eriocaulon sinicum Miq., J. Bot. Néerl. 1: 87. 1861; FKH 292. 1912.

Annual herb. Roots many, fibrous, tufted. Leaves linearlanceolate, 5–25 cm × 3–15 mm, apex very pointed, glabrous. Scapes 10–25(–35) cm, scarcely angular. Flower-heads subglobose, 5–7 mm in diam., glaucous, base truncate; receptacle glabrous; involucral bracts straw-coloured, subrounded, in 1 series, about 1/3 the length of the head, leathery, abaxially white clavate hairy; floral bracts obovate, 2–2.5 mm, leathery, very closely imbricate, apex obtuse or with a very short inflected point, and slightly mealy at the tip, abaxially hairy toward apex. Male flowers: sepals 3, ± connate at the base, of which 2 boat-shaped, with a winged keel, another one oblong-lanceolate, much smaller, flat, irregularly and minutely toothed at apex; petals (2–)3, linear, base united into a tube, apex pubescent, gland indistinct or absent; anthers (4–)6, black. Female flowers: sepals (2–)3, ovate, of which 2 larger, similar to that in males, another one smaller, lanceolate, sometimes reduced or absent; petals (2–)3, linear, unequal, membranous, occasionally villous at centre, apex white clavate hairy; ovary (2–)3-locular; style (2–)3-cleft.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 1941; Y. S. Lau 346, 2336.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Philippines, Indochina, Myanmar, Thailand, India, Sri Lanka, Malaysia, Africa.
Ecology: Paddy fields and other moist situations. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Mar. of the following year.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Wong Nai Chung, Lan Nai Wan, Shek O
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Eriocaulon tonkinense Ruhland 越南穀精草
Pflanzenr. IV 30 (Heft 13): 72. 1903; Z. X. Zhang, Diss. Bot. 194. 1999; FOC 24: 12. 2000; FGD 9: 164. 2009.
Eriocaulon cristatum Mart. var. brevicalyx C. H. Wright, J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 36(251): 199. 1903.
Eriocaulon yaoshanense Ruhland var. brevicalyx (C. H. Wright) W. L. Ma, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 29(4): 301. 1991; FRPS 13(3): 42. 1997; Check List HK Plants 305. 2002; 108. 2004.
Eriocaulon cristatum auct. non Mart.: Benth., FHK 382. 1861; FKH 292. 1912.

Herb caulescent. Rhizomes elongate, 2–3 cm. Leaves all radical, narrow-linear to almost subulate, 7–25 cm × 0.6–0.8 mm. Scapes 15–25(–30) cm, stiff, 5–7-ribbed. Flower-heads subglobose, 3–8 mm in diam., brown or black at base and grey at apex; receptacle glabrous; involucral bracts broadly obovate, straw-coloured, blackish at apex; floral bracts obovate to cuneate, dark at the top and fringed with short white hairs. Male flowers: sepals connate into a spathe, apex 3-lobed, lobes nearly equal, posterior one flat, lateral ones boatlike, all fringed with short white hairs at top; petals 3, obovate to elliptic, with one larger than others, adaxially white clavate hairy toward apex, gland black; stamens 6, anthers milky white to brownish. Female flowers: sepals 3, similar that in males; petals 3, free, oblanceolatelinear, white clavate hairy adaxially and at apex, gland black; ovary 3-locular; style 3-cleft.

Locality: Wong Nai Chung, Lan Nai Wan, Shek O. W. J. Tutcher 7245; Y. S. Lau 1488; HK sheet 35728.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi; Vietnam, India.
Ecology: Marshlands. Flowering & fruiting: Oct.–Jan. of the following year.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Sham Tseng, Ho Pui, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Eriocaulon truncatum Buch.-Ham. ex Mart. 菲律賓穀精草
Pl. Asiat. Rar. 3: 29. 1832; FHK 382. 1861; FKH 292. 1912; FHN 4: 85. 1977; FRPS 13(3): 62. 1997; Z. X. Zhang, Diss. Bot. 179. 1999; FOC 24: 13. 2000; FGD 9: 165. 2009.
Eriocaulon merrillii Ruhland ex Perkins, Fragm. Fl. Philipp. 1: 136. 1904; FRPS 13(3): 47. 1997; Check List HK Plants 305. 2002; 108. 2004.

Annual herb. Roots many, fibrous, tufted. Leaves all radical, linear-lanceolate, 2–6 cm × 2–5(–6) mm. Scapes 2–13 cm. Flowerheads straw-coloured, at first hemispherical, nearly globular when full grown, 4–5 mm in diam.; receptacle glabrous or subglabrous to villous; involucral bracts straw-coloured, various in shape, ovate-elliptic, oblong to obovate-oblong, almost as long as the head, membranous, apex obtuse, glabrous; floral bracts obovate to oblanceolate, hyaline, glabrous or sparsely hairy. Male flowers: sepals 2, connate into a spathe, 1–1.8 mm, blackish, glabrous or sparsely hairy at margin, apex 2–3-lobed; petals united into a tube at base, apex 3-lobed, lobes puberulous, each with a black gland or gland absent; anthers (5–)6, black. Female flowers: sepals 2, linear, blackish, free, usually glabrous; petals 3(–4), villous adaxially and at margin, apex white clavate hairy; ovary 3-locular; style 3-cleft.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Sham Tseng, Ho Pui, Lantau Island. Y. W. Lam 934, 1780, 2172.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Taiwan; Japan, Philippines, Thailand, Indonesia.
Ecology: Paddy fields and other wet places. Flowering & fruiting: May–Dec.

Juncus effusus L. 燈心草
Sp. Pl. 1: 326. 1753; FRPS 13(3): 160. 1997; FOC 24: 48. 2000; FGD 6: 403. 2005.

Perennial herb, densely tufted. Rhizome shortly creeping, thick. Stems terete, 25–90 cm or taller, 1–3(–4) mm in diam., striate; pith continuous. Cataphylls closely embracing stem, reddish brown to chestnut brown, sheath-like, 2–22 cm. Inflorescences pseudolateral, densely to laxly many-flowered; involucral bract erect, seemingly a continuation of stem, terete, 5–28 cm. Perianth segments usually pale brown, linear-lanceolate, 2–2.7 × ca. 0.8 mm, unequal, with outer ones slightly longer than inner ones, apex acute. Stamens 3(or 6), about 2/3 the length of perianth; anthers 0.5–0.7 mm, slightly shorter than filaments. Ovary 3-locular; style very short. Capsules ovoid to oblong, slightly depressed or not, subequaling or slightly longer than perianth, 3-septate, apex obtuse. Seeds ovoid-oblong, 0.5–0.6 mm, reticulate.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. HK sheet 29955, 42769.
Distribution: Widely distributed worldwide.
Ecology: Wet places. Flowering: Apr.–Jul.; fruiting: May–Sep.
Uses: Material (weaving), medicinal (folklore).

Juncus prismatocarpus R. Br. 笄石菖
Prodr. 259. 1810; FKH 285. 1912; FHN 4: 265. 1977; FOC 24: 54. 2000; FGD 6: 405. 2005.
Juncus leschenaultii J. Gay ex Laharpe, Mem. Soc. Hist. Nat. Paris 3: 137. 1827; FHK 330. 1861.
Juncus prismatocarpus R. Br. var. leschenaultii (J. Gay ex Laharpe) Buchenau, Pflanzenr. 25(36): 180. 1906.
Juncus alatus auct non Franch. & Sav.: FKH 285. 1912.

Perennial herb, tufted, (8–)10–65 cm tall. Stems erect or ascending, terete or compressed, 0.7–3 mm in diam. Basal leaves few, cauline leaves 2–4; leaf sheath auricles obtuse, short; leaf blade linear, terete to compressed, 10–25 cm × (1–)2–4 mm, distinctly and perfectly to incompletely septate, apex obtuse, acute, or acuminate. Inflorescences terminal, sparingly or much branched; involucral bract leaf-like, shorter than inflorescence; heads 5–10(–30), globose to hemispheric, 7–10 mm in diam., (3–)8–15(–20)-flowered. Bracts 2–2.5 mm, broadly ovate to ovate-lanceolate, thinly membranous. Perianth segments narrowly lanceolate to linear-lanceolate, 3.5–4 mm, subequal, veins longitudinal, apex acute. Stamens 3, inserted opposite to outer perianth segments; filaments 1.2–1.4 mm; anthers 0.9–1 mm. Stigmas very long, often recurved or sinuous. Capsules narrowly prismatic, 3.8–4.5 mm; angles prominent, acute; placentas not or only slightly intruded, hence fruit 1-locular. Seeds wax-yellow, oblong, 0.6–0.8 mm, regularly longitudinally ribbed; transverse veins faint, remote.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Sai Kung. Y. W. Lam 1761; HK sheet 7667, 39861.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Zhejiang, Taiwan; widely distributed worldwide temperate and subtropical sea area and salt lakes.
Ecology: Wet places. Flowering: May–Aug.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tsing Fai Tong, Sha Lo Tung
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Juncus prismatocarpus R. Br. subsp. teretifolius K. F. Wu 圓柱葉燈心草
Acta Phytotax. Sin. 32: 455. 1994; FRPS 13(3): 193. 1997; FOC 24: 55. 2000; FGD 6: 406. 2005.

Differs in these characters: Plants large, robust. Leaf blade terete, sometimes slightly compressed when dry, distinctly and perfectly septate.

Locality: Tsing Fai Tong, Sha Lo Tung. Y. Yip s.n. (HK sheet 42848, 42849)
Distribution: Xizang, Yunnan, Guangdong, Zhejiang, Jiangsu.
Ecology: Paddy fields, marshes. Fruiting: Jun.–Jul.
Notes: According to FOC (24: 54. 2000), this subspecies is morphologically very close to Juncus wallichianus, and their relationship awaits further research to clarify. Juncus wallichianus differs in the apex of its capsules being cuspidate (cf. FOC Ill. 24: fig. 44: 7 – 9. 2002; Fl. Nei Mongol., ed. 2, 5: 453, fig. 187: 1–5. 1994).

Abildgaardia ovata (Burm. f.) Kral 獨穗柄果莎
Sida 4(2): 72. 1971. Carex ovata Burm. f., Fl. Indica 194. 1768.
Fimbristylis ovata (Burm. f.) Kern, Blumea 15(1): 126. 1967; FHN 4: 298. 1977; FTW ed. 2, 5: 274. 2000; FYN 15: 615. 2003; FGD 8: 310. 2007; FOC 23: 217. 2010; Check List HK Plants 314. 2002; 111. 2004.
Cyperus monostachyus L., Mant. Pl. 2: 180. 1771.
Abildgaardia monostachya (L.) Vahl, Enum. Pl. 2: 296. 1805; FHK 389. 1861.
Fimbristylis monostachya (L.) Hassk., Pl. Jav. Rar. 61. 1848; FKH 298. 1912; FRPS 11: 229. 1961.

Perennial; rhizomes short. Culms tufted, 6–40 cm tall, 0.3–0.8 mm thick, trigonous, smooth below, spinulose-scabrous above. Leaves basal; blade narrowly linear, up to 30 cm × 0.5–1.2 mm, flattish with weakly incurved margins or weakly inrolled; sheath 1–6 cm, dorsally pale green to pale brown, ventrally whitish-hyaline; ligule absent. Involucral bracts 2–3, glume-like or with setaceous blade 0.5–1 cm. Inflorescence reduced to 1 terminal spikelet, with a 1–2 cm long peduncle. Spikelets ovate, ovate-lanceolate, somewhat flattened, 8–15 × 3–7 mm, 10–20-flowered. Glumes 8–20 per spikelet, 2-ranked below, ± spirally arranged above, ovate to broadly ovate, 3–6 × 2–4 mm, apex acute, slightly incurved, 3-veined, greenish. Stamens 3; anthers linear, ca. 2 mm. Style 3-sided, glabrous, basally inflated; stigmas 3. Achenes broadly obvoid, trigonous, 2–2.5 × 1.3–1.5 mm, stiple ca. 0.5 mm, white or cream, ± densely verruculose.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. J. C. Shaw 604; Y. W. Lam 258, 953.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou, Sichuan, Hunan, Fujian, Zhejiang, Taiwan; tropical and subtropical regions of the world.
Ecology: Grasslands. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Sep.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Mount Nicholson, Deep Water Bay Rd., Lower Shing Mun Reservoir
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Actinoschoenus chinensis (Benth.) Benth. 中華星穗莎
Hooker's Icon. Pl. 14: 33, 1881; Gen. Pl. 3: 1058. 1883.
Arthrostylis chinensis Benth., FHK 397. 1861.
Fimbristylis chinensis (Benth.) Tang & Wang, FRPS 11: 106. 1961; FHN 4: 296. 1977.
Fimbristylis actinoschoenus auct. non C. B. Clarke: FKH 298. 1912.
Fimbristylis thouarsii auct. non (Kunth) Merr.: FGD 8: 309. 2007; FOC 23: 253. 2010; Check List HK Plants 315. 2002; 111. 2004.

Perennial. Culms tufted, 15–40 cm tall, triquetrous, slender, with 2 sheaths at base. Leaves basal, reduced to bladeless sheath. Sheath brown, with prominent ribes, margin membranous and darker. Involucral bracts subulate, shorter than inflorescence, soon reflexed and hidden by inflorescence. Inflorescence capitate. Spikelets 1–2(–6), lanceolate, 6–8 × 0.5–2 mm, few-flowered. Glumes 5–7, lower ones distichous, lowest 3 without flowers, uppermost one with sterile flower, variable in shape and size, smaller upward, semiorbicular, broadly ovate or oblong-ovate, 0.25–2 mm, membranous, brown, glabrous, 3-veined, apex mucronate. Stamens 3; anthers linear. Style slender, base enlarged; stigmas 3. Achenes cream-coloured to light brownish, obovoid, 1–1.2 mm, trigonous, smooth to verruculose and indistinctly reticulate.

Locality: Mount Nicholson, Deep Water Bay Rd., Lower Shing Mun Reservoir. Y. W. Lam 1641; HK sheet 41766, 41767.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong.
Ecology: Sandy farmlands, forests, rocks.
Notes: The type specimen (C. Wright s.n.) Benth. was collected from Hong Kong in 1850s. The species was considered conspecific with Actinoschoenus thouarsii (Kunth) Benth. (= Fimbristylis thouarsii Kunth) by many authors, but A. chinensis is easily distinguished from the latter by its spikelets being 1–2(–6) and glumes much broader.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Deep Water Bay, Tai Lung, Wu Shek Kok, Tung Chung, Yi O
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Bulbostylis barbata (Rottb.) Kunth 球柱草
Enum. Pl. 2: 208. 1837; FKH 300. 1912; FRPS 11: 71. 1961; FHN 4: 285. 1977; FTW ed. 2, 5: 193. 2000; FYN 15: 597. 2003; FGD 8: 293. 2007; FOC 23: 219. 2010.
Scirpus barbatus Rottb., Progr. 27. 1772.
Isolepis barbata (Rottb.) R. Br., Prodr., Fl. Nov. Holl. 222. 1810; FHK 393. 1861.

Annual. Rhizome absent. Culms densely tufted, 5–30 cm tall, 0.2–0.4 mm thick, ± terete, smooth, glabrous. Leaves basal; blade filiform, 4–10 cm × 0.2–0.5 mm, acute, glabrous to sparsely pilose above; sheath 0.5–2 cm, brownish. Involucral bracts 1–3, setaceous, the longest 0.3–2.5 cm. Inflorescence capitate, 5–15 mm wide. Spikelets 2–20, lanceolate to ovoid-conical, angular, 3–8 × 1–1.8 mm. Glumes 7–15 per spikelet, ovate, 1.5–2.3 × 1–1.5 mm, apex acute, recurvedmucronate, sides membranous, yellowish green to rusty or chestnut brown, ciliolate to puberulent, margins hyaline, keel acute. Stamen 1(–2); anther oblong, 0.2–0.3 mm. Stigmas 3. Achenes whitish, obovoid-orbicular, trigonous, 0.6–0.8 × 0.4–0.6 mm, ± smooth to finely papillose.

Locality: Deep Water Bay, Tai Lung, Wu Shek Kok, Tung Chung, Yi O. Y. W. Lam 799, 826; Y. S. Lau 2626.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China except NW regions; pantropics.
Ecology: Open-dry sandy places, frequent on dunes and sandy ground near sea. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Oct.

Bulbostylis densa (Wall.) Hand.-Mazz. 絲葉球柱草
Vegetationsbilder 20(7): 16. 1930; FRPS 11: 70. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 194. 2000; FYN 15: 597. 2003; FGD 8: 292. 2007; FOC 23: 218. 2010.
Scirpus densus Wall., Fl. Ind., ed. 1820, 1: 231. 1820.
Bulbostylis cappillarus auct. non (L.) Kunth: FKH 300. 1912.

Annual; rhizome absent. Culms tufted, filiform, 5–40 cm tall, 0.2–0.5 mm thick, smooth, glabrous. Leaves basal; blade filiform, 2–10 cm × 0.4–0.5 mm, apex acute, glabrous to sparsely pilose; sheath pale brown. Involucral bracts setaceous to ± glume-like, the longest up to 0.7 cm. Inflorescence simple to compound, sometimes condensed and appearing ± capitate; primary branches 1–5, 2–5 cm. Spikelets (1–)2–8, solitary or clustered, cylindrical-ovoid to ovoid, somewhat angular, 3–6 × 1.5 mm. Glumes 5–18 per spikelet, ovate to broadly ovate, 1.5–2 × 1 mm, light chestnut brown, glabrous, apex subacute, sides membranous, margins hyaline, keel acute, pale brown. Stamens 2; anthers oblong, 0.2–0.3 mm long. Style ca. 1 mm, stigmas 3. Achenes obovoid-orbicular, trigonous, 0.7–0.9 × 0.5–0.8 mm, maturing greyish, indistinctly transversely wrinkled, minutely papillose.

Locality: Sunset Peak. Y. S. Lau 2740; HK sheet 42189.
Distribution: Areas S of Huanghe; widespread in the Old World tropics.
Ecology: Open, wet, grassy places or on wet rock outcrops. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Dec.

Bulbostylis puberula (Poir.) Kunth 毛鱗球柱草
Enum. Pl. 2: 213. 1837; FRPS 11: 70. 1961; FHN 4: 285. 1977; FGD 8: 293. 2007; FOC 23: 218. 2010.
Scirpus puberulus Poir. in Lamk., Enc. 6: 767. 1804.

Annual; rhizome absent. Culms densely tufted, 7–40 cm tall, 0.3–0.8 mm thick, scabrid, glabrous to puberulent. Leaves basal; blade filiform, 2–9 cm × 0.3–0.6 mm, glabrous to puberulent; sheath 0.8–3 cm long, pubescent, pale brown. Involucral bracts 2–4, leaf-like, the longest up to 4 cm. Inflorescence simple, often condensed and appearing ± capitate, 1–1.5 × 1.5 cm. Spikelets (1–)5–20, solitary, ovoid to cylindrical-ovoid, angular, 4–8 × 1.4–1.6 mm. Glumes 5–14 per spikelet, broadly ovate, 1.7–2.2 × 1.5–2 mm, densely pubescent, apex acute, recurved-mucronate, side membranous, pale greenish to light brown, margins hyaline, keel acute. Stamen 1; anther 0.5–0.7 mm long. Style ca. 1 mm; stigmas 3. Achenes broadly obovoid, triquetrous, 0.8–1 × 0.5–0.8 mm, whitish to pale yellowish, transversely wrinkled, obscurely reticulate with longitudinally oblong epidermal cells.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. HK sheet 13499.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong; widespread in tropical Africa and Asia.
Ecology: Sandy places near seashore. Flowering & fruiting: Feb.–Jun.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Carex arisanensis Hayata 阿里山薹草
J. Coll. Sci. Univ. Tokyo 30: 378. 1911 et Icon. Pl. Form. 6: 130, pl. 18. 1916; FTW 5: 349. 1978; FTW ed. 2, 5: 200. 2000; FRPS 12: 348–349. 2000; FGD 8: 388. 2007; FOC 23: 400. 2010.

Rhizome short. Culms lateral and borne in axils of leaves, 10–40 cm tall, slender and flaccid, trigonous, smooth, base of culms with short leafy-sheaths. Leaves shorter or longer than the culm, linear, 4–8 mm wide, flat, soft herbaceous. Upper bracts spathe-like, upper part glumaceous to rarely with short lanceolate leaf blade 5–10 mm, sheath less than 2 mm to not exist; lower bracts have longer leaf blade, 1–4 cm, and longer sheaths 2–4 mm. Spikes (2–)3–4, terminal spike staminate, lanceolate-oblong, 5–8 mm, peduncle short, < 2 mm to sessile, very close to the adjacent pistillate spike; lateral spikes all pistillate, oblong to elliptic, 8–10 cm, spikelets very few, 2–3(–4), densely clustered; peduncles of upper spikes short to almost absent, lower spikes with slender and rather flaccid peduncles up to 3 cm long-exserted beyond the bract sheath. Male glumes oblong to elliptic, 3–4 × ca. 1.5 mm, apex broad-acute or obtuse, midrib green, margin broad hyaline. Female glumes ovate-oblong, 3.5–5 × 1.2 mm, apex acute, pale, margin broad hyaline, midrib green. Utricles longer than glumes, ovate-fusiform, trigonous, 6.5–7 mm, glabrous, brown-green, membranous, many-veined, base cuneate, upper part attenuate to a long beak; orifice hyaline, emarginate, 2-toothed. Achenes tightly enveloped, obovate-elliptic, trigonous, ca. 3 mm, pale brown; style base not thickened; stigmas 3.

Locality: Sunset Peak, Tai Mo Shan. Y. W. Lam 1392, 2269; H. G. Ye. et al. 1163, 1168.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Taiwan.
Ecology: Montane hillside forests, usually in wet seepages or streamsides, alt. 600–900 m. Fruiting: Feb.–Apr.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Carex baccans Nees 漿果薹草
Wight, Contr. Bot. India 122. 1834; S. T. Dunn, J. Bot. 47: 325. 1910; FKH 305. 1912; FHN 4: 337. 1977; FTW 5: 310, pl. 1347. 1978; Flora Malesiana Ser. I 9(1): 137, fig. 119: 15, 127, 131i. 1979; FFJ 6: 350. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 200. 2000; FRPS 12: 62, pl. 13: 1–4. 2000; FYN 15: 702, fig. 163: 1–4. 2003; FGD 8: 367. 2007; FOC 23: 288. 2010.

Rhizome woody. Culms central to borne in leave axils, erect and robust, 80–150 cm tall, 0.5–0.6 cm thick, trigonous, glabrous, leafy below middle-part. Leaves both cauline and basal, flat, 8–12 mm wide, glabrous abaxially, scabrid adaxially, papery, basal persistent leaf sheaths red-brown, reticulate. Bracts leafy, longer than inflorescence, long-sheathed; panicle compound, ovate, 10–35 cm; inflorescence branches 3–8, single, oblong to ovate, 5–6 × 3–4 cm, lower 1–3 branches more widely-spaced, axis bluntly triquetrous, nearly glabrous; bractlets glumaceous, lanceolate, 3.5–4 mm, leathery, only the basal one with short sheath, others sheathless, awned; peduncles of inflorescence branches rigid, the basal one 12–14 cm, upper ones gradually shorter, usually enclosed in bractlet-sheath; spikes producing from utriculiform cladoprophylls, numerous, cylindrical, 3–6 cm, bisexual and androgynous; male part of spike tenuous, with only few spikelets, 1/2 or 1/3 length of female part; female part with dense and numerous spikelets; male glumes broadly ovate, 3–4.5 × 2–2.5 mm, awned, membranous, chestnut-brown; female glumes broadly ovate, 2–2.5 × 2–2.5 mm, awned, papery, purplish brown or chestnutbrown, with 1 green midvein, margins hyaline; utricles obovate-globose or nearly globose, inflated, 3.5–4.5 mm, nearly leathery, red to purplish red when mature, shining, with many vertical veins, upper margins hairy, shortly stipulate at base, shortly beaked at apex, beak mouth minutely bidentate. Achene elliptic, trigonous, 3–3.5 mm, brown when mature, shortly stipulate at base, apex apiculate; style base not thickened, stigmas 3.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai. Y. W. Lam 1310, 1740; HK sheet 13913.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Sichuan, Guizhou, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; Laos, Cambodia, Thailand, Vietnam, Malaysia, Nepal, India.
Ecology: Montane hillside grasslands, alt. 700–900 m. Fruiting: Aug.–Dec.
Notes: The utricle is berry-like and brightly coloured when ripe. It may be adapted for seed dispersals by birds and mammals.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): High West, Nam Fung Rd., Magazine Gap, Wan Chai Gap, Pik Uk
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Carex bodinieri Franch. 濱海薹草
Bull. Soc. Philom. Paris, ser. 8, 7: 85. 1895 et in Nouv. Arch. Mus. Paris 3, ser. 8: 243, 1896; C. B. Clarke, J. Linn. Soc. Bot, 36: 295. 1903, pro syn. sub C. longipes D. Don; FFJ 6: 349, fig. 311. 1995; FRPS 12: 445, pl. 91: 5 – 7. 2000; FGD 8: 392. 2007; FOC 23: 436. 2010.
Carex brunnea auct. non Thunb.: Dunn, J. Bot. 47: 325. 1910; FKH 306. 1912.
Carex longipes auct. non D. Don: FKH 306. 1912.

Rhizome short and woody. Culms tufted or loosely tufted, rather slender, 35–60 cm tall, trigonous, smooth. Leaves basal, shorter than culm, 1.7–2.8 mm wide, flat, rather stiff, scabrous on both surfaces and margins; sheaths short, usually splitting to base into fibers. Bracts sheathed, sheaths 1.0–3.0 cm, the lower bracts leafy, upper blades reduced to bristle-like. Inflorescence a diffuse and loose compound raceme, lower bracts bear 2(–3) branches, among them usually 1 is compound, with several 2 or more spikes; middle and upper bracts each with 1(–2) spikes, very rarely more; bracts and branches loosely distributed, the lower branches can be up to 10 cm apart, the upper branches closer to each other. Spikes many, androgynous, cylindrical to narrow-lanceolate, 1–2.5 cm, male part range from less than 1/4 of the length for lower spike to nearly 1/2 for the upper spikes, female spikelets 9–12, rather loosely distributed on spikes, peduncle slender and extend out of the sheath by up to 4 cm. Male glume narrowly ovate, 3–6 mm, apex acute, yellowbrown, hyaline, with brown short lines, midrib green 1-veined. Female glumes broad-ovate, 2.8–3 mm, apex acute, muticous or rarely with short awn, membranous, yellow-brown to brown, middle with brown short lines, midrib green 3-veined. Utricle suberect, slightly longer than glume, broad-elliptic, compressed plano-convex, 3.9–4.5 mm, membranous, pale brown to reddishbrown, dorsal side with up to 9 thin veins, glabrous or with sparse hairs towards the margins, upper margins loosely hispid, upper part abruptly contracted into a medium length beak ca. 1.3 mm, base gradually contracted to a short stipe; orifice 2-toothed. Achenes tightly enveloped, ovate to broad-elliptic, compressed plano-convex, 2–2.3 × 1.3–1.6 mm, yellowish to dark brown; style base slightly thickened; stigmas 2, usually shorter than to occasionally equal to utricle.

Locality: High West, Nam Fung Rd., Magazine Gap, Wan Chai Gap, Pik Uk. S. T. Dunn Ex Herb. Hongk. 7187 (K), S. C. Ng 1552, 2810; HK sheet 42115, 42117.
Distribution: Guangdong, Hunan, Fujian, Zhejiang, Jiangsu, Anhui; Japan. Ecology: Montane hillside open forests; alt. 500–900 m. Fruiting: Sep.–Nov.
Notes: The type specimen (Bodinier 1334 (P)) was collected from Happy Valley, Hong Kong Island in 1895.

Specimens of this species were reported as Carex brunnea Thunb. previously (S. T. Dunn l.c.; Check List HK Plants 306. 2002; 108. 2004; Corlett et al., Mem. Hong Kong. Nat. Hist. Soc. 23: 113).

Clarke (1903) identified Bodinier 334 from Happy Valley of Hong Kong as C. longipes, which he considered as conspecific with C. bodinieri. Without citing any specimen, FGD 8: 393 also mentioned C. longipes distributed in Hong Kong and “recorded from coastal region of Guangdong”, but this is not mentioned by FRPS and FOC. In this study, I follow the FRPS treatment of considering C. longipes and C. bodinieri different species. I have not noted any specimen of C. longipes in Hong Kong. Bodinier 334 was not examined by me, but it is unlikely to be C. longipes, as the inclusion of Hong Kong into its distribution range results in disjunct distribution for this species. It happens that the specimen cited by Clarke (1903) is very similar to the type specimen of C. bodinieri (Bodinier 1334) in collection number and locality. A possibility is that Bodinier 334 may be a typo mistake of Bodinier 1334.

Carex breviculmis R. Br. 青綠薹草
Prodr. Fl. Nov. Holland. 242. 1810; FTW 5: 335. 1978; Fl. Malesiana. Ser. I 9(1): 150. 1979; FTW ed. 2, 5: 205. 2000; FRPS 12: 161, pl. 33: 1 – 4. 2000; FYN 15: 727. 2003; FGD 8: 376. 2007; FOC 23: 326. 2010.
Carex leucochlora Bunge, Enum. Pl. Chin. Bor. 68. 1833, FFJ 6: 360, fig. 325. 1995.

Rhizome short. Culms tufted and borne in leave axils, erect to oblique, ca. 20 cm tall, trigonous, slender. Basal sheaths pale-brown and split into fibers. Leaves longer or shorter than the culm, blades 2–3 mm wide, flat, margins scabrid, papery. Lowest bract leafy, longer than the subtended spikes, sheath ca. 9.2 mm; upper bracts bristle-like, nearly sheathless. Spikes 2–5, upper spikes contiguous, lower spikes more remotely spaced. Terminal spike staminate, oblong, 1–1.2 cm × 2–3 mm, nearly sessile, close to the next lateral spike. Lateral spikes androgynous, but the uppermost lateral spikes is occasionally a short mainly male spike, other lateral spikes are mainly pistillate, oblong-ovate, 8–15 × 3–4 mm wide, spikelets 30 – 50, densely distributed on spikes; peduncles up to 3.5 cm for the lowest spike, to almost absent for the upper spikes. Male glumes obovate-oblong, apex acuminate and shortly mucronate, membranous, pale-yellow. Female glumes oblong, 1.7–2 mm (excluding awn) × ca. 0.8 mm, apex truncate or rounded, midrib 3-veined, excurrent into an awn 0.7–1 mm, membranous, pale greenish to pale yellowish. Utricles nearly equal the glume, obovate, obtusely trigonous, 2.3–2.4 mm, membranous, pale yellowish green, many-veined, upper part densely puberulent, suddenly contracted to a conical beak, orifice emarginate, base attenuate into a short stipe. Achene tightly enveloped, ovate, 1.8 mm, dark brown, apex discoid-annulate; stylebase conically thickened; stigmas 3.

Locality: Cheung Sheung. S. C. Ng 1081.
Distribution: Widespread from NE through C to S and SW China; India, Myanmar, Russia (Far East), Korea, Japan.
Ecology: Hillside grasslands, alt. 400 m. Fruiting: Apr.–Jun.

Carex canina Dunn 長柄薹草（果柄薹草）
J. Bot. 47: 325. 1910; FKH 305. 1912; FGD 8: 385. 2007.
Carex hastata Kük., Fedde Repert. Spec. Nov. Regni Veg. 27: 110. 1929, syn. nov.; FRPS 12: 325, pl. 70: 9 – 11. 2000; FOC 23: 394. 2010.
Carex lianchengensis S. Y. Liang et Y. Z. Huang, FFJ 6: 690. 1995, syn. nov.; FRPS 12: 334. 2000 [“lienchengensis”]; FOC 23: 396. 2010.

Rhizome short, woody, covered with fibers of dark brown disintegrating leaf sheath. Culms lateral to tufted and borne in axils of leaves, 25–40 cm tall, slender, trigonous, upper part scabrid, basal sheaths bladeless or having short leaf blade less than 8 cm. Leaves longer than or equal to the culms, linear, 4–6 mm wide, flat, stiff papery, margins scabrid. Bracts short leafy; sheath short, 3–4 mm. Spikes 2–3, cluster towards the top of culms, uppermost lateral spikes almost at the same height as the terminal spike; terminal spike staminate, linear, ca. 1 cm, peduncle short, 3–9 mm; pistillate spikes lateral, oblong-ovate to ovate, 10–15 × 7–10 mm, spikelets very few, only 2–7, but densely distributed on spikes, peduncle short 7–13 mm. Male glumes lanceolate, ca. 3.8 × 1.5 mm, apex obtuse, pale green, midrib green. Female glumes ovate, 5–7 × 2–2.5 mm, apex acute, pale green, 3-veined, green. Utricles longer than the glume, obliquely patent, rhomboid, 7.5–9.2 mm, membranous, yellow-green, glabrous, finely many-veined, base cuneate, upper part abruptly contracted above to a beak 1.5 × 2 mm, orifice 2-toothed. Achenes tightly enveloped, elliptic, trigonous, up to 4.3–5 mm, yellow-brown to black, middle of achene constricted to excavated, base attenuate into a short erect stipe 0.5–1 mm, upper part attenuate into an erect and robust cylindrical beak ca. 1 mm, apex of beak annulate; style-base thickened, stigmas 3.

Locality: Sunset Peak. S. C. Ng 2930, 3054, 3056; Y. W. Lam 1372.
Distribution: Guangdong, Hunan, Fujian, Zhejiang.
Ecology: Montane hillside open forests, alt. 500–900 m. Fruiting: Feb.–Apr.
Notes: The type specimen (S. T. Dunn 7154, HK) was collected from Lantau Island in 1909. The author has examined the types of C. canina and C. hastata (Y. L. Keng 2353, PE), and found them similar in their inflorescence, glumes, utricles and achenes, as well as their leaves and growth form. Carex lianchengensis (H. B. Chen, s.n. [Chinese National Herbarium 28928], PE, isotype), is also similar to C. canina in all aspects apart from the culm and leaf length, which are not enough to separate two species, as size varies greatly among specimens of C. canina from Hong Kong. The author has noted small size plants of C. canina in the field comparable to the size of the isotype of C. lianchengensis.

FRPS mentioned that C. lianchengensis differs from C. canina in culm position. However, culm position is not a reliable character for separation of species in the section Rhomboidales Kükenthal to which all these species belong. Species in this section vary within species with respect to the lateral culms position, which may be borne in axils of middle or lateral leaves, as demonstrated in C. manca and C. harlandii.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Tai Po, Lamma Island, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Carex chinensis Retz. 中華薹草
Retz. Observ. Bot. 3: 42. 1783; FHK 402. 1861; C. B. Clarke, J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 36: 280. 1903–04; FKH 305. 1912; FFJ 6: 371, fig. 338. 1995; FRPS 12: 314. 2000; FGD 8: 383. 2007; FOC 23: 386. 2010.

Rhizome short and woody, obliquely ascending, covered with brown fibers formed from old disintegrating leaf sheaths. Culms tufted and borne in leave axils, oblique to erect, slender, 20–55 cm tall, obtusely trigonous, basal sheaths brown and tinging reddish. Leaves longer than the culm, 3.5–5.5 mm wide, margins scabrid, papery. Bracts with short leaf blade, 8–12 cm, sheath long, 1–3 cm. Spikes 4–5, distant; male spike terminal, narrow-lanceolate to linear, 2.5–3 × 2.5–5.2 mm; peduncle 2–3 cm; lateral, spikes almost completely pistillate 2–3.5 cm × 6–6.5 mm, female spikelets 26 – 75, rather densely distributed on spikes; peduncles erect, slender, 2.5–4.5 cm. Male glumes 4.5–6.5 mm, oblanceolate to oblong, apex with awn, light brown. Female glumes oblong, apex truncate or sometimes emarginate or acuminate, 4.5–5.7 × 0.6–0.9 mm, pale, the midrib extend into a scabrid long awn, 1–2 mm. Utricles slightly shorter than the glume, obliquely patent, rhomboid-elliptic, trigonous, 3–3.5 mm, membranous, yellow-green, sparsely puberulent, many-veined, upper part abruptly contract into a medium beak, orifice 2-toothed, base attenuate into a stipe. Achenes tightly enveloped, rhomboid, trigonous, 1.7–2.2 × ca. 1 mm wide, upper part broadly acute, beak short, apex annulate or rarely not so; style thickened at base; stigmas 3.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Po, Lamma Island, Lantau Island. H. C. Tang 1232, 2351; Y. S. Lau 2703; S. P. Lau 86.
Distribution: Guangdong, Yunnan, Guizhou, Shaanxi, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian.
Ecology: Fairly common in montane hillside open forests, alt. 100–800 m. Fruiting: Mar.–Apr.

Carex cruciata Wahlenb. 十字薹草
Kongl. Vetensk. Acad. Nya Handl. 24: 149. 1803; C. B. Clarke, J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 36: 281. 1903-04; FKH 305. 1912; FHN 4: 338. 1977; FTW 5: 310, pl. 1347. 1978; Fl. Malesiana Ser. I 9(1): 118, fig. 118: 3a; 124a – d. 1979; FFJ 6: 350 – 51, fig. 313. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 209, pl. 80. 2000; FRPS 12: 72, pl. 14: 9 – 11. 2000; FYN 15: 707, fig. 165: 6 – 8. 2003; FGD 8: 368. 2007; FOC 23: 291. 2010.
Carex benghalensis Roxb., Fl. Ind. 3: 572. 1832; FHK 401. 1861.

Rhizome thick, woody, with stolons. Culms central to borne in leave axils, erect, 40–90 cm tall, shorter than or ± equal to leaves, 2–4 mm thick, trigonous, smooth. Leaves mainly basal, a few cauline, flat, 4–8 mm wide, scabrid abaxially and adaxially along midrib, veins and margins, papery, persistent sheaths dark brown, fibriform. Bracts leafy, longer than inflorescence branches, long-sheathed towards base; panicle compound; inflorescence branches ovate-triangular, 4–10 × 3–6 cm wide, usually single; peduncles of inflorescence branches rigid, smooth, trigonous to flattened, lowest one 10–18 cm, upper ones gradually shorter; inflorescence axis trigonous to slightly flattened, covered in dense short hairs; bractlets glumaceous and awned, 0.7–3.0 mm, hairy abaxially; cladoprophylls utriculiform, without flower, several-veined and hairy abaxially; spikes many, all producing from cladoprophylls, patent horizontally, 4–17 mm, bisexual, androgynous; male part of spike about one-third to as long as female part; male glumes lanceolate, 2.5–3.0 mm, acuminate, mucronate, membranous, pale brownish white, with dense brown spots and short lines; female glumes ovate, ca. 2 mm, membranous, apex obtuse to acute, shortly awned ca. 0.4 mm, 3-veined. Utricles longer than glumes, elliptic, inflated trigonous, 3–3.2 mm, pale brownish white, with brown spots and short lines, smooth or upper part loosely hairy, with several raised veins, nearly sessile, apex attenuate into medium beak about 1/3 length of utricle, hairy or glabrous laterally, beak opening obliquely truncate. Achenes ovateelliptic, trigonous, 1.5–1.8 mm, dark brown when mature; base of style slightly thickened, stigma 3.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 2127; S. C. Ng 2229; L. T. Lo 161.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Bhutan, Nepal, India, Indonesia, Thailand, Vietnam, Japan, Madagascar.
Ecology: Hillside grasslands, roadsides, alt. 50–900 m. Fruiting: Aug.–Dec.
Notes: The ripe utricle is fleshy and white. It may be adapted for dispersals by birds.

Carex cryptostachys Brongn. 隱穗薹草
Duperrey, Voy. Monde, Phanerog. 152. 1832; FHK 403. 1861; C. B. Clarke, J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 36: 281. 1903 – 04; FKH 306. 1912; FHN 4: 340. 1977; Fl. Malesiana. Ser. I 9(1): 148, fig. 120: 26. 1979; FFJ 6: 358, fig. 322. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 209, pl. 81. 2000; FRPS 12: 141, pl. 29: 1–5. 2000; FYN 15: 723, fig. 169: 1–5. 2003; FGD 8: 372. 2007; FOC 23: 317. 2010.

Rhizome oblique, woody, covered with dark brown fibrous remains of basal sheaths. Culms tufted and borne in leave axils, slightly pendent to oblique, slender, 10–25 cm tall, slender and weak, flattened trigonous. Leaves longer than or as long as the culms, blades 3–16 mm wide, flat, smooth on both surfaces, slightly scabrid along margins, stiff papery. Bracts bristle-like, sheath 4–8 mm and spathe-like. Spikes 6–10, all androgynous, oblong to cylindrical, 8–25 mm, spikelets rather loose; male part short, 2–4 mm; peduncle 4–8 mm, only slightly longer than sheath, slender. Female glumes ovate-oblong to ovate, 2–2.3 mm, pale-brown to yellow-green, the midrib green, apex acute, mucronate to acuminate. Utricles distinctly longer than the glume, 3-ribbed longitudinally, elliptic to oblongfusiform, obscurely trigonous or slightly flattened, 3–3.8 mm, membranous, yellow-green to pale yellow, puberulent above, many-veined, base cuneate with short stipe 0.5–1 mm, attenuate above into a short beak, orifice minutely 2-toothed. Achene 2.2–2.5 mm; shape is either trigonous rhombic or trigonous but flattened dorsiventually into elliptic-fusiform shape; faces excavated both at upper and lower parts, and angles excavated at middle; yellowish to dark brown; style-base curved and persistent; stigmas 3.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 1206; Y. S. Lau, 3037; S. C. Ng 1268, 2917; Y. W. Lam 1367; HK sheet 13995.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam, Thailand, Malay Peninsula, Indonesia, Philippines, Australia (Queensland).
Ecology: Common in almost all forest habitats in Hong Kong, occasionally also found in rock crevices along streamsides of steep ravine, alt. 50–800 m. Fruiting: Mar.–Aug.
Notes: Two extreme forms with some intermediates were observed among Hong Kong specimen. The trigonous form characterised by trigonous rhombic urtricle and achene, with excavation at the middle of achene angles and on all faces is close to the description of FRPS and FTW (e.g. HK sheet 13995; H. C. Tang 1206). It is usually found in forest habitat with relatively thick soil. The flattened form is characterized by dorsiventrally flattened utricle and secondarily flattened trigonous achene, excavation is shallow or even absent (e.g. Y. S. Lau 3037; S. C. Ng 1268, 2917). It generally has narrower and shorter leaves, and usually found in rock crevices along streamsides of steep ravine. Intermediates with less obvious dorsiventrally flattened utricle and achene and intermediate constriction at the achene angle had been observed in both Hong Kong (Y. W. Lam 1367) and Hainan (S.K. Lau 606 (PE) and Y. Zhong 4198 (PE)) specimens.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Victoria Peak, Tai Mo Shan, Nei Lak Shan, Shek Pik
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Carex filicina Nees 蕨狀薹草
Wight, Contrib. Bot. India, 123. 1834; FHN 4: 339. 1977; Fl. Malesiana Ser. I 9(1): 122, fig. 118: 4. 1979; FFJ 6: 351, fig. 314. 1995; FRPS 12: 75, pl. 15: 6 – 9. 2000; FTW ed. 2, 5: 212. 2000; FYN 15: 704, fig. 164: 6 – 9. 2003; FGD 8: 369. 2007; FOC 23: 292. 2010.

Rhizome thick, woody. Culms borne in leave axils, loosely tufted, oblique to erect, 40–90 cm tall, shorter than leaves or rarely longer, 2–2.5 mm thick, trigonous, glabrous. Leaves flat, 4–10 mm wide, glabrous on both sides, papery; sheaths persistent, purplish red or purplish brown, split into fibers towards base. Bracts leafy, longer than inflorescence branches, long-sheathed; panicle compound, 20–50 cm; inflorescence branches 4–8, triangular-ovate, 4–8 cm wide, 3–5 cm, single, rarely binate; peduncles of inflorescence branches tenuous, trigonous, lowest one 10–20 cm, upper ones gradually shorter, sparsely hairy on ridges; rachis sharply trigonous to slightly flattened, short hairy; bractlets glumaceous, 1–1.5 mm, apex with or without awn; cladoprophylls utriculiform, without flower; spikes all producing from cladoprophylls, numerous, patent or slightly patent, oblong or oblong-cylindrical, 5–15 mm, bisexual, androgynous, male part of spike shorter than female part, with 3–7 spikelets; female part with 2–16 spikelets. Male glumes lanceolate, 2–3 mm, acuminate, membranous, brown or reddish brown; female glumes ovate or lanceolate, 1.5–2 mm, membranous, acuminate or acute, brown, reddish brown or pale brown with reddish brown spots and short lines, glabrous, with 1 midvein. Utricles membranous, brown or reddish brown, or wholly pale brown with reddish brown spots and short lines, elliptic or narrowly elliptic, trigonous, 3–3.4 mm, glabrous, with 2 lateral veins and several fine veins abaxially, nearly sessile, apex contracted into long excurved beak about 1/2 or more the length of utricle, beak opening obliquely truncate. Achenes narrow elliptic to rounded-rhomboid, trigonous, ca. 1.6 mm, yellowish brown to dark brown when mature; base of style not thickened, stigma 3.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Tai Mo Shan, Nei Lak Shan, Shek Pik. Y. W. Lam 1395; S. C. Ng 1593; J. C. Shaw 105.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Myanmar, Thailand, Vietnam, Malaysia, Indonesia, Philippines.
Ecology: Margins of hillside forests and grasslands, alt. 500–900 m. Fruiting: Sep.–Nov.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Authority: F. T. Wang & Tang ex P. C. Li
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Pok Fu Lam, Castle Peak, Mui Wo, Yi O, San Tau
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Carex funhuangshanica F. T. Wang & Tang ex P. C. Li 鳳凰山薹草
Acta Phytotax. Sin. 37(2): 168, fig. 7. 1999; FRPS 12: 179, pl. 35; 9 – 11. 2000 [“fenghuangshanica”]; FOC 23: 332. 2010.

Rhizome short. Culms borne in leave axils, oblique, slender and rather flaccid, 15–25 cm tall, 0.8 mm thick, trigonous, smooth. Leaves longer than the culm, flat, 1.5–4 mm wide, stiff papery, margins smooth to slightly scabrid, persistent sheaths brown and spilt into fibers. Bracts leafy and longer than the inflorescence, up to 12 cm, lowest bract not different with sterile leaves; sheath 2–7 mm. Spikes (1–)2, lowest spike may be borne near the base of culm, androgynous, oblong, 1–2 cm × 4 – 5 mm, peduncle slender, ca. 1 cm; male part 1/4–1/2 the length spike, male spikelets 8 – 13, rather densely distributed on the male part. Male glumes ovate, 2.2–2.6 mm, apex obtuse, papery, yellowish green to yellowish brown, abaxial side with 1 green midrib and several weak veins. Female glumes ovate or broad-ovate, 2.5–3 mm, apex obtuse, leathery, abaxial side with 1 green midrib and several weak vein, yellowish green on both sides, margins white hyaline. Utricles ovate to broad-elliptic, trigonous, 4.3–4.9 mm, greenish to yellowish brown, leathery, glabrous, each side with several robust veins, margins narrowly winged and ciliate, upper part attenuate into a short beak, orifice minutely 2-toothed, base cuneate and nearly sessile. Achene ovate to broad-elliptic, trigonous, 3–3.5 mm, brownish, base attenuate into a short stipe, apex without beak; style-base thickened conically, stigmas 3.

Locality: Pok Fu Lam, Castle Peak, Mui Wo, Yi O, San Tau. S. C. Ng 1333; Y. W. Lam 1495; HK sheet 14008.
Distribution: Guangxi.
Ecology: Lowland sparse forests, alt. 10–200 m. Fruiting: May – Jun.
Notes: The species was reported as Carex speciosa Kunth previously (Check List HK Plants 308. 2002; 109. 2004).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Mount Nicholson, Shek O, Kowloon Peak, Tai Mo Shan, Soko Islands
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Carex harlandii Boott 長囊薹草
Ill. Gen. Carex 2: 87, pl. 255. 1860; FHK 403. 1861; C. B. Clarke, J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 36: 289. 1903–04; FKH 306. 1912; FFJ 6: 371, fig. 339. 1995; FRPS 12: 323, pl. 65: 1–4. 2000; FGD 8: 384. 2007; FOC 23: 393. 2010.
Carex anomocarya Nelmes, Kew Bull. 1950: 202. 1951; FHN 4: 344. 1977; Fl. Malesiana Ser. I 9(1): 144, fig. 120: 22, fig. 128. 1979.

Rhizome thick and woody, covered with fibers of disintegrating leaf sheath. Culms lateral or borne in axils of leaves, oblique to erect, 30–90 cm tall, trigonous, smooth, basal leaves 2–5, ranging from short and sheath-like to long leaf-like equal to culms. Leaves of sterile ramets longer than the culm, broad-linear, 10–25 cm wide, flat, base plicate, upper margins slightly scabrous, papery, apex acuminate. Bracts leafy, with sheath, lower bracts longer than the subtended spikelets, becoming shorter for upper bracts. Spikes (2–)3–4 at the upper part of culm, upper spikes close, more distally spaced down the culm. Male spike terminal, linear-cylindrical, 4.5–7 cm, peduncle short to almost absent. Lateral spikes androgynous, pistillate on the lower four-fifths or more, cylindrical, 5–8 cm × 8–10 mm wide, spikelets 28–70, rather densely distributed on spikes, peduncles 5 cm or less. Female glumes ovate-oblong or oblong, ca. 6 mm (including awn), pale-green, 3-veined, midrib excurrent into a scabrous awn ca. 1.8 mm. Utricles longer than the glumes, 8–9 mm (including beak), obliquely patent, elliptic-rhomboid, papery, brown, yellow-green or green, glabrous, many-veined, lower part attenuate toward base, upper part attenuate into a long beak 3.3–3.8 mm, orifice 2-toothed. Achenes tightly enveloped, rhomboid-elliptic, trigonous, 5–5.7 mm, yellow-brown to dark brown, middle of the achene constricted on angles, base attenuate into a curve stipe, upper part attenuate to a robust and erect cylindrical beak, apex of beak annulate; style base thickened conical, stigmas 3.

Locality: Mount Nicholson, Shek O, Kowloon Peak, Tai Mo Shan, Soko Islands. Y. W. Lam 1393, 2085; J. C. Shaw 365.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan, Fujian, Anhui, Zhejiang, Jiangxi, Hubei; Myanmar, Thailand, N Vietnam, Indonesia.
Ecology: Common in hillside and lowland forests, alt. 10–700 m. Fruiting: Feb.–Jun.
Notes: The type specimen was collected by C. Harland from Hong Kong Island in 1850s.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Pok Fu Lam, Ma On Shan, Tai Mo Shan, Sunset Peak
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Carex ligata Boott ex Benth. 香港薹草（顯柱薹草）
FHK 402. 1861; Boott, Ill. Gen. Carex 4: 211. 1867; C. B. Clarke, J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 36: 294. 1903–04; Kük., Pflanzenr. 38(IV, 20): 473, fig. 75G–K. 1909; FKH 306. 1912; FRPS 12: 146. 2000 pro parte, excluding C. nexa Boott ex Benth.; FGD 8: 374. 2007; FOC 23: 319. 2010 pro parte, excluding C. nexa Boott ex Benth.
Carex hongkongensis Franch., Nouv. Arch. Mus. Paris III 10: 93. 1898.

Rhizome short and woody. Culms borne in leave axils, erect, 25–40 cm tall, slender, obtusely trigonous, smooth, basal sheaths dark brown and split into fibers. Leaves longer than the culm, 3–5 mm wide, flat, abaxial surface slightly scabrid, margins scabrid, papery. Bracts leafy, 2–3 cm, shorter than the subtended spikes; sheath brownish to greenish, 0.5–1 cm. Spikes 3–4, remote and ± regularly spaced on the stem; male spike terminal, narrowly cylindrical, 3–4 cm, ca. 1 – 1.3 mm thick, peduncle 3–4 cm; pistillate spikes lateral, cylindrical, 1–2 cm × 3.5–4 mm, spikelets 10–40, rather densely distributed on spikes, peduncle 1.5–2.5 cm, slender. Male glumes oblong, apex rounded, 2.4–2.9 × 1–1.3 mm, lower margins clasping the spike rachis to almost amplexicaul, pale greenish with broad hyaline margin and green midrib. Female glumes obovate-oblong, apex acute to obtuse, 2.2–2.8 mm, greenish with broad hyaline margin and 1–3 green midribs. Utricles longer than the glumes, rhombic, trigonous, 3–3.3 mm, membranous, puberulent above, many-veined, base cuneate with short stipe, upper part cuspidate into a beak 0.3–0.4 mm, orifice 2-toothed. Achene tightly enveloped, rhombic, trigonous, 2.1–2.4 mm; upper part of the achene form into a ivory-coloured stout, cylindrical crown 0.3–0.4 mm, shallowly concave at top; faces slightly depressed to excavated at both the upper and lower part, middle of achene raised into angle longitudinally, base attenuate into a stipe ca. 0.2 mm; style base thickened; stigmas 3.

Locality: Pok Fu Lam, Ma On Shan, Tai Mo Shan, Sunset Peak. S. C. Ng 1233, 2916; HK sheet 42104.
Distribution: Guangdong, Fujian.
Ecology: Hillside and ravine forests, alt. 300–700 m. Fruiting: Mar.–May.
Notes: The syntype specimens (Harland 790 ex parte; C. Wright 8, 78, 79, & 602; Wilford 263, all deposited at K) were collected from Hong Kong. FRPS also mentioned this species distributed in Anhui province. The author had examined the Anhui specimen at PE (S. W. Su 87033), and found it very different from the above type specimens with respect to its achene and male spikelet.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Pat Sin Leng, Shing Mun Arboretum, Tai Mo Shan
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Carex maculata Boott 斑點果薹草
Trans. Linn. Soc. 20: 128. 1846; Hayata, Icon. Plant Formos. 10: 60. 1921; FTW 5: 359, pl. 1360. 1978; Fl. Malesiana. Ser. I 9(1): 157, fig. 121: 39. 1979; FFJ 6: 354, fig. 317. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 220, pl. 84. 2000; FRPS 12: 140, pl. 28: 1–4. 2000; FGD 8: 372. 2007; FOC 23: 317. 2010.

Rhizome slender and woody. Culms borne in leave axils, oblique to erect, 40–50 cm tall, trigonous, smooth, with a few brown leafless sheath at the base. Leaves equal to or shorter than culm, sheathed, blades 3–6 mm wide, flat, smooth but slightly scabrid along leaf margins and toward apex, herbaceous. Bracts sheathed and leafy, longer than inflorescences, sheath up to 4 cm for the lowest spikes, getting shorter towards the terminal of the inflorescence. Spikes 3–4, the lowest spike remote, the others congregated towards top of culm; terminal spike staminate, linear-cylindrical, 1.2–2.5 cm, peduncle short (3 mm) to almost obsolete; lateral spikes pistillate, oblong-cylindrical to cylindrical, 1.5–2.5 cm, spikelets dense, the lower spikes has rather long peduncle up to 5 cm, peduncle becoming shorter (to 3 mm) for higher spikes. Male glumes oblong-lanceolate, 3.5–4 mm, obtuse, sometimes mucronate, membranous, with 3 longitudinal green veins. Female glumes oblong-ovate to ovate, 1.5–1.7 mm, acute to obtuse, membranous, yellowish brown with brown short lines. Utricles borne obliquely, longer than glume, broad-obovate to broad-elliptic, trigonous but slightly flattened dorsiventrally, 2.1–2.5 mm, membranous, brown, reddish brown to dark-purple, densely papillate, 3–5-veined on each side, base attenuate to cuneate, apex abruptly contracted into a short beak, orifice subtruncate to slightly emarginate. Achene tightly enveloped in utricle, broad-obovate to broad-elliptical, trigonous, 1.5–1.7 mm, yellowish brown to pale yellow or pale brown, base abruptly contracted to a short stipe, apex with a short curved style base, style base not thickened, stigma 3.

Locality: Pat Sin Leng, Shing Mun Arboretum, Tai Mo Shan. S. Y. Hu 13584 (K); S. C. Ng 1309; HK sheet 42078.
Distribution: Guangdong, Hunan, Sichuan, Jiangxi, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Sri Lanka, Indonesia.
Ecology: Streamsides, open hillside forests, alt. 300–900 m. Fruiting: Mar.–May
Notes: A distinctive species characterised by reddish brown female spikelets. The leaves, although erect, are rather soft in texture and resemble that of wetland grasses.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Victoria Peak, Pok Fu Lam, Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Carex manca Boott ex Benth. 彎柄薹草（紅苞薹草）
FHK 402. 1861; Boott, Ill. Gen. Carex 4: 131, t. 425. 1867; C. B. Clarke, J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 36: 297. 1903–04; FKH 306. 1912; FFJ 6: 372. 1995; FRPS 12: 319. 2000; X. F. Jing et al., J. Wuhan Bot. Res. 22(1): 50. 2004; FGD 8: 384. 2007; FOC 23: 391. 2010.

Rhizome thick and short, woody, covered with brown disintegrating leaf sheath. Culms lateral or borne in axils of leaves at the outside, oblique, slender, 30–70 cm tall, trigonous, smooth, base of culms with leafless sheathes. Basal leaves shorter than the culms (7–10 cm) or absent; leaves of sterile ramets longer than the culms, 6–8.5 mm wide, flat, leaf base plicate, papery, upper margins scabrid, adaxial side pale green. Bracts with short leaf blade, 1 cm or less, sheath loose, 1–2.5 cm. Spikes 2–3; male spike terminal, linear-cylindrical, 3.5–4.5 cm, borne on long peduncle 5.5–7.5 cm; lateral spikes androgynous, female for the lower half to two-thirds, oblong-cylindrical, 2–3 cm, female spikelets 12–18, rather loosely distributed on spikes, peduncles less than 7 cm. Male glumes oblanceolate-oblong, ca. 7 mm × 2–2.4 mm, apex acute, pale to yellow-brown, hyaline, midrib 3-veined green. Female glumes oblonglanceolate or ovate-lanceolate, ca. 5.5 mm, apex acute to rounded, or rarely truncate or emarginate, pale to yellowish, 3-veined, green; midrib extend into a short mucronate point or rarely with an awn to 1.2 mm. Utricles longer than the glume, rhomboid-elliptic, trigonous, 6–6.5 mm, membranous, many-veined, yellow-green, upper part sparsely puberulent and abruptly contracted above to a smooth long beak ca. 2 mm, orifice 2-toothed, base cuneate into a short beak. Achenes tightly enveloped, yellow-brown to dark brown, ovate to broad-elliptic, 3–4 mm (including beak), trigonous, angles constricted at the middle, upper part abruptly contracted into a cylindrical beak which is often curved, base abruptly end in a curved stipe; stigmas 3.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Pok Fu Lam, Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan. S. C. Ng 1344; HK sheet 42076, 42077.
Distribution: Guangdong, Hubei.
Ecology: Montane hillside open forests, alt. 200–500 m. Fruiting: Mar.–Apr.
Notes: The type specimen (C. Harland 790 ex parte (K)) was collected from Hong Kong Island in 1850s.

Carex nemostachys Steud. 條穗薹草（線穗薹草）
Flora 29: 23. 1846 et Synops. Cyper. 218. 1855; FHN 4: 341. 1977; FTW 5: 351. 1978; FFJ 6: 367, fig. 334. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 223. 2000; FRPS 12: 285, pl. 58: 1 – 3. 2000; FGD 8: 380, fig. 210. 2007; FOC 23: 374. 2010.

Rhizomes thick, sometimes stoloniferous. Culms 40–90 cm tall, erect, robust and stiff, trigonous, upper part scabrid, basal sheaths disintegrating into yellow-brown fibers. Leaves slightly longer than the culms, 4–7 mm wide, stiff, thick papery to leathery, lower part plicate, becoming flat towards upper part, veins and margins scabrid. Bracts sheathless, lower bracts leafy and longer than subtended spikes, 10–17 cm, upper bracts reduced to bristle shorter than spikes. Spikes 5–8, contiguous towards the top of culm, becoming more spaced towards middle of culm; male spike terminal, cylindrical-linear, 6–8 cm, peduncle short to almost obsolete; female spikes lateral, cylindrical, 5–8 cm × 2.5–3 mm, female spikelets very abundant, more than 100, and rather densely distributed on the long spikes, peduncle short for the lower spikes, almost absent for upper spikes. Male glumes ca. 5 mm, linear to narrow-lanceolate, margins scabrid and with rough hairs, 1–3-veined yellowish. Female glumes 3.5–4.5 × ca. 0.4 mm, narrow-lanceolate, apex with awn, margins of awn scabrid, membranous, pale-greyish, 1–3-veined. Utricles patent, curved outward away from rachis, slightly shorter than glume (including awn), ovate or broad-ovate, obtusely trigonous, 3–3.6 mm, membranous, brown, few-veined, hispidulous, base cuneate, upper part abruptly contracted to a slender, recurved beak, orifice obliquely truncate to minutely 2-toothed. Achene loosely enveloped, broad-obovate to broad-elliptical, trigonous, 1.8–2.0 mm, brownish yellow to brown; style base not thickened, stigmas 3.

Locality: Sha Lo Tung, Fo Tan. H. C. Tang 2297; Y. S. Lau 3080; HK sheet 36026.
Distribution: Guangdong, Fujian, Zhejiang, Jiangsu, Anhui, Jiangxi, Hunan, Hubei, Guizhou, Yunnan; India, Bengladesh, Myanmar, Thailand, Vietnam, Cambodia, Japan.
Ecology: Streamsides, wet places under forests, open grassy abandoned farmlands, alt. ca. 200 m. Fruiting: Nov.–Jan. of the following year.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Victoria Peak, D'Aguilar Peak, Ma On Shan, Castle Peak, Tung Lung Chau, Shek Pik, Ngong Ping (Lantau Island)
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Carex nexa Boott ex Benth. 聯結薹草
FHK 402. 1861; Boott, Ill. Gen. Carex 4: 194. 1867; C. B. Clarke, J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 36: 300. 1903–04; FKH 306. 1912; FRPS 12: 211. 2000 pro syn. sub C. ligata Boott ex Benth.; FGD 8: 374. 2007; FOC 23: 319. 2010 pro syn. sub C. ligata Boott ex Benth.
Carex ligata Boott ex Benth. var. nexa (Boott ex Benth.) Kük., Pflanzenr. 38(IV, 20): 474. 1909.

Rhizome short and woody. Culms borne in leave axils, 30–50 cm tall, oblique to erect, slender, obtusely trigonous to flattened trigonous, smooth, basal sheaths dark brown and split into fibers. Leaves longer than or equal to the culm, 3–4.5 mm wide, flat, smooth dorsally and slightly scabrid along margins, papery. Bracts leafy, ca. 5 cm and longer than subtended spikes for lower bracts, becoming shorter and bristle-like towards top of culms; sheath greenish, 5–25 mm, getting shorter towards top of culms. Spikes 3–5, rather remote, regularly spaced; terminal spike staminate, linear, 5–6 cm × 1.8–2.2 mm, peduncle 2–3 cm; lateral spikes pistillate or androgynous, cylindrical, 2–3.5 cm × 3.5–3.9 mm, spikelets 18–35, and fairly densely distributed on spikes, peduncle slender 6–40 cm, getting shorter towards top of culm. Male glumes oblanceolate to oblong-obovate, apex acute, 6.7–7.5 × 1.3–1.4 mm, yellowish to brownish, hyaline, 1–3-veined at the middle, midrib brown. Female glumes oblong, 3.1–3.6 × 0.9–1.1 mm, apex acute, acuminate to shortly awned, pale yellowish green to brownish, midrib brown. Utricles longer than the glume, slightly curved outward from the rachis, ellipticfusiform, trigonous, 3.2–3.7 × 0.9–1 mm, membranous, many-veined, base cuneate with short stipe, gradually attenuate above to a beak ca. 0.5 mm, orifice minutely 2-toothed. Achene tightly enveloped, elliptic-fusiform, trigonous, 2.1–2.3 mm; upper part of the achene form into an ivory-coloured, cylindrical crown 0.1–0.2 mm, shallowly concave to flat at top; faces slightly depressed at both the upper and lower part, middle of achene ridges excavated, base attenuate into a stipe ca. 0.2 mm; style base thickened; stigmas 3.

Locality: Victoria Peak, D’Aguilar Peak, Ma On Shan, Castle Peak, Tung Lung Chau, Shek Pik, Ngong Ping (Lantau Island). S. C. Ng 1169; HK sheet 8219, 14015, 42197.
Distribution: Guangdong, Fujian.
Ecology: Hillside open forests, alt. 500–900 m. Fruiting: Mar.–May.
Notes: The type specimens (C. Harland 790 ex parte (K); C. Wright 100, 607 (K)) were collected from Hong Kong Island in 1850s. This species was treated as a variety of C. ligata by Kükenthal (1909) FRPS and FOC have considered it a synonym of C. ligata. I have examined the type specimens of these two species at K, and found their differences are significant enough to be considered as different species. The achene of C. ligata is rhombic and without excavation at the middle of the achene. The male spikelet of C. ligata is narrowcylindrical, and the male glumes are greenish in colour and much shorter than that of C. nexa.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Beacon Hill, Kwun Yam Shan Tsuen, Sha Lo Tung, Sunset Peak
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Carex phacota Spreng. 鏡子薹草
Syst. Veg. 3: 826. 1826; FKH 306. 1912; FHN 4: 341. 1977; FTW 5: 365. 1978; Fl. Malesiana. Ser. I 9(1): 170, fig. 122: 52, 132: c. 1979; FFJ 6: 346, fig. 307. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 225. 2000; FRPS 12: 431. 2000; FYN 15: 782. 2003; FGD 8: 391, fig. 212. 2007; FOC 23: 431. 2010.

Rhizome short and woody. Culms central, with basal leaves, 50–70 cm tall, acute-trigonous, base with yellow green to yellowishbrown sheaths, which splitting into reticulate fibers. Leaves longer or shorter than the culm, 2–5 mm wide, flat, margins slightly revolute, base plicate. Lower bracts leaf-like, longer than spikes, sheath absent to very short, ca. 2 mm, upper bracts bristle-like. Spikes 3–5, close to each other, pendent to somewhat extent; male spike terminal, linear-cylindrical, 3–6 cm × 2–2.5 mm wide, peduncle 2–2.5 cm; lateral spikes pistillate, often pendent, long-cylindrical, 2.5–6.5 cm × 3–4.5 mm, spikelets 100–120 and very densely distributed. Male glumes oblong to lanceolate, ca. 2.5 (awn excluded) × 0.5 mm, apex emarginate to obtuse, with an awn ca. 0.5 mm. Female glumes oblong, 2–2.9 mm, (awn excluded), apex truncate or emarginate, pale and hyaline with rusty dots and short lines, midrib green 3-veined, extend into a scabrous awn 0.9–1.2 mm. Utricles longer than the glume, broad-ovate or elliptic, 2–2.5 × 1.7–1.8 mm, biconvex, densely papillose, greenish brown to dark brown, upper part abruptly contracted above to a short beak ca. 0.2 mm, the orifice entire to slightly emarginate. Achenes rather loosely enveloped, rounded or broadly ovate, ca. 1.8 mm, biconvex, brown, densely papillose; style long, base not thickened; stigmas 2.

Locality: Beacon Hill, Kwun Yam Shan Tsuen, Sha Lo Tung, Sunset Peak. S.Y. Hu 9829 (K); HK sheet 41813, 42081.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Shandong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Nepal, India, Sri Lanka, Myanmar, N Thailand, Vietnam, Malaysia, Indonesia.
Ecology: Streamsides, open wetlands and abandoned farmlands, alt. 200–800 m. Fruiting: Feb.–Mar.

Carex pruinosa Boott 粉被薹草
Proc. Linn. Soc. 1: 255. 1858 et Ill. Gen. Carex 1: 65, t. 174. 1858; C. B. Clarke, J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 36: 306. 1903 – 04; FKH 306. 1912; FFJ 6: 346, fig. 306. 1995; FRPS 12: 428. 2000; FYN 15: 782. 2003; FGD 8: 390, fig. 211. 2007; FOC 23: 430. 2010.

Rhizome short. Culms tufted, 30–80 cm tall, rather stiff, smooth, with red-brown sheaths at base. Leaves equal to or shorter than the culm, 3–5 mm wide, flat, margins revolute. Bracts leafy, longer than spikes. Spikes 3–5, well-spaced at the upper part of culm, peduncle slender 1.5–4 cm; male spike terminal, occasionally with several male spikelets at apex, narrow-cylindrical, 2–3 mm; lateral spikes male, pendent, sometimes with male flowers at apex, cylindrical, 15–35 × 4–7 mm, male spikelets 50–80 and very densely distributed. Female glumes ovate to oblong, ca. 3.3 × 1.4 mm, apex acuminate with short mucronate tip < 0.5 mm, midrib 3-veined green, hyaline on the two sides, with dense ferruginous dots and short lines. Utricles equal to or slightly longer than the glume, oblongovate, 2.5–3 × 2–2.3 mm, densely papillose and red-brown glandular, base broad-cuneate, abruptly contracted above into a short beak, orifice emarginate. Achenes rather loosely enveloped, broad-ovate, biconvex, ca. 2 × 1.5 mm, yellow-brown; stigmas 2.

Locality: Mount Kellet.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuen, Henan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Shandong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian; India, Bhutan, N Thailand, Indonesia.
Ecology: Ravines, streamsides, grasslands, alt. 50–2500 m. Fruiting: Mar.–Jun.
Notes: Record of this species in Hong Kong was mentioned in C. B. Clarke (1903) and FKH (1912), but no specimen of this species had been deposited in the Hong Kong Herbarium. Although Clarke (1903) had cited a specimen from Mount Kellet (Bodinier 1431), but it was not seen in K. The above description and information are based on FRPS and a Guangdong specimen deposited in HK (HK sheet 14101).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Authority: Tang & F. T. Wang ex S. Y. Liang
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Ng Tung Chai, Nei Lak Shan
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Carex pseudolaticeps Tang & F. T. Wang ex S. Y. Liang 彌勒山薹草
Acta Phytotax. Sin. 36: 536, fig. 3: 1 – 5. 1998; FRPS 12: 326, pl. 67: 1 – 5. 2000 [“pseudo-laticeps”]; FGD 8: 385. 2007; FOC 23: 394. 2010.

Rhizome short and woody with brown fibers of disintegrated leaf sheath. Plant pubescent throughout. Culms lateral or borne in axils of outer leaves, lateral culms with or without basal leaves, 7 – 35 cm tall, trigonous, base of culm with leafless sheath. Leaves longer than the culms, 6 – 12 mm wide, flat, base plicate, soft papery. Bracts short leafy to bristle-like, sheath up to 2.5 cm. Spikes 3 – 4, fairly close towards the top of culms; male spike terminal, narrowly cylindrical, ca. 3.5 cm, peduncle less than 3 cm; lateral spikes 3, androgynous, male part short at the top one-fifth to one-eighth, cylindrical, 1 – 4 cm, spikelets 13 – 48, rather densely distributed on spikes, peduncles 0.5 – 3 cm. Male glumes ovate, ca. 3.5 × 1.4 mm, apex rounded to broad-acute, hyaline, midrib green and keeled. Female glumes lanceolate, ca. 4.5 mm, pale greenish; midrib green, 3-veined and excurrent into a mucronate tip ca. 1.5 mm. Utricles longer than the glume, obliquely patent, ovate-elliptic, 7 – 7.5 mm, papery, green-brown, densely pubescent, many-veined, base attenuate, upper part attenuate to a long beak 2.8 – 3.2 mm, orifice 2-toothed. Achenes tightly enveloped, rhomboid-ovate to broad-elliptic, 4.2 – 4.5 mm, trigonous, middle of achenes constricted on the angles, black, base with a short curved stipe, upper part attenuate into an erect cylindrical beak 1.4 – 1.8 mm, apex of beak annulate; style base thickened at base; stigmas 3.

Locality: Ng Tung Chai, Nei Lak Shan. S. C. Ng 2920, 3048.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi.
Ecology: Montane hillside forests, alt. 600 – 800 m. Fruiting: Mar. – Apr.
Notes: The type specimen (C. L. Tso 20216, PE, holotype) was collected from Nei Lak Shan, Lantau Island in 1929.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Sai Kung (Tai Long Wan), Pak Shek Kok
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Carex pumila Thunb. 矮生薹草
Murray, Syst. Veg., ed. 14, 846. 1784; FHK 402. 1861; C. B. Clarke, J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 36: 307. 1903 – 04; FKH 305. 1912; FTW 5: 357, pl. 1359. 1978; FFJ 6: 356, fig. 320. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 227, pl. 88. 2000; FRPS 12: 373, pl. 78: 1 – 4. 2000; Y. L. Zheng & Y. F. Deng, Guihaia 23(6): 542. 2003; FGD 8: 388. 2007; FOC 23: 408. 2010.

Rhizome slender, stoloniferous. Culms central, 10–20 cm tall, trigonous, middle and basal part completely enclosed by sheath of basal leaves, lowest sheaths bladeless and reddish brown. Leaves longer than or equalling culm, blades 2–3.5 mm wide, flat, leathery, upper part of the leaves scabrous along veins and margins, with long sheath. Lower bracts leafy, longer than or shorter than culms, 5–10 cm, sheath short ca. 6 mm; upper bracts become smaller, reducing to bristle or glume for the terminal spike. Spikes 3–6, the top 1–2 staminate, clavate or narrowly cylindrical, 1.5–2.5 cm, peduncle short, < 0.7 mm; the other spikes pistillate, oblong or oblongcylindrical, 1.5–2 cm, ca. 8 mm wide, spikelets quite many, 13–19, rather loosely distributed, peduncle short, < 8 mm. Male glumes oblong, ca. 5.8 × 2 mm, apex acute and with or without short mucronate tip, yellowish brown and with magenta dots and short lines towards the base and middle of glume, midrib leathery, margins hyaline. Female glumes broad-ovate, 4.5–5.5 mm, apex acute and mucronate, membranous, brownish with rusty or magenta short lines, midrib 3-veined green, margin white and hyaline.
