Utricles longer than glumes, obliquely patent, ovate, inflated-trigonous, 6.2–6.6 × ca. 2.1 mm, corky, yellowish or yellowish brown, glabrous, distinctly several-veined, abruptly contracted to a broadly cuneate base and a thick stipe < 1 mm, upper part gradually narrowed to a rather broad and short beak ca. 2 mm, orifice 2-toothed. Achenes rather tightly enveloped, broad-obovate to elliptic, trigonous, 3.5 × 1.7 mm, base with short-stipe, style-base not thickened, stigmas 3.

Locality: Sai Kung (Tai Long Wan), Pak Shek Kok. J. C. Shaw 393; S. C. Ng 1392; Y. W. Lam 1767.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Liaoning, Hebei, Shandong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Russia (Far East), Korea, Japan.
Ecology: Coastal sandy beaches. Grow in mobile sand at the seaward margin of sand dune vegetation, alt. 0–2 m. Fruiting: Apr.–Oct.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan, Lantau Peak, Sunset Peak
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Carex scaposa C. B. Clarke 花葶薹草
Bot. Mag. 113, pl. 6940. 1887; FKH 305. 1912; FHN 4: 337. 1977; FFJ 6: 352, fig. 315. 1995; FRPS 12: 82, pl. 16: 1–4. 2000; FYN 15: 710, fig. 166: 1–4. 2003; FGD 8: 369. 2007; FOC 23: 294. 2010.

Rhizome woody. Culms central, oblique to erect, 35–70 cm tall, 1–3 mm thick, blunty trigonous, sparsely pubescent, with or without leafless glabrous papery pale brown spathe-like sheath at the base or on the culm towards the base. Leaves basal, tufted, longer or shorter than culms; petiole 20–30 cm, glabrous, papery, sometimes leaf base extending downwards forming narrow wings; leaf blade elliptic, elliptic-linear, to elliptic-oblanceolate, 20–35 × 2.5–4.5 cm wide, with 3 longitudinal veins, base attenuate to acuminate, glabrous on both surfaces or scabrid abaxially. Bracts spathe-like, shorter than inflorescence branches; inflorescence compound, 3  several-branched; inflorescence branches paniculate, triangular-ovate, 2–3.5 × 2–3 cm wide, single or binate; peduncles rigid, trigonous, 4–8 cm, densely pubescent; axis of inflorescence branches sharply trigonous to flattened, densely pubescent; bractlets glumaceous, broad lanceolate, 2–5 mm, brown to pale brown; cladoprophylls utriculiform, without flower. Spikes about 20, all producing from cladoprophylls, patent, bisexual, androgynous, oblong-cylindrical, 7–15 mm. Male part of spike linear-lanceolate, shorter than female part, and fewer spikelets; male glumes ovate-lanceolate, 2.5–3 mm, membranous, pale brown. Female part with 5–7 spikelets; female glumes ovate, 2.5–2.7 mm, membranous, acuminate, brown with spots and 3 longitudinal veins, margins ciliate when young. Utricles elliptic, trigonous, 3–3.5 mm, papery, pale brown with dense brown spots, with 2 lateral veins abaxially, glabrous, nearly sessile, apex contracted gradually into medium beak up to 1/2 of the utricle length, beak opening emarginate. Achenes broad elliptic, trigonous, 2–2.5 mm, brown when mature; base of style not thickened, stigma 3.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan, Lantau Peak, Sunset Peak. Y. W. Lam 435; HK sheet 39599, 41605.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian; Vietnam.
Ecology: Montane hillside forests, alt. 600–900 m. Fruiting: Aug.–Nov.
Notes: A distinctive species characterised by broad lanceolate leaves with rather long petiole. The local specimens are rather consistent in leaf shape and petiole length, but FRPS (12: 82 – 84) has reported considerable variation among specimens within China.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Aberdeen, Happy Valley, Bride's Pool, Tai Mo Shan, Sha Tin, Sunset Peak
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Carex teinogyna Boott 長柱頭薹草（細梗薹草）
Ill. Gen. Carex 1: 60, pl. 158. 1858; Fl. Malesiana. Ser. I 9(1): 175, fig. 123: 59. 1979; FFJ 6: 347, fig. 308. 1995; FRPS 12: 436, pl. 89. 2000; FYN 15: 788, fig. 185: 1–4. 2003; FGD 8: 392. 2007; FOC 23: 433. 2010.

Rhizome short and woody. Culms densely tufted, 25–60(–90) cm tall, rather slender, trigonous to flattened, scabrid. Leaves shorter than or equalling the culms, 2.5–3 mm wide, lower part conduplicate, midrib canaliculate, becoming flat towards upper part, veins and margins scabrous, basal sheaths usually splitting into fibers. Bracts shorter than or equal to branches of inflorescence, the lower bracts leaf-like, < 12 cm, upper bracts reducing to bristle-like; sheaths 5–25 mm. Inflorescence compound, spikes rather dense on inflorescences, lower bracts with (2–)3 branches of inflorescence, among them at least one branched further into 2 or more spikes; middle and upper bracts bear (1–)2–3 spikes. Spikes linear, 1–5 cm, androgynous, male part only ca. 1/4 of the spikes, remaining part of spikes male, male spikelets 7–25 and rather loosely distributed, peduncle slender but short, ca. 4–5 mm, usually only slightly longer than subtending bract-sheath. Male glumes similar to male glumes. Female glumes oblong-ovate, 3.5–4 mm, apex acute with a short scabrid mucronate point or awn, hyaline, brown to reddish brown, midrib green 3-veined. Utricles equal to or shorter than glume, oblong or narrow-elliptic, plano-convex, 3.2–4.7 × 1.1–1.3 mm, membranous, dark-brown to brown, hispidulous but a little bit less so at the middle, severalveined, base abruptly contracted to a short stipe, abruptly narrowed above to a rather long beak 1–1.4 mm, orifice minutely 2-toothed. Achenes tightly enveloped, elliptic, 1.8–2.3 × 1.1–1.3 mm, yellowish to dark-brown or black, sessile; style base slightly thickened, stigmas 2, slender and longer than utricle (including beak), persistent.

Locality: Aberdeen, Happy Valley, Bride's Pool, Tai Mo Shan, Sha Tin, Sunset Peak. Y. S. Lau 2807; L. T. Lo 420; Y. W. Lam 1443.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang; India, Myanmar, Vietnam, Korea, Japan.
Ecology: Common in hillside forests and streamsides, alt. 100–700 m. Fruiting: Nov.–Jan. of the following year.
Notes: Its long persistent styles may help dispersal by attaching to passing-by mammals and birds or by assisting floatation on water surface.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Victoria Peak, Happy Valley, Ma On Shan, Pai Ngak Shan, Sunset Peak
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Carex tenebrosa Boott 芒尖鱗薹草（薄葉薹草）
Ill. Gen. Carex 2: 88, t. 256. 1860; FHK 402. 1861; C. B. Clarke, J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 36: 313. 1903 – 04; FKH 306. 1912; FRPS 12: 331–332. 2000; FGD 8: 386. 2007; FOC 23: 395. 2010.

Rhizome stout and woody, with dark brown fibers of disintegrating leaf sheath. Dried specimen dark olive-green. Culms central or lateral with basal leaves, 80–100 cm tall, trigonous, smooth, leathery. Leaves longer than the culms, 5–8 mm wide, flat to moderately revolute, margins scabrid, leathery. Lower bracts leaf-like, ca. 8 cm, reducing to setaceous for upper bracts, scabrous, sheath less than 5 cm. Spikes 3–4; male spike terminal, broad-linear with tapering ends, 4–9 cm, peduncle long, < 10 cm; lateral spikes 2–3, androgynous, male part about two- to three-fifths of the spike, cylindrical, 6–9.5 cm, spikelets 80–100 and very densely distributed on spikes, peduncle long for lower spikes, become shorter for upper spikes, 3–20 cm. Male glume oblong, 5–6 × 1.4–2.5 mm, apex emarginate to truncate with a hispid awn ca. 1.5 mm, membranous, pale brown. Female glumes oblong, 6.5–7.5 × 2.2–2.8 mm, apex truncate to emarginate, brown-green, the midrib project extend into a scabrous awn 3–4 mm. Utricles longer than the glume, rhomboid, 7–8.5 mm, stiff papery, dark olive-green, many-veined, base cunneate, sparsely hispid on margins, upper part attenuate into a long beak 3–4 mm, margin of beak scabrous along margins, orifice deeply 2-toothed. Achenes tightly enveloped, 4.7–5 × ca. 2 mm, rhomboid, trigonous, middle of achenes constricted, upper part contracted to an erect or slightly oblique cylindrical beak 1.5–2 mm, apex of beak slightly inflated; style-base slightly thickened; stigmas 3, rather long.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Happy Valley, Ma On Shan, Pai Ngak Shan, Sunset Peak. S. C. Ng 1226, 2152; HK sheet 42079.
Distribution: Guangdong.
Ecology: Montane hillside open forests, alt. 500–900 m. Fruiting: Feb.–Apr.
Notes: The species was reported as Carex thibetica Franch. previously (Check List HK Plants 308. 2002; 109. 2004).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Po Kau, Ma On Shan, Nei Lak Shan, Keung Shan, Sunset Peak
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Carex tenuispicula Tang ex S. Y. Liang 纖穗薹草
Acta Phytotax. Sin. 34: 92, fig. 1. 1996; FRPS 12: 149, pl. 30: 9 – 12. 2000; FGD 8: 375. 2007; FOC 23: 320. 2010.
Carex tenuispicula Y. C. Tang, FFJ 6: 359. 1995. ined.

Rhizome short. Culms borne in the leave axil, trigonous, 10–30 cm tall, oblique, very slender and rather flaccid, pale brownish to pale greenish. Basal sheaths split into dark brown fibers. Leaves shorter than or longer than culms, 7–40 cm × 2–4 mm, flat, scabrid along margins, papery. Bracts leafy and longer than spikes for lower bracts, 5–12 cm, becoming shorter and bristle-like towards top of culms; sheath ca. 2 mm for lower and middle bracts, or absent for upper bracts. Spikes 4 – 6, pale brownish to pale yellowish, remote especially for lower spikes, lowerest spikes are often from near base of culms; male spike terminal, linear, 3–4 cm × 0.5–0.7 mm, peduncle 3–4 mm. Lateral spikes androgynous, mainly pistillate, narrowly cylindrical, 1–4 cm × 1.5–1.7 mm, female spikelets 9–28, rather loosely distributed, peduncle long and slender, 4–10 cm, lower spikes often pendent with longer peduncle. Male glumes broad ovate, apex rounded, 1.5–1.6 cm, margin ciliate, very pale brownish. Pistillate glumes broad ovate, apex obtuse to rounded, 1.3–1.5 mm, membranous, pale-brown, margin hyaline and ciliate. Utricles longer than the glume, fusiform, trigonous, 2.2–3 × ca. 1 mm, membranous, very pale brownish, many-veined, upper part gradually attenuate forming a short beak, orifice slightly 2-toothed. Achene tightly enveloped, pale brownish to brown, rhombic or fusiform, trigonous, 1.9–2.1 × ca. 0.9 mm, faces slightly depressed at upper and lower part, upper part of the achene form into a short cylindrical neck ca. 0.2 × 0.2 mm, pale yellowish to pale brownish, apex flat; base attenuate into a stipe; style-base slightly thickened; stigmas 3.

Locality: Tai Po Kau, Ma On Shan, Nei Lak Shan, Keung Shan, Sunset Peak. HK sheet 41935, 41936, 41939.
Distribution: Guangdong, Fujian.
Ecology: Montane hillside open forests, alt. 300–500 m. Fruiting: Jan.–Mar.

Carex tristachya Thunb. 三穗薹草
Syst. Veg., ed. 14, 845. 1784; FKH 306. 1912; FHN 4: 342. 1977; FFJ 6: 361, fig. 326. 1995; FRPS 12: 158, pl. 32: 1–4. 2000; FGD 8: 375. 2007; FOC 23: 324. 2010.

Rhizome short. Culms tufted and borne in leave axils, erect to oblique, 12–40 cm tall, slender, obtusely trigonous, smooth. Basal sheath dark brown and split into fibers. Leaves shorter or equal to the culm, 2–3 mm wide, flat, papery, margins scabrid. Bracts leafy for the lowest spikes, longer than the subtended spikes, 2–4 cm, upper bracts reduce to sheath similar to glumes in colour, texture and size; lower sheath up to 2 cm. Spikes 4–6, upper ones closer to contiguous, more remotely spaced for lower spikes; terminal spike staminate, narrowly linear-cylindrical, 18–23 × ca. 1.5 mm, peduncle very short to obsolete; lateral spikes pistillate, cylindrical, 1–1.5 cm × 2–2.5 mm, spikelets 12–17, rather densely distributed on spikes; peduncles of lowest spikes extend far beyond sheath, up to 10 cm, those of upper spikes getting shorter, the peduncle of the uppermost spike is short and only slightly extend out of sheath. Male glumes broad ovate, ca. 2.4 × 1.3 mm, base of margin free or slightly connate to below the middle; filament of stamen thread-like or flat. Female glumes elliptic to oblong, 1.8–1.9 × 1.0–1.1 mm, apex mucronate, obtuse to truncate, pale yellow, midrib green. Utricles longer than the glumes, erect, ovate-fusiform, trigonous, 2.8–3.0 mm × ca. 1 mm, membranous, green, many-veined, puberulent, upper part attenuate into a short beak, orifice minutely 2-toothed, base attenuate into a short stipe. Achene tightly enveloped, ovate, ca. 2.1 mm, brown to dark brown, apex discoid-annulate; style base thickened conically; stigmas 3.

Locality: San Tau, Tung Lung Chau. S. C. Ng 2153; HK sheet 41933, 41934.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Hunan, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian; Korea, Japan.
Ecology: Hillside open forests and shrublands, alt. 10–100 m. Fruiting: Mar.–Apr.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Pok Fu Lam, Mount Nicholson, Tai Mo Shan, Wu Kau Tang, Nam Chung, Sha Lo Tung, Lantau Peak, Cheung Chau
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Carex truncatigluma C. B. Clarke 截鱗薹草
J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 36: 315. 1904; FFJ 6: 359, fig. 323. 1995; FRPS 12: 144, pl. 30: 1 – 4. 2000; FYN 15: 725, fig. 169: 6 – 9. 2003; FGD 8: 373. 2007; FOC 23: 318. 2010.
Carex gracilispica Hayata, Icon. Pl. Form 10: 62, fig. 39. 1921; FTW 5: 331, pl. 1355. 1978; Fl. Malesiana. Ser. I 9(1): 149. 1979; FTW ed. 2, 5: 213, pl. 82. 2000.

Rhizome woody, obliquely ascending, covered with greyish brown fibrous remains of leaf sheath. Culms tufted and borne in leave axils to lateral, oblique to erect, slender, 15–35 cm tall, trigonous. Leaves longer than or equal to the culms, 5–8 mm wide, flat, slightly scabrid to smooth on both surfaces, stiff papery. Bracts bristle-like to short-leafy, with sheath 6–8 mm. Spikes 3–6, male spike terminal, linear cylindrical, 3.5–5 × 0.1 cm, peduncle almost obsolete or very short, ca. 0.5 cm. Lateral spikes female, cylindrical, 3.5–5 × 0.2–0.3 cm thick, spikelets rather loose; the highest pistillate spike surpass or equal the staminate spike in length, with peduncle equal to or slightly longer than the enclosing bract sheath; the lower pistillate spikes remote and with longer peduncles up to 2–4 cm, extending beyond the sheath. Male glumes oblong, apex rounded, 3–3.5 mm, pale yellowish brown. Female glumes broad-obovate, apex truncate or rounded to minutely murconate, yellowish, margins broadly hyaline, midrib green. Utricles longer than the glume, rhombic-fusiform, trigonous, 3.4–4.2 × 1–1.1 mm, pale greenish brown, membranous, puberulent, many-veined, base cuneate with short stipe, upper part cuspidate into a short beak, orifice minutely 2-toothed. Achene tightly enveloped, rhombic-fusiform, trigonous, 2.5–3 × 1–1.1 mm, pale brown to dark brown; upper part of the achene form into a ivory-coloured stout, cylindrical crown, ca. 0.5 mm, apex truncate to shallowly concave; faces of achene excavated at the lower part, but only slightly so at the upper part; base attenuate into a stipe ca. 0.5 mm; style base slightly thickened and persistent; stigmas 3.

Locality: Pok Fu Lam, Mount Nicholson, Tai Mo Shan, Wu Kau Tang, Nam Chung, Sha Lo Tung, Lantau Peak, Cheung Chau. J. C. Shaw 410; S. C. Ng 1208; HK sheet 36834.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam, Malay Peninsula, Philippines.
Ecology: Fairly common in hillside forests, alt. 50–900 m. Fruiting: Feb.–Apr.

Carex tsiangii F. T. Wang & Tang 三念薹草
Contrib. Inst. Bot. Nat. Acad. Peiping 6(2): 59. 1949; FRPS 12: 92. 2000; FGD 8: 371. 2007; FOC 23: 298. 2010.

Rhizome woody, with stolons. Culms lateral, erect to oblique, 45–55 cm tall, 1–1.5 mm thick, trigonous to flattened, glabrous, with leafless brown sheaths at culm base and towards lower part of the culm. Leaves longer than culms, basal, several leaves and basal leafless brown sheaths forming a high shoot, leaf blades linear, flat, 5–7 mm wide, glabrous to slightly scabrous on both sides, margins entire or scabrid, soft papery. Bracts spathe-like and leafless, shorter than inflorescence branches; panicle compound, 10–30 cm, 3–10-branched; inflorescence branches broadly ovate, ca. 2 × 2 cm, single or binate, each with 3–10 spikes, peduncles tenuous, 2–7 cm, pubescent; inflorescence axis sharply trigonous, densely hirsutus when young; bractlets glumaceous, lanceolate, 3–9 mm, pale brown with brown dots, loosely pubescent; spikes horizontally patent, bisexual, androgynous, 8–12 mm, cylindrical, male part equal to female part, female part with 3–15 spikelets; male glumes lanceolate, 3–3.5 mm, acute, brown with brown spots and short lines, with 1 midvein; female glumes ovate to ovate-lanceolate, 2.5–3 mm, acute, membranous, pale brown with brown spots and short lines, with 1 midvein, loosely pubescent, margins ciliate. Utricles broad-elliptic, obtusely trigonous, 3–4.2 mm wide, papery, brown, glabrous, with several fine veins, apex contracted into long beak about 50% of the whole length of utricle, orifice minutely 2-toothed. Achenes elliptic or broad-elliptic, trigonous, ca. 2 mm; style base thickened, stigma 3.

Locality: Sunset Peak, Lantau Peak. S. C. Ng 1531, 2651.
Distribution: Guangdong.
Ecology: Margins of montane hillside open forests and hillside forests with grasslands, alt. 700–900 m. Fruiting: Sep.–Oct.

Carex zunyiensis Tang & F. T. Wang 遵義薹草
Acta Phytotax. Sin. 24: 241. 1986; FRPS 12: 336, pl. 70: 1–4. 2000; FYN 15: 772. 2003; Y. L. Zheng & Y. F. Deng, Guihaia 23(6): 542. 2003; X. F. Jing et al., J. Wuhan Bot. Res. 22(1): 51. 2004; FGD 8: 387. 2007; FOC 23: 397. 2010.

Rhizome short and woody. Culms lateral or in axils of outer leaves, 4–12 cm tall, much shorter than leaves, basal leaves sheath-like with leaf blade, 5–9 cm, or without leaf blade. Sterile leaves 25–60 × 0.8–1 cm, flat, base plicate, blade smooth on both sides, margins slightly revolute and scabrid, basal sheaths split into dark brown fibers. Bracts short leafy, longer than subtending spikelets but less than 8 cm for lower spikelets, pale yellowish to pale greenish. Spikes 2–3, close together towards top of culm; male spike terminal, linearcylindrical, 3–3.5 cm × ca. 2 mm; female spikes lateral, oblong-cylindrical, 2.5–3 × ca. 1 cm, spikelets many and dense on the spikes, peduncle short 0.8–1 cm. Male glumes narrow-oblong to lanceolate, ca. 3.4 × 0.8 mm, apex acuminate, yellowish, midrib 3-veined. Female glumes lanceolate, 4.5–5.8 mm, apex acute, greenish yellow to pale yellow, margins scabrous, midrib raised. Utricles longer than the glume, obliquely patent, elliptic, 4–5 × 2.1–2.4 mm, thin papery, pale yellow to green, many-veined, base cuneate, upper part contracted into an erect cylindrical beak ca. 2.2 mm, orifice 2-toothed. Achenes 4.3–4.9 × 2.4–2.6 mm, tightly enveloped, pale yellow to yellowish brown, ovate-elliptic, trigonous, middle of achene excavated on the angles, base cuneate into a short and slightly curved stipe, upper part contract into a short curved beak ca. 1 mm, apex of beak annulate; stigmas 3.

Locality: Sunset Peak. S. C. Ng 2161, 3055.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Anhui, Zhejiang.
Ecology: Montane hillside open forests, alt. 500–900 m. Fruiting: Jan.–Apr.
Notes: A distinctive species characterised by its short inflorescence borne near or half-buried in the ground.

Cladium chinense Nees ex Hook. & Arn. 華克拉莎
Bot. Beech. Voy. 227. 1838; FRPS 11: 118. 1961.
Cladium jamaicence Crantz subsp. chinense (Nees) T. Koyama in H. Hara, Stearn & L. H. J. Williams, Enum. Fl. Pl. Nepal 1: 105. 1978; FOC 23: 258. 2010.
Cladium mariscus (L.) Pohl subsp. chinense (Nees) Govaerts, World Checkl. Seed Pl. 3(1): 15. 1999.
Mariscus chinensis (Nees) Fernald, Rhodora 25: 51. 1923.
Cladium mariscus (L.) Pohl subsp. jamaicense auct. non (Crantz) Kük.: FGD 8: 318. 2007; Check List HK Plants 309. 2002; 109. 2004.
Cladium jamaicense auct. non Crantz: FKH 302. 1912; FTW ed. 2, 5: 237. 2000.
Cladium mariscus auct. non R. Br.: FHK 397. 1861.

Perennial; rhizome thick, horizontal. Culm solitary, 1–3 m tall, terete, many-nodose, often bearing extra-vaginal shoot at lower nodes. Leaves cauline; blades elongate, broadly linear, flat, 60–90 × 0.8–1.5 cm, thickly leathery, gradually tapering above to 3-sided caudate apex, strongly serrulate-scabrous on margins; sheaths shorter than the internode. Inflorescence 30–90 cm, with terminal and lateral 5–9 anthelas, those rather contiguous or the lower ones spaced; bracts leafy, sheathing at base, the lower bract-blades much surpassing their subtending anthelas; anthelas 4–8 cm long and as broad, the peduncle and anthelas flattened. Spikelets congested in globose heads of 4–12, 4–9 mm in diam., the spikelets ovateelliptic to broadly so, 3 × 2 mm, rusty brown. Glumes 6–8, broadly ovate to ovate, 1–2.5 mm, abruptly contracted above to obtuse or subacute apex, the lower 4–6 empty, each of the apical 2 bearing a bisexual flower, the upper flower only producing achene. Stamens 2; anthers oblong, ca. 2 mm. Style slender; stigmas 3, pilose. Achene ovoid, ca. 2.5 mm, brown, rounded at base, apiculate.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. W. Lam 2168; S. P. Lau 48; HK sheet 33347.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Taiwan; Vietnam, Japan, Korea.
Ecology: Forests, streams and marshes. Flowering & fruiting: May–Jun.

Cyperus compressus L. 扁穗莎草
Sp. Pl. 1: 46. 1753; FKH 295. 1912; FRPS 11: 147. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 239. 2000; FGD 8: 330. 2007; FOC 23: 237. 2010.

Annual. Rhizome absent, roots fibrous. Culms tufted, 8–35(–50) cm tall, 1–2 mm thick, trigonous, smooth. Leaves basal; blade linear, 3–20 cm × 1–4 mm, acute, flat to channelled; sheath 1–7 cm, pale brown to reddish brown. Involucral bracts 2–5 cm, the longest up to 30 cm. Inflorescence simple to ± capitate, open to congested, 1.5–10 × 2–10 cm; primary branches (when present) 2–5, 0.8–15 cm; spikes solitary. Spikes ovate, 1.2–1.3 × 1.5–4 cm; axis 0.1– 0.5 cm. Spikelets 3–10 per spike, patent to spreading, often appearing finger-like, linear to oblong-lanceolate, 10–25 × 2.5–4 mm, flattened; axis zigzag. Glumes ovate, 3–4 × 2–2.7 mm, apex acute, mucronate, sides herbaceous or papery, 3-veined, pale green to pale golden brown, keel sharply acute, green. Stamens 3; anthers 0.7–1 mm. Stigmas 3. Achenes broadly obovoid, trigonous, 1–1.5 × 0.7–1 mm, dark brown, shiny, minutely punctate.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. J. C. Shaw & G Reels 75; Y. W. Lam 763; HK sheet 37111.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guizhou, Sichuan, Chongqing, Yunnan, Xizang, Gansu, Hebei, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Shandong, Shanxi, Liaoning, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; tropics.
Ecology: Wastelands. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Dec.

Cyperus cuspidatus Kunth 長尖莎草
Nov. Gen. Sp. (quarto ed.) 1: 204–205. 1815[1816]; FRPS 11: 155. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 240. 2000; FYN 15: 642. 2003; FGD 8: 331. 2007; FOC 23: 227. 2010.
Cyperus uncinatus auct. non Poir.: FKH 295. 1912.

Annual. Roots fibrous. Culms tufted, 3–15 cm tall, flaccid, trigonous, smooth, base with few leaves. Leaves shorter than culm; leaf blade 1–2 mm wide, usually folded. Involucral bracts 2–3, linear, longer than inflorescence. Inflorescences simple to capitate, 1.5 – 4 × 2.5 – 6 cm; primary branches 2–6, mostly to 2 cm. Spikelets 5– many, digitately arranged at a primary branches, linear, 5–15 × 2–3 mm, strongly flattened; axis straight, wingless. Glumes narrowly elliptic, 1–1.5 × 0.6–1 mm, emarginate, strongly recurvedmucronate, awn 0.5–1 mm, sides thinly papery, rusty brown to chestnut-brown, keel acute, 3-veined, greenish sometimes purplishlineolate. Stamens 2–3; anthers 0.2–0.3 mm. Style 0.3–0.6 mm; stigmas 3. Achenes obovoid to cylindrical-obovoid, trigonous, 0.5–0.6 × 0.3–0.4 mm, dark brown, minutely punctate.

Locality: Beacon Hill, Tai Mo Shan. S. P. Lau 24; HK sheet 7841, 13237.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Zhejiang, Jiangsu, Anhui, Jiangxi, Shandong, Fujian, Taiwan; pantropics.
Ecology: Open grasslands. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Sep.

Cyperus difformis L. 異型莎草
Cent. Pl. II 6. 1756; FHK 385. 1861; FKH 295. 1912; FRPS 11: 152. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 240. 2000; FYN 15: 642. 2003; FGD 8: 332. 2007; FOC 23: 226. 2010.

Annual. Rhizome absent; roots fibrous. Culms tufted, (10–)25–60 cm tall, 2–5 mm thick, sharply triquetrous, sides concave. Leaves slightly shorter than culm; blade linear, 2–22 × 2–6 mm, acute, folded, sheath 2–10 mm, pale or yellowish brown to pinkish. Involucral bracts 2–3, unequal, the longest up to 25 cm. Inflorescence simple, open, occasionally congested; primary branches 3–9, 1–4 cm. Spikelets many, in congested globose clusters, 2–6 × 2–6 mm, linear to linear-oblong, 2–8 × 1–1.3 mm, flattened; axis straight. Glumes ± orbicular, 0.5–0.8 × 0.4–0.8 mm, apex rounded or shallowly emarginate, sides membranous, faintly 3-veined, deep green tinged with brownish purple, margins white hyaline, keel yellowish. Stamens 1–2; anthers 0.1 mm. Style short, stigmas 3. Achenes ellipsoidal-obovoid, trigonous, 0.5–0.7 × 0.3 mm, maturing yellowish.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. J. C. Shaw 155; Y. S. Lau 2489; Y. W. Lam 1585.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; tropical and subtropical regions of the Old World.
Ecology: Wet grasslands and along streams. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Dec.

Cyperus diffusus Vahl 多脈莎草（綠穗莎草）
Enum. Pl. 2: 321. 1805; FHK 295. 1912; FRPS 11: 148. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 248. 2000.
Cyperus laxus Lam.: FGD 8: 331. 2007.

Perennial. Rhizomatous short. Culms ± tufted, 30–80 cm tall, 3–5 mm thick, trigonous to subtriquetrous, smooth. Leaf blades linear, 8–48 × 0.3–2 cm, abruptly acute, flattish, sheath 4–10 cm, pale green to rusty or purplish brown. Involucral bracts 4–12, unequal, the longest up to 50 cm. Inflorescence simple to decompound, open to rather dense, 6 20 × 7–30 cm; primary branches 10 – 20 or more, 2.5 – 20 cm; secondary and tertiary branches 0.5–4 cm. Spikelets in open finger-like clusters of (1–)2–9, oblong, subterete, 3–10 × 1.5–3 mm; axis straight. Glumes 6–20 per spikelet, ovate-orbicular, 1.5–2 × 1.5–2 mm, obtuse, recurved-mucronate, awn 0.2–0.5 mm, sides thinly herbaceous, indistinctly to prominently 7–11-veined, greenish tinged with pale or reddish brown, keel acute to subobtuse, greenish. Stamens 3; anthers 0.8–1 mm. Stigmas 3. Achenes elliptic, trigonous, 1.2–1.5 × 0.7–0.8 mm, blackish brown, indistinctly minutely punctate.

Locality: Ng Tung Chai, Tai Po. Y. W. Lam 1309, 1311, 2086.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan, Xizang, Yunnan, Taiwan; Nepal, Bhutan, Sri Lanka, India, Myanmar, Laos, Thailand, Cambodia, Vietnam, Malaysia, Indonesia, Philippines, Australia, Indian Ocean islands, Pacific islands.
Ecology: Forests of valleys and wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Oct.

Cyperus distans L. f. 疏穗莎草
Suppl. Pl. 103. 1781; FHK 387. 1861; FKH 295. 1912; FRPS 11: 138. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 242. 2000; FYN 15: 631. 2003; FGD 8: 329. 2007; FOC 23: 233. 2010.

Perennial. Rhizome short, woody. Culms 1–few, 20–100 cm tall, 2–5 mm thick, triquetrous, smooth, thicked at base. Leaves basal, shorter than culm; blade linear, up to 100 cm × 4–10 mm, acuminate, weakly folded; sheath 5–20 cm, light brown to purple brown. Involucral bracts 4–6, the longest 20–60 cm. Inflorescence simple, rarely compound, open, 9–28 × 9–27 cm; primary branches 5–12, 3–17 cm; secondary branches 0.5–3 cm. Spikes broadly ovoid-pyramidal, 4–6 × 3–5 cm; axis 0.2–0.3 cm. Spikelets 8–20 per spike, mostly spreading, rather distant, linear, 8–40 × 0.8–1 mm, subterete; axis zigzag, winged, visible between glumes. Glumes 9 or more on the longest spikelets, rather distant, elliptic or oblong-ovate, 1.8–2 × 1–1.2 mm, apex obtuse to rounded-obtuse, sides membranous, 3–5-veined below keel, light to dark reddish brown, margins narrowly hyaline around apex, keel greenish. Stamens 3; anthers 0.5–0.7 mm. Stigmas 3. Achenes cylindrical to cylindrical-ellipsoidal, trigonous, 1.5–1.8 × 0.3–0.5 mm, dark brown, minutely punctate.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 2256; Y. W. Lam 328, 761.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Taiwan; Nepal, Sikkim, Bhutan, Sri Lanka, India, Myanmar, Cambodia, Laos, Thailand, Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Papua New Guinea, Vietnam, Africa, Australia, America.
Ecology: Paddy fields and other wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Aug.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Stonecutters Island, Port Shelter, New Territories
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Cyperus eleusinoides Kunth 穇穗莎草
Enum. Pl. 2: 39. 1837; FKH 296. 1912; FRPS 11: 139. 1961; FYN 15: 631. 2003; FGD 8: 325. 2007; FOC 23: 233. 2010.
Cyperus nutans Vahl subsp. eleusinoides (Kunth) T. Koyama, Gard. Bull. Singapore 30: 136. 1977.
Cyperus nutans Vahl var. eleusinoides (Kunth) R.W. Haines, Bot. Bihar Orissa 5: 898. 1924.

Perennial; rhizome short, surculose. Culms stout, to 1 m tall, trigonous, smooth, base swollen, tuber-shaped, with leaves at basal part. Leaves shorter than culm; leaf blade 6–12 mm wide, flat, margin scabrous; sheath long, brown. Bracts 5–6, basal 2–3 longer than inflorescence. Anthelas compound or decompound, 6–12, to 18 cm, each with 3–6 anthelalets; anthelalets mostly to 4 cm, unequal in length. Spikes oblong to cylindrical, 1–3 cm × 4–10 mm, with very many spikelets, suberect. Spikelets polystichous, densely arranged, linear-oblong, 4–8 × ca. 2 mm, 6  2-flowered; rachilla winged, wings white hyaline, early deciduous. Glumes lax, ovate-elliptic, ca. 2 mm, pale and brown striate or brown, apex mucronate, membranous, apical margin white hyaline, veins 5–7, keel green. Stamens 3; anthers linear; connective prominent above anther. Style short; stigmas 3. Achene obovoid, trigonous, ca. 2/3 as long as scale, dark brown, surface densely and slightly prominently punctate.

Locality: Stonecutters Island, Port Shelter, New Territories. S. L. Thrower 1289 (CUHK).
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Yunnan, Taiwan; tropical Asia and Africa, Australia.
Ecology: Ravines. Flowering & fruiting: May–Oct.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Castle Peak, Hong Kong Wetland Park
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Cyperus exaltatus Retz. 高稈莎草
Observ. Bot. 5: 11. 1789; FKH 296. 1912; FRPS 11: 130. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 242. 2000; FGD 8: 324. 2007; FOC 23: 230. 2010.

Rhizomatous perennial. Culms tufted, 60–180 cm tall, 6–10 mm thick, trigonous, smooth. Leaves basal; blade linear, up to 170 cm × 6–15 mm, acuminate, flattish-plicate; sheath purplebrown. Involucral bracts 4–6, the longest up to 70 cm. Inflorescence simple to compound, 15–27 × 17–30 cm; primary branches 5–9, 3–18 cm; secondary branches 0.5–5 cm, or spikes ± sessile clusters. Spikes erect-patent to patent, narrowly to broadly cylindrical, 2 – 5 × 0.7–1.5 cm; axis 1.5–4.8 cm. Spikelets 20–40, crowded, erect-patent to patent ± 2-ranked, oblong-lanceolate to linear, 4–10 × 1–2 mm, flattened; axis straight, winged. Glumes 9 or more on the longest spikelets, ovate to broadly ovate, 1.5–2 × 1.2–1.5 mm, acute, mucronate, sides membranous, 3–5-veined, greenish to yellowish brown, keel pale to mid-brown. Stamens 3; anthers 0.5–0.7 mm, connective minute. Stigmas 3. Achenes ellipsoidal to ellipsoidal-obovoid, trigonous, 0.7–0.8 × 0.3–0.5 mm, yellowish brown, minutely punctate.

Locality: Castle Peak, Hong Kong Wetland Park. Y. S. Lau 2275; S. C. Ng 986; HK sheet 40461.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam, India, Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Australia, Africa.
Ecology: Wet places and marshes. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Aug.

Cyperus haspan L. 畦畔莎草
Sp. Pl. 1: 45. 1753; FHK 386. 1861; FKH 295. 1912; FRPS 11: 153. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 244. 2000; FYN 15: 639. 2003; FGD 8: 332. 2007; FOC 23: 227. 2010.

Annual or short-lived perennial; rhizome short to slightly long. Culms tufted or solitary, 10–40 cm tall, 0.5–2.2 mm thick, rather weak, sharply triquetrous, smooth. Leaves shorter than culm; blade linear, 2–20 cm × 2–5 mm, acute, flattish-plicate; sheath up to 6 cm, reddish purple to purplish. Involucral bracts 2–3, unequal, the longest up to 10 cm. Inflorescence simple to decompound, open to somewhat congested, 3–15 × 3–15 cm; primary branches 10–22, 1.2–10(–20) cm × 0.2–0.7 mm; secondary and tertiary branches 1–2.5 cm or 0. Spikelets 1 or in finger-like clusters of 3–6(–10), linear-oblong or linear-lanceolate, 5–10 × 1–2 mm, flattened; axis straight. Glumes ± oblong to elliptic-lanceolate or ovate, (1–)1.1–1.5 × 0.5–0.7 mm, at apex obtuse or mucronulate, straight to slightly recurved, sides membranous, pale brownish and often tinged with rusty brown or purplish brown, keel greenish or pale brown, 3-veined. Stamens 1–3; anthers narrowly oblong, ca. 0.5 mm, connective hispidulous. Style short, stigmas 3. Achenes broadly obovoid, trigonous, sides ± flat, 0.4–0.5 × 0.4–0.5 mm, creamy yellow, verruculose.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. J. C. Shaw 159; HK sheet 38161, 42177.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Henan, Hunan, Hubei, Anhui, Jiangxi, Jiangsu, Fujian, Zhejiang, Taiwan; tropical and subtropical regions.
Ecology: Wet places and paddy fields. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Oct.

Cyperus imbricatus Retz. 疊穗莎草
Observ. Bot. 5: 12. 1788; FRPS 11: 131. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 244. 2000; FGD 8: 325. 2007; FOC 23: 231. 2010.

Perennial. Rhizome short. Culms 37–130 cm tall, 2–8 mm thick, indistinctly to distinctly trigonous, smooth. Leaves basal; blade narrowly linear, up to 60 × 5–15 cm, acuminate, flattish; sheath dark brown or reddish brown. Involucral bracts 3–5, the longest up to 60 cm. Inflorescence simple, rarely compound, 8–22 × 10–25 cm; primary branches 5–8, up to 15 cm; secondary branches 1–2 cm, spikes more usually in ± sessile clusters. Spikes erect-patent to patent, narrowly cylindrical, 1.5–4 × 0.3–0.9 cm, pale yellowish brown, axis 1.5–5 cm, winged, usually obscured by spikelets. Spikelets 50–70 or more, densely imbricate, suberect, lanceolate to linear-oblong, 3–6 × 1–2 mm, flattened; axis straight. Glumes 9 or more, in longest spikelets, ovate to ovate-oval, 1.2–1.8 × 1 mm, obtuse, recurved mucronate, sides membranous, 3-veined, yellowish brown, keel greenish. Stamens 3; anthers 0.3 mm, connective minute. Stigmas 3. Achenes ellipsoidal to ± ovoid, trigonous, 0.6–0.8 × 0.4 mm, slightly obcompressed, yellowish.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 2215; HK sheet 37122; 39386.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan, Taiwan; Japan, Vietnam, India, Nepal, Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Myanmar, Laos, Thailand, Vietnam, Malaysia, Papua New Guinea, Philippines, Madagascar, Africa, America, SW Asia, Indian Ocean islands.
Ecology: Wet places and paddy fields. Flowering & fruiting: Sep.–Oct.

Cyperus involucratus Rottb. 風車草
Descr. Pl. Rar. 22. 1772; FGD 8: 330. 2007.
Cyperus alternifolius L. subsp. flabelliformis (Rottb.) Kük., Pflnanzenr. 4 (20, heft 101): 193. 1936; FRPS 11: 148. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 239. 2000; FYN 15: 637. 2003.

Perennial. Rhizome white, short, thick. Culms tufted, 0.5–1.8 cm tall, 3–10 mm thick, trigonous to ± terete at base, scabrous below inflorescence. Leaves bladeless, reduced to sheaths; sheaths 10–20 cm, pale greenish to yellow brown, apex obliquely truncate. Involucral bracts 15 or more, ± equal, 20–50 × 0.5–1.5 cm. Inflorescence simple to compound, 9–12 × 15–30 cm; primary branches many, ± equal, 7–10 cm, patent; secondary branches 1–1.5 cm. Spikelets in clusters of 3–10, oblonglanceolate to elliptic, flattened, 3–8 × 1.5–3 mm, densely 8–36-flowered, light green to rusty brown, the midrib green, axis straight. Glumes ovate, 1.8–2 × 1.2–1.5 mm, acute, sides membranous, 3–5-veined, pale green sometimes tinged with rusty brown, keel acute, greenish to pale brown. Stamens 3, anther linear, yellow, ca. 1 mm. Ovary trigonous, 0.5 mm; style ca. 1 mm, stigmas 3, ca. 1 mm. Achenes trigonous, broadly elliptic, ca. 0.5 mm wide, brown, reticulate-tuberculate, cell margin wavy; wave raised.

Locality: Cultivated or naturalized. H. C. Tang 2346; J. C. Shaw 895; HK sheet 32811.
Distribution: Cultivated in Guangdong, Hunan, Taiwan; native to Africa.
Ecology: Cultivated in gardens. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Aug.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: The species was reported as Cyperus flabelliformis Rottb. previously (Check List HK Plants 309. 2002; 109. 2004).

Cyperus iria L. 碎米莎草
Sp. Pl. 1: 45. 1753; FHK 386. 1861; FKH 295. 1912; FRPS 11: 143. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 245. 2000; FYN 15: 635. 2003; FGD 8: 329. 2007; FOC 23: 235. 2010.

Annual. Rhizome absent, roots fibrous. Culms 1–several, 8–60 cm tall, 2–3(–5) mm thick, triquetrous, smooth. Leaves 2–3 per culm; blade linear, 4–18 cm × 2–6 mm, flattish to weakly channelled; sheath 2–10 mm, reddish to purplish brown. Involucral bracts 3–5, the longest up to 40 cm. Inflorescence simple to compound, open, 5–20 × 3–15 cm; primary branches 3–7, 2–12(–15) cm; secondary branches very short or 0, the spikes in clusters of 3–5. Spikes broadly ovoid to oblong-ovate or linear-oblong, 1–5 × 0.2–0.7 cm; axis 1–2.5 cm. Spikelets spicately arranged, erectpatent, oblong-elliptic to linear-oblong, 9–13 × 1.6–2 mm, flattened; axis straight. Glumes obovate-orbicular, 0.7–1.3 × 1–1.5 mm, rounded to shallowly emarginate, mucronulate, sides thinly herbaceous, 3–5-veined, greenish to yellowish or midbrown, margins whitish-hyaline above, keel acute, green. Stamens 2–3; anthers 0.2–0.3 mm. Stigmas 3. Achenes ellipsoidal to obovoid, trigonous, 1–1.5 × 0.5–0.8 mm, dark brown, minutely punctate.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1965; J. C. Shaw 507; K. L. Yip 4196.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; Russia, Korea, Japan, Vietnam, India, Iran, N Australia, Africa.
Ecology: Wet places and paddy fields. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Oct.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Yuen Long, Castle Peak, Sha Po Tsuen, Lung Kwu Tan, Silver Mine Bay
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Cyperus malaccensis Lam. 茳芏
Tabl. Encycl. 1: 146. 1791; FKH 295. 1912; FRPS 11: 141. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 245. 2000; FGD 8: 327. 2007; FOC 23: 234. 2010.

Perennial; rhizome long-creeping. Culms 1–few, 60–180 cm tall, 7–12(–15) mm thick, smooth, sharply triquetrous. Leaves reduced to bladeless sheaths except for upper 1–3 leaves; blade linear, linear-lanceolate, 5–25 cm × 3–16 mm, acute or shortly acuminate, ± flattened; sheath 8–20 cm, greenish to reddish brown. Involucral bracts 3–4, the longest up to 30 cm × 8–15 mm. Inflorescence simple to compound, somewhat congested, subglobose, 2–10 × 4–15 cm; primary branches 3–8, unequal, 3–10 cm; secondary branches 0.3–1.6 cm. Spikes ovoid, 1–2.5 cm; axis 0.2–1 cm, smooth, glabrous. Spikelets 2–15 per spike, linear, 10–13 × 1.2–1.8 mm, subterete; axis straight. Glumes 9 or more on the longest spikelets, elliptic to ovate, 2–2.2 × 1–1.5 mm, obtuse, sides papery, indistinctly 5–7-veined around keel, glaucous and tinged or flecked with brown or dark reddish, the margins widely pale-membranous, keel rounded, brownish. Stamens 3; anthers 0.8–1 mm. Stigmas 3. Achenes cylindrical, trigonous, 1.7–2 × 0.5 mm, blackish brown, minutely punctate.

Locality: Yuen Long, Castle Peak, Sha Po Tsuen, Lung Kwu Tan, Silver Mine Bay. Y. W. Lam 1590; HK sheet 39092, 39650.
Distribution: Guangdong, Hainan, Taiwan; Sri Lanka, India, Nepal, Myanmar, Thailand, Vietnam, Malaysia, Indonesia, Philippines, Papua New Guinea, Japan, Australia.
Ecology: Ditches or muddy places near estuary. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Nov.
Uses: Weaving.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Cape D'Aguilar, Sha Tin, Castle Peak, Mai Po, Sai Kung, Nai Chung, Sam A Tsuen, Yung Shue O, Silver Mine Bay
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Cyperus malaccensis Lam. var. brevifolius Boeck. 短葉茳芏（鹹水草）
Linnaea 35: 604. 1867; FRPS 11: 141. 1961.
Cyperus malaccensis Lam. subsp. monophyllus (Vahl) T. Koyama, FTW ed. 2, 5: 246. 2000; FOC 23: 234. 2010.
Cyperus monophyllus Vahl, Enum. Pl. 2: 352. 1806.
Cyperus tegetiformis auct. non Roxb.: FKH 296. 1912.

Leaves blade short to very short, sometimes basalmost sheath bladeless. Involucral bracts shorter than inflorescence. Glumes not incurved.

Locality: Cape D'Aguilar, Sha Tin, Castle Peak, Mai Po, Sai Kung, Nai Chung, Sam A Tsuen, Yung Shue O, Silver Mine Bay. J. C. Shaw 672; Y. S. Lau 1995; Y. W. Lam 682.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Sichuan, Jiangxi, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Vietnam, Indonesia.
Ecology: Wet places near streams. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Nov.
Uses: Ties, strings (clums).

Cyperus nutans Vahl 垂穗莎草
Enum. Pl. 2: 363. 1805; FRPS 11: 138. 1961; FYN 15: 631. 2003; FGD 8: 325. 2007; FOC 23: 233. 2010.

Perennial; rhizome short. Culms 1–few, 70–120(–150) cm tall, 4–10 mm thick, trigonous to triquetrous above, smooth. Leaves basal; blade linear, 20–40 cm × 6–15 mm, acute, flattish-plicate, whitish below; sheath 10–30 cm, greenish to reddish brown. Involucral bracts 4–6, the longest 50–75 cm. Inflorescence simple, rarely compound, lax, 15–30 × 8–20 cm; primary branches 6–12, erect-patent, up to 30 cm; secondary branches 0.3 – 3.5 cm. Spikes subsessile, 6 × 1 cm, radically spreading. Spikelets 1.5–2 mm wide. Glumes up to 2.2 mm, more conspicuously mucronate, tinged with glaucous green. Stamens 3; anthers linear-oblong. Style very short; stigmas 3. Achenes obovate to broadly elliptic, 1–1.2 × 0.5–0.7 mm, rather abruptly narrowed to apiculate apex.

Locality: Tai Shui Hang. HK sheet 13120, 13122.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hunan, Yunnan, Sichuan, Taiwan; Vietnam, Laos, Thailand, Sri Lanka, India, Nepal, Bhutan, Philippines, Indonesia, Malaysia, Papua New Guinea, Australia, Africa.
Ecology: Ravines. Flowering & fruiting: May–Oct.
Notes: The species was reported as Cyperus nutans Vahl var. eleusinoides (Kunth) Haines previously (Check List HK Plants 88. 1993).

Cyperus orthostachyus Franch. & Sav. 三輪草
Enum. Pl. Jap. 218. 1879; FRPS 11: 145. 1961; FOC 23: 236. 2010.
Cyperus truncatus Turcz. ex Ledeb. var. orthostachyus (Franch. & Sav.) C. B. Clarke, J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 36: 218. 1903.

Annual, rhizome absent, with only fibrous roots. Culms slender, 8–65 cm tall, compressed triquetrous, smooth, with few leaves at basal part. Leaves shorter than or equalling culm; sheath brownish; leaf blade 3–6 mm wide, flat, margin scabrous. Bracts 3–4, leaf-shaped, very much longer than inflorescence or basalmost 1–2 longer than inflorescence, margin scabrous. Anthela simple, rarely compound; anthelas 5–11, mostly to 15(–20) cm, unequal in length, each with 1(–5) spike. Spikes ovate-oblong, broadly ovate, or oblong cylindrical in outline, 1–3.5 × 1–3 cm, with 5–32 or many spikelets. Spikelets slightly laxly or densely arranged, lanceolate to linear, 0.3–2.5 cm × 1–2 mm, obliquely spreading or suberect, sometimes level spreading after anthesis, 6–46-flowered; rachilla wings white, narrow, hyaline; glumes greyish brown, broadly ovate to elliptic, ca. 1.5 mm, membranous, keel abaxially green, veins 5–7 and obscure, margin apically white hyaline, apex rounded to retuse and muticous. Stamens 3; anthers ellipsoidal, short; connective prominent above anther. Style short; stigmas 3, slightly short. Achene brown, obovoid, nearly as long as scale, trigonous, surface puncticulate, apex mucronate.

Locality: Yuen Long. Y. W. Lam 1341.
Distribution: Chongqing, Hunan, Hubei, Guizhou, Anhui, Fujian, Jiangxi, Jiangsu, Shaanxi, Shandong, Zhejiang, Liaoning, Jilin, Heilongjiang; Japan, Korea, Russia, Vietnam.
Ecology: Cultivated. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Aug.
Uses: Ornamental.

Cyperus papyrus L. 紙莎草
Sp. Pl. 47. 1753.

Perennial. Rhizome short, woody. Culms 1–5 m tall, 2–4 cm thick, trigonous, smooth. Leaves reduced to bladeless sheaths. Involucral bracts up to 12, the longest 5–10 cm. Inflorescence simple to compound, 20–35 cm in diam.; primary branches many (up to 200 or more), ± equal, 10–30 cm; secondary branches up to 2 cm, spikes more usually in sessile clusters. Spikes cylindrical, 1–3 × 0.6–1 cm; axis 1.5–3 cm. Spikelets spreading, linear, 6–12 × 1 mm, subterete; axis straight, winged. Glumes 5–17 per spikelet, elliptic to ovateelliptic, 2–2.5 mm, obtuse, sides membranous, 3-veined below keel, light brownish, keel green. Stamens 3. Stigmas 3. Achenes ovoid, trigonous, 0.9–11 × 0.4–0.5 mm, greyish, smooth.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 42173.
Distribution: Native to tropical Africa.
Ecology: Cultivated in ponds or wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Aug.
Uses: Ornamental, paper making.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Mo Shan, Castle Peak, Sheung Miu Tin, Tung Chung, Shui Hau
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Cyperus pilosus Vahl 毛軸莎草
Enum. Pl. 2: 354. 1805; FHK 387. 1861; FKH 295. 1912; FRPS 11: 141. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 248. 2000; FYN 15: 633. 2003; FGD 8: 326. 2007; FOC 23: 234. 2010.

Perennial. Rhizome with long stolons. Culms 1–few, 25–28(–120) cm tall, 5–8 mm thick, sharply triquetrous, smooth or scabrid on angles below inflorescence. Leaves few to several per culm; blade broadly linear, 13–47 cm × 6–13 mm, acute, flattish to plicate; sheath 3–10 cm, pale greenish to purplish brown. Involucral bracts 3–5, the longest up to 50 cm. Inflorescence simple to compound, open to rather congested; primary branches 4–7(–10), 12–14(–20) cm; secondary branches 0.5–2 cm or spikes in ± sessile clusters. Spikes ± oblong, 2–3 × 1–2 cm; axis 1.5–3 cm, densely shortly hispid. Spikelets 5–25 per spike, rather distant, spreading, linearlanceolate to elliptic-oblong, 4–15 × 1–2 mm, flattened to subterete; axis straight. Glumes 5–9 or more on the longest spikelets, ovate to broadly deltoid-ovate, 1.8–2.5 × 1.2–1.5 mm, acute, often mucronulate, sides thinly papery to membranous, 5–7-veined, pale brown tinged with reddish brown, margins whitish-hyaline, keel obtuse, green, smooth. Stamens 3; anthers 0.5–0.8 mm. Stigmas 3. Achenes broadly ellipsoidal to obovoid, trigonous, 1–1.5 × 0.5–0.8 mm, maturing dark brown, ± smooth.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Castle Peak, Sheung Miu Tin, Tung Chung, Shui Hau. Y. W. Lam 2231; J. C. Shaw & G. Reels 163; HK sheet 39642.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Chongqing, Hunan, Hubei, Shaanxi, Xizang, Jiangxi, Jiangsu, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, C Asia, tropical Asia, Australia.
Ecology: Marshes, paddy fields and other wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Nov.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong. (fide H. G. Ye & S. L. Peng (eds.), Plant Div. Inventory of Guangdong 583. 2006)
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Cyperus platystylis R. Br. 盤柱莎草
Prodr. 214. 1810; FTW ed. 2, 5: 248. 2000; FOC 23: 224. 2010.

Perennial. Rhizome short. Culms 1–3, 30–90(–120) cm tall, 3–8 mm thick, triquetrous, scabrid on angles. Leaves ± equalling culm; blade linear, up to 90 cm × 5–12(–20) mm, long-acuminate, flattish-plicate, sheath light brown to purplish brown, Involucral bracts 4–12, unequal, the longest 30 – 80 cm. Inflorescence simple to compound, 7–20(–30) × 4–10 cm; primary branches 10–17, unequal, 2–10 cm; secondary branches up to 4 cm, arising along a short axis. Spikelets in finger-like clusters of 2–8, oblong-lanceolate to lanceolate, 5–20 × 2.5–3 mm, flattened; axis straight. Glumes ovate to broadly ovate, 2–2.5 × 1.5–2 mm, subobtuse, mucronate, sides thickly membranous to herbaceous, greenish to brown. Stamens 3; anthers 1 mm. Stigmas 3. Achenes cylindrical-ellipsoidal or cylindrical-ovoid, trigonous, laterally compressed, adaxial side concave, 1.7–2 × 0.8–1 mm, mid-brown with broad pale brown thickening on angles and apex, shiny, ± smooth.

Locality: Hong Kong. (fide H. G. Ye & S. L. Peng (eds.), Plant Div. Inventory of Guangdong 583. 2006)
Distribution: Taiwan; India, Sri Lanka, Malaysia, Australia.
Ecology: Marshes and paddy fields. Flowering & fruiting: Mar.–Oct.

Cyperus procerus Rottb. 闊穗莎草
Descr. Icon. Rar. Pl. 29, t. 5, fig. 3. 1773; FKH 296. 1912; FTW ed. 2, 5: 248. 2000; FGD 8: 326. 2007; FOC 23: 235. 2010.

Perennial. Rhizome with long stolons. Culms 1–few, 50–100(–150) cm tall, 4–7(–10) mm thick, smooth, triquetrous. Leaves surpassing culm; blade linear, up to 60–150 cm × 7–10(–15) mm, long-acute, often subtriquetrous toward apex, canaliculate; sheath 8–28 cm, pale greenish to purplish brown. Involucral bracts 3 – 4, the longest 20 – 70 cm. Inflorescence simple to compound, rather open, 10–15 cm × 8–12 cm; primary branches 3–7, 6–15(–20) cm; secondary branches up to 2 cm or spikes sometimes solitary. Spikes broadly ovoid, 2–4 cm; axis 2–3 cm, scabrid. Spikelets 4–8 per spike, rather distant, patent to spreading, oblong to linearlanceolate, 5–18 × 2.5–3.5 mm, flattened; axis straight. Glumes 9 or more on the longest spikelets, oval or ovate, 2.5–3 × 2–2.2 mm, sides membranous, 5–7-veined, pale brown to reddish brown, margins broadly white-hyaline near apex, keel obtuse, reddish brown, smooth. Stamens 3; anthers 1.2–1.8 mm. Stigmas 3. Achenes ellipsoidal, trigonous, 1.3–1.5 × 0.6–0.8 mm, maturing dark brown, ± smooth.

Locality: Yung Shue Au. S. C. Ng 4488.
Distribution: S & SW China; India, Vietnam, Malaysia, Australia, Africa.
Ecology: Wet places near water. Flowering & fruiting: Mar.–Oct.

Cyperus pygmaeus Rottb. 矮莎草
Descr. Icon. Rar. Pl. 20, pl. 14, fig. 4 – 5. 1773; FRPS 11: 157. 1961; FGD 8: 334. 2007; FOC 23: 228. 2010.

Annual. Rhizome absent, with fibrous roots. Culms tufted, 12–18 cm tall, compressed triquetrous, slightly concave on 3 sides, few leaved basally. Leaves shorter than culm; sheath reddish brown, short; leaf blade 2–2.5 mm wide, flat, apical margin and abaxially midvein spinulose. Involucral bracts 4–7, leaf-like, longer than inflorescence, ± horizontal to sometimes downwards reflexed. Inflorescences capitate, with many spikelets. Spikelets densely aggregated, narrowly oblong-ovoid to suboblong, 4–5 × ca. 1.5 mm, 10–15-flowered. Glumes distichous, oblong-lanceolate, ca. 2 mm, yellowish white but medially rust brown and shortly striate, 3-veined, midvein green and apically forming a slight keel, apex acute and excurved mucronate. Stamen usually 1; anther short, linear; connective slightly prominent beyond anthers. Style short; stigmas 2(–3), longer than style. Achene oblong, 1–1.2 mm, 2/3–3/4 as long as subtending glume, lenticular with one flat and one convex side, minutely papillose.

Locality: Chek Keng. HK sheet 42208.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hubei, Henan, Anhui, Zhejiang, Taiwan; Mediterranean and E Africa through W Asia and India to SE Asia, Malesia and Australia.
Ecology: Margins of ponds, wet places in sand.

Cyperus rotundus L. 香附子
Sp. Pl. 1: 45. 1753; FHK 387. 1861; FKH 296. 1912; FRPS 11: 134. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 250. 2000; FYN 15: 627. 2003; FGD 8: 328. 2007; FOC 23: 232. 2010.

Perennial. Rhizome with stolons, terminated by a globose-ovoid tuber. Culms tuberous at base, 10–60 cm tall, 1–2 mm thick, triquetrous, smooth. Leaves few, shorter than culm; blade linear, up to 60 cm × 2–5 mm, acuminate, flattish; sheath pale brown. Involucral bracts 2–3(–5), the longest usually equalling or shorter than inflorescence, 2–35 cm. Inflorescence simple, rarely compound, 3–8(–15) × 2–5(–10) cm; primary branches 2–10, 1–8(–12) cm; secondary branches (when present), 0.7–2 cm, spikes usually solitary. Spikes obovoid, 1.5–5 cm; axis 0.2–0.8 cm. Spikelets 3–10 per spike, suberect to patent, narrowly oblong to linear, 10–30 × 1.5–3 mm, flattened; axis ± straight, winged. Glumes 9 or more on the longest spikelets, ovate or ovate-elliptic, 3–3.5 × 2 mm, obtuse, mucronate, ± recurved, sides membranous, 5–7-veined, reddish or slightly purplish brown with pale narrow hyaline margins, keel greenish. Stamens 3; anthers 1 mm. Stigmas 3. Achenes cylindrical to obovoid-cylindrical, trigonous, 1.3–1.5 × 0.5–0.7 mm, brown, minutely punctate.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 2229; J. C. Shaw 432; HK sheet 37085.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Gansu, Shaanxi, Shanxi, Hebei, Henan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Shandong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; widely distributed in temperate regions.
Ecology: Wastelands. Flowering & fruiting: May–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Sai Kung, Castle Peak, Lamma Island, Lautau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Cyperus stoloniferus Retz. 粗根莖莎草
Observ. Bot. 4: 10. 1786; FKH 296. 1912; FRPS 11: 134. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 251. 2000; FGD 8: 328. 2007; FOC 23: 231. 2010.

Perennial. Rhizome long, thick, woody, base of shoot with ellipsoidal to ovoid tubers. Culms 1–2, 8–40 cm tall, 0.7–3 mm thick, trigonous, smooth, base swollen. Leaves usually shorter than culm; blade linear, up to 50 cm × 2–4 mm, acuminate, flattish to canaliculate; sheath pale brown, becoming fibrous. Involucral bracts 2–3, the longest 10–30 cm. Inflorescence simple, often congested, up to 6 × 6 cm; primary branches 2–5, 0.5–6 cm, spikes solitary. Spikes obovoid, 1.5–2.5 cm; axis 0.3 – 0.5 cm. Spikelets 3 – 8 per spike, suberect to patent, linear oblong to oblong-lanceolate, 6–15 × 1.5–2 mm, often weakly curved; axis slightly zigzag, winged. Glumes 9 or more on the longest spikelets, broadly ovate, 2.2–2.7 × 2–2.3 mm, obtuse, mucronate, sides thickly membranous, 5–7-veined, pale brown to dark reddish brown, keel pale green. Stamens 3; anthers 1.5–2 mm. Stigmas 3. Achenes ovoid, trigonous, 1–1.5 × 1 mm, dark brown, minutely punctate.

Locality: Sai Kung, Castle Peak, Lamma Island, Lautau Island. J. C. Shaw 537; HK sheet 39434, 40719.
Distribution: Guangdong, Hainan, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Vietnam, Laos, Cambodia, Thailand, Myanmar, India, Pakistan, Malaysia, Indonesia, Philippines, Papua New Guinea, Australia, Madagascar, Indian Ocean islands, Pacific islands.
Ecology: Sandy beaches and mudflats. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Aug.

Cyperus tenuiculmis Bóeck. 四棱穗莎草（棱穗莎草）
Linnaea 30: 286. 1870; FTW ed. 2, 5: 251. 2000; FYN 15: 629. 2003; FGD 8: 328. 2007; FOC 23: 233. 2010.
Cyperus zollingeri auct. non Steud.: FKH 296. 1912; FRPS 11: 137. 1961; Check List HK Plants 311. 2002; 110. 2004.

Perennial; rhizome short. Culms 1–few, 35–70(–90) cm tall, 1–2 mm thick, triquetrous, smooth. Leaf blades narrowly linear, 9–28 × 0.2–0.6 cm, sharply acute, folded; sheath 2–16 cm, light brown. Involucral 2–7, the longest up to 20 cm. Inflorescence simple, lax, occasionally congested, up to 15 cm; primary branches 2–8, 1–16 cm; spikes solitary. Spikes ovoid, up to 5 cm; axis 0.5–1.3 cm. Spikelets 7–14 per spike, suberect to patent, often appearing ± finger-like, linear to linear-lanceolate, 10–30 × 1.5–2 mm, slightly flattened; axis zigzag, winged. Glumes 9 or more on the longest spikelets, ovate-elliptic to elliptic, 3.5–4 × 2–2.5 mm, apex obtuse to ± acute, sides papery, 7–9-veined, yellow brown to mid-brown, keel similar. Stamens 3; anthers 1–1.5 mm long. Stigmas 3. Achenes elliptic or obovate, triquetrous with concave sides, 1.7–2 × 0.8–1 mm, maturing blackish, minutely punctate.

Locality: Hong Kong.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Sichuan, Yunnan, Fujian, Zhejiang, Taiwan; Nepal, Sikkim, Bhutan, Sri Lanka, India, Myanmar, Cambodia, Thailand, Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Papua New Guinea, Vietnam, Africa, Australia, America.
Ecology: Hillslopes, wastelands. Flowering & fruiting: May–Nov.
Notes: C. zollingeri Steud. is closely related and occurs in Peninsula Malaysia.

Cyperus tenuispica Steud. 窄穗莎草
Syn. Pl. Glumac. 2: 11. 1854; FRPS 11: 153. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 253. 2000; FGD 8: 332. 2007; FOC 23: 227. 2010. Cyperus flavidus C. B. Clarke, J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 20: 287. 1883.

Annual or rarely short-lived perennial. Culms tufted, (3–)5–35 cm tall, 1–2 mm thick, triquetrous, smooth. Leaves shorter than culm; blade linear, up to 20 cm × 2–4 mm, acute, flat, soft; sheath up to 5 cm long, reddish brown to purplish brown. Involucral bracts 1–3, unequal, the longest up to 20 cm. Inflorescence simple to compound, open to rather congested, 3–10 × 3–10 cm; primary branches 5–10, 3–10 cm × 0.4–0.7 mm; secondary branches 0 or 0.4–2 cm. Spikelets 1 or in finger-like clusters of 2–9, linear-oblong, 3–12 × 1–1.5 mm, flattened; axis slightly zigzag. Glumes ovate to oblong-ovate, 0.8–1 × 0.5–0.8 mm, apex truncate or obtuse, shortly recurved-mucronate, straight to slightly recurved, sides membranous, veins inconspicuous, reddish brown or purplish brown, keel yellow green. Stamens 1–2; anthers 0.2–0.4 mm. Stigmas 3. Achenes obovoid-orbicular or ovoid, broadly trigonous, sides rounded, 0.3–0.5 × 0.2–0.3 mm, maturing white or creamy yellow, usually minutely tuberculate.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Shing Mun. HK sheet 7831, 13127.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Xizang, Sichuan, Hunan, Anhui, Jiangxi, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Taiwan; widely distributed in temperate and subtropical regions of Asia, Africa and Australia.
Ecology: Open grasslands. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Oct.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Pok Fu Lam, Victoria Peak, Kwun Tong, Sai Kung, Tung Chung
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Diplacrum caricinum R. Br. 裂穎茅
Prodr. 241. 1810; FKH 304. 1912; FGZ 766. 1956; FRPS 11: 217. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 254. 2000; FGD 8: 362. 2007; FOC 23: 269. 2010.
Scleria caricina (R. Br.) Benth., Fl. Austr. 7: 426. 1878.

Small, diffuse, slender annual. Culms loosely tufted, 10–30 cm tall, ca. 1 mm thick, sharply triquetrous, smooth, glabrous. Leaves basal and cauline, linear, 1–4 × 0.2–0.5 cm, apex shortly acute, margin minutely scabrous toward apex; sheaths slightly dilated upwards, wingless. Inflorescence consisting of axillary clusters of spikelets almost throughout the length of the culm; spikelets unisexual, 1–2 mm long; peduncles short, scarcely exserted from the leaf sheath. Primary bracts leaf-like. Male spikelets ca. 1.5 mm long, few-flowered. Stamen 1; filament up to 1.5 mm long; anther oblong, ca. 0.4 mm long. Female spikelet ca. 2 mm long. Glumes paired, ca. 2 mm long, broadly oblong, apex 3-lobed, side thinly membranous, 5–8-veined, pale greenish. Stigmas 3. Achenes tightly enveloped by 2 subtending glumes and falling off with them, globose, 0.7–1 mm in diam., umbonulate at apex, with 3 prominent, longitudinal ribs, irregularly ribbed, slightly hispidulous at apex, whitish. Disk adnate to base of the achene, obtusely triangular in outline.

Locality: Pok Fu Lam, Victoria Peak, Kwun Tong, Sai Kung, Tung Chung. H. C. Tang 1399; Y. S. Lau 3184; Y. W. Lam 1626.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan, Jiangsu, Fujian, Taiwan, Zhejiang; India, Sri Lanka, Vietnam, Thailand, Malaysia, Philippines, Japan, Micronesia, Australia.
Ecology: Farmlands and wastelands. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Oct.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Sha Tin, Wu Kau Tang, Fanling
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Eleocharis acicularis (L.) R. Br. 牛毛氈
Prodr. 1: 224. 1810; Roem. & Schult., Syst. Veg. 2: 154. 1817; FKH 297. 1912; FTW ed. 2, 5: 254. 2000; FGD 8: 291. 2007.
Scirpus acicularis L., Sp. Pl. 1: 48. 1753.
Eleocharis yokoscensis (Franch. & Sav.) Tang & F. T. Wang, FRPS 11: 54, pl. 20: 10–13. 1961; Flora Guizhouensis 8: 567. 1988; FYN 15: 590. 2003; FOC 23: 193. 2010.

Perennial, with capillary stolons, usually forming dense mats. Culms erect, capillary, angular-sulcate (usually 4-angled), smooth, 3–10(–30) cm tall, 0.1  .3(–0.5) mm thick, often much elongate in deep or running water. Sheaths thinly membranous, loose, oblique at the mouth, often reddish at the base, the apex scarious and often somewhat inflated. Spikelet ovate to lanceolate, ± flattened, acute, (3–)5–8( –15)-flowered, 2–4(–7) × 1–1.5 mm. Glumes thinly membranous, suberect, oblong-ovate, 1.5–2 × 1–1.5 mm, apex ± obtuse, pale green with scarious margins and often reddish brown sides, the lower ones subdistichous, 1-veined. Perianth segments 1–4, very slender, equalling or exceeding the achenes, often reduced or absent. Stamens 2–3; anthers linear, 0.6–1 mm; connective shortly produced. Sigmas 3. Achenes whitish to light brown, obovate-oblong, 0.7–1 × 0.4–0.5 mm, almost terete or trigonous, on each face with 2 – 4 distinct longitudinal ribs connected by many transverse cross-ridges; epidermal cells transversely linear; style bases minute, depressed pyramidal, 1/3–1/2 as wide as the achene.

Locality: Sha Tin, Wu Kau Tang, Fanling. Y. S. Lau 1501, 2173; S. T. Chan 199.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; N America, Europe, E Russia, Korea, Japan, India, Myanmar, Vietnam, Indonesia, Philippines, Sri Lanka.
Ecology: Wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Nov.

Eleocharis acutangula (Roxb.) Schult. 銳棱荸薺
Mant, 2: 91. 1824; FHN 4: 282. 1977; FTW ed. 2, 5: 255. 2000; FGD 8: 289. 2007; FOC 23. 192. 2010.
Scirpus acutangulus Roxb., Fl. Ind., ed. 1820, 1: 216. 1820.
Eleocharis fistulosa Link, Jahrb. Gewächsk. 3: 78. 1820; FRPS 11: 51. 1961.

Stoloniferous perennial; stolons often terminated by a small tuber. Culms tufted, 30–70 cm tall, 2.5–4 mm thick, sharply triquetrous, smooth. Sheaths up to 10 cm, triangular-acute, pale green to brownish. Spikelets cylindrical, 2–4 cm × 3–4 mm. Glumes ovate to ovate-elliptic, 4–5 mm, rounded, herbaceous, green, margins hyaline. Perianth segments 6, longer than achenes, usually barbellate. Stamens 2–3; anthers 1.5–1.7 mm long. Stigmas 3. Achenes broadly obovate, compressed-trigonous, 1.5–2 × 1.4 mm, apex constricted into a short neck, style base subulate-deltoid, surface yellowish brown, indistinctly shallowly pitted transversely oblong epidermal cell.

Locality: Aberdeen, Sai Kung. Y. W. Lam 1722, 2169, 2225.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam, Myanmar, India, Sri Lanka, Malay Peninsula.
Ecology: Marshes and paddy fields. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Sep.

Eleocharis atropurpurea (Retz.) J. Presl & C. Presl 紫果藺
Reliq. Haenk. 1(3): 196. 1828; FRPS 11: 62. 1961; FHN 4: 284. 1977; Flora Guizhouensis 8: 571. 1988; FTW ed. 2, 5: 255. 2000; FYN 15: 595. 2003; FGD 8: 290. 2007; FOC 23: 197. 2010.
Scirpus atropurpureus Retz., Observ. Bot. 5: 14. 1789.

Dwarf annual; rhizome absent. Stems tufted, erect or curved, capillary, angular-sulcate, smooth, 4–15 cm tall, 0.3–0.7 mm thick. Sheaths appressed, purplish or brownish at the base, apex of the uppermost oblique, often attenuate. Spikelets oblong-ovoid, ± obtuse, somewhat angular, densely many-flowered, 2–4 (finally lengthening to 8) mm, 1.5–2 mm across. Glumes elliptic, 0.9–1.3 × 0.5–0.7 mm, apex obtuse, membranous, keeled, 1-veined, with green keel and pale or ± purplish sides. Perianth segments 3–6, slender, minutely retrorsely scabrous to almost smooth, shorter than to about as long as the achene, whitish, translucent, not rarely vestigial or absent. Stamens 1–2; anthers linear or oblong-linear, minutely apiculate, 0.3–0.7 mm. Stigmas 2. Achene black, obovate, biconvex, 0.5–0.7 × 0.3–0.4 mm, smooth, shining; epidermal cells very inconspicuous. Style base minute, flattened, strongly depressed, disciform or depressed-conical, 1/4–1/3 as wide as the achene.

Locality: Castle Peak, Tung Lung Chau. HK sheet 13341, 37014.
Distribution: Anhui, Shandong, Taiwan, Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Sichuan, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangsu; widely spread over tropical regions of the world.
Ecology: Paddy fields and wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Oct.

Eleocharis dulcis (Burm. f.) Trin. ex Hensch. 荸薺（馬蹄）
Vita Rumphii 186. 1833; FRPS 11: 49. 1961; FHN 4: 280. 1977; FTW ed. 2, 5: 257. 2000; FYN 15: 588. 2003; FGD 8: 288. 2007; FOC 23: 191. 2010.
Andropogon dulcis Burm. f., Fl. Indica 219. 1768.
Eleocharis tuberosa Schult., Mant. 2: 86. 1824; FKH 297. 1912.
Eleocharis plantaginea R. Br., Prodr. 1: 224. 1810; FKH 297. 1912.

Perennial. Stolons elongate, terminated by a small tuber. Tubers 5–7 mm across. Culms tufted, 40–90 cm tall, 3–7 mm thick, terete, transversely sepatate, spongiose, easily flattened when dry. Sheaths 3–20 cm, apex truncate, reddish brown. Spikelet cylindrical, 2–5 × 0.4–0.6 cm. Glumes many per spikelet, ellipticoblong to oblong-obovate, 5–6.5 × 1.7–3.2 mm, apex obtuse to rounded-truncate, sides herbaceous or papery, whitish, margins narrow, hyaline, midrib greenish. Perianth segments 6–8, longer than achenes, flattened below, barbellate above. Stamens 3; anthers 2.5–3 mm long. Stigmas 2. Achenes brown, obovate, biconvex, 1.7–2.2 × 1.5–1.8 mm, apex indistinctly annulate, style base triangular-conical, surface shiny yellowish or greyish brown, indistinctly cancellate.

Locality: Cultivated. P. S. Choi 536; Y. W. Lam 1775; HK sheet 39700.
Distribution: Widely cultivated in China; Korea, Japan, Vietnam, Malaysia, Madagascar, W Africa, Australia.
Ecology: Ponds, marshes and paddy fields. Flowering & fruiting: May–Oct.
Uses: Food (tuber).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Yuen Long, Mai Po, Kuk Po, Lai Chi Wo, Tai Mo Shan, Ma Wan
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Eleocharis equisetina J. Presl & C. Presl 木賊狀荸薺
Reliq. Haenk. 1(3): 195. 1828; FRPS 11: 48. 1961; FHN 4: 280. 1977; FGD 8: 287. 2007.
Eleocharis kuroguwai Ohwi, J. Jap. Bot. 12(9): 654. 1936.
Eleocharis dulcis auct. non (Burm. f.) Trin. ex Hensch.: FOC 23: 191. 2010, p.p.

Perennial. Stolons elongate, terminated by a small tuber. Culms tufted, 30–50 cm tall, 2–3 mm thick, terete, transversely septate, spongiose, easily flattened when dry. Sheaths 5–15 cm, apex truncate, reddish brown, glabrous. Spikelet cylindrical, 2–4 × 0.2–0.3 cm. Glumes oblong-obovate, 3–8 × 4 mm, apex obtuse, subleathery, greenish or brownish, margin hyaline. Perianth 7–8, ca. 1.5 times of achenes. Stamens 3, anthers linear. Stigmas 3. Achenes ca. 2 × 1.2 mm, obovoid or ellipsoidal, biconvex, yellow, apex indistinctly annulate, style base triangular-conical, surface shiny yellowish or greyish brown, indistinctly cancellate.

Locality: Yuen Long, Mai Po, Kuk Po, Lai Chi Wo, Tai Mo Shan, Ma Wan. Y. W. Lam 1208, 1848; J. C. Shaw 114.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Jiangsu, Taiwan; Japan, SE Asia, India.
Ecology: Marshes and wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Sep.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Sai Wan, Shap Sze Heung, Yung Shue O, San Tau
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Eleocharis geniculata (L.) Roem. & Schult. 黑籽荸薺
Syst. Veg. 2: 150. 1817; FHN 4: 284. 1977; FTW ed. 2, 5: 259. 2000; FGD 8: 290. 2007; FOC 23: 197. 2010.
Scirpus geniculatus L., Sp. Pl. 1: 48. 1753.
Eleocharis capitata R. Br., Prodr. 1: 225. 1810; FKH 297. 1912.
Scirpus capitatus Willd., Sp. Pl. 1: 294. 1798. non L. 1753; FHK 394. 1861.
Eleocharis caribaea (Rottb.) S. F. Blake, Rhodora 20: 24. 1918; FRPS 11: 61. 1961.

Annual; rhizome absent. Culms densely tufted, 7–40 cm tall, 0.2–0.4(–0.7) mm thick. Sheaths 0.5–3 cm, apex obliquely truncate, pale green, to reddish or purple brown below. Spikelets ovoid-globose to ovoid-ellipsoidal, 3–7 × 3–4 mm. Glumes many per spikelet, closely imbricate, broadly elliptic to ovate, 1.8–2 × 1.2 mm, apex obtuse, sides membranous, pale brown, midrib green. Perianth segments 6–8, slightly longer than achenes, sparsely barbellate. Stamens 2–3; anthers linear, ca. 0.5 mm long. Stigmas 2. Achenes black, broadly obovate, biconvex, 0.9–1 × 0.7– 0.8 mm, rounded, maturing shinny black, ± smooth; style base depressed-conical.

Locality: Sai Wan, Shap Sze Heung, Yung Shue O, San Tau. Y. W. Lam 1640, 2168; Y. S. Lau 669.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian, Taiwan; tropical and subtropical regions of the world.
Ecology: Marshes, wet places and paddy fields. Flowering & fruiting: Jan.–Jul.

Eleocharis ochrostachys Steud. 假馬蹄（假荸薺）
Syn. Pl. Glumac. 2: 80. 1855; FRPS 11: 51. 1961; FHN 4: 282. 1977; FTW ed. 2, 5: 259. 2000; FGD 8: 289. 2007; FOC 23: 192. 2010.
Eleocharis variegata auct. non Kunth: FKH 297. 1912; Check List HK Plants 89. 1993.

Perennial. Stolons elongate, 1.5–2.5 mm thick. Culms tufted, 40–80 cm tall, 2–3 mm thick, terete to weakly angular, without transverse septa, longitudinally canaliculate on surface when dry. Sheaths 6–15 cm, apex mucronulate, pale brown to reddish brown. Spikelets cylindrical to ovoid, 1–2.5 cm × 3–4 m. Glumes several to many per spikelet, ovate to ovate-oblong, 4–5 × 2–2.2 mm, apex obtuse, sides herbaceous, pale green, finely striate, margins broadly membranous. Perianth segments 6–7, much exceeding achenes, barbellate. Stamens 3; anthers 0.7–0.8 mm. Stigmas 3. Achenes broadly obovate, compressed-trigonous, 1.5–2 × 1.3–1.6 mm, apex annulate, surface yellowish brown, shiny, with longitudinal rows of transversely linear-oblong epidermal cells.

Locality: Aberdeen, Kwun Tong, Lantau Island. Y. W. Lam 916, 1302; HK sheet 13364.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam, Thailand, Myanmar, India, Malaysia, Indonesia, Japan, Micronesia.
Ecology: Marshes, paddy fields and lakes. Flowering & fruiting: Sep.–Nov.

Eleocharis pellucida var. japonica (Miq.) Tang & F. T. Wang 稻田荸薺
FRPS 11: 58. 1961; FHN 4: 283. 1977; FYN 15: 593. 2003; FOC 23: 195. 2010.
Eleocharis congesta auct. non D. Don: FGD 8: 292. 2007; Check List HK Plants 312. 2002; 110. 2004.
Eleocharis japonica Miq., Ann. Mus. Bot. Lugduno-Batavum 2: 142. 1865.
Eleocharis congesta D. Don subsp. japonica (Miq.) T. Koyama, FTW 5: 220. 1978, ed. 2, 5: 257. 2000.
Scirpus japonicus (Miq.) Franch. & Sav., Enum. Pl. Jap. 2: 109. 1877.
Eleocharis afflata Steud., Zoll. Verz. Ind. Archip. 84. 1851; FKH 297. 1912.
Scirpus afflatus (Steud.) Benth., FHK 394. 1861.

Stoloniferous perennial; stolons often terminated by a small tuber. Culms tufted, 30–70 cm tall, 2.5–4 mm thick, sharply triquetrous, smooth. Sheaths 4–10 cm, triangular-acute, pale green to brownish. Spikelets cylindrical, 2 – 4 cm × 3–4 mm. Glumes ovate to ovateelliptic, ca. 2.2 × 1 mm, rounded, herbaceous, green, margins hyaline. Perianth segments 6, longer than achenes, usually barbellate. Stamens 2–3; anthers 1.5–1.7 mm long. Stigmas 3. Achenes yellowish brown, broadly obovate, 1.5–2 × 1.4 mm, compressed-trigonous, apex constricted into a short neck, style base subulate-deltoid, surface indistinctly shallowly pitted transversely oblong epidermal cell.

Locality: Sai Kung, Sha Tin. Y. S. Lau 3089; Y. W. Lam 1703; HK sheet 39235.
Distribution: S, SE & SW China; Russia, Korea, Japan, India, Myanmar, Indochina, Indonesia, Philippines, Europe, N America. Ecology: Marshes, paddy fields and ditches. Flowering & fruiting: May – Aug.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Sai Kung, Lai Chi Wo, Ham Tin, Pui O
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Eleocharis retroflexa (Poir.) Urb. 貝殼葉荸薺
Symb. Antill. 2: 165. 1900; FHN 4: 283. 1977; FGD 8: 290. 2007; FOC 23: 193. 2010.
Scirpus retroflexus Poir., Encycl. 6(2): 753. 1805.
Eleocharis chaetaria Roem. & Schult., Syst. Veg. 2: 154. 1817; FRPS 11: 54. 1961.

Annual; rhizome absent. Culms tufted, often recurved, 4–14 cm tall, 0.2–0.3 mm thick, angular. Sheaths 0.3–0.5 cm long, apex lanceolate, acute, pale brown to reddish brown below. Spikelets broadly ovate, 3–4 × 1.7–2.5 mm, laterally ± flattened. Glumes 3–8 per spikelet, ± 2-ranked, ovate to ovate-elliptic, 2.5–3 × 1.5–2 mm, pale brown to reddish, sides membranous, apex subacute, margins broad-hyaline, the glumes keeled, keel ± acute. Perianth segments 6, flattened, equalling to slightly longer than achenes, sparsely scabrid above. Stamens 3; anthers linear. Stigmas 3. Achenes broadly obovoid, trigonous, 0.7–1 × 0.6–0.7 mm, apex rounded, style base depressed-conical, decurrent with apex, surface trabeculate with 7–9 rows of deeply pitted epidermal cells, pale yellow.

Locality: Sai Kung, Lai Chi Wo, Ham Tin, Pui O. Y. W. Lam 1718; S. C. Ng 1080; HK sheet 39295.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Yunnan, Fujian; Japan, Vietnam, Thailand, Cambodia, India, Sri Lanka, Myanmar, Malaysia, Indonesia, Philippines, Papua New Guinea, Australia, tropical America.
Ecology: Margins of ponds, streamsides. Flowering & fruiting: Oct.–Nov.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Wu Kai Sha, Yuen Long, Yung Shue O, Mai Po, Plover Cove, Tai Ho
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Eleocharis spiralis (Rottb.) Roem. & Schult. 螺旋鱗荸薺
Syst. Veg. 2: 155. 1817; FRPS 11: 50, pl. 19: 1 – 3. 1961; FHN 4: 281. 1977; FGD 8: 289. 2007.
Scirpus spiralis Rottb., Descr. Icon. Rar. Pl. 45, t. 15, fig. 1. 1773.

Stoloniferous perennial. Stolons ca. 3 mm thick. Culms tufted, 30–60 cm tall, 2–4 mm thick, usually triquetrous, rarely subterete, smooth. Sheaths 3–17 cm, light green to purplish, apex often with setaceous blade 1–4 mm. Spikelets cylindrical, yellowish, 1.5–3 cm × 4–6 mm. Glumes many per spikelet, densely imbricate, broadly obovate, 3.2–4 × 2–2.5 mm, very broadly obtuse to truncate, sides subleathery, yellowish brown. Perianth segments 5–6, slender, shorter than or equalling achenes, rarely longer, pale brownish, sparsely patent-spinulose. Stamens 3; anthers linear, 2–2.3 mm long. Stigmas 3. Achenes black, obovoid to ovoid, biconvex, 1.5–1.7 × 1.2–1.4 mm, apex rounded or indistinctly annulate, style base conical, surface maturing dark brown, indistinctly cancellate.

Locality: Wu Kai Sha, Yuen Long, Yung Shue O, Mai Po, Plover Cove, Tai Ho. J. C. Shaw 671; Y. W. Lam 746, 1142.
Distribution: Guangdong, Hainan; Africa, Madagascar, Australia.
Ecology: Margins of ponds. Flowering & fruiting: Oct.–Jan. of the following year.
Uses: Weaving.

Eleocharis tetraquetra Nees 龍師草
Contr. Bot. India 113. 1834; FRPS 11: 55. 1961; FHN 4: 283. 1977; FTW ed. 2, 5: 259. 2000; FGD 8: 291. 2007; FOC 23: 194. 2010.

Stoloniferous perennial; stolons slender. Culms tufted, 30–90 cm tall, 1–2.5 mm thick, acutely 4(–5)-angled. Sheaths 6–15 cm, apex obtuse, mucronulate, pale brown to reddish or purple brown. Spikelet somewhat oblique, oblong or lanceolate, 8–10 × 3–5 mm. Glumes many per spikelet, oblong to ovate, 3–4 × 1.5–2 mm, apex obtuse, sides papery, rusty brown above, margins narrowly hyaline, midrib greenish. Perianth segments 6(–8), slightly longer to twice as long as achenes body, retrorsely barbellate, spinules rather long. Stigmas 3. Achenes obovate, flattened trigonous, 1.5–2 × 1–1.2 mm, apex rounded, style base deltoid, surface smooth, maturing greenish brown, ± smooth.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Penny's Bay. J. C. Shaw & R. Corlett 115; Y. W. Law 1593; HK sheet 38291.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hunan, Jiangxi, Henan, Anhui, Jiangsu, Fujian, Jiangxi, Heilongjiang, Liaoning, Sichuan, Yunnan, Zhejiang, Taiwan; Japan, Russia, Afghanistan, Bhutan, Sri Lanka, India, Nepal, Pakistan, Thailand, Vietnam, Indonesia, Philippines, Papua New Guinea, Australia.
Ecology: Margins of ponds and other wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Sep.–Nov.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Aberdeen, Mount Kellet, Yung Shue O, Chek Keng, Sai Kung, Ham Tin
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Fimbristylis acuminata Vahl 披針穗飄拂草
Enum. Pl. 2: 285. 1806; FHK 391. 1861; FKH 299. 1912; FRPS 11: 102. 1961; FHN 4: 295. 1977; FTW ed. 2, 5: 262. 2000; FGD 8: 309. 2007; FOC 23: 215. 2010.
Fimbristylis setacea Benth., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 2: 239. 1843.

Annual or short-lived perennial. Rhizome absent. Culms densely tufted, 3–35 cm tall, 0.2–0.6 mm thick, triquetrous, smooth. Leaves reduced to basal sheaths; sheaths cylindrical, 1.5–5 cm, pale green to light brown. Ligule absent. Involucral bracts 1, glume-like. Inflorescence a single terminal spikelet. Spikelet ovoid to ovoid-conical, terete, (4–)6–13 × 2–3 mm. Glumes 5–15 per spikelet, broadly ovate to elliptic, 2.7–4 × 1.5–2 mm, apex subacute, sides thinly papery to membranous, pale greenish, yellow brown to reddish brown, margins pale-hyaline, keel obtuse. Stamens 2; anthers 0.8–1 mm. Style long and compressed, sparsely ciliate, basally inflated; stigmas 2. Achenes obovate to orbicular, biconvex, 1–1.3 × 1–1.3 mm, whitish to cream, coarsely transversely wrinkled, very finely striate.

Locality: Aberdeen, Mount Kellet, Yung Shue O, Chek Keng, Sai Kung, Ham Tin. Y. W. Lam 1717, 1723, 1726.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; Sri Lanka, India, Malaysia, Laos, Thailand, Vietnam, Papua New Guinea, Japan, tropical Australia.
Ecology: Sandy farmlands, secondary forests and crevices of rocks. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Sep.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Kau Wa Keng, Lam Tsuen, Tung Chung River
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Fimbristylis aestivalis (Retz.) Vahl 夏飄拂草
Enum. Pl. 2: 288. 1806; FHK 392. 1861; FKH 299. 1912; FRPS 11: 99. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 262. 2000; FYN 15: 614. 2003; FGD 8: 306. 2007; FOC 23: 214. 2010.
Scirpus aestivalis Retz., Observ. Bot. IV.: 12. 1791[1786].

Annual; rhizome absent. Culms densely tufted, 3–20 cm tall, 0.3–0.5 mm thick, trigonous, smooth. Leaves basal; blade linear, 1.5–4 cm × 0.3–0.6 mm, acuminate, flattish or with incurved margins, ± pilose; sheath 0.5–1.5 cm, pale green to yellowish brown; ligule absent. Involucral bracts 2–3(–6), leaf-like, the longest 1–5 cm. Inflorescence simple to compound, 2–7 × 2–7 cm; primary branches 3–7, 0.5–3.3 cm. Spikelets many per inflorescence, solitary, ovoid-conical, subterete, 2.5–7 × 1–1.5 mm. Glumes 10–40 per spikelet, spirally imbricate, ovate, 1–1.5 × 0.6–0.8 mm, acute, recurved-mucronate to shortly cuspidate, sides membranous, yellowish brown, keel subacute, finely 3-veined, green. Stamens 1, anthers 0.3 mm. Style long and compressed, basally inflated, apically ciliate; stigmas 2. Style-base glabrous or ciliolate. Achenes obovate, thickly biconvex, 0.5–0.6 × 0.3–0.4 mm, maturing yellowish, sometimes slightly shiny, smooth or faintly cancellate with a few rows of transversely oblong epidermal cells.

Locality: Kau Wa Keng, Lam Tsuen, Tung Chung River. Y. S. Lau 2681; J. C. Shaw & Macia 291; HK sheet 40872.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Chongqing, Hunan, Hubei, Heilongjiang, Shaanxi, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Anhui, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Nepal, Sri Lanka, India, Thailand, Indonesia, Philippines, Australia.
Ecology: Marshes, paddy fields and other wet places. Flowering & fruiting: May–Aug.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Mo Shan, Sai Kung, Tung Chung
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Fimbristylis complanata (Retz.) Link 扁鞘飄拂草
Hort. Berol. 1: 292. 1827; FHK 393. 1861; FKH 300. 1912; FRPS 11: 81. 1961; Flora Guizhouensis 8: 575. 1988; FTW ed. 2, 5: 265. 2000; FYN 15: 603. 2003; FGD 8: 298. 2007; FOC 23: 205. 2010.
Scirpus complanatus Retz., Observ. Bot. 5: 14. 1791.

Perennial. Rhizomes short. Culms crowded in series along rhizome to ± tufted, 30–70 cm tall, 0.9–5 mm thick, flattened, smooth to scabrid, narrowly winged above. Leaves basal; blade linear, up to 26 cm × 2–5 mm, obtuse to rounded, flat, margins incurved; sheath 1–8 cm, obliquely truncate, pale to rusty brown; ligule a fringe of short hairs. Involucral bracts 2–4, the longest suberect, 1–8 cm. Inflorescence compound, 4–10 cm; primary branches 4–7, 1–5 cm. Spikelets ellipsoidal to ovoid-lanceolate, terete, 4–9 × 1–2 mm. Glumes 5–20 per spikelet spirally arranged, ovate to ovate-lanceolate, 1.8–2.5(–3) mm long, mucronate, sides chartaceous, yellowish brown to brown, margins paler, keel acute, green. Stamens 2–3; anthers 1 mm long. Style 3-sided, glabrous, basally inflated to conic; stigmas 3. Achenes broadly obovoid, trigonous, 0.5–0.7 × 0.3–0.4 mm whitish, finely cancellate with several rows of transversely oblong epidermal cells.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Sai Kung, Tung Chung. Y. W. Lam 812, 954, 1623.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hubei, Jiangsu, Fujian, Taiwan; tropics.
Ecology: Muddy seashores, wet places by streams or paddy fields. Flowering & fruiting: May–Aug.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Cape D'Aguilar, Stonecutters Island, Castle Peak, Ping Chau
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Fimbristylis cymosa (Lam.) R. Br. 黑果飄拂草
Prodr. 228. 1810; FRPS 11: 82. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 266. 2000; FGD 8: 299. 2007; FOC 23: 206. 2010.
Scirpus cymosus Lam. Tabl. 1: 141. 1791.
