Fimbristylis spathacea Roth, Nov. Pl. Sp. 24. 1821; FKH 299. 1912.
Fimbristylis cymosa R. Br. var. spathacea (Roth) T. Koyama, J. Jap. Bot. 46(3): 66. 1971; FOC 23: 207. 2010. Fimbristylis wightiana Nees, Contrib. 99. 1834; FHK 392. 1861.

Perennial; rhizomes not or hardly elongate. Culms tufted, 5–60 cm tall, 1–2 mm thick, trigonous, smooth. Leaves basal, rosetteforming; blade narrowly linear, 5–30 cm × 1–4 mm, subobtuse, subleathery, flattish to weakly inrolled; sheath up to 3 cm, whitish or cinnamon-brown; ligule absent. Involucral bracts 1–3, leaf-like, the longest shorter than inflorescence, 0.5–1.8 cm. Inflorescence simple to compound, open to congested; primary branches 2–6, 1–3 cm. Spikelets few to many per inflorescence, ellipsoidal-cylindrical to ovoid-cylindrical, 2–6 × 1–2 mm. Glumes many per spikelet, spirally arranged, ovate to broadly ovate, 1–2.2 × 0.5–1.5 mm, apex obtuse, sides membranous, mid-brown, margins broadly white-hyaline, keel obtuse, obscurely 3–5-veined, paler brown. Stamens 1–3; anthers 0.8–1 mm, connective smooth. Style slender, not ciliate, basally slightly thickened; stigmas 2(–3). Achenes obovate, biconvex to rarely compressed-trigonous, 0.7–0.9 × 0.5–0.7 mm, maturing dark brown to black, smooth to indistinctly cancellate.

Locality: Cape D'Aguilar, Stonecutters Island, Castle Peak, Ping Chau. J. C. Shaw 583; Y. W. Lam 986; Y. S. Lau 2476.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan, Zhejiang; tropics.
Ecology: Sandy beaches and mangroves. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Oct.

Fimbristylis dichotoma (L.) Vahl 兩歧飄拂草
Enum. Pl. 2: 287. 1805; FKH 299. 1912; FRPS 11: 89. 1961; Flora Guizhouensis 8: 580. 1988; FTW ed. 2, 5: 266. 2000; FYN 15: 609. 2003; FGD 8: 303. 2007; FOC 23: 210. 2010.
Scirpus dichotomus L., Sp. Pl. 1: 50. 1753.
Fimbristylis diphylla (Retz.) Vahl, Enum. Pl. 2: 289–290. 1805; FHK 392. 1861; C. B. Clarke, J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 36: 233. 1903; FKH 299. 1912.

Annual or short-lived perennial. Rhizomes short. Culms loosely tufted, 10–70 cm tall, 0.5–2.5 mm thick, triquetrous, glabrous to sparsely pubescent smooth. Leaves basal; blade narrowly linear, (3–)10–30 cm × 1.5–5 mm, obtuse, flattish, margins ± incurved; sheath 2–12 cm, pale green to mid-brown, apex truncate; ligule a fringe of dense hairs. Involucral bracts 2–7, the longest 1–2 leaf-like, 2–8 cm. Inflorescence simple to compound, open to congested, 2–17 × 1–15 cm; primary branches 2–12, 1–8 cm. Spikelets 2 – many per inflorescence, solitary or in clusters of 2–3, ovoid to ovoid-ellipsoidal, 3–10 × 2.5–3.5 mm. Glumes many per spikelet, spirally arranged, broadly ovate to suborbicular, 1.5–3(–4) × 1.5–2.2 mm, subacute, mucronate, sides thinly chartaceous, 2–4-veined or veins 0, mid-brown to dark reddish brown, margins pale-hyaline, keel obtuse, greenish to pale brown. Stamens (1–)2–3, anthers 0.5–1.7 mm long. Style compressed, apically ciliate, basally inflated; stigmas 2. Achenes obovate to broadly obovate, biconvex, 0.7–1.3 × 0.8–1 mm, maturing cream to pale brown, deeply cancellate with 5–13 rows of transversely oblong epidermal cells, occasionally verrucose on shoulder.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. J. C. Shaw 529; Y. W. Lam 1217; K. L. Yip 4040.
Distribution: Spread over most provinces of China; widely distributed in subtropical and temperate regions.
Ecology: Open grassy fields. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Oct.
Uses: Forage.
Notes: The type specimens of Fimbristylis diphylla Vahl var. leptophylla Benth. (FHK 392. 1861) were collected by H. F. Hance, C. Harland and C. Wright from Hong Kong in 1850s, but is not treated because no material is available. Clarke (J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 36: 233 – 235. 1903) discussed the range of variation of this widespread species, including the two varieties from Hong Kong Island described by Bentham (FHK 392. 1861).

Fimbristylis diphylloides Makino 擬二葉飄拂草
J. Jap. Bot. 11(4): 252, fig. 3. 1935; FRPS 11: 87. 1961; Flora Guizhouensis 8: 578. 1988; FGD 8: 301. 2007; FOC 23: 209. 2010.

Annual. Rhizome absent or very short. Culms tufted, thin, flatly 4-angled, striate, 15–50 cm tall, bearing 1–2 bladeless sheaths at base, sheaths cylindrical, 2.5 – 6.5 cm, mouth obliquely truncate, acute, covered with fibriform old sheaths; leaves shorter than or nearly equalling culms, flat, acute at apex, finely toothed at margins, 1.2–2.2 mm wide; sheaths membranous and rusty-brown adaxially, mouth obliquely split, without ligule. Bracts 4–6, much shorter than inflorescence, setaceous, dilated at base, finely serrulate on margins; anthelae simple or nearly compound, 1.5–6 × 2–6 cm; anthelae 4–8, scabrid, 0.6–4 cm; spikelets solitary, obovate or oblong-obovate, obtuse or nearly acute, 2.5–7.5 × 1.5–2.5(–3) mm, densely many-flowered; glumes broadly ovate or oblong-ovate, ca. 1.5 × 1 mm, membranous, extremely obtuse at apex, margins hyaline, 3-veined abaxially, veins green and slightly keeled. Stamens 2, anthers oblong, ca. 0.8 mm, about 1/2 length of filaments. Style not ciliate, base slightly inflated, stigmas 2–3, slightly longer than or nearly equalling style. Achenes broadly obovoid, trigonous or biconvex, ca. 1 mm, brown, with sparse verrucae and transversely oblong reticulation.

Locality: Lung Kwu Tan. HK sheet 37113.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian; Japan, Korea.
Ecology: Paddy fields and other wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Jun. – Sep.

Fimbristylis eragrostis (Nees) Hance 知風飄拂草
J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 13: 132. 1873; FRPS 11: 103. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 269. 2000; FGD 8: 311. 2007; FOC 23: 216. 2010.
Abildgaardia eragrostis Nees, Contr. Bot. India 95. 1834; FKH 299. 1912.

Perennial; rhizome short. Culms 1–few, 10–70 cm tall, 0.5–3 mm thick, 4–5-angled, smooth. Leaves basal; rosette-forming; blade linear, 5–20 cm × 1.5–5 mm, apex obtuse to ± truncate, mucronate, flattish, subleathery, margins often incurved; sheath 1–3 cm, brownish to yellowish brown; ligule absent. Involucral bracts 2–5, narrowly lanceolate to ± setaceous, 0.3–2 cm. Inflorescence simple to compound, open to rather congested, 2–8 × 2–8 cm; primary branches 2–6, 1–6 cm. Spikelets 12– many per inflorescence, oblong to oblong-lanceolate, 6–13 × 2–4 mm, often twisted, somewhat flattened. Glumes 8–25 per spikelet, ± 2-ranked to spirally arranged above, ovate, 3–5 × 2–3 mm, apex subacute, mucronate, sides papery, slightly shiny yellowish brown tinged dark brown, margins pale-hyaline, keel acute, 1-veined. Stamens 3; anthers 1.5–2 mm long. Style brown, 3-sided, basally inflated; stigmas 3. Achenes broadly obovoid, trigonous, 0.7–1 × 0.5–0.7 mm, light brown, verruculose.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Castle Peak. H. C. Tang 1988; HK sheet 13476.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian, Taiwan, Yunnan; Cambodia, Sri Lanka, India, Malaysia, tropical Australia.
Ecology: Thin forests and grasslands. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Sep.

Fimbristylis exaltata (T. Koyama) Y. F. Deng, st. nov. 血色飄拂草
Fimbristylis complanata (Retz.) Link f. exaltata T. Koyama, Bull. Arts Sci. Div. Ryukyu Univ. 3: 70. 1959.
Fimbristylis complanata (Retz.) Link var. exaltata (T. Koyama) Y. C. Tang ex S. R. Zhang & T. Koyama, FOC 23: 205. 2010.
Fimbristylis consanguinea auct. non Kunth: FGD 8: 297. 2007; Check List HK Plants 314. 2002; 110. 2004.
Fimbristylis complanata (Retz.) Link var. kraussiana auct. non (Hook. ex Steud.) C. B. Clarke: FRPS 11: 81. 1961.

Perennial; rhizome short, covered with pale brownish scales. Culms densely tufted, often forming a large clump, slender, 15–50 cm tall, 1–1.5 mm thick, trigonous, smooth, glabrous, glaucous-green leaved at base. Leaf blades herbaceous, glabrous, mostly 1/2–2/3 as long as the culm, linear, 1–2.5 mm wide, margin apically finely serrulate, apex acute; ligule a fringe of short whitish pubescence; sheaths cylindrical with obtuse pale green back, 1–6 cm, the hyaline ventral side tinged with light brown, the orifice obliquely truncate, ciliolate, generally ± auriculate. Corymbs simple or in part subcompound, subdensely bearing 3–20 spikelets, 1–2.5 cm long and as wide; bracts 2–4, elongate, the lowest leaf-like, 5–25 mm, slightly shorter than to surpassing the corymb; anthelas 1–3.5 mm. Spikelets few, solitary, oblong to ovate-lanceolate, 4–6 × 1.5–2 mm, brown to dark brown, several–10-flowered. Glumes spirally imbricated, ovate or ovate-oblong, 2.5–3 × ca. 2 mm, shallowly boat-shaped with convex keel, apex mucronate, thinly membranous, brown, finely 1–3-veined. Stamens 3; anther oblong, ca. 1.5 mm. Style 3-sided, ca. 2 mm, glabrous, basally inflated to conical; stigmas 3. Achenes obovoid, trigonous, 1–1.2 × 0.8–0.9 mm, apex rounded to mucronulate, base cuneate, pale yellowish, substantially smooth, with transverse oblong reticulation.

Locality: Happy Valley. HK sheet 8087.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Anhui, Shandong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Korea, Japan.
Ecology: Marshes and other wet places. Flowering & fruiting: May–Aug.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Aberdeen, Cape D'Aguilar, Mount Kellet, Tai Mo Shan, Castle Peak
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Fimbristylis fusca (Nees) Benth. 褐穗飄拂草
Gen. Pl. 3: 1048. 1883; FKH 299. 1912; FRPS 11: 105. 1961; FYN 15: 615. 2003; FGD 8: 313. 2007; FOC 23: 217. 2010.
Abildgaardia fusca Nees, Contr. Bot. India 95. 1834; FHK 390. 1861.

Perennial; rhizome woody, covered with fibrous leaf sheath remnants. Culms few to several, (15–)30–55 cm tall, 0.5–1 mm thick, angular, smooth to hispid-scabrid above. Leaves basal; blade linear, 4–15 cm × (1–)2–4 mm, often weakly falcate, obtuse to rounded shortly acuminate, flat; sheath ca. 0.5 cm, yellowish brown; ligule absent. Involucral bracts 3–5, setaceous, 0.7–3 cm, glabrous or pubescent. Inflorescence simple to compound, open, 2–15 × 1–12 cm; primary branches up to 10 cm. Spikelets 3– many per inflorescence, lanceolate, subterete to ± flattened, 5–10 × 1.7–2.5 mm. Glumes 3–10 per spikelet, 2-ranked, lanceolate, 4–6.5 × 2–2.5 mm, sides herbaceous to ± papery, shortly hispid, chestnut-brown, margins narrow, hyaline, keel subacute, 1-veined, brown. Stamens 3; anthers 1.5–2 mm. Style 4–5 mm, 3-sided, basally inflated; stigmas 3. Achenes obvoid, trigonous, 0.9–1 × 0.6–0.8 mm, light brownish, densely verrucose, obscurely reticulate.

Locality: Aberdeen, Cape D'Aguilar, Mount Kellet, Tai Mo Shan, Castle Peak. J. C. Shaw 526; S. C. Ng 1439; HK sheet 7976.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou, Hunan, Zhejiang, Anhui, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Nepal, India, Myanmar, Thailand, Vietnam, Malaysia, Papua New Guinea, Australia.
Ecology: Wastelands. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Sep.

Fimbristylis hookeriana Bócklr. 金色飄拂草（羅浮飄拂草）
Linnaea 37: 22. 1871; FRPS 11: 94. 1961; FGD 8: 302. 2007; FOC 23: 212. 2010.
Fimbristylis fordii C. B. Clarke, J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 36: 236. 1903; FKH 299. 1912; FRPS 11: 94. 1961; Check List HK Plants 314. 2002; 111. 2004.

Annual or short-lived perennial. Rhizome absent. Culms tufted, 6–40 cm tall, without rhizome. Leaves nearly equalling culms, ciliate, 1–2.5 mm wide, apex acute, midvein prominent abaxially. Bracts 2–5, leafy, longer than inflorescence, sometimes up to 8 cm, apex acuminate or acute; anthelae simple, rarely compound, with few slender anthelas; spikelets solitary, narrowly lanceolate or linear, 7–17 × ca. 2 mm, lowest 1–2 glumes empty; flowering glumes oblong-ovate, 2.5–3.5 × 1.5–2 mm, greyish green or brown-hued, apex mucronate or awned, sometimes hairy, margins hyaline, with 3 or more veins abaxially. Stamens 3; anthers oblong, ca. 0.8 mm. Style slender, compressed, apically ciliate, basally slightly inflated, stigmas 2. Achenes obovate, biconvex, white, ca. 1 mm, shortly stipitate, verruculose.

Locality: Cape D'Aguilar. S. C. Ng 2005, 4047; HK sheet 42172.
Distribution: Guangdong, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Jiangsu; India, Vietnam, Laos, Thailand, Philippines.
Ecology: Grassy fields, rocks along streams. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Sep.

Fimbristylis insignis Thwaites 硬穗飄拂草
Enum. Pl. Zeyl. 349. 1864; FKH 300. 1912; FGD 8: 300. 2007; FOC 23: 207. 2010.

Perennial; rhizomes short. Culms densely tufted, 20–60 cm tall, 0.5–2 mm thick, ± trigonous, smooth. Leaves basal, many; blade linear, often somewhat falcate, 5–18 cm × 1–4 mm, rounded, leathery, margins serrulate, incurved; sheath 1–2 cm, pale greenish; ligule absent. Involucral bracts 2–3, subulate, erect, the longest shorter than inflorescence, 0.5–1.5 cm. Inflorescence simple, rarely compound, 3–10 × 3–5 cm; primary branches 2–6, 1–8 cm. Spikelets (2–)4–18 per inflorescence, oblong-conical to cylindrical, terete, 12–20 × 2–4 mm. Glumes many per spikelet, spirally imbricate, ovate, 4–7 × 2.5–4 mm, apex obtuse, shortly cuspidate, sides chartaceous, orange brown, slightly shiny, margins narrowly pale-hyaline, keel obtuse, 1-veined, yellowish. Stamens 3; anthers 1.5–2 mm. Styles 0.5–1 mm, 3-sided, glabrous; stigmas 3. Achenes broadly obovoid to obovoid-pyriform, trigonous, 1–1.3 × 0.8–1 mm, apex ± truncate, deeply furrowed on each side, indistinctly cancellate, sometimes verruculose.

Locality: Pok Fu Lam. S. Y. Hu 8497, 10876 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong; Vietnam, Laos, Thailand, Sri Lanka, India, Malaysia, Indonesia, Philippines, Australia.
Ecology: Burnt-over grasslands, rock outcrops, rarely wet forest floors.

Fimbristylis leptoclada Benth. 纖細飄拂草
FHK 393. 1861; FKH 300. 1912; FGD 8: 297. 2007; FOC 23: 208. 2010.

Perennial. Rhizome short. Culms tufted, 15–60 cm tall, 0.2–1.5 mm thick, trigonous, smooth to scabird. Leaves basal, few; blade filiform, 10–30 cm × 0.3–0.5 mm, obtuse margins ± incurved; sheath 1.5–4 cm, pale-hyaline to mid-brown, apex oblique; ligule absent. Involucral bracts 1–3, glume-like or setaceous, the longest 5–20 mm. Inflorescence simple or capitate, 5–20 × 5–8 mm; primary branches (when present) up to 2 cm. Spikelets 3–12 per inflorescence, in clusters of 2–8, ellipsoidal, 2.2–3.5 × 1.5–2 mm. Glumes 10–15 per spikelet, spirally imbricate, broadly ovate, 1–1.5 × 0.7–1.3 mm, rounded-truncate or shallowly emarginate, mucronulate, sides membranous, brown, densely gland-dotted, margins pale-hyaline, fimbriate-ciliate above, keel obtuse, 3-veined, pale brown. Stamens 1–2; anthers 0.5 mm. Style 3-sided, glabrous, basally inflated; stigmas 3. Achenes obovoid, trigonous, 0.7–0.9 × 0.5–0.7 mm, cream, verruculose.

Locality: High West. HK sheet 7977.
Distribution: Guangdong, Fujian; Japan, Sri Lanka, Vietnam, Thailand, Malaysia, Papua New Guinea.
Ecology: Dry sandy grasslands. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Aug.
Notes: The type specimen (C. Wright 579, K, holotype; US, isotype) was collected by C. Wright from Hong Kong in 1850s.

Fimbristylis littoralis Gaudich. 水虱草（日照飄拂草）
Voy. Uranie 10: 413. 1829; FTW ed. 2, 5: 271. 2000; FOC 23: 208. 2010.
Fimbristylis miliacea (L.) Vahl, Enum. Pl. 2: 287. 1805, nom. rej.; FHK 393. 1861; FKH 300. 1912; FRPS 11: 85. 1961; Flora Guizhouensis 8: 577. 1988; FTW ed. 2, 5: 271. 2000; FYN 15: 604. 2003; FGD 8: 300. 2007; Check List HK Plants 314. 2002; 111. 2004.
Scirpus miliaceus L., Syst. Nat. (ed. 10) 868. 1759, nom. rej.

Annual or short-lived perennial. Rhizome short. Clumstufted, 10–60(–90) cm tall, 1–3 mm thick, 4-sided, smooth, bearing 1–3 bladeless sheath at base. Leaves basal, or cauline reduced to bladeless sheaths; blade linear, 10–50 cm × 1–4 mm, apex subacute, bilaterally flattened; basal sheaths 1–18 cm, open, cauline sheaths tubular, 2–10 cm; ligule absent. Involucral bracts 2–4, setaceous, the longest 1 –3 cm. Inflorescence compound to decompound, open, 3–10 × 3–10 cm; primary branches 3–7, 1–7 cm. Spikelets many per inflorescence, ovoid-globose to globose, 1.5–3(–5) × 1–2.1 mm, 6–10-flowered. Glumes many per spikelet, spirally arranged, broadly ovate, 1–1.2 × 0.6–0.8 mm, apex obtuse, sides membranous, reddish brown, margins broadly hyaline, keel obtuse, yellowish, obscurely 3-veined. Stamens 1(–2); anthers oblong, ca. 0.6 mm long. Style 3-sided, apically compressed, sparsely pilose, basally inflated; stigmas 3. Achenes obovoid, trigonous, 0.6–0.8 × 0.3–0.5 mm, creamy yellow, sparsely verruculose especially on angles, cancellate with 5–7 longitudinal rows of transversely linear-oblong cells.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1556; Y. W. Lam 1555; HK sheet 42185.
Distribution: Widely spread over S, SW and E China; tropical and subtropical regions of the world.
Ecology: Paddy fields and other wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Oct.

Fimbristylis longispica Steud. 長穗飄拂草
Syn. Pl. Glumac. 2: 118. 1855; FKH 299. 1912; FRPS 11: 91. 1961; FYN 15: 608. 2003; FGD 8: 304. 2007; FOC 23: 211. 2010.

Perennial. Rhizomes short. Culms tufted, 25–60 cm. tall, with some leafless sheaths at base. Leaves shorter than culms, nearly glabrous, 1.5–2.5 mm wide, subglabrous, apex obtuse, margins often involute. Sheath brownish, glabrous. Bracts 2–3, leafy, the lowest one usually longer than inflorescence, apex obtuse; anthelae compound, decompound or simple, with 3–6 anthelas; spikelets solitary, narrowly oblong, oblong or oblong-ovate or ovate, 6–20 × 3–4 mm, apex acute or obtuse; glumes spirally arranged, broadly ovate, boat-shaped, ca. 3 × 2.5 mm, with 3–5 brown or pale brown veins, glabrous, apex mucronate. Stamens 3; anthers linear, ca. 3 mm. Style slightly longer than achene, apically ciliate, basally slightly inflated, stigmas 2. Achenes globose-obovate, biconvex, 1.2–1.5 mm, pale brown to brown, sessile, with hexagonal reticulation, without vertical ribs and verrucae.

Locality: No precise locality. Faber 221 (K).
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Zhejiang, Jiangsu, Shandong, Liaoning, Jilin, Heilongjiang; Japan, Myanmar, Vietnam, Malaysia.
Ecology: Coastal area and wet places.

Fimbristylis nutans (Retz.) Vahl 垂穗飄拂草
Enum. Pl. 2: 285. 1806; FHK 391. 1861; FKH 299. 1912; FRPS 11: 102. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 272. 2000; FGD 8: 309. 2007; FOC 23: 215. 2010.
Scirpus nutans Retz., Observ. Bot. 4: 12. 1786.

Perennial; rhizome short. Culms 20–75 cm tall, 0.5–1.5 mm thick, subterete to trigonous above, smooth. Leaves reduced to basal sheaths; sheaths cylindrical, 1–12 cm, light green to pale brownish, apex obliquely truncate; ligule absent. Involucral bracts 1, glumelike. Inflorescence a single terminal spikelet, erect at first, soon becoming patent to ± horizontal. Spikelets ovoid to ovoid-ellipsoidal, terete, 8–16 × 4–6 mm. Glumes many per spikelet, spirally imbricate, broadly ovate to ovate, 4–5 × 2.5–3 mm, apex rounded, mucronate, sides membranous to thinly papery, mid-brown, striate with dark brown below keel, margins broadly pale-hyaline, keel flattish to obtuse, indistinctly 4–5-veined, yellowish brown. Stamens 3; anthers 2 mm long. Style long and compressed, 3-sided, basally slightly inflated, apically sparsely ciliate; stigmas 3. Achenes broadly obovate, unequally biconvex, 1.25–1.5 × 0.8–1 mm, maturing cream to slightly brownish, coarsely transversely wrinkled.

Locality: Aberdeen, Lion Rock, Tung Chung. Y. S. Lau 2798; Y. W. Lam 1262; HK sheet 13448.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Taiwan; Japan, Vietnam, Myanmar, Thailand, Sri Lanka, India, Malaysia, New Guinea, Australia.
Ecology: Marshes, paddy fields and other wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Aug.

Fimbristylis pauciflora R. Br. 海南飄拂草
Prodr. 1: 225. 1810; FHN 4: 295. 1977; FGD 8: 308. 2007; FOC 23: 215. 2010.
Fimbristylis hainanensis Tang & F. T. Wang, FRPS 11: 101, 228. 1961.

Perennial. Rhizomes hardly developed. Culms densely tufted, 5–18 cm tall, slender, short, flatly cylindrical, smooth, glabrous, with few leaf sheaths at base. Leaves bladeless; sheath brown, cylindrical, apically attenuate, margins membranous, mouth obliquely truncate. Involucral bracts absent. Inflorescences reduced to a single terminal spikelet, narrowly oblong to clavate-oblong, 3.5–4.5 × 1–1.5 mm, few-flowered, with basalmost glume empty. Glumes pale with rust-coloured short lines, oblong to oblong-ovate, 3–4.5 × 1–1.5 mm, 7–9-veined, midvein abaxially green, apex obtuse and not mucronate. Stamens 3; anthers linear. Style long and compressed, sparsely ciliate, basally slightly broader; stigmas 3, with sparse papillae. Achenes white, obovoid, ca. 0.8 mm, trigonous, with sparse verrucae and nearly hexagonal reticulation.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. HK sheet 42200.
Distribution: Guangdong, Hainan; India, Indonesia, Japan (Ryukyu Islands), Malaysia, Myanmar, Papua New Guinea, Thailand, Vietnam, Australia, Pacific islands.
Ecology: Wet places by ponds

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Victoria Peak, Rocky Harbour, Yi O
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Fimbristylis polytrichoides (Retz.) Vahl 細葉飄拂草
Enum. Pl. 2: 248. 1806; FRPS 11: 96. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 274. 2000; FGD 8: 305. 2007; FOC 23: 213. 2010.
Scirpus polytrichoides Retz., Observ. Bot. 4: 11. 1786.

Annual or short-lived perennial. Rhizome very short or absent, with many remnant fibers from old leaves. Culms 5–30 cm tall, 0.3 – 0.5 mm thick, subterete to trigonous, smooth, glabrous. Leaves basal; blade filiform, up to 4 cm × 0.2–0.5 mm, obtuse, shallowly canaliculate, often reduced to bladeless sheath; sheath 1–4 cm, yellowish brown, apex obliquely truncate; ligule absent. Involucral bracts 1, glume-like or setaceous, 0.3–2.5 cm. Inflorescence a single, terminal spikelet. Spikelets ellipsoidal to oblong-ovoid 5–9 × 2.5–3.5 mm, obtuse. Glumes many per spikelet, spirally imbricate, elliptic to oblong-elliptic, 2.5–3.2 × 1–1.3 mm, obtuse, sides thinly membranous, pale brown on upper part, margins hyaline, keel obtuse, 1-veined. Stamens 1–2; anthers 0.7–1 mm. Style long, slightly compressed, basally inflated, apical half ciliate; stigmas 2. Achenes obovate, biconvex, 0.8–1 × ca. 0.5 mm, maturing brown to greyish purple, minutely cancellate with 15–20 longitudinal rows of transversely linear epidermal cells, often verruculose above.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Rocky Harbour, Yi O. J. C. Shaw 701; Y. W. Lam 925; HK sheet 41737.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian, Taiwan; tropical Africa, Asia, Australia.
Ecology: Muddy seashores and crevices of rocks. Flowering & fruiting: Mar.–Sep.

Fimbristylis rigidula Nees 結壯飄拂草
Contr. Bot. India 99. 1834; FKH 299. 1912; FRPS 11: 91. 1961; Flora Guizhouensis 8: 581. 1988; FYN 15: 609. 2003; FGD 8: 303. 2007; FOC 23: 211. 2010.

Perennial; rhizomes short, woody, covered with fibrous leaf sheath remnant. Culms usually solitary, 15–50 cm tall, 0.5–1.2 mm thick, trigonous, smooth, often sparsely hairy above. Leaves basal; blade linear, 4–20 cm × 2–3.5 mm, acute, shortly apiculate, flat margins weakly incurved, glaucous; sheath 3–7 cm, pale to mid-brown; ligule absent. Involucral bracts 3–5, the longest leaf-like, 1.5–4 cm. Inflorescence simple to compound, rarely decompound, 2–5 × 2–3 cm; primary branches 3 – 6, up to 4 cm. Spikelets 5–20 per inflorescence, solitary or in pairs, broadly ovoid to ovoid-ellipsoidal, 5–8(–12) × 3–4 mm. Glumes many per spikelet, spirally arranged, ovate to broadly ovate, 3–3.2 × 2 mm, apex obtuse, often mucronate, sides chartceous, 3–4-veined, reddish brown, margins broadly white-hyaline, keel obtuse, 3-veined, greenish. Stamens 3; anthers 1.7–2 mm. Style slender, compressed, apically ciliate, basally inflated; stigmas 2. Achenes obovate-orbicular, biconvex, 1–1.5 × 0.8–1.2 mm, greyish brown, verruculose, with 25 – 30 fine longitudinal rows of epidermal cells.

Locality: Lantau Island. H. C. Tang 1256; HK sheet 8057.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan, Guizhou, Hunan, Hubei, Zhejiang, Jiangsu, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Nepal, Bangladesh, Myanmar, Nepal, Pakistan, India, Thailand, Philippines.
Ecology: Grasslands of hillslopes. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Jun.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Aberdeen, Pok Fu Lam, Chek Keng
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Fimbristylis schoenoides (Retz.) Vahl 少穗飄拂草
Enum. Pl. 2: 286. 1805; FHK 391. 1861; FKH 299. 1912; FRPS 11: 95. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 274. 2000; FYN 15: 610. 2003; FGD 8: 305. 2007; FOC 23: 213. 2010.
Scirpus schoenoides Retz., Observ. Bot. 5: 14. 1789.

Perennial; rhizome very short. Culms tufted, 5–50 cm tall, 0.3–0.8 mm thick, smooth. Leaves basal; blade narrowly linear to ± filiform, 2–16 cm × 0.5–1 mm, flattish or with inrolled margins; sheath 2–6 cm, cinnamon-brown, apex obliquely truncate, ciliolate; ligule a fringe of dense short hairs. Involucral bracts 1–2, glume-like, rarely with short setaceous blade. Inflorescence usually a solitary spikelet sometimes simple; primary branches (when present) 1–2, 1–3 cm. Spikelets 1–2(–3) per inflorescence, ovoid to ellipsoidal, 5–10 × 3–4 mm. Glumes many per spikelet, ovate-orbicular, 2.5–3.2 × 2–3 mm, apex obtuse to rounded, shortly mucronate, sides thinly papery, 5–7-veined, pale to orange brown, slightly shiny, keel rounded. Stamens 2; anthers 0.5 mm. Style long, compressed, basally inflated, apical half ciliate; stigmas 3. Achenes obovate-orbicular, biconvex, 1.1–1.3 × 1–1.2 mm, ± rounded, maturing yellowish white, smooth with minute isodiametric epidermal cells.

Locality: Aberdeen, Pok Fu Lam, Chek Keng. Y. W. Lam 1073; HK sheet 13457, 42171.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; S & SE Asia, Australia.
Ecology: Wastelands. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Nov.

Fimbristylis sericea (Poir.) R. Br. 絹毛飄拂草
Prodr. 228. 1810; FKH 299. 1912; FRPS 11: 83. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 276. 2000; FGD 8: 299. 2007; FOC 23: 208. 2010.
Scirpus sericeus Poir., Encycl., Suppl. 5: 99. 1804.

Perennial; rhizomes long-creeping, covered with often blackish brown fibers from old leaf sheaths. Culms erect, (10 – )30 – 60 cm tall, 1.2–2.5 mm thick, trigonous, smooth. Leaves basal, many; blade linear, 4–10 cm × 1.7–4 mm, obtuse, margins inrolled, glaucous, with appressed silky hairs on the lower surface; sheath 2–3 cm, pale green to dark rusty brown, apex obliquely truncate; ligule absent. Involucral bracts 2–3, leaf-like, the longest up to 2 cm. Inflorescence simple to compound, 3–10 cm × 3–4 cm; primary branches 2–6, 1–8 cm. Spikelets few to many per inflorescence, in cluster of 3–10, ovoid to oblong-ovoid, terete, 6–12 × 2.5–4 mm. Glumes many per spikelet, spirally arranged, ovate to broadly ovate, 2.5–4 × 2–3 mm, subacute to subobtuse, mucronate, sides herbaceous, brownish grey, shortly pubescent, margins whitish-hyaline, keel obtuse, brown. Stamens 2–3; anthers 1.5 mm. Style slightly compressed, basally slightly inflated and hairy, apically slightly pubescent; stigmas 2–3. Achenes obovate, biconvex, 1–1.5 × 0.8–1 mm, purplish or dark brown, ± smooth to minutely dotted.

Locality: Long Ke, Tai Wan (Sai Kung). Y. W. Lam 1736; HK sheet 39433, 41561.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Vietnam, Thailand, Japan, Korea, Malaysia, Australia.
Ecology: Sandy beaches and wet sand dunes. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Oct.

Fimbristylis sieboldii Miq. ex Franch. & Sav. 鏽鱗飄拂草
Enum. Pl. Jap. 2: 118. 1877 [“sieboldi”]; FOC 23: 212. 2010.
Fimbristylis ferruginea (L.) Vahl var. sieboldii (Miq. ex Franch. & Sav.) Ohwi, J. Jap. Bot. 14: 576. 1938; FRPS 11: 93. 1961.
Fimbristylis ferruginea auct. non (L.) Vahl: FHK 391. 1861; FKH 299. 1912; FRPS 11: 93. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 269. 2000; FGD 8: 303. 2007; Check List HK Plants 314. 2002; 110. 2004.

Perennial; rhizome woody, creeping. Culms tufted, often forming clumps or crowded along creeping rhizome, 15–5 cm tall, 0.5–1.5 mm thick, trigonous, smooth. Leaves arising from lower part of culm; blade narrowly linear, 1–15 cm × 0.6–2.5 mm, obtuse, canaliculate to inrolled-margined; sheath cylindrical 2–12 cm, pale glaucous to brown or orange brown, apex truncate; ligule a fringe of short hairs. Involucral bracts 1–3, leaf-like, the longest ± erect, shorter to longer than inflorescence, 1–3 cm. Inflorescence simple, rarely compound, rather compact, 1.2 – 5 × 1– 3.5 cm; primary branches 3–7, 0.7–4 cm. Spikelets (1–)3–15 per inflorescence, usually solitary, ovoid-conical or ellipsoidal-conical, terete, 8–20 × 2.5–4 mm. Glumes many per spikelet, spirally imbricate, broadly ovateelliptic or broadly ovate, 3.5–4.2 × 1.8–2.8 mm, apex obtuse, mucronate, sides thinly chartaceous, pale to dark brown, sparsely to densely shortly pubescent, margins ciliate, keel obtuse, 1-veined. Stamens 3; anthers 1.5–7 mm. Style long and flat, sparsely ciliate, basally broader; stigmas 2. Achenes broadly obovate, biconvex, 1–1.2 × 0.7–0.8 mm, maturing light orange brown or yellowish brown, ± smooth, with indistinct isodiametric epidermal cells.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. W. Lam 2166; K. L. Yip 4193; Y. S. Lau 2490.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian, Zhejiang, Jiangsu, Anhui, Shandong, Taiwan; Japan, Korea.
Ecology: Margins of ponds and wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Aug.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Aberdeen, Happy Valley, Wu Kai Sha, Tung Chung
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Fimbristylis subbispicata Nees & Meyen 雙穗飄拂草
Nov. Actorum Acad. Caes. Leop.-Carol. Nat. Cur. 29(Suppl. 1): 75. 1843; FHK 391. 1861; FKH 299. 1912; FRPS 11: 95. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 277. 2000; FGD 8: 305. 2007; FOC 23: 213. 2010.

Annual. Rhizome absent. Culms tufted, slim, 7–60 cm tall, flatly trigonous, greyish green, smooth, striate, with few leaves at base. Leaves shorter than culms, ca. 1 mm wide, slightly stiff, flat, upper part ciliate, sometimes involute. Bracts absent or only 1, erect, linear, longer than inflorescence, 0.7–10 cm; spikelet usually single and terminal, rarely 2, ovate, oblong-ovate or oblong-lanceolate, cylindrical, 8–30 × 4–8 mm, many-flowered; glumes spiral, membranous, ovate, broadly ovate or nearly elliptic, 5–7 × 3–4 mm, apex obtuse, mucronate, brown with short rusty-brown lines, not keeled, with many veins abaxially. Stamens 3, anthers linear, 2–2.5 mm. Style slender, compressed, ciliate, base slightly inflated, stigmas 2. Achenes globose to obovoid, flatly biconvex, brown, 1.5–1.7 mm, stipitate, with hexagonal reticulation, slightly shining.

Locality: Aberdeen, Happy Valley, Wu Kai Sha, Tung Chung. J. C. Shaw 667; Y. W. Lam 810, 1621.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian, Zhejiang, Jiangsu, Shandong, Hunan, Henan, Hebei, Shanxi, Shaanxi, Liaoning, Jilin, Heilongjiang, Taiwan; Japan, Korea, Vietnam.
Ecology: Hillslopes, ravines along streams, marshes. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Oct.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Aberdeen, Wong Chuk Hang, Wong Nai Chung
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Fimbristylis tetragona R. Br. 四棱飄拂草
Prodr. 1: 226. 1810; FKH 299. 1912; FRPS 11: 100. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 277. 2000; FGD 8: 308. 2007; FOC 23: 215. 2010.

Annual or perennial. Rhizome poorly developed. Culms densely tufted, 10–60 cm tall, 0.8–1.3 mm thick, sharply 4-angled, smooth. Leaves reduced to bladeless sheaths; sheaths 1 – 15 cm, pale greenish adaxially, yellowish brown abaxially, apex obliquely truncate, broadly hyaline; ligule absent. Inflorescence a single, terminal spikelet. Involucral bracts glume-like, inconspicuous. Spikelets broadly ellipsoidal to ovoid-ellipsoidal, terete, 5–12 × 4–6 mm. Glumes many per spikelet, spirally imbricate, oblong-elliptic, 3–4.5 × 1.2–1.5 mm, apex rounded, incurved, sides membranous, finely many-veined, yellowish brown and often tinged darker brown below keel, keel broad, 3-veined. Stamen 3; anthers 1–1.5 mm. Style long and compressed, sparsely ciliate, basally gradually broader and nearly as wide as nutlet; stigmas 2–3. Achenes linear-oblong to oblong, biconvex, 1.5–1.7 × 0.3–0.4 mm, cream, cancellate with 5 – 8 longitudinal rows of transversely oblong-hexagonal epidermal cells.

Locality: Aberdeen, Wong Chuk Hang, Wong Nai Chung. HK sheet 8085, 39296, 41584.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka, India, Thailand, Indochina, Malaysia, Philippines, Australia.
Ecology: Paddy fields and marshes. Flowering & fruiting: Sep.–Oct.

Fimbristylis thomsonii Boeck. 西南飄拂草
Linnaea 37: 37–38. 1871; FHK 393. 1861; FKH 300. 1912; FRPS 11: 80. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 279. 2000; FYN 15: 602. 2003; FGD 8: 297. 2007; FOC 23: 205. 2010.

Perennial. Rhizomes short, stout. Culms 1–several, 20–80 cm tall, 0.7–2 mm thick, flattened-trigonous, smooth. Leaves basal, 2-ranked; blade linear, up to 40 cm × 2–5 mm, abruptly acuminate, flattish; sheath up to 5 cm, truncate, pale green to rusty brown; ligule a dense fringe of short hairs. Involucral bracts 2–4, the longest suberect, 1–8 cm. Inflorescence compound, rather open, 5–12 × 4–8 cm; primary branches 2–5, 0.7–9 cm. Spikelets oblong-ovoid to ovoid-lanceolate, angular, 5–8 × 2–3 mm. Glumes 6 – 17 per spikelet, spirally arranged, ovate, 3–4 × 2–2.5 mm, acute to mucronate, sides papery, indistinctly 5–7-veined, chestnut-brown, margins membranous, keel acute, green. Stamens 3; anthers 2 mm. Style 3-sided, glabrous, basally inflated; stigmas 3. Achenes obovoid, trigonous, 1.2–1.5 × 0.7–1 mm, whitish yellow, cancellate with several rows of hexagonal to transversely oblong epidermal cells and scattered papillae towards apex.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. J. C. Shaw 390; H. C. Tang 1932; Y. S. Lau 1802.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Taiwan; India, Myanmar, Thailand, Malaysia, Vietnam, Laos, Japan.
Ecology: Thickets and wet grasslands. Flowering & fruiting: May–Jul.

Fimbristylis tomentosa Vahl 絨毛飄拂草
Enum. Pl. 2: 290. 1805; FYN 15: 610. 2003; FGD 8: 304. 2007.
Fimbristylis diphylla (Retz.) Vahl var. tomentosa (Vahl) Benth., FHK 392. 1861.
Fimbristylis podocarpa Nees, Contr. Bot. India 98. 1834; FHK 391. 1861; C. B. Clarke, J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 36: 233. 1903.FKH 299. 1912.
Fimbristylis dichotoma (L.) Vahl subsp. podocarpa (Nees) T. Koyama, Micronesica 1: 87. 1964; FOC 23: 211. 2010.

Caespitose annual; rhizome absent, with fibrous roots. Stems tufted, angular, compressed just below the inflorescence, smooth, 40–60 cm tall, 0.5–1 mm thick. Leaves nearly distichous, ascending, 1/2–3/4 the length of the culms, 2–3 mm wide, flat, abruptly acuminate, softly hairy, rarely glabrous, scabrid on the margins in the upper part; sheaths margin ciliate-scabrid, abaxial surface pilosehirsute. Inflorescence simple or compound, loose, with 5–25 spikelets, very rarely reduced to a single spikelet, up to 8 cm. Involucral bracts up to 5, the longest overtopping the inflorescence, up to 10 cm. Primary anthelas obliquely erect, compressed, glabrous and smooth, the longest 2–4 cm. Spikelets solitary, ovoid or oblong-ovoid, rarely oblong, terete, 5–10(–15) × (1.5–)3–4 mm, apex acute, densely many-flowered, brown; rachilla narrowly winged. Glumes spiral, papery, appressed, broadly ovate or orbicular, 3 – 3.5 × 3.2 – 3.5 mm, apex mucronulate, scarcely keeled, with strong midvein. Stamens (1–)2; anthers oblong-linear, 0.7–1 mm. Style 1.2–1.5 mm, compressed, short and broad, hyaline-margined, gradually but slightly dilated towards the base, ciliate in the upper 2/3–3/4; stigmas 2, shorter than the style. Achene biconvex, broadly elliptic to orbicular, 1.1–1.5 × 0.9–1.4 mm, prominently stipitate (the gynophores obpyramidal, often somewhat saucer-shaped, 0.3–0.5 mm long and wide), umbonulate, sometimes tuberculate, especially towards the obtuse, thickened edges, at first white, finally stramineous, reticulate by the impressed epidermal cells superposed in 16–24 vertical rows on either face, verrucose.

Locality: Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 1256; S. Y. Hu 6266 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Jiangxi, Taiwan, Yunnan; tropical Africa and Asia, Australia.
Ecology: Open places or light shaded moist grasslands.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Cape D'Aguilar, Shek O, Sha Tin
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Fimbristylis tristachya R. Br. 三穗飄拂草
Prodr. 227. 1810; FGD 8: 306. 2007; FOC 23: 213. 2010.

Perennial; rhizome short. Culms tufted, 30–70(–100) cm tall, 1–1.5 mm thick, angular, smooth to scabrid above. Leaves basal; blade narrowly linear, 7–27 cm × 0.5–1.5 mm, apex obtuse to shortly acuminate, flattish to canaliculate; sheath up to 15 cm, yellowish to brown, apex truncate; ligule a fringe of short hairs. Involucral bracts 1–2, leaf-like, the longest suberect, 0.5–3 cm. Inflorescence a single spikelet or simple to compound open; primary branches (when present) 0.8–4 cm. Spikelets (1–)3–6 per inflorescence, solitary, ovoid to ovoid-cylindrical, terete, (6–)10–25 × 4–6 mm. Glumes many per spikelet, spirally arranged, broadly ovate, 4–6 × 3–4.5 mm, apex obtuse, mucronulate, sides papery, indistinctly 7–10-veined, mid- to chestnut-brown, margins scarious, keel obtuse. Stamens 3; anthers 1.8–2.5 mm. Style ca. 3 mm long, compressed, apically ciliate, basally inflated; stigmas 2. Achenes obovate, biconvex, (1–)1.2–1.5 × 0.8–1 mm, rounded, yellowish brown, smooth, somewhat shiny, with minute isodiametric epidermal cells.

Locality: Cape D'Aguilar, Shek O, Sha Tin. Y. S. Lau 2504, 2520; Y. W. Lam 790.
Distribution: Guangdong, Hainan; Asia, tropical Australia, Africa.
Ecology: Thickets and thin forests. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Oct.

Fimbristylis velata R. Br. 曲芒飄拂草
Prodr. 1: 227. 1810; FGD 8: 306. 2007.
Fimbristylis squarrosa Vahl, Enum. Pl. 2: 289. 1805; FHK 392. 1861; FKH 299. 1912; FRPS 11: 97. 1961; FYN 15: 612. 2003.
Fimbristylis aestivalis (Retz.) Vahl var. esquarrosa (Makino) T. Koyama, J. Fac. Sci. Univ. Tokyo 3. 8: 116. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 265. 2000; FOC 23: 214. 2010.

Annual; rhizome absent. Culms densely tufted, 10–25 cm, compressed and obtusely trigonous, with fewer leaves at base. Leaves shorter than culms, extremely narrow, less than 1 mm wide, flat or sometimes folded, sparsely pubescent on both surfaces, sheaths pale brown, densely pubescent. Bracts 3–7, leafy, the lowest equalling or slightly shorter than inflorescence, base broader, pubescent; anthelae compound or decompound, spreading; anthelas many to fewer, up to 2.5 cm, slim; spikelets solitary, lanceolate or oblong, 3–7 × 1.2–2 mm, apex acute, many-flowered; glumes spiral, membranous, oblong, 1.5–2 mm, yellowish brown, obtuse, with 1 midvein abaxially, vein slightly upheaving extending into short awn ca. 1/5 length of glumes, slightly recurved; stamen 1, anther linear, ca. 0.5 mm; style long, slightly compressed, sparsely ciliate, base inflated with white long filiform pendent hairs covering the top of achene; stigmas 2, with papillae. Achenes obovate, flatly biconvex, yellow, ca. 0.5 mm, shortly stipitate, almost smooth or with very indistinct hexagonal reticulation.

Locality: Aberdeen. J. C. Shaw 345; Y. W. Lam 1505.
Distribution: Guangdong, Hainan, Yunnan, Shandong, Hebei, Heilongjiang, Taiwan; India, Myanmar, Japan, Korea, Russia, S Europe to S Africa.
Ecology: Margins of ponds and other wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Oct.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Castle Peak, Sha Tin, Sai Kung
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Fuirena ciliaris (L.) Roxb. 毛芙蘭草
Hort. Beng. 81. 1814, nom. nud.; Fl. Ind. ed. 1820, 1: 184. 1820; FRPS 11: 43. 1961; FHN 4: 279. 1977; FTW ed. 2, 5: 281. 2000; FYN 15: 585. 2003; FGD 8: 286. 2007; FOC 23: 179. 2010.
Scirpus ciliaris L., Mant. Pl. 2: 182. 1771.
Fuirena glomerata Lam., Tabl. Encycl. 1: 150. 1791; FHK 396. 1861.

Annual. Rhizomes short. Culms tufted, 5–50 cm tall, 1–2 mm thick, ciliate-pubescent above. Cauline leaves 5–7; blade linear, 5–15 cm × 3–8 mm, abruptly acute, margins pubescent or ciliate; sheath 1–3 cm, pubescent. Inflorescence with 1–3 clusters of spikelets; peduncles short, ciliate-pubescent. Spikelets ovoid or oblong-ellipsoidal, 4–7 × 3 mm, subacute, squarrose, greyish green. Glumes obovate to obovate-oblong elliptic, 1.5–1.7 × 1.25 mm, apex acute or obtuse, thinly membranous, shortly pubescent outside with pilose centre, awn ca. 1 mm, ciliate. Perianth segments 6; 3 outer ones needle-like, occasionally much reduced, scaberulose or smooth; 3 inner ones with a subquadrate blades, apex mucronate, base abruptly narrowed to a distinct stipe for ca. 0.3 mm long. Stamens 3; Anthers oblong, ca. 0.25 mm. Styles linear, stigmas 3. Achenes obovoid to ellipsoidal, 0.8–1 × 0.5–0.6 mm, brown, smooth to obscurely wrinkled.

Locality: Castle Peak, Sha Tin, Sai Kung. Y. S. Lau 1467; Y. W. Lam 1218; HK sheet 39282.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hubei, Fujian, Jiangsu, Shandong, Taiwan, Yunnan; tropical Africa, Indian Subcontinent, SE Asia, Japan, Malesia and Australia.
Ecology: Margins of ponds and other wet places.

Fuirena umbellata Rottb. 芙蘭草
Descr. Icon. Rar. Nov. Pl. 70, tb. 19, fig. 3. 1773; FHK 395. 1861; FKH 301. 1912; FRPS 11: 44. 1961; FHN 4: 278. 1977; FTW ed. 2, 5: 282. 2000; FYN 15: 587. 2003; FGD 8: 285. 2007; FOC 23: 179. 2010.

Perennial. Rhizomes horizontally creeping. Culms solitary, erect, 30–100 cm tall, 6–9 mm thick, 5-angled, pubescent below inflorescence. Cauline leaves 5–7; blade lanceolate to linearlanceolate, 10–20 cm × 5–25 mm, apex acute, ciliate at base; sheath 2–5 cm, usually glabrous. Inflorescence with 3–12 clusters of spikelets; peduncles whitish villous. Spikelets ovoid or ovoidellipsoidal, ± squarrose, 4–10 × 2.5–3 mm, apex acute, brownish green or dark brownish green. Glumes obovate to ovate elliptic, 2–2.5 × 1.2–1.5 mm, apex rounded, shortly pubescent, awn 0.8–1 mm, often pilose. Perianth segments 3, in 1 whorl only, obovate, all alike, obovate, membranous, truncate, subsessile, gradually narrowed at base. Stamens 3; anthers oblong, 0.5–0.7 mm. Styles linear, stigmas 3, equalling the style. Achenes obovoid to ellipsoidal, 0.8–1.2 × 0.6–0.7 mm, shiny, smooth to obscurely wrinkled.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. P. S. Choi 266, 289; Y. W. Lam 2107.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Xizang, Fujian, Taiwan; pantropics.
Ecology: Moist grasslands, near rivers or in paddy fields.

Gahnia tristis Nees ex Hook. & Arn. 黑莎草
Bot. Beech. Voy 228, 1837 [Linnaea 9: 301. 1834, nom. nud.]; FHK 398. 1861; FKH 303. 1912; FRPS 11: 121. 1961; FHN 4: 303. 1977; Flora Guizhouensis 8: 588. 1988; FTW ed. 2, 5: 283. 2000; FGD 8: 319. 2007; FOC 23: 258. 2010.

Perennial. Culms densely tufted, 50–100 cm tall, 2–5 cm thick, subterete to trigonous, smooth. Leaves basal and cauline; blade rigid, 40–120 cm × 3–12 mm, caudate-acuminate, leathery, margins strongly inrolled, cauline sheaths 7–15 cm, yellowish brown, basal sheaths up to 30 cm, dark or chestnut brown. Involucral bracts several, leaf-like, the lowest up to 30 cm; sheath up to 3 cm. Inflorescence paniculate, resembling a spike, ± cylindrical to linear-oblong, 15–50 × 3–7 cm with 10–28 ± sessile partial inflorescence each 1–5 × 1.2–1.7 mm. Spikelets many, densely clustered, oblong, becoming turbinate in achene, 7–10 mm, 6–8-glumed, 1-flowered. Glumes ovate-lanceolate, 10–12 mm, long-acuminate, sides papery, dark brown, upper 2–3 glumes broadly ovate, much shorter, ciliolate, obtuse to rounded. Perianth segments absent. Stamens 3; filaments slender, enveloped by glumes; anthers linear, 3–4 mm. Stigmas 3. Achenes ellipsoidal, trigonous, 4.5 × 2 mm, conical, dark brown to shiny black, smooth.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. J. C. Shaw 344; H. C. Tang 1931; HK sheet 8198.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangxi, Guangdong, Hunan, Fujian, Jiangsu, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Taiwan; Thailand, Vietnam, Japan, Malaysia.
Ecology: Thickets on hillslopes. Flowering & fruiting: Mar.–Dec.
Uses: Material (oil).

Hypolytrum hainanense (Merr.) Tang & Wang 海南割雞芒
FRPS 11: 201. 1961; FGD 8: 352. 2007 [“hainanensis”]; FOC 23: 169. 2010.
Mapania hainanensis Merr., Lingn. Sci. J. 9: 35. 1903.

Perennial. Roots fibrous. Rhizomes stout, woody. Culms lateral, 30–40 cm tall, 3-angled, basally with several scales and bladeless sheaths. Basal scales broadly ovate. Bladeless sheaths dark greyish brown, densely spirally arranged. Leaves basal, tufted; leaf sheath reddish, to 14 cm, not closed, slightly folded, smooth, margin thickly membranous; leaf blade flat, ca. 1 m × 1–1.8 cm, gradually narrowed towards apex, papery, glabrous, margin and abaxial midvein serrulate. Involucral bracts 2–3, leaf-like, 1.5–5 cm, slightly longer than inflorescence; basalmost bract sheathing. Inflorescences a corymbose panicle congested into a head, 1.3–2 × 1.5– 2.5 cm, with many spikes. Spikes narrowly ellipsoidal, becoming globose in fruit, 5 – 6 mm in diam., with many glume-like bracts and spicoids. Glume-like bracts yellowish brown, spirally and imbricately arranged, oblong-obovate, 2.5–3 mm, leathery, punctate, keeled, each subtending a spicoid. Spicoids ca. 2 mm, with 2 glumes, 2 male flowers, and 1 female flower; glumes dark greyish brown, lateral and opposite, narrowly elliptic and cymbiform, ca. 2.5 mm, keeled, membranous, connate on adaxial side, spinulose on keel, each with a male flower. Anther narrowly oblong; connective apex not prominent beyond anther. Stigmas 2. Achenes dark greyish brown, broadly obovoid to ovoid, ca. 3 mm, biconvex, irregularly longitudinally rugose, apex with a conical beak.

Locality: Tai Po Kau. S. C. Ng 1413.
Distribution: Hainan.
Ecology: Forests and thickets, wet places along streams. Flowering & fruiting: May–Aug.

Hypolytrum nemorum (Vahl) Spreng. 割雞芒（海薄利）
Syst. Veg. 1: 233. 1825; FHN 4: 271. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 283. 2000; FYN 15: 667. 2003; FGD 8: 352. 2007; FOC 23: 168. 2010.
Schoenus nemorum Vahl, Symb. Bot. 3: 8. 1794.
Hypaelyptum nemorum (Vahl) P. Beauv., Fl. Oware 2: 13. 1810.
Hypolytrum latifolium Rich. ex Pers., Syn. Pl. 1: 70. 1805; FHK 389. 1861; FKH 301. 1912; FRPS 11: 199. 1961.

Rhizomes short, slightly thick, woody, with dense reddish scales. Culms central, 35–90 cm tall, 1–3 mm thick, trigonous, smooth to scabrid. Leaves mostly basal or 1–2 cauline; blade linear, 6–130 × 1–2.3 cm, apex and base gradually narrowed, 3-veined; pseudopetiole absent; basal sheaths 2–15 cm, reddish brown to purple, cauline sheaths light purple or cinnamon brown. Involucral bracts 2–3, leaf-like, 10–40 cm, much longer than the inflorescence. Inflorescence an open panicle, hemispherical or broadly ovoid, 2–7 × 3–10 cm, comprising up to 10 primary peduncles each subtending up to 6 secondary peduncles terminating in 1–3 sessile or shortly stalked spikes. Spikes ± elliptic-globose, 3–7 × 2.5–6 mm, light to mid-brown. Spicoids bracts ovateorbicular 1.3–2.5 × 1.2–2 mm, apex rounded. Spicoids ± equalling the spicoid bracts. Floral bracts 2, free or ± connate on abaxial side, 1.2–1.8 mm long, keel ciliate. Stigmas 3. Achenes broadly ovoid, 1.8–3 × 1.3–1.5 mm, apex conical, irregularly 2–5-ridged.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 2247; Y. W. Lam 1308, 2052.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Taiwan; tropical Asia, Africa.
Ecology: Forests and thickets. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Aug.

Juncellus serotinus (Rottb.) C. B. Clarke 水莎草
Fl. Brit. India 6: 594. 1893; FKH 294. 1912; FRPS 11: 159. 1961; FYN 15: 644. 2003; FGD 8: 335. 2007.
Cyperus serotinus Rottb., Descr. Icon. Rar. Pl. 31. 1773; FTW ed. 2, 5: 250. 2000; FOC 23: 239. 2010.

Perennial; rhizomes stoloniferous, slender stolons terminated by a small tuber. Culms solitary or a few together, erect, 40–100 cm tall, triquetrous with shallowly concave sides, rather soft. Leaves few, usually shorter than the culms, rarely slightly overtopping culm; blades linear, 3–10 mm wide, folded toward base, flattish above, soft; sheaths brownish. Corymbs compound, sublax, 7–15 cm long and as wide; anthelas 5–7, unequal, 2–16 cm, each bearing 1–3 spikes; spikes ovate-elliptic, 2–4 cm, subloosely bearing 5–17 spikelets; rachis hispidulous to nearly smooth; leafy bracts 3–4, lowest to 8 mm wide, to twice as long as corymb. Spikelets patent, linear to linear-lanceolate, 1–2 cm × 2–2.75 mm, 10–34-flowered. Glumes broadly ovate, 2–2.5 × 2 mm, reddish brown to dark brown, apex obtuse, 5–7-veined, keel greenish. Stamens 3; anthers linear. Style short; stigmas 2. Achenes orbicular-obovate, plano-convex, 1.5 mm, greyish brown.

Locality: New Territories. W. J. Tutcher 8115; S. Y. Hu 8281 (CUHK).
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; Korea, Japan, NW Himalaya, C Europe, Mediterranean region.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Oct.

Kyllinga brevifolia Rottb. 短葉水蜈蚣
Descr. Icon. Rar. Pl. 13, pl. 4, fig. 3. 1773; FKH 297. 1912; FRPS 11: 187. 1961; Flora Guizhouensis 8: 610. 1988; FTW ed. 2, 5: 284. 2000; FYN 15: 658. 2003; FGD 8: 347. 2007; FOC 23: 248. 2010.
Cyperus brevifolia (Rottb.) Hassk., Cat. Hort. Bot. Bogor. 24. 1844.

Perennial; rhizome slender, long-creeping. Culms arranged in a row along the rhizome, 7–30 cm tall, 1–1.5 mm thick, triquetrous, smooth. Leaves radical and subradical; blade narrowly linear, 2–17 × 1–3 mm, acute, flattish-plicate; sheath 1–20 cm, brownish to purplish brown. Involucral bracts 2–4, the longest 3–20 cm × 1.7–2.4 mm, sometimes erect. Inflorescence capitate, globose. Spikes 1(–3), globose, 0.5–1 × 0.5–1 cm. Spikelets oblonglanceolate to elliptic-lanceolate, 3–3.5 × 1 mm, 1(–2)-flowered. Glumes ovate-elliptic, 1–3.5 mm, shortly cuspidate, sides membranous, 5–7-veined, pale green to pale brown, keel sparsely spinulose, green. Stamens 1–3; anthers 1 mm long. Style slender; stigmas 2. Achenes 1–2 per spike, obovate or elliptic, 1–1.5 × 0.5–0.7 mm, brownish, minutely punctate.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. W. Lam 329; S. P. Lau 5; K. L. Yip 4079.
Distribution: Widely spread over Areas S of Changjiang; tropics.
Ecology: Thickets on hillslopes, wet places. Flowering & fruiting: May–Sep.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Authority: (J. R. Forst. & G. Forst.) Dandy ex Hutch. & Dalziel
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Kyllinga nemoralis (J. R. Forst. & G. Forst.) Dandy ex Hutch. & Dalz. 單穗水蜈蚣
Fl. W. Trop. Afr. 2: 486. 1936; FTW ed. 2, 5: 286. 2002; FYN 15: 659. 2003; FGD 8: 346. 2007; FOC 23: 249. 2010.
Thryocephalon nemorale J. R. Forst. & G. Forst., Char. Gen. Pl. (ed. 2) 129–130, pl. 65. 1776.
Kyllinga monocephala Rottb., Descr. Icon. Rar. Nov. Pl. 13, t. 4, fig. 4. 1773, nom. illeg.; FHK 388. 1861; FKH 296. 1912; FRPS 11: 190. 1961; Check List HK Plants 317. 2002; 111. 2004.
Kyllinga triceps auct. non Rottb.: FKH 297. 1912; Check List HK Plants 88. 1993.

Perennial. Rhizome long creeping. Culms tufted, close together or spaced along rhizome, erect, 10–45 cm tall, triquetrous, not thickened at base. Leaves many, usually shorter than culm; blades narrowly linear, 2–5 mm wide, rather soft, flattish; sheaths brown to purplish brownish. Inflorescence a single head, bearing a globose central spike and 2–3 small lateral spikes; central spike 5–10 × 5–7 mm, densely bearing many spikelets, whitish; leafy bracts 3–4, spreading to reflexed, lowest to 30 cm. Spikelets ovate-elliptic to lanceolate-ovate, 2.7–3.5 × 1.5 mm, 1-flowered. Glumes usually 5, lowest two smaller or narrow, 1–1.5 mm, remaining glumes 2.5–3.5 mm, boat-shaped, thinly membranous, whitish and eventually becoming straw-coloured, variegate with rusty brown, 3–4-veined on each side, broadly winged on acute green keel, wing serrulate, keel ending in a short usually recurved cusp. Stamens 3. Style slender, stigmas 2. Achenes oblong-obovate or suborbicular, biconvex, 1.25–1.5 mm, maturing brownish.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. S. P. Lau 5; J. C. Shaw 569; K. L. Yip 4018.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Yunnan, Taiwan; Bhutan, Nepal, Pakistan, India, Sri Lanka, Myanmar, Thailand, Laos, Cambodia, Vietnam, Malaysia, Indonesia, Philippines, Puapua New Guinea, Japan, Australia, Madagascar, tropical Africa, Indian Ocean islands, Pacific islands.
Ecology: Wastelands. Flowering & fruiting: May–Aug.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Victoria Park, Tsiu Hang, Tai Po Kau
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Kyllinga polyphylla Willd. ex Kunth 水蜈蚣（香根水蜈蚣）
Enum. Pl. 2: 134. 1837; FOC 23: 248. 2010.
Kyllinga aromatica Ridl., Trans. Linn. Soc. London, Bot. 2: 146. 1884.

Perennial; rhizome horizontally creeping. Culms crowded in series along rhizome, up to 75 cm tall, triquetrous, smooth. Leave on uppermost 1–2 sheaths only, linear-lanceolate, 2–6.5 × 0.4–0.5 cm, apex acute, flat; sheaths up to 15 cm, greenish to purplish. Involucral bracts 4–7, linear, the longest up to 14 cm. Inflorescence capitate. Spikes 4–5; terminal spike ± spherical, 0.7 × 0.7 cm, lateral spikes smaller, in axils of involucral bracts. Spikelets elliptic, 3–3.7 × 0.8–0.9 mm, 1–2-flowered. Glumes ovate-elliptic, 2.5–3 × 2 mm, apex obtuse, shortly mucronate, sides membranous, indistinctly 3–5-veined, whitish to pale greenish, keel greenish, smooth to sparsely toothed. Stamens 1; anther 1–1.2 mm. Stamens 3; anther linear. Style slender; stigmas 2. Achenes oblong-obovate, 1 × 0.6 mm, greyish brown.

Locality: Victoria Park, Tsiu Hang, Tai Po Kau. Y. S. Lau 2254, 3090; Y. W. Lam 327.
Distribution: Taiwan; native to W Africa, widely cultivated.
Ecology: Wastelands. Flowering & fruiting: May–Aug.
Uses: Spice.
Notes: The species was reported as Kyllinga aromatica (Ridl.) Mattf. & Kunth previously (Check List HK Plants 316. 2002; 111. 2004).

Lepidosperma chinense Nees 鱗子莎
Linnaea 9: 302. 1834; FHK 398. 1861; FKH 302. 1912; FRPS 11: 120. 1961; FGD 8: 321. 2007; FOC 23: 260. 2010.

Perennial; rhizome stout, short. Culms slender to rather stout, rigid, (25–)40–150(–250) cm tall, 1–3 mm thick, subterete or slightly angular, smooth, few-leaved at the base. Leaves shorter than the stems, almost terete, 2–4 mm thick, with a shallow, very inconspicuous groove, rigid, glaucous, pith chambered by many approximate transverse partitions; sheaths chestnut-coloured, lower ones bladeless. Panicle narrowly oblong, dense, often somewhat interrupted at the base, 3–10 cm, consisting of several oblong-lanceolate, suberect spikes. Involucral bracts spathe-like, shortly sheathing, blackish brown, rounded at the apex, the lowest ending in a short pungent blade. Spikelets crowded, oblonglanceolate, 5–6 mm, 2-flowered. Glumes 5–7, firm, oblong to lanceolate, 3–5 mm, black with rusty margins, apex obtuse to acute, the empty ones mucronulate, the upper ones subacute. Hypogynous scales small, connate at the base, whitish, 0.5–0.7 mm. Stamens 3, anthers ca. 2 mm, yellow. Styles slender, stigmas 3. Achene ellipsoidal, 2.5–4 × 1.5–3 mm, apiculate, shining rusty, purplish dotted.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. J. C. Shaw 493; Y. W. Lam 1330; Y. S. Lau 2479.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan, Hunan, Fujian, Zhejiang; Vietnam, Malaysia, Indonesia, Papua New Guinea.
Ecology: Grasslands in valleys. Flowering & fruiting: May–Dec.

Lepironia articulata (Retz.) Domin. 石龍芻（蒲草、肇慶草）
Biblioth. Bot. 85: 486. 1915; FHN 4: 269. 1977; FTW ed. 2, 5: 286. 2000; FGD 8: 349. 2007; FOC 23: 171. 2010.
Restio articulatus Retz., Observ. Bot. 4: 14. 1786.
Lepironia mucronata Rich., Syn. Pl. 1: 70. 1805; FKH 301. 1912; FRPS 11: 202. 1961.

Perennial. Rhizome with greyish brown scales at least distally. Culms crowded in row along rhizome, stiff, 10–120 cm tall, 2–7 mm thick, terete, smooth. Leaf sheath open, the uppermost 12–26 cm long. Apex obliquely truncate. Involucral bract subulate, terete, 2.2–6 cm long. Inflorescence comprising 1 spike. Spike elliptic or oblong, terete, 10–35 × 3–7 mm, green to chestnut brown or purplish brown. Spicoid bracts oval, ovate-orbicular, 3.2–6.7 × 3–6.2 mm, apex rounded and often weakly recurved, easily detaching when mature. Spicoids ± equalling spicoid bracts. Floral bracts up to 15, lowest 2 linear-lanceolate, 4–6 mm long, keel ciliate. Achenes ovate or obovate to broadly obovate, biconvex, 3–4 × 2–2.8 mm (excluding 0.5 mm long beak), hard, brown, ± smooth to indistinctly longitudinally veined, often spinulose at apex.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. Y. W. Lam 1776; K. L. Yip 4204; HK sheet 20634.
Distribution: Guangdong; Madagascar, India, Sri Lanka, Laos, Thailand, Vietnam, Cambodia, Malesia, Micronesia, Australia, New Caledonia and Fiji.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Feb.–Jun.
Uses: Weaving.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Aberdeen, Happy Valley, Yung Shue O, Wu Kau Tang, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Lipocarpha chinensis (Osbeck) Kern 華湖瓜草
Blumea, Suppl. 4: 167. 1958; FRPS 11: 192. 1961; FHN 4: 373. 1977; Flora Guizhouensis 8: 613. 1988; FTW ed. 2, 5: 287. 2000; FYN 15: 662. 2003; FGD 8: 348. 2007; FOC 23: 250. 2010.
Scirpus chinensis Osbeck, Dagb. Ostind. Resa 220. 1757.
Scirpus senegalensis Lam., Tabl. Encycl. 1: 140. 1791.
Lipocarpha senegalensis (Lam.) T. Durand & H. Durand, Syll. Fl. Congol. 619. 1909; Flora Guizhouensis 8: 613. 1988.
Lipocarpha argentea R. Br., Narr. Exped. Zaire 459. 1818, nom. illeg.; FHK 388. 1861; FKH 301. 1912.

Annual or perennial. Rhizome absent. Clums tufted, 15–70 cm tall, 1–2 mm thick, flat or compressed triquetrous, longitudinally sulcate, sparsely puberulent. Leaves basal; blade up to 40 cm × 2–4 mm, ± flat, apex acuminate; sheath 1–15 cm, reddish brown or reddish purple, glabrous. Involucral bract 2–3(–5), the longest up to 20 cm, basal ones bladeless, apical ones leaved. Inflorescence terminal clustered spikes. Spikes (1–)3–10, oblong or ovoid-ellipsoidal, 5–8 × 4–5 mm. Spikelet bracts spathulate to obovate or oblong, 1.5–2.7 × 0.4–1.3 mm, triangular-acute, apical part 1 2 mm long, membranous, white to pale yellowish or greenish brown, midvein green. Spikelets with two glumes and 1 bisexual flower; glumes elliptic or ovate-lanceolate, 1.5–2 mm, apex obtuse or acute. Stamens 2; anthers narrowly oblong, ca. 1 mm long. Style slender; stigmas 3, puberulent. Achenes oblong or oblong-ovoid, trigonous, 1–1.2 × 0.3–0.5 mm, pale yellowish brown.

Locality: Aberdeen, Happy Valley, Yung Shue O, Wu Kau Tang, Lantau Island. Y. W. Lam 2155; J. C. Shaw & G. Reels 258; HK sheet 42192.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Hunan, Jiangxi, Shandong, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; tropical Asia, Africa, Australia.
Ecology: Marshes, paddy fields and other wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Oct.

Lipocarpha microcephala (R. Br.) Kunth 湖瓜草
Enum. Pl. 2: 268. 1837; FHK 388. 1861; FKH 301. 1912; FHN 4: 273. 1977; FTW ed. 2, 5: 287. 2000; FYN 15: 664. 2003; FGD 8: 348. 2007; FOC 23: 250. 2010.
Hypaelyptum microcephalum R. Br., Prodr. 220. 1810.

Annual. Rhizome absent. Clums densely tufted, 5–40 cm tall, 0.5–1 mm thick. Leaves basal; blade up to 10 cm × 1–2 mm, flattish or weakly inrolled; sheath up to 3 cm, pale to purplish brown. Involucral bracts 2–3, the longest 5–10 cm. Inflorescence terminal. Spikes (1–)2–4(–5), ellipsoidal to ovoid-ellipsoidal, 3–8 × 2–3 mm. Spikelet bracts obovate-oblong, 1–1.5 × 0.2–0.4 mm, acuminate, the apical part recurved, 0.5–0.8 mm, scaberulous at tip, yellowish to brown, midvein green. Spikelets with 2 glumes and 1 bisexual flower. Glumes linear-oblong to oblong-lanceolate, 1–1.3 × 0.2 mm, white, 5-veined, apex obtuse or acute. Stamens 2; anthers linearoblong, 2–3 mm. Style slender, exserted from subtending glumes; stigmas 3, puberulent. Achenes linear-oblong, often slightly curved, trigonous, 0.9–1 × 0.2–0.3 mm, yellowish brown, densely puncticulate, shiny, apex acuminate.

Locality: Fanling, Yung Shue O. S. P. Lau 23; HK sheet 13660, 42164.
Distribution: Widely spread over NE, E, S & SW China; Japan, Korea, Vietnam, Cambodia, Laos, Myanmar, Thailand, India, Malaysia, Indonesia, Philippines, Papua New Guinea, Australia.
Ecology: Wet places. Flowering & fruiting: May–Oct.

Machaerina ensigera (Hance) T. Koyama 劍葉莎
Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 69: 63. 1956; FOC 23: 259. 2010.
Cladium ensigerum Hance, J. Bot. 23: 80. 1885; FKH 302. 1912; FRPS 11: 119. 1961.
Baumea ensigera (Hance) S. T. Blake, Contr. Queensland Herb. 8: 29. 1969.
Mariscus ensiger (Hance) Fernald, Rhodora 25: 53. 1923.
Rhizomes horizontal, 4.5–7 mm thick. Culms flattened.

Leaves basal; blade ensiform, 3.8–50 × (0.7–)1–2.5 cm, rigid, manyveined, margin purple, finely scabrous, and denticulate. Inflorescences paniculate, narrow, usually 3-branched. Spikelets purple, ca. 11.3 × 3.5 mm, 2–3-flowered. Glumes ovate-lanceolate, apex acuminate. Achene subdrupaceous, ellipsoidal, 3-furrowed, glabrous; persistent style base thickened.

Locality: Pok Fu Lam, Sai Kung. HK sheet 8180, 8181.
Distribution: Endemic to Hong Kong.
Ecology: Forests, streamsides. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Aug.
Notes: The type specimen of Cladium ensigerum (Hance Herb. No. 22181) was collected by C. Ford from Pok Fu Lam in May 1883. The species is very close to M. myriantha (Chun & F. C. How) Y. C. Tang and differs in its leaf blades being shorter, to 50 cm, margin serrulate and spikes 1–1.2 cm long.

Machaerina rubiginosa (Spreng.) T. Koyama 圓葉劍葉莎
Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 69: 65. 1956; FOC 23: 259. 2010.
Schoenus rubiginosus Sol. ex G. Forst., Fl. Ins. Austr. 89. 1786.
Fuirena rubiginosa Spreng., Mant. Prima Fl. Hal. 29. 1807.
Cladium glomeratum auct. non R. Br. ex C. B. Clarke: FKH 302. 1912.

Perennial; rhizome short, emitting long horizontal stolons covered with 2-ranked, pale, lanceolate scales. Culms tufted, slender, compressed-biconvex to subterete, usually with 1 node above the base, smooth, (30–)100–180 cm tall, (2–)3–6 mm thick. Basal leaves shorter than to about as long as stems, erect, biconvex with obtuse edges to subterete, smooth, pungent, spongiose inside, (2–)4–7 mm wide; cauline leaf long-sheathing, with short blade. Panicle erect, narrow, dense or interrupted, (10–)20–50 cm, consisting of 3–7 fascicles of branches, the lower branches distant, subtended by long-sheathing, shortly laminate bracts; upper branches approximate, their bracts gradually shorter. Lower branches often solitary, up to 25 cm, upper ones 2–4 together, erect, rigid, scabrous, much shorter. Spikelets in oblong to almost globose clusters, lanceolate or finally ovate, 2–3-flowered, maturing 1–2 achenes, 4–7 × 2–2.5 mm. Glumes 5, ovate to lanceolate, acuminate, long-ciliate, the longest 4.5–6.5 mm. Perianth segments absent. Stamens 3; anthers 1.5–2 mm, with distinctly produced connective. Stigmas 3. Achenes ellipsoidal to oblong-ellipsoidal, trigonous, sessile, smooth, shining, orange to reddish-brown, 3–5 × 1.5–2 mm, densely pubescent, persistent style base included.

Locality: Hong Kong. HK sheet 8197.
Distribution: Yunnan; Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, India, Indoneasia, Philippines, New Guinea, Japan, New Zealand, Australia.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Aug.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Sai Kung, Wong Chuk Yeung, Pat Sin Leng, Wang Shan Keuk
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Mapania silhetensis C. B. Clarke 華擂鼓藶（擂鼓藶）
Fl. Brit. India 6: 681. 1894; FOC 23: 170. 2010.
Mapania sinensis H. Uittien, Recueil Trav. Bot. Néerl. 33: 288. 1936; FRPS 11: 197. 1961.
Mapania wallichii auct. non C. B. Clarke: FGD 8: 350. 2007, p.p. quod syn. M. sinensis H. Uittien; Check List HK Plants 317. 2002.

Perennial. Rhizomes thick, woody. Culms lateral, 25–55 cm tall, ca. 3 mm thick, with several cataphylls toward base. Leaves basal, distichous; leaf sheath brownish, ca. 12 cm, margin thickly membranous; leaf blade ca. 130 × 2.5–3.5 cm or longer, subleathery, smooth, 3-veined, apical margin and abaxial midvein serrulate, apex caudate to acuminate. Involucral bracts brown, glumelike, ovate to ovate-deltate, 1.5–2.5 cm, shorter than inflorescence, leathery, apex acute. Inflorescences capitate, broadly ovoid, 2–4.5 × 1.5–2 cm, with 4 spikes fascicled at apex of culm, with many glume-like bracts and spicoids. Glume-like bracts straw-coloured, spirally and imbricately arranged, narrowly oblong, ca. 1 cm, papery, apex obtuse. Spicoids with 6 glumes, 3 male flowers, and 1 female flower; basal 2 glumes opposite, cymbiform, membranous, keeled, spinulose on apical part of keel, each subtending 1 male flower; remaining 4 bracts narrowly oblong, outermost one subtending a male flower. Filaments to 1.6 cm; anthers linear, 7–8 mm. Style ca. 6.5 mm; stigmas 3. Achene dark brown, obovoid, 4–4.5 mm, obtusely 3-sided, outer surface succulent, apex conically rostrate.

Locality: Sai Kung, Wong Chuk Yeung, Pat Sin Leng, Wang Shan Keuk. F. W. Xing 6973, 7161.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi; Bangladesh, India, Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering & fruiting: Sep.–Oct.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Cape D'Aguilar, Shing Mun, Hong Kong Wetland Park, Hau Hok Wan
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Mariscus cyperinus (Retz.) Vahl 莎草磚子苗
Enum. Pl. 2: 377. 1805; FKH 296. 1912; FRPS 11: 182. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 290. 2000; FYN 15: 655. 2003; FGD 8: 343. 2007.
Kyllinga cyperina Retz., Observ. Bot. 6: 21. 1791
Cyperus cyperinus (Retz.) J. V. Suringar, Cyperus, 154. 1898; FOC 23: 238. 2010.
Mariscus sieberianus Nees ex C. B. Clarke, Fl. Brit. India 6: 622. 1893; FKH 296. 1912.
Cyperus umbellatus auct. non (Vahl) Benth.: FHK 386. 1861.

Perennial. Rhizome short, woody, clothed with brown fibers. Culms solitary or few together, erect, 20–70 cm tall, triquetrous, smooth, leaved at ± thickened base. Leaves several, shorter than culm; blades narrowly linear, 5–7 mm wide, herbaceous, flattish plicate; sheaths pale green and stained with purplish pink. Corymbs simple, open, with short anthelas, sometimes nearly head-like; anthelas 6–10, 0–5 cm, each terminated by a cylindrical or oblong, spike narrowed to base, 1.5–3 × 8–12 mm, greenish, densely bearing many spikelets; leafy bracts 4–10, lower few surpassing corymb. Spikelets patent to erect-patent, linear-lanceolate, subterete, 4–6.5 mm × 1 mm, bearing 4–7 glumes and 2–3 achenes; rachilla with lanceolate wings, jointed above prophyll. Glumes tightly erect, elliptic to oblong-elliptic, 3–3.5 mm, inrolled, membranous to thinly chartaceous, obtuse or suddenly acute at apex, glaucous green and eventually tinged with straw-brown, 3–4-veined on both sides, green keel convex. Stamens 3; anthers linear. Style slightly longer than achene; stigmas 3. Achenes linear-oblong, trigonous, 1.5–1.8 × 0.6–0.9 mm, brown, minutely granulate.

Locality: Cape D'Aguilar, Shing Mun, Hong Kong Wetland Park, Hau Hok Wan. J. C. Shaw 411, 456; HK sheet 42176.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Sichuan, Hunan, Fujian, Jiangxi, Taiwan, Zhejiang, Sichuan; Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, Nepal, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Thailand, Vietnam, Malaysia, Indonesia, Philippines, Papua New Guinea, Japan, Australia, SW Asia, Pacific islands, Indian Ocean islands.
Ecology: Moist grasslands of valleys and hillslopes. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Sep.

Mariscus cyperoides (L.) Urb. 磚子苗
Symb. Antill. 2(1): 164. 1900; FGD 8: 342. 2007.
Scirpus cyperoides L., Mant. Pl. 2: 181. 1771.
Mariscus umbellatus (Rottb.) Vahl, Enum. Pl. 2: 376. 1805; FRPS 11: 179. 1961; Flora Guizhouensis 8: 608. 1988.
Kyllinga umbellata Rottb., Descr. Icon. Rar. Pl. 1773; Check List HK Plants 357. 2004.
Cyperus umbellatus Benth., FHK 386. 1861.
Mariscus sumatrensis (Retz.) J. Anthelanal, Adansonia n. s. 15: 110. 1975; FTW ed. 2, 5: 291. 2000; FYN 15: 654. 2003.
Kyllinga sumatrensis Retz., Observ. Bot. 4: 13. 1786.
Mariscus albescens Gaudich., Voy. Bonite, Bot. 415. 1826; FKH 296. 1912.

Perennial with short woody rhizome clothed with brown fibers. Culms solitary or few together, erect, triquetrous, 10–50 cm tall, smooth, ± thickened base leafy. Leaves rather many, shorter than to equalling culm; blades linear, 3–6 mm wide, flattish plicate, herbaceous; sheaths pale, eventually becoming brownish or reddish brownish. Corymbs simple, open, 3–8 cm wide; anthelas 3–12, patent, longer ones to 8 cm, terminated by a spike; spikes cylindrical, 1–2.5 cm × 6–10 mm, densely bearing many spikelets, greenish; leafy bracts 3–8, lower ones surpassing corymb. Spikelets spreading or lower ones ± reflexed, linear-lanceolate, 3–5 × 0.7 mm, bearing 4–5 glumes, 1–2-fruited; rachilla jointed above base, with white-hyaline lanceolate wings. Glumes lanceolate-oblong, ca. 3 mm long, membranous, pale green, apex obtuse or mucronate, margined inrolled, several-veined, keel 3-veined, forming an obtuse back. Stamens 3; anthers linear. Style ca. 1 mm; stigmas 3. Achenes linear-oblong, ca. 2 mm long, straw-coloured, minutely puncticulate.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. J. C. Shaw 483; K. L. Yip 4080; Y. W. Lam 754.
Distribution: S, E, C & SW China; SE Asia, Himalaya, Africa, Australia, America.
Ecology: Grasslands of hillslopes. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Oct.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Pok Fu Lam, Shek O, Sha Tin
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Mariscus javanicus (Houtt.) Merr. & F. T. Metc. 羽穗磚子苗
Lingnan Sci. J. 21: 4. 1945; FRPS 11: 177. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 290. 2000; FGD 8: 340. 2007.
Cyperus javanicus Houtt., Nat. Hist. 2: 13, pl. 88, fig. 1. 1782; FOC 23: 237. 2010.

Coarse perennial. Rhizome short, woody, thick. Culms tufted, robust, 40–110 cm tall, 3–5 mm thick, obtusely trigonous, minutely granulate, glaucous green. Leaves many, mostly surpassing culms; blades linear, 8–12 mm wide, leathery, plicate below middle, flattish to incurvd-marginate above middle, glaucous-green and often whitish powdery, separate-nodulose, prominently scabrous on margins; sheaths dark brown or purplish brown, cylindrical, septate-nodulose. Corymbs compound to decompound, ample, 10–15 cm; primary anthelas 6–10(–12) cm, patent, subrigid; secondary corymbs with 3–6 anthelalets; spikes cylindrical to oblong, 1.5–3 × 8–12 mm, bearing many spikelets; leafy bracts 5–6, lower ones much surpassing corymb. Spikelets divergent to slightly reflexed, lanceolate to oblong-lanceolate, 4.5–6 × 1.8–2 mm, turgid, 4–6-flowered; rhachilla rather broadly winged, jointed above prophyll. Glumes broadly ovate, ca. 3 mm, subleathery, brownish with rusty lineaolate, apex acuminate, margins whitish hyaline, many-veined; keel hardly ridged, forming an obtuse back. Stamens 3; anther linear. Style slender, 1–1.5 mm; stigmas 3. Achenes oval to obovate, trigonous, ca. 1/2 as long as glume, black-brown at maturity, minutely puncticulate; style elongate.

Locality: Pok Fu Lam, Shek O, Sha Tin. Y. W. Lam 755; Y. S. Lau 2305; HK sheet 7848.
Distribution: Guangdong, Hainan, Taiwan; Sri Lanka, India, Cambodia, Vietnam, Myanmar, Thailand, Malaysia, Philippines, Japan, Madagascar, tropical Africa, Australia, Hawaii.
Ecology: Sandy beaches, marshes. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Jul.

Mariscus radians (Nees & Meyen) Tang & F. T. Wang 輻射磚子苗
FRPS 11: 177. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 290. 2000; FGD 8: 341. 2007.
Cyperus radians Nees & Meyen ex Kunth, Enum. Pl. 2: 95. 1837 [“radiates”]; FHK 386. 1861; FKH 295. 1912; FOC 23: 225. 2010.

Perennial. Rhizome short, clothed with brownish fibers. Culms ± tufted, very low, 2–6 cm tall; obtusely trigonous smooth, usually hidden in leaf tuft, which much surpass culm. Leaves several, surpassing corymb; blades linear, plicate, 2–4 mm wide, stiffish; sheaths purplish brown. Corymbs simple with 2–7 elongate anthelas; anthelas somewhat unequal, patent, lower ones 9 – 12 cm, each terminated by a head-like cluster of spikelets; leafy bracts 3–7, equalling or shorter than corymb anthelas. Heads globose, 8–25 mm across, bearing 5–20 spikelets. Spikelets ovate to lanceolate-ovate, 6–12 × 2–4 mm, slightly turgid, bearing 4–15 flowers, pale green and tinged with brown. Glumes broadly ovate, 3.5–4 mm, papery, pale-green with purplish brown striate, sometimes tinged with purple brown, 11–13-veined, greenish keel convex, ending in a short recurved cusp at acute apex of glume. Stamens 3; anther broadly linear. Style slender; stigmas 3. Achene oval, trigonous with shallowly concave sides, 1.5–2 mm, dark brown, style elongate.

Locality: Sai Kung. S. C. Ng 2212.
Distribution: Guangdong, Fujian, Zhejiang, Shandong, Taiwan; Sri Lanka, Vietnam, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia.
Ecology: Sandy beach. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Sep.

Pycreus flavidus (Retz.) T. Koyama 球穗扁莎
J. Jap. Bot. 51: 316. 1976; FTW ed. 2, 5: 292. 2000; FYN 15: 648. 2003; FGD 8: 337. 2007; FOC. 23: 343. 2010.
Cyperus flavidus Retz., Observ. Bot. 5: 13. 1788.
Pycreus globosus Rchb., Fl. Germ. Excurs. 140. 1830; FKH 294. 1912; FRPS 11: 166. 1961.
Cyperus vulgaris Siebold ex Kunth, Enum. Pl. 2: 4. 1837; FHK 385. 1861.

Annual or perennial. Rhizome short; roots fibrous. Culms densely tufted, 8–60 cm tall, 1–1.5 mm thick, trigonous, smooth. Leaves shorter than culm; blade narrowly linear to setaceous, 2–24 cm × 1–2 mm, acuminate, flattish-plicate or canaliculate; sheath 1–10 cm, reddish brown. Involucral bracts 2–4, the longest up to 25 cm. Inflorescence simple, open congested and appearing ± capitate; primary branches   6, 0.5–7 cm. Spikes broadly ovoid to ± globose, 1–3 × 1.2–4 cm; axis 0.1–1 cm. Spikelets 5–20 per spike, spreading, linear or linear-oblong, 6 – 30 × 1.5–3 mm, axis straight. Glumes oblong-obovate, 1.5–2.5 × 1  .5 mm, narrowly obtuse, sides chartaceous, pale brown to dark reddish brown, shiny, margins pale-hyaline, keel acute, 3-veined, greenish. Stamens 2; anthers 0.5 mm. Style short; stigmas 2. Achenes narrowly obovate to oblong-elliptic, 0.8–1.2 × 0.4–0.6 mm, dark brown, minutely punctate.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. J. C. Shaw & G. Reels 259; Y. S. Lau 2540; K. L. Yip 4044.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China except NW regions; Japan, Korea, Mediterranean regions, S Africa, Australia.
Ecology: Wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Nov.

Pycreus polystachyos (Rottb.) P. Beauv. 多枝扁莎（多穗扁莎）
Fl. Oware 2: 48, t. 86, f. 2. 1807 [“polystachyus”]; FKH 294. 1912; FRPS 11: 169. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 292. 2000; FGD 8: 337. 2007; FOC 23: 244. 2010.
Cyperus polystachyus Rottb., Descr. Icon. Rar. Pl. 21. 1773 [“polystachyus”]; FHK 385. 1861.

Annual or short-lived perennial. Rhizome absent; roots fibrous. Clums tufted, 10–80 cm tall, 1–3 mm thick, trigonous to triquetrous above, smooth. Leaves shorter than culm; blade linear, 4–25 cm × 1.5–3(–4) mm, apex acuminate, flattish-plicate, soft or subrigid; sheaths reddish brown. Involucral bract 3–5, lowest up to 20 cm. Inflorescence simple, open to congested or ± capitate; primary branches (when present) 2–8, up to 7 cm. Spikes 1.8–3 × 1.3–2.2 cm; axis 0.1–0.8 cm. Spikelets 4–25 per spike, erect or erect-patent, crowded, linear to linear-lanceolate, 5–13 × 1.5–2 mm, flattened; axis zigzag. Glumes oblong-ovate to ovate-elliptic, 1.7–2.5 × 0.8–1 mm, apex acute to sometimes narrowly obtuse, mucronate, sides thinly chartaceous, pale brown or greenish to reddish brown, margins narrowly white-hyaline, keel acute, 3-veined, greenish. Stamens (1–)2; anthers 0.5–1 mm. Style slender; stigmas 2. Achenes oblong to oblongobovoid, 1–1.5 × 0.5 mm, dark brown, minutely punctate.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. L. T. Lo 91; HK sheet 30228, 39701.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Taiwan, Liaoning; tropical and warm temperate regions of the world.
Ecology: Streamsides and other wet places. Flowering & fruiting: May–Oct.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Aberdeen, Sheung Shui, Tai Mo Shan, Tai Wan (Sai Kung), Po Toi Islands
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Pycreus pumilus (L.) Domin 矮扁莎
Bibliogr. Bot. Cracow 85: 417. 1915; FRPS 11: 170. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 293. 2000; FGD 8: 336. 2007; FOC 23: 245. 2010.
Cyperus pumilus L., Cent. Pl. II 6. 1756.
Pycreus pulvinatus Nees, Contrib. 74. 1834; FKH 294. 1912.

Annual. Culms tufted, 1–20 cm tall, 0.5–1 mm thick, triquetrous, smooth. Leaves few, shorter than to surpassing culm; blade narrowly linear, 1–19 cm × 1–2 mm, gradually narrowed, long-acuminate, flat; sheath 0.5–4 cm, pale brown to light reddish brown. Involucral bracts 3–5, the lowest   20 cm. Inflorescence capitate or simple, primary branches 0–6, up to 3 cm. Spikes ovoid to subglobose, 0.6–1.5 × 1–1.2 cm; axis up to 0.3 cm, often distinct. Spikelets 3–many, spreading, oblong to oblonglanceolate, 3–10 × 1.5–2.5 mm, flattened; axis ± straight. Glumes ovate to ovate-elliptic, 1–1.8 × 1–1.3 mm, apex rounded-truncate to emarginate, mucronate, sides translucent, pale greenish to brownish, keel acute, 3  -veined, green to reddish brown. Stamens 2; anthers 0.3 mm. Style ca. 0.5 mm; stigmas 2, ca. 0.3 mm. Achenes elliptic to elliptic-lanceolate, 0.5–0.8 × 0.3–0.5 mm, brownish, minutely punctate.

Locality: Aberdeen, Sheung Shui, Tai Mo Shan, Tai Wan (Sai Kung), Po Toi Islands. S. P. Lau 25; J. C. Shaw 640; HK sheet 30229.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Nepal, Myanmar, Vietnam, Malaysia, Indonesia, Philippines.
Ecology: Wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Nov.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Castle Peak, Sai Kung, Pui O
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Pycreus sanguinolentus (Vahl) Nees 紅鱗扁莎
Linnaea 9: 283. 1835; FKH 294. 1912; FRPS 11: 170. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 293. 2000; FYN 15: 649. 2003; FGD 8: 338. 2007; FOC 23: 245. 2010.
Cyperus sanguinolentus Vahl, Enum. Pl. 2: 351. 1805.
Cyperus eragrostis Vahl, Enum. Pl. 2: 322. 1805, non Lam. 1791; FHK 385. 1861.

Annual or short-lived perennial. Culms tufted, 10–60 cm tall, 0.7–2 mm thick, trigonous, smooth, lower part with several nodes. Leaves shorter than culm; blade linear, 4–11 cm × 2–4 mm, acuminate, flattish-plicate; sheath 1–3 cm, pale green to reddish brown. Involucral bracts 3–5, the longest 10–15 cm. Inflorescence ± capitate or simple; primary branches 2–5, 1–4 cm. Spikes ovoid, 0.9–2 × 1–2 cm; axis 1–4 mm. Spikelets 3–17, narrowly ovate or oblong-lanceolate, 7–20 × 2–3.5 mm, axis straight. Glumes ovate or broadly ovate, 2–2.5 × 1.5–2 mm, obtuse, sides membranous, pale brown to reddish or purple brown, keel rather broad, often distinctly furrowed on both sides of keel, 3–5-veined, green. Stamens 3; anthers 0.7 – 1 mm. Style slender; stigmas 2. Achenes broadly obovate, 1–1.3 × 0.8– 1 mm, black, minutely punctate.

Locality: Castle Peak, Sai Kung, Pui O. Y. W. Lam 1624, 2219, 2232.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; C to E Asia, Mediterranean region, Africa and Australia.
Ecology: Paddy fields and grasslands. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Dec.

Remirea maritima Aubl. 海濱莎
Hist. Pl. Guiane 1: 45, pl. 16. 1775; FKH 302. 1912; FRPS 11: 123. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 295. 2000; FGD 8: 344. 2007; FOC 23: 242. 2010.
Miegia maritima (Aubl.) Willd., Sp. Pl. 1(1): 311 – 312. 1797.

Perennial; rhizomes slender, rigid, horizontally long-creeping, branching, internodes 1–10 cm, clothed with brown sheaths and their fibrous remnants. Culms solitary or a few together at nodes of rhizome, 3–15 cm tall, usually with a considerable length of lower part in sand, 1–2 mm thick, triquetrous, smooth. Leaves aggregated on lower part of upper ground portion of culms; blades linear, shorter than or occasionally equalling the culm, 3–8 × 0.4–0.5 cm, acute, leathery, glaucous-green, canaliculate; sheaths 1–1.5 cm, light to reddish brown. Inflorescence terminal, capitate, usually 3–8 congested in a head-like cluster at culm-apex, 1–2 × 1–3 cm. Leafy bracts 3–8, patent or reflexed, equalling or longer than inflorescence, longest one to 8 cm. Spikes ellipsoidal to ovoid, 1–3 × 0.7–1 cm, densely bearing many spikelets, glaucous or yellowish brown. Spikelets ovoid, terete to weakly laterally flattened, 4– 5 × 1–2 mm, acute, bearing 4 glumes, 1-fruited; rachilla jointed above base. Glumes ovate to broadly ovate, lowest 3 empty, fourth bearing a bisexual flower, 3–4.5 × 1.5–1.7 mm, acute to mucronate, margin membranous to chartaceous, 3–5-veined, pale to mid-brown, keel obtuse, brown. Stamens 3; anthers 2 mm long. Achenes oblong, trigonous, ca. 2.5 × 0.7 mm, maturing greyish brown, smooth; style shorter than achene; stigmas 3.

Locality: Hong Kong. HK sheet 8088.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Taiwan; pantropics.
Ecology: Sandy beaches. Flowering & fruiting: Sep.–Dec.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Tam, Aberdeen, Shing Mun, Castle Peak, Yung Shue O, Tung Chung
