PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Rhynchospora brownii Roem. & Schult. 皺果刺子莞
Syst. Veg. 2: 86. 1817; FRPS 11: 111. 1961; Flora Guizhouensis 8: 584. 1988; FYN 15: 617. 2003.
Rhynchospora rugosa (Vahl) Gale subsp. brownii (Roem. & Schultes) T. Koyama in Williams, Pl. Coll. Nepal 118. 1978; FTW ed. 2, 5: 298. 2000; FOC 23: 254. 2010.
Rhynchospora rugosa auct. non (Vahl) Gale: FGD 8: 314. 2007; Check List HK Plants 319. 2002; 112. 2004.

Perennial. Rhizome short. Culms loosely tufted, 30–70 cm tall, 1–1.7 mm thick, trigonous, smooth to scabrid above. Leaves basal and 2–3 cauline; blade narrowly linear, up to 55 cm × 1.5–3 mm, gradually acute, flattish to canaliculate; basal sheath up 8 cm, greyish brown, cauline sheaths up to 5 cm, greenish. Involucral bracts leaf-like, the longest up to 20 cm. Inflorescence narrow, panicle-like, 10–30 cm, with 2–3(–4) distant nodes each subtending 1–3 pedunculate spikelet clusters, the clusters rarely with primary and secondary anthelas. Spikelets 2–40 per cluster, ovate-lanceolate to ovate-elliptic, subterete, 3–4.5 mm. Glumes 5–7, ovate to broadly ovate, 1–3.5 mm long, acute, mucronate, sides thinly papery, dark brown. Perianth segments 6(–7), shorter or slightly longer than achene. Stamens (1–)2–3; anthers linear, 1–1.5 mm. Stigmas 2. Achenes broadly obovate, biconvex, 1.5–1.8 × 1–1.5 mm, maturing light brown, weakly transversely winkled and lineolate with longitudinally oblong epidermal cells; style-base conical, ± as broad as achenes abruptly widening below.

Locality: Tai Tam, Aberdeen, Shing Mun, Castle Peak, Yung Shue O, Tung Chung. Y. W. Lam 2175; S. C. Ng 1359.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Shandong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan, Yunnan, Sichuan; tropical and subtropical regions.
Ecology: Marshes and grasslands. Flowering & fruiting: May–Oct.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Aberdeen, Stanley Rd., Tai Tam Reservoir, Castle Peak, Sai Kung, Yung Shue O, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Rhynchospora chinensis Nees & Meyen 華刺子莞
Nov. Actorum Acad. Caes. Leop.-Carol. Nat. Cur. 19(Suppl. 1): 108. 1843; Linnaea 37: 586. 1873; FRPS 11: 111. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 297. 2000; FOC 23: 254. 2010.
Rhynchospora glauca Vahl var. chinensis (Nees & Meyen) C. B. Clarke, Fl. Brit. India 6: 672. 1893.
Rhychospora glauca auct. non Vahl: FKH 302. 1912.
Rhychospora laxa auct. non R. Br.: FHK 397. 1861.

Perennial; rhizome very short. Culms loosely to densely tufted (30–)50–140 cm tall, 1–3 mm thick, trigonous to triquetrous above, smooth or scabrid above. Leaves basal and 2–4 cauline, blade linear, 10–60 cm × 3–5 mm, long-acuminate, flattish to plicate; basal sheaths yellowish brown to mid-brown, cauline sheaths greenish. Involucral bracts leaf-like, the longest up to 13 cm. Inflorescence narrow, panicle-like, 20–40 cm, with 3–5(–6) nodes each subtending 1–3 pedunculate spikelet clusters. Spikelets up to 15 per cluster, ovate-lanceolate, 6–8 × 1.5–2.5 mm. Glumes 5–8, ovate to ovate-lanceolate, 1–5 cm, acute to mucronate, sides membranous, midbrown to rusty brown. Perianth segments 6, longer than achene. Stamens 2(–3); anthers 2–2.5 mm. Stigmas 2. Achenes broadly obovate, compressed, 1.9–2.5 × 1.5–1.8 mm, slightly shiny, yellowish to mid-brown, weakly transversely winkled and lineolate; style base conical, gradually widening below.

Locality: Aberdeen, Stanley Rd., Tai Tam Reservoir, Castle Peak, Sai Kung, Yung Shue O, Lantau Island. S. C. Ng 1337; HK sheet 13768.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Hainan, Hubei, Zhejiang, Shandong, Anhui, Fujian, Jiangsu, Jiangxi, Taiwan; Korea, Japan, India, Sri Lanka, Myanmar, Vietnam, Indonesia, Madagascar.
Ecology: Wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Oct.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Kau Sai Chau, Sha Lo Tung, Wu Kau Tang
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Rhynchospora corymbosa (L.) Britton 傘房刺子莞
Trans. New York Acad. Sci. 11: 84. 1892; FRPS 11: 110. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 297. 2002; FYN 15: 618. 2003; FGD 8: 314. 2007; FOC 23: 253. 2010.
Scirpus corymbosus L., Cent. Pl. II 7. 1756.
Rhynchospora aurea Vahl, Enum. Pl. 2: 229. 1805; FHK 396. 1861; FKH 302. 1912.

Perennial; rhizome short. Culms 1– few, 80–120(–150) cm tall, 3–10 mm thick, triquetrous, smooth to scabrid above. Leaves basal and 2–3 cauline; blade narrowly linear, 20–70 cm × 0.8–1.6 mm, long-acuminate, flattish, glabrous; basal sheaths up to 20 cm, pale brown, cauline sheaths 5–8 mm, greenish. Involucral bracts leaf-like, the longest 10–30 cm. Inflorescence panicle-like, open, 20–40 cm, comprising 2–5 rather distant partial inflorescence, the terminal one corymb-like, 10–15 × 10–15 cm, simple to compound, with primary anthelas (8–)12– many, up to 12 cm. Spikelets in clusters of 2–10, lanceolate or elliptic, subterete, 6–9 mm. Glumes 5–7, sub-distichous, ovate to oblong-ovate, 2.5–6 mm, acute to mucronulate, sides membranous, reddish brown. Perianth segments in bisexual flower 6, ± equalling achene. Stamens 3; anthers 2–3 mm long. Styles ca. 2 mm, stigma 2 or sometimes undivided, very short. Achenes obdeltoid-obovate, compressed, 2.5–3.5 × 2 mm, apex without short neck, glabrous, dull yellowish brown to mid-brown, finely transversely winkled to rugose, style base elongate-conical, 4–5 mm.

Locality: Kau Sai Chau, Sha Lo Tung, Wu Kau Tang. K. L. Yip 4041; J. C. Shaw & G. Reels 333; Y. W. Lam 1849.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Taiwan; tropical and subtropical regions.
Ecology: Farmlands and river banks. Flowering & fruiting: Mar.–Dec.

Rhynchospora gracillima Thwaites 柔弱刺子莞
Enum. Pl. Zeyl. 435. 1864; FKH 302. 1912; FGD 8: 315. 2007 [“gracilima”]; FOC 23: 255. 2010.

Annual or short-lived perennial; rhizome very short. Culms densely tufted, 20–60 cm tall, 0.2–0.5 mm thick, triquetrous, smooth. Leaves basal; blade setaceous, up to 30 × 0.5–1.3 mm, subacute, canaliculated; sheath 1–4 cm, light green to light brown. Involucral bracts leaf-like, the longest 2–4 cm. Inflorescence 8–20 cm, with 1–3 nodes each with 1 open partial inflorescence; terminal partial inflorescence up to 4 cm, with primary and secondary anthelas; primary anthelas 3–5, up to 4 cm. Spikelets up to 7 per partial inflorescence, solitary, lanceolate, 5–7 × 1.5–2 mm. Glumes 6–7(–8), ovate to broadly ovate, 2–4 cm, subacute to mucronulate, sides membranous, light rusty brown. Perianth segments absent. Stamens 2–3; anthers linear, 1.5–2 mm long. Stigmas 2. Achenes obovoid, compressed, 1.2–1.5 × 1.2–1.5 mm, light grey, undulate-rugose with 6–8 ridges; style base depressed-conical, much wider than long.

Locality: Ho Pui Reservoir. Y. W. Lam 1488; S. C. Ng 2032.
Distribution: Guangdong, Fujian; Sri Lanka, India, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia, tropical Africa, Madagascar, Australia.
Ecology: Wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Mar.–Dec.

Rhynchospora malasica C. B. Clarke 馬來刺子莞（日本刺子莞）
Fl. Brit. India 6: 670. 1893; FTW ed. 2, 5: 298. 2000; FGD 8: 316. 2007; FOC 23: 255. 2010.
Rhynchospora nipponica Makino, Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 18: 145. 1904; FRPS 11: 114. 1961.

Perennial; rhizome long creeping. Sterile shoots elongate to 80 cm, bearing a dense leaf fascicle at distal end. Culms 60 – 100 cm tall, simple, erect, several-nodose, obtusely triquetrous below, regularly triquetrous with acute edges above, surrounded at base with dusky brown sub-aphyllous sheaths, sub-densely leaved on midway portion. Leaves broadly linear, overtopping culm, flattish, 40–60 cm × 5–9 mm, fresh green, gradually tapering above to acute apex, scabrid abaxially and margin; sheath elongate, tightly surrounding culm; ligule short, membranous, rusty brown. Inflorescence 5–20 cm, spicately bearing 2–7 heads, sub-contiguous above, interrupted toward base; bracts not sheathing at base, lower ones with elongate blade 7–20 cm. Inflorescence spicate or racemose, with 2–7 spicate heads; heads sessile, globose, 10–15 mm across, densely many-spiculose, greyish stramineous and tinged with red-brown. Spikelets lanceolateovate to lanceolate, 6–7 mm, weakly laterally compressed, contracted at base, gradually tapering above to acuminate apex, 1-flowered, 1-fruited; glumes 5–6, lower 3–4 ovate, much smaller than lanceolate-ovate upper 2, all 1-veined, acute, membranous, greyish brown. Stamens 3; anthers linear, ca. 2 mm. Stigmas 2, style filiform, 2 mm. Perianth segments 6, filiform, flexuose, smooth, 3.5–4.5 mm. Achenes broadly obovate, 2–2.5 mm, thickly biconvexed with obtuse edges, faintly transversely wrinkled, dark brown; style base narrowly conicalsubulate, 4–4.5 mm, somewhat constricted at base, gradually attenuate from above base to slender style.

Locality: Tai Tam Reservoir. S. T. Chan 590.
Distribution: Guangdong, Taiwan; Japan, Korea, Thailand, Indonesia, Malesia.
Ecology: Marshes and swamps. Flowering & fruiting: May–Oct.

Rhynchospora rubra (Lour.) Makino 刺子莞
Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 17: 180. 1903; FRPS 11: 113. 1961; FGZ 8: 584. 1988; FTW ed. 2, 5: 298. 2002; FYN 15: 619. 2003; FGD 8: 315. 2007; FOC 23: 255. 2010.
Schoenus ruber Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 1: 41. 1790.
Rhychospora wallichiana Kunth, Enum. Pl. 289. 1837; FHK 396. 1861; FKH 302. 1912.

Annual or short-lived perennial; rhizome very short or absent. Culms tufted, 20–70(–100) cm tall, 1–2 mm thick, triquetrous. Leaves basal; blade narrowly linear, shorter than culms, up to 42 cm × 2–4 mm, subacute, flattish to folded or canaliculate; sheath 1–7 cm, yellowish brown. Involucral bracts 4–8, leaf-like, eventually reflexed, the longest up to 8 cm, base dilated, margins ciliate. Inflorescence with one terminal head; head subglobose to globose, 1.0–1.7 cm in diam. Spikelets many, ovate-lanceolate, somewhat flattened, 6–8 × 1.5–2 mm, 2–3-flowered. Glumes 6–8, ovate to lanceolate, up to 6.5 mm, acute, sides thinly papery, pale to mid-brown, lower ones sterile. Stamens (2–)3; anthers linear, ca. 2 mm. Perianth segments 3–6, unequal, up to half the length of achene. Style filiform, stigmas 2 or sometimes undivided. Achenes obovate to broadly obovate, bilaterally compressed, 1.3– 1.8 × 1–1.5 mm, scabrid-hispid along margins, maturing somewhat shiny mid-brown, smooth to indistinctly minutely papillose; style base depressed-conical, ca. 0.5 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 2505; H. C. Tang 2256; Y. W. Lam 713.
Distribution: Areas S of Changjiang; tropical regions of Asia and Australia.
Ecology: Roadsides, grasslands and open areas. Flowering & fruiting: May–Nov.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Wu Kai Sha, Sai Kung, Pui O
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Schoenoplectus juncoides (Roxb.) Palla 螢藺
Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 10: 229. 1889; Flora Guizhouensis 8: 561. 1988; FTW ed. 2, 5: 300. 2000; FYN 15: 577. 2003; FOC 23: 186. 2010.
Scirpus juncoides Roxb., Fl. Ind., ed. 1820, 1: 228. 1820; FHK 395. 1861; FRPS 11: 23. 1961; FHN 4: 277. 1977; FGD 8: 284. 2007; Check List HK Plants 319. 2002; 112. 2004.
Schoenoplectiella juncoides (Roxb.) Lye, Lidia 6(1): 25. 2003.
Scirpus erectus auct. non Poir.: FKH 301. 1912; Check List HK Plants 89. 1993.

Perennial. Rhizome short, roots many, fibrous. Culms tufted, 15–70 cm tall, 1–3 mm thick, subterete or obtusely severalangled, smooth. Leaf sheaths 3–4, lower scale-like, brownish, upper 5–15 cm, obliquely truncate, mucronate. Involucral bracts 1, 1.5–15 cm, abruptly subacute, base dilated, 1-furrowed on ventral side. Inflorescence pseudolateral, capitate, with (1–)2–12 spikelets. Spikelets oblong to ovoid-oblong, 6–18 × 3–6 mm, pale yellowish brown. Glumes ovate to broadly ovate, 3–4 × 1.8–2.7 mm, apex rounded to shallowly emarginate, mucronate, thickly membranous, pale brown, keel green, 1–3-veined. Perianth segments 4–6, ± retrorsely scabrous, of which 4 equalling or slightly longer than achene, remainder ± as long as achenes or less. Stamens 3; anthers oblong, ca. 2 mm. Style ca. 2 mm, stigmas 2, one of them rudimentary. Achenes broadly obovate, unequally biconvex, 1.8–2 × 1.5 mm, shiny dark brown, transversely wrinkled.

Locality: Wu Kai Sha, Sai Kung, Pui O. Y. S. Lau 244; Y. W. Lam 2224; J. C. Shaw 200.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China except Nei Mongol, Xizang and Gansu; Madagascar, tropical and subtropical Asia, Australia, Fiji, Hawaii.
Ecology: Marshes, paddy fields and other wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Nov.

Schoenoplectus lateriflorus (J. F. Gmel.) Lye 側花水蔥
Bot. Not. 124: 290. 1971.
Scirpus lateriflorus J. F. Gmel., Syst. Nat. 1: 127. 1791; FRPS 11: 27. 1961; FGD 8: 282. 2007.
Schoenoplectus supinus (L.) Palla subsp. lateriflorus (J. F. Gmel.) Soják, Cas. Nar. Muz. (Prague) 141: 62. 1972; FTW ed. 2, 5: 303. 2000; FYN 15: 576. 2003; FOC 23: 188. 2010.
Scirpus supinus L. var. lateriflorus (J. F. Gmel.) T. Koyama, J. Fac. Sci. Univ. Tokyo, Sect. 3, Bot. 7(6): 302. 1958; FHN 4: 277. 1977.
Scirpus supinus auct. non L.: FKH 300. 1912.
Isolepis supinus auct. non (L.) R. Br.: FHK 394. 1861.

Annual. Rhizome absent. Culms tufted, 5–30 cm tall, 1–2 mm thick, trigonous, striate. Leaf sheath 5–15 cm, brown, apex obliquely truncate, mucronate, the uppermost sheath sometimes with a compressed-triangular blade to 10 cm. Involucral bracts 1, the lower bract erect, 3–12 cm, ventrally sulcate. Inflorescence pseudolateral, capitate or short, paniculate, simple, branches 4, unequal, with 3–10 spikelets; small secondary inflorescence often present at culm base. Spikelets ovate-lanceolate to oblong, 4–8 × 2–3 mm. Glumes elliptic or elliptic-ovate, boat-shaped, 1.8–2.5 × ca. 2 mm, apex acute, mucronate, green to pale yellowish brown. Perianth segments absent, rarely rudimentary. Stamens 3; anthers oblong, connective pilose. Style slender, ca. 0.5 mm, stigmas 3. Achenes broadly obovoid, trigonous, 1–1.3 mm, black, sides transversely wrinkled.

Locality: Hong Kong. C. Wilford 271; C. Wright 590 (K).
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Jiangsu, Yunnan, Taiwan; Afghanistan, Pakistan, Nepal, India, Sri Lanka, Myanmar, Thailand, Vietnam, Malaysia, Indonesia, Australia, Philippines, Madagascar, Africa.
Ecology: Wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Sep.
Notes: The species was reported as Scirpus supinus L. var. lateriflorus Gmel. previously (Check List HK Plants 320. 2002; 112. 2004).

Schoenoplectus subulatus (Vahl) Lye 鑽苞水蔥
Skr. Utg. Svensk Linné-Sällsk. 124: 290. 1971; FOC 23: 183. 2010.
Scirpus subulatus Vahl, Enum. Pl. 2: 268. 1806; FRPS 11: 17. 1961; FHN 4: 276. 1977.
Schoenoplectus litoralis (Schrad.) Palla subsp. subulatus (Vahl) T. Koyama, Fl. Ceylon 5: 157. 1985.
Scirpus littoralis auct. non Schard.: FGD 8: 282. 2007; Check List HK Plants 320. 2002; 112. 2004.

Perennial. Rhizome short; stolons terminated by a tuber. Culms erect, 60–150 cm tall, 0.5–0.8 mm thick, terete to trigonous below inflorescence, smooth, closed with leafless sheath at base. Leaf sheath cylindrical, 4–20 cm, membranous, septate-nodulose, becoming fibrous with age, apex with a recurved setaceous blade for 5–10 mm. Involucral bracts 1, subcompressed, ± equalling inflorescence, obtuse. Inflorescence paniculate, simple; branches 3–7, unequal, up to 5 cm, scabrous, terminated by 1–3 spikelets. Spikelets oblongovate or elliptic-ovate, 7–15 × 3–4 mm, many-flowered. Glumes oblong-ovate or elliptic, 3.5–4 × 1.8–2 mm, ± obtuse, shortly mucronate, rust brown, the margins tinged red. Perianth segments 3–4, broadly linear to ± spathulate, slightly exceeding achene, fimbriate. Stamens 3; anthers linear, ca. 2 mm. Stigmas 2. Achenes broadly obovate, biconvex, 2 × 1.5–1.7 mm, somewhat shiny, chestnut-brown, very minutely papillose.

Locality: Plover Cove, Mai Po. K. L. Yip 4203; Y. W. Lam 1777; J. C. Shaw 268.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Sichuan, Shanxi, Gansu; India, Sri Lanka, Malesia, Australia, Japan and Micronesia.
Ecology: Wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Oct.
Notes: The species was merged with Scirpus littoralis Schard. or treated as a subspecies of the latter by some authors, but it is easily distinguished from the latter by its terete to trigonous culm and narrower, more laxly fimbriate perianth segments.

Schoenoplectus triangulatus (Roxb.) Soják 水毛花
Čas. Nár. Mus., Odd. Přír. 141(1 – 2): 62. 1972.
Scirpus triangulatus Roxb., Fl. Ind. ed. 1820, 1: 219. 1820; FRPS 11: 21. 1961.
Schoenoplectus mucronatus (L.) Palla subsp. robustus (Miq.) T. Koyama, FTW 5: 214. 1978; FOC 23: 184. 2010.
Scirpus mucronatus auct. non L.: FGD 8: 282. 2007; Check List HK Plants 112. 2004.

Perennial. Rhizomes short. Culms deep green, slightly densely tufted, 45–130 cm tall, 5–11 mm thick, sharply 3-angled with shallowly concave sides, clothed at base with 2–4 leaf sheaths. Leaf sheaths brown, 7–25 cm, membranous to herbaceous, obliquely truncate at orifice. Involucral bract 1, culm-like, upright or obliquely bent, 2–10 cm. Inflorescences a pseudo-lateral hemispherical head, with (3–)5–20 spikelets. Spikelets ovoid, oblong-ovoid, to narrowly ovoid, 10–20 × 4–6 mm, terete, densely many-flowered, apex subacute. Glumes broadly obovate, ovate, broadly ovate, 3.8–5 × 2.5–3 mm, pale green and brownish tinged usually with reddish brown, very concave, papery, margin apically minutely ciliolate, apex with a green 1–3-veined costa excurrent in a mucro. Perianth segments 6, 1.5–2 mm, retrorsely scabrous. Stamens 3; anthers linear, ca. 2.5 mm; connective apex slightly prominent beyond anthers. Style ca. 4 mm; stigmas 3. Achene blackish brown at maturity, obovoid to broadly obovoid, 2–2.5 × 1.5–2 mm, compressed 3-sided, conspicuously or inconspicuously transversely wrinkled, ± shiny, base contracted to cuneate, apex rounded to mucronate.

Locality: San Tin, Kam Tin. Y. W. Lam 1774; HK sheet 40625.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, SE Xizang, Sichuan, Shanxi, Shaanxi, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Shandong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Indonesia, Japan, Korea, Malaysia, Sri Lanka; Africa, Europe, Madagascar.
Ecology: Pond and lake margins, swamps, grasslands in streamsides, paddy fields. Flowering & fruiting: May–Nov.

Schoenus falcatus R. Br. 赤箭莎
Prodr. 232. 1810; FRPS 11: 116. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 308. 2000; FOC 23: 256. 2010.
Schoenus sinensis Hand.-Mazz., Akad. Wiss. Wien, Math.-Naturwiss. Kl., Anz. 62: 150. 1925.

Perennial. Rhizome short, woody. Culms 60–100(–150) cm tall, 2–5 mm thick, obtusely angular, smooth, glabrous. Leaves mostly basal, 3–4-cauline; blade narrowly linear, rigid, 90 cm × 2–7 mm, long-acuminate channeled, glabrous; basal sheath 3–5 cm, dark purplish, cauline sheath 1.5–3 cm. Involucral bract several, lowest bract 3–16 cm. Inflorescence narrow, panicle-like, 20–40 cm, with 4–10 distant nodes each subtending 2–4 partial inflorescence. Spikelets many, shortly pedunculate, oblong-lanceolate, weakly flattened, 7–14 × 2.5 mm, 8–10-glumed, 3–8-flowered. Glumes ovate-lanceolate to oblong-lanceolate, 5–7 × 1 mm, acute, mucronate, sides papery, brown, margins paler, keel acute, yellow green, the lower 2–5 glumes empty, shorter. Perianth segments 1–3, ± equalling achene. Stamens 3; filaments slender; anthers linear, ca. 3 mm. Style 3–4 mm; stigmas 3. Achenes broadly ellipsoidal or obovoid, trigonous, 1–1.3 × 0.8–1 mm, apex pubescent, rust brown, pittedreticulate with large epidermal cells.

Locality: Penny's Bay. S. C. Ng 1719, 1825.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Taiwan; Vietnam, Thailand, Malaysia, New Guinea, Japan, Australia, Pacific islands.
Ecology: Rocks near seashore, thin forests by rivers. Flowering & fruiting: May–Jul.

Scirpus hainanensis S. M. Huang 海南藨草
FHN 4: 538, fig. 1143. 1977; FGD 8: 279. 2007; FOC 23: 174. 2010.

Perennial. Rhizome short or absent. Culms terete, several-noded, glabrous, 60 – 90 cm tall, 3–5 mm thick. Leaves basal or 3–5 cauline, blades linear, flat, shorter than culms, 3–5 mm wide, apex gradually acuminate, margin scaberulous; sheath brown, 1.5–3 cm. Involucral bracts leafy, usually shorter than inflorescence, gradually shorter upward, with sheath. Inflorescence decompound, primary branches 4–6, unequal. Spikelets in finger-like clusters of 3–12, 5–7 × 2–3 mm, 10–15-flowered. Glumes ovate or oblong-ovate, 2–2.5 × ca. 1.5 mm, apex acute or shortly mucronate, membranous, 1-veined, abaxially yellowish-green in the middle, yellowish or brownish laterally, with brown stripes. Perianth segments 6, ca. 1.5 mm, scaberulous above. Stamen 1, anther oblong, less than 1 mm. Style ca. 1.5 mm, slightly inflated at base, stigmas 3. Achenes obovoid or broadly obovoid, trigonous, ca. 1.5 mm, pale brown, smooth.

Locality: Sunset Peak (fide Corlett et al., 2000).
Distribution: Hainan, Fujian, Jiangsu.
Ecology: Forests along streams. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Sep.

Scirpus ternatanus Reinw. ex Miq. 百穗藨草
Fl. Ned. Ind. 3: 307. 1856; FRPS 11: 13. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 309. 2000; FOC 23: 173. 2010.
Scirpus ternatensis C. B. Clarke, J. L. Soc., Bot. 36: 254. 1903; FKH 301. 1912.
Scirpus chinensis Munro, Bot. Voy. Herald 428. 1857, non Osbeck, 1757; FHK 395. 1861.

Perennial. Culms erect, rather stout to stout, 50–200 cm tall, 4–8 mm thick, trigonous to triquetrous above, several-noded. Leaves basal and up to 7 cauline; blades up to 70 × 0.7–2.5 cm, acuminate, flattish; basal sheaths pale to chestnut brown, cauline sheaths greenish brown. Involucral bracts 3 – 5, leafy, up to 50 cm. Inflorescence decompound, 10–25 × 10–25 cm; primary branches up to 8, unequal, up to 10 cm; secondary and tertiary branches up to 5 cm. Spikelets in finger-like to ± globose clusters of 3–10, ovoid to oblong-ovoid, 2.5–6 × 2–3 mm, obtuse, rarely subacute, dark brown. Gulmes ovate to ± orbicular, 1.2–2.5 × 1–1.5 mm, obtuse, ± mucronulate, membranous. Perianth segments 0–3(–6), delicate, sparsely antrorsely scaberulous in the upper half. Stamens 2–3, anthers ablong-linear, 0.7–1 mm. Style glabrous, stigmas 2(–3). Achenes obovate, 0.7–1 × 0.5–0.8 mm, plano-convex or biconvex, strongly dorsiventrally compressed, minutely apiculate, pale brown, smooth.

Locality: Tai Tam Reservior. J. C. Shaw 929; H. G. Ye et al 1162; HK sheet 8104.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Xizang, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Fujian, Jiangsu, Shandong, Taiwan; Malaysia, Indonesia, Philippines, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Vietnam, Thailand, Japan.
Ecology: Wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Aug.
Notes: The type specimen of Scirpus chinensis Munro was collected by Hance from Hong Kong.

Scleria ciliaris Nees 緣毛珍珠茅
Wight, Contr. 117. 1834; FGD 8: 356. 2007; FOC 23: 265. 2010.
Scleria chinensis Kunth, Enum. Pl. 2: 357. 1837, based on S. ciliaris Nees, nom. superfl.; FHK 400. 1861; FKH 303. 1912; FRPS 11: 211. 1961.

Perennial; rhizome woody, covered with purplish scales. Culms tufted, 0.4–1.5 m tall, 2.5–6 mm thick, triquetrous, smooth to scabrid. Leaves cauline; blades linear, 15–50 × 0.7–1.5 cm, apex subobtuse, flattish, glabrous or scabrid; sheaths 4–8 cm, narrowly to broadly winged; contraligule oblong-lanceolate, 1–1.5 cm long. Lowest involucral bract leaf-like, up to 20 cm. Inflorescence paniculate but often appearing spike-like, 7–60 × 3–13 cm; nodes 2–3, close or rarely distant, each subtending a single partial inflorescence; partial inflorescence shortly pedunculate, ovoid-lanceolate, compound, 5–15 cm; bracteoles prominent, stiff. Spikelets unisexual, in clusters of 2–3; female spikelets ovoid, 4–5 mm; male spikelets lanceolate, 3.5–4 mm. Glumes ovate to lanceolate, 3–5 mm, acuminate, sides membranous, pale brown to mid-reddish brown. Stamens 3; anther linear, ca. 2 mm. Achenes ovoid-globose to ± depressed-ovoid, obscurely trigonous, 2–2.3 × 2.3–2.5 mm, rounded, shiny white or slightly purplish grey, reticulate or undulate-rugose, usually glabrous; disk 3-lobed, lobes semicircular, brown, acute, obtuse, reflexed.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. J. C. Shaw 695, H. C. Tang 1257; HK sheet 41683.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong; Myanmar, Thailand, Vietnam, Cambodia, Malaysia, Philippines, Papua New Guinea, tropical Africa, Pacific islands.
Ecology: Forest floors and grasslands.

Scleria corymbosa Roxb. 傘房珍珠茅
Fl. Ind., ed. 1820, 3: 574. 1832; FGD 8: 354. 2007; FOC 23: 263. 2010.
Scleria ridleyi C. B. Clarke, Fl. Brit. India 6: 686. 1894; FHK 400. 1861; FKH 303. 1912.

Perennial; rhizome woody, horizontal. Culms solitary, 60–200 cm tall, 0.5–3 cm thick, triquetrous, glabrous, scabrid along angles. Leaves cauline; blade broadly linear, 30–70 cm × 6–25 mm, abruptly acute to subobtuse, flat; sheath 6 – 15 cm, green to brown; contraligule depressed-deltoid, brown. Involucral bracts leaf-like, the longest up to 47 cm, the lowest one longer than inflorescence, glabrous. Inflorescence paniculate, 35–80 cm; nodes 3–5, each subtending 2 – 3 long-pedunculate, corymbiform partial inflorescence. Spikelets bisexual and male, intermingled, solitary or in groups of 2–5; bisexual spikelets ovoid, 4–5 mm, with a male spikelet in axils of the uppermost glume; male spikelets ovate-lanceolate, 4–4.5 cm long, 7–8-flowered. Glumes broadly ovate to ovate-lanceolate, 3.5–4 mm, acute, mucronate, sides dark chestnut brown, glabrous. Stamens 3, anthers linear, ca. 2 mm. Achenes ovoid, trigonous, 3–3.5 × 2–2.5 mm, apex ± acute, base with 3 shallow depressions, shiny white, smooth, glabrous; disk triangular, adnate to base of achene.

Locality: Sunset Peak. S. C. Ng 1534.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong; Sri Lanka, India, Myanmar, Thailand, Laos, Cambodia, Malaysia, Indonesia, Philippines, Papua New Guinea.
Ecology: Wet and swampy forest floors, less frequently in open wet grassy places. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Dec.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Pok Fu Lam, Shek O, Tai Po Kau
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Scleria harlandii Hance 圓稈珍珠茅（夏蘭珍珠茅）

Ann. Sci. Nat. Bot., sér. 5, 5: 248. 1866; FKH 303. 1912; FRPS 11: 216. 1961; FYN 15: 672. 2003; FGD 8: 357. 2007; FOC 23: 268. 2010.
Scleria purpurascens auct. non Steud.: FHK 400. 1861.

Perennial; rhizome woody, covered with reddish brown scales. Culms to more than 1 m tall, ca. 6 mm thick, terete to sometimes slightly triquetrous, shiny, glabrous. Leaf sheath 4–6 cm, yellow with purple lines, tightly embracing culm, thinly leathery, wingless, sometimes pilose, apical ones often overlapped; contraligule semicircular or subtriangular, 2–3 mm, purple, margin ciliate, cilia ca. 1 mm; leaf blade linear, ca. 30 × 0.6–0.8 cm, thinly leathery, slightly scabrous, glabrous, apex attenuate. Involucral bracts leaf-like, basalmost to 35 cm, sheathing; bractlets setaceous, nearly equalling spikelets, hairy, base auricled. Inflorescences compound paniculate, to 40 cm, with 8–9 branches; branches ca. 5 cm, triangular, axes often pubescent. Spikelets 1–2, light rust-coloured to purple, 3–4 mm, mostly unisexual. Male spikelets oblong-ovoid to narrowly ovoid, apex truncate to acute; glumes 1.4–3 mm, membranous, with rusty lines. Female spikelets usually at base of branch, narrowly ovoid, apex acuminate; glumes broadly ovate to ovate-lanceolate, ± keeled, margin apically ciliate, apex cuspidate. Male flowers: stamens 3; anthers linear, ca. 1 mm; connective apex ca. 0.3 mm. Female flowers: stigmas 3. Achene white, subspherical or ovoid, ca. 2.5 mm in diam., bluntly 3-sided, smooth, shiny, only apical part sparsely hairy, apex tipped; disk yellow with light rust-coloured lines, ca. 2 mm in diam., 3-lobed; lobes triangular, margins reflexed, apex acute to acuminate or 2–3-lobed.

Locality: Pok Fu Lam, Shek O, Tai Po Kau. J. C. Shaw 478; L. T. Lo 164; H. C. Tang 1942.
Distribution: Fujian, Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; Vietnam, Cambodia.
Ecology: Forest. Flowering & fruiting: Mar.–Sep.
Notes: The type specimens were collected by C. Harland and J. Lamont from Hong Kong Island in 1850s.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Shek O, Kwun Tong, Tung Chung
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Scleria laxa R. Br. 疏鬆珍珠茅
Prodr. Fl. Nov. Holland. 240. 1810; FGD 8: 360. 2007; FOC 23: 264. 2010.

Annual; rhizome absent. Stem very slender, smooth, 1–2-noded below the inflorescence, 20–45 cm tall, 1–1.5 mm thick. Leaves narrowly linear, 5–15 cm × 1–3 mm, apex rather abruptly narrowed to the ± obtuse tip, glabrous, smooth or scabrid on the margins and the main veins near the apex, 3–5-veined; sheaths narrow, wingless, upper ones glabrous, lower ones often leafless, pubescent, purplish; contraligule short, broadly rounded, ciliate. Inflorescence occupying by far the greater part of the stem, narrow, very loose, consisting of about 3 very remote fascicles of partial panicles, the terminal panicle not larger than the lateral ones, 1–2 cm; peduncles 3–4 together at the nodes, exserted from the sheaths, ± noding, filiform, slightly incrassate at the apex, 2–4 cm; primary bracts erect, as long as or overtopping the inflorescence. Spikelets unisexual; male spikelets about as long as their peduncles, linear-lanceolate, 1.5–2.5 mm; stamen 1; anther oblong-linear, 0.7–1 mm; female spikelets 3.5–4 mm, without a trace of a male part; glumes ovate, acute or mucronate. Cupula very small, 0.7 mm wide, hardly lobed. Achenes globose, ca. 1.7 mm across, deeply longitudinally ribbed, with 3 of the ribs more prominent, ± trabeculate between the ribs, slightly tuberculate at the top, umbonulate, glabrous, shining, white, the ribs not all reaching the base of the achene, but leaving a smooth triangular area above each disk-lobe; disk small, shortly 3-lobed; lobes obtuse, semi-orbicular.

Locality: Shek O, Kwun Tong, Tung Chung. Y. W. Lam 1258; HK sheet 13874, 39380.
Distribution: Guangdong, Hainan, Fujian; Philippines, Queensland, New Guinea.
Ecology: Grasslands of hillslopes. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.

Scleria levis Retz. 毛果珍珠茅
Obs. 4: 13. 1786; FHK 400. 1861; FTW ed. 2, 5: 311. 2002; FYN 15: 673. 2003; FGD 8: 358. 2007; FOC 23: 266. 2010.
Scleria hebecarpa Nees in Wight, Contrib. Bot. Ind. 117. 1834; FKH 303. 1912; FRPS 11: 213. 1961.
Scleria pubescens Steud., Syn. Cyp. 168. 1855; FHK 400. 1861.
Scleria hebecarpa Nees var. pubescens (Steud.) C. B. Clarke, Fl. Brit. India 6: 689. 1894; FRPS 11: 214. 1961.

Perennial; rhizome woody, creeping, covered with brown scales. Culms 30–90 cm tall, 1–3 mm thick, triquetrous, glabrous to puberulent. Leaves cauline; blade linear, 18–35 cm × 2–8(–12) mm, glabrous, scabrid on the margin and along the midvein abaxially, gradually narrowed towards apex, flat; sheath 5–8 cm, winged, green to reddish or purplish brown; contraligule shallowly rounded, pubescent. Lowest involucral bracts leaf-like, up to 13 cm, upper bracts and bracteoles prominent, setaceous. Inflorescence paniculate, open to compact, sometimes appearing head-like, 5–13 × 1.5–2.5 cm; nodes 3–4, each subtending a single partial inflorescence; partial inflorescence sessile or shortly pedunculate, ovate-lanceolate, 2–8 cm. Spikelets female and male in groups of 2–4; female spikelets sessile, obovoid, 4–6 mm; male spikelets pedunculate, oblong-lanceolate, 3–4 mm. Glumes ovate, 2–4 mm, acuminate, sides membranous, mid-brown to chestnut brown. Stamens 3; anther linear, ca. 3 mm. Achenes globose, ± terete, 1.7–2.5 × 1.7–2.5 mm, rounded, white, smoothish, pubescent to glabrous; disk 3-lobed, the lobes lanceolate-triangular, acute, minutely toothed at apex.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. W. Lam 753; Y. S. Lau 2544, 3138.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; widely distributed from India to Myanmar, Vietnam, Japan, throughout Malesia to Queensland and New Caledonia.
Ecology: Grasslands, floors of open forests, margins of rice fields. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Oct.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Aberdeen, To Tei Wan, Middle Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Scleria lithosperma (L.) Sw. 石果珍珠茅
Prodr. 18. 1788; FHK 399. 1861; FKH 303. 1912; FRPS 11: 206. 1961; FTW ed. 2, 5: 312. 2000; FGD 8: 354. 2007; FOC 23: 263. 2010.
Scirpus lithosperma L., Sp. Pl. 51. 1753.

Perennial; rhizomatous woody. Culms loosely tufted, base bulbous, 40–80 cm tall, 1–2 mm thick, triquetrous, glabrous. Leaves cauline; blade narrowly linear, 8–40 cm × 1.5–4 mm, gradually narrowed, subobtuse; sheath 6–9 cm, reddish brown, puberulent; contraligule depressed-rounded or depressed-deltoid, ciliate. Lowest involucral bracts leaf-like, up to 10 cm. Inflorescence paniculate, with 3–4 nodes each subtending a single, open, pedunculate narrow partial inflorescence, sometimes the whole inflorescence becoming ± spike-like; peduncles filiform. Spikelets bisexual, 1–3, ovate-turbinate, 3–5 mm long. Glumes ovate, 3–4 mm long, acuminate or acute, mucronate, sides membranous, glabrous, rusty brown, stamens 1(–2). Achenes obovoid-ellipsoidal, trigonous, 2–2.8 × 1.7–2 mm, apex rounded, base cuneate with 3 depressions, shiny white, smooth; disk small, annular.

Locality: Aberdeen, To Tei Wan, Middle Island. Y. W. Lam 1514; J. C. Shaw 559; HK sheet 8209.
Distribution: Guangdong, Hainan, Taiwan, Yunnan; tropics.
Ecology: Semi-dry open grassy places, floors and margins of forests, particularly near the coast. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Oct.

Scleria parvula Steud. 小型珍珠茅
Syn. Pl. Glumac. 2: 174. 1855; FYN 15: 670. 2003; FGD 8: 360. 2007; FOC 23: 264. 2010.
Scleria biflora auct. non Roxb.: FKH 303. 1912; FRPS 11: 208. 1961; Check List HK Plants 103. 1993.
Scleria tessellata auct. non Willd.: FHK 399. 1861.

Annual; rhizome absent. Culms tufted, (10–)30–90 cm tall, 1–3 mm thick, triquetrous, scabrid on angles. Leaves cauline; blade linear, 20–35 cm × 2–6 mm, acute, flattish, glabrous, scabrid on upper margin; sheath 3–10 cm, narrowly winged or wingless, greenish to reddish purple, pubescent along the wing; contraligule rounded-truncate, margin ciliate. Lowest involucral bracts leaf-like, up to 20 cm. Inflorescence paniculate, 10–20 cm; nodes 2–4, distant, each subtending 1–3 partial inflorescence; partial inflorescence sessile to long-pedunculate, ± simple, narrowly elliptic, 1–4 cm, bracteoles rather prominent. Spikelets unisexual; female spikelets somewhat turbinate, 4–5 mm; male spikelets lanceolate, 4–5 mm, peduncle 1–3 mm. Glumes ovate, 3.5 mm long, acute, mucronate, sides membranous, pale brown to reddish brown, keel green. Stamens 3; anther linear, 1–1.5 mm. Achenes globose to ± ellipsoidal, 2–2.3 × 1.7–2 mm, shiny white, cancellate with regular, longitudinally oblong lacunae, glabrous to ± rufous pubescent; disk deeply 3-lobed, lobes ovate to elliptic-ovate, without deep pit at sinus between lobes.

Locality: Quarry Bay. Y. S. Lau 2546.
Distribution: Guangdong, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Jiangsu, Shandong, Zhejiang, Guizhou, Sichuan, Yunnan, Xizang; Sri Lanka, India, Nepal, Thailand, Vietnam, Laos, Cambodia, Japan, Korea, Malaysia, Philippines, New Guinea, tropical Africa.
Ecology: Wet, open grasslands, swamps and occasionally floors of open forests. Flowering & fruiting: Oct.

Scleria rugosa R. Br. 皺果珍珠茅
Prodr. Fl. Nov. Holland. 240. 1810; FTW ed. 2, 5: 312. 2000; FYN 15: 669. 2003; FGD 8: 360. 2007; FOC 23: 263. 2010.
Scleria onoei Franch. & Savat., Enum. Pl. Jap. 2: 122, 549. 1879; FRPS 11: 209. 1961.

Annual; rhizome absent. Culms densely tufted, 10–35 cm tall, 0.7–1.5 mm thick, triquetrous, pubescent. Leaves cauline; blade narrowly linear, 5–15 cm × 2–4 mm, ± obtuse, folded, pubescent; sheath 1.5–3.5 cm long, narrowly winged or wingless, pale to midbrown; contraligule rounded-deltoid to suborbicular, ciliate. Lowest involucral bracts leaf-like, up to 14 cm. Inflorescence paniculate, 9–20 cm; nodes 2–3, distant, each subtending 1(–2) partial inflorescence; partial inflorescence sessile to shortly pedunculate, simple, 1–2 cm, with few spikelets. Spikelets unisexual, solitary or in pairs; female spikelets broadly obovate, 3–4 mm; male spikelets shortly pedunculate, lanceolate, 2–2.5 mm. Glumes ovate, 2.5–4 mm long, acute, sides membranous, pale green sometimes tingled with reddish brown, keel green. Stamens 1. Achenes globose or broadly obovoid-globose, terete, 1.2–1.8 × 1.2–1.8 mm, white, usually smooth or transversely wrinkled above, rarely trabeculate, glabrous; disk shallowly 3-lobed, lobes suborbicular, densely glandular.

Locality: Fung Mun Au. HK sheet 34219.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Jiangsu, Hainan, Taiwan, Yunnan; India, Sri Lanka, Vietnam, Laos, Thailand, Cambodia, Japan, Malaysia, Micronesia, Australia and New Caledonia.
Ecology: Open, wet grasslands and rice fields. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Sep.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Mount Kellet, Sha Lo Tung, Tai Mo Shan, Bride's Pool
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Scleria terrestris (L.) Fassett 高稈珍珠茅
Rhodora 26: 159. 1924; FTW ed. 2, 5: 313 2000; FYN 15: 676. 2003; FGD 8: 358. 2007; FOC 23: 265. 2010.
Zizania terrestris L., Sp. Pl. 2: 991. 1753.
Scleria elata Thw., Enum. Pl. Zeyl. 353. 1864; FKH 303. 1912; FRPS 11: 211. 1961.
Scleria radula Hance, Ann. Sci. Nat. Bot., sér. 4, 18: 232. 1862; FKH 303. 1912; FRPS 11: 206. 1961.
Scleria vestita Boeck., Linnaea 38: 482. 1875. nom. illeg. (type same as Scleria radula Hance.)
Scleria laevis Retz. var. scaberrima Benth., FHK 400. 1861.

Perennial; rhizome woody, covered with purple scales. Culms sometimes climbing, (0.6–)1–4 m tall, 3–6 mm thick, triquetrous, scabird, Leaves cauline; often closely spaced; blade linear, 15–40(–60) cm × (5–)7–20 mm, glabrous or scabrid, apex long caudate, flattish; sheath 6–15 cm, triquetrous, winged or not, reddish or purplish brown; contraligule crescent-shaped or depressed rounded, 2–4 mm, ciliate or glabrescent. Lowest involucral bracts leaf-like, up to 40 cm. Inflorescence paniculate, 25–50 × 5–10 cm; nodes 2–4, rather distant, each subtending a single partial inflorescence; partial inflorescence long-pedunculate, ovate-pyramidal to broadly ovoid, compound, 4–14 cm; bracteoles indistinct. Spikelets solitary or in groups of 2–3; female spikelets sessile, broadly ovoid, 3.7–5 mm; male spikelets lanceolate or oblong-lanceolate, 3–4 mm. Glumes broadly ovate, 3.5–4 mm, abruptly acute. Achene 2.5–3 × 2.5–2.8 mm, spherical, shiny white to dark purplish, smooth or indistinctly scrobiculate, puberulent to glabrous; disk shallowly 3-lobed, lobes broadly triangular, obtuse to rounded or ± emarginate.

Locality: Mount Kellet, Sha Lo Tung, Tai Mo Shan, Bride's Pool. J. C. Shaw 624; Y. S. Lau 1942; K. L. Yip 4087.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Chongqing, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan, Zhejiang, Jiangsu; India, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Myanmar, Laos, Cambodia, Vietnam, Japan, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia, Australia.
Ecology: Floors of forests, thickets and wet grasslands.
Notes: The type specimens of Scleria radula (Hance 1157) and Scleria laevis var. scaberrima (Harland s.n.) were collected from Hong Kong Island in 1850s.

Acroceras tonkinense (Balansa) C. E. Hubbard ex Bor 山雞穀草
Indian Forest Rec., Bot. 1(3): 78. 1938; FHN 4: 414. 1977; FOC 22: 515. 2006; FGD 9: 412. 2009.
Panicum tonkinense Balansa, J. Bot. (Morot) 4: 140. 1890.
Neohusnotia tonkinensis (Balansa) A. Camus, Bull. Mus. Natl. Hist. Nat. 26(7): 664. 1921; FRPS 10(1): 236. 1990.

Perennial. Culms 65(–100) cm tall, nodes densely pubescent with soft white hairs. Leaf sheaths glabrous or with tubercle-based hairs, one margin tuberculate-ciliate; leaf blades lanceolate, 10–20 × 1–3 cm, glabrous or abaxial surface pilose, margins thickened, pectinate-ciliate at base, scabrous, midvein prominent abaxially, apex narrowly acuminate; ligule ca. 1 mm, obtuse. Panicle open, 15–25 × 5–10 cm, axis and branches stiff, scabrous; racemes ascending, with secondary branching; spikelets widely spaced, paired or single in upper part. Spikelets 5–5.5 mm; lower glume broadly elliptic, 3/4 spikelet length, 5-veined; upper glume and lower lemma as long as spikelet, 5-veined, apex slightly thickened; lower palea hyaline, narrow; upper lemma smooth, shining, slightly shorter than spikelet, apex thickened and protruding.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. S. Y. Hu 9931.
Distribution: Hainan, Yunnan; India, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, Thailand, Vietnam.
Ecology: Margins of forests under shade. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.
Notes: This species is more robust in habit than Acroceras munroanum (鳳頭黍), with larger leaves and harshly scabrous leaf margins and inflorescence. The species was reported as Acroceras munroanum (Balansa) Henrard previously (Check List HK Plants 321. 2002; 113. 2004).

Alloteropsis cimicina (L.) Stapf 臭蟲草
Fl. Trop. Afr. 9: 487. 1919; FHN 4: 430. 1977; FRPS 10(1): 303, pl. 93: 7–11. 1990; FOC 22: 519. 2006; FGD 9: 432. 2009.
Milium cimicinum L., Mant. Pl. 184. 1771.
Axonopus cimicinus (L.) P. Beauv., Ess. Agrostogr. 12, 154. 1812; FKH 313. 1912.

Annual herb. Culms tufted, ascending, up to 60 cm tall. Leaf sheaths tuberculate-hispid; leaf blades linear-lanceolate, cordate, 3–10 × 1–2 cm, glabrous, abaxial surface pectinate-setose along margins and veins, adaxial surface glabrous; ligule ca. 1 mm, ciliate. Inflorescence digitate; racemes 4–6, 10–15 cm, narrowly ascending, rachis glabrous, bare of spikelets in the lower part, spikelets paired or solitary. Lower glume ovate-lanceolate, ca. 2 mm, 3-veined, acuminate; upper glume as long as spikelet, papery, margins stiff ciliate, apex acute; lower lemma similar to upper glume but thicker and glabrous, palea small, stamens 3; upper lemma ovate-elliptic, tuberculate, awn 2–3 mm; upper palea papillose with swollen lacrimiform hairs.

Locality: Kowloon. HK sheet 38086.
Distribution: Hainan; Indian Subcontinent, Indochina, Malay Peninsula, Pacific islands, Cambodia, New Guinea, Australia, Africa.
Ecology: Weedy places, thin forests. Flowering: Sep.

Alloteropsis semialata (R. Br.) Hitchc. 毛穎草
Contr. U. S. Natl. Herb. 12: 210. 1909; FHN 4: 429. 1977; FRPS 10(1): 301, pl. 93: 1–4. 1990; FFJ 6: 227, fig. 193. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 454, pl. 188. 2000; FOC 22: 519. 2006; FGD 9: 432, fig. 223. 2009.
Panicum semialatum R. Br., Prodr. 192. 1810.
Axonopus semialatus (R. Br.) Hook. f., Fl. of Brit. Ind. 7(21): 64. 1897[1896]; FKH 313. 1912.

Perennial herb with a short rhizome. Culms erect, tufted, 30–70 cm, ± pubescent below inflorescence and bearded at nodes. Leaf sheaths persistent, densely and conspicuously silky hairy, upper glabrous or margins and mouth pilose; leaf blades linear, flat or convolute, stiff, 10–50 × 0.1–1 cm, abaxial surface glabrous, tuberculate-pilose, adaxial surface sparsely to densely hairy; ligule membranous, ca. 1 mm. Inflorescence digitate; racemes 2–4, 3–13 cm, rachis slender, triangled, pilose. Spikelets lanceolate, 5–6 mm, usually paired on one side; lower glume ovate, ca. 1/2 length of spikelet, 3-veined, mucronate or awn-tipped; upper glume as long as spikelet, 5-veined, margins ciliate, occasionally winged, awntipped; lower lemma as long as upper glume, awnless, often sparsely ciliate along margins, embraced a short hyaline, clefted, small palea; upper lemma ovate-lanceolate, ca. 4 mm, smooth, with a rigid 2–3 mm awn-point. Anthers orange, ca. 3 mm; style exserted apically.

Locality: Aberdeen, Kadoorie Farm, Tuen Mun. S. C. Ng 2169; HK sheet 8231, 32244.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan, Fujian, Taiwan; Indian Subcontinent, Indochina, Malay Peninsula, Indonesia, Pacific islands, Africa.
Ecology: Hillslopes. Flowering & fruiting: Feb. – Aug.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Sha Tin, Sheung Shui, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Alopecurus aequalis Sobol. 看麥娘
Fl. Petrop. 16. 1799; FKH 325. 1912; FRPS 9(3): 264, pl. 64: 8 – 9. 1987; FFJ 6: 113, fig. 85. 1995; FOC 22: 366. 2006; FGD 9: 396, fig. 203. 2009.
Alopecurus amurensis Kom., Izv. Imp. Bot. Sada Petra Velikago 16: 151. 1961.
Alopecurus aequalis Sobol. var. amurensis (Kom.) Ohwi, Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 55: 360. 1941; FTW ed. 2, 5: 343. 2000.

Annual or short-lived perennial herb, 10–45 cm tall. Culms loosely tufted, ascending from geniculate base. Leaf blades soft, 2–10 cm × 2–6 mm, abaxial surface smooth, glabrous, adaxial surface closely ribbed, scaberulous; ligule 2–5 mm, obtuse; leaf sheaths smooth, slightly inflated. Panicle narrowly cylindrical, 2–7 × 3–6 mm, pale grey-green. Spikelets elliptic or oblong, 1.5–3 mm; glumes membranous, smooth, keels ciliate-hispid, lateral veins hispid on lower part, margins connate at base, ± parallel at the tips, apices obtuse; lemma equalling or slightly longer than glumes, margins connate below middle, awned from lower 1/4–1/3, apex obtuse; awn included within spikelet or exserted up to 1.2 mm, straight. Anthers orange, 0.5–0.8 mm.

Locality: Sha Tin, Sheung Shui, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 836, 1539; S. P. Lau 106.
Distribution: Spread over most provinces of China; widely distributed in Europe, temperate Asia and N America.
Ecology: Banks of ditches, rice fields, farmlands. Flowering & fruiting: Mar.–May.

Alopecurus japonicus Steud. 日本看麥娘
Syn. Pl. Glumac. 1: 149. 1854; FKH 325. 1912; FRPS 9(3): 262, pl. 64: 6–7. 1987; FFJ 6: 114. 1995; FOC 22: 366. 2006; FGD 9: 396. 2009.

Annual herb, 25–50 cm tall. Culms tufted, erect or geniculate at base, often forming large clump. Leaf blades soft, glaucous, 3–12 × 0.3–0.7 cm, abaxial surface smooth, adaxial surface scaberulous; ligule 2–5 mm. Panicle cylindrical, 3–10 cm, yellowgreen; leaf sheaths lax, smooth, glabrous, upper sheaths inflated. Spikelets ovate-oblong, 4.8–7 mm; glumes herbaceous, smooth, keels wingless, stiffly ciliate, lateral veins pubescent near base or glabrous, margins connate only at extreme base, apices subacute; lemma slightly longer than glumes, herbaceous, margins connate in lower 2/5, awned from near base, apex subacute; awn exserted 5 – 8 mm from spikelet, weakly geniculate, column not twisted. Anthers white, ca. 1 mm.

Locality: Ma On Shan. HK sheet 30736.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hubei, Henan, Shaanxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian; Japan, Korea.
Ecology: Banks of rice fields and other wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Feb.–May.

Andropogon chinensis (Nees) Merr. 華鬚芒草
Philipp. J. Sci. 12: 101. 1917; FHN 4: 478, fig. 1264. 1977; FFJ 6: 274, fig. 248. 1995; FRPS 10(2): 185, pl. 45: 1–15. 1997; FOC 22: 623. 2006; FGD 9: 497, fig. 263. 2009.
Homoeatherum chinense Nees, Nat. Syst. Bot., 448. 1836.

Perennial herb. Culms erect, tufted, 40–100 cm tall, glabrous. Leaf sheaths glabrous or pilose; leaf blades linear, flat or involute when dry, 8–25 × 0.2–0.3 cm; ligule 1–2.5 mm, membranous, obtuse. Racemes paired, 1.5–3(–5) cm, exserted from spatheole; spatheoles boat-shaped or linear; peduncle puberulous; rachis internodes subequal to pedicels, cuneate, the lower with 1–3 mm hairs, tips cupular, obliquely toothed. Sessile spikelet linear, ca. 5 mm, callus acute and pungent; lower glume deeply concave between dorsal keels, glabrous, shortly awned, mucronate or 2-toothed; upper glume boat-shaped, 2-lobed, with an awn from the sinus; awn 6–10 mm; lower lemma linear-oblong, hyaline membranous; upper lemma 2-lobed, an awn from the sinus; awn 2–3 cm; palea 1/2 length of lower glume, margins ciliate; lodicules 2; stamens 3; style free, glumose. Pedicellate spikelet oblong-lanceolate, ca. 4 mm, 2-awned; awn of lower glume 4–10 mm, awn of upper glume much shorter.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Castle Peak. S. C. Ng 1521.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan; India, Myanmar, Thailand, Indochina, Africa, SW Asia (Yemen).
Ecology: Open grassy fields, hillslopes. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Dec.

Apluda mutica L. 水蔗草
Sp. Pl. 1: 82. 1753; FHK 422. 1861; FKH 325. 1912; FHN 4: 462, fig. 1249. 1977; FFJ 6: 254, fig. 223. 1995; FRPS 10(2): 167, pl. 39: 1 – 10. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 5: 522, pl. 220. 2000; FOC 22: 614. 2006; FGD 9: 478, fig. 250. 2009.

Perennial herb. Culms erect or ascending from decumbent base, up to 3 m tall. Leaf sheaths ciliate or not; leaf blades linear-lanceolate, 10–35× 0.3–2 cm, base petiolate, apex acuminate; ligule membranous, 1–2 mm. Spathate panicle up to 50 cm, branches very slender with spaced spathes subtending small clusters of spatheoles. Sessile spikelet 4–6 mm, bisexual; lower glume long ovate, rounded, margins slightly inrolled, obtuse; upper glume boat-shaped, 5–7-veined; lower lemma subequal to lower glume; upper lemma boatshaped, deeply 2-lobed with 4–12 mm awn, or entire to emarginate and awnless. Pedicellate spikelet reduced to lemma; normal pedicellate spikelet 2-floret, lower glume long ovate, papery to thin-leathery, apex acute or slightly 2-toothed, upper glume as long as or slightly shorter than lower glume; lower floret staminate; upper floret staminate or seldom bisexual and fertile.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1029, 1044; HK sheet 35847.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; SW Asia, Indian Subcontinent, Indochina, Malesia, Pacific islands, Australia (Queensland), Indian Ocean islands (Mascarenes), Madagascar.
Ecology: Margins of forests and thickets, sometimes forming large colonies. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Dec.

Apocopis intermedius (A. Camus) Chai-Anan 異穗楔穎草
Thai Forest Bull. Bot. 6: 46. 1972; FOC 22: 599. 2006; FGD 9: 472. 2009.
Lophopogon intermedium A. Camus, Bull. Mus. Natl. Hist. Nat. 25: 285. 1919.
Apocopis heterogamus Keng & S. L. Chen, FRPS 10(2): 112, pl. 26: 1–3. 1997; FYN 9: 644. 2003.
Apocopis wrightii Munro var. macranthus S. L. Chen, FRPS 10(2): 112. 1997; Check List HK Plants 322. 2002; 113. 2004.

Perennial herb. Culms erect, ca. 40–60 cm tall. Leaf sheaths glabrous to hirsute; leaf blades linear-lanceolate, 6–15 × 0.3–0.5 cm, tuberculate-pilose when young, or sometimes densely hispid; ligule ca. 1.5 mm. Racemes 2, 2–4 cm, lowermost spikelets barren, awnless; rachis internodes 2.5–3 mm, loosely ciliate with yellowish brown soft hairs. Sessile spikelet 6–9 mm; callus hairs yellowish brown; lower glume oblong, firmly herbaceous, glabrous or hispid, greenish yellow with a scarious brown or red band across apex, veins green, straight, connected there by transverse veinlets, terminating below apex, truncate or ciliate; upper glume oblong, as long as lower glume or slightly longer, submembranous, dark red on the upper, emarginate and short ciliate, 3-veined; lower lemma oblong-lanceolate, as long as lower glume or slightly shorter, hyaline membranous, apex ciliate; upper floret staminate or barren, lemma linear-lanceolate, apex entire or 2-toothed, awned or awnless; awn geniculate, 2–3 cm. Pedicellate spikelet developed, ca. 5 mm, awned.

Locality: Sai Wan, Tai Mo Shan. H. C. Tang 2000; HK sheet 15247.
Distribution: Guangdong, S Yunnan, Zhejiang; Thailand, N Vietnam.
Ecology: Open grassy fields. Flowering & fruiting: Autumn.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Mo Shan, High Island, Wang Shan Keuk
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Apocopis wrightii Munro 瑞氏楔穎草
Proc. Amer. Acad. Arts. 4: 363. 1860; FHK 421. 1861; FKH 320. 1912; FRPS 10(2): 111. 1997; FOC 22: 599. 2006; FGD 9: 471. 2009.

Perennial herb. Culms tufted, 30–60 cm tall, branching above base, 6–7-noded. Leaf sheaths glabrous or pilose; leaf blades linear, 8–12 × 0.2–0.6 cm, tuberculate-pilose, rarely glabrous, apex acuminate; ligule ca. 1 mm. Racemes 2–5 cm, lowermost spikelets barren, awnless; rachis internodes 1.5–2 mm, yellowish brown ciliate; pedicel yellowish brown bearded. Sessile spikelet 3.5–6 mm; callus yellowish brown bearded; lower glume obovate-oblong, firmly herbaceous, glabrous or thinly hispid, greenish yellow with a scarious red-brown band across apex, veins green, straight, terminating below apex, connected there by transverse veinlets, apex truncate, ciliate; lower florets exserted from the apex, lemma oblong-lanceolate; upper floret bisexual, lemma apex 2-denticulate or subentire, awned; awn geniculate, 2–3 cm. Pedicellate spikelet absent or rudimentary.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, High Island, Wang Shan Keuk. S. Y. Hu 7769, 8501, 10881 (CUHK).
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian; Thailand.
Ecology: Open grassy hillsides. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Oct.

Aristida chinensis Munro 華三芒草
Proc. Amer. Acad. Arts. 4: 363. 1860; FHK 427. 1861; FKH 325. 1912; FHN 4: 371, fig. 1182. 1977; FRPS 10(1): 115. 1990; FTW ed. 2, 5: 366. 2000; FOC 22: 454. 2006; FGD 9: 343, fig. 163. 2009.
Aristida formosana Honda, Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 41: 379. 1927.

Perennial herb, 30–60 cm tall. Culms densely tufted, erect, glabrous, unbranched. Leaf blades involute, filiform, curling when dry, 10–20 cm × 1–1.5 mm, abaxial surface smooth, adaxial surface pubescent; ligule a fringe of hairs, ca. 0.2–0.5 mm. Panicle ovate in outline, open, loose, 1/3 to 1/2 length of plant; branches 3–15 cm, divaricate, solitary or in small widely spaced groups along central axis, bearded in axils, strongly scabrid, lower part naked. Spikelets ca. 8 mm, 1-flowered, grey-green to purple; glumes linear-lanceolate, subleathery, 1–3-veined, acuminate-mucronate, unequal, lower one 8–14 mm, scabrid on vein, the upper one shorter and smooth; callus ca. 0.5 mm; lemma 5–8 mm, terete, smooth, margin slightly inrolled; awn branches arising directly from lemma apex, central branch 1–1.5 cm, laterals slightly shorter or subequal to central branch; palea minute, linear-lanceolate, papery, 2–keeled, ca. 1.5 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. P. P. H. But 157; HK sheet 8619, 30744.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam, Cambodia, Thailand, Indonesia, Philippines.
Ecology: Grassy hillslopes. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Dec.

Aristida cumingiana Trin. & Rupr. 黃草毛（黃毛草）
Sp. Gram. Stipac. 141. 1842; FKH 325. 1912; FRPS 10(1): 119, pl. 37: 1–2. 1990; FOC 22: 453. 2006; FGD 9: 343. 2009.

Annual herb, 6–20 cm tall. Culms slender, erect from geniculate base, branched. Leaf blades linear, involute, 2.5–10 cm, abaxial surface glabrous, adaxial surface hairy; ligule ca. 0.2 mm, inconspicuous. Panicle oblong to ovate in outline, loose, open, 5–10 cm; branches slender, ascending, in pairs or 3 together along main axis; pedicel long. Spikelets 3–3.5 mm, green or purple; glumes unequal, 1-veined, scabrid on vein, apex acuminate-mucronate, lower glume lanceolate, 2–2.5 mm, upper glume narrowly lanceolate-oblong, 2.8–3.5 mm; callus small, broadly obtuse; lemma 1.7–2 mm, upper part scabrid; awn arising directly from lemma apex, stiffly spreading, central branch 5–8 mm, laterals about half as long.

Locality: Aberdeen (fide FKH 325. 1912).
Distribution: Guangdong, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian; Vietnam, Laos, Myanmar, Thailand, India, Nepal, Indonesia, Philippines, New Guinea, N Australia, Africa.
Ecology: Hillslopes, dry grasslands. Flowering & fruiting: Summer to autumn.

Arthraxon hispidus (Thunb.) Makino 藎草
Bot. Mag. (Tokyo). 26: 214. 1912; FFJ 6: 260, fig. 231. 1995; FRPS 10(2): 218, pl. 54: 1–7. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 5: 524, pl. 221. 2000; FOC 22: 619. 2006; FGD 9: 487, fig. 257. 2009.
Phalaris hispida Thunb., Fl. Jap. 44. 1784.
Arthraxon pauciflorus Honda, Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 39: 276. 1925; FTW ed. 2, 5: 526. 2000.
Arthraxon ciliaris P. Beauv, Ess. Agrostogr. 111, pl. 11, fig. 6. 1812; FKH 321. 1912.
Arthraxon hispidus (Thunb.) Makino var. cryptatherus (Hackel) Honda, FHN 4: 474. 1977; FRPS 10(2): 221. 1997.

Annual herb. Culms slender, glabrous, sprawling, creeping and rooting at lower nodes, 30–60 cm tall, many-branched. Leaf sheaths shorter than internode, glabrous or tuberculate-hispid; leaf blades ovate-lanceolate, 2–5 × 0.6–1.5 cm, glabrous, pubescent or tuberculate-pilose, base amplexicaul, margins pectinate-setose at least around base; ligule membranous, margins ciliate. Racemes slender, 2–10 or more, digitate or fascicles, terminal. Sessile spikelet greyish green or purplish, ovate-lanceolate, laterally compressed; lower glume lanceolate, herbaceous, abaxially rounded, margins membranous, 6–9-veined, veins scabridhispidulous to spinulose; upper glume boat-shaped, as long as lower glume, 3-veined; lower lemma oblong, 2/3 lower glume length, hyaline membranous, acute; upper lemma as long as lower palea, hyaline membranous, with a geniculate awn near the base; awn up to 12 mm, well developed and exserted from glumes, or sometimes reduced and included. Pedicellate spikelet usually absent; pedicel reduced to a minute stump, sometimes up to 2 mm or more.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. HK sheet 42047.
Distribution: Widely spread over most provinces of China; tropical to temperate regions of the Old World.
Ecology: Shade and moist places. Flowering & fruiting: Sep.–Nov.

Arundinella nepalensis Trin. 石芒草（石珍芒）
Gram. Panic. 62. 1826; FHK 416. 1861; FKH 318. 1912; FHN 4: 445. 1977; FFJ 6: 188, fig. 156. 1995; FRPS 10(1): 147, fig. 45: 1–3. 1990; FOC 22: 568. 2006; FGD 9: 398. 2009.

Perennial herb. Culms erect, stout, 0.6–2(–3) m tall, simple or branched, internodes usually glabrous, nodes appressed silky pubescent. Leaf sheaths shorter than internodes except 1–2 nodes at base, glabrous or pubescent; leaf blades linear or linear-lanceolate, 10–50 × 0.5–2 cm, glabrous or thinly to densely tuberculate-pilose, base rounded, apex long acuminate; ligule dry membranous, very short. Panicle open or loosely contracted; central axis ribbed, smooth; branches slender, alternate, fasciculate or subverticillate; pedicels unequal, glabrous. Glumes usually glabrous; lower glume ovate-lanceolate, 2–4 mm, 3–5-veined; upper glume as long as spikelet, 4.5–5.5 mm, 5-veined; lower floret staminate or barren; upper floret bisexual, lemma awned; awn geniculate with brown twisted column.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. S. P. Lau 583; Y. W. Lam 939; HK sheet 14993.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, SE Xizang, Hubei, Fujian; Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Pakistan, Thailand, Vietnam, Africa, Australia.
Ecology: Mountain grasslands, hill thickets. Flowering & fruiting: Sep.–Nov.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Shatin Pass Rd., Ma Liu Shui, Ninepin Group, Lantau Island, Po Toi Islands
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Arundinella setosa Trin. 刺芒野古草
Gram. Panic. 63. 1826; FHK 416. 1861; FKH 318. 1912; FHN 4: 445, fig. 1236. 1977; FFJ 6: 187, fig. 155. 1995; FRPS 10(1): 163, pl. 51: 1–3. 1990; FTW ed. 2, 5: 444, pl. 183. 2000; FOC 22: 565. 2006; FGD 9: 399. 2009.
Arundinella sinensis Rendle, J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 36: 342. 1904; FKH 318. 1912.

Perennial stout herb. Culms erect, tufted or solitary, (35–)60–190 cm tall, nodes glabrous or pubescent. Leaf sheaths glabrous or tuberculate-hispid; leaf blades linear, flat or margins slightly inrolled, 10 – 30(–70) × 0.3–1 cm, glabrous or tuberculatehispid; ligule dry membranous, ca. 0.5 mm, ciliate. Panicle open or somewhat contracted, 10–45 cm; central axis and branches scabrid; branches spreading or ascending, usually solitary; pedicels scabrid, unequal, apex usually with several white long stiff hairs. Spikelets 5–7 mm; glumes ovate-lanceolate, apex acuminate and awn-pointed, glabrous or scaberulous along veins; lower glume 4–6 mm, 3–5-veined; upper glume 5–7 mm, 5-veined; lower floret male or barren; upper floret bisexual, awned, flanked by 2 slender erect bristles; bristles mostly 1–3 mm; awn geniculate with brown twisted column, 6–10 mm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Shatin Pass Rd., Ma Liu Shui, Ninepin Group, Lantau Island, Po Toi Islands. Y. W. Lam 1059; HK sheet 41946, 42042.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Hubei, Henan, Anhui, Jiangxi, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; widely spread over India, Indochina through Malay Peninsula to Indonesia, Philippines, New Guinea and Australia.
Ecology: Margins of forests, grassy hillsides. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Dec.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Siu Lek Yuen, Chuen Lung, Peng Chau
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Arundo donax L. 蘆竹
Sp. Pl. 1: 81. 1753; FKH 327. 1912; FHN 4: 367. 1977; FFJ 6: 130, fig. 101. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 326, pl. 123. 2000; FRPS 9(2): 20. 2002; FOC 22: 448. 2006; FGD 9: 339. 2009.

Perennial, reed-like herb, 2–6 m tall. Culms stout, erect, 1–3 cm in diam., often with slender branches from upper nodes. Leaf blades linear-lanceolate, flat, 30–60 × 2–5 cm, base rounded or cordate, amplexicaul, margins scabrous; ligule ca. 2 mm, fimbriate on upper margin, siliceous on dorsal side; leaf sheaths longer than internodes, usually glabrous except hairy at mouth. Panicle 30–70 × 5–8(10) cm, usually purplish, densely branched; branches 10–25 cm, ascending, axes strigose at nodes. Spikelets terete, 10–15 mm, 2–5-flowered; glumes subequal, (8–)10–13 mm, lanceolate to narrowly lanceolate, papery, siliceous, 3–5-veined, apex acute or with short awn; lower glume covered with a few silky hairs abaxially; lemma linear-lanceolate, (6–)8–13 mm, 3–7-veined, midvein prolonged into ca. 3 mm awn, 2 lateral veins also shortly extended, basal part densely covered with long silky hairs which are nearly as long as lemma; palea ca. 1/2 length of lemma, 2-keeled, margins ciliate, apex truncate; lodicules 2, truncate, veined. Stamens 3, anthers ca. 2.5 mm.

Locality: Siu Lek Yuen, Chuen Lung, Peng Chau. Y. S. Lau 2538; L. Y. Lo 363; HK sheet 41736.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan (cultivated); Asia-Temperate, Indochina, Indian Subcontinent, N Africa, cultivated and naturalized elsewhere.
Ecology: River banks and other damp places. Flowering & fruiting: Oct.–Dec.
Uses: Ornamental, fuel (potential biomass for energy generation).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Wong Chuk Hang, Tai Lung Farm
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Avena fatua L. 野燕麥
Sp. Pl. 1: 80. 1753; FHK 430. 1861; FKH 326. 1912; FRPS 9(3): 172, pl. 44: 4–6. 1987; FFJ 6: 126, fig. 97. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 351. 2000; FOC 22: 324. 2006; FGD 9: 389. 2009.
Avena fatua L. subsp. meridionalis Malzev, Trudy Prikl. Bot. 20: 140. 1929.
Avena meridionalis (Malzev) Roshev., Fl. Turkm. 1: 105. 1932; FRPS 9(3): 170. 1987.

Annual herb, 60 – 120 cm tall. Culms erect or geniculate at base, glabrous, 2–4-noded. Leaf blades linear, 10–30 × 0.4–1.5 cm, scabrid or adaxial surface and margins pilose; ligule tongue-shaped, 1–5 mm; leaf sheaths glabrous or basal sheaths puberulous. Panicle narrowly to broadly pyramidal, 10–40 cm, branches scabrid. Spikelets pendulous, 1.8–2.5 cm, 2–3-flowered; rachilla articulate beneath each floret, easily disarticulating at maturity, internodes hirsute or glabrous, callus densely bearded with hairs up to 4 mm; glumes lanceolate, subequal, herbaceous, 9–11-veined, apex finely acute; lemmas 1.5–2.5 cm, leathery, densely hispid in lower half, green and scaberulous above, awned from near middle, apex unequally and shortly 2–4-toothed; awn 2–4 cm, geniculate, column twisted, blackish brown; palea flattened, 2-keeled, margins ciliate. Caryopsis hairy; hilum linear.

Locality: Wong Chuk Hang, Tai Lung Farm. HK sheet 30756.
Distribution: Widely spread over all provinces of China; native to Europe and W Asia.
Ecology: Farmlands, margins of fields, and abandoned lands. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Sep.
Uses: Animal food (fodder).

Avena fatua L. var. glabrata Peterm. 光稃野燕麥
Fl. Bienitz 13. 1841; FRPS 9(3): 173, pl. 44: 7. 1987; FFJ 6: 127. 1995; FOC 22: 325. 2006; FGD 9: 389. 2009.

It differs from the type variety by its lemmas being glabrous, and turning yellowish at maturity.

Locality: Fanling. Y. S. Lau 3113.
Distribution: The same as for the species.
Ecology: Grassy mountain slopes, roadsides, farmlands. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Sep.

Avena sativa L. 燕麥
Sp. Pl. 1: 79. 1753; FRPS 9(3): 173, pl. 44: 9 – 11. 1987; FTW ed. 2, 5: 351. 2000; FOC 22: 324. 2006; FGD 9: 389. 2009.

Annual herb, 40–80 cm tall. Leaf blades linear, 8–30 × 0.4–1.5 cm, glabrous, margins sometimes scaberulous; ligule papery, tongue-shaped, 2–6 mm; leaf sheaths usually glabrous. Panicle (10–)20–40 cm, nodding; branches spreading or contracted. Spikelets nodding, 2–3 cm, 1–2-flowered; rachilla ± glabrous, straight, not disarticulating or fracturing irregularly at maturity, florets lacking a basal bearded callus; glumes lanceolate, subequal, as long as spikelet, 7–9-veined; lemmas 1.2–2.5 cm, leathery in lower half, herbaceous and distinctly veined above, apex minutely and irregularly 2–4-denticulate; awn 2.5 –3.5 cm, weakly geniculate or rudimentary or absent; palea shorter than the lemma, minutely hairy on the two keels. Caryopsis hairy, adherent to lemma and palea at maturity, hilum linear.

Locality: So Kon Po, Castle Peak. Y. S. Lau 3285; HK sheet 8637, 8638.
Distribution: Cultivated throughout China.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Sep.
Uses: Food (cereal), animal food (fodder).

Axonopus compressus (Sw.) P. Beauv. 地毯草
Ess. Agrostogr. 12. 1812; FHN 4: 424, fig. 1223. 1977; FRPS 10(1): 278, pl. 84. 1990; FFJ 6: 224. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 456, pl. 189. 2000; FOC 22: 531. 2006; FGD 9: 426, fig. 220. 2009.
Milium compressum Sw., Prodr. 24. 1788.

Perennial herb, with creeping, long stolons. Culms 8–60 cm tall, nodes bearded. Leaf sheaths loose, strongly compressed, keeled, basal sheaths imbricate; leaf blades broadly linear to lanceolate, flat or folded, 5–20 × 0.6–1.2 cm, glabrous or adaxial surface pilose, apex rounded, margins sparsely ciliate at the base; ligule ca. 0.5 mm. Racemes 2–5, digitate or subdigitate, 4–10 cm; rachis triangular, glabrous; spikelets in 2-rows along one-side. Spikelets solitary, oblong-lanceolate, 2–3 mm, pilose or glabrous; lower lemma absent; upper glume as long as or longer than lower lemma, 2–4-veined, midvein absent; upper lemma oblong-elliptic, shorter than spikelet, leathery, margins slightly thicken and inrolled embraced same texture palea, obtuse with an apical tuft of hairs, mucronate and pubescent at apex; stigmas plumose, pale.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong (naturalised). Y. S. Lau 1799, 2253; S. P. Lau 49.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou,Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; originated from tropical America, widely introduced elsewhere.
Ecology: Roadsides, weedy places on moist ground. Flowering & fruiting: Summer to autumn.
Uses: Environment (erosion control), animal food (forage).

Axonopus fissifolius (Raddi) Kuhlm. 類地毯草
Comm. Linh. Telegr., Bot. 67(Bot. 11): 87. 1922; FOC 22: 531. 2006; FGD 9: 426. 2009.
Paspalum fissifolium Raddi, Agrostogr. Bras. 26. 1823.
Axonopus affinis Chase, J. Wash. Acad. Sci 28: 180. fig. 1, 2. 1938; FRPS 10(1): 280. 1990; FTW ed. 2, 5: 456. 2000; Check List HK Plants 324. 2002; 114. 2004.

Perennial herb; stolons creeping. Culms compressed, 15–50 cm tall, nodes glabrous. Leaf sheaths compressed; leaf blades broadly linear, folded, 5–20 × 0.3–0.6 cm, obtuse; ligule ciliate. Racemes 2–4, 2-paired, any others spaced slightly below, 3–8 cm, only slightly diverging; rachis glabrous. Spikelets oblong-lanceolate, 1.5–2 mm, pilose near margins and apex or subglabrous; upper glume and lower lemma 2–4-veined, margins with silky hairs; upper floret bisexual, lemma pale, ovate, leathery, obtuse; stigmas purple. Caryopsis elliptic-oblong.

Locality: Tai Lung Farm (cultivated). S. P. Lau 191; HK sheet 35848.
Distribution: Taiwan, Xizang (cultivated or naturalised); native to tropical America, naturalized in paleotropics.
Ecology: Moist muddy or sandy meadows. Flowering & fruiting: Summer to autumn.
Uses: Environment (erosion control), animal food (forage).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Kowloon, Sha Tin, Tai Po Kau, Tai Po, Sheung Shui, Lantau Island (cultivated)
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Bambusa beecheyana Munro 吊絲球竹
Trans. Linn. Soc. London. 26: 108. 1868; FKH 331. 1912; HKB 27. 1985; FOC 22: 36. 2006; FGD 9: 265, fig. 133. 2009.
Arundarbor beecheyana (Munro) Kuntze, Revis. Gen. Pl. 2: 761. 1891.
Dendrocalamopsis beecheyana (Munro) Keng f., J. Bamboo Res. 2(1): 12. 1983; FRPS 9(1): 143. 1996.
Neosinocalamus beecheyanus (Munro) Keng f. & T. H. Wen, J. Bamboo Res. 4(2): 18. 1985.
Sinocalamus beecheyanus (Munro) McClure, Lingnan Univ. Sci. Bull. 9: 67. 1940.

Culms to 16 m, 9–10 cm in diam., apically long pendulous; internodes 34–41 cm, initially thickly white powdery, sparsely pubescent, without a brown pubescent ring below nodes; wall 1.5–2 cm thick; nodes flat, basal ones without branches. Branches several, 1–3 dominant. Culm sheaths deciduous, leathery, initially with uneven, dark brown, spinous hairs; auricles small at lower nodes, larger at distal nodes; oral setae present or absent; ligule 2–4 mm, ciliate; blade recurved, triangular, base 1/2–4/5 as wide as sheath apex, adaxially hirtellous. Leaf sheaths initially hirtellous; ligule truncate, 0.5–1 mm; auricles absent or minute; oral setae scarce or absent; blade oblong-lanceolate, 11–28 × 1.5–3.5 cm. Pseudospikelets 1.5–2 × 0.5–0.8 cm; florets 6–8; rachilla not disarticulating, internodes ca. 2 mm. Glumes 2, cordate, 4–5 mm, ciliate; lemma ca. 0.9 × 0.9 cm; palea 4–8 mm, abaxially hirtellous, apex acuminate or obtuse; lodicules 3, ciliate. Anthers ca. 5 mm. Ovary ovoid, ca. 1.5 mm; styles 3–4 mm; stigmas 2–4, ca. 6 mm. Caryopsis unknown.

Locality: Kowloon, Sha Tin, Tai Po Kau, Tai Po, Sheung Shui, Lantau Island (cultivated). H. C. Tang 1127; Y. S. Lau 2671; L. T. Lo 637.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan, Taiwan.
Ecology: New shoots: Jun.–Jul.; flowering: Sep.–Dec.
Uses: Vegetable.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Shing Mun, Sha Tin, Tai Po Kau (cultivated)
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Bambusa chungii McClure 粉簞竹
Lingnan Sci. J. 15: 639. 1936; HKB 28. 1985; FRPS 9(1): 120, pl. 29. 1996; FOC 22: 33. 2006; FGD 9: 258, fig. 132. 2009.
Lingnania chungii (McClure) McClure, Lingnan Univ. Sci. Bull. 9: 35. 1940.
Lingnania chungii (McClure) McClure var. petilla T. H. Wen, J. Bamboo. Res. 1(1): 34. 1982.

Culms 5–10(–18) m, 3–5(–7) cm in diam.; internodes 30–45(–100) cm, initially white powdery, glabrous; wall 3–5 mm thick; nodes flat; sheath scars corky, initially with a ring of dense, brown hairs; branching from distal nodes only. Branches many, subequal. Culm sheaths deciduous, thinly leathery, initially white powdery, silky hairy, apex later glabrous, concave; auricles narrowly oblong, glossy; ligule ca. 1.5 mm, serrulate or long fimbriate; blade deciduous, strongly reflexed, base 1/5–1/3 as wide as sheath apex, adaxially hispidulous. Leaf sheaths glabrous; auricles usually developed; oral setae straight; blade lanceolate, 10–16(–20) × 1–2(–3.5) cm. Pseudospikelets ca. 2 cm; gemmiferous bracts 1–2; florets 4–5. Glumes 1–2; lemma 9–12 mm; palea about as long as lemma. Styles 1–2 mm; stigmas 3 or 2. Caryopsis triangular, 8 – 9 mm.

Locality: Shing Mun, Sha Tin, Tai Po Kau (cultivated). H. C. Tang 1125; Nan-Zhu 1125.
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, S Hunan, SE Yunnan.
Ecology: New shoots: Summer.
Uses: Ornamental.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Authority: L. C. Chia & H. L. Fung
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Bambusa chunii L. C. Chia & H. L. Fung 煥鏞簕竹
Kew Bull. 37: 593. 1983; HKB 29. 1985; FRPS 9(1): 58, pl. 13: 12. 1996; FOC 22: 13. 2006; FGD 9: 230. 2009.

Culms 10–12 m, 4.5–6.5 cm in diam., basally flexuose, apically drooping; internodes slightly curved, 25–30 cm, very thinly white powdery, very sparsely stiffly hairy, with a ring of grey hairs below each node; wall thick; branching to base. Branches at lower nodes usually solitary, with tough, sharp thorns, at upper nodes 3–several with central 3 longer and thicker. Culm sheaths tardily deciduous, with several marginal white stripes on each side, leathery, glabrous, apex obliquely truncate with unequal, triangular protuberance on each shoulder; auricles unequal, linear-lanceolate, small, usually wrinkled, abaxially hispidulous; oral setae well developed, 5–10 mm, undulate, hispidulous at base; ligule 5–7 mm, margin irregular, dentate, laciniate; blade erect, broadly lanceolate, abaxially glabrous, base nearly 1/2 width of sheath apex. Leaf blade lanceolate, 9.5–19 × 1.5–2 cm, abaxially pubescent, adaxially glabrous. Pseudospiklets linear, compressed, ca. 4.5 cm long, clustered at nodes of flowering branches; gemmiferous bracts 1–2, ovate, apex minutely obtuse or acute; fertile florets 5–14, and 1–2 sterile floret at apex; rachilla segments ca. 2 mm long, ciliate; lemma 9–10 × 4–4.5 mm, glossy and glabrous, veins in 9–11, apex acute; palea shorter than lemma, 8–9 × 3.5–4 mm, oblong, 2-keeled, glabrous, minutely ciliate on margins at its base, apex obtuse or sometimes emarginate; lodicules 3 subequal, ovate or obovate, 2 × 1 mm, 3-veined, the veins faint, ﬁmbriate along margins; stamens 6, anthers 3 × 0.3 mm, apex obtuse. Ovary narrow obovoid, apex thickened and scabrous, ciliate; style short; stigmas 3, long, plumose; Fruit ovoid, deep furrow lined, 6–7 × 2–2.5 cm.

Locality: Yuen Long. HK sheet 35339, 35340.
Distribution: Endemic to Hong Kong
Ecology: Cultivated around villages. New shoots: Summer.
Notes: The type specimen (Nan-Zhu (南竹隊) 2802, IBSC) was collected from Ko Po Tsuen, Yuen Long, New Territories in 1980. The species epithet is respectfully dedicated to Professor Woon-Young Chun, the founder and former Director of South China Botanical Garden. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Authority: L. C. Chia & H. L. Fung

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Bambusa eutuldoides McClure 大眼竹
Lingnan Univ. Sci. Bull. 9: 8. 1940; HKB 33. 1985; FRPS 9(1): 82, pl. 17: 1–12. 1996; FOC 22: 22. 2006; FGD 9: 241. 2009.

Culms 6–12 m, 4–6 cm in diam., basally straight, apically slightly drooping; internodes 30–40 cm, fistulose, initially thinly white powdery, sometimes sparsely deciduously stiffly hairy below nodes; wall ca. 5 mm thick; nodes slightly prominent, basal several with rings of grey-white silky hairs below and above sheath scar; branching from 2nd or 3rd node up. Branches several or many, clustered, central 3 dominant. Culm sheaths deciduous, triangular to narrowly triangular, leathery, glabrous or sometimes very sparsely stiffly strigose, apex long slanted along one side, extremely asymmetric, arched; auricles extremely asymmetric, of various shapes, rigid, wrinkled; larger auricle extremely decurrent, oblanceolate to narrowly oblong, 5–6.5 × ca. 1.5 cm; smaller auricle suborbicular or oblong, ca. 1 cm in diam., or sometimes thoroughly joined to blade base; oral setae undulate; ligule 3–5 mm, irregularly dentate or laciniate, shortly fimbriate; blade deciduous, erect, asymmetric, triangular to narrowly triangular, base slightly narrowed and then extending outward to join auricles, nearly 3/5 width of sheath apex, abaxially sparsely stiffly deciduous-hairy. Leaf blade abaxially green, lanceolate to broadly lanceolate, usually 12–25 × 1.4–2.5 cm, abaxially densely pubescent, adaxially glabrous. Pseudospikelets sessile, clustered at each node of flowering branches and branchlets, linear, 2.5–5.5 cm, with several bud-bearing bracts at base; florets 5–6; rachilla segments flat, 3–4 mm, apex inflated and ciliolate. Glume 1, with very small purple spots, oblong, 9–10 mm, 11-veined, glabrous, apex acute, apiculate; lemma similar to glumes, oblong, 1.2–1.3 cm, 13–15-veined; palea lanceolate, ca. 1.1 cm, keels ciliolate toward tip, 4-veined between and 2-veined on either side of keels; lodicules 3, unequal, anterior 2 narrow, ca. 2 mm, apex long ciliate, posterior 1 larger, broadly ovate or suborbicular, ca. 2 mm. Anthers ca. 5 mm, apex bifid. Ovary subglobose, ca. 1 mm in diam., apex hispidulous; style very short, hispidulous; stigmas 3. Caryopsis initially nearly obovoid, ca. 5 mm, apex hispidulous with persistent style base.

Locality: Tai Po Kau, Sheung Shui (cultivated). Nan-Zhu 2771; H. C. Tang 1100.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi.
Ecology: New shoots: Summer.
Uses: Environmental, ornamental.

Bambusa flexuosa Munro 小簕竹
Trans. Linn. Soc. London. 26: 101. 1868; FKH 331. 1912; HKB 34. 1985; FOC 22: 12. 2006; FGD 9: 228. 2009.
Arundarbor flexuosa (Munro) Kuntze, Revis. Gen. Pl. 2: 760. 1891.
Bambusa scabriculma W. T. Lin, J. S. China Agric. Univ. 14(1): 46. 1993.

Culms 6–7 m, 3.5–6 cm in diam., basally flexuose, apically nodding; internodes 20–30 cm, sparsely stiffly brown strigose, with a ring of silky brown hairs below each node; wall thick. Branches to base, solitary at lower nodes, flexuose, densely interwoven, branchlets specialized into tough thorns, higher nodes with 3–several branches. Culm sheaths tardily deciduous, leathery, prominently ribbed-striate when dry, sparsely stiffly dark brown strigose, apex concave with a triangular protuberance on each shoulder; auricles narrowly filiform or absent; ligule 4–5 mm, dentate or laciniate, fimbriate; blade erect or recurved, ovate-lanceolate to lanceolate, base ca. 1/2 as wide as sheath apex. Leaf blade narrowly lanceolate to lanceolate, 7–11 × 1.2–1.6 cm, both surfaces glabrous. Pseudospikelets solitary or clustered, slightly compressed, 2–3 cm, gemmiferous bracts ca. 4; florets 8–12 with middle florets perfect; rachilla flexuose, internodes flat, 2–2.5 mm, hispid. Glumes usually absent; lemma oblong-lanceolate, 8–10 mm, apex acute; palea usually shorter than lemma, keels ciliate; lodicules 3, subequal, margins long ciliate, apex obtuse. Filaments enlarged at base; anther obtuse at apex. Style short; stigmas 3.

Locality: Sha Tin, Fanling, Lantau Island (cultivated). H. C. Tang 1121; Y. S. Lau 2470; Nan-Zhu 2757.
Distribution: Guangdong, Hainan.
Ecology: Hills, river banks. New shoots: Summer.
Uses: Hedges. Notes: It has been named incorrectly by some authors as Bambusa bambos (L.) Voss.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Victoria Peak, New Territories, Lantau Island (cultivated)
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Bambusa gibba McClure 坭竹
Lingnan Univ. Sci. Bull. 9: 10. 1940; FHN 4: 354. 1977; HKB 35. 1985; FRPS 9(1): 68, pl. 14: 1–10. 1996; FOC 22: 16. 2006; FGD 9: 235. 2009.

Culms 7–10 m, 3.5–6 cm in diam., basally flexuose, apically suberect; internodes 30–40 cm, inflated near base, initially white powdery, basal internodes initially sparsely stiffly grey-white or brown strigose; wall 3–5 mm thick; nodes glabrous; branching to base. Branches usually 3 at lower nodes with branchlets sometimes specialized into weak thorns; several on middle and upper nodes, 3 central branches dominant. Culm sheaths deciduous, ribbed-striate when dry, glabrous, apex obliquely truncate, with a triangular protuberance on higher shoulder; auricles obviously unequal, sometimes weak; larger auricle ovate-lanceolate or narrowly oblong, 5–6 mm; smaller auricle ovate or elliptic, 2–3 mm; oral setae slender, undulate; ligule arched, 2–3 mm, finely dentate and fimbriate; blade deciduous, erect, narrowly triangular, base not narrowed, nearly 2/3 as wide as sheath apex. Leaf blade linear-lanceolate to narrowly lanceolate, 8.5–14.5 × 0.8–1.3 cm, abaxially densely pubescent, adaxially glabrous. Pseudospikelets linear, 2–3 cm; prophylls ovate, ca. 1.5 mm, keels ciliate, apex obtuse; gemmiferous bracts 4, ovate, 1.5–3.5 mm, apex obtuse and mucronate; florets 4–8; rachilla segments flat, ca. 3.5 mm, slightly hairy, apex inflated and ciliolate. Glume 1, ovate-elliptic, 6–6.5 mm, 15-veined, apex acute, mucronate; lemma ovate-oblong, ca. 1.1 cm, 17-veined, apex acute, mucronate; palea nearly as long as lemma or shorter, keels glabrous, 3-veined between and on either side of keels, apex obtuse with a cluster of white hairs; lodicules 3, subequal, ca. 1.5 mm, margins long ciliate toward apex, base thickened, anterior 2 broadly elliptic, posterior ovate. Anther obtuse at apex. Ovary ovoid, ca. 0.5 mm, base stalked, apex hairy; style ca. 0.5 mm; stigmas 3. Fruit unknown.

Locality: Victoria Peak, New Territories, Lantau Island (cultivated). Nan-Zhu 2770.
