Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan, Jiangxi; Vietnam.
Ecology: Low hills, around villages. New shoots: Summer.
Uses: Hedges, timber.

Bambusa gibboides W. T. Lin 魚肚腩竹
Acta Phytotax. Sin. 16(1): 70. 1978; HKB 36. 1985; FRPS 9(1): 98, pl. 18: 1 – 10. 1996; FOC 22: 26. 2006; FGD 9: 247. 2009.

Culms 10–12 m, 5–7 cm in diam., basally flexuose, apically drooping; internodes slightly curved, basally slightly swollen, 40–47 cm, initially thinly white powdery, stiffly brown strigose; wall slightly thick; nodes slightly prominent, basal 2 usually with rings of greywhite silky hairs; branching from basal or 2nd node up. Branches solitary on basal nodes, several to many at mid-culm and distal nodes, central obviously dominant. Culm sheaths deciduous, ribbed-striate when dry, with appressed, dull brown hairs near base, apex subtruncate; auricles unequal, horizontal along both sides of sheath apex, larger ones oblong to narrowly oblong, ca. 2 × 0.5–0.6 cm, smaller auricle elliptic, ca. 1/2 size of larger one; oral setae undulate; ligule 2–3 mm, dentate, shortly fringed; blade erect, narrowly ovate to ovatetriangular, ca. 1/2 as long as sheath, base slightly rounded and joined to auricles for ca. 3 mm, ca. 2/3 width of sheath apex. Leaf blade linear-lanceolate to narrowly lanceolate, 10–20 × 1.3–2 cm, abaxially densely pubescent, adaxially glabrous. Pseudospikelets several, clustered at nodes of flowering branches, linear-lanceolate, slightly flat, 3–4 cm; prophylls ovate, keels ciliolate toward apex, apex obtuse; gemmiferous bracts usually 2, ovate; florets 5–7, apical 1–2 usually sterile; rachilla segments flat, 3–4 mm, apex inflated and hairy. Glume 1, ovate, 6–8 mm, many-veined, apex mucronate; lemma ovate-elliptic, 1–1.4 cm, glabrous, many-veined, apex acute, mucronate; palea slightly longer than lemma, sparsely very shortly ciliolate near apex or sometimes subglabrous, 6–7-veined between and 3–4-veined on either side of keels, apex obtuse; lodicules 3, unequal, posterior 1 slightly larger, obovate, base thickened, margin finely ciliate. Filaments short; anthers yellow, apex obtuse. Ovary ovoid, apex hispidulous; style very short; stigmas 3. Caryopsis unknown.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 3299; Nan-Zhu 2775.
Distribution: Guangdong.
Ecology: New shoots: Summer.
Uses: Vegetable.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Victoria Peak, Tai Po Kau, Sheung Shui (cultivated)
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Bambusa multiplex (Lour.) Raeusch. ex Schult. & Schult. f. 孝順竹（蓬來竹）
Syst. Veg. 7(2): 1350. 1830; FGZ 771. 1956; FHN 4: 355. 1977; FRPS 9(1): 108, pl. 26: 1–15. 1996; FOC 22: 30. 2006; FGD 9: 251. 2009.
Arundo multiplex Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 1: 58. 1790.
Arundinaria glaucescens (Willd.) P. Beauv., Ess. Agrostogr. 144, 152. 1812.
Bambusa glaucescens (Willd.) Merr., Philipp. J. Sci. 7(4): 230. 1912; HKB 37. 1985.
Bambusa nana Roxb., Fl. Ind. (ed. 1832) 2: 199. 1832.
Ludolfia glaucescens Willd., Ges. Naturf. Freunde Berlin Mag. Neuesten Entdeck. Gesammten Naturk. 2: 320. 1808.

Culms suberect or apically slightly drooping, 4–7 m, 1.5–2.5 cm in diam.; internodes 30–50 cm, thinly white powdery, distally stiffly deciduously brown or dull brown hairy, especially densely so below nodes; wall usually rather thin; nodes slightly prominent, glabrous; branching from 2nd or 3rd node up. Branches several to many, clustered, subequal or central slightly dominant. Culm sheaths deciduous, trapezoid, initially thinly white powdery, glabrous, asymmetrically arched, slanted along outer side, apex asymmetrically arched, convex; auricles very small to inconspicuous, oral setae few; ligule 1–1.5 mm, irregularly dentate; blade deciduous, erect, narrowly triangular, base nearly as wide as sheath apex, abaxially with scattered, stiff, dull brown hairs, adaxially scabrous, apex acuminate. Leaves 5–12 per ultimate branch; leaf blade abaxially pale glaucous, adaxially bright green, linear, 5–16 × 0.7–1.6 cm, abaxially densely pubescent, adaxially glabrous. Pseudospikelets solitary or several clustered at nodes of flowering branches, linear to linear-lanceolate, 3–6 cm; prophylls ca. 3.5 mm, 2-keeled, keels ciliolate; gemmiferous bracts usually 1 or 2, ovate to narrowly ovate, 4–7.5 mm, glabrous, 9–13-veined, apex obtuse or acute; florets (3–)5–13, middle ones fertile; rachilla segments flat, 4–4.5 mm, glabrous. Glumes absent; lemma asymmetrical, oblong-lanceolate, ca. 1.8 cm, glabrous, 19–21-veined, apex acute; palea linear, 1.4–1.6 cm, keels ciliolate, 6-veined between and 4-veined on one side and 3-veined on other side of keels, apex subtruncate, ciliolate, with a fine hairy tip on each side; lodicules 3, anterior 2 subovate, 2.5–3 mm, posterior narrowly lanceolate, 3–5 mm, margins glabrous. Filaments 0.8–1 cm; anthers purple, ca. 6 mm, apex penicillate. Ovary ovoid, ca. 1 mm, base with stalk ca. 1 mm, apex thickened and hispidulous; stigmas 3 or variable in number, ca. 5 mm, directly exserted from ovary apex. Mature caryopsis unknown.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Tai Po Kau, Sheung Shui (cultivated). Y. S. Lau 3047; L. T. Lo 637; S. C. Lau 747. Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan, Yunnan; SE Asia.
Ecology: Wild and cultivated, fields, mountains, low hills, riversides. New shoots: Summer.
Uses: Ornamental, hedges.

It differs from B. multiplex var. multiplex by culm internodes yellow with green stripes.

Locality: Cultivated.
Distribution: Guangdong.

Bambusa multiplex (Lour.) Raeusch. ex Schult. & Schult. f. 'Fernleaf' 鳳尾竹
R. A. Young, Agric. Handb. 193: 40. 1961; FTW 5: 755. 1978; FRPS 9(1): 113. 1996.
Bambusa glaucescens (Willd.) Siebold ex Munro ‘Fernleaf’, Phytologia 52(4): 258. 1982; HKB 38. 1985.
Bambusa multiplex (Lour.) Raeusch. ex Schult. & Schult. f. var. fernleaf R. A. Young, Natl. Hort. Mag. 25: 261. 1946.
Bambusa multiplex (Lour.) Raeusch. ex Schult. & Schult. f. f. fernleaf (R. A. Young) T. P. Yi, J. Sichuan For. Sci. & Techn. 28(3): 17. 2007.

It differs from B. multiplex var. riviereorum by plants 3–6 m tall, culm internodes hollow, branchlets slightly curved downwards, with 9–13 leaves, leaf blade 3.3–6.5 × 0.4–0.7 cm.

Locality: Ma Liu Shui, Sheung Shui (cultivated). H. C. Tang 1116.
Distribution: S, E & SW China.
Ecology: Wild and cultivated, fields, mountains, low hills, riversides. New shoots: Summer.

R. A. Young, Agric. Handb. 193: 41. 1961; FRPS 9(1): 112. 1996.
Bambusa glaucescens (Willd.) Siebold ex Munro ‘Silvrstripe’ L.C. Chia & But; Phytologia 52(4): 259. 1982; HKB 39. 1985.

Bambusa lapidea McClure 油簕竹（油刺竹）
Lingnan Sci. J. 19: 531. 1940; FGZ 774. 1956; HKB 41. 1985; FRPS 9(1): 63, pl. 15: 13. 1996; FOC 22: 15. 2006; FGD 9: 233. 2009.
Bambusa miyiensis T. P. Yi, Bull. Bot. Res., Harbin 2(4): 99. 1982.

Culms 7  7 m, 4–7 cm in diam., basally straight, apically slightly drooping; internodes 20–35 cm, obviously shorter and slightly swollen near base and sometimes inconspicuously pale green striped and purple streaked, glabrous; wall 1–2 cm thick; nodes with a ring of grey-white silky hairs below and above sheath scar, several basal nodes usually with short aerial roots, lower ones with a ring of silky hairs above sheath scar; branching from basal 3rd or 4th node up. Branches usually several to many, clustered at mid-culm and basal nodes, central 3 codominant; branchlets usually specialized into weak or tough thorns. Culm sheaths tardily deciduous, leathery, glossy when fresh, ribbed-striate when dry, glabrous or stiffly hairy at basal margins only, apex subtruncate or slightly asymmetrical, arched; auricles undulate, wrinkled, inflated outward, densely hispidulous or subglabrous abaxially, unequal; larger auricle slightly decurrent, orbicular or ovate, 3.5–4 × 1–1.5 cm; small ones oblong or ovate, ca. 3 × 1–1.5 cm; ligule 4–5 mm, margin nearly entire and densely fimbriate; blade persistent, erect, inflated outward, ovate to oval, base slightly narrowed and then extended toward both sides and joined to auricles, apex abruptly acuminate, sharply tipped. Leaf blade linear-lanceolate to lanceolate, usually 8–23 × 1–2 cm, both surfaces glabrous. Pseudospikelets linear, compressed, more than 2 cm; gemmiferous bracts 2–4; fertile florets 5–6, then 2 sterile florets; rachilla segments usually fistulose, ca. 2.5 cm, apex ciliolate. Glumes absent; lemma to 8.5 mm, abaxially glossy and glabrous, many-veined, margins glabrous, apex obtuse or acute and finely tipped; palea slightly shorter than lemma, keels ciliate near apex, 2-veined between and scabrous on either side of keels, apex obtuse or sometimes emarginate; lodicules 3, subequal, ovate or obovate, ca. 1.5 mm, margins ciliate, apex obtuse. Anthers ca. 4 mm, apex obtuse. Ovary narrowly obovoid, apex thickened and scabrous; style very short, scabrous; stigmas 3.

Locality: Tai Po Kau, Sheung Shui, Kam Tin (cultivated). H. C. Tang 1104, 1132; N. K. Chan 2759.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Sichuan, Yunnan.
Ecology: Plains, hills, riversides, around villages. New shoots: Summer; flowering: Aug.–Sep.
Uses: Scaffolding, construction.

Bambusa pachinensis Hayata var. hirsutissima (Odash.) W. C. Lin 長毛米篩竹
Bull. Taiwan Forest. Res. Inst. 98: 21. 1964; FRPS 9(1): 105, pl. 25: 15 – 16. 1996; FOC 22: 28. 2006; FGD 9: 249. 2009.
Leleba beisitiku Odash. var. hirsutissima Odash., J. Soc. Trop. Agric. 8: 58. 1936.
Bambusa textilis McClure var. fusca McClure, Lingnan Univ. Sci. Bull. 9: 16. 1940; HKB 48. 1985.
Leleba pachinensis (Hayata) Nakai var. hir-sutissima (Odash.) W. C. Lin, Bull. Taiwan Forest. Res. Inst. 69: 61, fig. 28–29. 1961.

Culms 3–8 m, 1–4.5 cm in diam., apically slightly drooping; internodes 30–70 cm, initially thinly white powdery, sparsely stiffly pale or dark brown strigose; wall thin; nodes flat, basal 5 nodes usually with rings of grey-white silky hairs below and above sheath scar; branching from 8th to 10th node up. Branches several to many, clustered, 3 central dominant. Culm sheaths deciduous, leathery, rigid, broadly arched, uniformly stiffly dull brown strigose, apex slanted on outer side, asymmetrical; auricles unequal, slightly wrinkled, larger ones oblong or lanceolate, 1–1.5 × 0.4–0.5 cm, ends subrounded and slanted downward, smaller auricle subovate, ca. 1/3 size of larger one, ends slightly ascending; oral setae fine, curved, long; ligule ca. 1 mm, long fimbriate, fimbriae 5–10 mm; blade erect, slightly asymmetrically ovate to ovate-triangular, 1/3–1/2 length of sheath, base slightly cordate, narrowed and joined with auricles for 2–3 mm, abaxially very sparsely brown hairy, adaxially scabrous, apex acuminate, apiculate. Leaf blade linear to lanceolate, 8–18 × 1–2 cm, abaxially densely villous, adaxially glabrous. Pseudospikelets lanceolate to linear-lanceolate, 2–3.5 × 0.4–0.5 cm; prophylls ca. 2.5 mm, keels ciliolate; gemmiferous bracts 2–3, ovate, to 7 mm, glabrous, 15–17-veined, apex obtuse and mucronate. Lemma ovate-elliptic, ca. 1.2 cm, glabrous, 17–19-veined, apex acute, mucronate; palea lanceolate, ca. 1.1 cm, slightly shorter than lemma, keels not ciliate, 5–6-veined between and 3–4-veined on either side of keels, margin irregularly dentate, apex 3-fid and with a cluster of white long hairs; lodicules 3, unequal, anterior 2 spatulate, ca. 3 mm, margins long ciliate, posterior 1 nearly obovate-elliptic, ca. 1.6 mm. Filaments slender; anthers ca. 4 mm. Ovary ovoid, ca. 1.5 mm, base stalked, apex thickened and hispid; style ca. 0.5 mm, hispid; stigmas 3, ca. 5 mm. Mature caryopsis unknown.

Locality: Tai Po Kau, Sha Tin, Lantau Island. Nan-Zhu 2776, 2785; HK sheet 0883.
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Taiwan, Zhejiang.
Ecology: Usually cultivated, low hills, around villages. New shoots: Summer.
Uses: Weaving.

Bambusa rutila McClure 木竹
Lingnan Sci. J. 19: 533. 1940; HKB 45. 1985; FRPS 9(1): 63, pl. 14: 11. 1996; FOC 22: 14. 2006; FGD 9: 232. 2009.
Bambusa shuangliuensis T. P. Yi, Bull. Bot. Res. (Harbin) 2(4): 100, fig. 2. 1982.

Culms 8–12 m, 4–6 cm in diam., basally slightly flexuose, apically slightly drooping; internodes 30–35 cm; wall thick; lower internodes usually initially densely stiffly dark brown strigose, basal internodes sometimes with several inconspicuous pale yellow stripes; nodes with a ring of grey-white silky hairs below and above sheath scar and a ring of stiff, brown hairs on sheath scar, several basal nodes usually with short aerial roots; branching from 3rd or 4th node up. Branches usually 3–12 on mid-culm and basal nodes; central 3 dominant, reflexed; those on lower nodes usually with branchlets specialized into weak or tough thorns. Culm sheaths tardily deciduous, ribbed-striate when dry, glabrous or with stiff, dark brown hairs near margins and base, apex slightly oblique and truncate; auricles extremely unequal, abaxially densely hispidulous; larger auricle ovate-oblong, oblong, or narrowly reniform, inflated outward, undulate, wrinkled, ca. 1.5 cm wide; smaller auricle subovate or elliptic, ca. 1 cm wide, undulate, wrinkled; ligule 4–5 mm, dentate, fimbriate; blade persistent, erect, subtriangular or ovate, base nearly 2/5 as wide as sheath apex. Leaf blade linear-lanceolate to narrowly lanceolate, usually 10–18 × 1–1.7 cm, abaxially densely pubescent, adaxially glabrous. Pseudospikelets linear-lanceolate, compressed, to 3 cm; prophylls obtuse at apex, keels ciliolate; gemmiferous bracts 3–8, ovate, 1–4 mm, margins ciliolate or subglabrous near apex, apex obtuse and finely tipped; florets ca. 9, apical 1–2 florets sterile; rachilla segments 2–3 mm, apex ciliolate. Glumes absent; lemma ovate-lanceolate, to 8 mm, abaxially glabrous, many-veined, margins ciliolate near apex, finely tipped, apex obtuse or acute and scabrous; palea longer or shorter than lemma, keels ciliate or scabrous at apex, 2–3-veined between keels, apex penicillate; lodicules 3, subequal, ovate or obovate, margins ciliate. Anther obtuse at apex. Ovary obovoid, apex thickened and hairy; style very short; stigmas 3, scabrid.

Locality: Fanling, Chung Mei (cultivated). N. K. Chan 2755; HK sheet 16466.
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Sichuan.
Ecology: Open fields, around villages. New shoots: Summer; flowering: Oct.–Dec.
Uses: Materials (construction).

Bambusa sinospinosa McClure 車筒竹
Lingnan Sci. J. 19: 411. 1940; HKB 46. 1985; FRPS 9(1): 56, pl. 13: 1–11. 1996; FOC 22: 12. 2006; FGD 9: 229. 2009.

Culms 15–24 m, 8–14 cm in diam., apically slightly drooping; internodes 20–26 cm, mainly glabrous but with a ring of grey silky hairs below basal 1 or 2 nodes; wall 10–30 mm thick; branching to base. Branches usually solitary at lower nodes, with tough thorns; branchlets interwoven; branches 3–several above lower nodes. Culm sheaths tardily deciduous, leathery, densely stiffly dark brown hairy toward base, apex truncate; auricles usually reflexed, oblong to obovate, subequal, rugose, adaxially densely strigose, margin with undulate or erect setae; ligule 3–5 mm, dentate, fimbriate; blade erect or recurved, base ca. 1/2 width of sheath apex. Leaf blade linearlanceolate, 7–17 × 1.2–1.6 cm, both surfaces glabrous or abaxially proximally pilose. Pseudospikelets solitary or several clustered at each node of flowering branch, linear to linear-lanceolate, slightly compressed, to 4 cm, prophylls obtuse, keels ciliolate; gemmiferous bracts 3–5, narrowly triangular or subovate, glabrous, obtuse; fertile florets 6–12; rachilla internodes 2–4 mm. Glumes usually absent; lemma ovate-oblong, 5–9.5 mm, many-veined, apex obtusely acute or acute with fine tip; palea usually slightly longer than lemma, keels ciliolate, 3–5-veined between keels; lodicules 3, unequal, obovate, ca. 1.4 mm, obtuse, margins ciliate. Filaments distinct; anther obtuse at apex. Ovary narrow, apex thickened and hispidulous; style slender, hispidulous; stigmas 3.

Locality: New Territiories (cultivated). Nan-Zhu 2772.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan.
Ecology: Riversides, near villages. New shoots: May–Jun.; flowering: Aug.–Dec.
Uses: Materials (construction), environmental.
Notes: Bambusa arundo sensu Benth. (FHK 435. 1861) perhaps belongs to this species.

Bambusa textilis McClure 青皮竹
Lingnan Univ. Sci. Bull. 9: 14. 1940; FGZ 772. 1956; HKB 47. 1985; FRPS 9(1): 122, pl. 30: 1–12. 1996; FOC 22: 29. 2006; FGD 9: 250. 2009.

Culms 8–10 m, 3–5 cm in diam., apically slightly drooping; internodes green, 40–70 cm, initially thinly white powdery, ± stiffly pale brown hairy; wall 2–5 mm thick; nodes flat, glabrous; branching from 7th to 11th node upward. Culm sheaths deciduous, leathery, rigid, slightly glossy, basally stiffly dull brown strigose, apex slightly slanted and asymmetric, broadly arched; auricles unequal, ends not decurrent, larger one narrowly oblong to lanceolate, slightly slanted, ca. 1.5 × 0.4–0.5 cm, smaller one oblong, not slanted, ca. 1/2 size of larger; oral setae slender, undulate; ligule ca. 2 mm, dentate or sometimes laciniate, ciliolate; blade deciduous, erect, narrowly ovatetriangular, ca. 2/3 as long as sheath, abaxially sometimes stiffly hairy between veins, basally sparsely dull brown hairy, adaxially scabrid, base slightly cordate, narrowed, nearly 2/3 as wide as sheath apex. Leaf blade linear-lanceolate to narrowly lanceolate, 9–17 × 1–2 cm, abaxially densely pubescent, adaxially glabrous. Pseudospikelets solitary or several to many, clustered at each node of flowering branches, dull purple when fresh, bronze-coloured when dry, linear-lanceolate, slightly curved, 3–4.5 × 0.5–0.8 cm; prophylls ovate, ca. 3 mm, keels glabrous; gemmiferous bracts 2–3, ovate, 3–4.5 mm, glabrous, apex acute, mucronate; florets 5–8, apical one sterile; rachilla segments subterete or flat, ca. 4 mm, apex enlarged. Glume 1, ovate, ca. 6 mm, ca. 20-veined, glabrous, apex acute, mucronate; lemma elliptic, 1.1–1.4 cm, glabrous, ca. 25-veined, apex acute, mucronate; palea lanceolate, 1.2–1.4 cm, slightly longer than lemma, keels glabrous, ca. 10-veined between and 4-veined on either side of keels; lodicules unequal; anterior 2 subspatulate, ca. 3 mm, margins long ciliate; posterior obovate-elliptic, ca. 2 mm. Filaments slender; anthers yellow, ca. 5 mm. Ovary broadly ovoid, ca. 2 mm in diam., base stalked, apex thickened and hispidulous; style ca. 0.7 mm, hispidulous; stigmas 3, 6–7 mm. Mature caryopsis unknown.

Locality: Tai Po Kau, Kwun Yam Shan, Sheung Shui (cultivated). H. C. Tang 1109; Nan-Zhu 2768; S. C. Lau 753.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi. E
cology: Usually cultivated, along rivers, around villages. New shoots: Summer.
Uses: Weaving, ornamental.

Bambusa textilis McClure var. glabra McClure 光稈青皮竹（黃竹）
Lingnan Univ. Sci. Bull. 9: 16. 1940; HKB 49. 1985; FRPS 9(1): 125. 1996; FOC 22: 30. 2006; FGD 9: 251. 2009.

Culms 3–5 cm in diam.; internodes and sheaths glabrous. Culm sheath blade nearly 1/2 as long as sheath proper, base slightly rounded; ligule 1–1.5 mm.

Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi.

Locality: New Territories (cultivated). Nan-Zhu 2764.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi.

Bambusa tuldoides Munro 青稈竹（花眉竹）
Trans. Linn. Soc. London. 26: 93. 1868; FKH 331. 1912; HKB 51. 1985; FRPS 9(1): 87, pl. 20: 1–10. 1996; FOC 22: 23. 2006; FGD 9: 243, fig. 131. 2009.
Bambusa angulata Munro, Trans. Linn. Soc. London 26(1): 94. 1868.
Bambusa breviflora Munro, Trans. Linn. Soc. London 26(1): 96. 1868.
Bambusa fauriei Hack., Bull. Herb. Boissier, sér. 2, 4(6): 529. 1904.
Bambusa flavonoda W. T. Lin, J. Bamboo Res. 1986(2): 23. 1986.
Bambusa longiflora W. T. Lin, Bull. Bot. Lab. N.-E. Forest. Inst., Harbin 1980(6): 85, fig. 1. 1980.
Bambusa parvifolia W. T. Lin, Bamboo Res. 1986(2): 22. 1986.
Chimonobambusa angulata (Munro) Nakai, Sci. Educ. (Tokyo) 15(16): 67. 1932.
Tetragonocalamus angulatus (Munro) Nakai, J. Jap. Bot. 9(2): 86, 88, pl. 10. 1933.
Bambusa tulda auct. non Roxb.: FHK 434. 1861.

Culms 6–10 m, 3–5 cm in diam., apically slightly drooping; internodes 30–36 cm, initially thinly white powdery; wall thick; nodes slightly prominent, basal 1 or 2 with rings of grey-white silky hairs below and above sheath scar; branching from base up. Branches several to many, clustered, central 3 dominant. Culm sheaths deciduous, convex and slanted along outer margin for 1/10–1/8 of length of sheath, with 1–3 pale yellow stripes toward outer margin, glabrous, apex asymmetrically arched; auricles unequal, outer one larger, ovate to ovate-elliptic, ca. 2.5 × 1–1.4 cm, slightly wrinkled; inner one smaller, ovate to elliptic, ascending, ca. 1/2 size of larger; oral setae slender, undulate; ligule 3–4 mm, laciniate, dznsely fimbriate; blade deciduous, erect, asymmetrically ovate-triangular to narrowly triangular, sparsely deciduously stiffly brown or pale brown strigose, base slightly rounded and then extending outward to join auricles for 5–7 mm, nearly 2/3–3/4 width of sheath apex, margin slightly wrinkled near base and fringed, apex subulate, acuminate. Leaf blade lanceolate to narrowly lanceolate, 10–18 × 1.5–2 cm, abaxially densely pubescent, adaxially glabrous or sparsely pilose near base. Pseudospikelets several at each node of flowering branches, pale green, linear-lanceolate, slightly flat, 2–3 × 0.3–0.4 cm; prophylls 2-keeled, keels ciliate, subtended by sheath-like bracts; gemmiferous bracts 2, glabrous, apex obtuse; florets 6 – 7, proximally and distally sterile; rachilla segments flat, 3–4 mm, apex inflated and cupular, hairy. Glume 1, ovateoblong, ca. 8.5 mm, glabrous, apex acute; lemma ovate-oblong, 1.1–1.4 cm, ca. 19-veined, glabrous, apex obtuse, mucronate; palea about as long as or slightly shorter than lemma, 4-veined between and 4-veined on either side of keels, penicillate; lodicules 3, anterior 2 obovate, oblique, short, ca. 2.5 mm, broad, margins long ciliate; posterior 1 long, ca. 3 mm, narrow. Anthers ca. 3 mm, apex emarginate. Ovary obovoid, ca. 1.2 mm, stalked, apex thickened and hispid; style ca. 0.7 mm, hispid; stigmas 3, ca. 5.5 mm. Caryopsis terete, slightly curved, ca. 8 mm, ca. 1.5 mm in diam., apex obtuse and thickened, hispid, with remains of style.

Locality: New Territories, Lantau Island. H. C. Tang 1108; Y. S. Lau 849, 2686.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi.
Ecology: Low hills, river banks, commonly cultivated around villages. New shoots: Summer.
Uses: Timber, weaving.
Notes: The type specimen (Hance 3657, K) was collected from Hong Kong in 1862.

Bambusa ventricosa McClure 佛肚竹
Lingnan Sci. J. 17: 57. 1938; FGZ 770. 1956; FHN 4: 354. 1977; FTW 5: 764, pl. 1511. 1978; HKB 52. 1985; FRPS 9(1): 70, pl. 15: 1–12. 1996; FOC 22: 17. 2006; FGD 9: 236. 2009.
Leleba ventricosa (McClure) W. C. Lin, Bull. Taiwan Forest Res. Inst. 150: 1305, fig. 1. 1963.

Culms dimorphic; normal culms 8–10 m, 3–5 cm in diam., basally flexuose, apically slightly drooping; internodes 30–35 cm, basally slightly swollen, not white powdery, initially glabrous; lower nodes with rings of grey-white silky hairs below and above sheath scar; branching from 3rd or 4th node up, basal 1 or 2 nodes also with short aerial roots; branches 1–3 on lower nodes; branchlets of these sometimes condensed into weak thorns; branches several to many at mid-culm and upper nodes, with central 3 slightly longer and thicker. Abnormal culms (usual in potted plants) 25–50 cm, 1–2 cm in diam., internodes shortened and swollen at base, branch internodes also shortened and swollen; branches only on upper nodes, usually solitary, without thorns. Culm sheaths deciduous, obviously ribbedstriate, glabrous, apex nearly symmetrical, broadly arched or subtruncate; auricles unequal; larger auricle narrowly ovate to ovatelanceolate, 5–6 mm; smaller auricle ovate, 3–5 mm; oral setae curved; ligule 0.5–1 mm, very shortly finely fimbriate; blade deciduous, erect or recurved, ovate to ovate-lanceolate, base slightly arched, narrowed, slightly narrower than sheath apex. Leaf sheath glabrous; ligule subtruncate, very short; auricles ovate or falcate; oral setae several, curved; blade linear-lanceolate to lanceolate, 9–18 × 1–2 cm, abaxially densely pubescent, adaxially glabrous. Pseudospikelets solitary or many clustered on each node, linear-lanceolate, slightly compressed, 3–4 cm; prophylls oval, 2.5–3 mm, 2-keeled, apex obtuse; gemmiferous bracts 1–2, narrowly ovate, 4–5 mm, 13–15-veined, apex acute; florets 6–8, basal 1–2 and apical 2–3 usually sterile; rachilla segments flat, 2–3 mm, apex inflated and cupular. Glumes absent or 1, ovate-elliptic, 6.5–8 mm, 15–17-veined, apex acute; lemma ovate-elliptic, 9–11 mm, glabrous, 19–21-veined, apex acute; palea nearly as long as lemma, ciliolate near apex, 4-veined between and on either side of keels, apex acuminate with a cluster of white hairs; lodicules 3, ca. 2 mm, margins long ciliate, anterior 2 slightly asymmetrical, posterior broadly elliptic. Filaments slender; anthers yellow, ca. 6 mm, apex obtuse. Ovary broadly ovoid, 1–1.2 mm, stalked, apex thickened and hairy; style very short, hairy; stigmas 3, ca. 6 mm. Fruit unknown.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Tai Po and gardens (cultivated). S. C. Lau 793.
Distribution: Guangdong.
Ecology: New shoots: Late summer to autumn.
Uses: Hedges, ornamental.
Notes: Widely cultivated in S China as an ornamental potted plant, this bamboo is sometimes considered to be a cultivar of Bambusa tuldoides, but the flowering material on which that decision was based, collected in the United States, may not represent this species. Moreover, in China the culm sheath of B. ventricosa is substantially different from that of B. tuldoides.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Po Kau, Sheung Shui, Shing Mun Arboretum and gardens (cultivated)
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Bambusa vulgaris Schrad. ex J. C. Wendl. 龍頭竹（銀竹、泰山竹）
Coll. Pl. 2: 26. 1810; FTW 5: 765, pl. 1512. 1978; HKB 53. 1985; FRPS 9(1): 96, pl. 24: 1–3. 1996; FOC 22: 25. 2006; FGD 9: 254. 2009.

Clumps rather open. Culms 8–15 m, 5–9 cm in diam., basally straight or flexuose, apically drooping; internodes deep green, 20–30 cm, initially thinly white powdery, stiffly pale brown strigose; wall slightly thick; nodes slightly prominent, basal several with aerial roots and rings of greyish white silky hairs below and above sheath scar; usually branching from lower nodes. Branches several to many, clustered, central dominant. Culm sheaths deciduous, ribbed-striate when dry, densely stiffly deciduously dark brown hairy, apex arched below blade, concave below auricles; auricles conspicuous, ascending, nearly equal in shape and size, oblong or reniform, 8–10 mm; oral setae curved, fine; ligule 3–4 mm, serrate, very shortly white ciliolate; blade deciduous, erect or deflexed, broadly triangular to triangular, base slightly rounded, ca. 1/2 width of sheath apex, abaxially sparsely stiffly dull brown hairy, adaxially densely stiffly dull brown hairy between veins, apex involute, sharply apiculate. Leaf blade narrowly lanceolate, 10–30 × 1.3–2.5 cm, both surfaces glabrous. Pseudospikelets several, clustered at nodes, narrowly lanceolate to linear-lanceolate, slightly flattened, 2–3.5 × 0.4–0.5 mm, apparently bifid; gemmiferous bracts several; florets 5–10; rachilla segments 1.5–3 mm. Glumes 1–2, abaxially shortly hairy near apex, apex apiculate; lemma 8–10 mm, abaxially shortly hairy near apex, apex apiculate; palea slightly shorter than lemma, keels ciliolate; lodicules 3, 2–2.5 mm, margins long ciliate. Anthers ca. 6 mm, apex penicillate. Style 3–7 mm, slender; stigmas 3, short.

Locality: Tai Po Kau, Sheung Shui, Shing Mun Arboretum and gardens (cultivated). H. C. Tang 1103; N. K. Chan 2763.
Distribution: Yunnan; SE Asia; cultivated in the tropical and subtropical regions all over the world.
Ecology: Riversides, open forests. New shoots: Summer.
Uses: Ornamental.

Bambusa vulgaris Schrad. ex J. C. Wendl. 'Vittata' 黃金間碧竹
Fieldiana, Bot., n.s. 24(2): 60. 1955; FRPS 9(1): 97. 1996; FGD 9: 254. 2009.
Bambusa striata Lodd. ex Lindl., Penny Cyclop. 3: 357. 1835.
Bambusa vulgaris Schrad. ex J. C. Wendl. var. striata (Lodd. ex Lindl.) Gamble, Ann. Roy. Bot. Gard. (Calcutta) 7: 44. 1896; FGZ 771. 1956; FHN 4: 354. 1977; FTW 5: 766. 1978.
Bambusa vulgaris Schrad. ex J. C. Wendl. var. vittata Rivière & C. Rivière, Bull. Soc. Natl. Acclim. France , ser. 3, 5: 640. 1878; HKB 54. 1985.

It differs from B. vulgaris by culm internodes yellow with green stripes.

Locality: Widely cultivated in Hong Kong. K. S. Pang 13.
Distribution: Widely cultivated in the tropical and subtropical regions of the world.
Ecology: New shoots: Summer.
Uses: Ornamental.

Bambusa vulgaris Schrad. ex J. C. Wendl. 'Wamin' 大佛肚竹
McClure, Bamb. 162, f. 72(5–6). 1966; FTW 5: 766. 1978; HKB 55. 1985; FRPS 9(1): 97. 1996; FGD 9: 255. 2009.
Bambusa ? wamin Brandis ex E. G. Camus, Bambus. 135. 1913.
Bambusa vulgaris Schrad. ex J. C. Wendl. f. waminii T. H. Wen, J. Bamboo Res. 4(2): 16. 1985.

It differs from B. vulgaris by culm internodes shortened and basally swollen.

Locality: Cultivated. P. S. Choi 273.
Distribution: Widely cultivated in the tropical and subtropical regions of the world.
Ecology: New shoots: Summer.
Uses: Ornamental.

Bothriochloa bladhii (Retz.) S. T. Blake 臭根子草
Proc. Roy. Soc. Queensland. 80: 62. 1969; FRPS 10(2): 148. 1997; FYN 9: 663, pl. 110: 4–6. 2003; FOC 22: 607. 2006; FGD 9: 494. 2009.

Andropogon bladhii Retz., Observ. Bot. 2: 27. 1761.
Andropogon intermedius R. Br., Prodr. 1: 202. 1810; FKH 323. 1912.
Andropogon vachellii Nees, Bot. Beechey Voy. 243. 1838; FHK 423. 1861.
Bothriochloa intermedia (R. Br.) A. Camus, Ann. Soc. Linn. Lyon, sér. 2, 76(1930): 164. 1931; FFJ 6: 267, fig. 239. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 527. 2000.
Bothriochloa glabra (Roxb.) A. Camus, Ann. Soc. Linn. Lyon, sér. 2, 76: 164. 1931; FHN 4: 476, fig. 1262. 1977; FRPS 10(2): 149. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 5: 527, pl. 222. 2000.

Perennial herb. Culms erect or decumbent at base, 60–90(–150) cm tall. Leaf sheaths glabrous, the upper shorter and the lower longer than internodes; leaf blades linear, 10–30 × 0.2–1 cm, glabrous or with tubercle-based hairs on both surfaces; ligule membranous, 0.5–2 mm, truncate. Inflorescence composed of many racemes borne in loose whorls along an elongate central axis; rachis internodes and pedicels thinly ciliate. Sessile spikelet bisexual, oblong-lanceolate, callus white bearded; lower glume narrowly oblong-lanceolate, dorsally compressed, glabrous or pubescent below middle, abaxially slightly concave, margins inrolled to 2-keeled, ciliate on keel, 5–7-veined; upper glume boat-shaped, margins membranous and the upper ciliate, acute; lower lemma ovate or oblong-lanceolate, seldom margins and apex sparsely ciliate, acute; upper lemma absent, linear, a geniculate awn arising from the apex, awn 10–16 mm. Pedicellate spikelet barren or rarely staminate, narrower than sessile spikelet.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. L. T. Lo 120, 589; Y. S. Lau 2250.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Xinjiang, Hubei, Hunan, Anhui, Fujian, Taiwan; Indian Subcontinent, Indochina, Malay Peninsula, Indonesia, SW Asia, Australia.
Ecology: Open grassy hillslopes, wastelands. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Oct.

Bothriochloa ischaemum (L.) Keng 白羊草
Contr. Biol. Lab. Chin. Assoc. Advancem. Sci., Sect. Bot. 10: 201. 1936; FHN 4: 476. 1977; FFJ 6: 266, fig. 238. 1995; FRPS 10(2): 144. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 5: 527, pl. 223. 2000; FOC 22: 608. 2006; FGD 9: 493. 2009.
Andropogon ischaemum L., Sp. Pl. 2: 1047. 1753; FKH 323. 1912.

Perennial herb. Culms tufted, erect or geniculately ascending, 30–70 cm tall. Leaf sheaths glabrous, congested at plant base; leaf blades linear, 3–18 × 0.2–0.3 cm, usually sparingly hairy with tubercle-based hairs, the lower glabrous, base rounded, apex acuminate; ligule ca. 1 mm, membranous, obtuse or rounded, ciliate. Inflorescence composed of 4–15 racemes, subdigitate; rachis internodes and pedicels ciliate with long white or pinkish silky hairs. Sessile spikelet oblong-lanceolate, callus bearded; lower glume usually cartilaginous, sometimes herbaceous, silky-pilose below 1/3 length, apex obtuse and membranous, margins inrolled, 5–7-veined; upper glume boatshaped, keel scabrous, ciliate above the middle, margins submembranous; lower lemma oblong-lanceolate, apex acute, upper margins sparsely ciliate; upper lemma reduced to linear, with a geniculate awn arising from the apex; stamens 3. Pedicellate spikelet staminate or barren, subequal to sessile spikelet, glabrous.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. S. C. Ng 2023.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Qinghai, Xinjiang, Ningxia, Nei Mongol, Hebei, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Shandong, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; C and SW Asia, Europe, N Africa, naturalized elsewhere.
Ecology: Grassy hillslopes, roadsides, disturbed places. Flowering & fruiting: Autumn.
Uses: Animal food (forage), environmental (erosion control).

Bothriochloa pertusa (L.) A. Camus 孔穎草
Ann. Soc. Linn. Lyon, N. S. 76: 164. 1931 [“1930”]; H. B. Gill. et al, Fl. Malaya 3: 281. 1971; FRPS 10(2): 145, pl. 35: 1–6, 77: 2. 1997; FYN 9: 666, pl. 110: 9–10. 2003; FOC 22: 608. 2006; FGD 9: 493, fig. 260. 2009.
Holcus pertusus L., Mant. Pl. 2: 301. 1771.

Perennial herb. Culms erect or geniculately ascending, up to 100 cm tall, 5- or more-noded, nodes bearded. Leaf sheaths glabrous, keeled; leaf blades linear, 5–20 × 0.1 – 0.4 cm, tuberclebased hairs on both surfaces or abaxial surface glabrous, apex acute, margins scabrous; ligule 0.5–2 mm, dry membranous. Inflorescence composed of 3–8(–13) racemes, subdigitate; rachis internodes and pedicels ciliate with long silky hairs. Sessile spikelet lanceolate, callus bearded; lower glume papery, a circular pit in the upper 1/3, glabrous sparsely hirtellous to silky-pilose below middle, margins incurved and 2-keeled, scabrous on the keel, 5–7-veined; upper glume boat-shaped, acute; lower lemma oblong, glabrous; upper lemma linear, a geniculate awn arising from the apex, awn 1–2 cm long. Pedicellate spikelet staminate or barren, purplish, subequal to sessile spikelet, glabrous.

Locality: Quarry Bay. HK sheet 15532.
Distribution: Guangdong, Sichuan, Yunnan; Indian Subcontinent, Indochina, Malesia, naturalized elsewhere in tropics. Ecology: Grassy hills, disturbed grounds, alt. 1200–1500 m. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Oct.
Uses: Animal food (forage), environmental (erosion control).

Brachiaria brizantha (Hochst. ex A. Rich) Stapf 柵狀臂形草（信號草）
Fl. trop. Afr. 9: 531. 1919.
Panicum brizanthum Hochst. ex A. Rich., Tent. Fl. Abyss. 2: 363. 1851.

Perennial herb. Culms erect, or geniculately ascending, to 100–200(–300) cm tall. Leaf blades linear, or lanceolate; ligule a fringe of hairs. Inflorescence composed of racemes; racemes (1–)2–16; borne along a central axis; rhachis narrowly winged, margins ciliate. Spikelet single, packing adaxial, 1-rowed. Spikelets elliptic, 4–6 mm, falling entire, dorsally compressed, subacute or acute; glumes dissimilar; lower glume ovate, clasping, 1/3 length of spikelet, membranous, no keels, 7–11-veined, obtuse or acute; upper glume oblong, as long as spikelet, cartilaginous, no keels, 7–9-veined, glabrous or pubescent, obtuse or acute; lower florets staminate, with palea; lower lemma similar to upper glume; upper lemma elliptic, 3.5–5.5 mm.

Locality: Ta Kwu Ling. Y. W. Lam 859; HK sheet 35005.
Distribution: Africa; naturalized elsewhere in tropics.
Ecology: Wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Spring to autumn.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Aberdeen, Sha Tin, Yuen Long, Nam Sang Wai, San Tin, Mai Po, Plover Cove, Tsing Yi
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Brachiaria mutica (Forssk.) Stapf 巴拉草
Fl. Trop. Afr. 9: 526. 1919; FRPS 10(1): 269. 1990; FFJ 6: 218. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 458, pl. 190. 2000; FOC 22: 520. 2006; FGD 9: 423. 2009.
Panicum muticum Forssk., Fl. Aegypt.-Arab. 20. 1775.
Urochloa mutica (Forssk.) T. Q. Nguyen, Novosti Sist. Vysa. Rast. 1966: 13. 1966.

Perennial herb. Culms stout, to 3 m tall, nodes densely villous. Leaf sheaths glabrous or villous at mouth, longer than internode; leaf blades broadly linear, 10–30 × 1–2 cm, thinly pilose or subglabrous; ligule membranous, ca. 1 mm. Inflorescence racemose; racemes 10–20 cm, solitary, paired or grouped; spikelets paired or solitary in upper part of raceme, in untidy rows or sometimes on short secondary branchlets in lower part of raceme. Spikelets green or purplish, elliptic, 2.5–3.5 mm; lower glume triangular, 1/4–1/3 length of spikelet, 1-veined; upper glume as long as spikelet, 5-veined; lower floret staminate, lower lemma 5-veined, rugulose, palea subequal to lemma; upper lemma ca. 3 mm, crustaceous, margins narrowly incurved.

Locality: Aberdeen, Sha Tin, Yuen Long, Nam Sang Wai, San Tin, Mai Po, Plover Cove, Tsing Yi. Y. S. Lau 2533; L. T. Lo 552; HK sheet 39681.
Distribution: Cultivated in Fujian and Taiwan, probably originated from tropical Africa, now widely introduced and naturalized in tropical regions.
Ecology: Streamsides, other wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Nov.
Uses: Animal food (forage).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Aberdeen, Kowloon Peak, To Fung Shan, Plover Cove, Peng Chau
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Brachiaria subquadripara (Trin.) Hitchc. 四生臂形草
Lingnan Sci. J. 7: 214. 1931 [“1929”]; FHN 4: 420. 1977; FRPS 10(1): 266, pl. 80: 1–5. 1990; FFJ 6: 217, fig. 184. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 460. 2000; FOC 22: 522. 2006; FGD 9: 422, fig. 217. 2009.
Panicum subquadriparum Trin., Gram. Panic. 145. 1826.
Urochloa subquadripara (Trin.) R. D. Webster, Austral. Paniceae 252. 1987.

Annual herb. Culms slender, straggling, rooting at lower nodes, 20–60 cm tall, nodes pubescent. Leaf sheaths loose, usually glabrous, rarely with tubercle-based hairs; leaf blades lanceolate or linear-lanceolate, 4–15 × 0.4–1 cm, glabrous or pubescent, base subrounded, apex acute or acuminate, margins thicker and scabrous. Inflorescence axis 3–10 cm; racemes 3–6, 2–4 cm, divergent to reflexed; rachis, narrowly winged, nearly glabrous; spikelets single, in 2 rows; pedicels glabrous. Spikelets elliptic, 3.5–4 mm, glabrous, acute; lower glume broadly ovate, 1/3–1/2 spikelet length, 5–7-veined; upper glume as long as spikelet, 5–7-veined; lower lemma as long as spikelet, 7-veined; upper lemma finely rugose, margins slightly inrolled embraced same texture palea, subacute; stamens 3; style base free.

Locality: Aberdeen, Kowloon Peak, To Fung Shan, Plover Cove, Peng Chau. Y. W. Lam 778, 989, 1610.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; E Asia, Indian Subcontinent, Indochina, Malesia, Australia, widely naturalized in the tropics.
Ecology: Grassy places of hillslopes, open fields and thin forests. Flowering & fruiting: Sep.–Nov.

Capillipedium assimile (Steud.) A. Camus 硬稈子草（竹枝細柄草）
Fl. Indo-Chine. 7: 314. 1922; FFJ 6: 268, fig. 240. 1995; FRPS 10(2): 152, pl. 36: 1–6, 77: 1. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 5: 530. 2000; FOC 22: 606. 2006; FGD 9: 495. 2009.
Andropogon montanus Roxb., Fl. Ind., ed. 1820, 1: 271. 1820; FHK 423. 1861.
Andropogon assimilis Steud., Syn. Pl. Glumac. 1: 397. 1854; FKH 323. 1912.

Perennial herb. Culms hard, 1.5–3.5 m tall, geniculate at base. Leaf sheaths glabrous, bearded at mouth; leaf blades linear-lanceolate, 4–15 × 0.2–0.6 cm, glabrous or hispidulous, base tapering, apex setaceously acuminate, margins scabrous; ligule 0.5–1 mm, dry membranous, truncate or obtuse. Panicle open, branches fascicles; branches pilose in axils; rachis internodes and pedicels long-ciliate, fragile. Sessile spikelet oblong, dorsally compressed, callus bearded; lower glume obtuse, scabrous or hispidulous, 2-keeled, ciliatehispid on keel, 2–5-veined; upper glume as long as lower glume, 3-veined; lower lemma oblong, 2/3 upper lemma length, obtuse; upper lemma linear, an awn of 0.6–1.5 cm long arising from the apex. Pedicellate spikelet staminate, linear-lanceolate, up to twice length of sessile spikelet.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Shing Mun. Y. S. Lau 2283; HK sheet 41992.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Shandong, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Indian Subcontinent, Indochina, Malay Peninsula, Indonesia.
Ecology: Forests, streamsides. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Dec.

Capillipedium parviflorum (R. Br.) Stapf 細柄草（吊絲草）
Fl. Trop. Afr. 9: 169. 1917; FHN 4: 475, fig. 1261. 1977; FFJ 6: 269, fig. 241. 1995; FRPS 10(2): 151, pl. 36: 7–11, 76: 4. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 5: 531, pl. 225. 2000; FOC 22: 606. 2006; FGD 9: 495, fig. 261. 2009.
Holcus parviflorus R. Br., Prodr. 199. 1810.

Perennial herb. Culms tufted, erect or slightly decumbent at base, 30–150 cm tall; nodes shortly bearded. Leaf sheaths shorter or longer than internode, glabrous or pilose, ciliate at mouth; leaf blades linear, 10–30 × 0.2–0.8 cm, glabrous or hispid, base rounded, apex acuminate; ligule dry membranous, 0.5–1.5 mm. Panicle oblong; branches fasciculate, pilose in axils; racemes usually composed of triads, occasionally with 1–2 additional spikelet pairs; rachis internodes and pedicels 1/2 the length of sessile spikelet, shortly ciliate at base. Sessile spikelet bisexual, oblong, 3–4 mm; lower glume shallowly concave between veins, 4-veined, margins keeled, hispidulous above middle keel, apex narrowly obtuse; upper glume boat-shaped, as long as lower glume, slightly scabrous on keel, acute, 3-veined, upper margins ciliate; lower lemma 1/4–1/3 glume length, obtuse or dentate; upper lemma linear, tipped with an awn of 1–1.5 cm. Pedicellate spikelet equal to the sessile spikelet and often staminate, or smaller and barren.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1866; P. S. Choi 107; Y. W. Lam 2171.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Hebei, Henan, Hubei, Anhui, Shandong, Zhejiang, Fujain, Taiwan; tropical and subtropical regions of the Old World.
Ecology: Grassy field on hillslopes, streamsides. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Dec.
Uses: Animal food (forage).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Pok Fu Lam, Tai Hang, Kau Wa Keng, Sha Tin, Tai Po Kau
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Cenchrus echinatus L. 蒺藜草
Sp. Pl. 2: 1050. 1753; FRPS 10(1): 375, pl. 114: 14–22. 1990; FFJ 6: 191. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 462, pl. 192. 2000; FOC 22: 553. 2006; FGD 9: 445, fig. 228. 2009.
Cenchrus calyculatus auct. non Gavan: FHN 4: 440, pl. 1231. 1977.

Annual herb. Culms geniculate, usually rooting at basal nodes, ca. 50 cm tall. Leaf sheaths loose, compressed, keeled, glabrous or upper margins ciliate, overlapping at base; leaf blades linear or linear-lanceolate, 5–20(–40) × 0.4–1 cm, glabrous to pubescent; ligule ca. 1 mm, a ring of hairs. Inflorescence a solitary raceme, 3–10 × ca. 1 cm; axis scabrous; burs globose, 0.4–1 cm, truncate, stipe pubescent, all spines and bristles whorled and retrorsely barbed, inner spines connate for 1/3–1/2 their length forming a globose cupule, dorsally fuzz, margins white ciliate, outer spines in 2 divergent whorls, a median whorl of stout rigid spines equaling the inner teeth, and an outermost whorl of relatively few short, slender bristles. Spikelets 2–4(–6) in bur, elliptic-lanceolate, 2-floret; lower glume triangular-lanceolate, 1/3–1/2 spikelet length, acute, 1-veined; upper glume 2/3 – 3/4 spikelet length, 5-veined; lower floret staminate or neuter, lower lemma as long as spikelet, 5-veined, palea 2/3 length of lower lemma; upper floret bisexual, lemma 5-veined, inrolled embraced same texture palea; lodicules absent; style penicillate. Caryopsis depressed-globose.

Locality: Pok Fu Lam, Tai Hang, Kau Wa Keng, Sha Tin, Tai Po Kau. Y. S. Lau 1560, 1972; Y. W. Lam 5.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; a widespread weed of the tropics and subtropics, native to America.
Ecology: Sandy grasslands near seashores. Flowering & fruiting: Summer.

Centotheca lappacea (L.) Desv. 假淡竹葉
Nouv. Bull. Sci. Soc. Philm. Paris 2: 189. 1810; FKH 329. 1912; FFJ 6: 132, fig. 104. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 332. 2000; FRPS 9(2): 34, pl. 3: 4. 2002; FOC 22: 445. 2006; FGD 9: 384, fig. 192. 2009.
Cenchrus lappaceus L., Sp. Pl., ed. 2, 2: 1488. 1763.

Perennial herb, 40–100 cm tall. Culms loosely tufted, erect, smooth, 4–7-noded, clothed at base with few cataphylls. Leaf blades lanceolate-elliptic, 4–15 × 1–3 cm, base petiole-like, abaxial surface glabrous with cross veins, adaxial surface glabrous or loosely hispidulous, apex long attenuate; ligule 1–1.5 mm, apex rounded; leaf sheaths smooth or ciliate along one margin. Panicle large, open, 12–25 cm, primary branches up to 15 cm; pedicels 2.5–3 mm, slender, pubescent. Spikelets 4–8 mm, florets 2–3; glumes subleathery, elliptic, apex acute, (3–)5-veined; lower glume 2–2.5 mm, upper glume 3–3.5 mm; lowest lemma ca. 4 mm, subleathery, 7-veined, glabrous, apex acute; upper lemmas slightly smaller than the lowest, coarsely setose with tuberclebased, reflexing bristles near upper margins, the hairs retrorsely hispid when mature; paleae ca. 3 mm, firm, 2-keeled, ciliolate along keels, apex acute, hispid on the upper part of keel. Caryopsis ellipsoidal, 1–1.2 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. S. Y. Hu & S. Liu 155; S. Y. Hu 8595 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; Indochina, Indian Subcontinent, Malesia, W tropical Africa, Australia, Pacific islands.
Ecology: Margins of forests, shady roadsides and other moist shady ground. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Oct.
Uses: Animal food (fodder).

Cephalostachyum pergracile Munro 香糯竹
Trans. Linn. Soc. London. 26: 141. 1868; HKB 56. 1985; FRPS 9(1): 29, pl. 6: 1–10. 1996; FOC 22: 55. 2006; FGD 9: 279. 2009.
Schizostachyum pergracile (Munro) R. B. Majumdar, Fl. Ind. Enumerat.-Monocot. 282. 1989.

Culms erect, 9–12 m, 5–7.5 cm in diam., apically drooping; internodes 30–45 cm, initially densely appressed setose; wall thin. Culm sheaths tardily deciduous, brown, shorter than culms, 10–15 × 15–20 cm, thickly leathery, smooth, densely glossy black-brown setose; auricles rounded, undulate, hirsute near margins; ligule inconspicuous; blade reflexed, ovate-acuminate, ca. 5 cm, articulate with sheath, adaxially densely hairy. Leaf sheath margins ciliate; ligule ciliate; blade narrowly lanceolate, 15–35 × 2.5–3.8(–6) cm, base rounded. Inflorescences capitate, at nodes of leafless branch, 1.5–3 cm in diam., subtended by bracts. Pseudospikelet 1.2–2 × ca. 0.2 cm, densely yellow hirtellous, rachilla extended, 5–6 mm. Glumes 2–3, 0.6–1.1 cm; lemma 1.3–1.8 cm, densely hairy, apex long mucronate or awned; palea about as long as or longer than lemma, apex bifid; lodicules lanceolate, narrow, membranous, apex acute. Anthers purple. Stigmas 3. Caryopsis 6–8 × 2–3 mm, glabrous, apex with persistent style base.

Locality: Tai Po Kau (cultivated).
Distribution: S Yunnan; Myanmar, Thailand, Laos, Vietnam.
Ecology: Cultivated. New Shoots: Summer.
Uses: Ornamental.

Chimonobambusa quadrangularis (Franceschi) Makino 方竹（四方竹）
Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 28: 153. 1914; HKB 57. 1985; FRPS 9(1): 340, pl. 93: 1 – 6. 1996; FOC 22: 158. 2006; FGD 9: 314, fig. 148. 2009.
Bambusa quadrangularis Franceschi, Bull. Soc. Tosc. Ortic. 5: 401. 1880.
Arundinaria quadrangularis (Franceschi) Makino, Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 9: 71. 1895.
Phyllostachys quadrangularis (Franceschi) Rendle, J. Linn. Soc. 36: 443. 1904.

Culms erect, 3–8 m tall, to 2.5 cm in diam.; internodes obtusely 4-angled, 8–22 cm, sparsely coarsely scabrid, apically more densely so; nodes prominent, supra-nodal ridge raised at branching nodes, level at branchless nodes, lower nodes each with a ring of short, declined root thorns; sheath scar corky, initially with a fulvous, tomentose, minutely setose ring. Culm sheaths deciduous, shorter than internodes, papery, veins prominent, transverse veinlets purple-brown, margins ciliate; auricles, oral setae, and ligule absent; blade deciduous, subulate, 3–5 mm, articulate. Leaves 2–5 per ultimate branch; sheaths leathery, glabrous, margins apically ciliate; oral setae deciduous, erect, glabrate; ligule truncate, short, ciliate, with minute setae; pseudopetiole ca. 1.8 mm; blade elliptical to lanceolate, 8–29 × 1–2.7 cm, papery, abaxially initially pubescent, adaxially glabrous, secondary veins 4–7-paired, tertiary veins 5–7, apex acuminate. Inflorescence racemose or paniculate, terminal ones slender, glabrous, subtended by persistent, gradually enlarged bracts. Spikelets (1–)2–4, 2–3 cm, slender; florets 2–5, basal absent to 2 rudimentary. Glumes 1–3, lanceolate, 4–5 mm; lemma green, lanceolate or oblong-lanceolate, subequal to palea, papery, 5–7-veined; lodicules narrowly ovate. Anthers 3.5–4 mm. Stigmas 2.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. HK sheet 16457, 16459.
Distribution: Anhui, Fujian, Guangxi, Hunan, Jiangsu, Jiangxi, Taiwan, Zhejiang; Japan, cultivated in Europe and N America.
Ecology: New shoots: Autumn.
Uses: Ornamental.

Chloris barbata Sw. 孟仁草
Fl. Ind. Occid. 1: 200. 1797; FHK 429. 1861; FKH 327. 1912; FRPS 10(1): 75, pl. 23: 5–8. 1990; FFJ 6: 162. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 403. 2000; FOC 22: 490. 2006; FGD 9: 374. 2009.
Andropogon barbatus L., Mant. Pl. Altera 302. 1771, non Linnaeus (1759).
Chloris inflata Link, Enum. Hort. Berol. 1: 105. 1821.

Annual or short-lived perennial herb. Culms ascending from the decumbent base, 0.2–1 m tall, usually rooting at lower nodes. Leaf blades usually folded, 10–40 × 0.3–0.8 cm, glabrous, apex acute; ligule ciliate, ca. 0.3 mm; leaf sheaths keeled, glabrous. Inflorescence of 5–9 digitately arranged spikes; spikes erect or ascending, 3–8 cm, ± flexuous and purplish; rachis scabrous. Spikelets with 3- or 4-flowered, 3(–4)-awned; glumes membranous, conspicuously 1-veined; the lower deltoid-lanceolate, 1.2–1.5 mm, apex acute; the upper narrowly lanceolate, 1.7–2.5 mm, apex shortly mucronate; lower floret fertile, lemmas elliptic in side view, 1.7–2.5 mm, pilose on keel, ciliate on upper margins with 1–1.5 mm hairs, awn 4.5–7 mm; palea ca. 2.2 mm; upper florets sterile, lemmas empty, inflated, overlapping to form a knob at side of fertile floret; second lemma turbinate, truncate, 1–1.5 mm, glabrous or sparsely appressed-pilose on back, awn 2.5–7 mm. Stamens 3, anthers ca. 0.5 mm. Caryopsis ca. 1.6 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. W. Lam 851, 882; HK sheet 42064.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian, Taiwan; widely spread over tropical to warm-temperate regions of the world.
Ecology: Beaches, wastelands, roadsides. Flowering & fruiting: Mar.–Aug.

Chloris formosana (Honda) Keng 台灣虎尾草
FHN 4: 385, fig. 1193. 1977; FTW ed. 2, 5: 403. 2000; FGD 9: 375. 2009;
Chloris barbata Sw. var. formosana Honda, Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 40: 437. 1926.

Annual herb. Culms erect from the decumbent base, 20–70 cm tall, usually rooting at lower nodes. Leaf blades usually folded, 4–40 × 0.2–0.3 cm, glabrous, sometimes scabrous on adaxial surface and margins; ligule 0.5–1 mm, ciliate; leaf sheaths laterally compressed, keeled, glabrous, apex acute. Inflorescence of 4–9 digitately arranged spikes; spikes 3–8 cm, erect or somewhat lax, pallid or purplish; rachis puberulous. Spikelets 3-flowered, 3-awned, ca. 2.5 mm (excluding the awn), sessile; glumes membranous, 1-veined; lower glume 1–2 mm, lanceolate, apex acute; upper glume 2–3 mm, with a sinus at the apex, midrib prolong into an awn; lemma of fertile floret ovate, 2.3–3 mm, with a lateral groove, glabrous on keel, densely ciliate on upper margins with ca. 1 mm hairs; awn (2–)4–6 mm; palea as long as the lemma, rounded at the apex, 2-keeled; upper florets sterile, lemmas empty, flattened or only slightly inflated, overlapping to form a knob at side of fertile floret; second lemma oblanceolate, truncate, 1.6–2 mm, glabrous, awn 2.5–5 mm. Caryopsis ca. 1.6 mm, ellipsoidal.

Locality: Sai Kung, Tai Po Kau. HK sheet 34207, 34660, 41957.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Sandy or gravelly soils near seashore. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Dec.

Chloris virgata Sw. 虎尾草
Fl. Ind. Occid. 1: 203. 1797; FKH 327. 1912; FTW 5: 464. 1978; FRPS 10(1): 79. pl. 22: 1–4. 1990; FOC 22: 489. 2006; FGD 9: 374. 2009.
Chloris caudata Trin. ex Bunge, Enum. Pl. Chin. Bor. 70. 1833.

Annual. Culms erect or geniculately ascending, 12–75 cm tall. Basal leaf sheaths keeled, glabrous; leaf blades linear, flat or folded, 5–30 cm, 2–7 mm wide; ligule 0.5–1 mm. Racemes digitate, 5–12, erect or slightly slanting, 2–10 cm; rachis scabrous or hispid. Spikelets with 2 or 3 florets, 2-awned; lower glume 1.8–2.2 mm; upper glume 3–4 mm, acuminate; lemma of fertile floret obovatelanceolate in side view, 2.8–3.5 mm, keel gibbous, conspicuously bearded on upper margins with a spreading tuft of 2.5–3.5 mm silky hairs, margins, keel and flanks silky-ciliate or glabrous; awn 5–15 mm; second floret sterile, oblong, glabrous, awn 4–10 mm; third floret occasionally present, reduced to a small clavate scale, awnless.

Locality: High Island Reservoir. HK Sheet 34207.
Distribution: Common in China; Afghanistan, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Pakistan; Africa, America, SW Asia, Australia, Pacific islands.
Ecology: Common on stony slopes, steppes, sandy riversides, roadsides, fields, plantations, frequent on walls and roofs, alt. 3700 m. Flowering and fruiting: Jun.–Oct.

Chrysopogon aciculatus (Retz.) Trin. 竹節草
Fund. Agrost. 188. 1820; FHK 424. 1861; FKH 324. 1912; FHN 4: 472, fig. 1259. 1977; FFJ 6: 265, fig. 236. 1995; FRPS 10(2): 135, pl. 32: 1–7. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 5: 534, pl. 226. 2000; FOC 22: 604. 2006; FGD 9: 491, fig. 259. 2009.
Andropogon aciculatus Retz., Observ. Bot. 5: 22. 1789.

Perennial rhizomatous and stoloniferous herb. Culms erect or prostrate at the base, 20–50 cm tall. Leaf sheaths glabrous or ciliate at mouth; leaf blades linear-lanceolate, 2–5 × 0.3–0.5 cm, glabrous or adaxial surface pilose near base, apex obtuse, margins serrate; ligule short, 0.1–0.3 mm. Panicle terminal, purplish brown, oblong or linear-oblong; branches erect when dry, slender, usually whorled, each bearing one sessile and perfect, two pedicellate and sterile spikelet. Sessile spikelet cylindrical-lanceolate; callus acicular, 4–6 mm, bearded with golden hairs, obliquely attached to branch apex; glumes leathery; lower glume lanceolate, 2-keeled upward, keels hispidulous, apex acute to 2-toothed; upper glume boat-shaped, setulose on back and upper keel, acuminate or mucronate, mucro 1–2 mm; lower lemma linear-oblong, slightly shorter than glume; upper lemma entire, awned; awn straight, 4–7 mm. Pedicellate spikelet staminate, 3/4 length of sessile spikelet.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1854; S. P. Lau 4; HK sheet 40715.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; Indian Subcontinent, Indochina, Malay Peninsula, Indonesia, Philippines, Pacific islands, Australia.
Ecology: Open grassy fields, wastelands. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Oct.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Authority: (Wight & Arn. ex Steud.) Munro ex Benth.
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Coelachne simpliciuscula (Wight & Arn. ex Steud.) Munro ex Benth. 小麗草
J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 19: 93. 1881; FFJ 6: 165, fig. 135. 1995; FOC 22: 560. 2006; FGD 9: 367, fig. 179. 2009.
Panicum simpliciusculum Wight & Arn. ex Steud., Syn. Pl. Glumac. 1: 96. 1854.
Coelachne pulchella auct. non R. Br.: FHK 428. 1861; FKH 326. 1912.

Annual herb, 10–20 cm tall. Culms slender, ascending from the decumbent base, rooting at lower nodes. Leaf blades soft, lanceolate, 1–3 × 0.2–0.5 cm, glabrous or hirtellous along veins; ligule a line of short hairs; leaf sheaths loose, glabrous or upper margins ciliolate. Panicle linear, loosely spiciform, 3–8 × 0.5–1 cm. Spikelets green or often purplish, 2–3 mm, borne on short erect branches; rachilla internode 0.6–0.8 mm; glumes broadly ovate, herbaceous with membranous margins, lower glume 0.9–1.2 mm, 1–3(–5)-veined, upper glume ca. 1.5 mm, 5–7-veined; lemmas lanceolate, lower lemma 2–2.3 mm, glabrous or puberulous, lower palea equal to lemma; upper lemma 1.6–1.7 mm, pubescent below middle on centre back and margins. Anthers 2–3, ca. 0.3 mm. Caryopsis brown at maturity, ca. 1.2 mm.

Locality: Hong Kong Wai. C. Wilford 253 (K).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan; Vietnam, Cambodia, Myanmar, Thailand, Sri Lanka, India, Nepal.
Ecology: Marshy places and streamsides. Flowering & fruiting: Sep.–Dec.

Coix lacryma-jobi L. 薏苡
Sp. Pl. 2: 972. 1753; FKH 317. 1912; FRPS 10(2): 293, pl. 73: 1–2. 1997; FFJ 6: 277, fig. 252. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 536. 2000; FOC 22: 648. 2006; FGD 9: 510, fig. 272. 2009.

Annual herb. Culms erect, robust, 1–2 m tall, glabrous, branched. Leaf sheaths shorter than internode, glabrous; leaf blades linearlanceolate, flat and open, 10–40 × 1.5–7 cm, usually glabrous, midvein stout, base subrounded or cordate, apex acuminate or long acuminate, margins scabrous; ligule ca.1 mm, dry membranous, ciliate. Male raceme 1–5 cm, spikelets in pairs with terminal triad. Male spikelets oblong-ovate; glumes many-veined, lower glume winged on keels, wing margin ciliolate; anthers 4–5 mm. Female spikelet usually 3, one fertile, and 2 sterile at base; lower glume acuminate and beak-like; stamen usually absent; style thin and long, exserted apically from apex of involucre. Caryopsis ovoid or subglobose, ca. 5–8 mm in diam.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 912, 1018, 2299.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; Indian Subcontinent, Indochina, Malesia, widely naturalized in tropics, cultivated in paleotropics.
Ecology: Wet places by streams, ditches and open fields, often cultivated. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Dec.
Uses: Food (beverage base), medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Mount Parker, Cape D'Aguilar, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Cymbopogon goeringii (Steud.) A. Camus 橘草
Rev. Bot. Appl. Agric. Colon. 1: 286. 1921; FRPS 10(2): 204, pl. 51: 8–14. 1997; FYN 9: 686, pl. 112: 14–17. 2003; FOC 22: 629. 2006; FGD 9: 499. 2009.
Andropogon goeringii Steud., Flora 29: 22. 1846.

Perennial herb. Culms erect, tufted, 50–110 cm tall. Leaf sheaths glabrous, the upper shorter than internode; leaf blades linear, 15–40 × 0.3–0.5 cm, glabrous, margins scabrous, apex finely acuminate; ligule 0.5–4.5 mm, obtuse and rounded. Spathate compound panicle narrow, loose, 15–35 cm, 1–2 tiers of branching; spatheoles 1.5–2 cm, purple; racemes often purplish, paired; rachis internodes and pedicels apex cupular, margins ciliate. Sessile spikelet oblong-lanceolate, 4.5– 6 mm, callus ca. 0.5 mm, pubescent and subglabrous; lower glume flat or slightly concave toward base, sharply 2-keeled throughout; keels winged above middle; upper glume boat-shaped, margins narrow membranous and ciliate, narrow wing on the keel, acute; lower lemma about 3/4 length of glume, narrow and acuminate, 2-keeled, ciliate; upper lemma very narrow, ca. 3 mm, with a geniculate awn from sinus; upper lemma 2-lobed; awn 1–2 cm; palea absent; style brown, penicillate, exerted laterally. Pedicellate spikelet 4–6 mm, pedicel white long pilose.

Locality: Mount Parker, Cape D'Aguilar, Lantau Island. HK sheet 38089, 41940, 42036.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou, Hunan, Hubei, Henan, Hebei, Shandong, Anhui, Jiangxi, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, S Korea.
Ecology: Open grassy fields, hillslopes, roadsides. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Oct.

Cymbopogon martini (Roxb.) W. Watson 魯沙香茅
Himalayan Districts N.W. Prov. India. 392. 1882; FRPS 10(2): 192. 1997 [“martinii”]; FOC 22: 626. 2006.
Andropogon martini Roxb., Fl. Ind. 1: 280. 1820; FHK 424. 1861.
Cymbopogon schoenanthus Spreng., Pl. Min. Cogn. Pug. 2: 15. 1815; FKH 323. 1912.

Perennial herb, with a short woody rootstock. Culms tufted, up to 3 m tall, lower nodes often swollen, mealy. Leaf sheaths glabrous; leaf blades usually glaucous at abaxial surface, dark green at adaxial surface, lanceolate, up to 50 × 2–3 cm, glabrous, base cordate, often amplexicaul, apex filiform; ligule 2–4 mm. Spathate panicle narrow, dense, erect, 20–30 cm; spatheoles green becoming reddish, 2–4 cm; racemes 1.5–2 cm; rachis internodes and pedicels ciliate on margins; pedicel of homogamous pair swollen, barrel-shaped, shiny, fused to internode at base. Sessile spikelet oblong, 3.5–4.5 mm; lower glume deeply grooved below middle, appearing as a line or keel on inside; keels winged above middle, veinless or 2-veined between keels; upper lemma 2-lobed; awn 1.4–1.8 cm. Pedicellate spikelet 3.5–4 mm.

Locality: Cultivated. S. L. Thrower s.n. (CUHK).
Distribution: Sichuan, Yunnan; Indian Subcontinent, widely cultivated in tropical Asia.
Ecology: Grassy hillslopes. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Oct.
Uses: Material (essential oil).

Cymbopogon mekongensis A. Camus 青香茅
Bull. Mus. Natl. Hist. Nat. 26: 563. 1920; FOC 22: 626. 2006.
Cymbopogon caesius auct. non Stapf: FHN 4: 480. 1977; FRPS 10(2): 196, pl. 46: 8–14. 1997; FGD 9: 498. 2009; Check List HK Plants 329. 2002; 116. 2004.

Perennial herb. Culms erect or geniculate, tufted, 30–80 cm tall. Leaf sheaths glabrous, the upper shorter than internodes; leaf blades linear, glabrous, 10–25 × 0.2–0.6 cm, apex filiform; ligule 0.7–3 mm. Spathate compound panicle narrow, 10–30 cm, spathes densely clustered, racemes paired; rachis internodes and pedicels ca. 1.5 mm. Sessile spikelet oblanceolate; lower glume ovatelanceolate, deeply grooved below middle; keels broadly winged above middle, veinless or obscurely 2-veined between keels; upper glume boat-shaped, narrow wing on the keel, margins membranous and ciliate, acute; upper lemma deeply 2-lobed; awn 1–1.5 cm, from the sinus, geniculate; stamens 3. Pedicellate spikelet 3–4 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. W. J. Tutcher 5126; S. P. Lau 133; HK sheet 15738.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Zhejiang; Laos, Thailand, Vietnam.
Ecology: Roadsides, hillslopes. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Sep.

Cymbopogon nardus (L.) Rendle 亞香茅
Cat. Afr. Pl. 2: 155. 1899; FKH 323. 1912; H. B. Gill. et al., Fl. Malaya 3: 296. 1971; FHN 4: 479, fig. 1265. 1977; FFJ 6: 276. 1995; FRPS 10(2): 199. 1997; FOC 22: 628. 2006; FGD 9: 499. 2009.
Andropogon nardus L., Sp. Pl. 2: 1046. 1753.

Perennial herb. Culms densely tufted. Leaf sheaths reddish purple at base, smooth, glabrous, the upper shorter than internode, most crowded at base of culm; leaf blades dark green or dark brown when dry, linear, flat, 30–50 × 0.5–2 cm, glabrous, adaxial surface smooth, abaxial surface scabrid, base narrow, apex attenuate to needle, margins scabrous; ligule 2–3 mm, membranous, glabrous. Spathate panicle large, narrow, congested, 60–90 cm; spatheoles reddish brown, 1–2.5 cm; racemes 1–2 cm; rachis internodes and pedicels ciliate on margins, back glabrous or pubescent. Sessile spikelet oblong-lanceolate; lower glume reddish brown or purplish upward, papery, flat or slightly concave, sharply 2-keeled; keels narrowly winged, veinless or obscurely veined between keels; upper glume boat-shaped, membranous, ciliate; lower lemma oblong, ciliate, veinless; upper lemma linear, entire or slightly 2-lobed, mucronate or very shortly awned; stamens 3. Pedicellate spikelet staminate or seldom neuter, 3.5–7 mm.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 31542, 33469.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan (cultivated); Indian Subcontinent, widely cultivated in tropical Asia.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Nov.–Apr. of the following year.
Uses: Additive (flavoring), material (essential oil).

Cymbopogon tortilis (J. Presl) A. Camus 扭鞘香茅
Rev. Bot. Appl. Agric. Colon. 5: 206. 1925; FHN 4: 481. 1977; FFJ 6: 275, fig. 249. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 536. 2000; FOC 22: 628. 2006.
Anthistiria tortilis J. Presl in C. Presl, Reliq. Haenk. 1: 347. 1830.
Cymbopogon hamatulus (Hook. & Arn.) A. Camus, Bot. Beechey Voy. 244. 1838; FRPS 10(2): 207, pl. 51: 1–7. 1997; FGD 9: 500. 2009.

Perennial herb. Culms tufted, slender, 50–150 cm tall, glabrous. Leaf sheaths glabrous, shorter than internode; leaf blades linear, flat, glabrous or tomentose near the base of adaxial surface, 25–60 × 0.2–0.7 cm, base gradually narrowed, apex finely acuminate; ligule 2–3 mm, dry membranous. Spathate compound panicle narrow, 20–35 cm, 2–3 tiers of branching; spatheoles reddish brown, 1.2–1.5 cm; racemes 1–1.5 cm, paired; rachis internodes and pedicels obliquely cupular, margins ciliate. Sessile spikelet oblonglanceolate, 3.5–4.5 mm, callus very short; lower glume flat, sharply 2-keeled throughout; keels narrowly winged above middle, 2–5-veined between keels; upper glume boat-shaped, narrow wing on the keel, acute; lower lemma oblong-lanceolate, 2-keeled, ciliate; upper lemma very narrow, 2-lobed; awn 0.7–1 cm; palea absent. Pedicellate spikelet 3–3.5 mm, awnless.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. S. P. Lau 53; Y. S. Lau 2534; Y. W. Lam 6.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guizhou, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Philippines, Vietnam.
Ecology: Open grassy fields, hillslopes, roadsides. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Oct.
Notes: The species was reported as Cymbopogon hamatulus (Nees ex Hook. & Arn.) A. Camus previously (Check List HK Plants 330. 2002; 116. 2004).

Cynodon dactylon (L.) Pers. 狗牙根
Syn. Pl. 1: 85. 1805; FHK 428. 1861; FKH 326. 1912; FHN 4: 387, fig. 1195. 1977; FRPS 10(1): 84, pl. 25: 1–6. 1990; FFJ 6: 163, fig. 133. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 406. 2000; FOC 22: 493. 2006; FGD 9: 376, fig. 185. 2009.
Panicum dactylon L., Sp. Pl. 1: 85. 1753.

Perennial herb, stoloniferous. Culms slender, erect or ascending from the creeping stolons, 10–40 cm tall. Leaf blades linear, 1–12 × 0.1–0.4 cm, usually glabrous, scaberulous, apex subacute; auricles and orifices bearded; ligule a short ciliolate rim; leaf sheaths bearded at mouth, otherwise glabrous or thinly pilose. Spikes (2–)3–6, digitately arranged, 2–7 cm, spreading. Spikelets usually 1-flowered, sessile, imbricate in 2 rows on one side of axis, 2–2.7(–3) mm, purplish or green, breaking up above the glumes at maturity; glumes linear-lanceolate, membranous, often purplish, equal or slightly unequal, 1.5–2 mm, 1-veined, keel scabrous, thickened; lemma as long as spikelet, silky villous along keel, hairs straight, otherwise glabrous or lateral veins thinly villous, apex subacute; palea glabrous, keels scaberulous. Anthers 3, more than 1 mm. Caryopsis subterete, tightly enclosed between the hardened lemma and palea, usually turgid or scarcely laterally compressed.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. S. P. Lau 15; Y. S. Lau 2251; HK sheet 39699.
Distribution: Widely distributed in regions S of Huanghe; tropical and warm-temperate regions of the world.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides, margins of fields. Flowering & fruiting: May–Oct.
Uses: Environmental (erosion control, ornamental), animal food (fodder, forage).

Cyrtococcum patens (L.) A. Camus 弓果黍
Bull. Mus. Natl. Hist. Nat. 27: 118. 1921; FHN 4: 412. 1977; FRPS 10(1): 195, pl. 59: 10. 1990; FFJ 6: 200, fig. 167. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 465. 2000; FOC 22: 514. 2006; FGD 9: 409. 2009.
Panicum patens L., Sp. Pl. 1: 18. 1753; FKH 315. 1912.

Annual herb. Culms slender, smooth and glabrous, basal nodes branching and rooting, 15–30 cm tall. Leaf sheaths usually shorter than internode, glabrous or loosely pilose with tubercle-based hairs; leaf blades linear-lanceolate or lanceolate, 3–8 × 0.3–1 cm, pubescent on both surfaces or subglabrous, basal margins with a few long, stiff, tubercle-based hairs, apex acuminate; ligule membranous, 0.5–1 mm, rounded. Panicle 5–15 cm, often diffuse, branches loosely ascending to widely spreading, very slender, glabrous; pedicels filiform, longer than spikelets. Spikelets purplish at maturity, 1–2 mm, varying from glabrous to appressed-pubescent or shortly hispid with stiff, conspicuously tubercle-based hairs; glumes 3-veined, the lower ovate, ca. 1/2 length of spikelet, the upper boat-shaped, 2/3 length of spikelet; lower lemma subequal to spikelet, 5-veined, margins ciliate, obtuse; upper lemma ca. 1.5 mm, gibbous convex, with a scar at apex; upper palea oblong, included in upper lemma.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. W. Lam 1627; HK sheet 42007.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; widely spread over tropical Asia and Pacific islands (Polynesia).
Ecology: Moist places in forests and grasslands. Flowering & fruiting: Sep.–Feb. of the following year.

Cyrtococcum patens (L.) A. Camus var. latifolium (Honda) Ohwi 散穗弓果黍
Acta Phytotax. Geobot. 11: 47. 1942; FRPS 10(1): 196, pl. 59: 9. 1990; FOC 22: 514. 2006; FGD 9: 410. 2009.
Panicum patens f. latifolium Honda, Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 37: 25. 1923.
Cyrtococcum accrescens (Trin.) Stapf, Hooker's Icon. Pl. 31(4): 2, t. 3096. 1922; FHN 4: 412. 1977; FTW ed. 2, 5: 462, pl. 193. 2000; Check List HK Plants 330. 2002; 116. 2004.

It differs from var. patens by its culms up to 60 cm tall, leaf blades 7–15 × 1.2–2 cm; ligule 1–2 mm, panicle larger, 16–30 cm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1030, 1664; P. S. Choi 281.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Hunan, Taiwan; India, Japan (Ryukyu Islands), Malay Peninsula, Thailand, Vietnam.
Ecology: Moist places in forests. Flowering & fruiting: Autumn to winter.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Aberdeen, Repulse Bay, Wong Chuk Hang, Tai Mo Shan, Fanling, Tai A Chau
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Dactyloctenium aegyptium (L.) Willd. 龍爪茅
Enum. Pl. 2: 1029. 1809; FHK 429. 1861; FKH 327. 1912; FHN 4: 384. 1977; FRPS 10(1): 66, pl. 19. 1990; FFJ 6: 144, fig. 118. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 410. 2000; FOC 22: 481. 2006; FGD 9: 358, fig. 171. 2009.
Cynosurus aegyptius L., Sp. Pl. 1: 72. 1753.

Annual herb. Culms erect or ascending from the decumbent base, 15–70 cm tall. Leaf blades flat, 3–25 × 0.2–0.7 cm, tuberculatepilose on both surfaces, especially along the margins, apex acute or acuminate; ligule membranous, 1–2 mm, margin ciliate; leaf sheaths with ciliate margin. Inflorescence of 2–7(–9) stout digitate spikes. Spikelets broadly ovate, 3–4.5 mm, 3–4-flowered; glumes subequal, 1.5–2.2 mm; lower glume narrowly lanceolate, keel thick, hispidulous; upper glume elliptic to narrowly obovate, keel smooth, extended into a stout scabrid awn 1/2–2 times length of glume body; lemmas ovate, 2.6–4 mm, keel gibbous, hispidulous above middle, often extended into a stout cusp or mucro up to 1 mm; palea equal to lemma, tip 2-toothed. Anthers 3, 0.25–0.8 mm. Grain ca. 1 mm, broadly obtriangular, transversely rugose.

Locality: Aberdeen, Repulse Bay, Wong Chuk Hang, Tai Mo Shan, Fanling, Tai A Chau. HK sheet 39143, 41735, 42000.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; tropical and subtropical regions throughout the world.
Ecology: Open grassy fields, wastelands, roadsides and other weedy places. Flowering & fruiting: May–Oct.
Notes: The species was reported as Dactyloctenium aegyptium (L.) P. Beauv. previously (Check List HK Plants 330. 2002; 116. 2004).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Authority: (Schult. & Schult. f.) Backer ex K. Heyne
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Dendrocalamus asper (Schult. & Schult. f.) Backer ex K. Heyne 馬來甜龍竹
Nutt. Pl. Ned.-Ind., ed. 2. 1: 301. 1927; HKB 58. 1985; FRPS 9(1): 193, pl. 49: 1–2. 1996; FOC 22: 43. 2006; FGD 9: 270. 2009.
Bambusa aspera Schult. & Schult. f., Syst. Veg. 7: 1352. 1830.
Dendrocalamus flagellifer Munro, Trans. Linn. Soc. London 26(1): 150. 1868.

Culms 15–20 m, 6–10(–12) cm in diam.; internodes 30–50 cm. Branches from ca. 9th node up, central branch dominant. Culm sheaths deciduous, initially light green, leathery, apex rounded; ligule 7–10 mm, margin with brown setae; auricles linear, ca. 20 × 7 mm, margin undulate; oral setae present; blade reflexed, lanceolate. Leaf sheaths initially sparsely hairy, becoming glabrous; ligule truncate, ca. 2 mm, entire or serrulate; blade variable, lanceolate or oblong-lanceolate, (10–)20–30(–35) × (1.5–)3 – 5 cm. Spikelets 6–9 mm; florets 4–5, apical one sterile. Glumes 1–2, ovate-lanceolate; lemma broadly ovate, margins ciliate; palea about as long as lemma, keels and margins ciliate, 1–3-veined between and 2-veined on either side of keels. Anthers 3–5 mm, apex apiculate. Ovary hairy; style hairy; stigma 1. Fruit unknown.

Locality: Sha Tin, Castle Peak (cultivated). Nan-Zhu 2804.
Distribution: Taiwan, Yunnan; Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, Philippines, Thailand.
Ecology: New shoots: Summer.
Uses: Vegetable.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Sha Tin, Tai Po, Sheung Shui, Lantau Island (cultivated)
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Dendrocalamus latiflorus Munro 麻竹
Trans. Linn. Soc. London. 26: 152. 1868; FKH 331. 1912; HKB 59. 1985; FRPS 9(1): 162. 1996; FOC 22: 45. 2006; FGD 9: 270. 2009.
Bambusa latiflora (Munro) Kurz, J. Asiat. Soc. Bengal, Pt. 2. Nat. Hist. 42(2): 250. 1873.
Sinocalamus latiflorus (Munro) McClure, Lingnan Univ. Sci. Bull. 9: 67. 1940.
Bambusa verticillata auct. non Willd.: FHK 434. 1861.

Culms 20–25 m, 15–30 cm in diam.; internodes 45–60 cm; wall 1–3 cm thick. Branches several, central branch dominant. Culm sheaths deciduous, thickly leathery; auricles small; ligule 1–3 mm, serrulate; blade reflexed, ovate to lanceolate. Leaf sheaths initially slightly hairy, becoming glabrous; ligule 1–2 mm, serrulate; blade oblong-lanceolate, 15–35(–50) × 2.5–7 cm. Pseudospikelets 1–7 or more per node. Spikelets 12–15 × 7–13 mm; florets 6–8. Glumes 2 or more, ca. 5 mm, margins ciliate; lemma 12–13 × 7–16 mm; palea 7–11 × 3–4 mm. Anthers yellow, 5–6 mm, apex mucronate. Ovary broadly ovoid; style white hairy; stigma 1. Caryopsis 8–12 mm.

Locality: Sha Tin, Tai Po, Sheung Shui, Lantau Island (cultivated). H. C. Tang 1095, 1115; Y. S. Lau 3046.
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hainan, Sichuan, Taiwan, Yunnan, cultivated in SW Jiangsu and S Zhejiang; Myanmar, Vietnam.
Ecology: New shoots: Summer.
Uses: Edible (shoot).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Authority: (McClure) L. C. Chia & H. L. Fung

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Dendrocalamus pulverulentus L. C. Chia & But 粉麻竹
Kew Bull. 43: 115. 1988; HKB 60. 1985; FRPS 9(1): 177, pl. 44: 1–2. 1996; FOC 22: 42. 2006; FGD 9: 272. 2009.

Culms to 8 m, 4–6 cm in diam.; internodes 25–30 cm; wall thick. Branches usually from ca. 10th node upward, several, dominant branches longer and thicker. Culm sheaths deciduous, abaxially appressed brown setose; auricles small or absent; ligule ca. 4 mm, margin hairy, apex arched; blade reflexed, lanceolate. Leaf sheaths glabrous; ligule ca. 1 mm, serrulate; blade lanceolate to oblong-lanceolate, 13–20 × 2.5–3.3 cm. Inflorescence unknown.

Locality: Tai Po Kau and gardens (cultivated). HK sheet 34844.
Distribution: Guangdong.
Ecology: New shoots: Summer.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: The type specimen (Nan-Zhu 2780, IBSC) was collected from Tai Po Kau Nature Reserve in 1985.

(Q. H. Dai & C. F. Huang) N. H. Xia & R. S. Lin

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Dichanthium annulatum (Forssk.) Stapf 雙花草
Fl. Trop. Afr. 9: 178. 1917; FHN 4: 477, fig. 1263. 1977; FRPS 10(2): 139, pl. 33: 1–10. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 5: 537. 2000; FYN 9: 657, fig. 109: 7 – 9. 2003; FOC 22: 605. 2006; FGD 9: 496, fig. 262. 2009.
Andropogon annulatus Forssk., Fl. Aegypt.-Arab. 173. 1775; FKH 323. 1912.

Perennial herb. Culms tufted, erect, 30 – 100 cm tall, nodes densely bearded. Leaf sheaths terete, shorter than internode except the base; leaf blades narrowly linear, 8–30 × 0.2–0.4 cm, adaxial surface covered with tubercle-based silky hairs, abaxial surface usually glabrous, base rounded, apex acuminate, margins scabrous; ligule 1–2 mm, dry membranous, ciliate. Inflorescence terminal; peduncle glabrous; racemes 2–8, subdigitate, with 0 – 6 pairs of homogamous spikelets; rachis internode and pedicel 1/2 length of sessile spikelet, margins long ciliate. Sessile spikelet bisexual, ovate-oblong or elliptic-oblong or oblong, 3–5 mm; lower glume dorsally flat, shallowly concave in the middle, apex membranous and obtuse, margins inrolled or keeled, keels shortly ciliate; upper glume boat-shaped, as long as lower glume, ciliate along keel and margins; lower lemma linear-oblong, hyaline membranous, veinless; upper lemma narrow, tipped with a long flexuose awn arising from the apex; awn 1.5–2.5 cm. Caryopsis obovate-oblong. Pedicellate spikelet as long as sessile spikelet, staminate or neuter.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Kowloon. Y. S. Lau 2591; L. T. Lo 588; HK sheet 41927.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hubei, Taiwan; Indian Subcontinent, Malay Peninsula, Indonesia, Philippines, Pacific islands, Africa.
Ecology: Hillslopes, disturbed places. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Nov.

Digitaria ciliaris (Retz.) Koeler 纖毛馬唐（升馬唐）
Descr. Gram. 27. 1802; H. B. Gill. et al., Fl. Malaya 3: 196, fig. 40. 1971; FRPS 10(1): 326, pl. 102: 1–3. 1990; FFJ 6: 234, fig. 201. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 466. 2000; FOC 22: 543. 2006; FGD 9: 438. 2009.
Panicum ciliare Retz., Observ. Bot. 4: 16. 1786.

Annual herb. Culms ascending from decumbent base, branching and rooting at lower nodes, 20–100 cm tall. Leaf sheaths usually shorter than internode, ± tubercle-based pilose; leaf blades linear to lanceolate, 3–25 × 0.2–1 2 cm, adaxial surface usually pilose, margins thickened and scabrous; ligule membranous, 1–3 mm. Inflorescence digitate or subdigitate, axis short; racemes 3–12, 5–17 cm; spikelets paired; rachis winged, ca. 1 mm wide, margins scabrous (serrate). Spikelets lanceolate, 2.5–3.5 mm, suppressed on one side of rachis; pedicels unequal, triangular, serrate; lower glume very small, triangular; upper glume lanceolate, 1/2–4/5 length of spikelet, narrow, margins ciliate, 3-veined; lower lemma as long as spikelet, 7-veined, veins evenly spaced or a broader glabrous interspace flanking the midvein, lateral interveins appressed pubescent to ciliate or villous; upper lemma elliptic, as long as spikelet, coriaceous, apex acuminate.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1693, 2252; Y. W. Lam 1064.
Distribution: Widely spread over almost all provinces of China; and throughout the tropics and subtropics, but rare in Africa.
Ecology: Roadsides, weedy places. Flowering & fruiting: May–Oct.

Digitaria cruciata (Nees ex Steudel) A. Camus 十字馬唐
Lecomte, Fl. Indo-Chine. 7: 399. 1922; FRPS 10(1): 329. 1990; FYN 9: 553. 2003; FOC 22: 543. 2006.
Panicum cruciatum Nees ex Steudel, Syn. Pl. Glum. 1: 39. 1853.

Annual herb. Culms decumbent at base, branching and rooting at lower nodes, 30–100 cm tall, nodes thinly hispid. Leaf sheaths glabrous or hispid, usually shorter than internode; leaf blades linear-lanceolate, 5–20 × 0.3–1 cm, papillose-hispid on both surfaces or adaxial surface glabrous, margins thickened, undulate, scabrous; ligule 1–2.5 mm. Inflorescence subdigitate, axis 1–5 cm; racemes 5–8, 3–15 cm; spikelets paired, imbricate; rachis winged, ca. 1 mm broad, midrib triquetrous, margins slightly scabrous. Spikelets plumply elliptic-oblong, 2.5–3 mm, ca. 1.2 mm broad; lower glume minute, veinless; upper glume broadly ovate, 1/3 as long as spikelet, 3-veined, subglabrous, margins membranous, apex broadly obtuse; lower lemma slightly shorter than upper lemma, 7-veined with intervein spaces nearly equidistant, glabrous or margins pilose; upper lemma pale purplish grey at maturity, apex abruptly apiculate, exserted from spikelet.

Locality: Hong Kong Island. Y. S. Lau 627.
Distribution: Hubei, Sichuan, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang; India, Sikkim, Nepal.
Ecology: Grassy hillslopes. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Oct.

Digitaria fibrosa (Hack.) Stapf 纖維馬唐
Bull. Misc. Inform. Kew. 1912: 428. 1912; FRPS 10(1): 312. 1990; FFJ 6: 230, fig. 196. 1995; FOC 22: 541. 2006; FGD 9: 434. 2009.
