Panicum fibrosum Hack., Oesterr. Bot. Z. 51: 330. 1901
Digitaria setifolia auct. non Stapf: FKH 314. 1912.

Perennial herb. Culms erect, tufted, 20–50 cm tall, girthed at base by fibrous remains of old leaf sheaths. Leaf sheaths pilose at lower part and mouth; leaf blades linear, flat or involute, 3  0 × 0.25–0.4 cm, pilose or subglabrous, apex acuminate, terminal blade short and small; ligule ca. 0.5 mm, membranous, truncate. Inflorescence subdigitate, axis usually glabrous; racemes 2–5, alternating; spikelets paired or ternate or solitary in the upper, loosely arranged; rachis slenderly triquetrous, smooth, glabrous, not winged; pedicels tips slightly swollen. Spikelets oblong-lanceolate, 3–3.5 mm; lower glume very small, subrounded or broad triangular; upper glume ca. 4/5 length of spikelet but narrow, pallid yellow-brown, 3-veined, pilose between veins and margins; lower lemma as long as spikelet, 7-veined, hairiness variable, usually glabrous on either side of midvein, 2nd intervein space and margins usually pilose, acuminate; upper lemma slightly shorter than or equal to spikelets.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. HK sheet 20646.
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan; Laos, Myanmar, Thailand.
Ecology: Hillslopes, roadsides. Flowering & fruiting: May–Aug.

Digitaria henryi Rendle 亨利馬唐
J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 36: 323. 1904; FRPS 10(1): 325. 1990; FFJ 6: 233. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 467, pl. 194. 2000; FOC 22: 543. 2006; FGD 9: 437. 2009.

Perennial herb. Culms tufted, slender, creeping and often rooting at base, 20–50 cm tall. Leaf sheaths glabrous; leaf blades narrowly lanceolate, 3–8 × 0.2–0.5 cm, glabrous or sparingly hispid near base; ligule membranous, 1–2 mm. Inflorescence subdigitate, axis short; racemes 3–10, 3–8 cm; spikelets lanceolate, ca. 2.5 mm, paired; rachis flat, winged, ca. 0.5 mm broad. Spikelets lanceolate, 2–3 mm, acuminate; lower glume ca. 0.2 mm; upper glume lanceolate, 1/2 as long as spikelet, 3 – 5-veined, margins pubescent; lower lemma slightly longer than upper lemma, 7-veined with broader intervein spaces flanking the midvein, pilose along lateral intervein spaces and margins; upper lemma subleathery, acuminate.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. HK sheet 41963, 42009.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Vietnam, naturalized in Hawaii.
Ecology: Grassy fields, sandy seashores. Flowering & fruiting: Summer to autumn.

Digitaria heterantha (Hook. f.) Merr. 二型馬唐
Enum. Philipp. Fl. Pl. 1: 54. 1923; FHN 4: 433. 1977; FRPS 10(1): 332, pl. 104. 1990; FFJ 6: 231, fig. 198. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 467. 2000; FOC 22: 541. 2006; FGD 9: 435, fig. 224. 2009.
Paspalum heteranthum Hook. f., Fl. Brit. Ind. 7: 16. 1896[1897], based on Panicum heteranthum Nees & Meyen (1841) not Link (1827).
Panicum barbatum auct non (Willd) Kunth: FHK 410. 1861.
Digitaria barbata auct. non Willd.: FKH 314. 1912.

Perennial herb, stoloniferous. Culms branching and rooting at lower nodes, 50–100 cm tall. Leaf sheaths usually shorter than internode, subcompressed, glabrous to papillose-pilose, densely pilose at the base; leaf blades broadly linear, 5–15 × 0.3–0.6 cm, glabrous to papillose-pilose on both surfaces; ligule membranous, 1–2 mm. Inflorescence digitate; racemes 2–4, 5–25 cm, the lower ± bare; rachis triquetrous, thick, rigid, winged. Spikelets paired, ca. 4 mm, pedicellate one villous, sessile one glabrous, rather far apart on rachis, lanceolate; lower glume very small, veinless; upper glume lanceolate, more than 1/2 length of spikelet, 3–5-veined, margins glabrous or ciliate above 1/3–1/2 in sessile spikelet, appressed pubescent in pedicellate spikelet; lower lemma glabrous in sessile spikelet and with spreading hairs in pedicellate spikelet, 5–9-veined, veins equally distant, thick, prominent, interspaces slit-like, acuminate; upper lemma lanceolate, pale and ± leathery, acuminate.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. HK sheet 42048, 42049.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian, Taiwan; Indochina, Malay Peninsula, Indonesia, Philippines.
Ecology: Sandy beaches. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Oct.

Digitaria longiflora (Retz.) Pers. 長花馬唐
Syn. Pl. 1: 85. 1805; FKH 314. 1912; FRPS 10(1): 308, pl. 95: 6–10. 1990; FFJ 6: 229. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 469. 2000; FOC 22: 546. 2006; FGD 9: 433. 2009.
Paspalum longiflorum Retz., Observ. Bot. 4: 15. 1786.
Paspalum brevifolium Fluegge, Gram. Monogr. Paspalum 150. 1810; FHK 408. 1861.

Perennial herb, usually with slender stolons. Culms slender, glabrous, 10–40 cm tall. Leaf sheaths shorter than internode, pubescent or glabrous; leaf blades broadly linear to lanceolate, 1–5 × 0.2–0.5 cm, glabrous or papillose-pilose at base; ligule membranous, 1–1.5 mm, ± truncate. Inflorescence digitate; racemes 2–4, 2–8 cm, usually curving outward; rachis ribbon-like, winged, 0.5–0.8 mm wide, winged; pedicels cylindrical, smooth, with discoid tips. Spikelets elliptic, 1.2–1.5 mm, minutely pubescent near margins, acuminate; lower glume absent; upper glume as long as spikelet, 3–5-veined, back and margins densely appressed-pubescent; lower lemma as long as spikelet, 5–7-veined, glabrous between middle and lateral veins, otherwise pubescent; upper lemma yellowish brown, apex acuminate.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 628, 2249; HK sheet 41978.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; Indian Subcontinent, Indochina, Malay Peninsula, Old World tropics, America.
Ecology: Grassy fields, weedy places. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Oct.

Digitaria radicosa (J. Presl) Miq. 紅尾翎
Fl. Ned. Ind. 3: 437. 1857; FRPS 10(1): 325. 1990; FFJ 6: 233. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 470. 2000; FOC 22: 542. 2006; FGD 9: 437. 2009.
Panicum radicosum J. Presl, Reliq. Haenk. 1: 297. 1830.
Digitaria tenuispica Rendle, J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 36(253): 326–327. 1904; FKH 314. 1912.

Annual herb. Culms slender, prostrate at base, branching, 20–50 cm tall, glabrous, lower nodes rooted. Leaf sheaths shorter than internode, usually glabrous or pubescent; leaf blades linear-lanceolate, 2–8 × 0.2–0.7 cm, adaxial surface glabrous, abaxial surface scabrous, pubescent or papillose-pilose at base; ligule membranous, truncate, 1–2 mm. Inflorescence digitate; racemes 2–3(–4), slender, 4–10 cm; rachis triquetrous, narrowly winged, margins smooth or almost so or slightly scabrous; spikelets narrowly lanceolate, 2.8–3 mm, acute or acuminate, paired, one pedicellate and other very shortly pedicellate or subsessile; lower glume triangular, 0.2–0.3 mm; upper glume lanceolate, 1/3–2/3 length of spikelet, villous, 1–3-veined; lower lemma as long as spikelet, 5–7-veined, a broad intervein space on either side of midvein, lateral veins very close together near margin, lateral veins and margins pilose; upper lemma yellowish at maturity, narrowly lanceolate, thicken papery. Anthers 0.5–1 mm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, New Territories. HK sheet 40844, 41962, 42030.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Yunnan, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; SE Asia, Malesia, Australia, Indian Ocean islands, Madagascar.
Ecology: Moist weedy places, roadsides. Flowering & fruiting: Summer to autumn.

Digitaria sanguinalis (L.) Scop. 馬唐
Fl. Carniol. ed. 2, 1: 52. 1771; FKH 314. 1912; FRPS 10(1): 329, pl. 103: 7–9. 1990; FTW ed. 2, 5: 470. 2000; FOC 22: 542. 2006; FGD 9: 436, fig. 225. 2009.
Panicum sanguinale L., Sp. Pl. 1: 57. 1753; FHK 410. 1861.
Panicum commutatum auct. non (Schult. f.) Nees: FHK 410. 1861.

Annual herb. Culms erect or ascending from decumbent base, 10–100 cm tall, glabrous or hairy at nodes. Leaf sheaths usually shorter than internode, glabrous or sparsely papillose-pilose; leaf blades linear-lanceolate, 5–20 × 0.3–1.2 cm, glabrous or pilose, base rounded, margins thickened, scabrous; ligule 1–3 mm, membranous, obtuse. Inflorescence digitate or subdigitate, axis 1–2 cm; racemes 4–12, stiff, 5–18 cm, upper alternating or digitate, the base subverticillate; rachis winged, margins scabrous. Spikelets usually paired, one pedicellate and other sessile or shortly pedicellate, elliptic-lanceolate, 3–3.5 mm, acute; lower glume small, triangular, veinless; upper glume lanceolate, 1/3–3/4 spikelet length, 3-veined, pubescent, margins ciliate; lower lemma as long as spikelet, 5–7-veined, veins evenly spaced or a broader interspace flanking the midvein, midvein smooth, lateral veins setiform-scabrous especially toward the apex, appressed-pubescent on lateral intervein spaces and margins; upper lemma greenish grey, as long as spikelet, subcoriaceous, lanceolate, apex acuminate.

Locality: Tuen Mun. HK sheet 14537, 34217.
Distribution: Widely spread over most provinces of China; warm-temperate subtropical regions throughout the world.
Ecology: Roadsides, weedy places. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Sep.

Digitaria setigera Roth ex Roem. & Schult. 海南馬唐
Syst. Veg. 2: 474. 1817; FRPS 10(1): 324, pl. 101: 6 – 9. 1990; FTW ed. 2, 5: 471, pl. 195. 2000; FOC 22: 542. 2006; FGD 9: 436. 2009.
Digitaria microbachne Henrard, Mede. Rijks-Herb. 61: 13. 1930; Check List HK Plants 332. 2002; 116. 2004.

Annual or perennial herb. Culms tufted, creeping and rooting at lower nodes, 30–100 cm tall, many noded, glabrous. Leaf sheaths glabrous or papillose-pilose; leaf blades linear-lanceolate, 5–20 × 0.3–1.2 cm, glabrous on both surfaces, papillose-pilose at base, base subrounded, apex acuminate; ligule membranous, 1–2 mm. Inflorescence digitate or subdigitate, axis 1–4 cm; racemes 5–12, stiff, 5–15 cm; spikelets paired; rachis triquetrous, narrowly winged, margins scabrous. Spikelets narrowly lanceolate-oblong, 2–3 mm, acute; lower glume absent or a minute rim; upper glume up to 1/3 length of spikelet, 1–3-veined or veinless, margins ciliate; lower lemma as long as spikelet, 5–7-veined, veins evenly spaced or with a wider interspace flanking the midvein, lateral intervein spaces and margins appressed pubescent to villous, rarely ciliate or setose; upper lemma yellowish to grey, subequalling lower lemma, acuminate.

Locality: Happy Valley. HK sheet 33912, 41964, 42031.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; tropical Asia.
Ecology: Margins of forests, open fields. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Nov.

Digitaria violascens Link 紫馬唐
Hort. Berol. 1: 229. 1827; FRPS 10(1): 308, pl. 95: 1–5. 1990; FFJ 6: 229, fig. 194. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 471, pl. 196. 2000; FOC 22: 547. 2006; FGD 9: 434. 2009.
Digitaria violascens Link var. villosa Keng, Sunyatsenia 3: 19. 1935.

Annual herb. Culms tufted, 20–50(–70) cm tall, glabrous. Leaf sheaths mostly shorter than internode, glabrous or pilose; leaf blades linear-lanceolate, 5–15 × 0.2–0.7 cm, glabrous or adaxial surface pilose at base and mouth, margins scabrous; ligule 1–2 mm, membranous. Inflorescence subdigitate; racemes (2–)4–7(–10), ascending, 3–14 cm; rachis slightly scabrous; pedicels scabrous, with discoid tips. Spikelets elliptic, 2 or 3 per node, 1–2.5 mm; lower glume absent; upper glume lanceolate, slightly shorter than spikelet, 3-veined, intervein spaces and margins appressed-pubescent; lower lemma as long as spikelet, 5–7-veined, intervein spaces and margins pubescent, but usually glabrous flanking the middle vein; upper lemma dark brown or blackish purple at maturity, as long as spikelet, coriaceous, apex acute.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. HK sheet 8293, 30738, 31899.
Distribution: Widely spread over C to S and E to W China; Indian Subcontinent, Indochina, Malay Peninsula, Indonesia, Australia, S America.
Ecology: Grassy hillsides, roadsides, weedy places. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Nov.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Victoria Peak, Lower Shing Mun, Wang Shan Keuk
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Dimeria falcata Hack. 鐮形觿茅
Monogr. Phan. 6: 85. 1889; FKH 320. 1912; FFJ 6: 236, fig. 203. 1995; FRPS 10(2): 177, pl. 42: 1–9. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 5: 538, pl. 227. 2000; FOC 22: 615. 2006; FGD 9: 453. 2009.
Dimeria falcata Hack. var. tenuior Keng & Y. L. Yang, J. Nanjing Univ., Nat. Sci. ed. 1980(4): 106. 1980.
Dimeria fuscescens auct. non Trin.: FHK 419. 1861.

Annual herb. Culms erect, tufted, 20–70 cm tall. Leaf sheaths hirsute with short tubercle-based hairs or glabrous at base, the lower longer than internode and the upper shorter than internode; leaf blades dark green or reddish, linear, 4–20 × 0.2–0.3 mm, hirsute, apex finely acuminate; ligule 0.4–0.5 mm. Racemes 2–3, digitate, slightly curved; rachis flattened, margin scabrid or white-ciliate. Spikelets solitary, alternating, reddish brown or nearly purplish, linear-oblong, laterally compressed, base bearded; glumes papery, lower glume ca. 2.8 mm, chartaceous, dorsally keeled and ciliate, 1-veined; upper glume keeled, white-pilose near margins and on keel, margins broadly scabrous, apex acute; lower lemma oblanceolate, membranous, hyaline, 1-veined, upper margins ciliate; upper lemma shorter than upper glume, oblonglanceolate, hyaline membranous, 2-lobed, a slender awn exserted from the sinus; awn 7–10 mm, geniculate; upper palea absent.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Lower Shing Mun, Wang Shan Keuk. HK sheet 41943, 41947, 42005.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Myanmar, Thailand.
Ecology: Moist grassy fields. Flowering & fruiting: Autumn.

Dimeria ornithopoda Trin. 觿茅
Fund. Agrost. 167. 1820; FFJ 6: 235, fig. 202. 1995; FRPS 10(2): 171, pl. 42: 20. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 5: 540. 2000; FOC 22: 615. 2006; FGD 9: 452, fig. 234. 2009.

Annual herb. Culms slender, erect or geniculate at base, glabrous, 3–40 cm tall. Leaf sheaths keeled, with scattered tubercle-based hairs; leaf blades linear, soft, 1.5–5 × 0.1–0.3 cm, hispid with scattered tubercle-based hairs or glabrescent, acuminate; ligule 0.5–1 mm, ciliate at the apex. Racemes 2–3, subdigitate, ascending at first, then divergent; rachis triquetrous, flexuose or straight linear, scabrid on angles; pedicels glabrous, alternate in one side of rachis. Spikelets linear-oblong or narrow elliptic, strongly laterally compressed, usually purple or reddish brown; glumes herbaceous with broad scarious margins, sometimes with a few long stiff hairs near apex of keel, or stiffly pilose throughout, keel usually wingless, occasionally upper glume narrowly winged, with rounded midline or sharply keeled apex; lower lemma shorter than spikelet, extremely compressed, dorsally scabrid, stiffly pilose throughout, margins thin, acute; upper lemma as long as spikelet; laterally compressed, margin hyaline membranous, acute, 2-lobed, an slender awn from the sinus; awn geniculate; upper palea absent; stamens 2; styles 2. Caryopsis linear-oblong.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, New Territories. Y. W. Lam 470, 1320; HK sheet 41993.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Korea, Japan, India, Malaysia, Philippines, Australia.
Ecology: Streamsides and other moist places. Flowering & fruiting: Oct.–Nov.

Dimeria sinensis Rendle 華觿茅
Linn. Soc., Bot. 36: 359. 1904; FKH 320. 1912; FFJ 6: 236. 1995; FRPS 10(2): 181, pl. 44: 1–9. 1997; FOC 22: 616. 2006; FGD 9: 453. 2009.

Annual herb. Culms slender, erect, 12–40 cm tall. Leaf sheaths hispid with tubercle-based hairs; leaf blades linear, 1.5–9 × 0.2–0.4 cm, setose with tubercle-based bristles; ligule ca. 0.5 mm, dry membranous. Raceme solitary, slightly flexuous, margins densely short ciliate; rachis flat, margins narrowly winged, densely ciliate with white silky hairs, white bearded on outer margin. Spikelets reddish brown or purplish brown, oblong, callus short and truncate, bearded; lower glume slightly shorter than spikelet, keel densely bearded, margins and flank densely or sparsely white-ciliate, below the apex with sparsely hispid hairy near margins, acute; upper glume as long as spikelet, glabrous or sparsely ciliate, sharply keeled, margins hyaline membranous, silky-white villous near margin, apex acute keel with broadly wings; lower lemma lanceolate, hyaline membranous, margins sparsely ciliate, veinless; upper lemma hyaline membranous, 2-lobed, with an awn from the sinus, upper palea absent; awn geniculate in the middle, column twisted, yellowish brown; stamen 2; anthers ca. 1 mm; style base short, connate. Caryopsis oblong.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, New Territories. F. W. Xing 9600; HK sheet 39423, 41952.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian; Thailand.
Ecology: Moist places on hillsides, roadsides and grassy fields.

Echinochloa colona (L.) Link 光頭稗
Hort. Berol. 2: 209. 1833; FHN 4: 418. 1977 [“colonum”]; FRPS 10(1): 252, pl. 77: 1–3. 1990 [“colonum”]; FFJ 6: 213, fig. 180. 1995 [“colonum”]; FTW ed. 2, 5: 474. 2000; FOC 22: 517. 2006; FGD 9: 418. 2009.
Panicum colonum L., Syst. Nat., ed. 10, 2: 870. 1759; FHK 411. 1861; FKH 315. 1912.

Annual herb. Culms erect, 10–60 cm tall, glabrous. Leaf sheaths compressed and keeled, glabrous; leaf blades linear, flat, 3–30 × 0.2–0.8 cm, glabrous, base rounded, apex acuminate, margins slightly scabrous; ligule absent. Panicle narrow, 5–10 cm; central axis slender, triquetrous, glabrous; racemes 1–2 cm, erect or sometimes stiffly diverging, simple, separated or overlapping by up to half their length or more, spikelets tightly congested in 4 neat rows. Spikelets ovate-oblong, 2–3 mm, hirtellous; lower glume triangular, 1/3 to 1/2 length of spikelet, 3-veined; upper glume similar to lower lemma, mucronate to awn-pointed, 5–7-veined; lower floret usually neuter, palea membranous, slightly shorter than lemma, obtuse, 2-keeled, with short ciliate on the keel; upper lemma elliptic, smooth and shiny, margins inrolled embraced a hyaline palea of equal length.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. W. Lam 1342; HK sheet 40835, 41984.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Xinjiang, Shaanxi, Sichuan, Hebei, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; warm regions throughout the world.
Ecology: A weed of farmlands and other wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Summer to autumn.

Echinochloa crusgalli (L.) P. Beauv. 稗
Ess. Agrostogr. 53. 1812; FHN 4: 419. 1977; FRPS 10(1): 252, pl. 77: 4–7. 1990; FFJ 6: 214, fig. 181. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 474, pl. 197. 2000; FOC 22: 517. 2006; FGD 9: 418, fig. 216. 2009.
Panicum crusgalli L., Sp. Pl. 1: 56. 1753; FHK 411. 1861; FKH 315. 1912.

Annual herb. Culms erect, glabrous, 20–160 cm tall. Leaf sheath loose, glabrous, the lower longer and the upper shorter than internode; leaf blades linear, flat, 5–40 × 0.2–2 cm, usually glabrous, smooth except for scabrous margins, base rounded, apex acute or acuminate; ligule absent. Panicle erect, lanceolate to ovate or pyramidal, 6–26 cm; central axis ribbed, rib scabrous or usually with tubercle-based setae; racemes 2–10 cm, usually ascending or slightly close to central axis, simple or the longest with inconspicuous branchlets near the base, rachis scabrous or usually with tubercle-based setae, spikelets loosely to densely crowded. Spikelets green or purplish, ovate, 3–4 mm, spinulose along veins; lower glume triangular, ca. 1/3–1/2 length of spikelet, 3–5-veined, tuberculate-pilose on veins, base embraced spikelet, acute; floret neuter, lemmas herbaceous, 7-veined, tuberculate-pilose on veins, tipped with an robust awn arising from the apex, palea thin membranous, narrow, 2-keeled; upper lemma elliptic, smooth, shiny, mucronate.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. HK sheet 35647, 42202, 42203.
Distribution: Widely spread over most provinces of China; throughout subtropical and warm-temperate regions of the world.
Ecology: Paddy fields, marshes, other wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Summer to autumn.

Echinochloa crusgalli (L.) P. Beauv. var. austrojaponensis Ohwi 小旱稗（小果稗）
Acta Phytotax. Geobot. 11: 38. 1942 [“austro-japonensis”]; FRPS 10(1): 253. 1990; FYN 9: 514. 2003; FOC 22: 518. 2006; FGD 9: 419. 2009.

Culms 20–40 cm tall. Leaf blades often involute, 0.2–0.5 cm broad. Inflorescence narrow and slender; racemes short, erect, appressed to axis, simple. Spikelets purplish, 2.5–3 mm, hispid along veins, lower lemma awnless or with a short awn.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, New Territories. Y. S. Lau 1610; L. T. Lo 581; HK sheet 39688.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou, Hunan, Jiangxi, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan (Ryukyu Islands), Philippines.
Ecology: Marshes, ditches, damp grasslands.

Echinochloa crusgalli (L.) P. Beauv. var. breviseta (Döll) Podp. 短芒稗
Prace Morav.-Slez. Akad. Ved. Prir. 2(sign. 20): 745. 1925; FHN 4: 419. 1977; FRPS 10(1): 253. 1990; FOC 22: 518. 2006; FGD 9: 419. 2009.
Panicum crusgalli L. var. brevisetum Döll, Fl. Bad. 1: 232. 1857.

Culms 30–75 cm tall. Leaf blades 8–15 × 0.4–0.6 cm. Inflorescence narrow, 8–10 cm; racemes simple. Spikelets green, ovateelliptic, ca. 3 mm, hispid along veins, mucronate or with a short awn less than 5 mm.

Locality: Fanling, Peng Shan, Mai Po. Y. W. Lam 1344; HK sheet 14443, 41966.
Distribution: Guangdong, Taiwan; India, Malaysia, Sri Lanka, tropical Africa.
Ecology: Weedy places.

Echinochloa cruspavonis (Kunth) Schult. 孔雀稗
Mant. 2: 269. 1824; FRPS 10(1): 256, pl. 78: 5–8. 1990; FFJ 6: 215. 1995; FOC 22: 517. 2006; FGD 9: 420. 2009.
Oplismenus cruspavonis Kunth, Nov. Gen. Sp. (quarto ed.) 1: 108. 1815 [“1816”].

Annual or perennial herb. Culms robust, straggling and rooting at base, 1.2–1.8 m tall. Leaf sheaths loose, smooth and glabrous; leaf blades linear, flat, 10–40 × 1–1.5 cm, glabrous, margins harshly scabrous; ligule absent. Inflorescence nodding, large, loose, 15–25 cm; branches mostly compound, spikelets many, crowded on secondary branchlets. Spikelets purple-tinged, ovate-lanceolate, 2–3 mm, hispid on veins, the hairs not tubercle-based; lower glume triangular, 1/3–2/5 length of spikelet, 3-veined; upper glume as long as spikelet, rostrate, 5-veined, stiff hairs on the veins; lower lemma sterile, herbaceous, 5–7-veined, with a stout awn, 1–1.5 cm; upper lemma leathery, smooth and shiny, mucronate.

Locality: Wan Chai Gap. H. C. Tang 1969.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guizhou, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Anhui, Fujian; widely spread over tropical regions.
Ecology: Marshes and other damp places. Flowering & fruiting: Summer to autumn.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Kowloon, Castle Peak, Yuen Long, Sai Kung
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Echinochloa glabrescens Munro ex Hook. f. 硬稃稗
Fl. Brit. Ind. 7(21): 31. 1897; FRPS 10(1): 258, pl. 78: 1–4. 1990; FYN 9: 515. 2003; FGD 9: 420. 2009.
Echinochloa crusgalli (L.) P. Beauv. var. formosensis Ohwi, Acta Phytotax. Geobot. 11(1): 38. 1942 [“Crus-galli”]; FHN 4: 419. 1977; FTW 5: 554. 1978.
Echinochloa glabrescens Kossenko, Bot. Mater. Gerb. Bot. Inst. Komarova Akad. Nauk SSSR. 11: 40. 1949; FOC 22: 517. 2006.

Annual herb. Culms erect or slightly decumbent at base, 30–120 cm tall. Leaf sheaths smooth and glabrous; leaf blades linearlanceolate or linear, flat, 10–38 × 0.6–1.5 cm, glabrous, margins thickened, acuminate; ligule absent. Inflorescence narrow panicle, 5–25 × 1–2(–4) cm; racemes 1–4 cm, simple or the middle subverticillate. Spikelets light green, 3.5–5 mm, glabrous or tuberculatepilose; lower glume 1/3–1/2 length of spikelet, 3-veined, acute; upper glume equal to spikelet, 5-veined, inconspicuously scabrous to shortly hispid along veins; lower floret neuter; lemmas coriaceous, hard and shiny, especially down the centre, tuberculate-pilose on the veins, the lower cuspidate to awned. Caryopsis broad elliptic.

Locality: Kowloon, Castle Peak, Yuen Long, Sai Kung. Y. W. Lam 742, 2201; HK sheet 14441.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Jiangsu, Zhejiang; Bhutan, NE India, Japan, Korea, Nepal, Africa.
Ecology: Margins of ponds, other wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Summer to autumn.

Eleusine coracana (L.) Gaertn. 穇
Fruct. Sem. Pl. 1: 8, t. 1, fig. 11. 1788; FKH 327. 1912; FHN 4: 384. 1977; FRPS 10(1): 66, pl. 18: 10–17. 1990; FFJ 6: 144. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 412. 2000; FOC 22: 482. 2006; FGD 9: 357, fig. 170. 2009.
Cynosurus coracanus L., Syst. Nat. ed. 10, 2: 875. 1759.

Annual herb. Culms tufted, robust, erect or ascending, usually branched, 50–120 cm tall. Leaf blades flat, 30–60 × 0.6–1.2 cm, pilose or glabrous; ligule 1–2 mm, a fringe of hairs; leaf sheaths glabrous, overlapping. Inflorescence of subdigitate one-sided spikes; the spikes 5–10 cm × 8–10 mm, often incurved at maturity. Spikelets very closely imbricate, ovate, 5–9 mm, 6–9-flowered, not disarticulating at maturity; glumes lanceolate-oblong, scabrid along the winged keel; lower glume 3-veined, 1.5–3 mm; upper glume with additional veins in keel, 1.8–5 mm; lemmas triangular-ovate, 2.2–4.7 mm, keel 3-veined, scabrid and narrowly winged, subacute; palea as long as the lemma, narrowly ovate, keels scabrid, winged. Grain an utricle, ca. 1 mm, yellowish brown, globose, finely striatepunctuate.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 16002.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Ningxia, Henan, Hubei, Shandong, Anhui, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan (cultivated); widely cultivated in Old World tropics. Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: May–Sep.
Uses: Food (cereal), animal food (fodder).

Eleusine indica (L.) Gaertn. 牛筋草
Fruct. Sem. Pl. 1: 8. 1789; FHK 429. 1861; FKH 327. 1912; FHN 4: 383. 1977; FRPS 10(1): 64, pl. 18: 1–9. 1990; FFJ 6: 143, fig. 117. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 412. 2000; FOC 22: 482. 2006; FGD 9: 356. 2009.
Cynosurus indicus L., Sp. Pl. 1: 72. 1753.

Annual herb. Culms tufted, erect or geniculate at base, 10–90 cm tall. Leaf blades flat or folded, 10–15 × 0.3–0.5 cm, glabrous or tuberculate-pilose on adaxial surface; ligule ca. 1 mm, membranous, at most sparsely ciliolate. Leaf sheaths laterally compressed and keeled, glabrous or tuberculate-pilose. Inflorescence of 2–7 digitate spikes; the spikes ascending, 3–10 cm × 3–5 mm. Spikelets elliptic, 4.5–8 mm, 3–9-flowered; glumes lanceolate, scabrid along keel; lower glume 1-veined, 1.5–2 mm, lowest floret ca. 3 mm; upper glume with small additional veins in the thickened keel, 2–3 mm; lemmas ovate, 2–4 mm, keeled along small additional veins, keel acute; palea membranous, 2-keeled, shorter than the lemma. Anthers 3, ca. 0.6 mm. Grain ca. 1.5 mm, blackish, oblong or ovate, ventrally grooved, obliquely striate with fine close lines running vertically between the striae.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1025, 2233; S. P. Lau 17.
Distribution: Widely spread over most provinces of China; tropical and subtropical regions worldwide.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides, open fields. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Oct.
Uses: Animal food (fodder).

Enteropogon dolichostachyus (Lag.) Keng ex Lazarides 腸鬚草
Austral. J. Bot., Suppl. Ser. 5: 31. 1972; FOC 22: 490. 2006.
Chloris dolichostachya Lag., Gen. Sp. Pl. 5. 1816; FHN 4: 386, fig. 1194. 1977.
Enteropogon dolichostachyus (Lag.) Keng, Claves Gen. Sp. Gram. Prim. Sinic. 197. 1957 (nom. inval.); FTW ed. 2, 5: 406, pl. 165. 2000; FGD 9: 375, fig. 184. 2009; Check List HK Plants 334. 2002; 117. 2004.

Perennial herb. Culms tufted, erect or geniculate at base, (0.5–)1–1.5(–2) m tall. Leaf blades linear, flat or rolled, 15–45 × 0.4–1.5 cm, midrib white, conspicuous, surface scabrous, loosely glandular hairy, often tuberculate-hispid near ligule, apex setaceous; ligule ca. 0.5 mm, fimbriate; leaf sheaths glabrous or tuberculate-hispid, especially on margin, pilose at mouth. Spikes 10–20 cm, 3–5(–10) digitately arranged, ascending at first, later divaricate or drooping; rachis triquetrous, scabrous. Spikelets 5–7 mm, 2-flowered; glumes papery, deltoid-lanceolate, apex acute and aristate, conspicuously 1-veined; lower glume linearlanceolate, 2–3 mm; upper glume lanceolate, 3–5 mm, awnpointed; lemma of fertile floret purplish, oblong-lanceolate, 3.5–5 mm, glabrous, scabrous along either side of midvein and toward apex; awn 8–16 mm; palea linear-lanceolate, upper margin siliceous, with the same texture and length as the lemma, keels scabrous; upper floret reduced to an oblong 0.8 – 1.8 mm sterile lemma with 2–5 mm awn, appressed to fertile floret. Caryopsis reddish brown, ellipsoidal, ca. 3.5 mm.

Locality: Ping Chau. S. C. Ng 2031.
Distribution: Hainan, S Yunnan, Taiwan; Afghanistan through India to SE Asia.
Ecology: Open grassy fields, seashores. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Oct.

Eragrostis atrovirens (Desf.) Trin. ex Steud. 鼠婦草
Nom. Bot., ed. 2, 1: 562. 1840; FHN 4: 376. 1977; FRPS 10(1): 16, pl. 4: 1–2. 1990; FFJ 6: 150. 1995; FOC 22: 474. 2006; FGD 9: 349. 2009.
Poa atrovirens Desf., Fl. Atlant. 1: 73, pl. 17. 1798.
Eragrostis elegantula (Kunth) Nees ex Steud., Syn. Pl. Glumac. 1: 266. 1854; FKH 329. 1912.

Perennial herb. Culms loosely tufted, erect from the geniculate base, 50–120 cm tall, 4–6(–8)-noded. Leaf blades flat or inrolled, 4–17 × 0.2–0.3 cm, adaxial surface scabrous, near base pilose, abaxial surface glabrous; ligules a ciliolate membrane, 0.2–0.3 mm; leaf sheaths glabrous but pilose along summit. Panicle open, 5–20(–25) × 2–15 cm; branches 1–several per node. Spikelets plumbeous and purplish, narrowly oblong, 5–15(–25) × 1.5–2.5 mm, 8–50-flowered, pedicels 0.5–5(–15) mm; breaking up from the base, rachilla persistent, glabrous in axils; glumes subequal, ovate-elliptic, 1-veined; lower glume ovate, 1–1.3 mm, apex acute; upper glume narrowly ovate, 1.3–2.3 mm, apex acuminate; lemmas broadly ovate and acute to subacute when flattened, 1.8–2.2 mm, apex acute; palea loosely ciliate along keel, 1.6–1.8 mm. Stamens 3; anthers 0.5–1 mm. Caryopsis ellipsoidal, ca. 1 mm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, New Territories. Y. W. Lam 809, 1323; HK sheet 42029.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan; tropical and subtropical regions of Asia and Africa.
Ecology: Roadsides, stream banks. Flowering & fruiting: Summer to autumn.

Eragrostis autumnalis Keng 秋畫眉草
Contr. Biol. Lab. Chin. Assoc. Advancem. Sci. Sect. Bot. 10: 178. 1936; FRPS 10(1): 24, pl. 6: 4. 1990; FFJ 6: 149. 1995; FOC 22: 476. 2006; FGD 9: 348. 2009.

Annual herb. Culms erect from the geniculate base, 15–45 cm tall, 3–4-noded, often branched at the lower nodes. Leaf blades usually inrolled or plicate, 6–12 × 0.2–0.3 cm; ligules a line of hairs; leaf sheaths compressed, glabrous, along summit with long deciduous hairs. Panicle 6–15 × 3–5 cm; branches usually clustered, glabrous in axils. Spikelets grey-green, 3–5 × ca. 2 mm, 3–10-flowered, with pedicels 1–5 mm; glumes 1-veined, lower glume ca. 1.5 mm, upper glume ca. 2 mm; lemma broadly ovate, apex acute, lower lemma ca. 2 mm; palea ca. 1.5 mm, 2-keeled, along keels ciliate, persistent or tardily deciduous. Stamens 3; anthers ca. 0.5 mm. Caryopsis red-brown, ca. 1 mm.

Locality: Chuen Lung. Y. S. Lau 2223; Y. W. Lam 938.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guizhou, Jiangxi, Hubei, Anhui, Shandong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian.
Ecology: Grasslands, roadsides. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Nov.
Notes: The species was reported as Eragrostis perennans Keng previously (Check List HK Plants 92. 1993).

Eragrostis brownii (Kunth) Nees 長畫眉草
Cat. Indian Pl. 105. 1834; FOC 22: 473. 2006; FGD 9: 351. 2009.
Eragrostis zeylanica Nees & Meyen, Nov. Act. Acad. Caes Leop-Carol, 19(Suppl.): 204. 1843; FHK 433. 1861; FHN 4: 378. 1977; FRPS 10(1): 13, pl. 3: 1–2. 1990; Check List HK Plants 335. 2002; 117. 2004.
Eragrostis elongata auct. non Jacq.: FKH 329. 1912.

Perennial herb. Culms tufted, erect or geniculate at base, 15–60 cm tall, 2–5-noded, branched at lower nodes. Leaf blades flat or inrolled, 3–10 cm × 1–3 mm; ligules membranous, ca. 0.2 mm; leaf sheaths glabrous and smooth, pilose along summit. Panicle 3–18 cm; branches solitary with spikelets at base. Spikelets livid green, purplish or dark brown, oblong-elliptic, 4–20 × 1.5–2.5 mm, 7–manyflowered, subsessile or with very short pedicel, apex acute; glumes ovate-lanceolate, 1–2 mm; lower glume 1-veined, ca. 1.2 mm; upper glume 1–3-veined, the laterals usually faint, ca. 1.8 mm; lower lemmas 2–2.5 mm; palea slightly shorter than lemma, 1.5–2 mm, ciliolate along keels, apex emarginate. Stamens 3; anthers 0.3–1.3 mm. Caryopsis dark brown, ca. 0.5 mm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island. HK sheet 8666, 16144, 42043.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Yunnan, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian; widely spread over Japan, Indochina, Indian Subcontinent, Malesia, Pacific islands, Australia.
Ecology: Open fields, mountain slopes, roadsides. Flowering & fruiting: Spring.

Eragrostis cumingii Steud. 珠芽畫眉草（扭枝畫眉草）
Syn. Pl. Glumac. 1: 266. 1854; FOC 22: 475. 2006; FGD 9: 348. 2009.
Eragrostis reflexa Hack., Philip. J. Sci. 3: 168. 1948; FRPS 10(1): 13, pl. 3: 3–5, 120: 2. 1990; Check List HK Plants 335. 2002; 117. 2004.

Annual herb. Culms erect, ca. 25 cm tall, glabrous, usually with scaly buds at base. Leaf blades linear, inrolled, 5  9 × 0.1–0.2 cm, glabrous on both surfaces, except with long pilose at base of adaxial surface; ligule 0.1–0.3 mm, fimbriate; leaf sheaths compressed at base, glabrous, but long pilose along summit. Panicle open, 8–30 × 4–8 cm; branches solitary, naked at lower part, glabrous in axils. Spikelets yellowish green or grey-green, narrowly oblong, 5–20 × 2–2.5 mm, 8–40-flowered, pedicels without glands; glumes papery, deltoid-oblong, easily falling off when mature, lower glume 1-veined, ca. 1 mm, upper glume 1–3-veined, ca. 1.3 mm; lemmas broadly ovate, lateral veins nearly parallel, lower lemma ca. 2 mm; palea papery, oblanceolate, persistent or tardily deciduous, strongly 2-keeled, along keels ciliolate. Anthers ca. 0.2 mm. Caryopsis elliptic, terete to laterally flattened, 0.8–1 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 2262; HK sheet 8665, 16143.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Hubei Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang; Japan, SE Asia, Australia.
Ecology: Open fields, roadsides. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Sep.

Eragrostis curvula (Schrad.) Nees 彎葉畫眉草
Fl. Afr. Austral. Ill. 397. 1841; FRPS 10(1): 18, pl. 120: 9, 124: 1. 1990; FFJ 6: 152. 1995; FOC 22: 474. 2006. Poa curvula Schrad., Gött. Gel. Anz. 3: 2073. 1821.

Perennial herb. Culms densely tufted, erect, 80–120 cm tall, slightly compressed at the base. Leaf blades linear to filiform, (5–)10–40 cm × 1–2.5(–3) mm, attenuate to a fine point, arcuate spreading, scabrous; leaf sheaths scabrous with retrorse hairs at lower part, glabrous upward, shorter than internodes, long pilose along the summit. Panicles open, 12–35 × 6–9 cm; branches solitary or in pairs, ascending, naked at base, at least the lower densely pilose in axils. Spikelets grey-green, (4–)6–11 × 1.5–2 mm, 5–16-flowered, breaking up from the base, rachilla persistent below but fragile above; glumes lanceolate, apex acuminate, 1-veined, lower glume lanceolate, 1–1.5 mm, upper glume narrowly ovate, 1.8–2.5 mm; lemmas broadly oblong, apex acute or obtuse, veins prominent, 1.8–2.6 mm, appressed to the rachilla; palea subequal to lemma, 2-keeled, smooth or minutely scaberulous on the keels, persistent or tardily deciduous. Stamens 3; anthers 0.8–1.2 mm. Caryopsis ellipsoidal to obovoid, dorsally compressed, adaxial surface with a shallow, broad groove or ungrooved, smooth, mostly translucent, light brown, 1–1.7 mm.

Locality: Mai Po, Shing Mun (introduced). Y. S. Lau 3039; HK sheet 34228.
Distribution: Cultivated in Guangxi, Yunnan, Xinjiang, Hubei, Jiangsu, Fujian; native to Africa.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Sep.
Uses: Animal food (fodder), ornamental.

Eragrostis cylindrica (Roxb.) Nees ex Hook. & Arn. 短穗畫眉草
Bot. Beechey Voy. 251. 1838; FFJ 6: 150, fig. 123. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 418. 2000; FOC 22: 473. 2006; FGD 9: 350. 2009.
Poa cylindrica Roxb., Fl. Ind. 1: 335. 1820.
Eragrostis geniculata Nees & Meyen, Gramineae 71–72. 1841; FHK 433. 1861; FKH 329. 1912.

Perennial herb. Culms tufted, ascending from the geniculate base, 20–70 cm tall, glabrous, 3–4-noded. Leaf linear, usually inrolled, 3–15 cm × 2–5 mm, pilose; ligules reduced into a fringe of hairs; leaf sheaths shorter than internodes, pilose, especially near the summit. Panicle constricted and spike-like, 2 –8 × 1–2.5 cm, lower branches 0.5–1.5 cm, erect-ascending, pilose in axils. Spikelets yellowish brown or tinged with purple, sessile or nearly so, ca. 7 cm × 22.5–3 mm, 4–17-flowered; glume 1-veined, lanceolate, apex acute, lower glume ca. 1.5 mm, upper glume ca. 2 mm; lemma papery, ovate-oblong, apex mucronate, lowest lemma ca. 2 mm; palea persistent, elliptic, papery, ca. 1.8 mm, apex acute, along keels and margins ciliate. Stamens 3. Caryopsis yellow, ellipsoidal, ca. 0.5 mm.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Lantau Island. HK sheet 42012, 42014.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Grassy mountain slopes. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Oct.

Eragrostis fauriei Ohwi 佛歐里畫眉草
Bot. Mag. (Tokyo). 55: 278. 1941; FTW ed. 2, 5: 420. 2000; FOC 22: 474. 2006.
Eragrostis stenophylla auct. non Hack.: FKH 329. 1912.

Perennial herb. Culms densely tufted, erect, glabrous, 30–60 cm tall. Leaf blades leathery, 10 × 2–5 mm, margins inrolled; ligule long ciliate; leaf sheaths shorter than the internode. Panicle 10–15 cm, loose, branches ascending, scabrous, axils glabrous. Spikelets lanceolate, slightly compressed, 5–10 × 2.5 mm, 6–15-flowered, ascending or slightly appressed, distinctly pedicellate, greyish or slightly tinged with purple; glumes broadly lanceolate, acuminate, 1-veined; lower glume 1–1.5 mm; upper glume 1.5–1.7 mm; lemmas ca. 2 mm, ovate, apex acute; minutely punctate, keels distinctly scabrous, lateral veins distinct, subparallel, ca. 2/3 length of lemma; palea persistent, keels arc-shaped, ciliate-scabrous; rachilla persistent, slightly compressed; stamens 3, anthers oblong, blackish purple, ca. 0.5 mm. Caryopsis elliptic, slightly compressed, obscurely striolate, ca. 0.7 mm.

Locality: Aberdeen, Sai Kung. L. T. Lo 553; HK sheet 8688.
Distribution: Taiwan.
Ecology: Flowering: Mar.–May; fruiting: Jul.–Aug.

Eragrostis ferruginea P. Beauv. 知風草
Ess. Agrostogr. 71. 1812; FRPS 10(1): 22, pl. 122: 8. 1990; FFJ 6: 151. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 420. 2000; FOC 22: 475. 2006; FGD 9: 350. 2009.
Poa ferruginea Thunb., Syst. Veg., ed. 14 (J. A. Murray). 114. 1784.

Perennial herb. Culms tufted, erect or geniculate at base, 30–110 cm tall. Leaf blades linear-lanceolate, (4–)20–40 × 2–6 mm, glabrous or sparingly covered with silky hairs on basal part of adaxial surface; ligules a line of hairs, ca. 1 mm; leaf sheaths laterally compressed, densely pilose along margins and summit, sometimes glandular along main vein. Panicle large and open, 15–40 × 4–15 cm, 1–3-branched at each node, glabrous in axils; branchlet and pedicel usually glandular at middle or above middle. Spikelets oblong, blackish purple, grey-green, rarely yellowish green, 5–10 × 2–2.5 mm, (4–)7–12-flowered; glumes subleathery, lanceolate, open, 1-veined, apex acuminate, lower glume linear-lanceolate, 1–2 mm, upper glume lanceolate, 1.5–3 mm; lemmas subleathery, ovatelanceolate to oblong, 2.4–3 mm, 3-veined, apex obtuse, lower lemma ca. 3 mm; palea persistent, papery, elliptic, ca. 2 mm, 2-keeled, ciliolate along keels. Anthers ca. 1 mm. Caryopsis rectangular-prismatic with a shallow, narrow adaxial groove, laterally compressed, faintly striate, reddish brown, 0.7–1.5 mm.

Locality: Clear Water Bay. Y. S. Lau 3099, 3190.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Hubei, Henan, Hebei, Shaanxi, Anhui, Shandong, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Korea, Vietnam, Laos, Nepal, Bhutan, Sikkim.
Ecology: Grassy hillslopes, roadsides. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Dec.
Uses: Animal food (fodder).

Eragrostis japonica (Thunb.) Trin. 亂草
Mém. Acad. Imp. Sci. St.-Pétersb., Sér. 6. 1: 405. 1831; FRPS 10(1): 30, pl. 123: 4. 1990; FFJ 6: 147. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 420. 2000; FOC 22: 479. 2006; FGD 9: 347. 2009.
Poa japonica Thunb., Fl. Jap. 51. 1784.
Eragrostis tenella auct. non P. Beauv.: FHK 431. 1861.
Eragrostis interrupta auct. non P. Beauv.: FKH 328. 1912.

Annual herb. Culms tufted, 30–100 cm tall, 3–4-noded. Leaf blades flat, 3–25 × 0.3–0.5 cm, smooth and glabrous; ligule scarious, ca. 0.5 mm, truncate, ciliate at apex; leaf sheaths usually loose, longer than internodes, glabrous. Panicle elongate, 6–40 × 1.5–6 cm, branches 3–14 cm, slender, clustered or verticillate, glabrous in axils. Spikelets usually purplish at maturity, ovate, 1–2(–3) mm, 4–8-flowered; rachilla fragile, distarticulating between florets from top downward at maturity; glumes papery, ovate-lanceolate, subequal, 0.6–0.8 mm, 1-veined, apex acute to obtuse; lemmas papery, broadly elliptic, distinctly 3-veined, basal part inrolled, apex obtuse, lower lemma ca. 1 mm; palea subequal to lemma, 2-keeled, scabrous along keels. Stamens 2; anthers ca. 0.2 mm. Caryopsis red-brown, ovoid, circular in cross-section, 0.3–0.5 mm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, New Territories. HK sheet 8675.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou, Hubei, Henan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Vietnam, Myanmar, Thailand, India, Nepal, Bhutan, Malaysia, Indonesia, New Guinea, Philippines.
Ecology: Open fields, roadsides, stream banks and other moist places. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Nov.

Eragrostis pilosa (L.) P. Beauv. var. imberbis Franch. 無毛畫眉草
Nouv. Arch. Mus. Hist. Nat. Paris 11, 7: 145, 1884; Fl. Ill. Pl. Prim. Sin. Gram. 315. 1959; FRPS 10(1): 23, pl. 121: 1. 1990; FFJ 6: 150. 1995.
Eragrostis pilosa auct. non (L.) P. Beauv, Check List HK Plants 92. 1993.

Annual herb. Culms loosely tufted, erect or geniculate at base, 15–30 cm tall, 4-noded, smooth. Leaf blades flat or inrolled, 6–20 × 0.2–0.4 cm, glabrous; ligule ca. 0.4 mm, upper half turned into a fringe of hairs; leaf sheaths glabrous at mouth, compressed, margin submembranous. Panicle elliptic to ovate, 10–25 × 3.5–14 cm; branches solitary to verticillate, glabrous in axils, usually ascending, pedicels as long or longer than spikelets. Spikelets linear, 3–10 × 1–1.5 mm, purplish-green, 4–14-flowered, florets ± appressed to the rachilla, breaking up from the base, the rachilla persistent; glumes membranous, lanceolate, apex acuminate, lower glume without vein, 0.4–0.7 mm, upper glume indistinctly 1-veined, 0.7–1.3 mm; lemmas papery, ovate, apex acute, lower lemma ca. 1.8 mm; palea papery, oblanceolate, apex obtuse, ca. 1.5 mm, along keels persistent or tardily deciduous ciliate. Stamens 3; anthers 0.1–0.3 mm. Caryopsis ellipsoidal with one side straight, 0.6–1 mm.

Locality: Aberdeen, Wong Nai Chung. H. C. Tang 1916; HK sheet 8677.
Distribution: Widely spread over most provinces of China (except Xinjiang, Gansu); very widely distributed in tropical and warm regions of the Old World.
Ecology: Farmlands and other moist places. Flowering & fruiting : Jul.–Nov.
Uses: Animal food (forage).

Eragrostis pilosissima Link 多毛知風草
Hort. Berol. 1: 189. 1827; FHK 432. 1861; FKH 329. 1912; FHN 4: 377. 1977; FRPS 10(1): 18, pl. 122: 1. 1990; FFJ 6: 154. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 423. 2000; FOC 22: 474. 2006; FGD 9: 352. 2009.

Perennial herb. Culms tufted, erect, slender and rigid, 30–40 cm tall. Leaf blades usually inrolled, 5–10 × 0.1–0.2 cm, densely pilose on both surfaces; ligule a fringe of hairs, ca. 0.3 mm; leaf sheaths densely pilose, usually shorter than internodes but longer than internodes at base. Panicle lax, 4–10 × 2–5 cm; branch usually solitary, slender, glabrous in axils. Spikelets yellow, oblong, 3–7 × ca. 2 mm, 7–14-flowered; rachilla zigzag-shaped; glumes papery, 1-veined, lanceolate; lower glume emarginate or obtuse at the apex, ca. 0.8 mm; upper glume obtuse at the apex, ca. 1.2 mm; lemmas ovate-oblong, papery, margins membranous, ca. 1.8 mm, 3-veined, lateral veins faint, mucronate, deciduous; palea slightly shorter than lemma, slightly arc-shaped, 2-keeled, ca. 1.6 mm, minutely ciliate along keels, persistent or tardily deciduous. Stamens 3; anthers ca. 0.8 mm. Caryopsis ovate, bluntly triangular in section, ca. 0.8 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. S. P. Lau 159; Y. W. Lam 1066, 1034.
Distribution: Fujian, Hainan, Guangdong, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; SE Asia.
Ecology: Dry hillslopes, open grassy fields. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.

Eragrostis spartinoides Steud. 呂宋畫眉草
Syn. Pl. Glum. 1: 265. 1854; Check List HK Plants 335. 2002.
Poa polymorpha var. α R. Br., Prodr. Fl. Nov. Holland. 180. 1810.
Eragrostis elongata (Willd.) J. Jacq. var. brachyclados Domin, Biblioth. Bot. 20(85): 400. 1915, p.p.
Eragrostis elongata (Willd.) J. Jacq. var. festucoides Domin, Biblioth. Bot. 20(85): 400. 1915.
Eragrostis cumingii Steud. var. novaguineensis Jansen, Reinwardtia 2: 271. 1953.

Perennial herb. Culms tufted, 20–80 cm tall. Leaf sheaths pilose or ciliolate on the outer or both margins; leaf blades usually involute (rarely flat), 1–3 mm wide, filiform or linear, sometimes with scattered hairs; ligules a fringe of hairs, 0.2–0.3 mm. Panicle open, linear or lanceolate, 5–60 × 3–6 cm; branches spreading to divaricate, sparsely divided, entirely spikelet-bearing or naked near axil. Spikelets linear, laterally compressed, 5–28 × 1.5–2.5 mm; rachilla zig-zagged, thick, wider at internode apex; fertile florets 8–57, pedicels 0.5–1.5 mm; breaking up at maturity, rachilla persistent; glumes subequal, ovate, 1-veined, apex acute; lower glume ca. 1.5 mm, upper glume 0.9–2.8 mm; lemmas lanceolate to ovate, 1.5 –2.3 mm, apex acute, deciduous; palea ± as long as lemma, persistent and tardily deciduous. Stamens (2–)3; anthers 0.3–0.7 mm. Caryopsis strongly laterally compressed, oblong-ellipsoidal, ca. 0.6 mm; pericarp tardily free on moistening.

Locality: New Territories, CUHK campus. HK sheet 35875.
Distribution: Tropical Asia, Australia.
Ecology: Creek banks, sandy clay. Flowering & fruiting: All year round.

Eragrostis tenella (L.) P. Beauv. ex Roem. & Schult. 鯽魚草
Syst. Veg. 2: 576. 1817; FKH 329. 1912; FHN 4: 374. 1977; FRPS 10(1): 28, pl. 123: 2. 1990; FFJ 6: 146, fig. 119. 1995; FOC 22: 478. 2006; FGD 9: 346. 2009.
Poa tenella L., Sp. Pl. 1: 69. 1753.
Eragrostis plumosa auct. non Link: FHK 431. 1861.

Annual herb. Culms slender, 10–60 cm tall, glabrous, striate. Leaf blades flat, 3–10 × 0.2–0.5 cm, adaxial surface scabrous, abaxial surface glabrous and smooth; ligule a line of short hairs; leaf sheaths shorter than internodes, pilose along margin and summit. Panicle open, 5–16 cm; branches spreading and with long hairs at axils, branchlets and pedicels with oblong yellowish glands. Spikelets ovate or oblong-ovate, 2–2.5 mm, 4–10-flowered; rachilla fragile, disarticulate between florets from above downward at maturity; glumes membranous, 1-veined, subequal, 0.5–1 mm, falling off when mature; lemmas broadly ovate, apex obtuse, smooth or scaberulous, ca. 1 mm; palea persistent or tardily deciduous, ciliate along keels, hairs ca. 0.3 mm, rigidly spreading at maturity. Stamens 3; anthers ca. 0.3 mm. Caryopsis red, ovoid, ca. 0.5 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1686, 2800; S. P. Lau 7.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Xizang, Hubei, Anhui, Shandong, Fujian, Taiwan; widely spread over tropical regions of the Old World.
Ecology: Open fields, moist places. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Aug.
Uses: Animal food (fodder).

Eragrostis unioloides (Retz.) Nees ex Steud. 牛虱草
Syn. Pl. Glumac. 1: 264. 1854; FHK 432. 1861; FHN 4: 375. 1977; FRPS 10(1): 27, pl. 121: 6 .1990; FFJ 6: 147, fig. 120. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 425. 2000; FOC 22: 477. 2006; FGD 9: 347, fig. 165. 2009.
Poa unioloides Retz., Observ. Bot. 5: 19. 1788.
Poa amabilis L., Sp. Pl. 1: 68. 1753.
Eragrostis amabilis (L.) Wight & Arn., Cat. Indian Pl. 1834: no. 1777. 1834; FKH 329. 1912.
Eragrostis formosana Hayata, Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 21: 53. 1907.

Annual or short-lived perennial herb. Culms erect from the geniculate base, 20–80 cm tall, 3–5-noded. Leaf blades linear, flat or inrolled, 2–20 × 0.2–0.4 cm, subamplexicaul at the base, adaxial surface long pilose, abaxial surface smooth; ligule membranous, ca. 0.8 mm; leaf sheaths glabrous and smooth, long pilose along the summit. Panicle open, 5–20 × 3–5 cm; branches slender, glabrous in axils. Spikelets purplish red at maturity, oblong, 5–10 × 2–4 mm, 10–20-flowered, closely imbricate, pedicel 0.2–1 cm, distarticulating between florets from base upwards at maturity; rachilla persistent; glumes narrowly lanceolate in side-view, 1-veined, the lower 1.5–2 mm, the upper 2–2.5 mm, apex subacute; lemmas broadly ovate to suborbicular when flattened, puncticulate, veins prominent, ca. 2 mm, mucronulate; palea slightly shorter than the lemma, 2-keeled, very narrowly winged and ciliolate, falling off together with its lemma at maturity. Stamens 2; anthers purple, 0.2–0.5 mm. Caryopsis orange-brown, laterally compressed, ellipsoidal, ca. 0.8 mm.

Locality: Widely distributed in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1638; L. T. Lo 113; HK sheet 16203.
Distribution: Fujian, Jiangxi, Taiwan, Yunnan, S China.
Ecology: Mountain slopes, grasslands, roadsides. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Oct.

Eremochloa ciliaris (L.) Merr. 蜈蚣草
Philipp. J. Sci. 1(Suppl. 5): 331. 1906; FHN 4: 464. 1977; FFJ 6: 256, fig. 226. 1995; FRPS 10(2): 271, pl. 68: 4. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 5: 542. 2000; FOC 22: 646. 2006; FGD 9: 485. 2009.
Nardus ciliaris L., Sp. Pl. 1: 53. 1753.
Ischaemum leersioides Munro, Proc. Amer. Acad. Arts 4: 363. 1860; FHK 425. 1861.
Eremochloa leersioides Hack., Monogr. Phan. 6: 264. 1889; FKH 321. 1912.

Perennial herb. Culms slender, erect, tufted, 20–60 cm tall. Leaf sheaths crowded at base of culm, overlapping, the upper shorter than internodes, mouth ciliate; leaf blades 3–15 × 0.1–0.4 cm, glabrous or pubescent, acute; ligule membranous, 0.5–1 mm. Raceme solitary, falcately curved; rachis internodes rib-like, puberulous to thinly hirsute. Sessile spikelet ovate, imbricate in one side of rachis; lower glume oblong-ovate, firmly papery, pubescent on back or subglabrous, marginal spines longer than glume width, longest 1.5–5 mm, 6–7-veined; upper glume as long as lower glume, thicken membranous, narrow wing on the lower part of keel, 3-veined; lower floret staminate, lemma slightly shorter than glume, ovate-oblong, apex obtuse; palea narrow; upper floret bisexual or pistillate, lemma oblong, slightly shorter than lower lemma, apex obtuse, palea narrow; style free, yellowish brown, penicillate. Caryopsis oblong. Pedicellate spikelet absent; pedicel narrowly ellipsoidal, ending in short point.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. HK sheet 39389, 39390, 41990.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; Indochina, Myanmar, Thailand, Malay Peninsula, Indonesia, New Guinea, Philippines, Australia.
Ecology: Open places on hills. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Oct.

Eremochloa ophiuroides (Munro) Hack. 假儉草
Monogr. Phan. 6: 261. 1889; FKH 321. 1912; FHN 4: 463, fig. 1250. 1977; FFJ 6: 255, fig. 225. 1995; FRPS 10(2): 271, pl. 68: 1–2, 79: 1. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 5: 544, pl. 229. 2000; FOC 22: 645. 2006; FGD 9: 484, fig. 255. 2009.
Ischaemum ophiuroides Munro, Proc. Amer. Acad. Arts 4: 363. 1860; FHK 425. 1861.

Perennial herb, stoloniferous. Culms decumbent, 10–30 cm tall. Leaf sheaths compressed, overlapping at base, hairy at mouth; leaf blades flat, (1–)3–10 × 0.2–0.4 cm, usually glabrous, apex obtuse, terminal absent; ligule 0.2–5 mm, margin ciliate. Raceme terminal, compressed, erect or slightly curved; rachis internodes narrowly oblong-clavate. Sessile spikelet oblong, imbricate in axis along one side; lower glume oblong, ± leathery, glabrous, marginal spines short along incurving lower keels or reduced to knobs, apex acute but appearing broadly truncate because of flanking membranous wings, 5–7-veined; upper glume boat-shaped, thicken membranous, 3-veined; lower floret staminate, lemma membranous, subequal to glume; upper floret bisexual, lemma apex obtuse; style reddish brown. Pedicellate spikelet vestigial or absent; pedicel ± leaf-like, ellipsoidal-subulate.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, New Territories. S. P. Lau 50; HK sheet 40710, 41956.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Hunan, Hubei, Henan, Anhui, Jiangxi, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Moist grassy fields, hillsides. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Oct.

Eremochloa zeylanica (Hack. ex Trimen) Hack. 馬陸草
Monogr. Phan. 6: 263. 1889; FRPS 10(2): 273, pl. 68: 3. 1997; FYN 9: 732. 2003; FOC 22: 646. 2006.
Ischaemum zeylanicum Hack. ex Trimen, Cat. Ceyl. Pl. 107. 1885.

Perennial herb. Culms erect, slender, tufted, 20–60 cm tall. Leaves mostly basal; leaf sheaths mostly imbricate at the base, glabrous; leaf blades linear, (1–)3–15 × 0.1–0.5 cm, glabrous or sparsely pilose, apex rounded, cuspidate; ligule ca. 0.5–1 mm, membranous. Raceme solitary, terminal, flexuous, erect or curved; rachis internodes clavate, with a ring of pilose at the base. Sessile spikelet elliptic, overlapping in one side; lower glume elliptic-ovate, hard papery, glabrous, marginal spines terete, equalling or much longer than glume width flanked by narrow wings, apex acute; upper glume boat-shaped, membranous, 2-keeled, the lower keel with narrow wings; lower floret staminate, lemma oblong, hyaline membranous, acute, 3-veined; palea as long as lemma and narrower; upper floret bisexual, lemma hyaline membranous, truncate. Pedicellate spikelet a very small rudiment; pedicel subulate.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. W. Lam 1333; HK sheet 42004, 42060.
Distribution: W Guangxi, Sichuan, SE Yunnan; Sri Lanka.
Ecology: Open grassy fields.

Eriachne pallescens R. Br. 鷓鴣草
Prodr. 184. 1810; FKH 326. 1912; FHN 4: 371, fig. 1181. 1977; FRPS 9(3): 123, fig. 30: 4–6. 1987; FOC 22: 561. 2006; FGD 9: 341. 2009.

Perennial herb, 20–60 cm tall, with many wiry roots. Culms tufted, erect, sometimes branched from the base, glabrous. Leaf blade 2–10 cm, stiff, usually rolled and needle-like, usually papillose-pilose; ligule ca. 0.5 mm, ciliate; leaf sheaths usually shorter than internodes, ciliate along margins and mouth. Panicle open, 5–10 cm; branches very slender, smooth and glabrous. Spikelets purplish, 4–5.5 mm; glumes ovate-lanceolate, 3–4 mm, glabrous, 9–10-veined; lemmas 3–3.5 mm, densely hispid, apex constricted, bidentate, awned from sinus; awn erect, subequal to lemma body; palea equal to its lemma, dorsally hispid. Anthers 2, 2–2.5 mm. Caryopsis oblong, ca. 2 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. L. T. Lo 562; HK sheet 41944, 41954.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Jiangxi, Fujian; Indochina, Indian Subcontinent, Malay Peninsula, Indonesia, Philippines.

Eriochloa procera (Retz.) C. E. Hubb. 高野黍
Bull. Misc. Inform. Kew 1930: 256. 1930; FHN 4: 423, fig. 1222. 1977; FRPS 10(1): 277, pl. 83: 5–8. 1990; FFJ 6: 219. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 476. 2000; FOC 22: 525. 2006; FGD 9: 425. 2009.
Agrostis procera Retz., Observ. Bot. 4: 19. 1786.
Eriochloa annulata (Flüggé) Kunth, Révis. Gramin 1: 30. 1829; FHK 409. 1861.
Eriochloa ramosa (Retz.) Kuntze, Revis. Gen. Pl. 2: 775. 1891; FKH 313. 1912.

Annual or short-lived perennial herb, 30–150 cm tall. Culms erect or ascending from the geniculate base, usually pubescent at nodes. Leaf blades linear, 8–20 × 0.2–0.8 cm, glabrous, apex acuminate; ligule a fringe of white hairs of ca. 0.6 mm; leaf sheaths keeled, glabrous. Panicle 10–20 cm, composed of several racemes; racemes 3–7 cm, loosely ascending, bare of spikelets proximally, which mostly paired, single toward raceme apex; axis and rachis very slender, puberulous, pedicels usually without setae, those of a pair often partially connate. Spikelets lanceolate, 3–4 mm, herbaceous, sharply acute, basal swelling ca. 0.3 mm and often purplish; lower glume minute; upper glume and lower lemma 5-veined, pilose with appressed silky hairs, lower palea absent; upper lemma rugulose-punctulate, mucro 0.3 – 0.5 mm.

Locality: Sai Kung, Yuen Long. Y. W. Lam 735; HK sheet 39648, 41619.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian, Taiwan; Indochina, Malesia, Indian Subcontinent. Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides. Flowering & fruiting: Summer to autumn.
Uses: Animal food (forage).

Eulalia phaeothrix (Hack.) Kuntze 棕茅
Revis. Gen. Pl. 2: 775. 1891; FHN 4: 454. 1977; FRPS 10(2): 85. 1997; FYN 9: 624. 2003; FOC 22: 587. 2006; FGD 9: 466. 2009.
Pollinia phaeothrix Hack., Monogr. Phan. 6: 168. 1889.

Perennial herb. Culms slender, 0.3–0.8(–1) m tall, white-villous below inflorescence. Leaf sheaths longer or the upper slightly shorter than internode, pilose or glabrescent, basal sheaths woolly with dark reddish brown hairs, finally fibrous; leaf blades narrowly linear, 15–45 × 0.1–0.6 cm, glabrous or pilose, apex acute; ligule 0.5–1 mm, truncate, ciliate. Racemes (1–)2–8, digitate, golden brown or yellowish brown; rachis internodes and pedicels 1/2–2/3 spikelet length, densely ciliate. Sessile spikelet oblong-lanceolate, dark brown; callus hairs 1/8 spikelet length; lower glume papery, oblong-lanceolate, abaxial flat or slightly concave; upper glume boatshaped, apex slightly obtuse, tri-denticulate, pilose along upper margins and keel; lower lemma oblong-lanceolate, slightly shorter than glumes, narrower to the apex, the upper margins ciliate; lower palea absent; upper lemma narrow, 2-lobed nearly to the middle, an awn arising from the sinus; awn 1–2 cm, indistinct 2-geniculate; upper palea absent; stamen 3; anthers 2.5–3 mm. Pedicellate spikelet similar to sessile spikelet.

Locality: Kwun Tong. HK sheet 15177.
Distribution: Hainan, Sichuan, Yunnan; Vietnam, Thailand, S India, Sri Lanka.
Ecology: Grassy hillsides. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Nov.

Eulalia quadrinervis (Hack.) Kuntze 四脈金茅
Revis. Gen. Pl. 2: 775. 1891; FFJ 6: 245, fig. 214. 1995; FRPS 10(2): 89, pl. 19: 1 – 8. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 5: 546. 2000; FOC 22: 587. 2006; FGD 9: 464. 2009.
Pollinia quadrinervis Hack., Monogr. Phan. 6: 158. 1889.

Perennial herb. Culms erect, 80 – 120 cm tall, glabrous or puberulous at nodes. Leaf sheaths glabrous, rarely thinly appressed pilose between veins, the lower longer and the upper shorter than internodes; leaf blades linear, 10–40 × 0.4–0.6 cm, glabrous to tuberculate-villous, abaxial surface glaucous, apex acuminatefiliform, terminal usually absent; ligule 1–1.5 mm, truncate. Racemes 2–7, subdigitate, brown yellow; rachis internodes and pedicels 1/2–2/3 spikelet length, silky villous. Sessile spikelet golden brown, oblong-lanceolate; callus hairs 1/6–1/3 spikelet length; lower glume narrowly elliptic, back slightly concave and villous below middle, 2–4 green veins between keels, connected by veinlets below apex and between lateral veins, upper keels shortly pectinate-ciliate, apex membranous, subacute; upper glume boatshaped, membranous, glabrous, scabrous along keel, apex acute; lower floret usually 1 lemma, oblong-lanceolate, as long as or shorter than glume; upper lemma ovate-oblong, 2-lobed in upper 1/3, with an geniculate awn arising from the sinus; awn 1.2–2 cm; palea oblong-lanceolate; stamens 3. Pedicellate spikelet similar to sessile spikelet, pedicel as long as or slightly shorter than rachis internode.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. L. T. Lo 311, 564; Y. S. Lau 3011.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan, Henan, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Bhutan, Nepal, N India, Myanmar, Thailand, Vietnam, Japan, Korea, Philippines.
Ecology: Hillslopes, open grassy fields. Flowering & fruiting: Sep.–Nov.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Tsing Yi, Lai Chi Chong
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Eulalia speciosa (Debeaux) Kuntze 金茅
Revis. Gen. Pl. 2: 775. 1891; FHN 4: 453. 1977; FFJ 6: 245. 1995; FRPS 10(2): 83, pl. 19: 9 – 12. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 6: 548. 2000; FOC 22: 586. 2006; FGD 9: 465. 2009.
Erianthus speciosus Debeaux, Acta Soc. Linn. Bordeaux 32: 53. 1878.

Perennial herb. Culms stout, to 1 m tall. Basal leaf sheaths with golden brown hairs, finally fibrous; leaf blades linear-lanceolate, 25–50 × 0.4–0.7 cm, adaxially farinose, white pilose at base, otherwise glabrous, apex acuminate; ligule ca. 1 mm, truncate and ciliate. Racemes 4–7(–13) on a 3–4 cm axis, digitate, 10–25 cm, hairs whitish, yellowish or golden brown; rachis internodes and pedicels 2/3 as long to subequaling spikelet, ciliate. Sessile 4.6–5.7 mm, dark brown; callus hairs 1/6-1/3 spikelet length; lower glume narrowly lanceolate-oblong, back concave, villous below middle, veinless between keels, upper keels stiffly ciliate, apex subobtuse; upper lemma narrow, margin pilose, 2-toothed in upper 1/3; awn 1.5–2 cm. Anthers 2.5–3 mm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tsing Yi, Lai Chi Chong. S. Y. Hu 8330, 8472, 11193 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Hubei, Henan, Shandong, Anhui, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; India, SE Asia, Philippines.
Ecology: Hillslopes, grassy fields.

Garnotia acutigluma (Steud.) Ohwi 三芒耳稃草
Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 55: 393. 1941; FTW ed. 2, 5: 429. 2000; FOC 22: 563. 2006; FGD 9: 363. 2009.
Urachne acutigluma Steud., Syn. Pl. Glumac. 1: 121. 1854.
Garnotia triseta Hitchc., Lingnan Sci. J. 7: 200. 1931; FRPS 10(1): 139. 1990; FFJ 6: 182. 1995; Check List HK Plants 337. 2002; 118. 2004.

Perennial, tufted herb. Culms glabrous, 20–60 cm tall, nodes pubescent. Leaf sheaths longer than internodes, usually with a ring of stiff hairs along mouth and the membranous margins, otherwise glabrous; leaf blades linear to narrowly lanceolate, flat or folded, 5–20(–35) × 0.2–0.7 cm, adaxial surface hispid or scabrid, hairs tubercle-based or not, abaxial surface usually glabrous; ligule membranous, 0.2–0.5 mm. Panicle narrow, branches appressed or loosely erect or ascending, slightly scabrous; spikelets in threes at lower nodes, paired or solitary toward apex. Spikelets narrow lanceolate, 3–5 mm, base usually conspicuously pilose, pedicels slightly scabrous; glumes narrow lanceolate, subequal, membranous, scabrid on veins, apex acute to awned; lemma lanceolate, as long as glume, papery, smooth, 1–3-veined, acuminate and awned; awn slender, slightly scabrous, slightly flexuous, 8–15 mm; palea elliptic, slightly shorter than lemma, membranous, margins ciliate, 2-veined; lodicules 2, small, cuneate, emarginate, smooth.

Locality: Hong Kong (fide FGD 9: 363. 2009).
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; widespread over India, Myanmar, Vietnam through Indonesia, Malay Peninsula to Indonesia and Philippines.
Ecology: Moist mountain slopes and shady places along streams. Flowering & fruiting: Sep.–Oct.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Ma On Shan, Fo Tan, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Garnotia patula (Munro) Benth. 耳稃草（葛氏草）
FHK 416. 1861; FKH 317. 1912; FRPS 10(1): 140. 1990; FFJ 6: 182, fig. 149. 1995; FOC 22: 563. 2006; FGD 9: 363, fig. 175. 2009.
Berghausia patula Munro, Amer. Acad. Arts 4: 362. 1860.

Perennial herb. Culms erect, tufted, 60–130 cm tall, glabrous, nodes pubescent. Leaf sheaths keeled, longer than internode, glabrous or thinly pilose; leaf blades linear or linear-lanceolate, 15–60 × 0.4–1.2 cm, glabrous to sparsely pilose, sometimes with tubercle-based hairs, margins slightly scabrous; ligule membranous, 2–5 mm, ciliate. Panicle open, 15–40(–60) cm; branches stiff and very spreading, up to 12 cm. Spikelets narrow lanceolate, 4–4.5 mm, base shortly pubescent; glumes awned; awn of lower glume 2–8 mm; lemma as long as glume, glabrous, 3-veined, apex acuminate, awned; awn 7–15 mm, very slender.

Locality: Ma On Shan, Fo Tan, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 3094; Y. W. Lam 1240; HK sheet 42038.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian; E Myanmar, N Vietnam.
Ecology: Margins of forests, moist grassy slopes. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Oct.
Notes: The type specimen was collected by C. Wright from Hong Kong Island between 1853 and 1856.

Garnotia patula (Munro) Benth. var. mutica (Munro) Rendle 無芒耳稃草
J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 36: 387. 1904; FOC 22: 563. 2006; FGD 9: 364. 2009.
Berghausia mutica Munro, Proc. Amer. Acad. Arts 4: 362. 1864.
Garnotia mutica (Munro) Druce, Bot. Exch. Club Soc. Brit. Isles 4: 624. 1917; FRPS 10(1): 136, pl. 42: 1–4. 1990; Check List HK Plants 336. 2002; 118. 2004.
Garnotia stricta auct. non Brongn.: FHK 416. 1861.

Culms 30–100 cm tall. Glumes acuminate or lower glume with a mucro; lemma acuminate, awnless or with a mucro to 1.5 mm.

Locality: No precise locality. C. Wright s.n. (K).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; E Myanmar, N Vietnam.
Ecology: Margins of moist woodlands, streamsides. Flowering & fruiting: Sep.–Oct.
Notes: The type specimen was collected by C. Wright from Hong Kong Island between 1853 and 1856.

Gigantochloa atroviolacea Widjaja 黑毛巨竹
Reinwardtia 10(3): 323. 1987.
Gigantochloa nigrociliata auct. non (Buse) Kurz: HKB 62. 1985; FRPS 9(1): 197, pl. 50: 12 – 14. 1996; FOC 22: 47. 2006; FGD 9: 274. 2009; Check List HK Plants 337. 2002; 118. 2004.

Culms 8–15 m, 4–10 cm in diam.; internodes 36–46 cm, yellow striate, brown hispid; wall thick. Branches several, central ones prominent. Culm sheaths deciduous, brown, 18–22 cm, leathery, densely dark brown hispid; auricles minute; ligule ca. 4 mm, serrulate; blade recurved. Ultimate branches with ca. 11 leaves. Leaf sheath initially sparsely pubescent; ligule ca. 1 mm; blade 19–36 × 3–5 cm. Pseudospikelets in heads ca. 2.5 cm in diam. Spikelets 1–1.2 × 0.2–0.3 cm; florets 2. Glumes 2–3, ovate, dark brown ciliate; lemma margins dark brown ciliate; palea shorter than lemma. Anthers yellow. Ovary ovoid; style 6–7 mm; stigma 1. Caryopsis unknown.

Locality: HKU campus, Tsiu Hang (cultivated). P. S. Choi 268; Nan-Zhu 2844.
Distribution: Indonesia.
Ecology: New shoots: Summer.
Uses: Ornamental.

Gigantochloa verticillata (Willd.) Munro 花巨竹
Trans. Linn. Soc. London. 26: 123. 1868; FRPS 9(1): 200. 1996; FOC 22: 47. 2006; FGD 9: 275. 2009.
Bambusa verticillata Willd., Sp. Pl. 2: 245. 1799.
Arundo maxima Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 1: 58. 1790, nom. illeg. hom.
Bambusa maxima (Lour.) Poir., Encycl., Suppl. 8: 704. 1808, nom. Illeg.
Bambusa pseudoarundinacea Steud., Syn. Pl. Glumac. 1: 330. 1854.
Gigantochloa maxima (Lour.) Kurz, Natuurk. Tijdschr. Ned.-Indië 27: 226. 1864, nom. illeg.; HKB 61. 1985.
Gigantochloa pseudoarundinacea (Steud.) Widjaja, Reinwardtia 10(3): 305. 1987; Check List HK Plants 337. 2002; 118. 2004.

Culms 8–15 m, 7–10 cm in diam.; internodes yellow striate, 28–42 cm, white or brown hispid; wall ca. 1.6 cm thick. Branches several, central dominant. Culm sheaths deciduous, green, yellow striate initially, later brown, leathery, initially densely white hispid, margins ciliate; auricles minute, inconspicuous; oral setae absent; ligule ca. 3 mm, irregularly serrate or fimbriate; blade reflexed. Leaf sheath initially pubescent; ligule 5–10 mm, entire; blade 24–47 × 3.5–7 cm. Inflorescence unknown.

Locality: Cultivated. P. S. Choi 270; Nan-Zhu 2868.
Distribution: S Yunnan; India, Indonesia, Malaysia, Myanmar, Thailand, Vietnam.
Ecology: New shoots: Summer to early autumn.
Uses: Ornamental.

Hackelochloa granularis (L.) Kuntze 球穗草
Revis. Gen. Pl. 2: 776. 1891; FHN 4: 465, fig. 1252. 1977; FFJ 6: 257, fig. 227. 1995; FRPS 10(2): 278, pl. 70: 1–3, 79: 2. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 5: 549, pl. 231. 2000; FOC 22: 647. 2006; FGD 9: 485, fig. 256. 2009.
Cenchrus granularis L., Mant. Pl. 2: 575. 1771.

Annual herb. Culms tufted, erect, branched, 20–60(–100) cm tall, glabrous or sparsely hispid. Leaf sheaths loose, usually shorter than internode, papillose-hispid; leaf blades linear-lanceolate, 5–20 × 0.4–1 cm, coarsely hispid, base ± cordate, apex subacute; ligule ca. 1 mm, membranous, margins ciliate. Racemes lower part usually included in terminal sheaths, rachis-joint and pedicel grown together. Sessile spikelet hemispherical, usually cream-coloured at maturity; lower glume leathery, hemispherical, coarsely reticulate-rugose, pits shallow and separated by broad rounded ribs; upper glume thicken membranous, hyaline, appressed to the cavity formed by rachis-joint and pedicel, 3-veined; lower lemma hyaline; upper lemma hyaline; stamens 3. Pedicellate spikelet ovate, glumes with prominent green veins and whitish wings.

Locality: Fanling, Po Toi Islands. Y. W. Lam 1047; HK sheet 15312.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; spread throughout the tropics.
Ecology: Farmlands, open grassy places. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Oct.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Aberdeen, Shing Mun, Sai Kung, Wu Kau Tang
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Hemarthria compressa (L. f.) R. Br. 扁穗牛鞭草
Prodr. 207. 1810; FHN 4: 464, fig. 1251. 1977; FFJ 6: 255, fig. 224. 1995; FRPS 10(2): 262, pl. 65: 4–6. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 5: 551, pl. 232. 2000; FOC 22: 642. 2006; FGD 9: 480, fig. 251. 2009.
Rottboellia compressa L. f., Suppl. Pl. 114. 1782 ["1781"]; FKH 321. 1912.
Hemarthria fasciculata auct. non (Lam.) Kunth: FHK 418. 1861.

Perennial herb, with horizontal rhizomes. Culms erect, 60–150 cm. Leaf sheaths glabrous or hairy along mouth, often shorter than internode; leaf blades linear, 2–15 × 0.2–0.5 cm, glabrous, base rounded, margins scabrous; ligule 0.3–1 mm. Racemes solitary or few per node, sometimes several aggregated. Sessile spikelet sunken in a cavity formed by the adnation of the rachis and the pedicel, long ovate, with a distinct callus of 1–2 mm; lower glume ovate-lanceolate, leathery, flat or subconvex on abaxial surface, marginally keeled, apex acute or slightly obtuse; upper glume boat-shaped, adnate to rachis, equalling lower glume; lower floret absent to lemma; upper floret bisexual, lemma hyaline membranous. Pedicellate spikelet lanceolate, as long as or slightly longer than sessile spikelet, lower glume ovate-lanceolate, herbaceous; upper glume boat-shaped, completely adnate to rachis cavity, acuminate-caudate.

Locality: Aberdeen, Shing Mun, Sai Kung, Wu Kau Tang. Y. S. Lau 2281; Y. W. Lam 892, 2177.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Nei Mongol, Fujian, Taiwan; Indian Subcontinent, Indochina, Malay Peninsula, SW Asia (Iraq).
Ecology: Farmlands and other wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Sep.

Heteropogon contortus (L.) P. Beauv. ex Roem. & Schult. 黃茅
Syst. Veg. 2: 836. 1817; FKH 322. 1912; FHN 4: 483, fig. 1268. 1977; FFJ 6: 269, fig. 242. 1995; FRPS 10(2): 240, pl. 60: 1–12. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 5: 551, pl. 233. 2000; FOC 22: 638. 2006; FGD 9: 503, fig. 267. 2009.
Andropogon contortus L., Sp. Pl. 2: 1045. 1753.
Heteropogon hirtus Pers., Syn. Pl. 2: 533. 1807; FHK 424. 1861.

Perennial herb. Culms slender, tufted, usually geniculate at base, glabrous, 20–100 cm tall. Leaf sheaths keeled, longer than the internode, pilose at mouth; leaf blades flat or folded, 10–30 × 0.3–0.6 cm, scabrid or adaxial surface pilose at base; ligule short, membranous, ciliate, truncate. Racemes 3–6(–10) cm, mostly long exserted, solitary or aggregated into a scanty false panicle, the awns forming a twisted spire. Spikelets paired, basal 3–10 spikelets imbricate, sterile, persistent, awnless; upper 7–12 spikelets paired, heterogamous, 1 pedicellate, other sessile. Sessile spikelet ca. 7 mm, bisexual; callus fiercely pungent, acute and pungent, brown bearded; lower glume narrow oblong, hispidulous, abaxially rounded, apex obtuse, margins embraced same texture upper glume; upper glume narrow, 2-veined, hispidulous between veins, apex obtuse, margins membranous; lower lemma oblong; upper lemma membranous, very narrow, apex tipped with a geniculate awn of 6–10 cm long, column twisted and hairy, dark brown, column white-hirtellous, tips of successive awns often twisting together; stamens 3. Pedicellate spikelet oblong-lanceolate, barren.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. W. Lam 802, 987; K. L. Yip 4382.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Gansu, Shaanxi, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; tropics and subtropics of the world, extending to Mediterranean and other warm-temperate areas.
Ecology: Grassy hillslopes, roadsides. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Dec.

Hymenachne amplexicaulis (Rudge) Nees 膜稃草
Fl. Bras. Enum. Pl. 2: 276. 1829; FOC 22: 510. 2006; FGD 9: 430. 2009.
Panicum amplexicaule Rudge, Pl. Guian. 1: 21. 1805;
Hymenachne acutigluma (Steud.) Gilliland, Gard. Bull. Sing. 20: 314. 1964; FRPS 10(1): 298, pl. 92: 1–5. 1990; FYN 9: 501. 2003; Check List HK Plants 338. 2002; 118. 2004.
Hymenachne pseudointerrupta C. Muell., Bot. Zeit. 19: 333. 1861; FTW ed. 2, 5: 478, pl. 199. 2000.

Perennial herb. Culms spongy, creeping and rooting at the base, up to 1 m tall, many-noded, glabrous. Leaf sheath slightly shorter than internode, nodes pubescent. Leaf blades broadly linear, thick, 30–40 × ca. 2 cm, glabrous or the adaxial surface and margins loosely tuberculate-hairy, base rounded and slightly clasping, apex acuminate; ligule membranous, 1–2 mm. Panicle 20–40 × 1–2 cm; spike-like, branches 0.5–2 cm, erect, appressed; rachis winged, fasciculate spikelets in one side; pedicels very short, scabrous. Spikelets narrowly lanceolate, 3.5–5 mm; lower glume ovate, ca. 1.5 mm, membranous, 1-veined; upper glume and lower lemma lanceolate, 3–4 mm, herbaceous, apex with 0.5–2 mm awn; upper lemma ca. 3 mm, membranous, acuminate; palea 2, mucronate; anthers ca. 1 mm. Caryopsis ca. 1.5 mm, apex rounded.

Locality: Hong Kong. HK sheet 33914.
Distribution: Hainan, Yunnan, Taiwan; India, Thailand, Myanmar, Vietnam, Malay Peninsula, Philippines.
Ecology: Ponds and marshes in shallow water. Flowering & fruiting: Summer to autumn.

Hyparrhenia diplandra (Hack.) Stapf 短梗苞茅
Fl. Trop. Africa. 9: 368. 1919; FRPS 10(2): 235, pl. 58: 4. 1997; FYN 9: 705. 2003; FOC 22: 633. 2006; FGD 9: 501. 2009.
Andropogon diplandrus Hack., Flora 68: 123. 1855.
Hyparrhenia eberhardtii (A. Camus) Hitchc., Lingnan Sci. J. 7: 247 – 248. 1929[1931]; FHN 4: 482, fig. 1226. 1977.

Perennial herb. Culms tufted, coarse, 1–2 m tall. Leaf sheaths glabrous or upper margins hispidulous; leaf blades linear to narrowly linear, 30–60 × 0.3–0.6 cm, glabrous or hirsute at base, margins scabrid; ligule reddish brown, ca. 2 mm, dry membranous, apex obtuse and rounded, ciliate. Spathate panicle loose, peduncle scarcely exserted from spatheole, densely golden tuberculatehirtose; racemes 4–8-awned per pair, reflexed at maturity; raceme bases subequal, flattened, short, broadly oblong, glabrous on outer face; usually 2 pairs of homogamous spikelets at base of both lower and upper raceme of pair; pedicel longer than rachis internodes, ca. 1/2 length of sessile spikelet. Sessile spikelet lanceolate, glabrous or pilose, callus acute and pungent, densely bearded; callus 1–1.5 mm, sharply acute, white bearded; lower glume lanceolate, margins inrolled, obtuse; upper glume slightly longer than lower glume, boat-shaped, apex rounded and obtuse, 3-veined; lower lemma lanceolate, hyaline membranous, ciliate; upper lemma linear, 2-lobed; awn geniculate, column with white or brown ca. 0.5 mm hairs; palea absent; stamens 3 or absent. Pedicellate spikelet narrow, staminate or barren.

Locality: Castle Peak. HK sheet 15837.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; Vietnam, Thailand, Indonesia, tropical Africa.
Ecology: Hillslopes, thickets. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Nov.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Victoria Peak, Tai Mo Shan, Tseng Lan Shue, Tai Po Kau, Lantau Peak
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Ichnanthus pallens (Sw.) Munro ex Benth. var. major (Nees) Stieber 大距花黍（距花黍）
Syst. Bot. 12: 207. 1987; FHK 414. 1861; FKH 316. 1912; FOC 22: 504. 2006; FGD 9: 407, fig. 208. 2009.
Panicum pallens Swartz var. majus Nees, Fl. Bras. Enum. Pl. 2: 138. 1829.
Ichnanthus vicinus (F. M. Bailey) Merr., FHN 4: 408, fig. 1212. 1977; FRPS 10(1): 219, pl. 66. 1990; FFJ 6: 208, fig. 176. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 480, pl. 200. 2000; Check List HK Plants 338. 2002; 118. 2004.

Perennial herb. Culms slender, prostrate and rooting at the lower nodes. Leaf sheaths usually shorter than internode, pubescent or only ciliate; leaf blades ovate-lanceolate, flat, 3–9 × 1–2.5 cm, glabrous or puberulous on both surfaces, base asymmetrically cordate, apex acute or acuminate; ligule ca. 1 mm, a ciliate membrane. Panicles terminal and axillary from upper nodes, 5–15 cm; usually with soft hairs in the axils; branches spaced, loosely ascending, subracemose with laxly arranged spikelets. Spikelets lanceolate, 3–5 mm, laterally compressed; glumes open at maturity; lower glume 3–3.5 mm, 3-veined; upper glume equal to lower glume, 5-veined, acuminate; lower lemma herbaceous, 5-veined; lower palea elliptic, narrow, small, membranous, sometimes inrolled embraced stamens; upper lemma oblong, 2–2.5 mm, leathery, scars at base, obtuse.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Tai Mo Shan, Tseng Lan Shue, Tai Po Kau, Lantau Peak. L. T. 298; Y. W. Lam 380; HK sheet 41991.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; widely spread over tropical Asia, W Africa, Australia (Queensland), Pacific islands (Polynesia) and S America.
Ecology: Moist places of hillslopes and grasslands. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Nov.

Imperata cylindrica (L.) Raeusch. var. major (Nees) C. E. Hubb. 大白茅（絲茅）
Grass. of Mauritius & Rodriguez 96. 1940; FHN 4: 446. 1977; FFJ 6: 239, fig. 206. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 554, pl. 234, photo 61. 2000; FOC 22: 584. 2006; FGD 9: 455, fig. 236. 2009.
Imperata koenigii (Retz.) P. Beauv. var. major Nees, Fl. Afr. Austral. Ill. 90. 1841.
Imperata koenigii (Retz.) P. Beauv., Ess. Agrostogr. 165. 1812; FRPS 10(2): 32, pl. 7: 1–8. 1997; Check List HK Plants 338. 2002; 118. 2004.
Imperata arundinacea Cirillo var. koenigii (Retz.) Benth., FHK 419. 1861.

Perennial herb; rhizomes long-spreading, white, articulate. Culms erect, 30–90 cm tall, nodes often bearded. Leaf sheaths glabrous or pilose at margin and mouth, basal fibrous; leaf blades flat, stiffly erect, 15–60 × 0.5–0.9 cm, adaxial surface puberulous, base narrowed, apex hard, spiny, margins scabrid; ligule ca. 1 mm. Panicle cylindrical, copiously hairy, 5–20 × 1.5–3 cm. Spikelets lanceolate or oblong, 2.5–4 mm; callus with 10–15 mm silky hairs; glumes 3–6-veined, back with long silky hairs ca. 3 times glume length, apex slightly obtuse or acuminate; lower lemma ovate-lanceolate, 2/3 length of glumes, ciliate, acute or denticulate; upper lemma ovate, 1/2 length of glumes, denticulate, ciliate, palea equal to lemma. Anthers 2–3 mm. Stigmas purplish black.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. P. P. H. But 19; Y. S. Lau 1921; S. P. Lau 29.
Distribution: Widely spread over all provinces of China; warm and temperate parts of Asia, and extending to Australia, E and S Africa.
Ecology: Wastelands, disturbed lands, open grassy places, forming extensive colonies.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Victoria Peak, Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Indocalamus herklotsii McClure 粽巴箬竹（光籜箬竹）
Lingnan Univ. Sci. Bull. 9: 22. 1940; HKB 63. 1985; FRPS 9(1): 686, pl. 210: 5–6. 1996; FOC 22: 137. 2006; FGD 9: 304. 2009.

Culms to 2 m, 3–6 mm in diam.; internodes glossy, glabrous, subsolid, with small lumen; nodes flat. Culm sheaths leathery, glossy, fragile, margins usually densely ciliate; auricles absent or minute; oral setae sometimes developed, few, dark brown, rigid, scabrid; ligule truncate or slightly arcuate, very short, hirtellous, ciliolate; blade erect, initially rosy red, ovate-lanceolate, thinly papery, glabrous, base broad and amplexicaul, apex long acuminate.
