Leaves ca. 3 per ultimate branch; sheath obscurely striate on upper part, margins densely brown ciliate; auricles usually absent; oral setae few or absent, dark brown or straw-coloured, rigid, scabrid; ligule short, hirtellous, ciliolate; pseudopetiole 1–4 mm, hirtellous toward apex; blade lanceolate or oblong-lanceolate, 14–29 × 1–5 cm, glabrous, secondary veins 6–9 pairs, tessellations rectangular, apex caudate. Panicle spreading, purple, 7–8 cm; peduncle to 8.5 cm, glabrous, axis and branches slender, glabrous. Spikelets oblong-lanceolate, to 1.5 cm, slightly compressed; pedicels 3–15 cm, pulvinate; florets ca. 4. Rachilla internodes glabrous on side facing floret, otherwise scabrous. Glumes 2, glabrous; lower glume 5–5.5 mm, apex obtuse; upper glume 6.5–8 mm, apex acute; lemma lanceolate, 6.5(–7) mm, thinly papery, fragile, glabrous, 5-veined, apex obtuse; palea slightly longer or sometimes shorter than lemma, glabrous, keels distally ciliate; lodicules transparent, anterior ca. 1.3 mm, posterior slightly longer. Anthers ca. 5 mm. Ovary fusiform, dorsi-ventrally compressed, subglabrous; stigmas 2.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan, Lantau Island. HK sheet 42220.
Distribution: Hong Kong.
Ecology: Open forests, thickets.
Notes: The type specimen (F. A. McClure 20838, US) was collected from Lantau Island between 5–13 Oct. 1938. It was named after G. A. C. Herklots (1902 – 1986), local naturalist, and Secretary for Development (who was considered former head of AFCD) after World War II, who invited F. A. McClure to study bamboos in Hong Kong in the late 1930s.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Mo Shan, Lam Tsuen Valley
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Indocalamus longiauritus Hand.-Mazz. 箬葉竹
Anz. Akad. Wiss. Wien, Math.-Naturwiss. Kl. 62: 254. 1925; HKB 64. 1985; FRPS 9(1): 695, pl. 213: 1–7. 1996; FOC 22: 138. 2006; FGD 9: 304, fig. 144. 2009.
Arundinaria longiaurita (Hand.-Mazz.) Hand.-Mazz., Symb. Sin. 7: 1271. 1936.

Culms 0.8–1 m, 0.35–0.8 cm in diam.; internodes dull green, (8–)10–55 cm, white pubescent, with a pale red-brown tomentose ring below nodes; wall 1.5–2 mm thick; nodes prominent. Culm sheaths purple-green, leathery, dark brown strigose and white tomentose, base with raised corky ring; auricles well developed, narrowly falcate, long, purple-green, becoming brown when dry; oral setae radiate, brown, ca. 1 cm; ligule truncate, 0.5–1 mm, ciliate or not; blade purple-green, narrowly triangular to ovate-lanceolate, base abruptly rounded, apex acuminate. Leaf sheath rigid, glabrous or abaxially initially finely strigose, outer margin ciliate; auricles usually developed; oral setae radiate, brown; ligule truncate, 1–1.5 mm, puberulent, fimbriate, margin setose; blade 10–35 × 1.5–6.5 cm, abaxially glabrous, secondary veins 5–12 pairs, veins forming rectangular tessellations, base cuneate, apex long acuminate. Panicles 8–15 cm, rather narrow, axis densely white tomentose. Spikelets greenish or straw-coloured at maturity, 1.5–3.7 cm; florets 4–6. Rachilla internodes compressed-clavate, 6.8–7.2 mm, angular, densely white tomentose, apex truncate. Glumes 2, acuminate with an awn-like point; 1st glume 3–5 mm, 3–5-veined, 2nd glume 6–8 mm, 7–9-veined; lemma oblong-lanceolate, apex awn-like, first lemma 1–1.4 cm, 11–13-veined; palea of 1st floret 0.7 – 1 cm, keels ciliate. Anthers ca. 5 mm. Stigmas 2. Caryopsis oblong.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Lam Tsuen Valley. HK sheet 41768.
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Henan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Sichuan.
Ecology: Mountain slopes, hillsides, roadsides. New shoots: Apr.–May; flowering: May–Jul.

Indocalamus sinicus (Hance) Nakai 水銀竹（華箬竹）
J. Arnold Arbor. 6: 148. 1925; HKB 65. 1985; FRPS 9(1): 692, pl. 212: 1–7. 1996; FOC 22: 136. 2006; FGD 9: 305. 2009.
Arundinaria sinica Hance, Ann. Sci. Nat., Bot., sér. 4, 18: 235. 1862.
Arundinaria longiramea Munro, Trans. Linn. Soc. 26: 19. 1868.
Arundinaria wightii Nees ex Benth., FHK 434. 1861.

Culms 1–3.8 m, 0.5–1 cm in diam.; internodes green, straw-coloured when dry, glossy, glabrous; wall 3–4 mm thick; nodes flat. Culm sheaths purple-brown, leathery-papery, striate, sparsely white or colourless hairy, margins densely bright grey ciliate; auricles absent; oral setae several, to 1 cm; ligule red-brown, truncate, 1–1.4 mm, ciliate or not; blade erect to reflexed, narrowly triangular-subulate on midculm sheaths, ovate-lanceolate on upper ones, apex long acuminate. Leaves 7–14 per ultimate branch; sheath yellow-brown, leathery, glossy, glabrous; auricles absent; oral setae yellow-brown, to 1.6 cm; ligule red-brown, truncate, short, ciliolate or not; blade broadly lanceolate, 14–60 × 2.2–6.8 cm, thinly leathery, both surfaces usually glabrous, secondary veins 8–9 pairs, transverse veins sparse, tessellations narrowly rectangular, base cuneate, apex long acuminate. Panicles ample, 23.5–30 cm or more; branches spreading, pulvinate. Spikelets purple-green, pedicel 2–6 cm; florets 3–4. Rachilla internodes glabrous. Glumes 2, papery; lower glume oblong-lanceolate, 4.5–5 mm, 3-veined, apex slightly acute, upper glume 5–6.5 mm, 5-veined, apex acuminate; lemma 9–10 mm, papery, adaxially scabrid, 7-veined, apex acuminate; palea nearly as long as lemma, keels and apex ciliate; lodicules unequal in size, anterior pair larger. Stamens unknown. Style short; stigmas 2.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. L. T. Lo 563; Y. S. Lau 2975; N. K. Chan 2798.
Distribution: Guangdong, Hainan.
Ecology: Open forests, thickets on hills and in valleys, alt. 600–700 m. New shoots: Apr.; flowering: May.
Notes: Bentham's A. wightii (FHK 434. 1861) is merely an orthographical variant of A. wightiana Nees. (Linnaea 9: 482. 1835). In FHK, “A. Wightii, Nees” is cited from Ruprecht, Bambuseae, 26. 1839, which in turn cites “A. WIGHTIANA NE 1834”, i.e. A. wightiana Nees. Bentham misapplied the name described from "Peninsula Indiae orientalis" to a specimen from Hong Kong, while at the same time describing Indian plants.

Isachne albens Trin. 白花柳葉箬
Sp. Gram. 1(8): t. 85. 1828; FRPS 10(1): 185. 1990; FFJ 6: 169, fig. 138. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 448. 2000; FOC 22: 559. 2006; FGD 9: 370. 2009.

Perennial herb. Culms slender, erect or decumbent at base, tufted, 30–100 cm tall, branching and rooting at basal nodes. Leaf sheaths usually shorter than the internode, with ciliate margins; leaf blades firm, narrowly lanceolate, 7–15 × 0.8–1.8 cm, abaxial surface glabrous, adaxial surface glabrous to hispidulous, margins thickened; ligule 1–2 mm, a row of hairs. Panicle pyramidal, 10–20 cm; branchlets and pedicels without glandular bands. Spikelets whitish green, elliptic-globose, 1–1.5 mm; florets similar, lower floret usually bisexual, upper floret usually female; glumes herbaceous, subequal to spikelet, usually glabrous, occasionally with a few stiff bristles above middle, obtuse, 5–7(–9)-veined; lower lemma globose to elliptic-ovate, leathery, puberulous or subglabrous, obtuse. Caryopsis elliptic.

Locality: Hong Kong (fide Corlett et al. 2000).
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Fujian, Taiwan; Bhutan, Nepal, N India, Myanmar, Thailand, Vietnam, Philippines, Indonesia.
Ecology: Hillsides, margins of forests, other moist open grassy fields. Flowering & fruiting: Summer to autumn.

Isachne globosa (Thunb. ex Murray) Kuntze 柳葉箬
Revis. Gen. Pl. 2: 778. 1891; FHN 4: 401, fig. 1029. 1977; FRPS 10(1): 188. 1990; FFJ 6: 171, fig. 139. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 448, pl. 185. 2000; FOC 22: 555. 2006; FGD 9: 371, fig. 180. 2009.
Milium globosum Thunb. ex Murray, Syst. Veg., ed. 14, 109. 1784.
Isachne australis R. Br., Prod. 1: 196. 1810; FHK 414. 1861; FKH 313. 1912.

Perennial herb. Culms rather slender, tufted, decumbent, creeping and rooting at the lower nodes, ascending to 80 cm tall or more, nodes glabrous. Leaf sheaths shorter than internode, ciliate on margins; leaf blades narrowly lanceolate, 3–10 × 0.4–0.8 cm, very rough with a minute pubescence, base rounded or slightly cordate; ligule 1–2 mm, a ring of hairs ciliate. Panicle open, ovoid, spreading, 4–11 cm, rather loose; pedicels variable in length, shorter or longer than spikelets, mostly marked with a pellucid discoloration or gland. Spikelets greenish or purplish brown, elliptic-globose, 1.5–2 mm; outer glumes glabrous; lower floret usually male, with a glabrous glume, upper floret female, pubescent; lower lemma oblong, soft texture, glabrous; upper lemma abaxial glabrous or puberulous, upper margins ciliate; lodicules cuneate, truncate and emarginate. Caryopsis subglobose.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. W. Lam 1687, 2239; HK sheet 41607.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Hebei, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Shandong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; widely spread over Nepal, India, Malay Peninsula to Indonesia, New Guinea, Philippines, and northward to Japan and Korea.
Ecology: Moist places of grasslands, path between paddy fields. Flowering & fruiting: Summer to autumn.

Isachne myosotis Nees 荏弱柳葉箬
Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 2: 98. 1850; FHK 415. 1861; FTW ed. 2, 5: 449, pl. 187. 2000; FOC 22: 558. 2006.
Isachne debilis Rendle, J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 36: 322. 1904; FRPS 10(1): 179, pl. 56: 11–14. 1990; FFJ 6: 168. 1995.
Isachne firmula Büse, Pl. Jungh. 3: 39. 1854; FKH 313. 1912; Check List HK Plants 338. 2002; 118. 2004.

Annual herb. Culms slender, decumbent, branching and rooting at nodes, flowering branches up to 10 cm tall. Leaf sheaths less than 1/2 length of the internode, thinly to densely hispid with spreading hairs, or hairs confined to margins; leaf blades ovatelanceolate, 1–3 × 0.2–0.5 cm, rough, ± appressed-hairy on both surfaces, base rounded, apex acute; ligule a ring of hairs. Panicle ovate or contracted, 1.5 – 5 cm; branches spiculate to base, with short stiff branchlets and pedicels, smooth. Spikelets tinged purplish, subglobose, 1–1.5 mm; florets similar; glumes equal to spikelet, separated by a short internode, ovate-oblong, 5–7-veined, hispid, usually with a few stiff hairs toward the apex, obtuse; lemmas strongly convex, leathery, puberulous to densely pubescent.

Locality: Kam Shan, Tai Mo Shan. L. T. Lo 226; HK sheet 14969, 35873.
Distribution: Guangdong, Fujian, Taiwan; Philippines, Indonesia to New Guinea.
Ecology: Moist grassy fields. Flowering & fruiting: May–Oct.

Ischaemum aristatum L. 有芒鴨嘴草
Sp. Pl. 2: 1049. 1753; FKH 322. 1912; FHN 4: 460. 1977; FFJ 6: 252, fig. 221. 1995; FRPS 10(2): 163, pl. 38: 10–13. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 5: 557, pl. 235. 2000; FOC 22: 610. 2006; FGD 9: 474. 2009.
Ischaemum barbatum auct. non Retz.: FHK 425. 1861.

Perennial herb. Culms loosely tufted, ascending or branched, 40–90 cm tall, glabrous or bearded. Leaf sheaths glabrous or pilose, shorter than internode except the base, sometimes long-ciliate near mouth; leaf blades linear-lanceolate, 5–25 × 0.4–1 cm, glabrous or thinly pilose, apex acuminate, margins scabrous; ligule membranous, 2–3 mm. Racemes terminal, paired, appressed back to back, long exserted from uppermost sheath; rachis internodes clavate, triquetrous, scabrid or ciliate along outer angle. Sessile spikelet lanceolate; lower glume obtuse or slightly 2-toothed, broader and 2-keeled above, keels narrowly to broadly winged, wing margin scabrous, 5–7-veined; upper glume boat-shaped, as long as lower glume, keeled, margins ciliate, apex acute; lower floret staminate, slightly shorter than glume; lemma papery, acute, obscurely 3-veined; palea membranous, 2-keeled; upper floret bisexual, lemma 2-cleft to the middle, with a geniculate awn from sinus, exserted from spikelet; palea as long as or slightly shorter than lemma; stamens 3; style free. Pedicellate spikelet dorsally compressed, similar to sessile.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. S. L. Thrower s.n.; S. Y. Hu & P. P. H. But 20878, 22741 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Liaoning, Hebei, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Shandong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Korea, Vietnam.
Ecology: Open grassy sandy places. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Oct.

Ischaemum aristatum L. var. glaucum (Honda) T. Koyama 鴨嘴草
J. Jap. Bot. 37: 239. 1962; FFJ 6: 253. 1995; FRPS 10(2): 163. 1997; FOC 22: 611. 2006; FGD 9: 475. 2009.
Ischaemum crassipes (steud.) Thell. var. glaucum Honda, J. Fac. Sci. Univ. Tokyo, Sect. 3, Bot. 3: 355. 1930.

Rachis internodes and pedicels scabrid or shortly ciliate on outer angle, inner angles glabrous or shortly ciliate. Sessile spikelet oblanceolate, narrowly to broadly winged, mucronate or shortly awned; awn included within spikelet.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. HK sheet 32262.
Distribution: S Anhui, Hebei, Jiangsu, Liaoning, Shandong, Zhejiang; Japan, Korea, Vietnam.
Ecology: Sandy places, usually near the sea.

Ischaemum barbatum Retz. 粗毛鴨嘴草
Observ. Bot. 6: 35. 1791; FHN 4: 460. 1977; FFJ 6: 253, fig. 222. 1995; FRPS 10(2): 156, pl. 37: 6 – 11. 1997; FOC 22: 613. 2006; FGD 9: 474. 2009.

Perennial herb. Culms erect or ascending, 30–100 cm tall. Leaf sheaths glabrous to villous; leaf blades linear or narrowly lanceolate, 5–30 × 0.3–0.8 cm, apex acute; ligule 1–5 mm. Racemes terminal, paired, usually appressed back to back; rachis internodes oblong, triquetrous, ciliate along outer angle, inner angles glabrous or shortly ciliate. Sessile spikelet lanceolate-oblong, callus bearded; lower glume leathery, herbaceous above with many anastomosing green veins, glabrous to villous, marginal nodules at lower 2/3, these sometimes extended into weak transverse ridges, 2-keeled, keels asymmetrically winged, one wing wider than the other; upper glume as long as lower glume, hard papery; lower floret staminate, lemma boat-shaped, 1-veined; upper floret bisexual, lemma hyaline membranous, 2-deeply-clefted, with a geniculate awn from sinus; palea slightly shorter than lemma. Pedicellate spikelet dorsally compressed, as large as sessile but marginal nodules less developed, awnless or awned.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. W. Lam 817, 2174; HK sheet 40833.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Indian Subcontinent, Indochina, Malesia, Australia, W Africa.
Ecology: Open grassy hillslopes. Flowering & fruiting: Summer and autumn.

Ischaemum ciliare Retz. 細毛鴨嘴草
Observ. Bot. 6: 36. 1791; FKH 322. 1912; FOC 22: 611. 2006; FGD 9: 475, fig. 248. 2009.
Spodiopogon obliquivalvis auct. non Nees: FHK 426. 1861.
Spodiopogon obliquivalvis Nees var. villosus Benth., FHK 426. 1861.
Ischaemum indicum auct. non (Houtt.) Merr.: FHN 4: 461. 1977; FFJ 6: 252. 1995; FRPS 10(2): 159. 1997; Check List HK Plants 339. 2002; 119. 2004.

Perennial herb. Culms tufted or creeping and rooting at the base, ascending or erect, 30–60 cm tall. Leaf sheaths sparsely to densely pilose with tubercle-based hairs, mouth haired; leaf blades linear or linear-lanceolate, 5–25 × 0.5–1cm, ± pubescent, base rounded, apex acuminate; ligule 1–2 mm, membranous. Racemes terminal, paired (seldom 3 or 4); rachis internodes and pedicels subequal, oblong, triquetrous, ciliate along angles. Sessile spikelet obovate-oblong, callus ca. 1 mm, pubescent; lower glume leathery with rounded flanks in lower half, upper half flat, papery, sometimes wrinkled, flanks keeled, winged, forming 2 rounded lobes at apex; upper glume boat-shaped, swollen and keeled above middle, keel narrowly winged; lower floret staminate, lemma papery, obscurely veined, apex acuminate; upper floret bisexual, lemma short, apex 2-clefted to the middle, with an awn arising from sinus; awn 1–1.5 cm. Pedicellate spikelet laterally compressed; lower glume with a solitary median winged keel; upper lemma awned.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. W. Lam 931, 1261, 1321.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Indian Subcontinent, Indochina, Malay Peninsula, Indonesia.
Ecology: Open grassy fields.

Ischaemum muticum L. 無芒鴨嘴草
Sp. Pl. 2: 1049. 1753; H. B. Gill. et al., Fl. Malaya 3: 255. 1971; FRPS 10(2): 161, pl. 38: 6. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 5: 560. 2000; FOC 22: 610. 2006.

Perennial herb, rhizomatous. Culms erect, geniculate at base, with a shallow groove along one side, glabrous. Leaf sheaths ciliate along outer margin, inner margin glabrous or sparsely appressed hairy; leaf blades long ovate-lanceolate to linear, lanceolate, tinged reddish brown, 2–10(–18) × 0.3–2 cm, base cordate, very shortly pseudo-petiolate, apex acute; ligule membranous, truncate, 0.2–0.6 mm. Racemes usually paired, appressed back to back, base enclosed by subtending sheath; rachis internodes and pedicels oblong, triquetrous, outer angle narrowly winged, inner angles glabrous or ciliolate. Sessile spikelet lanceolate; lower glume broad lanceolate, herbaceous, glabrous, winged from near base, apex entire; upper glume boat-shaped, thinly leathery, winged on upper keel, 3-veined; lower floret staminate, slightly shorter than glume, lemma and palea hyaline membranous; lodicules cuneate; pistil absent; upper floret bisexual, lemma long ovate, apex 2-toothed, midvein extend to a short and straight awn; upper lemma subentire, mucronate or with ca. 1 mm awnlet. Pedicellate spikelet laterally compressed, otherwise resembling sessile or smaller, awnless.

Locality: Hong Kong. HK sheet 32263.
Distribution: Taiwan; Japan (S Ryukyu Islands), India, Indochina, Malesia, Australia (Queensland).
Ecology: Coastal area.

Ischaemum rugosum Salisb. 田間鴨嘴草
Icon. Stirp. Rar. 1, t. 1. 1791; FKH 322. 1912; FRPS 10(2): 158, pl. 37: 12. 1997; FYN 9: 672. 2003; FOC 22: 613. 2006; FGD 9: 474. 2009.

Annual herb. Culms erect, loosely tufted or solitary, 20–100 cm tall, nodes pubescent. Leaf sheaths longer or upper shorter than internode, glabrous or sparsely pilose, ciliate; leaf blades linear or linear-lanceolate, 5–30 × 0.5–2 cm, pilose or covered with scattered tubercle-based hairs, apex acuminate, margins scabrid; ligule membranous, oblong, 2–5 mm. Racemes terminal and axillary, paired, appressed back to back, or usually separated, fragile; rachis internodes inflated, thickly clavate, outer margins ciliate. Sessile spikelet ovate; lower glume 2-keeled, crustaceous, transversely 4–7-ridged below, ridges sharp, mostly continuous, herbaceous above with many anastomosing green veins, keels scabrid, wingless or winged on one side, apex obliquely obtuse; upper glume boat-shaped, abaxially keeled; lower floret staminate, lemma as long as or slightly shorter than lower glume, apex acuminate; stamens 3; palea as long as or slightly shorter than lemma; upper floret bisexual, lemma membranous, apex 2-lobed to middle; awn exerted from sinus, geniculate and twisted; palea shorter than lemma. Pedicellate spikelet dorsally compressed, variable in size, often much reduced especially toward raceme apex, awnless; pedicel elongate when spikelet rudimentary.

Locality: High Island, Nai Chung. S. Y. Hu 8087, 8466, 8679 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Taiwan; Indian Subcontinent, SE Asia, Malesia, Australia (Queensland).
Ecology: Stream and ditch banks, other wet places. Flowering & fruiting: Summer to autumn.

Leersia hexandra Sw. 李氏禾
Prodr. 21. 1788; FKH 317. 1912; FTW ed. 2, 6: 321. 2000; FRPS 9(2): 9, pl. 2: 4. 2002; FOC 22: 184. 2006; FGD 9: 333. 2009.

Perennial herb. Culms loosely tufted, erect from decumbent base, up to 50 cm or more tall, nodes swollen, retrorsely puberulent. Leaf blades narrowly linear-lanceolate, 3–12 × 0.2–0.6 cm, flat or sometimes rolled, abaxial surface scabrid on midrib, base contracted, apex sharply acute; ligules membranous, 1–3 mm, truncate; leaf sheaths smooth or scabrid. Panicle loose, lanceolateoblong in outline, 5–10 cm. Spikelets narrowly elliptic to ellipticoblong, 3–5 × 1.2– 1.5 mm, pale green or purple tinged, contracted at base; lemma 5-veined, conspicuously pectinate-hispid on keel, lateral veins and sometimes surface sparsely spinulose, margins shortly hispid, apex contracted into a short obtuse beak; palea same texture and length as lemma, 3-veined. Stamens 6, anthers 2–2.5 mm.

Locality: Widely distributed in Hong Kong. Y. W. Lam 891; HK sheet 30737, 41941.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Fujian, Taiwan; tropical regions of the world.
Ecology: Marshlands, stream banks, shallow water. Flowering & fruiting: May–Dec.

Leptochloa chinensis (L.) Nees 千金子
Syll. Pl. Nov. 1: 4. 1824; FHK 430. 1861; FKH 327. 1912; FHN 4: 383. 1977; FRPS 10(1): 56, pl. 16: 7–12. 1990; FFJ 6: 158, fig. 130. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 425. 2000; FOC 22: 470. 2006; FGD 9: 353. 2009.
Poa chinensis L., Sp. Pl. 1: 69. 1753.

Annual herb, 30 – 100 cm tall. Culms erect or geniculate at base, glabrous. Leaf blades flat or slightly involute, 5–25 × 0.2 – 0.9 cm, glabrous, scabrid on both surfaces or abaxial surface smooth, apex acuminate; ligule membranous, 1–5 mm; leaf sheaths glabrous. Panicle 10–50 cm, composed of many unilateral racemes; rachis scabrid. Spikelets usually purplish or brownish green, narrowly elliptic-oblong, laterally compressed, 2–4 mm, 3–7-flowered; glumes scabrid along keels and sometimes laterally; lower glume lanceolate, 1–1.5 mm, apex acute; upper glume elliptic-oblong, 1.2–2 mm, apex obtuse; lemmas elliptic-oblong, keeled, lowest ca. 1.5 mm, shortly appressed-hairy along lower margins and on either side of midvein, apex obtuse or minutely emarginate; palea minutely hispid on keels, appressed hairy on back and flaps. Anthers ca. 0.5 mm. Caryopsis oblong, 0.7–0.9 mm, plano-convex.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. W. Lam 1352; HK sheet 42037, 42063.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Shandong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; tropical and subtropical regions of Asia.
Ecology: Moist places in farmlands. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Nov.
Uses: Animal food (fodder).

Leptochloa fusca (L.) Kunth 雙稃草
Revis. Gramin. 1: 91. 1829; FOC 22: 469. 2006; FGD 9: 353. 2009.
Festuca fusca L., Syst. Nat., ed. 10, 2: 876. 1759.
Diplachne fusca (L.) P. Beauv., Ess. Agrost. 80, 163. 1812; FHN 4: 381. 1977; FRPS 10(1): 54, pl. 16: 1–6. 1990; FTW ed. 2, 5: 410. 2000; FYN 9: 433. 2003; Check List HK Plants 333. 2002; 117. 2004 [“Diplachine”].

Perennial herb, 60–150 cm tall. Culms tufted, erect or geniculate at base, often rooting and branching from the lower nodes. Leaf blades tough, usually inrolled and needle-like, 10–45 cm × 1.5–3 mm, scabrid, grey-green with a broad white central vein; ligule hyaline, ca. 2 mm, tongue-shaped; leaf sheath glabrous. Inflorescence a contracted panicle, 15–35 cm, composed of many slender racemes of 7–15 cm. Spikelets narrowly elliptic to elliptic, 8–15 mm, slightly overlapping, grey-green or olivegreen, shortly pedicellate, 6 – 11-flowered; glumes papery, conspicuously 1-veined, keeled, scabrid on the keels, the lower lanceolate to narrowly lanceolate, 2–4.5 mm, apex acute or acuminate, the upper narrowly oblong, 3–7.5 mm, apex acute or obtuse and minutely mucronate; lemmas narrowly oblong, 3–6 mm, 3-veined, pilose on the lower part of the veins, 2- or more toothed and mucronate; midrib prolonged into a short awn of ca. 1.5 mm; palea elliptic, papery, 2-keeled, siliceous on keels. Anther ca. 0.5 mm. Caryopsis ca. 2 mm, dorso-ventrally flattened.

Locality: Sha Tin, Mai Po. Y. W. Lam 852; HK sheet 34224, 39692.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Yunnan, Hebei, Henan, Liaoning, Shandong, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; widely distributed from India through Malaysia, Indonesia to Australia, and extending to Africa.
Ecology: Swamps, marshes and other places with shallow water. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Sep.

Leptochloa panicea (Retz.) Ohwi 蟣子草
Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 55: 311. 1941; FHN 4: 382. 1977; FRPS 10(1): 57, pl. 16: 3. 1990; FFJ 6: 159. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 427. 2000; FOC 22: 470. 2006; FGD 9: 354. 2009.
Poa panicea Retz., Observ. Bot. 3: 11. 1783.
Leptochloa filiformis auct. non Roem. & Schult: FKH 327. 1912.

Annual herb, 30–80 cm tall. Culms slender, tufted, ascending from the geniculate base. Leaf blades linear-lanceolate, 4–20 × 0.3–0.7 cm, glabrous or sparsely covered with tubercular hairs along lateral veins; ligule membranous, 1–2 mm, usually lacerate; leaf sheaths papillate-pilose. Panicle elliptic to oblong, 10–30(–50) cm, often purplish, composed of many slender unilateral racemes; rachis scabrid. Spikelets glaucous-green or purplish green, elliptic, ± laterally compressed, 1.4–2.5 mm, 2–5-flowered; glumes subequal, scabrid along keel; lower glume lanceolate, 0.7–1.5 mm, apex acuminate; upper glume narrowly oblong, 0.9–1.6 mm, apex acute or obtuse and mucronate; lemmas longer than the glumes, elliptic-oblong, keeled, lowest 0.8–1.3 mm, veins puberulous, usually also a few appressed hairs between veins, apex obtuse; palea keels scaberulous. Anthers ca. 0.2 mm. Caryopsis broadly elliptic, 0.7–0.8 mm, brown, obtusely trigonous, apex obtuse.

Locality: New Territories. Y. S. Lau 1954; L. T. Lo 575.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; tropical and subtropical regions of Asia, Africa, America.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides, rice fields. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Oct.
Uses: Animal food (fodder).

Lolium perenne L. 黑麥草
Sp. Pl. 1: 83. 1753; FRPS 9(2): 289, pl. 33: 6. 2002; FOC 22: 244. 2006; FGD 9: 387. 2009.

Perennial herb, 20–90 cm tall. Culms tufted, erect or spreading, 1–2.5 mm in diam., 3–4-noded, sometimes prostrate and rooting from the lower nodes. Leaf blades linear, soft, 5–20(–30) cm × 3–6 mm, glabrous, folded when young, with or without 3 mm auricles at the base; ligule membranous, tongue-shaped, 1.5–2.5 mm; leaf sheaths 5–20 cm, glabrous. Raceme stiffly erect, or rarely slightly curved, 10–30 cm; rachis glabrous, smooth. Spikelets 0.5–2 cm, florets 3–10(–14); rachilla internodes ca. 1 mm, smooth, glabrous; lower glume absent, upper glume lanceolate, 1/3 as long to subequalling spikelet, 3–9-veined, margins narrowly membranous, apex acute or obtuse; lemmas oblong, herbaceous, 5–9 mm, 5-veined, smooth, apex obtuse to subacute, not turgid at maturity, usually awnless, rarely with an awn up to 8 mm; palea oblong, as long as the lemma, 2-keeled, minutely ciliate along keels, apex sinus. Anther ca. 3 mm. Caryopsis length more than 3 times width.

Locality: Cape D'Aguilar, Tseng Lan Shue (cultivated). HK sheet 35645, 38096.
Distribution: Commonly cultivated in China; widely distributed in Europe, N Africa and the temperate regions of Asia.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: May–Jul.
Uses: Environmental (erosion control), animal food (fodder, forage).

Lophatherum gracile Brongn. 淡竹葉
Duperrey, Voy. Monde 2: 50. 1831; FHK 433. 1861; FKH 329. 1912; FHN 4. 366, fig. 1176. 1977; FFJ 6: 133. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 334, pl. 128. 2000; FRPS 9(2): 35, pl. 3: 5. 2002; FOC 22: 445. 2006; FGD 9: 385, fig. 193. 2009.

Perennial herb, 60–150 cm tall, with short, knotty rhizomes and spindle-shaped root tubers. Culms loosely tufted, slender, stiffly erect. Leaf blades lanceolate, 5 –30 × 2–5 cm, tesselate veined, base rounded to a 8–12 mm pseudopetiole, glabrous or with long hairs on both surfaces; ligule ca. 0.5 mm, brown, hispid on backside; leaf sheaths glabrous or pilose. Inflorescence loose, outline elliptic, 10–30 cm. Spikelets narrowly lanceolate, subterete, sessile, 7–12 mm, base glabrous or hairy, with 1 perfect and 3–7 neutral florets; glumes ovate, rounded on back, subleathery with membranous margins; lower glume 3–4.5 mm, 5-veined, glabrous or stiffly hairy near margins and apex, apex acute; upper glume ca. 5 mm, 5–7-veined, glabrous, apex obtuse; sterile lemma subleathery, 5–6 mm, siliceous, 7–9-veined, apex obtuse with 1.5–2 mm awn; fertile lemma oblong with straight back, 6–7 mm, awn 1.5–2 mm; palea lanceolate, hyaline, 2-keeled, ca. 5 mm. Caryopsis 3.5 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 149, 2028; HK sheet 42059.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, S Korea, Indochina, Myanmar, Thailand, India, Malesia.
Ecology: Shady slopes, roadsides and moist forests. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), animal food (fodder).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): So Kon Po, Yau Tong Wan (locally naturalized)
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Melinis minutiflora P. Beauv. 糖蜜草
Ess. Agrostogr. 54. 1812; FRPS 10(1): 228, pl. 69. 1990; FTW ed. 2, 5: 480. 2000; FYN 9: 548, fig. 94: 7–11. 2003; FOC 22: 539. 2006; FGD 9: 400, fig. 206. 2009.

Perennial herb, densely tomentose with glandular, slightly sticky hairs and a strong smell. Culms tufted, branched, rooting at lower nodes, 50–150 cm tall, nodes pubescent. Leaf sheaths shorter than internode, sparsely villous or tuberculate-pilose; leaf blades linear, 5–20 × 0.5–1.5 cm; ligule short, membranous, apex hairy. Panicle purplish, spreading, 10–20 cm. Spikelets narrowly ovate-oblong, ca. 2 mm, ± laterally compressed, glabrous; lower glume minute, veinless; upper glume oblong, 7-veined, 2-lobed, awnless or with a mucro to 1 mm from the sinus; lower floret neuter without a palea, lemma narrower oblong, 5-veined, 2-lobed, awnless or with a slender awn to 15 mm from the sinus; upper floret bisexual, lemma ovate-lanceolate, 3-veined, 2-lobed, hyaline; lodicules 2; styles 2. Caryopsis oblong.

Locality: So Kon Po, Yau Tong Wan (locally naturalized). L. T. Lo 223; Y. S. Lau 2713; Y. W. Lam 1204.
Distribution: Yunnan, Taiwan; a fodder grass of Africa origin.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Oct.
Uses: Animal food.

Melinis repens (Willd.) Zizka 紅毛草
Biblioth. Bot. 138: 55. 1988; FOC 22: 539. 2006.
Saccharum repens Willd., Sp. Pl., ed. 4, 1: 322. 1797.
Rhynchelytrum repens (Willd.) C. E. Hubb., Kew Bull. 1934: 110. 1934; FRPS 10(1): 232, pl. 70. 1990; FFJ 6: 184, fig. 152. 1995; FTW ed, 2. 5: 507. 2000; FGD 9: 401. 2009; Check List HK Plants 345. 2002; 120. 2004.

Perennial herb. Culms erect, branched, up to 1(–1.5) m tall. Leaf sheaths loose, usually with tubercle-based hairs, mostly shorter than internode; leaf blades linear, up to 20 × 0.2–1.4 cm, glabrous; ligule a ring of long (ca. 1 mm ) hairs. Panicle silverypink or purple, ovate to oblong, 8–20 cm; branches capillary; pedicels with a few long hairs. Spikelets ovate, laterally compressed, 2–5 mm, densely villous, hairs up to 6 mm; lower glume narrowly oblong, 0.3–1.5 mm, 1-veined, with stiff short hairs; upper glume 5-veined, pink hairs, gibbous below middle, tapering upward into a glabrous membranous beak, emarginate, mucronate or with short awn up to 1 mm; lower floret staminate, lemma similar to upper glume but narrower and less gibbous, pink hairs, palea keels ciliate; upper floret whitish, ca. 2 mm, thinly cartilaginous, smooth, shining; lodicules 2; stamens 3, anthers 2 mm; styles 2, free, stigma plumose.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong (naturalized). H. C. Tang 628; Y. S. Lau 754; HK sheet 14556.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; originated from tropical S Africa, now introduced into most warm countries.
Ecology: Grasslands, wastelands. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Nov.

Microchloa indica (L. f.) P. Beauv. 小草
Ess. Agrostogr. Expl. Pl. 13. 1812; FRPS 10(1): 87. 1990; FFJ 6: 163. 1995; FOC 22: 492. 2006; FGD 9: 378, fig. 187. 2009.
Microchloa setacea R. Br., Prodr. 208. 1810; FHK 428. 1861; FKH 326. 1912.

Perennial herb, 10–20 cm tall. Culms very slender, densely tufted and clothed at base with fibres of disintegrated leaf sheaths. Leaves mostly basal; leaf blades narrowly linear, 1–6 cm × 0.5–1.2 mm, adaxial surface usually with long scattered hairs, margins scabrous, midrib and submarginal veins thickened, apex obtuse; ligule 0.1–0.3 mm. Spike (3–)5–20(–25) cm, falcate when dry; rachis shortly ciliate on margins or glabrous. Spikelets light green, lanceolate, 1.6–4 mm, acute; lower glume slightly asymmetrical; lemma 1.5–3 mm, mucronate. Caryopsis ca. 1 mm.

Locality: No precise locality. C. Wright s.n. (K)
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Yunnan, Fujian; tropical and subtropical regions of the world.
Ecology: Dry and stony places. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Oct.

Microstegium ciliatum (Trin.) A. Camus 剛莠竹
Ann. Soc. Linn. Lyon, N. S. 68: 201. 1921; FFJ 6: 242. 1995; FRPS 10(2): 69, pl. 16: 11–13. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 5: 563, photo 62. 2000; FOC 22: 597. 2006; FGD 9: 463. 2009.
Pollinia ciliata Trin., Mem. Acad. St. Petersb. ser. 6, 2: 305. 1833.

Perennial herb. Culms ascending from creeping base, up to 1 m tall, pubescent below inflorescence. Leaf sheaths longer or the upper shorter than internode, pilose or glabrous; leaf blades linear or linear-lanceolate, 6–20 × 0.5–1.8 cm, pubescent, base narrow, apex acuminate, margins scabrous; ligule 1–2 mm, membranous, ciliate. Racemes terminal, 3–20 digitate; rachis internodes linear, slightly inflated upward, margins ciliate. Sessile spikelet 3–3.5 mm, callus hairy; lower glume oblong, 2-keeled, 2–4-veined between keels, upper keels stiffly pectinate-ciliate, acute, obtuse or 2-toothed; upper glume boat-shaped, sharply keeled, apex acuminate into a 0.3–3 mm hair-like awnlet; lower lemma absent or very small; upper lemma linear or lanceolate, occasionally broader, 0.5–1 mm, apex usually entire; awn 1–2 cm, flexuose with weakly developed column and fine hair-like apex; anthers 3. Caryopsis oblong. Pedicellate spikelet similar to sessile spikelet; pedicel 2–3 mm, margins densely ciliate.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1684; L. T. Lo 115, 582.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; Indian Subcontinent, Indochina, Malay Peninsula.
Ecology: Thin forests, open grassy fields. Flowering & fruiting: Sep.–Dec.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Ma On Shan, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Microstegium fasciculatum (L.) Henrard 蔓生莠竹
Blumea 3: 453. 1940; FOC 22: 597. 2006; FGD 9: 463, fig. 240. 2009.
Andropogon fasciculatus L., Sp. Pl. 2: 1047. 1753.
Microstegium vagans (Nees ex Steud.) A. Camus, Ann. Soc. Linn. Lyon, sér. 2, 68: 200. 1921[1922]; FRPS 10(2): 72, pl. 16: 1–5. 1997; Check List HK Plants 340. 2002; 119. 2004.

Perennial herb. Culms rambling, up to 1 m or more. Leaf sheaths glabrous or tuberculate-hispid; leaf blades linearlanceolate, 10–18 × (0.5–)0.8–2 cm, pubescent, base narrow, stipe-like, apex acuminate into a setaceous point, margins scabrous; ligule 1–2 mm. Racemes 3–12, digitate in glabrous rachis, purplish; rachis internode ciliate at margins. Sessile spikelet oblong; callus hairs ca. 1 mm; lower glume elliptic-oblong, scabrid-hispidulous, 2-veined between keels, upper keels stiffly pectinate-ciliate, abaxial shallowly grooved or almost flat, apex subentire or 2-lobed; upper glume sharply keeled, apex acuminate or with a brief mucro; lower floret usually absent; upper lemma ovate, ca. 0.5 mm, 2-lobed, with an awn arising from the sinus; awn geniculate with distinct column. Pedicellate spikelet similar to sessile spikelet, lower glume keel scabrous, glabrous.

Locality: Ma On Shan, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island. S. Y. Hu 6204, 11157, 11239 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hubei; Indian Subcontinent, Indochina, Malay Peninsula, Indonesia, Africa.
Ecology: Shade and moist banks, hillslopes. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Jan. of the following year.

Microstegium vimineum (Trin.) A. Camus 柔枝莠竹（莠竹）
Ann. Soc. Linn. Lyon, N. S. 68: 201. 1921; FFJ 6: 242, fig. 210. 1995; FRPS 10(2): 76, pl. 15: 5–7. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 5: 565, pl. 238. 2000; FOC 22: 596. 2006; FGD 9: 462. 2009.
Microstegium nodosum (Kom.) Tzvelev, Bot. Mater. Gerb. Bot. Inst. Komarova Acad. Nauk SSSR 21: 23. 1961; Check List HK Plants 340. 2002; 119. 2004.
Arthraxon nodosus Kom., Trudy Glavn. Bot. Sada 18: 448. 1901.
Andropogon vimineus Trin., Mem. Acad. St. Petersb. VI. Math, Phys. Nat. 2: 268. 1832.

Annual herb. Culms slender, erect from the decumbent base, up to 1 m, with deep groove in one side, glabrous. Leaf sheaths shorter than internode, glabrous except margins and mouth pilose; leaf blades linear-lanceolate, 4–9 × 0.5–1 cm, often sparsely pubescent, midvein white, apex acuminate; ligule ca. 0.5 mm, membranous, truncate. Racemes   6, subdigitately arranged; rachis internode linearclavate, ciliate, shorter than spikelet. Sessile spikelet 4–5.5 mm, callus with a few short hairs; lower glume narrowly lanceolate-oblong, abaxial deeply grooved, puberulous-scaberulous or occasionally hispidulous, 0–4-veined between keels, veins connected by veinlets below apex; upper glume boat-shaped, scabrid on keel, acuminate; lower floret reduced to an inconspicuous linear-lanceolate scale or absent; upper lemma very narrow, 1–1.5 mm, with a mucro or an awn of about 5 mm long, arising from the apex; awn weakly geniculate, often included within spikelet; upper palea ovate, ca. 1 mm; anthers 3.

Locality: Sha Tin. S. P. Lau 586.
Distribution: Widely distributed from N to S China; Indian Subcontinent, SW to E Asia, Indochina, Philippines, introduced in America and elsewhere.
Ecology: Margins of forests, moist grassy places.

Miscanthus floridulus (Labill.) Warb. ex K. Schum. & Lauterb. 五節芒
Fl. Schutzgeb. Südsee. 166. 1901; FHN 4: 448. 1977; FFJ 6: 240, fig. 208. 1995; FRPS 10(2): 4, pl. 1: 1–6. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 5: 567, pl. 239, photo 64. 2000; FOC 22: 582. 2006; FGD 9: 454. 2009.
Miscanthus japonicus (Trin.) Andersson, Öfvers. af Förh. Kongl. Svenska Vetensk.-Akad. 12: 166. 1855.
Eulalia japonicum Trin., Mém. Acad. Imp. Sci. St.-Pétersbourg, Sér. 6, Sci. Math. 2(3): 333. 1832; FHK 420. 1861.
Saccharum floridulum Labill., Sert. Austro-Caledon. 13: t. 18. 1824.

Perennial herb. Culms erect, 1.5–4 m tall, glabrous, unbranched. Leaf sheaths glabrous or margins sparsely ciliate, longer than internode or the upper slightly shorter than internode; ligule 1–3 mm, rounded, ciliate; leaf blades linear, flat, tough, 20–85 × 0.5–4 cm, glabrous or pilose on the base of adaxial surface, midrib prominent, margins scabrid. Panicle oblong or elliptic, dense, 30–50 cm; axis more than 2/3 the length of the panicle; racemes many, 10–30 cm, appressed or ascending, glabrous, scaberulous. Spikelets of a pair similar, unequally pedicellate along a slender continuous rachis; callus hairs as long as or slightly longer than the spikelet, white, spreading; glumes subequal, membranous, margins pilose near apex, veins obscure, acuminate; lower lemma boat-shaped, hyaline, pilose, acuminate; upper lemma similar to the lower, glabrous or margins sparsely short ciliate at the lower, acute, slightly 2-toothed; awn straight or geniculate; upper palea a small hyaline scale; anthers 3, 1–1.5 mm. Caryopsis oblong.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1865; K. L. Yip 4181, 4246.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Henan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; SE Asia.
Ecology: Hillslopes, valleys, open grassy fields.

Miscanthus sinensis Andersson 芒
Öfvers. Kongl. Vetensk.-Akad. Förh. 12: 166. 1855; FKH 319. 1912; FHN 4: 448, fig. 1238. 1977; FFJ 6: 241, fig. 209. 1995; FRPS 10(2): 6, pl. 1: 7–11. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 5: 567, photo 65. 2000; FOC 22: 582. 2006; FGD 9: 454. 2009.

Perennial herb. Culms tufted, 1–2 m tall, solid, unbranched, glabrous or puberulous at nodes. Leaf sheaths glabrous, longer than internode; leaf blades linear, flat, 20–50 × 0.6–1 cm, glabrous, glaucous or pilose, midrib prominent, base tapering or broad and rounded, apex acuminate, margins scabrid or smooth; ligule 0.5–4 mm, ciliolate. Panicle 20–50 cm; axis up to 1/2 the length of the panicle, subglabrous to pilose or puberulous. Raceme 10–30 cm; rachis internodes glabrous, scaberulous or smooth, nodes glabrous; lower pedicel 2 mm, upper pedicel 4–6 mm. Spikelets 4.5–5 mm, callus hairs as long as spikelet; lower glume 3–4-veined, abaxial surface glabrous or pilose, apex acuminate; upper glume 1-veined, upper margins inrolled and ciliate; lower lemma oblong, hyaline, margins ciliate; upper lemma shorter than lower lemma, bifid, with an awn from the sinus; awn geniculate, 9–12 mm; upper palea 1/2 length of upper lemma.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. HK sheet 41504, 41961.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Hebei, Hubei, Jiangxi, Anhui, Shandong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Korea.
Ecology: Hillslopes, rivers and stream banks. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Dec.

Mnesithea laevis (Retz.) Kunth 假蛇尾草
Révis. Gramin. 1: 154. 1829; FOC 22: 643. 2006; FGD 9: 483. 2009.
Rottboellia laevis Retz., Observ. Bot. 3: 11. 1783.
Heteropholis cochinchinensis (Lour.) Clayton, Kew Bull. 35(4): 816. 1981; FRPS 10(2): 276. pl. 67: 3–4. 1997; Check List HK Plants 337. 2002; 118. 2004.
Thaumastochloa cochinchinensis (Lour.) C. E. Hubb., FHN 4: 467, fig. 1255. 1977; FFJ 6: 259, fig. 230. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 583, pl. 246. 2000.

Perennial herb. Culms tufted, erect, slender, glabrous, 15–70 cm tall. Leaf sheaths shorter than internode, glabrous, often keeled; leaf blades linear, 8–25 × 0.1–0.4 cm, glabrous; ligule 0.5–1 mm. Racemes solitary, terminal or axillary, cylindrical; sessile spikelets paired at each joint and separated by a pedicel, or triads present only at raceme base, or whole raceme with solitary sessile spikelets; rachis internodes clavate, 3.5–4 mm. Sessile spikelet 3–5 mm; lower glume oblong, smooth, or slightly sunken between lower part of veins, or ribbed throughout, rarely pitted, margins not winged, apex obtuse; upper glume boat-shaped, equal to lower glume, membranous; lower lemma slightly shorter than glumes, palea absent; upper lemma ca. 2.5 mm; stamens 3; style free. Pedicellate spikelet minute or absent; pedicel linear, adnate to rachis internode, when paired sessile spikelets present the pedicel between them often adnate only at apex.

Locality: Hong Kong Island. Y. S. Lau 1039; Y. W. Lam 952; HK sheet 8435.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; Indian Subcontinent, Indochina, Indonesia, Philippines, Pacific islands (Polynesia).
Ecology: Open grassy fields. Flowering & fruiting: Autumn.

Mnesithea mollicoma (Hance) A. Camus 毛儉草
Bull. Mus. Natl. Hist. Nat. 25: 57. 1919; FHN 4: 468, fig. 1256. 1977; FRPS 10(2): 280, pl. 66: 1–3, 78: 4. 1997; FOC 22: 643. 2006; FGD 9: 483, fig. 254. 2009.
Rottboellia mollicoma Hance, J. Bot. 9: 134. 1871; FKH 321. 1912.

Perennial herb. Culms erect, up to 1.5 m, softly pilose. Leaf sheathes the upper usually shorter than internode, densely pilose or with caducous tubercle-based hairs; leaf blades linear-lanceolate, 10–60 × 0.5–2 cm, softly pubescent, tapering to both ends; ligule 1–2 mm, glabrous or ciliolate. Racemes 5–10 cm; rachis internode as long as or slightly shorter than spikelet, with short hairs at base; sessile spikelets 3–4 mm, paired at each node and separated by a pedicel, or occasionally only one sessile spikelet present; lower glume leathery, rib-like veins separated by deep slits, slits interrupted by tubercle-based hairs along their length, margins narrowly winged toward apex; upper glume boat-shaped, keeled toward apex; lower floret usually reduced, lemma membranous, 3-veined; upper floret bisexual, upper lemma and palea subequal. Pedicellate spikelet ca. 0.5 mm, linear, flattened, pilose, reduced to a glume, pedicel subequal to sessile spikelet, ca. 0.5 mm wide.

Locality: Sha Tin. P. P. H. But 284; S. Y. Hu 11197 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi; Vietnam, Thailand, Malay Peninsula, Indonesia.
Ecology: Grassy fields.

Neyraudia reynaudiana (Kunth) Keng ex Hitchc. 類蘆（石珍茅）
Amer. J. Bot. 21(3): 131. 1934; FHN 4: 369, fig. 1176. 1977; FTW 5: 386. 1978; FFJ 6: 131. 1995; FRPS 9(2): 23, pl. 4: 5, 5a. 2002; FOC 22: 460. 2006; FGD 9: 340, fig. 160. 2009.
Arundo reynaudiana Kunth, Révis. Gramin. 1: 275. 1830.
Neyraudia arundinacea auct. non (L.) Henr.: FTW ed. 2, 5: 329. 2000.
Neyraudia madagascariensis auct. non (Kunth) Hook. f.: FKH 328. 1912.

Perennial herb, 1–3 m tall, with short, woody rhizomes. Culms reed-like, erect, 3–10 mm in diam., usually fasciculately branched, many-noded, internodes somewhat glaucous, nodes purple. Leaf blades flat or involute, 20–70 × 0.4–1 cm, glabrous or adaxial surface pilose, apex long acuminate; ligule 1–2 mm, truncate, shortly ciliate on dorsal side; leaf sheaths pilose at mouth. Panicle 30 – 70 cm, branches slender, ± nodding; pedicels 1–4 mm. Spikelets 5–9 mm, 4–10-flowered, the lowest floret sterile, resembling glumes but somewhat longer; glumes membranous, lanceolate, golden-brown or purplish, glabrous, subequal, 1.5–3 mm, apex acute; lemmas purplish, ca. 4 mm, lateral veins ciliate with white, soft, ca. 2 mm hairs, awn recurved, 1–2 mm; palea membranous, ca. 3 mm, 2– keeled, apex slightly cleft, minutely ciliate along keels.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 3180; HK sheet 32294, 35659.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Gansu, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Vietnam, Cambodia, Laos, Myanmar, Thailand, India, Nepal, Bhutan, Malaysia, Indonesia.
Ecology: Streamsides, hillslopes, rocky places. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Dec.
Uses: Environmental (erosion control).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Authority: (L. C. Chia & But) G. H. Ye & Z. P. Wang
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Arundinaria shiuyingiana Chia & But 秀英竹
Kew Bull. 37: 591. 1983; HKB 25. 1985; FGD 9: 299, fig. 142. 2009.
Oligostachyum shiuyingianum (L. C. Chia & But) G. H. Ye & Z. P. Wang, J. Nanjing Univ., Nat. Sci. Ed. 26(3): 486. 1990; FRPS 9(1): 582, pl. 178: 1–3. 1996; FOC 22: 130. 2006.

Culms 4–6 m, 1–2 cm in diam.; internodes grey-green, usually with purple speckles, initially usually white powdery below nodes and sparsely setulose; nodes elevated, supra-nodal ridge more prominent than sheath scar. Culm sheaths yellow-green with purple-green base, brown strigose, margins ciliate; auricles small; oral setae 2–several; ligule truncate, ca. 1 mm, white ciliate; blade erect, brown-green, ovate-lanceolate or lanceolate, base ca. 1/2 as wide as apex of culm sheath. Leaves 5–9 per flowering branch; sheath with purple speckles, glabrous; auricles not developed; oral setae 2–3; ligule purple, truncate, 0.5 – 1 mm, weakly exserted, hairy; blade 12–20 × 0.8–1.3 cm, both surfaces glabrous, abaxially transverse veins distinct, rectangular. Racemes or small panicles with 2–4 spikelets, partially exserted from leaf sheaths; axis and branches slender, glabrous or branches sparsely hirtellous along angles. Spikelets lanceolate, 3–8 × ca. 0.5 cm; florets 5–15. Glumes 2, 1st smaller, 8–9 mm; lemma purple speckled, 1.7–2 cm, deciduously pubescent, apex with mucro 2–3 mm; palea 1.2–1.4 cm, pubescent, keels sparsely ciliolate, apex obtuse, thickly hairy; lodicules 3. Stamens 3. Style 1; stigmas 3.

Locality: New Territories. Y. S. Lau 3163; Nan-Zhu 2809; F. W. Xing 9874.
Distribution: Endemic to Hong Kong.
Ecology: Partially shaded slopes of hills, alt. below 100 m.
Uses: Environmental.
Notes: The type specimen (Nan-Zhu 2862, IBSC) was collected from Eagle's Nest on 21 June 1981. It was named in honour of Prof. Shiu- ying Hu. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Oplismenus compositus (L.) P. Beauv. 竹葉草
Ess. Agrostogr. 54. 1812; FKH 316. 1912; FHN 4: 416. 1977; FRPS 10(1): 245, pl. 75: 1–3. 1990; FFJ 6: 211, fig. 179. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 482, pl. 201. 2000; FOC 22: 502. 2006.
Panicum compositum L., Sp. Pl. 1: 57. 1753; FHK 411. 1861; FGD 9: 416, fig. 215. 2009.

Perennial herb. Culms stoloniferous, creeping and rooting at lower nodes, upper part ascending, 20–80 cm. Leaf sheaths shorter or the upper longer than internode, glabrous, pilose or tuberculatehairy; leaf blades lanceolate to ovate-lanceolate, 3–20 × 0.5–3 cm, subglabrous to tuberculate-hairy, base ± embraced stem and usually asymmetrical oblique. Inflorescence axis 5–15(–25) cm, glabrous to tuberculate-hairy; racemes 3–6, alternating, ascending to erect. Spikelets lanceolate, glabrous to thinly pilose; glumes herbaceous, subequal, ca. 1/2–2/3 length of spikelet, margins usually ciliate; lower glume awn 5–10 mm; upper glume awn to 1–2 mm or occasionally absent; lower floret neuter, lemma papery, 7–9-veined, acute or with a stout mucro, palea membranous, narrow or absent; upper lemma coriaceous, smooth, margins inrolled embraced same texture palea.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1031; HK sheet 42019, 42066.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; tropical Asia and Australia, extending westward through India to E Africa.
Ecology: Margins of forests, other moist places. Flowering & fruiting: Sep.–Nov.

Oryza sativa L. 稻
Sp. Pl. 1: 333. 1753; FKH 317. 1912; FHN 4: 396. 1977; FTW ed. 2, 5: 323. 2000; FOC 22: 183. 2006; FGD 9: 332. 2009.
Oryza formosana Masam. & Suzuki, Trans. Nat. Hist. Soc. Formosa 25: 320. 1935.

Annual or short-lived perennial herb, 0.5–1.5 m tall. Culms tufted, erect. Leaf sheaths glabrous; auricles falcate, ciliate; leaf blades cauline, linear, 25–80 × 0.5–3 cm, glabrous, smooth or scabrid on both sides, margins scabrid, apex acuminate; ligule ovate to lanceolate, 10–40 mm, margins decurrent to the sheath; leaf sheaths slightly inflated below, upper sheaths tight, glabrous, auricles falcate, ciliate. Panicle loosely contracted, up to 30 cm, nodding at maturity; branches 1–3 at lowest node, longest 2–12 cm, axils bearded or glabrous. Spikelets flattened, oblong to oblong-lanceolate, 6–10 mm; sterile lemmas lanceolate, 1.5–4 mm, apex acuminate; fertile lemma 5-veined, hard, siliceous, hispidulous, apex acuminate, as long as spikelet; palea 3-veined, same texture and length as lemma; awn very variable, slender or stout, up to 60 mm or more, scaberulous, sometimes absent. Anthers 1–3 mm. Caryopsis ovate or elliptic to cylindrical, 5–7 mm, whitish yellow to brown or blackish.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 2419; HK sheet 14939, 14943.
Distribution: Cultivated throughout tropical, subtropical, and warm temperate regions.
Ecology: Usually two crops a year in Hong Kong.
Uses: Food (cereal).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Mo Shan, Tai Po Kau, San Tau
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Ottochloa nodosa (Kunth) Dandy 露籽草
J. Bot. 69: 55. 1931; FHN 4: 409, fig. 1213. 1977; FRPS 10(1): 222, pl. 67: 1–9. 1990; FTW ed. 2, 5: 485, pl. 202. 2000; FOC 22: 512. 2006 ; FGD 9: 408, fig. 209. 2009.
Panicum nodosum Kunth, Enum. Pl. 1: 97. 1833, not Lamarck (1798); FHK 412. 1861; FKH 315. 1912.

Perennial herb. Culms slender, decumbent and rooting at the lower nodes, ascending up to 60 cm tall. Leaf sheaths conspicuously ciliate along one margin; leaf blades narrowly lanceolate, 4–11 × 0.5–1 cm, smooth, glabrous, base rounded or cordate, apex acuminate, margins scabrous; ligule ca. 0.3 mm. Panicle 10–15 cm, branches 3–8 cm, stiffly spreading, subverticillate in the lower part, the spikelets grouped in clusters or short racemelets, or sometimes loosely spaced. Spikelets elliptic to elliptic-oblong, 2.8–3.2 mm, acute; glumes lanceolate, lower glume 1/2 spikelet length, 3–5-veined; upper glume 1/2–2/3 spikelet length, 5–7-veined; lower lemma 7-veined; upper lemma smooth, apex laterally compressed to a very small crest.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Tai Po Kau, San Tau. HK sheet 42018, 42021, 42025.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; Indian Subcontinent, Indochina, Malesia, Pacific islands, Africa.
Ecology: Margins of forests, wet places in ravines. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Sep.

(Balansa ex A. Camus) S. M. Phillips & S. L. Chen
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Ottochloa nodosa (Kunth) Dandy var. micrantha (Balansa ex A. Camus) S. L. Chen & S. M. Phillips 小花露籽草
Novon. 13: 467. 2003; FRPS 10(1): 222, pl. 67: 10–17. 1990; FFJ 6: 202. 1995; FOC 22: 513. 2006; FGD 9: 408. 2009.
Ottochloa nodosa (Kunth) Dandy var. micrantha (Balansa ex A. Camus) Keng f., Iconogr. Cormophytorum Sinicorum 5: 160, fig. 7150. 1976, nom. inval.
Hemigymnia arnottiana Stapf var. micrantha Balansa ex A. Camus, Fl. Indo-Chine 7: 455. 1922.

Spikelets 2–2.5 mm; upper glume ovate, ca. 1/2 spikelet length, 7-veined; lower lemma 5–7-veined.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. HK sheet 42003, 42006, 42008.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong; Vietnam.
Ecology: Margins of forests. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Nov.
Notes: The species was reported as Ottochloa malabarica (L.) Dandy previously (Check List HK Plants 341. 2002; 119. 2004).

Panicum brevifolium L. 短葉黍
Sp. Pl. 1: 59. 1753; FKH 316. 1912; FHN 4: 404. 1977; FRPS 10(1): 216, pl. 64: 1–7. 1990; FFJ 6: 204, fig. 171. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 487, pl. 204. 2000; FOC 22: 509. 2006; FGD 9: 406. 2009.
Panicum ovalifolium Poir., Encycl., Suppl. 4: 279. 1816; FHK 413. 1861.

Annual herb. Culms rambling and rooting at lower nodes, flowering branches 10–50 cm tall, nodes glabrous or pubescent. Leaf sheaths shorter than internode, puberulous or glabrous, margins ciliate; leaf blades ovate or ovate-lanceolate, 2–10 × 0.5–3 cm, glabrous or sparsely pilose, base cordate, amplexicaul, apex acute, margins scabrous or the base with tuberculate-ciliate; ligule ca. 0.2 mm, a ciliolate membrane. Panicle oblong or ovate in outline, spreading, much branched, usually glandular patches present. Spikelets elliptic, 1.5–2 mm, sparsely puberulous to pilose; lower glume oblong-lanceolate, slightly shorter than or as long as spikelet, 3-veined; upper glume as long as spikelet, 5-veined, dorsally convex, apex beak-like; lower lemma oblong, similar to upper glume, palea well developed; upper floret ovate.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 2032; L. T. Lo 559; HK sheet 42039.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; Indian Subcontinent, Indochina, Malay Peninsula, tropical Africa.
Ecology: Humid places in open fields and margins of forests. Flowering & fruiting: May – Dec.

Panicum dichotomiflorum Michx. 洋野黍（水生黍）
Fl. Bor. Amer. 1: 48. 1803; FRPS 10(1): 207. 1990; FTW ed. 2, 5: 490. 2000; FOC 22: 506. 2006; FGD 9: 403. 2009.
Panicum paludosum Roxb., Fl. Ind. 1: 310. 1820; FRPS 10(1): 206. 1990; Check List HK Plants 342. 2002; 119. 2004.

Annual or perennial hydrophilous herb. Culms creeping and rooting at lower nodes, branching, 30–110 cm, upper nodes glabrous. Leaves cauline; leaf sheaths striate, glabrous, longer than internode; leaf blades linear, flat, 7–35 × 0.5–1.5 cm, glabrous, scabrid, base straight or subcordate, apex acute; ligule 1–2 mm, a ciliate membrane. Panicle terminal or axillary, open, 10–30 cm, much branched; branches glabrous, scabrid, secondary and tertiary branches often appressed. Spikelets lanceolate to narrowly ovate, 3–4 mm, glabrous, acuminate; lower glume 1/6 – 1/3 length of spikelet, clasping at the base of the spikelet, membranous, 0–1-veined, apex obtuse to acute; upper glume as long as spikelet, 7–9-veined; lower lemma similar to upper glume, palea absent or well developed, narrow and small; upper floret green or pale yellow, 2/3 length of spikelet, smooth, shiny, acute.

Locality: New Territories. Y. W. Lam 1574; HK sheet 41942, 42013.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan , Fujian, Taiwan; India, Malaysia, tropical regions of the New World.
Ecology: Swampy places in shallow waters. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Oct.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Causeway Bay, Fung Yuen, Ng Tung Chai, Cheung Chau
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Panicum incomtum Trin. 藤竹草
Gram. Panic. 200. 1826; FHN 4: 406. 1977; FRPS 10(1): 211, pl. 63: 14–17. 1990; FFJ 6: 207. 1995; FOC 22: 509. 2006; FGD 9: 405. 2009.
Panicum sarmentosum auct. non Roxb.: FHK 412. 1861; FKH 315. 1912.

Perennial herb. Culms woody, branching and scrambling, up to 10 m. Leaf sheaths loose, puberulous; leaf blades narrowly lanceolate, 10–25 × 1–3 cm, pilose, base rounded, apex acuminate; ligule ca. 0.5–1 mm, ciliate. Panicle spreading, 10–20 cm; central axis erect, much branched, viscid. Spikelets ovate, 1.5–2.2 mm, obtuse or slightly acute; lower glume ovate, 2/3–3/4 length of spikelet, 3–5-veined, base inrolled embraced spikelet, acute or ciliate; upper glume as long as spikelet, 5-veined; lower lemma similar to upper glume, palea well developed; upper floret as long as spikelet, brown, smooth, shiny.

Locality: Causeway Bay, Fung Yuen, Ng Tung Chai, Cheung Chau. Y. W. Lam 1314, 1735; HK sheet 41721.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; Indochina, Indian Subcontinent, Malesia, Australia.
Ecology: Shade in forests. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Mar.

Panicum maximum Jacq. 大黍
Icon. Pl. Rar. 1: 2. 1781; FKH 315. 1912; FHN 4: 405. 1977; FRPS 10(1): 214, pl. 63: 18–22. 1990; FFJ 6: 205. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 490, pl. 205. 2000; FOC 22: 506. 2006; FGD 9: 405. 2009.

Perennial herb, rhizomatous. Culms stout, erect, 1–3 m tall, nodes glabrous or densely pilose. Leaf sheaths sparsely tuberculatehispid; leaf blades linear to narrowly lanceolate, flat, 20–60 × 1–3 cm, adaxial surface tuberculate-hispid near base, base broad, taping downward, apex acuminate, margins scabrous; ligule 1–1.5 mm, membranous, long-ciliate. Panicle oblong, spreading, 20–35 cm, much branched; branches spreading, lowest arranged in a whorl. Spikelets oblong, ca. 3 mm; lower glume broadly ovate, 1/3–1/2 length of spikelet, 1–3-veined or veinless; upper glume elliptic, as long as spikelet, 5-veined, acute; lower floret staminate, lemma similar to upper glume, palea well developed, stamens 3; upper floret oblong, thinly coriaceous, shiny, finely transverse rugulose.

Locality: Cultivated for forage. Y. S. Lau 2232, 2537; HK sheet 35001.
Distribution: Guangdong, Fujian, Taiwan (introduced); Africa, Arabian Peninsula; widely naturalized in the tropics.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Oct.
Uses: Animal food (fodder, forage).

Panicum notatum Retz. 心葉稷（山黍）
Observ. Bot. 4: 18. 1786; FHN 4: 404. 1977; FRPS 10(1): 210, pl. 63: 10 – 13. 1990; FFJ 6: 207, fig. 175. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 491. 2000; FYN 9: 496. 2003; FOC 22: 509. 2006; FGD 9: 404. 2009.
Panicum montanum Roxb., Fl. Ind. 1: 315. 1820; FHK 412. 1861; FKH 315. 1912.

Perennial herb. Culms erect or geniculately ascending, often rooting at lower nodes, branched. Leaf sheaths shorter than internode, ciliate; leaf blades lanceolate, 5–12 × 1–3 cm, subglabrous to pubescent, cross veins present, base cordate, apex finely pointed to acuminate, margins scabrid; ligule very short, a ciliate membrane. Panicle broadly ovate, spreading, much branched; branches slender, spreading, glabrous, smooth or scabrid, bearing spikelets toward the extremities. Spikelets elliptic, 2–2.5 mm, glabrous or puberulous; lower glume ovate or oblong, nearly equaling or slightly shorter than the spikelet, 3 –5-veined; upper glume as long as spikelet, 5-veined, acute; lower lemma similar to upper glume, 5-veined, palea absent; upper floret as long as spikelet, leathery, smooth, shiny.

Locality: New Territories. Y. W. Lam 426; HK sheet 41979, 41980.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Xizang, Fujian, Taiwan; Indian Subcontinent, Indochina, Malesia. Ecology: Margins of forests. Flowering & fruiting: May–Nov.

Panicum repens L. 鋪地黍
Sp. Pl., ed. 2, 1: 87. 1762; FHK 412. 1861; FKH 315. 1912; FHN 4: 404. 1977; FRPS 10(1): 207, pl. 62: 1–8. 1990; FTW ed. 2, 5: 491. 2000; FOC 22: 506. 2006; FGD 9: 404. 2009.

Perennial, rhizomatous herb. Culms erect or decumbent, 20–120 cm tall. Leaf sheaths glabrous, puberulous to ciliate on margins; leaf blades linear, 5–25 × 0.2–0.8 cm, flat or convolute, often stiff and pungent, apex acute or acuminate; ligule 0.5–1.5 mm, a ciliate membrane. Panicle terminal, narrowly oblong, open, 5–20 cm; branches ascending. Spikelets oblong, ca. 3 mm, glabrous, acute; lower glume 1/4–1/3 length of spikelet, thin membranous, hyaline, clasping at the base of the spikelet, obtuse or truncate; upper glume as long as spikelet, membranous, 7–9-veined, beak-like; lower floret staminate, lemma similar to upper glume, stamens 3, palea well developed; upper floret bisexual, nearly equal to spikelet, oblong, acute, smooth and shiny.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1637, 2282; Y. W. Lam 760.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; pantropics.
Ecology: Streamsides, paddy fields and other moist places. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Nov.

Paspalum conjugatum P. J. Bergius 兩耳草
Acta Helv. Phys.-Math. 7: 129. 1772; FKH 313. 1912; FHN 4: 425. 1977; FRPS 10(1): 288, pl. 88: 1–6. 1990; FFJ 6: 220. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 495, pl. 206, photo 56. 2000; FOC 22: 526. 2006; FGD 9: 427. 2009.

Perennial herb, rhizomatous. Culms in small tufts along rhizomes, 20–60 cm tall. Leaf sheaths keeled, glabrous or pilose along upper margins and mouth; leaf blades linear-lanceolate, thin, 5–20 × 0.5–1.3 cm, glabrous or papillose-pilose along margins, apex acute; ligule very short, a ring of hairs. Inflorescence of a pair of racemes, racemes 6–12 cm; spikelets solitary, in 2 rows; rachis 0.5–1 mm wide, serrate. Spikelets solitary, ovate to suborbicular, 1.5–1.8 mm, 2-floret; lower glume absent; upper glume as long as lower lemma, hyaline, thin, margins with long silky hairs; lower lemma similar but not ciliate; upper lemma pallid at maturity, ovate, margins inrolled embraced same texture palea.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. S. P. Lau 6; Y. S. Lau 1692, 3133.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; tropics and subtropics throughout the world.
Ecology: Grassy fields, margins of forests. Flowering & fruiting: May–Sep.

Paspalum dilatatum Poir. 毛花雀稗
Encycl. 5: 35. 1804; FRPS 10(1): 294, pl. 88: 7–12. 1990; FFJ 6: 221, fig. 187. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 497, pl. 207. 2000; FOC 22: 527. 2006; FGD 9: 428. 2009.

Perennial herb. Culms tuft, erect from a short rhizome, 50–150 cm tall, glabrous. Leaf sheaths glabrous or pilose in the lower part; leaf blades linear, 10–45 × 0.3–1 cm, glabrous; ligule 2–5 mm, truncate, membranous, glabrous. Racemes 2–10, spaced, diverging, axils pilose. Spikelets broadly ovate, in 4-rows, 3–4 mm; lower glume absent; upper glume membranous, as long as spikelet, 5–9-veined, sparsely pubescent to almost glabrous on back, margins fringed with long white hairs; lower floret barren, lemma ovate-lanceolate, 5–7-veined, glabrous; upper lemma pallid at maturity, orbicular, ca. 2 mm, leathery, papillose-striate, apex rounded.

Locality: New Territories. HK sheet 39684, 41557, 42050.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou, Hubei, Jiangxi, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; originated from S America, naturalized elsewhere.
Ecology: Grassy fields, roadsides. Flowering & fruiting: May–Jul.

Paspalum distichum L. 雙穗雀稗
Syst. Nat. ed. 10, 2: 855. 1759; FKH 313. 1912; FHN 4: 426. 1977; FTW ed. 2, 5: 497, pl. 208. 2000; FOC 22: 528. 2006; FGD 9: 428. 2009.
Paspalum paspaloides (Michx.) Scribn., FRPS 10(1): 290, pl. 89: 6–11. 1990; FFJ 6: 220, fig. 186. 1995; Check List HK Plants 342. 2002; 120. 2004.

Perennial herb, rhizomatous. Culms ascending from creeping and rooting base, 20–60 cm tall, nodes usually pubescent. Leaf sheaths shorter than internode, keeled, glabrous, margins ciliate; leaf blades lanceolate, 5–15 × 0.3–0.7 cm, glabrous, apex acute; ligule membranous, 2–3 mm, glabrous. Racemes 2, arising together or separated by a short axis, raceme 3–5 cm; spikelets solitary, in 2 rows; rachis flat, 1.5–2 mm wide. Spikelets obovate-oblong, 3–3.5 mm, loosely pubescent, acute; lower glume usually absent or small; upper glume papery, 3–5-veined with distinct middle vein, loosely appressed pubescent; lower lemma 3–5-veined, usually glabrous, apex acute; upper lemma pale green, subequal to spikelet, cartilaginous, apex apiculate and minutely pubescent.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 2255; Y. W. Lam 2223; HK sheet 39654.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Hubei, Henan, Jiangsu, Shandong, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; tropical and warm-temperate regions of the world.
Ecology: Farmlands, grassy fields, roadsides, ditches and other disturbed places. Flowering & fruiting: May–Sep.

Paspalum longifolium Roxb. 長葉雀稗
Fl. Ind. 1: 283. 1820; FHN 4: 425. 1977; FRPS 10(1): 288, pl. 87: 1–5. 1990; FFJ 6: 222, fig. 188. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 497. 2000; FOC 22: 530. 2006; FGD 9: 429. 2009.

Perennial stout herb. Culms tufted, erect, 80–150 cm tall, many-noded, glabrous. Leaf sheaths longer than internode, keeled, papillose-pilose along margins; leaf blades linear, 10–60 × 0.5–1.2 cm, glabrous, apex acuminate; ligule membranous, 1–2 mm. Inflorescence axis 4–10 cm; racemes 5–20, 4–8 cm, ascending; spikelets normally paired, occasionally solitary but 2nd vestigial spikelet present; densely overlapping; rachis broadly winged, purplish, margins scabrous with conspicuous close-set teeth. Spikelets purple or pale green, broadly obovate, paired, in 4 rows; lower glume absent; upper glume as long as lower lemma, membranous, 3-veined, minutely crisped-pubescent, apex slightly acute; upper lemma pallid, yellow-green, indurate.

Locality: Tai Tam, Lin Tong Mei. P. S. Choi 521; HK sheet 41949.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Indian Subcontinent, Indochina, Malay Peninsula, Indonesia, Pacific islands, N Australia.
Ecology: Hillslopes, grassy fields, swampy places. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Oct.

Paspalum scrobiculatum L. 鴨乸草
Mant. Pl. 1: 29. 1767; FHK 408. 1861; FKH 313. 1912; FRPS 10(1): 282, pl. 85: 1–6. 1990; FFJ 6: 223. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 500. 2000; FOC 22: 528. 2006; FGD 9: 430. 2009.

Perennial or annual herb. Culms tufted, erect or decumbent at base, 90–150 cm tall. Leaf sheaths longer or upper shorter than internode, compressed, keeled, usually glabrous; leaf blades lanceolate or linear-lanceolate, 10–20 × 0.4–1.2 cm, usually glabrous, base subrounded, apex acuminate, margins scabrous; ligule membranous, 0.5–1 mm. Inflorescence of 2–5(–8) racemes, subdigitate or on a short axis; racemes 3–10 cm, ascending to widely spreading. Spikelets usually solitary, suborbicular or broadly elliptic, 2–3 mm, glabrous; lower glume absent; upper glume membranous, 7–13-veined; lower lemma 7 –9-veined, veins often concolorous with back; upper lemma dark brown at maturity.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1037, 1870; HK sheet 36082.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Taiwan; India, tropical SE Asia.
Ecology: Wastelands, roadsides. Flowering & fruiting: May–Sep.

Paspalum scrobiculatum L. var. orbiculare (G. Forst.) Hack. 圓果雀稗
Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 6: 233. 1885; FOC 22: 529. 2006; FGD 9: 430. 2009.
Paspalum orbiculare G. Forst., Fl. Ins. Austr. 7. 1786; FHN 4: 427. 1977; FFJ 6: 223, fig. 190. 1995; FRPS 10(1): 284, pl. 87: 12 – 16. 1990; FTW ed. 2, 5: 500. 2000; Check List HK Plants 342. 2002; 120. 2004.

Spikelets elliptic or broadly obovate, 2–2.2 mm, often paired, imbricate, in 2 rows; lower glume absent; upper glume as long as lower lemma, membranous, 3–5-veined, slightly acute; upper lemma yellow-brown or mid-brown at maturity, as long as spikelet.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 3181; Y. W. Lam 2176; HK sheet 41983.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; SE Asia, Australia, Pacific islands (Polynesia).
Ecology: Hillslopes, roadsides, fields. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Nov.

Paspalum urvillei Steud. 絲毛雀稗
Syn. Pl. Glumac. 1: 24. 1853; FRPS 10(1): 294. 1990; FFJ 6: 221. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 501. 2000; FOC 22: 527. 2006; FGD 9: 428. 2009.

Perennial stout herb, with a short rhizome. Culms tufted, up to 2 m tall, glabrous. Leaf sheaths densely hispid, with long hairs at the mouth; leaf blades linear, 15–30 × 0.5–1.5 cm, glabrous or pilose at the base; ligule 3–5 mm, tipped with long hairs. Inflorescence axis 10–40 cm; racemes 10–25, 8–15 cm, narrowly ascending or suberect; spikelets paired, 2–3-rows on one side of rachis; rachis ca. 0.5 mm wide. Spikelets light green or purplish, ovate, 2–3 mm, margins densely covered with silky long hairs, sharply acute; lower glume reduced; upper glume membranous; lower lemma similar to upper glume; upper lemma elliptic, coriaceous, smooth, margins inrolled.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, New Territories. Y. W. Lam 853; S. C. Ng 1850; HK sheet 40839.
Distribution: Fujian, Taiwan (cultivated); native to S America, but widely introduced and naturalized in war areas.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: May – Oct.

Paspalum vaginatum Sw. 海雀稗
Prodr. 21. 1788; H. B. Gill. et al., Fl. Malaya 3: 182. 1971; FRPS 10(1): 290, pl. 89: 1–5. 1990; FTW ed. 2, 5: 501. 2000; FOC 22: 528. 2006; FGD 9: 428. 2009.

Perennial halophilous herb, with short rhizome and long stolons. Culms solitary or tufted, many-noded, flowering culm 6–60 cm tall. Leaf sheaths longer than internode, imbricate, often keeled, margins membranous, mouth with long pilose; leaf blades linear, 2.5–15 × 0.3–0.8 cm, inrolled, acute; ligule membranous, truncate, 0.5–1 mm. Inflorescence of (1–)2(–3) racemes arising together at culm apex; racemes 2–5 cm, usually closely approximate when young, later spreading; spikelets solitary, in 2 rows; rachis 1–2 mm wide, glabrous, triangular, often zigzag. Spikelets ovate-lanceolate, 3.5–4 mm, acute; lower glume absent or rarely a tiny vestige; upper glume thin papery or membranous, midvein often compressed, glabrous; lower lemma similar to upper glume, glabrous; upper lemma 2.5–3 mm, shorter than spikelet, cartilaginous, apex minutely pubescent; upper palea ca. 2/3 length of upper lemma.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. W. Lam 1639; K. L. Yip 4208; HK sheet 37212.
Distribution: Hainan, Taiwan, Yunnan; tropics and subtropics throughout the world.
Ecology: Sandy seashores, margins of streams. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Sep.

Pennisetum alopecuroides (L.) Spreng. 狼尾草
Syst. Veg. 1: 303. 1825; FRPS 10(1): 366, pl. 111: 1 – 4. 1990; FFJ 6: 197, fig. 164. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 502, pl. 209. 2000; FOC 22: 550. 2006; FGD 9: 444. 2009.
Panicum alopecuroides L., Sp. Pl. 1: 55. 1753.
Pennisetum compressum R. Br., Prod. 195. 1810; FKH 316. 1912.
Gymnothrix japonica Benth., FHK 413. 1860.

Perennial herb. Culms erect, tufted, 30 – 120 cm tall, hispid below inflorescence. Leaf sheaths longer than internode at the upper part, keeled, imbricate at base; leaf blades linear, flat or often involute, 10 – 80 × 0.3 – 1 cm, base papillose-hispid, apex long acuminate; ligule a ring of hairs, ca. 0.5 mm. Panicle cylindrical, spike-like, 5 – 25 × 1.5 – 3.5 cm; axis hispid, peduncle stumps short with crateriform tips; involucre usually enclosing one spikelet, rarely 2, basal stipe (1 – )2 – 3 mm; bristles greenish or purple, longest 2 – 3 cm but not conspicuously longer than the others, all slender, hispid. Spikelet solitary, seldom paired, lanceolate, 5 – 8 mm; lower glume minute or absent; upper glume ovatelanceolate, 1/3 – 2/3 length of spikelet, 3 – 5-veined; lower lemma as long as spikelet, 7 – 11-veined; upper lemma lanceolate, as long as spikelet, 3 – 7-veined, margins inrolled embraced same texture palea; lodicules 2; stamens 3, style base connate. Caryopsis oblong.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1504; HK sheet 39643, 40814.
Distribution: Widely spread over most provinces of China; and tropical Asia, naturalized elsewhere.
Ecology: Grassy fields, roadsides, paths between paddy fields. Flowering & fruiting: Summer to autumn.

Pennisetum polystachion (L.) Schult. 牧地狼尾草（多穗狼尾草）
Mant. 2: 146. 1824; FTW ed. 2, 5: 505. 2000; FOC 22: 550. 2006; FGD 9: 444. 2009.
Panicum polystachion L., Syst. Nat., ed. 10, 2: 870. 1759.
Pennisetum setosum (Sw.) Rich., Syn. Pl. 1: 72. 1805; FRPS 10(1): 365. 1990.

Perennial or annual herb with short rhizomes. Culms tufted, 50–150 cm tall. Leaf sheath loose, hispid, margin ciliate. Leaf blades linear, 10–20 × 0.3–1.5 cm, hispid; ligule a ring of long hairs, ca. 1 mm. Panicle contracted panicle, yellow or purplish, 10–25 cm; bristles unequal, outer ones shorter, inner ones feathery, up to 1 cm. Spikelet ovate-lanceolate, 3–5 mm; lower glume absent or a small triangular scale; upper glume as long as spikelet or slightly longer, 5-veined; lower floret staminate or neuter, lemma similar but slightly shorter than spikelet, 5-veined, obtusely 3-lobed; upper floret shorter than spikelet, cartilaginous, smooth, shiny, readily deciduous at maturity.

Locality: New Territories. L. T. Lo 411; Y. W. Lam 1205; HK sheet 42645.
Distribution: Hainan, Taiwan; native to Africa, naturalized throughout the tropics.
Uses: Animal food (potential as forage).
Notes: The species was reported as Pennisetum polystachyum (L.) Schult. previously (Check List HK Plants 343. 2002; 120. 2004).

Pennisetum purpureum Schumach. 象草
Beskr. Guin. Pl. 44. 1827; FRPS 10(1): 373, pl. 111: 5–8. 1990; FFJ 6: 198, fig. 165. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 505. 2000. FOC 22: 550. 2006; FGD 9: 443. 2009.

Perennial herb. Culms stout, erect, 2–4 m tall. Leaf sheaths glabrous or hispid; leaf blades linear, flat, 20–50 × 1–2 cm, adaxial surface hispid or papillos-pilose at base, abaxial surface glabrous, margins scabrous; ligule 1.5–5 mm, ciliate. Panicle golden, brownish or purplish, cylindrical, 10–30 × 1–3 cm; axis densely pilose, closely beset with small peduncle stumps. Spikelets solitary or 2–3-fasciculate, subsessile, lanceolate, 5–8 mm, subrounded by an involucre of bristles, falling off together with spikelet at maturity; lower glume ca. 0.5 mm or absent; upper glume lanceolate, 1/4–1/2 length of spikelet; lower floret staminate or neuters, lemma 1/2–4/5 spikelet length, 5–7-veined; upper lemma as long as spikelet, smooth and shiny, 5-veined; lodicules 2, small; stamens 3, anthers with a tuft of short hairs at tip; style base connate.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 1674; L. T. Lo 38; Y. W. Lam 1206.
Distribution: Fujian, Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan, Jiangxi, Jiangsu, Fujian, Taiwan; native to Africa.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Oct.
Uses: Environmental (erosion control), animal food (forage).

Perotis indica (L.) Kuntze 茅根
Rev. Gen. Pl. 2: 787. 1891; FHN 4: 393, fig. 1202. 1977; FRPS 10(1): 124. 1990; FTW ed. 2, 5: 431, pl. 176. 2000; FOC 22: 498. 2006; FGD 9: 365, fig. 177. 2009.
Anthoxanthum indicum L., Sp. Pl. 1: 28. 1753.
Perotis latifolia Aiton, Hort. Kew. 1: 85. 1789; FHK 418. 1861; FKH 318. 1912.

Annual herb. Culms loosely tufted, erect or decumbent at base, 20–30 cm tall. Leaf blades lanceolate to narrowly ovate, flat or margins involute, tough, 2–4 × 0.2–0.6 cm, glaucous, glabrous, margins spiny-scabrous especially near base, apex acute; ligule membranous, ca. 0.5 mm; leaf sheaths usually glabrous. Inflorescence a terminal raceme, up to 13 cm, ascending or horizontally spreading; rachis scabrous. Spikelets 1-flowered, 1.5–2.5 mm (excluding awns); basal callus 0.2–0.5 mm, subacute; glumes papery, narrowly lanceolate, back uniformly hirtellous with short white hairs, midvein scabrous, apex obtuse, clearly demarcated from awn; lower glume ca. 1.8 mm, awn ca. 10 mm; upper glume ca. 1.5 mm, awn ca. 5 mm; lemma hyaline, lanceolate, 0.5–1 mm. Anthers ca. 0.3 mm. Caryopsis terete, narrowly ellipsoidal, 1–1.8 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. S. Y. Hu & P. P. H. But 22370.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Yunnan, Shandong, Taiwan; Indochina, Malesia, Indian Subcontinent.
Ecology: Sandy stream banks, roadsides and other weedy places. Flowering & fruiting: Summer to autumn.

Perotis rara R. Br. 大花茅根
Prodr. 172. 1810; FOC 22: 498. 2006; FGD 9: 365. 2009.
Perotis macrantha Honda, Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 41: 638. 1927; FRPS 10(1): 122, pl. 38: 1–3. 1990; FFJ 6: 174, fig. 142. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 431. 2000; Check List HK Plants 343. 2002; 120. 2004.

Annual or short-lived perennial herb. Culms loosely tufted, decumbent at base, 20–40 cm tall. Leaf blades lanceolate to narrowly ovate, flat or margins involute, tough, 1.5–5 × 0.2–0.5 cm, glabrous, glaucous, margins spiny-scabrous, pectinate at base, apex acute; ligule ca. 0.2 mm, minutely ciliate on upper margin; leaf sheaths glabrous. Inflorescence a single terminal raceme, up to 20 cm, with laxly arranged spikelets, horizontally spreading, lightly reflexed at maturity; rachis scaberuloushirtellous. Spikelets 1-flowered, 3.5–4.5 mm (excluding awns); basal callus 0.5–1.5 mm, narrowly obconical, flattened, sometimes laterally pubescent; glumes linear-lanceolate, back evenly scaberulous-hirtellous with short white hairs, midvein scabrous with longer prickles toward awn, apex gradually tapering into awn; awn 1–2.5 cm; lemma lanceolate, hyaline, acute, 1.2–1.5 mm; palea hyaline, ca. 0.8 mm, minutely ciliate at the apex. Anthers ca. 0.6 mm. Caryopsis terete, subulate, ca. 2.5 mm.

Locality: Deep Water Bay, Sai Kung. HK sheet 8830, 35664.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; SE Asia, New Guinea, Australia.
Ecology: Coastal sandy places. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Nov.

Phalaris canariensis L. 加那利虉草（虉草）
Sp. Pl. 1: 54. 1753; FTW ed. 2, 5: 361. 2000; FOC 22: 335. 2006.

Annual herb. Culms loosely tufted, 30–60(–100) cm tall, glabrous. Leaf blades 10–30 × 0.5–1.2 cm, glabrous; ligule acute, 3–8 mm; leaf sheaths cylindrical, mostly shorter than the internode. Panicle spike-like, 1.5–4 × 1.5–2 cm, ovate to oblong-ovate. Spikelets obovate, 3-flowered, extremely compressed, 6–9 mm; glumes 7–10 mm, oblanceolate, glabrous or puberulent, whitish with green longitudinal stripes, keel broadly winged above middle, apex acute; sterile lemmas 2, equal, narrowly elliptic, chaffy, 2.5–4 mm, appressed-pilose; fertile lemma lanceolate, 5–6 mm, shiny, densely appressed-pubescent; palea oblong, 2-veined. Anthers 3–4 mm.

Locality: Clear Water Bay (cultivated). L. T. Lo 615.
Distribution: Hebei, Shanghai, Taiwan (cultivated or naturalized); native to Madagascar and N Africa, naturalized throughout the world.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Oct.

Phragmites australis (Cav.) Trin. ex Steud. 蘆葦
Nomecl. Bot. ed. 2, 1: 143. 1840; FFJ 6: 129, fig. 100. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 329. 2000; FRPS 9(2): 27, pl. 4: 3, 3a. 2002; FOC 22: 449. 2006; FGD 9: 338, fig. 158. 2009.
Arundo australis Cav., Hist., Nat. 1: 100. 1799.
Arundo phragmites L., Sp. Pl. 81. 1753.
Phragmites communis Trin., Fund. Agrostis 134. 1820; FKH 328. 1912.

Perennial reed, with creeping rhizomes. Culms erect, 1.5–3(–6) m tall, ca. 6 mm in diam., usually farinose below nodes. Leaf blade linear-lanceolate, 15–45(–60) × 1–3.5 cm, smooth or margins scabrous; ligule a minute membranous rim, ca. 1 mm, ciliate, hairs 0.2–0.6 mm; leaf sheaths glabrous or thinly hairy. Panicle 10–40 cm, usually hirsute at axils of lower branches; pedicels 2–4 mm, glabrous or pilose at base. Spikelets 10–20 mm, florets 4–5; glumes lanceolate, 3-veined, lower glume up to 1/2 length of lowest lemma, 3–7 mm; upper glume 5–10 mm, sharply acute, usually apiculate; lowest lemma linear-lanceolate, 8–15 mm; floret callus elongate with hairs equal to lemma; palea 2.5–4 mm, 2-keeled, margins minutely ciliate, apex truncate.

Locality: New Territories, Lantau Island. HK sheet 8663, 16103, 16109.
Distribution: A worldwide weed.
Ecology: Beaches, river banks, margins of ponds. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Nov.
Uses: Environmental (ornamental, erosion control).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Mai Po, Castle Peak, Lin Au, Sai Kung, Lantau Island, Soko Islands
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Phragmites vallatorius (L.) Veldkamp 卡開蘆
Blumea 37(1): 233. 1992; FTW ed. 2, 5: 332. 2000.
