Arundo vallatoria Pluk. ex L., Herb. Amb. 15. 1754.
Phragmites karka (Retz.) Trin. ex Steud., Nomenl. Bot., ed. 2, 1: 144. 1840; FKH 328. 1912; FHN 4: 368. 1977; FFJ 6: 129. 1995; FRPS 9(2): 25, pl. 4: 4, 4a. 2002; FOC 22: 449. 2006; FGD 9: 337. 2009; Check List HK Plants 344. 2002; 120. 2004.
Arundo karka Retz., Observ. Bot. 4: 21. 1786.
Phragmites karka (Retz.) Trin. ex Steud. var. cincta Hook. f., Fl. Brit. India 7: 305. 1897; FHN 4: 368. 1977.

Perennial reed, 4–6 m tall, with creeping rhizomes. Culms very stout, woody, 1.5–2.5 cm in diam. Leaf blades linearlanceolate 20–50 × 2–3 cm, base slightly narrowed, apex long acuminate, glabrous; ligule 0.3–1 mm, upper margin ciliolate; leaf sheaths glabrous. Panicle 30–60 × 10–20 cm, copiously branched; branches mostly in whorls, the lowermost branches bare of spikelets toward base, ± glabrous at insertion. Spikelets 9–12 mm, 4–6-flowered, rachilla-hairs 4 – 7 mm, rather sparse; glumes lanceolate-elliptic, obtuse to acuminate, lower glume up to 1/2 length of the upper lowest lemma, 2.5–4 mm, upper glume 4–6 mm; lowest lemma narrowly elliptic, 7–12 mm; bisexual lemmas linear-lanceolate, 8.5–11 mm, apex long attenuate; floret callus elongate with 4–8 mm hairs; palea 3 mm, 2-keeled, margins minutely ciliate, apex truncate.

Locality: Mai Po, Castle Peak, Lin Au, Sai Kung, Lantau Island, Soko Islands. Y. W. Lam 1300; HK sheet 40925, 41502.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan, Fujian, Taiwan; tropical Asia, N Australia, Pacific islands, Africa.
Ecology: Beaches, river banks, shady roadsides, swamps. Flowering & fruiting: Autumn.
Uses: Environmental (ornamental, erosion control).

Phyllostachys aurea Carrière ex Rivière & C. Rivière 人面竹
Bull. Soc. Natl. Acclim. France, sér. 3. 5: 716. 1878; FTW 5: 723, pl. 1489. 1978; HKB 67. 1985; FRPS 9(1): 255, pl. 67: 5–7. 1996; FOC 22: 168. 2006; FGD 9: 319, fig. 150. 2009.
Phyllostachys bambusoides Siebold & Zucc. var. aurea (Carrière ex Rivière & C. Rivière) Makino, Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 11: 158. 1897.
Phyllostachys breviligula W. T. Lin & Z. M. Wu, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 26(3): 229, pl. 8. 1988.
Phyllostachys formosana Hayata, Icon. Pl. Form. 6: 140. 1916.
Phyllostachys reticulata (Ruprecht) K. Koch var. aurea (Carrière ex Rivière & C. Rivière) Makino, Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 26: 22. 1912.

Culms 5–12 m, 2–5 cm in diam.; internodes 15–30 cm, usually strongly shortened and commonly ventricose at basal nodes, distally inflated for several minimetres below node at mid-culm and basal nodes, initially white powdery, glabrous; wall 4 – 8 mm thick; nodal ridge as prominent as sheath scar or slightly more prominent; sheath scar initially fringed with white pubescence. Culm sheaths yellowgreen or pale red-brown, becoming straw-coloured, with variably sized brown spots, base edged with white pubescence; auricles and oral setae absent; ligule yellow-green, truncate or weakly convex at apex, very short, 1–2 mm, margin longer pale green ciliate; blade reflexed, green, with yellow margins, linear, flat or crinkled in upper sheaths. Leaves 2–3 per ultimate branch; sheath glabrous; auricles and oral setae absent or deciduous; ligule short; blade 6–12 × 1–1.8 cm, abaxially pilose especially near petiole.

Locality: Kadoorie Farm (cultivated). Nan-Zhu 2874.
Distribution: Guangdong, Fujian, Zhejiang.
Uses: Ornamental.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Victoria Peak, Sheung Shui, Lantau Island (cultivated)
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Phyllostachys reticulata (Rupr.) K. Koch 桂竹
Dendrologie. 2(2): 356. 1873; FOC 22: 176. 2006; FGD 9: 322. 2009.
Bambusa reticulata Rupr., Bambuseae, 58. 1839.
Phyllostachys bambusoides Siebold & Zucc., Abh. Math.-Phys. Cl. Königl. Bayer. Akad. Wiss. 3(3): 746, pl. 5, fig. 3. 1843; FTW 5: 725, pl. 1490. 1978; HKB 68. 1985; FRPS 9(1): 292. 1996; Check List HK Plants 344. 2002; 120. 2004.
Phyllostachys lithophila Hayata, Icon. Pl. Formosan. 6: 141, fig. 51. 1916.
Phyllostachys megastachya Steud., Flora 29: 21. 1846.
Phyllostachys pinyanensis T. H. Wen, Bull. Bot. Res., Harbin 2(1): 67, fig. 6. 1982.
Phyllostachys quilioi Rivière & C. Rivière, Bull. Soc. Natl. Acclim. France 5: 697, fig. 24 – 27. 1878.

Culms to 20 m, to ca. 15 cm in diam.; internodes to 40 cm, not white powdery or initially faintly so below nodes, glabrous; wall ca. 5 mm thick; nodal ridge slightly more prominent than sheath scar. Culm sheaths yellow-brown, sometimes tinged with green or purple, with dense, variably sized, purple-brown spots, glabrous or sparsely deciduously erectly brown hairy; auricles deciduous, sometimes absent, purple-brown, small to large and falcate; oral setae radiate; ligule brown or green, arcuate, ciliate; blade reflexed, green in centre, purple or brown on both sides, pale yellow along margins, linear, flat or sometimes slightly wavy at apex. Leaves 2–4 per ultimate branch; auricles suborbicular; oral setae well developed, radiate; ligule obviously exserted, arcuate or sometimes truncate; blade 5.5–15 × 1.5–2.5 cm. Flowering branchlets spicate, 5–8(–10) cm, scaly bracts 3–5; spathes 6–8; auricles small or inconspicuous, oral setae usually developed, blade orbicular-ovate to linear-lanceolate, base rounded, apex subulate-acuminate. Pseudospikelets 1–2(–3) per spathe, absent from basal 1–3 deciduous spathes. Spikelets lanceolate, 2.5–3 cm; florets 1–2(–3). Glumes absent or 1; rachilla pubescent, extension glabrous, terminated with a rudimentary floret; lemma 2–2.5 cm, sparsely puberulent, apex aristulate-acuminate; palea slightly shorter than lemma, glabrous except for keels or pubescent at apex; lodicules rhomboid-oblong, 3.5–4 cm. Anthers 1.1–1.4 cm. Stigmas 3.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Sheung Shui, Lantau Island (cultivated). Nan-Zhu 2877; S. C. Lau 760; HK sheet 16404.
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangsu, Jiangxi, Shaanxi, Shandong, Sichuan, Taiwan, Yunnan, Zhejiang; Japan.
Ecology: New shoots: Late May.
Uses: Ornamental, materials (construction, flooring and furniture).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Authority: C. Y. Yao & S. Y. Chen

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Sai Kung, Ma On Shan, Mui Tsz Lam, Mau Ping, Sha Tin, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Phyllostachys nidularia Munro 篌竹（白筍竹、花竹）
Gard. Chron., n.s., 6: 773. 1876; FKH 330. 1912; FRPS 9(1): 304. 1996; FOC 22: 178. 2006; FGD 9: 324, fig. 152. 2009.
Phyllostachys cantoniensis W. T. Lin, J. S. China Agric. Univ. 14(3): 112, fig. 4. 1993.
Phyllostachys subulata W. T. Lin & Z. M. Wu, J. Bamboo Res. 13(2): 16, fig. 2. 1994.

Culms to 10 m, to 4 cm in diam., straight; internodes to 30 cm, white powdery, glabrous or initially setulose below nodes; wall ca. 3 mm or more thick; nodal ridge conspicuously elevated, equaling or more prominent than sheath scar; sheath scar flared, glabrous or initially with margin brown setose. Culm sheaths green, unmarked, distally milky-white striped, otherwise usually purple striped, white powdery, densely brown strigose toward base or glabrous, margins purple-red or brown ciliate; auricles at culm apex green-purple, very broad, contiguous with and extending from swollen cupped base of blade; auricles absent on mid- and lower culm; oral setae absent or few, radiate, short; ligule purplebrown, slightly arcuate, broad, margin densely white ciliate; blade erect, broadly triangular to triangular, cupped. Leaves usually 1 per ultimate branch, pendulous; auricles and oral setae weakly developed or absent; ligule short, weakly or not exserted; blade 4–13 × 1–2 cm. Flowering branchlets densely capitate, 1.5–2 cm, scaly bracts 2–4; spathes 1–6, basal ones ovate, distal ones narrower and papery, to 1.6 cm, both sides and apex ± hairy, margins ciliate, blade inconspicuous to narrowly ovate. Pseudospikelets 2 – 8 per spathe; bracts narrow, variable in size or sometimes absent, membranous, keeled, 5–7-veined, pubescent on keels and near apex. Spikelets with 2–5 florets, distal 1–2 sterile. Glumes 1(–3), resembling uppermost bract, to 1.5 cm; rachilla internodes elevated, compressed and sparsely pubescent on side facing floret, apex truncate; lemma leafy, densely hirsute, many-veined, apex acuminate with an awn-like tip, 1st lemma 1–1.2(–1.6) cm; palea shorter than lemma, 0.6–1.1 cm, densely hirsute. Anthers 4.5–5.5 mm. Stigmas (1–)3.

Locality: Sai Kung, Ma On Shan, Mui Tsz Lam, Mau Ping, Sha Tin, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island. Nan-Zhu 2773, 2865; HK sheet 16421.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Henan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Shaanxi, Yunnan, Zhejiang; introduced in Europe and N America.
Ecology: Forests, thickets. New shoots: Apr.–May; flowering: Apr.–May.
Uses: Vegetable (shoots), ornamental.

Phyllostachys nigra (Lodd. ex Lindl.) Munro 紫竹
Trans. Linn. Soc. London. 26: 38. 1868; FTW 5: 730, pl. 1493. 1978; HKB 71. 1985; FRPS 9(1): 288. 1996; FOC 22: 175. 2006; FGD 9: 321. 2009.
Bambusa nigra Lodd. ex Lindl., Penny Cyclop. 3: 357. 1835.
Phyllostachys filifera McClure, Lingnan Univ. Sci. Bull. 9: 42. 1940.
Phyllostachys nana Rendle, J. Linn. Soc. 36: 441. 1904.
Phyllostachys nigripes Hayata, Icon. Pl. Form. 6: 142, fig. 53. 1916.

Culms 4–8(–10) m, to 5 cm or more in diam.; initially green, gradually developing purple-brown or brown-black spots and patches, or finally becoming uniformly purple-brown or brown-black, 25–30 cm, initially white powdery, densely puberulent; wall ca. 3 mm thick; nodal ridge slightly more prominent than or equaling sheath scar; sheath scar initially brown hairy on margin. Culm sheaths redbrown, sometimes tinged with green, unmarked or densely extremely minutely and imperceptibly dark brown spotted, spots aggregating into a distal dark brown patch, thinly white powdery, brown strigose; auricles and oral setae well developed, purple-black; ligule purple, arcuate to acutely so, long ciliate; blade erect or gradually deflexed, green or tinged with purple on both sides, triangular to triangularlanceolate, navicular, ± wavy. Leaves 2–3 per ultimate branch; auricles weak or absent; oral setae deciduous; ligule slightly exserted; blade thin, 7–10 × ca. 1.2 cm. Flowering branchlets shortly spicate, 3.5–5 cm, scaly bracts 4–8. Spathes 4–6, glabrous or puberulous; auricles absent; oral setae few or absent; blade usually subulate or ovate-lanceolate, small. Pseudospikelets 1–3 per spathe. Spikelets lanceolate, 1.5–2 cm; florets 2–3. Glumes (absent or)1–3, abaxially ± distally pubescent; rachilla pubescent; lemma 1.2–1.5 cm, densely pubescent; palea shorter than lemma. Anthers ca. 8 mm. Stigmas 3.

Locality: Lung Tsai Ng Yuen (cultivated). Nan-Zhu 2794; N. K. Chun 2840; HK sheet 35371.
Distribution: S Hunan, cultivated elsewhere in China.
Ecology: New shoots: late Apr.; flowering: May.
Uses: Ornamental.

Poa annua L. 早熟禾
Sp. Pl. 1: 68. 1753; FFJ 6: 141. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 386. 2000; FRPS 9(2): 159. 2002; FOC 22: 263. 2006; FGD 9: 386, fig. 194. 2009.

Annual or biennial herb, 6–30 cm tall. Culms loosely tufted, erect or geniculate at base, smooth. Leaf blades flat or folded, thin, 1–12 cm × 1–2(–5) mm, apex acutely prow-tipped, often transversely wrinkled, margins slightly scabrid; ligules membranous, collar-shaped, 1–3 mm, glabrous, apex obtuse, margin irregularly dentate, smooth; leaf sheaths slightly compressed, thin, smooth, uppermost closed for ca. 1/3 of length. Panicle open, broadly ovoid to pyramidal, (1–)3–10 cm. Spikelets ovate to oblong, dark to light green, (3–)4–6 mm, florets 3–5, distal fertile florets often female; rachilla internodes 0.5–1.5 mm, smooth, glabrous; glumes unequal, smooth or rarely keeled with hooks, the lower lanceolate to ovate, 1.5–3mm, 1-veined, the upper elliptic or oblong, 2–4 mm, 3-veined; lemmas ovate, 2.2–4 mm, apex and margins broadly membranous; palea narrowly lanceolate, apex blunt to acute, 2–2.5 mm, 2-veined, villous on veins. Anthers 0.6–1 mm. Caryopsis ellipsoidal, 1–1.5 mm, apex villous.

Locality: Sha Tin. Y. S. Lau 2958; HK sheet 30339.
Distribution: A worldwide weed, also widely distributed in China.
Ecology: Moist shady places. Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: Apr.–Jul.
Uses: Animal food (fodder).

Pogonatherum crinitum (Thunb.) Kunth 金絲草
Enum. Pl. 1: 478. 1833; FHN 4: 457, fig. 1246. 1977; FFJ 6: 237, fig. 204. 1995; FRPS 10(2): 106, pl. 24: 14–21. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 5: 570, pl. 240. 2000; FOC 22: 591. 2006; FGD 9: 470, fig. 245. 2009.
Andropogon crinitus Thunb., Syst. Veg. (ed. 14) 903. 1784.
Pogonatherum saccharoideum auct. non P. Beauv.: FHK 421. 1861; FKH 320. 1912.

Perennial herb. Culms erect or geniculate, tufted, 10–30 cm tall, nodes bearded. Leaf sheaths glabrous or puberulous, mouth long ciliate; leaf blades linear, flat, 1.5–5 × 0.1–0.4 cm, inrolled, scaberulous-puberulous, apex acute; ligule short, ciliate. Inflorescence a solitary raceme, yellowish; rachis internodes and pedicels both compressed, 1/3–2/3 spikelet length, hairs silky white. Sessile spikelet 1–2 mm, membranous; callus hairs equal to or slightly longer than spikelet; lower glume flat, scabrid on abaxial surface, apex truncate, ciliate with ca. 0.2 mm hairs; upper glume boat-shaped, 1-veined to keeled, awn 1.5–1.8 cm; lower floret absent or only lemma present; upper lemma slightly shorter than lower glume, 2-lobed, with an slender awn from the sinus; awn 1.5–2.5 cm, strongly geniculate near base, palea shorter than lemma, broad ovate, 2-veined; stamen 1, anther ca. 1 mm. Pedicellate spikelet similar to sessile spikelet but smaller; lower glume awnless. Caryopsis ovate-oblong.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 2177; Y. S. Lau 1041, 1791.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Indian Subcontinent, Indochina, Malesia, New Guinea, Australia (Queensland).
Ecology: Forests, ravines, shade and moist places along roadsides and streams. Flowering & fruiting: May–Sep.
Uses. Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): High Island, Sai Kung, Sha Lo Tung
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Pogonatherum paniceum (Lam.) Hack. 金髮草
Allg. Bot. Z. Syst. 12: 178. 1906; FRPS 10(2): 102, pl. 24: 1–13. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 5: 570. 2000; FYN 9: 631, fig. 106: 1–3. 2003; FOC 22: 592. 2006; FGD 9: 470. 2009.

Saccharum paniceum Lam., Encycl. 1: 595. 1785. Pogonatherum saccharoideum P. Beauv., Ess. Agrostogr. 56: 176–177, pl. 11, fig. 7. 1812, nom. illeg. superfl.; FHK 421. 1861; FKH 320. 1912. Perennial herb. Culms tufted, 30–60 cm tall, nodes bearded. Leaf sheaths glabrous or puberulous, mouth long ciliate; leaf blades stiff, 1.5–5.5 × 0.15–0.4 cm, scabrid, apex acuminate. Raceme 1.3–3 cm (excluding awns), yellowish; rachis internodes and pedicels ca. 1/2 spikelet length, hairs silky white. Sessile spikelet 2.5–3 mm, thinly cartilaginous; callus hairs shorter than spikelet; lower glume scabrid or puberulous on back, apex ciliate with 0.5–1 mm hairs; upper glume awn 1–2 cm; lower floret male, lemma slightly shorter than lower glume, palea subequaling lemma; awn of upper lemma 1.5–2 cm, weakly geniculate near base, column not strongly demarcated, limb very fine. Stamens 2, anthers ca. 1.8 mm. Pedicellate spikelet similar to sessile spikelet but smaller; lower glume awnless.

Locality: High Island, Sai Kung, Sha Lo Tung. S. Y. Hu 8555, 8901; S. Y. Hu & P. P. H. But 20719 (CUHK).
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hubei, Hunan, Sichuan, Taiwan, Yunnan; Afghanistan, Bhutan, India, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, Nepal, Pakistan, Thailand, Vietnam, SW Asia (Arabia), Australia (Queensland).
Ecology: Hillslopes, roadsides, streams; alt. 100–2300 m. Flowering & fruiting: Mar.–Oct.

Polypogon fugax Nees ex Steud. 棒頭草
Syn. Pl. Glumac. 1: 184. 1854; FFJ 6: 123, fig. 92. 1995; FOC 22: 362. 2006; FGD 9: 393. 2009.
Polypogon littoralis auct. non Sm.: FHK 427. 1861; FKH 326. 1912.

Annual herb, 10–75 cm tall. Culms tufted, geniculate at base, mostly glabrous. Leaf blades narrowly to broadly linear, 2.5–15 × 3–4 cm, scabrid or abaxial surface smooth, apex acute; ligule membranous, 3–8 mm, apex 2-fid or irregularly toothed. Panicle spikelike, 4–15 × 1–3.5 cm, pale green or tinged with purple; branches narrowly ascending, up to 4 cm, bearing densely clustered spikelets. Spikelets narrowly oblong, 1-flowered, 2–2.5 mm; glumes narrowly oblong, puberulous, vein scabrid-aculeate, margins ciliate in lower half, slightly notched at the apex, with an awn equal to or shorter than glume body; lemma papery, elliptic, 1–1.2 mm, apex shortly 4-toothed, midvein extended into a fine, straight, ca. 2 mm awn; palea membranous, as long as lemma, oblong. Stamens 3. Anthers ca. 0.7 mm. Caryopsis ellipsoidal, ca. 1 mm.

Locality: No precise locality. HK sheet 41965.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Xinjiang, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Shanxi, Henan, Hubei, Anhui, Shandong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; tropical and warmtemperate regions of Asia.
Ecology: Farmlands and other moist places. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Sep.

Polypogon monspeliensis (L.) Desf. 長芒棒頭草
Fl. Atlant. 1: 67. 1798; FKH 326. 1912; FRPS 9(3): 253, pl. 62: 1–3. 1987; FFJ 6: 123, fig. 93. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 364. 2000; FOC 22: 362. 2006; FGD 9: 394, fig. 201. 2009.
Alopecurus monspeliensis L., Sp. Pl. 1: 61. 1753.

Annual herb, up to 60 cm tall. Culms tufted, erect or geniculate at base, 1.5 mm in diam., 2–3-noded. Leaf blades narrowly to broadly linear, 2–13 × 0.2–0.9 cm, adaxial surface and margins scabrid, abaxial surface smooth, apex acute; ligule papery, tongueshaped, 3–8 mm. Panicle spike-like, 1.5–16 × 1–3.5 cm, pale green, thickly clothed in yellow bristles. Spikelets narrowly oblong, 1-flowered, 1.5–3 mm; glumes as long as the spikelet, papery, narrowly obovate-oblong, vein scabrid-aculeate, margins ciliate, slightly notched at the apex, with a 4–7 mm straight awn; lemma papery, obovate, 1–1.2 mm, apex slightly 4-toothed, midvein extended into a fine, readily deciduous awn; palea membranous, as long as lemma, oblong. Stamens 3. Anthers ca. 0.8 mm. Caryopsis obovate-oblong, ca. 1 mm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island. H. G. Goddard s.n. (CUHK).
Distribution: Widely spread over most provinces of China; tropical and warm-temperate regions throughout the world.
Ecology: Moist places, shallow waters. Flowering & fruiting: May–Oct.

Polytrias indica (Houtt.) Veldkamp 單序草
Blumea 36: 180. 1991; FOC 22: 593. 2006.
Phleum indicum Houtt., Nat. Hist. 13: 198. 1782.
Polytrias amaura (Buse) Kuntze, Revis. Gen. Pl. 2: 788. 1891; FRPS 10(2): 99, pl. 23: 1–5. 1997.

Perennial herb. Culms slender, creeping and rooting at lower nodes, flowering shoots ascending, 10–30 cm tall. Leaf sheaths lightly compressed, glabrous or rarely pubescent; leaf blades purplish glaucous, linear-lanceolate, 2–5 × 0.2–0.4 cm, stiffly pilose with tubercle-based hairs, apex acuminate; ligule 0.2–0.5 mm. Raceme 2–7 cm, densely pilose, shortly exserted from uppermost leaf sheath at maturity; rachis internodes and pedicels much shorter than spikelet, golden-ciliate. Spikelets 3 per node, oblong or linear-oblong, brown, densely hairy with soft golden hairs; callus hairs 1/3 spikelet length; lower glume membranous, long villous, hairs extending beyond glume apex; upper glume oblong, submembranous, truncate, densely pubescent except near base, keel villous on the upper; upper lemma shorter than upper glume, cordate, bidenate, ciliate, with an awn (ca. 1 cm) from the sinus, puberulous; anthers 2.5–3 mm, stigmas exserted from apex of spikelet.

Locality: Happy Valley, Repulse Bay. L. T. Lo 216; Y. S. Lau 3079.
Distribution: Vietnam, Myanmar, Malay Peninsula, Indonesia, New Guinea, Philippines; introduced elsewhere as a lawn grass.
Ecology: Grassy places. Flowering & fruiting: Summer to autumn.

Pseudopogonatherum contortum (Brongn.) A. Camus 筆草
Ann. Soc. Linn. Lyon, sér. 2, 68: 205. 1921[1922]; FFJ 6: 247, fig. 215. 1995; FRPS 10(2): 93. 1997; FOC 22: 590. 2006.
Pogonatherum contortum Brongn., Voy. Monde 2(2): 90. 1831.

Annual herb. Culms slender, erect, 25–60 cm tall. Leaf sheaths glabrous; leaf blades narrow linear, involute, 10–30 × 0.1–0.2 cm, abaxial surface glabrous, adaxial surface thinly pilose; ligule ca. 0.2 mm. Racemes 3–6, subdigitate, white hairy, all spikelets pedicellate, falling from pedicels at maturity; pedicels usually unequal, as long as or shorter than internode, villous. Spikelets brown, glossy; callus hairs up to 1/2 spikelet length; lower glume narrowly oblong or lanceolate-oblong; upper glume with mucro or awn 0.5–4(–12) mm; upper lemma entire or minutely toothed; awn 1.5–3 cm, column pilose.

Locality: Sha Tin. S. Y. Hu 12350 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan, Jiangxi, Fujian; Bhutan, Indian Subcontinent, Indochina, Malay Peninsula, Indonesia, Pacific islands, Australia.
Ecology: Grassy hillslopes, open and disturbed grassy hillsides.

Pseudopogonatherum koretrostachys (Trin.) Henrard 刺葉假金髮草
Blumea 4: 521. 1941; FOC 22: 591. 2006.
Andropogon koretrostachys Trin., Mém. Acad. Imp. Sci. St.- Pétersbourg, Sér. 6, Sci. Math. 2: 273. 1833.
Pseudopogonatherum setifolium (Nees) A. Camus in Lecomte, Fl. Gen. de L’IndoChine. 7: 256. 1922; FHN 4: 455. 1977; FRPS 10(2): 96. 1997; FYN 9: 634. 2003; Check List HK Plants 345. 2002; 120. 2004.

Annual herb. Culms erect or geniculately ascending, 30–60 cm tall, glabrous. Leaf sheaths glabrous; leaf blades narrowly linear, usually involute, 5–20 × 0.1–0.2 cm, glabrous or adaxial surface pilose; ligule ca. 0.5 mm, ciliate. Racemes (1–)7–25 or more, subdigitate, 2–8 cm, white hairy, tardily fragile, one spikelet of a pair sessile, the other pedicellate; rachis internodes and pedicels 1/2 spikelet length, villous. Spikelets lanceolate, 2–3 mm, brown; callus hairs 1/5–1/4 spikelet length; lower glume narrowly lanceolateoblong, villous except near apex, sometimes sparsely so or glabrous, upper flanks villous, apex 2-toothed or truncate and minutely 2-mucronate; upper glume boat-shaped, with 3–6 mm awn; lower lemma oblong, ca. 1 mm; upper lemma, shortly 2-toothed; awn 1.5–2 cm, column shortly ciliate, hairs ca. 0.25 mm. Anthers 3, 0.5–0.7 mm. Pedicellate spikelet similar to sessile ones, easily deciduous, maturing before sessile spikelet.

Locality: Sha Tin, Fanling. HK sheet 15587, 31551.
Distribution: S and E China, Yunnan; Malaysia, Indonesia.
Ecology: Hillslopes, roadsides. Flowering and fruiting: Sep.–Nov.

Arundinaria amabilis McClure 茶稈竹（籬竹）
Lingnan Sci. J. 10(1): 6, pl. 1–8. 1931; HKB 21. 1985; FGD 9: 292. 2009.
Pseudosasa amabilis (McClure) Keng f. ex S. L. Chen et al., FRPS 9(1): 641. 1996; FOC 22: 117. 2006.

Culms 7–13 m, 2–6 cm in diam.; internodes terete, olive-green, 30–40(–50) cm, sparsely brown hispidulous at first, glabrescent, initially grey waxy; wall thick; pith lamellate or spongy. Nodal ridge flat or weakly prominent. Branches (1–)3 per node, deflexed, secondary branchlets undeveloped. Culm sheaths gradually deciduous, dark brown, rigid, fragile when dry, densely brown setose abaxially, margins with ciliate, apex truncate; auricles absent; oral setae several, erect, ca. 1.5 cm, undulate; ligule arcuate, irregular, ciliate; blade erect, dark brown, narrowly triangular, scabrid. Leaves 2–3 per ultimate branch; sheath glabrous abaxially, margins ciliolate; auricles minute; oral setae curved, 0.7–1.5 mm; ligule 1–2 mm, densely ciliolate; blade narrowly lanceolate, 16–35 × 1.6–3.5 cm, glabrous, secondary veins 7–9-paired. Inflorescence paniculate with 3–15 spikelets; spikelets 2.5–5.5 cm, rachilla internodes ca. 3 mm; florets 5–16. Glumes 2, unequal, densely puberulous, margins apically densely ciliolate; lemma ovate-lanceolate, densely puberulous; palea broadly lanceolate, keels puberulous. Lodicules unequal. Ovary fusiform, glabrous. Caryopsis 5–6 mm.

Locality: Cultivated. Nan-Zhu 2783, 2866; HK sheet 24998.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, S Jiangxi, Fujian.
Ecology: New shoots: Mar.–May.
Uses: Ornamental, environmental, cane (clums).

Arundinaria cantorii (Munro) L. C. Chia 托竹
Kew Bull. 37(4): 591. 1983; HKB 22. 1985; FGD 9: 294. 2009.
Bambusa cantorii Munro, Trans. Linn. Soc. London 26(1): 111. 1868; FKH 331. 1912.
Arundarbor cantorii (Munro) Kuntze, Revis. Gen. Pl. 2: 761. 1891.
Arundinaria basiaurita W. T. Lin, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 26(3): 231, pl. 10. 1988.
Arundinaria basigibbosa McClure, Lingnan Univ. Sci. Bull. 9: 1. 1940.
Arundinaria funghomii McClure, Lingnan Univ. Sci. Bull. 9: 3. 1940.
Arundinaria pubiannula W. T. Lin & Z. J. Feng, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 30(6): 560 – 561, pl. 2, fig. 5 – 8. 1992.
Pseudosasa cantorii (Munro) Keng f. ex S. L. Chen et al., FRPS 9(1): 654. 1996 [“cantori”]; FOC 22: 120. 2006.
Pseudosasa hainanensis G. A. Fu, J. Bamboo Res. 13(3): 1 – 3, fig. 1. 1994.

Culms 2–4 m, 5–10 mm in diam.; internodes terete, 24–33 cm; nodal ridge obscure. Branches 3 per node. Culm sheaths tardily deciduous, thickly papery or thinly leathery, brownish yellow, ± purplish, ca. 1/2 as long as internodes, glabrous or sparsely brown setose, apex subtruncate or slightly convex, margins densely golden yellow ciliolate; auricles well-developed, semilunar or falcate; oral setae many, erect, wavy, 6–13 mm; ligule arcuate or truncate, slightly concave, scabrid, ciliolate; blade erect, narrowly ovate-lanceolate, glabrous abaxially, basally 1/2–3/5 as wide as sheath apex, margins serrulate. Leaves 5–10 per ultimate branch; sheath stramineous, purplish, ca. 4 mm, glabrous or puberulous abaxially, margins ciliate; auricles falcate or semilunar; oral setae ca. 5 mm, deciduous; ligule truncate, short, slightly hairy, entire or laciniate; blade narrowly lanceolate or oblong-lanceolate, 12–20(–32) × 1.2–2.5(–4.5) cm, both surfaces glabrous, base broadly cuneate, margins serrulate, secondary veins 5–9-paired. Inflorescence paniculate or racemose, terminal on lateral leafy branches; spikelets 3–4 cm, pedicel 0.5–1.5 cm; florets 4–9; rachilla internodes 4–6 mm, flat, thickened toward apex. Glumes 2; lemma 11 mm, 11–13-veined, glabrous abaxially, margins densely ciliolate; palea shorter than lemma, ciliolate along keels and margins, 2–3-veined between keels; lodicules oblong, 2–3 mm; anthers 6–7 mm. Ovary cylindrical, 1.5 mm, glabrous; styles very short; stigmas 3. Caryopsis unknown.

Locality: Sha Tin, Sai Kung, Tai Po Kau, Green Island, Lantau Island. Nan-Zhu 2823, 2875; S. C. Ng 1308.
Distribution: S Fujian, Guangdong, Hainan, S Jiangxi.
Ecology: Hillslopes. New shoots: Mar.
Uses: Environmental.
Notes: The type specimen (Cantor s.n., K) was collected from Lantau Island in 1840. The species epithet was naming after the collector of type materials, Dr. Theodore Cantor.

Arundinaria hindsii Munro 篲竹
Trans. Linn. Soc. London 26(1): 31. 1868; FKH 330. 1912; FTW ed. 2, 5: 596. 2000; FGD 9: 293. 2009.
Pseudosasa hindsii (Munro) S. L. Chen & G. Y. Sheng ex T. G. Liang, Fujian Bamboos. 142. 1987; FRPS 9(1): 653, pl. 119: 11–12. 1996; FOC 22: 120. 2006.
Acidosasa denigrata W. T. Lin, J. South China Agr. Univ. 14(1): 48, fig. 4. 1998.
Arundinaria cerata McClure, Lingnan Univ. Sci. Bull. 9: 2. 1940.
Arundinaria flexuosa Hance, J. Bot. 14(167): 339. 1876.
Arundinaria hirtivaginata W. T. Lin, Bull. Bot. Res., Harbin 12(4): 354, fig. 4. 1992.
Arundinaria maudiae (Dunn) Keng ex Keng f., Techn. Bull. Natl. Forest. Res. Bur. 8: 13. 1948.
Arundinaria multifloscula W. T. Lin, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 26(3): 231–232, pl. 11. 1988.
Arundinaria orthotropoides (W. T. Lin) W. T. Lin, J. Bamboo Res. 19(1): 8. 2000.
Arundinaria panda Keng, Sinensia 7(3): 416, fig. 5. 1936.
Arundinaria quadrangula W. T. Lin & Z. J. Feng, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 30(6): 559, pl. 2, fig. 1–4. 1992.
Arundinaria yangshanensis W. T. Lin, J. Bamboo Res. 16(3): 26, fig. 3. 1997.
Oligostachyum orthotropoides W. T. Lin, J. South China Agr. Univ. 14(1): 49, fig. 5. 1993.
Phyllostachys maudiae Dunn, FKH 10: 330. 1912.
Pleioblastus hindsii (Munro) Nakai, J. Arnold Arbor. 6(3): 146. 1925.
Pleioblastus hispidulus W. T. Lin, J. South China Agr. Univ. 14(1): 50. 1993.
Pleioblastus pandus (Keng) Keng f., Techn. Bull. Natl. Forest. Res. Bur. 8: 14. 1949.
Pseudosasa aureo-vagina W. T. Lin, J. Bamboo Res. 12(3): 4, fig. 5. 1993.
Pseudosasa baiyunensis W. T. Lin, J. Bamboo Res. 13(2): 20, fig. 5. 1994.
Pseudosasa multifloscula (W. T. Lin) W. T. Lin, Guihaia 10(1): 18. 1990.
Pseudosasa nigronodis G. A. Fu, J. Bamboo Res. 15(1): 4, fig. 1. 1996 ["nigro-nodis"].
Thamnocalamus hindsii (Munro) E. G. Camus, Bambusées 52, pl. 25, fig. a. 1913.

Culms 3–5 m, ca. 1 cm in diam.; internodes dark green, 20–36 cm, basal ones glabrous but apical internodes hairy, initially glaucous. Branches 3–5 per node, erect. Culm sheaths persistent, sparsely white or light brown setose; auricles falcate; oral setae curved; ligule arcuate, ca. 3 mm; blade erect, broadly ovate-lanceolate, nearly as wide as sheath apex, base slightly constricted. Leaves 4–9 per ultimate branch; sheath deciduous, glabrous or sparsely setulose, margins ciliolate; auricles absent; oral setae few; ligule truncate, rigid, 1–1.5 mm; pseudopetiole ca. 2 mm; blade linear-lanceolate or narrowly oblong, 7–22 × ca. 1.6 cm, glabrous or abaxially slightly hairy, secondary veins 3–5-paired, base cuneate, one margin spinescently serrulate, other margin entire, apex acuminate. Inflorescence unknown.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, To Fung Shan, Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai, Lantau Island. N. K. Chun 2841; Nan-Zhu 2799; HK sheet 40923.
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang.
Ecology: Coastal hills, mountains. New shoots: May–Jun.
Uses: Environmental.
Notes: The type specimen was collected R. B. Hinds from Victoria Peak in 1841.

Rottboellia cochinchinensis (Lour.) Clayton 筒軸茅
Kew Bull. 35: 817. 1981; FOC 22: 645. 2006; FGD 9: 481, fig. 252. 2009.
Stegosia cochinchinensis Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 51. 1790.
Rottboellia exaltata L. f., Suppl. Pl. 114. 1781[1782], not (L.) L. f. (1779); FKH 321. 1912; FHN 4: 466, fig. 1253. 1977; FFJ 6: 258, fig. 228. 1995; FRPS 10(2): 268, pl. 67: 1–2. 1997; Check List HK Plants 345. 2002; 121. 2004.

Annual herb. Culms stout, 1–3 m tall. Leaf sheaths tuberculatehispid with stiff irritant hairs or sometimes glabrescent; leaf blades linear to linear-lanceolate, 20–50 × 0.5–2.5 cm, glabrous or adaxial surface hispidulous, very scabrid along margins, midrib broad, white, apex acuminate; ligule a ciliate membrane, 1–2 mm. Racemes yellow and green; rachis internode 4–7 mm. Sessile spikelet pale yellow, sunken in a cylindrical rachis-joint; lower glume ovate, minutely scaberulous on abaxial surface, 2-keeled only toward entire or very minutely 2–3-toothed apex, narrow wings along keels; upper glume abaxial convex and keeled, keel with narrow wings, acute; lower floret staminate, lemma oblong, acute, 3-veined; upper floret bisexual, upper lemma broad ovate, acute. Pedicellate spikelet green, variable, 3–5 mm, narrowly ovate, herbaceous.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1046; P. P. H. But 68; P. S. Choi 367.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; widely spread over Old World tropics.
Ecology: Open grassy fields, farmlands. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Oct.

Saccharum arundinaceum Retz. 斑茅（大密）
Observ. Bot. 4: 14. 1786; FKH 319. 1912; FHN 4: 450. 1977; FFJ 6: 250, fig. 218. 1995; FRPS 10(2): 43. 1997; FOC 22: 579. 2006; FGD 9: 458. 2009.

Perennial stout herb. Culms erect, 2–4 m tall, glabrous. Leaf sheaths longer than internode, pilose at mouth and margins; leaf blades linear-lanceolate, (60–)100–200 × 1–2.5 cm, glabrous or adaxial surface with long soft hairs on the base, base narrowing, apex acuminate, margins serrate scabrous; ligule 1–2 mm, membranous, truncate. Panicle large and dense, axis glabrous; rachis internode 3–6 mm, pilose with long silky hairs. Spikelets narrowly lanceolate, callus small, with hairs ca. 1 mm; glumes subequal, lower glume thinly cartilaginous, abaxial surface with silky hairs twice length of spikelet, 2-keeled; upper glume boat-shaped, upper margins ciliate, 3(–5)-veined; lower lemma oblong-lanceolate, subequal to glumes; upper lemma lanceolate, apex mucronate or with awn to 3 mm. Lodicules glabrous. Pedicellate spikelet similar to sessile spikelet; pedicel 3–3.5 mm, with long silk hairs, apex slightly swollen.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 2481; HK sheet 42034.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Gansu, Shaanxi, Hebei, Henan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Indian Subcontinent, Indochina, Malay Peninsula, Indonesia.
Ecology: Hillslopes, rivers and stream banks. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Dec.
Uses: Environmental (erosion control), animal food.

Saccharum fallax Balansa 金貓尾
J. Bot. (Morot). 4: 80. 1890; FYN 9: 604, fig. 102: 9–11. 2003; FOC 22: 581. 2006.
Narenga fallax (Balansa) Bor, Kew Bull. 3: 162. 1948; FHN 4: 449. 1977; FRPS 10(2): 37, pl. 8. 1997; FGD 9: 459, fig. 238. 2009; Check List HK Plants 341. 2002; 119. 2004.

Perennial stout herb. Culms erect, 1.5–3 m tall, nodes bearded with golden-brown hairs, hirsute below panicle. Leaf sheaths usually longer than internode, margin brown-hirsute, nodes with yellow pilose; leaf blades stiff, 40–80 × 1–1.5 cm, uppermost usually very small, glabrous or tuberculate-pilose, base narrowed, apex acuminate, margins scabrid; ligule ca. 1.5 mm, thicken membranous. Panicle loosely oblong in outline, 30–60 cm, axis golden or ferruginous brown pilose, bearded at nodes, many branches per node, branches ascending, primary branches sparsely branched in lower part; racemes flexuosely ascending, densely spiculate; rachis internode and pedicel apex slightly swollen, ciliate. Spikelets oblong-lanceolate, 3–4 mm; callus hairs a little shorter than spikelet, brown; lower glume oblong-lanceolate, papery and becoming herbaceous toward apex, abaxially with brown hairs, apex narrowly truncate; upper glume boat-shaped, 3-veined; lower lemma lanceolate, slightly shorter than glumes, margins ciliate; upper lemma oblong, 1/2 length of glume, obtuse and awnless or minutely mucronate, varying to shortly 2-toothed and awned from sinus; upper palea small; anthers 3.

Locality: Tai Po Kau. Y. S. Lau 3015.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan; Indochina, Myanmar, NE India, Indonesia.
Ecology: Hillslopes. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Oct.

Saccharum officinarum L. 甘蔗
Sp. Pl. 1: 54. 1753; FHK 419. 1861; FKH 319. 1912; H. B. Gill. et al., Fl. Malaya 3: 327. 1971; FHN 4: 450. 1977; FFJ 6: 250. 1995; FRPS 10(2): 41. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 5: 574. 2000; FOC 22: 579. 2006; FGD 9: 458. 2009.

Perennial stout herb. Culms 2–4(–6) m tall, white ciliate below inflorescence, lower internode shorten and swollen. Leaf sheaths longer than internode, glabrous, imbricate, pilose at mouth; leaf blades 70–150 × 4–6 cm, usually glabrous, midrib large and white, margins sharply serrate; ligule 2 mm, membranous, truncate. Panicle dense, very large, up to 50 cm; rachis internode pubescent. Spikelets paired, one sessile, other pedicellate; callus hairs 2–3 times length of spikelet; lower glume oblong, subpapery, 2-keeled, margins membranous; upper glume boat-shaped, 3–5-veined, acute; lower lemma oblong-lanceolate, obscurely 1-veined, acute; upper lemma small, awnless or absent, palea lanceolate; stamens 3; lodicules glabrous. Pedicellate spikelet similar to sessile spikelet; pedicel 3–4 mm, glabrous, apex slightly swollen.

Locality: Cultivated.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, S Hunan, S Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan (cultivated); widely cultivated in warm regions of the world.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Autumn.
Uses: Food (sugar, alcohol, beverage base).

Saccharum spontaneum L. 甜根子草
Mant. Pl. 2: 183. 1771; FKH 319. 1912; FHN 4: 451, fig. 1240. 1977; FFJ 6: 251, fig. 219. 1995; FRPS 10(2): 40, pl. 9: 1 – 6. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 5: 574, pl. 242. 2000; FOC 22: 578. 2006; FGD 9: 457. 2009.

Perennial herb, with long rhizomes. Culms erect, 1–4 m tall, softly pilose below inflorescence. Leaf sheaths pilose at mouth and margin; leaf blades linear, 30–60 × 0.2–0.8 cm, glabrous, tapering to midrib at base, apex acuminate, margins serrate; ligule brown, ca. 2 mm, membranous, apex obtuse, shortly ciliate. Inflorescence a large panicle of about 20 cm; branches erect, rachis and pedicels slender, rachis internodes slightly swollen at apex, pilose with long silky hairs. Spikelets paired, 3–5 mm; callus hairs 3–4 times length of spikelet; lower glume lanceolate, 2-keeled, the upper slightly membranous, margins ciliate; upper glume boat-shaped, keel and margins ciliate, acuminate; lower lemma lanceolate, subequal to glumes, acute, fringed at the apex; upper lemma linear or linear-oblong, awnless; lodicules obovate, ca. 1 mm, ciliate; anthers 3. Pedicellate spikelet similar to the sessile, pedicel 2.5–3 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 3095; HK sheet 8394, 15150.
Distribution: Widely distributed in the warmer regions of Old World.
Ecology: Hillslopes, rivers and stream banks. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Sep.

Sacciolepis indica (L.) Chase 囊穎草（滑草）
Proc. Biol. Soc. Washington. 21: 8. 1908; FHN 4: 410. 1977; FRPS 10(1): 224, pl. 68: 1–7. 1990; FFJ 6: 199, fig. 166. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 509, pl. 212. 2000; FOC 22: 511. 2006; FGD 9: 410, fig. 211. 2009.
Aira indica L., Sp. Pl. 1: 63. 1753.
Panicum indicum auct. non Mill.: FHK 413. 1861; FKH 315. 1912.

Annual herb. Culms usually tufted, erect or geniculate at base, 20–100 cm tall. Leaf sheaths loose, slightly keeled, shorter than internode, glabrous or tuberculate-pilose; leaf blades linear, flat to slightly involute, 5–20 × 0.2–0.5 cm, glabrous or hairy, base slightly narrow, apex acute; ligule membranous, 0.2–0.5 mm, pubescent. Panicle spike-like, 10–16 × 0.3–0.5 cm. Spikelets green or purplish green, ovate-lanceolate, laterally compressed, 2–3 mm, glabrous or papillose-hispid; lower glume 1/3–1/2 length of spikelet, usually 3-veined; upper glume as long as spikelet, dorsally gibbous, 7–11-veined; lower lemma as long as upper glume, usually 9-veined; palea small and absent, hyaline; upper lemma yellowish, narrowly ovate, 1/2 length of spikelet, smooth and glossy. Caryopsis elliptic.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1867; K. L. Yip 4039; HK sheet 35849.
Distribution: Widely spread over E, S, SW and C China; Bhutan, India, Japan, Myanmar, Nepal, Thailand, Vietnam, Africa, Australia, Pacific islands.
Ecology: Margins of paddy fields and other moist places. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Nov.

Sasa subglabra McClure 光笹竹
Lingnan Univ. Sci. Bull. 9: 45. 1940; HKB 75. 1985; FRPS 9(1): 674. 1996; FGD 9: 291. 2009.

Shrubby running bamboo; culms erect, 1.5–2 m tall, 5–6 mm in diam.; internodes terete, 15–20 cm long, smooth and glabrous. Branches usually solitary at each node, (2–)3 at upper nodes. Culm leaves persistent; sheaths tightly culm-clasping, minute hairy abaxially when young, glabrescent, subtruncate at apex, margin densely ciliate; auricles lacking; ligules 1–1.5 mm high; blades erect, lanceolate, hispidulous on both surfaces when young. Foliage leaves: sheaths puberulous when young; auricles lacking; ligules 1–1.5 mm high; blades ovate-lanceolate to oblong-lanceolate, 12–30 cm long, 2.5–5.5 cm wide, shortly pubescent toward base beneath, reticulate veinlets conspicuous.

Locality: Shatin. Nan Zhu 2824, 2835 (CUHK); HK sheet 37522, 37523.
Distribution: Endemic to Hong Kong.
Ecology: Forests.
Notes: The type specimen (H. Fung 21251, SYS, holotype; US, isotype) was collected by H. Fung from Sha Tin Tsuen on 2 May 1938. Discovered in 1938 from Sha Tin Tsuen in ravines on moist clay, this species is endemic to Hong Kong. Up till now, no flowering specimen is available. Therefore its systematic position is still unclear and is thus of special botanical interest. The locality of its occurrence is very close to a village, and its distribution is likely due to folk use. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Schizachyrium brevifolium (Sw.) Nees ex Büse 裂稃草
Pl. Jungh. 3: 359. 1854; FHN 4: 482, fig. 1267. 1977; FFJ 6: 273, fig. 246. 1995; FRPS 10(2): 210, pl. 52: 1–10. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 5: 576, pl. 243. 2000; FOC 22: 622. 2006; FGD 9: 502, fig. 266. 2009.
Andropogon brevifolius Sw., Prodr. 26. 1788; FHK 423. 1861; FKH 323. 1912.

Annual herb. Culms erect or trailing, slender, 10–70 cm long. Leaf sheaths shorter than internode, keeled, glabrous; leaf blades linear to oblong, flat or folded, 1.5–4 × (0.1–)0.2–0.7 cm, glabrous, base subrounded, apex obtuse, margins scabrous; ligule short, membranous. Raceme slender, enclosed at base by spatheole; rachis internodes and pedicels inflated upward, apex cupular and oblique, glabrous to villous. Sessile spikelet linear-lanceolate, ca. 3 mm; lower glume linear-lanceolate, subleathery, abaxially flat, glabrous to thinly pilose, indistinctly 4–5-veined, flanks keeled toward apex, keels wingless, apex minutely 2-toothed; upper glume boat-shaped, thicken membranous, midvein keeled, 3-veined; lemma hyaline membranous; lower lemma linear-lanceolate, slightly shorter than glume, margins ciliate, apex acute; upper lemma 2/3 glume length, 2-lobed to near base; with a flexuous awn arising from sinus, geniculate; style free. Caryopsis linear, flat. Pedicellate spikelet reduced to 1 or 2 glumes, up to 0.7 mm, lower glume with 3–5 mm awn.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1040; P. P. H. But 140; Y. W. Lam 425.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Hubei, Henan, Hebei, Shandong, Anhui, Jiangxi, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Indian Subcontinent, S and SE Asia, Indonesia, Philippines.
Ecology: Open grassy banks, margins of fields, weedy places. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Dec.

Schizachyrium sanguineum (Retz.) Alston 紅裂稃草
Handb. Fl. Ceylon. 6: 334. 1931; FHN 4: 483. 1977; FFJ 6: 273, fig. 247. 1995; FRPS 10(2): 212, pl. 52: 11–12. 1997; FOC 22: 622. 2006; FGD 9: 502. 2009.
Rottboellia sanguinea Retz., Observ. Bot. 3: 25. 1783.
Andropogon zeylanicus Arn. ex Benth., FHK 423. 1861, non Nees ex Steud (1854).
Andropogon hirtiflorus (Nees) Kunth, Rév. Gram. 2: 571. 1833; FKH 323. 1912.

Perennial herb, whole plant usually reddish brown. Culms erect, hard, 50–120 cm tall, simple or branched, glabrous. Leaf sheaths keeled, glabrous; leaf blades linear, flat, 5–25 × 0.1–0.5 cm, glabrous, apex acute, margins scabrid; ligule ca. 1 mm, membranous, apex subtruncate. Raceme solitary, dark purplish red, very slender, erect, 3–9 cm, finally long exserted from spatheole; rachis internodes and pedicels linear-clavate, equalling or slightly shorter than sessile spikelet, margin glabrous or white-ciliate. Sessile spikelet linear-lanceolate, slightly appressed into the cavity of rachis; lower glume linear, leathery, convex with inflexed margins, keeled from below middle to apex, abaxially scabrid; keels very narrowly winged toward apex, apex 2-toothed; upper glume boat-shaped, thicken membranous, narrow wings on the upper keel; lower lemma linear-lanceolate, slightly shorter than glume, margins ciliate; upper lemma 2-lobed to near base; awn 1–2 cm; styles 2. Caryopsis linear, flat. Pedicellate spikelet lanceolate, reduced to 1 or 2 glumes.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. W. Lam 818, 949, 1332.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian; India, Sri Lanka, Myanmar, Thailand, Vietnam, Malay Peninsula, Indonesia, Philippines, Australia, Africa, America.
Ecology: Open grassy fields, hillslopes. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Dec.

Schizostachyum dumetorum (Hance ex Walp.) Munro 苗仔竹
Bot. Voy. Herald. 424. 1857; FHK 435. 1861; FKH 331. 1912; HKB 76. 1985; FRPS 9(1): 20, pl. 3: 1 – 12. 1996; FOC 22: 52. 2006; FGD 9: 277. 2009.
Bambusa dumetorum Hance ex Walp., Ann. Bot. Syst. 3: 781. 1853.

Culms flexuose, 3 – 10 m long, 0.5 – 1.1 cm in diam., apically clambering; internodes to 60 cm, smooth and glabrous near base, otherwise white powdery and white strigose; wall ca. 1 mm thick. Branches ca. 40 cm. Culm sheaths deciduous, abaxially slightly glabrous, base of outer margin usually with a conspicuous subcircular expansion below point of attachment, apex truncate with equal sides; auricles usually inconspicuous; oral setae many, straight, 5 – 7 mm; ligule less than 1 mm, glabrous, margin undulate; blade reflexed, those on lower nodes of culm less than 1/2 length of sheath, those on upper nodes of culm longer. Leaves 5 – 7 per ultimate branch; sheaths 2 – 3.5 cm, glabrous; auricles usually inconspicuous; oral setae several, 3 – 5 mm; ligule less than 1 mm; blade lanceolate, 5 – 18 × 1.2 – 7 cm. Pseudospikelets fusiform, 1 – 2.2 cm; prophylls small; bracts 4 – 6, navicular, 1 – 5.5 mm, papery, rigid, keeled, apex obtuse; rachilla disarticulating. Glumes absent; lemma oblong-lanceolate, 1.2 – 1.4 cm, involute, many-veined, apex acute, mucronate; palea oblong-lanceolate, to 1.5 cm, markedly involute, thinly papery, apex truncate or emarginate; lodicules absent. Filaments white, ca. 2 cm, base ± connate; anthers yellow, 5 – 6 mm. Ovary ovoid,glabrous, stalked; style purple; stigmas 3, purple-red, 3 – 5 mm, plumose. Caryopsis fusiform, 10 – 13 × ca. 1.5 mm, glabrous, apex beaked.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 3053, 3154; Y. W. Lam 1895.
Distribution: Guangdong, Jiangxi.
Ecology: Thickets, forests. New shoots: Summer.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: The type specimen was collected by H. F. Hance from Hong Kong before 1853.

Setaria faberi R. A. W. Herrm. 大狗尾草
Beitr. Biol. Pflanzen. 10: 51. 1910; FRPS 10(1): 356, pl. 109: 12–19. 1990; FFJ 6: 195, fig. 162. 1995 [“faberii”]; FTW ed. 2, 5: 510. 2000; FOC 22: 535. 2006; FGD 9: 441. 2009 [“faberii”].

Annual herb. Culms tufted, erect or geniculate at the lower nodes, 50–120 cm tall, glabrous. Leaf sheaths loose, ciliate on upper margins; leaf blades linear-lanceolate, 10–40 × 0.5–2 cm, glabrous or adaxial surface with scattered hairs, obtuse or narrowed to base, apex acuminate, margins serrate; ligule 1–2 mm, a ring of hairs. Panicle densely cylindrical, 5–24 × 0.6–1.3 cm, nodding, branchlets bearing several spikelets each subtended by 1–3 bristles; axis white-pilose; bristles green or brownish purple. Spikelets elliptic, ca. 3 mm; lower glume 1/3–1/2 length of spikelet, broad ovate, acute, 3-veined; upper glume 3/4 length of spikelet or slightly shorter, acute, 5–9-veined; lower floret neuter, lemma 5–8-veined; palea membranous, small; upper lemma strongly convex, distinctly transversely rugose-tuberculate, coriaceous, 5-veined. Caryopsis elliptic.

Locality: Sha Tin. L. T. Lo 375.
Distribution: Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Heilongjiang, Jilin, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Shandong, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Korea; naturalized elsewhere.
Ecology: Hillslopes, roadsides, wastelands. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Oct.

Setaria italica (L.) P. Beauv. 粱
Ess. Agrostogr. 51. 1812; FKH 316. 1912; FRPS 10(1): 353. 1990; FFJ 6: 194. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 510, pl. 214. 2000; FOC 22: 535. 2006; FGD 9: 441. 2009.
Panicum italicum L., Sp. Pl. 1: 56. 1753.

Annual herb. Culms stout, erect, up to 150 cm. Leaf sheaths loosely embraced culm, glabrous or tuberculate-pilose, margins ciliate; leaf blades long lanceolate or linear-lanceolate, 15–45 × 0.6–3 cm, adaxial surface scabrous, abaxial surface slightly smooth, base rounded and obtuse, apex acute; ligule 1–3 mm, a ring of hairs. Panicle cylindrical or subfusiform, nodding when mature, 6–40 × 0.5–5 cm; central axis densely hairy; spikelets subtended by several bristles 1–5 times as long as spikelet. Spikelets yellow, brown, orange or purple, elliptic or subglobose, 2–3 mm; lower glume 1/3–1/2 length of spikelet, 3-veined; upper glume subequal spikelet, 5–7(–9)-veined; lower lemma as long as spikelet, 5–7-veined; lower palea hyaline, lanceolate; upper lemma as long as lower lemma, oblong or ovate-oblong, cartilaginous, deciduous at maturity, finely rugose to smooth and shiny.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 3221.
Distribution: Widely cultivated, origin unknown.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Summer to autumn.
Uses: Food (beverage base, cereal).

Setaria palmifolia (J. König) Stapf 棕葉狗尾草
J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 42: 186. 1914; FHN 4: 436. 1977 [“palmaefolia”]; FRPS 10(1): 337, pl. 105: 1–8. 1990; FFJ 6: 193, fig. 159. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 512, pl. 215, photo 57. 2000; FOC 22: 532. 2006; FGD 9: 439. 2009.
Panicum palmifolium J. König, Naturforscher 23: 208. 1788.

Perennial herb, with a short knotty rhizome. Culms erect or slightly geniculate, 75–200 cm tall. Leaf sheaths loose, usually sparsely hispid, margins tuberculate-ciliate near ligule, otherwise glabrous; leaf blades fusiform-lanceolate, 20–60 × 2–7 cm, glabrous or hispid, plicate, narrowed toward base and petiolate, margins tuberculate-ciliate, acuminate; ligule 1.5–2 m, a ring of hairs. Panicle open or slightly pyramid, 20–60 × 2–10 cm, branches up to 20 cm, laxly spreading, flexuous, some spikelets subtended by a solitary 5–15 mm bristle. Spikelets ovate-lanceolate, 3–4 mm, densely or sparsely arranged in one side; lower glume triangular-ovate, 1/3–1/2 length of spikelet, 3–5-veined; upper glume ovate, 1/2–3/4 length of spikelet, 5–7-veined, acute; lower lemma staminate or neuter, as long as spikelet or slightly longer, 5-veined, tipped with a short incurved beak; lower palea narrow, 2/3 length of lemma, hyaline; upper lemma indistinctly rugulose to almost smooth, slightly shiny, apex apiculate. Caryopsis ovate-lanceolate.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 2011; L. T. Lo 103; HK sheet 40815.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; tropical Asia, naturalized elsewhere.
Ecology: Open forests and other moist places. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Dec.

Setaria parviflora (Poir.) Kerguélen 幽狗尾草（褐毛狗尾草）
Lejeunia. 120: 161. 1987; FOC 22: 535. 2006; FGD 9: 442. 2009.
Cenchrus parviflorus Poir., Encycl. 6: 52. 1804.
Setaria glauca (L.) P. Beauv. var. pallidefusca (Schumach.) T. Koyama, J. Jap. Bot. 37(8): 237. 1962; FHN 4: 438, fig. 1228. 1977.
Setaria pallidefusca (Schumach.) Stapf & C. E. Hubb., Bull. Misc. Inform. Kew 1930: 259. 1930; FRPS 10(1): 358. 1990 [“pallidifusca”]; FFJ 6: 196. 1995 [“pallidifusca”]; FTW ed. 2, 5: 512. 2000; Check List HK Plants 347. 2002; 121. 2004 [“pallidifusca”].
Panicum glaucum auct. non L.: Benth., FHK 411. 1861.
Setaria glauca auct. non (L.) P. Beauv.: FKH 316. 1912.

Annual or biennial herb. Culms erect or geniculate at lower nodes, 20–90 cm tall. Leaf sheaths compressed, slightly keeled, glabrous; leaf blades linear-lanceolate, stiff, flat or slight infolded, 5–30 × 0.2–0.8 cm, glabrous or adaxial surface pilose at base, apex acuminate; ligule very short, margin a ring of ciliate. Panicle densely cylindrical, 2–15 × 0.5–1.2 cm; axis pubescent; bristles golden or purplish brown at maturity, 2–3 times spikelet length. Spikelets elliptic, 2–3 mm; lower glume triangular-ovate or broad ovate, 1/3–1/2 length of spikelet, acute, 3-veined; upper glume broadly ovate, ca. 1/2 length of spikelet, thin papery, 5-veined; lower floret neuter, lemma 5-veined, palea similar to upper lemma, membranous; upper floret bisexual, lemma cartilaginous, finely rugose, margins inrolled embraced same texture palea, mucronate; lodicules cuneate, apex finely fringed, stamens 3; styles 2, penicillate.

Locality: Wong Chuk Hang, Sai Kung. Y. S. Lau 2188, 3185.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; widely spread throughout the tropics and subtropics.
Ecology: Hillslopes, roadsides, wastelands. Flowering & fruiting: Oct.–Dec.

Setaria plicata (Lam.) T. Cooke 皺葉狗尾草
Fl. Bombay. 2: 919. 1908; FHN 4: 436. 1977; FRPS 10(1): 340, pl. 105: 9–17. 1990; FFJ 6: 193, fig. 160. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 512, pl. 216. 2000; FOC 22: 532. 2006; FGD 9: 439. 2009.
Panicum plicatum Lam., Tab. Encycl. Meth. Bot. 4: 736. 1791; FHK 411. 1861.
Panicum excurrens Trin., Sp. Gram. 1(8): pl. 89. 1827; FHK 412. 1861.
Setaria mauritiana auct. non Spreng.: FKH 316. 1912.

Perennial herb. Culms loosely tufted, erect or decumbent from a knotty rootstock, 45–130 cm tall, glabrous or sparsely pubescent. Leaf sheaths submembranous, ± papillose-pilose, margins usually ciliate except at base; leaf blades narrowly lanceolate, thin, 10–45 × 1–3 cm, plicate, papillose-pilose, hispidulous or glabrous, narrowed toward base, apex attenuate; ligule ca. 2 mm, consisting of a ring of hairs. Panicle narrow oblong or linear, 15–35 cm, branches up to 8 cm, loose, ascending, some spikelets subtended by a solitary 10–20 mm bristle; central axis ribbed, finely pubescent and scabrous. Spikelets ovate-lanceolate, 3–4 mm; lower glume broad ovate, 1/4–1/3 length of spikelet, obtuse to truncate, 3–5-veined; upper glume 1/2–3/4 length of spikelet, obtuse or acute, 5–7-veined; lower lemma staminate or neuter, 5-veined; lower palea often well developed, margins slightly inrolled, 2-veined; upper lemma bisexual, as long as or slightly shorter than lower lemma, usually distinctly and finely rugose, rarely smooth, mucronate.

Locality: Hong Kong Island. F. W. Xing 8032; Y. W. Lam 1556; HK sheet 40046.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Indochina, Thailand, India, Nepal, Malay Peninsula.
Ecology: Margins of forests, ravines and shady pathsides. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Oct.

Setaria verticillata (L.) P. Beauv. 倒刺狗尾草
Ess. Agrostogr. 51. 1812; FRPS 10(1): 351, pl. 108: 11–18. 1990; FTW ed. 2, 5: 515. 2000; FYN 9: 543. 2003; FOC 22: 537. 2006; FGD 9: 441. 2009.
Panicum verticillatum L., Sp. Pl., ed. 2, 1: 82. 1762.

Annual herb. Culms tufted, ascending from geniculate base, much branched, 20–100 cm tall, glabrous. Leaf sheaths thin and soft, glabrous or papillose-puberulous, margins ciliolate; leaf blades linear-lanceolate, flaccid, 5–20 × 0.4–1.8 cm, usually glabrous or adaxially slightly scabrous, base subrounded, apex long acuminate, margins scabrous; ligule 0.5–1 mm, a ring of hairs. Panicle contracted, cylindrical, 4–15 cm, spikelets subtended by 1–4 bristles; bristles green or brownish, 3–8 mm, retrorsely barbed and often becoming entangled. Spikelets elliptic, 1.8–2.4 mm, obtuse; lower glume 1/3–1/2 length of spikelet, 3-veined; upper glume boat-shaped, as long as spikelet or slightly short, 5–7-veined; lower floret neuter, lower lemma as long as spikelet or slightly longer, 5-veined; lower palea much reduced; upper lemma as long as lower lemma or slightly short, dorsally compressed, finely and transversely rugose; lodicules cuneate, emarginate. Caryopsis elliptic.

Locality: Fung Kat Heung. HK sheet 35660.
Distribution: Nei Mongol, Taiwan, Yunnan; widespread tropical weed, originated from paleotropics.
Ecology: Roadsides, open weedy places. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Sep.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Victoria Peak, HKU campus, Sha Tin (cultivated)
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Sinobambusa tootsik (Makino) Makino 唐竹
J. Jap. Bot. 2: 8. 1918; FTW 5: 739, pl. 1499. 1978; HKB 77. 1985; FRPS 9(1): 226, pl. 60. 1996; FOC 22: 148. 2006; FGD 9: 309. 2009.
Arundinaria tootsik Makino, Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 19: 63. 1905.
Arundinaria dolichantha Keng, Sinensia 7: 418, fig. 6. 1936.
Neobambos dolichanthus (Keng) P. C. Keng, Techn. Bull. Nat’l. For. Res. Bur. China No. 8: 15. 1948.
Pleioblastus dolichanthus (Keng) P. C. Keng, Clav. Gen. Sp. Gram. Prim. Sin. 154. 1957.
Semiarundinaria okuboi Makino, J. Jap. Bot. 8: 43. 1933.
Semiarundinaria tootsik (Makino) Muroi, Amat. Herb. 10: 210. 1942.

Culms 5–12 m, 2–6 cm in diam.; internodes initially deep green, flattened above branches, 30–40(–80) cm, glaucous, glabrous, apically minutely papillate. Culm sheaths initially redbrown, basally suboblong, leathery, slightly glaucous, setose, densely so at base, apex broadly rounded, margins ciliate; auricles very variable, scabrid, tomentose; oral setae curved, ca. 2 cm; ligule arcuate, ca. 3–4 mm, uniform; blade reflexed, green, lanceolate. Leaves 3–6(–9) per ultimate branch; sheath glabrous; auricles obscure; oral setae deciduous, radiate, ca. 1.5 cm, undulate; ligule truncate or subrounded; blade 6 – 22 × 1–3.5 cm, secondary veins 4–8-paired, margins serrulate, abaxially pubescent. Spikelets 1–3(–5), lateral spikelets sessile, terminal spikelet on 2–11 mm pedicel, linear, 8–20 × 0.2–0.3 cm; florets 7–12 mm, glabrous. Lemma ovate, ca. 7 mm wide, margins ciliate, apex acute; palea elliptic; lodicules nearly rhombic, elliptic or ovate, ca. 2.5 mm, ciliolate, with 7–9 veins. Anthers light yellow. Ovary glabrous; style 1, extremely short; stigmas 3, 3–4 mm.

Locality: Victoria Peak, HKU campus, Sha Tin (cultivated). Nan-Zhu 2778, 2845.
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi; N Vietnam, introduced in Japan.
Ecology: New shoots: Apr.–May.
Uses: Ornamental.

Sorghum bicolor (L.) Moench 高粱
Methodus 207. 1794; FRPS 10(2): 128, pl. 30: 5–7, 75: 4. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 5: 578. 2000; FYN 9: 648, pl. 108: 5–7. 2003; FOC 22: 601. 2006; FGD 9: 490. 2009.
Holcus bicolor L., Mant. Alt. 301. 1771.
Sorghum vulgare (L.) Pers., Syn. Pl. 1: 101. 1805; FKH 324. 1912; FHN 4: 470. 1977; FFJ 6: 263, fig. 233. 1995.

Annual stout herb; culms solid, erect, 2–4 m tall. Leaf sheath usually shorter than internodes, glabrous; ligule ca. 12 mm, hard membranous, apex rounded; leaf blades linear-lanceolate or narrow lanceolate, 30–60 × 2–7 cm, glabrous, apex acuminate, margins scabrous. Panicle dense, 15–30 cm; branches subverticillate, base densely white pilose; rachis internode short, not fragile. Spikelets paired, dimorphic, sessile spikelets ca. 5 mm, ovate; glumes dark brown when mature, coriaceous, midsection glabrous, shiny, upper portion and callus hispid; lower glume ca. 5–6 mm, margins inrolled; upper glume ± boat-shaped, rounded; lower lemma long elliptic, membranous, margins inrolled, ciliate; upper lemma subtriangular, membranous, ciliate; awn geniculate ca. 10 mm; palea linear. Pedicellate spikelets short, staminate.

Locality: Cultivated. P. P. H. But 124; L. T. Lo 179, 378.
Distribution: Cultivated throughout tropical, subtropical and warm temperate regions.
Uses: Food (beverage base, cereal, sugar), animal food (fodder, forage).

Sorghum halepense (L.) Pers. 石茅（亞刺伯高粱）
Syn. Pl. 1: 101. 1805; FKH 324. 1912; FHN 4: 469, fig. 1257. 1977; FFJ 6: 262. 1995; FRPS 10(2): 119, pl. 28. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 5: 579. 2000; FOC 22: 601. 2006; FGD 9: 489. 2009.
Holcus halepensis L., Sp. Pl. 2: 1047. 1753.

Perennial herb. Culms erect, 0.5–3 m tall. Leaf sheaths glabrous, or puberulous at base nodes; leaf blades linear or linear-lanceolate, 20–90 × 0.5–4 cm, glabrous, margins scabrous, midvein white, conspicuous; ligule membranous. Panicle lanceolate to pyramidal in outline, with soft white hairs in basal axil; primary branches solitary or whorled, spreading, lower part bare, upper part branched, the secondary branches tipped by racemes; racemes fragile, composed of 2–5 spikelet pairs. Sessile spikelet elliptic or ovate-elliptic; callus obtuse, bearded; lower glume subleathery, veins distinct in upper part, keel winged, apex 3-denticulate; upper glume slightly boat-shaped, keeled in upper part; lower lemma lanceolate or oblong-lanceolate, hyaline membranous; upper lemma oblong, acute and mucronate or 2-lobed and awned; awn 1–1.6 cm; lodicules 2, broad obovate, emarginate; stamens 3; styles 2, base connate. Pedicellate spikelet staminate, narrowly lanceolate.

Locality: Ma Liu Shui, Tai Po. P. P. H. But 73; Y. S. Lau 1978, 3111.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan, Anhui, Fujian, Taiwan; N Africa, Caucasus, C and W Asia, Indian Subcontinent, naturalized in warm temperate regions, exact native range obscure.
Ecology: Streams, valleys, wastelands, a weed in fields. Flowering & fruiting: Summer to autumn.
Uses: Animal food (forage).

Sorghum nitidum (Vahl) Pers. 光高粱
Syn. Pl. 1: 101. 1805; FHN 4: 469. 1977; FFJ 6: 262, fig. 232. 1995; FRPS 10(2): 118, pl. 30: 8. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 5: 579, pl. 244. 2000; FOC 22: 600. 2006; FGD 9: 488, fig. 258. 2009.
Holcus nitidus Vahl, Symb. Bot. 2: 102. 1791.
Andropogon tropicus Spreng, Syst. Veg. 1: 287. 1825; FHK 423. 1861.
Sorghum fulvum (R. Br.) P. Beauv., Ess. Agrostogr. 164. 1812; FKH 324. 1912.

Perennial herb. Culms erect, 0.6–2 m tall; nodes bearded with pale spreading hairs. Leaf sheaths clasping, glabrous or pilose; leaf blades linear, 10–40(–50) × 0.4–1 cm, glabrous to hispid, dorsally convex; ligule obtuse, 1–1.5 mm. Panicle loose, glabrous but with soft hairs at the nodes; primary branches whorled, simple, flexuous, lower part bare; racemes borne at branch ends, fragile, composed of 2–4 spikelet pairs; internodes and pedicels brown-ciliate. Sessile spikelet ovate-lanceolate, brown bearded, callus obtuse; lower glume leathery, glossy, upper part and margins hispid with brown hairs; upper glume lightly boat-shaped; lower lemma slightly shorter than glume, thicken membranous, subchartaceous, margins inrolled, ciliate; upper lemma hyaline membranous; awn 1–1.7 cm, or awnless; lodicules 2, glabrous; style free, penicillate, brown. Caryopsis oblong. Pedicellate spikelet usually staminate, elliptic.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, New Territories. Y. S. Lau 3006; HK sheet 15749, 38095.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Shandong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Indian Subcontinent, SE Asia, Indonesia, Philippines, Pacific islands, NE Australia.
Ecology: Grassy hillsides.

Sorghum propinquum (Kunth) Hitchc. 擬高粱
Lingnan Sci. J. 7: 249. 1931 [“1929”] ; FFJ 6: 262. 1995; FRPS 10(2): 121, pl. 29. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 5: 579. 2000; FOC 22: 601. 2006; FGD 9: 490. 2009 [“propinqum”].
Andropogon propinquus Kunth, Enum. Pl. 1: 502. 1833.

Perennial herb, rhizomatous. Culms erect, 1–3 m tall, many-noded; nodes puberulous. Leaf sheaths glabrous, ciliate at mouth and margins; leaf blades linear or linear-lanceolate, 40–90 × 3–5 cm, glabrous, midvein robust, margins scabrous; ligule 0.5–1 mm, puberulous. Panicle open, ovate or broadly ovate; primary branches in whorls of 3–6; lower part bare, upper part branched, branches tipped by racemes; racemes fragile, composed of 3–7 spikelet pairs. Sessile spikelet elliptic or elliptic-lanceolate; callus obtuse, pubescent with pale hairs; lower glume subleathery, upper keeled, apex sharply acute, entire or tridenticulate; upper glume lanceolate, upper keeled, pilose; lower lemma lanceolate, hyaline membranous, ciliate; upper lemma broad oblong, acute or emarginate, awnless, rarely with short awn; palea very short; styles 2, free or base connate; stigma penicillate. Pedicellate spikelet staminate, linear-lanceolate, narrower than sessile spikelet, glabrous.

Locality: So Kon Po (cultivated). HK sheet 8613.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Yunnan, Sichuan, Fujian, Taiwan; S India, Sri Lanka, Malay Peninsula, Indonesia, Philippines.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Summer to autumn.

Sorghum sudanense (Piper) Stapf 蘇丹草
Fl. Trop. Afr. 9: 113. 1917; FFJ 6: 263, fig. 234. 1995; FRPS 10(2): 124. 1997; FOC 22: 601. 2006; FGD 9: 490. 2009.
Andropogon sorghum (L.) Brot. subsp. sudanensis Piper, Proc. Biol. Soc. Washington 28(4): 33. 1915.

Annual herb. Culms erect, 1–3 m tall, nodes pubescent. Leaf sheaths longer than internodes at the base, the upper shorter than internodes, glabrous or pilose at mouth and base; leaf blades linear or linear-lanceolate; 15–40 × 1–5 cm, glabrous, abaxially convex, margins scabrous, midvein white; ligule hard membranous, apex ciliate. Panicle narrow ovate to pyramid, branches slender, subverticillate, obliquely spreading; racemes usually tardily fragile at maturity, composed of 2–5 spikelet pairs. Sessile spikelet elliptic or oblonglanceolate; callus obtuse, pubescent; lower glume ovate, margins inrolled above the middle, keeled near apex, margins ciliate; upper glume boat-shaped, inrolled, margins membranous; lower lemma elliptic-lanceolate, hyaline membranous, glabrous or margins ciliate; upper lemma ovate or ovate-elliptic, apex 2-lobed, awned; awn 10–16 mm, geniculate; stamen 3; style 2. Caryopsis elliptic or obovateelliptic. Pedicellate spikelet staminate or barren, linear-lanceolate, persistent.

Locality: So Kon Po (cultivated). HK sheet 15804.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guizhou, Heilongjiang, Henan, Nei Mongol, Ningxia, Xinjiang, Shaanxi, Hebei, Henan, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian (cultivated or naturalized); native to Africa, now widely cultivated for forage.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Sep.
Uses: Animal food (forage).

Sphaerocaryum malaccense (Trin.) Pilg. 稗藎
Repert. Spec. Nov. Regni Veg. 45: 2. 1938; FHN 4: 393, fig. 1201. 1977; FRPS 10(1): 172, pl. 54. 1990; FFJ 6: 183, fig. 151. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 446, pl. 184. 2000; FOC 22: 560. 2006; FGD 9: 372, fig. 181. 2009.
Panicum malaccense Trin., Gram. Panic. 204. 1826.
Isachne pulchella auct. non Roth.: FHK 414. 1861.
Sphaerocaryum elegans Nees ex Steud., Nomencl. Bot. (ed. 2) 2: 620. 1841; FKH 317. 1912.

Annual herb. Culms very slender, prostrate, 10–30 cm, rooting at lower nodes, nodes bearded. Leaf sheaths shorter than internode, ciliate along margins; leaf blades ovate-cordate, amplexicaul, 1–1.5 × 0.6–1 cm, ± hispidulous, margins ciliate-serrulate; ligule ca. 1 mm, a ring of hairs. Panicle shortly exserted from uppermost sheath, ovate, 2–5 × 1–2 cm, with many spikelets on 1–3 mm capillary glandular pedicels. Spikelets 1-flowered, ca. 1 mm; glumes hyaline, glabrous, the lower 2/3 spikelet length, veinless; the upper equal to spikelet or slightly shorter, 11-veined; lemma as long as spikelet, pubescent; palea similar to lemma; anthers 3, yellow. Caryopsis brownish at maturity.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 3016; D. P. M. Guile 729; HK sheet 30747.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; widespread over India, SE Asia and southward to Malay Peninsula and Indonesia
Ecology: Watersides and other damp places. Flowering & fruiting: Autumn.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Long Ke, Tai Long Sai Wan, Ham Tin, Tai Wan, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Spinifex littoreus (Burm. f.) Merr. 鬣刺
Philipp. J. Sci. 7: 229. 1912; FHN 4: 444. 1977; FRPS 10(1): 391, pl. 119, 129: 18. 1990; FFJ 6: 188, fig. 157. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 518, pl. 218. 2000; FOC 22: 553. 2006; FGD 9: 450, fig. 233. 2009.
Stipa littorea Burm. f., Fl. Ind. 29. 1767.
Spinifex squarrosus L., Mant. Pl. 300. 1771; FHK 415. 1861; FKH 317. 1912.

Perennial herb. Culms stoloniferous, hard, stout, many-noded, rooting and copiously branching at nodes, flowering shoots ascending to 30–100 cm or more. Leaf sheaths broad, glabrous or pubescent, imbricate, margins ciliate; leaf blades linear, 5–20 × 0.2–0.3 cm, very tough, involute-subulate, curved, glabrous, margins scabrous, apex spiny; ligule small, densely ciliate. Male inflorescence of 2–5 clustered; racemes 3–6 cm, bearing 5–10 loosely imbricate spikelets. Male spikelets lanceolate, 8–12 mm; glumes oblong-lanceolate, unequal, 7–9-veined; lower glume 1/2 spikelet length; upper glume 2/3 spikelet length; lower lemma 8–10 mm, 5-veined, palea as long as lemma, 2-veined. Female inflorescence globose; racemes with needle-like 10–18 cm rachis, with 1 spikelet at base. Female spikelets lanceolate-oblong, ca. 12 mm; glumes herbaceous; lower glume slightly shorter than spikelet, many-veined; lower lemma as long as spikelet, 5-veined, palea absent; upper lemma as long as palea, thickened papery, 5-veined.

Locality: Long Ke, Tai Long Sai Wan, Ham Tin, Tai Wan, Lantau Island. S. P. Lau 76; Y. S. Lau 2585; HK sheet 34662.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam, Cambodia, Thailand, Myanmar, India, Malay Peninsula, Indonesia, Philippines.
Ecology: Sandy beaches, seashore dunes. Flowering & fruiting: Summer to autumn.

Sporobolus fertilis (Steud.) Clayton 鼠尾粟
Kew Bull. 19(2): 291. 1965; FRPS 10(1): 99, pl. 31: 6–10. 1990; FFJ 6: 178, fig. 146. 1995; FOC 22: 484. 2006; FGD 9: 360, fig. 173. 2009.
Agrostis fertilis Steud., Syn. Pl. Glumac. 1: 170. 1854.
Sporobolus indicus (L.) var. major (Buse) Baaijens, Blumea 35: 437. 1991; FTW ed. 2, 5: 435. 2000.
Sporobolus indicus auct. non R. Br.: FHK 426. 1861; FKH 325. 1912.

Perennial herb. Culms tufted, erect, 25–100(–120) cm tall. Leaf blades linear, flat or involute, 15–50(–65) × 0.2–0.5 cm, glabrous or thinly pilose on adaxial surface, tapering to a long filiform apex; ligule ca. 0.5 mm; leaf sheaths glabrous but margin ciliolate, basal sheaths papery, lightly keeled. Panicle linear, contracted to spike-like, 19–45 × 0.5–1.5 cm; branches 1–2.5(–5) cm, erect and appressed to main axis, or looser and narrowly ascending, densely spiculate throughout. Spikelets greyish or yellowish green, 1.7–2 mm; lower glume oblong, ca. 0.5 mm, veinless, apex truncate-erose; upper glume oblong-elliptic, 1/2–2/3 spikelet length, 1-veined, apex ± acute; lemma ovate, as long as spikelet, indistinctly 1(–3)-veined, acute. Anthers 3, 0.8–1 mm. Grain red-brown, obovate-elliptic, 0.9–1.2 mm, distinctly shorter than its lemma and palea, these gaping widely beyond its top, apex truncate.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1047; K. L. Yip 4042, 4483.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Gansu, Shaanxi, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Shandong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Indochina, Malesia, Indian Subcontinent.
Ecology: Roadsides, wastelands, grassy hillslopes. Flowering & fruiting: Mar.–Dec.

Sporobolus virginicus (L.) Kunth 鹽地鼠尾粟
Rev. Gramin. 1: 67. 1829; FRPS 10(1): 99, pl. 31: 11–14. 1990; FFJ 6: 179. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 438. 2000; FOC 22: 483. 2006; FGD 9: 360. 2009.
Agrostis virginica L., Sp. Pl. 1: 63. 1753.

Perennial herb, with woody rhizomes. Culms erect or decumbent at base, 15–30(–60) cm tall, often fastigiately branched in upper part. Leaf blades leathery, glaucous, stiff, distichous, flat at first, soon inrolled and needle-like, 2–10 × 0.1–0.4 cm, abaxial surface smooth, adaxial surface scabrid, apex pungent; ligule ca. 0.2 mm, upper margin and abaxial surface ciliate; leaf sheaths tightly overlapping, loosely pubescent at mouth. Panicle linear, spike-like, 2–10 × 0.4–1 cm, branches 0.5–1.5 cm, erect, closely appressed to rachis. Spikelets grey-green or greenish yellow, fusiform, 2.3–2.7 mm, with 1 floret; glumes acute, papery; lower glume lanceolate, 2/3–4/5 spikelet length, 1-veined; upper glume narrowly ovate, as long as spikelet, 1-veined; lemma and palea the same texture with the glume; lemma ovate-lanceolate, 1-veined, boat-shaped, about 2 mm long; palea ovate, 2-keeled, truncate at the apex. Anthers 3, 1–1.5 mm. Grain subglobose 0.7–1 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. S. P. Lau 155; Y. W. Lam 1584; K. Y. Tam 144.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; widespread in tropics and subtropics.
Ecology: Coastal sands. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Sep.
Uses: Environmental (erosion control).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Clear Water Bay
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Stenotaphrum helferi Munro ex Hook. f. 鈍葉草
Fl. Brit. India. 7(21): 91. 1896 [“1897”]; FRPS 10(1): 385, pl. 117. 1990; FFJ 6: 190. 1995; FOC 22: 538. 2006; FGD 9: 449, fig. 231. 2009.
Stenotaphrum americanum Schrank, Pl. Rar. Hort. Monac. 2(10): t. 98. 1819[1822]; FKH 317. 1912.

Perennial herb. Culms creeping and rooting at base, flowering shoots 10–40 cm tall. Leaf sheaths loose, usually longer than internode, compressed, keeled, glabrous; leaf blades broadly linear, 5–17 × 0.5–1.1 cm, glabrous, base truncate or subrounded, apex slightly obtuse or mucronate, margins scabrous; ligule ca. 0.3 mm, apex with white short ciliate. Inflorescence 10–15 cm; axis flattened and winged, 3–5 mm wide, margins scabrous; racemes 7–18 mm, appressed within the curves of the midrib; raceme rachis triquetrous, margins scabrous, tipped with a mucro arising from the terminal spikelet. Spikelets ovate-lanceolate, 4–4.5 mm; lower glume broadly ovate, 1/2–2/3 the length of spikelet, (3–)5–7-veined; upper glume as long as spikelet, 9–11-veined; lower floret staminate or neuter, lemma as long as spikelet, 7-veined, palea well developed, slightly shorter than lemma; upper lemma coriaceous, smooth, cuspidate-mucronate, margins inrolled embraced palea.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Clear Water Bay. P. P. H. But 248; HK sheet 8357, 42035.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian, Yunnan; Vietnam, Thailand, Myanmar, Malay Peninsula.
Ecology: Open forests, moist grasslands. Flowering & fruiting: Autumn.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Tam, Tai Lung, Tai Mo Shan, Nim Shue Wan
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Stenotaphrum secundatum (Walter) Kuntze 側鈍葉草
Revis. Gen. Pl. 2: 794. 1891; FOC 22: 538. 2006.
Ischaemum secundatum Walter, Fl. Carol. 249. 1788.

Perennial stoloniferous herb. Culms much branched, forming a dense turf; flowering shoots 10–30 cm tall. Leaf sheaths strongly keeled, often grouped in flabellate clusters; leaf blades broadly linear, folded when young, up to 15 × 0.4–1 cm, apex obtuse; ligule ca. 0.5 mm. Inflorescence 5–12 cm, slender, cylindrical; axis corky, disarticulating into segments at maturity; racemes 4–10 mm, reduced to 1–3 spikelets embedded in one face of the rachis, alternating on either side of the sinuous midrib; raceme rachis a stout pointed appendage within the axis cavity. Spikelets lanceolate, 4–5 mm, acute; lower glume up to 1/4 as long as spikelet; upper glume as long as spikelet; lower floret staminate, lemma cartilaginous, 3-veined, palea well developed; upper lemma papery, subequal to spikelet, smooth, acute.

Locality: Tai Tam, Tai Lung, Tai Mo Shan, Nim Shue Wan. S. L. Thrower 1190; S. Y. Hu 9929 (CUHK).
Distribution: Maxico, USA, S America; widely naturalized, exact native range obscure.
Ecology: Cultivated as lawn grass in Hong Kong. Flowering & fruiting: Summer.
Notes: The species was reported as Stenotaphrum dimidiatum (L.) Brongn. previously (Check List HK Plants 349. 2002; 122. 2004).

Themeda triandra Forssk. 黃背草
Fl. Aegypt.-Arab. 178. 1775; FKH 324. 1912; FRPS 10(2): 252. 1997; FYN 9: 721. 2003; FOC 22: 634. 2006; FGD 9: 507. 2009.
Themeda japonica (Willd.) Tanaka, Bult. Sci. Fak. Terk. Kjusu Imp. Univ. 1: 194. 1925; FHN 4: 484. 1977; FRPS 10(2): 253, pl. 63: 1 – 11, 79: 3. 1997; FTW ed. 2, 5: 585, pl. 247. 2000; Check List HK Plants 349. 2002; 122. 2004.
Anthistiria japonica Willd., Sp. Pl. 4: 901. 1805.

Perennial herb. Culms stout, erect or geniculate at the base, 0.5–1.5 m tall, glabrous. Leaf sheaths usually hispid with tuberclebased hairs; leaf blades linear, 10–50 × 0.4–0.8 cm, glabrous or pilose, base subrounded, apex finely acuminate; ligule 1–2 mm, truncate, ciliate. Compound panicle lax, open, with spaced, often nodding spathate fascicles; spathes and spatheoles narrowly lanceolate, glabrous or thinly to densely tuberculate-hispid. Raceme composed of a triad of 1 sessile and 2 pedicellate spikelets above the involucre of 2 homogamous pairs. Homogamous spikelets all sessile, arising at same level, staminate, both glumes present, oblong-lanceolate with lateral scarious wings, glabrous or hispid with tubercle-based hairs. Sessile spikelet bisexual, fusiform-cylindrical; callus 1.5–3 mm, pungent, brown bearded, apex exposed; lower glume dark brown, abaxially rounded, glossy, hispidulous in upper 1/3, smooth below; upper glume and lower glume the same texture, equal, linear-oblong; lower lemma shorter than glume, lanceolate, glabrous; upper lemma 1-veined, awned from the apex. Caryopsis oblong. Pedicellate spikelet similar to involucral spikelet, male or barren.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, New Territories. Y. S. Lau 184; Y. W. Lam 403, 1150.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Hebei, Henan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Anhui, Shandong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; widely spread over E to S and SW Asia, Australia, Africa.
Ecology: Dry hillslopes, roadsides. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Dec.

Themeda villosa (Poir.) A. Camus 菅
Fl. Indo-Chine. 7: 364. 1922; H. B. Gill. et al., Fl. Malaya 3: 301, fig. 65. 1971; FRPS 10(2): 248, pl. 62: 5. 1997; FYN 9: 721, pl. 117: 1–2. 2003; FOC 22: 635. 2006; FGD 9: 506, fig. 269. 2009.
Anthistiria villosa Poir, Encycl. 1: 396. 1812.
Themeda gigantea (Cav.) Hack. var. villosa (Poir.) Hack., Monogr. Phan. 6: 675. 1889.
Themeda gigantea auct. non (Cav.) Hack.: FKH 324. 1912.

Perennial herb. Culms tufted, stout, 2–4 m tall, smooth. Leaf sheaths glabrous, basal sheaths strongly compressed; leaf blades linear, ca. 100 × 0.7–1.5 cm, scabrid, gradually narrowed to the thicken white midrib toward base, apex acuminate; ligule ca. 1 mm, membranous, ciliate. Inflorescence a leafy compound panicle composed of short racemes; raceme usually 2–3 cm, spathe boat-shaped, glabrous, composed of (1–)2 spikelet pairs and a terminal triad above the involucre of 2 homogamous pairs; homogamous spikelets arising at slightly different levels, staminate or barren, narrowly lanceolate, wingless, shortly pubescent. Sessile spikelet 7–8 mm; callus 1–2 mm, acute; lower glume oblong-lanceolate, abaxially compressed with shallow central groove, densely brown strigose, apex truncate, margins inrolled, abaxial surface and margins with dense brown hairs; upper glume margins embraced by lower glume, abaxial surface with brown hairs; upper lemma lanceolate, midvein produced into mucro or poorly developed short awn. Pedicellate spikelet similar to involucral spikelets.

Locality: New Territories. Y. S. Lau 1092, 1681; Y. W. Lam 1285.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian; Indian Subcontinent, Indochina, Malay Peninsula, Indonesia, Philippines.
Ecology: Open grassy fields, hillslopes, disturbed moist grassy places. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Jan. of the following year.

Thuarea involuta (G. Forst.) R. Br. ex Sm. 蒭雷草
Cycl. 35. 1817; FHN 4: 443. 1977; FRPS 10(1): 387, pl. 118. 1990; FTW ed. 2, 5: 518, pl. 219. 2000; FOC 22: 525. 2006; FGD 9: 449, fig. 232. 2009.
Ischaemum involutum G. Forst., Fl. Ins. Austr. 73. 1786.
Thuarea sarmentosa Pers., Syn. Pl. 1: 110. 1805; FHK 415. 1861; FKH 317. 1912.

Perennial herb. Culms long and creeping, much branched, rooting at nodes, flowering culms up to 20 cm tall. Leaf sheaths loose, ca. 1/2 length of internode, pilose or only ciliate along margins; leaf blades lanceolate, 2–5 × 0.3–0.8 cm, usually puberulous on both surfaces, margins usually rugulose; ligule very short, a row of white short ciliate. Inflorescence a terminal onesided raceme, enclosed by a spathe; rachis broad and wing-like in lower fertile part, narrowed above in staminate part. Bisexual spikelets ovate-lanceolate, 3.5–4.5 mm, 2-floret, only upper floret fertile; lower glume absent or narrow and small, membranous; upper glume subequal to spikelet, leathery, abaxially hairy, 7-veined; lower lemma herbaceous, 5–7-veined, palea membranous, stamen 3; upper lemma thick-papery, palea 2-veined, stamen 3. Male spikelet oblong-lanceolate, 3–4 mm; lower glume absent; upper glume herbaceous, abaxially hairy, 3–5-veined; lower lemma papery, broad lanceolate, 5-veined; palea membranous, 2-veined, 2-lobed; stamen 3; upper lemma papery, 5-veined; palea 2-veined; male spikelet deciduous at maturity, leaf-like rachis inrolled embraced fertile spikelet.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Ping Chau. H. F. Hance 10230 (BM).
