Distribution: Guangdong, Hainan, Taiwan; widely spread over SE Asia, Malesia, Pacific islands, New Guinea, Australia, Indian Ocean islands and Madagascar.
Ecology: Sandy beaches. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Dec.

Thysanolaena latifolia (Roxb. ex Hornem.) Honda 粽葉蘆
J. Fac. Sci. Univ. Tokyo, Sect. 3, Bot. 3: 312. 1930; FTW ed. 2, 5: 336. 2000; FOC 22: 446. 2006; FGD 9: 340, fig. 161. 2009.
Melica latifolia Roxb. ex Hornem., Suppl. Hort. Bot. Hafn. 117. 1819.
Thysanolaena maxima (Roxb.) Kuntze, Revis. Gen. Pl. 2: 794. 1891; FHN 4: 370, fig. 1180. 1977; FFJ 6: 128, fig. 99. 1995; FRPS 9(2): 30, pl. 4: 1. 2002.
Thysanolaena acarifera Arn. & Nees, Gramineae 49. 1841; FHK 417. 1861.
Thysanolaena agrostis Nees, Edinburgh New Philos. J. 18: 180. 1835; FKH 318. 1912; Check List HK Plants 349. 2002; 122. 2004.

Tall reed-like perennial herb, 1–4 m tall. Culms woody, with white pith. Leaf blades lanceolate, leathery, 30–50 × 3 – 7(–10) cm, base sub-amplexicaul, apex acuminate, glabrous; ligule 1–2 mm, subleathery, truncate. Panicle up to 60 cm, open or contracted, elliptic in outline; main branches 1–3 per node, pilose in axils; pedicels ca. 2 mm. Spikelets 1.5–2 mm, cylindrical, the margins ciliate-hispid, florets 2–3; lower floret reduced to only a ca. 1.5 mm lemma; upper floret ca. 1 mm; glumes 1/5–1/4 spikelet length, ovate-lanceolate, margins siliceous; lower glume apex with sinus; upper glume apex rounded; sterile lemma glabrous, as long as spikelet; fertile lemma slightly shorter than lower lemma, ciliate on the margin with 1 mm hairs, spreading at maturity, apex slightly recurved. Caryopsis oblong, ca. 0.5 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 2301, 3301; K. L. Yip 4081.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Taiwan; Indochina, Indian Subcontinent, Malesia, Indian Ocean islands.
Ecology: Margins of forests, moist grasslands. Flowering & fruiting: Mar.–Apr.
Uses: Animal food (forage), material (fiber).

Zea mays L. 玉蜀黍
Sp. Pl. 2: 971. 1753; FKH 317. 1912; FHN 4: 488, fig. 1272. 1977; FRPS 10(2): 287, pl. 72: 1–3. 1997; FOC 22: 650. 2006; FGD 9: 511, fig. 273. 2009.

Annual herb. Culms erect, solid, 1–4 m tall. Leaf sheaths with transverse veinlets; leaf blades flat and broad, linear-lanceolate, 30–90 × 3–12 cm, glabrous or with tubercle-based hairs, base rounded, margins scabrid, midvein stout; ligule ca. 2 mm, membranous. Female inflorescence axillary, the spikelets in many rows on a thicken, almost woody axis, enclosed by many large foliaceous bracts or spathes; glumes equal, veinless, margins ciliate; florets hyaline, style extremely long and slender, like silky threads. Caryopsis globose or depressed globose. Male inflorescence a "tassel" of many digitate racemes, terminal; spikelets paired, pedicel unequal, one 1–2 mm, the other 2–4 mm, slender pilose; glumes subequal, membranous, ciliate; lemma and palea hyaline membranous, slightly shorter than glume; anthers orange, ca. 5 mm.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 2753.
Distribution: Originated from America, widely cultivated elsewhere.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Summer to autumn.
Uses: Food (beverage base, oil/fat, starch, vegetable).

Zoysia matrella (L.) Merr. 溝葉結縷草
Philipp. Sci. 7(4): 230. 1912; Fl. Ill. Pl. Prim. Sin. Gram. 737, pl. 685. 1959; FTW 5: 508. 1978; FRPS 10(1): 129. 1990; FFJ 6: 176, fig. 144. 1995; FOC 22: 497. 2006; FGD 9: 366, fig. 178. 2009.
Agrostis matrella L., Mant. Pl. 2: 185. 1771.
Zoysia pungens Willd., Ges. Naturf. Feunde Berlin Neue Schriften 3: 441. 1801; FKH 318. 1912.
Zoysia tenuifolia Thiele, Linnaea 9(3): 309. 1835.
Zoysia tenuifolia Willd. ex Trin., Mem. Acad. Sci. Petersb. ser. 6, 4: 96. 1836.

Perennial herb, rhizomatous or stoloniferous. Culms up to 20 cm tall. Leaf blades flat or involute, tough, suberect to spreading, 3 – 8 × 0.1–0.3 cm, glabrous or adaxial surface thinly pilose, apex acute; ligule a ring of hairs ca. 0.1 mm; leaf sheaths glabrous, bearded at mouth with 4–5 mm hairs. Inflorescence linear, 2–4 × 0.2–0.3 cm, exserted above leaves, composed of 10 – 30, loosely overlapping spikelets; rachis somewhat wavy; pedicels shorter than spikelet, 1–3 mm, widened at apex. Spikelets 1-flowered, 2–3 × ca. 1 mm, laterally compressed, lanceolate, yellowish brown or purplish brown, shortly pedicellate; lower glume usually absent; upper glume as long as the spikelet, lanceolate, 5-veined, midrib prominent, sometimes scabrous toward apex, lateral veins obscure, margins thinner and inrolled, apex obtuse; lemma oblong-ovate, 2–2.5 mm, obscurely 3-veined, midvein sometimes shortly excurrent; palea lanceolate, hyaline, 1/2 length as lemma. Anthers 1–1.5 mm. Caryopsis ca. 1.5 mm.

Locality: New Territories. S. P. Lau 190; Y. S. Lau 2288; S. C. Ng 1220.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian, Taiwan; widely distributed in the tropical regions of Asia.
Ecology: Sandy places near seaside. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Oct.

Zoysia pacifica (Goudswaard) M. Hotta & Kuroki 細葉結縷草
Acta Phytotax. Geobot. 45: 71. 1994; FOC 22: 498. 2006; FGD 9: 367. 2009.
Zoysia matrella (L.) Merr. var. paucifica Goudswaard, Blumea 26: 172. 1980.
Zoysia tenuifolia auct. non Willd. ex Trin.: FRPS 10(1): 131, pl. 40: 4–5. 1990; FFJ 6: 177, fig. 145. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 440. 2000; Check List HK Plants 350. 2002; 122. 2004.

Perennial herb, stoloniferous. Culms densely tufted, 5–10 cm tall, much branched. Leaf blades setaceous, soft, 4–6 × ca. 0.1 cm; ligule 0.3 mm, upper part a fringe of hairs; leaf sheaths glabrous, bearded at mouth with 2–5 mm hairs. Inflorescence linear, up to 1.5 cm, with 6–12 loosely overlapping spikelets; rachis somewhat wavy; pedicels shorter than spikelet, up to 1.6 mm, scabrous, slightly widened at apex. Spikelets lanceolate, 1-flowered, 2–3 × ca. 0.6 mm, straw-coloured tinged purplish; lower glume absent; upper glume as long as the spikelet, lanceolate, shiny, obscurely 5-veined, apex subacute, sometimes with subapical awn-point; lemma slightly shorter than upper glume, 1-veined; palea and lodicule reduced. Anthers 0.6–0.8 mm.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 2199; Y. W. Lam 31; HK sheet 42001.
Distribution: Taiwan; Japan, Philippines, Pacific islands; widely introduced in tropical and subtropical regions as lawn plant.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Dec.
Uses: Environmental (excellent for lawns).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Ma On Shan, Castle Peak, Sai Kung, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Zoysia sinica Hance 中華結縷草
J. Bot. 7: 168. 1869; FKH 318. 1912; FRPS 10(1): 126. 1990; FFJ 6: 176. 1995; FTW ed. 2, 5: 440. 2000; FOC 22: 497. 2006; FGD 9: 366. 2009.
Zoysia pengens auct. non Willd.: FHK 418. 1861.

Perennial herb with creeping rhizomes. Culms tufted, erect, arising from nodes of rhizome, stiff, 10–30 cm tall, branched at base. Leaf blades broadly linear, flat or margins involute, stiff, suberect to patent, 2–10 × 0.2–0.3 cm, green or grey-green, glabrous, apex pungent; ligule ca. 0.2 mm, upper part a fringe of hairs; leaf sheaths glabrous, usually persistent at base, pilose at mouth. Inflorescence linear-elliptic, 2–4(–8) × 0.4–0.5 cm, usually shortly exserted from uppermost leaf sheath, with many closely overlapping spikelets; pedicels shorter than spikelet, ca. 3 mm, widened at apex. Spikelets 1-flowered, 4–8 × 1–1.5 mm, yellowish brown or purplish brown; lower glume absent; upper glume as long as the spikelet, leathery, lanceolate-oblong to narrowly oblong, with slightly falcate apex, obscurely 7–11-veined, midvein usually shortly excurrent; lemma membranous, lanceolate- oblong, 3–4 mm, truncate or with a sinus, 1-veined; palea and lodicule reduced. Anthers 1.5–2.5 mm.

Locality: Ma On Shan, Castle Peak, Sai Kung, Lantau Island. Y. W. Lam 2167; K. L. Yip 4209; HK sheet 39436.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hebei, Liaoning, Shandong, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Korea.
Ecology: Coastal sands, river banks, roadsides and weedy places. Flowering & fruiting: May–Oct.
Notes: Listed in Rare and Precious Plants in Hong Kong.

Typha angustifolia L. 水燭
Sp. Pl. 2: 971. 1753; FRPS 8: 7, pl. 2: 6–7. 1992; FFJ 6: 3, fig. 1. 1995; FGD 6: 379. 2005; FOC 23: 162. 2010.

Perennial marsh herb; stems erect, 0.5–1.5(–3) m tall, stout. Leaves linear, spongy, 50–80(–120) cm × 4–10 mm, transverse section semicircular. Inflorescences a club-shaped spike, 30–60 cm, with a naked gap about 0.5–10 cm between the upper staminate part and the lower pistillate part. Male flowers with 2–3 stamens; female flowers with many filiform bracteoles on the stalk of ovary. Fruit narrowly elliptical.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. W. Lam 732, 1166; HK sheet 41712.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; temperate and subtropical regions of Asia, N Africa, Europe and N America.
Ecology: Marshes, swamps, shallow water of lakes and ponds. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Sep.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Aechmea fasciata (Lindl.) Baker 蜻蜓鳳梨
J. Bot. 17: 231. 1879.
Billbergia fasciata Lindl., Bot. Reg. 13: t. 1130. 1828.

Perennial herb. Leaves rosulate; leaf sheath broad, usually brownish-red, leaf blade ligulate, outer ones apex acute, inner ones apex rounded, with a minutely cuspidate tip, green, glaucous, with very manifest transverse, white bars (consisting of white scales), margin with robust, brownish black spines. Inflorescence a panicle, terminal on a robust, white-woolly peduncle; flowers of a same branch arranged to 3 or more directions; floral bracts well-developed, lanceolate, outer ones to 10 cm, narrower and shorter inwards, margin serrulate, pink to crimson. Sepals keeled, basally connate, with a rounded, minutely apiculate tip, white hairy. Petals violet or red, rounded, 2–3 cm.

Locality: Cultivated.
Distribution: Native to Brazil.
Uses: Ornamental.

Ananas comosus (L.) Merr. 鳳梨
Interpr. Herb. Amboin. 133. 1917; FHN 4: 86. 1977; FOC 24: 18. 2000.
Bromelia comosa L., Stickm. Herb. Amb. 21, 1754.

Perennial herb, with a simple, short stem, usually with suckers arising from the the base. Leaves closely and spirally arranged in a rosette, leaf blade sword-shaped, margin coarsely and laxly spinose-serrate. Inflorescence strobiliform, many-flowered, with a tuft of sterile leafy bracts at apex; floral bracts inconspicuous, margin serrulate or entire. Flowers many. Sepals free, slightly asymmetric, apex obtuse. Petals violet or reddish, free but connivent and tube-like. Stamens included. Syncarp globose, ovoid, or elongate, 15 cm or longer at maturity, becoming fleshy and fragrant. Seeds absent or very rare.

Locality: Cultivated.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan (cultivated); widely cultivated in tropical and subtropical regions; native to tropical America.
Uses: Fruit.

Billbergia pyramidalis (Sims) Lindl. 水塔花
Bot. Reg. 13: sub pl. 1068. 1827; FRPS 13(3): 67. 1997.
Bromelia pyramidalis Sims, Bot. Reg. 42: pl. 1732. 1815.

Stem very short. Leaves 6–15, forming a rosette; leaf blade lorate, 25–40 × 2–4 cm, apex acute or acuminate, with closely set, small marginal spines, abaxially usually with many white transverse bands, adaxially and basally pale or dark coloured. Spikes erect; bracts pink, lanceolate, 5–7 cm. Sepals 3, obtuse, pale red. Petals 3, bright red, ca. 4 cm, tipped with violet, during anthesis erect, with recurved, slightly broadened and rounded tips. Filaments equalling the corolla or slightly shorter; stigmas contorted, violet. Fruit a berry.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 28122, 28133.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong (cultivated); native to tropical America, widely cultivated in tropical regions.
Ecology: Flowering: Sep.
Uses: Ornamental.

Cryptanthus bromelioides Otto & A. Dietr. 銀背姬鳳梨
Allg. Gartenzeitung 4: 297. 1836; L. H. Bailey, Hortus Third 339. 1976.

Leaves all alike, not petioled, green adaxially, silvery abaxially, to 17 × 3.5 cm, spiny-margined. Inflorescences on a scape of 15 cm. Flowers many, in clusters of 4–6 in axils of keeled bracts, milky-white, ca. 4 cm, tube of calyx longer than lobes.

Locality: Cultivated.
Distribution: Native to Brazil, widely cultivated in tropical regions.
Uses: Ornamental.

Cryptanthus bromelioides Otto & A. Dietr. var. tricolor M. B. Foster 三色鳳梨
Bull. Bromeliad Soc. 3: 30. 1953; L. H. Bailey, Hortus Third 339. 1976.

It differs from var. bromelioides by leaves striped with ivory-white and green, overlaid with carmine-rose.

Locality: Cultivated. Distribution: Native to Brazil, widely cultivated in tropical regions.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: The species was reported as Cryptanthus bromelioides Otto & A. Dietr. cv. Tricolor previously (Check List HK Plants 350. 2002; 122. 2004).

Vriesea fosteriana L. B. Sm. 紅票
Arq. Bot. Estado São Paulo (2)1: 116, pl. 121. 1943; L. H. Bailey, Hortus Third 1164. 1976.

Plant to 1.8 m tall. Leaves forming a dense compact rosette, blue-green with maroon pencilling, to 65 × 7 cm. Spikes prominent with 2 opposed rows of multiple bracts at top end, unbranched. Petals green with purplish tips, to 3 cm or more, longer than stamens.

Locality: Cultivated.
Distribution: Native to Brazil.
Uses: Ornamental.

Vriesea splendens (Brongn.) Lem. 火劍
Fl. des Serres 162, f. 1850; L. H. Bailey, Man. Cult. Pl. 193. 1949, et Hortus Third. 1165. 1976.
Tillandsia splendens Brongn., Ann. Fl. Pomone 14: 311. 1845.

Plant to 90 cm tall. Leaves green with many irregularly dark-brown cross bands on both surfaces, ligulate or ligulate-lanceolate, 30–60 × 5–7 cm, concave above, with a rounded, shortly cuspidate tip. Scape equalling or exceeding foliage. Spike flalttened, densely imbricate bright red bracts. Sepals coriaceous, light yellow with a pale base, at the top whether or not tinged with red, 2–2.5 cm. Petals curved, slightly exceeding the bracts, yellow, obliquely opened at the top. Stamens exserted.

Locality: Cultivated.
Distribution: Native to tropical America.
Uses: Ornamental.

Ravenala madagascariensis Sonn. 旅人蕉
Voy. Ind. Orient. 2: 223, pl. 124–126. 1782; FHN 4: 89. 1977; FRPS 16(2): 16, fig. 4. 1981; FGD 2: 396, fig. 272. 1991.

Trunk palm-like, woody, 5–6(–30) m tall. Leaves large, musa-like in 2 ranks toward top of stem, giving the plant a fan-shaped appearance; leaf blade oblong, 1.5–2 m × 50–75 cm, slightly narrower toward the rounded apex, base subtruncate, concolorous on both surfaces. Inflorescences axillary; bracts 6–12, large and boat-shaped, one above the other and distichously arranged, each enveloping 5–12 flowers; sepals 3, lanceolate, ca. 20 × 1.2 cm, leathery; petals like the sepals, but the middle one shorter and narrower; stamens 6, slender, 15–16 cm, anthers two times as long as the filaments; ovary depressed, 4–5 mm; style equaling the sepals, stigma fusiform. Capsule woody, dehiscing by 3 valves.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens.
Distribution: Native to Madagascar; widely cultivated in tropical areas.
Ecology: Fertile soils. Flowering: All year around.
Uses: Ornamental.

Strelitzia nicolai Regel & Koern. 大鶴望蘭
Gartenflora 7: 265, pl. 235. 1858; FRPS 16(2): 18, pl. 5. 1981; FGD 2: 397. 1991.

Trunk up to 8 m, woody. Leaves in 2 ranks crowded toward apex of the trunk; leaf blade oblong, 90–120 × 45–60 cm, base subrounded, asymmetric, apex broadly obtuse; petiole to 1.8 m, sheathed at base. Inflorescences axillary; peduncle shorter than petiole, distally bearing 2 large spathe-bracts; spathe-bracts rigid, 25 – 32 cm, boat-shaped, ca. 6 cm across at the conduplicate base, green and tinged with purple. Flowers 4–9 in a helicoids cyme (cincinnus), with the lower part (ovary) enveloped in the spathe-bracts; sepals white, lanceolate, 13–17 × 1.5–3 cm, the anterior one narrower and keeled dorsally; petals 3, the middle one small, elliptic, 1.6 × 1.1 cm, apex mucronate, translucent, the lateral 2 connivent and forming an arrow-shaped organ, 10–12 cm, auricled on either side, dull blue; stamens concealed in the groove of the 2 connivent petals and slightly shorter than it, anthers linear, longer than the filaments; style rigid; stigma clavate, 3-branched.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. HK sheet 28106, 28107.
Distribution: Native to S Africa, widely cultivated in tropical regions.
Ecology: Flowering: May–Jul.
Uses: Ornamental.

Strelitzia reginae Aiton 鶴望蘭
Hort. Kew 1: 285. 1789; FRPS 16(2): 16. 1981; FGD 2: 397, fig. 273. 1991.

Perennial herb, 1–1.5 m tall, trunkless. Leaves distichous, blade oblong-lanceolate, 25–45 × 10 cm, base broadly cuneate to subrounded, apex acute, margin entire or ± undulate; petiole equaling or longer than the blade. Peduncle rising from axils of leaves, nearly or quite as long as petiole, usually bearing 1 spathe-bract; spathe-bracts boat-shaped, to 20 cm, green with purple margins. Flowers several in a helicoids cyme, subtended and partly enveloped by the spathe-bracts; sepals lanceolate, orange, 7.5–10 cm; petals 3, the middle one small, the lateral 2 connivent and forming an arrow-shaped organ, auricled on either side, dark blue; stamens as long as petals, anthers linear; style exserted; stigma 3-branched.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. HK sheet 28108.
Distribution: Native to S Africa.
Ecology: Flowering: Winter.
Uses: Ornamental.

Musa × paradisiaca L. 大蕉（甘蕉）
Sp. Pl. 2: 1043. 1753; FHN 4: 87. 1977; FGD 2: 394. 1991; FOC 24: 317. 2000.
Musa saepientum L., Sp. Pl. ed. 2, 1477. 1763; FKH 273. 1912.
Musa paradisiaca L. subsp. sapientum (L.) Kuntze, Rev. Gen. 2: 692. 1891.

Pseudostems clumped, 3–7 m tall, pruinose. Petiole pruinose, more than 30 cm, margin closed; leaf blade oblong, 1.5–3 m × 40–60 cm, base subcordate to auriculate, subsymmetric, apex acute, adaxially deep green, abaxially light green and distinctly pruinose. Inflorescence pendulous; rachis glabrous. Bracts adaxially deep red, abaxially purple, ovate to ovate-lanceolate, 15–30 cm or more, deciduous. Flowers in 2 rows in each bract; male flowers with tepals yellow to pale yellow. Compound tepal 4–6.5 cm; free tepal suborbicular to oblong, about half the length of compound tepal, waxy, apex acuminate or rolling into a sac. Infructescence with 7 or 8 clusters of berries. Berries straight or slightly curved, oblong, 10–20 cm, angled; pulp sweet or sweet and acidic, not very fragrant; stalk elongate. Seeds absent or few.

Locality: Cultivated. W. J. Tutcher 9190.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; widely cultivated.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: All year round.
Uses: Edible fruit.

Musa acuminata 'Dwarf Cavendish' 香蕉
Mem. Reale Accad. Sci. Torino 25: 394–395. 1820; FGD 2: 394. 1991; FOC 24: 316. 2000.
Musa nana Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 644. 1790; FRPS 16(2): 9. 1981.
Musa cavendishii Lamb. ex Paxt., Mag. Bot. 3: 51, pl. s.n. f. 1. 1837.
Musa chinensis Sweet, Hort. Britann. ed. 2, 596. 1826.

Pseudostems clumped, ca. 6 m tall, yellow-green, often with large, black markings. Petiole 60–75 cm, margin open, ca. 2 cm wide, often closed when young; leaf blade ovate-oblong, ca. 2.9 m × 90 cm, base auriculate, asymmetric, adaxially green and slightly pruinose or not. Inflorescence pendulous, ca. 2.5; peduncle and rachis glabrous. Bracts of bisexual and male flowers adaxially purple-red, abaxially brownish purple to yellow-green and pruinose, ovate to lanceolate, persistent, apex obtuse, reflexed after flowering; bracts of female flowers deciduous. Male flowers up to 20 per bract, in 2 rows. Compound tepal adaxially pale purple, abaxially pale purple-white, 4–5 cm, striate, teeth yellow to orange; free tepal milky white, translucent, obovate, about half the length of compound tepal, apex emarginate, shortly mucronate-apiculate. Infructescence pendulous, with ca. 8 clusters (“hands”) each of 15 or 16 berries in 2 rows. Berries grey-green, obovoid, ca. 13 × 4 cm, distinctly angled at maturity, base arrowed into a stalk ca. 2.5 cm, apex contracted or not into a short, angled column ca. 2 cm. Seeds many, brown, oblate, 5–10 mm in diam., minutely warty.

Locality: Cultivated. W. J. Tutcher 9189.
Distribution: S China; widely cultivated in tropical regions.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: All year round.
Uses: Edible fruit.
Notes: The species was reported as Musa acuminata ‘Cavendishii’ previously (Check List HK Plants 351. 2002; 122. 2004).

Musa balbisiana Colla 野蕉
Mem. Reale Accad. Sci. Torino 25: 384. 1820; Cheesm., Kew Bull. 1948(1): 14. 1948; FHN 4: 88. 1977; FRPS 16(2): 8. 1981; FGD 2: 393. 1991; FOC 24: 317. 2000.
Musa × paradisiaca L. subsp. seminifera (Lour.) Baker, Ann. Bot. 7: 213. 1893.
Musa seminifera Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 644. 1790.

Pseudostems clumped, to 6 m tall, yellow-green, often with black blotches. Petioles 60–75 cm, margin open, ca. 2 cm wide, often closed when young; leaf blade oblong, 2.9 m × 90 cm, base auriculate, asymmetric, adaxially green and slightly pruinose or not. Inflorescence pendulous, ca. 2.5 m; peduncle and rachis glabrous. Bracts of bisexual and male flowers adaxially purple-red, abaxially brownish purple to yellow-green and pruinose, ovate to lanceolate, persistent, apex obtuse, reflexed after flowering; bracts of female flowers deciduous. Male flowers up to 20 per bract, in 2 rows. Compound tepal abaxially pale purple, abaxially pale purple-white, 4–5 cm, striate, teeth yellow to orange; free tepal milky white, translucent, obovate, about half the length of compound tepal, apex emarginate, shortly mucronate-apiculate. Infructescence pendulous, with ca. 8 clusters (“hands”) each of 15 or 16 berries in 2 rows. Berries grey-green, obovoid, ca. 13 × 4 cm, distinctly angled at maturity, base narrowed into a stalk ca. 2.5 cm, apex contracted or not, into a short, angled column ca. 2 cm. Seeds many, brown, oblate, 5–10 mm in diam., minutely warty.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. Y. S. Lau 756; Y. W. Lam 1154.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; S & SE Asia.
Ecology: Moist places in ravines.

Musa coccinea Andrews 紅蕉
Bot. Repos. 1: pl. 47. 1799; FRPS 16(2): 14. 1981; FGD 2: 392. 1991; FOC 24: 316. 2000.
Musa uranoscopos Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 645. 1790.

Pseudostems 1–1.5 m tall, green. Petioles 30–40 cm, with narrow erect margins clasping pseudostem, not becoming scarious; leaf blade oblong or lanceolate, 55–100 × 15–25 cm, base rounded or obtuse, noticeably asymmetric, yellow-green, not pruinose. Inflorescence erect, elliptic, to 30 × 12 cm, very shortly pedunculate above sheath of topmost normal leaf, rachis glabrous. Bracts bright scarlet with green tips, lanceolate or oblong, 5.5–15 × 2.5–5.5 cm, after anthesis persisting during a very long time in an unfaded state. Male flowers 2 per bract, orange. Syntepalum 3.5–4 cm, 5-obtuse-dentated at top, free tepal nearly equaling syntepalum. Female flowers 1–3 per bract; perianth as in male flowers. Ovary orange-yellow, dorsiventrally compressed. Berries orange-yellow at full maturity, oblong, 4–10 cm, crowned persistent perianth; stalk 3–3.5 cm. Seeds many, cylindrical, 6 × 4 mm.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 28086.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan (cultivated); Vietnam.
Ecology: Flowering: Nearly all year round.
Uses: Ornamental.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Clear Water Bay, Tai Au Mun, Tin Ha Village
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Alpinia calcarata Roscoe 距花山薑
Trans. Linn. Soc. London 8: 347. 1807; FKH 272. 1912; FHN 4: 97. 1977; FRPS 16(2): 84. 1981; FOC 24: 336. 2000.

Pseudostems to 1.3 m. Leaves sessile; ligule 8 – 15 mm, glabrous, apex obtuse; leaf blade linear-lanceolate, 20–32 × 2–3.5 cm or narrower, base attenuate, apex acuminate and caudate-mucronate, margin with well-spaced, short bristles, glabrous. Panicles less than 10 cm; rachis slightly velvety; proximal branches 3–4-flowered. Bracteoles oblong, to 1.7 cm, membranous, apex obtuse. Pedicel ca. 3 mm. Calyx to 1.2 cm, split on 1 side, pubescent, apex 3-toothed. Corolla tube white, ca. 9 mm; lobes oblong, ca. 2.2 cm. Lateral staminodes red, subulate, ca. 3 mm, adnate to base of labellum. Labellum white with rose red and purple streaks, obovate, 2.7–3.5 × 1.5–2 cm, apex emarginate. Filaments ca. 1.3 cm; anther 5–7 mm. Ovary 3–4 mm in diam., sericeous. Capsules red, globose.

Locality: Clear Water Bay, Tai Au Mun, Tin Ha Village. Y. S. Lau 2998; HK sheet 34821.
Distribution: Guangdong; Myanmar, India, Sri Lanka.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: May–Sep.
Uses: Ornamental.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Wai, Tai Mo Shan
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Alpinia formosana K. Schum. 美山薑
Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 27(3): 283. 1899; FRPS 16(2): 86. 1981; FOC 24: 336. 2000.

Pseudostems to 1(–3.5) m. Ligule to 1 cm, abaxially villous, apex obtuse; petiole absent or to 1 cm; leaf blade lanceolate or oblonglanceolate, 50–70 × 8–12 cm, both ends acuminate. Panicles narrow, 15–20 cm; rachis glabrous or sparsely villous; branches 2–3-flowered; bracteoles elliptic, ca. 1.5 cm, apex mucronate. Pedicel ca. 3 mm. Calyx 1.3–1.7 cm, split on 1 side, apex 3-toothed, ciliate. Corolla tube ca. 1 cm, glabrous; lobes oblong, ca. 1.5 cm, apex ciliate. Lateral staminodes subulate, less than 2 mm. Labellum white tinged with yellow, marked with red stripes at centre, broadly ovate, ca. 3 cm, apex shortly 2-cleft, crisped. Stamen ca. 2 cm, with a knee-like bend. Ovary subglobose, white sericeous. Capsule vermilion, ellipsoidal, wrinkled.

Locality: Hong Kong Wai, Tai Mo Shan. S. Y. Hu 5526 (CUHK).
Distribution: Taiwan; Japan.
Ecology: Flowering: May.
Uses: Ornamental.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Victoria Peak, Shing Mun, Ma Nam Wat, Tsung Tsai Yuen, Sha Lo Tung, Chung Mei, Nam Chung
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Alpinia galanga (L.) Willd. 紅豆蔻
Sp. Pl. 1(1): 12. 1797; FHK 348. 1861; FKH 272. 1912; FHN 4: 97. 1977; FRPS 16(2): 71. 1981; FGD 2: 411. 1991; FOC 24: 343. 2000.

Rhizomes tuberous. Pseudostems ca. 2 m. Ligule suborbicular, ca. 5 mm; petiole ca. 6 mm; leaf blade oblong or lanceolate, 25–35 × 6–10 cm, base attenuate, apex acute or acuminate, glabrous or abaxially pubescent. Panicles ca. 20 × 30 cm; rachis glabrous or pubescent; branches many, 2–4 cm, 3–6-flowered. Bracts and bracteoles persistent; bracteoles lanceolate, 5–8 mm. Flowers greenwhite, fragrant. Calyx tubular, 6–10 mm, persistent. Corolla tube 6–10 mm; lobes oblong, 1.6–1.8 cm. Lateral staminodes purple, subulate or linear, 2–10 mm. Labellum white with red lines, obovate-spatulate, ca. 2 cm, apex deeply 2-cleft. Filaments ca. 1 cm; anther ca. 7 mm. Capsules brown or red when dry, oblong, slightly contracted at middle, 1–1.5 cm × ca. 7 mm, thin, glabrous. Seeds 3–6.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Shing Mun, Ma Nam Wat, Tsung Tsai Yuen, Sha Lo Tung, Chung Mei, Nam Chung. H. C. Tang 226; Y. S. Lau 2732; L. T. Lo 497.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; tropical Asia.
Ecology: Secondary forests and thickets. Flowering: May–Aug.; fruiting: Sep.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Alpinia hainanensis K. Schum. 草豆蔻
Pflanzenr. 46(20): 335. 1904; FHN 4: 99. 1977; FRPS 16(2): 83. 1981; FGD 2: 414. 1991; FOC 24: 339. 2000.
Alpinia katsumada Hayata, Icon. Plan. Formosan. 5: 224. 1915; FPRS 16(2): 91. 1981; FGD 2: 416. 1991.
Alpinia henryi K. Schum., Pflanzenr. 20(IV.46): 335. 1904; FPRS 16(2): 92. 1981; FGD 2: 417. 1991.
Alpinia kainanntensis Masam., Trans. Nat. Hist. Soc. Taiwan 33: 28. 1943.

Pseudostems to 3 m. Ligule (3–)5–10 mm, abaxially hirsute; petiole absent to 2 cm; leaf blade linear-lanceolate, 20–65 × 2–12 cm, base obliquely attenuate, margin hairy, apex acuminate, with spirally caudate mucro, glabrous or rarely abaxially sparsely hirsute. Racemes erect, 10–30 cm, yellow hirsute; bracts 4–4.5 cm, glabrous; bracteoles milky white, broadly elliptic, 2–3.5 cm, hirsute at base and gradually becoming glabrous toward mucronate apex. Pedicel 2–3 mm. Calyx campanulate, 2–3 cm, split on 1 side, abaxially hairy, apex 2-toothed. Corolla tube 8–10 mm; lobes lanceolate, 2.5–3 cm, margin ciliate. Lateral staminodes subulate, ca. 3 mm. Labellum marked with radiate, purple stripes from centre to margin, triangular-ovate, 3.5–4.5 cm, apex shallowly 2-cleft. Filament ca. 1.5 cm; anther 1.2–1.5 cm. Ovary hirsute, ca. 5 mm in diam. Capsule globose, 2–3 cm in diam., yellow hirsute.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 173; L. T. Lo 24; HK sheet 28026.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.; fruiting: May–Aug.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore)

Alpinia japonica (Thunb.) Miq. 山薑
Ann. Mus. Bot. Lugduno-Batavum 3: 140. 1867; FRPS 16(2): 102. 1981; FGD 2: 419. 1991; FOC 24: 341. 2000.
Globba japonica Thunb. in Murray, Syst. Veg., ed. 14, 73. 1784.

Pseudostems 35–70 cm. Ligule 2-cleft, ca. 2 mm, pubescent; petiole to 2 cm; leaf blade lanceolate, oblanceolate, or narrowly long elliptic, 25–40 × 4–7 cm, base attenuate, apex acuminate, mucronate, pubescent especially abaxially. Racemes 15–30 cm; rachis densely tomentose; involucral bracts lanceolate, ca. 9 cm, deciduous at anthesis; bracteoles very small, early deciduous. Flowers usually paired on rachis, often also with degenerate flowers; pedicel ca. 2 mm. Calyx clavate, 1–1.2 cm, pubescent, apex 3-toothed. Corolla tube ca. 1 cm, sparsely puberulent; lobes oblong, ca. 1 cm, abaxially tomentose, central one hood-like. Lateral staminodes linear, ca. 5 mm. Labellum white marked with red stripes, ovate, ca. 6 mm wide, margin irregularly notched, apex 2-cleft. Stamen 1.2–1.4 cm. Ovary densely tomentose. Capsule salmon red, globose or ellipsoidal, 1–1.5 cm in diam., pubescent, apex with persistent calyx. Seeds ca. 5 × 3 mm, many-angled, with camphor-like odour.

Locality: Sunset Peak. F. W. Xing 7093; HK sheet 36003.
Distribution: SE to SW China; Japan.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Apr.–Aug.; fruiting: Jul.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Chuk Kok
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Alpinia oblongifolia Hayata 華山薑
Icon. Pl. Formosan. 5: 215. 1915; FOC 24: 342. 2000.
Alpinia chinensis auct. non (Retz.) Rosc.: FHK 349. 1861; FKH 273. 1912; FHN 4: 96. 1977; FRPS 16(2): 77. 1981.
Alpinia suishaensis Hayata, Icon. Pl. Formosan. 9: 123. 1920; R. M. Sm, Edinb. J. Bot. 47(1): 59. 1990.

Pseudostems ca. 1 m. Ligule 4–10 mm, membranous, margin ciliate; petiole ca. 5 mm; leaf blade oblong, ovate-lanceolate or lanceolate, 20–30 × 3–10 cm, glabrous, base rounded or attenuate, apex acuminate or caudate-acuminate. Panicles narrow, 15–30 × 2–2.5 cm; branches 3–10 mm, 1–4-flowered; bracteoles 1–3 mm, deciduous. Pedicel to 1 mm. Calyx tubular, 5–7 mm, apex 3-toothed. Corolla tube slightly longer than calyx; lobes oblong, 6–7 mm. Lateral staminodes subulate, 1–2 mm. Labellum white with 2 red stripes from base to middle, ovate, 6–8 mm, apex 2-lobed. Filament ca. 5 mm; anther ca. 3 mm. Ovary globose. Capsule red, globose, 5–8 mm in diam. Seeds 5–8.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Chuk Kok. Y. W. Lam 2263; HK sheet 34246, 35852.
Distribution: SW to SE China.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.; fruiting: Jun.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Au Mun, Clear Water Bay, Tung Lung Chau
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Alpinia officinarum Hance 高良薑
J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 13: 6. 1873; FHN 4: 98. 1977; FRPS 16(2): 100. 1981; FGD 2: 418. 1991; FOC 24: 340. 2000.

Rhizomes elongate, terete. Pseudostems 40–110 cm. Leaves sessile; ligule lanceolate, entire, 2–3(–5) cm, membranous; leaf blade linear, 20–30 × 1.2–2.5 cm, base attenuate, apex caudate, glabrous. Racemes erect, 6–10 cm; rachis tomentose; bracteoles very small, less than 1 cm. Pedicel 1–2 mm. Calyx 8–10 cm, puberulent, apex 3-toothed. Corolla tube slightly shorter than calyx; lobes oblong, ca. 1.5 cm, central one hood-like. Labellum white with red streaks, ovate, ca. 2 cm. Filament ca. 1 cm; anther ca. 6 mm. Ovary tomentose. Capsules red, globose, ca. 1 cm in diam.

Locality: Tai Au Mun, Clear Water Bay, Tung Lung Chau. Y. S. Lau 2834; Y. W. Lam 1788; S. C. Ng 2816.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi.
Ecology: Thickets and thin forests. Flowering: Apr.–Sep.; fruiting: May–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (forklore).

Alpinia sichuanensis Z. Y. Zhu 四川山薑（箭稈風）
Bull. Sichuan School Chin. Mat. Med. 8: 15. 1986; FOC 24: 342. 2000; Z. L. Zhao, Act. Phytotax. Sin. 41(6): 575. 2003.
Alpinia jianganfeng T. L. Wu, Novon 7: 441. 1997; FOC 24: 342. 2000.

Pseudostems to 1 m. Ligule 2-cleft, ca. 2 mm, margin ciliate; petiole absent to 4 cm; leaf blade lanceolate or linear-lanceolate, 20–30 × 2–4 (–6) cm, base attenuate, apex narrowly caudate, glabrous except hispid at subapical margin. Spikes erect, 10–20 cm; rachis tomentose; bracteoles very small. Flowers in clusters of 3 on rachis. Calyx cylindrical, abaxially pubescent, apex 3-cleft. Corolla tube subequaling or slightly longer than calyx; lobes oblong, 8–10 mm, abaxially villous. Lateral staminodes linear, ca. 2 mm. Labellum obovate, 0.7–1.3 cm, margin crisped, apex 2-cleft. Stamen longer than labellum; anther ca. 4 mm. Ovary globose, pubescent. Capsule globose, 7–8 mm in diam., pubescent, apex with persistent calyx. Seeds 5–6.

Locality: Sunset Peak. HK sheet 34721, 34722, 36147.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi.
Ecology: Thickets and thin forests. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.; fruiting: Jun.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (forklore).

Alpinia stachyodes Hance 密苞山薑
J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 13: 126. 1873; FKH 272. 1912; FOC 24: 345. 2000.
Alpinia densibracteata T. L. Wu & Senjen, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 16(3): 32. 1978; FRPS 16(2): 80. 1981; FGD 2: 413. 1991.

Pseudostems 1–1.5 m. Leaf sheath tomentose; ligule orbicular, 2-cleft, ca. 1 cm, tomentose, margin ciliate; petiole 0.5–2 cm, tomentose; leaf blade oblong-lanceolate, 20–40 × 4–7 cm, leathery, base attenuate, apex acuminate, with caudate tip ca. 2.5 cm, glabrous except tomentose at margin and apex, or abaxially tomentose especially on median veins. Spikes erect, subsessile, cylindrical, 10–16 cm; involucral bract linear, 8–9 cm × 8–10 mm; bracts ovate or lanceolate, 1.5–2.5 cm, densely imbricate tomentose, 3-flowered, persistent; bracteoles lanceolate, 5–10 mm, tomentose, persistent. Flowers fragrant, tomentose. Calyx tubular, 1–1.5 cm, apex 3-toothed. Corolla tube ca. 1.2 cm; lobes oblong, ca. 6 mm, concave. Lateral staminodes linear, ca. 2 mm. Labellum striped at centre, rhomboidal-ovate, obscurely 3-lobed, ca. 7 × 3 mm, margin undulate.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 94, 451, 667.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Jiangxi.
Ecology: Thickets and thin forests. Flowering: Apr.–Sep.; fruiting: May–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (forlklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Authority: (Pers.) B. L. Burtt & R. M. Sm.
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Alpinia zerumbet (Pers.) B. L. Burtt & R. M. Sm. 豔山薑
Notes Roy. Bot. Gard. Edinburgh 31(2): 204. 1972; FHN 4: 96. 1977; FRPS 16(2): 86. 1981; FGD 2: 415. 1991; FOC 24: 336. 2000.
Costus zerumbet Pers., Syn. Pl. 1: 3. 1805.
Alpinia speciosa (Wendl.) K. Schum., Pflanzenr. (IV.46): 339. 1904, non Dietr.(1839).
Alpinia nutans auct. non (L.) Rosc.: FHK 348. 1861; FKH 272. 1912.

Pseudostems 2–3 m. Ligule 5–10 mm, abaxially hairy; petiole 1–1.5 cm; leaf blade lanceolate, 30–60 × 5–10 cm, base attenuate, apex acuminate with a spiral mucro, glabrous except pubescent at margin. Panicles drooping, to 30 cm, enclosed by 2 long sheaths when young; rachis purple-red, velvety; branches very short, 1–2(–3)-flowered; bracteoles enclose flower buds, white with pink apex, elliptic, 3–3.5 cm, glabrous. Pedicel 1–2 cm. Calyx white, subcampanulate, ca. 2 cm, split on 1 side, apex toothed. Corolla tube shorter than calyx; lobes milky white with pink apex, oblong, ca. 3 mm; central lobe larger than lateral ones. Lateral staminodes subulate, ca. 2 mm. Labellum yellow with purple-red stripes, broadly ovate-spatulate, 4–6 cm, crisped. Stamen ca. 2.5 mm. Ovary golden yellow hirsute. Capsule vermilion, globose, ca. 2 cm in diam., ribbed, apex with persistent calyx. Seeds angled.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. HK sheet 42838.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Taiwan; Vietnam, Cambodia, Laos, Thailand, Myanmar, Bangladesh, India, Sri Lanka, Malaysia, Indonesia, Philippines.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr.–Jun.; fruiting: Jul.–Oct.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: A cultivar (Alpinia zerumbet ‘Variegata’ 花葉豔山薑) is cultivated in Hong Kong for ornamental use. It is characterized by its leaves variegated in feather design with stripes and bands of creamy yellow.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Authority: (Pers.) B. L. Burtt & R. M. Sm.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Shing Mun, Mau Ping, Tai Po
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Curcuma aromatica Salisb. 郁金（鬱金）
Parad. Lond. 1: pl. 96. 1807; FHN 4: 95. 1977; FRPS 16(2): 60. 1981; FGD 2: 407. 1991; FOC 24: 362. 2000.

Plants ca. 1 m tall. Rhizomes yellow inside, elliptic or narrowly so, fleshy, aromatic; roots with fusiform tubers. Petiole equaling leaf blade; leaf blade oblong, 30–60 × 10–20 cm, base attenuate, apex narrowly caudate, adaxially glabrous, abaxially pubescent. Inflorescences on separate shoots arising from rhizomes, usually appearing before leaves; spike cylindrical, ca. 15 × 8 cm; fertile bracts pale green, ovate, 4–5 cm; coma bracts white, tinged with red.

Locality: Shing Mun, Mau Ping, Tai Po. Aubrey 11548; L. T. Lo 474; HK sheet 27957.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Taiwan; tropical Asia.
Ecology: Thin Forests.

Curcuma longa L. 薑黃
Sp. Pl. 1: 2. 1753; FRPS 16(2): 62. 1981; FGD 2: 408. 1991; FOC 24: 361. 2000.
Curcuma domestica Valeton, Bull. Jard. Bot. Buitenz. 2 ser. 27: 31. 1918; FHN 4: 94. 1977.

Plants ca. 1 m tall. Rhizomes many-branched, orange inside, cylindrical, aromatic; roots tuberous at tip. Petiole 20–45 cm, leaf blade green, oblong or elliptic, 30–45(–90) × 15–18 cm, base attenuate, apex shortly acuminate, glabrous. Inflorescences terminal on pseudostems. Peduncle 12–20 cm; spike cylindrical, 12–18 × 4–9 cm; fertile bracts pale green, ovate or oblong, 3–5 cm, apex obtuse; coma bracts spreading, white and green, sometimes tinged reddish purple, apex acute. Calyx white, 0.8–1.2 cm, puberulent, apex unequally 3-toothed. Corolla pale yellow; tube to 3 cm; lobes deltoid, 1–1.5 cm, central one larger, apex mucronate. Lateral staminodes shorter than labellum. Labellum yellowish with central, yellow band, obovate, 1.2–2 cm. Anther spurred at base. Ovary sparsely hairy.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 27960.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Taiwan; tropical Asia.
Ecology: Flowering: Aug.
Uses: Medicinal (forklore), spice.

Hedychium coronarium J. König 薑花
Observ Bot. 3: 73. 1783; FRPS 16(2): 26. 1981; FGD 2: 402. 1991; FOC 24: 372. 2000.

Pseudostems usually 1–1.5 m. Leaves sessile; ligule 2–3 cm, membranous; leaf blade oblong-lanceolate or lanceolate, 20–40 × 4.5–8 cm, base acute, apex long acuminate, adaxially glabrous, abaxially finely pubescent or thinly hairy. Spikes ellipsoidal, 10–20 × 4–8 cm; bracts imbricate, ovate, 4.5–5 × 2.5–4 cm, 2–3-flowered. Flowers white, fragrant. Calyx ca. 4 cm, split on 1 side. Corolla tube ca. 8 cm, slender; lobes lanceolate, ca. 5 cm, central one spatulate, apex mucronate. Lateral staminodes oblonglanceolate, ca. 5 cm. Labellum white, pale yellow at base, obcordate, 4–6 × 4–6 cm, apex 2-cleft. Filament ca. 3 cm; anther ca. 1.5 cm. Ovary sericeous.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 2086, 2421.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Sichuan, Yunnan, Taiwan; Vietnam, Myanmar, Thailand, Nepal, Sikkim, Bhutan, India, Sri Lanka, Malaysia, Indonesia, Australia.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Mo Shan, Tai Long Sai Wan
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Zingiber corallinum Hance 珊瑚薑
J. Bot. 18: 301. 1880; FHN 4: 102. 1977; FRPS 16(2): 142. 1981; FGD 2: 430. 1991; FOC 24: 326. 2000.

Pseudostems ca. 1 m tall. Leaves sessile; leaf sheath sparsely hairy or glabrous; ligule 2–4 mm; leaf blade oblong-lanceolate or lanceolate, 20–30 × 4–6 cm, adaxially glabrous, abaxially sparsely hairy or glabrous. Inflorescences arising from rhizomes, oblong, 15–30 cm; peduncle 15–20 cm; scale-like sheaths 4–5 cm; bracts red, ovate, 3–4 cm, apex acute. Calyx 1.5–1.8 cm, split to middle. Corolla tube 2.5 cm, lobes with purple stripes, oblong, ca. 1.5 cm, apex acute, central one larger than lateral ones; central lobe of labellum obovate, ca. 1.5 cm; lateral lobes ca. 8 mm, apex acute. Anther sessile, ca. 1 cm; connective appendage beak-like, curved, ca. 5 mm. Ovary 2–2.5 mm, sericeous. Seeds black, glossy.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Tai Long Sai Wan. Y. S. Lau 1027; HK sheet 27972, 27973.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi.
Ecology: Forests or cultivated. Flowering: May–Aug.; fruiting: Aug.–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (forklore).

Zingiber integrilabrum Hance 全唇薑
J. Bot. 20: 80. 1882; FKH 272. 1912; FRPS 16(2): 148. 1981; FGD 2: 431. 1991; FOC 24: 327. 2000.

Rhizomes branched, odourless. Pseudostems 40–100 cm high. Ligule orbicular, 2-lobed, to 1 mm; petiole absent to 5 mm; leaf blade lanceolate, 15–18 × ca. 3 cm, adaxially glabrous, abaxially pubescent or pilose. Inflorescences arising from rhizomes, ca. 1/2 embedded in ground, 4–5-flowered; peduncle 1–2 times as long as inflorescence; scale-like sheaths 2–3 cm; bracts becoming brownish when old, lanceolate, 2–3 cm, glabrous; bracteoles ca. 2 cm, membranous. Calyx ca. 2 cm, split on one side, glabrous. Corolla ivory white; tube ca. 2.7 cm; lobes lanceolate ca. 1.8 cm. Labellum elliptic, lateral lobes reduced into rounded teeth or absent. Anther sessile, ca. 8 mm; connective appendage ca. 7 mm.

Locality: Mount Gough. HK sheet 7228.
Distribution: Endemic to Hong Kong.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Apr.–Oct.
Notes: The type specimen (Hance Herb No. 21812, BM) was collected by C. Ford from Mount Gough in April 1881. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Zingiber mioga (Thunb.) Roscoe 蘘荷
Trans. Linn. Soc. London 8: 348. 1807; FHN 4: 102. 1977; FRPS 16(2): 146. 1981; FGD 2: 430. 1991. FOC 24: 332. 2000.
Amomum mioga Thunb., Syst. Veg. (ed. 14) 51. 1784.

Rhizomes yellowish. Ligule 2-lobed, 3–12 mm, membranous; petiole absent to 1.7 cm; leaf blade lanceolate-elliptic or linearlanceolate, 20–37 × 4–6 cm, apex caudate, glabrous or abaxially pilose. Inflorescences arising from rhizomes, ellipsoidal, 5–7 cm; peduncle absent to 17 cm; scale-like sheaths oblong; bracts reddish green with purple veins, elliptic. Calyx 2–3 cm. Corolla tube longer than calyx; lobes yellowish, lanceolate 2.7–3 cm × ca. 7 mm. Labellum ovate, ca. 3 cm; central lobe yellow with white margin, ca. 2.5 × 1.8 cm; lateral lobes 1.3 cm × 4 mm. Anther ca. 1 cm; connective appendage ca. 1 cm. Capsule obovoid, loculicidally dehiscent; pericarp red inside. Seeds black; aril white.

Locality: Ma On Shan, Sunset Peak. F. W. Xing 7543; HK sheet 34827.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang; Japan.
Ecology: Moist places in mountain valleys. Flowering: Aug.–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (forklore), vegetable (young inflorescence).

Zingiber officinale Roscoe 薑
Trans. Linn. Soc. London 8: 348. 1807; FKH 272. 1912; FHN 4: 102. 1977; FRPS 16(2): 141. 1981; FGD 2: 429. 1991; FOC 24: 325. 2000.

Rhizomes branched, yellowish inside, thickened, fleshy, strongly aromatic. Pseudostems 50 – 100 cm. Leaves sessile; ligule slightly 2-lobed, 2 – 4 mm, membranous; leaf blade lanceolate or linear-lanceolate, 15 – 30 × 2 – 2.5 cm, glabrescent. Inflorescences arising from rhizomes, ovoid, 4 – 5 × ca. 1.5 cm; peduncle to 25 cm; bracts pale green, sometimes yellowish at margin, ovate, ca. 22.5 cm, apex mucronate; bracteoles equaling bracts. Calyx ca. 1 cm. Corolla yellowish green; tube 2 – 2.5 cm; lobes lanceolate, ca. 1.8 cm. Central lobe of labellum with purple stripes and cream blotches, oblong-obovate, shorter than corolla lobes; lateral lobes ovate, ca. 6 mm, free nearly to base. Stamen dark purple; anther ca. 9 mm; connective appendage curved, ca. 7 mm.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 27976, 32657.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Shandong, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; widely cultivated in tropics in Asia.
Ecology: Cultivated in vegetable gardens. Flowering: Oct.
Uses: Flavour, medicinal (forklore).

Zingiber striolatum Diels 陽荷
Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 29: 262. 1901; FRPS 16(2): 146. 1981; FGD 2: 431. 1991; FOC 24: 332. 2000.

Rhizomes white, slightly fragrant. Pseudostems 1–1.5 m. Ligule brown striped, 2-lobed, 4–7 mm, membranous; petiole 0.8–1.2 cm; leaf blade lanceolate or elliptic-lanceolate, 25–35 × 3–6 cm, base attenuate, apex caudate, abaxially glabrous or sparsely villose. Inflorescences arising from rhizomes, subovoid; peduncle 1.5–2 cm or longer; scale-like sheaths 2–3; bracts red, broadly ovate or elliptic, 3–5 cm, pubescent. Calyx ca. 2.5 cm, membranous. Corolla tube white, 4–6 cm; lobes white or yellowish with purplish brown stripes, oblong-lanceolate, 3–3.5 cm. Labellum pale purple, obovate, ca. 3 × 2.6 cm; lateral lobes ca. 5 mm. Filaments very short; anther lanceolate, ca. 1.5 cm; connective appendage ca. 1.5 cm. Capsule loculicidally dehiscent; pericarp red inside. Seeds black; aril white.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. G. Barretto 254; HK sheet 34253.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Jul.–Oct.; fruiting: Sep.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (forklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Tam Tuk, Pok Fu Lam, Peel Rise, Bowen Rd., Tung Chung
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Zingiber zerumbet (L.) Roscoe ex Sm. 紅球薑
Exot. Bot. 2: 105. 1806; FKH 272. 1912; FHN 4: 102. 1977; FRPS 16(2): 142. 1981; FGD 2: 429. 1991; FOC 24: 326. 2000.
Amomum zerumbet L., Sp. Pl. 1: 1. 1753.

Rhizomes yellowish inside. Pseudostems 0.6–2 m. Leaves sessile or shortly petiolate; ligule entire, 1.5–2 cm, leaf blade lanceolate or oblong-lanceolate, 15–40 × 3–8 cm, base narrowed, apex acuminate, glabrescent or abaxially somewhat pilose. Inflorescences arising from rhizomes, conical or ovoid-oblong, 6–15 × 3.5–5 cm, apex obtuse; peduncle 10–30 cm; scale-like sheaths 5–7; bracts closely imbricate, green when young, red when old, slightly hairy, slimy adaxially, margin membranous; bracteoles ca. 1.5 cm. Calyx 1.2–2 cm, membranous, split on 1 side, apex 3-toothed. Corolla tube 2–3 cm, slender; lobes pale yellow, lanceolate, central one 1.5–2.5 cm. Labellum pale yellow, ca. 1.5 × 2.5 cm; central lobe suborbicular or subobovate, 1.5–2 × ca. 1.5 cm, apex emarginate; lateral lobes obovate, ca. 1 cm, free nearly to base. Stamen ca. 1 cm; connective appendage beak-like, ca. 8 mm. Ovary ca. 4 mm, glabrous. Capsule ellipsoidal, 0.8–1.2 cm. Seeds black.

Locality: Tai Tam Tuk, Pok Fu Lam, Peel Rise, Bowen Rd., Tung Chung. H. C. Tang 2050; Y. S. Lau 1567; S. C. Ng 2633.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Taiwan; Vietnam, Cambodia, Laos, Myanmar, Thailand, Malaysia, India, Sri Lanka.
Ecology: Moist places in forest. Flowering: Jul.–Sep.; fruiting: Oct.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal (forklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Mount Gough, Tai Hang Rd., Lantau Peak
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Costus speciosus (J. König) Sm. 閉鞘薑
Trans. Linn. Soc. London 1: 249. 1791; FHN 4: 91. 1977; FRPS 16(2): 149. 1981; FGD 2: 432. 1991; FOC 24: 321. 2000.
Banksea speciosa J. König, Observ. Bot. 3: 75. 1783.

Stems 1–3 m, base slightly woody, apex branched and spirally twisted when old. Petiole 5–7 mm; leaf blade oblong or lanceolate, 15–20 × 6–10 cm, base subrounded, apex acuminate or caudateacuminate, abaxially densely sericeous. Inflorescences terminal, ellipsoidal or ovoid, 5–15 cm. Bracts bright red, ovate, ca. 2 cm, leathery, pubescent, apex sharply pointed; bracteoles pale red, 1.2–1.5 cm. Calyx red, 1.8–2 cm, leathery, apex 3-lobed; lobes reddish black, rigid, and densely sericeous at apex. Corolla tube ca. 1 cm; lobes oblong-elliptic, ca. 5 cm, apex white or red. Labellum white, trumpet-shaped, 6.5–9 cm, apex toothed and crisped, with edges overlapping. Stamens petaloid, white with orange-yellow base, urceolate, ca. 4.5–1.3 cm, pubescent. Capsules red, globose, ca. 1.5 cm, slightly woody. Seeds black, glossy, ca. 3 mm.

Locality: Mount Gough, Tai Hang Rd., Lantau Peak. H. C. Tang 605; Y. S. Lau 2123; HK sheet 39872.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Taiwan; tropical Asia.
Ecology: Thin forests. Flowering: Jul.–Sep.; fruiting: Sep.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (forklore).

Canna × generalis L. H. Bailey & E. Z. Bailey 大花美人蕉
Hortus 118. 1930, et Man. Cult. Pl. 291. 1949; FRPS 16(2): 155. 1981; FGD 2: 434. 1991.
Canna orchioides Bailey, Man. Cult. Pl. 291. 1949.

Plant ca. 1.5 m tall; stems, leaves and inflorescences glaucous. Leaves elliptic, to 40 × 20 cm, sheath and margins purple. Racemes terminal, 15–30 cm; flower large dense, 1–2 each bract; sepals lanceolate, 1.5–3 cm; corolla tube 5–10 mm, lobes lanceolate, 4.5–6.5 cm; outer cycle staminodes 3, obovate-spathulate, 5–10 × 2–5 cm, various coloured, red, orange, white, etc.; labellum obovatespathulate, ca. 4.5 × 1.2–4 cm; stamen lanceolate, ca. 4 × 2.5 cm; style loriform.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 2715.
Distribution: Widely cultivated in tropical and subtropical regions.
Ecology: Flowering: Summer to autumn.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: There are many cultivars in this species, common ones are ‘President’, ‘Striates’, ‘Scarlet Beauty’ and ‘King Humbert’.

Canna glauca L. 粉美人蕉
Sp. Pl. 1: 1. 1753; FRPS 16(2): 155. 1981; FGD 2: 434. 1991.

Rhizomes elongate; stem 1.5–2 m, green. Leaves green, glaucous, lanceolate, to 50 × 10–15 cm, base attenuate, apex long-acuminate, margin hyaline. Racemes simple or sparingly branched, with a green, pruinose rachis; bracts round, brown; flowers in pairs, rarely in threes; light yellow, not dotted; sepals green, ovate, 1.2 cm; corolla tube 1–2 cm, lobes linear-lanceolate, 2.5–5 × 5 cm, erect; outer cycle staminodes 3, obovate-oblong, 6–7.5 × 2–3 cm, entire; labellum yellowish, much narrower, linear-lanceolate, bifid at apex, twisty at medium; stamens obovatesubfalcate, apex acute, revolute; style narrow-lanceolate. Capsules oblong, 3.5 cm.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 32948.
Distribution: Widely cultivated in tropical and subtropical regions, native to S America.
Ecology: Flowering: Summer to autumn.
Uses: Ornamental.

Canna indica L. 美人蕉
Sp. Pl. 1: 1. 1753; FHK 349. 1861; FKH 273. 1912; FHN 4: 103. 1977; FRPS 16(2): 157. 1981; FGD 2: 435. 1991; FOC 24: 378. 2000.
Canna edulis Ker, Bot. Reg. 9: t. 775. 1823; FHN 4: 104. 1977; FRPS 16(2): 157. 1981; FGD 2: 435. 1991.

Rhizome developed, much branched. Stems stout, to 2.5 m. Leaf sheath green or purple; petiole short; leaf blade ovate-oblong to oblong, 30–60 × 10–20 cm, adaxially green, abaxially and at margin green or purple. Inflorescence a raceme of cincinni. Bracts light purple, ovate, ca. 8 mm. Flowers 1–2 per cincinnus. Sepals pale purplish green, lanceolate, ca. 1.5 cm. Corolla tube apricot yellow, ca. 1.5 cm; lobes erect, red to apricot yellow with purplish apex, lanceolate, ca. 4 cm. Staminodes 2(–3), erect, red with apricot yellow base, oblanceolate, 4–5.5 cm × 7–10 mm, 1 with apex emarginate; labellum red, sometimes with yellow spots, lanceolate, ca. 4.5 cm, margin revolute, apex emarginate; fertile stamen with filament reddish apricot yellow, lanceolate, ca. 4.2 cm. Anther ca. 9 mm. Ovary green, globose, ca. 6 mm in diam., warty. Style red to apricot yellow, narrow, ca. 6 cm, base adnate to staminode column. Capsule broadly ovoid, 1.2–1.8 cm.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 2428, 3075; HK sheet 7351.
Distribution: Widely cultivated in China; native to India.
Ecology: Flowering: Mar.–Dec.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal (forklore), food (tuberous rhizome).

Calathea ornata (Lindl.) Körn. 肖竹芋
Bull. Soc. Imp. Naturalistes Moscou 35(1): 127. 1862; FRPS 16(2): 165. 1981.

Strong virgorous plant, 30 – 90 cm tall. Leaves oblonglanceolate, 30–90 cm, young leaves often marked with pink and white lines along lateral veins; adult foliage rich green adaxially and dull purple-red abaxially, ± cordate at base, apex acute; petiole becoming 60 cm or more long with age. Spike ovoid, ca. 8 cm; peduncles to 35 cm; petals violet; staminode yellowish.

Locality: Cultivated.
Distribution: Taiwan (cultivated); native to S America.
Ecology: Flowering: May–Jun.
Uses: Ornamental.

Calathea zebrina (Sims) Lindl. 絨葉肖竹芋（斑葉肖竹芋）
Bot. Reg. sub pl. 1210. 1829; FRPS 16(2): 165. 1981; FGD 2: 439. 1991.
Maranta zebrina Sims, Curt's Bot. Mag. t. 1926. 1817.

Plant 50–100 cm tall. Leaves cauline; petioles to 45 cm; leaf blade oblong-lanceolate, 30–60 cm long and nearly or quite half as broad, base unequilateral, apex obtuse or very short-acute, velvety green and with alternating bars of pale yellow-green and olive-green extending outward from midrib adaxially, purplish-red abaxially in adult. Head solitary on scape, nearly globular or ovoid; bracts imbricate, dilate-ovate, ca. 5 cm wide, purple inside; sepals oblong, to 2.5 cm; corolla blue-purple or white, lobes oblonglanceolate, 1.5 cm; staminode pale lilac, 1.7 cm.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 3219, 3288; HK sheet 28072.
Distribution: Guangdong, Taiwan (cultivated); native to Brazil.
Ecology: Flowering: May–Jun.
Uses: Ornamental.

Maranta arundinacea L. 竹芋
Sp. Pl. 1: 2. 1753; Curt's Bot. Mag. t. 2307. 1822; FHN 4: 106. 1977; FRPS 16(2): 167, pl. 59. 1981; FGD 2: 440. 1991; FOC 24: 382. 2000.

Herb, 40–130 cm tall. Rhizomes sympodial, spindle-shaped, fleshy, starchy. Stems slender, erect, dichotomous branched. Basal leaves 4–8; cauline leaves 1–8; petiole 3.5–20 cm in basal leaves, often absent in cauline leaves, pulvinus 5–10 mm; leaf blade green, ovate-oblong, 10–20 × 4–10 cm, base round, apex acuminate, abaxially glabrous or sparsely pilose. Racemes terminal, 15–20 cm, loose. Bracts linear-lanceolate, 3–4 cm, involute. Flowers mostly self-pollinating; pedicels ca. 1 cm. Sepals green, narrowly lanceolate, 1.2–1.4 cm. Corolla white; tube curved, ca. 1.3 cm, base inflated; lobes 8–10 mm. Staminodes white; outer staminodes 2, obovate, ca. 1 cm, inner staminodes 1/2 as long as outer ones. Ovary glabrous or pubescent. Capsules green or tinged reddish brown, oblong, 7–8 × 4–5 mm, dehiscent. Seeds brown, rugose; aril basal, white, 2-lobed.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 28063.
Distribution: Widely cultivated elsewhere in tropics; native to tropical America.
Ecology: Flowering: Summer to autumn.
Uses: Ornamental, food (starch).

Maranta bicolor Ker Gawl. 花葉竹芋
Bot. Reg. pl. 786. 1824; FRPS 16(2): 169. 1981; FGD 2: 440. 1991.

Herb compact, 25–40 cm tall, bearing tubers at base. Petioles up to 2.5 cm; pulvinus 5 mm; leaf blade oblong, elliptic or ovate, 7–12 × 5–7 cm, base rounded or cordate, apex round, mucronate, margin ± undulate, glaucous-green and with dark brown spots adaxially. Racemes simple; peduncle 6–10 cm; bracts 2–4, lanceolate, 2.5–3 cm; flower-pairs 3 each bract; sepals 5 mm; corolla white, tube 4 mm, lobes lanceolate, ca. 8 mm; outer 2 staminodes larger, obovate, emarginate, white with violet spots and striped, inner staminode very small.

Locality: Cultivated.
Distribution: Widely cultivated in tropical regions, native to Brazil.
Ecology: Flowering: Summer to autumn.
Uses: Ornamental.

Phrynium placentarium (Lour.) Merr. 尖苞柊葉
Philip. J. Sci. 15: 230. 1919; FHN 4: 105. 1977; FRPS 16(2): 164. 1981; FGD 2: 439. 1991; FOC 24: 380. 2000.
Phyllodes placentaria Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 1: 13. 1790.

Plant ca. 1 m tall. Leaves basal 1(–2); petiole to 30 cm, pulvinus 2–3 cm; leaf blade thinly leathery, oblong-lanceolate or ovate-lanceolate, 30–55 × ca. 20 cm, glabrous, base rounded with an acute centre, apex acuminate. Inflorescence sessile, composed of 4–5 or more spikelets, globose, 3 – 8 m in diam. Bracts crowded, oblong, 2–2.5 cm, apex with a spinescent acumen. Flowers 2 per bract, white to yellowish white. Sepals linear, ca. 5 mm. Corolla tube ca. 8 mm; lobes elliptic, ca. 5 × 2 mm. Outer staminodes obovate, ca. 5 mm. Ovary glabrous or apically puberulent. Fruits oblong, ca. 1.2 cm; exocarp thin. Seed 1, ellipsoidal, ca. 1 cm; aril red.

Locality: Tai Po. L. T. Lo 426; Y. S. Lau 2840.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan; S to SE Asia.
Ecology: Flowering: Feb.–May.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Phrynium rheedei Suresh & Nicolson 柊葉
Taxon 35: 355. 1986; FOC 24: 380. 2000.
Phrynium capitatum Willd., Sp. Pl. 1: 17. 1797, nom. illeg. (included Pontederia ovata); FHN 4: 105. 1977; FRPS 16(2): 162. 1981; FGD 2: 437. 1991.

Plant ca. 1 m tall, with tuberous rhizomes. Basal leaves several, thinly leathery; petiole to 60 cm, pulvinus 3–7 cm; leaf blade ovate-oblong to oblong, 25–50 × 10–12 cm, base acute, apex shortly acuminate, glabrous. Inflorescence sessile, composed of 4–5 or more spikelets, capitate, ca. 5 cm in diam. Bracts crowded, oblong-lanceolate, 2–3 cm, apex initially acute, shredding into fibers after anthesis. Flowers 3 per bract, sessile. Sepals linear, ca. 1 cm, sericeous. Corolla tube violet, shorter than calyx; lobes dark red, oblong-obovate. Outer staminodes light red, obovate, slightly corrugated; cucullate and callose staminodes yellowish, shorter than outer staminodes. Ovary sericeous. Fruit dark red, shining, pyriform, ca. 1 cm, slightly 3-angled; exocarp hard. Seeds 2–3, shallowly grooved.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan. HK sheet 42839.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian; Vietnam, India.
Ecology: Wet and shaded places in forests. Flowering: May–Jul.

Stromanthe sanguinea Sond. 紫背竹芋
Hamburger Garten-Blumenzeitung 5: 225. 1849; FGD 2: 441. 1991.

Perennial herb, ca. 1 m tall, rhizomes creeping, nearly fleshy. Leaves basal and cauline; basal leaves long-petiolate, cauline leaves shortly petiolate or sessile; leaf blade elliptic-oblong, 30–45 × 6–12 cm, base rounded or acute, apex acuminate, dark green and shining adaxially, wine-purple or striped with green abaxially. Panicles with long peduncle, rachis slightly zigzag; bracts cherry-red, ovate, 1.5–3 cm; sepals cherry-red, oblong, 8–9 mm; corolla white, tube 1 mm; lobes lanceolate, 9 mm; 2 outer staminodes linear, subequal, inner staminode broader. Ovary sericeous.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 32243, 32962.
Distribution: Guangdong (cultivated); native to Brazil.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr.–May.
Uses: Ornamental.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Lan Nai Wan, Ham Tin, Sai Kung, Tai Lam Chung, Wu Kau Tang, Yung Shue O, Wang Toi Shan, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Philydrum lanuginosum Banks & Sol. ex Gaertn. 田蔥
Fruct. Sem. Pl. 1: 62, fig. 16. 1788; FHK 380. 1861; FKH 282. 1912; FHN 4: 182. 1977; FRPS 13(3): 144. 1997; FOC 24: 43. 2000; FGD 5: 455. 2003.

Leaves 40–80 cm long (including basal sheath), glabrous, thick, aerenchymatous; sheath 14–30 × 1–1.5 cm. Inflorescence 20–60 cm long; scape slender, terete, glabrate below, villous towards the flowers; bracts ovate to subulate, 2–10 cm × 7.5–10 mm, woolly on abaxial side, short-acuminate to attenuate. Flowers with thin perianth, outer tepals 10–15 × ca. 10 mm, manyveined, long villous outside, the upper with 2 stronger veins and bidentate, acute, margins inflexed, inner tepals spathulate, ca. 8 × 2 mm, membranous, 3-veined, with base hairy outside. Stamen ca. 9 mm long, glabrous, anther ± spherical. Ovary densely longwoolly; style glabrous; stigma broad-triangular, long-papillose. Fruit 9–12 × 4–5 mm. Seeds dark reddish-brown, bulb-shaped, ca. 1 mm long.

Locality: Lan Nai Wan, Ham Tin, Sai Kung, Tai Lam Chung, Wu Kau Tang, Yung Shue O, Wang Toi Shan, Lantau Island. R. M. K. Saunders s.n. (HKU); Y. S. Lau 2071, 1447.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Vietnam, Thailand, Myanmar, Andaman Islands, Malaysia, Australia, New Guinea.
Ecology: Freshwater ponds and marshes at low altitudes. Flowering: Jun.–Jul.; fruiting: Sep.–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Eichhornia crassipes (Mart.) Solms 鳳眼藍
A. DC & C. DC, Monogr. Phan. 4: 527. 1883; FHN 4: 122, fig. 1029. 1977; FFJ 6: 464, fig. 417. 1995; FRPS 13(3): 139, pl. 33. 1997; FOC 24: 41. 2000; FTW ed. 2, 5: 133. 2000; FGD 8: 275, fig. 169. 2007.
Pontederia crassipes Mart., Nov. Gen. Sp. Pl. 1: 9. 1823.
Eichhornia speciosa Kunth, Enum. Pl. 5(4): 131. 1843; FKH 281. 1912.

Aquatic herb, floating, 25–60 cm tall, with long stolons and many black fibrous roots. Stems very short. Leaves radical, rosulate; leaf blade orbicular, broadly ovate, or rhomboidal, 4.5–14.5 × 5–14 cm, leathery, glabrous, densely veined, base shallowly cordate, rounded, or broadly cuneate; petiole 10–40 cm, spongy, usually very much swollen at or below middle. Racemes 7–15-flowered; peduncle 35–45 cm. Perianth segments 6, purplish blue, petaloid, ovate to elliptic, upper one larger, with yellow blotch at centre adaxially, the others subequal but lower one narrower. Stamens 6, 3 long and 3 short; filaments curved, glandular hairy. Pistil heterostylic; stigma glandular hairy. Capsule ovoid.

Locality: Naturalised in Hong Kong. HK sheet 29199.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, S Shaanxi, Hebei, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Shandong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan (naturalized); native to Brazil, now widely introduced and naturalized in tropics and subtropics.
Ecology: Ponds, ditches, streams, paddy fields. Flowering: Jul.–Oct.; fruiting: Aug.–Nov.
Uses: Animal food (forage), noxious weed.

Monochoria hastata (L.) Solms 箭葉雨久花
A. DC & C. DC, Monogr. Phan. 4: 523. 1883; FHN 4: 121. 1977; FFJ 6: 463. 1995; FRPS 13(3): 136, pl. 32: 11. 1997; FOC 24: 41. 2000; FGD 8: 274, fig. 168. 2007.
Pontederia hastata L., Sp. Pl. 1: 288. 1753.
Monochoria hastifolia C. Presl, Reliq. Haenk. 1(2): 128. 1827, nom. illeg. (included Pontederia hastata); FKH 281. 1912.

Perennial aquatic herb, 50–200 cm tall. Stems often long and robust. Leaves radical or alternate on stems; leaf blade triangular or triangular-ovate, 5–15 × 3–15 cm, base sagittate to hastate, apex acute to acuminate; petiole 7–10 cm, broadened and sheathed at base. Racemes 8–18 cm, 10–40-flowered, erect or suberect; peduncle distinctly shorter than associated leaf petiole. Perianth segments bluish with green median vein and reddish blotch, ovate, 1–1.6 cm. Stamens 6, one larger with blue anther (ca. 6 mm), the others smaller, with yellow anthers (ca. 3 mm); style hairy at apex. Capsule oblong, ca. 1 cm.

Locality: Fanling. W. J. Tutcher 9626.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Fujian; Indochina, Malesia, Indian Subcontinent.
Ecology: Ponds, paddy fields. Flowering: Aug.–Mar. of the following year.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Sha Tin, Tai Wan, She Shan Tsuen, Tai Ho
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Monochoria vaginalis (Burm. f.) C. Presl ex Kunth 鴨舌草
Enum. Pl. 4: 134. 1843; FHK 374. 1861; FKH 281. 1912; FHN 4: 121, fig. 1028. 1977; FFJ 6: 463, fig. 416. 1995; FRPS 13(3): 138, pl. 32: 1–6. 1997; FOC 24: 41. 2000; FTW ed. 2, 5: 135, pl. 52. 2000; FGD 8: 275. 2007.
Pontederia vaginalis Burm. f., Fl. Ind. 80. 1768.

Perennial aquatic herb, 12–45 cm tall, with very short rhizomes. Stems usually inconspicuous. Leaves radical or spirally arranged; leaf blade ovate, oblong-ovate to lanceolate, 2 – 6 × 1–4 cm, base subrounded or shallowly cordate, apex acute to acuminate, margin entire; petiole dilated and with a broad sheath at base. Racemes 2.5–5 cm, 2–20-flowered, initially erect, soon reflexed; peduncle 1–3 cm, base bracteate; bract lanceolate. Perianth segments purplish, ovate-lanceolate to oblong, 0.8–1.5 cm. Stamens 6, one larger and longer, the others smaller and shorter; anther 1.8–4 mm in larger stamen, 1.5–3 mm in smaller stamens. Capsule ovoid to ellipsoidal, 0.7–1 cm.

Locality: Sha Tin, Tai Wan, She Shan Tsuen, Tai Ho. P. S. Choi 416; Y. W. Lam 2226; S. C. Ng 1043.
Distribution: Widely spread throughout China; Korea, Japan, Indochina, Malesia, Indian Subcontinent, Africa, Australia.
Ecology: Paddy field, ponds and ditches. Flowering: Aug.–Sep.; fruiting: Sep.–Oct.

Allium chinense G. Don 蕎頭
Mem. Wern. Nat. Hist. Soc. 6: 83. 1827; FRPS 14: 259, pl. 84. 1980; FOC 24: 196. 2000; FGD 5: 448. 2003.

Perennial herb. Bulbs clustered, narrowly ovoid, 1–1.5 cm in diam.; coated with white or reddish tunic. Leaves radical, 2–5, semiterete, fistulose, 25–45 cm × 1–3 mm, obscurely 3–5-angled. Scape lateral, subequalling leaves, terete, covered with leaf sheaths only at base. Involucral bract 2-valved, persistent. Umbel nearly hemispheric, laxly flowered; pedicels subequal, 2–4 times longer than perianth, bracteolate. Perianth pale purple to dull purple; segments 6 in 2 series, outer ones slightly shorter than inner ones, broadly elliptic to suborbicular, 4–6 × 3–4 mm. Stamens 6; filaments equal, about one and a half the length of perianth segments, connate at base and adnate to perianth segments; outer ones subulate; inner ones broadened at base, 1-toothed on each side. Ovary obovoid-globose, with concave nectaries covered by hood-like projections at base; style exserted.

Locality: Cultivated. W. J. Tutcher 11871.
Distribution: Widely cultivated in tropical and subtropical China, Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hunan, Hubei, Henan, Anhui, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian; Indochina, Japan.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Oct.–Nov.
Uses: Food (vegetable).

Allium fistulosum L. 蔥
Sp. Pl. 1: 301. 1753; FRPS 14: 256, pl. 80. 1980; FOC 24: 193. 2000; FGD 5: 449. 2003.

Perennial herb. Bulb cylindrical, solitary or clustered, coated with white or red-brown tunic. Leaves cylindrical, fistulose, 25–50 × 0.5–1 cm, gradually narrowed toward the pointed apex. Scape erect, terete, fistulose, slightly longer than leaves, covered with leaf sheaths for ca. 1/3 its length. Involucral bract 2-valved, persistent. Umbel globose, many-flowered; pedicels subequal, slender, 2–3 times longer than perianth; bracteoles absent. Perianth white; segments 6 in 2 series, outer ones slightly shorter than inner ones, ovate, 4–7 × 2–3 mm, apex acuminate, with a reflexed point. Stamens 6; filaments equal, about 1.5–2 times longer than perianth segments, connate at base and adnate to perianth segments. Ovary obovoid, with inconspicuous nectaries at base; style exserted.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 2679; K. S. Pang 8.
Distribution: Possibly native to W China, but no wild plants have been collected; widely cultivated elsewhere.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Aug.
Uses: Additive (flavoring), food (vegetable).

Allium sativum L. 蒜頭
Sp. Pl. 1: 296. 1753; FRPS 14: 268, pl. 96. 1980; FOC 24: 200. 2000; FGD 5: 449. 2003.

Perennial herb. Bulb solitary, globose to applanate-globose, usually consisting of 6–10 bulbils enclosed in a common tunic; tunic white to purplish, membranous, entire. Leaves broadly linear to linear-lanceolate, flat or keeled abaxially, shorter than scape, to 2.5 cm wide, apex acuminate. Scape 25–60 cm, terete, covered with leaf sheaths for ca. 1/2 its length. Involucral bract united into a tube enclosing the umbel, upward gradually narrowed into a beak of 7–20 cm, deciduous. Umbel with many bulblets and few flowers; pedicels slender, longer than perianth; bracteoles ovate, rather large, membranous, apex acute. Perianth usually pale red; segments 6 in 2 series, outer ones ovate-lanceolate, ca. 4 × 1.4 mm; inner ones ovate, ca. 3 × 1.4 mm. Stamens 6; filaments shorter than perianth segments, connate at base and adnate to perianth segments; outer ones subulate; inner ones broadened at base, 1-toothed on each side, teeth with apex filiform and longer than perianth segments. Ovary globose; style not exserted.

Locality: Cultivated. K. S. Pang 9.
Distribution: Only cultivated, possibly of W Asia origin.
Ecology: Flowering: Jul.
Uses: Additive (flavoring), food (vegetable), medicinal (folklore).

Allium tuberosum Rottler ex Spreng. 韭
Syst. Veg. 2: 38. 1825; FRPS 14: 221, pl. 47. 1980; FOC 24: 179. 2000; FGD 5: 450. 2003.
Allium odorum auct. non L.: FKH 280. 1912.

Perennial herb. Bulbs cylindrical, clustered, coated with yellowish brown tunic. Leaves radical, linear, flat and solid, 15–30 cm × 1.5–8 mm, margin smooth. Scape terete, 20–50 cm, ± 2-angled, covered with leaf sheaths only at base. Involucral bract 2–3-valved, persistent. Umbel hemispheric to subglobose, laxly many-flowered; pedicels subequal, 2–4 times longer than perianth, bracteolate. Perianth white; segments 6 in 2 series, outer ones oblong-ovate to oblong-lanceolate, 4–7 × 1.8–3 mm, inner ones oblong-ovate, 4–7 × 2–3.5 mm. Stamens 6; filaments equal, about 4/5 the length of perianth segments, connate at base and adnate to perianth segments. Ovary obconical-globose, without concave nectaries at base.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 2594.
Distribution: Widely cultivated in China and elsewhere.
Ecology: Flowering & fruiting: May–Oct.
Uses: Additive (flavoring), food (vegetable).

Asparagus cochinchinensis (Lour.) Merr. 天門冬
Fl. Indo-Chine 6: 780. 1908, et Philipp. J. Sci. 15: 230. 1919; FRPS 15: 106, pl. 33: 6 – 7. 1978; FOC 24: 211. 2000; FGD 6: 341, fig. 196. 2005.
Asparagus lucidus Lindl., Edwards's Bot. Reg. 7: 29. 1844; FHK 371. 1861; FKH 278. 1912.
Asparagus sinicus (Miq.) C. H. Wright, J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 36(250): 103. 1903; FKH 278. 1912.
Asparagopsis sinica Miq., J. Bot. Neerl. 1: 90. 1861.
Melanthium cochinchinense Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 1: 216. 1790.

Perennial herb. Roots cord-like, often swollen or with tuberous part at end. Stems straggling or half-climbing, 1–2 m, often woody at base, much branched, with short frequently reflexed prickles under most of the branches. Cladodes usually in fascicles of 3, subfalcate, 0.5–8 cm × 1–2 mm, flat or slightly 3-angled. Flowers small, dioecious, 1–2(–8) in axillary cluster; pedicels 2–6 mm, articulate at middle. Male flowers: perianth segments 6, free, green or greenish white, obovate-oblanceoate, 2–3 mm; stamens 6, adnate to the base of perianth segments, included, anthers ovoid, ca. 0.5 mm; pistillode very small. Female flowers with staminode, ovary ca. 2 mm; style very short. Berry green, 6–7 mm in diam., 1–2-seeded.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. S. P. Lau 145; HK sheet 35876.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Gansu, Shaanxi, Shanxi, Hebei, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Shandong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Korea, Japan, Vietnam, Laos.
Ecology: Margins of forests, roadsides in ravines. Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: Aug.–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Authority: F. T. Wang & K. Y. Lang
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Aspidistra fimbriata F. T. Wang & K. Y. Lang 流蘇蜘蛛抱蛋
Acta Phytotax. Sin. 16(1): 76. 1978; FRPS 15: 22, pl. 7: 1–3. 1978; FOC 24: 245. 2000; FGD 6: 366. 2005.
Aspidistra lurida auct. non Ker Gawl.: FKH 279. 1912.

Perennial herb. Rhizome horizontal, subterete, 5–6 mm thick. Leaves solitary, 3–4 cm spaced; petiole 25–35 cm, stiff; leaf blade oblong-lanceolate, 30–45 × 3.5–6 cm, basally gradually narrowed, apex acuminate, margin entire or sometimes minutely serrulate. Scape 3–10 mm; bracts 4–5. Flower solitary. Perianth campanulate, tube 7–9 mm, 1–1.5 cm in diam., 8–10-lobed apically; lobes ovate-deltoid slightly spreading, 6–8 × 3.5–5 mm, purple speckled abaxially, pink and with 4 fleshy, fimbriate keels adaxially. Stamens 8–10, inserted proximally in perianth tube, subsessile; anthers broadly ovate, ca. 1.8 mm. Pistil ca. 4 mm; stigma purple, peltate, large, ca. 7 mm in diam., 4-lobed at margin, lobes emarginate at apex.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Mount Parker. HK sheet 7600.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian.
Ecology: Forests along ravines. Flowering: Nov.–Dec.
Uses: Ornamental.

Aspidistra lurida Ker Gawl. 九龍盤
Bot. Reg. 8: pl. 628. 1822; FKH 279. 1912; FRPS 15: 19. 1978; FOC 24: 246. 2000; FGD 6: 366. 2005.
Aspidistra elatior auct. non Blume: FKH 279. 1912; Check List HK Plants 125. 2004.
Aspidistra punctata auct. non Lindl.: FKH 279. 1912.

Perennial herb. Rhizome horizontal, terete, to 8 mm thick. Leaves solitary, 1–2 cm spaced; petioles 10–30 cm, stiff; leaf blade narrowly elliptic to oblong-lanceolate, 15–40 × 3–8 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate, margin entire. Scape 1–3 cm, arching; bracts 3–4, broadly ovate, 7–8 mm, dark reddish, membranous. Flower solitary, nodding. Perianth campanulate, 10 – 15 mm, apex 6 – 8-lobed, purplish red abaxially, dark purple adaxially; tube 5–8 mm, 6–10 mm in diam.; lobes ovate-deltoid, spreading, 5–7 mm, with 2–4 papillose keels near the base adaxially. Stamens 6(–8), inserted proximally in perianth tube, subsessile. Pistil equalling perianth tube; ovary speckled with purple; stigma peltate, orbicular, 5–8 mm in diam., strongly convex, inconspicuously 4-lobed at margin, lobes entire at apex.

Locality: Wong Nai Chung Gap. HK sheet 7603, 7604, 24985.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Dec.

Aspidistra minutiflora Stapf 小花蜘蛛抱蛋


J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 36: 113. 1903; FKH 279. 1912; FRPS 15: 22, pl. 8: 5 – 6. 1978; FOC 24: 250. 2000; FGD 6: 365, fig. 218. 2005. Perennial herb. Rhizome horizontal, subterete, 5–6 mm thick. Leaves 2–3-tufted, borne on nodes of rhizome; leaf blade linear, rarely lorate to lorate-oblanceolate, 26–65 × 1–2.5 cm, basally gradually narrowed into inconspicuous petiole, apex acuminate, parallel-veined, midvein distinct, margin entire or distally serrulate. Scape solitary, slender, 1–2.5 cm; bracts 2–4, broadly ovate. Flower solitary, terminal. Perianth urceolate, green, tinged and speckled with purple, 4.5–5 × 4–6 mm, ± fleshy; apex shallowly 4–6-lobed; lobes erect, deltoid, 1–2 × 1–1.5 mm. Stamens (4–)6, inserted at base of perianth tube, subsessile; anthers nearly broadly ovate, ca. 1.5 mm. Ovary 3-locular; style short; stigma orbicular, 1.5–2.5 mm in diam., margin (4–)6-crenate. Berry subglobose, ca. 5 mm in diam.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island. Y. W. Lam 388; HK sheet 30763.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hunan.
Ecology: Moist places on hillsides, cliffs. Flowering: Oct.
Uses: Ornamental.

Aspidistra punctata Lindl. 紫點蜘蛛抱蛋
Bot. Reg. 12. pl. 799. 1826; FOC 24: 243. 2000; FGD 6: 366. 2005.

Perennial herb. Rhizome terete. Leaves solitary; petioles 7.5–50 cm, stiff; leaf blade lanceolate, 25–30 × 4.5–5.5 cm. Scape rather short; bracts ca. 5, dotted with purplish brown spots. Flower solitary, nodding. Perianth campanulate, pale green, dotted with purplish brown spots abaxially, fleshy, 8-lobed apically; lobes ovate, adaxially yellowish green and with 2 fleshy keels; keels dark purple, densely and minutely papillose. Stamens 8, inserted at middle of perianth tube, subsessile, lower than stigma in position; anthers oblong. Ovary with deeply coloured speckles, ovoid, angled; stigma white, orbicular, large, ca. 9 mm in diam., apically with 4 radial, fork-tipped ridges from centre to margin.

Locality: Hong Kong Island. C. P. Lau 97, 100 (CUHK).
Distribution: Guangdong.
Ecology: Forests, streamsides. Flowering: Feb.–Mar.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Cape D'Aguilar, Mount Violet, Tai Tam Tuk, Victoria Peak
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Barnardia japonica (Thunb.) Schult. & Schult. f. 綿棗兒
Syst. Veg. 7: 555. 1829; FOC 24: 203. 2000; FGD 6: 337, fig. 192. 2005.
Scilla chinensis Benth., FHK 373. 1861, nom. illeg. (included B. scilloides Lindl.).
Scilla scilloides (Lindl.) Druce, Rep. Bot. Soc. Exch. Club Brit. Isles. 4: 646. 1917; FRPS 14: 166, fig. 22. 1980; Check List HK Plants 126. 2004.
Barnardia scilloides Lindl., Sketch Veg. Swan R. pl. 1029. 1826.
Ornithogalum japonicum Thunb. Syst. Veg., ed. 14, 328. 1784.

Perennial herb. Bulbs ovoid, 1–3 cm across, covered with blackish brown tunic. Leaves narrow-linear, 15–30 cm × 2–8 mm. Scape erect, longer than leaves. Raceme 5–20 cm, densely flowered; bracts narrowly lanceolate, membranous; pedicels 6–12 mm. Perianth segments rose purple, pink, or white, obovate, elliptic, or narrowly elliptic, 2.5–4 × 1–2 mm, slightly connate and discoid at base. Stamens 2–3.5 mm; filaments sublanceolate, papillose-puberulent or glabrous. Ovary 1.5–2 mm, papillosepuberulent; style 1–1.3 mm. Capsule subobovoid, 3–6 × 2–4 mm. Seeds 1–3, 2.5–5 mm, black.

Locality: Cape D'Aguilar, Mount Violet, Tai Tam Tuk, Victoria Peak. P. S. Choi 51; Y. S. Lau 2335.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan, Shanxi, Henan, Hebei, Nei Mongol, Jilin, Liaoning, Heilongjiang, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Jiangsu, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Korea, E Russia.
Ecology: Hillsides, amongst grass. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Nov.
Uses: Ornamental.

Campylandra wattii C. B. Clarke 彎蕊開口箭
J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 25: 78. 1889; FOC 24: 236. 2000; FGD 6: 346, fig. 201. 2005.
Campylandra cauliflora Chun, Sunyatsenia 1(4): 213–215. 1934.
Tupistra wattii (C. B. Clarke) Hook. f., Fl. Brit. India 6(18): 325. 1892; Check List HK Plants 126. 2004.

Perennial herb. Rhizome elongate, stem-like, ± curved, to 1.2 cm thick. Stem elongate. Leaves spirally arranged on stem, subdistichous; petioles 3–9 cm, basally dilated and amplexicaul; leaf blade ovate-elliptic to narrowly elliptic or elliptic-lanceolate, 8–20 × 3–7 cm, base attenuate, apex acuminate. Spikes 3–6, densely flowered, with several sterile bracts apically; peduncle 1.5–2.5 cm; fertile bracts linear-lanceolate, 1.2–1.8(–5) cm. Perianth tube 3–5 mm; segments red-brown or yellowish green, broadly ovate, 3.5–4 × 2–4 mm, fleshy. Stamens 6; filaments proximally widened and adnate to perianth tube, free part incurved, 1.5–2 mm. Ovary globose; style inconspicuous; stigma 3-lobed. Berry red at maturity, globose, 0.9–1.1 cm in diam.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. Y. W. Lam 166, 433.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Yunnan; Bhutan, India.
Ecology: Shaded and moist places in forests. Flowering: Feb.–May.

Chionographis chinensis K. Krause 白絲草（中國白絲草）
Notizbl. Bot. Gart. Berlin-Dahlem 10: 807. 1929; FRPS 14: 14. 1980; FOC 24: 88. 2000; FGD 6: 344, fig. 198. 2005.

Perennial herb, with short thick rhizome. Leaves radical, rosulate; petioles 1–6 cm; leaf blade ellipitic to ovate-oblong, (1–)3–7 × 1–3 cm, base attenuate, apex acute, margin slightly undulate, glabrous on both surfaces. Scape 14–40 cm, with 4–5 alternate, small, bract-like leaves. Flowers fragrant, in a dense flowered terminal spike. Perianth segments 6, white to pale yellow; upper 3–4 narrowly spatulate, 3–8 × 0.2–0.5 mm; lower 2–3 much smaller, sometimes absent. Stamens 6, unequal, 1–1.5 mm, 3 longer than others; anthers subcordate-ovate, with locules confluent. Capsule ellipsoidal to ± obovoid, ca. 4 × 2 mm, ± 3-angled, dehiscent distally.

Locality: Ma On Shan. Y. W. Lam 217; HK sheet 30333.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Fujian.
Ecology: Forests, other shady and damp places. Flowering: Mar.–May; fruiting: Jun.–Sep.
Notes: The species was reported as Chionographis japonica Maxim. previously (Check List HK Plants 80. 1993).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Chai Wan, Tai Tam Tuk, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Chlorophytum laxum R. Br. 小花吊蘭
Prodr. 277. 1810; FKH 279. 1912; FRPS 14: 45, pl. 10: 4–5. 1980; FOC 24: 206. 2000; FGD 6: 364, fig. 217. 2005.
Anthericum parviflorum (Wight) Benth., FHK 373. 1861.
Phalangium parviflorum Wight, Icon. Pl. Ind. Orient., pl. 2039. 1840.

Perennial herb. Rhizome inconspicuous, with many ± fleshy roots. Leaves sessile, subdistichous, linear, grass-like, 10–20 cm × 3–5 mm, glabrous, 11–15-veined.
