Scape slender, erect or arching, 10–30 cm, simple or sometimes with 1–2 branches. Raceme laxly flowered; bracts narrowly deltoid to lanceolate, very small; pedicels 2–4 mm, lengthening to 5 mm in fruit, articulate proximally. Perianth segments 6, white to greenish white, lanceolate, ca. 3 mm, closely 3-veined. Stamens shorter than perianth segments; anthers subglobose, ca. 0.4 mm. Capsule broadly globose to broadly obcordate, ca. 3 × 5(–7.5) mm; seeds usually 1 per valve.

Locality: Chai Wan, Tai Tam Tuk, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 2590; Y. W. Lam 907.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong; Thailand, Myanmar, India, Sri Lanka, Malaysia, Indonesia, Australia, tropical Africa.
Ecology: Shade and moist places in forests. Flowering & fruiting: Almost all year round.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: Chlorophytum comosum (Thunb.) Jacques, native to S Africa, is cultivated in Hong Kong as an ornamental. It can be easily recognized by its rosulate (not subdistichous) leaves and larger flowers (perianth segments to 1 cm long).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Long Sai Wan, Ham Tin, Tai Wan, Long Ke, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Crinum asiaticum L. var. sinicum (Roxb. ex Herb.) Baker 文殊蘭
Handb. Amaryll. 75. 1888; FHN 4: 145, fig. 1050. 1977; FRPS 16(1): 8, pl. 2: 1–2. 1985; FGD 5: 446, fig. 240. 2003.
Crinum sinicum Roxb. ex Herb., Bot. Mag. 47: 7, sub pl. 2121. 1820.
Crinum asiaticum auct. non L.: FHK 388. 1861.

Stout perennial herb, glabrous throughout. Bulbs narrowly cylindrical, up to 30 cm long and 10–15 cm in diam. Leaves basal, linear-lanceolate, 50–120 × 6–10(–15) cm, apex shortly acuminate, sharply pointed, margin entire, dark green; midvein impressed adaxially, keeled abaxially. Scape solid, 0.6–1 m. Umbel 10–20-flowered; involucres 2, broadly lanceolate, 7–12.5 × 3.5–4.5 cm, green, herbaceous; bracts linear, 7–11 cm × 3–5 mm, membranous. Flowers white, fragrant; pedicels 0.5–2 cm. Perianth salverform; tube greenish white, straight, 6–9 cm; segments linear-lanceolate, 6 –8 cm × 6–10 mm, apex acuminate. Stamens 6, subequal; filament ca. 4 cm, purplish apically; anther linear, 1.5–2 cm. Style filiform, slightly shorter than stamens, declinate. Capsule subglobose, 3–5 cm in diam.

Locality: Tai Long Sai Wan, Ham Tin, Tai Wan, Long Ke, Lantau Island. L. T. Lo 508; Y. S. Lau 2317.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Sandy places near seaside and river banks. Flowering: Jun.–Sep.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal (folklore).
Notes: Crinum latifolium L. is cultivated for ornamental purpose in Hong Kong. It can be easily recognized by its rosepurple and larger flower.

Curculigo capitulata (Lour.) Kuntze 大葉仙茅
Revis. Gen. Pl. 2: 703. 1891; FKH 275. 1912; FRPS 16(1): 34. 1985; FOC 24: 271. 2000; FGD 4: 412, fig. 250. 2000.
Curculigo recurvata W. T. Aiton, FKH 275. 1912.
Leucojum capitulatum Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 1: 199. 1790.

Perennial stout herb, 0.8–1 m tall. Rhizomes tuberous, thick, with creeping, slender stolons. Leaves radical; petioles 30–50(–80) cm, base dilated and clasping the root stock, densely brown pubescent; leaf blade oblong-lanceolate to suboblong, 30–90 × 4–16 cm, apex acuminate, margin entire, veins conspicuous, plicate, adaxially glabrous, abaxially pubescent especially on veins. Scape 6–15(–20) cm, ± compressed, brown villous. Racemes densely flowered, condensed to a head, 2.5–5.5 cm in diam.; bracts lanceolate, 2–6 cm, brown villous on veins and margin; pedicels 8–10 mm, brown villous. Perianth ca. 2 cm, brown villous abaxially; tube ca. 1 cm; segments yellow, elliptic-lanceolate, 8–10 × 3.5–5 mm, apex obtuse. Stamens 6; filament slender, 2–3 mm; anther linear, 4–5 mm. Ovary subglobose to oblong, hairy; style longer than stamens, slender; stigma subcapitate. Berry white, subglobose, 4–5 mm in diam., beakless.

Locality: Mount Parker, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 1696; L. T. Lo 477.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Philippines, Indochina, Myanmar, Thailand, Bhutan, Sikkim, India, Sri Lanka, Indonesia, Papua New Guinea.
Ecology: Forests, moist places in ravines. Flowering: May–Sep.; fruiting: Aug.–Nov.
Uses: Ornamental.

Curculigo orchioides Gaertn. 仙茅
Fruct. Sem. Pl. 1: 63. 1788; FKH 275. 1912; FRPS 16(1): 37. 1985; FOC 24: 272. 2000; FGD 4: 413. 2000.
Curculigo orchioides Gaertn. var. minor Benth., FHK 366. 1861.

Perennial herb, 10–20(–40) cm tall. Rhizomes vertical, subterete, ca. 10 × 1 cm, similar to taproot. Leaves radical, grass-like, sessile or shortly petiolate; leaf blade lanceolate to linear, usually 10–20(–40) × 0.5–2.5 cm, base gradually narrowed, apex narrowly acuminate, laxly pilose or glabrous; veins inconspicuous. Scape short, 6–7 cm, nearly enclosed in base of sheathing petiole, pilose; bracts lanceolate, 2.5–5 cm, margin ciliate. Racemes umbel-like, 4–6-flowered; pedicels ca. 2 mm. Perianth yellow; tube filiform, ca. 18 mm; segments oblong-lanceolate, 8–12 × 2.5–3 mm, outer ones sometimes abaxially laxly pilose. Stamens 6, about half the length of perianth segments; filament 1.5–2.5 mm; anther 2–4 mm. Ovary narrowly oblong, to 7.5 mm, pilose. Stigma lobes longer than style. Berry ± fusiform, ca. 1.5 cm, beaked at apex.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. HK sheet 28455, 32791.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Philippines, Indochina, Thailand, Myanmar, Pakistan, India, Indonesia, Papua New Guinea.
Ecology: Open grassy hillslopes, thin forests. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Sep.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Dianella ensifolia (L.) DC. 山菅（山菅蘭）
Liliac. 1: pl. 1. 1802; FHK 372. 1861; FRPS 14: 35. 1980; FOC 24: 161. 2000; FGD 6: 347, fig. 202. 2005.
Dianella nemorosa Lam., Encycl. 2(1): 276. 1786; FKH 280. 1912.
Dracaena ensifolia L., Mant. Pl. 1: 63. 1767.

Perennial evergreen herb, with creeping rhizomes. Stems erect, 0.7–1.5(–2) m tall, ± compressed. Leaves basal and distichous on the short base of the stem; upper stem-leaves 2–3, much reduced, bract-like; leaf sheath 7–15 cm, conduplicate, basally clasping; leaf blade leathery, linear-lanceolate, 30–70 × 1–3.5 cm, base gradually narrowed into the sheath, apex long acuminate, midvein abaxially and margin scabrous. Inflorescence a laxly branched panicle, 10–40 cm; pedicels 7–12 mm, usually arcuate. Perianth segments 6, spreading, lanceolate to narrowly oblong, 7–8 × 3–4 mm, inner 3 yellowish, outer ones brownish abaxially. Stamens 6, ca. 6 mm, slightly shorter than perianth; filaments ca. 2 mm, distally thickened, yellow and gland-like. Ovary globose; style ca. 6 mm. Berries deep blue, subglobose, 7–10 mm in diam., 3–6-seeded. Seeds ovoid, slightly compressed, ca. 3 × 4.5 mm, black and shining.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 1926.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; tropical Asia, E Australia, Pacific islands, Africa (Madagascar).
Ecology: Grassy places on hillsides. Flowering & fruiting: Mar.–Aug.
Uses: Poisonous.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Disporum uniflorum Baker ex S. Moore 少花萬壽竹
J. Bot. 13: 230. 1875; FOC 24: 157. 2000.
Disporum sessile auct. non D. Don: FKH 281. 1912; FRPS 15: 45, pl. 16: 4. 1978; Check List HK Plants 125. 2004.

Perennial herb, 20–80 cm tall. Rhizome fleshy, shortly creeping, often with stolons. Stems erect, smooth, simple or bifurcately branched on distal part. Leaves alternate; petioles 5 – 10 mm; leaf blade broadly elliptic, oblong-ovate to lanceolate, 4–9 × 1–6.5 cm, base subrounded to broadly cuneate, apex shortly acuminate to acute, glabrous, papillose on margin and veins. Flowers yellow, 1–3(–5) terminal on branches; pedicels 3–5 mm. Perianth segments 6, spatulate-oblanceolate to obovate, 2–3 cm × 5–10 mm, base gibbous-spurred; spurs 1–2 mm. Stamens 6, included; filaments 1.5–2 cm, minutely papillose proximally; anthers 4–8 mm. Ovary 4–5 mm; style 1.5 – 2.3 cm; stigma 3-lobed. Berries blue-black, subglobose, 8–10 mm in diam.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan. P. S. Choi 196; Y. S. Lau 1529.
Distribution: Guangdong, Jiangxi, Hubei, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Hebei, Anhui, Jiangsu, Shandong, Liaoning; Korea.
Ecology: Forests and thickets. Flowering: Mar.–May; fruiting: Jun.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: Disporum cantoniense (Lour.) Merr., distributed in SW to SE China, is also cultivated in Hong Kong as an ornamental. It can be recognized by its creeping rhizome without stolon and slightly opening flowers and purplish tepals.

Hippeastrum vittatum (L'Hér.) Herb. 花朱頂蘭
Appendix 31. 1821; FRPS 16(1): 15. 1985; FGD 5: 445, fig. 238. 2003.
Amaryllis vittata L’Hér., Sert. Angl. 8, pl. 15. 1788.

Perennial herb, glabrous throughout. Bulbs large, globose, to 7.5 cm in diam. Leaves basal, linear to strap-shaped, 30–40 × 2–6 cm, appearing with or after the flowers. Scape erect, hollow, 40–50(–70) cm. Umbel 2–6-flowered; involucres 2, lanceolate, 6 – 8.5 cm, recurved; bracts linear or lanceolate, 4–6.5 cm; pedicels 3.5–5 cm. Perianth funnel-shaped; tube ca. 3 cm, with minute scales at throat; segments obovate-elliptic, 10–15 × 2.5–4 cm, inner ones narrower, apex acute, red with white stripes. Stamens 6, insert in the throat, shorter than perianth segments. Style erect or slightly declinate, with a 3-lobed stigma. Capsule globose, loculicidally 3-valved.

Locality: Cultivated.
Distribution: Widely cultivated in China; native to S America.
Ecology: Flowering: Mar. – Apr.
Uses: Ornamental.

Hymenocallis littoralis (Jacq.) Salisb. 水鬼蕉（蜘蛛蘭）
Trans. Hort. Soc. London 1: 338. 1812; FRPS 16(1): 14. 1985; FGD 5: 446, fig. 239. 2003.
Pancratium littorale Jacq., Select. Stirp. Amer. Hist. 99, t. 179, fig. 94. 1763.
Pancratium biflorum auct. non Roxb.: FHK 367. 1861; FKH 275. 1912.

Perennial herb, stout, bulbiferous, glabrous throughout. Leaves basal, ensiform, to 100 × 7.5 cm, slightly narrowed at base, tapering to apex, dark green, midvein impressed adaxially, keeled abaxially. Scape erect, to 1.5 m, slightly flattened and 2 ridged. Umbel 3–8-flowered; involucres 2, ovate-lanceolate, 5–8 cm, membranous; bracts lanceolate, ca. 4 cm; Flowers sessile, fragrant. Perianth tube slender, 5–13 cm, greenish white; segments white, linear, 6.5–10 × 0.5–0.7 cm, apex acuminate. Staminal cup white, petaloid, to 3 cm high, free parts of filament green, 4–5 cm; anther linear, versatile, ca. 1.8 cm, apex acuminate. Style exceeding stamens; stigma capitate.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 1912.
Distribution: Cultivated in Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; native to Mesoamerica.
Ecology: Flowering: Jun.–Aug.
Uses: Ornamental.

Hypoxis aurea Lour. 小金梅草
Fl. Cochinch. 1: 200. 1790; FGZ 719. 1956; FRPS 16(1): 39. 1985; FOC 24: 273. 2000.

Perennial small herb, yellowish brown pilose throughout. Rhizomes globose to cylindrical, fleshy, covered with fibers. Leaves basal, 4–12, linear, 7–30 cm × 2–6 mm, base membranous, apex narrowly acute. Flowering stems slender, 2.5–10 cm or more, bearing 1–2 flowers; bracts 2, setaceous, small. Perianth yellow; segments oblong, 6–8 mm, persistent. Stamens inserted at the base of perianth lobes; filaments short. Ovary 3–6 mm, pilose. Style short; stigma erect, 3-lobed. Capsule clavate, 6–12 mm, 3-valved. Seeds numerous, subglobose, tuberculate.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. HK sheet 41865, 41874.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Yunnan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Fujian, Taiwan; Bhutan, Cambodia, India, Indonesia, Japan, Korea, Laos, Myanmar, Nepal, Pakistan, Papua New Guinea, Philippines, Thailand, Vietnam.
Ecology: Grassy mountain slopes, alt. ca. 800 m. Flowering: May.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Mount Violet, Kowloon Peak, Shing Mun, Tai Mo Shan, Clear Water Bay, Tsing Yi
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Lilium brownii F. E. Brown ex Miellez 野百合
Cat. Expos. Soc. Hort. Lille. 1841; FKH 280. 1912; FRPS 14: 121, pl. 31: 7. 1980; FOC 24: 147. 2000; FGD 6: 339. 2005.
Lilium longiflorum auct. non Thunb.: FHK 374. 1861; FKH 280. 1912.

Perennial herb. Bulb globose, 3–5 cm in diam.; scales white, lanceolate, 2–4 cm. Stem 0.7–2 m, green or sometimes with purplish strips. Leaves scattered, lower leaves lanceolate to ellipticlanceolate, or obovate, 5–15 × 0.6–2 cm, base gradually narrowed, apex acuminate, 5–7-veined; distal ones gradually becoming smaller, lanceolate or linear. Flowers funnel-shaped, fragrant, solitary or 2–3 on a short peduncle; pedicels 3–10 cm, bent downward; bracts lanceolate, 3–9 × 1–2 cm. Perianth segments 6, oblong-oblanceolate to spatulate, 13–18 × (1–)2–4.3 cm, spreading distally and recurved apically, milk white adaxially, unspotted, with bronzy purple markings abaxially; nectaries papillose on both surfaces. Stamens curved upward; filaments 10–12 cm, densely pilose to glabrous; anthers oblong, 1–1.5 cm. Style 8.5–11 cm. Capsule subcylindrical, 4.5–6 cm.

Locality: Mount Violet, Kowloon Peak, Shing Mun, Tai Mo Shan, Clear Water Bay, Tsing Yi. Y. S. Lau 2497.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Gansu, Shaanxi, Shanxi, Hebei, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian.
Ecology: Hillsides amongst grass. Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: Sep.–Oct.
Uses: Food, medicinal (folklore).
Notes: Lilium longiflorum Thunb. is cultivated for ornamental in Hong Kong. It resembles L. brownii in aspect but may be distinguished by its glabrous filaments and the not papillose nectaries.

Liriope spicata (Thunb.) Lour. 山麥冬（麥門冬）
Fl. Cochinch. 1: 201. 1790; FKH 273. 1912; FRPS 15: 128, pl. 41: 1–2. 1978; FOC 24: 251. 2000; FGD 6: 359. 2005.
Ophiopogon spicatus (Thunb.) Ker Gawl., Bot. Reg. 7: pl. 593. 1821; FHK 371. 1861.
Convallaria spicata Thunb., Syst. Veg., ed. 14, 334. 1784.

Perennial herb, to 50 cm tall, with short rhizomes and creeping stolons; roots usually with fusiform, fleshy tuberous part near tip. Leaves radical, tufted, narrowly linear, grass-like, 20–60 cm × 4–6 mm, distinctly 5-veined, margin serrulate. Scape erect, about the length of leaves or longer. Flowers in clusters of (2–)3–5 in the axil of a scarious bract and surrounded by several smaller bracts, forming a rather dense narrow raceme of 6–18 cm; pedicels ca. 4 mm, articulate above middle or near apex. Perianth purplish or bluish; segments 6, in 2 series, suboblong, 4–5 × 2–2.5 mm. Stamens 6; filaments ca. 2 mm; anthers narrowly oblong, about the length of filaments. Ovary superior; style ca. 2 mm; stigma as wide as style. Seeds subglobose, ca. 5 mm in diam.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. S. P. Lau 82; HK sheet 30224.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Gansu, Shaanxi, Shanxi, Hebei, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Shandong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Korea, Japan, Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests, moist places in ravines. Flowering: May–Jul.; fruiting: Aug.–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.

Narcissus tazetta L. var. chinensis M. Roemer 水仙
Fam. Nat. Syn. Monogr. 4: 223. 1847; FRPS 16(1): 28, pl. 8: 1–2. 1985; FOC 24: 269. 2000; FGD 5: 444, fig. 237. 2003.

Perennial herb, whole plant somewhat glaucous. Bulbs ovoid. Leaves broadly linear, flat, 20–40 × 0.8–1.5 cm, apex obtuse, margin entire. Scape erect, about the length of the leaves. Umbels 4–10-flowered; involucres membranous. Flowers fragrant, spreading or nodding; pedicels unequal, perianth salverform; tube slender, ca. 2 cm, pale green, nearly 3-angled; segments 6, white, widely spreading, broadly elliptic to obovate, ca. 1.5 cm, apex shortly acute; corona pale yellow, shallowly cupular, scarcely half the length of the perianth, margin not undulate. Stamens 6, inserted at upper part of perianth tube; filaments very short. Ovary 3-angled, green, with a slender style and a 3-lobed stigma.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 28331.
Distribution: Fujian, Zhejiang; possibly of Mediterranean origin.
Ecology: Usually the plant is cultivated in water as a pot plant, especially during the Chinese New Year. Flowering: Jan.–Feb.
Uses: Ornamental.

Ophiopogon japonicus (L. f.) Ker Gawl. 麥冬（沿階草）
Bot. Mag. 27: pl. 1063. 1807; FKH 274. 1912; FRPS 15: 163, pl. 55: 3–5. 1978; FOC 24: 261. 2000; FGD 6: 361, fig. 214. 2005.
Convallaria japonica L. f., Suppl. Pl. 204. 1782.

Perennial herb, stoloniferous. Roots cord-like, usually with tuberous part near middle or tip; tubers fusiform, 1–2 × 0.5–1 cm, fleshy. Leaves radical, tufted, sessile, grass-like, generally 15–45 cm × 1.5–3 mm, 3–7-veined, margin serrulate. Scape 6 – 15( – 27) cm, much shorter than leaves. Inflorescence a raceme or reduced panicle, 2–5 cm, several- to more than 10-flowered; bracts lanceolate, basal one 7–8 mm. Flowers solitary or paired, usually nodding; pedicels 3–4 mm, articulate near middle. Perianth segments 6, white or purplish, lanceolate, ca. 5 × 2 mm. Stamens 6; filaments very short; anthers ca. 3 mm. Ovary semi-inferior, style somewhat narrowly conical, ca. 4 mm, narrowed gradually upward from the widened base. Seeds globose, 7–8 mm in diam.

Locality: Lantau Island. W. J. Tutcher 7202.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Hebei, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Shandong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Korea, Japan.
Ecology: Forests, moist and shady places in ravines. Flowering: May–Aug.; fruiting: Aug.–Sep.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Mount Violet, Mount Parker, Tai Mo Shan, Tai Po
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Ophiopogon reversus C. C. Huang 高節沿階草（廣東沿階草）
FHN 4: 534. 1977; FRPS 15: 160. 1978; FOC 24: 260. 2000; FGD 6: 362. 2005.

Perennial herb, without creeping stolons and tuberous roots. Leaves radical, tufted, sessile, long linear, 18–50 cm × 3–8 mm, (5–)7–9-veined, base attenuate, without membranous sheath, margin subentire or serrulate distally. Scape 18–25 cm, slightly flattened and ridged. Inflorescence a raceme or reduced panicle, 5–7 cm, many-flowered; bracts deltoid to ovate, basal one to 2 cm. Flowers in clusters of 2–3 or solitary; pedicels curved, 5–10 mm, articulate above middle. Perianth purple, or white tinged with purple; segments 6, oblong-ovate, ca. 5 × 2 mm, 1-veined. Stamens 6; filaments short; anthers oblong. Style 5–6 mm, slender. Seeds ellipsoidal or globose, purple-blue at maturity.

Locality: Mount Violet, Mount Parker, Tai Mo Shan, Tai Po. G. Barretto 275; HK sheet 36143.
Distribution: Guangxi, Hainan.
Ecology: Moist places in forests. Flowering: Sep.–Oct.; fruiting: Dec.–Mar. of the following year.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Mount Parker, Shek O Rd., Lantau Island, Sunset Peak
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Paris polyphylla Sm. var. chinensis (Franch.) H. Hara 華重樓（重樓）
J. Fac. Sci. Univ. Tokyo, Sect. 3, 10: 176. 1969; FRPS 15: 92. 1978; FOC 24: 91. 2000.
Paris chinensis Franch., Nouv. Arch. Mus. Hist. Nat., ser. 2, 10: 97. 1888.
Paris polyphylla auct. non Sm.: FKH 281. 1912.

Perennial herb, glabrous throughout, 30–100 cm tall, with thick horizontal jointed and scarred rhizome. Leaves 5–10, but usually 7, in a terminal whorl; petiole 0.5–3 cm; leaf blade variable, oblong-lanceolate or obovate-oblanceolate, 5–20 × 2–5 cm, base cuneate, apex acuminate or acute. Flower terminal, solitary; peduncle 1.8–10 cm. Outer perianth segments 5–6, ovate-lanceolate 2–6 × 1–2 cm, leaf-like, green or yellow-green; inner ones linear, usually shorter than outer ones, 1–1.5 mm wide, usually yellow-green. Stamens 8–10, in 2 series; filaments 5–6 mm; anthers 10–12 mm; free portion of connective 0.5–1.5 mm. Ovary subglobose, ribbed, 1-locular, sometimes tuberculate; style short, base enlarged, purple to white; stigma lobes (4–)5. Capsule globose, sometimes tuberculate. Seeds enveloped by red, succulent aril.

Locality: Mount Parker, Shek O Rd., Lantau Island, Sunset Peak. Y. S. Lau 2126.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam, Laos, Thailand, Myanmar.
Ecology: Forests, ravines in humus soil. Flowering: May–Jul.; fruiting: Aug.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Peliosanthes macrostegia Hance 大蓋球子草
J. Bot. 23: 328. 1885; FKH 273. 1912; FRPS 15: 167, pl. 56: 1–2. 1978; FOC 24: 263. 2000; FGD 6: 357, fig. 212. 2005.

Perennial herb, with short rhizomes and thick roots. Leaves 2–5, basal; petiole 7–30 cm; leaf blade lanceolate-oblong, 14–27 × 3–6 cm, base attenuate, apex acuminate or acute, with 5–9 parallel veins, netted veins conspicuous. Scape 15–29 cm. Inflorescence a raceme, 10–22 cm, rachis purplish when dry; bracts ovate-lanceolate, 6–15 mm, membranous. Flowers solitary; pedicels 2–5 mm, articulate near apex; bracteole 1, 3–5 mm. Perianth purple; tube ca. 2 mm, basally adnate to ovary; segments 6, ovate-oblong, 4–5 mm. Stamens 6; filaments connate into a fleshy ring; anthers ca. 1 mm. Ovary 3-locular; style short; stigma 3-lobed. Seeds subglobose, ca. 1 cm, berry-like.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. Y. S. Lau 1726; HK sheet 30161.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, SE Yunnan, NE Sichuan, Hunan, Taiwan.
Ecology: Forests, thickets, shady and humid rocky places. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.; fruiting: Jul.–Sep.

Thysanotus chinensis Benth. 異蕊草
FHK 372. 1861; FKH 280. 1912; FRPS 14: 48. 1980; FOC 24: 203. 2000; FGD 6: 356, fig. 211. 2005.

Perennial herb, with short rhizome and fibrous roots. Leaves radical, tufted, linear-subulate, erect and stiff, 13–20 cm × 1–1.5 mm, glabrous. Scape erect, slender, as long as or slightly longer than leaves, bearing a terminal umbel. Umbel 4–10-flowered; bracts ovate or lanceolate, 3–5 mm, membranous and scale-like; pedicels 1–1.5 cm, articulate near base, recurved after flowering. Perianth blue; segments 6, suboblong, 7–8 × 1–2 mm, membranous, 3–5-veined; inner ones sometimes fimbriate-denticulate at margin proximally. Stamens 6, 4–5 mm; outer anthers ca. 1.2 mm, inner ones ca. 2.2 mm. Capsule ellipsoidal, ca. 4 × 3 mm, 1–2-seeded.

Locality: Aberdeen, Fanling, So Kwun Wat. Y. W. Lam 1725; HK sheet 38434.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; Philippines, Vietnam, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia, Australia.
Ecology: Thin forests, grassy hillslopes. Flowering & fruiting: May–Dec.

Tulipa gesneriana L. 鬱金香
Sp. Pl. 1: 306. 1753; FRPS 14: 90. 1980; FGD 6: 338, fig. 194. 2005.

Perennial herb. Bulbs ovoid, slightly tapering upward, ca. 2 cm in diam.; tunic thin, papery, with a few appressed hairs near base and summit. Stem erect, 20–40 cm. Leaves 3–5, alternate, linear-lanceolate to ovate-lanceolate, 10–21 × 1–6 cm, sessile and clasping at base, fringed with a few short hairs near apex. Flowers large, solitary and terminal, variously coloured, ranging from white to yellow, pink to purple. Perianth segments 6, free, outer 3 elliptic to lanceolate, 5–7 × 2–4 cm, inner ones shorter and broader, obovate. Stamens 6, equal; filaments glabrous, dilated below middle; anthers basifixed. Style obsolete; stigma 3-lobed, lobes thickened. Capsule loculicidally 3-valved.

Locality: Cultivated. K. S. Pang 11.
Distribution: Cultivated in China and elsewhere; possibly originated from SW or S Asia.
Ecology: Flowering: Spring.
Uses: Ornamental.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Mount Parker, Tai Mo Shan, Sunset Peak, Lantau Peak
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Veratrum schindleri Loes. 牯嶺藜蘆
Verh. Bot. Vereins Prov. Brandenburg. 68: 139. 1926; FRPS 14: 28. 1980; FOC 24: 84. 2000; FGD 6: 347, fig. 203. 2005.
Veratrum nigrum auct. non L.: FKH 281. 1912.
Veratrum japonicum auct. non Loes.: FRPS 14: 28. 1980; Check List HK Plants 126. 2004.

Perennial herb. Stem simple, erect, to 1 m tall, clothed with brown, reticulate fibers of disintegrated leaf sheaths. Leaves basal and alternate on stem; petioles of basal leaves rather long and tightly enclosing the stem; stem leaves with a short, clasping petiole; leaf blade broadly elliptic to lorate, 15–30 × 2–6(–10) cm, gradually reduce in size upward glabrous, base cuneate, apex acute to acuminate, strongly plicately veined. Panicle variable in length, laxly many-flowered; branches spreading; rachis and pedicels greywhite woolly; bracts ovate-lanceolate, 5–7 mm, abaxially woolly; pedicels 6–8(–14) mm. Perianth segments 6, yellowish green, greenish white or brownish, subelliptic, oblong, oblong-lanceolate, or obovate-elliptic, 5–8 × 2–3 mm, base not clawed, apex obtuse or subacute; outer segments pubescent at least at abaxial base. Stamens 6, 2–5 mm, inserted at the base of perianth segments. Ovary glabrous. Capsule erect, 1–2 × ca. 1 cm. Seeds black, flattened, narrowly winged.

Locality: Mount Parker, Tai Mo Shan, Sunset Peak, Lantau Peak. H. C. Tang 2418; Y. S. Lau 2605.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Hubei, Henan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian.
Ecology: Shaded and moist places in forests and ravines. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Zephyranthes candida (Lindl.) Herb. 蔥蓮（玉簾）
Bot. Mag. 53: pl. 2607. 1826; FGZ 701. 1956; FRPS 16(1): 5, pl. 1: 3. 1985; FOC 24: 265. 2000; FGD 5: 440. 2003
Amaryllis candida Lindl., Bot. Reg. 9: pl. 724. 1823.

Perennial herb, glabrous throughout. Bulbs ovoid, 2–3 cm in diam. Leaves all basal, linear, 15–38 × 3–4 mm, adaxial surface ± concave, abaxial surface convex. Scape slender, erect, 18 – 25 cm, fistulose. Flowers solitary and terminal; involucre 1, spathiform, ca. 2.3 cm, membranous, basically united into a tube, upper part splitting on one side; pedicels ca. 1.5 cm. Perianth tube very short, 2–3 mm; segments 6, white, but green at base, outer 3 larger, obovate-elliptic, 3–3.5 × 1.3–1.6 cm, inner 3 narrower. Stamens 6, 7–9 mm, green; anthers linear, 7–8 mm. Style slender, slightly longer than stamens; stigma 3-notched. Capsule subglobose.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 1956; HK sheet 28341.
Distribution: Widely cultivated in China; native to S America.
Ecology: Flowering: Jul.–Sep.
Uses: Ornamental.

Zephyranthes carinata Herb. 韭蓮（風雨花）
Bot. Mag. 52: t. 2594. 1825; FOC 24: 265. 2000; FGD 5: 441, fig. 233. 2003.
Zephyranthes grandiflora Lindl., Bot. Reg. 11: pl. 902. 1825; FGZ 701. 1956; FRPS 16(1): 7, pl. 1: 4–5. 1985; Check List HK Plants 126. 2004.

Perennial herb, glabrous throughout. Bulbs ovoid, 2–3 cm in diam. Leaves all basal, linear, 15–35(–40) × 6–8 mm, nearly flat, midvein raised abaxially. Scape slender, erect, 18–25 cm, fistulose. Flowers solitary and terminal; involucre 1, spathiform, 3–4 cm, membranous, basically united into a tube, upper part splitting on one side; pedicels ca. 2.5–3.5 cm. Perianth tube 2–2.5 cm, green; segments elliptic, 5–6 × 1.8–2.5 cm, rose to pink. Stamens 6, subequal, ca. 2.3 cm; anthers linear, ca. 1.8 cm, versatile. Style slender, longer than stamens, with a 3–4-lobed stigma. Capsule subglobse.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 28336, 32971.
Distribution: Widely cultivated in China; native to S America.
Ecology: Flowering: Jul.–Sep.
Uses: Ornamental.

Belamcanda chinensis (L.) DC. 射干
Liliac. 3: t. 121. 1805; FHK 365. 1861; FKH 274. 1912; FRPS 16(1): 131, pl. 42: 1–5. 1985; FOC 24: 312. 2000; FGD 6: 381, fig. 226. 2005.
Ixia chinensis L., Sp. Pl. 1: 36. 1753.
Belamcanda chinensis (L.) DC. var. taiwanensis S. S. Ying, Coloured Illustr. Pl. Taiwan 1: 273. 1980.
Belamcanda pampaninii H. Lév., Repert. Spec. Nov. Regni Veg. 8(160–162): 59–60. 1910.
Belamcanda punctata Moench, Methodus 529. 1794.
Pardanthus chinensis (L.) Ker Gawl., Ann. Bot. (König & Sims) 1: 246. 1805.

Rhizome yellow or pale brown. Stems 1–1.5 m. Leaves 20–60 × 2–4 cm, apex acuminate, midvein obscure. Flowers reddish orange with dark spots, 3–4 cm in diam.; pedicel slender, ca. 1.5 cm. Bracts lanceolate or ovate, membranous; outer perianth segments obovate or elliptic, ca. 2.5 × 1 cm, base cuneate, apex obtuse or emarginate; inner ones slightly narrower and shorter. Stamens 1.8–2 cm, filaments subterete, slightly broader at base, anthers linear, extrorse. Style 3-lobed at apex, lobes spreading. Capsule 2.5–3 × 1.5–2.5 cm, apex not beaked. Seeds ca. 5 mm in diam.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 7409, 28298.
Distribution: All over China except NW part; SE Asia and Russia.
Ecology: Flowering: Jun.–Aug.; fruiting: Jul.–Sep.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Gladiolus × gandavensis Van Houtte 唐菖蒲（劍蘭）
Fl. Serres Jard. Eur. pl. 1. 1846; FGZ 706, fig. 370. 1956; FRPS 16(1): 124, pl. 39: 7–8. 1985; FGD 6: 386, fig. 231. 2005.

Perennial herb; bulbs compressed globose, 2.5–4.5 cm in diam., with brown or yellowish brown membranes. Leaves basal or alternate at the basal part of scapes, sword-shaped, 40–60 × 2–4 cm, base sheathing, apex acuminate, greyish green. Scapes erect, 50–80 cm, unbranched, with several basal leaves. Spikes terminal, 25–35 cm, bracts usually 2 below each flower, membranous, yellowish green, ovate or broadly lanceolate, 4–5 × 1.8–3 cm, midveins conspicuous. Flowers solitary in each bract, red, yellow or pink, etc., 6–8 cm in diam.; tube ca. 2.5 cm, curved at base; perianth segments ovate or elliptic, unequal, upper 3 (2 in outer whorl, 1 in inner whorl) slightly larger, the upper one of inner whorl much broader and larger, helmet-shaped; stamens 3, erect, adnate to the helmet-like inner segment, ca. 5.5 cm, anthers linear, reddish purple or dark purple, filaments white. Ovary ellipsoidal, green, style ca. 6 cm, apex 3-lobed, stigmas slightly enlarged, flat, tomentose.

Locality: Cultivated. K. S. Pang 12.
Distribution: Widely cultivated all over the world.
Ecology: Flowering: Jul.–Sep.; fruiting: Aug.–Dec. Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: This species is a hybrid. Perhaps G. psittacinus Hook. and G. cardinalis Curtis are its parents. It is widely cultivated as a cutting-flower.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Cape D'Aguilar, Tai Tam, Sunset Peak, Po Toi Islands
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Iris speculatrix Hance 小花鳶尾
J. Bot. 13: 196. 1875; FKH 274. 1912; FRPS 16(1): 174, pl. 56: 1–4. 1985; FOC 24: 309. 2000; FGD 6: 383, fig. 227. 2005.
Iris cavaleriei H. Lév., Liliac. & Chine 18. 1905.
Iris grijsii Maxim., Bull. Acad. Imp. Sci. Saint-Petersbourg 26: 527. 1880.

Rhizomes creeping. Roots thick. Leaves slightly curved, dark green, glossy, linear, 15–30 × 0.6–1.2 cm, veins 3 – 5. Flowering stems 20–25 cm, 1–2-leaved; spathes 2 – 3, green, lanceolate, 5.5–8 cm, 1–2-flowered, apex acuminate. Flowers violet or light blue, 5.6–6 cm in diam.; pedicel 3–7 cm. Perianth tube ca. 5 mm; outer segments spreading, spatulate, with a central, dark circular patch, 3–4 cm, crest yellow; inner segments erect, narrowly oblanceolate, 3–3.7 cm. Stamens ca. 1.2 cm; anthers white. Ovary fusiform, 1.6–2 cm. Style branches ca. 2.5 cm × 7 mm. Capsule ellipsoidal, ca. 5–5.5 cm, apex long beaked. Seeds dark brown, angled, with aril drying as a pale brown wing.

Locality: Cape D'Aguilar, Tai Tam, Sunset Peak, Po Toi Islands. Y. S. Lau 2564; P. S. Choi 351, 459.
Distribution: Guangdong, Hainan, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hubei, Hunan, Anhui, Jiangxi, Fujian, Zhejiang, Jiangsu, Qinghai, Shaanxi, Shanxi, Sichuan, Xizang, Yunnan.
Ecology: Forests, moist grasslands. Flowering: May; fruiting: Jul. – Aug. Uses: Ornamental (flowers).
Notes: The type specimen was collected by H. F. Hance (Herb. No. 18465, BM) from Victoria Peak and Mount Davis in April 1874. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Aloe vera (L.) Burm. f. 蘆薈
Fl. Indica 83. 1768; FOC 24: 160. 2000; FGD 6: 355, fig. 210. 2005.
Aloe perfoliata L. var. vera L., Sp. Pl. 1: 320. 1753.
Aloe barbadensis Mill. var. chinensis Haw., Supp. Pl. Succ. 45. 1819.
Aloe chinensis (Haw.) Baker, Bot. Mag. pl. 6301. 1877.
Aloe vera (L.) Burm. f. var. chinensis (Haw.) A. Berger, Pflanzenr. 33(IV, 38, 3): 230. 1908; FRPS 14: 62, fig. 8. 1980; Check List HK Plants 365. 2002; 127. 2004.

A succulent herb. Stems short, suckering freely to form dense clumps. Leaves nearly basal, pale green, sometimes with pale spots in very young plants, linear-lanceolate, 15–35(–50) × 4–5(–7) cm, apex 2–3-dentate-pointed, margin sparsely spiny-dentate. Inflorescence erect, 60–90 cm; peduncle to 2 cm thick; raceme 30–40 cm, sometimes with 1–2 branches, many-flowered; bracts whitish, broadly lanceolate, ca. 1 cm, veins 5–7, apex acute. Flowers reflexed; pedicel nearly half as long as bract. Perianth pale yellow mottled with red, slightly ventricose, 2.5(–3) cm, outer lobes slightly recurved at apex. Style conspicuously exserted.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 28788, 28789.
Distribution: Widely cultivated in S and SW China; probably originated in Mediterranean region, widely cultivated and occasionally naturalized in tropical and subtropical regions.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal (folklore).

Agave americana L. 龍舌蘭
Sp. Pl. 1: 323. 1753; FHN 4: 157. 1977; FTW 5: 87. 1978; FRPS 16(1): 31. 1985; FTW ed. 2, 5: 75. 2000; FOC 24: 271. 2000; FGD 9: 219. 2009.

Stems indistinct. Leaves usually 30–40 or more, in a basal rosette, oblanceolate, 1–2 m × 15–20 cm, fleshy, apex recurved and tipped with a dark brown spine 1.5–2.5 cm, margin sparsely spiny, glaucous adaxially. Panicle large, many-branched, 6–12 m. Perianth greenish yellow, segments sometimes with 1 green stripe; tube ca. 1.2 cm; lobes 2.5–3 cm. Stamens ca. twice as long as perianth. Capsule ellipsoidal, ca. 5 cm.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 28381.
Distribution: Widely cultivated in S and SW China, naturalized in some regions of S China; native to tropical America.
Uses: Material (fibre), ornamental.

Cordyline fruticosa (L.) A. Chev. 朱蕉
Cat. Pl. Jard. Bot. Saigon. 66. 1919; FRPS 14: 273, pl. 51: 2. 1980; FOC 24: 204. 2000; FGD 9: 212, fig. 121. 2009.
Convallaria fruticosa L., Herb. Amb. 16. 1754.
Asparagus terminalis L., Sp. Pl. (ed. 2) 1: 450. 1762, nom. illeg. superfl.(included Convallaria fruticosa L. 1754).
Dracaena terminalis L., Syst. Nat. (ed. 12) 12: 246. 1767.
Cordyline terminalis (L.) Kunth, Abh. Königl. Akad. Wiss. Berlin 30. 1820; FTW ed. 2, 5: 76. 2000.
Aletris chinensis Lam., Encycl. 1: 79. 1873.

Erect shrubby plant, 1–3 m. Stems simple or sometimes branched. Leaves petiolate; petiole 10–30 cm, sulcate adaxially; leaf blade green or variously coloured, oblong-lanceolate to narrowly oblong, 25 – 50 × 5–10 cm, midvein distinct and raised abaxially, base amplexicaul, apex aristate. Panicle 30–60 cm; branches many, spreading, 6–13 cm, many-flowered. Flowers subsessile or shortly pedicellate; bracteoles 3, ovate, 2–3 mm, apex cuspidate, margin broadly membranous. Perianth reddish, yellowish, or bluish purple; tube 5–6 mm; lobes erect or recurved, nearly as long as tube. Stamens inserted in throat of perianth, slightly shorter than perianth. Fruit reddish, several-seeded.

Locality: Cultivated.
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan; probably native to Pacific islands but cultivated pantropically.
Ecology: Flowering: Nov.–Mar. of the following year.
Uses: Ornamental.

Dracaena fragrans (L.) Ker Gawl. 巴西鐵樹
Bot. Mag. 27: pl. 1081. 1808; FTW ed. 2, 5: 77. 2000; FGD 9: 213. 2009.
Aletris fragrans L., Sp. Pl. (ed. 2) 456. 1762.

Arborescent or shrubby plant, to 6 m. Stem erect, simple or rarely branched at apex, greyish brown, smooth, with circular leaf scars when young. Leaves crowded at apex of stem and branches, oblong-lanceolate, 30–90 × 6–9 cm, apex acute, margin ± wavy, green or with white or yellow stripes, midveins raised on both surfaces. Panicles erect, 30–60 cm. Bracts acute, scarious; pedicels 7–21 cm. Flowers small, pale yellow, fragrant. Perianth campanulate, 1–2 cm, lobes ± reflexed. Ovary sessile. Berries globose, red.

Locality: Cultivated.
Distribution: Widely cultivated in tropical and subtropical regions, native to Africa.
Uses: Ornamental.

Sansevieria trifasciata Prain 虎尾蘭
Beng. Pl. 2: 1054. 1903; FGZ 709. 1956; FRPS 14: 278, pl. 51: 1. 1980; FGD 9: 215, fig. 123. 2009.

Leaves basal, often 1–2, sometimes 3–6, erect, thickly leathery, flat, linear-lanceolate, 30–70(–120) × 3–5(–8) cm, with transverse green stripes, margin green, gradually attenuate toward base and forming sulcate petiole. Inflorescence 30 – 80 cm, with pale brown membranous sheath at base. Flowers pale green or white, 3 – 8 in clusters, arranged in racemes; pedicel 5–8 mm, articulate in middle; perianth 1.6–2.8 cm, tube nearly as long as lobes. Berries 7–8 mm in diam.

Locality: Cultivated. HK sheet 28222, 38594.
Distribution: Widely cultivated in China; native to W Africa.
Ecology: Flowering: Nov.–Dec.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: This species is widely cultivated in parks and gardens of Hong Kong.

Schizocapsa plantaginea Hance 裂果薯
J. Bot. 19: 292. 1881; FKH 275. 1912; FRPS 16(1): 50, pl. 12: 1 – 7. 1985; FOC 24: 275. 2000; FGD 9: 223, fig. 129. 2009.
Tacca plantaginea (Hance) Drenth, Blumea 20(2): 391. 1972.

Plant 20 – 30 cm tall. Rhizomes thick and short, often curved. Petiole (5–)–11(–16) cm, winged; leaf blade narrowly elliptic to narrowly elliptic-lanceolate, 10–15(–25) × 4 6(–8) cm, base decurrent, apex acuminate. Scape 6 – 13 cm; involucral bracts ovate to deltoid-ovate, 1–2 cm; umbel 8 – 15(–20)-flowered. Perianth light or dark green or light purple; lobes pointed at apex, outer lobes lanceolate, inner ones ovate, slightly shorter and wider than outer ones. Filaments extremely short, apical hood projected downward into 2 auricles. Stigma 3-lobed, lobes bifid. Capsule obovoid, 6–8 mm, 3-valved; valves splitting to base. Seeds semilunar, oblong or irregularly so, striate.

Locality: Repulse Bay, Lady Clementi's Ride. H. C. Tang 1974; Y. S. Lau 642.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, S Hunan, S Jiangxi, Yunnan; Laos, Thailand, Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests, along rivers, valleys. Flowering & fruiting: Apr.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Stemona tuberosa Lour. 大百部（百部）
Fl. Cochinch. 2: 404. 1790; FKH 276. 1912; FHN 4: 147, fig. 1053. 1977; FTW 5: 85, pl. 1287. 1978; FRPS 13(3): 256, pl. 62: 4–6. 1997; FOC 24: 71. 2000; FGD 9: 208. 2009.
Stemona acuta C. H. Wright, J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 32: 493. 1889; FKH 276. 1912.

Perennial twining herb, thoroughly glabrous. Tubers terete or fusiform, 15–30 cm. Stems often branched, base woody. Leaves opposite, rarely whorled or alternate; petiole slender, 3.5–7.5 cm; leaf blade ovate to ovate-lanceolate, 10–15 × 5–10 cm, membranous, base cordate, apex acuminate, margin slightly undulate, basal veins 7–13. Inflorescence racemose, 1–3-flowered; peduncle or pedicel axillary or rarely borne on petiole, 0.5–1.5 cm; bracts lanceolate, 0.5–1 cm. Perianth segments greenish with purplish veins, lanceolate, 4–6 × 1.5 cm. Stamens purple, slightly shorter than perianth; filaments stout, 2–5 mm; anthers linear, ca. 1 cm; appendages partially adherent. Capsule ovoid-ellipsoidal, 4–5 cm. Seeds several, ellipsoidal, ca. 7 mm.

Locality: Mount Parker, Plover Cove. Y. W. Lam 1759; HK sheet 7548.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; Bangladesh, Cambodia, NE India, Laos, Myanmar, Philippines, Thailand, Vietnam.
Ecology: Margins of forests, thickets, mountain slopes. Flowering: Apr.–Jul.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Heterosmilax gaudichaudiana (Kunth) Maxim. 合絲肖菝葜
Bull. Acad. Imp. Sci. Saint-Pétersbourg. 17: 176. 1872; FHK 370. 1861; FKH 277. 1912; FHN 4: 127, fig. 1031. 1977; FOC 24: 117. 2000; FGD 6: 377. 2005.
Smilax gaudichaudiana Kunth, Enum. Pl. 5: 252. 1850.
Heterosmilax gaudichaudiana (Kunth) Maxim. var. hongkongensis (Seem.) A. DC., Monogr. Phan. 1: 45. 1878.
Heterosmilax gaudichaudiana (Kunth) Maxim. var. latifolia Bodinier ex H. Lév., Liliac. etc. Chine 22. 1905.
Heterosmilax japonica Kunth var. gaudichaudiana (Kunth) F. T. Wang & T. Tang, FRPS 15: 244. 1978; Check List HK Plants 367. 2002; 128. 2004.
Oligosmilax gaudichaudiana (Kunth) Seem., J. Bot. 6(68): 258, pl. 83. 1868.
Smilax hongkongensis Seem., Bot. Voy. Herald 420. 1857.

Climbing vine. Stems woody, 3–6 m, glabrous. Petiole 1–2.5 cm, narrowly winged at lower part; tendrils well developed; leaf blade broadly ovate to orbicular, 5–15 × 2–8 cm, base truncate, rounded or cordate, apex long acuminate, 5–7(–9)-veined. Peduncle 1–3.5(–9) cm, slightly flat. Umbels often 20–40-flowered; pedicels slender, 0.5–1.5 cm. Male flowers: perianth tube red-purple, ovoid-ellipsoidal, 4–7 mm, teeth 3, deltoid; stamens 3, 3–4 mm; filaments nearly connate for its full length and forming a column; anthers ovoid, 0.5–0.7 mm. Female flowers slightly shorter than male ones, staminodes 3. Ovary ovoid. Berries purplish red, compressed globose, 6–9 mm in diam.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 2197; Y. S. Lau 324, 2592.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian; Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests and hillsides. Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: Jul.–Dec.
Notes: The syntypes (Hance s.n., Seemann s.n.) of Smilax hongkongensis Seem. were collected from Hong Kong Island in 1850s.

Heterosmilax japonica Kunth 肖菝葜
Enum. Pl. 5: 270. 1850; FTW 5: 137. 1978; FRPS 15: 242, pl. 80: 1–3. 1978; FTW ed. 2, 5: 100, pl. 32. 2000; FOC 24: 117. 2000; FGD 6: 377, fig. 224. 2005.

Climbing vine, glabrous. Stem woody, branches slightly ridged. Petiole 1–3 cm, narrowly winged at lower 1/4–1/3; tendrils well developed; leaf blade papery, ovate, ovate-lanceolate to nearly heart-shaped, 6–20 × 2.5–12 cm, base subcordate, apex acuminate, mucronate, main veins 5–7. Umbels borne in axil of leaf or scalelike bract, 20–50-flowered; peduncle 1–3 cm, ± flat; pedicels slender, 2–7 mm. Male flowers: perianth ellipsoidal or narrowly obovoid, 3.5–4.5 mm; stamens 3, as long as 2/3 of perianth; filaments connate at lower half, forming a column. Female flowers: perianth ovoid, 2.5–3 mm; stigmas erect; staminodes 3. Berries globose, slightly compressed, black, 6–10 mm in diam.

Locality: Pok Fu Lam. HK sheet 10539.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Gansu, Anhui, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Zhejiang, Taiwan; Bhutan, India, Japan.
Ecology: Thickets. Flowering: Jun.–Aug.; fruiting: Jul.–Nov.

Smilax china L. 菝葜
Sp. Pl. 2: 1029. 1753; FKH 278. 1912; FGZ 685. 1956; FHN 4: 125. 1977; FTW 5: 117. 1978; FRPS 15: 193, pl. 63: 1–3. 1978; FTW ed. 2, 5: 106. 2000; FOC 24: 101. 2000; FGD 6: 374, fig. 222. 2005.
Coprosmanthus japonicus Kunth, Enum. Pl. 5: 268. 1850.
Smilax japonica A. Gray, Mem. Amer. Acad. Arts, n.s. 6(2): 412. 1858, nom. illeg. superfl.
Smilax china L. var. taiheiensis (Hayata) T. Koyama, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 10: 9. 1957.
Smilax pteropus Miq., J. Bot. Neerl. 1: 89. 1861.
Smilax taiheiensis Hayata, Icon. Pl. Formosan. 9: 134. 1920.
Smilax ferox auct. non Wall. ex Kunth: FHK 370. 1861.

Deciduous climbing vine. Rhizomes rigid, thick, irregular, 2–3 cm in thickness. Stem branched, terete, 1–5 m, woody, sparsely prickly. Petiole 0.5–1.5 cm, narrowly winged at lower 1/2–2/3 of its length, abscission zone just above winged portion, tendrils often present; leaf blade leathery to thickly papery, ovate to orbicular, 3–10 × 2–9 cm, base acute to cordate, apex acute, rounded to emarginate, pale green to glaucous abaxially, main veins 5–7. Umbels axillary, solitary, 10–25-flowered, not prophyllate at base; peduncle 1–2 cm; bracteoles many, small, ovate-lanceolate. Male flowers: tepals yellowish green, 4–5 mm; stamens 3–4 mm; filaments filiform. Female flowers: staminodes 6, linear. Berries globose, red, 0.6–1.5 cm in diam., minutely white powdery.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. W. J. Tutcher 11649; H. C. Tang 389; HK sheet 41500.
Distribution: Areas S of Changjiang; Myanmar, Philippines, Thailand, Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests and thickets. Flowering: Feb.–May; fruiting: Sep.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Smilax cocculoides Warb. 銀葉菝葜
Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 29: 257. 1900; FRPS 15: 228, pl. 74: 1–4. 1978; FOC 24: 112. 2000; FGD 6: 373. 2005.

Subscandent shrub, unarmed. Stem suberect, branched, 0.5–2 m, woody, inconspicuously ridged. Petiole usually curved, 0.5–1 cm, narrowly winged at base, wings sometimes auriculate apically, abscission zone at middle, tendrils absent; leaf blade thickly papery to subleathery, elliptic-ovate or ovate-lanceolate, 5–12 × 2.5–4 cm, base broadly cuneate, apex long acuminate, abaxially pale green, slightly shiny, midvein slightly impressed adaxially. Umbels solitary, rarely paired, 3–15-flowered; peduncle 1–2 cm, prophyllate at base. Male flowers: tepals yellowish green, outer ones 2.5–3.5 × 1–1.5 mm, inner ones narrower; stamens very short. Berries globose, ca. 8 mm in diam., bluish black when matured.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Sunset Peak. Y. W. Lam 167, 1292.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan.
Ecology: Forests, thickets. Flowering: Feb.–Apr.; fruiting: Nov.
Notes: The species was reported as Smilax astrosperma F. T. Wang & Tang previously (Check List HK Plants 367. 2002; 128. 2004).

Smilax glabra Roxb. 土茯苓（光葉菝葜）
Fl. Ind. ed. 1832, 3: 792. 1832; FHK 369. 1861; FKH 278. 1912; FGZ 685. 1956; FHN 4: 125, fig. 1030. 1977; FTW 5: 130. 1978; FRPS 15: 212, pl. 69. 1978; FOC 24: 108. 2000; FGD 6: 373. 2005.
Smilax blinii H. Lév., Fl. Kouy-Tchéou 256. 1914.
Smilax dunniana H. Lév., Repert. Spec. Nov. Regni Veg. 9(222–226): 446. 1911.
Smilax glabra Roxb. var. maculata Bodinier ex H. Lév., Liliac. etc. Chine 23. 1905.
Smilax mengmaensis R. H. Miao, Acta Sci. Nat. Univ. Sunyatseni 1982(3): 75. 1982
Smilax trigona Warb., Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 29(2): 258. 1900.

Climbing vine. Stem branched, terete, 1–4 m, woody, smooth, unarmed. Petiole 0.5–2.5 cm, narrowly winged at lower 1/4–3/5 of its length, abscission zone apical, tendrils well developed; leaf blade leathery to thinly leathery, elliptic-lanceolate to narrowly ovatelanceolate, 3–15 × 1–7 cm, base rounded, apex acuminate, ± glaucous abaxially, main veins 5. Umbels 10–30(–60)-flowered, basally not prophyllate; peduncle 1–5 mm; bracteoles many, persistent. Male flowers: perianth greenish white, slightly 6-angled; outer tepals broadly obovate-orbicular, cucullate, ca. 2 mm, inner ones ca. 1 mm wide, margin irregularly denticulate; stamens nearly as long as inner tepals. Female flowers: staminodes 3. Berries globose, blue-black, 0.7–1 cm in diam., white powdery.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 69, 2402; C. H. Tsou 1879.
Distribution: Areas S of Changjiang; India, Myanmar, Thailand, Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests and thickets. Flowering: Jul.–Nov.; fruiting: Nov.–Apr. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (rhizome).

Smilax hypoglauca Benth. 粉背菝葜
FHK 369. 1861; FKH 278. 1912; FRPS 15: 208, pl. 66: 1. 1978; FOC 24: 106. 2000.
Smilax corbularia Kunth var. hypoglauca (Benth.) T. Koyama, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 13: 15. 1960.
Smilax corbularia auct. non Kunth: FGD 6: 372. 2005, quoad syn. Smilax hypoglauca Benth.

Climbing vine. Stem branched, 2–(–4) m, woody, unarmed. Petiole 0.7–1.3 cm, narrowly winged at lower half, wings each with a lanceolate auricle apically, abscission zone apical, tendrils usually present; leaf blade leathery, narrowly elliptic to ovate-oblong, 5–12 × 2–5 cm, base subrounded, apex acuminate, margin slightly recurved, glaucous abaxially, main veins 3–5, reticulate veins conspicuous adaxially. Umbels axillary, 10–20-flowered, basally not prophyllate; peduncle 0.2–1.5 cm; bracteoles many, small, persistent. Male flowers: tepals greenish yellow, outer ones ca. 2.5 mm, inner ones smaller, filaments connate, forming a short column. Female flowers: tepals 2.2–2.5 mm; staminodes 3. Berries dark red, globose, 0.8–1.0 cm in diam.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 2234; Y. S. Lau 242, 1371.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guizhou, Fujian, Jiangxi.
Ecology: Forests, thickets. Flowering: Jul.–Aug.; fruiting: Dec.
Notes: The syntypes were collected from Happy Valley. The species was reported as Smilax corbularia Kunth previously (Check List HK Plants 80. 1993; 128. 2004).

Smilax lanceifolia Roxb. var. opaca A. DC. 暗色菝葜
Monogr. Phan. 1: 57. 1878; FGZ 686. 1956; FRPS 15: 218, pl. 71: 3. 1978; FOC 24: 110. 2000.
Smilax kainantensis Masam., Trans. Nat. Hist. Soc. Taiwan 33: 27. 1943.
Smilax laevis Wall. ex A. DC., Monogr. Phan. 1. 6. 1878.
Smilax laevis Wall. ex A. DC. var. ophirensis A. DC., Monogr. Phan. 1: 57. 1878.
Smilax laevis Wall. ex A. DC. var. parkii A. DC., Monogr. Phan. 1: 57. 1878.
Smilax opaca (A. DC.) J. B. Norton, Pl. Wilson. 3(1): 11. 1916.
Smilax lanceifolia Roxb. subsp. opaca (A. DC.) T. Koyama, Fl. E. Himalaya 2: 172. 1971.
Smilax lanceifolia auct. non Roxb.: FHK 370. 1861; FKH 278. 1912; FTW ed. 2, 5: 117, pl. 43. 2000; FGD 6: 372. 2005; Check List HK Plants 81. 1993.

Climbing vine. Stem branched, terete, 1–2.5 m, woody, usually unarmed, rarely sparsely armed. Petiole 0.8–2.5 cm, narrowly winged at lower 1/5–1/4 of its length, abscission zone at middle, tendrils usually present; leaf blade leathery, oblong-lanceolate to ovate-lanceolate, 6–5 × 2–6 cm, base rounded to broadly cuneate, apex acute, obviously shiny adaxially, pale green abaxially; main veins 5, raised adaxially. Umbels axillary, many-flowered, basally prophyllate; peduncle 1–2 cm, proximally articulate. Male flowers: tepals yellowish green, 3–4.5 × ca. 1 mm, reflexed; stamens exserted, filaments 2.5–3.5 mm, anthers ca. 1 mm. Female flowers smaller, staminodes 6. Berries purplish black, globose, 6–8 mm in diam.

Locality: Aberdeen Reservoir, The Peak, Ma On Shan, Tai Mo Shan, Sunset Peak. H. G. Ye et al. 1017; S. C. Ng 4114; F. W. Xing 7562.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Thailand, Vietnam.
Ecology: Thickets and sparse forests. Flowering: Sep.–Mar.; fruiting: Oct.–Nov.

Smilax ocreata A. DC. 抱莖菝葜
Monogr. Phan. 1: 191. 1878; FRPS 15: 234, pl. 75: 2. 1978; FOC 24: 114. 2000.
Smilax perulata H. Lév. & Vaniot, Repert. Spec. Nov. Regni Veg. 9(199–201): 78. 1910.

Climbing vine. Stem up to 7 m, woody, sparsely prickly. Petiole 2–3.5 cm, broadly winged at lower 1/3–1/2 of its length, wings 0.5–2 cm wide, basally deeply clasping node, abscission zone at middle or distal; tendrils usually developed; leaf blade leathery, ovate to elliptic, to 23 × 12.5 cm, base broadly cuneate to shallowly cordate, pale green abaxially. Flowers and fruits unknown.

Locality: Tsuen Wan. S. C. Ng 3441.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Yunnan; Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Vietnam.
Ecology: Open forests. Flowering: Mar.–Jun.; fruiting: Jul.–Oct.
Notes: It was treated as a synonym of S. perfoliata in FGD.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Authority: (F. T. Wang & Tang) S. C. Chen
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Smilax retroflexa (F. T. Wang & T. Tang) S. C. Chen 蒼白菝葜
Acta Phytotax. Sin. 34: 436. 1996; FOC 24: 107. 2000.
Smilax aberrans Gagnep. var. retroflexa F. T. Wang & Tang, FRPS 15: 254. 1978.
Smilax aberrans Gagnep. subsp. retroflexa (F. T. Wang & Tang) T. Koyama, Fl. Cambodge, Laos & Vietnam 20: 82. 1983.
Smilax ovalifolia auct. non Roxb. ex D. Don: FHK 370. 1861; FKH 278. 1912.

Climbing vine. Stem stout, branched, to 10 m, woody, prickly. Petiole 1.6–3 cm, narrowly winged at lower 1/2–2/3 of its length, abscission zone subapical, tendrils well developed; leaf blade ovate to suborbicular, 12–26 × 8–20 cm, main veins 5–7. Umbels several together in axillary racemes or panicles, 1.5–4 cm, 12–40-flowered, basally prophyllate; peduncle 1.3–3 cm. Male flowers: outer tepals 5–6 × ca. 1.5 mm, inner ones much narrower. Female flowers: tepals slightly smaller than male ones; staminodes 3. Berries dark red, ellipsoidal-globose, 0.9–1.2 cm in diam.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Sunset Peak. W. J. Tutcher 10595; Y. W. Lam 2266.
Distribution: Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Yunnan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Apr.; fruiting: Nov.

Dioscorea alata L. 參薯
Sp. Pl. 2: 1033. 1753; FHN 4: 152. 1977; FRPS 16(1): 117, pl. 37: 1–6. 1985; FFJ 6: 550. 1995; FOC 24: 296. 2000; FTW ed. 2, 5: 88. 2000; FGD 6: 395, fig. 236. 2005; Wilkin P. & C. Thapuai, Fl. Thailand 10(1): 11, fig. 1, 2. 2009.

Herbaceous twining vines; tubers variable, globose, conical or cylindrical, usually branched. Stem twining to right, glabrous, with 4 narrow ridges or membranous wings, sometimes prickly at base, usually bearing bulblets in leaf axils. Leaves alternate, but opposite distally on stem, simple; petiole green or purplish red, 3–10(–15) cm; leaf blade papery, ovate to triangular-ovate, 6–15(–20) × 3–13 cm, base sagittate to deeply cordate, apex shortly acuminate or caudate, glabrous on both surfaces, green or purplish red; basal veins 5–7. Male spikes solitary or a few together, 1.5–4 cm, sometimes forming a panicle to 20 – 30 cm; rachis ± zigzagged; male flowers light green, outer perianth lobes broadly ovate, 1.5–2 mm; stamens 6. Female spikes solitary or 2–3 together in leaf axils. Female flowers with 6 staminodes; ovary glabrous. Capsule of 3 flat wing-like oblate, sometimes obcordate lobes, 1.5–2.5 cm. Seeds inserted near middle of capsule, winged all round.

Locality: Cultivated. K. S. Pang 10.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; widely cultivated in tropical and subtropical area.
Ecology: Flowering: Nov.–Jan. of the following year; fruiting: Dec.–Jan. of the following year.
Uses: Food.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Shek O, Sai Kung, Ma On Shan, Lantau Peak
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Dioscorea benthamii Prain & Burkill 大青薯（邊氏薯蕷）
J. Asiat. Soc. Bengal 4: 448. 1908; FRPS 16(1): 108, pl. 33: 17–19. 1985; FFJ 6: 549. 1995; FOC 24: 294. 2000; FTW ed. 2, 5: 89. 2000; FGD 6: 397. 2005.
Dioscorea oppositifolia auct. non L.: FHK 367. 1861.

Herbaceous twining vines, glabrous throughout, with tuberous rootstock. Stem twining to right, slender, to 20 m. Leaves papery, usually opposite, simple; petiole 0.5–2 cm; leaf blade obovate-oblong or oblong to ovate-lanceolate, 2–7(–9) × 0.7–4 cm, base rounded, apex acute to acuminate, margin entire, abaxially whitish; basal veins 3or5(or7). Male spikes solitary or 2–3 together in leaf axils, 2–3 cm, or forming short panicles; rachis obviously zigzagged; male flowers sessile; bracts and perianth lobes purplish brown dotted; stamens 6. Female spikes usually solitary or paired, 3–10 cm; female flowers subsessile, bracts ovate, apex acuminate; outer perianth lobes broadly ovate; staminodes 6. Capsule of 3 flat wing-like oblate lobes, ca. 1.5 cm. Seeds inserted near middle of capsule, winged all round.

Locality: Shek O, Sai Kung, Ma On Shan, Lantau Peak. Y. W. Lam 284, 751; HK sheet 41994.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Thickets on mountain slopes and in ravines. Flowering: May–Jun.; fruiting: Jul.–Sep.
Notes: The syntype specimens were collected from Little Hong Kong, Happy Valley and Tai Tam between 1878 and 1879.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Tai Po Kau, Lam Tsuen, Sham Tseng, Ta Kwu Ling
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Dioscorea bulbifera L. 黃獨
Sp. Pl. 2: 1033. 1753; FKH 276. 1912; FHN 4: 151. 1977; FRPS 16(1): 88, pl. 26: 1–5. 1985; FFJ 6: 545. 1995; FOC 24: 287. 2000; FTW ed. 2, 5: 89. 2000; FGD 6: 395. 2005; Wilkin P. & C. Thapuai, Fl. Thailand 10(1): 25, fig. 9, 10. 2009.
Dioscorea sativa auct. non L.: FHK 368. 1861; FKH 276. 1912.

Herbaceous twining vines; tubers usually solitary, globular to pyriform, 4–10 cm thick, with black cork and many fibrous roots. Stem twining to left, glabrous, smooth, bearing bulblets in axils of leaves. Leaves alternate, simple; petiole 2.5–12 cm; leaf blade broadly cordate, 5–15(–26) × 4–14(–26) cm, apex caudate-acuminate, margin entire or slightly undulate, glabrous. Male spikes usually clustered in leaf axils, drooping, sometimes forming panicles, 3–10 cm or longer; male flowers solitary, ± contiguous along rachis; perianth purple; stamens 6, inserted at base of perianth, filaments nearly as long as anthers. Female spikes often 2 or more together, similar to male ones, 20–50 cm; female flowers sessile, erect; staminodes 6. Capsule of 3 flat wing-like oblong-orbicular lobes, 1.5–3 cm, straw-coloured, densely purplish dotted, glabrous, base and apex rounded. Seeds inserted near apex of capsule, dark brown, winged toward base.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Po Kau, Lam Tsuen, Sham Tseng, Ta Kwu Ling. P. S. Choi 522; F. W. Xing 7396; HK sheet 40753.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Gansu, Shaanxi, Henan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Jiangsu, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Korea, Japan, Vietnam, Cambodia, Myanmar, Thailand, India, Bhutan, Africa, Oceania.
Ecology: Margins of forests, thickets, ravines, river banks. Flowering: Jul.–Oct.; fruiting: Aug.–Nov.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Dioscorea cirrhosa Lour. 薯莨
Fl. Cochinch. 2: 625. 1790; FRPS 16(1): 108, pl. 34: 1–4. 1985; FFJ 6: 551, fig. 484. 1995; FOC 24: 294. 2000; FGD 6: 396. 2005; Wilkin P. & C. Thapuai, Fl. Thailand 10(1): 29, fig. 11, 12. 2009.
Dioscorea rhipogonoides Oliv., Hooker's Icon. Pl. t. 1868; FKH 276. 1912.
Dioscorea matsudae Hayata, Icon. Pl. Formosan. 96. 1896; FTW ed. 2, 5: 96. 2000.

Twining vines, glabrous throughout; tubers variable in shape, globose, ovoid, oblong or gourd-shaped, very hard; cork dark brown; transverse section light brown or red, purplish black when dry. Stem twining to right, to 18 m or longer, almost woody, prickly at base. Leaves alternate on the lower part of stem, opposite on the upper part of stem, simple; petiole 2–6 cm; leaf blade ovate to linear, 5–20 × 0.6–14 cm, leathery, base rounded, sometimes triangular lobed, apex acute or acuminate, margin entire, adaxially dark green, abaxially whitish, basal veins 3 or 5, reticulate veins prominent. Male spikes axillary, forming panicles of 2–14 cm or longer; rachis straight; male flowers with 6 stamens. Female spike solitary, to 10 cm. Capsule of 3 flat wing-like oblate lobes, 2–3.5 cm, base emarginate, attenuate into pedicel ca. 7 mm. Seeds inserted near middle of capsule, winged all round.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Y. S. Lau 2472; Y. W. Lam 14; K. L. Yip 4098.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Xizang, Yunnan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam, Thailand.
Ecology: Margins of forests, thickets on mountain slopes, and in ravines. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.; fruiting: Jul.–Jan. of the following year.
Uses: Material (tannin, dye), medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Tai Po, Fung Yuen, Lantau Peak
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Dioscorea fordii Prain & Burkill 山薯
J. Asiat. Soc. Bengal 4: 450. 1908; FKH 276. 1912; FRPS 16(1): 114, pl. 36: 5 – 10. 1985; FFJ 6: 554, fig. 488. 1995; FOC 24: 295. 2000; FGD 6: 398. 2005.
Dioscorea batatas auct. non Decne: FHK 368. 1861; FKH 276. 1912.

Herbaceous twining vines; tubers vertical, cylindrical; cork brown. Stem twining to right, glabrous, prickly at base. Leaves papery, simple, alternate on lower part of stem, opposite on upper part of stem; petioles 3–6 cm; leaf blade broadly lanceolate, oblong-ovate to elliptic-ovate, 5–12 × 2.5–8.5 cm, base sagittate or hastate to deeply cordate or rounded, apex acuminate or caudate, margin entire, glabrous on both surfaces; basal veins 5 or 7, outermost ones near margin. Male spikes axillary, solitary or 2–4 together, 1.5–3 cm, or forming panicles to 40 cm; rachis zigzagged; male flowers sessile; outer perianth lobes broadly ovate, 1.5–2 mm, inner ones obovate, narrower but thicker than outer; stamens 6. Female spike often solitary, to 25 cm in fruit. Capsule of 3 flat, wing-like oblate lobes, 1.5–3 cm. Seeds inserted near middle of capsule, winged all round.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Po, Fung Yuen, Lantau Peak. Y. S. Lau 766; L. T. Lo 314; HK sheet 40826.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Zhejiang, Fujian.
Ecology: Margins of forests, thickets on mountain slopes and in ravines. Flowering: Oct.–Jan. of the following year; fruiting: Dec.–Jan. of the following year.
Notes: The syntype specimens (C. Ford 6, K. Wong 659, Lamont 758, K) were collected from Hong Kong Island and Lantau Island between 1851 and 1890s.

Dioscorea futschauensis Uline ex R. Knuth 福州薯蕷
Pflanzenr. 87(IV. 43): 264. 1924; FRPS 16(1): 73, pl. 20: 1–4. 1985; FFJ 6: 548, fig. 481. 1995; FOC 24: 282. 2000; FGD 6: 393, fig. 235. 2005.

Herbaceous twining vines; rhizomes horizontal, irregularly cylindrical, hard, cork yellowish brown. Stem twining to left, glabrous. Leaves alternate, simple, ± leathery; petiole 4–5 cm; leaf blade ovate-triangular in outline, to 10 × 11 cm, base deeply cordate, apex acuminate, uniformly hispidulous, densely so abaxially, reticulate veins prominent; leaves on lower part of stem palmately 7-lobed; lobes variable in size, those on upper part of stem margin entire or slightly undulate. Male spikes axillary, usually forming panicles; male flowers solitary or occasionally paired; pedicel 1–1.5 mm; perianth orange, 4–5 mm, 6-lobed; lobes oblong-ovate, 1.5–2 mm, apex rounded; stamens 6, sometimes only 3 developed. Female spikes to 7 cm, few-flowered; female flowers with staminodes; ovary oblong-ellipsoidal. Capsule of 3 flat wing-like broadly obovoid lobes, 1.5–1.8 × 1–1.2 cm, base rounded, apex slightly emarginate to truncate, dark brown, not shiny. Seeds inserted near middle of capsule, 4–5 mm in diam. (excluding wing), winged all round.

Locality: Ping Chau. F. W. Xing 9098; Y. W. Lam 275.
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Zhejiang.
Ecology: Thickets, margins of forests, mountain slopes, ravines. Flowering: Jun.–Jul.; fruiting: Jul.–Oct.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Po, Lam Tsuen, Sai Kung, Man Kam To, Tai A Chau
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Dioscorea hamiltonii Hook. f. 褐苞薯蕷
Fl. Brit. Ind. 6: 295. 1892; Prain & Burkill, J. Proc. Asiat. Soc. Bengal 10: 39. 1914; R. Knuth, Pflanzenr. 4, 43: 266. 1924; Wilkin P. & C. Thapuai, Fl. Thailand 10(1.): 63, fig. 33, 34. 2009.
Dioscorea persimilis Prain & Burkill, J. Proc. Asiat. Soc. Bengal 4: 454. 1908; FKH 276. 1912; FRPS 16(1): 114, pl. 37: 7–12. 1985; FFJ 6: 552, fig. 486. 1995; FOC 24: 295. 2000; FTW ed. 2, 5: 96. 2000; FGD 6: 398. 2005; Check List HK Plants 369. 2002; 128. 2004.

Herbaceous twining vines; tubers cylindrical, cork yellowish brown. Stem twining to right, glabrous, often 4–8-ridged. Leaves papery, simple, alternate on lower part of stem, opposite on upper part of stem; leaf blade orbicular, ovate, or triangular to elliptic-ovate, 3–13 × 1.5–8 cm, base sagittate or hastate or deeply or broadly cordate, apex acute, acuminate, or caudate, margin entire, glabrous on both surfaces, reddish brown when dry; basal veins 7 or 9, reticulate veins prominent. Male spikes axillary, solitary or 2–4 together, 1–4 cm, usually forming panicles to 40 cm; rachis obviously zigzagged; male flowers sessile; bracts and outer perianth lobes brown spotted; stamens 6. Female spikes solitary or paired, to 20 cm in fruiting time; female flowers subsessile; staminodes small. Capsule of 3 flat wing-like oblate lobes, 1.5–2.5 cm. Seeds inserted near middle of capsule, winged all round.

Locality: Tai Po, Lam Tsuen, Sai Kung, Man Kam To, Tai A Chau. S. P. Lau 160; P. S. Choi 288; HK sheet 40256.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou, Hunan, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Mixed forests, thickets, on mountain slopes and in ravines. Flowering: Jul.–Dec.; fruiting: Sep.–Jan. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Fung Yuen, Lin O
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Dioscorea hispida Dennst. 白薯莨
Schlussel Hortortus Malab. 15, 33. 1818; FRPS 16(1): 99, pl. 31: 1–5. 1985; FFJ 6: 543, fig. 477. 1995; FOC 24: 290. 2000; FTW ed. 2, 5: 93. 2000; FGD 6: 392. 2005; Wilkin P. & C. Thapuai, Fl. Thailand 10(1): 67, fig. 35, 36. 2009.

Herbaceous twining vines; tubers ovoid or irregularly shaped and variable in size. Stem terete, twining to left, to 25 m or longer, prickly, initially pubescent. Leaves alternate, palmately 3-foliolate; petiole to 30 cm, hairy; central leaflet ± ovate to elliptic, 6–12(–17.5) × 4–12 cm, base obtuse to truncate, apex acuminate, adaxially sparsely hispid, glabrescent, abaxially hispid, palmately-veined; lateral leaflets ovateelliptic or nearly broadly oblong, oblique, smaller than middle leaflet, margin entire; petiolules terete, 0.5–1 cm. Male spikes in axillary panicles, 15–50 cm, densely tomentose; male flowers sessile, in dense clusters; stamens 6. Female spikes simple, to 40 cm. Capsule of 3 flat wing-like ellipsoidal lobes, 4–6 × 2.5–3 cm, leathery, densely pubescent. Seeds inserted near apex of capsule, winged toward base.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Fung Yuen, Lin O. W. J. Tutcher 10953, 11772; Y. S. Lau 2493.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan, Yunnan, E Xizang; Bhutan, India, Sikkim, Thailand to Malesia.
Ecology: Margins of forests, thickets. Flowering: Apr.–May; fruiting: Jul.–Sep.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Dioscorea pentaphylla L. 五葉薯蕷
Sp. Pl. 2: 1032. 1753; FRPS 16(1): 95, pl. 28: 7–10. 1985; FFJ 6: 544. 1995; FOC 24: 289. 2000; FGD 6: 393, fig. 234. 2005; Wilkin P. & C. Thapuai, Fl. Thailand 10(1): 95, fig. 52, 53. 2009.

Herbaceous twining vines; tubers variously shaped, usually long ovoid, with many fibrous roots. Stem terete, twining to left, prickly and sparsely puberulent when young, usually bearing bulblets in leaf axils. Leaves alternate, palmately 3–7-foliolate; petiole 3–13 cm, densely reddish brown pubescent; leaflets obovate-elliptic, oblong to elliptic (the outermost 2 lateral ones obliquely ovate-elliptic), 6.5–24 × 1.5–9 cm, base attenuate into a ± tomentose petiolule, apex acute, margin entire, adaxially appressed pubescent or subglabrous, abaxially sparsely pubescent, pinnately-veined. Male spikes in axillary panicles to 50 cm, with brown short pubescence on axis; male flowers sessile or subsessile, with bract and reniform bracteole forming an involucel around perianth, sparsely hairy; stamens 3. Female spikes simple or branched, to 25 cm, brown puberulent; female flowers subsessile; bracts, perianth, and ovary hairy. Capsule of 3 flat wing-like ellipsoidal lobes, 2–2.5 × 1–1.3 cm, thinly leathery, sparsely hairy, black at maturity. Seeds inserted near apex of capsule, winged toward base.

Locality: Ma On Shan, Tai Lam. HK sheet 7524, 39080.
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Jiangxi, Yunnan, Xizang; Japan, Philippines, Vietnam, Myanmar, Laos, Nepal, India, Malaysia, Indonesia, New Guinea, Africa, Australia, Pacific islands.
Ecology: Margins of forests, thickets. Flowering: Aug.–Oct.; fruiting: Nov.–Feb. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

Burmannia championii Thwaites 頭花水玉簪
Enum. Pl. Zeyl. 325. 1864; Hook. f., Fl. Brit. Ind. 5: 666. 1890; Ridl., Mat. Fl. Mal. Penins. 2: 72. 1908; Ridl., Fl. Mal. Penins. 4: 306. 1924; Jonker, Meded. Bot. Mus. Herb. Rijks Univ. Utrecht 51: 138. 1938; Jonker, Fl. Males., ser. I, 4(1): 17–18. 1948; Ohwi, Fl. Jap., 336. 1953; FRPS 16(2): 173. 1981; FGD 2: 480. 1991; FOC 23: 123. 2010.
Burmannia dazielii Rendle, J. Bot. 40: 311. 1902.
Burmannia hunanensis K. M. Liu & C. L. Long, Ann. Bot. Fennici 38: 211. 2001.

Achlorophyllous, holomycotrophic herb, flowering at 3–22 cm. Stem white, slender. Basal rosette leaves absent. Cauline leaves ovate-triangular, 1.5–6 × 1–3 mm. Bracts ovate-triangular, 1.5–6 mm. Inflorescences with 3–13 flowers. Flowers pedicellate or sessile, white with yellow tepals, 5–11 mm long. Perianth tube 3–5 mm long; wings reduced to ribs or absent; outer tepals narrowly triangular, 1.5–3 mm long, with single margin; inner tepals spathulate, 0.8–1.4 mm long, with single margin. Stamens sessile or with short filament, basally adnate to perianth; connectives sometimes with 2 small apical crests but lacking a pendent basal spur. Ovary ellipsoidal or obovoid, 2.5–3.5 mm long. Capsule subglobose. Seeds subglobose.

Locality: Mount Violet, Tai Mo Shan. R. Barretto & K. Barretto s.n.; S. C. Ng s.n. (HKU).
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong, Hunan, Taiwan; India, Indonesia, Japan, Malaysia, New Guinea, Sri Lanka, Thailand, Pacific islands.
Ecology: Wet areas in forests. Flowering & fruiting: May–Aug.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Pok Fu Lam Reservoir, HKU Campus, Tai Tam Tuk, Ho Pui, Crescent Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Burmannia chinensis Gand. 香港水玉簪
Bull. Soc. Bot. Fr. 66: 290. 1919; D. X. Zhang & R. M. K. Saunders, Nord. J. Bot. 20: 391 – 392. 2000; FOC 23: 122. 2010.
Burmannia pusilla (Wall. ex Miers) Thwaites var. hongkongensis Jonker, Meded. Bot. Mus. Herb. Rijks Univ. Utrecht 51: 131–132. 1938; FRPS 16(2): 171. 1981; FGD 2: 479. 1991; Check List HK Plants 369. 2002; 128. 2004.

Chlorophyllous, semi-mycotrophic herb, flowering at 4.5–20 cm. Stems green, slender. Basal rosette leaves few, lanceolate, 0.3–1.2 cm × 1–3 mm. Cauline leaves linear, 5–18 × ca. 2 mm. Bracts lanceolate, 5–6 mm. Inflorescences with 1–3(–4) flowers. Flowers pedicellate or subsessile, purple or yellow, 3–8 mm long. Perianth tube 4–6.5 mm long; wings conspicuous, 1–3 mm wide; outer tepals broadly ovate, 1–3 mm long, with single or shallow double margin; inner tepals spathulate, 0.5–1.2 mm long, with single margin. Stamens sessile; connectives with 2 apical crests and sometimes a pendent basal spur. Ovary ellipsoidal or obovoid, 2.5–7 mm long. Capsule obovoid. Seeds ellipsoidal.

Locality: Pok Fu Lam Reservoir, HKU Campus, Tai Tam Tuk, Ho Pui, Crescent Island. E. Bodinier 924 (HK, LY, P); E. Bodinier 924 bis (E, HK, P); HK sheet 7053.
Distribution: Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Yunnan, Zhejiang; India, Laos, Thailand, Vietnam.
Ecology: Generally wet grasslands. Flowering: Jun.–Oct.; fruiting: Jul.–Jan. of the following year.

Burmannia coelestis D. Don 三品一枝花（雛錫杖）
Prodr. Fl. Nepal. 44. 1825; Schultes, Syst. Veg. 7(2): 75. 1830; Hook. f., Fl. Brit. Ind. 5: 665. 1888; Ridl., J. Str. Br. Roy. As. Soc. 22: 333. 1890; Ridl., Mat. Fl. Mal. Penins. 2: 71. 1908; Ridl., Fl. Mal. Penins. 4: 304. 1924; Jonker, Meded. Bot. Mus. Herb. Rijks Univ. Utrecht 51: 120. 1938; Jonker, Fl. Males., ser. I, 4(1): 17. 1948; FRPS 16(2): 171. 1981; FGD 2: 479. 1991; D. X. Zhang & R. M. K. Saunders, Nord. J. Bot. 20: 388–391. 2000; FOC 23: 122. 2010.

Chlorophyllous, semi-mycotrophic herb, flowering at 10–40 cm. Stems green, slender. Basal rosette leaves few, linear-lanceolate, 0.5–2 cm × ca. 3 mm. Cauline leaves linear, 5–30 × ca. 2.5 mm. Bracts lanceolate, 3–6 mm. Inflorescences with (1–)2–6(–8) flowers. Flowers pedicellate or subsessile, blue-purple with yellow tepals, 10–15 mm long. Perianth tube 4.5–13 mm long; wings conspicuous, 1.5–3 mm wide; outer tepals ovate-triangular, 1–2 mm long, with prominent double margin; inner tepals triangular, 0.5–1 mm long, with double margin. Stamens sessile; connectives with 2 apical crests and a pendent basal spur. Ovary ellipsoidal or obovoid, 3–7 mm long. Capsule obovoid. Seeds ellipsoidal.

Locality: Sheung Shui. W. J. Tutcher 8152.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan; Bangladesh, Brunei, Cambodia, India, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, Nepal, New Guinea, Thailand, Vietnam, Australia.
Ecology: Generally wet grasslands. Flowering: Jun.–Oct.; fruiting: Oct.–Feb. of the following year.

Burmannia itoana Makino 纖草
Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 27: 1. 1913; Jonker, Meded. Bot. Mus. Herb. Rijks Univ. Utrecht 51: 153. 1938; Ohwi, Fl. Jap., 337. 1953; T. L. Wu & S. Chen, FRPS 16(2): 173. 1981; FGD 2: 480. 1991; FOC 23: 123. 2010.
Burmannia takeoi Hayata, Icon. Pl. Formosan. 5: 212. 1915.
Burmannia pingbienensis H. Li, Acta Phytotax. Sin. 21(2): 127. 1983.

Achlorophyllous, holomycotrophic herb, flowering at 5–15 cm. Stem light blue, slender. Basal rosette leaves absent. Cauline leaves ovate-lanceolate, 2.5–3.5 × 1.5–2.5 mm. Bracts ovate-lanceolate, ca. 5 mm. Inflorescences with 1–3 flowers. Flowers pedicellate, blue-purple, 8–11 mm long. Perianth tube 3.5–5.5 mm long; wings conspicuous, 1–2 mm wide; outer tepals ovate-triangular, 1.5–2 mm long, with single margin; inner tepals orbiculate, very small, with single margin. Stamens sessile; connectives with 1 apical crest and a pendent basal spur. Ovary subglobose, 2–3.5 mm long. Capsule subglobose. Seeds ellipsoidal.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island. G. Siu & K. Chu s.n. (HKU); R. T. Corlett s.n. (HKU); D. X. Zhang 98001 (HKU); Y. W. Lam 1787.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan, Taiwan, Yunnan; Japan.
Ecology: Wet, evergreen forests. Flowering & fruiting: Jun.–Dec.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Cape D'Aguilar, Tai Tam Tuk, Bride's Pool, Pat Sin Leng, Tai Po Kau, Wu Kau Tang
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Burmannia wallichii (Miers) Hook. f. 亭立（華氏水玉簪）
Fl. Brit. India 5: 666. 1888; Ridl., Mat. Fl. Mal. Penins. 2: 71. 1908; Gagnep. in Lecomte & Humbert, Fl. Gén. Indo-Chine 6: 21. 1908; Ridl., Fl. Mal. Penins. 4: 305. 1924; Jonker, Meded. Bot. Mus. Herb. Rijks Univ. Utrecht 51: 145. 1938; FRPS 16(2): 173. 1981; FGD 2: 480. 1991; R. M. K. Saunders, Blumea 41: 336. 1996; FOC 23: 123. 2010.
Gonyanthes wallichii Miers, Trans. Linn. Soc. London 18: 537. 1841.

Achlorophyllous, holomycotrophic herb, flowering at 4–11.5 cm. Stem purple, slender. Basal rosette leaves absent. Cauline leaves triangular-subulate, 1.5–3.5 × 1–1.5 mm. Bracts triangular-lanceolate, 2–3.5 mm. Inflorescences with 1–3 flowers. Flowers sessile, blue-purple, 5–10 mm long. Perianth tube 2.5–5.5 mm long; wings narrow or reduced to ribs, 0.2–0.8 mm wide; outer tepals ovatetriangular, ca. 1 mm long, with single margin; inner tepals orbiculate, very small, with single margin. Stamens sessile; connectives lacking apical crests, sometimes with a pendent basal spur. Ovary ellipsoidal to subglobose, 1.5–3 mm long. Capsule subglobose. Seeds ellipsoidal.

Locality: Cape D'Aguilar, Tai Tam Tuk, Bride's Pool, Pat Sin Leng, Tai Po Kau, Wu Kau Tang. S. Y. Hu 5921 (A, US), 13913 (A); H.C. Tang 2513; Y. S. Lau 2057; D. X. Zhang 95001 (HKU).
Distribution: Guangdong, Hainan, Yunnan; Myanmar, Thailand, Vietnam, Peninsular Malaysia.
Ecology: Wet areas in dense forests. Flowering & fruiting: Jul.–Nov.

Thismia tentaculata K. Larsen & Averyanov 三絲水玉杯
Rheedea 17: 16. 2007; Ho et al., J. Syst. Evol. 47: 605-607. 2009; FOC 23: 124. 2010.

Plant holomycotrophic. Stems white, unbranched, erect, 2.5–3 cm. Leaves scale-like, 1.5–5.7 × 0.8–1.1 mm. Flowers 1–4, subsessile, with subtending bracts. Perianth tube white, translucent, actinomorphic, urceolate, ca. 7.3 × 4.8 mm, circumscissile. Outer tepals broadly triangular, ca. 1.4 mm, lacking appendage. Inner tepals narrowly triangular, ca. 2.3 mm excluding appendage; appendage orangish red, spreading, filiform, ca. 1.7 cm. Stamens apically connate. Capsule white, translucent, cup-shaped. Seeds ellipsoidal.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. HK sheet 41925.
Distribution: Vietnam.
Ecology: Evergreen montane forests. Flowering & fruiting: Aug.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Shek O, Kowloon Peak, Fo Tan Valley, Ma On Shan, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Acampe rigida (Buch.-Ham. ex Sm.) P. F. Hunt 多花脆蘭
Kew Bull. 24: 98. 1970; FRPS 19: 286, pl. 43: 1–2. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 735, pl. 310. 2000; FGD 7: 496, fig. 256. 2006; FOC 25: 449. 2009.
Aerides rigida Buch.-Ham. ex Sm., Rees Cyclopedia 39. 1819.
Acampe multiflora (Lindl.) Lindl., Fol. Orch. Acampe 1. 1853; FHK 358. 1861; FKH 266. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 25(1–2): 41. 1972, et Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 112. 1977.

Roots thick and strong, many, branching profusely, up to 50 cm long, 3–10 mm in diam.; stem upright, monopodial, leafy, stout, covered by overlapping leaf sheaths. Leaves distichous, dull green, thick coriaceous, linear, 20–35 × 4–4.5 cm, base folded, apex obtuse or obliqueretuse, midrib inconspicuous above, elevated beneath. Inflorescence an axillary panicle; flowers non-resupinate, very fleshy, creamy white, turning yellow when old, speckled with bright reddish purple on the outside and streaked horizontally on the inside; sepals all alike in size, shape and colour, oblong, slightly incurved, apex rounded or obtuse, 11 × 6–7 mm; petals narrower than the sepals, spathulate, 12 × 4.5 mm, apex rounded; lip very fleshy, non-movable, midlobe tongue-like, ovate, creamy yellow tinged lavender with irregular red specks above and below, margin erose, apex curved downwards, lateral lobes wall-like, velvety inside; disk with a yellow median ridge; column fleshy, very short, 2 mm high, bright purplish red; anther yellow, apical to the column; pollinia fixed at the end of a narrow caudicle; ovary smooth, with inconspicuous lines.

Locality: Shek O, Kowloon Peak, Fo Tan Valley, Ma On Shan, Lantau Island. K. Y. Chan 1374 (CUHK); S. Y. Hu 7352 (CUHK); Y. S. Lau 2024, 2364.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan; S and SE Asia.
Ecology: Damp rocks under trees along streams. Flowering: May–Sep.; fruiting: Oct.–Dec.

Acanthephippium striatum Lindl. 錐囊罎花蘭（中華罎花蘭）
Edwards's Bot. Reg. 24(Misc.): 41. 1838; FOC 25: 310. 2009.
Acanthephippium sinense Rolfe, Kew Bull. 142. 1913; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 25: 11. 1972, et Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 90, fig. 50. 1977; FRPS 18: 323. 1999; FGD 7: 404, fig. 206. 2006; Check List HK Plants 369. 2002; 129. 2004.

Terrestrial perennial herb; pseudobulb ovoid-cylindrical, covered with several membranous sheaths. Leaves papery, obovateelliptic, 20–25 cm, base attenuating into a petiole, apex acute or acuminate. Flowers medium-sized, the odd sepal elliptic-oblong, 1.8–2 × 0.8–1 cm, apex obtuse; lateral ones oblique ovate, slightly wider than the odd sepal, with a 1.3 cm long conical mentum at base; petals ovate-oblong, 2 × 0.7 cm, apex acuminate; lip 3-lobed, lateral lobes erect, apex rounded, curved forward; midlobe rhombic-triangular, 10 × 8 mm, lamellate, apex acute, disk becoming thick near the two lateral lobes, with 3 ridges; column 1.3 cm, with a 8–10 mm long column-foot; pollinia 8 in 2 groups; ovary cylindrical.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. S. Y. Hu 10166, 13699 (CUHK).
Distribution: Guangdong.
Ecology: Flowering: Apr.–May.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Stubb Rd., Repulse Bay, Sha Tin, Ma On Shan, Castle Peak, Wong Lung Hang
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Ania hongkongensis (Rolfe) T. Tang & F. T. Wang 香港安蘭（香港帶唇蘭）
Acta Phytotax. 1: 46. 88. 1951; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 25: 48. 1972, et Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 68, fig. 34. 1977.
Tainia hongkongensis Rolfe, Bull. Misc. Inform. Kew 195. 1896; FKH 264. 1912; FRPS 18: 240. 1999; FGD 7: 406. 2006; FOC 25: 282. 2009; Check List HK Plants 383. 2002; 133. 2004.
Ania angustifolia auct. non Lindl.: FHK 356. 1861.

Terrestrial herb, pseudobulbs ovoid, sheathing when young, bearing a terminal leaf. Leaves petiolate; petioles slender, 13–16 × 0.2–0.3 cm, base covered with a 6 cm tube-like sheath; leaf blades oblong-elliptic, 26 × 3–4 cm, base attenuate into petioles, apex acuminate. Flowers yellowish green with purplish brown spots or veins; sepals subequal, oblong-lanceolate, 20 × 2.2–3.5 mm, apex acuminate; lateral sepals connate to the column base; petals obovate-lanceolate, similar size with sepals, apex acuminate, base attenuate; lip white with yellowish green veins, obovate, apiculate at apex, base spurred, the two sides near base ± covering the column, disk with 3 narrow ridges; column white with light purple, slightly enlarged at apex; anther obovoid, truncate at the base; pollinia 8 in 2 groups.
