Locality: Stubb Rd., Repulse Bay, Sha Tin, Ma On Shan, Castle Peak, Wong Lung Hang. S. Y. Hu 9853, 13219 (CUHK); Y. S. Lau 2129.
Distribution: Guangdong, Fujian.
Ecology: Among loose rocks or under trees from hillsides. Flowering: Mar.–Apr.
Notes: The type specimen was collected by C. Wilford from Mount Parker in 1858.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Sai Kung, Pat Sin Leng, Sha Tau Kok
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Ania ruybarrettoi S. Y. Hu & Barretto 南方安蘭（南方帶唇蘭）
Chung Chi Journal 13(2): 25 fig. 12. 1976.
Tainia ruybarrettoi (S. Y. Hu & Barretto) Aver., Opred. Orkhid. V’etnama. 403. 1994; FOC 25: 283. 2009.
Tainia ruybarrettoi (S. Y. Hu & Barretto) Z. H. Tsi, FRPS 18: 243. 1999; FGD 7: 406. 2006; Check List HK Plants 383. 2002; 133. 2004.

Terrestrial herb; rhizome horizontal, the terminal internode enlarging into a pseudobulb; pseudobulbs crowded together or very closely spaced, ovoid and smooth when young, grooved and winkled when old, dull green or purple in colour at anthesis bearing 2 cataphylls and a terminal leaf. Leaves solitary, dark green, slightly grooved at apex, petiolate; petioles 15 – 25 cm, oriented at the apex of the pseudobulb; leaf blades lanceolate, 30–45 × 4.5–5.3 cm, conspicuously veined with 9 longitudinal veins, prominently elevated beneath. Flowers 5 – 28, well-spaced; sepals and petals similar in size and colour, palmately arranged in one plane, 2.7–3.5 × 0.4–0.5 cm, purplish yellow with 3– 5 purple longitudinal veins running from the base to apex, margin yellow; odd sepal dorsal, linear-lanceolate, lateral ones slightly falcate; petals oblique-oblanceolate; lip 3-lobed, spurred, bent, crescent-shaped, the sides erect, covering almost the entire column, extending forward into a distinct rounded lobe at the apex, streaked and dotted bright purple, the inner surface marked with lines of bright purple hairs, the midlobe ovate, slightly curved downwards, margin wavy, apex acute, pale lavender flushed yellow, darker purple beneath, disk longitudinally 5-ridged, becoming 5-crested at the throat; spur orange-yellow, rounded and smooth at apex; column back white, the front streaked purple, truncate, slightly arcuate; anther hanging, ovoid, creamy yellow; pollina 8 in 4 pairs.

Locality: Sai Kung, Pat Sin Leng, Sha Tau Kok. S. Y. Hu 13098 (CUHK); HK sheet 30331, 30431.
Distribution: Guangxi.
Ecology: Bamboo forests. Flowering: Mar.
Notes: The type specimen (S. Y. Hu 13098A, K, holotype; PE, isotype) was collected by Ruy Barretto from Pat Sin Leng in 1968. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Anoectochilus yungianus S. Y. Hu 香港金線蘭（容氏開唇蘭）
Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 24(3–4): 257, fig. 1a, 2a–e. 1971; 25(1–2): 50. 1972; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 45, fig. 17. 1977; FRPS 17: 221. 1999; FGD 7: 364. 2006; FOC 25: 79. 2009, pro syn. sub A. roxburghii.

Terrestrial herb, 10–20 cm tall, the basal 3–5 internodes lying on the forest floor having the appearance of rhizome, the distal upright portion consisting of 4 or 5 internodes, short and bearing a rosette of leaves. Leaves petiolate, leaf blades ovate, 1.5–5 × 1–3 cm, base subtruncate, apex acute, velvety green above, purple beneath, with 5 coral-red veins and distinct reticulation of veinlets. Flowers white, 4–5, in a terminal raceme; pedicels 2–3 mm; sepal distinct, villose, the dorsal one ovate, strongly recurved at the apex, gibbous at base; the lateral two spreading, 6–7 mm; petals white, falcate, oblique, 6–7 mm, flush with the margin of the odd sepal and lining its inside; lip white, with a conical spur, attached to column, bending at an angle of 90º, fringed on the sides, prolonged into 2 terminal lobes (epichile); column short, with 2 front wings; anther ovoid, apex long, pointed; pollinia 2, sectile; ovary 13–16 mm, villose, hairs glandular.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan. C. P. Lau 173 (CUHK); Y. S. Lau 3230; Y. W. Lam 1171.
Distribution: Endemic to Hong Kong.
Ecology: Shade and moist places in forests, alt. 400 m. Flowering: Nov.–Jan. of the following year.
Notes: The type specimen was collected by S. Y. Hu from Tai Mo Shan in 1971.

Aphyllorchis montana Rchb. f. 無葉蘭
Linnaea 41: 57. 1877; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 54, fig. 24. 1977; FRPS 17: 84, pl. 10: 6–7. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 749. 2000; FGD 7: 339, fig. 168. 2006; FOC 25: 178. 2009.

Saprophytic herb, 40 70 cm tall at flowering time; the lower portion of the stem marked by sheaths of 0.5–2 cm, the middle portion by scales of 1–1.3 cm, the apical portion being the raceme of 10–20 cm. Flowers pale yellow, subtended by linear-lanceolate bracts of 6–14 mm; dorsal sepal oblong-obovate, 9–11 mm, obtuse; lateral sepals slightly shorter; petals oblong; lip trilobed, 7–9 mm, the lateral lobes deltoid, the apical lobe ovate, 5–7 mm, obtuse; column 7–10 mm, enlarged at the distal end.

Locality: Sha Tin (Hu 1977), Tsuen Wan (Siu 2000).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangxi, Yunnan, Taiwan; widespread species occurring in N India to Sri Lanka thence eastward, through warm areas in China to Indonesia, Philippines, northward to Japan.
Ecology: Shade of large trees. Flowering: Aug.–Sep.
Notes: This species was first recorded in 1975. Recent studies (e.g. M. Roy et al., BMC Biology 7: 51. 2009) show that the species is associated with a board spectrum of ectomycorrhizal fungi.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Mount Parker, Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan, Tai Po Kau, Wong Lung Hang
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Appendicula cornuta Blume 牛齒蘭
Bijdr. 6: fig. 12, et 7: 302. 1825; FRPS 19: 58, pl. 9: 7–9. 1999; FGD 7: 445, fig. 224. 2006; FOC 25: 364. 2009.
Apendicula bifaria Lindl. ex Benth., Hook. J. Bot. Kew Misc. 7: 35. 1855; FHK 358. 1861; FKH 266. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 57, fig. 26. 1977.

Epiphytic caespitose perennial herb; stems erect or hanging, subcylindrical. Leaves distichous, ovate-elliptic or oblong, 2–4 × 0.5–1.2 cm, base sheathing, apex obtuse, notched, apiculate. Flowers white, very small, non-resupinate, 2–6 in axillary spikes; sepals subequal, the odd one ovate or elliptic, 3–4 mm, concave, apex acuminate; the lateral ones oblique-triangular, slightly longer than the odd sepal, adnate to the column foot forming a mentum; petals ovate or ovate-oblong, 2–3 × 1.5 mm, obtuse; lip fleshy, undivided, attached to the column foot, produced into a conical spur filled with a fleshy appendage at the apical portion and a membranous appendage near the base, apex obtuse and reflexed, margin wavy, disk with an unicorn-like callus; column short, stout; pollinia 6, in 2 groups of 3; ovary cylindrical, subsessile.

Locality: Mount Parker, Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan, Tai Po Kau, Wong Lung Hang. S. Y. Hu 8990, 10863 (CUHK); Y. W. Lam 178.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; S to SE Asia.
Ecology: Forests, streamsides. Flowering: Jul.–Aug.; fruiting: Sep.–Nov.

Arundina graminifolia (D. Don) Hochr. 竹葉蘭
Bull. New York Bot. Gard. 6: 270. 1910; FRPS 18: 334, pl. 56: 1–3. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 755, pl. 321. 2000; FGD 7: 395, fig. 201. 2006; FOC 25: 315. 2009.
Bletia graminifolia D. Don, Prodr. Fl. Nepal. 29. 1825.
Arundina chinensis Blume, Bijdr. 8: 402. 1825; FHK 355. 1861; FKH 265. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 62, fig. 29. 1977.

Terrestrial herb; stems erect, grass-like and stiff, leafy, the basal portion swelling into a small ovoid pseudobulb covered by imbricate brown tough scales, the aerial portion cylindrical, covered by fresh or persistent sheaths. Leaves linear-lanceolate, thinly leathery or papery, 5–20 × 0.6 cm, base slightly narrowed and bearing cylindrical sheaths, apex acute; sheaths amplexicaul and overlapping, 2–4 cm, articulate at the apical end. Inflorescences terminal, racemose or paniculate; flowers resupinate, colourful and showy; sepals elliptic or elliptic-lanceolate, 2.5–4 × 0.7–0.9 cm, apex acute, pale rose-mauve; petals elliptic or ovate-elliptic, 2.5 –3.5 × 1.3–1.8 cm, rose-mauve with darker median veins; lip trumpet-shaped, 3–4 cm, embracing the column, wavy at the margin, deeply cleft at the apex, pale magenta and deepening into bright rose-purple towards the margin and apex; column slender, curved and slightly winged at the apical end; anther terminal, 2-celled; pollinia 8, discoid; ovary slender, glabrous, striate.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. S. Y. Hu 9432, 12294A (CUHK); Y. S. Lau 3135; HK sheet 34780.
Distribution: C, E, S & SW China; tropical Asia.
Ecology: Grassy slopes or along the banks of streams in exposed areas. Flowering: Jul.–Dec.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.

Bletilla striata (Thunb. ex Murray) Rchb. f. 白芨
Bot. Zeit. 36: 75. 1878; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 74, fig. 37. 1977; FRPS 18: 50, pl. 6: 1–3. 1999; FGD 7: 340, fig. 169. 2006; FOC 25: 210. 2009.
Limodorum striatum Thunb. ex Murray, Syst. Veg. ed. 14, 816. 1784.
Bletia hyacinthina (Sm.) R. Br., Hort. Kew ed. 2, 5: 206. 1813; FKH 263. 1912.
Cymbidium hyacinthinum Sm., Exot. Bot. 1: 117, t. 60. 1804.

Terrestrial perennial herb; rhizomes compressed, ginger-like. Leaves petiolate, petioles sheathing with conspicuous joint; leaf blades elliptic or lanceolate, 10–15(–30) × 2–4 cm. Flowers resupinate, bright purple, wide open; sepals and petals similar in length and width, 2.5–3 × 0.5–0.7 cm; dorsal sepal linear-oblong, obtuse at apex; lateral ones oblique-falcate; petals almost horizontal, oblong-oblanceolate-oblique, slightly twisted; lip horizontal, tubular and covering the column, slightly enlarged towards the apex, 3-lobed, 2 × 0.7–0.8 cm, light purple, darker towards apex and margin, lateral lobes erect, midlobe tongue-like, with 5 longitudinal wavy crests running all the way, 2 additional ridges near to the base, the margin ruffled and wavy; column long, slender, slightly arcuate; anther oblong, white; pollinia 8 in 4 pairs, ovary slender, slightly curved.

Locality: Cultivated in Hong Kong; Y. K. Leung 26 (CUHK); S. Y. Hu 11699 (CUHK); HK sheet 35812.
Distribution: Shaanxi, Gansu, areas S of Changjiang; Korea, Japan.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Feb.–Apr.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Victoria Peak, Kowloon Peak, Ma On Shan, Shing Mun
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Brachycorythis galeandra (Rchb. f.) Summerh. 短距苞葉蘭（頭盔蘭）
Kew Bull. 10: 241. 1955; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 30, fig. 7. 1977; FRPS 17: 284, pl. 41: 4–6. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 760. 2000; FGD 7: 765, fig. 186. 2006; FOC 25: 101. 2009.
Platanthera galeandra Rchb. f., Linnaea 25: 226. 1852.
Habenaria galeandra (Rchb. f.) Benth., FHK 363. 1861.
Platanthera obcordata auct. non Rchb. f.: FKH 269. 1912.

Terrestrial herb up to 25 cm tall, needing a resting period during winter dry season; underground tuber ellipsoidal, 1.5 2 cm thick. Leaves 9–15, all cauline, internodes 1.5–2 cm; petiolate; leaf blade lanceolate-elliptic, 3–4.5 × 1–1.5 cm. Flowers white with rose-lilac lines; lip spurred; column white; anthers with parallel thecae; pollinia 2; ovary cylindrical, 1.2 cm, papillose.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Kowloon Peak, Ma On Shan, Shing Mun. K. K. Mark 25(2844) (CUHK); S. Y. Hu 10521 (CUHK); Y. S. Lau 2495.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Taiwan.
Ecology: Short grasses on windy peaks of high mountains in Hong Kong. Flowering: Jun.–Jul.

Bulbophyllum affine Lindl. 赤唇石豆蘭
Gen. Sp. Orch. Pl. 48. 1830; FRPS 19: 173, pl. 25: 1–3. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 763. 2000; FGD 7: 424, fig. 215. 2006; FOC 25: 410. 2009.

Rhizomes stout and thick, 4–5 mm in diam., with imbricate scale-like sheaths. Pseudobulb erect, subcylindrical, 3–4 cm long, 5–8 mm in diam., terminated with 1 leaf. Leaves thickly coriaceous or fleshy, upright, oblong, 5–25 × 1–5 cm, apex obtuse and notched, midrib impressed above, elevated beneath. Flowers light yellow with purple veins, thick; odd sepal lanceolate, 1.5–2 × 0.4–0.5 cm, apex acute; lateral sepals falcate-lanceolate, same length with the odd one, apex acute, base oblique and slightly wider, adnate to the column foot forming a mentum; petals lanceolate, 1–1.5 cm, apex acute, margin entire; lip fleshy, lanceolate, shorter than the petals, apex acuminate, slightly curved downward, grooved at base, lateral margins dark purple; column short and thick, 5 mm.

Locality: Lantau Island.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan, Taiwan; Vietnam, Laos, Thailand, India, Japan.
Ecology: Rocks along streams in forests. Flowering: May–Jul.

Bulbophyllum ambrosia (Hance) Schltr. 芳香石豆蘭（馥石蘭）
Fedde Repert. Sp. Nov. Beih. 4: 247. 1919; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 86. 1977; FRPS 19: 174, pl. 25: 7. 1999; FGD 7: 425. 2006; FOC 25: 407. 2009.
Eria ambrosia Hance, J. Bot. 21(8): 232. 1883.
Bulbophyllum watsonianum Rchb. f., Flora 71: 155. 1888; FKH 262. 1912.

Rhizomes 2–4 mm in diam., with imbricate scale-like sheaths. Pseudobulbs erect or slightly curved upward, cylindrical, 2–5 cm long, 3–6 mm in diam., terminated with 1 leaf. Leaves leathery, oblong, 3.5–12 × 1–2.5 cm, base attenuate into a petiole 3–6 mm, apex obtuse and slightly notched. Flowers light purplish yellow; odd sepal broad-ovate or oblong, 1 × 0.5 cm, apex acute, glabrous, margin entire; lateral sepals oblique ovate-triangular, same length with the odd one but slightly wider, the upper portion oblique and twisted to become beak-like, apex obtuse, base adnate to the column foot forming a mentum; petals triangular, 5–6 × 0.3 cm, margin entire; lip subovate, thicker at apex, winged in the middle, grooved at base, margin slightly wavy, strongly recurved; column short and thick.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Lantau Island. K. K. Mark 5(2144) (CUHK); Y. S. Lau 1763; HK sheet 7064.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Mar.–May.
Notes: The type specimen (Hance Herb. No. 22156, BM) was collected by C. Ford from Victoria Peak in Mar. 1875.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Tsuen Wan, Tai Mo Shan, Sha Tin, Tai Po, Castle Peak, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Bulbophyllum kwangtungense Schltr. 廣東石豆蘭
Fedde Repert. Sp. Nov. 19: 381. 1924; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 25(1–2): 62. 1972; FRPS 19: 196, pl. 28: 7. 1999; FGD 7: 427, fig. 217. 2006; FOC 25: 414. 2009.
Bulbophyllum radiatum auct. non Lindl.: Rolfe, J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 36: 13. 1903; FHK 353. 1861; FKH 262. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 86. 1977.

Rhizomes 2 mm in diam.; pseudobulbs erect, cylindrical, 1–2.5 cm long, 2–5 mm in diam., terminated with 1 leaf. Leaves coriaceous, oblong, 2.5–3 × 0.5–1.5 cm, apex obtuse and slightly notched. Flowers light yellow; sepals separate, lanceolate, 8–10 × 1–1.5 mm, apex acuminate, margin from the middle to apex curved inward; lateral sepals slightly longer than the odd one, adnate to the column foot at base, mentum not obvious; petals ovate-lanceolate, 4–5 × 0.5 mm, apex acuminate, margin entire; lip fleshy, lanceolate, curved outward, 1.5 × 0.5 mm, apex obtuse, grooved below the middle, with 2–3 small keels becoming a thick one from the middle to apex; column 0.5 mm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tsuen Wan, Tai Mo Shan, Sha Tin, Tai Po, Castle Peak, Lantau Island. K. K. Mark 1, 4 (CUHK); HK sheet 27295, 34409.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian.
Ecology: Rocks in forests and ravines. Flowering: May–Aug.

Bulbophyllum levinei Schltr. 齒瓣石豆蘭
Fedde Repert. Sp. Nov. 19: 389. 1924; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 25(1 – 2): 62. 1972, et Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 87, fig. 47. 1977; FRPS 19: 191, pl. 29: 7–9. 1999; FGD 7: 425. 2006; FOC 25: 417. 2009.

Rhizomes slender, prostrate; pseudobulbs aggregated at rhizomes, subcylindrical, 5–10 mm long, 2–4 mm in diam. Leaves thinly coriaceous, oblong or obovate-lanceolate, 3–4 × 0.5–0.7 cm, base attenuate into a petiole 4–10 mm, apex acute, margin slightly wavy, midrib usually impressed above. Flowers membraneous, purplish white; odd sepal ovate-lanceolate, notched, 4–5 × 1.5–2 mm, upper portion narrower and thicker, apex acute, margin denticulate; lateral sepals oblique ovate-lanceolate, 5–6 mm, same width with the odd one, upper portion thicker, base adnate to the column forming a mentum, margin entire; petals ovate-lanceolate, 3.5 × 1.5 mm, margin denticulate, apex acute; lip fleshy, grooved below the middle, curved outside and downwards, apex acute, base truncate; column 1.2 mm.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. N. H. Li 96 (CUHK); P. S. Choi 406.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian.
Ecology: Trunks along streams in forests. Flowering: May–Aug.

Bulbophyllum odoratissimum (Sm.) Lindl. 密花石豆蘭（香石豆蘭）
Gen. Sp. Orch. Pl. 55. 1830; FKH 262. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 25(1–2): 62. 1972; FRPS 19: 195, pl. 28: 8–9. 1999; FGD 7: 426, fig. 206. 2006; FOC 25: 414. 2009.
Stelis odoratissima Sm., Ress Cyclop. 34: 12. 1814.

Rizomes 2–4 mm in diam., branched; pseudobulbs subcylindrical, erect, 2.5–5 cm long, 3–6 mm in diam., terminated with 1 leaf. Leaves coriaceous, oblong, 4–13.5 × 1–2.5 cm, base attenuate, apex obtuse and notched. Flowers fragrant, white at the beginning and turning orange-yellow in the upper portion of both sepals and petals; sepals separate, lanceolate, apex obtuse or acute, margin curved inward, appearing like a narrow tube; odd sepal notched, ovate or ovate-lanceolate, 3–7 × 1.5 mm, lateral sepals 4–14 × 2 mm; petals thinner than sepals, subovate or elliptic, 1–2 × 1–1.5 mm, apex obtuse; lip orange-red, fleshy, tongue-shaped, slightly curved outward and downward, with 2 papillose keels, apex obtuse, adnate to the column foot at base, margin with tiny papillae or white hairs; column short and thick, 1 mm; column foot orangered, 1 mm.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Nai Chung. S. Y. Hu 7321A (CUHK); HK sheet 27291, 32981.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Sichuan, Yunnan, Xizang; Nepal, Sikkim, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Thailand, Laos, Vietnam.
Ecology: Bare rocks or rocks in shade in forests. Flowering: Feb.–Jun.

Bulbophyllum stenobulbon Parish & Rchb. f. 短足石豆蘭
Trans. Linn. Soc. 30: 153. 1874; FRPS 19: 194. 1999; FOC 25: 413. 2009.
Bulbophyllum youngsayeanum S. Y. Hu & Barretto, Chung Chi Journal 13(2): 29. 1976.

Rhizomes 1–1.5 mm in diam., branched, bearing a pseudobulb between 1.5–3 cm. Roots growing at the node bearing the pseudobulb. Pseudobulb erect, ovoid-cylindrical or cylindrical, 1–1.5 cm long, changeable in sizes, 3–6 mm across middle, bearing 1 leaf at the apex. Leaves leathery, oblong, 1.5–3.3 × 1 cm; base narrowed into petioles 2–3 mm; apex round-obtuse and emarginate; midrib depressed above. Scapes 1 or 2, emerged from base of pseudobulb, slender as hairs, longer than pseudobulb; racemes shortened into umbel-form, bearing 2–4 flowers; peduncle bearing 3–4 membranous-tubular sheaths; bracts 2–3 mm, ovate-lanceolate, emarginate, longer or shorter than the pedicel and ovary together, apex acute; sepals and petals pale yellow; sepals distinct, thin; the dorsal one lanceolate, 4.5–5 × 1.3–1.5 mm, ± uncurved above middle, acuminate at apex with 3 veins; petals thin, ovate, 2–2.4 × 0.8–1 mm across middle, apex obtuse, entire with 3 veins, only the middle one reaching the apex; lip orange, fleshy, tongue-like or ovate-lanceolate, flat, 2 × 0.5–0.7 mm, rounded or truncate at apex, slightly recurved, grooved at base, densely fine papillose on the back, often with 3 vertical ribs above, the sides thickened and swell up; column 1 mm, the apical teeth same height with anther, awl-like, 0.5 mm; foot very short, turning upward slightly, 1–1.3 mm, the free portion 0.3 mm; anther hemispherical, short in front.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Sha Tin. S. Y. Hu 10136, 12052 (CUHK); Y. S. Lau 1749.
Distribution: Guangdong, Yunnan; Sikkim, Bhutan, Myanmar, Thailand, Laos, Vietnam.
Ecology: Trunks or rocks in forests. Flowering: May–Jun.
Notes: The holotype specimen of B. youngsayeanum (S. Y. Hu 12052, K) was collected from Tai Mo Shan in 1969.

Calanthe graciliflora Hayata 鈎距蝦脊蘭
J. Coll. Sci. Univ. Tokyo 30: 329. 1911, et Icon. Pl. Formos. 4: 68, t. 31. 1914; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 25(3–4): 202. 1972; FRPS 18: 316. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 786. 2000; FGD 7: 418. 2006; FOC 25: 307. 2009.
Calanthe striata auct. non (Sw.) R. Br.: S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 93. 1977.

Terrestrial herb, rhizomes inconspicuous; pseudobulbs short, subovoid, covered by cataphylls and leaf sheaths. Leaves basal, elliptic or ovate-elliptic, 15–23(–33) × 6–8 cm, conspicuously plicate, base gradually attenuating into sheathing petioles, apex acuminate, glabrous at two sides. Flowers resupinate, fragrant, pale lemon-yellow, deeper towards the margin, with sepals and petals washed brownish outside; sepal similar in shape and colour, equally spaced, elliptic, 10–15 ×, 5–6 mm, apex acute; petals obovate or obovatelanceolate, 10–13 × 3–4 mm, apex acute; lip 3-lobed, white with purplish marks on lateral and midlobes; lateral lobes obovate-triangular, 3–4 mm; midlobe obovate, straight, truncate and apiculate at the middle, column 4 mm, glabrous, rounded at the apex, broadly winged on each side; anther white, ovate; pollinia 8 in 4 pairs.

Locality: Sunset Peak. S. Y. Hu 11552A (CUHK); HK sheet 32508, 34043.
Distribution: Guangdong, Hunan, Sichuan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Taiwan.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Mar.–May.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Po Kau, Pat Sin Leng, Sha Tau Kok
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Calanthe speciosa (Blume) Lindl. 二列葉蝦脊蘭
Gen. Sp. Orch. 250. 1833; Su, Quart. J. Expt. Forest. Natl. Taiwan Univ. 4(3): 87, pl. 3. 1990; FTW ed. 2, 5: 789. 2000; FOC 25: 296. 2009.
Amblyglottis speciosa Blume, Bijdr. Fl. Ned. Ind. 371. 1925.
Calanthe formosana Rolfe, Ann. Bot. 9: 157. 1895; FRPS 18: 278, pl. 48: 5. 1999; FGD 7: 415. 2006; Check List HK Plants 372. 2002; 129. 2004.
Calanthe curculigoides auct. non Lindl.: FKH 264. 1912.
Calanthe patsinensis S. Y. Hu, Chung Chi Journal 11: 13, fig. 1. 1972, et Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 25(3–4): 202. 1972, et Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 93. 1977.

Terrestrial herb, up to 120 cm tall, completely glabrous; pseudobulbs cylindrical, sheathing. Leaves distichous, oblong-elliptic or elliptic-lanceolate, 20–60(–95) × 4–6 cm, base attenuating into a long petiole, apex acuminate; petiole stout, 6–10(–20) cm, base enlarging into sheaths. Flowers yellow or yellow-orange, in a terminal raceme; sepals subequal, elliptic or ovate-lanceolate, 10–15 × 4–5 mm, apex acuminate; petals ovate-elliptic or oblong-elliptic, 10–13 × 5–6 mm, apex acute; lip adnate to the sides of the column, 3-lobed; lateral lobes ovate-triangular, 5 mm apart from each other; apical lobe fan-shaped, 5 × 5 mm, truncate, apiculate at the apex, gradually narrowed towards the base; column 3–5 mm, winged at the apex; anther elongate-conical; pollinia 8, strongly attenuate; ovary subcylindrical, subtrigonous, glabrous.

Locality: Tai Po Kau, Pat Sin Leng, Sha Tau Kok. K. K. Mark 2 (CUHK); L. T. Lo 570; Y. W. Lam 179.
Distribution: Hainan, Taiwan.
Ecology: Shade and moist places in forests. Flowering: Oct.–Nov.
Notes: The type specimen of C. patsinensis (S. Y. Hu 10013, A, holotype) was collected from Pat Sin Leng in 1970.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Victoria Peak, Ma On Shan, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Calanthe sylvatica (Thouars) Lindl. 長距蝦脊蘭（粉紅蝦脊蘭）
Gen. Sp. Orchid. Pl. 250. 1833; FRPS 18: 301. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 789. 2000; FGD 7: 416. 2006; FOC 25: 300. 2009.
Centrosis sylvatica Thouars, Hist. Orchid. pl. 35 & 36. 1822.
Bletia masuca D. Don, Prodr. Fl. Nepal 30. 1825.
Calanthe masuca (D. Don) Lindl., Gen. Sp. Orch. Pl. 249. 1833; FKH 265. 1912.
Calanthe masuca Lindl. var. sinensis Rendle, J. Bot. Brit. For. 40: 310. 1902; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 93, fig. 52. 1977.

Terrestrial herb up to 80 cm, rhizomes inconspicuous; pseudobulbs narrow conical, 1–2 cm long, 1 cm across at base. Leaves all basal, elliptic to ovate, 15–40 × 7–11 cm, base attenuate into petioles, apex acute or acuminate, margin wavy. Flowers rather large, sepals all alike in colour, delightfully bright lavender, darker on the outside; odd sepal elliptic, 18–20 × 6–10 mm, apex acute; lateral sepals oblique-elliptic or oblong, apex acute; petals obovate or oblong, lavender shading to white inside along the centre, 1.5–2.5 × 1–1.3 cm, apex obtuse or acute; lip adnate to the sides of the column, 3-lobed; lateral lobes deep purple, oblique, falcate-lanceolate, 3–5 × 1.5–2 mm; midlobe light purple, fan-shaped, 1–1.5 × 1.5–1.8 cm, the apex bilobed with an acute recurved point between the lobes; column white, waxy; anther white, ovate; pollinia 8 in 4 pairs, all white; ovary hairy, with pink ridges and green depressions.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Ma On Shan, Lantau Island. S. Y. Hu 12676 (CUHK); Y. S. Lau 1639; HK sheet 34679.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Xizang, Hunan, Taiwan; Nepal, India, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia, Japan.
Ecology: Shade and moist places in forest. Flowering: Apr.–Sep.
Uses: Ornamental.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Deep Water Bay, Sha Tin, Sha Tau Kok, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Calanthe triplicata (Willemet) Ames 三褶蝦脊蘭（白花蝦脊蘭）
Philipp. J. Sci. Bot. 2(4): 326. 1907; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 25(3–4): 207. 1972, et Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 93. 1977; FRPS 18: 308, pl. 53: 3. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 791. 2000; FGD 7: 417. 2006; FOC 25: 302. 2009.
Orchis triplicata Willemet, Usteri Ann. Bot. 18: 52. 1796.
Calanthe veratrifolia R. Br., Bot. Reg. 9: ad t. 720. 1823; FKH 265. 1912.

Perennial herb, bearing no leaf at anthesis; stems short, fleshy, consisting of 1–3 green fleshy stems; stems with 2 or 3 oblong joints, each joint 1.3–4 cm long, 1.2–3.5 cm in diam., slightly compressed, partially covered by remnants of sheaths. Leaves emerging after anthesis. Flowers white, 2–few, in a terminal raceme; stipe 35–40 cm, bracts 3 or 4, greenish, the upper ones 1.5 cm; pedicels 2–3 cm, hairy; flowers 4 cm across; dorsal sepal ovate-lanceolate, 25 × 6 mm, acute, lateral sepals similar in size and shape, turning upwards against the dorsal one; petals elliptic-oblong, 2.5 cm, apex obtuse; lip conspicuous, the lateral lobes connate to the column forming a funnel; the front lobe turning 90° upward, enlarged into a trilobed suborbicular epichile, biparted at apex.

Locality: Deep Water Bay, Sha Tin, Sha Tau Kok, Lantau Island. S. Y. Hu 10701, 13822 (CUHK); HK sheet 7097, 27424.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; tropical Asia, Australia, Madagascar.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Mar.–Jul.
Uses: Ornamental.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Victoria Peak, Shing Mun, Pat Sin Leng, Sheung Tsat Muk Kiu
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Cephalantheropsis obcordata (Lindl.) Ormerod 黃蘭（嶺南黃蘭）
Orchid Digest. 62: 157. 1998; FOC 25: 289. 2009.
Bletia obcordata Lindl., Gen. Sp. Orchid. Pl. 123. 1831.
Calanthe gracilis Lindl., Gen. Sp. Orchid. Pl. 251. 1833; FKH 254. 1912.
Cephalantheropsis gracilis (Lindl.) S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 25(3–4): 213. 1972, et Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 56, fig. 25. 1977; FRPS 18: 255, pl. 45: 7. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 795. 2000; Check List HK Plants 372. 2002; 129. 2004.
Limatodes gracilis (Lindl.) Lindl., Fol. Orchid. Limatodis 1. 1855; FHK 359. 1861.

Perennial herb. Stems cane-like growing close together on a short creeping rhizome, to 1 m tall; internodes many, 5–10 cm. Leaves 5–8, papery, oblong-lanceolate, 30 × 5–8 cm; scapes 60 cm, rachis 5–20 cm; bracts membraneous. Flowers yellow; segments oblong, 9–11 × 4 mm, hairy outside; lip trilobed, lateral lobes erect; epichile 2-lobed, crisped; column fleshy; anther terminal; pollinia 8.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Shing Mun, Pat Sin Leng, Sheung Tsat Muk Kiu. S. Y. Hu 10013, 10014 (CUHK); Y. W. Lam 502.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Myanmar, Laos, Thailand, Malaysia.
Ecology: Clinging to wet rocks in shade along streams. Flowering: Nov.–Mar. of the following year.

Cheirostylis chinensis Rolfe 中華叉柱蘭（甌蘭）
Ann. Bot. 9: 158. 1895, et J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 36: 43. 1903; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 44, fig. 16. 1977; FRPS 17: 166, pl. 21: 12–15. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 796, pl. 335. 2000; FGD 7: 355. 2006; FOC 25: 62. 2009.

Perennial saxicolous small herb; rhizomes succulent, 4.5 cm long, 1.2 cm thick; stem erect. Leaves ovate-cordate, 2.5–4 × 2–3 cm, acute. Flowers white, resupinate, 4–5 in a terminal raceme; scape 15–20 cm, villose glandular; pedicels 2–3 mm; calyx urceolate, 6–7 mm, tube 4 mm, 3-lobed, the odd lobe dorsal; petals oblique lanceolate, 5 mm; lip bilobed, base gibbous, bilobed at the apex, fringed; column 2 mm; anthers orange; pollinia 4 in 2 pairs, granular; ovary glandular-villose.

Locality: New Territories, Lantau Island. Y. W. Lam 205; HK sheet 33354.
Distribution: Guangxi, Guizhou, Taiwan; Philippines.
Ecology: Damp moss-covered rocks in forests. Flowering: May–Jun.

Cheirostylis clibborndyeri S. Y. Hu & Barreto 叉柱蘭（太魯閣叉柱蘭）
Chung Chi Journal. 13(2): 15, fig. 8. 1976; FOC 25: 60. 2009.
Cheirostylis hungyehensis T. P. Lin, Native Orch. Taiwan 2: 73(f.) 1977; FTW ed. 2, 5: 798, pl. 336. 2000.
Cheirostylis tatewakii auct. non Masam.: Masam. ex S. S. Ying, Col. Illust. Fl. Taiwan 4: 802. 1992; FRPS 17: 164. 1999; FGD 7: 355. 2006; Check List HK Plants 373. 2002; 130. 2004.

Small succulent perennial herb, 12–15 cm tall at flowering time; rhizome worm-like, 4–6 cm, fleshy, consisting of 4 to 6 internodes, those on the ends thinner. Leaves 3 or 4, terminal to the apical end; leaf blades ovate, 1–2 × 0.7–1.2 cm, green and variegated with lighter green bands, apex acute. Flowers white or greenish white, 5 or 6 in a raceme terminal to a scape of 12–15 cm; pedicels 2 or 3 mm; calyx tubular, 5 mm including the 2 mm free portions; petals white, 5 mm, oblanceolate-spathulate; lip white, unguiculate, entire, 2–5 mm, apex tongue-like, 2 mm; column 1 mm, with 2 arms at the apex, each with a gland; anther sagittate, orange; pollinia 4 in 2 pairs, granular; ovary ellipsoidal, 5 cm, glabrous. Fruit ovoid-ellipsoidal, 7 mm, with tubercles on ridges.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. S. Y. Hu 9900, 13055 (CUHK); L. T. Lo 289; Y. W. Lam 216.
Distribution: Taiwan.
Ecology: Wet rocks in shade of forest-ravines and hillslopes. Flowering: Jan–Apr.
Notes: The type specimen (S. Y. Hu 13055, K, holotype; A, CUHK, HK, PE, isotypes) was collected by R. Clibborn-Dyer from Victoria Peak on 6 Mar. 1973.

Cheirostylis jamesleungii S. Y. Hu & Barreto 粉紅叉柱蘭（毛甌蘭）
Chung Chi Journal 13(2): 13, fig. 6. 1976; FRPS 17: 166. 1999; FGD 7: 355. 2006; FOC 25: 62. 2009.

Small succulent perennial herb, before flowering, the plant consisting of a worm-like rhizome, 4–5 cm long, 2–6 mm in diam., with 6 – 7 internodes. At flowering time, a slender scape 10 cm high emerged from the apical end. Leaves 3 terminal to rhizome, petiolate; leaf blade cordate, 3–8 mm long and wide, acute, papillose. Flowers 2–3, subsessile; calyx 4 mm, oblique tubular; petals oblique-lanceolate; lip white, 2-lobed, 5 mm, 3 mm across apex, each lobe with 5–6 coarse teeth; anther dorsal; pollinia 4 in 2 pairs; ovary villose, 5 mm, pink.

Locality: Lantau Island S. Y. Hu 9720A (K).
Distribution: Endemic to Hong Kong.
Ecology: Moist places, alt. 600 m. Flowering: Mar.
Notes: The holotype specimen (S. Y. Hu 9720A, K) was collected by J. Leung from Lantau Island on 22 Mar. 1970.

Cheirostylis liukiuensis Masam. 琉球叉柱蘭
J. Soc. Trop. Agric. 2: 36. 1930; FTW ed. 2, 5: 800. 2000; FOC 25: 60. 2009.

Perennial herb, 5–9 cm tall; rhizome moniliform, 8–10 mm in diam., sometimes branching, fleshy; roots hair-like. Leaves 3–4, scattered along stem; leaf blades ovate to ovate-orbicular, 2–3 × 1–2 cm, base rounded or slightly cordate, apex acute, abaxially reddish purple, adaxially dark greyish green; petiole-like base and sheath 0.7–1 cm. Flowers white or greenish white, 5 or 7 in a terminal raceme. Peduncle hairy, initially ca. 5 cm, gradually elongate to 10 – 20 cm after anthesis; pedicels 2–3 mm; calyx tubular, pubescent, 4.5–5 mm including the 2.5 mm free portions; petals white, 4.5 mm, oblong-oblanceolate; lip white, 6 mm, tripartite; column erect, 2.2–2.4 mm, with 2 arms at the apex; anther broadly ovoid; pollinia ca. 1.2 mm; ovary ellipsoidal, pubescent.

Locality: Sha Tin (Siu 2000).
Distribution: Taiwan; Japan (Ryukyus).
Ecology: Shade of forest-ravines. Flowering: Jan.–Feb.

Cheirostylis monteiroi S. Y. Hu & Barreto 箭藥叉柱蘭（大花甌蘭）
Chung Chi Journal 13(2): 15, fig. 7. 1976; FRPS 17: 169. 1999; FGD 7: 356. 2006; FOC 25: 61. 2009.
Cheirostylis flabellata auct. non Wight: Icon. Pl. Ind. Orient. 5: 16, pl. 1727. 1852; FKH 267. 1912.

Perennial succulent saxicolous herb; rhizomes fleshy, with 4–6 internodes. Leaves 2–3, ovate, 1.2–1.6 × 0.8 –1 cm, acute or acuminate. Flowers white, 2–8 terminal to a scape of 7–9 cm; calyx tubular, without distinct sepals, glabrous, tube 3 mm; lobes 2 mm; petals white, oblique-lanceolate, 5 × 1.5 mm; lip bilobed, 4.5 mm, adnate to column, apical lobes suborbicular, 7 mm in diam., white with green centre, fringed; column 1 mm, with an anterior arm of 1.5 mm on each side; anther yellow, sagittate; pollinia 4 in 2 pairs; ovary cylindrical, 5–6 mm, glabrous.

Locality: Mount Parker, Violet Hill. S. Y. Hu 13056 (CUHK); U. A. On s.n. (HK sheet 7133).
Distribution: Endemic to Hong Kong.
Ecology: Rocks in ravine of forests, alt. 300 m. Flowering: Mar.–May.
Notes: The type specimen (S. Y. Hu 13056, K, holotype; A, CUHK, HK, PE, isotypes) was collected by R. Clibborn-Dyer from Violet Hill on 6 Mar. 1973. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Cirrhopetalum bicolor (Lindl.) Rolfe 二色卷瓣蘭（二色石豆蘭）
J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 36(249): 14. 1903; FKH 262. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 86. 1977.
Bulbophyllum bicolor Lindl., Gen. Sp. Orchid. Pl. 49. 1830; FRPS 19: 227. 1999; FGD 7: 430. 2006; FOC 25: 428. 2009; Check List HK Plants 370. 2002; 129. 2004.

Rhizome stout, 3–4 mm in diam.; pseudobulbs ovoid-spherical, 1.5–2 cm long, 8–13 mm in diam., terminated with 1 leaf. Leaves leathery, oblong, 10–15 × 2–2.5 cm, base attenuate into a petiole 1.5 cm, apex obtuse and slightly notched. Flowers light yellow, inside base with purple dots, purplish red at tips of both sepals and petals; odd sepal oblong, 15 × 10 mm, apex acuminate, margin with thick red cilia; lateral sepals oblique ovate-lanceolate, 20 × 7.5 mm, apex obtuse, twisted above the base; petals oblong, 10 × 6 mm, apex apiculate, margin entire; lip olive green, turning orange-red in later time, ovate, curved downwards, adnate to the column foot, apex obtuse.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Sha Tin. S. Y. Hu 10162 (CUHK); Y. S. Lau 1805; HK sheet 30760.
Distribution: Endemic to Hong Kong.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: May.
Notes: Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Victoria Peak, Cape D'Aguilar, Tai Mo Shan
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Cirrhopetalum delitescens (Hance) Rolfe 直唇卷瓣蘭
Gard. Chron. n. s. 18: 461. 1882; FKH 262. 1912.
Bulbophyllum delitescens Hance, J. Bot. 14(2): 44. 1876; FRPS 19: 209, pl. 32: 1. 1999; FGD 7: 429. 2006; FOC 25: 423. 2009; Check List HK Plants 371. 2002; 129. 2004.

Rhizomes stout, prostrate, 4 mm in diam.; pseudobulb ovoid or subglobose, 1.7–3.5 cm long, 5–10 mm in diam., terminated with 1 leaf. Leaves thin-leathery, oblong or elliptic, sometimes obovate-oblong, 16–25 × 3.5–6 cm, base cuneat, apex obtuse or acute. Flowers purple, odd sepal ovate, depressed to become boat-shaped, 1 × 3 mm, apex truncate and notched, with an awn to 7 mm in the middle of the notch, margin entire; lateral sepals narrowly lanceolate, 6 × 0.2 cm, apex acuminate, adnate to the column foot, twisted above the base, upper and lower margins connate; petals falcate-lanceolate, 5–7 × 1.5–2 mm, apex truncate and notched, with an awn in the middle of the notch, margin entire; lip fleshy, tongue-like, recurved, 5 mm, apex obtuse, base grooved and adnate to the column foot, glabrous; column 3 mm, winged.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Cape D'Aguilar, Tai Mo Shan. HK sheet 7065, 27305, 34047.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Yunnan, Xizang, Fujian; India, Vietnam.
Ecology: Trunks and rocks in forests. Flowering: Feb.–Jul.
Notes: The type specimens were collected by J. Lamont and C. Ford from Victoria Peak before 1876.

Cirrhopetalum miniatum Rolfe 斑唇卷瓣蘭
Bull. Misc. Inform. Kew. 1913(1): 28. 1913; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 186. 1977.
Bulbophyllum pecten-veneris (Gagnep.) Seidenf., Dansk Bot. Ark. 29(1): 37. 1973, et Opera Bot. 114: 278, fig. 182. 1992; FRPS 19: 233. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 771. 2000; FGD 7: 430. 2006; FOC 25: 433. 2009; Check List HK Plants 371. 2002; 129. 2004.

Rhizomes 1–2 mm in diam., prostrate; pseudobulbs ovoid-spherical, 5–12 mm long, 5–10 mm in diam., terminated with 1 leaf. Leaves thickly leathery, elliptic, oblong-lanceolate or ovate, 1–6 × 0.7–1.8 cm, apex obtuse or sometimes slightly retuse. Flowers yellowish green or yellow with some brown colour; odd sepal ovate, notched, 5 × 2.5 mm, apex acute, margin above base with fimbriate hairs; lateral sepals narrowly lanceolate, 3.5–5 × 0.25 cm, apex long and caudate, base adnate to the column foot, twisted above the base, upper and lower margins connate to each other, margins curved inwards, attenuate to apex forming a long tail-like tube; petals oblique ovate, 2.5–3 × 1.5 mm, apex acute, margins above middle with fimbriate hairs; lip fleshy, tongue-like, curved outwards and downwards, 2.5 mm, apex acute, glabrous; column 2 mm.

Locality: Sha Tin (Siu 2000).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangxi, Hubei, Anhui, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam, Laos.
Ecology: Trunks and rocks in forests. Flowering: Apr.–Sep.

Cirrhopetalum tigridum (Hance) Rolfe 虎斑卷瓣蘭
J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 36(249): 15. 1903; FKH 262. 1912.
Bulbophyllum tigridum Hance, J. Bot. 21(8): 232. 1883; FGD 7: 428. 2006; FOC 25: 427. 2009.
Bulbophyllum retusiusculum Rchb. f. var. tigridum (Hance) Z. H. Tsi, Guihaia 15(2): 108. 1995; FRPS 19: 222. 1999; Check List HK Plants 371. 2002; 129. 2004.

Rhizomes prostrate, 2 mm in diam.; pseudobulbs ovoid-conical, 5–25 mm long, 4–13 mm in diam., terminated with 1 leaf. Leaves leathery, oblong or ovate-lanceolate, 1.5–8 × 0.5–2 cm, base attenuate into a short petiole, apex obtuse and slightly notched. Flowers small, dull red with purplish red veins; odd sepal oblong-ovate or subrectangular, apex subtruncate; lateral sepals lanceolate or linear, 5–7 mm, apex acuminate, adnate to the column foot at base; petals subequal to the odd sepal, apex obtuse, adnate to the column foot at base; lip fleshy, tongue-like, curved outwards and downwards, apex obtuse, grooved near base; column winged, wider near base; column foot curved upwards.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. G. Barretto 137; HK sheet 27310.
Distribution: Guangdong.
Ecology: Rocks or trunks in forests. Flowering: Sep.–Nov.

Cirrhopetalum tseanum S. Y. Hu & Barretto 香港卷瓣蘭
Chung Chi Journal 13(2): 30, fig. 14. 1976; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 84. 1977.
Bulbophyllum tseanum (S. Y. Hu & Barretto) Z. H. Tsi, FRPS 19: 239. 1999; FGD 7: 432. 2006; FOC 25: 434. 2009; Check List HK Plants 371. 2002; 129. 2004.

Saxicolous orchid; root fibrous, many; rhizomes creeping, 3 mm in diam., covered by straw-like scales; pseudobulbs oblique-ovoid, 1–1.5 cm long, 6 – 8 mm across the base. Leaves solitary, petiolate, petioles 3–7 mm, folded, articulate at base; leaf blades thick, leathery, oblong, 4–7 × 1.7–2.5 cm, base obtuse, apex rotundate and retuse, midrib impressed above, hardly visible beneath. Flowers 4 or 5 in a subumbelliform raceme terminal to the scape, bracts subulate, 3 mm, acuminate and apiculate; odd sepal cucullate, 5 × 4 mm, light yellow and uniformly crimson-lake along the margin, ciliate, hairs dark red, apex extending forward to a caudate filiform process, 4 mm; lateral sepals oblique, twisted, turning upwards with the upper margins meeting in front of the lip, to form a tongue-like elliptic blade, 1.8–2 × 0.7–0.8 cm, densely mottled dull purplish red and light yellow, margin yellow, recurved, apex retuse; petals obliqueovate, 4 × 2.5 mm, light yellow, dark red along the margin, ciliate and acuminate, apex filiform, 4 mm; lip attached to the apex of the long mentum, movable, glossy orange, fleshy, tongue-like, recurved, with a median longitudinal ridge and a groove along each side; column 3 mm, stout and winged on each side; pollinia 4 in 2 pairs; ovary obconical, 2 mm.

Locality: Sha Tin, Sha Tau Kok (Siu 2000).
Distribution: Endemic to Hong Kong.
Ecology: Rocks in forests. Flowering: Mar.–Apr.
Notes: The holotype specimen (S. Y. Hu 13586, K) was collected by S. C. Tse from Pat Sin Leng in 1974.

Cleisostoma paniculatum (Ker Gawl.) Garay 大序隔距蘭
Bot. Mus. Leafl. Harvard Univ. 23(4): 173. 1972; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 115. 1977; FRPS 19: 323, pl. 47: 11–14. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 808, pl. 341. 2000; FGD 7: 493, fig. 254. 2006; FOC 25: 461. 2009.
Aerides paniculata Ker Gawl., Bot. Reg. 3: t. 220. 1817.
Sarcanthus cerinus (Hance) Rolfe, J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 36: 36. 1903; FKH 266. 1912.
Cleisostoma cerinum Hance, J. Bot. 20: 359. 1882.

Monopodial herb; stems erect, compressed cylindrical, 18–25 cm tall. Leaves band-like, apex retuse or bilobed, the longest 14 cm. Inflorescence a panicle with many small flowers; flowers yellow, with 2 fairly broad bands of lilac-mauve on sepals and petals; odd sepal dorsal, oblong, 6 × 3.5 mm, apex obtuse; lateral ones oblique-oblong, 4.5 × 3 mm, apex acute, pointing upwards; petals linearoblong, 4 × 1.7 mm, apex obtuse; lip 5 mm, with a unicorn-like callus at the entrance and continued downwards to the spur, as a membrane-like partition; column 3 mm; anther cap 2-lobed; pollinia 4 in 2 pairs, attached to a horse-shoe-like viscid disk by a wide stipe; stigma pear-shaped, situated beneath the rostellum; ovary and pedicel 6 mm.

Locality: Lantau Island. HK sheet 27571, 34211.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Xizang, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan; Thailand, Vietnam, NE India.
Ecology: Trunks or rocks in forests. Flowering: May–Sep.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Fo Tan Valley, Tai Mo Shan, Nam Chung, Yi O
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Cleisostoma rostratum (Lodd. ex Lindl.) Garay 尖喙隔距蘭（福氏隔距蘭）
Bot. Mus. Leafl. 23: 174. 1972; FOC 25: 460. 2009.
Sarcanthus rostratus Lodd. ex Lindl., Coll. Bot. ad pl. 39B. 1826.
Cleisostoma fordii Hance, J. Bot. Brit. For. 14: 45. 1875; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 115, fig. 69. 1977; Check List HK Plants 373. 2002; 130. 2004.
Cleisostoma rostratum (Lodd. ex Lindl.) Seidef. ex Averyanov, Vasc. Pl. Syn. Vietnam. Fl. 1: 53. 1990, et Iden. Guide Vietnam. Orch. 376. 1994; FRPS 19: 319. 1999; FGD 7: 492. 2006, nom. illeg. prior.
Sarcanthus fordii (Hance) Rolfe, J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 36: 37. 1903; FKH 266. 1912.

Epiphytic or saxicolous; roots wire-like, light grey, greyish green when mature, slightly compressed; stems subterete, dark green, longitudinally striate below the insertion of the leaf blades and horizontally wrinkled elsewhere. Leaves distichous, dark green, rather fleshy, stiff, linear-lanceolate, 8–14 × 1–1.6 cm, midrib narrowly compressed above, distinctly elevated below, base cuneate and distinctly articulate, apex suddenly constricted and long acuminate. Flowers resupinate, erect; sepals and petals similar in colour and design, apex acute, yellowish green with 2 carminered bands on each side; odd sepal dorsal, elliptic, 7 × 3 mm, concave and arcuate; lateral ones rather low, in line with the lip, oblique obovate-elliptic, 6 × 3 mm, reflexed; petals laterally partitioned, pointing slightly forward, oblong, 6 × 2.5 mm; lip calcarate, 3-lobed, lilac-mauve, white at base, lateral lobes erect, cuspidate at apex, midlobe folded along the sides and curved upwards forming a beak-like structure, with a fleshy tongue-like callus; column white, fleshy, apex truncate, slightly narrowed at the centre; anther cordate and beak-like at apex; pollinia 4 in 2 pairs; ovary very small, 2–3 mm.

Locality: Fo Tan Valley, Tai Mo Shan, Nam Chung, Yi O. K. Y. Chan 1373 (CUHK); Y. S. Lau 1765; Y. W. Lam 944.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan; Thailand, Laos, Vietnam.
Ecology: Trunks and rocks in forests. Flowering: Jul.–Aug.

Cleisostoma simondii (Gagnep.) Seidenf. var. guangdongense Z. H. Tsi 廣東隔距蘭（柱葉隔距蘭）
Bull. Bot. Res. 3(4): 84, fig. 1. 1983; FRPS 19: 330. 1999; FGD 7: 492. 2006; FOC 25: 463. 2009.
Sarcanthus teretifolius auct. non (Lindl.) Lindl.: FKH 266. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 28 (1, 2): 156. 1975.

Epiphytic herb, to 50 cm tall; stems 4 mm in diam., branched. Leaves terete, 7–11 cm, 3 mm in diam., apex obtuse. Flowers having the size and shape of a bee, in axillary racemes; dorsal sepal rounded; lateral sepals and petals oblong, all greenish marked with red longitudinal lines, apex rounded; lip saccate, lateral lobes erect, midlobe oblong; apex triangular-acute, white with pink veins. Column 3 mm. Capsules cylindrical, 3.5 × 0.6 cm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. S. Y. Hu 9754, 12294B (CUHK); K. L. Yip 4518.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Fujian.
Ecology: Trunks in forests. Flowering: May–Nov.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Ma On Shan
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Cleisostoma williamsonii (Rchb. f.) Garay 紅花隔距蘭
Bot. Mus. Leafl. 23: 176. 1972; FRPS 19: 324. 1999; FGD 7: 491. 2006; FOC 25: 462. 2009.
Sarcanthus williamsonii Rchb. f., Gard. Chron. 674. 1865.
Cleisostoma hongkongense (Rolfe) Garay, Bot. Mus. Leafl. 23(4): 172. 1972.
Sarcanthus hongkongensis Rolfe, Kew Bull. 1898: 198. 1898; J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 36: 37. 1903; FKH 266. 1912; FHN 4: 262. 1977.

Epiphytic herb, to 70 cm tall; stems 3–4 mm in diam., branched or unbranched, internodes 1–2.5 cm. Leaves terete, 6–10 cm × 2–3 mm, apex obtuse. Racemes or panicles lateral; bracts ovate-lanceolate, ca. 2 mm. Flowers pale lilac, opening widely, dorsal sepal ovate-elliptic, cymbiform, ca. 2.2 × 1.5 mm, rounded; lateral sepals ovate-elliptic, ca. 2.5 × 1.5 mm, apex obtuse. Petals oblong, ca. 2.2 × 1 mm; lip saccate, lateral lobes erect, ligulate-oblong; midlobe narrowly ovate-triangular, fleshy, adaxially with a ridge raised and triangular near spur entrance; spur globose, ca. 2 mm in diam. Column ca. 2 mm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Ma On Shan. C. Ford s.n. (K); HK sheet 34049.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan; NE India to Indochina and Indonesia.
Ecology: Trunks in forests. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.
Notes: The type specimen of Sarcanthus hongkongensis (C. Ford. s.n.) was collected from Hong Kong before 1893. Rolfe (1903) noted that “the flowers are pale lilac, with the column, the side-lobes of the lip, and the base of the front lobes bright purple”.

Coelogyne fimbriata Lindl. 流蘇貝母蘭
Bot. Reg. 11: t. 868. 1825; FHK 354. 1861; FKH 264. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 83, fig. 45. 1977; FRPS 18: 344, pl. 57: 3–4. 1999; FGD 7: 463, fig. 232. 2006; FOC 25: 318. 2009.

Creeping terrestrial herb; rhizomes 2–3 mm thick consisting of 8–10 internodes; annual growth consisting of a rhizome ending with an oblong or ellipsoidal pseudobulb of 3–4 × 1–2 cm, terminated with 2 leaves. Leaves petiolate, petioles 5–6 mm; leaf blades oblong-elliptic, 4.5–10 × 1.5–2 cm, apex acute. Flowers lemon-yellow, 2 (sometimes 1 or 3) terminal to a short scape of 2–3 cm; sepals alike, oriented in an equal triangle, ovate, 2 × 0.8–0.9 cm, apex acute; petals linear, 2 × 0.2 cm; lip with fimbriate apical lobe, yellow and marked with cinnamon-brown lines and patches on the side; column 12–13 mm, winged; anther conical; pollinia 4 in 2 pairs; ovary 4 × 2 mm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. S. Y. Hu 6176, 11094 (CUHK); G. Barretto 316.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Xizang, Jiangxi; Sikkim, India, Vietnam, Thailand, Laos, Cambodia, Malaysia.
Ecology: Tree trunks or large rocks in forests. Flowering: Mar.–Dec.

Coelogyne leungiana S. Y. Hu 單唇貝母蘭
Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 25: 223, fig. 9a–e. 1972, et Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 84. 1977; FRPS 18: 341. 1999; FGD 7: 463. 2006; FOC 25: 318. 2009.

Epiphytic herb, rhizomes elongate, 1 mm thick, branched; pseudobulbs oblong-ellipsoidal, 2–4 × 0.8–1.5 cm, the base subtended by scales of 1–2 cm. Leaves petiolate, petioles 6–8 mm; leaf blades oblong-elliptic, 5–8 × 1.3–2.5 cm, apex acute. Flowers yellow, 1 or 2 apical to a scape of 2.5–3.5 cm; pedicels 3–4 mm; sepals and petals similar, ovate-lanceolate, 2 cm; lip entire, ovate-lanceolate, 2 × 0.7 cm across middle; column narrowly winged, 1.4 cm; anther ovoid, 3 mm across middle; pollinia 4 in 2 pairs; ovary subturbinate, 3–4 mm.

Locality: Pat Sin Leng. S. Y. Hu 11004, 12454 (CUHK).
Distribution: Endemic to Hong Kong.
Ecology: Exposed rocks. Flowering: Mar.–Dec.
Notes: The type specimen was collected by J. Leung from New Territories in 1969.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Violet Hill, Sai Kung
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Cryptostylis arachnites (Blume) Hassk. 隱柱蘭
Cat. Bog. 8. 1844; FKH 268. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 39, fig. 13. 1977, et Enum. Sperm. Hong Kong 102. 2002; FRPS 17: 237. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 819. 2000; FGD 7: 346, fig. 147. 2006.
Zosterostylis arachnites Blume, Bijdr. 419. 1825.
Cryptostylis arachnites (Blume) Blume, Coll. Orchid. 133. 1859; FOC 25: 89. 2009.

Terrestrial herb, 25–30 cm tall at flowering time. Leaves petiolate; petioles 4–12 cm; leaf blades ovate-elliptic, 8–11 × 3.5–5.5 cm, apex acuminate and apiculate, with many lateral veins running to the apex, purple-green beneath. Flowers very unusual; sepals 3, widely separate, linear, acuminate, light green, 1.2–1.3 × 0.2 cm at base, margin in-rolled, the lateral ones 2.5 cm between apices, the odd one shorter; petals shorter than sepals, lanceolate, aculeate, pale green, 7–8 mm, margin in-rolled; lip ovate, erect, reflexed, base concave and slightly saccate, apex acute, 1.2–1.3 × 0.6–0.8 cm, completely covered with velvet red-brown hairs, lemon-yellow, with 5 brown veins running palmately from base to margin and apex, with some red-brown patches; column 0.5 mm, with a glandular auricle on each side; anther erect, 2 mm, cap yellow and papillose; pollinia 4 in 2 pairs, viscidium violet; stigma large, discoid, covering the entire front of the column; ovary glabrous, 8 mm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Violet Hill, Sai Kung. HK sheet 7134.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Taiwan; SE & S Asia, Pacific islands.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Mar.–Apr.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan, Fo Tan Valley, High Island Reservoir, Tung Chung
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Cymbidium ensifolium (L.) Sw. 建蘭
Nov. Acta Soc. Sci. Upsal. 6: 77. 1799; FHK 357. 1861; FKH 265. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 98, fig. 55. 1977; FFJ 6: 616. 1995; FRPS 18: 213. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 823. 2000; FGD 7: 395, fig. 195. 2006; FOC 25: 274. 2009.
Epidendrum ensifolium L., Sp. Pl. 2: 954. 1753.
Cymbidium xiphiifolium Lindl., Bot. Reg. 7: t. 529. 1821; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 96. 1977.

Terrestrial herb; pseudobulbs very small, ovoid, subterranean. Leaves grass-like, tufted, linear, 50–70 cm. Flowers fragrant, 3–5 cm across, racemose, on scapes as long as leaves; sepals spreading, white tinged green, occasionally lined red near base; petals white, shorter and wider than sepals, forming a roof over the column; lip pale yellow or white with irregular red blotches, the midlobe papillose, recurved. Column short, hidden by the petals.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan, Fo Tan Valley, High Island Reservoir, Tung Chung. K. K. Mark 13(2404) (CUHK); S. Y. Hu 8212 (CUHK); Y. W. Lam 126.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian; widely distributed in SE and S Asia.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Jun.–Dec.
Uses: Ornamental.

Cymbidium kanran Makino 寒蘭
Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 16: 10. 1902; FRPS 18: 217. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 828. 2000; FGD 7: 386. 2006; FOC 25: 275. 2009.

Terrestrial herb; pseudobulbs narrowly ovoid, ± compressed. Leaves usually 4–5 on pseudobulb, linear, 40–70 × 0.9–1.7 cm, dark green, thinly leathery. Scape arising from base of pseudobulb, 25–60–(80) cm. Racemes 10- or more-flowered; bracts linear-lanceolate, 2.5–3 × 0.3–0.4 cm; pedicel and ovary 20–25(–30) mm. Flowers fragrant, 3–5 cm across, variable in colour; sepals and petals pale yellowish green with purplish red striations; lip yellowish, mottled purplish red; petals narrowly ovate or ovate-lanceolate, 20–30 × 5–10 mm; lip obovate obscurely 3-lobed. Column whitish, 10–17 mm, with reddish spots on ventral side.

Locality: Ma On Shan. Y. W. Lam 1189.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, SE Xizang, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, Korea.
Ecology: Forests, streamsides. Flowering: Aug.–Dec.
Uses: Ornamental.

Cymbidium lancifolium Hook. 兔耳蘭
Exot. Bot. 1: t. 51. 1823; FRPS 18: 225, pl. 36: 3. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 829. 2000; FGD 7: 384, fig. 194. 2006; FOC 25: 278. 2009.

Terrestrial herb; pseudobulbs ellipsoidal, slightly compressed, 4–5 cm long, 10 cm across one way, 6 cm across the other. Leaves petiolate, 2–4 terminal to pseudobulbs; petioles slender, folded, faintly articulate; leaf blades dark green, elliptic, 10–19 × 3.5–4.5 cm, base gradually attenuate to the folded petiole, apex shortly acuminate or acute, midrib impressed above and elevated beneath, lateral veins obscure above, evident beneath. Inflorescences racemose, light green; flowers pale green, creamy white, with red and purple blotches and streaks; sepals uniformly pale green with a satin sheen, linear-lanceolate, 3.5 × 0.5 cm, slightly recurved; petals oblique-lanceolate, 2.5 × 0.7 cm, inner margin slightly overlapping, creamy white with a conspicuous purplish red longitudinal median line within; lip fleshy, delicately creamy white; lateral lobes erect, brilliant purplish red suffused with creamy white on inner sides; midlobe oblong-ovate, apex obtuse and strongly recurved, irregularly and sparsely marked with red patches; column arching, creamy white, inconspicuously diffused pink at the back, with red lines and streaks at the front; anther subglobose, yellowish, papillose; pollinia 4 in 2 pairs.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. HK sheet 34239, 35993.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Hunan, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, India, Indonesia.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.
Uses: Ornamental.

Cymbidium maclehoseae S. Y. Hu 冬月蘭
Chung Chi Journal 11: 15, fig. 2. 1972; FRPS 18: 225. 1999; FGD 7: 384, fig. 194. 2006; FOC 25: 278. 2009, pro syn. sub C. lancifolium.

Large terrestrial herb; pseudobulbs elongate-ellipsoidal, 8–10 cm long, 1.5–1.7 cm in diam. Leaves petiolate, petioles equitant, lower portion sheathing, upper part subcylindrical-canaliculate; leaf blades elliptic, 13–21 × 3.5–5.5 cm, base cuneate, apex acute, midrib impressed above and elevated beneath. Inflorescences racemose, lateral to the pseudobulb; flowers greenish cream-white; sepals lanceolate, 2.5 × 0.4 cm, basal one-third recurved; petals lanceolate, 2.2 × 0.45 cm, slightly oblique and falcate at base, basal one-fourth faintly purple-lined on the inside; lip irregularly purple maculate; lateral lobes erect, narrow, fleshy; midlobe tongue-like, recurved and rolling backward, trough deeply grooved along the median longitudinal line, fleshy; column slightly arcuate, cream-white, maculate purple on the flat front surface; anther subglobose; pollinia 4 in 2 pairs.

Locality: New Territories. S. Y. Hu 9369 (A).
Distribution: Known only from Hong Kong.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Dec. (fide Hu, 1972)
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: The holotype specimen (S. Y. Hu 9369, A) was collected by S. Y. Hu from New Territories in 1969. The species has been synonymised under Cymbidium lancifolium Hook. s.l. by some authors (e.g. FOC 25: 278. 2009).

Cymbidium sinense (Jacks. ex Andrews) Willd. 墨蘭（報歲蘭）
Sp. Pl. ed. 4. 111. 1805; FHN 4: 246. 1977; FRPS 18: 215. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 831. 2000; FGD 7: 386. 2006; FOC 25: 274. 2009.

Terrestrial herb; pseudobulbs ovoid, 3 cm long, 2 cm in diam. Leaves narrow-linear, shorter than the scape. Flowers 5 cm in diam., in racemes above the foliage, on greenish-brown rachis; sepals and petals lanceolate, pale-yellow, faintly red-lined, red toward base; lip red, narrowly yellow along the margin, yellow patched with white-centre at base, without distinct lateral lobes; column short, white.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Sunset Peak. S. Y. Hu 9492, 11504 (CUHK); HK sheet 34337.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou, Hunan, Jiangxi, Anhui, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Burma, Myanmar, Laos, Vietnam, Cambodia, Thailand, Japan (Ryukyu).
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Jan.–Feb.
Uses: Ornamental.

Dendrobium aduncum Wall. ex Lindl. 鈎狀石斛
Bot. Reg. 28(Misc): 58. 1842; FKH 261. 1912; FRPS 19: 123, pl. 15: 3–4. 1999; FGD 7: 411. 2006; FOC 25: 389. 2009.
Dendrobium hercoglossum auct. non Rchb. f.: S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 59, et 122, fig. 73-B. 1977.

Root fibrous, many- and much branched; stem cylindrical, hanging, up to 70 cm or longer, consisting of 35 or more joints, bearing 2–10 leaves at apex. Leaves distichous, petiolate; petioles sheathed, 15–30 mm; leaf blades oblong-lanceolate, conduplicate in bud, 7–9 × 1.7–2.7 cm, base convex, apex acute or short-acuminate, midrib impressed above, elevated beneath, secondary veins many, parallel from base to apex. Inflorescence a short 2–5-flowered raceme; flowers rosy-lavender, darker along the margin; the odd sepal ovate-lanceolate, 2 × 0.8 cm, apex acute; lateral ones widely separate, 3.3 cm between apices, oblique-ovate, base connate and adnate to the column foot forming an inflated sac-like mentum; petals elliptic, 18 × 8 mm, apex acuminate, base cuneate; lip semi-urceolate, unguiculate, jade-white, ciliate both along the front and back margins; column short, thick, subconical, extending into a curved foot, apex truncate and slightly winged, base of the front with brilliant dark violet papillose; anther globose, bilobate, deep violet, densely papillose; pollinia 4 in 2 pairs; ovary striate, curved.

Locality: Sha Tin. S. Y. Hu 13824; HK sheet 27202, 34336.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou, Hunan; Vietnam, Thailand, Myanmar, India.
Ecology: Trunks in forests. Flowering: Jun.–Aug.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal (folklore).

Dendrobium loddigesii Rolfe 美花石斛
Gard. Chron. ser. 3. 2: 155. 786. 1887, et J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 36: 12. 1903; FKH 261. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 60, fig. 28. 1977; FRPS 19: 104, pl. 15: 2. 1999; FGD 7: 443. 2006; FOC 25: 379. 2009.

Rots slender, 6–12 originated from a node; stem slender, annual growth 3–25 cm long, the longer ones with 20 nodes, each 8–17 mm long. Leaves fleshy, alternate, ovate-oblong or elliptic, 15–35 × 5–11 mm, base obtuse, shortly pedicellate or subsessile, apex acute, leaf sheath 3–4 mm, midrib impressed above, plane beneath, lateral veins inconspicuous. Flower solitary, occurring on a very short, slender lateral branchlet; sepals lavender-pink, lighter at base, darker at apex; odd sepal dorsal, ovate-lanceolate, 2 × 0.6 cm, slightly reflexed along the margins, base truncate, apex acute; lateral ones triangular-lanceolate, 2.5 × 0.9 cm, adnate to the column foot forming a mentum with the lower margins forming a horizontal line; petals oblong-obovate, 23 × 12 mm, colour same as sepals; lip shelllike, with a saccate base attached to the foot, completely covering the column, apex enlarging, apron-like, margin heavily fringed, central portion deep orange-yellow, bordered by a white halo, turning to deep lavender-pink along the fringed margin; column superior, subconical, jade-white, apex truncate with a triangular lobe on each side, base brilliantly purple with a white median longitudinal line in front; anther creamy white, compressed, globose, with filament, papillose throughout; pollinia 4 in 2 pairs, waxy, golden.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Lantau Island. S. Y. Hu 13273; HK sheet 37603.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan; Laos, Vietnam.
Ecology: Trunks or rocks in forests. Flowering: Mar.–May.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal (folklore).
Notes: Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Dendrobium spatella Rchb. f. 劍葉石斛
Hamburger Garten-Blumenzeitung 21: 298. 1865; FOC 25: 396. 2009.
Dendrobium acinaciforme auct. non Roxb.: FRPS 19: 142, pl. 21: 1–2. 1999; FGD 7: 439. 2006; Check List HK Plants 374. 2002; 130. 2004.

Small tufted saxicolous herb; roots fibrous, stringy and strong; rhizomes horizontal, closely knotted; stem upright, 5–7 cm tall, with up to 20 joints. Leaves closely arranged in 2 ranks, fleshy, scimitar-like, articulate at base, 25–40 × 4–6 mm, apex acute, green, turning dull purple with exposure to strong sunshine and cold dry weather. Flowers solitary, about 2 occurring on small lateral branchlets on the subapical leafless nodes of a mature leafy shoot; sepals pale rosy mauve, the odd one ovate, oblique, broad triangular-ovate, 3 mm across the middle, the basal fused portion extended downwards into a curved mentum 6–7 mm; petals ivory-white, oblique-ovate, 2 mm, acute, inconspicuously 3-veined; lip free from the apex of the mentum, deltoid, cuneate, 9 – 10 mm, the margin of the basal one-third involute, rosy purple, the enlarged apical portion wavy, 6–8 mm wide, white, tinged pale mauve and dusted with rosy mauve dots, notched, and with yellow crest at the centre, overlaid with many rosy mauve specks; column white, short and stout, 2 mm long including the foot; anthers subglobose, 2-lobed, papillose; pollinia 4 in 2 oblong pairs; ovary small, obconical, inconspicuously 6-striate.

Locality: Lantau Island. S. Y. Hu & K. H. Yung 233.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian; Myanmar, Laos, Vietnam, Cambodia, Thailand, India.
Ecology: Trunks or rocks in forests. Flowering: May–Jun.
Uses: Ornamental.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Violet Hill, The Peak, Wong Nai Chung, Mount Kellett, Pok Fu Lam Country Park
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Diploprora championii (Lindl.) Hook. f. 蛇舌蘭
Fl. Brit. Ind. 6: 26. 1890, et Hook., Icon. Pl. 2: t. 2120. 1892; FHK 357. 1861; FKH 266. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 26(3–4): 375. 1973, et Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 108, fig. 62. 1977; FRPS 19: 282, pl. 43: 3–4. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 854, pl. 362. 2000; FGD 7: 489, fig. 252. 2006; FOC 25: 448. 2009.
Cottonia championii Lindl., J. Bot. Kew (Misc.) 7: 35. 1855; FHK 357. 1861.

Monopodial herb; roots cord-like, grooved, 15 cm or longer, 2 mm in diam.; stem leafy, green, slightly compressed and zig-zag. Leaves sessile, fleshy, evergreen, distichous, oblong or oblonglanceolate, 4–8 × 1.2–2.2 cm, base oblique or slightly twisted, apex acute, slightly recurved, midrib impressed above, elevated beneath. Inflorescence a hanging raceme; flowers 3–8 on a rachis; sepals and petals pale cream to yellow, deepening with age, wide spread, apex obtuse; odd sepal dorsal, plane, oblong-ovate, 9–10 × 5 mm, truncate at base; lateral sepals ovate-elliptic, 8 × 5 mm, apex tinged pink; petals oblique-oblong, 8 × 3.5 mm; lip suborbicular, with the margin raised forming a shallow saucer, base uneven with a flat floor, elevated in middle with lower lateral and apical sides depressed, delicately lavender-pink with bright yellow patches within, the front extending into a filiform process, triangular at base, forked at apex; column lilac, short, thick and smooth, rounded at the back and apex; anther globose, lavender, apex pointed; pollinia 4 in 2 pairs, globose, waxy.

Locality: Violet Hill, The Peak, Wong Nai Chung, Mount Kellett, Pok Fu Lam Country Park. S. Y. Hu 9349, 11663A (CUHK); Y. S. Lau 1766; P. S. Choi 222.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; Sikkim, India, Myanmar, Thailand, Vietnam.
Ecology: Trees or rocks in shade areas in forests. Flowering: Feb.–Aug.; fruiting: Mar.–Sep.
Notes: The type specimen was collected by J. G. Champion from Victoria Peak between 1847 and 1850.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Kowloon Peak, Ma On Shan, Sunset Peak, Lantau Peak
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Disperis lantauensis S. Y. Hu 香港雙袋蘭（象鼻蘭）
Chung Chi Journal 11(1): 17, fig. 3(a–c). 1972; Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 26(3–4): 376. 1973; Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 36, fig. 11. 1977; FRPS 17: 494. 1999 [“D. nantauensis”]; Kurzweil, Blumea 50: 145. 2005 & FOC 25: 165. 2009, pro syn. sub Disperis neilgherrensis Wight (1851).

Perennial terrestrial herb, 5 cm tall at flowering time, with an underground corm 4 mm in diam. Leaves cauline, sessile, ovate, 4 mm long and wide, entire, acute. Flowers solitary or two, terminal to stem; dorsal sepal erect, orbicular, 4 mm in diam.; petals oblique elliptic, 2 mm, base oblique cuneate, apex acute, forming a shield with the dorsal sepal, lateral sepals connate at base, 5 mm between apex, each with an obtuse spur; ovary and pedicel forming a cylinder of 6 mm.

Locality: Kowloon Peak, Ma On Shan, Sunset Peak, Lantau Peak. G. Barretto 295.
Distribution: Endemic to Hong Kong.
Ecology: Grassy mountain slopes. Flowering: Jul.
Notes: The holotype specimen (S. Y. Hu 10812, A) was collected by S. Y. Hu from Sunset Peak, Lantau Island on 30 Jul. 1970. Some authors (e.g. Seidenfaden, Bot. Tidsskr. 65: 103. 1969; Kurzweil, 2005) adopted a broad species concept which included all Asian species under the synonymy of Disperis neilgherrensis, sensu lato, which is known for the high variability in characters used previously to delimit such taxa.

Epipogium roseum (D. Don) Lindl. 虎舌蘭
J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 1: 177. 1857; Barretto, Mem. Hong Kong Nat. Hist. Soc. 18: 47, fig. 1. 1988; FRPS 18: 43. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 863. 2000; FGD 7: 334, fig. 163. 2006; FOC 25: 208. 2009.
Limodorum roseum D. Don, Prodr. Fl. Nepal. 30. 1825.

Saprophytic herb, pink-white, lacking chlorophyll, 30–40 cm tall at flowering time; rhizome fusiform, 2–3 ×1–1.5 cm; upright stems, 20–30 cm tall, bearing scale-like bracts and terminal racemes. Flowers white to pink, pedicellate, resupinate, nutant after anthesis, about 10 in a raceme; bracts longer than ovary; pedicels 2 mm, bending; sepals and petals alike, ovate-lanceolate, 8–12 × 2–4 mm; lip white with irregular patches of rose-mauve, ovate, 8–10 mm, trowel-shaped, spur clavate, 5.5 mm; column 3.5–4 mm, apex auriculate; anther fleshy; pollinia 2, glandular. Capsule oblong, 7 mm.

Locality: Victoria Peak. HK sheet 34554.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Yunnan, Xizang, Taiwan; Nepal, Sikkim, India, Thailand, E Himalayan regions, then eastward to the Philippines and Australia.
Ecology: Shade places in forests. Flowering: May.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Mount Parker, Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Eria corneri Rchb. f. 半柱毛蘭
Gard. Chron. n. s. 2: 106. 1878; FKH 263. 1912; FRPS 19: 15. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 864, photo 109. 2000; FGD 7: 400. 2006; FOC 25: 345. 2009.

Roots wire-like, young portion densely hairy, older ones branched; stems very short, obscured by the aggregated pseudobulbs; pseudobulbs subtetragonous, compressed-ovoid. Leaves 2, persistent on 2-year-old pseudobulb; petioles 1.5–2 × 0.8 cm, slightly folded; leaf blades linear-lanceolate, 15–25 × 2.7–5.5 cm, attenuate at both ends, apex acuminate, cuspidate at the tip; midrib plane above, elevated beneath, with 2 major veins parallel on each side. Inflorescence a scape, 10–15 cm, furnished with 3 imbricate scales at the base, a sterile bract at the middle and a terminal raceme of 6–50 flowers; bracts caducous; flowers cream-white, tinged yellow at the apices of the sepals, petals and the mentum; odd sepal dorsal, linear-lanceolate, 13–14 × 2.5 mm, apex obtuse; lateral sepals obliqueovate, united with the column foot forming the mentum, the lower margin shorter and strongly curved; petals linear-falcate, 10–11 × 2 mm, apex round; lip movable, 3-lobed, cream-white, speckled reddish purple, curved, the lateral lobes erect, short and broad, midlobe ovate-subrotundate, lamellate, margin erose; column subcylindrical, 3 × 1.5 mm, the foot 5 mm; anther oblong, 1.5 mm; pollinia 8 in 4 pairs; ovary obconical-subcylindrical, glabrous.

Locality: Mount Parker, Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai. S. Y. Hu 9748, 12758 (CUHK); Y. S. Lau 1757.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam, Japan.
Ecology: Shade and wet rocks along bank of streams. Flowering: Aug.–Sep.; fruiting: Oct.–Dec.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Authority: A. D. Hawkes & A. H. Heller
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Eria gagnepainii A. D. Hawkes & A. H. Heller 香港毛蘭
Lloydia 20: 130. 1957 [“gagnepaini”]; FRPS 19: 17, pl. 3: 5–6. 1999; FGD 7: 400. 2006; FOC 25: 345. 2009.
Eria coronaria auct. non Rchb. f.: Herklots, Hongkong Naturalist 6: 24, fig. 3. 1935.
Eria herklotsii P. J. Cribb, Orch. Rev. 84: 130, fig. 76, 77. 1976.

Epiphytic herb, glabrous throughout; rhizome creeping, 4–5 mm in diam., with funnel-shaped sheaths 0.7–1.5 cm. Pseudobulb cylindrical, 5–20 cm × 3–6 mm with a long, lacerate sheath at base. Leaves 2, subterminal, sessile, narrowly elliptic, obovate-elliptic or elliptic-lanceolate, 10–25 × 2.5–6 cm, apex acuminate, with 5–9 main veins. Flowers 5–12, bracts ovate-lanceolate to linear, 6–11 × 1.5–2 mm; pedicel including ovary 1–1.5 mm; dorsal sepals narrowly elliptic or oblong-elliptic, 14–16 × 3 – 5 mm, apex acute or obtuse; lateral sepals falcate-lanceolate, 12–16 × 5–8 mm, obtuse or acuminate, connate and forming a mentum (ca. 5 mm) at base; petals initially white, gradually turning cream-yellow, oblong-oblanceolate, 11–13 × 1.5–3 mm, acute or obtuse; lip ca. 9 × 8 mm, 3-lobed, lateral lobes parallel to midlobe, suboblong to ovate-triangular, obtuse; midlobe subtriangular or ovate-triangular, 2–3 × 2 mm. Column light green, ca. 5 mm.

Locality: Sha Tin (Siu 2000).
Distribution: Hainan, SE Xizang.
Ecology: Rocks in forests. Flowering: Feb.–Apr.
Notes: The type specimen of E. herklotsii was collected by G. A. C. Herklots from Tai Mo Shan before 1935.

Eria lasiopetala (Willd.) Ormerod 白綿毛蘭
Opera Bot. 124: 22. 1995; FRPS 19: 26. 1999; FGD 7: 402. 2006.
Aerides lasiopetala Willd., Sp. Pl. 4: 130. 1805.
Eria flava Lindl., Gen. Sp. Orch. Pl. 65. 1830; FKH 263. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 89. 1977.
Dendrolirium lasiopetalum (Willd.) S. C. Chen & J. J. Wood, FOC 25: 351. 2009.

Epiphytic herb; roots brownish, purplish red when young; rhizome slender, creeping, consisting of 3–5 internodes and terminated by an erect oblong-ovoid pseudobulb bearing leaves at apex. Leaves 3–4, petioles 1.5–2.5 cm, folded; leaf blades thick, leathery, lanceolate-linear, 9–18 × 1.2–3 cm, attenuate at both ends, apex acute. Flowers 2–5, bracts lanceolate, caducous; sepals yellowish green, densely woolly outside, lime-green and tinged yellow inside; the odd one dorsal, oblong-ovate, 16 × 5 mm, apex obtuse; lateral sepals oblique-ovate, 2.5–3 cm between apices, connate and forming a mentum at base, 2 cm from apex of mentum to the acute tip; petals lime-green, oblong-oblanceolate, 12 × 2 mm, apex obtuse; lip greenish yellow, movable, 3-lobed, lateral lobe erect, triangular, obtuse, 2–3 mm long; midlobe spathulate-obcordate, 11–12 × 7 mm, slightly recurved, margin slightly wavy, dull violet, middle thickened and slightly crested; column light green, apex shortly produced, rounded; anther yellow, oblong-subglobose; pollinia 8 in 2 groups of 4, each group with 2 larger ones and 2 smaller ones; ovary obconical, woolly.

Locality: Fo Tan Valley, Tai Po. S. Y. Hu 13146 (CUHK); Y. S. Lau 3071, 3268.
Distribution: Hainan; Indochina, Myanmar, Thailand, Nepal, India.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Nov.–Apr. of the following year.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Ma On Shan, Wu Kau Tang, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Eria rosea Lindl. 玫瑰毛蘭
Bot. Reg. 12: t. 978. 1826; FHK 353. 1861; FKH 263. 1912; FRPS 19: 13, pl. 2: 1–4. 1999; FGD 7: 399. 2006.
Cryptochilus roseus (Lindl.) S. C. Chen & J. J. Wood, FOC 25: 362. 2009.

Rizome horizontal, with short internodes; pseudobulbs large, slightly compressed, ovoid, 2–3 cm long, 2–3.5 cm across, growing close to each other. Leaf solitary; new growth with scale leaves 1–8 cm, sheath-like, green and rather fleshy at anthesis, apex mucronate, turning brown and parchment-like and completely disintegrating by the second year; foliaceous leaf leathery, fleshy and firm, base elongate into a cylindrical petiole after anthesis; leaf blade oblong-elliptic, 5–23 × 1.5–4.5 cm, about 2–3 mm thick, base cuneate and gradually attenuate into the petiole, apex obtuse and apiculate. Inflorescence a scape, bearing 3 or 4 flowers; flowers incompletely resupinate, projecting the column and the lip in a horizontal position; sepals greenish white; the odd one ovate, slightly arcuate, 12–13 × 6 mm; lateral sepals tinged pink at base, triangular-ovate, obliquely ridged along the middle, base connate and adnate to the foot forming a double-headed sac; petals white with pink lines at base, ovate, 11–12 × 8–9 mm; lip 3-lobed, pink marked with purplish red veins especially on lateral lobes, distinctly golden on the ridges of the front lobe, base saccate and adnate to the foot, front lobe slightly recurved; column slightly enlarged at apex and extending into 2 foliaceous lateral lobes; anther red, subglobose; pollinia 8 in 4 pairs; ovary subsessile, striate-sulcate.

Locality: Ma On Shan, Wu Kau Tang, Lantau Island. S. Y. Hu 11457 (CUHK); Y. S. Lau 1761; S. P. Lau 87.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong.
Ecology: Shade and damp rocks in forests. Flowering & fruiting: Jan.–May.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Victoria Peak, Tai Mo Shan, Tung Chung, Lantau Peak
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Eria sinica (Lindl.) Lindl. 小毛蘭
J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 3: 48. 1859; FKH 263. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 88, fig. 48. 1977; FRPS. 19: 12, pl. 1: 6–8. 1999; FGD 7: 398. 2006.
Conchidium sinicum Lindl., J. Bot. Kew (Misc.) 7: 34. 1855.
Eria pusilla (Griff.) Lindl., J. Linn. Soc. 3: 48. 1859; FHK 353. 1861; FRPS 19: 11. 1999; FGD 7: 398. 2006.
Conchidium pusillum Griff., Pl. Asiat. 3: 321, pl. 310. 1851; FOC 25: 347. 2009.

Rhizomes thread-like, originating from the lower side of a pseudobulb, scales inconspicuous; pseudobulbs dorsiventrally compressed-globose, often formed in pairs, generally crowded together in colonies, 3–6 mm in diam. Leaves entire, ovate, lanceolate, obovate or oblanceolate, 7–10 × 2–4 mm, base obtuse or cuneate, apex acute and apiculate, the midrib evident. Inflorescence a scape, slender, 3–4 mm, the flower bract terminal, 1–5 mm, sheathing below and cymbiform above. Flower solitary, greenish-yellow, pedicel and ovary together 1.5 mm; perianth (4–)5 mm, segments lanceolate, 1–2 mm at the base; lateral sepals fusing at their lower portion forming a prominent, swollen irregularly shaped sac; lip tongue-like, movable, shorter than the lateral sepals and the petals, the margin minutely denticulate; column minute, 0.5 mm long and wide; anther cap rugose; pollinia partially exposed, the base viscid, 8 in 4 pairs.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Tai Mo Shan, Tung Chung, Lantau Peak. S. Y. Hu 9104, 9207, 12874 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan.
Ecology: Growing with mosses and ferns over surface of exposed rocks, on top of mountain. Flowering: Oct.–Nov.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Tam, Cape D'Aguilar, Lantau Island, Lamma Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Eulophia flava (Lindl.) Hook. f. 黃花美冠蘭
Fl. Brit. Ind. 6: 7. 1890; FKH 265. 1912; FRPS 18: 177. 1999; FGD 7: 389. 2006; FOC 25: 256. 2009.
Cyrtopera flava Lindl., Gen. Sp. Orch. Pl. 189. 1833; FHK 357. 1861.

Terrestrial herb; roots wire-like, 4–5 mm in diam.; rhizomes tuber-like, white, irregularly ovoid, 6–8 cm long, 3–5 cm in diam., with distinct oblique, black concentric joints. Leaves 2–4, pedicellate, the pedicels sheathing, 25 cm or longer, covered by cataphylls 12–30 cm; leaf blades plicate, oblong-elliptic, (25–)45–50 × (4.5–)10 cm. Inflorescence a raceme; flowers bright canary-yellow and creamy yellow; dorsal sepal elliptic, 3 × 1 cm, apex acuminate, with 7 longitudinal veins slightly elevated above; lateral sepals wide-spreading, subfalcate-oblong, with 1 median longitudinal ridge, 2.5–3 × 0.8–1 cm, base oblique, truncate, apex acuminate and slightly keeled; petals situated below the dorsal sepal, broadelliptic, 2.6 × 1.5 cm, with the inner edge overlapping above the column; lip 3-lobed, subconical, saccate at base; lateral lobes creamy yellow, slightly reflexed; front lobe yellow, rounded, margin wavy and curved upwards; column arching, white or very light yellow, tinged greenish at apex, apex enlarged, apiculate at the back; anther conical, honey-yellow; pollinia 2, orange, roundish and compressed; ovary smooth, shallowly grooved.

Locality: Tai Tam, Cape D'Aguilar, Lantau Island, Lamma Island. S. Y. Hu 10164 (CUHK); Y. S. Lau 2637; HK sheet 33096.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangxi; Nepal, India, Myanmar, Vietnam, Thailand.
Ecology: Crevices of rocks along streams, open grassy slopes. Flowering: Mar.–Oct.
Uses: Ornamental.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Ho Chung, Sha Tin, Lam Tsuen, Pillar Point
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Eulophia graminea Lindl. 美冠蘭
Gen. Sp. Orch. Pl. 182. 1833; FRPS 18: 182, pl. 32: 4–5. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 874. 2000; FGD 7: 388, fig. 196. 2006; FOC 25: 255. 2009.
Eulophia sinensis Miq., J. Bot. Neerl. 1: 91. 1861; FKH 265. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 72, fig. 36. 1977.

Terrestrial herb; roots many, 2 mm in diam.; at anthesis rhizomes partially exposed, globular-conical, green at the basal half, covered by fibrous, stiff, dead leaf scales. Leaves 7–8 developed at post-anthesis, equitant, bluish green, 4–12(–35) × (0.7–)1–1.5 cm, deeply furrowed along the midrib, apex acuminate and acute. Flowers 9–20, rather small; sepals similar in colour and size, the dorsal one oblong, 12 × 2 mm, apex acute, slightly recurved; lateral sepals widespread, olive-green with a satin-like sheen, faintly tinged with purplish red stripes; petals oblong, slightly shorter than the sepals, 8–9 × 2 mm, apex acute, recurved with a rather broad, faint purplish red mid-longitudinal vein and 2 narrower ones; lip distinctly spurred and trilobed, midlobe obovate, margins crisped, apex acute, white, lateral lobes running upward and forward, greenish outside with 4–5 palmate, oblique, purplish red ridges inside; column 3.5 mm, smooth, green tinged pink, apex produced into a sharp point and enlarged into a scalloped crest; anther yellow, with 2 rounded, apical, ear-like papillose lobes; pollinia 2, subglobose; ovary 4–5 mm, glossy greenish maroon.

Locality: Ho Chung, Sha Tin, Lam Tsuen, Pillar Point. K. Y. Chan 1472 (CUHK); S. Y. Hu 13781A (CUHK); K. L. Yip 4064; HK sheet 40320.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Anhui, Taiwan; tropical Asia.
Ecology: Thin forests, grassy slopes, open fields. Flowering: Apr.–Aug.
Uses: Ornamental.
