Notes: Recent studies of reproductive biology and genetics show that this species is a self-compatible but pollinator-dependent outcrossing colonizer (Sun, Am. J. Bot. 84: 224–232. 1997; Sun & Wong, Am. J. Bot. 88: 2180–2188. 2001).

Eulophia zollingeri (Rchb. f.) J. J. Sm. 無葉美冠蘭
Fl. Buitenz. 6: 228. 1905; FFJ 6: 600, fig. 521. 1995; FRPS 18: 185. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 878, pl. 373. 2000; FOC 25: 254. 2009.
Cyrtopera zollingeri Rchb. f., Bonplandia 5: 38. 1857.
Eulophia yushuiana S. Y. Hu, Chung Chi Journal 11: 19, fig. 3(d–h). 1972.

Terrestrial herb appearing as scapes bearing brownish yellow-red flowers; roots many, fleshy, brittle; rhizomes irregularly cylindrical, ginger-like, those of the flowering plants 6–13 cm long, 2.3 cm in diam. Scape 30–50 cm long, 4–8 mm in diam., with 3–5 brownishgreen cataphylls at the base, the internodes 6–7 cm, olive-green, the flowering axis 10–20 cm, with 15 – 30 flowers well spaced; pedicels 7 mm. Flowers brownish red-green, the odd sepal ovate-oblong, 20 × 8 mm, base truncate, apex acuminate; lateral sepals spreading, oblique ovate-elliptic, 25 × 8–9 mm; petals obovate, shiny brownish red, 1.7 cm; lip shortly spurred, saccate at the base, 3-lobed, 2-ridged at the throat, purplish beige outside, purplish red and sparsely hairy inside, the front lobe ovate, slightly recurved, 7 × 5 mm, hairy, margin purplish red, centre yellow; column 10 mm, light green; anther yellow-red and trimmed with maroon at the basal end; pollinia 2; rostellum fleshy; ovary beige-brown, 13 mm long, 2.5 mm in diam., striate-sulcate.

Locality: Clear Water Bay, New Territories. S. Y. Hu 10274 (CUHK); L. T. Lo 406, 453.
Distribution: Yunnan, Guangxi, Guangdong, Jiangxi, Taiwan; India, Sri Lanka, Malaysia, Indonesia, Ryukyu.
Ecology: Margins of swamps. Flowering: May–Jun.
Notes: The type specimen of Eulophia yushuiana (S. Y. Hu 10274, A, holotype; CUHK, isotype) was collected from Clear Water Bay on 29 May 1970.

Gastrochilus japonicus (Makino) Schltr. 黃松盆距蘭（港盆距蘭）
Fedde Repert. Sp. Nov. Beih. 12: 315. 1913, et l. c. 4: 288. 1919; FRPS 19: 407, pl. 60: 7. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 887, pl. 378. 2000; FGD 7: 475. 2006; FOC 25: 494. 2009.
Gastrochilus holttumianus S. Y. Hu & Barretto, Chung Chi Journal 13(2): 32. 1976; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 114. 1977.

Epiphytic monopodial herb; roots many, greyish green, 2 mm in diam.; stems very short. Leaves dull green, conduplicate in bud, articulate at base and slightly papillose at the joint; leaf blades elliptic, 4–6 × 1–1.2 cm, base oblique and twisted, apex acute, midrib canaliculate above, elevated beneath, margin strongly wavy. Flowers yellowish green; sepals and petals almost similar in colour, shape and size, equally spaced, forming a semicircle behind the column, the segments fleshy, rounded at apex, cuneate at base, 5 × 2–3 mm, petals slightly narrower; lip saccate, yellowish to white, very smooth inside, red at base and dotted red here and there along the margin, the front lobe rounded, 3 × 7 mm, notched at apex, margin slightly recurved, greenish white, the middle portion yellow with red dots; column very short, red, 1.5 × 5 mm, adnate to the lip by a short foot; anther dorso-ventrally compressed, the back globular, gradually attenuate at apex, yellow; pollinia 2, front view spherical, back view slightly flat with a depression at centre, supported by a slender transparent stipe; ovary and pedicel indistinct, glabrous, shallowly grooved.

Locality: Victoria Peak. S. Y. Hu 12349B (CUHK).
Distribution: Taiwan; Japan (Ryukyu).
Ecology: Trunks in forests.
Notes: The holotype specimen of G. holttumianus (S. Y. Hu 12349B, K) was collected by H. Tai from Victoria Peak in 1962.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Authority: Kumar, S. W. Gale, Kocyan, G. A. Fisch. & Aver.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Wong Nai Chung, Aberdeen, Sai Kung
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Geodorum densiflorum (Lam.) Schltr. 地寶蘭
Fedde Repert. Sp. Nor. Beih. 4: 259. 1919; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 96, fig. 54. 1977; FRPS 18: 187, pl. 31: 4–5. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 896, pl. 381. 2000; FGD 7: 390, fig. 197. 2006; FOC 25: 259. 2009.
Limodorum densiflorum Lam., Encycl. 3: 516. 1789.
Geodorum semicristatum Lindl., Fol. Orch. Geodorum 2. 1854; FKH 265. 1912.
Geodorum dilatatum auct. non (Roxb.) Aiton: FKH 265. 1912.

Terrestrial herb; roots cord-like, 3–4 mm in diam.; pseudobulbs subglobose and dorso-ventrally compressed-globose. Leaves 2–4, all basal; petioles sheathing, the sheaths closed; leaf blades plicate-venose, chartaceous, delicate green, elliptic or lanceolate, 20–30 × 4.5–7.5 cm, slightly wavy along the lower margin, base cuneate, apex acute or acuminate. Flowers white, or light purplish pink, crowded, non-resupinate; sepals uniform in colour and similar in size and shape; the odd one oblong-elliptic, 10 × 3 mm, apex obtuse and mucronate; lateral sepals widespread, 18 mm between apices, oblong-elliptic, 12 × 3 mm; petals oblong, 10 mm between apices, 11–12 × 5 mm, apex obtuse; lip trowel-shaped, base saccate, adnate to the broad column foot, delicately fleshy, white within, margin slightly wavy or crisped, apex rounded or notched, disk papillose, yellow or orange along the upper middle portion, rugosely keeled; column white, short and very broad, 4 mm broad, 3 mm wide, extending to a broad triangular foot white or maculated maroon; anther semispherical; pollinia 2, waxy, globes in front and strongly sulcate at the back; ovary shiny green, glabrous, striate and sulcate.

Locality: Wong Nai Chung, Aberdeen, Sai Kung. H. C. Tang 1026; Y. W. Lam 35; HK sheet 34724.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou, Taiwan; Philippines, tropical Asia.
Ecology: Forests, streamsides and grassy slopes. Flowering: Jun.–Jul.

Goodyera foliosa (Lindl.) Benth. ex Clarke 多葉斑葉蘭
J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 25: 73. 1889; FKH 268. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 26(3 – 4): 400. 1973; FRPS 17: 142. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 904. 2000; FOC 25: 51. 2009.
Georchis foliosa Lindl., Gen. Sp. Orchid. Pl. 496. 1840.
Goodyera foliosa (Lindl.) Hook. f. var. alba S. Y. Hu & Barretto, Chung Chi Journal 13(2): 8. 1967; Check List HK Plants 376. 2002; 131. 2004.

Terrestrial herb, 10–17 cm tall at flowering time. Leaves ovate or oblong, 2.5–7 × 1.5–2.5 cm, acute; petioles 1–2 cm. Flower colour varying greatly, salmon-pink with orange lip white at apex; dorsal sepal pink with white margin, lateral sepals 5–7 × 0.4 cm, margin strongly curved; petals salmon-pink, creamy-white along margin, 5–7 × 4 mm; lip deep orange, white at apex, strongly saccate and round at base; column yellow, 2 mm; anther ovoid, 2.5 mm.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. S. Y. Hu 11037, 11059 (CUHK); HK sheet 35642.
Distribution: Guangdong, Yunnan, S China; Bhutan, Nepal, N India, Myanmar, Japan.
Ecology: Ravines near mountain streams. Flowering: Sep.–Jan. of the following year.
Notes: The holotype specimen of G. foliosa var. alba (G. Barretto 100, K) was collected by Ruy Barretto from Tai Mo Shan in Jul., 1970.

Goodyera procera (Ker Gawl.) Hook. 高斑葉蘭
Exot. Fl. 1: t. 39. 1823; FHK 360. 1861; FKH 268. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 26(3–4): 402. 1973, et Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 48, fig. 19. 1977; FRPS 17: 151. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 908. 2000; FGD 7: 351. 2006; FOC 25: 51. 2009.
Neottia procera Ker Gawl., Bot. Reg. 8: t. 639. 1822.

Terrestrial herb; stem upright, to 35 cm tall, pubescent. Leaves petiolate; petioles 2.5–8 cm; leaf blades elliptic or lanceolate, 6–12 × 1.3–4.5 cm, reticulation obscure, apex acuminate or acute. Scape 32 cm; flowers small, greenish white, up to 120 in a terminal raceme; dorsal sepal 3 × 1.5 mm, lateral sepals 2.5 mm; petals white, forming a roof with the odd sepal; lip fleshy, white, 2.5 mm, attached to a column foot; column 2 mm; anther globose; pollinia 4 in 2 pairs; ovary and pedicel 3–4.5 cm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. S. Y. Hu 9946, 11846 (CUHK); HK sheet 40375.
Distribution: S, E & SW China; Japan, Philippines, S to SE Asia.
Ecology: Earth pockets on rocks in stream bed. Flowering: Mar.–Apr.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Fo Tan Valley, Pat Sin Leng
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Goodyera seikoomontana Yamam. 歌綠斑葉蘭（香港斑葉蘭）
J. Soc. Trop. Agric. 4: 187, 1932; FRPS 17: 152. 1999; FOC 25: 49. 2009.
Goodyera youngsayei S. Y. Hu & Barretto, Chung Chi Journal 13(2): 10, fig. 5. 1976; FRPS 17: 153. 1999.

Small terrestrial herb, 10–15 cm tall; stems creeping, consisting of 5–10 internodes. Leaves petiolate; petiole 1.5–3 cm; leaf blades oblique-ovate, 3–7.5 × 1.7–3.6 cm, apex triangular-acute. Flowers pearl-colour, slightly pink at apex; 1–3 in a small spike terminal to a scape of 8–12 cm; odd sepal 1.5 × 0.6 cm, arcuate and hood-like; lateral sepals ovate-lanceolate, 1.4 × 0.6 cm, spreading and pointing backward; petals oblique oblanceolate-spathulate, 14 mm; lip ventricose, apex recurved; column ivory white; anther sagittate; pollinia 4 in 2 pairs; ovary cylindrical, 11–15 mm, villose at apex. Fruit a capsule.

Locality: Fo Tan Valley, Pat Sin Leng. Y. S. Lau 1778; HK sheet 30752.
Distribution: S Taiwan.
Ecology: Shade and moist places in forests.
Notes: The type specimen of G. youngsayei (G. Barretto 107, K, holotype; A, isotype) was collected from Pat Sin Leng in 1975.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Pok Fu Lam, Kowloon Peak, Tai Mo Shan, Fanling
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Goodyera viridiflora (Blume) Blume 綠花斑葉蘭
Orch. Archip. Ind. 41, pl. 9c, f. 2(12–16). 1858; FRPS 17: 152. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 912, photo 121. 2000; FOC 25: 50. 2009.
Neottia viridiflora Blume, Bijdr. 408. 1825.
Goodyera cordata (Lindl.) Benth. ex Hook. f., Fl. Brit. Ind. 6: 114. 1890, et Hooker's Icon. Pl. t. 2187. 1894; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 46. 1977.

Small terrestrial herb, 10–15 cm tall at flowering time; portion of stem lying on the damp ground as a rhizome, slightly swollen, internodes 5–7 mm long, 2 mm in diam., ascending and bearing a rosette of leaves. Leaves 3–5, petiolate; leaf blades ovate-cordate, 2.5–4.5 × 1.5–2.5 cm, apex acute. Flowers greenish pink, 2–5 in a terminal spike; odd sepal cucullate, 1 cm; lateral sepals same colour, ovate-lanceolate, 9–10 × 3–4 mm, reflexed; petals greenish-pink, whitish along margin, linear-falcate, 8 × 1.5 mm, upper margin coalescent with margin of odd sepal; lip white, tinged green, base slightly saccate, 8 mm; column green, very short (2.5 mm); anther ovate-cordate, beaked; pollinia 4; ovary and pedicel hairy.

Locality: Pok Fu Lam, Kowloon Peak, Tai Mo Shan, Fanling. S. Y. Hu 9905 (CUHK); HK sheet 41730.
Distribution: Endemic to Hong Kong.
Ecology: Wet grounds along streams in shade.

Goodyera yangmeishanensis T. P. Lin 小小斑葉蘭
Native. Orch. Taiwan 2: 173. 1977; FTW ed. 2, 5: 914. 2000; FOC 25: 54. 2009.
Goodyera shixingensis K. Y. Lang, Act. Phytotax. Sin. 34(6): 636, fig. 2. 1996; FRPS 17: 140, fig. 18: 5–6. 1999; FGD 7: 349. 2006.

Small terrestrial herb; stem erect from the creeping base, 8–11 cm tall, reddish or reddish brown, bearing 3–5 leaves near the base. Leaves petiolate; leaf blades ovate to elliptic, 1.5–4.5 × 0.8–1.5 cm, base rounded, apex acute, dark green, with fine white network on adaxial surface; petiole 1–1.5 cm, dilated and amplexicaul at base. Peduncle 5–8 cm, glabrous proximally, hairy distally; floral bracts ovate-lanceolate, ca. 6 × 3.2 mm, apex caudate-acuminate, serrulate or entire at base. Flowers small, several to more than 10 in a terminal raceme, and usually turning on one side; sepal greenish brown, dorsal one ovate-elliptic, 3–3.3 × 2.5 mm; lateral ones obliquely ovate, 4 × 2.8 mm; petals white, obliquely spatulate, ca. 3 × 1 mm; lip 4–5 mm, undivided, base deeply saccate, hairy inside, limb ovate, irregularly toothed at margin near apex; column 2–2.5 mm; anther cordate; pollinia 4; ovary and pedicel glabrous.

Locality: Hong Kong Island. HK sheet 33355.
Distribution: Guangdong, Hunan, Taiwan.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Jul.–Sep.

Habenaria ciliolaris Kraenzl. 毛葶玉鳳花
Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 16(2): 169. 1892, et Orch. Gen. Sp. 1: 367. 1898; FKH 270. 1912; FRPS 17: 462, pl. 76: 1–5. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 914. 2000; FGD 7: 373, fig. 191. 2006; FOC 25: 155. 2009.

Perennial terrestrial herb requiring winter resting underground, to 30 cm tall at flowering time. Leaves basal, ovate or lanceolate, 8–12 × 3 cm. Flowers white or greenish-white, occasionally washed pink; 6 15 terminal to a raceme, 30 cm; rachis pedicels and ovary pilose; dorsal sepal ovate, 6–9 mm, acute or obtuse, lateral sepals ovate, recurved, 10 mm; petals erect, lanceolate, 6–7 mm; lip 3-lobed, the lateral one filiform; ovary pilose and stellate.

Locality: Hong Kong Peak. HK sheet 7137.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Hillslopes or shaded places of forests. Flowering: Jul.–Sep.
Notes: The type specimen was collected by C. Ford (K, holotype) from Little Hong Kong in 1884.

Habenaria coultousii Barretto 香港玉鳳花
Orchadian 7(1): 10, fig. 1. 1981; FRPS 17: 450. 1999; FOC 25: 152. 2009.

Perennial herb 15–45 cm tall, requiring a resting winter period underground. Leaves 3–4, lanceolate to ovate-lanceolate, 2.5–5.2 × 0.8–1.2 cm. Raceme 2–9-flowered; scape glabrous. Flowers white, 1.5–2 cm; petals oblique ovate; lip trilobate, 9–12 × 1.5 mm, spur pale yellow-green, 2–2.4 cm, longer than ovary and pedicel together; column greenish white; pollinia 2, yellow, viscidia exposed; rostellum erect, 1.5 mm, glands conical. Capsules 2.5–2.9 cm.

Locality: Violet Hill, Tai Tam. HK sheet 34048.
Distribution: Endemic to Hong Kong.
Ecology: Forests along streams, alt. 300 m. Flowering: Oct.
Notes: The type specimen was collected by B. Coultous from Violet Hill in 1978. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Habenaria dentata (Sw.) Schltr. 鵝毛玉鳳花（齒片鷺蘭）
Repert. Spec. Nov. Regni Veg. Beih. 4: 125. 1919; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 33, fig. 9. 1977; FRPS 17: 472, pl. 78. 2. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 915. 2000; FGD 7: 375. 2006; FOC 25: 157. 2009.
Orchis dentata Sw., Kongl. Vetensk. Acad. Handl. 21: 207. 1800.
Habenaria miersiana Champ. ex Benth., J. Bot. Kew Misc. 7: 37. 1855; FHK 363. 1861; FKH 270. 1912.

Perennial herb 25–50 cm tall at flowering time. Leaves all cauline, the lowerest one ovate, 5 × 3 cm, apex acute; the upper ones elliptic-lanceolate, 10–15 × 2–4 cm, acute to acuminate at apex. Flowers white, in terminal spikes consisting of 8–20 flowers; sepals papillose along margin, the dorsal one ovate, 12–13 mm; lateral sepals spreading, oblique-ovate; petals small, falcate-lanceolate, 11 × 2.5 mm; lip 3-lobed, spur 4 cm; column broad; anther with divergent thecae; pollinia 2; ovary clavate, 2 cm, papillose.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. K. K. Mark 24(2821) (CUHK); P. S. Choi 5.
Distribution: Areas S of Changjiang; Nepal, Sikkim, India, Myanmar, Vietnam, Laos, Thailand, Cambodia, Japan.
Ecology: Hillsides. Flowering: Jul.–Sep.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: The type specimens of Habenaria miersiana (Champion 336, K) was collected by J. G. Champion from Victoria Peak in Sep. 1847 and 1848.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Victoria Peak, Cape D'Aguilar, Aberdeen, Ma On Shan, Fanling
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Habenaria leptoloba Benth. 細裂玉鳳花（天使蘭、仙子蘭）
FHK 362. 1861; FKH 270. 1912; FRPS 17: 483. 1999; FOC 25: 159. 2009.

Perennial herb 25 cm tall, requiring winter rest; underground tubers ellipsoidal, ca. 2 cm long and 8 mm thick. Leaves basal and subcauline, oblong-lanceolate, 6–8 cm, the next two linear-lanceolate, 10–14 × 1–1.7 cm, acuminate and acute. Flowers light yellowgreen, 6–14 on a terminal raceme; pedicels 1–2 mm; dorsal sepal ovate, 3.5 mm, obtuse, lateral sepals oblique-ovate; petals obliqueovate, 4 mm; lip plane, spur calcarate; column deeply notched at apex; anther with widely separate thecae; pollinia 2; ovary cylindrical, 7–8 mm.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Cape D'Aguilar, Aberdeen, Ma On Shan, Fanling. K. K. Mark 19(2765) (CUHK); K. Y. Chan 1181 (CUHK); Y. S. Lau 2521.
Distribution: Endemic to Hong Kong.
Ecology: Wet places near streams. Flowering: Aug.–Sep.
Notes: The type specimens were collected by C. Harland and H. F. Hance from Hong Kong Island before 1857. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan, Pat Sin Leng, Fanling, Yuen Long, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Habenaria linguella Lindl. 坡參
Gen. Sp. Orchid. Pl. 325. 1835; FHK 362. 1861; FRPS 17: 467, pl. 80: 1–5. 1999; FGD 7: 372. 2006; FOC 25: 156. 2009.
Habenaria acuifera auct. non Lindl.: FKH 270. 1912.

Perennial herb up to 45–60 cm tall at flowering time. Leaves all cauline; leaf blade linear-lanceolate; 7.5–9.5 × 0.7–1.4 cm, amplexicaul at base, apex acute. Flowers bright sulphur-yellow, in a spike of 10–35 flowers; dorsal sepal ovate, 4 × 3.5 mm, obtuse; lateral sepals spreading side-wide, oblique-ovate, 4 × 2 mm; spur of lip 2.7 cm, column broad-triangular, 4 mm wide; pollinia 2; ovary clavate, 1.7 cm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan, Pat Sin Leng, Fanling, Yuen Long, Lantau Island. S. Y. Hu 10706, 10784 (CUHK); L. T. Lo 254.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Moist grassy slopes. Flowering: Jul.–Sep.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Mount Parker, Victoria Peak, Ma On Shan, Sai Kung
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Habenaria reniformis (D. Don) Hook. f. 腎葉玉鳳花
Fl. Brit. India 6: 152. 1894; FKH 270. 1912; FHN 4: 192. 1977; FRPS 17: 436. 1999; FGD 7: 374. 2006; FOC 25: 149. 2009.
Listera reniformis D. Don, Prodr. Fl. Nepal 28. 1825.
Aopla reniformis Lindl., Bot. Reg. 20: t. 1701. 1834; FHK 363. 1861.

Perennial herb with a winter resting period, 18–20 cm tall at flowering time; underground tubers, 1 cm long, 7–8 mm thick. Leaves 2, basal, lying flat on the ground; the lower one larger, 2.5 cm. Flowers green-yellow, 3 to 8 in a terminal raceme; pedicels 2–3 mm; dorsal sepal ovate, 6 × 3 mm, obtuse; lateral sepals ovate, 6 × 2.5 mm, acute; petals linear-falcate, connivent with the dorsal sepal; lip yellow-green, lanceolate, 6 mm, 3-lobed; column V-shaped at apex; anther with 2 subparallel thecae; pollinia 2; ovary 1.2 cm.

Locality: Mount Parker, Victoria Peak, Ma On Shan, Sai Kung. Y. S. Lau 1445; HK sheet 27749, 34221.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong; Vietnam, Cambodia, Thailand, Nepal, India.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Aug.–Sep.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Mount Parker, Aberdeen, Kowloon Peak, Shing Mun Reservoir, Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai, Ho Chung, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Habenaria rhodocheila Hance 橙黃玉鳳花（紅人蘭）
Ann. Sci. Nat. Bot. ser. 5. 5: 243. 1856; FKH 270. 1912; FRPS 17: 470, pl. 79: 1–3. 1999; FGD 7: 374. 2006; FOC 25: 157. 2009.

Perennial herb 20–25 cm tall, with a winter resting stage underground. Leaves all cauline; the lowerest one ovate or oblong, 4–8 × 1.5–3 cm; the middle one oblong-elliptic, 8–15 × 1.7–3 cm, acute at apex. Flower coral red; racemes consisting of 5–10 flowers on scape of 12–15; dorsal sepal cucullate, 1 cm; petals linear; spur 3.5–4 cm; anther with 2 parallel thecae; ovary 9 mm. Fruit unknown.

Locality: Mount Parker, Aberdeen, Kowloon Peak, Shing Mun Reservoir, Tai Mo Shan, Ng Tung Chai, Ho Chung, Lantau Island. S. Y. Hu 10738A (CUHK); K. Y. Chan 1153 (CUHK); Y. S. Lau 1739.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian; Vietnam, Laos, Cambodia, Thailand, Malaysia, Philippines.
Ecology: Rocks on the banks of streams. Flowering: Apr.–May.
Uses: Ornamental.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Tsuen Wan, Tai Po, Wang Shan Keuk, Sha Tau Kok
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Hetaeria abbreviata Lindl. 小片翻唇蘭（亮葉翻唇蘭）
Gen. Sp. Orchid. Pl. 481. 1840.
Rhomboda abbreviata (Lindl.) Ormerod, Orchadian 11: 329. 1995; FOC 25: 68. 2009.
Hetaeria cristata auct. non Blume: FKH 268. 1917; FRPS 17: 183, pl. 25: 1–3. 1999; FGD 7: 358, fig. 182. 2006; Check List HK Plants 378. 2002; 131. 2004.

Terrestrial herb; stems rhizome-like, lower part lying on ground, consisting of 6–7 internodes; the upright stem purple-green, including flowering portion up to 20 cm tall, usually lower. Leaves petiolate; petioles 1.5–3.5 cm, salmon-pink; leaf blades ovate-elliptic, 5–6 × 2–2.3 cm, dark green with inconspicuous lateral veins. Flowers creamy white, 5–13 in a terminal spike; odd sepal ovate, 4 × 2 mm, apex acute, sparsely hairy; lateral sepals oblique-ovate, 4 × 2.5 mm; petals forming a hood with the odd sepal over the column; lip uppermost, 4 mm, transparent and pink tinged, ovate, completely covered by lateral sepals, gibbose at base; apex truncate; column white, 1 mm, the front with 2 parallel wings, each with a large gland at apex; anther ovate; pollinia 2 on short caudicles; ovary glabrous, brown-red, 1 cm. Capsule oblong, 1 cm, dull red.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tsuen Wan, Tai Po, Wang Shan Keuk, Sha Tau Kok. S. Y. Hu 12129, 12387A (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou; NE India, Myanmar, Nepal, Thailand.
Ecology: Humus in the shade of dense shrubs and along bank of streams. Flowering: Aug.–Oct.
Notes: The species was reported as Anoectochilus abbreviatus (Lindl.) Seidenf. previously (Check List HK Plants 369. 2002; 129. 2004).

Hetaeria youngsayei Ormerod 香港翻唇蘭（卵葉翻唇蘭）
Oasis Suppl. 3: 7. 2004; FOC 25: 66. 2009.
Hetaeria shiuyingiana L. Li & F. W. Xing, Novon 19: 187–190. 2009.
Hetaeria nitida auct. non Ridl.: S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 51, fig. 21. 1977, et Enum. Sperm. Hong Kong 104. 2002; Check List HK Plants 378. 2002; 131. 2004.

Terrestrial herb, 30–40 cm tall at flowering time; internodes 2–3 cm; annual growth bearing 3 large leaves at the apical end. Leaves petiolate; petioles sheathing, 2.5–3 cm; leaf blades oblique-ovate, 3–6 × 2–3.5 cm, shortly acuminate at apex. Flowers small, 9–10 in terminal spike; sepals 2 above, 1 below, densely glandularly hairy, ovate, 6–7 × 3–4 mm, all free, green with pink margin and apex; petals glabrous, obliquely ovate, 6 × 4 mm, apex obtuse, pink-white; lip honey-yellow, conical, 5 × 2 mm, slightly saccate; column fleshy, extending forward into a wing on each side; anther red; pollinia 4 in 2 pairs; ovary densely glandular, villose, 9 mm.

Locality: Mount Gough. S. Y. Hu 13233 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan; Thailand.
Ecology: Along ravines in forests. Flowering: Apr.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Violet Hill, Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan, Ng Tung Chai, Pak Tai To Yan, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Liparis bootanensis Griff. 鐮翅羊耳蒜
Not. Pl. Asiat. 3: 278. 1851; FRPS 18: 80, pl. 13: 1–3. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 938. 2000; FGD 7: 450. 2006; FOC 25: 221. 2009.
Liparis plicata Franch. & Sav., Enum. Pl. Jap. 2: 509. 1879; FKH 261. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 72. 1977.

Epiphytic small herb, glabrous throughout; pseudobulbs crowded, compressed, bearing 4 cataphylls and 1 leaf. Leaf 1 to each pseudobulb, yellowish green to green, petiolate; petioles folded, articulate; leaf blades linear-lanceolate, 4.5–15 × 1.5–2.5 cm, slightly plicate, apex acute. Flowers 5–9, non-resupinate, in varying shades of green, turning to orange with age; the odd sepal linear-oblong, slightly recurved, 6–7 × 2 mm, obtuse at apex; lateral ones curving backward, lanceolate, 6 × 2 mm, obtuse; petals linear-filiform, 6 × 1 mm, obtuse; lip olive-green, tongue-like, curved downwards, apex truncate, slightly notched, with 2 distinct calli at the base, dark green; column snow-white, cylindrical, slightly compressed, base enlarged, apex arcuate, with a triangular wing on each side; anther cap ovoid, greenish, notched at the apex; pollinia 4 in 2 pairs; ovary strongly ridged and sulcate.

Locality: Violet Hill, Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan, Ng Tung Chai, Pak Tai To Yan, Lantau Island. S. Y. Hu 12747, 12763 (CUHK); P. S. Choi 487.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Fujian, Taiwan; Sikkim, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Vietnam, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia, Philippines, Japan.
Ecology: Rocks in shady ravines. Flowering: Oct.–Jan. of the following year.

Liparis ferruginea Lindl. 鏽色羊耳蒜
Gard. Chron. 1848: 55. 1848; FRPS 18: 75, pl. 11: 1–3. 1999; FGD 7: 449. 2006; FOC 25: 220. 2009.

Terrestrial herb; pseudobulbs narrowly ovoid, very small. Leaves 3–6, linear to lanceolate, (13–)20–33 × 0.8–1.2 cm, membranous or herbaceous, base slightly contracted and decurrent into amplexicaul sheath, not articulate, apex acute or shortly acuminate. Racemes several to 10-flowered; rachis 8 – 20 cm; pedicel 8–10 mm at fruiting time; floral bracts lanceolate, (2–)4–6 mm. Flowers yellow, lip pale yellowish brown slightly tinged with pale purple. Dorsal sepal linear, 6–7 × ca. 1.5 mm, 3-veined, margin revolute, apex obtuse; lateral sepals reflexed, obliquely ovate-oblong, ca. 6 × 2.5 mm, 5-veined. Petals nearly linear or narrowly oblanceolate-linear, ca. 6 × 1 mm, 1-veined, margin revolute; lip ± recurved, obovate-oblong, 4–5 × ca. 3 mm, with a pair of basal auricles backward spreading and 2 calli near base, apex broadly truncate, often emarginate and sinus apiculate. Column 3–4 mm, upper part with narrow wings on both sides. Capsule oblong or obovoid-oblong, ca. 1.5 cm × 6 mm.

Locality: Sai Kung. P. S. Choi 504; Y. W. Lam 700.
Distribution: Hainan, Fujian; Vietnam, Cambodia, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia.
Ecology: Streamsides, swamps. Flowering: Jul.

Liparis gigantea C. L. Tso 紫花羊耳蒜
Sunyatsenia 1: 136. 1933; FOC 25: 219. 2009.
Liparis macrantha Rolfe, Ann. Bot. 9: 156. 1895, non Hook. f. 1854; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 72. 1977.
Liparis nigra auct. non Seidenf.: FRPS 18: 73, pl. 10: 4. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 948. 2000; FGD 7: 449. 2006; Check List HK Plants 378. 2002; 132. 2004.

Terrestrial herb, 12–25 cm tall at flowering time; pseudobulbs cylindrical; the third year's plant bearing 2 leaves. Leaves petiolate; petioles 2–3 cm; leaf blades ovate-elliptic, 5–15 × 2.5–6.5 cm, apex acuminate. Flowers dark-purple, almost black, in a terminal raceme on scapes of 10–20 cm; pedicels 1–1.5 cm; odd sepal linear, 2 × 0.2–0.25 cm, curved backward, apex obtuse; lateral sepals 1.7 × 0.4 cm, falcate, pointing forwards, recurved, parallel to the lip; petals linear, 1.5–2 × 0.1 cm, pointing backward, obtuse; lip 1.2–2.2 cm, bent at middle, basal portion narrowed, apical portion 1–1.1 × 1.2–1.3 cm, truncate, sharply toothed; column 1 cm, light green, arcuate turning reddish purple at fading; anther subglobose; pollinia 4 in 2 pairs; ovary 4–6 mm.

Locality: Sai Kung, Lantau Island. S. Y. Hu 13643 (CUHK).
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, SE Xizang, Taiwan.
Ecology: Rocks or shade places in forests. Flowering: Feb.–May.

Liparis nervosa (Thunb. ex A. Murray) Lindl. 見血青（脈羊耳蒜）
Gen. Sp. Orch. Pl. 26. 1830; FHK 352. 1861; FKH 261. 1912; FRPS 18: 71, pl. 10: 1–3. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 947. 2000; FGD 7: 448, fig. 226. 2006; FOC 25: 218. 2009.
Ophrys nervosa Thunb. ex A. Murray, Linn. Syst. Veg. ed. 14, 814. 1784.

Caespitose terrestrial herb, 15–25 cm tall at flowering time; pseudobulbs elongate-conical, 5–10 cm or longer, 0.8–1.3 cm thick. Leaves petiolate; petioles 1–4 cm, that of the lowest leaf the longest; leaf blades ovate-elliptic, 2–19 × 1.5–8.5 cm, base unequal, one side subcordate, the other cuneate, apex acuminate. Flowers dull purplish green, very variable, sepals green or rosepurple or purple tinged green, even greenish yellow; odd sepal oblong or ovate-falcate, pointing upward, 6–12 mm; lateral 2 ovate-falcate, 4.5–9 × 2–4 mm; petals rose-purple or greenish yellow, linear, 5–10 mm; lip purple and light-green at base, tonguelike, curving downward; column fleshy, winged at apical end, green; anther purple; pollinia 4 in 2 pairs; ovary striate-sulcate.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. S. Y. Hu 12885A, 13659 (CUHK); Y. W. Lam 427.
Distribution: S, E & SW China; widely distributed in tropical and subtropical regions.
Ecology: Rocks along streams in shade of forests. Flowering: Jan.–May.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore)

Liparis odorata (Willd.) Lindl. 香花羊耳蒜
Gen. Sp. Orch. Pl. 26. 1830; FHK 352. 1861; FKH 261. 1912; FFJ 6: 630. 1995; FRPS 18: 69, pl. 11: 6–8. 1999; FGD 7: 449. 2006; FOC 25: 218. 2009.
Malaxis odorata Willd., Sp. Pl. 4: 91. 1805.

Terrestrial herb; pseudobulbs subglobose, 1–2 cm long and 1–1.5 cm in diam., articulate, covered with membranous white sheaths. Leaves 2 or 3, ovate-oblong or linear-lanceolate, membranous, 6–15 × 2–5 cm, base attenuating gradually into a sheath-like petiole, apex acuminate; petiole non-articulate, 2–10. Flowers greenish yellow; odd sepal oblanceolate, strongly recurved along the margin, appearing linear, 7–10 × 1–1.5 mm, pointing backward, apex obtuse and thickened; lateral sepals ovate-oblong, reflexed, curved downwards, 5–7 × 3 mm, apex acute; petals filiform, 4–7 × 0.5 mm, wide spread and curved backward; lip green or tinged rose-pink, notched, with 2 triangular calli near the base, apex subtruncate; column arcuate, winged; anther greenish, apex mucronate; pollinia 4 in 2 pairs; ovary strongly ridged, the ridges winged and spiral.

Locality: Sunset Peak. S. T. Dunn 192; Y. S. Lau 2743.
Distribution: S, E & SW China; India, Myanmar, Laos, Thailand, Vietnam, Japan.
Ecology: Among short grasses in full sun at high elevations on exposed mountain tops. Flowering: Apr.–Jul.

Liparis ruybarrettoi S. Y. Hu & Barratto 包瑞羊耳蒜
Chung Chi Journal 13(2): 22. 1976; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 72. 1977; FRPS 18: 80. 1999; FOC 25: 211. 2009, pro syn. sub L. bootanensis Griff.

Epiphytic herb; pseudobulbs compressed-ovoid, the oldest the smallest, 5–6 close together forming an irregular curved line, with each succeeding pseudobulb emerging from the base of the previous one. Leaf 1 to each pseudobulb, linear-lanceolate, 11–17 × 1.4–2.5 cm, the basal half slightly plicate at anthesis, becoming plane and slightly folded near the base, apex acuminate and acute; midrib impressed above, elevated beneath, the 1 or 2 lateral parallel veins on each side rather obscure. Flowers non-resupinate, in various shades of green; sepals green, the odd one linear, farthest away from the rachis, 7 × 1 mm, apex slightly curved outwards; lateral sepals ovate-lanceolate, oriented below the lip and strongly curved outwards, 6 × 1.5–2 mm wide at middle; petals filiform, yellowish green, 7 × 0.25 mm, slightly curved forward; lip olive-green, tongue-like, curved downwards, apex truncate with a small obtuse middle projection, base furnished with 1 prominent shiny dark green glandular tubercle; column light yellow tinged green, curved forward; anther cap-like, ovate-lanceolate, acute; pollinia 4 in 2 pairs; ovary subtriangular-cylindrical, striate-sulcate.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Sunset Peak. S. Y. Hu 11444A, 12569 (isotype), 12570 (holotype) (CUHK).
Distribution: Endemic to Hong Kong.
Ecology: Cliffs in shade and mossy rocks, alt. 500 m. Flowering: Oct.–Jan. of the following year.
Notes: The type specimen (S. Y. Hu 12569, K, holotype; A, CUHK, US, isotype) was collected from Tai Mo Shan in 1972.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Mount Parker, Kowloon Peak, Tai Mo Shan, Sha Tin, Ng Tung Chai
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Liparis stricklandiana Rchb. f. 扇唇羊耳蒜
Gard. Chron. n. s. 13: 232. 1880; FRPS 18: 95, pl. 14: 5–6. 1999; FGD 7: 453. 2006; FOC 25: 225. 2009.
Liparis chloroxantha Hance, J. Bot. 21: 231. 1883; FKH 261. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 77, fig. 40. 1977.

Epiphytic herb; pseudobulbs oblique-ovoid to oblong-ovoid, slightly compressed, 2–4 cm long and 0.5–1.5 cm in diam., bearing 2 leaves at apex. Leaves petiolate; petioles articulate, 4–15 cm; leaf blades chartaceous, oblanceolate or linearoblanceolate, 15–45 × 2–3 cm, base attenuate, apex acuminate. Flowers non-resupinate, greenish yellow; sepals narrowly obovate, 4–5 × 1.5–2 mm, lateral ones slightly wider; petals filiform, 5 × 1 mm; lip fan-shaped, 5 × 6 mm, apex truncate, mucronate, margin unevenly denticulate, base attenuate with an oblate callus; column slender, arcuate, slightly swollen at base; anther terminal, suborbicular; pollinia 4 in 2 pairs, faveolate.

Locality: Mount Parker, Kowloon Peak, Tai Mo Shan, Sha Tin, Ng Tung Chai. S. Y. Hu 9484, 12757 (CUHK); Y. S. Lau 1760.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; Bhutan, Sikkim, India.
Ecology: Rocks along streams in shade. Flowering: Oct.–Jan. of the following year.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Violet Hill, Tai Tam, Kowloon Peak, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Peak
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Liparis viridiflora (Blume) Lindl. 長莖羊耳蒜
Gen. Sp. Orch. Pl. 31. 1830; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 27(3–4). 428. 1974; FRPS 18: 90, pl. 16: 1–2. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 950. 2000; FGD 7: 452. 2006; FOC 25: 224. 2009.
Malaxis viridiflora Blume, Bijdr. Fl. Ned. Ind. 392. 1825.
Liparis longipes (Lindl.) Rchb. f., Bonplondia 3: 250. 1855; FHK 352. 1861; FKH 261. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 72. 1977.

Caespitose herb, 10–25 cm tall; pseudobulbs 8–9 cm or longer, 0.4–1 cm in diam. Leaves 2, linear-lanceolate, 15–21 × 2–3 cm, apex acute. Flowers non-light green, many in a terminal raceme 7–12 cm; scapes 5–10 cm, odd sepals recurved backward, 3 × 0.7 mm; lateral sepals ovate-lanceolate, pointing forward, 3 × 1.5 mm; petals linear, turning backward, 3 mm; lip fleshy, light green, apical portion ovate, obtuse; column erect, 2 mm, cylindrical; anther green; pollinia 4; ovary cylindrical, 1.5 mm. Capsule obovoid, 4–5 mm.

Locality: Violet Hill, Tai Tam, Kowloon Peak, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Peak. S. Y. Hu 10629, 11097 (CUHK); Y. S. Lau 1756.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Taiwan; S & SE Asia.
Ecology: Wet rocks and damp places in forests or ravines. Flowering: Sep.–Nov.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Castle Peak, Sha Tin, Pat Sin Leng, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Ludisia discolor (Ker Gawl.) A. Rich. 血葉蘭（石蠶）
Dict. Class. Hist. Nat. 7: 437. 1825; FHN 4: 199, fig. 1089. 1977; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 47, fig. 18. 1977; FRPS 17: 157. 1999; FGD 7: 353, fig. 178. 2006; FOC 25: 55. 2009.
Goodyera discolor Ker Gawl., Bot. Reg. 4: 271. 1818.
Haemaria discolor (Ker Gawl.) Lindl., Gen. Sp. Orch. 490. 1840; FHK 361. 1861; FKH 267. 1912.

Saxicolous herb clinging onto bare damp rock; stem creeping, succulent, 8–15 cm, internodes 7–8 mm in diam.; ascending stems 12–40 cm tall, bearing 4–5 leaves with pink petioles, midrib and margin. Leaves oblong-elliptic, 2.5–6 × 1.2–2.5 cm, apex acute and mucronate, metallic green above, reddish maroon beneath. Flowers white; dorsal sepal and petals forming a white shell of 9–10 mm long and 3 mm wide; lateral sepals white with pink tips, ovate, 8 × 5 mm, twisted at base, turning backward; petals falcate, 8–10 × 2.5 mm, obtuse; lip white, saccate at base, adnate to the column, the apical lobe tongue-like, bilobed, one curving backward, the other stretching forward; column 3 mm, apical end enlarged, the sides and front extending forward, forming a twisted beak-like rostellum; anther elongate-ovate, yellow, fitting into the centre of the beak, apex acuminate; pollinia 2, tessellate; ovary hairy. Fruit an oblong capsule.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Castle Peak, Sha Tin, Pat Sin Leng, Lantau Island. S. Y. Hu 13144, 13274 (CUHK); HK sheet 41805.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan; Myanmar, Thailand, Vietnam, Malaysia, Indonesia.
Ecology: Shade and moist places in forests. Flowering: Mar.–Apr.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore), ornamental.
Notes: Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Tam, Repulse Bay, Tai Mo Shan, Sha Tin
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Malaxis acuminata D. Don 淺裂沼蘭（紫盾沼蘭）
Prodr. Fl. Nepal. 29. 1825; FRPS 18: 116, pl. 20: 5–6. 1999.
Crepidium acuminatum (D. Don) Szlach., Fragm. Florist. Geobot. Suppl. 3: 123. 1995; FOC 25: 233. 2009.
Malaxis allanii S. Y. Hu & Barretto, Chung Chi Journal 13(2): 18, fig. 9. 1976; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 79. 1977.

Terrestrial or half-epiphytic herb; pseudobulbs fleshy, cylindrical, 4–9 mm in diam., articulate, covered by ochreous dried leaf sheaths. Leaves 3–5, oblique-ovate or elliptic, 6–10 × 3–5 cm, base attenuating into a petiole, apex acuminate; petiole sheath-like, 2–4 cm, lower portion amplexicaul. Flowers purplish red, 1.5 cm in diam.; odd sepal linear, 8–10 × 2 mm, apex obtuse, margin recurved; lateral sepals oblong, 5–7 × 3–4 mm, apex obtuse, margin recurved; petals linear, 8–10 × 1 mm, margin recurved; lip ovate-oblong or obovate-oblong, 1 cm, the basal lobes pointing from the middle downwards, the apical lobe faintly cleft at the tip; column very short, 1–1.5 mm; anther suborbicular, wax-yellow and red at the base; pollinia 4 in 2 pairs, waxy; ovary 6-striate and sulcate, curved downwards.

Locality: Tai Tam, Repulse Bay, Tai Mo Shan, Sha Tin. S. Y. Hu 1355 (holotype of M. allanii S. Y. Hu), 13010 (CUHK); Y. S. Lau 2993.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guizhou, Yunnan, Taiwan; Nepal, India, Myanmar, Vietnam, Laos, Indonesia, Java, Philippines, Australia.
Ecology: Forests and ravines. Flowering: Jun.
Notes: The type specimen of M. allanii (S. Y. Hu 13551, K, holotype; A, CUHK, isotype) was collected by W. G. L. Allen from Repulse Bay in 1969.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Mo Shan, Wu Kau Tang, Sunset Peak
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Malaxis latifolia Sm. 闊葉沼蘭
Rees Cyclop. 22. Malaxis n. 3. 1812; FHN 4: 207, fig. 1096. 1977; FRPS 18: 111. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 964, pl. 409. 2000; FGD 7: 455, fig. 228. 2006.
Dienia congesta Lindl., Bot. Reg. 10: sub t. 825. 1824; FHK 352. 1861.
Dienia ophrydis (J. Koenig) Ormerod & Seidenf., Contr. Orchid. Fl. Thailand 13: 18. 1997; FOC 25: 235. 2009.
Microstylis congesta (L.) Rchb. F., Walp. Ann 6: 206. 1861; FKH 260. 1912.
Malaxis parvissima S. Y. Hu & Barretto, Chung Chi Journal 13(2): 22, fig. 10. 1976.

Terrestrial or half-epiphytic herb; pseudobulbs fleshy, cylindrical, 3–11 cm, articulate, covered by the sheathing base of degenerated leaves. Leaves 4–5, oblique ovate-elliptic or elliptic-lanceolate, 6–17 × 3–8 cm, base attenuating into a petiole, apex acuminate; petiole sheath-like, 3–5 cm, amplexicaul. Flowers purplish red or greenish yellow, non-resupinate; odd sepal narrowly oblong, 3–5 × 1–1.5 mm, apex obtuse; lateral sepals oblique-ovate, curved inward and forward, 2–3 × 1–2 mm, apex obtuse; petals linear, 3–4 × 1–1.5 mm, apex obtuse; lip dark purplish red, 2–3 × 2.5 mm, 3-lobed; midlobe narrowly ovate, 0.5–1 mm, apex obtuse; lateral lobes very short or not obvious, apex obtuse; column very short, 1.5 mm; anther 2-celled, sunk in the apical cavity of the column, attached at the back; pollinia 4, in 2 obovoid pairs, waxy; ovary very short, green with 6 purple cristate ridges, not twisted nor sulcate.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Wu Kau Tang, Sunset Peak. Y. S. Lau 3305.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; India, Indochina, Malesia, Australia.
Ecology: Along banks of streams in wooded areas. Flowering: May–Jul.
Notes: The type specimen of M. parvissima (S. Y. Hu 12453, K, holotype; A, CUHK, isotype) was collected by W. G. L. Allen from Tai Mo Shan in 1972.

Mischobulbum cordifolium (Hook. f.) Schltr. 心葉球柄蘭
Fedde Repert. Sp. Nov. Beih. 1: 98. 1911, et 4: 180. 1919; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 66, fig. 32. 1977; FRPS 18: 231. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 971, pl. 413. 2000; FGD 7: 409, fig. 210. 2006.
Tainia cordifolia Hook. f., Hooker's Icon. Pl. 19(3): pl. 1861. 1889; FOC 25: 282. 2009.

Terrestrial herb; pseudobulbs petiole-like, 8 cm or longer, 3–4 mm thick, unifoliate. Leaves semi-succulent, ovate-cordate, 7–13 × 4–8 cm, base cordate, apex acute, dull green, with 6 arching primary veins in addition to the midrib and faintly reticulate veinlets. Flowers large, bracts small, lanceolate, 7 mm, apex acuminate; sepals and petals brown with purple-brown veins; sepals subequal, lanceolate; the odd one 2–2.5 × 0.3–0.5 cm, apex acuminate; lateral ones oblique, connate at the base forming the mentum of 12–14 mm; petals slightly larger than sepals, lanceolate, 2–2.2 × 0.5–0.7 cm, acute, oblique at the base, 5-veined and keeled along the midvein; lip fleshy, attached to the mentum, rhomboid, 2.4 × 1.4 cm, the apex triangular and acute, with 3 prominent ridges, purple; column erect, fleshy, slightly curved, winged along both sides; anther terminal, with 2 ear-like projections; pollinia 8 in 4 pairs; ovary subcylindrical, striate, glabrous.

Locality: Lantau Island. HK sheet 34413.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian, Taiwan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Shade and moist places in forests. Flowering: May–Jul.
Uses: Ornamental.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Victoria Peak, Ma On Shan, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Nephelaphyllum tenuiflorum Blume 雲葉蘭
Bijdr. 8: 373. 1825; FRPS 18: 232, pl. 39: 7–12. 1999; FGD 7: 408, fig. 209. 2006; FOC 25: 281. 2009.
Nephelaphyllum cristatum Rolfe, Kew Bull. 194. 1896; J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 36: 19. 1903; FKH 263. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 27: 442. 1974, et Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 64, fig. 31. 1977.

Terrestrial creeping herb; rhizomes fleshy, 2–5 mm in diam., with 1 cm long membranous sheaths; pseudobulbs petiole-like, fleshy, 1–2 cm long, 1–2 mm thick, unifoliate. Leaves ovatecordate, slightly fleshy, 2–5 × 1–4 cm, base cordate, apex acute. Flowers non-resupinate; sepals and petals alike in colour, shiny light green, striped purplish red; sepals obovate-lanceolate, apex acuminate, 1 × 0.3 cm, lateral ones being narrower; petals spathulate, same length with sepals but being wider, apex acute; lip nearly elliptic, slightly notched, 1 × 0.5–0.7 cm, inobviously 3-lobed; lateral lobes growing downwards, midlobe curving upwards, apex slightly notched, margin crispate; column flat, veined along the sides; anther cornute, rectangular; pollinia 8 in 4 pairs, oblong, compressed; ovary obconical, green tinged purplish red.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Ma On Shan, Lantau Island. Y. S. Lau 1891; Y. W. Lam 235, 1648.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong. Ecology: Forests. Flowering: Jun.–Jul.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: The type specimen of N. cristatum (C. Ford 48, 254, K) was collected by C. Ford from Victoria Peak before 1884. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Tam, Aberdeen, Clear Water Bay
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Nervilia fordii (Hance) Schltr. 毛唇芋蘭（毛葉芋蘭）
Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 45(3): 403. 1911; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 38, fig. 12. 1977, et Enum. Sperm. Hong Kong 104. 2002; FRPS 18: 25, pl. 4: 4–5.1999; FOC 25: 200. 2009.
Pogonia fordii Hance, J. Bot. 23(272): 247. 1885; FKH 268. 1912.
Pogonia pulchella auct. non Hook. f.: FKH 268. 1912.

Terrestrial herb without aerial stem except the scape; rhizome delicate, terminated by a globose corm 1.5–2 cm in diam. Leaves lying flat on ground, solitary, cordate, 5–9 cm in diam., green above, purple-green beneath. Flowers rose-pink, two terminal to a purplepink scape of 12–15 cm, emerged from the corm before growth of leaf; pedicels 6 mm; sepals greenish pink, oblanceolate, the odd one 2–2.5 × 0.6 cm, apex truncate, cuspidate; lateral sepals narrower; petals linear-lanceolate, 2.4 × 0.3 cm, acute and cuspidate; lip 2.5 cm, embracing the column, slightly gibbous at base, apical one-third rose-pink, apex retuse and notched; column 7 × 2.5 mm, dumb-bellshaped; anther 2-celled, white; pollinia 4 in 2 pairs, glandular; ovary 3–4 mm.

Locality: Tai Tam, Aberdeen, Clear Water Bay. S. Y. Hu 13686 (CUHK); P. S. Choi 530; S. C. Tse 427.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Sichuan, Yunnan; Thailand, Vietnam, India, Myanmar, Malaysia, Indonesia, Philippines.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: May–Aug.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The species was reported as Nervilia plicata (Andr.) Schltr. previously (Check List HK Plants 379. 2002; 132. 2004).

Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 45(3): 403. 1911; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 38, fig. 12. 1977, et Enum. Sperm. Hong Kong 104. 2002; FRPS 18: 25, pl. 4: 4–5.1999; FOC 25: 200. 2009.
Pogonia fordii Hance, J. Bot. 23(272): 247. 1885; FKH 268. 1912.
Pogonia pulchella auct. non Hook. f.: FKH 268. 1912.

Terrestrial herb without aerial stem except the scape; rhizome delicate, terminated by a globose corm 1.5–2 cm in diam. Leaves lying flat on ground, solitary, cordate, 5–9 cm in diam., green above, purple-green beneath. Flowers rose-pink, two terminal to a purplepink scape of 12–15 cm, emerged from the corm before growth of leaf; pedicels 6 mm; sepals greenish pink, oblanceolate, the odd one 2–2.5 × 0.6 cm, apex truncate, cuspidate; lateral sepals narrower; petals linear-lanceolate, 2.4 × 0.3 cm, acute and cuspidate; lip 2.5 cm, embracing the column, slightly gibbous at base, apical one-third rose-pink, apex retuse and notched; column 7 × 2.5 mm, dumb-bellshaped; anther 2-celled, white; pollinia 4 in 2 pairs, glandular; ovary 3–4 mm.

Locality: Tai Tam, Aberdeen, Clear Water Bay. S. Y. Hu 13686 (CUHK); P. S. Choi 530; S. C. Tse 427.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Sichuan, Yunnan; Thailand, Vietnam, India, Myanmar, Malaysia, Indonesia, Philippines.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: May–Aug.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The species was reported as Nervilia plicata (Andr.) Schltr. previously (Check List HK Plants 379. 2002; 132. 2004).

Neuwiedia singapureana (Baker) Rolfe 三蕊蘭
Bull. Misc. Inform. Kew 1907: 412. 1907; FRPS 17: 15. 1999; FOC 25: 21. 2009.
Tupistra singapureana Baker, J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 14: 581. 1874.
Neuwiedia veratrifolia auct. non Blume: S. Y. Hu, Enum. Sperm. Hong Kong 107. 2004.

Perennial rhizomatous erect herb 40–50 cm tall. Leaves 4–5, elliptic or elliptic-lanceolate, 13–25 × 3.5–6.5 cm, base acute, apex acuminate; petioles 6–10 cm. Inflorescence racemose, 8–9 cm. Flowers white, fragrant; scapes bracteate; bracts 3–4 × 1.5–2 cm, hispid; perianth erect, 1.5 cm, connate at base forming a slender (about 4 mm) tube; anthers white, 5 mm; ovary inferior, ellipsoidal, 5 × 3 mm. Capsule ellipsoidal.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Lantau Peak. H. W. Mak ex N. H. Li 191 (CUHK); HK sheet 36122, 35377.
Distribution: Hainan, Yunnan; Vietnam, Thailand, Singapore, Indonesia.
Ecology: Forests. Flowering: May–Jun.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Mount Kellet, Ma On Shan, Fanling, Luk Keng, Sai Kung, Nai Chung, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Pachystoma pubescens Blume 粉口蘭
Bijdr. 376. t. 29. 1825; FRPS 18: 249, pl. 42: 7–8. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 993. 2000; FGD 7: 405, fig. 207. 2006; FOC 25: 286. 2009.
Pachystoma chinense (Lindl.) Rchb. f., Bonplandia 3: 251. 1855; FHK 356. 1861; FKH 263. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 70, fig. 35. 1977.

Terrestrial herb; rhizome fibrous or yoke-shaped. Leaves 1–2, produced after anthesis, papery, linear-lanceolate, 7–40 × 0.5–1.2 cm, cuneate at base, acute at apex. Flowers 5–13, purple, hanging; pedicels 4–5 mm, hirsute; dorsal sepal elliptic or oblonglanceolate, 11–15 × 4–6 mm, truncate at base, obtuse at apex, with 5 pink veins, glabrous above, sparsely pubescent towards the base beneath; lateral sepals oblique, slightly narrower, pubescent on both surfaces; petal linear-oblong or oblanceolate, 12–13 × 1.5–3 mm, apex acute or acuminate, ciliate along margin; lip 3-lobed, fleshy, pubescent at base, connate to the column foot; lateral lobes erect, rounded, purplish red on both surfaces; midlobe ovate-oblong, recurved at apex, bright purplish red with 3–5 papillose, rough, bright yellow-green ridges; column uniformly dark purple, arcuate, hirsute; anther sparsely pubescent, dark purple; pollinia 8 in 2 groups of 4 pairs.

Locality: Mount Kellet, Ma On Shan, Fanling, Luk Keng, Sai Kung, Nai Chung, Lantau Island. S. Y. Hu 7322, 11849 (CUHK); L. T. Lo 607.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Taiwan; tropical Asia.
Ecology: Grassy mountain slopes. Flowering: Mar.–May.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Authority: S. C. Chen & F. Y. Liu
S. C. Chen & Z. H. Tsi

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Kowloon Peak, Tai Mo Shan, Pat Sin Leng, Clear Water Bay, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Paphiopedilum purpuratum (Lindl.) Stein 紫紋兜蘭（香港兜蘭）
Orchideenbuch 481. 1892; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 27, fig. 5. 1977; FRPS 17: 69, pl. 8: 1. 1999; FGD 7: 330, fig. 160. 2006; Z. J. Liu et al., Genus Paphiopedilum in China 181. 2009; FOC 25: 43. 2009.
Cypripedium purpuratum Lindl., Edward's Bot. Reg. 23: t. 1991. 1837; FHK 364. 1861.
Paphiopedilum purpuratum (Lindl.) Pfitzer, Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 19(1): 40. 1894; FKH 270. 1912.
Cypripedium sinicum Hance ex Rchb. f., Walp. Ann. 3: 602. 1853.

Terrestrial or semi-epiphytic herb. Leaves 4–8, distichous, elliptic to oblong-elliptic, 8–17 × 2–4 cm, tessellated dark and light green above, pale green beneath; margins ciliate near the base. Flower solitary; scape 15 – 20 cm, purple, pubescent; bract ovate-lanceolate, 1.5–2.5 × 1 cm, villose at margin; perianth 8 cm across; dorsal sepal ovate-cordate, 3–4 × 2.5–3 cm, white, veined purple-maroon; synsepalum ovate or ovate-lanceolate, 2–3 × 1–1.5 cm, pale green with dark veins; petals horizontal, ellipticoblong, 4–5 × 1–1.5 cm, glossy maroon or pale chestnut with dark veins, flushed green-white and spotted black-maroon; lip 4 × 2 cm, incurved, lateral lobes verrucose, brown-maroon; staminode lunate, 8 ×10 mm, pale ochre-purple veined darker.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Kowloon Peak, Tai Mo Shan, Pat Sin Leng, Clear Water Bay, Lantau Island. K. K. Mark 38 (CUHK); Y. S. Lau 632, 1762.
Distribution: S Fujian, S Guangdong, Hainan, S Guangxi, SE Yunnan; N Vietnam.
Ecology: Humus-rich stony places in forests. Flowering: Nov.–May of the following year.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: The holotype specimen of Cypripedium sinicum Hance ex Rchb. f. (Hance s.n., W) was collected by H. F. Hance from Hong Kong Island around 1850. Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Kowloon Peak, Tai Mo Shan, Pat Sin Leng, Clear Water Bay, Lantau Peak
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Pecteilis susannae (L.) Raf. 白蝶蘭（鵝毛白蝶花）
Fl. Tellur. 2: 38. 1837 [“susanna”]; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 28, fig. 6. 1977; FRPS 17: 395, pl. 62. 1–2. 1999; FGD 7: 370, fig. 190. 2006; FOC 25: 136. 2009.
Orchis susannae L., Sp. Pl. 939. 1753.
Habenaria susannae (L.) R. Br., Prod. Fl. Nepal 321. 1819; FHK 363. 1861.
Platanthera susannae (L.) Lindl., Gen. Sp. Orch. Pl. 295. 1835; FKH 269. 1912.

Perennial large herb requiring a winter rest period underground 30–40 cm tall at flowering time. Leaves all cauline, ovate-oblong, 5.5–11 × 2–4 cm, acute. Flowers fragrant, large, showy, 2–5 in a terminal raceme; pedicels 1.5 cm; dorsal sepals, suborbicular, 2.5 cm in diam.; lateral sepals 4–5 cm, pointing upward, apex obtuse; petals cornute, small, inconspicuous, 12 × 2 mm; lip long, 3-lobed at base, butterfly-like, the lateral lobes triangular, 3 × 4 cm, prominently fringed, midlobe linear, 3 × 0.6 cm; spur 12 cm, 2–3 mm in diam.; column fleshy, 1.7 × 1 cm, rounded and notched at apex; anther with widely separate thecae; pollinia 2; ovary ellipsoidal.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Kowloon Peak, Tai Mo Shan, Pat Sin Leng, Clear Water Bay, Lantau Peak. J. P. W. Woo 110 (CUHK); S. P. Lau 31; Y. S. Lau 1604.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian; Nepal, India, Myanmar, Malaysia, Indonesia.
Ecology: Forests, ditches or grassy slopes. Flowering: Jun.–Jul.
Uses: Ornamental.

Pelexia obliqua (J. J. Sm.) Garay 肥根蘭
Bot. Mus. Leafl. Harvard Univ. 28(4): 345. 1980; FRPS 17: 231. 1999; S. Y. Hu, Enum. Sperm. Hong Kong 107. 2003; FOC 25: 86. 2009.
Spiranthes obliqua J. J. Sm., Bull. Dep. Agric. Indes Neerl. 43: 74. 1910.
Manniella hongkongensis S. Y. Hu & Barretto, Chung Chi Journal 13(2): 6, fig. 13. 1976; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 42, fig. 15. 1977.

Terrestrial herb; leaves and flowering plants appearing in different seasons. Leaves caespitose, petiolate; petioles up to 1 cm; leaf blades elliptic to oblong-elliptic, 3.5–6.5 × 1.5–3.5 cm, apex acute. Flowers small, white, 5–18 terminal to a scape of 12–15 cm; sepals longer than petals, glandularly hairy on the basal portion, 4 mm, the lateral two connate at base; petals 4 mm; lip fleshy, the lower portion forming a groove and extending backward into 2 appendages, hooked at the ends in the spur; column short, apex ovoid; anther lanceolate; pollinia 2; rostellum ovate; stigmas 2; ovary glandularly hairy.

Locality: New Territories. S. Y. Hu 13266 (CUHK).
Distribution: Indonesia.
Ecology: Ravines. Flowering: Sep.
Notes: The holotype specimen of M. hongkongensis (S. Y. Hu 13266, K) was collected from Sha Tin in 1965.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Tam Tuk, Cloudy Hill, Tsing Yi, Tung Chung
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Peristylus calcaratus (Rolfe) S. Y. Hu 長鬚闊蕊蘭
Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 26: 398. 1973; 27: 160, 460, fig. 22. 1974; FRPS 17: 404. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 994. 2000; FGD 7: 378. 2006; FOC 25: 139. 2009.
Glossula calcarata Rolfe, Bull. Misc. Inform. Kew 1913(4): 145. 1913.

Terrestrial herb 25–30 cm tall. Leaves 4, crowded at the base of stem just above ground level; leaf blades obovate-oblanceolate, the middle two larger, 3.5–7.5 × 1.5–2 cm, apex acute. Flowers green or yellowish green, 20–35 in a terminal spike; dorsal sepal ovateoblong, 3 × 2 mm, obtuse; lateral sepals obovate, conduplicate and turning outward, 3.5 mm; petals light green, oblique-ovate, with the inner half below the odd sepal, forming a hood, apex rounded, base connate to the column arm; lip yellow-green, 3-lobed, the lateral lobes filiform, 1–1.2 cm, midlobe tongue-like, 1.5 × 1 mm; spur clavate, 5 mm, apex bilobate; column short; anthers 2, parallel; pollinia 2; ovary 6 mm, cylindrical, slightly twisted at base.

Locality: Tai Tam Tuk, Cloudy Hill, Tsing Yi, Tung Chung. S. Y. Hu 10860, 10946 (CUHK); HK sheet 7158, 7159.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Jiangsu, Hunan, Zhejiang, Jiangxi, Taiwan; Indochina.
Ecology: Forests and grassy hillsides. Flowering: Aug.
Notes: The syntypes of Glossula calcarata (Hongkong Herb. No. 9620, 9621, K, HK) were collected by E. A. Voretzsch from Mount Gough in 1911.

Peristylus densus (Lindl.) Santapau & Kapadia 稠密闊蕊蘭（狹穗闊蕊蘭）
J. Bomb. Nat. Hist. Soc. 57: 128. 1960; FRPS 17: 405, pl. 64: 1–3. 1999; FGD 7: 377, fig. 192. 2006; FOC 25: 139. 2009.
Coeloglossum densum Lindl., Gen. Sp. Orchid. Pl. 302. 1835.
Habenaria stenostachya (Lindl. ex Benth.) Benth., FHK 362. 1861.
Platanthera stenostachya Lindl. ex Benth., J. Bot. Kew Misc. 7: 37. 1855; FKH 269. 1912.

Terrestrial herb requiring a resting period in winter, 25 cm tall at flowering time. Leaves 6 or 7, petiolate; petioles sheathing, 7–10 mm; leaf blades ovate or ovate-elliptic, 2–4 × 0.5–2 cm, acute. Flowers yellowish green, sessile, in terminal spike of 6–7 cm; dorsal sepal 3 × 1.5 mm, apex rounded; lateral sepals 3 × 1 mm; petals erect, narrowly ovate-oblong, obtuse; lip 3-lobed; spur 4 mm; column short; anthers parallel.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Lantau Island. HK sheet 7151, 27804.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Zhejiang; India, Burma, Myanmar, Thailand, Vietnam, Bangaladesh.
Ecology: Forests and grasses. Flowering: Jun.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).
Notes: The type specimen of Platanthera stenostachya was collected by J. G. Champion from Hong Kong Island between 1847 and 1850.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Peristylus goodyeroides (D. Don) Lindl. 闊蕊蘭
Gen. Sp. Orchid. Pl. 299. 1835; FKH 269. 1912; FRPS 17: 415, pl. 66: 1–4. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 995, pl. 423. 2000; FGD 7: 376. 2006; FOC 25: 141. 2009.
Habenaria goodyeroides D. Don, Prodr. Fl. Nepal. 25. 1825.

Terrestrial herb requiring a resting period in winter; natural flowering plants up to 40 cm tall, with the lower 15–20 cm bearing 2 or 3 sheathing cataphylls and 4–5 leaves in the middle. Leaves petiolate; petioles sheathing, 2.5 cm; leaf blade elliptic, 6–16 × 3–5.5 cm, base cuneate, margin undulate, apex acute. Flowers creamy-white, on scapes of 8 to 10 cm, forming a terminal, fusiform spike; dorsal sepal yellowish green, ovate, 5 × 3 mm, obtuse; lateral sepals oblique-ovate, 5 mm, obtuse, light green; petals creamy white, 4 mm long and wide, obtuse; lip white, trilobed, spur globose-ovoid; column wide, the base extending forward, united to lower margin of petals; anthers 2, thecae parallel, attached to sides of column; pollinia 2, sectile; ovary 4 mm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan, Lantau Island. L. T. Lo 380; HK sheet 7155, 7156.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Taiwan; Bhutan, Nepal, India, Myanmar, Laos, Vietnam, Thailand, Cambodia, Malaysia, Philippines, Indonesia, New Guinea.
Ecology: Exposed grassy hillsides. Flowering: Jul.–Aug.

Peristylus lacertifer (Lindl.) J. J. Sm. 撕唇闊蕊蘭
Bull. Buitenz. 3. s. 9: 23. 1927; FRPS 17: 418, pl. 64: 9–11. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 998. 2000; FOC 25: 142. 2009.
Peristylus chloranthus Lindl., J. Bot. Kew Misc. 7: 37. 1855; FKH 269. 1912.
Coeloglossum lacertiferum Lindl., Gen. Sp. Orchid. Pl. 302. 1835.
Habenaria lacertifera Benth., FHK 362. 1861.
Peristylus spiranthes (Schauer) S. Y. Hu, Chung Chi Journal 13(2): 2, fig. 1. 1976, et Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 34, fig. 10. 1977.

Perennial herb 1.5–3 cm tall. Leaves 2–3, crowded at ground level; leaf blades variable according to locality, lanceolate, ovate or ovate-elliptic, 5–12 × 1.5–3.5 cm, acute. Flowers small, 12–16 in a terminal spiral spike; the odd sepal erect, 1.8 mm wide; lateral sepals 3–3.5 mm; petals hidden by sepals; lip trilobate, lateral lobes linear; column green, 1.5 mm, spur pointed; column green; anther with parallel thecae; pollinia 2; ovary 1 cm, glabrous.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. Hu & But 21082 (CUHK); H. C. Tang 1023; Y. S. Lau 128.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan, Fujian; SE Asia.
Ecology: Grassy hillside in partial shade at the foot of banks along seldom used paths, forests and thickets. Flowering: Jul.–Aug.
Notes: The species was reported as Peristylus lacertiferus (Lindl.) J. J. Sm. previously (Check List HK Plants 381. 2002; 132. 2004).

Peristylus tentaculatus (Lindl.) J. J. Sm. 觸鬚闊蕊蘭
Fl. Buitenz. 6: 35. 1905; FRPS 17: 401, pl. 64: 4 – 6. 1999; FGD 7: 378. 2006; FOC 25: 139. 2009.
Glossula tentaculata Lindl., Bot. Reg. 10: pl. 862. 1825; FKH 270. 1912.
Glossaspis tentaculata (Lindl.) Spreng., Sys. 3: 694. 1826; FHK 361. 1861.

Terrestrial herb requiring a winter rest period underground; plants 17–30 cm high at flowering time. Leaves 3–4, crowded at the lower portion of stem; petioles sheathed, 4–6 mm; leaf blades elliptic, 3–6 × 1–1.2 cm, apex obtuse. Flowers green, 20–50 in a spike; sepals herbaceous, the dorsal one triangular, the lateral two oblique-falcate; petals light green, ovate, 3–4 mm; lip 3-lobed, the lateral lobes slender, elongate, filiform, 1–2.5 cm, the midlobe ovate-lanceolate, pointing down, 2–4 × 0.75 mm; spur subglobose, 2–2.75 mm; column short; ovary 6–7 mm, twisted.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. S. Y. Hu 11456, 13062 (CUHK); HK sheet 35658.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian; Vietnam, Thailand, Cambodia.
Ecology: Damp grassy banks, rocks along streams. Flowering: Sep.–Mar. of the following year.
Uses: Medicinal (folklore).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Mount Parker, Sham Chung, Tai Mo Shan, Sai Kung
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Phaius tankervilliae (L'Her.) Blume 鶴頂蘭
Mus. Bot. 2: 177. 1856 [“tankervillii”]; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 27(3–4): 464. 1974, et Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 92, fig. 51. 1977; FRPS 18: 265, pl. 45: 5. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 1001, photo 131. 2000; Cribb, M. Sun & G. Barretto, Kew Bull. 59: 549, fig. 1 – 2. 2004; FGD 7: 421, fig. 214. 2006; FOC 25: 291. 2009; Check List HK Plants 382. 2002; 133. 2004.
Limodorum tankervilliae Banks ex L’Her., Sert. Angl. 28: 1788.
Phaius grandifolius Lour., Fl. Cochinch. 2: 529. 1790; FHK 355. 1861; FKH 263. 1912.
Phaius tankervilliae (L’Her.) Blume f. veronicae S. Y. Hu & Barretto, Chung Chi Journal 13(2): 25. 1976.

Terrestrial perennial herb; pseudobulbs large, oblique-ovoid or conical, 3–6 × 3–3.5 cm, often partially covered by degenerated leaf-bases; cataphylls green, sheathing. Leaves 2–6, elliptic or oblong-lanceolate, plicate, glabrous, 20–60 × 3–10 cm, base attenuating into a petiole, apex acuminate; petiole 9–20 cm. Inflorescence a raceme, bracts membraneous, caducous, cymbiform; flowers large, resupinate, uniform in colour and shape, white outside, brown inside; sepals subequal, ovate-elliptic or oblong-lanceolate, 4–6 × 1–1.5 cm, base subcordate, apex acute and apiculate; petals elliptic or oblong, same length with sepals but slightly narrower, base cuneate and slightly reflexed, apex acuminate and slightly recurved; lip trumpet-like, embracing the column, base slightly adnate to the column-foot, the basal two-thirds of the outside whitish purple, the apical one-third dull purple, lighter along the margin, the basal portion of the inside dull purple maculated with darker lines towards the base, slightly villose with 2 calli at the middle; column white, apical end winged; anther white, protected by wings of the column; pollinia 8 in 4 pairs; ovary glabrous, whitish green.

Locality: Mount Parker, Sham Chung, Tai Mo Shan, Sai Kung. S. Y. Hu 9926, 11844 (CUHK); P. S. Choi 251.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Xizang, Fujian, Taiwan; tropical and subtropical Asia, Australia.
Ecology: Shade banks of streams in forests. Flowering: Mar.–Apr.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: The type specimen of Phaius tankervilliae (L’Her.) Blume f. veronicae S. Y. Hu & Barretto (S. Y. Hu 13145A, K, holotype; CUHK, isotype) was collected from Mount Parker in 1975. This coloured form is distinguished by the lemon-yellow sepal and petals, the lip being more tubular with a smaller ruffled yellow apical portion, and the anther being densely pilose on the sides. Moreover, a distinct species P. wallichii Lindl. has been reported recently by Cribb et al. (Kew Bull. 59: 547–554, fig. 3–4. 2004; voucher specimen: Barretto 146, K). Locally known from the estate of the Kadoorie Farm and Botanic Garden (KFBG) and thus being referred as the “Kadoorie Phaius” (Barretto, Check List of Plants at KFBG: 57. 2004), P. wallichii could be distinguished by these features: flowering spreading; tepals ochre-coloured, acuminate; lip with a yellow and purple-marked throat and a large, white, cuspidate, deflexed midlobe; spur slender, 11–20 mm long, distinctly bifid at the tip.

Pholidota cantonensis Rolfe 細葉石仙桃
Kew Bull. 1896: 196. 1896, et J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 36: 23. 1903; FHK 354. 1861; FKH 264. 1912; FRPS 18: 392. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 1005, pl. 427. 2000; FGD 7: 460, fig. 230. 2006; FOC 25: 338. 2009.

A small terrestrial herb; rhizome zig-zag, covered with brown scales; pseudobulbs globose-ovoid. Leaves petiolate, petioles 2–4 mm; leaf blades linear-lanceolate, 4–8 × 0.4–0.7 cm, acute. Flowers white-yellow, in a terminal raceme; pedicels 2 mm; sepals all white, 5 × 2.5 mm, acute; petals similar; lip undivided, ventricose, 3 mm, gibbose at base, apex subobtuse; column very short, 1.5 mm; anther suborbicular; pollinia 4; ovary 1 mm. Capsule ellipsoidal, 7 mm.

Locality: Tai Po, Lantau Island. S. Y. Hu 9701 (CUHK).
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Rocks in forests. Flowering: May–Jun.

Pholidota chinensis Lindl. 石仙桃
J. Hort. Soc. London 2: 308. 1847; FHK 354. 1861; FKH 264. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 82, fig. 44. 1977; FRPS 18: 394, pl. 65: 5–6. 1999; FGD 7: 460. 2006; FOC 25: 338. 2009.
Coelogyne chinensis (Lindl.) Rchb. f., Ann. Bot. Syst. 6: 237. 1861.

Terrestrial herb; rhizomes creeping; pseudobulbs ovate-oblong, 2–8 cm. Leaves 2, terminal to pseudobulb; petioles 1–2 cm; leaf blades ovate-elliptic, 10–20 × 3–4 cm, apex acute to acumninate. Flowers white to pale yellow, 5–20 in a pendant raceme on scapes of 2–4 cm; dorsal sepal ovate-elliptic, 10–12 × 5–8 mm; lateral sepals 11 × 7 mm, broader; petals ovate-oblong, 9–10 × 4 mm; lip firmly attached to base of column, fleshy, enlarged and sac-like at base, the rounded front lobe turning downward; column white 5 mm, winged; anther suborbicular; pollinia 4; ovary cylindrical. Capsules ellipsoidal, 1.2–1.8 cm, 6 ridged.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. S. Y. Hu 11089, 12744 (CUHK); P. S. Choi 199, 222.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Zhejiang, Fujian.
Ecology: Boulders in damp ravines in forests, high shaded valleys. Flowering: Jul.–Sep.
Uses: Ornamental, medicinal (folklore).

Platanthera mandarinorum Rchb. f. 尾瓣舌唇蘭
Linnaea 25: 226. 1852; FKH 269. 1912; FFJ 6: 644, fig. 569. 1995 [“mandarinonum”]; FRPS 17: 298, pl. 43. 6–7. 1999; FGD 7: 366. 2006; FOC 25: 105. 2009.

Terrestrial herb, up to 20 cm tall at flowering time; stems angular. Leaves one normal, 2–4 strongly reduced; normal leaf ellipticlanceolate, 3–5 × 0.8–1.7 cm, apex obtuse; the reduced upper leaves linear-lanceolate 1.5–3.5 × 4–7 mm. Flowers green, 5–12 in a terminal spike; dorsal sepal ovate-cordate, 4 mm long and wide, apex acuminate, acumen 1.5 mm; lateral sepals pointing downward, oblique linear-falcate, 8 × 2 mm, twisted at base; petals oblique ovate-lanceolate, pale green, 6–7 × 4 mm; lip tongue-like, 10 × 2 mm; spur slender, 1.5 cm, green; column creamy-white; anthers 2-thecae; pollinia 2, tessellate; ovary ellipsoidal, twisted and ridged.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan. S. Y. Hu 11628A (CUHK); HK sheet 27798.
Distribution: S, E & SW China, Henan, Shandong; Japan, Korea.
Ecology: Short grasses on exposed mountain tops. Flowering: Mar.–Jul.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tai Mo Shan, Shing Mun, Ma On Shan, Sunset Peak
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Platanthera minor (Miq.) Rchb. f. 小舌唇蘭
Bot. Zeit. Berlin 36: 75. 1878; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 31, fig. 8. 1977; FRPS 17: 303, pl. 43: 4–5. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 1014. 2000; FGD 7: 367, fig. 187. 2006; FOC 25: 109. 2009.
Habenaria japonica (Thunb.) A. Gray var. minor Miq., Ann. Mus. Bot. Lugduno-Batavum 2: 207. 1865.
Platanthera interrupta Maxim., Bull. Acad. Sci. St. Petersb. 31: 106. 1886; FKH 269. 1912.

Terrestrial herb, 15 30 cm tall at flowering time; stems 5-angled. Leaves one basal, the largest, ovate-elliptic to oblonglanceolate, petiolate, petioles 1.5 cm; cauline leaves linearlanceolate, sessile, 8–10 × 1.3–1.5 cm. Flowers yellowish green, 5–12 in a terminal spike; odd sepal ovate, 6 × 5 mm, acute; lateral sepals ovate-falcate, 7 × 2.5 mm; petals oblique-ovate, 6 mm, the upper margin connivent with odd sepal; lip calcarate, ovatelanceolate, 9 × 3–3.5 mm, greenish yellow, with a slender spur 1.4 cm; column 2.5 mm; anthers 2, obovate, at each side of the column.

Locality: Tai Mo Shan, Shing Mun, Ma On Shan, Sunset Peak. S. Y. Hu & P. P. H. But 20548 (CUHK); Y. S. Lau 2171, 2972.
Distribution: NE, E, C, S & SW China; Korea, Japan.
Ecology: Grasses on sunny mountain slopes or shade of ravines on humus-covered rock niches. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.

Robiquetia succisa (Lindl.) Seidenf. & Garay 寄樹蘭（小葉寄樹蘭）
Bot. Tisskr. 67: 119. 1972; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 116, fig. 68. 1977; FRPS 19: 368, pl. 55: 1–2. 1999; FGD 7: 484. 2006; FOC 25: 476. 2009.
Sarcanthus succisus Lindl., Bot. Reg. 12: t. 1014. 1826.

Epiphytic herb; roots cord-like, shiny grey, turning to olive green when old; stems monopodial. Leaves distichous, petiolate; petioles sheathing, green; leaf blades leathery, linear-oblong, 5–10 × 1.5–2.3 cm, midrib shallowly impressed above, evident beneath, base truncate, apex erose, emarginate, truncate and apiculate. Flowers non-resupinate; pale greenish yellow to lemon-yellow, in places washed and streaked red; sepals orbicular, fleshy, odd sepal concave, 4 mm in diam., apex rounded, greenish yellow washed red in the centre; lateral sepals plane, 5 mm in diam.; petals orbicular, the inner margin fitting into the concave depression of the odd sepal, waxy yellow, flushed red throughout; lip calcarate, disk funnel-shaped, the anterior side extended into a tongue-like lobe with 2 longitudinal ridges in the centre, lateral lobes thickened below, wing-like, erect above with a well-marked deep purple vertical line on each side; column white, short, thick, apex truncate, concave, the anterior portion extended upwards into 2 stout arms, the foot thick and united with the posterior wall of the funnelshaped portion of the lip, extending into a screen-like callus partially covering the throat of the spur; anther white, suborbicular, concave; pollinia 4 in 2 pairs, waxy, attached by a short filament onto the stipe; ovary short, ridged and canaliculate.

Locality: New Territories. S. Y. Hu 10815A (CUHK); HK sheet 7117.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Fujian; Indochina, Myanmar, Thailand, N India, Sikkim, Bhutan.
Ecology: Shade cliffs along streams. Flowering: Jun.–Sep

Spathoglottis pubescens Lindl. 苞舌蘭
Gen. Sp. Orch. Pl. 120. 1831, et Bot. Reg. 8(n. s.): sub. t. 19. 1845; FKH 263. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 75, fig. 38. 1977; FRPS 18: 252, pl. 44: 3–4. 1999; FGD 7: 411, fig. 211. 2006; FOC 25: 288. 2009.
Spathoglottis fortunei Lindl., Bot. Reg. 31: pl. 19. 1845; FHK 355. 1861; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 71. 1977.

Terrestrial herb, requiring a dormant period over dry season; roots profuse, fibrous, originating from a basal point of the pseudobulb; pseudobulbs irregularly tuberous, compressed, often angular or irregularly humped. Leaves 2–4, all basal, emerging from the base of the pseudobulb; petioles sheathing, purplish; cataphylls membraneous, purplish and soon disintegrating; leaf blades linear-lanceolate, plicate, 12–35(–43) × 1–3(–4.5) cm, base cuneate, apex acute or acuminate. Flowers bright yellow, resupinate; sepals similar in length and width, 1.2–1.6 × 0.5–0.7 cm; the odd one ovate-elliptic, concave, apex acute; lateral ones oblique ovate-oblong, apex acute; petals ovate, similar length with sepals but slightly wider, conspicuously veined; lip strongly 3-lobed, the base bluntly saccate, the interior of the sac with 2 barbate ridges along the disk; lateral lobes oblong, extending forward, the inner surface flecked, speckled or wholly bright brownish red; the midlobe panduriform, with 2 waxy, fleshy, orange calli at the base, with a ridge between the calli extending forward to apex, column long, arching, yellow, winged along the side with a basal annulus; anther pointing downward, ovate, yellow; pollinia 8 in 2 groups of 4, waxy; ovary inconspicuously sulcate, very hairy.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. S. Y. Hu 10780, 10862 (CUHK); Y. S. Lau 3173.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang; India, Myanmar, Thailand, Indochina.
Ecology: Open grassy slopes, fire-resistant. Flowering: Jul.–Sep.
Uses: Ornamental.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Tsz Wan Shan, Shing Mun, Sai Kung, Lantau Island, Lamma Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Spiranthes hongkongensis S. Y. Hu & Barretto 香港綬草
Chung Chi Journal 13(2): 2, fig. 2b–f. 1976; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 41, fig. 14(B–F). 1977, et Enum. Sperm. Hong Kong 105. 2002; FOC 25: 85. 2009.

Acaulescent terrestrial orchid 12–37 cm tall at flowering time. Leaves all basal, oblanceolate, 4–12 × 0.5–0.9 cm, apex acute. Flowers white, many, spirally arranged in a hairy spike of 3–12 cm; sepals glandular hairy; odd sepal oblong, 4 mm, white, apex obtuse; lateral sepals white, tinged pink slightly; petals in close contact to odd sepal; lip straight, thickened at base, each side with a transparent gland; column 1 mm, triangular at apex; anther ovate; pollinia 4 in 2 pairs, powdery; rostellum narrow, membranous, truncate; stigma shield-like, trilobate along the upper margin. Ovary densely glandularly hairy.

Locality: Tsz Wan Shan, Shing Mun, Sai Kung, Lantau Island, Lamma Island. S. Y. Hu 10035, 13552 (CUHK); P. S. Choi 435.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guizhou, Yunnan, Shandong, Zhejiang, Fujian; Japan, Australia.
Ecology: Along little streams, paths between paddy, sunny grassy hillsides, newly available open habitats. Flowering: Mar.–Apr.
Notes: The type specimen (S. Y. Hu 13658, K, holotype; A, CUHK, isotype) was collected from Tai Po in 1975. Further to Hu and Barretto's (1976) observations, Sun (1996a, Amer. J. Bot. 83: 252–260) discussed the allopolyploid origin of this self-fertile species, which is a tetraploid (chromosome number ≈60) with putative parents being S. sinensis and S. spiralis (L.) Chevall. Spiranthes sinensis is a pollinator-dependent outcrosser, whereas S. hongkongensis is a pollinator-independent selfer, flowering 2–3 weeks earlier than S. sinensis (Sun 1996b, Conservation Biol. 10: 785–795). Spiranthes sinensis is glabrous on floral parts and its flower colour is normally pink and occasionally white, in a prominent spiral spike, whereas S. hongkongensis has grandular hairs on its bracts, sepals and ovaries in the creamy white flowers, inconspicuously arranged on a spiral spike. Rare occurrence of natural hybrids have also been observed, featuring both pinkish flowers and glandular hairs on floral parts.

Spiranthes sinensis (Pers.) Ames 綬草
Orchidaceae 2: 53. 1908; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 41, fig. 14(G–K). 1977; FRPS 17: 228. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 1034, pl. 442. 2000; FGD 7: 348, fig. 176. 2006; FOC 25: 85. 2009.
Neottia sinensis Pers., Syst. Pl. 2: 53. 1807.
Spiranthes australis Lindl., Bot. Reg. 10: sub. t. 823. 1824; FHK 360. 1861; FKH 267. 1912.

Terrestrial caespitose herb, glabrous throughout, requiring a resting period in winter. Leaves all basal, linear, 10–12 × 0.3–0.4 cm. Flowers pink, spirally arranged on a terminal spike; scape 15–20 cm; odd sepal dorsal, ovate-lanceolate, 3 mm; lateral sepals oblique-ovate, 3 × 1 mm, 4 mm between apices; petals adhering to dorsal sepal; lip white, recurved; column short, arcuate; anther buried in the clinandrium; pollinia 4 in 2 pairs; rostellum membranous, bifid; stigma discoid, green; ovary ovoid, 5 mm, glabrous. Capsule ellipsoidal.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. S. Y. Hu 10070, 13655 (CUHK); HK sheet 36119.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; E Asia, S to SE Asia, Australia.
Ecology: Sunny grassy hillsides. Flowering: Apr.–Jun.

Tainia dunnii Rolfe 帶唇蘭
J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 38: 368. 1908; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 67, fig. 33. 1977; FRPS 18: 237, pl. 40: 1–5. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 1043, pl. 447. 2000; FGD 7: 407, fig. 208. 2006; FOC 25: 284. 2009.

Terrestrial perennial herb; rhizome short and thick, consisting of 4 joints; pseudobulbs dull dark green or dull purple, ovatelanceolate, 1.5–3(–7) cm long, 5–12 mm in diam. Leaf solitary, terminal to the pseudobulb; petiole short, 3–5 cm; leaf blade lanceolate or elliptic-lanceolate, 20–30 × 2–4 cm, attenuate at both ends, with 3 prominent veins running from base to apex. Flowers resupinate, up to 21 in a well-spaced raceme; sepals and petals dull purple, tinged yellow, similar in length and width, 10–15 × 2–3 mm; odd sepal linear, apex obtuse; lateral ones falcate-linear, base joined to the column foot forming a short mentum, apex obtuse; petals falcate-linear, apex obtuse or acute; lip attached to a short mentum, 1 cm, narrowed at the base, widening to a 3-lobed blade; lateral lobes erect, light yellow densely speckled with purple inside, flushed dull purple outside, triangular-ovate, 2 mm, obtuse; midlobe panduriform, bright yellow, 6 mm across, truncate, lightly produced and obtuse at middle, with 3 longitudinal creamy yellow ridges, 2 lateral ones higher and more fleshy; column arcuate, winged at both sides; anther resembling the head of a cat, bright reddish purple; pollinia 8 in 4 pairs, ovary oblanceolate, glabrous.

Locality: Sunset Peak, Lantau Peak. Y. S. Lau 2988, 3097; HK sheet 34321.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan.
Ecology: Forests and ravines. Flowering: Mar.–Apr.

Thelasis pygmaea (Griff.) Blume 矮柱蘭
Fl. Jav. Orch. 23. 1858; FRPS 19: 62. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 1046, pl. 448. 2000; FOC 25: 366. 2009.
Euproboscis pygmaea Griff., Calc. J. Nat. Hist. 5: 731, t. 26. 1845.
Thelasis hongkongensis Rolfe, Kew Bull. 199. 1896, et J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 36: 39. 1903; FKH 267. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 76, fig. 39. 1977.

Saxicolous herb; pseudobulbs compressed, globose, growing close together, 7–11 mm in diam. Leaves terminal, solitary, leathery, oblong or oblanceolate, 1–4.5 × 0.7–1 cm, base cuneate, apex rotundate or obtuse, midrib impressed above, slightly elevated beneath. Flowers non-resupinate, creamy white with a greenish tinge; odd sepal ovate-lanceolate, 2 × 1 mm; lateral sepals folded, 2.5 × 1 mm, apex rotundate, back with a keel running down to the base of the ovary; petals shorter than the sepals, oblong-linear, transparent with 1 medium-longitudinal vein, apex obtuse; lip simple, undivided, ovate-lanceolate and triangular, 2 mm, the base shortly stiped, apex obtuse, margins slightly curved upwards near the base; column very short, horizontal, dorso-ventrally compressed, ovoid, beak-like at the apex, the dorsal side concave, containing an ovoid beak-like 2-chambered anther; pollinia 8 in 2 groups; ovary obconical, winged.

Locality: Aberdeen, Cape D'Aguilar. HK sheet 7120.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Yunnan, Taiwan; Nepal, Sikkim, India, Myanmar, Thailand, Vietnam, Malaysia, Indonesia, Philippines.
Ecology: Trunks or rocks by streams. Flowering: Apr.–Oct.
Notes: The type specimens of T. hongkongensis (H. F. Hance 1287, BM; C. Ford 13, K) were collected from Hong Kong Island around 1880.

Thrixspermum centipeda Lour. 白點蘭
Fl. Cochinch. 520. 1790; S. Y. Hu, Quart. J. Taiwan Mus. 28(1–2): 171. 1975, et Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 105, fig. 59. 1977, et Enum. Sperm. Hong Kong 109. 2002; FRPS 19: 345, pl. 50: 3. 1999; FGD 7: 486, fig. 249. 2006; FOC 25: 470. 2009.

Epiphytic herb; roots cord-like, shiny grey; stems monopodial, slightly compressed. Leaves distichous, thick, smooth, appearing sessile, leaf blades oblong-linear, 3.5–7 × 0.8–1.6 cm, base obtuse, apex rotundate, obliquely retuse and apiculate, midrib slightly impressed above. Flowers resupinate, pale yellow, two-ranked, ephemeral; sepals and petals linear-lanceolate, evenly spaced, forming a semicircle; odd sepal dorsal, 2.6 × 0.3 cm; lateral sepals widespread, oblique, 3 mm wide at base; petals slanting upwards, 2.2 × 0.2 cm; lip 3-lobed, white, fleshy, saccate; lateral lobes very short, 2 mm, arching over the column with downy hair along the margin; midlobe triangular, 6 mm, curved, base with a white callus 2.5 mm; disk speckled red both inside and outside; spur stout and rounded at base, papillose inside and at tip, lemon-yellow and fainly dotted pink; column white, very short, fleshy, triangular at the sides; pollinia 4 in 2 pairs, unequal; ovary shiny, smooth, light green.

Locality: Castle Peak, Sai Kung. HK sheet 27536, 33094.
