Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Yunnan; Sikkim, India, Myanmar, Indochina, Indonesia.
Ecology: Trunks in forests. Flowering: Aug.–Sep.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Tropidia curculigoides Lindl. 短穗竹莖蘭（仙茅竹莖蘭）
Gen. Sp. Orch. Pl. 497. 1840; FHK 359. 1861; FRPS 17: 122. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 1057. 2000; FGD 7: 342, fig. 171. 2006; FOC 25: 195. 2009.
Tropidia hongkongensis Rolfe, J. Linn. Soc. Bot. 36(249): 40. 1903; FKH 267. 1912; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 53, fig. 23. 1977.

Terrestrial herb, 30–70 cm tall at flowering time, with short and thick rhizome and fibrous roots. Stems erect, unbranched or occasionally branched, internodes usually 2–4 cm. Leaves elliptic-lanceolate, 15–25 × 2–4 cm, apex acuminate. Flowers green-white, in terminal or axillary racemes; sepals lanceolate, 7–10 mm, base of the lateral two connate; petals 6–8 mm; lip ovate-lanceolate, acute; column 3 mm; anthers 1.5 mm. Capsules oblong, 2 cm.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Tai Mo Shan. HK sheet 7119.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Xizang, Taiwan; India, Sikkim, Myanmar, Vietnam, Cambodia, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia.
Ecology: Shady area along streams. Flowering: Jul.–Aug.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Hong Kong Island, Ma On Shan, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Vrydagzynea nuda Blume 二尾蘭
Fl. Jav. Orch. 61, t. 20, fig. 3(3–8). 1858; FKH 267. 1912; FHN 4: 204. 1977; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 52, fig. 22. 1977, et Enum. Sperm. Hong Kong 106. 2002; FRPS 17: 203. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 1070, pl. 460. 2000; FGD 7: 362, fig. 184. 2006; FOC 25: 76. 2009.

Small glabrous herb, 5–15 cm tall; rhizome elongate, creeping, wire-like, up to 30 cm, internodes 2.5–3 cm, 3 mm in diam.; upright stem continuing the rhizome, bearing 3–4 leaves before flowering. Leaves petiolate; petioles 1.3–1.6 cm; leaf blades ovate-elliptic, 2.5–4 × 1.5–2 cm, apex acute. Flowers creamy-white; odd sepal ovate-oblong, 5 mm; lateral sepals oblique-ovate, 5 mm, the lower portion covering the spur; petals white, shorter than sepals, partially concealed by sepal; lip undivided, calcarate, concealed by the sepals; spur bladder-like; column green, 1.5 mm; anther discoid, orange-brown; pollinia 2; ovary cylindrical, 5–6 mm, hairy.

Locality: Hong Kong Island, Ma On Shan, Lantau Island. S. Y. Hu 11810 (CUHK); C. P. Lau 108 (CUHK); HK sheet 38876.
Distribution: Hainan, Guangdong, Taiwan; Indonesia.
Ecology: Well-drained soil in forests. Flowering: Apr.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Victoria Peak, Lugard Rd., Mount Parker, Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Zeuxine affinis (Lindl.) Benth. 纖細線柱蘭
Fl. Brit. India 6: 108. 1890; FOC 25: 75. 2009.
Monochilus affinis Lindl., Gen. Sp. Orchid. Pl. 487. 1840.
Zeuxine gracilis auct. non (Breda) Blume, S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 50, fig. 20. 1977; Check List HK Plants 384. 2002; 133. 2004.

Small terrestrial herb; stems trailing, 3 mm in diam. Leaves 4–7, cauline, leaf blades ovate, 1–4 × 0.6–2 cm, apex acute. Flowers small, white, 5–10 in a terminal spike; odd sepal ovate, 6 × 5 mm at base, green with pink apex; lateral sepals elongatetriangular, 5 × 2 mm, apex obtuse; petals oblique-ovate, 4 mm, white, the upper margin adhere to odd sepal forming a galea; lip white, fleshy, wavy, saccate, apex 2-lobed; column 1 mm long; anther elongate-ovoid, 2.5 mm; pollinia 2, sectile; ovary woolly, 8 mm long. Capsule ellipsoidal, 7 mm, hairy.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Lugard Rd., Mount Parker, Tai Mo Shan, Ma On Shan. S. Y. Hu 12276, 12277 (CUHK); HK sheet 34778.
Distribution: Hainan, Yunnan.
Ecology: Sunny slopes, roadsides. Flowering: Sep.–Oct.

Zeuxine parvifolia (Ridl.) Seudebf. 白花線柱蘭
Dansk Bot. Ark. 32(2): 82. 1978; FRPS 17: 199, pl. 27: 5–7. 1999 [“parviflora”]; FGD 7: 361. 2006 [“parviflora”]; FOC 25: 74. 2009.
Hetaeria parvifolia Ridl., J. Straits Branch Roy. Asiat. Soc. 39: 87. 1903.
Zeuxine leucochila Schltr., Repert. Spec. Nov. Regni Veg. 3: 46. 1907; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 49. 1977.

Small terrestrial herb, 15–20 cm tall. Leaves 3–5, ovate-oblong, 2–4 × 1–1.5 cm, apex acute. Flowers small, white, 3–9 in a terminal raceme on stipe 10 cm; odd sepal ovate-lanceolate, 4 mm, lateral sepals oblong-ovate, 4.5 × 2 mm, acute; petals white, oblonglanceolate, 4.5 mm, obtuse, forming a galea with the odd sepal; lip T-shaped, white and yellow at base, 4.5–5 mm, base saccate, apex 4 mm, 2-lobed, lobes oblong, entire or shallowly toothed.

Locality: New Territories (Hu 1977), Sai Kung (Siu 2000).
Distribution: Hainan, Yunnan, Taiwan; Thailand, Malaysia, Myanmar, Laos, Cambodia, Vietnam, Philippines, Japan.
Ecology: Forests and hillslopes. Flowering: Feb.–Apr.
Notes: The species was reported as Zeuxine parviflora (Blume) J. J. Sm. previously (Check List HK Plants 133. 2004).

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Victoria Peak, Sha Tin, Ma On Shan, Fanling, Tai Lung, Tsang Tsui, Sham Chung, Lantau Island
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Zeuxine strateumatica (L.) Schltr. 線柱蘭
Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 45(3): 394. 1911; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 49. 1977; FRPS 17: 194. 1999; FTW ed. 2, 5: 1080. 2000; FGD 7: 360, fig. 183. 2006; FOC 25: 72. 2009.
Orchis strateumatica L., Sp. Pl. 2: 943. 1753.
Zeuxine membranacea Lindl., Gen. Sp. Orch. 486. 1840; S. Y. Hu, Genera Orchid. Hong Kong 49. 1977.
Zeuxine sulcata Lindl., Gen. Sp. Orch. Pl. 485. 1840; FHK 360. 1861; FKH 267. 1912.

Delicate terrestrial herb with a rhizome consisting of 4 internodes; stem upright. Leaves 8 or 9, olive-green with pink veins and margin, leaf blade linear-lanceolate, the middle larger ones 2.5–3.5 × 0.3–0.5 cm, glabrous. Flowers white, with pink veins 5–15 in a terminal spike 2 cm long, with pink lower bracts; dorsal sepal ovate-oblong, 6 mm, base saccate; lateral sepal 4 mm, ovate-oblong; petals oblique-linear, forming a hood with the odd sepal; column short; anther ovate-oblong; pollinia 2, sectile; ovary obovoidellipsoidal. Capsule 5 mm.

Locality: Victoria Peak, Sha Tin, Ma On Shan, Fanling, Tai Lung, Tsang Tsui, Sham Chung, Lantau Island. S. Y. Hu 12807 (CUHK); S. Y. Hu & P. P. H. But 23110 (CUHK); Y. S. Lau 3202.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hubei, Fujian, Taiwan; Japan, tropical Asia.
Ecology: Damp open grasslands, open ground between large trees in forests. Flowering: Nov.–Feb. of the following year.

Ginkgo biloba L. 銀杏
Mant. Pl. 2: 313. 1771; FRPS 7: 18. 1978; FOC 4: 8. 1999; FGD 4: 6, fig. 3. 2000.

Tree, deciduous, up to 40 m high and 4 m in d.b.h.; bark greyish brown, fissured and rough; branches nearly verticillate, ascending; long branches pale brownish yellow to grey; brachyblasts densely covered by leaf scar, grey. Leaves spirally arranged on 1st year branches, and 3–8 in clusters on brachyblasts, pale green, turning yellow before fallen off in autumn, fan-shaped, 5–8 cm wide at apex, notched or bilobed, base broadly cuneate, glabrous, with many dichotomous veins; petiole 3–10 cm. Pollen cones pedunculate, catkinlike, pendulous, microsporophylls with short stipe. Seed ellipsoid or ovoid, 2.5–3.5 × 2 cm, yellow or orange when mature, glaucous.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. P. S. Choi 417, 472.
Distribution: Zhejiang (Tianmushan). Widely cultivated in China and E Asia, Europe and America.
Ecology: Pollinating: Mar.–Apr.; seed maturing: Aug.–Oct. Uses: Ornamental, medicinal, food (seeds).

Araucaria cunninghamii Aiton ex D. Don 南洋杉
Lambert, Descr. Pinus, ed. 2, 3: t. 79. 1837; FRPS 7: 28. 1978; FOC 4: 9. 1999; FGD 4: 8. 2000.

Tree to 30 m tall (up to 70 m in original habitats); bark grey-brown or dark grey, rough, transversely split; crown tower-shaped; lateral branchlets dense, drooping. Leaves dimorphic: leaves of young trees and lateral branchlets loosely arranged, needlelike, falcate, subulate, or triangular, ca. 0.7–1.7 cm × 2.5 mm wide at base, stomatal lines numerous adaxially and weakly evident abaxially; leaves on mature trees and cone-bearing branchlets densely arranged, overlapping, stretching upward, ovate to triangular, 0.6–1 cm, ca. 4 mm wide at base, ridged or not, midvein obvious or not, with many white stomatal lines adaxially, only with irregular stomatal lines at lower half abaxially. Pollen cones terminal, solitary, ovoid or ellipsoid. Seed cones ovoid or ellipsoid, 6–10 × 4.5–7.5 cm; bracts narrowly obovate, sharply ridged, with thin, lateral wing, apex caudate, thickened, acute, obviously reflexed; seed scales thin at apex. Seeds ellipsoid, with a membranous, lateral wing.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. Y. S. Lau 433; L. T. Lo 476.
Distribution: Cultivated in S & SW China. Native to Papua New Guinea; NE Australia.
Uses: Ornamental.

Araucaria heterophylla (Salisb.) Franco 異葉南洋杉
Anais Inst. Super. Agron. 19: 11. 1952; FRPS 7: 30. 1978; FOC 4: 10. 1999; FGD 4: 9. 2000.
Eutassa heterophylla Salisb., Trans. Linn. Soc. London 8:316. 1807.

Tree to 30 m (up to 70 m in original habitats); bark dark grey, flaking; crown tower-shaped; branchlets spreading horizontally or drooping; lateral branchlets usually pinnately arranged, drooping. Leaves dimorphic: those of young trees and lateral branchlets loosely arranged, spreading openly, bright green, glaucous abaxially, subulate, usually laterally depressed, upcurved, 6–12 mm, 3- or 4- ridged; those of mature trees and cone-bearing branchlets densely arranged, slightly openly spreading, broadly ovate or triangularovate, 5 –9 mm, widest at base, midvein obviously raised or not, apex obtuse. Pollen cones terminal, solitary. Seed cones subglobose, 8 –12 × 7–11 cm, sometimes wider than long; apex of bracts triangular, flattened, acute, upcurved. Seeds ellipsoid, slightly flattened, with a lateral wing.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. Y. S. Lau 432; HK sheet40551.
Distribution: Cultivated in SE & SW China; native to Australia(Norfolk Island).
Uses: Ornamental.

Keteleeria fortunei (A. Murr.) Carr. 油杉
Rev. Hort. 37: 449. 1866; FRPS 7: 50. 1978; FOC 4: 42. 1999; FGD 4: 12. 2000.
Picea fortunei A. Murr., Proc. Hort. Soc. 421. 1862.

Tree to 30 m tall; trunk to 1 m d.b.h.; bark dark grey, rough, irregularly fissured; branches spreading; young branchlets hairy or glabrous, reddish or pale pink when dry, 2 or 3 years old branchlets pale yellowish grey or yellowish brown. Leaves linear, 1.2–3 cm long, 2–4 mm wide, base attenuate, apex obtuse or rounded, green and glossy adaxially, pale green abaxially, stomatal lines 12–17 on each side abaxially. Seed cones cylindric, 6–18 cm long, 5–6.5 cm in diam. Seed scales compressed orbicular, rhombic-orbicular, or rarely oblong, thick or thin, 2.5–3.2 × 2.7–3.5 cm, exposed part glabrous abaxially, margin entire, apex convex, rounded, or roundedtruncate. Seeds oblong, 1–1.3 cm × 5–6 mm; wing yellowish brown, more or less cuneate, apex oblique.

Locality: Cape D'Aguilar, Stanley. Y. S. Lau 1584, 1266.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Zhejiang, Jiangxi, Hunan, Guizhou, Yunnan; Vietnam.
Ecology: In secondary forests, on coastal hillside. Pollinating: Mar.–Apr.; seed maturing: Oct.
Uses: The species is propagated locally for afforestation and ex-situ conservation.
Notes: Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

Pinus elliottii Engelm. 濕地松
Trans. Acad. Sci. St. Louis. 4: 186, pl. 1–3. 1880; FRPS 7: 274, pl. 65: 8 –14. 1978; FOC 4: 20. 1999; FGD 4: 17. 2000.

Tree to 30 m tall; trunk to 0.8 m d.b.h. in native range; bark orange- or purple-brown, furrowed into irregularly oblong, large, papery, scaly plates; branchlets growing twice or more each year, orange-brown, later becoming brown to greyish brown, stout, roughly scaly; winter buds silvery brown, cylindric, scales fringed at margin. Needles 2 or 3 per bundle, 18–25 cm × 2 mm, stout, yellow- or blue-green, stomatal lines present on all surfaces, base with persistent sheath 1–2 cm, margin finely serrulate, resin canals 2–9(–11), mostly internal. Seed cones solitary or paired, pedunculate (peduncle to 3 cm), pale brown, ovoid or ovoidcylindric when open, (7–)9–18(–20) cm, maturing in 2 years. Apophyses lustrous, slightly raised, strongly cross keeled; umbo depressed-pyramidal, with a short, stout prickle. Seeds dark brown, ellipsoid, 6–7 mm, apex oblique; wing to 2 cm.

Locality: Widely planted in countryside. Y. S. Lau 2950.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Fujian, Taiwan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Jiangsu, Anhui, Hubei (introduced). Native to SE United States.
Uses: Afforestation.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Common in Hong Kong, also widely planted in countryside
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Pinus massoniana Lamb. 馬尾松
Descr. Pinus. 1: 17. 1803; FKH 10: 256. 1912; FRPS 7: 263, pl. 63: 1– 6. 1978; FOC 4: 14. 1999; FGD 4: 16. 2000.
Pinus sinensis auct. non Lamb.: FHK. 337. 1861

Tree to 45 m tall; trunk to 1.5 m d.b.h.; bark red-brown, irregularly scaly and flaking; crown broadly pyramidal or umbrellalike; branchlets usually growing once per year, yellowish brown, occasionally glaucous; winter buds brown, ovoid-cylindric or cylindric. Needles 2(rarely 3) per bundle, slender, slightly twisted, 10–18 cm, stomatal lines present on all surfaces, resin canals 4–8, marginal, base with persistent sheath. Seed cones pendulous, shortly pedunculate, green, turning chestnut brown at maturity, ovoid, conical-ovoid, or ovoid-cylindric, 4–7 × 2.5–5 cm. Seed scales suboblong-obovoid or subsquare; apophyses rhombic, slightly swollen or flat, slightly transversely ridged; umbo flattened, slightly sunken, blunt or shortly mucronate in apical part of cone. Seeds narrowly ovoid, 4–6 mm; wing 1.6–2.1 cm.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong, also widely planted in countryside. Champion s.n. (K); H. C. Tang 1227. Distribution: Areas S of Changjiang River.
Ecology: On hills. Pollinating: Apr.–May; seed maturing: Oct.–Dec. of 2nd year.
Uses: Afforestation.
Notes: The local populations of the species declined because of the attack of pinewood nematodes from 1978 onwards.

Cunninghamia lanceolata (Lamb.) Hook. 杉木
Bot. Mag. 54: t. 2743. 1827; FRPS 7: 285, pl. 66: 1–13. 1978; FOC 4: 55. 1999; FGD 4: 19, fig. 10. 2000.
Cunninghamia sinensis auct. non R. Br. ex Rich: FHK 337.1861; FKH 256. 1912.

Tree up to 50 m tall; trunk to 3 m d.b.h.; bark dark grey to dark brown, or reddish brown, longitudinally fissured, inner bark pale red. Leaves narrowly linear-lanceolate, straight or slightly falcate, 2– 6 cm × 3 –5 mm, base decurrent, apex usually symmetric and spinescent, margin denticulate, adaxial surface glossy deep green,with 2 narrow stomatal bands, bands white powdery or not, abaxial surface pale green, with 1 stomatal band along midvein each side, band white powdery. Pollen cone conical, 0.5–1.5 cm long, with a short peduncle, usually 40 clustered at apex. Seed cones terminal, 1–4 together, ovoid or subglobose; bracts glaucous or rather glossy, broadly ovate or triangular-ovate, base with short claw 1. Seeds dark brown, oblong or narrowly ovate, 5–6 × ca. 4 mm, narrowly winged laterally.

Locality: Widely planted in countryside. Y. S. Hsu s.n.; C. C. Luo 1281.
Distribution: Exact native distribution uncertain owing to widespread planting. Widely cultivated in areas S of Qinling Range; Cambodia, Laos, N Vietnam.
Ecology: Pollinating: Jan.–May; seed maturing: Aug.–Nov.
Uses: Afforestation, timber.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Fanling (recorded at Tai Hang Village in 1912, probably planted but no longer exist; see Iu & Lay, J. Roy. Asiatic Soc. H. K. Br. 22: 302–305. 1982). Also cultivated in gardens
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Glyptostrobus pensilis (Staunton ex D. Don) K. Koch 水松
Dendrologie. 2(2): 191. 1873; FRPS 7: 299, pl. 69. 1978; FOC 4: 57. 1999; FGD 4: 22, fig. 12. 2000.
Thuja pensilis Staunton ex D. Don in Lamb., Descr. Pinus, ed. 2, 2: 115. 1828.
Glyptostrobus heterophyllus (Brongn.) Endl., Syn. Conif. 70. 1847; FKH 255. 1912.
Glyptostrobus sinensis A. Henry ex Loder, Gard. Chron., ser. 3, 66: 259, fig. 118, 122, 123. 1919.
Taxodium japonicum (Thunb. ex L. f.) Brongn. var. heterophyllum Brongn, Ann. Sci. Nat. (Paris) 30: 184. 1833.
Taxodium sinense J. Forb., Pinet. Woburn. 179. 1839.

Semi-deciduous tree to 15(–25) m tall; trunk to 1.2 m d.b.h., basal part (ca. 0.7 m) buttressed; bark brown or greyish white with brown tinge, cracking into long, irregular strips; main branches spreading horizontally; lateral branchlets in 2 rows, those of older branches often very dense and broomlike. Scale leaves on mature branchlets appressed, ca. 2 mm long, with scattered, white, stomatal spots, adaxial surface convex, persistent; linear leaves compressed, thin, usually in 2-rows, 1–3 cm × 1.5–4 mm, pale green, base narrow, apex acute, with stomatal bands along midveins on each side abaxially; linear-subulate leaves compressed, slightly falcately recurved distally, 4–11 mm long, in 3-rows; linear and linearsubulate leaves deciduous with short branchlets in winters. Seed cones obovoid, 1.4–2.5 × 0.9–1.5 cm. Seeds brown, ellipsoid, slightly flattened, 5–7 × 3–4 mm, with a basal wing 4–7 mm.

Locality: Fanling (recorded at Tai Hang Village in 1912, probably planted but no longer exist; see Iu & Lay, J. Roy. Asiatic Soc. H. K. Br. 22: 302–305. 1982). Also cultivated in gardens. S. C. Lau s.n.; L. T. Lo 280.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Sichuan, Jiangxi, Fujian; N Vietnam.
Ecology: River deltas, etc., on flooded or waterlogged soil in full sun; near sea level. Pollinating: Jan.–Mar.; seed maturing: Sep.– Oct.(–Nov.), persisting until following spring.
Uses: Ornamental.

Metasequoia glyptostroboides Hu & W. C. Cheng 水杉
Bull. Fan Mem. Inst. Biol., n.s. 1: 154. 1948; FRPS 7: 310, pl. 71. 1978; FOC 4: 60. 1999; FGD 4: 24, fig. 14. 2000.

Tree to 50 m tall; trunk buttressed at base, to 2.5 m d.b.h.; bark of young trees pale orange-brown, dark reddish brown to grey, fissured; branches ascending; branchlets pendulous; winter buds ovoid or ellipsoid, apex obtuse, scales yellowish brown. Leaves linear, (0.8–)1.3–2 (–3.5) cm × (1–)1.5–2(–2.5) mm, pale green, with 4–8 stomatal bands along midvein each side. Pollen cones ovoid, 2.5 –5.5 × 2–3.8 mm; bracts triangular-ovate or obovate, ca. 4 × 3 mm, lowest minutely ciliate distally, others glabrous. Seed cones purplish black when young, oblong-ellipsoid and to 9 × 5.5 mm at pollination, subglobose and 1.4 –2.5 × 1.6 –2.3 cm when mature; basal cone scales 9-ovulate, middle 7-ovulate, distal 5-ovulate, apical sterile. Seeds ca. 5 × 4 mm.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. Y. S. Lau 429; HK sheet 40548.
Distribution: Widely cultivated in China. Native to E Sichuan & NW Hubei.
Ecology: Pollinating: Jan.–Mar.; seed maturing: Sep.–Oct.
Uses: Ornamental.

Taxodium distichum (L.) Rich. 落羽杉
Ann. Nat. Hist. 16: 298. 1810; FRPS 7: 304, pl. 70: 1–3. 1978; FOC 4: 58. 1999; FGD 4: 22, fig. 13. 2000.

Deciduous tree, to 50 m tall, 2 m in d.b.h. in native habitat; pneumatophores present or absent around trunk; trunk swollen and buttressed at base, strongly tapered upward; bark brown, peeling off in long strips; main branches spreading horizontally or ascending; lateral branchlets 2-ranked. Leaves linear, flat, base twisted, 2-ranked on annual branchlets, 1–1.5 cm × 1 mm, apex acute, pale green, midvein depressed adaxially, yellowish green or greyish green, midvein raised abaxially, stomatal lines 4–8 on each side. Pollen cones borne in terminal, crowded, short, dense racemes or panicles 5–12 cm, shortly pedunculate, ovoid. Seed cones brownish yellow or white powdery, globose, oblong-globose, or ovoid, ca. 2.5 cm in diam.; cone scales shield-shaped, woody, ± conspicuously longitudinally grooved at apex. Seeds brown or reddish brown, irregularly triangular-pyramidal, 1.2–1.8 cm long, sharply ridged.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. Y. S. Lau 1705; HK sheet 34504.
Distribution: Introduced to Guangdong, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Shanghai, Jiangsu, Hubei, Henan. Native to SE region of N America.
Ecology: Pollinating: Mar.–Apr.; seed maturing: (Jul.–)Oct.
Uses: Ornamental.

Juniperus chinensis L. 圓柏
Syst. Nat., ed. 12, 2: 660. 1767; Mant. Pl. 1: 127. 1767; FOC 4:74. 1999; FGD 4: 30. 2000.
Sabina chinensis (L.) Ant., Cupress. Gatt. 54. 1857; FRPS 7:362, pl. 80: 6 – 8. 1978.

Tree to 25 m, 3.5 m in d.b.h., dioecious, rarely monoecious; bark greyish brown, fissured; branches spreading; branchlets straight or slightly curved, terete or 4-angled, 1–1.2 mm in diam.; crown of trees pyramidal to open, broad and irregular. Leaves dimorphic; needlelike leaves present on both young and adult plants, decussate or in whorls of 3, loosely arranged, ascending, nearly lanceolate, 6 –12 mm, with 2 white stomatal bands adaxially; scalelike leaves present on adult plants, decussate, closely appressed, 2.5–5 mm, abaxially with an elliptic slightly concave gland near center. Pollen cones yellow, ellipsoid, 2.5 –3.5 mm; microsporophylls 10–18, each with 3 or 4 pollen sacs. Seed cones mature in 2nd year, brown when ripe, usually glaucous, subglobose, 6–8 mm in diam., 1– 4-seeded. Seeds ovoid, 3–6 × 2–5 mm, slightly flattened, ridged, with resin pits, apex blunt.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. Y. S. Lau 2704; HK sheet 26824.
Distribution: Widely distributed in China; Korea, Japan, Myanmar, E Russia.
Uses: Ornamental.
Notes: Juniperus chinensis L. ‘Kaizuca’ (龍柏) is also cultivated in gardens in Hong Kong for ornamental purpose. It differs from J.chinensis by its crown being cylindrical or pyramidal, branches initiating from lower part and twisted.

Platycladus orientalis (L.) Franco 側柏
Portug. Acta Biol., ser. B, Sist. Suppl. 33. 1949; FRPS 7: 322, pl. 74: 5 –7. 1978; FOC 4: 64. 1999.
Thuja orientalis L., Sp. Pl. 2: 1002. 1753; FGD 4: 25, fig. 15. 2000.
Biota orientalis (L.) Endl., Syn. Conif. 47. 1847; FHN 1: 213. 1964.

Tree 8–20 m tall; trunk to 1 m (or more) d.b.h.; crown pyramidal when young, broadly ovoid when old. Leaves 1–3 mm, green, not glaucous, apex bluntly pointed; facial leaves rhomboid, with a conspicuous, linear, glandular groove at center abaxially; lateral leaves overlapping facial ones, boat-shaped, ridged, apex slightly incurved. Pollen cones yellowish green, ovoid, 2–3 mm. Seed cones when immature bluish green, when ripe reddish brown, subovoid, 1.5 –2.5 × 1–1.5 cm; fertile cone scale 1–2-seeded. Seeds greyish brown or purplish brown, ovoid, 5–7 × 3–4 mm, slightly ridged, usually wingless.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. S. C. Lau s.n.; Y. S. Lau 2067.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Fujian, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Jiangsu, Anhui, Shandong, Hunan, Hubei, Sichuan, Henan, Shaanxi, Gansu, Shanxi, Hebei, Inner Mongolia, Jilin, Liaoning; Korea, Russia.
Ecology: Pollinating: Mar.–Apr.; seed maturing: Oct.
Uses: Timber, ornamental.

Nageia nagi (Thunb.) Kuntze 竹柏
Revis. Gen. Pl. 2: 798. 1891; FOC 4: 80. 1999; FGD 4: 33, fig.22. 2000.
Myrica nagi Thunb., Syst. Veg. (ed. 14) 884. 1784.
Podocarpus nagi (Thunb.) Makino, Bot. Mag. (Tokyo) 17:113. 1903; FRPS 7: 404, pl. 90. 1978.

Tree to 20 m tall; bark nearly smooth, reddish brown, dark purplish red, peeling off in small, thin flakes; branchlets spreading; crown broadly conical. Leaves opposite; petiole strongly twisted at base; blade leathery, ovate-lanceolate, elliptic-lanceolate, or narrowly elliptic, 3.5–9 × 1.5–2.5 cm, base attenuate, apex acuminate, dark green and glossy adaxially, pale green abaxially, parallel veins indistinct. Pollen cones axillary, solitary or in clusters of up to 10, cylindric, 1.8–2.5 cm. Seed-bearing structures axillary, solitary rarely paired. Receptacle obsolete, consisting of few bracts. Epimatium green with white bloom when young, dark purple with sparser white bloom when ripe. Seed globose to pyriform, 1–1.5 cm in diam., with dense punctiform depressions, base pointed, apex rounded.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. HK sheet 26939, 34481.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Zhejiang; Japan.
Ecology: Pollinating: Mar.–May; seed maturing: Aug.–Nov.
Uses: Ornamental.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Coastal hillslopes on eastern seashores. It is also cultivated in urban parks and gardens
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Podocarpus macrophyllus (Thunb.) Sweet 羅漢松
Hort. Suburb. Londin. 211. 1818; FRPS 7: 412, pl. 93: 1–2. 1978; FOC 4: 83. 1999; FGD 4: 35. 2000.
Taxus macrophyllus Thunb., Syst. Veg. (ed. 14) 895. 1784.

Tree to 15 m tall; trunk to 30 cm d.b.h.; bark grey or greyish brown, irregularly fissured; branches dense, spreading, pale brown. Leaves spirally arranged on upper half of branchlets, sessile; blade linear-lanceolate, oblanceolate, or oblong-oblanceolate, 7–12 cm × 7–10 mm, base cuneate, apex mucronate or acute to long acuminate, margin slightly recurved, dark green and glossy adaxially, greyish green, pale green abaxially, midvein prominently raised adaxially, slightly raised abaxially. Pollen cones axillary, usually in clusters of 3–5, spikelike, 3–5 cm, subsessile, microsporangia ovoid. Seed-bearing structures axillary, solitary, shortly pedunculate. Receptacle red or purplish red when ripe, columnar. Epimatium purplish black when ripe, with white powder. Seed ellipsoid or ovoid, ca. 1 cm in diam., apex rounded, with a projected mucro.

Locality: Coastal hillslopes on eastern seashores. It is also cultivated in urban parks and gardens. P. S. Choi 340; Y. S. Lau 666.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Hunan, Anhui, Jiangxi, Fujian, Zhejiang, Jiangsu; Japan.
Ecology: Open thickets. Pollinating: Apr.–May; seed maturing: Aug.–Sep.
Uses: Ornamental.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Cultivated in urban parks and gardens
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Podocarpus macrophyllus var. maki Sieb. & Zucc. 短葉羅漢松
Abh. Math.-Phys. Cl. Königl. Bayer. Akad. Wiss. 4(3): 232.1846.
Podocarpus chinensis Wall. ex J. Forbes, Pinet. Woburn. 212.1839; FKH 256. 1912.

A small tree or shrublike. It differs from var. macrophyllus byshorter and denser leaves, 2–7 cm × 3–7 mm.

Locality: Cultivated in urban parks and gardens. HK sheet 26927, 26928, 40769.
Distribution: Cultivated in Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Fujian, Zhejiang, Jiangsu; Japan. Possibly native in Guangdong, Taiwan and Zhejiang.
Ecology: Pollinating: Apr.–May; seed maturing: Aug.–Sep.
Uses: Ornamental.

Podocarpus neriifolius D. Don 百日青
Lambert, Descr. Pinus. 2: 21. 1824; FRPS 7: 409, pl. 92: 1– 4.1978; FOC 4: 82. 1999; FGD 4: 35, fig. 24. 2000.

Tree to 25 m tall; trunk usually to 50 cm d.b.h.; bark greyish brown, shallowly fissured; branches spreading or ascending. Leaf blade lanceolate, leathery, usually slightly curved, 7–15 × 0.9 –1.3 cm, base cuneate into short petiole, apex long acuminate, midvein raised adaxially, flat or slightly raised abaxially. Pollen cones solitary or in clusters of 2 or 3, 2.5–5 cm, basal bracts numerous, spirally arranged. Seed-bearing structures axillary, solitary; peduncle 0.9 –2.2 cm. Receptacle orange-red when ripe, obconical-ellipsoid, 8–10 × 5–8 mm, base with 2 subulate bracts 2–6 mm. Epimatium purplish red when ripe. Seed ovoid or ovoid-subglobose, 0.8–1.6 cm, apex rounded or obtuse.

Locality: Victoria Peak. HK sheet 7044.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Xizang, Sichuan, Hunan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Taiwan; Nepal, NE India,Sikkim, Bhutan, Myanmar, Vietnam, Laos, Cambodia, Indonesia, Malaysia, Papua New Guinea, Philippines, Thailand, Pacific Islands.
Ecology: In forests. Pollinating: May; seed maturing: Aug.–Nov.
Uses: Ornamental.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Ma On Shan, Tai Mo Shan, Mount Parker, Sunset Peak, Lantau Peak, Sai Kung
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Amentotaxus argotaenia (Hance) Pilg. 穗花杉
Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 54: 41. 1916; FRPS 7: 455, pl. 104: 4–7. 1978; FFrev. ed. 1: 321, fig. 298. 1991; FOC 4: 92. 1999; FGD 4: 42. 2000.
Podocarpus argotaenia Hance, Journ. Bot. 21: 357. 1883;FKH 256. 1913.

Shrub or small tree to 7 m; bark greyish brown or pale reddish brown. Leafy branchlets ascending or suberect. Leaves subsessile or with a petiole up to 3 mm, dark green adaxially, linear or linearlanceolate, falcate or straight, 2–11 cm × 5–11 mm, leathery, base cuneate to attenuate, asymmetric, margin flat or very narrowly revolute, apex dark, callose, rounded to sharply triangular, abaxial surface with two 1–2 mm wide stomatal bands. Pollen-cone racemes borne (1 or)2– 4(–10) together, 1.5–6.5 cm; cones in ca. 12 pairs, ovoid, ca. 3.5 × 2.5 –3.2 mm; bracts ca. 6 at base of otherwise naked peduncle, distal bract ca. 2.5 × 2 mm, keeled; microsporophylls 6–8, peltate, each with (2 or)3(–5) pollen sacs. Seed-bearing structures with peduncle to ca. 2/3 length of subtending leaf. Aril bright red when ripe. Seed finally red, narrowly obovoid-ellipsoid, 1.9 –2.6 × 1–1.3 cm, with small, mucronulate apex; peduncle 1.1–1.4 cm, compressed-quadrangular, dilated below bracts, naked.

Locality: Ma On Shan, Tai Mo Shan, Mount Parker, Sunset Peak, Lantau Peak, Sai Kung. Y. W. Lam 165, 206.
Distribution: Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Sichuan, Xizang, Gansu, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Taiwan, Zhejiang, Jiangsu;Vietnam.
Ecology: In forests. Pollinating: Apr.; seed maturing: Oct.
Uses: Ornamental.
Note: Listed in Rare and Precious Plants of Hong Kong.

PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.Locality (FOHK English Version): Widely cultivated in gardens and parks
PlantInfo_HKHerbarium.flora_of_hk_content:
Cycas revoluta Thunb. 蘇鐵
Verh. Holl. Maatsch. Weetensch. Haarlem. 20(2): 424, 426 – 427.1782; FKH 256. 1912; FRPS 7: 7, pl. 1: 1– 6. 1978; FFJ rev. ed.1: 268, fig. 252. 1991; FOC 4: 4. 1999; FGD 4: 3, fig. 1. 2000.

Trunk to 2–8 m; bark grey-black, scaly. Leaves fascicled at apex of stem, 1-pinnate; petiole subtetragonal in cross section, 10–20 cm, with 6–18 spines along each side; leaflets in 60–150 pairs, straight to subfalcate, 10–20 cm × 4–7 mm, leathery, sparsely pubescent abaxially, base decurrent, margin strongly recurved, apex acuminate, pungent. Pollen cones pale yellow, ovoid-cylindric, 30–60 × 8–15 cm; microsporophylls narrowly cuneate, 3.5–6 × 1.7–2.5 cm, apex rounded-truncate, cuspidate. Megasporophylls yellow to pale brown, 14–22 cm, densely tomentose; stalk 7–12 cm; sterile blade ovate to narrowly so, 6–11 × 4–7 cm, deeply laciniate, with 21–35 lobes 1–3 cm; ovules 2 or 3 on each side of stalk, densely pale brown tomentose. Seeds 2(–5), orange to red, obovoid or ellipsoid, somewhat compressed, (3–)4–5 × 2.5–3.5 cm, sparsely hairy; sclerotesta not grooved on sides.

Locality: Widely cultivated in gardens and parks. HK sheet27073; Y. S. Lau 1896.
Ecology: Pollinating: May–Jul.; seed maturity: Sep.– Oct.
Distribution: Guangdong, Fujian, Taiwan. Widely cultivatedin China.
Uses: Ornamental.

Cycas taiwaniana Carruth. 廣東蘇鐵（台灣蘇鐵）
J. Bot. 31: 2. 1893; FKH 256. 1912; FRPS 7: 9, pl. 2: 1–4. 1978; FFJ rev. ed. 1: 268, fig. 253. 1991; FOC 4: 5. 1999; FGD 4: 4, fig. 2. 2000.
Cycas fairylakea D. Y. Wang, Cycads in China (eds. F.X. Wang & H.B. Liang): 54. 1996; FGD 4: 4. 2000.
Cycas revoluta Thunb. var. taiwaniana (Carruth.) J. Schust., Pflanzenr. 99, 4(1): 84. 1932.
Cycas siamensis auct. non Miq.: Check List HK Plants 26. 1993.

Trunk cylindric, to 3.5 m; bark dark brown or grey-brown, scaly. Leaves fascicled at apex of stem, 1-pinnate; petiole obovate in cross section, 40 –120 cm, with 30 –60 spines along each side of basal part, glabrous; leaflets in 70 –150 pairs, often falcate, 18 –35 cm × 11–14 mm, leathery, glabrous abaxially, midvein raised on both surfaces only when fresh, slightly raised or flat abaxially when dry, base decurrent, margin flat, apex attenuate, pungent. Pollen cones ovoid or ellipsoid-cylindric, 30–45 × 8–10 cm; microsporophylls narrowly cuneate, 2–3 cm × 5– 8 mm; apex obtuse-rounded, with very short, upcurved mucro. Megasporophylls more than 30, tightly grouped, 15 –22 cm, pale brown tomentose; stalk 8 –12 cm; sterile blade rhombic-ovate, 7–12 × 6 –7 cm, margin glabresent and pectinate, with (11–)23 – 47 lobes 2–3.5 cm, terminal lobe ± flattened, 2–3.5 cm × 5–10 mm, margin usually irregularly serrulate, apex acute; ovules 2 or 3 on each side of distal part of stalk, glabrous. Seeds 2(–4), pale yellowish, globose, or broadly obovoid, slightly compressed, 2.8–3.3 × 2.5 –3 cm; sclerotesta finely verrucose.

Locality: Cultivated. Y. S. Lau 690; HK sheet 27079.
Distribution: Guangdong, E Guangxi, SW Hunan, SE Yunnan; Vietnam.
Ecology: Pollinating: Apr.–May; seed maturing: Sep.–Nov.
Uses: Ornamental.

Zamia furfuracea L. f. 澤米蘇鐵（牙買加蘇鐵）
Aiton Hortus Kew. 3: 477. 1789.
Palmifolium furfuraceum (L. f.) Kuntze, Revis. Gen. Pl. 2: 803. 1891.

Stem tuberous, cylindrical, to 75 cm tall or more, ca. 20 cm in diam., old plants branched at apex. Leaves 5 –7 per crown, 0.5–2 × 0.1–0.25 m; petioles 15–25 cm, spiny, rare unarmed; leaflets 10–15 pairs, thick and stiff, obovate-oblong 16–18 × 4–6 cm, apex obtuse or irregular. Pollen cones solitary, erect, cylindrical, 7–12 cm long, 1.8 –2.5 cm in diam., densely light brown tomentose; peduncles 8 –10 cm long, 0.8 –1 cm in diam., densely light tomentose; microsporophylls in 10–12 vertical rows of 18 –20 each; sporangia in two patches on the lower edges of the sporophyll with a sterile center band 2–5 mm wide. Seed cones solitary, erect, cylindrical, 16–24 cm long, 6.5 –7 cm in diam., densely reddish tomentose, the sterile apex mucronate, ca. 2 cm long; megasporophylls arranged in 10–12 vertical rows of 14–15 each; peduncle 10–20 cm long, 1.5–2 cm in diam., densely tan tomentose. Seeds red when ripe, 1.1–1.5 × 0.8 –1 cm, light tan, smooth.

Locality: Cultivated in gardens. Y. W. Lam s.n. (HK sheet 34677)
Distribution: S China (cultivated). Native to Mexico.
Uses: Ornamental.

Gnetum luofuense C. Y. Cheng 羅浮買麻藤
W. C. Cheng et al., Acta Phytotax. Sin. 13(4): 89. 1975; FOC 4: 105. 1999; FGD 4: 44, fig. 31. 2000.
Gnetum scandens auct. non Roxb.: FHK 336. 1861, p.p.; FKH 255. 1912, p.p.
Gnetum montanum auct. non Makgraf: FRPS 7: 492, pl. 114: 1–5. 1978; FFJ rev. ed. 1: 324. 1991.

Bark purplish brown, lenticels shallow, obscure. Petiole 8–12 mm; leaf blade oblong, elliptic or oblong-ovate, 10–20 × 4 – 10 cm, leathery or papery, base rounded or broadly cuneate, apex shortly acuminate, glossy, reticulate veins evident on both surfaces. Male spikes simple or once branched; involucral collars 12–20, each collar with 60–80 male flowers plus 15–30 sterile female flowers, often patent at anthesis; male flower: basal hairs dense, brown, false perianth slightly succulent, in irregular rhomboid tube, apex truncate. Female spikes with 10–20 involucral collars, each collar with 8–13 female flowers. Seeds sessile, ellipsoid, 1.5–2.8 × 1.5–1.8 cm, very fleshy, base often contracted into an apparent stipe when dried, apex acute with a mucro, outer coat orange-red, coarsely reticulate-wrinkled when dried.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. H. C. Tang 1369; Y. W.Lam 635.
Distribution: Guangdong, Hainan, Fujian, Jiangxi, Hunan,Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan.
Ecology: Forest; Pollinating: May–Jul.; seed maturing:Aug.– Oct.

Gnetum parvifolium (Warb.) C. Y. Cheng ex Chun 小葉買麻藤
Acta Phytotax. Sin. 9: 386. 1964; FRPS 7: 498, pl. 117. 1978; FFJ rev. ed. 1: 325, fig. 301. 1991; FOC 4: 104. 1999; FGD 4: 44, fig. 30. 2000.
Gnetum scandens Roxb. var. parvifolium Warb., Monsunia 1: 196. 1900.
Gnetum montanum Markgraf. f. parvifolium (Warb.) Markgraf., Bull. Jard. Bot. Buitenzorg, ser. 3, 10: 468. 1930.
Gnetum scandens auct. non Roxb.: FHK 336. 1861, p.p.; FKH 255. 1912, p.p.

Bark pale or greyish brown, lenticels usually relatively conspicuous. Petiole 5 – 8(–10) mm; leaf blade elliptic to narrowly elliptic, or long-obovate, 4 –10 × 2.5 cm, leathery, base cuneate to subrounded, apex acute or attenuate, sometimes obtuse, lateral veins usually inconspicuous adaxially, reticulate veins conspicuous abaxially. Male inflorescences simple or once branched; peduncle slender, 0.5 –1.5 cm; involucral collars 5 –10, each collar with 40 –70 male flowers plus 10 –12 sterile female flowers, enclosed at anthesis; male flower: basal hairs few, brown, short, false perianth rhomboid. Female inflorescences usually borne on old branches, 10 –15 cm in fruit; peduncle 1.5 –2 cm; female spikes with involucral collars 6 –9 mm apart, nodes each with 5 – 8 female flowers, basal hairs brown, short. Seeds sessile or nearly so, red, elongate ellipsoid or fusiform to narrowly oblong-obovoid, (1.3 –)1.6 –2.2 cm × (4 –)5 – 8(–10) mm, 2–3 times as long as wide, apex usually with a small, pointed tip, outer coat thin, longitudinally striate when dried.

Locality: Common in Hong Kong. P. S. Choi 448; Y. W. Lam 844.
Distribution: Guangdong, Hainan, Guangxi, Guizhou, Fujian, Jiangxi, Hunan; Laos, Vietnam.
Ecology: Forests; 100 –1000 m. Pollinating: Apr.–Jun.; seed maturing: Jun.–Nov.
Uses: Food (seeds).
